title: PREREQ (BLOCKING): composition spike — batch-partition invariance of Voyage /v1/embeddings against live Voyage
description:
RDR-195 § Prerequisites, item 1. THIS BLOCKS ALL IMPLEMENTATION. Critical Assumption 1 — 'Voyage's /v1/embeddings embeds each input independently, so partitioning a batch does not change any individual vector' — is the ONLY assumption in this RDR whose failure is SILENT: wrong vectors stored, no error, no 400, no log line. Every other failure mode is loud. Gate round 1 reclassified it from a false 'Verified (Docs Only)' and that is why the round returned BLOCKED.

Spike shape (T2 `nexus_rdr/195-research-3`): embed one fixed text ALONE, then embed the same text INSIDE a large mixed batch, against LIVE voyage-code-3. Diff the vectors per text; expect per-text cosine ~1.

Supporting evidence that is NOT a substitute for the spike: (a) CceEmbedder.java:202 states that batching into one CONTEXTUALIZED call changes embeddings via cross-document context propagation, making the standard endpoint the deliberate contrasting case; (b) the status quo already depends on the property (300 texts/request today, and ChunkBatcher's bisect at chunk_batcher.py:477 already re-composes batches in production); (c) Bge768BatchCompositionTest gates the analogous property for a DIFFERENT embedder — analogy, not corroboration.

Requires a live VOYAGE_API_KEY. Consider /conexus:composition-probe.

If the spike FAILS (per-text vectors differ across compositions), STOP: the whole RDR's approach is invalid and the RDR must be iterated, not the code. Report that outcome loudly rather than proceeding.

---
Context pointers: RDR file `docs/rdr/rdr-195-voyage-batch-token-limit.md` (§ named above). T2: `nx memory get -p nexus_rdr -t 195-research-3` (spike shape), `195-research-2`, `195-research-1`. nx search terms: "VoyageEmbedder batch planner", "Bge768Embedder planBatches MAX_PADDED_TOKEN_AREA", "upsert_chunks per_collection_chunk_cap paging".
Discipline: TDD (test file before implementation); `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for any non-obvious design choice; SPAWN subagents for exploration/implementation rather than grinding inline (standing authorization); update continuation state via `memory_put(project="nexus", title="rdr-195-continuation.md")` at each milestone.
acceptance_criteria: Spike executed against live voyage-code-3 with per-text cosine measured for alone-vs-in-batch; result recorded in T2 as `nexus_rdr/195-research-3` with status flipped from unverified to verified (or the RDR reopened on failure); the RDR's Prerequisites checkbox 1 ticked.

title: RDR-194 P3c round 3: diag-view reassign fix leaves install-binary restart path + crash-loop recovery unprotected
design:
substantive-critic round-3 final verification (T2 nexus/rdr194-p3c-round3-final-verification-2026-08-17 [22766]): the nexus-v5lk3 three-fix round (reassign_diag_view_owner_before_restart + generation-aware heal + defer-to-existing provision) is wired ONLY into converge_engine's two restart-triggering call sites (upgrade_finish.py ~1146, ~1344).

GAP 1 (unprotected path): `nx daemon service install-binary <tag>` (commands/daemon.py service_install_binary_cmd) installs the new engine binary directly, then prints "nx daemon service stop && nx daemon service start" as the manual restart instruction -- neither call touches converge_engine or the reassign. This is the DOCUMENTED way to refresh the engine independent of a conexus package bump (AGENTS.md Engine-service release section), and is the literal escape hatch converge_engine's own NEEDS-HUMAN/DEFERRED messages point operators at. Crossing the taxonomy-011 floor this way hits the round-2 RAISE EXCEPTION on first boot, unprotected.

GAP 2 (no recovery once wedged): converge_engine's own decision tree treats "service not up" as an ordinary silent state (`return []`) -- verified this is the case whether the service was never started OR crashed via the RAISE EXCEPTION. `nx daemon restart-stale` delegates the engine leg entirely to converge_engine (no independent restart attempt). `nx doctor`'s `_check_engine_convergence` is read-only. `nx daemon service start` (used by OS autostart units too) never calls converge_engine at all. So once wedged via GAP 1, or via a transient PG-unreachable-at-predrop-moment failure inside converge_engine's own paths (reassign degrades to [] on probe failure and the restart proceeds anyway, by design), there is no automated backstop -- only the changeset's own RAISE EXCEPTION log message, requiring manual SQL as the OS-level PG superuser.

Scoped/bounded: this is a ONE-TIME floor-crossing exposure per install (once one taxonomy-011 walk succeeds, fix #2/#3 keep it stable) -- not a recurring wedge. But reachability at the crossing is the same "essentially every existing local install" population round 2 already found CRITICAL, and install-binary is arguably the MORE likely path for an engine-only refresh, not less.

Fix shape (not prescriptive): wire the same reassign_diag_view_owner_before_restart call into service_install_binary_cmd's own restart instruction path (or into its printed remedy becoming an automatic action), AND/OR give converge_engine (or nx doctor/restart-stale) a branch that detects "on-disk correct, service down/unresponsive, floor-crossing view still foreign-owned" and retries the reassign+restart rather than staying silent. Needs a real regression test exercising the install-binary restart path and a crash-recovery attempt, not just the reassign function in isolation (tests/db/test_pg_provision.py's existing 16 tests all cover the function, none cover the wiring gap).

Verdict: not-justified. critical_count 1.

title: taxonomy-011-1's bare DROP VIEW nexus.diag_chash_conformance is unguarded against the deliberately superuser-owned production view (GH #1402 class) -- will abort the entire P3c migration walk on cloud
design: Critical fix round (nexus-i3k3e) wrapped taxonomy-011-8's CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW / GRANT in insufficient_privilege exception handlers for foreign-owned-view safety, but changeset 1's own 'DROP VIEW IF EXISTS nexus.diag_chash_conformance;' (taxonomy-011-doc-id-bytea.xml, changeset taxonomy-011-1, bare SQL inside splitStatements=true, no DO/EXCEPTION wrap) was left unguarded. nexus_admin (Liquibase's migration role) is NOSUPERUSER and is never granted membership in or ownership-equivalent rights over the view-creating superuser role (verified: only pg_monitor WITH ADMIN OPTION + CREATE on DB/SCHEMA are granted to nexus_admin in pg_provision.py). nexus.diag_chash_conformance is DELIBERATELY superuser-owned by design (heal_diag_view_grants_and_ownership actively reassigns ownership back to the superuser/os_user on drift, RLS-exempt-owner requirement nexus-vounk) and GH #1402 already proved production carries this exact superuser-owned view (GrantsSvcForeignOwnedRelationTest's own javadoc: 'the deliberately superuser-owned nexus.diag_chash_conformance view'). DROP VIEW IF EXISTS only suppresses the object-does-not-exist error class; it does NOT bypass PostgreSQL's ownership check for DROP. On the real cloud upgrade path (an existing cluster where _provision_diag_conformance_view already created the view as the superuser BEFORE this Liquibase changeset ever runs), nexus_admin's DROP VIEW IF EXISTS will raise 'must be owner of view' and the changeset transaction rolls back -- the doc_id TEXT->bytea ALTER (the entire point of P3c) never executes. No test catches this: GrantsSvcForeignOwnedRelationTest only reconstructs foreign ownership AFTER the full changelog already ran once (so the DROP was a no-op the first time, view didn't exist yet); migration-rehearsal/run.sh never seeds/provisions the diag view before the candidate walk at all. taxonomy-011-8's own rollback ('DROP VIEW IF EXISTS nexus.diag_chash_conformance;') has the identical unwrapped-DROP gap. Fix: wrap changeset 1's DROP VIEW (and changeset 8's rollback DROP VIEW) in the same nested BEGIN/EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege pattern changeset 8's CREATE/GRANT already uses, degrading to a graceful skip (the foreign owner's stale TEXT-doc_id-referencing view definition would then need its own remediation path -- likely: since the view can no longer typecheck against a doc_id that is now bytea, the STALE view becomes broken/unusable for any query against it until the foreign owner manually drops or the ownership-healing path reasserts nexus_admin/BYPASSRLS ownership -- this consequence needs to be decided and documented, not just silently skipped). Add a test that seeds a superuser-owned diag view via the container superuser BEFORE running the full changelog for the first time (not after), proving the walk still completes.

title: _prune_misclassified_in_collection's F8c manifest-guard write always TypeErrors: atomic_manifest_replace() missing required 'collection' kwarg, silently no-ops every guarded prune
description:
Discovered rebuilding the RDR-191 GATE-2 regression tripwire (nexus-o8dil.7 acceptance item 3, rebuild authorized 2026-08-13). Both the pre-existing composition test and a new nexus-tbj48 shared-chash test in tests/test_o8dil7_prune_misclassified_manifest_antijoin_engine.py go RED against the real engine for the SAME reason.

## The bug

`src/nexus/indexer.py::_prune_misclassified_in_collection`'s inner `_guarded_delete` (around line 2646-2662) resolves the catalog writer's `atomic_manifest_replace` method and calls it as:

    writer(did, [_row_to_chunk_dict(r) for r in kept])

Exactly two positional args: `doc_id`, `chunks`. No `collection=` keyword.

`atomic_manifest_replace`'s real signature (`HttpCatalogClient.atomic_manifest_replace`, `src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:3054-3061`) is:

    def atomic_manifest_replace(self, doc_id, chunks, *, collection, new_collection=None, new_chunk_count=None)

`collection` is keyword-only with NO default (RDR-191, Hal ruling 2026-08-12 — "writers SEND the collection; the engine STAMPS it verbatim, NEVER infers it"). Calling without it raises:

    TypeError: HttpCatalogClient.atomic_manifest_replace() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'collection'

## Effect — silent, fail-safe-but-broken

The TypeError is caught by `_guarded_delete`'s own `except Exception` (indexer.py ~2653), which sets `ok = False`, logs `prune_misclassified_manifest_guard_write_failed` at WARNING, and refuses the delete entirely (`prune_misclassified_manifest_guard_refused_delete`). No dangling manifest row results — the failure mode is fail-safe in the data-integrity sense — but the practical effect is that `_prune_misclassified_in_collection` can NEVER successfully clean up a misclassified chunk that still has ANY live manifest reference, for ANY caller, ANY collection, unconditionally. It has presumably been silently no-op'ing since `collection` became required (RDR-191, ~2026-08-12), with only a WARNING-level log line as any signal — no exception surfaces to the caller, no CI test caught it (the only two existing real-engine tests of this path are the ones written for this rebuild; the rest are `_FakeCol`/`_FakeCatalog` doubles that never call the real client method and so never see the TypeError).

## Fix shape (not applied — this bead is detector-only scope)

`ManifestRow` (`src/nexus/catalog/types.py:296`) now carries a `.collection` field (nexus-kzso5's wire exposure). The straightforward fix is to pass `collection=` through to `atomic_manifest_replace` at the `_guarded_delete` call site — either from `doc_rows[did][0].collection` (the retracted row's own stamped collection) or, if that can be `None` talking to an older engine, from the document's registered `physical_collection`. Needs a decision on which is authoritative when they disagree (RDR-191 decoupled per-row `collection` from the owning doc's `physical_collection` on purpose — nexus-kzso5's own close note), not a unilateral pick.

## Reproduction

    uv run pytest tests/test_o8dil7_prune_misclassified_manifest_antijoin_engine.py -m integration -o addopts=""

Both `test_prune_misclassified_real_engine_no_dangling_manifest_row` and `test_prune_misclassified_shared_chash_second_live_document_protected` fail with the TypeError above (visible in the captured warning log + traceback), 2026-08-13, develop @ 2b792358a plus this rebuild's two test files (untracked).

## Constraints
- No silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems (this already fails safe, but silently — the WARNING-only signal is itself a gap).
- Detector-only task scope forbade fixing this in the same pass; filed per standing directive (never leave a finding in prose).
close_reason: Fixed in 8c75a61a3: _guarded_delete derives collection= from the manifest rows' own stamps (kept-else-full, unanimous-non-blank-else-loud-refusal via prune_misclassified_manifest_guard_collection_unresolved). Empirical proof: both RED tripwire tests GREEN post-fix; fakes hardened signature-strict in test_o8dil2 AND test_o8dil45 (same bug class found in its local fake). Stacked review clean ([22387]/[22388] r2). Full suites green.

title: nexus-mmkqe's tombstoned-owner protection reverses o8dil.5's reap-then-delete ordering, breaking nx store delete/expire and MCP store_delete for the common single-owner case
description:
PgVectorRepository.delete's anti-join (nexus-mmkqe, uncommitted @ f7796ab09) drops the
DELETED_AT.isNull() predicate so that a tombstoned owner's manifest row now COUNTS AS
"still referenced" and blocks chunk deletion. mmkqe's own javadoc claims: "Per
store_hook.py:738-741, delete_document tombstones ONLY -- it does not delete chunks in
the same call -- so no production caller in the funnel actually performs that immediate
pairing; the concern was hypothetical."

THIS IS FALSE, verified against three call sites still in the tree unmodified by this diff:

1. src/nexus/commands/store.py:474-486 (`nx store delete --id`, delete_cmd): calls
   `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids([doc_id], ...)` (tombstones the owning document) THEN
   `db.delete_by_id(col_name, doc_id)` (deletes the T3 chunk). The comment at :474-482
   explicitly documents this as the nexus-o8dil.5 round-2 fix: "Reaping first tombstones
   the owning document so the anti-join sees no live reference and the delete can
   actually succeed."

2. src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:2799-2825,2860 (`nx store expire`, `expire()`):
   identical pattern -- `reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes(expired_ids, ...)` runs BEFORE
   `self.batch_delete(name, expired_ids)`, same o8dil.5 round-2 rationale quoted in the
   docstring.

3. src/nexus/mcp/core.py:4604-4618 (MCP `store_delete`): `store_delete_catalog_cleanup`
   runs BEFORE `t3.delete_by_id`, same pattern, same o8dil.5 round-2 rationale in the
   inline comment at :4604-4614.

All three orderings exist SPECIFICALLY because the round-2 anti-join ("Live excludes
tombstoned owners") let the chunk delete succeed once its own manifest row was
tombstoned. mmkqe's reversal means: after the reap step tombstones the target document,
the chunk delete's stillReferenced check now finds that SAME just-tombstoned manifest
row and refuses to delete -- for the single-owner case, which is the overwhelmingly
common one.

CONCRETE BREAKAGE:
- `nx store delete --id X` (ordinary single-owner delete): `db.delete_by_id` returns
  False (server reports deleted=0) -> `delete_cmd` raises ClickException
  ("... existed ... moments ago but the delete did not remove it").
- `nx store expire`: `batch_delete`'s summed actual-deleted count is 0 for every
  TTL-lapsed note whose only reference was the just-reaped note itself -- the TTL sweep
  silently stops removing anything (not a lie -- it reports the true, now-always-zero
  count -- but the sweep is functionally dead).
- MCP `store_delete`: returns "Entry ... existed ... moments ago but the delete did not
  remove it -- likely anti-join-protected by another live reference" for EVERY ordinary
  note deletion.

NO TEST IN THIS DIFF CATCHES THIS. The only new test coverage
(PgVectorRepositoryDeleteAntiJoinTest#delete_tombstonedOwner_stillProtectsChunk_untilPurgeTrashReapsBoth)
exercises vectorRepo.delete() directly at the Java unit level with a manually seeded
fixture -- it does not go through the Python reap-then-delete caller sequence. No
Python-level test (unit, integration, or E2E) in the diff exercises `nx store delete`,
`nx store expire`, or MCP `store_delete` against the new anti-join semantics; git status
confirms none of store.py/store_hook.py/http_vector_client.py/mcp/core.py were touched
by this wave.

RESOLUTION NEEDS DESIGN, not a quick revert: mmkqe's underlying goal (a chunk whose ONLY
remaining reference is a DIFFERENT, tombstoned document should not be strandable by an
unrelated delete call) is real and worth keeping. What's wrong is conflating that with
"the document being deleted right now, via its own reap-then-delete call, should not be
able to delete its own chunk." Candidate fixes: (a) scope the anti-join's protection to
EXCLUDE the manifest row(s) belonging to the specific doc_id/chash pairing the caller is
currently reaping+deleting (a same-transaction carve-out), (b) have delete_document's
tombstone step ALSO retract (not just leave in place) the manifest rows for chashes the
SAME call is about to delete, (c) change the Python callers to delete-then-reap again
but solve the original round-2 problem a different way, (d) something else -- Hal
decides.

Origin: substantive-critic review of the nexus-191 delete-path quartet (mmkqe, 5da44,
wnpet, 4nll0) + erwvd, 2026-08-13, dispatched to critique against T2
nexus/rdr-191-dangling-definition-of-record [22364].
close_reason: Closed

title: ManifestCollectionStampTest.java fails test-compile — calls pre-collection-param writeManifest/appendManifestChunks/importChunksBatch signatures
description:
RDR-191 GATE-2 (nexus-o8dil.7) round: CatalogRepository.writeManifest/appendManifestChunks/importChunksBatch were changed to a REQUIRED 4-arg (tenant, docId, collection, rows) signature with no backward-compatible 3-arg overload. service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/ManifestCollectionStampTest.java (pre-existing tests AND all 12 new tests added this round, including the "6 heterogeneous batch" tests meant to prove the fix) still call the OLD 3-arg (tenant, docId, rows) form throughout.

Empirically confirmed: `cd service && ./mvnw -q -o test-compile` exits 1 with 205 [ERROR] lines, ALL located in this one file (no other test file has errors — CatalogRepositoryTest.java, StagingPromoteOpsIntegrationTest.java, http/CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest.java were all correctly updated to the new signature in this same round).

Beyond the compile break: the new tests' own content (eachRowStampedWithOwnVerifiedCollection_notPooled, partialResolution_unresolvedRowSkipped, ambiguousChashMembership_skipsRatherThanGuessing) test a per-chash "C-membership + sibling-tiebreak" resolution algorithm that catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml's own header comment says was explicitly REJECTED in favor of Hal's final ruling (writers send collection, engine never infers). The test file was written against the rejected rev-2 design and never reconciled with the shipped rev-3 (caller-supplied-only) design.

Fix: rewrite every repo.writeManifest/appendManifestChunks/importChunksBatch call in this file to pass the required collection argument, and replace the 12 stale-design tests' assertions with the actual shipped contract (uniform per-call collection stamp, no per-row resolution left at this layer).

Sibling defect: StagingPromoteOpsIntegrationTest.java's new Order(27)/Order(28) tests (finalizeTenant_manifestInsert_ghostDoc_resolvesFromVerifiedChashMembership / ...ambiguousChashMembership_staysUnresolved) test the SAME rejected chash-membership-verification design against StagingPromoteOps.java, which actually resolves collection SOLELY from the per-document CATALOG_DOCUMENTS.PHYSICAL_COLLECTION field (docPhysicalCollection, StagingPromoteOps.java:704-729) with no chash-membership check at all. Test #27 sets physical_collection='' for its ghost-doc fixture and expects a row to land verified by chash membership; under the shipped code docPhysicalCollection.isNotNull() is false for that doc so manifestPromotable is false and no row is ever written — the test's count()==1 assertion should read 0 (runtime failure, not a compile error, currently masked by the compile break above).
close_reason: Fixed and verified: test evidence reconciled to shipped caller-supplied-collection contract, 3 review rounds, suites green (Java 2004/0/0, Python 12613/0), landed in 498c9295. Dependency direction was inverted at filing (j862l blocks o8dil.7, not vice versa); o8dil.7 remains in_progress on its own merits.

title: physicalCollectionOf's ghost C-membership resolves per-CALL (pooled), not per-ROW like catalog-025 — reproduces nexus-c30ew on multi-chash batches
design:
## The defect

CatalogRepository.physicalCollectionOf's new ghost-resolution branch
(java:3632-3684, added by nexus-o8dil.7 to fix the LIMIT-1 unverified-stamp
Critical) computes `C` = the union of distinct collections in
chunks_384/768/1024 that contain ANY chash across the WHOLE `rows` list
passed to the call (java:3644-3667). Its own javadoc says so verbatim:
"C = the distinct collections ... that actually contain ANY chash in this
call's rows" (java:3551-3553). When |C|==1, that ONE value is stamped onto
EVERY row in the call via the per-row insert loop (writeManifestRows
:4208-4210, appendManifestChunks :5156-5158, importChunksBatch :7633-7641)
— including rows whose OWN chash never matched anything in any chunks_<dim>
table.

Concretely: a ghost-doc batch write with chashes {A, B} where A genuinely
lives in collection X and B exists nowhere (dangling/orphaned/not-yet-
embedded) yields cSet={X} (B contributes nothing to the union), and B's row
is stamped X anyway — completely unverified. This reproduces nexus-c30ew's
exact failure mode (m.collection = c.collection FALSE, NOT EXISTS TRUE, GC
quarantines a still-referenced chunk) on a row this SAME repair creates.

Reachable single-threaded, no concurrency required — just a multi-row
batch write to a ghost document where not every chash independently
verifies. Affects 3 of the 4 call sites the repair touched:
  - writeManifestRows (REPLACE — a doc's WHOLE manifest, easily >1 chunk)
  - appendManifestChunks (arbitrary-size append batch)
  - importChunksBatch (bulk ETL import, RDR-176 P3, explicitly multi-row)
Only doImportChunk (single-row call, N=1) is safe by construction.

## Why this is NOT what catalog-025 does

catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml's `row_membership` CTE computes C
SEPARATELY per (tenant_id, doc_id, position, chash) — genuinely per
manifest ROW (migration lines 125-136). StagingPromoteOps.
existingManifestCollection (StagingPromoteOps.java:775-798) correctly
mirrors this: its chashMembershipCount/chashSoleCollection/
chashSiblingAgreedCollection are correlated subqueries scoped to THIS
row's own `resolvedChash`. The "mirrors catalog-025 verbatim" claim in
CatalogRepository's javadoc is therefore true for the SQL twin
(StagingPromoteOps) and FALSE for the Java twin (CatalogRepository) —
the Java version pools the call's chashes into one shared decision instead
of evaluating per row.

## Zero test coverage of this shape

Every ManifestCollectionStampTest fixture (all 12 tests read in full)
passes a single-row, single-chash `rows` list to the ghost-resolution
path. The multi-chash, heterogeneous-membership case was never exercised,
which is why this went undetected through 5 review rounds.

## Fix shape

Evaluate C per-row: correlate the membership query to each row's own
chash (mirroring the migration's per-row CTE / StagingPromoteOps' own
correlated-subquery idiom) rather than pooling the call's chashes into one
shared cSet used for every row.

## Distinct from nexus-hiynr

nexus-hiynr is a TOCTOU (needs concurrent writers on the same doc). This
is deterministic and needs nothing but an ordinary multi-chunk ghost-doc
write — narrower trigger conditions than hiynr, arguably higher priority.

## Origin

Found by substantive-critic during the nexus-o8dil.7 GATE-2 follow-up
review (T2 nexus/critique-nexus-o8dil7-verified-stamp-followup-2026-08-12),
pressure-testing whether the review's own prior Critical (T2 22322,
unverified LIMIT-1 stamp) was closed or relocated by the fix. It was
relocated, not closed, for the multi-row-batch case.
close_reason: ARTIFACT of the rejected collection-INFERENCE design. title: nexus-71gw2's SKIP-when-coll-null guard swallows real constraint violations: physicalCollectionOf returns null for BOTH ghost-document and document-does-not-exist, so a write against a nonexistent doc_id is silently reported as SUCCESS instead of landing in failed_doc_ids
description:
nexus-71gw2's SKIP-when-coll-null guard swallows real constraint violations: `physicalCollectionOf` returns null for BOTH "ghost document" and "document does not exist", so a write against a nonexistent doc_id is now silently reported as SUCCESS instead of landing in failed_doc_ids

## The defect

`insertManifestChunkRows` (CatalogRepository.java ~:3867) returns early when
`coll == null`, BEFORE the INSERT reaches Postgres. But `coll` comes from
`physicalCollectionOf(docId)`, which returns null for TWO CATEGORICALLY DIFFERENT
conditions and the guard cannot tell them apart:

  (a) the document EXISTS and is a ghost — no `physical_collection`. Skipping is
      arguably right: there is no collection to write.
  (b) the document DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL. Skipping is WRONG. Pre-change the INSERT
      ran, violated the fk-001 FK on (tenant_id, doc_id), threw, and the caller
      recorded the doc in `failed_doc_ids`. Now the guard returns first, nothing
      throws, and the write is REPORTED AS SUCCESS.

Same for any row that would have violated a real NOT NULL or FK constraint: the
violation never fires because the statement never runs.

So `writeManifestMany`'s per-document failure reporting is broken for this class. A
caller asking to write a manifest for a document that is not there gets silence.

## Confirmed by two independent existing tests

  CatalogEngineDefects70Test.a3kbf_writeManifestManyContainsPerDocFailure
  CatalogRepositoryTest.writeManifestMany_violatingRow_isolatedToFailedDocIds

Both currently FAIL against the uncommitted nexus-71gw2 tree. ⛔ THEIR ASSERTIONS ARE
CORRECT AND THE PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG. Do NOT "fix" them by giving their
fixtures a `physical_collection` — that masks this defect. They are the regression
tests for it, and they should return to green by fixing production, unmodified.

## The required contract — THREE cases, not one

The guard collapses three distinct situations into a single silent return. The fix is
to distinguish them, not to tune the guard:

  1. DOCUMENT DOES NOT EXIST -> must FAIL, exactly as before. Either let the INSERT
     run so the FK fires, or throw explicitly. `failed_doc_ids` must repopulate.
  2. GHOST DOCUMENT WITH EXISTING COLLECTION-STAMPED MANIFEST ROWS -> resolve the
     collection FROM THOSE ROWS and write normally. This is also the fix for the
     related upsert-drop finding (legitimate chash / chunk_index / line / char
     refreshes were being discarded for these documents).
  3. GHOST DOCUMENT WITH NO EXISTING ROWS -> the ONLY genuine "nothing to write"
     case. An empty manifest is the truthful state. Log at WARN, never `debug`.

## Why a redesign and not a fourth patch

This is the THIRD defect traced to this one guard, each found by a different
reviewer from a different angle:
  - the manifest wipe + `chunk_count` desync (`nexus-9kj5j`),
  - the dropped upsert refreshes for already-stamped positions,
  - this one, the swallowed constraint violations.
Three findings on one guard is the root-cause signal, not an invitation to add a
fourth condition to it. Fix the contract once.

Note the file's own convention, stated ~20 lines below the guard in
`writeManifestRows`: "FAIL LOUD (not the stampIndexedAt silent-noop shape): this is
a data-bearing manifest writer ... a silent 0-row update here would misreport success
to the caller". The guard violates the rule its own file states.

## Also check StagingPromoteOps

Its guard is a different shape — `docPhysicalCollection.isNotNull()` gating an
INSERT...SELECT rather than an early return — so it may or may not carry the same
overload. Determine whether "document absent" is distinguishable there, and apply the
same three-case contract if it is not. Do not assume it is safe because it looks
different.

## Origin

Found by the `nexus-7nrvr` fixture agent while reading the failing test bodies, after
it was stopped from patching those fixtures. Its full per-file mechanism tracing
(plain-SKIP vs this defect vs premise-impossible) is in T2
`nexus/nexus-7nrvr-fixture-breakage-analysis-and-skip-guard-defects-2026-08-12`.
Blocks `nexus-71gw2`.
notes:
## ⛔ 2026-08-12 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERION CORRECTED. The DESCRIPTION above over-generalises.

Recorded here because a plan critique caught that this bead was the ONLY one in the arc
carrying a reversal in its description with nothing in NOTES — every sibling records its
corrections. That is a bookkeeping failure of mine, not of anyone who worked the bead.

WHAT THE DESCRIPTION SAYS, and where it is wrong: it names BOTH
`a3kbf_writeManifestManyContainsPerDocFailure` and
`writeManifestMany_violatingRow_isolatedToFailedDocIds` as tests that must go green
UNMODIFIED, and forbids giving either fixture a `physical_collection`. That is correct
for the first and WRONG for the second.

  - `a3kbf` — its failure WAS the swallowed violation. Production was wrong, the test was
    right, fixing production fixed the test. It IS green unmodified, verified
    byte-for-byte. The instruction holds.
  - `writeManifestMany_violatingRow_isolatedToFailedDocIds` — its subject is CROSS-DOC
    FAILURE ISOLATION. Its documents' ghost-ness is INCIDENTAL to that subject, so under
    the corrected contract its healthy doc legitimately writes nothing and the test can
    no longer demonstrate isolation. That is category (1) in `nexus-7nrvr`'s taxonomy —
    incidental ghost-ness — and giving the fixtures a real `physical_collection` REPAIRS
    the test rather than masking anything. The defect it detects (violations isolating
    to `failed_doc_ids`) is preserved and still asserted.

CORRECTED CRITERION: `a3kbf` green unmodified; `violatingRow` is a category-(1) fixture
repair whose isolation assertion must survive intact.

AS IMPLEMENTED, and it corrected my reasoning a second time: I had said "if `wmm.bad` is
NONEXISTENT leave it alone; if it is an EXISTING ghost it needs a collection too." It is
the second — registered via `upsertDocument`, therefore case 3 (ghost, no existing rows),
not case 1. Both `wmm.good` and `wmm.bad` now carry
`knowledge__wmm-isolation__voyage-context-3__v1`, which is what lets `wmm.bad`'s INSERT
actually RUN so its intended chash NOT NULL violation fires.
NON-VACUITY EVIDENCE, at runtime:
  failed=1 of=2 sample=[{doc_id=wmm.bad, reason=not-null violation, sqlstate=23502}]
i.e. a genuine violation, not a case-3 skip producing a vacuous green — which was the
exact way this repair could have gone wrong. Isolation assertions unweakened: docs==1,
failed_doc_ids==[wmm.bad], good doc manifest 1 / chunk_count 1, bad doc manifest empty /
chunk_count 0. A fixture comment now names this bead and the reasoning so nobody
re-vacuates it.

Both reviewers independently ruled the repair correct and not an over-correction.

## WHY THE OVER-GENERALISATION HAPPENED, so it is not repeated

I wrote the blanket instruction from an analysis that listed the two tests TOGETHER as
confirming the swallowed-violation defect. They confirmed different things: one was the
defect, one merely touched it. "These tests confirm X" is not the same claim as "these
tests exist to test X", and a fixture whose failure is incidental to the defect needs a
different remedy from one whose failure IS the defect. Check the SUBJECT of a test before
declaring its fixture untouchable.

title: RDR-191 71gw2: writeManifestRows folds chunk_count=rows.size() even when insertManifestChunkRows SKIPs all rows (coll==null), desyncing chunk_count from an empty manifest
design:
CatalogRepository.java:4031 (writeManifestRows, the PLAIN/REPLACE path behind
writeManifest/writeManifestMany) sets documents.chunk_count = rows.size() --
the CALLER'S intended row count -- not a re-derived COUNT(*) of what actually
landed. Since catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml (nexus-71gw2) made
insertManifestChunkRows SKIP every row when coll==null
(CatalogRepository.java:3867-3868), a ghost document (no physical_collection)
written via writeManifest with real chunk rows gets: manifest stays EMPTY
(all rows skipped), but chunk_count is stamped to rows.size() (stale,
nonzero) anyway. This is a NEW divergence -- pre-71gw2, insertManifestChunkRows
never skipped, so rows.size() == actual inserted row count always held.

Consequence: completeIndexRun's referenced()!=chunkCount 409 refusal
(CatalogRepository.java ~5068-5085) will misfire on any later completion
attempt for that document -- a silent data-correctness bug on the primary
`nx index` write path, not merely a test-fixture convention issue.

Contrast (both correct, for reference): appendManifestChunks
(CatalogRepository.java:4954) re-derives via manifestRowCount() COUNT(*).
StagingPromoteOps's chunk_count_resynced step (StagingPromoteOps.java:768-772)
re-derives via grouped COUNT(*) over actually-promoted rows.

PROOF: CatalogRepositoryTest.java:1222-1243
(manifest_write_foldsChunkCountLikeWriteManifestMany, UNMODIFIED by the
71gw2 diff) registers a doc with no physical_collection, writes 3 rows,
asserts chunk_count==3, but never asserts getManifest() is non-empty. Ran
live (mvn test -Dnexus.test.forks=1 -Dtest=CatalogRepositoryTest#manifest_write_foldsChunkCountLikeWriteManifestMany):
PASSES (vacuously) -- it passes because chunk_count is set from rows.size()
regardless of the skip, while the manifest is actually empty underneath.

FIX: writeManifestRows must fold chunk_count from an actual post-insert
COUNT(*) (or a summed count of only the rows that were NOT skipped), the
same discipline appendManifestChunks and StagingPromoteOps already apply,
rather than trusting the input list size.

plan-rdr191-p0-burndown-2026-08-12.md. Full detail: T2

The chunk_count desync was caused by insertManifestChunkRows SKIPping rows when the inferred collection was null; there is no SKIP branch any more because there is nothing to infer. title: nexus-71gw2's sentinel does not protect case-3 (multi-collection chash) rows from nexus-c30ew's GC chain; also strips RDR-191's MATCH-SIMPLE NULL exemption, creating guaranteed FK-VALIDATE failures
description:
Found during substantive-critic review of scratchpad plan-rdr191-p0-burndown-2026-08-12.md, BEFORE dispatch.

## Finding 1: case-3 sentinel rows remain live victims of nexus-c30ew's exact chain

nexus-71gw2's design text claims: "Sentinel rows (cases 2 and 3: chash in zero
collections, or ambiguously in two or more) have NO CHUNK to destroy, so the
data-loss chain documented above has no fuel."

True for case 2 (zero collections contain the chash — nothing to destroy).
FALSE for case 3: the chash EXISTS, in >=2 collections, by definition of the
case. Once the manifest row's collection is stamped '__orphan__', every GC
function's `m.collection = c.collection` join fails to match EITHER real
collection value — a definite FALSE (sentinel != real string), not a NULL/
unknown. The net effect on chunk protection is IDENTICAL to today's
NULL-comparison bug: the anti-join in gc_quarantine_orphans still returns
NOT EXISTS = TRUE for both of the case-3 chunk's collection-scoped copies,
so both remain unprotected and vulnerable to quarantine-then-expire, exactly
as nexus-c30ew describes, just via string-inequality instead of three-valued
NULL logic.

This is NOT one-time migration residue. physicalCollectionOf(...) returns
null for any ghost document, permanently (there is no physical_collection to
ever backfill from). So insertManifestChunkRows' sentinel substitution
(finding #1 from the reverted attempt) means EVERY FUTURE ghost-document
manifest write is permanently sentinel-stamped. Any such write whose chash
happens to be shared with a live collection (RDR-108's shared-chunk-across-
collections is designed-in, not rare) reproduces c30ew's chain going forward,
not just for pre-existing rows.

## Finding 2: sentinel rows lose RDR-191's own MATCH SIMPLE NULL-exemption

RDR-191 C1/F6 (docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md):
"Under PostgreSQL's default MATCH SIMPLE, a row with a NULL in ANY column of
the foreign key is exempt from enforcement entirely... those rows remain
unenforced. The FK gives them no guarantee — it neither fixes nor worsens
them." Decision item 4 explicitly keeps `_check_manifest_null_collection`
alive BECAUSE this permanently-unenforced population needs visibility.

71gw2 eliminates the NULL that made this exemption apply. Once `collection`
is NOT NULL for every row (real value or sentinel), NO row is ever exempt
from the eventual manifest FK under MATCH SIMPLE. Every sentinel row (case 2
AND case 3) becomes a GUARANTEED VALIDATE CONSTRAINT failure at RDR-191
Phase 5 (nexus-o8dil.37), because '__orphan__' will never match a real row
in the unified nexus.chunks table. Neither 71gw2's bead text, the RDR's own
Decision item 6, nor the plan under review states this consequence.
nexus-xehfx's reclaim population (6,501 dangling rows, measured 2026-08-11)
does not currently account for the sentinel population 71gw2 will create —
it needs to, or Phase 5 inherits a NEW class of guaranteed VALIDATE failure
that this fix itself introduces.

## Ask

1. Correct 71gw2's design text: case-3 sentinel rows are NOT safe against
   c30ew's chain. State this plainly rather than "no chunk to destroy."
2. Decide what actually protects a case-3 (or any future ghost) sentinel
   row's shared chunk from GC — options include: gate the GC functions to
   also protect any chunk referenced by ANY manifest row for the same chash
   regardless of collection (reopens the "teach GC three-valued/multi-valued
   logic" door Hal explicitly closed, but the sentinel does not close it,
   it relocates it), or exclude sentinel-collection rows from every
   collection's live population entirely (converts them to intentional
   orphans, consistent with their being unresolved data, but then their
   chunks SHOULD be reclaimed rather than left live and vulnerable).
3. Wire the sentinel-row population into nexus-xehfx's or nexus-o8dil.37's
   Phase 5 reclaim accounting before VALIDATE CONSTRAINT runs, or explicitly
   decide sentinel rows ship FK NOT VALID / never VALIDATE (RDR-191 open
   question 9's candidate disposition (c), extended to this new population).

## Constraints
- Do NOT teach the GC functions three-valued (or now multi-valued) logic
  unilaterally — Hal ruled the other way for the NULL case; the same
  question needs the same explicit ruling for the sentinel case.
- All DDL through Liquibase.

## Origin
Substantive-critic review of plan-rdr191-p0-burndown-2026-08-12.md, dispatched
before any implementation. Full critique in T2 nexus/critique-plan-rdr191-p0-burndown-2026-08-12.
notes:
## 2026-08-12 — CLOSING: both findings are CORRECT, and they killed the design they critique

This bead is closed not because it is wrong but because it WON. Hal ruled the
sentinel dead on 2026-08-12, hours after this was filed, on exactly these two
grounds plus an independent census that reached the same two conclusions from the
other direction (finding D-2 = this bead's finding 1; finding D-1 = finding 2).

Ruling, verbatim: "An unresolvable manifest row is invalid. Delete it. NOT NULL
with no sentinel, no DEFAULT."

There is no `__orphan__` sentinel to defend against. Under the delete design every
surviving manifest row carries a REAL collection recovered either from a
single-collection chash match or from the document's sibling manifest rows; rows
that cannot be resolved to any chunk are DELETED. So:

  - finding 1 has no subject: no sentinel-stamped row exists to be a case-3
    victim, and every surviving row's `m.collection = c.collection` join matches
    when the reference is genuine;
  - finding 2 has no subject: no non-NULL row without a matching chunk survives,
    so nothing moves from MATCH-SIMPLE-exempt to guaranteed-FK-violating. The FK
    population is unchanged by this work, which is what `nexus-xehfx` needs.

Recorded in `nexus-71gw2` notes, `nexus-c30ew` notes, and §6 of
scratchpad/plan-rdr191-p0-burndown-2026-08-12.md so the reversal cannot be
re-litigated from memory.

### ONE THING FROM FINDING 1 SURVIVES, and it is carried forward, not dropped

This bead established that the ghost path is PERMANENT, not migration residue:
`physicalCollectionOf(...)` returns null for a ghost document forever, since there
is no `physical_collection` to ever backfill from. Under the sentinel that meant
every future ghost write was permanently sentinel-stamped. Under the delete design
it means something still load-bearing: a one-time sweep is NOT sufficient, because
the insert sites would keep trying to write unresolvable rows after the column is
NOT NULL — and would then THROW rather than silently write.

So the insert sites must be made incapable of producing such a row at all, and
that is a permanent behavioural decision (refuse the insert, or skip the row),
not a migration step. Carried into `nexus-71gw2`'s mandatory-edit list for both
sites: `CatalogRepository.insertManifestChunkRows` and
`StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant` (the latter independently filed as
`nexus-lyhac`, which stays OPEN and folds into the same changeset).

Closed as superseded-by-ruling. Findings preserved above rather than deleted.
close_reason: Superseded by Hal's 2026-08-12 ruling: the sentinel design both findings attack was killed on these exact grounds. Findings preserved in notes; the permanent-ghost-path consequence carried into nexus-71gw2's mandatory-edit list.

title: RDR-191: manifest writers SEND the collection; engine stamps it verbatim; unresolvable rows are DELETED and the column goes NOT NULL (no sentinel, no backfill)
description:
Hal's directive, 2026-08-12: stop writing NULL-tolerant logic in every consumer. Eliminate the NULL. Backfill `catalog_document_chunks.collection` where the answer is knowable, stamp a sentinel where it is not, then make the column NOT NULL with that sentinel as DEFAULT.

## Why this and not the per-consumer fixes

`collection` is nullable, and NULL forces every consumer to implement SQL three-valued logic correctly. They do not. `nexus-c30ew` (P0, unrecoverable data loss) is exactly this: `m.collection = c.collection` yields NULL, never TRUE, so a NULL-collection manifest row silently fails to protect its chunk in `gc_quarantine_orphans` AND in `gc_restore_rereferenced`'s rescue predicate. The GATE-2 tripwire built to detect it was itself written vacuously for the same reason. That is four independent instruments getting the same NULL wrong.

Making the state unrepresentable kills the class. Fixing each consumer leaves the next one to rediscover it.

## The three-way backfill (NOT two-way)

For each row with `collection IS NULL`, look for its chash in `chunks_384/768/1024` scoped to the row's `tenant_id`:

1. **exactly ONE collection contains it** -> BACKFILL that collection. Knowable.
2. **ZERO collections contain it** -> SENTINEL. There is no chunk; the row is genuinely dangling and stamping a sentinel makes that visible rather than hiding it behind a NULL.
3. **TWO OR MORE collections contain it** -> SENTINEL, deliberately.

⛔ Case 3 is the load-bearing one and must NOT be guessed. A chash is content-addressed, so identical text legitimately lives in `code__*` AND `docs__*` (RDR-108 shared-chunk collapse is per-collection). The normal tiebreak would be the owning document's `physical_collection` -- but a NULL row exists PRECISELY BECAUSE its document is a ghost with no `physical_collection` (health.py:4092-4104: for ghosts it "stays NULL FOREVER"). The disambiguator is the missing field. Circular.

Writing a guess into a column we are about to make authoritative converts an honest unknown into a silent wrong answer, and the FK will then enforce the wrong answer. Sentinel is correct here.

## Why the sentinel makes the NOT NULL promotion SAFE

This is the part that matters for sequencing, and it is a genuine improvement over RDR-191 Phase 7's existing plan.

`nexus-o8dil.37` promotes this column to NOT NULL via Liquibase, which runs UNCONDITIONALLY AT ENGINE BOOT. Plan-audit pass 2 finding HIGH-2 already flagged that a deployment with un-remediated NULL residue fails the ALTER at boot -> MigrationException -> exit 1: the third boot-brick of a family RDR-191 has now caught three times (F14b, `.23`'s VALIDATE, and this).

Phase 7's original shape needed a MANUAL, per-deployment remediation (`nexus-o8dil.36`) to complete BEFORE the promotion, which is exactly the incompatibility that bricks a late upgrader.

A sentinel removes that dependency: the backfill is EXHAUSTIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, because every row that is not knowable gets the sentinel. Backfill and promotion can therefore live in ONE changeset, in order, with no manual step and no operator sequencing:

    1. UPDATE ... SET collection = <resolved>   -- case 1
    2. UPDATE ... SET collection = <sentinel>   -- cases 2 and 3, catches everything remaining
    3. ALTER ... ALTER COLUMN collection SET DEFAULT <sentinel>
    4. ALTER ... ALTER COLUMN collection SET NOT NULL

Step 2 guarantees step 4 cannot fail. That dissolves the boot-brick rather than sequencing around it.

## Sentinel value

Needs to be a name no real collection can collide with, and it must survive the conformant-collection-name shape (`<content_type>__<owner>__<model>__v<n>`, RDR-103). Proposal: a reserved name that is deliberately NOT conformant so nothing routes to it, e.g. `__orphan__`. Decide explicitly and check it against the collection-name validators and `split_part(collection,'__',3)` model-token routing (`catalog-004-manifest-functions.xml`), which WILL be handed this value and must not crash or mis-route on it.

⛔ Verify before shipping: `manifest_orphans` routes by `split_part(collection,'__',3)`. A sentinel with the wrong underscore count changes what that returns. This is the `nexus-h1zu0` divergence surface; the sentinel must land in `unroutable_collections` deliberately, not silently route to a dim.

## What this DOES resolve

- `nexus-c30ew` (P0) in full: no NULL, no NULL-comparison, all three GC functions' joins behave. Case-2/3 sentinel rows have no chunk to destroy, so the data-loss chain has no fuel.
- The NULL-collection arm of GATE-2's criterion (`nexus-o8dil.7` item 2) becomes structurally unrepresentable rather than merely untested.
- `nexus-o8dil.36` (remediate the NULL population) collapses into this changeset.
- `nexus-o8dil.37`'s boot-brick risk (plan-audit HIGH-2).
- F12b/F12c's damage MODE: an omitted `collection` on insert now takes the DEFAULT instead of NULL, and an explicit NULL now FAILS LOUD instead of silently demoting.
- The tripwire's NULL-arm assertions become trivially checkable (`SELECT count(*) WHERE collection IS NULL` must be 0, permanently).

## What this DOES NOT resolve -- stated plainly so nobody reads this as closing GATE-2

- The DANGLING arm. Five live producers remain, of which c30ew was only one. `contentCollapseDelete`, RekeyOps' chash-only enforcement, and the sweepChunks cross-transaction windows are untouched.
- `nexus-mmkqe` and `nexus-5da44`: both are `deleted_at`/tombstone-axis defects. Completely unaffected.
- `nexus-ajlz5`: the engine-pin inversion. Unrelated.
- `nexus-k1uw5`: PARTIALLY. It records TWO definitional axes. This closes the NULL axis; the TOMBSTONED-PARENT axis remains fully open and is the one that collides with the FK.
- The case-3 rows remain genuinely unresolved data. They are now HONESTLY labelled rather than silently NULL, which is the point, but somebody still has to decide what happens to them (reclaim, re-index, or accept as permanent orphans).

## Constraints

- ALL DDL through Liquibase. Never Python. The backfill UPDATEs go in the same changeset as the ALTERs.
- Must carry a rollback block (this table family's changesets do).
- TDD: a test seeding all THREE cases (one-match, zero-match, multi-match) and asserting each lands correctly, PLUS a test that the promotion succeeds on a corpus that started with NULLs -- i.e. prove the boot-brick is actually dissolved, do not assert it.
- Non-vacuity: the multi-match case must be seeded deliberately (same chunk_text in two collections). It is the case most likely to be absent from a synthetic fixture and it is the one the design turns on.
- Re-count the live NULL population immediately before the window. It measured 0 on 2026-08-11, which is consistent with boot-time `manifest_backfill` (catalog-014:59) already reducing it, so the backfill may be a no-op on the live corpus and the value here is structural: making the state unrepresentable going forward.

## Sequencing against RDR-191

Sits naturally in Phase 7 alongside `.36`/`.37`, but is NOT gated behind the unification: it touches only `catalog_document_chunks.collection` and needs nothing from `nexus.chunks`. Given it dissolves a live P0 data-loss bug, it should be pulled EARLIER than Phase 7 and shipped with the next engine cut (`nexus-ajlz5`).

## Origin

Hal directive, 2026-08-12, in response to the c30ew analysis: "this is all trying to compensate for a null? make a default, orphan collection. anything without a collection gets that. why make this difficult." Three-way split (rather than the two-way he described) is this bead's addition, for the multi-match ambiguity; flagged to and approved by him in the same exchange.
notes:
## 2026-08-12 — IMPLEMENTATION ATTEMPT REVERTED (Hal directive). Design STANDS.

An implementation run was stopped and fully reverted. The DESIGN in this bead is
unchanged and was not the problem; the execution was.

WHY REVERTED: the dispatch was briefed as ONE Liquibase changeset and reached 18
files / 1192 insertions, touching 3 production Java files (CatalogRepository,
StagingPromoteOps, CatalogHandler) and 3 production Python files (health.py,
http_catalog_client.py, reconcile.py). Some was justified (a mid-flight relay
correctly asked it to fix the doctor check the sentinel would blind); most was
unjustified and unreviewed. Hal called the session's overall pattern thrashing,
correctly.

WORK PRESERVED, NOT DESTROYED:
  patch:     scratchpad/71gw2-snapshot/71gw2-tracked-changes.patch (2453 lines)
  untracked: scratchpad/71gw2-snapshot/untracked/
             service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml
             service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/Rdr71gw2CollectionNotNullBackfillTest.java
NOTE: the scratchpad is SESSION-SCOPED and will not survive indefinitely. If any
of it is wanted, harvest it early.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THE ATTEMPT WORTH KEEPING — both are real and should survive
into the next plan:

1. ⛔ A DB-LEVEL DEFAULT IS NOT SUFFICIENT. A column DEFAULT fires only when the
   column is OMITTED from an INSERT's column list. `insertManifestChunkRows`
   ALWAYS supplies `collection` explicitly, so a ghost document
   (`physicalCollectionOf` -> null) would send a literal SQL NULL into a NOT
   NULL column and THROW at runtime. The sentinel must ALSO be substituted in
   Java at the insert site. Without that, this change converts 'writes a NULL
   row' into 'hard failure on the ghost path'. This is the single most important
   thing the attempt established.

2. ⛔ THE SENTINEL BREAKS F12c's UPSERT PRECEDENCE UNLESS GUARDED. The existing
   arm is `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.collection, existing)`, meaning an incoming NULL
   yields to an existing good value. Once 'no collection' arrives as the
   sentinel rather than NULL, plain COALESCE sees a REAL value and overwrites a
   correctly-stamped row with the sentinel. Needs
   `COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.collection, <sentinel>), existing)`. Without it,
   this fix silently demotes good stamps on every append and import — the
   sentinel introducing the very defect class it exists to remove.

NOT NULL with no sentinel, no DEFAULT."

case-2/case-3 sentinel arms and the `__orphan__` value analysis in note 3. The

case 1 survives.

   `'__orphan__' = 'x'` are behaviourally IDENTICAL inside `EXISTS` /

`nexus/rdr-191-71gw2-collection-null-consumer-census-2026-08-12`.

### The design of record now

Resolution order, recovery BEFORE deletion:

1. chash resolves in EXACTLY ONE collection (scoped to the row's tenant_id)
   -> BACKFILL that collection. Unchanged from the original design.
2. chash AMBIGUOUS across 2+ collections -> disambiguate by the SIBLING manifest
   rows of the same doc_id. A document's chunks all live in one collection, so
   any sibling row for that doc_id carrying a non-NULL collection IS the
   disambiguator. NEW, and it is not circular: this bead's description looked
   only at the PARENT's `physical_collection`, hit the ghost circularity
   (health.py:4092-4104, "stays NULL FOREVER"), and concluded unknowable. The
   siblings are a second, independent source. Expected to collapse most of both
   the ambiguous and zero-match populations.
3. Whatever remains unresolvable -> DELETE THE ROW. The manifest is DERIVED
   data: it records composition, it is not the source of truth. A row that
   points at no resolvable chunk loses nothing when removed, and a re-index
   regenerates a real one. Deleting the false pointer then lets the chunk's fate
   be decided by whether any REAL reference exists — which is what the GC is
   for, correctly, rather than by a broken row's accidental protection.

step 3 removes every row step 1 and 2 could not resolve, so the ALTER cannot
fail. The boot-brick is dissolved for real this time, and no row survives that
the FK will later reject.

data whose collection is unknown; it is a row asserting a chunk membership that
cannot be resolved to anything retrievable. It is residue from defects — F12b
(StagingPromoteOps omitted the column), F12c (upsert demotion), both already
fixed on develop — plus ghost documents that have no chunks to compose. Keeping
it and renaming it warps the schema around the residue and, per finding 2 above,
warps it in the direction of a guaranteed FK failure. Deleting it removes the
residue and lets the schema say something true.

empty population is free now and free forever after.

title: [bug] gc_quarantine_orphans' manifest anti-join matches on collection, so a NULL-collection manifest row never protects its chunk: the GC CONVERTS null-collection rows into dangling rows, on every nx index
description:
`nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans` anti-joins the manifest on the FULL triple including `collection`. A manifest row with `collection IS NULL` can never satisfy that join, so its chunk reads as an orphan, is quarantined and DELETED, and the manifest row becomes DANGLING. This is a live producer of dangling manifest rows, it is NOT among the five RDR-191 Phase 2 fixes, and it is NOT fixed by the pending engine cut (nexus-ajlz5).

## The defect, verified directly

`service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-024-quarantine-collection-registration.xml:119-128` (live body, dim=384 arm; the 768 and 1024 arms are identical):

    SELECT array_agg(c.chash) INTO v_chashes
      FROM nexus.chunks_384 c
     WHERE c.tenant_id  = p_tenant_id
       AND c.collection = p_collection
       AND NOT EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks m
              WHERE m.tenant_id  = c.tenant_id
                AND m.collection = c.collection      <-- THE BUG
                AND m.chash      = c.chash
           );

When `m.collection IS NULL`, `m.collection = c.collection` evaluates to NULL, never TRUE. `NOT EXISTS` is therefore TRUE and the chunk is selected as an orphan. `v_chashes` then drives an INSERT into the quarantine collection followed by `DELETE FROM nexus.chunks_384 ... WHERE c.chash = ANY(v_chashes)` (:160-164).

Net effect: a NULL-COLLECTION manifest row is CONVERTED INTO A DANGLING manifest row. One defect class is laundered into the other.

## The asymmetry that proves it is unintended

`nexus.purge_trash` joins the manifest COLLECTION-BLIND — `service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-003-soft-delete.xml:226-229`:

    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks m
             WHERE m.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
               AND m.chash     = c.chash ...)

so there a NULL-collection manifest row STILL GATES and still protects its chunk. Two functions in the same schema, both deciding "is this chunk still referenced", disagree on whether a NULL-collection manifest row counts as a reference. `purge_trash` says yes, `gc_quarantine_orphans` says no. Both cannot be right.

## Reachability: the ORDINARY `nx index` path, automatic, no flag

Verified:
  src/nexus/indexer.py:5151   _prune_deleted_files(...)   <- runs on every index; the
                              full-walk path always reaches it (:5141-5155)
  src/nexus/indexer.py:3195   -> _prune_collection_serverside(...)
  src/nexus/indexer.py:2999   -> quarantine_orphans_serverside(...)
  -> POST /v1/vectors/gc/quarantine-orphans (VectorHandler.java:803)
  -> PgVectorRepository.java:2266-2269

This is not an admin path and not opt-in. Every `nx index` run fires it.

## HYPOTHESIS, explicitly labelled, NOT established

This may explain a shape the 2026-08-11 live census left unexplained: the NULL-collection arm measured **0** while the dangling arm measured 6,501. A population that is continuously CONVERTED would read 0 at rest while feeding the other number. F12b (StagingPromoteOps' manifest insert omitting `collection`) is a live NULL-collection producer in the deployed engine, which would be the fuel.

⛔ Do NOT record this as the explanation. A competing benign explanation exists and must be eliminated first: `catalog-014-manifest-collection-stamp.xml:59` invokes `manifest_backfill` at EVERY engine boot, and `manifest_backfill` (catalog-004-manifest-functions.xml:179) strictly REDUCES the NULL population (its WHERE requires `d.physical_collection IS NOT NULL AND != ''`). Boot-time backfill alone could produce a 0 reading. Distinguishing them needs a measurement, not an argument.

## Ask

1. Decide the correct semantics: should a NULL-collection manifest row count as a reference that protects its chunk? `purge_trash` already answers yes. If that is right, the gc functions' anti-join must match on `(tenant_id, chash)` or handle NULL explicitly (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`), and the fix goes through Liquibase.
2. All six gc arms need it, not one: `gc_quarantine_orphans` and `gc_restore_rereferenced` live bodies in catalog-024 (DELETEs :161/:219/:277 and :544/:591/:638), plus `gc_expire_quarantine` in catalog-023 (:503/:532/:561), which per the census never reads the manifest at all and needs its own verdict.
3. This blocks GATE-2 (nexus-o8dil.7) independently of nexus-ajlz5. Even after engine-service-v0.1.72 deploys the five Phase 2 fixes, THIS producer remains live, so "zero live producers" is still false.
4. The regression tripwire being built for GATE-2 must cover this path, or it certifies a criterion it does not test.

## Constraints

- ALL DDL through Liquibase. Never DDL in Python.
- No silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems.
- Do NOT clean rows to make the census look better; under a live producer the population refills.

## Origin

Found assembling GATE-2's acceptance-item-1 producer census (nexus-o8dil.7), from a Liquibase-changelog enumeration. The scoping asymmetry was relayed; both join predicates and the `nx index` reachability chain were then verified directly at the cited lines.
notes:
## ESCALATION — this is UNRECOVERABLE DATA LOSS, not only row corruption

The original description stopped at 'the manifest row becomes dangling'. The full
three-function pipeline is worse: the CHUNK IS PERMANENTLY DESTROYED, and the two
mechanisms that exist to prevent exactly that both fail on the same NULL.

### The chain, each link verified at the cited line

1. gc_quarantine_orphans (catalog-024:119-128) — the NULL-collection manifest row
   is invisible to `m.collection = c.collection`, so the chunk is classified an
   orphan, copied to the quarantine collection, and DELETED from its origin
   (:160-164).

2. gc_restore_rereferenced (catalog-024, restore predicate ~:556-560) — the rescue
   path. VERIFIED: its EXISTS requires

       AND m.collection = p_origin_collection

   A NULL-collection manifest row can never satisfy that either. The chunk is
   referenced, but the function cannot see the reference, so it is NEVER restored.
   The safety net has the identical defect as the thing it is meant to catch.

3. gc_expire_quarantine (catalog-023:503/:532/:561) — hard-deletes from quarantine
   and, per the changelog census, NEVER READS THE MANIFEST AT ALL. No third chance.

=> A chunk whose only manifest reference has collection IS NULL is quarantined,
   cannot be restored, and is then hard-deleted. Permanently. On the ordinary
   `nx index` path, with no flag and no operator action.

### Why the safety net failing matters more than the first bug

Quarantine-then-expire exists precisely so that a misclassification is recoverable
during the window. Here the misclassification and the recovery check share the same
predicate, so the window provides no protection for this class: it is not that the
restore was not attempted, it is that the restore CANNOT succeed by construction.
Any fix must correct ALL THREE functions. Fixing only gc_quarantine_orphans leaves
already-quarantined chunks stranded and still doomed at expiry.

### Direction of the asymmetry, stated precisely

purge_trash's collection-blind join is OVER-protective: it can only decline to
sweep a chunk it should have swept. Harmless in this direction.
The gc_* full-triple join is UNDER-protective: it destroys a chunk that is still
referenced. The two errors are NOT symmetric, and the safe direction is the
collection-blind one.

### Consequence for remediation ordering

Anything that BACKFILLS collection (manifest_backfill, invoked at every engine boot
per catalog-014:59) reduces the exposed population, but it cannot resurrect chunks
already expired out of quarantine. Losses to date, if any, are not recoverable by
fixing this. Sizing what has already been lost needs a measurement against the
quarantine collections before the next expiry runs, and that measurement is
time-sensitive in a way the fix is not.

  chunks_1024  quarantine-rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1      1   2026-08-06 18:14
  chunks_384 / chunks_768: zero (both effectively empty tables)

Predicate used: `collection ILIKE 'quarantine%'` on all three dim tables, plus a
manual eyeball of chunks_1024's full 99-collection inventory. Not a predicate miss.
So the code path is live and exercised, not theoretical.

### But every one of the 1,429 was quarantined CORRECTLY

  A  no manifest row anywhere carries this chash                          1,427
  B  manifest row with collection == origin_collection                        0
  C  manifest row with collection IS NULL                                     0
  C  manifest row with collection <> origin_collection                        2  -> see below
                                                                         ------
                                                                          1,429

Bucket B is the fatal one (a chunk referenced in its OWN collection, quarantined
anyway) and it is ZERO. The two apparent bucket-C rows are NOT wrongly quarantined —
see the taxonomy correction below.

VERDICT: `nexus-c30ew` has NOT destroyed user data on this deployment. It is a real
defect that has not yet bitten, not a loss.

### ⛔ MY BUCKET-C TAXONOMY WAS WRONG, and the correction is worth more than the count

I defined bucket C as "a manifest row carries this chash under a DIFFERENT collection,
therefore the chunk was still referenced, therefore quarantining it was wrong."

That inference requires chunk storage to be collection-agnostic. IT IS NOT. Chunk rows
are stored PER COLLECTION — the same chash is independently materialised under every
collection that uses it (this is RDR-108's shared-chunk collapse being PER-COLLECTION,
a fact already recorded in AGENTS.md, which I had and did not apply). So each
cross-collection manifest reference is satisfied BY ITS OWN collection's chunk row, and
the quarantined copy is a different row that nothing points at.

Measured for the two chashes:
  245843ab…  chunk rows in code__1-15, code__1-16, code__1-33, code__1-6,
             quarantine-code__1-1
             manifest rows by collection: code__1-15 (18), code__1-6 (5),
             code__1-16 (1), code__1-33 (1) — **code__1-1: ZERO**
  956b5191…  chunk rows in code__1-30, quarantine-code__1-1
             manifest rows by collection: code__1-30 (2) — **code__1-1: ZERO**

Neither had a single manifest row referencing it in its OWN collection. Both were
genuinely unreferenced. Restoring them would re-create rows in a collection nothing
points at.

CORRECTED PREDICATE, for any future census: bucket C needs
`AND no chunk row exists at (tenant_id, m.collection, chash)`.
Without it, bucket C produces FALSE POSITIVES on any deployment with cross-collection
content duplication — which is NORMAL for a code corpus, where identical file content
appears across many indexed repos. conexus caught this before reporting and nearly
handed me "2 restore candidates" instead.

NOTE FOR nexus-71gw2: this does NOT change that design, it VALIDATES it. Its resolution
rule already defines `C = {collections whose chunks_<dim> contain this (tenant_id,
chash)}` and forbids stamping any collection outside `C` — i.e. it already treats
collection as part of chunk identity, which is exactly the property my bucket-C
inference violated. The `|C| >= 2` case IS the cross-collection duplication case.

### C-NULL = 0 is NOT exoneration, as predicted and as they accept

`manifest_backfill()` runs at every engine boot (catalog-014:57-61) and only ever
REDUCES the NULL-collection population. So "NULL now" cannot distinguish "never was
NULL" from "was NULL at quarantine time, since backfilled". Neither side can settle it.

### ⚠ WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN — and the mitigation nobody designed

The defect needs a NULL-collection manifest row as its precondition. That population
measures 0, and it measures 0 BECAUSE the boot-time `manifest_backfill()` keeps
draining it. So `manifest_backfill` is currently, accidentally, THE MITIGATION holding
this P0 harmless.
⛔ CONSEQUENCE: do NOT retire or disable `manifest_backfill` before `nexus-71gw2`
lands. The 71gw2 plan correctly calls it vestigial AFTER the column is NOT NULL, and
RDR-191 Phase 6 retires it — but in the window between now and then it is load-bearing.
Retiring it early re-arms this bug.

### Their hypothesis, formed and killed — recorded so nobody re-derives it

They hypothesised that c30ew is a PRODUCER of GATE-2's 37 dangling rows (quarantining a
chunk orphans the manifest rows referencing it). MEASURED FALSE: of the 37
FK-violating live-parent rows, ZERO have a chash among the quarantined set. The
populations are disjoint, for the same per-collection-storage reason as above.

### Expiry schedule and the disposition

  2026-08-06  1,274 rows  expires ~2026-08-20
  2026-08-07    151 rows  expires ~2026-08-21
  2026-08-10      4 rows  expires ~2026-08-24
All 1,429 carry well-formed `origin_collection` and `quarantined_at` (0 malformed), so
a deliberate copy-back remains possible if anyone ever wants one, and none is immortal
via the COALESCE-to-9999 path.

ON THE EVIDENCE, LETTING THEM EXPIRE IS CORRECT. They are genuine orphans. No restore
is indicated. Nothing was restored, expired, forced, or vacuumed to obtain this.

`NX_GC_QUARANTINE_DAYS`: confirmed UNSET on the engine container by them, and confirmed
UNSET in this checkout's shell environment here. They correctly flagged that the GC runs
on the `nx index` CLIENT path, so the client environment is what governs; the two checks
together cover the engine and this box, and no repo file sets it either.

### What does NOT change

The defect is real, reproduced by test through the production entry point, and live in
the deployed engine. All three GC functions still share the defective predicate, the
rescue path still cannot rescue, and a single future NULL-collection manifest row
whose chunk is referenced would execute the full unrecoverable chain. `nexus-71gw2`
remains the fix and remains P0. What changed is that we are fixing this BEFORE it
costs data rather than after — which is the good version of this outcome, not a reason
to slow down.
close_reason: ARTIFACT of the rejected collection-INFERENCE design. Hal ruling 2026-08-12 (T2 nexus/rdr-191-ruling-stop-guessing-the-collection-2026-08-12). The GC anti-join was never wrong: 'm.collection = c.collection' is correct once a manifest row's collection is a caller-supplied verified fact instead of an inferred nullable. With catalog-025 deleting every NULL-collection row and SET NOT NULL, no NULL row can exist and this path is unreachable. The six-arm anti-join rewrite (gc_quarantine_orphans / gc_restore_rereferenced / gc_expire_quarantine) is CANCELLED, not deferred — do not reopen it as debt.

title: [bug] v7.6.1 pinned engine v0.1.71 predates its own RDR-191 producer fixes: the F10c data-loss fix is INERT in the deployed cloud engine
description:
v7.6.1 SHIPPED the client halves of the RDR-191 Phase 2 producer fixes while pinning an engine tag that does NOT contain their engine halves. The F10c fix, for a bug the RDR calls "A LIVE SILENT DATA-LOSS BUG, TODAY", is INERT for every cloud-mode user on v7.6.1.

## Verified, by direct command (2026-08-11)

  $ git tag --contains 831a4e81      -> v7.6.1        (no engine tag)
  $ git tag --contains 936e05a0      -> v7.6.1        (no engine tag)
  $ git merge-base --is-ancestor 831a4e81 engine-service-v0.1.71  -> NOT contained
  $ git merge-base --is-ancestor 936e05a0 engine-service-v0.1.71  -> NOT contained
  $ git merge-base --is-ancestor 831a4e81 v7.6.1                  -> IN v7.6.1
  $ git merge-base --is-ancestor 936e05a0 v7.6.1                  -> IN v7.6.1

  engine-service-v0.1.71 = 8c2e9fa6, committed 2026-08-11T04:16:18-07:00
  936e05a0 (F10c)                     committed 2026-08-11T08:22:54-07:00   (+4h)
  831a4e81 (F14a/F8c/F12b/F12c/F8d)   committed 2026-08-11T12:38:57-07:00   (+8h)
  v7.6.1 tagged                                 2026-08-11T14:43:29-07:00

  $ git show v7.6.1:src/nexus/engine_version.py | grep REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION
  :351 REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION: tuple[int,int,int] = (0, 1, 71)

  $ git diff --stat 8c2e9fa6 v7.6.1 -- service/src/main/java/
    CatalogRepository.java    |  39 +++-
    StagingPromoteOps.java    |  23 ++-
    VectorHandler.java        |  17 +--
    PgVectorRepository.java   | 100 ++++++++--
    4 files changed, 156 insertions(+), 23 deletions(-)

v7.6.1 ships 156 insertions of changed engine Java that its own pinned engine tag lacks.

## Why this is the inversion class, by name

AGENTS.md's paired-release choreography names this exact failure: "the 7.1.0/v0.1.62 inversion: floor lagging a release ships a client whose pinned engine lacks the engine halves of its own features." That is precisely what happened, one release later, with a data-loss fix rather than a feature.

Blob identity confirms the deployed source is pre-fix byte-for-byte (relayed, from the attribution analysis): PgVectorRepository.java, VectorHandler.java, CatalogRepository.java and StagingPromoteOps.java at v0.1.71 hash-match their pre-fix parents.

## User-visible consequence

Cloud-mode users on v7.6.1 still run the pre-fix engine. F10c (PgVectorRepository.delete destroying chunks another document's manifest references) reaches them through >=11 caller paths including `nx store delete`, TTL expire, and MCP store_delete. The client-side fix cannot help: the delete executes IN the engine.

F8c is the one genuine exception, being client-side Python; v7.6.1 is the first released client carrying it.

## Ask

1. Cut engine-service-v0.1.72 containing 936e05a0 and 831a4e81, per the engine-release skill's full pre-tag battery. Tag cut is never blocked (AGENTS.md: A TAG GATES DELIVERY, NOT WORK).
2. Deploy and cloud-gate it.
3. Decide whether v7.6.1 needs a follow-up client release bumping REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION to 0.1.72, or whether the deploy alone closes the exposure. Note the deploy alone DOES close it for cloud users, since cloud users get whatever conexus deployed; local-mode installs get only what REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION names.
4. Releaser is human. This bead prepares; it does not cut.

## Constraint

Do NOT clean any dangling manifest rows before the engine carrying these fixes is deployed. Under live producers the population refills. See nexus-o8dil.7 and nexus-xehfx.

## Origin

Found while establishing producer-vs-residue attribution for RDR-191 GATE-2 (nexus-o8dil.7). The gate's residue hypothesis is refuted by this same evidence.
