title: [P0] GH#1454: T1 scratch entries orphaned by any claude -p-spawning tool call in the same MCP session (7.6.0, Steve)
description:
GH #1454, reported by Steve Harris against conexus 7.6.0 (PyPI, `uv tool`), macOS, local/self-hosted T3 mode, nx-mcp.

T1 scratch entries become UNREACHABLE to `scratch get`/`list` in the SAME MCP session as soon as any tool that dispatches a `claude -p` subprocess runs in between. `operator_summarize`, `operator_extract` and `nx_answer` all reproduce. `get`/`delete` report "Not found"; `list` reports "No scratch entries."

## Reproduction — 3/3 trials, WITH A CLEAN CONTROL

1. `scratch put` -> entry stored, id returned.
2. `scratch get`/`list` immediately after -> visible. (control passes)
3. Any operator call (`operator_summarize`, `operator_extract`) with unrelated content.
4. `scratch get`/`list` for the same entry -> "Not found" / "No scratch entries."
5. A fresh `scratch put` after step 3 is visible again, until the NEXT operator call orphans it identically. Held across 3 consecutive operator calls.

**CONTROL:** substituting a non-subprocess tool (`search`) at step 3 does NOT reproduce. The entry stays visible. That control is strong evidence the subprocess dispatch is the trigger and not elapsed time, call count, or TTL.

The reporter's methodology is good. Do not re-litigate the repro; start from it.

## ⛔ THE CENTRAL TENSION — this is the real question

`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/architecture.md` ("T1's three scopes") state MCP-tool T1 is **frozen to the session id at MCP-server spawn**, and that the scope moves only on a CONSUMED handoff marker, "never a per-call re-resolve" (nexus-d76vc).

If that were true, a child process clobbering a machine-wide marker COULD NOT affect the MCP scratch tool. So one of these is false and we need to know which:

  (a) the scratch MCP tool DOES re-resolve session id per call and frozen-at-spawn is aspirational or regressed;
  (b) the child `claude -p` writes something `_t1_handoff_tick` consumes, causing a legitimate-looking re-lease;
  (c) the entries move rather than the scope;
  (d) something else.

**If our own architecture doc is wrong, that is a finding in its own right** and must be corrected, not quietly worked around.

## Anchors to check (do not take on trust)

- `resolve_active_session_id()`, whose tier-4 fallback reads the flat file `~/.config/nexus/current_session` — our own docs call this "a machine-wide last-writer-wins file a concurrent session can own."
- `src/nexus/db/t1.py`: `t1_session_lease.<session_id>`, `publish_t1_session_lease` / `read_t1_session_lease`.
- `nexus.mcp.core._t1_handoff_tick`, marker `~/.config/nexus/t1_handoff.<mcp_pid>`, ancestry-authenticated via `nexus.session.find_mcp_sibling_pids`, plus `mcp_infra.reset_t1_for_release()`.
- `nexus-bjltu` established that `ephemeral=True` mints a fresh PG-backed T1 session per dispatch ONLY when the dispatch grants tool access (`mcp_servers`/`allowed_tools` set), and that the TOOL-FREE default (~15/17 call sites, including extract/rank/compare/summarize) mints NOTHING. Steve's repro uses exactly those tool-free operators. Establish whether the tool-free path is minting when it should not, or whether the cause is elsewhere entirely.
- Whether the child inherits or WRITES `NX_SESSION_ID` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and whether anything in the dispatch path writes `~/.config/nexus/current_session`.

## Why this is more than a user-visible annoyance

⚠ **This project's own agent workflow depends on the broken thing.** We use T1 scratch as the orchestrator-to-subagent bus and call `operator_*` / `nx_answer` routinely in the same sessions. If Steve is right, our own subagent write-backs and `review-completed` markers may be silently orphaned mid-session.

That has a specific consequence worth checking: the pre-push review-gate hook reads a `review-completed` T1 marker. If markers can be orphaned by an intervening operator call, that gate can fail open or fail closed for reasons unrelated to whether a review happened.

It also retroactively weakens a documented lesson. `CLAUDE.md` records that a suspected lost T1 write-back once traced to a TIMING RACE rather than scope confusion. That diagnosis may need revisiting if per-call scope drift is real.

## Determinations required

- ORPHANED vs DELETED. The reporter believes orphaned (entries still in PG under the old session id, just unaddressable). This decides whether users can recover data and materially changes severity.
- BLAST RADIUS: T1 only, or does T2 `memory_put` share the resolution path? T2 is our documented durable cross-process bus, so if it is affected the recommended workaround collapses.

## Reporter's stated workaround (verify before repeating it to users)

Use `memory_put` (T2), or `scratch_manage(action="promote")` before any operator call runs. This is only sound if T2 is genuinely unaffected.

## Constraints for whoever picks this up

⛔ Do NOT reproduce using the live `nx` CLI. This box runs Hal's PRODUCTION cloud-mode install beside the dev checkout; isolate via `--config-dir` or a sandboxed HOME (see `feedback_check_install_mode_before_diagnosing.md`). Missing pg_credentials and "no service lease" are CORRECT states here.

Strongly prefer a HERMETIC failing test. If it can be made to fail without the live install, the bug is nailed and we get the regression gate for free.
notes:
## 2026-08-11 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND VERIFIED. Data is DELETED, not orphaned.

Reproduced FIRST-PARTY in one shot before diagnosis: `scratch list` = 6 entries ->
one `operator_summarize` with a throwaway payload -> "No scratch entries."
`get` by explicit id also gone. This session had run for hours across dozens of
tool calls with T1 stable and had NEVER called an operator or `nx_answer`, so it
is a clean single-variable experiment. Rules out TTL, elapsed time, call volume,
and Agent-tool dispatch effects.

Steve's follow-up sweep (GH #1454 comment 5258808734) then confirmed 11/11
LLM-dispatched paths reproduce, and that `operator_aggregate` forced onto its SQL
fast path (`source="aspects"`, recognized reducer) does NOT. Trigger is precisely
"spawns a `claude -p` subprocess", not "is an operator".

## THE CHAIN (seven links, all VERIFIED-IN-CODE by me, not adopted on trust)

1. `operators/dispatch.py:212-213` — ephemeral dispatch STRIPS `NX_T1_SESSION` /
   `NX_T1_SESSION_ID` from the child env.
2. `dispatch.py:245-246` — but SETS `NX_SESSION_ID = <PARENT's session id>`.
3. Child exits -> Claude Code fires SessionEnd -> `_session_end_launcher.py`
   double-forks; the grandchild inherits that env via fork().
4. `hooks.py:305` `_open_t1()` -> `resolve_t1_routing_tiers` (`t1.py:1126-1159`).
   Tier 1 MISSES (vars stripped). Tier 2 resolves `resolve_active_session_id()`
   to the PARENT's id, finds the parent MCP's live refreshed lease, returns
   **USE_LEASED**, binding to the parent's session_id + token (`t1.py:1626-1629`).
5. `hooks.py:354-355` — `if t1 is not None: t1.clear()`
6. `HttpScratchStore.clear()` -> `close_session()` -> `POST /v1/t1/session/close`
7. `ScratchRepository.java:258-266` — unconditional
   `deleteFrom(SCRATCH).where(SCRATCH.SESSION_ID.eq(sessionId)).execute()`

## ⛔ THE SMOKING GUN — hooks.py:350-353

The comment immediately above the defect ASSERTS the exact safety property being
violated: only ever call clear() on a store "this process can prove is scoped to
ITS OWN session", and then enumerates `USE_LEASED` as qualifying. A USE_LEASED
resolution is BY CONSTRUCTION a borrow of a scope another live process owns. The
comment names the bug and blesses it. This is why the defect survived review, and
correcting the comment is part of the fix.

## DELETED, UNRECOVERABLE — not orphaned

Hard SQL DELETE, no tombstone, no re-scope. The recovery path that could have
existed does not fire: the flush copies `flagged_entries()` to T2 first, but the
MCP scratch tool never sets `persist=True` (`mcp/core.py:4249`), so MCP-written
rows are never flagged. Corroborated empirically: T2 project `scratch_sessions`
is EMPTY. Steve's data is gone. So are our six entries.

## T2 `memory_put` IS SAFE — the workaround is shippable

The flush's only T2 action is `db.expire()`, which reaps already-expired rows;
T2 has no session partition (`hooks.py:317-339`). "Use T2 instead" is CORRECT
advice and can go in the release note.

## ⛔ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER INFERENCE — DO NOT PATCH THE RESOLUTION CHAIN

Both the orchestrator's leading hypothesis and Hal's "it's the boundaries" read
pointed at session-identity leaking through `~/.config/nexus/current_session`.
THAT IS WRONG, and acting on it would have been a wrong-target fix on a P0.

The `frozen-at-spawn` claim in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md is **TRUE and
unregressed**: `mcp_infra.get_t1()` caches `_t1_instance` (`mcp_infra.py:296-313`),
reset only by `reset_t1_for_release()` from the handoff tick. The scope never
moved. A THIRD process deleted the rows underneath it. `get` by explicit id said
"Not found" because the ROW IS GONE, not because the id became unaddressable.

DO NOT file a doc defect against frozen-at-spawn. It is accurate.

## FIX (in progress)

Gate the destructive `clear()` on OWNERSHIP: clear only when T1 resolved via
tier-1 `USE_INHERITED` (a scope handed to this process outright), never via a
tier-2 lease BORROW. Precedent: `nexus-6a19f` fenced the shared-scope case for
the same reason, one tier over.

ACCEPTED TRADEOFF: a genuine SessionEnd whose MCP already tore down its lease
skips the clear, leaving rows to the 24h TTL sweep. Strictly the safe direction —
leaking rows to a TTL is recoverable; deleting a live process's working memory is
not.

## REGRESSION GATE

Hermetic repro exists and currently FAILS (the failure IS the bug): no live
service, ~0.05s, 2 pass / 1 fail, and it carries a CONTROL proving the causal
variable (`grants_tool_access=True` -> child mints its own session, clears only
its own). Being promoted into the repo with the patch. The control must survive —
without it the test could pass for the wrong reason.

## SPUN OUT, deliberately NOT in the P0 patch
- SessionEnd volume on every operator dispatch (P2)
- tier-2 resolving via the machine-wide `current_session` file (P2; its
  DELETION half is closed by this fix, its wrong-scope-read half is not)
- `HttpScratchStore.clear()` docstring overstatement (P3)

## RELEASE
Needs a 7.6.1 patch. 7.6.0 is the affected shipped release.
## ✅ 2026-08-11 — SHIPPED AND VERIFIED in conexus 7.6.1

Fix: commit 6f7fddfa on develop, released via PR #1455, tag v7.6.1 -> ce0ac901.

PUBLICATION VERIFIED (not assumed — closing before this check is the
publish-was-skipped failure class):
  - GH release v7.6.1 published, non-draft
  - PyPI latest = 7.6.1, wheel + sdist present
  - a real resolver installs it (uv, with --refresh; the first probe failure was
    uv's stale index cache, not PyPI)
  - fresh-install-mvv.sh --published 7.6.1: PASSED, 9/9 legs, doctor zero ✗ /
    zero ⚠, non-vacuity leg green, engine v0.1.71 sha256+signature verified
  - `mcp` resolved to 1.29.0 from the real published artifact — the nexus-l2ku5
    dependency-RESOLUTION class is clean. No pre-tag gate can prove this.

Both stacked reviewers cleared the patch. Red-before/green-after was verified
THREE times independently: implementer, code-review-expert (temp-swap + SHA-256
restore check), and orchestrator.

Shipped with a REDUCED pre-tag battery, authorized by Hal. Record of what was
skipped and why: T2 `nexus/emergency-release-flow-7.6.1-skip-record` [22278].

### Open follow-ups from this arc (none blocking, all filed)
  nexus-5uoxu P1 — re-land telemetry --dry-run PAIRED with an engine cut
  nexus-b6rw2 P2 — `nx scratch clear` reaches the same USE_LEASED path
  nexus-4xvy1 P2 — tier-2 via machine-wide current_session (premise corrected)

### The lasting lesson
The comment above the old `clear()` asserted the exact safety property the code
did not have, and that is why the defect survived review. The replacement states

title: RDR-191 P2: HttpVectorClient.expire() reaps catalog manifest with NO collection scoping, unlike --id/--title
description:
Round-3 substantive-critic finding on the uncommitted nexus-c53hy fix (2026-08-11).

nexus-c53hy closed the deterministic "reap tombstones a live document in a
DIFFERENT collection" hazard for `nx store delete --id` and MCP
`store_delete` by (a) adding a collection-scoped T3 existence check BEFORE
reaping, and (b) threading an `expected_collection` guard into
`reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes` / `store_delete_catalog_cleanup`. The
`--title` branch also passes `expected_collection=col_name` even though its
ids are already collection-pre-resolved (defense-in-depth).

`HttpVectorClient.expire()` (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:2846) was
NOT threaded through, despite sitting in the exact same shape:

    for entry in self.list_collections():
        name = entry.get("name", "")
        ...
        if expired_ids:
            reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes(expired_ids)   # <- no expected_collection=name
            total += self.batch_delete(name, expired_ids)

`name` is trivially in scope at the call site (it is the loop variable used
one line later for `batch_delete`), so passing `expected_collection=name`
is a one-line fix mirroring what `commands/store.py`'s `--title` branch
already does at line 510.

Without it, `reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes`'s per-chash resolution
(`resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash`, a GLOBAL chash lookup with no
collection filter) will tombstone WHATEVER catalog document owns that
chash -- even if it lives in a totally different `knowledge__*` collection
than the TTL-lapsed note actually being expired. This reproduces whenever
two knowledge__ collections each contain a chunk with byte-identical
content (full sha256 match) where one copy is a TTL-lapsed note in
collection X and the other is a permanent store_put-origin document in
collection Y != X: `expire()` walking collection X will resolve the shared
chash to its (possibly Y-owned) catalog entry and tombstone it, believing
it is cleaning up its own TTL note.

This is the SAME bug class nexus-c53hy fixed for --id/MCP, left open at a
third call site, with an explicit but incomplete rationalization in the
c53hy fix writeup (T2 nexus/nexus-c53hy-fix-reap-before-existence-check):
"NOT threaded through http_vector_client.py::expire()'s call (out of
scope, its ids are already collection-pre-resolved same as --title, zero
behavior change by not touching it)." The "ids are collection-pre-resolved"
half is true (expired_ids are guaranteed to exist as T3 rows in `name`) --
that closes the EXISTENCE half of the c53hy bug. It does NOT close the
CATALOG-OWNER-IN-A-DIFFERENT-COLLECTION half, which is exactly what
`expected_collection` guards against and is exactly what --title also
still needed the guard for despite being equally "pre-resolved".

Severity CRITICAL, not just tracked debt, because:
1. expire() is the unattended/automated path (cron-shaped, `nx store
   expire`) -- there is no operator present to notice or attribute a
   wrongly-tombstoned document, unlike an interactive --id/--collection
   typo a human might investigate.
2. It is the identical silent-data-loss-adjacent shape (unconditional
   destructive catalog action with no collection verification) the whole
   RDR-191 F10c saga (3 rounds so far) exists to eliminate.
3. Untested: tests/test_o8dil5_expire_manifest_reap.py's
   test_expire_preserves_a_chunk_genuinely_shared_with_a_live_document
   registers its "permanent twin" under the SAME collection
   (`physical_collection=_COLLECTION`) as the TTL note -- the cross-
   collection case this bead describes is not exercised anywhere.

Suggested fix: `reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes(expired_ids,
expected_collection=name)` at http_vector_client.py:2846, plus a new
integration test mirroring test_o8dil5_expire_manifest_reap.py's shared
test but registering the twin under a DIFFERENT physical_collection,
asserting the twin survives AND the TTL note's own chunk is still
correctly reclaimed (since the guard should only skip the reap for chashes
whose resolved owner is elsewhere -- verify it does not also block the
common single-owner case).

Origin: substantive-critic round-3 pass on nexus-c53hy's uncommitted diff,
2026-08-11 (T2 nexus/rdr-191-o8dil5-substantive-critique-round3-2026-08-11).
Sibling: nexus-c53hy (same bug class, --id/MCP call sites, already fixed).
close_reason: Fixed in 936e05a0 on develop (pushed). RDR-191 F10c anti-join bundle: deletion scoped by anti-join excluding tombstoned owners; TTL expire retracts the manifest and reports the actual reclaimed count; the catalog reap runs only after a collection-scoped existence pre-check; expected_collection is now a REQUIRED keyword on all three guard functions, sweep verified repo-wide. Four stacked-review rounds, round 4 clean: code-review-expert 0 Critical/0 High 'commit as one commit'; substantive-critic JUSTIFIED, 0 critical, cascade terminated, severity trend shrinking R1->R4. Non-vacuity proven RED/GREEN on every layer, including that the obvious form of the h7nax test does NOT reproduce. Engine suite 1980/0/1 on the merged tree. NOT closed by this: nexus-o8dil.45, nexus-o8dil.2, nexus-o8dil.39, nexus-fokts, nexus-uyl70.

title: RDR-191 P2: nx store delete --id / MCP store_delete tombstone catalog UNCONDITIONALLY before verifying the T3 delete succeeded
description:
nexus-o8dil.5 round-2 remediation reordered nx store delete --id (commands/store.py:449-462, delete_cmd) and MCP store_delete (mcp/core.py:4566-4615) from delete-then-reap to reap-then-delete, so PgVectorRepository#delete's F10c anti-join (which now refuses to delete a chash any live manifest row still references, including the document's OWN not-yet-tombstoned manifest row) does not block the common single-owner case.

The reorder is directionally correct and necessary for Fix 1 to work end-to-end, but as implemented it invokes the catalog reap UNCONDITIONALLY -- before any check that the T3 delete will actually find and remove anything:

- commands/store.py delete_cmd (--id branch), line 459: `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids([doc_id])` runs, THEN line 460 checks `db.delete_by_id(...)`; if that returns False, a ClickException("not found") is raised -- but the catalog document has already been tombstoned as a side effect, with zero indication in the error message.
- mcp/core.py store_delete, line 4603: `store_delete_catalog_cleanup(doc_id)` runs, THEN line 4605 checks `t3.delete_by_id(...)`; if False, the function returns "Not found: {doc_id!r} in {col_name}" -- again with the catalog already mutated and no mention of it.

Both `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids`/`reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes` and `store_delete_catalog_cleanup` resolve purely by chash via `resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash` (docs_for_chashes) -- they perform NO check that the id actually exists in the target T3 collection, and no check that the delete is about to succeed. So this fires on:
  - a bogus/stale/already-deleted doc_id (e.g. a client retry after a timeout, or a stale id from an old store_list),
  - a doc_id passed with the WRONG `collection` argument (t3.delete_by_id scopes to the named physical collection; the catalog reap does not scope by collection at all),

in either case tombstoning a live, unrelated-to-the-failed-request catalog document while reporting a clean "not found" / non-mutating-looking error.

This is the inverse of the very bug class nexus-o8dil.5 fixes (F10c: silent data loss via unconditional destructive action with no verification) -- it is unconditional destructive catalog action gated on nothing, on the FAILURE path of an operation that is supposed to be a no-op when it fails.

Not caught by the existing test suite: tests/test_store_cmd.py::test_store_delete_by_id[False-...] exercises the not-found branch but uses a MagicMock T3 client and never mocks/observes nexus.catalog.store_hook.reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes or store_delete_catalog_cleanup, so it cannot detect whether the catalog reap fired. No test asserts catalog state (or lack of catalog mutation) on the not-found path for either the CLI --id branch or MCP store_delete.

Suggested shape (not prescriptive): gate the reap on a resolve-first-then-reap-then-delete-then-verify sequence, or perform the reap and delete inside a single unit where a resolve confirms the chash both exists in the target collection AND belongs to the document about to be acted on before any tombstone happens; alternatively, invert to reap-in-recovery: attempt delete first, and only if PgVectorRepository#delete's anti-join is suspected of blocking a legitimate single-owner delete (i.e., delete_by_id reports not-found AND a catalog resolve confirms a live owning document exists), reap then retry the delete once. Either approach avoids mutating catalog state on a request that never actually deletes anything.

Origin: substantive-critic round-2 pass on nexus-o8dil.5's uncommitted diff, 2026-08-11. Sibling: nexus-o8dil.45 (discarded delete-count over-reporting -- a different concern, this bug is about an unconditional catalog mutation on the not-found path, not about the delete count).
close_reason: Fixed in 936e05a0 on develop (pushed). RDR-191 F10c anti-join bundle: deletion scoped by anti-join excluding tombstoned owners; TTL expire retracts the manifest and reports the actual reclaimed count; the catalog reap runs only after a collection-scoped existence pre-check; expected_collection is now a REQUIRED keyword on all three guard functions, sweep verified repo-wide. Four stacked-review rounds, round 4 clean: code-review-expert 0 Critical/0 High 'commit as one commit'; substantive-critic JUSTIFIED, 0 critical, cascade terminated, severity trend shrinking R1->R4. Non-vacuity proven RED/GREEN on every layer, including that the obvious form of the h7nax test does NOT reproduce. Engine suite 1980/0/1 on the merged tree. comments.text:
STATUS UPDATE (round-3 substantive-critic verification, 2026-08-11, T2 nexus/rdr-191-o8dil5-substantive-critique-round3-2026-08-11): this bead is FIXED, uncommitted, on develop main checkout. Fix shape: collection-scoped `t3.get_by_id(col_name, doc_id)` / `t3.get_by_id` pre-check before either reap call (commands/store.py delete_cmd --id branch; mcp/core.py store_delete), plus a second `expected_collection` defense-in-depth kwarg threaded into `reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes` / `store_delete_catalog_cleanup`. Not-found and anti-join-protected/race are now distinguished in both CLI and MCP error messages. New test file tests/test_c53hy_delete_reap_scoping.py (4 tests, real ActiveCatalog + real T3Database substrate) is RED pre-fix / GREEN post-fix on the two wrong-collection cases.

CORRECTION to this bead's own filed description: the text above ("So this fires on: a bogus/stale/already-deleted doc_id ... OR a doc_id passed with the WRONG collection argument ... in either case tombstoning a live, unrelated ... document") OVERSTATES the bogus-doc_id half. Verified (both analytically and via the new test suite's bogus-id regression-pin tests, which pass unchanged under OLD code too): `resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash` on a genuinely unregistered chash returns None under BOTH the pre-fix and post-fix code paths, so a bogus/never-registered doc_id was NEVER a live reproducer -- there is no catalog entry to resolve, so no reap fires, regardless of ordering. Only the WRONG-COLLECTION case (a REAL doc_id, naming the wrong --collection/collection argument) is the deterministic RED reproducer. Of the 4 new tests, 2 (wrong-collection, CLI+MCP) are genuine RED-before-fix reproducers; the other 2 (bogus-id, CLI+MCP) are non-regression pins for behavior that was already correct, not fix verification. This does not change the fix's correctness or this bead's priority, but the bug's blast radius as originally filed was overstated by conflating two scenarios of different actual risk.

Independent round-3 concurrency review of the get_by_id-then-reap-then-delete sequence found no NEW incorrect-tombstone window: the expected_collection guard is evaluated fresh (against a newly-resolved catalog entry) at reap time, not cached from the earlier T3 read, so a narrow existence-check-to-reap race degrades at worst to "correct document tombstoned a moment earlier than ideal" or a "concurrent modification" message, never a wrong-document tombstone. Strictly safer than the round-2 code this replaced (which had no existence check at all).

New sibling filed this round from this same bug class, NOT yet fixed: nexus-h7nax (CRITICAL) -- HttpVectorClient.expire() was not threaded with the expected_collection guard despite sitting in the identical shape, and remains exposed to the cross-collection-duplicate-chash hazard this bead closed for --id/MCP.

Recommend: (1) mark this bead's status to reflect the fix is implemented (uncommitted), (2) attach a corrected one-line summary of the bogus-vs-wrong-collection distinction to the bead's title or description for future readers, (3) do not close until committed and until nexus-h7nax's sibling gap is at least explicitly deferred with a tracking note (not silently dropped).

title: RDR-191 P2: audit AT LEAST TEN (not NINE) PgVectorRepository.delete callers, of which SIX+ take no manifest action (F8b, corrected); GATE-2 is unsatisfiable without this
description:
**PLAN-AUDIT FINDING A1 [HIGH]: GATE-2's exit criterion is known-unsatisfiable by the beads that existed when it was written.**

Beads `.1`-`.5` fix four named sites. **None of them is one of F8b's nine callers.**

## F8b, verbatim
`PgVectorRepository.delete` *"has NO manifest leg at all, the javadoc assigns the obligation to the caller, citing T2 `nexus_rdr/155-manifest-fk-decision`, and it is the funnel for **NINE** distinct Python calling functions (both superseded sweeps, all three quarantine paths, the misclassified prune, `nx t3 gc`, `nx store delete`, and the TTL expiry). Of those nine, **SIX perform no catalog or manifest action whatsoever**; two rely on the manifest having been rewritten by a prior separate call; one only tombstones the parent document and leaves the manifest rows."*

*"Every dangling-manifest exposure in the system traces through this single Java method, which cannot detect or refuse it... That makes it the single best place to enforce the invariant, and the single best explanation for why the class recurs."*

## CORRECTION (2026-08-11): the "NINE" count above is proven wrong

F8b's census was proven incomplete by `nexus-o8dil.5`'s own caller audit (posted as a comment on that bead, and independently verified in this correction — see `nexus-o8dil.5` comment thread for file:line detail). Two additional distinct Python calling functions reach `PgVectorRepository.delete` beyond F8b's nine:

- **10th (confirmed live producer, not named in F8b's prose):** `_force_t3_orphan_cleanup` (`src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:702`, called from `:833`) — the `--force` deadlock-break helper. Deletes by content_hash lookup with zero manifest action. Falls into the same "no manifest action" bucket as six of the original nine, so it does not change the acceptance-criteria SHAPE, but it does change the count and must be enumerated explicitly, not skipped.
- **11th (verified real as a distinct calling function, this session):** MCP `store_delete` (`src/nexus/mcp/core.py:4566`) — the MCP-tool twin of `nx store delete --id`. Both resolve to the same underlying `HttpVectorClient.delete_by_id`, but they are separate entry points (CLI command vs. MCP tool), consistent with how this census already counts callers 3-5 (`chunk_quarantine.py`'s three functions) as distinct despite sharing infrastructure. It needs no manifest-action fix (`delete_by_id` already surfaces a blocked delete as "not found"), it needs to be COUNTED.

**The true count is AT LEAST TEN, possibly ELEVEN.** Do not enumerate "the nine" as a closed set — enumerate everything that actually calls into the delete funnel, then reconcile against F8b's list.

The exit criterion is "zero live PRODUCERS". Six callers that delete chunks and take no manifest action are producers. Fixing the funnel's data-loss bug (bead `.5`) does not discharge them, it stops the funnel destroying SHARED chunks; it does not make the six callers clean up their own manifest rows.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Enumerate ALL callers explicitly by name and file:line — AT LEAST TEN, not nine (see CORRECTION above). Do not work from the RDR's parenthetical, and do not stop at F8b's list even corrected — re-derive from the codebase.
- [ ] For EACH: classify as (a) needs no manifest action, with the reason; (b) needs one and lacks it, so FIX it; (c) relies on a prior separate call, so identify the call and whether the ordering is ENFORCED or merely conventional. F8c's lesson is that unenforced ordering is the bug.
- [ ] Every (b) fixed with a test. Every (c) either enforced or converted to (b).
- [ ] Attach the full caller table (ten-plus rows) to this bead. GATE-2 cannot close without it. NOTE: `nexus-o8dil.5` has an audit table of its own attached as a comment (2026-08-11) covering the same ground with the corrected count — reconcile against it rather than re-deriving from scratch; if this bead's stricter (b)/(c) classification adds fixes beyond `.5`'s scope, do that work here.
- [ ] Consider whether the invariant belongs IN `PgVectorRepository.delete`, the RDR calls it "the single best place to enforce" it.
- [ ] Note: `nexus-o8dil.45` (filed 2026-08-11) separately tracks that `HttpVectorClient.delete()`/`batch_delete()` discard the server's actual deleted-count, so several of these callers (the misclassified-prune arms, `nx store delete --title`, `_force_t3_orphan_cleanup`) can now silently over-report success when the anti-join partially blocks them. That is a distinct concern from this bead's manifest-action audit — do not fold it in here, but be aware of it when judging whether a caller is "clean."

## Context
- RDR: `docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md` (accepted 2026-08-10, gate PASSED run 5). Read the named findings IN FULL; every phase has load-bearing detail.
- Verified code anchors: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-code-anchors-verified-2026-08-10` (verified file:line sheet; RDR line numbers have drifted in 5 places)
- Plan: T2 `nexus/plan-rdr-191-phases-2-7`
- Retrieval: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_search(query="RDR-191", project="nexus")`; `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__nx_answer(question=..., scope="code")`

## Standing constraints (non-negotiable)
- ALL DDL through Liquibase. NEVER DDL in Python. NEVER a new SQLite table.
- Key on the NATURAL id (`chunks_<dim>.chash`), never a metadata copy of it.
- THREE FULL HNSW indexes, never partial (F13, measured: partial buys 0.11% and costs a silent ~250x seq-scan).
- FK is `ON UPDATE CASCADE` + deferrable on the delete side. NOT `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
- TDD: test file before implementation. Code must compile including tests.
- Do NOT touch the write-side chunk caps (16 / 64 / 300), measured, not residue.

## Execution reminders
- Use `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for the analysis phase.
- SPAWN parallel sub-agents to conserve orchestrator context; sub-agents may spawn their own children for intensive work.
- Update continuation state after each milestone: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_put(project="nexus", title="rdr-191-continuation-state")`.

title: RDR-191 P2: fix F10c, where PgVectorRepository.delete destroys chunks other documents reference (live data loss)
description:
Fix F10c: `PgVectorRepository.delete` destroys chunks that other documents still reference. **A live silent data-loss bug, today, independent of this RDR**, and a dangling-manifest producer, so it falls inside GATE-2's exit criterion.

## Why
By RDR-108 design, identical chunk text in a collection collapses to ONE row shared by many manifest rows. So deleting document A's chunks currently SUCCEEDS and destroys a chunk document B still references. No error, no signal. B's manifest rows become dangling.

F8b sizes the blast radius: `PgVectorRepository.delete` (RDR-stated `:2132-2140`) has NO manifest leg at all, the javadoc assigns the obligation to the caller, and it is the funnel for **NINE** distinct Python calling functions (both superseded sweeps, all three quarantine paths, the misclassified prune, `nx t3 gc`, `nx store delete`, TTL expiry). **SIX of the nine perform no catalog or manifest action whatsoever.** Every dangling-manifest exposure in the system traces through this one Java method, which cannot detect or refuse it; the failure surfaces later and elsewhere as `fetchDocumentChunks`' `IllegalStateException`.

The RDR's fix: **anti-join-scoped deletion** (verified working in F10c).

## Scope note
The RDR's Phase 2 enumeration lists only F8c/F12b/F12c, but Phase 2's EXIT CRITERION is the broader "zero live producers of dangling-manifest or NULL-collection rows". F10c is a dangling-manifest producer, so it is inside the criterion even though the enumeration omits it. Flagged during planning; do not drop it on the grounds that it is not in the phase's bullet list.

## Acceptance
- [x] TEST FIRST: two documents share a chunk (identical text, same collection); delete document A's chunks; assert the shared chunk SURVIVES and document B still reads. — MET: `PgVectorRepositoryDeleteAntiJoinTest.java`, RED confirmed pre-fix (in-place revert/restore), GREEN post-fix.
- [x] Deletion is scoped by anti-join against `catalog_document_chunks`, not by chunk id set alone. — MET: `PgVectorRepository.delete` now correlated-subquery anti-joins on `catalog_document_chunks` (tenant_id/collection/chash), same idiom as `nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans`.
- [x] Audit all NINE Python callers of `PgVectorRepository.delete`; for each, record whether it now needs no manifest action, or a manifest action it is missing. Attach the table to this bead. — MET AS OF THIS COMMENT (table attached below), WITH CAVEATS: (1) the "NINE" premise itself is wrong — the audit found a 10th live caller and a plausible/verified 11th, see the table and `nexus-o8dil.39` (being corrected separately to carry the true count); (2) sibling bead `nexus-o8dil.39` independently owns a stricter version of this same audit and depends on `.5` — ownership between the two is not fully disambiguated by this comment alone.
- [x] Non-vacuity: the shared-chunk test fails (data loss observed) against pre-fix code. — MET: RED confirmed by temporarily reverting the method body in-place and restoring (git stash blocked for subagents in shared tree, per project constraint).

**NOT closing this bead on the strength of these four ticks.** A 2026-08-11 substantive-critic pass (T2 `nexus/rdr-191-o8dil5-substantive-critique-2026-08-11`, verdict: not-justified, 4 criticals) found issues this bead's stated acceptance criteria do not cover: (a) `HttpVectorClient.delete()`/`batch_delete()` discard the server's actual deleted-count, so every caller that now can be partially blocked by the anti-join has zero client-side visibility into that (tracked separately as `nexus-o8dil.45`); (b) the continuation-state note's claim "Closes F8c as a side effect" is disputed — sibling bead `nexus-o8dil.2` owns F8c with stricter acceptance (explicit per-arm action-or-refuse + dedicated test) that this diff does not satisfy, and `nexus-o8dil.2` has been annotated accordingly so it is not closed on that basis.

## Context
- RDR: `docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md` (accepted 2026-08-10, gate PASSED run 5). Read the named findings IN FULL; every phase has load-bearing detail.
- Verified code anchors: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-code-anchors-verified-2026-08-10` (verified file:line sheet; RDR line numbers have drifted in 5 places)
- Plan: T2 `nexus/plan-rdr-191-phases-2-7`
- Retrieval: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_search(query="RDR-191", project="nexus")`; `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__nx_answer(question=..., scope="code")`

## Standing constraints (non-negotiable)
- ALL DDL through Liquibase. NEVER DDL in Python. NEVER a new SQLite table.
- Key on the NATURAL id (`chunks_<dim>.chash`), never a metadata copy of it.
- THREE FULL HNSW indexes, never partial (F13, measured: partial buys 0.11% and costs a silent ~250x seq-scan).
- FK is `ON UPDATE CASCADE` + deferrable on the delete side. NOT `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
- TDD: test file before implementation. Code must compile including tests.
- Do NOT touch the write-side chunk caps (16 / 64 / 300), measured, not residue.

## Execution reminders
- Use `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for the analysis phase.
- SPAWN parallel sub-agents to conserve orchestrator context; sub-agents may spawn their own children for intensive work.
- Update continuation state after each milestone: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_put(project="nexus", title="rdr-191-continuation-state")`.
- STACKED REVIEW is mandatory at the phase boundary: `code-review-expert` AND `substantive-critic`. Both run. A clean code review does not permit skipping the critic.

title: RELEASE BLOCKER 7.5.0: combined write moves local embedding server-side at a 300-chunk cap sized for a client-side embedder — engine hits 77GB and wedges on nx index repo
description:
Found in the v7.5.0 release battery, step 6c (release-sandbox shakedown). Reproduced 3/3 on a cleaned machine. Hal identified the mechanism; this bead records the verified chain.

## Symptom

nx index repo over a 36-FILE fixture corpus wedges the local engine:
  PID 54311 STAT Rs  %CPU 1542.8  RSS 80832144 KB
  Physical footprint: 77.4G (peak 77.4G)
Roughly 15 cores pegged, ~77 GB resident. /livez stops answering while pg_ok stays true, so the supervisor correctly fires storage_service_stuck_exit at consecutive_unhealthy=4 and exits 3 for an OS restart a sandbox never provides. Client side shows manifest_write_transient_error_retry / ReadTimeout on the combined write. No exception and no crash log: the process never gets far enough to throw.

## Verified causal chain

1. CLIENT CAP. per_collection_chunk_cap (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:508) returns 64 for CCE prefixes (docs/knowledge/rdr) because Voyage contextual embed is slow behind a 30s gateway. nexus-w3hzw (commit 0218ddf0) added: when the engine reports embedding_mode onnx-local, those prefixes get _CODE_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP = 300 instead. Local mode IS onnx-local. Landed BEFORE v7.4.0 — this half is pre-existing and was SAFE on its own.

2. WHO EMBEDS CHANGED IN 7.5.0. Under the old two-call shape the chunk leg went through db.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings — embeddings computed CLIENT-side. The 7.5.0 combined write (nexus-kl2z6/nexus-wxjr6) sends {chash, text, metadata} and CombinedWriteService (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CombinedWriteService.java, javadoc lines 24-41) resolves (chash, text, vector) itself, embedding via EmbedderRouter "in ONE batch call". So local-mode embedding moved from client to engine.

3. NO SUB-BATCHING AT THE ENGINE. Bge768Embedder.embed() calls embedBatch(texts) directly (no partitioning, no backpressure). embedBatch sets .optPadding(false) and pads to a RECTANGULAR [batchSize, maxLen] tensor, maxLen = min(longest sequence, MAX_SEQ_LEN=512). ONNX then produces last_hidden_state [batch, seq, 768] and, internally, attention tensors of [batch, heads, seq, seq].

4. THE ARITHMETIC. Attention is O(batch * seq^2):
     batch=64,  seq=512 -> 0.81 GB per attention tensor, 0.10 GB hidden state
     batch=300, seq=512 -> 3.77 GB per attention tensor, 0.47 GB hidden state
   BERT-base is 12 layers with several intermediates live at once; ~20 such buffers reaches the observed 77.4 GB. At the old 64 cap this path stayed roughly 4.7x smaller and survived, which is why it was never seen.

## Regression status

Each half predates the other, but the INTERACTION is new in 7.5.0: the 300 cap was chosen when the local path was NOT the thing doing the embedding. Treat as a 7.5.0 regression in effect.

## Why every other gate stayed green

- fresh-install-mvv indexes ONE md file — never reaches a 300-chunk CCE flush.
- Cloud/managed mode is voyage, so the cap stays 64 and this path is not taken.
- Unit suite does not run a 36-file local index through the combined write.
Nothing in the battery except the shakedown exercises local + large corpus + combined write together. This is exactly the coverage the shakedown exists to provide.

## Note on the cap contract

per_collection_chunk_cap has exactly TWO consumers: indexer.py:4193 (ChunkBatcher flush cap) and http_vector_client.py:1265 (upsert_chunks oversize paging). The combined-write client, src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py, references NEITHER — its only paging is _REGISTER_MANY_PAGE for docs, not chunks. The flush cap is therefore the single remaining bound on what reaches the engine embedder.

## Fix options (Hal decides)

A. CLIENT-ONLY, ships in 7.5.0 with NO engine re-cut: stop returning 300 for CCE prefixes on the onnx-local path, or give the combined-write path its own smaller embed-batch cap. Cheapest correct fix.
B. ENGINE: sub-batch inside Bge768Embedder.embedBatch (or in CombinedWriteService before the embed call) so a large POST degrades in throughput instead of memory. Correct defense in depth — a client sending 300 must never be able to OOM the engine — but needs a new engine tag and a re-gate.
C. Both: A now to unblock 7.5.0, B on the next engine cut.

Recommend C.

## Evidence

Stack sample, ps, and logs: scratchpad/wedge-capture/ (service.sample 2098 lines; native image is unsymbolized, so the arithmetic and javadoc are the proof, not frame names). Release-cut state: T2 [22131].
close_reason:
CLIENT HALF SHIPPED in conexus 7.5.0 (commit f4a675f2, tag v7.5.0 on 3b91b303, PyPI + GH release verified). Closing on shipped scope; the remaining work is tracked separately and is NOT silently dropped — see the carve-out below.

## What shipped

per_collection_chunk_cap now applies a memory-derived _ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP=16 to EVERY prefix when the serving engine reports onnx-local, ahead of the Voyage CCE/code split (which is unchanged — there the embed is a network call and the 30s control-plane timeout reasoning still holds). Root mismatch fixed: a TIMEOUT-derived cap (300) was governing a MEMORY-bound path, since Bge768Embedder.embed() -> embedBatch() runs one ONNX forward pass over a rectangular [batch, maxLen<=512] tensor with no sub-batching, and attention is O(batch * heads * seq^2).

Applying the cap before the prefix split also closed a latent hole found by code review: non-CCE prefixes previously skipped the mode check entirely and always got 300.

## Verification

Measured on the original 36-file repro, same box, continuous external RSS sampling:
  cap=300 -> 77.4 GB peak, ~15 cores pegged, /livez starved, supervisor stuck_exit. Reproduced 3/3.
  cap=16  -> 3.03 GB peak, release-sandbox shakedown PASSED 11/11, zero storage_service_unhealthy events, /livez 200 throughout.
Peaks recorded WITH flush_concurrency=3 genuinely active, so not a single-flush budget. Full battery green: unit 12350/0, lint 697/0, smoke, upgrade-shakeout 12/12, fresh-install-mvv, engine floor exit 0, parity 32/0. Dual-reviewed: code-review-expert (mechanically correct) + substantive-critic (round 1 not-justified 3 Critical -> corrections -> round 2 partial, ZERO Criticals).

## NOT closed by this — deliberately carved out, do not read this close as "done"

- nexus-zu4ma (P1) — ENGINE-side sub-batching. This fix bounds what THIS client sends; it is not a ceiling at the engine. Any other caller, an older client, or a future code path can still POST a large batch and reproduce the OOM. Next engine cut.
- nexus-b32rx (P1) — why v7.4.0 SURVIVES at the same 300 cap is UNEXPLAINED. The bisect that produced that observation also moved the pinned engine (v0.1.68 vs v0.1.69), so it isolates nothing. Shipped as a known-open item.
- nexus-97dp4 (P2) — the shakedown fixture is only ~92 chunks, so at cap=16 the cap never binds (largest flush 15). The gate caught THIS blowup only because a near-whole-corpus batch was already catastrophic; it will NOT catch a future cap raise.
- nexus-lqrec (P2) — retry-storm risk: an abandoned request may continue server-side while a retry starts a second one; more round trips = more retry opportunities at scale. The passing run is one corpus at one size.
- nexus-fdn1c (P2) — the shipped 7.5.0 release note asserted a throughput cost ("~19x more round trips", "noticeably longer") that was NEVER measured. Retracted in-repo on develop (17d48b6b); published release notes are frozen with the original wording. Measure it properly before restating it.

## Corrections made during this work, recorded so they are not re-derived

Two claims I asserted and retracted: (1) "v7.5.0 moved local embedding client->server" is FALSE — upsert_chunks_with_embeddings:1372 forwards TEXT and ignores caller embeddings, so the old path embedded server-side too; (2) "the bisect shows a 7.5.0 client delta" is FALSE — engine-version confound. Also falsified along the way: orphaned JVMs as the cause (killed all 16, reproduced clean) and an advisory-lock deadlock (it is runaway allocation, not blocking). Full detail in the bead comment thread and T2 release-7.5.0-cut-state-2026-08-09.

title: kl2z6 combined-write: CombinedWriteService.stripNul strips SPACE not NUL — silently corrupts all chunk text/metadata written through the new path
design:
CRITICAL: CombinedWriteService.java private static String stripNul(String s) uses the Java space-character literal (ASCII 0x20) instead of the NUL character literal (0x00) in both the indexOf check and the replace call. Reference implementation PgVectorRepository.java around line 2840 uses the correct NUL literal. Docstring claims this mirrors PgVectorRepository.stripNul but it does not.

IMPACT: every chunk text and every metadata string value written through the new combined-write path has every space character silently stripped before storage in chunks_dim. A two-word sentence becomes one run-together word. This is silent content corruption on essentially all real text (natural language and code both use spaces near-universally) -- exactly the failure class kl2z6/wxjr6 exists to eliminate, introduced by the commit meant to close it. It also fails to strip actual NUL bytes, so text with a real NUL byte still hits Postgres NUL rejection inside the per-doc transaction.

WHY UNCAUGHT: CombinedWriteRepositoryTest's chunk() helper always passes empty metadata, so metadata sanitization is never exercised with real content. Tests that send multi-word text via chunk(x, "cw1 text x") only assert existence booleans and chunks_written counts, never assert stored text equality against combined-write-path content. The one place stored text content IS asserted reads content seeded via raw SQL (seedChunk384), bypassing CombinedWriteService entirely.

FIX: replace the space literal with the NUL literal in both places. Add a regression test that writes a multi-word chunk through the real combined-write call and asserts the stored text is byte-identical, plus a metadata string value containing a space. Consider extracting one shared sanitization utility instead of maintaining two independently hand-copied implementations.

BLOCKS MERGE: this is a data-correctness regression on commit ec42b531 (worktree-agent-aeee9cbd6284c934e, not yet on develop) on the exact axis the kl2z6 initiative protects.
notes: ADJUDICATED 2026-08-09 (developer, worktree-agent-aeee9cbd6284c934e): DOES NOT REPRODUCE at runtime. Added the prescribed regression test (combinedWrite_multiWordTextAndSpacedMetadata_storedByteIdentical -- multi-word text + metadata containing spaces, through the real writeManyCombined path, byte-identical read-back from chunks_384) and ran it FIRST against the unfixed code per falsify-then-fix discipline: it PASSED. Raw byte inspection (od -c) of both stripNul call sites confirmed the literal was already a genuine 0x00 NUL byte, not 0x20 space -- but embedded as a LITERAL raw byte in the .java source rather than the standard Java unicode escape sequence PgVectorRepository.stripNul uses for the identical literal. A raw NUL byte renders as a blank/space glyph in text viewers, which is almost certainly what produced this report: a visual-parsing false positive on an actual NUL byte, not a wrong-character defect. No functional/data-correctness bug; nothing to fix for correctness. Replaced both raw NUL bytes with the explicit escape-sequence form anyway (now byte-for-byte matching PgVectorRepository.stripNul's own form) purely to remove the rendering ambiguity that has now produced this same misreading twice independently (once during my own implementation, once during this review). Commit 1b86be3b. Full detail: T2 nexus/nexus-kl2z6-engine-increment1-adjudication-2026-08-09 [21989]. Recommend closing as adjudicated-false-positive (not 'fixed' -- runtime behavior was already correct); leaving OPEN pending the orchestrator's disposition since bd close is gated on a fresh review-completed marker I should not mint myself as the implementing developer.
close_reason: false-positive, adjudicated by substantive-critic 2026-08-09 with byte-level (od -c) verification; defensive cleanup + regression test landed in 1b86be3b anyway

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: ADJUDICATED FALSE POSITIVE (2026-08-09, substantive-critic verification). Verified via git show ec42b531:...CombinedWriteService.java | sed -n '243,246p' | od -c: the character between the single quotes and inside the double-quoted string at both stripNul call sites was a genuine raw 0x00 NUL byte (od -c renders it literally as '\0'), NOT the space character (0x20, which od -c would render as a literal space glyph between the printed characters). 'file' also reports the original source as binary ('data'), consistent with an embedded raw NUL byte -- the same phenomenon CollectionRegistry.key's comment already documents from a prior incident in this codebase. My original read via text-rendering tooling mis-displayed the invisible NUL glyph as a blank/space and I incorrectly concluded it was a space-character literal. title: release/v7.4.0: _resolve_mcp_binary crashes nx doctor on RuntimeError from Path.home()
description:
health.py _resolve_mcp_binary (HOME-scoping fix, nexus-k0lk9 sibling, uncommitted on release/v7.4.0) calls Path.home().resolve() inside `except OSError:` only. Path.home() (via pathlib's expanduser) raises RuntimeError("Could not determine home directory."), NOT OSError, when HOME is unset and no matching /etc/passwd entry exists for the current UID -- a real shape in containers/Kubernetes/OpenShift running under an arbitrary assigned UID, or minimal/distroless images.

Empirically reproduced: mocking Path.home to raise RuntimeError propagates uncaught through _resolve_mcp_binary -> _check_mcp_entry_points -> run_health_checks -> commands/doctor.py's `results, is_local = run_health_checks()` call, which has NO try/except wrapper. This crashes `nx doctor` outright.

Contradicts the file's own pervasive invariant: dozens of other except-Exception blocks in health.py carry the explicit comment "must not crash `nx doctor`" / "boundary fallback -- degrade gracefully". This new code path is the one exception.

Fix: catch a broader exception (at minimum `except (OSError, RuntimeError):`) around Path.home().resolve(), consistent with the rest of the file's degrade-not-crash pattern. File: src/nexus/health.py, _resolve_mcp_binary, the `try: home = str(Path.home().resolve())` block.

Found during substantive-critique of the release/v7.4.0 branch (uncommitted gate fixes for the 7.4.0 shakedown battery).
close_reason: Fixed at 4c17077c: except (OSError, RuntimeError) around Path.home(); regression test proven non-vacuous by the critic via scratch-copy revert. Critic closure: APPROVE.

title: _normalize_mineru_latex strips whitespace from prose between two ESCAPED dollar signs — the same PROSE-not-formula corruption as gtltb, a trigger 57a392ff did not cover
description:
Second instance of the nexus-gtltb corruption class. 57a392ff fixed the $$ desync;
this one is still live on develop HEAD 76a2f07c and is corrupting freshly-indexed
documents RIGHT NOW, including documents already "remediated".

MinerU emits literal currency as \$ . The inline pass at
src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py:374-378 is

    md = re.sub(r"\$([^$]+?)\$", lambda m: f"${normalize_latex_spacing(m.group(1))}$", md)

which does not honour the backslash escape. The prose BETWEEN two \$ occurrences is
therefore treated as an inline math span and gets re.sub(r"\s+", "", s) applied —
prose stripped instead of formula, exactly the gtltb inversion.

MINIMAL REPRO, verified against develop HEAD 76a2f07c:

    from nexus.pdf_extractor import _normalize_mineru_latex as N
    N(r"costs \$5 and then \$9 later.")
    # -> 'costs \\$5andthen\\$9 later.'

The gtltb control is clean, which confirms 57a392ff took and that this is a
distinct trigger:

    N(r"$$a + b$$ some prose here $c$ more prose $d$ end.")
    # -> '$$a+b$$ some prose here $c$ more prose $d$ end.'

LIVE CORRUPTION, catalog doc 1.14.23 (Natural Language to What), chunk
375b2d1ad6ab17a1, written AFTER the 57a392ff fix:

    contracts above \$1M.Iftheenvironmentisarelationaldatabasewithtablesforsuppliers,
    contracts,andlocations,thetargetisnaturallySQL.Thesystemmustidentifytherelevant
    tables,attributes,...

Partition of that document's 371 title-matching T3 rows:
    IN-MANIFEST (current): 175 rows, 3 glued  <- real glued prose, post-fix
    NOT-IN-MANIFEST (stale): 196 rows, 0 glued

Inverted from the natural hypothesis: the STALE rows are clean and the CURRENT
rows carry the glue.

FIX SHAPE
Protect \$ (and \$$) with the same placeholder discipline already used for display
blocks and \text{}, before the inline pass runs.

REGRESSION TESTS REQUIRED
  - N(r"costs \$5 and then \$9 later.") is a no-op
  - the gtltb $$ / $ control above stays clean
  - an odd number of \$ occurrences does not desync the pass

SCOPE CONSEQUENCE
Any currency-bearing document is still corrupted after remediation, so the
nexus-gtltb remediation worklist is UNDER-SCOPED and the corpus scan must be
re-run with this trigger included before remediation is declared complete.

title: _normalize_mineru_latex desyncs on $$ delimiters and strips whitespace from PROSE — every formula-bearing PDF indexed since 2026-06-03 has corrupted, embedded text
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 investigating whether MinerU PDF intake was healthy. It is not.
This is SILENT DATA CORRUPTION that reached stored, embedded, searchable content.

MINIMAL REPRO — no MinerU, no PDF, instant:

    from nexus.pdf_extractor import _normalize_mineru_latex as f
    f(r"$$a + b$$ some prose here $c$ more prose $d$ end.")
    -> '$$a+b$$someprosehere$c$moreprose$d$ end.'

"some prose here" becomes "someprosehere". Verified by hand, not only by the
investigation.

MECHANISM. _normalize_mineru_latex (src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py ~L332) normalizes
in two passes over one string. The DISPLAY pass substitutes but leaves the `$$`
delimiters in the output. The INLINE pass then runs
    re.sub(r"\$([^$]+?)\$", ...)
which cannot match the empty string between a `$$` pair, so it begins matching
ONE `$` INTO each pair. That consumes a delimiter and desyncs every subsequent
open/close pairing on the page. From the first `$$` block onward, the regions
treated as "math" are the PROSE BETWEEN formulas — and math regions get
    re.sub(r"\s+", "", s)

ACCOUNTING ON THE TEST FIXTURE, exact and with zero residual:
    raw joined length (pre-normalizer)   60135   == the locked constant exactly
    normalized                           59217   == the observed failure exactly
    removed                                918
      from genuine formula spans           326   (36%, legitimate)
      FROM PROSE                           592   (64%, the bug)
So the drift I filed earlier as "cause not isolated" is fully explained by code.

REAL DAMAGE, page 3 of the fixture:
  BEFORE '...significantly faster to compute.\n\n## 1.2. Set reconciliation via
          bloom filters\n\nSet reconciliation is a problem in computer science...'
  AFTER  '...significantlyfastertocompute.##1.2.Setreconciliationviabloomfilters
          Setreconciliationisaproblemincomputerscience...'
Paragraph breaks (\n\n) and markdown headings (##) are destroyed too, so the
CHUNKER loses its boundary signals as well.

IT IS IN PRODUCTION DATA. `nx index pdf` on a scratch config dir indexed 55
chunks; `nx search` returns stored, embedded text containing
"pute.##1.2.SetreconciliationviabloomfiltersSetreconciliationisaproblemin...".
Embeddings were computed over word-boundary-free text. Retrieval quality on every
affected document is degraded and cannot recover without a re-index.

BLAST RADIUS: commits 55691515 and 217072cc, both 2026-06-03 ("closes #1049").
Every formula-bearing PDF indexed since then. Damage scales with $$-block density
and position — 680 of the 918 lost chars came from 2 of 17 fragments on this
fixture, so per-document severity varies and has NOT been surveyed across the
corpus.

THE INVERSION, which is the sharpest part: the fix does the OPPOSITE of its

title: [catalog] the arbiter converge path blanks repo_root/repo_hash/description on an existing owner when the payload omits them — silent overwrite where the old code failed loudly
description:
BLOCKS the nexus-0ehwe arbiter branch (worktree-agent-ac05d5f0e63fe7ddc, 6b6f1ed5). Found
by a deep-analyst review, then independently re-verified line by line. Full analysis: T2
[21316] nexus/arbiter-branch-merge-readiness-analysis-2026-07-31.

THE REGRESSION. The branch's converge path turns a LOUD NO-OP into a SILENT PARTIAL
OVERWRITE of an existing owner row.

  CatalogRepository.java:432   prefix = existing;          <- the new converge decision
  CatalogRepository.java:452   INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix)
  CatalogRepository.java:459-464  DO UPDATE SET repo_hash / description / repo_root /
                                  head_hash  =  EXCLUDED.*     <- BLIND, unconditional

Setting prefix = existing makes the statement conflict on the PK, which routes it into a
DO UPDATE arm that overwrites every column from EXCLUDED. For a payload that OMITS those
fields, EXCLUDED carries emptiness, not the incumbent value:
  s(o,"repo_hash")        -> null   (:4453, returns null when the key is absent)
  nne(s(o,"repo_root"))   -> ""     (:4483)

PRE-FIX THIS WAS DATA-SAFE. A prefix-less payload allocated a FRESH prefix, collided on
catalog_owners_unique_name_type, and rolled back -- a loud 23505 that changed nothing. The
branch makes the statement REACH a row it previously could never reach, and then blanks
fields on it.

REACHABLE END-TO-END, not theoretical:
  src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:366-374  register_owner builds its payload
  omit-if-falsy -- every field past name/owner_type is conditional. So
  register_owner("nexus", "repo") sends exactly {name, owner_type}: the destructive shape.
  CatalogHandler.java:942-947 passes the body straight through.
  (register_repo_owner always sends repo_hash + repo_root, so `nx index repo` is safe. It
  is the bare register_owner call that carries the hazard.)

WHY repo_root IS THE SEVERE ONE. deriveSourceUri anchors every derived source_uri on
repo_root (RDR-096 / nexus-3e4s). Blank it and the idempotency SELECT misses, so files that
are ALREADY registered draw NEW tumblers -- the duplicate-document class catalog-016 exists
to prevent. The partial unique index cannot catch it, because the resulting source_uris
genuinely differ. Note nexus-3e4s was itself a ~6,500-row contamination from mis-anchored
source_uris; this is a second door into the same state.

THE SUITE IS BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION. The headline converge pin
(ArbiterCompletenessTest:285) uses precisely the destructive payload and asserts only
hasSize(1) plus tumbler_prefix -- never that the incumbent's other columns SURVIVED. Same
wrong-assertion shape the author already caught once in their own mutation table (M1 did
not kill the test they expected). A green suite is not evidence here.

THE FIX, and it follows the author's own converge/refuse principle: PRESERVE-ON-OMIT in the
CONVERGE branch only. Build the DO UPDATE set-map conditionally on the payload actually
CONTAINING each key, so an omitted field is left alone rather than blanked. Leave the
address-explicit branch's blind overwrite as it is -- that behaviour is PRE-EXISTING, not
introduced here, and changing it is a separate decision.

Required with the fix: a pin that registers an owner WITH repo_hash/repo_root/description,
re-registers it with the bare {name, owner_type} payload, and asserts every omitted column
still holds its original value. Deleting the preserve-on-omit guard must turn that pin red.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-07-31, commit 8aecc39e, merged into develop (NOT yet pushed — the combined
engine suite is the gate).

Preserve-on-omit, scoped to the CONVERGE path only: the DO UPDATE set-map is now built
conditionally on the payload actually CONTAINING each key, so an omitted field is left
alone instead of overwritten with null / "".

THREE JUDGMENT CALLS, recorded because each could reasonably have gone the other way:

 1. PRESENCE, NOT TRUTHINESS. containsKey, not a null/blank check — so a caller that
    explicitly sends "" can still CLEAR a field. A COALESCE-shaped fix would have silently
    removed that capability while looking equivalent.
 2. CONVERGE PATH ONLY. When the caller supplies an explicit tumbler_prefix they named that
    row deliberately, and the blind overwrite there PRE-DATES this branch. Widening the fix
    to it is a separate decision; folding it in here would have been silent scope creep
    inside a P0.
 3. TWO PINS, OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. One asserts omitted fields survive; one asserts sent
    fields still apply. Without the second, preserve-on-omit could later become
    preserve-always with the suite staying green.

FALSIFIED: making the assignments unconditional again fails EXACTLY ONE test on EXACTLY the
repo_root assertion, observed value "" (the nne path, not null — which is the difference
between "a test went red" and "the mechanism I described is the one operating"), while the
converse pin stays green. Restored: 26/26.

THE LESSON THAT GENERALISES, and it is the second instance in one week. The pre-existing
converge pin could not have caught this: it creates its owner WITHOUT
repo_hash/repo_root/description, so there was nothing for a blind overwrite to destroy, and
it asserted only hasSize(1) + tumbler_prefix. Twenty-four green tests missed a P0 because
THE FIXTURE DECIDED WHAT THE PIN COULD PROVE — exactly what seedCollections did to the
rename pins in nexus-v6za0 one commit earlier. When a pin's fixture omits the state the
hazard acts on, the pin is decorative no matter how strong its assertions look.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part worth keeping: a deep-analyst review I would NOT have
run unprompted. The branch was green — full suite ARB2-RC=0, ArbiterCompletenessTest 24/24
— and I was about to merge it. Hal had to intervene and ask for the specialist agents. That
near-miss is the concrete evidence behind nexus-3sij7 and the nexus-h33x8 epic.

Engine-side: reaches nobody until an engine tag + deploy. Hal relays that.

title: [bug] rename onto a supersede-marked collection that still holds data silently MERGES two collections and erases the supersede chain (1232585d regression)
description:
REGRESSION introduced by 1232585d (the nexus-u4e20 fix). Found by the re-review
stacked-reviewer pass 2026-07-31; VERIFIED by direct reading, not taken on the
reviewer's word.

## The defect

A catalog tombstone has TWO provenances, and 1232585d's guard reasons about only one.

(a) renameCollectionTxn step 3 leaves an EMPTY tombstone at X — every child was
    re-homed to Y first. This is the case the fix analysed, and for it the fix is
    correct.

(b) POST /v1/catalog/collections/supersede leaves a FULLY POPULATED one.
    CatalogRepository.supersedeCollection's own javadoc says it: "This method stays
    a pure UPDATE." It never touches chunks, documents, taxonomy or aspects. A
    collection superseded by a model migration keeps ALL its data until an explicit
    later purge.

For (b), liveCollectionExists(Y) is false, so the collision guard at
CatalogHandler.java:1114 now PASSES where it previously 409'd, and
renameCollectionTxn takes the canonical FULL-REHOME branch:

  1. step 1's upsert conflicts on Y and REVIVES it — the doUpdate arm overwrites
     CONTENT_TYPE / OWNER_ID / EMBEDDING_MODEL / MODEL_VERSION / DISPLAY_NAME /
     LEGACY_GRANDFATHERED with X's, and clears superseded_by, ERASING the Y->Z
     supersession pointer with no audit;
  2. step 2 re-homes X's chunks_384/768/1024, catalog_document_chunks, taxonomy,
     aspects and documents ON TOP OF Y's existing rows;
  3. step 3 tombstones X -> Y.

## Impact

Two distinct collections silently merged under one name. Because a supersede is
most often a MODEL migration, X and Y routinely differ in embedding model and
dimension, so the result is chunks from two vector spaces under one registry row
that claims a single model. The erased Y->Z pointer is exactly the unaudited chain
rewrite handleCollectionSupersede guard 2 exists to refuse, reached through the
rename door instead.

Before 1232585d this 409'd, because collectionExists(Y) was true.

## Why the existing guards do not save it

Both CLI rename verbs pre-flight probe_collection_state(new), which reads T3 CHUNK
PRESENCE (src/nexus/db/collection_state.py) and never consults
catalog_collections.superseded_by. A data-bearing Y reads PRESENT and the CLI
refuses -- so the only thing standing between a caller and the merge is a
CLIENT-SIDE guard protecting an ENGINE-SIDE invariant. That is precisely the
reasoning pattern u4e20 was filed to reject.

Worse, the new cross_model 409 message added by the same commit actively says
"Drop cross_model to rename onto the retired name instead." — steering a
direct-HTTP caller into the merge.

## Fix

Gate the revive on the tombstone's IDENTITY, not merely its non-liveness: permit
the canonical branch onto a non-live target only when
tombstone.superseded_by == oldName. That predicate is exactly the round-trip undo
the fix exists for, and it excludes every supersede-marked, data-bearing target.
Anything else 409s with a message naming the real remedy (purge or restore), not
"drop cross_model".

Also correct the false premise comment at CatalogRepository.java:2929-2932.

## Pins owed

Through the real HTTP endpoint: supersede Y->Z (leaving Y populated), then
rename X->Y, and assert 409 + Y's rows untouched + Y.superseded_by still Z.
Mutation-falsify by reverting the identity gate.

Engine-side; reaches nobody until an engine-service tag + conexus deploy, so there
is a clean window to fix before the cut.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REOPENED 2026-07-31. The 351874c5 fix does NOT close this. Proven, not argued.

BOTH stacked reviewers found it independently, and a falsification probe confirmed it
before either finished reporting:

    supersede(X -> Y)     leaves X POPULATED with superseded_by = Y
    rename(Y -> X)        oldName = "Y", tgtSuperseded = "Y"  -> IDENTITY MATCHES
                          -> guard does not fire -> canonical FULL-REHOME -> MERGE

    Probe result: expected 409 but was 200.

THE REASONING ERROR, and it is the SAME ONE the fix was written to correct:

  1232585d used LIVENESS as a proxy for EMPTINESS.  Wrong: supersede tombstones are
                                                    non-live AND populated.
  351874c5 used IDENTITY as a proxy for EMPTINESS.  Wrong: a supersede tombstone can
                                                    point at the rename source.

Neither column records provenance. `renameCollectionTxn` step 3 and `supersedeCollection`
both write `.set(SUPERSEDED_BY, <target>)` — the rows are byte-indistinguishable. So
identity discriminates DIRECTION, not PROVENANCE.

WORSE, THE PIN PICKED THE SAFE CONFIGURATION. post_renameOntoASupersedeMarkedCollection
seeds src/tgt/successor and supersedes tgt -> successor, i.e. a THIRD-PARTY successor,
which is the one arrangement where identity and provenance happen to agree. The dominant
real shape is supersede(old -> its own successor) then rename the successor back onto the
old name — which is exactly what `nx catalog doctor --collections-drift` steers an
operator into (nexus-e1k14), and what a partial model migration leaves behind.

Reviewer note worth keeping: because a cross-model supersede means different dimensions,
the two collections' rows land in DIFFERENT chunks_<dim> tables, so nothing collides and
nothing aborts. The merge is silent by construction.

THE FIX MUST MEASURE THE HAZARD, NOT INFER IT. Both reviewers converged on the same
prescription independently: inside renameCollectionTxn, on the non-live-target path,
refuse unless the target is verifiably EMPTY (no rows in chunks_384/768/1024,
catalog_document_chunks, catalog_documents). That is the property the canonical branch
actually depends on, stated in the branch selector's own snapshot — and it also collapses
nexus-mijr4, since the check stops being restated across the handler/txn boundary.

Identity may remain as a complementary assertion. It cannot be the gate.

REQUIRED PIN: supersede(tgt -> src), then rename(src -> tgt), assert 409. The one-line
variant of the existing pin that it should have been.

NOT READY FOR AN ENGINE TAG until this lands.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED and pushed to develop 2026-07-31 (6fb31f1d, hardened by 34ab012b).

The handoff set an explicit closure precondition: "do NOT close without running the
falsifying arrangement -- supersede(tgt -> src), then rename(src -> tgt), assert 409 and
that the data survived." That arrangement is now a pin:
post_supersedeThenRenameSuccessorOntoIt_409sInsteadOfMerging. It seeds a DOCUMENT into
the tombstone (seedCollections alone creates a registry row only, which is why every
earlier rename pin exercised an empty target and could not see this hazard), supersedes
x -> y, renames y -> x, asserts 409, asserts the message names the EMPTINESS condition
specifically (identity is TRUE in that arrangement, so asserting the generic refusal
would not have discriminated), and asserts the target's superseded_by survived intact.
CatalogHandlerRenameTest 25/25 green.

THE FIX MEASURES THE HAZARD instead of inferring it. Attempts 1 and 2 used liveness and
then identity as proxies for emptiness; neither column can carry provenance, because
renameCollectionTxn step 3 and supersedeCollection write superseded_by identically. The
revive now requires BOTH emptiness (the data-safety half, re-measured inside the acting
transaction) AND superseded_by == oldName (the audit-pointer half, checked in the handler
and safe there because supersedeCollection's WHERE clause is a compare-and-swap -- see
nexus-2sovp for that adjudication).

COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES makes the re-home set and the emptiness set equal by
construction, so the 17-vs-5 drift that caused the merge is no longer expressible.

Verification: engine suite 1541/0, Python 11562 -> 11567 (the +5 being the new gate,
which is how I know it ran rather than skipped). Both stacked reviewers ran TWICE -- on
the fix and again on the fixed fix, because pushing 351874c5 before re-review is what let
1232585d ship. Round 2: 0 Critical, 0 High, both said safe to push.

FOUND AND FIXED DURING REVIEW, in this same arc: gc_audit was missing from the list --
