title: rollback-floor tag is positionally correct only on databases initialized after it shipped — on an already-migrated cluster it applies LAST, so rollback-to-tag silently no-ops
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 while landing nexus-a0m60's rollback round-trip harness. Reasoned from
Liquibase's rollback-to-tag semantics and the observed rollback ordering, NOT yet
measured against a real pre-existing cluster — see VERIFY below before acting.

THE MECHANISM. floor-001-rollback-floor.xml adds <tagDatabase tag="rollback-floor"/> as
the SECOND changeset in master order. liquibase.rollback(tag) rolls back everything
executed AFTER that tag's DATABASECHANGELOG row, by orderexecuted.

  FRESH database  — the floor runs in position 2, so orderexecuted=2 and every
                    migration-owned changeset sits above it. rollback(tag) reverts the
                    whole schema. This is what SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest
                    exercises, and it is GREEN (208 rollback statements, down through
                    memory-001-1 to the tag).

  EXISTING cluster — the floor changeset is UNRUN, so it applies on the next boot and
                    lands with the HIGHEST orderexecuted. Everything else executed
                    BEFORE it. rollback(tag) therefore finds nothing after the tag and
                    reverts approximately nothing — while reporting success.

That second case is precisely the failure class this whole arc exists to kill: a
rollback that is green having done nothing. It affects every cluster that already
exists, which is every cluster operators actually care about, including production.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN THE CHANGELOG. A tag records WHEN it was applied; it cannot
retroactively claim a position it did not occupy. runAlways would make it strictly
worse (re-stamped to the tail on every boot = permanently useless). So the tag is
correct only for databases initialized after it shipped.

WHAT TO DECIDE:
  - Scope the tag honestly as a TEST fixture and drop the operator-facing framing, or
  - Keep it operator-facing but document that on pre-existing clusters the supported
    target is rollbackCount / rollbackToDate, not the tag, or
  - Have the engine stamp the tag at the correct position during an upgrade (invasive;
    Liquibase offers changelogSync-style tools that could place it, needs design).

VERIFY FIRST — this is reasoned, not measured. The measurement is an old-tree hop in the
shape of SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest: git archive a pre-floor changelog tree,
apply it, then apply HEAD's tree, then read the floor tag's orderexecuted and attempt
rollback(tag). If the tag's orderexecuted comes out low, this bead is wrong and should be
closed with that evidence. Do not act on the reasoning alone.

RELATED: nexus-ixsxa (duplicate DATABASECHANGELOG rows) is a separate reason
rollbackCount is unreliable, which is what pushed the design toward a tag in the first
place. If the tag turns out to be unusable on existing clusters, both count-based and
tag-based targets have caveats and the operator guidance needs to say so explicitly.
close_reason:
CLOSED — the artifact this bead is about no longer exists.

Hal's call 2026-07-27: the floor tag has NO VALUE. Schema rollback is not an
operational path here — the engine never calls it, and the 7.0.0 migration amounts to a
highly-orchestrated one-way cut. So a named operator rollback target was never worth
anything, and the only thing this tag actually did was ship a promise that was false on
every cluster that already exists.

REMOVED: floor-001-rollback-floor.xml and its master include, plus the
ROLLBACK_FLOOR_TAG constant and all prose referencing it. Safe to delete outright — the
changeset was added 2026-07-27 in 42b1cc86 and engine-service-v0.1.57 was cut from
5079f388, BEFORE it, so no deployed cluster has ever run it. schema_changeset_count
returns 208 -> 207, so there is nothing to relay to conexus after all.

WHAT REPLACES IT — and it is what Hal actually asked for ('ensure moving forward we can
at least get back to here'): SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest now rolls back BY
COUNT, all the way to ZERO rows, and asserts DATABASECHANGELOG ends empty. If the chain
can walk all the way back it can certainly walk back to any intermediate point, so the
'a future release can return to this state' guarantee is proven directly rather than
promised via a tag. Verified green: full depth reached, 208 rows reverted.

Counting rows is honest where the tag was not: the count is read from the database the
test just built, so it neither rots as changesets land nor cares about nexus-ixsxa's
duplicate rows (they are simply more rows to revert).

Full depth is reachable at all because the three changesets with no executable inverse
now declare themselves irreversible: role-001-1 (roles are cluster-level, pre-existing),
vectors-001-1 and catalog-016-0 (both added by nexus-a0m60).

THE FINDING ITSELF STAYS TRUE AND IS RECORDED, so nobody re-derives it: tagDatabase tags
the MOST RECENTLY EXECUTED DATABASECHANGELOG row, not its own. Established from
TagDatabaseGenerator (liquibase-core 4.29.0: UPDATE joined against ORDER BY DATEEXECUTED
DESC, ORDEREXECUTED DESC LIMIT 1) and confirmed by our own run log, where the floor
changeset was itself rolled back. Consequence: any tag retrofitted into an
already-migrated cluster lands at the TAIL, so a rollback to it reverts almost nothing,
exits 0, and — because staging-4-svc-grants' rollback REVOKEs nexus_svc's staging USAGE
and table privileges — actively breaks land/promote until the next restart.
A comment at the old include site in db.changelog-master.xml says do not re-add a tag
without reading this bead.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RAISED TO P0 AND RE-CHARACTERISED 2026-07-27, after both stacked reviewers independently
measured the mechanism. THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION UNDERSTATED THIS IN TWO WAYS: it said
"reasoned, not measured" (it is now measured) and it framed the outcome as a silent no-op
(it is not — it actively revokes production grants).

THE MECHANISM, MEASURED. tagDatabase tags the MOST RECENTLY EXECUTED DATABASECHANGELOG
row, not its own row. Established two ways:
  - liquibase.sqlgenerator.core.TagDatabaseGenerator (javap over liquibase-core-4.29.0)
    emits an UPDATE joined against `SELECT ORDEREXECUTED, DATEEXECUTED FROM
    DATABASECHANGELOG ORDER BY DATEEXECUTED DESC, ORDEREXECUTED DESC LIMIT 1`.
  - Direct evidence already in our own green run: the log shows
    "Rolling Back Changeset: ...floor-1-rollback-floor" — the floor changeset is ITSELF
    rolled back. That only happens if the tag sits on an EARLIER row. On a fresh DB that
    row is role-001-1, which is exactly why the test reaches the bottom.

CONSEQUENCE ON AN ALREADY-MIGRATED CLUSTER. floor-1-rollback-floor is unrun, so it
executes on the next boot at max(orderexecuted)+1, and the five runAlways changesets then
re-stamp to max+2..max+6. `liquibase rollback rollback-floor` therefore reverts EXACTLY
those five grants changesets and exits 0.

THAT IS NOT A NO-OP. staging-4-svc-grants' rollback runs
    EXECUTE format('REVOKE ALL ON staging.%I FROM nexus_svc', rel.relname);
    REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA staging FROM nexus_svc;
and our own new test now proves that block genuinely EXECUTES (it asserts nexus_svc holds
zero staging privileges after a rollback, and it passes). So an operator following the
documented procedure during an incident gets: exit 0, schema untouched at HEAD, and
nexus_svc stripped of USAGE on staging plus all privileges on its tables. land/promote/
finalize start failing immediately. It self-heals only on the next service restart, when
runAlways re-grants.

That is verbatim the failure mode SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest names as its
reason for existing — "a rollback that silently stops early and reports success" — and the
harness structurally cannot see it, because it always starts from a fresh container where
the floor sits at position 2.

DONE ALREADY (2026-07-27, uncommitted at time of writing): the operator-facing prose that
invited this has been corrected in floor-001-rollback-floor.xml, db.changelog-master.xml
and the ROLLBACK_FLOOR_TAG javadoc. All three now state the fresh-init precondition
explicitly and name this bead.

STILL TO DECIDE (the reason this stays open at P0):
  1. MEASURE IT IN THE SUITE. SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest already materialises an
     OLD_TAG changelog tree via `git archive` and applies it, then HEAD. That is exactly
     the fixture. A leg that does OLD_TAG -> HEAD -> rollback("rollback-floor") and asserts
     the resulting changelogRowCount closes this in the same suite with an existing
     pattern. Until that exists, the harness's green is fresh-init-only by construction.
  2. WHETHER THE SHIPPED TAG EARNS ITS KEEP. Its only value beyond the test was the
     operator-facing target, which is precisely what does not work on the clusters
     operators have. The alternative is to drop the changeset (reverting
     schema_changeset_count 208 -> 207) and have the test tag at runtime via
     update(1) -> tag() -> update(). That removes the false promise entirely at the cost
     of the named target on future fresh installs.
  3. OPERATOR GUIDANCE. On a pre-existing cluster the substitute is rollbackToDate against
     the release's deploy timestamp, or a manually placed tag. Note nexus-ixsxa makes
     rollbackCount unreliable on those same clusters (it counts ROWS and they accumulate
     one per boot), so BOTH count- and tag-based targets carry caveats and the runbook has
     to say so.

title: [bug] service-mode memory search cannot find entries by any word inside a dotted title — every .md-suffixed T2 note is unfindable by title fragment
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk (RDR-158/155 substrate port), bucket 4 — a GENUINE SERVICE GAP, not test debt. Measured 2026-07-25 against the engine substrate (service JAR at develop 8a8ce284) versus the SQLite baseline, same store method, same inputs:

  title                        query          sqlite  service
  RDR-025-implementation.md    RDR-025             1        0
  xylophone99.md               xylophone99         1        0
  xylophone99.md               xylophone99.md      1        1
  auth-design.md               auth                1        0
  auth-design.md               auth-design         1        0
  plaintitle                   plaintitle          1        1

ROOT CAUSE — tokenizer divergence, not a missing index. Title IS indexed: memory-001-baseline.xml changeset 4 builds a STORED tsvector with setweight(to_tsvector('english', title), 'A'). But PostgreSQL's text-search parser classifies 'auth-design.md' as a FILE token and keeps it WHOLE, whereas FTS5's default unicode61 tokenizer splits on every non-alphanumeric and emits 'auth', 'design', 'md' as separate tokens. plainto_tsquery('english','auth') therefore has nothing to match. A title is findable in service mode ONLY by its exact full string, or when it contains no '.' at all.

WHY THIS IS P0-SHAPED. Service is the storage default since 6.0 (storage_backend_for hard default = SERVICE). '<name>.md' is the dominant T2 title convention — this repo's own nexus/nexus_rdr namespaces are almost entirely .md-suffixed. So on the default substrate, 'nx memory search RDR-025' silently returns nothing for an entry titled RDR-025-implementation.md. Silent wrong-answer on a read path, which is the no-silent-fallbacks class: the search succeeds, returns 200, and reports zero hits.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED (do this first): whether the deployed cloud engine behaves identically (measured only against a locally built JAR), and how much of the live corpus is affected. Both are cheap to check and change the severity conversation.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not decided):
  - Index a tokenizer-neutral projection of title alongside it — e.g. append translate(title, './-_', '    ') to the tsvector expression so the parts are separately lexed. Liquibase changeset, regenerates the STORED column.
  - Switch the title leg to the 'simple' config over a pre-split title.
  - to_tsquery with :* prefix matching — does NOT fix this case (the stored side is the problem, not the query side).
Whichever lands needs a parity contract asserting the six rows above match across substrates, so the divergence cannot silently return.

TEST FALLOUT: test_t2.py::test_search_finds_by_title (2 params), test_search_title_with_project_filter, test_fts_migration_is_idempotent fail under the engine substrate for exactly this reason. They assert correct user-facing intent and must NOT be rewritten to accommodate the gap — they are blocked on the fix.

BLOCKS: nexus-aqbrk (the port cannot land these files green without it).
close_reason:
Fixed in the engine, deployed, verified live, and now PINNED for local installs.

Commits: 73fdd124 (FTS finds words inside dotted titles) + c52068bb (fold Latin-1
diacritics in memory FTS, matching FTS5 remove_diacritics=1).

Shipped in engine-service-v0.1.57, deployed to api.conexus-nexus.com 2026-07-27.
Verified LIVE by conexus's read-only probe, 11/11 PASS — not inferred from a green
aggregate: 'auth-design.md' matches auth / auth-design / auth-design.md;
'RDR-025-implementation.md' matches 'RDR-025'; 'plaintitle' still matches itself; a
non-matching term still does NOT match (the fix does not match everything).

STEP-6 structurally could not see this — its legs read chunks_{384,768,1024} while
memory-002 touches nexus.memory. The separate probe is the evidence. T2 [21164].

Delivery to local-mode installs closed by 721cd3f7 (REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION -> (0,1,57));
before that bump the fix reached cloud users only.

Fold boundary is pinned and must not drift to unaccent:
MemoryRepositoryTest.search_diacriticFold_stopsWhereFts5Stops.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REPRODUCED ON THE LIVE INSTALL, not just the test substrate (2026-07-25, via the running MCP against Hal's real T2).

  memory_get(project=nexus, title="postmortem-macos-pg-bundle-nonrelocatable-2026-07-01.md")  -> returns the entry
  memory_search("nonrelocatable")                                                             -> "No results."
  memory_search("dyld")                                                                       -> returns THAT SAME entry (rank 1)

"nonrelocatable" as a single token occurs ONLY in that entry's title (the body writes it hyphenated, "non-relocatable", a different lexeme). "dyld" is a plain word in the body. So the corpus is indexed and search works — the title is simply not reachable by any word inside it. Confirms the divergence is user-facing on a real, populated, service-backed install, not an artifact of the freshly minted test tenant.

Severity now settled: this is a silent wrong-answer on a default-on read path, in production, today. The remaining unknown from the description is narrowed to one item — whether the DEPLOYED cloud engine tokenizes identically to the locally built JAR. Corpus impact no longer needs estimating: every .md-suffixed title is affected, which in this repo's own namespaces is nearly all of them.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
TWO MORE DIVERGENCES IN THE SAME SUBSYSTEM, found finishing the test_t2.py port. Same root (PostgreSQL text-search configuration vs FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer), same file to fix, so recording here rather than splitting — but note they need DIFFERENT changes, not one:

2. ACCENT FOLDING LOST. Content "résumé cafetière naïve", query "resume": sqlite 1 hit, service 0. FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer folds diacritics by default; to_tsvector('english', ...) does not. Fix needs the unaccent extension applied on BOTH the stored expression and the query side (unaccent is not installed by default — this is a Liquibase CREATE EXTENSION plus a regenerated STORED column).

3. PREFIX-QUERY SYNTAX LOST. Content "authentication authorization tokens", query "auth*": sqlite 1 hit, service 0. FTS5 supports the trailing-* prefix operator; plainto_tsquery discards the * as punctuation. Fix is query-side only: to_tsquery with a ':*' suffix per trailing-*-bearing term, which also means the service must parse the query rather than hand it wholesale to plainto_tsquery (and plainto_tsquery's injection-safety is currently doing real work — the replacement has to keep that).

So the memory-search parity gap is three distinct behaviours, not one: dotted-title tokenization (the original finding), accent folding, and prefix syntax. Whatever lands should be gated by ONE parity contract exercising all three across substrates. Suggest retitling this bead to "memory FTS parity: service-mode search diverges from FTS5 on tokenization, accent folding, and prefix syntax" when it is picked up.

Test fallout grows by two: test_t2.py::test_fts_special_characters[fr.md-...-resume] and [auth.md-...-auth*].

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
OPEN QUESTION CLOSED 2026-07-26: the DEPLOYED CLOUD ENGINE tokenizes identically. This was the one item the description said to establish FIRST, and it is now measured rather than assumed.

ENDPOINT CONFIRMED, not inferred:
  nx service probe -> managed nexus service reachable: https://api.conexus-nexus.com
                     release_version: 0.1.56
  storage_backend_for('memory') -> StorageBackend.SERVICE
  get_credential('service_url')  -> https://api.conexus-nexus.com

So this install's MCP reads go to the deployed cloud engine at the CURRENT release (0.1.56 — the same version the floor pins and the same one cloud is running), not to a locally built JAR and not to a local supervisor.

REPRODUCED AGAINST IT, just now:
  memory_search('nonrelocatable') -> 'No results.'
  memory_search('dyld')           -> [9447] nexus/postmortem-macos-pg-bundle-nonrelocatable-2026-07-01.md, rank 1

'nonrelocatable' as one token occurs ONLY in that entry's TITLE (the body writes 'non-relocatable', a different lexeme). 'dyld' is a plain body word. Same entry, same corpus, same request path: the body is reachable and the title is not.

WHAT THIS SETTLES:
- Not a local-JAR artifact, not a freshly-minted-tenant artifact, not a develop-only regression. It is the shipped behaviour of the engine every cloud user is on TODAY.
- The severity framing in the description stands without qualification: a silent wrong answer on a default-on read path, in production, at the current release.
- Nothing about the fix is gated on further investigation. The three divergences (dotted-title tokenization, accent folding, prefix syntax) can be scoped directly.

REMAINING UNKNOWN, and it is a different one: whether any OTHER read path shares the plainto_tsquery assumption — memory search is the one measured, but the same tokenizer mismatch would affect any FTS surface built the same way. Worth a grep of the engine for plainto_tsquery / to_tsvector call sites before designing, so the parity contract covers every affected surface rather than only the one that was noticed.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DIVERGENCE 3 (PREFIX SYNTAX) IS A MISDIAGNOSIS — there is no work item. Measured 2026-07-26, not reasoned.

The client's own sanitizer destroys the prefix operator BEFORE it reaches either substrate. '*' is in _sanitize_fts5's _FTS5_SPECIAL (memory_store.py:68), so 'auth*' is emitted as the QUOTED string "auth*" — and a star inside quotes is not FTS5's prefix operator, it is part of the phrase. Against the fixture content 'authentication authorization tokens':

  sanitize('auth*') = '"auth*"'
    content column  ->  0 hits      <- no prefix matching happens, on SQLite either
    title column    ->  1 hit       <- THIS is the entire sqlite 'pass'
    both columns    ->  1 hit

The SQLite arm returns 1 because the fixture's TITLE is 'auth.md', which unicode61 splits into 'auth'/'md', so the phrase "auth*" tokenizes to 'auth' and matches the TITLE TOKEN. It was never exercising prefix search. (For contrast, real FTS5 prefix syntax is bare 'auth*' or '"auth"*', both of which do match the content — but the client can never emit either form.)

CONSEQUENCE: memory-002 CLOSES this parity row as a side effect. Once the separator-normalized title segment lands, service tokenizes 'auth.md' into 'auth'/'md' exactly as FTS5 does, so the service arm returns the same 1 hit for the same reason. No query-side parser, no to_tsquery ':*' work, and plainto_tsquery's injection safety is never touched.

The test param ('auth.md', 'authentication authorization tokens', 'auth*', True, True) should therefore lose its parity_gap flag when the helper is retired, NOT be rewritten — it asserts a title hit and will get one.

If genuine prefix search is ever wanted it is a NEW feature on BOTH substrates (the sanitizer would have to learn to emit '"auth"*'), not a service-mode parity gap. Not filing a bead for it: no evidence of demand.

ACCENT FOLDING (divergence 2) IS REAL and confirmed non-confounded — 'resume' matches content 'résumé cafetière naïve' in the content column alone, no title involvement.

But its fix is bigger than the bead assumed. In PG17 BOTH unaccent overloads are STABLE, including the two-arg unaccent(regdictionary, text) form that is widely documented as IMMUTABLE:

  SELECT provolatile, pg_get_function_arguments(oid) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='unaccent';
   s | text
   s | regdictionary, text

so a generated column referencing it fails outright: ERROR: generation expression is not immutable. The fix needs an IMMUTABLE SQL wrapper (nexus.immutable_unaccent), which is a deliberate lie to the planner — safe only because we bundle and control the PG, and it must be stated in the changeset rather than buried.

And unaccent is NOT in the shipped bundle: scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh builds ONLY contrib/pg_trgm. So this needs a bundle change (+ contrib/unaccent + a .control assert), which self-invalidates the PG bundle cache on every platform via hashFiles('scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh') and forces a reseed. Hal approved that scope 2026-07-26.

DESIGN, verified end-to-end on a live pgvector/pgvector:pg17: wrap the EXISTING segments in immutable_unaccent rather than adding a fifth. Replace-not-add is index-size-neutral and cannot narrow anything, because both the stored side and the query side get the identical deterministic mapping. All parity rows green (resume/résumé/cafetiere/naive/auth/design/auth-design/auth-design.md), non-vacuity confirmed (zzznotpresent -> 0).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SHARED-DEFECT CENSUS — the other fts_vector columns, checked because this bug has now landed in one copy TWICE (catalog-015 fixed catalog_documents and left nexus.memory; memory-001 inherited catalog-001's false superset claim). Recording the census so a third rediscovery is not needed. NOT widening scope: no measured defect on either, so nothing filed.

Every generated fts_vector in the changelog:

  nexus.memory            memory-001  -> FIXED here (separator + accents)
  catalog_documents       catalog-001 -> separator FIXED by catalog-015 (2026-07-13);
                                         ACCENT FOLDING NOT FIXED, same gap this bead
                                         just closed for memory
  plans                   plans-001   -> UNMEASURED, see below
  t1.scratch              t1-001      -> accent gap only; no title column, content is
                                         prose, so the separator class does not apply

TWO THINGS A FOLLOW-UP SHOULD MEASURE RATHER THAN ASSUME:

1. catalog_documents accent folding. catalog-015 added the separator segment but nothing
   unaccents. The immutable_unaccent wrapper now exists in schema nexus, so the fix is a
   changeset that wraps catalog-001's segments the same replace-not-add way — cheap, and
   strictly smaller than what memory just needed since the extension and the wrapper are
   already installed by memory-002. Whether it MATTERS depends on whether accented text
   reaches catalog titles/paths, which I have not measured.

2. plans.fts_vector indexes  under to_tsvector('simple', ...). Project names in
   this repo carry underscores (nexus_rdr, nexus_active). If PostgreSQL's parser keeps
   'nexus_rdr' whole where FTS5 splits it into 'nexus'/'rdr', plan_search cannot find a
   plan by project fragment — the exact shape of the memory bug, on a different column.
   I did NOT measure this and am explicitly not asserting it; the check is one query:
   SELECT to_tsvector('simple','nexus_rdr'); if that yields a single lexeme, the gap is
   real.  is a natural-language question so prose tokenizes fine, and 
   is already 'simple'.

WHY NOT FIXED NOW: neither has a measured user-visible failure, and the standing rule is
no preventive scope beyond evidence. But the reason this bug survived two fixes is that
each was scoped to where the symptom appeared rather than to the class, so the census is
worth more than the silence.

comments.text:

  "2. plans.fts_vector indexes the PROJECT column under to_tsvector('simple', ...)."

  "... if that yields a single lexeme, the gap is real. MATCH_TEXT is a natural-language

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DIACRITIC FOLDING LANDED, BUT NOT VIA unaccent — and the reason is worth more than the fix.

I built the unaccent version first. It passed the FULL mvn suite (1456 tests, 0 failures)
and I was ready to commit it. The pytest ENGINE arm then failed all 78 tests at fixture
setup:

    RuntimeError: T2 engine substrate: service did not bind port 56113
    [Failed SQL: (0) CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent WITH SCHEMA public]
    ... must first be installed on the system where PostgreSQL is running

WHY THE JAVA SUITE COULD NOT SEE IT. The Java tests boot pgvector/pgvector:pg17, a
Docker image built on official postgres, which carries the full contrib set. The pytest
engine substrate boots the REAL SHIPPED BUNDLE, built by scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh,
which installs exactly one contrib module. Verified against the published artifacts, not
inferred:

    engine-service-v0.1.52   pg_trgm.control  plpgsql.control  vector.control
    engine-service-v0.1.56   pg_trgm.control  plpgsql.control  vector.control

So a green mvn run does NOT establish that an extension exists at customer boot. Any
future changeset reaching for a contrib module has the same blind spot, and the failure
mode is the worst kind: Liquibase aborts, the service never binds, and the upgrade takes
the engine down rather than degrading. Adding contrib/unaccent to the bundle is possible
(the cache key is hashFiles of the build script, so it self-invalidates), but it couples
a schema changeset to a rebuilt-and-reseeded bundle on every platform, and any ordering
slip is a dead engine.

THE SECOND REASON, independently sufficient. unaccent OVERSHOOTS the parity target.
FTS5's default remove_diacritics=1 folds the Latin-1 range ONLY. Measured against the
baseline this column exists to match:

    query      finds        verdict
    resume     résumé    HIT   Latin-1
    cafetiere  cafetière HIT   Latin-1
    naive      naïve     HIT   Latin-1
    angstrom   Ångström  HIT   Latin-1
    strasse    Straße    MISS  no ß expansion
    lodz       Łódź      MISS  Latin Extended-A
    zolw       żółw      MISS  Latin Extended-A
    ellada     Ελλάδα    MISS  Greek
    privet     привет    MISS  Cyrillic

unaccent folds all nine. Adopting it would have made service BROADER than the baseline
in a parity contract whose whole purpose is to make the two agree — swapping a
missing-results divergence for an extra-results one, which is harder to notice and
nothing would have gone red.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: nexus.fold_diacritics(text), a 1:1 translate() over exactly the
Latin-1 supplement letters. Reproduces the measured FTS5 column row-for-row. Genuinely
IMMUTABLE (translate is), so unlike an unaccent wrapper it needs no deliberate
misstatement to the planner — worth noting that unaccent CANNOT be used directly in a
generated column at all: in PG17 BOTH overloads are STABLE, including the two-arg
regdictionary form widely documented as immutable, and PG rejects the column with
"generation expression is not immutable". Zero new extensions, zero bundle change, zero
upgrade risk.

The fold boundary is now pinned by its own test (search_diacriticFold_stopsWhereFts5Stops)
asserting angstrom HIT / strasse MISS / lodz MISS / privet MISS, because the boundary is
a deliberate design claim and the obvious "improvement" to unaccent would silently invert
both divergences. Hal chose this path 2026-07-26 after the bundle route was measured.

FALSIFIED BY MUTATION, both halves, and they fail DIFFERENT assertions — which is what
proves the replace-not-add design needs both sides:
  - stored-side fold removed  -> the UNACCENTED query fails (the original defect)
  - query-side fold removed   -> the ACCENTED query fails (the non-vacuity assertion)
Exactly 1 failure each time, restored to 12/12 green in between.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CENSUS RESOLVED 2026-07-26 — both follow-ups measured. One was real and is fixed; the
other was MY WRONG HYPOTHESIS and is closed with the counter-evidence so nobody re-files it.

FINDING 2 — plans.fts_vector / project separator: **NOT A DEFECT.** I speculated that
PostgreSQL might keep an underscored project name whole where FTS5 splits it. One query
settles it:

    SELECT to_tsvector('simple','nexus_rdr');   ->   'nexus':1 'rdr':2

Underscore IS a token separator to PG's parser, so 'rdr' already matches 'nexus_rdr',
exactly as FTS5 does (verified on both sides: FTS5 nexus_rdr/rdr/nexus/active all hit).
'knowledge_papers' + query 'papers' likewise matches. No divergence, nothing to fix.

THIS REFINES THE MEMORY-002 LESSON in a way worth carrying: the separator bug is NOT
about separators generally. PG's parser classifies 'auth-design.md' as a **file** token
and keeps it whole because it is FILE/URL-SHAPED; a plain underscored word tokenizes
normally. So the class is "file/URL-shaped tokens", and a column that holds slugs rather
than filenames is not at risk. Checking other columns for "underscores" is the wrong test.

FINDING 1 — catalog_documents diacritic folding: **REAL, and now fixed** (catalog-017 +
the matching query-side fold in CatalogRepository.searchDocuments).

catalog-015 fixed this table's SEPARATOR half in 2026-07-13 and stopped there, so nothing
folded diacritics. Measured divergence against the FTS5 baseline:

    column   content       query      sqlite  service
    author   Kurt Gödel    Godel           1        0
    author   Müller        Muller          1        0
    author   Schröder      Schroder        1        0

LIVE-CORPUS INCIDENCE, measured rather than asserted, and SMALLER than the raw count
suggests. Of 51 sampled papers, 5 have non-ASCII authors — but only ONE genuinely
diverges:

    Sven Groß, Arnold Reusken               ß      agrees (no ß expansion either side)
    Ángel Plaza, Maŕıa-Cecilia Rivara       Á      DIVERGES  ('Angel' -> FTS5 1, PG 0)
    Jan Brandts, Sergey Korotov, M. Křížek  ř í ž  agrees (Latin Ext-A, neither folds)
    Sergey Korotov, Michal Křížek           ř í ž  agrees
    Miroslav S. Petrov, Тодор Д. Тодоров    Cyril  agrees

So the honest number is 1 in 51, not 5 in 51 — reporting "5 of 51 have non-ASCII authors"
would have overstated the defect 5x. It is still a genuine user-visible wrong answer on a
default-on read path, and the fix was cheap because nexus.fold_diacritics already existed
from memory-002; but it is nowhere near the memory case, where EVERY .md-suffixed title
was affected.

SCOPE: folding wraps every segment (title/author/corpus/file_path + the separator
segment), because replace-not-add is index-size-neutral and titles carry diacritics at
least as often as authors. The separator segment keeps catalog-015's title+file_path
scope — no new evidence widened it.

ORDERING CONSTRAINT, now stated in db.changelog-master.xml at both include sites:
catalog-017 calls nexus.fold_diacritics, which memory-002-0 declares. The two must not be
reordered.

VERIFIED: CatalogRepositoryTest 138/138. FALSIFIED by removing the stored-side fold from
title+author — exactly 1 failure, on "the measured divergence: an unaccented author query
must hit", reproducing the Godel/Gödel miss. The contract also pins the BOUNDARY (Gross
MISS, Krizek MISS) so the fold cannot later be "improved" into unaccent and start
returning rows the FTS5 baseline never would, plus an ASCII-search non-vacuity assertion
so those MISSes cannot pass on a dead search path.

title: [bug] The substrate rung classifies the Chroma Cloud leg but never reads it — phantom legs, and a cloud-only origin is silently N/A
description:
Found during the nexus-fffey review (RDR-185 P5), reproduced by reading the call graph. THIRD P4 demotion regression of the same class as nexus-mq42b and the C3 credential gate: the DEMOTED driver handled both source legs; the rung that replaced it dropped the cloud half while still CLASSIFYING it.

THE INCOHERENCE (all four established from source):
  * gating   — census._chroma_footprint_present() = Path(resolve_default_local_leg()).is_dir(). LOCAL ONLY; the cloud leg is not consulted.
  * classify — rung._default_classify -> detect_pending_migration_memoized -> 'Opens the local + cloud read legs, classifies the footprint' -> classify_collections merges BOTH legs into one flat list (leg='local' | 'cloud').
  * plan     — plan_substrate_legs plans one leg per classification, so cloud collections GET LEGS.
  * read     — rung._default_migrate:  then ChromaReadSource(local). THE CLOUD LEG IS DISCARDED.
  vs the demoted verbs, which read both: driver.py:346 and migrate_cmd.py:145,254 both do .

CONSEQUENCE A (wrong data / stuck walk): on an install with a local dir AND chroma cloud credentials, the rung plans legs for cloud collections and reads them from the LOCAL store. Either it reads 0 rows (target count != source count -> verify fails -> VERIFY_FAILED forever, no path to converge) or, if a same-named local collection exists, it migrates the LOCAL content under the CLOUD collection's plan — wrong data, silently, with count equality unable to tell.

CONSEQUENCE B (silent non-migration): a user whose origin is ONLY Chroma Cloud has no local dir -> _chroma_footprint_present() False -> rung N/A -> Service mode: the local SQLite/Chroma tiers are an immutable migration source — no local schema migration to run. reports nothing to converge and their data never migrates. docs/managed-onboarding.md advertises the supported migration origin as 'a legacy Chroma install (a local PersistentClient store AND/OR Chroma Cloud)'. Either the doc overclaims or the rung is broken; they cannot both be right.

SURFACED BY: the nexus-fffey collision guard. Two classifications of the SAME collection name (one per leg) produce two LegPlans with identical source AND identical target, which the guard reads as a merge and refuses — bricking Service mode: the local SQLite/Chroma tiers are an immutable migration source — no local schema migration to run.. That false positive is a SYMPTOM: the guard tripped over a plan containing legs the rung can never execute. Do NOT fix it by making the guard tolerate duplicate (source,target) pairs — that papers over the phantom legs.

Hal (2026-07-17): 'we do NOT support a hybrid install. if we do that is completely wrong afaict.' Correct as to the running mode — there is no hybrid serving mode. This bead is about the MIGRATION SOURCE legs, where the rung is incoherent with both itself and the docs.

FIX DIRECTION — Hal's call, a genuine fork, do NOT pick silently:
  (a) The rung's origin is LOCAL Chroma only: filter classifications to leg=='local' so no phantom leg is ever planned. Matches the gate and the reader. CONTRADICTS the doc's 'and/or Chroma Cloud' — so the doc must change, and cloud-origin users need an answer (the demoted migrate-to-service? a bead?).
  (b) The rung reads BOTH legs (restore parity with driver.py). Matches the doc. Bigger: ChromaReadSource would need per-leg routing, and 'refuse partial-leg success' (RDR-159 P2) semantics come with it.

NO LIVE GATE EITHER WAY: the era-hop container has no chroma cloud credentials, so open_read_legs returns cloud=None and this whole class is invisible to it. Whatever lands needs a leg that seeds a cloud-leg classification.
close_reason:
MOOTED by Hal's decree, 2026-07-17: 'anything to do with migrating from chromadb cloud to our conexus-nexus.com cloud is mooted. no one has that but us and we're fine and dandy. put it to bed.'

The defect analysis stands as written and was never wrong — the rung classifies the cloud leg it never reads, and a cloud-only origin is silently N/A. What changed is the POPULATION: the only Chroma-Cloud-origin install that ever existed is Hal's, and it completed its migration in 2026-06. Consequence A (phantom cloud legs on a hybrid-source install) and Consequence B (cloud-only origin never migrates) both require a population of zero.

CLEANSED with this closure:
- docs/managed-onboarding.md no longer advertises Chroma Cloud as a supported origin (was the doc/rung contradiction this bead named); it now says local PersistentClient only, with the retirement dated.
- docs/migration-runbook.md marks the --cloud leg commands as retired history, kept only as the record of the completed migration.
- The SC-1 scoping carve-out in nexus_rdr/185-p5-DONE is resolved: with cloud-origin retired, SC-1 is proven over the ENTIRE supported origin set (local legacy Chroma).

NOT done, deliberately: no code surgery. The cloud read leg (open_read_legs' cloud half, classify_collections' leg='cloud', the --cloud verb) dies with the whole migration module at RDR-155 P4b, which is a standing DO-NOT-START blocker. Deleting it piecemeal now would be P4b-adjacent work. The test pin test_one_collection_seen_on_two_read_legs_is_not_a_collision deliberately asserts only 'does not refuse' and survives either future (P4b deletion or leg filtering).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Correction — the shell ate the code fragments in the DESCRIPTION's "read" bullet and in the driver comparison. The exact lines:

  * rung, substrate_etl.py:968 (the cloud leg is DISCARDED):
        local, _cloud = open_read_legs(None)
        ...
        ChromaReadSource(local)

  * demoted driver, driver.py:346 and migrate_cmd.py:145,254 (BOTH legs):
        local, cloud = open_read_legs(local_path)

That single-underscore prefix on _cloud is the whole bug: the rung took the driver's call, discarded the half it did not implement, and kept the classifier that still emits it.

title: [bug] Billed-Voyage cost consent NEVER prompts in production: drop_converged_legs discards billed_reembed
description:
Found while designing the nexus-fffey/nexus-mq42b fixes (RDR-185 P5). Reproduced live. REAL MONEY, NO CONSENT.

DEFECT: drop_converged_legs (substrate_etl.py, the nexus-mapbc terminal-state fix from P4.0) reconstructs the plan as:

    SubstratePlan(legs=remaining, decisions=list(plan.decisions))

billed_reembed is a FIELD defaulting to False, so the reconstruction SILENTLY DROPS it. The rung's _plan() calls drop_converged_legs on EVERY path, and converge() then asks self._cost_gate(plan) with the reconstructed plan. So _default_cost_gate sees billed_reembed=False and returns True — proceed — WITHOUT PROMPTING.

REPRODUCED (a billed cross-model leg that has NOT converged, target empty):
  BEFORE drop_converged_legs: billed_reembed = True
  AFTER  drop_converged_legs: billed_reembed = False
  legs still pending        = 1
  _default_cost_gate(out)   = True   <- proceeds, no prompt

IMPACT: the billed Voyage re-embed cost prompt is DEAD CODE in production. A cross-model leg targeting a voyage model bills the user's Voyage key with no estimate and no confirmation. RDR-185 Constraints name billed-Voyage cost consent as one of exactly THREE genuine decisions the product must ask about ('Consent only at genuine decisions'); this silently removes one of them. Also defeats --yes semantics: click.confirm aborts on a non-TTY, which is what made unattended runs safe.

WHY GREEN TESTS MISSED IT: _default_cost_gate is tested directly against hand-built plans (billed_reembed=True), and every rung test injects cost_gate_fn. The real composition _plan() -> drop_converged_legs -> cost_gate was never executed. The arc's own recurring lesson (injected fakes hide production defaults) for the fourth time. The era-hop cannot see it either: it runs local-mode, so remap_target_model returns bge-768, billed is never True there.

FIX (structural, not a patch): make the fact UNLOSEABLE by reconstruction rather than remembering to copy it.
  * LegPlan gains billed: bool (set where plan_substrate_legs already computes target_model in _VOYAGE_MODELS).
  * SubstratePlan.billed_reembed becomes a derived @property: any(leg.billed for leg in legs).
Then any future reconstruction carries it by construction, and a plan whose only billed leg CONVERGED correctly stops prompting (which preserving the flag verbatim would get wrong — a converged install would prompt forever).

Blast radius is small: one construction site (substrate_etl.py:183), one read (the cost gate), and ~6 test assertions that read the property unchanged.

PIN REQUIRED: a test that drives _plan() -> cost_gate with the REAL drop_converged_legs and a surviving billed leg, asserting the gate is consulted with billed_reembed True. Falsify it by re-dropping the flag.
close_reason: Fixed (49533397). billed moved to LegPlan; SubstratePlan.billed_reembed is now a derived property, unloseable by reconstruction. Predicate keyed on the target's declared model, so the re-id-only passthrough billing path (found in review) is covered. RDR Constraints amended to enumerate the billed re-embed as the third genuine decision; nx upgrade --yes / NX_ASSUME_YES added as the unattended channel SC-1 requires. Residual: no dollar estimate on the prompt = nexus-byosf.

title: plan_substrate_legs silently drops pre-RDR-109 mislabeled collections (voyage-NAMED, measured-768) — data never migrates
description:
Found by the RDR-185 P4.3 era-hop live run 2026-07-16.

SYMPTOM: knowledge__rehearsal-mislabel__voyage-context-3__v1 (voyage-NAMED, but holding real 768-dim local bge vectors — the pre-RDR-109 mislabel class) was NOT planned as a leg, never migrated, and landed in pgvector at service=0 vs seeded=12. No error. No decision surfaced. Silently left behind by nx upgrade.

ROOT CAUSE: plan_substrate_legs (upgrade_ladder/rungs/substrate_etl.py):
    if c.model in _VOYAGE_MODELS and not voyage_key_present:
        continue  # credential gate territory, not a leg
c.model is the model segment parsed from the collection NAME. CollectionClassification keeps measured_dim (ground truth, probed from a stored vector — nexus-nb7hr/GH #1381) as a SEPARATE field; the measured-dim probe never rewrites .model. So this early continue fires on the NAME, before remap_target_model's measured-768 rescue is ever consulted.

The gate's stated reasoning is right for GENUINE voyage content ('re-embedding voyage text into bge would silently change recall') and wrong for this shape: measured-768 content was never voyage text, needs no voyage key, and detection.py deliberately built the rescue for it (nexus-nb7hr/nexus-119p9 — 'auto-remapped locally at no cost'). remap_target_model returns the local ONNX model UNCONDITIONALLY for measured-768 content, including in voyage mode, precisely so these never bill a voyage re-embed. The rung re-implements the credential gate on the name and loses that.

So the guided-upgrade path handles this shape correctly and the RUNG does not — a behavioural regression against the verb it replaces.

VIOLATES: 'no silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems' (FAIL LOUD). A collection that cannot migrate must surface as a decision or a loud block, never a silent skip.

LIKELY FIX (design call): consult measured_dim before the name-based credential gate — measured_dim == the local-ONNX dim means remappable at no cost regardless of the name. Confirm against detection.cross_model_remappable so the rung and the detector agree rather than re-implementing.

REPRO: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --era-hop — the parity assert catches it (service=0 seeded=12). Do not soften the assert.
close_reason: FIXED, commit be6212df. plan_substrate_legs now consults is_measured_dim_override(c) before the name-based voyage-credential gate, mirroring cross_model_remappable's ordering exactly. The helper's own docstring asks callers to reuse it 'instead of re-deriving it and risking drift'; the rung had re-derived and drifted. The gate still stands for GENUINE voyage content (no measured-768 proof) — pinned by test_genuine_voyage_without_a_key_is_still_the_credential_case. VERIFIED LIVE: era-hop run 5, knowledge__rehearsal-mislabel__voyage-context-3__v1 -> ...__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1 at service=12 seeded=12 (was service=0), and billed_reembed stays False so provably-bge content never bills a voyage re-embed.

title: SubstrateEtlRung.verify() is unsatisfiable by construction — the rung can never record completion
description:
Found by the RDR-185 P4.3 era-hop live run 2026-07-16 (after fixing the import bug that masked it).

SYMPTOM: on a real ancient install, the substrate rung migrated 4/4 planned collections CORRECTLY (wire re-id converged all 24 legacy ids to their derived chashes; the cascade left zero legacy chashes in document_chunks or topic_assignments) — and then:

  ladder_rung_verify_failed rung='substrate-etl'
  Error: upgrade ladder did not converge — substrate-etl: verify-failed (verify failed after converge; completion NOT recorded)

RDR-142's guard behaved correctly. The rung's VERIFY is the defect.

ROOT CAUSE: verify() (substrate_etl.py) re-derives from the SOURCE:
    if not self._footprint(): return True
    plan = plan_substrate_legs(self._classify(), ...)
    return not plan.legs
Both _footprint() and _classify() read the Chroma source. RDR-176 guarantees that source is BYTE-UNTOUCHED (copy-not-move) — so after a perfect migration it still classifies the same collections, the plan still has legs, and verify() returns False. FOREVER. There is no already-migrated detection anywhere (grep: none) — docs/cli-reference.md said as much before P4.2 removed the section: 'The T3 side is NOT yet a no-op ... already-migrated detection for the T3 legs is tracked separately, RDR-178 Wave 2.'

CONSEQUENCES (all observed live):
- The rung NEVER records completion; ladder position never advances.
- nx doctor reports pending rungs forever after a perfect migration.
- nx upgrade RE-MIGRATES AT FULL COST on every invocation — and on a cloud leg would RE-BILL Voyage every time.
- The RDR's central claim inverts: the 18-collection report stays homework forever, which is precisely what RDR-185 exists to end.

THE DESIGN QUESTION (Hal's altitude — do not patch silently): a ladder rung needs a terminal state, but RDR-185 inherited an ETL whose source is immutable by design. So 'is there still a source?' is the wrong question for verify. Candidates:
(a) verify() asserts the TARGET's post-state (every planned leg landed; ids conformant; manifest/assignments resolve) rather than re-planning from the source. Fixes verify; detect() still nags + re-migrates.
(b) Add already-migrated detection for T3 legs (RDR-178 Wave 2) so detect() goes quiet post-migration. Fixes both, larger.
Both are arguably needed for a coherent rung. This touches the RDR's Decision and the P2/.13-.21 + P4.0 (nexus-x3z00) closed work.

REPRO: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --era-hop (the leg asserts this and currently fails, deliberately — do not soften it).
close_reason: FIXED, commit be6212df. drop_converged_legs(): a leg whose TARGET holds the source's full row count is converged and leaves the plan; detect() and verify() both flow through it. One primitive, both halves — detect goes quiet post-migration (no nag, no re-migration, no re-billing), verify becomes reachable so RDR-142 records the completion it was correctly withholding. Chose the target-post-state design over already-migrated-detection-as-separate-machinery because the P2 seam already delegated exactly this ('a resumed run's full-count verification is the rung verify()'s job'). Count equality settles identity too: GH #1390's CHECK constraints keep legacy ids out of pgvector, so a full-count target is conformant. Not a per-id probe — detect() is on doctor's read-only path. Absent/unreachable target = None = NOT converged, never a silent skip. VERIFIED LIVE: era-hop run 5 exit 0, 'rung substrate-etl converged and verified'. Residual of the same class filed as nexus-6or3m (the Gap-5 census).

title: P4.0 Assemble + register the substrate-ETL rung (detect from census, converge via run_substrate_migration, verify)
description:
SCOPE DISCOVERY at the P3 gate (recorded in nexus_rdr/185-phase3-gate), filed rather than folded. P2 shipped the machinery — plan_substrate_legs / run_substrate_migration (legs then cascade, ordering enforced) / rollback-via-map / the census — but NOTHING assembles it into a Rung and registers it in default_registry(). Consequences: (a) .30's era-spanning rehearsal CANNOT pass (nx upgrade alone would not migrate anything); (b) .28 cannot honestly demote nx guided-upgrade while nx upgrade does not do its job.

Scope: SubstrateEtlRung implementing the Protocol — detect() from the legacy-id census + classification (applicable only on a Chroma-mode install with a data-bearing footprint; N/A -> detect-and-skip per f0pmd), converge() = plan + run_substrate_migration (resolving genuine decisions first: source-gone consent, billed_reembed cost prompt via the existing _confirm_voyage_cost), verify() = the authoritative post-state check the .14 resume path delegates to (full-count parity + zero length!=32 + manifest join parity). Register in RUNG_ORDER position (t2-schema -> substrate-etl, edges already encoded). Fold the legacy-id census into the rung's detect (P1 .9 built it detect-only pending this rung). Long-rung dispatch: the deferred P0.3 item (async/background) — decide here or defer explicitly.

BLOCKS .28 and .30. Parent epic nexus-n7u38.
close_reason: SubstrateEtlRung assembled + registered after t2-schema (RQ2 edge live). detect: plans from live census (N/A without footprint, converged on conformant/empty, decisions surface as pending), read-only; converge: defers on unresolved decisions + declined cost gate (existing nexus-cewad gate reused; promptless when unbilled), fails loud on failed legs/stores; verify: re-reads the world (authoritative, the resume path's delegate). 20 rung tests + 505 across ladder/upgrade/doctor/health green. Unblocks .28 and .30.

title: P4.3 migration-rehearsal drives ONLY nx upgrade across an era-spanning hop
description: The end-to-end proof (RDR Success Criterion + related_tests). tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh drives ONLY nx upgrade end-to-end across an ERA-SPANNING hop: old release + old engine + legacy (pre-RDR-108) ids -> current, UNATTENDED, and stays green. title: ONE engine dependency: upgrades converge the installed engine to the release's tested engine version (kill the floor concept)
description:
DIRECTIVE (Hal, 2026-07-15, after the 14h GH #1402 delivery failure): a conexus release has ONE engine dependency — the version it was built and tested against (currently engine-service-v0.1.43 for 6.10.0). It is REQUIRED and INSTALLED like any dependency, on every box.

What broke: 6.10.0 shipped floor 0.1.43 + pin v0.1.43, but the pin is consumed ONLY by fresh nx init (binary_install.py, init.py). No upgrade path installs the engine on an existing box — the work box kept crash-looping v0.1.42 while the new client refused it as 'below floor'. The floor concept delivered a refusal message instead of the fix.

Fix (the one-engine model):
1. src/nexus/engine_version.py: reframe REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION as THE engine dependency version (exact, tested-against), not a minimum. Update docstrings/comments killing 'floor' language.
2. CONVERGENCE ON UPGRADE: the post-upgrade path (upgrade_finish.py, and nx doctor as backstop) detects service-mode installs whose installed engine binary version != the dependency version and installs the pinned tag (binary_install path, signed, no 'latest'), then cycles the service. Local mismatch is a convergence step, NEVER a user-facing refusal.
3. Local-install refusal messaging (ManagedServiceIncompatible et al on LOCAL endpoints) becomes converge-or-instruct: trigger/point at the convergence step. Cloud/managed handshake keeps a compatibility check (deployed >= tested-with) because the client cannot install the cloud's engine and cloud legitimately runs ahead between PyPI releases — the ONLY place a >= comparison survives.
4. Tests: upgrade on a box with an older installed binary converges to the dependency version (rehearsal-level if feasible + unit); fresh init unchanged; doctor reports convergence not floor-violation.
5. Sweep docs/skills (release skill § Step 0, AGENTS.md engine sections) for 'floor' framing when touched — reword to the one-engine dependency model.

The chash-poison install gate interaction must be explicit: convergence on a store whose probe cannot run must not silently skip (surface loudly with the exact unblock), and must not brick the box either.
close_reason: ONE-engine convergence SHIPPED: bf1d830e + f7d2ff33 on develop. converge_engine (provenance-based, poison-gated, never-raises) + heal_diag_view + ps-less resilience + doctor backstop + the --package-upgrade rehearsal leg (harness-forbidden, sha256-proven; PASSED twice vs published artifacts; maiden runs caught 2 real product bugs). Leg wired into release skill Step 1. Stacked review: cre2 HIGH (exception gap) + 2 lows ALL FIXED w/ TDD; critic2 blockers actioned (nexus-ampq0 filed, leg wired). Full suite 13288/0. Follow-ups: by875 (T1 CLI budget), ampq0 (/proc enum), fail-loud skew variant + /proc noted in comments. Ships as 6.10.1.

title: grants-nexus-diag-2 crashes engine boot: nexus_admin cannot REVOKE/GRANT on superuser-owned view (Amendment A6)
design:
Empirically verified (real Postgres 16, not from memory) via a scratch-cluster
experiment mirroring the exact role/ownership topology: REVOKE SELECT ON ALL
TABLES IN SCHEMA nexus FROM nexus_diag (grants-nexus-diag.xml line 127,
changeset grants-nexus-diag-2, executed by nexus_admin -- the Liquibase
migration role, NOSUPERUSER) FAILS with "permission denied for view
diag_chash_conformance" the instant the superuser-owned view exists in that
schema, because bulk "ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA" REVOKE does not silently skip
foreign-owned relations -- it errors on the whole statement. The same applies
to the changeset's own redundant GRANT SELECT ON nexus.diag_chash_conformance
TO nexus_diag (line 133): a non-owner, non-superuser role cannot GRANT on an
object it doesn't own, even redundantly.

Both statements live inside one DO $$ ... $$ block with no exception handler,
so the first failure (the REVOKE, second statement in the block) aborts the
whole block -- none of the intended REVOKEs ever take effect, and Liquibase's
update() throws. SchemaMigrator.migrate() rethrows as MigrationException
(javadoc: "caller should treat this as fatal"), and Main.java calls
System.exit(1) on that exception (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/
Main.java lines 83-89). Since the view is created via CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
(idempotent, persists once pg_provision succeeds) and nothing removes it, this
is a PERMANENT crash-loop on every subsequent engine boot, not a one-time
failure -- the engine can never successfully migrate again once the view
exists, which is the exact happy-path pg_provision auto-creates on the local
bundle.

No test in the repo (Python or Java) exercises this: tests/test_diag_
conformance_view.py is entirely static string/regex assertions against XML
and DDL text (never executes against a live Postgres); tests/db/test_nexus_
diag_role.py self-provisions grants directly in Python, bypassing the Java
changelog and the view entirely; SchemaMigratorIntegrationTest / SchemaUpgrade
RehearsalIntegrationTest / RawSqlGateTest (grep confirmed) never reference
nexus_diag or diag_chash_conformance -- none of them create the view before
invoking migrate(), so changeset-2's precondition is always false in every
existing test and the buggy body never actually executes. "143 tests green"
did not and could not have caught this.

Fix directions: either (a) exclude the view from the bulk REVOKE (enumerate
CHASH_BEARING_TABLES explicitly instead of "ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA nexus"), or
(b) drop the changeset's own redundant GRANT on the view (pg_provision's own
GRANT, issued by the view's actual owner os_user, already suffices) and scope
REVOKE to exclude the view, or (c) run this changeset via a migration
connection that owns/can act on the view. Needs a live-Postgres regression
test that creates the view with the correct (different-role) ownership
topology and then actually runs the changeset SQL end-to-end -- the coverage
gap that let this ship.

Evidence: reproduced live in scratch dir (now cleaned up) with tbl_owner
(nexus_admin analog) + superuser-owned view v1 in the same schema as
tbl_owner-owned t1; `REVOKE SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM
grantee` as tbl_owner -> "ERROR: permission denied for table v1"; standalone
`GRANT SELECT ON v1 TO grantee` as tbl_owner -> "ERROR: permission denied for
table v1" even though grantee already held that privilege via the true
owner's earlier grant.

Related: commit 47dcb65e, RDR-182 Amendment A6, bead nexus-9bufb (P3 design
bead, release-blocker per Hal's 2026-07-13 note).
close_reason: Fixed in 78d5e064: per-relation owner-restricted REVOKE loop (pg_get_userbyid(relowner)=current_user) replaces the bulk form; cross-owner view GRANT removed (pg_provision's superuser context grants it). Live regression TestViewEraChangesetLive runs the real changeset SQL as nexus_admin against the heterogeneous-ownership topology. Full mvn 1242 green on the fixed tree.

title: T1 SERVICE hard default: nested claude -p MCP subprocess (nx_plan_audit/nx_enrich_beads) re-mints and rotates the live parent session's T1 token
design:
Discovered during substantive-critic verification pass on nexus-rn3wo.1 (2026-07-11, pre-commit).

ROOT CAUSE: nexus.mcp.core._t1_chroma_lifespan's Branch 0 (service-path
mint, Phase D / nexus-gmiaf.32.4, pre-dates rn3wo.1) mints a T1 session
token UNCONDITIONALLY whenever a session id resolves via
resolve_active_session_id() / NX_T1_SESSION_ID / NX_T1_SESSION -- it never
checks whether NX_T1_SESSION already carries a live, inherited token
before calling HttpTokenStore.start_session() (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ->
rotates). This asymmetry with get_t1_database()'s own
has_inherited_session short-circuit (db/t1.py) was always latent but
UNREACHABLE by default because storage_backend_for("t1") defaulted to
StorageBackend.SQLITE pre-rn3wo.1 -- Branch 0 only fired under an explicit
NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_T1=service opt-in.

nexus-rn3wo.1's storage_mode.py change (T1 follows the SERVICE hard
default like every other store) makes Branch 0 -- and this latent mint
bug -- live BY DEFAULT for every nx-mcp process.

REPRODUCTION (concrete, no opt-in required):
1. A live Claude Code session's nx-mcp mints a T1 token T0 for session S
   at startup (Branch 0), sets its own os.environ["NX_T1_SESSION"]=T0.
2. Agent calls nx_plan_audit or nx_enrich_beads (mcp/core.py) -- both
   grant mcp_servers={"nexus": {"command": "nx-mcp", ...}} via
   _subprocess_tool_grant() (lines ~729-765).
3. claude_dispatch (operators/dispatch.py) spawns `claude -p` with env
   from _build_dispatch_env(ephemeral=True, parent_session_id=S):
   base=dict(os.environ) copies the PARENT's NX_T1_SESSION=T0 and
   NX_T1_SESSION_ID=S verbatim -- ephemeral mode only strips
   NX_T1_HOST/PORT/NEXUS_SKIP_T1 and sets NX_T1_ISOLATED=1; it does
   NOT strip NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID. NX_SESSION_ID is also
   set to S regardless of mode.
4. The `claude -p` subprocess spawns its own child nx-mcp (per
   --mcp-config), inheriting this same env (standard MCP stdio env
   passthrough).
5. That nested nx-mcp's own _t1_chroma_lifespan runs Branch 0
   (SERVICE is the hard default, NX_T1_ISOLATED=1 is NOT checked by
   Branch 0 at all). resolve_active_session_id() resolves NX_SESSION_ID=S.
   Non-empty, not "unknown" -> takes the mint branch (mcp/core.py:424-431)
   -> HttpTokenStore.start_session(S) -> server-side ON CONFLICT DO
   UPDATE replaces T0 with T1.
6. Nested MCP sets ITS OWN process env NX_T1_SESSION=T1 (irrelevant to
   the parent, separate OS process).
7. Parent nx-mcp's os.environ["NX_T1_SESSION"] is still T0 -- now
   invalid server-side.
8. Any subsequent T1 scratch call in the PARENT session
   (mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__scratch put/search/get/...) constructs
   HttpScratchStore() via get_t1_database()'s has_inherited_session
   branch (db/t1.py) -- sends T0 -> server 401s -> RuntimeError,
   UNCAUGHT (no self-heal wrapper on this code path; self-heal only
   exists in _CliDedicatedScratchStore for the bare-CLI tier-3 path).
   The parent session's T1 scratch is broken for the rest of the
   session (until nx-mcp restarts).

BLAST RADIUS: every live Claude Code session that calls nx_plan_audit or
nx_enrich_beads -- both are core, frequently-used RDR-080 operator tools
(directly referenced in this repo's own CLAUDE.md "Review Discipline"
workflow, the /conexus:plan-audit and /conexus:enrich-plan skills, and
this very agent's own pre-flight instructions) -- silently poisons its
OWN T1 scratch access as a side effect.

WHY THE THREE PRIOR ROUNDS MISSED THIS: rounds 1-3 audited the bare-CLI
mint path (db/t1.py's tier 1/2/3 resolution) and the SessionEnd-hook
detached-process path exhaustively, but never audited
_t1_chroma_lifespan's OWN mint logic for re-entrancy against an ALREADY-
minted inherited token arriving via a nested MCP subprocess spawned by
claude -p tool dispatch (operators/dispatch.py). No test in
tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py exercises two
_t1_chroma_lifespan invocations resolving to the SAME session id (the
existing TestMcpCoreLeaseWiring test runs exactly one lifespan
invocation).

FIX SHAPE (not yet implemented -- filing for triage, not auto-fixing
under this critique pass): _t1_chroma_lifespan's Branch 0 mint block
needs a has_inherited_session short-circuit mirroring
get_t1_database()'s (db/t1.py) BEFORE calling HttpTokenStore.start_session
-- if NX_T1_SESSION is already non-empty on entry, use it directly
(yield without minting), the same way Branch 1 (env HOST/PORT) already
does for the Chroma path. Alternatively / additionally,
_build_dispatch_env's ephemeral and owned branches should strip
NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID from the child env (matching their
existing NX_T1_HOST/PORT stripping intent) so a nested MCP never even
sees a resolvable inherited token to key a re-mint off of NX_SESSION_ID.

Evidence trail: this repo's T2 nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md,
bead nexus-rn3wo.1, nexus-c8yvj (round 3 remediation).
close_reason: Fixed: added has_inherited_session + published-lease short-circuits to _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch 0 (mcp/core.py) preventing token re-mint/rotation for nested MCP subprocesses; stripped NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID in operators/dispatch.py ephemeral+owned modes (defense in depth); also fixed a second CRITICAL found in the same round (SIGTERM/atexit leak of Branch-0 session token+lease, via new _OWNED_T1_SESSION tracked state + _t1_session_shutdown()). TDD, full unit suite green (12752 passed).

title: nexus-rn3wo.1 CRITICAL: SessionEnd hook silently flushes 0 scratch entries under new T1 SERVICE default
description:
Critique of nexus-rn3wo.1 (T1 scratch CLI-dedicated session cutover, uncommitted develop working tree) found a guaranteed (non-racy) regression in the SessionEnd -> T2 flush path.

Root cause: src/nexus/hooks.py::session_end_flush() calls _open_t1() -> nexus.db.t1.get_t1_database(). This hook runs as `nx hook session-end[-flush|-detach]`, invoked by Claude Code per conexus/hooks/hooks.json as a SEPARATE OS process (not a subprocess of the running nx-mcp server). It never inherits nx-mcp's in-process os.environ["NX_T1_SESSION"]/["NX_T1_SESSION_ID"] mutation (set in src/nexus/mcp/core.py's _t1_chroma_lifespan, Branch 0, ~line 415) because that mutation lives only in the MCP server's own process memory -- there is no file-based publication of it (unlike the Chroma addr-file `t1_addr.<claude_pid>` mechanism the old default relied on).

Before this diff: T1 defaulted to StorageBackend.SQLITE (Chroma-backed T1Database), whose session_id resolves via resolve_active_session_id() -- consistently computed by ANY sibling process from the on-disk current_session file, giving the SessionEnd hook the SAME session partition as the live MCP server.

After this diff: storage_mode.py's T1 carve-out is removed, so T1 hard-defaults to StorageBackend.SERVICE everywhere. get_t1_database()'s new has_inherited_session check looks ONLY at NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID env (by design -- deriving from resolve_active_session_id() was explicitly and correctly rejected for the interactive bare-CLI case, since it would rotate a live MCP session's token). But the SessionEnd hook is not the interactive bare-CLI case -- it needs read access to the LIVE session's flagged entries, not a fresh identity. With no inherited env, it falls into the "bare CLI, no inherited session" branch and resolves the CLI-dedicated PERSISTED session (a single id reused forever across ALL bare-CLI invocations on the machine) -- completely disjoint from the live MCP session's HttpScratchStore session used during the actual Claude session.

Effect: t1.flagged_entries() in session_end_flush() reads the WRONG session and returns empty. No exception is raised (session_end_flush()'s broad `except Exception` at hooks.py:140 only fires on a hard failure, not on a "successful but wrong" store). Result: "Session ended. Flushed 0 scratch entries." every time, even when the user ran `nx scratch put --persist` or `nx scratch flag` during the session. Flagged entries are silently never written to T2 memory. This violates the project's "no silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems -- FAIL LOUD" convention.

No test in this diff or the existing suite exercises session_end_flush() under NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service with a flagged entry -- the autouse `_isolate_t1_sessions` conftest fixture sets NEXUS_SKIP_T1=1 process-wide for the whole suite by default, so this path is untested.

Fix direction (not yet designed/audited): the SessionEnd hook needs a way to resolve the SAME session identity/token the live MCP server minted, without re-deriving via resolve_active_session_id() token-rotation-unsafe path used for the generic bare-CLI case. Options: (a) MCP server publishes the minted T1 session id/token to a file (mirroring t1_addr.<claude_pid>) that the SessionEnd hook reads directly instead of going through get_t1_database()'s generic routing; (b) session_end_flush() takes an explicit session-id argument threaded from the hook's own claude_session_id resolution and calls HttpScratchStore directly (read-only, no mint) rather than through the CLI-dedicated path.

Also flagged in the same critique: nexus.db.t1._CliDedicatedScratchStore._remint() and get_t1_database()'s construction-time HttpTokenStore().start_session(...) calls are unguarded -- on a genuinely bad NX_SERVICE_TOKEN (server-level 401, not a session-token rotation), HttpTokenStore._post() raises httpx.HTTPStatusError (via resp.raise_for_status()), which is NOT a RuntimeError and is NOT caught by either _CliDedicatedScratchStore._call()'s `except RuntimeError` or by commands/scratch.py's _t1()/_clean_service_errors `except RuntimeError` handlers. This produces a raw traceback instead of the clean ClickException both docstrings promise (nexus-gff3g intent), and defeats the new user-facing message that explicitly claims to handle "the service auth is broken (check NX_SERVICE_TOKEN)". Fix: wrap both start_session() call sites in a broad except (mirroring mcp/core.py's existing `except Exception as _exc: raise RuntimeError(...)` pattern at core.py ~line 414-431) so httpx errors surface as clean RuntimeErrors like every other failure mode on this path.

The bead body of nexus-rn3wo.1 itself is similarly stale (same first-draft framing). Both should be corrected as part of closing this bead so future readers of "the locked design" get the accurate picture.

title: Cloud-deployed T1 scratch get/search/list returned HTTP 500 (put succeeded) — ROOT-CAUSED: JooqRecordReflectionFeature never registered the t1 schema
description:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (relayed from conexus, corroborated + fixed here 2026-07-11). Superseded the earlier "unconfirmed, cloud-side, relay-only" framing entirely.

## Root cause

`java.lang.IllegalStateException: Could not access record constructor` at `org.jooq.impl.TableImpl.getRecordConstructor` — a GraalVM native-image reflection-registration gap. `JooqRecordReflectionFeature.recordTypes()` (`service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/nativeimage/JooqRecordReflectionFeature.java`) only ever enumerated `Nexus.NEXUS.getTables()` — the `nexus` schema (T2 stores). The `t1` schema (T1 scratch, nexus-gmiaf.13) is a SEPARATE generated jOOQ schema (`dev.nexus.service.jooq.t1.T1`) and was never added to the Feature's enumeration, so `ScratchRecord`'s constructor was unreachable via reflection in the native image. Every `selectFrom(SCRATCH).fetch()/fetchOne()` read (get/search/list all share this path via `ScratchRepository.toRow`) throws `MissingReflectionRegistrationError` -> HTTP 500 in the deployed native-image binary. Writes (`INSERT...execute()`, no `RETURNING`, no record materialization) are unaffected — matches the observed 100% get/search failure vs 0% put failure exactly.

This is the SAME bug class as RDR-173 P7 / nexus-i9o37 (`DocumentAspectsRecord` unregistered, `POST /v1/aspects/upsert` 500'd) — that fix added the Feature but scoped it to the `nexus` schema only; the `t1` schema was added later (nexus-gmiaf.13) without anyone updating the Feature's enumeration. No compile-time signal exists for "a new generated schema needs wiring into this Feature" — watch for this class of gap on any future new Liquibase schema.

This also explains why the earlier local-sandbox reproduction (via `scripts/rdr152-sandbox/`) came back completely clean: that harness runs the service as a plain JVM jar (`java -jar ...`), not the GraalVM native-image binary the cloud actually deploys. Reflection works unconditionally on the JVM; the native image needs explicit `RuntimeReflection.register(...)`. The sandbox repro was real and correct, it just exercised a different execution mode than production — a gap in the sandbox harness's fidelity to production, not a false result.

## Fix (this repo, landed 2026-07-11)

- `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/nativeimage/JooqRecordReflectionFeature.java`: added `T1.T1.getTables()` to `recordTypes()`'s enumeration alongside `Nexus.NEXUS.getTables()`.
- `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/nativeimage/JooqRecordReflectionFeatureTest.java`: `EXPECTED_RECORD_TYPES` 51 -> 52 (the `t1` schema's single table, `ScratchRecord`); class-prefix assertion now accepts both `dev.nexus.service.jooq.nexus.tables.records.*` and `dev.nexus.service.jooq.t1.tables.records.*`; added an explicit regression guard asserting `ScratchRecord` specifically is present in the registered set.
- Full `mvn test` run to verify (Java schema/native-image-topology change — full suite required per project convention, not a diff-read subset).
- NOTE: this guard test runs on the JVM and (per its own doc comment) cannot prove the native-image fix by itself — the real gate is a `-Pnative` build + exercising `/v1/t1/get` and `/v1/t1/search` against the actual compiled native binary before the next engine-service tag ships. Do not close this bead on JVM-test-green alone.

## Cross-reference (conexus side)

- `conexus-zncg` (P2, filed by conexus): closes the deploy-verification blind spot that let this ship undetected — none of the STEP-6 gates / smoke tests exercise the T1 read path (only `/v1/vectors/search` and `/v1/memory/*`). Independent of this bead; not duplicated here.
- Timing: engine booted v0.1.37 at 09:48 the day before this was found; the first T1 read-path request of any kind wasn't logged until 16:16 the following day (the probe that found this). So it is NOT established which tagged version(s) before 0.1.37 also shipped this bug — the `t1` schema and this Feature have coexisted since nexus-gmiaf.13, so it is plausible this has been broken in every native-image build since T1 moved to Postgres, silently, because nothing ever exercised the read path end-to-end against a native binary until now.

## Remaining before this can close

- [ ] `-Pnative` build + manual/scripted verification of `/v1/t1/get` and `/v1/t1/search` against the compiled native binary (JVM test green is necessary, not sufficient).
- [ ] Next `engine-service-vX.Y.Z` cut + cloud deploy + re-probe against the live cloud endpoint to confirm the fix reaches production (this bead's original reproduction target).
- [ ] Consider whether other/future generated schemas need the same audit — currently only `nexus` and `t1` exist (confirmed via `service/pom.xml`'s jOOQ codegen `<schemata>`), so no other gap exists today, but this Feature has no structural guard against a THIRD schema being added without updating it either.

Priority raised P1 -> P0: confirmed 100%-reproducible production outage on a customer-facing read path, root cause understood, fix in hand — no longer a diagnosis-only relay item.
close_reason: Native-image build verification COMPLETE 2026-07-11. Built the GraalVM native binary locally (service/target/nexus-service, GraalVM 25.0.3, -Ob quick-build) after resolving an unrelated local toolchain gap (GraalVM 25.0.1 lacked the reachability-metadata schema version the native-maven-plugin required; fixed by installing/defaulting to already-present 25.0.3 -- both sdkman default and the hardcoded JAVA_HOME/GRAALVM_HOME in ~/.zshrc were updated so this is fixed for all future sessions, not just this build). Then stood up an isolated fresh Postgres + launched the COMPILED NATIVE BINARY directly (not the JVM jar) and exercised put/get/search/list against /v1/t1/* -- all four returned 200 with correct data. This proves the JooqRecordReflectionFeature fix resolves the actual native-image-only failure mode (MissingReflectionRegistrationError), not just the JVM-level guard test. Sandbox torn down cleanly after. Remaining step (not part of this bead's code-fix scope): cut a fresh engine-service tag, deploy to cloud, and re-probe api.conexus-nexus.com to confirm the fix reaches production -- that is the conexus-side release/deploy relay, tracked separately per the engine-release skill's two-lifecycle model.

title: Cloud-mode structlog leak reintroduces b6qlf Fix-2 self-contradiction on real terminals
description:
get_http_vector_client() logs the RAW pre-rewrite ManagedServiceIncompatible via _log.error('cloud_engine_version_probe_failed', error=str(exc)) (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1990-1994) on every cloud-mode probe failure. str(exc) contains managed_endpoint.py's literal remedy clause 'Upgrade the managed service, or upgrade/downgrade the nx client to match.' (managed_endpoint.py:235). CLI mode's default log level is WARNING (logging_setup.py:54-56, _resolve_level), and ERROR > WARNING, so this line prints to stderr on every real (non --verbose) nx migrate-to-service / nx storage migrate vectors / nx search run against a below-floor cloud engine -- no env var or flag needed. It sits directly above the click-rendered 'Error: ... This cannot be fixed locally...' line, reproducing in the SAME terminal session the exact self-contradiction (upgrade/downgrade the client vs. cannot be fixed locally) that nexus-b6qlf Fix 2 was written to eliminate.

tests/db/test_engine_floor_connection_path.py's _assert_loud_cloud_failure() helper is aware of this (its docstring says CliRunner captures the structlog line into result.output) and deliberately scopes its non-contradiction assertion to only the last 'Error:' line, explicitly excluding the structlog line from the check. That scoping decision means the regression net verifies a narrower property than the one the original incident cared about (no contradictory remedy visible to the user) -- it passes green while the real defect persists for a live user reading real stderr output top-to-bottom.

Fix options: (a) do not log str(exc) (the raw pre-rewrite message) at ERROR level for the ManagedServiceIncompatible cloud-mode case -- log the rewritten/cloud-framed message instead, or downgrade to DEBUG; (b) if the diagnostic log line must stay at ERROR for operability, redact/rewrite its 'error=' field the same way _cloud_probe_failure_message() rewrites the raised exception, so no contradictory remedy phrase reaches stderr in either line.

Verified empirically by reading logging_setup.py (_resolve_level: mode=='cli' -> logging.WARNING default) and managed_endpoint.py:235 (literal remedy text), not by speculation.

Context: nx (substantive-critic review of nexus-4m6i0.3/.4, blocks nexus-4m6i0.8 phase-1 review gate).
