Review Critical nexus-dizod (structlog leaking the pre-rewrite contradictory remedy to stderr) fixed at the log site and pinned by a whole-output assertion, mutation-verified. Stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic) both rounds' findings fixed.

title: Round-4 critique: _PRECONDITIONS_COVERAGE_RE ignores sqlCheck expectedResult direction — inverted-guard false accept
description:
nexus-4m6i0.2 round-4 critique (substantive-critic) found a NEW critical: the
round-4 anchoring fix (_PRECONDITIONS_COVERAGE_RE / _constraint_named_in_preconditions
in tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py) correctly rejects the
round-3 decoy classes (unrelated table, comment-only mention, typo'd conname)
but does NOT read the <sqlCheck expectedResult="N"> attribute at all
(_iter_changesets_for_validate builds preconditions_text via pc_el.itertext(),
which yields only text nodes, never attribute values). The coverage check is
purely a textual SQL-shape + constraint-name match, blind to whether the
query's expectedResult asserts EXISTENCE (correct, safe) or ABSENCE (backwards,
unsafe) of the constraint.

Empirically demonstrated (adversarial synthetic changesets against the real
analyze_changelog()):
  - <sqlCheck expectedResult="0">SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE
    conname = 'widgets_len_check'</sqlCheck> guarding a VALIDATE of
    widgets_len_check -> ZERO violations reported (i.e. treated as "covered"),
    despite the guard's real semantics being "pass only if the constraint does
    NOT exist" -- the exact inverse of what a VALIDATE guard needs.
  - Two-sqlCheck case under one <preConditions> (implicit Liquibase AND):
    one sqlCheck expectedResult=1 for a_check (correct), a second
    expectedResult=0 for b_check (asserts b_check must NOT exist) guarding
    VALIDATE CONSTRAINT b_check -> b_check reported as covered. Given
    Liquibase's implicit AND over preConditions siblings, on a box where
    b_check IS missing (the exact dangerous case), BOTH sqlChecks pass ->
    changeset executes -> VALIDATE CONSTRAINT b_check hard-ERRORs -> crash
    loop. This is the identical ms57z incident shape, reproduced through a
    guard the lint now certifies as "safe."

Same underlying bug class as nexus-d4vy6 (round 1) and nexus-8rgaj (round 3):
"the guard looks present but doesn't cover the risk." Shape 2 (DO $$ IF
EXISTS ... THEN VALIDATE) is NOT vulnerable to this variant -- its guard is
executable control flow tied directly to the VALIDATE, with no separate
declarative expectedResult number to invert. Shape 1's heuristic/textual
check is inherently more fragile than Shape 2's semantically-executable
guard; worth noting as a structural asymmetry even independent of this fix.

Fix direction: _iter_changesets_for_validate must also capture each
<sqlCheck>'s expectedResult attribute (not just itertext()), and
_constraint_named_in_preconditions must reject a match whose expectedResult
indicates non-existence (e.g. "0") for the single-name form, and validate the
IN-list form's expectedResult equals (or is consistent with) an existence
assertion. Needs new regression tests: expectedResult="0" single-name
inversion, and the two-sqlCheck mixed-direction case.

Two lesser (Significant, not Critical -- fail-safe direction, not
fail-dangerous) robustness gaps also found in the same regex:
  - _PRECONDITIONS_COVERAGE_RE requires a literal whitespace between
    'conname' and '=' (conname\s+=...); a real, equally-safe
    conname='X' (no space) shape is FALSELY FLAGGED as a violation.
  - The regex hardcodes COUNT(*) verbatim; a real, equally-safe
    SELECT COUNT(1) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'X' shape is
    FALSELY FLAGGED.
  Both would only cause spurious CI failures on a future changeset using
  either variant, not a safety hole, but are worth broadening for
  robustness given the RLS lint's own admission of similar blind spots.

Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-4m6i0.2-round4-validate-precondition-lint.md

title: Tier1: retrofit catalog-013-2 VALIDATE CONSTRAINT with pg_constraint preconditions (ms57z direct fix; GATES engine cut)
description:
TDD (test-first — write the failing repro before the fix).

PROBLEM: service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml:126 changeset catalog-013-2 runs five bare `ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ...` statements (chunks_384/768/1024, catalog_document_chunks, chash_index). On an aged box where chunks_384_chash_len_check was never created (empty bge-768 box; the constraint lives on chunks_768), VALIDATE of a non-existent constraint is a hard ERROR -> the whole service crash-loops on boot (nexus-ms57z / GH #1390).

Confirmed NOT the cause (do not re-investigate): catalog-002-hygiene.xml:84 catalog-002-2-chash-checks adds all chunks_<dim> checks UNCONDITIONALLY (analysis verified at commit 34c23773 / tag engine-service-v0.1.29). The divergence originated out-of-band, so the VALIDATE step must be defensive regardless.

FIX: wrap each VALIDATE (or the whole changeset per-statement) in a precondition — either Liquibase <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"> checking pg_constraint for (conname exists AND convalidated=false) per table, or an equivalent DO $$ ... IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname=...) THEN ... END $$ guard. Per-statement guarding is required because the five tables can diverge independently (some dims empty/never-populated).

TEST-FIRST repro: add a JUnit case in service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/SchemaMigratorIntegrationTest.java that migrates a fresh container up through catalog-002, DROPs chunks_384_chash_len_check to model the aged box, then applies the rest of the chain including catalog-013-2 and asserts migrate() completes (RED before fix, GREEN after).

Test cmd: cd service && ./mvnw -q test -Dtest=SchemaMigratorIntegrationTest

GATING: this is the operational-coupling gate — the patched engine cut (sibling bead) depends on this; no REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION raise / next engine tag the floor relies on until this ships in a deployed+cloud-gated engine.

title: HttpVectorClient() bypasses in migrate_cmd.py/storage_cmd.py skip the cloud version-floor gate
description:
nexus-b6qlf Phase 2 (nexus-jn0nm) wired the cloud engine-compatibility probe into get_http_vector_client() (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py). However src/nexus/commands/migrate_cmd.py:241 and src/nexus/commands/storage_cmd.py:1342 construct `HttpVectorClient()` directly (bypassing the gated singleton getter entirely). Confirmed via grep — these are the ONLY other constructor call sites of HttpVectorClient in src/nexus besides the singleton itself. Both are cloud-relevant paths (storage_cmd's --cloud leg, migrate_cmd's guided migration), and both only pre-flight via _resolve_endpoint() (URL resolvability), never probe_managed_service() (version compatibility). title: Cloud-mode engine version floor is stale and silently permits incompatible engines
description:
managed_endpoint.MIN_MANAGED_RELEASE_VERSION (src/nexus/db/managed_endpoint.py:62) has been hardcoded at (0,1,8) since it was introduced in commit c2c7eb13 (2026-06-24, nexus-x2g1z) and has NEVER been bumped since. Meanwhile the native/local engine floor, guided_upgrade.REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION (src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py:571), has climbed to (0,1,34) as client features shipped.

Concretely observed: a 6.5.1 client (which pins engine-service-v0.1.30 for local mode) ran `nx index repo .` in cloud mode against api.conexus-nexus.com, which per T2 memory has been sitting at engine-service-v0.1.17 since 2026-07-01. v0.1.17 lacks the `get-all-metadata` endpoint (added v0.1.30), so indexing degraded to the slower paginated-sweep fallback with only a buried structlog warning — no upfront failure, no clear signal to the user that anything was wrong.

Root causes (compounding):
1. `MIN_MANAGED_RELEASE_VERSION` and `REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION` are two independent, hand-maintained constants with no cross-check test. Nothing fails CI when they diverge.
2. `probe_managed_service()` (the only place that checks MIN_MANAGED_RELEASE_VERSION) is called ONLY from `nx init` (once, at setup), `nx doctor` (manual), and `nx service probe`/`record-deploy` (manual/operator). It is NEVER called from the actual cloud-mode HTTP vector client construction/connection path (`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py`), which has its own independent endpoint resolver with zero version checking.
3. The one warning message that DOES fire (indexer_utils.py:327, "upgrade the engine this install is pointed at") is actively MISLEADING for cloud-mode users: they have no ability to upgrade a shared multi-tenant cloud engine themselves. Only the maintainer/operator can cut+deploy+cloud-gate a new engine-service tag.
4. The release process's own "engine-freshness gate" (AGENTS.md § Cutting a release, step 0) is a manual checklist step, not an enforced/automated one — evidenced by it being skipped across multiple releases while the cloud engine sat at v0.1.17.

User directive (2026-07-09): fix this for real. The normal update process should keep the cloud engine current automatically; the end user should ideally need to do NOTHING. If any manual step is ever genuinely required, it must be surfaced clearly and loudly at the moment it's needed — never silently degraded or buried in a log line.

Scope for the fix (to be finalized via brainstorming-gate + strategic-planning):
- Unify or lock-step MIN_MANAGED_RELEASE_VERSION and REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION with an enforced test so they cannot silently diverge.
- Wire a real compatibility check into the actual cloud-mode connection path so a too-old engine fails loud immediately, not after some specific feature 404s deep in a workflow.
- Fix cloud-mode-specific messaging to never tell end users to do something only the operator can do.
- Consider making the release-process engine-freshness gate an automated/enforced check (e.g. a script that queries the live cloud /version and fails the release if behind) rather than a manual checklist step.

title: INCIDENT: catalog-013 VALIDATE failed on cloud deploy of v0.1.33 — FORCE RLS silently no-op'd the 013-0 normalization DML for the non-BYPASSRLS owner
description: conexus deploy of engine-service-v0.1.33 failed at catalog-013-2 (VALIDATE chash_index_chash_len_check violated), brief outage, clean rollback to 0.1.32 (T2 nexus/conexus-to-nexus-INCIDENT-engine-v0133-deploy-FAILED-rolled-back-catalog013-2026-07-08, conexus-ml1z). ROOT CAUSE: nexus_admin is table owner WITHOUT BYPASSRLS and nexus.chash_index has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — so 013-0's dedupe+truncate DML saw ZERO rows (silent no-op), while 013-2's VALIDATE (DDL, not row-filtered) saw the un-normalized legacy 64-char rows and failed. Tests never caught it: Testcontainers Liquibase runs as superuser (implicit BYPASSRLS). LIVE RESIDUAL: 013-1 committed → the NOT VALID CHECK now rejects new 64-char chash_index writes on the cloud tenant under the rolled-back 0.1.32 server (6.4.0 clients send 64-char; server-side normalization only exists in 0.1.33+). FIX: new changeset catalog-013-1b (between recorded 013-1 and unrecorded 013-2): NO FORCE RLS → idempotent re-run of the dedupe+truncate → FORCE RLS, one transaction; 013-0/013-1 untouched (checksum immutability). Serving role is non-owner so tenant isolation is unaffected by the toggle. Plus: regression test running the changelog as a non-superuser non-BYPASSRLS owner with seeded 64-char rows; CHANGELOG remedy correction (condition is length(chash) != 32, and plain SELECTs as nexus_admin return 0 rows on FORCE-RLS tables — the documented remedy was unrunnable, conexus Finding 2). title: P0 macOS PG bundle non-relocatable — every engine-service release through v0.1.15 shipped broken psql/createdb/etc
description: User report (gpollatos): nx init -> pg_provision_failed -> psql SIGABRT 'Library not loaded: /Users/runner/work/nexus/nexus/bundle/lib/libpq.5.dylib'. Root cause: macOS configure/make install bakes the literal absolute --prefix into every libpq-linked client binary's LC_LOAD_DYLIB (psql/createdb/dropdb/pg_dump/pg_restore/initdb/pg_isready/reindexdb/vacuumdb/clusterdb/pg_rewind/pg_basebackup/createuser/dropuser/pg_dumpall/pg_createsubscriber/pg_receivewal/pg_recvlogical/pg_upgrade/pg_amcheck/pgbench + libpq.5/libecpg.6/libpgtypes.3/libecpg_compat.3/libpqwalreceiver dylibs = 26 files). Linux gets $ORIGIN-relative RPATH from PG's own build system by default; macOS never got equivalent treatment. Fixed on develop (925452b7): scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh fixup_macos_relocatability() (install_name_tool @rpath rewrite + build-time smoke) + engine-service-release.yml relocation gate (extracts the exact artifact, proves initdb->start->CREATE EXTENSION vector, BEFORE signing). Systemic gap: tests/db/test_pg_bundle_relocation.py existed but only ran path-filtered in ci.yml against a self-built bundle, never against the release artifact; this session's --cold validations were Linux-container-only. title: Implement JooqRecordReflectionFeature + wire pom native profile (constructors only)
description:
Implement Approach B (APPROVED, do not re-litigate): a build-time GraalVM Feature that enumerates jOOQ record types from the schema model and registers their CONSTRUCTORS for native-image reflection. Scope discipline: constructors ONLY (the exact failing mechanism) — do NOT pre-register methods/fields.

TDD — write the structural GUARD test FIRST (it is a guard, NOT the proof; see acceptance):
  NEW test (JVM, junit5): service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/nativeimage/JooqRecordReflectionFeatureTest.java
  Assert dev.nexus.service.jooq.nexus.Nexus.NEXUS.getTables().stream().map(Table::getRecordType) yields EXACTLY 50 distinct record classes, matching the count of *.class generated under service/target/generated-sources/jooq/dev/nexus/service/jooq/nexus/tables/records/. Exact == 50 (per feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression — count from the generated dir at test time, not a hardcode if a constant is available). This catches "Feature silently registers nothing" / schema-model drift. It does NOT prove native reflection works (JVM reflection always succeeds — native is the only real gate; see native-verify bead).

THEN implement:
1. NEW file: service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/nativeimage/JooqRecordReflectionFeature.java implements org.graalvm.nativeimage.hosted.Feature. In beforeAnalysis(BeforeAnalysisAccess): for (Table<?> t : Nexus.NEXUS.getTables()) { Class<?> rec = t.getRecordType(); RuntimeReflection.register(rec); RuntimeReflection.register(rec.getDeclaredConstructors()); }  (imports: org.jooq.Table, dev.nexus.service.jooq.nexus.Nexus, org.graalvm.nativeimage.hosted.{Feature,RuntimeReflection}). Structured logging only if any; no System.out.
2. GraalVM SDK dependency: service/pom.xml currently has org.graalvm.buildtools plugin + graalvm-reachability-metadata but NO compile/provided SDK artifact for the hosted Feature/RuntimeReflection API. Verify whether native-build-tools brings org.graalvm.sdk:nativeimage transitively at build time; if the Feature does not compile under `./mvnw test-compile`, add a `provided`-scope dep (org.graalvm.sdk:nativeimage or graal-sdk, version aligned to the toolchain). Add ONLY if needed.
3. Wire the Feature into the `native` profile buildArgs in service/pom.xml (buildArgs block is lines 504-557): add <buildArg>--features=dev.nexus.service.nativeimage.JooqRecordReflectionFeature</buildArg>.

PROOF GATE for THIS bead: FULL `./mvnw test` GREEN (Java-schema rule — Java CI is advisory/pytest-only, so the full Maven suite is the real local check). Native build + --fullstack are the next bead.

COMMANDS:
  cd service && ./mvnw -q test-compile          # confirms Feature + SDK API compile
  ./mvnw test                                   # FULL suite, must be green
Prefer Serena (find_symbol / get_symbols_overview) for navigating generated jOOQ sources.
Context: T2 nexus/design-engine-jooq-record-reflection.md (## Decision, ## Scope discipline).
acceptance_criteria: Structural guard test written FIRST and asserts == 50 record types; JooqRecordReflectionFeature.java created registering record constructors only; --features buildArg added to native profile; GraalVM SDK provided dep added only if compile requires it; FULL ./mvnw test GREEN. notes: AUDIT ADVISORY (nx_plan_audit, medium): the ==50 guard test must exercise the FEATURE'S OWN record-discovery code path, else it is vacuous. Do NOT inline getTables() in the test; instead expose the enumeration the Feature registers as a package-visible static (e.g. static Collection<Class<?>> recordTypes() returning what beforeAnalysis() iterates) and assert recordTypes().size()==50 (count derived from the generated records dir). title: Engine native-image: jOOQ generated *Record classes unregistered for reflection — every INSERT…RETURNING write 500s (document_aspects, plans, memory, catalog…)
description:
Discovered by RDR-173 P7 --fullstack (nexus-rsabu), 2026-06-30, engine-service-v0.1.12 native binary.

SYMPTOM: POST /v1/aspects/upsert returns 500 'Could not construct new record'. The aspect pipeline never persists -> document_aspects stays 0.

ROOT CAUSE: jOOQ INSERT…RETURNING (Tools.recordFactory -> TableImpl.getRecordConstructor) reflectively invokes the no-arg ctor of the generated record class. service/src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/reflect-config.json registers ZERO jOOQ classes; all 50 records under dev.nexus.service.jooq.nexus.tables.records.* are unregistered -> org.graalvm.nativeimage.MissingReflectionRegistrationError (NoSuchMethodException DocumentAspectsRecord.<init>()). Stacktrace: storage_service_native.log:771; full at T2 rdr/173-P7-ROOT-CAUSE-engine-jooq-reflection-2026-06-30.

SCOPE: affects EVERY RETURNING-based write across the schema (DocumentAspects, Plans, Memory, Catalog*), not aspects alone. Broken since the native-image cutover.

PRODUCTION (verify): cloud runs the same native binary; cloud gate doesn't exercise the aspect/RETURNING write path -> aspect extraction likely silently broken in prod.

FIX: register the jOOQ records package for reflection in the native image. Prefer a GraalVM Feature iterating dev.nexus.service.jooq.nexus.tables.records.** with RuntimeReflection.register (robust to future-generated records) over enumerating 50 entries in reflect-config.json. Then FULL ./mvnw test + native build + run.sh --fullstack must show document_aspects>0. New engine cut required; deploy+re-gate are conexus relays. Blocks RDR-173 P7 / RDR-172 P2.5 close.
close_reason: Native-image jOOQ INSERT…RETURNING reflection bug FIXED + shipped in engine-service-v0.1.13 (PR #1352, develop 7b748269). Schema-model-driven GraalVM Feature registers all 50 *Record constructors + build-time-init org.xml.sax.helpers. Cloud-deployed + cloud-gated GREEN 2026-07-01; prod aspects/plans/memory RETURNING writes restored. All subtasks .1-.6 closed.

title: RDR-157 P3.2: CA-2 spike — -H:IncludeResources embed vs ship-alongside (measure + decide)
description: Spike -H:IncludeResources embedding of the PG bundle into the native binary + first-run self-extract (same mechanism the binary uses for ONNX/DJL native libs). MEASURE: build cost, binary bloat, first-run extract latency. Decide embed vs ship-alongside ({binary, pg-<plat>.txz} archive fallback) with the numbers recorded. Use sequential-thinking for the tradeoff. Record decision + measurements in T2 (rdr/157-CA2 already has the research finding RF-157-8; this records the build-out verdict). DEPENDS ON P3.1 (need a real bundle to embed).
notes: VERDICT 2026-06-15: SHIP-ALONGSIDE (not embed). User-directed + measurement-confirmed. title: [P0 EMERGENCY] T1 scratch hard-fails on 5.10.x: MCP session-id (NX_SESSION_ID) diverges from SessionStart current_session, warm-publish drops claude_pid fallback
description:
EMERGENCY PATCH (5.10.x regression, RDR-149 P4). Full forensics in T2: `nx memory get -p nexus -t t1-session-mismatch-emergency-forensics-2026-06-05`.

SYMPTOM: `nx scratch` (CLI, dumps raw traceback) and MCP scratch tool both raise T1ServerNotFoundError. Broke after 5.10.1 update + MCP reconnect; worked on 5.10.0 earlier same session.

ROOT CAUSE: The conexus MCP server publishes its T1 lease keyed on NX_SESSION_ID (live: 219073cf...), but SessionStart writes ~/.config/nexus/current_session from claude_session_id (live: 2b0e933e). Shell `nx scratch` resolves current_session -> discover_t1_lease finds no lease for it -> fail. The two Claude-provided session ids diverge on resume / multi-frontend (Code CLI + Desktop .mcpb share one global current_session) / version skew (live MCPs at both 5.10.0 and 5.10.1).

WHY THE FALLBACK IS DEAD: the nexus-0x16i Bash-sibling escape hatch (match a live T1 by immediate Claude ancestor pid) is inert because:
1. t1_lease.py:_payload (line 162) records claude_pid ONLY when session_id is None. Warm publishes (NX_SESSION_ID set at MCP startup) key directly on the session and DROP claude_pid. All 4 live leases have claude_pid=None. => fallback dead in the COMMON config, not an edge case.
2. t1_lease.py:discover_t1_transient_for_claude skips session-keyed leases entirely (`if session_id is not None: continue`).

PATCH (P0-A, restores function, low risk):
- t1_lease.py:_payload — always include claude_pid (remove the `session_id is None and` guard).
- t1_lease.py:discover_t1_transient_for_claude — match session-keyed leases by claude_pid too (still ancestor-pid-targeted + TTL-bounded => no cross-session mis-bind). Rename -> discover_t1_by_claude_ancestor.
- t1.py:_init_new_discovery — verify the fallback ordering (already runs after discover_t1_lease==None).
P1: commands/scratch.py — catch T1ServerNotFoundError, print friendly hint / optional ephemeral fallback (no traceback).
P1: hooks.py:session_start — message "T1 scratch initialized" is false (hook doesn't start T1); reword.
P2 (post-emergency): reconcile NX_SESSION_ID vs claude_session_id (single authoritative id) / have lifespan also stamp current_session.

REGRESSION WINDOW: dbaa8974 + 702de913 (RDR-149 P4), shipped 5.10.0 -> 5.10.1.

BLAST RADIUS: all shell-side nx CLI (scratch/doctor/SessionEnd flush) when MCP session != current_session. MCP-tool-side T1 unaffected (injected EphemeralClient).

title: TOCTOU race in ensure_owner_for_repo creates duplicate owners (RDR-137 followup CRITICAL-5)
description:
Source: Edge-cases scenario 5 + F1.

PROBLEM: src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:995-1030 ensure_owner_for_repo is check-then-act:
  existing = self.owner_for_repo(repo_hash)
  if existing is not None: return existing
  return self.register_owner(...)

Schema (db/t2/catalog.py:88-115) declares only UNIQUE(name, owner_type) — no UNIQUE on repo_hash. Concurrent invocations (parallel CI runs against shared ~/.config/nexus, session-start hook racing first index, multi-window operator) can both pass the lookup, both allocate distinct tumbler prefixes (1.5 and 1.6), both INSERT for the same repo_hash. Documents under one prefix become invisible to lookups returning the other.

FIX:
- Add CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_owners_repo_hash ON owners(repo_hash) WHERE repo_hash != '' (partial index excludes curator rows with empty repo_hash).
- ensure_owner_for_repo catches sqlite3.IntegrityError after register_owner, re-runs owner_for_repo, returns the now-present existing owner.

REVIEWERS: edge-case-analyst.
LABELS: critical, rdr-137-followup, catalog, concurrency
notes: Enrichment-surfaced extra context: indexer already has its own per-repo lock at src/nexus/indexer.py:208-260 (writes ~/.config/nexus/locks/<hash8>.lock). If ensure_owner_for_repo is always called inside that lock, the TOCTOU window collapses without schema changes. Verify call-site contexts BEFORE adding a redundant unique-index layer — may be a cheaper fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: OwnerRecord missing head_hash field — rebuild silently wipes column (RDR-137 followup CRITICAL-1)
description:
Source: Schema/Migration review C1 + Edge-cases F-extra-A (flagged by 2 independent reviewers).

PROBLEM: OwnerRecord (src/nexus/catalog/tumbler.py:135) has 6 fields, no head_hash. Chain:
1. set_owner_head_hash (catalog.py:1049) writes head_hash to SQLite owners column — correct
2. register_owner constructs OwnerRecord(...) with 6 fields, no head_hash
3. catalog.py:972 appends rec.__dict__ to owners.jsonl — head_hash absent from event log
4. _rebuild_inner (db/t2/catalog.py:805) INSERTs only 6 columns — head_hash never restored

CONSEQUENCE: every catalog rebuild zeros owners.head_hash for all owners. Phase 3.8 staleness optimization defeated the moment any consumer reads it.

FIX:
- Add head_hash: str = '' to OwnerRecord (tumbler.py:135).
- Thread head_hash through register_owner serialization to owners.jsonl.
- Update _rebuild_inner INSERT to include head_hash column.
- Decide canonical source: either (a) emit OwnerHeadHashSet event so JSONL replay restores it, or (b) accept derived-signal status and re-derive from disk post-rebuild.
- Regression test: set_owner_head_hash → trigger Catalog.rebuild() → assert head_hash survives.

REVIEWERS: schema-review + edge-case-analyst.
LABELS: critical, rdr-137-followup, catalog, head_hash
notes:
Enrichment-surfaced extra context (T2: nexus/rdr-137-followup-enrichment-2026-05-28):

Fix scope must include register_owner (src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:944-985), not just the rebuild projector. Both write paths INSERT 6 columns and wipe head_hash.

Event-sourcing design question: head_hash either lives in OwnerRegistered event payload (round-trip via projector) OR gets a separate _v0_set_owner_head_hash event. Current epsilon-allow at catalog.py:1044-1048 preserves no-event-sourcing boundary; the design question is how to keep that boundary while making field round-trippable.

Test pattern: test_owner_record_head_hash_survives_rebuild — open catalog, set_owner_head_hash, trigger projector rebuild (delete + re-apply from events.jsonl), assert non-null. Pin exact expected value (feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression).

title: conexus commands: literal triple-backtick inside fenced-bang block truncates it (17/25 broken in 5.1.2)
description: Regression introduced by nexus-ln9y5 (5.1.2). Claude Code closes a fenced-bang command bash block at the FIRST literal triple-backtick in the SOURCE, anywhere on a line (e.g. inside echo of a backtick-fence, or a Python print/regex), not only at a bare closing-fence line. A 4-backtick opening fence does NOT help (probe confirmed: CC still finds the bang-opener and closes at the first inner triple-backtick), so the block is truncated mid-content and the shell errors with unmatched quote. 17 of 25 commands affected: 14 shell commands that echo a code fence around command output, plus phase-review-gate, rdr-close, rdr-gate whose Python contains literal triple-backticks. User hit it on /conexus:review-code. How it slipped: the ln9y5 verification checked only for BARE fence lines (CommonMark rule) not any-position triple-backtick; the effect-test extracted the block with a CommonMark-correct regex so it ran the full body in bash and passed; cc-validation scenario 19 only exercised rdr-list (a Python block with no literal triple-backtick). FIX: remove every literal triple-backtick from block sources (shell builds the fence via printf octal or drops the wrapping; Python uses chr(96)*3). GUARD: assert no triple-backtick inside any fenced-bang block (matches CC parser); add a cc-validation scenario running a converted echo-fence command through real CC. Ship 5.1.3.
acceptance_criteria: No command fenced-bang block source contains a literal triple-backtick; all 25 commands render through real Claude Code without truncation (cc-validation scenario covering an echo-fence command passes); a static guard rejects any triple-backtick inside a fenced-bang block; full suite green.
notes: Durable fix tracked in RDR-130 (command preambles via nx CLI). User chose the nx-CLI path over a quick inline patch. RDR-130 P1 = RDR commands to nx rdr preamble; P2 = agent-relay shell to nx command-context; P3 = retire inline machinery. Interim P0 relief (strip literal triple-backticks from the 17 blocks) available if 5.1.2 breakage cannot wait for P1.
close_reason: Interim fix shipped in conexus 5.1.3 (published PyPI 2026-05-26). All 25 command fenced-bang blocks free of literal triple-backticks; verified through real Claude Code (cc-validation scenarios 19+20, fresh creds) and live /conexus:rdr-list. Guard test_no_inner_triple_backtick_in_bang_block added. Durable fix = RDR-130 (nx CLI migration).

title: GUI-spawned nx-mcp ignores shell-env credentials → cloud mode misdetected as local
description:
When nx-mcp is spawned by a GUI parent (Claude Desktop, Cowork via SDK bridge), the child process inherits launchd's environment, NOT the user's interactive shell env. If credentials live only as shell exports (CHROMA_API_KEY, VOYAGE_API_KEY in .zshrc), get_credential() returns empty, is_local_mode() returns True, make_t3() routes to make_t3_client() (the daemon path), and the call fails with 'T3 daemon not running' even though the user is configured for cloud.

Discovered 2026-05-23 via Cowork live test for RDR-126. Host has CHROMA_API_KEY + VOYAGE_API_KEY in shell env, ~/.config/nexus/config.yml has only credentials.migrated:'1'. is_local_mode() returns False under the shell but True under launchd.

Affected surfaces:
- Claude Desktop chat MCP (.mcpb future)
- Claude Desktop local-agent mode (TODAY — observed in /tmp/.../main.log session local_168c694c-b941-4e90-b95e-2a1ee7bb23d6)
- Cowork via SDK transport (TODAY)
- ANY GUI-spawned nx-mcp consumer

Code paths involved:
- src/nexus/config.py:465 is_local_mode() — auto-detect 'both keys missing' branch
- src/nexus/config.py:647 get_credential() — env > file > empty
- src/nexus/db/__init__.py:30 make_t3() — dispatch on is_local_mode()
- src/nexus/daemon/t3_client.py:74 make_t3_client() — raises T3DaemonError on missing daemon

Fix options:

A. Immediate user-side workaround (documented in README + nx doctor):
   nx config set chroma_api_key $CHROMA_API_KEY
   nx config set voyage_api_key $VOYAGE_API_KEY
   nx config set chroma_tenant $CHROMA_TENANT
   nx config set chroma_database $CHROMA_DATABASE
   (after which credentials live in ~/.config/nexus/config.yml and are visible to launchd-spawned children)

B. Code-side: nx doctor detect 'credentials in env only, not in config file' state and warn the user that GUI-spawned MCP consumers will fail. Concrete check:
   - both CHROMA_API_KEY and VOYAGE_API_KEY present in os.environ
   - AND ~/.config/nexus/config.yml is missing or has no credentials.chroma_api_key + credentials.voyage_api_key
   - → emit warning with the four nx config set commands

C. Code-side: on first run from CLI, opportunistically migrate env-only credentials into the config file if the user runs nx with creds in env but missing from file. Asking before writing is the safer pattern.

D. Code-side: make_t3() dispatch could be more defensive — if is_local_mode() returns True BUT NX_LOCAL is not explicitly '1' AND no daemon discovery file exists, emit a structured error pointing at the credential persistence path before attempting the daemon connection. This makes the failure self-diagnosing.

Probably ship B + D as the conexus 4.34.7 patch. C is a separate ergonomic decision (autoamigration has its own pitfalls).

Test scenarios:
- Fresh install, credentials in env only, GUI spawn (Claude Desktop) → nx doctor emits warning, nx-mcp fails fast with credential-persistence message instead of obscure T3DaemonError
- Fresh install, credentials in env only, CLI spawn → no warning (CLI env IS the truth source for that session)
- Credentials in config.yml, env unset, GUI spawn → works (file fallback used)
- Credentials in both env and config.yml → works, env wins per existing precedence

Linked: nexus-bsjro (RDR-126 epic — this bug is on the critical path because it blocks every Claude Desktop deployment scenario the RDR addresses)
close_reason: Fix shipped in PR #935 (squash-merged to develop as 4f54f77e on 2026-05-23). Verified by tests/test_credential_persistence_gui_spawn.py + nx doctor 'Credential persistence (GUI spawn)' health check.

title: RDR-112 P3.2 — T2Client drop-in compatibility (context manager + facade delegates)
description:
## Context

Phase 3 (nexus-hpxl) flipped mcp_infra.t2_ctx() to return T2Client in daemon mode. 47 call sites across src/nexus use the pattern `with t2_ctx() as db: db.put(...)` (or db.get / db.search / db.resolve_title / etc.). T2Database supports this — it has __enter__/__exit__ AND facade delegate methods that forward to self.memory.put etc. T2Client does NOT: it has only store proxies (client.memory.put). Result: every `nx memory put` / `nx memory get` / etc. invocation under the new daemon default fails with AttributeError: 'T2Client' object has no attribute 'put'.

This shipped silently with the default-flip-to-daemon (commit 3ae5f39f, 2026-05-17) + Phase 3 hpxl flip (commit 3ca98761, 2026-05-18). The Phase 3 review verified t2_ctx returns the correct TYPE under each mode but did not exercise the CALL-SITE USAGE PATTERN. This is exactly the prompt-rigour failure that the new /nx:code-review § Prompt rigour discipline targets — it lived in a class named there ('integration-boundary defects that live between two files').

## Acceptance

- T2Client.__enter__ / __exit__ defined (no-op cleanup; the pool is lazy).
- T2Client gains facade delegate methods mirroring T2Database lines 408-700+: put, get, resolve_title, search, list_entries, get_projects_with_prefix, search_glob, search_by_tag, get_all, delete (memory-only — cross-domain taxonomy cascade documented as known difference), find_overlapping_memories, merge_memories, flag_stale_memories, save_plan, search_plans, list_plans, plan_exists, log_relevance, log_relevance_batch, get_relevance_log, expire_relevance_log, expire (housekeeping), rename_collection_cascade.
- Integration test: spawn nx daemon t2; run `nx memory put` via subprocess under NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon; verify success.
- Regression sweep: the 47 `with t2_ctx() as db: db.X(...)` call sites continue to work in BOTH modes.
- Direct-mode behavior unchanged.
- Code review MANDATORY after impl — with the boundary-spanning prompt-rigour relay template per the new /nx:code-review skill.

## Why P0

Production-broken state. Every CLI command that uses t2_ctx fails under the new default. Phase 4 ports cannot land cleanly until this fix is in.

## Files

- src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py — add context-manager protocol + facade delegates
- tests/daemon/test_t2_client_facade.py (new) — test every facade method round-trips
- tests/mcp/test_t2_ctx_call_site_compat.py (new) — `with t2_ctx() as db: db.put(...)` under both modes

## Reminders

- Lock the test for the regression: subprocess test that runs `nx memory put` against a live daemon. The unit-level type tests in test_storage_mode_flip don't catch this; only an end-to-end subprocess test will.
- Per the lesson: when dispatching code-review-expert for this, include 'integration-boundary defects between CLI and substrate' as an explicit suspect category in the relay.
close_reason: Substrate fix landed on develop (commit 912491c4). T2Client gains 22 facade delegate methods + signature parity tests + round-trip integration tests + the context-manager-with-facade regression test that locks the call-site pattern. nx memory put/get/search now work under daemon mode (production-broken pre-fix). 38 new tests pass; wider sweep 1209 clean. All 5 Phase 4 beads (idqd, yfqv, uar6, mmvf, pac1) now have the substrate dependency satisfied.

title: (BUG) T360-SEC-1: Python callable injection via binding YAML action
description:
src/nexus/cockpit/bindings.py:340-348 (_resolve_python_callable) + :466

_resolve_python_callable calls importlib.import_module(mod_name) where mod_name is taken directly from a user-authored YAML action.callable field. NO module-path allowlist. Any same-UID agent (or process that drops a YAML into ~/.config/nexus/bindings/profiles/) can specify os:system, subprocess:Popen, shutil:rmtree, or any installed package callable. YAML is loaded at daemon start AND on every mtime-triggered hot-reload (50ms watcher tick). Module-import side effects execute even when the (event, binding, context) arg-shape mismatch raises.

Exploit: write a YAML with action: {kind: python, callable: "os:system"} → wait 50ms → daemon imports os and calls os.system(event, binding, context). The import alone may suffice for malicious side effects in a top-level module body.

SR-1 profile-name allowlist + new schema_version gate are INSUFFICIENT: neither restricts what module or function the callable path names.

Fix shape:
- Add a callable-allowlist registry (e.g. only callables in nexus.* and nexus_plugins.* namespaces are resolvable).
- OR require pre-registration via a decorator (callables register their dotted path; load_profile rejects un-registered targets).
- Surfaced + filed under nexus-ftpm (second 360°) review: dim-10 unicode covered SR-1 but NOT callable-target validation.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: action.callable must reject unsanctioned import targets; test covers both happy path (allowlisted) and reject path.
close_reason: Closed

title: CR-4: RDR-112 §5 storage-boundary lint allowlist diverges from RDR text (db/ missing)
description:
RDR-112 §5 specifies that the storage-boundary lint (nx doctor --check-storage-boundary) allowlist contains src/nexus/db/ as a legitimate location for direct sqlite3.connect calls. The shipped lint at src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:874 allows only src/nexus/daemon/.

Running the lint today reports 36 violations, 8 of which are legitimate src/nexus/db/t2/*.py daemon-internal stores. The lint is unusable as a CI gate in its current state — which is why CR-5 (the CI integration step that RDR §5 also specifies) was never wired.

Fix: add src/nexus/db/ to the allowlist. Re-run the lint to confirm clean state, then proceed to CR-5 (wire into CI) and CR-6 (extend scope to chromadb.PersistentClient).

Alternative: amend RDR-112 §5 to narrow the allowlist intentionally — but then the 8 db/t2/ violations must be relocated or annotated with '# storage-boundary-allow:' comments.

## Steps to Reproduce

title: CR-2: typed RPC exceptions collapse to generic T2DaemonError over the wire
description:
In src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py, _reraise_remote_error (~lines 377-404) only resolves remote exception qualnames against builtins. The new typed exceptions shipped this arc:
- BlockingTakeResourceExhausted(RuntimeError) — HR-1
- InvalidTimeoutError(ValueError)
both have qualnames like 'nexus.daemon.tuplespace_service.BlockingTakeResourceExhausted' which are not builtins. The wire-arrival path therefore collapses them to generic T2DaemonError.

This breaks:
- HR-1 docstring claim that clients can catch BlockingTakeResourceExhausted by class.
- External retry logic catching TimeoutError + BlockingTakeResourceExhausted (only T2DaemonError catches now).
- SR-2 in-process test does NOT exercise the wire-traversal path, so the bug is untested.

Fix: maintain an explicit registry on the client side:
{ 'nexus.daemon.tuplespace_service.BlockingTakeResourceExhausted': BlockingTakeResourceExhausted,
  'nexus.tuplespace.api.InvalidTimeoutError': InvalidTimeoutError,
  ... }
consulted before the builtin fallback.

Alternative considered: inherit BlockingTakeResourceExhausted from TimeoutError so prior retry logic transparently catches it.

Test gap: add a wire-traversal test that exercises t2_client → t2_daemon → service path so the exception class survives serialization.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start daemon. Run `nx daemon t2 start`.
2. From a different process, open a T2Client and call `take(subspace='x', pattern=...)` with timeout=0 to force InvalidTimeoutError, OR saturate the daemon with 16 concurrent blocking_take calls and trigger HR-1 BlockingTakeResourceExhausted.
3. The exception is raised inside the daemon and serialized over the UDS frame.
4. On the client side, observe that the caller's `except BlockingTakeResourceExhausted` does NOT catch — only `except T2DaemonError` catches.
5. Inspect t2_client.py _reraise_remote_error: the type lookup only consults `builtins`, so the qualname 'nexus.daemon.tuplespace_service.BlockingTakeResourceExhausted' falls through to the generic fallback.
6. Confirm test gap: `tests/daemon/test_360_remediation_hr.py` and `test_360_remediation_sr.py` exercise the in-process service path, not the wire-traversal client path.

title: CR-1: socket timeout never restored after blocking-mode override on pooled connection
description:
In src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py around line 298, the finally clause that restores the socket timeout has the guard 'if original_timeout is not None and recv_timeout_override is not None'. When the connection started in default blocking mode (original_timeout is None), the override stays installed after the call. A pooled socket then carries the prior call's timeout into the next request.

Failure modes:
- Pool reuse: blocking_take with 35s budget executed first, then a fast ping inherits 35s — truly hung calls don't surface.
- Reverse: a short-timeout call leaves a 5s budget on the socket, a later long call wedges or times out incorrectly.

Fix: track 'was_overridden = recv_timeout_override is not None' separately, and in the override branch restore unconditionally to the original (including back to None via settimeout(None) or setblocking(True)).

Test gap: add a test that exercises both pool-reuse-after-blocking-mode-override and the inverse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the daemon: `nx daemon t2 start`.
2. Open a T2Client and make a single `blocking_take(timeout=30)` call from a pooled socket. The socket starts blocking (`gettimeout()` returns None) but the call installs a recv timeout override.
3. After the blocking_take returns, immediately reuse the pooled socket for a fast `ping` or `recent_events` call.
4. Observe that the second call inherits the prior 35s recv timeout instead of being restored to blocking-mode.
5. Verify in t2_client.py:298 that the finally guard `if original_timeout is not None and recv_timeout_override is not None` short-circuits when `original_timeout is None`.
design: Single-file fix to t2_client.py; new test in tests/daemon/.
acceptance_criteria: Pool-reuse test added covering both override directions; restore is unconditional within the override branch; CI green.

title: SR-1: Path traversal in binding_create / binding_delete MCP tools
description:
**CRITICAL.** From the 360° security review.

## Bug

`src/nexus/cockpit/bindings_crud.py:49` `_profile_path(profiles_dir, profile)` returns `profiles_dir / f"{profile}.yml"` with **zero validation** of `profile`. The MCP tools `binding_create` and `binding_delete` (`src/nexus/mcp/core.py:4600`, `:4698`) accept arbitrary strings.

## Exploit shapes (same-UID)

- `profile="../malicious"` writes to `~/.config/nexus/bindings/malicious.yml` (escapes `profiles/`)
- `profile="/etc/passwd"` writes `/etc/passwd.yml` (absolute path swallows the join)
- `delete_binding(profile="../../foo")` calls `path.unlink()` on any user-writable .yml

## Combined impact

If the planted YAML lands inside the watcher's scan roots AND has `kind: python` action, `importlib.import_module(callable_ref)` fires on the next event. A misbehaving MCP-capable agent can plant arbitrary code execution at any user-writable .yml path.

## Fix

Validate `profile` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` before reaching `_profile_path`, OR `resolve().relative_to(target_dir)` check. Tests for both forms (path-with-slash, leading-..) before fix; assert they raise.

title: Fix _build_content JSON truncation producing invalid JSON
description:
Security critic S4: src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py:549 return raw[:12000] produces invalid JSON on truncation. Content field is 'stored verbatim, not embedded' but downstream consumers (cockpit panels, doctor, future tools) reading it as JSON parse-error on any payload >12 KB. Common: Bash hook with large tool_response diff.

Fix: structured truncation preserving JSON envelope. {'truncated': true, 'head': raw[:12000]} or store as named string field that doesn't claim to be JSON.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

**Location:** `src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py:541-549`

```python
def _build_content(hook_type: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    raw = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)
    # Stay well within SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES = 12288
    return raw[:12000]
```

Byte-slice `raw[:12000]` can land mid-string, escape sequence, or nested object → unparseable content downstream.

### Why this matters
- Called for every Claude Code hook fire via `emit()` (line 269); any payload >12000 bytes hits bug.
- Stored verbatim in tuplespace `content` column; surfaced by cockpit panels.
- Silent truncation — no error, no marker.

### Fix options
- **(a)** Drop cap, accept size. ChromaDB `MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES = 16384`; `SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES = 12288` soft limit. Payload stored verbatim (not embedded), so column-write quota is what matters. Verify before raising cap.
- **(b)** Drop trailing fields until JSON fits. Preserves valid JSON; loses tail.
- **(c)** Wrap in JSON string literal: `json.dumps(raw[:N])`. Consumers see string. `json.loads()` succeeds. Cheapest fix.

### Recommended
Option (b) with (c) fallback:
1. Try full `json.dumps(payload)`; if ≤ 12000 bytes, return.
2. Else build projection with stable small fields (`session_id`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `cwd`, truncated `_overflow_note`); if fits, return.
3. Else return `json.dumps({"_truncated_raw": raw[:11800]})`.

### Test strategy
Add unit tests in `tests/cockpit/test_hook_bridge.py`:
- Payload < 12000 bytes → `json.loads(result) == payload`.
- Payload > 12000 bytes with truncatable trailing → `json.loads(result)` succeeds, preserves required keys.
- Minimum projection still overflows → `json.loads(result)` succeeds (string or wrapper).
- Property test (optional): random payloads, `json.loads(_build_content(...))` never raises.

### Constraints
- Pure function — no I/O, no INFO logging.
- Must not raise on plausible payload (hook-fire hot path).
- Within `SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES = 12288` per `src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py`.
- Preserve `ensure_ascii=False`.
- Do not change function signature.

title: Test take() idempotent-retake path (CA-1/CA-2 contract)
description:
Test critic C-3: api.py:704-713 take() short-circuits and returns existing tuple+claim_id when the same claimant already holds an active lease. Lines 706-713 fully uncovered.

Fix: test out() -> take() as claimant A -> take() again as claimant A before expiry -> assert same claim_id returned. Pins the CA-1 (idempotent retake) and CA-2 (single-active-claim-per-claimant) contracts.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

RDR-110 CA-1/CA-2 require `tuplespace.take()` idempotent: same claimant re-taking owned tuple → **same** `claim_id`, **no** new `tuple_claim_log` row, no rotation of `claim_id` on `tuples`.

### Implementation status
Idempotent-retake path **already implemented** in `src/nexus/tuplespace/api.py:690-713` (read-then-update probe above the single-statement CAS). Emits structured-log event `tuplespace_take_idempotent_retake`. **No regression test** — this bead is test-only.

### Test must assert
For single tuple in subspace, one claimant calling `take` twice with active lease:
1. Second `take` returns `(tuple_dict, claim_id)` (not `None`).
2. `claim_id` second call **equals** first call's.
3. `tuples.claim_id` row value unchanged.
4. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tuple_claim_log WHERE tuple_id=? AND transition='claim'` returns exactly **1**.
5. (Recommended) Different claimant attempting `take` while lease live does NOT hit idempotent path (counter-test — returns `None`).

### Location
New class `TestTakeIdempotentRetake` in `tests/tuplespace/test_api.py` immediately after `TestTakeCASRace` (line 558), before `TestTakeExact` (line 638). Reuse `db_conn`, `index`, `registry` fixtures from `TestTakeSemantic`. Pattern after `test_take_returns_tuple_and_claim_id` (445) and `test_take_writes_claim_log_entry` (478).

### Constraints
- Deterministic: `time.time()` patching only if needed for lease-expiry; happy-path within default lease window.
- Integration over mocks: real sqlite via `db_conn`; no mocking `_claim_id` or sqlite.
- Exact equality (`== 1`) for claim-log count, NOT inequality.
- Do NOT modify `src/nexus/tuplespace/api.py` — test-only.

title: Test SQLite-fails-AFTER-Chroma-write (atomicity asymmetry)
description:
Test critic C-5: tests/tuplespace/test_api_atomicity.py covers Chroma-fails-first; no test covers SQLite-fails-after-Chroma-succeeded. Reversing the api.out ordering (silently breaking the nexus-qmrr invariant) would leave the existing test green.

Fix: mock conn.commit() to raise after index.out() succeeds. Assert (a) exception propagates, (b) Chroma row exists (orphan state, recoverable). Pins the SQLite-presence-implies-Chroma-presence invariant.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

### Context
`src/nexus/tuplespace/api.py:415-454` (`out()`) writes Chroma **first**, then commits SQLite. `tests/tuplespace/test_api_atomicity.py` already covers Chroma-fails-first (nexus-qmrr — `test_chroma_failure_leaves_no_sqlite_row` at 113), proving "SQLite presence implies Chroma presence."

This bead covers inverse: if `conn.execute(INSERT INTO tuples...)` or `conn.commit()` at api.py:444-454 raises *after* `index.out()` at 430 succeeded, Chroma record is orphaned with no SQLite row.

### Current documented behavior (api.py:415-424 comments)
Code explicitly accepts orphan Chroma:
- "Worst case is orphan Chroma record from prior partial write of same tuple_id"
- "Chroma upserts idempotent — reclaimed on retry"
- "retention sweeper picks up stragglers"

No active rollback. Tuple IDs deterministic (`_tuple_id(subspace, content, dimensions, mt)` at 391), so refire upserts same Chroma ID idempotently.

### Tests to add (in `tests/tuplespace/test_api_atomicity.py`)

1. **`test_sqlite_failure_after_chroma_leaves_orphan_chroma`** — monkeypatch `db_conn.execute` (or `commit`) to raise after `index.out` succeeds; assert:
   - `out()` raises SQLite error
   - SQLite has no row for tuple_id
   - Chroma **does** contain tuple_id (locks orphan-acceptance contract)
2. **`test_refire_after_sqlite_failure_recovers`** — call `out()` again identical args; assert consistent end state (idempotent Chroma upsert + new SQLite row on retry). Locks documented recovery model.

Default reading: lock orphan-accepted + idempotent-retry-recovers behavior with docstring naming alternatives.

### Implementation notes
- Reuse fixtures `db_conn`, `index`, `registry`, `chroma_client`, `_valid_task_dims()` already in file.
- Inspect Chroma directly via `TupleIndex` collection (`index._collections["tasks/<project>"].get(ids=[tid])`) — avoids semantic-search nondeterminism.
- Patch SQLite failure: `monkeypatch.setattr(db_conn, "execute", boom)` or wrap to fail only on `INSERT INTO tuples`.
- Reference nexus-qmrr (sibling invariant) and this bead in docstring.
- Deterministic, `chromadb.EphemeralClient`, tmp-path SQLite, no data-store mocks.

description:

## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

### Goal

title: Wrap migration sequence in a transaction or document rollback procedure
description:
Operational critic C5: t2_daemon.py:646-656 calls run_daemon_migrations then immediately logs success. If a migration raises mid-list, memory.db is partially-migrated and _nexus_version may not be updated. No transaction wrapper around the migration list; no _nexus_version-pinned recovery path. RDR-112 §9 promises per-migration idempotency (confirmed); cross-migration recovery is undefined.

Fix: either (a) wrap migration sequence in BEGIN/COMMIT (tricky with DDL), or (b) document recovery procedure when migrations partially fail (downgrade conexus, manually fix _nexus_version, re-run upgrade), or (c) snapshot/restore memory.db before migrations.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

### Problem
`src/nexus/db/migrations.py::apply_pending()` (lines 3554–3682) iterates `MIGRATIONS` (line 3128) and invokes `m.fn(conn)` sequentially. No outer `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`:
- Individual migrations call `conn.commit()` at their own boundaries (e.g. 1684, 1753, 3663).
- A few use explicit `BEGIN` (1684, 1753) or `with conn:` (2191).
- If migration N fails, 1..N-1 already committed; `_nexus_version.cli_version` updated only after loop (3658–3663). Partial state from failing migration N can wedge DB.
- `MigrationRetry` is sanctioned partial-failure path (3625–3651); hard `MigrationError` propagates with mixed state.

### Recommended approach: hybrid
Outer transaction not safe:
1. Several migrations rely on mid-fn `conn.commit()` (executescript, 100K-row backfills).
2. SQLite supports most DDL in transactions but WAL (set at 3761) + `ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN` under `_attach_catalog` (1972) interact awkwardly.

**Hybrid**:
1. **Per-migration atomicity audit** — verify every `MIGRATIONS` entry uses `with conn:` or explicit `BEGIN…COMMIT/ROLLBACK`. Wrap missing ones.
2. **Pre-migration backup** — before first step (3614), copy `memory.db` to `memory.db.bak-<from_version>` via `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` (WAL-safe). Keep last N.
3. **Document rollback** — add `## Migration Recovery` to `docs/architecture.md` or new `docs/MIGRATIONS.md`: identify failing step from `migration_step_start`/`migration_step_done` structlog (3618, 3635); restore `.bak-<version>`; `MigrationRetry` vs `MigrationError`; re-run via `nx upgrade`.

### Constraints
- **Daemon mode** (`NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon`, 3718): `run_if_needed` is client no-op; daemon owns migrations (RDR-112 P0-gate, nexus-907o/w0et). Backup logic in `apply_pending`, not `run_if_needed`.
- Preserve `MigrationRetry` semantics (42–55, 3625–3651).
- `_upgrade_lock` (3734) + `_upgrade_done` remain source of truth.
- No `print()` — structlog `_log.info(event="migration_backup_created", …)`.
- Use `Connection.backup()` (online backup API), NOT file copy, due to WAL.
- Tests: `conftest._auto_migrate_t2_in_tests` shim — backups skippable via `NX_MIGRATION_BACKUP=0` or tmp_path heuristic.
- DDL-in-transaction caveats: `_attach_catalog`/`_detach_catalog` (1972, 1983), `_migrate_document_aspects_pk_via_apply_pending` (2486) cannot live inside parent transaction.

### Scope boundary
Recovery posture only. Do not refactor 41-entry MIGRATIONS list beyond adding missing per-fn transactions. Do not change version-gating logic (3658–3663).
close_reason: Closed

title: Add pid-liveness probe to find_t2_daemon() (stale discovery file)
description:
Operational critic C1: src/nexus/daemon/discovery.py:38-56 find_t2_daemon() reads JSON and returns without checking pid is alive or UDS path exists. Crash scenarios (hard reboot, SIGKILL, OOM, panic between _write_discovery and _unlink_discovery): bridge falls through to direct mode with WAL conflicts when a new daemon eventually starts.

Fix: in find_t2_daemon, send os.kill(pid, 0). On ProcessLookupError, unlink the discovery file and return None. Also verify uds_path exists; on missing, treat as stale.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

## Task
Add a PID liveness probe to `find_t2_daemon()` in `src/nexus/daemon/discovery.py` so stale discovery files (daemon killed without cleanup) are detected and treated as "no daemon present".

## Current state (discovery.py:38–56)
`find_t2_daemon()` reads `<config_dir>/t2_addr.<uid>` and returns the parsed JSON payload as-is. Payload contains a `pid` field. No liveness verification is performed. Note: the discovery path uses `t2_addr.<uid>` (not `t2_daemon.<uid>.addr` as worded in the bead title — the implementation is the source of truth).

## Implementation
After parsing the JSON:
1. Extract `pid = payload.get("pid")`.
2. If positive int, call `os.kill(pid, 0)`:
   - `ProcessLookupError` → daemon dead; log `t2_discovery_stale_pid` warning; best-effort `path.unlink(missing_ok=True)`; return `None`.
   - `PermissionError` → process under another uid; treat as live, return payload.
   - success → return payload.
3. Missing/invalid pid → warning, return `None`.

Keep existing `OSError`/`JSONDecodeError` handling intact.

## Constraints
- `os.kill(pid, 0)` is canonical POSIX liveness probe; no signal delivered.
- Stale-file removal must be best-effort, never raise. Use `missing_ok=True`, swallow `OSError`.
- PID reuse race unavoidable in principle; probe narrows window.
- Structured logging only.

## Tests
Add `tests/daemon/test_discovery_liveness.py`:
- Live PID (`os.getpid()`) → payload returned.
- Dead PID (spawn-and-wait subprocess, write its pid) → returns `None`, file removed.
- Missing `pid` key → returns `None`.
- Existing OSError/JSONDecodeError paths still return `None` (regression).

Use tmp_path + `config_dir` parameter for isolation.

## Callers (no changes expected)
- `src/nexus/mcp/core.py` — daemon-mode T2Client construction.
- `src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py` — hook tuple routing.
- `tests/cockpit/test_hook_bridge_daemon_routing.py`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix _resolve_nx_bin multi-token fallback for launchd/systemd substitution
description:
Operational critic C6: commands/daemon.py:657-667 returns f'{sys.executable} -m nexus.cli' when shutil.which('nx') fails. The plist <string>__NX_BIN__</string> is a single ProgramArguments slot — multi-token string produces invalid plist (launchctl silently refuses). systemd ExecStart parses first token as executable; '/path/python -m nexus.cli ...' becomes ExecStart=/path/python with the rest as one argv element.

Fix: render NX_BIN as a structured token list. For plist: emit multiple <string> entries. For systemd: emit bare-word tokens. Alternative: refuse install if 'which nx' fails (require canonical install).
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

**Location correction:** Bead names `src/nexus/daemon/install.py`, but function actually lives at `src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:657-667`.

### Current behavior (`src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:657`)
```python
def _resolve_nx_bin() -> str:
    found = shutil.which("nx")
    if found:
        return found
    return f"{sys.executable} -m nexus.cli"   # ← multi-token string
```

Splatted via `str.replace("__NX_BIN__", nx_bin)` into two templates under `src/nexus/_resources/daemon/`:
- **`com.nexus.t2.plist`** — `__NX_BIN__` sits inside a single `<string>` element of `ProgramArguments`. launchd treats that as the *executable path*; `/usr/bin/python3 -m nexus.cli` interpreted as single binary, fails with `posix_spawn: No such file or directory`. **This is the bug.**
- **`nexus-t2.service`** — `ExecStart=__NX_BIN__ daemon t2 start --foreground`. systemd *does* split on whitespace, so multi-token happens to work but is fragile.

### Fix approach (preferred)
**Return a token list** from `_resolve_nx_bin` (`list[str]`) and change rendering:
- plist: splice into `<array>` with one `<string>` per token.
- systemd: shlex-quoted join into `ExecStart=`.
- Single-token case is `[found]`.

Alternative: generate a shim script. Approach (1) lower blast radius, matches bead text.

### Tests
- Update `tests/commands/test_daemon_autostart.py:54` `test_resolve_nx_bin_uses_which`.
- Update `tests/commands/test_daemon_autostart.py:59` `test_resolve_nx_bin_falls_back_to_python_module` — new shape.
- Add render-template test: multi-token fallback through both templates; plist has N `<string>` children; systemd `ExecStart=` round-trips through `shlex.split`.

### Constraints
- No hardcoded `/usr/local/bin/nx`.
- Tests stay deterministic — no real `launchctl`/`systemctl`.
- Templates under `src/nexus/_resources/daemon/`; force-included in wheel.
- Decide whether `__NX_BIN__` marker expands to multiple `<string>` tags or template restructured in Python.

title: Fix launchd / systemd flap loop on 'nx daemon t2 stop'
description:
Operational critic C4: launchd plist has KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }; systemd unit has Restart=on-failure. On SIGTERM (which 'nx daemon t2 stop' likely sends), the process exits 128+SIGNUM (143). Both supervisors treat exit 143 as failure and respawn instantly, making 'stop' ineffective under autostart.

Fix:
- systemd: add SuccessExitStatus=143 to nx/daemon/nexus-t2.service.
- launchd: review KeepAlive policy; consider 'ExitTimeOut + Crashed' alternative to SuccessfulExit=false, OR signal-handler that exits 0 on SIGTERM.
- Test: install autostart, run 'stop', verify daemon stays down.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

### Problem
`nx daemon t2 stop` (src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:156-189) sends SIGTERM to the daemon PID. If bootstrapped via autostall, the supervisor respawns:
- **launchd plist** (`nx/daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist`): `KeepAlive = { SuccessfulExit = false }` + `RunAtLoad=true`.
- **systemd unit** (`nx/daemon/nexus-t2.service`): `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=5s`.

### Resolution options
1. **(a) Stop-aware unstow** — detect loaded unit (`launchctl print gui/$UID/com.nexus.t2` / `systemctl --user is-active nexus-t2.service`), use supervisor's stop verb.
2. **(b) Refuse-with-message** — detect supervised mode, refuse, instruct user to run `nx daemon t2 uninstall --autostart`.
3. **(c) Change `KeepAlive` semantics** — drop `KeepAlive` / set `Restart=no`. Defeats auto-recovery.

**Recommendation: (a) with `--keep-loaded` escape hatch.** Add helper `_is_supervised()`. macOS: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.nexus.t2`. Linux: `systemctl --user stop nexus-t2.service`. For symmetry `start` should `launchctl bootstrap` / `systemctl --user start` when unit file exists.

### Files
- `src/nexus/commands/daemon.py` — extend `stop_cmd` (156), likely `start_cmd`. Reuse `_autostart_platform`, `_LAUNCHD_LABEL`, `_autostart_install_dir`, `_autostart_filename`.
- `nx/daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist` — narrow `KeepAlive` to `Crashed`.
- `nx/daemon/nexus-t2.service` — verify SIGTERM exit code in `src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py`.
- `tests/commands/test_daemon_autostart.py` — stop-while-supervised cases.
- Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md` daemon section.

### Constraints
- Don't break unsupervised stop (SIGTERM by PID when no supervisor unit).
- `launchctl bootout` on `gui/$UID` domain works without sudo.
- Idempotency: `bootout` nonzero if already unloaded — treat as success.
- Verify daemon SIGTERM path returns exit 0; otherwise launchd respawns regardless.
- Tests use `subprocess.run` monkeypatching, no real `launchctl`/`systemctl`.

title: Auto-invoke or strongly prompt 'nx daemon t2 install --autostart' on first run
description:
Operational critic C3: pyproject.toml ships templates inside the wheel but install --autostart is never auto-invoked. No post-install hook (pip wheels don't run them), no SessionStart prompt in the plugin, no nx doctor auto-remediation. The discovery file does not appear until manual daemon start. Bridge writes during that window go to direct mode and contend with the daemon when it finally starts. _ROUTING_TBA='daemon' silently degrades.

Options (pick one):
- Add to nx doctor an auto-remediation prompt.
- Add SessionStart hook that prompts 'run nx daemon t2 install --autostart for full ORB cockpit features'.
- Add nx upgrade --auto invocation of install --autostart if env supports it.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

### Problem
First-time `nx` users have no T2 daemon installed. T2 silently falls back to **direct-mode** (per-process SQLite open), so cross-MCP-process state sharing silently degrades. No user-facing signal; no nudge in `nx doctor` or first-run.

### Goal
Either (a) auto-install autostart on first `nx` invocation with consent prompt, or (b) emit strongly-worded actionable warning from `nx doctor` and first-run CLI path naming `nx daemon t2 install --autostart`.

### Surface area
The autostart machinery already exists — this bead is about **discovery and invocation**.
- `src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:600-770` — `install --autostart` already implemented (RDR-112, nexus-6w0c).
- `src/nexus/cli.py:70-140` — `main()` has direct-mode branch on `NX_STORAGE_MODE != "daemon"` (line 102). Natural hook point.
- `src/nexus/commands/doctor.py` — gap: doesn't recommend autostart when daemon absent.
- `src/nexus/session.py:79` — "first run, file not created" pattern.

### Implementation
1. Probe: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.t2.plist` (darwin) or `~/.config/systemd/user/nexus-t2.service` (linux). Helpers: `_autostart_install_dir()`, `_autostart_filename()` at daemon.py:621,670.
2. **Option A (auto-install consent)**: in `cli.py:main()`, when direct-mode + no autostart + TTY, prompt. Persist `~/.config/nexus/no_autostart` marker.
3. **Option B (warn loudly)**: `click.echo(..., err=True)` on first-run direct-mode. Add `nx doctor` check.
4. Respect `NX_STORAGE_MODE=direct` opt-out.
5. TTY-gate all prompts (cf. `cli.py:128-130`).

### Edge cases
- Don't auto-install in CI — gate on `sys.stdin.isatty()` + absence of `CI` env var.
- Unsupported platforms — warn-only.
- Subagent / MCP-spawned `nx` — detect via `NX_T1_HOST` / `CLAUDE_*` env vars, short-circuit.

title: Wire _BindingWatcher.start() into cockpit startup path
description:
Architectural critic S1: _BindingWatcher shipped in PR #787 (nexus-0xaq) is fully implemented in src/nexus/cockpit/bindings.py but NO caller imports/instantiates it. No reference in src/nexus/mcp/core.py, src/nexus/commands/cockpit.py, or any daemon module. Cockpit show/dashboard are static one-shots. RDR-111 Phase 2 Step 6 requires the watcher to run as a long-lived async task. As deployed, no binding ever reacts to any event. Closing nexus-0xaq under-delivered.

Fix: instantiate and start _BindingWatcher from the daemon startup path (most natural home) or via a cockpit CLI 'nx cockpit watch'. Coordinate with CA-5 binding-reaction-latency benchmark (RDR-111:373) which cannot close until this lands.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

## Goal
Wire the `_BindingWatcher` reaction loop into the cockpit/daemon startup path so that loaded binding profiles actually fire on tuple events. Today `bindings.py` defines a complete polling loop (`_BindingWatcher.run()` / `request_stop()`) but no code path constructs or schedules a watcher — bindings are loaded for the `nx cockpit show active-bindings` panel only. The daemon starts, `tuples.db` accumulates `events` rows, and nothing reacts.

## Naming note
The bead asks for `start()` / `stop()`. The current class exposes `run()` (the loop coroutine) and `request_stop()` (set-stop-event). Either:
- (a) add thin `start()` / `stop()` wrappers on `_BindingWatcher` that create the task and await it on stop (preferred — matches the bead title and the docstring example at `bindings.py:463-474`), or
- (b) keep `run()` / `request_stop()` and call those directly from the daemon.

Pick (a); it gives the daemon a uniform lifecycle handle and lets `T2Daemon.stop()` await the watcher without exposing the task field.

## Required changes

1. **Lifecycle wrappers** in `src/nexus/cockpit/bindings.py` (around `_BindingWatcher`, lines 456-622):
   - `def start(self) -> asyncio.Task` — creates and stores `self._task = asyncio.create_task(self.run())`, returns it. Idempotent.
   - `async def stop(self) -> None` — calls `self.request_stop()`, awaits `self._task` with bounded timeout (~5s, matching `t2_daemon.py:744`).

2. **Daemon wiring** in `src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py`:
   - In `T2Daemon.start()` (line 630), after the builtin-seed block (~691) and sockets bind (~711), construct one `_BindingWatcher`. Load profiles via `load_profiles_dir(default_profiles_dir())`. Build `BindingContext(conn, index, registry)` from `self._tuplespace_service`. Store as `self._binding_watcher`.
   - In `T2Daemon.stop()` (line 721), between retention-cancel (727-734) and server close, `await self._binding_watcher.stop()`. Mirror retention pattern.
   - Add `NX_COCKPIT_BINDINGS_DISABLE=1` env override (consistent with `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE`).

3. **Connection reuse** — daemon owns one SQLite connection on `tuples.db` already. Reuse it; do NOT open a second connection (`check_same_thread` issue noted at `bindings.py:511-518`).

4. **Profile discovery** — `default_profiles_dir()` returns `nx/tuplespace/builtin/bindings/profiles` (`bindings.py:630-635`).

## Dependency
Blocked on **nexus-8wvs** (idempotency table). Without it, a crash between `_dispatch_event` and `_save_cursor` (`bindings.py:576-587`) replays events on restart with no dedup.

## Test plan
- Add tests for `start()`/`stop()` wrappers in `tests/cockpit/test_binding_watcher.py` (idempotent start, stop-before-start, timeout).
- New integration test under `tests/daemon/`: spawn `T2Daemon`, write a tuple, assert binding fires within ~250ms.
- Verify `NX_COCKPIT_BINDINGS_DISABLE=1` short-circuits construction.
- Daemon shutdown ≤5s end-to-end.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add action_idempotency table + check-before-dispatch (RDR-111 line 933)
description:
Architectural critic Critical: RDR-111 lines 909-942 specify an action_idempotency DDL table, pre-dispatch SELECT 1 check, post-dispatch INSERT, and nightly sweep. None of these exist in the codebase. _tick advances cursor after dispatch (correct) but with no dedup. Watcher crash between _dispatch_event and _save_cursor leaves cursor at pre-event value; restart replays events with no idempotency check. At-least-once contract broken.

Fix: add action_idempotency to TUPLES_SCHEMA_DDL (src/nexus/tuplespace/store.py) or a new tuples_db migration, check in _dispatch_action before executing (src/nexus/cockpit/bindings.py), insert after success, sweep in retention loop. Schema given verbatim in RDR-111:933.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

## Goal
Implement RDR-111 §lines 909-942 idempotency contract: add `action_idempotency` dedup table to `memory.db`, gate `_dispatch_action` on a pre-execute SELECT, INSERT the key on success, and sweep expired rows in the liveness/retention loop. Without this, a watcher crash between `_dispatch_event` and `_save_cursor` (bindings.py:576-582) replays events on restart with no dedup — the at-least-once contract is broken because handlers have no way to detect duplicates.

## Required changes

1. **Schema migration** — add a new `migrate_action_idempotency_table` function in `src/nexus/db/migrations.py` (sibling to `migrate_liveness_table` at line 2847) and register it in the migration list near line 3328. Per RDR-111:933 verbatim:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS action_idempotency (
       idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
       expires_at      REAL NOT NULL  -- epoch seconds; TTL default 300s
   );
   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_action_idempotency_expires ON action_idempotency (expires_at);
   ```
   Target DB: `memory.db` (NOT `tuples.db` — RDR is explicit: "home: `memory.db`, added via `src/nexus/db/migrations.py`, same migration entry as `liveness`").

2. **Action descriptor field** — extend `Action` dataclass at `src/nexus/cockpit/bindings.py:92` with `idempotency_key: str | None = None`. Compute default in the binding event-loop as `sha256(binding.name + event.tuple_id).hexdigest()` (RDR-111:923).

3. **Pre-dispatch check + post-dispatch insert** — wrap `_dispatch_action` body (bindings.py:276): SELECT 1 on the key; if hit, log `binding_action_dedup_skip` and return success. After successful dispatch, INSERT the key with `expires_at = time.time() + 300`. Skip the check for `kind == "log"` (idempotent already) — only `python` (and future `tool_call`) actions need dedup.

4. **Sweep** — add `DELETE FROM action_idempotency WHERE expires_at < unixepoch()` to the liveness sweep task (locate via `grep migrate_liveness_table` callers / liveness sweep loop).

## Test plan
- Unit: migration applies idempotently; second `_dispatch_action` call with same key is a no-op (count handler invocations == 1).
- Crash-replay: simulate dispatch → no cursor save → restart → replay; assert handler not re-invoked.
- TTL: insert key with `expires_at` in past → sweep → row gone; subsequent dispatch executes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE in hook bridge (privacy claim violation)
description:
Security critic C1: docs/tuplespace-env.md:44,67 + src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:976 + src/nexus/commands/cockpit.py:80 reference NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE as the user-facing escape hatch. Nothing in src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py or nx/hooks/scripts/orb_bridge_*.py reads the variable. emit() only gates on CLAUDECODE. Users who set NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE=1 are still observed.

Fix: in emit() after the CLAUDECODE check, add:
  if os.environ.get('NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE', '').strip() not in ('', '0', 'false', 'False'):
      return
Also short-circuit output_for_hook() if RDR-111 requires (verify).
Lock the semantics of '0' / 'false' / '' in RDR-111.
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-16)

**Problem.** Documentation and operator-facing tools (`docs/tuplespace-env.md`, `nx doctor`, `nx cockpit status`) advertise `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE=1` as the user-facing kill switch for the RDR-111 hook-to-tuple bridge. The variable is never actually read by the bridge. `emit()` in `src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py` gates only on `CLAUDECODE` (line 259). Users following the documented opt-out are still observed — a P0 privacy-claim-vs-behaviour violation surfaced by the RDR-110–113 360° critique.

**Fix scope.**

1. In `emit()` (`src/nexus/cockpit/hook_bridge.py:227`), immediately after the `CLAUDECODE` guard at line 259, add a second guard reading `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE`:

   ```python
   if os.environ.get("NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE", "").strip() not in ("", "0", "false", "False"):
       _log.debug("hook_bridge_skip_disabled", hook_type=hook_type)
       return
   ```

   Lock the semantics: empty / `"0"` / `"false"` / `"False"` are "disabled flag is OFF" (bridge runs). Any other non-empty value (`"1"`, `"true"`, `"yes"`, etc.) disables the bridge. Document this in the function docstring alongside the existing RF-5 note.

2. **Verify `output_for_hook()` behaviour.** `output_for_hook()` (line 206) is a pure function not gated on `CLAUDECODE` — by design per the existing docstring, because Claude Code still needs a valid hook response (e.g. `PermissionRequest` transparent-allow JSON) even when emission is silenced. RDR-111 §RF-5 explicitly separates "do not contaminate non-Claude environments with tuples" from "do not break the hook protocol". Re-read RDR-111 to confirm whether `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE` should also short-circuit `output_for_hook()` (the bead notes this requires verification). Recommendation: do **not** short-circuit `output_for_hook()` — disabling tuple emission must not corrupt the user's tool flow with a missing or malformed hook response. If RDR-111 disagrees, update the RDR rather than weaken the hook protocol.

3. **Tests.** Add cases to `tests/cockpit/test_hook_bridge.py` covering:
   - `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE` unset → emit proceeds (existing behaviour).
   - `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE=""` / `"0"` / `"false"` / `"False"` → emit proceeds.
   - `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE="1"` / `"true"` / `"yes"` / `" 1 "` (whitespace) → emit returns early; no tuplespace side-effects (assert no `_direct_out` / `_emit_routed` call via injected mocks or zero rows after the call).
   - With `CLAUDECODE` set but `NX_BRIDGE_DISABLE=1`, `output_for_hook("PermissionRequest")` still returns the transparent-allow JSON (regression guard for the hook protocol).

4. **Docs.** `docs/tuplespace-env.md:44,67` already documents the variable; reconcile the wording so it matches the implemented truthy/falsy semantics (list the recognised falsy tokens `""`, `"0"`, `"false"`). Confirm `doctor.py:976` and `cockpit.py:80` messages stay accurate.

**Out of scope.** Other env vars (`NX_T1_ISOLATED`, `NEXUS_SKIP_T1`). Routing changes. Daemon path (the disable check belongs in `emit()` before routing, so it covers both daemon and direct fallback automatically).

description: PR #618 (fd09a7f4) made document_chunks manifest authoritative for chunk identity, but documents.chunk_count is a denormalized cache that's only initialized to 0 (at catalog-register time, which runs before per-file indexing). title: P0: _prune_deleted_files silently wipes collection when manifest is empty (RDR-108 Phase 4 review S1)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay review (substantive-critic agent a55f4d22df1ba44b9, scratch finding tag izay-finding,substantive-critic).

## Problem
src/nexus/indexer.py:_prune_deleted_files (lines 1644-1689) guards on \`catalog is None\` but NOT on \`catalog is not None and document_chunks is empty\`. When \`chashes_for_collection\` returns an empty set (manifest never populated, or migration in flight), every chunk in the collection is classified as orphan via \`if chash not in referenced\` and gets deleted. This fires on first \`nx index repo\` run after the schema migration lands on a system that has not yet run manifest backfill.

## Impact
SILENT FULL-COLLECTION WIPE on the first index run post-migration. The unsafe_skipped log path covers chunks lacking chunk_text_hash but does NOT cover the empty-manifest case.

## Fix
Add at the top of the per-collection loop (after \`chashes_for_collection\`):

\`\`\`python
if not referenced:
    _log.warning(
        \"manifest_empty_skipping_gc\",
        collection=collection_name,
        note=\"manifest is empty; cannot determine orphans safely. \"
             \"Run 'nx catalog backfill-manifest' to populate.\",
    )
    continue
\`\`\`

## Acceptance
- The guard is in place.
- Regression test asserts: when manifest is empty for a collection that has T3 chunks, no chunks are deleted and a warning is logged.
- Existing _prune_deleted_files tests pass unchanged.
close_reason: Closed
