title: RDR-108 D1 indexer write-path bug: duplicate IDs in batch upsert
description:
## Symptom

Re-indexing a real-world repo crashes with:

\`\`\`
chromadb.errors.DuplicateIDError: Expected IDs to be unique, found 13
duplicated IDs: 7b5cd95cc4cfaf2870f4143eea386795, ... in upsert.
\`\`\`

Reproduction: \`nx index repo /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/scheme-evolution-research --force\`
on the post-nexus-kmb6 indexer.

## Root cause

After nexus-kmb6 retargeted the indexer write paths to use
\`chunk_text_hash[:32]\` as the Chroma natural ID (RDR-108 D1),
identical chunk text in the same batch produces duplicate IDs.
ChromaDB's \`col.upsert\` rejects duplicates in a single batch
(unlike the per-call upsert semantics, the within-batch contract
requires unique ids).

The reidentify verb already handles this via \`seen_new_ids\`
deduplication (\`t3_reidentify.py:218-224\`), but the indexer
write path \`T3Database._write_batch\` does not. All 5 indexers
(code, prose PDF, prose markdown, doc PDF + streaming, plus
\`T3Database.put\`) flow through this single chokepoint, so the
fix is centralized.

## Fix

Add a duplicate-ID dedup step in \`T3Database._write_batch\`
before the chunked \`col.upsert\` loop. Keep the first occurrence
(first-wins is content-equivalent to last-wins under D1 since
identical chunk_text yields identical content + embedding +
metadata in the canonical fields).

Log at info level with the dedup count so operators can correlate
with collection collapse rates.

## Test gap

The original nexus-kmb6 test suite used distinct chunk content per
test, so the within-batch duplicate scenario was never exercised.
Tests that flag identical-content scenarios (e.g. boilerplate
copyright headers, repeated license blurbs across files) would
have caught this.

## Affected files

- \`src/nexus/db/t3.py\` (\`_write_batch\`, ~511-533)
- \`tests/test_t3.py\` (regression test for batch-dedup contract)

## Refs

- nexus-kmb6: indexer write-path retargeting (introduced the regression)
- t3_reidentify.py:218-224: the existing dedup pattern this commit ports
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: RDR-108 Phase 1 remediation T-D: manifest read API + event-sourced backfill (Phase 2 prerequisite)
description:
RDR-108 Phase 1 multi-lens review identified manifest layer is write-only and bypasses event-sourced authority. This is the Phase 2 sequencing prerequisite — must land BEFORE nexus-jc63 (T3 chunk re-upsert) starts.

## Findings to address

K6 (architecture A-S1): Manifest is write-only — no Catalog.get_manifest read API
- Catalog.write_manifest exists at catalog/catalog.py:1449-1455
- No corresponding read API
- Phase 2 (nexus-jc63) strips doc_id/chunk_index/chunk_count from T3 chunk metadata
- Phase 4 retrieval rewrites need to read manifest, but cannot proceed without read API
- Without this, Phase 2 BREAKS retrieval

Fix: add to Catalog (delegating to a new module or catalog_writes/catalog_reads):
```python
def get_manifest(self, doc_id: str) -> list[ManifestRow]:
    """Return ordered list of (position, chash, chunk_index, line_start, line_end, char_start, char_end)
    for the document's chunks. Empty list when no manifest entries exist."""
```

Plus the cross-doc helper used by Phase 4 doc-grouping:
```python
def docs_for_chashes(self, chashes: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[doc_id]]:
    """Reverse-lookup: given chash values, return mapping chash -> [doc_id]."""
```

K7 (migration CRIT-5): mydi backfill bypasses event-sourced authority
- catalog_db.py:443-463 direct-INSERTs collections rows on every CatalogDB open
- Default mode is event-sourced (events.jsonl is canonical, SQLite is projection)
- Backfilled rows have no backing CollectionCreated event
- Catalog.rebuild() (catalog_db.py:498-510) does DELETE FROM collections + JSONL replay → backfilled rows vanish
- Audit tools comparing events.jsonl to projection flag every legacy_grandfathered=1 row as a phantom

Fix: emit synthetic CollectionCreated event per backfilled name with legacy_grandfathered=1
- Need to verify event payload supports this flag (catalog/events.py)
- May need a new event type if CollectionCreated doesn't carry the flag
- Update projector to handle the flag

OBS-3 (migration): indexing pipelines don't write to document_chunks yet
- After nexus-mydi/j43k landed, manifest backfilled but new ingest still creates chunks without manifest entries
- Manifest goes stale immediately after any new index run until operator re-runs nx t3 backfill-manifest
- Fix: wire manifest write into the post-store hook chain (catalog_writes.write_manifest after each chunk batch)
- Phase 1 → Phase 2 dependency

SG-3 (coverage): >300 chunk batching test
- write_manifest at catalog_writes.py:697 batches at 300 inside a single transaction
- No test verifies a >300-chunk doc produces multiple INSERT batches
- Fix: add a regression test with 350-chunk fixture

## Branch / PR

- Branch: feature/nexus-rdr108-r-d-manifest-read-api off develop
- Touches: src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py, src/nexus/catalog/catalog_writes.py (or new catalog_reads.py), src/nexus/catalog/catalog_db.py (replace backfill with event emission), src/nexus/catalog/projector.py (handle legacy_grandfathered flag), src/nexus/catalog/events.py (if new event type needed), post-store hook wiring
- May conflict with T-A on catalog_db.py if T-A touches it; coordinate
- Phase 2 BLOCKS-ON this landing
notes: PR #614 opened. ManifestRow dataclass + get_manifest() + docs_for_chashes() in catalog_writes._WriteOps. Event-sourced backfill via _emit_backfilled_collection_events. Post-store hook manifest_write_batch_hook registered in mcp_infra/core. 27 new tests passing. Auto-merge enabled.
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: RDR-108 Phase 1 remediation T-B: drain protocol UX + tests
description:
RDR-108 Phase 1 multi-lens review (i35j) surfaced drain-protocol gaps in he24's implementation.

## Findings to address

S-5 (code-quality): drain_worker thread.join(timeout=2.0) silent — return value not checked, no log on timeout. Operator-diagnostic gap.

title: P0: RDR-108 Phase 1 remediation T-A: migration plumbing (FK CASCADE, drain wiring, atomicity, ATTACH)
description:
RDR-108 Phase 1 multi-lens review (i35j) surfaced critical migration plumbing issues. This bead bundles them.

## Findings to address

K1 (FK CASCADE — architecture A-C2 + migration CRIT-1):
- document_chunks.doc_id REFERENCES documents(tumbler) has NO ON DELETE CASCADE
- After backfill, ALL 5 deletion paths fail with IntegrityError:
  - projector.py:295-298 (DocumentDeleted event handler)
  - catalog_db.py:498 (rebuild — DELETE FROM documents)
  - dedupe.py:379 (batch delete)
  - catalog_writes.py:765 (delete_document)
  - catalog_sync.py:529 (full wipe + rebuild)
- Fix: add ON DELETE CASCADE to FK; new migration recreates the table (12-step ALTER, since CREATE IF NOT EXISTS won't pick up FK changes on existing DBs)
- Audit each deletion site: verify CASCADE handles them OR add explicit DELETE FROM document_chunks WHERE doc_id = ? before the parent DELETE

K2 (drain_worker has zero callers — architecture A-C1 + migration SIG-3,5):
- _migrate_aspect_queue_pk_via_apply_pending raises MigrationError if queue is non-empty
- Nothing calls drain_worker() before apply_pending invocation
- T2Database.__init__ runs apply_pending; if AspectWorker has in-flight rows → MigrationError → crash → re-runs forever (boot loop)
- Fix: wire drain_worker(timeout=30) into _migrate_aspect_queue_pk_via_apply_pending BEFORE the precondition check
- Add nx aspects drain CLI verb for operator-driven recovery
- MigrationError message must include actionable nx aspects drain command

K3 (executescript() atomicity gap — code-quality C-2):
- conn.executescript('CREATE TABLE new ... DROP TABLE old ... RENAME ...') autocommits each DDL
- Crash between DROP and RENAME loses the table entirely
- Both migrate_document_aspects_pk_to_doc_id AND migrate_aspect_extraction_queue_pk_to_doc_id affected
- Fix: replace executescript with explicit conn.execute() inside `with conn:` (or BEGIN/COMMIT)

K5 (ATTACH SQL injection — code-quality C-1 + migration OBS-5):
- migrations.py:~1878 uses f-string: f'ATTACH DATABASE \\'{catalog_db_path}\\' AS cat_db'
- Path with single quote breaks ATTACH (e.g. /Users/O'Brien/...)
- Fix: conn.execute('ATTACH DATABASE ? AS cat_db', (str(catalog_db_path),))

K8 (dedup query correctness — migration CRIT-4 + code-quality S-4 + coverage O-3):
- migrations.py:2087-2106: HAVING extracted_at = MAX(extracted_at) is a misleading no-op
- Actual dedup relies on ORDER BY DESC + INSERT OR IGNORE — undocumented SQLite behavior
- Refactor "fixing" the misleading HAVING silently breaks dedup
- Fix: rewrite as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY doc_id ORDER BY extracted_at DESC) CTE

K11 (migration skip caching — migration SIG-2):
- _migrate_*_via_apply_pending early-returns if catalog DB absent
- _upgrade_done caches success state → migration permanently skipped on first-open even if catalog later appears
- Fix: don't cache "skipped" state; require catalog presence to mark migration complete

## Tests to add (from coverage lens)

- CG-2: apply_pending no-catalog-path test (early-return is currently untested)
- SG-4: high-volume orphan threshold boundary (exactly 10 rows: > 10 strict means 10 silently deleted; verify intent)

## Code-quality fixes (small)

- S-3: _has_doc_id_pk cache check race (move hasattr inside the lock — broken double-checked lock pattern, db/t2/document_aspects.py:166-174)
- O-5: Replace WHERE physical_collection NOT IN (SELECT ...) with INSERT OR IGNORE (catalog_db.py:447) — perf

## Branch / PR

- Branch: feature/nexus-rdr108-r-a-migration-plumbing off develop
- PR targets develop
- Closes parent nexus-i35j partially

## Dependencies

- None at start; runs in parallel with R-B/C/D/E
- May conflict with R-E on db/t2/__init__.py — coordinate at merge time

title: RDR-108 Phase 4 S2: manifest-based GC rewrite (_prune_deleted_files via catalog.chashes_for_collection)
description:
## Context
RDR-108 re-gate hazard S2. After Phase 2 strips doc_id from T3 chunk metadata, indexer.py:1606-1620 (_prune_deleted_files) becomes a no-op for migrated collections — silently re-creating the stale-chunk root bug RDR-108 set out to fix. RDR-101 RF-3 stated 'GC keys on chunk_id, not chash, because chash is non-unique across documents'; under the manifest model the answer is 'GC keys on absence-from-manifest in the catalog'.

RDR file: docs/rdr/rdr-108-graph-identity-normalization.md § Phase 4 GC rewrite (re-gate S2)
Branch: feature/rdr-108-graph-identity-normalization

## Goal
Replace _prune_deleted_files's metadata-based path with catalog.chashes_for_collection-based orphan detection.

New catalog helper:
  catalog.chashes_for_collection(physical_collection: str) -> set[str]
  -- SELECT DISTINCT substr(chash, 1, 32) FROM document_chunks dc
  --   JOIN documents d ON d.tumbler = dc.doc_id
  --   WHERE d.physical_collection = ?

GC contract:
  referenced = catalog.chashes_for_collection(col.name)
  for page of col.get(limit=300, include=[]):
    orphans = [cid for cid in page.ids if cid not in referenced]
  batch col.delete(orphan_ids) in 300-batches

## Files
- src/nexus/indexer.py:1606-1620 (_prune_deleted_files rewrite)
- src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py (new chashes_for_collection helper)
- src/nexus/commands/t3.py (gc subcommand integration if separate driver)

## Dependencies
- Phase 2 (nexus-jc63) must complete (depends on chash[:32] == natural ID identity)
- Phase 1b (nexus-j43k) must complete (manifest must be populated)

## Branch
feature/rdr-108-graph-identity-normalization

## TDD
- Test: orphan chunk (in T3 but not in manifest) is deleted.
- Test: live chunk (in manifest) is preserved.
- Test: empty manifest with chunks in T3 -> all deleted (covers fully-rotted doc).
- Test: post-fact pre-D1 [:16] chunk is deleted by manifest mismatch (cleanup of O1 mixed-state).
- Test: idempotent re-run (second run finds zero orphans).

- Sequential thinking for edge-case design
- TDD

title: RDR-108 Phase 1 S1: AspectWorker stop-and-drain protocol (pending AND in_progress)
description:
## Context
RDR-108 re-gate hazard S1. Pre-PK-swap precondition for D3.

The aspect_extraction_queue is a 3-state machine (pending / in_progress / failed). Workers transition rows pending->in_progress via claim_next (aspect_extraction_queue.py:317). Checking only status='pending' misses in-flight rows that lose their completion signal during the PK swap. The full check is:

  SELECT count(*) FROM aspect_extraction_queue WHERE status != 'failed';
  -- Must return 0 before the PK swap runs.

## Goal
Implement stop-and-drain control for AspectWorker:
1. Signal worker to stop claiming new rows (no new pending->in_progress transitions).
2. Wait for any in-progress rows to complete (poll the count check).
3. Verify SQL precondition returns 0 before PK swap.
4. Restart worker after PK swap completes.

## Files
- src/nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py:317 (claim_next path)
- AspectWorker thread location (search via Serena)
- new helper: stop_and_drain() routine, integrated into Phase 1c migration runner

## TDD
1. Test: stop signal blocks new claims.
2. Test: drain returns 0 iff queue has only failed rows.
3. Test: PK swap is gated on the precondition.
4. Test: worker restarts cleanly after swap.

## Branch
feature/rdr-108-graph-identity-normalization

## Reminders
- Use mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking to reason about race windows
- Serena: jet_brains_find_symbol AspectWorker; jet_brains_find_referencing_symbols for callers
- TDD
notes: PR #608 opened, commit d4d7e4c9. 17 new tests, 336 aspect-scoped tests green. is_drained() SQL: WHERE status != 'failed'. drain_worker(timeout=30, poll=0.1). Auto-merge enabled.

title: RDR-108 epic: graph identity normalization (catalog manifest + content-addressed T3)
description:
## Summary

Implement RDR-108: normalize identity across catalog/T3 so the catalog holds the document tree (manifest of chashes) and T3 becomes a flat content-addressed blob store. RDR file: docs/rdr/rdr-108-graph-identity-normalization.md (accepted 2026-05-08, gate PASSED).

## Locked decisions
- D1: T3 chunk natural ID = chunk_text_hash[:32] (pure content addressing)
- D2: catalog Document.chunks manifest (new document_chunks table)
- D3: document_aspects + aspect_extraction_queue PK migration to (doc_id) with drain-queue precondition (full status != 'failed' check)
- D4: RDR-107 superseded
- D5: chash_index drops chunk_chroma_id column

## Phases
- Phase 0 GATE: complete
- Phase 1: catalog schema migrations (manifest table, manifest backfill, aspect PK migration, cascade wiring)

title: RDR-108 Phase 1c: document_aspects + aspect_extraction_queue PK migration to (doc_id)
description:
## Symptom

T2 `memory.db.document_aspects` table holds 753 RDR-089 structured-aspect extractions. Cross-referenced against `~/.config/nexus/catalog/.catalog.db` `documents.physical_collection`:

- 181 / 753 (24.0%) match a current catalog physical_collection
- 107 / 753 (14.2%) match BOTH (physical_collection, file_path)
- **572 / 753 (76.0%) orphans** — extracted aspects pointing at collections the catalog no longer has

Orphan breakdown:

- **318 (42.2%)** reference legacy pre-RDR-103 collection names (e.g. `rdr__nexus-571b8edd`, `rdr__ART-8c2e74c0`, `code__Delos-5af9bfe0` style — should be `rdr__1-2188__voyage-context-3__v1` etc. post-RDR-103)
- **118 (15.7%)** reference test-fixture collection names (`knowledge__cli-*`, `knowledge__nexus-integration-test`, `knowledge__reproducer`, `knowledge__pagtest`, `knowledge__pagend`)
- **136 (~18%)** other (renamed/deleted collections, no clear pattern)

## Probe evidence (2026-05-08)

Top 15 aspect collections (most rows):

```
count= 224  rdr__nexus-571b8edd                       <- LEGACY
count= 104  knowledge__art-grossberg-papers__voyage-context-3__v1
count=  94  rdr__ART-8c2e74c0                         <- LEGACY
count=  78  knowledge__art-papers
count=  75  knowledge__reproducer                     <- TEST FIXTURE
count=  49  rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1            <- VALID
count=  44  knowledge__nexus-integration-test         <- TEST FIXTURE
count=  22  knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1
count=   6  knowledge__knowledge
count=   5  knowledge__pagtest__voyage-context-3__v1  <- TEST FIXTURE
```

Catalog has 133 distinct physical_collection values. Aspects has 59. Intersection: only 7.

## Why it matters

1. **Storage waste**: 572 rows × ~3 KB each = ~1.7 MB of stale extractions. Small in absolute terms but the trend is bad — every renamed/deleted collection leaves behind aspect rows forever.
2. **Re-extraction confusion**: when a document is re-extracted under a new collection name, the old aspect row remains, and lookups by (current_collection, file_path) miss the legacy data. The catalog/aspect path has no awareness of collection renames.
3. **Cost waste, retroactive**: ~$X spent on Claude haiku-4-5 calls (extractor `scholarly-paper-v1`) for these 572 orphan extractions. Not recoverable but informs the cleanup ROI.
4. **Cross-table drift confirmed**: parallel finding to nexus-mmf5 (chash_index 1,697 collections vs T3 150). Same root: tables that depend on collection names don't get reconciled when RDR-103 renames happen or when collections are deleted.

## Probe code

```python
mem = sqlite3.connect(...memory.db, ro)
cat = sqlite3.connect(...catalog/.catalog.db, ro)

# Distinct aspect collections vs catalog physical_collections
asp_set = {r[0] for r in mem.execute("SELECT DISTINCT collection FROM document_aspects")}
cat_pc_set = {r[0] for r in cat.execute("SELECT DISTINCT physical_collection FROM documents WHERE physical_collection != ''")}

# 76% orphan
orphan_collections = asp_set - cat_pc_set
orphan_rows = sum(mem.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM document_aspects WHERE collection = ?", (c,)).fetchone()[0] for c in orphan_collections)
```

## Fix outline

Two-pass cleanup mirrored on nexus-mmf5 (chash_index reconcile):

1. **Audit verb**: `nx aspects audit` — report orphan rows, classify by type (legacy / test-fixture / other), recommend disposition.
2. **Reconcile verb**: `nx aspects reconcile [--dry-run] [--apply] [--keep-test-fixtures]`
   - Test-fixture orphans: hard-delete (118 rows). They came from CLI tests that should never have persisted.
   - Legacy-collection-name orphans: try to map to current collection name via RDR-103 collection-name-authority lookup; if mapping found, UPDATE collection field. If not, hard-delete.
   - Other orphans: leave for manual review (one-off renamed collections).
3. **Prevention**: when `nx catalog rename-collection` runs (does this verb exist? if not, file separately), it must also update document_aspects.collection in the same transaction.
4. **Prevention 2**: when a collection is deleted via `nx t3 delete <coll>`, the deletion must cascade to chash_index, document_aspects, and any other tables keyed on physical_collection.

## Out of scope

- aspect_extraction_queue is empty (0 rows). No queue cleanup needed.
- document_aspects schema is otherwise healthy. The (collection, source_path) PK is correct; no PK violations.

## Affected files

- New: src/nexus/commands/aspects.py — `audit` and `reconcile` subcommands
- src/nexus/db/t2/aspects.py (or wherever document_aspects accessor lives) — bulk delete + bulk update by collection
- New: tests/test_aspects_reconcile.py
- src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py or commands/catalog.py — cascade collection-rename to dependent tables

## Refs

- 2026-05-08 prod-shakeout aspect probe (this bead's evidence)
- nexus-mmf5 (chash_index namespace drift, parallel surface)
- nexus-nifd (test-fixture cache file leakage, similar pattern from earlier probe)
- RDR-089 (structured aspects)
- RDR-103 (collection-name authority — the rename source)
notes: PR #610 opened, commit 6e9b27bb. 32 new tests + 555 aspect/migration tests pass. ATTACH DATABASE for cross-DB JOIN; high-volume threshold=10 fails loud; dedup by latest extracted_at; mark_done backward-compat preserved.

title: RDR-108 Phase 2: T3 chunk re-upsert with content-derived natural IDs (chunk_text_hash[:32])
description:
## Background

Probe on 2026-05-08 confirmed code__1-2188__voyage-code-3__v1 has 23,714/28,512 (83%) chunks involved in dupe groups; 1,630 (source_path, chunk_index) keys map to >1 chunk ID. Root cause: `src/nexus/code_indexer.py:298-496` (`index_code_file`) has no stale-chunk prune step. Doc/PDF path (`doc_indexer.py:697-717`) does prune; code path doesn't. See superseded bead nexus-j1ro for the prune-as-fix sketch.

User-Hal directs (2026-05-08): the architecturally correct fix is soft-delete, not hard-prune, because hard-prune breaks Xanadu's immutable-link discipline. This bead drafts the steady-state mechanism. Bead [A].

## Problem

When a code file is re-indexed with edits, all old chunk IDs become unreachable via current retrieval but remain physically present in T3. Two consequences:

1. **Storage drift**: every edit-then-reindex cycle leaks a chunk-set's worth of data; over months the working set bloats unboundedly.
2. **Link integrity gap**: external links pointing at the *old* chunk ID still resolve to its content (which is good for Xanadu fidelity), BUT current retrieval can return the same logical content twice (the new chunk + a stale older version), polluting search results.

Hard-prune solves #1 by deleting old chunks but breaks #2 (links 404). Soft-delete solves both: tombstone the old chunk, default-filter retrieval, retain link resolution.

## Proposed mechanism

### Schema additions to T3 chunk metadata

- `is_current: bool` — default True on insert; flipped to False when superseded
- `superseded_by: str` — optional; if set, points at the new chunk ID for redirect-style retrieval
- `superseded_at: ISO8601` — when the supersede flag flipped
- (optional) `version: int` — incrementing per (source_path, chunk_index) so consumers can request "give me v3 explicitly"

### Re-index hot path

After `ctx.db.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings(...)` in `code_indexer.py:467` (and the equivalent in `doc_indexer.py:665`):

```python
prune_where = _identity_where(file_path, corpus)
current_ids_set = set(ids)
to_supersede = []
offset = 0
while True:
    batch = _chroma_with_retry(col.get, where=prune_where, include=["metadatas"], limit=300, offset=offset)
    if not batch["ids"]:
        break
    for cid, md in zip(batch["ids"], batch["metadatas"]):
        if cid not in current_ids_set and md.get("is_current", True):
            to_supersede.append(cid)
    if len(batch["ids"]) < 300:
        break
    offset += 300
if to_supersede:
    _chroma_with_retry(col.update, ids=to_supersede,
        metadatas=[{"is_current": False, "superseded_at": now_iso, "superseded_by": ""} for _ in to_supersede])
```

Note: `chromadb.update` does metadata-only updates without re-embedding. Verify cost.

### Retrieval default

`store_get`, `search`, `query`, `nx_answer`, T3 retrieval helpers all default-filter `where={"is_current": True}` (or `where={"is_current": {"$ne": False}}` for backward compat with pre-existing chunks that lack the field). Add an explicit `include_superseded=True` flag for link-resolution paths.

### Link resolution path

When a catalog link references a chunk ID directly (`chash:` span), the resolver fetches the chunk regardless of `is_current` — that's the whole point: even superseded versions remain link-targets.

### Compaction (separate verb, separate bead)

HNSW index space + embedding cost still grow linearly with stale chunks. A `nx t3 vacuum-superseded --older-than=30d` verb physically drops chunks where `is_current=False AND superseded_at < now - 30d`. Mirrors RDR-106's `vacuum-backups`. NOT in scope of this bead — file separately if Bead [B] is approved.

## Architectural home

Two options:

(i) Extend RDR-106 (currently catalog-only) with a §"T3 chunk soft-delete" extension. Same pattern, sibling implementation. Keeps the soft-delete story in one document.

(ii) File RDR-107 as a sibling: T3 chunks have different mechanics (HNSW, embedding cost, retention compaction) that warrant their own treatment. Cross-link to RDR-106 and RDR-053 (Xanadu Fidelity).

Recommendation: (ii). RDR-106 is close to gate; loading T3 onto it now is scope creep. RDR-107 can move at its own pace and import the schema-pattern from RDR-106's tombstone work.

## Out of scope

- Cleanup of existing stale chunks (no `is_current` field at all on pre-fix chunks). Filed separately as Bead [B].
- HNSW vacuum / compaction. Filed separately after RDR-107 lands.
- Link-resolution path migration to honor superseded chunks. Tracked in RDR-053 follow-up.

## Tests

- regression: re-index a code file twice; assert pre-edit chunk's ID is still fetchable but `is_current=False`, post-edit chunk's ID is `is_current=True`, retrieval default-filters to the post-edit only
- contract: `_identity_where`-keyed prune query returns BOTH versions
- backward-compat: pre-fix chunks (no `is_current` key) are treated as current
- compaction: vacuum-superseded only removes chunks past the retention window

## Affected files

- src/nexus/code_indexer.py:298-496 (add supersede pass after upsert)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:697-717 (replace hard-delete with supersede)
- src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:918-985 (PDF path prune → supersede)
- src/nexus/metadata_schema.py (add `is_current`, `superseded_at`, `superseded_by` fields with defaults)
- All retrieval call sites: search, query, nx_answer, store_get, plus catalog resolvers
notes: Branch discipline (per Hal direction 2026-05-09): feature branch off develop, NOT main. Branch naming: feature/<bead-id>-<description>. PR targets develop. main only receives RDR docs + completed-and-reviewed develop merges via develop→main PR (pattern: PR #589). Develop is currently behind main; needs catch-up before Phase 1 starts.

title: P0: code_indexer.index_code_file lacks stale-chunk prune — re-index leaks old chunks
description:
## Symptom

Code collections accumulate stale chunks every time a file is edited and re-indexed. Quantified on code__1-2188__voyage-code-3__v1 (Nexus repo, 28,512 chunks):

- 25% of (source_path, chunk_index) keys have >1 chunk ID
- 83% of chunks (23,714 of 28,512) are involved in some dupe group
- 346 dupe-groups have IDENTICAL chunk_text_hash (chunk content unchanged but ID still differs)
- 1,284 dupe-groups have DIFFERENT chunk_text_hash (stale prior version of chunk content)

## Root cause

`src/nexus/code_indexer.py:298-496` (`index_code_file`) does:

  1. content read + hash
  2. staleness check
  3. chunk
  4. build chunk_chroma_id = sha256(f"{corpus}:{title}:chunk{i}")[:32]   where title = "{rel_path}:{line_start}-{line_end}"
  5. embed
  6. ctx.db.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings(...)
  7. fire post-store hooks
  8. return

There is no prune step. When a file is edited (any line shift above a chunk), the chunk's `line_start-line_end` title changes, so `chunk_chroma_id` changes, the upsert writes new IDs, and the old chunks are never deleted.

Compare `src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:697-717` (markdown / PDF path) which does have a prune:

```
prune_where = _identity_where(sp, corpus)   # {"doc_id": tumbler}
... col.get(where=prune_where, ...) → stale_ids = ids not in current_ids_set
... col.delete(ids=stale_ids[i:i+300])
```

The asymmetry is the bug.

## Reproduction

In any code__ collection:

```python
res = coll.get(limit=300, include=['metadatas'], offset=...)  # paginate
groups = defaultdict(list)
for _id, md in zip(ids, metadatas):
    groups[(md['source_path'], md['chunk_index'])].append(_id)
dupe_keys = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) > 1}  # nonzero
```

Concrete example from code__1-2188:
- tests/test_e2e.py chunk_index=4: 2 chunks with identical chunk_text_hash, different content_hash, indexed_at 2026-05-03 vs 2026-05-04. Same doc_id (1.2188.74) so a doc_id-keyed prune *would* find both.

## Fix outline

Mirror `doc_indexer._identity_where`-based prune in `code_indexer.index_code_file` after the upsert at line 473:

```python
from nexus.doc_indexer import _identity_where, _chroma_with_retry
prune_where = _identity_where(str(file_path), ctx.corpus)
current_ids_set = set(ids)
stale_ids = []
offset = 0
while True:
    batch = _chroma_with_retry(ctx.col.get, where=prune_where, include=[], limit=300, offset=offset)
    batch_ids = batch.get("ids", [])
    stale_ids.extend(eid for eid in batch_ids if eid not in current_ids_set)
    if len(batch_ids) < 300:
        break
    offset += 300
if stale_ids:
    for i in range(0, len(stale_ids), 300):
        _chroma_with_retry(ctx.col.delete, ids=stale_ids[i:i + 300])
```

## Open question — Xanadu immutability

Discussed with Hal: the architectural tension is whether stale chunks should be deleted or versioned. Right now they're silently leaked (neither). RDR-053 (Xanadu Fidelity, draft) is the natural place to choose: (a) prune-at-reindex (fix this bug), (b) keep all versions and add a is_current flag for retrieval to filter (Xanadu-true, but T3 grows unboundedly), (c) tombstone old chunks via a soft-delete column. RDR-106 already drafted Option B tombstones for catalog rows; T3 chunks deserve a parallel decision.

## Backfill

Independent of the fix: a one-shot sweep `nx t3 dedupe-stale --collection <coll>` to clean existing stale chunks. ~25% of 290k = ~72k stale chunks across the 15 code collections. Quantify per-collection before sweeping.

## Affected files

- src/nexus/code_indexer.py:298-496 (no prune)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:104-120 (_identity_where helper, reusable)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:697-717 (reference prune impl)

## Tests

- tests/test_code_indexer.py: add a regression test that re-indexes a modified file twice and asserts only the new chunk IDs remain
- tests/test_doc_indexer.py: confirm the existing prune still works (don't regress the md/pdf path)
notes: Superseded 2026-05-08 by user direction: hard-prune breaks Xanadu link immutability. Replaced with two beads: nexus-jc63 (P0, steady-state soft-delete) + nexus-b5mh (P1, one-shot backfill, blocked-by jc63). RDR-107 candidate to formalize T3 chunk soft-delete (sibling to RDR-106).
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: chunker emits oversized chunks for minified JS (50,917 bytes) - blocks re-embed
description: 2026-05-08 chunk-size audit found 84 chunks > Voyage MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (16384) in code__1-2188__voyage-code-3__v1, all from src/nexus/console/static/htmx.min.js at 50,917 bytes each (3.1× the limit). Plus 1 oversized in docs__1-2153 (chatsome CROSSMODAL_GPU_ARC docs, 17,572 bytes), 4 singletons elsewhere. These 85 chunks would FAIL on next re-embed call to Voyage — ChromaError: Quota exceeded. Root cause: chunker doesn't enforce SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES (12288) or MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (16384) hard cap. For minified files (single-line JS/CSS), line-based AST chunking can't help - need character-count splitting or a 'skip minified' content-type heuristic. Fix: add post-chunk validation in the indexer that hard-caps chunk text bytes, plus a pre-chunk filter that skips known minified extensions (.min.js, .min.css) by default with an opt-in flag. Also add 'nx catalog doctor --chunk-size-distribution' check that surfaces > MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES count + p99 + max bytes per collection. References: src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py QUOTAS for limits; src/nexus/indexer.py:1226 _pdf_chunks; AST chunker entry points.
notes:
2026-05-10 audit: the 84-oversized-chunks claim is no longer true on current prod T3. ``MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES`` audit returned 0 oversized chunks across all live collections. The RDR-108 reidentify pass cleaned them up.

Fix shape pivots accordingly:
- The T3 write-path guard (``db/t3.py:460`` ``MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES`` filter, drops oversized + structured warning) is already in place. Defense-in-depth holds.
- The chunker's ``_enforce_byte_cap`` (AST) + ``_line_chunk`` (line-fallback) byte-binary-search both cap at SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES. So new writes can't introduce the class.
- What was MISSING was the upstream skip: minified bundles (``htmx.min.js``, ``react.min.css``, ``vendor.bundle.js``) get classified as CODE on extension alone, then chunked with mostly-zero search signal (mangled identifiers), wasting Voyage budget even when the chunks fit.

Shipping the upstream skip rather than another byte-cap layer:
- ``classifier.py``: new ``_MINIFIED_BASENAME_PATTERNS`` (``.min.js``, ``.min.mjs``, ``.min.cjs``, ``.min.css``, ``.bundle.js``, ``.bundle.mjs``). Files matching these classify as SKIP unless the operator opts in via ``indexing_config["index_minified"] = True``.
- 8 new ``TestMinifiedBundleSkip`` cases lock the contract.

Closes nexus-haet.

title: P0: 95 T3 collections / 45,027 chunks lack doc_id metadata (catalog linkage broken)
description: 2026-05-08 deep T3 metadata audit found 95 of 150 collections (45,027 of 290,646 chunks, ~16% of T3 surface) have NO doc_id field at all in chunk metadata. Largest offenders: docs__default (12,007 chunks - in catalog), knowledge__knowledge (12,485 chunks - also missing chunk_index and content_hash, written by MCP memory_put path), knowledge__art (5,725), knowledge__delos (2,007). 86 of these 95 collections are 'docs__*' style with metadata {chunk_index, chunk_text_hash, content_hash, embedding_model} present but {doc_id, source_uri, content_type} MISSING. Functional impact: chunks are vector-searchable but cannot be linked back to catalog documents at chunk granularity. nx_answer / link traversal / coverage stats / aspect filtering all silently underreport for these 45k chunks. The catalog says 23,378 docs - but T3 has chunks for 45k more that have no document records at all. Also: 8 otherwise-conformant collections lack source_uri (RDR-096 unification didn't backfill). Action: (1) audit src/nexus/index/* and src/nexus/mcp/* for the older write paths that omit doc_id; (2) backfill doc_id onto existing chunks via chunk_text_hash → catalog doc_id mapping where possible; (3) re-index where mapping fails. Constraint: read-only investigation first; do NOT delete or rewrite T3 chunks until the older write paths are identified and gated. References: 2026-05-08 chunk-metadata fingerprint probe; src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py for write contracts; RDR-101 phases 4-5b for doc_id introduction; RDR-096 for source_uri unification.
notes:
2026-05-11 verification post PR #674 (orphan-backfill substrate):

Per `nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage --json`:
- docs__default: total=11496, with_doc_id=11496, coverage=1.0, pass=true
- knowledge__knowledge: total=12399, with_doc_id=12399, coverage=1.0, pass=true

- All 136 collections in audit: pass=true on doc_id coverage

The original concern ("95 collections / 45,027 chunks lack doc_id
metadata") is resolved. Every chunk now has a doc_id (catalog tumbler
or synthesized_orphan). The 18.72% global orphan_ratio is event-log

Closing.

title: P0: knowledge__art-papers (9,996 T3 chunks) orphaned from catalog (UUID doc_ids)
description: 2026-05-08 T3 health probe found knowledge__art-papers has 9,996 T3 cloud chunks but ZERO matching catalog documents. Sample chunk metadata shows UUID-style doc_ids (e.g. '019de646-6e73-73d5-8b96-a1a163c57228') with full bib enrichment (bib_authors, bib_doi, bib_openalex_id, etc.) and meaningful titles ('Ames Grossberg 2008 Speaker Normalization Cortical Strip'). These predate the RDR-101 tumbler scheme — chunks were ingested before the catalog became authoritative. Impact: 9,996 chunks searchable via raw 'nx search' but INVISIBLE to catalog-aware paths (nx_answer, link traversal, audit-membership, coverage). User's nx_answer queries miss this entire collection. Action: backfill catalog DocumentRegistered events for the 9,996 chunks by grouping chunk metadata into doc-level rows (group_by doc_id, derive title/source/etc from metadata, generate fresh tumblers under the appropriate owner). title: [bug] catalog prune-stale + t3 prune-stale: cwd-dependent Path.exists() misclassifies relative paths as stale
description: Both nx catalog prune-stale and nx t3 prune-stale use 'not Path(fp).exists()' to classify entries/chunks as stale. For relative file_paths (most catalog code/docs entries store paths relative to their owner's repo_root, e.g. 'art-modules/art-laminar/.../File.java'), Path(fp).exists() resolves against the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY of the running process. Running 'nx catalog prune-stale --no-dry-run --confirm' from the wrong cwd would delete thousands of valid entries. Caught 2026-05-08 during prod shakeout: in a live catalog with 23,370 documents, prune-stale reported 11,837 'stale' entries; ground-truth check (resolve relative paths against owner.repo_root) showed only 71 are actually stale, with 11,766 being valid entries misclassified. T3 prune-stale has the same bug AND no event-log audit trail (deleted chunks require re-embedding via Voyage AI - real $ cost). Fix: when file_path/source_path is relative, look up the owner's repo_root from the catalog (RDR-060 added this column) and resolve. When the owner has no repo_root, skip with structured warning rather than auto-classify-as-stale. Acceptance: prune-stale on the live prod catalog reports 71 stale entries (the truly missing absolute paths + relative paths missing under their owner.repo_root), not 11,837.
close_reason: Closed

title: sweep_orphan_tmpdirs must also reap PPID=1 multiprocessing.resource_tracker leaks
description:
Chronic POSIX-semaphore-namespace exhaustion: each ungraceful MCP shutdown (SIGKILL/OOM) leaves chroma's multiprocessing workers' resource_tracker subprocesses re-parented to init (PPID=1). The trackers continue holding their POSIX named semaphores until killed; the next MCP startup's sweep only handles tmpdirs and addr files, not orphan tracker processes.

Live evidence (2026-05-08 03:30 PT shakeout):
- 25 orphan nx_t1_* tmpdirs vs 2 live chromas
- 3,314 orphan multiprocessing.resource_tracker processes with PPID=1
- 8,359 POSIX semaphores held vs kern.posix.sem.max=10,000 (83% exhaustion)
- Oldest orphan tracker: 11 days, 19 hours of accumulation predating any recent T1 work
- Manual SIGTERM of all PPID=1 multiprocessing trackers reduced sem count to 74 (no live state disturbed)

Root cause: src/nexus/session.py::stop_t1_server uses safe_killpg(server_pid, …) which only signals the CURRENT chroma's process group. Workers from PRIOR sessions whose chroma died ungracefully have different PGIDs and cannot be reached by safe_killpg from a new MCP startup. sweep_orphan_tmpdirs reaps the directories but leaves the processes.

Proposed fix: extend sweep at MCP top-level startup (src/nexus/mcp/core.py:166-173) to also enumerate PPID=1 'multiprocessing.resource_tracker' / 'multiprocessing.spawn ... --multiprocessing-fork' processes whose PGID has no living members other than themselves, and SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after 3s) any whose PGID matches a chroma we've already swept the tmpdir for. Conservative match: must contain 'multiprocessing' AND have PPID=1 AND PGID not equal to any live nx server pid.

Even more conservative: kill PPID=1 multiprocessing.* whose original tmpdir (recoverable from /proc/<pid>/cwd or environ on Linux; on macOS use lsof) matches a swept-and-reaped nx_t1_* path.

Impact: silent semaphore exhaustion → cryptic Errno 28 failures across the system (not just nexus) once the cap is hit. This was the original failure mode for beads nexus-dc57 and nexus-ze2a.

Acceptance criteria:
- sweep at MCP startup reduces orphan tracker count to 0 on a system with leaked workers
- Test: synthesize the scenario (start chroma, SIGKILL, restart MCP, assert tracker count is 0)
- nx doctor --check-semaphores surfaces the count and warns above a threshold (e.g. 1000)
notes: PR #598 open. Live shakeout 2026-05-08 cleared 3314 trackers / 8359 sems. Awaiting CI.
close_reason: Closed

title: GH #579: chroma child reaped within seconds + watchdog double-spawn race
description: 4.26.8 P1 shakeout: every chroma child the lifespan owns dies within ~5-30s of spawn (chroma_died_externally), leaving T1 scratch unreachable session-wide after first reap. Plus a watchdog double-spawn race for the same claude_pid where the second's startup removes the first's session file via session_file_removed. Sits downstream of #567/#572/#575/#576 — loud-fail and reconnect plumbing is correct; residual is the reaping cycle + idempotency gap. Investigate (a) root cause of chroma reaping (sweep_stale_sessions vs crash vs race), (b) watchdog idempotency per claude_pid, (c) HOW this shipped — what test coverage gap let 4.26.5..4.26.8 land without catching the chroma-restart-kills-itself loop, (d) HOW to close that gap.
notes:
Investigation complete. T1 scratch entry: 88cba8f2 (full analysis).

ROOT CAUSE (most likely): cross-process spawn-and-overwrite.
- A 2nd MCP server starting under the same claude_pid (subagent dispatch / hook MCP / restart) runs _t1_chroma_init_if_owner.
- _OWNED_CHROMA is per-process. Idempotency does not cross processes.
- TCP probe (0.5s timeout) can fail under load → spawn path fires → write_session_record_by_id OVERWRITES the existing canonical record's server_pid with the new chroma's.
- Old watchdog: _find_record_by_chroma_pid(old_pid) returns None → exit reason=session_file_removed → _cleanup → stop_t1_server(old_pid).
- Old chroma killed.

Why only since 4.26.7: PR #574/#575 added the session_file_removed exit. Pre-fix the watchdog kept polling and would not have killed its own chroma. Fix made loud-fail correct, exposed the latent class.

GAPS (HOW IT GOT THROUGH):
1. All _t1_chroma_init_if_owner tests run in a single process (TestInitIfOwner has 7 cases, none multi-process).
2. All tests mock start_t1_server. Nothing boots a real chroma + watchdog.
3. Release sandbox shakedown uses short-lived nx CLI commands, not persistent MCP server.
4. No CI parser / assertion against ~/.config/nexus/logs/watchdog.log.
5. test_t1_invariants.py encodes WITNESSED bugs only; misses the class invariant "no MCP should silently overwrite another's record while the other's chroma is alive."

PROPOSED FIXES:
A. Cross-process spawn guard in _t1_chroma_init_if_owner: extend tcp_probe timeout to 2s; on probe-fail with live server_pid, BACKOFF + retry (don't spawn — chroma may be starting up or under load); only spawn if probe fails N times AND server_pid dead.
B. New invariant test: subprocess B's _t1_chroma_init_if_owner with same session_id pointer must NOT overwrite A's record.
C. Real-chroma 30s soak test: spawn real chroma + watchdog, assert chroma alive + record intact after wall-clock interval.
D. Release sandbox: background MCP server scenario, post-hoc parse watchdog.log for chroma_died_externally.
E. Capture chroma stderr to ~/.config/nexus/logs/chroma.<pid>.log (start_t1_server currently DEVNULLs).
F. Loud log on duplicate_chroma_claim when about to spawn but a live record + live server_pid exist for same claude_pid.

NEXT: write up summary for user, await go-ahead before implementing.
close_reason: Investigation complete; RDR-105 accepted (PR #580). Implementation tracked under epic nexus-d73b. Critical-path bead nexus-4fek (P1 spike) is unblocked. Six-bug class-elimination strategy adopted in lieu of patch fix.

title: RDR-101 Phase 3 follow-up A: atomic dedupe (events batched, projector in transaction, flock acquired)
description:
Multi-reviewer convergence on src/nexus/catalog/dedupe.py::apply_remove_plan ES path:

(C3) Per-event interleave of _write_to_event_log + _projector.apply leaves split state on mid-loop projector exception. Events 1..N-1 are durable in events.jsonl (append-only, fcntl+flush at catalog.py:869-885); SQLite mutations 1..N-1 roll back at uncommitted close. Replay produces partial deletion as canonical state with no operator diagnostic. doctor --replay-equality cannot detect (replay IS source).

(C4) apply_remove_plan does not call _acquire_lock at entry; CLI handler doesn't either. _write_to_event_log:872 contract requires caller hold catalog directory flock. Every other ES mutator (set_alias:1414, unlink, register, etc.) acquires it. Concurrent process running nx catalog register produces non-linear interleaving in events.jsonl AND legacy JSONL appends.

Fix:
1. Acquire flock at apply_remove_plan entry; release in finally.
2. Build all event envelopes upfront (LinkDeleted x N, DocumentDeleted x N, OwnerDeleted x 1).
3. EventLog.append_many for atomic batched write to events.jsonl under the flock.
4. Wrap projector.apply_all inside cat._db.transaction() so partial projection rolls back atomically. If apply raises, events are durable but SQLite is rolled back; next _ensure_consistent re-projects deterministically.
5. Tests:
   - Mid-loop projector raise: assert events.jsonl has all events AND SQLite reflects pre-state (transaction rolled back); next _ensure_consistent reaches same final state via replay
   - Concurrent flock contention: spawn second process, verify serialization (or at minimum lock acquired, releasable)

Source: convergent review findings nx:substantive-critic + nx:deep-analyst (2026-05-01). Both confirmed via code inspection of dedupe.py:283-332.
acceptance_criteria: apply_remove_plan acquires flock at entry. Events emitted via EventLog.append_many (single fsync+flock). Projector applies inside cat._db.transaction(). Test: projector mid-loop exception leaves events.jsonl complete + SQLite at pre-state; subsequent _ensure_consistent rebuild produces final post-dedupe state. Test: concurrent dedupe + register from another process serialize correctly. All existing dedupe tests still pass. doctor --replay-equality passes after dedupe under ES.
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: MinerU leaks POSIX named semaphores, exhausting kernel namespace system-wide
description:
CRITICAL: The MinerU subprocess (`mineru-api` HTTP server) leaks POSIX named semaphores during PDF extraction. After a handful of PDFs, the system's global `kern.posix.sem.max = 10000` namespace is exhausted. Every subsequent call to `_multiprocessing.SemLock()` — by ANY process on the system — fails with `[Errno 28] No space left on device`.

This is not a Nexus bug strictly, but Nexus depends on MinerU and this completely breaks formula-heavy PDF indexing, and collaterally breaks every other Python multiprocessing workload on the machine until the user reboots or kills leaking processes.

## Reproduction

1. Start MinerU: `nx mineru start` — server starts, SemLock works.
2. `nx index pdf --dir <papers-with-formulas>/ --collection knowledge__delos` — MinerU routing triggers for formula-detected papers.
3. After ~1-3 PDFs, MinerU returns HTTP 409 with body:
   ```json
   {"status":"failed", "error":"[Errno 28] No space left on device"}
   ```
4. All subsequent PDF extractions via MinerU fail with the same error.
5. `python3 -c "from _multiprocessing import SemLock; SemLock(0,0,1,name='/t', unlink=True)"` — FAILS with Errno 28.
6. Stop MinerU (`nx mineru stop`) — SemLock works again.

## Why this is P0

- **System-wide scope**: once the POSIX sem namespace is exhausted, EVERY Python multiprocessing workload on the machine fails. Our own `nx` commands start emitting the joblib warning on every invocation (the warning cascade we fixed earlier today via orphan-chroma reaping — bead nexus-dc57 — is the same symptom).
- **Silent cascade**: users see "joblib operating in serial mode" warnings with no context. They don't know MinerU is the culprit. They don't know rebooting will fix it. They might assume the system is fundamentally broken.
- **Blocks core functionality**: PDF extraction with formula support (our auto-routing target for scholarly papers) is unusable. `knowledge__*` collections — the intended home for external papers — are degraded.
- **Repeats an already-filed issue**: nexus-dc57 captured a related symptom (orphan chroma leaks); this is the same *class* of resource leak from a different source. Both need hardening.

## Immediate workaround

`nx index pdf --extractor docling` — forces Docling through, skipping the formula-detection + MinerU routing branch. Docling handles formulas less well but does not leak semaphores.

Paired with the `knowledge__delos` re-index currently in flight (started immediately after this bead).

## Root cause hypothesis (needs verification)

MinerU uses Python multiprocessing internally for PDF analysis (almost certainly — it's ML-heavy, torch + OCR). Workers spawn SemLocks (`name=/...`) for IPC and do not `sem_unlink()` them before exit. macOS POSIX sem namespace persists unlinked semaphores until reboot. Over time, accumulated semaphores exhaust the namespace.

Hypothesis is testable:
- Start MinerU
- Run `lsof -p <mineru-pid>` before and after a PDF extraction; look for growing `semaphore` entries
- Profile MinerU's multiprocessing init to see if it sets `multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn')` or relies on fork (fork would inherit parent's semaphore registry)

## Possible fixes (ordered by cost)

1. **Document workaround in CLI**: `nx index pdf --help` notes known MinerU issue, recommends `--extractor docling` for large batches.
2. **Auto-restart MinerU every N PDFs**: `pdf_extractor.py` could track request count, kill + restart MinerU after every ~5 PDFs to clear leaked semaphores. Expensive (MinerU startup is ~2-3s) but reliable.
3. **File upstream bug at MinerU**: github.com/opendatalab/MinerU (or wherever their repo lives). Provide minimal repro.
4. **Contribute fix upstream**: audit MinerU's `multiprocessing` usage, add explicit `sem_unlink` or `Manager.shutdown()` calls.
5. **Consider alternative extractors**: Grobid? Marker? PyMuPDF-only? If MinerU is unmaintainable, the auto-routing value goes down.

## Related

- **nexus-dc57** (P1, 2026-04-17) — T1 chroma orphan leak, same Errno 28 symptom, different source (chroma + multiprocessing trackers). The fix pattern for nexus-dc57 (SessionEnd hook, atexit cleanup, process-group isolation) does not apply to MinerU — MinerU is a third-party process. This needs its own approach.
- **nexus-vatx** (P2, 2026-04-17) — ingest observability. Would have surfaced "MinerU error 409 on every request after 3 successes" much faster if phase markers and error logs were more visible.
- **RDR-044** — PDF extraction auto-routing (Docling → MinerU → PyMuPDF). The auto-routing is actively harmful right now for formula-heavy papers because MinerU is broken; we prefer the all-Docling path until this lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify hypothesis: confirm MinerU worker processes are the semaphore source (lsof audit + repro on clean machine).
- [ ] File upstream at MinerU with minimal repro.
- [ ] Implement CLI workaround documentation in `nx index pdf --help`.
- [ ] Implement MinerU auto-restart every N PDFs in `pdf_extractor.py`.
- [ ] Add `nx doctor --check=mineru` to detect semaphore leak during indexing and warn the user.
- [ ] Regression test: batch-index 10 formula-heavy PDFs, verify 0-chunk rate stays < 10%.

## Discovery context

Found 2026-04-17 during Delos paper re-index. First attempt: 3/16 PDFs succeeded, 13 failed. Symptom was MinerU HTTP 409. Direct curl to `POST /file_parse` revealed the 409 body contained `"error":"[Errno 28] No space left on device"`. Cross-referenced with earlier same-session cleanup (nexus-dc57) which had recovered from the same Errno 28 state after reaping 333 orphan chromas + 2 leaked multiprocessing trackers. Killing `nx mineru stop` immediately restored SemLock capability, confirming MinerU is the current leak source.
close_reason: Root cause fixed in v4.6.4 (commit 9696cc5) — start_new_session=True + os.killpg at shutdown so resource_tracker runs sem_unlink cleanly on MinerU worker teardown. Empirically verified 2026-04-18: full 15-paper Delos re-index (2007 chunks, ~25 min continuous MinerU server operation) completed with POSIX sem namespace at full 9990-slot headroom throughout. nx doctor --check-resources now surfaces pressure early. Repro script preserved at ~/nexus-blog/repro/mineru_sem_leak.py for future regression verification.

title: [hook] subagents must not run git checkout/restore/switch/reset on the shared tree — extend the stash guard (reviewer wiped 3 uncommitted fixes 2026-08-20)
description: Incident 2026-08-20 (T2 nexus/lessons-coordination-2026-08-20, nexus/review-nexus-pfuns [23062]): a code-review-expert subagent falsified nexus-pfuns' fixes by running 'git checkout -- <file>' on src/nexus/commands/t3.py, src/nexus/gc_purge_marker.py and conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/_lib.py in the shared checkout and could not restore them; the critic then found the fixes missing. Recovered only from an orchestrator-side diff snapshot. The existing subagent guard (feedback_subagents_stash_the_shared_tree; conexus PreToolUse hook on Bash for subagents) blocks 'git stash' but not checkout/restore/switch/reset/clean. Do: extend the hook to deny, for subagent contexts, any of: git checkout (with pathspec or branch), git restore, git switch, git reset (any mode), git clean, git stash; allow read-only git (status/diff/log/show/blame). Deny message must name the orchestrator-commits rule and suggest 'git show HEAD:<path> > /tmp/...' for falsification by comparison. Tests: tests/hooks/ parity + one test per denied verb + one allowed verb. Ship in conexus plugin (PENDING_RELEASE.md entry).
notes: Commit c758bbc36. Rounds: T2 3c92m-code-review-2026-08-20, -round2..-round9, review-nexus-3c92m [23074]; dev notes [23065]. Out of scope, recorded: non-git file mutation by subagents (python heredoc rewrites) has no guard — candidate bead if it recurs.
close_reason: Guard redesigned fail-closed: normalise (CRLF, continuations, ANSI-C, default/echo resolution, backslash+quote strip), deny git+verb on the text AND on its zero-expansion form, deny spliced expansions that could spell git or in any git-containing command; switch added; three verbatim incident commands pinned; 187 tests; residuals and accepted false positives documented. Commit on develop; PENDING_RELEASE declared.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (2026-08-20, orchestrator, from the reviewer transcript): the three wiping 'git checkout -- <file>' calls were Bash tool calls on the installed 7.13.0 plugin and the hook returned permissionDecision=allow for each — NOT a stale pin. Each was a MULTI-LINE command: cd ...; echo ...; python3 - <<'EOF' ... EOF (rewrites the file); test run; then 'git checkout -- <path>' on a later line. The guard inspects only the leading segment / stops at the heredoc. Fix = parse every line/segment (newline, ;, &&, ||, |, $(...)) and classify heredoc bodies by consumer. 'switch' addition stands as a secondary gap.

title: Rotation TOCTOU: concurrent double-rotation can clobber real .1 generation (capability_census.jsonl / routing_log.jsonl)
design:
_rotate_log_if_oversized (src/nexus/_session_end_census.py + conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/_lib.py + sn twin) does stat() then os.replace() with no re-check immediately before the rename and no locking. Only the BENIGN race (a second rotator's os.replace() hits FileNotFoundError because the live path is already gone) is handled/tested.

An UNHANDLED, UNTESTED destructive race exists: P1 stat()s oversize file, rotates it to .1 (real history), reopens+appends (recreating a small live file). P2 had independently stat()'d the file BEFORE P1's rotation (saw it oversize, correctly at the time) but is scheduled late; by the time P2 calls os.replace(live, live.1), the live path has been recreated by P1 (small, exists) so P2's rename SUCCEEDS -- clobbering the real, just-rotated .1 content with P2's near-empty live file. P1's rotated-away history (which could be years of accumulated capability-census records, or ~5MB of routing_log.jsonl history on first rotation of an existing install) is silently, permanently destroyed. No error, no log line -- this is the exact 'foot cannon' Sam asked to be pressure-tested for.

Neither test file (tests/test_session_end_capability_census.py::TestLogRotation, tests/test_routing_hooks.py) covers this interleaving -- both only test the safe ENOENT race and the intentional single-writer '.1 gets clobbered by design' case.

Fix options: re-stat() immediately before the rename and abort if size dropped below cap since the initial check (narrows but doesn't eliminate the window); or use flock/lockfile around stat+replace; or rotate to a unique per-process/per-timestamp name and let a separate compaction step merge, avoiding the fixed-name clobber entirely.

Found by substantive-critic during the Sam-directed rotation-safety review, 2026-08-20. T2: nexus/substantive-critique-rotation-2026-08-20.
close_reason: Fixed in 49a6353ba: rotation escalates from lock-free stat to non-blocking advisory lock on <name>.rotate.lock held across {re-stat, os.replace} — stale-observation rename eliminated by construction, applied identically in _session_end_census.py, conexus _lib.py, and the byte-identical sn/ twin. Red-first: the clobber interleaving reproduced deterministically pre-fix; the held-lock contention test discriminates the lock from a bare re-stat non-fix (critic empirically verified by replaying against the rejected narrowing). Critic round-2: CLOSED, no starvation, crash-safe (flock auto-release). Marker T2 review-rotation-pass-2026-08-20 [22948].

title: PDF ingest + bib-enrich quality fixes surfaced by indexing arXiv 2512.11001: MinerU <sub> heading shredding, filename-stem catalog titles on every PDF path, dead service-mode nx enrich bib, 2-token title guard mis-attribution
description:
Surfaced 2026-08-19 while indexing papers/2512.11001.pdf (Kaoudi & Giurgiu, catalog 1.14.51) and watching the result instead of trusting the tool output. Four defects, all fixed in one commit:

1. MinerU renders ACM small-caps headings/captions/run-in heads as letter-interleaved <sub> spans (30/70 chunks, 17/35 headings on this paper; sibling 1.14.23 too). Fix: _unwrap_mineru_font_tags next to _normalize_mineru_latex.
2. Catalog title was ALWAYS the filename stem for PDFs: pre-flight registers title=stem, _catalog_pdf_hook existing-branch never wrote title/author/year (the PDF twin of nexus-ivzw8), the streaming tail read metadata['title']/['author'] keys no extractor emits, and the MinerU path had no H1 fallback (derive_title body=None). Fix: resolve_pdf_title (one chain, 3 call sites) + stem-guard backfill in the hook.
3. nx enrich bib dead in service mode since the Chroma retirement: _ServiceCollectionStub had no update(). Fix: forward to /v1/vectors/update-metadata.
4. Once alive, one run stamped 3 WRONG works on 3 papers/644 chunks: _titles_compatible auto-accepted on >=2 shared tokens, which a reference-list DOI (same subfield) and OpenAlex's rank-1 stranger both satisfy. Fix: containment ratio >=0.5 on the shorter title + walk top-5 title-search results for the first compatible one. Live damage reverted and re-run verified against OpenAlex (3 wrong -> 2 right + 1 honest miss).

Existing indexed PDFs need a re-index to pick up 1/2; already-stamped bib_* on other collections may carry the class-4 error and want an audit (not done here).

title: P3.0: Minimum Viable Validation — index the large repo with zero TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH; record the four metrics
description:
RDR-195 § Minimum Viable Validation and § Performance Expectations. IN SCOPE, NOT DEFERRED — this is the exact journey that fails today. Runs BEFORE Phase 3 activation, against a LOCALLY BUILT engine (the reporting environment is mode: local, so no cloud deploy is needed to prove it).

Journey: re-index the large PHP repository that produced the original failure, end to end, with ZERO TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH occurrences, then confirm semantic search returns hits from the newly indexed files.

RECORD FOUR MEASUREMENTS (measurement strategy, not estimates — no throughput target is asserted):
1. Voyage requests per upsert page.
2. Count of adaptive-split events. A non-zero STEADY-STATE count means the divisor is too optimistic and every affected batch is paying for rejected tokenization.
3. Observed bytes-per-token ratio for PHP source — this CALIBRATES the divisor. A request count materially above the theoretical minimum means the divisor is too pessimistic.
4. THE 429 COUNT (gate remediation 2026-08-19). Sub-batching makes rate-limit pressure STRICTLY WORSE — one logical embed that was one oversized POST becomes N smaller POSTs in quick succession, multiplied again across pages by a bulk run. conexus-ddh0 (2026-08-15 bulk index run tripping Voyage rate limits with today's one-POST-per-page behavior) is the live precedent. callApi's retry path already logs 429s; this run records the total.

BLOCKING TRIGGER: a NON-ZERO 429 count on this single-repository run triggers the caller-pacing remedy named in § Technical Design (pacing at the caller — the staged bulk-load pipeline nexus-b50zw, or inter-sub-request delay) BEFORE Phase 3 activation, not after a field incident. File that remedy as a bead and block P3.1 on it. Do NOT loosen the planner in response: the planner's job is validity, not throughput shaping.

Record all four measurements in T2 (`memory_put project=nexus title=rdr-195-mvv-measurements`) — the divisor calibration is worthless if it lives only in a transcript.

title: P2.3: typed TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH error, adaptive halving above callApi, MAX_SUB_REQUESTS_PER_BATCH=64
description:
RDR-195 § Technical Design (typed error, Termination and cost bound) and § Phase 2 / Step 3.

Today `callApi` treats only 429 and >=500 as retryable (:223) and maps 401/403 to the typed `UpstreamAuthException` (:230-237); every other status — including this precisely described, perfectly actionable 400 — falls through to a bare RuntimeException (:238-239), which VectorHandler renders as a 500 (VectorHandler.java:211-217). Client-side `_GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES = {502,503,504}` excludes 500, so nothing retries and nothing adapts.

Work:
- Recognize 400 with `error_code == "TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH"` in callApi and surface it as a TYPED exception, following the existing UpstreamAuthException convention.
- PLACEMENT IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL: the split must live ABOVE callApi, in the caller owning the sub-batch list. callApi retries only 429/5xx, so this keeps the split path and the transient-retry path ORTHOGONAL — each sub-request keeps its own independent 3-attempt budget and halving contributes a separate O(log) factor instead of compounding into 3^depth.
- The caller catches the typed error, HALVES that sub-batch, and retries the halves.
- A single text that still trips it is RETHROWN with the upstream detail intact — a genuine un-splittable input must fail loudly, never be dropped. This arm is DEFENSIVE (for an upstream contract change or an undocumented model whose context exceeds its ceiling), not a path the design expects to reach: `truncation: true` is always sent (:166; nexus-f4wcg records that omitting it is load-bearing for parity), so Voyage truncates each text to the model context BEFORE evaluating the aggregate — the live 400 body's 'after truncation' is the empirical evidence for that ordering, and it is the premise of the termination argument.
- `MAX_SUB_REQUESTS_PER_BATCH = 64` beside the planner's other constants (gate remediation 2026-08-19): >= 2*log2(n) for any n the 1000-input API cap admits, with wide margin over the ceil(1000/300)-to-tens range the planner produces in practice, so it can only fire on adversarial input, never on calibration drift. ON EXHAUSTION the embed fails with the typed oversize error CARRYING THE SUB-REQUEST COUNT AND THE OFFENDING BATCH'S SIZE — same loud path as the single-unsplittable-text rethrow, NEVER a silent partial result.
- Structured log event per adaptive split (`event=voyage_*` idiom) so a post-hoc log read distinguishes 'planned correctly' from 'estimator missed and recovered'.

Billing note (inherits the existing documented stance at :203-206): `usage.total_tokens` comes from the final successful response, so the reported total under-counts tokenization Voyage billed for rejected attempts. Same safe direction as today, not a new divergence. Do NOT 'fix' it here.

Do NOT make 400 generically retryable in callApi (briefly-rejected alternative): resending an identical oversize body is guaranteed to fail again and bills tokenization twice. The batch must CHANGE.

title: P2.2: token-aware sub-batch planner in VoyageEmbedder (per-model budgets, provisional estimator, fast path)
description:
RDR-195 § Technical Design (Engine) and § Phase 2 / Step 2. Reuse the `nexus-zu4ma` `Bge768Embedder.planBatches`/`MAX_PADDED_TOKEN_AREA` PATTERN (:119-124, :247-300), not its code — the budget unit differs (padded token area vs estimated API tokens) but the greedy-planner shape, documented-provenance constant, single-call fast path, and invocation-counter instrument transfer directly.

Constants beside :61-63, each documented with provenance:
- `MAX_BATCH_TEXTS` = 1000, the documented API input cap. ASSERTED, never silently truncated, following `VoyageReranker.MAX_DOCS_PER_REQUEST` (:58-59, :130-135).
- `MAX_BATCH_ESTIMATED_TOKENS` — RESOLVED PER MODEL, NOT HARDCODED. VoyageEmbedder is instantiated with TWO models: voyage-code-3 (EmbedderRouter.java:104, :142) and voyage-3 (:112, :145). Ceilings are per tier (120,000 for voyage-code-3; 320,000 for the voyage-3.5/voyage-2 tier). A single constant would be incorrect for one and punitive for the other. Key off the instance's own `model` field with an explicit FAIL-SAFE DEFAULT OF THE TIGHTEST DOCUMENTED CEILING (120,000) for any model absent from the table — an unknown model can then only ever be OVER-split (costs round trips) never UNDER-split (fails). voyage-3 does not appear in Voyage's published limit table at all, which is exactly why the default must be conservative rather than guessed.
- A bytes-to-tokens divisor, explicitly labelled PROVISIONAL and self-correcting.

Signatures (illustrative; verify during implementation): `List<List<String>> planBatches(List<String>)` (greedy; never emits an empty batch; a single over-budget text gets its own batch); `static long estimateTokens(String)` (UTF-8 length / divisor); `int voyageRequestCount()` and `void resetVoyageRequestCount()` (package-private non-vacuity instruments mirroring Bge768Embedder.onnxInvocationCount() :141-147, :362-370).

Wiring: `embed`, `embedWithUsage`, `embedDouble` (:100-146) iterate planBatches, concatenate results IN INPUT ORDER, and — for embedWithUsage — SUM `usage.total_tokens` across sub-calls exactly as `CceEmbedder.embedWithUsage` already does (:223-233).

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- SINGLE-REQUEST FAST PATH: when the input already fits, exactly ONE POST with a body BYTE-IDENTICAL to today's (Bge768Embedder :261 takes the same care).
- `buildJson` is NOT MODIFIED. Each sub-batch is serialized by the same unmodified method, so the `nexus-f4wcg` byte contract holds per request and `VoyageEmbedderBodyTest` needs NO CHANGE. A green unmodified VoyageEmbedderBodyTest is the direct evidence the contract was preserved rather than accommodated.
- Structured log events for the planned batch count, in the existing `event=voyage_*` idiom.

Do NOT hoist any of this into EmbedderRouter: it serves CceEmbedder too, which already fans out per text, so a router-level planner would double-batch it and push model-specific knowledge out of the class that owns it.

title: P1.1: byte-aware paging accumulator in upsert_chunks (client half, independent PyPI delivery)
description:
RDR-195 § Implementation Plan / Phase 1 / Step 1. File: `src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py`.

Replace the fixed-stride `range(0, n, cap)` paging at :1563-1567 (the self-described 'ONE choke point') with an accumulator that closes a page when EITHER the count cap OR a byte budget would be exceeded. Always emit at least one chunk per page, so a single large chunk still ships (already bounded by SAFE_CHUNK_BYTES).

Constraints, each of which the RDR states explicitly:
- New module constant beside `_CODE_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP` (:518), type-hinted per project convention.
- SIZED WITH DELIBERATE EXTRA HEADROOM BELOW the engine's per-model token budget — NOT tuned to the same target. Against a pre-fix engine this constant has no typed-400 backstop, so the layer without a safety net must be the more conservative of the two. Equal sizing is the one tuning choice this phase must not make. The constant's own DOCSTRING must carry that reason (gate round 2 SIGNIFICANT: the reason is not visible from the constant itself).
- Applied ONLY where the collection routes to a genuine multi-text Voyage batch: reuse the existing `_CCE_COLLECTION_PREFIXES` (:634) and `_serving_embedding_mode()` that `per_collection_chunk_cap` already consults (:748-759). CCE fans out per text; onnx-local has its own memory-derived cap. Neither changes.
- PASSTHROUGH PAGES ARE EXEMPT FROM THE BYTE BUDGET (maintainer addition 2026-08-19): a page carrying caller-supplied `embeddings` never reaches Voyage, so gating it by a Voyage-token-derived budget shrinks pages for no upstream benefit. Count-cap paging still applies to them unchanged.
- Preserve the `embeddings` passthrough slicing in lockstep with ids (:1576-1577) under the now-VARIABLE stride, and keep the existing per-page structured logging.
- ALSO IN SCOPE (RDR § Finalization Gate / Contradiction Check, 'Standing, and deliberate'): amend `per_collection_chunk_cap`'s docstring, which currently states a token budget is 'a throughput optimization for a future pass, not a correctness gap'. That reasoning is sound for the onnx-local memory constraint it was written about and does NOT transfer to a hard remote per-request ceiling. Record the distinction at the code, not only in the RDR. Omitting this is silent scope reduction.

Do NOT wire `ChunkBatcher(max_bytes=...)` (Alternative 1, rejected: constrains batch ASSEMBLY while the failure occurs in batch TRANSMISSION, and a single oversize file falls back to the legacy per-file path which routes through this same loop anyway).

---

T2: `nx memory get -p nexus_rdr -t 195-research-3` (spike shape), `195-research-2`, `195-research-1`. nx search terms: "VoyageEmbedder batch planner", "Bge768Embedder planBatches MAX_PADDED_TOKEN_AREA", "upsert_chunks per_collection_chunk_cap paging".

Tests written RED first.

title: EPIC: RDR-195 — token-aware Voyage batch splitting (make the 120K-tokens/request ceiling a planned bound)
description:
RDR-195 (accepted 2026-08-19, author Gerasimos Pollatos, PR #1466, maintainer-adopted; related GH #1465).

Indexing a large PHP repo into a `code__*` collection fails: the engine forwards the whole upsert batch into one Voyage /v1/embeddings POST, Voyage rejects it with 400 TOO_MANY_TOKENS_IN_BATCH (280,871 tokens against a 120,000 ceiling), and it reaches the user as an untyped engine 500. Every bound in the stack is a ROW COUNT; no layer has ever been token-aware.

Two changes, two layers, two distinct reasons:
1. ENGINE (authoritative, below every caller) — a token-aware sub-batch planner in VoyageEmbedder plus a typed oversize-batch error with adaptive halving. Planner = throughput mechanism; typed error = correctness mechanism. That split is the design's core argument (§ Decision Rationale).
2. CLIENT (version-skew half, independent PyPI delivery) — a byte budget on the upsert_chunks paging loop. Justified by decoupled release lifecycles, NOT as defense-in-depth. Sized with deliberate extra headroom BELOW the engine budget: it is the layer with no typed-400 backstop.

Out of scope by construction: CceEmbedder (voyage-context-3) fans out one API call per text, so it cannot exceed a batch ceiling; the fix must NOT be hoisted into EmbedderRouter, which serves both.

Sequencing: the composition spike BLOCKS all implementation. Phases 1 and 2 are independently correct and independently shippable in either order — they PARALLELIZE. The MVV runs before Phase 3 activation.

Granting nexus_diag SELECT on gc_audit therefore exposes document titles across every tenant to a non-tenant-scoped diagnostic role -- exactly the class of exposure RDR-182 s5's content boundary exists to prevent, and the developer's own write-up (T2 nexus/2026-08-19-gc-audit-diag-grant-fix [22859]) states explicitly: "widening beyond AUDIT_ONLY_TABLES would defeat A6's content boundary." AUDIT_ONLY_TABLES itself (nexus-34wrg) was defined for a DIFFERENT purpose (rename/merge emptiness-check exemption), not verified against the diagnostic content boundary before being reused here.

Mitigating context: nexus.chunks (CHASH_BEARING_TABLES, pre-existing grant since grants-nexus-diag-3 / nexus-lhuhe) already exposes full chunk_text to nexus_diag directly, so this is not a novel class of exposure, just an additional instance under the same accepted read-only-ops-role threat model. Still worth an explicit decision rather than a reused label carrying an unverified premise.

Recommendation: either (a) redact/omit the title field from gc_audit's chashes sample for gc_quarantine_orphans (or generally, do not store title in gc_audit at all), or (b) explicitly document that gc_audit is accepted to carry titles under the same threat model as CHASH_BEARING_TABLES, updating nexus-34wrg's "no content" language for AUDIT_ONLY_TABLES to say "no BODY content; may carry titles/paths" so it is not silently reused elsewhere on a false premise.

Also worth a lighter follow-up: hook_failures.error (str(exception)[:2000], src/nexus/hook_registry.py) and its doc_id/source_path columns can plausibly echo file paths or content fragments via exception messages -- less certain than the gc_audit case (no concrete proof found), but the same "AUDIT_ONLY_TABLES = no content" premise applies to it too and should get the same explicit-decision treatment.

Context: nx substantive-critique of grants-nexus-diag-4 / CatalogRepository.AUDIT_ONLY_TABLES publicization, 2026-08-19. Files: service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/grants-nexus-diag.xml, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java, service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/GrantsNexusDiagViewAccessIntegrationTest.java, service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest.java.

Independently re-verified 2026-08-19.

comments.text:
VERIFIED FALSE POSITIVE (independently re-verified by a second developer session, 2026-08-19).

catalog-033-gc-audit-producers.xml's gc_quarantine_orphans() function does NOT persist document titles into gc_audit.chashes. The write path is:

1. In-memory sample (line ~403): `SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('chash', encode(chash, 'hex'), 'title', title)) AS s` — v_sample DOES carry chash+title.
2. RETURN QUERY caller contract (line ~435): `RETURN QUERY SELECT v_moved, v_sample;` — v_sample (with title) is returned to the function's authenticated caller. This is the function's pre-existing, unrelated return contract.
3. gc_audit INSERT (line ~424, the actual finding under review): `(SELECT jsonb_agg(elem->>'chash') FROM jsonb_array_elements(COALESCE(v_sample, '[]'::jsonb)) elem)` — this extracts ONLY the chash field via elem->>'chash'. Title is dropped before the row is ever built. gc_audit.chashes never contains title.
4. Rollback block (lines ~566-584): restores vectors-005's original function body verbatim, which also builds v_sample with title and returns it via RETURN QUERY — but the rollback has NO gc_audit INSERT at all (no audit row is written on rollback), so title never reaches gc_audit there either.

The critic's claim conflated the in-memory sample / RETURN QUERY caller contract with what actually lands in the persisted gc_audit row. Closing as a confirmed false positive from a misread of the rollback block / in-memory sample.

title: nx collection reindex on code__ collections deletes data and never re-indexes (silent full-collection loss)
description:
Discovered while validating nexus-sjb52's reroute of reindex_cmd's delete hop from db.delete_collection(name) (a stub that unconditionally raised NotImplementedError, so nothing was ever actually deleted, for ANY collection type -- broken but non-destructive) to purge_collection_cascade(db, name) (the same cascade nx collection delete uses -- T3 chunks, chash index, taxonomy topics/assignments/centroids, catalog_documents, and the catalog_collections registry row, all really deleted).

commands/collection.py reindex_cmd's re-index dispatch (around line 615) only implements re-indexing for three of the four collection-name prefixes it recognizes:
  - rdr__      -> batch_index_markdowns (indexed = len(rdr_files))
  - docs__ / knowledge__ -> per-file index_markdown/index_pdf loop (indexed += 1)
  - code__     -> click.echo("Re-indexing code collection -- use 'nx index repo <path>' for full re-index") and NOTHING ELSE. indexed stays 0.

Post-nexus-sjb52-fix, invoking 'nx collection reindex code__<name>' now:
  1. Actually deletes the collection's T3 chunks, catalog documents, taxonomy state, and catalog_collections registry row (via purge_collection_cascade -- this part now WORKS, whereas pre-fix it always died first).
  2. Never re-indexes anything for the code__ branch -- indexed=0, no index_repository call.
  3. Reports 'Re-indexed: N -> 0 chunks (0 sources processed)' and exits 0 -- reads as a completed (if empty) operation, not a failure.

Net effect: pre-sjb52-fix, 'nx collection reindex code__X' was safe-but-broken (crashed before touching data). Post-fix it is destructive-and-silent for code__ collections specifically -- full permanent deletion with zero automatic rebuild, and an exit-0 message that does not read as data loss.

Fix options: (a) implement an actual code__ reindex path (call index_repository against the registered repo root, mirroring nx index repo), or (b) refuse code__ collections OUTRIGHT before the delete step (mirroring the sourceless-refuse pattern at reindex_cmd step 2) and point the operator at 'nx index repo <path> --force' instead, so nothing is destroyed by a verb that cannot rebuild it. (b) is the smaller, safer fix given the delete-then-print behavior has apparently existed unnoticed since before RDR-155 P4b.

Not to be confused with nexus-43qgm.13 (SIG-13, tests/test_rdr137_followup_batch_sigs.py) -- SIG-13 is about the L1-context-refresh registry-walk fallback missing a code_collection field match (a post-processing gap after a successful reindex); this bead is about the code__ reindex path performing NO reindex at all, before post-processing is ever reached.
acceptance_criteria: nx collection reindex code__<name> either (a) actually re-indexes the collection from its registered repo root, or (b) refuses before deleting anything, with a clear message pointing at nx index repo. Either way: never deletes a code__ collection's data while reporting exit 0 and 0 sources processed.

title: [bug] doc-only fast-lane predicate defeated on PR events: dorny's PR-files API returned an EMPTY changed-file list (PR #1464, CI started seconds after creation) -> docs_only=false -> full matrix on a 3-file docs/rdr diff
description: Evidence (run 32191107389, job 95885410163, 2026-08-18): dorny/paths-filter warned "'base' input parameter is ignored when action is triggered by pull request event", then logged 'Filter docs_only = false / Matching files: none / Changes output set to []' for a PR whose diff is exactly 3 files under docs/rdr/**. This CONTRADICTS the job's own fail-loud design: an empty changed-file set on a non-empty PR is a malformed predicate input and per the gate step's philosophy should exit 1 (or retry), never silently resolve. Keep the fail direction conservative (unprovable -> run the matrix) but make emptiness LOUD, and note the likely trigger is CI starting within seconds of PR creation (gh pr create then immediate run).
