title: release.yml ledger-block remedy (workflow_dispatch same-tag retry) is inoperable — tag immutability makes the documented fix a no-op
design:
Discovered in substantive-critic review of nexus-gc9ir (uncommitted, 2026-08-18).

release.yml's new "KNOWN FAILURE MODE, NO CI-SIDE BYPASS" comment (and its
mirror in .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md) instructs: on an unacknowledged
docs/wire-contract-pending.md ## Unshipped entry blocking --paired-deploy-auto
at tag-push publish time, edit the ledger, land the edit on the release
branch, then re-run via `workflow_dispatch` naming the SAME already-pushed
release tag.

This cannot work. The publish job's only actions/checkout step pins
`ref: ${{ inputs.tag }}` — an immutable tag by the workflow's own stated
design (marketplace.json source.ref depends on tags never moving; see the
workflow_dispatch trigger's own header comment). check_client_lag_ledger
(scripts/check_engine_release_floor.py) reads docs/wire-contract-pending.md
as a plain file off that checked-out tree (DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH =
_REPO_ROOT/docs/wire-contract-pending.md, scripts/check_wire_contract_pairing.py:99)
— never from origin/main. A ledger edit landed AFTER the tag exists is
invisible to a workflow_dispatch retry of that same tag: the retry re-reads
the frozen, still-unacknowledged ledger and fails identically.

Real remedy is either (a) cut a fresh version/tag carrying the ledger fix
(the retry mechanism is for CI-side failures, not artifact defects — this
would need reframing as "abandon this tag, bump again"), or (b) move the
wire-contract-ledger check earlier, into PR-gated release-branch CI before
Step 8's tag push, so an unacknowledged entry is caught while the tree is
still mutable.

Fix: rewrite both prose copies (release.yml step comment,
.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md) to state the correct remedy plainly, and
consider whether the earlier-check option (b) is worth implementing given
the ledger's whole purpose is exactly this class of gate.

Ship-blocker: no — narrow edge case (unacknowledged ledger entry surviving
to tag-push time), does not corrupt data or block the primary gc9ir fix.
Context: nx
close_reason: Shipped develop @ f2e6c0103. Prose remedy corrected earlier (gc9ir @ 585c77377); this lands option (b): release-ledger-gate runs the ack-required ledger check (--ledger-only, shared function with the publish path) on every PR to main, merge-blocking TODAY via the pytest-gate needs fan-in (skipped/failed both block on main PRs; 4 bash-execution tests + structural pin, self-falsified) — no branch-protection settings change needed. title: nexus-35ok4 gap: effective_embedding_model_for_writes() has 5+ ungrandfathered direct callers, breaking write grandfathering for nx index repo/md/pdf(no --collection)/dt import
description:
Substantive-critic round-4 finding on the nexus-35ok4 (GH #1461) uncommitted fix.

The round-2/round-3 grandfathering safety net (t3_collection_name()'s for_write=True + t3= probe: "key absent + pre-existing bge: writes grandfather onto bge") lives ONLY inside t3_collection_name(). effective_embedding_model_for_writes() -- the underlying primitive that raises LocalVoyageCredentialMissingError when local.embed_model is voyage-shaped and no key is configured -- has 6 other direct callers across the codebase that have NO knowledge of the grandfathering contract and NO t3 existence probe at all:

1. src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:2547 (collection_for_repo) -- called by indexer.py's _repo_collection_or_legacy() at the TOP of nx index repo's collection-name resolution (indexer.py:3676/3678) for an ALREADY catalog-registered repo. Only wrapped in `except LookupError` (indexer.py:477), which does NOT catch LocalVoyageCredentialMissingError (a RuntimeError). CONFIRMED via code read + live repro of the underlying raise: `nx index repo .` on any already-indexed, catalog-registered repo CRASHES the instant local.embed_model=voyage-* is set without voyage_api_key -- it does not grandfather onto the existing bge collection as the shipped truth table (docs/cli-reference.md "Local mode with Voyage") and T2 [22806] promise.
2. src/nexus/corpus.py:333 (docs_leaf_fallback_collection_name) -- hit by `nx index md <file>` / `nx index pdf <file>` WITHOUT --collection (collection_name=None passed to doc_indexer.index_markdown), which is the common ad-hoc/knowledge-note indexing pattern. Live-reproduced: raises unconditionally regardless of a pre-existing docs__<corpus>__bge-*__v1 collection.
3. src/nexus/indexer.py:516 (_conformant_name_for_repo) -- ad-hoc/unregistered-owner repo fallback.
4. src/nexus/indexer.py:681 (_migrate_legacy_collections, inside the RDR-103 migration-check loop) -- accidentally protected by an OUTER `except Exception` in the caller (indexer.py:4093-4100) that swallows and proceeds with pre-migration names, but this is incidental exception-swallowing, not a deliberate grandfather, and does not save call site #1 above (which runs first, unguarded, in the same nx index repo invocation).
5. src/nexus/repo_identity.py:331 (_resolve_repo_collection's synthesis fallback) -- reachable after its own `except Exception` around a `collection_for_repo` call falls through to a second, unguarded call.
6. src/nexus/commands/dt.py:63 (DEVONthink import command) -- same unguarded pattern.

Only nx store put / mcp store_put / nx memory promote (which route through t3_collection_name(..., t3=<real client>, for_write=True)) honor the documented grandfathering. nx index pdf/md --collection <explicit> ALSO skip grandfathering (t3=None short-circuits straight to the strict resolver in t3_collection_name), so even the explicit-collection indexing path diverges from store put's behavior for the identical config state.

Net effect: the shipped docs/cli-reference.md table's claim "Write (index / store put): grandfathers onto bge" (key absent + pre-existing bge row) is FALSE for indexing entry points -- the most common ones (`nx index repo`, `nx index md/pdf` without --collection) crash instead of grandfathering.

No test in the round-3 diff exercises any of these 6 call sites under the keyless-voyage + pre-existing-bge-collection scenario; all new tests target t3_collection_name() or the raw effective_embedding_model_for_writes() primitive in isolation.

Fix options: (a) route all 6 call sites through t3_collection_name(..., for_write=True) with a live t3 probe so grandfathering is uniform, or (b) give effective_embedding_model_for_writes() itself an optional grandfather-probe parameter these callers can supply, or (c) at minimum, narrow the credential gate to fire only when about to mint a name that does not already exist anywhere reachable. Needs a design decision, not a quick patch, since some call sites (http_catalog_client.py) are catalog-tier and don't have a t3 vector client handy.

Full trace and live-repro commands in substantive-critic verdict, T2 nexus/nexus-35ok4-fix-local-voyage-embed-model [22806] round 4 addendum.
notes:
Round 5 (nexus-35ok4's re-review round): the fix for this bead passed
re-review with 0 Critical. Two housekeeping items from that re-review
addressed alongside nexus-35ok4's own: the RDR-109 mode-declaration
census needed exclusion entries for the new test files this bead's fix
introduced (test_o5x2c_write_chokepoint_repros.py + 2 daemon tests),
and resolve_write_embedding_model gained structlog debug events for
grandfather/probe-failure observability. Full detail on nexus-35ok4 and
T2 nexus/nexus-35ok4-fix-local-voyage-embed-model round 5 entry.

Full suite green: 12991 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors.

Still OPEN/IN_PROGRESS, not self-closed -- ready to ship pending the
human commit/close step alongside nexus-35ok4.

title: ROOT CAUSE MEASURED: launchd ProcessType=Background confines engine ONNX inference to background QoS (E-cores) — 15x embedding slowdown, exactly reproduces field 0.5 chunks/s
description:
Field report (Gerasimos Pollatos, Slack 2026-08-18): fresh M4 Max install, indexing 542-file repo at ~0.5 chunks/s (16h ETA), 7-36s per 16-chunk upsert page, service profile all-hot in fp32 MlasSgemm, ~8 threads at ~37%, cv_wait churn, machine >75% idle, PG idle.

ROOT CAUSE — MEASURED, not inferred (probe: service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/Bge768ThroughputProbeTest.java, TEMPORARY do-not-commit; box: M4 Max 12P+4E 128GB, same HW class as reporter; ORT 1.20.0, real bge fp32 model, 16 texts x 512 tokens = worst-case upsert page mirroring Bge768Embedder.embedBatch exactly):

  default SessionOptions, normal QoS:      2.06-2.16 s/page  (~7.6 chunks/s)
  same, under taskpolicy -b (darwin bg):   31.6-33.6 s/page  (~0.5 chunks/s)  <- FIELD NUMBER, EXACT

conexus/daemon/com.nexus.service.plist line 72-73 sets ProcessType=Background. launchd applies the darwin background resource-management role to the whole supervisor tree (engine binary inherits); macOS confines background-QoS threads to the 4 E-cores. 15x slowdown. This exactly reproduces every field symptom: 0.5 chunks/s; 7-36s band (31s at full-512 pages, less for shorter chunks); ~8 ORT threads at low utilization fighting 4 E-cores with cv_wait churn; 12 P-cores idle (>75% machine idle).

RULED OUT by the same probe matrix (all normal-QoS):
  - undersized/default ORT intra-op pool: sweep intraop 1/4/8/12/16 -> 15.6/3.9/2.1/1.6/2.1 s. Default==8-16 behavior, near-optimal. (intraop=12, P-core count, is ~25% better than default — minor tuning opportunity only.)
  - per-item batch-1 inference (the field Fable hypothesis): batch16 one-pass 2.1s vs 16x batch1 sequential 2.0s — batching is fine either way at this size.
  - concurrent session.run contention (flush_concurrency=3): 3 concurrent batch16 = 5.2-5.3s wall (~9 chunks/s aggregate) — mild, no collapse.
  - fp32-CPU intrinsically too slow: at normal QoS the fp32 CPU EP does ~7.6 chunks/s worst-case-512, ~16h-ETA becomes ~1h; fp32 is NOT the binding constraint.

SCOPE: macOS only. conexus/daemon/nexus-service.service (systemd) has no Nice/CPUWeight/slice clamps. Also explains why perf differs wildly by START PATH: a session-started supervisor (heal-on-next-use, nx daemon service start from a shell) is NOT clamped; only the launchd-bootstrapped one is. Fresh installs register autostart at nx init (P2.4 decide-first), so new users get the clamped path — worst first impression by construction. Candidate confound for nexus-b32rx/nexus-33hpq measurements: which start path was live during those runs was not controlled.

FIX DIRECTION (not implemented — diagnosis only per Hal 2026-08-18): drop ProcessType=Background or set ProcessType=Standard/Adaptive in com.nexus.service.plist; alternatively have the supervisor or engine raise its own QoS (taskpolicy/setpriority) for embed work. Any fix must re-verify: (a) probe numbers under launchd-bootstrapped start, (b) peak-RSS class nexus-33hpq unaffected, (c) plist change propagates on upgrade (installed plists are rendered copies — an upgrade must re-render or users keep the clamped unit).
close_reason: Shipped develop @ 25de2c688. ProcessType=Background removed from com.nexus.service.plist; measured: 2.1s vs 31.7s per 16x512 page normal-vs-background QoS (clean box), reconfirmed 3-4s vs 37-86s under load. Convergence: upgrade-finish report-only NOTE + actual re-render/re-bootstrap in nx daemon restart-stale + nx doctor backstop sharing the same drift probe. Pin tests ban ProcessType (any value); Linux untouched (already clean). Stacked review: 1 Critical + 1 Significant, both fixed + re-verified (T2 [22805]). Disclosed deviation: no real launchd bootstrap dry-run (HOME does not isolate launchd; this box is the production install) — taskpolicy -b equivalence used; true bootstrap check needs a spare Mac.

title: Malformed shell quoting silently bypasses push-to-main, review-coverage, and bd-close review gates
description:
Found during code-review-expert review of nexus-cr4lp F1-F5/B1-B4 (T2 nexus/guard-evidence-cluster-root-cause-2026-08-18).

Three shlex-based segment tokenizers in the guard-evidence-cluster hooks catch ValueError (unbalanced
quotes) and `continue` -- silently SKIPPING the whole segment instead of degrading safely:
  1. _scan_command (git-add-wildcard rule) -- conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py
  2. _push_tokens (push-to-main + review-coverage rules, SAME file)
  3. the bash BD_VERBS matcher -- conexus/hooks/scripts/pre_close_verification_hook.sh

For (2) and (3), a segment that fails to tokenize means the rule's own VERB never matches (has_close_or_done
stays False / push_segments stays empty for that segment), so the entire hook fast-no-ops with a bare
ALLOW and ZERO warning -- a full, silent bypass of the guard, not merely "unverified".

Verified live (this checkout's own hook files):
  git push origin main --receive-pack="unterminated
    -> ALLOW, no context at all (push-to-main guard nexus-vduer fully bypassed)
  bd close nexus-abc12 --reason="unterminated
    -> ALLOW, no context at all (review-coverage close gate nexus-4av2n fully bypassed)

Contrast with nexus-cr4lp F3's OWN fix to BEAD_IDS_JSON harvesting (same pre-close hook file, ~30
lines below the BD_VERBS block): on the identical ValueError, F3 falls back to a raw regex scan over
the segment text -- the SAFE, over-inclusive direction. The bd-verb matcher and both python
tokenizers use the UNSAFE under-inclusive direction instead (silent full skip), directly adjacent
to code this diff touched but not itself modified by F2/F3.

Pre-existing (the try/except ValueError:continue pattern predates nexus-cr4lp in all three spots),
NOT a regression, NOT in the stated F1-F5/B1-B4 scope, so not a ship-blocker for nexus-cr4lp/
nexus-iwlq4. But it fully and silently defeats the primary guards this whole cluster of hooks
exists for (nexus-vduer push-to-main, nexus-4av2n review-coverage on both push and close), with a
plausible accidental trigger (an unescaped quote character anywhere in a --reason/-m value, or in
any argument of the gated command).

Recommend: apply the SAME safe fallback F3 already established (raw regex scan of the segment text
on ValueError) to all three sites listed above. Priority P1 given it fully and silently defeats the
security-relevant guards this cluster exists for; not blocking THIS release since it is pre-existing
and not a regression.

This is NOT a corner case. docs/managed-onboarding.md's own onboarding instructions are `nx config set service_url ...` -- config.yml, not an env export. docs/desktop-deployment.md is explicit: "The .mcpb reads config.yml, NOT your shell env ... Claude Desktop spawns the .mcpb as a GUI subprocess that does NOT inherit your interactive shell's environment." So the CANONICAL first-party managed-cloud onboarding path, and every Desktop (.mcpb) install, persists credentials in a shape this hook cannot read.

Consequence: for that population, is_local_mode()/get_credential() resolves the real client to cloud mode fine, but t2_prefix_scan.py raises _Unreachable on every SessionStart/SubagentStart, forever -- T2 injection stays exactly as absent as it was pre-fix, just with a visible line instead of silence.

Worse: the rendered fix_suggestion is actively wrong for this population -- "no NX_SERVICE_URL/NX_SERVICE_PORT env and no live supervisor lease at <path> (start it: nx daemon service start)" -- `nx daemon service start` is a LOCAL-mode-only command; a cloud-mode user has no local storage_service to start and following that advice does nothing.

Recommendation: either (a) add a minimal, stdlib-only line-scan for `service_url:`/`service_token:` under a `credentials:` block in config.yml (does not need a real YAML parser -- a bounded regex read of two known keys is safe and matches the hook's existing "narrow coverage, never silently wrong" posture), or (b) detect config.yml's mere presence-with-those-keys (even without extracting the value) and branch the warning message to name the real remedy (export NX_SERVICE_URL/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN in the shell that launches Claude Code/Desktop) instead of the local-mode-flavored one. Either way, stop emitting `nx daemon service start` unconditionally as the catch-all fix suggestion.

title: L1: DROP chash_alias — 4 writers, 8 reader sites, the legacy-width telemetry rows + regrowth CHECK, chash_old_bytes, and the dead chash_rekey rung, in one commit family
description:
THE DELETE. One session, one commit family. Everything dies together — writers, readers, table, legacy telemetry rows — because they all live in one repo and ship in one engine cut. There is no stop-writers-then-observe shape. jOOQ regeneration is the call-site census: removing the table removes Tables.CHASH_ALIAS and the compiler enumerates every survivor.

Plan of record: T2 `nexus/plan-legacy-retirement-2026-08-16`. Read it first.

PRECONDITION (already satisfied): RDR-194 P2 committed at 88921fc4f (remap-003-new-chash-bytea.xml). SOFT ordering: land after nexus-tk070.p3a to avoid merge friction on StagingPromoteOps.java (different methods, no textual conflict — not a correctness gate). DO NOT start while a developer holds the shared tree for P3a.

CENSUS DISCIPLINE, inverted for a delete world: the confirming census is a RAISE NOTICE count inside the deleting changeset (confirm-zero-or-delete-anyway). It is logged, it does not gate. Prevention lands WITH the deletion, never after it.

## New changelog `legacy-001-drop-chash-alias.xml`, tail-appended after remap-003, before the runAlways grants (RDR-194 D0.1)

(a) DELETE nexus.frecency rows WHERE chunk_id !~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'. RAISE NOTICE the count. frecency carries FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so RLS-toggle-wrap per the D0.3 precedent at catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:79-90.
(b) Same for nexus.relevance_log (FORCE RLS at telemetry-001-baseline.xml:84).
(c) ADD CHECK chunk_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' on both tables (+ any staging twin). This is the structural prevention.
(d) CREATE OR REPLACE nexus.remap_membership layered on remap-003-2, with the `LEFT JOIN nexus.chash_alias a ON a.old_bytes = r.new_chash` removed. chash_remap is EMPTY on cloud (RDR-194 cc2, BYPASSRLS-verified, T2 [22670]); that join was its supersession-chaining arm.
(e) DROP TABLE nexus.chash_alias (with its two indexes and RLS policy). DDL origin rdr180-001-bytea-chash.xml:315-337, changeset rdr180-12-chash-alias. No later ALTERs, only a GRANT MAINTAIN.
(f) DROP FUNCTION nexus.chash_old_bytes(text) — rdr180-002-hex-boundary-functions.xml:522-533. Only production caller is ChashSqlIdioms.oldBytesExpr:156, deleted in this commit. Precedent shape: nexus.manifest_orphans, already fully dropped.
(g) ANALYZE every rewritten table (D0.5, test_changelog_analyze_lint.py).

ROLLBACK (D0.6, and the nexus-cck6z data-fidelity lesson): recreate chash_alias EMPTY, recreate chash_old_bytes, restore the pre-drop remap_membership body verbatim, drop the two CHECKs. It CANNOT restore the deleted alias or telemetry rows — that is deliberate and the reason goes inline in the rollback naming this directive. Exercised by SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest.

## Java — writers (exactly 4, all die)

RekeyOps.java:231 (unconditional per rekey), :507 (synthesizeOrphans only); StagingPromoteOps.java:341 (per promoteCollection, legacy-refs-only filter), :565 (synthesizeOrphans only). Nothing ever DELETEs or UPDATEs the table.

## Java — readers (all die or lose their alias arm)

- ChashSqlIdioms.frecencyAliasAggregateDsl:304-317 (FRECENCY.CHUNK_ID -> OLD_REF join), plus OLD_REF_LEMMA:138, oldBytesExpr:156, typed rendering :198.
- ChashCensus:221-274 — the notExists CHASH_ALIAS arm in unresolvableHexCount, and EITHER_ERA_SHAPE (:203) for the frecency/relevance_log legs. PRECISION: (c)'s CHECK makes legacy WIDTH structurally impossible, so the shape filter and alias arm retire; it does NOT make DANGLING impossible, so those two dangling legs SURVIVE as pure 64-hex-only dangling checks. RDR-194 D7's no-FK grain argument is untouched and not reopened. The topic_assignments leg belongs to nexus-tk070.p3d — do not touch it here.
- ChashHandler.handleLookup:144-166 — GET /v1/chash/lookup dispatching legacy refs to resolveLegacyRef.
- CatalogHandler read-path 32-hex acceptance :1220/:1242 (write path already rejects at :2460-2484).
- CatalogRepository.stagingGuardCondition:4833-4844 — the third sweep guard's CHASH_ALIAS.OLD_REF notExists arm. LOCKSTEP INVARIANT stated in its own javadoc: coextensive-by-construction with StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant's manifestResolvable (:764-765) and its promote join (:821). Both alias arms MUST be removed in the SAME commit or guard and promote diverge. Both then reduce to the direct ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ admission arm — the fail-loud behaviour we want.
- RekeyOps:698-707 and StagingPromoteOps:1092-1111 — the alias-driven coalesce-to-hex telemetry UPDATE cascades. Readers of the map AND the mechanism that kept telemetry chunk_id canonical; (c) plus the handler enforcement below take over that job.

title: Cross-process data-token cache (lease-file pattern) or mint-rate headroom: permanent mint_token enablement fails loud past 5 back-to-back nx invocations/min (MintRateLimiter burst) and mints one scope=data row per CLI invocation
description:
From the nexus-rftfs gate critique (T2 nexus/nexus-rftfs-cross-process-mint-critique [22718]): DataTokenManager (04158dad4) caches per-process only; every nx subprocess mints fresh. Two consequences for PERMANENT mint_token enablement (single-read canary and MCP-server usage are unaffected: long-lived process, cache works): (1) engine MintRateLimiter defaults burst=5/sustained=1 per (credential,tenant) per minute (MintRateLimiter.java:14-21,145-159); >5 back-to-back nx invocations start failing loud with DataTokenMintError, and the client mint retry budget (3 attempts, 15s Retry-After cap, ~30s wall) cannot bridge a 60s refill window — release gates and bulk CLI loops routinely exceed this; (2) one short-TTL scope=data row per invocation feeds the nexus-lgiqw residue class until its reaper ships.

Two remedies, EITHER unblocks permanent enablement (do (a) regardless as cheap headroom): (a) config-only, engine-side: raise NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_BURST / NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE on deployed engines (e.g. burst>=20, sustained>=5/min) — cloud is a conexus deploy setting, local rides engine env; (b) durable, client-side: cross-process token cache persisted with tight perms using the lease-file pattern (db/t1.py t1_session_lease shape: ~/.config/nexus/data_token_lease.<host>.<tenant>, 0600, atomic write, TTL-stamped, corrupt/expired = re-mint), so all nx subprocesses share one live token; doctor "reused" then becomes real on the CLI.

POLICY (recorded on nexus-wrwb7 too): the canary window proceeds unaffected; do NOT set mint_token permanently on a live install until (a) or (b) lands. Doc honesty edits for the per-process reality shipped with the rftfs gate commit. Search keys: DataTokenManager, MintRateLimiter, data_token_lease, cross-process cache, nexus-lgiqw, nexus-rftfs, nexus-wrwb7.

title: DataTokenManager mint body sends tenant='default' — real mint-locked credentials are bound to a NAMED tenant (e.g. 'nexus'), DataTokenHandler.java:151 403s on mismatch
design:
Context: nx

CRITICAL finding from substantive-critic review of nexus-wrwb7 (T2 [22710]).

Every production construction site of HttpVectorClient / RefreshableHttpStoreMixin adopters / HttpScratchStore uses the literal DEFAULT_TENANT="default" (grep confirmed zero non-default tenant threading anywhere in src/nexus for any Http* store). DataTokenManager.bearer_for(base_url, tenant) forwards this same "default" string as the mint POST body's "tenant" field.

service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/DataTokenHandler.java:151:
  if (TokenStore.SCOPE_MINT_LOCKED.equals(scope) && !tenant.equals(RequestContext.tenant()))
      -> 403 "forbidden: this mint credential is locked to tenant '<credential's real tenant>' and cannot mint for tenant 'default'"

RequestContext.tenant() (AuthFilter.java:151) is SERVER-RESOLVED from the presented credential's own service_tokens.tenant_id row -- the client's tenant string is otherwise ignored on every OTHER route (AuthFilter.java:147-156, X-Nexus-Tenant header explicitly ignored), which is why the existing static service_token model has worked fine while always sending "default". The mint route is the ONE place a client-supplied tenant string is actually validated (body field, not header), and it must match the mint-locked credential's own bound tenant exactly.

Per bd show nexus-wrwb7 comments, Hal's real provisioned credential is described as "tenant nexus" (contrasted explicitly against conexus's own "gate-xr789" tenant in the same thread) -- strongly suggesting the real bound tenant_id is NOT the literal string "default".

If so, every mint attempt against the REAL credential will 403 immediately with a self-diagnosing error message (DataTokenMintError surfaces the server's verbatim text, confirmed by test_cross_tenant_403_surfaces_verbatim in tests/db/test_data_token.py).

WHY THE DEVELOPER'S E2E DID NOT CATCH THIS: tests/db/test_data_token_manager_e2e.py issues its OWN mint-locked credential for `tenant = t2_service_env` (a synthetic per-test tenant) and then mints using that SAME tenant string -- self-consistent by construction, so it structurally cannot exercise the mismatch a REAL client (always "default") x REAL credential (bound to a named tenant) would hit. Textbook "gate exercises a different path than the real client" (STEP-6 lesson).

RECOMMENDATION (before the "client half verified" relay or the canary window):
1. Verify server-side what literal tenant_id string Hal's actual mint-locked credential is bound to (ask conexus, or decode via a local admin lookup).
2. If it is not literally "default", thread the real tenant through the client's construction path (config key / env, e.g. NX_TENANT or reuse an existing identity source) so DataTokenManager.bearer_for() sends the credential's own tenant, not the DEFAULT_TENANT sentinel.
3. Add a regression test that mints against a credential bound to tenant X while the calling client's own tenant param is DEFAULT_TENANT ("default"), asserting the CURRENT 403 (documents the bug) then flips to asserting success once fixed.

Not caught by code-review-expert's line-level pass (this is a cross-file, cross-language, design-conformance gap, not a local bug).
close_reason: Fixed in 04158dad4: mint_tenant config (NX_MINT_TENANT) sent as the mint body tenant; 403 teaching error; tenant-asymmetric + wrong-tenant E2E arms green on the real engine substrate

title: Cross-instance REQUEST relays can silently never become work: mechanize an inbound-relay ack gate (T2 conexus-to-nexus-*REQUEST/QUESTION* entries must map to a nexus bead within N days, surfaced at SessionStart / nx doctor)
description:
Incident (Hal-flagged 2026-08-15): conexus wrote a P1 REQUEST relay to T2 on 2026-07-12 (conexus/conexus-to-nexus-REQUEST-nx-mcp-self-minting-client-gap-2026-07-12 [20682], their bead conexus-bv5z) naming the client at 6.6.1. It was never acknowledged nor turned into a nexus bead; five weeks and four client releases (6.6.1 -> 7.7.0) passed until conexus re-raised it live and nexus-wrwb7 was filed. The T2 relay bus has no delivery/ack guarantee: a session that is not the one live at write time never sees it, and nothing sweeps for unacknowledged inbound requests. conexus-3f is being asked for the full list of other unacknowledged items (record on this bead when it arrives).

Why P1: cross-instance requests are how cloud-side blockers reach the client repo; a dropped one can ship a global cutover (conexus-qomd) that 401s every live request.

What: (1) a sweep `nx relay inbox` (or a lint under tests/ + a SessionStart hook line) that lists T2 entries in project conexus (and nexus) whose title matches conexus-to-nexus-*(REQUEST|QUESTION|ASK|P1)* newer than the last recorded ack, and requires each to be referenced by a nexus bead (bd search for the T2 id or the conexus bead id in description/comments); unacknowledged items older than N days (say 3) print loudly at session start and fail `nx doctor` softly. (2) An explicit ack convention: the receiving side files a bead whose description carries the T2 relay id, and writes an ACK relay back; the sweep keys on that. (3) Symmetric outbound: nexus-to-conexus REQUEST relays we sent that have no ANSWER/ACK entry after N days are listed too. Non-vacuity: the sweep must assert it recognised at least one relay title in the corpus, else report BLINDSPOT not clean. Search keys: relay, cross-instance, conexus-to-nexus, ack, T2 bus, conexus-bv5z, nexus-wrwb7.
close_reason: Mechanism shipped: scripts/check_inbound_relay_acks.py + 38 tests, stacked-reviewed (marker T2 [22833]); anchored ack probe closes the false-ack surface the critique found. Residue stated on the bead: SessionStart/nx-doctor surfaces (release-cadence sweep is the current delivery, deferral-staleness precedent) and two Sam-judgment items (T2-only-answer-as-ack; the 8 live unacked relays).

Nothing in src/nexus references POST /v1/data-tokens/mint except a help string in commands/service_cmd.py:190; there is no mint-locked credential holder, no self-mint, no data-token presentation. Today the conexus edge injects a CP-held per-tenant engine token and EdgeProxyHandler strips any client Authorization header, so the static token is effectively ignored on the cloud path.

WHY P1: conexus-qomd (edge becomes pure pass-through per RDR-005 2a) is a GLOBAL cutover; if it ships while nx cannot self-mint, every request from the only live tenant (nexus, including this box's MCP servers) 401/403s immediately, and conexus STEP-6 gate would not catch it (it exercises gate-xr789, not the real nexus tenant client).

ACCEPTANCE (either, agreed with conexus): (a) nx-mcp/nx holds a mint-locked credential for the tenant, self-mints a data token via POST /v1/data-tokens/mint (schema per T2 nexus/conexus-to-nexus-COMPLETE-rdr005-2a-phase1-mint-locked-2026-07-11 [20611] and conexus/design-hnm1-phase1-mint-locked-provisioning.md [20597]), caches/refreshes it before expiry, presents it as Authorization on every engine call (T1/T2/T3 HTTP clients share the auth mixin), verified end-to-end against live BEFORE the qomd cutover; or (b) conexus redesigns qomd to keep an injection fallback so the cutover cannot break the nexus tenant without client changes. Decide (a) vs (b) with Hal; (a) is client work in this repo. Design surface: where the mint-locked credential lives (config.yml credential vs keychain), rotation, local-mode no-op (bundled engine has no edge), doctor check for token freshness. Search keys: data-tokens/mint, mint-locked, service_token, EdgeProxyHandler, RDR-005 2a, conexus-qomd, conexus-bv5z.

title: assign_from_chashes_<dim> topics doc_count UPDATE deadlocks under concurrent callers (unordered multi-row lock, 40P01 surfaces as 500)
description:
Observed by conexus (their bead conexus-ddh0) 2026-08-15 ~22:35-22:55Z during a bulk `nx index` run against tenant nexus on engine-service-v0.1.76: conexus-dev-edge-5xx-rate ALARM ~20 min, peak 12 5xx/min. Two symptoms: (1) 4x HTTP 500 from `ERROR: deadlock detected` inside nexus.assign_from_chashes_1024 (manifest write path); (2) manifest/write_many requests blocking past the public edge 30s upstream timeout. Engine was IDLE (load 0.07, container CPU 1.3%) so this is lock contention, not saturation. Deadlocks predate 0.1.76 (pg_stat_database: 12 all-time vs 8 in the post-deploy container).

Why: a deadlock is a normal outcome of concurrent writers and the loser is supposed to retry; surfacing 40P01 as a 500 pushes the retry (or the data loss) onto the client. The 30s blocking suggests the same lock ordering problem or a long transaction holding a lock the manifest write needs.

What: (a) identify the lock order in assign_from_chashes_1024 / the manifest write_many transaction that produces the cycle (pg_locks / deadlock log detail from the cloud engine log; ask conexus for the DETAIL lines); (b) either fix the ordering (sort chashes/doc rows before locking) or retry the statement on SQLSTATE 40P01 with bounded backoff at the engine layer, and return a 503/Retry-After only after retries are exhausted; (c) measure whether the >30s blocking is the same lock or a separate long transaction and address it. Reproduce with a concurrent-writer engine test (real PG) before fixing.

Search keys: assign_from_chashes, deadlock, 40P01, write_many, manifest, edge 30s timeout, conexus-ddh0. Recorded in T2 nexus/rdr194-cloud-count-2-2026-08-15 [22670].
close_reason: Fixed on develop d401e92ca..433246839 (2026-08-19): engine deadlock+gc_audit producers, client doctor check, split conservation, boost-layer gate, fixture env pin. Stacked-reviewed 3 rounds, engine suite 2148/0, pytest 13266/0, lint green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (conexus, engine container log Where: clauses, all 8 deadlock events): every event is "while locking tuple in relation topics", inside nexus.assign_from_chashes_<dim>, statement: UPDATE nexus.topics t SET doc_count = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nexus.topic_assignments ta WHERE ta.topic_id = t.id AND ta.tenant_id = t.tenant_id) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, topic_id FROM new_rows) a WHERE t.id = a.topic_id AND t.tenant_id = a.tenant_id. Mechanism: multi-row UPDATE driven by an UNORDERED DISTINCT set; two concurrent calls lock topics rows in plan order, A holds X wants Y, B holds Y wants X. Lock-order inversion of the statement against itself; only needs concurrency (explains the 4 pre-0.1.76 events). The v0.1.76 FKs (catalog_document_chunks->chunks, chunks->catalog_collections) are NOT in the cycle; earlier cross-table hypothesis struck. FIX: (1) correctness: take row locks in deterministic order first: SELECT (tenant_id, id) FROM nexus.topics WHERE ... ORDER BY tenant_id, id FOR UPDATE, then UPDATE (ORDER BY on the driving subquery alone is not reliable; the explicit ordered FOR UPDATE is). (2) probability: doc_count is a full COUNT(*) per affected topic which widens the lock window; use an incremental delta. Repro: concurrent-writer engine test on real PG. STILL OPEN: manifest/write_many >30s edge timeouts were the bulk of the 5xx and are NOT explained by this; possibly waiting behind the long doc_count transactions but unestablished. Function lives in the taxonomy changelogs (assign_from_chashes_<dim>, per-dim variants); DDL fix goes through Liquibase CREATE OR REPLACE tail-append.

comments.text: SCOPE NARROWED: the manifest/write_many >30s edge timeouts are NOT this bug and NOT a database problem. conexus traced them (engine events write_manifest_many_swept / catalog_handler_error op=/manifest/write_many, not "write_many"): CceEmbedder -> Voyage HTTP 429 (project RPM limit 4000/min for voyage-context-3) -> 74x cce_retry attempt=1 status=429 delay_ms 273-451 -> accumulated retry time exceeds the edge 30s upstream bound -> 5xx. register_many_timing during the window showed 10-25ms of DB work. Two independent incident causes: (1) write_many 5xx bulk = Voyage 429 + retry overrun (tracked separately, nexus-side CCE backoff bead + client-side concurrency bounding on conexus-ddh0); (2) 4x assign_from_chashes 500 = topics doc_count lock-order inversion = THIS bead. The ordered FOR UPDATE fix does not address (1); do not credit it with the whole incident.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DEVELOPER DISPOSITION (engine half, real-PG tested): FIXED, test-verified GREEN.

Two independent deadlock sources found (not one) — both now on develop (uncommitted, shared tree):
1. topics_doc_count_recount_ins/_del's own UPDATE lock-order inversion (the bead's named root cause). Fixed in taxonomy-013-doc-count-lock-order.xml via CREATE OR REPLACE: materialize the affected (tenant_id, topic_id) pairs into a plain array (array_agg, no locking clause), then acquire each topics row lock ONE AT A TIME via a single-table, PK-indexed `SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id=? AND id=? FOR UPDATE` in a PL/pgSQL loop over the pre-sorted array. This was the THIRD attempt — two earlier, textbook-looking approaches (bare `FOR UPDATE`, then `JOIN unnest(...) ... FOR UPDATE OF t`) both compiled and ran but did NOT actually serialize concurrent callers (verified empirically against real PG: PostgreSQL's LockRows node sits BELOW Sort for a JOIN plan, so ORDER BY does not control lock-acquisition order once a join is involved — only a genuinely single-table, join-free FOR UPDATE honors it). Full derivation + rejected hypotheses are in the changeset's own header comment.
2. A SECOND, independent hazard survives fix #1: assign_from_chashes_<dim>'s own INSERT (taxonomy-006's `persisted` CTE) carries an implicit FK-check lock on each referenced topics row, taken in `nearest`'s ORDER BY c.chash order (uncorrelated with topic_id) — BEFORE the trigger even runs. No trigger-level fix can close this. Mitigated via TaxonomyRepository#assignFromChashes now wrapping its transaction in DeadlockRetry (pre-existing nexus-ps9wb infra), matching the bead's own explicitly-authorized fallback ("retry the statement on SQLSTATE 40P01 with bounded backoff").

Test: service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/TopicsDocCountDeadlockConcurrencyTest.java. RED (raw INSERT, bypassing assignFromChashes/DeadlockRetry, against the pre-fix trigger body): real 40P01s reproduced reliably (surefire: 13.4s, pass). GREEN (real assignFromChashes call path, trigger fix + DeadlockRetry together): zero deadlocks escape across 20 concurrent rounds, doc_count exactly matches independent COUNT(*) (surefire: 22.4s, pass). Both phases pass per target/surefire-reports/TEST-...TopicsDocCountDeadlockConcurrencyTest.xml.

OUT OF SCOPE per bead: write_many >30s Voyage-429 edge-timeout class — untouched, not credited to this fix.

Changeset: taxonomy-013-doc-count-lock-order.xml (new), registered in db.changelog-master.xml at the established late-append tail (after vectors-007, before grants-nexus-svc.xml).

NOTE: this bead was worked concurrently by a second developer-agent dispatch on the same shared tree (source 2 + DeadlockRetry belt is their find/fix, converged with mine independently — see the changeset header's "CORRECTION" section for the joint derivation). Orchestrator should reconcile/commit once, not twice.

Full mvn suite + --candidate-migration NOT run by me (scoped runs only, per relay instructions) — orchestrator/release gate must run those before tag.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
developer (2nd pass, engine-side): GREEN, verified via TWO consecutive full runs of TopicsDocCountDeadlockConcurrencyTest against real PG.

TWO INDEPENDENT DEADLOCK SOURCES found empirically (not just reasoned about — three hypotheses were tried and disproven along the way, all documented in taxonomy-013-doc-count-lock-order.xml's header):

(1) topics_doc_count_recount_ins/_del's own UPDATE, unordered SELECT DISTINCT-driven lock acquisition — Hal's NAMED root cause. Fixed in taxonomy-013-doc-count-lock-order.xml: a single-table, single-row, PK-indexed 'SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id=? AND id=? FOR UPDATE' inside a PL/pgSQL loop over a pre-sorted (ORDER BY inside array_agg) array of affected topics. Two earlier attempts (bare FOR UPDATE on a DISTINCT-joined subquery; FOR UPDATE OF t on the same join with the dedup materialized into unnest() arrays) both looked correct by inspection and both failed against real PG: PostgreSQL rejects any locking clause in a statement whose FROM-list reaches a DISTINCT/GROUP BY subquery ANYWHERE (not just the top level), and separately, PG's LockRows executor node sits BELOW Sort for a JOIN plan, so a join-based ORDER BY...FOR UPDATE does not actually serialize concurrent callers even when it compiles and runs. Only the join-free single-row form actually works.

(2) An INDEPENDENT implicit FOR KEY SHARE lock Postgres takes on each referenced topics row as assign_from_chashes_<dim>'s own INSERT (the persisted CTE) processes rows, in nearest's ORDER BY c.chash order — uncorrelated with topic_id. This survives fix (1) structurally: by the time the trigger runs, the conflicting lock from the earlier, differently-ordered INSERT statement is already held, so no fix confined to the trigger function can close it. Verified empirically (20/20 rounds still deadlocked with fix (1) alone). (bead nexus-ps9wb's existing bounded-retry infrastructure, same pattern assignMany/importBatch already use in this file). Idempotent and safe — persisted's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus Postgres's full rollback of the deadlock loser before retry.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic (crit-fix pile review): SIGNIFICANT x2, otherwise sound.

(1) taxonomy-013's header comment gets PG locking semantics wrong on the hypothesis-2 rejection. Empirically verified against real PG 16 (docker, EXPLAIN + direct queries): 'FOR UPDATE OF t1' (unlike bare FOR UPDATE) is NOT rejected when a joined subquery contains DISTINCT — contradicts the header's claim that 'OF <table> ... does not exempt the statement from this restriction.' Also: EXPLAIN on the unnest-join + ORDER BY + FOR UPDATE OF t1 shape shows LockRows sits ABOVE Sort (receives sorted input) — the OPPOSITE of the header's claimed mechanism ('LockRows executor node sits BELOW the Sort node'). The likely real explanation for hypothesis-2's observed 17-20/20 deadlocks is contamination from the SECOND, independent FK-lock deadlock source, which was present throughout testing and never isolated out before hypothesis-2 was rejected. Does not threaten the shipped fix (the single-row loop is safe for an unrelated, airtight reason — sequential PL/pgSQL statement execution) but the changelog now carries a confidently-stated, incorrect PG mechanism as permanent documentation.

(2) TopicsDocCountDeadlockConcurrencyTest's GREEN phase is non-discriminating w.r.t. the trigger fix specifically: it runs through the real call path with DeadlockRetry (MAX_ATTEMPTS=4) active, only 2 threads/round (one possible pairing, loser gets up to 3 uncontended retries) — a regression of the trigger back to the unordered form would very likely still pass escaped==0 via the retry belt alone. RED correctly isolates the trigger pre-fix via raw-INSERT bypass; there's no analogous post-fix raw-INSERT-bypass check proving the ordered trigger closes source 1 on its own, independent of the retry belt (only an unverified ad hoc note in the changelog header claims 20/20 with only the trigger fix, attributed to source 2).

Both non-blocking for shipping the current fix. Recommend: (1) correct/soften the LockRows-vs-Sort claim in taxonomy-013's header, ideally re-attributing hypothesis-2's failure to source-2 contamination rather than a Postgres executor-ordering myth; (2) add a raw-INSERT-bypass round post-fix (bypassing DeadlockRetry) asserting the trigger alone drives deadlock rate near zero.

This directly undermines the specific failure mode nexus-sybbh exists to catch, even after the 4 producers are correctly wired (independently verified: all 4 are real, boundary-correct at exactly GC_AUDIT_MAX_CHASHES=5000, and the base64 RETURNING bug fix is properly tested). comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic (2026-08-19, second pass on the crit-fix remediation): the client-side _check_gc_audit_non_empty_after_purge fix (health.py) closes the reviewers' original "any past row false-cleans forever" defect, but introduces TWO NEW, still-untested correctness bugs of the same false-clean/false-alarm class:

1. FALSE-CLEAN (rolling blind spot): the check computes oldest_ts = min(m["ts"] for m in markers) across ALL markers in the 7-day window and compares gc_audit's newest purge_trash row against that OLDEST marker, not the newest. For any install running purge-trash on a recurring cadence (daily/weekly cron -- the realistic operating mode, since markers accumulate up to 50 entries over a rolling 7-day window), a writer regression that breaks AFTER an earlier successful audit in the same window stays silently green for the rest of the window: gc_audit's stale row from day 1 satisfies newest_dt >= oldest_dt - skew even though the day-2..day-7 purges went completely unaudited. Should compare against max(ts) (the most recent local purge), not min.

2. FALSE-ALARM (no-op real purges): will_act = (not dry_run) and confirm in purge_trash_cmd -- record_purge_marker fires on EVERY real invocation regardless of whether anything was actually purged. But nexus.purge_trash's own audit INSERT is correctly gated on IF v_chunk_count > 0 OR v_count > 0 (catalog-033) -- a genuinely no-op real purge (the common case: nothing has aged out yet) writes NO gc_audit row by design. The client check has no way to distinguish this from the actual defect (audit writer broken) and will warn "gc_audit is EMPTY ... NOT confirmed audited" on every healthy no-op purge. The marker already carries result["documents_purged"]/chunks info; the check should skip cross-referencing (or require coverage only for) markers whose stored result shows nonzero effect.

Both gaps are untested -- TestCheckGcAuditNonEmptyAfterPurge's _markers() helper uses identical timestamps across all markers and documents_purged: 1 unconditionally, so neither the differential-timestamp nor the no-op scenario is exercised. Full writeup + doctor.py/MCP-ranking pressure-point verification in T2 nexus/substantive-critique-crit-fix-remediation-2026-08-19.

title: RDR-194 P3d (D1): composite FK topic_assignments -> chunks in the catalog-029 three-step shape; retire ChashCensus leg C1 and its either-era shape filter
description:
RDR-194 **P3d** (Decision D1, commit 4 of 4). The composite FK, and the
one-for-one retirement of `ChashCensus` leg C1.

## What ships

`taxonomy-012-doc-id-chunk-fk.xml` at the changelog TAIL before the runAlways
grants (D0.1). `EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS=3` (design intent — RE-PIN to the file as
authored).

**FK over populated data — the catalog-029 three-step shape is MANDATORY**, all
three steps in ONE file, ONE release, ONE migration walk
(`catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:19-45`):
1. `ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID`:
   ```
   FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, source_collection, doc_id)
   REFERENCES nexus.chunks (tenant_id, collection, chash)
   ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE
   ```
   `ON UPDATE CASCADE` for the parent-key reason catalog-029 makes it mandatory
   (`catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:49-52`; fk-002-5 already uses it on this
   very table). `ON DELETE CASCADE` because an assignment whose chunk is gone is
   exactly the dangling row census leg C1 exists to report.
2. **Anti-join remediation, never a count comparison** (F17), RLS toggle-wrapped
   (`catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:79-90`), affected count RAISE NOTICE'd.
   **The population is COUNTED before it runs** (D0.4) — cloud-count-4's
   measurements are the count of record; if the anti-join's live population would
   differ materially from what cc4 recorded, stop and re-count rather than
   proceeding.
3. `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` with the per-constraint MARK_RAN precondition the
   blanket tripwire requires (`tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py`;
   `catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:219-221`).

**Why composite, and why this target.** `chunks` is keyed
`(tenant_id, collection, chash)` (`vectors-004-unify-chunks.xml:262-273`) since
RDR-191 unified the dim shards; `chash` alone is not unique, so a single-column FK
to `chunks(chash)` is NOT expressible (A3). A tumbler FK is rejected on direct
evidence: `fk_ta_catalog_doc` was added and DROPPED (nexus-sa14p) because
`catalog_documents(tumbler)` is "a different identity space" that "could never be
satisfied for chash-keyed rows" (`TaxonomyRepository.java:1215-1219`) — A2.

**Census leg retirement, SAME commit, never ahead (D0.10).** Retire `ChashCensus`
leg C1 `dangling.topic_assignments` (`ChashCensus.java:253-256`, sharing
`unresolvableHexCount` at `:212-221`) and its "either era" shape filter
(`ChashCensus.java:195` — that filter exists ONLY to accommodate the titles claim
P3a disproved, so it retires WITH the leg rather than being tightened first).

**Why the leg cannot retire early.** `ChashCensus` has NO `nx doctor` flag and NO
HTTP endpoint: it runs FATAL inside `StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant`
(`:1224-1231`, reached via `POST /v1/staging/finalize`) and report-only in
`RekeyOps.java:774-780`. Retiring a leg NARROWS what `finalize` refuses on, so it
must land WITH the FK that makes the leg impossible.

**Consequence to state in the changeset, so no later reader misreads it as data
loss.** With `ON DELETE CASCADE`, any deletion of a `nexus.chunks` row
(`purge_trash`'s orphan-chunk sweep, RDR-192-class superseded-chunk reaping,
collection deletion) now also removes that chunk's `topic_assignments` rows. That
is the intended semantics and is precisely what retires leg C1.

**Legs C2 and C3 STAY** (`frecency.chunk_id`, `relevance_log.chunk_id`, D7, by
grain) — do not retire them here and do not read their survival as an oversight.
Leg C4 is untouched.

## Execution notes

- `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` before authoring:
  reason through the cascade blast radius against the three named chunk-deletion
  paths.
- SPAWN a `conexus:developer` subagent; SPAWN `Explore` for the `finalizeTenant`
  refusal-surface impact sweep.
- TDD: a test that the FK actually REJECTS an assignment for a nonexistent chunk
  (non-vacuous), and a test that deleting a chunk cascades its assignments away.
- Non-vacuity check, explicit: assert the VALIDATE covers rows — a table left
  mostly NULL on `source_collection` would validate green while enforcing nothing.
  P3b's `SET NOT NULL` is the structural defence; verify it is in place.
- Agents never `git add` the shared tree.
- Update `nx memory put -p nexus -t rdr194-continuation-state`.

**Context**
- RDR: § D1, § P3d, § Consequences ("Retired detections, one-for-one")

  catalog-029 three-step, MATCH SIMPLE vacuous validate

title: RDR-194 P3c (D1): topic_assignments.doc_id hex TEXT -> bytea (all-or-nothing decode, no tolerant CASE) + the seven compiler-invisible TaxonomyHandler sites
description:
RDR-194 **P3c** (Decision D1, commit 3 of 4). `topic_assignments.doc_id` hex TEXT
-> `bytea`. **The arc's highest-risk single step.**

**HARD STOP inherited from P3b / cloud-count-4 (nexus-tk070.cc4).** This step is
ALL-OR-NOTHING: `ALTER COLUMN doc_id TYPE bytea USING decode(doc_id,'hex')`
cannot partially succeed. It RAISES on any non-hex value rather than coercing, and
**no CASE branch is added to absorb one** — that tolerant expression is rejected
as A4 under D0.9, because it would convert an open question (are there non-hex
rows?) into an un-asked one. Do not start this bead while cloud-count-4's non-hex
arm is nonzero and undispositioned.

## What ships

`taxonomy-011-doc-id-bytea.xml` at the changelog TAIL before the runAlways grants
(D0.1). `EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS=1` (design intent — RE-PIN to the file as
authored).

- `ALTER COLUMN doc_id TYPE bytea USING decode(doc_id,'hex')`
- **ANALYZE in the same pass** (D0.5, mandatory for a rewrite): the PK
  `(tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id)` and the four `doc_id` indexes at
  `taxonomy-001-baseline.xml:114-118` all rebuild.

**Java work list.** jOOQ regeneration turns the compiler into the work list for
the repository half — roughly twenty-five `TaxonomyRepository.java` sites bind or
read `doc_id` as an opaque String (`:375, 384, 394, 518, 527, 548, 554, 706-711,
718-724, 762-774, 787-792, 802, 1030, 1237, 1246, 1436, 1446-1451, 1820, 1875,
1923, 2086, 2094, 2196, 2202, 2332, 2335-2340`), plus `StagingPromoteOps.java:975,
986`.

**THE ONE THING THE COMPILER WILL NOT CATCH — hand-enumerated for exactly that
reason (§ Consequences, "Java work list", named exception).** Seven
`TaxonomyHandler.java` sites (`:412, 452, 514, 529, 659, 696, 945`) keep compiling
against a `String` DTO while the value underneath changes shape. Each gains an
EXPLICIT hex encode outbound and decode inbound (D0.8). A green build is NOT
evidence these are done; each must be visited and tested.

**Python is unchanged.** It sends and receives hex end to end
(`http_taxonomy_store.py:409, 422, 430-435, 445-470, 472-495, 740-753, 901,
939-949`; `search_engine.py:425, 673, 698, 734-738`; `scoring.py:312, 337`) and
continues to; two of those sites key a dict by `doc_id`, a further reason the wire
stays hex rather than moving to bytes or base64. `taxonomy-006`'s
`RETURNS TABLE (chash text)` contract is likewise unchanged. Only the column moves.

**Test-suite debt, IN SCOPE, fixed in this same commit.** Fixtures that write
non-hex `doc_id` break at the conversion BY DESIGN:
`tests/test_taxonomy.py:1010-1022`,
`tests/test_taxonomy_rebuild_link_cleanup.py:167-173`,
`TaxonomyRepositoryTest.java:865-1357`, and `seed_legacy.py:880-900` (which seeds a
16-char legacy chash). A fixture that could no longer be written after the change
is the POINT of the change, not collateral — fix them to write real chashes, never
relax the column to keep them.

  enumerate the handler sites and the wire boundary first, then convert.

title: RDR-194 P3b (D1): cloud-count-4 HARD STOP, then source_collection backfill + counted deletion of the ambiguous/unresolvable remainders + SET NOT NULL
description:
RDR-194 **P3b** (Decision D1, commit 2 of 4). Take cloud-count-4, then backfill
`source_collection` and promote it to NOT NULL.

**HARD STOP GATE — cloud-count-4 (nexus-tk070.cc4).** Run it FIRST and record it
in T2. **If its non-hex arm is nonzero, STOP and inspect** per D1's named
re-decision branch. Do NOT proceed to P3c on a nonzero count. The two named
dispositions (delete as unrecomputable derived garbage with the count recorded, or
RE-DECIDE D1 as a documented no-FK with census leg C1 staying and P3c/P3d
cancelled) are the only two; there is no third that coerces or absorbs.

The stop is real, not defensive theatre: `rdr180-001-bytea-chash.xml:22` hedges on
"historic tumblers in topic_assignments" that nobody has counted, and the in-tree
prose about this column was wrong in two directions for over a month (nexus-yo9mi).

**Ordering, not negotiable.** P3a (which closes every writer that could produce a
non-conformant value) is already landed. The count is taken now. Nothing converts
until P3c.

## What ships

`taxonomy-010-source-collection-backfill.xml` at the changelog TAIL before the
runAlways grants (D0.1). `EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS=1` (design intent — RE-PIN to the
file as authored).

Remediation in order (D1's steps b, c, d), each counted first (D0.4):
- **(b) Unique-resolution backfill.** Set `source_collection` for existing NULL
  rows whose `doc_id` resolves to exactly ONE collection in `nexus.chunks`.
- **(c) Counted DELETE of the remainders**, both counts RAISE NOTICE'd:
  - the AMBIGUOUS remainder (a chash present in more than one collection cannot
    be attributed after the fact), and
  - the UNRESOLVABLE remainder (no matching chunk).
  Priced as safe because topic assignments are DERIVED data, recomputable by
  re-running assignment, and the writers' own `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes
  recomputation idempotent. This is the § Trade-offs "deleting rows vs preserving
  them" trade, taken deliberately.
- **(d) `SET NOT NULL`** on `source_collection` — this is what closes P3d's
  composite FK MATCH SIMPLE exemption. Without it the FK's VALIDATE goes green
  over a mostly-exempt table.

RLS toggle-wrap the remediation if the DML is blocked by FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
(precedent `catalog-029-manifest-chunk-fk.xml:79-90`); note that FORCE-RLS
no-ops migration DML silently, so verify the affected-row NOTICE is nonzero
against a seeded fixture rather than trusting a clean run.

## Execution notes

- `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for the
  backfill-vs-delete boundary before authoring DDL.
- SPAWN a `conexus:developer` subagent for implementation.
- TDD: seed a fixture with one uniquely-resolvable row, one ambiguous row (same
  chash in two collections) and one unresolvable row; assert exactly one survives
  with the right collection and that BOTH delete counts are reported.
- Falsify by DELETING code: remove the ambiguity branch and the test must fail.
- Rollback restores the baseline; a deliberately empty rollback carries its reason
  inline (D0.6) — deleted derived rows are not restorable, so say so there.
- Agents never `git add` the shared tree.
- Update `nx memory put -p nexus -t rdr194-continuation-state`.

**Context**

- Search keys: source_collection backfill, ambiguous chash, MATCH SIMPLE,
  cloud-count-4, FORCE RLS migration DML noop

title: RDR-194 P3a (D1): persist source_collection on the centroid branch, close the two arbitrary-text writers, correct the seven propagated doc_id prose sites
description:
RDR-194 **P3a** (Decision D1, commit 1 of 4). Close every writer that can produce
a non-conformant `topic_assignments.doc_id`, and correct the seven prose sites
that made this decision reverse twice. **No data change.** This lands BEFORE
cloud-count-4 is taken — the ordering is not negotiable.

Closes nexus-yo9mi (the seven propagated-inference sites) except for the
`ChashCensus` shape-filter half, which retires with leg C1 at P3d.

## What ships

**1. `taxonomy-009-assign-source-collection.xml`** at the changelog TAIL before
the runAlways grants (D0.1). Layered `CREATE OR REPLACE` of
`assign_from_chashes_{384,768,1024}` on top of `vectors-005-16/17/18` — never an
edit to the applied changeset (D0.2). `EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS=3` (design intent,
RE-PIN to the file as authored).

**The bug being fixed, and why it is a prerequisite rather than a nicety.** At
current HEAD the retargeted writers persist `source_collection` only on the
`projection` branch (`vectors-005-repoint-functions-views.xml:2445-2451`); the
`centroid` branch inserts `(tenant_id, doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by)` only
(`:2478-2481`, twins at `:2574` and `:2736`) even though `c.collection =
p_collection` is that branch's own filter three lines above. **The collection is
known and discarded.** Without this fix every centroid row carries NULL
`source_collection`, escapes P3d's composite FK through MATCH SIMPLE, and the
VALIDATE goes green over a mostly-exempt table — the vacuous-gate failure mode.

**2. Java companion.** `StagingPromoteOps.java:974-986` — the legacy-SQLite ETL
passthrough `COALESCE(hex(chash_alias.new_chash), staging.doc_id)` with its
`notLikeRegex` arm, the only production path that can write arbitrary text. It
gains an explicit REJECT on a non-conformant value **with the offending value
named in the error**, rather than passing it through to a column that can no
longer hold it (D0.9).

**3. Python companion.** `taxonomy_cmd.py:883-899` — `nx taxonomy assign <DOC_ID>
<LABEL>` is an unvalidated click argument. It gains 64-hex validation at the CLI
boundary so the operator gets a named error, not a Postgres decode failure.

title: RDR-194 gate precondition (HAL RELAY): cloud-count-4 — topic_assignments non-hex doc_id + length + source_collection splits; HARD STOP if the non-hex arm is nonzero
description:
RDR-194 § Gate preconditions, row **cloud-count-4**. BLOCKS P3b
(nexus-tk070.p3b) and P3c (nexus-tk070.p3c). **This is a HARD STOP, not a
formality** (RDR § D1, "Fail-loud point, and the named stop").

**HAL/conexus cross-instance RELAY, not autonomous work.** Surface an explicit
"relay: run cloud-count-4 against the live store" to Hal.

Four measurements, all required:

```sql
-- 4a. THE HARD STOP ARM. Must be zero, or its rows dispositioned, before P3c.
SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.topic_assignments WHERE doc_id !~ '^([0-9a-f]{2})+$';

-- 4b. length census
SELECT length(doc_id), count(*) FROM nexus.topic_assignments GROUP BY 1;

-- 4c. source_collection NULL vs non-NULL split
SELECT source_collection IS NULL AS is_null, count(*)
FROM nexus.topic_assignments GROUP BY 1;

-- 4d. of the NULL rows, how many resolve to exactly one / more than one / no
--     collection in nexus.chunks
SELECT n_coll, count(*) FROM (
  SELECT ta.doc_id,
         (SELECT count(DISTINCT c.collection) FROM nexus.chunks c
           WHERE c.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND c.chash = decode(ta.doc_id,'hex')) AS n_coll
  FROM nexus.topic_assignments ta WHERE ta.source_collection IS NULL
) s GROUP BY 1;
```

**HARD STOP branch, named in advance (D1).** If 4a is NONZERO, the phase STOPS
and the rows are INSPECTED before anything converts. Do not proceed to P3c on a
nonzero count. Two dispositions, and no third:
- If the rows prove to be historic tumblers or ETL-era external ids from the two
  admitting paths P3a closes, they are DELETED as unrecomputable derived garbage
  **with the count recorded**.
- If they prove to be a live identity space the Decision did not find, **D1 is
  RE-DECIDED as a documented no-FK**, the census leg C1 STAYS, and P3c/P3d are
  cancelled rather than forced. That is a return to the RDR, not a workaround.

**Why the stop is real and not defensive theatre.** `rdr180-001-bytea-chash.xml:22`
hedges on "historic tumblers in topic_assignments" that nobody has ever counted,
and the in-tree prose about this column has been wrong in two directions for over
a month (nexus-yo9mi). `ALTER ... TYPE bytea USING decode(...)` cannot partially
succeed. Absorbing a surprise with a tolerant `CASE` is rejected as A4 under D0.9.

**Ordering is not negotiable.** P3a (which closes every writer that can produce a
non-conformant value) lands BEFORE this count is taken; the count is taken BEFORE
anything converts.

**Context**
- RDR: § D1, § Gate preconditions, § P3
- Search keys: cloud-count-4, topic_assignments doc_id, hex, source_collection,
  MATCH SIMPLE, ChashCensus C1

title: RDR-191 P5: collections_checked numerator (catalog manifest rows) and 'nx collection list' denominator (T3 physical collections) count different populations — GATE-5 == comparison can mismatch on zero-manifest-row collections, not damage
design:
Found during substantive-critic review of nexus-o8dil.24 (2026-08-14).

nexus.manifest_verify_all() (catalog-020-index-run-fence.xml changeset 4)
derives its `collection` set EXCLUSIVELY from
nexus.catalog_document_chunks (the manifest table), via:

  WITH manifest AS (
      SELECT c.chash, c.collection
        FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks c
        JOIN nexus.catalog_documents d ON ... AND d.deleted_at IS NULL
       WHERE c.tenant_id = current_setting('nexus.tenant', true)
         AND c.collection IS NOT NULL
  ), checked AS (... ) SELECT collection, ... GROUP BY collection

GROUP BY over an empty input for a given collection emits NO row for it
(same documented omission pattern as the sibling collection_health_meta
view: "The view GROUP BYs collection, so it emits NO row for a collection
with zero documents"). So `_manifest_verify_list`'s
`collections_checked = len(rows)` (nexus-o8dil.24, F16b) counts "distinct
collections with >=1 catalog_document_chunks manifest row" — NOT "all
known collections."

docs/runbooks/rdr-191-phase5-cloud-fk.md Section 1 step 2 names the
INDEPENDENT denominator as `nx collection list` (HttpVectorClient.
list_collections(), backed by /v1/vectors/stats) — this counts T3's
PHYSICAL vector collections with live chunk counts. That is a DIFFERENT
population: any collection that exists in T3 (has chunks) but has ZERO
catalog_document_chunks manifest rows registered against it (pre-catalog
data, T3-only artifacts, anything indexed before manifest tracking
existed) is invisible to collections_checked's numerator by construction,
while still counted in known_collection_count.

Effect: nexus-o8dil.28 (GATE-5-LOCAL) and nexus-o8dil.30 (GATE-5-CLOUD)'s
literal acceptance ("collections_checked == known_collection_count from an
INDEPENDENT source") can spuriously FAIL — or spuriously mismatch — for a
reason that is NOT manifest damage, NOT unroutable-model-token, and NOT
row-cap truncation (the only causes the runbook currently attributes a
mismatch to, Section 1 step 3). A zero-manifest-row T3 collection is a
structural, possibly-permanent population difference, not a defect the
Phase 5 FK migration is meant to detect.

Needs a decision BEFORE .28/.30 execute: either (a) reconcile the
denominator to the SAME population manifest_verify_all walks (e.g. "T3

title: HDBSCAN max_cluster_size floor=100 fails to prevent root-grab at n≈100 and produces worst-case noise (57-62%) at n=150-200
notes:
VERIFIED RESOLVED by substantive-critic (independent re-verification, not just trusting the fix author's numbers).

Re-ran my own boundary sweep (same seed=7 methodology as the original finding) against the revised code (MAX_CLUSTER_SIZE_FLOOR=50, MAX_CLUSTER_FRACTION_DIVISOR=4):

  n=100  cap=50 (was 100)  top-cluster 38/100=38% (was 79/100=79% with floor=100)
  n=150  cap=50            top-cluster 20/150=13%, noise=49% (was noise=62% spike with floor=100)
  n=200  cap=50            top-cluster 22/200=11%, noise=48% (was noise=57% spike with floor=100)
  n=300  cap=75            noise=46%
  n=400  cap=100           noise=45%

The n=150-200 noise spike I originally found (57-62%, worse than the >=400 steady state) is gone -- noise is now a flat ~45-49% band across n=100-400, matching the steady state rather than spiking above it.

Directly reproduced the new test_cluster_caps_midwindow_collection fixture case (seed=3, n=150): uncapped = [98,9,7] (98-of-150 root-grab, matches the docstring's claim exactly); capped (floor=50) = 8 clusters, largest 10. Falsified the test by reverting to the old floor=100 value: the test's `assert cap == tc.MAX_CLUSTER_SIZE_FLOOR` line fails immediately (100 != 50), so a regression back to the old floor is genuinely caught, not just documented.

Verified the "floor=50 == floor=25 everywhere swept" claim: spot-checked n=100/150/400 at both floor values, identical cluster sizes and noise counts in all three cases -- floor=50 is a deliberate safety margin over the empirically-sufficient 25, not a load-bearing-but-untested number.

Verified the new code comment's factual claim that sklearn's max_cluster_size no-ops under cluster_selection_method='leaf': ran HDBSCAN(leaf, max_cluster_size=100) vs HDBSCAN(leaf, no cap) on the real fixture -- byte-identical output (same 17 clusters, same sizes, same noise=204). Comment is accurate.

Residual (NOT a new Critical, not blocking close): the same mathematical construction (cap==n when n<=floor) still exists at n<=50 -- by definition, not something the fix removed, just moved the boundary down from ~100 to ~50. I swept n=50 on the real fixture (seed=7) and found no actual root-grab there (top cluster 23/50=46%, not pathological) -- but this is an absence-of-observed-failure, not a proof of absence at that regime. Given both real failures found so far (the original 2101-chunk corpus and the 150-doc subsample) occurred at n>=100, and n<=50 is a much smaller/less realistic collection size for nx taxonomy discover, I'm not filing a new bead for this -- flagging it here for the record in case a future n<=50 failure surfaces.

Closing as resolved.

title: nexus-oizh7 count() dim-guard breaks list_collections/count() existence invariant
design:
PgVectorRepository.count() was given an `.and(ch.embedding().isNotNull())` dim guard
(bead nexus-oizh7, uncommitted diff on develop). This makes count() report only the
collection's DISPATCHED-dim rows, while `/v1/vectors/stats` (collection_vector_stats view,
GROUP BY dim, then Python's list_collections() SUMS across dim per collection name) still
reports the collection TOTAL across all dims present.

For a mixed-dim collection (a state the diff's own D1-hazard comment calls "a real
reachable state, not just a corrupted-data hypothetical", mirroring TaxonomyCentroidRepository's
documented mid-migration stance):
  - list_collections()/collection_vector_stats reports the FULL (dim-summed) count.
  - count()/collection_info() now reports ONLY the collection's own-dim count.
If the collection is at the extreme (zero own-dim rows yet, all rows foreign-dim — the very
start of a re-embed/reindex before any new-dim row lands), count()==0, and
HttpVectorClient._count_or_key_error raises KeyError("Collection not found: ...") even though
list_collections() enumerates it as present with count>0 — directly violating that method's own
documented invariant ("callers that enumerate via list_collections can never hit the zero-count
branch").

Concrete real-world break: `nx collection reindex <name>` (src/nexus/commands/collection.py:483-487)
does `info = db.collection_info(name)` as its FIRST step, "check collection exists", and raises
click.ClickException("collection not found") on KeyError. So the exact command meant to FIX a
stuck/mixed-dim collection can now refuse to find it, precisely during the scenario the guard
was written to defend against. Even short of the 0-row edge case, ANY partial mix silently
understates the total shown by `nx store list` / `nx collection info` vs `nx collection list`'s
total for the same name — two commands disagreeing about one collection's size.

Additionally the precedent cited in the javadoc/scratch note ("mirrors TaxonomyCentroidRepository's
documented centroid-side stance") is inaccurate for count() specifically: TaxonomyCentroidRepository.count()
(service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/TaxonomyCentroidRepository.java:197-206) deliberately
does NOT dim-guard, with the opposite rationale in its own comment: "this method counts centroids,
not centroids-at-a-dim." The sibling repository already decided this exact question the other way for
its analogous `count()` method; the citation supports the diff's `dimensionProbe`-style guards, not its
`count()` guard.

Mitigations to evaluate: either (a) drop the dim guard from count() to match TaxonomyCentroidRepository's
collection-total stance and keep count()/stats/list_collections agreeing, or (b) keep the guard but
audit + fix every caller that treats count()==0 as a proxy for non-existence (_count_or_key_error,
nx collection reindex's existence check), update collection_vector_stats/list_collections to also report
per-dim (stop silently summing), and add a regression test for the reindex-existence-check + total-display
scenario, not just the mechanical exclusion the current PgVectorRepositoryDimGuardTest covers.

getEmbeddings' guard, by contrast, is validated as correct: chunk_quarantine.py's
_fetch_full (list ids via col.get(), then db.get_embeddings(collection_name, got_ids)) already
has an alignment guard (len(embs) != len(got_ids)) that safely catches the post-fix drop of
foreign-dim ids; pre-fix, a foreign-dim id got a same-length-but-empty embedding entry that would
NOT have tripped that guard, risking a shape-mismatch crash or silent corruption downstream.

Reference: substantive-critic critique for relay Task 'Deep critique of the nexus-oizh7 dim-guard
change' (2026-08-14), T1 scratch entry 03143044 (developer's self-report), review-completed marker
pending.
close_reason: Remediated per option (a) and verified by substantive-critic [22540]: count() reverted byte-for-byte to the collection-only predicate (agrees with list_collections' dim-summed total by construction; _count_or_key_error invariant and nx collection reindex existence path sound again); DECISION comment records the dim-agnostic contract with corrected precedent; renamed test pins count()==2 on the mixed-dim fixture, falsified both directions. HTTP-level cross-endpoint coverage filed separately (P3). Ships in the nexus-oizh7 commit.

title: Redesign or retire the chash-window rehearsal leg: its premise inverted when the floor crossed the RDR-180 cohort (and again at the RDR-191 unify)
description: Found while fixing nexus-azx14. rehearse_chash_window.sh's design requires CHASH_OLD_ENGINE_TAG == the floor (run.sh guard: converge_engine must no-op over the swapped-in cohort binary, else it re-downloads the floor tag over the swap and the window collapses). That premise only holds while the floor engine is PRE-cohort (TEXT chash). The floor crossed the RDR-180 cohort weeks ago (bytea from boot -> era guard aborts 'ALREADY bytea', by design), and at v0.1.75 the RDR-191 unify removed chunks_768 entirely (era guard now aborts on the table-absent arm added by azx14). There is NO env setting that reopens the window: repointing CHASH_OLD_ENGINE_TAG below the floor trips run.sh's own FATAL old-tag==floor guard. run.sh's comment block (:181-189) already prescribes the redesign direction: OLD_* moves to the last pre-cohort pair AND the swap step retires in favour of converge's real download path (i.e. stop faking the engine swap; let the product converge from the real pre-cohort tag to the real floor tag, which also exercises the sidecar/converge path honestly). Alternative: retire the leg outright like rehearse_guided.sh (exit 2 stub) if the pre-cohort population is deemed out of the support window -- the two-release deprecation-window argument that retired --guided applies here too once no supported install can still be pre-cohort. DECIDE, then implement. Until then the leg fails LOUD at the era guard (both arms), never vacuously. Related: nexus-azx14 (post-swap asserts retargeted to nexus.chunks so a redesigned leg inherits a schema-correct file), nexus-7ramw, nexus-dlhub (the analogous era-hop OLD_TAG redesign).
notes: DECISION (2026-08-14): REDESIGN, not retire. Rationale: the RDR-180 window is still live in production — 6.13.1 (the last pre-cohort release) installs upgrade through the chash-rekey rung today, and the leg's unique coverage (loud PENDING callout, open-window read/write safety, dual-width citations) is rehearsed nowhere else (critic [22534]: coverage hole total). Design per run.sh's own in-repo prescription (:181-189): OLD_* becomes the HISTORICAL PIN 6.13.1 + engine-service-v0.1.47 (verified: v6.13.1's REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION=(0,1,47)), frozen forever like ERA_RELEASE; the binary-swap stage retires in favour of converge_engine's REAL download path (sidecar at v0.1.47 < floor -> first new-client invocation downloads the published floor engine — the exact production path); Stage-6 asserts invert (binary MUST be replaced, /version MUST report the floor); a single cohort boot now walks BOTH eras (rdr180-001 text->bytea + vectors-004 unify). Scope note: the leg henceforth rehearses the client's window UX against the PUBLISHED floor engine, not the locally-built candidate (that is --shakeout's job) — recorded in engine-release SKILL.md. Acceptance gate: a real run.sh --chash-window container run must PASS end-to-end.
close_reason: Redesigned at fe2c3a4f3: historical pin 6.13.1+v0.1.47, converge real download path, cohort-boundary guard, retirement policy, honest coverage disclosure (residual gap beaded as nexus-z0ylb P2). Both reviewers clean after remediation ([22541]). LIVE acceptance: run.sh --chash-window PASSED end-to-end — the leg is green again for the first time since the floor crossed the cohort.
