title: RDR-191 Phase 5: re-count the dangling population at window open, then ADD FK + VALIDATE (reclaim SHIPPED in catalog-025 / engine-service-v0.1.73)
description:
⛔ STATUS 2026-08-12 — THE RECLAIM DECISION IS MADE AND SHIPPED. THIS BEAD IS UNBLOCKED.

Do NOT re-litigate the disposition. Hal ruled (2026-08-12): "An unresolvable
manifest row is invalid. Delete it." It is IMPLEMENTED as changeset
catalog-025-0 (service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml),
registered at db.changelog-master.xml:412, and shipped in engine-service-v0.1.73
(the only tag containing commit 498c92953). Its step-2 predicate is keyed on
(tenant_id, collection, chash) — definitionally the same set as measurement (c),
and it carries NO deleted_at filter, so it deletes BOTH the 6,464 tombstone-parent
rows AND the 37 live-parent rows. Steps 1+2 are exhaustive over the manifest;
no sub-class survives. Full predicate-level evidence chain in the 2026-08-12
diagnosis note below.

WHAT REMAINS OF THIS BEAD — one obligation only:
  * RE-COUNT the violating population immediately before the Phase 5 window, and
    then ADD the FK + VALIDATE. catalog-025 is a one-shot BACKWARD-LOOKING
    cleanup; rows created after it runs can re-violate (surviving producers ->
    GATE-2/nexus-o8dil.7, still a separate bead; and chunk-side deletion after
    the fact -> nexus-5da44, nexus-c30ew, which creates dangling rows with no
    manifest write at all).
  * Live post-deploy count is NOT verifiable from a dev box: the forensics tool
    is structurally local-only (nexus-y3wuu) and refuses in cloud mode. The two
    read-only one-liners for the credential holder are in the note below.

Everything under ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION is retained as the origin record. Its
"Ask — decide, then implement" items 1-3 are CLOSED; item 4 (re-count) is the
live one.

================================================================================
ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (2026-08-11, superseded above)
================================================================================

RDR-191's whole purpose is to make the manifest FK expressible. Measured 2026-08-11: the live cloud corpus carries dangling manifest rows, so `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` WILL FAIL when Phase 4 runs it. No existing Phase 4 bead covers this.

## The measurement

conexus relay [22273], superuser all-tenant against the managed `nexus` database:

  dangling manifest rows, chash-only anti-join      : 2,951
  dangling manifest rows, (tenant_id, chash)-scoped : 6,501
  denominator (nexus.catalog_document_chunks)       : 301,271   (0.98% / 2.16%)

Concentrated in one collection: `code__1-1__voyage-code-3__v1` = 2,942 of 2,951.

**6,501 is the operationally correct number.** The chunk PK is (tenant_id, collection, chash) and retrieval is RLS/tenant-scoped, so a manifest row in tenant `nexus` whose chash exists only under tenant `gate-xr789` does not resolve for `nexus` — it is dangling in practice even though a chash-only anti-join says otherwise. Content-addressed chash collisions across tenants are expected, not anomalous.

## Why this is a distinct bead

⛔ **The dangling count and the FK's COLUMN SET are the same question.** If the FK is keyed on chash alone, 2,951 rows violate it; if tenant-scoped, 6,501 do. Either way VALIDATE fails. Choosing the FK columns without deciding the reclaim is choosing a number of rows to trip over.

F9 measured VALIDATE at 333 ms over 280,695 manifest rows and it PASSED — on a SYNTHETIC corpus with no dangling rows. RDR-191's own F15 predicted exactly this: "Size-matching a corpus proves the TIMING of a migration; only defect-matching proves it COMPLETES." This is that prediction arriving.

## Ask — decide, then implement

1. Choose the FK column set (chash vs tenant-scoped) and record the reasoning. This decision fixes the violating-row population.
2. Choose the disposition for violating rows, explicitly:
   - REPAIR (re-point the manifest row at a chunk that does resolve for its tenant), or
   - DELETE the dangling manifest rows, or
   - defer: add the FK `NOT VALID` and never VALIDATE — which forfeits the enforcement this RDR exists to obtain, and should only be chosen deliberately and in writing.
3. Implement the chosen step in Phase 4 BEFORE the VALIDATE, inside the same transaction as the rest of the always-copy migration.
4. Re-count immediately before the window. 6,501 is a 2026-08-11 number and will drift.

## Constraints

- ALL DDL through Liquibase. Never DDL in Python.
- The migration is ALWAYS-COPY, one transaction, no CIC arm (T2 `nexus/rdr-191-DECISION-always-copy-accepted` [22271]). A reclaim step joins that transaction and rolls back with it.
- FK is `ON UPDATE CASCADE` + deferrable on the delete side, NOT `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
- No silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems. If VALIDATE fails at window time, FAIL LOUD and roll back; do not downgrade to NOT VALID automatically as a fallback.

## What this bead is NOT

Not GATE-2 (`nexus-o8dil.7`). GATE-2's criterion is "zero live PRODUCERS", and 6,501 existing rows are consistent with historical residue from producers already fixed in Phase 2. Cleaning these rows does NOT close GATE-2, and GATE-2's still-missing regression tripwire is not this bead's job. Do not let the two merge.

## Also worth a look, not in scope here

Reverse direction: 119,666 chunk rows have no manifest row at all. 116,491 are tenant `gate-xr789` (their conexus-16ei). The residual ~3,175 are tenant `nexus` chunks with no manifest reference. These do NOT violate a manifest->chunks FK (wrong direction), so they do not block VALIDATE, but nobody has explained them.

## Origin

conexus relay answer [22273]; analysis in T2 `nexus/rdr-191-relay-answer-analysis-2026-08-11` [22275].
notes:
## 2026-08-12 — MEASURED: this bead is 37 rows, not 6,501. Two orders of magnitude smaller.

conexus relay [22313], read-only against the managed substrate, with Hal's
2026-08-12 ruling on `nexus-k1uw5` (GATE-2 uses the ENGINE's live-parent definition)
applied.

  (a) dangling, LIVE parent (`d.deleted_at IS NULL`), tenant-scoped:        37
      same, chash-only (no tenant scoping):                                  1
  (b) dangling, unfiltered, tenant-scoped (the old headline figure):      6,501
  (c) THE FK's number — no chunk row at (tenant_id, collection, chash):   6,501
      split by parent state:   tombstoned parent 6,464   |   live parent 37

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. Essentially the entire 6,501 is BY-DESIGN soft-delete
residue that the engine's own `manifest_verify_all` already excludes
(catalog-020:243-246). The reclaim population that actually needs a decision is the
**37 live-parent rows**. The other 6,464 are tombstone residue whose disposition is
governed by the soft-delete contract and `purge_trash`, not by this bead.

⛔ AND THE 37 IS EXACTLY F15's 37. Two independently derived measurements of the
live-parent dangling population agree to the row — F15 was already measuring the right
thing, and it is NOT a fourth population as this thread previously assumed. That is
strong mutual corroboration for both numbers.

The 344-tombstoned x ~19-manifest-rows arithmetic that predicted ~6,536 is now
MEASURED at 6,464 tombstone-parent rows. It was a hypothesis on 2026-08-12 morning and
it is evidence now; it should be cited as measured, not as a lead.

⚠ CAVEAT, theirs and accepted: `(c) == (b) == 6,501` exactly — adding `collection` to
the join key changed nothing, because on current data every manifest row with a chunk
at `(tenant_id, chash)` also has one at `(tenant_id, collection, chash)`. That is an
EMPIRICAL property of this deployment's data, NOT an invariant. Do not generalise it
into the Phase 5 FK work; re-measure before relying on it.

### Consequence for Phase 5's VALIDATE

`VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` scans every row and does not care about `deleted_at`, so against
this deployment TODAY it would reject 6,501 rows: 6,464 tombstone residue + 37 genuine.
That is the number this bead has to answer for, and it is why `nexus-5da44` is now
wired as blocking both Phase 5 FK beads — `purge_trash`'s age-term asymmetry is what
converts tombstone residue into FK violations, so fixing it shrinks the VALIDATE
population rather than growing it.

### NOT relevant to this bead, checked and refuted

conexus hypothesised that `nexus-c30ew`'s quarantine path is a PRODUCER of these 37.
MEASURED FALSE: of the 37, ZERO have a chash among the 1,429 currently quarantined
chunks. Disjoint populations. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.

## 2026-08-12 (later) — DECISION ALREADY EXECUTED. This bead is UNBLOCKED, not decision-blocked.

Read-only diagnosis, repo evidence only (develop f7796ab09). No store writes, no nx
invocations, no service touched.

### The ruling shipped as catalog-025, and its predicate IS this bead's population

`service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml`
(changeSet `catalog-025-0`, author nexus-71gw2). Hal's ruling verbatim in the file
header: "An unresolvable manifest row is invalid. Delete it. NOT NULL with no
sentinel, no DEFAULT."

TWO DELETE arms, disjoint by construction:

* **Step 1 — NULL-collection arm** (:127-133)
      DELETE FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks WHERE collection IS NULL
  On THIS deployment this arm is a **no-op**: the 08-11 relay census measured
  arm (b) = 0 NULL-collection rows (and 0 empty-string). Nothing for it to take.

* **Step 2 — dangling arm** (:143-152), the one that matters here:
      DELETE FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks c
      WHERE c.collection IS NOT NULL
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_384  v
                         WHERE v.tenant_id=c.tenant_id AND v.collection=c.collection AND v.chash=c.chash)
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_768  v  ...same...)
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_1024 v  ...same...)

### Does it cover the 6,501? YES — it is definitionally the same set

Step 2's key is `(tenant_id, collection, chash)`. That is EXACTLY measurement (c)
in the note above — "no chunk row at (tenant_id, collection, chash): 6,501".
Same key, same three chunk tables, same anti-join. Not an approximation.

⛔ AND CRUCIALLY: **step 2 carries NO `deleted_at` predicate on the parent
document.** It filters on the manifest row only. So the 6,501 / 37 split is
irrelevant to coverage — BOTH classes are inside the predicate:

    tombstone-parent residue   6,464  -> deleted by step 2
    live-parent genuine           37  -> deleted by step 2
    -------------------------------------------------------
    total                      6,501  -> deleted by step 2

The 37 live-parent rows (F15's independently-derived 37) are NOT specially
handled and do NOT survive: a live parent does not exempt a manifest row whose
chash has no chunk at its stamped collection.

### Is there a surviving sub-class? NO — step1 ∪ step2 is exhaustive

Every manifest row is either `collection IS NULL` (step 1) or `collection IS NOT
NULL` (step 2's guard). Within step 2, a row survives iff a chunk EXISTS at
(tenant_id, collection, chash) in some dim. So after the changeset, the surviving
set is exactly "rows with a verified (tenant_id, collection, chash) chunk" — the
changeset's own header states this and it checks out: "Every surviving row is thus
a VERIFIED (tenant_id, collection, chash) match — FK-VALIDATE-able by
construction, before the FK exists."

The relay-measured populations that could have hidden a sub-class, and why none does:
* rows whose chash resolves under ANOTHER TENANT (the 3,550 that separated the
  2,951 chash-only figure from the 6,501 tenant-scoped one): step 2 pins
  `v.tenant_id = c.tenant_id`, so they are dangling to it and ARE deleted. The
  chash-only 2,951 reading has no arm anywhere in this changeset.
* rows whose collection names a real collection but the chash lives in a
  DIFFERENT dim table: step 2 checks all three (384/768/1024) — a hit in any one
  spares the row. No dim gap.
* the reverse-direction 119,666 chunks with no manifest row: untouched, and
  correctly so — wrong direction for a manifest->chunks FK.

### Shipped where

`git tag --contains` on the changeset's commit (498c92953, "fix(catalog):
caller-supplied manifest collection end to end") returns exactly ONE tag:
**engine-service-v0.1.73**. Registered in db.changelog-master.xml:412. So the
cleanup lands on cloud at the v0.1.73 deploy and on any local install at engine
convergence — nothing operator-sequenced, nothing manual (the header's
"Unfailable by construction" claim is structurally sound: the SET NOT NULL cannot
meet a residual row because step 1 just deleted them all, under an ACCESS
EXCLUSIVE lock held for the rest of the transaction).

### LIVE POST-DEPLOY COUNT — NOT verifiable read-only from this box. Marked.

Attempted and refused: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__forensics` returned its
playbook (the `claude_assisted_remediation` consent gate is OPEN), but its live
diagnostics REFUSED with: "this probe is LOCAL-ONLY by design (nexus-y3wuu) ...
This store is in service/cloud mode with nothing local to probe." It shells a
local psql at 127.0.0.1 and has no remote credential resolution — it can NEVER
read the managed tenant. No other MCP surface exposes a raw count.

TWO one-line checks for the conexus side / whoever holds managed-DB credentials
(both read-only):

1. DID IT RUN, AND WHEN (authoritative, and cheaper than recounting):
       SELECT id, author, dateexecuted, exectype, md5sum
         FROM nexus.databasechangelog WHERE id = 'catalog-025-0';
   A row with `exectype='EXECUTED'` is the deploy receipt.

2. RESIDUAL VIOLATING POPULATION (expected 0):
       SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.catalog_document_chunks c
        WHERE c.collection IS NULL
           OR (NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_384  v WHERE v.tenant_id=c.tenant_id AND v.collection=c.collection AND v.chash=c.chash)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_768  v WHERE v.tenant_id=c.tenant_id AND v.collection=c.collection AND v.chash=c.chash)
           AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chunks_1024 v WHERE v.tenant_id=c.tenant_id AND v.collection=c.collection AND v.chash=c.chash));

### DISPOSITION

This bead's three asks are all answered and none is still open:
  1. FK column set — settled at (tenant_id, collection, chash); catalog-025 has
     already normalised the data to that key.
  2. Disposition of violating rows — DELETE. Ruled by Hal, implemented, shipped.
  3. Implement before VALIDATE — done, and better than asked: it is a SEPARATE,
     EARLIER changeset, so Phase 5's transaction does not carry the reclaim at all.

Phase 5 reduces to "ADD the FK and VALIDATE" and should now succeed.

⚠ TWO THINGS THAT REMAIN TRUE AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED:

* **Ask 4 (re-count immediately before the window) STANDS, and is now the ONLY
  live obligation of this bead.** catalog-025 is a ONE-SHOT, BACKWARD-LOOKING
  cleanup — it proves nothing about rows created between its run and Phase 5's
  VALIDATE. Two known re-accumulation routes exist: any surviving producer
  (that is GATE-2 / nexus-o8dil.7's job — still do NOT merge these beads) and
  CHUNK-SIDE deletion after the fact, which converts a good manifest row into a
  dangling one without any manifest write at all (nexus-5da44's age-term
  asymmetry, nexus-c30ew's quarantine path). The re-count is not a formality.
* The `(b) == (c) == 6,501` coincidence stays an EMPIRICAL property, not an
  invariant — unchanged from the earlier note. catalog-025 keys on (c). If Phase
  5 keys the FK on anything else, the coverage argument above does not transfer.

STATUS: UNBLOCKED. Not decision-blocked. Retitle/rescope to the re-count +
FK-VALIDATE step; the reclaim decision is closed.

title: Account for the 08-03 cohort of 11,156 tombstones: collection-delete cascade vs out-of-band SQL (the 340 is SOLVED; purge-trash gate moves to nexus-5da44)
description:
Found by S5 of the 7.6.0 post-client-release shakedown, 2026-08-11 (umbrella T2 nexus/shakedown-2026-08-11-umbrella-post-7.6.0 [22251]; surface detail T2 nexus/shakedown-2026-08-11-S4-S5 [22248]).

THE DISCREPANCY. `nx catalog purge-trash` dry-run reports:
  - documents_purged (>=30d) = 0
  - documents_purged (--older-than-days 1) = 340
  - chunks_1024_stranded = 69
Against the 2026-08-03 cleanup record (T2 nexus/catalog-cleanup-2026-08-03-executed-and-prevention [21385]), which tombstoned 11,156 documents:
  - tombstone-vanished: 7,142 soft-tombstoned
  - tombstone-orphaned: 4,014 soft-tombstoned
  - post-run census: 10,535 live docs (21,691 - 11,156 tombstoned)

Those tombstones are 8 days old, so ALL 11,156 are older than 1 day. purge-trash sees 340. That is a factor-of-33 gap with no explanation.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The 08-03 record states the reclaim sequence explicitly: 'All 11,156 tombstones are soft (deleted_at) and content-intact-restorable UNTIL the first nx catalog purge-trash execute (whose chunk sweep is age-independent). purge-trash needs the NEXT engine-service tag deployed. Reclaim sequence remaining: engine tag+deploy -> purge-trash dry-run counts -> execute.'

engine-service-v0.1.71 is now DEPLOYED and cloud-verified (2026-08-11), so the prerequisite is satisfied and the sequence is UNBLOCKED FOR THE FIRST TIME. The restore window closes at the first execute, permanently, on 11,156 documents. Executing while the dry-run's population is unexplained risks either (a) reclaiming far less than intended and believing the job done, or (b) the chunk sweep — which is AGE-INDEPENDENT per the 08-03 record — acting on a population far larger than the 340 documents the dry-run named.

DO NOT EXECUTE purge-trash until this is explained. This bead is the gate.

HYPOTHESES TO TEST, none confirmed:
1. purge-trash's document arm counts a NARROWER population than the tombstone census did (different predicate, different join, or a collection/tenant scope the census did not apply).
2. Most of the 11,156 are not visible to purge-trash at all — e.g. tombstoned rows whose owning collection is one of the 5 vanished ones, or rows the RLS/tenant scope excludes.
3. Something between 08-03 and 08-11 already reclaimed or altered them. S5 found NO record of a --execute; searches of T2 for a purge execution returned nothing. Absence of a record is not proof, so verify against the substrate rather than the memory record.
4. The two numbers count different UNITS (documents vs manifest rows vs chunks) and the comparison is not like-for-like. Check this first — it is the cheapest and would dissolve the finding.

METHOD NOTE. The clean way to settle this is a substrate-direct count of rows with deleted_at set, compared against purge-trash's dry-run population. That count is currently UNAVAILABLE: no psql on the cloud-managed box (the standing S4/S5/S11 anchor gap). The sanctioned path is the forensics tool, which is consent-gated behind claude_assisted_remediation.enabled and correctly refused during the shakedown. So this bead may be BLOCKED on that opt-in — surface that to Hal rather than working around it.

RELATED: the 08-03 record's prevention doctrine names the pollution classes that created the 11,156 (worktree/temp indexing being 4,002 of them). This bead is about reclaiming safely, not about those guards.
notes:
## 2026-08-11 — NOT DISSOLVED. The explanation CHANGED SHAPE and the new shape is worse.

conexus relay ANSWER [22273] concluded UNIT MISMATCH, tombstones intact, nothing
ate them. They also flagged honestly that they could not see what our 08-03
census counted, and asked us to confirm. We can: T2 [21385] is on our side.
Having read it, their conclusion DOES NOT HOLD.

Full analysis: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-relay-answer-analysis-2026-08-11` [22275].

### What they measured (accepted, not disputed)

  catalog_documents: 344 tombstoned | 19,852 live | 20,196 total
  tenant `nexus`: 340 tombstoned — EXACTLY purge-trash's dry-run number, so
  purge-trash reads the substrate correctly and is NOT scoping narrowly.
  0 orphaned manifest rows. Reclaim prize = 69 chunks.

  TOMBSTONE AGE DISTRIBUTION:
    2026-07-05: 4 | 08-06: 279 | 08-07: 51 | 08-08: 1 | 08-09: 1 | 08-10: 8
    **2026-08-03: ZERO.**

### Why unit-mismatch fails — three verified points

1. VERIFIED: [21385] writes "POST-RUN CENSUS: 10,535 live docs (21,691 - 11,156
   tombstoned)". The parenthetical IS the arithmetic — the live count was
   COMPUTED, never measured. So comparisons against 10,535 compare against a
   derived number. (This half of their instinct was sound.)

2. ⛔ VERIFIED, AND IT KILLS THE STORY: their main pillar is that measured 7,089
   manifest-rows-for-tombstoned-docs ≈ our 7,142 "tombstone-vanished" (0.74%
   apart, very persuasive). But [21385] describes those 7,142 as
   "EMPTY-MANIFEST docs in the 29 dead collections". Empty-manifest docs have by
   definition ~ZERO manifest rows and therefore CANNOT be the source of 7,089
   manifest rows. The match is a COINCIDENCE.

3. ⛔ THE DATE. A unit mismatch changes what a number COUNTS. It cannot move
   11,156 soft tombstones off the date they were written. Today's 340 are dated
   08-06..08-10 — a LATER cohort entirely, not the 08-03 work.

4. Their negative evidence is weaker than presented: "0 orphaned manifest rows,
   so nobody purged" does not hold, because a CORRECT purge removes manifest
   rows too and leaves zero orphans BY CONSTRUCTION. Zero orphans is CONSISTENT
   with a clean purge, not evidence against one.

### WHERE IT NOW STANDS

The 08-03 cohort of 11,156 is UNACCOUNTED FOR: absent from the tombstone set
(nothing dated 08-03) and not bulk hard-removed (total fell only ~1,499).

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT PROVEN: RESTORATION — deleted_at cleared, rows returned
to live. A restore path demonstrably exists: `gc_restore_rereferenced`, named in
our own nexus-uyl70. If true, an automated GC path silently undid an
operator-approved, Hal-approved cleanup with no record. That is materially more
serious than a miscount.

CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE, ELIMINATE FIRST: [21385]'s counts were simply wrong at the
time, i.e. the 08-03 run did not tombstone what it reported.

### ⚠ ARITHMETIC TRAP — do not reuse

"9,317 restored + 1,499 removed + 340 tombstoned = 11,156, an exact fit" is an
ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY, true by construction, distinguishing NO hypothesis. I nearly
reported it as corroboration. It is not evidence.

### ⛔ THE GATE HOLDS. purge-trash still does NOT execute.

Not for the original reason (that number IS now explained as documents), but
because the explanation moved to a worse place. The prize is 69 chunks — trivial
against permanently closing a restore window on a population we cannot account
for.

### NEXT STEP (relay-back drafted)

One targeted question distinguishes restore-from-never-happened: does anything
in the audit/event trail show deleted_at transitioning NOT NULL -> NULL in bulk
between 08-03 and 08-11? Our side should also re-read the 08-03 run's actual
implementation to establish what it counted and whether it persisted.
## 2026-08-12 — THE 340 IS FULLY EXPLAINED AND EXACT. The leading hypothesis is REFUTED. The gate's REASON changes.

Read-only diagnosis, repo code + already-measured numbers. No store writes, no nx
invocations, no service touched, no reclaim executed.

================================================================================
## PART 1 — 340 vs 11,156: the 340 half is now arithmetic, not a mystery
================================================================================

### The dry-run's number is produced by exactly this, and nothing else

`CatalogRepository.agedTombstoneCount` (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/
db/CatalogRepository.java:2303-2318), called by `purgeTrashPreview` (:2326-2336):

    SELECT count(*) FROM catalog_documents
     WHERE tenant_id = :tenant AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL
       AND deleted_at <= now() - :interval

Tenant-scoped by `tenantScope.withTenant`. Mirrors `nexus.purge_trash`'s own
Step 4 WHERE, same clock, same interval units (nexus-ff85q pinned this).

### ⛔ THE ARITHMETIC NOBODY IN THIS THREAD DID — it closes exactly

Relay 08-11 measured: 344 tombstoned ALL-TENANT, of which tenant `nexus` = 340.
Relay 08-11 age distribution (which is the ALL-TENANT 344, not the 340):

    2026-07-05: 4 | 08-06: 279 | 08-07: 51 | 08-08: 1 | 08-09: 1 | 08-10: 8
    sum = 344  ✔ (all-tenant total)
    sum EXCLUDING the 07-05 cohort = 279+51+1+1+8 = **340**  ✔ (tenant nexus)

So the 4 rows dated 2026-07-05 are precisely the 344 − 340 = 4 non-`nexus`-tenant
rows, and **tenant `nexus`'s OLDEST tombstone is 2026-08-06**. That forces BOTH
dry-run readings on 08-11, with no defect anywhere:

    --older-than-days 30  ->  0    (nexus's oldest tombstone is 5 days old)
    --older-than-days 1   ->  340  (all 340 are >= 1 day old)

The "0 at 30d" reading — which looked like a second anomaly, and which would have
been a REAL defect if the 07-05 rows were nexus's — is explained by the same
tenant split. purge-trash's document arm is correct, correctly scoped, and
correctly aged. It is NOT under-counting. Hypotheses 1 and 2 in the description
are both REFUTED.

### And the 11,156 is a DIFFERENT COHORT, not a miscount of this one

Confirmed as the earlier note said: today's 340 are dated 08-06..08-10, a later
cohort entirely. The 08-03 population is simply not in the tombstone set.

================================================================================
## PART 2 — the 08-03 writes WERE real. That arm is closed.
================================================================================

The "cheapest alternative — [21385]'s counts were simply wrong at the time"
(named in the description as the thing to eliminate FIRST) is now ELIMINATED, by
reading the path that produced those counts:

`reconcile_stale.py:600` — `n_deleted = len(writer.delete_many(tumblers))`
  -> `HttpCatalogClient.delete_many` (http_catalog_client.py:1466-1499) returns
     `result["deleted"]`, the ENGINE's list, never an echo of the request
  -> `CatalogRepository.deleteDocumentsMany` (:2209-2220):

        UPDATE catalog_documents SET deleted_at = now()
         WHERE tumbler IN (...) AND tenant_id = ... AND deleted_at IS NULL
        RETURNING tumbler

`RETURNING` over the UPDATE means the reported 7,142 / 4,014 are counts of rows
the database ACTUALLY STAMPED in a committed transaction — not candidates, not
requests, not a client-side tally. The 08-03 record's numbers are trustworthy.

================================================================================
## PART 3 — SUBSTRATE MISMATCH: tested and REFUTED
================================================================================

The one hypothesis this thread had never raised, and the most likely-looking
given `project_system_of_record_ambiguity_postmortem` (root cause 3: the client
silently falls back to the LOCAL service lease): did the 08-03 dev-tree CLI write
to a LOCAL PG instead of the managed cloud tenant?

MEASURED, read-only, filesystem stat only (nothing started, nothing invoked):

    /Users/hal.hildebrand/.config/nexus/postgres/   <- the local bundle cluster
      global/pg_control                 last written  2026-07-02 22:05
      pg_wal/0000000100000001000000E1   last written  2026-07-02 22:05
      pg.log                            last written  2026-07-02 22:05
      postmaster.pid                    ABSENT (cluster not running)

The local cluster has been COLD SINCE 2026-07-02 — five weeks before the 08-03
run. It cannot have received those writes. The 08-03 tombstones went to the
managed cloud tenant `nexus`, which is the same substrate the 08-11 census read.
Substrate mismatch is OUT.

================================================================================
## PART 4 — "SILENT MASS RESTORE" — REFUTED ON FOUR INDEPENDENT GROUNDS
================================================================================

The description's LEADING HYPOTHESIS ("an automated GC path silently restored an
operator-approved cleanup, via `gc_restore_rereferenced`") does not survive
reading the code.

**(1) `gc_restore_rereferenced` CANNOT restore a document.** catalog-023-
quarantine-functions.xml:306-434. Its entire body moves rows between
`chunks_<dim>` collections (quarantine -> origin): SELECT chashes, INSERT into
the origin collection, DELETE from quarantine. It never references
`catalog_documents` and never touches `deleted_at`. It is a CHUNK mover. The
named suspect is innocent.

**(2) EXHAUSTIVE SWEEP: exactly TWO sites in the entire product clear
`deleted_at`.** (grep across all of service/src/main/java and every changelog)

  a. `nexus.document_restore(tumbler)` — catalog-003-soft-delete.xml:158-170.
     Single-tumbler. SECURITY INVOKER. **It has NO HTTP route** (CatalogHandler's
     route table carries /delete, /delete_many, /purge-trash, /collections/delete
     — no restore case) **and NO caller anywhere in src/nexus**. It is
     unreachable from the product; only direct SQL can invoke it.
  b. `CatalogRepository.upsertDocument`'s ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE arm — :793,
     `.set(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS.DELETED_AT, (OffsetDateTime) null)`, deliberately
     unconditional (nexus-mqd6t, "the ONE sanctioned resurrection").

**(3) Path (b) cannot fire at scale by accident.** It requires a register
addressed at an EXISTING `(tenant_id, tumbler)`. But every identity lookup that
could resolve a tombstoned row to its tumbler filters it out:
`findBySourceUri` :2907, `findByFilePath` :2890 — both `.and(DELETED_AT.isNull())`
— and the uniqueness backstop `ux_catalog_documents_live_source_uri` (catalog-016
:153-156) is partial `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND source_uri <> ''`, so a
tombstoned row's source_uri is not even in the live index. Consequently a
re-index of previously-tombstoned content MINTS A NEW TUMBLER
(`register_many` "claims the whole contiguous tumbler block",
http_catalog_client.py:1331) rather than resurrecting. Re-indexing GROWS the
document count and leaves tombstones standing — the opposite of what was
observed.

**(4) No migration did it either.** No changeset anywhere clears `deleted_at`
(the only three `deleted_at` writes in the whole changelog tree are
catalog-003:140 `= NOW()`, catalog-016:114 `= NOW()`, catalog-003:165 `= NULL`
inside document_restore). And of the changesets that landed 08-03..08-11
(catalog-022/023/024, fk-001, grants-nexus-svc, rdr180-021, staging-002,
taxonomy-006), none touches it.

CONCLUSION: there is **no reachable bulk-restore mechanism in this product**. A
mass un-tombstoning could only have come from direct SQL against the managed
database, outside the product. That is a materially different (and much less
alarming) proposition than "an automated GC path silently undid the cleanup".

================================================================================
## PART 5 — ⛔ THE INFERENCE THAT RULED OUT HARD-REMOVAL IS UNSOUND
================================================================================

Both the relay analysis and this bead's notes rest on:

  "total documents fell by only ~1,499, so [the 11,156] was not bulk
   hard-removed."

**That inference silently assumes ZERO documents were added between 08-03 and
08-11.** On this box that assumption is false — the window covers 7.3.0 and
7.4.0, several engine tags, shakedowns, and routine indexing. The total is a NET:

    total_08-11  =  total_08-03  −  hard_deleted  +  newly_indexed

−1,499 net is entirely consistent with, say, ~7,100 hard-deleted and ~5,600
newly indexed. The observed net constrains NOTHING about the gross hard-delete
count until the additions are known.

And a hard-delete path is not hypothetical, it is routine and squarely aimed at
this population: **`/collections/delete` -> `CatalogRepository.deleteCollection`
(:5986) / `deleteCollectionTxn` (:5996)**, a hard, cascading transaction
(fk-001 gives catalog_documents ON DELETE CASCADE to manifest, aspects,
highlights, queue). The 08-03 cohort was 7,142 "empty-manifest docs in the 29
DEAD collections" — deleting those 29 dead collections is the obvious,
well-motivated follow-up action, and it would remove those documents from the
tombstone count AND the total in one stroke, leaving no restore and no anomaly.

So the disjunction is now: **collection-delete cascade (benign, in-product,
expected) vs. out-of-band direct SQL (not benign).** Hard-removal is back as the
LEADING candidate, and the reasoning that had excluded it does not hold.

================================================================================
## PART 6 — TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN METHOD NOTE
================================================================================

**(A) This bead is NOT blocked on the `claude_assisted_remediation` opt-in.**
The description says the forensics tool "correctly refused" behind the consent
gate and "this bead may be BLOCKED on that opt-in". Tested today: the consent
gate is **OPEN** — `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__forensics` returned its full
playbook. It still cannot help, for a STRUCTURAL reason: "this probe is
LOCAL-ONLY by design (nexus-y3wuu) ... This store is in service/cloud mode with
nothing local to probe." It shells a local psql at 127.0.0.1 and has no remote
credential resolution. **Opting in would have changed nothing.** Chasing that
opt-in is a dead end; remove it as the unblock path.

**(B) `gc_audit` is NOT an evidence trail — it has no writers.**
catalog-018-gc-audit.xml built the table explicitly to answer "what did the GC
take on the 21st", with routes POST /v1/catalog/gc_audit/record and GET
/gc_audit/list. But a grep of all of `src/` finds **zero callers** of either
route — `gc_audit` appears in src/nexus only in health.py's table list and an
engine_version.py comment. The audit surface exists and nothing writes to it. So
gc_audit cannot corroborate or refute anything about 08-03, and it will not

================================================================================
## WHERE THIS LEAVES THE GATE
================================================================================

The original stated reason for the gate is GONE: the 340 is explained exactly,
purge-trash reads the substrate correctly, and the "silent mass restore" that
made the explanation "worse" is refuted. What is left is a bounded question about
where 11,156 documents went, whose leading answer is now a benign in-product
hard-delete.

⚠ BUT THE GATE SHOULD STILL HOLD, for a reason that is now BETTER SPECIFIED and
is NOT this bead: **nexus-5da44** (linked). `nexus.purge_trash`'s chunk sweep
(catalog-003 Steps 1-3) has NO age term while the document delete (Step 4) does.
Verified in the SQL. So the first `--no-dry-run --confirm` strips chunks from
EVERY currently-tombstoned document regardless of age — all 340, including the
ones tombstoned yesterday — while only the aged rows disappear. The prize is 69

RECOMMENDATION: **do not close as unexplained-and-scary; re-scope.** The
arithmetic half is SOLVED. Demote from P1 to P2, retitle to the residual
question ("account for the 08-03 cohort of 11,156: collection-delete cascade vs
out-of-band SQL"), and move the purge-trash execution gate to nexus-5da44 where
it structurally belongs.

### THE SINGLE NEXT ACTION (read-only, one query, settles Part 5)

Whoever holds managed-DB credentials (the conexus side — NOT runnable from this
box, and NOT via the forensics tool):

    SELECT date_trunc('day', indexed_at) AS d, count(*)
      FROM nexus.catalog_documents
     WHERE tenant_id = 'nexus' AND indexed_at >= '2026-08-03'
     GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

If that shows several thousand documents indexed in the 08-03..08-11 window, the
−1,499 net is explained by additions, hard-removal is confirmed as the mechanism,
and this bead resolves benignly. If it shows only a few hundred, additions cannot
absorb the difference and the out-of-band-SQL branch needs a real answer.
(Supporting: `SELECT count(*) FROM nexus.catalog_collections` vs the 29 dead
collections named in T2 [21385] — if they are gone, the cascade happened.)

title: RDR-191: HttpVectorClient discards server delete-count, so callers silently over-report success post-anti-join
description:
`HttpVectorClient`'s two delete surfaces discard the server's actual `{"deleted": N}` response, so no Python caller can observe how many chunks a delete actually removed — only how many it requested. `nexus-o8dil.5` (RDR-191 P2, F10c) makes this a live correctness gap: it anti-join-scopes `PgVectorRepository.delete` so the server can now legitimately delete FEWER than `ids.size()` (a chunk another live document still references is correctly retained instead of destroyed). Pre-fix, "requested == deleted" was always true, so the discard was harmless. Post-fix, partial-skip is an EXPECTED, non-error outcome the client has zero visibility into.

Violates this project's standing "no silent fallback for data-correctness problems — FAIL LOUD" directive: several callers now silently OVER-REPORT success on a request the server partially or fully refused.

## Verified discard sites
- `_ServiceCollectionStub.delete()` (`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1295-1309`) — posts to `/v1/vectors/store-delete`, never captures the response, method signature is `-> None`.
- `HttpVectorClient.batch_delete()` (`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:2577-2595`) — same pattern, batches the POST, never captures the response, `-> None`.
- Contrast: `HttpVectorClient.delete_by_id()` (`http_vector_client.py:2042-2052`) does NOT have this gap — it already captures `result.get("deleted", 0) > 0` and returns a bool. Any fix should generalize that pattern, not invent a new one.

## Verified over-reporting call sites (file:line, confirmed by reading the code, not assumed from the critic's write-up)
- `_batched_delete` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2492-2499`): calls `_vector_with_retry(col.delete, ids=batch)` and discards the result, then unconditionally does `deleted += len(batch)`.
- `_prune_misclassified_in_collection`, both arms (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2635` and `:2681`): each calls `_batched_delete(col, present_ids)` / `_batched_delete(col, existing["ids"])` and then does `pruned += len(present_ids)` / `pruned += len(existing["ids"])` — the REQUESTED/candidate size, not the actual deleted count. This is F8c's live producer arm: post-`.5`-fix, the anti-join can now legitimately refuse part of a misclassified-prune batch (chunk still referenced by the old-collection manifest), and this function will report success for chunks it never touched.
- `_force_t3_orphan_cleanup` (`src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:702-747`): calls `col.delete(orphan_ids)` at line 740, discards the result, then `return len(orphan_ids)` unconditionally at line 747 — directly contradicting its own docstring, which states "Fail-loud by design (no `except Exception` swallow)... Returns the number of orphan chunks deleted."
- `nx store delete --title` (`src/nexus/commands/store.py:484-486`): calls `db.batch_delete(col_name, ids)`, discards the result, then unconditionally prints `f"Deleted {len(ids)} ... entries"` — an operator-facing message that can now be wrong.

## Why this is a bead, not just cleanup
The anti-join in `.5` converted a silent DATA-LOSS bug into a silent OVER-REPORTING bug. That is strictly better (no data destroyed) but it is still a FAIL LOUD violation: every one of GATE-2's "zero live producers of dangling state" callers now has a blind spot exactly where the new safety mechanism can fire. `_force_t3_orphan_cleanup`'s docstring claim is actively false today. Nobody auditing GATE-2 or troubleshooting a `--force` deadlock or a misclassified-prune run can currently tell "did this actually clean up N items" from "the server silently protected N items and told nobody."

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive — the assignee should confirm the right contract)
1. Change `_ServiceCollectionStub.delete()` and `HttpVectorClient.batch_delete()` to capture and return the server's actual `deleted` count (`int`), mirroring `delete_by_id`'s existing pattern.
2. Update the four call sites above to use the actual count instead of the requested/candidate size.
3. Decide, per call site, whether `actual < requested` should just be reported accurately (safe for most) or should additionally WARN/raise for arms where a partial skip signals something callers need to know about (e.g. `_force_t3_orphan_cleanup`'s "Fail-loud by design" contract, and the misclassified-prune arm, which already has its own bead `nexus-o8dil.2` for the F8c manifest-completeness question — this bead is about visibility of the count, not about adding manifest actions; don't conflate the two).
4. Test coverage: at least one test per changed call site asserting the reported count matches the actual server-side deleted count when the anti-join partially blocks a batch.

## Context
- RDR: `docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md`
- Origin: substantive-critic pass on `nexus-o8dil.5`, T2 `nexus/rdr-191-o8dil5-substantive-critique-2026-08-11` (critical #3/#4)
- Sibling: `nexus-o8dil.2` (F8c, manifest-completeness for the misclassified-prune arms — separate concern, do not merge scope)
- Sibling: `nexus-o8dil.39` (GATE-2 caller census, corrected count)

## Standing constraint
No silent fallback for data-correctness problems — FAIL LOUD (project directive). This bead exists because that directive is currently violated at every listed call site.

title: [epic] Harden the e2e/release/CI gate suite against success-shaped emptiness (vacuous gates)
description:
A gate that reports PASS/GREEN despite having exercised zero relevant work. Named as a class in T2 nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10; the project's costliest recent incident shape (2026-08-09, five instances in one day: a gate scanning nothing, an assertion proving a false property, a rung verifying on silence, 11 fail-open-to-green surfaces, and a test suite passing because it exited early).

Created 2026-08-11 out of the P2 backlog triage. The five instances below were each filed separately and each was being fixed one at a time, with nothing tracking the CLASS — which is precisely why it kept recurring. This epic exists so the class has an owner.

CHILDREN: nexus-i1oh4, nexus-poplq, nexus-epj0b, nexus-jndz0, nexus-idtjs. Each fixes one concrete vacuous instrument.

EXIT CRITERION — deliberately stronger than 'all children closed': every child closed AND a durable tripwire/lint exists such that a NEW instance of the class surfaces WITHOUT anyone needing to file a NEW bead. Done when the class cannot recur silently, not when the five named instances are patched. An epic that closes on its children alone would reproduce the exact failure that created it.

Method note for whoever picks this up: MEASURE the detector against a deliberately broken fix before believing it works (the 2026-08-09 ceiling detector had a 1-in-12 false-pass rate until it was measured that way). And ask of each gate: 'what does this print when it genuinely passes, and can I tell that from what it prints when it exercises nothing?'

title: RDR-191: amend the RDR to record two deliberate plan deviations (5(b) placement, the late-upgrader boot-brick)
description:
**PLAN-AUDIT FINDING (Q4/Q5b) [MEDIUM]: record two deliberate deviations from the accepted RDR, or the phase-review gate will score them as SILENT SCOPE REDUCTION.**

The plan audit confirmed both deviations are CORRECT and, on one of them, better than the RDR. What is missing is bookkeeping, and this project gates on exactly that.

## Deviation 1: Decision item 5(b) sits in Phase 4, not Phase 2
The RDR assigns the rekey-rung retarget to Phase 2 while also requiring it in the SAME engine release as the DDL (Phase 4). It cannot be tested before `nexus.chunks` exists, and **shipping the retarget early strands boxes in the MIRROR direction of F14a**, the rung would target a table that does not yet exist. It is bead `.15`, wired to `.12`/`.14` and explicitly named in GATE-4's acceptance. The audit calls this better than the RDR's own Phasing.

## Deviation 2: the second boot-brick (bead `.23`) is not in the RDR at all
A deployment upgrading AFTER this release boots, Liquibase reaches VALIDATE, hits its own dangling population, `MigrationException`, exit 1.

**A PROPOSED RESOLUTION WAS CHECKED AND FOUND WRONG. RECORD THE OPEN QUESTION, NOT THE INFERENCE.** A plan-audit pass asserted that `fk-002-6-reconcile` already supplies the missing mechanism, and that `.23` therefore collapses to "follow the house pattern". Reading `fk-002-validate.xml` directly REFUTES that. `fk-002-6-reconcile` is an ADDITIVE PARENT-STUB `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` into `nexus.catalog_collections`, reconciling the COLLECTION-REGISTRY direction. Its destructive arm is DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and the changelog says it must STAY absent on this very table family: *"fk-002 tables (chunks_*, chash_index, topic_assignments) are the PRIMARY vector-serving layer, where an orphan chunk is real data, not lifecycle debris, deleting it would be data loss."* A stub-unsatisfiable orphan *"by design makes VALIDATE FAIL LOUD rather than admit bad data."* For RDR-191's manifest FK the missing object is the CHUNK, which carries chunk_text and an embedding and therefore cannot be stub-registered without FABRICATING data. The one arm that would clear the F15 population is the destructive arm, which this precedent explicitly refuses. **`.23` REMAINS A LIVE, OPEN DECISION**, and fk-002 is now evidence AGAINST its disposition (a).

## Acceptance
- [ ] RDR-191 amended: Decision item 5(b)'s phase placement corrected, with the mirror-direction-of-F14a reasoning.
- [ ] RDR-191 amended: the late-upgrader boot-brick added as a finding, recorded as an **OPEN QUESTION with its evidence**, never as a resolved one. State what was MEASURED (the F15 population; the unconditional Liquibase boot path) and what remains UNDECIDED (where VALIDATE runs). **Do NOT write `fk-002-6-reconcile` into the RDR as the answer.**
- [ ] The amendment distinguishes VERIFIED facts from INFERENCES in its own wording. Writing an inference into the permanent record as fact is a top-severity error, and an RDR is exactly that record.
- [ ] Both amendments made to the RDR FILE. Never delete an RDR; amend in place and note the date.
- [ ] `/conexus:phase-review-gate` at the Phase 2 boundary cross-walks cleanly against the amended text.
- [ ] Bead `.23` updated: its pass-1 "house pattern resolves this" note is RETRACTED, and the decision stays OPEN.

## Context
- RDR: `docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md` (accepted 2026-08-10, gate PASSED run 5). Read the named findings IN FULL; every phase has load-bearing detail.
- Verified code anchors: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-code-anchors-verified-2026-08-10` (verified file:line sheet; RDR line numbers have drifted in 5 places)
- Plan: T2 `nexus/plan-rdr-191-phases-2-7`
- Retrieval: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_search(query="RDR-191", project="nexus")`; `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__nx_answer(question=..., scope="code")`

## Standing constraints (non-negotiable)
- ALL DDL through Liquibase. NEVER DDL in Python. NEVER a new SQLite table.
- Key on the NATURAL id (`chunks_<dim>.chash`), never a metadata copy of it.
- THREE FULL HNSW indexes, never partial (F13, measured: partial buys 0.11% and costs a silent ~250x seq-scan).
- FK is `ON UPDATE CASCADE` + deferrable on the delete side. NOT `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
- TDD: test file before implementation. Code must compile including tests.
- Do NOT touch the write-side chunk caps (16 / 64 / 300), measured, not residue.

## Execution reminders
- Use `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` for the analysis phase.
- SPAWN parallel sub-agents to conserve orchestrator context; sub-agents may spawn their own children for intensive work.
- Update continuation state after each milestone: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_put(project="nexus", title="rdr-191-continuation-state")`.
- STACKED REVIEW is mandatory at the phase boundary: `code-review-expert` AND `substantive-critic`. Both run. A clean code review does not permit skipping the critic.
notes:
## 2026-08-11 — nexus-o8dil.9 adds THREE more amendment items (was: two deviations)

Derivation in T2 `nexus/rdr-191-cloud-measurements` Part 2. This bead's scope grows from the original two deviations to five items total. Items (i) and (ii) are FALSIFIED CLAIMS IN AN ACCEPTED RDR, not deviations from it — they are stronger than the original scope.

### (i) F9's "copy the split from chash_rekey.py" describes code that does not exist

RDR :1017-1023 says "chash_rekey.py already implements exactly this local/managed split and should be copied, not redesigned."

VERIFIED FALSE by a full read of `src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/rungs/chash_rekey.py` (761 lines):
- NO `CREATE INDEX` of any form in the rung; `CONCURRENTLY` appears NOWHERE in the Python tree (the only CIC strings in the repo are changelog comments REJECTING it).
- Its split is an APPLICABILITY split (`_locally_actionable`, :701-728 — "can I read pg_credentials"), NOT a DDL-form split.
- Neither arm opens a transaction. There is no rollback routine at all.

Taken at face value, Phase 3 would have budgeted zero for an arm that does not exist. Amend to say the CIC arm would have to be invented, and then (per item ii) that it should not be.

### (ii) F9's "CIC for cloud, in-transaction for local" is SUPERSEDED

F9's CIC recommendation was premised on cloud needing large NON-BLOCKING index builds. Under adopt-in-place there is no large build: a table rename carries its five indexes and PK without rebuild. With no large build, CIC's costs are all downside — it cannot run in a transaction, forfeits the free atomic rollback F9 itself verified, and can strand an INVALID index on failure.

Recommended replacement: ONE transaction on BOTH modes, no CIC arm. This also removes the `runInTransaction="false"` problem — that attribute has ZERO precedent in the changelog tree and is explicitly argued against in three files (vectors-002:18-24, vectors-003:18-28, staging-002:37).

### (iii) Decision item 2 assumes non-trivially-populated shards

"Move only the smaller two dims' rows" presupposes those dims hold meaningful data. Measured cloud: chunks_768 = 0 rows, chunks_384 = 1 row. The RDR nowhere considers a one-shard-holds-~100% distribution.

⛔ Amend CAREFULLY — the degenerate distribution is a CLOUD fact only. Local mode embeds with bge-768 (`src/nexus/health.py:405`), so local corpora live in chunks_768. The amendment must NOT license hardcoding chunks_1024 as the adoption target; that would brick every local box. Correct shape: adopt whichever shard holds the most rows, decided at RUNTIME.

### (iv) F14b does NOT evaporate under the degenerate distribution

Guard against the tempting misreading. chunks_384 holds ONE row, not zero, and a CHECK constraint is evaluated PER ROW — one row violates the inherited NOT VALID octet CHECK exactly as thoroughly as 267,000 do. F14b is about SCHEMA MECHANICS (drop / move / re-add NOT VALID under the canonical name), not volume. Its mandate survives intact; it merely stops being expensive. The amendment should state this explicitly so "the corpus is degenerate" cannot later be read as "the boot-brick is gone".

### (v) The delete funnel is ELEVEN callers, the RDR says NINE

F8b :1052 says "the funnel for NINE distinct Python calling functions", with a 6+2+1 disposition breakdown that also sums to 9. The word "eleven" does not appear in the file. Corrected count established by the nexus-o8dil.39 caller census.

### Related beads created by the same derivation
- nexus-4rbud (P1) — distribution test matrix; neither deployment exercises both migration paths.
- nexus-vk57q (P2) — chash_rekey's two divergent mode predicates.

### Gate
Items (i) and (ii) are pending a substantive-critic pass on the Part 2 derivation. Do NOT amend the RDR on their strength until that review returns and its prescriptions are verified — an earlier bead in this arc was filed from an unverified critic Critical whose load-bearing premises were false.
### (vi) + (vii) — TWO HAL CORRECTIONS, 2026-08-11

Full record: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-freeze-window-scope-correction` [22266]. READ IT
before drafting the amendment; it supersedes parts of the Part 2 derivation.

(vi) ALL THREE VECTOR LENGTHS ARE REQUIRED CAPABILITY. The measured cloud
distribution is a dated snapshot, not a design input. The amendment must record
it as provenance-dated OBSERVATION and must explicitly license NO schema
simplification: all three embedding columns and all three FULL HNSW indexes are
created unconditionally. Adopt-in-place optimizes DATA MOVEMENT ONLY, never
SCHEMA. The copy path is first-class on every deployment mode, not local-only.

(vii) HAL IS THE SOLE USER OF THE CLOUD DEPLOYMENT. The freeze window is a
correctness concern, not a coordination one. Do NOT write a maintenance-window
protocol, comms step, or scheduling negotiation into the amendment — that is
process for an audience of one. The decision to run remains Hal's; the ceremony
around scheduling it does not exist. Correctness items (schema completeness,
atomic rollback, F14b's boot-brick, INVALID-index hazards) keep full weight.
### (viii) SHAPE CHANGED — ALWAYS-COPY. The RDR's Phase 4 text is now WRONG.

Hal ruled 2026-08-11: "always-copy it is, go with that". Decision of record:
T2 `nexus/rdr-191-DECISION-always-copy-accepted` [22271].

THIS IS THE LARGEST AMENDMENT ITEM. Two places in the RDR state the retired
shape as fact and must be corrected, not merely annotated:

  - Phase 4, :528-529 — "Phase 4 - nexus.chunks + migration (adopt-in-place,
    inherited CHECK drop/re-add, constraint-name canonicalisation)". The
    parenthetical names adopt-in-place explicitly. WRONG.
  - Decision item 2 — "move only the smaller two dims' rows". Superseded:
    always-copy moves ALL dims' rows into a fresh nexus.chunks.

Also correct F9's conclusion (:1017-1023) per items (i) and (ii) above: the
chash_rekey "copy the split" claim describes code that does not exist, and
"CIC for cloud" is retired. Under always-copy there is no CIC arm at all, so
the local/managed DDL-form split the RDR describes simply does not exist in
the implementation.

WHAT THE AMENDMENT MUST NOT DO:
  - do NOT present always-copy as a cost optimisation. It is a SIMPLICITY and
    DETERMINISM choice, accepted at a cost of single-digit minutes;
  - do NOT drop the record of WHY adopt-in-place was retired. The fresh-install
    three-way-tie-at-zero-rows failure (three empty dim tables; RDR :777 fresh
    installs replay history in order) is the forcing reason and is exactly the
    kind of thing a future reader would otherwise re-propose;
  - do NOT license any schema simplification (item vi still binds: all three
    embedding columns, all three FULL HNSW indexes, unconditional).

ADD to the RDR as a new risk, not previously recorded anywhere in it:
  TRANSIENT DISK HEADROOM. Always-copy materialises a second copy before
  dropping the source — ~6.3 GB peak additional against a 6953 MB database.
  This is the one axis where the retired shape was better. UNMEASURED; gated
  as C5 on nexus-o8dil.10.

title: RDR-191 P4: F14c, where SchemaMigrator.preflightChashConstraints goes silently VACUOUS and needs a non-vacuity test
description:
**PLAN-AUDIT FINDING A5 [MEDIUM]: F14c has no owner. A vacuous preflight is worse than a missing one.**

## F14c, verbatim

`MATCH FULL` is *"the wrong instrument entirely."* Exactly ONE of the three FK columns (`collection`) is nullable, so every key is all-non-NULL or exactly-one-NULL, and **`MATCH FULL` differs from `MATCH SIMPLE` on 100% of the NULL-collection population, it rejects every row.** Measured: under `MATCH FULL`, VALIDATE fails AND a new NULL-collection INSERT is REJECTED **while the constraint is still `NOT VALID`**, no grace window, so the NOT VALID -> VALIDATE choreography does not apply at all.

title: RDR-191 P5: add the FK on LOCAL, with ON UPDATE CASCADE + deferrable delete side, NOT VALID then VALIDATE
description:
Add the FK on LOCAL: `catalog_document_chunks (tenant_id, collection, chash) -> nexus.chunks`, `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`.

## The constraint shape: each clause has a measured reason
- **`ON UPDATE CASCADE` is MANDATORY (F10a), not optional.** `chunks` is the PARENT, so collection rename (`UPDATE chunks SET collection = ...`) and the RDR-180 rekey (`UPDATE chunks SET chash = ...`) are PARENT-KEY UPDATES. Both are REJECTED while manifest rows reference them, under RESTRICT, under NO ACTION, and they survive `INITIALLY DEFERRED` only incidentally. `fk-002-5` already uses `ON UPDATE CASCADE` on `topic_assignments` for exactly this reason, house pattern, not a novel choice.
- **NOT `ON DELETE RESTRICT`** (Open Question 5, answered by F8a). THREE different orderings coexist for the same invariant: `deleteCollectionTxn` and `purge_trash` delete chunks BEFORE the manifest within one transaction (documented as deliberate); `RekeyOps` step-3 deletes manifest first; the `sweepChunks*` family splits the two across transaction BOUNDARIES. RESTRICT is immediate and undeferrable, so it would fail the first group outright.
- **F10b: RESTRICT and NO ACTION are behaviourally IDENTICAL** on every deletion case; `SET CONSTRAINTS` reports both as "not deferrable". **The axis was always DEFERRABILITY, not the action keyword.**
- **Pick one and record why:** `INITIALLY DEFERRED` (simple) vs `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE` + explicit `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED` at the two class-B sites. Both correct. The second preserves statement-local error locality elsewhere, *including on the combined-write hot path, where `INITIALLY DEFERRED` would move a dangling-INSERT failure from the offending statement to COMMIT.*
- `MATCH SIMPLE` throughout. **Do NOT adopt `MATCH FULL`**, measured: under `MATCH FULL`, VALIDATE fails AND a new NULL-collection INSERT is REJECTED **while the constraint is still `NOT VALID`**. There is no grace window, so the NOT VALID -> VALIDATE choreography does not apply at all.

## Also in scope
- `purge_trash`'s `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED` fix, **one line either way**, and verified to work inside a plpgsql function body.
- The two class-B sites.
- **F10d, an operability cost to plan for:** under `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with a non-owner role the FK enforces correctly but PostgreSQL **redacts** the message to `Key is still referenced from table "manifest"` with NO key values. Production failures under the `svc` role will not name the blocking chash. Ship a diagnostic path (an anti-join query behind a command) so an operator can find the blocking row.
- **F8d, a scoping asymmetry to check:** the collection cascade scopes chunks by `chunks_*.collection` but the manifest by `catalog_documents.physical_collection`. A manifest row whose parent document is homed elsewhere but whose own `collection` names this collection is not reached by the cascade.

## Cost (F9, measured over 280,695 manifest rows)
`ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID` = 0.8 ms; `VALIDATE` = 333 ms.

## Acceptance
- [ ] P5-0's decision implemented (where VALIDATE runs, and what remediates a late upgrader).
- [ ] `ON UPDATE CASCADE` present; a TEST covers both a collection rename and a chash rekey propagating to the manifest.
- [ ] The deferrability choice made, recorded with its reasoning, and covered by a test at each class-B site.
- [ ] `purge_trash` passes with the constraint live.
- [ ] TEST: a dangling manifest INSERT is rejected; deleting a referenced chunk is rejected; a NULL-collection row is still accepted (MATCH SIMPLE exemption preserved. F6).
- [ ] The F10d diagnostic exists and is exercised under the `svc` role.
- [ ] Re-run the verify AFTER `VALIDATE` (RDR Phase 5 step: "Re-run after VALIDATE").

title: RDR-191 P5: ESTABLISH the remediation instrument, because reconcile CANNOT fix this class (F17)
description:
**F17, the remediation instrument is UNKNOWN. Establishing it is the work of this bead. Do not assume `reconcile` works.**

## Why the obvious tool cannot do it
`nx catalog reconcile`'s gap detection (`src/nexus/catalog/manifest_heal.py:130-134`) selects heal candidates as `len(manifests.get(tumbler, [])) < e.chunk_count`, **a row-COUNT deficit**, plus a ghost arm for `chunk_count == 0`. **F15's damage is count-preserving by construction:**

**VERIFIED SCOPE CORRECTION.** The predicate is a **TWO-ARM DISJUNCTION**. Re-verified twice by direct read (`grep -n` and `awk`), against two earlier off-by-one claims:
```
130:    gapped = [
131:        e for e in candidates          <- element expr, NOT a predicate
132:        if len(manifests.get(...)) < e.chunk_count      <- DEFICIT arm
133:        or (e.chunk_count == 0 and not manifests.get(...))  <- GHOST arm
134:    ]
```
**DEFICIT arm :132. GHOST arm :133.** F17 describes only the DEFICIT arm, so the GHOST arm is the one an implementer would drop without noticing. **THE GHOST ARM AT :133 IS THE ONE TO PRESERVE.** Replacing the whole predicate with an anti-join would silently delete ghost-class healing that works today, trading one blind spot for another.
 every manifest row is present and correct in number; what is missing is the CHUNK each row names. The deficit is therefore zero, `gapped` comes back empty, and **reconcile returns having done nothing, reporting success**, silently no-opping on precisely the rows it was assigned.

The RDR notes this is the same blindness as F8c's root cause: *"both reason about manifest ROWS, neither joins to the chunk table."*

`nx index <path> --force` is *"plausible but not proven"*: the affected document reports a `chunk_count` and returns nothing, and re-indexing may silently no-op (nexus-5xn3k).

## The prescribed shape
*"Any future repair for this class must be an ANTI-JOIN against the chunk store, not a count comparison"*, the same operation Phase 1 pushed into SQL for the mirror-image population (chunks no manifest references).

## Acceptance: demonstration, not exit codes
- [ ] Build the anti-join-based remediation.
- [ ] **DEMONSTRATE it on ONE affected document** (from the F15 set: 1.11.391, 1.6.2114, 1.6.3, 1.9.164) and show the count MOVED, before running it anywhere else.
- [ ] **Do NOT treat any command's exit code as evidence.** The re-verify (`nx catalog manifest-verify --list`, with P5-1's `collections_checked`) is the only evidence that counts. The RDR says this explicitly.
- [ ] **The `manifest_heal.py` ghost arm (:132) still works.** A regression test pins it. Adding an anti-join must not replace the two-arm predicate wholesale.
- [ ] Decide and record: does remediation DELETE the dangling manifest rows, or RE-CREATE the missing chunks? These are different products with different data consequences; pick deliberately and write down why.
- [ ] Coordinate with the P5-0 decision, if VALIDATE is automated, this instrument's SQL is what the changeset runs.
- [ ] Supersedes `nexus-84w9a`; close that bead when this lands.

title: RDR-191 P5: add `collections_checked` to _manifest_verify_list's CLEAN and DAMAGED payloads (F16b)
description:
**F16b, a CODE task, not a process note.** Phase 5's exit criterion cannot be mechanically evaluated today.

## Verified anchors (the RDR's ":476-569" has drifted)
`_manifest_verify_list` in `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py` starts at **:452**.
- clean-path guard **:485** · **clean JSON payload :486-492** · clean return :496
- `ClickException` at **:480 AND :499** (TWO read-failure sites, not one)
- **damaged JSON payload :515-522** · `Exit(1)` :569

**`collections_checked` must be added to BOTH payloads, :486-492 AND :515-522.** Decision says "clean AND damaged"; a change to only the clean path leaves the damaged path unparseable by the same gate script.

## The hole (verified by reading `_manifest_verify_list`)
`nx catalog manifest-verify --list` is the right instrument, it fails loud in BOTH directions where `nx doctor` cannot (doctor's `_check_dangling_manifests` never sets `fatal=True` on ANY path, and returns `ok=True` when the engine is unreachable AND when zero collections were compared). But:

- read failure -> `ClickException` (non-zero). Good.
- damage -> **always** `Exit(1)`, with `incomplete_collections` and `unroutable_collections` emitted as warnings INSIDE the already-failing path, so partial enumeration can never downgrade a damaged verdict. Good.
- **clean path -> exit 0, INCLUDING when the census compared ZERO collections.** It prints `OK, no dangling manifest rows (0 collection(s) checked)` and exits 0.

**The trap:** the compared count exists ONLY in the human-readable string. The `--json` clean payload is `{"collections": [], "total_rows": 0, "unroutable_collections": [], "incomplete_collections": {}, "clean": true, ...}`, `collections` there is the DAMAGED list, not the checked count, and **no field carries N**. A gate script parsing `--json` therefore CANNOT implement the non-vacuity check and will pass vacuously on an empty census. *"Do not assume the JSON is the machine-readable superset of the text; here it is a strict subset in the one field that matters."*

## What to build
Emit **`collections_checked`** in `_manifest_verify_list`'s **clean AND damaged** payloads, then gate on that field. The RDR picks this remedy over text-scraping explicitly: *"an exit criterion that cannot be mechanically evaluated is not an exit criterion."*

## The denominator must come from an INDEPENDENT source (raised during planning)
The exit criterion is `collections_checked > 0 AND == the deployment's known collection count`. If the denominator is also read from manifest-verify's own output, the comparison is circular and vacuous, the same shape this whole finding exists to kill. Take it from the collection registry / `nx catalog stats`, not from the census.

## Acceptance
- [ ] TEST FIRST: `collections_checked` present and correct in the CLEAN payload; present and correct in the DAMAGED payload.
- [ ] TEST: a zero-collection census is distinguishable from a clean census **through `--json` alone**.
- [ ] The gate script reads `collections_checked` from JSON and the denominator from an INDEPENDENT source; a test pins that the two sources differ.
- [ ] Non-vacuity: run the gate against a deliberately-emptied census and confirm it FAILS. Measure the detector against a broken input; do not assume it works.
- [ ] **THE COMMAND ITSELF MUST REFUSE A ZERO-COMPARED CENSUS.** Emitting `collections_checked` while leaving enforcement to an external gate script reproduces F16b one layer out: a non-vacuity signal that nothing consumes. Preferred remedy: `_manifest_verify_list` exits NON-ZERO when `collections_checked == 0`, so "found nothing to look at" is indistinguishable from failure at the exit code, which is the property F16 says a gate needs. If instead the refusal is left external, this bead must NAME the consumer (file and function), and a test must prove the consumer fails on a zero-compared census. An unnamed consumer is not a consumer.
- [ ] TEST: a zero-compared census exits non-zero (or the named consumer fails). Demonstrate against a deliberately-emptied census; do not assert it.
- [ ] Note in the code that this field is migration scaffolding scheduled for deletion in Phase 6 with the rest of `manifest_verify_all`.

title: RDR-191 P5 DECISION: where does VALIDATE run, given that a late-upgrading deployment bricks at boot (2nd boot-brick, NOT in the RDR)
description:
**DECISION BEAD. Raised during planning; NOT in the RDR. Blocks the FK beads because the FK changeset's authoring depends on the answer.**

## The problem: a SECOND boot-brick, same terminal shape as F14b
The FK's `ADD CONSTRAINT NOT VALID` and `VALIDATE` go in Liquibase, V5's `fk-002` precedent, and the all-DDL-through-Liquibase directive leaves no alternative. Liquibase runs UNCONDITIONALLY at engine boot.

But RDR-191 Phase 5 describes remediation as a **manual, operator-driven, per-deployment procedure** run "immediately before VALIDATE", and says explicitly *"This is a per-deployment gate, not a one-time fix."*

Those are incompatible for any deployment that upgrades AFTER this release ships. It boots; Liquibase reaches the VALIDATE changeset; VALIDATE scans and hits THAT box's own dangling rows; `MigrationException`; engine exits 1. F15 proves the population is non-zero on a real corpus, and the F8c/F10c producers have been running everywhere, so this is the expected case, not the edge case.

## The precedent the RDR cites but does not follow
`fk-002` is a THREE-step sequence: `ADD NOT VALID` -> **`fk-002-0-backfill-stubs`** -> `VALIDATE`. `fk-002` needed that middle step for exactly this reason. RDR-191 cites the precedent and replaces its middle step with a manual procedure that only ever runs on the first deployment.

## Candidate dispositions: price them, do not pre-pick
- **(a) In-Liquibase anti-join remediation changeset** between NOT VALID and VALIDATE. Matches `fk-002` exactly. F17 already supplies the correct SQL shape (*"must be an anti-join against the chunk store, not a count comparison"*) and it is a single statement. Open question: is silently deleting manifest rows at engine boot acceptable? They already reference nothing, but it is still unattended data mutation.
- **(b) Move VALIDATE out of Liquibase into the RDR-185 upgrade ladder**, where it can fail LOUD without bricking the engine. **The repo's own precedent points here:** F11d records that nothing in Liquibase ever VALIDATEs the octet checks, DELIBERATELY, *"the GH #1390 crash-loop shape"*, the identical hazard, and that the owner is `chash_rekey.py`, i.e. Python. Collides with all-DDL-through-Liquibase; note that VALIDATE-in-the-ladder already has a sanctioned precedent in this exact codebase.
- **(c) Ship the constraint `NOT VALID` permanently and never VALIDATE.** Keeps enforcement for every NEW row; forgoes the historical guarantee. Cheapest, weakest.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Each disposition priced against: late-upgrader boot safety, the all-DDL-through-Liquibase directive, and whether the historical guarantee survives.
- [ ] A decision recorded in T2 (`nexus/rdr-191-validate-placement-decision`) and, if it changes RDR-191's Decision or Phasing text, the RDR AMENDED, an accepted RDR whose plan silently diverges is the failure mode this project tracks.
- [ ] Hal consulted if the answer is (b): it touches a standing directive, and directive exceptions are Hal's, never a code comment's.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, a TEST that a late-upgrading deployment WITH a dangling population boots successfully. **This test must fail against the naive shape.**

PLAN-AUDIT PASS 1 CLAIM RETRACTED (2026-08-10). An earlier note on this bead said fk-002-6-reconcile resolves this decision and that the three dispositions "collapse to the house pattern". THAT WAS WRONG, and it was an INFERENCE relayed from a plan-audit rather than a fact read from the file. Retracted in full.

VERIFIED BY READING service/.../db/changelog/fk-002-validate.xml DIRECTLY:
- fk-002-6-reconcile is an ADDITIVE PARENT-STUB backfill: five `INSERT INTO nexus.catalog_collections (tenant_id, name) SELECT DISTINCT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` statements. It reconciles the COLLECTION-REGISTRY direction, where the missing object is a registry row that can be legitimately synthesised from the child's own values.
- The destructive "DELETE genuinely-orphaned" arm (Q5 arm b) is DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED for this table family, and the changelog says it should stay absent: "fk-002 tables (chunks_*, chash_index, topic_assignments) are the PRIMARY vector-serving layer, where an orphan chunk is real data, not lifecycle debris; deleting it would be data loss."
- A stub-unsatisfiable orphan "by design makes VALIDATE FAIL LOUD rather than admit bad data."

WHY IT DOES NOT TRANSFER TO RDR-191. For the manifest FK the parent is nexus.chunks and the child is catalog_document_chunks, so THE MISSING OBJECT IS THE CHUNK. A chunk carries chunk_text and an embedding; there is nothing to stub-register, and a synthesised chunk row would be FABRICATED DATA, not a registry stub. The one arm that would clear the F15 population is the destructive arm, which this precedent explicitly refuses on exactly this table family.

CONSEQUENCE: this DECISION REMAINS LIVE AND OPEN. All three dispositions stay on the table, and the fk-002 precedent is now EVIDENCE AGAINST disposition (a) rather than evidence for it, since it shows the house style is to FAIL LOUD rather than auto-delete referencing rows at boot. Weigh that against disposition (b) (VALIDATE in the RDR-185 ladder, where fail-loud does not brick the engine), which the same evidence now favours more strongly.

META: two agents in a row asserted this resolution without opening the file. Read fk-002-validate.xml before pricing anything here.

title: RDR-191 GATE-4 CO-RELEASE: ONE engine tag carries both the unify DDL and the rung retarget
description:
**CO-RELEASE GATE. This is not expressible as an ordinary dependency and that is why it is its own bead.**

A dependency edge lets A close in one release and B close in the next. Decision item 5(b) forbids exactly that: the unify DDL and the rekey-rung retarget must be in **ONE engine release**. comments.text:
2026-08-13 — THE PHASE 4 REPOINT BATCH NOW HAS AN EXECUTION PLAN. Read it before dispatching either reviewer: T2 [22445] nexus/rdr-191-repoint-batch-execution-plan-2026-08-13.

WHERE THIS REVIEW SITS: the plan's Step H. It reviews ONE branch, feature/o8dil-repoint-batch, cut manually from develop into .claude/worktrees/o8dil-repoint-batch. The batch is atomic by construction — two (soon one, consolidated) three-state changelog coupling lints go RED on every half-way state, so develop never sees a partial batch and there is no incremental review to have done earlier. The diff under review spans roughly 110 decision sites plus a ~700-file test retarget wave.

BRIEF THE CRITIC WITH THE PLAN'S TWO DECISIONS, so it pressure-tests them rather than rediscovering them:

DECISION 1 — manifest_verify / manifest_verify_all are RE-CREATED in the batch, not early-deleted. Grounds: both are LANGUAGE sql, so DROP TABLE ... CASCADE kills them at migration time, not latently; health.py:3914 calls manifest_verify_all inside _check_dangling_manifests (registered at :5214, so every nx doctor run); CatalogRepository:5411 calls manifest_verify in a transaction and REFUSES on its result (the RUNFENCE index-run fence, a live WRITE path); and nexus-o8dil.28 (GATE-5-LOCAL) asserts manifest-verify exits 0 with collections_checked > 0, so a Phase 4 deletion makes a Phase 5 gate unrunnable. Phase 6 (.33) keeps them on its delete list but must RE-DERIVE that against .28 and the RUNFENCE call site rather than inherit it from .18's text.

DECISION 2 — the nine combined-query functions keep NINE TYPED ENTRY POINTS with byte-identical signatures; nine independent LANGUAGE sql bodies, each naming its own embedding_<dim>. No shared implementation, no dim-parameterised collapse. Grounds: a collapsed form needs an untyped vector param and runtime column choice, which un-binds the HNSW index and reintroduces F13's measured ~250x silent seq-scan, deployment-dependently; "typed facades over shared implementations" is not available because the shared body would need the embedding column as a parameter, forcing dynamic SQL, forcing LANGUAGE plpgsql, which both blinds pg_depend (reintroducing exactly the latent-breakage class round-2 fix 1 eliminated) and blocks SQL-function inlining; and identical signatures mean jOOQ regenerates identical constants, so PgVectorRepository's three switch (dim) blocks at :1781/:1824/:1916 need ZERO change. Accepted cost: nine near-identical bodies invite drift, mitigated MECHANICALLY by a lint asserting they are token-identical modulo 384|768|1024.

ADDITIONS TO THIS BEAD'S EXISTING CRITIC PROMPT (its own listed questions all still stand):
- Is the DERIVED dim column on nexus.live_chunks keyed on WHICH EMBEDDING COLUMN IS NON-NULL, or on the vector's own width? The latter is wrong and would pass a naive test.
- Did chash_rekey's CONTENT_OCTET_CHECKS / POINTER_OCTET_CHECKS actually stop using positional slices? At 4 entries to 2, [:3] silently yields BOTH and [3:] silently yields EMPTY. Neither raises. The plan calls this the single most likely silent break in the batch.
- Was every plpgsql body CALLED by a test? They survive CREATE with stale references and fail only on first call, so a green migration proves nothing.
- Are the four NOT EXISTS copies collapsed IN PLACE, or merged into one shared helper? Merging silently rescopes two of them (two are chash-only; CatalogRepository.sampleMissingChashes is tenant AND collection scoped).
- Is SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest GREEN, not skipped? It is the only proof of the F14a straddle that .21 gates on, and the F14a failure mode is now SILENT never-converged rather than a brick.
- Do the three raw-SQL bare-embedding sites (PgVectorRepository :993/:1324/:1337) each have a plan test proving FULL HNSW use from a query shape that OMITS any IS NOT NULL predicate? That omitting shape is precisely where F13's silent regression lands.
- What does the batch leave undefended for Phase 5, given nexus.chunks ships with ZERO collection FK (not even NOT VALID) until .29/.31?
