comments.text:
Implemented this session (2026-08-18), TDD throughout, on develop (uncommitted — orchestrator
commits per RDR-184 Gap-4 protocol).

## What shipped

1. `src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py`: `ChunkBatcher.__init__` gained `on_flush: Callable[[int, int,
   str, float, str | None], None] | None = None` — a CONSTRUCTOR callback (not a per-call
   parameter like `drain(on_progress=...)`, since `add()` is called once per file and dispatches
   flushes internally with no per-call site to hand a callback to). Fires once per SETTLED flush
   (`flush_num, chunks, collection, elapsed_s, error`) from the same completion point as the
   `chunk_flush_complete` structlog event — never for a bisect attempt, matching that event's own
   documented contract. Mutual exclusion with `drain()`'s own `on_progress`: a new `self._draining`
   flag (set under lock for the duration of `drain()`) suppresses `on_flush` so an in-flight flush
   dispatched earlier by `add()` but completing during drain's wait is reported by exactly one
   voice, not two — same two-liveness-voices class nexus-1iw8k fixed for
   `_ETATicker`/`_PhaseHeartbeat`.
2. `src/nexus/indexer.py`: `on_flush` threaded straight through `index_repository` -> `_run_index`
   -> `ChunkBatcher(on_flush=on_flush)`. `None` is a complete no-op (backward compat verified).
3. `src/nexus/commands/index.py`: new `on_flush_progress` closure renders exactly the bead's ask:
   `  [post] flush #N complete (Xs, M chunks, collection)`, ` — FAILED: <error>` appended on
   failure. Gated on the explicit `--monitor` flag ONLY (assessment 7.5) — NOT auto-enabled on
   non-TTY like `on_file`'s per-file lines, so the default transcript (including every existing
   non-interactive/CI run) is byte-for-byte unchanged; `on_flush=on_flush_progress if monitor else
   None` is passed to `index_repository`.

## Non-vacuous tests added

- `tests/test_chunk_batcher.py::TestOnFlushHook` (5 tests): fires once per mid-loop flush with
  advancing chunk counts (assertion "count of emissions == count of actual flush calls" — the
  exact gap this bead exists to close); failure reported at occurrence; NOT fired during drain
  (drain's own on_progress still fires — proves the mutual exclusion, not just "on_flush exists");
  defaults to None safely; NOT fired for a bisected attempt (only its settled halves).
- `tests/test_indexer.py`: `test_on_flush_threads_through_to_chunk_batcher` +
  `test_on_flush_defaults_to_none_when_omitted` — wiring-only, via a fake ChunkBatcher (real
  firing behaviour is TestOnFlushHook's job).
- `tests/test_index_cmd.py`: `test_monitor_wires_on_flush_and_renders_progress_line` (exact
  rendered shape, hard constraint 1 — no `^\s*\[N/M\]` — verified, no `\r`, `Done.` last),
  `test_default_no_monitor_on_flush_is_none` (pins the level assignment rather than assuming it),
  `test_monitor_flush_progress_emits_nothing_without_monitor_flag`,
  `test_monitor_flush_failure_surfaces_before_done` (asserts FAILED position is strictly before
  `Done.`'s position in the output string, not merely "present somewhere").

`uv run pytest tests/test_chunk_batcher.py tests/test_indexer.py tests/test_index_cmd.py
tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py -q` -> 261 passed. Full unit suite (`-n auto`)
and `-m lint` bucket both green (one unrelated pre-existing flake in
test_routing_push_review_coverage.py, passes in isolation, no relation to this diff).

Recommend closing.

title: index: prune-deleted-files page progress (collection i/3, page k/K)
description:
Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), section 3,
proposal a3, bead-breakdown item 3.

## Defect

`  [post] Pruning deleted files...` is followed by **547.8s (9m08s) of total silence** on a real
`nx index repo .` run: 45% of the run's post-processing, and the single largest black hole in the
transcript. Inside it there is one UNBROKEN 427.5s window with no output of any kind.

This is NOT an opaque blocking call. It is a page loop with an exactly computable denominator:

- `_prune_deleted_files` `src/nexus/indexer.py:2683`. Outer loop over 3 collections at
  `src/nexus/indexer.py:2751`. Per collection: `chashes_for_collection` (2761, single call),
  `restore_rereferenced` (2782), then `_paginated_get(col, include=["metadatas"])` (2795).
- `_paginated_get` `src/nexus/indexer.py:2346`, `while True` at **2360-2371**,
  `limit=_CHROMA_PAGE_SIZE` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2342` = **300**), `offset += 300`.
  No callback, no total. This is the 427.5s hole.
- The denominator is ONE `col.count()` away (`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1150`, also 2094).
  For the evidence repo: code 28,564 -> 96 pages, docs 4,849 -> 17, rdr 6,930 -> 24.
  **137 pages total, at ~4.5s/page.**

Verdict from the assessment: **progress counter, not spinner**. A heartbeat here would be a
downgrade from information that is already sitting in the loop.

## Ask (proposal a3, ~40 LOC)

1. Add an optional `on_page(page, total_pages, scanned)` callback to `_paginated_get`
   (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2346`). Optional, so the ~6 other call sites are unaffected.
2. `total_pages` from `col.count()` divided by `_CHROMA_PAGE_SIZE`, taken once before the loop.
3. `_prune_deleted_files` renders `collection i/3, page k/K`.

Emitted line shape (constraint 1 is load-bearing here, see below):
`  [post] Pruning deleted files: collection 1/3, page 42/96 (3m10s elapsed)`

Where a sub-step genuinely has no denominator (`chashes_for_collection`, a single
`get_manifests`), fall back to the phase heartbeat and say `still running (Xs elapsed)`. Never
fabricate a percentage or an ETA.

## Non-vacuous test

- Fake collection with a known chunk count spanning >= 3 pages; assert the callback fires once per
  page with a MONOTONIC page index and the CORRECT total, and that the last call has `page ==
  total_pages`. An off-by-one that renders `page 97/96` is exactly the class this test exists to
  catch.
- Assert the rendered line does NOT match `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]` (constraint 1). This assertion is
  the reason the bead is not a one-liner: the naive `[42/96]` rendering silently corrupts a
  release gate.
- Assert no `\r` reaches the non-TTY path.
- Non-vacuity: remove the `on_page` wiring from `_prune_deleted_files` and the test must go red.
- Guard the extra `col.count()` call: assert it is issued ONCE per collection, not per page.

## Related

- nexus-y2unb (open, P3) proposes skipping prune passes entirely on no-change runs. Complementary,
  not overlapping: this bead makes the pass observable, that one makes it sometimes unnecessary.
- The phase-heartbeat bead (assessment a1) covers the atomic sub-steps this counter cannot reach.
- nexus-441p5 / nexus-1kise (closed) are prior `_paginated_get` correctness work; neither touched
  progress.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS (binding on ANY change to `nx index` output)

From an exhaustive consumer sweep in T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` section 7.4.
Constraints 1 and 2 break their gate SILENTLY (wrong result, not a red). Read them before writing
a single line of output code.

1. **Never emit a new line matching `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]`.**
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:197-203` counts lines of that shape
   (`grep -cv skipped`) into a TWO-SIDED gate (run1 >= 10, run2 <= 6). A new line of that shape
   makes the gate fail silently wrong, not loudly.
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh:399-401` counts the same shape (>= 3).
   => Put any fraction LATER in the line, behind the `  [post] ` prefix. Correct shape:
   `  [post] Pruning deleted files: collection 1/3, page 42/96 (3m10s elapsed)`.
2. **Never emit `\r` on the non-TTY path.** `tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts
   `"\r" not in result.output`.
3. **Do not touch the `[debug-timing]` block.**
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/aggregate.py:20-21,27` hard-parses the header wording and the
   ordered stage rows and raises `ValueError` on drift.
4. **`Done.` must stay, and stay LAST.** 8 assertion sites across 6 files
   (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:84,103`; `tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py:277`;
   `tests/test_indexer_e2e.py:864,907`; `tests/test_index_taxonomy.py:106`;
   `tests/test_index_reminder.py:192,212`; `tests/test_scenario_journeys.py:411`), two of them
   deliberately on failure paths. Also `tail -5` consumers
   (`tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:528,535,560,568`; `scenarios/03_skills.sh:11`) degrade if new
   trailing lines are appended after the summary. Add nothing after `Done.`.
5. **Do not reword the summary sentences.** `tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` pins ~50 exact
   sentences including em-dashes and `(s)` pluralization; `tests/test_index_cmd.py:514,571-574,588`
   and `tests/test_index_pdf_batch.py:117-118,141,189` likewise.
6. **`[post]` is the SAFE channel to extend.** Nothing asserts on the `[post]` markers;
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/test_aggregate.py:19` fixtures one as noise the parser must
   skip. Nothing in `.github/workflows/**` or `conexus/hooks/**` parses `nx index` output at all.
   This is the single most useful fact for anything in this family.

## Conventions to REUSE, not reinvent (assessment 7.3)

- Completed duration: `({t:.1f}s)`.
- Projection: `~{_fmt_duration(...)} remaining` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2894-2903`: `42s` / `1m30s` / `2h05m`).
- Rate: `{rate*60:.1f} <unit>/min`.
- ETA regimes: `_format_eta` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:216-236`) -> `pending` / `~N min remaining` / `done`.
- Where no denominator exists, say so: `still running (1m12s elapsed)`. Never a fake percentage,
  never a fake ETA.

Source: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159).

Critic-verified against current code (T2 [22823]).

title: index: _ETATicker is stopped before the file loop and never fires
description:
Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), section 4,
proposal a2, bead-breakdown item 2.

## Defect (NEW BUG, found by the 2026-08-10 output-UX assessment)

`_ETATicker` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:249-320`) is designed to emit `[eta] ...` every 60s
REGARDLESS of TTY, precisely for background/CI runs. It emitted ZERO lines in a 14-minute

inside "metadata"/"meta".

## Root cause (file:line)

`on_phase` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:566-577`) STOPS the ticker on the FIRST phase marker, via
the `post_pass_started` latch. The in-code comment justifies it with "file walk is done by the time
the first post-pass phase fires". That is FALSE:

- `on_start` (which starts the ticker) is called at `src/nexus/indexer.py:3496`.
- The first unconditional `on_phase` is `"Registering N catalog entries..."` at
  `src/nexus/indexer.py:3725`, which fires BEFORE the per-file loop.

So the ticker is started and then killed within seconds, and is never alive for the file loop OR
for post-processing.

Non-TTY / CI / `nx hooks` runs (`src/nexus/commands/hooks.py:53-56` appends to

whatsoever during the 627.6s post pass measured in the assessment. The observability feature

Stop latching `post_pass_started` on the first `on_phase`. Latch on the REAL post-pass entry

- Regression test asserting >= 1 `[eta]` line on a simulated run longer than the ticker interval,
  with an INJECTED clock (no real 60s sleep) and a phase marker fired BEFORE the file loop, i.e. the

- Non-vacuity: the test must go RED against today's code. Run it against unpatched HEAD first and
  record that it fails; a test that passes both before and after is the failure mode that let this
  ship inert.
- Assert the `[eta]` line survives the non-TTY path (this ticker's whole purpose) and does not match
  `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]`.

## Related

- nexus-vatx (closed) is where `_ETATicker` came from (Gap 3). This bead is that feature never
  having fired.

title: index: post-processing phases must emit a liveness heartbeat
description:
Owner complaint, verbatim: "many long pauses with zero indication of life, etc. extremely bad uix".

Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), proposal a1,
bead-breakdown item 1. Evidence run: `nx index repo .` on nexus itself, cloud/voyage, conexus
7.5.0, no `--force`, exit 0, ~14 min wall (10:43:0x to 10:57:10), NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=INFO, 2155 log
lines.

## Defect

The complaint is NOT about the per-file loop. It is about POST-PROCESSING, which runs 627.6s
(45% of wall) behind eight start/done marker pairs and NOTHING in between: 16 lines for 627.6s,
i.e. one line per 39 seconds.

Measured silent windows in the default transcript (identical in TTY and non-TTY, because the
`[post]` markers at `src/nexus/commands/index.py:578` are unconditional on stderr):

| Last thing printed | Silence | What was actually running |
|---|---|---|
| `  [post] Pruning deleted files...` | **547.8s (9m08s)** | 3 collections x (chashes_for_collection + restore + full paginated metadata scan + delete) |
| (inside the above, no output at all) | **427.5s unbroken** | `_paginated_get(code_col, ["metadatas"])` over 28,564 chunks = 96 pages at ~4.5s/page |
| `  [post] Pruning misclassified chunks...` | **74.6s** | 2 sweeps, batched manifest resolve + `col.get(ids=)` batches |
| `  Catalog: linking 251 new entries...` | **37.4s** | rdr 8.1s + prose 25.9s + pdf 3.4s |
| `  [post]   staleness sweep: code...` | **17.7s** | docs staleness paginated sweep |

Two phases account for 622.4s of the 627.6s. `--monitor` does not relieve any of this: it adds
only the per-file `[N/M]` lines (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:337-338,556`), so it contributes
exactly nothing during post-processing. See assessment section 5.

## Ask (proposal a1)

Establish a LIVENESS GUARANTEE: no phase may exceed N seconds without producing output.

- TTY: N = 10s, rendered in place with `\r` (no scrollback cost).
- Non-TTY: N = 30s, appended as real lines (bounds log growth: a 14-min run adds <= 28 lines).

Rejecting 60s (the existing `_ETATicker` interval): at 60s the 74.6s prune emits exactly one tick,
which does not read as "alive". 10s matches tqdm's own `monitor_interval` default and is the point
where a human starts to suspect a hang.

Mechanism: generalize `_ETATicker` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:249-320`) into a phase-scoped
`_PhaseHeartbeat`, ARMED by `_phase()` on entry and DISARMED by the matching "done" marker. It
already has the daemon-thread lifecycle, double-start guard and lock discipline
(`src/nexus/commands/index.py:277-306`). Reuse it; do not write a second timer.

Emitted line shape: `  [post] <phase> still running (Xs elapsed)`.

## Non-vacuous test

- Drive a deliberately slow fake phase (injected clock, no real sleep) longer than the interval and
  assert the OUTPUT CONTAINS NO GAP > N between consecutive lines, measured on the injected clock.
  The assertion must be on inter-line gaps, not on "at least one heartbeat appeared": a single tick
  passes the weak form while leaving a 500s hole.
- Non-vacuity: delete the arming call and the test must go red. Prove it, do not assume it.
- Assert the emitted heartbeat line does NOT match `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]` (constraint 1 below) and
  contains no `\r` when `isatty()` is False (constraint 2).
- Assert `Done.` is still the last line.

## Related

- nexus-vatx (closed) built the 60s `_ETATicker` for exactly this class; it is dead on every run
  (see the sibling bead for the latch bug), which is why this gap survived.
- nexus-uizok (closed) added the drain phase markers; markers without a heartbeat is precisely the
  state measured here.
- nexus-47ubt (closed) is the earlier "no live progress" report, root-caused to buffering.
- nexus-zedf7 (closed) added ETA/rate to the drain loop specifically.
- Denominator-bearing siblings (page/sweep counters) are tracked separately; heartbeat is the
  FALLBACK for genuinely atomic sub-steps (`chashes_for_collection`, a single `get_manifests`),
  not a substitute for a real counter where a denominator exists.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS (binding on ANY change to `nx index` output)

From an exhaustive consumer sweep in T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` section 7.4.
Constraints 1 and 2 break their gate SILENTLY (wrong result, not a red). Read them before writing
a single line of output code.

1. **Never emit a new line matching `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]`.**
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:197-203` counts lines of that shape
   (`grep -cv skipped`) into a TWO-SIDED gate (run1 >= 10, run2 <= 6). A new line of that shape
   makes the gate fail silently wrong, not loudly.
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh:399-401` counts the same shape (>= 3).
   => Put any fraction LATER in the line, behind the `  [post] ` prefix. Correct shape:
   `  [post] Pruning deleted files: collection 1/3, page 42/96 (3m10s elapsed)`.
2. **Never emit `\r` on the non-TTY path.** `tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts
   `"\r" not in result.output`.
3. **Do not touch the `[debug-timing]` block.**
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/aggregate.py:20-21,27` hard-parses the header wording and the
   ordered stage rows and raises `ValueError` on drift.
4. **`Done.` must stay, and stay LAST.** 8 assertion sites across 6 files
   (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:84,103`; `tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py:277`;
   `tests/test_indexer_e2e.py:864,907`; `tests/test_index_taxonomy.py:106`;
   `tests/test_index_reminder.py:192,212`; `tests/test_scenario_journeys.py:411`), two of them
   deliberately on failure paths. Also `tail -5` consumers
   (`tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:528,535,560,568`; `scenarios/03_skills.sh:11`) degrade if new
   trailing lines are appended after the summary. Add nothing after `Done.`.
5. **Do not reword the summary sentences.** `tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` pins ~50 exact
   sentences including em-dashes and `(s)` pluralization; `tests/test_index_cmd.py:514,571-574,588`
   and `tests/test_index_pdf_batch.py:117-118,141,189` likewise.
6. **`[post]` is the SAFE channel to extend.** Nothing asserts on the `[post]` markers;
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/test_aggregate.py:19` fixtures one as noise the parser must
   skip. Nothing in `.github/workflows/**` or `conexus/hooks/**` parses `nx index` output at all.
   This is the single most useful fact for anything in this family.

## Conventions to REUSE, not reinvent (assessment 7.3)

- Completed duration: `({t:.1f}s)`.
- Projection: `~{_fmt_duration(...)} remaining` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2894-2903`: `42s` / `1m30s` / `2h05m`).
- Rate: `{rate*60:.1f} <unit>/min`.
- ETA regimes: `_format_eta` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:216-236`) -> `pending` / `~N min remaining` / `done`.
- Where no denominator exists, say so: `still running (1m12s elapsed)`. Never a fake percentage,
  never a fake ETA.

Source: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159).

title: y9t08's 600s timeout + unchanged retry makes a genuinely wedged engine surface 20x SLOWER than the pre-7.5.0 baseline, not just slower than the shipped-buggy 30s state
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 by substantive-critic review of the 5-commit Phase-1 batch
(127f2dbc nexus-y9t08, on develop @ HEAD after 3427a030).

## Established by code reading (not inferred)

The pre-7.5.0 baseline path (HttpVectorClient._request, urllib-based,
src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:711-795) explicitly EXCLUDES
TimeoutError from its retry classifier ("TimeoutError is intentionally
NOT in this retry classifier (it is not an auto-restart signature); it
propagates straight to the _get/_post handler" — :780-782). A synchronous-
embed timeout on that path fails ONCE, after ~600s, no retry.

The 7.5.0 combined-write path (HttpCatalogClient -> RefreshableHttpStoreMixin,
httpx-based) DOES retry ReadTimeout, at BOTH layers:
- _refreshable_client.py:_is_retryable_endpoint_error explicitly includes
  httpx.ReadTimeout (:106-118), for a DIFFERENT reason (supervisor-restart
  window), not tuned for "long synchronous compute-bound request."
- nexus/retry.py:_manifest_write_with_retry (4 attempts, delays 0.5/1/2s)
  wraps the whole call again; its own _is_connectivity_error (:566)
  matches httpx.TransportError, which covers ReadTimeout.
- Worst case: 4 outer attempts x 2 inner attempts = 8 POSTs per flush,
  EACH bounded by whatever timeout the client uses.

## The regression y9t08 introduces (quantified, not just qualitative)

y9t08 (127f2dbc) restored the per-request timeout from 30s to 600s on
this path WITHOUT touching the retry classifier (explicitly documented
as deliberate in the commit message, citing GH #1371 as the reason not
to narrow the shared classifier). The retry decision is genuinely
DELIBERATE and DOCUMENTED — this bead is not about silent scope
reduction, it is about the quantified consequence of that decision not
being written down anywhere.

Worst-case wall-clock for ONE flush against a genuinely WEDGED (not
merely slow) engine, before the client gives up and surfaces a failure:

  pre-7.5.0 baseline:        ~600s  (1 attempt, no retry)
  7.5.0 as shipped (buggy):  ~240s  (8 attempts x ~30s)
  post-y9t08 fix (this batch): ~4800s / 80 min  (8 attempts x 600s)

Each of those 8 attempts starts a FRESH, uncancelled server-side embed
(no cancellation path exists in CombinedWriteService.java /
Bge768Embedder.java — tracked separately as nexus-0o76a). So the fix
that correctly restores budget for the INTENDED case (a large legitimate
embed that needs more than 30s) simultaneously makes the DISASTER case
(engine truly wedged) both slower to surface AND accumulate more
uncancelled duplicate embeds than either prior state, for as long as
Phase 2 (admission control / cancellation, nexus-0o76a / nexus-zu4ma)
remains un-shipped.

## Why this matters for THIS release specifically

This release is explicitly framed as a stability/performance release
whose entire cluster (b32rx/y9t08/97dp4/4s1ww/v2mdd) exists because an
engine wedge already happened once in production. Shipping Phase 1 alone
does not make a wedge scenario safer than the pre-7.5.0 baseline — it
makes it worse, by design, until Phase 2 lands. Nothing in the y9t08
commit message, docstring, or bead currently states this quantified
comparison; it only states the retry-vs-narrow decision was deliberate,
which is true but incomplete.

## Ask

1. Decide explicitly whether the 8x multiplication is acceptable for
   this release given Phase 2 has no committed timeline (engine tag cut
   required).
2. Consider a narrower mitigation that does NOT touch the shared
   classifier: cap the OUTER retry count specifically for the
   chunk-carrying page (e.g. via a per-call retry-count override on
   _manifest_write_with_retry, mirroring the per-call timeout override
   pattern y9t08 already established), so a genuinely wedged engine still
   surfaces in a bounded multiple of 600s, not 8x.
3. At minimum, record the quantified worst-case comparison above
   somewhere durable (bead or docstring) so a future reader doesn't have
   to re-derive it.

Related: nexus-y9t08 (the fix that introduces this), nexus-0o76a (the
engine-side cancellation/admission-control half), nexus-zu4ma
(sub-batching), nexus-b32rx (the still-unexplained delta this cluster
exists to chase).

title: [bug] GH#1432: nx index repo prints 'Done.' and exits 0 when every chunk flush fails and zero chunks land
description:
GH #1432 (filed 2026-07-30 by hhildebrand-conductor, still open). Beaded 2026-08-10 during a
release-planning assessment that found it had NO bead — verified by scanning all 5000 beads
(4534 closed + 431 open + 35 deferred) across title/description/design/notes/acceptance for a
reference to 1431 or 1432. Zero hits. Its sibling #1431 was likewise untracked, and was
independently rediscovered ten days later as the 7.5.0 release blocker nexus-33hpq — the cost of
leaving a user report outside the tracker.

## Defect

When every file's chunk flush fails during `nx index repo`, the indexer prints "Done." to stdout
and exits 0. Zero chunks land. The structured log records 64 chunk_batch_flush_failed events and
59 bisect retries; nothing reaches stdout or the exit code.

Reported observation:

  [89/89] architecture.md - 3 chunks (1.2s)
  # (silence during the flush phase - service dies, 64 flushes fail)
  Tip: run `nx hooks install` to auto-index this repo on every commit.
  Done.
  $ echo $?
  0

The user has no reason to suspect a problem until a later search returns empty.

This is the no-silent-fallbacks-for-data-correctness class in its purest form: total failure of
the write path reported as success, by both channels a script or a human would check.

## Ask (from the issue, unchanged)

1. Non-zero exit code when flush failures > 0.
2. A summary line on stdout, e.g. "Warning: 64/89 files failed to flush (0 chunks landed).
   Re-run to retry."
3. `--monitor` should show flush progress (batch N/M) and failures rather than going silent
   between the last file and "Done."

## Test

Force every flush to fail and assert BOTH the non-zero exit and the stdout summary. Non-vacuity:
must go red if the exit-code propagation is removed. The existing coverage is what let this ship.

Related: GH #1431 (the trigger that produced the mass flush failures — the onnx-local blowup;
see nexus-33hpq closed, nexus-y9t08, nexus-b32rx). Fixing #1431 removes today's trigger; this bead
is about the reporting being wrong for ANY cause of flush failure.
close_reason: Verified ALREADY SHIPPED at 3ef64e69 (pre-dated this bead's pickup): commands/index.py fires stdout warning + ClickException on ANY chunk_flush_failed_files>0 — stronger than the bead's total-failure bar; both total- and partial-failure exit paths pinned by tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py. Independently confirmed by substantive-critic against the bead's own acceptance criteria (T2 [22823]).

Ask 3 of GH #1432 has been carved out into **nexus-rhwg5** (P1), filed 2026-08-10 from the
`nx index repo` output-UX assessment (T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10`,
entry 22159, section 6). This bead can close on asks 1 and 2 without leaving ask 3 unowned.

## What 3ef64e69 covered, and what it did not (measured, not inferred)

Covered (asks 1 and 2): `_drain_batcher_with_markers` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2966-2993`) appends
`, N file(s) failed` per flush line and ` - N file(s) failed to flush` to the close marker;
`src/nexus/commands/index.py` raises `ClickException` on `chunk_flush_failed_files`.

NOT covered (ask 3, verbatim: "`--monitor` should show flush progress (batch N/M) and failures
rather than going silent between the last file and 'Done.'"):

1. `_drain_batcher_with_markers` is called **exactly once**, at `src/nexus/indexer.py:4408` (the
   end-of-run drain). On a real `nx index repo .` run that drain covered **3 flushes / 3.7s**,

   There is no hook to attach to.
3. Correcting the record: the 3ef64e69 commit message says failures surface "AS THEY HAPPEN during
   the drain". True for the drain, FALSE for the mid-loop majority, where a flush failure surfaces
   only at the end via the summary plus exit code. Do not let the commit message stand as the

title: [bug] 7.5.0 combined write cut the synchronous embed timeout 600s -> 30s and retries the abandoned request — uncancelled server-side embeds stack
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 by a read-only deep-analyst assessment of the 7.5.0 local-index cluster
(T2 nexus/assess-local-index-cluster-2026-08-10 [22152]). Independently verified against
the tree by the dispatching session before filing.

## The regression

The 7.5.0 combined-write path dropped the synchronous server-side embed from a 600s HTTP
timeout to 30s.

- OLD path POST /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks passes timeout=600 explicitly:
  src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1403. Its docstring (:827-830) states WHY: the embed
  is synchronous inside the request.
- NEW path POST /v1/catalog/manifest/write_many passes NO timeout:
  src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:283 calls
  super().__init__(base_url=..., tenant=..., _token=...) with no timeout argument, so it
  inherits src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:79 _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0.

Same server-side work, 20x less time budget.

## Why it compounds instead of just failing

httpx.ReadTimeout is retryable in BOTH retry layers (_refreshable_client.py:106-118 and
nexus/retry.py:534) => up to 8 POSTs per flush. Nothing cancels the abandoned server-side
embed: no cancellation in CombinedWriteService.java or Bge768Embedder.java, and no
admission control (NexusService.java:393 is unbounded virtual-thread-per-request).
Multiply by ChunkBatcher flush_concurrency=3 (src/nexus/indexer.py:4196-4205).

So a timed-out flush leaves its embed running on the engine AND starts another one.

## Why this matters beyond itself

This is a coherent, code-grounded candidate mechanism for nexus-b32rx (the unexplained
~30GB on v7.4.0 vs 77.4GB on the 7.5.0 tree at the same cap=300) that no bead had.
Critically, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/ has an EMPTY diff between
engine-service-v0.1.68 and v0.1.69 — the embedder and router are byte-identical. The only
embedding-relevant delta between those tags is that CombinedWriteService.java is NEW in
v0.1.69 (commit 47995491, and it lives in service/.../db/, not vectors/). So the two runs
differ in WHICH CLIENT PATH they take and under WHAT TIMEOUT, around an unchanged embedder.

If this is the mechanism, the shipped cap=16 fix suppresses the symptom by making each
embed fast enough to fit in 30s, and the actual defect — a 20x timeout cut with retries and
no cancellation — is still present and still armed for any caller whose embed exceeds 30s.
nexus-b32rx's own round-1 critique predicted exactly this shape ("neutral-to-harmful if the
delta scales with REQUEST COUNT instead ... an abandoned client-timed-out request may keep
running server-side while a retry starts a second one").

## Ask

1. Set an explicit embed-appropriate timeout on the combined-write path (600s, matching the
   old path) rather than inheriting the 30s T2 default.
2. Decide deliberately whether ReadTimeout on a synchronous-embed POST should be retryable
   at all while the server-side work is uncancellable. Retrying an uncancelled embed is
   additive load, not a recovery.
3. Test: assert the combined-write client is constructed with an embed-grade timeout, and
   that it does not inherit _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S. Non-vacuity: it must go red if the explicit
   timeout is removed.

## Gating experiment (cheap, single-variable, ~15 min, no engine build, no tag)

On develop: restore the onnx-local cap to 300 AND change exactly one other thing —
timeout=600.0 on the combined-write client. Same tree, same engine v0.1.69, same 36-file
fixture. Compare peak RSS against the recorded 77.4GB and grep the client log for
manifest_write_transient_error_retry / refreshable_http_store.retry. This single run decides
whether the cluster is a MEMORY problem or a TIMEOUT problem, and therefore whether cap=16
is the fix or a workaround.

Related: nexus-b32rx (the unexplained delta this may explain), nexus-lqrec (retry storm),
nexus-zu4ma (engine-side bound), nexus-33hpq (closed, the shipped cap).
close_reason: CLOSE-SHIPPED — verified in commits 127f2dbc + 47c5a39a (2026-08-10, embed-grade timeout on the combined write / uncancellable-embed retry fix). Triage 2026-08-11; commits independently confirmed. Admin close of already-shipped work — review gate overridden deliberately.

title: era-hop-mvv is named "weekly + on ladder-path changes" but is workflow_dispatch-only — the 6.x upgrade journey has no cadence and last ran 2026-07-29
description:
Found 2026-08-09 when Hal asked whether anyone had tested upgrading from the 6.x series to 7.5.0. Answer: no, and the mechanism that would answer it is not running.

## The gap

.github/workflows/era-hop-mvv.yml is the journey that covers exactly this question. Its rehearse_era_hop.sh header states the claim precisely (RDR-185 P4.3 / nexus-n7u38.30): "a fresh-or-ancient install converges with nx upgrade alone — the 2026-07-16 work-instance shape (pre-RDR-108 ids, store_put-only collections, Chroma substrate) reaches current UNATTENDED". It installs a REAL old PyPI release (ERA_RELEASE default 6.0.0), stands it up the way that era actually did, seeds ancient data, then updates the code and asserts convergence.

TWO PROBLEMS:

1. NAME ADVERTISES A CADENCE IT DOES NOT HAVE.
   line 1:  name: Era-spanning upgrade hop (weekly + on ladder-path changes)
   line 80: on:
   line 81:   workflow_dispatch:
   That is the ENTIRE trigger block. No schedule. No path filter. No push. The workflow is named for a weekly run and an on-change run, and has neither. Anyone reading the run list sees a title asserting coverage that does not exist — the same class as a green that means nothing, except here it is a NAME that means nothing.

2. ITS LAST THREE RUNS ALL FAILED, AND NONE OF THEM PRODUCED PRODUCT SIGNAL.
   2026-07-29 failure, 2026-07-27 failure, 2026-07-27 failure. The 07-29 failure:
     event=service_bge_provision_failed ... [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
     Error: failed to provision the standard bge-768 ONNX (offline or download failed)
     FAIL nx init --service failed on 6.0.0
     ABORT (provision failed)
   That is the 416 MB bge-768 model download being reset on the GH runner — INFRASTRUCTURE, not a product defect. So the journey aborted during setup and told us nothing about whether 6.0.0 actually converges. Three consecutive runs of no-signal, then nothing for 11 days.

Net: 6.x -> 7.5.0 is UNVERIFIED. Not "verified broken" — genuinely unmeasured.

## Also unrun

  package-upgrade-mvv.yml        no runs at all
  stranded-redirect-rehearsal.yml no runs at all
(The --package-upgrade leg WAS run locally during the 7.5.0 release battery, one release back: 7.4.0 -> 7.5.0. The two-hop stranded journey was not run this release.)

## Asks

1. Give era-hop the cadence its name claims, or rename it to the truth. A dispatch-only workflow titled "weekly" is worse than an untitled one.
2. Make the bge-768 provision robust in CI, or cache it. Three consecutive infrastructure aborts means the gate has produced no product signal in a month; an abort during setup should be visibly distinct from a product failure, and repeated setup aborts should themselves raise something.
3. Run it against 7.5.0 and record the result. In flight locally as of this filing.
4. Decide the supported 6.x story explicitly and test the one that matters. Note RDR-155 P4b deleted Chroma and nx guided-upgrade, so a PRE-PG 6.x install cannot upgrade straight to 7.5.0 at all — it must two-hop via conexus==6.18.1. An already-migrated 6.18.x install should upgrade directly. Those are two different journeys (--era-hop and --stranded) and neither has been exercised against this release.

Related: nexus-8nlj4 (two-hop rehearsal), nexus-4922x (hop-3 redirect fix, shipped in 7.5.0 and NOT exercised end-to-end since), nexus-n7u38.30 (the era-hop journey itself).
close_reason: Ask 1 resolved via the rename-to-truth arm: the file's own 2026-08-08 resolution block forbids restoring the schedule (substrate-etl rung deleted at RDR-155 P4b; this file is a dispatch-only parts donor by design), so the name now says exactly that and points at the weekly successor. Asks 2-4 verified superseded: stranded-redirect-rehearsal.yml runs weekly and is green (2026-08-10, 2026-08-17 scheduled successes), the 6.x story is decided and armed (LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE=6.18.1, two-hop via 6.18.1), and the hop-3 residual was already filed. Watchdog blindness to dispatch-only workflows remains open separately.

title: warm-reindex skip gate goes RED on 7.5.0 and CANNOT be made green: CombinedWriteService emits no observability at all for its existence-partition
description:
Found in the T1 post-release shakedown of 7.5.0 (surface S6), 2026-08-09.

## Symptom

tests/e2e/warm-reindex-skip-gate.sh FAILS:
  Leg B: one perturbed file — sibling chunks must SKIP server-side
    staged=9 skip_lines=0 embedded=0
  WARM-REINDEX SKIP GATE FAILED: leg B produced NO upsert_embed_skipped lines

## Why the gate cannot see it

The gate greps for exactly one string (warm-reindex-skip-gate.sh:75-85, its own comment calls it "the ONLY INFO-level evidence"): event=upsert_embed_skipped. That line is emitted from exactly ONE place in the engine — PgVectorRepository.java:527, the OLD two-call upsert path.

The 7.5.0 ChunkBatcher path no longer goes there. CombinedWriteService does its OWN existence-partition (Phase 2a, lines 139-156: it builds needEmbedIdx and textsToEmbed, embedding only chashes whose stored text differs). This is the nexus-vw594 shape exactly: a gate patched at a seam the code no longer takes.

## The part that makes this P1 rather than a gate-only bug

CombinedWriteService emits NO LOG LINES AT ALL. Verified: `grep -nE "log\.(info|warn|debug|error)" CombinedWriteService.java` returns NOTHING. There is also no skipped/embedded count in its response envelope (the response carries chunks_written and sweep_detail, not embed accounting).

So the combined-write existence-partition is COMPLETELY UNOBSERVABLE. We cannot distinguish, from any artifact the running system produces:
  (a) the skip works correctly and silently, gate is merely blind; from
  (b) the skip is NOT firing and every warm reindex re-embeds unchanged chunks.
(b) costs real embedding spend on every reindex and would be invisible indefinitely. "known chashes never re-embedded" is called a HARD REQUIREMENT in the class own javadoc (RDR-181, design memo section 0) — and nothing measures it.

## NOT established

Whether this gate passed before 7.5.0. It is an S6 shakedown surface, not part of the release battery, so there is no recent baseline in hand. Do not assume this is a 7.5.0 regression OR that it is pre-existing until someone runs it against a pre-7.5.0 tree. (Note the tree/engine pairing confound that bit nexus-b32rx: v7.4.0 pins engine v0.1.68.)

## Asks, in order

1. Make the combined-write existence-partition observable: emit a structured line carrying skipped/embedded counts per call, or add the counts to the write_many response envelope. Without this nothing can gate it.
2. Repoint warm-reindex-skip-gate.sh at whatever evidence (1) produces, so it measures the path production actually takes. Do NOT just widen the grep — confirm the new signal is emitted on the ChunkBatcher path specifically.
3. MEASURE the detector against a deliberately broken fix: force-disable the existence-partition and confirm the repointed gate goes RED. A gate that has never been shown to fail is not a gate.
4. Determine empirically whether (a) or (b) is true on 7.5.0 today — this is the user-facing question and it is currently open.

Related: nexus-vw594 (same moved-seam shape, same release), nexus-33hpq (the combined-write cap work), nexus-97dp4 (gate fixture too small to bind), nexus-b32rx (version-pairing confound).
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: engine 2b0c59085 emits event=combined_write_embed_partition + envelope counts; gate repointed and proven fail-capable (9433cbdb9); engine-version guard added (ce4dfee9b) — warm-reindex-skip-gate.sh now greps the live event

title: UNEXPLAINED: v7.4.0 survives the onnx-local blowup at the same 300 cap that wedges v7.5.0 — cause not isolated (engine version is a confound)

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Filed from substantive-critic review of the uncommitted client-side fix (worktree agent-ad4a18a410c1c300f: src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py, tests/db/test_http_vector_client.py, CHANGELOG.md). Two findings not yet tracked anywhere:

1. PERMANENT-RECORD ACCURACY. The new docstring and the new CHANGELOG entry both assert: "the v7.5.0 combined write started routing every local-mode chunk batch through one uninterrupted, non-sub-batched Bge768Embedder.embedBatch() call" as the trigger for the blowup. This is the SAME causal claim nexus-33hpq's own 2026-08-09 21:20 comment explicitly RETRACTED ("Point 2 of the causal chain said 7.5.0 moved local embedding from client to engine. That is FALSE... Both shapes therefore deliver the same <=300-chunk batch to Bge768Embedder.embedBatch() in ONE forward pass"). The diff was authored/finalized without reconciling this — it restates the retracted framing as settled fact in two permanent artifacts (a docstring and a shipped CHANGELOG entry), which is a direct instance of the standing directive against writing an inference into a permanent record as fact.

   Compounding this: per the user's own bisection (not yet in the bead) — v7.4.0 at the SAME 300 cap reaches only ~30 GB, v7.5.0 at the SAME 300 cap reaches 77.4 GB. A real, unexplained 7.5.0-specific delta exists. Neither the docstring's linear single-datapoint model (calibrated ONLY on the 77.4 GB/batch=300 point) nor the "pre-existing, not 7.5.0-introduced" framing in the bead's retraction account for this. The cap-of-16 fix may suppress the SYMPTOM without the underlying mechanism being understood — capping batch size helps IF the delta scales with batch size, but is neutral-to-harmful if the delta scales with REQUEST COUNT instead (e.g. a retry-storm pattern: the bead's own symptom log shows manifest_write_transient_error_retry / ReadTimeout during the wedge, and no synchronization/serialization was found in Bge768Embedder.java or CombinedWriteService.java that would prevent an abandoned client-timed-out request from continuing to run server-side while a retry starts a second one). Recommend: run the v7.4.0-vs-v7.5.0 bisection to a real conclusion before treating "pre-existing, timeout-vs-memory mismatch" as settled, and soften the docstring/CHANGELOG causal language to match what is actually established.

2. MEMORY BUDGET IGNORES KNOWN CONCURRENCY. The new docstring derives "16" from a SINGLE-flush arithmetic (batch=16 -> ~4.13 GB peak, "~1 GB headroom on a 16 GB machine"). But nx index repo's ChunkBatcher (indexer.py:4195-4204, same function the new docstring cross-references for _cap_for) is constructed with flush_concurrency=3 — "3 concurrent flushes: inside the 10-concurrent-writes per-collection service quota with headroom" (indexer.py comment, unchanged by this diff). No serialization/lock was found in Bge768Embedder.java gating concurrent embedBatch() calls, and no bulkhead/concurrency throttle was found in CombinedWriteService.java. If 3 flushes (potentially spanning different collections, since ONE ChunkBatcher instance serves the whole repo-index run) land on the engine concurrently, worst-case transient peak could approach 3x the single-flush figure the budget was set against — eating most or all of the claimed headroom on exactly the machine profile (16 GB laptop) the docstring cites as the target. The docstring should either account for flush_concurrency in the budget arithmetic, or the two numbers (per-collection cap, flush concurrency) should be co-tuned with a stated combined worst case.

3. MINOR: the arithmetic itself doesn't cleanly justify 16. 300 * 5/77.4 ~= 19.4; the docstring rounds this DOWN to 16 citing a second, unrelated justification ("quarter of the old 64 CCE cap" — an unrelated Voyage-timeout-derived number) rather than 19 (the actual round-down of the derived figure). The number is a round aesthetic choice with the memory arithmetic stapled on after the fact, not a value that flows cleanly from the stated derivation. Also: no minimum-RAM spec exists anywhere in README/docs — "16 GB machine" is an unstated assumption invented for this budget, not an anchored support target.

Context: full critique returned to the dispatching session; see T2 project memory "nexus" for the complete write-up (title "critique-33hpq-client-cap-2026-08-09").

Docstring and CHANGELOG no longer claim v7.5.0 moved embedding server-side; both now correctly state the one-pass embed shape predates v7.5.0, citing upsert_chunks_with_embeddings' own docstring (verified directly: 'Server-side embed path: forward chunk text, ignore caller's embeddings' — src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1451). comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THE PLAN OF RECORD, 2026-08-10. Filed as a comment rather than a new bead
because it corrects an assumption in THIS bead's experiment design, not a separate defect.

Source: T2 [22174] `nexus/local-index-memory-gate-first-run-2026-08-10`, the first-ever real
execution of `tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`.

## First, the headline: NOTHING was measured

Both requested runs (`--cap 300` and `--cap 16`) aborted at step 3/6 with
`ERROR: service never became healthy`. No verdict line, no JSON line, no peak_gb. The
timeout hypothesis is **[NE] NOT ESTABLISHED** — do not record any conclusion about it from
that session. Root cause filed as nexus-wbeyi.

## The correction: a `--cap 300` run of this gate would NOT have been a near-single-variable test

The plan assumed running this gate at cap=300 would isolate the timeout hypothesis. It would
not have, and this is independent of the crash.

Per nexus-c7fht: the gate's corpus is all **oversize** files, so
`chunk_batcher.py:255-260` refuses every one of them (`len(ids) > cap -> return False`) and
routes them to the LEGACY per-file paged upload. The gate therefore exercises a DIFFERENT
code path from the one the 77.4 GB recording ran.

Enumerated differences vs the 77.4 GB recording ([E] = established unless marked):

1. **Code path** — legacy `/v1/vectors/upsert-chunks` here vs combined
   `/v1/catalog/manifest/write_many` in the recording.
2. **Timeout** — `timeout=600` on the legacy path (`http_vector_client.py:1505`), which is
   also what it was BEFORE 7.5.0. Unchanged. **Commits `127f2dbc` and `47c5a39a` are
   therefore INERT on the path this gate exercises.**
3. **Retry** — the legacy classifier at `http_vector_client.py:871-874` catches only
   `(URLError, ConnectionRefusedError, ConnectionResetError)`, with an explicit in-code
   comment: "TimeoutError is intentionally NOT in this retry classifier". No retry storm is
   available on this path at all.
4. **Concurrency** — the recording ran `flush_concurrency=3` (`indexer.py:4299`); this
   corpus (oversize files + 1 tiny) is effectively sequential.
5. **Batch size** — at cap=300 this gate sends 300 chunks in one embed vs the recording's
   ~82 (code) / ~28 (docs); per nexus-97dp4 the cap never bound in the original either.
   With `MAX_SEQ_LEN=512` saturated (~266 median whitespace tokens/chunk measured, so
   wordpiece >> 512) the attention working set is ~3.7x the original's largest batch. **[I]**
6. **Corpus** — 1 synthetic oversize file (+scale) vs 36 real mixed files across `code__`
   and `docs__`.
7. **Tree** — a7553c88 carries `_contain_transient_upsert` on the code path (nexus-nn6vb),
   absent from the recording.

**Design consequence:** a LOW peak from this gate would NOT have discriminated "retry storm"
from "no amplifiers present in this corpus shape", because on the legacy path there is no
30s timeout, no timeout-retry, and no concurrency to storm with. Testing the timeout
hypothesis requires a corpus of **many files each BELOW the cap**, so ChunkBatcher
accumulates to the cap and the combined write is the path under test. That is a
corpus-shape change to the gate (nexus-c7fht), not a flag — `--corpus-scale N` adds more
OVERSIZE files and scales the wrong axis.

## One thing that IS resolved

**Engine version is not a confound in this harness.** This tree and the 77.4 GB run are
both on engine v0.1.69, so the v0.1.68-vs-v0.1.69 confound named in this bead's 2026-08-09
scope-narrowing comment is absent HERE.

That does not resolve it for the ORIGINAL recording, which remains the confounded
comparison this bead exists to untangle. A clean answer still needs a single-variable run
(same client, both engines — or both clients, same engine).

Blocked on: nexus-wbeyi (gate cannot run at all), nexus-c7fht (gate cannot exercise the
relevant path). The recommended experiment in T2
`assess-local-index-cluster-2026-08-10` Q4 is untouched by this run and remains the right
one.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
[E] EXPERIMENT DESIGN IS UNSOUND — DO NOT RUN IT AS SPECIFIED (2026-08-10)

Filed as a comment, not a new bead: this corrects THIS bead's own experiment
design, it is not a separate defect. Source: T2 [22181]
`nexus/local-index-memory-gate-run-post-repair` — the SECOND failed attempt to
run `tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`. Reading is still **[NE] NOT
ESTABLISHED**, second session running: no memory datapoint exists.

The design recorded for this bead is unsound on TWO INDEPENDENT counts. Either
one alone invalidates the result.

## 1. The 20 GB RSS ceiling CENSORS the measurement

A `--rss-ceiling 20` run can only ever report "peak > 20 GB" (verdict KILLED)
or "peak <= 20 GB". The two competing hypotheses are:

  - retry storm responsible:  ~30 GB drove the escalation to 77.4 GB
  - retries irrelevant:       ~77 GB is the workload's intrinsic cost

**Both exceed 20 GB.** A KILLED verdict is therefore consistent with BOTH and
discriminates neither. Any interpretation band of the form "KILLED => memory-
driven independent of retries" is INVALID under censoring and must not be
applied to a run of this shape.

## 2. cap=300 is NOT the original workload

The 77.4 GB recording's cap NEVER BOUND — its observed batches were ~82 (code)
and ~28 (docs); see nexus-97dp4, which exists precisely because the fixture is
too small for the cap to bind. A cap=300 run sends 300-chunk batches, roughly
**3.7x the attention working set** of the original's largest batch (with
MAX_SEQ_LEN=512 saturated, attention is O(batch * heads * seq^2)).

So a peak >= 77.4 GB at cap=300 would NOT show "retries were irrelevant". It
would show only that a bigger workload costs more. This is not a
single-variable comparison against the recording.

## Design consequence

A valid experiment for this bead needs BOTH:

  - **~82-chunk batches, not 300** — i.e. a corpus of many files each BELOW the
    cap so ChunkBatcher accumulates to ~82, reproducing the recording's actual
    batch shape. (Note this also requires nexus-c7fht: the current corpus is
    all-oversize files, which fall off the combined-write path entirely, and
    `--corpus-scale N` adds more OVERSIZE files, scaling the wrong axis.)
  - **no ceiling, or a ceiling ABOVE both hypotheses** (i.e. > ~80 GB), so the
    verdict can discriminate rather than censor.

## Remaining deltas vs the 77.4 GB recording, for whoever runs this next

  - **Engine version**: v0.1.69 on BOTH sides in this harness. The
    v0.1.68-vs-v0.1.69 confound named in this bead's 2026-08-09 scope-narrowing
    comment is ABSENT HERE — but it is NOT RESOLVED for the original bisect.
  - **flush_concurrency = 3**: present on both sides.
  - **Corpus**: synthetic uniform filler here vs 36 real mixed files spanning
    `code__` and `docs__` in the recording.
  - **Tree**: this tree carries `_contain_transient_upsert` (nexus-nn6vb),
    absent from the recording.

## The non-vacuity assert is UNTESTED, not passing

The `cap NEVER BOUND` assert (`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:265-266`,
inside `_verdict`) has now been UNREACHED on a real run TWICE — both attempts
died at step 3/6, and `_emit_json` lives at step 6/6.

Precision correction to the source memo: the assert is NOT wholly unexercised —
`--self-test` drives that branch with SYNTHETIC arguments (`:408`, and
`_largest_flush_in_log` is unit-covered at `:325-342`). What has never happened
is the assert running against a REAL measured `largest_flush` from a real run.
That is the coverage that matters, and it is the same "verified everywhere
except in situ" shape that let both health-poll defects (nexus-wbeyi, and now
nexus-cwc8w) ship past a green self-test.

## Blocking defects filed from this run

  - nexus-f93r1 (P1, PRODUCT) — `nx <cmd> --json` emits a structlog warning on
    STDOUT at import time whenever `NX_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP` is set.
  - nexus-cwc8w (P2, gate) — the health poll cannot parse a payload with a
    prepended log line; aborts at 3/6 against a healthy service.
  - nexus-9dua3 (P2, gate) — that poll swallows the parse error into
    `print("")`, a silent fallback on a correctness decision.
  - nexus-0ovk0 (P3) — the gate builds its wheel from a moving tree; no run
    records the SHA or dirty-file list, so any future measurement's provenance
    is ambiguous.

title: engine: Bge768Embedder.embedBatch has no sub-batching — a large client POST is one ONNX forward pass and can OOM the engine
description:
Option B of nexus-33hpq (Hal chose C: client cap now, this on the next engine cut). MUST NOT ship as the only fix — pair with the client-side cap.

## Defect

service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/Bge768Embedder.java: embed() calls embedBatch(texts) directly. embedBatch pads the whole batch to a RECTANGULAR [batchSize, maxLen] tensor (.optPadding(false) at :144, maxLen = min(longest, MAX_SEQ_LEN=512) at :192) and runs ONE session.run(). ONNX attention is O(batch * heads * seq^2), so peak memory scales linearly in the client-chosen batch size with a very large constant.

EmbedderRouter does not sub-batch either (no subList/partition; it passes texts straight through). So NOTHING between the HTTP boundary and the ONNX session bounds the batch. Both /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks and the RDR-181 combined write (CombinedWriteService, "in ONE batch call") inherit this.

## Measured

batch=300, seq=512: 3.77 GB per attention tensor, 0.47 GB last_hidden_state. Observed peak 77.4 GB RSS with ~15 cores pegged on a 36-file corpus, taking the service so far into thrash that /livez went unanswerable and the supervisor stuck-exited (pg_ok stayed true throughout).
batch=64, seq=512: 0.81 GB per attention tensor.

## Why this is the ENGINE half

A client is allowed to send a big POST. The engine deciding to turn that into a single unbounded allocation is the engine trusting a caller-supplied size with no ceiling of its own. A client-side cap fixes THIS product today; it does not stop any other client, an older client, or a future caller from doing the same thing. Defense in depth belongs here.

## Ask

Sub-batch inside embedBatch (or in CombinedWriteService/EmbedderRouter before the embed call) so an oversize request degrades in THROUGHPUT, not memory. Size the internal sub-batch from a memory budget (batch * heads * seq^2), not from a request-count constant. Consider also bounding by total tokens rather than row count, since one long chunk inflates every padded row in its batch.

## Test that would catch it

An engine test that POSTs a large chunk batch of long texts and asserts peak RSS stays under a budget, or at minimum asserts the embedder issues >1 ONNX invocation above a threshold batch size. Non-vacuity: it must go red if the sub-batching is removed.

Parent: nexus-33hpq (see its CORRECTION comment — the blowup is PRE-EXISTING, not 7.5.0-introduced).
close_reason: Shipped and delivered: Bge768Embedder sub-batches internally on a padded-token-area budget (16*512^2, generalized from the 33hpq verified-safe point; a long chunk closes its own group instead of inflating every row). Red/green non-vacuity proven at implementation (invocation-count assert red under a reverted budget). Shipped engine-service-v0.1.81 (2026-08-19, full battery), deployed to cloud in v0.1.83 with STEP-6 gate PASS, delivered to local installs via the 7.12.0 floor bump (0,1,83). Paired client cap (33hpq option C) live since 7.5.0 — both halves of the 77.4GB class closed; the class's causal chain now fully documented at nexus-b32rx close (T2 [22949]). Residual engine edge (cancellation/admission) = nexus-0o76a. Marker T2 [22950].

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: W0 (the client-degradation precondition for the v0.1.70 design) completed 2026-08-10 — T2 [22168] nexus/engine-w0-503-client-degradation. Verdict: 503 is the correct status code, keep it; no RDR-181 atomicity violation (an embed-step failure means writeManifestMany is never called, so zero per-doc transactions open). Three beads filed from it: nexus-nn6vb (P1, BLOCKS W5 — uncontained code-file path aborts the run on a 5xx), nexus-00ez4 (P2, ChunkBatcher bisect multiplies status-coded transients by 2F-1), nexus-a3tko (P2, design §0.3's '503 is not retried [E]' is false; ADMISSION_WAIT_MS was sized on it).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Implementation landed (developer dispatch, 2026-08-18): Bge768Embedder now sub-batches internally.

## Design
- Bge768Embedder.embed() -> embedSubBatched(): tokenizes the whole input ONCE (cheap vs an ONNX forward pass), then greedily partitions into sub-batches IN ORDER (no sort/reorder needed) bounded by a padded-token-area budget: groupSize * maxLen^2 <= MAX_PADDED_TOKEN_AREA. A long chunk simply forces its own group to close sooner -- it can never inflate every OTHER row's padding cost, unlike the flat 300-row cap that caused the original 77.4GB blowup.
- Each group -> one runOnnxSubBatch() call (the sole session.run() invocation point, instrumented via a package-private AtomicInteger onnxInvocationCount for tests).
- Budget derivation: MAX_PADDED_TOKEN_AREA = 16 * 512^2 (4,194,304) -- reuses the nexus-33hpq VERIFIED-SAFE operating point (batch=16 @ full 512-token cap measured 3.03GB peak RSS w/ flush_concurrency=3 active, release-sandbox shakedown 11/11), generalized from "16 rows" to "16*512^2 units of padded-token-area" so any batch/length combo reaching the same area gets the same ceiling. ATTENTION_HEADS=12 confirmed against the measured numbers in this bead's own description (64*12*512*512*4 bytes = 805,306,368 = 0.81GB, exact match).
- Placement: inside Bge768Embedder itself (not EmbedderRouter/CombinedWriteService), per the bead's "defense in depth" argument -- the embedder owns the ceiling regardless of caller.
- Whole-batch-under-budget case degrades to exactly one group / one ONNX call -- identical to the pre-existing single-shot behavior (the "fast path" is the general algorithm's 1-iteration case, no separate code path needed).

## Non-vacuity (RED/GREEN), demonstrated 2026-08-18
Added Bge768BatchCompositionTest.oversizeBatch_internalSubBatching_multipleInvocations_outputsMatchSingles: drives embed() with a 20-row near-512-token batch (padded-token-area 20*512^2=5,242,880 > budget 4,194,304), asserts embedder.onnxInvocationCount() > 1, and cross-checks output parity against embedOne() per row (cosine > 1-1e-6).

- GREEN (real code): mvn -Dtest=Bge768BatchCompositionTest test -> 4/4 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failures.
- RED demo: temporarily set MAX_ATTENTION_TENSOR_BYTES = Long.MAX_VALUE (planner never splits) in a SCRATCH edit only (never staged/committed, reverted before re-running) -> same test FAILED exactly on the invocation-count assertion: "Expecting actual: 1 to be greater than: 1". Cosine assertions stayed green (single-group output unchanged), confirming the assertion isolates the sub-batching mechanism specifically, not a false positive from something else breaking.
- Reverted, re-ran GREEN again to confirm clean state: 4/4, 0 skipped.

## Files
- service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/Bge768Embedder.java
- service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/Bge768BatchCompositionTest.java (+javadoc update)

## Test results (scoped, not full suite)
Bge768BatchCompositionTest 4/4, Bge768ParityTest 4/4, Bge768EmbedderMathTest 4/4, EmbedderRouterBge768Test 6/6, Bge768ServiceEmbedIntegrationTest (integration group) 2/2, EmbedderRouterVoyageOnlyTest 6/6, PgVectorRepositoryContractTest 65/65 -- all green, 0 skipped. scripts/build-gate-jar.sh rebuilt successfully.

title: owes-report credit slot orphaned by a SubagentStop timeout kill permanently burns credit -> silent miss (nexus-7z7rj round-3 residual)
description:
CRITIQUE FINDING (substantive-critic, 2026-08-09) on nexus-7z7rj round 3 (a7cc2752).
Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-7z7rj-round3-2026-08-09 [22111].

Round 3 replaced lock-decided credit with an atomic slot symlink claim. The CEILING is
now genuinely kernel-enforced (independently re-verified: 40/40 exact with the lock
disabled; pre-fix logic 20/20 violate under the same adversary). But the DEFERRED-MISS
property that made 7z7rj P1 is NOT closed - it is re-introduced by a new route.

MECHANISM: expectations_owes_report claims a slot (ln -s, external binary) and THEN
appends the CONSUMED row (_expectations_append, a subshell fork). A process death in
that window leaves an ORPHAN SLOT: a permanent credit debit with NO ledger row.

REPRODUCED (scratchpad/orphan_probe.sh, calling _expectations_claim_credit with exactly
the arguments owes_report passes): credit=4, one orphan slot, then 4 genuine background
agents -> 3 blocked, the 4th told "does not owe" and STOPS UNBLOCKED, with the ledger
still reading 3 CONSUMED of credit 4 and zero BLOCKED rows for it. Identical RDR-184
silent-miss class the fix targets.

REACHABILITY IS NOT THEORETICAL: conexus/hooks/hooks.json gives SubagentStop a 10s
timeout, while NX_EXPECT_LOCK_TRIES is 200 in CI (20s) and clamps at 600 (60s). The
harness SIGKILLs this hook as a routine, load-correlated event in exactly the contention
regime this bead lives in.

REGRESSION vs pre-fix: pre-fix, a kill in that window wrote nothing and cost ONE
unblocked stop. Post-fix the same kill costs that stop AND permanently burns a credit,
so a SECOND future same-type agent also slips. Round 3 doubles the damage of a
timeout kill here.

OBSERVABILITY REGRESSION: the old spurious debit was a visible CONSUMED row (census
could see consumed>credit). The new one is a symlink no audit surface reads -
census/undeclared never look at slots. The docstring's "slots are derived state; the
CONSUMED rows are the durable record" is false in the direction that matters:
reconciliation flows rows->slots only, never slots->rows, so a slot with no row is
unreconcilable and unobservable.

CLAIM TO RETRACT: "a spurious debit can no longer be written at all" (commit message,
T2 22096, conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md) is true of ROWS and false of DEBITS. Same shape
as rounds 1-2's "mechanical invariant".

FIX (~6 lines, matches round 2's own precedent and the standing no-silent-fallbacks
directive): in the `new` branch, when the claim is LOST while credit > spent, the state
is provably inconsistent (slots claim more consumption than the durable ledger records).
Return 0 (BLOCK) with EXPECTATIONS_OWES_CAUSE="credit-slot-orphan" instead of returning
1 silently - fail-closed and disclosed, exactly like "lock-exhausted". Do NOT add a
bounded-age orphan reclaim: that is the check-then-act shape round 3 correctly refuses.

TEST OWED (this is the falsifier round 3 lacks): kill a claimant between the slot claim
and the CONSUMED append, then assert a subsequent genuine same-type agent is still
blocked. Nothing in tests/hooks/ models this today; the new
test_owes_report_credit_claim_survives_a_lock_that_grants_no_exclusion proves the
ceiling under zero mutual exclusion, which is a different property.

BLOCKS: closing nexus-7z7rj.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED at fc066671 (worktree-agent-a5af5eb2a64da3769, base develop f145f3de, not pushed).

CONFIRMED THE DECISIVE FACT FIRST: conexus/hooks/hooks.json gives SubagentStop timeout=10 (verified by parsing the file, not by reading the diff). Lock budget is 20s in CI and clamps at 60s. So the harness SIGKILLs this hook as a routine, load-correlated event, in exactly the contention regime the credit mechanism exists for. The critic is right that every round's 'needs an external kill in a fork+exec window, i.e. rare' reasoning was wrong.

FIX: a lost claim is no longer a silent return 1. Losing means either (a) the pool genuinely went dry between our read and our claim, or (b) a previous claimant was killed between its ln -s and its CONSUMED row. They are distinguishable by RE-READING: in (b) every slot is taken while the rows still say credit remains — provably inconsistent. That state now returns 0 (BLOCK) with EXPECTATIONS_OWES_CAUSE='credit-slot-orphan'.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE PRESCRIPTION, deliberate and verified: the bare form ('lost claim while credit > spent -> block') would over-block EVERY normal contention loser, because the comparison would use the racer's ORIGINAL pre-claim read. With 8 racers and 4 credits that is 4 spurious orphan-blocks per fleet stop, which would make the new cause fire constantly and become noise an operator learns to ignore. The re-read is what makes the condition actually mean 'inconsistent'. It runs twice, 0.1s apart, because a winner that has claimed but not yet appended is indistinguishable from an orphan for those microseconds. This is a READ retry, NOT the bounded-age orphan reclaim you excluded — nothing is deleted or stolen, so it cannot reintroduce the check-then-act shape.

ALSO DONE: the set -u hazard round 3 introduced (read -a on empty input yields a ZERO-element array; ${vfields[0]} then fatal) is guarded.

DETECTORS — both measured against deliberately broken fixes:
- Ceiling detector: was 1 false pass in 12 (reviewer). NX_EXPECT_CLAIM_DELAY_S now forces every racer to read the same state before any racer claims. Re-measured 0/90 (30 + 60 trials). At the 8.3% baseline, p ~= 0.0004.
- Orphan detector (new; nothing in the suite covered this before): SIGKILLs a racer between claim and append via NX_EXPECT_APPEND_DELAY_S, asserts the orphan exists (slot present, no row), requires the next agent to block with the disclosed cause. 0/30 false passes against the silent-return-1 version.
- Both pass against the good lib, so neither is vacuous. 354 passed in tests/hooks/.

FINDING WORTH KEEPING: a hook killed mid-claim orphans its LOCKDIR as well as its slot, so for ~60s later stops of that type block with cause=lock-exhausted and the stale lock MASKS the orphaned slot. The orphan only becomes a silent miss after the 60s reap clears the mask. The permanent test models that steady state explicitly rather than the first minute.

RESIDUAL, stated plainly and reflected in PENDING_RELEASE.md + T2 [22096]: the orphaned slot is still never reclaimed within a session. Over-count is closed at the source; under-count is narrowed and now DISCLOSED but live. Not claiming this one is 'mechanically' closed — that phrasing is what rounds 1, 2 and 3 each shipped on.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CLOSED at develop harvest 2026-08-09 (worktree fc066671 -> ae13a715). A lost claim while rows still say credit remains is now a BLOCK with EXPECTATIONS_OWES_CAUSE='credit-slot-orphan', not a silent return 1. Critic VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, re-running its own original falsifier against the fixed lib: the agent that previously stopped unblocked with zero ledger trace now blocks with the disclosed cause. The prescribed bare form was deliberately DEVIATED from (re-read, twice, 0.1s apart) because the bare form compares against the racer's pre-claim read and would over-block every contention loser — 4 spurious blocks per 8-racer fleet stop, which would have turned the new cause into noise. Critic adjudicated the deviation SOUND AND BETTER than its prescription: it mutates nothing, so it structurally cannot reintroduce the check-then-act class it excluded. False-positive window MEASURED: winner stalling 0.5s between ln -s and append = 12/12 false cause; 0.05s = 0/12; tolerance is exactly the 0.1s recheck spacing, and no MISS is introduced because spent and credit both only grow.

title: two fail-open-to-GREEN surfaces in the upgrade-ladder health path degrade together: health.py _check_pending_rungs returns ok=True on any exception (regression of the exact bug runner.pending_rungs' docstring says was fixed), and upgrade_finish.pending_data_rung_callout swallows a raising detect() as not-pending
description:
Found by a codebase-wide sweep for the 'asserts on absence of a negative signal' shape, run as the sibling-check for nexus-hdumg (2026-08-09). TWO HIGH findings that are NOT independent — the second one's named backstop is the first, so both degrade at once.
(1) src/nexus/health.py:3528-3531 — _check_pending_rungs' blanket handler returns HealthResult(label='Upgrade ladder', ok=True, detail='check failed (non-critical)'). This is a REGRESSION of a bug already fixed once: upgrade_ladder/runner.py:69-101's pending_rungs docstring quotes that exact string as the thing it fixed. The inner per-rung leak was closed; this OUTER handler was not. It still fires on failures above the loop (deferred imports, default_registry() -> default_chash_rekey_rung() construction, registry.py:172-182). ok=True renders as a green check (health.py:82), so a box whose ladder cannot even be ENUMERATED shows a clean Upgrade-ladder row in nx doctor.
(2) src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:1526-1531 — pending_data_rung_callout does except Exception: continue. A raising detect() becomes indistinguishable from 'not pending', silently deleting the chash-rekey PENDING warning — the one whose own comment says citations for pre-existing content silently break without it. Direct contrast: runner.pending_rungs converts the SAME failure into PENDING-with-reason.
FIX: (1) ok=False + warn=True + include the exception text; (2) emit an UNKNOWN/unavailable line instead of continue. Roughly 6 lines total. TEST REQUIREMENT: pin the OUTER handler, not just runner.pending_rungs — the existing test coverage is what let the regression back in. Same class as nexus-hdumg (the rung declaring verified after its diagnostic failed) and RDR-182's never-a-silent-all-clean design.
close_reason: Shipped on develop: commit 3e2a5317c (both surfaces: health._check_pending_rungs ok=False+warn+exc text; pending_data_rung_callout explicit unknown line) plus follow-on b87fca9bc guarding registry construction. Tests pin the OUTER handler per the acceptance bar: tests/upgrade/test_ladder_surfaces.py::test_doctor_check_is_crash_proof and tests/test_upgrade_finish.py detect()-raise tests.

title: upgrade ladder declares a rung 'converged and verified' after its conformance diagnostic FAILED to execute — diag_sql_failed on missing nexus.diag_chash_conformance, then chash-rekey verified anyway
description: Reported by conexus from the v0.1.69 deploy rehearsal (relay T2 conexus/[22070] + [22073], both flagged it untraced). During the upgrade ladder: event='diag_sql_failed' — relation \"nexus.diag_chash_conformance\" does not exist (statement: SELECT sum(non_conformant) ... table_name='nexus.chunks_384') — and the NEXT log line reported \"Upgrade ladder: rung 'chash-rekey' converged and verified\". A conformance diagnostic that could not run did not prevent the rung from declaring verification. DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS RDR-182's stated design (diagnostics unavailable degrades to an EXPLICIT unavailable note, never a silent all-clean) and the standing no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness directive. Questions to answer: (1) is the missing relation itself a defect (should nexus.diag_chash_conformance exist post-RDR-182/P2.1, or is absence legitimate on this install shape)? (2) regardless of (1), does the rung's verify path treat a failed diagnostic as pass-through — i.e. is 'verified' asserted on the ABSENCE of a non-conformance signal rather than the PRESENCE of a conformance signal (vacuous-verification class)? Fix direction: a rung whose verification query cannot execute must report unavailable/failed, never converged+verified. Reproduce from the rehearsal path; falsify by dropping the relation and asserting the rung refuses. Related: RDR-182, nexus-vounk (diag choke point).
close_reason: Fixed on develop and shipping in 7.5.0: 84e5a662 (a rung whose conformance diagnostic cannot run is NEVER converged+verified — ChashRekeyRung.verify() no longer asserts on ABSENCE of a bad signal; unmeasurable => VERIFY_FAILED, position pinned, nx upgrade exits non-zero) + 758e4c5f (corrected blast-radius claim, split the unmeasurable-store remedy by arm). Loud chash_rekey_probe_view_fallback_legacy warning added so the view-absent -> legacy-fallback -> measured sequence is readable AS a fallback rather than as the original bug. Verified during the 7.5.0 release battery: fresh-install-mvv shows diag_sql_failed on the absent view, the documented legacy fallback, a real measurement, and the ladder correctly advancing. Both halves dual-reviewed, CI green. Bead close was missed at land time; closing now during the release cut.

title: stranded-install de-strand signal is tenant-scoped not install-scoped — cross-machine false de-strand in managed/cloud mode
description:
Found during substantive-critique of nexus-4922x (commit e6d7a1fb, T2 critique
id 22009). The de-strand fix's new PRIMARY signal
(nexus.config._ladder_migration_verified -> HttpLadderStore().verified_rungs())
checks whether rung "substrate-etl" was EVER recorded for the resolved
(tenant, engine) pair -- nothing ties the completion fact to the SPECIFIC
pre-PG artifact files found on THIS machine's disk, and it is wired
unconditionally at all four call sites (health.py, cli.py, mcp/_first_run.py,
commands/init.py) with zero is_local_mode() gating.

The fix's own docstring rationale ("the SAME local PG database serves both
the pin and the current release across a package-only up/downgrade") only
holds for single-machine local mode. In managed/cloud mode (or any reuse of
the same account/tenant across two machines), a user who migrated on
machine A gets verified_rungs() returning the rung for machine B too, the
instant B is pointed at the same engine/tenant -- even if B carries its OWN,
distinct, never-migrated pre-PG Chroma data. B silently de-strands without
that data ever having reached PG -- the exact silent-data-loss-shaped
failure this detector exists to prevent.

This is narrower/broader than the old file-based _has_verified_migration_report
check in an important way: the old check required an actual local file copy
on THIS machine; the new primary signal is reached by nothing more than
being logged into the same cloud account from a different machine.

Recommendation (either):
(a) gate the ladder-based primary signal to is_local_mode() only, leaving
    managed/cloud mode on the legacy-report check (or a to-be-designed
    managed-mode-appropriate signal), or
(b) bind the completion record to something artifact-identifying (a hash of
    the discovered pre-PG file set, or the config-dir's own identity) rather
    than a bare tenant-wide boolean.

Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-4922x-destrand-2026-08-09 [22009].
Context: nx
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ADJUDICATED (developer, 2026-08-09), commit 355a4154 stacked on e6d7a1fb.

Cloud/managed mode: probe is NEVER called (call-counting test, not just untrusted) -- falls back to the exact pre-nexus-4922x legacy-report-only behavior.

comments.text:

comments.text:
