title: kl2z6 combined write: sweep gate keyed on doc's own physical_collection, not the request's chunkCollection — TOCTOU on mustAlreadyExist chashes
description:
Review of commit ec42b531 (nexus-kl2z6 engine increment 1, the COMBINED WRITE) found a Critical
atomicity gap. See T2 nexus/review-kl2z6-engine-increment1-2026-08-09 [21988] Critical C1 for the
full trace.

CatalogRepository.writeManifestRows (new 7-arg overload, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java:3784-3827):
acquires the sweep gate SHARED on `coll` (physicalCollectionOf(ctx, tenant, docId) — the doc's OWN
registered physical_collection, which can be null for an unregistered/"ghost" doc), NOT on
`chunkCollection` (the combined-write request's top-level `collection`, which is what
upsertManifestChunkVectors actually writes chunks_<dim> rows into). When coll is null or differs
from chunkCollection, the new chunk-vector upsert — specifically its `mustAlreadyExist` existence
check, a plain SELECT with no row lock — runs unprotected by the sweep gate, reopening a real
window where a concurrent sweep can delete a chash between this transaction's existence check and
its commit, landing a manifest row that references a chash with no corresponding chunk row. This
is exactly the hazard nexus-kl2z6 exists to close.

None of the 7 new CombinedWriteRepositoryTest tests exercise this — registerDoc() always stamps
physical_collection to the same value as chunkCollection, so the mismatch never triggers.

Fix: gate on chunkCollection unconditionally when resolvedChunks != null (closes the TOCTOU
structurally), or at minimum fail loud on coll != chunkCollection instead of silently gating on
the wrong key. Add a test: doc registered under collection A, combined-write called with
collection=B referencing a mustAlreadyExist chash concurrently dropped+swept by a sibling doc in
collection B — assert survival (mirrors 6a's shape, keyed on chunkCollection).

Blocks: nexus-kl2z6 increment 1 merge/tag until fixed and reverified.
notes: CONFIRMED-RESOLVED by commit 1b86be3b. Independently verified (not just trusted): (1) falsified the fix by reverting only the CatalogRepository.java gate-fix hunk and rerunning CombinedWriteRepositoryTest -- exactly the 2 new regression tests failed as predicted, confirming they prove gate IDENTITY not just 'some gate held'; (2) confirmed deadlock-safety of the 2-gate acquisition (both SHARED-mode advisory locks, architecturally cannot deadlock regardless of order); (3) confirmed the divergence-is-legal-not-400 semantics call is sound and consistent with Hal's binding constraint. 10/10 CombinedWriteRepositoryTest green post-fix, reproduced independently. Full delta review: T2 nexus/review-kl2z6-delta-2026-08-09-a-verdict [21994] + review-kl2z6-delta-2026-08-09-b-evidence [21995].

title: shared-cluster ALTER ROLE ... SET is cluster-wide, not database-scoped -- isolation-equivalence claim in SharedCluster.java is incomplete/incorrect and untested
description: substantive-critic finding on nexus-yhmav (per-fork PG container reuse, T2 [21931]). PostgreSQL's ALTER ROLE role SET param TO value (no IN DATABASE clause) writes to the shared/global pg_db_role_setting catalog (setdatabase=0), which is NOT copied or scoped by CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE -- it is genuinely cluster-wide, unlike ALTER DATABASE ... SET which SharedCluster.java's javadoc correctly documents as db-scoped. Repo-wide grep found ~90 test files executing 'ALTER ROLE nexus_svc SET search_path TO ...' (values diverge: 'nexus, public' vs 'nexus, t1, public' vs dynamic schema-variable forms) with zero IN DATABASE qualification. Empirically this self-heals today because every affected class re-issues its own ALTER ROLE immediately before opening its nexus_svc HikariDataSource pool, and surefire runs classes within a fork sequentially -- but this is an UNSTATED, UNTESTED, UNENFORCED ordering assumption, not the database-boundary isolation the design's safety argument claims. It is exactly the 'GUCs' risk category the parent bead's locked correctness-risk clause names explicitly. SharedClusterMutationFalsifyTest only proves table-ROW isolation (INSERT/SELECT via superuser on nexus.catalog_owners) -- it does not exercise role-level GUC state at all, so this gap has zero regression coverage. The suite's 4-category static sweep (GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE, bare CREATE ROLE, named-changelog Liquibase, bare CREATE TABLE) also would not have caught this -- it is a genuinely distinct 5th signature class. Additionally: CI (.github/workflows/service-ci.yml, -Dnexus.test.forks=1) does NOT set -Dnexus.test.pg.shared=false, so CI now runs the entire suite against ONE shared cluster by the code's own default -- a materially different isolation posture than the pre-yhmav per-class-fresh-container model, unexercised/unvalidated on GH runners per the implementer's own report.
design: Recommended fix: rewrite the ~90-occurrence ALTER ROLE boilerplate to ALTER ROLE nexus_svc IN DATABASE "<dbname>" SET search_path TO ... (pg.getDatabaseName() is already threaded through these bootstrap methods, same pattern SharedCluster already uses for ALTER DATABASE GUCs). This makes the pg_db_role_setting row genuinely per-database (setdatabase=<oid>, not 0), closing the cluster-wide leak at the root instead of relying on class-ordering self-healing. Add a falsification case to SharedClusterMutationFalsifyTest (or a sibling test) that sets a role-level GUC to a DISTINCT value in class/db A, then asserts a fresh clone's role-level default is NOT that value (mirrors the existing row-isolation falsify pattern).
close_reason: Fixed in 57ed3cce (same commit as yhmav): acquire-time RESET ALL of setdatabase=0 pg_db_role_setting rows in SharedCluster.acquireDatabase(); prescription swap from 90-site IN DATABASE rewrite ENDORSED by critic [21937] — seam-owned, covers future offenders. Virgin baseline verified (changelog has zero ALTER ROLE SET; production uses connectionInitSql). Falsify pair @Order(3)/(4) neuter-verified. Multi-acquire edge audited zero live instances + javadoc constraint; lint mechanization on rlgei.

title: Agent-tool isolation:worktree dispatch silently produced NO worktree — agent operated on the shared main tree believing itself isolated

FAILURE CLASS: silent isolation absence — worse than the known stale-base class (project_worktree_isolation_stale_base) because every shared-tree protection is assumed unnecessary inside a worktree. title: engine test suite is container-lifecycle-bound: amortize to per-fork PG container reuse (schema reset between classes, not container boot)
description: HAL-OBSERVED 2026-08-08 during the nexus-13eb0 parallel validation run: cpu/gpu/net barely registering while a 4-fork surefire full suite was actively mid-run — confirmed advancing (report XMLs streaming, PG containers cycling Up 5s/9s/10s). DIAGNOSIS: the suite's dominant cost is Docker container lifecycle, not compute — test classes boot fresh pgvector/pgvector:pg17 containers + apply Liquibase per class, and each fork spends most wall-clock waiting on container boot (host CPU idle = concurrency-constrained, not compute-constrained). FIX SHAPE: amortize to ONE PG container per surefire fork, reused across the fork's test classes, with a schema/database reset between classes (DROP/CREATE database, or template-database clone which is near-instant in PG, or Liquibase rollback-free re-apply onto a fresh database within the same cluster) instead of a full container boot. CORRECTNESS RISK to design against explicitly: state bleed between classes through the shared cluster (roles, extensions, GUCs, leftover databases, advisory locks) — the reset must be proven equivalent to a fresh container for the suite's assumptions, and any class that genuinely needs a virgin CLUSTER (e.g. asserts on cluster-wide state, tests bootstrap/grants) gets an opt-out annotation keeping its dedicated container, RawSqlGateTest-style sanctioned list with justifications. SEQUENCING: AFTER nexus-13eb0 lands (fork parallelism first — this bead multiplies its win); use 13eb0's timing table as the baseline. Evidence: 4 ryuk reapers (one per fork session) up 13min while containers churned at seconds-scale lifetimes; PgContainerHelper.newContainer() is the per-class boot site. Secondary knob if reuse proves too invasive: raise forkCount further — idle CPU shows headroom — but reuse attacks the actual dominant cost.
close_reason: Landed 57ed3cce: SharedCluster/SharedDatabaseHandle template-clone-per-class, one container per fork. Measured vs [21911] baseline: forks=4 1004s->271s (~73%), forks=8 crash->285s clean, forks=12 1081s->361s; pom default stays 4 (wall pinned by dedicated-container long pole ~180s). Opt-out roster 6 classes w/ justifications; mutation-falsify both row + role-GUC isolation (neuter-verified). Stacked gate: reviewer PASS, critic JUSTIFIED after tyiht rework [21937]. Report T2 [21931]. Follow-ons: rlgei (tripwires+lint+escape-hatch), jd36h (roster cost). Service CI validation on the pushed commit in flight (critic condition 1).

comments.text: PROMOTED P2->P1, follow-on -> PREREQUISITE, on nexus-13eb0's measured evidence (T2 [21911], 2026-08-08): full timing matrix shows fork scaling is DEAD past 4 — serial 1098s, forks=4 1004s (-9%, best of 3 runs 979-1025s), forks=8 1014s (flat), forks=12 1081s (-2%, near-serial); forks=8 CRASHED the Docker daemon outright on a 32GiB VM (SocketException, daemon gone, 75s in). title: parallelize the local maven engine suite (surefire fork-level) — serial 1911-test wall-clock is the local iteration bottleneck (Hal directive 2026-08-08 'asap')
description: HAL DIRECTIVE 2026-08-08: 'we really need to insert parallelism into the local maven build asap.' The full engine suite (cd service && ./mvnw -o test, 1911 tests) runs in ONE surefire JVM serially and has been the wall-clock bottleneck of every review/commit/push cycle. Substrate facts (verified): tests provision PG via Testcontainers (PgContainerHelper.newContainer(), pgvector:pg17, dynamic host ports, withStartupAttempts) — no fixed ports, container lifecycle already class/helper-scoped; surefire 3.5.2 with no forkCount config; deliberate NO-rerunFailingTestsCount policy (nexus-1hj1d) must be preserved. MUST: (a) same test count as serial, zero new flakes across 2+ consecutive parallel runs; (b) no shared-container cross-fork interference (prove, not assume — check PgContainerHelper for any static/singleton reuse across classes first); (c) CI cost discipline — this is the LOCAL loop; CI job shape/census unaffected or explicitly reconciled; (d) before/after wall-clock measured on a quiet box. title: stranded-install de-stranding gate (_has_verified_migration_report) reads a migration-reports/*.json format nothing in the current ladder writes — hop 3 (upgrade back to current) may re-trip the detector forever
description:
Found during substantive-critique of nexus-8nlj4's stranded-redirect rehearsal (2026-08-08).

src/nexus/stranded_install.py::detect_stranded_install only de-strands (returns
None despite pre-PG artifacts being present) when _has_verified_migration_report()
finds a <config>/migration-reports/migration-*.json file with
verification=="verified" and total_failed==0.

Exhaustive grep of src/nexus/ shows NOTHING writes to that directory/format
anymore. The old writer lived in the RDR-159 `nx guided-upgrade` / vector_etl
machinery, deleted at RDR-155 P4b. The CURRENT migration path the two-hop
message actually prescribes ("run `nx upgrade` there") converges via the
upgrade_ladder (substrate-etl rung), whose completion tracking moved
ENGINE-SIDE to PG (nexus.ladder_completions / HttpLadderStore per
upgrade_ladder/completion.py's RDR-186 .12 retirement note) — a completely
different mechanism that never touches <config>/migration-reports/.

Corroborating evidence: nexus-8nlj4's own rehearsal (T2 memory
nexus/nexus-8nlj4-stranded-rehearsal-2026-08-08, id 21879) observed, even AT
THE PIN release (conexus==6.18.1) after running `nx init` + `nx upgrade`
there: `nx doctor` reports "Migration reports: no migrations recorded". The
rehearsal's own Stage "Assert" treats this as informational (`note`, not
`bad` — non-fatal) rather than investigating further.

Consequence, not yet empirically verified: pre-PG artifact files are never
deleted (copy-not-move, by design — stranded_install.py's own docstring says
deletion is "a third, separately consented act ... never performed here").
If _has_verified_migration_report() can never return True via the real `nx
upgrade` remedy, then after a user completes hop 1 (redirect trips) and hop 2
(migrates at the pin) and attempts hop 3 (upgrade back to the current
release, per the message's own step 3: "upgrade back to this version"), the
SAME artifact files are still on disk, no verified report exists, and
detect_stranded_install would trip AGAIN — an unfollowable, infinite
two-hop-forever loop for any real user who does exactly what the message
tells them to do.

RECOMMENDATION: extend tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_stranded.sh
with a Stage 11 that performs the actual hop 3 (package-upgrade from the pin
back to the working-tree wheel a second time) and asserts nx doctor / nx init
/ CLI startup stay SILENT afterward — the adjudicating-fixture that would
confirm or falsify this hypothesis empirically. If confirmed, fix
_has_verified_migration_report to key off the actual ladder-completion
signal (or wire a report writer into the substrate-etl rung), not a JSON
format nothing produces anymore.

Not filed as a critique-only observation because it is squarely load-bearing
for the two-hop redirect's own documented third step, and evidence trail is
strong (static analysis + the rehearsal's own observed doctor output).
close_reason: Closed

title: kl2z6 combined-write design: staging guard's proposed index cannot accelerate the guard SQL, ~1s/sweep under exclusive gate at migration scale
design:
Found during substantive-critic design-stage review of T2 nexus/design-kl2z6-combined-write
[21804] (Hal's "fold these two calls into one, fix this right" directive), develop @ 1945fe60.
No source edited; this is a design critique against a design memo, not yet an implementation bug.

THE MEMO'S §4.2 PROPOSAL: close the staging-face residual (promoted-but-unmanifested content
sweepable between StagingPromoteOps.promoteCollection and finalizeTenant) with a third NOT EXISTS
guard on sweepChunks384/768/1024, reading staging.document_chunks (the staged manifest, landed
before promote runs), resolved through nexus.chash_alias with the SAME expression
finalizeTenant's own INSERT uses:

  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM staging.document_chunks s
    LEFT JOIN nexus.chash_alias a ON a.old_ref = s.chash
    WHERE COALESCE(a.new_chash,
                   CASE WHEN s.chash ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' THEN decode(s.chash,'hex') END)
          = chunks_<dim>.chash
  )

...plus "one Liquibase changeset: an index on staging.document_chunks(chash)" to "keep it
sub-statement_timeout" during a live migration.

THE PROBLEM, EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: that index cannot help this query. The function (decode +
regex validation) is applied to s.chash -- the column on the LARGE side (staging.document_chunks,
potentially hundreds of thousands of rows during an active RDR-176/RDR-180 guided migration), not
the small side (the per-doc dropped-chash candidate set, bounded by the flush chunk cap, ~500 max
per sweep). PostgreSQL cannot use a plain b-tree index on s.chash to satisfy an equality wrapped
in decode(...) -- and NOT EXISTS over a LEFT JOIN + COALESCE forces the planner into a Hash Anti
Join whose build side must materialize the resolved expression for EVERY staging row, once per
sweep invocation, regardless of any index on the raw column.

I built a schema-equivalent repro in a throwaway postgres:17-alpine container (torn down after,
no repo edits) -- staging_document_chunks seeded with 300,000 rows (64-hex TEXT chash, realistic
migration scale), chash_alias empty (the common case), 500 candidate rows in a chunks_384-shaped
table -- and ran EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, TIMING) against four variants:

  1. Guard as specified, NO index on staging chash:        1009.02ms
  2. Guard as specified, WITH the memo's plain index:       1016.08ms  (statistically IDENTICAL)
  3. Guard as specified, WITH an "obviously correct"
     expression index on decode(chash,'hex') instead:       1007.92ms  (ALSO identical)
  4. Guard RESTRUCTURED (function moved to the small/outer
     side) + the SAME plain index:                             1.68ms  (~600x faster)

Variant 4's guard shape:

  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM staging.document_chunks s
                   WHERE s.chash = encode(chunks_<dim>.chash, 'hex'))
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM nexus.chash_alias a
                   JOIN staging.document_chunks s2 ON s2.chash = a.old_ref
                   WHERE a.tenant_id = :tenant AND a.new_chash = chunks_<dim>.chash)

EXPLAIN confirms variant 4 plans as a genuine Index Scan (`Index Cond: (chash = encode(c.chash,
'hex'::text))`), scaling with the OUTER (bounded, cap-limited) side's cardinality instead of the
staging table's size -- the property the memo intended the index to buy, which the AS-WRITTEN
guard never actually gets.

WHY IT MATTERS: this guard runs inside the sweep's OWN transaction, which already holds the
collection's advisory gate EXCLUSIVE (nexus-11gh6, landed 1945fe60) -- so the ~1s cost is paid by
EVERY OTHER WRITER to that collection as pure stall time, on EVERY per-doc-immediate sweep, for as
long as staging has rows (i.e. for the duration of any live guided migration). At "hundreds of
thousands of rows" scale this is a meaningful fraction of SWEEP_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS (5000ms per
the parent 11gh6 design), and statement_timeout only cancels an ALREADY-RUNNING statement -- it
does not avoid paying the CPU cost, just caps how much is wasted before rollback. During an active
migration, sweep_skipped would become the ROUTINE outcome rather than the rare backstop the parent
design treats it as, silently masking real superseded-vector leaks for the migration's duration --
exactly the class of problem the whole 11gh6/kl2z6 thread exists to keep honest.

RECOMMENDATION: rewrite the §4.2 guard SQL to variant 4's shape (function on the bounded outer
side, two NOT EXISTS clauses instead of one LEFT JOIN + COALESCE) before implementation. Everything
else in the memo's §4 stays correct and unchanged: the "declaration of intent already exists, teach
the guard to read it" principle, the coextensive-with-finalizeTenant chash resolution, the
conditional-skip-when-staging-is-empty optimization (confirmed unnecessary for the TRUE steady
state -- Postgres already handles an empty inner table in ~3ms on its own -- but still worth
keeping for the active-migration case once the guard shape is fixed), and the single Liquibase
changeset (the SAME plain index the memo already proposed, just finally usable).

Filed as its own bead rather than folded into kl2z6 directly, since kl2z6 is IN_PROGRESS with its
own combined-write decision trail; this is a specific, scoped defect in ONE section (§4.2) of that
design, empirically diagnosed with a verified fix, not a rethink of the overall approach.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP (2026-08-09, nexus-ajt86 rebuild, T2 [22041]; drafted by critic [22042], posted by orchestrator). This bead's closing narrative ('EXPLAIN confirms variant 4 plans as a genuine Index Scan... ~1.68ms, ~600x faster') was measured in a throwaway container repro that did not exercise RLS or the production SVC_ROLE. ajt86's rebuild — running the REAL rendered SQL (CatalogRepository.renderSweepChunks384DeleteSql, sharing the exact builder production executes) through tenantScope.withTenant (real FORCE-RLS SVC_ROLE connection) at CANDIDATE_COUNT=300 (the real code-collection cap) — found the direct-hex arm plans as a HASH ANTI JOIN, not Nested Loop/Index Scan.
NOT a reopening of REV-1's pathology: REV-1 wrapped the STAGING side's join key in decode()/regex (index unusable under ANY strategy, per-row function eval across the table). The property this bead guarantees — no per-row function evaluation over the staging side — holds under EITHER join strategy; it is a property of the SQL shape, not of one chosen plan.
NOT re-verified: the specific ~1.68ms/600x figure describes the plan the non-RLS repro happened to get, not the plan production actually gets; no EXPLAIN ANALYZE exists for the Hash Anti Join at realistic scale. title: CAS-narrowed shared-client eviction closes instance mid-flight for concurrent healthy callers (catalog/factory.py + mcp_infra.py T2 lock)
description:
Found during substantive-critic review of the uncommitted eslkl+u2u0n+ldab2 bundle (2026-08-08), develop @ 6ebee497. Critique: T2 memory nexus/critique-eslkl-bundle-2026-08-08.

Both _SharedServiceCatalogHandle._call (catalog/factory.py) and _service_t2_write_locked (mcp_infra.py) now resolve their shared singleton under a lock, RELEASE the lock, then run the network call OUTSIDE it. This genuinely enables concurrent in-flight calls sharing one client/db instance (the whole point of u2u0n/ldab2). But the exception handler that evicts+closes the instance on failure is a bare `except Exception:` — it fires on ROUTINE, EXPECTED conditions, not just connectivity failures. Concrete example: HttpCatalogClient.complete_index_run raises IndexRunVerifyRefused (409, "doc not fully committed yet" — a normal, documented, non-fatal per-doc outcome) which is an Exception subclass and reaches this handler.

When thread A's call raises (even a routine one) and wins the CAS, it calls current.close() on the SHARED instance. Any OTHER thread (B, C) that resolved the SAME instance before the eviction and is genuinely mid-network-call on it gets its connection torn down too — confirmed empirically (scratch probe: closing a shared httpx.Client from another thread while a request is in-flight produces ReadTimeout/ConnectionError on the in-flight caller, not a clean no-op). mcp_infra.py's hazard is broader: T2Database.close() tears down SEVEN independently-owned Http*Store clients (memory, plans, taxonomy, telemetry, chash_index, document_aspects, aspect_queue, document_highlights) regardless of which substore actually failed — so an aspect_enqueue failure can abort a concurrent, unrelated, healthy taxonomy_assign call sharing the same T2Database singleton. This directly interacts with THIS bundle's own taxonomy_assign_batch_hook.serialize=False, which is what first makes genuinely concurrent taxonomy_assign calls possible in production.

Net effect: a single routine per-doc failure can cascade into MULTIPLE otherwise-healthy sibling flush workers' catalog/T2 calls failing, which can withhold their fence completion stamps and force redundant re-indexing next run — directly working against the throughput goal the whole eslkl/u2u0n/ldab2 bundle exists to serve. Not a data-correctness bug (best-effort/tripwire paths absorb it) but a real reliability/throughput regression, and it is UNTESTED: both test_concurrent_double_failure_does_not_double_close tests (factory.py and mcp_infra.py) only cover TWO THREADS FAILING TOGETHER, never one thread failing while a sibling succeeds concurrently on the same shared instance.

The narrowing docstrings ('a resolver arriving after the slot is cleared always builds fresh rather than ever observing an instance mid-close') are TRUE but answer the wrong question — they protect FUTURE resolvers and double-close, not CURRENT concurrent holders of the pre-eviction instance, which is the actual hazard.

Fix directions: (a) narrow the eviction-triggering except clause to genuine connectivity/lease-rotation symptoms only (not business-logic exceptions like IndexRunVerifyRefused/ValueError/LookupError raised as routine control flow), so eviction only fires on conditions where aborting sibling in-flight calls is arguably correct anyway; (b) add a test proving a HEALTHY concurrent call is NOT aborted by a sibling's routine failure; (c) correct the docstrings to state the actual limitation (protects against double-close/future-resolver, does NOT protect in-flight users of the pre-eviction instance).
close_reason: Landed in develop 13cd7029; dual-reviewed; suite 12093 green.

title: nexus-11gh6 design gap: T3 vector-write-vs-sweep-delete race unaddressed, widened by trailing-sweep batching
design:
Found during substantive-critic design-stage review of T2 nexus/design-11gh6-sweep-write-skew-closure
[21768] (the proposed advisory-gate + trailing-sweep fix for nexus-11gh6), develop @ 6ebee497.
No source edited; this is a design critique, not an implementation bug yet.

CLAIM UNDER TEST: the design memo's §0 recommendation ("per-(tenant,collection) SHARED/EXCLUSIVE
advisory gate, sweep DELETE moved to a trailing per-collection-group transaction") states
"The write-skew is closed structurally, not probabilistically" and its §2.4 "Why this closes it"
argument is empirically CORRECT for the axis it analyzes: I stood up a throwaway postgres:17-alpine
container and reproduced, with 4 live psql sessions under manual transaction control, that a NEW
pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared request genuinely queues BEHIND a PENDING pg_advisory_xact_lock
(exclusive) request rather than jumping the queue (pid 124's shared request stayed granted=false
in pg_locks for the ENTIRE window pid 123's exclusive request was pending, unblocking only after
pid 123 itself acquired-then-released exclusive). So the gate DOES structurally close the race
between ENGINE-SIDE manifest-insert transactions (writeManifestRows/appendManifestChunks/
importChunksBatch/doImportChunk, all 4 sites, confirmed by direct grep -- no others exist) and the
trailing sweep's DELETE.

THE GAP: that is not the only way a dangling manifest reference gets created. Read
src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:436-486 (_flush_batch): the CLIENT's own flush-grain pipeline uploads
chunk VECTORS to T3 first (`self._flush(...)`, a real network round trip with its own upload_s
timing), and only AFTER that call returns does it fire `_on_batch_complete` (indexer.py:3884,
`_fire_flush_grain_hooks`) which is what actually calls the engine's gated
writeManifestMany/manifest-write endpoint. So for any chash X, "X's chunks_<dim> row exists in T3"
and "X is registered in some catalog_document_chunks manifest row" are TWO SEPARATE, non-atomic,
network-round-trip-separated events, and only the SECOND one is covered by the new advisory gate.
The FIRST one (the T3 vector write/upsert) is on an entirely different code path/table with no
lock, no gate, nothing.

Concretely: doc D1 drops shared chash X (X was previously live). D1's writeManifestMany commits,
contributing X to this batch's trailing-sweep candidate set for the collection. Concurrently, doc
D2 (a DIFFERENT, unrelated document -- the design memo's OWN §4.1 admits "three concurrent flush
workers sharing licence-header chashes" is the realistic case, and ChunkBatcher's
flush_concurrency=3 per chunk_batcher.py makes concurrent flush workers routine, not theoretical)
has ALREADY had its `_flush()` land (T3 vector for X exists / re-affirmed) but has NOT YET reached
its `_on_batch_complete` manifest-write call -- that call is still in flight over the network, or
simply hasn't been scheduled yet. If the trailing sweep for D1's collection group runs its guarded
DELETE in exactly this window, its NOT EXISTS check is TRUE (nothing manifests X yet, from ANYONE's
perspective -- D2 hasn't registered), so it deletes chunks_<dim>(X). Moments later D2's manifest
write proceeds (gate is free, nothing prevents the insert -- there is no FK, by design, per the
memo's own §4.3), and D2's manifest now dangles, pointing at a chunks_<dim> row that no longer
exists. This is the EXACT SAME symptom nexus-11gh6 exists to fix, just relocated one layer up
(T3-write vs sweep-delete, instead of manifest-insert vs sweep-delete) -- and the new advisory gate,
exactly as specified, does nothing for this axis, because it only wraps the 4 Java insertInto
(CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS...) sites, never the T3 vector-write path.

WHY THE REDESIGN MAKES THIS WORSE, NOT BETTER: in the CURRENTLY SHIPPED code (the thing nexus-11gh6
is about), the sweep runs immediately, inside D1's OWN per-doc transaction, right after D1's manifest
replace -- the window between "X's last reference drops" and "the sweep actually evaluates X" is
bounded by ONE per-doc transaction's latency. The design memo's proposed fix DEFERS the sweep to a
single TRAILING transaction run ONCE PER COLLECTION GROUP, after every doc in the whole batch has
been processed sequentially (memo §2.3). For a large batch this can be many docs / seconds later.
That is a strictly WIDER window for D2's flush (running as a totally separate, concurrent
writeManifestMany call, or even a later doc within the SAME batch) to land its T3 vector write for
X in the "nothing references it yet" gap before its own manifest write catches up. So the fix
correctly closes the axis it targets while measurably WIDENING an axis it does not mention at all.

WHAT THE MEMO IS MISSING: §3 ("What this does NOT close") enumerates three residuals --
document_restore, collection moves, purge_trash's own sweep -- but omits this one entirely, despite
it being the LARGEST practical exposure (routine concurrent flush activity, not an operator-triggered
edge case like the other three). §6 (throughput impact) discusses only statement-count reduction and
does not mention that batching the sweep to end-of-request trades away exposure-window tightness for
throughput. §0's "closed structurally, not probabilistically" is true only for the manifest-insert
axis and overclaims relative to the actual production symptom (dangling references from concurrent
indexing) the bead exists to fix -- the SAME class of overclaim that created nexus-11gh6 in round 1,
now recurring one layer down in round 2's own remedy.

RECOMMENDATION: before implementing the memo as written,
(a) add this race to §3 explicitly, with the chunk_batcher.py:436-486 / indexer.py:3884 citations;
(b) make an explicit, stated decision about the batching-window tradeoff -- either keep the sweep
    per-doc-immediate (sacrificing the statement-count win) rather than deferring to end-of-batch,
    OR accept the wider window with a stated, reasoned risk level (e.g., "no worse than today's
    already-accepted client-side-sweep window, because X") rather than silence;
(c) recognize that NO purely engine-side catalog lock (this gate, chash-locks, SERIALIZABLE+retry)
    can close this specific axis without also synchronizing the T3 vector-write path -- so this is
    either accepted residual risk (state it, size it) or needs a client-side ordering fix (e.g.,
    the client's OWN sweep, kept live per nexus-wxjr6's staging plan, is the ONLY thing positioned to
    catch this axis, which changes its role from "temporary belt during production mileage" to
    "permanently required" -- confirm which one Hal intends).

Filed as its own bead (not folded into 11gh6) since 11gh6 is IN_PROGRESS with its own accept-and-
downgrade decision already recorded; this is a genuinely new, separate finding against the ROUND-2
remedy, not a restatement of the original gap.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
architect-planner response (design memo rev 2, T2 nexus/design-11gh6-sweep-write-skew-closure [21768], updated in place).

FINDING ACCEPTED IN FULL. All three recommendations adopted:

(a) ADDED to the memo as section 3.1, promoted to the FIRST and largest residual (ahead of document_restore / collection-moves / purge_trash), with the chunk_batcher.py:437+:472 and indexer.py:3884/3888 citations verified independently this session.

(b) BATCHING-WINDOW TRADEOFF DECIDED, and decided your way: the sweep is now PER-DOC-IMMEDIATE in its own transaction fired right after that doc's manifest transaction commits, NOT batched to end-of-request. The deadlock constraint that forced the sweep out of the per-doc transaction (a txn holding the gate SHARED cannot upgrade to EXCLUSIVE without deterministic mutual deadlock between two concurrent sweep=true writers) never required deferring to end-of-BATCH -- rev 1 conflated "must leave the transaction" with "may as well batch it", and bought a statement-count win that was never a requirement. Per-doc-immediate keeps the window at the shipped width instead of widening it, AND bounds the sweeper's gate-HOLD duration to one doc's dropped set, which independently answers your Significant #2. One change, both findings.

(c) ADJUDICATED: BOUNDED RESIDUAL, owned by THIS bead, not closed by the 11gh6 design. Your point that no engine-side lock can close this axis is correct and is now stated as the tiebreak: the engine never learns "someone intends to reference X" until the manifest write arrives, so the only real closures are a client-held lease spanning both calls (TTL + crash recovery) or folding the vector write and manifest write into ONE call (protocol change). Both are larger than the bug.

WORK DONE FOR THIS BEAD'S OWNER (so you do not restart from zero):

CHEAPEST CANDIDATE EVALUATED: an age guard refusing to sweep chunk rows written within the last G seconds. NOT viable as the schema stands, and the reason is non-obvious: the hazard case is a re-affirmed PRE-EXISTING shared row, and PgVectorRepository.java:683-687's ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE sets only chunk_text, embedding, and metadata -- never created_at -- so a re-uploaded shared chash keeps its original timestamp and an age guard would not protect it. Adding created_at to that set-list makes the guard viable with NO DDL (the column already exists, vectors-001-baseline.xml:97) and incidentally makes collection_vector_stats.last_write honest: catalog-005-collection-vector-stats.xml:15,51 already NAMES that field last_write but computes max(created_at) over FIRST writes. Due diligence owed before adopting: audit every reader of chunks_<dim>.created_at for a first-write assumption.

DETECTION ANALYSIS (bounds the severity, does not close the gap): in the damaging interleaving SPECIFICALLY, detection is guaranteed rather than merely likely. The victim doc's own manifest write runs stampCompleteIfVerified (CatalogRepository.java:3701-3703) AFTER its inserts, calling manifest_verify (catalog-020-index-run-fence.xml:157-205), which reads all three chunks_<dim> tables under a fresh statement snapshot and therefore sees the sweep's committed delete: missing>=1 -> completion stamp refused fail-closed -> doc in complete_refused -> client logs write_manifest_many_complete_refused "doc is NOT fully indexed, index_state left as-was" (mcp_infra.py:1512) -> doc not marked complete -> re-indexed next run, re-uploading the chunk. The harmless ordering (victim's manifest commits first) makes the sweep's guard see the row and delete nothing, so the verify always runs AFTER the delete in the only order that causes damage. TWO BOUNDS: it requires the write to carry a `complete` map (the flush-grain file-atomic path does, mcp_infra.py:1556-1559; continuation slices and the single-doc writeManifest path do NOT and are silent until a repo-wide manifest_verify_all / nx doctor pass), and detection is not repair in the same run -- the chunk is genuinely absent from search results until re-index.

SCOPE NOTE: the hazard requires the chash to be a PRE-EXISTING shared row. A brand-new chash uploaded only by the in-flight doc was never in the dropping doc's manifest, so it is never in `dropped` and never a sweep candidate. That narrows the exposure to genuinely shared content (licence headers, imports, boilerplate) -- which is still routine, just not every chunk.

SEQUENCING: this bead does NOT block closing nexus-11gh6 (different axis, and 11gh6's closure does not regress this one). It DOES block the client-sweep-retirement half of nexus-wxjr6 -- your point (c) is now Hal question 3 in the memo, with three explicit options (keep the client sweep indefinitely and close this wont-fix-by-design / close this first then retire / retire anyway and accept the silent non-completing paths). Recommendation recorded: close this first, with "keep the client sweep" as the safe default until this bead is scheduled.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN MEMO: T2 nexus/design-kl2z6-combined-write [21804], permanent. Design-only, no source edited, develop @ 1945fe60 (11gh6 gate LANDED). Honors Hal's binding constraint: ONE call, ONE server-side transaction, no leases / 2PC / saga / cross-call coordination.

RECOMMENDATION: extend POST /v1/catalog/manifest/write_many with an optional top-level `chunks` array. When present, each doc's EXISTING per-doc transaction additionally upserts the chunks_<dim> rows its own manifest references — inside the same transaction, under the sweep gate it already takes SHARED (CatalogRepository.java:3752-3758). Embedding stays outside the transaction, exactly as PgVectorRepository.java:635-636 already requires. Two statements added mid-transaction; nothing about the gate or the sweep changes.

WHY IT CLOSES: a chunk row from this path can never be committed without a manifest row referencing it. No interval, so no window to size. A concurrent sweep runs entirely before (nothing exists) or entirely after (guard sees the manifest row) because a granted-or-pending EXCLUSIVE blocks new SHARED grants.

THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER
1. NO EMBEDDINGS ON THE WIRE. The engine embeds server-side: upsert_chunks_with_embeddings DISCARDS the caller's embeddings (http_vector_client.py:1313-1315, "Seam B: embed moves to JVM") and the production flush closure passes embeddings=[[] for _ in _ids] (indexer.py:3631). The relay's "1024 floats/chunk" payload concern describes the ETL/import leg, not the serving path. Payload is chunk TEXT, which today's upsert-chunks POST already carries.
2. THE BINDING CAP IS NOT MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE. It is per_collection_chunk_cap (http_vector_client.py:493-530): 64 CCE / 300 code, driven by the control-plane 30s requestTimeout for server-side embed, and it is ALREADY the ChunkBatcher flush cap (indexer.py:3886). One combined call per flush fits by construction. Manifest rows add ~120B/chunk (~1% of a payload already being sent). No engine body cap (VectorHandler.java:85: 413 mapping retired, pgvector imposes no limit).
3. ROUND TRIPS GO DOWN. A flush is 2 POSTs today (upsert-chunks at chunk_batcher.py:437, then write_many via _on_batch_complete at :472-478); it becomes 1. cb5b6000's win is extended, not regressed.

CHASHES_MANY / SKIP-CONTENT-FOR-KNOWN-CHASHES: REJECTED, four grounds, the fourth decisive. (a) Wrong tool — it returns MANIFEST chashes for doc_ids (CatalogHandler.java:976), not vector existence. (b) No production caller exists — grep of src/nexus finds one comment at mcp_infra.py:1645. (c) The saving is already realised server-side by RDR-181's existence partition (PgVectorRepository.java:642-650). (d) DECISIVE: a pre-flight "I already have X" is stale on arrival; if a sweep removes X in between, the client sends a manifest row for content it deliberately omitted and commits a dangling reference — the optimisation recreates this exact bug one call earlier.

PER-DOC, NOT PER-FLUSH TRANSACTION: a flush-wide transaction is simpler and stronger but destroys writeManifestMany's documented per-doc failure isolation (CatalogRepository.java:3548-3551). Chunk text is carried ONCE at the top level keyed by chash; each doc's transaction upserts the chashes its own manifest references (idempotent ON CONFLICT, same gate, no conflict).

STAGING FACE — the key observation is that the intent is ALREADY declared durably: staging.document_chunks holds the staged manifest before promote runs, and finalizeTenant's INSERT reads it (StagingPromoteOps.java:434-444). Unlike the client face, the engine HAS been told. RECOMMENDATION: a third NOT EXISTS guard on sweepChunks384/768/1024 refusing to delete any chash a staged manifest row will reference, resolving the chash with the SAME expression finalizeTenant's INSERT uses (COALESCE(a.new_chash, decode(s.chash,'hex')) + the 64-hex regex admission) so guard and INSERT cannot diverge — the coextensive-by-construction discipline round 3 already applied at StagingPromoteOps.java:400-408. Zero steady-state cost (staging is empty outside a migration; make the predicate conditional on staging being non-empty). Needs one Liquibase changeset: an index on staging.document_chunks(chash). This closes the WHOLE promote-to-finalize gap, not just the in-transaction slice the current gate covers (StagingPromoteOps.java:231-247 names it as unclosable without a structural change).
RUNNER-UP: merge promoteCollection + finalizeTenant. Tiebreak: finalizeTenant is deliberately tenant-wide, doc-scoped and idempotently re-runnable across promote waves (StagingPromoteOps.java:51-53), and carries tenant-wide item8 disposition plus an in-txn zero-residual verify (:66-74). Per-collection merging redefines "zero residual" mid-wave and redesigns a migration contract on a path being retired, to fix a window a predicate closes completely.

ONE MECHANISM DECISION, stated as one PRINCIPLE (not one implementation): the sweep may delete a chunk only when no live DECLARATION OF INTENT references it. Client face: no declaration existed and there was nowhere to put one, so the fix removes the need by making content+manifest atomic. Staging face: the declaration already exists durably, so the fix teaches the guard to read it. Anything else invents a declaration mechanism where one is unnecessary or already present.

BACKWARD COMPAT: old client + new engine is safe by construction (absent field = today's path, the discipline the sweep flag already used at CatalogRepository.java:3589-3592). NEW CLIENT + OLD ENGINE IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION — an old engine ignores the unknown `chunks` field, manifest rows land, chunk rows never do: SILENT CONTENT LOSS. Two mechanisms, both required: (1) REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION floor bumped in the SAME release (structural, paired-release choreography); (2) a `chunks_written` ack echo in the response, with the client failing LOUD if it sent chunks and the key is absent — reusing upsert_chunks' existing "ack mismatch" discipline (http_vector_client.py:1291). The floor is a release-construction invariant; the ack is a runtime one, and being wrong here is undetectable missing content.

CLIENT SWEEP RETIREMENT + ACCOUNTING (39upx: skips never silent): _sweep_superseded_vectors_many is called ONLY from _manifest_write_loop (mcp_infra.py:1184), i.e. exactly the path this makes atomic, so it retires. But the CLI summary must be fed from the engine response: swept -> _record_superseded_swept, and sweep_detail[].errored -> _record_superseded_sweep_skip. THAT REQUIRES AN ENGINE CHANGE: runSweepTransaction currently collapses every failure into a bare errored=true (CatalogRepository.java:4219-4228). Add a machine-readable `reason` with a closed vocabulary (gate_timeout 55P03 / statement_timeout 57014 / before_read_failed / sweep_failed), else the client can only report "something was skipped" — the silent-skip failure 39upx exists to prevent.

SCOPE HONESTY: this closes kl2z6 for the FLUSH-GRAIN path. /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks stays and its other callers keep the two-step shape (http_vector_client.py:497-501 enumerates: oversize per-file fallbacks in prose/code/doc_indexer, exporter, pipeline, reindex, consolidation). Only callers that ALSO write a manifest can dangle; content-only writes are manifest-less chunks already protected by the notes guard and live_chunks' manifest-less-is-live contract (catalog-003-soft-delete.xml:33-39). The implementing pass owes a per-caller table. Do NOT close this bead claiming universal closure. Continuation slices (no position 0, routed to appendManifestChunks at mcp_infra.py:1503-1509) also keep the window unless the combined call gains a per-doc append mode.

wxjr6 BECOMES: engine tag with the combined write + sweep_detail.reason + staging guard; then ONE client release that switches the flush-grain path, bumps the floor to that tag, retires the client sweep, and rewires the accounting; deploy at client-tag push.

TEST PLAN (memo §6): 6a atomicity via external EXCLUSIVE gate holder + executor timeout, asserting NEITHER row is visible; 6b the kl2z6 characterization test flips; 6c no-orphan invariant after a forced mid-transaction rollback (the Order-17 column-REVOKE technique, CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest.java:544-551) which tests atomicity AND per-doc isolation together; 6d staging guard, deterministic, no threads; 6e full-cap flush for both cap classes; 6f route/fake/census move together (RouteSpec at CatalogHandlerEnvelopeConformanceGateTest.java:218, fake at test_fake_catalog_handler_route_census.py:208); 6g Python client surface incl. the ack-echo failure; 6h every existing test green with no `chunks` field.

THREE OPEN QUESTIONS FOR HAL (memo §7): append mode in scope or follow-up; convert-vs-record the other upsert-chunks callers; staging guard vs the promote/finalize merge the bead's second-face note names.
