title: Engine sweep fold has NO notes guard — can delete a live manifest-less note's T3 content (nexus-eslkl)
design:
Found during substantive-critic review of the nexus-eslkl engine-side sweep fold,
develop uncommitted @cb5b6000. More severe than the write-skew finding
(companion bead) because this gap is UNCONDITIONAL, not a narrow race window.

BACKGROUND: the client-side sweep (mcp_infra._sweep_superseded_vectors /
_sweep_superseded_vectors_many) runs TWO guards in sequence:
  1. union guard: orphaned_chashes(reader, doc_id, dropped) via
     docs_for_chashes -- keep a chash if any OTHER live document's manifest
     (catalog_document_chunks) still references it.
  2. NOTES guard: live_note_chashes(documents) via a SEPARATE catalog read
     (list_by_collection -> is_note_shaped -> meta["doc_id"]) -- keep a
     chash if it is the T3 identity of a manifest-less MCP store_put / nx
     store put note. Notes are DELIBERATELY written with ZERO
     catalog_document_chunks rows (store_hook.py's
     single_chunk_manifest_metadata / "if not metadatas: return" comment,
     confirmed: "no catalog_document_chunks manifest row ... is ever
     written for these two callers"). A note's liveness is tracked ONLY via
     its own catalog document row's meta["doc_id"] field -- a completely
     separate mechanism from catalog_document_chunks.

Both guards exist because content-addressing collapses identical chunk text
to ONE T3 row: if a note's content happens to be byte-identical to a chunk
some real document X also indexes, they share the SAME chunks_* row. When X
re-indexes and drops that chunk from its OWN manifest, guard 1 alone
(docs_for_chashes/NOT EXISTS against catalog_document_chunks) sees ZERO
references anywhere -- a note NEVER has a catalog_document_chunks row, so it
is indistinguishable from a true orphan by guard 1's logic. Guard 2 is the
ONLY thing preventing that shared row's deletion in that case.

THE ENGINE FOLD IMPLEMENTS ONLY GUARD 1. sweepSupersededVectors /
sweepChunks384/768/1024 (CatalogRepository.java) run a single NOT EXISTS
against catalog_document_chunks joined to catalog_documents -- there is no
query anywhere in the diff that reads content_type/file_path/meta to find
notes (grepped: zero "note"-related identifiers in CatalogRepository.java's
sweep code).

THE JAVADOC'S CLAIM THIS IS UNNECESSARY IS A NON SEQUITUR. It argues: "dropped
is a subset of before [doc_id's own prior catalog_document_chunks rows] ...
so a genuine manifest-less note can never appear in dropped in the first
place." That's true but answers the wrong question -- it shows a NOTE'S OWN
chash can't appear in `before` (correct, notes have no catalog_document_chunks
rows at all, ever, for ANY doc_id). It does NOT show that a chash validly
dropped from a REAL document X's manifest cannot ALSO be the exact content a
separate live note depends on -- which is precisely the scenario guard 2
exists for, and is entirely possible (X's re-index legitimately drops chash C
from X's own manifest; C is also, coincidentally or not, a note's content).
In that case the engine's guard 1 alone says "orphaned" and deletes C,
destroying the note's content while its catalog document row survives
pointing at nothing.

TEST DOES NOT COVER THE HAZARD: CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest#
writeManifestMany_sweepTrue_manifestLessNote_notSwept (Order 12) never
constructs a real note (no catalog document row with content_type=knowledge,
empty file_path, meta.doc_id set -- the actual identity predicate
indexer_utils.is_note_shaped checks). It seeds a raw chunks_384 row via the
test helper seedChunk384 and shows an UNRELATED document's write doesn't
touch a chash it never references -- true, but not the guard-2 scenario at
all. The test name promises coverage the test body doesn't provide.

IMPACT: not live yet -- nothing sends sweep=true (nexus-wxjr6, tracked). But
if wxjr6 wires sweep=true and retires the client-side sweep (one of the two
options wxjr6's own description lists), this becomes a live data-loss path:
a note's content can be silently deleted the next time some other document's
re-index happens to drop the same content hash from its manifest.

RECOMMENDATION: before nexus-wxjr6 retires (or even runs alongside) the
client-side sweep, either (a) port guard 2 server-side -- a NOT EXISTS/EXISTS
clause against catalog_documents where content_type/file_path/meta identify
a note-shaped row referencing this chash (mirroring is_note_shaped's
predicate in SQL) -- or (b) keep the client-side notes guard as a mandatory
second pass and never treat the engine fold as sufficient on its own. Add a
real test that constructs an actual note (matching is_note_shaped's
predicate) whose content chash collides with a chunk a real document drops,
and assert the row survives -- the current Order-12 test does not exercise
this path and should not be read as proof.
close_reason: Fixed at 6ebee497: server-side notes guard is a faithful is_note_shaped mirror (second NOT EXISTS, collection-scoped, hex-consistent); the genuine manifest-less-note test constructs the exact round-1 hazard (content-identical chash dropped by an unrelated doc) and proves it survives. Critic round-2 closure: CLOSE.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED (round 2). Ported guard 2 server-side (option (a) of the bead's own
recommendation), mirroring indexer_utils.is_note_shaped's EXACT predicate
(file_path IS NULL/empty AND metadata->>'doc_id' == candidate chash --
content_type is NOT part of is_note_shaped's own check, despite this bead's
prose mentioning "content_type=knowledge"; that filter belongs to a DIFFERENT
predicate, resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash's, not the one live_note_chashes/
the sweep actually uses -- confirmed by reading indexer_utils.py:186-188
directly).

sweepChunks384/768/1024 (CatalogRepository.java) each now carry a SECOND
NOT EXISTS clause, collection-scoped like catalog_documents_for_collection:

  NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM catalog_documents d2
    WHERE d2.tenant_id = ? AND d2.physical_collection = ?
      AND d2.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND (d2.file_path IS NULL OR d2.file_path = '')
      AND (d2.metadata ->> 'doc_id') = encode(chunks_<dim>.chash, 'hex')
  )

New field constant DOC_META_DOC_ID (metadata->>'doc_id', TEXT). Note: cannot
compare it directly against the existing ChashHex-converted chash fields --
ChashHex's Converter only operates at JDBC value-BINDING time, not by
rewriting SQL for a bare field-to-field reference, so a first attempt
(DOC_META_DOC_ID.eq(C384_CHASH_HEX)) rendered literally as
`metadata->>'doc_id' = chunks_384.chash` (TEXT = BYTEA) and Postgres 25P02'd
with "operator does not exist: text = bytea" -- caught by the test run
itself. Fixed via explicit encode(chash,'hex') on the chash side (TEXT =
TEXT), matching ChashHex's own lowercase-hex convention.

sweepSupersededVectors's javadoc rewritten with the FULL correction --
explains the earlier "structural" argument's actual flaw (proves a note's
OWN chash can't appear in `dropped`, says nothing about a note's content
coincidentally matching a chash a DIFFERENT document drops) rather than
just asserting the fix.

TEST: replaced the vacuous Order-12 test (writeManifestMany_sweepTrue_
manifestLessNote_notSwept, which this bead correctly identified as never
constructing a real note) with writeManifestMany_sweepTrue_
genuineManifestLessNote_notSwept -- builds an actual note-shaped
catalog_documents row (file_path omitted/empty, metadata={"doc_id":
noteChash}, ZERO catalog_document_chunks rows ever written for its
tumbler), then has an UNRELATED document reference and drop that same
chash, and asserts survival. Verified this test FAILS against the pre-fix
single-guard code (confirmed via the intermediate compile/test cycle before
the notes-guard SQL was added -- the old single-NOT-EXISTS guard swept it).

Full mvn suite in progress (SQL semantics changed here, so the standing
green run doesn't cover this). Targeted: 11/11 CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest,
7/7 CatalogHandlerSweepAndChashesManyTest, both green with the new guard.

title: Engine sweep fold: write-skew race not actually closed by READ COMMITTED NOT EXISTS (nexus-eslkl)
design:
Found during substantive-critic review of the nexus-eslkl engine-side sweep fold
(CatalogRepository.writeManifestMany's sweep overload / sweepSupersededVectors /
sweepChunks384-768-1024), develop uncommitted @cb5b6000.

CLAIM (Javadoc on sweepSupersededVectors + writeManifestMany(..., boolean sweep),
also T2 nexus/design-eslkl-hook-lock-narrowing §8.1, also restated in bead
nexus-wxjr6's description): folding the sweep's NOT EXISTS guard into the
per-doc write transaction "closes the TOCTOU" / "closing the cross-fire TOCTOU"
because the check-then-delete is one SQL statement's plan, "nothing else can
observe or mutate catalog_document_chunks between the check and the delete."

WHY THAT'S WRONG: the hazard is a cross-TRANSACTION write-skew, not a
within-transaction TOCTOU. TenantScope opens each per-doc write on a plain
JDBC connection with NO isolation level override (grep confirms no
setTransactionIsolation call anywhere in TenantScope.java) — Postgres default
is READ COMMITTED. Under READ COMMITTED, writer A's DELETE-with-NOT-EXISTS
takes its own statement-level snapshot; it cannot see writer B's INSERT into
catalog_document_chunks (a new manifest row referencing the same shared chash)
if B has not yet committed at the instant A's snapshot is taken. There is no
FK from catalog_document_chunks(chash) to chunks_384/768/1024(chash) (checked
fk-002-collection-registry.xml / catalog-001-baseline.xml — the only FK is
(tenant_id, collection)), so B's insert takes no lock A's delete would
conflict with. Concretely:

  A: currentManifestChashes(before) includes shared chash X
  A: writeManifestRows drops X from A's own manifest
  A: sweepSupersededVectors's DELETE ... NOT EXISTS(...) starts its snapshot
     -- B has not committed yet -- NOT EXISTS is TRUE -- X is deleted
  B: INSERTs a NEW catalog_document_chunks row referencing X (a fresh
     reference, not previously in B's manifest) -- commits
  --> B's manifest now points at a chunks_* row that no longer exists.

This is the textbook Postgres "write skew" anomaly; only SERIALIZABLE
isolation (which this code explicitly is NOT using -- the Javadoc even says
"SERIALIZABLE-free") closes it. The fold shrinks the race window from
client-round-trip scale (seconds, per the measured op latencies in the design
memo) down to intra-transaction scale (sub-millisecond to low-millisecond),
which is a real and valuable improvement -- but it is a probability
reduction, not structural closure, and every place that says "closes"/
"closing" (the two Javadocs, the design memo, and bead nexus-wxjr6's
description) overclaims.

TEST EVIDENCE THE OVERCLAIM WASN'T CAUGHT: the concurrency test
(CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest#writeManifestMany_sweepTrue_
concurrentInterleave_liveReferenceSurvives, Order 16) starts two threads
with a CountDownLatch barrier at the TOP of each thread (both call
writeManifestMany with no injected pause point at the actual seam) then
asserts a weakly-true invariant ("if B's reference is visible... the row
survives"). It has no rendezvous forcing A's DELETE snapshot to be taken
strictly between B's INSERT and B's COMMIT -- the one interleaving that
would actually falsify the "closed" claim -- so it is very likely to pass
regardless of whether the race exists (connection-acquisition and per-txn
overhead alone probably serializes the two threads most runs). This is NOT
the T1-falsification-test pattern the design memo itself specifies in §7
("Monkeypatch ... to rendezvous on a 2-party barrier at the exact seam...
MUST FAIL before the fix").

RECOMMENDATION: either (a) correct every "closes"/"closing" claim to
"narrows the window from round-trip-scale to intra-transaction-scale; the
underlying write-skew is unresolved" and accept the residual risk explicitly
(document it, decide if acceptable), or (b) actually close it: SELECT ...
FOR UPDATE (or an advisory lock keyed on chash) on the chunks_* row before
the NOT EXISTS check, or run the sweep step under SERIALIZABLE with retry.
Whichever direction, add a REAL falsification test with an injected pause
point/barrier at the exact seam (per the design memo's own §7 T1 pattern)
before trusting this as "the sole safety argument" for retiring the
client-side sweep (nexus-wxjr6 item 2).
close_reason: Closed by develop commit 1945fe60: per-(tenant,collection) advisory sweep gate at all 8 discovered writers across 3 files, sweep relocated per-doc-immediate post-commit (3wtku by construction), tripwire flipped to prove closure, whole-tree structural allowlist scan. 3 review rounds, final critic verdict JUSTIFIED. Residuals: kl2z6 (both faces), t76bp. wxjr6 opt-in half now unblocked; retirement half gated on kl2z6.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DECISION (round 2, accept-and-downgrade, option (b) of the two the critic offered):

Chose NOT to close this for real in this round. A correct closure (SERIALIZABLE
+ retry, or an advisory lock keyed on chash with a deadlock-safe acquisition
order across a batch) is a real design change to the write path with genuine
throughput tradeoffs (advisory locks would serialize concurrent writers that
touch the same shared chash tenant-wide; SERIALIZABLE+retry adds abort/retry
plumbing to a path with no such handling today) that deserves its own
deliberate design pass, not a round-2 patch under review-cycle pressure. This
is also not a regression versus the status quo: the client's OWN sweep
(cb5b6000, shipped, live in production today) has the IDENTICAL write-skew
at a LARGER window (two separate HTTP round trips vs one intra-transaction
statement) -- the engine fold is a net improvement even accepted as-is.

Fixed instead (this round):
1. Every overclaiming "closes the TOCTOU" / "closing the TOCTOU" comment in
   CatalogRepository.java (sweepSupersededVectors's javadoc, the sweep-flagged
   writeManifestMany overload's javadoc) corrected to "narrows... does not
   eliminate... residual cross-transaction write-skew window remains
   (nexus-11gh6)" with the exact mechanism spelled out.
2. The vacuous CountDownLatch-based Order-16 test
   (writeManifestMany_sweepTrue_concurrentInterleave_liveReferenceSurvives,
   which the critic correctly judged "passes regardless of the race" since it
   only synchronized thread START, never the actual seam) DELETED and replaced
   with sweepGuardSql_crossTransactionWriteSkew_isTheDocumentedNexus11gh6Gap:
   a DETERMINISTIC two-JDBC-connection proof (no threads at all -- explicit
   manual transaction/commit-order control) that reproduces this exact gap on
   every run, unconditionally, and asserts the CURRENTLY-ACCEPTED (known-gap)
   outcome. If this bead is ever closed via a real fix, that test's final two
   assertions will need to flip (documented in the test's own comment) --
   which makes the test a live tripwire for exactly this bead's resolution.
3. nexus-wxjr6 updated: client-side sweep (_sweep_superseded_vectors_many)
   must NOT be retired until THIS bead resolves for real -- hard dependency
   recorded there.

Gate-jar rebuilt, targeted classes green (11/11 CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest,
7/7 CatalogHandlerSweepAndChashesManyTest), full ./mvnw test run in progress
for final sign-off (SQL semantics changed for the SIBLING nl3fn fix in the
same commit, so the full suite reruns regardless).

Remains OPEN. Real closure (option a from the critique) is a separate,
deliberate follow-up -- not filed as a new bead since this one already names
it; whoever picks it up should choose between SERIALIZABLE+retry and an
advisory-lock scheme and weigh both against write-path throughput before
picking.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN MEMO REV 2 (architect-planner, after substantive-critic review). T2 nexus/design-11gh6-sweep-write-skew-closure [21768], updated IN PLACE. Critique: T2 [21774], verdict PARTIAL (1 Critical + 2 Significant). Critical filed as nexus-kl2z6.

RECOMMENDATION (unchanged in mechanism, changed in placement): per-(tenant, collection) SHARED/EXCLUSIVE advisory gate. Manifest writers take pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(hashtext('sweepgate:'||tenant||'/'||collection)); the sweep takes the same key EXCLUSIVE in its OWN transaction under lock_timeout + statement_timeout. No Liquibase changeset. Precedent: TaxonomyRepository.lockTaxonomyCollection (TaxonomyRepository.java:118-136).

WHAT CHANGED IN REV 2
1. Sweep placement: per-doc-IMMEDIATE in a separate transaction fired right after that doc's manifest transaction commits, NOT batched to end-of-request. The deadlock constraint (a txn holding the gate shared cannot upgrade to exclusive; two concurrent sweep=true writers doing that deadlock deterministically under flush_concurrency=3) forces the sweep out of the per-doc transaction, but it never required deferring to end-of-batch. Rev 1's batching widened the kl2z6 exposure window and unbounded the sweeper's gate-hold duration. One change fixes both.
2. Headline claim downgraded. Rev 1 said "the write-skew is closed structurally". Now scoped precisely: this closes the ENGINE-SIDE manifest-insert-vs-sweep-delete write-skew (the axis this bead names, the axis its tripwire pins). It does NOT close the client-side upload-window race. Rev 1 repeated the same overclaim class that created this bead in round 1.
3. New section 3.1 on nexus-kl2z6, adjudicated as a BOUNDED RESIDUAL, not an extended mechanism.
4. Throughput claim WITHDRAWN. Rev 1 claimed "net statements minus 2". Honest accounting is a small net COST: roughly +4 statements and +1 transaction per SWEEPING doc, +1 statement per non-sweeping doc. HTTP round trips unchanged, so the 327-to-4 batching win is untouched.
5. Test 7d rewritten: rev 1's source scan for an inline gate call at each of the 4 insert sites is blind to helper indirection. Replaced with single-homing (all 4 sites funnel through ONE private insert helper that takes the gate; assert the file has exactly ONE insertInto(CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS) site) plus 7c, a behavioural per-entry-point test that holds the gate EXCLUSIVE externally and asserts each of the 5 public entry points BLOCKS. Behavioural tests are blind to indirection by construction.
6. Deadlock claim made precise: with the current lock set NO deadlock is possible with or without the gate-then-indexrun ordering rule (writers take the gate only SHARED, the sweeper is a wait-sink). The ordering rule is future-proofing, not load-bearing today. Say so in the javadoc.

KL2Z6 ADJUDICATION: BOUNDED RESIDUAL. Tiebreak: no engine-side lock can close an axis whose two events are client-side and network-separated (chunk_batcher.py:437 self._flush uploads vectors, then :472 self._on_batch_complete fires the manifest write via indexer.py:3884; flush_concurrency=3 at indexer.py:3888). The two mechanisms that WOULD close it are both larger than the bug: a client-held lease spanning both calls (TTL + crash recovery), or folding the vector write and manifest write into one call (protocol change). Cheapest candidate handed to kl2z6 with the analysis pre-done: an age guard refusing to sweep recently-written chunks, NOT viable as the schema stands because the hazard case is a re-affirmed PRE-EXISTING row and PgVectorRepository.java:683-687's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE sets only chunk_text/embedding/metadata, never created_at; adding created_at to that set-list makes it viable with NO DDL (column exists, vectors-001-baseline.xml:97) and incidentally makes collection_vector_stats.last_write honest (catalog-005:15,51 already NAMES it last_write but computes max-of-first-write).

WHY THE RESIDUAL IS LOUD AND SELF-HEALING ON THE DOMINANT PATH: in the damaging interleaving specifically, detection is GUARANTEED, not merely likely. The victim doc's own manifest write runs stampCompleteIfVerified (CatalogRepository.java:3701-3703) AFTER its inserts, calling manifest_verify (catalog-020-index-run-fence.xml:157-205), which reads all three chunks_<dim> tables under a fresh statement snapshot and sees the sweep's committed delete: missing>=1, stamp refused fail-closed, doc reported in complete_refused, client logs write_manifest_many_complete_refused "doc is NOT fully indexed, index_state left as-was" (mcp_infra.py:1512), doc re-indexed next run. The harmless ordering makes the guard see the row and delete nothing, so the verify always runs after the delete in the only order that causes damage. TWO BOUNDS, stated not glossed: it requires the write to carry a `complete` map (the flush-grain file-atomic path does; continuation slices and the single-doc writeManifest path do NOT, and are silent until a repo-wide manifest_verify_all / nx doctor pass), and detection is not repair in the same run.

WINDOW SIZING: rev 2 does not widen the window (per-doc-immediate is the same placement as the shipped fold) and is considerably NARROWER than the client-side sweep still live in production, which evaluates after the whole batch's POST returns plus its own reverse-lookup round trip.

HAL QUESTIONS (question 3 changed materially)
1. Gate the two Java collection-move paths (updateDocumentCollection / renameCollectionTxn) in this bead, or defer with document_restore into one P3? Recommendation: gate the Java ones here.
2. SWEEP_GATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 (sweeper's ACQUISITION wait) and SWEEP_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 (sweeper's HOLD, and therefore the worst-case writer stall). Rev 1 had only the first and mis-described what it bounded.
3. CHANGED: is the client-side sweep PERMANENTLY required? Section 3.1 establishes no engine-side mechanism can close the upload-window axis and that _sweep_superseded_vectors_many is the only actor positioned to catch it. Rev 1's wxjr6 staging treated its retirement as a formality gated on "production mileage"; that is now wrong. Pick one: (a) keep the client sweep indefinitely, close kl2z6 as wont-fix-by-design; (b) close kl2z6 first (age guard, or combined vector+manifest write) then retire; (c) retire anyway on the strength of the completion-fence detection, accepting that the non-completing write paths are silent. Recommendation: (b), with (a) as the safe default until kl2z6 is scheduled.

SEQUENCING IMPACT: nexus-kl2z6 does NOT block closing this bead (different axis). It DOES block the client-sweep retirement half of nexus-wxjr6. wxjr6's opt-in half (turn sweep=true on, bump REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION to the v0.1.69 candidate in the SAME release, keep the client sweep live) is unblocked once this bead closes.

title: owes-report exhaustion default converts stale-lock into silent session-wide guard-off (nexus-7z7rj follow-on)
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit 58fad215: the round-1 pass-on-exhaustion default (which inverted the guard's failure direction via the 60s stale-reap window) replaced by per-type locks + block-with-named-cause; critic closure JUSTIFIED (T2 21740).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Found during substantive-critic review of the uncommitted nexus-7z7rj fix (develop@94949df9, files: tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh, conexus/hooks/scripts/expectations.sh, tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py). Full critique: T2 project=nexus title=critique-7z7rj-owes-report-decision-under-lock [21735].

Summary: nexus-7z7rj gates the owes-report credit read+CONSUMED-append to only run while holding "${file}.owes.lock" (file keyed by session_id only, NOT agent_type). On lock-budget exhaustion the new fixed default is 'does not owe' (return 1) WITHOUT consulting the ledger at all -- a behavior change from the old fail-open path, which still fell through to an unlocked-but-live read of the real ledger state.

The pre-existing 1-minute mtime-based stale-lock reap (unchanged by this fix) means an orphaned/killed lock holder leaves the lockdir looking 'fresh' for up to 60s. During that window EVERY subsequent subagent-stop in the SESSION (any agent_type, since the lockdir is session-scoped not per-type) spins its try-budget, exhausts, and now silently returns 'does not owe' with no ledger consultation -- the owes-report guard goes fully dark session-wide for up to 60s, observable only under --debug. Pre-fix this same window degraded to a racy-but-live read (could over-block, never silently missed). This inverts the guard's failure direction from safe (false-positive/over-block) to unsafe (false-negative/miss) in exactly the RDR-184 failure class it exists to catch, and is empirically reachable: this same session orphaned a lock-spin test process at PPID 1 during work on this very fix.

Recommended fix: per-type lockdir ("${file}.owes.${agent_type}.lock", agent_type already charset-validated) removes the cross-type-contention justification the developer gave for choosing the unsafe 'no' default, which would then allow reverting to the safer fixed default (block/owes) on exhaustion without cross-type misfire risk. Also flagged: the two concurrency tests' relaxed assertions (blocked<=credit, no lower bound) would pass even if the concurrent path always returned 'no' -- add a lower-bound assertion that the lock WINNER still blocks under forced contention.

title: reinstall default dance still refuses on storage-service holder -- nexus-otnvr's 'no flag ladder' goal unmet for the documented canonical scenario
close_reason: Storage service folded into the default dance via its existing stop/start choreography; critic round-2 closure: APPROVE — CLOSE. Canonical scenario replayed: one bare command, no flag ladder.

title: reinstall journey: the canonical post-release reinstall must work BY DEFAULT — no flag ladder, no mystery reconnect, no silent auto-converge race
description: Hal directive 2026-08-08 (verbatim frustration: 'literally the scenario we always do... extremely bad uix'). The canonical scenario — post-release reinstall on the dev box with a live Claude session — today takes: refusal #1 (MCP holders) -> add --cycle-mcp -> refusal #2 (daemon holder) -> add --cycle-daemons -> refusal #3 (classifier bug, see sibling bead) -> operator kills pids by hand -> reinstall -> discover /mcp reconnect is needed. Design-level fix, fold into the journey: (1) DEFAULT does the dance — enumerate holders, classify, cycle the safely-cyclable classes without flags (own/live-session MCP servers by ancestry; queue-backed daemons like aspect-worker which reclaim in_progress rows); REFUSE only genuinely unsafe holders (an in-flight interactive nx invocation mid-write); flags become opt-OUTs (--no-cycle). (2) End state is ANNOUNCED: print exactly the one remaining manual action (/mcp reconnect) — the reconnect itself is a Claude-Code harness constraint (a running server process cannot hot-swap its loaded code; only the harness can restart MCP servers, and it only does so on /mcp or session restart), so nexus cannot remove it, but it must be a stated instruction, never a discovered mystery. (3) Detect-and-prompt version skew: doctor / session-start compares each running nx-mcp's loaded version against the installed dist-info and says 'servers are on 7.3.0, install is 7.4.0 — run /mcp' — kills the mystery class permanently. (4) Related surprise from tonight: the lockstep/auto-converge path swapped the tool venv to PyPI 7.4.0 at session start (dist-info mtime 00:17, MCP servers spawning 00:17:31) — silent, racing the server boot, and it left the operator unable to tell what code the running servers had loaded; the skew probe in (3) is the fix for the detection half, and the swap itself should log loudly. Precedent: hrqox folded HALF the dance into the journey (nexus-hrqox); this finishes it. Related: the classifier bug bead filed alongside.
close_reason: Delivered: default dance cycles all four holder classes (session-MCP, aspect-worker w/ standalone restart, mineru, storage service) with pre-kill re-verify; refusal only for unrecognized/in-flight holders, one exact next command, /mcp instruction announced; lockstep swap loudly logged w/ rotation; session-start stale-mcp NOTE closes the other-sessions gap. Both reviewers APPROVE round 2. Residual visibility bead filed.

title: reinstall --cycle-mcp ancestry classifier misclassifies LIVE-session nx-mcp servers as non-MCP holders — the flag refuses in exactly the case it exists for
description: Proven live 2026-08-08 (7.4.0 reinstall): nx-mcp (55375) and nx-mcp-catalog (55401), DIRECT children of the live claude process (55162, verified via ps ppid), were listed under 'Non-MCP (or no MCP) holder(s) remain' and --cycle-mcp refused. The hrqox refusal/cycle design (ae5e2e86) is only as good as its classifier, and the classifier failed the canonical shape: a live session's own servers, one ancestry hop away. Suspect the claude-process detection (name/pattern matching on the parent chain) — find and fix with a real-process test (spawn a fake 'claude'-named parent + child, assert classification), not string fixtures. Until fixed, --cycle-mcp is inert in the primary scenario and users fall through to kill-by-hand or --force.
close_reason: Fixed on develop (uncommitted->committing now): _is_mcp_server_cmd token-2 shebang-aware matching (root cause: uv-tool shims exec via shebang so nx-mcp is never argv token 1); real-process falsified 4/4. Dual-reviewed two rounds, both APPROVE.

title: owes-report concurrent-stop race persists past the 4b8sz lock-budget knob — blocked=credit+1 at NX_EXPECT_LOCK_TRIES=200 in CI
description: Recurrence 2026-08-08, PR #1445 run 31244456036 shard 1/4: tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py::TestBlockMode::test_owes_report_concurrent_stops_never_exceed_credit failed 'expected exactly 4 blocked, got 5' WITH the nexus-4b8sz env knob already at 200 tries. Same tree passed this test on develop pushes 1a7632b7/763ed77f-292e3022/c763d400 the same day — load-dependent race, not a branch regression. Direction is OVER-blocking (5 > credit 4): under lock-contention fail-open, two concurrent stops appear to read the same credit state and both block — safe direction for the guard (no undeclared dispatch slips), wrong for the exactness the test pins. The 4b8sz fix tuned the RETRY BUDGET but the credit read+decrement is evidently still not atomic under the fail-open path. Fix direction: make read+decrement atomic under the same lock (never decide from an unlocked read), or explicitly define the fail-open contract as may-over-block and relax the test's exactness to blocked >= credit with an upper bound + a loud stderr marker — pick deliberately, not by flake-chasing. Evidence: job 93070706807. Prior art: nexus-4b8sz (09d1b4f0), original flake run 31215840624.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: REOPENED 2026-08-09: the MECHANICAL invariant the 58fad215 fix claimed to establish was VIOLATED in a local full-parallel run (orchestrator harvest of nexus-ui654, develop @ f145f3de, gw11). Failure is NOT the old blocked>credit shape — it is the ledger ceiling itself: 'assert len(consumed_rows) <= credit' -> 'assert 5 <= 4', with 5 CONSUMED rows (arace00/01/05/06/... worker-race) written at the SAME second 15:54:07Z. The round-2 close asserted 'consumed<=credit mechanical' via decision-only-under-lock + per-type lockdirs; five consumed rows for four credits means two racers made a consume decision from the same credit state, i.e. the read-decide-append is still not atomic under this contention, OR the per-type lockdir did not serialize these same-type stops. NOT caused by the diff under test: ui654 touches only tests/_engine_substrate.py + new substrate test files + a sweep script (fully disjoint from tests/hooks/ + the mkdir-lockdir mechanism); the file passes 50/50 STANDALONE immediately after. Load profile is the likely trigger (this run was the ui654 boot-semaphore's own live trial, which changes worker timing). Evidence: local run log scratchpad/pytest-ui654-harvest.log, 12325 passed / 1 failed. Fix direction unchanged from the original bead's own framing — either make read+decide+append genuinely atomic under one lock, or define and pin the fail-open contract honestly; do not re-close on a passing rerun.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SEVERITY CALL 2026-08-09 (debugger, EMPIRICAL — probe at scratchpad/sev_probe.sh against the real lib at f145f3de, two ledgers differing only by one extra CONSUMED row): **safe AT the race, REAL SILENT MISS afterwards.** Promoted P2->P1.
MECHANISM (expectations.sh:466-500): a CONSUMED row is not a pass — it is a DEBIT against a fungible per-type credit pool. verdict 'new' (credit>spent) -> append CONSUMED -> OWES -> BLOCK. verdict 'no' (credit<=spent, pool dry) -> DOES NOT OWE -> agent STOPS UNBLOCKED. Consuming credit causes blocks; running the pool DRY is what waves agents through.
IMMEDIATE: both racers read spent=3/credit=4, both append, both BLOCK — one extra agent blocked, nobody who owed slipped. That is the 'safe direction' the original bead rested on, and it holds ONLY for that instant.
DEFERRED (does NOT inherit the safety): the spurious row is a PERMANENT extra debit for the life of the session ledger; the pool is fungible and type-keyed and the debit is never repaid. The NEXT genuinely-new background dispatch of that SAME TYPE in that SAME SESSION finds credit==spent and is SILENTLY waved through — no BLOCKED row, no cause field, nothing an operator can see. Exactly the RDR-184 class the ledger exists to catch. Probe: ledger A (4 consumed/5 credits) -> fresh agent BLOCKED (correct); ledger B (5 consumed/5 credits, one spurious row) -> fresh agent STOPS UNBLOCKED (MISS). One spurious row = one future same-type background agent silently unguarded.
DIRECTION IS UNIFORM (the good news): the only interleaving produced is 'two racers both observe unspent credit', which can only OVER-count spent — never under-count. Deterministically over-block now, deterministically miss-later once >=1 further same-type background dispatch occurs. Trigger is not exotic: repeated same-type fleet dispatch is explicitly encouraged, and the ledger is session-scoped and long-lived.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD: the 58fad215 close reason ('consumed<=credit mechanical') was both violated AND rested on a safe-direction premise that does not survive past the instant of the race. This is shipped plugin code on the SubagentStop path in every conexus session. Fix rides the pending client release; do not ship it as 'flaky test, safe direction'.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CUT-TIME RECONCILIATION (orchestrator, for the 7.5.0 changelog placeholder — the release-prep agent correctly flagged an apparent contradiction and refused to guess): BOTH facts are true and non-contradictory. (1) Commit 58fad215 IS in the v7.4.0..HEAD range and IS the ROUND-2 fix (decision-only-under-lock, per-type lockdirs, exhaustion blocks with disclosed cause) — it landed 08-08 and this bead was closed on it, so PENDING_RELEASE.md item 4's narrative of Rounds 1-2 is ACCURATE for what the release already contains. (2) This bead was REOPENED 2026-08-09 because that fix's OWN claimed mechanical invariant (consumed<=credit) was violated in a local full-parallel run, and the severity call then established the deferred-miss property that retires the 'safe direction' premise. So the release currently contains rounds 1-2; ROUND 3 is in flight. CHANGELOG RESOLUTION AT CUT: if round 3 lands before the cut (expected), the conexus/CHANGELOG.md placeholder becomes an entry describing the round-3 fix and the reopening is invisible to users — one honest line about the SubagentStop ledger guard being made correct under concurrent stops. If round 3 does NOT land, DELETE the placeholder (do not describe rounds 1-2 as a fix for a bug that is currently open) and the release ships with the bug known-open — which would be a deliberate decision to record, not a silent omission.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROUND 3 ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED on worktree-agent-a5af5eb2a64da3769 @ a7cc2752 (+ 6ae85883), based on develop f145f3de. NOT pushed.

ROOT CAUSE — not the critical section, which is what rounds 1 and 2 both hardened. It is the stale-lock reap that runs BEFORE acquisition: '[[ -d ]]' / 'find -mmin -1' / 'rmdir' are three steps and the lock can change hands between them, so the rmdir deletes a LIVE holder's lock and two racers end up inside the critical section reading the same credit state. Window == one fork+exec, hence load-triggered. Reproduced DETERMINISTICALLY with injected scheduling delay (no logic change); trace shows C ACQUIRED -> C READ new -> B 'RMDIR SUCCEEDED (stole a lock it does not own)' -> B ACQUIRED -> B READ new -> both APPEND. consumed=2 for credit=1.

Falsified en route so nobody re-runs it: the BSD 'find -mmin -1 never matches a fresh dir' theory is WRONG on this box; the TOCTOU, not the predicate, is the defect.

PRIMITIVE VERDICT: safely stealing a name-based lock needs an atomic compare-and-delete on a path, which POSIX does not provide. The reap was never tunable — only 'never reap' or 'stop depending on the lock'.

FIX: a unit of credit is now claimed by creating a slot SYMLINK <file>.credit.<type>.<n>. symlink(2) is atomic and fails EEXIST, so exactly one racer per slot name can ever win; the link target is the claiming agent_id so claim+stamp is one atomic op. 'credit > spent' still gates whether a claim is attempted but no longer decides. Pre-change ledgers are reconciled into slots on first use. The lock is kept as a pure efficiency measure; all of round 2's disclosure guarantees are preserved and still tested, but none is load-bearing for the ceiling any more.

DEFERRED HALF closed at the source: the only path that appends a CONSUMED row must first WIN a slot, so a spurious debit cannot be written.

FALSIFICATION — the new permanent test asserts the PROPERTY, not an interleaving: NX_EXPECT_LOCK_DISABLE=1 turns the lock off entirely (zero mutual exclusion, strictly stronger than any stolen lock) and requires exactly 'credit' rows, both bounds. Pre-fix under that adversary: pytest 'assert 5 == 4' with five rows in one second (the wild signature), and 25/25 stress trials violate at 8-11 rows for 4 credits. Post-fix: 100/100 trials exact, 0 over / 0 under, 12 racers. 353 passed in tests/hooks/.

Side findings filed: nexus-ma5tg (P2, agent-dispatch-expect.sh has the identical reap TOCTOU), nexus-s6htm (P3, expectations_test.sh has been aborting at Test 4 under set -u since round 2 — Tests 4-15 dark for two days during an active fix round on this machinery; guard fixed in 6ae85883 and it immediately caught a real defect in the round-3 change), nexus-ad624 (P3, test_lock_tries_clamped_to_ceiling is load-sensitive by construction).

Full write-up: T2 nexus/nexus-7z7rj-round3-2026-08-09 [22096].

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: EPISTEMIC FINDING from round 3 — WHY ROUNDS 1 AND 2 COULD SHIP BELIEVING THEY HAD VERIFIED. The unguarded $NX_EXPECT_LOCK_HOLD_DELAY_S dereference (expectations.sh:462, fixed in 6ae85883) was NOT merely latent: expectations_test.sh runs , so that dereference had been ABORTING the test script at Test 4 since round 2 — leaving Tests 4-15 DARK for two days, during an active fix round on this exact machinery. The suite did not fail; it stopped running and reported what it had gotten through. Restoring those tests immediately caught a real defect in the round-3 change itself. So this bead's own history includes a period where the primary validation harness for the fix was silently truncated — which is the same vacuous-verification shape as the code defects this session has been chasing (a gate that passes because it scanned nothing), one level up: a TEST SUITE that passes because it exited early. Lesson for the close: 'the tests passed' was not evidence during rounds 1-2, and nothing in the output said so. Related: nexus-s6htm (P3, stale shell assertions the Test-4 abort was hiding), and the wider sweep at T2 [22088].

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CLOSED round 3, 2026-08-09 — landed on develop as 01039206 + bed9b8d9 + ae13a715 (worktree a7cc2752/6ae85883/fc066671). ROOT CAUSE, after two rounds fixed the wrong thing: NOT the critical section but the stale-lock reap BEFORE acquisition — [[ -d ]] then find then rmdir is three steps and the lock can change hands between them, so the rmdir deletes a LIVE holder's lock and two racers enter. Safely stealing a name-based lock needs an atomic compare-and-delete POSIX does not offer, so the fix stops making the ceiling depend on the lock at all: credit is claimed by atomic slot symlink (EEXIST, one winner, link target = ownership stamp). Ceiling verified kernel-enforced: 40/40 exact with the lock DISABLED, vs 20/20 violations for pre-fix logic under the identical adversary. THE CRITICAL FOUND IN REVIEW (ols6a, now closed): hooks.json gives SubagentStop a 10s timeout while the lock budget is 20-60s, so the harness SIGKILLs this hook as a ROUTINE load-correlated event — and round 3 initially DOUBLED that kill's damage (the stop was lost AND a credit burned). Fixed: an orphaned slot now BLOCKS with cause=credit-slot-orphan instead of silently passing. DETECTORS MEASURED AGAINST A BROKEN FIX, which is the part worth carrying: the ceiling detector had a 1-in-12 FALSE-PASS rate — fixed structurally (NX_EXPECT_CLAIM_DELAY_S forces all racers to read the same state) to 0/90, p~0.0004; the orphan detector is new (nothing covered that path) at 0/30. THE PATTERN: rounds 1, 2 and 3 each moved the unsafe window somewhere that round's own test could not see (critical section -> pre-lock reap -> claim/append), and all three shipped on 'the tests passed' — which was never evidence, since expectations_test.sh had been ABORTING at Test 4 since round 2 and was dark for two days during the active fix round. TWO GENERALIZABLE COUNTERMEASURES: ask 'what TERMINATES this process, and where can it be when that happens?' (hooks.json answers it in one line and would have caught all three rounds at design time), and MEASURE the detector against a deliberately broken fix before believing a green run. Residuals: y1kpz P2 (census/guard disagree; self-heal measured, decay NOT monotonic), dl2jb P3, 4wtnl P3, 49dj2 P3, ma5tg P2 (direction verified over-block-only). Marker [22120].

title: repo-scope guard: Signal A (origin URL) short-circuits Signal B (marker) — real nexus checkout with non-'nexus' origin basename silently loses push-to-main protection
description:
Empirically verified (2026-08-07, substantive-critic review of nexus-vscgz) against
conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py's
_repo_scope_is_nexus(): Signal B (the conexus/.claude-plugin/plugin.json marker
file check) only runs when Signal A (origin remote URL basename) is UNDETERMINABLE
(no origin remote, or the git call fails). It does NOT run when Signal A succeeds
but resolves to a basename other than "nexus".

Repro: a real nexus checkout (marker file present, i.e. genuinely nexus by the
code's own Signal B heuristic) whose `origin` remote is a local-path pointing at
a directory NOT literally named `nexus` (e.g. a scratch clone `nexus-2`, a
tarball unpack, a renamed local mirror -- the exact pattern this file's OWN test
fixtures use to opt repos in/out) gets classified NOT-nexus. Confirmed end-to-end:
a bare `git push` on `main` in that checkout is silently ALLOWED by the hook --
the nexus-vduer guard (born from the real 2026-07-23 direct-push-to-main incident)
is defeated with no warning, no log signal distinguishing it from an intentionally
out-of-scope foreign repo.

Not covered by any of the nexus-vscgz regression tests (all nexus-scoped test
fixtures use an origin whose basename is literally "nexus"; the marker-fallback
tests only exercise the no-origin-remote case, never origin-present-but-mismatched).
Not documented as a residual risk in the module docstring or registry.yaml
rationale added by nexus-vscgz.

Fix direction: change scope resolution from "B only if A undeterminable" to an OR:
nexus iff (Signal A matches "nexus") OR (Signal B marker file present) -- check the
marker unconditionally whenever Signal A does not affirmatively match, not only
when it errors out. This preserves the fail-open behavior for genuine foreign
repos (which won't have the marker file) while closing the false-negative inside
nexus itself. Add a regression test: nexus checkout (marker present) + origin
remote whose basename is NOT "nexus" -> push-to-main must still be blocked.

Context: nx (relates to nexus-vscgz).
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit 1a7632b7: Signal B is a true OR with Signal A, not fallback-only; regression test_renamed_origin_with_plugin_marker_still_guards is non-vacuous (critic reproduced pre-fix False). Critic round-2 closure: CONFIRMED CLOSED.

title: plugin-drift-ledger CI job is vacuous-green: autouse engine-substrate fixture skips all 12 tests on the minimal runner
description: Evidence: run 31223172021 (develop @ 599e4980, 2026-08-07) — 'Run the ledger contract' step output ends '12 skipped in 0.23s', job SUCCESS, while that very commit carried undeclared drift (conexus/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md changed post-v7.3.0-tag with no PENDING_RELEASE.md entry; test_every_drifted_file_is_declared_in_the_ledger fails on it locally). Mechanism: tests/conftest.py _pin_t2_substrate (autouse, nexus-i711w engine cutover) pulls t2_service_env for EVERY test unless NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=none; the plugin-drift-ledger.yml runner ('No matrix, no native build, no service, no PG' by design) cannot provision the engine, so every test in tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py skips at fixture setup. The file's own anti-vacuity mechanism (NX_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_DRIFT_CHECK=1, which turns the TAGLESS skip into a hard failure) sits INSIDE the test bodies and never runs — the fixture skip preempts it. The gate has likely been vacuous since the substrate cutover landed. Fix: (1) set NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=none in the workflow's pytest step env — these tests are pure git/YAML and need no substrate; (2) add a non-vacuity guard so this cannot recur silently: under NX_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_DRIFT_CHECK=1 ANY skipped test in this file fails the run (e.g. sessionfinish hook or workflow-level skip-count check), per the standing 'a gate that skip-passes when its dependency is absent must carry a max-skip/non-vacuity assert' invariant; (3) backfill the missing SKILL.md ledger entry (being done in the nexus-vscgz commit). Related: feedback_read_the_gates_own_assert_not_a_proxy.
close_reason: Fixed at 763ed77f: drift-ledger workflow opts out of the engine substrate (tests are pure git/YAML) plus a skip-grep non-vacuity belt that fails the job on any skip. SKILL.md ledger backfill landed at 1a7632b7. Reviewed clean by both reviewers (T2 21648/21649).

title: Push guard (nexus-vduer) fires outside the nexus repo — missing repo-scope check
description:
Evidence 2026-08-07: in ChiralBehaviors/inviscid (hobby repo, no develop branch, no marketplace surface), the conexus push guard blocked 'git push origin master' with the nexus-vduer message (PRs only, develop->main promotion, marketplace surface). That policy is nexus-specific; the guard applied it to an unrelated repo purely because the hook is installed globally. User bypassed via the auditable '# routing-allow' escape hatch (reason recorded in routing log).

Fix: before enforcing develop->main routing, the guard must verify it is operating in the nexus repo — e.g. match origin remote URL against the nexus repo, or check a repo-root marker file — and no-op (allow) in any other repo. Add a regression test: push from a non-nexus repo with a master default branch must not be blocked.
notes: (2026-08-18: an analysis note was mis-targeted here by a bead-search mismatch and has been moved to nexus-2mb2j, the extracted-personal-hook scope-decision bead. This bead's closure record is authoritative and unaffected.)
close_reason: Fixed at 1a7632b7: _repo_scope_is_nexus gates rules 2+3 (origin basename 'nexus' OR conexus plugin marker, undeterminable=foreign/allow); regression tests incl. the exact inviscid shape (explicit push origin master + bare push, both allowed in foreign repos). Dual-reviewed clean over two rounds.

title: nx doctor --check-t1 / health._check_orphan_t1 / console/watchers.py all diagnose a permanently-empty t1_addr.* format (nexus-yfh5x follow-up)
design:
Substantive-critique finding on the uncommitted nexus-yfh5x + nexus-9l147 batch (src/nexus/daemon/t1_lease.py, service_registry.py, health.py, AGENTS.md; tests/daemon/test_t1_lease.py, test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py, test_doctor_cmd.py, test_doctor_integrity.py, test_t1_discovery.py).

nexus-yfh5x's own investigation independently re-verified (fresh grep across src/, tests/, docs/, conexus hooks): T1LeasePublisher had zero production construction sites and is genuinely dead; its deletion is sound. But the SAME investigation proves a broader, unaddressed fact: ServiceRegistry(tier="t1") now has exactly ONE production construction site in the whole tree -- t1_lease.py:55 inside discover_t1_lease -- and it only ever calls .discover(), never .publish(). Nothing anywhere writes the t1_addr.* lease format any more.

Three live production consumers still treat that format as a meaningful signal, all now permanently stale, none touched by this batch, none bead-tracked before now:

1. `nx doctor --check-t1` (src/nexus/commands/doctor.py `_run_check_t1`, ~line 1787): for ANY resolved session-id, discover_t1_lease() now returns None unconditionally (nothing ever publishes), so this command reports `[X] T1: session '...' resolves but no live lease` and exits 1 for every real user, EVERY TIME -- not intermittently. The diagnosed causes it prints ("MCP server crashed before publishing", "lease aged out", "still booting") are all false; the real cause (no publisher exists) isn't one of the listed causes. The healthy-path message text is also independently stale: "chroma reachable" / "spawn a fresh chroma" -- chroma was fully retired project-wide at RDR-155 P4b, and t1_lease.py's own new docstring in this diff says so. tests/test_doctor_cmd.py::TestCheckT1::test_healthy and test_lease_present_but_unreachable still hand-publish a lease via ServiceRegistry.publish() directly to exercise this "healthy" branch -- a state doctor can never reach via any real code path in production, so the test suite is green while the feature is silently always-broken.

2. `console/watchers.py::scan_sessions_sync` (~line 104): docstring says "T1 publishes a leased registry record per live session" (present tense, false). This backs whatever session-list UI/cockpit consumes it -- it will now show ZERO live T1 sessions regardless of how many MCP servers are actually running. Silent, misleading blind spot, not just a CLI quirk.

3. `health._check_orphan_t1` (src/nexus/health.py ~line 1378): docstring likewise claims "T1 publishes a leased registry record at ~/.config/nexus/t1_addr.<session_id>" in the present tense. Lower severity than 1/2 since it degrades to an always-green no-op ("no live T1 sessions") rather than a false failure, but the docstring is still a documented lie sitting two functions above the NEW _check_orphan_t1_handoff this same diff adds (which correctly documents the CURRENT t1_handoff.* mechanism right next to the stale one).

None of this is hidden -- it follows directly and mechanically from t1_lease.py's own new module docstring in this diff ("Nothing in production publishes the t1_addr.* format any more"). The t1_lease.py docstring claims this gap is "tracked as a separate, lower-priority cleanup in nexus-yfh5x's own comment thread" -- verified false: `bd show nexus-yfh5x` has no COMMENTS section and no other bead references t1_addr.*/check-t1 staleness. This is the exact "never leave a finding in prose -- it becomes a bead, unasked" violation the project's own standing directive exists to catch, compounded because the finding was already flagged once (T2 nexus/nexus-d76vc-substantive-critique, 2026-08-07) as "the 3 existing stale-file scanners don't recognize the new t1_handoff.* prefix" -- but that framing undersold it: the scanners' EXISTING t1_addr.* behavior is not just incomplete, it is now actively wrong for #1 and #2 above.

Fix options: (a) delete discover_t1_lease/_run_check_t1/scan_sessions_sync's t1_addr.* path entirely alongside T1LeasePublisher (same "genuinely dead, port-or-delete" logic yfh5x already applied to the write side), or (b) if a future T1 publisher is anticipated, downgrade `--check-t1`'s missing-lease branch to informational (not exit 1) and fix the chroma-era message text, and update watchers.py/health.py docstrings to state the read path is currently unfed. Whichever is chosen, the T1RecordHarness in tests/daemon/test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py (TIERS = ("t1", "storage_service", "aspect_worker")) should also be reconsidered: it still runs t1 through the FULL publish/self-heal/fence/reap conformance battery via the shared ServiceSupervisor, which is fine as "if a writer existed, the primitive would work for t1's TTL" coverage, but nothing in the diff states that's the intent -- worth an explicit one-line docstring note (Significant, not blocking) so a future reader doesn't mistake it for coverage of a live production path, the same phantom-tier confusion AGENTS.md already had to spell out for t2/t3.
close_reason: Fixed at 292e3022: dead t1_addr read surface deleted (t1_lease.py, both registry sweeps, conformance t1 tier per phantom-tier precedent); doctor --check-t1 ported to 4-branch t1_session_lease semantics (kills the always-exit-1); health check reaps expired lease litter; console card truthful. Dual-reviewed; critic's AGENTS.md Critical fixed pre-commit. Engine session-list residual tracked as a separate P3 bead (see commit message).

title: purge-trash execute: post-commit VACUUM can exceed the 30s default httpx client timeout, undocumented
design:
Substantive critique of nexus-0ys55/nexus-4e465 engine implementation (worktree agent-aac5877fb7e37173d) found: CatalogRepository#purgeTrash (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java, applyPostPurgeVacuum) now runs TenantScope#vacuumAnalyze SYNCHRONOUSLY on the HTTP request thread, post-commit, before CatalogHandler#handlePurgeTrash (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/CatalogHandler.java:527-558) sends its HTTP 200 response. vacuumAnalyze runs 5 VACUUM (ANALYZE) statements SEQUENTIALLY on one borrowed connection (chunks_384, chunks_768, chunks_1024, catalog_document_chunks, catalog_documents).

The production incident that motivated this P1 bead (bd show nexus-0ys55) reported chunks_1024 ALONE took 195s to VACUUM manually (11,594-doc purge, ~60k dead tuples). The Python client's shared httpx.Client timeout is a hardcoded 30.0s default (src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:79, _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S) with no per-call override anywhere in HttpCatalogClient.purge_trash (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1351-1401) or the _post/_send chain, and HttpCatalogClient.__init__ (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:277) takes no timeout parameter.

Consequence: `nx catalog purge-trash --no-dry-run --confirm` run at anywhere near the incident's scale will almost certainly blow the 30s client timeout WHILE the 5-table VACUUM sequence (plausibly minutes, given multiple bloated tables) is still running server-side. The CLI's exception handling (src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/purge_trash.py:233-241) only catches httpx.HTTPStatusError for the 404-engine-floor case -- an httpx.ReadTimeout/ConnectTimeout propagates uncaught, with no message telling the operator the underlying DELETE already committed and the VACUUM is still progressing server-side (there is no statement/query timeout server-side -- confirmed no setQueryTimeout/statement_timeout config in the pool -- so the VACUUM itself completes fine, just invisibly to the timed-out caller). An operator who reasonably retries the "failed" command risks a second full VACUUM sequence starting concurrently with the first one still in flight against the same 5 tables, compounding load during exactly the kind of incident window this bead exists to help recover from.

None of this is acknowledged in the CatalogRepository/TenantScope javadocs, the grants-nexus-svc.xml changeset comment, the bead descriptions, or the http_catalog_client.py purge_trash() docstring (which also doesn't mention the new vacuumed/skipped_reason envelope keys at all).

Fix shape (client + engine, needs both a docs/timeout decision and possibly an async execution model): either (a) give purge-trash's client call a materially larger timeout override (bounded, documented) sized to the worst observed multi-table VACUUM duration, (b) catch httpx.TimeoutException specifically in purge_trash_cmd and print a message clarifying the purge committed and vacuum may still be running, and/or (c) move the VACUUM off the request thread entirely (fire-and-forget with status queryable separately) so the HTTP response returns promptly after the DELETE commits. Whichever is chosen, document the choice at both the CatalogRepository#applyPostPurgeVacuum javadoc and the http_catalog_client.py purge_trash() docstring.

Full critique record: T2 nexus/critique-nexus-0ys55-4e465-t23zk-6yps0-engine-2026-08-07.
close_reason: Shipped develop d3aea8d0: VACUUM moved off the request thread (single-thread daemon executor, CAS single-flight before submit, envelope vacuum=scheduled|already-running|skipped:*, completion detail in executor log events). Critic re-review CLEAN tag-ready (T2 21626): 30s-client-timeout arm and retry-storm arm both closed.

title: grants-nexus-svc.xml: GRANT MAINTAIN on purge-trash VACUUM tables (chunks_384/768/1024, catalog_document_chunks, catalog_documents)
description: nexus-0ys55 engine-side implementation (worktree agent-aac5877fb7e37173d, uncommitted) added TenantScope.vacuumAnalyze() + CatalogRepository.applyPostPurgeVacuum(), invoked post-commit by purge-trash execute. Verified LIVE against a real PG17 testcontainer (CatalogPurgeTrashVacuumTest) that nexus_svc's CURRENT grants (grants-nexus-svc.xml grants-nexus-svc-1: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only) are NOT sufficient to actually vacuum these 5 tables -- nexus_svc does not own them (nexus_admin does) and holds no MAINTAIN grant on them (only nexus.chash_alias has one, added at rdr180-17/F2). PostgreSQL does not throw for this -- vacuum_rel emits a WARNING ('permission denied to vacuum "<table>", skipping it', confirmed exact PG17 wording via the test) and silently no-ops the statement. The engine-side code already detects this via Statement.getWarnings() and reports vacuumed=false/skipped_reason accordingly -- it never crashes or lies about success -- but the bead's actual production goal (VACUUM actually running after a bulk purge, closing the 60k-dead-tuple gap that motivated P1) will NOT be met until a Liquibase changeset grants MAINTAIN on: nexus.chunks_384, nexus.chunks_768, nexus.chunks_1024, nexus.catalog_document_chunks, nexus.catalog_documents -- to nexus_svc, mirroring grants-nexus-svc.xml lines 124-162 (the chash_alias MAINTAIN grant, including its PG17+ version guard and NOTICE-on-unavailable fallback for older substrates). I deliberately did NOT add this changeset myself -- the task's explicit instruction was to STOP and flag rather than add DDL.
close_reason: Shipped develop d3aea8d0: grants-003-purge-vacuum-maintain, chash_alias-precedent shape (PG17+ guard, runAlways, RAISE NOTICE fallback). Default-role real-vacuum test proves the changeset provisions MAINTAIN end-to-end; three-site lockstep (parity test + behavioral pin comment).

title: operators/dispatch.py ephemeral mode: eager T1 mint blocks tool-free operator dispatch on storage-service unavailability
design:
nexus-4lkmz review finding (substantive-critic, uncommitted tree review 2026-08-07).

src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py `_build_dispatch_env(ephemeral=True)` (~lines
161-171) now calls `nexus.db.t1.mint_t1_session_token()` SYNCHRONOUSLY before
`claude_dispatch()` spawns the `claude -p` subprocess, and lets a mint
failure (RuntimeError) propagate UNHANDLED out of claude_dispatch (no
try/except at any of the ~17 call sites in mcp/core.py, taxonomy_cmd.py,
plans/bundle.py).

This makes EVERY operator dispatch — operator_summarize/extract/rank/
compare/generate/check/verify/aggregate/groupby/filter, nx_answer inline
planning, nx_tidy, nx_plan_audit, nx_enrich_beads, taxonomy auto-labeling —
depend on a live storage-service round-trip before the subprocess even
starts, and hard-fails the WHOLE dispatch if that mint fails. But per
claude_dispatch's own docstring, "Base argv is the stateless, tool-free
default" — mcp_servers=None/allowed_tools=None is the default for ~15 of 17
call sites, meaning the spawned subprocess has NO MCP tool access and
therefore CANNOT reach T1 at all. The minted session is dead weight for the
common case, and a mint failure now kills operator calls that never touch
T1.

This contradicts the "a T1-only failure must cost T1 only" principle this
SAME bead establishes for mcp/core.py's Branch 0 (nexus-brw1s / GH #1405) —
dispatch.py's own docstring claims "same posture as mcp.core's Branch 0"
(dispatch.py ~131-133), which is factually wrong: mcp.core DEFERS the mint
via a pre-init hook and scopes failure to T1-touching calls only (the
server starts, every non-T1 tool works); dispatch.py mints eagerly and
scopes failure to the ENTIRE dispatch.

No test exercises this blast radius — tests/test_operator_dispatch.py's
module-autouse `_fake_t1_dispatch_mint` fixture only ever stubs a
SUCCESSFUL mint; there is no test asserting what happens to claude_dispatch
when the mint raises.

Prior behavior (NX_T1_ISOLATED=1, a plain env-var assignment) had ZERO
network dependency for this path. This is a genuine new single point of
failure.

Fix direction (not prescriptive): don't mint synchronously for the
tool-free default path — only mint when mcp_servers/allowed_tools actually
grants T1 access, OR make mint failure non-fatal (log + omit
NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID, mirroring mcp.core's deferred-mint pattern)
so a tool-free claude -p call still proceeds when it doesn't need T1.

Also relatedly flagged (Significant, same review): no close_session/cleanup
for the freshly minted per-dispatch session — relies entirely on the
passive 24h TTL sweep backstop, unlike mcp.core's Branch 0 MINT path which
explicitly closes on teardown. Given operator dispatch is the high-volume
default path, this is real session-row accretion.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t nexus-4lkmz-implementation-notes.md
close_reason: Verified fixed in the nexus-4lkmz fix round (re-review 2026-08-07): grants_tool_access=bool(mcp_servers or allowed_tools) is the real, exhaustive dispatch-time signal (confirmed only 2/17 claude_dispatch call sites -- nx_enrich_beads, nx_plan_audit -- ever pass tool grants, both unconditionally via _subprocess_tool_grant()); tool-free dispatches (~15/17) never mint at all; mint failure on tool-granted dispatches logs a warning and leaves NX_T1_SESSION/SESSION_ID unset (no null-store branch, no raise). Non-vacuous tests confirmed (test_t1_discovery.py::TestDispatcherEphemeralMode + test_operator_dispatch.py::TestSubprocessContract, 105 tests total, all pass; ruff clean). A narrower follow-on nuance (mint-failure + live-parent-lease falls back to borrowing the parent's session rather than reaching the documented T1UnavailableThisProcessError, for the 2 tool-granted sites only -- not a rn3wo.1 violation, not a blast-radius regression) filed separately as nexus-ylof9 (P3, discovered-from nexus-4lkmz).

title: release-sandbox.sh step 7: unguarded echo|head -3|sed reintroduces SIGPIPE+pipefail+errexit false-abort (nexus-i66g4 class)
description:
tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh lines 628 and 632 (step 7/11, T2 memory roundtrip, uncommitted round-2/3 gate-fix diff): after the round-2 fix correctly wrapped `MEMORY_GET_OUT=$(nx memory get ...)` in an `if !` guard (immune to set -e per bash semantics — verified), the display line immediately inside BOTH branches is a bare, unguarded pipeline:

    echo "$MEMORY_GET_OUT" | head -3 | sed 's/^/  /'

`head -3` is an early-exit consumer: once it has read 3 lines it closes its stdin and exits, regardless of how much more data `echo` still has queued. Under `set -euo pipefail` this is the EXACT bug class already diagnosed and fixed elsewhere in this same diff (nexus-i66g4, T2 [21596] item 1: echo|grep -q on a degraded pipe buffer caused a false UPSHAKE failure this same session). Empirically reproduced 20/20 on this machine (currently healthy pipe state) with a >~50-100KB multi-line payload piped through `echo "$VAR" | head -3 | sed ...` under `set -euo pipefail`: the script aborts silently (raw SIGPIPE-driven errexit, no diagnostic) instead of continuing. The threshold scales down with pipe-buffer health — this machine measured a 512-byte degraded buffer earlier THIS SAME SESSION (T2 [21596]), at which size even a modest multi-line failure message (e.g. a Python traceback captured via 2>&1 on a real `nx memory get` failure) could trigger it.

Severity: the display line runs BEFORE the `SHAKEDOWN_FAILED+=(...)` bookkeeping line in both the if- and else-branches, so a SIGPIPE abort here means the step's OWN failure never gets recorded and the script dies with an unexplained raw exit instead of the intended "SHAKEDOWN FAILED: N release-gate step(s)..." banner — defeating the exact design intent (collect-and-continue + explicit verdict) that this round of fixes exists to guarantee, precisely in the scenario (large multi-line failure output) where that guarantee matters most.

Contrast: step 6's equivalent display (`echo "$SEARCH_OUT" | tail -10 | sed ...`, lines 608/612) uses `tail`, which reads to EOF and never early-exits — no SIGPIPE risk. Step 7's `head -3` is the outlier. The project already has the correct idiom for this exact hazard twice in this same file (line 100: `head -1 ... || true`; line 669: `... | head -15 | sed ... || true`) — just not applied to the two new step-7 sites.

Fix (2-line, safe): append `|| true` to both display lines. title: Shakedown release-checklist trigger list is under-inclusive for MinerU/docling version drift (uv.lock omitted; pyproject.toml has no mineru pin to diff)
description:
substantive-critic review of the uncommitted nexus-6xkdu diff (2026-08-06) found
that the new conditional release-checklist wiring (AGENTS.md 6c, docs/contributing.md
7c, .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md 6c) triggers the sandbox shakedown only when the
release diff touches: src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py, src/nexus/doc_indexer.py,
src/nexus/indexer.py, src/nexus/commands/index.py, src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py, or
"the mineru/docling pins in pyproject.toml".

VERIFIED (2026-08-06): pyproject.toml carries NO version pin for mineru at all --
line 121 is the fully unconstrained `"mineru[pipeline]"`. docling has only a floor
(`"docling>=2.76.0"`, line 75). The actual resolved/locked versions (mineru==3.1.11
per uv.lock:1826) live in uv.lock, which is NOT in the trigger-path list on any of
the three doc surfaces.

CONSEQUENCE: a routine `uv lock --upgrade` / dependency-bump commit that changes
mineru's or docling's resolved version touches uv.lock only -- none of the five
listed source files, and nothing in pyproject.toml (there is no mineru version
string there to change). Per the documented rule, that release would NOT require
the shakedown, so a MinerU (or Docling) package bump -- the most direct mechanism
by which its bundled model-loading/extraction behavior could change -- ships
unverified. This reproduces the exact bug class nexus-6xkdu was filed to close:
"nothing would tell us MinerU broke," now scoped specifically to the
package-version-bump case.

nexus-6xkdu's own bead text names the same class of risk explicitly: "nexus-go5ou
(unpinned HuggingFace weights - MinerU's ~2-3 GB are also unpinned, which is a
candidate cause of the drift and a reproducibility hole in its own right)" -- go5ou
itself is scoped to the cross-encoder ONNX fetch, not MinerU, but the general
"unpinned upstream artifact drifts silently" mechanism it documents applies
identically to MinerU's own weight-serving behavior per a given mineru package
version, which nexus does not control or pin beyond uv.lock's package-version
capture.

Hal's revised recommendation on nexus-6xkdu (2026-08-01) called for shakedown to
run "at release" without a stated diff-based qualifier, and gave the cost estimate
"~5-10 min warm... per release" -- reading as unconditional. The implementer's
choice to make the wiring conditional (mirroring the pre-existing, also-unmechanized
SKILL.md 6b "upgrade-shakeout" precedent) was not bounced back to Hal for
confirmation and is not flagged anywhere in the T2 implementation record (21518)
as a deviation requiring sign-off, nor is this specific residual (uv.lock-only
mineru/docling bumps escape the trigger) tracked in any bead or docstring -- unlike
the NX_MINERU_EXPECTED dormancy, which IS honestly disclosed.

FIX OPTIONS (Hal's call, per this repo's convention):
  (a) add uv.lock to the trigger-path list (crude, but any resolved mineru/docling
      version change touches it -- closes the gap mechanically)
  (b) confirm with Hal that "conditional, these 5 files + pyproject.toml pins" is
      accepted as satisfying "run shakedown at release" given this residual
  (c) drop conditionality for the shakedown specifically and run it on every
      release, matching the literal wording of option (a) as written in the bead
  (d) mechanize the trigger check (git diff <tag>..HEAD -- <paths>, blocking
      assert) rather than leaving it to a human read of three markdown paragraphs
      -- see also the parallel SIGNIFICANT finding about doc-only enforcement in
      the same critique.

Also: the docstring rewrite in tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py (test_mineru_path_
preserves_formulas, nexus-6xkdu) states unconditionally "the release process ...
invokes the shakedown so that coverage is real rather than aspirational" without
noting the conditional trigger three lines above it in AGENTS.md -- a smaller
version of the same overclaim.

Full critique: T2 nexus/nexus-6xkdu-critique-2026-08-06.
close_reason: Structurally mooted: the conditionality/trigger-list was dropped entirely (round 2 of nexus-6xkdu) — shakedown runs unconditionally on every release per Hal's original bead text, so no diff-based heuristic (uv.lock included) is load-bearing. Critic's round-2 closure verification (T2 [21520] round-2 section): zero residue repo-wide, three checklist surfaces aligned, and unconditional is strictly better than patching the list since MinerU weight-serving can drift with zero diff to any nexus-tracked file. Residual supply-chain observation beaded separately as nexus-ctmtq (P3).

title: nx t3 gc corpus-wide sweep lacks the RUNFENCE index_state='complete' precondition Hal required for fix (b)
design:
Bead nexus-39upx's own comment thread (Hal, 2026-08-02 11:23) states, verbatim:
"PRECONDITION ON OPTION (b) from the 5xn3k RUNFENCE design... The corpus-wide
sweep (b) MUST filter on index_state = 'complete'. Sweeping a document that is
mid-index would delete chunks an in-flight run has already written but has not
yet manifested... Treat this as a stated requirement on (b), not a
nice-to-have."

`nx t3 gc` (src/nexus/commands/t3.py::gc_cmd) IS fix (b) — the corpus-wide
manifest-diff sweep the bead's FIX OPTIONS section describes. Verified this
precondition is NOT implemented anywhere in the chain gc_cmd uses, as of the
2026-08-05/06 nexus-39upx diff (RDR-145 note-protection fix) landing on
develop:

- `grep index_state src/nexus/commands/t3.py` — zero hits.
- `CatalogRepository.chashesForCollection` (service/.../CatalogRepository.java
  ~3937, the exact SQL gc_cmd's alive-set reads) filters ONLY
  PHYSICAL_COLLECTION + DELETED_AT IS NULL — no index_state predicate.
- The RUNFENCE arc (nexus-5xn3k.1 through .7, all CLOSED) wired
  index_state/begin/complete/fail/verify into the INDEXING pipeline
  (producer side: doc_indexer.py, mcp_infra.py, commands/index.py,
  commands/catalog.py, health.py) but never into nx t3 gc's
  candidate-filtering (confirmed via `grep -rl index_state src/nexus/` — 10
  files, commands/t3.py absent).
- docs/cli-reference.md's `nx t3 gc` section documents the age-based
  --orphan-window (default 30d) as the ONLY temporal safety net; no
  index_state/concurrency caveat anywhere.

The 30-day orphan-window is NOT a substitute for the stated requirement: it
protects the common case (fresh chunks from a fast in-flight reindex are
excluded by recency) but not a stalled/long-running reindex whose OLD,
superseded chunks are already >30 days stale while a NEW extraction is still
in flight and has not yet atomically replaced the manifest.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, NOT LATER: T2 session memory (2026-08-04/05 ship log)
records "Hal arms: ... t3 gc at next shakedown" as the actual planned next
step for fix (b) — a corpus-wide `nx t3 gc` run against the ~8,234 orphaned
chunks measured across 6 collections (SHAKEOUT-7.1.1). Running it without this
filter carries exactly the data-loss hazard Hal named on the bead.

Neither the nexus-39upx implementation record (T2 21513) nor its code review
(T2 21514, SHIP verdict) mentions this precondition — it is not in the hazard
list (1-4), not in the DEFER-LOUD list. Found during substantive-critique of
that diff (T2 21515).

FIX SHAPE (not yet designed in detail): gc_cmd's candidate computation needs
an index_state='complete' filter alongside chashes_for_collection /
live_note_chashes, sourced from catalog_documents.index_state — either a new
client-side read (documentsByContentType-style, scoped to --collection) or a
server-side predicate added to chashesForCollection / a dedicated endpoint.
Must not silently skip the check on a pre-RUNFENCE engine (same fail-open-to-
today's-behavior floor-tolerance stance the RUNFENCE arc used elsewhere).

Blocks: the corpus-wide "t3 gc at next shakedown" operator run should not
proceed until this lands, or the run must be scoped/timed to guarantee no
concurrent indexing against the target collection(s).
close_reason: Landed as 5528bbb7, CI green. nx t3 gc refuses any destructive run when the collection holds a document not index_state='complete' (collection-level circuit breaker — post-RDR-108 chunks carry no doc_id so per-candidate attribution is impossible), override --allow-incomplete-index-state; note-shaped docs and pre-RUNFENCE engines (index_state_reported=False) do not block. Critic-verified against Hal's verbatim bead comments incl. the in-band-sweep-needs-no-guard reasoning (Hal's position-0 manifest-replace argument, independently verified). The 2 initially-vacuous refusal tests un-masked from the jqrtp guard and falsified red/green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Round-2 substantive-critique verification (T2 nexus/nexus-39upx-critique-2026-08-05):
the implementation is CORRECT (verified independently, code reads correctly and the
refusal fires in isolation), but 2 of its 3 "refuses" tests in tests/test_t3_gc.py are
VACUOUS:

  test_gc_refuses_when_a_document_is_actively_indexing
  test_gc_refuses_when_a_document_is_fence_failed

Neither test's fixture (_register_indexing_doc_active / _register_failed_doc_active)

title: dt.py isinstance-dispatch on PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS is non-exhaustive — 3rd tuple member crashes with AttributeError, re-aborting the batch
description:
substantive-critic finding on nexus-rlkgu (T1 cc3d9989, T2 pending write).

src/nexus/commands/dt.py's two per-record catch sites (index_cmd ~line
737 and ~line 812) now do:

    except PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
        if isinstance(exc, IndexRunVerifyRefused):
            ...
        else:  # ChunkLandingUnverifiedError -- the D1 stale-positive fence
            _log.error(..., collection=exc.collection, count=exc.count)
            failed.append((uuid, path, str(exc)))

This binary if/else silently assumes PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS has
EXACTLY two members forever. Empirically verified (probe reverted, not
committed): adding a third member to the tuple in errors.py, and
classifying it in the test file's _RECORD_LEVEL set so
test_record_level_matches_production_tuple stays green, makes ALL 14
tests in tests/test_rlkgu_per_record_catch_tripwire.py pass -- gate 1
(loop coverage) and gate 2 (classification completeness) both report
green, giving the appearance the tripwire's job is done.

But at runtime, raising the third exception type through dt.py's actual
handler crashes with AttributeError (e.g. 'ManifestQuotaExceededError'
object has no attribute 'collection'), because the else-branch
unconditionally treats "not IndexRunVerifyRefused" as
"must be ChunkLandingUnverifiedError". That AttributeError propagates
OUT of the except block and out of the per-record try/except entirely --
reproducing the EXACT bug class (nexus-2fyb/qo84l/9800y/hb10j: one
offending record aborts the whole batch) that nexus-rlkgu exists to
prevent, for occurrence 4, with both tripwire gates reporting green.

The AST-based gates (both in test_rlkgu_per_record_catch_tripwire.py)
only check that an except clause's TYPE EXPRESSION covers the tuple --
neither gate inspects the handler BODY, so a non-exhaustive isinstance
dispatch inside a covering except clause is invisible to both.

Fix: replace the binary if/else with an exhaustive dispatch (elif chain
ending in `else: raise` to fail loud on an unhandled member per the
no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness standing directive, or a dict/table
keyed by exact type) at both dt.py call sites, AND add a Gate 3 test
that raises EVERY live member of PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS through
the real dt.py handler (or asserts the dispatch's isinstance-branch count
tracks len(PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS) mechanically) so a future
third member fails a RUNTIME kill control, not just the AST shape checks.

Repro steps (probe, already reverted):
1. Add `class ProbeError(NexusError): pass` before the
   PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS tuple in errors.py; add it to the
   tuple.
