title: fresh-install-mvv.sh --published mode does not scrub ambient UV_*/PIP_* env before uv tool install — 'never touches the live install' claim is false under UV_TOOL_DIR override
description:
Found during substantive-critic review of nexus-796zn (T1 8fdf... developer commit b69b26b1).

tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh's --published branch runs:
  env HOME="$HOME_DIR" uv tool install --python 3.12 "$PKG_SPEC"
  TOOL_DIR="$(env HOME="$HOME_DIR" uv tool dir)"
  TOOL_BIN_DIR="$(env HOME="$HOME_DIR" uv tool dir --bin)"

Only HOME is overridden — ambient UV_TOOL_DIR / UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR / UV_INDEX_URL /
UV_DEFAULT_INDEX / PIP_INDEX_URL pass straight through, unlike _nx()'s runtime
calls which use `env -i` with an explicit allowlist (the r5f3c-lesson pattern
the script's own header claims to follow: "nothing ambient is trusted").

Empirically verified (2026-08-05):
  $ env UV_TOOL_DIR=/tmp/probe HOME=/tmp/home2 uv tool dir
  /tmp/probe          <- NOT HOME-derived when UV_TOOL_DIR is set ambient

So the script's own comment — "`uv tool dir` ... is purely HOME-derived ...
resolves entirely inside the sandbox" — is false whenever UV_TOOL_DIR (or
UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR) is set in the operator's shell. The comment cites
scripts/reinstall-tool.sh as "the identical pattern", but reinstall-tool.sh
is explicitly the NON-sandboxed live-install tool (it never sets HOME) — it
demonstrates HOME-derivation in the common case, not isolation from env
override, so citing it as precedent for the isolation invariant is a false
equivalence.

Impact if UV_TOOL_DIR ever IS set ambiently (devcontainer, CI runner, some
shells' rc files, a future workflow): `uv tool install` clobbers whatever
"conexus" tool lives at that location — which, if it coincides with the
operator's real uv tool dir, IS the live nx install (same mechanism
scripts/reinstall-tool.sh uses deliberately). This is exactly the incident
class feedback_dont_break_live_nexus_install is a top-severity standing
directive to prevent, and it is NEW exposure (the pre-existing local-wheel
layer's `uv build`/`uv venv` calls always target an explicit `$VENV` path
with no "live tool" ambiguity; `uv tool install` structurally does).

UV_CACHE_DIR was checked separately and confirmed benign (cache location
only, does not affect uv tool dir / resolution outcome).

Fix: either (a) run the install step through env -i with an explicit
allowlist matching _nx()'s pattern (HOME, PATH, proxy vars only), or (b)
explicitly force UV_TOOL_DIR="$HOME_DIR/.local/share/uv/tools" and
UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR="$HOME_DIR/.local/bin" on the uv tool install / uv tool dir
invocations so the sandbox wins regardless of ambient state, or (c) both.
Also correct or remove the false "identical pattern" comment referencing
reinstall-tool.sh.

Relay: nexus-796zn (P1, developer commit b69b26b1). Critique: substantive-critic pass, 2026-08-05.
close_reason: Fixed in this diff: uv tool install/dir scrubbed via env -i allowlist (_uv_sandboxed()) instead of bare env HOME=..., which left UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_BIN_HOME/UV_INDEX_URL/PIP_INDEX_URL reachable. Regression test tests/test_fresh_install_mvv_published_mode.py::test_published_install_scrubs_ambient_uv_tool_env proves isolation holds with all six set to decoy values via a stub uv on PATH. Re-verified local-wheel mode e2e PASSED post-fix.

title: nexus-tp8yk's new integration test has zero CI wiring — the only real-engine proof of D1 never runs automatically
description:
tests/integration/test_tp8yk_manifest_never_outruns_chunks.py is the sole production-
layer test that drives index_pdf() against a REAL engine/T3 substrate and proves D1
(the core fix: manifest rows structurally unreachable for an unconfirmed chunk batch),
including the mandatory kill control (test_kill_control_reverting_the_raise_reproduces_
the_damage) that falsifies the fix by reverting it.

It is marked @pytest.mark.integration, which the repo's default addopts
(`-m 'not integration and not slow'`, pyproject.toml:211) excludes from every routine
`uv run pytest` invocation. Exhaustive grep across every .github/workflows/*.yml and all
.sh files repo-wide for "tp8yk" and "tests/integration/" returns ZERO hits — this file is
not wired into ci.yml, local-service-gate-nightly.yml, or any other workflow.

This project already built the exact infrastructure needed for this class of file one
week earlier: nexus-5opzu (local-service-gate-nightly.yml, "Ungated integration files")
maintains a closed FILES allowlist of tests/db/* modules with NO other automated gate,
run nightly via `-o addopts="" -m integration`, backstopped by a non-vacuity assert
script requiring >=1 non-skipped testcase per named file. test_tp8yk_manifest_never_
outruns_chunks.py was not added to that set (it's tests/integration/, not tests/db/, but
the same principle applies) or to any other gate.

Per CLAUDE.md: "Functional gates are self-provisioning scripts, never ambient machine
state. A gate that skip-passes when its dependency is absent must carry a max-skip /
non-vacuity assert." Here there is no gate at all to skip-pass — the file simply never
runs unless a human remembers to type
`uv run pytest tests/integration/test_tp8yk_manifest_never_outruns_chunks.py -m integration`.

Fix: add this file (or a new tests/integration/ FILES set) to local-service-gate-
nightly.yml's ungated-integration-files step + its non-vacuity assert, or an equivalent
scheduled/CI gate.

Found by substantive-critic review of nexus-tp8yk's uncommitted implementation,
2026-08-04.

title: nx dt index: ChunkLandingUnverifiedError not caught per-record, aborts whole DT batch (nexus-tp8yk D1 regression of nexus-2fyb/qo84l class)

description:
REVIEW GATE after nexus-utpuw .2 .3 .4. Blocks P2/P3.

This is the highest-subtlety surface in the arc; three constraints here are the whole design and each fails SILENTLY if got wrong:

 2. Each venv MUST be built AT its final versioned path (shebangs bake absolute paths; the tree is not relocatable). Verify no build-then-move anywhere.
 3. Flip MUST be symlink-then-rename. 'ln -sfn' is unlink+symlink and leaves a window with no 'current'. Verify the actual command, incl. macOS mv -h vs GNU mv -T.

Critic should specifically pressure-test: are the shim-template tests NON-VACUOUS (do they assert the absence of a bare exec-through-current, or merely that some exec exists)? title: utpuw P7a: live-holder flip E2E, FAST tier — assert the CPython sys.prefix property that q3xrx is made of
description:
PHASE 7 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .4 .3 .6. THE MANDATED LIVE-HOLDER TEST (relay deliverable). Fast tier so it guards the shim form on EVERY run.

The q3xrx root cause is a CPython fact (research finding 2): Modules/getpath.py checks for pyvenv.cfg adjacent to the executable AS INVOKED (unresolved) BEFORE realpath. So the test must assert the PROPERTY, not merely that nothing crashed:

  A1. build generation A, flip, spawn a holder THROUGH THE SHIM
  A2. assert the holder sys.prefix contains the gen-A path and does NOT contain the substring 'current'
  A3. build generation B, flip
  A4. tell the holder (over stdin) to import a module it has NOT yet imported
  A5. assert the import SUCCEEDS and mod.__file__ is under generation A
  A6. assert a NEW spawn through the same shim lands in generation B
  A7. assert generation A still exists on disk (GC did not reap it under its holder)

A2 IS THE REGRESSION TRIPWIRE and must be its own NAMED test, not an incidental assert: it is what fails loudly if someone later 'simplifies' the shim to exec .../current/bin/nx. It fails BEFORE any flip, which makes the diagnosis obvious.

COST CONTROL: the property is package-INDEPENDENT, so this tier uses two generations of a 3-line FIXTURE package with one console script — seconds, not the 60-90s two real conexus builds would cost. That requires the installer parameterized on package name; legitimize it as the same isolation-knob family as NX_TOOLS_DIR/NX_BIN_DIR (.1), NOT as a test-only backdoor.

Follow the repo bash-script test convention: tests/scripts/, subprocess.run(['bash', _SCRIPT, ...]), env HOME=tmp_path, curated PATH excluding ~/.local/bin (template: tests/scripts/test_reinstall_tool_downgrade_guard.py:30-105).

GOTCHA: project memory — Bash 5.3 heredocs >512B deadlock when macOS degrades pipes. Prefer sibling .py fixture files over large heredocs in the spawned holder.

- :50 _PROC_MARKERS = ('uv/tools/conexus', '.local/bin/nx'). The first substring never appears in a generation argv. The second survives but only for nx-argv'd processes.
- :444 the pre-kill pid-recycle re-check uses the HARDCODED _PROC_MARKERS even though :372 derives a good marker from _install_root().parents[2]. So even after fixing :372, every legitimate aspect-worker is rejected as 'gone or recycled; skipped' and nothing is ever restarted.

- --force (:30, :34) — every remaining use;
- --cycle-daemons (:29, :33, :49-55, :195-198).

NEGATIVE SWEEP (do not skip — these become instructions for flags that no longer exist): AGENTS.md:163, CLAUDE.md:163, .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:172, tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:184 all still reference --force/--cycle-daemons. Also reinstall-tool.sh's own :21-24,50,123,125,191,193.

--- AUDIT FINDING F4 (nx_plan_audit 2026-08-04) — FOLDED IN ---
Deleting --force leaves the SURVIVING guards with no deliberate-override story, and both have
legitimate override cases: the script's own advice at the old :110 tells you to install a released
build over a dev one (which trips the registry-over-directory guard), and a genuine downgrade is a
real workflow.

RESOLUTION: the surviving guards keep an override, but NOT a resurrected general-purpose --force.

made safety impossible (the holder refusal, --force, --cycle-daemons). The downgrade and
divergent-source guards are a DIFFERENT failure class which comment 1 explicitly preserves, and a
guard you cannot deliberately override is not a guard, it is a wall.

MUST NOT: reintroduce a single flag that bypasses BOTH guards at once — that is --force wearing a
new name and it will drift back into bypassing everything.

comments.text:
EXPLAIN verdict (debugger, local repro). CONFIRMED: dcf77fb7's live_chunks predicate is the cause — but NOT via a defeated index, and the bead's partial-index-on-deleted_at hypothesis is REFUTED with EXPLAIN evidence (plan byte-identical, index never used).

Repro: pgvector/pgvector:pg17 Testcontainer + Liquibase master, 76k chunks_384 / 57k manifest rows / 1k docs / 37 tombstoned, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) as the NOBYPASSRLS svc role with RLS live.

Three mechanisms:
M1 PG turns both correlated EXISTS into HASHED SubPlans that SEQ-SCAN the ENTIRE catalog_document_chunks manifest twice per query (idx_catalog_chunks_chash never used). Fixed per-query cost LINEAR IN TOTAL MANIFEST SIZE, not in rows examined — so it grows with the corpus. Best fit for the cloud step.
M2 Cost estimate inflates ~160x (8,130 -> 1,290,101), crossing jit_above_cost + jit_inline/optimize: ~118ms of pure JIT COMPILE added per query.
M3 Same inflation flips the gate probe off Seq Scan onto chunks_384_pk Index Scan, ~10x buffers (6,415 -> 63,166).

Gate probe, same session: no-predicate 8,130 cost / 1,355ms / no JIT / 6,415 bufs | SHIPPED 1,290,101 / 1,536ms / 118ms JIT / 63,166 bufs | FIX 12,009 / 1,364ms / no JIT / 21,288 bufs. HNSW-first: 153 / 180 / 160 ms.

FIX (in working tree, UNCOMMITTED, no DDL, no Liquibase): rewrite liveChunksPredicate to the DEAD-SET form — one EXISTS bounded by the tombstoned population instead of the whole manifest. live <=> NOT EXISTS(dead parent AND no live parent), exactly equivalent to NOT EXISTS(dead) OR EXISTS(live). Plan becomes a Nested Loop Anti Join off the 37 tombstoned docs; cost/JIT/plan restored to the pre-dcf77fb7 shape.

EQUIVALENCE CAVEAT (brief reviewers on this): the forms differ on exactly one input — a manifest row with no owning document (old=DEAD, new=LIVE). Unreachable because fk_catalog_chunks_catalog_doc (fk-001-5) deletes orphans then adds the FK with NO 'NOT VALID'. Contract tests cannot construct that case, so green tests do not prove equivalence on their own; the FK does.

Also rejected with evidence: covering index INCLUDE(doc_id) (no change); partial idx WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL (identical plans with the fix at 1k docs — projected-only value at cloud doc counts, do not ship as 'the fix'); dead-parent-first two-subquery variant (live-side hash still builds, cost got worse).

Secondary (NOT applied): the predicate is folded into 'scope', so on the selective branch it is evaluated TWICE — redundant on the rank query since liveness is a pure function of (tenant_id, chash) and every chash in the IN-list already passed the gate. Moving the append from scope to gate drops it safely. Deferred: the fix already restores baseline and this changes which read sites carry the filter (3ck2g-class, deserves its own review).

Latent: at small work_mem PG cannot hash the subplans and falls back to per-row correlated execution (bufs 63,166 -> 75,636) — a silent strategy change as the cloud manifest outgrows work_mem.

Drift: search_topic_scoped_384/768/1024 (catalog-006 cs4-6, carried into catalog-019) still carry the OLD two-subquery shape in SQL-function bodies — now divergent from the Java predicate. Follow-up bead warranted.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN RECORD (Hal, captured by debugger) — why chunk liveness is derived at read time, and what would change that.

WHY DERIVED, NOT STORED. Chunks are content-addressed and SHARED: identical chunk text in a collection collapses to one row by design (RDR-108/RDR-180), and the catalog manifest preserves position via (doc_id, position) rows pointing at the shared chash. A shared chunk therefore has no liveness OF ITS OWN — its visibility is a function of the set of documents currently pointing at it. Document-level soft-delete stays drift-free precisely BECAUSE reads consult that truth at read time instead of caching it: there is no second copy of the liveness fact to fall out of sync, and tombstone/restore/purge-trash all move exactly one field (catalog_documents.deleted_at) with no fan-out write. That is the design, and it is unchanged by this bead.

WHAT THE BUG ACTUALLY WAS. The whole-manifest scan was ACCIDENTAL PREDICATE PHRASING, not design intent. The intended shape has always been a per-candidate indexed lookup: for the chunk in hand, ask whether any live document points at it — an index probe on idx_catalog_chunks_chash plus a PK probe on catalog_documents. The shipped phrasing `NOT EXISTS(any manifest) OR EXISTS(live manifest)` instead gave PostgreSQL two subqueries it could only satisfy by hashing the ENTIRE manifest, converting a per-candidate probe into a fixed per-query full-table cost (and, downstream, ~160x cost inflation -> JIT compile -> outer plan flip). The dead-set rewrite restores the intended shape; it does not change the model. Read-time derivation was never the problem.

ESCALATION PATH, IF EVER NEEDED. If cloud scale ever makes even the corrected plan hot — i.e. post-deploy p50 shows the fixed component still material — the escalation is materialized liveness on the chunk row: refcounts or an is_live flag on chunks_<dim>, maintained by the manifest write path. That is a genuine model change (it introduces the second copy of the liveness fact that the current design deliberately does not have), so it is a full RDR, not a patch, and its central design obligation is the DRIFT TRIPWIRE: a materialized refcount that silently disagrees with the manifest resurrects tombstoned content in search results, which is the nexus-3ck2g failure class with a worse blast radius. The tripwire gets designed in from the start, not bolted on.

DECISION: deliberately DEFERRED behind post-deploy p50 evidence. We do not take on a materialized-state design — and its permanent drift-surveillance obligation — on the strength of a projection. The dead-set rewrite is the cheap, model-preserving fix; measure the cloud after it deploys, and only then decide whether anything further is warranted.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Consolidated review round applied (debugger). Full engine suite GREEN on the result: ./mvnw -o test -Pprebuilt-jooq -> BUILD SUCCESS, 149 classes, 0 failures, 0 errors.

1. jOOQ TWIN (Sig-2) — ANSWER: YES, M1 present, and proportionally MUCH worse than hybrid. Probed by reflecting the private liveChunksCondition and EXPLAINing jOOQ's OWN rendered SQL (not a hand-copy); rendered form confirmed as a plain bytea comparison. Same two whole-manifest hashed SubPlans (56,972 rows each). get() 200 ids: 0.270ms -> 27.329ms (101x), buffers 723 -> 2,715. list() 100 rows: 0.037ms -> 27.331ms (739x), buffers 125 -> 2,121. The fixed SubPlan tax is a rounding error on a ~1.4s hybrid query but is essentially the ENTIRE cost of a point lookup — the critic's proportionality hypothesis is confirmed with numbers. REWRITTEN to the typed dead-set form: get() -> 0.917ms, list() -> 1.059ms (~30x and ~26x better than the old shape), driven as a Nested Loop Anti Join with per-candidate index probes.
   TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS: (a) an intermediate probe that spliced an UNALIASED raw-SQL dead-set into the rendered list() query measured only 27.3 -> 25.1ms, and I wrote that up as a residual in the code comment. The ACTUAL typed implementation (lcc_m2/lcc_d2 aliases) does not reproduce it — 1.059ms. Comment corrected; no residual, no bead filed. The aliasing is load-bearing and is now flagged in-code against future "simplification". (b) I briefly suspected ChashHex.hex() wrapped the indexed column in a SQL function; it does not — retracted, verified against jOOQ output.

2. Dead-set-size sweep (Sig-3) — NO CROSSOVER through 60% tombstoned. Mutated deleted_at on the same fixture + re-ANALYZE. tombstoned 3%/10%/30%/60% = 1,702/5,674/17,033/34,125 dead manifest rows. OLD form: 1,521 / 1,527 / 1,516 / 1,527 ms, JIT 120-127ms every time, estimated cost CONSTANT at 1,291,402 (manifest-driven, dead-set-INVARIANT). DEAD-SET: 1,368 / 530 / 536 / 523 ms, no JIT, cost flat ~12,000. The dead-set form wins at every fraction by a WIDENING margin — a mass-tombstone event does not flip the ordering. Honest caveat: the improvement at higher fractions partly reflects fewer surviving rows for the trigram filter, not purely predicate cost; the claim supported is the one asked (ordering never flips). Operationally purge-trash drains the dead set, so steady state stays at the low end.

3. Magnitude language softened (Sig-1). T2 [21409] now separates PROVEN (mechanism identified and locally eliminated) from PENDING (that these account for the specific ~250ms cloud step). It states plainly that locally the 172ms delta is DOMINATED by M2's JIT (118ms, ~69%), not M1, and that M2 is inert if jit=off in cloud. Relay items are now a prominent top-of-document list: SHOW jit/jit_above_cost/jit_inline_above_cost/work_mem; tenant catalog_document_chunks count; before/after p50.

4. FK coupling discoverable from BOTH ends (reviewer M1). Added ForeignKeyConstraintTest#manifestFk_isValidated_liveChunksPredicateDependsOnIt asserting pg_constraint.convalidated = true for fk_catalog_chunks_catalog_doc, with a javadoc explaining that a merely-PRESENT constraint is insufficient (a NOT VALID FK leaves pre-existing orphans and silently flips those chunks visible). ForeignKeyConstraintTest 28/28. Added a pointer comment in fk-001-catalog-cross-store.xml changeset fk-001-5 — placed as an XML comment OUTSIDE <sql> deliberately, so the changeset checksum on already-migrated deployments is unaffected (an in-SQL comment would have broken them, since these changesets use stripComments="false").

5. strandedChunkCount (reviewer L1) — comment added: retains the old shape, diagnostics-only (~3 calls per operator-invoked report), and unlike the predicate it computes the dead set as its RESULT rather than filtering by it. Names the porting trigger (periodic health poll / dashboard / per-request census) and points at liveChunksPredicate + T2 [21409].

6. Design record captured as a separate bd comment on this bead (derived-liveness rationale, accidental-phrasing diagnosis, materialized-refcount escalation path behind a full RDR with drift tripwire, deliberately deferred behind post-deploy p50 evidence).

STILL UNDISPOSED — critic Sig-4: there is no automated cost/plan-shape regression gate anywhere in the service suite (TombstoneFilterGateTest is purely structural name-presence regexes). dcf77fb7 shipped green through every existing gate and surfaced only via a cloud p50 relay; this fix adds no tripwire either. Needs a disposition from Hal/orchestrator: bead a perf tripwire, or explicitly accept conexus-side cloud monitoring as the only guard. I have deliberately NOT filed a bead for it — it is a scope decision, not a finding.

Tree (uncommitted): PgVectorRepository.java (both predicates), CatalogRepository.java (comment), ForeignKeyConstraintTest.java (new assertion), fk-001-catalog-cross-store.xml (XML comment). Both throwaway harnesses deleted from the tree, archived at /tmp/msz9i-HybridExplainProbeTest.java.bak and /tmp/msz9i-MzProbeTest.java.bak.

title: purge-trash execute purges only a fraction of its own dry-run population — 2 of 63 age-eligible docs purged, 61 left, reported as success
description: First production execute (2026-08-03, engine v0.1.63, dev-tree client 7e3e8f55): dry-run reported documents_purged=63, chunks_1024_stranded=285. Execute reported documents_purged=2, chunks_1024_stranded=285. Post-execute dry-run census: 61 docs STILL eligible, chunks 0 (sweep half worked completely). No error surfaced — partial execution reported as success, the silent-partial class. Hypothesis to check first: the execute path's doc-purge query joins docs to their swept chunks (INNER JOIN semantics — only docs owning stranded chunks purged: the 2 purged docs may be exactly the owners of the 285 chunks) while dry-run counts age-eligible tombstoned docs unconditionally — a dry-run/execute population divergence. Engine half dcf77fb7; client verb unreleased (dev tree only). Production state: safe (nothing wrongly deleted; under-deletion only), re-run of execute is NOT the fix until root-caused.
close_reason: Fully resolved end-to-end same day: root cause jOOQ Duration→interval calendar normalization (dry-run exact-days vs execute calendar-months; latent over-deletion in short months); fixed at 9b3c89ad (day-only interval, single server-side predicate, partial-never-silent contract), dual-reviewed 0-Critical, falsify-verified both halves; shipped in engine-service-v0.1.64, deployed + edge-gated; production re-execute purged 61/61 with eligible==purged and post-census 0. Residual test hardening rides nexus-nhfqa (re-scoped). Records: T2 ff85q-root-cause [21403], critique [21404].

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (tree uncommitted, awaiting orchestrator review). Full writeup: T2 nexus/ff85q-root-cause [21403].

ROOT CAUSE: CatalogRepository.purgeTrash built nexus.purge_trash's 'older_than interval' argument via YearToSecond.valueOf(Duration.ofDays(n)). jOOQ normalises a Duration into an interval's year/month/day fields using FIXED 30-day months and 365.25-day years, so 30 days becomes the interval '+0-1 +0' -- literally '1 mon'. PostgreSQL evaluates NOW() - interval '1 mon' with CALENDAR arithmetic (28-31 real days). Meanwhile the dry-run preview (agedTombstoneCount) independently computed OffsetDateTime.now(UTC).minusDays(n) -- exact days, Java clock. Two cut points over one population; every tombstone in the gap is counted by the preview and skipped by the DELETE, silently.

Production arithmetic (2026-08-03, default 30 days): preview threshold 2026-07-04, execute threshold 2026-07-03 (July has 31 days) -- a 24h gap. The 61 skipped docs are predicted to be a single bulk-tombstone batch inside that window; the 2 purged are older than it.

THE BEAD'S LEAD HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. catalog-003-soft-delete.xml:286-289 Step 4 is 'DELETE FROM nexus.catalog_documents WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at <= NOW() - older_than' -- no chunk join, no LIMIT, no per-row precondition, no trigger on catalog_documents, identical RLS/tenant predicate on both sides. The divergence was in the Java argument BINDING, plus the preview being a second independently-written definition of the same population.

DANGEROUS COROLLARY: the skew's SIGN depends on the month. From a March run, NOW() - interval '1 mon' is 28 days back -- LATER than a 30-day threshold -- so the execute would delete tombstones 28-30 days old that the dry-run never showed. This was a latent OVER-deletion (data-loss) bug; August happened to give the safe direction.

FIX (3 parts): (1) olderThanInterval() builds new YearToSecond(new YearToMonth(0,0), new DayToSecond(n)) -- all magnitude in the DAY field, nothing for jOOQ to normalise; (2) agedTombstoneCount now evaluates its threshold SERVER-SIDE from the identical now()-{interval} expression and the same interval argument, so one population has one predicate and one clock (also removes cloud app-host/DB-host clock skew); (3) purgeTrash measures the eligible population in the SAME transaction before the call and returns documents_eligible next to documents_purged, WARN-logging event=purge_trash_partial on mismatch -- and nx catalog purge-trash prints the report then EXITS NON-ZERO naming the shortfall, so a partial can never again read as bare success.

BUG-CLASS SWEEP: nexus.purge_trash is the only interval-bound routine in the codebase; no sibling instances.

TESTS: new CatalogPurgeTrashPopulationParityTest (3) -- RED before the fix with 'expected: 6L but was: 2L' and survivors exactly the tombstones inside the interval gap, the production signature at small scale. Uses a 365-day threshold deliberately: a 30-day threshold's skew is ZERO whenever the preceding month has 30 days (Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov), so a 30-day test would pass a third of the year regardless of the bug. Plus 5 client tests (TestPartialPurgeIsNeverReportedAsSuccess), falsified mechanically. Green: 250 Java, 334 Python. Service jar rebuilt.

STILL OPEN (read-only, needs production): the MECHANISM is proven, the MAGNITUDE (61 docs in one 24h window) is inferred. Discriminator, all safe dry-runs: 'nx catalog purge-trash --older-than-days 30/32/33 --json'. A sharp drop between 32 and 33 confirms the single-2026-07-03-batch reading; if the count stays high at 33+, something else also contributes and this bead should not close on this fix alone.

DEPLOYMENT: the load-bearing half is ENGINE-side, inert until the next engine-service tag + deploy. Do NOT re-run the production execute against the currently deployed engine.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REVIEW ITEMS APPLIED (tree still uncommitted). Dual review: code-review-expert APPROVED (0 Critical/High/Medium); substantive-critic 0 Critical / 3 Significant (T2 nexus/ff85q-critique-2026-08-04 [21404]). All settled.

1. Sig-1 (test pins one direction only) — CatalogPurgeTrashPopulationParityTest class javadoc now carries an explicit SCOPE paragraph: this suite pins the UNDER-deletion direction ONLY, and green here is NOT 'both directions pinned'. The 365-day threshold chosen for month-independent determinism structurally guarantees the buggy calendar interval is LARGER than exact days (370/371 > 365), so the over-deletion corollary (short-month shrinkage -> purging tombstones NEWER than the dry-run showed = real data loss) is never exercised, and no fixed day-count can force it since the sign depends on which real months 'now' spans. The fix is symmetric by construction (day-only field leaves nothing to normalize either direction), so this is a regression-coverage gap, not a correctness gap. Clock-injected test tracked on nexus-nhfqa.

2. Sig-2/Sig-3 (partial-report message) — _fail_on_partial_purge rewritten. Keeps the non-zero exit (partial-never-silent is the contract) but the message now: states both magnitudes ('2 of 63 ... 61 still eligible'); names the benign cause explicitly with the magnitude that distinguishes it ('a concurrent tombstone or restore committing between the eligibility count and the delete is a legitimate read-committed race — a shortfall of 1-2 on an actively-used catalog is plausibly that; a larger shortfall is not'); and DROPS the old 'if the shortfall repeats, report it' line, which promised a repeat-check the mechanism never implemented. No repeat-detector, magnitude threshold, or retry was added — each would reintroduce a silent window, the exact property this bead removes. Docstring updated to match; one new test (test_message_promises_no_behaviour_the_command_does_not_implement) pins that the message advertises nothing it does not do, and the existing message test now pins the magnitudes + benign-cause wording.

3. Reviewer Low-1 — http_catalog_client.purge_trash docstring: the documents_eligible paragraph no longer splices mid-sentence into the dry_run explanation; it follows the dry_run=True/False sentences as its own paragraph.

4. Reviewer Low-2 — T2 COUNT CORRECTION. Rev 1 of nexus/ff85q-root-cause [21403] claimed 'Java 250'. That was WRONG: it summed two overlapping batch runs and double-counted the parity (3) and CatalogPurgeTrash (4) classes. The scoped battery is 243, verified in ONE run of all nine classes: parity 3 + CatalogPurgeTrash 4 + CatalogHandlerPurgeTrash 4 + SoftDelete 15 + TombstoneFilterGate 23 + CatalogDocumentCascade 3 + CatalogRepository 160 + ManifestVerify 16 + ManifestFunctions 15 = 243. T2 [21403] rewritten with the correction called out explicitly plus the review outcome.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE: stale artifact, NOT an engine regression. The shakeout never tested abbcf1bd — it tested a native binary dated 2026-07-22 15:34 (12 days stale, 34 newer service/src/main files).

tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh:315 guarded the GraalVM native build with a pure existence test (`if [ ! -x service/target/nexus-service ]`). mvn package leaves that artifact on disk and nothing removes it, so once any native build had happened every later run.sh --shakeout silently reused it forever. --guided/--chash-window force a fresh build; --shakeout did not.

Date boundary matches all four symptoms exactly (binary 2026-07-22):
- manifest/chashes count   e3fe1f30 2026-07-24 (v0.1.55)
- manifest/get_many count  81867a30 2026-08-01 (v0.1.61)
- docs_for_chashes count   81867a30 2026-08-01 (v0.1.61)  <- 4th endpoint, log lines 157/159
- store-get count          897d5c29 2026-08-03 (HEAD)

Decisive identity probe: strings on the binary -> 'purge-trash' count 0 (route added 2026-08-03 by dcf77fb7, present twice in HEAD CatalogHandler); control 'manifest/chashes' -> 1, so the probe is valid.

JVM-vs-native discriminator: NEITHER. CatalogHandler.java:878/906/947 emit count via Map.of(...), which cannot omit a key, and CatalogHandlerManifestEnvelopeTest asserts containsKeys(manifests,count) over live HTTP and is green on this tree. No jar build needed. The client fail-loud guards at http_catalog_client.py:2512/2688/2625 behaved CORRECTLY — they detected a pre-floor engine (floors verified correct by git ancestry).

FIX APPLIED (uncommitted): run.sh guard is now freshness-aware (find service/src service/pom.xml -newer <bin>); reuse branch prints the artifact build date; NEW static gate tests/test_rehearsal_native_build_freshness.py (RED before, GREEN after, behaviourally falsified 3 cases). No Java test could have caught this — the Java source was never wrong; the defect is the harness's artifact CHOICE.

RESIDUAL (needs its own bead + a design call): shakeout Phase A never asserts the SERVED process is the artifact this run built. Version identity cannot protect it — candidates are unstamped by design (release_version blank), so REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION=(0,1,62) is bypassed. build_ref (nexus-308ph) is the right discriminator but is wired only into the JVM jar gate (build-gate-jar.sh / local-service-gate.sh:481); extending it to the native candidate means restating that gate's invariant from 'native => no build_ref' to 'native RELEASE => no build_ref'.

title: n0ful CI-sharding tree: required-check rename wedges next release PR to main + .test_durations.json never committed
design:
Two CRITICAL gaps found in substantive-critique of the uncommitted nexus-n0ful CI-sharding tree (ci.yml + pyproject.toml diff, .test_durations.json untracked):

1. REQUIRED-CHECK RENAME SEQUENCING TRAP (verified via 'gh api repos/Hellblazer/nexus/branches/{develop,main}/protection'): develop currently requires status check 'pytest (Python 3.12)'; main requires BOTH 'pytest (Python 3.12)' and 'pytest (Python 3.13)'. The diff renames the per-leg job to 'pytest (Python X, shard N/4)' and introduces a new aggregating job 'pytest-gate' — neither old context string is ever produced again by any workflow run once this lands. The in-YAML comment says to do the branch-protection swap 'in the SAME PR that lands this workflow change', but this change lands via DIRECT PUSH to develop per AGENTS.md convention ('routine work commits direct to develop') — there is no PR. Concrete impact: any PR opened against develop shows 'pytest (Python 3.12)' as permanently 'Expected — waiting' (blocks merge); the NEXT release PR (develop -> main, and this project ships releases same-day per recent git log: 7.1.0/7.1.1/7.1.2 all landed within 24h) will show BOTH main required checks stuck 'Expected — waiting' and be UNMERGEABLE until Hal manually swaps both develop's and main's required-status-check contexts to 'pytest-gate'. This swap must happen BEFORE (or atomically with) the push landing on develop, and again before attempting the next release PR to main.

2. .test_durations.json NEVER COMMITTED: git status shows it '??' (untracked), not gitignored (git check-ignore confirms no match). Every ci.yml/pyproject.toml comment in the diff asserts the split is 'keyed off the committed .test_durations.json' as settled fact. Verified empirically: with the file present, pytest-split produces a tight duration-balance (~206s +/-2s per shard, via --collect-only's 'estimated duration' output); with the file ABSENT (== CI's actual state on a fresh checkout, since it's untracked), pytest-split's Base.__init__ catches FileNotFoundError -> cached_durations={} -> DurationBasedChunksAlgorithm falls back to avg_duration_per_test=1 -> naive contiguous count-based chunking in collection order. Measured against the REAL per-test durations in the untracked file, that naive split's actual shard costs were 220.5s/163.9s/186.3s/255.1s (1.55x max/min skew) vs the balanced split's ~206s/208s/206s/205s (near-perfect). The entire 'duration-balanced 4-way shard' design premise this bead's decision packet was approved on is silently inert until 'git add .test_durations.json' + commit happens. No error, no CI signal — pytest-split only prints an easily-missed stdout notice ('No test durations found').

Partition completeness/determinism/deselection-consistency were independently verified CLEAN (2960+3772+3402+2232=12366 matches no-split --collect-only exactly; group N is deterministic across repeated runs; the historical suite's 555 deselected count matches both the baseline-generation run and the shard-invocation's addopts, no -m mismatch).

Recommendation: (a) git add + commit .test_durations.json in the SAME commit as the ci.yml/pyproject.toml changes, not a follow-up; (b) before pushing to develop, swap develop's required status check 'pytest (Python 3.12)' -> 'pytest-gate' in repo settings; (c) before the next release PR to main, swap main's two required checks ('pytest (Python 3.12)', 'pytest (Python 3.13)') -> 'pytest-gate' — flag this explicitly to Hal as a blocking pre-release step, not an inline YAML comment easily missed.
close_reason: Both Criticals resolved at e57ba4e1: .test_durations.json committed in the same commit as ci.yml (the balanced split is live, not inert); the required-check swap is documented for the direct-push landing path with exact develop/main context swaps and surfaced to Hal as a blocking post-push click.

title: nexus-f7xyq's fail-loud gate breaks pre_close_verification_hook.sh review-completed advisory
description:
Round-1 substantive critique of nexus-f7xyq (T1 CLI unleased-explicit-session fail-loud, session.py/db/t1.py) found the fix's classification of "explicit session id" (resolve_explicit_session_id: NX_SESSION_ID OR CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) is too broad: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is ambient (set on every Claude Code subprocess) not a deliberate caller ask, and per the bead's own supporting research (T2 subagent-reliability-findings-2026-08-03 Q1) the MCP-vs-CLI T1 scope split-brain is routine, not rare.

Empirically proven live (session fc3875cf, 2026-08-03): `uv run nx scratch list` hard-errors ("lease for 'fc3875cf...' missing or expired") while the MCP scratch tool returns 65 entries via a differently-scoped lease (session 32c786f0). Simulating ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/nexus-plugins/conexus/hooks/scripts/pre_close_verification_hook.sh's own pattern (`NX_SESSION_ID=<this session> nx scratch list 2>/dev/null`) reproduces exit 1 with EMPTY stdout -- meaning that hook's SCRATCH_RESULTS var goes empty and its "review-completed" grep always misses, so the advisory falsely reports "No review marker found for <bead>" even when review WAS completed and the marker exists in the shared CLI-dedicated scope.

The hook is advisory/non-blocking (bd close still succeeds) but this silently defeats the mechanized review-gate signal CLAUDE.md and the stacked-reviewer discipline depend on. Narrowing "explicit" to NX_SESSION_ID only does NOT fix it -- the hook deliberately sets NX_SESSION_ID itself (nexus-36q84) to route around the machine-wide current_session clobber, assuming the pre-fix MINT-branch fallback to the shared CLI-dedicated scope. The real missing distinction is "does a live lease exist for this id" vs "is a session-id-shaped string present in env."

Fix direction: either (a) pre_close_verification_hook.sh (and any other script forcing NX_SESSION_ID for identity-continuity reasons) needs an explicit NX_T1_ISOLATED=1 or graceful-degrade wrapper around its nx scratch list call, or (b) the fail-loud gate needs a narrower trigger than "any explicit session id" -- e.g. only fire when the caller is a live, interactive session that plausibly HAD a lease and lost it, not a detached script whose whole point is env-forced identity continuity across a scope that was never guaranteed to have a fresh lease.

Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-f7xyq-round1-2026-08-03. T1 write-back: 0e7fcbd6-fd10-4fa3-a7f1-c21b8aede2df.

title: CONSUMED-verb settlement (nexus-hbr4x) is order-dependent — exit criterion 1 ('no sync agent is blocked') not satisfiable in the adverse stop order
design:
Wave-1 subagent-reliability-burndown (T2 nexus/subagent-reliability-burndown-2026-08-03). nexus-hbr4x implemented CONSUMED-verb ledger settlement in expectations_owes_report (tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh:223-264 + byte-identical conexus/hooks/scripts/expectations.sh) to close the qc4p1 false-block class: a SYNC stop sharing a subagent_type with a background EXPECT must not be blocked.

PROBLEM: settlement consumes credit in STOP order, not dispatch or START order. In a session with B background + S sync dispatches of one shared type, whichever agent's SubagentStop fires FIRST claims a unit of the B background credits, regardless of whether that agent is actually the sync or the background one. The mandated non-vacuity test (test_sync_stop_after_background_credit_consumed_not_blocked) only exercises the FAVORABLE order (background stops first, then sync) — there is zero test coverage for the adverse order, which the implementation's own code comment (expectations.sh:207-221) explicitly documents as unresolved: "if the false-positive (sync) stop fires BEFORE the true background stop consumes the credit, the ordering inverts."

Per Claude Code Agent-tool semantics (run_in_background:false blocks the orchestrator's turn until the dispatch completes; run_in_background:true continues independently), a sync dispatch issued alongside a background dispatch of the SAME type very plausibly STOPS FIRST — sync-first may be the common case, not a rare edge. Under that ordering:
  1. The sync agent is falsely told "You are the named background teammate ... and your orchestrator expects a completion report" (subagent-stop.sh:190) — confusing/misleading, one wasted round-trip (bounded by the once-guard, so not an infinite loop).
  2. The REAL background agent's later stop finds the credit already spent and is waved through UNCHECKED even if it never sent a report — silently reproducing the exact Finding-0 defect (T2 [21371]) this whole burndown exists to fix, now MASKED behind an apparently-functioning guard.

Exit criterion 1 (T2 [21374]) states literally: "in a session mixing sync+background of ONE type, no sync agent is blocked." As implemented this holds only under the favorable order, not as a general invariant — the criterion is not satisfiable by this design without either (a) explicit sign-off accepting the order-dependent residual risk as satisfying an amended criterion, or (b) falling back to the plan's own option (ii) (no-mixed-type: never enforce for a type that ever has both sync and background dispatches in a session) for shared types, trading detection power for a hard zero-false-block guarantee.

Also note: general-purpose (the a795d fallback default for omitted subagent_type) is the single most commonly dispatched type in this harness, making it the most likely type to collide sync+background in one session — compounding this risk rather than being an independent edge case.

RECOMMENDATION: take this back to Hal/plan owner for an explicit decision: accept documented order-dependent residual risk (amend exit criterion 1's wording), or adopt the no-mixed-type fallback per-type (only refuse to enforce for types that are session-locally mixed, rather than a global switch), or add a live adversarial-order test/measurement before declaring 1a done.

Full pressure-test writeup: T1 scratch (wave1 critique write-back), same session.
close_reason: Resolved in the hbr4x fix round, shipped develop 97cfcf1f: per-type unmixed-ness gate makes the false-block class structurally impossible in either stop order; both-orders tests + 8-way concurrency test. Critique round2-final JUSTIFIED 0/0 (T1 09e6ca57).

title: PgVectorRepository.list() leaks tombstoned chunk ids/metadata via POST /v1/vectors/store-list (nx store list / store_list MCP tool) — same leak class as nexus-8j1zx, missed by both fix rounds
design:
Found during round-2 substantive critique of nexus-3ck2g/nexus-8j1zx fix round (2026-08-03).

nexus-8j1zx fixed get()/getWhere()/getEmbeddings()/getAllMetadata() by adding
liveChunksCondition(ctx, ch) to their WHERE clause, and extended
TombstoneFilterGateTest.scanTypedChunksSites with a name-list allowlist
(TYPED_CHUNKS_READ_METHODS = {"PgVectorRepository.java": [get, getWhere,
getEmbeddings, getAllMetadata]}). Both the fix-round developer's own caller-grep
("grepped every engine-internal caller of get/getWhere/getEmbeddings/getAllMetadata")
and my own round-1 critique were scoped ONLY to those 4 already-named methods —
neither swept the file for OTHER occurrences of the same
`DimTables.CHUNKS.get(dim)` typed-read shape.

PgVectorRepository.list(tenant, collection, limit, offset) — service/src/main/java/
dev/nexus/service/vectors/PgVectorRepository.java:2005-2025 — has the IDENTICAL
shape: typed DimTables.ChunkTable read (`ch.chash()`, `ch.metadata()` from
`ch.table()`), zero tombstone predicate, no CATALOG_DOCUMENTS/CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS
token, no liveChunksCondition( call. It is:
  - NOT in TYPED_CHUNKS_READ_METHODS (TombstoneFilterGateTest silently does not
    scan it — structurally invisible to the gate, same as the original 8j1zx gap)
  - NOT covered by any test asserting tombstone exclusion (grepped
    PgVectorRepositoryContractTest's only .list( callers — pagination/tenant-
    isolation assertions only, lines 982/984/1011)
  - LIVE and reachable: called from VectorHandler.handleStoreList
    (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/VectorHandler.java:653-664),
    which backs POST /v1/vectors/store-list — the wire route for `nx store list`
    / `nx store list --docs` / the MCP `store_list` tool (src/nexus/db/
    http_vector_client.py:2029), one of the most basic and commonly invoked T3
    read verbs.

Impact: after `nx catalog delete`, a chunk whose only manifest parent is the
tombstoned doc still appears in plain `nx store list` / `store_list` output —
its chash and full metadata (which can include title, source_uri, spans) are
returned indefinitely, even on a fully-patched nexus-3ck2g/nexus-8j1zx engine.
This is reachable with no out-of-band chash needed (unlike get/getWhere/
getEmbeddings which need a known id) — a plain listing call surfaces it by
default. Same leak semantics as nexus-8j1zx (manifest-parent-tombstoned chunk
never filtered), same fix shape (add `.and(liveChunksCondition(ctx, ch))` to
the WHERE clause) and same gate-extension shape (add "list" to
TYPED_CHUNKS_READ_METHODS's PgVectorRepository.java entry, add
list_afterTombstone-style coverage to PgVectorTombstoneFilterTest).

Related, NOT the same bug (pre-existing, separately tracked): PgVectorRepository
.count() (line 2054) is also unfiltered but is nexus-dzs62's known scope
(count/stats disagreement), not a new finding here.

Also noted, lower priority (currently UNREACHABLE, no live caller): fetchChunkText
(line 2529) is wired only through ChromaSchemeHandler/UriSchemeResolverRegistry,
which has zero HTTP-handler consumers today (grepped) — a landmine for whoever
wires that resolver up later without checking tombstone status, not a live leak.
Not filing separately; note here for whoever eventually wires the resolver.

title: PgVectorRepository get/getWhere/getEmbeddings/getAllMetadata leak tombstoned chunk content — invisible to TombstoneFilterGateTest
design:
Found during nexus-3ck2g round-1 substantive critique (2026-08-03).

nexus-3ck2g fixed searchWithTokens + hybridSearch (3 branches) to exclude tombstoned
docs' chunks via an inlined liveChunksPredicate, and extended TombstoneFilterGateTest
to structurally require it on those two methods. But four sibling read methods in the
same class read nexus.chunks_<dim> with ZERO tombstone filtering and are invisible to
BOTH of the gate's scans:

  - PgVectorRepository.get(...)            ~line 1321 -> POST /v1/vectors/get
  - PgVectorRepository.getWhere(...)        ~line 1456 -> POST /v1/vectors/get (where=)
  - PgVectorRepository.getEmbeddings(...)   ~line 1374 -> POST /v1/vectors/get-embeddings
  - PgVectorRepository.getAllMetadata(...)  ~line 1541 -> POST /v1/vectors/get-all-metadata

All four read via a typed DimTables.ChunkTable (ch.table()/ch.chash()/...), never the
raw chunksTable(int) string helper and never a CATALOG_DOCUMENTS/CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS
reference — so they satisfy neither of TombstoneFilterGateTest's scans:
  - scanDocAndChunkSites keys off CATALOG_DOCUMENTS/CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS tokens (absent)
  - scanRawChunksSites (added by nexus-3ck2g E2) keys off the literal "chunksTable(" call
    (absent — these methods never call it)

Impact: a chash known out-of-band (cached from a prior search result taken before
tombstoning, or fetched deliberately) still returns FULL tombstoned chunk content and

title: store_put writes source_uri=NULL and file_path=NULL — RDR-108 identity can never match, so re-putting the same doc creates unlimited duplicates with contradictory content
description: SHAKEOUT-7.1.1 wave 2 (2026-08-03, isolated sandbox, psql-verified): three nx store put runs of the same --title (two of them the SAME source file, edited between) created three separate catalog documents 1.1.1/1.1.2/1.1.3, all simultaneously retrievable with contradictory content. title: pipeline-buffer resume after clear_orphan_wal trusts stale progress counters, silently truncating a retry
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 while building the nexus-5xn3k.7 RUNFENCE gate
(tests/db/test_5xn3k_runfence_gate.py), driving REAL pipeline_index_pdf /
index_pdf against a real engine + PG with an injected uploader_loop
exception.

## The defect

pipeline_index_pdf's caught-exception handler calls, in order:
  db.mark_failed(content_hash, error=...)
  db.clear_orphan_wal(content_hash)

clear_orphan_wal wipes the pdf_pages/pdf_chunks WAL rows server-side but
does NOT reset the pipeline row's PROGRESS COUNTERS (pages_extracted,
total_pages, chunks_created, chunks_embedded, chunks_uploaded,
extraction_meta) — those stay at their pre-failure values.

On retry (create_pipeline -> "resuming"):
  1. extractor_loop's resume-fast-path trusts the STALE
     `pages_extracted >= total_pages` + `extraction_meta` to SKIP real
     extraction entirely, returning ExtractionResult(text="", ...).
  2. chunker_loop's resume seed (`db.read_pages(content_hash)`) finds
     NOTHING (the WAL pages were genuinely cleared), so
     `accumulated_text` stays empty. Correctly (chunker_loop's own
     logic), it reports zero new chunks and calls
     `db.update_progress(chunks_created=0, chunks_embedded=0)`.
  3. uploader_loop then reads the pipeline state and sees the STALE
     `chunks_uploaded` (e.g. 100, the count from BEFORE the failure)
     already `>= chunks_created` (now correctly 0) — and calls
     `db.mark_completed(content_hash)` IMMEDIATELY, without uploading
     anything.

The retry "completes" successfully, reporting only the PRE-FAILURE
chunk count as the total. The remaining content is silently NEVER
re-attempted. Because manifest writes and the RUNFENCE completion stamp
both read the state THIS (already-truncated) retry produced, the fence
correctly stamps 'complete' over what it can see — but what it can see
is itself wrong. The engine's fail-closed verify does not catch this
either, because referenced == chunk_count == the truncated manifest
this retry wrote.

## Reproduction

tests/db/test_5xn3k_runfence_gate.py's `_kill_mid_index` helper +
`_reset_pipeline_buffer` docstring reproduce and work around this: a
200-chunk streaming PDF index, killed after the first ~100-chunk
upload batch (RuntimeError injected in uploader_loop's upsert), left
to run pipeline_index_pdf's real mark_failed+clear_orphan_wal handler.
Without a full `db.delete_pipeline_data(content_hash)` reset before the
retry, `index_pdf()`'s second call returns 100 (not 200) — silently
half the document, permanently.

## Scope note

This is orthogonal to nexus-5xn3k (the RUNFENCE catalog fence itself
behaves correctly throughout — index_state stays 'indexing', then
correctly stamps 'complete' given what it can observe). This is a
defect in the T2 PIPELINE BUFFER's own crash-resume bookkeeping
(concurrency/resume mechanics are explicitly "the pipeline row's job"
per nexus-5xn3k.7's own nexus-lcmbp non-goal ruling), not the fence.

## Suggested fix directions (not investigated in depth)

- clear_orphan_wal should also reset the progress counters it
  invalidates (pages_extracted, total_pages, chunks_created,
  chunks_embedded, chunks_uploaded, extraction_meta) so a resume after
  it genuinely starts from zero, matching what create_pipeline's
  "resuming" contract implies.
- OR: extractor_loop's resume-fast-path should verify the WAL pages it
  is trusting still exist (e.g. a cheap read_pages count check) rather
  than trusting progress-counter fields alone.

Context: nx
close_reason: FIXED e1884d4d, candidate C (defensive resume): extractor_loop's fast path verifies the WAL backs the counters before trusting them; falls through to genuine re-extraction on mismatch. Heals pre-existing poisoned rows structurally. A/B blocked at the Java layer (verified). Falsified: reset-free retry RED at 100/200-stamped-complete pre-fix, GREEN post-fix, permanent as test_consistent_truncation_recovers_without_force_no_reset in the CI-wired gate. Reviewer approved all claims; arc critic verdict justified. Residuals: glzrn (availability sibling, open, reachable-precondition note recorded), page-count endpoint bead (engine batch).

title: dt.py index_cmd doesn't catch IndexRunVerifyRefused — a fenced-refusal on a large DT PDF crashes the whole batch with a raw traceback
description:
src/nexus/commands/dt.py::index_cmd's per-record try/except (~:740) only catches
(RuntimeError, ImportError). IndexRunVerifyRefused (errors.py:196) subclasses
NexusError(Exception), not RuntimeError, so it is uncaught.

Call-graph (verified): _index_record -> index_pdf() -> (pipeline_index_pdf for
streaming, or _index_pdf_incremental for chunk_count > _INCREMENTAL_THRESHOLD=128)
-> _fence_complete() (doc_indexer.py:1597 / pipeline_stages.py:959), which
RE-RAISES IndexRunVerifyRefused on a refused completion (propagating by contract,
distinct from mcp_infra's non-propagating flush-grain path). Nothing in dt.py's
loop or index_cmd catches it, and there is no outer try/except around the loop.

Consequence: a DEVONthink record large enough to hit the streaming or incremental
path, whose completion is refused by the engine's fail-closed verify, crashes the
ENTIRE `nx dt index` batch with a raw traceback -- remaining records unprocessed,
no summary printed. Violates dt.py's own documented nexus-2fyb contract two lines
above the except clause ("a single indexing failure must NOT kill the whole DT
batch"). commands/index.py's index_pdf_cmd (single-file + --dir batch) explicitly
catches this exception via _index_run_refused_message() -- the same fix was never
applied to dt.py.

Test gap: tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py::TestDtIndexSummaryTruthful::
test_refused_completion_reported_as_own_bucket mocks dt._index_record itself
(never calls the real body), so it cannot and does not exercise this propagation
path.

Fix: catch IndexRunVerifyRefused in dt.py's per-record try/except, converting it
to a failed-record entry (mirroring index.py's _index_run_refused_message), and
add a test that mocks index_pdf/index_markdown (not _index_record) to raise it.

Found during substantive-critic review of uncommitted nexus-5xn3k.6 (develop @
49f00284). Full critique: T2 nexus/5xn3k6-critique-2026-08-02 (id 21355).
close_reason: Fixed in aea55043: dt.py per-record except IndexRunVerifyRefused -> failed bucket via the shared _index_run_refused_message; batch survival + no-traceback pinned by TestDtIndexRefusalPropagation mocking index_pdf (the real boundary), per the critique's layer requirement. title: [index] REGRESSION in 4b0c5fb5 (.4): seam-b second index of identical content upserts 1 instead of no-op — fence state left non-complete makes the three-way staleness re-index every run
description:

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (evidence-confirmed, instrumented run against the stamped fence-aware jar):

Chain — first _index_document call:
  _fence_begin(doc_id='1.1.1') -> engine row index_state='indexing'  [write lands]
  fire_batch manifest_complete={'1.1.1': eee7c966...}                [threaded, declaring=1/2 hooks]
  manifest_write_batch_hook receives it                              [hook reachable]
  _manifest_write_loop cat=_ServiceCatalogWriter has_write_many=FALSE  <-- THE BREAK
Second call:
  _index_fence_state('1.1.1') -> ('indexing', eee7c966...) -> _index_run_fresh=False -> 1 upsert.

H1(b)/(c), H2 and H3 all FALSIFIED: the complete map reaches the hook intact, doc_id is stable ('1.1.1' both calls), hash-once holds (identical hash at begin, in the map, and in the second call's gate).

Mechanism: .4's completion stamp rides write_manifest_many's `complete` map, but write_manifest_many is on NEITHER CATALOG_WRITE_OPS NOR _SERVICE_ONLY_WRITE_OPS, so _ServiceCatalogWriter.__getattr__ raises AttributeError and callable(getattr(cat,'write_manifest_many',None)) is False on every production run. The ride is dead code in service mode (= every mode since RDR-158 P4). Pre-existing, already filed as nexus-67qsd; .4 built the stamp on top of it. Every pre-existing loop test used a bare MagicMock cat, which answers to any attribute — so the ride was 100%% covered on a branch production cannot reach.

FIX (mcp_infra.py, no whitelist change): new _stamp_index_run_complete() called from _manifest_write_loop's per-doc position-0 branch after rows+sweep+resync, via the already-whitelisted cat.complete_index_run. Contract parity with stampCompleteIfVerified: chunk_count=len(rows written); 409 -> _record_complete_refusal + WARNING under the SAME event name; None (pre-fence 404) is neither success nor refusal; never propagates. Continuation slices are never stamped (warned, once). Deliberately NOT fixed by whitelisting write_manifest_many — nexus-jk88j: that activates the fast branch which SKIPS _sweep_superseded_vectors and re-creates nexus-39upx.

title: local-service-gate step 1 (nx init --service) auto-starts the pinned release binary, silently making step 3's launch-artifact selection a no-op
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 while implementing nexus-x81ks's smoke leg. 'nx init --service' (commands/init.py -> ensure_storage_supervisor) installs the CURRENT PINNED RELEASE native binary and starts it as a side effect of provisioning, publishing a live ServiceRegistry lease in the gate's scratch config dir. tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh step 3 then runs 'nx daemon service start' with NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR (or NEXUS_SERVICE_BIN) set, intending to launch the freshly-rebuilt/stamped dev jar (or a caller-supplied native binary) — but storage_service_daemon.py's _start_locked() short-circuits unconditionally on any existing lease (a documented idempotency guarantee) WITHOUT inspecting NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR/NEXUS_SERVICE_BIN at all. So step 3 is a no-op whenever step 1 already started a service, which is every gate run (step 1 runs unconditionally). The gate's whole jar-rebuild-and-stamp machinery (step 2, the 'Stamp discipline' block) has therefore been vestigial since nexus-edwlp (2026-07-07): the service actually serving the whole gate run — both the pytest leg and (until fixed) the new x81ks smoke leg — is whatever the CURRENT PINNED RELEASE (REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION) binary is, never local service/ source changes. Confirmed live: RUNFENCE routes (unreleased, post-v0.1.61, present in the freshly-built jar's bytecode) 404'd against the running service even immediately after a fresh jar rebuild, because the actually-running process was still the pinned v0.1.61 binary init had installed minutes earlier (same pid before and after step 3). /version's release_version check cannot detect this — the pinned binary and the dev-HEAD floor report the identical version number by construction, so that assertion passes vacuously regardless of which artifact is actually running. Worked around locally in x81ks by inserting 'nx daemon service stop' between step 1 and step 2/3 (PG is left running; only the storage service is stopped) so step 3's launch-artifact selection actually takes effect. That workaround should be reviewed/hardened properly rather than treated as the permanent fix — e.g. should 'nx init --service' expose a --no-start flag for gate/test callers, or should the gate stop being surprised by init's side effect via a comment-only fix. Also worth asking: does this affect other self-provisioning E2E gates that call 'nx init --service' then later try to control the launch artifact?

## Context
nexus-x81ks (parent investigation); tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh; src/nexus/commands/daemon.py service_start_cmd / ensure_storage_supervisor; src/nexus/daemon/storage_service_daemon.py _start_locked (idempotent short-circuit) + _resolve_launch_artifact; src/nexus/commands/init.py ~line 246-262
close_reason: Shipped develop b8b21068: shared explicit-artifact mismatch check at BOTH short-circuits (ensure_storage_supervisor — the load-bearing one the bead misattributed — and _start_locked); canonical-absolute path comparison; pre-fix leases degrade allow+warn one release; GH #1369 exit-0 semantics preserved; RDR-161 confinement; gate comment corrected, stop-insertion + build_ref kept as defense in depth. Two dual-review rounds, final justified 0/0. Raise arm covered at real-fixture unit layer only (gate stays lease-free by design — recorded). Residual: nexus-86aaz (well-known-path swap class, RDR-scale).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Two critic-verified foreclosures (2026-08-02, x81ks critique): (1) NO OTHER E2E caller is exposed — release-sandbox.sh sets NEXUS_SERVICE_BIN BEFORE nx init --service --no-autostart so init's own start already uses the intended artifact; mac-signed-binary-gate.sh never invokes the swap pattern. The gate script was the only exposed call site. (2) --no-autostart is NOT a fix candidate: commands/init.py's _decide_autostart/_provision_and_autostart_service both branches still end in a live lease-publishing service via ensure_storage_supervisor — the flag changes how persistence registers, not whether a service starts. The real fix remains the daemon start path honoring NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR/BIN (or an explicit no-start init mode); the stop-insertion workaround ships with x81ks.

title: [gate] the local-service gate's throwaway service is largely VESTIGIAL to its own pytest leg — isolation fixtures route the suite at self-provisioned substrates, and the FLOOR/BUDGET guard structurally cannot see the hollowing
description:
Found 2026-08-02 during the nexus-tmsnz investigation (T2 nexus/tmsnz-7.0.1-lsg-hermeticity-verdict.md [21353]).

Since the engine-substrate cutover (nexus-g37fr / nexus-i711w, 2026-07-23/28), autouse conftest fixtures (_isolate_service_endpoint_env conftest.py:356-399, _isolate_config_dir :570-608, _pin_t2_substrate :402-460) strip the gate's NX_SERVICE_* env and route every test body at a session-scoped substrate the suite boots ITSELF. The gate still spends ~10 min provisioning a throwaway PG + downloading/installing the native binary + rebuilding a stamped jar for a service that — per the FIXED gate's own -rs output (CI run 30754672235) — nothing resolves: test_mcp_server.py:1134 skips with 'no service endpoint resolvable in the isolated test env... or run via tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh'. The gate's docstring premise (~370 tests exercising the throwaway) is stale.

This is the vacuity class the gate exists to prevent, from the inside: the tests still pass (against the substitute substrate), so FLOOR/BUDGET cannot detect that the gate's SUBJECT is unreachable. Empirically confirmed by the 467/33 byte-identical pre/post-376115c1 hand-runs — removing the env changed NOTHING, which should have been impossible if the throwaway were load-bearing.

Acceptance: decide the gate's real contract — either (a) re-wire the local-service family to actually resolve the gate's throwaway (fixtures honor the gate's env when present, with a non-vacuity assert counting tests that resolved it, floor > 0), or (b) retire the throwaway provisioning and re-scope the gate honestly around the self-provisioned substrates it actually exercises (recovering ~10 min/run). Either way the gate must carry an assert that its stated subject is exercised — a count, not prose.

Cross-refs: nexus-tmsnz (closed), e926106c (env fix), 30742736685/30754672235 (the CI delta runs).
close_reason: SHIPPED with 25f31333's sibling commit. Smoke leg 11/11 live, exact-count non-vacuity, honest two-proofs re-scope; 4e96a workaround proven (artifact swap now real); 308ph revisit trigger mechanized as a red-at-floor-bump test. Both reviewers + critic clean, all findings dispositioned. Residuals: 4e96a (daemon-side real fix), 308ph (nonce), 5a8ic (schedule reachability).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: DECISION 2026-08-02 (Hal: deal with it now): option (b)-with-teeth. (a) full re-wire is structurally infeasible — the deep integration tests require superuser access to their OWN substrate PG (Liquibase/seeding/tenant minting), which a foreign service cannot grant; a partial re-wire would punch conditional holes in the isolation fixtures that exist to prevent the live-install-leak class. (b)+teeth: KEEP a lean throwaway leg, driven by the GATE SCRIPT ITSELF (outside pytest, immune to the autouse isolation): after boot, a counted direct-smoke sequence against the throwaway — health+version-floor, catalog doc/register, vectors upsert+search-returns-it, index-run begin/complete round-trip (fence routes on a stamped service, free) — exact-count non-vacuity assert, fail-loud. Re-scope the gate docstring honestly: pytest family = functional surface on self-provisioned substrates; smoke leg = shipped-shape service boots via real daemon machinery and serves. The FLOOR/BUDGET guard keeps its current meaning; the new counter guards the gate's SUBJECT.

title: 5xn3k RUNFENCE GATE: integration falsification — consistent-truncation partial index recovers WITHOUT --force, driven at pipeline_index_pdf, plus the fence-pinned-complete kill control
description:
PHASE-EXIT GATE. Memo §7 ("the falsification, stated first"). Blocked on every other bead in
this arc. Nothing in this arc is called done until this is green — and green WITH its kill
control.

## The falsification test

`tests/integration/test_5xn3k_partial_index_recovers.py` — real engine + real PG, driving
**production `pipeline_index_pdf`**. THE LAYER TEST discipline: driven at the layer production
uses, NOT at `_manifest_is_fully_present`. A test below the layer production uses proves the
layer, not the feature.

1. Index a multi-batch document; inject an exception in `uploader_loop` after batch *k*.
2. Assert the **CONSISTENT-TRUNCATION shape**: `chunks == manifest_rows` and both `< total`,
   and `index_state == 'indexing'`.
   Asserting the two counts **AGREE** is what makes this the state AC2 structurally cannot see,
   rather than the post-hoc-deletion state (`manifest − T3 = 207`) it can. Get this assertion
   wrong and the whole test degrades to re-proving AC2.
3. Re-index **WITHOUT `--force`**.
4. Assert full chunk count, full manifest, `index_state == 'complete'`, and a return value > 0.

## The kill control — non-negotiable, same bead

A sibling test that monkeypatches the fence read to a constant `'complete'` and asserts the
**no-op REAPPEARS** (return 0, chunk count unchanged).

Without it the main test could pass for an incidental reason — e.g. the chash probe happening to
miss. With it, the test's power is provably the fence and nothing else. A green main test with
no kill control is a vacuous gate; do not accept one.

## Gate checklist for the arc

- [ ] Falsification test green, kill control red-when-fenced / green-when-not, both driven at
      `pipeline_index_pdf`
- [ ] Full Java suite green (schema + handler changes touched it)
- [ ] Full `uv run pytest` green
- [ ] Stacked review at the phase boundary: **code-review-expert AND substantive-critic**, both,
      neither substituting for the other. Brief the critic with the memo (T2 21348) as the locked
      spec so it checks implementation-vs-design, not style. Then test-validator.
- [ ] `/conexus:phase-review-gate` cross-walk of the memo's §3/§4 against what actually closed —
      catches silent scope reduction
- [ ] AC1 recorded as **closed BY the fence** with the long-transaction argument stated out
      loud on nexus-5xn3k at closure; AC4/AC6/AC7 closed by their beads
- [ ] **AC8 (`col.get(where=...)` non-determinism) NOT closed here** — its blast radius shrinks
      (the question stops being answered by a metadata scan and becomes one SQL anti-join) but it
      keeps its own bead
- [ ] nexus-ac4id closed on this work; nexus-39upx (b) carries the
      `index_state='complete'` filter precondition as a stated requirement
- [ ] Engine tag + deploy + cloud-gate coordinated with nexus-lcmbp (same engine tag, memo §5),
      then `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION` bumped AFTER the deploy

## Explicitly OUT of scope (named, not absorbed — memo §8)

AC8 `col.get` non-determinism; the `--extractor docling` silent quality collapse; nexus-mok9x
boilerplate ingest. Separate beads, all three.
## Design of record

T2 **21348** — `nx memory get -p nexus -t "5xn3k-design-2026-08-02"`. That memo is the LOCKED
design (READ-ONLY analysis, develop @ d6b8abc4, 2026-08-02). Do not redesign it; implement the
section named below. Parent bug: nexus-5xn3k.

Core finding this arc exists to fix (memo §1): no comparison of two artifacts both written by
the same run can detect that the run did not finish. A death mid-index leaves
`T3 chunks == manifest rows`, both truncated — a CONSISTENT truncation that `manifest − T3`
(the AC2 check that already landed in 6ad6b2a9) returns clean on. Only a record of intent vs
completion sees it. That record is the RUNFENCE.

## Standing rulings — apply to EVERY bead in this arc

- **AC1 (transactional chunks+manifest) is CLOSED BY THE FENCE, explicitly.** One PG
  transaction spanning the chunk writes and the manifest is now *possible* (post-RDR-155 both
  tables live in the same Postgres) and is still WRONG: chunk upserts stream over many HTTP
  calls across minutes while MinerU extracts, so one transaction means a long-running
  transaction, bloat, and an RLS connection pinned through the pooler for the length of a
  69-page extraction. The fence buys the same guarantee — a partial document is never
  observable as complete — without holding a transaction across the network. AC1 gets closed
  BY this argument, stated out loud at closure; it is not silently dropped.
- **nexus-ac4id closes on this work** (memo §3.2 / §4). Its part (1) dict-shape fix becomes
  moot — the doctor check stops enumerating collections client-side entirely; its part (2)
  "engine-side anti-join" IS `nexus.manifest_verify_all()`. Do NOT fix the dict shape
  separately. ac4id stays OPEN (noted, not closed) until this arc lands.
- **nexus-39upx (b) precondition**: the corpus-wide orphan sweep MUST filter on
  `index_state = 'complete'`. Sweeping a mid-index document would delete chunks an in-flight
  run has written but not yet manifested. The fence is precisely what makes (b) safe.
- **nexus-lcmbp non-goal — THE FENCE IS NOT A LOCK.** `index_state='indexing'` ALWAYS means
  *re-index*. It must NEVER mean *skip, someone else is running*. Reading it as a lock rebuilds
  lcmbp's exact bug one layer up. Concurrency remains the pipeline row's job.
- **Engine-floor tolerance**: the client ships WITHOUT waiting on `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION`.
  A pre-fence engine 404s the index-run routes and omits the fence fields; the client treats
  both as `unknown` and falls through to verification (today's post-AC2 behaviour). The floor
  bump RIDES THE NEXT ENGINE TAG per AGENTS.md § Engine-service release — never a tag cut for
  this arc alone. Fence unreadable => fail open to today's behaviour, logged at **WARNING**;
  a fence that silently stops working is ac4id all over again.

OWED: the empirical CI dispatch verification post-push — running now. Dual-reviewed; arc critic justified.

title: mark_failed: /fail POST failure itself reproduces ptctu's two consequences (wrong error surfaced + row strands)
design:
Uncommitted fix for nexus-ptctu (src/nexus/db/http_pipeline_client.py mark_failed)
wraps the cleanup flush() in try/except so a flush failure no longer masks the
original error or blocks the /fail POST. That closes ONE of the two axes that can
enter mark_failed's error path.

The other axis is unguarded: the trailing `self._post("/v1/pipeline/fail", ...)`
call is not wrapped. If /fail itself hits a persistent (non-retryable, e.g.
application-level 500) failure -- plausible under the same engine-degraded
conditions that caused the original gtltb doc-3 incident -- mark_failed raises
that NEW exception to its caller (pipeline_stages.py:807). Because the raise
happens before line 808/809, `db.clear_orphan_wal(content_hash)` never runs and
`raise first_exc` never runs -- the caller instead sees the /fail POST's own
exception, and the pipeline row strands `status='running'`, `error=''`, with no
audit trail. This is the SAME two consequences nexus-ptctu was filed to close,
just moved one call downstream.

Undocumented: the new mark_failed docstring says "/fail is always attempted"
but does not state what happens if that attempt itself fails. Untested: neither
of the two new tests in tests/db/test_http_pipeline_client.py exercises a
persistent /fail failure (only cleanup-flush failure with /fail succeeding is
covered).

Fix shape (not started): either give /fail POST itself a bounded best-effort
retry/guard with a terminal fallback that still guarantees the row leaves
'running' (e.g. a local/last-resort marker), or explicitly document this as an
accepted residual window (Hal's call, mirroring the audit-trail-window carve-out
already accepted elsewhere in commands/t3.py::gc_cmd) rather than leaving it
silent.

title: 5xn3k RUNFENCE C3 (client, AC6): re-route update-chunks misses through a full upsert so a stale existing_ids probe stops silently dropping content
description:
CLIENT half, step 3 of 4 — AC6. Memo §3.6. Blocked on the engine bead (which makes the misses
reportable).

## The defect

`_upsert_skip_reembed` (`doc_indexer.py:784-875`) splits on `db.existing_ids(...)`. `old_idx`
goes to `update_chunks`, which writes **metadata only**. When the probe is a stale positive —
the id is reported present but the row is gone — the content is **silently dropped**. This is
the mechanism behind the parent bug's worst observed state: manifest 515 / T3 108, 407 chunks
metadata-only-updated into nothing, and a green summary line on top of it.

## The fix — at the source, not just detected

`/v1/vectors/update-chunks` now returns `{"updated": n, "missing": [ids...]}` (engine bead).
The client re-routes every id in `missing` through `upsert_chunks_with_embeddings` — a full
upsert with content and embeddings, not a metadata patch.

Detection alone (the `/complete` verify 409) leaves the run failing LOUDLY but not self-healing.
**Ship both.** The 409 is the guard rail; this is the repair.

Engine-floor tolerance applies here too: an older engine returns no `missing` key. Treat absent
as "cannot tell", keep today's behaviour, and log at WARNING — never assume zero misses.

## Tests (TDD)

`tests/test_5xn3k_update_chunks_missing.py` — a stale `existing_ids` that returns ids absent
from the store; assert the misses are re-routed to a full upsert **and the content actually
lands** (assert on retrieved chunk text, not on a call count). **Falsify by deleting the
reroute** — the test must go red when the reroute code is removed, not merely when it is
mis-parameterised.

## Done when

A stale-positive existing_ids probe can no longer lose content, the falsification is
demonstrated by deletion, and an engine without the `missing` key degrades to today's behaviour
with a WARNING rather than a silent assumption of zero.
## Design of record

T2 **21348** — `nx memory get -p nexus -t "5xn3k-design-2026-08-02"`. That memo is the LOCKED
design (READ-ONLY analysis, develop @ d6b8abc4, 2026-08-02). Do not redesign it; implement the
section named below. Parent bug: nexus-5xn3k.

Core finding this arc exists to fix (memo §1): no comparison of two artifacts both written by
the same run can detect that the run did not finish. A death mid-index leaves
`T3 chunks == manifest rows`, both truncated — a CONSISTENT truncation that `manifest − T3`
(the AC2 check that already landed in 6ad6b2a9) returns clean on. Only a record of intent vs
completion sees it. That record is the RUNFENCE.

## Standing rulings — apply to EVERY bead in this arc

- **AC1 (transactional chunks+manifest) is CLOSED BY THE FENCE, explicitly.** One PG
  transaction spanning the chunk writes and the manifest is now *possible* (post-RDR-155 both
  tables live in the same Postgres) and is still WRONG: chunk upserts stream over many HTTP
  calls across minutes while MinerU extracts, so one transaction means a long-running
  transaction, bloat, and an RLS connection pinned through the pooler for the length of a
  69-page extraction. The fence buys the same guarantee — a partial document is never
  observable as complete — without holding a transaction across the network. AC1 gets closed
  BY this argument, stated out loud at closure; it is not silently dropped.
- **nexus-ac4id closes on this work** (memo §3.2 / §4). Its part (1) dict-shape fix becomes
  moot — the doctor check stops enumerating collections client-side entirely; its part (2)
  "engine-side anti-join" IS `nexus.manifest_verify_all()`. Do NOT fix the dict shape
  separately. ac4id stays OPEN (noted, not closed) until this arc lands.
- **nexus-39upx (b) precondition**: the corpus-wide orphan sweep MUST filter on
  `index_state = 'complete'`. Sweeping a mid-index document would delete chunks an in-flight
  run has written but not yet manifested. The fence is precisely what makes (b) safe.
- **nexus-lcmbp non-goal — THE FENCE IS NOT A LOCK.** `index_state='indexing'` ALWAYS means
  *re-index*. It must NEVER mean *skip, someone else is running*. Reading it as a lock rebuilds
  lcmbp's exact bug one layer up. Concurrency remains the pipeline row's job.
- **Engine-floor tolerance**: the client ships WITHOUT waiting on `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION`.
  A pre-fence engine 404s the index-run routes and omits the fence fields; the client treats
  both as `unknown` and falls through to verification (today's post-AC2 behaviour). The floor
  bump RIDES THE NEXT ENGINE TAG per AGENTS.md § Engine-service release — never a tag cut for
  this arc alone. Fence unreadable => fail open to today's behaviour, logged at **WARNING**;
  a fence that silently stops working is ac4id all over again.
close_reason: SHIPPED 962392d0. Done-when met, all three legs: (1) stale-positive existing_ids probe can no longer lose content — missing ids reroute through a full upsert with content+embeddings, content-landing assertions; (2) falsification by deletion DEMONSTRATED (reroute removed -> 2/8 red) plus a second falsification reintroducing the review-caught OR-accumulation bug (mixed-page test red with page-1 ids wrongly landing); (3) absent-key engine degrades to today's behaviour with WARNING (log-once/process), never assumed zero — ALL-PAGES-REPORTED semantics, cannot-tell dominates mixed-version fleets. Dual-reviewed to clean; 8/8 + combined 320 green.
