comments.text:
BEAD-TEXT AMENDMENT from substantive-critic review of .2's engine diff (T2 nexus/5xn3k2-critique-2026-08-02) -- three MUST/SHOULD requirements for this bead's mcp_infra.py / pipeline_stages.py bracketing work, none of which are covered by .2's engine-side tests alone:

MUST -- check complete_refused: the caller of write_manifest_many's optional complete map (mcp_infra.py _manifest_write_loop) MUST inspect the response's complete_refused list. A non-empty entry means the doc's manifest rows were written correctly (no data lost -- over-work-never-under-work holds) but the completion stamp was refused (verify still shows missing>0 or referenced!=chunk_count), and index_state remains whatever it was before the call (typically 'indexing', never silently 'complete'). The caller MUST NOT report the affected doc_id as fully indexed/succeeded; log at WARNING (matching the engine's own event=write_manifest_many_complete_refused log line) and either explicitly retry POST /index-run/complete for that doc_id once the missing chunk work is redone, or leave it for the next un-forced re-index. Silently discarding complete_refused while reporting the batch as fully successful reproduces, one layer up, the exact 'Indexed N record(s)' silent-success shape this arc exists to close.

MUST -- no chunk_count=0 to /complete for content-bearing docs: before calling /index-run/complete (or passing a doc into the complete map), the client MUST NOT supply chunk_count=0 for a document expected to have content. A document whose extraction produced zero chunks is a FAILURE, not a completion -- route it through /index-run/fail instead. chunk_count=0 otherwise satisfies the fail-closed gate trivially whenever the manifest write also produced nothing (referenced=0 == chunk_count=0), stamping 'complete' on what may be a silently-failed extraction. An explicit, named exception is required for any content type that is legitimately content-free.

SHOULD -- reuse, never recompute, content_hash between begin and complete: pass the SAME content_hash value to /index-run/begin and its corresponding /index-run/complete call for one run (compute once, thread through). The engine does not cross-validate begin's stored hash against complete's supplied hash -- completeIndexRun stamps whatever /complete last supplied. If the two diverge (e.g. the client recomputes against a source that changed mid-run), the stamped hash can defeat the client-side staleness check's meaning on a later comparison.

Full critique available on request.

title: 5xn3k RUNFENCE E2 (engine): CatalogRepository begin/complete/fail/verify + 5 CatalogHandler routes with /complete's verify-then-stamp 409, write_manifest_many complete map, update-chunks missing-ids
description:
ENGINE half, step 2 of 2. Memo §3.3 + §3.6 (engine side). Blocked on the schema/verify bead.

## Scope

**`CatalogRepository.java`**: `beginIndexRun` / `completeIndexRun` / `failIndexRun` /
`manifestVerify`.

**`CatalogHandler.java`** — 5 routes:

```
POST /v1/catalog/index-run/begin     {doc_id, content_hash, run_id, collection}
POST /v1/catalog/index-run/complete  {doc_id, content_hash, chunk_count}
POST /v1/catalog/index-run/fail      {doc_id, error}
GET  /v1/catalog/manifest/verify?doc_id=X
GET  /v1/catalog/manifest/verify_all
```

### `/complete` is the load-bearing one — verify-then-stamp, in ONE transaction

Run `nexus.manifest_verify(doc_id)`. If `missing > 0` **REFUSE**: leave `index_state='indexing'`
untouched and return **409** carrying the counts. Only on `missing == 0`:
`UPDATE catalog_documents SET index_state='complete', index_content_hash=$h, chunk_count=$n`.

That single behaviour delivers AC7 at zero extra transfer and catches the worst incident in the
parent bug: manifest 515 / T3 108 after `_upsert_skip_reembed` took the metadata-only path for
407 deleted chunks. Verify sees 407 missing -> 409 -> the run fails LOUDLY instead of printing
`Indexed 1 record(s)`. No silent fallback for a data-correctness problem.

**`/begin` is idempotent.** **`/complete` without a prior `/begin` is accepted but flagged** —
legacy documents and out-of-band writers have to be able to converge.

### `write_manifest_many` gains an optional `complete: {doc_id: content_hash}` map

So the flush-grain repo path (`ChunkBatcher`, file-atomic, position 0 always present) stamps
completion inside the transaction it ALREADY runs — **no extra round trip on the hot repo
path**. The explicit `/complete` call is for multi-batch documents only.

### `/v1/vectors/update-chunks` returns `{"updated": n, "missing": [ids...]}` (AC6, engine half)

`_upsert_skip_reembed` splits on `db.existing_ids(...)` and routes `old_idx` to `update_chunks`,
which writes **metadata only** — so a stale-positive probe silently drops content. The engine
must report which ids it could not update. The client-side reroute is a separate bead; this one
only makes the misses *reportable*. Detection alone leaves the run failing loudly but not
self-healing — both halves ship.

## Ordering guarantee this bead is responsible for (memo §3.5)

Per-document commit order: **T0** `begin` committed BEFORE the first chunk upsert -> **T1..Tn**
chunks + manifest rows -> **Tn+1** `complete` (verify, then stamp) AFTER the last manifest
write. Crash anywhere in T1..Tn leaves `'indexing'` -> next run re-indexes. Crash at Tn+1 with
everything written leaves `'indexing'` -> one wasted, idempotent re-index (chash-addressed
upsert, atomic manifest replace). **Over-work, never under-work** — that asymmetry is the whole
point; the current design fails toward *skipping*.

Ordering vs nexus-39upx (a): the already-landed `_sweep_superseded_vectors` runs inside the
position-0 manifest-replace path, so `/complete`'s verify runs after the last sweep. No race, by
construction.

## Tests (TDD)

`service/.../IndexRunFenceTest.java`:
- `/complete` refuses with **409** and leaves `index_state='indexing'` when verify shows missing
- success stamps `index_state` + `index_content_hash` + `chunk_count` **atomically**
- `/begin` idempotent
- `/complete` without prior `/begin` accepted-but-flagged
- `write_manifest_many` with the `complete` map stamps in-transaction (no second round trip)
- `update-chunks` returns the missing ids for ids absent from the store

Java schema/handler change => **FULL `./mvnw test`**.

## Ship note

Engine work is fine to land now; it needs no tag of its own. The tag + deploy + cloud-gate ride
the next engine cut (coordinate with nexus-lcmbp — memo §5 says both should land in the SAME
engine tag), and the `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION` bump follows the deploy, never precedes it.
## Design of record

T2 **21348** — `nx memory get -p nexus -t "5xn3k-design-2026-08-02"`. That memo is the LOCKED
design (READ-ONLY analysis, develop @ d6b8abc4, 2026-08-02). Do not redesign it; implement the
section named below. Parent bug: nexus-5xn3k.

Core finding this arc exists to fix (memo §1): no comparison of two artifacts both written by
the same run can detect that the run did not finish. A death mid-index leaves
`T3 chunks == manifest rows`, both truncated — a CONSISTENT truncation that `manifest − T3`
(the AC2 check that already landed in 6ad6b2a9) returns clean on. Only a record of intent vs
completion sees it. That record is the RUNFENCE.

## Standing rulings — apply to EVERY bead in this arc

- **AC1 (transactional chunks+manifest) is CLOSED BY THE FENCE, explicitly.** One PG
  transaction spanning the chunk writes and the manifest is now *possible* (post-RDR-155 both
  tables live in the same Postgres) and is still WRONG: chunk upserts stream over many HTTP
  calls across minutes while MinerU extracts, so one transaction means a long-running
  transaction, bloat, and an RLS connection pinned through the pooler for the length of a
  69-page extraction. The fence buys the same guarantee — a partial document is never
  observable as complete — without holding a transaction across the network. AC1 gets closed
  BY this argument, stated out loud at closure; it is not silently dropped.
- **nexus-ac4id closes on this work** (memo §3.2 / §4). Its part (1) dict-shape fix becomes
  moot — the doctor check stops enumerating collections client-side entirely; its part (2)
  "engine-side anti-join" IS `nexus.manifest_verify_all()`. Do NOT fix the dict shape
  separately. ac4id stays OPEN (noted, not closed) until this arc lands.
- **nexus-39upx (b) precondition**: the corpus-wide orphan sweep MUST filter on
  `index_state = 'complete'`. Sweeping a mid-index document would delete chunks an in-flight
  run has written but not yet manifested. The fence is precisely what makes (b) safe.
- **nexus-lcmbp non-goal — THE FENCE IS NOT A LOCK.** `index_state='indexing'` ALWAYS means
  *re-index*. It must NEVER mean *skip, someone else is running*. Reading it as a lock rebuilds
  lcmbp's exact bug one layer up. Concurrency remains the pipeline row's job.
- **Engine-floor tolerance**: the client ships WITHOUT waiting on `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION`.
  A pre-fence engine 404s the index-run routes and omits the fence fields; the client treats
  both as `unknown` and falls through to verification (today's post-AC2 behaviour). The floor
  bump RIDES THE NEXT ENGINE TAG per AGENTS.md § Engine-service release — never a tag cut for
  this arc alone. Fence unreadable => fail open to today's behaviour, logged at **WARNING**;
  a fence that silently stops working is ac4id all over again.
close_reason: Closed

GO overall — no Critical; the amended fail-closed gate (missing==0 AND referenced==chunkCount) is correctly implemented and tested (IndexRunFenceTest covers the zero-content case). description:

no Python `CREATE TABLE`, no SQLite anywhere):

```sql
ALTER TABLE nexus.catalog_documents
  ADD COLUMN index_state        TEXT,            -- NULL | 'indexing' | 'complete' | 'failed'
  ADD COLUMN index_content_hash TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  ADD COLUMN index_run_id       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  ADD COLUMN index_started_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '';

```

- **`collection IS NULL` rows are pre-backfill state, NOT orphans.** Get this wrong and every

doctor stops paging 156k chunk metadata rows (the nexus-ac4id part-2 transfer problem).

title: /v1/vectors get-by-ids silently truncates at 10 rows — no count, no error, requested ids beyond 10 simply absent
description: Found 2026-08-02 during gtltb pilot verification. HttpVectorClient collection.get(ids=[...]) against the deployed v0.1.61 engine returns AT MOST 10 rows regardless of ids requested: probe requested=5→5, 10→10, 20→10, 50→10, 157→10 (collection knowledge__dt-papers, all ids known-present). The response carries no count field and no truncation signal, so any consumer doing existence checks over >10 ids gets FALSE NEGATIVES (our first verification pass concluded 147/157 manifest chunks were MISSING from T3 — pure artifact). Third surface of the ocf52/uu4b9 silent-truncation class (docs_for_chashes, manifest get_many, now vectors get-by-ids). Fix shape per that class: server-side cap honored with an explicit count + client-side reconciliation/paging in HttpVectorClient (assert len(returned)==len(requested) or page transparently). QuotaValidator says 300 is the page limit, so the client legitimately sends 157-id batches today.
notes: SHAKEOUT-7.1.1 re-diagnosis (2026-08-03, agent D, live wire vs v0.1.62): the 10-row cap is CLIENT-SIDE, not a server cap. POST /v1/vectors/store-get honors limit faithfully to >=300 (20 ids/limit=300 -> 20; 50/300 -> 50). The observed truncation is HttpVectorClient.get()'s own signature default limit=10 (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:735) forwarded verbatim (~:758-767). SECOND latent cap: limit OMITTED -> server defaults to 20 (50 ids, no limit -> 20). The no-count/no-truncation-signal half of this bead stands (response keys exactly chashes/documents/ids/metadatas/spans). RE-SCOPE the fix: (1) client: default limit to len(ids) or page internally; (2) server: omitted-limit default 20 is its own silent cap — either len(ids)-bounded or explicit; (3) truncation signal/count still wanted. Primarily a client change, not the server-cap-plus-count shape the description prescribes.
close_reason: BOTH halves shipped (train commits e7a28071 client + this engine commit, unpushed pending n0ful closer). Client: limit default None, per-page len(batch), internal 300-paging, truncation tripwire, composition guards (offset/limit fail loud), masking doubles fixed, consumer asserts. Engine: ids.size() default, 1000 cap, single-statement COUNT(*) OVER() live-count with empty-page fallback, client advisory consumption. Blast radius was worse than filed: aspect extraction fed 10-of-157 fragments, taxonomy centroids from 4% of corpus — all silent-green via mirror-then-diverge test doubles. Bead corrections: endpoint was store-get not get; NO server cap existed (client signature default was the whole cause); store_get_many and catalog verify were never affected. Reviews: client 2 rounds + engine 3 rounds, final justified 0/0 each. ENGINE HALF RIDES THE NEXT TAG. Residuals: nexus-7g7fk (tombstone/sweep interaction), nexus-fnl6p.

title: nx daemon service stop concludes 'already stopped' from a lease MISS — a TTL-expired lease on a stalled-but-alive supervisor makes the documented stop&&start remedy a no-op race
description: Root-caused during the 7.0.0 package-upgrade gate (2026-08-01). stop_storage_service (storage_service_daemon.py:1436-1439) signals only what discover() names; a TTL-expired lease (15s) on a stalled supervisor (the lz3f2/f9y78 stall signature: alive, serving, not heartbeating) returns None -> 'No storage service lease found — already stopped', exit 0, nothing signalled. start then short-circuits on the next heartbeat's revived lease. The CONVERGENCE path is fixed in-release (upgrade_finish process-table snapshot + survivor sweep with /proc fallback), but the operator verb itself keeps the hole: stop&&start can leave the old process serving or double-spawn. Fix belongs in the SHARED daemon-lifecycle primitive (service_registry/RDR-149 conformance) — stop must consult the process table when the lease is absent, not conclude from absence. Evidence: two supervisors+two engines alive simultaneously captured mid-rehearsal; T1 scratch d76828f7. Deliberately NOT smuggled into the release-blocker patch; flag at v7.0.0 tag review.
notes: WAVE-2 DETERMINISTIC REPRO + ESCALATION (2026-08-03, sandbox, 3 commands — no stall needed, rm the lease file with supervisor+engine alive): (a) FALSE ALL-CLEAR: stop prints 'No storage service lease found — already stopped' rc=0 while the engine still serves /health 200. (b) STOP&&START SILENT NO-OP: live supervisor rewrites the lease within a heartbeat; start short-circuits to the SAME pid, generation NOT incremented — any convergence flow cycling the service to pick up a new binary keeps running the old one. (c) DOUBLE-SPAWN: SIGSTOP the supervisor (lz3f2/f9y78 alive-not-heartbeating signature) + rm lease + stop&&start -> TWO supervisor+engine pairs, both generation=1, both writing the same PG — the single-writer guarantee is DEFEATED (generation never increments) rather than violated-and-detected. Also: the engine child survives supervisor SIGSTOP and SIGTERM (had to be killed separately) — stop must signal the discovered TREE, not just what discover() names. Escalation-worthy: (c) is data-integrity, not just ergonomics.
close_reason: Landed as f2b26717, CI green run 31071743182. stop_storage_service is 3-phase (lease-signalled, process-table fallback on lease miss, unconditional tree-completion sweep), returns StopOutcome(pids, stubborn, source, lease_seen, sweep_verified); CLI exits non-zero on stubborn survivors or unverifiable process table so stop&&start breaks on failure; process-table primitives consolidated into service_registry.py per RDR-149 (upgrade_finish delegates, behavior preserved); one pid_alive with alive-on-ambiguous-OSError semantics pinned at both call sites. All three repro modes (false all-clear / silent same-pid restart / double-spawn) plus tree-signalling covered by non-vacuous tests, falsified empirically in review. 3 review rounds: code-review [21508], critique+closure [21510], implementation [21507].

title: MACHINE: kernel pipe-buffer pool exhausted — fresh pipes degraded to 512B; reboot needed, and the accumulator should be identified
description: Found 2026-08-01 root-causing nexus-2gcqk. A fresh pipe on this box accepts exactly 512 bytes before blocking (normal 16384). macOS xnu degrades new pipes when system-wide pipe memory is under pressure; the box has been up since Jul 5 accumulating pipes across Docker, IDEA, many Claude sessions and stale multiprocessing workers (some with 4+ day etimes parented to launchpid 1). ACTIONS (Hal): (1) reboot the box — restores 16KB pipes immediately; (2) optionally before reboot, identify the accumulator: 'lsof -n | awk $5=="PIPE"' per-PID counts were modest individually (idea 87, Claude sessions ~8 each, Docker ~50 across procs) so this looks like many-holders-times-long-uptime, the same chronic-accumulator class as the POSIX-semaphore exhaustion (see bd memory posix-semaphore-exhaustion). title: docs_for_chashes has no count-reconciliation like its chashes_for_collection sibling — a silently truncated tumblers list makes the union guard delete a live shared T3 row
design:
Found during code-review of 43b7932d (nexus-kgos1), diff 76a2f07c..HEAD.

_sweep_superseded_vectors (mcp_infra.py:923) trusts docs_for_chashes
(http_catalog_client.py:2212) as its union guard: a dropped chash is only
deleted from T3 if NO other document's manifest references it. That
correctness property depends entirely on docs_for_chashes returning a
COMPLETE reverse-lookup, not merely one that doesn't raise.

docs_for_chashes is a two-round-trip client-side reconstruction:
  1. POST /manifest/docs_for_chashes -> {"tumblers": [...]}  (flat list,
     no count field, no verification of completeness)
  2. get_manifests(tumblers) to rebuild chash -> [doc_id] edges

Round 2 is hardened: get_manifests's own docstring says "A page failure
propagates (whole call fails loud). Deliberate" (http_catalog_client.py
~2183). Round 1 has NO analogous protection: if /manifest/docs_for_chashes
returns a silently-truncated `tumblers` list (pagination limit, a
field-stripping proxy hop, engine query limit) WITHOUT erroring, some doc
that legitimately still references one of the dropped chashes goes missing
from the reverse lookup. _sweep_superseded_vectors then sees no other
referencer and hard-deletes a T3 row a live document still points to.

This is not hypothetical speculation about a new failure class: the
SIBLING reverse-lookup function in the same file, chashes_for_collection
(http_catalog_client.py:2273), was hardened against exactly this
(nexus-ir6eh / the nexus-znwc2 "field-stripping hop" class) by having the
engine emit a `count` field (floor >= v0.1.55) and having the client
reconcile len(chashes) == count, raising RuntimeError on any deviation
rather than trusting a 200 OK as proof of completeness. That fix was never
applied to docs_for_chashes.

Distinct from the two already-filed beads on this same union guard:
  - nexus-fcx2s is a TOCTOU race (a concurrent WRITE lands in the gap)
  - nexus-flkdc is a scope bug (the lookup is global, delete is
    collection-scoped)
This bead is neither: it's an INTEGRITY bug in a single point-in-time read
that can silently return an incomplete answer without raising, same as the
already-fixed chashes_for_collection defect, but here it feeds a DELETE
decision instead of a GC alive-set.

Because 43b7932d activates real deletion against live production T3 data
for the first time (nexus-kgos1), this determines whether an over-deletion
is actually reachable in practice, not just in theory.

Recommend: give /manifest/docs_for_chashes the same treatment as
/manifest/chashes — emit a count (or equivalent) alongside tumblers and
have the client fail loud on a mismatch, mirroring chashes_for_collection's
existing pattern in the same file.
close_reason: Closed

title: a retry against a stranded 'running' pipeline row younger than 5 minutes returns rc=0 with 0 chunks — nx index reports success for a complete no-op
description:
Direct violation of the no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness directive, found while
diagnosing the stranded pipeline row from the nexus-gtltb remediation.

service/.../db/PipelineRepository.java create():92-108 returns "skip" for an existing
`running` row younger than 5 minutes. Downstream, `nx index` exits rc=0 having written
ZERO chunks. Older than 5 minutes it returns "resuming" and re-fails loudly, which is
the correct behaviour.

So the observable contract is time-dependent: the SAME retry is a loud failure or a
silent success depending only on how long ago the previous attempt stranded.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE
The stranding bug (mark_failed ordering) leaves rows in exactly this state, so the
natural operator response — retry the failed document — reports success and does
nothing. A remediation driver that checks return codes would mark the document
remediated. This is how corrupted data survives a remediation pass while every gate
reads green.

FIX
"Nothing was done" must not exit 0. Either exit non-zero with a distinct code, or emit
a machine-readable "skipped, another run holds this content_hash" that callers must
handle. The 5-minute window is a reasonable concurrency guard; reporting success is
not the way to express it.

Note the interaction: fixing the mark_failed ordering removes the common way rows
strand, but does not fix this — a genuinely concurrent run hits the same path.
close_reason: Closed

title: mark_failed flushes BEFORE posting /fail, so a flush-triggered error re-raises and the pipeline row strands as 'running' with an empty error field — and the caller sees the CLEANUP error, not the original
description:
Found while diagnosing the /v1/pipeline/pages 500 on nexus-gtltb remediation doc 3.

src/nexus/db/http_pipeline_client.py:146-148 — mark_failed() calls flush() first. When
the original failure came FROM a flush, the raise had already restored the failing
pages into the buffer (:269-276), so cleanup re-POSTs the identical payload, takes the
identical error, and raises before the /fail POST is ever issued. Control therefore
never reaches pipeline_stages.py:793-795, so clear_orphan_wal() does not run and
`raise first_exc` does not run.

TWO CONSEQUENCES
1. The error surfaced to the caller is the SECOND one, from cleanup — not the original.
   Every log line and every bead written from that output names the wrong event.
2. The pipeline row strands. Probed live (content_hash=441da98b...):
       status='running'    <- not 'failed'
       error=''            <- no audit trail at all
       pages_extracted=0, total_pages=None, pdf_pages rows=0
       started_at == updated_at == 2026-08-01T10:12:38Z
   which is exactly the doc-3 window in the driver log.

FIX
POST /fail FIRST, then flush (or flush inside a suppressed block). The failure record
is the thing that must survive; buffered pages are best-effort. Add a regression test
that drives mark_failed with a flush that raises and asserts the /fail POST still went
out and the row reads 'failed' with a non-empty error.

Client-side, so it ships with a normal PyPI release and does not need an engine cut.
close_reason: Closed

title: the engine binds page_text unsanitized, so a PDF with NUL bytes in its text layer 500s /v1/pipeline/pages — a verbatim recurrence of CLOSED nexus-rvfwj one substrate layer over
description:
Hit while remediating nexus-gtltb: document 3 of 21, "Short term memory in echo state
networks", failed with

    HttpPipelineDB./v1/pipeline/pages failed: HTTP 500: internal server error

against the managed cloud engine (release 0.1.60).

ROOT CAUSE
The PDF's ToUnicode CMap is broken; its PyMuPDF text layer carries 949 NUL (0x00)
bytes and 79,183 C0 control characters across 60 pages. Postgres `text` cannot store
0x00 (SQLSTATE 22021). The engine binds page_text unsanitized at
service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/PipelineRepository.java:207
    (String) page.get("page_text")
Handler validation is type-only and content-blind (http/PipelineHandler.java:189-195).

THE DEFECT IS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT AN OVERSIGHT
The engine ALREADY strips NUL on the T3 vector path:
    PgVectorRepository.java:2507-2510  stripNul, applied at :441, :1145, :2525, :2530
which is exactly the fix that closed nexus-rvfwj (PR #1152). The RDR-186 .16 pipeline
buffer was added later and re-introduced the identical unsanitized bind against
different tables. Confirmed empirically: the 86 surviving T3 rows for this document
contain ZERO NULs, while the same source text 500s the pipeline path.

DIFFERENTIAL SCAN over the remediation worklist (proves document-specificity, and
that NUL alone is not sufficient — it needs NUL AND routing to the raw PyMuPDF
_extract_normalized fallback, whose normalizer only collapses whitespace):

    doc  pages  NUL  ctrl    outcome
     1     69    69   798    OK  (MinerU regenerated the text)
     3     60   949 79183    FAILED — the only doc on the raw PyMuPDF fallback
     6     18     4     8    OK  (Docling)
   2,4,5,7,8      0     0    OK

FIX (engine side — SECOND RELEASE LIFECYCLE: needs an engine-service tag, deploy,
cloud gate, then a REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION bump; it cannot ship with a PyPI release)
  - stripNul in writePages / writeChunks / metadata, mirroring PgVectorRepository.
  - See the split-out bead for the SQLSTATE 22021 mapping.

A client-side defensive strip of NUL/C0 from page_text is tracked separately and
stands alone without an engine cut. It is safe for PAGES specifically because no
chash derives from page text — do NOT blanket-strip chunk text, whose chunk_id/chash
is caller identity carried verbatim.
close_reason: Closed

title: path-based re-indexing forks a SECOND catalog document when the original was registered under an x-devonthink-item:// source_uri — the corrupted original stays live and searchable
description:
Found while remediating nexus-gtltb. The remediation driver ran
`nx index pdf <path> --collection <base> --force`, which keys document identity on
the file path. For a document originally registered from DEVONthink the registered
source_uri is x-devonthink-item://..., so the path-keyed index does NOT match it and
mints a NEW catalog document instead of updating the existing one.

MEASURED, knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1, "Zoology: Measuring and
Improving Recall in Efficient Language Models":

  tumbler   corpus    source_uri                          indexed_at    manifest
  1.12.104  dt        x-devonthink-item://169ADD1E-...    2026-07-27    400 chashes
  1.14.25   default   file:///.../pdf/24/Zoology- ....pdf 2026-08-01    395 chashes

Partition of the 638 title-matching T3 rows:
  only in 1.12.104 (old doc): 262 rows, 195 glued, 1222 glue matches
  in BOTH manifests (shared): 132 rows,   0 glued
  only in 1.14.25 (fresh):    244 rows,   3 "glued", all false positives
                                          (\phantom{xxxx...} inside a legitimate
                                           $$\begin{array}...$$ block)

So the re-index wrote correct chunks AND left the 262 corrupted chunks live — they
are in the OLD document's OWN CURRENT MANIFEST, so they are not orphans and no
orphan sweep would ever remove them. They remain searchable.

Likely identity-miss cause: title punctuation plus an embedded newline
("Zoology: ... Language Models" vs "Zoology- ... Language\nModels").

CONSEQUENCE
This makes the whole path-based remediation strategy wrong for DEVONthink-registered
documents: it doubles the corpus and leaves the corruption in place. Any remediation
must either re-index through the original source_uri identity, or explicitly

title: re-index replaces the manifest but never sweeps the T3 rows that fall out of it — orphaned chunks stay searchable because vector search reads T3, not the manifest
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 during the nexus-gtltb remediation, in answer to a direct
question: if chunks are content-addressed by chash, how can a re-index ADD rows?

THE ANSWER, and it is not a chash defect. chash keying works exactly as
intended: identical text upserts to the same row. The growth happens when the
text CHANGES — as it did when the normalizer fix landed. New text hashes to new
chashes, so the new chunks are genuinely new rows.

MEASURED on tumbler 1.14.19 immediately after `nx index pdf --force`:

    manifest rows          182     (the NEW extraction — correctly replaced)
    manifest unique chashes 163     (position-duplication; identical chunk text
                                     collapses to one T3 row by design)
    T3 rows for the title   180
    in manifest, not in T3    0     <- every referenced chunk IS present
    in T3, not in manifest   17     <- referenced by nothing

163 referenced + 17 orphaned = 180. The catalog layer is CORRECT. What is
missing is the sweep: nothing deletes T3 rows that fall out of the manifest.

WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING: vector search reads T3, NOT the manifest. An
orphaned chunk is unreferenced by the catalog and still fully searchable. After
a corruption fix, the corrupted text therefore keeps being retrieved and keeps
being embedded in results, while `nx catalog show` reports a clean manifest. The
document looks remediated by every catalog-level check and is not.

THIS IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE 4,108. The 2026-08-01 corpus audit measured 4,108
T3 chunks present in no manifest — code__1-1 2,807/32,285 (8.7%),
code__arcaneum 412/2,363 (17%), knowledge__knowledge 242/1,451 (17%). Those
proportions are what accumulated re-indexing would produce. The audit could not
attribute them because ids_for_source/delete_by_source are dead against the HTTP
client; this mechanism explains them without needing that handle.

It also matches the 2026-07-27 forensics memo's defect 5, "re-indexing ADDS, it
does not replace", which was recorded as an observation without a mechanism.
This is the mechanism.

THE CORRECT PURGE IS A MANIFEST DIFF. During remediation I first purged by
corruption-signature, which removes the visibly-broken orphans and leaves
clean-looking stale ones — 17 survived on a document I had already called fixed.
The manifest is the only authority on what belongs:

    keep    = set(get_chunk_chashes(tumbler))
    orphans = [id for id in t3_rows_for_document if id not in keep]

FIX OPTIONS:
 (a) sweep at the end of index/re-index — after the manifest is replaced, delete
     the document's T3 rows not in the new chash set. Narrow, correct, and the
     natural home.
 (b) a reconcile verb that does it corpus-wide, for the 4,108 already there.
 (c) both — (a) stops the bleeding, (b) cleans up.
(a) alone leaves the existing 4,108; (b) alone lets them keep accumulating.

CAUTION FOR (b): an orphan is not always garbage. Shared chunk text collapses to
one row referenced by MULTIPLE documents' manifests, so "not in THIS document's
manifest" is not "unreferenced" — a corpus-wide sweep must diff against the
UNION of all manifests, or it will delete chunks other documents depend on. The
per-document sweep in (a) has the same hazard and must check the union too.

RELATED: nexus-gtltb (the corruption whose remediation exposed this),
nexus-5xn3k (failed index poisons a document), nexus-jqrtp (t3 gc alive-set
unreachable in service mode), and the corpus audit's 4,108 figure.
notes:
SHAKEOUT-7.1.1 agent B corpus quantification (2026-08-03, live cloud store): ~8,234 orphaned chunks across 6 collections (code__1-1 6,511 @ 20.17% unjoined; knowledge__knowledge 408 @ 23.6%; rdr__1-1 825; docs__1-1 429; code__1-20 61 @ 0.21%; dt-papers 0). MECHANISM PROVEN in the data: orphan load is a function of RE-INDEX COUNT not corpus age (repeatedly-reindexed 20.17% vs indexed-once 0.21%/0.0%); orphans are superseded versions of files that still exist. SEARCHABLE AT RANK 1 (3/3 probes): catalog-003-soft-delete.xml:311-337 live_chunks treats manifest-less chunks as live BY DESIGN (RDR-145 store_put notes exemption), and re-index orphans inherit it. SWEEP PREDICATE CONSTRAINT (load-bearing): must distinguish re-index orphans from legitimate RDR-145 manifest-less notes or the sweep DELETES LIVE KNOWLEDGE — knowledge__knowledge's 23.6% is partly legitimate note load; the code__/rdr__/docs__ rates are defect load. source_uri populated 300/300 in catalog sample, so NULL joins are genuinely missing manifest rows, not column gaps.
WAVE-2 SCOPE NARROWING (2026-08-03, sandbox, psql-exact): the end-of-index orphan sweep this bead proposes as fix (a) ALREADY EXISTS AND WORKS on the md and code index paths — three mutation classes (md edit-in-place, code edit, md shrink 6->4 sections) all measured ZERO orphans; superseded T3 rows are DELETED at re-index (86573cb0 removed, stale-text probe returns only the new chunk). The bead's own founding evidence is nx index pdf --force on tumbler 1.14.19, and wave-1's corpus load concentrates in historically re-indexed collections. BEFORE implementing: reproduce on the PDF/--force path and interrupted-run path specifically — otherwise fix (a) gets written where it already runs. The corpus-scale sweep (wave-1 numbers) is still needed for the HISTORICAL load regardless of which path leaks today.

EXPLICIT SCOPE HANDOFF, not silent reduction: the corpus-wide cleanup of the ~8,234 measured orphans has NOT run — it is Hal's operator arm (nx t3 gc at next shakedown, method T2 [21454]); the tool is now note-safe and fence-safe for that run. comments.text:
PRECONDITION ON OPTION (b) from the 5xn3k RUNFENCE design — T2 21348
(`nx memory get -p nexus -t "5xn3k-design-2026-08-02"`), §5.

**The corpus-wide sweep (b) MUST filter on `index_state = 'complete'`.** Sweeping a document
that is mid-index would delete chunks an in-flight run has already written but has not yet
manifested — a hazard (b) creates on its own, and the RUNFENCE (nexus-5xn3k.1/.2) is what makes
it avoidable. Treat this as a stated requirement on (b), not a nice-to-have.

Ordering vs (a), which already landed (`_sweep_superseded_vectors`, 76a2f07c): the sweep runs
inside the position-0 manifest-replace path, so the fence's `/complete` verify runs AFTER the
last sweep. No race, by construction.

comments.text: From the 5xn3k.4 critique (2026-08-02): store_put-origin documents NEVER carry index_state (registered exclusion on nexus-5xn3k, accepted design) — your (b) sweep's index_state='complete' precondition therefore EXCLUDES them entirely. That is the conservative direction (their chunks are never swept: over-retention, not deletion) and is correct; do not 'fix' it by widening the filter to NULL — NULL means unknown, and sweeping unknown-state docs is exactly the mid-index-deletion hazard the precondition exists to prevent.

title: MinerU server pid file proved liveness, not identity — uv.lock did not control which mineru version extracted
description:
FIXED at e4d8ea8c. Filing for the record, since it was found and fixed inside the
nexus-gtltb investigation rather than reported first.

config.get_mineru_server_url step 2 adopts whatever server the shared config dir
registers, validated by is_process_alive() alone. The pid file recorded pid,
port, started_at, output_root — nothing identifying WHICH mineru that process
runs.

MEASURED: ~/.config/nexus/mineru.pid pointed at pid 15100, owned by
.../uv/tools/conexus/bin/python3 running mineru 3.4.4, while the develop venv
pins 3.1.11. Every `uv run` from develop with the default config dir extracted
through 3.4.4.

Correctness, not tidiness: the same fixture gave 59217 chars / 44 formulas on
3.1.11 and 58897 / 48 on 3.4.4. A test locking an exact length measures whichever
server happened to be registered — and so does every indexed document.

FIX: spawn stamps mineru_version + python into the pid file; discovery compares
and REFUSES a known mismatch (returns None so a matching server is spawned),
logging both versions, the registered interpreter and the remedy. Pid files
predating the change are still adopted, with a debug breadcrumb — absent identity
is not matching identity, and the log distinguishes them.

RESIDUAL, worth a follow-up decision rather than silently leaving: I observed
FOUR live mineru-api servers on this box at once (one from the installed tool,
three leaked by my own fresh-config-dir runs during the investigation). Each
fresh NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR autostarts a server and nothing reaps it. This fix stops a
skewed server being USED; it does not stop them accumulating. That is the same
class as nexus-lgdy1 (atexit-only teardown leaks substrate postmasters) and may
belong with it.

title: catalog /stats reports ~487 more documents than any enumeration returns — they are invisible to every list-based audit, GC and reconcile
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 by a live-corpus audit.

VERIFICATION LEVEL, stated up front. I confirmed MYSELF against the live cloud
catalog that stats reports doc_count = 22173. The enumeration figure (21,686
unique tumblers) comes from the dispatched audit, NOT from my own re-run —
HttpCatalogClient exposes no general document enumerator (only list_by_collection,
list_collections, list_owners, list_owners_by_type), so I could not cheaply
reproduce it by the same path. Treat the delta as well-evidenced but
second-hand; re-derive before acting.

THE DISCREPANCY: /stats 22,172-22,173 vs enumeration 21,686. ~487 documents
(2.2%) are COUNTED but never LISTED.

The audit excluded the obvious explanations:
 - not client paging: page sizes 500/1000/2000 return the same set with zero
   duplicate tumblers;
 - not a single-branch artifact: the separate content_type single-request branch
   agrees with the paginated one.
So two server endpoints disagree about how many documents exist.

SKEWED BY TYPE, which is the useful clue: rdr stats 459 vs list 91; prose 7,799
vs 7,699. The shortfall is not uniform, so whatever hides them correlates with
content_type or with something that co-varies with it.

WHY P1. These documents are invisible to EVERY list-based tool: audits, GC,
reconcile, drift detection, and the audit that found them. A GC that enumerates
to build its alive-set would treat their chunks as unreferenced. That is the same
hazard class as nexus-jqrtp (t3 gc's empty-alive-set guard unreachable in service
mode) — a sweep computing "alive" from an incomplete enumeration is a deletion
risk, not merely an accounting one.

It also caps the confidence of every corpus measurement made tonight, including
the extraction-quality distributions in nexus-gtltb: they cover the 21,686 that
are reachable, and nothing can say what the other 487 look like.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC STEP: compare the two server-side queries directly — whatever
/stats counts vs whatever the list route paginates. A predicate present in one
and absent in the other (deleted_at, a collection join, a tenant scope, a
NULL-column filter) is the likely shape, and it is the same family as
nexus-q8rbu, where listCollections has no superseded_by predicate.

RELATED: nexus-jqrtp (gc alive-set), nexus-q8rbu (list vs raw projection),
nexus-wnlit (catalog_link_audit returns {} in service mode).

title: extraction_method is recorded NOWHERE — no chunk or catalog document says which extractor produced it, so extractor quality cannot be compared or attributed retroactively
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 by a live-corpus audit that set out to compare mineru vs docling
vs pymupdf output quality and COULD NOT, because the pipeline does not record
which extractor produced anything.

MEASURED, exhaustively: every metadata key across all 11,374 chunks in the 10
PDF-bearing collections — 29 distinct keys, and `extraction_method` is not one of
them. Nor is it on catalog document meta: 0 of 422 PDF-typed documents carry it.
The only extraction-related key anywhere is `extraction_source: dt_content` on
108 chunks, all in knowledge__shakedown.

WHY THIS IS A REAL GAP, not bookkeeping. extraction_method EXISTS at extraction
time — tests assert on it (test_pdf_subsystem.py checks
result.metadata["extraction_method"] == "mineru"), the auto-router picks between
docling/mineru/pymupdf per document, and nexus-wi1uv is an open bug about docling
silently degrading. It is produced, asserted in tests, used to route... and
discarded before storage.

WHAT IT COSTS, concretely and today:
 - nexus-gtltb (P0, mineru's normalizer corrupting prose) cannot have its blast
   radius scoped from the data. "Which documents did mineru extract?" is
   unanswerable, so the re-index set must be inferred from a whitespace heuristic
   instead of read off the metadata.
 - nexus-wi1uv ("--extractor docling can complete with space-stripped,
   unsearchable output and report success") cannot be audited retroactively at
   all — no way to select docling-extracted chunks.
 - Any future extractor regression is equally unattributable. The corpus cannot
   answer "did quality change when we switched routing".

CONTRAST: the audit COULD measure quality (space ratios, per-document
distributions, catastrophic-chunk counts) and could NOT attribute any of it. That
asymmetry is the whole bug — we can see damage and not its source.

FIX: stamp extraction_method onto chunk metadata at write time (and/or the
catalog document meta). It is already in PDFExtractor's result.metadata; the
value simply is not carried through doc_indexer into the chunk write. Cheap, and
it makes every future extractor question answerable.

WORTH DECIDING AT THE SAME TIME: whether to backfill. Existing chunks cannot be
attributed without re-extraction, so a backfill is only possible as part of the
gtltb re-index — if that re-index happens without stamping the field, the
opportunity is lost again.

RELATED: nexus-gtltb (P0, needs this to scope its re-index), nexus-wi1uv
(docling degradation, unauditable without it), nexus-6xkdu (no automated
coverage of the mineru path at all).
close_reason: Closed

title: the slow and stress pytest markers are selected by ZERO commands repo-wide — anything marked slow is operationally deleted, and three docstrings claim otherwise
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 by an indexing-coverage survey during the 7.0.0 dry run. This is
the ROOT ENABLER behind nexus-6xkdu (MinerU has no coverage) and it is broader
than PDFs.

MEASURED, verified by grep across .github/, tests/, scripts/:

  -m slow      selected by NOTHING. Every occurrence outside pyproject addopts
               is a COMMENT.
  -m stress    selected by NOTHING. tests/stress/ contains only __init__.py, so
               the marker has no tests at all — it is dead.

pyproject.toml:195 addopts is
    -m 'not integration and not slow and not stress'
so both are deselected by default. `integration` HAS homes (the nightly
local-service gate, CA-3 jobs, the write-seam gate) with real non-vacuity guards.
`slow` and `stress` have none.

CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: a test marked `slow` is operationally DELETED. It
never runs, nothing counts it, no floor notices its absence, and no lint flags
the marker as unselected. It is worse than deleting the test, because the file
still reads as coverage to anyone opening it.

AND THE CODEBASE ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE IN THREE PLACES:
  tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py:452  "the release-sandbox shakedown step 3b still
      exercises MinerU end-to-end ... on every release run"
  tests/test_doctor_search.py:157  "CI and pre-release runs opt in with -m slow"
  tests/test_exporter.py:401       "run with uv run pytest -m slow or as part of
      the release shakedown"
None is true. Nothing invokes shakedown; nothing passes -m slow. Three
independent authors each recorded a coverage guarantee that does not exist —
which is why this is a P1 about the MECHANISM, not three doc fixes.

WHY IT WENT UNSEEN: the absence is unobservable by construction. A deselected
test produces no output, no skip line, no count. Contrast `integration`, whose
absence IS observable — local-service-gate.sh:285-295 asserts LIVED_IN_EXPECTED=39
exactly, :320-333 asserts CLOUD_MODE_EXPECTED=3 exactly, and :381-397 enforces a
passed floor and skip budget. Nobody built the equivalent for slow because
nothing ever ran it to notice.

WHAT TO DECIDE:
 (a) Give `slow` a home — a scheduled weekly job running `-m slow`, the way the
     nightly gate hosts `integration`. Pairs with nexus-5opzu (the same question
     for integration-only files that no gate covers).
 (b) Un-mark the tests that should always run and delete the marker.
 (c) Keep them dark deliberately — but then DELETE the three docstrings claiming
     coverage, and add a lint asserting no marker is unselected, so the next
     person cannot re-acquire the belief.
Doing nothing is (c) minus the corrections, which is the current state and the
one that produced this.

MECHANISATION WORTH HAVING REGARDLESS: a test that asserts every marker declared
in pyproject is selected by at least one command in .github/ or tests/e2e/. That
is a cheap, exact check and it would have caught both markers the day they went
dark. Same shape as the plugin release-drift ledger, which exists precisely
because merged-but-inert is invisible otherwise.

RELATED: nexus-6xkdu (MinerU, the worst instance), nexus-5opzu (integration
files with no gate), and the release-sandbox shakedown's `|| true` on all four
indexing steps (on 6xkdu).

title: MinerU end-to-end has ZERO automated coverage — the slow marker was justified by a shakedown that no release run invokes, and the one real test was red the first time anything ran it
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01. Asked directly whether the MinerU PDF intake path was broken,
untested, or masked. Measured answer: no automated coverage, and the justification
for removing it does not hold.

THE CHAIN, each link verified:

1. test_mineru_path_preserves_formulas is marked `slow`, and pyproject.toml
   addopts deselects slow by default. So no ordinary pytest run touches it.

2. Its docstring justifies that marker explicitly:
     "The release-sandbox shakedown step 3b still exercises MinerU end-to-end
      through the production `nx index pdf` path on EVERY RELEASE RUN, so this
      marker does not regress the user-facing fail-loud regression guard's
      reach."
   Step 3b is real - release-sandbox.sh:295, "3b/11 nx index pdf (bft-to-smr.pdf
   - MinerU path, formulas)". The claim about WHEN it runs is not.

3. The release checklist (CLAUDE.md step 6) runs `release-sandbox.sh smoke`.
   NOT shakedown. Grepped the whole repo: `shakedown` appears in CHANGELOGs,
   .gitignore and a few test files, and in NO workflow and NO checklist step as
   an invocation. Nothing runs it automatically, on a release or otherwise.

4. No workflow runs `-m slow` at all. The only mineru reference in .github/ is a
   ci.yml comment noting the HF cache exists for "the cross-encoder reranker and
   (under -m slow) MinerU's weights" - i.e. CI caches weights for a selector CI
   never uses.

5. A SECOND masking layer underneath: the test opens with
   `pytest.importorskip("mineru.cli.common")`. Even if someone ran `-m slow`
   without mineru installed, it SKIPS rather than fails. Absent coverage and
   absent dependency are indistinguishable in the output.

CONSEQUENCE, observed rather than predicted: the first time anything ran it in
this repo in a while - gate 1b of the 7.0.0 dry run, with slow included - it
FAILED. Text length 59217 against a locked 60135 (nexus's PDF-drift bead). Same
MinerU version (3.1.11, pinned since 2026-03-31), same page count, same 44
formulas, 918 fewer characters. Whatever caused it has been unobserved since the
constant was locked on 2026-05-05, across 17 commits to src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py
including the RDR-148 timeout/RLIMIT/degrade-to-docling arc and the nexus-c7odl /
nexus-1qdb9 on-demand lifecycle work.

SO THE HONEST STATEMENT OF RISK: MinerU extraction is not known to be broken -
formula_count and page_count still match, which is real evidence the core path
works. What is established is that NOTHING WOULD HAVE TOLD US either way, and the
one signal that exists went unread for ~3 months.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this is the bead's point, not the drift itself):
  (a) Run shakedown at release. It is written, it has the step, and the whole
      justification chain assumes it happens. Cheapest fix to the actual gap, and
      makes the docstring true rather than aspirational. Cost: 5-10 min warm,
      +10-15 min cold, per release.
  (b) Run `-m slow` in a scheduled job (weekly), so drift is caught within days
      rather than at the next release. Pairs with nexus-5opzu, which is the same
      question for integration-marked tests.
  (c) Keep it manual, but then FIX THE DOCSTRING - a comment asserting a
      guarantee nothing provides is the exact failure class this dry run has hit
      six times tonight.
Doing nothing is choosing (c) without the correction, which is the worst option.

ALSO FIX REGARDLESS: the importorskip should be conditional on an explicit
"mineru expected here" signal (an env var CI/shakedown sets), so an environment
that SHOULD have mineru fails loudly instead of skipping. Same non-vacuity shape
as NX_T2_SUBSTRATE_EXPECTED, which re-arms fail-loud once CI provisions the jar.

which is a candidate cause of the drift and a reproducibility hole in its own
right); nexus-5opzu (integration-marked tests with no gate anywhere).

title: nx doctor reports "T2 integrity" from the frozen SQLite migration source — and passes vacuously on a fresh box where the file does not exist
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 sweeping for further instances of the nexus-ypori class after
that one was fixed. This is the same defect, in health.py rather than doctor.py,
and it is reached by EVERY nx doctor run.

THE DEFECT. _check_t2_integrity (src/nexus/health.py:1218) calls
default_db_path() and opens it with sqlite3.connect - no service-mode branch,
no is_local_mode() consultation. It then labels its finding "T2 integrity".

T2 is Postgres in every mode since RDR-158 P4. The file it inspects is the FROZEN
SQLite MIGRATION SOURCE. So an operator reading "T2 integrity: ok" is being told
about a relic, under a label naming the store the system actually uses.

It is reached from run_health_checks() at health.py:3160 - the main sweep, not an
opt-in check.

TWO FAILURE MODES, the second worse than the first:

1. BOX WITH A LEGACY FILE: reports that file's PRAGMA integrity_check and FTS5
   probe as "T2 integrity". False attribution - a corrupt relic would raise an
   alarm about a store that is fine, and a healthy relic reassures about a store
   never examined.

2. FRESH BOX, NO FILE (health.py:1222-1223):
       if not db_path.exists():
           return [HealthResult(label="T2 integrity", ok=True, detail="not created yet")]
   A clean PASS that measured nothing. "not created yet" is true of the SQLite
   file and irrelevant to T2. This is the false-clean shape: ok=True is
   indistinguishable, to every caller, from a check that ran and found the store
   healthy.

   AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING RIGHT NOW: tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh requires
   "doctor: zero X, zero warn". On a virgin box this check contributes a green
   that asserts nothing - so the gate whose entire purpose is proving a fresh
   install works counts this as evidence.

CONTRAST, to show the fix is not speculative. The two neighbours in the same
sweep are already correct:
  _check_t2_dropped_writes (:1285) reads the telemetry meter, not SQLite, and
    degrades to an honest "meter unavailable: <exc>";
  _check_next_seq_drift (:3000) asks the catalog reader and says "skipped
    (engine does not report next_seq)" rather than rendering an all-clear it
    cannot support.
And the house fix-shape is established three times over: _report_aspect_queue_
service (nexus-k0luu), _report_dangling_links_service (nexus-i711w), and
linkDrift (nexus-ypori, 1b5b6275).

FIX: either ask the engine for T2 integrity (Postgres has its own answer -
Liquibase changeset state, or a cheap probe), or relabel and rescope this to
"legacy source integrity" so the name stops claiming the live store. What it must
NOT keep doing is return ok=True under a T2 label having looked at neither.

RELATED: nexus-ypori (same defect, doctor.py, fixed), nexus-vl8lk (two doctor
checks stubbed to a silent pass), nexus-k0luu and nexus-i711w (prior instances of
this exact class, both fixed by porting to a service reader).
notes: WAVE-2 confirmation (virgin sandbox): '✓ T2 integrity: not created yet' while three real rows sit in nexus.memory (PG). health.py:1233-1235 short-circuits on a missing SQLite file that on a PG install NEVER exists — the check is permanently vacuous for the entire supported install shape, not merely fresh boxes. Strengthens this bead's priority case.
close_reason: Landed as 1afef1dc, CI green run 31064208022. _check_t2_integrity retired and reborn as _check_t2_schema_applied: Liquibase changelog fingerprint via the engine's existing GET /version (probe_t2_schema_fingerprint), capability-honest absent-vs-null; frozen SQLite file demoted to its own informational line item. Dual-reviewed: code-review SHIP + substantive-critic partial (0 Critical; residuals beaded nexus-jvlmc, docstring fixed in-commit). Verdicts T2 [21499]/[21500], implementation [21495].

title: two nx doctor checks are N/A stubs that always pass — the SQLite retirement removed their diagnostics and never ported them to the engine
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31, generalising from nexus-ypori. That bead fixed --check-taxonomy
by giving it an engine path instead of the N/A its siblings print. The siblings
still print N/A, and the same argument applies to them: the question each asks is
real, so answering it against the wrong store should have become answering it
against the right one, not declining to answer.

THE TWO STUBS. Of 13 --check-* verbs in nx doctor, these do NO work and ALWAYS
exit 0:

  _run_check_schema (doctor.py:60)
    "T2 schema is service-backed (Postgres, Liquibase-managed) - local SQLite
     schema check N/A in service mode."
    LOST: the table/index/FTS5 census, which verified the schema was actually
    present and complete. The engine applies 209 Liquibase changesets at
    startup; nothing asks whether they applied. HealthHandler exposes no
    changelog/schema-version surface (grepped: no changelog, liquibase or
    schema_version references).

  _run_check_plan_library (doctor.py:296)
    "Plan library is service-backed (Postgres) - local SQLite dimensional
     census N/A in service mode."
    LOST: the authored / backfilled / non-dimensional counts AND the
    global-builtin floor - i.e. the check that the builtin plan templates are
    actually there.

A DEAD LOOP IN A RELEASE GATE, which is how this stops being theoretical.
tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:221-227 (smoke arm) still does:

    # nx catalog setup seeds 12 builtin plan templates that
    # --check-plan-library verifies. Without this step the doctor
    # check fails on every fresh sandbox...
    nx catalog setup 2>&1 | tail -5 | sed 's/^/    /' || true

`nx catalog setup` is RETIRED and raises (commands/catalog.py:299); the error is
swallowed by the `|| true`. The check it feeds always passes. So a release gate
runs a retired seeder to satisfy a stubbed verifier, and the comment explaining
why the pairing matters is still sitting above it. Both halves are dead and the
gate reports green.

WHY P1 RATHER THAN P2. These are not merely absent - they are absent and
REPORTING SUCCESS. A stub that prints and exits 0 is indistinguishable, to any
caller or gate, from a check that ran and found nothing wrong. That is the
false-clean class this project already has beads about, sitting inside the
diagnostic command operators run when something is already wrong.

RELATED BUT DIFFERENT, and deliberately not in scope here: a family of verbs was
RETIRED to a loud error rather than a silent pass - nx catalog init/setup,
taxonomy backfill-source-collection, aspects gc, aspects gc-fixtures, aspects
backfill-source-uri, aspects gc-pre-rdr096. Those are honest: they refuse and say
why. They are still capability losses (aspects gc was garbage collection) and may
each deserve an engine port, but they cannot mislead a gate. Worth its own audit,
not this bead.

WHAT TO DO, per check:
  schema        - ask the engine for applied-changeset state (a /health or admin
                  route reporting Liquibase status), or state plainly that the
                  engine self-applies at boot and the check is retired by design
                  - but then DELETE the verb rather than leave it passing.
  plan-library  - the builtin-template floor is the valuable half and is
                  answerable: the plan library lives in Postgres and the templates
                  are countable. Port the floor check; drop the SQLite-shaped
                  dimensional census if it no longer means anything.
  release gate  - remove the retired `nx catalog setup` call from the smoke arm
                  regardless of what happens to the check.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS ARGUES FOR: when a substrate retirement removes a
diagnostic, the check should either be PORTED or DELETED. Leaving it as a
passing stub is the worst of the three - it keeps the gate green, keeps the verb
in --help, and keeps operators believing something is checked.
close_reason: Landed as 1afef1dc, CI green run 31064208022. --check-schema: shared /version fingerprint probe, exit 2 unreachable / 1 schema_error or zero changesets / 0 OK or honest N/A. --check-plan-library: whole-library census via HttpPlanLibrary.list_plans, bucketing preserved, builtin floor reinstated, page-cap NOTE non-vacuous; sandbox seeding un-broken (nx plan reseed replaces retired nx catalog setup swallowed by || true). SQLITE_CONNECT_ALLOWLIST 3->2. Dual-reviewed; floor-drift tripwire beaded nexus-jvlmc.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DEFINITIVE COUNT + PRECEDENT, from an AST parse of every check rather than the
grep I filed this on.

Exactly TWO stubs remain of 15 _run_check_* functions:
    _run_check_schema         13 LOC  "N/A in service mode", no calls
    _run_check_plan_library   14 LOC  "N/A in service mode", no calls
Everything else does real work (LOC 15-120, 1-11 distinct calls). My original
filing said "of 13 --check-* verbs" from a CLI-option grep; the function-level
count is 15 and the stub count is unchanged at 2.

THE IMPORTANT PART — THIS CLASS HAS BEEN FIXED TWICE ALREADY, and the fix shape
is established. Two checks that looked thin in the parse turned out to be
DELEGATIONS to service implementations, and their docstrings describe exactly
the defect nexus-ypori just fixed for taxonomy:

  _run_check_aspect_queue -> _report_aspect_queue_service()
    "nexus-k0luu: reads the SERVICE queue (PG). This check once had no service
     branch - on a migrated box it read the FROZEN SQLite queue and reported it
     as current while the live queue was in PG, which is worse than useless
     here: `nx aspects requeue-failed` directs operators to this very check for
     backlog visibility."

  _run_check_dangling_links -> _report_dangling_links_service(strict=strict)
    "Service-only since nexus-i711w: the sqlite branch died with the local
     catalog - the catalog is service-backed in every mode."

So the pattern is: port the body into a _report_<thing>_service() helper and
have the check delegate. taxonomy (ypori) is the THIRD instance; schema and
plan_library are the fourth and fifth, and the only ones left.

WHAT THAT CHANGES ABOUT THIS BEAD: it is no longer a design question. There is
a house style for the fix, two worked examples in the same file, and a third
just landed. The remaining work is mechanical for plan_library (count the
builtin templates in PG, restore the floor) and a decision only for schema
(ask the engine for applied-changeset state, or delete the verb — but not leave
it passing).

Also worth recording: the k0luu docstring's reasoning is the argument for P1
here. It calls reading the frozen source "worse than useless" precisely because
another command points operators AT the check. --check-plan-library has the
same property: release-sandbox.sh runs a (now retired) seeder specifically to
satisfy it.

title: nx doctor --check-taxonomy diagnoses the FROZEN SQLite migration source in service mode — its two sibling checks correctly say N/A, and it now blocks the release smoke gate
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 by the 7.0.0 release dry run. The release-sandbox smoke gate is
RED because of this, and the failure it reports is not about the running system.

THE DEFECT. _run_check_taxonomy (src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:1926) calls
default_db_path() at :1940 and opens it at :1949 through _t2_diagnostic_connect
(:18), i.e. sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro"). It references
is_local_mode(), service_url and NX_STORAGE_BACKEND NOWHERE — verified by
inspecting the function source. So in service/cloud mode it silently diagnoses
~/.config/nexus/memory.db: the FROZEN SQLITE MIGRATION SOURCE, a read-only relic
by design, and reports that file's staleness as a live fault.

THE CONTRAST MAKES IT UNAMBIGUOUS. The same doctor loop runs three checks. In
service mode:
    nx doctor --check-schema        -> "T2 schema is service-backed (Postgres,
                                        Liquibase-managed) - local SQLite schema
                                        check N/A in service mode."  [pass]
    nx doctor --check-plan-library  -> "Plan library is service-backed (Postgres)
                                        - local SQLite dimensional census N/A in
                                        service mode."               [pass]
    nx doctor --check-taxonomy      -> reports 50/986 drift off the SQLite file
                                                                     [FAIL]
Two of three siblings already have the service-mode branch. The third was missed.

WHAT IT REPORTED, AND WHY IT IS NOISE. "topic_links drift: 50/986 topic(s) have
projection assignments but no topic_links row", all rendering "(unlabelled id=N)".
Measured: ZERO of those 50 ids exist in the cloud (get_topic_by_id returns None
for 1062, 1097, 1671, 1676 individually); the cloud holds 403 topics; the
local/cloud id intersection is 157 and excludes all 50. The rows are orphaned
topic_ids left in the local file by a 2026-05-13 taxonomy rebuild that restarted
the topics id sequence at 3012 without cascading deletes; their assignment
timestamps stop at 2026-05-12. Unlabelled because the LEFT JOIN finds no topics
row at all - topics.label is TEXT NOT NULL, so a null label is impossible.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, BOTH LIVE:

1. RELEASE GATE. tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh smoke now propagates doctor failures
   (fixed at d5deea05 - it previously printed [FAIL] and exited 0). With that fix
   in place this check makes the smoke gate exit non-zero on every box carrying a
   populated legacy memory.db. A release is now blocked by stale migration-source
   data. The gate fix is correct and should stay; this check is what needs the
   branch.

2. THE CHECK IS UNMEASURABLE WHERE IT MATTERS. Nobody can currently ask "does the
   LIVE catalog have topic_links drift?" through nx doctor. Whether the cloud has
   an equivalent divergence is UNKNOWN and was not determinable: get_topic_link_pairs
   requires an explicit topic_ids argument and no bulk assignments-by-topic read
   surface was found. So this is not merely a false positive - it is a false
   positive standing where a real check should be.

FIX: give it the sibling branch. Either the honest N/A the other two print, or -
better, since the question is real - a service-mode implementation that asks the
engine. If the engine lacks the read surface for it, the N/A is the correct
interim and the missing route is its own bead.

RELATED: nexus-m3t93 was filed earlier today claiming this drift was in the shared
cloud taxonomy; that scope claim is RETRACTED on the bead. NO-SQLITE context: this
is one of the three allowlisted surviving sqlite3.connect sites (storage_boundary_
lint.py SQLITE_CONNECT_ALLOWLIST names doctor.py), so the site is sanctioned -
what is wrong is running it when the operator is not on that substrate.
close_reason:
FIXED at 1b5b6275 — given an engine path rather than the N/A its siblings print.

Engine: TaxonomyRepository.linkDrift(tenant, limit) + POST /links/drift, with the predicate deliberately co-located with refreshProjectionLinks so the audit and the materializer cannot drift apart again (they already had, in opposite directions — nexus-346q's inversion, fixed at d0e9173e). drift_count exact, rows capped.

Client: service first; the SQLite census demoted from verdict to a no-engine fallback note. Kept rather than deleted because it is the only taxonomy inspection of the frozen source and RDR-176 Gap 2 wants those probes working with no engine running — it is why storage_boundary_lint allowlists this module's sqlite3.connect. The fallback names the store it read and withholds the 'nx taxonomy project --backfill --persist' remedy, which rebuilds the Postgres view and would do nothing to the SQLite file just shown.

Two bugs found by running it live, both invisible to the mocks: a mis-scoped 'suppress' whose cleanup raised UnboundLocalError WHILE handling the 404 and replaced it (so the operator was told about a local variable instead of a missing route), and the 404 itself, which now reads distinctly from 'no service' because the operator's action differs.

My own service-branch tests were VACUOUS and are fixed: they passed while the branch was crashing, because the fallback's 'invariant holds' wording matched the assertion. Now they assert the legacy markers are ABSENT, plus a pin that makes get_link_drift raise 404 so the masking regression cannot return.

Verified: 24 phase5 + 65 health Python; 61 TaxonomyRepositoryTest (59 + 2 new), read from fresh surefire reports rather than an exit code. Falsified both sides — inverting the Java predicate fails the new Java test; removing the client branch fails exactly the three service tests.

DELIVERY: /links/drift ships with the next engine tag. Until deployed the client 404s, says so precisely, and falls back — verified against the live cloud engine, which correctly lacks the route.

GENERALISED: nexus-vl8lk (the two doctor checks still stubbed to a silent pass) and nexus-1i5nn/audit bead for the loudly-retired verb family.

title: fresh-install MVV is RED: every owner created by a virgin install has next_seq stranded at its high-water mark — nx doctor warns on a brand-new box
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 by the 7.0.0 release dry run. This is a RELEASE BLOCKER as the checklist stands: step 1b (fresh-install MVV) must end 'FRESH-INSTALL MVV PASSED' and it does not.

THE FAILURE, verbatim from a scrubbed-env virgin HOME:

  ⚠ tumbler allocator drift: 2 owner(s) whose allocator is at or below their
    highest existing tumbler: 1.2 (next_seq=1, highest child=1);
    1.1 (next_seq=1, highest child=1). The engine floors past this on the next
    registration, so these self-heal when next written to.
  FRESH-INSTALL MVV FAILED: non-allowlisted warnings in a virgin box's doctor

Evidence preserved at /tmp/fresh-mvv-zM8Doc/logs (doctor.log, catalog-store.log,
catalog-md.log). Owner 1.1 is created by the journey's ; 1.2 by its
. BOTH drift. This is not an edge case in the journey — it is every
owner the journey creates.

WHAT IT MEANS. health.py:3062 flags drift as . next_seq=1 with an
existing child at 1 means the allocator's next hand-out COLLIDES with a tumbler that
already exists. registerDocument allocated the child without advancing next_seq past
it, so the allocator is stranded at its own high-water mark the moment an owner gets
its first document.

THIS IS THE nexus-pbawi / nexus-0ehwe CLASS, ON A FRESH BOX, WITH THE CURRENT ENGINE.
pbawi describes exactly this ('next_seq stranded below high-water mark'). The
difference is that pbawi was found as a wedge on a long-lived install; this shows the
condition is created at owner birth, on v0.1.60, by the ordinary happy path.

WHY IT SURFACED ONLY NOW — and why that is the observability working. The doctor
check fails SAFE when the engine omits the field: 'skipped (engine does not report
next_seq — needs the nexus-0ehwe engine change)', with an explicit non-vacuity
comment saying an all-clear it cannot support must not be rendered. The check has
therefore been SKIPPING, not passing. The engine change that reports next_seq is now
live, the check became non-vacuous, and it immediately found drift on the first
virgin box it saw. Nothing regressed today; a blind spot opened its eyes.

description:

  test_memory_get_and_search_shape_parity_live
  test_telemetry_consents_and_relevance_shape_parity_live
  test_taxonomy_topics_shape_parity_live
all take the module-scoped sqlite_db fixture (tests/db/test_http_shape_parity_integration.py:33), which does:

  os.environ['NX_STORAGE_BACKEND'] = 'sqlite'
  return T2Database(tmp/'t2.db', run_migrations=True)

That now raises StorageModeFlagError: 'NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite selects the retired SQLite storage backend. The SQLite T2 stores and the local SQLite catalog were deleted in the RDR-158 P4 retirement.'

NOT A MECHANICAL FIX. These are PARITY tests: they assert the HTTP store returns the same dict KEYS as the local SQLite store, with a frozen divergence allowlist (_MEMORY_ALLOW is EMPTY — full parity is the contract). The SQLite side is the ORACLE, and it was deleted. There is nothing left to compare against, so the test cannot do its job as written.

The fixture's own docstring is worth reading before deciding — it explains why the pin exists at all: T2Database's hard default is StorageBackend.SERVICE, so an UNPINNED construction routes to whatever service endpoint resolves; under the gate that was the gate's own service (wrong bearer -> 401 on every op), and on a dev box the LIVE supervisor lease, i.e. the test would write probe rows into production T2 and compare the service against itself.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
 (a) DELETE the three tests + the fixture. Honest, but drops the only live-service pin on those three row shapes — exactly the class nexus-5opzu is about (a sole pin that runs nowhere is bad; a sole pin deleted is worse).
 (b) CONVERT to service-shape snapshot pins: freeze the expected key sets as literals. Preserves the contract but blesses whatever the service returns TODAY, including any regression already present. No better oracle exists now that SQLite is gone.
 (c) Re-point the local half at a fake in-process handler, the way tests/db/test_t2_return_shape_parity.py does.

NOTE ON (c), stated as an OPEN QUESTION not a finding: test_t2_return_shape_parity.py names its fixture 'sqlite_store' and its section header says 'SQLite MemoryStore vs HttpMemoryStore', but it carries ZERO backend pins (grep: 0 hits for NX_STORAGE_BACKEND/StorageBackend), so with the SERVICE default that store is not SQLite. Its docstrings are stale at minimum. I checked the obvious hazard and it did NOT reproduce: running it left no 'shape' project in live T2, so the suite's _isolate_config_dir / _isolate_service_endpoint_env fixtures appear to contain it. What that file's comparison actually proves post-P4 is unverified and should be established before copying its pattern.

title: guidance delivery: re-plumb the SessionStart imperative from cat-SKILL.md (Tier C, pinned) to nx hook session-start (Tier B, PyPI) — collapses the dormancy window for all future guidance edits
description:
TIER C (edits conexus/hooks/hooks.json) -- DORMANT until the next plugin release,
MUST be declared in conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md. This is the LAST time guidance
work has to pay that cost. That is the entire point of the bead.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM, not a wording problem. The guidance imperative currently
reaches sessions as hooks.json SessionStart entry #6:

    "command": "cat $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/using-nx-skills/SKILL.md"

`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` resolves to the PINNED release tag. So every future edit to
the wording, ordering, or trigger conditions of the guidance imperative is inert
until a plugin release. This problem has now failed TWICE at the guidance layer
(nexus-4av2n, then nexus-3sij7 reproducing it with 4av2n's own diagnosis in
context the whole time). Iterating a fix on a release cadence, when each
iteration takes a release to even become observable, is why it has not converged.

THE FIX: re-plumb the imperative to be emitted by `nx hook session-start`, which
is ALREADY a hooks.json SessionStart entry (#3) and is ALREADY a PyPI binary --
i.e. Tier B. After this one dormant change, every subsequent guidance edit is
live at the next session. Guidance iteration goes from release-cadence to
session-cadence, permanently.

This is the highest-leverage item in nexus-h33x8 and it was in none of the four
proposed directions.

BUILD
 - move the imperative text into the wheel (src/nexus/), emitted by
   `nx hook session-start`;
 - drop or reduce the `cat .../using-nx-skills/SKILL.md` entry accordingly;
 - the SKILL.md file itself REMAINS as the Skill's own body -- this changes the
   SessionStart DELIVERY channel only, not the skill.

SEQUENCING vs nexus-h33x8.5: .5 (content restructure + volume cut) should land
AFTER this, so that .5 and every later revision are session-cadence rather than
release-cadence. Landing .5 first means the content iteration itself is dormant,
which is the trap.

HONEST LIMIT: this does NOT make guidance outrank a system prompt. Text delivered
at SessionStart is still text, whichever tier delivers it, and nexus-4av2n
already concluded a line cannot be relied on to outrank a system-prompt line.
What this buys is ITERATION SPEED on the layer that is admittedly weak, plus the
ability to A/B a wording change against nexus-h33x8.1's census within days.
Mechanism remains nexus-4av2n's.

=== VERIFICATION ===
1. TIER PROOF, the assertion that matters: after this ships, change ONE WORD of
   the imperative in the wheel only, run `nx upgrade`, start a fresh session, and
   confirm the changed word appears -- with NO plugin release and NO change to
   hooks.json. If that round-trip does not work, the bead has not delivered,
   regardless of the diff looking correct.
2. Byte-parity check on first landing: the imperative that reaches a session must
   be equivalent in content to what `cat SKILL.md` delivered, so this change is
   isolated to CHANNEL. Any content change is .5's job and must not be smuggled
   in here -- otherwise a later regression cannot be attributed to either bead.
3. PENDING_RELEASE.md entry exists and names this bead. Enforced by the existing
   tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py -- if the entry is missing the suite
   fails, so this verification is already mechanical.
4. DO NOT CLOSE ON MERGE. This is Tier C: it is inert until the plugin release
   ships. Closing on merge would repeat the 2026-07-25 error the ledger's own
   header records. Close only after verification 1 passes on a released plugin.

title: census: recognize Agent dispatches from transcript subagent_type+ordinal — the recognizer nexus-nu7fo's name-morphology can never provide
description:
TIER A (PyPI wheel). Live next session. No plugin release. DEPENDS ON nexus-h33x8.1.

THE DEBT THIS PAYS: nexus-nu7fo records FOUR consecutive sessions in which the
RDR-184 Gap-1 guard recognised ZERO dispatches -- 0/6, then 0/10, then 0/7, then a
fourth. Root cause is structural: the guard keys on a NAME-MORPHOLOGY (`a<name>-<hash>`)
and the Agent tool in this harness has NO `name` parameter, so the morphology can
never be present and `undeclared=0` is UNFALSIFIABLE by construction. nu7fo's own
fix option (a) is "key the guard on something the runtime actually emits".

THE RUNTIME DOES EMIT IT -- VERIFIED, not assumed. Every `Agent` tool_use block in
the transcript carries `input.subagent_type` and `input.description`. Checked on
session 75695009: all 7 dispatches recoverable with types, e.g.
  subagent_type=conexus:code-review-expert   description="Code review attempt-3 fix"
  subagent_type=conexus:substantive-critic   description="Critique attempt-3 fix"
So the transcript IS the recognizer that name-morphology can never be.

BUILD
  `nx census dispatches [--session <id>] [--json]`
  - enumerate every Agent tool_use with (ordinal, subagent_type, description);
  - key on (subagent_type, ordinal-within-session). Ordinal is required because
    the same type is dispatched repeatedly (code-review-expert appears 3x in the
    golden session) and type alone cannot distinguish them;
  - emit in a form the expectations ledger can consume, so nexus-nu7fo can adopt
    it without re-deriving the parse.

SANITIZATION, or the rows will be rejected: `expectations_expect` validates
`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`. Plugin-namespaced types carry a colon
(`conexus:substantive-critic`) and MUST be sanitized before emission or the row
cannot be accepted at all. This is called out in the repo AGENTS.md hot rules and
is the exact trap that has already cost sessions.

SCOPE FENCE: this bead SUPPLIES the recognizer. It does NOT modify
conexus/hooks/scripts/expectations.sh, does NOT change the ledger's verdict
logic, and does NOT close nexus-nu7fo -- that bead owns the decision between its
options (a), (b) and (c), and (b) (fail loud when recognized==0 while start>0)
should land regardless of this work. Adopting this recognizer is nu7fo's call.
Note also that expectations.sh is TIER C and already sits in
conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md, so the ledger half is dormant while this half is not.

=== VERIFICATION ===
1. GOLDEN, exact: on session 75695009 report EXACTLY 7 dispatches, with the
   multiset of subagent_types matching the transcript. Contrast this directly
   against the ledger's recorded 0/7 for the same class of session -- that
   0-vs-7 delta IS the proof, and the bead should print both numbers side by
   side when it closes.
2. Across the corpus: recognised dispatch count must equal the raw `Agent`
   tool_use count from nexus-h33x8.1 (1,012 lifetime). Any shortfall is a
   recognizer gap and must be reported, not rounded away.
3. NON-VACUITY: a session with zero dispatches must report UNMEASURABLE-vs-ZERO
   distinctly (same rule as .1). A recognizer that reports a confident 0 for a
   file it could not parse recreates the exact defect nu7fo documents.
4. SANITIZATION test: assert `conexus:substantive-critic` is emitted in a form
   matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`. Without this the whole output is
   unusable downstream and the bead would close green while delivering nothing.
