PLAN AUDIT 2026-07-31 — SIGNIFICANT: THE PROPOSED KEY IS THE WRONG ONE, AND AN EXACT JOIN
KEY EXISTS THAT THE BEAD DID NOT LOOK FOR. The bead asks whether (subagent_type, ordinal)
can pair against what SubagentStart stamps. Answer: not directly, and it does not need to.

WHAT SubagentStart ACTUALLY STAMPS (conexus/hooks/scripts/subagent-start-stamp.sh, and the
row format at expectations.sh:32):
    <iso-utc-ts> TAB START TAB <agent_id> TAB <agent_type>
There is NO ordinal anywhere in a START row. Pairing on (type, ordinal) would require
reconstructing the ordinal on the ledger side from row order — precisely the fragile
positional inference that produced nexus-nu7fo. Ordinal also breaks under concurrent
dispatch, which this repo does constantly.

WHAT THE TRANSCRIPT ACTUALLY OFFERS — richer than the bead states. Each sidechain carries a
SIBLING META FILE the bead never mentions:
    75695009.../subagents/agent-a08b06e6ef9d295b4.meta.json
    {"agentType":"conexus:substantive-critic","description":"Critique attempt-3 fix",
     "toolUseId":"toolu_019MCCAf2y8HWRzpQPeFd6ND","spawnDepth":1}
`toolUseId` IS the dispatching Agent tool_use block's `id` — verified, it matches dispatch
#2 of 8 in the main file exactly. And the transcript FILENAME carries the agent_id that
SubagentStart stamps. So there are two exact joins available:
    orchestrator Agent tool_use.id  <-->  meta.toolUseId   (dispatch -> run)
    filename agent-<agent_id>       <-->  START row $3     (run -> ledger)
RECOMMEND: key on agent_id, carry subagent_type as an ATTRIBUTE, use toolUseId to link back
to the dispatch. Ordinal becomes a display convenience, not an identity. Bonus: agent_id
(`a08b06e6ef9d295b4`) already satisfies `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` natively, so the
sanitization problem disappears for the KEY and remains only for the type attribute.

SIGNIFICANT 2 — PART OF WHAT THIS BEAD PROPOSES TO BUILD ALREADY EXISTS IN THE LEDGER, and
the bead's stated goal ("emit in a form the expectations ledger can consume, so nu7fo can
adopt it without re-deriving the parse") will not be met without knowing this. Read
expectations.sh:323-331 and :369:
    $2 == "START" { started[$4] = 1 }                       # keyed by agent_TYPE
    for (nm in expect) if (!(nm in started)) print "EXPECTED_NO_START..."
So the TYPE-KEYED half already works today: an EXPECT row whose name equals the sanitized
agent_type ALREADY pairs. What is broken is only the `undeclared` half, computed per
agent_id via `name[$3]`, which line 326 gates behind the morphology
`index($3, "a" $4 "-") == 1`. But line 331 proves the agent_id -> agent_type mapping is
ALREADY IN THE START ROW ($3 and $4, side by side). The morphology gate is discarding a
mapping it is holding.

title: census: nx census capability — offline per-capability tool-use census over transcript JSONL (Tier A, no plugin release)
description:
TIER A (PyPI wheel). Live at the next session via `nx upgrade --auto`. NO plugin
release, NO new hooks.json entry, NO CI job. Independently executable today.

WHY THIS FIRST: non-use is currently undetectable, and nexus-nu7fo proves even
dispatch counting is broken. You cannot enforce what you cannot measure, and
every other child in nexus-h33x8 is gated on this one's numbers.

WHY NO HOOK IS NEEDED (this is the cheap insight): the substrate is already
complete on disk. Every tool call is a `tool_use` block in the session transcript
JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, carrying `name` and full `input`. The
whole baseline table in nexus-h33x8 was computed from it with ~20 lines of
Python. A hook-based census would have been dormant, would have cost hot-path
time, and would NOT have been retroactive. This is retroactive over every
transcript already on disk.

PRECEDENT TO COPY, do not invent a new shape: `nx hook routing-stats`
(src/nexus/commands/hook.py) already aggregates a JSONL log into per-rule
fire/deny/escape stats, and its own docstring names the use case -- "spot ...
inert matchers (zero fires)". Same problem, same shape, different log.

BUILD
  `nx census capability [--session <id>] [--since <date>] [--json]`
  - walks transcript JSONL (main + subagent sidechain dirs; sidechain = file in a
    subdirectory), counts `tool_use` blocks by name;
  - classifies into capability buckets: Skill, Agent, Serena (mcp__plugin_sn_serena*),
    nx_answer, search/query, other-nx-MCP, Bash/Read/Edit/Write (baseline);
  - reports PER SESSION and AGGREGATE, and splits ORCHESTRATOR vs SUBAGENT --
    that split is the epic's sharpest signal (plan_search 12 vs 281) and a census
    that collapses it hides the finding.
  - parser must be a PURE function over parsed records so it is unit-testable
    with fixtures and needs no substrate.

HARD REQUIREMENT -- distinguish "forgotten" from "correctly rejected". A census
that cannot tell those apart will manufacture false compliance debt. See child .6:
nx_answer's non-use is probably a RATIONAL latency trade, not a discipline
failure. Minimum viable form: report raw counts and explicitly REFUSE to emit any
compliance verdict. Counts are the deliverable; judgement is not.

NON-VACUITY, borrowed from nexus-nu7fo's BLINDSPOT line, which is the only reason
that guard's false-clean was ever caught: when the census cannot parse a
transcript, or finds zero tool_use blocks, it must report UNMEASURABLE and exit
non-zero -- never a clean zero. A zero that means "measured zero" and a zero that
means "measured nothing" must be textually distinguishable in the output.

=== VERIFICATION (how you know it WORKED, given silent non-use looks like success) ===
1. GOLDEN SESSION, exact assertions: run against session
   75695009-d060-4433-a687-214cb946389a and assert EXACTLY
   Bash=150, Edit=19, Agent=7, Read=6, Write=3, ToolSearch=2,
   Skill=0, serena=0, nx-MCP=0.
   Exact, not >=. These are the numbers in nexus-3sij7 and they must reproduce.
2. CORPUS REPRODUCTION: aggregate over the full project corpus must reproduce the
   nexus-h33x8 baseline table -- Skill 61/100, Serena 13/100, nx_answer 2/100
   (4 lifetime calls), Agent 69/100 -- or the discrepancy is explained in writing
   before the bead closes.
3. NON-VACUITY, the one that matters: feed (a) an empty file, (b) a truncated /
   corrupt-JSON file, (c) a valid transcript with no tool_use blocks. All three
   must report UNMEASURABLE and exit non-zero. If any returns a clean 0, the
   census reproduces exactly the false-clean failure of nexus-nu7fo and is worse
   than nothing.
4. FALSIFY BY DELETION: delete the Skill-classification branch; test 1 must fail.
   A census whose assertions survive deleting the code under test is vacuous.

DOES NOT: emit at session end (child .3), judge compliance, or close nexus-nu7fo.

title: EPIC: restore the agent tool-guidance layer — make capability non-use measurable first, mechanical second
description:
MEASURED, not impressionistic. Evidence bead: nexus-3sij7 (session 75695009, 2026-07-31).

=== THE MEASUREMENT (this epic's baseline; re-derivable, see child .1) ===
Corpus: 1,606 transcript JSONL files under
~/.claude/projects/-Users-hal-hildebrand-git-nexus/ (main + subagent sidechains),
100 sessions carrying >=1 tool call, 82 of them "substantial" (>=50 calls).

  capability      sessions w/ >=1 use      lifetime calls
  Skill                  61/100 (61.0%)              185
  Serena (any)           13/100 (13.0%)              464
  search / query         33/100 (33.0%)              138
  nx_answer               2/100 ( 2.0%)                4   <-- four. lifetime.
  Agent                  69/100 (69.0%)            1,012
  Bash                        --                   58,640

Evidence session 75695009 exactly as nexus-3sij7 reports: Bash 150, Edit 19,
Agent 7, Read 6, Write 3, ToolSearch 2 -- Skill 0, nx MCP 0, Serena 0.

=== THE FRAMING IS PARTLY WRONG, AND THAT MATTERS FOR TARGETING ===
"We have lost almost any use of our tools" is TRUE for nx_answer (4 lifetime) and
Serena (13%); HALF-TRUE for Skills (61%, but 39% of sessions use none); and FALSE
for T2 memory / scratch / plan_search -- 87% of sessions touch some nx MCP tool.
A design treating "tools" as one block will mis-target. Everything here is
PER-CAPABILITY.

=== THE SHARPEST SIGNAL: ORCHESTRATOR vs SUBAGENT ===
                     MAIN   SUBAGENT
  plan_search          12        281
  scratch              61        929
  memory_search       149        588
  nx_answer             2          2
The SubagentStart preflight ("run these four reads BEFORE substantive work")
gets 15-23x the compliance of the SessionStart delivery of the same instruction,
on a SMALLER channel: measured SubagentStart 3,721 bytes vs SessionStart 12,817
bytes (7,507 using-nx-skills SKILL.md + 5,278 session_start_hook.py + 32
`nx hook session-start`).
CONFOUNDED three ways -- proximity, context length, and the absence of a
competing restriction in a subagent prompt. Volume is ONE of four candidate
causes and the cheapest to test. Do not present it as the fix.
nx_answer is 2/2: near-zero on BOTH sides, so its defect is NOT the channel.

=== DIRECTION REJECTED, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED ===
"A hook that detects the prompt-layer conflict and prints it" is NOT
IMPLEMENTABLE. A hook cannot read the session system prompt:
 - documented payload is session_id / transcript_path / cwd / permission_mode /
   hook_event_name (+ tool_name, tool_input, tool_result, user_prompt, reason).
   No system prompt.
 - the transcript does not carry it either. Record types present: attachment,
   assistant, user, ai-title, agent-name, last-prompt, mode, queue-operation,
   pr-link, system/stop_hook_summary, system/turn_duration, file-history-*.
   No systemPrompt / appendSystemPrompt key in any of 494 files.
 - all 4 hits for "Do not call the AgentTool" in the evidence transcript are the
   AGENT QUOTING IT in prose. Self-report, not machine-readable state.
REPLACEMENT: you cannot DETECT the conflict; you can make it MOOT. A hook's
permissionDecisionReason / additionalContext is not a prompt -- it is a runtime
message delivered AFTER the model decided to act, so no prompt line preempts it.
That is the only mechanism here that structurally outranks a system-prompt line,
and it is proven (RDR-184's shared-tree git-write block has held).
SHARP LIMIT: PreToolUse fires only on a tool actually CALLED, so it can never
prompt a dispatch that does not happen. Decision-time authorization must ride on
a trigger the agent does reach (the git push) -- which is nexus-4av2n item (b).
This epic DEPENDS ON 4av2n and does not duplicate it.

=== THE DORMANCY ANSWER: THREE DELIVERY TIERS, NOT ONE ===
 TIER A  PyPI (`nx <verb>`). `nx upgrade --auto` is hooks.json SessionStart entry
         #1, so a wheel change is live at the NEXT SESSION. No plugin release.
 TIER B  an EXISTING hooks.json entry whose command is a PyPI binary. Two are
         already wired: `nx hook session-start`, `nx-session-end-launcher`. The
         ENTRY is pinned; the BEHAVIOUR ships with the wheel. Live next session.
 TIER C  a NEW hooks.json entry, or any conexus/ script/skill/agent change.
         Fully dormant until the next plugin release; MUST be declared in
         conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md (11 entries currently pending vs pinned
         v6.18.1; ledger test-enforced by tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py,
         and it records a real incident where three merged guards protected
         nothing for a whole window).

WHAT HOLDS THE LINE DURING THE DORMANCY WINDOW: phase 1 (.1 .2 .3) is entirely
Tier A + Tier B. It is not IN the window. Child .4 then removes the window for
all FUTURE guidance edits by re-plumbing the imperative from Tier C to Tier B --
one dormant change that permanently converts guidance iteration from
release-cadence to session-cadence.

=== CI COST (directive, stated deliberately) ===
NO new CI job, NO new gate, NO scheduled workflow anywhere in this epic. The
census is an offline command over local files. Total CI delta is unit-test files
for pure parser functions -- fast, no substrate, no network. Any child that later
wants a CI gate must justify it separately; this epic declines to add one.

=== WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SOLVE ===
It does not stop a session prompt from restricting dispatch. It does not make any
capability mandatory. It does not close nexus-4av2n / nexus-qc4p1 / nexus-nu7fo.
It makes non-use VISIBLE and makes guidance ITERABLE. Mechanism (deny-at-
decision-time) stays owned by 4av2n where it already lives.

=== HOW THIS DESIGN IS FALSIFIED ===
Baselines: nx_answer 4 lifetime; Serena 13% of sessions; Skill 61% (69.5% of
substantial); SessionStart 12,817 bytes.
 (i) After .3 + .4 ship, Skill share of substantial sessions must exceed 69.5%
     and Serena must exceed 15.9%. If they do not move, the volume/salience
     hypothesis is DEAD and only Tier-C mechanism remains. Say so; do not re-cut.
 (ii) nx_answer will NOT move on guidance alone. If it does, the latency-
     rationality reading in .6 was wrong.
Stating (ii) as a prediction rather than a hedge is what makes this falsifiable.

=== SCOPE CAVEAT ===
All numbers are from ONE project directory on ONE machine (Hal's). They are a
baseline for this repo, not a general claim about the plugin's users.

FAMILY (do not close or modify from this epic): nexus-3sij7 (evidence),
nexus-4av2n (stacked-reviewer gate never blocks), nexus-qc4p1 (EXPECT rows),
nexus-nu7fo (dispatch recognizer unfalsifiable, 0/6 0/10 0/7 0/N).
notes: CLOSE FRAMING (2026-08-20): the original failure class — a session silently declining to dispatch specialists — is MEASURED, NOT PREVENTED. Deliberate scope: continuous measurement (nx census capability + per-session capability_census.jsonl), honest guidance (narrowed mandates, measured costs, imperative-first 4,428B SessionStart), tool-side rationality defects fixed (.6). PREVENTION lives in the mechanization bead nexus-4av2n — CLOSED + ACTIVATED at the v7.3.0 pin (close-gate + push-gate live), so the standing 'must not displace' constraint is satisfied, not just noted. OUTSTANDING BY DESIGN: .5's pre-registered prediction (Skill >71.1% / Serena >47.4% substantial-share, post-2026-08-20 sessions; reopen .5 as hypothesis-falsified if flat) and .6's prediction (guidance-only changes do NOT move nx_answer; re-base denominator on narrowed shapes).

Full framing + outstanding pre-registered predictions recorded in the bead NOTES (measured-not-prevented; prevention shipped separately and is live). Reviews for the final two children: T2 [22941].

title: plugin tool guidance is silently overridden by session-prompt restrictions — measured snapshot: zero Skill, zero nx_answer, zero search/query, zero Serena, one nx MCP call (plan_audit); full session later reached Skill=1, nx MCP=4
description:
MEASURED FROM A REAL SESSION, 2026-07-31 (session 75695009). Hal: "we've lost almost any
use of our tools and cannot leverage them effectively."  This bead is the measurement, not
the impression.

WHAT THE SESSION ACTUALLY USED over many hours of catalog P0 work:
  bd, memory_put (mostly BY SUBAGENTS, not the orchestrator), raw Bash/Read/Grep/Edit,
  and the expectations shell lib.

WHAT IT NEVER INVOKED ONCE:
  - ANY Skill. Not /conexus:debug when a Java test failed. Not /conexus:deep-analysis.
    Not /conexus:review-code. Not /conexus:brainstorming-gate before implementing.
  - nx_answer, search, query, plan_search -- despite the SessionStart hook stating that
    ALL analytical questions route through nx_answer, and that T3/T2 are checked BEFORE
    researching from scratch. Every analytical question in the session was answered by
    hand-rolled grep.
  - Serena symbol tools. A change set altering identity/uniqueness semantics across
    ~1170 lines was reviewed with grep, while CLAUDE.md says explicitly to run
    find_referencing_symbols BEFORE any signature change.
  - The debugger and deep-analyst agents were spawned ONLY after Hal intervened. Within
    one dispatch the deep-analyst found a P0 (nexus-upg3s, silent owner-field overwrite)
    that the orchestrator was about to merge on the strength of a green suite.

THE MECHANISM -- a PROMPT-LAYER CONFLICT that resolves silently toward doing nothing.

This session's system prompt carried:
    "Do not call the AgentTool unless the user requested it"
    "Do not use workflows or deep-research unless the user requested it"
CLAUDE.md carried the opposite for the stacked reviewers ("STANDING AUTHORIZATION -- this
line IS the request... permanently"). The using-nx-skills SessionStart hook carried "you
MUST invoke Skill for any matching skill BEFORE producing any other response."

Three layers, two directions. The agent resolved the conflict conservatively EVERY TIME,
and never surfaced that it was doing so. Nothing errored; the capability simply went
unused, which is indistinguishable from the capability not existing.

THIS IS NOT NEW -- IT IS nexus-4av2n's DOCUMENTED FAILURE, RECURRING. That bead already
records: "a CLAUDE.md line cannot be relied on to outrank a system prompt." The note was
in the orchestrator's context for the entire session and did not change the outcome. A
guidance fix that has now failed twice, with the diagnosis already written down, is not a
guidance problem. It is a mechanism problem.

CONTRIBUTING FACTOR, worth separating: SessionStart emits ~12KB across several hooks --
skill routing tables, plugin inventory, bd prime, T2 listing, capability lists. At that
volume the block reads as boilerplate, and the single genuinely imperative sentence sits
buried inside it. High volume is not high salience; it may be the opposite.

WHAT TO CONSIDER (not a decided design -- this bead is the evidence, the fix needs a call):
 1. Make the conflict IMPOSSIBLE rather than adjudicated. If a standing authorization
    exists, it belongs somewhere the session prompt cannot contradict -- or the hook must
    detect the contradiction and say so out loud at session start, rather than leaving a
    silent resolution.
 2. Make non-use OBSERVABLE. Zero Skill invocations and zero nx_answer calls across a
    multi-hour session is a measurable signal. A SessionEnd/Stop hook could report the
    census the way expectations_census reports dispatch declarations -- silence today
    looks identical to "no skill applied."
 3. Cut SessionStart volume hard, and put the imperative FIRST and ALONE. Inventory can be
    fetched on demand; the directive cannot.
 4. Trigger on EVENTS rather than on session start. "A test failed" is the moment to
    surface /conexus:debug -- not 12KB at boot, hours earlier, before any failure exists.

RELATED: nexus-4av2n (mechanize the stacked-reviewer gate; hook never blocks and does not
gate push), nexus-qc4p1 (the same class for EXPECT rows -- mechanized because remembering
did not work), nexus-nu7fo (the ledger cannot even MEASURE dispatches, so non-use is
currently unfalsifiable).

title: [test-infra] atexit-only teardown leaks substrate postmasters that squat Docker's ephemeral ports — a Python test leak silently fails the JAVA engine suite
description:
Root-caused 2026-07-31 by a debugger agent, then independently re-verified. Full analysis:
T2 [21315] nexus/cascade-test-container-failure-diagnosis-2026-07-31.

SYMPTOM. A Java engine-suite class fails at container bring-up with
  PSQLException: FATAL: role "postgres" does not exist
after burning ~124s, while every other class in the same run passes. Looks like a flaky
testcontainers start. It is not.

MECHANISM, and it is cross-language -- a PYTHON test leak breaks the JAVA suite.

 1. tests/_engine_substrate.py::_free_port() picks a port with bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)),
    drawing from the SAME ephemeral range Docker publishes container ports into.
 2. That PG is started with listen_addresses = '127.0.0.1' -- a SPECIFIC bind.
 3. Teardown is atexit.register(_teardown) ONLY. atexit does not run on SIGKILL, OOM, or a
    hard-killed pytest, so the postmaster survives its parent and reparents to PID 1.
 4. Docker Desktop publishes container ports WILDCARD (0.0.0.0 + [::]). Binding 0.0.0.0:P
    while 127.0.0.1:P is already held does NOT error.
 5. BSD/macOS routes an inbound connection to the MOST SPECIFIC bound socket. A
    testcontainers client dialling localhost:P therefore reaches THE ORPHAN, never the
    container. The container is healthy and simply unreachable.
 6. The orphan was initdb --auth=trust with superuser = $USER, so it has no `postgres`
    role. Testcontainers connects as `postgres` and gets a clean FATAL at the auth
    handshake -- which reads exactly like a broken container.

PROOF. Reproduced 16 minutes after the failure, container long destroyed:
  psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 64270 -U postgres -d postgres -c "select 1"
  FATAL: role "postgres" does not exist
and lsof shows: postgres 95728 ... TCP 127.0.0.1:64270 (LISTEN), PPID=1, started Jul 26 --
five days before the failure, holding the exact port testcontainers had published on.

SCALE. TEN orphaned postmasters live on this box right now, PPID=1, spanning
engine-service-v0.1.56 through v0.1.59, Jul 26 -> Jul 31. At 10 squatters over the ~16k
ephemeral range that is ~0.06% per container, and a full engine suite starts ~110
containers -> roughly 6% chance of one collision PER SUITE RUN. That matches the observed
"exactly one class of 100+". THE PROBABILITY GROWS MONOTONICALLY as more leak, so this
gets worse on its own.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, with evidence -- so nobody re-derives it:
 - NOT an initdb race. The container reported started in 3.97s via a LogMessageWaitStrategy
   requiring the ready-line twice; and during initdb the entrypoint's temp server sets
   listen_addresses='' (unix socket only), so a TCP client cannot reach it to GET a role
   error. The 124.6s is 3.97s startup + a 120s connect-retry loop of identical deterministic
   refusals.
 - NOT the recorded Docker port-forwarding wedge (project_docker_port_forwarding_wedges).
   That signature is a HANG, host psql rc=124. Here the client got an immediate well-formed
   FATAL. Forwarding was not wedged, it was BYPASSED. Sibling failure mode, different fix --
   restarting Docker does NOTHING here, because the squatter is a host process.
 - NOT caused by the branch under test (nexus-0ehwe arbiter work, 6b6f1ed5). The failure is
   the first statement of @BeforeAll, in readStartupMessages, before Liquibase and before any
   SQL is parsed. That branch touches no changelog and no role bootstrap, and the squatter
   predates it by five days.

THE FIX (two parts, and the second is the durable one):
 a. Reap the 10 live orphans. They are host processes; Docker restart will not clear them.
 b. Make tests/_engine_substrate.py CRASH-DURABLE: atexit is not a teardown mechanism. Write
    a PID/port sidecar next to the pgdata dir and sweep stale
    $TMPDIR/nexus_t2_substrate_pg_* clusters at session start. Consider binding the
    substrate outside Docker's ephemeral range so a leak cannot collide even if one escapes.
 c. Optional hardening: make the Java suite fail FAST and LOUD on a foreign server (assert
    the connected server's identity, or shrink withConnectTimeoutSeconds) so this stops
    presenting as a 120-second product bug.

RELATED: same FAMILY as T3 analysis-deep-orphan-resource-leak-nexus-t2-2026-06-05
(detached test daemons reparented to launchd, reaper blind), different instance. NEW and
previously unrecorded: the cross-language blast radius, a leaked Python-suite PG silently
corrupting the Java engine suite through Docker host-port allocation.

NOT VERIFIED: no direct capture of the simultaneous double-bind at failure time (container
was gone); which pytest run leaked PID 95728 (no per-run provenance); Docker Desktop's
actual port-allocation policy, so the ~6% figure assumes uniform allocation.
close_reason: Fix (b) landed as b3c56373, CI green. Crash-durable teardown: atomic PID/port sidecar per cluster; session-start sweep with verify-ALL-legs-before-killing-ANY (mismatch refuses the whole cluster), engine-first killpg then pg_ctl -m immediate, owner staleness = dead OR pid-reused-different-cmdline; legacy sidecar-less strays named loudly never auto-killed; ports moved to 20000-29000 (below Docker's publish range — an escaped pair can no longer intercept container traffic) sharded per xdist worker against the probe-vs-bind race. Fix (a) was Hal's 07-31 manual reap. 35 sweeper tests, key ones falsified red/green; reviews [21524] FIX-FIRST->clean, critique [21526] 3 rounds to JUSTIFIED. Residuals beaded: soqa8 (Java fail-fast, in flight), kk63b (pg_ctl start window), ucfky (doctor visibility for the 7 legacy squatters still on this box — manual reap still owed for those).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
EXTENSION, found while verifying the diagnosis before reaping: THE LEAK IS A PAIR, not a
single process, and the bead's remediation must account for both.

Alongside the 10 orphaned postmasters there are FIVE orphaned ENGINE processes (java -jar
nexus-service-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar), all PPID=1, each pid-adjacent to a postmaster and started
at the IDENTICAL second:

  48472 <-> 48461   Wed Jul 29 05:45:16
  50138 <-> 50127   Wed Jul 29 04:56:03
  53125 <-> 53114   Wed Jul 29 04:40:46
  58648 <-> 58637   Wed Jul 29 05:46:52
  83962 <-> 83951   Fri Jul 31 02:21:30

_boot() starts a PG and then a service JAR; both are registered only with
atexit.register(_teardown), so a hard-killed pytest strands BOTH.

CONSEQUENCE THE ORIGINAL WRITE-UP MISSED: the engine also holds a port (NX_SERVICE_PORT,
picked by the same _free_port()), so each leak squats TWO ephemeral ports, not one. That
roughly DOUBLES the collision probability per leak -- the ~6%-per-suite estimate is
therefore a floor, not a ceiling.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS AN ANOMALY worth recording, because it looks alarming and is not. Several
orphaned postmasters show client backends with timestamps from MINUTES ago
("nexus_svc nexus_t2_substrate 127.0.0.1(50781) idle"). That is not a current test run
connecting to a stale substrate -- it is the orphaned ENGINE's connection pool recycling
against its own orphaned PG. Both halves are alive and talking to each other, days after
the pytest that created them exited. Checked specifically because if current runs WERE
reaching a five-day-old PG, every green result today would be suspect. They are not: every
orphan predates the session that found this.

So the reaper in fix (b) must sweep the JAR process too, not just the postmaster, or half
the leak survives and keeps holding its port.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REAPED 2026-07-31, fix (a) of this bead's remediation. Fix (b), the durable one, is NOT
done -- this bead stays OPEN for it.

Killed 5 orphaned engine JARs (SIGTERM) then 10 orphaned postmasters (SIGINT, fast
shutdown), engines first so their pool connections closed before the servers went. Each PID
was re-matched against its expected command line immediately before signalling, so PID
reuse could not redirect a kill at an unrelated process. Verified after: 0 orphaned engines,
0 orphaned postmasters, and 127.0.0.1:64270 -- the port that caused the failure -- is free.

Every reaped process had PPID=1 and a start time predating the session that found them, so
none belonged to in-flight work.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. It clears the accumulated landmine field and drops the
per-suite collision probability back to ~0. It changes NOTHING about the cause: the next
hard-killed pytest leaks another pair, and the field regrows. Until _engine_substrate.py has
a crash-durable teardown, this reap is a treatment, not a cure, and anyone reading a green
suite after today should know the reap is why.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED END-TO-END by the post-reap suite run, 2026-07-31.

Same branch, same commit, same code -- the ONLY change was reaping the orphaned
substrate pairs:

                (FATAL: role "postgres" does not exist)
  AFTER reap:   CatalogDocumentCascadeTest -- Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0,
                Time elapsed: 5.783 s

That is the controlled experiment the isolation run could not provide. An isolation run
proves only that a different port was drawn; this shows the SAME class, in the SAME
full-suite position, flipping from a 124-second deterministic failure to a 5.8-second pass
once the squatters are gone. The 124.6s -> 5.8s delta is itself the signature: the old
number was 3.97s of container startup plus a 120s connect-retry loop against a server that
was never going to accept the credentials.

This also closes out the alternative hypotheses for the record: nothing about the branch,
the test, or Docker changed between the two runs.

Still OPEN for the durable fix. The reap is a treatment; atexit-only teardown remains, so
the next hard-killed pytest starts the field regrowing.

title: engine: seedRootToken ON CONFLICT(token_hash) ignores idx_service_tokens_single_root — rotating NX_SERVICE_TOKEN raises an unhandled 23505 on the auth bootstrap path
description:
FIFTH instance of the nexus-0ehwe ON CONFLICT arbiter class, found 2026-07-31 by the
same whole-changelog enumeration that produced nexus-q2ign. This one is on the AUTH
BOOTSTRAP path, which is why it is filed separately and at higher priority.

## The instance

`nexus.service_tokens` has TWO CALLER-determined unique keys:

  1. `service_tokens_pk` PRIMARY KEY (token_hash)          service-tokens-001-baseline.xml:85
  2. `idx_service_tokens_single_root`
     UNIQUE (label) WHERE label = 'bootstrap-legacy-token'  service-tokens-002-single-root-index.xml:31

`TokenStore.seedRootToken` (TokenStore.java:~190-197) inserts
`(sha256(rawToken), tenantId, ROOT_TOKEN_LABEL, SCOPE_ROOT)` and arbitrates on
`SERVICE_TOKENS.TOKEN_HASH` ONLY:

```java
.values(hash, tenantId, ROOT_TOKEN_LABEL, SCOPE_ROOT)
.onConflict(SERVICE_TOKENS.TOKEN_HASH)
.doNothing()
```

`ROOT_TOKEN_LABEL` is `"bootstrap-legacy-token"` (TokenStore.java:172) — literally the
value in the partial index's predicate.

## Why it fires, and why the DDL predicted it

A ROTATED `NX_SERVICE_TOKEN` has a DIFFERENT `token_hash` but the SAME `label`. So the
arbiter does not match, the DO NOTHING arm never engages, and
`idx_service_tokens_single_root` raises a raw 23505.

The index's own changeset comment describes exactly this scenario as the thing it exists
to catch:

    "Partial unique index pinning at most one ROOT_TOKEN_LABEL row, so the
     'operator = the single root token' model cannot be silently violated by
     a second root-labelled insert (e.g. a rotated NX_SERVICE_TOKEN re-seed)."

So — same shape as nexus-z3ssg — the guard was designed for a case the insert beside it
structurally cannot handle. The result is not a silent violation (the index does its job)
but an unhandled integrity error on the seed path.

## Severity: this is a boot-path failure, not a data-path one

`seedRootToken` runs during service bootstrap. An operator who rotates
`NX_SERVICE_TOKEN` and restarts gets an opaque integrity-constraint failure on the auth
seed rather than either (a) the new token being accepted or (b) a clear "a root token
already exists; revoke it first" refusal. Neither outcome is currently reachable.

NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME. This is read from source + DDL; I did not stand up a service and
rotate a root token, and the exact blast radius (does bootstrap abort, or is the throw
swallowed upstream?) depends on `seedRootToken`'s caller, which I did not trace. That
tracing is the first step of the fix, and the claim above should be confirmed before the
severity is trusted.

## Suggested fix

Decide ONE meaning of "the root token already exists" — almost certainly: resolve by
LABEL first, and either converge (same token re-seeded) or refuse by name ("a root token
already exists under a different hash; revoke before re-seeding"). Reuse
`dev.nexus.service.db.SqlConstraints` for the constraint-name branch. Also settle whether
a rotated root token SHOULD replace the incumbent — that is a security decision, not a
mechanical one, and should not be answered by whichever branch is easier to write.

## Also noted, NOT filed separately (low severity)

`session_tokens`: PK `(session_token_hash)` + `session_tokens_tenant_session_uq
(tenant_id, session_id)`. `TokenStore:534` arbitrates the uq, so it is exposed to the PK.
A `session_token_hash` collision means the same random token was minted twice —
effectively unreachable. Mentioned so a future audit does not have to re-derive that it
was considered and dismissed, and dismissed for a REASON.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-07-31, commit 15dd7799 on develop (merged, NOT yet pushed pending the combined
engine suite).

SEVERITY WAS UNDER-RATED, and the bead said so: it was filed P1 with the blast radius
explicitly PROVISIONAL pending a trace of the caller. The trace was done and it is WORSE
than advertised, not better:

  - The method is `ensureBootstrapToken`, not `seedRootToken` (that symbol does not exist).
  - Main.java's only try/catch spans the Liquibase migration (:82-:84); the call at :100 was
    inside NO try, and `main` declares `throws Exception`.
  - So the unhandled 23505 propagated out of main: JVM exits non-zero, HTTP never binds,
    bare stack trace. Boot HARD-ABORTS on the auth bootstrap path.
  - It is not self-healing: the index predicate carries no revoked_at term, so revoking the
    incumbent does not free the slot, and NX_SERVICE_TOKEN stays rotated across restarts —
    it recurs on every boot until someone edits the database by hand.
  - The two anticipated startup failures beside it (Liquibase, PoolerModeCheck) both
    log.error + exit(1). This was the only one of the three whose failure was
    un-diagnosable.

THE MECHANISM. ensureBootstrapToken arbitrated ON CONFLICT (token_hash) DO NOTHING — the
PK — while the table also carries idx_service_tokens_single_root, a partial unique index on
(label) WHERE label = 'bootstrap-legacy-token'. A rotated token has a NEW hash and the SAME
label, so the arbiter missed entirely and the label index fired. Textbook nexus-0ehwe
arbiter class: a predicate naming one key on a table that has more than one.

THE FIX resolves by LABEL first, then decides — prevent-rather-than-catch, needing no
constraint-name extraction, so it does NOT depend on the arbiter branch's SqlConstraints:

  no incumbent            insert (unchanged)
  same hash               no-op, the common path
  different hash, live    ROTATE: replace in place via compare-and-swap, log an audit event
  different hash, revoked REFUSE with a typed BootstrapTokenConflict naming the remedy

THE SECURITY DECISION, made deliberately and stated so it can be reversed. This bead said
the replace-vs-refuse question "is a security decision, not a mechanical one, and should
not be answered by whichever branch is easier to write". ROTATION REPLACES, because
rotation exists to invalidate the old credential: had the previous hash kept working, a
"rotated" compromised token would still authenticate — silently, which is a worse outcome
than the crash being fixed. NX_SERVICE_TOKEN is the source of truth and the row is its
binding; an operator who changes the env and restarts has stated their intent and already
controls the service either way. A REVOKED incumbent is the one case deliberately left
unresolved, because both silent options are wrong (resurrecting overrides a deliberate
revocation; rotating onto it mints a root token that authenticates nothing).

Main now reports failures here like the two checks above it: logged error naming the
remedy, then exit(1).

VERIFICATION. Six pins in a DEDICATED container — the root slot is GLOBALLY unique (the
index has no tenant_id), so sharing TokenScopeResolutionTest's container would couple the
assertions to whichever test seeded the slot first. 6/6 green.
FALSIFIED by forcing the old always-insert path: reproduces the exact defect,
`duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_service_tokens_single_root"` on the
`on conflict ("token_hash") do nothing` statement, breaking 4 of the 6. The failing cause
was READ, not merely observed to be red.

ALSO NOTED, still true and NOT fixed here (was already recorded on this bead as considered
and dismissed with a reason): session_tokens' PK/uq pair is exposed the same way, but a
session_token_hash collision means the same random token was minted twice — effectively
unreachable.

REACHES NOBODY UNTIL AN ENGINE TAG + DEPLOY. This is engine-side; Hal relays that.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my closing comment, same day. I claimed more verification than I have, and
Hal asked the right question ("did we actually fix kjjab?").

WHAT IS PROVEN: the arbiter defect in TokenStore.ensureBootstrapToken. Rotation no longer
throws; falsified by forcing the old always-insert path, which reproduces
`duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_service_tokens_single_root"` and
breaks 4 of the 6 pins. That half is solid, and it is the half that caused the reported
symptom — boot aborted BECAUSE the insert threw, so removing the throw removes the abort.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: the Main.java half. NO TEST REACHES Main's STARTUP PATH AT ALL.
ServiceIntegrationTest constructs `new NexusService(0, TOKEN, svcDs)` directly
(ServiceIntegrationTest.java:65) and never calls Main.main, so the root-token seeding
call, my try/catch, the log.error lines and the exit(1) are executed by ZERO tests.

My six pins assert BootstrapTokenConflict at the TOKENSTORE layer
(BootstrapTokenRotationTest.java:181). That proves TokenStore THROWS it. It does not prove
Main CATCHES it, that the catch ordering is right, or that the process exits 1 with the
message rather than a bare stack trace. This is exactly the recorded layer-test trap: a
test below the layer production uses proves the LAYER, not the FEATURE. I wrote pins one
layer beneath the thing that actually broke.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated honestly rather than talked down: LOW but not zero. The paths that
now reach Main's handler are the ones this fix INTRODUCED (revoked incumbent, lost CAS).
If that handler is wrong, those degrade back to a bare stack trace — the original
un-diagnosable shape, on a rarer trigger. Nothing regresses to the pre-fix behaviour.

The bead stays CLOSED because the defect it describes is fixed. The missing coverage is
filed separately rather than left implied.

title: [catalog] chash_remap is excluded from COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES and the re-home/emptiness halves want opposite answers
description:
Found in the stacked review of the nexus-v6za0 attempt-3 fix (2026-07-31). The two
reviewers DISAGREED about this table and the disagreement is the finding.

nexus.chash_remap carries source_collection AND target_collection, and it is NOT in
COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES. Whether it belongs there has no single answer, because the
two consumers of that list want OPPOSITE treatment:

RE-HOME half says INCLUDE. The table is read live, keyed on the collection name:
RemapRepository.entriesForCollection / count / membership / clearLeg / sourceCollections
all filter on SOURCE_COLLECTION. After a rename X->Y with no re-home, every one of those
lookups keyed on Y returns nothing. The remap ledger silently detaches.

EMPTINESS half says EXCLUDE, for two independent reasons:
  1. source_collection is inside the PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, source_collection, old_id).
     Re-homing rewrites a PK, and collides with 23505 if the target already holds the
     same old_id -- turning a rename into an aborted transaction.
  2. It is an RF-186-1 raw-fact ledger, i.e. a PERMANENT historical record. Rows about a
     past migration never age out, so a collection that was ever a migration source would
     read NON-EMPTY forever and could never be revived by a legitimate undo rename.

So this is not a missing-entry bug to patch. It is the first real case where the
EQUALITY invariant on COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES (re-home set == emptiness set) is
argued against by the domain, and it needs a decision:

  (a) include it, accept PK rewrite + permanent undo blocking;
  (b) exclude it, accept that rename detaches the remap ledger (file the detach as its
      own bug);
  (c) SPLIT the list into a re-home set and an emptiness set, with the difference
      explicitly enumerated and a test asserting the difference is exactly the
      documented one -- which preserves the anti-drift property that made the shared
      list worth having, instead of abandoning it.

(c) looks right but it weakens the invariant that just took three attempts to establish,
so it should be decided deliberately and not inside a P0 fix. NOT ACTED ON in the
attempt-3 commit; the table is documented there as a deliberate exclusion with these
reasons, per the class's own principle that exclusions must be visible.
close_reason: Closed

title: COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES is equal-by-construction to the re-home set but nothing cross-checks it against the SCHEMA — a new denorm-collection table can be missing from both consistently
description:
Found while fixing nexus-v6za0 attempt 3, 2026-07-31. The honest limitation of that fix.

COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES in CatalogRepository now drives BOTH renameCollectionTxn step 2's
re-home loop AND collectionIsEmpty. That makes the two sets EQUAL BY CONSTRUCTION — the
drift that caused the merge (re-home covered 17 tables, the emptiness check covered 5) is
no longer expressible, in either direction.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROTECT: a denorm-collection table that is missing from the list ENTIRELY.
Adding a new table with a `collection` column and forgetting to register it leaves it
un-re-homed AND invisible to the emptiness check simultaneously — consistent, and wrong.
No test can catch that today, because both consumers agree.

WHY NO EXISTING MECHANISM COVERS IT: the list is a Java literal; the schema is Liquibase.
Nothing cross-checks them. This is the same shape as nexus-mijr4 one level down — that bead
is about two PREDICATES agreeing; this is about the list agreeing with the SCHEMA.

PROPOSED: a test that introspects information_schema for every table in the nexus schema
carrying a column named `collection` / `source_collection` / `physical_collection`, and
asserts the set equals COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES' membership. Deliberate exclusions become
a named allowlist WITH a reason, so an exclusion is visible rather than implicit — and per
the standing lesson, that allowlist needs a LIVENESS check too, or it silently grants
permission to whatever lands there next.

NOTE ON WHERE IT SHOULD LIVE: service-ci is NOT a required check on develop or main
(nexus-hq9na), so a Java-only version of this gate would be advisory at merge. A Python
test that reads the Liquibase changelogs and greps the Java literal would ride
`pytest (Python 3.12)`, which IS required — the same reasoning as the nexus-mijr4 design
memo.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1. The severity in the original description undersold this: it was
written as a FUTURE risk ("nothing cross-checks the list against the schema"). It is a
REALIZED defect, and was already realized on the day the bead was filed.

Evidence, from the stacked review of the attempt-3 fix (2026-07-31). BOTH reviewers
independently found that COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES omitted nexus.gc_audit:

  - gc_audit was added 2026-07-30 (catalog-018-gc-audit.xml, nexus-jqvzk), ONE DAY before
    the attempt-3 fix was written.
  - It carries a denormalized `collection TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` with a purpose-built
    index idx_gc_audit_collection (tenant_id, collection, id DESC).
  - GC_AUDIT is a fully wired jOOQ table written at CatalogRepository.java:4338 -- so this
    was a plain omission, not a codegen gap.
  - It is the newest member of the SAME audit-table family (relevance_log,
    search_telemetry, hook_failures) that the very same diff re-homes explicitly.

That is the exact defect class the shared list was introduced to make unexpressible,
recurring one layer down, within 24 hours, caught only because two humans-in-the-loop
reviewers read the schema by hand. The list is equal-by-construction to ITSELF; nothing
ties it to the schema, so a new table is invisible to it by default.

A second omission (nexus.chash_remap) was found in the same pass, but that one is a
genuine design question rather than a miss -- see nexus-4nll0.

WHERE THE GATE MUST LIVE -- this is the load-bearing half. service-ci is NOT a required
check on develop or main (nexus-hq9na, re-verified against the GitHub API during this
review). A Java-only test would be ADVISORY at merge, which for a three-times-recurring
P0 class is not a gate at all. The test must ride `pytest (Python 3.12)`, which IS
required: read the Liquibase changelogs for every table carrying a
collection / source_collection / physical_collection column, parse the
COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES literal out of the Java source, and assert set equality.
Precedent for parsing Java from Python already exists in
tests/catalog/test_fake_catalog_handler_route_census.py.

Deliberate exclusions become a NAMED allowlist WITH a reason (currently pdf_pipeline --
transient work queue; chash_remap -- see nexus-4nll0). Per the standing lesson, the
allowlist itself needs a liveness check, or it silently grants permission to whatever
lands there next.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
BUILT and pushed 2026-07-31 (9e89bdb4, corrected by 612ed9f1 and 34ab012b).
Gate: tests/catalog/test_collection_scoped_tables_schema_parity.py

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT, not a synthetic mutation. On the tree before the
gc_audit fix it failed with exactly [('gc_audit', 'collection')]; after, 5/5 green. The
full-suite delta 11562 -> 11567 confirms all five ran rather than skipped.

IMPLEMENTATION DIFFERS FROM THE PROPOSAL, deliberately. This bead proposed introspecting
information_schema (Java-shaped) and my own follow-up comment proposed parsing the
Liquibase changelogs from Python. Neither is what shipped, and the reason matters:

  - A changelog parser would be a PROXY FOR THE SCHEMA -- the fourth proxy in an arc
    whose every bug was a proxy. It would also be wrong TODAY: gc_audit's column is
    declared inside a raw <sql> block rather than a <column name=...> attribute, so an
    attribute scanner reports it absent.
  - A Java test would be ADVISORY, since service-ci was not a required check.

So it queries information_schema from PYTEST, via the engine substrate (ensure_engine
boots a real PG and the engine applies every changelog). Exact AND on a required check.
Placement verified rather than assumed: ci.yml:144 sets NX_T2_SUBSTRATE_EXPECTED=1 in the
required pytest job, which disarms the substrate skip leg and re-arms fail-loud, so the
gate cannot silently stop running.

WHAT IT ASSERTS: parity in both directions (an unregistered collection column fails; a
registered column absent from the schema fails), a liveness check on the exclusion
allowlist (a dead exclusion silently pre-approves whatever takes that name next), a
count-key/table agreement check, and a parser non-vacuity floor so a refactor that breaks
the regex fails loudly instead of passing on an empty set.

HONEST RESIDUAL, stated in the file rather than glossed. The gate asks Postgres what
columns EXIST -- ground truth -- but which of them COUNT is still decided by
LIKE '%collection%'. So it does not see a scalar column holding a collection name without
"collection" in its name, a name nested in JSONB, or a reference through an id. The first
class is the dangerous one because it looks exactly like what the gate does catch; closing
it needs a value-shaped check rather than a name-shaped one. My first draft enumerated
three column names and immediately reproduced the very defect class the gate exists to
catch (it could not see chash_remap.target_collection) -- which is why the residual is now
written down instead of claimed away.

FOUND A SECOND GAP ON ITS FIRST RUN: migration_jobs' JSONB collection set and derived
idempotency key, which a scalar UPDATE cannot rewrite -- filed as nexus-rvr1n with
PROVISIONAL severity, because I did not trace the job runner's resolution path.

Related: nexus-hq9na (service-ci advisory) is now acted on -- service-ci was restructured
to report on every PR so it CAN be required (5ae42cbd). The branch-protection flip itself
is deliberately NOT done in that commit; it must follow an observed skip-report or it
wedges every non-service PR.

title: expectations_test.sh (62 assertions on the RDR-184 ledger shellib) is run by NO gate — ambient-only, so lib semantics can drift green
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-31 while implementing nexus-qc4p1.

tests/e2e/lib/expectations_test.sh is a 624-line, 62-assertion unit suite for the
expectations shellib — the RDR-184 Gap-1 ledger that the SubagentStop guard, the
census, and the declaration audit all read. Its own header says 'Run directly:
bash tests/e2e/lib/expectations_test.sh'.

Nothing runs it. Grepped the whole tree: the only references to the file are its
own header lines and a bead-interaction record. No pytest wrapper, no CI job, no
e2e runner step. So the documented way to validate a change to that lib is a
command a human has to remember — which is the 'gates scripted, not ambient'
class exactly.

WHY IT MATTERS CONCRETELY. nexus-qc4p1 rewrote the recognisers inside
expectations_undeclared and expectations_census (agent_type keying + N-of-type
credit matching). Those 62 assertions are the only unit-level coverage of the
awk. They pass — I ran them by hand — but a future edit that breaks them is
invisible to CI. The qc4p1 change added pytest coverage of the NEW semantics via
tests/hooks/test_agent_dispatch_expect.py (which shells out to the real scripts),
so CI is not blind to the lib entirely; it is blind to the 62 pre-existing
assertions.

SUGGESTED FIX: a thin pytest wrapper under tests/hooks/ that subprocess-runs the
shell suite and asserts rc==0 plus a non-vacuity floor on the reported pass count
(the suite prints 'expectations_test.sh: N passed, M failed'), so a suite that
silently stops running its own tests fails instead of reporting zero failures.

RELATED: nexus-qc4p1, nexus-nu7fo, nexus-mk3tw.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: PROMOTED P2 -> P1 2026-08-09. This bead was filed 07-31 as a theoretical drift risk ('lib semantics can drift green'). It is no longer theoretical — it is now the ROOT ENABLER of a two-day blind window on the exact machinery it guards, with a documented chain: (1) nexus-a4nun (08-07): expectations_test.sh had 2 known failures on develop HEAD — un-gated, so nothing blocked on them; (2) round 2 of nexus-7z7rj (08-08) added an unguarded $NX_EXPECT_LOCK_HOLD_DELAY_S dereference, and since that script runs , the suite began ABORTING AT TEST 4 — turning those 2 failures from un-gated into UNREACHABLE and taking Tests 4-15 dark; (3) BECAUSE NO GATE RUNS THIS SUITE (this bead), an rc=1 abort sat unnoticed for two days — during an active multi-round fix effort on that very shellib; (4) when round 3 restored the suite (commit 6ae85883), it immediately caught a real defect in round 3's own change. So the absence of this gate is a direct contributing cause of why nexus-7z7rj shipped 'fixed' twice while its own validation harness was silently truncated. THE SHAPE: this is the same vacuous-verification class as the code defects swept in T2 [22088] and fixed in nexus-hdumg / nexus-v2mdd — a green that means 'nothing was checked' — but one level up, at the harness. FIX VALUE is now concrete, not hypothetical: a gate here would have caught the abort within one CI cycle instead of two days. Note the suite must be run in a shape that FAILS on early abort (rc != 0), not one that greps for failure lines — an abort produces neither.

comments.text: GATE WIRED 2026-08-09, commit 5e528443 on worktree-agent-a6a54f53f8c54924b: tests/hooks/test_expectations_shellib_gate.py runs the real expectations_test.sh as a subprocess, gates on returncode FIRST (not stdout-grep), then on an exact pinned (passed=63, failed=0) parse of the summary line as a non-vacuity floor. title: [bug] engine: owner-ensure ON CONFLICT ignores idx_catalog_owners_repo_hash (a documented TOCTOU guard) on BOTH the insert and the do-update arm
description:
THIRD instance of the nexus-0ehwe / nexus-pbawi / nexus-jq53b class, found 2026-07-31 by
auditing EVERY ON CONFLICT arbiter in CatalogRepository against its table's FULL
unique-constraint set — the audit 0ehwe scopes. Not previously filed.

## The constraint set vs the arbiters

nexus.catalog_owners carries THREE unique keys (catalog-001-baseline.xml:46-53):

  1. catalog_owners_pk                PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix)
  2. catalog_owners_unique_name_type  UNIQUE (tenant_id, name, owner_type)
  3. idx_catalog_owners_repo_hash     UNIQUE (tenant_id, repo_hash)
                                      WHERE repo_hash IS NOT NULL AND repo_hash != ''
                                      -- comment in the DDL: "TOCTOU guard"

EVERY owner-ensure / import site arbitrates on (1) ONLY:
  CatalogRepository.java:306, :495, :653, :3568, :3594

Constraint (2) unhandled is nexus-jq53b (observed as a CI flake, PR #1423).
Constraint (3) unhandled is THIS BEAD, and it is not covered by jq53b's fix.

## Why (3) is reachable, verified by reading site :299-312

The insert writes REPO_HASH in its values list AND the DO UPDATE arm re-sets it from the
excluded row (.set(CATALOG_OWNERS.REPO_HASH, EX_OWN_REPO)). So repo_hash is populated on
both arms while the arbiter names only tumbler_prefix.

TWO distinct failure paths:
  (a) INSERT path — two owners with DIFFERENT tumbler_prefix but the SAME repo_hash. The
      arbiter does not match, so PG raises a raw 23505 on idx_catalog_owners_repo_hash
      instead of taking the DO UPDATE branch.
  (b) CONFLICT path — an upsert that legitimately resolves the tumbler_prefix conflict
      then SETS repo_hash from the excluded row, and can violate the repo_hash index in
      the same statement. The DO UPDATE arm has no WHERE and no guard against this.

Path (a) is the ordinary two-owners-one-repo case. Path (b) is nastier because the
conflict was already "handled".

## Why the DDL comment matters

The index is documented as a TOCTOU guard, which means it exists precisely to fire under
CONCURRENT registration — the same condition under which jq53b was observed. So this will
present as another intermittent CI failure with an unrelated-looking constraint name, and
be triaged as a flake.

## The generalisable rule this class needs

An ON CONFLICT arbiter must be chosen against the target table's COMPLETE unique-key set,
not against the one key the author had in mind. The same audit over catalog_documents
shows the identical split: PK (tenant_id, tumbler) vs the partial unique
ux_catalog_documents_live_source_uri (catalog-016:153). Sites :403/:3650/:3700 arbitrate
on the PK, sites :577/:793 on source_uri, and each is exposed to the other constraint —
that is exactly nexus-pbawi.

CLEAN by this audit: catalog_links, catalog_document_chunks, catalog_collections,
catalog_meta — each has arbiters matching its only unique key.

So the whole class lives in TWO tables, catalog_owners (3 keys, 1 handled) and
catalog_documents (2 keys, 1 handled per site). Fixing it table-wise rather than
site-wise is what closes it.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] nx catalog doctor --collections-drift prints a SUPERSEDE recipe against restorable trashed data — turns a reversible trash into an unreachable orphan
description:
Found by the nexus-5577r terminology census, 2026-07-31. VERIFIED end to end by
reading, not taken on the agent's word.

## The chain

1. doctor.py:241-244 builds t3_names from t3_db.list_collections(). On HttpVectorClient
   that is the collection_vector_stats view.
2. catalog-005-collection-vector-stats.xml:16-23 pins the view's semantics verbatim:
   "TOMBSTONE-FILTERED by construction ... A collection with zero live chunks does not
   appear." So a collection whose every document is TRASHED (soft-deleted, deleted_at
   set) vanishes from t3_names.
3. Trashing documents NEVER touches catalog_collections, so the registry row stays LIVE
   (superseded_by == ''). It is therefore in projection_names and NOT in
   superseded_names.
4. doctor.py:266-268: projection_not_in_t3 = projection_names - t3_names -
   superseded_names. The fully-trashed collection lands in it.
5. doctor.py:309-330 prints:
       "Projection rows whose T3 collection is gone and not superseded (N):"
   and then:
       "Remediate: register a target collection and supersede manually:
          w.register_collection('<TARGET>'); w.supersede_collection('<OLD>','<TARGET>')"

## Why this is destructive

The chunks are NOT gone. They are physically present and restorable via document
restore. The operator is told "T3 collection is gone" and handed a supersede recipe.

Superseding sets superseded_by != '', which permanently excludes the name from
CatalogRepository.collectionForTuple (it resolves on superseded_by = ''). The
restorable data becomes unreachable BY NAME. And since nexus-v6za0 the revive path is
identity-gated: only the collection the row was superseded FROM may revive it — which
here is a <TARGET> the operator invented on the spot to satisfy the recipe.

So the command converts a REVERSIBLE trash into an IRREVERSIBLE orphan, from its own
printed remediation, while reporting the situation in words ("gone") that are false.

## The root

This is the sharpest instance of the nexus-5577r conflation: the DETECTION reads the
T3 trashed-document notion of "gone" and the REMEDY acts on the catalog-registry
notion. The word "tombstone" appears nowhere in this code path, which is exactly why
it is the worst site — the two concepts have been silently unified into one English
sentence with no term left to disambiguate them.

## Fix

doctor.py must distinguish "T3 collection genuinely absent" from "T3 collection is
tombstone-filtered but restorable" BEFORE printing the supersede recipe.
probe_collection_state already returns that distinction (ABSENT vs TOMBSTONED). For the
TOMBSTONED case the correct remedy is document restore, not supersede, and the report
line must not say "gone".

## Pin owed

A doctor test seeding a collection whose every document is trashed, asserting it is NOT
reported under projection_not_in_t3 with the supersede recipe. Mutation-falsify by
reverting the discrimination.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] rename old==new onto a tombstone self-supersedes the row (1232585d removed the incidental guard)
description:
Found by the re-review of 1232585d, 2026-07-31.

handleCollectionRename has NO explicit oldName.equals(newName) guard. Before 1232585d
the collision guard caught it incidentally: collectionExists(newName) was true for
newName == oldName (the source must exist to have passed guard 1), so X -> X always
409'd. Widening to liveCollectionExists removed that incidental cover FOR TOMBSTONES.

SCENARIO:
  1. POST /rename {old_name: X, new_name: Y} — succeeds, leaves X a tombstone
     (superseded_by = Y).
  2. POST /rename {old_name: X, new_name: X} — a normalizing script, or an operator retry.
     - guard 1 collectionExists(X) -> true (tombstone-inclusive), passes
     - collision guard liveCollectionExists(X) -> FALSE, passes
     - cross_model guard skipped
     - renameCollectionTxn(X, X): liveTargetExists false -> canonical branch. Step 1's
       upsert conflicts on X and REVIVES it. Step 2's child updates are X -> X no-ops.
       Step 3 sets superseded_by = "X" ON X.
  3. Result: X.superseded_by == "X". A SELF-SUPERSEDED row, permanently excluded from
     collectionForTuple with nothing to redirect to.

That is verbatim the state the sibling verb's guard 0 calls fatal
(CatalogHandler.java:1025-1032). And CatalogHandler.java:1027-1028 asserts "Its sibling
handleCollectionRename refuses the identical old==new case for the same reason" — a claim
that was only INCIDENTALLY true and is now false.

The Python CLI does guard it (collections.py:297) — the same layer asymmetry u4e20 is about.

FIX: mirror guard 0 — if (oldName.equals(newName)) -> 400, before the collision guard.
close_reason: FIXED on develop 351874c5. Explicit old==new guard returning 400, mirroring handleCollectionSupersede's guard 0 — whose comment already CLAIMED this sibling refused the case, a claim that was only incidentally true and is now genuinely true. Pin: post_renameToItself_400s, covering both the plain case and the tombstoned variant the widened guard actually let through, asserting the row is not self-superseded. Mutation-falsified.

title: [bug] renameCollection copies superseded_by from the source, so renaming a retired collection creates a born-dead target invisible to collectionForTuple
description:
Found by the re-review of 1232585d, 2026-07-31. VERIFIED by direct reading.

renameCollectionTxn step 1's INSERT ... SELECT copies CATALOG_COLLECTIONS.SUPERSEDED_BY
and SUPERSEDED_AT from X's row (CatalogRepository.java select-list). Only the
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE arm clears them. On the FRESH-INSERT arm (target name free),
renaming a superseded X (superseded_by = Z) to Y creates Y ALREADY CARRYING
superseded_by = Z — permanently filtered out of collectionForTuple, which resolves
(content_type, owner_id, embedding_model) with superseded_by = '' ORDER BY name DESC.
Step 2 then re-homes all of X's data onto that invisible name.

THE JUSTIFYING COMMENT IS FALSE ON TWO SHIPPED PATHS. CatalogRepository.java:2958-2960
says "the CLI refuses to rename an already-superseded row, so X is live".
rename_collection_cmd DOES check superseded_by (collections.py:269-274). But
rename_collection_data_plane (collection_rename.py:85-93) checks ONLY
probe_collection_state — T3 chunk presence — so a superseded, chunk-bearing X reads
PRESENT and passes. That function is the entry point for `nx collection rename` AND for
indexer.py's UNATTENDED RDR-103 P5 legacy->conformant migrator (indexer.py:745-755),
which calls it inside try/except Exception: log.warning — so a born-dead outcome would
not even surface as an error.

IMPACT: a collection's entire content relocated to a name tuple resolution refuses to
return. Every subsequent write resolves to a different (empty or newly created) name
while the data sits unreachable. Silent, and unattended on the indexer path.
Recoverable only by hand-clearing superseded_by.

FIX (two independent, both cheap):
  1. Set SUPERSEDED_BY = '' / SUPERSEDED_AT = null EXPLICITLY in the INSERT's
     select-list, not just in the DO UPDATE arm. The "explicit beats incidental"
     argument the comment already makes for the conflict arm applies verbatim here.
  2. Make handleCollectionRename's source guard (CatalogHandler.java:1097, currently
     collectionExists) liveness-aware and 409 on a retired source, naming the remedy.

Do not leave the correctness of an engine transaction resting on which of two CLI verbs
the operator typed.
close_reason: FIXED on develop 351874c5, both halves. (1) Step 1's INSERT select-list now sets SUPERSEDED_BY='' / SUPERSEDED_AT=null EXPLICITLY instead of copying them from the source, so the fresh-insert arm cannot produce a born-dead target. (2) handleCollectionRename's source guard is liveness-aware and 409s a retired source, so the engine no longer depends on which CLI verb the operator typed. Pin: post_renameFromARetiredSource_409s, asserting the would-be born-dead row does not exist at all. Mutation-falsified. Verified behaviour change on the unattended RDR-103 P5 indexer path and recorded it on the bead: it moves from silent unreachable-data corruption to warn-and-fall-back inside the existing except arm.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
BEHAVIOUR CHANGE ON A LIVE PATH — verified, not assumed, before shipping the fix.

The new source-liveness guard 409s a rename whose SOURCE is superseded. One caller
can reach that state in production: indexer.py's RDR-103 P5 legacy->conformant
migrator. It picks `legacy` by T3 CHUNK PRESENCE (probe_collection_state) and renames
when legacy_exists and not conformant_exists — and a superseded collection that still
holds chunks reads PRESENT, which is exactly the conflation nexus-5577r is about.

So a superseded legacy collection, which previously went through and produced a
BORN-DEAD conformant row, now gets a 409.

That is the intended direction and it is safe: the call already sits inside
try/except Exception -> log.warning("phase4_migration_data_plane_failed"), and the
except arm falls back to indexing against the existing legacy data. So the outcome
moves from "silent unreachable-data corruption" to "warn and use the data where it
already is". No crash, no new failure mode.

Stated explicitly because it IS a behaviour change on an unattended path, and
"the guard is obviously right" is not the same as having checked what it breaks.

title: Round-trip collection rename is blocked by 409 through the only production path; nexus-cecqy's tombstone-revival logic is unreachable dead code
design:
Context: nx

Verified 2026-07-31 while critiquing commits 1d854b7a/8846799c/19801b9e/b2980b26/b008726b
(nexus-cecqy, nexus-g8z8n, nexus-bm8dd, nexus-3m01p, nexus-ao29z) on develop.

CatalogRepository.renameCollectionTxn (service/.../db/CatalogRepository.java:2862-2995)
was extended so that renaming X->Y retires X as a superseded tombstone, and a
round-trip rename (Y->X) is supposed to REVIVE the tombstone via an
INSERT...ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (step 1, lines 2895-2931), gated by a
`liveTargetExists` check (superseded_by = '') at lines 2871-2874.

This repository-level logic is verified ONLY by CatalogRenameCollectionTest,
which calls `repo.renameCollection(...)` DIRECTLY — bypassing the HTTP handler.

The ACTUAL production path is CatalogHandler.handleCollectionRename
(service/.../http/CatalogHandler.java:1072-1101), which guards at line 1094:

    if (!crossModel && repo.collectionExists(tenant, newName)) { ... 409 ... }

`collectionExists` (CatalogRepository.java:2811-2814) is an unconditional
`SELECT 1 ... WHERE name=?` — it does NOT filter on superseded_by, so it
returns true for a TOMBSTONED row exactly as for a live one. Consequence:
renaming Y back to X (a name retired by an earlier X->Y rename) hits this
409 ("target collection already exists") BEFORE ever reaching
renameCollectionTxn's revival logic, unless the caller passes
cross_model:true — a flag intended for the unrelated RDR-162 cross-model
COPY scenario, not documented or used for round-trip revival, and never
exercised together with a real tombstone target in any test.

No test anywhere (Java or Python) exercises a round-trip rename through the
actual HTTP endpoint. CatalogHandlerRenameTest's 409 test
(post_renameOntoExistingCollection_returns409) uses two fresh live rows, not
a tombstone, so it never proves whether a tombstoned target is exempted (it
is not).

WORSE: the CLI's own pre-flight validation (rename_collection_cmd,
src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:301-306) checks
`probe_collection_state(t3_db, new)`, which for a real HttpVectorClient
reads T3 CHUNK presence (chunks_384/768/1024 rows), NOT the catalog
registry's superseded_by column. After a forward rename, X's chunk rows
have all been re-homed to Y, so X reads as CollectionState.ABSENT at the
T3 layer even though catalog_collections still holds X as a live tombstone.
The CLI's guard therefore does NOT catch the conflict — it lets the
operator proceed — and the underlying rename_collection_data_plane() call
(collections.py:319, OUTSIDE the try/except that wraps the later
register/supersede calls at 329+) then raises an unhandled
httpx.HTTPStatusError(409) up through the CLI.

Net effect: an operator who renames a collection and later wants to
reverse/undo that rename via `nx catalog rename-collection Y X` gets an
unhandled exception, not a clean message — and the elaborate tombstone-
revival mechanism this session built exists only for a code path the
product's own guard never lets a real caller reach.

FIX SHAPE (not yet implemented): either (a) collectionExists should accept
a superseded_by='' filter (or the handler should probe getCollection and
check superseded_by before treating an existing row as a blocking
collision), or (b) the CLI/HTTP guard should recognize a tombstoned target
as revivable-not-colliding and only 409 on a genuinely LIVE target. Add an
end-to-end test that renames X->Y->X through the real CLI/HTTP path (not
repo.renameCollection() directly) to pin the fix.
close_reason:
FIXED on develop, commit 1232585d. Confirmed by reading before acting — both reviewers
found this independently, and the diagnosis is exactly right.

ROOT CAUSE: 1d854b7a changed renameCollectionTxn's branch selector to a LIVE target
(superseded_by = '') and left CatalogHandler.handleCollectionRename's collision guard on
collectionExists(), a bare row-existence check that sees tombstones. Two predicates, one
question, different answers. The 409 fired before the revive branch was reachable.

REGRESSION, not a pre-existing gap: before the tombstone change step 3 DELETEd the old row,
so X genuinely vanished and the undo worked.

FIX: CatalogRepository.liveCollectionExists() — one predicate, used by both the handler and
(inlined, same txn ctx) the branch selector, with a comment on each saying change one change
both. Renaming back onto a RETIRED name is a revive; onto a LIVE one is still the
nexus-gaou3 collision and still 409s.

ALSO CLOSED, the converse mismatch the reviewer spotted: cross_model:true against a
TOMBSTONED target would have taken the canonical FULL-REHOME branch (moving chunks,
taxonomy, aspects) under a flag whose contract is COPY-only-repoint against a LIVE
ETL-populated target. Now 409s naming the target as retired.

PINS, all through the real HTTP endpoint (the gap that let this ship):
  post_renameBackOntoATombstonedName_revivesItInsteadOf409
  post_renameOntoALIVEcollection_still409s          (the guard must not be weakened)
  post_crossModelOntoATOMBSTONE_409s
Mutation-verified: restoring collectionExists() in the guard fails exactly the round-trip
test and nothing else.

Engine 1533 passed / 0 failures. Python 11561 passed / 0 failures.

THE LESSON, recorded because it is now the third instance in two days: the repo-level
round-trip test I wrote for this very behaviour (CatalogRenameCollectionTest @Order(40))
calls repo.renameCollection() DIRECTLY and so never crosses the guard that blocks it. A test
that exercises a layer below the one production uses proves the layer, not the feature.
Same shape as nexus-cecqy's legacy_grandfathered (client-sent vs server-stored) and
nexus-bm8dd (fake_post manufacturing a metadata key the real server cannot return).

The CLI-side observation on this bead is also correct and NOT separately fixed:
rename_collection_cmd's pre-flight uses probe_collection_state (T3 chunk presence), which
cannot see a catalog tombstone. It no longer matters for this path — the handler now allows
the rename — but the pre-flight remains blind to registry state generally. Not filed
separately; noted here because if a future guard depends on that pre-flight, it will be
wrong for the same reason.

title: mechanize the stacked-reviewer gate: the close-time hook never blocks, stamps verification=passed anyway, and does not gate git push at all
description:
Filed 2026-07-31 per the escalation rule in the global orchestration directive: a recurring
miss becomes a MECHANIZATION bead, not a retro note.

THE MISS, measured. Five commits went to develop today (1d854b7a, 8846799c, 19801b9e,
b2980b26, b008726b) with ZERO code-review-expert and ZERO substantive-critic runs. Two
defects the pair exists to catch shipped:
  - a probe bypass added next to a better in-repo mechanism (ci.yml's JAR stamping) that
    was never read — an unvalidated-assumption finding, the critic's class;
  - a scratch reproduction test leaked into 19801b9e and turned develop's CI red — a
    line-level finding, the reviewer's class.

WHY IT WAS SKIPPED. This session's system prompt carries "Do not call the AgentTool unless
the user requested it". Both reviewers ARE Agent dispatches, so a STANDING gate became a
PER-INSTANCE ask, and the ask did not happen. The line is not in any file Hal controls
(checked: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/, both settings.json — neither has a
systemPrompt/appendSystemPrompt key — no output-styles, no shell wrapper); it appears to be
harness-injected, most likely a background-job policy. So it will keep recurring in exactly
the sessions nobody is watching, and it cannot be fixed by editing the repo.

THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR MECHANIZING RATHER THAN DOCUMENTING: a gate that depends on the
agent choosing to ask is not a gate when an instruction discourages asking.

=== THREE CONCRETE DEFECTS IN THE EXISTING MECHANISM ===

conexus/hooks/scripts/pre_close_verification_hook.sh is a PreToolUse hook on `bd close`.

1. IT NEVER BLOCKS. Its own section header says so: "Advisory: review scratch marker check
   (never blocks)". On a missing marker it sets REVIEW_MSG to "ADVISORY: No review marker
   found for $BEAD_ID — consider running /conexus:review-code before closing." and then
   calls `allow "$REVIEW_MSG"` (:249, :274). It fired twice today, on nexus-z6y58 and
   nexus-3m01p, and both closes proceeded.

2. IT STAMPS verification=passed REGARDLESS. Lines 268-272 run
   `bd set-state "$BEAD_ID" verification=passed` unconditionally — the same code path,
   whether or not a review marker was found. So a bead nobody reviewed acquires an audit
   record saying verification passed. That is worse than no record: it is a false one, and
   it is the shape the no-silent-fallbacks directive exists to prevent.

3. IT GATES THE WRONG EVENT. `bd close` is the only hooked verb; hooks.json has no
   PreToolUse entry matching `git push` or `git commit`. Unreviewed code reaches develop
   at PUSH, and today all five pushes happened BEFORE any bead close. Even a blocking
   version of this hook would not have stopped a single one of them.

=== WHAT TO BUILD, needs a call on scope ===

  (a) Make the close-time check BLOCK (deny) instead of advise, and move the
      verification=passed stamp inside the marker-found branch. Smallest change; fixes (1)
      and (2); does nothing for (3).
  (b) Add a PreToolUse hook on `git push` that denies when HEAD's commits touch source
      paths and no review marker covers them. This is the one that would have caught
      today. Needs a rule for what "covers" means — per-bead markers do not map cleanly
      onto a push of five commits, so it likely needs a per-BRANCH or per-RANGE marker.
  (c) Both.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT (hot rule): this file lives under conexus/, which loads from the
PINNED release tag. Any edit is INERT until the next plugin release and MUST be declared in
conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md. So the fix does not take effect on Hal's machine when merged —
only when the plugin is next cut. Plan for that gap; do not close this bead on merge.

COMPANION, not a substitute: a standing pre-authorization line is being added to
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so the reviewers are requested durably rather than per-instance. That
addresses the instruction's CONDITION. It does not make the gate mechanical, and a
CLAUDE.md line cannot be relied on to outrank a system-prompt line in a future session —
which is exactly why this bead exists.
close_reason: ACTIVATED at the v7.3.0 pin advance (PyPI published, marketplace source.ref -> v7.3.0): the mechanized close-gate (bd close blocks on missing review marker, verification stamped only on evidence) and push-gate (review coverage on gated paths) are live in installed sessions from the next plugin update. Pin-inert period over; the bead's own activation condition met 2026-08-07.

comments.text:
NOT SUPERSEDED BY nexus-h33x8 — flagged as a CRITICAL in that epic's critique (2026-07-31,
T2 [21318]), recorded here so it is visible from THIS bead too rather than only from the
epic's.

h33x8 is a measurement epic: if all seven of its children ship, a session that silently
declines to dispatch specialists would be MEASURED, not PREVENTED. The prevention lives
HERE — item (b), the git-push gate. It is the only piece in either bead that would have

comments.text: Gate-mechanization datum (2026-08-03): the pre-close review-marker hook is defeated by shell loop variables — 'for b in ...; do bd close $b ...' made the hook look up a marker for the literal string $b and emit a false-positive advisory, even though the review-completed marker (15b31e97, tags review-completed,3ck2g,8j1zx,txcbo) existed. The only other git-capable actor on the checkout is IntelliJ IDEA (RemoteMavenServer36 live; IDEA update/checkout flows run 'git stash' with the default 'WIP on <branch>' message, which is exactly stash@{0}'s message). Unproven but the best fit. Action items stand: (1) the guard cannot see top-level sessions or IDE actions — with two sessions on one checkout the tree is unguarded; (2) when edits vanish, check 'git stash list' FIRST (an un-popped stash is recoverable); (3) the earlier top-level 'git stash -q && ruff && git stash pop' in nexus-0d was a real guard miss for top-level sessions.
