title: four engine-booting integration gates have ERRORED at setup since 2026-07-09: the cloud version probe fail-closes on the unstamped dev JAR the fixtures themselves build
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while building a reproduction for nexus-bm8dd. MEASURED, not inferred.

Every integration gate that boots the in-repo service JAR and drives HttpVectorClient
ERRORS AT SETUP. Not a failure inside a test -- the fixture cannot construct the client:

  nexus.db.managed_endpoint.ManagedServiceIncompatible: ... reported no usable
  release_version on /version (got None) -- a dev/unstamped or pre-release engine is
  older than the minimum this client supports (v0.1.59)

Confirmed dead, one test run from each file, all four fail identically:
  tests/db/test_http_combined_query_integration.py
  tests/db/test_write_seam_gate_integration.py
  tests/db/test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py
  tests/db/test_frecency_enehl_integration.py

MECHANISM, and note that NEITHER SIDE IS WRONG:
  - service/src/main/resources/META-INF/nexus/release.properties ships release_version
    BLANK by design; it is stamped only at native-build time from an engine-service-vX.Y.Z
    tag. VersionHandler.normalizeReleaseVersion maps blank/SNAPSHOT/dev to null, because
    an unstamped engine is by definition not a tagged release.
  - get_http_vector_client() runs a one-time-per-process probe in cloud mode and
    fail-closes on a null release_version (RDR-002 ez5.4).
  - The fixtures boot a `mvn package` JAR -- which can only ever be unstamped -- and then
    put the client in cloud mode (they delenv NX_LOCAL, set NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_VECTORS
    =service). So the gate refuses the very engine the test built.

The gap is in the HARNESS, not the product. A harness that builds and boots the engine
under test knows its identity by construction; there is no skew for the hosted-service
compatibility gate to catch.

DATE IT BROKE: 2026-07-09, commit 3cb14f96 "fix(engine-version): fail-loud cloud probe on
the real connection path". That commit did not touch any of the four files. Three weeks
dead, and nothing reported it, because all four are -m integration and CI does not run
that marker -- the same visibility hole as nexus-5opzu, different cause.

WHY THIS ONE HURTS MOST. test_http_combined_query_integration.py exists BECAUSE
request-shape-only tests let a silent-empty-join reach a live tenant (nexus-x6kdz, the
6.5.0 shakeout where every combined-query SQL function returned zero rows). Its own
docstring says so: "Every Python combined-query unit/integration test monkeypatched
HttpVectorClient._post and asserted request SHAPE only -- none of them round-tripped
through a real Postgres-backed service, so the join could not actually fail in those
tests." The gate written to close that hole has itself been unrunnable since 07-09.

The probe's OWN contract stays pinned by hermetic unit tests and is not in question here:
tests/db/test_managed_endpoint.py, tests/db/test_engine_floor_connection_path.py,
tests/db/test_http_vector_client_version_gate.py.
close_reason:
FIXED on develop, commit 8846799c. All four gates run again.

FIX: mark_version_probe_satisfied_for_tests() in http_vector_client -- a test-only
declaration for harnesses that BUILD AND BOOT the engine under test. Identity is known by
construction there, so there is no skew for the hosted-service compatibility gate to
catch. Production behaviour unchanged: the override defaults False and its only writer is
the helper.

STICKY ON PURPOSE, and this was the second bug. The first attempt set the existing
_version_probe_done flag, which reset_http_vector_client_for_tests() clears -- and
mcp_infra.reset_singletons() calls that helper internally. So the seam-b fixture marked,
then reset, then lost the declaration, and the probe fired mid-test: three of four gates
went green and the fourth did not. The override now lives in its own global that reset
does not touch, with clear_version_probe_override_for_tests() to undo it deliberately. An
ordering rule invisible from the call site is not a fix.

TRIPWIRES, in the ROUTINE suite (not behind -m integration -- running only there is how
this went unseen for three weeks): TestIntegrationHarnessOverride pins that the override
suppresses the probe, SURVIVES a reset (the exact trap above), and is clearable. Each
carries a non-vacuity half proving the probe still fires without it. The file's autouse
fixture now clears the sticky override too, or one test would silently disable the gate
for every test after it. Mutation-verified: ignoring the override fails all three and
nothing else.

The probe's own contract is untouched and still pinned by the same hermetic unit tests
(tests/db/test_managed_endpoint.py, tests/db/test_engine_floor_connection_path.py, and the
15 pre-existing tests in tests/db/test_http_vector_client_version_gate.py).

MEASURED GREEN, each file in its own process:
  test_http_combined_query_integration.py   4 passed
  test_write_seam_gate_integration.py       4 passed
  test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py        2 passed
  test_frecency_enehl_integration.py        1 passed
Full Python suite: 11563 passed, 0 failures.

SPUN OUT: nexus-z6y58 -- running all four in ONE pytest process errors at setup (7 passed
/ 4 errors, all in the write-seam gate, all PSQLException) while each file alone is green.
Suspected the documented Docker port-forwarding wedge; NOT root-caused, so the
combined-query docstring says to run it in its own process rather than claiming a cause.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION to this bead's closure and to commit 8846799c. Two things I got wrong.

1. "THREE WEEKS DEAD, AND NOTHING SAID SO" IS WRONG FOR CI. ci.yml's write-seam job runs
   test_write_seam_gate_integration.py AND test_http_combined_query_integration.py behind
   a paths filter, with a non-vacuity assert (scripts/assert_write_seam_ran.py), and it
   has been PASSING throughout. Verified across the last 8 CI runs. The breakage was
   LOCAL-only. Accurate statement of the defect: a developer's `mvn package` produced a
   JAR none of the four suites could use.

   Coverage as it actually stands:
     test_write_seam_gate_integration.py        CI seam job (stamped JAR)   local: was broken
     test_http_combined_query_integration.py    CI seam job (stamped JAR)   local: was broken
     test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py         NO CI job                   local: was broken
     test_frecency_enehl_integration.py         NO CI job                   local: was broken
     test_http_catalog_integration.py           NO CI job                   local: fine (no vector client)
     test_i711w_gap_xfails.py                   NO CI job                   local: fine (no vector client)

2. THE FIX WAS THE WRONG SHAPE. That CI job hit this on the same day the probe landed
   (3cb14f96) and solved it by STAMPING release_version into the gate JAR, with a comment
   saying explicitly why it did not bypass the probe: the gate then exercises a CONFORMANT
   engine and "the hardening stays intact." I did not read it, and shipped a probe bypass
   (mark_version_probe_satisfied_for_tests) alongside a better in-repo mechanism — and
   left local runs proving something weaker than CI proves.

REPLACED in commit b008726b: the bypass is deleted (helper, sticky global, cloud_mode
carve-out, and the three tripwires that only pinned it). scripts/build-gate-jar.sh is
CI's stamping step for a developer machine — version from REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION, and
release.properties restored on every exit path so the tree never carries a stamp. The four
suites carry a needs_stamped_jar marker and tests/db/conftest.py refuses an unstamped JAR
with the build command (skip locally, FAIL in CI — the sibling jar-freshness disposition).
10 hermetic pins on the guard run in the routine suite; mutation-verified.

All four suites verified green against a stamped JAR with the hardening intact (4/4/2/1),
and an unstamped JAR now skips with a legible remedy instead of a message blaming the
hosted service.

The two files with NO automated coverage anywhere remain uncovered — tracked on
nexus-5opzu, which now carries the full coverage map.

title: integration-only strict-xfail pins go stale unseen: 6 XPASS(strict) sat red for a session because CI never runs -m integration

      integration-marked catalog files and reports. Cheapest signal, matches the

The two prior red nightlies were NOT leg failures — they were the 376115c1 env-prefix regression (fixed e926106c, nexus-tmsnz tracks the release-window exposure). comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SHARPENED, 2026-07-31, after two more instances the same day. Partly fixed; the remainder
is a CI-cost decision for Hal, so this stays OPEN.

SECOND AND THIRD INSTANCES, both today:
  - A throwaway reproduction I wrote (test_bm8dd_probe_ids_for_source) shipped in 19801b9e
    asserting the behaviour that same commit retired. The routine suite could not see it —
    -m integration file — and develop's write-seam CI job went red on it. Removed in
    b2980b26. This one WAS caught, by CI, roughly an hour later.
  - nexus-ao29z: four suites unusable locally for three weeks.

THE COVERAGE MAP, measured (this is what the bead was missing):

  test_write_seam_gate_integration.py       CI seam job, paths-filtered, non-vacuity assert
  test_http_combined_query_integration.py   same job, same invocation
  test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py        NO automated gate anywhere
  test_frecency_enehl_integration.py        NO automated gate anywhere
  test_http_catalog_integration.py          NO automated gate anywhere
  test_i711w_gap_xfails.py                  NO automated gate anywhere   <-- the original instance

So the problem is NOT "integration tests never run in CI" as filed. Two of them run and
work. The problem is four specific files with no gate, one of which holds the SOLE
repo-wide pins on five service-catalog contracts.

WHY THEY CANNOT SIMPLY JOIN THE SEAM JOB: the seam job provisions Docker PG. All four
uncovered files want LOCAL PG binaries (pg_bin_dir() / pg_ctl), which that job does not
have. CI does cache PG bundles, but in the CA-3 / bundle jobs (ci.yml ~558-660), not this
one. Adding a bundle to the seam job — or adding a job — is real CI cost, and CI cost
discipline is a directive, so it is Hal's call, not mine.

NEEDS A DECISION:
  (a) Add the PG bundle to the existing seam job and fold the four files into its single
      pytest invocation. Cheapest incremental cost (the job already boots JAR + ONNX), but
      it widens a paths-filtered job's prerequisites, and each added file needs its own
      non-vacuity entry in scripts/assert_write_seam_ran.py or a prereq-skip silently
      restores exactly today's hole.
  (b) A scheduled job (the scheduled-failure watchdog already exists on main to report
      it). Off the PR critical path, so cost is bounded and predictable — but schedules
      fire only from the DEFAULT branch, so it must land on main to be live.
  (c) Leave CI alone and rely on the local path, now that scripts/build-gate-jar.sh and
      the needs_stamped_jar guard make a local run actually work. Zero cost, and zero
      signal when nobody runs it — which is the state that produced all three instances.

MY RECOMMENDATION: (b). These are slow, infrastructure-heavy gates whose value is
catching drift over weeks, not blocking a PR; a scheduled run with the existing watchdog
matches that cadence and the cost directive. (a) puts multi-minute PG provisioning onto a
PR-blocking path for tests that have never caught a same-PR regression.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED (nexus-ao29z, commit b008726b): the local path works again for the
four vector-driving suites, and an unstamped JAR now refuses with the build command
instead of an error blaming the hosted service. That removes the friction excuse for not
running them locally, but it is not a gate.

title: [bug] --extractor docling can complete with space-stripped, unsearchable output and report success — the documented MinerU recovery silently degrades
description:
Found while fixing nexus-5xn3k AC2, 2026-07-31. Filed rather than left as a comment.

nexus-5xn3k's second "Related defect": on a 69-page paper, `--extractor docling` COMPLETED and reported success while producing space-stripped text — "istheasetofthe", "aspartofasequenceofinput" — heavy raw-LaTeX noise, and chunks carrying no title (search rendered them as bare chashes). The document did not match a semantic query quoting its own central finding verbatim.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. --help presents docling as the SAFE RECOVERY for MinerU failures ("formula-stripped, but always completes"). So the documented remedy for one failure silently produces an unsearchable document. Nothing in the pipeline flags it; the run is indistinguishable from success, which is the same silent-quality-collapse class as an audit that returns {} or a gate that skips a broken document. A LOUD failure (MinerU) is strictly safer than a silent quality collapse that is then indexed, embedded, and paid for.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (from the bead, not yet designed): a post-extraction sanity gate — whitespace ratio, mean token length, or dictionary-word fraction — that FAILS the run rather than indexing garbage. Needs a threshold chosen against real corpora so it does not reject legitimate dense-notation papers; that calibration is the actual work, not the check.

Note the AC2 staleness fix does NOT help here: garbage that indexed successfully has a complete manifest, so it is "whole" by every structural measure. Only content quality distinguishes it.
close_reason: Landed fb3e4915 + fe8f2424 (census declaration), CI green run on tip fe8f2424. Calibrated post-extraction quality gate at the single extractor choke point: 25-real-sample calibration incl. the incident paper's dense-LaTeX from T3, >=2.3x margins; ExtractionQualityError record-survivable (occurrence-5 wrapper-gap caught in review); per-file containment in nx index repo; durable quality_gate_overridden metadata (searchable); CJK capability-honest skip; token floor. 2 review rounds to closure ([21550]/[21551]); residuals: 4th63 P3 (all-whitespace edge), 1y9i1/l22vg P3 (stability follow-ups).

title: [bug] T3.ids_for_source and delete_by_source silently return 0 in service mode — the documented 'delete chunks and re-index' recovery does nothing
description:
Found while fixing nexus-5xn3k AC2 (staleness verification), 2026-07-31. Filed rather than left in a commit message.

nexus-5xn3k's own "Related defect" section reports that BOTH T3.ids_for_source(collection, source_path) and delete_by_source(collection, source_path) return 0 against the HTTP client — for a .dt-content markdown path AND a PDF path, with and without the embedded-newline filename. So the natural recovery for a damaged document ("delete this document's chunks and re-index") is UNAVAILABLE in service mode, which is every mode after nexus-i711w.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE AFTER THE AC2 FIX, not less. The staleness gate now re-indexes when the manifest is not fully present, so a partially-indexed document is repairable by re-indexing. But an operator who instead reaches for the documented "delete the chunks and start over" path gets a silent 0 — no error, no deletion — and concludes the tooling is broken. Worse, PARTIAL deletion is now known to be actively harmful (nexus-5xn3k root cause: one surviving chunk used to re-arm the skip), so a delete verb that silently deletes NOTHING is the safest of the bad outcomes but still leaves the operator with no working recovery command.

SCOPE: establish whether source-path chunk addressing is meant to survive at all post-RDR-108. Chunk identity is the chash (RDR-180) and source_path was retired from chunk metadata in RDR-108 Phase 3, so these two methods may be addressing a key space that no longer exists — in which case the honest fix is to make them RAISE (unsupported) rather than return 0, per the no-silent-fallbacks directive. If they ARE meant to work, they need to route through the manifest (doc -> chashes -> delete by id) like the rest of the post-108 readers.

Same family as the orphan_backfill.py:130 service-mode crash on nexus-mok9x.
close_reason:
FIXED on develop, commit 19801b9e.

THE SCOPE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and it is the first branch this bead offered: source-path
chunk addressing was NOT meant to survive. RDR-102 D2 hard-removed source_path from the
chunk schema -- it is not in metadata_schema.ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL and make_chunk_metadata()
raises TypeError if a caller passes it. No chunk this codebase writes has carried the key
since. (The bead guessed RDR-108 Phase 3; the removal is RDR-102 D2, one RDR earlier.)

PROVEN, not inferred: an engine-backed probe (real JAR + real PG, via the harness revived
under nexus-ao29z) confirmed ids_for_source/delete_by_source work correctly when a chunk
DOES carry source_path. The mechanism was never broken. What is broken is that nothing
puts the key there -- which is why the wire-shape tests all passed.

SCOPE WAS WIDER THAN TWO METHODS. Four, and three call sites:
  ids_for_source, delete_by_source, update_source_path, list_unique_source_paths
  nx t3 prune-stale         -- printed a clean "0 stale" on every corpus regardless of
                               how many indexed files were gone from disk. It had a
                               SECOND independent failure: it opened the local catalog by
                               probing for documents.jsonl, gone since nexus-i711w.
  nx doctor --fix-paths     -- reported "(n chunks)" / "N T3 chunks updated", n always 0.
  MCP traverse              -- returned ids=[] on every call, silently (per-node except).

RESOLUTION
  - The four methods RAISE, naming the cause and the replacement addressing.
    T3Database's Chroma twins untouched: make_t3() has not returned that class since
    nexus-i711w and it dies with the Chroma leg.
  - nx t3 prune-stale RETIRED, not rebuilt. `nx catalog prune-stale` + `nx t3 gc` already
    does strictly more, and in the right order: dropping the document first avoids the
    dangling manifest that a chunk-only sweep creates (nexus-5xn3k).
  - nx doctor --fix-paths: T3 leg deleted; the repair is the catalog row.
  - traverse: chunk ids from the catalog manifest, one batched call for all nodes.

WHY THE PINS DID NOT CATCH IT -- the durable lesson. Every test asserted what the CLIENT
SENT. TestDeleteBySource / TestUpdateSourcePath covered pagination, 404 handling and
mid-pagination re-raise, all green against dead methods. The two "real client" service-mode
tests went further and MANUFACTURED the key: their own fake_post returned chunk metadata
containing source_path, then asserted the sweep "deleted 2 chunk(s)". My own first
reproduction did the same and passed -- it only worked because I hand-wrote the metadata
through upsert_chunks, bypassing make_chunk_metadata. Same class as the nexus-cecqy
legacy_grandfathered finding earlier today; recorded in auto-memory.

15 pins on the old behaviour replaced by pins on the retirement, each asserting an EFFECT
rather than a call. Mutation-verified for the traverse change. Full suite 11554 passed,
0 failures.

title: [bug] service link/link_if_absent skips dangling-endpoint validation — auto_link CREATES dangling links where local skipped them
description: Found live by the terminal-deletion verification (2026-07-30, tests/test_auto_linker.py). The local catalog's link_if_absent raised ValueError for a missing endpoint; auto_link (catalog/auto_linker.py:~136) depends on that raise to count skipped_missing_endpoint. HttpCatalogClient.link_if_absent -> engine upsertLink performs NO endpoint-existence validation, so a stale/absent target tumbler produces created=1 and a DANGLING edge written into the live catalog — silent graph corruption from any stale link-context (the auto-linker runs on every dt/index pass). title: RDR-184 Gap-1 guard cannot recognise ANY dispatch in this harness: name-morphology keys on a name the Agent tool has no parameter for, so undeclared=0 is structurally unfalsifiable (0/6 then 0/10 in consecutive sessions)
description:
MECHANIZATION BEAD, filed per the RDR-184 escalation rule (any undeclared background teammate
in a retro -> bead, not a retro note). This is the SECOND consecutive session with the same
result, so it is a mechanism defect, not an operator lapse.

MEASURED, session febd7635-6fb6-4618-ae89-9866d67c312e (2026-07-29, 10 dispatches):
  expectations_undeclared:
    SUMMARY   checked=10 recognized=0 unrecognized=10 undeclared=0
    BLINDSPOT guard recognised 0 of 10 dispatched agent(s) by name-morphology -
              undeclared=0 here is NOT evidence of compliance, it means nothing was checkable
  expectations_census:
    ROWS       expect=0 start=10 reported=0 blocked=0 wouldblock=0
    CLASSIFIED reported=0 blocked_resolved=0 (immediate=0 later=0) blocked_unresolved=0
               wouldblock=0 no_terminal=0 undeclared=0 no_start=0 expected_no_start=0
    BLINDSPOT  checked=10 recognized=0 unrecognized=10
Prior session: identical shape at 0 of 6 (recorded on nexus-qc4p1).

ROOT CAUSE, and it is structural. The guard recognises teammates by NAME-MORPHOLOGY, the
`a<name>-<hash>` encoding that tests/cc-validation scenario 27 pins as production-load-bearing.
But in this harness the Agent tool has NO `name` parameter. Names can only be stated inside the
prompt text ("You are classifier sweep-A-coremodules"), which the runtime never sees; it assigns
opaque ids like `aac68ed38da538978`. So the morphology the guard looks for is never present, and
`recognized` can never be greater than 0 no matter how disciplined the operator is.

CONSEQUENCE: `undeclared=0` is not a weak signal, it is an UNFALSIFIABLE one. The only reason
two sessions did not report a false PASS is that the BLINDSPOT line exists and was read. A
future session that reads the SUMMARY line alone gets a clean bill of health from a guard that
checked nothing. That is the exact failure class RDR-184 was built to prevent, sitting inside
RDR-184's own audit.

MY OWN ERROR, recorded so it is not repeated: I concluded earlier this session that the EXPECT
mechanism was simply unavailable, because `expectations_expect` is not an MCP tool in this
session's tool set and `nx expectations` is not a CLI verb. I wrote that on nexus-i711w as a
blindspot. It is WRONG: `expectations_expect` exists as a shell function at
tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh:91 and was available the whole time. I checked two surfaces and
declared absence without checking the repo's own lib. So all 10 dispatches genuinely could have
had EXPECT rows and did not. Corrected here.

FIX OPTIONS, needs a decision:
 (a) Key the guard on the agentId the Agent tool RETURNS at spawn, and make the dispatch
     convention record agentId -> intended-name at dispatch time. This is the only option that
     works in a harness where the tool takes no name.
 (b) If name-morphology must stay the key, then the guard has to FAIL LOUD when
     recognized==0 while start>0, instead of reporting undeclared=0. A guard that cannot see
     its subject must say so in its verdict, not only in a separate BLINDSPOT line.
 (c) Both. (b) is the cheap safety net and should land regardless of (a).

Do NOT close this by writing EXPECT rows more diligently. The rows were not the failing part:
`expect=0` and `recognized=0` are independent, and fixing only the first still leaves a guard
that recognises nothing.

RELATED: nexus-qc4p1 carries the prior session's evidence. The two sessions together are the
non-vacuity argument for this bead.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION + the cleanest falsification yet, 2026-07-31 (session cf2ecd4c).

## First: a WRONG sub-cause recorded on this bead is retracted

A prior session recorded, as a new sub-cause, that "expectations_expect was not
present in the tool set at all (confirmed via ToolSearch), so expect=0 is not an
agent skipping the convention, it is an agent with no way to comply."

THAT IS FALSE. `expectations_expect` exists and works. It is a SOURCED BASH
FUNCTION, not an MCP tool:

    source tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh      # plugin copy: conexus/hooks/scripts/expectations.sh
    expectations_expect <session_id> <name> background

Searching the MCP tool registry for it will always come up empty, by design. The
orchestration skill names this exact trap already (nexus-3ra9h: "the declaration
surface is a SHELL LIB, not an nx verb"). I repeated the inherited claim in this
session before checking, then checked. The retracted sub-cause should not be used
as evidence for anything.

## Second: the ACTUAL structural claim is CONFIRMED, with better evidence

The prior four sessions all reported expect=0, which leaves the innocent
explanation open: maybe the orchestrator just never declared. This session
declared PROPERLY and the guard still cannot pair the rows.

Ledger after two background dispatches (code-review-expert + substantive-critic),
both declared BEFORE-in-intent (rows written late in wall-clock, see caveat):

    START   a29d3cfdd53ae3e98        conexus:code-review-expert
    START   abac57f3bdc8d411a        conexus:substantive-critic
    EXPECT  reviewer-cre-1232585d    background
    EXPECT  critic-sc-1232585d       background

    census:     ROWS expect=2 start=2 ... expected_no_start=2
                BLINDSPOT checked=2 recognized=0 unrecognized=2      rc=1
    undeclared: SUMMARY checked=2 recognized=0 unrecognized=2 undeclared=0   rc=1

expect=2, start=2, SAME TWO AGENTS, recognized=0. Both EXPECT rows classify as
EXPECTED_NO_START and both STARTs as unrecognized, simultaneously. The innocent
explanation is now eliminated: this is not non-compliance, it is unpairable keys.

## Root cause, verified against the live Agent tool schema

The Agent tool's parameters are exactly: description, prompt, subagent_type,
model, isolation, run_in_background. THERE IS NO `name` PARAMETER.

So the two sides of the ledger are keyed on values that can never be the same
string:
  - EXPECT is keyed on a name the ORCHESTRATOR invents. The only place that name
    can be put is inside the prompt TEXT, which the SubagentStart hook never sees.
  - START is keyed on the FRAMEWORK's agent_id (a29d3...) plus agent_type
    (conexus:code-review-expert).

Name-morphology matching between them is not "unreliable in this harness", it is
structurally impossible. undeclared=0 is unfalsifiable exactly as this bead says.

## What would actually fix it

Match on `agent_type` (which BOTH sides can know) rather than on an
orchestrator-invented name, or have the orchestrator declare the subagent_type it
is about to dispatch and pair on that + ordinal. A dispatch of two DIFFERENT types
is then fully pairable; two of the SAME type needs an ordinal. That is a real
design change to the ledger key, not a convention fix, and it is what this bead
should carry.

## Caveat, stated rather than hidden

The two EXPECT rows above were written AFTER the dispatches, not before, because I
believed the inherited claim that the function did not exist until I checked
mid-turn. Write-before-dispatch is load-bearing for the stop-guard; it is NOT
load-bearing for the pairing result shown here, since pairing is by key content,
not by timestamp order. The recognized=0 finding stands independent of the late
write.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
AUDIT HALF FIXED 2026-07-31 in the nexus-qc4p1 worktree (3 commits, unmerged); BLOCKING half deliberately untouched.

## The structural claim on this bead is CONFIRMED by measurement, and the fix is now the type key

Probed the live payloads rather than reasoning from the schema (catch-all
PreToolUse + SubagentStart loggers, real dispatches, sandboxed HOME):

  PreToolUse    tool_name="Agent"
                tool_input = {description, prompt, subagent_type, run_in_background}
                top level  = {session_id, tool_use_id, prompt_id, cwd,
                              hook_event_name, permission_mode, effort, transcript_path}
  SubagentStart {agent_id, agent_type, cwd, hook_event_name, prompt_id,
                 session_id, transcript_path}

Three dispatches in ONE turn (general-purpose, general-purpose, Explore) produced
agent_type == subagent_type VERBATIM for all three, under the SAME session_id.
agent_ids were a94a5d54.., a4dae47b.., a5943d9b.. — bare 'a<hash>', confirming the
name-morphology can never appear. So option (a) on this bead is right, with one
correction: key on agent_type, NOT on 'agentId recorded at dispatch time' — the
PreToolUse payload carries NO agent_id (the agent does not exist yet), so there is
nothing to record a mapping FROM at dispatch time.

## An ordinal is NOT available either — measured, not assumed

tool_use_id is unique per dispatch but ABSENT from the SubagentStart payload.
prompt_id is present in BOTH but is the TURN id: identical across all three
dispatches in the message. There is no per-instance key in either direction, so an
ordinal invented at write time would be exactly as unpairable as the name is. The
audit therefore does N-of-type credit matching (N EXPECT rows of a type against N
STARTs of that type, first-appearance order) and reports the deficit.

## What changed

expectations_undeclared and expectations_census now recognise a START row by
EITHER key — legacy 'a<name>-<hash>' morphology OR agent_type present among EXPECT
names — and decide declared/undeclared by credit rather than set membership. The
BLINDSPOT hard-failure is unchanged and still fires when nothing was checkable,
which is now precisely what an inert dispatch hook looks like. Verified by
mutation: reverting the recogniser to morphology-only turns the pairing tests red.

## What did NOT change, stated as scope and not hidden

expectations_owes_report — the BLOCKING stop-guard consult — is untouched and
still requires the 'a<name>-' morphology, so it still returns 1 for every agent in
this harness and the guard still never blocks. That is option (b)/(c) territory
and it needs a decision, because dropping the morphology gate there introduces a
false-block class the gate exists to kill: a SYNC agent of a type that ALSO had a
background dispatch would be told it owes a report. Not taken unilaterally on a
live default-ON guard.

So after this change: undeclared=0 becomes MEANINGFUL (recognized>0 is reachable),
but the guard's ability to actually block is still zero. This bead should stay
open for that.

The cause is not name-morphology guessing and not a missing Agent-tool parameter: SubagentStart records agent_type VERBATIM including the colon, and pairing works when the EXPECT row carries that same verbatim string.

WHAT ACTUALLY BROKE IT: AGENTS.md instructs agents to sanitize the colon, on the stated grounds that expectations_expect 'validates ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, so a plugin-namespaced type like conexus:substantive-critic must have its colon sanitized before it is accepted at all.' That is FALSE. tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh:137 is ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_:-]{0,63}$ — the colon IS in the charset, and the colon form is accepted with rc=0 and written verbatim. Every session that followed the documented sanitization guidance destroyed its own pairing key.

This is a fifth instance of this week's headline pattern: a doc asserting a constraint that does not exist.

COROLLARY 1 — the qc4p1 hook is already correct. conexus/hooks/scripts/agent-dispatch-expect.sh:95 writes str(ti.get('subagent_type')) with no sanitization, so when the plugin release makes it live it will pair. The predicted post-release recognized=0 outcome that this bead says would falsify the design should now be predicted as recognized=N instead.

COROLLARY 2 — nexus-h33x8.2 ('recognize dispatches by subagent_type+ordinal') may be largely moot for the recognition half; subagent_type alone already pairs. Re-scope it to the ordinal/multiplicity question only.

This session's own live ledger was left UNCORRECTED on purpose (expect=2 sanitized, start=2 colon, recognized=0) so the retro record stays truthful rather than retro-fitted.

title: alias following does not exist service-side: resolve() declares follow_alias=True and never reads it, resolve_alias returns its input, and updateDocument has no alias hop — set_alias writes a pointer nothing follows
description:
Found during the nexus-i711w C-store port (commit b234142a). MEASURED first
(`assert ('1.1.1', 99) == ('1.1.1', 0)` when porting
test_alias_of_survives_legacy_update_through_alias), then settled from source.

THREE INDEPENDENT PLACES WHERE THE ALIAS HOP IS MISSING:

1. src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:877-888
     def resolve(self, tumbler, *, follow_alias: bool = True) -> CatalogEntry | None:
   The parameter is DECLARED, DEFAULTED TO TRUE, and never read. The body GETs
   /show?tumbler=... and returns _to_entry(result). A caller passing follow_alias=True — which
   is every caller, since it is the default — silently gets no alias resolution.

2. src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1144-1148
     def resolve_alias(self, tumbler, *, max_hops=16) -> Tumbler:
         entry = self.resolve(tumbler, follow_alias=True)
         if entry: return entry.tumbler
         return Tumbler.parse(str(tumbler))
   Because (1) ignores follow_alias, entry.tumbler IS the input tumbler. So resolve_alias is an
   identity function service-side. `max_hops` is dead too.

3. service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java:485-501
   updateDocument is `WHERE tumbler = ?` with no alias hop, so an update addressed to an ALIAS
   updates the alias row itself rather than its canonical target. That is what the measurement
   above caught: the legacy-path update landed on the alias.

CONSEQUENCE. `set_alias` still WRITES alias_of (client :1141-1142 POSTs /update with alias_of),
so the data is there and looks correct in the store. Nothing FOLLOWS it. An alias is therefore
a pointer the system records and then ignores: resolving an alias returns the alias, and
updating through an alias mutates the alias. No error, no warning — the wrong row, silently.
This is the no-silent-fallbacks-for-data-correctness case: a declared-and-ignored parameter is
worse than an unimplemented one, because the signature advertises the behaviour.

RELATED, and this now looks like a cluster rather than three unrelated bugs:
  - nexus-iltyk  set_alias has a cross-substrate ROUTING gap (the write goes somewhere the
                 caller cannot observe).
  - nexus-tz1cx  by_doc_id asks a different question on each substrate, silently returning None.
  - this bead    alias_of is written but never followed, on three separate code paths.
All three are the alias/identity surface of the service client diverging from the local
implementation while keeping identical signatures. Worth one coordinated pass over
HttpCatalogClient's identity methods rather than three point fixes — and worth asking what else
in that class has a parameter it does not read.

FIX OPTIONS, needs a decision:
  (a) implement the hop — client-side loop honouring max_hops, or server-side in /show and
      updateDocument (the latter needs an engine change + tag, and is the only place that can
      fix (3) correctly);
  (b) if aliases are not intended to work on the service substrate, then DELETE the follow_alias
      parameter and make resolve_alias raise, so the ~dozen call sites fail loudly instead of
      getting the wrong row.
Leaving a declared parameter unread is the one option that is not acceptable.

TEST STATE: test_alias_of_survives_legacy_update_through_alias is left PORT-BLOCKED and
annotated with this trail in tests/test_rdr101_round3_correctness.py. It becomes the regression
test. Note also i711w.1 items 18/19 (projector tombstone non-resurrection, alias_of population)
are partly pre-answered by this: alias_of IS written service-side but never followed, so the
honest disposition there is "not implemented yet", not "N/A".
close_reason: Engine fix shipped on develop 96b3d97c (merge d06f8cfc, branch worktree-agent-a7495f323076364cf). Engine suite 1514 passed / 0 failed; Python suite 11531 passed / 0 failed. Stacked-reviewed; every reviewer finding fixed or filed; reviewer-flagged fixes falsified by reverting each one. NOT YET TAGGED — the engine-service tag cut, conexus deploy and cloud gate are Hal's relay, and REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION bumps only AFTER that deploy (GH #1402 ordering).

title: CatalogEntry and CatalogLink are DEFINED in the dying catalog.py and imported by the SURVIVING service client — deleting the module wholesale breaks the service arm outright
description:
HARD DELETION BLOCKER for nexus-i711w. Found during the C-store port (commit b234142a),
verified in source.

src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:84
    from nexus.catalog.catalog import CatalogEntry, CatalogLink, Tumbler
src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:86
    from nexus.catalog.catalog_writes import ManifestRow

And those types are DEFINED in the dying module:
    CatalogEntry  src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:430
    CatalogLink   src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:500
(`Tumbler` is only re-exported through catalog.py — it actually lives at
src/nexus/catalog/tumbler.py:16 — so that one import just needs re-pointing.)

HttpCatalogClient is THE SURVIVING SUBSTRATE. Its entire read API is typed in terms of
CatalogEntry (every resolve / by_file_path / by_doc_id / list returns one) and its link API in
terms of CatalogLink. So deleting nexus/catalog/catalog.py wholesale does not merely remove
the local arm — it breaks the service arm, which is the arm that is supposed to be left
standing. i711w cannot land as a module-level delete.

ACTION: move CatalogEntry, CatalogLink and ManifestRow into a surviving module before the
deletion commit. They are plain data types with no SQLite dependency; a types/records module
with no catalog-implementation dependency is the natural home, and moving them there also kills
a family of circular-dep deferrals that only exist because they live next to the local Catalog.
Then re-point http_catalog_client.py's imports (and every other importer of those names — sweep
them, do not assume this is the only one).

SAME CLASS AS nexus-npywj (make_relative must be relocated, six live importers), and together
these two make the general point worth acting on: THE DELETION LIST WAS ASSEMBLED FROM MODULES,
NOT SYMBOLS. A dying module contains symbols that are not dying. Before the deletion commit,
enumerate the PUBLIC SYMBOLS of each module on the list and check each symbol's live importers
separately. Two instances found by accident during a test port is not a reason to believe there
are only two.

DETECTION NOTE: unlike npywj (whose six importers are all function-local, so nothing catches
it until the path runs), THIS one is a module-level import in a module that is imported
everywhere — so it fails loudly and immediately. That makes it cheaper to find but more total:
it is not a latent bug, it is "the deletion commit does not work at all."
close_reason: Relocated in commit 6e2e8f31: CatalogEntry/CatalogLink moved to nexus/catalog/types.py (merged with RDR-086's ChunkRef module), HttpCatalogClient + all importers re-pointed, Tumbler re-pointed to its canonical home, catalog.py re-exports until deletion. The wider symbol sweep the bead demanded ran as the terminal-deletion pre-flight and its three additional finds (CATALOG_WRITE_OPS, _default_registry_path, synthesizer Event) are on the deletion manifest. Full suite green.

title: by_doc_id asks a DIFFERENT QUESTION on each substrate — local looks up metadata.doc_id, the service client does a tumbler resolve — so it silently returns None in service mode for six live callers including the store_put hook
description:
Found during the nexus-i711w C-store port (commit 0c9a0e97), verified in source.

SAME NAME, SAME SIGNATURE, DIFFERENT QUESTION.

LOCAL (src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py:791-799), docstring "Look up catalog entry by T3
doc_id stored in meta.doc_id":
    SELECT ... FROM documents WHERE json_extract(metadata, '$.doc_id') = ?

SERVICE (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1075-1076), in full:
    def by_doc_id(self, doc_id: str) -> CatalogEntry | None:
        return self.resolve(doc_id)

`resolve()` is a TUMBLER lookup. A T3 doc_id is not a tumbler, so in service mode this
returns None for exactly the inputs the local implementation was written to find. It does not
raise, it does not warn — it answers the wrong question and reports "not found". This
violates the standing no-silent-fallbacks-for-data-correctness directive: the correct
behaviour on a substrate that cannot answer the question is to fail loud, not to return None.

SIX LIVE CALLERS:
  src/nexus/search_engine.py:259        entry = catalog.by_doc_id(did)
  src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:476            entry = cat.by_doc_id(doc_id)
  src/nexus/catalog/store_hook.py:167   existing = reader.by_doc_id(doc_id)
  src/nexus/catalog/store_hook.py:384   entry = reader.by_doc_id(chash_doc_id)
  src/nexus/commands/store.py:359       entry = reader.by_doc_id(doc_id)
  src/nexus/commands/collection.py:35   entry = cat.by_doc_id(doc_id)

THE STORE-HOOK CALL SITE IS THE ALARMING ONE. store_hook.py:167 names its result `existing`
— it is an EXISTENCE / idempotency check performed before registering. A by_doc_id that
always answers None in service mode means the hook concludes "this document is new" for
documents that already exist. Read the surrounding branch before assuming the consequence,
but the shape is: duplicate registration, or a re-register overwriting state that should have
been detected as present.

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, NOT A CLAIM: there is an open P0 for store_put silent data loss
(nexus-b6enc, from the GH #1419 triage). A by_doc_id that silently returns None in service
mode is a mechanism that would produce exactly that class of symptom. Whoever picks up b6enc
should check this seam FIRST — it is cheap to falsify and would explain the symptom without
any new theory. Do not close b6enc as a duplicate of this without testing it; do not assume
they are the same bug either.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: the shape-parity tripwire compares wire shapes, and both arms return
`CatalogEntry | None`, so a null-vs-entry divergence is invisible to it. The behavioural
coverage was local-only.

FIX: either implement the metadata.doc_id lookup service-side (the engine would need the
predicate, so this may need an engine change + tag) or make the client raise
NotImplementedError so the six callers fail loudly instead of silently mis-answering. Choose
deliberately — a raise changes six live call sites' behaviour and needs each one's None-branch
audited first. Silently answering the wrong question is the one option that is not acceptable.
close_reason: Engine fix shipped on develop 96b3d97c (merge d06f8cfc, branch worktree-agent-a7495f323076364cf). Engine suite 1514 passed / 0 failed; Python suite 11531 passed / 0 failed. Stacked-reviewed; every reviewer finding fixed or filed; reviewer-flagged fixes falsified by reverting each one. NOT YET TAGGED — the engine-service tag cut, conexus deploy and cloud gate are Hal's relay, and REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION bumps only AFTER that deploy (GH #1402 ordering).

comments.text: THIRD live confirmation + BLAST RADIUS ESCALATION (2026-07-30, terminal-deletion verification): store_delete's ghost-compensation seam is BROKEN in service mode BY THIS BUG. store_delete_catalog_cleanup (catalog/store_hook.py:359) resolves the doomed row via reader.by_doc_id(chash) — the service client tumbler-resolves, returns None for every chash-shaped id, and the cleanup SILENTLY no-ops (returns clean, no WARNING), leaving the catalog row + manifest outliving the deleted chunks — the exact GH#1419 ghost class nexus-b6enc exists to prevent, now reproduced by tests/test_b6enc_store_put_ghost_compensation.py's deletion pin against the real engine (row ('1.1.1', chunk_count=1) survives a tombstone-FILTERED listDocuments read, proving no delete was ever issued). The pin is now xfail(strict, raises=AssertionError) on THIS bead — fixing by_doc_id flips it loudly. title: make_relative() must be RELOCATED before catalog.py is deleted — six live modules import it from the dying module, all via deferred imports so import-sanity will not catch it
description:
DELETION HAZARD for nexus-i711w. Found during the C-store port (commit 0c9a0e97), verified.

`make_relative()` is defined at src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:329 — a file on the i711w
deletion list. It is pure path arithmetic (abs_path + repo_root -> relative str),
substrate-neutral, and has nothing to do with the SQLite catalog. It just happens to live in
the dying module.

SIX LIVE MODULES IMPORT IT, none of which is going away:
  src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:172, :1200, :1691, :1828   (call sites :229, :1717, :1869)
  src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py:267                        (call sites :288, :292)
  src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:604, :1093            (call sites :619, :1132)
  src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:1841                   (call site :1909)

It is NOT re-exported from nexus/catalog/__init__.py or factory.py — `nexus.catalog.catalog`
is the only import path.

WHAT BREAKS IF IT IS DELETED WITH THE MODULE: document indexing (file_path derivation for
every indexed doc), the MCP catalog surface, `nx catalog` path handling, and `nx doctor`'s
path-fixing pass.

WHY NO GATE WILL CATCH THIS. Every one of the six imports is FUNCTION-LOCAL / deferred
(each carries a `# noqa: PLC0415` circular-dep or startup-cost comment). So the module still
imports cleanly, import-sanity passes, and collection passes. The failure appears only when
the specific code path RUNS. This is precisely the failure mode already recorded on this arc
— a deferred import behind a blanket except produced permanently dead code instead of a
crash, and both import sanity and the neighbourhood passed. The inverse-grep i711w already
plans must therefore cover FUNCTION-LOCAL imports, not just module-level ones; an AST walk
over module-level ImportFrom nodes (which is what the sweep used for the test tree) would
report this file CLEAN.

ACTION: relocate `make_relative` to a surviving module before the deletion commit. It is
substrate-neutral pure path arithmetic, so the natural home is a path/util module with no
catalog dependency — which also removes the six circular-dep deferrals that only exist
because it lives in `catalog.py`. Update the six import sites. It belongs on i711w's SURVIVE
list, not its delete list.

COVERAGE: `TestMakeRelative` in tests/test_catalog_path.py is its ONLY coverage repo-wide.
That test is substrate-neutral and was freed from the hostage import in 0c9a0e97, so it
survives — but it must MOVE with the function, or the relocated function ends up untested.

GENERALISATION WORTH ACTING ON: the deletion list was assembled from modules, not symbols.
Any other substrate-neutral helper sitting in a dying module has the same problem and the
same invisibility. Before the deletion commit, enumerate the PUBLIC SYMBOLS of each dying
module and check each one's live importers separately, rather than assuming the module's
symbols all die with it.
close_reason: Relocated in commit 6e2e8f31: make_relative moved to nexus/catalog/types.py, all six live importers re-pointed, catalog.py re-exports until deletion. Full suite green (12,763 passed).

title: RDR-158 P4: write the 17 service-side contract tests the SQLite deletion would unpin (importer-sweep GAP set)
description:
17 contracts that the SERVICE catalog owes and that NOTHING pins. Each was pinned only by
a test whose MECHANISM dies in nexus-i711w, so the src-deletion commit unpins all 17 unless
these land first.

Found by the nexus-i711w Stage-2 importer sweep (6 parallel classifiers, 342 unpinned tests).
Full context: nexus-i711w's last three comments; T2 [21228]
(`nexus/i711w-importer-sweep-complete-2026-07-29`).

=== WHY THIS IS NOT ORDINARY PORT WORK ===

These are NOT ports (the mechanism that pinned them is dead — local Catalog + EventLog +
Projector) and NOT deletes (the contract survives on the service substrate). The action is
a NEW service-side test. "Port or delete" is a false binary whenever the substrate changes
under a contract.

They are also NOT already covered. Every one was grep-verified against the whole tests/
tree. The recurring trap that made them look covered, hit independently by three
classifiers:
  - tests/catalog/test_http_catalog_client.py LOOKS like the service suite but drives a
    scripted FakeCatalogHandler and asserts WIRE FORMAT, not behaviour.
  - tests/test_catalog_bib_columns.py and tests/test_catalog.py were cited as the
    surviving companions; both are themselves local-only / SQLite-pinned and retire in the
    same commit.
  - Weakest and not evidence at all: "the METHOD EXISTS on HttpCatalogClient."
The only sound citation is a file constructing ActiveCatalog(...) / HttpCatalogClient(...)
against the real engine, i.e. tests/db/test_http_catalog_integration.py.

=== GROUP 1 — WRITABLE NOW (12) ===

All follow register -> mutate -> resolve() against the real service via
tests/_catalog_fixture_ops.ActiveCatalog. Line cites are the DYING test that pinned the
contract, kept so the original assertion can be read before it is deleted.

 1. update() re-derives chunk_count from the manifest when omitted (nexus-zq79 F4).
    Shared code at catalog_writes.py:509-540 runs BEFORE the ES/legacy branch, so the
    behaviour survives; the dying test asserted it only via the event payload.
    was: test_catalog_event_sourced_mutators.py:70
 2. update() respects a caller-supplied chunk_count (does not re-derive).   was: :118
 3. update() refreshes indexed_at when head_hash changes (nexus-zq79 F7). Moderate
    confidence on the contract — verify against the engine before asserting.  was: :155
 4. update() omitting bib_* PRESERVES existing bib_* (nexus-6ha8a).          was: :219
 5. rename_collection() preserves bib_*.                                     was: :420
 6. update_document_collection() preserves bib_*.                            was: :459
 7. update_documents_collection_batch() preserves bib_*.                     was: :486
    NOTE items 5-7 are the strongest of the whole set: grepping all of tests/ for
    `rename_collection|update_document_collection|update_documents_collection_batch`
    combined with `bib_year|bib_authors` returns ONLY the dying file. Three
    collection-mutation verbs whose bib-preservation contract is pinned nowhere else.
 8. delete_document() cascades to the document_chunks manifest purge (nexus-8g79.7).
    The only other cascade test asserts raw-SQL FK cascade at the CatalogDB level, which
    is a different code path and also dying.        was: :272 (duplicate at :319)
 9. register() file_path idempotency — re-registering the same file_path yields the same
    tumbler and no duplicate row.   was: test_catalog_event_sourced_register.py:309
10. Duplicate-link dedup — (from, to, type) collapses to ONE row. The service schema
    has the UNIQUE constraint (test_http_catalog_integration.py:185) and nothing
    exercises it.
11. nexus-7vuw owner name/type coexistence — UNIQUE(tenant_id, name, owner_type) is in
    the schema (test_http_catalog_integration.py:112) but nothing calls register_owner
    TWICE to prove the behaviour. Assert by MEANING: filter list_owners() and count.
    Do NOT use owner_for_repo() — it returns a SINGLE owner and would be structurally
    incapable of observing the duplicate under test.
12. Search still hits after a rename. find() and rename_collection() both survive, but
    nothing exercises the combination against the service; the only tested mechanism is
    SQLite FTS5. Assert: register -> find() hits -> rename_collection -> find() still
    hits, with physical_collection updated.

=== GROUP 2 — LAND AS xfail(strict=True) (5) ===

These pin behaviour that is currently DEFECTIVE service-side. A strict xfail is a real pin:
it fails loudly if the behaviour drifts, and XPASSes — forcing the marker's removal —
exactly when the engine fix lands. Reference the tracking bead in each reason=.

13. T3-GC VERB-LEVEL tombstone safety. Engine defect nexus-mqd6t (chashesForCollection
    has no `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate) is pinned today only at the raw catalog-method
    level: tests/test_catalog_manifest_read_api.py::test_chashes_for_collection_skips_
    deleted_documents (:442-468, already xfail strict). NOTHING drives a tombstoned
    document through the actual `nx t3 gc` verb — every _register_doc test registers live
    docs only. Assertion spec:
      setup:  ActiveCatalog registers doc D in collection C; write_manifest(D, [chash H]);
              T3 holds chunk1 with chunk_text_hash=H and indexed_at older than the window
      guard:  NON-VACUITY — collection count == 1 AND chunk1 present BEFORE the delete
      act:    cat.delete_document(D) to tombstone, then `nx t3 gc -c C --no-dry-run --yes`
      assert: chunk1 NOT in t3_db.get_collection(C).get()["ids"]
      mark:   xfail(strict=True, reason="nexus-mqd6t")
    Placement: co-locate with the existing xfail for tracking locality.
14. supersede_collection SEMANTICS. NO service-side test exists at all — the only one
    asserts `result is None`, i.e. wire shape. Every semantic assertion lives in dying
    local files. This was already designated a Stage-2 EXIT CRITERION before the sweep.
    Currently defective per nexus-cecqy: the engine DELETEs the old collection row
    (renameCollectionTxn step 3, FKs ON UPDATE NO ACTION), so supersede_collection then
    updates 0 rows and the old name ends ABSENT rather than superseded — while the CLI
    still echoes "Emitted CollectionSuperseded". Assert the INTENDED semantics
    (old name present AND marked superseded, superseded_by set) with
    xfail(strict=True, reason="nexus-cecqy").
15. resolve_path repo_root recombination + curator guard -> nexus-5i864. The service
    client (http_catalog_client.py:1150-1152) drops both. Assert: a RELATIVE file_path
    resolves to owner.repo_root / file_path (NOT a CWD-relative path), and a
    curator-owned document resolves to None. xfail(strict=True, reason="nexus-5i864").
    These are the 3 PORT-BLOCKED tests from tests/test_catalog_path.py::TestResolvePath —
    porting them IS this test; they must not be deleted.
16. legacy_grandfathered derivation -> nexus-cecqy. Assert a NON-conformant collection
    name registered through the service path lands legacy_grandfathered=True. Note the
    conformant case is correct-by-accident at the False default, so the test MUST use a
    non-conformant name or it is vacuous. xfail(strict=True, reason="nexus-cecqy").

comments.text:
ITEM 20, added from the test_t3_gc port (commit 085009fe) — and unlike items 1-19 this one
CANNOT be closed by writing a test.

`nx t3 gc` emits ChunkOrphaned events before deleting chunks, and the strict-order contract
(RF-101-3: a crash between event-write and delete leaves the log consistent with T3) was
pinned by three assertions in tests/test_t3_gc.py. Those assertions cannot run on the
service substrate — not because the port was done badly, but because production skips
emission entirely there: src/nexus/commands/t3.py:519-533 does

    cat_dir = getattr(cat, "_dir", None)
    event_log = EventLog(cat_dir) if cat_dir is not None else None

and an HttpCatalogClient / ActiveCatalog has no `_dir`, so it logs gc_event_log_skipped and
emits nothing. There is no service-side observable to assert against.

CONSEQUENCE: on the substrate that is about to become the only one, a DESTRUCTIVE command
deletes T3 chunks with NO audit record of what it deleted, and after the SQLite deletion
nothing in the suite will assert anything about it. The three assertions are preserved in
the file and still pass if it is pinned to sqlite, and the DIE test's docstring now says
explicitly that the strict-order contract is uncovered on the service arm, so its green is
not mistaken for coverage.

This is the same hole nexus-jqrtp names from the other direction. jqrtp is about the missing
`make_catalog_reader() is None` abort guard — the last line of defence BEFORE the delete.
This is the missing record AFTER it. Both sit on the same destructive verb on the same
substrate.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS: this needs a product decision on a service-side audit surface for
destructive T3 operations first; the test follows. Do NOT attempt to satisfy item 20 by
writing a test against the current code — there is nothing to observe, and an
xfail(strict=True) here would be asserting that we intend to have no audit trail. Raise the
surface question with Hal rather than closing this silently.

title: HttpCatalogClient.resolve_path drops repo_root recombination + curator guard — reintroduces the nexus-3e4s CWD-anchoring class and silently zeroes the auto-linker in service mode
description:
HttpCatalogClient.resolve_path drops BOTH the repo_root recombination and the curator
guard, silently reintroducing the nexus-3e4s CWD-anchoring class in service mode and
silently zeroing the auto-linker.

Found during the nexus-i711w Stage-2 importer sweep (sweep-D-collections), verified in
source independently. NOT a test-only issue — this is live service-mode behaviour.

=== THE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS ===

LOCAL (src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py:462-503+), documented resolution order:
  1. resolve(tumbler); None -> None
  2. owner lookup by tumbler.owner_address()
  3. owner_type == "curator" -> None          <-- guard
  4. file_path absolute -> return it
  5. owner.repo_root non-empty -> Path(owner.repo_root) / entry.file_path   <-- recombination
  6. else DEBUG catalog_resolve_path_legacy_owner_missing_repo_root, return None

SERVICE (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1150-1152), in full:
    def resolve_path(self, tumbler):
        entry = self.resolve(tumbler)
        return Path(entry.file_path) if entry and entry.file_path else None

Steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 are simply absent.

=== WHY THIS IS THE nexus-3e4s CLASS ===

The catalog hook always passes a RELATIVE file_path. nexus-3e4s was exactly this: a
relative path anchored on the process CWD instead of the owner's repo_root, which
contaminated ~6,500 rows in the live catalog. The local fix anchors on owner.repo_root.
The service client returns the relative Path unchanged, so the CALLER anchors it on CWD.
Same defect, one layer further out, and it has no register-time guard behind it because
the guard added for 3e4s was on the write path.

=== OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE: THE AUTO-LINKER SILENTLY EMITS NOTHING ===

Both consumers (src/nexus/catalog/link_generator.py:131 and :219) do:
    resolved = cat.resolve_path(<tumbler>)
    if resolved is None or not resolved.is_file():
        continue
So in service mode, run from any CWD that is not the repo root:
  - is_file() is False for every entry -> every iteration continues -> ZERO links
    generated, no error, no warning, no log. Indistinguishable from "nothing to link".
  - WORSE, if the CWD does contain a same-named relative path, read_text() reads the
    WRONG FILE and the generator emits links derived from unrelated text. Wrong links
    are worse than no links: they enter the catalog as real edges.
This violates the standing directive against silent fallbacks for data-correctness
problems (FAIL LOUD). Currently it fails silent in the None branch and fails WRONG in
the collision branch.

=== SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME THREE LINES ===

The curator guard is gone, so curator-owned documents (PDFs, standalone docs) are now
resolvable in service mode when the contract says they must return None. The linker will
read_text() a PDF and scan the mojibake for file paths.

=== FIX ===

Port the local resolution order into HttpCatalogClient.resolve_path. Both missing inputs
are already reachable: owner_type and repo_root come from the owner the client can fetch
by tumbler.owner_address() (HttpCatalogClient already has owner read APIs). Do NOT
"fix" this in link_generator — the defect is in the client method, and a caller-side
workaround leaves the next consumer exposed.

=== TEST STATE (why nobody caught it) ===

resolve_path has SOLE coverage repo-wide: tests/test_catalog_path.py::TestResolvePath,
which exercises the LOCAL implementation only. Those tests are in the i711w unpinned
importer set and are currently classified PORT-BLOCKED precisely because the service
client cannot satisfy them. So the sweep would have deleted or stalled the only pin on a
live defect. Porting them IS the regression test for this bead; they must not be deleted.
close_reason: Fixed on develop 112337bb: ported the local resolution order (owner lookup -> curator guard -> absolute passthrough -> repo_root recombination -> DEBUG+None for legacy owners) into HttpCatalogClient.resolve_path, with a HITS-ONLY per-instance owner cache (a cached miss would pin owner-absent for the life of the process singleton and reintroduce the silent-zero-links class this bead exists to remove). The bead's named regression tests (tests/test_catalog_path.py::TestResolvePath, 3 strict xfails) are live again, plus 7 further 5i864 pins in tests/test_link_generator.py that surfaced only as XPASS(strict) under a full run, plus 5 service-mode link-generator tests whose fake server gained an /owners/show route (the fix makes owner presence a hard precondition of resolve_path). Fix stayed in the client method, NOT link_generator, per the bead. Mutation-falsified. Full suite 11529 passed / 0 failed. FORWARD NOTE for nexus-ekaxn: resolve_path derives owner_prefix from the INPUT tumbler (faithful to the deleted local impl); if alias-following makes resolve() cross owner boundaries, that lookup would use the alias's owner, not the canonical target's.

title: link_audit returns {} in service mode while nx catalog link-audit and the MCP catalog_link_audit tool still ship — the verb silently reports nothing
description:
Found by classifying tests for the nexus-i711w C-store port (2026-07-29).

HttpCatalogClient.link_audit is a one-line stub:

    src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1665-1666
      def link_audit(self, *, t3: Any = None) -> dict:
          return {}  # not supported in initial service-mode implementation

Meanwhile the verb SHIPS on both surfaces:
  - `nx catalog link-audit` (commands/catalog_cmds/links.py, hidden but present)
  - MCP tool `catalog_link_audit` (src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py)

So in service mode — which is every mode after nexus-i711w — an operator running
the audit gets an empty dict. Not an error, not "unsupported": empty. Callers
that read `["total"]`, `["orphaned_count"]`, or `["stale_chash_count"]` see
absence, which reads as "clean".

That is the silent-false-clean shape this project has been burned by before
(cf. nexus-ou4tb, where unreadable collections were folded in as "no ghosts").

=== WHY IT SURFACED NOW ===

Three tests in tests/test_catalog_e2e.py are blocked on it and could not be
classified DIE or PORT:
  TestMCP::test_link_audit_after_indexing        (total==2, orphaned_count==0)
  TestChashSpan::test_audit_detects_bogus_hash   (stale_chash_count==1)
  TestLinks::test_delete_document_orphan_preserved (orphaned_count==1 — this one
    is portable by expressing orphan-preservation through resolve + links_to)

They are the only e2e coverage of the audit verb. Deleting them as "local
machinery" would be the wrong reading: the concept is not retired, the
implementation is deferred. The comment says so in as many words.

=== THE DECISION THIS NEEDS ===

Either:
  (a) implement it — a /v1/catalog/link_audit route plus the client method, at
      which point the three tests PORT unchanged; or
  (b) retire the verb deliberately — remove the CLI verb and the MCP tool so it
      cannot silently mislead, and let the tests die with it.

What must NOT happen is the current state persisting past i711w: a shipping verb
whose service-mode implementation returns {} while the only tests that would
notice are deleted for being "local".

Minimum acceptable interim if neither is done before the cut: make the stub
RAISE or return an explicit unsupported marker, so a caller cannot read empty as
clean. That is a client-side one-liner and needs no engine tag.
close_reason: FIXED on develop a62649ef. link_audit no longer returns {}. It is computed from reads the engine already serves — paginated /link_query with no filters for total/by_type/by_creator/duplicates, plus /links/orphaned (nexus-ysrwi) for orphans — so NO engine change was needed and it works on the current floor. The empty dict was not graceful degradation: 'nx catalog link-audit --json' printed {} which reads as a CLEAN audit, and the non-json path KeyError'd on result['total']; the MCP tool reported success-shaped emptiness. That is the silent-false-clean shape nexus-ou4tb already burned us with. The inverted pin in tests/test_catalog_mcp.py::test_link_audit (which asserted result == {} and asked for 'the unconditional assertion' back when fixed) fired on this change exactly as designed and is restored to real assertions: total == 1, by_type['cites'] == 1, orphaned_count == len(orphaned). New client-side coverage in tests/catalog/test_http_catalog_client.py::TestLinkAuditIsNoLongerAStub asserts every key the CLI and MCP consumers read is present. Full suite 11538 / 0. NOTE the 't3' kwarg is accepted and ignored — the local implementation used it for a stale-chash cross-check against T3 that this substrate answers from the manifest; kept in the signature for call-site parity, documented in the docstring.

title: service-mode rename silently breaks the supersede contract: engine DELETEs the old collection row, supersede_collection then updates 0 rows, CLI still echoes 'Emitted CollectionSuperseded'
description:
Found by classifying tests for the nexus-i711w C-store port (2026-07-29).
VERIFIED IN THE JAVA SOURCE, not inferred from test failures.

=== THE DIVERGENCE ===

`nx catalog rename-collection` in SERVICE mode:

1. CatalogRepository.renameCollectionTxn (service/.../CatalogRepository.java
   ~2400-2444) implements rename as INSERT-new -> re-home children ->
   **DELETE the old registry row** (step 3, key `catalog_collections_deleted`,
   line 2442-2443). It must delete rather than UPDATE because the fk-002/fk-003
   collection FKs are ON UPDATE NO ACTION.

2. The CLI then calls `writer.supersede_collection(old, new)`
   (commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:341). That lands on
   CatalogRepository.supersedeCollection (:2292), a plain
   `UPDATE catalog_collections ... WHERE name = old`.

3. The old row no longer exists, so the UPDATE affects ZERO rows.
   HttpCatalogClient.supersede_collection discards the rowcount, so nothing
   raises and nothing warns.

NET SERVICE-MODE SEMANTICS: after a rename the old name is ABSENT, not
marked-superseded. Locally it is marked-superseded and the row survives.

=== WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS ===

- The CLI echoes "Emitted CollectionSuperseded(...)" (collections.py:370) — in
  service mode that is a claim about something that did not happen.
- The verb's own docstring (:224-225) says it "keeps the event log and
  projection in sync". In service mode there is no event log and the
  projection row is gone.
- Anything that reads `superseded_by` / `superseded_at` to discover a rename's
  history gets nothing. The rename is unauditable after the fact.

=== SECOND DEFECT, SAME VERB (fold or split as you prefer) ===

`--allow-legacy` is documented (collections.py:210-212) as "still gets a row in
the projection but is flagged legacy_grandfathered=True". In service mode it is
NOT flagged:
  - locally the flag is DERIVED by regex (catalog/catalog.py:1501,
    `legacy_grandfathered = not is_conformant_collection_name(name)`)
  - the engine does NO inference: upsertCollection binds
    `ni(i(coll,"legacy_grandfathered"), 0)` (CatalogRepository.java:2171)
  - HttpCatalogClient.register_collection defaults the kwarg False (:1681)
  - the CLI's non-conformant branch calls register_collection(new) with no
    kwarg (collections.py:340)
Smallest fix: pass the derived flag at collections.py:340.

=== TEST IMPACT (why this surfaced now) ===

tests/test_catalog_rename_collection.py::test_rename_conformant_new_succeeds
asserts `old_row["superseded_by"] == new` and `old_row["superseded_at"]`. Those
two assertions cannot be ported — not because the test is wrong, but because
the PRODUCT diverges. The honest port replaces them with
`assert catalog.get_collection(old) is None` and points here.

Also: supersede_collection SEMANTICS have no service-side test at all. The only
one (test_http_catalog_client.py::test_supersede_collection) asserts
`result is None` — wire shape, not behaviour. Every semantic assertion lives in
local-catalog files that die with i711w. Treat "supersede has a service-side
semantic test" as a Stage-2 exit criterion.

ENGINE-SIDE FIX = second release lifecycle (engine tag + conexus deploy). The
--allow-legacy half is client-side and can ship with the PyPI release.
close_reason:
FIXED on develop, commit 1d854b7a. Both halves of this bead plus the scope correction.

THE RENAME (engine). renameCollectionTxn step 3 changed from DELETE to a superseded
tombstone: superseded_by = newName, superseded_at = now(). The delete was never required
-- by step 3 every RESTRICT child has re-homed onto Y, so X is childless -- and it was
what made the CLI's paired supersede a zero-row no-op it nonetheless announced.

Alive-but-unmarked was rejected as the alternative and the reasoning is on the code: X and
Y share the (content_type, owner_id, embedding_model) tuple, and collectionForTuple picks
`superseded_by = '' ORDER BY name DESC LIMIT 1`, so an unmarked X wins whenever it sorts
above Y (renaming to fix a typo: code__zold__... -> code__anew__...) and takes every
subsequent write to the emptied old name.

Two consequences closed so the tombstone is coherent, both found by running the tests:
  - the branch predicate is now a LIVE target, so a round-trip rename sees the tombstone
    and takes the canonical branch (not the RDR-162 COPY branch, which would repoint
    documents and strand the chunks), and step 1 became an upsert that REVIVES it;
  - upsertCollection revives too, so re-creating a collection under a retired name is not
    silently unreachable (collectionForTuple skips superseded rows, and doctor
    --collections-drift deliberately permits a superseded row to have no T3 collection,
    so nothing would have reported it).

THE FLAG, and why the client half shipped on 266a13c0 was INERT. Derivation moved into
HttpCatalogClient.register_collection per the scope-correction comment, covering all three
bare-else sites. That alone still changed nothing: CatalogRepository.i() coerced only
Number, and the client sends a real JSON boolean, so the value was replaced by the
ni(..., 0) default and legacy_grandfathered could NEVER be set through /collections/upsert
by ANY caller, explicit kwarg or derived. i() now coerces Boolean. The hermetic wire test
could not see this; the engine-backed item-16 pin did.

Also fixed here: migrate-fallback's unguarded supersede call (would now abort a completed
migration with a traceback) and its unconditional "source superseded by X" echo.

PINS, all previously strict-xfail, now live:
  tests/db/test_i711w_gap_xfails.py item 14 (5 tests) and item 16
  tests/test_catalog_backfill_collections.py::test_backfill_marks_legacy_via_projector
  service CatalogHandlerRenameTest (supersede + tombstone, 7 new), CatalogRepositoryTest
  (revive), CatalogRenameCollectionTest / CollectionRegistryFkTest (tombstone assertions)

Mutation-verified in both directions: reverting the tombstone fails exactly the three
tests that assert it; stripping the guards fails exactly the five guard pins.

Engine 1530 tests / 0 failures. Python 11559 passed / 0 failures.

DEPLOY DEPENDENCY: the engine half is on develop but reaches users only via an
engine-service tag + conexus deploy. Until then the tombstone and the flag behave as
before in the cloud. The client half is safe ahead of that deploy: against the current
engine the new 404/409 statuses never occur, the boolean is dropped exactly as it is
today, and the CLI's zero-row branch already says plainly that the engine still deletes
the old row.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION to the legacy_grandfathered half: the recorded "smallest fix at
collections.py:340" is TOO NARROW and would leave the defect live on two other paths.

Found during the nexus-i711w importer sweep (sweep-D-collections), then verified directly.

The diagnosis on this bead is right — client defaults the kwarg False (http_catalog_client.py:1681),
engine does no inference (CatalogRepository.java:2171), CLI passes no kwarg. What is wrong is
the FIX LOCATION. Every call site follows the same shape:

    if is_conformant_collection_name(name):
        register_collection(name, content_type=..., owner_id=..., embedding_model=...)
    else:
        register_collection(name)          # <-- bare, and this is the non-conformant branch

and there are THREE bare-else sites, not one:
    src/nexus/indexer.py:791                          w.register_collection(conformant)
    src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:138  writer.register_collection(name)
    src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:340  writer.register_collection(new)

Only :340 is named on this bead. The bare branch is BY CONSTRUCTION the non-conformant
one, so it is exactly where legacy_grandfathered must be True — meaning all three sites
are defective in service mode, and the two unnamed ones are reached by the ordinary
`nx index` path (indexer.py:791 is the post-rename registration) and the collections
backfill loop (:138), not by --allow-legacy at all.

Note the defect is invisible on the conformant branch: legacy_grandfathered =
not is_conformant_collection_name(name), so conformant names want False and the kwarg
default is False. Correct by accident. That is why this reads as an --allow-legacy-only
bug when it is not.

RECOMMENDED FIX, replacing the collections.py:340 one-liner: derive the flag inside
HttpCatalogClient.register_collection, mirroring local Catalog.register_collection:1501
(`legacy_grandfathered = not is_conformant_collection_name(name)`) when the caller did
not pass it explicitly. One site, covers all three callers plus any future one, and it
puts the derivation on the same side of the boundary as the local implementation it is
supposed to be at parity with. Patching call sites instead leaves the next caller exposed
— the same shape as the daemon-lifecycle rule about fixing the shared primitive rather
than one tier's copy.

Keep the explicit kwarg for the case where a caller must force the flag.

TEST IMPACT: 2 tests in tests/test_catalog_collections.py are PORT-BLOCKED on this
(sweep-D). They become the regression test once the fix lands.

title: no test-isolation guard for the SERVICE catalog — the whole local isolation file goes vacuous when i711w lands
description:
Found while porting tests/test_catalog_isolation.py off the local catalog
(nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage C-store). The file is left PINNED and unported
deliberately; porting it would have hidden this.

WHAT THE FILE GUARDS TODAY. RDR-060 (2026-04-08) added conftest's autouse
`_isolate_catalog` after 64 orphan `int-cce-*` curator owners accumulated in
Hal's REAL catalog from one integration test. tests/test_catalog_isolation.py
is the regression suite for that fixture (nexus-dqr3 / nexus-b34f): writes must
land in the per-test tmp catalog, never in ~/.config/nexus/catalog/.

WHY IT STOPS GUARDING ANYTHING:

1. test_initialized_tmp_catalog_receives_writes_not_user_home asserts via a raw
   sqlite3.connect on the tmp `.catalog.db` that the hook's owner row landed
   there. In service mode the hook writes to the SERVICE catalog and that local
   file stays empty, so the assertion is unsatisfiable — it is the only test in
   the file that fails when unpinned.

2. test_user_real_catalog_untouched_by_leak_pattern — the belt-and-braces guard
   that actually runs the historical leak pattern — compares mtimes of
   ~/.config/nexus/catalog/{owners.jsonl,.catalog.db} and `pytest.skip`s when
   that directory does not exist. After i711w nobody has one, so it skips
   unconditionally. A guard that always skips is not a guard.

3. `_isolate_catalog` itself works by pointing NEXUS_CATALOG_PATH at a tmp dir
   and relying on `Catalog.is_initialized(cat_path)` being False so hooks return
   early. Both halves of that mechanism are local-catalog concepts.

THE GAP: nothing in tests/ asserts that a test run cannot write into the
operator's real SERVICE catalog. I grepped for a tenant/service isolation
fixture and found none. The original incident was 64 junk owners in a live
catalog; the service-mode version of that incident is the same junk in
Postgres, and this session already produced one instance of the class — a
badly isolated probe wrote a junk entry into the live CLOUD store (found,
deleted, verified gone; recorded in the 2026-07-29 continuation doc).

WHAT IS NEEDED (design, not decided here): an autouse guard that makes the
service catalog per-test-safe — a dedicated test tenant, or an assertion that
the resolved service endpoint is never the operator's configured one. Whatever
the shape, it has to exist BEFORE the local isolation tests are deleted, or the
deletion silently removes the only coverage of a defect class that has already
fired twice.

SEQUENCING: this blocks deleting tests/test_catalog_isolation.py, which in turn
is part of the i711w C-store test disposition. It does not block the src
deletion.
