title: engine catalog reads miss the tombstone filter: chashesForCollection leaks deleted docs into T3 GC, docsForChashes attributes search hits to deleted docs
description:
FOUND BY PORTING A TEST off the local catalog (nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage
C-store). Not a port artifact — two engine-side reads genuinely lack the
soft-delete filter, and they are MISSED SIBLINGS of a fix already made.

nexus-23wlw (2026-07-26) fixed exactly this class: "the service TOMBSTONED it
and documentsByCollection -- along with twenty sibling reads -- had no
deleted_at IS NULL filter". That sweep was narrower than it looked: the whole
Java tree contains only THREE occurrences of `deleted_at IS NULL`.

=== BUG 1: CatalogRepository.chashesForCollection (~line 1916) ===
Joins CATALOG_DOCUMENTS but filters only on PHYSICAL_COLLECTION. A tombstoned
document's chunks stay in the returned chash set.

  CONSUMER: src/nexus/commands/t3.py:431 -- `referenced =
  cat.chashes_for_collection(collection)`, the T3 GC alive-set. Also
  indexer.py:2617.
  IMPACT: GC treats a deleted document's chunks as still-referenced and never
  collects them. Vectors for deleted documents leak permanently. Fail-SAFE
  direction (no data loss), but `nx t3 gc` silently under-collects forever.

=== BUG 2: CatalogRepository.docsForChashes (~line 1931) ===
Worse: does not join CATALOG_DOCUMENTS AT ALL, so there is nothing to filter.

  CONSUMER: src/nexus/search_engine.py:104 -- `chash_to_docs =
  catalog.docs_for_chashes(nonempty)`, which maps result chunks back to their
  documents. Also mcp/core.py:2421, indexer_utils.py:428, embed_migrate.py:212.
  IMPACT: USER-VISIBLE. A search hit can be attributed to a document the user
  deleted. This is the more serious of the two.

=== REPRODUCTION ===
tests/test_catalog_manifest_read_api.py::TestChashesForCollection::
test_chashes_for_collection_skips_deleted_documents -- register a doc, write
its manifest, delete_document(), then read chashes_for_collection(). SQLite
returns an empty set (it hard-deletes); the service returns the chash. The test
is currently xfail(strict=True) referencing this bead; a fix makes it XPASS and
fails the suite, which is the intended forcing function.

=== WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE ===
The test was pinned to `local_catalog_backend`, so it only ever ran against
SQLite, whose hard-delete made the assertion pass for a substrate reason rather
than a behavioural one. This is the third instance this arc of a test passing
for a reason nobody wrote down, and the second where deleting the SQLite path
is what exposed it.

FIX: add the deleted_at IS NULL predicate to both reads (and audit the rest of
CatalogRepository for the same omission -- three occurrences repo-wide strongly
suggests more). Engine change => engine-service tag + conexus deploy, i.e. the
second release lifecycle, not the PyPI one.
close_reason: Engine fix shipped on develop 96b3d97c (merge d06f8cfc, branch worktree-agent-a7495f323076364cf). Engine suite 1514 passed / 0 failed; Python suite 11531 passed / 0 failed. Stacked-reviewed; every reviewer finding fixed or filed; reviewer-flagged fixes falsified by reverting each one. NOT YET TAGGED — the engine-service tag cut, conexus deploy and cloud gate are Hal's relay, and REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION bumps only AFTER that deploy (GH #1402 ordering).

The 23wlw carve-out covers only the write-path helper, not this read. Add to this bead's engine fix set alongside chashesForCollection + docsForChashes. Pinned by the item-8 strict xfail in tests/db/test_i711w_gap_contracts.py.

Pin with one test when this bead's engine fix lands. title: mode-lint exclusion sets had no liveness check — 21/58 nodeids and 4/73 files were dead
description:
The RDR-109 mode-lint exclusion sets (`_MODE_LINT_EXCLUDE_NODEIDS`,
`_MODE_LINT_EXCLUDE_FILES` in tests/conftest.py) were guarded only by
`len(set) == CEILING`. Nothing checked that an entry still resolved to a
real test, which produced two failures:

LOUD: a rename silently downgrades a granted exclusion into a
non-exclusion. 9c0cff18 renamed the taxonomy tripwire test out from under
its entry; the lint went red on develop and stayed red, because it only
fires on a whole-session collection and the authoring runs were
path-scoped.

QUIET (the worse one): a deletion leaves a dead slot that still satisfies
the count. 88d91bd5 (RDR-155 P4b P2, Chroma migration machinery) orphaned
21 of 58 nodeid entries and 4 of 73 file entries. Because the ceiling
asserts EXACT equality, each dead slot was a free exclusion a later edit
could swap into with no bump and no rationale -- precisely the
grandfathering the ratchet exists to prevent. That hole was open from
2026-07-25 to 2026-07-29.

FIXED (this bead): two liveness assertions in
tests/test_mode_declarations_are_explicit.py --
`test_mode_lint_exclude_nodeids_all_resolve` and
`..._files_all_resolve`. Filesystem + AST, deliberately NOT
collection-based: a collection-based check would inherit the same
whole-session blind spot that hid both incidents, and would call almost
every entry dead under a path-scoped run. Validates nodeid SHAPE too
(file::test vs file::Class::test), so a method addressed as a two-part
nodeid is caught.

Burned down all 25 dead entries; ceilings 58 -> 37 and 73 -> 69. All 21
nodeids verified GONE rather than moved (no surviving definition of any
of those names under tests/), so every one was a clean drop.

Falsified by mutation, 4/4 caught, and in every case the COUNT ratchet
passed while only the liveness test failed -- which is the whole point:
  M1 dead-slot swap (count unchanged)     -> caught
  M2 bogus class segment                  -> caught
  M3 dead FILES basename (count unchanged)-> caught
  M4 method addressed as 2-part nodeid    -> caught

GENERALISABLE: any allowlist/denylist guarded by a count has this hole.
Worth checking the other census/baseline constants in this repo for the
same "counts entries, never validates they resolve" shape.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP on the "GENERALISABLE" note in the description: I checked, and the
answer is NO -- the mode-lint ratchet was the OUTLIER, not an instance of a
widespread pattern. Do not spend time sweeping for more.

Every other census in the repo is already BIDIRECTIONAL, i.e. it fails on a
stale entry rather than only on growth:

  DDL_CENSUS / ALTER_CENSUS / EPSILON_CENSUS (tests/test_no_new_sqlite.py)
    _census_delta compares over `live.keys() | census.keys()`, so a deleted
    file gives live=0 < census -> `shrunk` -> FAIL ("stale census count").
    This is exactly what forced the taxonomy_cmd.py 17 -> 3 lowering in the
    sub-stage C commit.

  PRIVATE_HANDLE_CENSUS (tests/test_private_handle_access_census.py)
    has an explicit test_census_has_no_stale_entries with the same shape.

File-keyed ALLOWLISTs (test_no_chash_truncation, http_vector_client_factory_
lint, changelog_rls_lint, release_artifact_verb_rot) reference no dead paths
today; the single apparent hit was the glob "tests/e2e/**/*.sh", not a
literal path.

So the distinguishing defect was specific: the mode-lint sets were guarded by
a ONE-SIDED count (len == CEILING) where every sibling ledger is two-sided.
The liveness tests bring it up to the standard the rest of the repo already
held.

title: TestT3StepsThroughLadderLedger depends on a deleted side effect — re-ground its version gate in RDR-158 P4 sub-stage A
description:
Handed forward from nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage C (Hal decision 2026-07-29). Two tests, xfail(strict) until this lands:

  tests/test_upgrade_cmd.py::TestT3StepsThroughLadderLedger
      ::test_step_completion_recorded_and_skipped_on_rerun
      ::test_failed_step_records_nothing_and_force_retries_it

WHAT BROKE. The class exists to test the T3 ladder block and deliberately does not exercise the T2 migration chain. It never actually skipped that chain — it relied on an UNDECLARED side effect: opening a T2Database on the test path ran the T2 migrations because CatalogTaxonomy's constructor bootstrapped its own tables, leaving the DB current before nx upgrade was invoked. Sub-stage C deletes CatalogTaxonomy, the side effect goes, and upgrade.py now genuinely applies 40 T2 migrations inside these two tests.

THE STATED SKIP HAS NEVER WORKED. _run patches nexus.db.migrations.MIGRATIONS to []. upgrade.py binds it with 'from nexus.db.migrations import MIGRATIONS' at import time, so rebinding the source module never reaches upgrade.py's pending_t2 computation (upgrade.py:611). The patch is inert for this purpose and always was.

DO NOT re-target that patch at nexus.commands.upgrade.MIGRATIONS. It DEADLOCKS — with pending empty, _run_upgrade holds t2_migration_flock and then constructs a T2Database whose bootstrap_schema opens the same lock file on a second fd. See nexus-f20el. Two runs sat for 48+ minutes at ~2s CPU before this was understood.

FIVE ATTEMPTS FAILED, recorded so the next person does not repeat them (baseline is 2 failures; each of these made it worse):
  1. patch nexus.commands.upgrade.MIGRATIONS          -> deadlock, forever
  2. hand-stamp schema_meta/schema_version            -> 3 failures (wrong table)
  3. hand-stamp _nexus_version/cli_version            -> 3 failures
  4. patch T2Database.bootstrap_schema to a no-op     -> 2 failures, chain still ran
     (upgrade.py calls apply_pending DIRECTLY, not via bootstrap_schema)
  5. bootstrap_version + apply_pending in setup       -> 6 failures

WHY SUB-STAGE A. The real fix is in upgrade.py's version gating (pending_t2 / apply_pending / the _nexus_version seed), which is the same surface sub-stage A retires along with the SQLite stores and db/migrations.py. Fixing it inside a CatalogTaxonomy deletion is scope bleed in the wrong direction, and the flow is not understood well enough to patch safely from here.

ACCEPTANCE: remove the xfail markers. strict=True means a fix makes them XPASS and FAIL the suite, so they cannot silently outlive the problem.

Refs nexus-i711w, nexus-f20el
close_reason:
RESOLVED BY DELETION — closing on evidence, 2026-07-31. The subject no longer exists, and neither does the mechanism the bead was written to work around.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE, not inferred:
  - src/nexus/db/migrations.py: DOES NOT EXIST (deleted in RDR-158 P4 Stage 4, commit 7dcecfd2, along with bootstrap_schema and _run_upgrade's local leg). So `nexus.db.migrations.MIGRATIONS` — the binding this bead's whole analysis turns on — is gone, and there is no T2 migration chain left for these tests to accidentally run.
  - `MIGRATIONS` appears NOWHERE in src/nexus/commands/upgrade.py.
  - TestT3StepsThroughLadderLedger no longer exists: `pytest ...::TestT3StepsThroughLadderLedger` reports "not found ... no match in any of [<Module test_upgrade_cmd.py>]".
  - tests/test_upgrade_cmd.py's own module docstring records the disposition: "the classes that drove it (TestUpgradeCommand, TestT3StepsThroughLadderLedger — already deleted at Stage 3 — plus TestT3UpgradeStep and the T3-step short-circuit pin) are gone with their subject. What survives is the whole verb surface on this version: the service no-op message, the frozen-source non-mutation, and the stranded =sqlite export redirect."

So the two xfail(strict) tests this bead was meant to un-xfail are not xfailed — they are DELETED, deliberately, as part of the same arc that removed what they tested. There is nothing left to re-ground.

THE FIVE FAILED ATTEMPTS AND THE DEADLOCK WARNING STAY VALUABLE and are preserved above rather than being lost with the close: the deadlock (patching nexus.commands.upgrade.MIGRATIONS while _run_upgrade held t2_migration_flock, then constructing a T2Database whose bootstrap_schema opened the same lock file on a second fd — nexus-f20el, two runs sat 48+ minutes at ~2s CPU) is a real hazard class, even though both the flock and bootstrap_schema are themselves now deleted. Anyone re-encountering "patch a module-level binding that the consumer imported at import time" should read this bead's history: the inert-patch finding generalises well past this case, and bit again in a DIFFERENT test on 2026-07-31 (three separate probe_collection_state bindings needed patching in tests/test_catalog_rename_collection.py).

Fourth stale bead retired this session on the same pattern — a bead describing a world where SQLite still existed. Siblings: nexus-16f77 (--force already shipped in March), nexus-uvn3t (script already deleted), nexus-senub (re-scoped, its mechanism was FTS5's).

title: t2_handle fails loud in SQLite mode while MCP still writes SQLite — decide the CLI/MCP asymmetry
description:
Raised by the substantive-critic pass on nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage B (it called this a Critical; the diagnosis is confirmed, the prescribed fix is NOT available to an implementer — see below).

STATE AFTER SUB-STAGE B, on a box with NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite (the RDR-152 copy-not-move rollback lever):

  nx memory list/get/put/search   -> exit 1, ClickException  (commands/_helpers.py t2_handle)
  nx config / nx remediation      -> same, they share t2_handle
  MCP memory_put / scratch_put    -> SUCCEEDS, writes SQLite  (mcp_infra.t2_ctx, unconditional T2Database)
  nx index repo (T2 index write)  -> SUCCEEDS, writes SQLite  (mcp_infra.t2_index_write SQLite arm)
  nx plan                         -> SUCCEEDS, opens T2 directly

Verified by execution by the critic: 'NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite nx memory list' exits 1 while t2_ctx().memory.put() on the same config dir succeeds.

So the fail-loud's stated rationale — 'rather than quietly opening a second unarbitrated writer' — does not hold: unarbitrated writers already exist on the MCP side and were deliberately preserved in the same commit. The CLI raise removes function without buying the arbitration safety it names.

WHY IT WAS NOT SIMPLY FIXED. The critic's recommendation was to open a direct T2Database with an epsilon-allow mirroring t2_index_write. That is a NEW raw-SQLite site: pre-retirement t2_handle held a T2Client, never a connection. tests/test_no_new_sqlite.py's EPSILON_CENSUS fails on ANY upward move, and its directive text is explicit: 'Raising a count in this census requires an explicit Hal decision recorded on a bead, referenced inline.' Same for a read-only variant. So both of the critic's options need a Hal decision.

THE FORK (Hal's call):
  a) Accept the fail-loud. SQLite-mode CLI is dead until sub-stage A; document it as such. Cheapest, and consistent with no-new-SQLite. Cost: the rollback lever is half-functional exactly while sub-stage C — the 'attempt to write a readonly database' cohort — is the sub-stage most likely to need it.
  b) Let t2_handle's SQLite arm delegate to the GRANDFATHERED mcp_infra.t2_ctx arm. No new census entry (reuses an existing epsilon-allow), restores CLI function, makes CLI and MCP consistent. Cost: a commands/ -> mcp_infra layering import, and it does make the second-writer situation explicit rather than merely actual.
  c) Raise the census by 1 with an explicit decision recorded here and referenced inline, per the directive's own escape hatch.

DONE IN THE REVIEW-FIX COMMIT (not the fork itself):
  - the in-code justification was rewritten. It previously read 'The branch itself goes with storage_mode in sub-stage A, at which point the SERVICE path above becomes unconditional' — the exact scope-bleed reasoning the staged deletion forbids (deletion-discipline rule 2). It now states the real constraint (no-new-SQLite) and names this bead.
  - the message now says reads are blocked too, and names nx config; it previously said only 'arbitrated SQLite-mode writes'.
  - test coverage added (there was none: not the exit code, not the one-liner-not-traceback contract, not the hint).

Sub-stage A subsumes this if it lands first — at that point the SERVICE path becomes unconditional and the branch disappears. This bead exists because C runs BEFORE A.
close_reason: moot: probe (implementer + reviewer + critic, independently) confirms both SQLite arms deleted post-i711w — t2_handle and mcp t2_ctx unconditionally service-backed; no asymmetry remains to decide

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RESOLVED (a) — Hal, 2026-07-28. Commit 588bbd85 on develop.

DECISION: accept the fail-loud. Hal's framing was 'what leads us to the path of
eliminating SQLite — it can't be creating a new store, right?' Correct: (c) is
out by definition. And (b) is out for the same reason one rung down — reusing
the grandfathered mcp_infra arm adds a commands/ -> mcp_infra import that
sub-stage A must then unpick. It invests in the substrate we are deleting.
(a) adds nothing and the branch goes whole in A.

THE BEAD OVERSTATED THE COST, and this is now measured rather than argued.
'The rollback lever is half-functional exactly while sub-stage C needs it' is
not right: migrating FORWARD never touches t2_handle.
  - nx upgrade / nx doctor construct T2Database directly (epsilon-allow)
  - tests/e2e/t2-migration-sqlite/rehearse_t2.sh, the SQLite-mode E2E gate,
    drives exactly those two verbs and nothing else — unaffected
  - seed_legacy.py and rehearse_hole_punch.sh open T2Database in-process
No gate exercises the fail-loud path. What is dead is interactive browsing of a
SQLite-mode store, not the rollback lever.

BLAST RADIUS WAS UNDERCOUNTED HERE TOO: t2_handle has FOUR callers, not the two
this bead listed — memory.py, config_cmd.py, remediation_cmd.py AND
service_cmd.py. The message named only nx memory and nx config, so nx
remediation / nx service would have read as an unrelated bug. All four now
named, and the message states that migrating forward is unaffected and is the
supported path.

FOLLOW-THROUGH FOR SUB-STAGE A: tests/commands/test_t2_handle_sqlite_arm.py
should be DELETED, not rewritten, when A lands — storage_backend_for will have
no SQLite answer for this helper and the arm will not exist. Its docstring now
says so.

title: RDR-126 P6 desktop-MVV harness is dead by construction after the T2 daemon retirement
description:
Found by the nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage B stacked review (code-review-expert High-3 neighbourhood, extended).

scripts/p6-clean-run.sh is the documented AUTOMATED PRE-RELEASE gate for RDR-126 Desktop deployment (docs/desktop-deployment.md:192). Its MCP probe asserts:

  line 115  check(PLIST.exists(), 'LaunchAgent written into sandbox')
  line 132  check(PLIST.exists(), 'dry-run did NOT remove the unit')
  line 139  check(not PLIST.exists(), 'unit removed after confirm=true')

where PLIST = $SANDBOX/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.t2.plist. The MCP first-run path that WROTE that unit — nexus.mcp._first_run.ensure_installed_and_running — was deleted in nexus-i711w Stage 2 sub-stage B (commit 9cfb157e; a tombstone comment sits at mcp/_first_run.py:35). The unit is therefore never written, so line 115 fails and the two daemon_uninstall legs assert against a unit that never existed.

Nothing in CI runs it, so it fails silently and only at a release cut, by a human.

Sub-stage B fixed only the dead 'nx daemon t2 stop' verb in its cleanup() (line 42) and the 'nx daemon t2 install --autostart' prose in p6-desktop-profile.sh. The structural death was NOT addressed, deliberately: deleting a documented pre-release gate is Hal's call, not a review-fix.

DISPOSITION NEEDED (one of):
  a) delete the P6-A harness + its docs/desktop-deployment.md section — the banner/first-run-install behaviour it gates no longer exists;
  b) repoint it at the SERVICE autostart unit (com.nexus.service.plist) IF the .mcpb first-run still installs one — needs checking, the first-run install path may be gone entirely;
  c) keep it and accept it is red.

P6-B (p6-desktop-profile.sh, manual) has the same question: its in-window checklist still says the Desktop .mcpb installs a daemon into the real ~/Library/LaunchAgents.

Also verify docs/desktop-deployment.md:192/194 against whatever is decided — both paragraphs describe LaunchAgent behaviour that may no longer happen.
close_reason: RESOLVED by deletion, unblocked now that nexus-i711w is closed. Hal ruled 'delete it' 2026-07-28; scripts/p6-clean-run.sh was removed in commit 1356ecd0 ('chore(rdr-126): delete the dead P6-A desktop MVV harness — nexus-uvn3t resolved') and is confirmed absent from the tree today. The bead could not be closed at the time because bd refused it while its dependency nexus-i711w was open; i711w closed 2026-07-30, so this is the deferred sweep, not new work. Option (b) — repoint the harness rather than delete — was not viable: the MCP first-run path that WROTE the com.nexus.t2 LaunchAgent (nexus.mcp._first_run.ensure_installed_and_running) was itself deleted in i711w sub-stage B (9cfb157e, tombstone at mcp/_first_run.py:35), so there is no first-run install left to point at. P6-B (p6-desktop-profile.sh) is KEPT — it is daemon-independent — with its two factual errors corrected and a STRONGER warning that daemon_uninstall is a host-level teardown the isolated Desktop profile does not scope. OPEN QUESTION carried forward, surfaced to Hal and NOT decided here: P6-B's original purpose died with the banner, so what remains is Desktop smoke rather than RDR-126 P6 — if that distinction matters for the release gate it wants its own bead.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RESOLVED (a) — Hal, 2026-07-28: 'delete it'. Commit 1356ecd0 on develop.

scripts/p6-clean-run.sh deleted. Confirmed dead by construction, not merely
stale: the first-run install path that wrote the com.nexus.t2 plist was deleted
in 9cfb157e, and it was also the banner's SOLE producer, so both the
PLIST.exists() checks and the banner check fail. Confirmed nothing under
.github/ referenced it — it would have failed first at a release cut, by hand.

Option (b) was not viable: there is no first-run install to repoint at. The
.mcpb first run now installs nothing.

DOCS SWEPT: docs/desktop-deployment.md's P6-A paragraph (described it as a live
gate naming checks that cannot pass) and p6-desktop-profile.sh's pointer to it
as 'the automated, pre-release half'.

Desktop profile via --user-data-dir) is daemon-independent and still verifies a

If Hal wants P6-B gone as well, say so — its original PURPOSE (verify the

the banner. What is left is .mcpb install + memory round-trip + uninstall,
which is Desktop smoke rather than RDR-126 P6.

Post-mortem references left alone: docs/rdr/post-mortem/126-*.md is a record.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
P6-B DELETED TOO — Hal, 2026-07-28. Commit f537a37e.

Reverses the carve-out in 1356ecd0, which kept p6-desktop-profile.sh on the
reasoning that its mechanism was daemon-independent and it still verified a
real surface. Hal's question ('memory round trip — is that a euphemism for
sqlite?') collapsed that.

WAS a euphemism, verbatim in the deleted P6-A: 'memory_* is pure T2/SQLite, so
no Voyage/Chroma creds are needed'. That is WHY the round-trip was the chosen

Is no longer SQLite, and that is what kills it. RDR-152 flipped the hard

first-run install block is a tombstone). P6-B's round-trip therefore CANNOT
pass on a fresh Desktop install; it passes only where a working install already
exists, which is not the fresh-account journey it claimed to be. That left

METHOD NOTE, because it nearly produced a wrong answer: my first probe unset
only NX_STORAGE_BACKEND while this shell exports NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR /
NX_SERVICE_URL / NX_SERVICE_TOKEN, so it reported SUCCEEDED — by writing a junk
entry into the live CLOUD store (deleted, verified gone). Off that bad probe I
also asserted 'lease discovery is not HOME-scoped', which was wrong and is
retracted. An isolated HOME does NOT isolate a nexus probe; scrub
NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR and NX_SERVICE_* too.

SWEEP MISS in the same doc: 2606729b swept docs/desktop-deployment.md (23
lines) but FIVE live falsehoods survived — SessionStart 'auto-installs the host
T2 daemon', Desktop first launch 'auto-installs the T2 daemon and starts it',

title: [bug] retrieval drift gate measures BELOW the boost layer — client-side re-weighting is invisible to it (ekn9n would not have been caught)
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-28 by a conexus relay (T2 21218). They hit a v0.1.58 parity move
caused by nexus-ekn9n reviving the service-mode topic boost, and flagged that
cross-run ranking comparisons can be confounded. Checking our side answered their
question and surfaced a DIFFERENT, larger gap of our own.

WE DO NOT SHARE THEIR CONFOUND. tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py
builds a FRESH hermetic PG per run (tempfile.mkdtemp + initdb) over a fixed
25-doc judged corpus, so taxonomy state is a deterministic function of the
corpus rather than drifting on a long-lived instance. Their conexus-npf7
(taxonomy fingerprint in the gate report) has no analogue we need.

THE ACTUAL GAP: THE GATE MEASURES THE WRONG LAYER.

  tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py:249
      rows = client.search(q["query"], [_COLLECTION], n_results=_K)
  where client is HttpVectorClient (line 221-223) — the raw vector-store layer.

  nexus/search_engine.py:850-862 applies apply_topic_boost ABOVE that client,
  on the merged all_results, along with apply_link_boost (:789), topic grouping
  (:824), Ward clustering (:839) and the salience boost (:874).

So every client-side ranking layer is invisible to the gate. Concretely: ekn9n
was a total loss of the topic boost in service mode — the default substrate
since the aqbrk flip — and this gate would have reported no drift at all,
because the boost never executes on the path it measures.

THE DOCSTRING OVERCLAIMS, which is how this stayed unnoticed. It says the
symmetric +/-0.05 band catches "embedding model change, rank re-weighting". True
for ENGINE-side re-weighting; false for the four client-side re-weighters above.
It also says "over the production-local retrieval path" — but the production
path for a user request goes through search_engine, not HttpVectorClient.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS TODAY'S OTHER FINDINGS, worth stating so the
class is recognised rather than fixed one instance at a time: a gate whose SCOPE
is narrower than its NAME, reported as coverage. Cf. nexus-onjvy (columns
written that no route reads), the aggregate-vs-per-query split conexus hit
(STEP-6 exit 0 while a query flipped), and test_storage_boundary_lint giving up
a real guarantee on the strength of a gate test that did not exist.

OPTIONS, not yet chosen:
 (a) add a SECOND gate at the search_engine layer over the same judged corpus,
     with topics discovered so the boost actually fires. Keeps the existing
     stack-level gate honest about what it is.
 (b) re-point this gate at search_engine. Loses the clean "is the ENGINE
     ranking drifting" signal by mixing in client re-weighting — probably wrong.
 (c) docstring-only correction. Cheapest, closes the overclaim, closes no
     coverage.
Leaning (a) + the (c) docstring fix regardless, since the overclaim is what made
the gap invisible. Needs a call before implementing.

NON-VACUITY REQUIREMENT for whatever lands: the new gate must FAIL when the
topic boost is disabled. ekn9n is the natural mutation — revert
HttpTaxonomyStore.get_topic_link_pairs to the triple shape and the boost dies
silently inside search_engine's best-effort except; the gate must go red.
close_reason: Fixed on develop d401e92ca..433246839 (2026-08-19): engine deadlock+gc_audit producers, client doctor check, split conservation, boost-layer gate, fixture env pin. Stacked-reviewed 3 rounds, engine suite 2148/0, pytest 13266/0, lint green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-28 — THE CAUSATION IN THIS BEAD'S OPENING PARAGRAPH IS
WITHDRAWN. The finding is not. conexus relay r4 (T2 21219).

WHAT THIS BEAD SAID, and what was wrong with it: "They hit a v0.1.58 parity move
caused by nexus-ekn9n reviving the service-mode topic boost." That attribution
was MINE, I gave it to them confidently in relay r1, and it cannot be true.

WHY IT CANNOT BE TRUE. apply_topic_boost exists ONLY in the Python client
(search_engine.py / scoring.py). It appears NOWHERE in service/src/main/java/.
Their STEP-6 POSTs raw HTTP to /v1/vectors/search and /v1/vectors/hybrid-search,
served by VectorHandler.java — pure cosine / hybrid rank, no Python client in the
path at all. So the boost never executes on the path they measure. They did not
observe ekn9n and COULD NOT HAVE.

THEIR ACTUAL CAUSE: corpus drift. chunks_1024 260,573 -> 262,087 (+1,514) and
catalog_documents 22,133 -> 22,167 (+34) between the two captures. An
approximate-ANN top-10 over a corpus that gained 1,514 chunks moves at the tail:
single-document swaps, set size held at 10, bidirectional. Fully explains the
signature with no code change. Their taxonomy-churn confound (r2) is out for the
same reason — topics do not enter engine-side ranking at all.

MY ERROR, recorded because the shape matters more than the instance. I analysed
ekn9n's MECHANISM correctly — constant-subtraction re-rank, truncation to
n_results, bidirectional tail swaps — and I did check the one thing I thought
could refute it (whether the boost is modality-gated; it is not). But I never
asked whether their MEASUREMENT PATH reaches the boost at all. One message later
I asked exactly that question about OUR gate, found the answer, and did not think
to apply it backwards to theirs. I had the decisive fact in hand and did not
turn it around. A mechanism that explains a signature is not evidence that the
mechanism ran.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED, per their explicit statement: the boost was totally
dead in service mode since the aqbrk flip, that is a real production defect, and
this gate cannot see it. Every layer claim in the description above
(HttpVectorClient at :249 vs apply_topic_boost at search_engine.py:860) was
verified against our tree and stands.

AND THE CASE FOR THIS BEAD GETS STRONGER, not weaker. Their gate sits below the

title: [bug] restart-stale installs the new engine binary but the session-supervised service keeps running the old one — package-upgrade MVV fails convergence (v0.1.52 -> v0.1.57)
description:
FOUND 2026-07-28 by tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --package-upgrade, run as the RDR-155 P4b gate's pre-cut shakeout (nexus-8zpmf). 2 checks failed; both are one bug.

=== WHAT HAPPENED ===
  Stage 2  nx init --service provisions PG + engine-service-v0.1.52, /version = 0.1.52     PASS
  Stage 3  seed a pre-upgrade T1 scratch row                                                PASS
  Stage 4  uv pip install --reinstall <worktree wheel>; engine binary sha256 UNCHANGED      PASS
  Stage 5  nx daemon restart-stale
             'converged engine: installed engine-service-v0.1.57 (was 0.1.52)'
             'NEEDS HUMAN: the service restarted but is STILL running v0.1.52, not the
              required v0.1.57. The restart exited cleanly, so something is holding the
              old engine (a supervisor that re-execs a different binary, or a second
              service process).'
  ASSERT   /version release_version=0.1.52, expected 0.1.57                                 FAIL
  ASSERT   a NEEDS HUMAN line appeared                                                      FAIL
  ASSERT   engine binary sha256 CHANGED by convergence (b8217a52 -> e84e3569)               PASS

So the download+install half WORKED (verified by sha256 change — a real re-acquire, not a no-op). The RUNNING PROCESS never moved onto it.

=== TWO EASY EXPLANATIONS RULED OUT, WITH EVIDENCE ===
1. 'The container lacks procps so skew detection was skipped.' The skip is real but NOT causal. Dockerfile.package-upgrade:18 is DELIBERATELY procps-less and says so: 'the product's process-skew detection must degrade that ONE leg gracefully... Do not add it back to make this leg pass; that papers over the class of bug this leg exists to catch.' And src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:2085 states process-skew detection 'is independent of engine convergence', with a try/except specifically so a ps-less box does not block convergence. Adding procps would be papering over.
2. 'It is nexus-4yf4u.' That bead is CLOSED (b5cb380a, 2026-07-24) and its fix is what PRODUCED the NEEDS HUMAN line — it shipped 'post-restart convergence OBSERVED, not inferred from returncodes'. The detection is working exactly as designed. What fails is the convergence underneath it. 4yf4u's own close text claims 'a real improvement for every case where the service is observably up' — here the service IS observably up and answering /version, and it still did not converge.

=== LIKELY MECHANISM (not yet confirmed — do not implement against this) ===
The container has no systemd. Provision logged: 'Could not activate the autostart unit (systemctl not found on PATH; file installed but not activated); starting the service for this session instead.' So the service is SESSION-SUPERVISED, not unit-managed. The new binary lands at /home/nexus/.config/nexus/service/nexus-service and the sha256 there changes, but the session supervisor appears to bring the process back on the old image (already-exec'd binary held open, or a re-exec of a cached path). Confirm by tracing what the session supervisor re-execs before changing anything.
Scope question that follows: this is the no-systemd/no-launchd fallback path — containers, CI, and any box where unit activation failed. A macOS launchd or Linux systemd box may converge fine. Establish which before sizing.

=== WHY NOBODY SAW IT: the upgrade axis has NO working automated gate ===
There is no scheduled workflow for --package-upgrade at all. The only rehearsal workflows are cold-install-rehearsal.yml (disabled) and guided-upgrade-mvv.yml (RED since 2026-07-24 per nexus-x7xjj, and it drives nx guided-upgrade which P4b DELETED). So the entire upgrade-journey axis is currently ungated, and this leg is manual-only with no history to say whether this is a regression or long-standing. That gap is arguably the more important finding.

=== WHAT PASSED, and it matters for the P4b gate ===
The migrated-data axis this leg was chosen for is GREEN: the pre-upgrade T1 row seeded on 6.18.0/v0.1.52 SURVIVED the package upgrade and service cycle; post-convergence T1 put/get round-trips; the skew-window put/get against the old engine was bounded and non-silent; and the chash-poison probe answered via the VIEW path (nexus.diag_chash_conformance, zero non-conformant rows, no legacy fallback).

RELATED: nexus-4yf4u (closed, the detection that caught this), nexus-n66kv (promote engine convergence to a real ladder rung — this is evidence for it), nexus-x7xjj (the other red rehearsal gates).
LOG: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/package-upgrade.log (session-scoped; re-run with ./tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --package-upgrade, ~10 min, Docker required).
close_reason: FIXED-BY-DUPLICATE, verified 2026-08-06 by debugger (T2 [21562]): the bead's re-exec hypothesis REFUTED structurally (one exec site, fixed well-known path, atomic replace, no held image — procfs proof: fresh pids, inode change, no deleted-suffix) — real mechanism was the stop/start compose race on a stalled 15s lease (stop no-ops on lease MISS, start short-circuits on the revived lease). Fixed by 21cf872d (nexus-cfgo9: pre-stop process-table snapshot + survivor sweep) and f2b26717 (nexus-oyo2g: stop consults the process table + signals the tree). Rehearsal --package-upgrade now PASSES 23/0 incl. both originally-failed asserts; converged with NO sweep clause (oyo2g stop killed the tree alone). Scope answer: race was platform-independent, not no-unit-specific; unit-managed installs converge but leave session-scoped ownership (RDR-183 territory). Residual gap beaded separately: the upgrade axis has no automated gate.

title: [test-infra] t2_store_contract checks parameter names but never return shapes — a twin diverged on a public API for the whole life of the port
description:
tests/db/t2_store_contract.py is the parity suite between CatalogTaxonomy (and the other SQLite twins) and their Http counterparts. Its assertion surface is a dict of method -> parameter-name list. It cannot see return types at all.

That hole let nexus-ekn9n live undetected: HttpTaxonomyStore.get_topic_link_pairs returned list[(from,to,count)] where the oracle returns dict[(from,to),count], across the entire life of the RDR-152 port. The consequence was a P1 silent search regression — apply_topic_boost's 'for (a, b) in links' raised ValueError inside search_engine's best-effort except Exception, discarding the whole topic boost in service mode. The parity suite was green throughout.

PROPOSAL: extend the contract to assert return-shape parity for every method in the roster. Cheapest credible form is a differential call — invoke the method on both twins against equivalent seeded state and compare type(result) plus, for containers, the element shape. That is the same differential-substrate discipline the 8zpmf gate already requires of the vector stores (comment 2026-07-23, item 1), applied to T2.

SCOPE NOTE: the transition window is finite. The differential leg only exists while both twins do, so this is worth doing NOW or not at all — after nexus-i711w deletes the SQLite twins there is no oracle to diff against, and whatever shapes the Http twins happen to have become the contract by default. That is precisely how get_topic_link_pairs would have been frozen wrong.

title: [taxonomy] split silently drops ~95% of the parent's assignments: 1,330-doc topic split into children totalling 60 docs, 1,270 assignments deleted without warning
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 on knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1.

Sequence:
1. Topic "Transformer attention mathematics" held 351 docs from discovery; incremental
   assignment (after ~1,080 new chunks were indexed) grew it to **1,330**.
2. `nx taxonomy split "Transformer attention mathematics" -k 3 -c <coll>` reported success:
   "Split 'Transformer attention mathematics' into 3 sub-topics."
3. Result: parent shows **0 docs**; the three children hold **27 + 20 + 13 = 60**.
   Collection totals: **6,728 assigned before → 5,458 after** = 1,270 assignments silently
   deleted. No warning, no count in the output.

Per the command's own docstring the persist is "DELETE parent assignments + INSERT children" —
the DELETE covered all 1,330; the KMeans/INSERT phase evidently operated on only a tiny subset
(60). Plausible mechanisms worth checking: the compute phase fetches only the topic's
discovery-time exemplars rather than all current assignments; or the T3 fetch applies a limit;
or only chunks passing a confidence threshold are re-inserted while the rest are dropped rather
than retained on the parent.

## Why this bit hard here

Incremental assignment funnels ALL novel-subject chunks into the nearest existing topic (here,
~979 reservoir-computing chunks into a transformer-math topic — no mechanism creates new topics
between rebuilds), so "split the bloated topic" is exactly the repair the design invites. As
shipped, that repair destroys the assignments instead of redistributing them.

## Acceptance

1. Split must be conservation-checked: sum(children) + retained == parent's pre-split count, or
   the command fails/rolls back. Silent shrinkage is the defect, whatever the mechanism.
2. Chunks the re-cluster can't confidently place go to an explicit "unassigned" child or stay on
   the parent — never dropped.
3. Report the redistribution in the output ("1,330 → 610/480/240" style).
4. Regression: split a topic that has post-discovery incremental assignments; assert none vanish.

Recovery used here: full `nx taxonomy rebuild` + label + auto-review (the 1,270 weren't lost
from T3, only their topic assignments; rebuild re-clusters everything and — since discovery now
sees the RC corpus — should form genuine RC topics rather than a 60-doc stub).

Related: nexus-afnht (review --auto dry-run not predictive), nexus-1d5y6 (markup tokens in
discovery vocabulary).

(<retained> retained on parent)') by reading back db.taxonomy.get_topics(parent_id=topic_id) after a successful split — satisfies acceptance #3.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic (crit-fix pile review): SIGNIFICANT deviation from literal acceptance criterion 2, otherwise sound and verified closing the reported incident.

Acceptance criterion 2 ('chunks the re-cluster can't confidently place go to an explicit unassigned child or stay on the parent — never dropped') is not implemented as written. The shipped fix substitutes all-or-nothing refusal (any fetch coverage gap refuses the ENTIRE split, parent fully untouched) for the described graceful/partial degradation with an explicit unassigned-child escape hatch. Checked compute_split (taxonomy_compute.py): KMeans has no per-doc confidence-based rejection — every fetched embedding is hard-assigned to one of k clusters (mask.any() only skips empty clusters), so criterion 2's literal 'clusterer can't confidently place' scenario cannot arise in this algorithm; fetch-completeness (what the guard actually checks) is the only real gap mechanism. So the substitution is defensible given the real algorithm, but it was never called out anywhere as a scoped/documented deviation from the bead's own acceptance text, and it has a real UX cost: one transient partial-fetch (e.g. a single flaky row) now refuses the WHOLE split rather than completing an almost-full one, with no operator-facing retry surfaced.

Also minor: acceptance criterion 4 ('regression: split a topic that has post-discovery incremental assignments; assert none vanish') isn't represented by a test framed that way — the added tests (pagination past 250, partial-fetch refusal) cover the actual confirmed root cause (general T3 fetch-coverage gaps) rather than the bead's original discovery-vs-incremental hypothesis, which was correctly superseded during diagnosis but never reflected back into the acceptance text. Functionally fine, just a traceability gap.

Verified sound: the guard applies uniformly to both the service-backed and non-service branches (independently confirmed via code read — the non-service branch's per-batch got_ids can legitimately be shorter than requested without tripping vectors_unavailable, which is exactly the gap the new guard closes there too), the defense-in-depth assert is correctly placed, and the CLI redistribution reporting re-reads topics fresh from the DB rather than trusting in-memory state.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
developer (crit-fix pile follow-up, 2026-08-19): confirming and recording the scoped deviation substantive-critic flagged. Acceptance criterion 2 as literally written ("chunks the re-cluster can't confidently place go to an explicit unassigned child or stay on parent -- never dropped") is NOT what shipped. The shipped fix is all-or-nothing refusal: any T3 fetch-coverage gap refuses the ENTIRE split (return 0, parent fully untouched) rather than routing the unplaceable subset to an unassigned child or leaving it on the parent.

This is a deliberate, verified-defensible substitution, not an oversight: compute_split's clusterer (KMeans, taxonomy_compute.py) has no per-doc confidence-based rejection path -- every embedding it receives is hard-assigned to exactly one of k clusters (mask.any() only ever skips a cluster that received zero points). Criterion 2's literal scenario ("the re-cluster can't confidently place" a doc) cannot arise in this algorithm; the only real gap mechanism is fetch-completeness (T3 returning fewer ids/embeddings than requested), which is what the shipped guard actually checks.

Trade-off this carries, called out explicitly since it wasn't before: a single transient partial-fetch (e.g. one flaky row) now refuses the WHOLE split rather than completing an almost-full one, with no operator-facing retry surfaced. Accepted here because refusing is unconditionally safer than the alternative this bead exists to close -- silent partial persistence (the 2026-07-27 incident: 1,330 docs -> 60 reported as success). Revisit only if transient partial-fetch refusals prove operationally costly in practice.

Verified by substantive-critic (2026-08-19, T2 nexus/2026-08-19-critfix-pile-critique-0uuit-sybbh-i6eg8-j46lz [22849]): guard applies uniformly to both service-backed and non-service branches, defense-in-depth assert correctly placed (now a real SplitConservationViolatedError, not a bare assert -- see code-review-expert's separate finding, also fixed this pass), CLI redistribution reporting re-reads topics fresh from DB.

title: [bug] local-service gate: the voyage/CCE subset 422s because nx init --service stamps bge-768 and the r5f3c guard then refuses to plumb the key the workflow supplies
description:
FOUND BY the nexus-8zpmf (RDR-155 P4b) gate, 2026-07-28, while establishing why
local-service-gate-nightly has been red. Six of that run's 33 failures are this.
Full taxonomy: T2 [21196]. Gate record: T2 [21195].

SYMPTOM. local-service-gate-nightly run 30315955619 (workflow_dispatch, tree =
develop @ 71c23b99):

  HTTP 422: service (embedding mode onnx-local) has no embedder for model
  'voyage-code-3' — refusing to embed collection
  'code__int-crossmodel-125f3699__voyage-code-3__v1' with a different model

Three in tests/test_integration.py (test_voyage_code3_index_and_query,
test_cce_query_retrieves_cce_indexed_markdown,
test_t3_put_embedding_model_in_search_metadata) and, consistent with the same
cause because chunks never materialize when the embed is refused, three in
tests/test_indexer_e2e.py (test_smart_index_rdr_routing,
test_reindex_self_heals_missing_manifest,
test_migration_moves_prose_from_code_to_docs).

THE KEY IS PRESENT. This is not the missing-secret case. The workflow wires
VOYAGE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.VOYAGE_API_KEY }} and hard-fails before pytest if it
is empty (local-service-gate-nightly.yml ~line 172: "VOYAGE_API_KEY secret is not
configured — the gate would fail on every voyage/CCE test"). The run got past that
check, so the variable was non-empty in the gate's environment.

MECHANISM (proven by reading the code, not inferred from the symptom):

  1. tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh:182 runs `NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR="$SCRATCH"
     uv run nx init --service`.
  2. src/nexus/commands/init.py:73 `_provision_service_embedder_step` does
     `set_config_value("local.embed_model", _TIER1_MODEL)` and echoes
     "Saved: local.embed_model = ... (service: bge-768 only)". bge-768 is the only
     valid value in the service topology (RDR-160); the RDR-144 picker that once
     varied it was removed in RDR-174 P1.3.
  3. src/nexus/daemon/storage_service_daemon.py:603-616, the nexus-r5f3c guard
     (b745589c, 2026-07-21): when NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is absent it reads
     `local_embed_model_choice()`; if that value is set and does NOT start with
     "voyage", it logs storage_service_voyage_key_not_plumbed and does NOT plumb
     the ambient key from the credential chain. Only an unset choice or a voyage
     choice reaches `get_credential("voyage_api_key")`.
  4. So the service spawns onnx-local and 422s every voyage-* collection —
     precisely the consequence the sibling warning branch predicts
     ("embedding_mode=onnx-local, consequence=voyage-* collections will be
     refused (HTTP 422)").

r5f3c's guard is CORRECT for real users and must not be reverted: its whole point
is that an ambient VOYAGE_API_KEY used to flip a bge install voyage-only and 422
the first store against the bge collections the client builds — a broken first run
for anyone with a Voyage key exported.

FIX SHAPE. The code names its own escape hatch: "Explicit NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY still
always passes through." The gate should export NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY (not rely on the
ambient VOYAGE_API_KEY credential chain) when it intends to exercise voyage
collections. Prefer that over weakening the guard. The gate script's comment at
~line 140 still asserts "the supervisor plumbs VOYAGE_API_KEY -> NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY
into the service env at spawn" — that has been conditionally false since 07-21 and
must be corrected in the same change, or the next reader re-derives this.

UNEXPLAINED, AND THE FIRST THING TO CHECK — do not treat the mechanism above as
complete until this is resolved. The guard landed 2026-07-21 and the init stamp has
existed since 2026-06-15/06-28, yet the gate was GREEN on 07-22, 07-23 and 07-24 and
only went red on 07-25. Both halves were in place during those green runs, so
something else must have kept the key flowing then. Leading hypothesis: the daemon
resolves `local_embed_model_choice()` through `_global_config_path()` ->
`nexus_config_dir()`, and the gate only sets NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR="$SCRATCH" on
individual commands; if the service spawn previously read a config dir with no
local.embed_model (returning None, which the guard treats as "plumb"), and now
reads the scratch config where init stamped bge-768, that flips exactly this
behavior with no change to either the guard or the stamp. DECISIVE EXPERIMENT: dump
the effective config path and the resolved embed choice at spawn time in the gate,
and check for the storage_service_voyage_key_not_plumbed log line in the service
spawn output. If that line is present, the mechanism holds; if it is absent, the
422 has a different origin and this bead's mechanism section is wrong.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE LOCALLY on 2026-07-27: the local gate rebuilds the service jar via
Maven, and testcontainers' ryuk returned Status 500 (the known wedged-Docker class,
auto-memory project_docker_port_forwarding_wedges). Diagnosis above is from code
reading plus CI logs only.

SCOPE BOUNDARY. Not nexus-12m77: that bead's category (a) is the version-pin /
ManagedServiceIncompatible and endpoint-plumbing family, and its triage note treats
voyage as "credentials not present on this box" — the opposite of this case, where
the credential IS present and is deliberately withheld from the service. Not
nexus-qvs2h either: qvs2h owns the substrate-port debt in test_indexer_e2e (32
failures, dominant signature httpx.UnsupportedProtocol / empty base URL), which is a
different failure mode from the three indexer failures here.

BLOCKS nexus-8zpmf's certification of capability-ledger row 45 (T2 [21097]), which
names the local-service gate in the validation battery for the chromadb dependency
drop.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-07-28 by Hal determination: 'we do no embedding on the client so this key is dropped. It was a vestige of reranking, that was on the client, but is now in the engine.'

THE REMAINING ITEM WAS NOT A GAP. This bead stayed open after b53f8d06 for the coverage gap the cloud_mode carve-out created — 'the voyage/CCE embedding path has no gate' — with three options recorded and none chosen. The determination dissolves it: there is no CLIENT-side voyage/CCE embedding path left to gate. What needs gating is the ENGINE's voyage embedding, which is engine-side and belongs to the engine suite + tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh, not to a client gate. Option (a) PARTITION, which I recommended, is what b53f8d06 already did; it needed no follow-up, only a correct reading of what was on the other side of the partition.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE rather than accepted — and the tree had already been prepared for this:
- RERANK: client path DELETED by RDR-188. cross_encoder.py:12-16 — 'The rerank caller (scoring.rerank_results / _rerank_local) is DELETED: local-mode reranking now runs [server-side]... Do not re-grow a client rerank path on this substrate.' engine_version.py:124-126 pins the floor at (0,1,52) for it.
- SEARCH THRESHOLDS: RDR-188 P3.2 (nexus-9o6y2.14) repointed _voyage_thresholds_active from the client credential to the SERVER's reported embedder family (GET /version). Its comment states the intent outright: 'The former client-key heuristic is retired with the client's Voyage consumption. Removing the now-unconsumed client voyage key can no longer silently regress search quality (Gap 3).'
- EMBEDDING: every remaining client-side consumer is in the ELSE of a service-mode branch — indexer.py:3144 (whose voyageai.Client line already carries '# epsilon-allow: Phase-4 deletion target — legacy non-service embed path'), doc_indexer.py:807/983/1535, pipeline_stages.py:723. Service mode is the default in BOTH local and cloud, so these are unreachable on every shipping configuration.
- DOCTOR: health.py:737 already says 'moved reranking server-side — no client code path consumes this key'.

SAFETY CHECK THAT MATTERED MOST, done because THIS BEAD is the incident that teaches it: dropping the CHROMA_* trio flipped is_local_mode() and caused this bug. So before endorsing dropping VOYAGE_API_KEY I checked whether it is also a mode signal. IT IS NOT — is_local_mode() (config.py:554-605) keys on the mode record, then service_url, then pg_credentials, then defaults local; it never consults the voyage key. Dropping it cannot repeat the w6h2m mechanism.
STALE DOCSTRING FOUND WHILE CHECKING: health.py:1450-1480 _check_credential_persistence still claims that when VOYAGE_API_KEY is env-only 'is_local_mode() flips to True'. That was true pre-RDR-155 and is not true now. Rolled into the deletion bead.

RESIDUAL WORK FILED SEPARATELY: the client-side Voyage credential surface deletion (57 references), plus the one genuinely open sub-question — whether storage_service_daemon's NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY plumb into a LOCALLY-SPAWNED engine survives, which is credential passthrough rather than client embedding and turns on whether a local engine may ever run voyage mode (RDR-160 says a local service IS bge-768).

The bead's own scope note asked for a retitle if (a) was chosen. Moot on close.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
TIMELINE RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — the 'STILL UNEXPLAINED' section of this bead is now closed. The red IS P4b-caused, via a two-hop path.

EVIDENCE, from the gate logs either side of the boundary:
  07-24 GREEN run 30084672054: NO 'Saved: local.embed_model' line, and no bge-768 provisioning step at all.
  07-25 RED  run 30153561209: 'Saved: local.embed_model = BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 (service: bge-768 only)' plus the bge provisioning lines.

THE CHAIN:
1. _provision_service_embedder_step (the only writer of local.embed_model) is reached from init.py:673, and init.py:667-670 returns EARLY when is_local_mode() is False.
2. Until 2026-07-25 the nightly workflow passed CHROMA_API_KEY / CHROMA_TENANT / CHROMA_DATABASE. Its own header (pre-edit) said what they were for: 'CHROMA_* trio drives cloud-mode detection plus one idempotent...'.
3. So is_local_mode() was FALSE, init returned early, nothing stamped local.embed_model, local_embed_model_choice() returned None — which is precisely the r5f3c guard's 'no choice recorded' branch that DOES plumb the ambient key. Service came up voyage-capable. Voyage/CCE tests passed. GREEN.
4. Commit 534251da (2026-07-25 05:01, 'docs+ci: retire the Chroma dispositions — dead secrets, false module inventory', RDR-155 P4b P3) removed the three secrets. Correctly — they were dead.
5. is_local_mode() flipped TRUE. init now runs the embedder step and stamps bge-768. The r5f3c guard sees a non-voyage configured model and refuses the plumb. Service comes up onnx-local. Every voyage-* collection 422s. First red run 2026-07-25 09:54Z, four hours after the commit.

Both changes were correct in isolation: deleting dead Chroma credentials, and gating the voyage plumb on the configured embed model (r5f3c, 07-21, which fixed a real broken-first-run for users with an exported Voyage key). Nobody examined the composition. The bug lives entirely in the interaction.

SECOND-ORDER FINDING, worth more than the bug: this gate had been detecting CLOUD mode for its entire life. It is named 'Local-service functional gate' and its job is a hermetic local PG + service, but the Chroma credentials it carried made is_local_mode() answer False, so init took its cloud branch. The gate went red on the first day it genuinely ran local. Its previous green therefore certified a path that was not the one it advertised — worth a look at whatever ELSE branched on is_local_mode() inside this gate before trusting the pre-07-25 green history. Filed here rather than as a separate bead because it is the same root; split it out if it grows.

The fix in 6b04cd1b stands unchanged and is now better motivated: setting NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY explicitly is the documented override, it survives regardless of which mode the gate detects, and it does not weaken the r5f3c guard for real installs.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIX REVERTED 2026-07-28 (commit 699369b0). It worked and was still wrong. Measured on gate run 30320503026 against the tree carrying 6b04cd1b.

WHAT THE FIX DID: exactly what it claimed. Zero 'onnx-local' 422s in the run, the NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY promote line fired, the voyage/CCE subset stopped failing. And the identical cluster reappeared pointing the other way:

  HTTP 422: service (embedding mode voyage) has no embedder for model 'bge-base-en-v15-768' — refusing to embed collection 'docs__int-cce-0cafe877__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1' with a different model. Available models: [voyage-3, voyage-...]

That is verbatim the failure nexus-r5f3c was written to prevent — its docstring warns that plumbing an ambient VOYAGE_API_KEY 'flipped the engine voyage-only and 422d the first store against the bge collections the client builds'. The fix reintroduced it inside the gate. Totals moved 33 failed/2 errors -> 32 failed/1 error: a wash, bought by swapping which half of the corpus is broken.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, which this bead's title understates. The gate exercises BOTH bge-768 collections (tests/test_integration.py T3 round-trips, tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py) AND voyage/CCE collections, while the service runs ONE embedding mode at a time:
   key withheld -> embedding mode onnx-local -> voyage/CCE collections 422 (~6)
   key plumbed  -> embedding mode voyage     -> bge-768 collections 422 (~5)
No value of this knob makes the gate green. Turning it is the wrong move by construction.

WHY IT EVER PASSED — it was never running local. The CHROMA_* secrets made is_local_mode() answer False, so 'nx init --service' returned at init.py:670 BEFORE stamping local.embed_model, the client never configured bge-768, and it built voyage collections that matched the voyage-mode service. Everything agreed because everything was cloud. Removing those dead credentials (534251da, RDR-155 P4b P3) made the client honestly bge-768 — correct for a local service install, where RDR-160 makes bge-768 the only valid value — and put it permanently at odds with a test corpus written for cloud mode.

SO THE DECISION IS WHICH LANE THE GATE IS IN. Three options, for Hal or whoever picks this up:
 (a) PARTITION. The 'Local-service functional gate' stops exercising voyage/CCE collections; those move to a cloud-mode gate. Cleanest read of intent — RDR-160 says a local service IS bge-768, so voyage collections are not a local-mode configuration and testing them here tests a product state that no longer exists. Cost: the voyage/CCE embedding path loses its only current gate, so it needs a home before this lands, not after.
 (b) TWO PASSES. Same gate, run twice, once per embedding mode, each asserting only its own corpus. Keeps coverage, roughly doubles the runtime, and needs the FLOOR/BUDGET vacuity guards split per pass or they go vacuous.
 (c) MULTI-EMBEDDER SERVICE. The engine serves more than one embedding mode concurrently and routes per collection by the model segment. Largest change, engine-side, and it is a real product question rather than a test-infra one — a box with both bge and voyage collections is a legitimate post-migration state.

Recommend (a), with (b) as the fallback if the voyage/CCE path has no other gate. Not implementing either without a call — this is a scope question, and I have already once mistaken 'the number moved' for 'the problem is solved' on this bead.

BEAD SCOPE NOTE: retitle if (a) is chosen — the defect is not 'the guard refuses to plumb the key', it is 'the gate's corpus spans two embedding modes the service cannot serve at once'.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIX VERIFIED 2026-07-28, commit b53f8d06, gate run 30321753068.

  before (run 30315955619, tree 71c23b99):  33 failed / 443 passed / 2 errors
  after  (run 30321753068, tree b53f8d06):  22 failed / 453 passed / 0 errors

13 cleared, and the arithmetic is exact rather than approximate: 5 chash (k7te2) + 3 catalog._db (da79ac6a) + 2 start_t1_server errors (ae019bfd, now PASSING not merely collecting) + 3 voyage (deselected by the cloud_mode carve-out). Every one of the remaining 22 belongs to another bead — nexus-qvs2h (9 l9hd8 + 5 taxonomy_e2e + 3 indexer_e2e) and nexus-12m77 (5 catalog reader-path). None is owned by RDR-155 P4b.

⚠️ ONE PART OF THE FIX IS CURRENTLY INERT, and it is the same trap that made this bead hard to diagnose in the first place. The run logged 'NX_GATE_FLOOR: 455', not the 452 I set. The gate SCRIPT (tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh) is checked out from develop and took effect immediately; the WORKFLOW file (.github/workflows/local-service-gate-nightly.yml), which is where NX_GATE_FLOOR lives, runs from the DEFAULT BRANCH — main — because that is how GitHub resolves scheduled and dispatched workflow definitions. So the floor change does not apply until develop promotes to main.

Consequence today: none visible, because the run fails on 22 real test failures long before the vacuity guard is consulted. Consequence later: if the remaining 22 are fixed while the workflow file is still on main's old value, passed would be ~475 against a floor of 455 and nothing trips. The 455-vs-452 distinction only bites in the narrow band where the carve-out's 3 missing passes matter. Not worth a separate fix — it corrects itself at the next promote — but it MUST NOT be forgotten, because 'the workflow file lives on main, the script it runs lives on develop' is exactly the split that made this gate's redness read as a main-branch problem for three days.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: the voyage/CCE embedding path has no gate. That is the gap the carve-out created, deliberately and in writing. tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh is the candidate home. Until it lands, a regression in service-side voyage embedding would be caught by nothing.

title: two scheduled rehearsal gates have been standing RED since 2026-07-24 and nobody noticed — guided-upgrade MVV invokes a journey P4b deleted, era-hop aborts its own non-vacuity gate
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 as a SIDE EFFECT of pushing nexus-rrc8t. Editing
src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py matched the migration-path and ladder-path push
triggers, firing two workflows that otherwise only run WEEKLY. Both were
already red. The push did not break them; it made them visible.

=== WORKFLOW 1: "Guided-upgrade MVV (weekly + on migration-path changes)" ===
Run history on develop, ALL failure:

exits 2 immediately with the rehearsal script's own refusal:

  (nexus-8nlj4). The surviving journeys are --era-hop, --package-upgrade,
  --shakeout, --fullstack, --chash-window, and the default rehearse.sh.

So the WORKFLOW still invokes a journey the P4b deletion removed. The script is
behaving correctly — it refuses rather than silently passing. The workflow is
stale. Note nexus-8nlj4 (RDR-185 acceptance harness reshape post-P4b) is
already open and names the replacement; this workflow should either be retired
with the journey or repointed at the two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal, which
is 8nlj4's scope. Check whether this is simply part of 8nlj4 before doing
separate work.

=== WORKFLOW 2: "Era-spanning upgrade hop (weekly + on ladder-path changes)" ===
Run history on develop, ALL failure:
  2026-07-27T21:58, 2026-07-27T13:49, 2026-07-26T01:59, 2026-07-26T01:47,
  2026-07-25T23:45, 2026-07-25T22:28, 2026-07-25T20:28, 2026-07-25T18:37
Job "nx upgrade alone, across an era (container-isolated)" gets as far as
Stage 4 (package upgrade PASSES, engine-untouched assert PASSES) then aborts on
its own non-vacuity gate:

  FAIL nx upgrade --dry-run does NOT report the substrate rung pending — the
  seeded footprint is invisible to the product (check
  NX_LOCAL_CHROMA_PATH=/home/nexus/legacy-chroma vs the rung's resolver).
  Every convergence assert below would grade a no-op.
  == ABORT (vacuous fixture — refusing to report a pass over work that never
  existed) ==

The gate is doing exactly its job. Either the seeding no longer matches the
rung's resolver, or the rung stopped reporting pending. Diagnose before
touching the fixture: a "fix" that makes the gate pass without restoring
visibility converts this into the silent no-op it exists to prevent.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO WORKFLOWS ===
Weekly-scheduled gates fail silently: nothing surfaces a red scheduled run the
way a PR check does. These two had been red for 3+ days across at least 8 runs
each. Worth deciding whether scheduled-workflow failures should notify (the
general fix) rather than only fixing these two instances.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
FULL WORKFLOW SURVEY 2026-07-27 — it is FOUR gates, not two.

Latest run per workflow (all branches):

  ci.yml                          in-progress  develop
  cold-install-rehearsal.yml      NEVER RUN    (workflow_dispatch only)
  engine-service-release.yml      success      engine-service-v0.1.57
  era-hop-mvv.yml                 FAILURE      develop

  plugin-drift-ledger.yml         success      feature/...
  release.yml                     success      v6.18.1
  service-ci.yml                  success      develop

BROKEN, by class:

1. guided-upgrade-mvv.yml — STANDING RED since 2026-07-24 (8+ runs).
   Invokes `run.sh --guided`; that journey was deleted by RDR-155 P4b P2.
   The workflow's OWN header states its purpose: "The migration tool ships in
   release N and is DELETED in release N+1 (RDR-155 P4b) — this gate is what
   protects the deprecation window users cross." Its subject is now gone, so
   the gate is obsolete BY DESIGN, not merely broken. Retiring it is literally
   the first half of nexus-8nlj4 ("retire guided-migration rehearsals"); the
   second half (build the two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal) is unbuilt.

2. cold-install-rehearsal.yml — DORMANT AND BROKEN. workflow_dispatch only, so
   it has never run and never goes red; but it invokes `run.sh --cold`, which
   is in the SAME retired set as --guided. It would fail the moment anyone
   dispatched it. Same disposition as (1): 8nlj4's retire-half.

3. era-hop-mvv.yml — STANDING RED since 2026-07-25 (8+ runs). NOT stale
   plumbing: it reaches Stage 4, PASSES the package upgrade and the
   engine-untouched assert, then its own non-vacuity gate aborts:
     FAIL nx upgrade --dry-run does NOT report the substrate rung pending —
     the seeded footprint is invisible to the product (check
     NX_LOCAL_CHROMA_PATH=/home/nexus/legacy-chroma vs the rung's resolver).
     Every convergence assert below would grade a no-op.
     == ABORT (vacuous fixture — refusing to report a pass over work that
     never existed) ==
   This is the highest-value one: either the seeding drifted from the rung's
   resolver, or THE RUNG STOPPED REPORTING PENDING — the latter would be a
   real product bug in the upgrade ladder. Diagnose before touching the
   fixture; a change that merely makes the gate green converts it into exactly
   the silent no-op it exists to prevent.

4. local-service-gate-nightly.yml — STANDING RED on main since at least
   2026-07-25 (3+ nightly runs). NOT yet diagnosed. Separate from the three
   above and on a different branch.

=== THE GENERAL DEFECT ===
All four are scheduled/dispatch gates. A red scheduled run surfaces NOWHERE —
no PR check, no notification — so these accumulated for days unnoticed. The
per-workflow fixes do not address that. Worth deciding whether scheduled-
workflow failure should notify, which is the fix that would have caught all
four on day one. (These only became visible because a push touching
src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py matched the migration-path and ladder-path
triggers, firing two weekly workflows off-schedule.)

=== NOT IN THIS BEAD ===
The CA-3 linux-amd64 failure in the same push was a Docker Hub registry
timeout pulling liquibase/liquibase:4.31, not a gate defect. Fixed at the
mechanism in scripts/liquibase_bundle_smoke.sh: explicit `docker pull` with
bounded retries and a distinct failure message, so a registry blip can no
longer read as a schema failure.

title: [index] expose the existing force parameter as --force on nx index and nx dt index — the pipeline already supports it, nothing reaches it
description:
`_index_file` in `src/nexus/doc_indexer.py` already takes a `force` parameter that bypasses the
staleness gate:

```python
    if not force and existing["metadatas"]:
        stored_hash  = existing["metadatas"][0].get("content_hash", "")
        stored_model = existing["metadatas"][0].get("embedding_model", "")
        if stored_hash == content_hash and stored_model == target_model:
            return 0
```

**No CLI surface passes it.** Not `nx index repo`, `nx index pdf`, `nx index md`, and not
`nx dt index`. So the one-line escape hatch the pipeline was designed with is unreachable from
any supported command.

## Why this matters (concrete, 2026-07-27)

Indexing a 69-page PDF (Zoology, arXiv 2312.04927, DT UUID 169ADD1E-…) failed partway — vector
gateway 504s, extractor cancelled. Three subsequent repair attempts across two extractors all
printed `Indexed 1 record(s)` and all wrote **zero chunks**, because 3 surviving chunks from the
botched run still carried the source's `content_hash` and the `limit=1` staleness probe accepted
them as proof the document was fully indexed.

Recovery required, in order: reconstructing the live-chunk set from 46 other documents' manifests
to identify orphans safely; deleting the catalog entry (which did NOT help, since the probe reads
T3, not the catalog); then finally computing the file's sha256 by hand and issuing
`col.get(where={"content_hash": h})` through the Python client to find and delete the 3 blockers.

`--force` would have made every one of those steps unnecessary.

## Acceptance

1. Thread `force` through to `_index_file` from:
   - `nx index pdf` / `nx index md` / `nx index repo`
   - `nx dt index` (all selectors: `--uuid`, `--selection`, `--tag`, `--group`, `--smart-group`)
2. Semantics: skip the staleness gate and re-extract + re-upsert. Because re-indexing ADDS
   rather than replaces (see nexus-mok9x), `--force` MUST first delete the source's existing
   chunks — otherwise it doubles the document. Deleting by `content_hash` is the working handle
   in service mode; `delete_by_source` returns 0 there.
3. Help text should state that it re-embeds (i.e. costs money on a billed key) so it is not
   reached for casually.
4. Test: partially index a document, delete a subset of its chunks, assert a normal re-index
   no-ops and a `--force` re-index restores full chunk count with no duplicates.

Blocks the recovery half of nexus-5xn3k. Independent of the deeper fix there (making the
staleness probe count-aware rather than existence-aware) — this is the cheap escape hatch, that
is the correctness fix, and both are wanted.
close_reason: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — closing as stale, not as work done. Verified end-to-end on develop 2026-07-31 rather than taken on faith: '--force' exists on all four surfaces (4 occurrences in src/nexus/commands/index.py covering nx index repo/pdf/md/rdr, 1 in src/nexus/commands/dt.py for nx dt index), and the flag REACHES the specific gate the bead quotes. Chain traced for the markdown path: index_md_cmd(force) -> index_markdown(force=force) [commands/index.py:1566,1573] -> _index_document(force=force) [doc_indexer.py:1860] -> the 'if not force and existing["metadatas"]' staleness gate [doc_indexer.py:772]. The PDF path is likewise wired (pipeline_index_pdf force=force at :1421, _index_pdf_incremental force=force at :1483). Provenance: commit f39a3a43 'feat(nexus-wk85): add --force CLI flags to all four nx index subcommands', dated 2026-03-03 — nearly five months BEFORE this bead was filed (2026-07-27), so the bead was filed against a state that already had the flags rather than describing a regression. Its premise line ('No CLI surface passes it') was simply not true at filing time. No code change made. If a specific force scenario still misbehaves, that is a different defect and wants its own bead with the failing invocation.

## VALIDATED 2026-07-27 — `force=True` is confirmed as the fix

Zoology (arXiv 2312.04927) could not be indexed by any CLI path after a gateway-timeout killed its
first run. Five attempts; four reported success and wrote nothing usable.

Calling the pipeline directly with force, after purging by content_hash:

    ids = col.get(where={"content_hash": sha256(pdf_bytes)}, limit=10000)["ids"]
    t3.delete_by_chunk_ids(COLL, ids)          # loop until empty — the get is non-deterministic
    index_pdf(P, corpus="dt", collection_name=COLL, force=True, extractor="mineru")
    # -> 400 chunks

Before vs after:

| | broken run | force=True |
|---|---|---|
| chunks in T3 | 108 (manifest claimed 515) | **394-400** |
| stored text | 147,994 chars | **535,713 chars** |
| main-body markers (`Arora`, `82%`, `Pile`, `perplexity`, `gated convolution`) | **all zero** | present (Mqar ×189, Hyena ×172, associative recall ×114) |
| thesis-query distance | 0.4742 (returned appendix math) | **0.1882** (returns the exact sentence) |

So `--force` is not a convenience flag — on this document it was the difference between a
plausible-looking index missing the entire paper and a correct one. Note acceptance item 2 held up
