title: [index] a failed index poisons the document permanently: manifest keeps dangling chashes, staleness check then treats it as up-to-date, and every re-index silently no-ops while reporting success
description:
Hit 2026-07-27 indexing a 69-page PDF (Zoology, arXiv 2312.04927) via `nx dt index`. Three
consecutive repair attempts all reported success and all did nothing. The document could not
be repaired by any supported command.

## The failure chain

1. **First index dies mid-write.** MinerU extraction + `/v1/vectors/upsert-chunks` returned
   `HTTP 504: Gateway Timeout` three times (backoff 5s, 10s); MinerU then reported
   `mineru_server_lost` at pages 49-50 and `PipelineCancelled`. Final line:
   `Indexed 0 record(s) (0 skipped, ..., 1 failed)`.

2. **But 207 chunks and a manifest were already committed.** `nx catalog show` reported
   `Chunks: 207` for a document whose index had just failed. There is no transaction spanning
   the chunk writes and the manifest, so a partial index leaves a *plausible-looking* catalog row.

3. **The manifest survives chunk deletion.** Deleting those 207 chunks from T3 (via
   `delete_by_chunk_ids`) left the manifest still listing all 207 chashes. Every one of them
   now hydrates to empty. `nx catalog show` still says `Chunks: 207`. Nothing reports the
   document as broken.

4. **The staleness check then locks the damage in.** Because the catalog row exists with a
   chunk_count and an unchanged source hash, the indexer's staleness path concludes
   "already indexed and unchanged" and writes NO chunks — while `nx dt index` still prints
   `Indexed 1 record(s) (0 skipped, ..., 1 written back to DT)` and performs the DT writeback.
   Ran twice with different extractors; both reported success; both wrote nothing.

Net: **a document whose index failed is permanently un-indexable by any supported command**,
and every attempt claims success. The only escape found was `nx catalog delete <tumbler>`
followed by a fresh index, which mints a new tumbler and drops any links the document had.

## Acceptance

1. **Make the manifest a truthful oracle.** Either write chunks+manifest transactionally, or
   have a failed/partial index roll the manifest back. A catalog row must not claim chunks
   that do not exist in T3.
2. **Staleness must verify, not assume.** The up-to-date decision currently trusts
   `chunk_count > 0` + source hash. It must confirm the manifest's chashes actually resolve in
   T3 (a cheap existence check, not a hydrate) before skipping.
3. **`--force` / `--reindex` on `nx dt index` and `nx index`.** There is currently no supported
   way to say "discard what you think you know and index this again". Deleting the catalog
   entry should not be the only recovery.
4. **Never report `Indexed 1 record(s)` when zero chunks were written.** The staleness skip is
   logged at debug (`dt_content_unchanged`) and invisible at normal verbosity; the summary line
   actively misreports it. Distinguish indexed / unchanged / failed in the summary.
5. **`nx catalog doctor` check for dangling manifests**: any document whose manifest chashes do
   not resolve in T3. This class is currently undetectable — see also the ghost class in
   `nx catalog reconcile` (GH #1397), which covers chunk_count>0 with an EMPTY manifest but not
   a POPULATED manifest full of dead chashes.

## Related defect: source-path chunk addressing is dead in service mode

Both `T3.ids_for_source(collection, source_path)` and `delete_by_source(collection, source_path)`
return **0** against the HTTP client, for both the `.dt-content` markdown path and a PDF path
(tested with and without the embedded-newline filename). So the natural "delete this document's
chunks and re-index" recovery is unavailable, and cleanup must fall back to content-based
attribution — reconstructing the live chunk set from every other document's manifest
(5,373 chashes across 46 docs) to distinguish true orphans. Same family as the
`orphan_backfill.py:130` service-mode crash on nexus-mok9x.

## Related defect: `--extractor docling` completes with unusable output and reports success

The `--help` presents docling as the safe recovery for MinerU failures ("formula-stripped, but
always completes"). On this paper it completed and produced **space-stripped** text —
`istheasetofthe`, `aspartofasequenceofinput` — heavy raw-LaTeX noise, and chunks carrying no
title (search rendered them as bare chashes). The document did not match a semantic query
quoting its own central finding verbatim. Nothing in the pipeline flags this; the run is
indistinguishable from success. A loud failure (MinerU) is strictly safer than a silent
quality collapse. Suggest a post-extraction sanity gate: e.g. whitespace ratio, mean token
length, or a dictionary-word fraction, failing the run rather than indexing garbage.
close_reason: ARC CLOSED e1884d4d, honestly: the parent symptom ('a failed index poisons the document permanently; every re-index silently no-ops while reporting success') is DEAD on a fence-aware engine, proven by falsification at BOTH layers it lived in — the fence layer (.1-.6: intent-vs-completion record, fail-closed /complete, three-way staleness, truthful summaries) and the buffer layer (gl99l: the resume path that could truncate-and-stamp now verifies WAL reality; the reset-free retry converges without --force). The gate (.7) pins all of it in CI with non-vacuity asserts and a fence-blinded kill control proving causation. AC1 closed BY the fence per the memo ruling (stated, not silent). Registered residuals, none silent: glzrn (availability hang, loud+doctor-visible, never silent-success), l6tr7 (mixed-refusal footer arithmetic, dormant pre-v0.1.62), azsyb (inline-ride direct coverage), 39upx(b) precondition armed, 308ph discriminator, ft7eg walk consolidation. Fence features activate for users at the v0.1.62 deploy; dormant-by-design against v0.1.61.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## CORRECTION: root cause is the T3-side staleness probe, not the catalog

My first read blamed the catalog manifest. Wrong. The actual gate is in
`src/nexus/doc_indexer.py` (~L775-785):

```python
incremental_where = _identity_where(sp, corpus, content_hash=content_hash)
existing = _vector_with_retry(col.get, where=incremental_where, include=["metadatas"], limit=1)
if not force and existing["metadatas"]:
    stored_hash  = existing["metadatas"][0].get("content_hash", "")
    stored_model = existing["metadatas"][0].get("embedding_model", "")
    if stored_hash == content_hash and stored_model == target_model:
        return 0
```

Staleness is decided by asking **T3** whether ANY chunk carries this source's
`content_hash` + embedding model — `limit=1`. It is not derived from the catalog at all.

That makes the failure mode sharper and worse than I described:

- **A single surviving chunk pins the whole document as "already indexed."** After a partial or
  botched index, ANY leftover chunk with the right content_hash — even one, even orphaned, even
  from a *different and worse* extractor run — makes every subsequent index a silent no-op.
- **Deleting the catalog entry does not help**, because the catalog is not consulted. I deleted
  tumbler 1.12.103, re-registered as 1.12.104, and still got zero chunks; MinerU never even ran
  (zero page lines in the log). The document registered clean and indexed nothing.
- In this case exactly **3** leftover docling chunks (out of ~27 that run wrote) were blocking a
  69-page re-index. Deleting those 3 unblocked it.

Enumerating them requires going around the CLI entirely, since `ids_for_source` /
`delete_by_source` are dead in service mode:

```python
col.get(where={"content_hash": sha256_of_file_bytes}, include=["metadatas"], limit=5000)
```

(content_hash is the sha256 of the SOURCE FILE bytes, not of extracted text — confirmed by the
match surviving an extractor change from mineru to docling.)

### Revised acceptance

- Item 2 restated: the staleness probe must not accept a `limit=1` sample as proof the document
  is fully indexed. At minimum compare the found chunk COUNT against the catalog manifest, and
  treat a mismatch as stale. A one-chunk existence probe cannot distinguish "fully indexed" from
  "3 chunks survived a failed run".
- Item 3 gains urgency: **`force` already exists as a parameter on the indexing pipeline but is
  not exposed on any CLI surface.** Wiring `--force` through `nx index` and `nx dt index` is a
  small change that converts this from unrecoverable to trivially recoverable.
- New: `nx t3` needs a supported `--by-content-hash` enumerate/delete, since that is the only
  working handle on "this source's chunks" in service mode.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## SECOND silent-data-loss mechanism: manifest says 515, T3 holds 108, main body absent

After clearing the staleness blockers, a clean `nx dt index --extractor mineru` ran to
completion — `MinerU: 69/69 done`, `Indexed 1 record(s)`. Every surface reported success.
It was still wrong.

**Measured on tumbler 1.12.104:**

| | |
|---|---|
| manifest (`get_chunk_chashes`) | **515** |
| chunks actually in T3 (`col.get(where={"content_hash": h})`) | **108** |
| total stored text | 147,994 chars |

**Content check across all stored text — the robust signal, independent of any count:**

```
'Tim' -> 0        'Rice' -> 0         '82%' -> 0        'Arora' -> 0
'Eyuboglu' -> 0   'Zoology' -> 0      'abstract' -> 0   'perplexity' -> 0
'Pile' -> 0       'gated convolution' -> 0
'associative recall' -> 16            'Hyena' -> 4
```

Zero occurrences of any main-body marker. Only appendix theory. Retrieval agrees: queries
quoting the abstract's own claims, and the Figure-1 "Tim/Rice" example, return nothing or return
only appendix math — even at `threshold=0.95` (72 hits, all tables/theory/appendix).

**The entire main paper (pages 1-11) is missing while the run reported success.**

### Strong hypothesis (evidence-backed, not confirmed)

`_upsert_skip_reembed` (doc_indexer.py ~L552-643) probes `db.existing_ids(collection, ids)` and
splits:

```python
new_idx = [i for i, cid in enumerate(ids) if cid not in present]
old_idx = [i for i, cid in enumerate(ids) if cid in present]
if new_idx: db.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings(...)   # content written
if old_idx: db.update_chunks(...)                    # METADATA ONLY — no content
return len(new_idx)
```

Chunks judged "already present" take a **metadata-only** path that writes no content. If the
probe reports chunks that were deleted from T3, their content is never written and the loss is
silent.

The distribution fits exactly: the surviving 108 chunks correspond to appendix pages ~49-69 —
the region the earlier partial run (which died at page 49) had NEVER indexed, so their chashes
were genuinely new. Everything pages 1-48 — the whole main paper — had been written by that
partial run, deleted by me, and was then skipped as "present".

I could not confirm the probe is stale: a direct `existing_ids` test returned 0-of-50 for
known-missing chashes. But that test is untrustworthy because **`col.get(where=...)` is
non-deterministic** — successive identical calls returned 515-equivalent and 108 rows. That
non-determinism is itself worth a finding: any reconciliation built on that query will produce
different answers on different runs.

### Added acceptance

6. **A metadata-only update path must verify the row exists.** `update_chunks` against a
   non-existent id must fail loudly or fall through to a full upsert — never silently no-op.
7. **Reconcile manifest vs T3 after every index**, and fail the run on mismatch. `Indexed 1
   record(s)` while 407 of 515 chunks are absent is the worst outcome in this whole bead: the
   document looks indexed, is searchable, returns plausible chunks, and is missing its entire
   substance.
8. **Investigate `col.get(where=...)` non-determinism in service mode** — returning different
   row counts for identical calls undermines every audit/GC/reconcile verb built on it.

### Corrections to earlier comments on this bead

- My "docling produces uniquely mangled output" claim was **overstated**. Measuring MinerU's
  output properly: median space ratio **0.135** (normal English ~0.16), 73.7% of chunks above
  0.12, only 9.6% severely space-stripped — i.e. mostly clean, with stripping concentrated in
  LaTeX-dense appendix regions. I had sampled math-heavy chunks both times and generalized. I
  can no longer measure docling directly (those chunks are deleted), so the docling-vs-mineru
  quality comparison is **withdrawn** — what stands is that neither extractor's output is
  validated, and a post-extraction sanity gate is still warranted.
- The claim that deleting the catalog entry forces a fresh index is **wrong** and was already
  corrected: the staleness probe reads T3, not the catalog.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## Correction: `col.get(where=...)` non-determinism was in-flight, not inherent

An earlier comment on this bead claimed identical `col.get(where={"content_hash": h})` calls
returned 515-equivalent and 108 rows, and warned that any verb built on that query is unreliable.
**That overstates it.** Re-tested once the document settled — five identical queries:

    [394, 394, 394, 394, 394]
    union 394 | intersection 394 | unstable ids 0
    manifest 394 | manifest∖union 0 | union∖manifest 0

Stable and exact. The variance was eventual consistency **while an index was in flight**, not a
property of the query. Same for the transient manifest 400 vs T3 394 (delta 6) immediately
post-index — both settled at 394, no chunks lost.

Revised acceptance item 8: **withdraw** "investigate col.get non-determinism" as a standalone
defect. Replace with: the reconcile check in item 7 must run **after writes settle**, and must not
treat a mid-write delta as data loss.

**This does not weaken 6b.** The metadata-only-upsert loss was established by a *content* check —
zero occurrences of `Arora`, `82%`, `Pile`, `perplexity`, `gated convolution` across 148K chars of
stored text — which is timing-independent. It required `force=True` to fix and produced 3.6× the
stored text (147,994 → 535,713 chars). Counts were the symptom; content was the proof.

**Sharpening for item 7:** make the post-index gate a *content* assertion where possible (does the
stored text contain the document's title/authors?), not only a count reconciliation. The count
check is subject to in-flight consistency; the content check is not, and it is the only check that
caught this class.

## Final state of the two documents from this incident

| | 1.12.102 (CACM) | 1.12.104 (Zoology) |
|---|---|---|
| manifest vs T3 | 28 / 28 | 394 / 394 |
| own-thesis query | 0.2132 | 0.2035 |
| known-junk query | no match | n/a |

Both repaired, verified, linked, and analysed. Full record: T2
`nexus/forensics-2026-07-27-ingest-pipeline-failure-chain` +
`nexus/forensics-2026-07-27-addendum-verification-outcomes`.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and AC2's stated mechanism is WRONG, while AC2's stated REMEDY is right. Recording before implementing, per the bead's own warning against fixing against a hypothesis.

THE BEAD SAYS: "Because the catalog row exists with a chunk_count and an unchanged source hash, the indexer's staleness path concludes 'already indexed and unchanged'."

THAT IS NOT WHAT THE CODE DOES. Neither staleness gate consults the catalog at all. Both query T3:

  _index_document        doc_indexer.py:765-777   (markdown/prose path)
  _index_pdf_incremental doc_indexer.py:1388-1401 (the PDF path this bug hit)

both via _identity_where (doc_indexer.py:102-118), which returns exactly:

    {"content_hash": content_hash}

and both call col.get(where=..., include=["metadatas"], LIMIT=1).

So the skip fires iff AT LEAST ONE chunk in that collection carries this content_hash. chunk_count, the manifest, and the catalog row play NO part in the decision. If the 207 chunks had truly all been deleted, neither gate could have skipped — which is why the reported symptom did not reproduce from a first reading of the code.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM: **limit=1 makes ONE surviving chunk mark the WHOLE document fresh.**

The gate asks "does any chunk with this content_hash exist?" It does not ask "are this document's chunks all present?" So an index that dies mid-write — committing an arbitrary SUBSET of the document's chunks — leaves the document permanently "up to date": every subsequent re-index finds one of the survivors and returns 0. That matches every observed symptom (index failed with chunks committed; repeated re-indexes wrote nothing and reported success; the manifest listed more chashes than T3 held) WITHOUT requiring the catalog-trust story, and it explains why deleting chunks appeared not to help: unless the deletion removed EVERY chunk carrying that content_hash, one survivor re-arms the skip.

COROLLARY, worth stating because it inverts the recovery advice: partial deletion is worse than none. Removing 206 of 207 chunks leaves the document both broken AND still-skipped.

SO AC2 IS CORRECT AS WRITTEN AS A REMEDY — "confirm the manifest's chashes actually resolve in T3 (a cheap existence check, not a hydrate) before skipping" — it is the DIAGNOSIS above it that needs correcting. The fix is to compare the EXPECTED chash set (the manifest) against what is PRESENT in T3, and skip only when the manifest is fully satisfied.

THE VERIFICATION PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS AS OF TODAY: the nexus-5xn3k AC5 doctor check just landed (_check_dangling_manifests, health.py) computes exactly this difference — referenced_by_manifest - present_in_T3 — from cat.chashes_for_collection + t3.list_chunks_with_metadata. The staleness gate wants the same comparison scoped to one document. Sharing the primitive is what stops doctor and the indexer disagreeing about whether a document is whole.

NOT YET DONE, and each wants care:
  - Cost: the current gate is one indexed lookup with limit=1; the honest version needs the document's manifest chashes plus a presence check. Per-document, not per-collection, so scope the T3 read.
  - AC3 is ALREADY SATISFIED: --force reaches the staleness gate on all four index surfaces (verified while closing nexus-16f77 — commit f39a3a43, 2026-03-03). The bead's "there is currently no supported way" was untrue at filing.
  - The two related defects in the bead (service-mode delete_by_source/ids_for_source returning 0; --extractor docling producing space-stripped output while reporting success) are UNTOUCHED and independent of this root cause.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31 (3 commits, unmerged, worktree agent-a8d3df8a65389b13d off origin/develop). DO NOT CLOSE ON MERGE — conexus/ loads from the pinned release tag, so this is inert until the next plugin release; declared in conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md.

Direction 1 taken. Direction 3 is REFUTED: the input is fully introspectable.

Two things worth keeping that are not in the diff:

## 1. A latent-but-UNREACHABLE parse bug in subagent-start-stamp.sh, deliberately NOT fixed

Both stamp and dispatch hooks parsed their python-extracted fields with
IFS=$'\t' read. Tab is IFS *whitespace*, so bash COLLAPSES empty fields and
shifts every later value one position left. In the new dispatch hook this was
live enough to matter — it made a fail-open pin green for the WRONG reason (a
payload with no session_id exited at the tool-name gate holding 'Agent' in its
session slot, so mutating the guard the test was named for left it green). Fixed
there with a US (0x1f) delimiter, which is not IFS whitespace.

I then 'fixed' the identical construct in subagent-start-stamp.sh and reverted
it, because I could not falsify it: with only THREE fields, every possible shift
empties the last field, the all-three-non-empty guard absorbs it, and nothing is
written. Mutating the stamp back to IFS=tab left all 11 of its tests green
INCLUDING the new one I had just written for it. Shipping an unfalsifiable pin
plus preventive scope in a file outside this bead was the wrong trade, so both
came out.

It becomes REACHABLE the moment a 4th field is added to that parse. Whoever does
that should switch the delimiter in the same change.

## 2. The census/undeclared awk is the load-bearing part, and it is subtle

Recognition had to move from the START line into END, because an EXPECT row for a
START row's agent_type can appear anywhere in the file and a single pass cannot
classify a row as it arrives. One trap found in review of my own code: awk READS
auto-vivify keys, and term[] is read in the END loop, so 'id in term' is worthless
there — the code carries an explicit hasterm[] set for that reason.

title: [catalog] Make tumbler allocation self-healing + observable: eliminate the next_seq wedge class for good (sweep all owners, expose next_seq, doctor check)
description:
Durable remediation for the failure class diagnosed in **nexus-pbawi**, where owner
`1.12` (dt) was permanently unable to register any document. That bead fixed one owner
by hand; this one closes the class.

## The class, in one paragraph

`CatalogRepository.registerDocument` claims `catalog_owners.next_seq` under
`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, builds `tumbler = prefix + "." + (next_seq + 1)`, and inserts.
The INSERT's only `ON CONFLICT` arbiter is `(TENANT_ID, SOURCE_URI)`, but the only unique
key on `catalog_documents` is `(tenant_id, tumbler)` — so a tumbler collision has no arm
and escapes as a bare `HTTP 409: integrity constraint violation`. The `next_seq` increment
shares the failing transaction and rolls back with it, so the allocator never advances:
**one drifted owner is a permanent, total outage for that owner, and retry can never clear
it.** Same shape in `registerDocumentMany` (second claim site, ~L677).

## Why it cannot currently be audited

`next_seq` is exposed on **no read path**. `ownerByPrefix` (~L2484) does not even SELECT
it; `/owners/show`, `/owners/list`, and `nx catalog owners --json` all omit it. The only
way to tell a drifted owner from a healthy one today is to attempt a real registration and
see whether it 409s — a mutation used as a diagnostic. That unobservability is why the
original incident took a long investigation to localize, and it is why we cannot currently
answer "how many other owners are already wedged?"

## Acceptance

1. **Self-healing allocation.** On a `(tenant_id, tumbler)` collision, floor `next_seq` to
   `max(child seq)` over ALL rows for the owner **including tombstones** (the PK does not
   exclude them, unlike the source_uri partial index) and retry. A single drifted owner
   must never be a permanent outage. Apply at BOTH claim sites.
2. **Allocator cannot rewind.** Advance `next_seq` so a failed insert cannot roll the
   counter back into a permanent loop — separate transaction, or bump-on-conflict.
3. **Expose `next_seq`** on `ownerByPrefix` / `/owners/show` / `/owners/list` /
   `nx catalog owners --json`. Non-negotiable prerequisite for 4 and 5.
4. **`nx catalog doctor --next-seq-drift`.** Detect: any owner where
   `next_seq <= max child tumbler` (counting tombstones). Read-only, per RDR-185 rung
   shape. Converge step floors via the existing `GREATEST` upsert.
5. **One-shot sweep of the live cloud catalog.** 47 owners currently hold live docs; an
   unknown number may already be wedged and will surface as the same opaque 409 the next
   time anyone indexes into them. Floor every owner once (safe by construction — see
   below), and REPORT which ones were actually below their high-water mark so the blast
   radius of the original incident is known rather than guessed.
6. **Propagate the PG constraint name into the 409 body.** Independent of everything
   above. The bare "integrity constraint violation" is undiagnosable from the client and
   cost the entire original investigation.
7. **Regression test** beyond the existing ETL-time coverage
   (`test_next_seq_reconciled_no_tumbler_collision_post_cutover`): set an owner's
   `next_seq` below its high-water mark at RUNTIME, assert register still succeeds. The
   current test only covers the cutover path, which is why runtime drift slipped through.

## The safe primitive already exists

`importOwnersBatch` (~L2947) upserts `next_seq` with `EX_OWN_SEQ_GREATEST` —
`GREATEST(excluded, existing)`, monotonic, can only raise, never reuses a tumbler. Reachable
at `POST /v1/catalog/import/owner`. This is what `catalog_etl._reconcile_next_seq` drives at
cutover and what unwedged 1.12 by hand. The sweep in item 5 should use it. Gaps are
harmless; the invariant forbids REUSE, not gaps.

## Notes

- Deployed cloud engine is **0.1.57** (`nx service probe`) and carries the defect. No
  self-healing commit exists in the tree either (`git log CatalogRepository.java`).
- `catalog_owners.py:320` already flags the client-side half as CRITICAL: "next_seq is
  JSONL-only state (not in the snapshot) ... snapshot defaults next_seq=1".
- Runbook for the manual unwedge, pending this fix:
  T2 `nexus/runbook-unwedge-catalog-owner-next-seq-drift`.

## Collateral (tracked on nexus-pbawi, repeated here because they gate recovery)

- `nx dt index` exits SUCCESS when the register failed — writes T3 chunks, logs
  `preflight_register_failed` as a warning, prints "Indexed 0 (1 skipped)". Silent orphaning.
- `nx catalog orphan-backfill dt-link`, the documented recovery for those orphans, crashes
  in service mode: `AttributeError: 'HttpVectorClient' object has no attribute '_client'`

comments.text:
THE AUDIT THIS BEAD SCOPES IS DONE, 2026-07-31 (read-only pass; fixes not yet written).
Every ON CONFLICT arbiter in CatalogRepository.java cross-walked against its target
table's FULL unique-constraint set. Result below is the worklist.

## The class lives in exactly TWO tables

catalog_owners — THREE unique keys, ONE arbitrated (sites :306 :495 :653 :3568 :3594,
all using the PK):
  1. catalog_owners_pk               (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix)        HANDLED
  2. catalog_owners_unique_name_type (tenant_id, name, owner_type)      UNHANDLED -> nexus-jq53b
  3. idx_catalog_owners_repo_hash    (tenant_id, repo_hash) partial     UNHANDLED -> nexus-z3ssg (NEW)

catalog_documents — TWO unique keys, each site arbitrates only one:
  1. catalog_documents_pk                     (tenant_id, tumbler)      sites :403 :3650 :3700
  2. ux_catalog_documents_live_source_uri     partial unique            sites :577 :793
  Each set of sites is exposed to the OTHER constraint. That is nexus-pbawi exactly:
  registerDocument arbitrates on source_uri while the tumbler PK is what fires.

## Verified CLEAN — do not spend time here

catalog_links            PK (tenant_id, id) + unique (tenant_id, from, to, link_type);
                         arbiters use the 4-col unique, sites :1780 :3770 :3788
catalog_document_chunks  PK (tenant_id, doc_id, position); arbiters match, :2244 :3838 :3862
catalog_collections      PK (tenant_id, name); arbiters match, :2631 :2960 :3929 :3967
catalog_meta             PK (tenant_id, key); arbiter matches, :3052

## Why fixing table-wise beats fixing the three known instances

pbawi, jq53b and z3ssg are not three bugs. They are three sightings of one rule violation:
the arbiter was chosen against the key the author had in mind rather than against the
table's complete unique-key set. Fixing them one at a time leaves the fourth sighting to
be found in production — z3ssg was found only because the audit enumerated rather than
reacted, and its DDL comment says it is a TOCTOU guard, i.e. it fires under exactly the
concurrency that produced jq53b's CI flake.

## Suggested shape of the fix

Per table, one decision about what "already exists" means, applied at every site, plus a
test that drives EACH unique key to conflict and asserts the upsert converges instead of
raising 23505. The non-vacuity requirement is that the test fail if any one arbiter is
narrowed back.

Same defect shape as nexus-u4e20 / nexus-v6za0 in the same file: a predicate naming one
notion when the domain has more than one.

comments.text:
RUNBOOK — nexus-0ehwe item 5, rehearsed end-to-end 2026-08-02 against a throwaway dev-jar
service (develop 49f00284, jar rebuilt via scripts/build-gate-jar.sh, stamped 0.1.61). Full
transcript + the rehearsal script are below; this is now a verified copy-paste runbook, not
a first execution.

## THE CLOUD INVOCATION

```
curl -sS -X POST "$CLOUD_BASE_URL/v1/catalog/owners/sweep_next_seq_drift" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NX_CLOUD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

No request body fields — the sweep always covers the whole tenant the bearer token resolves
to (same tenant-derivation as every other /v1/catalog/* route; no separate tenant param).
Only POST is accepted (GET -> 405, pinned by CatalogHandlerSweepNextSeqDriftTest but not
re-verified live in this rehearsal — see "Not verified" below).

Expected report shape (verified live, see transcript):

```json
{
  "checked": <int>,               // owners actually examined this pass, tenant-wide
  "healed":  <int>,                // count of owners.length — how many were actually drifted
  "owners": [
    {
      "tumbler_prefix": "<owner prefix>",
      "next_seq":       <int>,     // the drifted value BEFORE flooring
      "high_water":     <int>,     // max child tumbler seq, tombstones included
      "floored_to":     <int>      // what next_seq was set to (== high_water)
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

`owners[]` is the blast-radius answer nexus-0ehwe item 5 demands: every entry was an owner
that was actually below its high-water mark, i.e. would have 409'd opaquely on its next
registration before this sweep ran. An owner NOT present in `owners[]` was checked and found
healthy — it does not mean "not checked"; `checked` is the total examined.

## PRECONDITIONS

- Cloud engine must be running a tag that includes commit `55615902` (feat(catalog):
  all-owners next_seq drift sweep — nexus-0ehwe item 5). That commit landed on develop
  2026-08-02 08:19:43-07:00, AFTER the `v0.1.61` tag (cut 2026-07-31 at 848a531c) — so
  v0.1.61 does NOT carry the sweep route and will 404 on this call. The next cut is
  `v0.1.62`, currently blocked by design on a conexus release carrying `9ba82a3b` (the
  client-precondition gate) landing first. Do not attempt this invocation against the
  currently-deployed v0.1.61 engine — it will 404, not silently no-op.
- `Authorization: Bearer` must be a token that resolves to the target cloud tenant (the one
  holding the 47 live owners named in the bead). No admin/elevated scope beyond a normal
  catalog bearer token was needed in rehearsal — the route has no additional auth check
  beyond the standard tenant-resolving bearer (confirmed by reading
  CatalogHandler.handleOwnersSweepNextSeqDrift: no role/admin check, just method==POST).

## COUNT SEMANTICS vs the 47-owner cloud expectation

`checked` counts every owner row in the tenant examined during this pass (one deleted
between the initial list and its probe is silently skipped, per
CatalogRepository.sweepNextSeqDrift's javadoc) — so on the real cloud tenant, expect
`checked` to land at or near 47 (all owners with live docs), possibly higher if there are
owners with zero docs that still exist as rows. `healed` and `owners[]` are the actual
finding: how many of those 47 were already drifted. Item 5's own framing was "an unknown
number may already be wedged" — this call is what turns that into a known number.

## IDEMPOTENCE

Safe to run twice (or on a schedule). A second run against an already-healed tenant reports
`healed: 0, owners: []` (verified live — see transcript run 2 below). The floor operation is
monotonic (`GREATEST(next_seq, high_water)`), so re-running never re-issues or perturbs a
tumbler.

## NOT VERIFIED IN THIS REHEARSAL

- The GET-not-allowed 405 path (unit-tested in `CatalogHandlerSweepNextSeqDriftTest.
  sweep_getIsNotAllowed`, not re-driven live here — out of scope for this rehearsal, which
  targeted the POST invocation itself).
- Behavior against a tenant with an owner whose row was deleted mid-sweep (covered by the
  repository javadoc's `checked` semantics, not independently reproduced live).
- Any cloud-specific auth/edge behavior (rate limiting, WAF, edge stubbing) — nexus-bwulw's
  lesson applies: an engine-direct gate does not prove client/edge visibility. Recommend
  running `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh` is unrelated to this route but the same
  caution applies — verify the edge actually proxies this route before trusting a first
  cloud invocation blindly.

## REHEARSAL TRANSCRIPT (throwaway dev-jar service, scratch config dir, PG bundle)

Provisioning followed tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh steps 1-4: scratch NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR ->
`nx init --service` -> `nx daemon service stop` (nexus-4e96a workaround: init auto-starts
the pinned v0.1.61 release binary, which does NOT serve the fence-aware routes this sweep's
sibling work added) -> dev jar rebuilt via `scripts/build-gate-jar.sh` (stamped 0.1.61,
release.properties restored on exit) -> `NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR=... nx daemon service start` ->
lease read from `$SCRATCH/storage_service_addr.*`.

Seeded 3 owners under the local install's single tenant (`default` — confirmed live via
direct psql; NOT `default` by assumption, by reading the row):
  - A (2 docs, high-water=2), B (1 doc, high-water=1), C (0 docs, high-water=0, healthy)

Drift driven exactly like `NextSeqSweepTest.driftNextSeq`: direct psql against the scratch
PG (bundled binaries under `$SCRATCH/pg-bundle/.../bin/psql`, credentials from
`$SCRATCH/pg_credentials`) — `UPDATE nexus.catalog_owners SET next_seq=0 WHERE tumbler_prefix
IN (A, B)`. C left untouched.

### [1] /health + fence-route discriminator
```
GET /health -> 200 {"status":"ok","db":"up"}
POST /v1/catalog/index-run/begin -> 200 {"ok":true}   (non-404 proves the fence-aware dev
                                                          jar is serving, not the pinned
                                                          v0.1.61 release binary)
```

### [2] Seed
```
POST /v1/catalog/owners/upsert x3 -> 200 {"ok":true} each  (A=7.572311, B=7.572312, C=7.572313)
POST /v1/catalog/doc/register (A, doc 1) -> 200 {"tumbler":"7.572311.1"}
POST /v1/catalog/doc/register (A, doc 2) -> 200 {"tumbler":"7.572311.2"}
POST /v1/catalog/doc/register (B, doc 1) -> 200 {"tumbler":"7.572312.1"}
```

### Drift via direct psql (IMPORTANT — RLS gotcha found live)
`nexus.catalog_owners` carries `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with policy
`tenant_id = current_setting('nexus.tenant', true)` (catalog-001-baseline.xml). This applies
even to the schema-owning `nexus_admin` role because of FORCE (not just ENABLE). A raw
`UPDATE`/`SELECT` with no session GUC set returned **zero rows silently** — no error, just
an empty result, on real data — until `SET nexus.tenant='default';` was added to the SAME
psql session (both statements must go through the same `-c` invocation / connection, since
SET is session-scoped). This is a documented trap for whoever runs the cloud invocation's
own verification queries directly against PG: the sweep route itself doesn't need this
(it's called via HTTP through the bearer token, which resolves tenant server-side), but ANY
direct psql cross-check against catalog_owners does.

```
SET nexus.tenant='default'; UPDATE nexus.catalog_owners SET next_seq=0
  WHERE tumbler_prefix IN ('7.572311','7.572312');
-> UPDATE 2

SET nexus.tenant='default'; SELECT tumbler_prefix, next_seq FROM nexus.catalog_owners
  WHERE tumbler_prefix IN ('7.572311','7.572312','7.572313') ORDER BY tumbler_prefix;
 tumbler_prefix | next_seq
-----------------+----------
 7.572311        |        0
 7.572312        |        0
 7.572313        |        0     <- C's own DEFAULT (never registered, so next_seq starts
                                    at 0 == its high_water of 0 -> healthy, not drifted)
```

### [3] THE INVOCATION — first run
```
POST /v1/catalog/owners/sweep_next_seq_drift {}
-> 200
{"checked":3,"healed":2,"owners":[
  {"tumbler_prefix":"7.572311","next_seq":0,"high_water":2,"floored_to":2},
  {"tumbler_prefix":"7.572312","next_seq":0,"high_water":1,"floored_to":1}
]}
```
Assertions verified: checked==3, healed==2, owners[] contains exactly A and B with correct
next_seq/high_water/floored_to; C is absent from owners[].

### [4] Idempotence — second run
```
POST /v1/catalog/owners/sweep_next_seq_drift {}
-> 200
{"checked":3,"healed":0,"owners":[]}
```

### [5] Post-sweep register under owner A
```
POST /v1/catalog/doc/register (A, doc 3) -> 200 {"tumbler":"7.572311.3"}
```
Succeeded with the NEXT tumbler in sequence (`.3`, following the pre-drift `.1`/`.2`) — no
collision, confirming the wedge class is dead for a swept owner.

`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hal-hildebrand-git-nexus/a616e3fb-4622-46ce-bb65-c6f34f04f060/scratchpad/0ehwe-rehearsal.sh`
(session scratchpad — not committed to the repo; paste its contents into the relay if a

title: [catalog] registerDocument wedges an owner permanently: next_seq stranded below high-water mark, tumbler PK collision unhandled by the source_uri-only ON CONFLICT arbiter (owner 1.12/dt)
description:
Found 2026-07-27 running `nx dt index` on a DEVONthink web archive (CACM
"Formal Reasoning Meets LLMs", DT UUID 00327AAD-83AE-4E82-ABF3-55F57D9964AB).

## Symptom

`POST /v1/catalog/doc/register` -> `HTTP 409: integrity constraint violation`
for EVERY register under owner `1.12`, regardless of title, file_path, corpus,
content_type, or physical_collection.

Inside `nx dt index` this surfaces as a non-fatal `preflight_register_failed`
warning. The run then CONTINUES, writes the T3 chunks, and reports:

    Indexed 0 record(s) (1 skipped, 0 semantically linked, 0 written back to DT, 0 highlights ingested)

with a trailing `dt_stamp_no_entry_found` warning. Exit status is success.

Net effect: **orphan chunks in T3 with no catalog Document** — searchable, but
no tumbler, therefore no `--link-semantic` edges and no `--writeback` to DT.
The summary line reads like a benign skip, so the data loss is easy to miss.

## Established by probe

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| register owner 1.12, real title + real path | 409 |
| register owner 1.12, novel title + novel path | 409 |
| register owner 1.11, novel title + novel path | OK -> 1.11.354 |

Fault is **owner-scoped to 1.12**, not a collision with the incoming document.

Ruled out:
- **Tombstone reuse.** Deleted 1.11.354, re-registered -> got 1.11.**355**.
  Allocation is monotonic and does not retry tombstoned tumblers, so a
  soft-deleted row at 1.12.54 is not the mechanism.
- **Duplicate owner rows.** `nx catalog owners | grep -w dt` -> exactly one
  (`1.12 curator dt`); no duplicate owner tumblers in the full list.
- **Visible collision.** dt has 44 live docs, max child `1.12.53`;
  `nx catalog show 1.12.54` / `1.12.55` -> Not found.

Root cause NOT identified. The storage service masks the constraint as a bare
"integrity constraint violation" with no constraint name in the HTTP body, and
nothing lands in ~/.config/nexus/logs/ (storage_service_jar.log stale since
Jul 1).

## Acceptance

1. Root-cause and fix the 409 so `nx dt index` registers under owner 1.12.
2. **Propagate the PG constraint name into the 409 response body.** Independent
   of root cause — the current message is undiagnosable from the client and
   cost most of the investigation time.
3. `nx dt index` must NOT report success when the catalog register failed.
   Either fail loud, or report a distinct non-zero "indexed chunks but no
   catalog identity" outcome. Silent orphaning is the real severity here.
4. Regression test: register N docs under a curator owner with existing live
   docs and tombstones, assert success.

## Blocked recovery path (fix together)

`nx catalog orphan-backfill dt-link <collection> --owner 1.12` — the documented
repair for exactly this orphan state — crashes in service mode:

    File "nexus/catalog/orphan_backfill.py", line 130, in gather_titled_chunks
      col = t3_db._client.get_collection(name=collection)
    AttributeError: 'HttpVectorClient' object has no attribute '_client'

It reaches for the local Chroma client API on an HTTP client. This is what makes
the primary defect unrecoverable rather than merely annoying. Also needs
`knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` added to `DEFAULT_COLLECTION_OWNER`
in src/nexus/catalog/orphan_backfill.py (currently errors "Unknown owner for
collection").

## Minor, same surface

`nx dt index --collection` requires the four-segment conformant name
(`knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1`). The --help example shows
`--collection knowledge__delos`, a two-segment form the vector service rejects
with `HTTP 400: not four-segment conformant`. Fix the help text or accept the
logical form.

## Current orphan state to reconcile

`knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` holds 31 chunks titled "Formal
Reasoning Meets LLMs: Toward AI for Mathematics and Verification -
Communications of the ACM" with no catalog Document. Re-running `nx dt index`
after the fix should reconcile them idempotently (chash-keyed) — worth using as
the verification case.

T2: nexus/defect-catalog-register-409-owner-dt-1.12
close_reason: Closed against acceptance items 1+2+4: wedge structurally fixed by claimNextSeq resolve-before-write under FOR UPDATE (5c8c978e both claim sites, verified by substantive-critic 2026-08-02), 409 body carries the PG constraint name (570def02), runtime-drift regression tests shipped (NextSeqSelfHealingTest + UniqueRaceRetry exhaustion test in 55615902). The all-owners sweep (0ehwe item 5, 55615902) turns this incident class from guessed to enumerated. CLIENT-side residuals SPLIT, not dropped: item 3 (nx dt index reports success when register failed) -> nexus-2xu6t (P1); orphan-backfill service-mode crash -> nexus-ne2ux (P2). Force past the 0ehwe dep: 0ehwe stays open ONLY for the live-cloud sweep invocation (HAL relay after next engine tag), which is 0ehwe's own item, not this bead's.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-07-27, from source)

`CatalogRepository.registerDocument` (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java, ~L465-520):

```java
long seq = ctx.select(NEXT_SEQ)...forUpdate().fetchOne(NEXT_SEQ);
ctx.update(CATALOG_OWNERS).set(NEXT_SEQ, seq + 1)...execute();
String tumbler = ownerPrefix + "." + (seq + 1);
int inserted = ctx.insertInto(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS, ...)
    .onConflict(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS.TENANT_ID, CATALOG_DOCUMENTS.SOURCE_URI)   // <-- ONLY arbiter
    .where(DELETED_AT.isNull().and(SOURCE_URI.ne("")))
    .doNothing()
    .execute();
```

Two facts combine into a permanent wedge:

1. **The only unique key on `catalog_documents` is `(tenant_id, tumbler)`** — stated
   verbatim in catalog-016-source-uri-unique.xml's header. The `ON CONFLICT` arbiter
   added by nexus-78n33 covers **only** `(tenant_id, source_uri)`. A tumbler PK
   collision has no arm and escapes the handler as a bare integrity-constraint
   violation -> HTTP 409.

2. **The `next_seq` increment shares the transaction with the failing INSERT**, so it
   rolls back with it. The owner's `next_seq` never advances past the occupied slot.
   Every subsequent register recomputes the SAME tumbler and fails identically —
   forever. Retry cannot clear it; this is why the failure is payload-independent and
   permanent rather than transient.

Owner `1.12` (dt) has 44 live docs, max tumbler `1.12.53`. Its `catalog_owners.next_seq`
is stranded at some value N where `1.12.N+1` is already occupied (live or tombstoned —
the PK does not exclude tombstones, unlike the source_uri partial index).

This is precisely the class `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_etl.py::_reconcile_next_seq` exists
to prevent — "Reconcile next_seq on each owner so post-cutover tumbler allocation can
neither collide with NOR reuse a migrated tumbler. The SQLite .catalog.db has no next_seq
column." Regression coverage exists at
`tests/db/test_catalog_etl.py::test_next_seq_reconciled_no_tumbler_collision_post_cutover`
("Without next_seq reconciliation every imported owner lands [in collision]"). Owner 1.12
either post-dates that reconciliation or was missed by it.

Note `catalog_owners.py:320` flags the same hazard client-side as CRITICAL: "preserve
next_seq from the most-recent existing OwnerRecord. next_seq is JSONL-only state (not in
the snapshot) ... snapshot defaults next_seq=1".

## Fix, in priority order

1. **Handle the tumbler collision.** Add a `(tenant_id, tumbler)` conflict arm that
   re-claims — or better, make allocation self-healing: on collision, floor `next_seq` to
   `SELECT max(seq) FROM catalog_documents WHERE tumbler LIKE ownerPrefix||'.%'` (INCLUDING
   tombstones) and retry. A single wedged owner should never be a permanent outage.
2. **Advance next_seq in its own committed transaction, or bump on conflict**, so a failed
   insert cannot rewind the allocator into a permanent loop.
3. **Propagate the PG constraint name into the 409 body.** The bare "integrity constraint
   violation" is undiagnosable from the client and cost the entire investigation.
4. **Expose an operator repair verb** — e.g. `nx catalog doctor --next-seq-drift` (detect:
   any owner whose next_seq <= max child tumbler) plus a converge step. Today the only
   reconciliation lives inside the ETL path, unreachable once cutover is done.
5. `nx dt index` must not report success when the register failed (see original description).

## Immediate unblock for this tenant (cloud)

Server-side only — no client verb reaches it:
`UPDATE nexus.catalog_owners SET next_seq = <max child tumbler for 1.12> WHERE tumbler_prefix='1.12' AND tenant_id=<tenant>;`
computed over ALL rows including tombstones.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## UNBLOCKED 2026-07-27 — repair verified, defect still open

`importOwnersBatch` (CatalogRepository ~L2947) upserts with
`.set(NEXT_SEQ, EX_OWN_SEQ_GREATEST)` — `GREATEST(excluded, existing)`, monotonic,
can only raise. That is the flooring primitive `_reconcile_next_seq` drives, and it is
reachable from any client at `POST /v1/catalog/import/owner`. Applied:

    POST /v1/catalog/import/owner
    {"tumbler_prefix":"1.12","name":"dt","owner_type":"curator",
     "repo_hash":"","description":"","repo_root":"","head_hash":"","next_seq":100}
    -> {"imported": 1}

Chose 100 because the PK counts tombstones (unlike the source_uri partial index), so the
true high-water mark is unobservable from the client; live max was 53. Gaps are harmless —
the invariant forbids REUSE, not gaps.

Immediately after: register succeeded (`1.12.101`), and a full
`nx dt index --dt-content --link-semantic --writeback --highlights` reported
`Indexed 1 record(s) (0 skipped, 1 from DT content, 1 semantically linked, 1 written back
to DT, 0 highlights ingested)` — tumbler `1.12.102`, 70 chunks, `relates` edge to
`1.12.46` via `dt_similar`, `nx-indexed` + `nx-tumbler:1.12.102` stamped back onto the DT
record. The 31 orphan chunks reconciled.

**This is a workaround on one owner, not the fix.** Still open:

- Any owner can still be wedged permanently the same way, and the only escape is an
  operator who knows about `/import/owner`. Fixes 1-2 in the previous comment (tumbler
  conflict arm + self-healing floor, and advancing next_seq outside the failing
  transaction) remain required.
- Deployed cloud engine is **0.1.57** (`nx service probe`) and carries the defect; no
  self-healing commit exists in the tree either (`git log CatalogRepository.java`).
- Worth auditing every other owner for the same drift before it bites again — a
  `nx catalog doctor --next-seq-drift` check (detect: `next_seq <= max child tumbler`,
  counting tombstones) would have turned this 90-minute investigation into one line.

Note the registered doc landed with `content_type: prose` (not `paper`) and empty `bib_*`
fields — `nx dt index` does not carry the DT record's resolved CrossRef metadata into the
catalog row. Minor, separable; the DOI/venue/authors ARE on the DT record.
