title: DATABASECHANGELOG grows by one row on EVERY boot of EVERY cluster — runAlways + onFail=MARK_RAN inserts instead of updating, and the two era-exclusive diag changesets cover both eras
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 by the first-ever execution of a Liquibase rollback round trip (nexus-a0m60's new SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest), on its very first run. Nothing else had ever looked.

MECHANISM. grants-nexus-diag-2 (service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/grants-nexus-diag.xml:99) is runAlways="true" with

    <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN">
      <sqlCheck expectedResult="1">... nexus.diag_chash_conformance exists ...</sqlCheck>
    </preConditions>

The view is created by the SUPERUSER PROVISIONING path, not by Liquibase. Where it is
absent the precondition fails, and Liquibase records MARK_RAN by INSERTING A NEW ROW —
it does not update in place the way it does for a RERAN. The changeset is runAlways, so
this repeats every boot.

MEASURED, two boots of a fresh container:
    boot 1 -> 207 rows
    boot 2 -> 208 rows
    duplicate: grants-nexus-diag-2 | nexus-9bufb | 2 rows
    tail: orderexecuted 212 MARK_RAN  <- new row
          orderexecuted 207 MARK_RAN  <- original, still there
The other four runAlways changesets are RERAN and correctly update in place (single row
each). Only the MARK_RAN one accumulates.

BLAST RADIUS. Unbounded DATABASECHANGELOG growth, one row per boot, on every cluster
where nexus.diag_chash_conformance does not exist — i.e. every dev box, every test
container, and any production cluster before the provisioning path has created the view.
On a cluster where the view DOES exist the precondition passes, the changeset RERANs,
and the row updates in place, so the growth does not occur there.

SECOND-ORDER EFFECT, and how it was noticed: it corrupts rollback DEPTH ARITHMETIC.
rollbackCount(N) counts ROWS, so each accumulated duplicate consumes a step. Any
operator computing 'roll back the last N changesets' against such a cluster reaches a
different set than they intended, and the discrepancy grows with uptime/boot count.

NOT FIXED HERE. Filed separately from nexus-a0m60 on purpose — a0m60 is the rollback
round-trip harness; this is a forward-path bookkeeping defect that the harness merely
exposed. a0m60's test does NOT assert this away: it asserts the invariant it genuinely
needs (the five runAlways changesets occupy the execution tail, which is what puts
staging-4-svc-grants within rollback reach) and leaves the row growth visible.

FIX DIRECTION, not decided: either make the changeset's precondition unnecessary (create
the view in the changelog rather than out of band), or drop runAlways in favour of a
runOnChange/idempotent forward, or accept MARK_RAN once and gate the re-run. Whichever
is chosen, a regression assertion belongs in the new rollback test's companion
(runAlwaysChangesetsFloatToTheExecutionTail already dumps the duplicate set).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — THE BLAST RADIUS ABOVE IS UNDERSTATED. MEASURED.

"On a cluster where the view DOES exist ... the growth does not occur there"
is FALSE. grants-nexus-diag-1 (expectedResult="0") and grants-nexus-diag-2
(expectedResult="1") are the EXCLUSIVE COMPLEMENT of each other on the SAME
probe. So exactly one of them MARK_RANs on every boot of EVERY cluster —
the duplicate does not disappear in the view era, it changes id:

    legacy era (view absent)  -> grants-nexus-diag-2 accumulates
    view era   (view present) -> grants-nexus-diag-1 accumulates

Measured by reverting the fix and re-running the harness (falsification run,
not reasoning):
    runAlwaysChangesetsFloatToTheExecutionTail (2 boots, legacy era)
        Expecting empty but was: ["grants-nexus-diag-2 (nexus-9bufb) x2"]
    eraTransitionRevokesTableSelectWithoutGrowingTheChangelog (3 boots, view era)
        Expecting empty but was: ["grants-nexus-diag-1 (nexus-ykzbj.8) x3"]

There is no era in which a cluster is safe. Every production cluster grows too.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED AT THE SOURCE (liquibase-core 4.29.0, pinned):
    ChangeSet.java:74-75   RERAN(ranBefore=true) / MARK_RAN(ranBefore=false)
    MarkChangeSetRanGenerator.java:65   ranBefore ? UpdateStatement : InsertStatement
    ShouldRunChangeSetFilter.java:64    runAlways accepted every boot
    ValidatingVisitor.java:127-128      MD5SUM check SKIPPED for shouldAlwaysRun()

FIX CHOSEN — era test moved into the DO $$ body, runAlways KEPT.
Both changesets now always execute, always record RERAN, and update their one
row in place. The last of the three fix directions on this bead ("create the
view in the changelog") was already foreclosed: the view must be superuser-
owned (nexus-vounk, FORCE RLS) and Liquibase runs as nexus_admin NOSUPERUSER.

runOnChange REJECTED, and it is a trap worth recording. It does stop the row
growth (ShouldRunChangeSetFilter:69 rejects an already-ran changeset without
evaluating its preconditions at all), but it silently forfeits BOTH self-heal
properties this changelog is built on:
  - a nexus_diag created later by the DBA would never be granted;
  - the view-era REVOKE would never fire when provisioning creates the view,
    leaving the RDR-182 s5 content boundary permanently unenforced.
Two silent-correctness bugs traded for one loud one. Checksum safety is NOT
the reason to avoid it — editing a runAlways body is checksum-exempt.

LANDED WITH:
  - service/.../db/changelog/grants-nexus-diag.xml — both era tests in body
  - SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest — the warn-only row-growth report is
    now a HARD assertion (legacy era), plus a new
    eraTransitionRevokesTableSelectWithoutGrowingTheChangelog covering the view
    era AND the legacy->view transition itself, which nothing had ever executed
  - tests/test_changelog_markran_lint.py — NEW corpus-wide lint: no runAlways
    changeset may gate on onFail/onError=MARK_RAN. Falsified against the
    pre-fix tree (flags both changesets); non-vacuity asserts on changeset
    count, runAlways count, and preConditions presence
  - tests/test_diag_conformance_view.py — parse-based, replaces a substring
    assert that collided with the new documentation prose

ACCEPTED RESIDUAL — historical duplicates are NOT cleaned up, deliberately.
The fix stops the growth; it does not delete rows already accumulated. On an
existing cluster the surviving duplicates stay, and because the RERAN UPDATE is
`WHERE id=? AND author=? AND filename=?` it re-stamps ALL of them to the same
ORDEREXECUTED each boot. Not cleaned up because:
  - the only remaining consequence is rollbackCount depth arithmetic, and Hal's
    standing ruling (nexus-9vg5g, 2026-07-27) is that schema rollback is not an
    operational path here;
  - DML against Liquibase's own bookkeeping table carries more risk than the
    residual it would remove;
  - dev boxes and test containers, where the accumulation is fastest, are
    recreated constantly.
If a future arc DOES need honest depth arithmetic against a long-lived cluster
(nexus-fhpof territory — partial release-to-release rollback), the dedupe has to
happen there and this is the record of why it was not done here.
close_reason: Fixed in 585c8c20 on develop. Both era tests moved from <preConditions onFail=MARK_RAN> into the DO $$ bodies as early-RETURN guards; runAlways kept. CI green on the pushed commit: Service CI 30302021005 success, CI 30302020899 success (13279 passed, 332 skipped = the ENGINE arm, 559 deselected, 2 xfailed). Full engine suite on the tree 1463/0/0/1. Blast radius corrected by measurement: BOTH eras grew (diag-2 x2 legacy, diag-1 x3 view), not just the legacy era as originally filed. Historical duplicate rows deliberately not swept; residual and rationale recorded in the notes.

title: CA-3 passes vacuously on branches that do not touch ca3_core — a defect there is invisible until someone trips the gate
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 on PR #1428, which is the first change in a while to touch a ca3_core
input (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and therefore the first to actually RUN this job.

THREE THINGS COMPOUND, and each is individually reasonable:

1. THE CACHED BUNDLE IS BROKEN. Every pg-bundle cache entry (all six, created
   2026-07-22 ~00:10-00:40, one pair per arch) restores successfully and then fails:
       ::error::bundle/bin/initdb missing after cache-restore/build — CA-3 cannot run
   Verified on linux-amd64, linux-arm64 and mac-arm64 — all three arches, both entries
   per arch. This is not scoping and not one poisoned entry (I diagnosed it that way
   first and was WRONG; deleting one per arch just moved the hit to the other).

2. A CACHE HIT SUPPRESSES THE REBUILD. ci.yml:500 —
       if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true' && steps.pg-bundle-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
   So the from-source build only runs on a cache MISS. A broken cache therefore cannot
   self-heal: it restores, the build is skipped, the verify fails, and the next run
   restores the same broken bytes. The only exit is deleting the entries by hand.

3. THE PATHS-FILTER HIDES IT. ci.yml:453 gates the whole job on ca3_core/ca3_deps. On
   any branch that does not touch those paths the job SKIPS, and a skipped job reports
   SUCCESS. Measured — work-lines (initdb / "Build complete PG" / assemble) in each
   branch's linux-arm64 CA-3 job:
       develop                                  0    <- did nothing, reported success
       fix/staging4-rollback-split              2    <- did nothing meaningful
       feature/nexus-aqbrk-flip-engine-default  2    <- gate fired, exposed the break
   So CA-3 has been green-by-skipping for at least five days while the artifact it
   exists to verify was unusable.

THE GATE ITSELF IS NOT THE BUG — path-filtering an expensive from-source PG build is
the documented CI-cost design and it is correct. The bug is that (1) went unnoticed
BECAUSE of (3) and could not fix itself BECAUSE of (2). Three individually-defensible
decisions producing a build-verification job that verified nothing.

IMMEDIATE ACTION TAKEN: purged all six pg-bundle entries (5941291629, 5941258447,
5941247648, then 5941804984, 5941794538, 5941764854) so the next CA-3 run rebuilds from
source and repopulates correctly. Left the two pg-bundle-Linux-16e335... entries alone —
those are the pytest job's test-substrate cache keyed on src/nexus/engine_version.py, a
different artifact.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE (not decided):
  - The verify step should distinguish "cache restored but incomplete" from "build
    failed", and on the former DELETE the entry and fall through to the build rather
    than hard-failing. A self-healing cache is the whole point of keying on content.
  - Consider a periodic (weekly?) unconditional CA-3 run so a broken bundle surfaces on
    a schedule instead of waiting for someone to touch ca3_core. This is the same
    "release-only procedures rot silently" class as nexus-1e2eh.
  - Whatever lands must not turn CA-3 into an every-PR from-source build — that cost is
    exactly what the paths-filter exists to avoid.

HOW MUCH LONGER IT WOULD HAVE GONE UNNOTICED: the cache entries have a 7-day idle
eviction. They were being touched by every skipped run, so they may have been renewed
indefinitely. The next person to touch a ca3_core path would have hit this and, like me,
first assumed their own change broke it.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS FALSIFIED, plus the documentation that stops it being refiled. See the second correction comment for the full measurement.

The bead's central claim — CA-3 green-by-skipping on develop — is false. CA-3 runs on
every develop push; the bead's own cited counter-example (run 30187251639) logged
'CA-3 PASS: 12 passed, 0 bundle-skips'. The work-lines metric counted from-source
rebuild lines, which a cache hit omits by design, so it measured cache-hit vs
cache-miss rather than ran vs skipped.

Root cause of the always-runs behaviour: dorny/paths-filter with no base: resolves PUSH
events against the repository default branch (main), not the previous develop commit,
and develop diverges from main in ci.yml and changelog/** — both ca3_core paths.

The real situation is the inverse: CA-3 OVER-runs on develop, at ~3 min of runner time
per push including ~74s of premium macOS. Not fixed here on purpose — that over-run is
what re-proves a PR whose CA-3 was gated off (PR run 30213539574: 571 log lines, zero
test execution, conclusion success). Trading it away needs a replacement net, so the
decision was to document rather than change behaviour (Hal, 2026-07-27).

SHIPPED: c7f22e60 — comment at both paths-filter sites recording the base semantics,
the run IDs proving it, the cost of pinning base:, and the instruction to read
assert_ca3_ran.py's 'CA-3 PASS: N passed' line rather than infer from build lines.
Comment only, no behaviour change.

The one demonstrated input hole (tests/conftest.py not in ca3_core) was already closed
by 842a918f pinning NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=sqlite on both CA-3 jobs.

NOT carried forward, deliberately: the self-healing-cache idea from the description. It
rested on 'the cached bundle is broken', which was a misread of cyan script echo. The
cache was never shown broken.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — THE CACHE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS WRONG.
Read this comment before acting on anything above it.

WHAT ACTUALLY BROKE CA-3: the nexus-aqbrk flip. It made the engine the DEFAULT test
substrate, so tests/db/test_pg_provision_ca3_bundle.py tried to boot an engine inside the
CA-3 jobs, which have NO service JAR (only the `test` job downloads that artifact). All 14
tests skipped, and scripts/assert_ca3_ran.py failed the job:

    SKIPPED: engine substrate: service JAR not provisioned on CI
    14 skipped in 1.67s
    AssertionError: core CREATE EXTENSION vector test did not pass — assemble path
    unproven (no passing testcase ending in 'test_create_extension_vector_loads')

Fixed in 842a918f by pinning NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=sqlite on both CA-3 jobs. That file
verifies PG BINARY provisioning (discovery, sharedir, control files, pg_trgm, the pgvector
assemble path) and has ZERO T2 references, so the pin restores its pre-flip behaviour
rather than weakening it.

THE PG-BUNDLE CACHE WAS PROBABLY FINE. The description above claims every entry was
missing bundle/bin/initdb since 07-22. That was inferred from a MISREAD log line:

    [36;1m  echo "::error::bundle/bin/initdb missing after cache-restore/build..."[0m

The cyan [36;1m prefix means GitHub is ECHOING THE SCRIPT SOURCE, not emitting an error.
That check never fired. The real failure was ~130 lines further down, in the assert. I
read the echo as output and built three successive wrong theories on it — cache scoping,
then a good/bad entry split, then a wholly broken bundle — and purged all six pg-bundle
entries across two rounds on that basis. The builds had SUCCEEDED every time
("Built: initdb (PostgreSQL) 17.5", "bundle complete"). The purge was avoidable churn;
harmless, since the entries repopulate from source on the next miss, but it was not the
problem.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND STILL WORTH FIXING — the reason to keep this bead open:

CA-3 PASSES VACUOUSLY on every branch that does not touch a ca3_core path. The
paths-filter at ci.yml:453 gates the job, and a skipped job reports SUCCESS. Measured —
work-lines (initdb / "Build complete PG" / assemble) in each branch's linux-arm64 CA-3
job on 2026-07-27:

    develop                                  0    <- did nothing, reported success
    fix/staging4-rollback-split              2    <- did nothing meaningful
    feature/nexus-aqbrk-flip-engine-default  2    <- gate fired, exposed the breakage

The GATE ITSELF IS NOT THE BUG — path-filtering an expensive from-source PG build is the
documented CI-cost design and it is correct. The point is the consequence: a defect in
CA-3's inputs, or in what CA-3 exercises, is invisible until someone happens to touch a
ca3_core path. Here that meant a substrate regression introduced by the flip sat
undetected until the very PR that introduced it also edited ci.yml. Had the flip NOT
touched ci.yml, it would have merged with CA-3 green and broken the next person to touch
ca3_core, who would then — like me — have assumed their own change was at fault.

WORTH CONSIDERING (not decided):
  - A periodic unconditional CA-3 run (weekly?) so rot surfaces on a schedule instead of
    ambushing whoever next trips the gate. Same class as nexus-1e2eh, release-only
    procedures rotting silently.
  - Whatever lands must NOT turn CA-3 into an every-PR from-source build; that cost is
    exactly what the paths-filter exists to avoid.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: scripts/assert_ca3_ran.py did its job perfectly. Without that
non-vacuity assert, CA-3 would have reported GREEN having executed nothing — the same
silent-mass-skip class NX_T2_SUBSTRATE_EXPECTED=1 guards on the pytest side. The gate
that caught this is the one piece of the system that behaved exactly as designed.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SECOND CORRECTION, 2026-07-27 — THE CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE. CA-3 does not pass
vacuously on develop. It runs on EVERY develop push. Read this before the earlier
correction; both of them predate the actual measurement.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT. The description's own counter-example, run
30187251639 (develop, 2026-07-26), cited as "0 work-lines, did nothing, reported
success", actually logged in its linux-arm64 CA-3 job:

    12 passed, 2 skipped in 1.59s
    CA-3 PASS: 12 passed, 0 bundle-skips, pgvector load + floor verified

Same on 30256819508 (308522b3) and 30272066728 (721cd3f7). The non-vacuity assert
printed its PASS line every time.

WHY THE WORK-LINES METRIC COULD NEVER HAVE SUPPORTED THE CLAIM. initdb /
"Build complete PG" / assemble are FROM-SOURCE REBUILD lines. They are absent on a
cache hit BY DESIGN — ci.yml runs the build only when pg-bundle-cache misses, per the
CI-cost directive "never rebuild deterministic artifacts". A cache-hit run that
executed every test scores ZERO. So "develop 0 / staging4 2 / flip 2" distinguished
cache-hit from cache-miss, never ran from skipped.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE ALWAYS-RUNS BEHAVIOUR. dorny/paths-filter with no `base:` resolves
PUSH events against the repository DEFAULT branch (main), not the previous develop
commit. develop diverges from main in ci.yml and service/.../changelog/**, both
ca3_core paths, so ca3_core is effectively always true on a develop push.

THE REAL SITUATION IS THE INVERSE OF THIS BEAD. CA-3 OVER-runs on develop. Cost
measured on run 30272066728: 39s linux-arm64 + 86s linux-amd64 + 74s mac-arm64 per
develop push — including a premium macOS runner on routine pushes, the one shape the
CI-cost directive names explicitly. Cheap while the cache hits; a key miss would fire
a ~10min from-source build on three arches unbidden.

WHAT IS GENUINELY TRUE, AND ONLY THIS. A PULL REQUEST touching no ca3_core path gets a
CA-3 that reports success having proven nothing — PR run 30213539574, 571 non-echo log
lines, zero test execution, conclusion success. That is the designed
always-run-report-skip pattern, and because of the main-base quirk the following
develop push re-proves it, one merge later.

THE ONE DEMONSTRATED INPUT HOLE IS ALREADY CLOSED. tests/conftest.py is not in
ca3_core and the substrate flip there did break CA-3, but 842a918f pinned
NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=sqlite on both CA-3 jobs, so it can no longer reach them.

SCORECARD ON THE THREE COMPOUNDING FINDINGS:
  (1) "the cached bundle is broken"        FALSE — misread cyan script echo
  (2) "a cache hit suppresses the rebuild" TRUE, but that is the intended design and
                                           "cannot self-heal" is unproven, because the
                                           cache was never shown broken
  (3) "the paths-filter hides it"          FALSE as measured

METHOD NOTE. Both wrong diagnoses on this bead came from reading a PROXY instead of the
thing itself: cyan script-echo read as emitted error output, then rebuild-lines read as
ran-at-all. The direct signal was one grep away both times —
scripts/assert_ca3_ran.py prints "CA-3 PASS: N passed" precisely so nobody has to infer
whether the gate fired.

Full evidence: T2 nexus/[21172]
(nexus-4k91k-premise-falsified-ca3-actually-over-runs-2026-07-27).

title: no test ever executes a Liquibase rollback — add an update -> rollback -> update round-trip to the service suite
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27, the root cause behind nexus's staging-4-svc-grants rollback defect
(fixed separately). Filed at Hal's direction as its own arc rather than bundled.

THE GAP. Nothing in the build or CI has ever executed `liquibase rollback`. The
service's SchemaMigrator calls liquibase.update(...) and nothing else — verified, its
conn.rollback() at :238 is a plain JDBC transaction rollback in the FORCE-RLS handling,
unrelated to changesets. So the asymmetry is structural:

    forward SQL  — runs on every deploy, every CI run, every dev box
    rollback SQL — runs approximately NEVER, until an incident

That is how staging-4-svc-grants shipped a rollback that could not execute at all
(raw-text <rollback> with a DO $$ body, split on the ';' inside its DECLARE ->
"Unterminated dollar quote"). It took out the ENTIRE rollback chain and was invisible
to every green signal we have. It was found by hand, not by a test.

WHAT TO BUILD. An update -> rollbackCount(N) -> update round trip against a
testcontainer, in the service suite. Precedent for the shape already exists:
SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest covers the UPGRADE axis; this is its missing twin.
The manual version run today caught staging-4 in one shot and then proved the fix:
  - rollbackCount reaches the target changesets (exit 0)
  - the DO block actually EXECUTED, not merely parsed (nexus_svc ended with zero
    privileges in the staging schema)
  - generated columns reverted (pg_get_expr readback) and BOTH GIN indexes came back
  - full round trip restored both the folded columns and the staging grants

WHY THE LINT IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE (tests/test_changelog_rollback_lint.py, landing with
the fix). It checks SHAPE — a $$ body must sit inside <sql splitStatements="false">.
A rollback can carry that attribute, parse cleanly, and still restore the WRONG THING:
drop an index and forget to recreate it, or revert a column to a different definition.
Only execution proves otherwise. The FTS rollback blocks happened to restore both GIN
indexes correctly — but nothing was checking, and that was luck plus care, not a gate.

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE FIRST, not obvious:
  - HOW FAR to roll back. Full 207 -> 0 is the strongest signal and the slowest; a
    trailing window (last N) is cheap but only covers recent changesets — and staging-4
    sat at position 204, so a small window WOULD have caught it. Consider: rollback to
    the previous engine tag's changeset count, which is the operationally meaningful
    depth.
  - runAlways changesets re-run on the way forward, so the round trip is not a pure
    identity — assert on SCHEMA SHAPE (pg_get_expr, pg_indexes, grants), not on
    databasechangelog row equality.
  - CI COST. This is a fresh container plus a triple Liquibase pass. Given the standing
    CI-cost directives it likely belongs at a merge boundary or nightly rather than on
    every PR — decide deliberately, do not default it onto the PR path.
  - CHECKSUM SAFETY is already established: Liquibase excludes <rollback> from the
    changeset md5sum (measured — staging-4 kept 9:84da1012... across its fix), so the
    test can exercise rollbacks without any validCheckSum ceremony.

WHY P1. The rollback path is what an incident response reaches for, and we have now
demonstrated it can be broken for an unknown length of time without anyone noticing.
engine-service-v0.1.57 is the first release where this became load-bearing: it is not
code-only (memory-002/catalog-017 regenerate fts_vector), so a binary-only rollback to
0.1.56 silently breaks accented queries and a SCHEMA rollback is mandatory.
close_reason:
DONE. Harness landed, five defects fixed, stacked review run and its two Criticals corrected.

SHIPPED: 42b1cc86 (the work) + 7944475b (review fixes). Both CI workflows green on
7944475b: Service CI with 208 rollback statements executed IN CI, and the engine-arm
pytest at 13277 passed / 332 skipped / 0 errors.

THE HARNESS. service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest.java
— update -> update -> rollback("rollback-floor") -> update against a testcontainer as a
production-shaped NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role. Asserts SCHEMA SHAPE (tables, index defs,
pg_get_expr generated columns, constraint defs, grants, pg_policies, RLS force flags,
column types), never DATABASECHANGELOG row equality — runAlways makes the trip a
non-identity at the bookkeeping level by construction.

THE BEAD'S THREE DESIGN QUESTIONS, ANSWERED:
  (a) HOW DEEP — to a TAG, not a count. rollbackCount(N) is wrong three ways: N must be
      re-derived on every changeset, it covers the wrong set when one is INSERTED rather
      than appended, and it counts ROWS, which nexus-ixsxa's per-boot duplicates drift.
      floor-001-rollback-floor.xml tags the boundary, included second in master.
  (b) ASSERT ON SCHEMA SHAPE — done, and extended after review to cover RLS policies and
      relforcerowsecurity, which the first cut missed entirely despite chash-001-2's
      rollback manipulating exactly those.
  (c) CI COST — the service suite is path-gated on service/**, so no new workflow and no
      every-PR Python cost. Stated at its REAL cost after review corrected an earlier
      claim that cited a changelog-subtree filter that does not exist.

FIVE DEFECTS FOUND BY EXECUTION, every one of which passed the shape lint, the full Java
suite, CI and every deploy:
  catalog-016-0                  no inverse at all; aborted the chain
  chash-001-2, fk-002-4,         four rollbacks referencing nexus.chash_index after
  catalog-013-1, rdr180-11       rdr187-2 retired it (IF EXISTS guards the CONSTRAINT,
                                 not the TABLE) — guarded with to_regclass, not deleted
  vectors-001-1                  dropped extensions a NOSUPERUSER role cannot own

STACKED REVIEW (code-review-expert + substantive-critic, T2 [21177]/[21178]) returned two
Criticals, both mine, both fixed in 7944475b:
  1. tagDatabase tags the MOST RECENTLY EXECUTED row, not its own — so on an
     already-migrated cluster rollback-to-tag reverts almost nothing while exiting 0, and
     revokes nexus_svc's staging grants on the way. I had shipped operator-facing prose
     promising the opposite. Corrected in three places; nexus-9vg5g raised to P0.
  2. The ROLLBACK_FLOOR_TAG javadoc still described the abandoned design.
Plus: the bead's own acceptance criterion (prove staging-4's DO block EXECUTED, not merely
parsed) had NOT landed and now does; the depth assertion did not check depth; the lint
rewrite still had the same false-negative class reordered (.text misses text after a
child).

RESIDUALS, all filed with evidence:
  nexus-9vg5g  P0  floor-tag semantics on upgraded clusters — three decisions on the bead
  nexus-ixsxa  P1  DATABASECHANGELOG grows one row per boot on MARK_RAN runAlways
  + P2s: unbounded empty-<rollback/> cohort (49 of 208, and this test rewards growing it);
    no partial release-to-release rollback coverage; undocumented non-owner precondition.

Full record: T2 [21175] (findings) and [21180] (post-review state).

title: Liquibase rollback chain is broken at staging-4-svc-grants — raw-text <rollback> with a DO $$ body gets split mid-block
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 while verifying whether engine-service-v0.1.56 remains a supported
rollback target for v0.1.57 (conexus ask, T2 [21164]).

REPRO, deterministic, against a fresh pgvector/pgvector:pg17 with the full changelog
applied (207 changesets):

  liquibase --changeLogFile=db/changelog/db.changelog-master.xml ... rollbackCount --count=10

  Rolling Back Changeset: ...grants-nexus-diag-2
  Rolling Back Changeset: ...grants-nexus-diag-1
  Rolling Back Changeset: ...grants-002-changelog-read
  Rolling Back Changeset: ...grants-nexus-svc-1
  Rolling Back Changeset: db/changelog/staging-001-landing-tables.xml::staging-4-svc-grants
  ERROR: Unterminated dollar quote started at position 3 in SQL DO $$
         DECLARE
             rel RECORD. Expected terminating $$
  [Failed SQL: (0) DO $$ DECLARE rel RECORD]

MECHANISM. staging-4-svc-grants's <rollback> is RAW TEXT (no <sql> child element), so it
does not and cannot carry splitStatements="false". Liquibase therefore splits it on `;`
— and the body is a DO $$ ... $$ block whose DECLARE section contains `rel RECORD;`. The
statement is torn in half before it reaches PostgreSQL. The changeset's FORWARD <sql>
elements DO carry splitStatements, which is why the forward path is fine and only
rollback breaks.

BLAST RADIUS — operator rollback only, NOT engine boot. Verified:
SchemaMigrator.java:112 calls liquibase.update(...) and nothing else; the conn.rollback()
at :238 is a plain JDBC transaction rollback inside the FORCE-RLS handling, unrelated to
changeset rollback. The engine has NO Liquibase rollback path. So this cannot affect a
normal deploy — it breaks precisely the path an incident response would reach for.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. v0.1.57 is not code-only: memory-002/catalog-017 regenerate
fts_vector on nexus.memory and nexus.catalog_documents. Rolling the BINARY back to
0.1.56 without rolling back the schema silently breaks accented queries (0.1.56's query
side does not fold; the stored side does), so a schema rollback is REQUIRED for a real
0.1.57 -> 0.1.56 rollback. That path is currently blocked here, six positions before it
reaches the FTS changesets.

THE FTS ROLLBACK BLOCKS THEMSELVES ARE FINE — verified in isolation on the same cluster
by executing them directly in reverse order under ON_ERROR_STOP=1:
  - fold_diacritics removed from BOTH generated columns (pg_get_expr readback)
  - nexus.fold_diacritics function dropped
  - BOTH GIN indexes correctly recreated, not left dropped
  - BEHAVIOURAL revert exact: 'resume' no longer matches 'résumé' (the original bug
    restored) while 'résumé' still does — i.e. precisely 0.1.56 semantics.
So this bead is about staging-4 only; do not conflate them.

SUGGESTED FIX (not decided): wrap the rollback body in <sql splitStatements="false">, the
same way the forward changesets in that file do. Worth a sweep for OTHER raw-text
<rollback> blocks containing DO $$ / function bodies — this is unlikely to be the only
one, and every such block is a rollback that only fails when someone actually needs it.
A lint in the shape of tests/test_changelog_analyze_lint.py would catch the class.

UNTIL FIXED: engine-service-v0.1.56 should be treated as NOT a supported rollback target
for v0.1.57. Roll forward only.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as c13d0c84 (PR #1430).

staging-4-svc-grants's <rollback> now sits inside <sql splitStatements="false">, so the
DO $$ ... $$ body reaches PostgreSQL intact instead of being torn at the ';' inside
DECLARE. Swept six more at-risk raw-text rollback blocks in the same PR (catalog-008-1..3,
catalog-012-1..3) which survived only because their LANGUAGE sql bodies happen to contain
no internal ';'.

Class is mechanical now: tests/test_changelog_rollback_lint.py requires any <rollback>
body containing $$ to sit inside <sql splitStatements="false">. 6 passed.

Checksum safety measured, not assumed: staging-4 kept 9:84da10127f33beb3b1602f9cb0b30163
across the fix, so already-executed changesets need no validCheckSum.

Verified end to end on a live cluster: rollbackCount reaches the three v0.1.57 FTS
changesets, fold_diacritics leaves both generated columns, the function drops, BOTH GIN
indexes are recreated, staging grants actually revoke, and update -> rollback -> update
round-trips clean.

Answer relayed to conexus in T2 conexus/[21168]: binary-only 0.1.57 -> 0.1.56 is NOT safe
and never will be, but binary + Liquibase rollback of the three FTS changesets now works,
and it needs no new engine tag because the engine has no Liquibase rollback path.

Root cause behind this surviving since it was written stays open as nexus-a0m60: no test
anywhere ever EXECUTES a rollback.

title: [bug] nx t3 gc's empty-alive-set guard is unreachable in service mode — the only check is 'catalog absent', which service mode cannot represent
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk porting tests/test_t3_gc.py to the engine substrate, and confirmed by
reading the guard's own rationale.

THE GUARD AND WHY IT EXISTS. commands/t3.py::_make_catalog() docstring, verbatim:

  "Without the init gate, running `nx t3 gc` on a fresh install either crashes with an
   opaque traceback inside Catalog.__init__ or, WORSE, SILENTLY PRODUCES AN EMPTY
   ALIVE-SET SO EVERY CHUNK IS TREATED AS ORPHAN (catastrophic when paired with
   --no-dry-run --yes)."

The implementation (t3.py:128-132) is:

    cat = make_catalog_reader()
    if cat is None:
        raise click.ClickException("Catalog not initialized. Run 'nx catalog setup' ...")

THE GAP. `cat is None` is a SQLITE-ONLY condition — the factory returns None only in
sqlite opt-out mode with an uninitialised local catalog. In service mode
make_catalog_reader() ALWAYS returns a _SharedServiceCatalogHandle, so the guard can never
fire. The hazard it was written to prevent is not guarded there at all.

The alive-set itself comes from t3.py:431:

    referenced = cat.chashes_for_collection(collection)

An EMPTY return makes every chash-carrying chunk an orphan candidate. Empty is reachable in
service mode without anything being "wrong" with the client: a fresh/mis-scoped tenant, a
catalog whose manifest rows were never backfilled for that collection, or a collection that
exists in T3 but has no catalog projection.

Note the guard only ever caught "catalog ABSENT". The "catalog PRESENT but EMPTY" case was
never guarded on either substrate — service mode simply removed the one case that was.

SEVERITY — REAL BUT LAYERED, stated honestly rather than alarmingly. Three other safety
layers survive:
  - --dry-run is the DEFAULT; deletion needs --no-dry-run
  - --yes is additionally required to actually delete
  - --orphan-window (default 30d) excludes anything whose indexed_at is inside the window,
    and zero/negative windows are rejected at parse time
So the catastrophic path needs `--no-dry-run --yes` against chunks older than the window
with an empty alive-set. Not a one-keystroke foot-gun, but the last line of defence for a
DESTRUCTIVE command is missing on the substrate that is about to become the only one.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (not started, and the choice matters):
  1. Guard on the ALIVE-SET, not on catalog presence: if `referenced` is empty while the
     collection has chunks, refuse and explain. This covers BOTH substrates and the
     present-but-empty case the original guard never reached.
  2. Optionally keep the `cat is None` check as a cheap early error for the sqlite arm.
Do NOT simply port the None-check to a service equivalent — there isn't one, and the
useful invariant was never "catalog object exists" but "alive-set is credible".

TEST STATE: tests/test_t3_gc.py::test_gc_aborts_on_uninitialized_catalog is PINNED to the
sqlite catalog by nexus-aqbrk, because its premise (an uninitialised catalog) is
unrepresentable in service mode. It therefore does NOT cover the service arm — that
coverage has to come with this fix. Do not read the green test as protection.
close_reason: Closed

title: by_doc_id is overloaded across two key types — migrate the 4 chash-passing callers onto docs_for_chashes, then collapse it into resolve()
description:
Scoped out of nexus-wji11, whose CONTRACT QUESTION Hal settled 2026-07-26: TUMBLER IS THE
ONLY DOCUMENT IDENTITY (matches RDR-108 per AGENTS.md — "Catalog Documents are graph nodes
addressed by tumblers; T3 chunks are content-addressed blobs whose natural ID is the FULL
sha256(chunk_text)"). wji11 keeps the contract record; this bead is the work.

=== THE DEFECT ===

catalog.by_doc_id() is called with TWO DIFFERENT KEY TYPES, and each substrate implements
only ONE of them, so each is broken for half its callers. Full census (all 6 traced to
their id source by reading, not inferred):

CLASS A — passes a CHASH. Broken on SERVICE. 4 sites:
  A1 catalog/store_hook.py:167   the store dedup ("Dedup by chunk_chroma_id stored in
       legacy meta.doc_id"). IMPACT: dedup never fires -> re-storing identical content
       mints a SECOND catalog Document. Adjacent to the nexus-b6enc duplicate-row class.
  A2 catalog/store_hook.py:384   by_doc_id(chash_doc_id) — delete-path lookup misses.
  A3 mcp_infra.py:678            the auto-linker. mcp/core.py:2659 passes doc_id (t3.put's
       chash) while catalog_doc_id (the TUMBLER) is in scope two lines up. IMPACT: zero
       links for every agent-stored doc on a migrated install; DEBUG is the only signal —
       the exact silence nexus-a414 already had to fix once.
  A4 commands/store.py:359       the post-delete catalog tombstone reap; both feeders are
       T3 chunk ids (--id -> delete_by_id, --title -> find_ids_by_title). IMPACT: the reap
       NEVER FIRES, so `nx store delete` leaves the catalog row behind — precisely the
       "delete isn't atomic" surprise the function exists to prevent, and a re-break of
       nexus-kmo9h's intent.

CLASS B — passes a TUMBLER. Broken on SQLITE, correct on service. 2 sites:
  B1 commands/collection.py:35 (from :551) — fed from the manifest, whose doc_id column IS
       the tumbler. SQLITE IMPACT: nx collection reindex treats every post-prune chunk as
       sourceless and the safety check always fires. Conservative but wrong.
  B2 search_engine.py:259 — same tumbler key; EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE (fallback for
       catalogs lacking resolve_many, which BOTH substrates define). Dead leg.

=== WHY NOT A POLYMORPHIC by_doc_id (Hal's question, 2026-07-26) ===

Attractive, and half-right: a chash IS a legitimate identity — of a CHUNK. But
chash -> document is ONE-TO-MANY. AGENTS.md: "Identical chunk text in the same collection
collapses to one T3 row by design; the manifest preserves position via (doc_id, position)
rows pointing at the shared chash." So a single chash can belong to N documents, and it
cannot back a single-valued accessor. A polymorphic by_doc_id would need DIFFERENT
CARDINALITY per key type (entry vs list), which makes it a different method, not a
polymorphic one — and re-creates the overload that caused this bug.

THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS, on both substrates, parity-registered:
    docs_for_chashes(chashes: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]     # chash -> [doc_id...]
    catalog.py:1843 / http_catalog_client.py:1944 / catalog_writes.py:1221
Its dict-of-LISTS shape is exactly the one-to-many relation, and it was already hardened
once for shape parity (nexus-h8rf6.3).

=== THE WORK ===

1. A3 (auto-linker) — smallest, do first. mcp/core.py:2659 already HAS the tumbler
   (catalog_doc_id) in scope; pass it instead of the chash. Verify catalog_doc_id can be
   "" (hook failure) and guard. tests/test_auto_linker.py currently asserts the BROKEN
   value with nexus-wji11 named — restore the strict assertion as part of this.
2. A2 / A4 — insert a chash -> doc resolution step via docs_for_chashes before the catalog
   lookup, and DECIDE the N>1 rule explicitly (reap/delete all matching docs? refuse and
   warn?). Do not let it default silently.
3. A1 (dedup) — the real design question, and the ONLY one that is not mechanical. The
   dedup asks "is there already a document for THIS content?", which under content
   addressing is genuinely ambiguous when a chash is shared. Likely needs
   (collection, chash) or source_uri as the key rather than chash alone. Decide before
   coding.
4. Once Class A passes tumblers, by_doc_id has only tumbler callers -> collapse it into
   resolve(), delete the SQLite meta.doc_id branch (catalog_docs.py:791), and B1/B2 are
   fixed for free. Add a parity entry so the two implementations cannot diverge again.

=== TEST STATE MEANWHILE ===
tests/test_auto_linker.py::_assert_auto_link pins the CURRENT broken value with wji11
named, so step 1 fails it loudly. No other test covers A1/A2/A4's service behaviour —
add coverage with the fix, do not assume the ports in nexus-aqbrk cover it.

CONFIDENCE: A1-A4 and B1 traced to a definite id source. B2's key type traced; its
unreachability inferred from both substrates defining resolve_many (grep-verified, not
confirmed at runtime).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
STEP 1 (class A3, the auto-linker) DONE on develop bc175f29. Steps 2-4 deliberately NOT done — they need decisions, see below.

WHAT SHIPPED. catalog_auto_link now takes the TUMBLER directly; the by_doc_id lookup is gone entirely (the helper only ever wanted entry.tumbler, so resolving a chash to get it was both wrong and a wasted round trip). mcp/core.py store_put passes catalog_doc_id, which was already in scope two lines above the call, guarded on empty (hook failure -> DEBUG auto_link_skip_no_catalog_tumbler, distinct from 'no link contexts'). Log fields renamed doc_id -> tumbler so the structlog output stops mislabelling the key type.

THE PART WORTH RECORDING. My first cut was under-tested and I nearly shipped it. tests/test_auto_linker.py's integration tests call _catalog_auto_link DIRECTLY, so they pass regardless of what store_put threads into it — and the CALL SITE is exactly where the defect lived. Reverting core.py alone left the whole file green. The pin now lives where the bug is: tests/test_mcp_store_put_doc_id.py already patched _catalog_auto_link without asserting its argument, so it now captures call_args and asserts the value is not a 64-hex chash. Mutation-verified: reverting the call site to doc_id fails it. Generalisable: when a bug is 'the caller passed the wrong variable', a test that calls the callee directly proves nothing.

PIN RESTORED as the bead instructed: _assert_auto_link asserted the BROKEN value (count == 0) with a message naming wji11 and asking for the unconditional assertion back. It fired on this change exactly as designed and now asserts count == expected plus a readable-back 'relates' link. The two integration tests were passing legacy meta ids ('test-doc-001', 'multi-doc-001/2') and now pass str(source_t) / str(doc1_t) / str(doc2_t).

STILL OPEN, and each needs YOUR call before code:

title: #1069 project-column scope_tags fallback writes a project-shaped tag that _scope_fit can never match — strictly worse than agnostic
description:
The #1069 project-column fallback writes a scope_tags value in a DIFFERENT NAMESPACE from the one _scope_fit compares against, so the plans it "helps" become invisible to every scoped caller. Leaving those plans agnostic would strictly outperform it.

## Proof

`src/nexus/db/t2/plan_library.py` save_plan, scope_tags=None branch: infer from plan_json retrieval steps; if inference yields '' AND a non-agnostic `project` was supplied, derive scope_tags from the PROJECT value (the #1069 fallback).

`_scope_fit` (src/nexus/plans/matcher.py) prefix-matches assuming COLLECTION-NAME shape, `<content_type>__<owner>`:
- direction 1: `scope.startswith(tag)`
- direction 2: `tag.startswith(scope)`, only when scope ends with `__`

A bare project name satisfies neither against a real collection scope. Measured:

    _scope_fit('nexus', 'rdr__nexus')                        = None   <- CONFLICT, dropped
    _scope_fit('',      'rdr__nexus')                        = 0.0    <- agnostic, KEPT
    _scope_fit('knowledge', 'knowledge__semantic-operators') = 1.0    <- inferred tag, matched

So for the exact population #1069 targets — plans with no inferable retrieval scope, i.e. corpus:all plans, which is what its own comment names — the fallback converts "kept as neutral" into "dropped as conflicting". It is strictly worse than doing nothing.

End-to-end reproduction (probe, 2026-07-26): seed a plan with `plan_json={"steps": [], ...}` (nothing to infer) and `project="nexus"`, no explicit scope_tags. Stored scope_tags comes back `'nexus'`. Then:

    plan_match(..., scope_preference="rdr__nexus")  -> []          (dropped, logs plan_match_scope_conflict_fallthrough)
    plan_match(...)                    no scope_pref -> [plan_id]  (matched)

## Live blast radius: currently NIL, but only by luck

Both grown plans in the live library have a non-blank project (353=conexus, 354=nexus) — the precondition — but inference SUCCEEDED for both, so the fallback never fired. Plan 354's scope_tags is 'knowledge' (collection-family shaped, inferred from its retrieval step), which correctly prefix-matches `knowledge__semantic-operators` at 1.0.

So no live plan is currently mis-tagged. The bug fires the first time a plan is saved with a project AND no inferable retrieval scope — precisely the corpus:all case #1069 exists to serve. It is latent, not theoretical.

## Why it was hard to see

The failure is silent and inverted: the plan is dropped, `plan_match_scope_conflict_fallthrough` fires, and the caller gets an answer from some OTHER plan. Until nexus-czoeu (fixed 2026-07-26) that record was emitted only when EVERY candidate was dropped, and at DEBUG, which `_resolve_level` never emits in MCP or CLI mode — so the drop left no trace at all in the common case.

## Options (not decided)

1. Drop the #1069 fallback. Agnostic (scope_tags='') already yields 0.0/kept, which is the behaviour the fallback was trying to approximate and fails to reach.
2. Normalize the project into collection-family shape before storing, if a defensible mapping exists (project -> owner segment). Note the shapes genuinely differ: `<content_type>__<owner>` vs a bare owner/project token, so this needs a real rule, not a guess.
3. Teach `_scope_fit` that a bare token may be an owner segment and match `<anything>__<token>`. Riskier — widens matching for every tag, and the RDR-090 spike (plan #52 leakage) is the recorded reason direction 2 is guarded by the `__` boundary in the first place.

Option 1 is the smallest and is supported by the measurement: the fallback's stated goal is provenance, but its effect is exclusion.

## Provenance

Found while writing the nexus-czoeu regression tests: an "agnostic" fixture plan would not survive a scope_preference. That turned out to be the fixture picking up a project-derived tag rather than staying agnostic — the fixture was accidentally reproducing this bug. Hal flagged it as smelling like a real bug; it is.

Related: RDR-091 (scope-aware matching), RDR-090 P1.2 / nexus-smhc (the direction-2 `__` guard), nexus-czoeu (why the drop left no log), issue #1069 (the fallback itself).
close_reason: Closed

title: matcher: binding_drops (and scope_conflict_drops/always_failing_drops) never logged when a runnable candidate wins
description:
src/nexus/plans/matcher.py plan_match(): the cache-hit branch's early `return matches` at line 472 (inside `if scored:`) executes BEFORE `_log_binding_drops(binding_drops)` at line 491. Whenever at least one candidate is runnable (scored is non-empty) AND another candidate was dropped as unrunnable (nexus-0yrjr's typed-binding filter), the drop is silently discarded -- the INFO log documented as "deliberately observable" in schema.py/matcher.py/tests/test_plan_match_binding_satisfiability.py's module docstring never fires.

Reproduced by tracing tests/test_plan_match_binding_satisfiability.py::test_a_satisfiable_plan_still_wins_when_a_sibling_is_dropped: two candidates (typed, plain) both clear min_confidence; typed is dropped into binding_drops and `continue`d; plain lands in `scored`; `scored` is truthy so the function returns at line 472 without ever calling _log_binding_drops. The test only asserts on the returned plan_id, not on logs, so it passes despite the gap.

Same early-return also skips the two PRE-EXISTING debug logs for scope_conflict_drops and always_failing_drops (lines ~483-490) -- this is a latent gap in the surrounding code that nexus-0yrjr's fix copied into a new counter without independently verifying non-vacuity in the winning-path case.

Fix: drain binding_drops (and ideally the other two counters) before the `if scored: ... return matches` early return, not after it. Add a test that seeds a winner alongside a dropped sibling and asserts on the log event, not just the returned plan_id -- test_a_satisfiable_plan_still_wins_when_a_sibling_is_dropped is the natural place to extend.

Found during substantive-critic review of feature/rdr-189-190-target-definition-plan-ir vs develop (PR #1425), relay teammate rev-0yrjr-critic-20260726. Directly undermines nexus-0yrjr's own "fail loudly instead of silently widening" premise: the drop-and-log design is not observable in the most common case (a runnable sibling exists).

title: nx_answer auto-alias stuffs the question text into typed catalog-filter bindings, narrowing retrieval to zero
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-07-25/26. nx_answer matched builtin plan 14 (type-scoped-search, required_bindings [question, content_type]). The caller supplied no content_type, so the auto-alias filled it with the whole question string. Step 1 ran the retrieval with content_type="Which indexed papers discuss intermediate representations for compiling natural-language queries?" — a catalog metadata filter whose real domain is code/paper/rdr/knowledge. Zero documents.

DIRECT A/B PROOF (query tool, same question):
- content_type = the question string -> "No documents found matching catalog filters (content_type=...)"
- content_type omitted               -> 5 documents, top hit the correct paper (0.4093, 192 chunks)

So the alias converted a working retrieval into a guaranteed-empty one. This is the functional half of what looked like "nx_answer is broken"; the counter half was nexus-yg49g (already fixed in 4cfcfa3e).

ROOT CAUSE: the alias was indiscriminate — for each required binding, if unset, assign the question text. It is correct and load-bearing for FREE-TEXT bindings (concept / area / topic; without it, library plans failed at dispatch with "missing required bindings"). It never distinguished those from typed ones.

FIX: _TYPED_FILTER_BINDINGS = {content_type, author, subtree, year, corpus, collection, follow_links, depth, limit} receive "" instead of the question. Two verified properties make "" the right value rather than omission:
- plan_run's gate is presence-only ("name not in bindings", runner.py:668-672), so "" satisfies a required binding.
- retrieval tools coerce empty filters away ("content_type or None", core.py ~1730), so "" means no-filter, not match-empty-string.
Logic extracted into _autoalias_bindings() for testability.

TESTS: tests/test_nx_answer_typed_binding_autoalias.py, 7 cases. Mutation-verified — reverting the carve-out to the pre-fix one-liner fails exactly 3 (the new-behaviour assertions) and leaves the 4 preserved-behaviour ones green. Surrounding suites: 277 passed (nx_answer / plan_run / plan_match / binding / yg49g), 262 passed (mcp_core / operator / plans). ruff clean.

NOT YET ACTIVE IN-SESSION: the live MCP server runs the installed wheel, so the fix does not take effect until a reinstall. Hal's call — do not force-reinstall against a live install.

BLAST RADIUS FOR REVIEW: any library plan declaring a typed binding as required now retrieves unfiltered where it previously retrieved nothing. That is the intended repair, but a plan that MEANT to be type-scoped now silently widens instead of failing. The honest alternative is to fail loudly on an unsatisfiable typed binding. Worth a reviewer's opinion before this merges.
notes:
RESOLUTION CHANGED 2026-07-26, on Hal's call: fail loudly, do not silently widen.

The first implementation (457c2b03) bound "" for typed bindings, which coerces to no-filter and restored results. Rejected: a plan that MEANT to be type-scoped would silently widen to the whole corpus — a data-correctness fallback of exactly the kind the project forbids.

FINAL BEHAVIOUR (ea85b77c). nx_answer raises PlanBindingUnsatisfiableError when a matched plan requires a binding whose domain is enumerated or numeric and neither the caller nor a plan default supplied one. The raise happens before any binding reaches the runner, so a plan never executes half-bound. The error names the plan id, the plan name, the binding, its legal domain (content_type -> code/paper/rdr/knowledge), and both remedies: call plan_run directly with an explicit value, or treat it as a mis-match.

The run records as a FAILURE, so a chronically mis-matched plan accrues a real failure rate and stops clearing promote.py's 0.80 threshold. That is deliberately consistent with the outcome-signal repair in 4cfcfa3e (nexus-yg49g).

IMPORTANT REFRAME — THE PLAN IS NOT AT FAULT. conexus/plans/builtin/type-scoped-search.yml describes itself as "useful when the caller knows the artefact kind (for example, 'search code for X' or 'search RDRs for Y')". Requiring content_type is therefore CORRECT for that plan. The real defect is upstream: the matcher selected a type-scoped plan for a question that specifies no type, and the auto-alias concealed the mis-match by inventing a value. This fix makes that mis-match visible rather than fixing the plan.

FOLLOW-ON WORTH CONSIDERING (not done here): should the matcher itself decline to offer a plan whose required typed bindings cannot be satisfied from the call? That would prevent the mis-match instead of reporting it, and would let nx_answer fall through to the next candidate or the inline planner rather than returning an error to the caller. Deliberately left as a separate decision — this bead's scope was to stop the silent-zero-result behaviour.

VERIFICATION: 8 tests in tests/test_nx_answer_typed_binding_autoalias.py, mutation-verified (reverting the raise fails exactly the four loud-failure assertions, leaves the four preserved-behaviour ones green). 523 passed across nx_answer / plan_run / plan_match / binding / yg49g / mcp_core / operator / plans. ruff clean. Match.name confirmed present on the matcher dataclass, so the call site's best.name is valid.

STILL NOT LIVE: the MCP server runs the installed wheel; a reinstall is required for this to take effect in a session. Hal's call.
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-26 — this bead's earlier NOTES are wrong about what shipped.

The note above says of the matcher-level filter: "FOLLOW-ON WORTH CONSIDERING (not done here) ... Deliberately left as a separate decision — this bead's scope was to stop the silent-zero-result behaviour."

That framing was then reversed and the work WAS done under this bead, without the note being updated. Flagged by the substantive-critic in review as an audit-trail contradiction. Recording the reversal and why.

WHY IT REVERSED. Hal's call, in sequence:
1. "fail loudly instead of silently widening" -> the runtime raise (ea85b77c), the state the stale note describes.
2. "Should the matcher decline to offer a plan whose required typed bindings can't be satisfied? I believe the answer is indeed yes" -> the matcher filter (8b708999), which the note said was not done here.
3. Review then established the reachability rationale for (2) was FALSE — there is no exposed plan_run MCP tool (grep: zero `async def plan_run`; conexus/skills/plan-first/SKILL.md: "there are no separately exposed plan_match / plan_run MCP tools. Do not attempt to call them"). So (2) as shipped made builtins type-scoped-search and find-by-author permanently unreachable — a silent capability loss.
4. Hal chose option 2 of three (accept dead builtins / restore reachability / revert the filter) -> the `bindings` parameter (89c29dd5).

WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED UNDER THIS BEAD, six commits on feature/rdr-189-190-target-definition-plan-ir, PR #1425:
- 457c2b03 bind "" for typed bindings — SUPERSEDED, kept in history because ea85b77c documents the supersession.
- ea85b77c runtime refusal: PlanBindingUnsatisfiableError, recorded as a plan failure so promote.py's 0.80 gate sees it.
- 8b708999 matcher declines to offer unrunnable plans (plan_match available_bindings), both T1 and FTS5 paths.
- 3274186a review fixes: drain binding drops before the early return (nexus-eedj4); ONE taxonomy — core.py's duplicate constant deleted, now imports from plans.schema; FTS5 over-fetch headroom; FTS5 drop-path coverage.
- 89c29dd5 nx_answer `bindings` parameter restores type-scoped reachability; corrected the TYPED_BINDING_DOMAINS content_type hint, which asserted a closed set omitting `prose` (2nd most common catalog value, 138 docs).
- plus a docstring cross-reference repair from the second-pass review.

REVIEW STATUS: code-review-expert second pass — all three prior findings CLOSED, no new Critical/High, one cosmetic nit (fixed). substantive-critic second pass in flight at time of writing; its first-pass verdict was not-justified on the two Criticals now fixed.

SPAWNED: nexus-eedj4 (the drain gap, fixed here), nexus-enrmd (P2 — rationalize the three disjoint content_type vocabularies; the reason `bindings` deliberately does NOT validate values), nexus-czoeu (P3 — the same early-return invisibility in the pre-existing scope_conflict / always_failing counters, left untouched as out-of-diff scope).

STILL NOT LIVE: the MCP server runs the installed wheel; a reinstall is required before any of this takes effect in a session. Hal's call.
RAISE REACHABILITY — CORRECTION 2026-07-26. I told the second-pass critic the PlanBindingUnsatisfiableError raise was 'now reachable' once the bindings param landed. It is NOT, and the critic traced why: available_bindings and run_bindings are both derived from the same _caller_run dict, so the matcher's 'req in available' and _autoalias_bindings' 'req in out' are the SAME membership test against the SAME set. A plan the matcher offers therefore always passes the autoalias without raising; a plan it drops never reaches the autoalias. The miss path cannot produce one either — its ad-hoc Match hardcodes required_bindings=['intent'].

So the raise is provably unreachable through nx_answer's call graph, BY CONSTRUCTION — a consequence of the same-dict symmetry built to stop the two mechanisms disagreeing. That is a good outcome, not a defect, and it is kept as defense-in-depth for any future caller that reaches _autoalias_bindings by another route. Do NOT go looking for integration coverage of a path that cannot execute; there is nothing to cover.

title: [bug] ttl=0 means EXPIRE IMMEDIATELY, not permanent — record-deploy destroyed its own tracker on every sweep, and a test pinned the bug
description:
FOUND 2026-07-26 by a conexus relay (T2 [21156], conexus-11q7 their side) while investigating
why nexus/deployed-engine-version kept vanishing. This is the real root cause of nexus-6igii,
which was CLOSED ON THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS.

THE SEMANTICS. Both expire() implementations agree — this is NOT a substrate divergence:

    SQLite  db/t2/memory_store.py:722   WHERE ttl IS NOT NULL
                                        effective_ttl = ttl * (1 + log(access_count + 1))
                                        if age_days > effective_ttl: DELETE
    engine  MemoryRepository.expire()   identical

So ttl=0 -> effective_ttl = 0 -> ANY row older than an instant is deleted on the next sweep.
ttl=0 means EXPIRE IMMEDIATELY. Permanent is NULL (None) — the only value the
`WHERE ttl IS NOT NULL` filter excludes.

WHO WAS BITTEN. Exactly one caller in src/ (audited by grep, 2026-07-26):
  src/nexus/commands/service_cmd.py:151   ttl=0,  # permanent operational record
It calls handle.memory.put DIRECTLY — store level, BELOW the MCP layer, which does coerce
(`ttl=ttl if ttl > 0 else None`, mcp/core.py:3157). So MCP callers were always safe and the
plugin skills that say ttl=0 are safe today; this caller was not.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE FOR SO LONG, and worth internalising: a 200 plus a returned row id
proves the WRITE, not its DURABILITY, and a re-read minutes later still passes because the
sweep has not run yet. The nexus_active pointer [20742] says of the 2026-07-25 attempt:
"wrote nexus/deployed-engine-version [21141] successfully, readable immediately" — both
statements TRUE, and both irrelevant. The row was gone a day later. nexus-6igii then
concluded the write step had been OMITTED. It had not; it ran and was destroyed.

A TEST PINNED THE BUG. tests/test_service_cmd.py asserted `put["ttl"] == 0` with the comment
"permanent operational record" — so the false belief was locked in, and anyone fixing the
caller would have been failed by the suite. Fixed to `is None` with the reasoning inline.

FIXED IN THIS CHANGE:
  - service_cmd.py ttl=0 -> None
  - the pinning assertion inverted, with a message explaining why 0 is wrong
  - mcp/core.py memory_put docstring: "0 for permanent" was true only because of this
    layer's coercion; it now says so explicitly and warns not to carry the belief outward
  - re-ran record-deploy; nexus/deployed-engine-version now written with ttl NULL

STILL OPEN — TWO ITEMS, NEITHER DONE HERE:

1. ENGINE COERCION (conexus explicitly prefers this, and so do I). Make the engine coerce
   ttl <= 0 -> NULL at POST /v1/memory/put, so the documented semantics become true for
   EVERY caller instead of only MCP users. Without it the footgun stays armed for anything
   that POSTs directly — which is exactly what conexus's own deploy relays do when MCP is
   401ing after a bearer rotation, and it cost them two relays. Engine-side: needs a tag +
   a Hal-relayed deploy, so it is not foldable into this fix.

2. DOC PROPAGATION. conexus/agents/_shared/ERROR_HANDLING.md:71 states "Use ttl=0 for
   permanent entries" as a general rule. True only via MCP. Several skills repeat it
   (rdr-audit SKILL.md, INCIDENT-TEMPLATE.md, skills/nexus/reference.md). All currently
   SAFE because they go through MCP — but the rule as written is wrong, and the next
   direct-POST caller inherits the footgun. Reword once the engine coercion lands, so the
   docs and the substrate change together rather than the docs alone.

title: [bug] memory search returns [] for a stopword-only query even when the corpus contains the word — a false 'no matches' the caller cannot distinguish (empty tsquery, not malformed input)
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk (RDR-158/155 substrate port), bucket 4 — a GENUINE SERVICE GAP, not test debt.
Surfaced by converting tests/test_memory.py::test_malformed_fts5_query_raises_valueerror.

MEASURED 2026-07-26, same T2Database facade method, same inputs, both arms:

  query        sqlite arm                                          service arm
  'AND'        ValueError: Invalid search query 'AND':             0 rows
               fts5: syntax error near "AND"
  'NOT'        ValueError: Invalid search query 'NOT':             0 rows
               fts5: syntax error near "NOT"
  'foo\"bar'    0 rows                                              0 rows      (agree)
  'content'    1 row                                               1 row       (agree)

So the divergence is precise: the SQLite path validates the query through
``memory_store._sanitize_fts5`` and raises ValueError with the offending token; the
service path performs NO equivalent validation and reports the malformed query as an
empty result set.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT COSMETIC. An empty result is a MEANINGFUL answer — it means "nothing
in the store matches." Returning it for a query the engine could not parse is a silent
false negative: the caller cannot distinguish "no such entry" from "your query was
malformed." That is the no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness class. A human types
`nx memory search AND`, is told there are no matches, and concludes the store is empty of
the thing they were looking for.

Worse for agents than humans: every retrieval skill treats an empty memory search as
evidence of absence and proceeds to re-derive from scratch.

RELATED, PROBABLY NOT DUPLICATE: nexus-22r1f (P0) is the other service-mode memory-search
false-negative — entries unfindable by any word inside a dotted title. Same subsystem, same
user-visible symptom (empty result where SQLite answers correctly), different mechanism
(that one is tokenisation of stored titles; this one is validation of the incoming query).
Fix them together if the cause turns out to be shared; do NOT close this as a dup without
establishing that.

FIX SHAPE (not started). Either (a) the service validates the query and returns a 4xx the
client raises as ValueError, matching the SQLite contract, or (b) the client validates
before dispatch via the SAME ``_sanitize_fts5`` the SQLite store uses. (b) is cheaper and
keeps ONE owner of the grammar, but only (a) also protects non-Python callers of the engine.
Decide deliberately — an unvalidated engine endpoint is the more general hole.

TEST STATE MEANWHILE: per the port's standing rule, the gap is ASSERTED AT ITS BROKEN VALUE
rather than xfailed or dropped, with this bead named in the assertion message, so whoever
fixes it gets a loud failure telling them to restore the strict assertion.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RE-MEASURED 2026-07-31 against the LIVE engine. This bead's framing does not survive the SQLite retirement, and both of its proposed fixes were written against a reference substrate that no longer exists. Recording before touching code.

THE FRAMING WAS: "service-mode memory search SILENTLY returns 0 rows for a malformed query that SQLite rejects loudly — a false 'no matches' for a syntax error."

THAT PRESUPPOSES THE QUERY IS MALFORMED. On the current substrate it is not. The two arms never shared a query grammar:

  SQLite (DELETED, RDR-158 P4): FTS5. There AND / NOT are OPERATORS, so a bare
    one is a genuine syntax error, and _sanitize_fts5 raised ValueError.
  Engine (the only substrate now): PostgreSQL plainto_tsquery — see
    http_memory_store.search's own docstring, "sanitized server-side by
    plainto_tsquery". plainto_tsquery is the PLAIN-TEXT entry point; accepting
    arbitrary text WITHOUT a syntax error is its entire purpose. There is no
    operator grammar to violate, so there is no malformed-query class to
    silently swallow.

MEASURED, live engine, this session:
  'AND'                      -> 50 MATCHES (titles containing the word "and":
                                "item-and-order", "column-map-and-cross-table").
                                Treated as an ORDINARY SEARCH TERM, not an operator.
  '"unclosed AND (broken'    -> "No results." No error, no crash — and correctly
                                so: no entry contains those tokens.
  'docling'                  -> 19 matches. Control: the path works.

So the engine is NOT swallowing an error. It is answering a one-word query for the literal word "and", which is the correct plain-text reading.

WHY THE BEAD RECORDED "0 rows": the pinning test (tests/test_memory.py::test_malformed_fts5_query_raises_valueerror) runs against an ISOLATED db holding ONE row — title "doc.md", content "some content". Neither contains "and" or "not". So [] there is a GENUINE no-match, not a false negative. The test asserts an accident of its own fixture data. Search the same term against a store that HAS the word and matches come back, as above.

DISPOSITION — NOT a live defect as written. Leaving it open would keep a P1 on the board for a divergence against a deleted substrate, which is the "stale bead" class we have already been bitten by twice today (nexus-16f77, nexus-uvn3t). But NOT closing it silently either, because two real questions fall out:

1. IS THERE ANY malformed-input class left on PG? plainto_tsquery does not raise on user text, so probably not via this path. If a future search surface uses to_tsquery (which DOES raise on bad syntax) rather than plainto_tsquery, this bead's concern becomes live again for THAT surface.
2. THE PINNING TEST IS NOW MISLEADING. It is named ..._raises_valueerror, documents a gap that does not exist, and its assertion passes for a reason unrelated to what it claims to measure. It should be rewritten to state the real contract — plain-text semantics, AND/NOT are ordinary terms — or deleted. Left as-is it will send the next reader chasing a phantom.

RECOMMEND: re-scope this bead to item 2 (fix the misleading test) and record item 1 as the condition under which the original concern returns. Not closing unilaterally — the original measurement was made in good faith and the re-measurement should be reviewed before the bead is retired.

Related: nexus-22r1f (P0) is the OTHER service-mode memory-search false-negative — entries unfindable by any word inside a dotted title. That one is a tokenisation defect in stored titles and is UNAFFECTED by this finding; do not fold them together.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RE-SCOPED 2026-07-31 (Hal: "rescope"). The bead is LIVE, but the mechanism in the title is wrong — and my own first re-measurement was also wrong. Both corrections recorded, because the second one was found by a test I wrote to prove the opposite.

CORRECTION 1 (previous comment): the "malformed query" framing does not survive the SQLite retirement. FTS5 treated AND/NOT as OPERATORS, so a bare one was a genuine syntax error. The engine uses PostgreSQL plainto_tsquery, whose entire purpose is accepting arbitrary user text WITHOUT a syntax error. There is no malformed-query class on this substrate, so nothing is being "silently swallowed" in the sense the title claims.

CORRECTION 2, to my own previous comment: I then asserted the engine treats AND as an ordinary search term, citing a live probe where 'AND' returned 50 matches against titles like "item-and-order". I wrote a test to pin that contract AND IT FAILED. Seeding a row whose content is literally "clause and clause" and searching 'and' returns []. So 'and' is an ENGLISH STOPWORD in the server's text-search config; plainto_tsquery reduces the query to an EMPTY TSQUERY, which matches nothing unconditionally, corpus-independent. (The 50 live matches came from the MCP memory_search tool, which evidently does not take the same path as T2Database.search — worth knowing separately, and NOT evidence about this path.)

THE REAL DEFECT, and it is a genuine instance of the class this bead was filed under: A QUERY THAT REDUCES ENTIRELY TO STOPWORDS RETURNS [] INDISTINGUISHABLY FROM A GENUINE NO-MATCH. Not "nothing relevant" — nothing, ever, even when the corpus provably contains the word. The caller cannot tell that from an empty store. A human concludes the entry is absent; an agent treats an empty memory search as evidence of absence and re-derives from scratch, which is the expensive failure.

So the bead's HEADLINE INSTINCT was right (a false 'no matches' the caller cannot distinguish) and its stated MECHANISM was wrong (syntax rejection vs stopword elimination). Neither of its two proposed fixes applies: (a) "the service validates the query and returns 4xx" — there is nothing invalid to reject; (b) "the client validates via the SAME _sanitize_fts5" — that would import a DELETED substrate's operator grammar onto a PG store, against the no-SQLite directive.

CORRECT FIX SHAPE: detect the EMPTY EFFECTIVE TSQUERY and report it rather than returning []. Something like "no searchable terms in query 'and' — every word was a stopword". Cheapest honest place is client-side, before or alongside dispatch; engine-side would also cover non-Python callers but needs a tag. NOT implemented here: choosing where, and choosing the wording an agent will parse, is a real decision and this bead has already been fixed against the wrong mechanism once.

TEST STATE: tests/test_memory.py now pins the REAL gap — a row containing "and" is seeded, the search still returns [], and the assertion is AT THE BROKEN VALUE with instructions to replace it when the fix lands. It carries a NON-VACUITY control (a non-stopword term in the same row DOES match), so the [] cannot be read as a broken fixture or a dead search path. The predecessor test (..._raises_valueerror) asserted an accident of its own single-row fixture and has been deleted.

REMAINS TRUE: nexus-22r1f (P0, dotted-title tokenisation) is a DIFFERENT mechanism in the same subsystem. Do not fold them.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my 2026-07-28 lead — the Phase-E tenancy hypothesis is WEAK, probably wrong. Retracting it before someone spends a day on it.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that l9hd8's fixtures are half-migrated to bearer-authoritative tenancy — static bearer 'l9hd8-inttest-bearer' for tenant A while tenant B gets a minted token — so seed and read resolve to different tenants and reads come back empty.

WHY IT DOES NOT HOLD: both halves use the SAME root token. Seeding is aspects_client.upsert(...) where aspects_client = HttpDocumentAspectsStore(tenant='l9hd8-tenant', _token=token), and the failing reads set NX_SERVICE_TOKEN to that same token. Under Phase E the X-Nexus-Tenant header is ignored and the BEARER decides — so both seed and read land in whatever tenant the root token maps to. Same tenant on both sides. The asymmetry I pointed at (tenant B minting its own token) is the file being CORRECT about the one case that genuinely needs it, not evidence of a half-migration.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SHOWS. test_service_path_taken_in_service_mode is the sharpest probe in the file: it points default_db_path at an EMPTY SQLite db so a SQLite fallback yields zero rows by construction, seeds one row into Postgres, and asserts the service path returns it. It gets []. So the service path is either not being taken, or is taken and finds nothing — and the SQLite comparand cannot be the explanation because it was deliberately emptied.

BETTER PLACE TO START than tenancy: the item->aspect-row identity resolution. aspect_sql.try_filter's SQL fast path keys on (collection, source_path); the tests build items via _items_json(['/l9hd8/filter-paxos.pdf'], 'knowledge__l9hd8') and rows via _make_aspect('filter-paxos', ...). If the service-side lookup normalises source_path/source_uri differently from what _make_aspect stored (RDR-096 P3.1 made source_uri the persistent identity, and nexus-3e4s is a prior incident where exactly this normalisation anchored on the wrong root), every lookup misses and every operator returns empty — which also explains the groupby/aggregate collapse to a single '_meta' key, since the operators would be grouping over rows they never matched. NOT CONFIRMED EITHER: I did not read the service-side resolution. Confirm before acting.

STILL TRUE AND USEFUL: these reproduce locally in ~20s without the gate script (T2 [21199]), and the CI numbers now isolate them cleanly. Gate run 30321753068 on develop @ b53f8d06 is 22 failed / 453 passed / 0 errors, and ALL 22 are this bead plus nexus-12m77: 9 l9hd8 + 5 taxonomy_e2e + 3 indexer_e2e here, 5 catalog reader-path there. comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED for the 9 l9hd8 failures — commit cd9bc492. It was not tenancy and not identity resolution; both of my earlier leads were wrong and are formally retracted.

IT WAS HTTP 401 — the reads were going to the WRONG SERVICE.

aspect_sql runs these operators in source='aspects' mode, which deliberately does NOT fall back to the LLM and instead returns an empty result WITH the reason in `rationale`. Nothing ever printed it. It said:

  service operator_filter failed: HttpDocumentAspectsStore./v1/aspects/operator-query failed: HTTP 401: unauthorized

And the '_meta' group key that I (and the bead) read as a data sentinel is the rationale row's own id — the ERROR surfaced as a group. That single misreading is what made this look like ten independent data bugs.

Dumping the env at failure time finished it:
  NX_SERVICE_URL  = http://127.0.0.1:56666   <- session engine-substrate service
  NX_SERVICE_PORT = 56588                    <- this test's own service
  fixture base_url  http://127.0.0.1:56588

The tests set NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT/TOKEN and never NX_SERVICE_URL. The URL leg OUTRANKS the host/port halves in service_endpoint's resolution order, and the session-scoped engine-substrate fixture (t2_service_env via _pin_t2_substrate) had already exported an NX_SERVICE_URL pointing elsewhere. Reads went to that other service carrying this fixture's bearer, which it does not know -> 401. WRITES landed correctly because they go through an explicitly-constructed client with base_url passed in — which is exactly why it presented as 'seeded but invisible', the signature of an RLS problem.

FIX: re-point NX_SERVICE_URL at each test's own service, 11 sites. FALSIFIED rather than assumed — removing just that line reproduces 9 failed / 2 passed, precisely this bead's l9hd8 set; restoring it gives 11 passed, against the real Java service, in 8 seconds.

THIS BEAD'S COUNT DROPS BY 9. Remaining here: 5 test_taxonomy_e2e + 3 test_indexer_e2e.

⚠️ CHECK THE REST OF THE 52 FOR THE SAME CLASS BEFORE PORTING ANY OF THEM. This was never substrate-port debt — no production code was wrong, the test harness was pointing at the wrong endpoint. Any other file in your list that sets NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT/TOKEN without NX_SERVICE_URL is a candidate for the identical misdiagnosis, and the tell is a 4xx hiding inside an empty-looking result. Note this bead's own headline signature, 'httpx.UnsupportedProtocol: Request URL is missing an http:// or https:// protocol (38 occurrences)', is ALSO an NX_SERVICE_URL-shaped symptom — an EMPTY base URL. Worth checking whether some of the 32 test_indexer_e2e failures are the same root before treating them as port work.

NOT the same cause: the 5 test_http_catalog_integration reader-path failures (nexus-12m77). I applied the identical fix there and it changed nothing — that cluster connects and returns structurally-valid zeros ({'owners': 0, 'documents': 0, ...}), so it is data-visibility, not routing. Reverted that edit rather than leave unevidenced churn.

Reproduce any of this locally in ~10s, no gate script needed: uv run pytest <file> -m integration -q (T2 [21199]).

Whenever any topic link existed among a result set's topics, the WHOLE topic boost — the same-topic half included — was silently discarded. Service mode has been the default since the aqbrk flip. Converged the Http twin to the mapping; tests/test_ekn9n_topic_link_pairs_contract.py pins the shape and the store->apply_topic_boost seam substrate-neutrally and was written failing.

Verified DISCRIMINATING by mutation — the same assertion fails against an L2-derived and an inner-product-derived similarity.

The autouse _legacy_vector_backend pins vectors local (nexus-o06g4) but the catalog half was never pinned, so post-flip the flow ran with vectors client-side and documents in the engine catalog. The legacy->conformant rename's data plane then 404'd trying to re-home a collection the service had never seen, leaving chunks under the legacy name while _repo_collection_or_legacy already returned the conformant one. Completing the pin with local_catalog_backend fixes all 3 and removes no coverage — no shipping install splits them. Your earlier note asked whether these were downstream of w6h2m; they were not, and they were not port work either.
