title: [bug] engine writes three columns and a whole table that NO route can read — topic_assignments quality + hook_failures + detect_hubs warn_stale
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk auditing the RDR-155 P4b dies-roster. Three roster entries turned out to be ACCURATE about their mechanism — and that is the problem. Each records an ENGINE CAPABILITY GAP as a TEST RETIREMENT. "Dies at the flip" implies nothing is lost; what is actually lost is the ability to read data the engine is still writing.

VERIFIED, not taken from the roster text:

1. topic_assignments QUALITY COLUMNS ARE WRITE-ONLY.
   TaxonomyRepository.getAssignmentsForDocs (:576) selects DOC_ID and TOPIC_ID and nothing else. similarity, assigned_at and source_collection are written by the assign path and are readable through NO route — not /assignments/for_docs, not /assignments/docs, not /assignments/by_label. 6 tests rostered on this (tests/test_projection_quality.py::_RAW_QUALITY_READ).
   Consequence: in service mode an operator cannot ask "how confident is this assignment", "when was it made", or "which collection did it come from". The GREATEST/CASE upsert parity the roster cites as mitigation pins that the WRITE is correct; it does not give anyone a way to READ it.

2. hook_failures IS WRITE-ONLY.
   TelemetryHandler exposes /v1/telemetry/hook_failures/record and /hook_failures/trim. There is no read route. 7 tests rostered across tests/test_post_document_hooks.py and tests/test_post_store_hook.py.
   Consequence: the post-document / post-store hook failure log — the thing you consult when an indexing hook silently drops work — can be written and trimmed in service mode but never inspected. That is an observability regression on exactly the path that exists to surface silent failures.

3. detect_hubs(warn_stale=...) IS SILENTLY INERT.
   http_taxonomy_store.py:1415 passes max_last_discover_at=None with the comment "warn_stale not implemented over HTTP". The parameter is accepted and ignored — the caller gets no warning and no error. 2 tests rostered.
   This is the same shape as nexus-ybj1b (include_heuristic accepted and ignored) and deserves the same treatment: a flag the client accepts and the backend drops is a silent contract break, not a pending feature.

WHY ONE BEAD: the class is one. Data the engine writes that no route returns. The three instances were found by auditing ~50 roster entries in one file-by-file pass, which is not a systematic search — A SWEEP IS THE VALUABLE OUTPUT HERE. Suggested shape: for each Liquibase-declared column, is there a route whose SELECT includes it? Anything write-only is either dead weight that should not be written, or an observability gap.

FIX SHAPES (each independent):
  1. widen getAssignmentsForDocs' projection, or add /assignments/detail
  2. add /v1/telemetry/hook_failures/list (mirroring get_relevance_log)
  3. either implement warn_stale over HTTP or make the client REFUSE warn_stale=True in service mode rather than silently dropping it

The rostered tests stay skipped until there is something to read — that part of the roster is right. What is wrong is the reason: they should point HERE, not at "dies at the flip".

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FOURTH WRITE-ONLY COLUMN, same class, found 2026-07-26 by the nexus-aqbrk substrate port: tier_writes.target_title.

MECHANISM. The engine accepts and stores it — TelemetryHandler.java:221 reads target_title off the request body, TelemetryRepository.recordTierWrite (line 471) and importTierWritesBatch (line 599/874) both set the column. But every one of the three TIER_WRITES.TARGET_TITLE references in service/src/main/java is an INSERT. There is NO SELECT of it anywhere in the engine, and the only read route — GET /v1/telemetry/tier_writes/query, via HttpTelemetryStore.query_tier_writes — returns an AGGREGATE shaped (tool, tier, agent, project, count). The column cannot be read back by any client in service mode.

USER-VISIBLE SHAPE. target_title records WHICH entry a tier write targeted. Locally it is queryable (the raw column, and telemetry_etl exports it); in service mode the value is accepted, persisted, and unreachable. Same profile as the three already on this bead: not data loss, but data that can only be written.

WHERE IT SURFACED. tests/test_memory_put_attribution.py::test_agent_appears_in_tier_writes_telemetry asserted target == 'attribution-test'. Rather than dropping the assertion, the port added _assert_target_title, which asserts None on the service arm with this bead named in the failure message — so when a read route lands the test FAILS loudly instead of the gap closing silently. Same treatment as _assert_fts_hits / _assert_heuristic_excluded.

title: [bug] service-mode catalog graph ignores include_heuristic — the implements-heuristic flood is back on by default
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk porting tests/test_catalog_graph_heuristic_filter.py to the engine substrate.

CONTRACT (local side): Catalog.graph / graph_many EXCLUDE implements-heuristic edges by default; callers opt back in with include_heuristic=True. That file's own docstring says why it exists: the auto-emitted heuristic flood was 66% of the 2026-05-08 production link graph, 562-660 inbound edges on high-traffic infrastructure RDRs, drowning out hand-curated edges.

SERVICE SIDE: the flag never reaches the query. http_catalog_client.py:1624 and :1651, both with the same comment:

    # include_heuristic: forwarded to service for future support; currently informational
    if include_heuristic:
        payload["include_heuristic"] = True

CatalogHandler.handleTraverse reads only body["link_types"] and calls repo.graphBFS(tenant, seeds, linkTypes, direction, depth). "include_heuristic" appears NOWHERE in service/src/main/java. So:

  - the DEFAULT does not exclude heuristic edges — the flood is back
  - include_heuristic=True is indistinguishable from the default — the opt-in is a no-op in both directions

REPRO: seed two docs, link them with "implements-heuristic", call graph_many([seed], depth=1). Local: the heuristic neighbour is absent. Service: present.

BLAST RADIUS. Every service-mode consumer of the graph traversal: nx catalog links, the catalog_links MCP tool, the traverse MCP tool, and anything building a neighbour set for context. On a real catalog this is not a subtle ranking shift — it is the 2:1 flood the local default was added to suppress, silently reinstated for every user on the 6.0 default backend.

WHY "informational" IS THE WRONG SHAPE regardless of when the server implements it: a flag the client sends and the server ignores is a silent contract break. Either the client filters client-side until the server supports it, or the client refuses/warns when include_heuristic is passed in service mode. Sending it and hoping is the failure mode.

FIX OPTIONS (needs a call):
  (a) server-side: filter link_type <> 'implements-heuristic' in graphBFS unless include_heuristic is set. Correct, and where the local semantics live.
  (b) client-side: when include_heuristic is False, pass an explicit link_types list that omits implements-heuristic. Works only if the caller has not already supplied link_types, and changes "all types except one" into "an enumerated list" — fragile as link types are added.
(a) is the real fix; (b) is a stopgap that at least makes the default honest.

Needs a parity contract asserting default-excludes / opt-in-includes across both substrates.

TEST FALLOUT:
  test_catalog_graph_heuristic_filter.py::TestGraphDefaultExcludesHeuristic::test_graph_default_skips_heuristic_neighbor
  test_catalog_graph_heuristic_filter.py::TestGraphDefaultExcludesHeuristic::test_graph_many_inherits_default_exclude

BLOCKS: nexus-aqbrk.

Fixed in the engine, deployed, and now PINNED for local installs.

title: [bug] catalog_link_audit silently returns {} in service mode — an audit that reports nothing reads as an audit that found nothing
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk porting tests/test_catalog_mcp.py to the engine substrate.

  src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:1655

    def link_audit(self, *, t3: Any = None) -> dict:
        return {}  # not supported in initial service-mode implementation

The MCP tool catalog_link_audit (src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py:625) calls straight through to it and returns the result verbatim. So in service mode — the 6.0 default — the tool returns {} with no error key.

WHY THIS IS THE SILENT-FALLBACK CLASS, not merely an unimplemented method. The tool's own docstring promises "total, by_type, by_creator, orphaned (+ count), duplicates (+ count), stale_spans (+ count), stale_chash (+ count)". A caller — human or agent — asking "audit the link graph for health issues" and receiving {} reads that as a CLEAN graph. It is indistinguishable from "audited, found nothing". Every failure mode the audit exists to surface (orphaned links, duplicates, stale positional spans, chash spans that no longer resolve in T3) is silently reported as absent.

This is the same shape as nexus-at2ff, which the comment three lines above in mcp/catalog.py records: link_audit ALREADY had one silent-degradation bug in production, where passing ._client instead of the handle raised an AttributeError that the tool's broad `except Exception` swallowed into an error dict. That one at least produced an error key. This returns success-shaped emptiness.

MINIMUM FIX, independent of implementing the audit: return an explicit unsupported marker (e.g. {"error": "link_audit is not implemented for the service catalog"}) so the tool is honest. The MCP handler already has an error-dict contract and callers already check for it (_require_catalog returns exactly that shape).

REAL FIX: implement the audit server-side. The four checks it performs are all graph/manifest queries the engine can answer; the stale_chash leg additionally needs the T3 handle, which is why the local version takes t3=.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any automated path (doctor, a scheduled sweep, an agent skill) calls catalog_link_audit and treats {} as healthy. That determines whether this has been quietly passing in production or is merely available to be. Worth checking — nexus-1e2eh found a dangling-catalog_links doctor check with 277 live rows, so the graph is not hypothetically dirty.

TEST FALLOUT: tests/test_catalog_mcp.py::test_link_audit.
close_reason: Already shipped: the real fix (not just the honest-error minimum) landed in a62649efb — HttpCatalogClient.link_audit de-stubbed into a real audit (totals/by_type/by_creator/duplicates via paginated link_query + orphaned via /links/orphaned; t3 accepted-and-ignored, manifest answers the stale-chash question on this substrate). The test the bead named (tests/test_catalog_mcp.py::test_link_audit) exercises it and cites this bead as fixed; verified passing 2026-08-18. Consumer audit from the 07-26 comment stands: doctor was already defended, CLI/MCP now get real data.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CONSUMER AUDIT DONE 2026-07-26 — this answers the 'NOT ESTABLISHED' question in nexus-aqbrk's pass-3 comment (whether doctor, a sweep, or a skill calls link_audit and treats {} as healthy). Read-only source audit; every caller of link_audit in src/ was traced.

THREE CONSUMERS, AND THE SEVERITY RANKING IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT WAS ASSUMED.

1. nx doctor — ALREADY DEFENDED, and defended DELIBERATELY. commands/doctor.py::_report_dangling_links branches on storage_backend_for('catalog') and in SERVICE mode routes to _report_dangling_links_service, which calls the dedicated reader.orphaned_links() (GET /v1/catalog/links/orphaned, engine v0.1.55) and NOT the generic audit. Its docstring names this stub as the reason in so many words: 'HttpCatalogClient.link_audit() is a service-mode stub returning {}; that is why this check calls the dedicated orphaned_links() method rather than the generic audit.' It also fails LOUD (click Exit(2)) on transport error rather than reporting a clean zero. So the highest-trust consumer — the one an operator runs to be told the install is healthy — is the one that cannot be fooled. The sqlite branch's cat.link_audit() at doctor.py:1065 is only reached when the catalog backend is SQLite, where the method is real.

2. nx catalog link-audit (commands/catalog_cmds/links.py:333, hidden=True) — UNDEFENDED, and it splits by output mode. _get_catalog() -> make_catalog_reader() returns the shared HttpCatalogClient in service mode, so result is {}:
     - human path: result['total'] raises KeyError. Ugly, but LOUD — a traceback, not a false clean.
     - --json path: prints '{}' and exits 0. SILENT false-clean, and --json is precisely the machine-consumed path.
   So the residual exposure is narrower than the bead implies but lands exactly where it does the most damage: the scripted consumer, not the human one.

3. catalog_link_audit MCP tool (mcp/catalog.py:625) — returns {} verbatim. The bead's original finding, unchanged.

NO scheduled sweep, hook, or agent skill calls it. Greps across src/, conexus/, sn/, docs/, scripts/ return only the three above plus documentation. docs/catalog.md line 272 does tell operators 'Run nx catalog link-audit' to detect stale spans, so consumer 2 is documented user-facing advice, not a vestige.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX. Implementing link_audit service-side remains the right fix. But if it is going to sit unimplemented for a while, the cheap interim is a service-mode guard on link_audit_cmd — the --json arm is the only place today that returns success-shaped emptiness to something that cannot notice. Doctor already shows the idiom to copy (dedicated endpoint + Exit(2) on unknown, never a clean zero).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PARTIALLY FIXED on develop a62649ef — and deliberately NOT closed, because the fix is narrower than this bead's contract.

nexus-ai41v was filed later against the SAME stub (http_catalog_client.py link_audit returning {}) and I closed it on that commit. link_audit is no longer success-shaped emptiness: it now computes total, by_type, by_creator, duplicates (+ duplicate_count) and orphaned (+ orphaned_count) from reads the engine already serves — paginated /link_query with no filters, plus /links/orphaned (nexus-ysrwi) — so no engine change was needed. The MCP inverted pin in tests/test_catalog_mcp.py::test_link_audit (which asserted result == {} and asked for the unconditional assertion back) fired on the change and is restored to real assertions.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL COVERS, and why it stays open: the tool's own docstring (mcp/catalog.py:629-632) promises TWO MORE legs that I did not implement — stale_spans (+ count, positional spans on re-indexed docs) and stale_chash (+ count, content-hash spans that no longer resolve in T3, each entry carrying a  of 'missing' or otherwise). Those keys are absent from my return dict, so a caller reading result['stale_chash_count'] still gets a KeyError, and a caller who checks 'is stale_chash in result' still reads absence as CLEAN. That is the same silent-false-clean shape this bead names, just narrowed from 'the whole audit' to 'two of its seven legs'. Do not close this on the ai41v commit.

WHAT THE REMAINING WORK NEEDS. stale_chash requires resolving each chash span against T3 to classify 'missing' vs otherwise — the local implementation took a  handle for exactly this, and my port accepts  and IGNORES it (documented in the docstring as call-site parity). So the honest next step is either to implement the two legs against T3 + the manifest, or to change the MCP docstring so it stops promising them — but NOT to leave the docstring advertising keys the substrate never returns, which is how this class propagates.

Related: nexus-at2ff (the PRIOR silent-degradation bug in this same verb, which at least produced an error key).

title: [bug] engine: catalog document LIST reads ignore deleted_at — every tombstoned document keeps appearing in nx catalog list and every by_* listing
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk (RDR-158/155 substrate port), porting tests/test_catalog_audit_membership.py to the engine substrate. Bucket 4 — a genuine service gap, not test debt.

REPRO (deterministic, single test):
  seed 8 documents in rdr__p: 5 with source_uri under /myproject, 3 under /elsewhere
  nx catalog audit-membership rdr__p --purge-non-canonical --yes
    -> "Deleted 3 of 3 non-canonical entries."   (the writes DID happen)
  catalog.list_by_collection("rdr__p")
    -> 8 entries                                  (all three deleted rows still listed)

MECHANISM. delete_document tombstones (sets catalog_documents.deleted_at); it does not remove the row. The POINT lookups correctly filter — CatalogRepository has DELETED_AT.isNull() at :452 :462 :520 :538 :624 :635 :728 :755 :804 :1016 :1039 :1070 :1900 — but the LIST reads do not. Unfiltered, all in CatalogRepository.java:

  listDocuments                :1117
  documentsByCollection        :1251
  documentsByFilePath          :1260
  documentsBySourceUri         :1269
  documentsByOwner             :1278
  documentsByOwnerAndFilePath  :1295
  documentsByContentType       :1306
  documentsByCorpus            :1316
  descendants                  :~1327

Intent is not ambiguous: catalog-004-manifest-functions.xml filters d.deleted_at IS NULL in three places and its own comment says "TOMBSTONE-AWARE". The list reads were simply missed.

USER-VISIBLE BLAST RADIUS, service mode (the 6.0 default):
  - nx catalog list  and  nx catalog list --collection/--content-type/--corpus/--owner  show deleted documents
  - every consumer of catalog.list_by_collection / by_file_path / by_source_uri / by_owner / by_content_type / by_corpus sees them
  - a delete reports success and appears not to have happened, which reads as a broken delete rather than a broken list
  - counts derived from these reads (audits, sweeps, coverage checks) are inflated by exactly the tombstone population

SQLite has no equivalent because it HARD-deletes, so this class cannot exist there — it is new with the pgvector/PG catalog and has no pre-migration analogue.

FIX is mechanical (add .and(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS.DELETED_AT.isNull()) to the nine), but TWO THINGS NEED A CALL FIRST:
  1. Is any caller deliberately relying on seeing tombstones (restore/undelete flows, doctor's orphan and drift checks, replay equality)? If so it needs an explicit include_deleted parameter rather than a blanket filter.
  2. descendants() feeds tumbler-allocation and cascade logic — filtering there changes whether a deleted child still reserves its tumbler. That is a semantics decision, not a bug fix.

Needs a parity contract asserting delete-then-list across both substrates, so the divergence cannot silently return.

TEST FALLOUT: test_catalog_audit_membership.py::TestPurge::test_purge_actually_deletes_non_canonical and ::test_canonical_home_override_when_contaminant_dominates fail under the engine substrate for exactly this. They assert correct user-facing intent and must NOT be rewritten to accommodate the gap.

BLOCKS: nexus-aqbrk.

Fixed in the engine, deployed, and now PINNED for local installs.

diacritics in catalog document search).

Shipped in engine-service-v0.1.57, deployed to api.conexus-nexus.com 2026-07-27,
cloud-gated GREEN (parity 105/113 byte-identical to the v0.1.56 baseline, zero
per-query regressions). Deployed-schema readback confirmed fold_diacritics present on
nexus.catalog_documents.fts_vector via pg_get_expr — the changeset applied on that
cluster, not merely reported.

Delivery to local-mode installs closed by 721cd3f7 (REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION -> (0,1,57)).

CatalogRepositoryTest.searchDocuments_foldsDiacritics_withinTheFts5Range.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME NINE METHODS, found in the same port pass (nexus-aqbrk, test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py): the collection-scoped list IGNORES ITS LIMIT.

  catalog.list_by_collection("knowledge__delos", limit=3)
    sqlite  -> 3 entries
    service -> 5 entries (everything)

MECHANISM. HttpCatalogClient.list_by_collection DOES send it (params["limit"] = limit, http_catalog_client.py:1067-1073). CatalogHandler's /list route parses `limit` and passes it to repo.listDocuments — but the collection branch calls repo.documentsByCollection(tenant, collection), whose signature has no limit at all (CatalogRepository.java:1251). Same for documentsByFilePath / BySourceUri / ByOwner / ByOwnerAndFilePath / ByContentType / ByCorpus / descendants: the client can ask, the service cannot honour, and nothing reports that the cap was dropped.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN ITS OWN BEAD: identical method set, identical fix site, and both are the same class of omission — the by_* readers were written as plain filtered selects while the parameters that listDocuments honours (deleted_at, limit) were never carried across. Fixing tombstones without fixing the limit means touching all nine twice.

USER-VISIBLE: any caller bounding a catalog read gets an unbounded one. On a large collection that is a latency and payload cliff, not just a wrong count — and it silently defeats every "peek at the first N" call site.

Test fallout adds: test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestListByCollection::test_limit_caps_result.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26 — commit 12614bdb on feature/nexus-aqbrk-substrate-port.

NOT YET: engine tag, conexus deploy, cloud re-gate. Second lifecycle, Hal-relayed.

THE TWO OPEN QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE, not assumption:

1. "Is any caller deliberately relying on seeing tombstones?" NO.
   - nx catalog undelete restores from a BACKUP FILE (catalog_backup.restore_documents
     re-registers the docs); it never reads live tombstones.
   - purge_trash reads deleted_at IS NOT NULL directly in PL/pgSQL (catalog-003
     changeset 5), not through any Java method.
   - The catalog-004 manifest functions were ALREADY tombstone-aware in SQL — their own
     comments say "TOMBSTONE-AWARE".
   - There is no trash-LISTING surface at all: document_trash / document_restore /
     purge_trash are all verbs operating on the table directly.
   So a blanket filter is correct and no include_deleted parameter is needed.

2. "Does filtering descendants() change whether a deleted child reserves its tumbler?"
   NO — the premise is wrong. Allocation never consults descendants(). registerDocument
   claims catalog_owners.NEXT_SEQ under FOR UPDATE (CatalogRepository ~line 468). The
   counter only moves forward, so a tombstone never released its tumbler in the first
   place and filtering cannot cause reuse or collision.

SCOPE WAS NINE; THE CLASS WAS TWENTY-TWO. A scripted audit of every
from(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS) / selectFrom(CATALOG_DOCUMENTS) in the class found 30 reads, 22
unfiltered. Beyond the nine on the bead:

  countDocuments                the inflated-counts symptom the bead DESCRIBES but did
                                not list as a site
  lookupDocByCollectionAndPath  resolves a tumbler for WRITES — a tombstone match hands
                                a caller a deleted document to write into. Arguably a
                                worse bug than the listing one that was reported.
  searchDocuments, graphBFS node hydration, chunkCountsForDocs, distinctDocCollections,
  docsWithAbsolutePaths, coverageByContentType, orphanedDocs, orphanedLinks (x2),
  documentExists

21 now filtered. Fixing the reported nine and leaving thirteen is the exact shape this
tree keeps repeating (catalog-015 fixed the catalog and left memory; j0nec was fixed in
one file and left in 23).

ONE DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, documented at its declaration so it does not read as an
oversight: physicalCollectionOf. It is a manifest WRITE helper (writeManifestRows,
appendManifestChunks, two import-chunk paths), not a reader. Filtering would stamp NULL
onto rows written for a tombstoned doc — re-introducing the silent-empty class the
nexus-x6kdz stamp exists to fix — and it would do it on the ETL/import leg, which
legitimately writes manifests for documents whose live state it does not control.

DECISION RULE used, in case a future reader wants to extend it: every one of these
methods documents itself as replacing a "SELECT ... FROM documents" SQLite statement,
and SQLite HARD-deletes, so that table never contains tombstones. Matching it is parity,
not new policy. The invariant is now: a tombstone is invisible to every read except the
trash/purge SQL functions.

TWO SEMANTIC CHANGES WORTH NAMING, since they alter doctor output rather than just
removing noise:
  - orphanedLinks now reports a link whose endpoint is TOMBSTONED as dangling. Correct
    under parity (SQLite would have hard-deleted the endpoint, so the link would already
    report orphaned there), and it predicts the true orphan purge_trash will create.
  - documentExists was filtered in LOCKSTEP with orphanedLinks' fromMissing/toMissing.
    If the two disagreed about tombstones a link would be reported orphaned with `side`
    naming neither endpoint. Noted at the declaration.

VERIFICATION: full mvn suite 1459 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors; SoftDeleteTest 15/15
(the tombstone-semantics suite, unchanged and green with all 21 reads filtered);
CatalogRepositoryTest 137/137.

FALSIFIED: reverting ONE filter (documentsByCollection — the bead's own repro) fails
tombstonedDocument_isInvisibleToEveryRead with ["9.1","9.2"], i.e. the tombstone leaking
into exactly the read the bead reported. The contract test also carries a non-vacuity
block, because every doesNotContain/isEmpty assertion in it is satisfied by an empty
tenant.

title: [bug] Hook/guard fixes are INERT until the next release — the pinned-source plugin means today's guards do not protect today
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-07-25 by a live miss, not by reasoning: a subagent ran `git stash -u` in the shared tree and the subagent_git_write guard did NOT block it — despite that guard explicitly covering stash and treating bare `git stash` as destructive.

ROOT CAUSE: the marketplace pinned-source release model. `marketplace.json` plugins[].source.ref is pinned to an immutable RELEASE TAG (currently v6.18.1). Claude Code loads hooks from the INSTALLED plugin at that tag, NOT from the working tree. So every hook/guard edit on develop is inert in every running session until a release is cut and installed.

CONFIRMED BLAST RADIUS — all three of today's guard commits are INERT right now:
  a7ef414d  git-write guard: blocked harmless verbs, permitted destructive ones (nexus-ays2l)
  d24f95db  direct-push-to-main guard, consolidated (nexus-vduer)
  df20ae28  Gap-1 blind-spot fix (nexus-mk3tw)

The stash coverage in a7ef414d landed TODAY, after v6.18.1. That is precisely why the stash was not blocked.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST 'working as designed': the pinned model is CORRECT and deliberate (it decouples installed users from main HEAD — do not propose changing it). The defect is the EXPECTATION GAP. We closed nexus-ays2l and nexus-vduer describing them as 'mechanized', and a reader — including a future session — will reasonably believe the control is active. It is not. A guard believed-live but actually inert is worse than a known-absent one, because nobody compensates for it.

The failure is self-demonstrating: the guard for exactly this slip was written, merged, closed as done, and then failed to prevent the slip it was written for, on the same day.

OPTIONS (Hal's call, do not pick unilaterally):
1. Accept + make visible. Hook-affecting commits state 'INERT until vX.Y.Z' in the commit and bead. Cheapest, no mechanism, relies on discipline — which is what already failed.
2. Dev-mode override: when CWD is the nexus repo itself, load hooks from the working tree rather than the installed plugin. Makes the repo dogfood its own guards immediately. Needs care: a broken in-tree hook would then break the session that is editing it.
3. A release-cadence rule: any commit touching conexus/hooks/** triggers a release bump, so guards never sit inert for long. Interacts with the 'bump cadence matches user-visible impact, not commit volume' directive.
4. A test/CI tripwire that fails when conexus/hooks/** has changed since the tag named in marketplace.json source.ref — turns the silent gap into a visible one without changing the release model.

RELATED: nexus-1e2eh (procedures naming things that no longer exist) is the same family — a control that looks authoritative but is not operative.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RESOLVED a4fbe2f7 — Hal chose the CI-tripwire option (option 4), then the design was refined once more during implementation.

WHY NOT THE ORIGINALLY-RECOMMENDED DOGFOOD OPTION: Hal first picked it and I was implementing when .claude/settings.json turned out to carry an explicit warning against exactly that mechanism. nexus-3h0u6 (CLOSED) is the precedent: RDR-184 .16 armed repo sessions from that file "without waiting for a plugin release", the plugin release then shipped, BOTH surfaces fired, and every hook-written START/REPORTED row was DUPLICATED — inflating the very census the bead existed to measure. A test now enforces single registration. Distinction that made it survivable-but-worse: those were ORCHESTRATION hooks that WRITE rows (duplication corrupts), whereas routing hooks are read-only deny/allow (duplication only wastes). But double-firing also doubles the routing latency to ~270ms against RDR-121 300ms budget, reopening the budget just closed by consolidating nexus-vduer. Surfaced to Hal, who switched to the tripwire.

THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: a plain drift tripwire — fail when the surface differs from the pinned tag — would be RED CONTINUOUSLY between releases, and this repo has documented repeatedly what happens to a check that cries wolf: blessed reflexively, stops meaning anything. So drift is NOT the failure. UNDECLARED drift is. conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md is the acknowledgement ledger; declaring costs one line and the ledger doubles as the "what goes live next release" list, which nobody had before.

SYMMETRY IS LOAD-BEARING: a STALE entry fails too. When a release advances the pin, drift returns to zero and the ledger must be emptied — otherwise it decays into a permanent list of already-shipped things, which reads exactly like a list of pending ones (the same believed-vs-actual confusion one level up). The release skill now clears it at the source.ref bump, so a forgotten clear BLOCKS the release.

SURFACE IS BROADER THAN HOOKS, on evidence: commands/ and skills/ are pinned identically. The same session edited continuation.md and orchestration/SKILL.md believing the fixes took effect immediately. They did not.

Six files declared pending right now — including the push-to-main and git-stash guards that are NOT protecting this repo today.

Non-vacuity: SURFACE prefixes must exist (a renamed dir cannot silently zero coverage); a FAILED git diff asserts rather than reporting zero drift; tagless shallow checkouts SKIP with taglessness VERIFIED not assumed. Mutation-verified both directions.

title: CI red on develop since a797dbd4 (17:55 UTC 2026-07-25): test_newest_published_engine_reads_real_tags fails in ci.yml's test job — no fetch-tags/fetch-depth:0 there
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CONFIRMED via gh run list --branch develop + gh run view --log-failed:

- CI 'test' job has failed on EVERY push since a797dbd4 (2026-07-25T17:55:19Z) through bfd3c25d, 459fdb8d, a23a2aa3 -- 4 consecutive commits, ~4h+ red, unaddressed.
- Failure: tests/scripts/test_check_engine_release_floor.py::test_newest_published_engine_reads_real_tags -> AssertionError: engine-service-v* tags exist in this repo.
- Root cause: the test calls gate.newest_published_engine() with no repo_root override, i.e. against whatever checkout CI gives it. It runs 'git tag -l engine-service-v*' via subprocess. .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'test' job checkout (line ~53) uses plain actions/checkout with NEITHER fetch-depth:0 NOR fetch-tags:true -- the shallow, tag-less default. Only .github/workflows/release.yml's checkout was patched with fetch-tags:true in this same diff (a797dbd4). Reproduced locally: 'git clone --depth 1 --no-tags' + calling newest_published_engine(repo_root=...) against it returns None, which is exactly the assertion that fails in CI.
- The commit's own claim ('Full unit suite: 13,353 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors') is accurate for a LOCAL run (full clone, real tags) and does not contradict this -- the gap is CI-environment-specific and was never exercised before push.
- Two other develop workflows are ALSO currently red (Guided-upgrade MVV, Era-spanning upgrade hop) but CONFIRMED pre-existing (failing since at least 2026-07-24T20:40, unrelated to this session) -- do not conflate with this finding.
- Not release-blocking (release.yml's own checkout IS correctly patched), but it is the ordinary per-push CI signal being red for hours across multiple commits with zero remediation, which is exactly the failure mode the four sibling directives (no-blanket-reruns, run crosscutting tripwires, never dismiss as pre-existing, full-suite-before-tag) exist to catch.

FIX SHAPE: add 'fetch-tags: true' (or 'fetch-depth: 0') to the 'test' job's checkout step in ci.yml, OR make test_newest_published_engine_reads_real_tags skip/xfail when running under a shallow CI checkout it cannot control, OR patch newest_published_engine's test to inject repo_root pointing at a location guaranteed to carry tags. Simplest, most consistent-with-existing-precedent fix: mirror the fetch-depth:0 pattern ci.yml already uses elsewhere (lines 236, 441, 611, 690) in the 'test' job.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CLOSED — CI GREEN on 538905c8, confirmed by an actual run (gh run list), not by a local clone. develop had been red from a797dbd4 through af4033ad.

TWO ATTEMPTS. The first fix (af4033ad, `fetch-tags: true` on ci.yml) was plausible, passed locally, and was WRONG: the engine-service-v* tags point at commits outside a depth-1 history, so the refs never materialise and the test still saw an empty list. Only CI could tell me that — which is precisely the property that let the original bug live for four commits.

FINAL SHAPE (538905c8), a split rather than one knob:
- ci.yml: fetch-tags REVERTED. Per-push jobs must not pay for a tag/history fetch, and it did not work anyway.
- release.yml: fetch-depth: 0. The only reliable way to see the tags, affordable once per release, and the only place the GATE actually runs.
- test_newest_published_engine_reads_real_tags now SKIPS with an explicit reason on a tagless checkout instead of asserting a property the environment controls. The parse bug it guards is covered hermetically by test_newest_published_engine_parses_the_tag_namespace, which builds its own repo. Verified against a real `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags`: 15 passed, 1 skipped.

LESSON, recorded because it generalises: a test that asserts a property of the CHECKOUT rather than of the CODE will pass locally and fail in CI forever. Non-vacuity guards are especially prone to it — they are written to prove the scanner sees real data, and "real data" is exactly what a shallow clone lacks. Build the non-vacuity fixture instead of reading the ambient repo.

title: RDR-158/155 substrate port: 157 files must move off the SQLite-pinned test substrate — the unbudgeted gate on the entire 7.0.0 wave
description:
THIS IS THE REAL GATE ON nexus-i711w AND THE WHOLE 7.0.0 WAVE, AND IT WAS NEVER A BEAD. It has existed only as three comments on nexus-g37fr since 2026-07-25. Everything downstream — i711w (delete 8 SQLite stores), 146xx.18 (census-to-empty), the RDR-155 P4b closeout — is blocked behind it, so an untracked item is holding up five epics.

MEASURED, not estimated (2026-07-25). Method: flip _pin_storage_backend_sqlite in tests/conftest.py to default to the engine substrate, run the full suite, REVERT. Nothing was committed.

  820 failed, 12,533 passed, 51 errors, 157 distinct files
  1,703s vs the 822s sqlite baseline = 2.07x

THE FAILURES ARE SEMANTIC, NOT INFRASTRUCTURAL. Canonical case: `assert make_catalog_reader() is None` means "no catalog file" under SQLite; in service mode there is always a _SharedServiceCatalogHandle, so the assertion is unsatisfiable rather than wrong. These are not flaky tests to re-run; each encodes a SQLite-shaped assumption that has to be re-expressed.

BUCKETS (full detail in the nexus-g37fr comments):
  164  raw .conn access — HttpMemoryStore 51, HttpTaxonomyStore 47, HttpPlanLibrary 25,
       HttpDocumentAspectsStore 9, HttpTelemetryStore 6. The Http stores fail LOUD with a
       directive message, so each site names its own fix. Most tractable.
  ~168 opaque bare asserts (103 `assert N == N`, 35 `assert False`, 16 `assert N != N`,
       14 `assert None is not None`). No diagnostic text.
  ~46  service-refusal semantics (TNEnsureOutcome.SERVICE_MODE_SKIP 22, plan-repair
       refusals 12, "No plan with id N" 12).
  ~14  GENUINE service gaps, not test debt.
  ~8   credential (voyage_api_key in cloud-path tests).

RECOMMENDED ORDER: bucket 1 (repetitive, builds the idiom), then 3 (mechanical once the
pattern is set), then 4 (gaps, possibly engine-gated), then 2 LAST — many opaque asserts
will resolve as side effects of 1 and 3, so diagnosing them first means diagnosing failures
that were about to disappear.

MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS: NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=engine routes the autouse pin to the engine
without editing a file, so subsets can be ported and dry-run incrementally with the pin
flipped LAST.

TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE HOW TO WORK IT:
1. A GREEN SUBSET CARRIES ALMOST NO SIGNAL. A 7-file dry run passed 118 tests; the full
   suite then failed 820. P0a "TEST-SIDE COMPLETE" covered a PRUNED sweep. Do not
   extrapolate from subsets — only the full flip is evidence.
2. NEW (2026-07-25, from nexus-at2ff): converting a SQLite read to an HTTP read adds a
   TRANSPORT-ERROR class the CALLER may not own. The SQLite path could only fail at OPEN
   time; a resolvable-but-dead service raises httpx errors that reach the user as a
   traceback, or worse get swallowed by a broad except and read as "unavailable, skipping".
   Audit the caller except arms, not just the store method. That exact shape had already
   disabled chash-span validation in production undetected.

THE 2.07x IS INHERENT — DO NOT TRY TO OPTIMISE IT AWAY. Measured: 400 tenant mints against
one engine session at mean 10ms, p50 10ms, p95 12ms, and latency DROPPED over the run
(0.71x drift). That extrapolates to ~138s of minting against an 881s gap, roughly 16%.
TENANT POOLING IS THE WRONG FIX AND MUST NOT BE BUILT. The remaining ~743s is every T2 op
crossing HTTP to a real PG instead of an in-process SQLite file. If this lands, a ~28
minute suite is the permanent price — which is its own argument for nexus-w1ip (suite
reduction) landing first or alongside.

BLOCKS: nexus-i711w -> nexus-146xx.18. Related: nexus-eqxxh (CI has no service JAR, so
engine-substrate tests SKIP in CI — this port cannot be CI-validated until that lands),
nexus-w1ip (suite reduction), nexus-uq3xs (containerised fan-out).
close_reason:
COMPLETE. The port landed, the flip landed, and the merge boundary is VERIFIED running the engine.

WHAT SHIPPED (four PRs, all merged to develop):
  #1426 5079f388  the substrate port itself — 820 failed / 51 errors / 157 files -> zero
  #1429 308522b3  ANALYZE the tables our migrations rewrite (BUG-0148 invariant + lint)
  #1428 9f59e473  the FLIP: engine becomes the default test substrate, plus the CI shape
  #1430 c13d0c84  the rollback chain could not execute (nexus-vx7a0)

THE FLIP. engine_substrate_selected() is spelled != "sqlite" on purpose: unset, a typo,
or a stale =engine all resolve to the ENGINE, and only the explicit
NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=sqlite opt-out reaches SQLite. Everything that is not the deliberate
opt-out fails toward the substrate the product ships on.

CI SHAPE (fea3472f, 842a918f). pull_request runs the SQLite arm (~13m); the develop PUSH
after each merge runs the ENGINE default. Timeout 30->45 because 3.12 was CANCELLED at
30m18s on the engine arm. Both CA-3 jobs pin sqlite — they have no service JAR.
ACCEPTED TRADE, stated so it is not rediscovered as a surprise: an engine-only regression
now surfaces at the merge boundary, one merge later than the PR that introduced it.

VERIFIED, not assumed — run 30268898443 (c13d0c84), job 89986724263, SUCCESS:
    NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE:           <- empty -> ENGINE
    NX_T2_SUBSTRATE_EXPECTED: 1     <- armed: an absent/stale JAR fails loudly
    13277 passed, 332 skipped, 559 deselected, 2 xfailed in 1834.83s (0:30:34)
The SKIP COUNT is the proof, not the pass count — both arms pass. Local: engine 333
skipped, sqlite 125. CI's 332 is the engine band; anything near 125-127 would have meant
the push branch of the substrate expression never resolved and the merge boundary was
silently vacuous. The CI-vs-local pass gap is the 559 deselected, not lost coverage.

WHAT THE PORT FOUND. Four engine defects, ALL silent-wrong-answer rather than error, none
of which any green signal would have surfaced: nexus-22r1f (memory FTS could not find a
word inside a dotted title), the Latin-1 diacritic fold gap in memory AND catalog search,
nexus-23wlw (tombstoned docs visible to 21 catalog LIST reads), nexus-ybj1b (graph
ignored include_heuristic). All fixed, shipped in engine-service-v0.1.57, deployed and
cloud-gated, and delivered to local-mode installs by the floor bump 721cd3f7. That is the
argument for the port stated as evidence: testing against SQLite could not see any of them.

DOWNSTREAM UNBLOCKED: nexus-i711w, nexus-146xx.18, the RDR-155 P4b closeout, and the rest
of the 7.0.0 wave.

RESIDUAL, filed not forgotten: nexus-a0m60 (no test ever EXECUTES a Liquibase rollback —
the root cause behind vx7a0), nexus-4k91k (CA-3 green-by-skipping; read its CORRECTION
comment, the description's cache diagnosis is wrong), and a P2 for the
stale-JAR-breaks-pure-static-tests friction the flip introduced.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PORT STARTED 2026-07-25 on feature/nexus-aqbrk-substrate-port (off develop 8a8ce284, after PR #1422 landed). Pilot file test_t2.py: 33 engine failures -> 0, sqlite still 78 green. Commit 42f1c0a9.

IDIOM ESTABLISHED (use this for the rest of bucket 1):
  1. READS NEED NO BRANCH. store.get_all(project) returns the full column set on both substrates AND tracks no access, unlike get()/search(). Every `SELECT <col> FROM memory WHERE ...` read-back becomes tests._t2_fixture_ops.memory_row(db, project, title). This alone covers a large share of the 164.
  2. WRITES BRANCH ONCE, IN A HELPER, NOT AT THE CALL SITE. tests/_t2_fixture_ops.py holds backdate_memory / set_memory_access_count / rewrite_memory_row / seed_relevance. SQLite arm = raw UPDATE, service arm = the store's import_* method (import_entry / import_relevance_row write timestamp+access_count VERBATIM, which is exactly what fixture manipulation needs). The existing per-file inline-branch idiom is correct but would have produced 51 copies for the HttpMemoryStore cluster alone; when i711w lands, one helper collapses instead of 51 sites.
  3. SQLITE-MACHINERY TESTS GET _require_sqlite_substrate(). Not "SQLite-shaped assertions" — tests OF the substrate: WAL journal mode, the FTS5 rebuild migration, sqlite3 connection lifecycle, the cross-process migration guard. It resolves via storage_backend_for, NOT NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE, so it survives the pin flip inverting the env var's meaning. Audit the skip reasons after every file — all 8 skips in test_t2.py carry that single reason.

TWO THINGS WORTH GENERALISING:

A. VACUOUS PASSES ARE A REAL RISK, and the full-flip run does NOT surface them. test_context_manager_closes_on_exit/-on_exception assert pytest.raises(Exception) around a .conn probe. The service-backed guard raises AttributeError — an Exception — so both tests PASS in service mode against a facade that never closed anything. They were not in the 820. Any test asserting a broad exception type around a raw handle is suspect; grep for `raises(Exception)` near `.conn` per file.

B. BUCKET 4 IS BIGGER THAN 14 AND IT STARTS IN THE FIRST FILE. Four of test_t2.py's 33 were genuine service defects, now nexus-22r1f (P0): service-mode memory search diverges from FTS5 on three axes — dotted-title tokenization (no word inside a .md title is findable), accent folding, and the trailing-* prefix operator. REPRODUCED AGAINST HAL'S LIVE INSTALL, not just the test tenant. Those tests are NOT rewritten to accommodate it; _assert_fts_hits asserts the known-broken service value so the eventual fix fails loudly instead of silently going green. Expect more of this shape — the rule is: if the test asserts correct user-facing intent, it is a bead, not a rewrite.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
TAXONOMY CLUSTER DONE 2026-07-25 — and it needed ZERO test edits. Commit 4283976d.

  tests/test_taxonomy.py                        44 failed -> 132 passed, 18 skipped
  + review_auto / rebuild_link_cleanup / status_links / backfill / test_context   63 passed, 8 skipped
  sqlite arm unchanged: 221 passed across the same six files

ALL of it was ONE defect in tests/conftest.py's next_import_seed_id, not substrate semantics. Full mechanism is in the commit message; the short version:

  - importTopic ends with advanceTopicsIdSequence(setval to GREATEST(last_value, srcId)) — correct and deliberate for a migrating tenant.
  - nexus.topics has a GLOBAL BIGSERIAL PK, so on the shared session engine one import at N drags the sequence to N for EVERY tenant.
  - Ordinary topic creation then consumes N+1, N+2, ... and overtakes the counter.
  - The next import draws a consumed id, ON CONFLICT (id) lands on another tenant's row, RLS rejects the WITH CHECK, and the handler reports HTTP 409 "supplied id is not available in this tenant".

The conftest comment asserted the opposite ("preserves ids VERBATIM without advancing the engine's serial sequences") — that stale claim is what made the counter design look sound. Fixed by giving the counter a 1,000,000 STRIDE; a bigger base does NOT work, because the serial path just follows the counter up from wherever it lands (verified with a pid-derived offset probe, which reproduced identically).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TAXONOMY CLUSTER — three things:

1. THE 820 CONTAINS INFRASTRUCTURE NOISE, and the bucketing cannot see it. These 44 sat in the "raw .conn access / HttpTaxonomyStore 47" bucket, which implied 47 call sites to rewrite. The real work was one line. Any bucket-1 file whose failures are httpx.HTTPStatusError rather than AttributeError deserves this suspicion FIRST — the fail-loud .conn guard is an AttributeError, so an HTTP error means the raw access was already ported and something else is wrong.

2. IT IS ORDER-DEPENDENT AND CUMULATIVE, which is the profile everyone is trained to call flake. It passes in isolation, moves under deselection, and the error text names a cause that is not the cause. The "these are not flaky tests to re-run" rule in this bead is right, but the corollary is that a genuinely order-dependent INFRASTRUCTURE failure will be mistaken for a semantic one, not the reverse.

3. RE-MEASURE BEFORE TRUSTING THE REMAINING BUCKET SIZES. The 820/157-file baseline was taken with this defect live. I have not re-run the full flip, so I do not know how much of the rest it accounts for — but it is now wrong to treat 820 as the work remaining.

NOT A PRODUCTION BUG, with one caveat worth its own look later: in production the sequence-advance is right for a single migrating tenant. The multi-tenant hazard is real but different — one tenant's ordinary usage can consume an id space another tenant later tries to import into, producing the same 409 on a real migration. The handler's own comment already treats cross-tenant id collision as accepted risk, so this is a note, not a bead, unless someone hits it.

NEXT: the plan-library cluster is NOT this class — 54 failures across test_plan_library / plan_repair_verbs / plan_cmd, and they are genuine bucket-3 service-refusal semantics ("plans are served by the storage service", "No plan with id N", no-DB-file paths).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PLAN-LIBRARY CLUSTER DONE 2026-07-25. Commits 5fe9efe6 (production fix) + d74e8702 (test port). 54 engine failures -> 0; 326 still green under the sqlite pin; 12 files verified on both substrates; 1 skip, audited.

BREAKDOWN — and only ONE of the four files was the bucket the census predicted:

  test_plan_library.py     23  genuine bucket 1 (AttributeError on .conn). Mechanical:
                               get_plan() returns the full column set identically on both
                               stores, so `SELECT <col> FROM plans WHERE id = ?` became
                               `plans.get_plan(row_id)["<col>"]` at 22 sites via script.
                               One test needed real created_at control -> seed_plan helper.
  test_plan_repair_verbs   17  NOT substrate semantics.
  test_plan_cmd            12  NOT substrate semantics.
  test_plan_disable         5  NOT substrate semantics.

THE 34 NON-SEMANTIC ONES ARE A THIRD FAILURE CLASS, distinct from both bucket 1 and the
taxonomy counter defect. These tests seed rows with a direct sqlite3.connect and invoke the
CLI with default_db_path patched at that file — they assert CLI behaviour AGAINST THE LOCAL
FILE. Under the engine the CLI reads the service, so the seeded rows are not where it looks.
Nothing is wrong with the test or the code.

The disposition is NOT a skip: `nx plan repair` refuses in service mode with "Set
NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite to deliberately repair the local file", so pinning the backend is
literally what the tool documents an operator to do, and it keeps coverage of a verb that
still works. Expect this class wherever a test drives a CLI against a hand-seeded file — the
tell is `sqlite3.connect` plus a patched default_db_path in the same test.

BEFORE PINNING, VERIFY THE SERVICE HALF IS OWNED SOMEWHERE. I checked rather than assumed:
test_plan_list_routes_to_service / test_plan_delete_routes_to_service and the two
*_refuses_in_service_mode tests cover it, and they set the backend themselves so they win
over an autouse pin. One real gap surfaced — `nx plan disable`/`enable` has NO service-mode
routing coverage at all — which is pre-existing, not caused by the port; recorded in the
class docstring rather than papered over. Worth a bead if anyone wants it closed.

BUCKET 4 AGAIN, AND AGAIN IN THE FIRST FILE: HttpPlanLibrary.set_scope_tags never normalized.
The service writes scope_tags verbatim (PlanHandler -> PlanRepository.setScopeTags, no
normalisation) exactly as it does for /v1/plans/save — and save_plan compensates client-side.
set_scope_tags did not, so service-mode `nx plan set-scope` stored hash suffixes and the "all"
sentinel raw, and the matcher reads a stored "all" as a scope NAMED all, conflicting with
every real tag (the RDR-091 C-3 failure, reintroduced one method over). NOT engine-gated —
pure client omission, fixed in 5fe9efe6 by giving the four copies of that logic one owner
(nexus.plans.scope.normalize_scope_tags). Fix committed separately from the test port so the
production change can be reviewed on its own.

RUNNING TALLY OF FAILURE CLASSES, none of which the 820-bucketing separates:
  1. genuine raw .conn -> rewrite through the public API (the census's bucket 1)
  2. test-infrastructure defects (the taxonomy id counter — 44 failures, one line)
  3. local-file CLI tests -> pin the backend, do not skip (34 here)
  4. genuine service gaps -> bead, do not accommodate (22r1f, set_scope_tags)

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CATALOG CLUSTER — IN PROGRESS 2026-07-25. Commit 63619899. 232 engine failures -> 108. Also merged develop in (8d4cd5c7) after fixing develop's red CI, see below.

DONE (10 files, 166 tests, 118 previously failing): every one died on "attempt to write a readonly database". That is the RDR-176 P1 Gap 2 invariant working as designed — Catalog forces read_only=True whenever storage_backend_for("catalog") is SERVICE and the file exists, because there the local .catalog.db is a FROZEN MIGRATION SOURCE. The tests call Catalog.init then register, so they want a writable LOCAL catalog on purpose.

Disposition is the plan-repair one, for the same documented reason: `nx catalog synthesize-log` and the doctor replay/consistency verbs are local-only BY DESIGN and say so in their own error text ("operate on the LOCAL catalog (event log / JSONL / projection); in service mode the live catalog is owned by the nexus service" — nexus-kmo9h). New conftest fixture `local_catalog_backend`, applied per file via an explicit pytestmark so every pinned file is greppable and carries its own reason. Files: synthesize_log, incremental_rebuild, decomposition_contracts, backup_and_safety, consistency_marker, prune_stale, doctor_replay_equality, bootstrap_guardrail, remediate_paths, backfill.

REMAINING 108, and they are NOT more of the same — this is where the genuinely semantic work starts:
  19 test_catalog_e2e            13 knowledge_hook      13 audit_membership
  12 indexer_hook                 9 mcp                  8 catalog/test_catalog_factory
  + a long tail of 1-4 each
Sampled shapes: "assert 0 == 2024", "assert '' == 'Vaswani et al.'", "assert 'rdr__contaminated' in 'Audited 5 collections: 0 contaminated, 5 clean.'" — the bucket-2 opaque-assert profile, all with the same root: the test seeds a LOCAL catalog and the code under test reads the SERVICE catalog, so every count comes back 0 and every field empty. Some of these are more local-seeded tests (pin); the hooks and e2e are catalog BEHAVIOUR that SHOULD run against the service, and pinning those would be real scope reduction. Each needs the judgement call made per file.

test_catalog_factory is the exception and is the canonical case this bead's description already names: `assert make_catalog_reader() is None` when uninitialised. In service mode there is always a _SharedServiceCatalogHandle, so it is unsatisfiable rather than wrong — assert the service behaviour.

--- SEPARATE FINDING, ALREADY FIXED AND PUSHED (f677728f, direct to develop) ---

DEVELOP'S CI WAS RED and had been since cad6408a. The nexus-9n485 tombstone probe named a voyage token inside a conformant RDR-103 collection name, tripping the RDR-109 mode lint. Excluded as "string-literal-as-name" (both tests patch HttpVectorClient's network boundary; cloud_mode would add a live-credential dependency without changing an assertion), ratchet bumped 56 -> 58.

WORTH NOTING AS A PATTERN, NOT A ONE-OFF: the ceiling comment already records the RDR-185 P4 pair failing the identical way — "the arc ran narrow, path-scoped selections, and this lint only fires when the whole session is collected". That is now twice. This lint cannot be caught by any scoped run, only by a full-session collection, which is exactly what a focused arc never does. It is a candidate for a cheap pre-push check that collects the whole session without running it.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CATALOG CLUSTER 2026-07-25, second pass. Commit 1fb7905a. 108 -> 93 engine failures; 1693 green under the sqlite pin across all 82 catalog files.

A THIRD TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECT, same class as the import-seed-id one, and it will have been poisoning far more than the catalog cluster:

  nexus.catalog.factory memoises ONE HttpCatalogClient for the life of the PROCESS (nexus-5en9j). Correct in production — the tenant never changes mid-process. Wrong for a pytest session, where the engine substrate mints a FRESH TENANT AND TOKEN PER TEST. The memoised client keeps the FIRST test's token, so every later test's catalog reads and writes land in tenant #1.

  The symptom is accumulation, not "wrong tenant": rows pile up in tenant #1 across a module until some register_owner that is the first of its name IN ITS OWN TEST hits a row an earlier test wrote, and the engine correctly refuses with HTTP 409 on catalog_owners_unique_name_type. Order-dependent, passes in isolation, error names a constraint rather than the cause.

  reset_shared_service_catalog_client_for_tests() ALREADY EXISTED for exactly this and nothing outside the one test that owns the caching behaviour ever called it. Now an autouse conftest fixture, reset on both sides.

  GENERALISE THIS: any process-lifetime memoised client is a per-test-tenant hazard under this substrate. Worth grepping for the other singletons (mcp_infra._service_t2_write_locked is named in the same bead as the same design) before trusting any remaining failure count.

THE BETTER DISPOSITION FOR SERVICE-AWARE VERBS — seed through the ACTIVE catalog, do not pin. Proven on test_catalog_audit_membership.py (13 -> 0):

  env fixture returns make_catalog_writer()   -> CatalogWriter on sqlite, _ServiceCatalogWriter on the engine
  read-backs go through _get_catalog().list_by_collection(...)  -> same signature and shape on Catalog and HttpCatalogClient

Verified the contract on both arms BEFORE converting: register_owner/register are on the CATALOG_WRITE_OPS whitelist and return identical Tumblers. The same test body now exercises the audit against whichever catalog is real, which is strictly MORE than it covered before — audit-membership is service-aware and its service path had no coverage at all. Use this for the hooks and e2e; keep the pin only for verbs that are local-only by design.

BUCKET 4, TWO MORE — both filed, both blocking this bead:

  nexus-23wlw (P1, NEW): the service TOMBSTONES a deleted document and NINE CatalogRepository list reads have no deleted_at IS NULL filter (listDocuments, documentsByCollection/ByFilePath/BySourceUri/ByOwner/ByOwnerAndFilePath/ByContentType/ByCorpus, descendants). The point lookups all filter correctly, and catalog-004-manifest-functions.xml filters and calls itself "TOMBSTONE-AWARE" — the list reads were just missed. User-visible: `nx catalog list` and every by_* listing show deleted documents, and a purge reports success while the listing is unchanged. Cannot exist on SQLite, which hard-deletes.

  nexus-jq53b (existing, SHARPENED): that bead frames the missing ON CONFLICT arbiter as an intermittent concurrency race. It is also reachable single-threaded and deterministically — two sequential register_owner calls with the same args 409. And the substrates DISAGREE about whether that is legal: SQLite silently creates a SECOND owner with the same (name, owner_type) under a new prefix, PG forbids it by constraint. That is direct evidence for the design question the bead says to settle first, and one of the two substrates is currently wrong about owner identity, silently. Worth deciding before the SQLite side is deleted and the evidence goes with it.

REMAINING 93: e2e 19, knowledge_hook 13, indexer_hook 10, mcp 9, catalog/test_catalog_factory 8, papers_curator_isolation 4, mcp_bootstrap_fallback 4, graph_heuristic_filter 4, then a tail of 1-3. The hooks and e2e take the seed-through-the-active-catalog treatment. test_catalog_factory is the local-factory file and takes the pin — its service twin (test_catalog_factory_service_mode_cache.py) already owns the "always returns a handle" behaviour that makes `assert make_catalog_reader() is None` unsatisfiable in service mode.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CATALOG CLUSTER third pass, 2026-07-25. Commits 88551598 + 2dd0d622. 72 -> 50 engine failures (27 failed + 23 errors). Files closed this pass: indexer_hook 10->0, pdf_hook 3->0, mcp 9->0, all verified on BOTH arms.

TWO TRAPS IN ActiveCatalog, both hit and both now documented in the commits:

1. DO NOT HAND THE FACADE TO A TEST THAT PATCHES THE FACTORIES. ActiveCatalog resolves every read through make_catalog_reader, so a spy installed AS make_catalog_reader that wraps the facade builds a cycle — the spy's target resolves back through the spy. Surfaces as RecursionError at commands/catalog.py:165, naming nothing useful. Wrap the live reader captured BEFORE the patch.

2. VERIFY BOTH ARMS PER FILE, NOT AT THE END. ActiveCatalog resolves via catalog_path(); the old direct-Catalog tests never had to agree with it. On knowledge_hook the ENGINE arm went green while the SQLITE arm broke — because the service catalog ignores the path entirely. That asymmetry means a one-substrate green is not evidence for this idiom at all. Every converted file now gets _point_catalog_path.

A FALSE ALARM WORTH RECORDING, because it looks exactly like a lost write: the batched-lookup tests asserted writers[0].calls["update"] == 1 and got 0 on the engine. Not a defect — update_many is service-mode-only BY DESIGN (nexus-xedhp puts it in _SERVICE_ONLY_WRITE_OPS precisely so the indexer's callable(getattr(writer, "update_many", None)) capability check can tell the two writers apart). A probe confirmed exactly one batched update and the head_hash landing correctly. The assertion pinned the substrate, not the contract. "0 == 1 on a write count" is the shape most likely to be mis-filed as a data-loss bug in this port; check for a capability-selected batch twin before filing.

BUCKET 4, one more, and it is the worst-shaped one yet:

  nexus-wnlit (P1, NEW) — HttpCatalogClient.link_audit is `return {}  # not supported in initial service-mode implementation`, and the MCP tool catalog_link_audit returns that verbatim. The docstring promises total / by_type / by_creator / orphaned / duplicates / stale_spans / stale_chash. So an agent or human asking "audit the link graph for health issues" gets {} and reads a CLEAN graph. Success-shaped emptiness — every failure mode the audit exists to surface is silently reported as absent. This is the SECOND silent-degradation bug on this exact method: nexus-at2ff (._client instead of the handle, AttributeError swallowed into an error dict) is recorded three lines above the call site. That one at least produced an error key.
  NOT ESTABLISHED and worth checking: whether doctor, a scheduled sweep, or an agent skill calls it and treats {} as healthy. nexus-1e2eh found 277 live dangling catalog_links rows, so the graph is not hypothetically dirty.

It was live.   Already diagnosed once, per-file: tests/test_rdr_084_plan_grow.py carried a local autouse reset_singletons() fixture whose docstring names the exact mechanism. IDENTICAL shape to the catalog client before 1fb7905a — an existing reset helper that only the one file affected ever called.

Scope deliberately narrower than reset_singletons(): only the credential-bearing T2 handle, because evicting _t1_instance/_t3_instance/_collections_cache autouse would invalidate module-scoped T1/T3 injections tests legitimately expect to survive a file.

Full-suite effect measuring now.

title: engine: owner-ensure ON CONFLICT arbiter misses catalog_owners_unique_name_type — concurrent register raises 23505
description:
Observed as a CI flake on PR #1423 (run 30159605428, job 89682661682): Catalog016SourceUriUniqueTest.concurrentBatchesConvergeWithNoDanglingTumblers errored with

  IntegrityConstraintViolationException: insert into nexus.catalog_owners (...) on conflict (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix) do nothing
  ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "catalog_owners_unique_name_type"

MECHANISM. catalog_owners carries TWO unique constraints: the (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix) key and catalog_owners_unique_name_type UNIQUE (tenant_id, name, owner_type) (catalog-001-baseline.xml:47). EVERY owner-ensure/import site targets only the first as the ON CONFLICT arbiter:

  CatalogRepository.java:263, :435, :595, :2869, :2895

Under concurrency the arbiter check can pass (the racer has not yet made its arbiter index entry visible) while the second unique index already conflicts, so the statement raises 23505 instead of taking the DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE path. A single-arbiter ON CONFLICT is only race-safe when the table has exactly one unique constraint.

BLAST RADIUS. This is not test-only. Any two concurrent registerDocument / registerDocumentMany calls for the same owner can surface a 500 to the client. The batch import paths (importOwnersBatch, doImportOwner) have the same shape.

REPRO. Intermittent. The class passes 10/10 locally in isolation; it failed once under the CI runner timing. Not reproduced on develop CI in the last 8 runs.

DESIGN QUESTION to settle before fixing. What does (tenant_id, name, owner_type) colliding under a DIFFERENT tumbler_prefix mean? Options: (a) catch 23505 on that constraint and re-select the existing owner (treats name+type as an alias key), (b) retry the whole ensure once, (c) decide the second constraint is wrong and the identity is really the prefix. (a) and (c) have different semantics for renaming an owner. Needs a call, not a reflex patch.

NOT fixed on the asaod branch: that PR is a scoped TaxonomyHandler 409 change and this is CatalogRepository. Filed separately per the no-scope-creep rule.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SHARPENING FROM nexus-aqbrk (2026-07-25) — the same constraint, but the trigger this bead names is not the only one, and the OTHER one is deterministic.

This bead frames catalog_owners_unique_name_type as a CONCURRENCY race ("intermittent", "passes 10/10 locally in isolation"). Porting the catalog tests to the engine substrate produced it single-threaded, on demand, with no concurrency at all:

  writer = make_catalog_writer()
  writer.register_owner("rdr", "rdr-curator")   -> Tumbler(1,1)
  writer.register_owner("rdr", "rdr-curator")   -> HTTP 409 integrity constraint violation

Sequential, same process, same args. The second call allocates a NEW tumbler_prefix, so the ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, tumbler_prefix) arbiter does not match, and catalog_owners_unique_name_type then fires. So the missing-arbiter defect is reachable by plain repeat registration, not only by a race — which makes it far easier to reproduce while you settle the design question.

AND THE TWO SUBSTRATES DISAGREE ABOUT WHETHER THIS IS LEGAL AT ALL, which is direct evidence for that design question. Same two calls on SQLite:

  Tumbler(1,1)  then  Tumbler(1,2)

SQLite silently creates a SECOND owner with the same (name, owner_type) under a different prefix. PG forbids it by constraint. So option (c) ("the second constraint is wrong and identity is really the prefix") is the one that matches today's SQLite behaviour, and option (a) ("treat name+type as an alias key, re-select the existing owner") is the one that matches the PG schema — and whichever is chosen, one of the two substrates is currently wrong about owner identity, silently. Worth deciding before the SQLite side is deleted and the evidence goes with it.

NOTE: my own test-side 409s in the audit-membership port turned out to be a DIFFERENT root (a process-lifetime shared catalog client leaking tenant #1's token across tests, fixed in conftest). The two-call repro above is the residue that survives that fix and is genuinely this bead.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CROSS-REF from nexus-aqbrk (2026-07-26): the CLIENT-SIDE equivalent of this race is now PINNED to SQLite, so nothing exercises the service-mode owner race.

tests/test_rdr137_followup_critical_345.py::TestCriticalFiveTOCTOUOwnerRace covers the RDR-137 CRITICAL-5 TOCTOU (ensure_owner_for_repo is check-then-act; two concurrent calls both pass the lookup and both INSERT). Under the engine substrate its writes died on 'attempt to write a readonly database' — the RDR-176 frozen-migration-source invariant working as designed against a test that wants the local catalog on purpose — so it is pinned with local_catalog_backend.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING WHILE FIXING THIS BEAD: the concurrency property is now asserted ONLY on the SQLite path. The engine path has no test and a live defect (this bead). Whoever fixes the ON CONFLICT arbiter should add the service-mode concurrency assertion at the same time, or the fix ships unverified on the substrate that will be the only one left after nexus-i711w deletes the SQLite stores this test rides on.

Not filing a separate bead for the missing test — it belongs to this fix, not beside it.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DECISION 2026-07-28 (Hal): OPTION (a) — (tenant_id, name, owner_type) IS an
identity key, and register_owner is idempotent by it. Same name+type returns
the SAME owner, every time.

WHY (a) AND NOT THE OTHER TWO, grounded in the call sites rather than taste:
every caller already uses register_owner as ENSURE semantics —
doc_indexer.py:227 and :1715, pipeline_stages.py:563, indexer.py:970,
catalog/store_hook.py:185 all call it on each index/store operation with the
same (owner_name, "curator") and expect the owner back. Not one wants a new
distinct owner. The PG constraint catalog_owners_unique_name_type already
asserts the same thing. So the defect is that the CODE disagrees with its own
SCHEMA: it allocates a fresh tumbler_prefix first, so ON CONFLICT
(tenant_id, tumbler_prefix) misses the existing row and the name+type
constraint then fires as a raw 23505.

  (b) retry is INSUFFICIENT — and this is what the bead's original framing got
      wrong. It was filed as a concurrency race, but the aqbrk evidence
      reproduces it SEQUENTIALLY, single-threaded. A retry fails identically
      because the conflicting row genuinely exists.
  (c) drop the constraint restores the SQLite behaviour where two owners share
      name+type; every call site above then gets a nondeterministic answer to
      "which owner is rdr/curator?" That is the shape that produced 83 orphan
      owners in the related empty-repo_hash case.

TWO CONSTRAINTS ON THE FIX, both load-bearing:

1. DO NOT ROUTE RENAME THROUGH THE ENSURE PATH. This is the hazard the bead's
   own design note names: renaming owner X onto Y's name would 23505, and a
   naive (a) would silently re-select Y and misroute writes. Rename needs its
   own explicit collision error, not ensure semantics.

2. LOOK UP BEFORE ALLOCATING, not after. The current code computes the next
   prefix (MAX(split_part(tumbler_prefix,'.',2))+1) BEFORE the insert. If the
   fix is allocate -> conflict -> re-select, every duplicate register_owner
   burns a next_seq value and discards it, feeding the wedge class in
   nexus-0ehwe / nexus-pbawi. The (tenant, name, owner_type) SELECT must come
   first, and allocation must happen only on a genuine miss.

SITES: CatalogRepository.java owner-ensure inserts at ~256, ~429, ~589, ~2961
(all four use the tumbler_prefix arbiter today).

SEQUENCING: this is ENGINE work, so it needs an engine tag + conexus deploy
before the behaviour reaches anyone — the same two-lifecycle path nexus-onjvy
just went through. It can ride the SAME tag as the i711w Stage 2 Q5/Q10 engine
equivalents rather than burning its own cut.

NOT STARTED YET, deliberately: i711w Stage 2 sub-stage B is uncommitted with a
full suite in flight. Opening a second large workstream on top of an
unfinished one is how both end up half-done.

title: [bug] engine: POST /v1/taxonomy/import/topic returns HTTP 500 on a WIRED route — live bug, not a missing endpoint
description:
ROOT CAUSE (found 2026-07-25) — NOT a broken route, and NOT the multitenancy gap first suspected.

POST /v1/taxonomy/import/topic returned 500 whenever a SECOND tenant supplied a preserved id that
another tenant already held. Reproduced against a live engine substrate; the Java stack from the
service log:

  Caused by: PSQLException: ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy
             (USING expression) for table "topics"      -> SQLSTATE 42501

The /import/* verbs preserve CLIENT-SUPPLIED ids verbatim (fidelity ETL round-trip) and
nexus.topics has a global BIGSERIAL PK. Global is DELIBERATE: topics_parent_fk is
self-referential, so a composite (tenant_id, id) key would force every parent_id to carry a tenant
too. Two tenants claiming one id -> the second INSERT is refused by the RLS POLICY, not the PK,
because RLS evaluates first: the row exists but is invisible to this tenant.

42501 is insufficient_privilege, NOT class 23 — so HttpUtil.sqlState23 correctly declined it and it
fell to catch (Exception) -> bare 500. The shared typed-DB-error ladder was already wired into
TaxonomyHandler; its mesh simply had the wrong shape for this signal.

CORRECTION OF RECORD: this bead originally speculated a PK collision and, from there, a missed
multitenancy story. BOTH WERE WRONG. This is tenant isolation WORKING — topics carries tenant_id,
every index is tenant-scoped, RLS enforces it. There is NO isolation question to file; the
follow-up bead that was going to be raised for it does not exist.

FIX (PR #1423, commit 5261515f): HttpUtil.isRlsRowRejection requires 42501 AND the PG
'row-level security policy' message; TaxonomyHandler returns 409 on /import/* when it fires.
  - not a bare 42501->409: that SQLSTATE also means a genuine privilege/grant fault, which must
    keep surfacing as 500 rather than being mislabelled as the caller's conflict;
  - scoped to /import/* where a client-supplied id is the known cause;
  - body is 'supplied id is not available in this tenant' and nothing more — naming the other
    tenant would be cross-tenant information disclosure.

TESTS: TaxonomyHandlerImportRlsTest (5), hermetic Testcontainers PG + real Liquibase schema +
NON-BYPASSRLS role so RLS can actually refuse. Load-bearing case: a plain 'permission denied' with
the SAME 42501 returns FALSE, so the fix cannot later be widened to any 42501 without something
noticing. Mutation-verified: disabling the wiring fails exactly the two 409 tests. Full Java suite
1447/0.

KNOWN FRAGILITY: the detector couples to a PG message string. A future PG reword makes it return
false and behaviour degrades to the old 500 — wrong status, never a wrong success. The test pins the
live wording.

SIDE FINDING: tests/conftest.py claims imports 'preserve ids VERBATIM without advancing the
engine's serial sequences'. The second clause is FALSE — importTopic calls setval() to keep the
sequence ahead, which is why the Java test needs GRANT UPDATE ON SEQUENCE topics_id_seq (production
grants it in taxonomy-005-topics-seq-update-grant.xml; checked, production is not missing it).
Correct that comment on the substrate-port branch.

DEPLOY: engine-side. Needs an engine-service tag + conexus deploy before it is live — NOT shipped by
the merge.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:

Deploy verified independently via `nx service probe` (release_version 0.1.56), not on the relay word. record-deploy written [21141]. Client identity bumped to (0,1,56) in bfd3c25d so local-mode installs receive it too.

RESIDUAL, filed as knowledge not a blocker: the 409 payload is well covered at the Java level — TaxonomyHandlerImportRlsTest, 6 tests against real PG with RLS: first-tenant-claims-id succeeds; second tenant on the same id gets 409 not 500; the body does NOT leak that the id exists under another tenant; a DIFFERENT id in the second tenant still succeeds (fires only on the contested id); and the detector requires BOTH the 42501 sqlstate AND the RLS message so a genuine grant/role fault still 500s. What is NOT covered is the path through the cloud EDGE. conexus flagged this themselves and offered to exercise it on throwaway tenants — worth taking, given nexus-bwulw (the edge stubbed /version and auth-gated /health, and three client features shipped green through every engine-direct gate).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
STACKED REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-07-25, run after the fact — this shipped before the gate, which is how H1 below reached production).

H1 FIXED — the guard was half-applied. `op.startsWith("/import/")` does NOT match "/import_batch" (no slash after "import"), so POST /v1/taxonomy/import_batch with kind=topic still returned the opaque 500 this bead was cut to remove. importTopicsBatch does the identical insertInto(TOPICS, TOPICS.ID, ...).onConflict(TOPICS.ID) against the same global BIGSERIAL PK — verified independently in TaxonomyRepository before acting. It is also the HEAVIER real path (the 190k-row dogfood bulk leg), so the fix landed on the less-used route. Extracted isImportOp(); added importBatch_secondTenantClaimingSameId_returns409_not500, mutation-verified (it fails against the original guard).

M1 ACCEPTED RISK, recorded in code — the 409-vs-200 status is itself a cross-tenant id-EXISTENCE oracle (global BIGSERIAL PK; RLS scopes rows, not the id space). Body and logs leak nothing further and there is a test pinning that. Accepted because the route is authenticated, ETL-shaped, and ids are each tenant own rowids. Enumeration surface NOT closed (no rate limiting on the route) — filed as nexus-4fpbl (P3). The source-level fix (composite (tenant_id, id) key) stays rejected: topics_parent_fk is self-referential.

L1 RECORDED — the message match assumes English lc_messages. A non-English PG locale silently degrades every RLS refusal back to 500. Noted at isRlsRowRejection.

M2 NOT DONE, stated rather than quietly dropped — there is still no INTEGRATION-level test that a genuine grant fault (e.g. REVOKE on the sequence) survives the full handler stack as a 500. Only the classifier unit test covers that direction. Matches the pre-existing TaxonomyHandlerAssignFkTest convention, so it is a known gap in the suite convention rather than a regression in this change.

OWED: H1 is a Java change and is NOT live until a new engine-service tag is cut and deployed. v0.1.56 carries the HALF-APPLIED fix.

title: [bug] service backend: promote_extras_field + list_promotions unimplemented on HttpDocumentAspectsStore — blocks the T2 substrate port
description:
Surfaced by the RDR-155 P4b P0a' substrate-pin flip measurement (2026-07-25). NOT test debt —
no test edit can fix it.

FAILURE: NotImplementedError: promote_extras_field not yet supported on the service backend
(document_aspects=service). 7 failures in the flipped full-suite run.

CONFIRMED IN SOURCE: src/nexus/db/t2/http_document_aspects_store.py:118 documents the gap in its
own docstring — promote_extras_field and list_promotions are absent from the service store while
the SQLite DocumentAspects store implements them.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TESTS: the flip makes the engine substrate the unit suite's default, so this
becomes a hard blocker for nexus-i711w (the eight-store SQLite deletion). More importantly, once
SQLite is deleted there is no fallback implementation — any production caller of
promote_extras_field would hit the same NotImplementedError. Needs the capability built
service-side (client + engine as required), not a skip.

DISCOVERY CONTEXT: full analysis of the flip on nexus-g37fr. The port's failure buckets were
164 raw-.conn test sites / ~168 opaque / ~46 service-refusal-semantics / ~14 genuine service gaps
(this bead + the taxonomy 500) / ~8 credential.
