comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RESOLVED by RETIREMENT, not by implementation (Hal decision 2026-07-25).

WHAT THE BEAD GOT RIGHT: promote_extras_field / list_promotions had no service implementation, and once SQLite is deleted a production caller would hit NotImplementedError. Real, not test debt.

WHAT THE INVESTIGATION FOUND, which changes the fix:

1. The engine ALREADY had the audit-log half. nexus.aspect_promotion_log exists (aspects-001-baseline.xml), with AspectRepository.recordPromotion / listPromotions / importPromotionRow / importPromotionBatch wired to POST /v1/aspects/promotion/record, GET /promotion/list, POST /promotion/import. list_promotions was therefore pure CLIENT wiring: no engine change, NO engine tag needed.

2. promote_extras_field could not be ported at all. Its step 1 is a RUNTIME ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN. Under the ALL-DDL-through-Liquibase directive there is no substrate where that is legal — implementing it service-side would have required an exemption. Its whole premise (operator-driven schema evolution without a migration) is a SQLite-era affordance PG does not grant.

HAL RULING: retire the runtime verb. Promoting extras.<name> is now ONE Liquibase changeset doing all three phases together (ADD COLUMN + backfill from extras + INSERT into aspect_promotion_log so --history still reports it). The optional extras prune stays a SEPARATE later changeset, preserving the dual-read cutover the original mechanic supported. Rejected alternatives: a backfill-only service endpoint (adds an endpoint + engine tag for work the changeset already does inline), and runtime ALTER TABLE behind a guard (directive violation).

SHIPPED:
- src/nexus/aspect_promotion.py — promote_extras_field, PromotionResult, the reserved/identifier validators, the lazy audit-table bootstrap and the audit writer all DELETED. Module keeps the changeset template plus PROMOTION_RETIRED and list_promotions.
- src/nexus/db/t2/document_aspects.py — list_promotions() reads the local log; returns [] when absent and does NOT create it.
- src/nexus/db/t2/http_document_aspects_store.py — list_promotions() over GET /v1/aspects/promotion/list.
- src/nexus/commands/enrich.py — command keeps its name so the old muscle memory lands on the recipe; --type/--prune removed rather than left as no-op flags; FIELD_NAME now optional so --history needs no dummy arg (the legacy --history <dummy> form still works).
- docs/cli-reference.md, RDR-089 phase table, CHANGELOG.

CENSUS/RATCHET MOVES, all DOWNWARD:
- DDL_CENSUS aspect_promotion.py 1 -> 0 (entry removed; migrations.migrate_aspect_promotion_log_table is now the sole creator).
- ALTER_CENSUS aspect_promotion.py 5 -> 2 (both survivors are the PG changeset RECIPE text, zero executed).
- EPSILON_CENSUS aspect_promotion.py 6 -> 0 (entry removed); enrich.py 9 -> 8.
- storage_boundary_lint t2database_constructions 35 -> 34 (the promotion write-open is gone; only the read-only --history open survives).

title: nx_answer success_count records success on zero-evidence runs — the plan-promotion signal cannot distinguish 'answered' from 'did not raise'
description:
OBSERVED, live probe 2026-07-25. nx_answer(question='Which indexed papers discuss intermediate representations for compiling natural-language queries?', dimensions={verb:research}, scope='knowledge__semantic-operators') matched builtin plan 14 (type-scoped-search), ran it, and returned:

  'No matching evidence found ... The plan's retrieval steps returned zero results'

Plan 14's counters after: use_count 1->2, success 1->2, failure 0->0. A run that produced no evidence was recorded as a SUCCESS.

MECHANISM (verified in source)
- src/nexus/mcp/core.py:5659 — _nx_answer_record_outcome(best.plan_id, success=True) is the fall-through after plan execution. success=False is only reached at :5654 (and :5598), i.e. ONLY when execution raised.
- src/nexus/mcp/core.py:5579 — the single-step query() reroute path likewise records success=True unconditionally, on a branch where result_text can literally be the string 'No results.' (:5563).
- So success/failure is an exception counter, not an outcome counter. 'The DAG did not throw' is recorded as 'the plan answered the question'.

WHY IT MATTERS
1. Plan-library curation: the matcher is supposed to be able to decay always-failing plans (RDR-179 item 3, 'the matcher never decays always-failing plans'). It cannot, because a plan that reliably retrieves nothing accrues a perfect success record. A plan can be 100%-success and 0%-useful.
2. RDR-189 D2 (draft): that RDR's promotion-signal question asked what could justify automatic promotion of an artifact whose defects are silent, and R8 recommended option (b) partly because 'it ran' is a weak signal. This probe shows it is weaker than assumed — it is not merely weak, it is non-discriminating on the zero-evidence case. Any auto-promotion keyed on success_count would preferentially promote plans that return nothing quickly.
3. Operator trust: nx plan list / show present success/failure as if they were quality signals.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not a design decision — for triage)
Record success=False, or a third outcome, when a plan completes but yields no evidence / an empty final. The zero-result condition is already detected for the user-facing message, so the signal exists at the point of decision and is simply not written through.

RELATED
- RDR-189 (draft) D2 / R8 — this is direct evidence for that decision.
- RDR-179 (draft) item 3 'Curation loop absent'.
- nexus-sbl4m — grown-plan TTL, same area, different defect.

NOTE ON A NEARBY NON-FINDING: plan 14 declares required_bindings [question, content_type] and the probe supplied no content_type, yet the plan still matched and ran. core.py:5635 does iterate best.required_bindings, so binding resolution is handled rather than skipped; whether the empty content_type contributed to the zero-result retrieval was NOT established and should not be assumed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plan-library reuse cannot compound: auto-grown plans TTL-expire at 30 days before they accumulate any reuse
description:
RDR-084 shipped auto-save of successful ad-hoc plans so 'the library compounds, and the plan-match hit rate should climb without any human curation step'. It cannot compound, by construction.

MECHANISM
- Auto-saved plans are written with scope=personal and a config-driven TTL: plans.ad_hoc_ttl, default 30 days (src/nexus/config.py:677, read by _load_ad_hoc_ttl at src/nexus/mcp/core.py:5270, applied at core.py:5761-5797).
- Every library read path filters to non-expired rows (src/nexus/db/t2/http_plan_library.py:354 list_active_plans, :400 recent-plans), so an expired grown plan silently leaves the matcher's pool.
- The only escape to a permanent tier is manual promotion via /conexus:plan-promote (personal -> project -> global). Nothing promotes automatically.
- Net cycle: plan-miss -> inline planner -> auto-save -> expire at 30d -> plan-miss again. A grown plan gets at most a 30-day window to be re-matched, and the library can never hold more than a rolling 30 days of personal plans.

EVIDENCE (live managed store, measured 2026-07-25)
- Library holds 17 plans: 15 builtin seeds + exactly 2 auto-grown (ids 353 created 2026-07-12, 354 created 2026-07-14 - both inside the 30d window; nothing older survives).
- Every last_used timestamp in the library predates the 2026-07-02 managed-cloud cutover: 2026-05-27, 2026-04-24, 2026-04-24. The other 14 plans are unused. No library plan has run in the ~3 weeks since cutover.
- Counters are inherited, not earned: src/nexus/db/t2/plan_etl.py:41-45 copies use_count / last_used / match_count / match_conf_sum verbatim through migration, so plan 14's match_count=136 / use_count=1 is pre-migration history.
- Both grown plans show match_count=0 - grown post-cutover, never offered since.
- nx plan hygiene reports the library clean, so this is not the RDR-179 pollution class.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND REUSE
Blocks RDR-189 D2(b). That RDR's recommended promotion model is 'auto-propose answer-object families from observed shapes, human-promote'. Observation cannot accumulate if the observations expire monthly - today the entire observable grown population is n=2. RDR-189 already carries depends_on: [RDR-179]; this is the concrete mechanism behind that dependency.

RELATED
- RDR-084 (closed) - shipped the auto-save whose stated goal this defeats.
- RDR-179 (draft) item 3 'Curation loop absent' - same area, different angle (that RDR's R28/R29 pollution findings are now partly stale: nx plan list/hygiene route live via _open_plan_library at src/nexus/commands/plan.py:434, and hygiene is clean).
- RDR-189 (draft) D2 / R8.

NOT YET ISOLATED
Whether TTL expiry is the sole cause of the post-cutover zero-reuse, or whether scope filtering (matcher.py:388-392 _scope_fit drops scope conflicts before scoring) and/or the 0.40 confidence gate also contribute. match_conf_sum is in the schema but nx plan show does not print it, so average match confidence could not be computed.
notes:

RESULT: plan 14 (type-scoped-search) went match_count 136->137, use_count 1->2, success 1->2, last_used -> 2026-07-25T04:34:51Z.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS STILL ABOUT (unchanged, still real): auto-grown plans carry a 30-day TTL and every read path filters non-expired, so the GROWN tier cannot accumulate across months without manual promotion. That mechanism claim is verified from source and stands.

The correct explanation for the April/May last_used timestamps is simply that nobody was driving nx_answer with library-matching questions in that window — not that the machinery had failed. Do NOT cite this bead as evidence the reuse loop is broken.

comments.text:
FIXED 4cfcfa3e — ENGINE-SIDE, so NOT LIVE until a tag is cut and deployed.

ROOT CAUSE was one clause, in three read paths: `extract(epoch from now() - created_at) / 86400 <= TTL`. Expiry measured AGE, not disuse, so a plan matched every single day still died at 30 days. RDR-084 promise ("the library compounds... without any human curation step") could not be true under an age anchor.

On the live library this is likely nothing (the bead measured every last_used as predating the 2026-07-02 cutover) but it should not be discovered after the fact.

There was NO engine-side expiry test at all before this. That is how a clause contradicting the RDR-084 goal survived: nothing asserted what expiry was supposed to MEAN. title: [blocker] P3 pyproject drop breaks the migration rehearsal: seed_legacy.py gets chromadb from conexus's OWN lock
description:
Discovered during RDR-155 P4b P3 (chromadb leaves pyproject). NOT in the plan's
docs/CI disposition list.

COUPLING: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/seed_legacy.py constructs a real Chroma store to
seed a legacy footprint. It does not install chromadb itself — run.sh:398 generates the
container's requirements.txt with 'uv export --locked' from the PROJECT lock, and
Dockerfile:38 states the intent: 'The conexus venv bin gives both nx and a python with the
SAME chromadb the tool uses (so seed_legacy.py writes a byte-compatible legacy store).'

So the moment chromadb leaves pyproject.toml + uv.lock, the rehearsal image loses it and
seed_legacy.py dies on ImportError. Consumers: run.sh legs at 415/447/454/464/476
(era-hop, cold, hole-punch, acquire, fullstack, guided, shakeout) + Dockerfile.era-hop:55.

This is a RELEASE GATE, so it cannot be left broken.

OPTIONS (ranked):
1. Sequence nexus-8nlj4 BEFORE the pyproject drop. Cleanest: the legs needing a real
   Chroma store are exactly the guided-migration ones 8nlj4 retires, and its replacement
   (two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal) does not need chromadb at all — the stranded
   detector keys on FILENAMES ('chroma.sqlite3' etc.) and stranded_install.py is
   AST-enforced dep-free, so the new seeder can fake a footprint with plain files.
   Cost: P3 cannot finish until 8nlj4 does — a real change to plan v4's phase ordering.
2. Bridge: pin chromadb explicitly in the rehearsal image requirements, decoupled from the
   project lock. Two lines, keeps every leg working, leaves retirement to 8nlj4.
   Cost: spends work on a harness that is being deleted.
3. Drop and accept a broken rehearsal until 8nlj4 lands. NOT recommended — it is a
   release gate.

RECOMMENDATION: option 1, since 8nlj4 must happen for 7.0.0 regardless. Hal's call because
it re-orders the phase plan.

STATE AT DISCOVERY: P3 otherwise nearly done — src/ at 2 chromadb imports (both the
auto-collapsing errors.py shims), test files 62 -> 6. Branch
feature/g37fr-p4b-chroma-deletion, commits 27c0c9d0/c81ae991/693a9b33/faa8437c/490515e5.
close_reason:
NON-ISSUE — original diagnosis was wrong. Closed with no code change; P3 is not blocked.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I conflated two different rehearsal images. tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/Dockerfile (guided/shakeout) DOES install from the 'uv export --locked' requirements, so I generalised that to the seeder's consumers. Dockerfile.era-hop — the only image whose leg actually invokes seed_legacy.py at runtime — does NOT.

EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION (built the era-hop image, 574MB, and inspected it):
  - python -c 'import chromadb' -> ModuleNotFoundError in BOTH the venv python and system python. chromadb is not in the image at all.
  - /home/nexus/nxenv site-packages: 3 entries (bare venv scaffolding, no conexus).
  - /tmp/requirements.txt: ABSENT. The era-hop image never consumes the project lock; Dockerfile.era-hop only COPYs the working-tree wheel and runs 'uv venv'.

WHY IT CANNOT BREAK: rehearse_era_hop.sh installs 'conexus==6.0.0' from REAL PyPI (line 81), THEN runs seed_legacy.py under that venv (line 172), and only afterwards --reinstalls the working-tree wheel (line 202). The seeder gets chromadb from the ERA RELEASE's own closure — which is the stated design intent ('writes the legacy Chroma + T2 + catalog through the ERA RELEASE's own libraries', Dockerfile.era-hop). An old conexus predates the drop by construction, so this holds for every future era pin below 7.0.0.

THE OTHER LEGS (reasoned, not empirically run — their real test is P3's battery): seed_legacy.py is COPYed into Dockerfile / Dockerfile.cold / Dockerfile.fullstack, but NO live leg invokes it. rehearse_shakeout.sh, rehearse_fullstack.sh and rehearse_acquire.sh have zero references; rehearse.sh's only call sits behind 'if nx migrate-to-service --help' (rehearse.sh:270), a verb deleted in P4b P2, so it never fires. A staged-but-uninvoked script with an unsatisfiable import is inert.

ALSO CHECKED AND NOT DONE: I proposed removing the 'vestigial' seed_legacy.py staging copies. All three Dockerfiles COPY seed_legacy.py, so dropping it from staging would BREAK those builds. Removing both sides is dead-weight cleanup belonging to nexus-8nlj4's rehearsal reshape, not to P3 — touching a release gate for zero functional gain.

RESIDUAL for nexus-8nlj4: the retired --cold/--hole-punch staging branch (run.sh:454) is unreachable behind the line-176 refusal, and the seed_legacy.py COPY in all three Dockerfiles is dead weight for every live leg. Hal's own 8nlj4 note flags the same class for COLD_TAG.

title: [blocker] Restore a published-artifact acquire gate — the engine binary MUST be exercised before conexus deploys it (Hal directive)
description:
HAL DIRECTIVE (2026-07-24, verbatim intent): "seems like we *must* exercise the binary before conexus... I don't want to test this live on prod". Accepting the gap is OFF THE TABLE — this is the decision that closes the option I had left open on the engine-release skill's step 5.

THE GAP. The skill's step 5 used to be `run.sh --cold`: on a bare box, install-binary the JUST-PUBLISHED tag, init, and drive it. RDR-155 P4b (7e47c285) retired --cold along with --guided/--hole-punch because all three drove the deleted `nx guided-upgrade`. There is now NO leg that acquires and validates an arbitrary just-published engine tag.

WHY THE PRE-TAG SHAKEOUT DOES NOT COVER IT. `--shakeout` exercises the LOCALLY BUILT -Ob candidate. The PUBLISHED artifact is a different set of bytes produced by a different builder: the release workflow's full native build (not -Ob), plus codesign, plus cosign signing, plus the PG bundle packaging. A defect introduced by the workflow — a signing step that breaks JNI dlopen (nexus-2oh5q is exactly this hazard, currently dormant only because the Apple secrets are unprovisioned), a mis-packaged bundle, a stripped resource — is invisible to the local shakeout by construction.

WHAT IT PROTECTED, historically: this gate caught nexus-pi3s3 and nexus-qeoxf on 2026-06-26 — defects in the PUBLISHED artifact that every local suite missed. That is the coverage currently at zero.

WHY --package-upgrade IS NOT THE SUBSTITUTE (checked, do not re-derive): it does acquire an engine for real and never has the harness supply it, which is the right shape. But it converges to NEW_ENGINE_TAG, which run.sh DERIVES from REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION — the compatibility FLOOR, not an arbitrary tag. So it can only validate a tag the PyPI release has already pinned, which is strictly after the moment this gate exists to protect.

OPTIONS (pick one; 3 is now forbidden by the directive above):
1. Teach the acquire path to honour an explicit NEXUS_SERVICE_TAG override so a specific just-published tag can be acquired and driven on a bare box. Smallest change; restores the old coverage directly. Needs a surviving journey to host it — --package-upgrade is the natural host since it already does a real acquire.
2. Build the published-artifact acquire leg into the two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal (nexus-8nlj4), which is already the designated replacement for the retired guided journeys. Larger, but lands the coverage where the acceptance story is being rebuilt anyway.
3. ~~Accept the gap~~ — REFUSED by Hal, 2026-07-24. Recorded so it is not silently re-proposed.

BLOCKING SEMANTICS: until this lands, handing an engine tag to conexus means conexus's cloud gate is the FIRST validation the published bytes receive — i.e. the first exercise happens on production. The engine-release skill's step 5 now says this out loud, and whoever hands over a tag must repeat it. For engine-service-v0.1.55 specifically, decide explicitly whether to build this first or to hand over with the gap stated; do not let it pass unremarked.

RELATED: nexus-8nlj4 (replacement acceptance rehearsal), nexus-1e2eh (the stale-release-procedure class this is an instance of), nexus-2oh5q (the dormant signing hazard this gate would catch when the Apple secrets land).
close_reason: Acquire gate built, validated against known-good v0.1.54, and used in production to gate engine-service-v0.1.55 (11 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0). Linux-platform scope limit and the mac post-sign verification gap are recorded on nexus-2oh5q.

comments.text:
GATE IS REAL NOW — first production use, 2026-07-24/25.

Validated in the order that matters:
1. Against the already-published, known-good engine-service-v0.1.54 FIRST. That
   run FAILED with "the published binary cannot embed/write" — and the binary was

   probe 1784935097 ...". Fixed in 3499bf3a (pipe via stdin + explicit --title).
   Pointing a new gate at a known-good artifact before a fresh one is what kept

2. Re-run vs v0.1.54: ACQUIRE GATE PASSED, 11 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0.

this gate does NOT cover. A mac leg would have to run on the host, not in

guard on the next line is unreachable. Both call sites now replay the build

title: Release-only procedures rot silently: mechanize a sweep so a deleted verb/contract cannot leave a gate naming it (3 incidents in one day)
description:
THE CLASS, named after it cost three runs in a single day (2026-07-24). A step that executes ONLY during a release — a script, a skill step, a workflow leg — silently rots when the thing underneath it is deleted or changed, because nothing exercises it between releases. It then fires at cut time, which is the worst possible moment to discover it.

THE THREE INCIDENTS, same shape each time:
1. service/native-smoke.sh burned engine-service-v0.1.53. nexus-piwya.11 flipped /v1/chash writes to 410 Gone; the smoke's real-Python-client leg still expected the pre-410 accept-and-no-op window. The script runs ONLY in the engine release workflow — not mvnw test, not PR CI, not the shakeout — so nothing caught it until the tag was already burned. Its own comment had PREDICTED the break.
2. tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh colour leak. `uv export > requirements.txt` emits ANSI escapes when FORCE_COLOR is set (an agent shell sets it), corrupting a file a container later parses. Passes for a human, fails for an agent — i.e. fails exactly when nobody is watching a terminal.
3. .claude/skills/engine-release step 3 AND step 5. RDR-155 P4b (7e47c285) retired --guided/--cold/--hole-punch; the skill still named --guided as "the only leg that builds the candidate" and --cold as the post-publish gate. Step 3 had a clean substitute (--shakeout). Step 5 did NOT, and that gap is now nexus-<published-artifact-gate>.

WHY THE OBVIOUS ANSWER IS INSUFFICIENT: "run the release steps more often" is not affordable — several legs cost 10x-billed macOS runners, multi-minute native builds, or a real cloud deploy. The CI-cost directive forbids exercising them casually. So the mechanism has to be a STATIC sweep, not more execution.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS (design, not decided):
a. Reference lint: extract every command/flag a release-only artifact names (skills/*.md fenced blocks, native-smoke.sh, engine-service-release.yml, run.sh leg dispatch) and assert each still resolves — CLI verb exists, run.sh flag is not in the RETIRED refusal list, workflow step's referenced script exists. Fails CI on a dangling reference. Catches incidents 1 and 3 by construction.
b. Retirement back-reference: when a verb/leg is retired, the retiring commit must update every release-only artifact naming it. Enforceable as a lint keyed on the RETIRED message text already present in run.sh — grep the repo for the retired flag names outside their own refusal branch.
c. Agent-shell parity: run the release-relevant harness steps once in CI under FORCE_COLOR/NO_TTY to catch the incident-2 class (output that is only corrupt for non-human runners). Cheap: it does not need the full leg, just the file-generating prefix.

SCOPE NOTE: (a) and (b) overlap; (b) is narrower and cheaper and would have caught incident 3 alone. (c) is a different failure mode (environmental, not referential) and is the only one of the three that catches incident 2. Pick deliberately rather than building all three.

ANCHOR: the standing directive is feedback_gates_scripted_not_ambient — a gate that only a human can notice is failing is ambient, not scripted.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
INCIDENTS 4 AND 5, same day (2026-07-24), both surfaced by CI on develop after
d4c0bb66 (PR #1421, RDR-155 P4b P1/P2) landed at 16:58. Both workflows were GREEN
at 02:23 and have failed on every push since.

INCIDENT 4 - "Guided-upgrade MVV (weekly + on migration-path changes)".
Step runs: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --guided
run.sh answers: "RETIRED (RDR-155 P4b): --guided/--cold/--hole-punch drive
nx guided-upgrade, deleted in P4b P2" and exits 2. The workflow cannot pass; it
is dead by construction. This is EXACTLY incident 3's shape (the skill naming
--guided) in a second artifact the retiring commit 7e47c285 did not sweep, which
is precisely what candidate mechanism (b) - retirement back-reference lint - would
have caught. Two artifacts missed by one retiring commit is the strongest evidence
yet for (b) over (a).

INCIDENT 5 - "Era-spanning upgrade hop (weekly + on ladder-path changes)".
NOT pure staleness, and worth separating from the other four: the leg runs, gets
through Stage 4, then ABORTS on its own non-vacuity gate:
  FAIL nx upgrade --dry-run does NOT report the substrate rung pending - the
  seeded footprint is invisible to the product (check NX_LOCAL_CHROMA_PATH=
  /home/nexus/legacy-chroma vs the rung's resolver). Every convergence assert
  below would grade a no-op.
  == ABORT (vacuous fixture - refusing to report a pass over work that never
  existed) ==
The harness is behaving CORRECTLY: 88d91bd5 deleted the Chroma client legs, so a
seeded legacy-chroma footprint is no longer visible to the product, and the gate
refuses to grade a no-op rather than reporting a green over nothing. That
non-vacuity assert is the only reason this did not silently become a passing
test of nothing - which is the failure mode this whole bead exists to prevent.

CLASS REFINEMENT. Incidents 1-4 are REFERENTIAL (an artifact names something
deleted). Incident 5 is FIXTURE-VACUITY (the artifact still runs, but the world it
seeds no longer exists). A static reference lint catches 1-4 and CANNOT catch 5.
Only a non-vacuity assert catches 5, and this one existed and worked. Recommend
the mechanism split accordingly: lint for the referential class, and a standing
requirement that every seeded-fixture gate carry a non-vacuity assert for the other.

DISPOSITION NOT TAKEN. Neither workflow was changed here. Both are coverage
decisions inside nexus-8nlj4's remit (the acceptance-harness reshape): incident 4
wants the workflow deleted or repointed at the two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal;
incident 5 wants its fixture re-seeded against a world that still exists. Left red
and documented rather than silently disabled.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED 42ce8872 (first of two commits in that push).

REAL ROT FOUND AND FIXED — the point of the exercise, not the guard: engine-service-release.yml release-notes prose told users to run `nx install-binary`. That verb does NOT exist and never did; the real form is `nx daemon service install-binary`. Anyone copy-pasting the release notes hit "No such command". Verified by running both forms.

THE SWEEP resolves every `nx <verb>` found in skill fenced code blocks, release-only shell scripts, and workflow run: bodies (YAML-parsed, not grepped) against the LIVE Click command tree. Resolving from the real tree is load-bearing — a hand-maintained list of valid verbs would be the same rot one level up.

PRECISION OVER RECALL, deliberately: a guard that cries wolf gets blessed reflexively and stops working. NOT covered: invocations deeper than 2 tokens, line-continuation-split commands, Python docstrings (already covered by tests/upgrade/test_verb_demotion.py). Allowlists require a REASON per entry AND are checked for staleness, so a tombstone that stops being one surfaces instead of lingering.

RETIRED-ON-PURPOSE handled, not papered over: rehearse_guided/_cold/_hole_punch self-guard with `if ! nx guided-upgrade --help; then RETIRED; exit 2; fi`, making later invocations provably unreachable. Whole-file allowlisted as RDR-155 P4b debris that nexus-8nlj4 owns deleting.

Mutation-verified independently of the authoring agent, mutation confirmed to land first: removing main.add_command(init_cmd, name="init") fails the sweep and names every artifact referencing init. Restored, cli.py diff empty. Two permanent monkeypatch mutation tests keep the property regression-tested without mutating files each CI run.

Left test_engine_release_skill_parity.py alone — narrower flag-level parity vs this broader verb-level sweep; merging blurs two failure modes. 17 tests.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
COVERAGE GAP IN THE TRIPWIRE THIS BEAD PRODUCED, found in the release-gate vacuity audit at develop a7553c88 (T2 [22175]).

tests/test_release_artifact_verb_rot.py catches a gate naming a DELETED CLI VERB. It does not catch a gate grepping for a DELETED LOG LITERAL. Two live escapes, both filed:

- nexus-xm0cp (P1): tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:185 and :239 grep for 'dual_write_failed'. Repo-wide those two assertions are the ONLY occurrences of the string — the hook was retired at RDR-187 / nexus-piwya.4 (src/nexus/hook_registry.py:515-516). Two permanent PASS lines per pre-tag engine run. Same file :238 greps the service log for 5xx patterns the service cannot emit (com.sun.net.httpserver with no request logger; logback.xml has one appender, pattern '%d %level [%thread] %logger - %msg', no access log). Same file :157 greps 'nx plan list' for 'T2 database not found', a literal only nx doctor produces (doctor.py:2222).
- nexus-x8fuq (P2): tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh:247 regexes five demoted verbs against nx doctor output; grep of those verbs in src/nexus/health.py returns 0.

Both are release-only procedures rotting silently — this bead's exact class, one token type outside the sweep. Widening the tripwire to log literals is the durable fix and is noted in xm0cp.

title: [bug] subagent git-write guard covers only commit/add — the WORKING-TREE-destroying verbs (checkout/restore/stash/clean) are unguarded
description:
Found 2026-07-24 while investigating three unexplained reversions of src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py during the nexus-4yf4u stacked review (orchestrator's in-flight fixes silently reverted on disk after the Edit tool reported success; no stash entry, no reflog entry).

THE GAP
conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/subagent_git_write_requires_orchestrator.py (RDR-184 Gap-4 mechanization, bead nexus-s88vq) enforces the standing rule 'agents in a shared tree NEVER git add/git commit'. Its verb set is:

    _WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS = {"commit", "add"}

That set is strictly narrower than the set of git verbs that can destroy an orchestrator's uncommitted work. NOT covered: checkout (incl. 'git checkout -- <path>'), restore, stash, clean, reset --hard, rm.

SEVERITY ARGUMENT (why P1, not a nit): 'git add' only mutates the INDEX and destroys nothing. 'git checkout -- <path>' / 'git restore <path>' / 'git stash' mutate the WORKING TREE and destroy uncommitted work outright. The guard blocks the harmless-but-untidy verbs and permits the destructive ones. The rule's own rationale ('the orchestrator commits pathspec-limited'; hand-back is diffs+paths) applies with MORE force to the verbs that can delete the diffs being handed back.

OBSERVED DAMAGE SIGNATURE (2026-07-24, nexus-4yf4u): src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py reverted to pre-edit content three times over ~10 minutes while two review subagents were live; sibling files edited in the same window (commands/daemon.py, both test files) were untouched. No stash entry and no reflog entry — which is exactly the trace 'git checkout -- <path>' leaves and 'git stash' does not. ATTRIBUTION NOT PROVEN: the review agents were never confirmed as the writer, and the critic's final partial output ('Stable now') reads more like a reviewer waiting out a moving file than the thing moving it. What IS established is that the guard would not have stopped any subagent that did run those verbs.

CORROBORATING: ~/.config/nexus/routing_log.jsonl has ZERO rows for 2026-07-24 (last write 2026-07-23 09:22), so no routing rule recorded an intervention during the session — consistent with the destructive verbs simply not being evaluated.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Extend _WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS to the working-tree-mutating set: checkout, restore, stash, clean, reset, rm. Keep the existing linked-worktree exemption (a worktree-isolated agent owns its tree) and the '# routing-allow:' escape.
2. Read-only forms must stay allowed so reviewers keep working: 'git stash list', 'git checkout' with no pathspec inside a linked worktree, 'git show'/'diff'/'log'/'status'. Prefer allowlisting the read-only invocations over blanket-denying the verb, so a review agent's legitimate 'git show HEAD:<path>' comparison is untouched.
3. Consider whether fail-open remains right for the destructive verbs. It is right for commit/add (hygiene). For 'checkout --' the failure mode is silent destruction of an orchestrator's uncommitted work, which argues for fail-closed on the narrow destructive set — Hal's call.

RELATED: nexus-mk3tw (orchestration Gap-1 guard blindness — undeclared teammates invisible to the census). Same family: a guard whose coverage is narrower than the rule it mechanizes. Distinct defect though: mk3tw is about WHICH AGENTS are seen, this is about WHICH VERBS are seen.

TEST: RED first — a subagent-shaped PreToolUse payload (agent_id present, primary checkout) running 'git checkout -- <path>' must be denied; the same payload running 'git stash list' and 'git show HEAD:<path>' must be allowed; a linked-worktree payload running 'git checkout -- <path>' must be allowed.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ATTRIBUTION NOW PROVEN (2026-07-24, same day). The rerun review agent (CRITIC-4YF4U-C) self-disclosed in its final report: it ran 'git stash' / 'git stash pop' to diff ruff output against HEAD — despite a HARD, explicit read-only constraint in its dispatch prompt that named git stash as forbidden AND explained the prior incident.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED: agent runs 'git stash' (working tree reverts to HEAD) -> orchestrator's Edit lands on the HEAD-state file during that window -> agent runs 'git stash pop' (restores the pre-edit snapshot over the orchestrator's new work). Net effect: the orchestrator's edits vanish after the Edit tool reported success, with NO surviving stash entry (it was popped) and NO reflog entry. That matches every observed symptom of the three upgrade_finish.py reversions, including why sibling files edited outside the stash window were untouched.

This upgrades the bead from 'guard would not have stopped it' to 'guard DID not stop it, twice, and the verb is confirmed in active use by review subagents'. 'stash' is absent from _WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS = {commit, add}.

TWO ADDITIONAL POINTS THIS PROVES:
1. Prompt-level fencing is INSUFFICIENT for this class. The rerun's prompt forbade git stash by name, in caps, with the incident explained — and the agent did it anyway (then disclosed honestly). That is precisely the argument RDR-184 Gap-4 already made for mechanizing the add/commit rule after planner-186 committed in a shared tree despite the prompt rule. Same lesson, new verb set.
2. The damage window is invisible to the victim. The orchestrator's Edit tool returns SUCCESS because the write genuinely succeeded; the loss happens later, on pop. Nothing in the orchestrator's own tooling surfaces it. This is why the guard, not the prompt, has to hold the line.

STRENGTHENS the fail-closed recommendation for the destructive verb set (proposed fix item 3): a cooperative, well-instructed agent violated the rule on its first opportunity.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DECISION (Hal, 2026-07-24): FAIL CLOSED for subagents on the destructive verb set.

So the guard splits into two postures rather than one:
- commit / add — keep FAIL-OPEN. Hygiene rule; the failure mode of a guard bug is untidy staging, and wedging agent work over tidiness is a bad trade. Unchanged from RDR-184.
- checkout / restore / stash / clean / reset --hard / rm — FAIL CLOSED. The failure mode of a guard bug here is the SILENT DESTRUCTION of an orchestrator's uncommitted work, which is strictly worse than a blocked agent. An agent that cannot determine its worktree state must be denied, not waved through.

EVIDENCE THAT SETTLED IT (same day, this session): a review subagent ran git stash / git stash pop in the shared tree AFTER its dispatch prompt forbade the verb by name, in caps, with the prior incident explained — then disclosed it honestly. Cooperative, well-instructed, still did it. Prompt-level fencing is not a control for this class; that is the same conclusion RDR-184 Gap-4 reached for add/commit after planner-186, one verb set later.

DESIGN NOTES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION:
- Keep the linked-worktree exemption for BOTH postures. A worktree-isolated agent owns its tree; that is the documented harvest choreography and the reason isolation exists.
- Keep read-only forms allowed or reviewers break: 'git stash list', 'git show HEAD:<path>', status/diff/log. Prefer allowlisting the read-only invocations over blanket-denying the verb — the legitimate need the offending agent HAD was comparing against HEAD, and 'git show HEAD:<path>' serves it without touching the tree. The deny message should name that alternative explicitly, so the guard teaches the right move instead of just blocking the wrong one.
- Keep the '# routing-allow:' escape (auditable in the routing log).
- Fail-closed means: cannot determine repo/worktree state -> DENY for this set. Note the routing log had ZERO rows for 2026-07-24, so verify the logging path actually fires under the new arm — an unlogged deny is nearly as bad as an unblocked write for forensics.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED a7ef414d. Verb set widened from {commit,add} to also cover checkout/restore/stash/clean/reset/rm. Hal ruling on item 3 (2026-07-25): fail CLOSED on the destroyers when worktree state is undeterminable, fail OPEN unchanged for commit/add, run_hook(fail_closed=False) unchanged so a crash in the guard cannot brick every agent Bash. Reads allowlisted (git stash list/show, show <ref>:<path>, status/diff/log); bare `git stash` explicitly not mistaken for a read. 28 new tests, all mutation-verified. registry.yaml rationale updated in the same commit so documented and enforced rules cannot drift.

NOT CLAIMED: attribution for the 2026-07-24 reversions. The bead says it was never proven and this fix does not establish it. What is closed is the guard gap.

title: [bug] code-symbol-002 cloud parity regression at v0.1.54: chunk_count fold (b6enc F5) is the only doc-join-path change in the tag
description:
conexus relay [21119] 2026-07-24: engine-service-v0.1.54 deployed, step-6 gate GREEN, but code-symbol-002 is a DETERMINISTIC parity regression — jaccard 0.818 (v0.1.52) -> 0.667 (v0.1.54). Cloud consistently DROPS doc chash ebb381d391b4f4e95db79d55739ff0f9c29e8461bda82e0f87c2ad04f0e49cc2 that v0.1.52 returned; oracle still expects it. n_cloud stayed 10 (one doc swapped out), identical set across two runs -> not ANN jitter.

FINDING (nexus side, evidence-complete): v0.1.54 contains ZERO search/ranking/HNSW changes. Full main-source diff v0.1.52..v0.1.54 (4 service commits: 0bf987c7, 7bcf29c6, 57d6ef22, 4a5579f4):
- PgVectorRepository = javadoc-only + ONE constant rehome (ChromaQuotaValidator.MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE -> SOURCE_URI_JOIN_BATCH, same value 300, same sourceUrisByChash batching). No SQL, no ORDER BY, no index/opclass, no embedder-routing delta.
- No Liquibase changeset touches chunks_<dim> or its HNSW index. New changesets are rdr187-002 (DROP staging.chash_index) and taxonomy-005 (topics seq grant). chash_index was never in the search read path — only a comment reference survives in PgVectorRepository.
- Deletions are all Chroma/migration surface, unreachable from /v1/vectors.
So the answer to conexus's question is NO, not intentional, and structurally not a ranking change.

HYPOTHESIS H1 (the only causal path from this tag to a document-level membership change): the nexus-b6enc F5 chunk_count fold. writeManifestRows now sets documents.chunk_count = rows.size() on the SINGLE-doc REPLACE path (v0.1.52 folded only in writeManifestMany); purgeManifest now zeroes it. Document-level results dedupe via the documents.tumbler -> document_chunks join, so a doc whose catalog state changed can drop out while n stays 10. NOTE appendManifestChunks does NOT fold the count — any ingest that writes a manifest as write(batch1)+append(batch2..N) now ends with chunk_count == batch1.size() instead of the prior correct value. Client-side the post-document hook is supposed to call write_manifest with the FINAL shape (catalog_writes.py:1049-1067 documents exactly this contract), which makes the fold correct; an ingest path that misses that hook makes it wrong.
PRECONDITION: H1 only fires if manifests were WRITTEN under v0.1.54. If the corpus is untouched since the v0.1.52 baseline, H1 is dead and H2 stands.

HYPOTHESIS H2: oracle/corpus drift — the baseline is v0.1.52-era; a re-index or re-chash since would make the oracle stale, not the engine.

DISCRIMINATING PROBES (for conexus, cheap):
1. For the dropped chash's document: documents.chunk_count vs SELECT count(*) FROM catalog_document_chunks WHERE doc_id = <tumbler>. Same for a doc that survived. Mismatch => H1 confirmed.
2. Is the doc still present in cloud at all, and is its indexed_at newer than the v0.1.52 baseline capture? => H2.
3. Is code-symbol-002's result set document-level (deduped by tumbler) or chunk-level? Determines whether the manifest join is in the path at all.

RECOMMENDATION: do NOT re-baseline the oracle until H1 is excluded — re-baselining would bake a possible catalog-state bug into the expected set.
close_reason:
NOT a v0.1.54 regression — H1 excluded, H2 (corpus drift) confirmed. conexus probe results [21122]: (P3) code-symbol-002 is /v1/vectors/search = CHUNK-level, ids are chunk chashes not doc tumblers, so the document-level manifest join H1 rides on is not in the path at all. (P1) chunk_count fold did not fire: dropped chunk ebb381d3 -> doc 1.1.2229 chunk_count=23 vs actual manifest rows=23 MATCH, chunk present in BOTH chunks_1024 and catalog_document_chunks at chunk_index=1; control doc 1.1.131 26 vs 26 MATCH. No undercount, no desync, and the write+append precondition never occurred for this doc. (P2) doc indexed_at 2026-07-23T05:39:46Z vs v0.1.52 baseline captured 2026-07-23T03:47:49Z, with v0.1.54 not deployed until 2026-07-24T18:2xZ — the code corpus was re-indexed ~2h AFTER the baseline and ~37h BEFORE the deploy, so the engine-version boundary is coincidental.

ARGUMENT IS COMPLETE WITHOUT AN A/B: the search path is byte-identical v0.1.52..v0.1.54 (this bead's diff evidence), so with identical code and demonstrably changed data, the data is the only possible cause. ebb381d3's own chash/embedding is unchanged (content-addressed); the re-index shifted the competitive field and pushed it past rank 10.

Re-baseline ACKed to conexus. Residual structural point raised in the relay back (not tracked here, conexus-side harness): the oracle fixture oracle-v1-20260611 is pinned against a LIVE actively-developed tree (file:///.../git/nexus/...), so it will re-stale at every code re-index — recommended they stamp a corpus fingerprint into each gate report so the next drift is DETECTED rather than inferred after the fact, and so a genuine engine regression is never dismissed as drift.

title: RDR-185 acceptance harness reshape post-P4b: retire guided-migration rehearsals, build two-hop stranded-redirect rehearsal (cut-time, gated on LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE stamp)
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2026-07-27 (nexus-x7xjj): THIS BEAD NOW OWNS THREE DISABLED WORKFLOWS.

The retire-half of this bead was effectively forced. 88d91bd5 (2026-07-24,
RDR-155 P4b P2) deleted the Chroma migration machinery — the --guided /
--cold / --hole-punch journeys AND the substrate-ETL rung — without the
harness reshape. Three workflows have been failing or dead since:

  .github/workflows/guided-upgrade-mvv.yml   RED since 07-24 (8+ runs)
  .github/workflows/era-hop-mvv.yml          RED since 07-25 (8+ runs)
  .github/workflows/cold-install-rehearsal.yml  dispatch-only, would exit 2

All three now have their schedule/push triggers REMOVED, leaving
workflow_dispatch, each with a header explaining why and pointing here. Files
kept deliberately, not deleted:
  - era-hop's Stages 1-4 (era install, old-engine pre-stage, package upgrade,
    engine-untouched assert) all PASS and are the raw material for the two-hop
    reshape;
  - guided-upgrade-mvv carries the self-hosted bge-asset wiring and
    container-isolation setup;
  - cold-install-rehearsal carries the cold-acquire wiring.
Restoring each schedule/push block is a one-line revert.

WHY era-hop CANNOT BE PATCHED GREEN FIRST (checked, not assumed):
Its non-vacuity gate greps "rung 'substrate-etl' pending". registry.py is now
RUNG_ORDER = (RUNG_CHASH_REKEY,) — that rung is gone for good. Repointing the
grep at chash-rekey would leave the fixture seeding a legacy Chroma store that
NOTHING consumes, i.e. a journey claiming to test an era hop while testing the
rekey. The honest successor is this bead's two-hop stranded-redirect journey,
and it is genuinely blocked: stranded_install.LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE is None
and is stamped at the N+1 CUT. Until then an ancient Chroma install gets
neither a substrate migration (rung deleted) nor a stranding redirect
(detector disarmed), so no rewrite can honestly assert either.

=> The two-hop rehearsal must be built AT the 7.0.0 cut, in the same change
   that stamps LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE. Add that coupling to this bead's
   acceptance: the stamp and the rehearsal land together, or the rehearsal is
   asserting against a disarmed detector and passes vacuously.

COVERAGE GAP ACCEPTED IN THE INTERIM: no era-spanning upgrade gate runs
automatically. There was none in practice anyway (three days of red), but it
is now explicit rather than disguised as a failing check.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
NOW ITEM 1 AUDIT RESULT (2026-07-24): writes DID stop at migration — with one conditional exception that is NOT split-brain but IS a rollback-source mutation.

EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE (this box, service mode, indexed heavily today):
  ~/.config/nexus/catalog/.catalog.db   11 tables, 0 documents, 0 links, mtime 2026-07-13
  ~/.config/nexus/catalog.db            0 BYTES, mtime 2026-05-06 (stray)
  ~/.config/nexus/catalog-archive-pre-service-migration-2026-06/.catalog.db  35MB, 17829 docs / 1779 links
  live PG (nx catalog stats)            22124 documents / 1902 links
A box that indexed thousands of documents today has a live-path .catalog.db last written 11 days ago holding ZERO rows. Row writes to the live path have stopped. Confirmed.

CODE-PATH EVIDENCE: catalog/factory.py make_catalog_writer dispatches on _is_catalog_service_mode() -> _ServiceCatalogWriter (HTTP) and never touches SQLite. storage_boundary_lint enforces CATALOG_CONSTRUCTION_BASELINE=0 (no bare Catalog() outside db//daemon//catalog/) and CATALOG_DB_ACCESS_BASELINE=1 (the two remaining ._db sites are epsilon-annotated backfill-owner-id writes in catalog.py).

THE EXCEPTION (found, not theorised): two allowlisted constructions in src/nexus/db/ open the LIVE path and are guarded ONLY by Catalog.is_initialized(), never by storage mode:
  - src/nexus/db/collection_purge.py:153 — constructs Catalog(cat_path, cat_path/'.catalog.db') then calls delete_document() per orphan tumbler. This WRITES.
  - src/nexus/db/embed_migrate.py:191 — same construction, read-only use.
On a service-mode box whose orphaned .catalog.db still holds rows (STEVE'S SHAPE — 532 docs, not this box's empty one),  would DELETE rows from the frozen migration source. It does not corrupt PG and it is not a split-brain writer (PG remains authoritative and unaffected), but it silently degrades the rollback target the two-hop contract preserves, and it is a SQLite write on a post-migration box.

DISPOSITION RECOMMENDATION (not taken unilaterally — no preventive scope beyond evidence): the rich-catalog SQLite stack DELETES at P3 per [21098], which removes both call sites anyway. Options: (a) leave it, accept that  may thin an orphaned rollback source until P3; (b) add a two-line service-mode gate now so the frozen source is genuinely frozen in the interim. (b) is cheap and matches the orphan-by-design contract; (a) is defensible because the window closes at P3 regardless. Hal's call.

NOW ITEM 2 DONE: health._check_catalog_legacy_file + wired into the doctor assembly; 10 tests. Labels BOTH shapes — populated-but-stale (Steve's) and empty-but-present (this box) — plus the 0-byte stray named separately so nobody chases it. Verified firing against this box's real config dir.

    nx collection purge

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RETRACTION of the "one conditional exception" in my NOW-ITEM-1 audit comment (2026-07-24). The exception does NOT exist. The audit's conclusion is now unqualified: no 6.x service-mode path writes .catalog.db.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: I reported that collection_purge.py:153 constructs a SQLite Catalog guarded "only by is_initialized, never by storage mode" and would delete rows from the frozen migration source on a service box. That is false. purge_collection_cascade branches at collection_purge.py:77 on storage_backend_for("catalog") == StorageBackend.SERVICE, performs the entire cascade server-side (the service response already carries catalog_documents and catalog_collections deletion counts), and RETURNS at line 111 from inside that branch. The SQLite catalog leg lives BELOW that return and is unreachable whenever the catalog is service-backed. I read the is_initialized guard in isolation and never checked the control flow above it.

embed_migrate.py:191 is likewise not a concern: its Catalog use is READ-only, collection_source_paths has no callers outside its own module, and the module operates on cross-embedder Chroma collections (pre-migration machinery that deletes at P3).

CONSEQUENCE: the disposition question I raised — (a) leave it vs (b) add a service-mode gate — was a false choice. Hal chose (b); there is nothing to gate. No code change made.

METHOD NOTE, since this is the second time today a finding rested on reading a guard without its control flow: for a "does X still happen in mode Y" question, trace from the function ENTRY to the call site, not outward from the call site. The empirical half of this audit (live-path .catalog.db last written Jul 13 with 0 rows against 22124 documents in PG, on a box indexed heavily that day) was correct and is what actually established the answer; the code-reading half added a defect that was not there.

A WRITER WAS LIVE. make_catalog_writer/make_catalog_reader both route to HTTP in service mode; make_catalog_admin did NOT — it checked initialization and daemon liveness, then returned a direct Catalog(path, path/".catalog.db"). Its only two callers are the MUTATING ones: `nx catalog dedupe-owners --apply` and `nx catalog undelete`. title: GH#1419.3a: no client-side timeout on indexing HTTP calls — 2+ hour silent hang (Mac sleep mid-request)
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 3. One indexing run hung silently 2+ hours, no client timeout fired (likely sleep mid-request); nexus-service simultaneously spinning with zero active queries (pg_stat_activity clean). Client must carry a read/total timeout + retry on every engine HTTP call in the indexing path (httpx timeouts exist elsewhere — audit the vector/index call sites for missing or infinite timeouts). Related evidence for nexus-29kr0 (Steve reindex forensics: 1-3 retries per repo, transient timeouts).
close_reason:
SHIPPED develop 5c6927e4 (2026-07-24). GH #1419 Issue 3a.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS FALSE — recorded because the next reader will otherwise repeat the audit. It asked for 'a read/total timeout on every engine HTTP call in the indexing path'. An AST audit of every blocking call site in src/nexus found 22 without an explicit timeout, and every one is a fire-and-forget subprocess.Popen or a fast local git/launchctl call. The vector client already bounded every request (120s default, 600s upsert-chunks). Adding timeouts would have shipped nothing.

ROOT CAUSE: Python derives socket-timeout deadlines from the MONOTONIC clock, and on Darwin that is mach_absolute_time() (VERIFIED on the box via time.get_clock_info), which does not advance during system sleep. A socket timeout budgets AWAKE time, not wall-clock time — a laptop sleeping mid-request burns almost none of a 600s budget. On wake the peer is gone but the connection is a zombie with no RST, and NO socket in the tree set SO_KEEPALIVE. Bounded timeout, unbounded hang. Steve's own guess was right.

FIX: TCP keepalive on the engine client's sockets via a urllib opener with subclassed connection classes (urllib exposes no socket-options hook). The IDLE knob is load-bearing — bare SO_KEEPALIVE inherits a 2-HOUR OS default on Darwin AND Linux, useless against a 2h hang. 60s/15s/4 detects a dead peer ~2min after wake as an ordinary connection error the existing retry path handles. Best-effort: a platform lacking the options degrades to an unkeepalived working connection, never a failed request.

ALSO: bounded commands/index.py:1577's git rev-parse, which ran unbounded while indexer_utils.find_repo_root runs the IDENTICAL command with timeout=10.

TESTS: 5, each RED first. One pins the PREMISE not the behaviour — if CPython moves Darwin to sleep-inclusive mach_continuous_time(), it fails and says the rationale needs revisiting. Two assertions initially read '== 1' and failed on Darwin, which returns the option BIT (8) from so_options while Linux normalizes to 1 — wrong on exactly the platform the bug came from; corrected to truthy with the reason recorded.

VERIFICATION: full suite 13326 passed; the 2 failures + 73 errors are byte-identically the same set as before the change (failure lists diffed, not eyeballed).

SPLIT OUT, not dropped: the engine-side spin (100-290% CPU, zero pg_stat_activity rows) is nexus-00wsf — client-unfixable, and the j0nec pipe-fill hypothesis is already excluded there (production routes the child's stdout to a file, never a pipe).

title: GH#1419.1: nx daemon restart-stale reports success without converging engine version (v0.1.49 stuck under 6.16.0)
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 1 — THE TRIGGER. restart-stale run twice against an engine at v0.1.49 with conexus 6.16.0 (requires v0.1.51); no error surfaced, doctor kept reporting mismatch, no forward progress. Only full uninstall + nx init -y converged (v0.1.51 first try, proving the install path works). restart-stale must verify post-restart engine version against REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION and FAIL LOUD on non-convergence (no-silent-fallback class), or escalate to the ladder's engine-binary rung (RDR-185 convergence territory — the ladder is the standing mechanism; restart-stale bypassing it is the design smell). Root-cause why the stale binary persisted across two restarts: suspect it restarts the running process without re-resolving PINNED_SERVICE_TAG/install state.
close_reason:
SHIPPED develop b5cb380a (2026-07-24). GH #1419 Issue 1.

ROOT CAUSE (elimination): doctor delegates to the SAME detect_engine_convergence, so doctor and restart-stale cannot disagree — doctor still showing the mismatch proves the sidecar never moved, so install_binary never succeeded. POISONED / install-failure / no-pinned-tag all emit loud NEEDS HUMAN and Steve reports none, leaving only UNKNOWN->DEFERRED, which was unbounded and unescalating. His 100-290% CPU service made the store unverifiable, and the deferral text named a condition ('once the service is up') already true on his box. GH #1414 had fixed one CAUSE of permanent UNKNOWN; the STRUCTURE was untouched.

SHIPPED: (1) UNKNOWN classified by whether the service is actually up — down defers, up-but-unanswerable is loud NEEDS HUMAN, up-and-answering defers WITH the running version; (2) the disk sidecar no longer short-circuits alone — only a confirmed-equal version or a stopped service stays silent, and a stale live process is restarted on the MANUAL verb only (the automatic post-upgrade pass reports instead, since cycling the service can sever an in-flight client per Issue 3b — Hal decision 2026-07-24); (3) post-restart convergence OBSERVED, not inferred from returncodes, bounded by attempt count AND wall clock.

RDR-185 Gap-4 honored: re-derived live, no retry counter or deferral marker (the banned form). CONSEQUENCE STATED HONESTLY: where the store stays unverifiable AND the service unanswerable, this is a LOUD repeating report, not a terminating one. That is the no-silent-fallback floor, not closure.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (recorded, not resolved — T2 ADDENDUM A2): C1 discriminates on discover_lease(), and the lease is renewed by the same wedged process. If the wedge starves the heartbeat thread, Steve's exact box lands in the UNCHANGED deferral and sees no behavior change; if instead the PG-pool exhaustion times out /version (Hikari 30s vs client 3s), he lands in the new loud arm. Unrecoverable from #1419 — he never pasted the output. The change is a real improvement for every case where the service is observably up; 'closes Steve's loop' was withdrawn as overstated.

VERIFICATION: 13 new tests, each proven RED first; all traced non-vacuous by the critic. 102 pass on the affected files, 945 across the change class, ruff clean. Full suite 13314 passed with 2 failures + 73 errors ALL verified pre-existing on clean HEAD (stashed-changes comparison).

STACKED REVIEW: code-review-expert 1 High (converged-but-unobserved sub-cases returned a bare [] the CLI rendered as 'converged' — silent-reassurance class reintroduced one layer down) + 1 Medium (poll loop uncovered; writing the test exposed a busy-spin under patched sleep) + 1 Low, all folded. substantive-critic PARTIAL, 0 Critical, 3 Significant, all folded (D3 reversal now recorded in the system of record; the overstated closure claim withdrawn; the unattended-restart scope taken back to Hal as an explicit decision).

RECORDS: T2 nexus/design-4yf4u-restart-stale-convergence.md + its ADDENDUM (the addendum supersedes where they conflict).
FOLLOW-UP: nexus-n66kv (ladder-rung promotion; decides provisioning.py's fate — its 4yf4u rationale lapsed since this landed without consuming it). Process defect found en route: nexus-ays2l (P1).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic finding (2026-07-23): refuse-hard-no-override posture is correct and well-grounded — matches RDR-176 Gap 2's "content-unchanged" non-mutation invariant (rdr-176 lines ~86-98/292-298) and the project's no-silent-fallback directive; --apply against the frozen local chash_index on a migrated box would be a genuine RDR-176 violation.

Two Significant precision issues (behavior is safe in both, but reasoning/messaging is not):
1. The guard fires on storage_backend_for("chash_index")==SERVICE BEFORE checking whether a local memory.db exists at all. On a fresh, never-migrated service-mode install (SERVICE is the RDR-152 hard default for every new install), the refusal unconditionally asserts "the local SQLite chash_index here is the FROZEN MIGRATION SOURCE" — false in that branch, since nothing was ever migrated and no local file may exist. Outcome (refuse) is still correct/safe; the stated reason is not. New test test_service_mode_refuses_loud only covers the "memory.db exists" branch.
2. No escape-hatch pointer in the refusal message for the legitimate false-positive case: a genuinely pre-migration, still-SQLite-authoritative box that happens to have NX_STORAGE_BACKEND(_CHASH_INDEX)=service set for unrelated reasons. The correct fix in that case is to correct the per-store env var (storage_backend_for is a routing flag, not a migration-state oracle per storage_mode.py's own docstring) — worth a one-line pointer so operators don't have to reverse-engineer the flag mechanism.

title: nx dt highlights split-brain: writer+reader hit local SQLite directly, bypassing the existing HTTP store (migrated boxes lose highlights both directions)
description: SQLite consumer sweep 2026-07-23 (T2 nexus/sqlite-consumer-sweep-2026-07-23 [21089]) finding 1, the only class-C on a non-hidden verb. WRITER: nx dt index --highlights (commands/dt.py:310) constructs DocumentHighlights(default_db_path()) directly — comment explicitly bypasses daemon AND T2Database — so highlights land in local SQLite where nothing service-side reads them (silent write-to-nowhere on migrated boxes). READER: nx dt highlights (dt.py:996) reads local SQLite only, so all pre-migration ETL'd-to-PG highlights report 'no ingested highlights'. The facade seam ALREADY EXISTS (HttpDocumentHighlightsStore, db/t2/__init__.py:498) and dt.py never uses it — fix is pure routing via storage_backend_for('document_highlights'). FOLD-IN (same subsystem, sweep finding 8): search_engine.py:1090-1093 salience boost constructs DocumentAspects(memory.db) directly bypassing the document_aspects seam — stale pre-migration salient_sentences, no boost for post-migration docs, swallowed at :879; route via facade in the same pass.
close_reason: Shipped 6aaeb6f2 + folds 804af0a0: writer+reader route via _open_highlights_store() (storage facade, per-use close — the batch loop leaked one httpx pool per record pre-fold); reader distinguishes service-unavailable from no-highlights; salience-boost fold-in routed via document_aspects facade with close-parity + first-failure-per-process warning. CRITIC CRITICAL RESOLVED AS MECHANISM: FRESHNESS_PROBES is multi-probe per ETL slot (aspects now also probes document_highlights.ingested_at) so the stranded-window population is recovered by a plain guided-upgrade re-run — the probe sees newer local writes and re-ships the slot; confidently-false-clean regression-pinned. Hal's box verified zero orphaned rows (critic empirical check). Suite 14,563 green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic finding (2026-07-23): salience-boost half of this fix (finding 8 fold-in) is sound — verified HttpDocumentAspectsStore.get_salient_sentences exists with method parity (http_document_aspects_store.py:282), and it does address BOTH audit-named failure shapes (stale frozen reads AND no-boost-for-post-migration-docs) since PG becomes the single live read path for all docs.

CRITICAL residual left by this commit: the document_highlights writer bug it fixes created a window of orphaned local-SQLite highlight rows (any `nx dt index --highlights` run on a migrated box between migration day and this fix). The natural recovery an operator would reach for — re-running `nx guided-upgrade` without --force — will NOT pick these up: guided_upgrade.py's FRESHNESS_PROBES["aspects"] anchors only on document_aspects.extracted_at, not document_highlights.ingested_at, so the freshness probe sees no newer rows and reports "aspects: already migrated ..., no newer local writes" (guided_upgrade.py:553) — a FALSE negative, contradicting the module's own "never silent, always auditable" design intent for StoreMigrationStatus.line. Only --force (unconditional full re-migration of every store) or manual `migrate_highlights()` invocation actually recovers the window. Not flagged in this commit, the bead, or elsewhere.

Verified empirically on this box: ~/.config/nexus/memory.db document_highlights has 0 rows (migration reports date to 2026-07-02) — no known live incident on this install, but the mechanism gap is real and would silently strand data on any other box that ingested highlights post-migration pre-fix.

Recommend: follow-up bead for (a) a FRESHNESS_PROBES entry/secondary anchor covering document_highlights specifically, or (b) an explicit one-time `nx dt highlights --backfill` / standalone migrate_highlights invocation surfaced in the fix's own release notes so affected boxes are told to recover the window.

title: znwc2 residual: structured distances lists still fabricate 0.0 for missing distance (audit item 4, 4 sites)
design:
2026-07-23 substantive-critic review of nexus-znwc2 diff. Audit T2 [21080] item 4 named
SIX sites for the distance-defaults-to-0.0 bug: _distance_key (mcp/core.py:1863) +
structured distances lists at mcp/core.py:2065,2139,2266,2506 + http_vector_client.py:1171.
The znwc2 diff fixed _distance_key (now +inf sentinel, used pervasively as the sort key in
_grouped_combined_query and search_topic_scoped's per-collection merge) and
http_vector_client.py's own structured search() distances list. It did NOT touch the other
four sites, which after the diff's line-shift live at mcp/core.py:2069 (search_metadata_scoped),
2143 (search_topic_scoped), 2270 (search_graph_hop), 2510 (query()'s service-mode dance path) —
all still `r.get("distance", 0.0)`. Verified unchanged post-diff by direct grep.

Sort ORDER is now correct at all four (each path's rows are sorted via _distance_key or
_grouped_combined_query before the structured dict is built), so a missing-distance row no
longer ranks first. But the *reported* distances[i] value returned to any caller of these four
MCP tools in structured=True mode (plan-runner steps, threshold filters, aggregate reducers)
is still a fabricated 0.0 -- exactly the "SILENT relevance corruption" class the audit flagged,
now manifesting as a wrong reported value instead of a wrong rank. A caller filtering on
distance < threshold, or reporting distance to a user, still reads a stripped/anomalous row as
a perfect match.

No log/warn is emitted at any of the four sites when this happens (unlike the diff's telemetry
and ingest-cloud-parity fixes, which both log a structured warning on the degraded path) --
totally silent, no operator visibility.

The new regression test (tests/test_znwc2_response_shape_trust.py::TestDistanceKeySentinel)
only exercises _distance_key directly and HttpVectorClient.search(structured=True); it does not
touch search_metadata_scoped, search_topic_scoped, or search_graph_hop's structured distances
list, so the gap is untested as well as unfixed.

Fix: apply the same `d if (d := r.get("distance")) is not None else float("inf")` pattern (plus
a structured warning, matching the telemetry/ingest-cloud precedent) at all four remaining sites,
and extend TestDistanceKeySentinel to cover them.
close_reason: Fixed in e3ed38c7 same-day: _reported_distances() helper at all four mcp/core.py sites emits honest None (never fabricated 0.0, never JSON-invalid inf) + structured warning + census tripwire in tests/test_znwc2_response_shape_trust.py. Suite 14,518 green.

title: install.mode record never backfilled for upgrade-path installs — perpetual pg_credentials ambiguity warning
description: Batch-f1655f55 critique (T2 nexus/critique-batch-f1655f55-663888e2 [21061]) Significant #1: set_config_value('install.mode', ...) is written ONLY in init.py (provision_service_stack + managed onboarding, 2 call sites). Installs that reached their current state via nx upgrade / guided-upgrade never get the record, so is_local_mode() falls through to the legacy pg_credentials/chroma-key inference — including its ambiguity warning — indefinitely, unless the user re-runs nx init. DECISION NEEDED (design level, no knob reflex): backfill opportunistically on successful upgrade convergence (fold into the journey), or record as accepted debt. Context: nexus-x3ugg 702bf6de.
notes: SEVERITY ESCALATION — SHAKEOUT agent E, E-1 HIGH (2026-08-03): the is_local_mode() pg_credentials-inference this bead describes does not just produce an ambiguity warning — on the production cloud-mode install it makes nx doctor SKIP three service checks outright ('service mode not configured (pg_credentials absent)'): storage-service health, SCHEMA MIGRATIONS, and RLS POLICIES. Liquibase migration state and RLS enforcement are UNVERIFIED on the production deployment while doctor presents an otherwise-green report. The install works (credentials.service_url + service_token in config.yml, get_credential() precedence fine) — only doctor's mode inference is wrong. Fix at the root (install.mode backfill) rather than per-check; the three skip sites then key correctly for free. This is the difference between 'doctor is confusing' and 'doctor cannot see production' — recommend P1.
close_reason: Fixed on develop 87f92054. backfill_install_mode_record() stamps install.mode on upgrade convergence (nx upgrade post-ladder + check_version_transition finish pass) from durable evidence only (persisted service_url -> managed, pg_credentials -> local; NX_LOCAL sessions and env-only NX_SERVICE_URL never stamp). Doctor's three service-check skip branches now state the nexus-y3wuu server-side contract on managed installs instead of 'not configured'. NOTE (corrects the escalation's premise): the three skip sites are creds-file probes, not is_local_mode() consumers — they could never 'key correctly for free'; message honesty was the achievable half. Client-side verification of managed migrations/RLS remains impossible BY DESIGN (nexus-y3wuu, Hal decision 2026-07-20) — that residual is permanent accepted debt, verified server-side by the store operator. Known residual: boxes whose every upgrade runs under a durable NX_LOCAL wrapper never backfill (init owns their stamp). Dual-reviewed: round1 1C/2S -> fixed -> round2 both reviewers clean.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SUBSTANTIVE CRITIQUE (2026-08-03): reviewed the uncommitted implementation against the locked design (T1 9982fd3a).

CRITICAL: backfill_install_mode_record()'s own docstring promises "Never raises" but only OSError around set_config_value is caught. load_config()/get_credential() call yaml.safe_load with NO try/except anywhere in config.py — a malformed config.yml raises yaml.YAMLError uncaught. upgrade_finish.py's call site defensively wraps the call in try/except Exception; commands/upgrade.py's call site does NOT (bare call, relies on the false "never raises" promise). Concrete regression: a box with a corrupted config.yml running plain `nx upgrade` (no --auto) — ladder succeeds, then backfill_install_mode_record() raises, propagates through the bare call, hits upgrade()'s outer `except Exception: ... raise` (non-auto path) -> nx upgrade now reports FAILURE even though the real upgrade work completed. Fix: wrap the commands/upgrade.py call site the same way upgrade_finish.py does, or make load_config()/get_credential() calls inside backfill exception-safe so the docstring's contract is actually true.

SIGNIFICANT: backfill_install_mode_record() ignores NX_LOCAL entirely; is_local_mode() gives NX_LOCAL top precedence over everything including the record. Docstring claims "precedence mirrors is_local_mode()'s own reading" but omits this. Scenario: pg_credentials present (documented migrated-install remnant case), no service_url, operator sets NX_LOCAL=0 to force managed for a session -> is_local_mode() correctly returns False that session, but `nx upgrade` in the same session stamps "local" permanently (ignoring NX_LOCAL). Next session once NX_LOCAL is unset, is_local_mode() now reads the persisted "local" record and flips to True -- silently contradicting the operator's own override. No test exercises NX_LOCAL interaction (TestBackfillInstallModeRecord unconditionally clears it).

SIGNIFICANT: this bead's own escalation note ("the three skip sites then key correctly for free") was found false by the design (T1 9982fd3a) and correctly worked around with explicit per-site is_local_mode() checks -- but the bead's notes/description here haven't been updated to say so, nor to record that true server-side migration/RLS verification for managed installs remains categorically impossible (nexus-y3wuu, permanent). The fix makes doctor's message honest; it does not restore verifiability. Recommend a note before closing so a future reader doesn't read "closed" as "production now verifiable."

Verified: the health.py fix is self-sufficient for the reported production scenario (service_url set) because is_local_mode() already gives service_url unconditional precedence over the record -- so the message fix works even independent of backfill success. The finish-pass hook (upgrade_finish.py) does correctly fire on the very next nx invocation after the box upgrades to the fix-containing release (genuine version transition), covering the "ancient upgraded-only install" case as intended. Tests are non-vacuous (real CliRunner + config.yml assertions in test_upgrade_cmd.py; is_local_mode pinned explicitly, never ambient, in health tests).

title: SessionStart RDR reconcile hook silently reverts open->draft (nexus-qsryj gap)
description: conexus/hooks/scripts/rdr_hook.py _STATUS_ORDER (used by _reconcile) does not include 'open', which 7a45359c (nexus-qsryj, GH #1409) made a first-class pre-accept status synonym for 'draft'. _STATUS_ORDER.get('open', -1) returns -1 (unknown rank). rdr-create's T2 record ALWAYS starts at status='draft' (conexus/skills/rdr-create/SKILL.md), rank 0. So any RDR file hand-authored or templated with frontmatter status: open gets silently rewritten to draft by the very next SessionStart hook run (t2_rank(0) > file_rank(-1) triggers _update_file_status, which does NOT go through nx rdr set-status and is not gated by any confirmation) -- directly undoing the status word the qsryj fix was meant to make first-class. Fix: add 'open': 0 (or a dedicated rank) to _STATUS_ORDER in rdr_hook.py so open and draft are reconciliation-equivalent, matching rdr.py's _KNOWN_STATUSES and preamble_rdr_accept's acceptance list. Found during stacked substantive-critique pass batch-critic-f1655f55 (range f1655f55..663888e2).
close_reason: Fixed in the batch-review fold commit: 'open' added to _STATUS_ORDER at draft rank in conexus/hooks/scripts/rdr_hook.py; _reconcile() regression tests added (open-vs-draft both directions no-op, open still advances to accepted). Found by substantive-critic on the f1655f55..663888e2 stacked review.

title: Reindex embed-skip verification: prove RDR-181's skip fires on the re-index path (hours->minutes for unchanged content; Steve-report prime suspect)
description: oub13 profile finding (2026-07-22, sandbox fresh index of the nexus repo, engine v0.1.52): the post-index flush drain IS the embed cost — 44,306 chunks, 216 flushes, ~90s server-side each at client concurrency 3, ~7 chunks/s aggregate, ~105min projected. A RE-index of unchanged content should bypass nearly all of it via RDR-181's server-side embed-skip (same text -> same chash -> vector present -> skip). Steve (stevengharris) reports HOURS on reindex — prime suspect: the skip not firing on his path (or era-32 re-id changed effective chunk identity). WORK: (1) when Steve's forensics land, check for embed-skip lines; (2) build a warm-reindex regression gate: index a corpus, reindex unchanged, assert the drain's server embed count ~= 0 and wall is minutes not hours (falsify by breaking the skip); (3) if the skip has a gap (e.g. keyed on collection+chash but reindex targets a different collection name, or the batcher path bypasses the skip route), fix at mechanism. Evidence: /tmp/oub13-profile-PZOF98 logs; engine upsert_dedup_collapsed lines show 64-cap docs flushes 8-22s apart.
notes: Live evidence 2026-08-19 (7.12.0 T1 shakedown): warm-reindex-skip-gate PASSED — legB 9up/8skip/1emb proves RDR-181 skip fires on warm re-index at the gate layer; remaining question is production-scale axis only.

title: codesign+notarize mac-arm64 engine binary likely breaks bundled onnxruntime/DJL JNI dlopen under Hardened Runtime library validation
design:
Follow-up on nexus-27i0m (96677bf7). The codesign step signs
service/target/nexus-service with `codesign --force --options runtime
--timestamp` and NO --entitlements plist. macOS Hardened Runtime
implicitly enables Library Validation: any dylib dlopen'd/System.load()'d
by the process at runtime must be signed by the SAME Team ID (or be an
Apple system library), or the load is refused.

The engine binary bundles TWO third-party native libs as native-image
resources (service/pom.xml -H:IncludeResources=ai/onnxruntime/native/...
and native/lib/${djl.native.dir}/...) — onnxruntime-java (Microsoft-signed
or unsigned) and DJL HuggingFace tokenizers native lib — extracted to a
temp file and System.load()'d at runtime by OnnxEmbedder/Bge768Embedder
(service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/OnnxEmbedder.java)
whenever local-mode embedding initializes (RDR-152/160, exercised by
`nx init --service` on every fresh mac-arm64 local install).

Documented precedent for this EXACT failure class: jnr-ffi #257 ("mac m1
+ code signing == failure"), zstd-jni #321 ("MacOS 10.14.6 incompatible
dylib binary") — third-party JNI dylibs failing dlopen under Hardened
Runtime library validation with errors like "code signature ... not valid
for use in process using Library Validation".

Today (ad-hoc signature, no hardened runtime) this works because library
validation is NOT enforced on non-hardened-runtime processes. Once
APPLE_DEV_ID_* secrets are provisioned and this ships, the SAME binary
becomes hardened-runtime-signed — library validation switches ON — and
local-mode embedding on mac-arm64 very likely starts failing
(UnsatisfiedLinkError / crash), i.e. a properly-signed binary that is
STRICTLY WORSE than the ad-hoc status quo it replaces.

Nothing in engine-service-release.yml or
tests/test_engine_release_workflow_signing.py catches this: mac-arm64 is
UNSMOKED (matrix.target.smoke=false, no Docker on GH macOS runners), the
10 shape-pin tests are pure YAML-text greps with no execution, and
codesign --verify --strict only validates the OUTER Mach-O's own
signature — it says nothing about runtime dlopen of embedded resources.

Fix: add com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation (via an
entitlements.plist passed to codesign --entitlements) OR independently
codesign the extracted onnxruntime/DJL dylibs with the same Developer ID
identity before the outer binary is signed. Either way this needs an
ACTUAL runtime smoke of local-mode embedding (construct
OrtEnvironment/HuggingFaceTokenizer) against the SIGNED+notarized binary
before it ships — not just codesign --verify on the outer binary.

Also validate against the (separately identified) tag-gating gap: the
codesign/notarize steps run on EVERY workflow_dispatch build (dev/smoke
path), unlike cosign which is explicitly gated to
startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/engine-service-v') — burns Apple
notarization submissions on every dev-iteration workflow_dispatch run,
inconsistent with the CI Cost Discipline directive and the adjacent
cosign step's own gating pattern in the same file.

Evidence: git show 96677bf7; service/pom.xml lines ~152-160, ~602-611;
service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/OnnxEmbedder.java;
.github/workflows/engine-service-release.yml lines 228-320.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: engine-service-release.yml:427 signs with service/deploy/mac-entitlements.plist; tests/e2e/mac-signed-binary-gate.sh (2cdfbd191) proves JNI load under Hardened Runtime
