comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
NEW EVIDENCE, 2026-07-24/25 (engine-service-v0.1.55 cut). Two findings; the
second is the one that turns this from a latent hazard into a shipping risk.

FINDING 1 — still dormant, confirmed from the run log, not inferred. Both steps
warn-and-skip on v0.1.55:
  ##[warning]APPLE_DEV_ID_* secrets not provisioned — publishing the
    ad-hoc-signed binary (browser downloads stay Gatekeeper-blocked)
  ##[warning]APPLE_NOTARY_* secrets not provisioned — Gatekeeper will block
    browser downloads even if Developer-ID signed
So nexus-service-mac-arm64 in v0.1.55 is AD-HOC signed: no Hardened Runtime, no
library validation, and therefore no dlopen breakage of the bundled
onnxruntime/DJL JNI libs. The workflow's all-three-or-none guard is also
working (partial config fails loud rather than silently shipping ad-hoc).
Why this has never bitten anyone: `install-binary` fetches via the API, not a
browser, so no com.apple.quarantine xattr is set and Gatekeeper never
adjudicates.

FINDING 2 — NOTHING WOULD CATCH THE BREAKAGE. Step order in the mac-arm64 job:
  Build native image -> Install nexus -> Native smoke test (boot against
  throwaway pgvector) -> Developer ID codesign -> Notarize -> Clean up keychain
  -> Stage artifact + sha256 -> Assert binary ABI floor -> cosign -> Publish
The native smoke runs BEFORE codesign/notarize. The SIGNED bytes are never
booted, never forced to embed, before publish. "Assert binary ABI floor" is
post-sign but static. And the new published-artifact acquire gate (nexus-1ddsy)
runs inside debian:bookworm-slim, so `current_platform_tag()` resolves to
linux-* and it exercises the LINUX artifact only — it cannot see a mac signing
defect by construction.

Net: the exact defect this bead predicts (library validation blocking JNI
dlopen) would ship GREEN through the release workflow and green through the
acquire gate, and first surface on a user's Mac.

IMPLICATION FOR SEQUENCING. Provisioning the Apple secrets is what ARMS this.
So the post-notarize verification should land BEFORE the secrets do, not after:
  a. Add a post-notarize step on the mac runner that boots the SIGNED binary and
     forces a real ONNX embed (the same drive the acquire gate does) — a version
     handshake is insufficient, since the failure mode is a binary that starts
     fine and dies the moment it must dlopen.
  b. Then provision APPLE_DEV_ID_* + APPLE_NOTARY_* and set the repo variable
     APPLE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=true (promotes later secret loss to a hard failure).
  c. Mitigation if (a) goes red: sign every bundled .dylib/.so under the same
     Team ID, or add com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation.
Doing (b) before (a) means the first signal is a user report.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
THE RUNTIME-EXERCISE GATE NOW EXISTS: tests/e2e/mac-signed-binary-gate.sh
(develop 2cdfbd19). This bead's remaining work was "validate ON MAC HARDWARE with
quarantine xattr intact — spctl AND one real local-mode embed"; there was no
script for it, so it was a prose instruction that would have been improvised
under release pressure. It is now a scripted gate, wired into the engine-release
skill next to the mac-gap scope limit it closes.

RUN IT after the first Developer-ID-signed tag publishes and BEFORE setting
APPLE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=true:

    NEXUS_SERVICE_TAG=engine-service-vX.Y.Z tests/e2e/mac-signed-binary-gate.sh

Must end MAC SIGNED-BINARY GATE PASSED.

WHAT IT ASSERTS, in order:
  1. Developer-ID signature, NOT ad-hoc (TeamIdentifier set)
  2. Hardened Runtime ACTIVE — without this Library Validation is off and every
     assertion below would pass for the wrong reason
  3. the disable-library-validation entitlement is present
  4. spctl accepts a QUARANTINED copy. The xattr is applied deliberately:
     install-binary fetches via the API and sets none, so Gatekeeper never
     adjudicates — which is precisely why this hazard has never bitten anyone.
  5. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: boots the SIGNED binary through native-smoke.sh (BIN
     override) and asserts the bge-768 embed ACTUALLY EXECUTED. That section
     drives the DJL tokenizer JNI + an onnxruntime session, i.e. the two
     System.load()s Library Validation refuses.

NON-VACUITY IS THE DESIGN POINT. native-smoke.sh WARN+skips its embed when the
bge model is absent. For this gate that skip would mean passing without loading a
single JNI library — so the model is a hard PRECONDITION and a skipped embed is
an explicit FAILURE, not a pass. Wrong arch / no Docker / no tag are ERRORS too,
never skips.

VALIDATED AGAINST A REAL ARTIFACT rather than syntax-checked: run against
engine-service-v0.1.57 it downloads the true 192MB published binary and correctly
FAILS on ad-hoc signature, no Hardened Runtime, and missing entitlement. That is
the discriminating power required — had it passed on an ad-hoc binary it would
have been vacuous. It also confirms empirically what this bead's 2026-07-25
comment inferred from run logs: v0.1.57 (and v0.1.58) ship ad-hoc.

WHY IT STAYS MANUAL, so nobody files "automate this" without the context:
mac-arm64 is smoke:false in engine-service-release.yml (macos-14 runners have no
Docker), and codesign runs AFTER the linux-only smoke — so CI never boots the mac
binary at all, and even if the runner gained Docker it would smoke the
PRE-signature bytes. codesign --verify cannot see a runtime dlopen refusal.

RELATED, same session: the six APPLE_* secrets are now scoped to a required-
reviewer `apple-signing` GitHub Environment restricted to the engine-service-v*
tag (develop c1dd5ce2), instead of being repo-wide readable. Landed BEFORE
provisioning on purpose, so the gate exists before there is anything to gate.

REMAINING on this bead is unchanged and is Hal's: provision the six secrets into
the environment, cut a tag, run this gate on mac hardware, and only then set
APPLE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=true.

title: N+1 P4b prereq: stranded-install detector — a pre-migration box that direct-upgrades to the post-deletion release gets a LOUD two-hop redirect, never a silent empty install
description: Hal's gap (2026-07-21): after P4b deletes Chroma + the migration tool (and RDR-158 P4 deletes SQLite T2), a 4.x/5.x/early-6.x user who pip-upgrades DIRECTLY to N+1 currently gets an UNSPECIFIED outcome — in practice a fresh empty PG install beside their unmigrated chroma/, t2.db, memory.db, catalog/.catalog.db, indistinguishable from data loss. g37fr's deletion scope (thorough on mechanics) contains no stranded-era handling; grep confirms no surviving refusal exists (last_seen_version is a stamp only). SPEC: a detection-only stub with ZERO chromadb/sqlite3 imports (pure file stats: chroma/chroma.sqlite3, t2.db, memory.db, catalog/.catalog.db presence + absence of a verified migration-report JSON + last_seen_version era) wired into nx init, first CLI/MCP run, and nx doctor. On detection: FAIL LOUD (no silent fallback — correctness class) with the literal two-hop instruction: 'this install carries pre-PG data from conexus <era>; install conexus==<LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE> (pinned constant, same one-constant discipline as REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION), run nx guided-upgrade, then upgrade back to this version.' The constant is stamped at N+1 cut time. Test: fresh-box negative (no false positive on virgin installs — the fresh-install MVV must stay green), migrated-box negative (report present → no trip), stranded-box positive (fixture files → exact message). Chain: BLOCKS nexus-g37fr (the deletion cannot land without this); also belongs in 8zpmf's gate checklist and the 19svb inverse-grep must NOT flag the detector's filename references (strings, not imports).
close_reason: Shipped on develop 071f0191: stdlib-only leaf detector (LAST_MIGRATION_CAPABLE=None, disarmed until N+1 cut), wired on nx init (refusal), CLI banner (ordered before check_version_transition), nx doctor (fatal check), and BOTH MCP servers via instructions channel. 35 tests incl. pyproject-derived wiring census + real-call-order era regression; mutation-falsified; stacked-reviewed (reviewer clean, critic's 3 Criticals + 3 Significants all fixed pre-commit). title: Fresh-install MVV release gate: virgin HOME -> init -> store -> ASSERT engine-catalog row + manifest -> index -> search -> doctor warnings-allowlist; add to the release checklist beside era-hop
description: Root-cause of why the release process missed the f1itv/e9ru2/r5f3c/9xfx5 class (Hal question 2026-07-21). Three structural blind spots, all verified: (1) tests/conftest.py:266 _pin_storage_backend_sqlite pins the entire unit suite to the SQLite opt-out backend — production's hard-default SERVICE mode is opt-in per test, so service-mode-reaches-local-era-code seams are structurally invisible; (2) every E2E release gate (rehearsal, era-hop, guided MVV, package-upgrade convergence) starts from a POPULATED install and tests the upgrade axis; migrated boxes are exactly where the stale local gates pass by accident via the frozen .catalog.db; the one fresh-machine leg (release-sandbox.sh service mode, RDR-157 P4.2) is not in the release checklist and stops at 'serving' — one step before the first data-journey bug; (3) the bugs are silent best-effort skips, so even a journey run would have passed without explicit assertions (the ou4tb thesis). Self-provisioning per feedback_gates_scripted_not_ambient; env-scrubbed (no VOYAGE_API_KEY leak — the r5f3c lesson). Wire into the release checklist (CLAUDE.md release steps + docs/contributing.md) beside the era-hop MVV. title: Era-hop MVV red since RDR-180 cutover: substrate-etl refuses 32-hex era ids on the unattended walk (design fork: recompute-rekey in ETL vs scenario redesign)
description: Diagnosis 2026-07-21 (6.15.0 release prep). Era-hop last GREEN 2026-07-18 (c7b5c8e2); red on every run since 2026-07-20 — predates the GH #1414 arc. Three stacked failure layers: (1) converge_engine deferred because health._run_psql lacked the _bundle_lib_env loader guard (fixed 91188512+3827e366, all 3 psql sites); (2) pre-P2.1 era box has no nexus_diag creds so the probe could never run (fixed 86f215c6: _poison_probe self-backfills via backfill_diag_role_best_effort). (3) REMAINING, pre-existing from the RDR-180 cutover: substrate-etl re-embed legs fail with etl_seam_nonconformant_post_transform written=0 on collections whose chunk ids are 32-hex era (knowledge__rehearsal{,-note,-mislabel}) — the RDR-180 no-guess policy refuses them with a re-index-first remedy the era box cannot perform (source content gone by scenario design). title: Post-RDR-187 FK census: enumerate every inter-table relationship that SHOULD be enforced now that all stores are co-resident in one PG (RDR candidate)
description:
Hal directive 2026-07-21 (mid-.9): 'this facilitates even further reduction and simplification. If nothing else, we need a once-over to ensure we have all the FK relationships we should, now that we finally have everything in the same DB.'

Scope sketch (design-level — RDR before implementation):
- The split-store era made these unenforceable by construction: SQLite stores could not reference PG rows; the chash_index router was a substrate-straddling derived copy (now dropped, RDR-187). Co-residency makes the census possible for the first time.
- Known candidates from prior arcs: the three TEXT chash-debt columns (topic_assignments.doc_id, frecency.chunk_id, relevance_log.chunk_id — the census's dangling legs exist precisely because no FK does that job); catalog_document_chunks.chash -> chunks_<dim> (design question: the referent lives in exactly ONE of three dim tables — partitioned FK? trigger? generated routing column?); the RDR-180 state memory's 'FK-anchored chash identity / retire the legacy-debt TEXT columns' RDR-candidate folds in here.
- Existing partial coverage to build on: fk-001/fk-002/fk-003 changelog families (catalog cross-store + collection-registry FKs, some NOT VALID); the ChashCensus dangling legs are the observability stopgap an FK would retire.
- Also in Hal's framing: 'further reduction and simplification' beyond FKs — candidates: census legs that FKs obsolete, the chash_alias-vs-FK interplay, staging exemptions (transient by design).
- Method: schema-wide join-column enumeration (information_schema-derived, census-style — not a hand list), classify each as FK-able now / needs-design / deliberately-loose, then RDR.
Sequencing: after RDR-187 closes (the .11 N+1 staging drop changes the table set again — decide whether to census before or after).
notes: RDR-194 ACCEPTED 2026-08-15. This bead is the ARC PARENT (id-prefix convention, as nexus-cefa1 was for the type-hygiene arc). Plan of record: T2 nexus/plan-rdr194-execution-2026-08-15. RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-194-fk-census-structural-schema-warts.md. 18 children created 2026-08-15: nexus-tk070.cc1-.cc6 (cloud-count HAL relay preconditions) and .p1/.p2/.p3a-.p3d/.p4/.p5a/.p5b/.p6a/.p6b/.p7 (phases). Critical path is strictly serial through the changelog tail: cc1 -> p1 -> cc2/p2 -> p3a -> cc4 (HARD STOP) -> p3b -> p3c -> p3d -> p4 -> cc5/p5a -> p5b -> cc6/p6a -> p6b -> cc3/p7. title: RDR-187 P1: Reimplement /v1/chash/* reads over chunks; writes accept-and-no-op (deprecation marker)

title: RDR-187: Retire chash_index — drop the router remnant of the split-store architecture
description:
Retire nexus.chash_index — the router half of the retired split-store architecture. Post-RDR-155/180 the chunks tables ARE the chash-keyed store (PK (tenant_id, collection, chash), one row per collection membership), so the router is a derived, FK-less copy maintained by dual-writes that drifted 292,230 rows on the production store (99.85% of the RDR-180 VALIDATE amnesty; blocks the octet CHECK). Drop it; serve every consumer from the chunks tables; keep the /v1/chash/* HTTP shape so clients are unaffected. chash_alias is NOT in scope (stays permanent). RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-187-retire-chash-index-router-table.md (accepted 2026-07-20, gate PASSED).

TWO RELEASE LIFECYCLES: (1) engine-service tags — Hal cuts them (P0 index, P1 reroute, P4 staging-engine, P5 DROP+ETL, P6 deferred); (2) conexus PyPI — client work (P2 hook removal, P4 staging-client, part of P3). Steps 2-7 (P1-P5) are ONE engine+client PAIRED release. P0 ships AHEAD on the next engine tag. P6 (step 8) ships ONE RELEASE LATER — not schedulable now.

title: chash-rekey rung VALIDATE policy: lived-in stores with orphan-pointer debt fail the all-five VALIDATE (align with production decision: gate three, report two)
description:
Production proof 2026-07-20 (bus [20980]/[20982]): the cloud store carried 292,230 chash_index + 426 catalog_document_chunks PRE-EXISTING orphan pointers (zero alias entries — content absent before the rekey; created_at 2026-04-18..07-06). Table-grain VALIDATE on those two CHECKs is arithmetic-impossible while the debt exists. The client rung (src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/rungs/chash_rekey.py OCTET_CHECKS) VALIDATEs ALL FIVE — any lived-in local store with the same delete-path debt fails nx upgrade at this step.

POLICY: VALIDATE the three chunks tables (the RDR-180 content contract); leave the two POINTER-table CHECKs NOT VALID when dangling pointers exist; REPORT the counts loudly. New writes stay enforced regardless (NOT VALID gates existing rows only).

*** IMPLEMENT AS A CEILING, NOT A TABLE EXEMPTION (conexus correction, Hal-caught, [20982]) ***
conexus's first cut implemented 'these two tables do not gate' — categorical and permanent. That converts a bounded amnesty for MEASURED debt into a permanent blind spot: a future rekey introducing 50,000 BRAND-NEW orphans would print them as observed and still PASS. That is the silent-scope-reduction shape.
CORRECT SHAPE: pin the debt as a CEILING measured at the decision point.
  grandfathered_debt = {catalog_document_chunks: <measured>, chash_index: <measured>}
  FAIL on any INCREASE; within-ceiling counts warn and still print.
For the RUNG the ceiling is per-store and must be measured at rung-run time (pre-VALIDATE census), persisted in the rung's completion record, and compared on subsequent passes.
NON-VACUITY (mirror conexus's proof): lowering the ceiling by ONE must flip the verdict to FAIL with a '+1 NEW non-conformant rows — amnesty covers pre-existing debt only' message. Red-first: seed a lived-in store with a dangling 16-byte chash_index row, prove (a) the rung completes with report instead of crashing, (b) adding one more dangling row FAILS.
close_reason: SHIPPED 79d234ec + 9400a014. Gate-three/report-two: the three CONTENT octet CHECKs always VALIDATE; the two POINTER checks are skipped while pre-existing orphan debt exists, counts reported with a remediation pointer. Implemented as a CEILING measured within the run (debt before the rekey vs after) — growth raises, pre-existing is grandfathered — NOT a table exemption, per conexus's own correction that Hal caught. Ceiling is run-local by design: the only cross-run store is the completion record's detail field, which protocol.py declares observability-only and accepted lossy, and a load-bearing gate must not ride a lossy field. pointer_debt_fn rides the read-only diag choke point; None (managed/no creds) leaves all-five behaviour untouched. Red-first, mutation-verified (blanket exemption fails the ceiling test); upgrade-ladder suite 569 passed.

title: RekeyOps: in-transaction ANALYZE of chash_alias — second-tenant planner catastrophe (F2, 101min->461s)
description: Production finding 2026-07-20 (bus [20980] F2, conexus rekey window): autoanalyze after tenant-1 commit froze chash_alias pg_stats at most_common_vals={tenant1} freqs=[1.0] n_distinct=1. Tenant 2's alias rows are inserted INSIDE its own transaction (invisible to planner) -> tenant_id predicate estimates rows=1 -> TRIPLE NESTED LOOP against ~134k x 466k actual -> 101 MINUTES (aborted clean). enable_nestloop=off empirically confirmed: same work 461s. FIX (one statement): ANALYZE nexus.chash_alias inside the rekey transaction, after the alias INSERT and before the cascade DELETEs — in-txn ANALYZE sees its own uncommitted rows. Every multi-tenant store hits this from the SECOND tenant onward; single-tenant/M1 structurally cannot. Check StagingPromoteOps for the same shape (alias-driven cascades after bulk INSERT). Third stale-stats incident in 24h (BUG-0148, rdr180-16, this) — the class is 'planner blind to just-written rows'. Engine lifecycle: rides next engine-service tag.
close_reason: SHIPPED 8573c15b. In-transaction ANALYZE of chash_alias in RekeyOps + StagingPromoteOps via ChashSqlIdioms.refreshAliasStats; GRANT MAINTAIN in grants-nexus-svc (runAlways, self-heals next boot); alias_stats_refreshed rides the envelope and the client rung surfaces a false. KEY FINDING: the bare statement is a SILENT no-op — Postgres WARNs+SKIPs for a non-owner rather than erroring (verified empirically: statement alone produced ZERO stats and threw nothing), so tests assert the RESULTING STATISTICS, never the statement. Version guard is load-bearing: has_table_privilege(...,'MAINTAIN') RAISES on PG16 rather than returning false, which would abort the whole rekey. Cloud verified PG 17.10 so the fix is live there on the next engine tag. Full engine suite 1355/0/0 on the final tree. Mutation-verified both directions.

title: RDR-180: guided migration becomes LAND-THEN-TRANSFORM — bulk-load legacy source into a PG staging schema, then one transactional in-DB re-id/promote (kills the per-leg in-flight rewrite class)
description:
DESIGN DIRECTIVE (Hal, 2026-07-19): all source tables land in the SAME PG database (own staging schema, width-free), and the re-id transforms run TRANSACTIONALLY IN THE DB — not as per-leg client-side in-flight rewrites (the Rube Goldberg class whose hand-carried id inventory produced 8 misses this arc, culminating in the --guided gate failure: catalog_etl posts 32-hex manifest rows verbatim and the cohort engine's strict boundary 400s them).

SHAPE:
1. LAND: guided migration bulk-loads the immutable Chroma/SQLite source VERBATIM into staging (chunks WITH text + embeddings for Voyage-free vector reuse; catalog document_chunks manifest; chash_index; topic_assignments; frecency; relevance_log — the Item6a chash-bearing set). Staging schema carries NO width constraints; DDL via Liquibase (engine lifecycle, rides the unpublished cohort tag).
2. TRANSFORM+PROMOTE: one RekeyOps-shaped engine-side transactional pass per tenant: staging chunk_text is the digest source (PG-native sha256), every staged chash-bearing row rewrites via set-based joins, chash_alias rows record in the SAME txn, promoted rows enter the nexus schema already canonical (strict checks never fought). Item8 dispositions (empty/orphaned text) apply in the same pass. Client's job collapses to: stream source bytes into staging + drive one endpoint + verify counts.
3. The in-store cutover path (rdr180-001 conversion + /v1/remap/rekey + chash-rekey rung) is UNTOUCHED — this bead re-vehicles only the guided MIGRATION path.

REPLACES the leg-patch design (each T2 ETL leg learns wire_reid re-id) — that fix ADDS to the class this directive kills. wire_reid stays for the vector-leg era it already shipped in; whether the vector leg also converges onto land-then-transform is a design question for the analysis.

title: RDR-180 Item8: Null/orphaned chunk_text disposition - three-way ETL policy
description:
LIFECYCLE: CLIENT (PyPI, ETL flag). Closes G2 robustly. MUST be its own bead (RDR Scope Verification - silent-scope-reduction risk if folded into schema change). Defined REGARDLESS of current zero residue (A-1 measured residue=0 on the two cloud tenants) precisely so a later text-sparse tenant does not surface it as unplanned work mid-migration.

Three-way disposition, in priority order, keyed off the union old->new map (old_chash -> sha256(chunk_text)):
1. Rehashable - non-empty chunk_text: new key = sha256(chunk_text). 100% of current corpus.
2. Reference-only, recoverable - null/empty chunk_text but old_chash has content on another row: remap via old->new map to sibling's new key. Never dropped, never synthesized.
3. Orphaned - null/empty chunk_text AND no content-bearing source anywhere: apply orphan_policy:
   - drop (default): delete the chunk row AND cascade to every catalog_document_chunks/chash_index pointer at that old_chash (else dangling manifest rows). Emit per-tenant count; never silent.
   - synthesize (opt-in): mint deterministic surrogate sha256('nexus:synthetic-chash:v1|'+tenant+'|'+collection+'|'+old_chash) (32 bytes) + stamp metadata->>'chash_origin'='synthetic'. The metadata flag is the honest signal, NOT the byte pattern.
Per-run ETL flag (default drop), logged with disposition counts (rehashed/remapped/dropped/synthesized). Item6's ETL consumes this policy.

TEST (synthetic fixture tenant): (a) rehashable->sha256(chunk_text); (b) reference-only w/ content sibling->remapped not dropped; (c) orphaned under drop->row gone AND pointers cascaded (no dangling scan hit); (d) orphaned under synthesize->surrogate present w/ chash_origin='synthetic', pointer preserved. Counts asserted.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
From read-endpoints critic (2026-07-18), THREE binding design inputs for the client half:
(1) STEADY-STATE N+1 (bigger than the .7 membership finding): _default_unreflected -> _global_view -> all_pairs backs detect()'s EMPTY-PLAN branch (substrate_etl.py:1093) = every nx doctor forever, and chash_remap never shrinks (permanent retention). Swapping all_pairs to paged HTTP = ceil(map_size/1000) round trips on the highest-frequency read path for exactly the large-history installs this RDR serves. Design a probe-before-fetch short-circuit (vgtff pattern; e.g. cheap COUNT round trip vs last-known total, skip full scan when unchanged since last clean check) BEFORE wiring HttpRemapStore.all_pairs.
(2) OFFSET TORN-READ GUARD: paged reads span multiple autocommit txns (no snapshot, unlike SQLite fetchall). A row shifted past an offset boundary is SILENTLY missing -> unreflected under-reports (no-silent-fallback class). Wrap the full paged read in a before/after total-count reconcile (rollback_collections precedent, vector_etl.py:1728) treating mismatch as could-not-tell; OR name the existing per-tenant run lock that enforces run-sequential writes/reads, one or the other.
(3) LOCAL-FACTS SEED: pre-existing chash_remap.db rows need a one-time paged record_batch backfill to PG BEFORE reads move HTTP-only, else upgrading installs silently lose remap history. Explicit .6 design item.
Also noted: old_ids_for has zero callers (no HTTP counterpart needed); cascade+unreflected share ONE /pairs read shape (don't build two client paths); /entries returns array-of-objects -> HttpRemapStore rebuilds the dict shape; /source_collections array -> frozenset.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Design caution for input (1), from the orchestrator (2026-07-18): the probe-before-fetch marker must not become a cached VERDICT. unreflected = map JOIN local stores; a /count-based marker only tracks the MAP side. If a local store regresses (backup restore reintroduces old ids) while the map count is unchanged, a count-only skip stops the answer tracking the world — the Gap-4 both-directions property, one level up. Design the short-circuit key over BOTH sides (e.g. map total + local-store mtimes/row-counts), or scope the skip to the doctor read path with an explicit staleness bound, and pressure-test against test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached's philosophy before wiring. This is why (1) is a design input, not a mechanical swap.

title: substrate-etl NEVER converges across embedder eras: count-equality drop-test fails when target was independently indexed to a different count than the stale source (hard-fails nx upgrade, no --skip-t3 escape)
description:
SERIOUS RDR-185 defect, surfaced on Hal's live 6.12.0 service install 2026-07-17 (the one complex multi-era production install). After clearing the dead cloud leg, nx upgrade's substrate-etl rung re-plans and re-upserts ALREADY-MIGRATED collections on every run, re-billing Voyage.

ROOT CAUSE: drop_converged_legs (substrate_etl.py:587) decides converged by COUNT EQUALITY: source_count == target_count. Live example: source rdr__1-1__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1 has 3 distinct chunks (stale pre-migration remnant), target rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1 has 6712 (the real, current, independently-indexed data). 3 != 6712 -> NOT converged -> migrate -> upsert the 3 stale chunks -> etl_ports.py:261 post-write check 6712 != 3 -> etl_seam_count_mismatch -> leg FAILED -> runner maps to RungOutcome.FAILED (hard edge) -> 'nx upgrade did not converge', exit nonzero. FOREVER.

The count test is fundamentally unreliable across embedder-era re-chunking: minilm-384 and voyage-context-3 (CCE) chunk the same documents into DIFFERENT counts, so source and target counts legitimately differ (either direction). '==' is too strict; '>=' handles target>source but not re-chunk-shrink (target<source). Count comparison cannot prove convergence across a re-chunking migration — which is exactly substrate-etl's job. The docstring even flags 'CONTENT equivalence: NO' — the terminal-state mechanism (nexus-mapbc) is broken for real multi-era installs.

NO CLI WORKAROUND: --skip-t3 does NOT skip the ladder (upgrade.py _run_ladder called unconditionally at line 108, no skip_t3 param); it only gates engine-install/process-cycle. So the rung fires every run with no escape.

BLAST RADIUS (this incident): minimal/non-destructive. etl_ports.py writes-then-validates with NO rollback, so a few chash-keyed rows were upserted into 1-2 already-populated targets before the count check failed (idempotent if text matches; at worst a few stale rows in a 6712-row collection). taxonomy__centroids wrote 0 (GH #1390 chash-derivation guard held). No deletes, no replace, no ladder rung recorded. Install healthy on 6.12.0.

POPULATION: one (Hal — only service+multi-era-local-Chroma install). His actual install is FINE; only nx upgrade's exit code + Voyage re-bill are affected.

FIX NEEDS DESIGN (not mechanical): count-equality can't be the cross-era convergence test. Options to weigh in an RDR-185 follow-up: (a) per-collection already-migrated marker (persisted, authoritative, replaces count-guess); (b) service-mode recognizes an already-populated target + stale-remnant source as converged without the count dance; (c) chash-set overlap probe (heavier, but detect() runs on nx doctor's read path — the reason count-equality was chosen); (d) make the substrate-etl rung genuinely skippable for an already-migrated install. Related: the dead-cloud-leg bead (same rung, same install) and nexus-ixl85 (detect() sweep cost).

DO NOT re-run nx upgrade on Hal's install until fixed (re-bills Voyage + re-upserts each time).

The live-membership convergence fix (drop_converged_legs, a2c230f6) shipped in 6.13.0; the forever-fail count-equality class is gone (legacy path too, nexus-83ld0). title: [task] Era-hop cannot see the billed-consent path at all — a dummy NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY would gate the whole class
description:
Found by the substantive-critic in RDR-185 P5 r4. The cheapest possible gate for an entire defect class, and it is one environment variable.

THE GAP: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_era_hop.sh provisions `nx init --service --embedder bge-768` with NO Voyage key. So:
  * the seeded knowledge__rehearsal__voyage-context-3__v2 collection is CREDENTIAL-GATED (no key -> no leg at all),
  * the _MISLABEL collection remaps to a bge-768 target, so _leg_can_bill is False.
No billed leg is ever planned. The one E2E whose own header says "UNATTENDED is load-bearing: no TTY, no prompts, no --yes on anything" is pointed AWAY from the consent prompt that two commits (49533397, 7af092e9) turned on.

Consequence, demonstrated: r3 shipped a Critical (click.Abort escaping -> exit 1 with an empty reason on an unattended install) and r4 shipped another (SC-1's own pure-re-id shape deferring forever at exit 0). BOTH are invisible to the only test that asserts SC-1. Each was found by a reviewer, not by the gate that exists to catch exactly this.

THE FIX (nearly free): export a DUMMY NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY in the era-hop. voyage_key_present is a PRESENCE check, not a validity check (detection.voyage_key_available), so:
  * wired_models gains the voyage models,
  * the already-seeded voyage-context-3 collection stops being credential-gated,
  * carrying legacy ids, it plans a PURE RE-ID leg — needs_reembed False, vectors passed through.
No Voyage call is made on that path (passthrough carries the stored vectors), so no money is spent and the dummy key is never validated.

WHAT IT GATES: SC-1 + SC-2 together — an ancient voyage-keyed install reaching current UNATTENDED with zero re-embedding for pure id conformance. That is the RDR's flagship promise and it currently has no live test.

CAUTION (why this is its own bead, not a drive-by): adding the key changes what the hop exercises. The voyage collection stops being credential-gated and starts actually migrating, so the hop's counts/asserts shift and the service must accept a passthrough upsert into a voyage-declared target. That deserves its own verification cycle rather than being bolted onto a fix round that has already introduced four Criticals in four attempts.

Related: nexus-92vz5 (the billed predicate this would gate), nexus-k1m2f (the consent gate itself).
close_reason:
Done differently than filed (eb8edd73) — the premise was disproven, and that is recorded in the test's docstring so nobody re-derives it.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG: a dummy NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY cannot gate the era-hop. voyage_key_available's own docstring says the service wires voyage iff the key is set AT LAUNCH (Main.java:111). Key AFTER launch -> the planner believes voyage is wired while the bge-768 service serves only bge -> 422 on every remapped leg. Key BEFORE launch -> the service wires 'voyage' and any real re-embed calls Voyage with a fake key -> 401. The era-hop's minilm shapes must re-embed into voyage either way, so the consent-GRANTED path is NOT container-testable without real Voyage spend. And the DECLINED path (which IS testable, since a deferred walk stops before any embed call) does not converge — the one thing the era-hop exists to assert. They cannot share a leg.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: tests/upgrade/test_billed_consent_unattended.py — a real Service mode: the local SQLite/Chroma tiers are an immutable migration source — no local schema migration to run. subprocess with stdin CLOSED, isolated config dir, seeded billable footprint, dummy key. ~4s, no container, no service, no money. Runs in the NORMAL suite (not -m integration), so it is a live gate rather than a last line of defense.

FALSIFIED AGAINST BOTH SHIPPED CRITICALS: click.Abort escaping -> exit 1 (r3's Critical, caught); the deferral no longer naming --yes -> message assertion fails (r4's class, caught).

BUILDING IT FOUND FOUR REAL THINGS: (1) the walk never reached the substrate rung — t2-schema defers on an absent catalog and a deferred rung HALTS the walk; the non-vacuity pin caught it. (2) the fixture leaked the developer's real Chroma credentials via dict(os.environ) -> the cloud read leg dialled the live service. (3) the SEVENTH vacuous pin — '--yes' asserted anywhere in the output also matches the cost gate's structlog WARNING, so stripping it from the user-facing deferral left the test green. (4) the premise above.

STILL UNGATED (deliberately, and it needs money not cleverness): the consent-GRANTED path — --yes -> proceed -> a real billed re-embed. That needs a voyage-capable service. If it is ever wanted, a fake voyage-wired service is the only no-spend route.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CLOSURE CORRECTED (critic review of eb8edd73, 2026-07-17): my close reason overclaimed the intractability. It said 'the consent-GRANTED path needs money'. FALSE for the shape this bead actually named: SC-1+SC-2's voyage-named + legacy-ids collection plans a PURE RE-ID passthrough with a key present — target==source, needs_reembed False, billed False, NO Voyage call. I conflated 'the era-hop's minilm shapes need money to re-embed into voyage' (true) with 'the consent path needs money' (false for this shape).

WHAT NOW SHIPS (follow-up commit to c86d74e6): the subprocess gate covers all three directions the amended Constraint promises —
  * r3: billed + no TTY -> DEFERS honestly (exit 0, user-facing line, channel named)
  * r4: the FREE pure-re-id shape sails past the gate UNPROMPTED (this is the exact regression that deferred SC-1's install forever at exit 0; falsified by re-applying the r4 predicate — test goes red)
  * grant: NX_ASSUME_YES carries a billed walk past the gate (falsified by ignoring consent — red)

THE HONEST RESIDUAL, precisely bounded now: the fixture's service is an unreachable address by design, so the grant/free tests prove their walks reach the SERVICE BOUNDARY (which a deferred walk never dials) and stop. Full convergence-and-verify of a voyage-named passthrough still needs a live voyage-capable target. That — and only that — is what remains ungated.

Also per the critic: the 'era-hop confirms it live' claim in eb8edd73's message covered the mislabel fix's UNAFFECTED branch (the hop runs keyless, where old and new logic are identical). The keyed branch is plan-tested only (test_a_measured_768_mislabel_remaps_in_BOTH_modes), structurally: --era-hop/--with-cloud are incoherent per seed_legacy.py's own guard.

title: [bug] Credential-gated legacy collection vanishes from the rung: nx upgrade silently no-ops, doctor warns forever
description:
Found by BOTH reviewers on nexus-6or3m (RDR-185 P5), reproduced live. PRE-EXISTING; the j5diu rule violated for the case j5diu did not cover.

DEFECT: plan_substrate_legs (substrate_etl.py:150-155) drops a voyage-named legacy collection with no Voyage key via a bare 'continue  # credential gate territory, not a leg' — no log, no SourceGoneDecision, no surface. Its OWN neighbouring comment states the rule it breaks: 'A collection that cannot migrate must surface LOUD or as a decision, never vanish.' The nexus-j5diu fix covered only the measured-dim-override case.

REPRODUCED (voyage-named legacy collection, no key):
  plan_substrate_legs -> legs=0 decisions=0
  rung.detect()       -> applicable=True converged=True pending_detail=''
  => the ladder row reports NO PENDING RUNGS over a collection that cannot migrate.

Note is_measured_dim_override can never rescue it: legacy_ids suppresses should_probe_dim, so measured_dim is None for legacy collections, making the override always False. The 'upstream credential gate (C3)' the code comment defers to does not fire on the nx upgrade / rung path.

USER-VISIBLE SHAPE (one nx doctor run, post-6or3m):
  * upgrade-ladder row: clean, no pending rungs
  * chunk-id era row:   1 collection(s) hold pre-RDR-108 legacy chunk ids
  The user has era debt, the ladder says there is no work, and nothing anywhere names the missing input (a Voyage key, or a re-index). Forever. That is the impossible-remedy / stays-homework shape RDR-185 exists to end.

This is why nexus-6or3m's doctor row deliberately issues NO directive: an earlier draft said 'Run: nx upgrade', which provably no-ops here. Both reviewers flagged it; the row now carries a non-directive text pinned by test_doctor_census_row_never_directs_the_user_to_a_verb. That is a workaround at the message layer — THIS bead is the actual defect.

FIX DIRECTION (Hal's call): surface the credential gate as a genuine decision. RDR-185's 'consent only at genuine decisions' arguably covers 'supply the key vs re-embed into a wired model vs drop' — the same shape as the existing SourceGoneDecision (re-acquire vs drop). Minimum: it must not vanish.

Gap-5 census correctly reports these as outstanding debt today (converged_source_collections only ever certifies a collection the PLANNER planned and the TARGET answered for) — pinned by test_credential_gated_legacy_collection_is_never_reported_converged.
close_reason: Fixed (49533397). SubstratePlan.credential_gated + WARNING log + LegacyCollection.blocked_reason + a doctor remedy naming the key. Advisory, never blocking (Hal's call: a decision would block every healthy collection and hard-fail nx upgrade via VERIFY_FAILED). Root cause recorded: P4 demoted migrate_cmd / the dry-run preview, which carried the C3 gate this skip deferred to.

title: [bug] Two legacy collections can remap onto ONE target: silent merge + wrong convergence in both directions
description:
Found by code review of nexus-6or3m (RDR-185 P5), reproduced live. PRE-EXISTING in the substrate rung; the Gap-5 census newly inherits it.

DEFECT: cross_model_target_name SYNTHESIZES for 2-segment names and SWAPS for 4-segment names, so two distinct legacy collections can produce the SAME target_collection. plan_substrate_legs has no duplicate-target guard.

  knowledge__old                        -> knowledge__old__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1
  knowledge__old__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1  -> knowledge__old__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1

REPRODUCED (converged_source_collections + plan_substrate_legs, voyage_key_present=False):
  * COLLISION: True — two legs, one target.
  * Partial migration (target holds 12): BOTH collections read as converged (each leg's want=12 matches the one migrated leg's got=12). Real debt silently erased from the census — the only surface that shows it.
  * Both migrated (target holds 24): NEITHER reads as converged (want=12 != got=24). nexus-6or3m recurs verbatim on this shape, fix or no fix.

WORSE THAN THE READING: the ETL itself would write BOTH sources into ONE target collection — a silent merge of two distinct collections' content. That is data corruption, not a census nit. drop_converged_legs' reachability argument (substrate_etl.py:389-392, 'targets are content-type+owner+model scoped so an accidental full-count collision from unrelated content is not a reachable shape') does NOT cover this: the content is RELATED — same content_type and owner, differing only in segment count.

REACHABILITY: needs a pre-RDR-103 (2-segment) and a pre-RDR-109 (4-segment minilm) collection with the same content_type+owner in one store. That is precisely the ancient-install shape GH #1408 describes and the era-hop exists to model. The era-hop does not currently seed a colliding pair.

FIX DIRECTION (Hal's call — this is a design fork, do not pick silently): plan_substrate_legs must refuse a plan with two legs sharing a target_collection, or surface it as a genuine decision. Per the standing directive, a data-correctness problem FAILS LOUD; it must not silently merge. Weigh against: raising in the planner makes detect()/nx doctor raise on such an install (health catches, but the rung would too).

ALSO: add a colliding pair to the era-hop's seed, or the fix has no live gate.

Bead nexus-6or3m is NOT blocked on this: its own reading is correct for every non-colliding shape, and this shape is already broken in the rung today.
close_reason: Fixed (49533397). plan_substrate_legs raises SubstrateTargetCollision on two DISTINCT sources sharing a target, naming both and the target. Keyed on distinct sources: the first draft used the raw list and bricked nx upgrade on any install whose collection classified once per read leg. pending_rungs now degrades per rung so a refusing detect() cannot print a green doctor row.

title: substrate rung detect() cost never amortizes: a full classification sweep on every nx doctor, forever
description:
P4.R1 Finding 1 (Medium-High), from the code-review-expert harvest 2026-07-16. The N+1 HTTP half is FIXED (see below); this bead is the residual DESIGN question, which is Hal's call because the reviewer's suggested fix contradicts a property the critic and the Gap-4 suite just pinned.

THE COST: SubstrateEtlRung._plan() short-circuits only on _chroma_footprint_present() — a bare directory-existence check on the legacy Chroma dir. RDR-176 guarantees that directory is NEVER deleted (it is the rollback target), so the gate is True permanently. LadderRunner._run_rung calls rung.detect() unconditionally BEFORE consulting store.verified_rungs() — deliberately: the runner is level-triggered ('every run re-detects from actual state'). For this rung detect() is not cheap: _classify() walks every legacy collection with per-collection dimension probing. So every nx doctor, for the life of the install, pays a full classification sweep to re-confirm 'yes, still converged'. Same shape as the index-perf arc's nexus-vgtff (300s -> 0.6s by probing before fetching).

ALREADY FIXED (commit pending): the N+1 network half. _default_target_counts() now answers every count from ONE list_collections() /stats round trip instead of count() per leg — on the 18-collection GH #1408 shape that was 18 sequential HTTP requests per doctor run. Only the classification sweep remains.

WHY NOT JUST CACHE IT (the reviewer's suggested fix (a)/(b)): both proposals make detect() consult the CompletionStore and skip the body when the rung is already recorded. That directly contradicts what P4.R2 Finding 4 established and what tests/upgrade/test_gap4_two_mechanisms.py::test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached now PINS: a rung's convergence answer must be re-derived from the live world, in BOTH directions. A completion-record fast-path means a rollback (target dropped, service re-provisioned, collection deleted) is never re-detected — the rung would report converged forever off a stale record, which is the marker-file-as-authority shape Gap-4 bans and the exact class the level-triggered design exists to survive. Fixing the cost by caching the verdict trades a perf problem for a correctness one.

SO THE REAL QUESTION: how do you make a level-triggered detect() cheap without making it stateful? Candidates worth weighing — (a) a cheaper applicability gate than 'the Chroma dir exists' (e.g. cheapest-possible source fingerprint: dir mtime + collection count, still live-derived, no verdict stored); (b) a process-local memo (per-invocation, not persisted — doctor calls detect once anyway, so this buys little); (c) accept the cost and bound it (classification is already memoized per-process via detect_pending_migration_memoized); (d) revisit once RDR-155 P4b deletes the Chroma read path, at which point the footprint gate goes permanently False and the whole cost disappears — this rung and its cost RETIRE with P4b by construction.

(d) is worth weighing first: this may be a cost with a known expiry date rather than a thing to engineer around.

Measure before designing: nobody has timed detect() on an 18-collection install. The era-hop's box is 5 collections.
close_reason:
MEASURED, no code change (Hal's call, 2026-07-20).

Full classification sweep on the real 15-collection legacy Chroma footprint: median 3.3 ms, per-collection 0.2 ms, 5 of 15 data-bearing so only 5 reach the dim probe. The bead framed this as the vgtff shape, but vgtff was 300 SECONDS and this is 3 MILLISECONDS.

Resolution (c) accept and bound, with (d) noted: the cost retires with RDR-155 P4b by construction when the footprint gate goes permanently False. Candidates (a) and (b) are explicitly NOT taken — both make detect() consult stored state and would contradict test_gap4_two_mechanisms.py::test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached, trading a 3ms perf non-issue for the marker-file-as-authority correctness class.

Scope limit recorded on the bead comment: measured on a LOCAL PersistentClient leg. A cloud legacy leg makes each data-bearing collection's probe a network round trip (5 here, not 15); the larger N+1 network half was already fixed. Re-measure there before reopening on a cloud-leg report.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RDR-185 P5 (nexus-6or3m) note — detect() now has a SECOND, structurally different call site.

The Gap-5 census (upgrade_ladder/census.py _default_converged) now reuses _default_target_counts to answer 'is this collection's debt outstanding'. Two consequences for this bead:

1. The cost shape is duplicated. RDR-176 keeps the Chroma dir forever, so on a fully CONVERGED install _chroma_footprint_present() stays true forever, the legacy classification stays non-empty forever, and the census probes on every nx doctor forever — always to answer 'all converged, print nothing'. Same non-amortizing shape this bead names, at a second site.

2. THE LIKELY FIX FOR THIS BEAD WILL NOT FIX THE CENSUS. A CompletionStore fast-path in detect() cannot be reused here: the census deliberately bypasses completion records to remain a Gap-5 DETECTOR (a persisted 'converged' verdict is the Gap-4 banned third mechanism, and pinned against by test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached). Whatever amortization lands must be evaluated against both call sites or the census keeps paying.

Partially mitigated already: the census now short-circuits BEFORE probing when (a) no legacy debt exists at all, and (b) no service is provisioned (census._no_target_provisioned). Neither helps the converged-install case, which is this bead's core.

Surfaced by the substantive-critic during the 6or3m review.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RDR-185 CLOSE disposition (2026-07-17): SURVIVES the close as standalone work — deliberately NOT closed with the RDR and NOT mooted by the voyage-keyed-migration decree. The cost lands on every LOCAL install that upgraded (a real, growing population, including the operator's own): RDR-176 keeps the Chroma dir forever, so _chroma_footprint_present() stays true forever and detect()'s classification sweep + the census's convergence probe run on every nx doctor, always answering 'converged, nothing to say'.

NATURAL RETIREMENT: RDR-155 P4b deletes the migration module + chroma read client, which makes the rung N/A and this cost vanish wholesale. So the real decision is only whether any release ships BETWEEN now and P4b to users with big footprints for whom doctor sluggishness matters. If P4b lands next, this bead closes unfixed with it. Two call sites now (rung detect + census _default_progress; noted 2026-07-16) — any interim fix must cover both, and the obvious CompletionStore fast-path CONTRADICTS the Gap-4 live-derivation invariant (pinned by test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached). Do not fix casually.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-07-20 (the bead's own 'measure before designing' precondition).

Method: classify_collections against a COPY of the real legacy Chroma footprint at ~/.config/nexus/chroma (copied to scratchpad; the live dir was never opened). 15 collections — close to the 18-collection GH #1408 shape the bead cites. 5 runs, fresh PersistentClient each.

RESULT: median 3.3 ms for the FULL classification sweep. min/max 3.1/17.9 ms. Per-collection 0.2 ms. Of 15 collections only 5 are data-bearing, so only 5 reach the dimension probe at all.

This dissolves the design question rather than answering it. The bead framed the cost as 'same shape as the index-perf arc's nexus-vgtff (300s -> 0.6s)' — but vgtff was 300 SECONDS and this is 3 MILLISECONDS. There is no cost here worth trading correctness for, which is what candidates (a) and (b) would have done: both make detect() consult stored state and would contradict test_gap4_two_mechanisms.py::test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached.

RECOMMENDATION: (c) accept and bound, with (d) noted — the cost retires with RDR-155 P4b by construction when the footprint gate goes permanently False. No code change.

SCOPE LIMIT, stated rather than glossed: this measures a LOCAL PersistentClient leg. A CLOUD legacy read leg would make each data-bearing collection's dim probe a network round trip (5 here, not 15 — empty collections short-circuit). That is bounded and small, and the N+1 HTTP half the bead describes as ALREADY FIXED was the larger network cost. If someone later reports doctor slowness on a cloud-leg install, re-measure there before reopening; do not assume this local number covers it.

title: Gap-5 legacy-id census still reports era debt after a verified migration (same immutable-source class as nexus-mapbc)
description:
Surfaced by the PASSING RDR-185 P4.3 era-hop run 2026-07-16 (run 5, exit 0).

SYMPTOM: on a fully converged install — substrate rung 'converged and verified', all collections at parity, all legacy ids re-id'd, doctor reporting '✓ Upgrade ladder: no pending rungs' — nx doctor ALSO prints:

  ⚠ Chunk-id era (upgrade ladder): 2 collection(s) hold pre-RDR-108 legacy chunk ids — pending upgrade-ladder debt: knowledge__rehearsal-era__... (12 chunks, local), knowledge__rehearsal-era-note__... (12 chunks, local)

The debt is GONE. Those collections were converged on the wire; pgvector holds only conformant 32-char chashes (the hop asserts it). The warning is false.

ROOT CAUSE: the SAME class as nexus-mapbc, third instance. legacy_id_census() (upgrade_ladder/census.py) gates on _chroma_footprint_present() and then reads the SOURCE via detect_pending_migration_memoized(). RDR-176 keeps that source byte-untouched forever as the rollback target, and it legitimately still holds its original legacy ids (the hop asserts THAT too — immutable source). So a source-derived census reports era debt forever after migration.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the RDR's Gap-5 surface. Its promise is 'era debt is visible the day it exists, not on migration day'. Post-migration it inverts into 'era debt is visible forever, including when it does not exist' — the same 'stays homework' failure RDR-185 exists to end, just in a different surface. A user who did everything right is told they still owe work.

NOT caught by the hop's asserts: the leg asserts on 'pending upgrade rung' (now correctly clean). It does not assert the census line. Consider adding that assertion with the fix — but only once the fix lands, or the leg goes red.

LIKELY FIX (same primitive as mapbc): a collection whose target already holds the source's full row count is not era debt. Either reuse drop_converged_legs' target-count probe, or have the census consult the rung's plan (which now filters converged legs) instead of re-deriving from the source. Prefer reuse — three independent re-derivations of 'is this converged?' is exactly the drift that produced mapbc and j5diu.

COST NOTE: this puts target counts on nx doctor's census path. Weigh against the census's cheap file-level gate design (its docstring is explicit that it never opens a store on non-Chroma installs).

REPRO: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --era-hop, read the doctor section of a PASSING run.
close_reason: Fixed + era-hop verified live (49533397). Census asks the TARGET via source_progress, reusing plan_substrate_legs + drop_converged_legs rather than a third convergence derivation. Era-hop: the false warning is gone, replaced by 'no outstanding legacy chunk-id debt', with a non-vacuity gate. Full suite 13772.

title: Verify the managed-migration leg converges under nx upgrade alone (config service_url -> walk)
description:
RDR-185 P4.2 (nexus-n7u38.29) rewrote docs/managed-onboarding.md to claim the managed journey is:

  nx config set service_url https://api.conexus-nexus.com
  export NX_SERVICE_TOKEN=<token>
  nx upgrade

The claim follows from the DESIGN, not from a test: upgrade_ladder/preconditions.py _default_provisioned() returns True when a service_url credential is configured, so the provisioning precondition is satisfied and the substrate rung's _default_migrate() resolves its target via make_t3(), which routes to the configured endpoint. That chain is read from the code, never exercised end-to-end.

It replaced 'nx guided-upgrade --service-url URL', which ALSO health-gated and version-pinned the managed endpoint before migrating. nx upgrade has no --service-url flag (and should not grow one: naming your service is configuration, not upgrade ceremony). Open question this bead answers: does the health-gate + version-pin still happen on the managed path? The engine-floor check is believed to ride the http client (the same engine-floor-checked client every cloud-mode caller uses), but 'believed' is the problem.

Not covered by nexus-n7u38.30: that rehearsal is a LOCAL era-spanning hop. The managed leg has no gate.

Acceptance: an integration/e2e leg drives config-service_url -> nx upgrade against a managed-shaped endpoint and asserts (a) the substrate rung migrates into it, (b) a not-ready or below-floor endpoint fails loud BEFORE any write (the guided-upgrade guarantee must not have been silently dropped), (c) docs/managed-onboarding.md's stated sequence is what the test runs. If (b) does not hold, that is a defect to fix, not a doc to soften.
close_reason:
MOOTED by Hal's decision, 2026-07-17, completing the voyage-keyed-migration population sweep (bmiq9, 92vz5, byosf, kpjk1, iz7zo, dpthy, an5cd, gggzn, 25l8q, ltp3k, icucl, oabh4): the managed-migration journey has no population. Managed-cloud users are GREENFIELD-ONLY — operator-provisioned tenants who index fresh against the endpoint; nobody with an existing local Chroma store migrates data INTO managed. The one data migration into the managed cloud that ever happened was Hal's own, completed 2026-06.

WHAT THIS BEAD WAS: the RDR-185 P4 gate recorded the 'applies across local, service, and managed-cloud modes' Success Criterion as managed-cloud UNVERIFIED — the docs' claimed journey (nx config set service_url -> nx upgrade) was design-derived from preconditions.py and never exercised, and the open question was whether the guided-upgrade health-gate/version-pin survived the demotion. The source-read answer (recorded in T2 nexus_rdr/185-p5-51djh-managed-gate-finding, never live-verified): the guarantee MOVED to the http client's one-time cloud probe (get_http_vector_client hard-fails below-floor/unreachable before any write), it did not vanish. That finding stays on record; with zero population it needs no test.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RDR-185's close: the 'managed-cloud mode' half of the applies-across-modes criterion is RESOLVED BY SCOPE REDUCTION, not by verification — managed-cloud MIGRATION is out of the product's supported surface by decree. Managed-cloud SERVING (greenfield tenants) is unaffected and remains covered by its own gates. The close writeup states this as a decree-scoped criterion, not a proven one.

DOC CONSEQUENCE (cleansed in the same commit): managed-onboarding.md's 'Migrating an existing local install to the managed service' section is retired — the managed journey is greenfield onboarding only.

title: P4.0b Service provisioning as a precondition leg (the guided-upgrade stage-2 job)
description:
SCOPE DISCOVERY at the P3 gate (nexus_rdr/185-phase3-gate), filed rather than folded. guided_upgrade_cmd is four stages: preflight detect -> cost consent -> PROVISION+VERIFY the service stack -> run T2+T3 migration. P3's precondition axes cover package/engine/process-FRESHNESS (cycle a stale supervisor) but NOT ACQUISITION of a service that does not exist yet — provision_and_serve / init.provision_and_start_service.

Without this, nx upgrade on a Chroma-only install has no target to migrate INTO, so the RDR Success Criterion 'fresh-or-ancient converges via nx upgrade alone' fails and .28 cannot demote guided-upgrade honestly.

Scope: extend the precondition axis set with provisioning (stateless verdict from on-disk evidence — pg_credentials presence + readiness, the legacy_footprint_pending shape), converge = the existing provision_and_serve path, consent = the existing gates (cost preview stays a genuine decision; provisioning an empty footprint must still no-op per nexus-ltix8). Keep the RDR-176 immutable-source discipline. BLOCKS .28's guided-upgrade demotion. Parent epic nexus-n7u38.
close_reason: Provisioning precondition shipped (3e693ec1 + b52cbfee): on-disk verdict (pg_credentials/service_url + census footprint gate), re-derived per call, never recorded; N/A on a fresh empty footprint (nexus-ltix8 no-op pinned — an empty footprint never provisions); converge reuses establish_verified_service verbatim (provision->health->version-pin->discoverability), reports not-ready honestly with the reason (no silent fallback — the walk then finds no verified target and the substrate rung stays pending); ordered before the process axis; --skip-t3 suppresses while still reporting; failures reported not raised. 11 axis tests + autouse live-probe isolation (same hazard class the P3 review caught for the process axis). 235 ladder tests green. Unblocks .28's guided-upgrade demotion.

title: nx-mcp startup lifespan crashes whole server when storage service unresolvable (GH #1405 SH 2026-07-16)
description:
Field report stevengharris GH #1405 comment 4994648235 (conexus 6.9.0, macOS): nx-mcp startup lifespan (_t1_chroma_lifespan -> mint_t1_session_token -> HttpTokenStore.__init__ -> resolve_service_endpoint) hard-requires the storage service at process start. Service not yet up (or ownership-churn respawn gap) -> RuntimeError escapes the stdio server TaskGroup -> mcp_server_crashed. Claude Code then caches the dead connection (~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json gains plugin:conexus:nexus) and never retries: ALL nexus-server tools unavailable for the session's whole lifetime, even after nx daemon service start mid-session. nx-mcp-catalog (no startup dependency) started fine both times.

Fix direction (Steve's option 3, aligns with RDR-185 preconditions contract: never hard-block on a network probe of a possibly-down process): do NOT block MCP server start on T1 token minting — mint lazily on first T1-touching tool call, degrade per-call while unavailable. Retry/backoff-at-startup (option 1) is weaker: any bounded budget still crashes the session that starts before the service. Note nexus-bgh2j (construction-time evidence gate for HttpTokenStore) is the same code path but does NOT cover this: its cold-start instant-fail-loud would still crash the server at startup — the startup surface needs the lazy/degrade treatment regardless. RDR-183 evidence family (defect-3 lineage).
close_reason:
Fixed (commit 80f914a5), full stacked review completed pre-push. The lifespan DEFERS a failed T1 mint instead of raising: server starts, non-T1 tools serve immediately, T1 mints lazily on first use via the mcp_infra.set_t1_pre_init_hook seam (before construction — Phase E and the CLI-dedicated isolation boundary intact), per-call actionable errors while the service is down, genuine self-heal on service arrival (resolve_service_endpoint caches no negative — verified). Shutdown sentinel closes the mid-mint teardown race. code-review-expert APPROVED (0C/0I; chokepoint audit: hook unbypassable); substantive-critic 0C/2S, both fixed (honest blast-radius wording naming nexus-5t1jp; tool-boundary + log-severity pins one frame up). Eight falsifications each red on the named test; full suite 13794/0.

Steve's user story: server no longer crashes, so Claude Code's needs-auth-cache never captures a dead connection; scratch degrades to an actionable string until nx daemon service start, then heals on the next call. The RDR-183 defect-3 lineage note stands — the ownership-churn respawn gap that CAUSED the service to be briefly down is 183's problem; this bead ends the crash that turned that gap into a whole-session outage.

Follow-ups filed/updated: nexus-5t1jp (cloud-mode T3 probe cached forever — the same disease one layer down, live serving path, NOT mooted); nexus-bgh2j annotated (its startup-crash surface is mooted by this boundary catch; evidence-gate semantics retain value).

title: P4.V Test validation (test-validator) - Phase 4
description: Validate full suite + rehearsal before declaring the epic done: uv run pytest && uv run pytest -m integration && tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh (era-spanning hop) + tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh. Full suite before any tag (release directive).
close_reason:
Test validation harvested (T2 nexus_rdr/185-p4-validation). Verdict PASS-WITH-GAPS. All gaps fixed, commit 733f7d04; era-hop green run 7 (exit 0), full suite 13718 passed / 0 failed.

FINDING A (CRITICAL, new, unfiled, and BOTH stacked reviewers signed off on the broken fix): the P4.R2 cascade-repair was architecturally unreachable. title: RDR-185: Single-Ladder Convergent Upgrade
description:
Collapse the accreted upgrade command-graph into ONE ordered migration ladder. Upgrade = update code; when newer code meets older data, migrate it. All DATA transitions (T2 schema, T3 substrate, chunk identity, embedder era, hooks/config) become rungs keyed by ONE ladder-position DERIVED from per-rung completion records; each rung detect->converge->verify, idempotent, resumable, immutable-source (rollback consults the persisted old->new id map where a rung rewrote identity). Package/engine acquisition + process freshness/provisioning are STATELESS preconditions re-derived live from ON-DISK state each invocation. nx doctor reports pending rungs read-only; nx upgrade (+SessionStart --auto) is the single trigger; every other upgrade verb demoted/deleted. RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-185-single-ladder-convergent-upgrade.md (accepted, gate PASSED r3). Subsumes nexus-8jlsl + GH #1408; wire-re-id remap machinery is a SUBSET of RDR-180's future 16->32-byte prerequisite (not built here). 5 phases P0-P4. Plan: T2 nexus/plan-rdr-185.md.

## Context
Success Criteria (RDR): fresh-or-ancient install converges with nx upgrade alone (2026-07-16 work-instance shape: pre-RDR-108 ids + store_put-only + Chroma -> current UNATTENDED); zero re-embed / zero source-file for id-scheme conformance (wire re-id, Chroma source untouched); nx doctor shows pending rungs; upgrade docs one paragraph; migration-rehearsal drives ONLY nx upgrade across era-spanning hop; no rung records complete without its verify (RDR-142 class pinned by test); Gap-4 falsifiable (exactly two answer mechanisms by class, no third authority); Gap-5 falsifiable (doctor reports legacy-id collections on Chroma-mode from the detector's release).
close_reason: RDR-185 CLOSED as implemented, 2026-07-17. All phases P0-P5 complete: P0 ladder substrate, P1 t2-schema rung + census, P2 remap machinery (etl_ports/wire_reid/cascade), P3 preconditions, P4 ceremony demotion + era-hop (gate PASSED, T2 nexus_rdr/185-phase4-gate), P5 the Gap-5 census fix + consent-gate arc (12 commits 49533397..a881cadc, record T2 nexus_rdr/185-p5-DONE). Both unmet Success Criteria from the P4 gate resolved: Gap-5 proven live (nexus-6or3m); managed-cloud resolved by scope reduction (nexus-51djh mooted by decree — managed onboarding is greenfield-only). SC-1+SC-2 proven over the entire supported origin set. Survivors, dispositioned on-bead: nexus-ixl85 (retires naturally at RDR-155 P4b), nexus-d8mts, nexus-z5j0t (P2 residuals). Post-mortem: docs/rdr/post-mortem/185-single-ladder-convergent-upgrade.md.

description: RDR-183 research finding 2 (nexus_rdr/183-research-2, hypothesis-refuting): nx upgrade --auto (SessionStart hook, matcher startup|resume|clear|compact) reaches _cycle_storage_service_to_current in its finally block, which unconditionally stop+starts any live storage-service supervisor. The T2 sibling delegates to version-aware ensure-running; the T3/service cycler forgot the gate. Fix: compare the discovered lease's version (published from importlib.metadata version('conexus') at supervisor start, storage_service_daemon.py:707) against the installed version; skip cycling when equal; empty/legacy version or mismatch still cycles (fail toward cycling — upgrade correctness preserved). Injectable seam consistent with existing _discover_fn/_run_fn/_nx_bin_fn. This is RDR-183 candidate 0 — independently shippable defect fix; the topology decision (candidates 1-3) remains draft.

title: doctor.py tier-discipline service-mode real-counts unreachable when local memory.db absent
design:
Root cause: _run_check_tier_discipline (src/nexus/commands/doctor.py) checks
`db_path.exists()` for the LOCAL SQLite T2 file BEFORE checking
storage_backend_for("telemetry") == SERVICE. Since RDR-152, `service` is the
hard default backend — a fresh/typical service-mode install may never create
the local memory.db file, so the check hits the pre-existing "T2 database not
found ... (skip)" branch and returns WITHOUT EVER reaching the new
nexus-59wjj real-counts code (lines ~894-926), regardless of whether the
engine has the tier_writes/query route.

Verified empirically (2026-07-16, substantive-critique of the uncommitted
observability batch): with NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service, NX_SESSION_ID set,
HttpTelemetryStore mocked to return real rows, and default_db_path() pointed
at a nonexistent path, _run_check_tier_discipline() prints "T2 database not
found ... (skip)" and never calls HttpTelemetryStore at all.

sibling tier_status.py does NOT have this bug: its service_mode branch is
checked and returned BEFORE the db_path existence check, so it correctly
reaches HttpTelemetryStore in the same scenario.

No existing test catches this: the only service-mode doctor test
(test_doctor_tier_discipline_service_mode in tests/test_tier_status_cli.py)
calls db.touch() to force the file to exist, masking the ordering hazard.
No new test was added for doctor's real-counts path at all.

Fix: reorder _run_check_tier_discipline to check storage_backend_for(...)
== SERVICE before (or independent of) the local db_path.exists() check,
mirroring tier_status.py's already-correct order. Add a test with
NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service + a nonexistent local db path + a mocked
HttpTelemetryStore returning real rows, asserting the real-counts path
(not the "T2 database not found" bail-out) is reached.
close_reason: Fixed in the same pre-commit pass that the critique reviewed: SERVICE check moved before the local db_path.exists() gate in _run_check_tier_discipline; regression test test_doctor_service_mode_real_counts_without_local_db (nonexistent db + mocked store -> real counts) added.

title: taxonomy discover (service mode): get_embeddings posts ALL ids in one request — deterministic 504 on large collections (28k chunks)
description:
Found during 6.10.2 post-release shakeout (2026-07-15), first index refresh in 19 days.

REPRO: nx index repo . (or nx taxonomy discover -c code__1-1__voyage-code-3__v1) in service mode against api.conexus-nexus.com. Taxonomy discovery for code__1-1__voyage-code-3__v1 (28,164 chunks) fails: POST /v1/vectors/get-embeddings -> HTTP 504 through the full gateway-retry ladder (2s/5s/10s). Reproduced twice — once during index-run load, once on an idle service — deterministic, not transient. docs__1-1 (4,655) and rdr__1-1 (6,703) succeed.

ROOT CAUSE: taxonomy_cmd.py _fetch_service_vectors pages the chunk-text fetch at 250/page (service quota-aware), but then calls t3.get_embeddings(collection_name, ids) with the ENTIRE id list. http_vector_client.py get_embeddings (~line 1417) sends one unbatched POST; the JSON response for 28k x 1024-dim float vectors is O(hundreds of MB) and cannot complete inside the gateway timeout. Collection size crossed the viability threshold somewhere between ~7k and 28k chunks.

FIX SHAPE: batch get_embeddings client-side (e.g. 250-300 ids/call, mirroring the MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE pattern used by ids_for_source directly below it), concatenating rows in request order to preserve the positional-alignment contract (nexus-7ydks S2 tripwire: len(embeddings)==len(ids) check must still hold across the concat). Alternatively a server-side pagination param on /v1/vectors/get-embeddings — but client batching needs no engine cut.

IMPACT: taxonomy refresh permanently broken for any large collection in service mode; code__1-1 topics are now stale (last successful discover predates this run). Search itself unaffected; topic-scoped search / taxonomy boost run on stale labels.
close_reason: Shipped ad298350 + live-verified twice: (1) uv run nx taxonomy discover fetched all 28,164 embeddings that previously deterministic-504'd; (2) norm-census refetch survived a mid-fetch transient 504 via the per-batch retry ladder. Stacked review clean (expert approved; critic justified/high-confidence, non-vacuity verified against pre-fix source). Follow-up filed for checkpoint/resume + progress feedback.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
START-payload determination: Empirically verified via cc-validation probe (new scenario tests/cc-validation/scenarios/27_subagent_start_payload.sh, 3/3 pass, live claude sessions on macOS keychain auth). Ran 3 dispatch shapes, each logging FULL raw stdin of SubagentStart + SessionStart.

SubagentStart payload FIELD SET (identical across ALL three shapes): session_id, transcript_path, cwd, prompt_id, agent_id, agent_type, hook_event_name. 7 fields. (SubagentStop by contrast has 11: adds permission_mode, effort, stop_hook_active, agent_transcript_path.) SubagentStart does NOT carry: name, permission_mode, effort, agent_transcript_path, stop_hook_active, nor any background flag.

Observed values:
- 27a sync Task (unnamed): agent_id=aa0ea686105206f0b, agent_type=general-purpose, prompt_id=7bb89655..., session_id=SPAWNER session.
- 27b background NAMED (name=startprobeB): agent_id=astartprobeB-6f59dab8bbb14864, agent_type=startprobeB, session_id=SPAWNER session.
- 27c background UNNAMED: agent_id=a16b397f79df79c42, agent_type=general-purpose, session_id=SPAWNER session.

ANSWERS:
1. name present? NO dedicated field. Name is INDIRECTLY encoded: a named agent's agent_type becomes the NAME (startprobeB, not general-purpose) and agent_id = "a<name>-<hash>"; an unnamed agent has agent_type=<subagent_type> and agent_id="a<hash>" (no dash). So named-vs-unnamed IS discriminable, but only via agent_id/agent_type morphology, not a clean field — and naming COSTS you the real subagent_type.
2. background-ness discriminable between sync vs background? NO. 27a (sync unnamed) and 27c (background unnamed) are byte-shape identical: same 7 fields, agent_type=general-purpose, agent_id="a<hash>", session_id=SPAWNER. Nothing distinguishes a background teammate from a sync Task dispatch. Crucially the background teammate fires SubagentStart in the SPAWNER's session (session_id + transcript_path = spawner's), NOT a separate session; there is NO separate teammate SessionStart (the lone SessionStart per leg is source=startup, the main session's own launch).
3. agent_id present at START? YES, all three shapes. START also carries prompt_id. Both are the same field names present at SubagentStop, so either is a viable START->STOP join key for an expectations file.
4. hook that did NOT fire? None missing. SubagentStart fired 3/3. Background teammate did NOT emit its own SessionStart. (No Stop/SubagentStop hooks were configured in this probe.)

DESIGN IMPLICATION for .7: The SubagentStart payload CANNOT key the consult/owes-report rule on background-ness — no field exposes it, and name-presence is not a reliable proxy (27c proves background can be unnamed; a sync dispatch could be named). Therefore the orchestrator write-BEFORE-dispatch is the REQUIRED (primary, load-bearing) path, confirming Assumption (b). The SubagentStart hook's only value-add is that it CAN stamp/backfill agent_id + prompt_id at start time (both present) keyed to the spawner session — useful as a cross-check or to capture the framework-assigned agent_id, but it cannot DECIDE background-ness. Net: keep the ground-truth discriminator in the orchestrator-written expectations file; do not rely on a Start-hook stamp to classify background vs sync.

Durable evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/scenario27_run.log (TEST_HOME auto-deleted on runner exit; payloads dumped to stdout survive there). Probe file left untracked, not committed.

title: MCP client: re-resolve lease + retry once on unresolvable-endpoint (GH #1405 defect 1 mitigation)
description: GH #1405 (6.10.1 shakeout): storage-service ownership churn creates 5-10s windows where the lease points at a dead endpoint (old supervisor TERM'd at session teardown, new one publishing on a NEW port). MCP tool calls landing in the window hard-fail with 'nexus-service endpoint is not resolvable' and never retry or re-resolve — observed: a parallel batch (search + store_get + memory_delete) all failed at 19:48:1xZ seconds after a successful store_put; every call succeeded on manual retry once the new lease published at 19:48:22Z. FIX (mitigation, not the root topology fix — that is the ownership RDR): on unresolvable-endpoint (and connect-refused against a lease-resolved local endpoint), re-resolve the lease ONCE and retry ONCE with a short bounded wait for lease publication (the observed gap is 5-10s; budget ~12s max, loud log line when the retry path fires). Applies to the local-lease resolution path only — never the managed-cloud URL. Must not stack with existing retry wrappers into unbounded totals (see nexus-by875 — coordinate budgets). Tests: fake lease flip mid-call → retry succeeds; lease never republishes → original error surfaces within the bounded budget; cloud path untouched.
