title: Extend event-sourced Catalog update() to persist bib_* columns
description:
Deferred from nexus-9l2lg (surface bib metadata on catalog Document rows). Under NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=1, _WriteOps.update()'s event-sourced branch (catalog_writes.py L536-547) cannot persist bib_* columns: DocumentRegisteredPayload (events.py L238-276) has no bib_* fields, and Projector._v0_document_registered (projector.py L220-276) intentionally omits bib_* from its INSERT/ON CONFLICT SET clause.

Naively adding bib_* to the payload + projector SET clause would introduce a NEW clobber bug: three other _DocumentRegisteredPayload emission sites read rows WITHOUT their bib_* columns and would silently reset bib_* to 0/"" on replay -- rename_collection (catalog_writes.py L604-731, two emission sites) and _update_document_collection_locked (catalog_writes.py L91-175, used by update_document_collection + update_documents_collection_batch).

Correct fix: audit all 4 _DocumentRegisteredPayload emission sites for existing documents, extend their SELECTs to carry forward current bib_* values (mirroring how source_mtime/source_uri/alias_of are already preserved across rename_collection), THEN extend DocumentRegisteredPayload with 8 bib_* fields and the projector's INSERT/SET clause to write them from the payload.

Regression pin already in place: tests/test_catalog_event_sourced_mutators.py::TestUpdateEventSourced::test_event_sourced_update_bib_kwargs_do_not_crash_but_do_not_persist documents the current deferred behavior (bib kwargs accepted, silently not persisted under event-sourced mode).

Not currently blocking: NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED is opt-in, Phase 3 beta, not the default path.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-15, same arc as nexus-9l2lg.

STALE PREMISE CORRECTED: this bead's original description said "Not currently
blocking: NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED is opt-in, Phase 3 beta, not the default path."
That was FALSE at the time of writing -- _read_event_sourced_gate() (catalog.py)
has defaulted to ON since RDR-101 Phase 3 PR zeta, confirmed via direct code
read (unset env -> True) and confirmed tests/conftest.py has no override. This
bug was therefore live for the DEFAULT local-catalog write path, not an
opt-in edge case -- which is why Hal escalated this bead to P1 same-arc rather
than leaving it deferred.

FIX: all 4 DocumentRegisteredPayload emission sites for EXISTING documents now
carry the row's current bib_* values forward into the payload (mirroring the
existing source_mtime/source_uri/alias_of carry-forward pattern):
  - _WriteOps.update() (catalog_writes.py) -- sources from rec_dict, which
    nexus-9l2lg Task 2 already seeds from entry.bib_* / caller kwargs.
  - _WriteOps.rename_collection() -- both the per-row event-sourced loop and
    the shadow-emit loop; SELECT widened to include all 8 bib_* columns.
  - _WriteOps._update_document_collection_locked() (backs
    update_document_collection + update_documents_collection_batch) -- SELECT
    widened, payload + rec dict extended.
DocumentRegisteredPayload (events.py) gained 8 bib_* fields (defaults 0/"").
Projector._v0_document_registered's INSERT/ON CONFLICT SET clause now writes
bib_* from the payload.

NOT touched (confirmed correctly out of scope): Catalog.register()'s
DocumentRegisteredPayload construction (catalog.py ~L1363) -- a brand-new
document has no prior bib_* to carry forward, defaults are correct. The
synthesizer's _document_registered_event() (synthesizer.py ~L311) -- builds
v:0 events from documents.jsonl rows for the doctor/synthesize-log verbs;
DocumentRecord/JSONL never carried bib_* (pre-existing, documented gap from
nexus-9l2lg's design "Out of scope" item 2), so this path cannot recover
bib_* from JSONL regardless.

REPLAY POSTURE (item 5 finding, not solved here, matching existing posture):
Event.from_dict filters parsed JSON to the payload's declared fields, so an
event written BEFORE this fix (no bib_* keys in its serialized JSON)
constructs with the 0/"" defaults on replay -- no crash. This means a FULL
COLD REPLAY of a pre-existing event log (the "do_full" bootstrap/invalidation
path in _SyncOps._ensure_consistent, catalog_sync.py) will reproduce
bib_year=0/etc for any document whose LAST DocumentRegistered-type event
predates this fix and was never re-touched by a post-fix write since. This is
NOT a new risk -- it's the same class of exposure alias_of/source_uri already
carry (both were added to DocumentRegisteredPayload after the type existed,
with the same replay-drift acceptance). The LIVE apply path (an event emitted
now, applied now via cat._projector.apply(event) immediately after write) is
fully correct. No migration/backfill-via-events machinery was built to
recover pre-fix bib_* into event history; SQLite remains the durable source
for any bib_* set before this fix, exactly matching the existing posture for
alias_of/source_uri and the already-documented JSONL-rebuild gap.

Tests: 5 new/flipped in test_catalog_event_sourced_mutators.py (flipped the
old "do not persist" pin to "persists"; added update-without-kwargs,
rename_collection, update_document_collection x2 clobber regressions -- all
red-then-green per emission site). Removed the NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=0 workaround
pins from test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py / test_enrich_command.py /
test_bib_enricher_write_back_service_mode.py (they now pass under the true
default). Kept test_catalog_bib_columns.py pinned to =0 throughout as the
dedicated legacy-path parity suite (docstring updated to explain why).
5-file narrow set: 69/69 green. tests -k "catalog or enrich": 2119 passed, 5
skipped, 0 failed.
close_reason: Shipped at 41b5f6bc (escalated P3->P1 into the same PR per Hal: ES defaults ON so the event-sourced path was the DEFAULT local write path). DocumentRegisteredPayload +8 bib fields; projector writes them; all 4 emission sites carry forward; full cold-replay test. Pre-fix-event replay posture matches alias_of/source_uri (documented in bead notes).

title: GH #1402: grants-nexus-svc bulk GRANT crashes on foreign-owned relations + diag probe grant/ownership fragmentation
description:
Recurrence of the nexus-46yy3 class, one changeset over. Root cause: grants-nexus-svc-1 (runAlways) uses bulk GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA nexus/t1, which hard-errors on any relation nexus_admin cannot grant on — e.g. the deliberately superuser-owned diag_chash_conformance view (RLS-exempt owner required for count-by-construction, nexus-vounk). grants-nexus-diag already fixed this for REVOKE (per-relation, owner-restricted) and preconditioned its own bulk GRANT on view-absence; grants-nexus-svc.xml never got the treatment.

Fix plan (two-sided):
1. ENGINE (service/, -> engine-service-v0.1.43): convert grants-nexus-svc-1's 4 bulk statements (tables+sequences x nexus+t1) to the owner-restricted per-relation DO-block pattern from grants-nexus-diag-2 (relkind r,p,v,m,f; pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner)=current_user). Preserve fail-loud on missing nexus_svc. Regression test: superuser-owned view present -> Liquibase boots clean (model on the 46yy3 test).
2. ENGINE conformance test: sweep ALL changelogs for unguarded bulk 'ON ALL (TABLES|SEQUENCES)' outside ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES — 3rd incident in this subsystem (FORCE-RLS DML no-op nexus-1wjmq, 46yy3 REVOKE, this) = class-level tripwire per root-cause-after-repeated-patches rule.
3. PYTHON: (a) pg_provision diag-view path: idempotent re-GRANT SELECT ON view TO nexus_diag for PRE-EXISTING views (a view created before the diag role existed carries no grant; probe then falls back and gets denied — the second symptom in #1402); (b) health.py chash_probe_view_fallback_legacy log note mislabels every view-path failure as 'view absent (pre-A6 engine)' — include the actual error and stop asserting the cause.
4. Field hazard to document: the issue's ALTER VIEW OWNER TO nexus_admin workaround silently breaks count-by-construction — non-BYPASSRLS owner + FORCE RLS fail-closed policy = probe counts 0 = FALSE CLEAN on a poisoned store. Must chown back to a superuser/BYPASSRLS role once the engine fix lands.

Engine-release implications: v0.1.43 cut + cloud gate + REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION floor bump in next conexus release (upgrade-path-critical fix; floor is local installs' fix-delivery vehicle).
close_reason: All scope items shipped. (1) Engine: grants-nexus-svc-1 owner-restricted per-relation DO block + skip NOTICE, commit 9e8735a8 on develop; red reproduced exact #1402 PSQLException, green post-fix; full mvnw clean test 1259/0/0. (2) Changelog tripwire: ChangelogBulkGrantConformanceTest (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed per-statement, sqlFile-presence guard, allowlist pins the diag-1 view-absence gate) — 8 tests. (3) Python: pg_provision re-grant confirmed already idempotent (no change needed); health.py fallback-note fix committed 84d47ae0. (4) Field hazard (admin-owned view = false-clean probe) documented in the GH #1402 comment. Stacked review: cre-auto found the sqlCheck scanner bug (fixed), critic-auto demonstrated 3 tripwire evasions (fixed) + verified NOTICE/split semantics structurally; both final verdicts clean. REMAINING (not this bead): engine-service-v0.1.43 cut (human), cloud deploy+gate relay, REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION floor bump at next conexus release.

title: T2 SQLite FK enforcement audit: PRAGMA foreign_keys never enabled — declared REFERENCES unenforced across stores
description: Found during nexus-6i01g stacked review: CatalogTaxonomy declares REFERENCES (e.g. topic_assignments.topic_id -> topics.id) but its connection never issues PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, so SQLite's default (OFF) leaves ALL declared FKs unenforced. The merge-chain assignment-orphaning CRITICAL (fixed at the CLI layer in 43c64f2a) was one instance of this class. Scope: (1) audit every T2 connection-open site (T2Database facade + each domain store) for FK enablement; (2) inventory declared FKs across the seven domain stores; (3) query the LIVE db for existing orphans (e.g. topic_assignments rows pointing at deleted topics — the 2026-07-14 manual review pass predates the guard and may have left some); (4) decide enable-vs-document per store (enabling FKs on a store with existing orphans fails writes — needs cleanup first); (5) orphan cleanup migration if warranted. Evidence: T2 nexus/taxonomy-review-auto-shipped.
close_reason: Audit complete + fixes shipped (bbaf7131 on develop). Findings: (1) PG leg clean by construction — enforced FKs + ON DELETE CASCADE since taxonomy-001-baseline; (2) taxonomy ETL orphan-aware (RDR-153 skip-and-record) — the 51,286 orphaned topic_assignments + ~6.9k orphaned topic_links in the frozen pre-migration SQLite store were correctly skipped at migration (explains live '0 topic links'); (3) FOUR current-code SQLite orphan generators found and fixed with explicit topic_links DELETEs: persist_rebuild_topics, delete_topic, merge_topics, purge_assignments_for_doc. 6 new tests (exact row-identity asserts); 458 taxonomy-sweep green. DECISION: PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON deliberately NOT enabled — topic_links lacks cascade so enforcement would convert silent orphans into hard IntegrityErrors at unguarded call sites (worst: T2Database.delete hot path); store scheduled for deletion in RDR-158 P4 (nexus-i711w). No orphan-cleanup migration for the frozen store: it is an inert rollback target, ETL already filters. Stacked review: cre-auto clean, critic-auto clean (verified merge semantics against Java TaxonomyRepository source).

title: Implement --auto/--yes/--dry-run/--batch-size on nx taxonomy review (TDD)
description:
Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t design-taxonomy-review-auto.md ; nx memory get -p nexus -t taxonomy-auto-review-2026-07-14 (reference rubric + results)
Search keywords: claude_dispatch verdict schema, t2_index_write, taxonomy review guards

Prerequisites: none (first task in the epic).

## Files
- src/nexus/commands/taxonomy_cmd.py — extend review_cmd (~line 875), add new schema + async batch-verdict dispatcher mirroring _LABEL_SCHEMA (~line 1391) / _generate_labels_batch (~line 1414).
- src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py — reuse existing get_unreviewed_topics, mark_topic_reviewed, rename_topic, delete_topic, merge_topics, get_topic_by_id, get_topic_doc_ids. No store-layer changes expected; if a guard needs a new query, add it here with a matching test in tests/test_taxonomy.py::TestReviewMethods style.
- src/nexus/mcp_infra.py — t2_index_write (~line 375), the only sanctioned write path (RDR-151 Phase 3).
- tests/test_taxonomy_review_auto.py — NEW FILE (parallel to tests/test_taxonomy_backfill.py, tests/test_taxonomy_service_wiring.py sibling-file convention; do not grow tests/test_taxonomy.py further, it is already 2600+ lines).
- docs/cli-reference.md — taxonomy command block ~line 876 plus a new `### nx taxonomy review --auto` subsection (model on the neighboring `### nx taxonomy validate-refs` subsection).

## TDD task list (write the failing test before each implementation step; run `uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy_review_auto.py -q` after each)

1. Schema + verdict-batch dispatcher (pure function, no CLI):
   - Add `_REVIEW_VERDICT_SCHEMA: dict` near `_LABEL_SCHEMA` in taxonomy_cmd.py: `{"type":"object","required":["verdicts"],"properties":{"verdicts":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","required":["idx","action"],"properties":{"idx":{"type":"integer","minimum":1},"action":{"type":"string","enum":["accept","rename","delete","merge"]},"label":{"type":"string","minLength":3,"maxLength":60},"target_id":{"type":"integer"},"reason":{"type":"string","maxLength":200}}}}}}`.
   - Add `async def _generate_review_verdicts_batch(items: list[tuple[int, str, list[str], list[str], str]]) -> list[dict | None]` — items are `(topic_id, label, terms, sample_doc_ids, collection)`. Mirrors `_generate_labels_batch`'s structure: build a numbered prompt (embed the real topic_id per line, terms[:5], doc basenames), dispatch via `nexus.operators.dispatch.claude_dispatch` (deferred import, same as `_generate_labels_batch`), wrap in try/except returning `[None]*len(items)` on ANY exception (fail-open, mirrors glossary labeler's `test_dispatch_exception_returns_all_none`).
   - Rubric text embedded in the prompt (verbatim intent from the validated reference run, T2 nexus/taxonomy-auto-review-2026-07-14): accept = specific coherent label; rename = coherent theme but a bad label (supply new_label, 3-60 chars); delete = syntax pattern-pollution (pytest/monkeypatch scaffolding, Java test boilerplate, license import headers, CSS blobs, home-dir path fragments — give a one-line `reason`); merge = near-duplicate of another topic (give the real `target_id` of the topic to merge into, same collection, plus a one-line `reason`).
   - Per-entry validation on the parsed payload (fail-open — invalid entry -> None at that slot, never raises): idx must be an in-range int; action must be one of the 4 strings; action=="rename" requires `label` with `3 <= len(label) <= 60` else None; action=="merge" requires `target_id` to be an int else None; malformed/missing `verdicts` key -> all None.
   - Tests (write first): idx-in-range accept parses; rename with valid/invalid label length; merge with/without target_id; delete with reason; unknown action string ignored; dispatch-raises returns all-None; missing `verdicts` key returns all-None; out-of-range idx ignored. Model directly on tests/test_rdr_085_glossary_labeler.py's `patch("nexus.operators.dispatch.claude_dispatch", ...)` pattern — patch at the SAME module path (`nexus.operators.dispatch.claude_dispatch`), not `nexus.commands.taxonomy_cmd.claude_dispatch`, because the import is deferred-at-call-time inside the function.

2. CLI flags + orchestration in review_cmd:
   - Add `@click.option("--auto", is_flag=True, ...)`, `@click.option("--yes", "-y", is_flag=True, ...)`, `@click.option("--dry-run", is_flag=True, ...)`, `@click.option("--batch-size", default=40, type=int, show_default=True, ...)`.
   - Change `--limit`/`-n`'s default from `15` to `None`; resolve to `15` for interactive, `5000` for `--auto` (matches `label_cmd`'s existing `limit=5000` convention) when the user did not pass `--limit` explicitly. Existing interactive tests in tests/test_taxonomy.py::TestReviewCLI must still pass unmodified (they never pass --limit) — this is a behavior-preserving default-resolution refactor, verify by re-running `uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k TestReviewCLI -q` after the change.
   - When `--auto` is set, dispatch to a new `_review_auto(db, collection, limit, yes, dry_run, batch_size)` helper and return; the existing interactive loop body is untouched otherwise.
   - `_review_auto`: fetch pending topics via `db.taxonomy.get_unreviewed_topics(collection=collection, limit=limit)`; if empty, print the SAME "No unreviewed topics. All done!" message as the interactive path (test parity) and return. Chunk into `batch_size`-sized batches; for each batch build items via `db.taxonomy.get_topic_doc_ids(topic_id, limit=3)` and call `asyncio.run(_generate_review_verdicts_batch(batch_items))` sequentially (no ThreadPoolExecutor — keep V1 simple/deterministic; parallelism is an explicit non-goal, note in code comment referencing this bead if revisited).
   - Bucket verdicts: accept/rename apply immediately via `t2_index_write` UNLESS `dry_run` (dry-run must suppress ALL applies including accept/rename per the design — this is the one place it differs from the "apply accept+rename immediately" default). delete/merge go into `candidate_deletes` / `candidate_merges` lists (topic dict + reason).
   - Second pass over `candidate_merges` (only after ALL batches processed, so the full delete-set is known): validate each merge — `target = db.taxonomy.get_topic_by_id(target_id)`; guard order: self-merge (`target_id == topic["id"]`) -> drop, stays pending; target is None -> drop, stays pending; `target["collection"] != topic["collection"]` -> drop, stays pending; `target_id` in `{d["id"] for d in candidate_deletes}` (target itself verdict-deleted this run) -> drop, stays pending. Surviving entries become `pending_merges`.
   - If not dry_run and (`candidate_deletes` or `pending_merges`): print a destructive plan grouped by action (deletes: id, label, doc_count, reason; merges: source label -> target label, doc counts, reason), then `if yes or click.confirm(...)`: apply each via `t2_index_write(lambda db, _t=tid: db.taxonomy.delete_topic(_t))` / `t2_index_write(lambda db, _s=src, _t=tgt: db.taxonomy.merge_topics(_s, _t))`; catch `(click.Abort, EOFError)` around the confirm exactly like the interactive loop's existing `except (click.Abort, EOFError)` and treat as decline. If declined: print "declined; topics remain pending", apply nothing.
   - If dry_run: print the same destructive-plan text plus what accept/rename WOULD have done, apply nothing at all.
   - Print a final summary line with exact counts: accepted, renamed, deleted, merged, skipped (fail-open + guard-dropped), matching the "exact-count assertions" project convention for the tests that will assert on it.

   Tests (write first, CLI-level, model directly on tests/test_taxonomy.py::TestReviewCLI's `_seed_topics` / `_t2_router` / `patch("nexus.commands.taxonomy_cmd._default_db_path", ...)` + `patch.object(_mi, "t2_index_write", self._t2_router(db_path))` pattern, plus `patch("nexus.operators.dispatch.claude_dispatch", ...)` for the verdict dispatch):
   a. accept verdict applies immediately, no confirm prompt needed (assert review_status == 'accepted').
   b. rename verdict applies immediately (assert label + review_status == 'accepted').
   c. delete verdict declined by default (`input="n\n"`, no --yes) -> topic count unchanged, review_status still 'pending'.
   d. delete verdict applied with `--yes` -> topic count == 0.
   e. merge verdict applied with confirm `input="y\n"` -> source gone, target doc_count updated.
   f. merge with nonexistent target_id -> stays pending, topic count unchanged (== N, not >=).
   g. merge with cross-collection target -> stays pending.
   h. merge with target_id == own id (self-merge) -> stays pending, does not appear in the printed destructive plan.
   i. merge whose target is ALSO verdict-deleted this run -> the merge stays pending; the delete (if confirmed) still applies to the target.
   j. `--dry-run` with a mixed batch (accept+rename+delete+merge all present) -> ZERO DB mutations of any kind (exact review_status/label assertions unchanged for every seeded topic), destructive-plan text is present in `result.output`.
   k. `claude_dispatch` raising -> all topics stay pending, `exit_code == 0`, summary reports the skip count.
   l. `--auto` with no `--limit` and 20 seeded pending topics -> all 20 considered (proves the 5000 default, not the interactive 15 default) — use all-accept verdicts + assert 20 accepted.
   m. `--auto --limit 5` with 20 seeded pending topics -> exactly 5 processed, 15 remain pending (== 15, not >=).
   n. `--batch-size 2` with 5 seeded topics -> the mocked `claude_dispatch` stub is called exactly 3 times (ceil(5/2)).
   o. no pending topics -> same "No unreviewed topics. All done!" message as interactive.
   p. mixed-outcome summary line reports the exact counts for a batch containing one of each action.

title: MinerU autostart: warm-up stall + OOM-fallback exposure multiplies across documents, not confined to the first PDF
description:
Critique of a29348b4 (nexus-1qdb9). PDFExtractor is instantiated fresh per document (doc_indexer.py:1102, pipeline_stages.py:92, commands/index.py:1155's per-pdf index_pdf() call), and _mineru_server_checked (pdf_extractor.py:375-379) is instance-scoped. During a model warm-up that exceeds ensure_mineru_running()'s _ENSURE_HEALTH_WAIT_S=120s window, EVERY document that arrives while warming re-enters the election, re-waits up to another 120s, and still falls back to the in-process subprocess path.

The mineru_lifecycle.py module docstring claims "timeout = this document falls back, the warming server serves the next one" — false once warm-up exceeds ~120s (e.g. first-ever model download, ~2-3GB). Multiple sequential documents each pay their own stall AND still hit the OOM-risk-on-macOS fallback (RLIMIT_AS ceiling is Linux-gated only per the Gap 6 comment in pdf_extractor.py), reproducing the pre-fix failure mode across a batch window instead of confining it to one document.

Secondary: no progress signal during the up-to-120s wait (structlog only, no click.echo/_progress()) — a `nx index pdf --dir` batch run shows "[i/total] file.pdf…" then hangs silently for up to 2 minutes per affected document, no indication autostart is in progress.

Recommendation: cache "warming, do not re-wait" state at a level broader than one PDFExtractor instance (e.g. a short-TTL process-local or config-dir-scoped marker) so only the FIRST document in a warm-up window pays the wait; subsequent documents either wait on the SAME in-flight health-check (coalesced) or skip straight to fallback without re-waiting. Add a progress signal (click.echo/_progress) when autostart begins waiting.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-nexus-1qdb9-mineru-lifecycle-a29348b4.md
close_reason: Warming marker (config-dir mineru_warming.json, pid-validated, cleared on healthy/death) makes the warm-up wait a shared budget — a >120s first start stalls the batch once, not per document; dead-child fast-fail removes the port-conflict 120s-per-document stall. Tests: shared-budget second-document <1s, dead-child <5s, stale-marker pid-mismatch. Residual marker-model observations noted on nexus-4yohu.

title: MinerU lifecycle: two pre-existing spawn paths (_restart_mineru_server, restart_stale) bypass the new election guard and policy gates
description:
Critique of a29348b4 (nexus-1qdb9). ensure_mineru_running() is the only one of THREE mineru-api spawn triggers that goes through ServiceRegistry.election():

1. PDFExtractor._restart_mineru_server() (pdf_extractor.py:1031-1145) fires on mid-document server-crash detection. Bare subprocess.Popen, zero synchronization, and does NOT check pdf.mineru_autostart or the remote-intent guard — always spawns locally on crash regardless of operator config.
2. upgrade_finish.restart_stale()'s mineru branch (upgrade_finish.py:269-277) shells out to `nx mineru stop && nx mineru start` during automated upgrade-finish skew detection. Also zero synchronization, also ignores the new config gate.

Both can race the election-guarded ensure_mineru_running() (or each other), producing two live mineru-api processes (duplicate model load) with the pid file left pointing at whichever writer won last — the loser is orphaned with no tooling able to find it.

Additionally: mineru is not a member of the RDR-149 cross-tier conformance suite's TIERS tuple (tests/daemon/test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py:68) — it never publishes a lease record, so it gets none of the lease/self-heal/reap guarantees the other 5 tiers get. Liveness is still plain os.kill(pid,0) (nexus/_mineru_pid.py) — no pid-reuse immunity, the exact hazard RDR-149 eliminated elsewhere. The bead nexus-1qdb9 explicitly asked for "discovery lease... self-heal... NOT another ad-hoc autostart bolted onto pdf_extractor" — this delivered single-writer spawn only, for one of three spawn triggers.

Recommendation: route _restart_mineru_server and restart_stale's mineru cycle through the same election(), and have both honor pdf.mineru_autostart / the remote-intent guard. Consider whether mineru needs a real lease record (publish/heartbeat) to join the conformance suite properly, or whether the bead's scope should be explicitly narrowed (with the bead description updated) to "single-writer cold-start spawn only" if full lease membership is deferred.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-nexus-1qdb9-mineru-lifecycle-a29348b4.md
close_reason: All three spawn triggers share spawn_policy_allows + ServiceRegistry.election (60ed904e); nx mineru stop's read-then-kill under the same election and restart_stale's automated cycle policy-gated (eb4c62eb). Tests: election single-spawner, restart gates both ways, stop-race closed by construction. Full suite 13147 green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Re-critique of remediation commit 60ed904e (2026-07-14): PARTIAL close only. _restart_mineru_server is now fully compliant (spawn_policy_allows + registry.election + shared spawn core) — Critical 2/3 from the original critique are closed for THAT trigger. But restart_stale's mineru cycle remains only half-fixed: 'nx mineru start' is now election-guarded (good) but is DELIBERATELY policy-ungated by design (comment in commands/mineru.py: 'the explicit verb is deliberately NOT policy-gated'), and restart_stale() (upgrade_finish.py) has ZERO mineru_autostart gate check anywhere in its call chain — grep confirms no 'mineru_autostart'/'spawn_policy_allows' reference in upgrade_finish.py. This means an operator who sets pdf.mineru_autostart:false to manage the server out-of-band still has it STOPPED and a new nx-controlled one STARTED on every upgrade-finish skew cycle — directly contradicts this bead's own recommendation text ('have both _restart_mineru_server and restart_stale honor pdf.mineru_autostart'). Separately, 'nx mineru stop' (the first half of restart_stale's shelled-out cycle) has NO election guard at all — it kills whatever pid is currently in the pid file with no coordination against a concurrent elector's in-flight spawn and no pid re-verification against the skew-report snapshot (unlike the aspect-worker path in the same file, which does re-verify via 'ps -p' before signaling). A concurrent legitimately-elected spawn can be killed by an uncoordinated restart_stale stop call; nx mineru start immediately after is election-safe so the system self-heals rather than duplicating servers, but the concurrent caller whose spawn was killed experiences an undetectable spurious failure. Full critique persisted: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-remediation-60ed904e-mineru-lifecycle.md

title: Quarantine collection naming collapses docs__/rdr__ into one physical collection — breaks restore + defeats expiry floor
description: Critique of 4cb743be (nexus-xukbj). quarantine_collection_name() strips only the content-type segment, keeping <owner>__<model>__v<n>. docs__ and rdr__ collections of the SAME repo share owner + voyage-context-3 model (RDR-103), so both resolve to the IDENTICAL quarantine__<owner>__voyage-context-3__v<n> sibling. Consequences: (1) if an identical chash is orphaned from both origins, the second upsert silently overwrites the first row's origin_collection/quarantined_at/content (Chroma upsert-by-id), permanently breaking restore_rereferenced's origin_collection filter for the overwritten origin — restore matching is NOT sound under cross-origin chash sharing. (2) expire_quarantine's floor calculation (frac = expired/all_ids) has NO origin filter — it scans the ENTIRE shared collection. A manifest-defect mass-quarantine burst in one origin (e.g. rdr__) can be diluted below NX_GC_FLOOR_FRACTION (0.25) by unrelated healthy quarantine volume from the other origin (docs__), silently defeating the ONE loud protection (locked design intent #3) this feature exists to provide. (3) expire_quarantine/restore_rereferenced run TWICE per GC pass against the same physical collection (once per colliding origin name), with logs always attributed to whichever origin is processed first in the fixed (code, docs, rdr) tuple order — misleading audit trail during incident response. Test test_prune_deleted_files_per_collection_orphan_isolation asserts only origin .delete() isolation, never inspects the (colliding) quarantine sibling, and passes only because its two test chashes happen to differ — the test's name overstates what it verifies. Fix direction: quarantine_collection_name must retain the content-type segment (or otherwise guarantee per-origin quarantine collection uniqueness), and expire_quarantine/restore_rereferenced must filter by origin_collection before computing floor fractions.
close_reason: Fixed in c1fb3d43: per-type quarantine names (quarantine-<type>__owner__model__vN) end the docs__/rdr__ collision; expire_quarantine filters rows by origin_collection before floor math; realistic shared-chash regression pins restore/expiry isolation.

title: MinerU server has no auto-start and no RDR-149 lifecycle membership — dies silently into the OOM-risk fallback
description: Live find (2026-07-14, 6.7.1 shakeout): the MinerU API server was killed during upgrade hygiene and NOTHING respawned it — nx doctor flagged 'unreachable... falling back to in-process subprocess on math PDFs (OOM-risk)' and it stayed that way until a human ran nx mineru start (the AI's 'respawns on demand' assumption was WRONG — no such path exists). On-demand spawn at first PDF op needing it (respecting the RDR-044 Docling->MinerU->PyMuPDF router), plus doctor fix-suggestion naming nx mineru start. Weigh the memory footprint concern (model load) as a config gate (mineru.autostart=true default?) rather than absent lifecycle. Related: nexus-4fq4h (process-boundary isolation) — same boundary, complementary.

title: manifest self-heal pass: GC-hazard ordering + fairness-bypass + recurring cost + partial-failure observability gaps
description:
Substantive critique of commit 4711f521 (nexus-c21fk manifest self-heal, src/nexus/catalog/manifest_heal.py + indexer.py _catalog_hook integration). Four issues, ranked:

1. CRITICAL — GC hazard (nexus-mr89x) only partially disarmed. heal_manifest_gaps runs BEFORE per-file indexing in _catalog_hook (indexer.py ~2895-2939), while the T3-chunk-level GC (_prune_misclassified/_prune_deleted_files, indexer.py:3439/3454) runs at the END of index_repository, after per-file embedding + manifest-write hooks. Heal correctly protects PRE-EXISTING gaps from this run's prune pass, but a gap CREATED by THIS SAME run's own manifest-write hook (the nexus-94fxl silent-early-return hypothesis, still deferred/unresolved) postdates heal and is exposed to that run's own prune at the end — one full cycle of exposure per newly-introduced gap, not zero. The claimed "keeps mr89x armed / this closes it" framing overstates the fix.

2. SIGNIFICANT — Unconditional full-owner-population re-walk on EVERY nx index repo invocation, including no-op runs, with no memoization. heal_manifest_gaps calls cat.by_owner(owner) a SECOND time (already fetched once at indexer.py:791; HTTP mode = one unbounded GET /list?owner=X), then get_manifests() + a re-derivation of "gapped" status for every never-chunked ghost entry (content_hash+physical_collection stamped, chunk_count==0) forever — commit's own docstring cites ~8.6k such ghosts from a live run. This reproduces the exact cost shape two prior P1s in this codebase already fixed (nexus-dst5h: "1h42m+ ... 8.7k gapped docs"; nexus-8g0ch: batched $in to avoid re-paying this walk) but now as a recurring per-run tax with no threshold/alarm/caching.

3. SIGNIFICANT — Bypasses the RDR-146 P2 fairness/yield contract. _catalog_hook Pass 1 (indexer.py:836-851) calls await_fair_window(writer.is_interactive_write_pending, on_locked) per file so a batch-priority background producer yields to a foreground interactive index (the GH #1046 starvation class named in this function's own docstring). heal_manifest_gaps's write loop (atomic_manifest_replace + resync_chunk_count_cache per gapped doc) has no such check — can starve a foreground write for a large gapped population.

4. SIGNIFICANT — Partial-failure loses all progress accounting. No try/except wraps heal_manifest_gaps's per-entry write; a raised exception propagates out of the function entirely, hits the indexer's blanket except (logs catalog_manifest_self_heal_failed with exc_info) — but the structured summary log (catalog_manifest_self_heal: candidates/gapped/reconciled/lost) and progress line only fire on a clean return, so a mid-pass crash is indistinguishable from "heal never ran." Contradicts the commit's own stated observability goal.

Verified NOT defects: owner-scope coverage of RDR docs (same _catalog_hook call, same owner — indexer.py:2907-2923); get_manifests batching (500/query SQLite, paged HTTP); no re-embedding (T3-read-only). Field-fix efficacy for the motivating 1.3.142-150 docs remains unverified — nexus-94fxl (root-cause hypothesis for those specific docs) is DEFERRED, not resolved.

Full critique: T2 memory nexus/critique-4711f521-c21fk-manifest-self-heal.md
close_reason: All four findings actioned in 8a8d6262: (1) CRITICAL placement — heal moved to index_repository AFTER per-file indexing and BEFORE the prune passes, ordering pinned by test_manifest_self_heal_runs_after_indexing_before_prunes (spies on the real calls); same-run gaps now healed before the GC ever sees them. (2) Cost — the duplicate by_owner fetch is GONE with the move (one fetch at the heal site); the remaining per-run detection (one by_owner + one batched get_manifests) is a documented, deliberate acceptance at the call site — ghost-class T3 fetches dedupe to near-nothing (identical empty files share one content_hash). (3) Fairness — await_fair_window threaded through yield_before_write; heal writes yield to a foreground interactive writer. (4) Partial-failure accounting — per-entry write failures caught, counted (result.write_failed), logged, pass continues, summary always emitted. Full suite 13129 green.

title: catalog reconcile in service mode: N+1 per-doc HTTP walk (1h42m+ on 21k docs) with zero progress output — batch it + emit progress
description: 6.7.0 shakeout live find (2026-07-13): nx catalog reconcile --dry-run against a 21,835-doc service-mode catalog ran 10+ minutes at ~1% CPU (network-bound HTTP round-trips) with NO output at all — indistinguishable from a hang, which caused the operator (and the AI driving it) to stack duplicate invocations. nx index rdr already has the convention: --monitor per-item progress lines, auto-enabled when stdout is not a TTY. Apply the same to catalog reconcile / doctor walks: periodic 'N/total scanned, M ghosts found' lines (rate-limited), plus a startup line stating the scan size and mode (service vs local) so expected duration is legible. Observability is a core product doctrine — a silent long walk is a defect, not a style choice. Also audit siblings: catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage, --collections-drift, t3 gc.
close_reason: Fixed in d470eda1 + 60ef882a: T3 fetches batch per collection via paged $in (64/predicate, verified live against pgvector); scan header + per-collection progress lines; batch failures visible in output; summary splits chunks-LOST (real gap) from never-chunked (expected). Live result: the walk that had not finished after 1h42m completed in ~4 min, healing 49 genuinely manifest-dropped documents; 8,653 unmatched correctly classified (~8.6k empty never-chunked files + 14 deleted collections). Stacked review findings all actioned; 15/15 reconcile + 152 catalog CLI tests green.

comments.text: ESCALATION (same shakeout): the silent walk is also an N+1 pathology — the dry-run ran 1h42m and was still going on a 21,835-doc service-mode catalog (~280ms/doc = per-doc HTTP round-trips to the cloud, likely manifest + chunk lookups each). Bulk endpoints exist post-xnz0o (collection-counts, orphaned, all_documents with offset). Fix is TWO halves: batch the walk (bulk fetch, page server-side) AND emit progress. As shipped, reconcile in service mode is effectively unusable on a real catalog.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic pass on d470eda1 (partial: 0 critical, 3 significant, logic verified correct):

1. No test exercises the batch-failure / collection-unavailable paths (only the all-success single-batch happy path is pinned) despite the commit message's explicit claim about preserving failure semantics.
2. Failure isolation granularity silently widened from 1 doc to up to 64 docs per persistent T3 fetch failure (one $in batch = up to 64 docs now share fate). Retries inside _paginated_get mitigate the practical risk (only durable failures propagate) but this isn't called out anywhere.

title: Upgrade UX: no single finish-the-upgrade step — running processes keep old code invisibly and doctor reports 'latest' while every live process is stale
description:
Live dogfood of the 6.5.2->6.7.0 upgrade (Hal, 2026-07-13): after 'uv tool install --reinstall conexus', nx --version said 6.7.0 and nx doctor said '6.7.0 (latest)' — while EVERY running conexus process (3 nx-mcp/nx-mcp-catalog pairs from 3 live Claude sessions, the aspect-worker child of one of them, mineru-api detached since Jul 6) still executed 6.5.2 code from memory. Nothing surfaces this skew and nothing fixes it short of tribal knowledge (quit all sessions; MinerU needs a manual kill because it is detached). Also bit: the tool receipt's source spec (directory vs pinned vs unpinned PyPI) silently determines whether 'uv tool upgrade' does anything at all — 'Nothing to upgrade' with zero explanation.

Wanted (design in bead, split as needed):
1. nx doctor check: enumerate running conexus processes (pgrep against the tool venv python + shim paths), compare each process's code version (start time vs venv mtime, or a version file stamped in the venv) against the installed version; WARN with the specific pids + the one-line remedy per process class.
2. A finish verb (nx upgrade --restart-stale or nx daemon cycle-all): kills detached daemons (mineru, aspect-worker where safely restartable) and prints exactly which Claude sessions must be exited (cannot kill those safely from inside).
3. nx doctor should also read the uv receipt and say WHICH source spec the install tracks (directory checkout / pinned / PyPI), so 'uv tool upgrade did nothing' is self-explanatory.
Evidence class: same 'disk upgraded, machine not' failure as project_daemon_restart_not_worker_fix.
close_reason: Shipped 38b7db3d + 21221df2 + 182de670: finish-the-upgrade. Process-skew engine (venv-root-scoped ps enumeration vs installed dist-info mtime, fail-loud on unlocatable metadata/failed ps), nx daemon restart-stale [--dry-run] (aspect-worker SIGTERM with pid re-verification + drain-poll honest reporting, MinerU cycled via its verbs, MCP hosts named for the human with kind-correct remedies), nx doctor Process-freshness check, uv-receipt source report via tomllib (directory/pinned/unpinned — the 6.7.0 upgrade-maze trio), and the last_seen_version auto-trigger in nx + nx-mcp + nx-mcp-catalog (O_EXCL single-transitioner lock; dev venvs consume the stamp but never act — the cross-venv guard the critic live-confirmed). Both reviewers' findings all actioned; 15/15 fixture-driven tests; live --dry-run probe verified on this box.

comments.text: Live evidence #2 (post-restart shakeout): the aspect-worker ORPHANED to ppid=1 when its hosting nx-mcp died with its session — the worker itself outlives the host (same class as design-rf8-pdeathsig-claude-child, one level up). Also: doctor/finish-verb must detect an nx-mcp pair whose parent claude session is still open — 'exit all sessions' left one alive invisibly (a forgotten tab).

comments.text: DESIGN ADDITION (Hal, 2026-07-14): 'shouldn't uv tool upgrade do the nx init?' — uv offers NO post-install hook (no package manager in this class does), so the finish choreography must trigger from the product side: stamp last_seen_version in the config dir; on first nx/nx-mcp invocation where installed dist version != stamp, auto-run the finish pass (schema migrations already auto via nx upgrade --auto in the session hook — extend with: process-skew detection [this bead's item 1], safe daemon cycling [mineru via nx mineru start per nexus-1qdb9's substrate work, aspect-worker], receipt-source report [item 3]) and emit ONE summary line. comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic on 38b7db3d (finish-the-upgrade P1). 3 Critical, 5 Significant. Full report in T2 nexus/nexus-4xgfy-commit-38b7db3d-critique.md.

CRITICAL:
1. Auto-trigger only wired into cli.py's main() (nx entry point). nx-mcp (nexus.mcp.core:main) and nx-mcp-catalog are SEPARATE entry points that never call cli.main — check_version_transition() never runs there. This contradicts the locked design text verbatim ("on first nx/nx-mcp invocation") and misses the dominant real-world path: all 3 live incidents' primary stale-process class was MCP hosts. If a box only ever runs Claude sessions post-upgrade (no bare `nx` invocation), the auto-restart of aspect-worker/mineru NEVER fires.
2. install_mtime_and_version() resolves importlib.metadata.distribution("conexus") from whichever venv is running THIS process, but _PROC_MARKERS in enumerate_processes() are hardcoded to production uv-tool-install paths ("uv/tools/conexus", ".local/bin/nx"). Running `uv run nx <cmd>` from a dev checkout (this project's own documented quick-start workflow) computes a fresh dev-venv mtime/version, then matches and can SIGTERM the live PRODUCTION aspect-worker system-wide based on a nonsensical cross-venv comparison. Direct violation of "never break the live nexus install."
3. restart_stale()'s aspect-worker branch is a raw os.kill(pid, 15) with no wait/verify/escalation, bypassing the RDR-149-leased tier's own fencing-based graceful-handoff lifecycle. On macOS (this exact dev box), T2 nexus/design-rf8-pdeathsig-claude-child.md documents PDEATHSIG is INACTIVE ("macOS gap... accepted, macOS dev-only") and the daemon's own stop() bounds drain to 10s while claude -p extraction can run up to ~180s. A SIGTERM landing mid-extraction on macOS can orphan the in-flight claude -p child (the exact RF8 class) while restart_stale unconditionally reports "restarted... respawns on demand" with zero verification.

SIGNIFICANT: (4) session_bound remedy text "belongs to a live Claude session — exit that session" is applied uniformly to ALL non-restartable kinds including "service" (T3/storage daemon) and "other" — factually wrong guidance for a stale storage daemon, which has its own `nx daemon t3 stop` lifecycle. (5) ps -e enumeration is box-wide with no uid scoping — cross-user false-positive stale reports on shared boxes. (6) No non-vacuity guard: hardcoded _PROC_MARKERS silently yield stale=[] (reported as fully healthy) for any install whose paths don't match the exact uv-tool-install layout (custom UV_TOOL_DIR, pipx, editable/system install) — indistinguishable from genuine health. (7) install_source() regex-parses the uv-receipt TOML instead of tomllib (stdlib, established project idiom) — fragile for a feature whose entire job is being authoritative. (8) Bypasses the RDR-149 shared daemon-lifecycle primitive (service_registry.py) per CLAUDE.md's own directive that lifecycle fixes must land there, not per-tier copies.

title: verify-fill relevance_log fill silently exhausts + misreports 'parity' after cutover+90d (frozen source vs live fill cutoff)
design:
Critique of commit 68509ac8 (nexus-24p05 close). The disjointness claim
("sweep deletes ONLY rows older than horizon; fill probes ONLY rows inside
it -- provably disjoint") is sound for the boundary-crossing case (single
shared clock, no skew) but the design has two unacknowledged failure modes:

1. PERMANENT BLINDNESS + FALSE "parity": the migration source (SQLite) is
   FROZEN post-cutover (verify_fill_watermark.py's own docstring: "the
   SQLite source is frozen post-cutover"). The fill's horizon filter
   (orchestrator.py:1125-1145) computes cutoff_iso = now_at_FILL - 90d
   using LIVE "now" each run, while source row timestamps never change.
   Once real-world time exceeds (newest frozen relevance_log timestamp +
   90 days), EVERY source row falls outside the fresh window forever --
   `rows` becomes permanently empty for relevance_log on every future
   verify-fill run. orchestrator.py:1168-1173 then reports
   `status: "parity", source_count: 0, missing: 0` -- INDISTINGUISHABLE
   from "verified, no holes found". Any relevance_log migration gap not
   caught within the first 90 days after cutover becomes permanently
   unverifiable AND is misreported as clean. `--verify-fill` is
   documented (docs/cli-reference.md:2397) as "a re-run to patch a small
   hole" with no stated time bound -- nx doctor explicitly suggests
   re-running it on ANY detected mismatch, potentially months later. This
   directly contradicts the close reason's "relevance_log is back in
   WATERMARK_TABLES soundly" and violates the project's own "no silent
   fallbacks for data-correctness problems -- FAIL LOUD" convention.

2. NO CLOCK-SKEW MARGIN: the "provably disjoint" proof requires the
   engine's (Java/PG, computes sweep cutoff via OffsetDateTime.now) and
   the orchestrator's (Python, computes fill cutoff via datetime.now(UTC))
   clocks to agree exactly, with zero buffer. If the orchestrator host's
   clock lags the engine's, fill's fresh-window edge is LESS strict than
   the engine's actual sweep-cutoff edge -- fill can then probe (and
   RE-IMPORT / resurrect) a row the engine has ALREADY correctly swept,
   the exact "resurrect expired rows" bug this commit was meant to close.
   No margin/buffer exists anywhere in the horizon comparison
   (orchestrator.py:1132-1136, verify_fill_watermark.py's cutoff logic
   mirrors it) despite running as two independent processes/hosts.

File:line: src/nexus/migration/orchestrator.py:1125-1173,
src/nexus/migration/verify_fill_watermark.py:56-81.

Full findings (with additional Significant issues re: days=90 coupling
and tenant-blind watermark cache key) in T2 memory project=nexus title
critique-68509ac8-nexus-24p05-y92yf.
close_reason: Fixed in the follow-up commit: expired_unverifiable status + horizon_excluded count + warning log replace the false parity for fully-aged-out retention tables; partial exclusions annotated; cli-reference documents the retention-window semantics; clock-skew safety margin (fill window one day strictly inside the sweep window) closes the two-clock hole in the disjointness argument. Acceptance test pins both.

title: ChashVectorConcurrencyTest: deterministic load (was: wall-clock loop that manufactured 503s/timeouts under host contention)
description: Release-gate class (Hal 2026-07-13: fix this flake, not an option). Three full-run failures on 2026-07-13 alone, each isolation-green: the 10s wall-clock tight loop couples request volume to host speed, so a busy machine (parallel pytest) slows server handling until the 3s pool-wait budget + 5x500ms retry budget + 20s client timeout all blow - manufacturing the exact 503/timeout signatures the zero-5xx assertion treats as regressions. This was nexus-xqrq0's explicitly deferred timeout follow-up. Fix: fixed per-worker iteration budget (deterministic volume), 90s client timeout, deeper 503 retry backoff; the typed-503 admission path and the zero-5xx-after-retry assertion stay fully load-bearing.
close_reason: Fixed 68509ac8: deterministic 200-iteration per-worker budget (2400 requests) replaces the 10s wall-clock tight loop; 90s client timeout; 8x2s 503 backoff. The zero-5xx-after-retry assertion and the typed-503 admission path are UNCHANGED and load-bearing. PROOF: the test passed inside the very next full ./mvnw run - the whole-suite-contention condition that produced three isolation-green failures earlier the same day. Closes nexus-xqrq0's explicitly deferred timeout follow-up (scope note updated in the test's own docstring trail).

title: verify-fill watermark trust-gate defeated by relevance_log's live TTL expiry (count non-decrease is not rollback-proof)
description:
nexus-te885.10 P2. verify_fill_watermark.py's usable_min_rowid() trusts a stored watermark whenever engine_count >= recorded target_count (verify_fill_watermark.py:93-101). This is defeated by ordinary steady-state churn: delete N rows + insert N new rows nets to an unchanged/growing count, so a real hole below the recorded floor goes undetected forever.

This is NOT hypothetical for relevance_log (one of the exact four watermarked tables): T2Database.expire() (src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py:1274) -> self.expire_relevance_log() -> self.telemetry.expire_relevance_log(), and in service mode self.telemetry IS HttpTelemetryStore (__init__.py:456) -> POST /v1/telemetry/relevance/expire -> TelemetryRepository.expireRelevanceLog -> `ctx.deleteFrom(RELEVANCE_LOG)` on the PG target table. This runs on EVERY SessionEnd hook (hooks.py:165, wired via nx-session-end-launcher, unconditional in any live service-mode install) as a 90-day TTL sweep, concurrent with continuous live relevance_log writes. That is exactly the delete+insert-offsetting profile the trust gate cannot see.

This directly contradicts telemetry_etl.py:674-681's documented invariant: "As of today NO retention/pruning mechanism deletes rows from these tables target-side" - that statement is already false for relevance_log as of THIS commit (the mechanism predates it; the watermark's soundness reasoning didn't account for it).

Fix options: (1) key the watermark's invalidation on something stronger than aggregate count (e.g. a per-row tombstone/max-deleted-rowid tracked by the TTL sweep itself, or a content hash/checksum over the watermarked range), (2) exclude relevance_log from the watermark table set until the TTL-interaction is resolved, (3) make expire_relevance_log advance-aware (write its own low-watermark invalidation signal when it deletes rows in a service-mode target).

Context: nx substantive-critic review of commit c0e4493e, 2026-07-13. Full findings: T2 memory project=nexus title=critique-c0e4493e-4l80g-te885.10-watermark.
notes: MITIGATED 38ebcda5: relevance_log EXCLUDED from WATERMARK_TABLES (full probe retained), telemetry_etl INVARIANT comment corrected (it falsely claimed no target-side retention exists), engine whitelist split into VERIFY_RELATIONS vs COUNT_ONLY_RELATIONS. REMAINING in this bead: (1) the stronger invalidation signal (TTL sweep publishes a max-deleted marker) so relevance_log can rejoin the watermark; (2) the PRE-EXISTING resurrect exposure - verify-fill over a >90-day-old source re-imports TTL-expired relevance_log rows (predates the watermark work entirely).
close_reason: BOTH halves implemented in 68509ac8 (not tracked - per Hal's keep-going directive): (1) retention markers - nexus.retention_markers (FORCE-RLS, telemetry-003) bumped by expireRelevanceLog + GET /v1/telemetry/retention/markers + both store twins with strict parity; the watermark trusts relevance_log only when the live marker >= the recorded baseline (rollback resets it - the count-offset scenario cannot fake it), missing marker distrusts fail-safe, success-with-absent normalizes to never-swept 0. (2) fresh-window fill - relevance_log probes only rows inside the 90-day horizon, making the sweep and fill domains provably disjoint AND closing the pre-existing resurrect-expired-rows exposure; the false no-retention INVARIANT comment now tells the truth; the wiring test pins never-re-import for expired-side holes. relevance_log is back in WATERMARK_TABLES soundly. Full pytest 13110 green; full mvn green modulo two isolation-confirmed infra flakes (Chash now FIXED, ChunksRls a Docker socket timeout). Rides the next engine cut.

title: nx CLI NUMERIC_FIELDS whitelist gap: non-whitelisted numeric metadata silently lexical-compared in service-mode range where-queries
description:
Follow-on to nexus-4l80g. src/nexus/filters.py NUMERIC_FIELDS is a hardcoded 8-field whitelist. coerce_value() leaves any other field's value as a Python str even when the value looks numeric and the underlying T3 metadata is a genuine JSON number. In service mode this hits PgVectorRepository's String-operand branch (PgVectorRepository.java:2632-2664 appendWherePredicate, :2715-2739 metadataCondition) which does a pure lexical text compare with no jsonb_typeof check for non-numeric-operand callers - silently WRONG ordering ('9' > '10'), not an error, not empty. This is worse than the bug 4l80g fixed (silently-empty). docs/cli-reference.md:24 documents the whitelist but never warns what happens outside it.

Fix options: (1) expand NUMERIC_FIELDS to cover more known fields and/or make it configurable, (2) have coerce_value attempt int/float parse for ANY field when unambiguous and not force string, reversing the current opt-in-whitelist design, (3) at minimum, document the silent-lexical-fallback risk prominently and/or add a runtime warning when a numeric-looking value is sent as a string operand for a range operator.

Context: nx substantive-critic review of commit c0e4493e, 2026-07-13. Full findings: T2 memory project=nexus title=critique-c0e4493e-4l80g-te885.10-watermark.
close_reason: Fixed 38ebcda5 (same session it was filed): parse_where types RANGE operands for ANY field - unambiguous numeric literal -> number (bridge numeric path), quoted value -> string (explicit lexical escape for ISO dates), non-numeric -> string; equality/!= deliberately unchanged. New tests/test_where_filters.py covers the gap case (custom_score>=80 numeric), the quote escape, and the unchanged-equality contract; cli-reference.md documents the rule + both hazards. The silently-wrong lexical path for non-whitelisted numeric range queries is closed.

title: RDR-182 P3 design: structural DB-level content scoping for nexus_diag (count views vs table SELECT)
description: critic-foundations Critical-1 residual (2026-07-12): nexus_diag's content boundary is currently enforced ONLY at the product choke point (nexus.db.diag_connection.run_diagnostic_sql lint) — the role's DB grants are full-column SELECT + BYPASSRLS, so a session opened OUTSIDE the helper could read cross-tenant content. Evaluate the structural fix: replace table-level SELECT with SELECT on purpose-built count/metadata views (e.g. nexus.diag_chash_conformance returning per-table non-conformant counts), revoking direct table SELECT. Trade-offs: view maintenance per diagnostic topic vs true read-scoped-by-construction; interaction with the runAlways grants changeset + engine release lifecycle. Decide during P3 (ykzbj.10/.11) while the diagnostic query set is being enumerated — the views should mirror exactly that set. Boundary documentation: grants-nexus-diag.xml BOUNDARY HONESTY block + diag_connection.py module docstring.
notes: RELEASE-GATE (Hal, 2026-07-13): no PyPI release cuts until this is DONE. Added to the release-blocker set.
close_reason: Amendment A6 shipped (47dcb65e + review fixes 78d5e064): superuser-owned nexus.diag_chash_conformance counts view; probe prefers view with legacy fallback (DiagnosticSqlViolation never retried); changeset revokes direct table SELECT per-relation owner-restricted. Count-by-construction replaces lint-only content scoping. Stacked review findings all actioned; full pytest 13122 + mvn 1242 + live diag suite green.

title: [bug] CRITICAL-class false-clean: health.py chash-conformance probe (and every psql RLS-table query) counts 0 under FORCE RLS — pnwu0 install-binary gate + nx doctor chash warning are vacuous
description: Found 2026-07-12 while enumerating nexus-ykzbj.8's decision surface; DEMONSTRATED live on a real bundled-PG store (engine v0.1.39 changelog): psql as nexus_admin with no nexus.tenant GUC returns count=0 from nexus.chunks_768 while 9 rows exist (tenant 'default'); setting the GUC returns 9. All five tables health.py:2125's chash_sql counts (chunks_384/768/1024, chash_index, catalog_document_chunks) carry ENABLE+FORCE RLS with the fail-closed tenant_isolation policy (current_setting('nexus.tenant', true) -> NULL -> zero rows). _run_psql sets no GUC, so Query 4 counts 0 UNCONDITIONALLY -> 'Chunk chash conformance' always reports clean -> the nexus-pnwu0 / GH #1390 install-binary gate (daemon.py _emit_chash_poison_gate) NEVER fires on a poisoned store, and nx doctor's warning likewise. This is the nexus-1wjmq asymmetry class verbatim (probe sees tenant-filtered nothing; Liquibase VALIDATE sees all rows and crash-loops) — the gate exists to prevent exactly the incident it cannot see. NOTE which probes are affected vs not: databasechangelog/databasechangeloglock queries (Queries 1-3) are NOT RLS'd -> fine; the RLS-structural probe (health.py ~2210) reads pg_class catalogs -> fine; ONLY row-counting queries against nexus.* tenant tables are vacuous. FIX DIRECTION (converges with RDR-182 ykzbj.8): run integrity probes on the nexus_diag SELECT-only + BYPASSRLS role (integrity diagnostics must see what VALIDATE sees — cross-tenant, read-only), or interim: set_config('nexus.tenant','default',false) in the probe session (covers single-tenant local installs only; managed multi-tenant needs BYPASSRLS or per-tenant union). Regression test must be a REAL-PG integration test (insert row via GUC, probe without GUC, assert the probe SEES it) — a mocked psql_runner reproduces the vacuity. Evidence transcript in session scratchpad itme7-demo + T1 scratch tag rdr-182.
notes: FIX PATH LOCKED (critic-foundations Critical-2, 2026-07-12): rewire health.py's _check_migration_state chash query (health.py:2125 chash_sql) AND the RLS-structural sibling probe's row-counting legs onto nexus.db.diag_connection.run_diagnostic_sql (the nexus_diag choke point: lint -> read-only session -> BYPASSRLS visibility). resolve_diag_credentials() returns None on pre-P2.1 credential files — degrade to the existing warn-skip posture, never a false-clean. Regression test MUST be real-PG (insert row via GUC as admin, probe via the helper with NO GUC, assert count sees it — the 0-vs-9 shape in tests/db/test_nexus_diag_role.py). Depends on nexus-ykzbj.8 (role + helper, shipped).
close_reason: FIXED (2026-07-13). health.py _check_migration_state chash leg rewired onto the nexus_diag path (resolve_diag_credentials + run_diagnostic_sql: SELECT-only BYPASSRLS, no tenant GUC -> sees every tenant's rows across the 5 chash-bearing tables, summed). Pre-P2.1 (no diag role) degrades to a loud 'could not run, do not read as clean' warn, never the old silent false-clean; heals via the nx init --service fast-path backfill. Both prod callers (nx doctor, install-binary gate) route through it. DRY: shared nexus.db.chash_tables.CHASH_BEARING_TABLES used by the health probe AND the forensics topic (drift-guard test). Non-vacuity PROVEN: unit test shows the leg uses the diag path (admin=0 but result shows diag count) + real-PG 0-vs-9 regression (nexus_admin NOSUPERUSER no-GUC counts 0, nexus_diag counts the poison). Full suite 13058 green. Commit 7580e4d9.

title: [bug] set_config_value crashes walking a dotted key through an existing flat scalar (TypeError: bool item assignment)
description: Found during the RDR-182 A4 spike critique (2026-07-12). config.py set_config_value builds the nested dict via 'node = data; for part in parts[:-1]: node = node.setdefault(part, {})' — when config.yml already holds a FLAT scalar at an intermediate key (e.g. hand-edited 'claude_assisted_remediation: true'), setdefault returns the existing scalar (True) and the next assignment does True['enabled']=... -> TypeError crash. Affects ANY dotted key colliding with an existing scalar, so the exact remedy command an RDR-182 refusal names ('nx config set claude_assisted_remediation.enabled true') crashes for precisely the user who hand-wrote the flat shape (the gate itself now refuses cleanly on that shape — see tests/mcp/test_rdr182_opt_in_gate.py::test_flat_scalar_section_refuses_without_crashing). Fix: replace non-dict intermediates with {} (documented overwrite) or raise a clean UsageError naming the conflicting key. Add a regression test in tests/test_config.py.
notes: PRIORITY RAISED to P1 (critic-final H3, 2026-07-13): this is the exact command every RDR-182 refusal string names as the remedy (nx config set claude_assisted_remediation.enabled true). A user who hand-wrote a flat scalar 'claude_assisted_remediation: true' gets a TypeError crash from the fix-it command instead of a clean enable — directly undercutting the 'make the safe path the easy path' thesis. The gate refuses cleanly on that shape; only the remedy command crashes.
close_reason: Fixed in ecf10a02. set_config_value now replaces non-dict intermediates on the dotted path with the nested form (logged via config_scalar_section_replaced with the discarded value) instead of crashing TypeError on setdefault returning the scalar. The RDR-182 remedy command (nx config set claude_assisted_remediation.enabled true) now converts a hand-written flat scalar cleanly. TDD: 3 regression tests (flat-scalar convert, deep chain through scalar, dict-intermediate merge preserves siblings); config + gate + config_cmd suites 87 green.

title: Stacked review gate (code-review-expert + substantive-critic) — blocks nexus-itme7 close
description:
Parent: nexus-itme7. Depends on nexus-5d022 (container run must be green first). MANDATORY gate before nexus-itme7 closes. BOTH reviewers run; the critic is NOT optional even if code-review is clean (they catch different classes).

DISPATCH BOTH (via /conexus:review-code and /conexus:substantive-critique, or the code-review-expert + substantive-critic agents):

1. code-review-expert — line-level review of the diff (seed_legacy.py + rehearse_guided.sh). Focus: shell-quoting/exit-code capture correctness under `set -uo pipefail`, the 16-char id helper, dim parameters, JSON manifest round-trip, no accidental product-source edits.

2. substantive-critic — brief it with the LOCKED design (memory: nexus/design-itme7-legacy-names-rehearsal.md) and the resolved open items (T1 scratch tag nexus-itme7). Pressure-test specifically:
   - NON-VACUITY: does each Phase-0 block assertion match a diagnostic that can ONLY appear when the intended guard fires? Could shape (i) be silently rescued by the nb7hr measured-dim override (dim=768 trap)? Could (ii) be blocking on model-support rather than legacy_ids? Is the collision (iv) actually firing the 5b9v0 guard, or something else?
   - SCOPE: is the design's row-6 "clean unlock / union count at target" honestly re-scoped to a BLOCK (guard fires first), with the discrepancy documented — not silently dropped?
   - MARKER MOVE: is the bundle-acquire assertion correctly relocated to Phase 0 (not left asserting on a rerun that never re-acquires -> false green)?
   - Does the success phase's parity for shape (iii) assert the TARGET holds SEED_N AND the source name holds 0 (both legs of the exact assertion), not just one?
   - Is the "removed the honest half of the collision pair in remediation" trade-off acknowledged vs. the faithful "remove only the stale mislabel" remediation?

Fix Critical/High from either reviewer, re-review the fixed area. Then write the project's review-completed marker (nx scratch put per the pre-push hook convention) naming this bead and both verdicts.

Acceptance:
- code-review-expert run, Critical/High resolved.
- substantive-critic run with the locked design as the spec, Critical/High resolved, non-vacuity explicitly confirmed.
- review-completed marker written.
- nexus-itme7 may close ONLY after this gate is clean AND nexus-5d022 (local run.sh --guided green) is the demonstrated closing criterion.
close_reason: STACKED REVIEW COMPLETE (both reviewers, per gate). code-review-expert: approve-with-followups — independently re-verified every pinned diagnostic + guard ordering against source; 6 Lows filed as nexus-qxmhx (none blocking). substantive-critic: approve — re-derived all 6 decision-surface rows from detection/pregate/driver/sequencer source; 1 Significant (shape iii on the shared main-seed path demonstrated only on the guided leg) ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE: run.sh --cold executed locally — caught the stale COLD_TAG (v0.1.37 < floor v0.1.39, the 2nd stale consumer of the floor bump; fixed + mechanically tripwired in test_engine_version.py) — then COLD-ACQUIRE MVV PASSED end-to-end incl. shape-iii parity (361692ee). Guided leg green locally AND in the GitHub MVV workflow on both arc commits. Critique bonus: the 'pre-existing CI failure' was verified rather than dismissed -> real breakage, fixed 975dcd9a.

title: Local run.sh --guided container run GREEN (the closing criterion)
description:
Parent: nexus-itme7. Depends on nexus-cs6t0. This is the bead's whole point: the Docker rehearsal container must pass locally BEFORE commit — CI is not the first place this runs.

RUN:  tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --guided
(Builds the wheel + LINUX native nexus-service binary in a GraalVM container, ~2-3m, then runs the full guided MVV. Several minutes total. Requires Docker Desktop up.)

PASS CRITERIA:
- Terminal line "GUIDED-UPGRADE MVV PASSED" printed, exit 0.
- The new "Phase 0 — blocked pre-flight" section prints its own PASS lines: non-zero exit observed for the blocking seed, all three block diagnostics matched, provisioning marker matched, remediation clean.
- The success phase still ends VERIFIED-and-unlocked with the extended parity (shape iii target holds SEED_N, source name 0).

IF IT FAILS:
- A VACUOUS pass (Phase 0's guided-upgrade exited 0 / a diagnostic didn't match) => the fixture dims/names are wrong (revisit it5wo's non-vacuity traps: (i) must be dim!=768; (ii) bge-768-named + 16-char ids; (iv) stale voyage half dim=768). Fix in it5wo/cs6t0 and re-run.
- A block firing on the WRONG cause (e.g. (ii) blocking on model-support instead of legacy_ids, or (i) blocked as voyage-no-key) => wrong seed shape; re-derive against detection.py/pregate.py.
- If a shipped guard genuinely does NOT fire end-to-end => that is a PRODUCT BUG: FILE a separate bead, do not weaken the assertion to make the rehearsal pass.

Also run `uv run pytest` (full unit suite) green — nothing in the unit tree may regress.

Acceptance:
- `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --guided` exits 0 with GUIDED-UPGRADE MVV PASSED locally, Phase-0 section green, non-vacuously (block asserts demonstrably matched real diagnostics).
- Full `uv run pytest` green.
- Capture the passing run's Phase-0 + parity output lines to T1 scratch (tag nexus-itme7) as the non-vacuity record.
Reminders: this is a long container run — do not background-accumulate multiple runs; one at a time.
close_reason: Closing criterion met: local tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --guided ended GUIDED-UPGRADE MVV PASSED with the new Phase-0 section fully green (sub-run A collision block + PG-acquire marker + no sentinel; sub-run B ModelPreGateBlocked naming both shapes + sentinel + clear-state; success run VERIFIED and unlocked; shape-iii parity; Chroma intact). Engine stamped 0.1.39, develop 147be437.

title: rehearse_guided.sh: Phase 0 blocked pre-flight + parity/marker placement
description:
Parent: nexus-itme7. Depends on nexus-it5wo (seed modes must exist). Add the Phase-0 blocked pre-flight section to tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_guided.sh and adjust marker/parity assertions.

CONTEXT: T1 scratch tag "nexus-itme7" (resolved open items + the demonstration bytes captured by nexus-it5wo). Design: memory_get(project="nexus", title="design-itme7-legacy-names-rehearsal.md").

Extract each row's `--path <value>` via regex. Return set of in-use paths. Mirror the parsing style of _parse_orphan_t1_chromadb_candidates (skip blank/non-matching/malformed rows). NOTE: ps command here is `pid,command` (no ppid/etime needed), distinct from the sibling's `pid,ppid,etime,command`.

2. New wrapper `_live_t1_chromadb_paths() -> set[str]`: run the ps subprocess, call the parser. Fail OPEN (return empty set) on subprocess.CalledProcessError / FileNotFoundError / OSError — matches every other sweep failure mode in this module (best-effort, non-fatal). Mirror the try/except in sweep_orphan_t1_chromadbs (~548).

3. `_sweep_one_tmpdir_root` (~229) gains optional param `live_paths: set[str] | None = None`. Before the mtime check (before line ~249), skip (log at debug via _log.debug, do NOT rmtree) any candidate whose `str(d)` is in live_paths.

4. `sweep_orphan_tmpdirs` (~262) computes live_paths once via `_live_t1_chromadb_paths()` and threads it through BOTH _sweep_one_tmpdir_root calls (config_dir/t1 ~296 + legacy OS-tempdir ~301).

CORRECTNESS PROPERTY (from design): str(d) from root.glob("nx_t1_*") is byte-identical to the --path value on the process cmdline — both originate from the same str(tmpdir) in _make_t1_store_dir (~206/221) passed to Popen([..., "--path", tmpdir]) in start_t1_server (~627, --path at ~675). Exact string match holds; no realpath/symlink resolution needed.

TDD ORDER (test file BEFORE impl):
- Parser tests -> tests/test_session_sweep_orphan_t1_chromadbs.py (sibling _parse_orphan_t1_chromadb_candidates tests live there). Cover: row with markers + --path extracted; row missing "chroma run"; row missing "nx_t1_"; row with live parent (ppid != 1) STILL matched (this is the key differentiator vs the kill gate — assert a non-init-parented row is included); malformed/blank rows skipped; empty input -> empty set; multiple live paths.
- _sweep_one_tmpdir_root live_paths tests -> tests/test_session.py (sweep_orphan_tmpdirs tests live there, ~225+). NON-VACUITY ASSERT (design step 2): in ONE call with live_paths={one candidate's path}, assert the live candidate SURVIVES despite mtime > cutoff AND a second non-live stale candidate IS reaped. Proves the skip is real, not that nothing was reaped.
- Regression: existing sweep_orphan_tmpdirs tests must stay green. If sweep_orphan_tmpdirs now calls _live_t1_chromadb_paths() internally, monkeypatch it (or the ps subprocess) to return empty set so existing mtime-only tests are unchanged. Confirm existing tests still pass.

CONSTRAINTS:
- structlog only (_log.debug for the skip), no print.
- Pure parser: no subprocess, no I/O — test against synthetic ps strings.
- Deterministic tests.

TEST COMMANDS (narrow first, full before handing to review):
  uv run pytest tests/test_session_sweep_orphan_t1_chromadbs.py tests/test_session.py -q
  uv run ruff check src/nexus/session.py tests/test_session.py tests/test_session_sweep_orphan_t1_chromadbs.py
  uv run pytest   # full unit suite green is the closing criterion

Use mcp__plugin_sn_serena__jet_brains_get_symbols_overview / find_symbol for navigation; insert_after_symbol for the new functions. Use sequential-thinking only if the regex/threading proves non-obvious (it should not).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PLAN-AUDIT CONCERN #1 (HIGH — not covered by the locked design's correctness property): ps command-column TRUNCATION.

`ps -eo command` truncates long command lines to terminal/column width. A live nx_t1_ path (config_dir + long tempfile suffix + other chroma args) can exceed that width, cutting off or mangling the `--path <value>` token -> exact str(d) match FAILS -> live dir reaped anyway == the reported bug reproduces.

FIX in the impl: run ps with truncation DISABLED — `ps -eo pid,command -ww` (double -w = unlimited width) for _live_t1_chromadb_paths. Add a test with a LONG synthetic nx_t1_ path to prove --path extraction survives full width.

WHY the sibling didn't need this: _parse_orphan_t1_chromadb_candidates (the KILL gate) only needs the nx_t1_ substring PRESENT, not the full path, so truncation is tolerable there. Our PROTECT gate needs the FULL path value, so -ww is load-bearing.
