title: P1.3 Adopt HttpMemoryStore onto the mixin (canonical first consumer)
description:
TDD step 3. Prove the mixin works on a REAL store, end-to-end, within Phase 1 (strong integration signal before the mass sweep). depends on P1.2.

File: src/nexus/db/t2/http_memory_store.py (currently: baked self._headers at :106-110, httpx.Client(headers=...) at :112-116, self._post at :539, self._raise_for_status at :545). Keep keyword-only _token ctor. Swap the baked pattern for mixin inheritance; delete the now-duplicated self._post/_raise.

Add a store-level self-heal test (in test_refreshable_client.py or the memory test file): construct HttpMemoryStore against the fake service, rotate the valid bearer, assert put() self-heals and succeeds.

Verify RawHandleGuardMixin MRO still works (HttpMemoryStore(RawHandleGuardMixin) -> now also RefreshableHttpStoreMixin). Confirm .conn/._lock still fail loud (nexus-9613q.2 contract).

Reminders: mcp sequential-thinking if MRO/init ordering gets subtle. This is the template the Phase-2 sweep beads copy — get it clean.
acceptance_criteria: HttpMemoryStore (src/nexus/db/t2/http_memory_store.py) inherits RefreshableHttpStoreMixin; its hand-rolled construction-time-baked self._headers + self._post + self._raise_for_status are replaced by the mixin's. Existing memory tests stay green: uv run pytest tests/db/test_http_memory_store_integration.py tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py -x. A new test proves a rotated bearer self-heals through HttpMemoryStore.put specifically.
notes:
AUDIT REVISION (HIGH): reframe from 'drop 3 baked methods' to 'route EVERY inline self._client.* call through the mixin'. HttpMemoryStore's READ methods (put uses self._post, but reads at ~:268-359 call self._client.* inline) must ALL go through the mixin's _post/_get or they gain zero retry coverage — the bug survives on reads. Acceptance now requires: grep 'self\._client\.' in http_memory_store.py returns ZERO inline call sites after conversion (all via mixin). Add a read-path self-heal test.
DEFERRED FROM nexus-bikit.3 review (substantive-critic Significant finding, round 1): add a scripted regression test guarding against future self._client.<verb>() bypasses of the mixin (grep-based, matching this project's 'gates must be scripted, not ambient' convention) -- e.g. assert zero matches for 'self._client\.(get|post|put|delete|request)\(' in any file that imports/inherits RefreshableHttpStoreMixin, outside _refreshable_client.py itself. Could not land in bikit.3 (mixin-only, no adopters exist yet -- the guard would need an allowlist that shrinks per-adopter, or should simply land once the first real adopter (this bead) exists to protect). Add this guard as part of adopting HttpMemoryStore.
close_reason:
HttpMemoryStore adopted onto RefreshableHttpStoreMixin as the canonical first consumer -- the template the f2qvx.* sweep beads copy. Zero inline self._client.* call sites remain (grep-verified: 0 matches across all ~12 original sites -- get, resolve_title, search, list_entries, get_projects_with_prefix, search_glob, search_by_tag, get_all, delete, expire, put, import_entry, put_or_merge, flag_stale_memories, merge_memories). get()'s 404-as-None and merge_memories()'s 409-as-KeyError contracts preserved. Mixin extended with _delete() (needed, didn't exist) and _resolve_token_only() (for base_url-explicit-token-omitted construction). New store-level self-heal tests (write + read path), a scripted bypass-guard regression test, and a mixin-level retry-path test. Full tests/db/ sweep green (935 passed), ruff clean, RawHandleGuardMixin's .conn/._lock fail-loud contract reconfirmed.

2 rounds of stacked review: round 1 found 1 Critical (the mixin's construction-time token-only-resolution fix was never mirrored into the RETRY path -- _invalidate_and_reresolve still called full resolve_service_endpoint() unconditionally, which would have broken self-heal for exactly the base_url-pinned callers the fix was meant to unblock) + a docstring overclaim + a process note about the fix landing without a dedicated re-review. Fixed with matching 3-way branch logic in _invalidate_and_reresolve, a new test proving the retry path specifically (empirically verified non-vacuous: reverted the fix, confirmed the test fails with the exact predicted error, restored, confirmed it passes), and a tightened docstring. Round 2: both reviewers independently re-traced the fix and re-verified non-vacuity themselves. Both clean, 0 remaining findings.

Committed 51eb39ad on develop.

title: P1.2 Implement RefreshableHttpStoreMixin
description:
TDD step 2. Make P1.1's failing tests pass. depends on P1.1.

New file: src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py — class RefreshableHttpStoreMixin.

Design shape (from locked memo):
- Per-instance state: self._base_url, self._tenant, self._token (cached, invalidatable), self._client (httpx.Client kept alive — no whole-client teardown on 401).
- _auth_headers(): build {Authorization: Bearer <self._token>, X-Nexus-Tenant, Content-Type} FRESH each call from the CURRENT cached token (not baked once at __init__).
- _post(path, payload) / _get(path, **params): issue request with per-request headers=_auth_headers(); on _is_retryable_endpoint_error -> _invalidate_and_reresolve() -> retry ONCE; second failure raises.
- _is_retryable classifier mirrors http_vector_client.py:194-213 (401 via httpx.HTTPStatusError.response.status_code==401; ConnectionRefusedError/ConnectionResetError incl. httpx.ConnectError/RemoteProtocolError).
- _invalidate_and_reresolve(): re-call resolve_service_endpoint() -> (base_url, token); update self._base_url AND self._token. CRITICAL (the f2qvx half): base_url MUST update — a supervisor restart changes the port; header-only refresh leaves the client pointed at a dead port. Reconcile with "keep the httpx.Client" by issuing requests against the resolved absolute URL / rebuilding the client's base_url on change. This reconciliation is the crux of closing BOTH halves — flag it clearly in code comments for the stacked review.
- _raise_for_status parity: match existing per-store descriptive httpx.HTTPStatusError shape (see http_memory_store.py:545-559).

Reminders: mcp sequential-thinking for the client-vs-base_url reconciliation decision. Do NOT touch HttpVectorClient, HttpScratchStore, HttpTokenStore (out of scope). Structured logging only. Type hints on all public methods.
acceptance_criteria: src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py defines RefreshableHttpStoreMixin. All three tests from P1.1 pass. Mixin: keeps ONE per-instance httpx.Client; resolves Authorization header FRESH per request from a per-instance cached-but-invalidatable token; _send/_post/_get retry EXACTLY once on 401 OR ConnectionRefused/Reset by invalidating cached credential and re-resolving via resolve_service_endpoint() (updating base_url too, for port churn); a second failure propagates. Run: uv run pytest tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py -x
notes: AUDIT REVISION (MEDIUM, urllib->httpx mismatch): do NOT copy http_vector_client's _is_retryable_endpoint_error verbatim — it classifies urllib.error.HTTPError/URLError. The T2 stores use httpx. Rewrite the classifier for httpx types: 401 via httpx.HTTPStatusError (resp.status_code==401 from raise_for_status), connection failures via httpx.ConnectError/ConnectTimeout/ReadError/RemoteProtocolError (and underlying ConnectionRefusedError/ConnectionResetError). Mirror the SHAPE (invalidate+retry-once), not the exception taxonomy. Mixin must provide BOTH _post AND _get (and any _request primitive) — every transport method self-heals, not just writes.
close_reason:
RefreshableHttpStoreMixin implemented: src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py. Both read (_get) and write (_post) paths route through one shared retry wrapper -- on 401 or connection-refused/timeout/reset, re-resolve the endpoint fresh (both base_url AND token, closing the f2qvx connection-staleness half) and retry exactly once. httpx.Client kept alive across refresh (base_url built per-request from a plain reassignable string field, not baked into the client at construction). All 12 tests pass (4 from bikit.2 + 8 added during review), full tests/db/ sweep green (930 passed, no regressions), ruff clean.

2 rounds of stacked review: round 1 found 1 Critical (classifier missed httpx.ConnectTimeout/ReadError, verified via real httpx MRO -- neither is a subclass of what was already handled, so 2 of the 4 documented restart-window failure signatures were silently unhandled) + 3 Significant (no bypass guard for direct self._client calls; POST retry-safety unenforced; retry silently overrode an explicit constructor pin). Fixed: classifier now covers all 4 signatures with 7 new direct unit tests; pin-tracking added (self._base_url_pinned/self._token_pinned captured in __init__ before env-resolution fallback overwrites the locals) so a fully-pinned instance fails loud with a clean RuntimeError instead of silently repointing to the ambient environment -- new test proves this via a real 401 round-trip, not a mocked shortcut. 2 lower-severity findings soundly deferred with concrete, checkable acceptance criteria recorded as bd notes on nexus-bikit.4 (bypass guard -- needs a real adopter to be non-vacuous) and nexus-f2qvx (POST idempotency audit -- needs a concrete non-idempotent consumer to design against). Round 2: both reviewers independently verified the httpx MRO claims live and confirmed the deferrals are genuinely sequenced, not corner-cutting. Both clean, 0 remaining findings.

Committed 6eaa0d22 on develop.

title: P1.1 TDD harness + failing mixin tests (generalized flat-bearer fake service)
description:
TDD step 1 for nexus-bikit. Write the generalized fake-server harness + failing tests BEFORE the mixin exists.

Context / reference reads:
- Design (locked): nx memory get -p nexus -t design-bikit-refreshable-http-store-mixin.md
- Harness to GENERALIZE (do NOT edit it): tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py — copy the _FakeHandler / _free_port / threaded-HTTPServer / module-level-mutable-state pattern (lines 40-223), but collapse the dual session-dict model (bearer + X-Nexus-T1-Session) down to a SINGLE flat mutable "currently valid bearer token".
- Reference pattern being mirrored: src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py — _is_retryable_endpoint_error (194-213), _invalidate_endpoint (187-191), one-shot retry.

Harness requirements (tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py):
1. Module-level mutable _VALID_BEARER (str) + _ALWAYS_401 flag; a fake handler that 401s when Authorization bearer != _VALID_BEARER.
2. A minimal concrete test-only store subclass of the (not-yet-built) RefreshableHttpStoreMixin exercising _post/_get against a trivial echo endpoint.
3. Levers: rotate _VALID_BEARER mid-test (token-republish sim); flip _ALWAYS_401 (persistent-failure sim); shutdown server + restart on a NEW port with env repointed (port-churn / connection-refused sim).
4. resolve_service_endpoint() reads NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT/TOKEN fresh per call (confirmed stateless) — mutate env via monkeypatch to drive re-resolution.

Three failing tests (mirror TestSelfHeal in the reference file):
- test_stale_bearer_selfheals_and_recovers
- test_persistent_401_retries_exactly_once_then_raises  (assert exactly ONE retry, not a loop)
- test_connection_refused_reresolves_baseurl_and_retries_once  (the f2qvx half — proves the PORT updates, not just the header)

Reminders: use mcp sequential-thinking for the harness design (the port-churn lever is the subtle bit). SPAWN nothing — this is single-file focused work. Keep randomness seeded, ports via port=0 (_free_port). Deterministic only.
acceptance_criteria: New tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py exists with a generalized flat-bearer fake-HTTP-server harness (NOT the session-dict model). Three failing tests: (a) token rotated out from under a live instance self-heals on next call; (b) persistent-401 retries exactly ONCE then raises cleanly; (c) connection-refused/port-churn after a supervisor restart re-resolves base_url via resolve_service_endpoint() and retries once. All FAIL because the mixin does not exist yet. Run: uv run pytest tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py -x
notes: AUDIT REVISION (HIGH): add a READ-path self-heal test, not just a write. The core 401 bug lives on GET/read call sites too. At least one test must rotate the bearer then exercise a _get/read op and assert it self-heals — a put-only test leaves read paths unproven.
close_reason: TDD harness complete: tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py, 4 tests (up from the planned 3 -- added a GET-path self-heal test during review) pinning the RefreshableHttpStoreMixin contract for bead nexus-bikit.3 to satisfy: retry-exactly-once on 401 (both read and write paths) and on connection-refused/port-churn, persistent-401 propagates cleanly after exactly one retry. All 4 tests confirmed failing for the correct reason (ModuleNotFoundError on the not-yet-built nexus.db.t2._refreshable_client). 2 rounds of stacked review: round 1 found and fixed 2 Critical gaps (read-path 401 was completely unexercised -- would let a _post-only fix pass; connection-refused test had no retry-count assertion -- would let an unbounded retry loop pass) + 1 Significant (docstring overclaim on a timeout constructor param). Round 2: both reviewers independently hand-traced the fix arithmetic and control flow, both clean, 0 remaining findings. Committed c97a1aff on develop. No regressions in tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py (41 passed).

title: native-smoke.sh T1 real-client section never runs in CI (engine-service-release.yml has no uv/Python)
design:
Confirmed via direct grep: engine-service-release.yml (the ONLY workflow that invokes service/native-smoke.sh) never installs uv/Python -- no astral-sh/setup-uv, no actions/setup-python. Every other repo workflow that DOES install uv (ci.yml, release.yml, guided-upgrade-mvv.yml, cold-install-rehearsal.yml, plan-schema-check.yml, local-service-gate-nightly.yml) never calls native-smoke.sh.

Effect: the new "T1 via the REAL Python client" section added to native-smoke.sh under nexus-97oz3 (uncommitted as of this critique) always hits `command -v uv` failure -> WARN+skip on both smoked matrix legs (linux-amd64, linux-arm64). mac-arm64 has matrix smoke:false and doesn't run native-smoke.sh at all. So the fix has zero effect in the actual release gate; it only exercises the real Python client path when a developer happens to have uv on PATH locally.

FIX: add an astral-sh/setup-uv step (pinned SHA, matching the convention already used in 6 other workflows) + `uv sync` (or minimal editable install) to engine-service-release.yml's build-publish job, before the "Native smoke test" step. Then verify via workflow_dispatch that the Actions log shows "ok t1 real-client put/get/search/list" rather than "WARN skipping".

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-native-smoke-97oz3-t1-real-client-ci-gap.md
Blocks proper closure of nexus-97oz3 (T1 routing+backend seam) -- that bead's fix is currently a local-dev-only convenience, not a closed CI gate.
close_reason: Shipped commit c3a8f249 on develop. Added astral-sh/setup-uv@37802adc94f370d6bfd71619e3f0bf239e1f3b78 (v7, pinned SHA matching this repo's existing convention) + 'uv sync' to engine-service-release.yml's build-publish job, gated on matrix.target.smoke (mac-arm64 doesn't smoke, doesn't pay for the toolchain). Verified locally: built a real macOS ARM64 native binary, ran native-smoke.sh twice (before/after review fixes), both times 'ok t1 real-client put/get/search/list', NATIVE SMOKE PASS, exit 0. Not yet verified via an actual GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch run (substantive-critic's recommendation) -- local verification confirms the Python client logic is correct against a real native artifact, but the CI-specific execution path (uv actually resolving/installing in the GH Actions runner) has not been dry-run. Flagging this gap explicitly rather than silently closing over it.

title: nexus-36q84 fix left 3 of 4 T1-touching hooks unpatched: post_compact_hook.sh, subagent-start.sh, divergence-language-guard.sh
design:
Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-ngcpo-36q84-t1-refresh-session-collision-2026-07-12

nexus-36q84 fixed session-id collision (current_session flat file clobbered by a
sibling top-level Claude Code session) ONLY in pre_close_verification_hook.sh
(PreToolUse/Bash), by parsing session_id out of the hook's own stdin JSON payload
and exporting NX_SESSION_ID before calling `nx scratch list`.

grep of conexus/hooks/scripts/*.sh for `nx scratch (list|put)` found 3 MORE call
sites with the identical vulnerability, none patched:

  - post_compact_hook.sh (PostCompact hook) line 23: `nx scratch list`.
    Does not currently capture stdin at all -- needs `STDIN=$(cat)` added first.
  - subagent-start.sh (SubagentStart hook) line 264: `nx scratch list`.
    Already captures `STDIN=$(cat)` (line 45) and parses task/prompt from it --
    adding session_id extraction + NX_SESSION_ID export is a same-shape addition.
  - divergence-language-guard.sh (PostToolUse/Write|Edit hook) line 75:
    `nx scratch put`. Already captures `STDIN=$(cat)` (line 20) and parses
    tool_name/file_path from it -- same trivial addition applies.

All 4 hooks (including the fixed one) are launched identically via
`bash $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/scripts/X.sh` per conexus/hooks/hooks.json --
none is the detached nx-session-end-launcher grandchild case. session.py's new
CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID env tier (added by this same nexus-36q84 round) is
documented as "verified empirically" only for Bash-tool-call subprocesses and
Agent-tool-dispatched subagents -- hook subprocess spawn is a THIRD, unverified
spawn mechanism. pre_close_verification_hook.sh's own fix deliberately avoided
relying on that env tier (parsing stdin JSON directly instead), which is
evidence the env tier was judged insufficient/unverified for hook contexts --
undermining any assumption that the other 3 hooks are covered transitively.

Fix: apply the identical stdin-session_id-export pattern to all 3 remaining
hooks (add stdin capture to post_compact_hook.sh first). Consider a grep-based
CI gate so a future hook touching T1/scratch can't reintroduce this class.
close_reason: Shipped commit cd24e057 on develop. Applied the proven pre_close_verification_hook.sh pattern to post_compact_hook.sh, subagent-start.sh, and divergence-language-guard.sh -- all three now export session_id from their own stdin JSON before any nx scratch call. New TDD tests for all three (9 new tests total). Full suite green (12790 passed, 0 failed).

title: current_session file is machine-wide, not scoped per top-level Claude Code session — silent T1 cross-session misdirection
description:
CLI-vs-MCP dual-interface critique of the T1 service cutover (nexus-rn3wo.1, 2026-07-11) found that src/nexus/session.py's CLAUDE_SESSION_FILE ('current_session' under nexus_config_dir()) is a SINGLE, machine-wide, unscoped flat file, not scoped per top-level Claude Code session.

ROOT CAUSE: hooks.session_start() (src/nexus/hooks.py ~lines 69-78) writes current_session unconditionally whenever NX_SESSION_ID is not already inherited from a parent process. Grepped the entire src/ and conexus/ tree for any programmatic export of NX_SESSION_ID into a top-level session's own environment -- there is none; only operators/dispatch.py forwards it deliberately for NESTED claude -p dispatch. Every ordinary top-level interactive Claude Code session therefore relies on this ONE shared file. resolve_active_session_id() (session.py) is consumed identically by T1Database._init_new_discovery Path B (t1.py ~190-205), get_t1_database()'s tier-2 lease lookup (t1.py ~1117-1125), and _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch 0's own resolution (mcp/core.py ~422-427).

IMPACT: if a SECOND top-level Claude Code session starts on the same machine/config dir (routine for this user -- parallel worktree-agent workflows, multiple concurrent terminal sessions across projects), its SessionStart hook CLOBBERS the file with its own session id. Any Bash-tool-spawned CLI subprocess or PreToolUse hook subprocess in the FIRST session, invoked after that point, resolves the SECOND session's id via the exact same flat-file fallback every T1 discovery path shares. Concretely: the review-completed marker convention's write (nx scratch put via Bash, CLI) and read (pre_close_verification_hook.sh's nx scratch list, CLI) can silently resolve into a DIFFERENT live session's T1 lease (or the shared CLI-dedicated identity) than the one that actually ran the review -- a false-positive or false-negative marker check across sessions. Also affects any other CLI-invoked T1 op (put/get/search/list) run from Bash mid-session once a second top-level session has started.

Damage is bounded today: pre_close_verification_hook.sh is explicitly advisory only (never blocks, per its own header comment), so this doesn't currently cause a hard failure -- but it undermines the per-bead correctness semantics the review-completed convention exists for, silently.

RECOMMENDATION (from the critique):
1. State this as an explicit, auditable invariant in t1.py's module docstring or the T1 cutover design doc (T2 nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md): 'CLI<->MCP write/read convergence holds only while current_session still points at the writing session -- i.e. only until a second top-level session starts on the same machine and overwrites it. Concurrent top-level sessions are not isolated for this path.'
2. Write a regression test simulating two hooks.session_start() calls racing to overwrite current_session (not just monkeypatching NX_SESSION_ID per-test, which is what every existing test in tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py does -- none exercise the flat-file-clobber scenario) and assert either isolation or a loud, detectable failure mode instead of silent cross-session misdirection.
3. Consider whether current_session should become scoped (e.g. keyed by parent PID or a session-specific identifier derivable without relying on the same collision-prone mechanism) rather than a single global file -- the deeper fix, not just documenting the risk.

Related: the review-completed marker's write-side reasoning ('must be CLI because the hook is CLI-only') is itself backwards per the same critique -- only the READ side (the bash hook) is structurally forced to CLI; the MCP-tool WRITE path is actually the STRONGER, more direct option (in-process, unambiguous, uses the token the MCP already owns) and nothing mechanically enforces which one gets used today (only a CLAUDE.md prose reminder). Worth considering as part of the same fix: either make the MCP scratch tool's put also best-effort publish to whatever the CLI-hook path reads (closing the gap mechanically), or add a cheap nx doctor self-check that round-trips a probe write-then-CLI-read within a live session to catch drift operationally.

Verified by direct code trace (session.py, hooks.py, t1.py, mcp/core.py), not inferred from design-doc prose. Full record: T2 nexus/t1-cli-mcp-dual-entry-point-critique-2026-07-12.md.
close_reason: Shipped commit 2f9144df on develop. resolve_active_session_id() gained a CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID tier (empirically verified identical across a top-level session and its Agent-tool subagents) between NX_SESSION_ID and the collision-prone current_session flat file. pre_close_verification_hook.sh hardened to extract session_id from its own stdin JSON independent of env-inheritance assumptions. Genuine collision-regression test proves the fix. Stacked review found 1 Critical (3 sibling hooks sharing the identical vulnerability, unpatched) -- fixed same session, nexus-7o1zh, commit cd24e057.

title: T1 SERVICE session tokens have no refresh mechanism — 24h TTL silently kills long-lived MCP sessions; lease-borrow has no freshness check, no ownership recovery
description:
Holistic substantive-critic review of the T1 service cutover (nexus-rn3wo.1, 602dcbcd/1c28381a/19e869e8, 2026-07-11) found a cluster of related gaps in session-token lifecycle management that none of the 5 remediation rounds addressed (they fixed clean-shutdown lease publish/clear and nested-dispatch rotation, never asked what happens across an UNCLEAN shutdown + long session lifetime).

ROOT CAUSE: HttpTokenStore.start_session() mints a token with a server-side default TTL of 24h (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/SessionTokenHandler.java DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS=86_400L). No Python caller passes ttl_seconds, so every mint gets exactly this default. Phase E (require-minted) means an expired token 401s rather than degrading to a trusted bare session id.

FINDING 1 (no refresh): mcp/core.py's _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch 0 (SERVICE path, the T1 hard default since this cutover) mints ONCE at MCP startup (line ~484: `_ts.start_session(_t1_session_id)`) and never re-mints again for the life of the process. There is no periodic refresh/keep-alive task for Branch 0 — contrast with Branch 3 (the old Chroma-owned path), which DOES have exactly this pattern: `_t1_heartbeat_loop` (core.py ~line 168), created after Branch 3's lease publish, re-stamping liveness periodically (RDR-149 P4). That mechanism was never extended to Branch 0. Any live MCP session that stays connected past 24h wall-clock (plausible: long dev sessions, scheduled/cron CCR agents via the `schedule` skill, laptop-sleep-preserved sessions) will have every T1 put/get/search/list start 401ing for the rest of the session, with no self-heal anywhere on this path (HttpScratchStore._post/_post_raw just raise RuntimeError(SESSION_UNAUTHORIZED_MARKER) on 401 -- no retry). The MCP-facing error surfaces via _mcp_tool_error, which (unlike commands/scratch.py's _clean_service_errors) does NOT special-case SESSION_UNAUTHORIZED_MARKER, so the agent gets a generic error with no "reconnect the MCP" guidance.

FINDING 2 (no lease freshness check): get_t1_database()'s tier-2 lease-borrow (src/nexus/db/t1.py ~line 1119-1125) and mcp/core.py Branch-0's own startup self-check (core.py ~line 441-450) both call read_t1_session_lease(), which is a bare file read with NO TTL/liveness check -- confirmed via the function's own docstring ("intentionally adds no orphan sweep / TTL of its own"). This directly contradicts the surrounding design comment's claim to "mirror the existing t1_addr.<session_id> Chroma-lease pattern" -- that pattern (nexus/daemon/t1_lease.py discover_t1_lease) DOES use TTL-based freshness ("Liveness is lease freshness (TTL), not pid"). A lease left behind by a non-cleanly-terminated (SIGKILL/OOM) prior MCP process for the same session id will be blindly borrowed by (a) a NEW live MCP restart for that same session id -- silently starting the whole new session on a token that may already be near/past its TTL, with no re-mint attempted -- and (b) any sibling bare-CLI/hook process (SessionEnd hook, or a plain terminal `nx scratch` call) reading the same lease, hitting a raw unguided 401 with no self-heal (unlike tier-3's self-healing _CliDedicatedScratchStore wrapper).

FINDING 3 (no ownership recovery): mcp/core.py Branch-0's "borrow lease, yield, return" path (core.py ~444-450) does NOT set _OWNED_T1_SESSION. _t1_chroma_shutdown's early-return guard (`if not _OWNED_CHROMA and not _OWNED_T1_SESSION: return`) means a process that borrowed a lease never revokes the token or clears the lease file on its OWN clean exit either. Once a lease goes stale, there is no natural recovery path -- it just keeps getting silently re-borrowed (or 401ing) until a human manually deletes the lease file at ~/.config/nexus/t1_session_lease.<session_id>.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) add a periodic re-mint/refresh task for Branch 0 mirroring Branch 3's heartbeat pattern, refreshing well before the 24h TTL; (b) add TTL/freshness checking to read_t1_session_lease / _t1_session_lease_path (store an expiry alongside the token, or re-validate via a lightweight HEAD-style check) so a stale lease is detected and the caller falls through to mint-fresh instead of borrowing; (c) give tier-2 consumers (or at least the Branch-0 self-check) an explicit ownership-claim mechanism so a process that ends up owning a previously-orphaned lease takes responsibility for its lifecycle; (d) wire SESSION_UNAUTHORIZED_MARKER into _mcp_tool_error's remediation-hint logic so an MCP-agent-facing 401 gets the same "reconnect" guidance the CLI already has.

Verified by direct code reading (not review-doc summary): src/nexus/mcp/core.py, src/nexus/db/t1.py, src/nexus/db/http_scratch_store.py, src/nexus/daemon/t1_lease.py, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/SessionTokenHandler.java. Design doc T2 nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md does not mention token TTL/refresh anywhere.

title: Add real return-shape (dict key) parity assertions for T2 HTTP store integration tests
description:
tests/db/test_http_t2_store_parity.py is a STATIC signature guard only (method names + shared-prefix param names) -- it does not and cannot check return-VALUE shape (dict keys). Its docstring previously (falsely) claimed 'Return-SHAPE parity (dict keys) is exercised behaviourally by the -m integration suites in tests/db/test_http_*_integration.py against the real service' -- verified false by grep (zero key-set/shape assertions found in test_http_memory_store_integration.py, test_http_taxonomy_store_integration.py, test_http_telemetry_store_integration.py, test_http_scratch_store_integration.py). Docstring corrected 2026-07-11 to state reality (nexus-c4143-adjacent finding, substantive-critic review of the search_cmd distance-KeyError fix, commit pending).

Root cause this leaves undefended: when a store has TWO implementations with genuinely different backing stores (T1 scratch's ChromaDB-backed T1Database vs Postgres-backed HttpScratchStore is the clearest example -- T1Database.search() always returns a 'distance' key, HttpScratchStore.search() never does, and nothing caught this until a live KeyError crash), a consumer that assumes a field present in one backend's row shape survives a backend swap has zero test coverage protecting it. The nexus-rn3wo.1 T1 default-backend flip (2026-07-11) is exactly the kind of change that triggers this class of bug, and it will recur on any future dual-backend surface.

Scope: extend the -m integration suites (tests/db/test_http_*_integration.py) with an actual key-set parity check per store method that has TWO real implementations to compare (not all 9 T2 stores necessarily have this -- audit which ones are genuinely dual-backend vs service-only). For T1 scratch specifically: assert T1Database.search()/get()/list_entries() and HttpScratchStore.search()/get()/list_entries() share a documented COMMON key floor (the fields every consumer can rely on), with backend-specific extras (e.g. Chroma's 'distance') explicitly allowed to diverge and documented as such -- not silently assumed present by any consumer. Consider whether this generalizes to the existing frozen-contract pattern in t2_store_contract.py or needs a separate mechanism.
notes: RELEASE-GATE (Hal, 2026-07-13): no PyPI release cuts until this is DONE. Added to the release-blocker set.

title: catalog blind to docs a full non-skip index run just registered (GH #1397 Run A): manifest hook silent early-returns / possible duplicate-tumbler registration
description:

title: re-index cannot heal a missing catalog manifest: staleness skip keys on T3 chunk state only, so chunk_count=0 docs stay manifest-less and catalog-blind forever
description:
Confirmed in the field post-heal (GH #1397 follow-up, Steve, 2026-07-11) and at code level: check_staleness (indexer_utils.py ~503) returns 'current, skip' when the stored T3 chunk's (content_hash, embedding_model) matches — it NEVER consults the catalog document_chunks manifest. document_chunks rows are written only by the post-store flush hooks, which skipped files never trigger. Consequence: a doc whose chunks exist in T3 but whose manifest rows are missing (interrupted run, failed hook, the GH #1397 07-09 incident class) is PERMANENTLY skipped as current, its chunk_count stays 0, its indexed_at stays frozen, and every catalog-routed surface (nx catalog search, query-tool catalog routing, FTS, link seeding) is blind to it — while raw vector search works fine, making the gap invisible until someone compares surfaces. Field data: 7 docs (tumblers 1.3.142-150) still chunk_count=0 / frozen indexed_at AFTER a full re-index that reported them 'skipped (0.0s)'. The documented self-heal advice ('re-index repairs the manifest') is structurally wrong for exactly the docs that need it; today the only fix is touching the file (or deleting T3 chunks) to force staleness.

Secondary hazard: the persistent manifest gap keeps the nexus-mr89x GC hazard armed — any manifest-keyed orphan GC run against these docs classifies their live chunks as orphans.

Fix directions (pick at design time): (a) staleness check consults the manifest too — a doc with T3-current chunks but zero manifest rows is NOT current (cheap: the staleness cache build already sweeps per collection; add a manifest-count join); (b) skipped-current files still run a manifest-presence check + backfill hook (no re-embed needed — chashes are derivable from the T3 sweep); (c) an explicit nx catalog repair --backfill-manifest verb. (a) or (b) make self-heal actually self-heal; (c) alone repeats the manual-runbook pattern. Repro: index a repo, delete a doc's document_chunks rows + zero chunk_count, re-run nx index repo — doc reports skipped, manifest stays empty.
close_reason: Fixed in 4711f521 + 8a8d6262: nx index repo now runs a manifest self-heal pass (shared core nexus/catalog/manifest_heal.py, also backing nx catalog reconcile) AFTER per-file indexing and BEFORE the GC prunes — manifest-less docs whose chunks live in T3 heal WITHOUT re-embedding, closing the permanent-skip ghost class. Regression reproduces the field configuration exactly (inline-doc_id chunks) and is non-vacuity-proven at the final placement. Stacked review findings ALL actioned (nexus-prj2c closed). Full pytest 13129 green. FORCE-close rationale: the blocking dep nexus-94fxl (manifest-hook root cause) was explicitly deferred by Hal 2026-07-13 ('proven unnecessary in reality'); the self-heal makes any recurrence of that hook failure self-repairing within the same index run, which is precisely why the root-cause hunt could be deferred. mr89x stays open for its GC-side scope.

The correct workaround is 'nx index repo <repo> --force' (bypasses the skip check; full pipeline incl. manifest-writing post-store hooks; chash-keyed upserts so no duplicates, but re-embeds the whole repo). Corrected on GH #1397 (comment 4949473334), in the recovery gist Phase 4b + Phase 5, and in Steve's workaround prompt. A future fix could add per-file force or make --force-stale manifest-aware to avoid the whole-repo cost.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Substantive-critic finding (GH #1397 remediation-advice review, 2026-07-12): the --force workaround prescribed to Steve is NOT proven by the evidence already in hand, and Step 2's verification instruction is a confirmed false-negative trap.

1) Run A (Steve's ORIGINAL 2026-07-11 09:08-09:16 index, captured in the forensics bundle BEFORE any heal) already executed the exact non-skip code path --force would force: "RDR documents: 23 indexed (collection rdr__) — 0 current, 0 failed", real chunk counts for all 7 affected files (e.g. RDR-021 — 27 chunks). Yet `nx catalog search "RDR-021"` returned "No results" immediately after, in the SAME run's forensics capture — before the plain re-index (Run B) that later demonstrated the staleness-skip bug. Since --force reproduces the same full-pipeline mechanics Run A already used, there's no code-level reason a bare repeat behaves differently, UNLESS Run A's manifest write failed for a transient/one-off reason rather than something specific to these 7 docs.

2) manifest_write_batch_hook (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:1050) has two SILENT failure paths beyond the one that gets logged: `if not metadatas: return` (mcp_infra.py:1095) and `if not by_doc: return` (mcp_infra.py:1104) when catalog_doc_id/meta["doc_id"] are both empty. Neither logs, neither populates the _MANIFEST_WRITE_FAILURES collector that nx index's end-of-run summary reads (commands/index.py:590-604). A clean "0 failed" / no-WARNING run is therefore NOT proof the manifest write was attempted, let alone succeeded.

3) nx catalog reconcile (commands/catalog.py:801, the tool GH #1371's own WARNING message points operators at) only considers documents with `chunk_count > 0` as reconcile candidates. Steve's 7 docs are stuck at chunk_count=0 on both sides of every run captured so far -- reconcile would silently skip all 7. This is a doubly-broken state (empty manifest AND un-refreshed chunk_count cache), not the simpler partial-gap case reconcile targets, and hints the failure may be tied to catalog *row identity* for these specific pre-existing (07-09-vintage, tumblers 1.3.142-150) rows rather than a generic transient HTTP blip that a retry would clear.

4) Step 2 of the prompt sent to Steve says to verify with "the same SQLite query as the forensics." That query is against ~/.config/nexus/.catalog.db, which is provably dead in service mode: make_catalog_reader() (catalog/factory.py:138-176) and manifest_write_batch_hook's writer both route through HttpCatalogClient over HTTP when storage_backend_for("catalog") == SERVICE -- .catalog.db is never touched. This query will read chunk_count=0 / indexed_at=2026-07-09T17:42:10 FOREVER regardless of whether --force fixes the live service side, turning the prompt's Stop Condition 2 into an always-true false alarm. Fix: replace with `nx catalog show <tumbler>` (service-mode aware, same _get_catalog() reader) for all 7 tumblers.

Also noted: the "nx catalog search miss on a live-registered doc" item flagged as needing its own probe/bead in the mr89x thread does not appear to have been filed separately (bd search turned up nothing) -- it has been silently folded into this bead's --force fix instead of being tracked/verified on its own.

Recommend: do NOT let Steve run --force as a one-shot "fix and close" step. Have him run it, then check via nx catalog show (not raw SQLite) AND check nx index's stderr for the manifest-write-failure WARNING specifically. If the 7 docs are still chunk_count=0 post-force via the service-routed check, that confirms verdict (b) -- --force is a dead end -- and the next probe should compare the pre-existing 1.3.142-150 catalog rows' identity/content_hash against whatever tumbler --force's fresh registration produces for the same files (duplicate/ghost-row hypothesis).

title: nx index GC pruned 6 LIVE RDR docs from local Chroma (manifest-gap orphan misclassification); local-only prune diverged from service copy
description:
Field evidence (Steve, 2026-07-11, mid guided-upgrade remediation): during a fresh 'nx index repo' of an RDR corpus, the run's real-time upserts put 529 RDR chunks (551 final) into the service, then the LOCAL post-processing prune ('Pruning misclassified chunks' / 'Pruning deleted files', indexer.py _prune_deleted_files) deleted 6 CURRENT RDR documents from the local Chroma copy — RDR-016, RDR-018, RDR-019 (doc + post-mortem), RDR-020, RDR-021 — leaving 397 local chunks. The service copy was never pruned (the GC runs only against the local db handle), so local ended a strict SUBSET of the service. The subsequent migrate-to-service count-mismatch guard fired (correctly — it refused to reconcile the service DOWN), stranding a migrated-failed sentinel and degraded-LOUD reads. RDR-021's content existed ONLY in the service copy at that point.

Two distinct defects:
1. OVER-AGGRESSIVE ORPHAN CLASSIFICATION: _prune_deleted_files keys liveness on catalog.chashes_for_collection(collection_name); a manifest GAP (rows missing or stamped under a different collection name) classifies live chunks as orphans and deletes them. The nexus-oqku guard only protects the manifest-EMPTY case, not partial gaps. Candidate causes for the gap on those 6 docs: the catalog_document_chunks.collection stamp class (nexus-x6kdz, fixed engine v0.1.35 + boot backfill — was Steve's engine current?); housekeeping miss_count>=2 doc deletion via path/source_uri anchoring (the nexus-3e4s CWD class); or manifest rows written under the new conformant collection name while GC swept the old name. Needs forensics from Steve's install: index-run log around the prune phases + manifest row counts per collection for the rdr collection.
2. PRUNE ASYMMETRY ACROSS THE DUAL-WRITE SEAM: during the transitional dual-write, deletes/GC apply only to local Chroma, never the service — any prune (correct or not) forks the two copies and the migration guard then fires on the divergence. Here the asymmetry accidentally SAVED the data, but the seam guarantees count-mismatch failures for anyone indexing between provisioning and cutover completion.

Proposed: (a) partial-gap safety floor in GC — refuse to delete more than N%% of a collection's chunks (or any doc whose file demonstrably exists on disk) without explicit confirmation, mirroring the manifest-empty guard; (b) log each pruned doc_id/source_uri at INFO (the run gave no per-doc visibility — Steve had to reverse-engineer the 6 docs from set difference); (c) decide the dual-write prune contract (mirror to service, or suppress GC while a migration sentinel/dual-write is active). Related-not-duplicate: nexus-y2unb (skip prune on no-change runs), nexus-oqku (empty-manifest guard).
close_reason: GC-side defenses shipped (e2423e3b + dbdfac57): (a) partial-gap safety floor — refuses a sweep when orphans > NX_GC_FLOOR_FRACTION (default 0.25, chosen so the ACTUAL 2026-07-09 shape 154/551=27.9% is refused — the review caught the 0.5 first draft sailing it through) of DECIDABLE chunks AND >= 100 chunks, NX_GC_FORCE=1 override, fail-safe config parse; (b) per-doc visibility — every prune logs count+fraction+bounded (chash12,title) sample at INFO, ids at DEBUG; (c) dual-write prune asymmetry resolved by architecture (make_t3() service-unconditional post-P4a.2 — no local copy to fork; noted, no code). Defense stack: c21fk self-heal runs BEFORE this GC (placement test-pinned), so the misclassification INPUT is repaired first and the floor is the backstop. 9 tests incl. the field-incident shape, cross-collection isolation, boundary, malformed-config sweep. Full pytest 13138 green; unmasked local-service gate PASSED 475/33 with the restored voyage key; --with-cloud rehearsal PASSED (first ever run). Forensics fork on Steve's install stays with the GH #1397 probes; these defenses stand regardless of which branch it lands.

title: docs: fix two broken/misleading commands in blog/post-00-installing-nexus.md
description:

Found during substantive-critique of the 6.x surgical rewrite (2026-07-11), T2 nexus/blog-post-00-critique-2026-07-11.

title: Phase 0 (RDR-155 P4b prereq): make T1 scratch non-Chroma before the inverse-grep gate — route local CLI T1 through the PG-backed HttpScratchStore service (mint own session)
description:
Phase 0 hard prerequisite for RDR-155 P4b (final ChromaDB deletion). Canonical scope
(LOCKED 2026-07-11, remediated 2026-07-11 per stacked review nexus-c8yvj): T2
nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md (full design + evidence trail).
Supersedes the dual-option framing in T2
nexus/design-rdr155-p4b-rdr158-cutover-replan-2026-07-11.md §2/§6; scope is LOCKED to a
single approach.

DECISION (LOCKED, AS-IMPLEMENTED). Route local-mode T1 (session scratch) through the
EXISTING PG-backed HttpScratchStore service — the same substrate T2/T3 already use.
`storage_backend_for("t1")` no longer special-cases T1: it follows the same SERVICE hard
default as every other store (the `if canonical == "t1": return StorageBackend.SQLITE`
carve-out in storage_mode.py is removed).

AS-IMPLEMENTED DESIGN (this supersedes the first-draft "fresh uuid4() per bare-CLI
invocation" framing that was in this bead's original body — that draft was rejected
before implementation; see T2 design doc's "Design history" section for the full
audit trail of why):

1. Inherited live MCP session (`NX_T1_SESSION`/`NX_T1_SESSION_ID` present in env) →
   `HttpScratchStore` directly, unchanged from the pre-existing MCP-context path.
2. No inherited env, but a live MCP session for this Claude session published a lease
   (nexus-c8yvj remediation, see below) → use that session's token DIRECTLY via the
   published lease. Never mints/rotates.
3. No inherited env and no published lease → bare CLI: mint (or reuse) a
   CLI-DEDICATED, PERSISTED session id (`nexus.db.t1._cli_dedicated_session_id`,
   cached at `nexus_config_dir()/t1_cli_dedicated_session`, fcntl-election +
   atomic-publish race-safe first-creation). NEVER derived from
   `resolve_active_session_id()`/`NX_SESSION_ID`/`current_session` — that chain
   resolves a LIVE MCP session's id, and re-minting against it would rotate the live
   MCP's token out from under it (`HttpTokenStore.start_session` is
   `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`). Self-heals on a 401 from a racing sibling bare-CLI
   process re-minting the same dedicated id: `_CliDedicatedScratchStore` re-mints
   once and retries before propagating.

nexus-c8yvj REMEDIATION (2026-07-11 stacked review, P0, now CLOSED as part of this
bead's completion) — three findings fixed in the same pass:

1. CRITICAL: session_end_flush() (the SessionEnd hook) runs as a DETACHED grandchild
   OS process (nx-session-end-launcher), not a child of the live nx-mcp server, so it
   never inherits the MCP's in-process NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID env mutation.
   Post-cutover, with no inherited env, it fell into the CLI-dedicated branch above —
   a persisted id shared by every bare-CLI invocation on the machine, completely
   disjoint from the live MCP session's actual scratch data. Result: "Flushed 0
   scratch entries" on every SessionEnd, silently, always — no exception, no log line
   (a regression from the pre-cutover "narrow race, logged" contract to "always,
   silent, unlogged"). FIX: `mcp/core.py`'s `_t1_chroma_lifespan` Branch 0 now
   publishes the minted `(session_id, session_token)` to a lease file
   (`nexus.db.t1.publish_t1_session_lease`, `nexus_config_dir()/t1_session_lease.<id>`,
   mode 0o600, atomic temp-file + os.replace publish) immediately after minting, and
   removes it on teardown (`clear_t1_session_lease`). `get_t1_database()` checks
   `resolve_active_session_id()` + `read_t1_session_lease()` BEFORE falling into the
   CLI-dedicated path — this is a READ of an already-minted lease, never a re-mint, so
   the token-rotation hazard above does not apply. A stale/unlinked lease (MCP crashed
   without teardown) degrades to a clean RuntimeError on first use, caught by the
   hook's existing best-effort `except Exception`, matching the ORIGINAL pre-cutover
   "narrow race, logged, flush skipped" contract rather than inventing a new stronger
   guarantee.
2. Significant: `HttpTokenStore.start_session()` raises `httpx.HTTPStatusError` (via
   `resp.raise_for_status()`) on a non-2xx, not `RuntimeError` — so a bad
   `NX_SERVICE_TOKEN` bypassed both `_CliDedicatedScratchStore._call`'s
   `except RuntimeError` and `commands/scratch.py`'s `_clean_service_errors`, surfacing
   a raw traceback instead of the promised clean error. FIX: both call sites (the
   construction-time mint in `get_t1_database()` and `_CliDedicatedScratchStore._remint()`)
   now wrap `start_session()` in `except Exception as exc: raise RuntimeError(...) from exc`,
   mirroring the existing pattern already used in `mcp/core.py`'s own mint call.
3. Documentation: this bead body and the T2 design doc were stale (described the
   rejected first-draft approach as final). Both corrected in this update.

TDD (as-implemented, tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py — extended for
nexus-c8yvj):
- CLI-dedicated cache file: created on first use, reused/shared across separate
  `get_t1_database()` invocations, independent of `resolve_active_session_id()`,
  race-safe under 8 concurrent first-creation threads.
- Inherited live session: unchanged, never touches the CLI-dedicated cache file.
- `storage_backend_for("t1")` no longer special-cases T1.
- Self-heal: stale token recovers via one remint+retry; a persistent 401 retries
  exactly once then raises.
- Live-session lease (nexus-c8yvj finding 1): publish/read/clear round-trip; lease
  file mode 0o600; `get_t1_database()` prefers a published lease over CLI-dedicated
  and never touches the CLI-dedicated cache file when a lease resolves; a detached
  process reads data the live session wrote via the lease (the actual regression
  proof); falls through to CLI-dedicated when no lease is published or after
  `clear_t1_session_lease`; a stale/unlinked lease degrades to a clean RuntimeError,
  not a crash. `session_end_flush()` end-to-end: a flagged (`persist=True`) entry
  written under a live session IS flushed ("Flushed 1") when the hook only has
  `NX_SESSION_ID` resolvable (simulating the detached grandchild) and a lease was
  published; the no-lease/no-session baseline still reports "Flushed 0" without
  raising.
- Clean-error wrapping (nexus-c8yvj finding 2): both the construction-time mint and
  `_CliDedicatedScratchStore._remint()` wrap a simulated `httpx.HTTPStatusError` mint
  failure as `RuntimeError`, not a raw httpx exception.

WHY THIS MATTERS / GATING. Until this lands, nexus-19svb (RDR-155 P4b test bead)
cannot assert total Chroma removal without lying — a live EphemeralClient/HttpClient
construction path would otherwise survive in db/t1.py. This bead BLOCKS nexus-19svb
and must land before Phase 2 (the RDR-155 P4b test phase) starts.

SEPARATE (do NOT block on): the deployed cloud engine's T1 read-path 500 was a
DISTINCT bug (native-image jOOQ reflection registration gap for the `t1` schema),
root-caused and fixed 2026-07-11 (T2 nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md),
tracked to closure on nexus-opr9m (native build + cloud redeploy verification). No
dependency edge to that bead from this one.
notes:

title: Credential-staleness pattern independently reinvented 3x with no shared abstraction
description:
substantive-critic finding (2026-07-10, reviewing merged PR #1392 /
nexus-64np7): the "long-lived Http*Store client bakes its bearer token
into self._headers/httpx.Client at __init__, never rebuilds on 401"
bug is not aspect-worker-specific -- it's the DEFAULT construction
shape for essentially every T2 Http*Store class: HttpMemoryStore,
HttpTaxonomyStore, HttpTelemetryStore, HttpCentroidStore,
HttpPlanLibrary, HttpDocumentHighlightsStore, HttpChashIndex,
HttpDocumentAspectsStore, HttpCatalogClient, HttpTokenStore,
HttpScratchStore (critic grepped self._headers= / self._client= /
_resolve_endpoint() across src/nexus/db/t2/*.py + catalog/scratch --
all match). Only HttpVectorClient (T3) is immune, because it resolves
the token fresh per-request off a shared, auto-invalidating
module-level lease cache instead of baking it into a per-instance
header dict.

The codebase already documents the correct invariant explicitly --
src/nexus/db/service_endpoint.py:140-144: "service-backed clients
resolve ONCE at construction and hold a long-lived httpx.Client --
they ride a supervisor restart only because callers construct a fresh
client per operation... Do not cache a store instance across an
operation that may span a restart." This bug class is a violation of
that already-documented rule, not a novel discovery.

It has now been fixed THREE separate times, independently, with three
different implementations, and no shared decorator/mixin/base-class
factors it out:
  1. mcp_infra._service_t2_write_locked -- evict-on-any-exception (earliest)
  2. catalog/factory.py::_get_shared_service_catalog_client -- reactive
     eviction, its own comment says "same design here... same shape as
     the T2 Http*Store classes _service_t2_write_locked already fixed"
  3. aspect_worker_daemon._reclaim_once (nexus-64np7, this PR) -- the
     3rd independent reinvention

No lint rule catches a repeat. storage_boundary_lint.py's
BANNED_CONSTRUCTORS only bans raw T2Database/T3Database/Catalog()
construction (a write-routing concern, unrelated to credential
staleness).

Critic audited every current constructor call site of the 11 classes
above and found NO other currently-live long-lived (multi-hour+)
holder beyond the three that already self-heal -- so there is no live
4th bug today. That is a snapshot, not a guarantee:
aspect_worker_daemon.py's own docstring calls itself "one more leased
tier on the unified substrate," implying more daemons are expected on
this pattern, and the next one can trivially reintroduce this exact
bug with nothing to catch it.

Recommend: factor the evict-on-401/on-exception behavior into one
shared wrapper/mixin/decorator that every long-lived Http*Store holder
uses, OR at minimum add a lint/grep-based CI check that flags a new
"construct once at __init__ / hold across a loop" pattern on these
classes without a paired eviction path, and point future daemon
authors at service_endpoint.py's docstring + the 3 known instances in
review checklists.

Deliberately NOT implemented as part of the incident-cleanup session
that surfaced it (2026-07-10) -- designing a shared abstraction across
11 classes with 3 independent existing implementations is its own
design decision (which eviction semantics? on ANY exception, or only
auth-shaped ones? does it need a shared base class or is a decorator
cleaner given these classes have varied constructors?) and deserves
proper scoping, not a 4th ad hoc patch bolted on at 11pm.

title: catalog-013-3 still crash-loops on VIOLATING (not just missing) chash constraints; install-binary has no doctor gate
notes:
Context: nx (substantive-critic catch-up review, T2 nexus/critique-sot7v-pnwu0-2e65f5c8-b2f5fc0c)

Root: service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml
catalog-013-3's per-table DO blocks only guard `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
WHERE conname = '...')` before VALIDATE CONSTRAINT — i.e. they skip a MISSING
constraint. They do NOT tolerate a PRESENT-but-NOT-VALID constraint whose rows
genuinely VIOLATE it. A bare VALIDATE CONSTRAINT failure inside the unguarded DO
block is uncaught -> the whole bare-SQL changeset FAILS -> per Liquibase semantics
documented in this same file (MarkChangeSetRanGenerator refuses to record FAILED
execTypes) the changeset is never recorded and re-attempts (and re-fails) on EVERY
subsequent boot -> permanent crash-loop. Same failure class as the original
ms57z/GH#1390 bug (missing-constraint case, now fixed by 013-3's IF EXISTS guard),
just triggered by the opposite condition (present + violating).

nexus-pnwu0 (closed) shipped ONLY the doctor advisory (src/nexus/health.py
_check_migration_state Query 4, commit b2f5fc0c) as the fix for exactly this
scenario ("do not upgrade the engine until remediated"). But `nx daemon service
install-binary` (src/nexus/commands/daemon.py service_install_binary_cmd) has NO
coupling to `nx doctor` — verified by reading the command: it downloads, verifies,
and installs the binary with no health-check gate. An operator (or any unattended/
auto-upgrade automation) can install + restart without ever seeing the warning.
The advisory does not prevent the crash it names; it only informs an operator who
chooses to run `nx doctor` first and heeds it.

Known affected: canon-chat box (hhildebrand) — chunks_768_chash_len_check was
re-added post-incident ("mechanism unclear") while chunks_384/1024/chash_index/
catalog_document_chunks constraints remain dropped (GH#1390 forensic, T2
nexus/gh1390-forensic-CLOSED-self-inflicted). If that re-added constraint is
NOT VALID and chunks_768 holds any non-32-char chash rows, the NEXT engine
version that ships catalog-013-3 crash-loops that box on boot, doctor warning
or not.

Fix options (pick one, scope out at implementation time):
1. Give catalog-013-3 a per-table row-violation precondition (count non-32-char
   rows before each VALIDATE; skip+MARK_RAN, mirroring the missing-constraint
   guard) so a violating-but-present constraint degrades to "unproven" instead

2. Wire `nx daemon service install-binary` (or the restart path) to run the
   chash-conformance probe and block/require --force on a nonzero count.
3. Both — (1) is the engine-side correctness fix or a violating row will crash
   REGARDLESS of client-side gating; (2) is the operator-safety net.

Secondary (Significant, non-blocking) findings from the same review:
- No automated remediation path for knowledge__ MCP-note collections with legacy
  ids: `nx store export`/`import` round-trips ids verbatim (does not recompute
  chash), so the runbook's "re-put notes" remediation is manual re-transcription,
  not a re-index — worth a doc clarification and/or a real tool.
- rollback_collections has zero test coverage against a legacy-id-poisoned
  collection even though it is architecturally unaffected (no id-length guard in
  the rollback path, verified by code read) — the pnwu0 recovery playbook's
  load-bearing step 2 is unverified by any regression test.
PARTIAL FIX SHIPPED + root-fix scoped (develop 17f3f986). The install-binary GATE half is DONE: nx daemon service install-binary now runs the chash-conformance probe and refuses (exit 3) on a poisoned store unless --force, emitting a clickable runbook URL + a paste-to-Claude remediation prompt. So an operator/automation can no longer boot a crash-looping engine blind (the actionable half of this bug).

The catalog-013-3 CHANGELOG half is NOT fixable as the critic suggested, and this note records WHY so it is not relitigated: (1) 013-3 body is checksum-locked — cannot add the guard inline; (2) a checksum-neutral <preConditions> sqlCheck runs as the NOBYPASSRLS migration role under FORCE RLS, so a count of violating rows sees ZERO while the VALIDATE it gates (DDL, bypasses RLS) trips on them — the exact nexus-1wjmq skew (verified: VALIDATE is a physical scan, RLS does not apply; SELECT count is row-filtered); (3) normalizing rows would sever the catalog_document_chunks manifest join (RDR-108); (4) dropping the constraint is the GH #1390 anti-pattern. ROOT FIX (this bead's remaining scope, engine-side, needs a cut): SchemaMigrator.migrate (Java) should, BEFORE invoking Liquibase, probe for present-but-violating chash constraints on a connection that bypasses RLS (toggle FORCE off transactionally like catalog-013-1b, or a BYPASSRLS-owned SECURITY DEFINER counter), and on finding violations FAIL CLEAN with the runbook pointer (recorded, non-crash-looping) instead of letting 013-3's bare VALIDATE crash. This is the only layer that both sees the true row set AND runs before 013-3. title: vector ETL copies legacy non-32-char Chroma chunk ids verbatim — guided-upgrade hard-fails (409 per upsert) on pre-RDR-108-era stores
description: GH#1390 forensic root cause, one level down (nexus-4m6i0.11 CLOSED with confirmed attribution): the canon-chat box's Chroma store held 16- and 18-char chunk ids from a legacy era; vector_etl passes c['id'] verbatim as chash (module docstring ASSUMES sha256(text)[:32]) and the catalog-002 CHECK (length(chash)=32) — NOT VALID, so enforcing on new writes — 409'd EVERY collection upsert. Also add an agent-facing guardrail note in the migration runbook/upgrade skill: NEVER drop nexus schema constraints to unblock a migration (fail-loud exists precisely to stop that). title: collision-audit: voyage_key_present drift can produce false-clean verdicts (nexus-p9vqa follow-up)
description:
src/nexus/migration/collision_audit.py's audit_target_collisions() defaults
voyage_key_present to TODAY's voyage_key_available() (same accessor
run_guided_upgrade/migrate_cmd use), and the CLI (migration_audit_cmd.py)
exposes no override. This is correct for a FRESH migration decision but wrong
for reconstructing a HISTORICAL one.

classify_model_support() flips a voyage-named collection's support between
"supported-voyage-1024"/"unsupported" based on voyage_key_present.
measured_dim (the nb7hr probe that detects the exact pre-RDR-109
mislabeled-collection bug this audit exists to find) is ONLY probed when
support == "unsupported" (detection.py _classify_leg ~line 364). So: a store
that silently merged in local mode (no voyage key at migration time), then
later had a Voyage key added (a plausible real sequence for a local->cloud
migration path), will have that same collection classify as "supported"
today -> measured_dim never probed -> never cross_model_remappable -> no
collision group built -> nx migration-audit reports "clean" on a genuinely
corrupted store. False "clean" is the worst failure mode for a
corruption-detection tool.

No documentation anywhere (module docstring, CLI help, docs/cli-reference.md)
warns of this drift risk; no override flag or logged voyage_key_present value
lets an operator detect or route around it.

Fix: (1) surface the voyage_key_present value actually used in every
report/finding; (2) add a CLI override (--voyage-key-present /
--no-voyage-key-present) so an operator with migration-history knowledge can
force the historical value; (3) document the drift risk explicitly in the
module docstring and nx migration-audit CLI help/docs.

Full critique: T2 nexus/nexus-p9vqa-collision-audit-critique.

title: nexus-4m6i0.2 round 5: Shape-2 DO-block guard has no THEN-branch structural check (ELSE/closed-IF VALIDATE falsely certified safe)
design:
Round 5 critique (substantive-critic) of tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py
(nexus-4m6i0.2) found this via adversarial testing against the shipped code.

Root cause: `analyze_changelog`'s Shape-2 guard check (DO $$ ... $$ block) only verifies
TEXTUAL PRECEDENCE of an `IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'X')`
match before the VALIDATE's regex-match position, within the same DO block span
(`_GUARD_RE.finditer(cleaned, block_start, pos)`). It never verifies the VALIDATE is
actually inside that IF's THEN-branch. Two adversarial constructions, confirmed
empirically against the live analyzer, are falsely certified as safe (zero violations):

1. VALIDATE in the ELSE branch of the guard:
   DO $$
   BEGIN
       IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'widgets_len_check') THEN
           NULL;
       ELSE
           ALTER TABLE nexus.widgets VALIDATE CONSTRAINT widgets_len_check;
       END IF;
   END $$;
   -- semantically "VALIDATE only when the constraint is ABSENT" -- the exact
   -- inversion-of-direction ms57z crash-loop shape, expressed via Shape 2 instead
   -- of Shape 1's expectedResult (which round 4 / nexus-e439y fixed for Shape 1).

2. VALIDATE placed unconditionally AFTER the guard's IF/END IF has already closed,
   later in the same DO block:
   DO $$
   BEGIN
       IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'widgets_len_check') THEN
           RAISE NOTICE 'present';
       END IF;
       ALTER TABLE nexus.widgets VALIDATE CONSTRAINT widgets_len_check;
   END $$;

Both reproduced with zero violations via `_analyze_synthetic`. Real corpus
(catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml) is clean today -- all five DO blocks use the
VALIDATE strictly inside the THEN branch, so this is not a currently-live crash-loop
risk, but it is an unacknowledged gap (not listed among the module docstring's
"Documented static blind spots") and fits the exact failure class every prior round
(1-4) found: a guard that is textually/superficially present but does not structurally
cover the risk.

Fix direction: track whether the VALIDATE position falls within the guard's THEN-span
specifically (e.g., locate the matched IF EXISTS's THEN...(ELSE|END IF) span via a
second regex/parse and require pos to fall strictly within [THEN, first-ELSE-or-END-IF)),
or add a same-class regression test set (mirroring the Shape-1 direction tests) and,
if fixing is deemed out of scope for a lint (vs. adding a defensive comment), at minimum
document this as an accepted blind spot the way the other four are documented, with a
grep-verified absent-from-corpus disclaimer -- consistent with the file's own stated
convention for known gaps.

Secondary, lower-priority observation from the same session (not blocking, informational):
whole-changeset <preConditions> coverage does not distinguish Liquibase's <and>/<or>
grouping semantics -- every discovered <sqlCheck> is treated as an independent
AND-multiplied gate regardless of whether it is nested under an explicit <or>, which
would (if used) allow a genuinely OR-gated pair of constraints to each be marked
"covered" even though only one is proven to exist at runtime. Zero current usage of
<and>/<or>/<not> in the real corpus (grep-verified 2026-07-09), so this is presently
inert, same posture as the file's own documented blind spots.

title: VALIDATE-precondition lint Shape-1 coverage check is unscoped textual match, not a pg_constraint-existence check
design:
Round 3 critique of tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py (nexus-4m6i0.2).

_constraint_named_in_preconditions() (and analyze_changelog's Shape-1 branch) treats a
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT as "covered" by a whole-changeset <preConditions> whenever the
constraint's name appears ANYWHERE in the preConditions element's itertext(), as a
word-bounded substring. It does not verify that the matched text is actually part of a
pg_constraint-existence check (unlike Shape 2's _GUARD_RE, which is anchored to the
literal "IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = '...')" shape).

Empirically demonstrated false accept (reproducible): a preConditions block whose
sqlCheck queries an unrelated table (e.g. nexus.audit_log) but happens to mention the
constraint name as a word-bounded substring in a string literal is accepted as
"covered" -- analyze_changelog() returns zero violations for a VALIDATE that has no
real existence guard at all. Real-world trigger: a descriptive SQL comment inside a
<sqlCheck> body naming the constraint correctly while the operative query has a typo
in the actual conname literal -- preconditions_text is never passed through
_strip_comments, so SQL comments are part of the matched text.

This defeats the entire point of the nexus-d4vy6 fix (presence -> per-constraint
coverage): "coverage" as implemented means "name mentioned somewhere in the blob," not
"name is being checked for existence in pg_constraint" -- the exact
looks-covered-but-isn't failure class nexus-ms57z/this lint exists to catch, now
present in the lint's own Shape-1 verification logic. Not yet live-exploited (only one
real Shape-1 precondition exists in the corpus today -- catalog-013-2 -- and it is a
genuine pg_constraint IN-list count check), but the CI gate itself is walkable by any
future changeset author (or bot) who adds a decoy/typo'd precondition.

Fix direction: scope the Shape-1 match to require the constraint name occur within an
actual pg_constraint-referencing existence/count clause (generalize _GUARD_RE's
anchoring to also accept "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname (= | IN (...))"
forms), and run _strip_comments over preconditions_text before matching (currently
entirely unprocessed).

Evidence: reproduction scripts run against tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py::analyze_changelog directly, 2026-07-09 (substantive-critic round 3 review). Full critique in T2 nexus/critique-4m6i0.2-round3-validate-precondition-lint.md.

title: nexus-4m6i0.2 lint: whole-changeset preConditions accepted without verifying it covers ALL VALIDATEd constraint names
design: Reviewer-found gap in tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py: analyze_changelog() treats ANY <preConditions> presence on a changeset as sufficient (has_preconditions short-circuits before scanning that changeset's VALIDATE statements at all), never checking whether the precondition's sqlCheck actually names every constraint the changeset VALIDATEs. Empirically reproduced: a changeset with <preConditions><sqlCheck>...conname='widgets_a_check'</sqlCheck></preConditions> plus THREE bare VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statements (widgets_a_check + two unrelated gadgets_b_check/sprockets_c_check on different tables) analyzes to zero violations -- the two unrelated VALIDATEs are completely unguarded and undetected. This is the same failure class as ms57z (unguarded VALIDATE crash-loop) hiding behind a guard that looks present but doesn't cover the risk. Fix: for Shape 1 (whole-changeset preConditions), extract every constraint name referenced by the changeset's VALIDATE statements and confirm each also appears in the preConditions block's condition text (e.g. the sqlCheck's conname IN (...) list) -- mirroring the name-matching discipline Shape 2's per-statement DO-guard already correctly enforces. Add a regression test pinning this exact partial-coverage shape as a FLAG case.
close_reason: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT precondition lint shipped (commit 19c4b661 on develop). Six adversarial review rounds, every finding fixed with a mutation-verified regression test; consciously-unfixed static-heuristic limits documented in the module blind-spots list. fk-002/fk-003 retrofit tracked separately as nexus-4m6i0.13.

title: Retrofit fk-002/fk-003 VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statements with pg_constraint preconditions (10 bare VALIDATEs grandfathered by nexus-4m6i0.2 lint)
description:
Real, currently-unmitigated crash-loop risk (same class as ms57z/catalog-013-2): fk-002-validate.xml and fk-003-validate.xml each run five bare `ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ...` statements, with no whole-changeset <preConditions> and no DO $$ IF EXISTS guard. On a divergent/aged box where any one of these ten FKs is missing, VALIDATE raises a hard Postgres ERROR and the migration -- hence the whole engine service -- crash-loops on every boot restart, identically to the ms57z incident that catalog-013-2 hit.

Grandfathered (not fixed) by the new CI lint tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py (bead nexus-4m6i0.2) via its ALLOWLIST, pending this follow-up:

fk-002-validate.xml:
  fk-002-7  -> nexus.chunks_384             (chunks_384_collection_fk)
  fk-002-8  -> nexus.chunks_768             (chunks_768_collection_fk)
  fk-002-9  -> nexus.chunks_1024            (chunks_1024_collection_fk)
  fk-002-10 -> nexus.chash_index            (chash_index_collection_fk, FK on physical_collection)
  fk-002-11 -> nexus.topic_assignments      (topic_assignments_collection_fk, FK on source_collection, nullable, ON UPDATE CASCADE)

fk-003-validate.xml:
  fk-003-7  -> nexus.document_aspects           (document_aspects_collection_fk)
  fk-003-8  -> nexus.aspect_extraction_queue    (aspect_extraction_queue_collection_fk)
  fk-003-9  -> nexus.topics                     (topics_collection_fk)
  fk-003-10 -> nexus.taxonomy_meta              (taxonomy_meta_collection_fk)
  fk-003-11 -> nexus.document_highlights        (document_highlights_collection_fk; null-collection rows escape via MATCH SIMPLE)

FIX approach (mirror nexus-4m6i0.1's precedent exactly): these changesets are checksum-immutable once executed on any deployed tenant, so they cannot be edited in place. Add NEW changesets (same file or a new validate-retrofit file, following the catalog-013-1b / catalog-013-3 "new changeset id + new author, originals untouched" pattern) that defensively re-VALIDATE each FK guarded by a per-statement DO $$ IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = '<fk_name>') THEN ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ...; END IF; END $$ block, OR a whole-changeset <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"> counting all ten FK names in pg_constraint (per-file, mirroring catalog-013-2's shape).

TDD: needs its own Testcontainers repro per nexus-4m6i0.1's precedent -- migrate to HEAD, DROP one of the ten FK constraints to model a divergent box, re-migrate, assert no MigrationException (RED before fix / GREEN after); then assert the CI lint (tests/test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py) allowlist entry for that changeset becomes UNUSED and must be removed once the new guarded changeset supersedes the grandfathered one -- actually re-check: the original fk-002-N/fk-003-N changesets stay bare (checksum-immutable) but become functionally superseded reads only if we ADD new changesets; the ALLOWLIST entries for fk-002-7..11/fk-003-7..11 remain valid (those specific checksummed changesets are still bare) but the lint should gain new ACCEPT-shape assertions pinning the new guarded changesets. Do not attempt to remove the allowlist entries for the original changesets -- they are permanently bare, only newly-added defensive changesets are guarded.

Test cmd: cd service && ./mvnw -q test -Dtest=SchemaMigratorIntegrationTest (or a new dedicated test class mirroring it)

title: catalog-013-2 permanently re-attempts + SEVERE-logs every boot on boxes with a genuinely-missing chash constraint
design:
Context: nx. Root: substantive-critic review of nexus-4m6i0.1 (service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml).

catalog-013-2 got failOnError="false" to stop it crash-looping the whole service. Verified against liquibase-core 4.29.0 source: a soft-failed (failOnError=false) changeset gets execType=FAILED, and MarkChangeSetRanGenerator explicitly refuses to write a DATABASECHANGELOG row for FAILED/SKIPPED execTypes ("don't mark"). So on any box where a chash-length CHECK constraint is genuinely, persistently missing (the real ms57z incident box), catalog-013-2 will re-attempt its 5 bare VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statements on EVERY boot, forever, hit the same Postgres error, and log a SEVERE stack trace every time. The crash-loop (service unavailability) is genuinely fixed by 013-3's per-table guards; this is a downgrade to permanent noisy-but-non-fatal log churn, not full resolution.

FIX (either):
(a) Retrofit catalog-013-2 with a whole-changeset <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"> checking all 5 constraints exist in one shot — preConditions are excluded from ChangeSet.generateCheckSum() same as failOnError, so this is equally checksum-neutral for already-succeeded boxes. ExecType.MARK_RAN, unlike FAILED/SKIPPED, DOES get written to DATABASECHANGELOG (confirmed: not in MarkChangeSetRanGenerator's exclusion list) -> one INFO-level skip message, then never retried again.
(b) Retire/delete changeset catalog-013-2 entirely once catalog-013-3 is confirmed doing the full defensive job -- Liquibase does not re-validate checksums for changesets removed from the changelog file; already-EXECUTED historical rows on healthy boxes are undisturbed.

Full analysis + verification trail: T2 nexus/critique-nexus-4m6i0.1-catalog-013-liquibase-fix.md and T3 knowledge/liquibase-failonerror-false-vs-preconditions-mark-ran-databasechangelog.
close_reason: Fixed via preConditions onFail=MARK_RAN replacing failOnError=false. Tests assert DATABASECHANGELOG.EXECTYPE='MARK_RAN' specifically, not just non-throwing, so a regression back to the superseded approach would be caught. Committed 1ac12e1f.

title: Fix B (nexus-5b9v0 round-3): validation-setup FileNotFoundError still escapes migrate_cmd.py raw, unwrapped
