comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Round-3 remediation of nexus-5b9v0 widened migrate_cmd.py's except clause from `except TargetNameCollisionBlocked` to `except RuntimeError` (migrate_cmd.py:310), claiming this also closes the separate validation-setup-failure raw re-raise in driver.py (run_guided_upgrade's VALIDATE step, driver.py:434-444: `except Exception as exc: ...; mark_failed(reason); raise`).

CONFIRMED BY REPRODUCTION (/tmp/repro_5b9v0_filenotfound.py, run standalone): when the validation-reopen step's reopen_leg raises FileNotFoundError (exactly what open_local_read_client at chroma_read.py:64 raises when the local Chroma store has vanished between the ETL write and the validation reopen -- the driver.py comment at line ~436 literally anticipates 'a reopened read leg vanished' as the motivating scenario), run_guided_upgrade bare-re-raises the ORIGINAL FileNotFoundError unchanged (not wrapped as RuntimeError). FileNotFoundError is NOT a subclass of RuntimeError (verified: FileNotFoundError.__mro__ = (FileNotFoundError, OSError, Exception, BaseException, object)). migrate_cmd.py's new `except RuntimeError as exc:` clause therefore does NOT catch it -- it propagates as a raw, unhandled Python traceback at the CLI boundary, exactly the UX bug the fix claims to close.

The new regression test (tests/commands/test_migrate_cost_guardrail.py::TestRunMigrationCollisionGuard::test_other_runtime_error_from_guided_upgrade_also_wrapped) is VACUOUS with respect to this specific claim: it monkeypatches nexus.migration.driver.run_guided_upgrade to directly raise a synthetic RuntimeError('validation could not be performed: gate exploded'), bypassing the actual code path (driver.py reopen_leg -> chroma_read.open_local_read_client) that produces a non-RuntimeError exception in production. The test passes trivially regardless of whether the real validation-setup failure path is fixed.

Fix: either (a) driver.py's validation-setup except-block should re-raise a RuntimeError wrapping the original exception (e.g. `raise RuntimeError(reason) from exc` instead of bare `raise`), which fixes it at the source and matches every other guard's convention (ModelPreGateBlocked/MigrationQuiesceBlocked/EtlPreflightFailed/ValidationCheckVacuous/TargetNameCollisionBlocked are all RuntimeError subclasses), or (b) migrate_cmd.py catches the broader Exception at this call site. (a) is preferable -- it fixes the guarantee at its source rather than CLI-side, and (a) also needs a real (not synthetic) regression test that exercises the actual reopen_leg -> FileNotFoundError path.

Evidence: src/nexus/migration/driver.py:407-444, src/nexus/migration/chroma_read.py:64, src/nexus/commands/migrate_cmd.py:310. Full critique in T2 nexus/nexus-5b9v0-collision-guard-review-round3.

title: Retroactive audit: detect already-corrupted pgvector targets from pre-guard silent target-name merges (nexus-5b9v0 follow-up)
description:
nexus-5b9v0 added a pre-flight guard (src/nexus/migration/driver.py `_assert_no_target_name_collisions`) that BLOCKS a fresh guided-upgrade run before any ETL if two or more distinct source collections would resolve to the same final pgvector target name. This closes the bug going FORWARD for any new run.

It does nothing for pgvector targets that may have ALREADY silently merged two source collections under one name in a run that happened BEFORE this guard existed. This is a real production-correctness concern:

- The overlapping-chash variant of the nexus-5b9v0 bug class is a SILENT merge with zero symptoms (no count mismatch, no error) — a fleet box that hit this pre-guard has a corrupted pgvector target collection right now with nothing surfacing it.
- The disjoint-chash variant is louder (a confusing `vector_etl_count_mismatch`) but may have been dismissed/retried rather than root-caused before nexus-5b9v0 diagnosed the actual mechanism.

Scope of the follow-up (NOT implemented as part of nexus-5b9v0 — explicitly deferred):

Build a retroactive audit tool that:
1. Re-runs `classify_collections()`-equivalent logic against an ALREADY-MIGRATED store's original Chroma source (if still retained; copy-not-move means the Chroma source is typically still present per RDR-159's rollback design) to reconstruct what the historical target-name map would have been.
2. Cross-checks for target-name multiplicity that WOULD have collided under `_assert_no_target_name_collisions` (i.e., two or more distinct, data-bearing, non-derived-skip source collections resolving to the same target).
3. For any flagged target, probes the actual pgvector target collection's row/chash population against what each individual source WOULD have contributed, to determine whether an already-migrated target shows evidence of the silent merge (e.g., a chash set that is a superset of two sources' expected outputs, or a count that doesn't match either individual source alone).
4. Reports flagged targets for operator remediation (re-migrate cleanly after removing/re-indexing the stale duplicate source).

Motivating context: nexus-5b9v0 (parent bug — vector_etl_count_mismatch root-caused to cross-model-remap target-NAME collision, confirmed via clean single-run repro). Substantive-critic review of the nexus-5b9v0 fix (T2 nexus/nexus-5b9v0-collision-guard-critique) flagged this as Significant issue 2: "no retroactive detection for already-corrupted targets."

This is intentionally NOT part of the nexus-5b9v0 fix itself — that fix only prevents NEW collisions. This bead tracks the separate, larger retroactive-audit effort.
close_reason: Shipped nx migration-audit (develop 4ff6a39a). All four bead items: (1) re-runs classify_collections against the retained Chroma source; (2) rebuilds the historical target map + collision groups via the guard's OWN extracted functions (build_cross_model_target_names/group_colliding_targets — no drift possible); (3) probes flagged pgvector targets per source via existing_ids with raw source ids (id-stable ETL), evidence-based verdicts merged/single-source/never-materialized/partial/indeterminate with fail-loud reachability + one-shot missing-id recheck; (4) operator remediation per verdict, human render carries model/measured_dim/reason, --json for machines, exit 0/1/2. Critic round-1 Critical (voyage_key_present drift -> false clean) fixed via dual-world union default + --assume-* override (bead nexus-772h2 filed+closed by critic); round-2 verdict JUSTIFIED. 24 new tests; migration suite 652 green. T2: nexus/nexus-p9vqa-migration-audit-shipped. Docs: cli-reference.md § nx migration-audit.

title: Migration ETL mishandles pre-RDR-109 misnamed local collections (nexus-59vl residue) — reproduce + fix
description:
Steve (external nexus user) hit a migration failure: `nx guided-upgrade`/storage-migrate on his box produced

    event='vector_etl_count_mismatch' collection='code__1-3__voyage-code-3__v1' source=400 target=675
    failed code__1-3__voyage-code-3__v1: source=400 written=400 (108.4s) — post-write count mismatch: source=400 target=675

Steve has no Voyage API key (ONNX-only / local mode). Strong hypothesis, confirmed via git archaeology: this collection is a residual instance of the nexus-59vl / GH #667 bug (fixed forward-only in v4.32.0, commit fb0c34fc, 2026-05-11 — RDR-109 Phase 2 "honest local-mode naming"). Before that fix, local-mode indexing (no Voyage key, ONNX embedder) mislabeled collections with voyage-* name tokens despite the vectors coming from the local embedder. Per the v4.32.0 CHANGELOG entry verbatim: "Existing local-mode collections keep their voyage-* names; only new writes pick up the honest token." So any collection indexed on v4.31.7 or earlier in local mode is PERMANENTLY mislabeled unless something explicitly corrects it — nothing currently does, at index time or at migration time.

Investigated and RULED OUT as the direct mechanism:
- Client-side dimension check in vector_etl.py's _provenance_ok (nexus-bfdri, MISMATCH-ONLY design): the server (PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal, PgVectorRepository.java:560-570) ALREADY hard-fails the whole batch with IllegalArgumentException on any dimension mismatch during passthrough — "this is ALSO the contamination guard: a supplied vector whose dim disagrees with the target table is rejected, never stored." A genuine dimension mismatch would surface as `vector_etl_upsert_failed` with an explicit dimension message, NOT the observed `vector_etl_count_mismatch` after an apparently-successful write (written=400, no exception).
- Cross-collection-table contamination: code__1-3__voyage-code-3__v1 (1024-dim -> chunks_1024) and code__1-3__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1 (768-dim -> chunks_768, migrated successfully just before with 275 rows) are DIFFERENT physical tables. The "675 = 400+275" numeric coincidence is likely NOT causal.

Leading (unconfirmed) hypothesis: a re-run after a prior partial/failed migration attempt — upsert is additive/idempotent by chash and never reconciles deletions from a shrunk/changed source, so a retry after the source changed would leave stale rows in the target, inflating target_count beyond current source_count. This needs to be confirmed or ruled out via an actual end-to-end reproduction, not further speculation.

ACTION: build a real (not mocked) reproduction — check out the last pre-fix tag (v4.31.7 or the fb0c34fc~1 commit), run ITS indexer in local mode (no Voyage key) against real sample content to produce a genuinely mislabeled local Chroma collection (name says voyage-*, vectors are actually ONNX), then run the CURRENT migration pipeline (vector_etl.py / nx migrate-to-service) against that real fixture and observe the actual failure mode. Design the fix from what's actually observed, not from speculation.

Related: nexus-bfdri (closed 2026-06-24) already hardened the SAME-MODEL passthrough path against metadata-verifiable mislabeling (MISMATCH-ONLY: re-embed when embedding_model metadata is present and disagrees with the declared name). Its own scope notes anticipated exactly this gap: "confirm whether any real mislabeled collection exists before broadening." This is that confirmation. Depending on repro findings, may need to widen nexus-bfdri's guard, OR fix a retry/reconciliation gap in migrate_collections, OR both.
close_reason: Root-caused via real reproduction (cross-model-remap target-name collision, not the initially-suspected dimension/provenance gap). Pre-flight collision guard implemented in driver.py, closing both the loud count-mismatch and silent-merge failure modes. 4 review rounds (code-review-expert + substantive-critic), all findings fixed with non-vacuous tests verified by revert-and-check. Full suite green (12568 passed). Committed 3d62de3e, merged to develop 994a8060.

title: Tier1: connection-path fail-loud integration test — real call graph rejects below-floor engine (b6qlf regression net)
description:

Point-fix (wiring the probe into get_http_vector_client) is bead nexus-jn0nm; routing the two bypasses is nexus-br90a. THIS bead is the regression net that proves the wiring end-to-end.

title: engine-service v0.1.36 crash-loops on catalog-013-2 Liquibase VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (chunks_384 missing chash_len_check)
description:
GH issue: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/1390

Upgrading the local engine supervisor v0.1.29 -> v0.1.36 crash-loops on startup. Liquibase changeset catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml::catalog-013-2::nexus-e0hd2 runs:

    ALTER TABLE nexus.chunks_384 VALIDATE CONSTRAINT chunks_384_chash_len_check

but that constraint was never created on chunks_384 (0 rows in pg_constraint for it), while it DOES exist on chunks_768. chunks_384 has zero rows and only chunks_384_pk / chunks_384_collection_fk. The prior changesets (catalog-013-0, catalog-013-1) are recorded EXECUTED, so the ADD CONSTRAINT step was likely conditional/skipped for empty/unused dimension tables, while the VALIDATE step assumes it ran unconditionally across all dimension tables.

Environment: conexus 6.5.2, PG 17.10 (Homebrew, local managed, port 50608), macOS arm64, 144 migrations applied pre-upgrade (0 failed per nx doctor), 75 T3 collections, 14036 catalog docs.

Mitigation applied: rolled back to engine-service-v0.1.29 via `nx daemon service install-binary engine-service-v0.1.29`. Service started successfully, no data loss.

Suggested fix (from the issue): the catalog-013-2 changeset should use IF EXISTS / a precondition check (e.g. Liquibase <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"> against pg_constraint, or a changeSetExecuted precondition on the corresponding ADD CONSTRAINT changeset per dimension table) before VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, since not every per-dimension chunks_<dim> table necessarily got the constraint added (empty/never-populated dimension tables).

RELEVANCE TO nexus-b6qlf: this directly undermines the assumption the engine-version-floor unification work depends on -- that deploying/upgrading to a current engine is a safe, routine operation. If upgrading TO a recent engine (v0.1.36, well above any REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION floor we might set) can crash-loop the service, then a fail-loud "your engine is too old, go upgrade it" gate could be steering operators straight into this crash. Worth checking whether v0.1.30-v0.1.36 (the range spanning our current floor work) is affected before finalizing floor values / before the next engine-service cut.
notes: Code fix SHIPPED on develop (1ac12e1f: catalog-013-2 precondition-guarded via MARK_RAN + catalog-013-3 defensive per-table re-validate; two stacked-review rounds; full mvn suite green). Incident bead stays OPEN until the patched engine-service tag is cut + deployed (nexus-4m6i0.5, human-gated relay) — the reporter's box recovers by upgrading to that tag; interim mitigation (rollback to v0.1.29) already in place per GH #1390.
close_reason: Fixed in engine-service-v0.1.37: catalog-013-2 preConditions onFail=MARK_RAN + catalog-013-3 defensive re-validate (1ac12e1f) + native-image reflection metadata for Liquibase precondition classes (01539f42). v0.1.37 deployed + cloud-gated GREEN 2026-07-10.

title: Cloud engine-incompatible error message self-contradicts on whether local action is possible
description:
src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py's _cloud_probe_failure_message() wraps a ManagedServiceIncompatible with: "This cannot be fixed locally -- it is a hosted-service issue... not by any local action you can take. Underlying probe failure: {exc}". The appended {exc} is managed_endpoint.py's own ManagedServiceIncompatible text (src/nexus/db/managed_endpoint.py:209-213), which ends "...Upgrade the managed service, or upgrade/downgrade the nx client to match." The final rendered message a cloud user sees literally contradicts itself: claims no local action is possible, then suggests downgrading the nx client (a local action) in the same string.

Verified via direct invocation of _cloud_probe_failure_message() against a realistic ManagedServiceIncompatible instance -- reproducible.

Fix: either strip/rewrite the "or upgrade/downgrade the nx client to match" clause when embedding the underlying message in cloud mode, or don't append the raw exception text verbatim -- summarize the version numbers only (deployed vs required) without carrying over the underlying message's remedy language, which was written for a different (local-capable) audience.

title: php10: same-changeset-backstop rule unsound for FROM/USING-join DML (target-not-force, referenced-force, coincidental target backstop silently suppresses)
description:
Follow-up from substantive-critic review of tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py (nexus-vtgeq, nexus-php10).

The analyzer's same-changeset-backstop acceptance rule (analyze_changelog, "if target in backstop_tables: continue") only checks whether the DML's TARGET table has a same-changeset immediately-valid ADD CONSTRAINT/UNIQUE/VALIDATE — it does NOT verify that the backstop is on whichever table's FORCE-RLS state actually gates the statement's visibility. For UPDATE ... FROM / DELETE ... USING join-shaped DML where the TARGET is never FORCE but a REFERENCED (joined) table IS FORCE and never toggled, an unrelated backstop on the target silently suppresses the finding, even though the join to the invisible referenced table can zero the affected-row set exactly like the no-op class this lint exists to prevent.

Empirically confirmed via synthetic repro (widgets never-forced target, gadgets forced-and-untoggled referenced via FROM, unrelated ADD CONSTRAINT backstop on widgets in same changeset) -> analyzer returns ZERO violations. This is the mirror-image gap of catalog-014-0's own documented incident ("toggling only the target table leaves the join yielding zero rows for the non-bypass owner" - caught there only by ManifestCollectionStampTest's Java restricted-role replay, NOT by any Python-side check).

Does NOT currently cause a false negative on the real changelog (grep confirmed zero UPDATE...FROM nexus./DELETE...USING nexus. shapes in the 39-file corpus today), so test_real_changelog_zero_violations_and_full_allowlist_consumption stays green. But the gap is untested and undocumented, and is precisely the shape through which nexus-php10's target class ("the class cannot grow") could grow undetected in a future migration.

Fix options (pick one, then add a synthetic test pinning the corrected behavior + document the boundary in the module docstring):
  (a) Require a backstop (or toggle) on EVERY forced table in target|referenced, not just target - matching the toggle path's existing all-referenced-tables symmetry.
  (b) Restrict the target-only-backstop exemption to WHERE-subquery-shaped DML (where the target's own RLS genuinely gates candidacy pre-subquery-evaluation) and require full-set coverage for FROM/USING join shapes.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t design-php10-force-rls-changelog-lint.md; nx memory get -p nexus -t php10-ground-truth-classification.md; tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py lines 434-458 (dml_events loop) and 100-104 (_ADD_CONSTRAINT_RE).
close_reason: Fixed via the corrected same-changeset-backstop rule in tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py: gating-aware (gated target -> requires a LATER same-changeset backstop specifically on the target; non-gated target -> any independently gated referenced/joined table is its own finding that no target-side backstop can excuse) AND order-sensitive (statement index tracked; a backstop before the DML no longer counts). Closes the exact repro in this bead's description (widgets never-force target + gadgets force-untoggled FROM-joined table + unrelated target backstop) -> now correctly flagged, pinned by test_unrelated_target_backstop_does_not_excuse_a_gated_read_table. Also closed the mirror order-sensitivity gap (code-review-expert Important #1) via test_backstop_before_dml_does_not_count, and pinned the still-sound fk-001 shape via test_gated_target_with_gated_subquery_read_and_later_backstop_accepted. Bundled into the same fix round: unused-allowlist detection test, sqlFile/customChange/createProcedure unscanned-element tripwire, case-insensitive table-key normalization, CREATE SCHEMA scope tripwire + 3 new docstring blind-spot paragraphs, and allowlist reason wording citing the concrete audit artifact. 14 -> 23 tests, all green under default addopts; real-corpus exact set unchanged (0 violations, 0 unused allowlist entries, 8 entries/39 files). Full detail: T2 nexus/php10-fqnii-fix-round.md.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t design-php10-force-rls-changelog-lint.md (locked design). nx memory get -p nexus -t php10-ground-truth-classification.md (php10.1 output). Diff/PR from php10.2 (tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py).

Depends on: nexus-0bd1n (php10.2) closed.

Per CLAUDE.md § Review Discipline — Stacked Reviewers: BOTH code-review-expert AND substantive-critic run. Never substitute one for the other; never skip the critic because the code reviewer approved. Dispatch code-review-expert first, fix Critical/High, then dispatch substantive-critic with this briefing (not just "review the diff") — brief it with the locked design (`nx memory get -p nexus -t design-php10-force-rls-changelog-lint.md`) and the bead's acceptance-criteria-sharpening comment so it checks implementation-vs-spec, not style.

Specific pressure-test points for the critic (do not let a generic pass substitute for these):
1. **Regex/parser robustness on the referenced-table extraction.** Does it handle:
   - Schema-qualified vs bare table names (`nexus.chunks_384` vs `chunks_384` inside a function body where `search_path` may already be `nexus`)?
   - Quoted identifiers (`"nexus"."chunks_384"`)?
   - `UPDATE ... FROM <other_table>` (the FROM-clause read target, not just the UPDATE target)?
   - `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM <other_table>` (source read, exactly the fk-002/fk-003 backfill shape)?
   - `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET ...` — confirm this is correctly treated as DML on the CONFLICT target table (same statement, not a separate exempt clause) — an analyzer that treats ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE as "just an INSERT" and ignores the DO UPDATE's own referenced-table implications would under-flag.
   - Multi-line statements split across the pretty-printed XML (aligned column layout like fk-001's UPDATE statements) — does the statement boundary detection (probably semicolon-based given Liquibase splitStatements="true") correctly bound each statement without over- or under-matching across `$$` bodies mixed with `splitStatements="true"` files?
2. **Does the exact-set expectation over-fit?** The real-changelog test locks an exact list of (changeset, table) dangerous-but-allowlisted pairs. Pressure-test: is the allowlist justification per-entry substantive (cites the audit date/bead, not just "grandfathered"), or could a rubber-stamp entry silently exempt something that SHOULD fail? Cross-check php10.1's fk-002-6-reconcile / fk-003-6-reconcile finding specifically — was it resolved with a real justification or hand-waved as "probably a no-op"?
3. **CI reachability.** Confirm `tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py` actually runs under the REQUIRED always-on Python CI with DEFAULT `uv run pytest` addopts — no `-m integration` or other marker gate that would silently exempt it from the required check (this is the whole point per the design: "Java service-ci is advisory; auto-merge can bypass it" — if this new test also ends up advisory-only or marker-gated, the tripwire has zero teeth). Check pyproject.toml `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` markers/addopts and confirm no `@pytest.mark.integration` or similar was applied to this file's tests.
4. **Non-vacuity of the exact-set assertion.** Per CLAUDE.md global feedback ("exact assertions in fixture regression tests" + "no silent fallbacks for correctness"): does the real-changelog test actually parse 31 files (assert a minimum file-count or explicit list, not just "no exception raised")? A silently-empty file glob (e.g. wrong path, or `master.xml` include-parsing silently returning zero files) would make the exact-set test vacuously pass by finding nothing to flag. Confirm there's a floor assertion (e.g. "at least N DML statements classified" or "all 31 files present in the walk") guarding against this.
5. **Toggle-wrap detector correctness on the missing-restore case.** Confirm the missing-restore synthetic test actually distinguishes "no toggle at all" from "toggled but not restored" with a DIFFERENT failure message/classification — if both collapse to the same generic "naked DML" finding, a future maintainer reading a real failure won't know which fix pattern applies (013-1b toggle-wrap vs "you forgot the FORCE restore").
6. **Same-changeset-backstop vs later-changeset-backstop boundary.** This is the single most safety-critical distinction in the whole design (it's literally what caused the outage). Confirm the synthetic "later-changeset backstop" test uses changeset IDs that are adjacent-but-distinct (mirroring 013-0/013-2's real shape) and that the detector genuinely checks changeset identity, not just "a backstop exists somewhere in the file" (a same-file-different-changeset bug would silently pass the outage-shape case).

Execution instructions:
1. Dispatch code-review-expert on the diff (tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py + any related bead/T2 updates).
2. Fix Critical/High findings, re-run `uv run pytest tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py -q`.
3. Dispatch substantive-critic with the briefing above (the locked design doc, the bead's acceptance-criteria comment, and pressure-test points 1-6).
4. Iterate Critical -> fix -> re-review until clean.
5. Record the review outcome in T2 memory (title e.g. "php10-review-outcome.md") and close nexus-vtgeq, then nexus-php10.

Success criteria:
- [ ] code-review-expert dispatched, Critical/High findings fixed.
- [ ] substantive-critic dispatched with the design + bead-comment briefing (not a generic "review this diff").
- [ ] All 6 pressure-test points explicitly addressed in the critic's findings or explicitly confirmed non-issues with evidence (not silently skipped).
- [ ] CI-reachability confirmed (default `uv run pytest` addopts, no marker gate).
- [ ] Review outcome persisted to T2 memory.
- [ ] nexus-vtgeq and nexus-php10 closed only after the critic pass is clean.

Depends on: nexus-fzbtu (php10.1) closed with the ground-truth table in T2.

Style reference: tests/test_storage_boundary_lint.py — AST-scan-style unit test, `_check()` helper wrapping a `scan_repo`-equivalent call, `tmp_path` fixtures for synthetic offenders, exact `==` assertions (never `>=`) on locked baselines with an inline comment explaining every baseline delta, `# epsilon-allow: <reason>` (>= 8 char) escape-hatch convention, `LintResult`-style dataclass with an `as_metric_dict()` helper. Mirror this discipline, not necessarily the module split — the design says the analyzer is EMBEDDED in tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py itself (pure XML/text parsing, no PG, no src/nexus/ module).

Execution instructions:
1. Use mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking before writing code — this analyzer has real edge-case surface (dollar-quote stripping, state-machine ordering, backstop windowing) worth thinking through before implementation, not after a failing test surprises you.
2. TDD: write the synthetic-XML fixture tests FIRST (flag cases and accept cases below), watch them fail against a stub analyzer, then implement.
3. Analyzer components (embed in tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py, may factor into module-level helper functions within the same file):
   a. Comment/dollar-quote stripper: remove `--` line comments, `/* */` block comments, and `$$...$$` bodies (record stripped $$ spans separately as "function-body, exempt").
   b. Master include-order walker: parse db.changelog-master.xml `<include file="...">` in document order to get the ordered changelog file sequence; within each file, changesets in document order. This is the canonical execution order for the per-table FORCE state machine — do NOT use filesystem/alphabetical order.
   c. Per-table FORCE-RLS state machine: walk changesets in master order; track state transitions on `ALTER TABLE <table> FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` / `NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. Also need to know when a table starts existing — ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY without FORCE is a distinct state, but per the design only FORCE state (not RLS-enabled state) gates the flag.
   d. DML detector: parse (regex or lightweight tokenizer — full SQL parsing is out of scope) top-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements per changeset, extract the target table AND every other `nexus.*` table referenced (FROM/JOIN/subquery/EXISTS/USING clauses) — this is the catalog-014 "both-tables" lesson, don't only check the target.
   e. Toggle-wrap detector: within a SINGLE changeset, is every FORCE-at-entry referenced table preceded by its own NO FORCE and followed by its own FORCE restore, both inside that same changeset's <sql> body?  Missing restore is its OWN finding (distinct message from "no toggle at all").
   f. Same-changeset backstop detector: does the SAME changeset contain (on the SAME table) an `ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY`/`ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE` (immediately valid, i.e. NOT `NOT VALID`), a `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`, or a `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`? Only SAME-changeset counts — a backstop in a later changeset must NOT suppress the finding (this is the literal catalog-013-0 bug shape; getting this backwards silently defeats the whole tripwire).
   g. Allowlist: a Python literal (list of dicts or dataclass) of `(changeset_id, table, reason)` tuples for the historical grandfather members that php10.1's ground-truth table classifies as DANGEROUS-but-known. Track which allowlist entries get consumed during the real-changelog run; UNUSED entries FAIL the test (rot detection) — assert the consumed set == the full allowlist set, not just "no new violations".
4. Synthetic-XML unit tests (each a minimal in-memory or tmp_path changelog fixture, mirroring test_storage_boundary_lint.py's tmp_path pattern):
   FLAG (must be caught):
   - naked DML: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on a FORCE table, no toggle, no backstop anywhere.
   - missing-restore: NO FORCE issued, DML runs, but FORCE is never restored before changeset end — flag even though the DML itself "succeeded" (this is a distinct message from naked DML: it's an isolation-window leak, not a no-op).
   - later-changeset backstop: DML in changeset A, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT / unique index in changeset B (later) — must NOT be treated as safe (the 013-0 regression case).
   - unwrapped join-table read: DML targets a non-FORCE table but JOINs/subqueries a DIFFERENT table that IS FORCE and not toggled — must flag on the referenced-table rule, not just the target-table rule (the catalog-014 both-tables lesson, inverted to prove the detector actually checks joins).
   ACCEPT (must NOT be flagged):
   - toggle-wrapped: NO FORCE / DML / FORCE all in one changeset, single table.
   - toggle-wrapped, both tables (catalog-014 shape): two tables toggled off/DML/restored in one changeset.
   - same-changeset backstop: DML + ADD CONSTRAINT ... immediately valid (or CREATE UNIQUE INDEX / VALIDATE CONSTRAINT) on the same table, same changeset.
   - function-body ($$-quoted) DML: a `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ... $$ ... UPDATE ... $$` body — exempt regardless of FORCE state (SECURITY INVOKER call-time semantics, catalog-003's purge_trash/document_trash class).
5. Real-changelog exact-set test: run the analyzer against the ACTUAL service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/ tree, assert the flagged (post-allowlist) set is empty (`== []` / `total_violations == 0`, matching the storage_boundary_lint.py convention) AND assert the allowlist's consumed-entries set equals its full declared set (no unused/rotted entries) using php10.1's ground-truth table as the source of truth for what "the six [or more — see php10.1 findings on fk-002/fk-003-validate.xml] historical members" actually are. If php10.1 determined fk-002-6-reconcile / fk-003-6-reconcile are genuinely dangerous-shape and NOT already covered by an existing fix, this task must decide (in consultation with the bead's acceptance criteria, flag to Hal if ambiguous) whether to allowlist them too or treat their absence from the "six" as a gap the test should legitimately catch as a NEW finding — do not silently allowlist something php10.1 flagged as unresolved.
6. Document the blind spot in the module/file docstring: `SELECT some_fn()` invoking a DML-performing function is statically invisible to this analyzer (catalog-014 sidesteps this by wrapping the toggles around the SELECT itself, not by the analyzer seeing into the function body).
7. Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py -q` (plain unit test, no markers, must be in the default `uv run pytest` addopts scope — verify this explicitly, see php10.3's CI-reachability check).
8. Update T1 scratch with a short summary (files touched, test count, pass/fail) tagged "php10,force-rls,implementation" before handing to php10.3.

Success criteria:
- [ ] tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py created, self-contained (embedded analyzer, no new src/nexus/ module) per the locked design.
- [ ] All synthetic FLAG cases (naked DML, missing-restore, later-changeset backstop, unwrapped join-table read) fail the analyzer (test asserts a violation IS produced).
- [ ] All synthetic ACCEPT cases (toggle-wrapped single/both-table, same-changeset backstop, function-body DML) produce NO violation.
- [ ] Real-changelog exact-set test passes using php10.1's ground-truth table as the expected set; allowlist has zero unused entries.
- [ ] The fk-002/fk-003-validate.xml finding from php10.1 is explicitly resolved (allowlisted with justification, or surfaced as a real finding) — not silently dropped.
- [ ] `uv run pytest tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py -q` green, and confirmed to run under plain `uv run pytest` (no special marker needed).
- [ ] Module/file docstring states the SELECT-invoking-a-DML-function blind spot.

Bead nexus-php10 comment carries the critic-1wjmq acceptance-criteria sharpening (two shapes: same-changeset backstop = safe; toggle-wrap = safe; later-changeset backstop = dangerous, catalog-013-0's exact outage shape).

Execution instructions:
1. Use mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking to structure the walk (one thought per changelog file group) — this is exactly the kind of enumeration where skipping a file silently produces an incomplete expected-set.
2. ls service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/ (31 files). Read db.changelog-master.xml FIRST to get the authoritative include order — the FORCE-RLS state machine must walk changesets in THIS order, not file-alphabetical order.
3. For every changelog file, for every <changeSet>, for every <sql> body (EXCLUDING <rollback> blocks — they never run at migration time):
   a. Strip -- and /* */ comments, and $$...$$ dollar-quoted bodies (record separately as "function-body DML, exempt class" — do not lose them, just tag them).
   b. Record every ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY / NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statement in changeset order — this builds the per-table FORCE-state timeline.
   c. Record every top-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statement: changeset id, target table, every OTHER table it reads via JOIN/subquery/EXISTS (the catalog-014 "both-tables" lesson), and the FORCE state of each referenced table AT THAT POINT in the chain.
4. Classify each DML statement against the design's decision tree:
   - function/trigger $$-body -> EXEMPT
   - target+all-referenced tables NOT FORCE at that point -> SAFE (not a finding)
   - toggle-wrapped (every referenced FORCE table NO-FORCE'd earlier in the SAME changeset, FORCE restored after) -> SAFE, cite the changeset
   - same-changeset backstop (ADD CONSTRAINT/CREATE UNIQUE INDEX/VALIDATE CONSTRAINT on the SAME table in the SAME changeset) -> SAFE (provably safe-or-loud), cite the changeset
   - later-changeset backstop or no backstop at all -> DANGEROUS, this is the exact-set the test must flag (grandfather-allowlist candidate if historical, hard-fail if new)
5. ALREADY-KNOWN GROUND TRUTH from initial planning grep (verify these, do not just trust this list):
   - FORCE-RLS tables established at baseline: aspects-001 (document_aspects, document_highlights, aspect_extraction_queue, aspect_promotion_log), catalog-001 (catalog_owners, catalog_documents, catalog_links, catalog_document_chunks, catalog_collections, catalog_meta), chash-001 (chash_index), memory-001 (memory), migration-001 (migration_jobs), plans-001 (plans), t1-001 (t1.scratch), taxonomy-002 (taxonomy_centroids_384/768/1024), taxonomy-001 (topics, taxonomy_meta, topic_assignments, topic_links), telemetry-001 (relevance_log, search_telemetry, tier_writes, nx_answer_runs, hook_failures, frecency), vectors-001 (chunks_384/768/1024).
   - Known DML-bearing files (grep-confirmed, verify classification): catalog-003-soft-delete.xml (DML inside $$ function bodies only — purge_trash — EXEMPT class), catalog-004-manifest-functions.xml ($$ function bodies), catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml (013-0 naked DML = later-changeset backstop via 013-2 = DANGEROUS/grandfather; 013-1b = toggle-wrap = SAFE), catalog-014-manifest-collection-stamp.xml (toggle-wrap, both tables — SAFE), taxonomy-004-dedup-root-topics.xml (004-1 DML, 004-2 unique index in a LATER changeset = same later-changeset-backstop shape as 013-0 = DANGEROUS/grandfather), fk-001-catalog-cross-store.xml (fk-001-2/3/4/5 orphan cleanup UPDATE/DELETE, no backstop at all visible in this file = DANGEROUS/grandfather candidates — verify), fk-002-collection-registry.xml (fk-002-0 backfill INSERT into catalog_collections, reads FROM chunks_384/768/1024/chash_index/topic_assignments which are ALL FORCE-RLS — check whether the SELECT side is even readable by a non-BYPASSRLS INSERT ... SELECT), fk-003-collection-registry-extra.xml (fk-003-0, same shape).
   - NEW FINDING, NOT in the bead's "six historical members" list — verify carefully: fk-002-validate.xml changeset fk-002-6-reconcile does an INSERT INTO catalog_collections SELECT DISTINCT ... FROM chunks_384/768/1024/chash_index/topic_assignments (same shape as fk-002-0), and its backstop (VALIDATE CONSTRAINT) lives in SEPARATE LATER changesets fk-002-7 through fk-002-11 — the exact later-changeset-backstop shape that caused the v0.1.33 outage in catalog-013-0. Same pattern in fk-003-validate.xml changeset fk-003-6-reconcile with fk-003-7..11. These may be additional dangerous-shape members the "six" count never audited (the RDR-153 world-block-lifted comment in both files suggests the reconcile is expected to be a no-op in practice by the time it runs, but the STATIC shape is unprotected — this is exactly the class the tripwire exists to catch, so do not wave it through on the "probably a no-op" rationale without checking whether the audit already covered it).
   - service-tokens-003-scope-column.xml has a naked UPDATE nexus.service_tokens SET scope=... — check FORCE state of service_tokens at that point (service-tokens-001 does NOT show FORCE RLS in the earlier grep — verify service_tokens is NOT FORCE-RLS by design, per its baseline comment "NO RLS... the token resolves the tenant").

title: Changelog tripwire: migration-time row-DML on a FORCE-RLS table must toggle NO FORCE (or prove visibility) — fail the suite otherwise
description: nexus-1wjmq follow-up. The silent-no-op class has SIX historical members (catalog-013-0, taxonomy-004 dedupe, fk-001/002/003 orphan cleanups) — all migration-time <sql> DML against FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY tables, all silently no-op'd in production because nexus_admin (owner, no BYPASSRLS) sees zero rows. Five were vacuously harmless (their own downstream VALIDATE/unique-index builds prove the data was clean); catalog-013-0's no-op took down the v0.1.33 deploy. Audit 2026-07-08 confirms no production data divergence today. Build the tripwire so the class cannot grow: a test that parses every changelog <sql> body, flags INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE targeting a table that (at that point in the chain) has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, unless the changeset wraps the DML in the NO FORCE / FORCE toggle (the catalog-013-1b pattern) or an explicit allowlist entry documents why visibility holds. Function/trigger bodies (SECURITY INVOKER, call-time) are exempt. Alternative stronger form: run the whole-changelog Liquibase conformance test as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner role instead of the superuser (Catalog013RlsReplayTest proves the harness pattern; the Liquibase autoCommit trap and ownership-transfer recipe are solved there).

title: [BUG] Migration classifier trusts collection-name model label instead of measuring actual embedding dimension — blocks legacy mislabeled bge-768 collections as 'needs Voyage key'
description:
## Symptom

`nx guided-upgrade` / `nx migrate-to-service --dry-run` classifies collections
by parsing the embedding model out of the collection NAME string only, and
reports a `dim` that is a static lookup from that same (possibly wrong) name
— never a measurement of what's actually stored. A user with legacy
mislabeled or non-conformant collections gets blocked from migrating data
that is in fact plain bge-768/ONNX and requires no re-embedding, no
credentials, and no cost.

First reported: Steve Harris, GH #1381 (comments 2026-07-08T15:14 /
15:39), during a 5.x -> 6.4.0 guided-upgrade. Of his 18 Chroma collections,
13 were reported blocked:
  - 5 named with a `voyage-code-3` / `voyage-context-3` model segment ->
    classifier says "unsupported, needs NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY"
  - 8 pre-RDR-103 two-segment names with no model segment at all ->
    classifier says "unsupported, non-conformant name, cannot resolve model"

Steve has no Voyage key and does not want one. All-or-nothing migration
sequencing (RDR-159 P2, `legs_with_data`) means his 5 already-clean bge
collections (2513 chunks) also can't move while these 13 are unresolved.

## Root cause

`classify_collections` / `_classify_leg` in
`src/nexus/migration/detection.py` (~line 245-270):

```python
model = embedding_model_for_collection_name(name)      # name-string parse only
dim, _dim_reason = _dim_for_collection(name)            # static lookup keyed by the SAME name
support, reason = classify_model_support(model, voyage_key_present=voyage_key_present)
```

`_dim_for_collection` (`src/nexus/migration/vector_etl.py:288`) maps the
model TOKEN to `_MODEL_DIMS[token]` (a static dict: voyage-*=1024,
bge-base-en-v15-768=768, minilm-l6-v2-384=384). It never opens the
collection and inspects a real stored vector. `CollectionClassification.dim`
is documented as "informational only" but is in fact the ONLY signal used —
there is no ground-truth check anywhere in the P0 detection path.

This is the migration-side blind spot for a bug we already fixed on the
WRITE side: RDR-109 Gap 1 / nexus-59vl / GH #667 ("local-ONNX collections
falsely labeled voyage-*"), closed 2026-05-20. That fix
(`src/nexus/catalog/collection_name.py:100`, `CollectionName` validates
against `CANONICAL_EMBEDDING_MODELS | LOCAL_EMBEDDING_MODELS`) makes NEW
writes honest. It does nothing for collections written before the fix
landed — exactly Steve's install. The migration classifier was never taught
to distrust a legacy name.

The codebase already has the right primitive for a ground-truth probe:
`src/nexus/collection_audit.py:165` — `col.get(limit=n,
include=["embeddings"])` — used today for `nx collection audit`'s live
distance sampling. `detection.py` does not use it.

## Suggested fix

In `_classify_leg` (detection.py), after computing `model`/`dim` from the
name, probe ONE real vector per collection:

```python
sample = client_collection.get(limit=1, include=["embeddings"])
embeddings = sample.get("embeddings")
actual_dim = len(embeddings[0]) if embeddings is not None and len(embeddings) else None
```

Compare `actual_dim` against the name-derived `dim`:

* `actual_dim == dim` (or name unresolvable and `actual_dim` is None because
  the collection is empty) -> classify as today, no behavior change.
* `actual_dim == 768` and `dim != 768` (or `dim is None`) -> the vectors are
  real bge-768/ONNX regardless of what the name claims. Reclassify as
  `supported-onnx`, with a distinct reason string noting the name was
  stale/non-conformant and will be corrected (rename to a conformant
  local-shaped token per the RDR-109 fix, e.g. via `cross_model_target_name`
  or a dedicated relabel-only path — NOT a re-embed, since the vectors
  already ARE bge-768). Passthrough copy, zero cost, no key needed.
* `actual_dim == 1024` and no voyage key present -> still genuinely blocked
  on credentials (unchanged from today) — this is the one case where the
  existing diagnostic is correct.
* `actual_dim` in neither known bucket -> keep today's "unsupported,
  re-index" diagnostic (unchanged).

This directly resolves the classic failure mode without requiring any
Voyage credential, and converges the migration detector onto the same
"measure, don't trust the name" discipline RDR-109 already established for
the write path.

## Secondary findings from the same report (fold in or split out — flag,
don't lose)

1. The guided-upgrade summary line "N classified unsupported — legacy-model
   collections are auto-remapped, not blocked" is misleading: `nx
   migrate-to-service --dry-run` reports these as flatly BLOCKED, nothing is
   auto-remapped for the non-conformant-name case. Reword to stop implying
   an auto-remap that doesn't happen for this class.
2. A validated block leaves the sentinel `migrated-failed` (degraded-LOUD
   reads) with `nx migration --clear-state` as the recovery step — that
   step is never mentioned in guided-upgrade's own output, only in
   `migrate-to-service`'s failure text. Users following guided-upgrade alone
   have no pointer to it.
3. Stale orphaned model-duplicate collections (e.g. a `bge-*` collection
   with a handful of chunks sitting alongside a `voyage-*` collection with
   hundreds, left over from before Voyage was configured) are invisible to
   any existing health check. Worth a `collection health`/gc flag, separate
   bead.

## Files

- src/nexus/migration/detection.py (`_classify_leg`, `classify_collections`,
  `classify_model_support`, `CollectionClassification.dim`)
- src/nexus/migration/vector_etl.py (`_dim_for_collection`, `_MODEL_DIMS`,
  `cross_model_target_name` — relabel-only path may reuse this)
- src/nexus/collection_audit.py (`sample_live_distances` — the existing
  `col.get(limit=n, include=["embeddings"])` precedent to follow)
- src/nexus/catalog/collection_name.py (RDR-109 fix — the write-side honest
  naming this bead extends to the read/migration side)
- docs/rdr/rdr-109-honest-naming-and-cross-encoder-salience.md (prior art)

## Repro

Use a Chroma fixture with a collection named
`code__owner__voyage-code-3__v1` whose actual stored vectors are 768-dim
(bge), plus a pre-RDR-103 two-segment collection (`code__owner`) also
actually 768-dim. `classify_collections` should report both as
`supported-onnx`, not `unsupported`.
close_reason: Fixed in baa1206c on develop. Classifier measures one stored vector for name-unsupported data-bearing collections; measured-768 auto-remaps through the cross-model path to a LOCAL ONNX target in every mode (no credentials, no billing). Two-segment names get conformant targets synthesized. Guided output: truthful banner + --clear-state recovery pointer. Best-effort probe (degrades to name-based diagnostic on failure). Both reviewers green; deviation-from-spec + out-of-scope residual recorded as comments. CLIENT-SIDE fix: reaches Steve (GH #1381) with the next PyPI release.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: DEVIATION FROM SUGGESTED FIX (recorded per substantive-critic): the bead said 'reclassify as supported-onnx... passthrough copy, zero cost — NOT a re-embed'. Shipped behavior instead routes measured-768 collections through the proven RDR-162 cross-model-remap machinery (cross_model_remappable / target_names / pre-gate exempt set): a LOCAL ONNX re-embed over the stored chunk text into a conformant-named target collection. Rationale: reuses end-to-end-proven rename+reference-remap+validation plumbing instead of new passthrough code; the two properties that matter to the reporter hold literally (zero Voyage billing, zero credentials — remap_target_model pins the target to ONNX in EVERY deployment mode, test-pinned). Cost difference vs literal spec: CPU/wall time to recompute ONNX vectors, no correctness delta.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: OUT-OF-SCOPE RESIDUAL (recorded per substantive-critic): the dim probe only fires for name-UNSUPPORTED collections. A collection whose name matches a known model but whose stored vectors have the WRONG dim (e.g. voyage-named + key present + actually 768) is never probed — it classifies supported and would fail later at the service upsert boundary. Not in the reporter's repro; acknowledged in test_measured_768_targets_onnx_even_in_cloud_mode's docstring. File a new bead if this shape ever appears in the field.

title: Guided MVV gate: strip ambient PostgreSQL from the rehearsal image (or add a no-host-PG variant) so the bare journey exercises PG-bundle auto-acquisition
description: Why the yv5m4 bug survived the MVV gate's maiden run: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/Dockerfile bakes postgresql-16 + postgresql-16-pgvector into the image via apt (line 34) and puts /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin on PATH. So the 'bare default-path journey' validates the bare COMMAND but not a bare MACHINE — discover_pg_binaries() finds host PG, the pgvector preflight passes, and the acquisition path (nexus-yv5m4's fix) is never reached. Inverse of feedback_gates_scripted_not_ambient: a gate whose environment pre-satisfies a dependency cannot detect that the product fails to self-satisfy it. Fix: remove host PG from the image (product must provision via the signed nexus-pg bundle) or add a second no-host-PG journey variant if other rehearsal legs genuinely need image PG. Acceptance: the MVV log shows the bundle download+verify+extract happening (grep for pg_bundle install marker), and a deliberate revert of the yv5m4 fix turns the gate RED. Also consider a fresh 'nx init' journey (not just guided-upgrade) so the README quickstart claim has a conformance gate.

So the original ask (strip ambient PG so the acquire path is exercised) is now HALF-satisfied automatically; remaining work inverts: (a) drop the dead apt install from the images, (b) decide whether the per-run GitHub download in a cost-conscious job should be cached (actions/cache on the .txz keyed by tag) per CI-cost directives, (c) keep the acceptance criterion: a deliberate revert of the always-install wiring must turn the guided MVV red.

title: bare nx init / nx guided-upgrade never auto-acquires the PG bundle — fresh machine dead-ends at the Homebrew pgvector wall (GH #1381 round 3)
description: provision_service_stack() runs _provision_postgres_step() BEFORE _ensure_service_binary_step(), and even the binary step calls only install_binary() — install_pg_bundle() is reachable solely via the explicit 'nx daemon service install-binary' CLI command. So on a fresh machine with no host PG, bare init/guided-upgrade raises PgBinaryNotFoundError with the brew postgresql@17 hint, which dead-ends because Homebrew's pgvector formula does not target the versioned postgresql@17 (stevengharris hit exactly this on 6.3.8, GH #1381). Even WITH host PG17-sans-pgvector present, discovery picks it and the pgvector preflight tells users to build pgvector from source. The signed nexus-pg-<platform>.txz (pgvector baked in) exists on every engine release and the verified install seam (install_pg_bundle) exists — it is just never invoked by init/guided-upgrade. Fix: acquire binary + PG bundle from the pinned tag (resolve_service_tag) BEFORE PG provisioning on the local-serving path, mirroring 'nx daemon service install-binary <tag>' semantics; only fall back to host-PG discovery/brew hints when no tag is pinned or download fails. Docs f53e7a0a already promise 'nx init auto-acquires' — this makes the promise true for the PG half. Workaround posted on #1381: nx daemon service install-binary engine-service-v0.1.32 && nx guided-upgrade.
close_reason: Fixed on develop bed75396. _acquire_pg_bundle_step downloads+verifies (sha256+Sigstore) nexus-pg-<platform>.txz from the pinned tag when host preflight raises PgBinaryNotFoundError/PgVectorNotInstalledError; wired into _provision_postgres_step before provision(). 10 regression tests (tests/test_init_pg_bundle_acquire.py). Stacked review: critic clean (test gap added), code-review High fixed (unguarded extraction). Workaround posted GH #1381 for 6.3.8 users: nx daemon service install-binary engine-service-v0.1.32. CI-exercise of this path = nexus-5qefg.

title: guided-upgrade probes ~/.config/nexus/chroma for the legacy footprint — the product has never written local Chroma there (real installs invisible)
description: GH #1381 (stevengharris) primary root cause. open_read_legs (src/nexus/migration/detection.py:361) defaults the local leg to nexus_config_dir()/'chroma' (~/.config/nexus/chroma). The product's local Chroma has ALWAYS lived at nexus.config._default_local_path(): NX_LOCAL_CHROMA_PATH -> $XDG_DATA_HOME/nexus/chroma -> ~/.local/share/nexus/chroma (verified identical at v5.4.5; used by t3_daemon, health, indexer). So a bare 'nx guided-upgrade' — the exact command the 6.0.0 CHANGELOG tells installed users to run — opens a directory no install ever wrote, finds no footprint, and no-ops with 'you are already on the service stack' while the user's real vectors sit at the XDG path. WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT: rehearse_guided.sh always passes --local-path $CHROMA_LOCAL, so the default-path resolution has never been exercised by any MVV (harness fidelity gap — fix the leg to seed at the container's _default_local_path and invoke bare guided-upgrade). Fix: detector default resolves via _default_local_path() (env-aware), with the old config-dir location retained as a secondary legacy probe; unit tests for the resolution matrix; rehearsal leg exercises the default. Sibling: nexus-ltix8 (the T3-only gate also skips T2 even when the footprint is genuinely empty) — fix together, ship as 6.3.8.
close_reason: Fixed on develop c83b35b9 (ships 6.3.8). resolve_default_local_leg() in migration/detection.py: product path (NX_LOCAL_CHROMA_PATH -> XDG -> ~/.local/share/nexus/chroma) wins when present, legacy <config>/chroma secondary probe. Deep chokepoint open_local_read_client(None) resolves it too (critique CRITICAL: detection-only fix would have provisioned then crashed the ETL on Path(None) — empirically A/B'd: pre-fix bare-journey MVV FAILED with NoneType at leg=local, post-fix PASSED). Same default fixed in nx storage migrate vectors (critique HIGH). Harness: rehearse_guided.sh seeds the product default + invokes BARE (the four-release mask). Tests: resolver matrix + None-chokepoint + CLI gates.

title: guided-upgrade's T3-only pre-flight gate falsely declares 'already on the service stack', skipping T2 migration entirely
description:
## Symptom

A user upgrades an existing pre-RDR-152 local-SQLite install via a bare
package upgrade (e.g. `uv tool upgrade conexus`), crossing the RDR-152 T2
default flip (SQLite -> Postgres-backed service). Afterward `nx doctor` shows
T2/catalog service checks failing (no service provisioned). Running
`nx guided-upgrade` to fix it prints:

  "No pre-RDR-160 Chroma footprint detected — nothing to migrate; you are
   already on the service stack."

...and exits immediately, WITHOUT provisioning anything and WITHOUT migrating
T2 data. The user's T2 stores (memory, catalog, plans, taxonomy, telemetry,
chash_index, document_aspects, aspect_queue) remain in local SQLite, unreachable,
because the hard default (`storage_backend_for`, src/nexus/db/storage_mode.py)
now routes them to a Postgres service that was never stood up.

## Root cause

`guided_upgrade_cmd.py`'s step 1 gate is T3-Chroma-only:

    pre = detect_pending_migration(local_path=local_path)
    if not pre.needs_migration:
        click.echo("No pre-RDR-160 Chroma footprint detected — nothing to "
                    "migrate; you are already on the service stack.")
        return

`detect_pending_migration()` (src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py) only
opens/classifies the local + cloud Chroma (T3 vector) legs via
`open_read_legs` / `classify_collections`. `needs_migration` is
`len(report.legs_with_data) > 0` — purely a vector-footprint signal. If the
local Chroma directory is empty, absent, or a path mismatch, this is False
even when the user has substantial UNMIGRATED T2 SQLite data.

Critically, the command RETURNS before ever reaching step 1a
(`detect_already_migrated`, same file, ~line 352) — the T2-SQLite-specific
already-migrated check — or before provisioning/verifying any service. So
"you are already on the service stack" is asserted without ever checking T2
at all. The message conflates "no vectors to move" with "fully migrated."

There is no `--force` escape hatch for this specific gate: `--force` only
affects `detect_already_migrated`'s per-store skip logic, which this early-
return path never reaches.

Contrast with `nx migrate-to-service` (src/nexus/commands/migrate_cmd.py,
`_run_migration`), which migrates T2 stores unconditionally (Chroma
classification there only feeds the voyage-cost-preview confirmation, never
gates T2) — so the underlying migration machinery is correct; only
guided-upgrade's convenience wrapper's step-1 gate is wrong.

## Impact

Any pre-RDR-152 local install with little/no local Chroma vector data (e.g.
mostly T2 usage: memory/catalog/taxonomy, or a T3 store that already looks
empty to the detector) gets falsely told it's fully migrated by the ONE
command whose entire purpose is to carry existing installs across safely
(RDR-159/RDR-002, shipped 6.0.0, CHANGELOG: "An installed user MUST migrate
their existing Chroma data — `nx guided-upgrade` does this in one command").
Compounds with two other gaps in the same upgrade arc:

  - A bare `uv tool upgrade conexus` crosses the RDR-152 breaking-change
    boundary with zero warning/prompt.
  - `nx upgrade` (src/nexus/commands/upgrade.py, `_run_upgrade`) also
    no-ops in service mode with a misleadingly reassuring message
    ("Service mode: ... no local schema migration to run") rather than
    flagging that no service is configured.

First reported via a relayed Steve/nexus support conversation, 2026-07-07.

## Suggested fix

`guided_upgrade_cmd.py` step 1 should not return "already on the service
stack" purely from the T3 Chroma signal. At minimum:
  - Also run `detect_already_migrated` (T2 SQLite check) before declaring
    nothing-to-do, and only no-op if BOTH T3 has no footprint AND every T2
    store is either empty or already-migrated per its report evidence.
  - Reword the message so "no Chroma footprint" and "T2 already migrated"
    are reported as distinct facts, never collapsed into one blanket
    "already on the service stack" claim.
  - Consider also tightening `nx upgrade`'s service-mode no-op message and/or
    surfacing a pointer to `nx guided-upgrade` from service-unreachable error
    paths (secondary, could be a follow-on bead).

## Repro

1. Existing local install, pre-RDR-152, with T2 SQLite data (memory/catalog)
   but an empty or absent `~/.config/nexus/chroma` directory.
2. `uv tool upgrade conexus` to a post-152 version.
3. `nx doctor` shows T2/catalog failing.
4. `nx guided-upgrade` prints "no footprint... already on the service stack"
   and exits 0 without provisioning or migrating anything.

## Files

- src/nexus/commands/guided_upgrade_cmd.py (step 1 gate)
- src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py (`detect_pending_migration`,
  `detect_already_migrated`)
- src/nexus/migration/detection.py (`open_read_legs`, `classify_collections`)
- src/nexus/commands/migrate_cmd.py (`_run_migration` — contrast, correct T2
  behavior)
- src/nexus/commands/upgrade.py (`_run_upgrade` — related misleading no-op)
- src/nexus/db/storage_mode.py (the RDR-152 hard-default flip this whole
  arc is meant to carry users across)
close_reason: Fixed on develop c83b35b9 (ships 6.3.8). guided-upgrade's no-op now requires BOTH legs clean: empty Chroma + absent T2 SQLite. T2-present proceeds to provision+migrate (T3 no-ops naturally; _run_migration ships T2 unconditionally). Fully-covered installs (all stores skipped by clean reports + no Chroma) reach a clean 'nothing to do' no-op (critique M3 — the mcp_infra degraded-write backstop leaves memory.db on disk in ordinary service-mode operation, so existence alone must not mean work). Success tail warns on exported NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite. Sibling path bug: nexus-id750. GH #1381 auto-closes at the 6.3.8 release merge (Fixes footer).

title: staleness-cache fast-path failure returns EMPTY cache instead of the documented paginated fallback — incremental indexing dark on engine<v0.1.30 (get-all-metadata 404) and over-cap collections
description: Observed live 2026-07-07 (Hal's second box, wheel 6.3.6 + install-era engine): POST /v1/vectors/get-all-metadata -> HTTP 404 during build_staleness_cache -> 'Staleness caches built — 0 docs' -> every subsequent index run treats all files stale = full re-process (and pre-v0.1.27 engines lack RDR-181 embed-skip => full re-EMBED, melted embed budget). Root cause: indexer_utils.build_staleness_cache docstring promises 'falls back to the paginated helper when ... the fast path raises' but the code chooses fast-vs-paginated by ATTRIBUTE PRESENCE only; an exception from get_all_metadata() lands in the outer except and returns an empty cache — the paginated fallback never engages. Same hole fires on CURRENT engines when a big collection trips the server row-count cap (VectorHandler get-all-metadata cap). Existing test test_build_falls_back_to_paginated_when_get_all_metadata_fails locked in the WRONG behavior (asserts empty cache) despite its name. Fix: fast path in its own try; on failure WARN (with engine-upgrade hint on 404) and fall through to _paginated_get; empty cache only when BOTH fail. Related: version-skew nudge (wheel calls routes older engines lack) is a broader gap — this fix makes the client tolerate it correctly at this callsite.
close_reason: Fixed on develop 32d3d6cf. build_staleness_cache now genuinely falls back to the paginated sweep on any fast-path exception (404 from pre-v0.1.30 engines gets an engine-upgrade hint; row-cap/transient failures warn + fall back); empty-cache degrade only when both paths fail; NEW loud warning for the silently-empty-fallback shape (service-mode HttpVectorClient.get swallows errors to empty pages — review HIGH). 47/47 tests incl. 3 new; both stacked reviewers clear (code-review-expert APPROVE; substantive-critic HIGH addressed in-arc). Follow-up nexus-qci5b filed for the .get() swallow-convention divergence. Dup nexus-1kise closed. title: MintRateLimiter: unbounded per-tenant bucket map keyed on attacker-supplied tenant string
description:
Gate-B critique (nexus-x1h07 Phase 4-5): MintRateLimiter.tryAcquire (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/MintRateLimiter.java) keys CredentialState.tenants (a ConcurrentHashMap<String,Bucket>) on the raw 'tenant' string taken verbatim from the mint request body (DataTokenHandler.handleMint passes body.get("tenant") straight through). tenant_id is a plain TEXT column with NO FK/existence validation anywhere in TokenStore, so ANY string is accepted. Every distinct tenant string a caller has ever presented gets a permanent Bucket entry -- created via computeIfAbsent BEFORE the global-rate check, on every call regardless of outcome -- and there is no eviction, TTL, or max-size cap anywhere in the class.

Impact: a single legitimately-issued-but-then-abusing (or merely buggy) scope=mint credential can grow this map without bound over the engine's lifetime (bounded only by the per-credential global rate, ~10/min default = ~14k/day), causing slow unbounded heap growth on the SINGLE engine instance that serves ALL tenants -- a full-service memory-exhaustion DoS, which directly inverts this feature's own stated goal of containing a compromised mint credential's blast radius to "one tenant, one TTL window" (RDR-005 pin ii/iii).

Precedent already exists in this codebase for exactly this class of risk: TokenCache.DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TokenCache.java) is a flood backstop for an analogous attacker-influenced-cardinality map. MintRateLimiter has no equivalent.

Fix: cap distinct tenant-bucket entries per credential (LRU eviction or a DEFAULT_MAX_TENANT_BUCKETS constant mirroring TokenCache's pattern), or evict buckets that have been at full capacity (unused) longer than some idle window. Lower-priority secondary observation: CredentialState entries for revoked/rotated mint credentials are also never removed from the outer 'credentials' map, but that dimension is root-issuance-bounded (not attacker-controlled) so is much lower severity.

Found during: substantive-critic Gate-B review of nexus-x1h07 Phases 4-5 (T2 nexus/design-868dq-x1h07-scoped-tokens-data-mint.md, plan nexus/plan-868dq-x1h07-scoped-tokens.md).
close_reason: Fixed in the same Gate-B remediation pass: MintRateLimiter bounds BOTH maps (MAX_CREDENTIALS=1000, MAX_TENANT_BUCKETS_PER_CREDENTIAL=10000) with the TokenCache evict-25% overflow pattern; eviction covered by MintRateLimiterTest (tenantBucketMap_boundedWithEviction, credentialMap_boundedWithEviction). Wildcard-tenant validation also moved BEFORE the rate-limit debit (the compounding vector).

title: Race: TTL-eviction closes cached service T2Database while in-flight write_fn() may still be using it
description:
Found during substantive-critique of nexus-53x7s's fix (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py `_get_cached_service_t2database` / `t2_index_write`).

_get_cached_service_t2database() acquires _service_t2_lock only for the get-or-create decision, then RELEASES it before the caller (t2_index_write) invokes write_fn(db) against the returned instance. On TTL expiry, a DIFFERENT thread's _get_cached_service_t2database() call acquires the lock, sees the cached (db, ts) is stale, and calls db.close() -- which recursively closes all 8 Http*Store httpx.Client connection pools -- with NO check for whether another thread is still mid-flight inside write_fn(db) using that same instance.

This is a genuine regression: the prior per-call-construction behavior never shared an instance across concurrent callers, so there was nothing to race. The new module-level cache introduces a shared, mutable, closeable resource with no reference counting / in-flight-usage tracking.

Blast radius: t2_index_write is called from mcp_infra.py's taxonomy_assign_batch_hook and chash_dual_write_batch_hook (both wrapped in broad `except Exception` -> debug-log-only, so a close-induced exception there would SILENTLY DROP the write -- and would NOT be caught by the RDR-129 dropped-writes meter, which only pattern-matches "locked"/"busy" error text, not a closed-client error) and from aspect_worker.py's poll loop (multiple call sites, ~line 48/84 per grep). Whether concurrent invocation is currently possible depends on whether the long-lived MCP server process (which this file's own comments repeatedly describe as long-lived/multi-call, e.g. get_catalog_writer/manifest_write_batch_hook docstrings) ever dispatches tool calls from more than one thread concurrently -- FastMCP-style servers typically run sync tool handlers in a thread pool, which would make this reachable in production, not just theoretical.

Fix direction: extend the lock's hold duration to cover the full checkout/use/return lifecycle (e.g. refcount the cached instance, defer close() until refcount reaches zero), or defer close() to a background reaper that only closes instances no longer referenced.

Full critique in T2 memory: nexus/critique-nexus-53x7s-t2-cache-fix.
close_reason: Fixed by the nexus-53x7s redesign (TTL cache -> process-lifetime singleton): _service_t2_lock is now held for the FULL checkout-through-write_fn span (t2_index_write wraps 'with _service_t2_lock: return _service_t2_write_locked(write_fn)'), not just the get-or-build decision. A concurrent caller can never close() the instance while another thread is mid-flight inside write_fn(db) -- the whole call is serialized under one lock. Verified via tests/test_t2_index_write_service_mode_cache.py (3 tests, all green) plus full suite (12276 passed).

title: t2_index_write's per-call T2Database construction in service mode drowns per-run logs in init noise (96% of log volume)
description:
Live shakeout 2026-07-06 (nx index repo on nexus itself, post v6.3.3): the new per-run log file (nexus-mjc9l) captured 3233 total lines, of which 3096 (96%) are repeated client-construction INFO messages:

  http_catalog_client.init (394x), http_telemetry_store.init (387x), http_taxonomy_store.init (387x),
  http_plan_library.init (387x), http_memory_store.init (387x), http_document_highlights_store.init (387x),
  http_document_aspects_store.init (387x), http_aspect_queue.init (387x), http_centroid_store.init (115x)

Root cause: mcp_infra.py:342-354, `t2_index_write()`. In SERVICE mode this is documented, by-design behavior:
"in SERVICE mode the Java service (PG) is the write arbiter ... route straight to a direct service-backed
T2Database" -- constructing a FRESH T2Database(...) (which builds all ~8 Http*Store sub-clients, each logging
an .init line) on EVERY call, not once per process/run. The aspect-worker's per-document hooks
(aspect_worker.py:334,403,509,548,580,1229,1357) call t2_index_write once per document, so ~387 documents
processed this run = ~387 fresh T2Database constructions = ~3096 near-identical init log lines.

Impact: this is exactly the kind of noise the per-run log file (nexus-mjc9l) was built to give operators clean
visibility into -- but 96% of the file's content is construction boilerplate that conveys zero indexing
progress information, actively burying the real per-file/RDR progress signal an operator (or `grep`) would
want. Likely also a minor efficiency cost (8x object construction per document instead of once per run),
though the __init__ bodies were not profiled -- may be cheap attribute-setting, or may do real work (auth/
session setup) worth checking.

Fix shape (not designed): two independent angles, likely both worth doing --
(a) Cache/reuse ONE service-backed T2Database instance across the whole `nx index repo` run (or at least
    across one aspect-worker processing pass) instead of constructing fresh per t2_index_write call in
    service mode -- t2_index_write's docstring already frames per-daemon-probe SQLite-mode construction as
    the exceptional path; the service-mode branch has no such excuse to construct fresh every time.
(b) Regardless of (a), downgrade the http_*_store.init events from INFO to DEBUG, or log once per process
    via a module-level "already logged" guard -- matches the spirit of "structured logging should be
    signal, not boilerplate" even if (a) isn't done.

Found via the same live shakeout that confirmed nexus-3lswy's RDR-loop batching (249 indexed, 0 failed, 253s)
and nexus-mjc9l's per-run log file both work correctly end-to-end -- this is a genuine, separate finding
about the QUALITY of what lands in that log file, not a regression in either of those two features.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SEVERITY CORRECTION (2026-07-06): this is NOT just log noise. Confirmed via src/nexus/db/t2/http_telemetry_store.py:63-103 (and presumably the other 7 Http*Store classes share the pattern): each __init__ constructs a FRESH httpx.Client(...) connection pool. The class docstring explicitly says 'Uses a keep-alive httpx.Client connection pool' — but since a new client is built on EVERY t2_index_write call in service mode (mcp_infra.py:342-354's documented per-call construction), the keep-alive pooling is completely defeated: every T2 write pays a fresh TCP+TLS handshake instead of reusing an established connection. Compounding factor: T2Database.__init__ eagerly constructs ALL 8 sub-store clients (catalog, telemetry, taxonomy, plan_library, memory, document_highlights, document_aspects, aspect_queue) regardless of which ONE the caller's write_fn actually touches — so a single aspect-worker document_aspects.upsert() call pays for 8 fresh connection pools when it needs 1.

This likely directly compounds with nexus-xedhp (the missing update_many / serial-per-file-catalog-update finding) if that code path also reconstructs its HTTP client per call rather than reusing one across the run — worth checking whether HttpCatalogClient specifically (used by _catalog_hook's Pass 1 inline updates) also pays fresh-connection cost per file, which would mean the 175.5s measured for 1718 serial updates includes N fresh TCP+TLS handshakes, not just N fast reused-connection round trips. That would make connection reuse a MUCH higher-leverage fix than adding update_many batching alone.

Recommend: (1) verify whether HttpCatalogClient's own __init__ is on this same fresh-per-call construction path during _catalog_hook's Pass 1, (2) if so, this bead and nexus-xedhp should likely be fixed together — connection-pool reuse first (cheaper, more general), THEN batching (update_many) on top.

comments.text: CORRECTION to my own prior comment: verified _catalog_hook's Pass 1 (nexus-xedhp's 175.5s serial-update finding) constructs its catalog writer ONCE (indexer.py:741, make_catalog_writer()) before the per-file loop and reuses that same object for all 1718 writer.update() calls (indexer.py:908) — so nexus-xedhp is NOT compounded by connection-pool churn, it's purely the missing-update_many batching gap as originally scoped. These two beads are INDEPENDENT, not compounding: nexus-xedhp = _catalog_hook's Pass 1 (already reuses its client, just lacks batching); nexus-53x7s = t2_index_write's service-mode path in the aspect-worker (genuinely reconstructs a fresh client, with fresh httpx.Client connection pools, on every call). Fix them separately; no shared root cause or shared fix ordering constraint after all.

comments.text: CONCRETE MEASUREMENT (same live shakeout, 2026-07-06): the run's own --debug-timing-style summary reported 'Chunk batching: 121 upload batches, 146.3s upload; hooks 1082.8s file-grain + 818.9s flush-grain' — hook time (1901.7s total, ~31.7 MINUTES) is ~13x the actual chunk upload time (146.3s). Hooks (file-grain + flush-grain, which include the aspect-worker's per-document t2_index_write calls this bead is about) are almost certainly THE dominant cost of the entire indexing run, not embedding/upload. This is strong, measured evidence this bead is a real, high-value perf fix, not a cosmetic log-noise cleanup — raising confidence significantly. Recommend profiling file-grain vs flush-grain hook time split specifically against the aspect-enqueue path to confirm t2_index_write's fresh-T2Database-per-call pattern is the/a major contributor before scoping the fix.

comments.text: ALREADY SHIPPED — closing as stranded-open (feedback_stranded_in_progress_beads pattern). Commit c29d834c (2026-07-05, on develop AND main, i.e. released in 6.3.x) implements BOTH fix angles: (a) process-lifetime service-mode T2Database singleton in mcp_infra.py (_service_t2_db + _service_t2_lock, held checkout-through-use; reactive eviction on write failure to recover from rotated storage_service leases) wired into t2_index_write's service branch, PLUS an HttpCatalogClient singleton on the catalog-factory path; (b) all 8 http_*_store.init events downgraded INFO->DEBUG. The bead's fresh-httpx-Client-per-call severity finding and the 8x-construction waste are both eliminated by the singleton; per-run log noise by the downgrade.

title: catalog write-path missing batched update_many — every git commit forces N serial per-file catalog updates
description:
Live shakeout of nx index repo (nexus repo itself, 2026-07-06, immediately after merging PRs #1363-1366 + cutting v6.3.3): catalog registration took 175.5s for "0 new, 1718 updated" — ~102ms/file, all serial.

Root cause: _catalog_hook's Pass 1 (indexer.py:~824-928) inline-calls writer.update() one file at a time for every doc whose head_hash/physical_collection/source_mtime/content_hash differs from the stored catalog row. Per the existing code comment (indexer.py:819): "a HEAD bump flips every doc's stored head_hash to changed" — since head_hash is the git commit SHA, ANY new commit invalidates the "unchanged, skip write" fast path (nexus-dst5h) for the ENTIRE repo, forcing every single file through an individual writer.update() network round-trip to the cloud catalog service.

Confirmed via HttpCatalogClient (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py): register_many exists (batched create, pages at 1000, "/doc/register_many"), but there is NO update_many — only a single-doc update() (line 824). Pass 2 (new docs) is properly batched; Pass 1 (existing-but-changed docs) has no batched path to call even if someone wanted one.

This is very likely a major, possibly THE major, contributor to nexus-duoak.11's still-open throughput miss (0.996s/file vs 0.5s/file target, measured 2026-07-05) — duoak.11's gate methodology (re-index after code changes = new commits = new HEAD) would hit this exact path on every single gate run.

Fix shape (not yet designed in detail): add a batched update_many to both the Java service (new endpoint, e.g. POST /doc/update_many, paged like register_many) and HttpCatalogClient, then change _catalog_hook's Pass 1 to accumulate changed-doc updates into a batch (mirroring the existing new_batch/register_many pattern at indexer.py:930+) instead of calling writer.update() inline per file. Needs design work: what fields does update_many take (same as single update()'s **fields kwarg, but per-doc heterogeneous field sets need a batch payload shape), does it need the same fairness-yield per-page semantics register_many has (RDR-146), server-side transaction semantics for partial-batch failure.

Also worth checking: the staleness-cache build phase (same shakeout run) took 101.97s for 1701 docs across 3 collections (staleness_caches_built log event) — may share a related root cause (per-collection by_owner-style fetch cost) or be a separate, distinct slow path worth its own look.
