title: RDR markdown indexing (_discover_and_index_rdrs/batch_index_markdowns) never got the nexus-duoak throughput-arc batching
description:
Discovered live during v6.3.2 shakeout re-index of nexus itself: the 249-file docs/rdr/*.md corpus took many minutes in the 'Discovering and indexing RDR markdown files...' phase, with real (if slow) CPU/network activity the whole time -- not a hang, not just a logging gap (see sibling bead nexus-47ubt for the observability side of this same incident).

Root cause: src/nexus/indexer.py:_discover_and_index_rdrs -> src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:batch_index_markdowns (line ~1886) does a plain `for path in paths: index_markdown(path, ...)` loop -- ONE FILE AT A TIME, sequential, no batching of staleness checks, no batched catalog registration, no chunk-upload batching across files. This is exactly the class of serial per-file round-trip cost that the entire nexus-duoak throughput arc (register_many, batched prune-misclassified manifest fetch, taxonomy/manifest batch endpoints, cross-file chunk batching via ChunkBatcher, flush-grain hooks -- commits 17c16c88, 02318195, b80b14d4, ea1128de, f90f59c1, etc., all shipped in v6.3.2) fixed for the MAIN code/prose/pdf file loop. The RDR corpus path was never brought into that batching work -- it's a separate code path (_discover_and_index_rdrs is explicitly EXCLUDED from the main run_file_loop per its own docstring: 'RDR files are excluded from the main _run_index file loop').

Consequence: on a repo with a large docs/rdr/ tree (this repo: 249 files), re-indexing pays N serial round-trips to the cloud engine for staleness-check + registration, even when RDR-181's embed-skip means most of those files don't need re-embedding at all -- the embed-skip win doesn't help if the SURROUNDING per-file overhead (catalog registration, staleness lookup) is still serial.

Recommended fix: port batch_index_markdowns (or _discover_and_index_rdrs's call site) onto the same batching primitives the main loop now uses -- ChunkBatcher / cross-file batching, register_many for RDR-collection catalog entries, and the existing on_file callback (already present in batch_index_markdowns's signature, just needs wiring + the underlying batching to make it worth watching). This is a genuine performance/scope gap in the nexus-duoak arc, not a logging cosmetic -- the RDR corpus is exactly the kind of doc-heavy repo (CCE embedder, docs__/rdr__ prefix) that RDR-181's own §Context calls out as the worst case for per-chunk sequential cost.

Related: nexus-47ubt (observability gap for this and other silent post-index phases) — fix that first/alongside so future work on this path is easier to verify in real time.
close_reason: Closed

description:

Extend updateMetadata (PgVectorRepository.java:1752-1774) to RETURN its affected-row count. For each have-vector chash, UPDATE metadata/position keeping the stored vector; IF 0 rows matched, move that chash into need-embed (self-heals the existence-check-vs-concurrent-GC-delete race, RDR Risks). TRANSACTION SCOPING (load-bearing, gate round 2): the existence SELECT + have-vector UPDATE-with-reroute run in ONE short txn that COMMITS before embed(); embed() runs OUTSIDE any txn (as today, :394-403); the final INSERT keeps its existing DeadlockRetry wrapper (nexus-ps9wb). title: P1.1 Engine: existence partition in upsertChunksInternal (selectExistingChashes + fail-safe)
description:
TDD, test-first. Add selectExistingChashes(tenant, collection, chashes): a PK-indexed lookup SELECT chash FROM chunks_<dim> WHERE tenant_id=? AND collection=? AND chash = ANY(?). The PK is (tenant_id, collection, chash) on chunks_384/768/1024 (vectors-001-baseline.xml:80/110/140), the same tuple as the ON CONFLICT target, so a batch ANY(?) over a few hundred keys is a ms PK-index lookup. title: [bug] concurrent index hangs ~10min on a propagated upsert failure (unbounded wait + 600s timeout); prose/CCE upserts uncontained
description:
SURFACED: duoak.11 re-gate on v0.1.25, 2026-07-05. When a per-file upsert raises (a prose-file 504 VectorServiceError), the CONCURRENT index run HANGS ~10 min (observed: 0% CPU, idle, 12 min silent at [2132/2133]) instead of failing fast.

ROOT CAUSE (two intertwined client defects):
1. run_file_loop (src/nexus/indexer_utils.py) failure path: on the first worker exception it cancels not-yet-started futures then does an UNBOUNDED wait(futures) for in-flight workers before re-raising. A sibling worker stuck in a slow upsert with _post(timeout=600) (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:625/318) blocks that wait for up to 600s → the whole run appears hung for ~10 min.
2. Prose/CCE upserts go DIRECT via _index_prose_file -> upsert_chunks -> _post, bypassing the ChunkBatcher's file-atomic failure containment + staleness-retry that code-file batches get. So a prose 504 propagates as a HARD run failure (uncontained), which then triggers (1).

IMPACT: a single transient 504 on one prose file can (a) hang the run ~10 min and (b) fail the whole run rather than deferring that file to staleness retry like code files. Amplifies any cloud-side 504 (sibling bead) into a multi-minute wedge + hard failure.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) bound the failure-path wait in run_file_loop (cancel-with-timeout / interrupt in-flight, don't wait full 600s); (b) lower/ýconfigure the 600s upsert timeout for the concurrent path; (c) give prose/CCE upserts the same file-atomic containment + staleness-retry as code batches so a transient 504 defers the file instead of failing the run. (c) is the real parity fix; (a) bounds the hang regardless.
close_reason: Transient-upsert containment (_contain_transient_upsert defers 502/503/504 to staleness) + bounded failure-drain observability, merged + reviewed (both reviewers). Re-gate showed 0 transient-defers needed (nf3n7 stopped 504s at source), but the containment is validated defensive code. Escalation follow-up okz5t.

title: [bug] 504 Gateway Timeout on upsert-chunks (prose/CCE) under load — v0.1.25 duoak.11 re-gate
description:
SURFACED: duoak.11 re-gate on engine-service-v0.1.25 (fastapi 2133 files, 2 workers, --force), 2026-07-05. The ps9wb deadlock is FIXED (0 HTTP 500, 0 40P01, 0 bisect this run). A DIFFERENT failure appeared: 4x HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout on POST /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks, all on the prose/CCE path (voyage-context-3). gateway_retry fired 3x; at least one 504 exhausted the client backoff and raised VectorServiceError.

CHARACTER: 504 = gateway/edge (ALB) timing out a slow upsert response, NOT a service 500/deadlock. Likely the CCE upsert (contextual-embedding, slower per-batch) exceeds the gateway response/idle timeout under sustained concurrent load. Client _post uses timeout=600s but the gateway cuts it at its own (lower) bound and returns 504.

ASK (conexus): characterize the gateway/ALB timeout on /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks — what is the edge response-timeout bound, and does a large CCE upsert batch legitimately exceed it under load? Options: raise the gateway timeout for upsert-chunks, or confirm the client should chunk CCE upserts smaller. Engine logs for the 504 windows would show whether the service completed the write after the gateway gave up (i.e. phantom-success). Pairs with nexus-side client bead (below).
notes:
---
ROOT CAUSE (conexus relay 2026-07-05): the 504 is generated by the control-plane EdgeProxyHandler, NOT the ALB/nginx. Binding = CONEXUS_UPSTREAM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30s, live-confirmed (no override). It bounds TIME-TO-RESPONSE-START (until engine returns status+headers); JDK HttpTimeoutException → 504. Ladder: CP requestTimeout 30s < CP exchangeDeadline 60s == ALB idle 60s < engine nginx 120s < client 180s — the 30s CP timeout fires FIRST. A CCE (voyage-context-3) upsert whose server-side Voyage embed + pgvector write + HNSW takes >30s to emit headers under concurrent load → 504.

FIX = CAP client CCE batch size (conexus recommendation). CP timeouts are GLOBAL (one handler for all /v1/*), deliberate DoS/worker-pool protections — can't raise for one route; raising is a 3-knob coordinated change (CP env ×2 + ALB idle) + redeploys, and widens the worker-pin window. So cap CCE batches so worst-case-under-concurrency response-start < ~25s. Start ~128 chunks (vs ~300 code cap; CCE slower), tune from re-gate p99. The incident was on the DIRECT/oversize-fallback upsert path: a prose file whose chunk count exceeds the 64-chunk CCE ChunkBatcher cap falls back to a single direct upsert of ALL its chunks → one giant slow upsert >30s → 504. Fix: page the direct/fallback prose+PDF upsert into <=128-chunk sub-batches.

PHANTOM-SUCCESS = EXPECTED: the 504 fires on time-to-response-start, but the engine request is in-flight in its own pg txn — the INSERT...ON CONFLICT commits regardless; engine then hits broken-pipe writing the response (row is durable). So a 504 does NOT mean "not written". Composes perfectly with nexus-7yfe6 containment: the deferred file's chunks actually LANDED, so staleness marks it current next run without re-upload. Zero data loss; the 504 count OVERSTATES real failures. (conexus caveat: architectural determination, not log-confirmed — heavy 504 traffic rotated out of the 3h engine log window; conexus offered engine-side elapsed+broken-pipe logging on next duoak run for hard confirmation.)

OPTIONAL (needs explicit go): conexus can do the coordinated edge bump (30→90s / 60→120s / ALB 60→120s) for edge headroom, but accepts a wider worker-pin window + terraform-apply + CP redeploy. Deferred unless the cap proves insufficient.

DEPLOY STANCE: no engine cut, no conexus deploy — the fix (cap CCE) is client-side. v0.1.25 stays.
close_reason: 504 root-caused (CP requestTimeout 30s) + FIXED client-side: HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks pages oversize upserts at per_collection_chunk_cap (CCE 64). VALIDATED: duoak.11 re-gate = 0 HTTP 504 (vs 4 pre-fix). No engine cut. Throughput tuning follow-up o1mbu/9mzkd.

title: [bug] upsert-chunks 504->500 on code__1-62 under batched load (engine-service-v0.1.24, duoak.11 gate)
description:
SURFACED BY: nexus-duoak.11 cloud validation (fastapi 0.115.0, 2133 files, 2 workers, --force) against DEPLOYED engine-service-v0.1.24 on api.conexus-nexus.com, 2026-07-05T01:13-01:16 UTC. Log: tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/results-duoak11-gate-v0124/w2.log.

SYMPTOM: POST /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks returns HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout, then after the client's 3x backoff retry (2s/5s/10s) the ChunkBatcher failure-bisection splits the batch and the SMALLER sub-batches return HTTP 500 internal server error (not 504). Bisection fails to isolate — every sub-batch 500s.

SCOPE: all failures on a SINGLE collection `code__1-62__voyage-code-3__v1` (fastapi code under a benchidx-* scratch owner). Batch sizes 273/278/291/296/298 chunks — all UNDER the 300-chunk code cap. Files 8-19 per batch. Window 01:13:31Z -> 01:16:05Z. 6x HTTP 500 + 4x 504 + 6 bisect events observed before drain.

ESCALATION SHAPE (504 timeout -> 500 on retry) suggests SERVICE-SIDE: the upsert first times out at the gateway, then the retried/smaller write errors 500 — pointing at pgvector write contention, a stuck txn/lock on that collection, or an engine bug in the v0.1.24 upsert-chunks path under sustained batched concurrent load, NOT a client batch-size violation (all within cap).

CLIENT BEHAVIOR IS CORRECT: file-atomic bisection contains the failure (those 8-19 files fail cleanly, staleness retries them next run) — the run does not crash. But the shakeout criterion for duoak.11 is ZERO 5xx at the new default, so this BLOCKS a clean duoak close and needs a service-side root-cause.

SECONDARY: http_taxonomy_store.py:88 emits `RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in matmul` (NaN) during the run — likely downstream of the missing vectors (partial collection), track only if it persists after the 500s are fixed.

ASK (conexus/engine): root-cause the upsert-chunks 500 on code__1-62 under batched load — check engine logs for that collection/tenant at 01:13-01:16Z, pgvector lock/txn state, and whether the 300-cap batched upsert path has a size/concurrency edge in v0.1.24. Determine if this is load-transient (service was busy) or a reproducible v0.1.24 regression.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (conexus relay 2026-07-05, engine host i-0a39ba5abf03bdee7 logs + live DB lock state):

pgvector DEADLOCK (SQLState 40P01) on the multi-row INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, collection, chash) DO UPDATE at PgVectorRepository.java:466 (upsertChunksInternal:435 <- upsertChunksWithTokens:265 <- VectorHandler.handleUpsertChunks:242). Two concurrent upsert batches into the SAME collection touch overlapping chash keys in DIFFERENT orders — the .values() list is built in dedup/arrival order (dedupIds), NOT sorted by the conflict key — so each txn holds a row lock the other needs -> cycle -> PG kills a victim -> HTTP 500.

504->500 EXPLAINED: first large batch slow -> edge 504; client file-atomic bisection then fires multiple concurrent sub-batches into the same collection -> more overlapping-key writers -> deadlock -> 500. Bisection AMPLIFIES (splitting doesn't remove cross-batch key overlap) -> every sub-batch 500s, can't isolate. Heavy intra-collection dup (upsert_dedup_collapsed received=286 kept=87) -> high cross-batch key overlap.

CLASSIFICATION: reproducible ENGINE concurrency bug. NOT client-side (bisection correct, just amplifying). NOT load-transient lock leak (DB clean now, victim rolled back, zero held locks). title: Reconcile the two chash width conventions (128-bit chunk-id vs 256-bit citation) BEFORE typing it
description: chash (sha256(content)[:32], 32 lowercase hex = 128 bits) is a load-bearing invariant enforced only at the DB via CHECK(length(chash)=32) on five tables (catalog_document_chunks, chunks_384/768/1024) plus an ad-hoc read-side guard in PgVectorRepository:2229. It is modelled everywhere as a bare String, so nothing at the HTTP boundary distinguishes a content hash from any text. A caller passing a full 64-char SHA-256 hex (the most natural mistake) passes every handler — they validate structure, never row payloads — and only trips the DB CHECK deep inside a per-row transaction, where write_many/append swallow it into failed_doc_ids with a log.debug and NO reason. Present but mute, at the wrong altitude. Cost 3 deploy-gate iterations on the v0.1.24 batch-endpoint probe (2026-07-04) before the 64->32 cause was found. Fix: a Chash record (parse-don't-validate newtype) whose compact constructor is the sole enforcement point; Jackson binds request-body chash fields through it -> uniform HTTP 400 at the boundary with the actual length in the message, before any txn. Repositories take Chash not String; DB CHECK demotes to belt-and-suspenders. A Chash.fromSha256() factory gives the [:32] truncation a named home, removing the implicit-truncation ambiguity that spawns the bare-64.
design: RECOMMENDED END-STATE (from operator, 2026-07-04): stop storing chash as hex TEXT; store the raw digest as BINARY and treat hex/base64 purely as interchange. Postgres: chash BYTEA with CHECK(octet_length(chash)=32) — 32 BYTES, unambiguous; the 32-vs-64 units bug cannot recur because bytes!=chars. Interchange at the edges only: encode(chash,'hex')=64-char citation out, decode(...,'hex') in; catalog chash:<64hex> grammar unchanged (it renders the key, never stores it). Half the index/disk width of text(64). Value type: record Chash wrapping byte[32] (equals/hashCode over contents), fromHex/toHex(+toBase64) at boundaries, @JsonValue emits hex so wire+existing citations stay byte-compatible; jOOQ binds bytea<->byte[] natively; the type holds bytes, the world sees hex. This is the full-256-bit branch done correctly (binary, not hex-text). COST: current stored chashes are truncated 128-bit ([:32] hex) and the discarded 128 bits are unrecoverable -> a reindex is required, BUT it is a REHASH pass over existing chunk_text (sha256 over stored text you already have) + old-id->new-id remap of chunk tables/manifests/chash_index — NOT a re-embed (no Voyage, vectors reused via id map). Offline ETL. Supersedes the earlier 'text(32) vs text(64)' framing; the drafted Chash.java (String-backed, LENGTH=32 hex) is provisional and should be rewritten byte[32]-backed once the RDR blesses the 32-byte binary target. Original earlier design notes retained below for the seam inventory.
acceptance_criteria: Chash type + unit test committed via nexus PR; at least the manifest write path (write/append/write_many) parses chash at the HTTP boundary so a 64-char chash returns 400 with the offending length (add a handler test asserting this); existing manifest/chash ITs stay green; follow-up bead filed for remaining seams (vectors, chash_index) and for VALIDATE-ing the five CHECK constraints.
notes: HANDOFF-READY (2026-07-04). RDR-180 draft COMPLETE (docs/rdr/rdr-180-content-address-chash-binary-32byte.md, uncommitted): full sections incl. Item8 null/orphaned chunk_text disposition (3-way: rehashable / reference-only-recoverable-remap / orphaned drop-cascade-or-synthesize-with-metadata.chash_origin flag), dangling-manifest + synthetic-key failure modes, test plan, Item6 ETL + Item8 each flagged for own closing bead. A-1 VERIFIED (residue 0, truncation corpus-wide). Provisional String-backed Chash.java + ChashTest.java in service/src (uncommitted) — REWRITE to byte[32] once width blessed. NEXT (nexus side): (1) register+gate RDR-180 via nexus rdr lifecycle; (2) verify A-2 (EXPLAIN bytea(32) vs text(32)), A-3 (external hex-string chunk-id consumers), A-5 (offline/freeze-gated remap, no racing writer); (3) decompose Items1-8 to closing beads; (4) rewrite Chash byte[32]. Does NOT touch the live 0.1.24 deploy. conexus-side origin: v0.1.24 batch-endpoint gate.

Today resolve_index_concurrency._backend_default (indexer_utils.py:594-603) checks only vectors + catalog service-mode; it deliberately does NOT check the T2 memory backend because LockedHookRegistry's blanket lock makes a diverging memory backend safe. Once the lock narrows (P2.3), the memory backend (chash/taxonomy/aspect-queue writes fired in hooks) must be service-backed too or concurrency is unsafe. Add a storage_backend_for('memory')==SERVICE clause to the gate. TDD: write tests/test_indexer_utils.py::test_concurrency_gate_requires_memory_service FIRST — default stays 1 when memory backend is not SERVICE even if vectors+catalog are. Update the resolve_index_concurrency docstring (currently says the gate 'deliberately does NOT check' memory). Test cmd: uv run pytest tests/test_indexer_utils.py -k concurrency. Depends P1.4.
notes: PARKED by design REV 2026-07-04: cross-file chunk batching (Phase 2C beads) supersedes hook-lock narrowing as the primary mechanism; revisit only if post-2C numbers still show hook serialization blocking the <=10min target.
close_reason: OBSOLETE: prerequisite for lock-narrowing; duoak.7 solved via flush-grain firing instead — blanket lock stays (6 flush-grain calls/run). No T2-gate extension needed.

title: Phase 1.4: DECISION GATE — analyze curve, route to Phase 2 or Phase 3
description: Analyze the P1.2 curve. Compute: does wall-clock keep dropping through 8 workers, or flatten early? What is hooks_s share of wall at each worker count? Decision: (A) if wall flattens well before ≤10min/1200-files AND hooks_s share is large/growing with workers → the blanket hook lock (LockedHookRegistry, hook_registry.py:487) + taxonomy re-fetch (mcp_infra.py:725) is the choke → do PHASE 2 then Phase 3. (B) if wall scales cleanly and a worker count in {4,8} already hits ≤10min/1200 → SKIP Phase 2, go straight to Phase 3 (just raise the default). Record the decision + evidence to T2 nexus/duoak-scaling-curve. Reference the T3 pattern note pattern-hook-lock-serialization-defeats-concurrency-nexus-cfc72. Depends P1.2.
notes: EVIDENCE for the decision gate (2026-07-04, accidental capture): an ALL-SKIP incremental re-index of a2ui (1,180 files, every file skipped at ~0s) still took 655s wall — dominated by post-store processing: full taxonomy re-cluster (fetch 1,461 chunks + kmeans), misclassified-chunk pruning, link generation. Implication: the worker-count sweep addresses FIRST-index wall time, but the incremental-index floor is the post pipeline's fixed cost, which no worker count touches. When analyzing the curve, separate per-file wall from post-phase wall (both are in the run logs); if post-phase dominates real-world re-index UX, consider a follow-up bead (skip/incrementalize post steps when 0 files changed) OUTSIDE duoak's <=10min-first-index stop criterion.
close_reason: DECISION MADE (de facto, Hal-approved 2026-07-04): curve flat at 2 workers + hooks_share dominant -> but route changed mid-flight to cross-file batching (design REV, beads f55fu/1ugqs) + flush-grain hooks (duoak.7). Progression 987->812->439s on flask/2w. Remaining: post-processing tail (evidence note on this bead), validation as 3midv/duoak.11.

title: nx collection rename does not re-embed; u37lw ClickException misdirects users into a same-class corruption path
description:
Found during substantive-critic final-gate review of the gc2ze/6lfdi/ke45f/u37lw/mzuj9 batch (2026-07-03/04).

commit c485041a (nexus-u37lw) adds a fail-loud guard in reembed_cmd: when service mode and --to
differs from the collection-name-encoded model, it raises:

    f"... Use 'nx collection rename' (cross-model) to move to a {target_model}-named "
    f"collection, which re-embeds under the new name."

This is false. `nx collection rename <old> <new>` (rename_cmd, src/nexus/commands/collection.py:194)
is documented as "O(1) metadata update -- no embedding re-upload, no Voyage cost, no ChromaDB
egress." Its only validation is a content-type PREFIX check (old.split("__",1)[0] vs new
prefix) gated by --force-prefix-change; it does NOT compare the embedding-model segment at all.
A same-content-type, different-model rename (e.g. code__nexus__voyage-code-3__v1 ->
code__nexus__voyage-code-4__v1) sails through with zero re-embed: rename_collection_data_plane
-> CatalogRepository.renameCollection (service/.../db/CatalogRepository.java:1556) is a pure
registry/identity re-home (verified: no embedding logic in renameCollectionTxn). The vectors
stay exactly as they were under the OLD model, now labeled with a name claiming the NEW model --
the same class of embedding_model-vs-actual-vector mismatch u37lw was written to eliminate, via
an unguarded path the fix didn't touch.

The ACTUAL cross-model re-embed pipeline lives in nexus.migration (RDR-162 P2:
remap_collection_references + vector_etl.py's stored-text re-embed via `nx migrate`/
`guided_upgrade`), a completely separate, heavier, admin-facing workflow -- not `nx collection
rename`. cross_model=True is only ever passed from remap_collection_references, never from
rename_cmd.

Fix options: (a) reword the ClickException to point at the actual migrate/guided-upgrade path
instead of `nx collection rename`; (b) add a model-segment check to rename_cmd itself that
rejects (or --force-flags) a same-prefix rename whose embedding-model segment differs, mirroring
the existing prefix guard; (c) both. Do NOT ship guidance text that sends operators toward a
silent-corruption path while the whole point of this arc was eliminating exactly that failure
mode.

Context: nx memory project=nexus title=critique-batch-gc2ze-6lfdi-ke45f-u37lw-mzuj9-2026-07-04
close_reason: Fixed in 8a24fde1: re-embed guidance now points at the real migration pipeline (rename never re-embeds); rename_cmd gains the model-segment guard mirroring the prefix guard. Final-critique Critical, same-day fix.

title: nx collection re-embed --no-dry-run silently no-ops (wrong model) in service mode
description:
nexus-c9xr2 (commit 502103a5) fixed the AttributeError crash on
db._client.get_collection(...) by switching to db.get_collection(). The
command no longer crashes, but the WRITE path (--no-dry-run) still does not
actually re-embed with --to <target_model> in service mode.

_reembed_collection (src/nexus/commands/collection.py:929) calls
db.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings(collection_name=col_name, ids=v_ids,
documents=v_docs, embeddings=embeddings, metadatas=v_metas) after computing
`embeddings` via voyageai.Client(...).embed(texts=batch, model=target_model).

On HttpVectorClient (service/cloud mode, the now-primary supported mode
post-RDR-155/release-boundary-lift), upsert_chunks_with_embeddings
(src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:587-609) explicitly DISCARDS the
caller-supplied embeddings and forwards only text via self.upsert_chunks(...)
with embeddings=None. Its own docstring says so: "Server-side embed path:
forward chunk text, ignore caller's embeddings... the Python-side embeddings
are discarded." The claim that this "matches T3Database.upsert_chunks_with_
embeddings so it works transparently as a drop-in" is false for this caller:
T3Database's version (src/nexus/db/t3.py:942) stores caller-supplied vectors
VERBATIM (bypasses the collection's embedding function) -- the opposite
contract.

Server-side (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/
PgVectorRepository.java upsertChunksInternal, via EmbedderRouter.
resolveEmbedderStrict) re-embeds using the model encoded in the COLLECTION
NAME (RDR-103 <content_type>__<owner>__<model>__v<n>), NOT target_model.
reembed_cmd's own docstring says the command deliberately does NOT rename
the collection. So in service mode:

1. The client-side Voyage call (model=target_model) is 100% wasted API
   spend -- its output is thrown away.
2. The server re-embeds every chunk using the OLD model (whatever the
   collection name already encodes) -- a same-model no-op re-embed
   whenever target_model != that old model, i.e. every real use of --to.
3. _reembed_collection stamps metadata["embedding_model"] = target_model
   before the call (collection.py:926-928) -- that false metadata is sent
   and persisted, corrupting check_staleness: future indexer passes will
   believe the chunks already carry target_model vectors when they don't.
4. reembed_cmd reports "re-embedded N chunk(s) ... with <target_model>"
   (collection.py:1022-1025) -- a false success message.

No is_local_mode()/is_service_backed() guard exists anywhere in
_reembed_collection/reembed_cmd to detect or reject this. No validation
compares target_model against embedding_model_for_collection(col_name)
(already imported at collection.py:11, unused for this purpose).

Test coverage gap: the new real-client E2E added by nexus-c9xr2
(tests/test_service_mode_cli_real_client.py::
test_collection_reembed_dry_run_service_mode_real_client) covers dry-run
ONLY. The unit test for the write path
(tests/test_collection_cmd.py::test_reembed_no_dry_run_writes_via_voyage)
uses fake_db = MagicMock(spec=HttpVectorClient) with
upsert_chunks_with_embeddings.side_effect replaced by a capture stub -- it
never runs the real HttpVectorClient method body, so it cannot catch this;
its assertions (and docstring: "embeds via Voyage and upserts the new
vectors") encode the wrong mental model of production behavior.

Fix options: (a) reject --to in service mode with a clear ClickException
until a server route exists to force a specific embedder for a batch
(rename-then-reembed or an explicit model override on /v1/vectors/
upsert-chunks), or (b) implement via db.upsert_chunks(..., embeddings=...)
using the existing same-model PASSTHROUGH (nexus-hxry2) ONLY when
target_model already equals the collection's encoded model, erroring
otherwise, or (c) extend the service to accept an explicit embed-model
override on upsert-chunks. Until fixed, do not advertise
`nx collection re-embed --no-dry-run` as working in service/cloud mode.

Found during substantive-critic review of commit 502103a5 (nexus-c9xr2)
before the develop batch push, 2026-07-04.
close_reason: Fixed in c485041a + test follow-up: cross-model --to fails loud pre-write in service mode (rename cross-model flow is the pointer); same-model routes through the nexus-hxry2 verbatim passthrough so client vectors are genuinely stored; real-client write-path E2Es pin both (rejection posts nothing; passthrough body carries the vectors). Found by the tail substantive-critic tracing the full client->Java chain; the prior unit test mocked the exact method whose real body diverged.

title: engine-service-release: cache-hit path for pg-bundle never re-verifies contrib-module completeness (pg_trgm)
description:
nexus-m8au7 (PG-bundle GHA cache) diff review finding (substantive-critic, 2026-07-03).

scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh's verify_and_mark() checks for vector.control AND
pg_trgm.control (RDR-155 needs pg_trgm) — but verify_and_mark() only runs
inside the script itself, i.e. on a cache MISS (fresh compile).

On a cache HIT (the new fast path added by nexus-m8au7), the ONLY
post-restore checks are:
  1. engine-service-release.yml "Package .txz": `[ -x "$bundle/bin/initdb" ]`
     (single-binary existence check)
  2. "Verify the PUBLISHED artifact is genuinely relocatable" (relocation
     gate): `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` + a SELECT check — vector
     only, pg_trgm is never exercised.

A corrupted/partial cache restore (GH Actions cache storage bit-rot or
partial-save) that lost pg_trgm.control/pg_trgm.so while leaving
initdb + vector intact would sail through both gates, get cosign-signed, and
get published to the release — undetected until a user's RDR-155
migration fails downstream. This is the same undetected-broken-published-
artifact failure shape as the 2026-07-01 macOS relocatability postmortem
(nx memory nexus/postmortem-macos-pg-bundle-nonrelocatable-2026-07-01.md)
that this very release pipeline was hardened against.

Fix options: extend the "Package .txz" hollow-prefix check (or the
relocation gate) to also assert
  pg_config --sharedir)/extension/pg_trgm.control exists, and/or
  CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm in the relocation gate,
so the cache-hit path re-verifies the same contrib-module completeness that
verify_and_mark() guarantees on a fresh compile.

Context: nx — see substantive-critic report on nexus-m8au7 diff, memory_put

title: Batch the per-file catalog round-trips in the pre-index sweep — owner-scoped list + local join (finding #3, 6.3.0 live shakeout)
description: 6.3.0 live shakeout (2026-07-03): a warm 'nx index repo .' against the cloud spent 25+ minutes in the PRE-INDEX phases before being cut short — near-zero CPU, low-KB/s traffic, serial WAN round-trips. Root cause: SQLite-era per-file loops survived the RDR-152 HTTP cutover. The catalog registration hook does a per-file by_file_path lookup (+register when absent) for every file in the repo (~1,400), and _build_frecency_doc_id_map does a SECOND per-file by_file_path pass — ~1,400-2,800 sequential HTTPS round-trips at WAN latency, paid on EVERY run even with zero changed files. The staleness cache is already batched (300/page) and fine. FIX (client-side, ~90% of the win, no engine cut needed): GET /v1/catalog/list?owner= already returns the owner's documents — fetch once (paged), build a file_path->doc dict locally, and join both the registration hook and the frecency map against it; only genuinely-missing files then register. CONDITIONAL engine half: if per-new-file registration is still chatty on first-index, add a register_batch endpoint or reuse the RDR-176 import_batch machinery — only matters on first-index, warm runs register nothing. Related but distinct: nexus-cfc72 (file-level concurrency) helps the processing phase; this bead kills the fixed per-run tax that dominates warm runs. Bandwidth profile evidence: download-heavy small-JSON (100KB-in/3.5KB-out per sample), no re-embed upload storm — the incremental machinery works, the loop SHAPE is the cost.
close_reason: Shipped 24db0265 on develop: one by_owner fetch + local join in both _catalog_hook and _build_frecency_doc_id_map; no-op update skip; loud per-file fallback on owner-list failure. Reviewed by code-review-expert + substantive-critic; both Criticals fixed same-session (failure blast radius, service-mode HttpCatalogClient test coverage through _to_entry JSON coercion). Engine register_batch half deferred per bead conditional (warm runs register nothing).

title: (BUG) nx store expire crashes in service mode — HttpVectorClient.expire missing (unguarded)
description: nexus-umvh2 sibling audit: 'nx store expire' calls _t3().expire() with NO try/except guard — AttributeError in service mode (HttpVectorClient has no expire()). Unlike find_ids_by_title/list_store/collection_info (fixed in nexus-umvh2), this was deliberately NOT fixed in that bead: T3Database.expire() needs a Mongo-style '{"ttl_days": {"$gt": 0}}' where-filter operator to pre-filter permanent (ttl_days=0) entries before the Python-side is_expired() check, and a grep of service/src/main/java found zero '$gt' handling in the where-filter path — the server-side /v1/vectors/get where-clause appears equality-only. Implementing expire() naively would either silently misbehave (if the server ignores the unsupported operator) or requires new engine-side support (out of scope for a client-only bead per RDR-158/155 port-gap convention). Needs a design decision: (a) add $gt support server-side, or (b) fetch all ttl_days-bearing rows client-side and filter Python-side (page through the WHOLE knowledge__* collection — could be expensive for large corpora). Fix: implement HttpVectorClient.expire() once the where-filter question is resolved.
close_reason: HttpVectorClient.expire() implemented (commit 61f61397): design call resolved client-side — server $ne 0 replaces $gt 0 (equivalent: TTLs never negative, is_expired authoritative Python-side, NULL-inclusive rows filtered). Accumulate-then-delete pagination, batch_delete at quota, errors propagate. 5 new tests + parity pin.

title: /v1/chash/upsert_many 500s under concurrent indexing load — chash-ledger dual-writes failing ~16/21 batches (data safe, ledger holed)
description: 6.2.0 shakeout indexing run (2026-07-03, live): chash_index_dual_write_failed on ~16 of the first 21 files (HTTP 500 'internal server error' from /v1/chash/upsert_many). DIFFERENTIAL: 1-row and 200-row batches both succeed solo (0.5s) — failures ONLY under concurrent indexing load (heavy /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks traffic with server-side Voyage embedding running simultaneously). 500 is the catch-all (not a typed 409) = unhandled server-side exception, likely pool/connection saturation on the engine (v0.1.19) — the AspectHandler-era enqueue path had similar contention classes. DATA IMPACT: none for chunks (T3 primary writes succeed; dual-write is best-effort by design, resolver falls back to per-collection scan) but the cloud chash ledger has HOLES for every failed batch — repair by re-running a ledger sweep after the fix. NEEDS: engine-side exception logs for the window (conexus relay) or RDR-177 handler metrics to identify the exact failure. Also: 201 inert probe chashes (shakeout-batch-*, shakeout500probe*) registered into knowledge__shakedown's ledger during the repro — clean with delete_stale or leave as ledger residue. Cross-links: RDR-177 (this is exactly the observability gap), nexus-1usso (server contention class).
close_reason: Shipped on develop (cherry-pick 6124a4e3; composed full suite 1036/1036). ROOT CAUSE (deterministically reproduced, CollectionRegistryTest): catalog_collections lock convoy — every batch write ran INSERT..ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the SAME (tenant,name) row; PG blocks that statement on ANY uncommitted concurrent write to the conflicting row; blocked txns hoard HikariCP connections -> pool exhaustion -> SQLTransientConnectionException -> opaque 500 (matches the ~16/21 shakeout failure rate). FIX: (1) process-local CollectionRegistry known-pairs cache, marked ONLY post-commit (verified at all 6 call sites — never inside the withTenant lambda, rollback cannot poison the cache); (2) PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal batched per-chunk INSERT loop into one multi-row statement (another un-batching instance, shrinks the blocking window); (3) SQLTransientConnectionException -> typed 503 in Chash/Vector handlers (retryable, pairs with the client ladder). Honest test limitation documented: localhost Testcontainers can't discriminate pre/post at the HTTP level; the deterministic lock-wait test is the mechanism proof. REACHES CLOUD ONLY via the next engine cut — live 500s persist until v0.1.20 deploys.

title: migrate_aspects hardcodes dropped document_aspects.source_path column — crashes migrate_all on any fresh T2 DB
description:
Discovered while running tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --hole-punch (nexus-s3dd4.7).

src/nexus/db/t2/aspects_etl.py:260 (migrate_aspects) hardcodes "source_path"
in its base_cols SELECT list for document_aspects, but that column was
dropped by RDR-096 P5.2 (nexus-ocu9.11, commits eb1ee8c4 / 694e50f7 #666/#676).
Every OTHER schema-evolution column (doc_id, source_uri, salient_sentences) is
presence-checked via extra_cols; source_path was never migrated to that
pattern when it was dropped.

Effect: `SELECT collection, source_path, ... FROM document_aspects` raises
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: source_path on ANY local T2
database created (or migrated) after RDR-096 P5.2 shipped — i.e. essentially
every current install. migrate_all's aspects store crashes unconditionally
(even with zero document_aspects rows, since the query itself is invalid
regardless of data). This propagates into nx storage migrate all --report
(total_failed=1) and, more importantly, blocks nx guided-upgrade entirely:
the sequencer (nexus.migration.sequencer.run_sequenced_migration) requires
T2 migrate-all's total_failed==0 before starting the T3 vector leg
("a dirty T2 keeps the downstream manifest validation non-vacuous"), so this
crash fails the WHOLE guided-upgrade / migrate-to-service journey, not just
the aspects store.

Repro (confirmed 2026-07-02, engine-service-v0.1.18, wheel built from
develop tip 4cc16a0e/4053531f):
  1. Fresh local T2 sqlite (T2Database(..., run_migrations=True) — any new
     install or e2e seed does this).
  2. nx storage migrate all --report /tmp/r.json  (or nx guided-upgrade)
  3. "aspects: CRASHED — no such column: source_path"; report shows
     STORE aspects TABLE aspects failed=1, reason "store-level ETL crash:
     no such column: source_path".

Fix: drop "source_path" from migrate_aspects' base_cols (or presence-check
it like the other evolved columns, defaulting to "" when absent), and audit
_transform_aspect's row.get("source_path") default. NOT touched by this bead
— tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --hole-punch is blocked pending this
fix; re-run once landed.

TDD failing-first; 1357 tests green. Found by the --hole-punch e2e journey (nexus-s3dd4.7).

title: cheap no-op gate for the four count-unmapped telemetry tables (engine whitelist + sound parity semantics)
description: R3b critic HIGH on d27f78b0 (P3b): relevance_log/search_telemetry/tier_writes/frecency have no _VERIFY_TABLES relation AND are absent from the engine's relation-counts whitelist (probed 2026-07-02: ServiceCountSource returns {} for all four), so every migrate-all --verify-fill probes their ENTIRE contents (search_telemetry=45,440 rows today = ~152 sequential probe requests per no-op run, unbounded growth). Context: still strictly cheaper than the pre-P3b unconditional full re-send, so not a regression — but the 'no-op verify = cheap' promise is unmet for telemetry. Fix needs BOTH: (1) engine-side: add the four relations to the relation-counts whitelist (rides an engine cut); (2) design a SOUND parity gate — naive count comparison is invalid here: DO NOTHING collapses source dupes (target<source ambiguous: collapse vs hole) and post-migration live writes land target-side directly (target>source proves nothing). Candidate: distinct-source-key count vs a target count restricted to... needs design; consider a watermark (probe only rows newer than last verified fill) as the practical alternative.
notes: RELEASE-GATE (Hal, 2026-07-13). The cheap outer loop: given a store's per-table WRITTEN/source counts, diff against target counts via the ALREADY-DEPLOYED relation_counts surface (HttpCatalogClient.relation_counts, src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:513 -> POST /v1/catalog/verify/relation-counts). NO new engine endpoint — this task is explicitly unblocked and can start immediately.

SCOPE:
- New module src/nexus/migration/verify_fill.py.
- Function verify_store_counts(store, count_source: CountSource, source_counts: dict[table,int]) -> dict[table, {"source_count", "target_count", "status"}] where status in {"parity","divergent","indeterminate"}. Reuse the existing CountSource Protocol + ServiceCountSource from src/nexus/migration/orchestrator.py:81-123 (do NOT duplicate; import or lift to a shared spot).
- Reuse the (store,table)->relation mapping _VERIFY_TABLES (orchestrator.py:45-59). A count-parity table (target_count >= source_count) is marked "parity" and the caller SKIPS its inner loop (design: no-op verify = one HTTP call per store). A missing/None count is "indeterminate" (never a pass — nexus-r0esi).
- Source counts read from the SQLite source per table (mirror each ETL's count_source_rows).

TDD (write FIRST): tests/migration/test_verify_fill_outer.py — a fake CountSource returning controlled counts; assert parity table -> "parity"/skip, short table -> "divergent", unreachable -> "indeterminate". Deterministic, no network.
Test cmd: uv run pytest tests/migration/test_verify_fill_outer.py -q

DEPENDS ON: nothing (zero engine dep — the whole point).
Reminder: sequentialthinking for the parity/indeterminate boundary; spawn no children; write the failing test before impl.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: AUDIT FIX: the outer count-diff MUST replicate the _VERIFY_TABLES_DEDUP special case (orchestrator.py:78, currently {nexus.plans}). plans is keyed UNIQUE(tenant_id,project,query) DO UPDATE, so source duplicates converge onto one PG row and target_count < source_count is convergence-by-design, NOT a hole. Mark dedup relations parity when 0 < target_count <= source_count (mirror verify_counts' dedup branch, orchestrator.py:308-335).

title: verify-fill P0: identity-surface inventory per T2 store+table (spike, gates Java + inner loop)
description:
SPIKE / analysis (RDR-178 wave-2, nexus-s3dd4). Produce the identity-surface inventory that gates the Java endpoint work (P1) and the inner diff+fill loop (P3). NO production code — output is a decision doc committed to T2 (nexus/verify-fill-identity-inventory.md) + the bead's design notes.

For EACH T2 store and each of its tables, record:
1. The server-side conflict-key tuple (the row "identity") — read from the Java repository doImportBatch SQL / migration schema, e.g. chash = (tenant_id, chash, physical_collection); plans = (tenant_id, project, query); memory = (tenant_id, project, title).
2. Whether a target-side identity surface ALREADY exists that can answer "which of these identities are present?" — either a full-enumeration endpoint (like GET /v1/chash/registered_chashes returning chash[:32] per collection) OR a membership-probe (like HttpVectorClient.existing_ids(collection, ids) at src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:996). List HAVE vs NEED.
3. The importBatch client method + route used to fill (e.g. HttpChashIndex -> POST /v1/chash/import).
4. The source-row columns each ETL reads (src/nexus/db/t2/<store>_etl.py).

DESIGN GUIDANCE to settle in the doc:
- Prefer a MEMBERSHIP-PROBE surface (send source identities as candidates, receive the present subset; missing = source - present) over full-enumeration where batch size (<=300 per chroma_quotas MAX_QUERY_RESULTS / write) allows. Cheaper than streaming ~448k identities to conclude "nothing to do" (design Rejected option C).
- Rank the tables by incident value: catalog.document_chunks (the 270-row hole, 2026-07-01) is the highest-value new endpoint.
- Endpoints that must be ADDED ride the wave-3 engine-service-v0.1.18 cut (design Constraints).

Files to read: service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/{Memory,Plan,Telemetry,Taxonomy,Aspect,Chash,Catalog}Handler.java; service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/*Repository.java; src/nexus/db/t2/*_etl.py; src/nexus/db/t2/http_*.py.

DELIVERABLE: a summary table store|table|conflict-key|has-surface?(route or NEED)|fill-route, + the recommended per-table diff strategy (probe vs enumerate). This IS the plan's Task-1 identity-endpoint inventory.

Reminder: use sequentialthinking for the probe-vs-enumerate tradeoff; spawn no children; TDD not applicable (analysis only).
close_reason: Inventory validated and accepted: T2 nexus/verify-fill-identity-inventory.md (planner pre-populated, spot-checked 2026-07-02 — existing_ids :996, upsert_chunks :489, get_embeddings :1108, relation_counts :513 -> POST /v1/catalog/verify/relation-counts, memory ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,project,title) all exact; registered_chashes + manifest/chashes routes confirmed in handlers). Key conclusions stand: only genuine new-endpoint gap is the six telemetry tables (rides v0.1.18); incident-recovery slice (chash + catalog document_chunks) engine-free; membership-probe preferred over enumeration where batch<=300. Gates lifted for nexus-s3dd4.3 (Java telemetry endpoints) and .4 (inner diff+fill, existing surfaces).

title: ingest-cloud async job semantics: POST returns job id, GET polls status — kill the fire-and-absorb-504 hack
description:
2026-07-01 production run of RDR-176 P4's /v1/migration/ingest-cloud at corpus scale (52 collections, 123,883 chunks): every collection over ~6k chunks (server-side copy >~60s at ~105 chunks/s) 504s at the nginx edge while the engine copy continues DETACHED — no completion signal, no progress, no error channel. The operator hack: fire, absorb the 504, poll dest counts until parity (idempotent on chash). That hack must not be the contract.

DESIGN (engine-side):
- POST /v1/migration/ingest-cloud returns 202 + {job_id} immediately (validate creds + collection existence synchronously first so a bad request still fails fast with 4xx).
- Engine runs the copy on a bounded executor (1-2 concurrent jobs; queue the rest — tonight had 3 detached copies stacking with zero visibility or admission control).
- GET /v1/migration/jobs/{job_id} -> {state: queued|running|done|failed, per_collection: {name: {copied, dest_count, expected}}, started_at, finished_at, error}.
- Jobs table in PG (tenant-scoped, RLS) so status survives engine restart and doctor/stats can surface orphaned jobs (feeds RDR-177 observability).
- Idempotency: re-POSTing the same collection set while a job is running returns the EXISTING job id, not a second copy.

CLIENT-side (nx storage migrate vectors --cloud delegation, pairs with the delegate bead):
- POST, then poll with progress rendering (the RDR-176 Gap 5 per-store progress UX, applied to vector jobs).
- Synchronous small-batch fast path can remain for <60s jobs if the engine reports both modes.

Also covers: the 5-chunk gate (ingest_cloud_gate.py) must grow a big-collection variant so the timeout class can never re-ship unnoticed.
close_reason: Shipped on develop (cherry-pick 1bd7234f, pushed after composed full Java suite 987/987 green with the chash batch change). POST /v1/migration/ingest-cloud now async-default: sync validation -> 202+job_id -> bounded 2-worker pool; GET /v1/migration/jobs/{id} tenant-scoped status; nexus.migration_jobs table with RLS + partial-unique dedup index (tenant, collections_key) WHERE state IN (queued,running) = idempotent re-POST; {sync:true} preserves the RDR-176 P4 contract byte-for-byte. CREDENTIAL NON-PERSISTENCE ENFORCED: no cred columns, pinned by migrationJobsTable_hasNoCredentialColumns scanning information_schema. Documented deviations: expected==copied for now; async requires explicit collections list (full-footprint stays sync). Also correctly bumped the jOOQ record-count guard 50->51. Reaches cloud on the next engine cut (wave 3).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: GATE-CRITIQUE CONSTRAINT (2026-07-02, SIGNIFICANT): the persistent jobs table MUST NOT persist ChromaCloud credentials. RDR-176's decision — client-supplied ephemeral creds, never persisted, never logged — is TEST-ENFORCED; the jobs table (which exists precisely to survive engine restarts) would silently violate it if source_api_key/tenant/database ride the job row. Design: creds live only in the in-memory job context; the PG row carries job_id/state/collections/counts/timestamps/error. EXTEND the existing RDR-176 non-persistence test to assert the jobs-table schema has no credential columns and no serialized-cred payloads.

title: incident path bypassed the EXISTING 502 retry — root-cause the bypass + add circuit breaker (was: retry does not cover 502)
description: 2026-07-01 live migration: two concurrent chash imports overloaded the ingress; nginx returned 502 for ~10s. The RDR-176 bounded transient-edge retry did NOT retry them — every batch in flight during the window failed permanently (11 batches in one leg, ~10 in the other; catalog manifest lost 270 rows in the same window), and the ETL burned through failing batches at ~3/second with no backoff. 502/503/504 from the ingress are the CANONICAL transient class and must be retried with exponential backoff + a circuit-breaker pause (e.g. 3 consecutive 5xx = pause 30s before resuming). Idempotent re-runs recovered everything, but a user running migrate-all once would silently end up with holes + a failed report.
close_reason: Harvested w1-retry agent commit 45b227a4, cherry-picked to develop as 11bc4a3e. Root cause was two-fold: (1) _RETRYABLE_ETL_HTTP_STATUSES was {403} only — 429/502/503/504 raised on first attempt despite call sites being correctly wired through _etl_with_retry; (2) catalog_etl document_chunks /import/chunk loop called client._post directly (genuine bypass, the 270-row manifest loss). Fix: expanded status set + EtlCircuitBreaker (3 consecutive exhausted cycles = 30s pause, 20-trip give-up) routed through every batch-import call site across all 8 ETL modules. Tests: 389 etl/retry green, 1245 migration+db green, incl. httpx.MockTransport 502-burst regression asserting zero permanently-failed batches.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: PLAN-AUDIT CORRECTION (2026-07-01, verified vs codebase): the original premise is STALE — _etl_with_retry ALREADY covers 429/502/503/504 across the ETL call sites (RDR-176 P5 Gap 6). Yet the 2026-07-01 incident showed chash import batches failing PERMANENTLY at ~3/s on 502 with no backoff (chash_etl_batch_error events, batch_start 173k-230k ranges, ~21 batches lost across two legs + 270 catalog manifest rows). RE-SCOPED WORK: (1) root-cause WHY the incident path bypassed the existing retry — candidate: chash_etl / catalog_etl batch loops call the HTTP client directly instead of through _etl_with_retry, or the retry wrapper excludes the import/import_batch endpoints; (2) route every batch-import call site through the retry ladder; (3) add the circuit-breaker pause (N consecutive 5xx = pause before resuming) so a sustained outage doesn't burn the retry budget at 3 batches/s; (4) regression test: a fake 502-burst server must yield zero permanently-failed batches.

title: post-migration SQLite divergence tripwire — local T2 accepted 68 writes after its stores were migrated to the cloud, silently
description: After the Jun-30 cloud migration, local SQLite memory.db kept receiving writes (68 rows by Jul-1) from old-venv MCP daemons while the cloud copy froze — three diverging memory stores with no warning anywhere. Fix: once a migration report records a cloud target for a store, subsequent local-SQLite writes to that store should warn loudly (write-path check or doctor check comparing memory.db max(timestamp) vs the migration report completed_at). The immutable-source rule (RDR-176 P1) covers service-mode reads; this is the write-side hole for clients still resolving the OLD backend.

Fixed-width UTC timestamp comparison. LIVE finding: per-store reports record target '(lease)' even when resolved to the cloud — report-writer follow-up on the epic.

title: Engine /v1/catalog/list ignores file_path when owner is set (GH #1350 Fix B)
description: Server-side root cause of GH #1350. CatalogHandler.handleList (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/CatalogHandler.java:262-265) branches: if owner is present it calls repo.documentsByOwner(tenant, owner) and DROPS the file_path param; only the else-if (no owner) branch calls documentsByFilePath (exact eq, F_DOC_FPATH.eq). Fix: when BOTH owner and file_path are set, filter by both (add a documentsByOwnerAndFilePath, or apply the file_path predicate to the owner query). Client-side Fix A (nexus-h9f1w) already stops the corruption on develop; this is the proper server fix. Verified register stores file_path VERBATIM (CatalogRepository:377,493 — no normalization), so exact-match is correct on both sides. Engine change -> engine-service cut + cloud deploy relay. Add a Java handler test: owner+file_path returns 0 for a new path, 1 for an existing one.
close_reason: Fix B merged to develop via PR #1354 (merge 40ee7c1f). CatalogHandler.handleList now dispatches to documentsByOwnerAndFilePath when both owner+file_path present; register stores file_path verbatim so exact match is correct both sides. Java repo test non-vacuous (owner+file_path returns exactly the match, 0 for a new path). Reaches cloud on next engine-service cut+deploy.

title: nexus DEVONthink bridge broken: is_running probe fails with opaque ExceptionGroup, nx dt Layer B/F silently no-op (GH #1351)
description: GitHub: Hellblazer/nexus#1351. nexus.mcp_client.devonthink probe of the upstream DT MCP server fails with 'ExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)' on is_running, so nx dt --link-semantic/--writeback silently no-op (0 linked, 0 written back). DEVONthink is healthy (direct MCP client is_running -> running:true; find_similar/tag/annotate all work), so the fault is nexus's proxy connection. Core defect: both handlers stringify the ExceptionGroup without unwrapping (mcp_client/devonthink.py:92, mcp/devonthink.py:125) so the real sub-exception is never logged. title: No supported downgrade + 6.0.0 mutates the local SQLite it treats as a migration SOURCE
description:
Two coupled deficits surfaced in Hal's 6.0.0 dogfood (2026-06-29):

(A) NO FIRST-CLASS DOWNGRADE. There is no 'nx downgrade' and no test that an older CLI can read a newer-stamped DB. Rollback 6.0.0→5.10.6 'works' ONLY incidentally because migrations.py is additive (ADD COLUMN DEFAULT / CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) and _nexus_version is advisory. That is luck, not design. Especially fraught for the 6.0.0 Chroma→pgvector cutover: a user who completed migration has no supported way back.

(B) 6.0.0 MUTATES THE LOCAL SQLITE THAT MIGRATION TREATS AS 'COPY-NOT-MOVE' SOURCE. Opening the local T2 DBs with 6.0.0 ran migrations.py → stamped _nexus_version=6.0.0 (confirmed in memory.db) and may have applied additive schema migrations. The vector migration is copy-not-move (Chroma untouched), but the T2 SQLite source is NOT immutable — the CLI alters it on open. A migration source should be read-only; mutating it undermines the rollback guarantee and the 'your source is safe' promise.

REQUIREMENTS (design/RDR — rollback is a cross-cutting release-lifecycle capability):
1. A SUPPORTED, TESTED downgrade path (or an explicit, documented 'no downgrade — restore from backup' contract with a pre-upgrade auto-backup the CLI takes).
2. Treat the local SQLite as IMMUTABLE during migration: open read-only for ETL source reads; never run migrations/stamp on a DB being used purely as a migration source. If a version stamp is needed, write it elsewhere.
3. Pre-upgrade auto-backup of ~/.config/nexus (DBs + config) as a first-class safety net, with a one-command restore.
4. Test: older-CLI-reads-newer-DB compatibility (or fail-loud-with-remedy if intentionally unsupported); and 'migration source DB byte-unchanged after a dry-run + after a real run'.

Origin: Hal 2026-06-29 ('we'd better have a downgrade … please tell me you do NOT modify the local sqlite for 6.0.0' — we do). Relates to the two-release deprecation window (forward-only today), nexus-1qpni (batching), nexus-icucl (cutover).
notes: ROOT CAUSE + FIX PROVEN (RDR-176 research-2, 2026-06-30). The stamp source is NOT the ETL (?mode=ro) — it's the T2 daemon launched UNCONDITIONALLY by mcp/_first_run.py:176-181 on every nx-mcp boot, NO backend check → T2Database(run_migrations=True) (t2_daemon.py:943) → apply_pending → UPDATE _nexus_version='6.0.0' (migrations.py:2976); same daemon opens .catalog.db rw+DDL (t2_daemon.py:1471). Also nx upgrade (upgrade.py:283-412) + nx doctor WAL-pragma writes (doctor.py:67/535/2060). FIX (5; #1+#3 sufficient): (1) _first_run.py skip daemon when backend==SERVICE; (2) t2_daemon._build_hosted_catalog→HttpCatalogClient in svc mode; (3) bootstrap_schema skip migration block in svc mode; (4) upgrade.py svc-mode guard; (5) doctor.py ?mode=ro. Verify: byte-identical-before/after across upgrade+full migration.
close_reason: Closed

title: T2 ETLs import PER-ROW (memory, taxonomy topic_assignments 190k, topics, plans) — pathological + fragile over a remote/cloud service
description:
Hal prod cloud cutover 2026-06-29: 'nx storage migrate all' crawls with spiky 5-40KB/s upload. Root cause: the T2 ETLs issue ONE HTTP round-trip per row.
- memory_etl: HttpMemoryStore.import_entry() per row (3,544 rows).
- taxonomy_etl: HttpTaxonomyStore.import_assignment() PER ROW — topic_assignments = 190,112 rows => 190k sequential round-trips. At cloud RTT ~100-300ms that is ~5-16 HOURS for taxonomy alone, and every call is exposed to the intermittent edge/WAF 403 already observed (644k+ total per-row calls across stores = many stochastic failures).
- topics(447), plans(114) also per-row.
- COUNTEREXAMPLE done right: chash_etl batches at _IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE=200 (448,434 rows survivable); vector ETL batches 300/upsert. T2 should match.

Per-row was fine when P5 ran against LOCALHOST (sub-ms RTT). It is unfit for the managed/cloud target — which is now the supported path (RDR-166). 

FIX: batch the T2 imports. Add bulk import endpoints (or batched payloads) for memory/taxonomy(topics+assignments)/plans/telemetry mirroring chash's batch loop + the vector ETL's 300-record batching. Reuse one keep-alive connection (the CLOSE_WAIT churn seen per-row suggests no connection reuse). Target: taxonomy 190k in minutes, not hours; bounded WAF exposure (1 call per 200-300 rows, not per row).
ALSO: combine with retry (nexus vector-403 bead) so a batch that hits a transient edge 403 retries instead of failing the row.
Origin: prod cutover 2026-06-29. Related: nexus-icucl, nexus-tteq8 (progress/metrics), nexus-zvcou (split-brain), the vector-403 retry bead.
notes: RESHAPED + scoped (RDR-176 research-2). Not just 'add batching' — right-shape transport. cloud→cloud: ChromaRestClient.cloud()+get/upsert ALREADY EXIST in Java (retired VectorRepository), PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksWithVectors() stores precomputed vectors → server-side ingest ≈ 200 LOC new handler + EgressProxy + cred plumbing. local→managed bulk: chash upsert_many(200) is the template; catalog endpoints already accept arrays (convert per-element loop → jOOQ batch); new import_batch for memory/plans/telemetry/taxonomy via withTenant (GUC once/batch). COPY = optional stretch. Test: transfer count O(1)..O(N/batch), never O(N rows).
close_reason: Closed

title: Unify service token/URL resolution across ALL storage commands — kill the T2/T3 split-brain
description:
T2/T3 are the SAME store served by the SAME service, but the CLI resolves the service endpoint + token INCONSISTENTLY across commands:
- T3: nx storage migrate vectors takes --service-url; token resolution per the managed chain.
- T2: nx storage migrate <store> reads token ONLY from NX_SERVICE_TOKEN env ('token is always read from NX_SERVICE_TOKEN'); nx storage migrate all has NO --service-url at all (uses NX_SERVICE_URL/PORT env).
- Meanwhile normal runtime resolves service_url/service_token from nx config (config.yml) with env override (managed-onboarding doc).

Result (Hal 2026-06-29): a user who correctly ran 'nx config set service_url/service_token' still has to separately export NX_SERVICE_URL + NX_SERVICE_TOKEN to run the T2 migration. Split-brain. 'That's madness — T2/T3 are in the same store and the same service provides both.'

FIX: one resolution chain for ALL storage/migration commands — env (NX_SERVICE_URL/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN) > config.yml (service_url/service_token) — identical to runtime. Add --service-url to 'migrate all'. Read token from the same resolver (not env-only). No command should require env when config is set.
Acceptance: with only 'nx config set service_url/service_token' (no exports), nx storage migrate all + nx storage migrate vectors both authenticate. Tests pin config-only resolution for both T2 and T3 paths.
Related: nexus-icucl (cutover exposed it), managed-onboarding doc, RDR-152/166.
notes: ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (Hal 2026-06-29, explicit): end state = TOKEN IN CONFIG ONLY, NO ENV REQUIRED. With just 'nx config set service_url/service_token' and ZERO exports (no NX_SERVICE_URL, no NX_SERVICE_TOKEN), ALL storage/migration commands authenticate — specifically 'nx storage migrate all' (and every per-store T2 migrate) + 'nx storage migrate vectors'. Until this ships, the bridge is 'export NX_SERVICE_URL/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN=$(nx config get … --show)' sourced from config (single source of truth). Tests pin: config-only (monkeypatched empty env) authenticates both T2 'migrate all' and T3 'migrate vectors'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Install-time bge-768 download: route through self-hosted asset (retire HuggingFace 429 dependency)
description:
src/nexus/db/service_bge_model.py:fetch_service_bge_onnx() provisions the standard fp32 bge-base-en-v1.5 ONNX (~416MB) at install time (nx init --service, guided-upgrade) by streaming from HuggingFace (_HF_RESOLVE = https://huggingface.co/Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5/resolve/main/...). Single origin, NO retry/backoff. HF rate-limits anonymous bulk pulls (HTTP 429), so a user install can fail the same way CI did. The CI half is fixed: a self-hosted GitHub release asset (tag ci-assets-bge-768-v1) now serves model.onnx + tokenizer.json, consumed by .github/actions/prime-bge-onnx with retry + sha256 verify (commit 304d2e00).

SCOPE: make the install path prefer the self-hosted asset:
- Primary source: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/releases/download/ci-assets-bge-768-v1/{model.onnx,tokenizer.json} (public; GITHUB_TOKEN not required). DECIDE: self-hosted-only vs self-hosted-primary-with-HF-fallback (brainstorming-gate).
- Add retry/backoff to _httpx_stream (currently none) — transient 429/5xx.
- Add sha256 verification (file currently has only size floors); reuse the published digests: model.onnx 9bc579acdba21c253c62a9bf866891355a63ffa3442b52c8a37d75b2ccb91848, tokenizer.json d241a60d5e8f04cc1b2b3e9ef7a4921b27bf526d9f6050ab90f9267a1f9e5c66.
- Keep the NX_SERVICE_BGE_DIR operator override + atomic .part rename + fail-loud (RDR-160 invariants).
- Versioning: if the model export ever changes, the asset tag + the CI cache -v suffix + these digests bump together. Document the single-bump contract.
- Cross-check: tests/db/test_service_bge_model.py (path/digest drift guard).

Related: CI fix commit 304d2e00 on develop; release asset ci-assets-bge-768-v1. Origin: Hal 2026-06-29 ('can we download from this location in our installs?').

Rehearsal Dockerfile ARG defaults also flipped to the self-hosted asset - last HF default in the repo retired. Drift-guard tests pin digests+tag to the CI action and the asset base to binary_install. title: Docs: container-integration.md still describes the pre-collapse SQLite-T2-daemon-over-socket model
description: RDR-174 P4.1 follow-up (flagged during the docs sweep). docs/container-integration.md (host-reachability matrix + Prerequisites, ~lines 30-95) is built around reaching the standalone SQLite T2 daemon over a UDS/TCP socket from a container (NX_T2_ADDR / NX_T2_SOCK, nx daemon t2 install). Post-RDR-152/155/174 the default config serves every tier (T2+T3) through the nexus-service over Postgres+pgvector, so the container->host reachability story likely changed (container reaches the service endpoint, not a T2-daemon socket). Rewriting needs the current container->service determination (is the SQLite T2 daemon still the container path, or the service?), which is RDR-158 (retire-SQLite-T2) territory — not a mechanical nx init --service -> nx init swap. Scope: rewrite the reachability matrix + Prerequisites for the service-backed default; keep the SQLite-T2-daemon path as an explicit opt-in. Also revisit docs/desktop-deployment.md:~69 t2 lifecycle ops in the same pass. Verified during sweep: contributing.md dev-setup was corrected (collapsed nx init flow; the unit suite needs no daemon).
notes: Grooming pass (2026-07-12): BUMP P2->P1. Verified RDR-152 (T2->Postgres) has actually landed (15 DONE sub-phase entries in T2 rdr project), so docs/container-integration.md's framing of RDR-152 as a future 'waypoint' is now actively wrong, not just likely-stale -- user-facing setup doc misdescribes current architecture.

Every env var verified against code.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: RESOLVE-ATTEMPT FINDING (2026-06-29): the container-reachability gap is rooted in a hardcoded Java bind. NexusService.java:188 = new InetSocketAddress('127.0.0.1', port), deliberate 'loopback only, no external TLS' (Main.java:40). So a container genuinely cannot reach the host service over TCP. Resolving the docs requires first resolving the ARCH: add an NX_SERVICE_BIND override (Java reads a bind host, default 127.0.0.1; set 0.0.0.0 for container hosting) — which needs (1) a Java-side change in NexusService, (2) Python plumbing to pass it (storage_service_daemon._spawn_service passes only NX_SERVICE_PORT today; probes stay 127.0.0.1), (3) a NEW engine-service release/deploy (two-lifecycle), and (4) a SECURITY decision: exposing an unTLS'd token-authed service beyond loopback. Until then, the SQLite-T2-daemon-over-socket model the doc describes IS the only viable container T2 path (it can bind a container-reachable addr). RECOMMEND: pair the doc rewrite with the NX_SERVICE_BIND engine change as one coordinated arc; do NOT rewrite the docs to 'reach the service' while the service is loopback-only.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: NX_SERVICE_BIND shipped in engine-service-v0.1.11 (deployed 2026-06-29): the Java service binds 127.0.0.1 by default, NX_SERVICE_BIND=0.0.0.0 opt-in for container reachability, loud security warn for non-loopback. This is the REACHABILITY half. REMAINING (keep open): the container still can't DISCOVER the service (dynamic OS-allocated port in the host lease the container can't read; lease host stays loopback by design) — needs a fixed/known-port mechanism + env-pinned NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT/TOKEN, plus the container-integration.md doc rewrite. cli-reference now documents NX_SERVICE_BIND + the necessary-not-sufficient caveat.

title: RDR-174 P2.4: TDD nx init autostart prompt — default yes; --yes accepts; --no-autostart skips; no silent unit write
description:
Approach §4 prompt UX. nx init OFFERS to register the service autostart unit: PROMPT, default YES. --yes accepts non-interactively; --no-autostart skips. NO silent system-unit write under any path.

BEHAVIOR:
- interactive nx init (LOCAL mode): prompts 'register service autostart? [Y/n]', default yes → installs unit (via P2.1-P2.3 path)
- nx init --yes: accepts non-interactively → installs unit
- nx init --no-autostart: skips unit; supervisor still starts for the session (ensure_storage_supervisor)
- MANAGED mode: no autostart prompt (no local supervisor to persist) — verify the prompt is gated to local mode
- never write a system unit without an explicit yes/--yes (consent gate)

TDD — tests FIRST in tests/test_init_cmd.py:
- prompt default-yes installs (mock prompt returning empty/default)
- --yes installs without prompting
- --no-autostart skips install, session supervisor still up
- managed mode: no prompt, no unit
- explicit 'n' at prompt: no unit, session supervisor still up

FILES: src/nexus/commands/init.py (add --no-autostart flag near --yes@609; prompt logic gated to local mode; call the P2.1 install path on yes).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REQUIREMENT FROM RDR-175 (Gap 3, decide-autostart-first). When this builds the nx init autostart prompt, it MUST install decide-first: decide autostart BEFORE starting any supervisor. If yes -> install the unit as the SOLE starter (do NOT also session-start via ensure_storage_supervisor) -> poll the lease for readiness. If no -> ensure_storage_supervisor session detach. Exactly one supervisor in either branch; never start a session supervisor under a unit.

WHY: RDR-175 retired the in-process respawn mechanism. If P2.4 prompts AFTER the unconditional provision_and_start_service session start (the ordering the init.py:523-530 invariant comment sketches), the installed unit's supervisor short-circuits on the session lease, _proc stays unset, heartbeat returns falsey, and the unit exits 3 -> OS restarts it every RestartSec=5s until the session lease expires (bounded coexistence crash-loop; no double-spawn). Decide-first eliminates the coexistence.

Behavior is PINNED by tests/daemon/test_storage_service_daemon.py::TestRdr175MvvSingleSupervisor::test_second_supervisor_under_live_lease_exits_nonzero and documented in RDR-175 §Approach (Gap 3 note) + §Consequences + §Risks. Do NOT add a parallel arbiter — RDR-149 lifecycle gate (test_lifecycle_gate.py) bans a bespoke lock/election outside service_registry.

PROVENANCE: this requirement was briefly mis-marked 'void' during RDR-175 close (a close-time premise error — P2.4 was treated as abandoned rather than planned); corrected 2026-06-28 and recorded here on the bead that owns the prompt.

title: RDR-174 P2.3: supervisor handoff — single-lease integration test + nx-init handoff-poll branch (lean on service_registry; no parallel arbiter)
description:
Approach §4 service-delta (b) (gate-locked, critic SIG-3). The autostart unit OWNS the lifecycle. When nx init installs the unit, it must NOT also leave its own detached ensure_storage_supervisor subprocess racing the unit's RunAtLoad/--now start.

MODEL (a) (RDR-locked): on install, the unit is the single starter; nx init POLLS for the lease to appear (service_registry lease) rather than spawning a second supervisor. Define + implement the single-writer/lease cleanup if both ever race (the RDR-149 service_registry election should already arbitrate; verify and lean on it, do not add a parallel arbiter). One lease after install — assert it.

INTEGRATION WITH nx init: this is where P1.3 (local provision) meets P2.1 autostart. When LOCAL init runs AND autostart is being installed, the install path must hand off — provision PG + binary + embedder, install the unit, let the unit start the supervisor, poll for lease. When autostart is declined/skipped, nx init keeps the existing ensure_storage_supervisor session-start (no unit, supervisor for the session only).

TDD — tests FIRST in tests/test_init_cmd.py + tests/test_daemon_cmd.py:
- after install-with-autostart there is exactly ONE lease (no double-supervisor) — assert count == 1
- nx init polls for lease appearance rather than spawning a second supervisor (assert ensure_storage_supervisor NOT directly spawned by init when the unit owns start; mock the unit start to publish a lease, assert init observes it)
- autostart-skipped path: nx init falls back to session ensure_storage_supervisor (existing behavior preserved)

Use find_referencing_symbols on ensure_storage_supervisor (daemon.py:1495) before changing call sites.

Its premise (autostart unit owns lifecycle; nx init must not double-spawn a second supervisor; poll for lease) is INDEPENDENT of the PG-ordering finding, BUT P2.1's substantive-critic already established (OBS-2) that ensure_storage_supervisor is LEASE-GATED via service_registry (RDR-149 TTL/election) → no double-spawn TODAY: if the unit's RunAtLoad start publishes a lease, a subsequent ensure_storage_supervisor discovers it and exits. title: RDR-174 P2.2: PG boot-ordering is a VERIFIED NO-OP — supervisor self-manages PG; add boot-robustness regression test (no After=/no wrapper)
description:
Approach §4 service-delta (a) (gate-locked, critic SIG-2). The supervisor connects to local Postgres, so the autostart unit must wait for PG — t2/t3 only declare After=network.target; the service unit DIVERGES.

LINUX (nexus-service.service): add After=postgresql.service AND Wants=postgresql.service (or the actual local PG unit name — verify what _provision_postgres_step provisions; PG may be a bundled cluster, not the distro postgresql.service. If bundled, the ordering target differs — resolve the correct unit/socket dependency).
MACOS (com.nexus.service.plist): launchd has NO ordering. The plist must exec a THIN WRAPPER that polls PG readiness (e.g. pg_isready / socket probe) before launching the supervisor. This avoids Restart/KeepAlive thrash on cold boot. Add the wrapper script (or an 'nx daemon service start --wait-for-pg' flag the wrapper invokes — prefer a flag on the existing command over a loose shell script if it fits the contract). Decide via sequentialthinking; document the choice on the bead.

TDD — tests FIRST in tests/test_daemon_cmd.py:
- rendered Linux unit contains After=postgresql.service (or resolved PG unit) + Wants=
- rendered macOS plist execs the PG-readiness wrapper (not the supervisor directly)
- wrapper/flag polls PG before exec (unit test the readiness-poll path with a mocked PG socket; port=0 / no hardcoded ports)

FILES: src/nexus/_resources/daemon/nexus-service.service + com.nexus.service.plist; installer.py _render_for_service (template vars for the ordering/wrapper); possibly a new wrapper resource or a --wait-for-pg flag in daemon.py service start.
VERIFY FIRST: read _provision_postgres_step to learn the actual PG unit/socket identity — do not assume distro postgresql.service.
TEST CMD: uv run pytest tests/test_daemon_cmd.py -x -q
notes:
PAUSED pending RDR-174 §Approach §4 design revisit (Hal decision 2026-06-28). FINDING (evidence-backed, file:line): the gate-locked premise (critic SIG-2: 'supervisor connects to local PG, so the autostart unit must wait for PG') does NOT match the architecture. The storage supervisor SELF-MANAGES an nx-owned PG cluster:
- storage_service_daemon.py:823 _start_locked → 856 _ensure_pg_running → 886 _start_cluster(discover_pg_binaries(), pgdata=creds[PG_DATA], port). The supervisor starts PG ITSELF as step 1 of startup, before the engine.
- pg_provision.py:165 discover_pg_binaries boot-safe order: NEXUS_PG_BIN env → extracted bundle under CONFIG DIR (RDR-157, comment lines 196-200 explicitly: 'so the storage-service daemon's PG-restart path _ensure_pg_running discovers the bundle') → candidate dirs → PATH initdb. Config-dir bundle path works at cold boot WITHOUT the provisioning-time env.
- Even 'host binaries' mode locates only BINARIES; the cluster started is nx's own PG_DATA/port, never the distro postgresql.service cluster.
CONCLUSION: no external postgresql.service/socket to order against in ANY mode. Linux After=postgresql.service would order against a unit that doesn't manage nx's cluster (and Wants= fails on hosts w/o distro PG). macOS PG-readiness wrapper would poll a PG nothing external starts — pointless; _ensure_pg_running IS the in-process readiness+start. Only real boot need = After=network.target (already in template; even that is generous for 127.0.0.1 loopback).
SO §4 service-delta (a) PG-ordering is a NO-OP for this design. The bead delegated 'resolve the correct unit/socket dependency; document the choice' — resolved dependency is NONE. NOT implementing After=/wrapper (would be wrong). Revisit §4 to either (i) close (a) as verified-no-op with a boot-robustness test, or (ii) re-scope to a real gap if one exists. See T2 nexus/rdr-174-p2-section4-finding.
close_reason: Closed

LOCKED DECISION (Candidate A): a LEASED aspect-worker daemon on the EXISTING RDR-149 service-registry substrate (src/nexus/daemon/service_registry.py) — NOT a new bespoke daemon class; one more leased tier mirroring the T2/T3 daemon. It owns (1) the extraction loop (HttpAspectQueue.claim_batch -> extract_aspects via claude -p -> upsert document_aspects -> mark_done) and (2) a reclaim_stale loop. The enqueue hook (aspect_worker.py:1216) stops spawning an in-process daemon thread and instead ensures-the-leased-daemon-is-up (spawn-if-absent via single-flight election).

Per-host would need BYPASSRLS (a per-host daemon claiming across tenants queries without nexus.tenant GUC -> RLS safe-default returns zero rows; BYPASSRLS is prohibited by RDR-152 for the service role). Per-tenant (one daemon per active tenant, each with its tenant's GUC) is the only RLS-compatible scope. v1 single default tenant => practical difference nil, but the constraint governs every later tenant.

title: RDR-173 P2.2 (CRITICAL): Establish + TEST the spawn-as-child inherited-env credential model; forbid credential-bare spawn paths
description:
Approach item 2, credential context — the load-bearing Critical from the gate. UNLIKE the T1/T2/T3 daemons (no LLM creds), the aspect-worker daemon issues claude -p (extract_aspects) and needs the claude binary on PATH, ~/.claude config dir, and the Anthropic credential context.

LOCKED DECISION: the daemon is spawned AS A CHILD of the process that first triggers the enqueue (MCP server / CLI store process via the single-flight election), so it INHERITS that process's environment — the same context those store paths already use to run claude -p. This is the ONLY permitted spawn model. A daemon started from a credential-bare context (e.g. a hypothetical 'nx daemon aspect start' with no inherited env) MUST NOT be a spawn path unless credentials are explicitly plumbed.

Do:
1. Implement the spawn so the child process inherits the parent env (PATH, HOME/claude config, Anthropic creds) — verify the inherited-env contract at the spawn site.
2. Add a GUARD: any credential-bare spawn entrypoint either refuses to start (loud) or requires explicit credential plumbing. No silent credential-bare daemon.
3. TEST (relay-mandated explicit test): assert the spawned daemon inherits the credential env from its parent; assert a credential-bare spawn path is rejected/guarded; assert (where feasible in isolation) that extract_aspects in the child can locate the claude binary. Integration-style — verify the real env handoff, do not mock the env.

This is a hard prerequisite so the spawn entrypoint is designed for inherited-env, not discovered after auth failures. Depends on P1-GATE; pairs with P2.1. Use mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking for the env-inheritance threat model.
