title: Service-mode aspect worker has no persistent host — short-lived store paths enqueue aspects that never extract
description:
CONFIRMED MECHANISM (distinct from the claim_batch fix nexus-575kd): ensure_worker_started() is called from exactly ONE place — the enqueue hook (aspect_worker.py:1216, inside aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook). There is NO persistent worker host: the T2 daemon only runs reclaim_stale ('aspect_worker.py deliberately stopped after we61e', t2_daemon.py:757), and nothing in mcp_infra / mcp / daemon / the Java service calls ensure_worker_started. The extraction worker is a daemon THREAD in whatever process fired the enqueue, and dies when that process exits.

IMPACT (service mode): aspect extraction completes ONLY if a single persistent process (an interactive Claude Code MCP session) stays alive long enough to claim + extract EVERY enqueued row (~25s/doc, haiku). Short-lived store paths — one-shot 'claude -p', CLI 'nx store put', scripts, fast batch ingest — enqueue rows that never extract -> document_aspects silently never populates for those paths. The --fullstack P2.5 run is a faithful repro: post claim_batch fix, the worker claimed 1 of 4 then died with the one-shot claude -p mid-extraction (pending=3, document_aspects=0).

EVIDENCE: --fullstack with the claim_batch fix: enqueued=4, pending=3 (1 claimed, claim_batch WORKS now), document_aspects=0 (worker killed before extraction completed). Pre-fix was pending=4 (claim_batch was the prior blocker; that is fixed).

OPEN QUESTIONS to scope the fix: (1) does service mode even have a reclaim_stale loop (the SQLite T2 daemon is retired in service mode)? If not, stranded in_progress rows never recover. (2) where SHOULD the service-mode worker run — a persistent worker daemon, Java-service-hosted extraction, or an explicit post-ingest 'nx aspects drain' that works against the SERVICE queue (current drain_worker is local-sqlite only, useless in service mode)? Likely RDR-worthy (architectural: aspect-worker hosting in the post-RDR-152 service topology).

BLOCKS: RDR-172 P2.5 (nexus-8zog5) green + epic close. The claim_batch fix (nexus-575kd, commit 5f560e64) is independent + ready to ship.
close_reason: Fixed by RDR-173 leased aspect-worker daemon (epic nexus-o2c42). The enqueue hook now ensures a leased daemon is up (spawn-if-absent, single-flight) on the RDR-149 service-registry substrate, owning the extraction loop + reclaim_stale — extraction no longer depends on the storing process's lifetime (RF-4). P7 --fullstack proved document_aspects=4 end-to-end against the deployed engine (v0.1.14 cloud).

A worker killed mid-extraction (the --fullstack repro: 1 row stuck in_progress) would never be reclaimed -> blocks is_drained() and the drain-before-migration gate. title: Service-mode claim_batch HTTP contract mismatch — worker never claims, ALL service-mode aspect extraction is dead
description:
RDR-172 P2.5 --fullstack run (engine-service-v0.1.10, 2026-06-28) HARD-FAILED on the P2.2 positive assertion: store_put x4 enqueued 4 rows (all status=pending), enqueue-failure tripwire GREEN (0 swallowed), but document_aspects=0 — the worker never claimed/drained the queue before nx-mcp teardown.

DIAGNOSIS: the enqueue path is healthy (RDR-172 fix confirmed: correct doc_id identity, 0 swallowed failures, rows durably pending). The failure is the DRAIN half: the lazy-spawned daemon worker thread did not extract before the process exited.

KEY UNRESOLVED QUESTION (do NOT assume production-bug without verifying): the --fullstack harness drives the workload via ONE-SHOT 'claude -p', which tears down nx-mcp immediately on completion — so the daemon worker (poll 2s, ~25s/doc extraction) cannot finish in-session. A REAL Claude Code session runs a PERSISTENT nexus MCP server where the worker would have time to drain. So this may be a HARNESS-MODEL artifact, not a production defect. Two paths to resolve:
  (a) Verify whether a persistent MCP server drains store_put aspects in service mode (if yes -> harness fix: the --fullstack should drain the queue explicitly or keep the MCP alive / poll longer; the P2.2 assertion's in-session-drain assumption is wrong for the one-shot model).
  (b) If even a persistent server doesn't drain in service mode -> a real worker-lifecycle bug (the lazy-spawn / daemon-thread model doesn't fit the service-mode MCP).

This is the exact worker-lifecycle gap the P2.2 substantive-critic flagged; the hard-fail surfaced it loudly (its purpose). Distinct from the RDR-172 enqueue fix (which works). Blocks closing P2.5 (nexus-8zog5) + the RDR-172 epic until triaged. Evidence: T2 nexus/6.0.0-fullstack-findings + the run log.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (corrects the earlier 'one-shot lifecycle artifact' framing — that was WRONG).

claim_batch HTTP response-envelope contract mismatch:
- Java handleQueueClaimBatch (AspectHandler.java ~line 207): HttpUtil.send(ex, 200, MAPPER.writeValueAsString(rows)) -> sends a BARE JSON ARRAY [ {...}, {...} ].
- Python HttpAspectQueue.claim_batch (http_aspect_queue.py:175-180): r = self._post('/claim_batch', ...); rows = r.get('rows', []) -> expects an OBJECT {"rows": [...]}.
- _post returns resp.json() verbatim, so r is a list; r.get('rows', []) raises AttributeError (or yields empty) EVERY poll.

The aspect WORKER polls via claim_batch (aspect_worker.py:349-352). So in service mode it claims NOTHING every poll -> document_aspects never populates. NOT a one-shot/persistence issue: ALL service-mode aspect extraction is dead, every session. Cloud v0.1.10 ships this — the aspect/enrichment pipeline is non-functional in service mode RIGHT NOW (STEP-6 gate doesn't exercise extraction, so it passed).

The only claim_batch tests (test_rename_lock_t1_2.py) are LOCAL sqlite, never HTTP. Zero HTTP coverage on claim_batch.

(A) Java side: wrap as {"rows": rows} (consistent with claim_next's envelope) -> requires a NEW engine-service cut + cloud deploy.
(B) Python client: accept the bare array (rows = r if isinstance(r,list) else r.get('rows',[])) -> ships in the Python release, NO engine cut; works against the already-deployed v0.1.10.

title: T1 scratch: chroma store under macOS $TMPDIR gets reaped (SQLITE_CANTOPEN) + no session-end GC of elect/addr/daemons
description:
## Symptom
T1 scratch (scratch_put / scratch action='put') fails with: `Database error: error returned from database: (code: 14) unable to open database file` (SQLITE_CANTOPEN). T2 (memory.db in ~/.config/nexus) is unaffected — only T1 fails. Observed in conexus/nexus 5.10.6 on macOS (M4 Max), 2026-06-27.

## Root cause (two layered bugs)

### 1. Fragile storage location (the CANTOPEN)
T1 is a per-session ChromaDB daemon: `chroma run --path $DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR/nx_t1_<rand>`. That temp base (`/var/folders/.../T/`) is actively reaped by macOS (idle-file purge ~3d + boot clear). Long-lived T1 daemons lose their backing `chroma.sqlite3` out from under them → every open fails CANTOPEN. Evidence: of 13 nx_t1_* temp dirs, only 3 still contained chroma.sqlite3; the rest were empty shells while their daemons were still registered as 'live'. T2 dodges this precisely because memory.db lives in ~/.config/nexus (not OS-temp).

### 2. No lifecycle GC (the pileup)
Session end never removes t1_elect.<sid>.lock / t1_addr.<sid> nor kills the per-session chroma daemon, and there is no startup sweep of dead-pid holders. Evidence (single machine): 353 elect locks dating to Jun 5, 14 addr files (4 marked status:'live' with DEAD claude_pid+server_pid), 9 orphan chroma daemons. Manual scoped cleanup (preserving the 6 genuinely-live sessions) removed 347 locks + 8 orphan addrs + 8 empty temp dirs + 1 orphan daemon.

### 3. In-process client doesn't re-elect mid-session
The MCP server establishes its T1 client (election + chroma endpoint) once at session start. Clearing on-disk cruft does NOT recover an active session — it holds a failed handle until the MCP server restarts (/clear or new session). Recovery should not require a restart.

## Proposed fix
1. Relocate the T1 chroma store out of OS-temp → e.g. ~/.config/nexus/t1/<session>/ (or mark the temp dir do-not-reap). Removes the reaping class entirely.
2. Recreate-on-CANTOPEN: if the store path is missing/unopenable, re-init it instead of bubbling a raw DB error.
3. Lifecycle GC: on session end remove that session's elect/addr + terminate its chroma daemon; on startup sweep dead-pid (claude_pid AND server_pid not alive) elect/addr/daemons.
4. (Nice-to-have) mid-session re-election or a clearer surfaced error so an active session can self-heal without restart.

## Repro
Leave several Claude sessions' nexus MCP servers idle across a macOS temp-reap window (or reboot), then call scratch_put in a session whose nx_t1 temp dir was reaped → CANTOPEN.

## Notes
- Surfaced during qwen-coprocessor-stack RDR-012 work (T1 used as planning-chain convenience bus). No data lost — plan/findings/beads went to T2/bd.
- Diagnostic + scoped-cleanup script logic available on request (liveness-checks every pid; never touches a holder with both claude_pid and server_pid alive).
close_reason: Merged in PR #1346. T1 scratch store relocated out of macOS $TMPDIR (CANTOPEN fix) + lifecycle GC (dead-pid t1_addr + t1_elect sweeps wired at startup, session-end relinquish cleanup) + clearer no-reconnect error. Stacked review complete; full suite 11459 green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DISCOVERED by the full-stack isolated shakeout (migration-rehearsal --fullstack, 2026-06-27): a real claude session driving the nexus MCP against the live 6.0.0 PG service.

OBSERVED: MCP store_put of a knowledge note (collection 'knowledge' → materialized knowledge__knowledge__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1) in SERVICE mode produces NO aspect activity: nexus.aspect_extraction_queue total=0, nexus.document_aspects=0 (queried tenant='default', the store's tenant). The store itself SUCCEEDS (collection materialized, search + nx_answer work).

EXPECTED (per code + RDR-089): store_put SHOULD enqueue aspects. Evidence it should:
- store_put fires the document-grain hook chain: src/nexus/mcp/core.py ~L2068 .
- the aspect-extraction enqueue hook IS registered on that chain: src/nexus/hook_registry.py ~L346-348 register_document(aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook).
- knowledge__* IS extractor-eligible: src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py select_config → scholarly-paper-v1 (so the hook does NOT early-return at the "no extractor" gate).
- enqueue is service-aware: t2.aspect_queue → HttpAspectQueue when NX_STORAGE_BACKEND[_ASPECT_QUEUE]=service (RDR-152 gmiaf.15).

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: the enqueue hook is BEST-EFFORT (src/nexus/aspect_worker.py aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook wraps the enqueue in try/except → log.warning 'aspect_extraction_enqueue_failed', non-fatal). In service mode the enqueue throws and is SWALLOWED. Most likely the aspect_extraction_queue→catalog_collections FK (aspect_extraction_queue_collection_fk, confirmed enforced by the --stress leg) fires at store-time BEFORE the collection is registered in catalog_collections, OR HttpAspectQueue.enqueue errors. Either way the user sees a clean store and never gets aspects.

IMPACT: knowledge added via the MCP store_put path (a primary path) never gets RDR-089 structured aspects in service mode (6.0.0). Silent (best-effort swallow) — green tests, dormant feature. The indexing path (nx index, doc_indexer install_default_hooks) is a separate path and NOT confirmed here either.

NEXT STEPS:
1. Capture the swallowed warning: re-run --fullstack with the claude/nx-mcp stderr surfaced (or NX log capture) to confirm 'aspect_extraction_enqueue_failed' + the exact exception (FK? Http error? ordering?).
2. Fix: ensure the collection/doc is registered before enqueue (ordering), or make the enqueue tolerate/await registration; consider making the swallow LOUD in CI (a tripwire) per feedback_no_silent_fallbacks_for_correctness.
3. Verify the INDEXING path (nx index of knowledge__/rdr__ content) end-to-end in service mode too (enqueue→worker→document_aspects); the worker lazy-spawns on enqueue + one-shot nx index may die before draining (worker-lifecycle question).

RELATED: RDR-089 (aspects at ingest), RDR-152 gmiaf.15 (aspect_queue service seam), RDR-163 (backoff ladder), RDR-129 (worker persist via daemon). Coverage map: T2 nexus/6.0.0-plugin-surface-coverage-gap [4733], nexus/6.0.0-fullstack-findings [4734]. Repro: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --fullstack.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE NARROWING (static, 2026-06-27): the enqueue path is CORRECTLY service-wired — NOT a local-vs-service misroute:
- t2_index_write (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py) SHORT-CIRCUITS to a direct service-backed T2Database in service mode (RDR-152 nexus-fjwxh), so t2.aspect_queue = HttpAspectQueue.
- storage_backend_for (src/nexus/db/storage_mode.py) HARD-DEFAULTS to 'service' (precedence: per-store env → NX_STORAGE_BACKEND → default service); aspect_queue + document_aspects both resolve to service.
- The Java service DOES implement POST /v1/aspects/queue/enqueue (AspectHandler.java, RDR-152 gmiaf.15).
So the wiring exists end-to-end. The enqueue therefore reaches HttpAspectQueue._post('/enqueue') and THROWS, swallowed by the hook's best-effort try/except → log.warning aspect_extraction_enqueue_failed. PRIME SUSPECT: the aspect_extraction_queue→catalog_collections FK fires before store_put has registered the collection in catalog_collections (hook order in core.py: fire_single → fire_batch → fire_document(enqueue); if collection registration is not committed before fire_document, the /enqueue insert FK-violates). Secondary: a /enqueue endpoint error (doc_id/content_hash/tenant).
CONFIRM NEXT (definitive): in the --fullstack container, run a direct python repro of aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook with logging.basicConfig(DEBUG) against the materialized knowledge collection → the swallowed exc_info traceback names the exact exception (FK vs HTTP vs other).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (dynamic capture, 2026-06-27, --fullstack container, direct no-swallow probe):

The enqueue reaches the service and the JAVA SERVICE RETURNS HTTP 500 on POST /v1/aspects/queue/enqueue:
  httpx.HTTPStatusError: Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url '…/v1/aspects/queue/enqueue'
  (probe stack: mcp_infra.t2_index_write → http_aspect_queue.enqueue → _post → raise_for_status)

MECHANISM (server-side, unhandled SQLException → 500):
- store_put fires the aspect hook with a NON-EMPTY doc_id: core.py:2068 `_hooks.fire_document(doc_id, col_name, content, doc_id=doc_id)`. `doc_id` at that point = the `t3.put(...)` return (chunk/content identity), DISTINCT from `catalog_doc_id` (the catalog tumbler returned by catalog_store_hook and passed to fire_batch).
- RDR-156 fk-001 (nexus-b7v6i) adds a composite FK `aspect_extraction_queue.doc_id → catalog_documents` ("non-NULL values are checked against the parent table"; '' is pre-flight-coerced to NULL).
- The enqueue's non-empty doc_id is NOT a committed catalog_documents key at enqueue time (tumbler-vs-chunkid mismatch and/or cross-HTTP-txn visibility) → FK violation.
- AspectHandler.java wraps repo.enqueue in `catch (Exception e) → send(500, e.getMessage())` (only IllegalArgumentException → 400). A constraint violation is therefore an unhandled 500, NOT a 4xx.
- The Python enqueue hook (aspect_worker.aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook) is best-effort: `except Exception: log.warning("aspect_extraction_enqueue_failed", exc_info=True)` and returns. The 500 is SWALLOWED.

NET: every service-mode MCP store_put silently skips aspect enqueue → RDR-089 extraction is inert for the store_put path. Zero green tests caught it (the swallow + the 500 both hide it) — same loud-fail-closed class as RDR-142/3lbhb.

Reproduced independently: a direct enqueue with a bogus doc_id ("ov0sw-probe", not in catalog_documents) produces the IDENTICAL 500 — confirms the doc_id FK is the dependent constraint.

FIX (needs an owner decision — likely small RDR; three coordinated parts):
1. SERVER: AspectHandler must map constraint violations (PSQLException SQLSTATE 23xxx) to 4xx, never a bare 500; AND/OR the queue insert should NULL-coerce an unregistered doc_id (mirror the '' → NULL pre-flight contract) so a not-yet-registered doc never hard-fails the enqueue.
2. CLIENT/ORDERING: store_put should enqueue with the REGISTERED catalog id (catalog_doc_id) — or doc_id='' — not the t3.put chunk id; OR guarantee the catalog_documents row is committed+visible before fire_document.
3. LOUDNESS: aspect_extraction_enqueue_failed must be a CI tripwire (fail closed) so a swallowed enqueue can never silently ship again. The --fullstack harness should assert document_aspects > 0 after the workload (currently a documented-gap note).

title: Frozen develop version (5.10.6) leaves T2 migrations dormant — registry already has an introduced=5.10.7 step that cannot fire
description:
## Problem

`apply_pending` (src/nexus/db/migrations.py:2487) runs a migration step only when `last_seen < introduced <= current_version`, where `current_version = expected_t2_schema_version()` is derived from the installed `conexus` package version (pyproject `version`).

develop is pinned at version `5.10.6` and stays there while it is unreleasable (release boundary, luxe6 / project_release_boundary_p4a). Any T2 migration registered on develop with `introduced > 5.10.6` therefore has `introduced <= current(5.10.6)` == False and NEVER runs on a develop build — it is silently dormant.

## Concrete instance (not hypothetical)

The MIGRATIONS registry tail (migrations.py:2197) already contains:
  Migration("5.10.7", "nexus-slcn7: merge duplicate root topics + unique (collection,label) index", migrate_dedup_root_topics)

On develop (version 5.10.6) this step's gate is `5.10.7 <= 5.10.6` = False → it does not apply. The dedup/unique-index it is supposed to enforce is absent on every develop install and on the daemon-owned schema.

## Why it bites later

When the first post-luxe6 release finally bumps the version to >= 5.10.7, ALL such accumulated migrations fire at once on the first DB open / daemon start / `nx upgrade`. Risks:
- A pile-up of long-dormant migrations running together (contention, longer first-open) — the class the RDR-128 t2_migration_flock was built to tame, but never exercised at this batch size.
- A dormant migration whose preconditions assumed it ran near its introduction may find data that drifted in the interim (e.g. duplicate root topics accumulating because the unique index was never created), so the migration that was a no-op at author time becomes a heavy/failing data-repair at release time.
- The schema develop actually runs on diverges silently from what the version string claims.

## Scope / asks

1. Decide the policy: should develop migrations use `introduced` values <= the frozen version so they DO apply on develop, or is dormant-until-release the intended contract? (If the latter, it must be documented and the release path must be hardened for the batch-apply.)
2. Add a CI tripwire: fail if any registry `introduced` exceeds the pyproject version (catches the silent-dormant case at author time), OR explicitly bless the gap with a recorded rationale.
3. Re-validate `migrate_dedup_root_topics` (slcn7) against current develop data before it un-dormants at the next release — duplicate root topics may have accumulated since it was authored.

## Pointers
- src/nexus/db/migrations.py: `apply_pending` (2487), `expected_t2_schema_version` (2345), MIGRATIONS registry (2022), the 5.10.7 entry (2197).
- Release boundary: T2 nexus/release-boundary-since-p4a; auto-memory project_release_boundary_p4a.
- Surfaced during RDR-651 cutover F4 analysis (conexus-jya7), 2026-06-25.
notes: RDR-170 accepted + implemented on feature/nexus-j25po-migration-not-gated-on-version. Drop apply_pending upper bound (lower-bound-only); expected_t2_schema_version()=max(package, version-aware registry max); fixed 3 pending-filter sites (apply_pending/upgrade --dry-run/doctor --check-schema) + upgrade._current_version + bootstrap_schema target + cold-start fast path. slcn7 (5.10.7 dedup root topics) un-dormants; validated on live-db copy (no dup roots, idempotent, partial unique index). Stacked review 0 Critical; all findings addressed (frozen-branch CLI tests added per RDR step 3). Full suite green.

title: Service-mode manifest empty: manifest post-store hook / catalog_doc_id threading does not populate catalog_document_chunks (RDR-168 P4 CA-4 2nd cause)
description:
RDR-168 P4 manifest-empty in service mode. TWO LAYERS:

LAYER 1 (FIXED, commit pending, mcp_infra.manifest_write_batch_hook): the manifest post-store hook silently ABORTED in service mode. Root cause: the read-handle cleanup did getattr(_gate, '_db', None) where _gate is HttpCatalogClient. HttpCatalogClient._db is a PROPERTY that raises RuntimeError in service mode ('catalog._db unavailable in service mode', nexus-xnz0o); getattr's default only swallows AttributeError, NOT RuntimeError → the raise propagated → caught by the hook's outer 'no catalog' except → debug log + return BEFORE the manifest write. Fix: guard the _db access in a try/except (service-mode reader has no SQLite handle; skip the local-only WAL-read-lock cleanup). Verified: the hook now FIRES the write (manifest_write_hook_failed now appears where before there was silence). Local-mode manifest population unaffected (test_code_indexer_doc_id/test_prose_indexer_doc_id still green).

LAYER 2 (OPEN, service-side): after layer 1, atomic_manifest_replace → POST /manifest/write returns 500. repo.writeManifest(tenant, docId, rows) insert fails. The JAR handler swallows the stack (only Liquibase INFO in stderr; no exception trace). Working live manifest tests (TestCatalogSpansManifest) succeed with rows=[{position, chash, line_start, line_end}]; the hook's rows additionally carry chunk_index/char_start/char_end (i() is null-safe, so likely NOT the cause). Candidates: composite FK catalog_document_chunks(tenant_id, doc_id)→catalog_documents(tenant_id, tumbler) under FORCE RLS; a NOT NULL; or a chash format/length issue. NEEDS: instrument the Java CatalogHandler/writeManifest to log the exception (or a debugger), then JAR rebuild + Java test. The MVV test_service_mode_index_populates_manifest is xfail(strict) on this; remove when /manifest/write succeeds.
close_reason: FULLY FIXED (both layers). L1 (commit fb2af99a): manifest hook no longer aborts on the HttpCatalogClient._db RuntimeError (getattr default doesn't swallow it). L2 (commit 2b6c6547): client truncates chash[:32] in manifest writes (was violating catalog_document_chunks_chash_len_check) + get_manifest returns typed ManifestRow (was list[dict] → _prune_misclassified crashed on row.chash). Live MVV GREEN: service-mode nx index repo populates documents + manifest end-to-end. Local-mode unaffected (224 tests green).

title: collection_for service endpoint is lookup-only (404 on new tuple) vs canonical render-v1 — prime CA-4 empty-catalog suspect
description: RDR-168 P3 substantive-critic finding (Significant, CA-4). Canonical _DocumentOps.collection_for RENDERS CollectionName v1 for an unregistered tuple (never None/raise). The service /collections/for_tuple (CatalogHandler.handleCollectionForTuple L777) returns 404 when repo.collectionForTuple is null — lookup-only. HttpCatalogClient.collection_for now raises KeyError on that 404 (type-consistent loud failure, but breaks first-index in service mode). This is very likely THE service-mode empty-catalog root cause (CA-4). FIX (decide with the live P4 MVV): either the service renders v1 like canonical (Java change, preferred — keeps naming authority server-side), OR the client constructs v1 (risks name fragmentation between local/service modes — discouraged). MUST be resolved/validated by the P4 live MVV nexus-pwclh before RDR-168 closes. Do NOT guess client-side v1 construction without the live service.
close_reason: FIXED in P4 (commit da4bc3e8). HttpCatalogClient.collection_for now renders the name with canonical helpers (owner_segment_for_tumbler + CollectionName): v1 for a new tuple (was 404→KeyError, the CA-4 cause), vN existing, vN+1 bump; service used only as version oracle. title: Kill per-search manifest N+1 (x2): add /manifest/get_many + batch-resolve on the service catalog API
description: Singleton (High). _attach_doc_ids_from_catalog batches chash->doc then loops get_manifest() per doc (search_engine.py:153); _attach_display_paths independently loops by_doc_id()->resolve() per doc (search_engine.py:202). Root cause: no /manifest/get_many or batch-resolve on the service catalog API (the inline 'one catalog query amortised' comment is true for doc_id resolution, false for the manifest fetch below it). FIX: add batch endpoints and collapse both loops.
notes:
## Kill per-search manifest N+1 (x2): add `/manifest/get_many` + batch-resolve on the service catalog API

### Problem
Two independent per-doc loops run on every search hit set in `src/nexus/search_engine.py`:

1. **`_attach_doc_ids_from_catalog`** (lines 73–167). Batches `chash→doc` correctly via `catalog.docs_for_chashes(nonempty)` (one call), but then loops `catalog.get_manifest(doc_id)` **once per distinct doc_id** (line 150, inside the `manifest_cache` loop at 141–157) to stamp `chunk_count`/`chunk_index`. The inline comment "each search hit pays one catalog query amortised" (lines 116–118) is **true for the `docs_for_chashes` doc_id resolution above it, false for the manifest fetch below it** — the manifest fetch is still N round-trips.

2. **`_attach_display_paths`** (lines 170–215). Independently loops `catalog.by_doc_id(did)` → `resolve()` (line 204, which calls `GET /show` per doc, see `http_catalog_client.py:746-747` → `:674`) **once per distinct doc_id** to fetch `file_path`.

Both run on the post-processing chain (`search_engine.py:596` and `:698`), so a single search with M distinct docs issues ~2M extra HTTP round-trips to the Java catalog service.

### Root cause
No batch endpoints on the service catalog API:
- No `/manifest/get_many` (only single `/manifest/get?doc_id=X` exists — `CatalogHandler.java:125`, `handleManifestGet` at `:473-481` → `repo.getManifest(tenant, docId)`).
- No batch-resolve / multi-doc `/show` (only single `/show?tumbler=X` — `handleShow`, routed at `CatalogHandler.java:107`; `resolve()` at `http_catalog_client.py:674`).

Note `/manifest/docs_for_chashes` (POST batch) already exists as the precedent pattern — `handleDocsForChashes` at `CatalogHandler.java:508-517` → `repo.docsForChashes(tenant, chashes)`. Mirror its shape.

### Fix (two new batch endpoints + collapse both loops)
1. **Java service** (`CatalogHandler.java` + `CatalogRepository.java`):
   - Add `POST /v1/catalog/manifest/get_many` → `repo.getManifestMany(tenant, docIds)` returning `{"manifests": {docId: [rows...], ...}}` (a per-doc-id map, unlike `docs_for_chashes`'s flat list). Register the new case in the dispatch switch (`CatalogHandler.java:123-131`).
   - Add a batch-resolve endpoint, e.g. `POST /v1/catalog/resolve_many` (or `/show_many`) → returns `{docId: entry, ...}` for `file_path`/full entry. Back it with a `SELECT ... WHERE doc_id IN (?)` in `CatalogRepository` (mirror `docsForChashes`).
2. **Python HTTP client** (`http_catalog_client.py`):
   - Add `get_manifests(doc_ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[Any]]` → `self._post("/manifest/get_many", {"doc_ids": doc_ids})`.
   - Add a batch entry-resolve method, e.g. `resolve_many(doc_ids) -> dict[str, CatalogEntry]` → `self._post("/resolve_many", {"doc_ids": doc_ids})`, parsing each via `_to_entry`.
3. **Local SQLite catalog** (`src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py` / `catalog_docs.py` / `catalog_writes.py`): add matching batch methods so both backends satisfy the same protocol (the `catalog: Any` passed to `_attach_*` may be either the HTTP client or the local catalog). Daemon-write-parity convention applies — see `tests/daemon/test_catalog_write_parity.py`.
4. **`search_engine.py`**: collapse the per-doc manifest loop (141–157) into one `get_manifests(list(resolved_doc_ids.values()))` call, and the per-doc resolve loop (202–208) into one `resolve_many(list(doc_ids))` call. Preserve existing semantics: legacy-`doc_id` preservation (124–137), "only inject when absent" guards (161–166, 211–215), and best-effort no-throw behaviour (the loops currently swallow exceptions per-doc; the batch versions must degrade gracefully on a single failed call, not poison the whole search).

### Backward-compat constraint
Both `_attach_*` functions take `catalog: Any | None` and must stay no-op-safe when the catalog backend predates the new batch methods (e.g. `getattr(catalog, "get_manifests", None)` fallback to the existing per-doc loop, or a capability check). Don't hard-require the new endpoint — older/local catalogs and tests must still pass.

This is a `Singleton (High)` bead — single-PR scope, no phasing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parallelize search_cross_corpus (reuse existing ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8)) + drop redundant per-collection count/re-embed
description: Singleton (High, structural). search_engine.py:482-497 loops collections one blocking HTTP round-trip at a time; the COUNT path (t3.py:1279) already uses ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) but the parallelism was never applied to the user-facing search hot path. Each iteration also pays a redundant col.count() and a redundant server-side embed of the identical query. corpus=all approx 3K serial network ops per logical query; dominant p95 contributor. FIX: parallelize the per-collection fan-out and embed the query once.
notes:
**Parallelize cross-corpus search fan-out + drop redundant per-collection count/re-embed**

The user-facing cross-corpus search hot path in `_search_collections` (`src/nexus/search_engine.py:482`) iterates `collections` serially, issuing one blocking `t3.search(query, [col], ...)` call per collection. Each call goes one HTTP round-trip at a time. For `corpus=all` (~thousands of collections) this serializes ~3K network ops per logical query and is the dominant p95 contributor.

The COUNT path (`T3Database.list_collections`, `src/nexus/db/t3.py:1257-1287`) already demonstrates the fix: it fans out `col.count()` across `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(8, len(names)))` with `as_completed` and per-future try/except. Mirror that pattern for the search fan-out — submit one `t3.search`-equivalent per collection, gather results, preserve the existing per-collection failure handling (`failed_collections[col]` on `VectorServiceError`, `continue`).

Two additional redundancies inside `T3Database.search` (`src/nexus/db/t3.py:1008`), executed once per collection today:
1. **Redundant `col.count()`** (`t3.py:1046`) — an extra HTTP round trip used only to clamp `actual_n = min(n_results, count, ...)` and skip empty collections. The query itself already returns ≤ requested results; the count call can be dropped (or made non-blocking) on the hot path.
2. **Redundant query embed** — for non-CCE cloud collections `_maybe_client_embed([query], name)` (`t3.py:1073`) falls through to server-side `query_texts` embedding, and CCE collections call `_cce_embed(query, input_type="query")` (`t3.py:1062`) per collection. The same query string is re-embedded for every collection. Embed the query **once per embedding-model group** (collections do NOT share one model — `voyage-code-3` for `code__*`, `voyage-context-3`/CCE for `docs__*`/`rdr__*`/`knowledge__*`), then reuse the vector across all collections in that group.

**Critical correctness constraints:** embed-once is only valid within a single embedding model — group collections by `index_model_for_collection(name)` (used at `t3.py:1035`) before sharing a vector; never collapse a CCE (`voyage-context-3`) query embedding with a `voyage-code-3` one. Parallelism must respect the ChromaDB quota `MAX_CONCURRENT_READS=10` per collection (`src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py`) and keep `per_k`/`n_results` clamped to `MAX_QUERY_RESULTS=300` (the existing cap at `search_engine.py:489` and `t3.py:1052`). Result ordering and the `diag_per_collection` / `min_raw_per_collection` / `total_raw` / `total_dropped` accumulators must remain deterministic regardless of completion order (sort/merge after gather, as `list_collections` sorts by name).
close_reason: Closed

title: Two-release deprecation-window mechanical gate: assert migration module present AND chroma_read importable, as a release-N gate
description: Singleton (High). The single irreversible step (RDR-155 P4b deletes the migration tool itself) is held only by bead-dependency ordering + human discipline; nothing in tests/ or .github/ asserts 'migration module present AND chroma_read importable' as a release gate. The intended hard gate (nexus-myk4e) is deferred until AFTER the boundary lifts, so it does not guard the very release it protects. FIX: add a release-N tripwire so a mis-sequenced P4b cannot merge into release N. Relates nexus-myk4e, nexus-h3ilf.
notes:
## Two-release deprecation-window mechanical gate (release-N tripwire)

**Goal:** Add a CI/test tripwire that fails if `src/nexus/migration/` (the ETL) or `src/nexus/migration/chroma_read.py` (the surviving Chroma read leg) is missing or non-importable. This guards release N of the two-release deprecation window: RDR-155 P4b deletes both modules *and the migration tool itself*, so a mis-sequenced P4b must not be able to merge into the migration-capable release. The intended hard gate (`nexus-myk4e`) is deferred until *after* the boundary lifts, so it cannot guard the very release it protects — this bead fills that gap with a mechanical assertion that lives and runs NOW.

### What exists today (confirmed)
- **Migration package:** `src/nexus/migration/__init__.py` — package docstring already names `chroma_read` as "the ONLY module in `src/nexus` allowed to construct Chroma clients after the Phase-4a serving retire."
- **Read leg:** `src/nexus/migration/chroma_read.py` (RDR-155 P4a.2, bead nexus-1k8s1). Exposes both legs: `chromadb.PersistentClient` (local) and `chromadb.CloudClient` (cloud). Read-only by convention. Header states full deletion is Phase 4b (nexus-19svb / nexus-g37fr), gated on P5.G.
- **Closest existing structural pattern:** `tests/test_rdr155_p4a_serving_retire.py` — already asserts presence/shape of `chroma_read.py` via `ETL_READ_LEG.is_file()` (`test_etl_read_leg_module_exists`, `test_etl_read_leg_contains_both_read_legs`) and survival pins (`TestPhase4aSurvivalPins`: `chroma_quotas` survives, Java read-client classes survive). This is the canonical home/idiom for "module must still be present" tripwires in this RDR. **Strongly prefer adding the new gate here** (or a sibling `test_rdr155_p4b_*` file) rather than inventing a new location.

### What the bead asks beyond what's there
The existing P4a tests assert `chroma_read.py` *file exists* and *contains* both legs (regex on source text), but do NOT assert the modules are **importable** (no `importlib.import_module("nexus.migration")` / `"nexus.migration.chroma_read"`). The new tripwire must add the import-success assertion — a file can exist but be broken/half-deleted. Assert BOTH: (1) `nexus.migration` package importable, (2) `nexus.migration.chroma_read` importable. Note: importing chroma_read pulls in `chromadb` — keep the import guarded/skipped consistently with how other tests handle the chromadb dependency, or assert on module-spec resolution (`importlib.util.find_spec`) to avoid heavyweight import side effects if chromadb isn't installed in the test env.

### Release-gate idiom for reference
`tests/test_plugin_structure.py::TestMarketplaceVersion` (e.g. `test_marketplace_source_ref_matches_pyproject`) is the existing "release-N parity gate" pattern: pure-Python structural assertions, no fixtures, CI-enforced, blocking on merge. The new tripwire should follow the same shape — a plain assertion test, no integration marker, runs in the default `uv run pytest` suite so it gates every PR including a stray P4b.

### Relations
- `nexus-myk4e` — the intended hard gate, deferred past the boundary (the gap this bead fills).
- `nexus-h3ilf` — related.
- P4b deletion beads this tripwire must block when mis-sequenced: `nexus-19svb`, `nexus-g37fr`, `nexus-8zpmf`.
- Standing release boundary: T2 `nexus/release-boundary-since-p4a`; memory `project_release_boundary_p4a.md`.

title: SHA-pin the pypi-publish and setup-graalvm GitHub Actions (currently float on mutable tags)
description: F5. release.yml:181 pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1 and service-ci.yml:34 graalvm/setup-graalvm@v1 float on mutable tags, while cosign-installer is SHA-pinned. The publish + build steps are higher-value supply-chain targets than the asset-signing step they feed. FIX: SHA-pin both actions (and audit other floating action refs in .github/workflows).
notes:
## SHA-pin floating GitHub Actions refs (supply-chain hardening)

**Goal:** Pin the high-value publish/build actions to immutable commit SHAs (they currently float on mutable tags), matching the SHA-pinning discipline already applied to `cosign-installer`, `action-gh-release`, and `dorny/paths-filter`. Then audit and decide policy for the remaining floating refs.

### Primary targets (named in F5)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:181` — `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` → pin to the commit SHA of the desired `gh-action-pypi-publish` release (the OIDC trusted-publisher step; highest-value target — it owns the PyPI publish identity). `release/v1` is a *moving branch ref*, the worst case.
- `.github/workflows/service-ci.yml:34` AND `:122` — `graalvm/setup-graalvm@v1` → pin to `bef4b0e916c7dd079bf60fb95d49139f67e32c5f` (the **exact SHA already used** in `engine-service-release.yml:62,113` and `ci.yml:469`). Note the bead names only line 34; line 122 is a **second occurrence in the same file** and must also be pinned to avoid leaving the file half-floating.

### Already-pinned precedent (the pattern to copy — `@<40-hex-sha>  # vX.Y.Z`)
- `release.yml:191` softprops/action-gh-release@718ea10b…  # v3.0.1
- `engine-service-release.yml` graalvm + sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f1778…  # v4.1.2
- `ci.yml` dorny/paths-filter@fbd0ab8f… + graalvm@bef4b0e9…  # v1

### Audit of remaining floating refs (the "audit other floating action refs" clause)
A full sweep (`grep -rnE 'uses:' .github/workflows/ | grep -vE '@[a-f0-9]{40}'`) shows the floaters are otherwise all **first-party `actions/*` and `astral-sh/setup-uv`** on major-version tags:
- `actions/checkout@v5`, `actions/cache@v5`, `actions/upload-artifact@v6`, `actions/download-artifact@v7` (across release/ci/engine-service/cold-install/plan-schema workflows)
- `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7`

These are lower-risk (GitHub-owned / well-known publisher, major-tag float) but inconsistent with the third-party pinning. **Decision needed:** the conservative/consistent move is to SHA-pin all of them with a trailing `# vN` comment so Dependabot can still surface updates; the minimal move is to pin only the two F5 targets. Recommend pinning everything for a clean inverse-grep (no floaters left), per `mem:feedback_exhaustive_surface_audit` — spot-fixing one surface per pass causes patch thrash.

### How to resolve a tag → SHA
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag> --jq .object.sha` (deref annotated tags with a second call to `git/tags/<sha>`), or `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> <tag>`. Always append `  # <human-tag>` after the SHA so the version stays readable and Dependabot-trackable.

### Notes
- No application code changes; CI-config only. No version bump, no manifest parity impact.
- This is bead `nexus-x0ndw` under the synthetic-aperture remediation epic. Target `develop` (integration branch), not `main`.
- Verification is "CI still green on a no-op push" — the pinned SHAs must resolve to the same action versions currently in use (graalvm precedent SHA guarantees this for service-ci).

title: Make MIN_MANAGED_APP_VERSION a meaningful floor (currently a no-op vs 1.0-SNAPSHOT)
description: F5. managed_endpoint.py:70 MIN_MANAGED_APP_VERSION=(1,0,0); both services report 1.0-SNAPSHOT -> parses to (1,0,0), clearing the floor trivially (the module docstring admits the no-op). The unauthenticated /version endpoint also discloses embedding_mode/models/schema id. FIX: bump the floor past 1.0-SNAPSHOT and make the version comparison enforce a real minimum; consider authenticating or trimming /version disclosure.
notes:
## Make MIN_MANAGED_APP_VERSION a meaningful floor (nexus-x2g1z, F5)

**Problem.** `src/nexus/db/managed_endpoint.py:70` sets `MIN_MANAGED_APP_VERSION = (1, 0, 0)`, and the comparison at `:225` (`parsed is None or parsed < MIN_MANAGED_APP_VERSION`) pins on the `app_version` field of the managed service's `GET /version` handshake. But the Java `VersionHandler` (`service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/VersionHandler.java:82-97`) sources `app_version` from the JAR's Maven `pom.properties`, which is frozen at the dev coordinate `1.0-SNAPSHOT`. `_parse_version("1.0-SNAPSHOT")` → `(1,0,0)`, which equals the floor, so the check is a structural no-op — the module docstring at `:46-69` openly admits this and a "relayed to conexus RDR-001" note acknowledges the managed floor "provides no version assurance until bumped." There is no `app_version` value any real build could report that would fail this gate.

**The correct fix already exists in a sibling.** `src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py:172` (`verify_service_version`, RDR-002 ez5.4) solves the identical problem for the NATIVE binary by pinning on the dedicated **`release_version`** field instead of `app_version`. `release_version` is the real release identity (`VersionHandler.java:109-149` `resolveReleaseVersion`/`normalizeReleaseVersion`): stamped from the `engine-service-vX.Y.Z` git tag at native-build time, and explicitly `null`/fail-closed on dev/SNAPSHOT/unstamped builds. `guided_upgrade` keys a fail-closed pin on it with `REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION = (0,1,5)` (`guided_upgrade.py:139`).

**Design tension to resolve (do NOT silently pick one).** The `managed_endpoint.py:59-69` docstring frames the `app_version` vs `release_version` split as a *deliberate RDR-002 asymmetry* ("two gates for two topologies") — managed gate pins `app_version`, native gate pins `release_version`. That rationale is the very thing that makes the managed floor vacuous: the managed service inherits the same frozen `1.0-SNAPSHOT` app_version. Two viable fixes, pick explicitly and update the docstring:
  1. **Pivot the managed gate onto `release_version`** (mirror `guided_upgrade.verify_service_version`, fail-closed on null/SNAPSHOT/dev) and set a real `REQUIRED_*` floor. This collapses the asymmetry but gives a genuine assurance. **Requires a cross-repo contract change**: the managed service (conexus RDR-001) must expose `release_version` unauthenticated on `/version`. The local Java `VersionHandler` already emits it (`:184-185`), so the conexus side is the open question — relay to conexus before landing.
  2. **Keep pinning `app_version` but bump the floor past `(1,0,0)`** only if/when the managed deployment starts reporting a real semver in `app_version`. This is the docstring's stated intent but is inert as long as the managed service mirrors `1.0-SNAPSHOT`; do not ship a cosmetic bump that is still a no-op.

Recommended: option 1 (pivot to `release_version`), because it reuses the proven fail-closed parser and gives an actual floor today. Confirm the conexus-side `/version` contract first (`mem:feedback_hal_relays_cross_instance_bus` — the bus is passive; surface an explicit "relay to conexus RDR-001" action).

**Secondary, in-scope concern (F5 second half): `/version` disclosure.** The unauthenticated `/version` (Java `VersionHandler.handle` — "No authentication required", `:18-21`) discloses `embedding_mode`, `embedding_models`, `schema_latest_id`, and `schema_changeset_count` (consumed into `ManagedCapabilities`, `managed_endpoint.py:91-101`). On the *local loopback* service this is fine (the Javadoc justifies it: loopback-only, crosses no trust boundary). On the **managed public-internet** service it is an information-disclosure surface. Options: authenticate the `/version` route for the managed deployment, or trim the managed `/version` payload to just the version field(s) the client needs for the floor check. This is a conexus-side (managed-service) change; relay it. Do not weaken the *local* `VersionHandler` — its loopback exemption is correct.

Sibling bead **nexus-3rq00** ("engine-service version pin into the parity machinery: `version(PINNED_SERVICE_TAG) >= REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION`") overlaps the version-floor theme — coordinate so the two don't define competing floors.

title: GUC-name allowlist in TenantScope.set_config (block request-derived GUC names)
description: F5. TenantScope.java:111 concatenates the GUC name into set_config SQL with only an isBlank() guard. The sole custom-GUC caller passes a static final literal (safe today), but any request-derived GUC name reopens injection into the session GUC namespace. FIX: enforce an allowlist of permitted GUC names before set_config; reject anything else.
notes:
## Bead: GUC-name allowlist in `TenantScope.set_config` (block request-derived GUC names)

**Epic:** nexus-whh61 (synthetic-aperture remediation) · **Bead:** nexus-utnjt · **Branch:** feature/arch-docs-staleness

### Problem
`TenantScope.withTenant(String tenant, String gucName, Function<DSLContext,T> work)` builds the GUC-stamp SQL by **string-concatenating `gucName` into the statement** at `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TenantScope.java:111`:

```java
try (var ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT set_config('" + gucName + "', ?, true)")) {
```

The only guard is `gucName == null || gucName.isBlank()` (lines 97–99). The `tenant` *value* is parameterized (injection-safe), but the GUC *name* is interpolated raw. Today the sole custom-GUC caller (`ScratchRepository`) passes a `static final` literal (`T1_TENANT_GUC = "nexus.t1_tenant"`, ScratchRepository.java:62), and the no-arg overload hardcodes `"nexus.tenant"` (line 77) — so it is safe *today*. But any future caller passing a request-derived GUC name reopens SQL injection into the session-GUC namespace.

### Fix
Enforce an **allowlist of permitted GUC names** before the `set_config` call; reject anything not on it (throw `IllegalArgumentException`, consistent with the existing null/blank guard at line 95/98). The allowlist is exactly the two GUC names in use across the codebase:
- `nexus.tenant` (default, hardcoded at TenantScope.java:77)
- `nexus.t1_tenant` (ScratchRepository.T1_TENANT_GUC)

Define these as a small `Set<String>` constant on `TenantScope` (e.g. `private static final Set<String> PERMITTED_GUCS = Set.of("nexus.tenant", "nexus.t1_tenant")`). Add the check inside `withTenant(String, String, Function)` immediately after the existing blank guard (after line 99, before line 101). Keep the comment at lines 108–110 honest by updating it: the GUC name is now allowlist-validated, not merely "a validated internal constant."

Consider also pointing `ScratchRepository.T1_TENANT_GUC` and the default `"nexus.tenant"` literal at the same constant set so the allowlist is the single source of truth (avoid drift). Defensive belt-and-suspenders option (do not skip the allowlist for it): also validate the name matches a `nexus.[a-z_]+` shape — but the allowlist is the primary required control.

### Tests
No existing `TenantScope*Test` file — add one (TDD: test before impl). The closest existing pattern is `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/TenantPoolingIsolationTest.java` (Testcontainers PostgreSQL + HikariCP + Liquibase). For the allowlist check you do **not** need a live DB — it can be a pure unit test asserting that `withTenant(tenant, "evil'); DROP ...", work)` and any non-allowlisted name throws `IllegalArgumentException` *before* a connection is borrowed, while `"nexus.tenant"` and `"nexus.t1_tenant"` are accepted. Add a non-vacuous assertion that an injection-shaped GUC name is rejected (per CLAUDE.md: exact assertions, fail-loud, no silent fallback). Keep the existing isolation tests green.

### Review gate
Java schema/security change → run the **full** `mvn` suite for the service module (per `feedback_java_schema_full_suite` — Java CI is advisory-only, auto-merge fires on pytest alone; constraint/security changes break fixtures a diff-read can't enumerate). Then stacked reviewers: `code-review-expert` then `substantive-critic` (security/auth boundary diff → critic should pressure-test that the allowlist is the sole writer path and that no caller bypasses `withTenant`).

title: Ship pgbouncer.ini (pool_mode=transaction) as a verified artifact or assert it at service startup
description: F5 (High, managed topology). TenantScope.java:33-37 requires pool_mode=transaction as a Javadoc invariant; repo-wide search finds ZERO pool_mode strings and no pgbouncer.ini. set_config(...,true) at :111 is SET LOCAL; under a session-mode pooler nexus.tenant leaks to the next borrower with FORCE RLS evaluating the leaked value -> cross-tenant read. FIX: ship a pgbouncer.ini with pool_mode=transaction as a checked-in artifact, and/or assert transaction-mode at service startup (fail closed). This is the reason RDR-166 exists; the invariant must be an artifact, not prose.
notes:
## nexus-bhzuv — Ship pgbouncer.ini (pool_mode=transaction) as a verified artifact or assert it at service startup

**Severity:** High (F5, managed topology). The Javadoc invariant in `TenantScope.java:33-37` is prose, not an enforced artifact. RDR-166 exists precisely because this invariant must be machine-checked, not documented.

### The defect
`TenantScope.withTenant(...)` (`service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TenantScope.java:111`) stamps the tenant with `SELECT set_config('nexus.tenant', ?, true)` — the third arg `true` means **SET LOCAL** (txn-local) semantics. This is safe ONLY under a transaction-mode pooler. Under a **session-mode** pooler (PgBouncer default), the GUC is not reset on transaction boundary; the server backend is returned to the pool still carrying `nexus.tenant`, and the next borrower inherits it. Every tenant table runs `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with `USING (tenant_id = current_setting('nexus.tenant', true))` (`TenantConstants.java:20`, `MemoryRepository.java:32`, `ScratchRepository.java:26`), so a leaked GUC is evaluated as the *previous* tenant → **cross-tenant read**.

Confirmed by the bead's claim and verified here: repo-wide search finds **zero `pool_mode` strings outside the test/Javadoc** and **no `pgbouncer.ini`**. The only enforcement today is `withEnv("POOL_MODE", "transaction")` inside `PgBouncerTenantIsolationTest.java:119` — which proves the engine *works* under txn-mode but does nothing to guarantee the *deployed* pooler is in txn-mode. The production topology (Crunchy Standard fronting PG with PgBouncer, per that test's class doc) is exactly where a misconfigured `pool_mode = session` would silently reintroduce the leak.

### Fix (the bead's "and/or" — either or both satisfy)
1. **Checked-in `pgbouncer.ini` artifact** with `pool_mode = transaction`, shipped as part of the managed/service deployment surface so the deployed pooler config is version-controlled and reviewable rather than hand-set. Decide the canonical home with the install story (RDR-152 / RDR-166 service-stack install; `nx init --service` wiring lives in `Main.java`).
2. **Fail-closed startup assertion** in `Main.main()` (`service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/Main.java`), run *before* `NexusService` binds the HTTP port (mirror the existing fail-fast pattern: schema migration already `System.exit(1)`s before bind). Detection options, in order of robustness:
   - **PgBouncer admin console probe** (most direct): if a pooler is interposed, connect to the special `pgbouncer` virtual DB and `SHOW DATABASES` / `SHOW CONFIG` — the `pool_mode` column must read `transaction`. Gate behind a new optional env (e.g. `NX_PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_URL`); absence = direct-PG deployment, assertion is a no-op (v1 connects directly, no pooler — `TenantScope` Javadoc line 35-36).
   - **Behavioral probe**: stamp a *session*-scoped GUC (`set_config('nexus.tenant', x, false)`) on one borrow, return it, then on a fresh borrow read `current_setting('nexus.tenant', true)` — non-empty ⇒ session-mode pooler or no reset ⇒ fail closed. (Note: a real pooler's `server_reset_query` can mask this; the admin-console probe is preferred where available.)
   - Whatever the mechanism: **fail closed** — log structured error and `System.exit(1)`, never warn-and-continue.

### Tie-in
This is the engine-side analog of the conexus `GucLeakTripwire`. `TenantPoolingIsolationTest.tenantGucIsResetAfterTransactionCommit` is the existing deterministic leak-property test (1-conn HikariCP, no external pooler) — a new startup-assertion unit/integration test should sit alongside it and `PgBouncerTenantIsolationTest`.

### Constraints / gotchas
- Startup assertion must run **before HTTP bind**, after the Hikari `DataSource` is built (`Main.java` ~line 60-100), matching the schema-migration fail-fast ordering.
- Do NOT make the assertion mandatory for the direct-PG (no-pooler) v1 path — it must no-op when no pooler is configured, or it breaks local/dev `nx init --service`.
- Per project rule: **this is a Java schema/topology-adjacent change — run the FULL `mvn` suite, not a diff-read subset.** The Java CI job is advisory-only (pytest auto-merge fires without it); constraint/config changes break fixtures a diff-read can't enumerate (`feedback_java_schema_full_suite`).
- Structured logging only (SLF4J `log.error("event=...", ...)`), `System.exit(1)` on failure — match `Main.java`'s `event=schema_migration_failed` pattern.
- Stage the new `pgbouncer.ini` by explicit path; never `git add -A`.
- This lands on the `service/` Java module; PR targets `develop`.

title: Single-writer: reclaimer-of-last-resort or fail-loud when no daemon is electable (direct-write fallback contention)
description: F4 (High). The single-writer WAL guarantee holds only while a daemon is live. t2_daemon.py:1201-1209 documents a direct-write fallback used when the daemon is crash-loop-suppressed — re-opening multi-process WAL contention in exactly the orphan/long-lived-MCP scenario that causes it, with reclaim being daemon-only (no reclaimer under suppression). FIX: add a reclaimer-of-last-resort that runs even under suppression, OR fail the worker loud when no daemon can be elected, so wedged direct-writes don't silently contend.
notes:
## F4 (High) — Single-writer: reclaimer-of-last-resort or fail-loud when no daemon is electable

### Problem
The single-writer WAL guarantee for T2 (`memory.db`) holds only while a T2 daemon is live and owns the WAL writer slot. When no daemon is electable (crash-loop-guard suppressed respawn, spawn failed, or version-skew cycle deferred), `t2_index_write()` deliberately degrades to a **direct `T2Database` write** as a documented fallback (`src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:315-461`, RDR-128 P3). This is the intended availability tradeoff for the write path.

The residual gap is on the **reclaim path**, not the write path. Stale `in_progress` aspect-queue rows are reclaimed *only* by `T2Daemon._reclaim_stale_loop` (`src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:1177-1227`), which is daemon-only by construction (nexus-we61e moved reclaim off the per-worker poll loop to kill N-fold WAL contention). The "Residual gap (accepted)" docstring at `t2_daemon.py:1201-1209` spells it out: while a daemon is crash-loop-suppressed, workers keep claiming/completing rows via the direct-write fallback, so a **worker crash during suppression strands an `in_progress` row with no reclaimer** — exactly the orphan/long-lived-MCP scenario (memory: `daemon-restart-not-worker-fix`) that produces the WAL contention RDR-128 was filed to close.

Today this self-heals only when a daemon comes back up: `_reclaim_stale_loop` runs reclaim-FIRST (`t2_daemon.py:1196-1199`, nexus-nhqll), clearing the backlog at once. The gap is the window where no daemon is electable AND a worker dies mid-claim.

### Fix options (from the bead)
1. **Reclaimer-of-last-resort under suppression** — a bounded reclaim path that runs even when no daemon is electable, without reintroducing the N-fold per-worker WAL contention RDR-128 closed (e.g. single-flight guarded by the same election flock, or capped to the fallback-write process that already holds a direct connection).
2. **Fail-loud** — when no daemon can be elected, make the worker loop fail loud rather than silently claiming rows it cannot guarantee reclamation for, so wedged direct-writes don't accumulate stranded `in_progress` rows invisibly.

### Key mechanisms to preserve
- Reclaim must NOT run from every per-process aspect worker (the regression nexus-we61e fixed; `aspect_worker.py:250-290`, `:143` "Stale-row reclamation is owned by the T2 daemon, not this worker").
- The daemon's own reclaim serialises through `_catalog_write_lock` (`t2_daemon.py:1229-1245`, RDR-151 nexus-xmohw) — any last-resort path must similarly avoid contending the WAL writer lock.
- Election/single-writer invariant lives in the shared primitive `service_registry.py` (RDR-149) + conformance suite, per CLAUDE.md "Daemon-lifecycle fixes land in the shared primitive, never one tier's copy." A reclaimer-of-last-resort that gates on electability should use the existing per-scope election flock, not a new mechanism.
- The four no-daemon outcomes are enumerated in `mcp_infra.py:281-303` (`DEFERRED_WRITE_LOCK`, `DEFERRED_SIGTERM`, `CRASHLOOP_SUPPRESSED`, `SPAWN_FAILED`) — the fix branches on `T2EnsureOutcome`.

### Design note
This is a correctness/observability hardening of an *accepted* residual gap, not a live bug. Before implementing, confirm with an RDR or at least pin which option (reclaimer vs fail-loud) — the docstring at `t2_daemon.py:1201-1209` explicitly rejected the naive worker-side reclaim, so the chosen fix must not re-add that. Per memory `feedback_no_preventive_scope_beyond_evidence`, scope to the demonstrated strand-during-suppression window, not speculative broadening.
close_reason: Obsoleted by RDR-152 (service/PG is the hard default; storage_mode.py:7-8). The single-writer WAL guarantee this bead hardens is a SQLite-T2-daemon property — the reclaimer-of-last-resort / fail-loud gap only exists on the legacy SQLite aspect-queue path. On the default service backend the aspect queue routes to Postgres (http_aspect_queue.py); there is no single-writer slot, no daemon-electability dependency, no stranded-in_progress-without-reclaimer window. The bead itself noted this is 'an accepted residual gap, not a live bug'. Owner decision 2026-06-23: close as obsoleted-by-RDR-152, same disposition as essw3.

title: Invert write-serialization coverage test to allowlist-of-mutations + behaviour-based RDR-149 lifecycle gate
description: F3 (latent High). Mechanical guards pin syntactic proxies not behaviour. test_rdr151_xmohw_write_serialization.py:127-132 matches a hardcoded verb regex; a future store method named tag/attach/touch/finalize/link/register MISSES it, is continue-skipped green (:150-151), and if absent from _WRITE_OPS (t2_daemon.py:686-721) dispatches un-serialised -> re-opens the #1137 WAL self-contention class. Today fully covered (set_ token), gap is prospective. FIX: invert to 'every dispatchable non-read store op MUST be in _WRITE_OPS'. Also rewrite test_lifecycle_gate.py:28-94 to assert behaviour (no bespoke flock election outside service_registry primitive) rather than banning dead fn names.
notes:
## Invert write-serialization coverage to allowlist-of-mutations + behaviour-based RDR-149 lifecycle gate

**Class:** F3 (latent High). Two mechanical guard tests pin *syntactic proxies* (a verb regex; banned function-name strings) instead of the behaviour they intend to enforce. Both are correct today but fail open prospectively. Fix both in one bead.

### Part A — invert `test_write_op_coverage` (write-serialization forcing function)

**Current shape** (`tests/daemon/test_rdr151_xmohw_write_serialization.py:114-161`): the coverage test enumerates every dispatchable store method, then **only checks an op for serialization if its name matches a hardcoded write-verb regex** (`:127-132`). The `continue` at `:150-151` (`if not write_verb.match(attr): continue`) is the hole: a future store method named with a verb *not* in the regex alphabet (e.g. `tag`, `attach`, `touch`, `finalize`, `link`, `register`, `bind`, `stamp`) is silently skipped — passes green — and if it is also absent from `_WRITE_OPS` (`src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:686-721`) it dispatches **un-serialised** through `_invoke_with_lock_retry` (`t2_daemon.py:1618`), re-opening the issue #1137 intra-daemon WAL self-contention class (parallel `to_thread` writers racing one SQLite write lock → SQLITE_BUSY spin → 100% CPU peg).

**Required inversion:** flip the default from "skip unless verb-matched" to **"every dispatchable non-read store op MUST be serialised (`in _WRITE_OPS` or `startswith(_WRITE_SERIALIZED_PREFIXES)`), unless explicitly classified as a read."** The verb regex (`write_verb`) is deleted; serialization becomes the default and **reads** become the named exception.

**Blocker — there is no read-op set today.** `_WRITE_OPS` (`t2_daemon.py:686`) and `_WRITE_SERIALIZED_PREFIXES` (`:668`, = `catalog_write.` + `taxonomy.`) exist; there is **no `_READ_OPS` / read allowlist** (grep confirms). Inverting requires introducing an explicit read classification so the test (and ideally `_dispatch` itself) can answer "is this op a read?" without a verb heuristic. Decide and document where this lives:
  - a `_READ_OPS` frozenset + read-prefix tuple in `t2_daemon.py` alongside `_WRITE_OPS`, enumerating the legitimately-concurrent reads (e.g. `database.hello`, `*.get`, `*.search`, `*.list`, `memory.*` readers, plan-match reads). The module docstring at `t2_daemon.py:670-685` already states "READS are intentionally NOT [serialised]" and names `database.hello` as the canonical one that must stay un-serialised — that rationale anchors the read allowlist.
  - The inverted test then asserts: for every dispatchable op (`op in table`, not in `_RPC_DENY_OPS`, public, callable), `op` is in exactly one of {read-set, write-set/prefix}. **`missing` = ops that are neither** (the new failure: an unclassified op is a defect, not a pass).

**Keep:** the dual `test_write_ops_have_no_stale_entries` (`:164-175`) already guards the reverse drift (`_WRITE_OPS` naming a non-dispatchable op). Add the symmetric guard for the new read-set (no stale read entries). The forcing-function comment at `t2_daemon.py:682-685` must be updated to describe the inverted (allowlist) contract.

**Watch:** `_RPC_DENY_OPS` (`t2_daemon.py:636-653`) ops are correctly excluded (not dispatchable). `database.*` pseudo-store ops (`_T2_DATABASE_METHODS`, `:621-626`) ARE dispatchable and must be classified. `catalog.commit` is in `_WRITE_OPS` while other `catalog.*` mutations route via the `catalog_write.` prefix — the read/write partition must account for both catalog surfaces.

### Part B — rewrite `test_lifecycle_gate.py` to assert behaviour

**Current shape** (`tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py:28-94`): three tests grep source text for **dead function-name strings** — `_BANNED_DEFS` (`:28-34`: `write_t1_addr`, `read_t1_addr_for`, `unlink_t1_addr`, `t1_addr_path`, `sweep_orphan_t1_addr_files`), a banned `class LeaseRecord` defined outside the primitive (`:62-75`), and a banned `def _elect(` outside the primitive (`:78-94`). These ban *specific historical names* P5 deleted; they do not stop a *new* bespoke flock election or addr-file scheme under a different name.

**Required:** assert the **behaviour/invariant** — "no bespoke per-scope flock election or on-disk lease/liveness mechanism exists outside the `ServiceRegistry` primitive (`src/nexus/daemon/service_registry.py`)" — rather than banning a fixed name list. Anchor to the real primitive API (confirmed present): `ServiceRegistry` (`service_registry.py:154`), `LeaseRecord` (`:107`), `_elect` (`:207`), `publish`/`heartbeat`/`publish_once`/`heartbeat_tick` (`:261/294/435/446`). Practical behaviour proxies to assert instead of name-strings:
  - the only `fcntl.flock` / `filelock` *election* call sites in `src/nexus/` for daemon-scope ownership resolve through `ServiceRegistry._elect` (search for the lock primitive, not the function name);
  - lease/liveness is **TTL freshness**, not a pid-keyed addr file — assert no module under `src/nexus/` writes a `t1_addr.<pid>`-style ownership file (the RDR-149 §Validation "no per-tier orphan sweep" invariant), checked by file-write behaviour or path-construction rather than the literal old function names.

The `# lifecycle-gate-allow:` escape token (`:36`) convention and `test_gate_doc_exists` (`:97-105`, pins `daemon/AGENTS.md` naming the primitive + conformance suite) should be preserved. Cross-check against the live conformance suite `tests/daemon/test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py` (present) so the gate test and the conformance test stay complementary, not redundant.

### Scope / risk notes
- This is a **test-quality** change plus (Part A) a small `t2_daemon.py` constant addition (`_READ_OPS`). No behavioural change to dispatch is *required*, but introducing `_READ_OPS` makes the read/write partition single-sourced — consider having `_dispatch` (`t2_daemon.py:1611`) consult it so test and runtime share one classification (avoids the test asserting a partition the code doesn't actually use).

title: Engine-service version pin into the parity machinery: parity test version(PINNED_SERVICE_TAG) >= REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION and pin-is-set
description: F2. conexus<->engine coupling rides two hand-edited constants outside the 7-manifest parity gate: PINNED_SERVICE_TAG (daemon/binary_install.py:90, currently None by design pre-6.0) and REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION=(0,1,5) (guided_upgrade.py:139), with no cross-check. Add a parity test asserting the pinned tag's numeric version >= REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION and that the pin is non-None at release time; add the engine pin as a first-class checked manifest in the release skill. Prevents a version-cut that ships a client incompatible with (or unable to auto-install) the engine.
notes:
## Engine-service version pin → parity machinery (nexus-whh61 epic; blocks nexus-h3ilf Release-N readiness gate)

### Problem
Two hand-edited constants govern conexus↔engine compatibility but sit **outside** the 7-manifest parity gate (`tests/test_plugin_structure.py::TestMarketplaceVersion`), with no cross-check between them:

- `PINNED_SERVICE_TAG: str | None` — `src/nexus/daemon/binary_install.py:90`. Build-time pin of the compatible `engine-service-v*` GitHub release tag. **Currently `None` by design** (no real `engine-service-v*` release exists yet pre-6.0); while `None`, `nx init --service` refuses to auto-install and instructs the user to pass an explicit tag. Env override: `SERVICE_TAG_ENV = "NEXUS_SERVICE_TAG"`. Namespace prefix constant: `TAG_NAMESPACE_PREFIX = "engine-service-v"`.
- `REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION: tuple[int, int, int] = (0, 1, 5)` — `src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py:139` (NOTE: bead said `daemon/guided_upgrade.py`, actual path is `migration/guided_upgrade.py`). RDR-002 floor the guided upgrade hands off to. Paired with `verify_service_version()` / `VersionPinOutcome` (dataclass, `ok`+`reason`) / `_parse_semver()` (fail-closed: rejects blank/`SNAPSHOT`/`dev`/pre-release/`+meta`).

A release could ship a client pinned to an engine tag whose numeric version is **below** `REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION` — i.e. a client that auto-installs an engine it then refuses as too old — and nothing catches it.

### What to build
1. **New parity test** (extend `class TestMarketplaceVersion` in `tests/test_plugin_structure.py`, or a sibling class in the same file — it already owns the parity surface and the `PYPROJECT_PATH`/`MARKETPLACE_PATH`/`REPO_ROOT` constants). Assertions:
   - `_parse_semver(PINNED_SERVICE_TAG) >= REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION` (reuse the existing `_parse_semver` from `guided_upgrade.py` rather than reimplementing — it strips the leading `v` and fails closed).
   - **pin-is-set at release time**: `PINNED_SERVICE_TAG is not None`. Because the pin is intentionally `None` pre-6.0, this assertion must be **conditional/gated**, not unconditional — gate it on a release marker (e.g. only enforce non-None when not a dev/pre-release pyproject version, or `xfail`/`skip` with a tracking reason until 6.0). Do NOT turn the existing green suite RED by asserting non-None unconditionally today. Mirror the fail-closed philosophy of `_parse_semver`.
   - Strip the `engine-service-v` `TAG_NAMESPACE_PREFIX` (not just a leading `v`) before parsing the tag — the pin format is `engine-service-vX.Y.Z`, not `vX.Y.Z`.
2. **Release-skill manifest**: add the engine pin as a first-class checked item in `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md` (the authoritative checklist; the conexus-plugin copy if one ships). Slot it alongside the existing manifest list (around SKILL.md:39-45 where `source.ref` and mcpb manifests are enumerated) so a release that advances the engine bumps `PINNED_SERVICE_TAG` in lock-step.

### Key references
- Existing pin-test prior art (mode/fail-closed patterns to mirror): `tests/migration/test_guided_upgrade_version_pin.py`.
- Parity-gate prior art (test shape, path constants, per-plugin loop): `tests/test_plugin_structure.py::TestMarketplaceVersion::test_marketplace_source_ref_matches_pyproject` (lines 674-699).
- The existing 7-manifest gate is documented in `CLAUDE.md` § "Cutting a release" step 3 and `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:39`.

### Constraints / gotchas
- Bead's path for `REQUIRED_RELEASE_VERSION` is wrong: it's `src/nexus/migration/guided_upgrade.py:139`, not `daemon/`.
- Branch `feature/arch-docs-staleness` is off `develop`; PR targets `develop`, not `main`.
- TDD: write the failing test first. Deterministic, no network — read the constants by import, not by hitting GitHub.
- Don't make the suite RED today: `PINNED_SERVICE_TAG is None` is the correct current state. The non-None assertion is a release-time gate that must be skipped/xfail'd until the first real engine-service release (6.0). Document the deferral with a tracking reason inline.

title: Behavioural cross-boundary write-seam CI gate (boot JAR, assert server-side dedup/quota against HttpVectorClient)
description: Audit F1 structural gap: no single CI gate exercises BOTH halves of a write-seam diff. pyproject addopts deselect integration; .github/workflows/service-ci.yml fires only on service/** paths (advisory/non-blocking), so a Python-only change to http_vector_client.py:512-550 can't trigger the Java VectorHandler tenant/dedup suite. Add a small integration job that boots the engine JAR and feeds >300-record / duplicate-chash / oversized inputs through the real HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks, asserting server-side enforcement (PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal dedup at :287-313; ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,collection,chash) DO UPDATE ~:386). Closes the 'signature-parity-not-behaviour-parity' root cause; incidentally co-gates tenant isolation. Report F1.
notes:
## Behavioural cross-boundary write-seam CI gate (F1)

**Root cause (structural gap F1):** No single CI gate exercises BOTH halves of a write-seam diff. The Python suite (`ci.yml`) runs `pytest` with the repo-default `addopts = "-m 'not integration and not slow and not stress'"` (`pyproject.toml:184`), so integration tests are deselected; auto-merge fires on the Python suite alone. Meanwhile `service-ci.yml` is **path-gated to `service/**` + `.github/workflows/service-ci.yml` only** (lines 8-15) — a Python-only change to `http_vector_client.py:upsert_chunks` (lines 477-550) **cannot trigger** the Java `VectorHandler`/`PgVectorRepository` tenant/dedup/quota suite. Result: "signature-parity-not-behaviour-parity" — `HttpVectorClient` mirrors `T3Database`'s signature (`tests/test_http_vector_client_parity.py`) but nothing asserts the *server* enforces dedup/quota/oversize behaviour on the real wire.

**What server-side enforcement actually does** (`PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal`, `service/.../vectors/PgVectorRepository.java`):
- **Dedup**: in-batch `seen` HashSet collapses duplicate `chash` ids before embed+write (lines 292-314); logs `event=upsert_dedup_collapsed received=/kept=/collapsed=`.
- **ON CONFLICT**: `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, collection, chash) DO UPDATE SET chunk_text/embedding/metadata` (lines 385-388) — cross-call idempotency / metadata refresh.
- **NUL sanitization** (lines 280-309) and **dim guard** (lines 340-346) are adjacent fail-loud paths the same test can incidentally cover.
- **Tenant isolation**: every write runs inside `tenantScope.withTenant(tenant, ...)` (line 369) under FORCE RLS — the gate "incidentally co-gates tenant isolation" as the bead notes.

Note the client-side quota path: `http_vector_client.py` batches at `QUOTAS.MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE` (300) for upsert/get/delete (lines 1015-1021, 1114, 1171-1172). The bead's ">300-record" assertion therefore tests that a single logical `upsert_chunks` call with >300 ids round-trips correctly through whatever batching/server enforcement exists (it should NOT raise `ChromaError: Quota exceeded` on the happy path; the gate proves the seam handles it end-to-end rather than only at the Python signature layer).

**The deliverable:** a small `-m integration` job (mirroring the CA-3 jobs in `ci.yml`, which run `pytest ... -o addopts="" -m integration`) that:
1. Builds + boots the engine JAR against a throwaway pgvector instance (reuse the established fixture pattern), and
2. Feeds **>300-record**, **duplicate-chash**, and **oversized (>16384-byte / `MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES`)** inputs through the **real** `HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks` (`NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_VECTORS=service`), asserting server-side enforcement: dedup collapse (verify kept count == unique chash count), ON CONFLICT idempotency (re-upsert same chash → updated, not duplicated), and oversize/quota behaviour. Also wire a **path filter** so a diff touching `src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py` (or the Java vectors handler) **triggers this job** — closing the gap where neither existing workflow fires.

**Anchor the new test on the existing harness** — do NOT invent a new boot path:
- `tests/db/_service_fixture.py` — `SERVICE_ROLES_SQL` (creates `nexus_svc`), `jar_freshness_skip_reason()` (stale-jar guard), token/session minting helpers.
- `tests/db/conftest.py:33-53` — autouse `_service_jar_freshness` fixture (skips/fails on stale jar; set `NX_REQUIRE_SERVICE_JAR=1`-style fail-loud in CI so the gate can't pass vacuously on a missing jar).
- `tests/db/test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py` — canonical boot-the-JAR + `NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_VECTORS=service` + index/search round-trip pattern (PG bin discovery lines 41-64, `pytestmark` skipif lines 66-70).
- `service/src/test/java/.../VectorHandlerEmbeddingModeTest.java`, `VectorIntegrationTest.java`, `PgVectorRepositoryContractTest.java` — existing Java-side coverage to avoid duplicating; the NEW value is the **Python-client → real-server** wire crossing, not re-testing the repo in-JVM.

**Vacuous-gate caution** (per nexus-9nv1d / substantive-critic history): the job must FAIL (not skip) when the JAR is missing/stale in CI, and the path filter must be SHA-pinned (`dorny/paths-filter@fbd0ab8...`, see `ci.yml:335`) so a compromised float tag can't silently emit `false` and skip the gate while reporting green.

title: guided-upgrade T2 migrate-all leg cannot auto-discover the service endpoint it just provisioned (migration BLOCKED, migrated-failed)
description: Surfaced by migration-rehearsal --guided (LOCAL onnx-local mode, no --with-cloud) 2026-06-22. Single nx guided-upgrade --local-path ... --yes invocation: provisioning published the lease (event=storage_service_lease_published scope=1000 port=52203 @13:26:36) AND the post-provision verify connected (Service verified at http://127.0.0.1:52203 healthy+version-pinned). But ~19s later the T2 migrate-all leg failed: event=migrate_all_verify_count_source_failed error='nexus-service endpoint is not resolvable (NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service): start the supervisor with nx daemon service start ... or export NX_SERVICE_PORT/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN'. Result: sequencer_t2_dirty_blocks_t3 total_failed=8, T3 vector migration never started, sentinel=migrated-failed, reads degraded-LOUD. The guided MVV harness FAILED 3 checks (guided-upgrade exited 1; no 'Migration VERIFIED and unlocked'; parity mismatch). Service stack itself is fine: PG16 provisioned, native bge-768 binary, healthy, version-pinned, liquibase 138 changesets applied, legacy Chroma untouched. Within one guided-upgrade process the verify path resolved the endpoint but the migrate-all path did NOT — an endpoint-discovery seam (RDR-105 T1 lease / RDR-149 discovery): the just-published lease (scope=1000) is not consumed by the migrate-all client. CONTRAST: nexus-4mm24 --cold path passed parity 12=12 (different flow: manual nx init --service + explicit env, not the guided auto-discovery). MUST TRIAGE harness-vs-product before classifying as a release-N blocker — but if product, this blocks the RDR-002 guided-upgrade UX = the luxe6 (b) migration-capable release. Log: /tmp/shakeout-rehearsal-guided-LOCAL-*.log.
design: Triage via /conexus:debug: (1) does the migrate-all leg read NX_SERVICE_*/lease from the same config-dir + scope the provisioning step wrote? (2) is it a timing/ordering issue (migrate-all runs before the lease is consumable) or a scope/path mismatch (uid scope 1000 vs client lookup)? (3) does guided-upgrade pass the in-process endpoint to the migrate-all leg, or does migrate-all re-resolve from scratch and fall back to NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service with no NX_SERVICE_*? Likely fix: thread the provisioned endpoint (host/port/token) explicitly into the migrate-all + T3 legs instead of relying on re-discovery, OR ensure the lease is published+consumable before the migrate sequencer runs.
acceptance_criteria: nx guided-upgrade completes end-to-end in the rehearsal (--guided): T2 migrate-all succeeds, T3 vector leg runs, 'Migration VERIFIED and unlocked', parity matches, sentinel cleared. Root cause classified harness-vs-product with evidence.
