title: Release-N gate 1/3: voyage-capability pre-flight (server /version embedding_models), not a client key
description: Release-N readiness gate 1/3 (parent nexus-h3ilf). Migration pre-flight for voyage-model collections. NOT a client-voyage-key check — in service/cloud mode embedding is SERVER-SIDE (http_vector_client.py:476); the engine holds the operator Voyage key, tenants never supply one (only NX_SERVICE_TOKEN). The REAL gate: when detect_pending_migration's footprint contains voyage-model collections AND the migration target is a voyage-backed service, assert the target /version reports voyage embedding capability (embedding_models includes voyage-*) BEFORE migrating — else those collections fail server-side at embed time (HTTP 422). For a bge-768-only LOCAL service, voyage sources are cross-model re-embedded to bge locally (no Voyage anywhere) -> no gate needed. Code is ours; doable now. See NOTES for the full correction history (Hal caught the original premise error 2026-06-19).
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-06-19 (Hal caught the premise error): the original framing — 'cloud user must supply NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY on --service-url' — is WRONG. In service/cloud mode embedding is SERVER-SIDE (http_vector_client.py:476 'Embeddings are computed server-side; any embeddings argument is ignored'); the engine holds ONE operator Voyage key (squid-proxied), tenants metered per (tenant_id,tokens) via nexus-ehc4q. There is NO per-tenant Voyage key; a tenant supplies only NX_SERVICE_TOKEN, never a Voyage key. So the client-voyage-key gate does not apply.

THE REAL (server-aware) GATE: when detect_pending_migration's footprint contains voyage-model collections AND the target service is voyage-target (not a bge-only local service that cross-model-remaps them), assert the target /version reports voyage embedding capability (embedding_models includes voyage-*) BEFORE migrating — else those collections fail SERVER-SIDE at embed time (HTTP 422). This is a /version capability check, NOT a client key. For a bge-768-only LOCAL service, voyage source collections are cross-model re-embedded to bge locally (no Voyage anywhere) — no gate needed. Net: reframe from 'client voyage key' to 'target-service voyage-capability pre-flight'.

A phase-review gate cross-walks the RDR §Approach against what actually shipped (silent-scope-reduction defense, feedback_phase_closeout_scope_audit) and validates BOTH deployments before close.

Code-review-expert + test-validator are scope-blind by construction; this cross-walk is a DISTINCT reviewer step. Use the /conexus:phase-review-gate skill.

title: P1 — service-stamped markRetry (signature change) + backend-agnostic worker ladder
description:
WHY: With the schema + claim gate in place (P0), wire the dormant mark_retry primitive into a bounded exponential-backoff ladder. mark_retry exists end-to-end (AspectRepository.java:619, daemon allowlist t2_daemon.py:710, http_aspect_queue.py:214-219) but NO worker code invokes it. This phase changes a LIVE API contract (markRetry gains a parameter) and inserts a failure-classification decision in front of the worker's two terminal-fail call sites.

WHAT (TDD, test-first):
Java service:
1. Add `intervalSeconds: Long` parameter to markRetry (AspectRepository.java:615-624). Body computes `next_retry_at = OffsetDateTime.now(ZoneOffset.UTC).plusSeconds(intervalSeconds)` SERVER-SIDE. Do NOT accept an absolute client timestamp — server-side stamping is the clock-skew defense for cloud (worker host != DB host). markRetry also increments retry_count (already does) and resets status -> pending.
HTTP client:
2. Update http_aspect_queue.py:214-219 to POST {collection, source_path, interval_seconds}. Update the store contract (t2_store_contract / its RDR-158 successor) in lock-step.
SQLite stub (parity-only):
3. The doomed SQLite mark_retry (aspect_extraction_queue.py:461-478) must ACCEPT-AND-IGNORE the new interval_seconds param so the parity tripwire stays green until RDR-152 P4.2 deletes it. Do NOT fully implement the ladder in SQLite.
Python worker (src/nexus/aspect_worker.py, backend-agnostic):
4. Add `_is_retryable(exc)` reusing the retry.py:96-117 transient vocabulary (API overload/timeout, transient I/O, Voyage transients, sqlite3.OperationalError 'database is locked'). Non-retryable (ValueError, type errors, malformed records) -> terminal immediately.
5. Add `_mark_retry_or_fail_routed(row, exc)`: non-retryable -> terminal mark_failed; retry_count >= CAP (typed module-level constant, default 5) -> terminal mark_failed; else mark_retry with interval = base * 2**retry_count and ±20% jitter (reuse retry.py:147 pattern). The WORKER chooses the interval; the SERVICE stamps the absolute time.
6. The two exception sites — extract-raise (aspect_worker.py:491-499) and persist-raise (:538-545) — call _mark_retry_or_fail_routed instead of _mark_failed_routed. Route through t2_index_write (nexus-zir76 daemon-write contract; worker NEVER writes memory.db directly). Keep the broad except + structured log so a routing failure falls to reclaim_stale, not a dead worker thread (mirror _mark_failed_routed at :424-447).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- [ ] Java markRetry accepts intervalSeconds and stamps next_retry_at = now()+interval server-side; AspectRepositoryTest covers it.
- [ ] HTTP client posts interval_seconds; t2_store_contract updated; parity tripwire test_http_t2_store_parity.py green (SQLite stub accepts-and-ignores).
- [ ] Worker: retryable under cap -> pending + retry_count+1 + next_retry_at within the jittered interval (assert next_retry_at - claimed_at ≈ interval within tolerance); cap+1 -> failed; non-retryable -> failed immediate.
- [ ] _is_retryable classification unit-tested in isolation (transient set vs programming-bug set), no host-clock patch.
- [ ] Worker decision + interval selection unit-tested separately from the DB-clock stamping.
- [ ] uv run pytest tests/ -k aspect green; full mvn suite green (Java signature change).

DESIGN NOTES:
- ±20% jitter avoids thundering-herd re-claims when a wide outage clears and all backed-off rows become eligible at once — critical for cloud multi-worker (Open Questions RESOLVED).
- Cap is MAX ± 1 under concurrent reclaim BY DESIGN (non-atomic read-decide-increment). Monotonic retry_count guarantees termination; the cap prevents indefinite loops, not exactly-MAX.

- ExtractFail stays a deliberate terminal SKIP (:515) — not a failure, do not route to retry. Unsupported collections keep mark_done.

title: Wire aspect-queue mark_retry into a bounded backoff-retry ladder (dormant primitive -> live)
description: The aspect worker terminal-fails on the FIRST exception that escapes the extractor's 3 internal attempts (aspect_worker.py:498 extract-raise, :545 persist-raise -> _mark_failed_routed -> status='failed'). Sustained-transient classes (Claude API 529 overload window, daemon WAL-contention spike, brief network loss) thus permanently fail items needing manual re-enqueue. Meanwhile mark_retry already exists in aspect_extraction_queue.py (resets status='pending', increments retry_count), is in the daemon RPC allowlist (t2_daemon.py:710), and is exposed on the http client (http_aspect_queue.py:216) — but NO caller invokes it. Wire it: on a RETRYABLE failure class, route through mark_retry with a bounded attempt cap + exponential backoff (next_retry_at), falling to terminal mark_failed only after the cap. Keep mark_done for ExtractFail/unsupported (already correct) and keep mark_failed terminal for non-retryable (programming-bug) exceptions.
design: Add next_retry_at (and confirm retry_count) columns to aspect_extraction_queue via a T2 migration; claim_next WHERE adds 'AND (next_retry_at IS NULL OR next_retry_at <= now)'. Classify retryable vs non-retryable in the worker (transient: API overload/timeout/lock; non-retryable: ValueError/type/programming bugs). Backoff schedule a small constant ladder (e.g. 30s,2m,10m,30m,2h). DECISION NEEDED at planning: does changing drain semantics warrant an RDR? Likely yes (alters observable queue behavior + schema). Route writes through the daemon (nexus-zir76) — worker never writes memory.db directly.
acceptance_criteria: A retryable exception re-queues the row with retry_count incremented and is re-claimed after a backoff delay; after N attempts (default 5) it goes terminal 'failed'. A non-retryable exception goes terminal immediately (no wasted retries). claim_next honors next_retry_at (does not re-claim before the delay elapses). Deterministic test (fixed clock, seeded) covers: retryable->retry->...->terminal, non-retryable->immediate-terminal, backoff timing, and crash-during-retry reclaim. Full unit suite green.

title: [epic] Harden async/queue processing — aspect-extraction retry ladder + MinerU OOM resilience
description: The aspect-extraction queue and MinerU PDF pipeline are PARTIALLY HARDENED. Verified state (2026-06-19, nexus instance investigation on develop): the aspect queue does NOT wedge or retry-forever (worker exception paths call mark_failed -> terminal 'failed'; claim_next only takes 'pending', so poison items fail out and stop blocking; reclaim_stale leases in_progress rows back after 300s — crash recovery is solid; nx doctor --check-aspect-queue gives visibility). The REAL gaps: (1) disposition is binary success|terminal-failed — anything outliving the extractor's 3 quick internal attempts (sustained Claude API 529 overload, daemon WAL-contention spike) terminal-fails with MANUAL-only re-enqueue; (2) mark_retry is a DORMANT primitive — defined + daemon-RPC-exposed (t2_daemon.py:710) + http-client-exposed (http_aspect_queue.py:216) but called by NOTHING; the retry-with-requeue ladder exists and is simply unwired; (3) no bulk failed-row recovery CLI. MinerU is the weaker subsystem: no memory guard before subprocess spawn (relies on OS OOM killer), whole-doc fail on per-page -9 SIGKILL, no per-page timeout. This epic groups the hardening work. title: Cloud engine: Voyage HttpClient ignores egress proxy (api.voyageai.com 30s timeout) — set proxy from env
description: conexus-001: STEP-6 voyage embed probe times out. VoyageEmbedder/CceEmbedder build java.net.http.HttpClient.newBuilder().build() with NO .proxy(), which ignores https.proxyHost system properties entirely (JVM AND native). The cloud deploy's IaC set the proxy via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Dhttps.proxyHost on the false premise that the client uses the default ProxySelector — it does not, so api.voyageai.com is hit directly and the private (no-NAT) subnet 30s-timeouts. native-image additionally ignores JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS. title: Reusable native-service build profile + published artifacts for conexus (and any) consumer
description:
Owner ask 2026-06-15: expose a build PROFILE that the conexus build (or anyone) can run to build the nexus native Java service FROM OUR SOURCE, tuned for their habitat (api.conexus-nexus.com multi-tenant cloud), and publish the resulting artifacts so consumers can either build-from-source or pull prebuilt.

Distinct from nexus-vwvv5.6 (RDR-157 P2.1), which builds OUR 3 desktop-target native binaries (linux-amd64/aarch64/mac-arm64) and attaches them to GH Releases + sha256 manifest. THIS bead is the consumer-runnable angle:
(1) A documented, stable build entrypoint/profile (e.g. a Maven profile like -Pnative-service or a make/CI target in service/) that an external pipeline invokes to produce the native service for a server habitat — not just our release matrix. Tuned-for-habitat knobs: target triple, managed-PG (no embedded), multi-tenant config surface.
(2) A publish channel for that artifact consumable by conexus (container image to a registry? maven artifact? the native binary as a release asset reused?). Decide the contract.
(3) The cloud DISTRIBUTION variant (RDR-157: native binary, no embedded DB, skip-provision + validate-remote) is the thing conexus runs; ensure the profile produces exactly that.

Build mechanism lives in nexus-ykrhb (native-image productionization) + service/pom.xml native profiles. Likely wants a short planning/RDR pass (build-profile design + publish-channel contract + consumer hand-off) rather than ad-hoc, since it spans repos (engine produces, conexus consumes). Cross-ref RDR-157 P2, conexus RDR-001.
acceptance_criteria: A documented build profile any consumer (incl. conexus CI) can run to produce the native nexus service for a server/cloud habitat; the cloud-distribution variant (no embedded DB) is produced by it; artifacts published on a defined channel with provenance; conexus RDR-001 can consume without bespoke build glue.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met + validated. (1) Build profile: service/pom.xml -Pnative + -Pprebuilt-jooq, runnable by any consumer (jOOQ codegen decoupled, nexus-f6j31). (2) Publish channel: engine-service-v0.0.1 GH Release with nexus-service-linux-amd64 + .sha256 provenance (channel separate from conexus PyPI vX.Y.Z; does not trip the RDR-155 P4a release boundary). (3) Cloud variant: binary runs no-embedded-DB against managed PG via NX_DB_URL, skips pg_provision. (4) conexus consumes without bespoke glue: deploy/engine/build-image.sh builds FROM the published binary (conexus #59/#60); first producer->consumer cycle validated (image smoke PASS, 102 changesets, app_version 0.0.1). Contract chosen: pull-prebuilt (conexus builds from published binary, not forked source); build-from-source path remains available via public Maven profiles. title: RDR-157 P3: make pg_provision relocation-aware (pg_config paths are build-prefix-bound)
description: CODE CHANGE (not packaging). check_pgvector_available (src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py ~L203-241) resolves vector.control via 'pg_config --sharedir', which reports the build-time absolute prefix. For a from-source Strategy-B bundle (RDR-157 CA-3/RF-157-9) extracted to a user-local path, pg_config returns the CI build prefix (nonexistent on the user machine), so the preflight wrongly reports pgvector ABSENT and first-run aborts. This is the principal first-run blocker for the LOCAL distribution. Audit every pg_config-derived path in pg_provision (sharedir, pkglibdir) and make them relocation-aware: resolve relative to the binary location (PG find_my_exec semantics) OR pin a fixed runtime extract prefix agreed at configure time OR a pg_config path-rewrite shim. MUST land before the P3 local-distro first-run E2E (nexus-vwvv5.18) is declared green. Surfaced by substantive-critic re-review of PR #1188 (S1).
acceptance_criteria: pg_provision resolves pgvector/extension paths correctly when the bundle is extracted to a path != its build prefix; a relocated-bundle test proves check_pgvector_available passes and CREATE EXTENSION works from the moved location.

title: pg_provision: nx init --service fails on Debian/Ubuntu — Unix socket lock in postgres-owned /var/run/postgresql
description: The migration dress-rehearsal harness (tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal) surfaced a real provisioning bug. _start_cluster() omits '-k <pgdata>' from pg_ctl believing that disables the Unix socket, but PostgreSQL still listens on a socket using the config-default unix_socket_directories. On Debian/PGDG that default is /var/run/postgresql (owned postgres:postgres), so a non-postgres OS user running 'nx init --service' fails: FATAL could not create lock file /var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.<port>.lock: Permission denied. Masked on macOS where the default is writable /tmp. Breaks the dominant Linux install base (pebfx install story / nexus-luxe6). Fix: _configure_cluster writes unix_socket_directories='' to postgresql.conf — matches the existing TCP-only intent (listen_addresses=127.0.0.1; all clients use -h 127.0.0.1) and also resolves the macOS 104-char socket-path concern that motivated dropping -k.
notes: FIXED in PR #1184 (develop). _configure_cluster writes unix_socket_directories=''; BEGIN/END sentinel idempotency; unconditional call self-heals existing stopped clusters. 6 unit tests. Validated end-to-end (both ONNX + Voyage legs) by tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged to develop in PR #1184 (merge commit on develop). unix_socket_directories='' + sentinel idempotency + unconditional self-heal; 6 unit tests; validated end-to-end by tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal (both ONNX + Voyage legs).

title: Sweep: wire stale-port lease-recovery into the 9 remaining resolve-once HTTP stores (om64x follow-on)
description: nexus-om64x fixed the two FATAL paths (http_token_store session-mint, http_scratch_store T1) with connection-failure → recover_endpoint_from_lease → rebind+retry-once (catching ConnectError + RemoteProtocolError + ReadError). The other long-lived service-backed stores resolve ONCE at construction and hold a long-lived httpx.Client, so they carry the SAME stale-port failure after a supervisor restart (degraded, not FATAL — user can retry): http_memory_store, http_taxonomy_store, http_plan_library, http_aspect_queue, http_chash_index, http_document_aspects_store, http_centroid_store, http_telemetry_store, http_document_highlights_store (and verify http_catalog_client). FIX: factor the rebind+retry scaffolding into a SHARED helper (per CLAUDE.md daemon-lifecycle shared-primitive rule — recover_endpoint_from_lease already shared; the catch+rebind+retry wrapper should be too, to avoid a third/Nth divergent copy across token/scratch/vector clients) and wire all 9. Consider also closing the om64x Phase-1 restart-window residual (old lease lingers ~TTL on SIGTERM; new lease publishes after JVM ready) via a bounded backoff or a relinquish-on-stop. Origin: om64x P5-gate review (substantive-critic Sig 2/3, 2026-06-14).
notes:
DEFERRED FROM nexus-bikit.3 review (substantive-critic Significant finding, round 1): RefreshableHttpStoreMixin's _post retry-on-failure assumes every caller's POST is idempotent (documented in the mixin's docstring/comments, not enforced). Before/during this adoption sweep, grep-audit each of the 9 target classes' POST call sites to confirm every one is genuinely idempotent (upsert/insert-with-conflict-handling, delete-by-id) -- if any non-idempotent POST is found, either exclude that specific call site from the mixin or add an explicit per-call idempotent=False opt-out to the mixin (not designed speculatively in bikit.3 since no concrete non-idempotent consumer exists yet -- YAGNI).
OBSERVATIONS from nexus-bikit.4 review (substantive-critic, non-blocking, worth addressing during this sweep):
1. Bypass-guard test scaling: each adopter must author its OWN scripted grep-based bypass-guard test (tests/db/test_http_memory_store_selfheal.py's TestNoBypassOfMixinTransport is the pattern to copy) -- there is no shared/automatic mechanism, remember it per adopter.
2. Bypass-guard regex hardening: the current pattern (self\._client\.(get|post|put|delete|patch|request)\() omits httpx.Client's .stream(/.send(/.build_request( and requires the verb token on the same physical line as self._client. -- not exploited today (grep confirms zero uses of those methods across the 9 not-yet-adopted stores) but worth tightening once if any adopter's code uses those methods.
3. Empty-body handling: _refreshable_client.py's _request_once now returns None for any 200-with-empty-body response (added for HttpMemoryStore.merge_memories's 204). Unverified whether any list-returning endpoint across the other 8 stores could receive a 200+empty-body response from the Java service (would silently return None instead of [], breaking a for-loop caller with TypeError) -- not confirmed as a live bug, but worth a quick check per-adopter.
close_reason: Adoption sweep complete; credential-staleness pattern closed via one shared, tested, twice-reviewed abstraction (RefreshableHttpStoreMixin, src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py). All 9 originally-scoped stores plus HttpCatalogClient (added mid-plan) adopted across batches A (nexus-f2qvx.1), B (nexus-f2qvx.2), C (nexus-f2qvx.3), gated by nexus-f2qvx.4's final combined-diff review. Decision persisted: T3 store title=decision-refreshable-http-store-mixin, T2 memory project=nexus title=refreshable-http-store-mixin-shipped. Full unit suite green throughout (12853 passed, 0 failed at final gate).

title: hybridSearch collapses on selective text gates — needs text-first two-phase plan
description: Found by the conexus RDR-001 production gate (2026-06-12, cloud corpus 116k chunks_1024 rows; conexus-1az). hybridSearch runs ONE query: HNSW ORDER BY embedding + iterative_scan=relaxed_order with the text gate as a scan filter. For SELECTIVE gates this collapses: a gate with ~6 text matches ranks deeper than hnsw.max_scan_tuples (20k default) from the query vector, so the endpoint returns 0 rows. Measured budget sweep (t3.small unlimited, Crunchy): 40k->4 rows/34s, 80k->6 rows/95s, 200k->6 rows/140s — full recall costs ~95s, past every HTTP timeout. A text-index-first plan (GIN bitmap on chunk_tsv/trgm, then order the gated set by distance) answers in ms — verified by hand (bare text-gate COUNT is instant). The SAME query against a LOCAL engine returns 6 at default budget by HNSW-graph luck (different insertion order) — which is how the cross-deployment gate caught it. Fix belongs in PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch (two-phase, or planner-aware dispatch on gate selectivity).
acceptance_criteria: hybridSearch returns the complete text-gate-matched top-k for selective gates (pathological case: 6/6) within interactive latency (<2s) at default GUCs, on both local and cloud deployments. Mirrors conexus-1az.
close_reason: Merged to develop via PR #1178 (branch synced with develop, CI CLEAN/green, plain --merge). Selectivity-aware text-first dispatch in hybridSearch; 2-round stacked review clean; residuals (non-selective 2x GIN, semi-selective far-clustered window) flagged on-bead for the conexus xr7.8.9 gate.

Scope = minimal two-phase / text-index-first plan: GIN bitmap on chunk_tsv/trgm to get the gated set, then ORDER BY embedding distance over that set (ms latency) — does NOT require the full server-side RRF fusion and does NOT share P5.2's conexus-xr7.8.9 world-block. P5.2 SUPERSEDES this eventually (RRF subsumes the two-phase dispatch), but shipping the targeted fix first is correct: the conexus production-scale hybrid-parity gate is blocked on it today (not live-tenant traffic — conexus is pre-cutover, so urgent-but-not-a-fire). Keep P1, keep independent. When P5.2 lands, its parity gate VERIFIES the selective-gate case (6/6, <2s at default GUCs, cloud 116k) rather than OWNING the fix.

Two follow-on items for the conexus xr7.8.9 production gate to verify (substantive-critic round 2): (1) the NON-SELECTIVE path now pays a 2x GIN gate evaluation (COUNT probe + scan filter) — verify it still meets <2s at default GUCs, not only the 6/116k selective case; (2) RESIDUAL semi-selective window — a gate matching count in (5000, hnsw.max_scan_tuples] whose matches all cluster FAR from the query vector can still under-return on the HNSW-first branch (same geometry as the original bug, narrower window). P5.2 RRF fusion closes it; until then the gate should probe a semi-selective far-clustered case. Both Criticals from review round 1 (non-selective work_mem spill; phantom test ref) resolved.

title: RDR-156 P4 follow-on: full query() repoint onto combined-query shapes (output re-hydration + chunk_text_hash preservation)
description: Repoint the query() MCP tool's ENTIRE catalog dance onto the combined-query SQL functions (metadata-scoped + graph-hop + subtree/where coverage), so search_cross_corpus + app-side group-by-doc is no longer used for the catalog-param path. Keep a dance FALLBACK for local/Chroma mode + catalog-absent. Accept the collection-granular→doc-granular content_type precision change. notes: PLAN-AUDIT conditions (2026-06-14, PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS) — RESOLVE before landing: (HIGH-1) chunk_text_hash must be the MATCHED CHUNK's chash returned BY the function (add chash output column to the combined fns, houg9/889ff), NOT a per-doc manifest guess — a guess corrupts RDR-086 citations. (HIGH-2) fallback-vs-delete contradiction: rzqto-keeps-local/Chroma-fallback conflicts with 2bqpn-deletes-dance. Resolve: is there still a local/Chroma query() path post-RDR-155 (Chroma retired from serving P4a)? If service is the only T3 path, NO fallback needed → 2bqpn fully deletes. If a local path remains, 2bqpn deletes only the service stitch. Decide explicitly. Output re-hydration (title/bib/chunk_count per tumbler) + dual-path as planned.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: HIGH-2 RESOLVED (2026-06-14): a local/Chroma query() path DOES still exist (tests + pre-migration users; develop unreleasable until the service-stack install story ships, so local mode is not yet retired). The combined-query functions are service-only (is_service_backed gate). DECISION: rzqto adds a SERVICE-MODE branch (is_service_backed + has_catalog_params + catalog present → combined functions + per-tumbler re-hydration) and KEEPS the existing dance + search_cross_corpus as the fallback for local/Chroma mode, catalog-absent, and the non-catalog-param corpus path. Therefore 2bqpn deletes ONLY the service-mode stitch that rzqto replaces (the catalog-dance branch when service-backed), NOT the whole dance — the local fallback stays until local-mode T3 is retired. title: RDR-156 P4 follow-on: subtree + where + substring-author coverage in metadata-scoped combined query
description: Extend the combined metadata-scoped query to cover the remaining query()-dance cases so query() can fully collapse: (1) subtree — tumbler-prefix predicate (WHERE d.tumbler LIKE p_subtree||'.%' or a tumbler-range); (2) where — arbitrary catalog metadata predicates (bib_year>=, tags=, etc.) pushed into the join WHERE; (3) author substring/case-insensitive — query() uses author.lower() IN (r.author or '').lower() (substring ILIKE), but search_metadata_scoped_<dim> does exact d.author=p_author — switch to ILIKE '%'||p_author||'%' or add a match-mode arg to preserve query() semantics (exact would silently regress 'Hildebrand' vs 'Hal Hildebrand'). Either extend search_metadata_scoped_<dim> signature (add p_subtree, p_where/jsonb, author match-mode) or add sibling functions. TDD RED + parity. Needed before the full query() repoint (the C bead).
notes: PLAN-AUDIT (2026-06-14): (HIGH, shared) the combined metadata-scoped function output MUST include the MATCHED CHUNK's chash column — required by rzqto for the structured chunk_text_hash contract (RDR-086/nx_answer). The currently-shipped search_metadata_scoped_<dim> returns only id=tumbler/content/distance/collection; this bead (or rzqto) must add the matched-chunk chash. subtree=prefix predicate, where=catalog predicates, author=ILIKE substring as planned.
close_reason: Merged to develop via PR #1179. catalog-008 extends search_metadata_scoped_<dim> with subtree (root-exclusive tumbler-prefix), where (jsonb equality containment, comparison ops rejected loudly), author ILIKE substring, alias_of filter, and matched-chunk chash output. Full stack + tests. Stacked review 2 rounds: 2 Critical (subtree root-inclusion divergence; where range silent-corruption) + 1 Significant (alias rows) all fixed; substantive-critic verdict justified. S2/M1/corpus documented as rzqto-facing notes. Unblocks rzqto.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REVIEW ROUND 1 (substantive-critic) — 2 Critical + 2 Significant, fixed/documented:
- C1 FIXED: subtree was root-INCLUSIVE (d.tumbler=p_subtree OR LIKE prefix.%), diverging from query()'s cat.descendants() which is root-EXCLUSIVE. Changed SQL to LIKE prefix||'.%' only. Test now asserts root 1.2 EXCLUDED.
- C2 FIXED: core.py where parser used raw split('=') → 'bib_year>=2020' became bogus key 'bib_year>' → JSONB matched nothing → filter silently dropped. Now uses parse_where_str; rejects comparison ops (>=,<=,>,<,!=) with a loud Error (equality-only). +tests (range rejected, numeric typed).
- S1 FIXED: added AND d.alias_of='' to all 3 funcs (+ catalog-006 had the same gap) so the function never returns alias tumblers (query() dereferences via resolve(follow_alias)).
RZQTO-FACING NOTES (documented divergences, NOT bugs — rzqto decides):
- S2: subtree+author — query() treats them as MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (subtree wins, author ignored); the SQL ANDs them (more capable). rzqto should not pass both if it must match query() exactly, or accept the additive behavior.
- M1: author ILIKE treats % and _ in the author value as wildcards (query()'s Python substring is literal). Theoretical for author names; rzqto/docs should note or escape if a literal % is ever needed.
- corpus: SQL p_corpus is an exact catalog-column filter; query() uses corpus for COLLECTION ROUTING (p_collections already handles that). rzqto should NOT pass corpus as the catalog filter naively.

STAGE 2 BLAST RADIUS MEASURED 2026-07-28 — probe reverted, nothing deleted, src/
clean. Method: forced storage_backend_for() to always return SERVICE (the
post-Stage-2 world, where every SQLite `else` branch is unreachable) and ran the
full suite. Same lever-flip shape as Stage 1b.

RESULT: 430 failed / 45 errors / 13,037 passed across 96 FILES (21:58).
For scale, Stage 1b's equivalent probe was 5 failures in 1 file. This is a
different order of magnitude and should be planned as such.

DOMINANT CAUSES, by signature count — the shape matters more than the total:

  116  sqlite3.OperationalError: attempt to write a readonly database
        NOT the T2 stores. This is the RDR-176 frozen-migration-source guard:
        Catalog forces read_only=True when storage_backend_for("catalog") is
        SERVICE and the file exists. Every test that inits a LOCAL catalog and
        writes to it hits this. These belong to the rich-Catalog deletion, not
        the T2-store deletion.
   64  httpx/httpcore UnsupportedProtocol: URL missing a protocol
        Tests that got an Http* twin where they expected a SQLite store, with no
        service endpoint configured. Fixture-shaped, not behavioural.
   25  AttributeError: "<Http*Store> is service-backed and has no raw SQLite
        'conn'" — RawHandleGuardMixin firing on the raw reach-ins.
   22  T2EnsureOutcome.SERVICE_MODE_SKIP — the T2 daemon refusing to start in
        service mode. Whole daemon stack is on the DELETE list.
   15  CLI verbs printing the "Service mode: the local SQL..." refusal.

THE USEFUL FINDING IS A DECOMPOSITION, not the number. The 96 files split by
SUBSYSTEM, and the subsystems are independently deletable:

  A. the 10 T2 store classes + t2/__init__ factory + storage_mode
  B. the T2 DAEMON stack (daemon/test_t2_*, rdr146_fairness, rdr151_* — the
     22-count SERVICE_MODE_SKIP cohort)
  C. the RICH SQLITE CATALOG stack (test_catalog_* — the 116-count readonly
     cohort; .catalog.db, Catalog, catalog_db, catalog_owners, catalog_sync,
     catalog_write_shim)
  D. verb-level casualties (plan repair, plan cmd, migration verbs)

Roughly half the 96 files test a subject that is ITSELF on the DELETE list, so
their tests die with their code rather than needing a port. The other half needs
individual triage and will NOT all be real work either — several (aspect
promotion, the daemon reclaim tests) also die.

RECOMMENDATION: land Stage 2 as SUB-STAGES BY SUBSYSTEM (B, then C, then A),
each independently green, rather than one 430-failure cutover. A/B/C are
separable because their test cohorts are disjoint by cause, which the signature
breakdown above demonstrates rather than assumes. A single big-bang Stage 2
would mean triaging 430 failures with no green checkpoint in between — the
condition under which real coverage loss gets waved through as "expected".

NOT YET DONE: per-file triage of the ~48 surviving-subject files. That is the
next measurement, and it should happen per sub-stage rather than all at once.

C-STORE PORT: REACH-IN COUNT FAILED AS A COST PREDICTOR (2026-07-29).

Recorded because the estimate it produced is in this bead's earlier comment and
should not be trusted.

I ranked the remaining local_catalog_backend files by private-reach-in count
(._db / ._projector / _append_jsonl / CatalogDB) and predicted:

  LOW  reach-in  = substrate USER        = ports mechanically
and from that split estimated ~349 die / ~292 port.

BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG, measured not guessed:

- test_catalog_manifest_read_api.py had the 2nd-highest reach-in count (37) and
  PORTED — 43 of 46 green against the live service catalog. Its reach-ins were
  test-data SEEDING funnelled through two helpers, not assertions about SQLite.

- The eight files with ZERO reach-ins were unpinned as a batch: 34 passed, 25
  FAILED, and exactly ONE (test_taxonomy_discover_no_reembed, 3 tests) was
  cleanly green. Several fail for the right reason — their subject is named in
  the test: TestSqliteBranchDetectsARealDanglingRow,
  test_register_or_lookup_sqlite_mode_still_auto_inits,
  ..._forwards_blank_doc_id_when_no_catalog. test_catalog_backup_and_safety
  fails 14/14 because backup snapshots live in the LOCAL `.deleted-backups/`
  dir reached via `cat._dir`.

WHY: reach-in count measures how a test SEEDS. Portability is decided by
whether the test's SUBJECT exists service-side. Those are independent. A test
can seed with raw SQL and assert a service-capable contract (ports), or seed
through the public API and assert a SQLite-only behaviour (dies).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING 28 FILES: classify per file on SUBJECT, by
reading it. There is no cheap proxy. The batch-unpin-and-see approach is fine
as a PROBE (it costs one command and the failures are informative) but its
output is a worklist, not a port.

comments.text:
DIE/PORT SPLIT REFINED — and the largest remaining disposition needs a ruling.

=== THE "CHEAP WINS" WERE NOT PORTS ===

I planned to take test_t3_gc (1 pin) and test_doc_indexer (2 pins) as quick
ports. All three are DIE-SET:

  test_t3_gc::test_gc_aborts_on_uninitialized_catalog — guard is
    `make_catalog_reader() is None`; the factory never returns None in service
    mode, so the guard is dead code once local mode goes. The test's own
    docstring already says the premise is UNREPRESENTABLE there and files the
    resulting service-arm gap as nexus-jqrtp (P1, open) — a DESTRUCTIVE command
    losing its last-line-of-defence guard on the surviving substrate.
  test_doc_indexer::..._auto_inits_catalog_when_absent... — premise is an
    ABSENT catalog. Same unrepresentability.
  test_doc_indexer::..._preflight_registration_idempotent_on_staleness_skip —
    asserts no duplicate DocumentRegistered event in events.jsonl. Local log.

So there is NO cheap port work left. Everything remaining is either die-set or
one of the three large module-pinned files.

=== NEEDS A RULING: test_indexer.py, 92 tests ===

Largest single disposition left in C-store. Its pin annotation is unusually
good and every factual claim in it VERIFIES:

  - It is a LOCAL-MODE indexing journey end to end: `_patches` stubs
    nexus.config.load_config with _DEFAULT_CONFIG and get_credential with a
    fake, and an autouse fixture pins vectors to chroma. A stubbed config
    carries no service_url, so under the engine substrate
    `_prune_deleted_files` -> `chashes_for_collection` reached
    HttpCatalogClient with an EMPTY base_url and died on
    httpx.UnsupportedProtocol — which reads as broken endpoint resolution
    rather than a missing pin.
  - It claims the service-mode indexer->catalog journey is covered elsewhere,
    and it is: tests/test_catalog_indexer_hook.py has exactly 33 tests, ZERO
    pins, driving the hook through ActiveCatalog; the specific failing call has
    direct coverage at test_http_catalog_client.py::test_chashes_for_collection
    plus a shape_parity_tripwire entry asserting both implementations agree.
    (I verified all four counts rather than trusting the comment.)
  - Same disposition already applied to test_catalog_e2e (commit f4030fe5).

THE QUESTION: after i711w the catalog is service-backed in BOTH local and
service DEPLOYMENT modes, so "local-mode indexing journey with a local catalog"
ceases to exist as a configuration — which argues die-set. But the file's
subject is indexer.py itself (status transitions, error paths, credential skip,
hidden-file filter), and the 33 hook tests cover the catalog HOOK, not those
indexer behaviours. So it is NOT a clean die: some fraction of the 92 may be
the only coverage of indexer paths that have no service-path equivalent.

Deleting 92 tests on the strength of "the journey is gone" without auditing
which of them test the JOURNEY vs the INDEXER is exactly the silent-scope-
reduction class the phase-review-gate exists to catch. Not deciding it
unilaterally. The same question applies to test_indexer_e2e (26) and
test_collection_name_migration (12).

RECOMMENDED next step if this is picked up: classify the 92 by whether the
assertion is about the local catalog/config or about indexer.py, then port the
latter group onto a config that HAS a service_url and delete only the former.

=== ⚠️ SCOPE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE PLAN ===

29 test files import nexus.catalog.event_log / projector / catalog_db /
nexus.db.t2.catalog. ONLY 7 are in the pinned cohort. The other ~22 are
currently GREEN and UNPINNED and will fail AT COLLECTION the moment those

The pinned cohort measures which tests are PINNED, never which will BREAK. Every
count I have put on this bead — including the "authoritative" AST one — measured
the wrong set. The Stage-2 sweep is materially wider than the cohort.
ACTION: before the src-deletion commit, enumerate importers of the dying modules
and disposition those too. `rdr101_round3` is the visible instance: it is
whole-file DELETE (14 tests), not the 4-of-14 excision I recorded, because its
module-level imports die.

=== FIVE SOLE-COVERAGE RISKS — PORT THESE, do not delete ===

1. register_owner duplicate-suppression cardinality
   (incremental_rebuild::test_double_apply_idempotency_owner_registered).
   Nothing else repo-wide asserts that a repeated identical register_owner does
   not grow the owner set. Other COUNT(*) FROM owners sites assert a DIFFERENT
   property and are themselves dying. Without it nothing pins that the client's
   /owners/upsert actually reaches the server's UNIQUE constraint.
2. head_hash survives an idempotent ensure_owner_for_repo
   (owners_head_hash::..._idempotent_call). Only assertion of this repo-wide;
   all three APIs survive service-side. The integration test checks the tumbler,
   never head_hash.
3. set_owner_head_hash returns 0 on a MISS (owners_head_hash::..._rowcount).
   The HIT half is covered service-side; the MISS half is not, and indexer.py's
   lost-write warning keys on exactly that zero.
4. owner_tumblers_by_name returns [] on miss
   (decomposition_contracts::test_owner_lookups_relocated_to_owner_ops, second
   half). Shape-parity covers non-empty only.
5. supersede_collection SEMANTICS — NO service-side test exists. The only one
   asserts `result is None` (wire shape). Every semantic assertion is in a dying
   local file. Make this a Stage-2 EXIT CRITERION.

=== PRODUCT DEFECTS FOUND, VERIFIED IN SOURCE, NOW FILED ===

- nexus-cecqy (P1): service-mode rename DELETEs the old collection row
  (renameCollectionTxn step 3 — FKs are ON UPDATE NO ACTION), then the CLI's
  supersede_collection UPDATEs 0 rows and discards the count, and the CLI still
  echoes "Emitted CollectionSuperseded". Old name ends ABSENT, not superseded.
  Includes a second defect: --allow-legacy does not set legacy_grandfathered in
  service mode (no server inference; CLI passes no kwarg). One-line client fix.
- nexus-ai41v (P1): HttpCatalogClient.link_audit is `return {}` while
  `nx catalog link-audit` and MCP catalog_link_audit both ship. Empty reads as
  clean. Blocks the 3 UNCERTAINs.

=== THE T3-RENAME DIAGNOSIS I FAILED AT, ANSWERED ===

rename_collection_data_plane branches on the CATALOG backend
(collection_rename.py:124), not the vector backend. In service mode it POSTs
/collections/rename and RETURNS at :154 — `t3_db.rename_collection` at :192 is
never reached, BY DESIGN, and that is already pinned by
test_collection_rename_service_mode.py:78 (`assert_not_called`). My port failed
because the test asserts against an INJECTED in-memory Chroma the engine has
never heard of. Fix: stop patching nexus.db.make_t3 in the happy-path tests and
observe the service store. The guard-only tests can keep the injected handle
because no rename executes in them.
Knock-on worth its own bead: post-i711w the entire LOCAL fan-out branch
(:156-206) becomes unreachable, so a catalog=service + vectors=chroma deployment
can never rename its Chroma collection.

FakeCatalogHandler, not a real engine — it asserts WIRE FORMAT, not behaviour. The real
PG-backed suite is tests/db/test_http_catalog_integration.py.

This matters because a DIE call justified by "the behaviour is covered service-side" is
only sound if the citation is the INTEGRATION suite. sweep-A cross-checked both and is
clean. sweep-B justified DIE calls by "the METHOD EXISTS on HttpCatalogClient" — method
existence is weaker than behavioural coverage, so B's 31 DIE calls carry residual risk.
B's files are SQLite schema mechanics (PRAGMA table_info, ALTER-on-open, raw _conn SQL)
and I independently verified test_catalog_owners_head_hash.py myself — all 4 genuinely
die. But before the deletion commit, re-check B's other three files against the
INTEGRATION suite rather than the method list.

RULE for the rest of this arc: inspect the FIXTURE, not the filename, before ruling a
behaviour already covered.

=== §3 TWO LOCKED HANDOFF ITEMS OVERTURNED ===

(1) test_t3_gc is NOT die-set. Handoff item 3 recorded "ONE pinned test, die-set, and
    swapping the shared fixture converted a 1-test job into a 19-test blast radius,"
    which frames the blast radius as a fixture-wiring accident. It is not. The imports
    are MODULE-LEVEL — tests/test_t3_gc.py:31 (Catalog) and :32 (EVENTS_FILENAME,

    The 2 DIE: test_gc_aborts_on_uninitialized_catalog (premise unrepresentable; its
    service-mode gap already filed as nexus-jqrtp) and
    test_gc_emits_chunk_orphaned_event_before_delete — verified in PRODUCTION source:

    is nothing to port the assertion to. Its other assertions are redundant with
    test_gc_paginates_above_300_chunk_boundary and
    test_delete_by_chunk_ids_deletes_only_listed, so nothing unique is lost.

(2) test_rdr101_round3_correctness whole-file DELETE is OVERTURNED. Module-level imports
    at lines 37-40 do die, so the file cannot collect as-is — that half was right. But

    deleting them.

    against the pinned cohort nor dropped between the two sweeps.

which reads the legacy .catalog.db through raw PARAMETERIZED ATTACH (migrations.py:1547-1555)

⚠️ THE IMPORTER SWEEP'S OWN SCOPE WAS UNDERSTATED — BY THE SAME ERROR IT WAS CREATED TO FIX.

The five port commits (085009fe, 1f6d0b89, 0c9a0e97, b234142a, f58430dd) are sound and land
as described. What is wrong is the SET they were computed over.

MY ERROR. The sweep inherited the handoff's grep — four modules:
  nexus.catalog.event_log / nexus.catalog.projector / nexus.catalog.catalog_db /
  nexus.db.t2.catalog
and I never checked whether that was the complete dying set. It is not. It OMITS
`nexus.catalog.catalog` — the module defining the local `Catalog` class itself, i.e. the
primary subject of the whole deletion — and `nexus.catalog.events`. I added both to the
dying set later, in the port briefs, without going back to re-measure the scope they implied.

This is precisely the failure the sweep exists to correct, one level up. The C-store
classification measured the PINNED cohort and missed the importers; the importer sweep
measured FOUR of SIX dying modules and missed the rest. Same shape: an inherited
enumeration trusted without verification.

RE-MEASURED, module-level imports only (function-local imports are NOT a collection hazard):

  Full dying set (6 modules):        85 files, 1278 tests
    in my 28-file narrow sweep:      13
    touching local_catalog_backend:  13
    NEITHER swept NOR pinned:        63 files, 1009 tests

And the hazard is NOT mechanically fixable: 79 of the 85 import `Catalog` — the dying class —
not a relocatable type. Exactly ONE newly-discovered file imports only types. So the
types-relocation work (nexus-37f4v) will not absorb this; it is a separate problem.

⚠️ BUT DO NOT READ 63 FILES / 1009 TESTS AS THE WORKLOAD. A module-level dying import is
harmless in a file that DIES ENTIRELY — the file is deleted in the same commit as the src, so
it never gets a chance to fail at collection. The hazard is only files that SURVIVE, wholly or
partly, while carrying one. Several of the 63 are already-ported suites from earlier sessions
(manifest_read_api 46, remediate_paths 29, link_generator 19, backfill 18, prune_stale 17,
backup_and_safety 14 — all in the ~190 previously ported) whose module-level `Catalog` import
most likely survives only to serve a local fixture for their DIE subset; making that import
function-local is a one-line fix per file, the same de-hostage move used in 1f6d0b89.

SO THE NEXT ENTRY-POINT TASK, before any more ports: split those 63 into
  (a) DIES ENTIRELY -> module-level import is fine, no action, retires with the src
  (b) SURVIVES wholly or partly -> the import must go function-local or be re-pointed
and do (b). Do NOT re-classify all 1009 tests — the disposition needed here is per FILE
(survives at all / does not), which is far cheaper than the per-test PORT/DIE/GAP work.
The per-test classification only matters for files already known to survive.

METHOD CORRECTION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the scope query is
  "module-level imports of the COMPLETE dying module set, in files that survive"
NOT "importers of the modules someone previously listed", and NOT the pinned cohort. Derive
the dying module set from the deletion plan itself and assert it, rather than inheriting a
grep. All three measurements on this arc have been wrong in the same direction, each time
because the enumeration was inherited rather than re-derived.

Also worth noting for the deletion commit: the same class of error applies to SYMBOLS, not
just modules — see nexus-npywj (make_relative, six live importers, all function-local so
nothing catches it) and nexus-37f4v (CatalogEntry/CatalogLink defined in the dying module and
imported by the surviving service client). The deletion list was assembled from modules; the
things that break are symbols.

comments.text:
ADOPTION-WINDOW GATE MOVED — Hal decision, 2026-07-28, four days ahead of the 2026-08-01 floor.

WHAT THE GATE WAS, so the record is not softened: "NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite is currently the ONLY thing keeping those installs functional — deleting it before they migrate hard-strands their T2 data." That is a third party's data, not an internal invariant. The 2026-07-11 sign-off set an explicit calendar floor of 2026-08-01 derived as 3 weeks from the 6.5.2 release, the release carrying BOTH storage paths plus the bundled migration tool. The bd --defer that enforced it mechanically was removed 2026-07-26, leaving the constraint prose-only — so nothing but this note stood between an ordinary merge and stranding a user.

THE CLAUSE THAT GOVERNS AN EARLY LAND, verbatim from the description: "Adjustable ONLY if better-informed evidence emerges (e.g. explicit confirmation from the GH#1381 external collaborator stevengharris that migration completed)."

THE EVIDENCE, checked rather than assumed:
- GH #1381 ("Upgrade from 5 to 6 fails to complete") is CLOSED.
- GH #1419, stevengharris's own postmortem, shows him running conexus 6.16.0 against a POSTGRES engine: he reports restart-stale failing to converge an engine from v0.1.49 to the v0.1.51 his 6.16.0 install requires; he recovers by pg_dump and queries nexus.catalog_documents / nexus.catalog_links directly; and he describes the legacy Chroma store as a BACKUP that "turned out to have no knowledge collection at all".
- A 5.x/SQLite install cannot produce any of that. The install this gate exists to protect no longer exists.

So the clause's condition is met on the evidence it names. The floor was a proxy for "has the affected user migrated"; the answer is yes, and the proxy is superseded by the fact it was standing in for.

DECISION: Hal, 2026-07-28 — proceed now. Recorded here because moving a user-data-safety gate on someone else's behalf must be attributable, not inferred from momentum. I raised it as a blocker, put the evidence and the do-nothing option (wait four days) in front of him, and he called it.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SCOPE FINDING (1di3r.9, surfaced 2026-06-12 — needs decision before impl proceeds): the bead's framing has two factual gaps about the T3-vs-centroid split.

1. "retire the reject guard" — _reject_service_backed_handle(t3) (taxonomy_cmd.py:48, called at 552/664/931) checks is_service_backed(T3), the T3 axis, NOT the taxonomy-store axis. It fires because the CLI reads CHUNK embeddings via raw chroma coll.get(include=["embeddings"]) (taxonomy_cmd.py:144), which retired with Chroma serving (RDR-155). The taxonomy STORE being service-backed does NOT change this. Retiring the guard requires the CLI chunk-embedding read to work on service-backed T3 = RDR-155 pgvector T3 (epic nexus-rn3wo, NOT done, gated behind the release boundary). So retiring it here is OUT OF SCOPE for RDR-152.

2. "project_against: fetch source embeddings via centroid-port get_by_collection" — WRONG. project_against (catalog_taxonomy.py:2527-2570) fetches SOURCE CHUNK embeddings from T3 (chroma_client.get_collection(source).get(include=["embeddings"])). Chunks are NOT centroids; the centroid-port serves topic CENTROIDS only. Source chunks live in T3 = RDR-155 again. Only the TARGET centroids come from the port. split_topic (1450) similarly fetches docs/texts from T3 + re-embeds.

CONSEQUENCE: the 5 orchestrators split into two classes:
- THIN-GLUE, T3-free (take pre-computed embeddings as ARGS; only centroids touch the port): discover_topics, rebuild_taxonomy, assign_batch. Fully implementable + unit-testable in THIS arc. They make the (chroma-T3 + service-taxonomy) config work end-to-end; guard doesn't fire there (T3 is chroma).
- HYBRID (need T3 CHUNK reads via chroma_client + centroids via port): project_against, split_topic. Implementable as chroma-T3-hybrid (chroma_client for chunks, port for centroids) so they work in chroma-T3 mode; but full service-mode (service-T3) is RDR-155.

RECOMMENDED: implement all 5 on HttpTaxonomyStore (thin-glue 3 pure; hybrid 2 keep chroma_client for T3 chunk reads, route centroids through port). Do NOT retire the reject guard (RDR-155-gated T3 axis); surface as a deliberate scope correction. The orchestrators are the RDR-152 parity deliverable; the guard guards the orthogonal RDR-155 T3 axis. DECISION at gate/user.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PARITY DRIFT FOUND (1di3r.4, surface to Phase 4 gate 1di3r.6 for decision): oracle upsert_topic_links (catalog_taxonomy.py:1405) uses INSERT OR REPLACE — on a matching (from,to) PK it OVERWRITES link_count with the freshly-computed value. Scope facts: /links/upsert has exactly ONE caller each side (handleUpsertLink <- upsert_topic_links); cooccurrence/projection/import links use separate repo methods (generateCooccurrenceLinks/refreshProjectionLinks/importTopicLink), so flipping upsertTopicLink GREATEST->REPLACE is safe for other callers. BUT TaxonomyRepositoryTest has an intentional "upsertTopicLink GREATEST on conflict" test (nexus-gmiaf.14) — flipping needs that test updated too. 

DECISION NEEDED at gate: (a) flip Java to REPLACE for true oracle parity (update the GREATEST test); or (b) accept GREATEST as a deliberate monotonic-link-strength choice and document the divergence. 1di3r.4 ships link_types json.dumps parity (the bead's named subtlety) regardless; the Python test pins the actual service GREATEST behavior with a comment pointing here.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SCOPE DECISION (verified against TaxonomyRepository.java, 2026-06-12). EXISTING (reuse): insertTopic(returns id), assignTopic, upsertTopicLink, purgeCollection(cascade {topics,assignments,links,meta}), persistSplit, getAllTopics. GENUINELY-NEW Java (3 endpoints+repo methods, all atomic/transactional):
1. read_rebuild_old_state T2-read half (oracle :2960) -> GET /v1/taxonomy/rebuild/old_state?collection= returns {old_topic_map:[{id,label,review_status}], manual_assignments:[{doc_id,topic_id}]} (manual = assigned_by='manual' JOIN topics on collection). The chroma centroid half moves to the centroid-port get_by_collection (NOT this endpoint).
2. persist_rebuild_topics (oracle :3140) -> POST /topics/persist_rebuild: MUST be ONE txn = DELETE topic_assignments+topics WHERE collection, INSERT new specs (label,collection,doc_count,created_at,terms,review_status) returning ids aligned to specs order, INSERT OR IGNORE chunk assignments, then INSERT OR REPLACE manual_transfers {doc_id:spec_index}->topic_ids[spec_index] assigned_by='manual'. REPLACE semantics: clears old rows even when specs empty (<5 docs/all-noise). A Python delete+insert loop is NON-atomic -> a batch endpoint is REQUIRED (the bead's rebuild-atomicity condition).
3. persist_discovered_topics (oracle :1996) -> POST /topics/persist_discovered: ONE txn = existing-topics guard (COUNT topics WHERE collection; if >0 return [] no-op) + INSERT specs returning ids + INSERT OR IGNORE assignments. Batch endpoint preserves the guard atomically (vs a TOCTOU Python count+loop).
persist_cross_links (oracle :2262): pairs -> INSERT OR REPLACE topic_links link_count link_types='[projection]'. Per-link upsertTopicLink loop from Python is ACCEPTABLE (idempotent, no cross-set atomicity need) — verify in P5.2, no new endpoint.
TDD: TaxonomyRepositoryTest extend — read_rebuild_old_state shape; persist_rebuild REPLACE (old gone/new present/manual applied/empty-specs still clears); persist_discovered existing-guard no-op. JsonInclude.ALWAYS on new handlers.

title: RDR-156 P4.1 (test): combined-query parity suite — metadata-scoped + topic-scoped search; query-vector-as-argument, EXPLAIN HNSW-survives-join, NARROW-COLLECTION exact-recall ==N fixture, parity vs stitched path
description:
TDD-RED for P4 (Decision 5, the unification deliverable). Two highest-traffic stitches FIRST: metadata-scoped search (the query MCP tool catalog-aware-routing dance) and topic-scoped search (topic_assignments ⋈ chunks_<dim>). FOUR MANDATORY ENCODINGS:
1. QUERY-VECTOR-AS-ARGUMENT (Finding 5a): every combined-query function takes the query vector as an ARGUMENT, never join-sourced. Test asserts literal/parameter vector path. EXPLAIN proves Index Scan using idx_chunks_<dim>_embedding (~2ms), NOT Seq Scan + top-N sort (~340ms) — a join-sourced vector is a hard FAIL.

- Changeset (a) THIS PHASE, deploys immediately: ADD CONSTRAINT ... Service change (Finding 2): make collection registration MANDATORY-AND-FIRST on every new-collection write path. Today indexer.py:598-611 registers AFTER data-plane writes inside except Exception: log.warning (silently skippable) — fix so registration precedes data-plane writes and a registration failure is a hard error. Backfill existing collection names before any VALIDATE. NEW standing rule: FKs require registration-before-write ordering in the service (record in src/nexus/db/AGENTS.md or service schema AGENTS.md).
Do NOT FK the manifest to chunk tables (Decision 2) — chunks_registry trigger rejected (RDR-154 app-unfixable bar); manifest orphan class served by P2 stored function + P2.1 fail-loud read backstop. Three chunks_<dim> changesets byte-identical modulo dim.
notes:
P0.2 design decisions (2026-06-11, pre-impl):
(1) ENFORCEMENT POINT: registration-mandatory-and-first lands SERVER-SIDE in PgVectorRepository.upsertChunks (ensure-registered in the same transaction, BEFORE chunk rows; conformant names parsed into content_type/owner_id/embedding_model/model_version stub, non-conformant get name-only stub). Rationale: every chunk write funnels through this one seam (all Python callers, the vector ETL via /v1/vectors/upsert, future writers); per-caller Python registration would be the per-tier-copy antipattern and would churn every existing Java fixture. FK remains the integrity backstop for direct-SQL writers. indexer.py phase4 explicit registration stays (richer rename metadata), no longer load-bearing.
(2) DEPLOY-ORDER LANDMINE + FIX: production has 115k chunk rows with EMPTY catalog_collections (vector migration ran pre-T2-ladder). NOT VALID FK would reject all NEW serving writes at next JAR deploy. fk-002 therefore opens with a stub BACKFILL (INSERT DISTINCT (tenant, collection) from chunks_384/768/1024 + chash_index + topic_assignments ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) before the ADD CONSTRAINTs.
(3) ETL COLLISION + FIX: catalog ETL importCollection is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING -> backfill/auto-registered stubs would permanently block real registry metadata. importCollection becomes DO UPDATE ... WHERE existing row IS a stub (embedding_model='' AND content_type='' AND owner_id=''): upgrades stubs, never clobbers genuinely-newer live rows. Preserves re-run idempotency + post-cutover safety.
(4) source_uri UNIQUE: DEFERRED — live audit found 201 duplicated source_uris (T2 nexus_rdr/156-P0-source-uri-audit); P0.1 pins the deferral with a no-unique-index assertion.
(5) Temporal typing coordination: CatalogRepository binds created_at/superseded_at via nne (null->'') — switch those two columns to empty->NULL helper in upsertCollection/importCollection/supersedeCollection or every bind fails on timestamptz.
(6) Rename-flow implication for the gate: only topic_assignments FK gets ON UPDATE CASCADE per locked spec; renaming a collection that owns chunk rows will violate the chunks FK unless done as insert-new/update-children/delete-old. renameCollection (Java) today touches documents+collections only. Surface at P0.G.

title: Embedding-mode fail-loud: refuse voyage-token collections in ONNX mode, startup mode banner, supervisor plumbs NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY from nexus config, model-identity (not just dim) validation
description: Java service (Main.java:111) silently falls back to local ONNX MiniLM (384) when NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is absent. On 2026-06-10 this turned the cloud-leg migration into per-collection HTTP 400 dim-mismatches — the PgVectorRepository MODEL_DIMS dim guard caught it ONLY because voyage models are 1024-dim; a same-dim wrong-model (e.g. two 1024-dim embedders) would CONTAMINATE silently. Violates no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness. Scope: (1) supervisor (storage_service_daemon._spawn_service) resolves the Voyage key from nexus config/.env resolution chain and passes NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY to the JAR env; (2) service logs a LOUD one-line embedding-mode banner at startup (mode=voyage|onnx-local, models available); (3) upsert-chunks REJECTS collections whose model segment names a voyage-* token when the service is in ONNX mode (explicit 422 'service has no Voyage credentials, refusing to embed collection X with wrong model' instead of relying on dim mismatch); (4) validate the collection model segment against the embedder identity actually used, not merely the output dim — closes the same-dim wrong-model hole. title: conexus-scp.3: OS-supervisor single-owner routing for cold-spawn
description:
Change 3 of 3. When the OS autostart unit is installed, route the cold-spawn respawn through the OS supervisor (single owner) instead of subprocess.Popen, so an ad-hoc client spawn does not steal ownership from the launchd/systemd unit. Popen stays as fallback on ANY supervisor failure (never trade a working path for zero daemons).

FILE: src/nexus/commands/daemon.py — _t2_ensure_running_inner (~line 969); cold-spawn branch at lines 1145-1160 (nx_bin = _resolve_nx_bin(); argv=[...]; proc = subprocess.Popen(...)).

REUSE (verified — do NOT reinvent):
  - _autostart_platform() @62, _autostart_install_dir() @67 (darwin: ~/Library/LaunchAgents ; linux: ~/.config/systemd/user), _autostart_filename_t2() @155 (com.nexus.t2.plist / nexus-t2.service), _T2_LAUNCHD_LABEL @59 = 'com.nexus.t2'.
  - installer.py _activate_cmd @118 shows the exact shell pattern: darwin -> ['launchctl','bootstrap',f'gui/{uid}',str(dest)] ; linux -> systemctl --user. Mirror for the RESPAWN: darwin -> launchctl bootstrap-if-needed (idempotent; bootstrap may already be loaded) THEN launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/com.nexus.t2 ; linux -> systemctl --user start nexus-t2.service.
  - NOTE: there is NO existing 'unit installed?' predicate — ADD one (e.g. _autostart_unit_installed() -> bool) = (_autostart_install_dir() / _autostart_filename_t2()).exists(), guard-railed by platform. Keep it a small testable indirection point like _autostart_platform().

DESIGN (binding):
  - In the cold-spawn branch: if _autostart_unit_installed(): try the supervisor route (subprocess.run the launchctl/systemctl invocation, check returncode). On success, proceed to the SAME migration-aware reachability wait that follows Popen today. On ANY failure (non-zero, FileNotFoundError, exception) -> log a warning + FALL BACK to the existing subprocess.Popen path. If the unit is NOT installed -> Popen as today (unchanged).
  - Version-skew cycle (lines 1059-1115): it SIGTERMs the stale daemon, waits for pid exit, then FALLS THROUGH to this shared cold-spawn branch (1145). Routing this one branch therefore covers version-skew respawn automatically — verify the fall-through still reaches the new routing and keeps its graceful-SIGTERM-then-respawn shape. Do not duplicate the routing.
  - Crash-loop guard (1117-1143) stays AHEAD of the spawn — supervisor route is still subject to it.

TEST FILE: tests/daemon/test_t2_ensure_running_inner.py (extend; harness: tmp_path config_dir, monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess,'Popen',...), _write_discovery, _t2_ensure_running_inner(str(tmp_path), timeout=..., quiet=True)).

    1. unit installed (darwin) -> respawn shells launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/com.nexus.t2 (assert recorded argv), NOT Popen; becomes reachable -> REACHABLE.
    2. unit installed (linux) -> systemctl --user start nexus-t2.service (assert recorded argv).
    3. unit installed but supervisor cmd returns non-zero / raises -> FALLS BACK to Popen (assert Popen called) and still converges.
    4. unit NOT installed -> Popen path unchanged (assert Popen called, no launchctl/systemctl).
    5. version-skew (stale running daemon) + unit installed -> after SIGTERM+exit, respawn goes through supervisor route (assert recorded argv), not Popen.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - [ ] Failing tests shown before implementation.
  - [ ] _autostart_unit_installed() added, reuses _autostart_install_dir()/_autostart_filename_t2(), platform-guarded, testable.
  - [ ] Cold-spawn routes via launchctl kickstart (darwin) / systemctl --user start (linux) when unit installed.
  - [ ] Popen fallback on ANY supervisor failure; unit-not-installed path unchanged.
  - [ ] Version-skew respawn flows through the same routed branch.

title: conexus-scp.2: discovery liveness probe + pid fast-path (T2 only)
description:
Change 2 of 3. Make staleness = process liveness, not heartbeat-age alone, so a healthy-but-slow daemon is not false-staled and a hard-killed daemon is detected instantly.

FILE: src/nexus/daemon/discovery.py — _resolve_lease_record (~line 210; the age>=ttl branch is lines 249-258).
SCOPE: T2 tier ONLY. find_t2_daemon (line 266) calls _resolve_lease_record(raw, path, tier='t2'). find_t3_daemon (line 286) ALSO calls it (tier='t3') — T3 endpoint is TCP chroma; the new UDS-probe + pid fast-path must be gated to tier=='t2' so the T3 path keeps its CURRENT behavior verbatim. (The function is tier-parameterized already — use the tier arg to gate.)

DESIGN (binding):
  (a) On age>=ttl with the endpoint pid ALIVE (tier t2): attempt a bounded UDS connect probe (~0.25s) to endpoint.uds_path. If it ANSWERS -> return the endpoint (lifted as today) + warning log t2_discovery_lease_stale_but_answering; do NOT unlink. If refused/dead/timeout -> unlink + None (CURRENT behavior).
  (b) Fresh lease (age<ttl) but endpoint pid DEAD -> treat as stale IMMEDIATELY (instant hard-kill detection): return None (and unlink, matching the expired path) instead of returning a live-looking endpoint for a corpse.
  - Clock-step guard (age<=-ttl) stays. TTL stays 3.0s. Legacy-payload path (_validate_discovery_payload) untouched. T3 path untouched.
  - pid-liveness check: reuse the existing pid-alive helper in this module if present (look for os.kill(pid,0)/_pid_alive/_predecessor_alive style); else add a small bounded helper. UDS probe: socket.AF_UNIX connect with a short timeout, close immediately (connectivity probe, no RPC).

TEST FILE: tests/daemon/test_discovery.py (extend; reuse its lease-record builders).
  FAILING TESTS FIRST (unit, deterministic — inject clock/time via monkeypatch, fake pid liveness, bind a real AF_UNIX socket on tmp_path for the answering case):
    1. expired lease (age>=ttl) + live ANSWERING UDS endpoint -> resolves to endpoint, file NOT unlinked, warning logged.
    2. expired lease + dead pid (or refused connect) -> None + file unlinked (regression-locks current behavior).
    3. fresh lease + DEAD endpoint pid -> None (new fast-path).
    4. T3 tier expired-lease path unchanged (no UDS probe attempted) — guard the gating.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - [ ] Failing tests shown before implementation.
  - [ ] T2 expired+answering resolves without unlink; expired+dead unlinks->None.
  - [ ] T2 fresh+dead-pid -> None (instant hard-kill detection).
  - [ ] T3 path byte-for-byte behavior preserved (gated on tier).
  - [ ] UDS probe bounded ~0.25s, never hangs.
  - [ ] uv run pytest tests/daemon/test_discovery.py -x -q green.

title: conexus-scp.1: heartbeat thread — move reassert off the event loop
description:
Change 1 of 3. Replace the asyncio _reassert_discovery_loop task with a dedicated threading.Thread ticking supervisor.heartbeat_tick() every _REASSERT_INTERVAL, independent of event-loop state. Lease freshness = process liveness (its actual contract); an event-loop stall >TTL (heavy ETL T2 writes) must no longer defer the heartbeat and false-stale a healthy daemon.

FILE: src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py
  - Start site: ~line 1101 (self._reassert_task = asyncio.create_task(self._reassert_discovery_loop()))
  - Loop body: _reassert_discovery_loop ~line 1115 (currently: while True / await asyncio.sleep / await asyncio.to_thread(supervisor.heartbeat_tick) / fenced-check / self._lease_record = supervisor.record)
  - Cancel site in stop(): ~line 1270 (self._reassert_task.cancel(); await it)

DESIGN (binding):
  - Dedicated threading.Thread (daemon thread) ticking supervisor.heartbeat_tick() every _REASSERT_INTERVAL.
  - PRESERVE all existing semantics: (a) fenced-detection — if supervisor.fenced log warning t2_daemon_discovery_fenced; else self._lease_record = supervisor.record; (b) self._lease_record refresh on each successful tick; (c) cancelled-at-START-of-stop (before discovery-file unlink) so it can never resurrect a shutting-down daemon's addr — use threading.Event + join(timeout) instead of task.cancel()/await; (d) never-crash-the-daemon error handling (best-effort, log t2_daemon_discovery_reassert_failed, continue).
  - heartbeat_tick already ran on a pool thread via to_thread, so single dedicated thread is strictly LESS concurrent — no new locking concerns. Wedged-loop coverage stays with the RDR-151 spin guard (do not remove it).

TEST FILE: tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_lifecycle.py (extend; reuse its daemon-boot fixtures/harness)
  FAILING TEST FIRST: integration — block the daemon event loop with a SYNCHRONOUS sleep > ttl via a test handler (registered RPC that does time.sleep), then assert (a) the lease stays fresh and (b) discovery still resolves (find_t2_daemon returns the endpoint) throughout the stall. With the old asyncio loop this fails (lease expires); with the thread it passes. Also assert stop() joins the thread cleanly and the discovery file is gone after stop (no resurrection). Deterministic: tmp_path config_dir, port 0, no real wall-clock sleeps-as-sync beyond the injected stall.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - [ ] Failing test committed/shown before implementation.
  - [ ] _reassert_task asyncio task replaced by a threading.Thread + threading.Event stop signal.
  - [ ] Event-loop stall > ttl no longer expires the lease (new test passes).
  - [ ] stop() sets the Event + joins (bounded) BEFORE the discovery-file unlink; no resurrection.
  - [ ] fenced-detection + _lease_record refresh + never-crash error handling preserved.
  - [ ] uv run pytest tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_lifecycle.py -x -q green.

title: RDR-155 P5.2 (impl): copy-not-move ETL (local PersistentClient leg + ChromaCloud REST leg) into pgvector with rollback flag; preserve source_collection verbatim
description: Implement copy-not-move ETL of existing Chroma collections into pgvector, mirroring conexus RDR-001 Phase 8 cutover. TWO DISTINCT LEGS: (1) local PersistentClient copy (direct read); (2) ChromaCloud has NO direct psql/pg_restore path — its leg reads via the Chroma REST/auth API and writes through the engine's pgvector upsert. Re-home vectors (re-embed ONLY if a model/dim change forces it). Rollback flag. Preserve collection names verbatim into the pgvector collection column (no normalization); if any normalization is ever required it must update topic_assignments.source_collection in lock-step. Makes P5.1 green. Use sequential-thinking for the two-leg ETL + rollback design. RDR §Migrate.
notes:

- Engine module src/nexus/migration/vector_etl.py, interface dictated by the locked P5.1 suite. Status vocabulary mirrors embed_migrate (migrated/failed/skipped/dry-run); report.ok=True only for all-migrated/dry-run; CLI exits non-zero on not-ok.

title: RDR-155 P5.1 (test): copy-not-move ETL integrity suite — row counts, vector identity, manifest FK, topic_assignments.source_collection resolves to migrated collection
description: TDD test bead — write BEFORE P5.2. Assert ETL integrity: (a) row counts match source Chroma collection → pgvector chunks_<dim>; (b) vector identity (verbatim-identical vectors, re-embed only if a model/dim change forces it); (c) manifest FK integrity post-migration (documents.tumbler → catalog_document_chunks(collection,chash) → chunks row resolves); (d) T2 CONSISTENCY: every topic_assignments.source_collection value (T2 taxonomy, four-segment Chroma names) resolves to a migrated pgvector collection — NO orphaned taxonomy attribution post-cutover (same string-copy-orphan class RDR-108 fixed). Collection names preserved VERBATIM (no namespace normalization). Cover BOTH legs: local PersistentClient copy + ChromaCloud REST/auth read. Exact-count assertions. RDR §Migrate, §Test Plan.
notes:
P2.1 contract constraint (from substantive-critic on nexus-duf53, 2026-06-09): PgVectorRepository.fetchDocumentChunks throws IllegalStateException on ANY unresolvable manifest row (application-enforced FK, fail-loud read backstop). During the P5 copy-not-move ETL window, partially migrated documents will trigger that ISE — so P5 migration-integrity validation MUST use direct SQL (catalog_document_chunks LEFT JOIN chunks_<dim> ... WHERE chunks.chash IS NULL), NOT the repository API. Do not weaken the repository fail-loud contract to accommodate the ETL window.

P4a.G gate Obs-1 (substantive-critic, 2026-06-10) — RESOLVE BEFORE AUTHORING THIS SUITE: the 'vector identity (verbatim-identical vectors, re-embed only if a model/dim change forces it)' criterion is AMBIGUOUS against the locked P4a.2 read-leg design. migration/chroma_read.py iter_collection_chunks deliberately does NOT fetch embeddings (include=[documents, metadatas]) — the pgvector side re-embeds server-side via Seam B, and dragging legacy vectors through the ETL invites RDR-109 cross-model contamination. Two readings: (a) 'vector identity' = TEXT transferred verbatim + recall equivalence (already established by the P3 dual-run harness with identical embedders) — satisfiable with the read leg as shipped, ETL accepts re-embed cost; (b) 'vector identity' = verbatim SOURCE-VECTOR copy — requires extending iter_collection_chunks with an include_embeddings=False-default parameter (heavier CloudClient REST pagination) and re-opens the cross-model-contamination question. Decide (a) vs (b) at P5.1 kickoff and record the decision here; if (b), the chroma_read extension is P5 scope. Default recommendation from the P4a.2 implementation: (a) — re-embed-on-migrate was the operative assumption (recorded in chroma_read.py docstring).

VECTOR-IDENTITY DECISION RECORDED (P5.1 kickoff, 2026-06-10): option (a) — text transferred VERBATIM + recall equivalence; the pgvector side re-embeds server-side via Seam B. Rationale: matches the locked P4a.2 read-leg design (iter_collection_chunks deliberately omits embeddings, pinned by test_embeddings_deliberately_not_fetched), avoids re-opening RDR-109 cross-model contamination, and recall equivalence with identical embedders is already established by the P3 dual-run harness. Consequence for this suite: 'vector identity' assertions = (1) chunk TEXT byte-identical source→target, (2) chash preserved verbatim (chash[:32] is the natural ID on both sides), (3) a pgvector row EXISTS with the correct dim for every migrated chunk; NO source-vector float comparison. Option (b) rejected; iter_collection_chunks stays embeddings-free.

P5.1 DUAL REVIEW (2026-06-10, commit 83b50746 + fixes): CRE 0 Critical/High, 2 Medium (WAL-discipline del in _make_local_store — FIXED; FakeVectorClient.collection_exists empty-collection asymmetry — awareness note for P5.2), 3 Low (orphan_sql(1024) test — ADDED via CANONICAL_EMBEDDING_MODELS authority import, mode-lint clean; PG state cleanup in manifest test — ADDED try/finally; sorted-results ordering pin — kept, deliberate determinism). Critic PASS-partial, 2 Significant, both ACTIONED: (S1) manifest_orphan_sql(1024) untested — test added covering all canonical voyage tokens + legacy voyage-3; (S2) cloud-leg integration gap REGISTERED as deferred obligation on nexus-a0i5u notes + suite docstring (unit routing coverage is the hermetic ceiling; live ChromaCloud run is a P5.G cutover-readiness item). P5.2 handoff notes from review: FakeVectorClient.upsert_chunks deliberately lacks the embeddings kwarg (decision (a) enforcement — real HttpVectorClient accepts-and-ignores it); report.ok=True for dry-run is the pinned semantic; rollback reads the SOURCE as its deletion manifest (O(source size)); page_size=300 exact-boundary loop termination is covered by chroma_read's suite, not re-pinned here.
