title: RDR-155 P4a.2 (impl): retire Chroma from serving/query/storage live paths + supersede nexus-skp06; KEEP minimal Chroma READ client + chroma_quotas for the P5 ETL
description: SPLIT FROM ORIGINAL P4.2 (nx_plan_audit ordering fix). Phase 4a — GATED BEHIND P3.G (hybrid-parity green). Retire Chroma from the SERVING/QUERY/STORAGE live paths only: no serving code constructs PersistentClient/CloudClient for query or upsert; all live retrieval/storage routes through pgvector. Remove the skp06 app-layer Chroma tenant guard (superseded — native FORCE RLS by tenant_id). PRESERVE a minimal Chroma READ client (local PersistentClient read leg + ChromaCloud REST/auth read leg) — the Phase-5 migration ETL reads through it. DO NOT delete chroma_quotas.py in 4a: it still governs the surviving read leg; full deletion of the read client + chroma_quotas moves to Phase 4b (nexus-4b2), which is GATED ON P5 MIGRATION COMPLETION (P5.G nexus-a0i5u). Use Serena (find_referencing_symbols before each removal, safe_delete) for symbol-scoped deletion. Makes P4a.1 green. RDR §Retire.
notes:
P2.2 contract constraints inherited from nexus-tqeg6 dual review (2026-06-09): (1) PgVectorRepository shares NO interface with the Chroma VectorRepository and every method takes tenant as the FIRST parameter (RLS is the tenant boundary); the serving cutover is NOT a drop-in swap — introduce a port interface or rewrite VectorHandler call sites. (2) Production wiring MUST use the PgVectorRepository(TenantScope, EmbedderRouter, EmbedderRouter) constructor — EmbedderRouter.embed() via the plain-Embedder constructor falls back to ONNX for ALL collections and breaks cloud-mode routing (caught only at first upsert by the dim check). (3) delete() does NOT pre-check catalog_document_chunks; whether the serving path needs manifest-cleanup enforcement (pre-delete check vs documented caller obligation, currently the latter per delete() javadoc) is a P4a write-path decision. (4) Handler IAE messages from dimForCollection include the collection name (owner segment); review HTTP error mapping before passing them verbatim into 400 bodies.

P4a.1 review additions (2026-06-10): (5) VectorHandler.handleGet silently IGNORES the include parameter the Python _ServiceCollectionStub sends (include=[metadatas]) — P4a.2 must decide: honor include or document always-full-return. (6) The serving retire scope INCLUDES the T3-daemon chromadb.HttpClient leg (daemon/t3_client.py) — local-mode make_t3() serves through it to the chroma daemon; the P4a.1 scan now covers it. P4a.2 must reroute local-mode T3 serving onto the pgvector service path, not just remove the db/t3.py constructions. (7) /embed absent-router 503 behavior is now a pinned invariant (PgVectorServingContractTest Order 13).

P4a.2 DECISIONS (2026-06-10, commit c97cde93): (1) DIRECT REWRITE, no port interface — PgVectorRepository would be the port's only implementation forever (P4b deletes the Chroma classes), and tenant-first signatures make any Chroma-shaped port a lie; VectorHandler call sites rewritten with requirePgRepo (503) + requireTenant (401) guards. (2) HONORED — Main.java wires PgVectorRepository(new TenantScope(ds), docRouter, qryRouter); the router-constructor invariant is restated in a comment at the wiring site. (3) CALLER OBLIGATION retained — no manifest pre-check on the serving delete path; a pre-check would cost a query per delete for callers (doc_indexer prune, MCP store_delete) that manage manifests at a higher layer, and fetchDocumentChunks already fails loud on dangling refs (detectable, never silent). Documented in handleStoreDelete javadoc. (4) VERBATIM — IAE messages (incl. dimForCollection's, which echo the collection name) pass into 400 bodies: the collection name is the caller's own request data and the bearer is already tenant-bound, so nothing crosses a trust boundary. (5) ACCEPTED-AND-IGNORED — /get always returns the full {ids,documents,metadatas} envelope; honoring include would make the envelope request-dependent for no consumer benefit (the Python stub normalises all three keys unconditionally). Documented in handleGet javadoc + class javadoc. (6) REROUTED — daemon/t3_client.py DELETED; make_t3() returns the HttpVectorClient singleton in BOTH modes when no test _client is injected; T3Database constructor fail-loud without injected client; ETL read legs carved into migration/chroma_read.py (both legs, read-only, epsilon-allow). (7) PRESERVED — /embed absent-router 503 pin green; the always-registered vectors context extends the same explicit-503 pattern to every route.

P4a.2 DEGRADED-SURFACE INVENTORY (migration window, until P5/follow-ons): chroma-client-coupled features now refuse or degrade on the service handle — taxonomy discover/rebuild/split CLI refuses cleanly (ClickException naming RDR-155 P4a + nexus-gmiaf.21+); mcp_infra taxonomy hooks skip with an instance-based guard (env guard was wrong post-cutover); chash-span resolution in catalog_links/catalog_spans degrades via existing try/except (resolve fails with logged warning); catalog diff/extract/link-audit/gc, orphan/manifest backfill, commands/t3.py list raise AttributeError('._client') loudly; doctor pipeline-version sweep + GH-1061 dim-mismatch probe RETIRED (pg path fails loud on dim at write via dimForCollection; collection-metadata stamps have no pgvector equivalent). doc_indexer/indexer Python-side embedding remains env-gated (NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_VECTORS=service skips it); with env unset embeddings are computed then discarded by the service client — flag-default flip is a candidate follow-on.

title: P5.3-F: Adversarial security test matrix — cross-tenant, cross-session, rotation, revocation, expiry, 401
description:
RDR-152 Phase 5.3, Phase F (cross-cutting adversarial test matrix). LOCKED design: T2 nexus_rdr/gmiaf.32-token-design-DECISIONS. Do NOT re-open.

SCOPE — the full boundary test matrix mandated by the locked decisions. Integration over mocks: real service + real tmp PG (port 0, seeded fixtures, deterministic clock for TTL/grace).
1. CROSS-TENANT denial: token bound to tenant A cannot act as tenant B; a forged/extra X-Nexus-Tenant header is ignored (server-resolved tenant wins). Assert RLS yields zero sibling-tenant rows AND auth resolves correct tenant.
2. CROSS-SESSION denial: session token for session X cannot read/write session Y within the SAME tenant (server-enforced, Decision 2). Non-vacuous: prove sibling-session data exists and is denied, not merely absent.
3. ROTATION overlap: after nx service token rotate, BOTH old and new tokens authorize through the grace window; old 401s after grace expiry. No rotation-induced 401 inside the window (Decision 3).
4. REVOCATION: revoked token 401s within the cache-TTL bound; assert the bound (document expected max latency).
5. EXPIRY: expired service_token and expired session_token both 401.
6. MISSING/BLANK: missing Authorization, blank bearer, malformed scheme all 401 (preserve current 401-no-WWW-Authenticate posture).

Use EXACT assertions (== N rows, == status), never inequalities (feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression). Lock every count/status.

CONTEXT
- Build on AuthFilter (Phase B), CLI lifecycle (Phase C), session mint (Phase D), root issuance (Phase E).
- Mirror existing service test style (tests/ for Java/service; tests/ + -m integration for Python E2E). Deterministic clock for grace/TTL windows.

EXECUTION
1. Author the matrix as the explicit deliverable (this bead IS the tests). TDD framing: each row is an executable assertion against the live boundary.
2. Run unit + integration; both green (this is the substrate the P5 gate gmiaf.34 requires).

DEPENDS ON: R-D + R-E (full surface live). VALIDATION: R-F trio — test-validator confirms assertions non-vacuous; substantive-critic confirms the matrix covers every locked-decision claim with no silent omission.
Context: nx
notes:
## Enrichment (nx_enrich_beads, 2026-06-08)

### Test matrix — 6 classes

**1. CROSS-TENANT denial**
- Token bound to tenant A cannot act as tenant B.
- Forged X-Nexus-Tenant header is ignored — server-resolved tenant wins (AuthFilter.java ATTR_TENANT at line 44).
- RLS silently filters (0 rows), NOT a 403 — assert both == 0 rows AND resolved-tenant correct.
- Non-vacuous: seed data as superuser for tenant B, prove token A returns == 0 rows in tenant B space.

**2. CROSS-SESSION denial**
- Session token for session X cannot read/write session Y within SAME tenant (server-enforced, Decision 2).
- Per t1-001-baseline.xml lines 20-26: session_id is a COLUMN predicate filter, not a GUC. The denial is a column-scoped filter.
- Non-vacuous: seed session Y data via superuser connection, then assert == 0 rows / 403 for session X token.

**3. ROTATION overlap**
- After nx service token rotate: BOTH old and new tokens authorize within grace window. No rotation-induced 401 inside window.
- Old token 401s just AFTER grace expiry.
- Requires deterministic clock: inject Clock/Instant supplier into token store; do NOT call Instant.now() directly. Or manipulate expires_at directly in test fixtures.
- Test both branches explicitly.

**4. REVOCATION**
- Revoked token 401s within cache-TTL bound.
- Document the expected bound; assert it explicitly: revoke, advance clock by cache_ttl+epsilon, assert == 401.
- Cache TTL is a real tested bound, not just documentation.

**5. EXPIRY**
- Expired service_token -> == 401.
- Expired session_token -> == 401.
- Both cases independently tested.

**6. MISSING/BLANK**
- Missing Authorization header -> == 401.
- Blank bearer -> == 401.
- Malformed scheme -> == 401.
- Preserve AuthFilter 401-no-WWW-Authenticate posture (lines 31-32 in AuthFilter.java docstring).

### Test harness design
- Java legs: EmbeddedPostgres.builder().start() (port 0, no Docker, established pattern in MemoryRepositoryTest/ScratchRepositoryTest), nexus_svc role as NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, RLS ENABLE+FORCE, GUC nexus.tenant via TenantScope.withTenant. Schema via Liquibase master changelog. Seed-via-superuser-connection for non-vacuous negatives.
- Python legs (client wiring test): freezegun or fixed datetime; the 4 HTTP clients (http_scratch_store.py lines 54/57/148-157, http_catalog_client.py lines 130-131, http_memory_store.py lines 66-67/94-95, http_vector_client.py lines 66-67/94-95) all must send Bearer + session header.
- EXACT assertions only (== N rows, == status code) — never >= or > inequalities (feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression).
- Deterministic clock for every grace/TTL/expiry window — do not rely on wall clock.

### Gate dependency
Depends on R-D (.32.10) + R-E (.32.11) — full token surface must be live. Current AuthFilter.java is still Phase 1-4 bootstrap (single shared NX_SERVICE_TOKEN, client-trusted X-Nexus-Tenant). Phase B rewrite (.2) must be live before writing the matrix against the new model.

### Validation
R-F trio (.32.12): test-validator confirms assertions non-vacuous; substantive-critic confirms matrix covers every locked-decision claim with no silent omission.

title: P5.3-B: AuthFilter rewrite — token->tenant resolution + cache + per-session verification
description:

- Rewrite service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/AuthFilter.java:
  - Hash the presented bearer, look up service_tokens row, resolve tenant_id SERVER-SIDE. STOP trusting client X-Nexus-Tenant (validate-or-ignore: if header present and != resolved tenant, reject or ignore per design — resolved tenant wins; do not 400 on missing X-Nexus-Tenant anymore since tenant comes from the token).

  - In-memory token_hash->tenant cache with TTL + revocation invalidation (invalidate on revoke/rotate; bounded TTL so expiry/revocation takes effect within window). Keep constant-time compare semantics only where comparing secrets; lookup is by hash.

A sub-agent token for session X cannot act as session Y even within one tenant (Decision 2 — stronger than RDR-105 client-side).

- Main.java: stop requiring single fixed NX_SERVICE_TOKEN as the auth secret; wire AuthFilter to the jOOQ-backed token store + cache (constructor injection — no singletons). The root token row (Phase E) is what bootstraps.

title: RDR-152 BLOCKER: topic_assignments.doc_id is chunk-chash but fk_ta_catalog_doc references document-tumbler — 180801/198986 assignments cannot migrate
description: Sandbox re-seed (prod-copy.sh against real prod) found taxonomy migrates only 7082/198986 topic_assignments; 180801 skipped. ROOT: topic_assignments.doc_id holds 32-char CHUNK content-hashes (chash) — 178147 of 180806 rows are 32-hex; 111376 distinct doc_ids match document_chunks.chash. But fk_ta_catalog_doc (nexus-b7v6i) references catalog_documents(tenant_id, tumbler), and tumblers are dotted ('1.1.10'), never 32-hex. So the cross-store FK targets the WRONG identity: taxonomy assigns CHUNKS (by chash) to topics, not documents (by tumbler). The correct relation is doc_id(chash) -> document_chunks.chash -> documents.tumbler. nexus-0a7xc's skip-and-count made the ETL resilient (no crash) but masks this: faithful migration is IMPOSSIBLE as-is — deleting SQLite (Phase-4) would lose 91% of taxonomy assignments. DESIGN DECISION NEEDED (RDR-level): (a) drop fk_ta_catalog_doc — chunks aren't a PG table so doc_id can't FK to anything; or (b) re-target FK to a chunk-identity table; or (c) re-key assignments chash->tumbler via document_chunks manifest (lossy: many chunks/doc). Also topic_links has FK failures (topic_links_from_topic_id_fkey) — some links reference topics not present; verify same-root. BLOCKS Phase-4 destructive deletion.
close_reason: doc_id is chunk chash not tumbler; fk_ta_catalog_doc never registered; 129520 assignments migrate (vs 7082); gate green 9757 passed

The changelogs ship in the jar but are applied only by test fixtures / external psql. In production the PG database would have no schema. Resolve before Phase 4 cutover: either the service runs Liquibase migrate on startup (idempotent), or nx init / nx storage provisions the schema (RDR-152 Phase 5 .31 Postgres provisioning). Liquibase is the version authority (closes RDR-142) so startup-migrate is the natural home. Cross-cutting (all stores).
close_reason: Phase-4 PREREQUISITE DONE: service applies Liquibase at startup. SchemaMigrator.migrate(ds) runs db.changelog-master.xml before HTTP bind; fail-fast (System.exit(1)) on failure — never serves unmigrated. Two-role topology: admin/owner pool (NX_DB_ADMIN_*, falls back to NX_DB_* in dev) runs DDL; service role nexus_svc (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS) does DML only. Stacked review 2 rounds: critic R1 not-justified — CRITICAL the per-store IF-EXISTS-skip nexus_svc grants were silently skipped + marked-applied (later-created role → 0 grants → permission-denied under load); SIGNIFICANT ALTER ROLE search_path needs superuser (broke the non-superuser-owner recommendation); test ran as superuser proving nothing. R2 fix: consolidated grants into ONE runAlways changeset (grants-nexus-svc.xml) at master tail, no IF-EXISTS (missing role → fail loud, correct); removed ALTER ROLE, search_path now via Hikari connectionInitSql (no role privilege); rewrote test to migrate as nexus_admin_test (NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE — genuine non-superuser owner) through all 52 changesets (NO superuser-only DDL found) + nexus_svc DML-under-RLS + fail-closed; code-review M1 (close migrationDs before exit), M2 (partial NX_DB_ADMIN_* throws), M3 (qual NPE guard). Critic R2: justified 0/0. Orchestrator fresh-jar verified: 322/322 Java green, non-superuser owner migrates, svc DML under RLS, fail-closed. Provisioning contract (create nexus_admin owner + nexus_svc BEFORE first start) documented for Phase-5 .31. Commits 318c3b73+69f24606. T2 152-net63-liquibase-startup-DONE. # routing-allow: prerequisite bead, not a phase-gate bead — no cross-walk sentinel applies

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
C3 native DB path acceptance criterion (from gmiaf.6 stacked-review fix): native binary MemoryRepository.upsert+findByTitle round-trip against live PG must pass without ExceptionInInitializerError/ConcurrentHashMap NPE (closes S0.4 C3 jOOQ DSL query path).

Root cause diagnosed in gmiaf.6: jOOQ 3.20.11 + GraalVM 25 has two conflicting failure modes:
(a) --initialize-at-run-time=org.jooq: binary builds but DSL.using() throws ExceptionInInitializerError at runtime. Community metadata 3.18.2 typeReachable guards force SQLDataType build-time init, conflicting with the run-time flag.
(b) --initialize-at-build-time=org.jooq: native-image fails at build time with UnsupportedFeatureException: org.xml.sax.helpers.LocatorImpl found in heap (jOOQ allocates it during static init of XML-related classes).

Resolution requires: jOOQ-provided GraalVM 25 reachability metadata (jOOQ 3.20.x community metadata update, currently only 3.18.2 in repo 0.10.4) OR a GraalVM Substitution for DefaultDataType static init that defers the ConcurrentHashMap population to run time safely.

jlink is the live fallback per S0.4 C1 until this is resolved.

title: P1.0: FTS5→tsvector parity contract (locked before memory migration)
description: RDR-152 Phase 1 — define the FTS parity contract that ALL FTS stores (memory, plans, catalog, taxonomy) inherit. SQLite FTS5 → Postgres tsvector/GIN. Byte-identical result order is NOT achievable (tokenization, BM25 vs ts_rank differ). Parity defined per store as: (1) top-K SET EQUALITY (exact) over a fixed query battery; (2) rank-correlation floor Spearman >= 0.90 where order matters. Labeled query set = each store's EXISTING FTS test fixtures. A store that cannot meet the floor ESCALATES to substantive-critic sign-off at its migration gate — the threshold is NOT silently lowered by the migration author. Stores asserting exact FTS order get those assertions relaxed to this definition as an explicit, reviewed migration step (not silent). This contract is locked BEFORE P1.2 (memory) begins. title: ARCH PIVOT: replace SQLite single-writer T2 daemon with Postgres + strict server + thin URL MCP bridge (CLI uses server only)
description: DECISION 2026-06-06 (Hal): abandon the SQLite single-writer T2 daemon model. It has been a recurring CPU-peg / write-contention / multi-daemon-spawn-race source across many releases (5.0.2-4, 5.10.0-5.10.5). RDR-151 shipped: 2.1a taxonomy write serialize, Phase 3 write routing, u2vmv spin guard (5.10.5), xmohw full write serialization. SHAKEOUT 2026-06-06 of 5.10.5 still found: (1) lone idle daemon pegs ~99% CPU (root never captured); (2) spin guard detector BLIND SPOT — only counted non-empty select returns, missed the actual empty-immediate-return (self-reschedule) spin shape, so it never fired/auto-captured (detector fix written on branch feature/nexus-u2vmv-detector-empty-return, UNCOMMITTED, now likely moot); (3) spawn STAMPEDE — N MCP clients (sessions + 5.10.4 desktop) all ensure-running when no daemon exists -> multiple daemons race the spawn-lock, sometimes none publishes discovery (3-daemon no-owner limbo). NEW ARCHITECTURE: Postgres as the storage substrate (real concurrent writers, no single-writer-lock contention class); a strict server process owning the DB; a thin URL-based MCP bridge (HTTP) so Claude Code / Desktop / CLI all talk to the server over a URL instead of spawning/contending daemons; the nx CLI uses the server only (no direct DB). This dissolves the entire single-writer-daemon peg/spawn-race/version-skew class. SUPERSEDES (mark when planned): RDR-151 daemon-peg remediation beads nexus-u2vmv, nexus-xmohw(merged but moot), nexus-nob1q (BEGIN IMMEDIATE/busy_timeout - moot under Postgres), nexus-5kcsq epic. NEXT: write an RDR for the Postgres+server+bridge architecture before implementing.
close_reason: Groomed 2026-07-08: superseded by RDR-152 (epic nexus-gmiaf) — this was the pre-RDR umbrella for the arch pivot; RDR-152 became the pivot and SHIPPED (6.0.0-era, Postgres+Java engine serving production at api.conexus-nexus.com since 2026-06; RDR-158 carries the SQLite retirement tail). No unique children; everything lives under gmiaf/tdkg1.

title: RDR-151 LIVE ORACLE FAILED: 5.10.4 T2 daemon pegs ~100% CPU at idle (selector/teardown spin, distinct from the write-contention peg)
description: Live deploy validation 2026-06-06 (conexus 5.10.4, fresh daemon pid 81300, all predecessors SIGKILLed first). A fresh daemon pegs ~97-100% CPU within ~60s at IDLE: no clients, no contenders (zero nx-mcp/worker procs), after only the supervisor hello + one CLI call. sample(1): main asyncio thread spinning in _PyEval event loop (dominant frames pure Python eval, NOT blocked in kevent), with an occasional context_run->pysqlite execute callback => classic selector busy-spin (select() returns immediately on a perpetually-ready fd, loop re-runs). Evidence: docs/postmortem/2026-06-06-daemon-5104-idle-peg-sample.txt. SIGNIFICANCE: this is the RF-1-shaped connection-teardown/event-loop spin. RDR-151 REFUTED RF-1 as the cause of the WRITE-CONTENTION peg and demoted P1.1 (pause/abort teardown) to 'hygiene, not the peg'. That conclusion was incomplete: a teardown/idle selector spin is real and pegs the daemon independent of write contention. Phase 3 (taxonomy write routing) is correct but does NOT fix this. PRE-EXISTING: prior-session handoff states the prod daemon pegged before Phase 3 (5.10.3 and earlier) => NOT a 5.10.4 regression; 5.10.4 is an incomplete fix. NEXT: re-instrument with the SIGUSR2 sys._current_frames() dump (sample gives only C symbols) to pin the exact spinning coroutine; determine whether a single client connect+disconnect induces it (P1.1 teardown path) or a self-rescheduling heartbeat/zero-delay reclaim does; also determine if it affects clean end-user installs vs is amplified by this dev env's known MCP/CLI churn. Epic nexus-5kcsq. Do NOT close nexus-uzay8/RDR-151 as peg-fixed.
close_reason: SHIPPED + SUPERSEDED. The cause-agnostic event-loop spin guard (the actual deliverable) is merged and live on develop: f02c5a07 'RDR-151 cause-agnostic event-loop spin guard' is an ancestor of develop; spin_guard.py (SpinGuardSelector + SpinWatchdog) is wired into t2_daemon.py via _run_main_spin_guarded; tests/daemon/test_spin_guard.py 9 tests pass on develop. Corrected diagnosis (Hal, 2026-06-06): a clean 5.10.4 daemon idles at 0%; the peg came from version-skewed client churn + respawn-race thrash, not steady state. The SQLite single-writer daemon this patches is superseded by RDR-152 (Postgres + Java service); label superseded-by-rdr-152, comment 'do not implement'. Contributing-cause hardening lives in SEPARATE ready beads (nexus-89url ensure-running 15s-timeout respawn race, takeover socket-close-timeout). NOT closing RDR-151 / nexus-uzay8 as peg-fixed (per bead directive). Disposition confirmed by Hal 2026-06-13.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-06, after instrumented investigation): the peg is NOT a clean-daemon steady-state bug. A cleanly-started 5.10.4 daemon idles at 0% CPU and stays at 0% through a client call AND a 6-way concurrent write burst (verified, direct-run and supervisor-spawned). The 97-100% peg reproduces under TWO conditions: (1) my own thrash (concurrent stop/kill/respawn racing the spawn lock + a takeover whose old-socket close timed out at 5s -> survivor inherits a half-closed fd -> selector spin); (2) the REAL environment here: the single T2 daemon has a ZOO of heterogeneous-version MCP clients — nx-mcp pid 73498 up 18h47m (version-skewed), a Claude Desktop .mcpb extension install (local.mcpb.hal-hildebrand.conexus, separate conexus + own T1 chroma, 12h+), the 5.10.3 plugin-cache install, AND the 5.10.4 uv-tool install — all connecting to one daemon. That cross-version client churn (the RDR-128/151 version-skew cascade) drives the peg. My earlier 'live oracle FAILED — pegs at idle' was MEASURED ON THRASHED/CHURNED daemons, not a clean one — retract the 'release is broken' framing. ACTIONABLE: (a) restart/retire stale clients (18h nx-mcp, desktop .mcpb extension, 5.10.3 plugin) so all clients are one version; (b) the daemon should be hardened to not peg under skewed-client churn (the remaining real work — related to the ensure-running 15s-timeout respawn race + takeover socket-close-timeout). Evidence: docs/postmortem/2026-06-06-daemon-5104-idle-peg-sample.txt + this session's process listing. nexus (15s timeout) is a contributing cause.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CONFIRMED 2026-06-06 by cleanup: removed the version-skew sources (58 stale plugin caches 5.0.1-5.10.1 kept only active 5.10.3; killed pre-5.10.4 in-memory procs: mineru-api 1d17h, resource_trackers, a 3h nx-index-Luciferase job) and restarted the T2 daemon clean. Result: single daemon, ~0.3% CPU, NOT pegged. This validates the corrected diagnosis — the peg was old/skewed-client churn, NOT clean-5.10.4-daemon steady state. Remaining hardening (daemon should not peg even under a skewed-client zoo; ensure-running 15s-timeout respawn race; takeover socket-close-timeout) stays open as the real work. Desktop .mcpb extension confirmed on 5.10.4.

description:
RDR-151 Phase 1 acceptance validation. Three distinct gates from RDR §Decision + §Validation:

1. GRACEFUL-STOP-UNDER-LOAD (operational acceptance bar). LIVE EVIDENCE: a SIGTERM 'nx daemon t2 stop' FAILED to stop the pegged daemon (stayed ~99% after the bounded stop returned; only SIGKILL cleared it). Test: assert SIGTERM / graceful stop terminates the daemon even under peak load within _GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT. This is the invariant the peg broke.

2. SOAK GATE (single, unambiguous, RDR §Validation): after the Phase 1 fix, run a LONE daemon under representative client churn for AT LEAST 30 minutes (well above the 12-min worst-case lone-from-zero peg) and require CPU to stay flat (no sustained core burn) AND the accepted-fd count to return to baseline between connections. Run in_background (Monitor with until-loop), NOT a foreground sleep. This is a manual/marked-integration gate, not a unit test.

3. CASCADE-SUPPRESSION (cross-check with P1.3): drive stop() concurrent with ensure-running, confirm no replacement is spawned AND no mid-cascade fast re-peg. (P1.3 owns the unit-level no-spawn assertion; this is the integrated behavioral check.)

DEPENDS ON all Phase 1 implementation beads (P1.1-P1.4) being merged. The rdr151_phase0_heavy.py regression (P1.1) is the unit-level peg gate; this bead is the integrated + soak gate.

Instrumentation note (RDR §Validation): macOS sample is the accepted live instrument (py-spy/lldb need root on macOS); consider registering a SIGUSR1 faulthandler handler in the daemon to make future all-thread captures one-step (optional add).

title: RDR-151 P1.4: to_thread(heartbeat_tick) so flock never blocks the event loop (Gap 4)
description:
RDR-151 Phase 1, Gap 4 / RC-3 (independent cascade path). _reassert_discovery_loop (t2_daemon.py:990) calls supervisor.heartbeat_tick() DIRECTLY in the coroutine, not via asyncio.to_thread. The chain reaches a blocking fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) (service_registry.py:200, under _elect :284). With DEFAULT_TTL = 3.0 (service_registry.py:64), any flock stall beyond 3s freezes the event-loop thread long enough for the daemon's own lease to age out, making a running daemon look absent and triggering a spawn.

FIX (locked in RDR §Decision item 3): dispatch heartbeat_tick() via asyncio.to_thread at t2_daemon.py:990 so the blocking flock never runs on the event-loop thread. Preserve the existing fenced/record handling around it (lines 991-998).

TDD: test-first. Assert the heartbeat dispatch does not block the loop: a simulated flock stall > TTL must NOT freeze concurrent loop work / age out the lease. RF-2 (RDR §Research Findings) is the live-quantification follow-up (whether the stall exceeds 3s in production — OPEN, resolve with loop.set_debug(True) slow-callback log); the fix is correct regardless.

Context: RDR-151 §Decision item 3, §Research Findings RF-2; T2 nexus/daemon-concurrency-diagnosis-2026-06-05 RC-3.

title: RDR-151 P1.3: mark_shutting_down() first in stop() (Gap 3, cascade trigger)
description:
RDR-151 Phase 1, Gap 3 / RC-2 (the nexus-x47yx cascade trigger). T2Daemon.stop() (t2_daemon.py:1079) closes servers (:1133-1136) and relinquishes the lease (:1151) but NEVER calls ServiceRegistry.mark_shutting_down() (exists service_registry.py:328, currently uncalled from the daemon). For the entire drain the lease reads 'live' (TTL 3.0s) while sockets close, so a concurrent ensure-running resolves an apparently-live endpoint, fails to connect (ECONNREFUSED), and counts it as a crash = the zero-daemon-window.

FIX (locked in RDR §Decision item 2): call self._registry.mark_shutting_down(self._lease_record) as the FIRST statement of stop() (t2_daemon.py:1079), before cancelling the reassert task or closing servers.

TDD: test-first. RDR Test Plan + §Decision: a stop()-during-ensure-running test asserting NO replacement daemon is spawned (the cascade-suppression check). Exact assertion: replacement spawn count == 0.

SHARED-PRIMITIVE NOTE (RDR-149 invariant): the T3 analog (T3Supervisor.stop() at t3_daemon.py:445 also never calls mark_shutting_down — filed as nexus-6o4uj, OUT of this epic). RDR §Out of Scope: the PREFERRED fix for both is to fold the mark_shutting_down call into a SHARED supervisor-stop path in src/nexus/daemon/service_registry.py rather than one tier's copy (per the RDR-149 'lands in the shared primitive, never one tier's copy' invariant, mechanically enforced by tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py). If you implement the shared path here, nexus-6o4uj is satisfied for free; if you land T2-only, nexus-6o4uj carries the T3 follow-on. PREFER the shared path. Check tests/daemon/test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py + test_lifecycle_gate.py do not break.

Context: RDR-151 §Decision item 2, §Out of Scope; T2 nexus/daemon-concurrency-diagnosis-2026-06-05 RC-2.

This is exactly this bead's thesis: mark_shutting_down()/release-lease-first on clean stop eliminates the zero-daemon window; the TTL wait should apply ONLY to crashes. Corollary for RF-2: the lease TTL bounds write-unavailability during failover (LiteFS Consul default 10s; nexus ~3.0s) — if the flock stall can exceed the TTL, a live primary gets falsely evicted. Same analog tracked for T3 in nexus-6o4uj.

title: RDR-151 P1.1: deregister/close accepted socket read-fd on peer-death-during-dispatch (Gap 1 + Gap 2, the peg)
description:
RDR-151 Phase 1, the LOAD-BEARING fix for the 100% CPU peg. Mechanism (CONFIRMED + REPRODUCED in Phase 0, nexus-8voni): a client RSTs/abruptly dies WHILE the handler is parked in 'await asyncio.to_thread(...)' mid-dispatch (NOT during readexactly — that path self-heals via IncompleteReadError at t2_daemon.py:1274). The peer's RST leaves the accepted socket's READ fd registered + perpetually-reported-ready by kqueue, spinning the event loop at kevent(timeout=0) = 100% CPU, no log. Post-dispatch writer.write/drain (t2_daemon.py:1298) then raises the uncaught ConnectionResetError.

FILES: src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py _handle_connection (1270-1304) + transport layer.

TDD (test-first, project rule):
1. The Gap-1 regression test ALREADY EXISTS: tests/daemon/rdr151_phase0_heavy.py (heavy churn: real memory.put writes + abrupt-RST-mid-write). Pre-fix it reproduces ~6500-7000 select/s (3x baseline, SPIN!) + 404k uncaught ConnectionResetError. Wire it as a pytest regression test (currently a standalone harness) asserting POST-FIX select/s stays at baseline (no SPIN! window) over the churn run. Exact threshold from the harness: baseline ~2150 select/s, bug >5000; assert sustained < a fixed bound (e.g. <=3000) — NOT an inequality that a regression could slip past (mem:feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression).
2. THEN implement: ensure the accepted socket read fd is deregistered/closed when the peer dies during dispatch. Candidate approaches: detect connection_lost at the transport level and close the writer; and/or guard the dispatch await so a mid-dispatch peer death tears the transport down rather than leaving the fd in the selector. Gap-2 catch of (ConnectionResetError, OSError) around dispatch+drain is NECESSARY hygiene (kills the RC-6 404k-traceback spam) but PROVEN INSUFFICIENT ALONE to stop the spin (Phase 0 proved this — do NOT ship the catch as 'the fix').

RF-1b amplification: harness spin DECAYS after ~4 min (3x), production SUSTAINED 100%; the sustained peg likely needs continuous mid-dispatch deaths (always-fresh leaked fds). The fix must zero the spin regardless; confirm amplification path during validation.

Use mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking for the transport-layer fix design (asyncio fd-lifecycle is subtle — normal asyncio DOES remove the reader on EOF and force-close on RST, so the fix is the abrupt-death-during-dispatch path specifically). Use Serena (find_referencing_symbols) before any signature change. Update continuation state (memory_put project=nexus title=continuation-state-rdr151.md) after each milestone. SPAWN parallel sub-agents to conserve context where independent.

Context: docs/rdr/rdr-151-daemon-event-loop-selector-spin-write-contention.md §Research Findings RF-1; T2 nexus/daemon-concurrency-diagnosis-2026-06-05; T1 scratch tag rdr-planning-context key c7465c8b.

comments.text: WEB-RESEARCH INPUT (RDR-147 instance, T3: research-sqlite-daemon-concurrency-architectures-2026-06-05): nexus is Bedrock-shaped (daemon owns sole writer). Bedrock DISABLED POSIX advisory locks to make non-daemon file writes structurally impossible — stronger than nexus's by-convention single-writer. The recurring database-is-locked class = incomplete daemon-fronting (every writer must go via the daemon). LiteFS elects its writer via lease + a FUSE interpose so apps do ordinary file I/O and the proxy routes writes — materially-different/arguably-better; eliminates the 'client forgot to use the daemon' seam. title: RDR-151 Phase 0: reproduce + pin the asyncio selector busy-loop (RF-1)
description: RDR-151 Phase 0 (gates the fix design). Build an instrumented asyncio UNIX-domain reproducer harness mirroring T2Daemon._handle_connection (readexactly-framed loop, IncompleteReadError break, finally writer.close(), NO ConnectionResetError catch). Drive clients through 4 exit modes: abrupt RST (SO_LINGER 0), half-close (shutdown SHUT_WR), mid-frame disconnect, idle-after-frame. Instrument the event loop's selector (wrap select()) to detect the kevent(timeout=0) spin and name the perpetually-ready fd. ACCEPTANCE: identify which exit mode pins the loop at ~100% CPU and which fd it reports ready every iteration; that answers RF-1 (discriminates candidate b = ConnectionResetError/transport-teardown vs a/c = event-loop-scheduling). The harness becomes the Gap-1 regression test. Until this lands, no Phase-1 transport fix is written (RDR-151 Decision). RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-151-daemon-event-loop-selector-spin-write-contention.md.
notes: RF-1 ANSWERED — SPIN REPRODUCED (rdr151_phase0_heavy.py, 2026-06-05). Heavy churn (real memory.put + abrupt-RST-mid-write) produced ~6500-7000 select/s spin (3x baseline, SPIN! for ~4min) with ready-fd set dominated by accepted connection sockets (fd 33/34/35/32/36), +404k uncaught ConnectionResetError. MECHANISM: RST while handler is parked in await asyncio.to_thread(write) mid-dispatch (NOT during readexactly — that path cleans up). The peer's RST leaves the accepted socket's READ fd registered+perpetually-ready in kqueue -> loop spins; post-dispatch writer.write/drain then raises uncaught ConnectionResetError. fd is a connection socket, not the self-pipe — matches live lsof. FIX must deregister/close the accepted fd on peer-death-during-dispatch (Gap-2 read-loop catch alone is insufficient, proven). Harness = Gap-1 regression test. Refinement RF-1b: harness spin decays after ~4min (3x), production sustained 100% — amplification (continuous mid-dispatch deaths) to confirm at Phase-1 validation. Repro log /tmp/rdr151-REPRO-heavy.log. Phase 0 COMPLETE.

title: [P1] Daemon self-pegs 100% CPU on aspect_queue.reclaim_stale + 'database is locked' — recurs on lone 5.10.2 daemon (we61e fix incomplete); root-cause RDR needed
description:
RECURRING across releases — per the repeated-patch rule (feedback_root_cause_after_repeated_patches), STOP patching and root-cause via RDR.

Observed live on 5.10.2 (Desktop-update shakeout 2026-06-05): a SINGLE clean daemon (38476, sole memory.db holder) sustains 100% CPU (100/100/100/98.4 over 16s, NOT a transient drain) spinning on op='aspect_queue.reclaim_stale' with 'database is locked' (6x in recent log). So this is INTRA-daemon contention: the daemon's own reclaim loop contends with its own request-serving path on the SQLite write lock, retried as a tight spin (no backoff) -> pegged core.

History: nexus-we61e (closed, shipped 5.10.1 PR #1126 "daemon-owned aspect reclaim") moved reclaim off per-process workers to a single daemon-owned loop. That fixed CROSS-process contention but the INTRA-daemon reclaim-vs-serve contention + tight lock-retry spin remain. The 100% CPU + reclaim_stale + database-is-locked signature is back on 5.10.2.

Downstream cascade (this is why it matters): the CPU peg makes the daemon slow to answer hello() -> ensure-running declares it stale and spawns a replacement -> takeover churn -> 2+ daemons coexist (nexus-x47yx) -> T2 writes hard-fail with 'database is locked'. So the reclaim spin is the UPSTREAM trigger of the x47yx multi-daemon T2-write-failure cascade.

Also observed: an entry reported 'Stored: id=2313' read back as 'entry not found' under the peg (read/write reliability under contention; possibly WAL-checkpoint-lag vs read-bypass, needs confirmation — could be a benign read-failure-as-not-found rather than data loss).

ROOT-CAUSE DIRECTIONS (for the RDR): exponential backoff (not tight retry) on reclaim lock failure; raise busy_timeout; run reclaim on a cadence that yields to serving (e.g. only when idle, or with a serialized single-writer queue inside the daemon); or make reclaim a separate connection with a bounded retry + skip-if-locked. The fix must stop the 100% CPU spin on a lone daemon.

Related: nexus-x47yx (the multi-daemon T2-write-failure cascade this triggers), nexus-we61e (the incomplete 5.10.1 fix).
notes: POST-5.10.3-DEPLOY VALIDATION (2026-06-05): the reclaim-RPC-noop fix shipped in 5.10.3. RESULT: T2 WRITES NOW WORK (put/get/delete clean, id=2315) — the user-visible 'database is locked' write-failure breakage is RESOLVED, because the daemon stays SINGULAR (spawn-lock guard holds, observed 'refusing to start a second instance') so there's no multi-daemon contention. HOWEVER the reclaim fix is NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT: a LONE 5.10.3 daemon STILL pegs ~100% CPU (trend 99/98/0.7/98/100/100/99/99 over 80s, singular throughout) with the reclaim no-op firing 0 times and ZERO log output. So this is a SEPARATE silent spin, NOT the reclaim flood (substantive-critic Q1 confirmed correct). Cannot py-spy without root. Pattern (mostly 100%, brief dips to ~0, no log, lone asyncio daemon) suggests a background coroutine busy-looping. NEXT: need 'sudo py-spy dump --pid <daemon>' to identify the spin, OR add a SIGUSR1 faulthandler stack-dump to the daemon. Keep this bead open as the silent-peg root-cause; reclaim flood is closed by 5.10.3.

title: Pre-push stacked-review reminder hook + T1 session-marker reliability fixes
description:
Opt-in conexus PreToolUse[Bash] hook that reminds (permissionDecision: ask, fail-open, never hard-block) when git push / gh pr create runs without a review-completed marker in this session's T1 scratch (the marker /conexus:code-review writes). Blocked on three real T1 reliability defects the prototype hit: (1) MCP scratch tool and nx scratch CLI resolve DIFFERENT T1 sessions, so an MCP-written marker is invisible to a shell hook (CLI-only); (2) nx scratch list/search session scope is looser than 'this Claude session' (marker found from unrelated cwd → cross-session leak); (3) nx scratch search is semantic/nondeterministic for a presence check, and list has no deterministic filter.

## Context
GH #956 (2026-05-25), filed from Luciferase RDR-004 where stacked review caught a CRITICAL silent-data-loss bug green tests missed. Directly automates the CLAUDE.md stacked-reviewers discipline (code-review-expert THEN substantive-critic at each increment).
design: Likely needs an RDR: defect #1 (MCP/CLI T1 session unification) is architectural and touches RDR-105 (T1 sub-agent contract) + RDR-094 (MCP-owned T1 chroma lifecycle). Sub-parts: (a) unify session resolution across MCP server + CLI OR make the marker contract explicitly CLI-only; (b) per-session signal (propagate real session id to CLI / --session flag); (c) nx scratch has deterministic primitive; (d) opt-in PreToolUse[Bash] hook (RDR-121 hook-enforced-routing precedent). /conexus:code-review + /conexus:substantive-critique write the canonical marker via the unified path.
acceptance_criteria: git push/gh pr create without a stacked-review marker -> ask reminder; with marker -> silent. No false positives on echo/commit-message text containing the phrases (segment-start anchoring). Marker reliably written/read regardless of MCP-vs-CLI write path, scoped to the current session. Deterministic presence primitive (e.g. nx scratch has <substr> [--tag][--session], exit 0/1). Fail-open; never hard-blocks on hook error. Hook shipped under conexus plugin hooks/, opt-in via setting/env.
notes:
EMPIRICAL PROBE 2026-06-04 (session c76c1995) — corrects issue #956 premise. MCP scratch put succeeded; 'nx scratch list' from a sibling shell raised T1ServerNotFoundError. resolve_active_session_id() returns the SAME c76c1995 on both MCP and CLI (via ~/.config/nexus/current_session), so #956 'defect #1: different sessions' is INACCURATE. Real defect: addr-file discovery fails from the sibling/hook context — find_immediate_claude_pid()=66380 but read_t1_addr_for(66380)=None (addr files on disk are for other pids: Desktop 21202, stale 3944/44358). The MCP published its T1 addr under a pid the shell PPID-walk doesn't resolve to. => a CLI marker check in the hook RAISES, not just misses. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: the PreToolUse[Bash] hook must NOT depend on T1/chroma discovery. Use a discovery-free marker file under ~/.config/nexus/ keyed by current_session (reliably readable from the shell), written by the review skills, read by the hook. This removes defects #1/#2/#3 (no nx scratch has primitive needed for the hook). Caveat: this Bash runs sandboxed; PPID-walk mismatch may be partly sandbox-specific, but the hook shares that context. RDR should start from this corrected premise.
LIVE on 5.10.1 (2026-06-05 shakeout): T1 scratch HARD-FAILS via BOTH CLI and MCP. Root: current_session='2b0e933e-...' but NO t1_addr.2b0e933e lease exists (live leases are under other UUIDs: 219073cf, 7d50e596, b1881c8e, fe9be73f, all 10:15). The interactive shell session (transcript a6951124) also has no lease. Session resolution chain: NX_SESSION_ID(unset) -> current_session(2b0e933e, stale from days ago) -> t1_addr.2b0e933e(absent) -> T1ServerNotFoundError (t1.py:263 _init_new_discovery). The SessionStart hook PRINTED 'T1 scratch initialized (session: 2b0e933e)' yet wrote no lease and started no T1 server for it — the marker reports success while the lease write is missing/stale. Two distinct defects: (1) current_session not refreshed on session resume + no T1 server spun for the resolved session (RDR-149 lease-based T1 made this hard-fail where it used to flakily work); (2) CLI 'nx scratch list' dumps a full Python traceback instead of catching T1ServerNotFoundError and printing the friendly hint that the MCP path returns. Workaround: reconnect the conexus MCP extension (re-runs SessionStart) or NX_T1_ISOLATED=1.
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-06-05 -> dedicated P0 emergency bead filed (see below) + full forensics in T2 t1-session-mismatch-emergency-forensics-2026-06-05. Core: MCP NX_SESSION_ID (lease key) diverges from SessionStart current_session; warm-publish drops the claude_pid fallback (t1_lease.py:_payload line 162) and discover_t1_transient_for_claude skips session-keyed leases.
close_reason: WONTFIX / never. Opt-in pre-push stacked-review reminder hook — decided not worth building (2026-06-24). The stacked-review discipline has held by convention without automation (it caught a real Critical in nexus-1714 this same session). Cost (RDR-scoped feature: marker write path + hook + opt-in wiring, plus the T1-reliability tangle in the notes) exceeds value. Corrected discovery-free-marker design preserved in bead notes if ever revived. GH #956 can be closed as wontfix.

title: P0.3: Design spike — interactive-vs-batch fairness cross-client signaling protocol (PC-2)
description: RDR-146 §Approach items 3+4 (collapsed per PC-5) + PC-2. THE main genuine design unknown. Serializing writes through the single T2 daemon removes WAL contention but starvation re-emerges if background fills the queue faster than the daemon drains. SPECIFY the cross-client signaling protocol BEFORE implementation: (a) how interactive clients register priority — priority bit on the write RPC, interactive|batch; (b) how background nx index repo learns an interactive catalog write is pending — daemon probe RPC vs push; (c) skip semantics — skip-until-retry-window vs buffer-locally. Mirror RDR-129 B2 bounded-retry in the serving dispatch. Resolve item-4 (--on-locked=skip target) as the SAME probe (PC-5: once the daemon owns the writer, 'catalog writer available' is always true to a background client, so item-4 becomes 'ask the daemon whether an interactive write is in flight'). Output: a locked design doc (T2 memory) that P2.1 implements. Run substantive-critic on the design before locking.
design: Leading option (Open Questions): daemon-side priority bit + 'background skips catalog writer when interactive write in flight' probe, against the respawn-within-1-min observation. FIFO-with-priority-bit alone only reorders queued items — the probe is what kills the race.
acceptance_criteria: Locked design doc in T2: priority-bit RPC shape, interactive-pending probe mechanism, skip semantics, bounded-retry contract; items 3 and 4 shown to collapse into one mechanism (or a documented reason to keep separate); substantive-critic clean
close_reason: Design spike complete: probe + producer back-pressure (NOT a daemon priority queue). Priority bit on RPC envelope (default batch), _interactive_write_deadline window + catalog.is_interactive_write_pending() read-only probe op, bounded indexer yield loop mirroring RDR-129 B2. Items 3+4 collapse (PC-5). Skip-not-buffer (indexer idempotent). Memo: T1 51f01bbb / T2 rdr/146-pc2-fairness-design. Feeds nexus-5p2ci.12.

title: P0.2: Decision — does the indexer hot path need catalog.register_many coarse op?
description: RDR-146 §Approach item 1 carried-unknown + PC-4 residual. The denylisted transaction()/bulk_load_documents() @contextmanager batch paths (t2_daemon.py:496-513) cannot route over RPC. RF-3 says the #1046 hot path (_catalog_hook per-file loop, indexer.py:717) is per-record register()/update() — ALREADY served — so likely NO new op is needed. INVESTIGATE and DECIDE: confirm RF-3 against the actual indexer write path; determine whether a JSON-shaped coarse op (catalog.register_many doing the transaction server-side) is warranted for indexer throughput, or whether per-record routing suffices. Output a written decision (T2 memory). This decision gates declaring the item-1 cutover complete — if register_many is needed it must exist BEFORE wave-B cutover routes the indexer batch paths.
design: If register_many warranted: server-side transaction wrapping N register() calls, JSON-round-trippable args, registered in _build_dispatch_table, exposed on T2Client.catalog. Mirror existing register RPC shape.
acceptance_criteria: Written decision recorded in T2: per-record-only vs register_many-needed, with file:line evidence from the indexer write path; if needed, scope of the new RPC op specified
close_reason: Decision: per-record register/update/create_link suffices; no register_many. Hot path (indexer _catalog_hook loop, doc_indexer, pipeline_stages, dt.py) is already per-record with per-record commits; transaction()/bulk_load_documents() are rebuild/manifest-only (denylisted, correctly client-local). Per-RPC overhead negligible vs per-record fsync. No preventive scope.

title: purposes.py registry path breaks in installed wheel — all purpose aliases resolve to 'unknown' in prod
description:
PURPOSES_YML in src/nexus/plans/purposes.py:39 uses `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent.parent / "conexus" / "plans" / "purposes.yml"`.

Resolves in the dev tree but NOT in any installed artifact (uv-tool, .mcpb, chat surface): there the registry ships at `nexus/_resources/plans/purposes.yml` (hatch force-include `conexus/plans` -> `nexus/_resources/plans`). So `PURPOSES_YML.exists()` is False -> `_load_registry()` returns `{}` -> `resolve_purpose()` reports every alias (find-implementations, decision-evolution, reference-chain, documentation-for, ...) as unknown. The entire RDR-078 P3 purpose-alias layer is DEAD in production.

Confirmed live 2026-06-02 via chat-surface shakeout: `traverse(purpose="find-implementations")` -> "warning: unknown purpose".

Fix: use `importlib.resources.files("nexus") / "_resources" / "plans" / "purposes.yml"` (same idiom as repair.py:360). Same broken pattern also at commands/catalog.py:57.

Root cause it shipped: the existing test uses `_registry_override`, bypassing the file load. Add a test that loads the REAL resource and asserts find-implementations -> [implements, implements-heuristic].
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1096 (merged to develop 2026-06-05, merge 4701e25c). purposes.yml now resolved via importlib.resources; regression test tests/test_purposes_registry.py added. Stranded in_progress/open after merge.

title: RDR-126 follow-up: first-run banner reaches the model but not the Claude Desktop user (content-prepend channel paraphrased away)

Root cause: in Claude Desktop chat the model summarizes/collapses tool-result content, so the content[0].text prepend (the banner's only channel, since A2/notifications was deemed likely-false) reaches the model+data layer but not the user's screen. The banner is RDR-126's signature feature and was designed FOR the Desktop surface, so a channel that Desktop paraphrases away undercuts it. Verified the mechanism works (p6-clean-run.sh reads raw content and sees the banner; green tests pass) -- this is a delivery-channel efficacy gap on the Desktop surface specifically, not a code bug. Options to evaluate: (a) deliver via MCP server 'instructions' at initialize (like apply_embedder_notice) so it shows in the extension's context rather than a tool result; (b) re-test A2 notifications/message on current Claude Desktop; (c) a system-reminder-style block the model is told to relay verbatim; (d) accept Desktop limitation + rely on docs. Relates RDR-126 §3, A2. Evidence: T2 (this bead) + the marker + conexus-5.9.0.dist-info under Claude-P6 profile.
close_reason: Closed

(A) Extend t2_status_cmd (src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:613). The status command already prints every discovery-file key via the for key, value in data.items() loop (daemon.py:652) — and the discovery payload already carries daemon_version (_build_discovery_payload, t2_daemon.py:522-538, field added at :536, sourced from _daemon_version() → importlib.metadata.version("conexus"), :556). So "daemon version from discovery token" is already surfaced by the generic key loop; verify P4.1's assertion shape — it likely wants an explicit/labeled daemon_version line and a --json field, not just incidental dict iteration. The genuinely new field is restart-count-in-interval: read it from the sentinel file (see B) and add it to both the human output (after the key loop, near the status: running line at :660) and the --json dict (merged like alive at :645).

(B) Sentinel-file crash-loop guard. There is currently NO respawn loop in-process — cold respawn happens in t2_ensure_running_cmd (daemon.py:733, subprocess.Popen at :891, one-shot per invocation) and via launchd/systemd KeepAlive. The guard is therefore a persistent counter keyed on a sentinel file under config_dir (alongside the discovery file; use t2_discovery_path(config_dir).parent or a sibling helper). Semantics from the plan: record daemon-start/crash timestamps in the sentinel; count restarts within a rolling window; after N failures in the window, stop respawning, log ONCE at error level (don't spam every attempt — use an "already-logged" flag in the sentinel), and clear the counter on healthy convergence (a daemon that comes up reachable and survives resets the window). The respawn-suppression check belongs in the cold-spawn path of t2_ensure_running_cmd (before the subprocess.Popen at :891) and the start-record/clear in run_t2_daemon (t2_daemon.py:1090+) / on reachability success in ensure-running (:911).

Follow the existing precedent exactly — see _T2_CYCLE_DB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS (daemon.py:668) and _T2_CYCLE_EXIT_TIMEOUT (daemon.py:679): module-level int/float with a docstring-style #: comment explaining rationale, so P4.1 can monkeypatch/shrink them without waiting a real window. Name them e.g. _CRASH_LOOP_MAX_RESTARTS: int and _CRASH_LOOP_WINDOW: float.

Atomic sentinel writes: reuse the _write_discovery_atomic pattern (t2_daemon.py:541, os.open 0o600 + os.replace) — never partial-write a file another process polls.

## RDR-140 P4.1 (nexus-0gyhe) — TESTS FIRST for daemon observability (Gap5)

Write failing tests (TDD) ahead of impl bead nexus-hrrpz. Extend tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_observability.py (currently 208 lines, 4 classes: TestDaemonLogging, TestStatusLiveness, TestStopBreadcrumbDurability). Add two new test classes covering the two Gap5 deliverables. DO NOT implement production code — these tests are expected RED until P4.2.

### (a) Status surface tests — `nx daemon t2 status` reports version + restart-count
t2_status_cmd at src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:613 currently iterates data.items() from the discovery JSON and appends a synthetic status: running / status: STALE line plus a liveness probe (os.kill(pid, 0)). The discovery payload already carries daemon_version and start_time (built by _build_discovery_payload at t2_daemon.py:524: format_version, uds_path, tcp_host, tcp_port, pid, daemon_version, start_time). So owner pid, socket liveness, and daemon version are already presentable — assert they SURFACE explicitly in status output (not just that the raw dict is dumped). The NEW requirement is restart count in interval, which does not yet exist in the payload — the test must assert the status surface reports it (sourced from the sentinel/crash-loop guard state, see (b)). Follow the existing TestStatusLiveness pattern: CliRunner().invoke(main, ["daemon","t2","status","--config-dir",str(tmp_path)]), seed discovery via a helper like _write_discovery(config_dir, pid) (extend the existing module-level _write_discovery which writes daemon_version: "5.0.2"). Assert on result.output for: owner pid present, socket-liveness state, daemon_version string, and restart-count-in-interval value. Use os.getpid() for the alive case (matches test_status_reports_running_when_pid_alive).

### (b) Crash-loop guard tests — log ONCE at error, STOP respawning after N in window
Assert that after N failures within a window, the guard logs exactly once at error level and then STOPS respawning (no Nth+1 traceback / no further spawn attempts). Determinism is mandatory: fixed clock (inject/monkeypatch the time source — do NOT call real time.monotonic/datetime.now), seeded window, and a sentinel file in tmp_path as the crash-loop state store. The respawn surface lives in the ensure-running path: t2_ensure_running_cmd at commands/daemon.py:760 (cold-spawn/respawn logic, see _T2_CYCLE_EXIT_TIMEOUT and reap comments at :670–:880). The guard is new code (P4.2) — the test pins its contract: count failures in a sliding/seeded window via the sentinel file; on the (N+1)th attempt within the window, emit a single structured error event (capture via a fake log or structlog capture, matching the _FakeLog pattern in TestStopBreadcrumbDurability) and refuse to respawn; the guard CLEARS on healthy convergence (test that a successful start resets the sentinel/count). Assert the log fires exactly once (not per-attempt) and that no exception/traceback propagates on the suppressed attempt.

### Conventions to follow
- macOS AF_UNIX 104-char cap: real-subprocess tests use tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=..., dir="/tmp") not tmp_path (see TestDaemonLogging). The two new classes are mostly CliRunner/unit-level and can use tmp_path, but any real daemon spawn must use the short /tmp config_dir.
- Exact assertions (== N), never >= — fixture-regression discipline (mem:feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression). Lock the restart count and the log-once count as exact equalities.
- Structured logging only; capture events by name (e.g. monkeypatch t2d._log with a fake that records (event, **kw)), mirroring TestStopBreadcrumbDurability._FakeLog.
- No real wall-clock sleeps for the window logic — inject the clock. Real time.sleep only for unavoidable subprocess-readiness polling.
- SPDX header already present at top of the test file; no new header needed.

### Cross-references
- Plan: T2 nexus/plan-rdr140-daemon-supervisor (epic nexus-7nxc2, P4 umbrella nexus-2vvdi, impl nexus-hrrpz, code-review nexus-d8qvr, critic nexus-b4nq1, validate+full-suite nexus-mxrws). P4 is blocked only on P2.5, parallel to P3.
- INVARIANT: RDR-128/129 single-writer flock is NOT touched by P4 (observability is contained/non-invariant). Don't weaken it.

## RDR-140 P3.2 (nexus-7ffls) — Implement Gap2: ownership/version-aware predecessor reaping

Goal. Replace the unconditional startup reap (the §P2 caveat) with an ownership-and-version guard in the T2 daemon's predecessor sweep. A peer is reaped ONLY IF one of:
1. its PID is dead, OR
2. daemon_version != current_version (cross-version transition), OR
3. a health-ping to its advertised socket fails (orphaned/hung writer).

A healthy, same-version peer must NOT be SIGTERM'd — the new daemon should attach to it and quietly exit (loser-attach path wired in P1/P2). The fcntl flock (RDR-128/129) stays the hard backstop and is NOT weakened. Orphaned writers (flock held but PID dead OR health-ping fails) MUST still be reaped. No new persisted state (A2) — the discovery token already carries pid + daemon_version + connection info (uds_path/tcp_host/tcp_port).

### Where the change lands
- src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:925 _reap_predecessor_daemon — currently builds a union of reap targets: (1) addr-file PID read from the discovery token at :957 (disc_path.read_text() → json.loads → payload["pid"]), and (2) same-db open-fd holders via _enumerate_t2_daemon_pids_for_db (:188). Today it reaps every distinct non-self target unconditionally (:972-978). The version/health guard must gate this decision.
- src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:980 _reap_one_daemon — currently liveness-checks (_pid_is_alive :97) + PID-reuse cmdline-guards (_is_t2_daemon_process :113) then SIGTERM→SIGKILL. Natural seat for the per-PID guard, OR add the guard at the call site in _reap_predecessor_daemon.

### Design notes for the guard
- current_version: _daemon_version() (:556) returns importlib.metadata.version("conexus") (falls back "0.0.0").
- peer version: read from the discovery token's daemon_version field (written by _build_discovery_payload :522, key set at :536). The open-fd-discovered side-orphans (target source #2) are NOT in the addr file, so they have no token daemon_version — decide their disposition explicitly (likely: no token ⇒ treat as not-same-version ⇒ reapable, OR health-ping only). Capture this decision; the P3.5 gate will cross-walk it.
- health-ping: there is currently NO ping RPC. Cheapest signal is a socket connect to the advertised endpoint (_connect_uds t2_client.py:146 / _connect_tcp :158). Successful connect (optionally a minimal round-trip frame via write_frame) = healthy; connect refused/timeout = failed-ping = reapable. Keep it bounded (short timeout) and best-effort/non-fatal, matching the existing "best-effort, never raises" contract of the reap helpers.
- The guard must be conservative on the orphan side: a peer that holds the flock/db but whose PID is dead or whose socket won't answer is exactly the WAL-contention orphan RDR-128/129 targets — it MUST still be reaped.

### Make P3.1 green
This is the impl bead for test bead nexus-r9hq0. The P3.1 tests (a)+(b)+(c) are the spec: (a) healthy same-version peer → attach, NOT reaped (assert no SIGTERM); (b) different-version peer → reaped; (c) dead-PID / failed-health-ping orphan → reaped. Run those first (RED), implement, then GREEN. If the P3.1 tests are not yet committed on this branch, confirm with the P3.1 bead before implementing — do not invent the contract.

### Gating
INVARIANT-TOUCHING. After impl: P3.3 code-review (nexus-4n1mw) + P3.4 substantive-critic (nexus-dzf1q) BRIEFED with the RDR-128/129 flock invariant, then P3.6 test-validate (nexus-zblru), then the P3.5 GATE (nexus-x2k4b) which runs the repeated multi-stack race harness + orphan-reap test + /conexus:phase-review-gate rdr-140 --phase 3 cross-walk. The schema-mismatch-fallback-while-daemon-alive scope decision must be recorded on the gate.

## RDR-140 P3.1 (nexus-r9hq0) — TESTS FIRST for ownership-aware reaping discrimination

Write failing tests (TDD; impl is P3.2 nexus-7ffls) that encode the P3 invariant the gate (P3.5 nexus-x2k4b) checks: _reap_predecessor_daemon / _reap_one_daemon must reap ONLY IF (pid dead) OR (daemon_version != current) OR (health-ping fails) — and must NEVER SIGTERM a healthy current-version peer (→ attach instead). The RDR-128/129 single-writer flock backstop is NOT weakened: orphan/dead-PID writers STILL get reaped.

### Where the work goes
Extend tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_startup_invariant.py. The existing TestDaemonReapsPredecessor (line 226) and TestDaemonSweepsSideOrphans (line 356) classes are the harness to build on — they monkeypatch td._is_t2_daemon_process, td._pid_is_alive, and td.os.kill (capturing kills: list[tuple[pid,sig]]) for determinism, and seed a discovery file via the per-class _write_discovery(config_dir, pid) helper. Add a sibling class (e.g. TestDaemonReapDiscrimination) plus extend the multi-stack race harness as the regression gate (P2.1 nexus-remh4 lands the NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR / K-parallel-ensure-running harness in this same file — build the version-skew convergence case on top of it).

### Three required cases with exact assertions
(a) Healthy current-version peer is NEVER reaped. Discovery token carries daemon_version == _daemon_version() (current) and the peer's health-ping succeeds → assert kills == [] (0 SIGTERM, 0 SIGKILL) and the new daemon attaches. The current _write_discovery helper writes only {pid, tcp_port} — extend it to also write daemon_version (and whatever conn field the health-ping reads) so the discrimination predicate has its inputs. A2 guarantees the token already carries pid+daemon_version+conn — assert NO new discovery state is introduced.

(b) Orphan-writer reap STILL works (RDR-128 backstop MUST NOT regress). Simulate a flock-escaped daemon whose PID is dead OR whose health-ping fails → assert it IS reaped (SIGTERM present in kills, escalating to SIGKILL on ignore per the existing test_escalates_to_sigkill_when_sigterm_ignored pattern). Cover both arms: dead-PID (_pid_is_alive → False) and health-ping-fails-while-alive.

(c) Version-skew convergence. Start an old-version daemon (discovery daemon_version != current), launch K current-version supervisors → assert exactly 1 reap of the stale daemon, 1 new daemon survives, the rest attach (0 additional reaps). This is the multi-stack harness extension; run it REPEATEDLY (stochastic, matching the P2.1 repeated-run discipline).

### Key implementation seams the tests pin (impl lands in P3.2)
_reap_predecessor_daemon (t2_daemon.py:925) currently reaps unconditionally — it unions the addr-file pid and the same-db open-fd sweep (_enumerate_t2_daemon_pids_for_db :188), then calls _reap_one_daemon (:980) for each non-self pid. _reap_one_daemon today guards only on _pid_is_alive (:97) and _is_t2_daemon_process (:113) before SIGTERM. P3 inserts the version/health discrimination BEFORE the kill. Current daemon version source is _daemon_version() (:556, importlib.metadata.version("conexus")); discovery payload built by _build_discovery_payload (:522, carries pid + daemon_version). Tests must read daemon_version off the discovery token and compare to _daemon_version(); monkeypatch _daemon_version to pin current vs stale deterministically rather than relying on the installed wheel version.

Note the existing reap covers two target sources (addr-file pid AND open-fd holders); discrimination tests should cover BOTH paths — a healthy current-version peer found via the open-fd sweep must also be spared, not just the addr-file one.

### Key files
- tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_startup_invariant.py — add discrimination + version-skew test classes; extend the per-class _write_discovery helper to emit daemon_version/conn; build the version-skew case on the P2.1 multi-stack harness (TestDaemonReapsPredecessor:226, TestDaemonSweepsSideOrphans:356)
- src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py — SUT: _reap_predecessor_daemon:925, _reap_one_daemon:980, _pid_is_alive:97, _is_t2_daemon_process:113, _enumerate_t2_daemon_pids_for_db:188, _daemon_version:556, _build_discovery_payload:522, _PREDECESSOR_REAP_TIMEOUT:75
- src/nexus/daemon/discovery.py — discovery token read/validate path (pid liveness, format_version); payload shape the tests seed
- src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py — handshake/version-compat reference (client_version:317, daemon_version handshake:358) for how health/version is read off a live peer
- docs/rdr/rdr-140-t2-daemon-supervisor-ownership-model.md — RDR being implemented; P3 §Approach the gate cross-walks

design:
## RDR-140 P2.2 (nexus-fkhe2) — Implement Gap3: election-coordination flock + re-discover

Goal. Add single-flight election around the discover→spawn decision in t2_ensure_running_cmd so K parallel `nx daemon t2 ensure-running` against one memory.db converge to exactly 1 cold spawn with K-1 quiet attaches — eliminating the crash+reap churn (A4 measured started=1/crashed=9/stop_requested=1). Makes the P2.1 harness (nexus-remh4) single-spawn convergence assertions pass.

### Where the change goes
src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:760 t2_ensure_running_cmd. Three control regions today:
1. Fast pre-discovery — running = _running_daemon() (line 815). If a matching-version daemon is up it echoes "already running" and returns. KEEP this as the lock-free fast path (common case skips the flock entirely).
2. Stale-version cycle — lines 826–880 (SIGTERM + bounded PID-exit poll). Untouched in spirit; the election lock wraps the spawn that follows.
3. Cold spawn + reachability poll — lines 882–933 (subprocess.Popen of `nx daemon t2 start`, then _daemon_is_alive() poll).

### Gap3 shape
After the fast pre-discovery misses (no live matching daemon), before cold-spawning:
- Acquire a blocking-with-timeout fcntl flock on a dedicated election lock file (NOT the daemon's own lifetime spawn lock — see constraint). Use fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX) with a bounded wait (signal.alarm or a bounded retry loop on LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB), since the daemon's _acquire_spawn_lock uses LOCK_NB and would never block.
- AFTER acquiring, RE-DISCOVER via _running_daemon(). If a matching-version daemon appeared while waiting, attach (echo quiet "already running"/skip) and return WITHOUT spawning — only the lock holder cold-spawns.
- Hold the election lock across spawn + reachability poll, then release (or let it auto-release on process exit).
- Wrap in try/finally so the fd is closed; fcntl flock auto-releases on holder death (A4 verified) → no deadlock if the holder crashes mid-spawn; waiters then win the lock, re-discover (no daemon), and one spawns. Add a module constant for the election-wait timeout (mirror _T2_CYCLE_EXIT_TIMEOUT / _T2_CYCLE_DB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS style at daemon.py:663–679 so tests can shrink it).

### Pattern to reuse
src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:1013 _acquire_spawn_lock (fcntl import, os.open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT, 0o600), errno EAGAIN/EACCES handling) and :239 _spawn_lock_path_for_db (data-file-sibling lock anchoring). The election lock must be a DISTINCT file from _SPAWN_LOCK_FILE (t2_spawn.lock, daemon.py:1027) and _spawn_lock_path_for_db (<db>.spawn_lock, daemon grabs for its lifetime at :1044). If ensure-running held the daemon's own spawn lock, the spawned child `nx daemon t2 start` would hit EAGAIN on its _acquire_spawn_lock and exit → zero daemons. Anchor the election lock on the db path too (e.g. <db>.election_lock) so daemons started from different config_dirs against the same data file contend on the same election.

### Critical constraints
- MUST NOT touch _reap_predecessor_daemon (t2_daemon.py:940) or _reap_one_daemon (:980) — that is P3 (gated). Unconditional startup-reap caveat remains; P2 only bounds healthy-peer-kill to the single-spawn case.
- Do NOT weaken the RDR-128/129 single-writer flock — it stays the hard backstop. The election lock is a coordination layer in front of spawn, separate from the daemon's lifetime writer-ownership lock.
- Election lock is blocking-with-timeout, not LOCK_NB (waiters block then re-discover, not fail fast).
- Common-case daemon-already-up path MUST stay lock-free (fast pre-discovery short-circuits before any flock).
- P2.1 harness convergence case must pass: 1 t2_daemon_started, K-1 quiet attaches, 0 t2_daemon_crashed, 0 healthy-peer SIGTERMs. Also election-lock-holder-dies-mid-spawn → waiters recover, no deadlock (A4 auto-release).
- Structured logging only (structlog.get_logger(__name__)); CLI user-facing output via click.echo(..., err=True) for warnings. No print().

design:
## RDR-140 P2.1 (nexus-remh4) — Multi-stack race harness (TESTS FIRST, P2/P3 gate)

Goal. Build a NEW, deterministic, load-bearing test harness that spawns K parallel `nx daemon t2 ensure-running` invocations against ONE memory.db (isolated via NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR) and asserts the convergence invariant. This harness is the gate artifact for both P2 and P3.

### What to build
New file: tests/daemon/test_t2_multistack_race.py

Scenario 1 — K-way cold-start race (run repeatedly). Spawn K concurrent ensure-running invocations sharing one config_dir / one memory.db. After convergence assert, from the daemon log stream:
- exactly 1 t2_daemon_started
- K-1 quiet attaches (idempotent no-ops — _running_daemon() returns the live current-version daemon, command returns silently)
- 0 t2_daemon_crashed
- 0 healthy-peer SIGTERMs (0 reaps/cycles of a healthy, current-version peer)

A4 baseline (what current code does — the reason this is a gate): current code converges to 1 daemon but via crash+reap churn — research recorded started=1 / crashed=9 / stop_requested=1. So the harness MUST run repeatedly (race outcomes stochastic); a single green pass proves nothing. Loop N times (or parametrize over a seed range) and assert clean-convergence on every iteration.

## RDR-140 P1.3 — Implement Gap1: loser quiet-attach + self-healing discovery re-assert (nexus-h2oko)

Make the spawn-lock LOSER a typed non-error outcome and make the spawn-lock HOLDER self-heal its own discovery file. Test bead nexus-266iu (P1.1) authors the failing tests first; this bead makes P1.1(b) green. Stacked review follows: P1.4 code-review (nexus-jtdsm) + P1.5 critic (nexus-ktsjv) → P1.6 test-validate (nexus-m63u0).

### IMPORTANT path correction
The bead text and plan say src/nexus/db/t2_daemon.py, but the file actually lives at src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py (cited lines :1013/:642/:709/:734/:1090/:1133 all match this file). src/nexus/db/t2_daemon.py does not exist.

### Part (1) — Loser becomes a typed quiet exit, NEVER constructs T2Database
_acquire_spawn_lock (t2_daemon.py:1013) currently raises T2DaemonError on OSError/errno.EAGAIN/errno.EACCES (BlockingIOError) for BOTH the config_dir-scoped flock (:1030) and the db_path-scoped flock (:1048). Today that T2DaemonError propagates up through start() (:645) → run_t2_daemon._main (:1121) → the bare except Exception: crash path at :1129–1134 which logs t2_daemon_crashed WITH a traceback and re-raises (nonzero exit).

Change required:
- On lock-contention (EAGAIN/EACCES) treat the loss as a typed non-error outcome, not an exception that reaches the crash path. Log t2_daemon_spawn_lost at info (no traceback), poll briefly for the winner's discovery file/socket, then exit 0.
- A1 invariant (verified — mem:140-research-A1, rdr140-a1-verification-spawn-lock-loser-2026-05-31): the loser must NEVER reach T2Database(...) construction at :658. Spawn lock acquired at start():645 strictly BEFORE T2Database open at :658, and _reap_predecessor_daemon() (:651) sits between them — the quiet-exit must short-circuit before both. Do not reorder.
- Discovered-but-unreachable socket: if the winner's discovery file exists but its UDS/TCP is not yet connectable, fall back to polling — do NOT treat a stale t2_addr as a live attach. A stale-pid discovery payload is a known hazard (_reap_predecessor_daemon reads t2_discovery_path at :957 and guards pid liveness via _pid_is_alive :97 + _is_t2_daemon_process :113). Reuse the liveness/connectability discriminators; a set-but-unreachable target keeps polling until loser_poll_timeout, then exits 0 regardless.

Mechanism note: cleanest seam is to signal "lost" from _acquire_spawn_lock distinctly from real errors (e.g. a dedicated SpawnLockLost/sentinel return) and handle it in run_t2_daemon / start BEFORE any T2Database construction, so the crash path at :1129 is never entered for a benign loss. Preserve the existing fd-leak cleanup on the second-lock-fail branch (:1050–1057) and the genuine-error re-raise for non-EAGAIN/EACCES OSError.

### Part (2) — Self-healing discovery re-assert (HOLDER only)
The spawn-lock WINNER starts a periodic asyncio task that re-asserts / validates its own t2_addr discovery file (path from t2_discovery_path(config_dir) :516; write via _write_discovery_atomic :541, payload via _build_discovery_payload :522). Start it after start() writes discovery at :679. Re-use the atomic-write helper; do not hand-roll a second writer.

RDR-129 early-unlink ordering constraint (hard): stop() (:709) unlinks t2_addr at :734 (self._discovery_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)) BEFORE the spawn lock releases (lock release deferred to OS-on-exit per RDR-129 A2 docstring :712–725). Therefore:
- (i) The re-assert task MUST be CANCELLED at the very START of stop() — before the :734 unlink — otherwise the periodic task re-creates the discovery file the unlink just removed (resurrection race). Add the cancel + await-cancelled as the first action in stop(), ahead of the server-close block at :726.
- (ii) loser_poll_timeout >= reassert_interval + worst_case_write_latency, so a loser polling for the winner's file never times out inside a window where the holder is mid-re-assert.

Module-constant defaults (place near _PREDECESSOR_REAP_TIMEOUT :75 / _DISPATCH_RETRY_SLEEPS :85, follow that naming + comment-rationale convention):
- _REASSERT_INTERVAL: float = 1.0
- _LOSER_POLL_TIMEOUT: float = 3.0
Keep them module-level so tests can shrink them.

- Loser NEVER constructs T2Database (A1; strictly before :658).
- t2_daemon_spawn_lost at info, NO traceback, exit 0.
- Discovered-but-unreachable → poll, do NOT attach to a stale addr.
- Re-assert task cancelled at START of stop() before the :734 unlink.
- _LOSER_POLL_TIMEOUT (3s) >= _REASSERT_INTERVAL (1s) + worst_case_write_latency.
- Defaults as module constants (1s / 3s).
- RDR-128/129 single-writer flock backstop NOT weakened — P1 is CONTAINED; only P3 touches the invariant. Genuine-error (non-contention OSError) path must still raise.
- Structured logging only (structlog, _log :71) — never print(). Type hints on new public surface.
- Use find_referencing_symbols on _acquire_spawn_lock / start / stop before changing signatures/control flow.

design:
## RDR-140 P1.2 (nexus-2p52a) — Gap4: WAL-already + version-match migration short-circuit

Goal: In T2Database.bootstrap_schema(path), add a lock-free fast-path that returns BEFORE entering the t2_migration_flock / connection-open / apply_pending block when the DB is already at current_version AND already in WAL journal mode. Makes companion test bead P1.1(a) (nexus-266iu) green.

### Implementation site
src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py:438 bootstrap_schema (staticmethod). Current structure (L455-512):
1. path.parent.mkdir + resolve path_key (L455-459)
2. In-process _upgrade_done fast-path under _upgrade_lock (L463-465)
3. t2_migration_flock(path.parent) → _upgrade_lock → double-check → version read → sqlite3.connect → busy_timeout → _apply_pending_with_lock_retry → _upgrade_done.add (L474-512)

### What A3 mandates (authoritative — overrides loose bead phrasing)
The bead text says "if bootstrap_version(conn)==current_version". Do NOT use bootstrap_version — it is a WRITER (migrations.py:2355 calls _create_base_tables + CREATE TABLE + conn.commit()), which defeats the lock-free intent. A3 (T2 nexus_rdr/140-research-A3, VERIFIED 2026-05-31) proved the correct primitives:
- SELECT value FROM _nexus_version WHERE key='cli_version' is lock-free (succeeds under a held EXCLUSIVE writer lock).
- PRAGMA journal_mode read is lock-free.
- PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL when already-WAL is a no-op that takes no writer lock.

Fast-path: open a short read-only connection, read the stored version row and PRAGMA journal_mode; if version == current_version AND mode is already wal, short-circuit (also seed _upgrade_done so the in-process check stays consistent). Must be placed BEFORE t2_migration_flock (L474) — that's where the elided cost (flock-wait + connection + no-op apply_pending) lives.

### Correctness guardrails (from bead + A3)
- NO silent fallback for correctness: a real pending migration MUST still run. Guard the skip behind BOTH conditions — version match AND explicit WAL-pragma check. If the version row is missing/0.0.0, or journal_mode != wal, or any read raises, fall through to the existing flock+migration path unchanged.
- Migration remains cross-process flock-serialized via t2_migration_flock (unchanged) for the non-fast-path case.
- current_version is importlib.metadata.version("conexus") (matches L481-485; default "0.0.0" on failure — a "0.0.0" current_version must NOT match a real stored version, which it won't).
- Re-weighting note from A3: Gap4 is a MODEST win (secondary to Gaps 1-3); scope this bead narrowly to the short-circuit, do not broaden.

### Pattern references
- Lock-free version read mirror: stored_schema_version (L402-419) already does the exact SELECT value FROM _nexus_version WHERE key='cli_version' + connect/close pattern — reuse its shape.
- journal_mode read pattern: memory_store.py:298 (PRAGMA journal_mode fetchone).
- Existing in-process short-circuit to mirror: _upgrade_done set (nexus.db.migrations).
