title: Local-ONNX collections falsely labeled as voyage-* (RDR-103 canonical set has no local-EF token) (GH #667)
description:
## GH issue

https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/667

## TL;DR

In local (ONNX) mode, conformant collection names AND per-chunk Chroma metadata both encode `voyage-context-3` / `voyage-code-3` even though the on-disk vectors are 384-dim `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` produced by `LocalEmbeddingFunction`. The RDR-103 canonical set is hard-coded to Voyage tokens and is consulted unconditionally; the local-mode bypass swaps the embedding function at `t3.py:363-365` but never reaches the naming/metadata authority.

## Today: cosmetic + observability bug

`nx doctor`, `collection_info()`, drift checks, and calibration analysis all see `voyage-*` while the bytes are MiniLM. RDR-059's invariant ("same model at index + query time") IS intact within a single mode because `_embedding_fn` selects on `_local_mode`, not on the name.

## On mode flip (local -> cloud): real correctness bug

The mislabel becomes a query-time correctness bug:
1. User runs in local mode; collection `knowledge__foo__voyage-context-3__v1` built with 384-dim MiniLM.
2. User adds `VOYAGE_API_KEY` + `CHROMA_API_KEY`; `is_local_mode()` returns False.
3. Query takes the cloud branch in `_embedding_fn`; builds `VoyageAIEmbeddingFunction` (1024-dim).
4. Query vectors don't match collection vectors. ChromaDB rejects on dim mismatch (1024 != 384), or silently produces noise if any path coerces dims.

This is the RDR-059 class of bug closed via the model-token-in-name fix; it does NOT work in local mode because the token doesn't reflect the actual EF.

## Affected paths (from GH #667)

Collection-name construction (via `canonical_embedding_model`):
- `src/nexus/corpus.py:274`, `:307`
- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py:385`
- `src/nexus/catalog/consolidation.py:41`
- `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:3083`
- `src/nexus/commands/dt.py:63`
- `src/nexus/commands/index.py:841`

Per-chunk metadata stamping (via `index_model_for_collection`):
- `src/nexus/db/t3.py:1485` (make_chunk_metadata)
- `src/nexus/db/t3.py:1489` (collection_info)

Catalog enforcement guards (would need updating with any new token):
- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py:303-307`
- `src/nexus/catalog/collection_name.py:94-98`

## Suggested fix directions (3 options, decision time)

1. **Mode-aware canonical model** (smallest code change). Make `canonical_embedding_model(content_type)` consult `is_local_mode()` and return a local-EF token (e.g. `minilm-l6-v2-384`). Add token to `CANONICAL_EMBEDDING_MODELS`. Update catalog guards. Con: switching modes silently re-targets writes to a different physical collection (operator needs to be told).
2. **Mode is part of collection identity, not just the token**. Equivalent to (1) framed as deliberate identity bifurcation.
3. **Decouple segment from EF identifier**. Make segment 3 a model-FAMILY id; store precise EF identity in catalog metadata. Pro: future-proof. Con: bigger architectural change, breaks RDR-101/103 "name is the identity" invariant.

In all three: the local-EF dimension (384 for MiniLM, 768 for proposed bge-base upgrade) needs to be pinned in the model token so a future EF swap cannot produce vectors of different dim against the same name.

## Priority rationale

P1 because of the local->cloud flip correctness bug. Today it's cosmetic; the moment a user adds API keys the prior local data becomes unqueryable (or worse, silently noisy if any future change bypasses the dim guard). The class is rare but the failure mode is severe (data loss or silent noise).

## Refs

- RDR-101: conformant collection-name schema.
- RDR-103: canonical embedding-model set + catalog as naming authority.
- RDR-059: original model-mismatch incident; precedent for why this class matters.
- Reporter env: conexus 4.29.2 on Windows 11, Python 3.13.13.

## Acceptance

- Pick a fix option (1/2/3) and ship the migration + catalog-guard update + naming-authority change.
- Add a test that locks the chosen invariant: in local mode, a fresh collection's name + per-chunk metadata both reflect the actual EF.
- Add a regression test for the mode-flip hazard: existing local-mode collections must NOT be silently retargeted by a cloud-credentials addition (either fail loud OR migrate transparently; pick one).
- `nx doctor` reports honest collection labels in local mode.
notes:
2026-05-10 escalated to RDR-109 ("Honest Local-Mode Naming and Cross-Encoder Salience"). The fix touches naming + EF dispatch + test-suite mode-default assumptions across 30+ tests; the autouse-fixture short-circuit broke 14 OTHER tests that depended on local-mode behavior. The bigger architectural surface (test-suite mode default) needs to be designed first.

Phases under RDR-109:
- Phase 1: test-suite mode-default redesign (foundation; removes the per-PR fixture shim cycle).
- Phase 2: honest local-mode naming (this bead's scope; ships under the new mode-aware test convention).

PR #668 closed; branch deleted. Bead remains open as the implementation tracker for Phase 2.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: _run_index_frecency_only + _prune_misclassified silently no-op (RDR-108 Phase 4 review D-H4)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay review (deep-analyst agent a3cef73cb84ece27d).

## Problem (two call sites)

1. \`indexer._run_index_frecency_only\`: reads \`doc_id\` from chunk metadata to find chunks to update with new frecency_score. Phase 3 removed doc_id; the lookup returns no chunks; frecency-only is a no-op.

2. \`indexer._prune_misclassified_in_collection\`: reads \`doc_id\` to identify misclassified chunks (e.g., a .py file's chunks living in docs__). Phase 3 removed doc_id; nothing gets pruned.

## Fix
Both should query the catalog manifest for doc_id rather than reading from chunk metadata. The pattern:

\`\`\`python
chash = meta.get(\"chunk_text_hash\", \"\")[:32]
chash_to_docs = catalog.docs_for_chashes([chash, ...])
doc_id = chash_to_docs.get(chash, [None])[0]
\`\`\`

## Acceptance
- frecency-only test: index a corpus, run frecency-only with a non-zero score; verify chunk metadata frecency_score updated.
- prune-misclassified test: seed a .py chunk in docs__ collection; run prune; verify the chunk is deleted.
- Both tests FAIL on develop pre-fix.

## Note
The frecency-only no-op is the more user-visible regression — every \`nx index repo --frecency-only\` run currently does nothing.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: catalog_spans.resolve_span_text chunk:char branch returns None (RDR-108 Phase 4 review D-H3)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay review (deep-analyst agent a3cef73cb84ece27d).

## Problem
In src/nexus/catalog/catalog_spans.py, the \`resolve_span_text\` chunk:char branch reads \`doc_id\`/\`chunk_index\` from chunk metadata to resolve a span back to its source text. Phase 3 removed those fields; the branch silently returns None (or empty quote-back).

## Impact
\`chash:<hex>:<start>-<end>\` link spans don't resolve their underlying quote text any more on Phase-3 chunks. Affects the link-rendering UX and any consumer that relies on quote-back.

## Fix
Use \`catalog.get_manifest(doc_id)\` and the chash[:32] match to identify the chunk, then read line/char offsets from the manifest row's \`line_start\` / \`line_end\` / \`char_start\` / \`char_end\` (already stored in document_chunks via the manifest_write_batch_hook).

## Acceptance
- A test that creates a catalog Document, writes manifest rows with span metadata, and resolves a chash:<hex>:<start>-<end> link → expects non-empty quote-back.
- Test FAILs on develop pre-fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: link-boost + display-paths read removed doc_id from T3 metadata (RDR-108 Phase 4 review D-H1+H2)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay review (deep-analyst agent a3cef73cb84ece27d, scratch finding tag izay-finding,deep-analyst).

## Problem (two call sites, same root cause)

1. \`scoring.apply_link_boost\`: reads \`r.metadata[\"doc_id\"]\` to apply link-boost. Phase 3 (nexus-bdag) removed doc_id from chunk metadata; field is now always missing/empty for new chunks. Link-boost is silently disabled.

2. \`search_engine._attach_display_paths\`: reads \`r.metadata[\"doc_id\"]\` to inject display paths into search results. Same root cause; display path silently never appears.

## Fix
Add a shared helper:

\`\`\`python
def _attach_doc_ids_from_catalog(results, catalog):
    \"\"\"Resolve chash -> doc_id once via the catalog manifest and
    write r.metadata['doc_id'] back.\"\"\"
    chashes = [r.metadata.get(\"chunk_text_hash\", \"\")[:32] for r in results]
    chash_to_docs = catalog.docs_for_chashes([c for c in chashes if c])
    for r, c in zip(results, chashes):
        docs = chash_to_docs.get(c, [])
        if docs:
            r.metadata[\"doc_id\"] = docs[0]
\`\`\`

Call from \`apply_link_boost\` and \`_attach_display_paths\` before either reads doc_id. Both then work unchanged.

## Acceptance
- Helper function added with tests.
- apply_link_boost test verifies a chunk with link metadata gets boosted (currently it doesn't).
- _attach_display_paths test verifies display path is non-empty for a known chunk.
- Both tests would FAIL on develop pre-fix.

## Refs
- Substantive-critic S2 (docs_for_chashes normalization contract): make sure the fix uses chash[:32] and that docs_for_chashes returns matching keys. May need to land S2 first or together.
close_reason: Closed

title: umbrella: CLI destructive-verb safety rails
description:
## Scope

Two CLI verbs that delete / mutate catalog state default to the
wrong (unsafe) behaviour or lack a confirmation rail. Both turn
an operator typo into data loss with no recovery path.

## Member beads

- nexus-tnz3 (P1, bug): \`nx catalog gc\` deletes by default
  (\`--dry-run\` is opt-in, not default). Inverts the standard
  shape (\`--apply\` to commit) used by chash-reconcile and
  collection-gc.
- nexus-9nim (P2, bug): \`nx catalog link-bulk-delete\` has no
  \`--confirm\` safety rail.

## Common shape

For each member bead:
1. Make the destructive default the SAFE one (dry-run / report
   only).
2. Require an explicit \`--apply\` (or \`--yes\` / \`--confirm\`)
   flag to commit.
3. Tests that lock the new default + verify the flag actually
   triggers the destructive path.
4. Doc note in CLI reference + a one-line warning in the help
   text of any other destructive verb that already does the
   right thing (chash-reconcile, collection-gc, store delete).

## Acceptance

- Both member beads close.
- \`nx catalog gc\` (no flags) is dry-run.
- \`nx catalog link-bulk-delete\` (no flags) refuses with a
  message naming the required \`--confirm\` flag.
- A regression test guards each.

## Refs

- nexus-ks40 + nexus-w9vq: example of the correct pattern
  (\`nx catalog collection-gc\`, \`nx catalog chash-reconcile\` —
  both default dry-run, require \`--apply\`).
close_reason: Closed

title: umbrella: Windows compat (GH #619 + #621 + #622)
description:
## Scope

The nx + sn plugins were developed Mac-first. A Windows shakedown
on 2026-05-09 surfaced three coupled defects that turn an enabled
plugin install into a silently-broken Claude Code session.

## Member beads

- nexus-vwu1 (P1) — GH #621: nx CLI crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252 console.
- nexus-njmg (P3) — GH #622: nx doctor 'Fix:' install hints lack Windows winget commands.
- nexus-hwbj (P1) — GH #619: enabled nx/sn plugins silently non-functional + routing guidance injects regardless.

## Recommended fix order

1. **vwu1 first** — without it, \`nx doctor\` (the diagnostic
   entry point) crashes on its own status glyphs.
2. **njmg second** — once doctor runs, its 'Fix:' hints need
   Windows install commands so users can act on them.
3. **hwbj last** — the architectural fix: gate the
   \`using-nx-skills\` routing-guidance injection on a working
   preflight, so a broken Windows install gets a degraded-mode
   notice rather than 600+ lines of confidently-wrong routing.

## Acceptance

- All three member beads close.
- A fresh Windows 11 + PowerShell 5.1 host with the plugins
  enabled but missing deps gets:
  - \`nx doctor\` running cleanly (no UnicodeEncodeError).
  - Doctor's Fix-lines naming \`winget install --id ... --scope user\`
    for every tool that has a winget package.
  - SessionStart injecting a degraded-mode notice (not the full
    \`using-nx-skills\` routing) until preflight passes.

## Refs

- All three filed 2026-05-09 from the same Windows shakedown.
- Could ship as one mini-PR series or one bundled PR.
close_reason: Closed

title: Windows: nx CLI crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on cp1252 console (GH #621)
description:
## GH issue

https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/621

## Symptom

On Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1 (default cp1252 encoding), any \`nx\`
command emitting non-ASCII glyphs (✓, ✗, ≥, ..., em-dashes) through
\`click.echo\` crashes with UnicodeEncodeError. \`nx doctor\` is the
fast repro:

\`\`\`
File \"...nexus/commands/doctor.py\", line 1277, in doctor_cmd
  click.echo(output)
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '✓' in position 25
\`\`\`

## Root cause

Python on Windows infers stdout encoding from the console code page,
which is cp1252 by default unless the user opts into UTF-8 globally.
\`click.echo\` writes the encoder's bytes; cp1252 can't encode the
glyphs nx uses in status output. There's no fallback or
\`errors=\"replace\"\`.

## Suggested fixes (any one would work — from GH)

1. Force UTF-8 stdout at CLI entry: in \`nexus/cli.py:main()\`, on
   Windows reconfigure \`sys.stdout\` / \`sys.stderr\` with
   \`encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"\`.
2. Wrap \`click.echo\` calls with a tolerant emit helper.
3. Replace the glyphs with ASCII fallbacks under cp1252.

#1 is the smallest blast radius and matches what gh / git / uv do.

## Acceptance

- \`nx doctor\` (and any other nx command emitting status glyphs)
  runs cleanly on a default Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1 host
  WITHOUT requiring the operator to set PYTHONIOENCODING or
  \`[Console]::OutputEncoding\`.
- Test (mock-based) verifies stdout is reconfigured for UTF-8
  on Windows entry.

## Priority rationale

P1: nx doctor is the entrypoint for diagnosing install issues
(GH #619); a doctor that crashes on its own status glyphs makes
the rest of the Windows story unrecoverable through self-help.
close_reason: Closed

title: Windows: enabled nx/sn plugins silently non-functional + routing guidance injects regardless (GH #619)
description:
## GH issue

https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/619

## TL;DR (from GH)

Fresh Windows 11 host with \`nx@nexus-plugins\` and \`sn@nexus-plugins\`
enabled: every nx feature is non-functional but Claude gets ~600+
lines of \`using-nx-skills\` routing guidance injected at SessionStart
confidently directing it to call tools and skills that have no
working backend.

## Root cause class

The plugin ecosystem was developed and tested primarily on macOS;
several Windows-specific assumptions break end-to-end:

1. All hook commands shell out to bash (\`bash $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/...\`,
   \`_run_python_hook.sh\`, etc.) — no .ps1 / .cmd companions.
2. \`.mcp.json\` uses bare binary names (\`"command": "nx-mcp"\`); needs
   .exe on Windows + Claude Code restart for PATH inheritance.
3. \`npx\` for sequential-thinking — Windows users need explicit Node.
4. Microsoft Store python.exe stubs trigger false-positive presence
   checks.
5. Hook stderr is invisible on Windows — the \`nx upgrade --auto\`
   self-upgrade hook's remediation message goes nowhere.
6. README's \`curl | sh\` install path is macOS / Linux only.

## Highest-leverage fix (per GH issue)

Run preflight on SessionStart, gate the routing-guidance injection
on the result. If preflight passes -> inject \`using-nx-skills\` as
today. If preflight fails -> inject a short degraded-mode notice
that disables the nx skills and tells the model to fall back to
direct Read/Grep/Glob.

## Acceptance

- A fresh Windows 11 host with the plugins enabled but missing
  deps gets a degraded-mode notice rather than full routing
  guidance to broken backends.
- The notice names the missing tools and one-line install hint
  per OS (winget on Windows).
- Preflight result is queryable from the model so it knows when
  nx skills are reachable.

## Priority rationale

P1: every nx feature is broken on Windows out of the box AND
the routing guidance actively misleads Claude. The combination
(broken + actively wrong) is worse than either alone.
close_reason: Closed

title: backfill-hash + reidentify: integration test against real chromadb under concurrent indexer write
description:
## Problem

Both nexus-o9an (backfill-hash two-pass) and nexus-qlm2 (parallel reidentify) ship with mock-based unit tests that validate the call-shape contract but no integration test exercises the real ChromaDB pagination behavior under concurrent indexer writes.

The two-pass design assumes pass 1 completes fast enough that the collection state stays consistent. The comment at \`commands/collection.py:_backfill_chunk_text_hash\` (pass-1 stability note from nexus-2exh review) acknowledges this is best-effort under concurrent writes.

## Fix

Integration test that:
1. Seeds a real chromadb.EphemeralClient collection with N>300 chunks (forces pass-1 multi-page).
2. Spawns a background thread that adds chunks during pass 1.
3. Runs backfill-hash / reidentify; asserts that ALL pre-existing chunks are processed (the new chunks may or may not be included depending on timing).
4. Re-runs the verb and asserts idempotence (any chunks missed in run 1 are picked up in run 2).

Locks the best-effort guarantee + idempotent-recovery contract.

## Refs
- nexus-2exh final review caveat (test infra gap)
close_reason: Closed

title: document_aspects: 50% orphan rate, lifecycle GC missing for aspects whose source document was deleted/renamed
description:
## Symptom

RDR-108 Phase 5 verification probe (2026-05-10) found:

\`\`\`
catalog documents:           23486
total document_aspects rows: 759
rows with non-empty source_uri orphaned: 385
orphan rate: 50.72%
\`\`\`

385 of 759 aspect rows reference a \`source_uri\` that no longer
appears in the catalog \`documents\` table.

## Background

\`document_aspects\` (RDR-089) stores structured aspects (problem
formulation, methods, datasets, baselines, results, etc.) extracted
from indexed documents. Rows are inserted by the
\`aspect_extraction_queue\` worker after a document is registered
in the catalog.

When a document is later deleted (\`cat.delete_document\`), renamed
(\`source_uri\` mutation), or its source file is removed (housekeeping
miss-count >= 2 path), the aspect rows are NOT cascaded — they
remain in the table pointing at a now-defunct \`source_uri\`.

This is independent of RDR-108. Surfaced during the Phase 5
verification probes; not a blocker for RDR-108 closure but a real
data-quality concern that affects retrieval (aspect-keyed queries
return rows for non-existent documents).

## Options

### Option A: Add CASCADE DELETE on aspects -> documents

Make \`document_aspects\` rows automatically deleted when their
parent \`Document\` is removed. RDR-108 K1 (nexus-lh8c) added
\`ON DELETE CASCADE\` to \`document_chunks\`; aspects need the
same treatment.

Caveat: aspects key by \`source_uri\` not \`tumbler\`. The
RDR-108 Phase 1c migration (nexus-je0b) was supposed to migrate
to \`doc_id\` but per the Phase 5 probe the column doesn't exist
yet (likely the migration is queued at version 4.30.0 and hasn't
fired locally). Whichever PK migration lands needs to wire the
cascade in the same change.

### Option B: Periodic GC verb

\`nx aspects gc [--dry-run] [--apply]\` that audits aspects
against catalog documents and deletes orphans. Mirrors the
chash-reconcile shape (also from this Phase 5 verification).

## Recommendation

Option A is structurally correct (cascade is the canonical fix);
Option B is a stop-gap for the legacy backlog. Could ship both:
A for the steady-state, B as a one-shot cleanup for the existing
385 orphans.

## Affected files

- \`src/nexus/db/migrations.py\` — new migration for FK CASCADE
  on aspects (likely paired with the deferred 4.30.0 PK migration).
- \`src/nexus/db/t2/document_aspects.py\` — schema + accessors.
- New: \`src/nexus/commands/aspects.py\` (if Option B).
- \`tests/test_document_aspects.py\` — cascade contract.

## Refs

- 2026-05-10 Phase 5 verification probe (T2 memory: rdr-108-phase5-verification-probes).
- RDR-108 K1 (nexus-lh8c): the prior precedent for CASCADE on a
  documents-keyed table.
close_reason: Closed

title: reidentify: use full canonical normalize instead of narrow _STRIPPED_META_FIELDS to handle over-quota chunks
description:
## Symptom

Phase 5 prod migration via \`nx t3 reidentify --all-collections --no-dry-run\`
errored on 2 collections out of 153 with:

\`\`\`
ERROR: docs__1-7__voyage-context-3__v1: Quota exceeded: 'Number of metadata
dictionary keys' exceeded quota limit for action 'Upsert': current usage of
33 exceeds limit of 32.

ERROR: knowledge__art-grossberg-papers__voyage-context-3__v1: Quota exceeded:
'Number of metadata dictionary keys' exceeded quota limit for action 'Upsert':
current usage of 37 exceeds limit of 32.
\`\`\`

## Root cause

\`reidentify_collection\` strips a narrow set at \`t3_reidentify.py:226-229\`:

\`\`\`python
new_meta = {
    k: v for k, v in meta.items()
    if k not in _STRIPPED_META_FIELDS
}
\`\`\`

where \`_STRIPPED_META_FIELDS = frozenset({"doc_id", "chunk_index",
"chunk_count"})\` (3 keys).

Many legacy chunks carry far more cargo than these 3:
\`corpus\`, \`store_type\`, \`expires_at\`, \`extraction_method\`,
\`format\`, \`is_image_pdf\`, \`has_formulas\`, \`page_count\`,
\`bib_*\` placeholders. The canonical schema funnel
(\`_normalize_for_write\` in \`db/t3.py:132\`) drops all of them, but
reidentify bypasses that and uses its own narrow set. After
narrow-strip + adding nothing, the merged metadata still exceeds
the 32-key Cloud quota on the upsert.

## Fix

Use \`_normalize_for_write\` in reidentify's pass 2:

\`\`\`python
from nexus.db.t3 import _normalize_for_write
...
new_meta = _normalize_for_write(meta, collection_name)
\`\`\`

This drops cargo (corpus, store_type, expires_at, etc.), pre-RDR-101-Phase-5c
fields, and bib_* placeholders, in addition to the 3 RDR-108 Phase 3 fields
already covered.

The change is purely additive (more drops, no fewer); the existing
\`_STRIPPED_META_FIELDS\` set becomes redundant since \`normalize\`
already drops those.

## Affected files

- \`src/nexus/db/t3_reidentify.py\` (\`reidentify_collection\`, ~205-230)
- \`tests/test_t3_reidentify.py\` (extend \`test_strips_doc_level_metadata_fields\`
  to also verify cargo is dropped)

## Out of scope

Backfill-hash uses the same \`_normalize_for_write\` path already (nexus-o9an).
This bead is the symmetric fix for reidentify.

## Refs

- Surfaced during RDR-108 Phase 5 prod migration; 2 of 153 collections still
  contain over-quota chunks after the main migration completed.
close_reason: Closed

title: backfill-hash misses chunks: offset-pagination instability + over-quota update failure
description:
## Symptom

\`\`\`bash
nx collection backfill-hash --all
\`\`\`

reports "90 updated, 11789 already had hash (11879 total)" against
\`docs__1-7__voyage-context-3__v1\`, but a follow-up reidentify run
still finds chunks without \`chunk_text_hash\` in that collection.
Direct paginated audit shows 600 chunks were missing the hash, not
90.

## Two root causes

### 1. Offset-pagination instability (the count bug)

\`_backfill_chunk_text_hash\` (\`commands/collection.py:613\`) uses
\`col.get(limit=N, offset=M)\` to paginate. ChromaDB Cloud's offset-
based pagination is order-unstable: the same row can appear in
multiple pages and other rows can be skipped entirely across calls.
Even though \`col.update\` doesn't add or remove rows, the
underlying collection state during a multi-minute walk shifts
enough for some rows to never be visited.

The reidentify verb avoids this with a two-pass design (pass 1:
collect ALL ids; pass 2: fetch by exact id). \`backfill-hash\`
should adopt the same pattern.

### 2. Over-quota update failure (the silent-skip bug)

When \`col.update(ids=..., metadatas=[{...}])\` fires against a
chunk whose existing metadata has 32+ keys, ChromaDB rejects with
\`Quota exceeded: NumMetadataKeys\`. Verified against the
\`docs__1-7\` chunks: many carry 33-34 metadata keys including
legacy cargo (\`corpus\`, \`store_type\`, \`expires_at\`,
\`extraction_method\`, \`format\`, \`is_image_pdf\`,
\`has_formulas\`, \`page_count\`) and pre-RDR-108 fields
(\`chunk_count\`, \`chunk_index\`).

The current code catches \`NumMetadataKeys\` and increments
\`skipped\`, but those chunks then SILENTLY remain without
\`chunk_text_hash\`, breaking downstream consumers that depend on
the field.

## Fix

Rewrite \`_backfill_chunk_text_hash\` with the same pattern as
\`reidentify_collection\`:

1. **Pass 1**: paginate \`col.get(include=[])\` to collect every
   chunk id. No writes; offset is stable because we only read.
2. **Pass 2**: for each batch of ids, \`col.get(ids=batch,
   include=['documents', 'embeddings', 'metadatas'])\`. For each
   missing-hash chunk, build a normalized payload via the canonical
   schema funnel (drops cargo + adds \`chunk_text_hash\`) and
   re-upsert with documents + embeddings. The upsert REPLACES
   (rather than merges) the metadata, sidestepping the quota issue.

## Affected files

- \`src/nexus/commands/collection.py:_backfill_chunk_text_hash\`
- \`tests/test_backfill_hash.py\`

## Refs

- Surfaced during RDR-108 Phase 5 prod migration on
  \`docs__1-7__voyage-context-3__v1\` (the conformant twin of
  \`docs__scheme-evolution-research-b7de0b63\`).
- Inline workaround script lives in shell history; this bead
  generalizes the fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-108 Phase 4 follow-up: reconcile nx t3 gc CLI to manifest path
description:
## Problem

After RDR-108 Phase 4, two GC implementations coexist with incompatible
semantics:

- `_prune_deleted_files` (triggered by `nx index`): manifest-based, keys
  on `meta.chunk_text_hash[:32]` against the catalog manifest.
- `nx t3 gc` CLI (`commands/t3.py:gc_cmd`): legacy doc_id metadata path.
  Skips chunks without `doc_id` as 'UNDECIDABLE'. Post-Phase-3 chunks
  have no doc_id in metadata, so this CLI silently skips them.

## Operator-facing impact

An operator who runs `nx t3 gc --dry-run` to preview deletions before
indexing will see zero candidates for post-Phase-3 chunks and conclude
the collection is clean, when in fact `_prune_deleted_files` will sweep
those chunks on the next `nx index` run.

## Fix

Update `gc_cmd` to:
1. Use the manifest-based path (`Catalog.chashes_for_collection`) for
   identifying orphans (matching `_prune_deleted_files`).
2. Preserve the existing dry-run + --yes confirmation UX as the
   authoritative preview for what `_prune_deleted_files` would delete.
3. Keep emitting `ChunkOrphaned` events on actual delete (the SOLE-emitter
   contract from RF-101-3).

## Out of scope

The pre-RDR-053 chunk class (no `chunk_text_hash`) — handled separately
by the warning+skip behavior added to `_prune_deleted_files`.

## Files

- `src/nexus/commands/t3.py:gc_cmd` (~340-460)
- `tests/test_t3_gc.py` (or wherever the gc tests live)

## Refs

- RDR-108 Phase 4 cross-cutting critique (T2 memory: rdr-108-phase4-cross-cutting-critique)
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-108 Phase 2 follow-up: indexer write-path content-derived chunk IDs
description:
## Problem

Phase 2 (nexus-jc63, shipped 2026-05-09 as PR #617) listed indexer
write-path formula replacement in its ## Files section but only
shipped the `nx t3 reidentify` verb. The actual write-path sites
still produce SYNTHETIC chunk IDs:

  - src/nexus/code_indexer.py:381   -- sha256(corpus:title:chunk{i})[:32]
  - src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:101  -- sha256(corpus:title)[:32] (markdown)
  - src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:165  -- sha256(corpus:title)[:32] (line-based)
  - src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:962    -- f"{content_hash[:16]}_{chunk_index}" (PDF)
  - src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:1046   -- f"{content_hash[:16]}_{chunk_index}" (markdown)
  - src/nexus/db/t3.py:690          -- sha256(collection:title)[:16] (single-chunk MCP put)
  - src/nexus/mcp/core.py:974       -- pre-computes [:16] for catalog dedup
  - src/nexus/commands/store.py:113 -- pre-computes [:16] for catalog dedup

Discovered while implementing nexus-dyxe (RDR-108 Phase 4 GC). The GC
spec assumes T3 chunk natural ID == chunk_text_hash[:32]; without this
write-path change, every newly-indexed chunk has a synthetic ID that
the manifest would never reference, and a literal-spec GC would wipe
all live data on every index run.

Worked around in nexus-dyxe by GC keying on meta.chunk_text_hash[:32]
rather than chunk_id, but the system does not converge until the
write path also uses content-derived IDs.

## Goal

Per RDR-108 D1, all T3 chunk natural IDs are chunk_text_hash[:32].
Update the 8 sites above so newly-indexed chunks land directly under
their natural ID (no reidentify pass needed for new content).

## Side effects (intentional)

- Identical chunk text in the same collection collapses to one T3
  record (the design goal of D1). Multiple manifest rows can point at
  the same chash.
- Re-indexing the same content is idempotent: the new chunk ID
  matches the existing chunk ID, upsert is a no-op.
- Old synthetic-ID chunks become orphans on first re-index. The
  manifest-based GC (nexus-dyxe) sweeps them on the same run.

## Files

- src/nexus/code_indexer.py:381
- src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:101, 165
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:962, 1046
- src/nexus/db/t3.py:690
- src/nexus/mcp/core.py:974
- src/nexus/commands/store.py:113

## TDD

- chunk_chroma_id == sha256(chunk_text)[:32] for every site
- identical chunk text collapses to one upsert
- re-indexing same content is idempotent (same ID, no churn)
- pre-Phase-A test fixtures still pass (chunk_text_hash always emitted)

## Branch
feature/nexus-dyxe-manifest-gc (bundling with nexus-dyxe Phase 4 work)
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: RDR-108 Phase 1 remediation T-C: cascade integrity + collision defense + missing tables
description:
RDR-108 Phase 1 multi-lens review surfaced cascade-atomicity issues in gp20's implementation.

## Findings to address

K4 (architecture A-? + migration CRIT-2,3 + coverage CG-1):
- commands/collection.py:175-254 — T3 rename runs first (irrevocable); T2 cascades each in own transaction, swallowed by `try/except Exception: on_warn(...)`
- Mid-cascade failure leaves chash_index pointing at new name while document_aspects/taxonomy still under old; CLI exits 0
- DocumentAspects.rename_collection and AspectExtractionQueue.rename_collection use plain UPDATE — NO collision defense
- chash_index.rename_collection has pre-DELETE collision defense at chash_index.py:178; aspect rename methods lack this
- If (new, source_path) already exists (e.g. wrongly-named earlier indexing run), UNIQUE constraint failed gets swallowed

Fixes:
- Span all four T2 cascades in single `with t2db.transaction():` block — atomic
- Mirror chash_index's pre-DELETE pattern in DocumentAspects.rename_collection AND AspectExtractionQueue.rename_collection
- Replace broad-except swallow with non-zero exit + actionable error message
- Reorder so T3 rename happens AFTER T2 cascades succeed (currently T3-first; T2-first preferred)

K9 (architecture A-S3): cascade gap on additional collection-bearing tables
- search_telemetry.collection (per migrations.py:420-430)
- hook_failures.collection (per migrations.py:590-610)
- Both indexed for lookup; rename leaves them orphaned
- Add: SearchTelemetry.rename_collection() + HookFailures.rename_collection() (or equivalent on the existing accessor classes)
- Wire into rename_collection_data_plane

CG-1 (coverage): half-cascade test missing
- Mock document_aspects.rename_collection to raise mid-cascade
- Assert aspect_queue.collection unchanged AND non-zero exit code

SIG-8 (migration): rename order T3-first → T2 partial drift more likely than necessary
- Reorder: T2 first, T3 last (rationale: T2 is reversible via UPDATE, T3 is irrevocable in chromadb)

## Significant docstring fix

A-S4: gp20's docstring on aspect_extraction_queue.rename_collection misrepresents post-je0b PK state
- Says "authoritative re-keying for the PK itself" but post-je0b, PK is doc_id; rename only updates denorm cache
- Simplify to "On migrated tables (PK=doc_id, post-RDR-108 Phase 1c), this updates only the denorm cache; PK is unaffected. On legacy tables (PK=(collection, source_path)), this is also the PK re-keying."

## Branch / PR

- Branch: feature/nexus-rdr108-r-c-cascade-integrity off develop
- Touches: src/nexus/commands/collection.py, src/nexus/db/t2/document_aspects.py, src/nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py, plus new rename_collection on whichever module owns search_telemetry + hook_failures

title: RDR-108 Phase 4a: chash_index simplification (drop chunk_chroma_id column)
description:
## Symptom

T2 `memory.db.chash_index` table contains 121,442 rows referencing **1,697 distinct `physical_collection` values**. T3 (ChromaDB Cloud) contains only **150 collections**. That's an 11.3× drift: ~1,547 collection names in chash_index that no longer exist in T3 (or never did under those names).

## Probe evidence (2026-05-08)

```
=== chash_index table ===
Total rows: 121442
Distinct collections: 1697
```

T3 collection count from `client.list_collections()`: 150.

Sampling chash_index distinct collections will likely show:

1. Pre-RDR-101 names (e.g., `code__nexus-571b8edd` instead of post-RDR-101 conformant `code__1-2188__voyage-code-3__v1`)
2. Test-fixture collection names that leaked into prod chash_index
3. Renamed/superseded collections that were never reconciled in chash_index

## Why it matters

`chash_index` is the lookup table the catalog uses to resolve `chash:<hex>` link spans. When a chash points to a now-renamed collection, the lookup still returns a row but the resolver hits T3 with a non-existent collection name — `chromadb` raises (or silently returns no results). RDR-101's `Catalog.resolve_chash` has self-heal logic (`chash_index.delete_stale`) that drops rows pointing at non-existent T3 collections, but that's a per-access correction, not a sweep.

## Fix

Two-pass cleanup:

1. **Audit** — `nx catalog chash-audit`: report chash_index rows whose `physical_collection` is not in `client.list_collections()` set.
2. **Reconcile** — `nx catalog chash-reconcile [--dry-run] [--apply]`: bulk-call `chash_index.delete_stale` for stale rows. Or, where possible, update `physical_collection` to the new conformant name (RDR-103 collection-name authority).

## Out of scope

title: RDR-108 Phase 5 verification: stale-chunk count goes to zero post-migration
description:
## Background

Probe on 2026-05-08 (code__1-2188__voyage-code-3__v1, 28,512 chunks):
- 1,630 (source_path, chunk_index) keys have >1 chunk ID
- 23,714 chunks (83%) involved in dupe groups
- Per-key, only the youngest by `indexed_at` is the current logical chunk; the older entries are stale-from-prior-index pre-soft-delete-fix.

Bead nexus-jc63 ([A]) introduces the steady-state soft-delete mechanism. This bead ([B]) covers the one-shot backfill: pre-existing stale chunks have no `is_current` field, so they need to be retroactively classified.

## Out-of-scope until A lands

This bead BLOCKS-ON nexus-jc63 ([A]). Don't run a backfill before the schema field is defined; rerunning the backfill after the schema lands is fine.

## Sweep design

Per collection (code__*, docs__*, rdr__*), paginated:

```python
for c in client.list_collections():
    if not c.name.startswith(('code__', 'docs__', 'rdr__')):
        continue
    by_loc = defaultdict(list)
    offset = 0
    while True:
        res = c.get(limit=300, offset=offset, include=['metadatas'])
        if not res['ids']: break
        for cid, md in zip(res['ids'], res['metadatas']):
            sp = md.get('source_path', md.get('title', ''))
            ci = md.get('chunk_index', -1)
            ts = md.get('indexed_at', '')
            by_loc[(sp, ci)].append((cid, ts, md.get('is_current', True)))
        if len(res['ids']) < 300: break
        offset += 300

    # For each (sp, ci) with >1 entry, youngest indexed_at is current.
    to_supersede = []
    for k, entries in by_loc.items():
        if len(entries) <= 1: continue
        entries.sort(key=lambda e: e[1])  # ascending
        for cid, ts, _ in entries[:-1]:   # all but the youngest
            to_supersede.append(cid)

    # Update in batches of 300
    for i in range(0, len(to_supersede), 300):
        batch = to_supersede[i:i+300]
        c.update(ids=batch, metadatas=[
            {"is_current": False,
             "superseded_at": "2026-05-08T00:00:00+00:00",
             "superseded_reason": "backfill-2026-05-08"} for _ in batch])
```

## Quantification step before sweep

Before writing, run a dry-run scan that emits per-collection counts:
- chunks total
- distinct (source_path, chunk_index) keys
- keys with >1 entry
- chunks that would be marked superseded
- estimated storage / embedding-cost reclaimed (hide for now, surface in vacuum-superseded planning)

Output to a JSON report at `~/.config/nexus/audits/dedup-baseline-2026-05-08.json` for posterity (this run is the baseline; future drift can be measured against it).

## Edge cases to handle

1. **Same indexed_at, multiple IDs**: shouldn't happen but if it does, prefer the chunk whose `chunk_text_hash` matches the current file's chunk at that position (read source, re-chunk, compare). If source is gone, mark all but one arbitrary as superseded.
2. **Source file deleted from repo**: ALL chunks for that (source_path, chunk_index) family are stale. The deleted-file prune (`indexer.py:1570 _prune_deleted_files`) should already handle these, but the dupe scan will surface any leaked here too. Cross-check.
3. **Cross-collection dupes (chunk_text_hash collision)**: 4,504 cross-collection chunk_text_hash dupes are LEGIT (boilerplate code, etc.) — do NOT supersede across collections, only within.
4. **Pre-RDR-101 chunks without doc_id**: still keyable on (source_path, chunk_index); the sweep doesn't depend on doc_id.

## Verb shape

`nx t3 dedup-backfill [--collection NAME] [--dry-run] [--report-path PATH]`

`--dry-run` is the default; user must pass `--apply` to actually update.

## Rollback

`nx t3 dedup-backfill --undo --from-report PATH` flips `is_current=False` chunks back to True if the user discovers the backfill misclassified anything. Cheap because soft-delete is just a metadata flag.

## Affected files

- New: src/nexus/commands/t3.py — add `dedup_backfill` subcommand
- src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py — verify `update` is in the same 300-record batching as `upsert`/`delete`
- New: tests/test_dedup_backfill.py — fixture with intentional dupes, assert correct supersede

## Estimated scope

- Code collections (15 colls, ~165k chunks): ~25% leaked = ~41k chunks to supersede
- Docs/RDR collections: probe needs to run to quantify
- Total elapsed: ~30 minutes (paginated reads bottleneck)

## Closes

Pre-existing leakage from before nexus-jc63 lands. Steady-state from then on is handled by the soft-delete supersede in [A].

title: investigate: catalog doctor --replay-equality FAIL on prod (projector vs SQLite)
description: 2026-05-08 prod probe: nx catalog doctor --replay-equality fails. Sample divergence: 'only in events' includes [code__Delos-5af9bfe0 1 ts=2026-05-08T20:59:27.989725Z], [code__Kramer-2c1f322c 1 ts=2026-05-08T20:59:27.990040Z]; 'only in projected' includes [code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1 0 ts=2026-05-05T02:05:02.851220Z], [code__ART-8c2e74c0 1 supersededby=code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1 ts=2026-05-05T02:05:02.851517Z]. Same drift class seen during 4.29.0 shakeout, now quantified. Hypotheses: (1) projector failed to apply some events; (2) legacy code path bypassed events.jsonl; (3) hand-supersede SupersededBy event mishap. Action: walk events.jsonl for divergent collection ids, identify class, backfill via nx catalog backfill-collections (dry-run first) if class 1/3, file follow-up RDR if class 2. Make --replay-equality part of CI smoke. READ-ONLY first; do NOT run backfill --no-dry-run until root cause known. Refs: src/nexus/commands/catalog.py doctor_cmd, src/nexus/catalog/projector.py, ~/.config/nexus/catalog/events.jsonl.
notes:
2026-05-08 deep probe — May 5 mystery solved + new finding

ROOT CAUSE: inconsistent semantics for duplicate CollectionCreated events:
- 2026-05-05 02:05: RDR-103 Phase 4 migration created code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1 + superseded code__ART-8c2e74c0 (clean event chain).
- 2026-05-08 20:59: nx catalog backfill-collections re-emitted CollectionCreated for already-existing collections (Delos, Kramer, etc.) with new timestamps.
- Live SQLite ignored the duplicates (first-wins / unique-key collision on collections.name PK).
- Replay projector ACCEPTED the duplicates as upserts (last-wins).

Result: same collection, different created_at in the two views → --replay-equality flags as divergence.

This is NOT a data drift; it's a semantics mismatch between two write paths. Two valid fixes:
(A) Projector: skip duplicate CollectionCreated when the row already exists (match SQLite's first-wins). Simple, idempotent, conservative.
(B) backfill-collections: don't emit CollectionCreated for collections already in the projection; emit a no-op marker or just no event. Cleaner but harder.

(A) is preferred — projector idempotence is a more general property than caller discipline.

ALSO: search for other "duplicate event creates timestamp drift" classes — DocumentRegistered, ChunkIndexed, OwnerRegistered all need the same idempotence guarantee. Audit src/nexus/catalog/projector.py for INSERT vs INSERT OR IGNORE / ON CONFLICT.

References:
- ~/.config/nexus/catalog/events.jsonl: 92,302 events reference code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1 (2 CollectionCreated, 1 CollectionSuperseded, 92,299 DocumentRegistered)
- src/nexus/commands/catalog.py: backfill-collections is the offender
- src/nexus/catalog/projector.py: needs idempotence audit

title: RDR-105 P4.1: Delete t1_watchdog.py + watchdog tests
description:
Sub-task of P4 (nexus-jnx7). Delete src/nexus/t1_watchdog.py entirely (~300 LOC) and tests/test_t1_watchdog.py.

Watchdog's two responsibilities are split (per RDR §'Watchdog disposition'):

title: RDR-105 P3.2: 10-parallel claude -p shared stress test (RF-3 verification)

title: RDR-105 P2.6: tests/test_t1_discovery.py — six T1 cases + failure paths + owned respawn race
description:
Sub-task of P2 (nexus-9fu7). Author tests/test_t1_discovery.py — end-to-end coverage for the new architecture, behind NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1.

Six T1 cases (per RDR §'The six T1 cases'):
1. Top-level MCP — owns the session (spawns chroma at lifespan start; tears down at finally).
2. Agent-tool sub-agent — same process as parent (uses parent's MCP scratch tool via tool dispatch; n/a separate T1).
3. claude -p shared (share_t1=True) — inherits NX_T1_HOST/PORT; HttpClient connects; raise T1ServerNotFoundError if env present but unreachable.
4. claude -p owned (default) — dispatcher unsets NX_T1_HOST/PORT/ISOLATED; subprocess MCP spawns own chroma + writes own t1_addr.<own_claude_pid>; sealed from parent.
5. claude -p ephemeral (ephemeral=True / NX_T1_ISOLATED=1) — opens its own EphemeralClient; no chroma spawn, no address file.
6. Bash-tool / shell nx scratch / SessionStart-SessionEnd hooks — sibling subprocess; find_immediate_claude_pid → t1_addr.<claude_pid> read → HttpClient connects.

Failure paths (must all fail-loud per RDR §'Fail-loud invariant'):
- env present but chroma unreachable → T1ServerNotFoundError
- no env and no file (no parent MCP found) → T1ServerNotFoundError
- no env, no file, no NX_T1_ISOLATED → T1ServerNotFoundError with explicit guidance message

CRITICAL test (per RDR §'Code changes (additions)' last bullet): owned-mode respawn race —
- Start an owned MCP (writes t1_addr.<own_pid>).
- Kill the MCP mid-flight (simulate crash).
- Start a respawned MCP under the same claude_pid.
- Verify it EITHER finds its own correctly-keyed address file OR raises T1ServerNotFoundError. NEVER lands on the parent's file.

This is the test that would have caught the #579 cross-process spawn-and-overwrite class.

TDD: write this file BEFORE the implementation in P2.1-P2.5 lands. Tests will fail until impl arrives — that's the point.

Use pytest fixtures for tmp_path-based ~/.config/nexus, monkeypatch for env-var setup, real chromadb.HttpClient against a real chroma subprocess (integration over mocks per project conventions). Port=0 for dynamic allocation.

title: RDR-105 P2.5: operators/dispatch.py — three-mode share_t1 / ephemeral parameters
description:
Sub-task of P2 (nexus-9fu7). Add three-mode dispatcher API to src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py and any other claude -p dispatch site.

API (per RDR §'Dispatcher policy'):
  def dispatch_claude_p(*, share_t1: bool = False, ephemeral: bool = False, ...):

Three semantically distinct modes (mutually exclusive — assert not both share_t1 and ephemeral):

1. share_t1=True (subprocess connects to caller's T1 via inherited env):
   - Read (host, port) from nexus.mcp._t1_state.T1_ADDR (P2.3).
   - If T1_ADDR is None → raise RuntimeError('share_t1=True requires top-level MCP T1 to be live').
   - Set env['NX_T1_HOST'] = host, env['NX_T1_PORT'] = str(port), env.pop('NX_T1_ISOLATED', None).
   - Subprocess constructor's Path A connects.

2. ephemeral=True (stateless one-shot subprocess; current operator dispatch pattern):
   - env.pop('NX_T1_HOST', None), env.pop('NX_T1_PORT', None).
   - env['NX_T1_ISOLATED'] = '1'. Subprocess constructor's Path C → EphemeralClient.
   - Maps to current NEXUS_SKIP_T1=1 behavior. NEXUS_SKIP_T1 honored alongside NX_T1_ISOLATED for 4.27 → 4.28 (deprecation; P5).

3. default (owned mode — subprocess gets its own T1 session):
   - env.pop('NX_T1_HOST', None), env.pop('NX_T1_PORT', None), env.pop('NX_T1_ISOLATED', None).
   - Subprocess MCP's lifespan (P2.4) hits Branch 3 → spawns own chroma + writes own t1_addr.<own_claude_pid>.
   - Sealed from parent; internally consistent.

Why owned-mode default (per RDR §'Dispatcher policy'): Current behavior implicitly shares with parent via on-disk-record discovery; the new default is sealed-from-parent, which is the safer default. Callers needing parent T1 visibility opt in via share_t1=True. Forces the question 'do I want this subprocess to see my session's notes, or to skip T1 entirely?' at dispatch time.

Mapping from current → new:
- Plan-runner dispatch → default (owned)
- Operator dispatch (currently sets NEXUS_SKIP_T1=1) → ephemeral=True (NEXUS_SKIP_T1 honored as alias through 4.28)

Behind NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1 flag. Flag-off retains existing dispatch behavior.

TDD: integration test for each mode. Mock subprocess; assert correct env-var setup for each mode. Assert share_t1=True against None T1_ADDR raises loudly.

See RDR-105 §'Dispatcher policy', §'Sub-agent T1 contract'. Files: src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py, tests/test_dispatch.py (or similar). Depends on P2.3 (_t1_state).

title: RDR-105 P2.4: mcp/core.py lifespan as @asynccontextmanager (3-branch spawn gate)
description:
Sub-task of P2 (nexus-9fu7). Replace _t1_chroma_init_if_owner in src/nexus/mcp/core.py with an @asynccontextmanager generator implementing the 3-branch spawn gate.

Three branches (symmetric with constructor signal hierarchy from P2.1, per RDR §'Lifespan spawn gate'):
1. NX_T1_HOST + NX_T1_PORT set (subprocess inherited parent's chroma) → yield without spawn or file-write. Constructor's Path A connects via env.
2. NX_T1_ISOLATED=1 (subprocess opted into ephemeral) → yield without spawn or file-write. Constructor's Path C uses EphemeralClient.
3. else (top-level OR owned subprocess MCP) → start_t1_server, find_immediate_claude_pid (P2.2), write_t1_addr (P2.2), set _t1_state.T1_ADDR = (host, port). On finally: stop_t1_server, unlink_t1_addr, set _t1_state.T1_ADDR = None.

Critical implementation details:
- Single @asynccontextmanager generator so (server_pid, claude_pid, host, port, tmpdir) are local variables shared across the yield. Two-function presentation (startup/shutdown) loses implicit shared closure and forces class-state or callback indirection (per RF-7 lifespan note).
- No os.environ mutation. Stores (host, port) in _t1_state.T1_ADDR module variable (P2.3) — NOT os.environ. Avoids GIL/thread-pool concerns.
- Address file deleted as last act on shutdown: stop chroma first, unlink address file last. A sibling reading mid-shutdown gets either prior valid contents (HTTP fails → fail-loud) or missing file (fail-loud). No partial-state window.
- Symmetric branches with constructor: each lifespan branch maps to exactly one constructor branch. No path can spawn chroma the constructor will then ignore (would leak orphan chroma).

Behind NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1 flag. Flag-off retains existing _t1_chroma_init_if_owner path (deleted in P4).

TDD: integration test (in tests/test_mcp_chroma_lifecycle.py) for each branch. Test that spawn happens in branch 3, NOT in branches 1+2. Test that _t1_state.T1_ADDR is populated/cleared correctly. Test that address file is unlinked AFTER chroma stops on shutdown.

See RDR-105 §'Lifespan spawn gate', RF-7. Files: src/nexus/mcp/core.py, tests/test_mcp_chroma_lifecycle.py. Depends on P2.2 (helpers) + P2.3 (_t1_state).

title: RDR-105 P2.2: find_immediate_claude_pid (FIRST claude ancestor, NOT topmost) + write_t1_addr/read_t1_addr_for helpers
description:
Sub-task of P2 (nexus-9fu7). Add three new helpers to src/nexus/session.py.

CRITICAL invariant: find_immediate_claude_pid MUST return the FIRST claude* ancestor encountered walking up from os.getpid(), NOT the topmost. The topmost-walk semantic in legacy find_claude_root_pid (session.py:680-682, 'Prefer topmost') is what would silently break owned-mode isolation per RDR-105 RF-6. Acceptance test: an owned subprocess MCP's find_immediate_claude_pid() must return its OWN claude_pid, not the user's top-level claude_pid. See RDR-105 §'Address file is keyed by IMMEDIATE Claude ancestor, not topmost'.

1. find_immediate_claude_pid() → int | None:
   - Walks PPID chain from os.getpid() via existing _ppid_of (session.py:120-147) + _command_name_of (session.py:638-653) primitives.
   - Returns the FIRST claude* ancestor encountered, NOT the topmost.
   - ~15 LOC variant of existing _ppid_of + _command_name_of usage.
   - CRITICAL: legacy find_claude_root_pid (topmost-walk) is what would silently break owned-mode isolation per RF-6. The IMMEDIATE semantic returns the correct claude_pid in all four nesting cases:
     * Bash from top-level Claude → top-level (same as topmost since only one claude in chain)
     * Owned subprocess MCP → own claude -p (NOT top-level — that would overwrite parent's address file)
     * Bash inside owned subprocess → own claude -p
     * nx scratch standalone → immediate_ppid fallback
   - Used by both lifespan address-file write (P2.4) AND constructor's Path B read (P2.1).
   - Legacy find_claude_root_pid stays in place during P2 (deleted in P4).

2. write_t1_addr(claude_pid: int, host: str, port: int) → None:
   - Atomic temp-then-Path.replace at ~/.config/nexus/t1_addr.<claude_pid>.
   - File contents: '<host>:<port>\\n' — exactly that, nothing more.
   - Single writer (top-level / owned MCP at lifespan start).

3. read_t1_addr_for(claude_pid: int) → tuple[str, int] | None:
   - Reads ~/.config/nexus/t1_addr.<claude_pid>; parses host:port; returns tuple or None if missing/malformed.

TDD: tests for find_immediate_claude_pid must cover all four nesting cases. Use fake process trees (mock _ppid_of + _command_name_of) — deterministic. write/read round-trip test with tmp_path.

See RDR-105 §'Address file is keyed by IMMEDIATE Claude ancestor', §'Code changes (additions)', RF-6. Files: src/nexus/session.py, tests/test_session.py (add cases) or tests/test_t1_discovery.py.

Introduce feature flag NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1 (NEW in this phase) to differentiate the legacy and new code paths; flag-off retains current architecture, flag-on activates new code path. Mutually exclusive per process.

Flag introduction is a P1 deliverable (load-bearing for the spike): without the flag, old vs new paths cannot coexist for differential validation. The flag persists into P2 (where it gates production-quality landing) and P3 (where it flips default to on).

CRITICAL load-bearing verification (per RDR §'Migration plan' Phase 1): demonstrate hybrid discovery END-TO-END across BOTH integration points before proceeding to P2.

Two integration points to validate:
1. Env-var passdown for MCP-dispatched subprocess (existing dispatcher pattern):
   - claude -p shared subprocess inherits NX_T1_HOST / NX_T1_PORT via subprocess.Popen(env={...}) at dispatch time.
   - Subprocess T1Database constructor reads from os.environ → connects via HTTP.
   - Standard POSIX subprocess semantics; the dispatcher already passes NEXUS_SKIP_T1 + NX_SESSION_ID via this mechanism. Should work, but run once to confirm FastMCP shell does not strip / rewrite env.

2. File-based discovery for Claude-Code-dispatched Bash-tool subprocess (NEW mechanism, the LOAD-BEARING verification):
   - Bash-tool subprocess (sibling of MCP, spawned by Claude Code) calls find_immediate_claude_pid() — first claude* ancestor walking up from os.getpid(), NOT topmost (per RF-6).
   - Reads ~/.config/nexus/t1_addr.<claude_pid> — single-writer file containing host:port\\n.
   - Connects to chroma via HTTP.
   - This path does NOT exist in current architecture; env-var inheritance from MCP server does NOT serve this case (per RF-1 / POSIX semantics: child cannot mutate parent env).

Both behind feature flag NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1. Flag-off retains current architecture; flag-on activates new code path. Mutually exclusive per process.

Exit criterion (from RDR §'Migration plan' Phase 1):
- Feature flag NX_T1_NEW_DISCOVERY=1 introduced and respected by spike code paths (legacy code untouched when flag-off)
- Spike branch demonstrates BOTH:
  (1) claude -p shared subprocess sees parent T1 via inherited env
  (2) nx scratch put from a Bash tool reaches parent MCP's chroma via address file
- Both with the OLD discovery code disabled by the feature flag
- Decide during spike: stick with ~/.config/nexus/t1_addr.<pid> OR conditional XDG_RUNTIME_DIR on Linux (residual from RDR §'Remaining low-stakes residuals')

Why find_immediate_claude_pid (not pass claude_pid via env): an owned claude -p subprocess's process tree contains TWO claude* ancestors (itself + user's top-level Claude). Topmost-walk semantic (legacy find_claude_root_pid) silently breaks owned isolation by writing/reading the parent's address file. find_immediate returns the FIRST claude* ancestor walking up — correct in all four nesting cases per RF-6.

See RDR §'Migration plan' Phase 1, §'Address file is keyed by IMMEDIATE Claude ancestor'.

title: nx catalog list --owner leaks Tumbler.parse ValueError on non-tumbler names (#537, 4.26.2)
description:
GitHub issue #537 (filed 2026-05-06 by hhildebrand-conductor against 4.26.1).

Same shape as nexus-blk2 Part 2 (catalog_resolve typed error) but on the CLI side. `nx catalog list --owner canon-conductor-compose` (a name, not a tumbler) leaks the raw int() ValueError to the user. CLI advertises --owner TEXT with no hint that it must be dotted-numeric.

## Source

src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:825-849:

```python
@catalog.command('list')
@click.option('--owner', default='')
def list_cmd(owner: str, content_type: str, ...) -> None:
    cat = _get_catalog()
    if owner:
        entries = cat.by_owner(Tumbler.parse(owner))
    ...
```

Tumbler.parse (nexus/catalog/tumbler.py:117-124) is strict on dotted-numeric segments and leaks int() ValueError on anything else.

## Two fix options

A. Typed error: catch ValueError, emit click.ClickException with a hint pointing at the dotted-tumbler form. Mirrors nexus-blk2's MCP fix.

B. Owner-by-name resolution: catalog has owners.name column ('canon-conductor-compose'). When --owner doesn't parse as Tumbler, fall back to looking up by name. More useful UX (operators can type the name they see in nx catalog list output).

Recommended: B, with A as the fallback when the name isn't unique. The schema has 35 distinct named owners per the reporter; resolving by name is the operationally hostile-friendly path.

## Acceptance

- nx catalog list --owner canon-conductor-compose returns entries owned by that named owner (not a stack trace)
- nx catalog list --owner 1.4 still works (existing dotted-tumbler form)
- nx catalog list --owner nonexistent surfaces a clean 'no owner matches X' message (typed error, not ValueError)
- Test in tests/test_catalog_cmd.py covers all three paths

## Out of scope

- Aliasing 'name' resolution into other catalog commands (nx catalog show, nx catalog resolve). One-bead-at-a-time.

Files: src/nexus/commands/catalog.py, src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py (if owner-by-name lookup), tests/test_catalog_cmd.py.
Ships: 4.26.2.
Issue: GH #537.

title: store_list bare-prefix resolver doesn't probe 2-segment legacy collection shape (#535, 4.26.2)
description:
GitHub issue #535 (filed 2026-05-06 by hhildebrand-conductor against 4.26.1).

## Symptom

`nx store list` (no args, default `--collection knowledge`) and MCP `store_list(collection='knowledge')` both fail on installs with legacy 2-segment collection names (`knowledge__knowledge`, etc.) created before the RDR-103 transition. The resolver promotes to the conformant 4-segment shape that doesn't exist, never trying the legacy 2-segment fallback.

## Root cause (per reporter's caller audit)

src/nexus/corpus.py:189-243 `t3_collection_name(user_arg='knowledge', t3=t3)`:
1. Not conformant; no '__' → ct='knowledge', rest='knowledge'
2. promoted = 'knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1'
3. Probes promoted → not exist
4. Probes user_arg 'knowledge' → not exist (legacy collection is 'knowledge__knowledge', NOT 'knowledge')
5. Returns the missing promoted name → 'No entries'

Every read-side caller already passes t3= correctly (reporter's audit confirms 11/12 callers pass it; the 12th is intentional per the in-source comment). The bug lives in the predicate itself.

## Fix (per reporter's patch sketch)

In the grandfathering branch, also probe the 2-segment legacy shape:

```python
try:
    if not t3.collection_exists(promoted):
        if t3.collection_exists(user_arg):
            return user_arg
        # Bare-prefix fallback: bridge to documented legacy 2-segment
        # shape (e.g. knowledge__knowledge) when operator typed only the
        # content_type.
        legacy_two_segment = f'{ct}__{owner_segment}'
        if legacy_two_segment != user_arg and t3.collection_exists(legacy_two_segment):
            return legacy_two_segment
except Exception:
    pass
return promoted
```

Symmetric with nexus-hmxi 'pre-existing legacy collections remain readable' design intent.

## Acceptance

- nx store list (no args) on install with knowledge__knowledge returns its entries (not 'No entries in knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1')
- mcp store_list(collection='knowledge') resolves to knowledge__knowledge when conformant doesn't exist
- Round-trip store_put + store_list against bare prefix 'knowledge' lands in the same physical collection (no read/write split)
- New unit test in tests/test_corpus.py: fixture with knowledge__knowledge present, no conformant, assert t3_collection_name('knowledge', t3=...) returns 'knowledge__knowledge'

## Out of scope (filed separately)

- Reporter's secondary finding: scratch action=get/delete should accept 8-char prefix (matching scratch action=list display + memory_get exact-then-prefix per nexus-e59o). Separate UX bead.
- Write-side policy for bare-prefix puts (always conformant vs grandfather to legacy) — the index-side comment at commands/index.py:647-654 argues 'always conformant, rename legacy first'. Read-fix here is sufficient for the hostile case.

Files: src/nexus/corpus.py:189-243, tests/test_corpus.py
Ships: 4.26.2 (alongside nexus-pnje source_uri backfill)

title: AUTO-LINK silently produces 0 links: MCP catalog_search returns empty tumblers + auto-linker swallows invalid-tumbler errors
description:
## Symptom

The AUTO-LINK recipe (catalog_search -> scratch put with link-context tag -> store_put) is documented in the SubagentStart hook (NX_AUTOLINK heredoc, nx/hooks/scripts/subagent-start.sh) and reinforced in 8+ skill / 10+ agent post-flight blocks. When followed end-to-end by a recipe-compliant subagent, **zero catalog links are created and no error signal is emitted to the caller**.

## Repro (live shakeout, conexus 4.25.2, 2026-05-05)

Dispatched nx:deep-research-synthesizer on a synthesis question that obviously references RDR-101 + RDR-104. Agent followed all 3 recipe steps cleanly:
- catalog_search for RDR-101 + RDR-104 (multiple variants)
- scratch put with `tags=["link-context"]`, entry f025d801-453f-4efd-a0e4-a931f40d3d2f
- store_put -> T3 chash e84d4ef78629b26e -> catalog 1.10.584

Result: `nx catalog links 1.10.584` -> "No links found." Same for the two other shakeout store_puts (1.10.582, 1.10.583).

## Two-part root cause

### Part 1: MCP catalog_search returns empty tumbler strings for RDR docs

Agent observed: "The nexus RDR documents indexed in `rdr__1-2188__voyage-context-3__v1` do not carry catalog tumblers in the structured results (tumblers returned as empty strings)."

But `nx catalog search "RDR-104"` from the CLI returns:
```
1.2189.146   prose      rdr-104-incremental-catalog-projection-rebuild
1.2188.863   rdr        rdr-104-incremental-catalog-projection-rebuild.md
```

So the catalog HAS the tumblers; the MCP catalog_search response shape isn't surfacing them under the query shape the agent used. Agent fell back to T3 chunk doc-IDs (`aca95577feec25d1`, `f6931790014e89ed`) as link targets - not parseable as `Tumbler` (1.X.Y).

### Part 2: Auto-linker silently swallows invalid-tumbler errors

`auto_link` (catalog/auto_linker.py:58-106) catches `ValueError` from `Tumbler.parse()` and `link_if_absent()` per-target with DEBUG-level log only. `_catalog_auto_link` is wrapped in a bare `except Exception: pass` at mcp/core.py:948-955. Net effect: invalid tumbler strings -> no link created, no error to caller, no INFO/WARN log, no telemetry.

The two parts compound: bad data feeds the auto-linker, the auto-linker silently drops it, the agent reports "AUTO-LINK recipe executed successfully", and the catalog graph stays empty.

## Coverage gap (independently flagged in same shakeout)

Sibling agent (nx:codebase-deep-analyzer) auditing test_auto_linker.py listed exactly this as gap #1:
> "bare-except swallow (mcp/core.py:950) - no test verifies the swallow behavior: inject a catalog that raises on any call, call the full store_put handler, assert it returns successfully without propagating. Without this, a regression that throws inside _catalog_auto_link for a non-obvious reason will pass silently with zero links created and no signal."

Plus gap #2: "Malformed JSON in scratch `content` field - `read_link_contexts` parses entry["content"] as JSON when present. No test passes a non-JSON string. Behavior on json.JSONDecodeError is untested."

## Acceptance

- Test that injects link-context entries with non-tumbler target strings, runs store_put, asserts the store call succeeds, AND asserts a WARN-level log was emitted naming the bad target. (Currently this combination passes silently.)
- Test that calls MCP catalog_search for an RDR document and asserts the result includes a non-empty `tumbler` field. (Catches Part 1.)
- Decide observability story: WARN log per-skipped-target, return count of skipped-vs-linked from auto_link, surface the count in store_put response, or some combination.

## Originating context

Surfaced during shakeout of conexus 4.25.2 reinforcement of T1/T2/T3 + AUTO-LINK + nx_answer discipline (PRs #519, #520). The recipe was followed correctly by the agent - the failure is in the executing layer, not the routing layer. Without the observability fix, every future recipe-compliant store_put is a 100% silent miss.

Related: nexus-wehp (different race in the catalog write path).
close_reason: Part 1 fixed in PR #532 (mcp catalog_search query+content_type routing). Part 2 (auto_link silent swallow + AutoLinkResult counts + WARNING on invalid tumblers) shipped in 4.25.3. Both halves of the silent-zero-link recipe now produce signal.

title: [RDR-104 Step 4] Equivalence regression test (gate for the whole arc)
description:
RDR-104 Phase 1 Step 4 — synthetic event-log harness. THIS IS THE GATE for the whole arc.

REFERENCE
- RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-104-incremental-catalog-projection-rebuild.md § Step 4 (line 346-348), Test Plan (lines 365-399), Validation (lines 403-413).
- Round 3 PASSED.

DELIVERABLE
New file: tests/test_catalog_incremental_rebuild.py

Synthetic event-log harness with row-by-row equality assertions of the SQLite projection (owners, documents, links, collections) AND FTS5 search-result equality between paths.

REQUIRED SCENARIOS (from RDR Test Plan, must be implemented)

Bootstrap and rebuild paths
- [ ] Cold catalog (no marker), 1000-event log → full rebuild + marker write. Assert marker stores (eof_offset, header_hash, header_window); projection matches single-pass replay; FTS5 hits stable.
- [ ] Warm catalog, events.jsonl truncated and replaced (same first 64KB) → pathological adversarial case bounded by Finding 1 idempotency; projection still converges via redundant replay; documented as known-cost-not-known-corruption.
- [ ] Warm catalog, events.jsonl truncated and replaced (first bytes differ) → header-hash mismatch detected; falls through to full rebuild; marker re-written.
- [ ] _HEADER_HASH_BYTES bumped → window mismatch → full rebuild; marker re-written with new window value.
- [ ] Collections rebuild equality (Critical #1): synthetic log with CollectionCreated then CollectionSuperseded; DELETE FROM collections + replay produces correct superseded_by/superseded_at; without DELETE, stale supersede metadata persists (NEGATIVE TEST PINNED).

Empty-delta and incremental paths
- [ ] Empty-delta fast path (Significant #4 — SEPARATED): events.jsonl unchanged but legacy JSONL (documents.jsonl) re-written → mtime advances but eof_offset unchanged → only last_consistency_mtime advances; assert no header_hash computation, no events read.
- [ ] Warm catalog, K new events appended (typical incremental) → only K events apply; marker advances by sum-of-line-bytes; projection matches single-pass full rebuild on combined log.
- [ ] Malformed-line append (separated from empty-delta — Round 1 Observation): a corrupt line fails JSON parse → incremental skips via warn-and-skip; marker advances past it; projection matches full-rebuild outcome on the same corrupt log.

Idempotency and concurrency
- [ ] Same event applied twice (double-apply equivalence) — projection identical after second apply; ALL 13 v0 verbs covered (programmatic loop over verb-fixture pairs).
- [ ] Split-pair (Significant #1): DocumentRegistered in already-applied window, DocumentAliased for the same document in the new-events window → incremental replay produces same final state as single-pass full rebuild. Pins the conditional-idempotency case for _v0_document_aliased.
- [ ] Collections events scenario (Significant #2): synthetic log includes CollectionCreated AND CollectionSuperseded; incremental replay's collections row equality matches full-rebuild's.
- [ ] Crash mid-incremental (Projector.apply_all raises) → transaction rolls back; offset+hash markers unchanged (4.24.4 atomicity); next run reads stale marker and re-applies the same delta successfully.
- [ ] apply_all(new_events, commit=False) invariant (Round 3 Significant #3): patch CatalogDB.commit to track call count; assert NOT called inside the incremental rebuild's transaction body. Connection-level commit at __exit__ of with self._conn: is allowed (the implicit one); explicit self._db.commit() is not.
- [ ] Degraded-path retry preserves supersede metadata (Round 3 Significant #1): collections row carries populated superseded_by from events before stored_offset; force a v=1 raise mid-delta; after rollback, next incremental retry encounters CollectionCreated for the same collection in the delta; assert COALESCE preserves the supersede metadata through the re-apply.

EventLog.replay_from contract scenarios (Significant #3)
- [ ] replay_from(0) == replay() — equivalence at offset-zero boundary, both unbounded and bounded form with limit_offset=eof.
- [ ] replay_from(eof) yields zero events (both bounded and unbounded).
- [ ] replay_from(mid_line_offset) yields a malformed first line — iterator follows warn-and-skip; orchestrator detects the corruption signal at the caller layer (zero events yielded against a non-empty [stored_offset, eof_offset_now) range) and escalates to full rebuild WITHOUT advancing the marker. Test asserts the CALLER-LEVEL ESCALATION, not a replay_from-internal raise.
- [ ] replay_from(offset > file_size) raises ValueError; caller path falls back to full rebuild.
- [ ] Bounded form (Round 2 Critical #1): file with N+M events; capture limit = byte_offset_after_event_N (use f.tell() per Round 3 Observation, NOT a computed sum); append M more events (live EOF advances); call replay_from(0, limit_offset=limit); assert iterator yields exactly events 0..N-1, none of the appended-after-snapshot tail.
- [ ] Concurrent-appender bounded-form scenario (Round 2 Critical #1, orchestrator-level): existing log with K events, marker at 0; capture eof_offset_now = byte_offset_after_event_K; append L more events; run incremental rebuild via the orchestrator path; assert marker advances to eof_offset_now (NOT live EOF including the L appended events); next run sees a non-empty delta of L events and applies them; final projection equals full-rebuild over K+L events.
- [ ] Binary-mode portability — byte offsets captured on this platform are valid (CI runs Linux + macOS).

PERFORMANCE ASSERTION
- [ ] Timing: incremental path completes in <100ms on a 100-event delta against a 100K-event base. Use a generous wall-clock margin; this is regression detection, not micro-bench.

EXECUTION
1. SPAWN dev work via /nx:implement.
2. mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking to plan harness shape — synthetic-event factory, projector-equivalence assertion helper, FTS5 search-result equality helper.
3. Build the synthetic-event factory (one event per verb, parameterized).
4. Build the assertion helpers (projection row-by-row equality across owners/documents/links/collections; FTS5 search hits).
5. Implement scenarios in the order above. Run after each batch.
6. Run uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_incremental_rebuild.py.
7. Run full uv run pytest before close (the gate is end-to-end green).
8. Test validation via /nx:test-validate before close.

DEPENDENCIES
- Step 1 (nexus-v386) — needs replay_from.
- Step 2 (nexus-rpgn) — needs marker storage.
- Step 3 (nexus-3sx1) — needs the incremental branch wired into _ensure_consistent.

ACCEPTANCE — THIS IS THE EPIC GATE
- [ ] All 21+ scenarios above implemented and green.
- [ ] Test validation via /nx:test-validate approved.
- [ ] uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_incremental_rebuild.py passes.
- [ ] Full uv run pytest passes (no regressions in existing 1000+ tests).
- [ ] Performance assertion (<100ms on 100-event delta against 100K base) holds.
- [ ] ART catalog smoke (~441K events, nx index repo) shows steady-state rebuild in <100ms — manual confirmation, document in the PR body.
- [ ] Concurrent-writer scenario (nx-mcp + nx index repo) does not produce marker oscillation — manual confirmation, document in the PR body.

CONTEXT FOR EXECUTOR
- USE mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking — this test file is the gate; over-investing in harness clarity pays.
- USE mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking again on the degraded-path retry scenario — it is the most subtle of the lot.
- nx search: 'projector apply_all v0 verbs idempotent' (corpus=code) — surfaces the projector verb-by-verb behavior for the double-apply scenario.
- Update continuation state: project='nexus', title='rdr-104-step-4-state.md'.
- SPAWN parallel sub-agents for INDEPENDENT scenario implementation if context budget gets tight; the harness is the bottleneck, not the individual scenarios once the harness is built.
- Round 3 Observation: use f.tell() AFTER writing event N's line to capture the half-open boundary, NOT a computed sum.

title: [RDR-104 Step 3] Incremental path branch in _ensure_consistent
description:
RDR-104 Phase 1 Step 3 — wire the bootstrap / empty-delta / steady-state / invalidated paths into _ensure_consistent.

REFERENCE
- RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-104-incremental-catalog-projection-rebuild.md § Step 3 (line 342-344), Technical Design pseudocode (lines 137-214), Concurrency notes (lines 236-242), Failure Modes (lines 301-307).
- Round 3 PASSED.

SCOPE — branches in _ensure_consistent (per pseudocode in Technical Design, lines 147-214)
1. Existing fast path: if current_mtime <= last_consistency_mtime and not degraded → return. UNCHANGED.
2. Bootstrap / no-events.jsonl path: legacy rebuild via CatalogDB.rebuild(consistency_mtime=current_mtime). UNCHANGED EXCEPT now CatalogDB.rebuild also DELETEs collections (Step 0 fix already in).
3. Empty-delta fast path (Significant #4): if eof_offset_now == stored_offset and stored_offset is not None → with transaction(): self._write_consistency_marker(current_mtime); return. The transaction() wrapper is MANDATORY (atomicity contract from 4.24.4) even though it is a single-row write.
4. Invalidated path (stored_offset is None OR stored_window != header_window OR stored_hash != header_hash_now): full rebuild path with transaction() + bulk_load_documents() fence. DELETE owners/documents/links/collections, apply_all(replay()), write all four marker rows atomically.
5. Incremental path (marker valid, delta non-empty): replay_from(stored_offset, limit_offset=eof_offset_now); inside transaction(), apply_all(new_events, commit=False), then write all four marker rows atomically.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS
1. apply_all(new_events, commit=False) is MANDATORY (Round 3 Significant #3). The Projector default is commit=True which would call self._db.commit() mid-transaction, finalizing the projection writes BEFORE the marker writes — defeating the rollback fence and re-introducing the 4.24.4-fixed ordering hazard. This mirrors the existing full-rebuild path at catalog.py:945 (verify the line number; symbol-search if drift).
2. replay_from MUST be called with limit_offset=eof_offset_now (the captured snapshot, NOT live EOF). Without the bound, a concurrent appender extends the file between stat() and the iterator's read window; the iterator consumes the appended tail; the marker the orchestrator persists is the pre-append snapshot. Marker is stale below the actual applied-event tail; empty-delta fast path never fires again for that range; incremental never settles.
3. Marker writes (offset + hash + window + mtime) MUST be inside the SAME transaction() as the projector writes. The Step 2 helper is built for this. _write_consistency_marker pattern from 4.24.4 is the precedent.
4. Caller-level corruption detection (Round 3 Significant #2): if the bounded iterator yields ZERO events from a non-empty delta range (stored_offset < eof_offset_now), escalate to full rebuild WITHOUT advancing the marker. There is no source_byte_offset field on Event — DO NOT add one. Zero-events-from-non-empty-range is the single concrete signal.
5. The existing rich-summary log line gains new rebuild-trigger reasons:
   - 'replayed N events incrementally'
   - 'header-hash drift → full rebuild'
   - 'window-size mismatch → full rebuild'
   - 'empty delta → mtime-only marker advance'
6. _write_consistency_marker swallows sqlite3.OperationalError silently (Round 2 Significant #1 / Tolerated failure mode). Add an inline comment at the except OperationalError: pass clause documenting the trade-off so a future reader does not see it as a contradiction with the docstring's 'MUST be inside the same transaction' contract.

EXECUTION
1. SPAWN dev work via /nx:implement.
2. mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking for the branch ordering — there are 5 paths and the precedence matters (fast path → bootstrap → empty-delta → invalidated → incremental).
3. Use Serena: jet_brains_find_symbol(name_path_pattern='Catalog/_ensure_consistent', include_body=true) to read current shape.
4. Use Serena: jet_brains_find_referencing_symbols(name_path='_ensure_consistent', relative_path='src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py') to confirm callers (no signature change expected, but verify).
5. TDD: write tests in tests/test_catalog_incremental_rebuild.py FIRST for the unit-level branches (Step 4 will add the equivalence-suite tests). At minimum:
   - bootstrap branch fires when no marker present.
   - empty-delta branch fires when eof_offset == stored_offset (assert no header_hash computation, no events read; mtime advances).
   - invalidated branch fires on header-hash drift.
   - invalidated branch fires on window-size mismatch.
   - incremental branch fires on stored_offset < eof_offset with valid hash.
   - apply_all called with commit=False on the incremental path (assert via mock or instrumentation; Step 4 will pin via patched commit-counter).
6. Implement the branch.
7. Run uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_consistency_marker.py tests/test_catalog_incremental_rebuild.py.
