title: RDR-078 P3: traverse operator + Catalog.graph_many() + purpose registry + link-type docs
description:
# RDR-078 P3: traverse operator + Catalog.graph_many() + purpose registry + link-type docs

**Quality lever — RDR-078's load-bearing phase.** Coordinator bead (depends on P1 + P2 + P4a).

**Before beginning the next bead, run `/nx:composition-probe nexus-05i.5` and verify PASS.** This bead has ≥2 blocking dependencies and is tagged as a coordinator candidate. The composition probe runs a 30-50 line smoke test against the coordinator's entry point to catch silent scope reduction at the composition boundary. If the probe fails, reopen the failing dependency bead before proceeding.

## graph_many() Contract (Audit Finding — Significant)

`Catalog.graph()` at `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:1440` takes `link_type: str` (singular). `graph_many()` takes `link_types: list[str]`. Two implementation strategies — **choose one and document it here before writing tests**:

**Option A — Fan-out per type (recommended)**: Call `graph()` once per `link_type` in `link_types`, merge results. Node dedup: `str(tumbler)`, first-seen wins, `seed_origin: list[str]` accumulated. Edge dedup: `(from, to, link_type)` triple. The `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500` cap applies to the **merged** frontier across all fan-out calls — not per-type. Short-circuit when cap hit mid-fan-out.

**Option B — Single call + post-filter**: Not viable — `graph()` takes singular `link_type`; no multi-type overload exists. Ruled out.

**Chosen approach**: Fan-out per type. Document this in the bead close note and in a docstring on `graph_many()`. The `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500` cap semantics must be stated: "cap on merged node count; partial results returned when exceeded; warning logged."

Use `mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` to design the merge invariants — node-key vs edge-key dedup, cap-across-merged-frontier, seed-origin metadata semantics.

## File Touchpoints

- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py` — add `Catalog.graph_many(seeds: list[str], depth: int, link_types: list[str], direction: str) -> dict`. Reference `Catalog.graph()` at line 1440 for the single-seed BFS implementation. No new SQL, no new graph algorithm.
- `src/nexus/plans/runner.py` — register `traverse` step kind; dispatch to `graph_many()` when seeds resolves to list, `graph()` when single seed. Step fields: `seeds` (literal list or `$stepN` ref), `link_types` OR `purpose` (mutually exclusive), `depth` (capped at 3), `direction` (out|in|both, default both), `return` (entries|collections|both).
- `src/nexus/plans/purposes.py` — **new file** — `purposes_resolve(name: str, project: str, scope: str) -> list[str]`. Loads `nx/plans/purposes.yml`. Filters resolved link types against `Catalog.registered_link_types()` — unknown types dropped with structured warning `purpose_unknown_link_type`.
- `nx/plans/purposes.yml` — **new file** — starter purpose set: `find-implementations`, `decision-evolution`, `reference-chain`, `documentation-for`, `soft-relations`, `all-implementations`.
- `docs/catalog-link-types.md` — **new file** — semantic definition per link type: directionality, source, traversal shape, when to use.
- `docs/catalog-purposes.md` — **new file** — purpose registry reference.

## Test Commands

```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_graph_many.py tests/test_traverse_step.py tests/test_purposes_resolve.py -v
```

Test functions:
1. `test_graph_many_node_dedup` — two seeds reaching same node: first-seen wins, `seed_origin` populated for both
2. `test_graph_many_edge_dedup` — `(from, to, link_type)` triple dedup across seed traversals
3. `test_graph_many_max_nodes_cap` — merged frontier hits `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500`, short-circuits, returns partial + logs warning
4. `test_traverse_seeds_from_step_ref` — `seeds: $step1.tumblers` resolves from prior retrieval step
5. `test_purpose_resolves_to_link_types` — `purpose:find-implementations` → `[implements, implements-heuristic]`
6. `test_purpose_unknown_link_type_warn_and_drop` — future link type in registry → subset returned, warning logged
7. `test_traverse_returns_collections_usable_as_subtree` — return shape `collections` feeds downstream `search(subtree=...)`

## Acceptance Criteria

- SC-4 (graph traversal): `test_graph_many_node_dedup`, `test_graph_many_edge_dedup`, `test_graph_many_max_nodes_cap`
- SC-5 (traverse→search composition): `test_traverse_returns_collections_usable_as_subtree`
- SC-16 (link_types + purpose mutual exclusion at runner level): validated in `test_traverse_step.py`
- SC-17 (purpose registry discoverable): companion docs catalog-indexed

## Known Gotchas

- P3 contract tests verify `traverse → search(scope=...)` composition end-to-end, which requires P2 scope plumbing live (hence the `nexus-05i.5 → nexus-05i.2` dependency edge). Without P2, tests would have to stub the downstream step — do not stub; the edge is now in the graph.
- `Catalog.registered_link_types()` may not exist yet — check `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py` before writing `purposes_resolve`. If absent, derive from the known link type constants in `catalog.py`.
- RDR-077 projection rows were wiped during development. Any test seeding taxonomy collections must create fresh projection rows — do not assume they exist.
- ChromaDB quota: graph traversal that resolves to collection queries must use `n_results ≤ 300` (`MAX_QUERY_RESULTS` in `src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py`). `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500` is a separate cap on BFS nodes, not on ChromaDB results.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: `nexus-05i.1` (P4c), `nexus-05i.2` (P1 — runner.py must exist; scope plumbing must be live for contract tests), `nexus-05i.3` (P2 — scope forwarding must work end-to-end), `nexus-05i.4` (P4a — schema validator must exist for `link_types`/`purpose` mutual exclusion).
acceptance_criteria: graph_many ships with merge invariants pinned by contract tests. traverse step registered. purpose registry resolves with warn-and-drop on unknown types. Both companion docs catalog-indexed and resolvable via plan_match ≥ 0.80 (SC-17). SC-4, SC-5, SC-16 met.
close_reason: P3 complete: Catalog.graph_many() (fan-out per type, merged-frontier 500-node cap, seed_origin accumulation, edge dedup) + nx/plans/purposes.yml (6 shipped purposes) + nexus.plans.purposes.resolve_purpose (warn-and-drop unknown link types) + traverse MCP tool ({tumblers,ids,collections} step output, SC-16 mutual exclusion at MCP boundary) + docs/catalog-link-types.md + docs/catalog-purposes.md. Composition probe PASSED earlier this session (1.92s, 6 assertion clusters across 4 deps). SC-4, SC-5, SC-16, SC-17 met. 12 P3 tests + 4121 full suite green.

# P3.2: taxonomy_assign_hook + discover post-pass projection (SC-4, SC-6)

## Context: nx
RDR-075 Phase 3 — wires cross-collection projection into automatic hooks. Blocked by nexus-d1q (cross_collection parameter must exist first).

## What to build

Two changes to make projection automatic and zero-friction:

### Change 1: `taxonomy_assign_hook` / `_run_taxonomy_assign` in `mcp_infra.py`

Modify `_run_taxonomy_assign()` at `src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:284` to add a second assignment call with `cross_collection=True` after the existing same-collection assignment.

**Current code** (lines 314–316):
```python
topic_id = taxonomy.assign_single(collection, embedding, chroma_client)
if topic_id is not None:
    taxonomy.assign_topic(doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by="centroid")
```

**After change** — add cross-collection projection:
```python
# Same-collection assignment (existing)
topic_id = taxonomy.assign_single(collection, embedding, chroma_client)
if topic_id is not None:
    taxonomy.assign_topic(doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by="centroid")

# Cross-collection projection (new — SC-4, SC-6)
cross_topic_id = taxonomy.assign_single(
    collection, embedding, chroma_client, cross_collection=True
)
if cross_topic_id is not None and cross_topic_id != topic_id:
    taxonomy.assign_topic(doc_id, cross_topic_id, assigned_by="projection")
```

The `cross_topic_id != topic_id` guard prevents double-inserting when same-collection centroid happens to be the global nearest too.

### Change 2: `discover_topics()` post-pass in `catalog_taxonomy.py`

After `discover_topics()` writes new centroids (after the `centroid_coll.upsert()` at line 1009), add a post-pass that queries other collections' centroids:

```python
# Post-discovery cross-collection projection pass (SC-6, Phase 3)
# For each newly discovered topic's centroid, find matching centroids in other collections
# Store as topic_links entries (Phase 4 will use these)
# This is lightweight: only M new centroids × N existing centroids
```

The post-pass implementation: after `centroid_coll.upsert()`, fetch all existing centroids for OTHER collections, compute centroid-to-centroid similarities for the newly added ones, store matches in `topic_links` via `upsert_topic_links()` (lines 559–584).

## Threshold configuration

Use the empirically validated threshold from nexus-78i. If 0.85 is confirmed, hard-code as module constant `_PROJECTION_THRESHOLD = 0.85` in `catalog_taxonomy.py` near `_LARGE_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD`.

## Audit finding (SC-10 interaction)

The `_run_taxonomy_assign()` fallback path (MiniLM, lines 308–312) can produce 384d embeddings against 1024d centroids. The `_check_centroid_dimension()` guard from nexus-eds handles this: the cross-collection `assign_single()` call will hit it and return None gracefully (with a structured warning log). No additional special handling needed here.

## Tests

File: `tests/test_taxonomy.py` or `tests/test_mcp_infra.py`.

Add `test_taxonomy_assign_hook_cross_collection()`: mock chroma_client with centroids from two collections. Call `taxonomy_assign_hook()` with a doc from collection A. Verify `topic_assignments` contains one row with `assigned_by='centroid'` AND one row with `assigned_by='projection'` pointing to the cross-collection topic.

Add `test_discover_topics_post_pass()`: discover on collection A (creates centroids). Then discover on collection B. Verify `topic_links` contains entries linking A-topics to B-topics where similarity ≥ threshold.

Test command: `uv run pytest tests/ -k "assign_hook" -v`

## Dependencies

Blocked by nexus-d1q (`cross_collection` parameter). Also soft-blocked by nexus-78i (threshold validation — should use validated threshold, but can use 0.85 default if validation is in progress).

## Completion criteria

- `_run_taxonomy_assign()` calls `assign_single(..., cross_collection=True)` after same-collection assignment
- New cross-collection assignments stored with `assigned_by='projection'`
- `discover_topics()` adds post-discovery centroid-to-centroid similarity pass
- SC-4 (projection assignments benefit search via apply_topic_boost) — confirmed by RF-4 (no search code changes needed)
- SC-6 (automatic projection on store_put) satisfied

# P3.1: Cross-collection query path in assign_single/assign_batch (SC-6)

## Context: nx
RDR-075 Phase 3 — adds the unscoped centroid query path to both methods. Blocked by nexus-20w (Phase 2 review). This bead unblocks nexus-bo4 (Phase 3.2 hooks).

## What to build

Add `cross_collection: bool = False` parameter to both `assign_single()` and `assign_batch()` in `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`. When `True`, the `where={"collection": collection_name}` filter is omitted, querying all centroids regardless of collection origin.

## Key files

- **Primary**: `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`
  - `assign_single()` lines 1016–1051 — add parameter, conditional where clause at line 1039
  - `assign_batch()` lines 1053–1097 — add parameter, conditional where clause at line 1082
  - `_check_centroid_dimension()` — from nexus-eds, already wired in — call remains unchanged
- **Test to preserve**: `test_assign_single_cross_collection_isolation()` in `tests/test_taxonomy.py` lines 290–312 — this test validates the DEFAULT (cross_collection=False) behavior. It must still pass unchanged.

## Implementation

**assign_single() change** (lines 1039–1044):
```python
def assign_single(
    self,
    collection_name: str,
    embedding: np.ndarray,
    chroma_client: Any,
    *,
    cross_collection: bool = False,  # NEW
) -> int | None:
    ...
    # Build where clause conditionally
    where = {} if cross_collection else {"collection": collection_name}
    try:
        results = centroid_coll.query(
            query_embeddings=[embedding.tolist()],
            n_results=1,
            **({"where": where} if where else {}),  # ChromaDB errors on empty where
        )
    except Exception:
        return None
```

**assign_batch() change** (lines 1082–1086): same pattern — build `where` conditionally, pass via `**kwargs`.

**ChromaDB empty-where caveat**: ChromaDB raises an error if `where={}` is passed. Use `**({"where": where} if where else {})` pattern when `cross_collection=True`.

## Returned metadata

When `cross_collection=True`, the centroid metadata includes `"collection"` — the caller can inspect `results["metadatas"][0][0]["collection"]` to know which source collection the matched centroid came from. This is important for nexus-bo4 which stores the projection source.

## Tests

File: `tests/test_taxonomy.py`.

Add `test_assign_single_cross_collection()`: create centroids from two different collections (A and B). Query from collection C with `cross_collection=True` — verify it can match centroids from both A and B. Query with `cross_collection=False` (default) — verify it only matches from C's own centroids (zero matches if C has none).

Existing `test_assign_single_cross_collection_isolation()` must still pass — verify it does.

Test command: `uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k "cross_collection" -v`

## Audit finding (RF-13 correction)

The RDR confirms BOTH `assign_single` and `assign_batch` enforce collection isolation — the gate critic's claim that `assign_single` was already unscoped was wrong (RF-13). This bead correctly adds the opt-in `cross_collection` parameter rather than removing the filter entirely.

```python
@taxonomy.command("project")
@click.argument("source_collection")

@click.option("--threshold", "-t", default=0.85, type=float, help="Cosine similarity threshold (default 0.85)", show_default=True)
@click.option("--top-k", default=3, type=int, help="Top-k centroids per chunk", show_default=True)
@click.option("--persist", is_flag=True, help="Write projection assignments to topic_assignments (assigned_by='projection')")
@click.option("--backfill", is_flag=True, help="Backfill all collections with cross-collection projection")
def project_cmd(source_collection: str, against: str, threshold: float, top_k: int, persist: bool, backfill: bool) -> None:
    """Project source collection chunks against target collection centroids."""
```

## Output format

```
Projecting docs__art-architecture (76 chunks) against 3 collections (219 centroids)...

Matched topics (threshold 0.85):
  [42] Cortical Adaptive Resonance Learning (knowledge__art)  — 12 chunks, avg sim 0.91
  [17] Neural Network Dynamics (rdr__ART-8c2e74c0)            — 8 chunks, avg sim 0.88
  ...

Novel chunks: 4 (no centroid match >= 0.85)

Total: 15 matched topics, 71/76 chunks covered
Run with --persist to write assignments to topic_assignments.
```

## --persist mode

When `--persist` is set, call `taxonomy.assign_topic(doc_id, topic_id, assigned_by="projection")` for each chunk→topic match above threshold. Use `assign_topic()` at `catalog_taxonomy.py:216` — it's idempotent via `INSERT OR IGNORE`.

## --backfill mode

When `--backfill` is set, enumerate all collections with existing topics via:
```python
collections = taxonomy.conn.execute(
    "SELECT DISTINCT collection FROM topics"
).fetchall()
```
Then for each collection, call `project_against()` against all *other* collections and persist. This is the manual re-runnable equivalent of the T3UpgradeStep in nexus-cjf.

The help text for `--threshold` should note: "0.85 is borrowed from the centroid merge threshold and may need calibration. Run `nx taxonomy project --threshold 0.85 --against <art-collections>` and manually review a sample of assignments to validate."

title: P2.2: project_against() core algorithm (SC-2, SC-3)
description:
# P2.2: project_against() core algorithm (SC-2, SC-3)

## Context: nx
RDR-075 Phase 2 — core matrix multiply for cross-collection similarity. Blocked by nexus-eds (dimension check must land first).

## What to build

Add `project_against()` to `CatalogTaxonomy` in `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`. This is the cross-collection similarity engine: chunk embeddings × topic centroids → cosine similarity matrix → top-k matches per chunk.

## Key files

- **Primary**: `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`
  - `_create_centroid_collection()` lines 843–854 — how to get the centroid collection
  - `assign_single()` lines 1016–1051 — reference for centroid `query()` pattern
  - `_check_centroid_dimension()` — will be added by nexus-eds, use it here
  - `topic_links` schema lines 88–94 — `(from_topic_id, to_topic_id, link_count, link_types)`
  - `upsert_topic_links()` lines 559–584 — final persistence step for SC-5 work (Phase 4 uses this)
- **Centroid metadata shape**: `{"topic_id": int, "label": str, "collection": str, "doc_count": int}`
- **ChromaDB `get()` for embeddings**: use `coll.get(include=["embeddings"])` — returns dict with `"ids"` and `"embeddings"` lists

## Signature

```python
def project_against(
    self,
    source_collection: str,
    target_collections: list[str],
    chroma_client: Any,
    *,
    threshold: float = 0.85,
    top_k: int = 3,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Project source collection chunks against target collection centroids.

    Returns:
        {
            "matched_topics": [
                {"topic_id": int, "label": str, "collection": str,
                 "chunk_count": int, "avg_similarity": float}
            ],
            "novel_chunks": [doc_id, ...],  # below threshold for all centroids
            "total_chunks": int,
            "total_centroids": int,
        }
    """
```

## Algorithm (from RDR-075 §Phase 2)

1. Fetch source chunk embeddings: `src_coll.get(include=["embeddings"])` → `src_ids`, `src_embs` (N × 1024d numpy array)
2. Fetch target centroids: `centroid_coll.get(where={"collection": {"$in": target_collections}}, include=["embeddings", "metadatas"])` → `ctr_embs` (M × 1024d), `ctr_metas`
3. Dimension check: call `_check_centroid_dimension()` — if mismatch, raise `ValueError("Dimension mismatch: source embeddings {D1}d, centroids {D2}d")`
4. Normalize both arrays: `src_norm = src / np.linalg.norm(src, axis=1, keepdims=True)` (cosine similarity via dot product)
5. Similarity matrix: `sim = src_norm @ ctr_norm.T` → shape (N, M); values in [-1, 1]
6. Per-chunk top-k: `top_indices = np.argsort(-sim, axis=1)[:, :top_k]`
7. Aggregate: for each centroid, count chunks with `sim[chunk_idx, ctr_idx] >= threshold`
8. Novel chunks: doc_ids where `sim[chunk_idx].max() < threshold` for all centroids

## Performance notes (RF-5)

- 76 × 219 × 1024d ≈ 17M FLOPs: well under 1ms
- Cap at `_LARGE_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD = 5000` chunks for interactive CLI use (line 859) — if source collection > 5000, batch in pages of 5000 and accumulate
- Bottleneck is ChromaDB `get()`, not matmul

## Tests

File: `tests/test_taxonomy.py`.

Add `test_project_against_basic()`: two in-memory chroma collections (source with 20 chunks, target with 10 centroids). Verify matched_topics contains expected entries above 0.85, novel_chunks contains expected low-similarity doc_ids.

Add `test_project_against_empty_target()`: target has no centroids — verify returns all chunks as novel.

Test command: `uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k "project_against" -v`

## Dependency

Requires nexus-eds (dimension check utility) to be merged first. The `_check_centroid_dimension()` function from nexus-eds is called in step 3.

## Completion criteria

- `project_against()` method on `CatalogTaxonomy`
- Returns correct matched_topics and novel_chunks
- Handles empty target gracefully
- Performance: < 1s for 5K×2K matrix on development hardware
- SC-2 (matches reported), SC-3 (novel chunks identified) satisfied
close_reason: Implemented and tested

# P2.1: Embedding dimension check utility (SC-10)

## Context: nx
RDR-075 Phase 2 — prerequisite to all projection work.

## What to build

Add a utility function that checks embedding dimension compatibility before making centroid `query()` calls. This is the guard against the silent `except Exception: return None` masking dimension mismatches (RF-15, SC-10).

## Key files

- **Primary**: `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`
  - `assign_single()` lines 1016–1051 — add dimension check before `centroid_coll.query()` at line 1039
  - `assign_batch()` lines 1053–1097 — add dimension check before `centroid_coll.query()` at line 1082
  - `_create_centroid_collection()` lines 843–854 — reference for how centroid collection is accessed
- **Hook path**: `src/nexus/mcp_infra.py`
  - `_run_taxonomy_assign()` lines 284–316 — has its own `except Exception: pass` at line 305 that masks dimension errors in the MiniLM fallback path (line 308–312)

## Implementation

Write a module-level helper (not a method) in `catalog_taxonomy.py`:

```python
def _check_centroid_dimension(embedding: np.ndarray, centroid_coll: Any) -> bool:
    """Return True if embedding dimension matches stored centroids.

    Logs a structured warning and returns False on mismatch.
    Skips check (returns True) if centroid collection is empty.
    """
    try:
        peek = centroid_coll.peek(1)
        if not peek["embeddings"] or peek["embeddings"][0] is None:
            return True  # Empty — no mismatch possible
        stored_dim = len(peek["embeddings"][0])
        query_dim = len(embedding)
        if query_dim != stored_dim:
            _log.warning(
                "centroid_dimension_mismatch",
                query_dim=query_dim,
                stored_dim=stored_dim,
            )
            return False
    except Exception:
        return True  # Can't check — optimistically proceed
    return True
```

Wire it into `assign_single()` BEFORE the `centroid_coll.query()` call at line 1039:
```python
if not _check_centroid_dimension(embedding, centroid_coll):
    return None
```

Wire it into `assign_batch()` BEFORE the `centroid_coll.query()` call at line 1082 (inside the per-doc loop):
```python
if not _check_centroid_dimension(np.array(emb), centroid_coll):
    continue
```

## Audit finding (SC-10)

The gate audit flagged that both `assign_single` (line 1045) and `assign_batch` (line 1087) have `except Exception: return None` / `continue` that silently swallow dimension errors. The dimension check must be placed BEFORE the query call, not inside the exception handler.

## Tests

File: `tests/test_taxonomy.py` (existing test suite).

Add `test_assign_single_dimension_mismatch()` and `test_assign_batch_dimension_mismatch()` — inject a centroid collection with 384d centroids, call assign with a 1024d embedding, verify structured log warning fires and None/0 is returned (not an exception).

Test command: `uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k "dimension_mismatch" -v`

## Dependencies

None — this is the root bead for Phase 2. Start here.

## Completion criteria

- `_check_centroid_dimension()` helper exists in `catalog_taxonomy.py`
- `assign_single()` calls it before `centroid_coll.query()`
- `assign_batch()` calls it before each `centroid_coll.query()` in the loop
- Tests for dimension mismatch pass
- SC-10 satisfied

## Phase 6: E2E Tests

End-to-end validation of the complete upgrade mechanism.

### Test Scenarios

1. **Fresh install**: No existing DB → apply_pending creates all tables, seeds "0.0.0", runs all migrations, updates to current version
2. **Existing install upgrade**: DB has memory table with data, no _nexus_version → bootstraps to PRE_REGISTRY_VERSION, runs only new migrations
3. **Same version**: _nexus_version matches CLI version → no-op (fast path)
4. **Downgrade warning**: _nexus_version > CLI version → warning logged but not blocked
5. **nx upgrade --dry-run**: Shows pending list, no changes applied
6. **nx upgrade --force**: Resets and re-runs, idempotent (no errors)
7. **nx upgrade --auto**: Quiet mode, T2 only, exit 0 always
8. **Concurrent access**: Two processes accessing same DB during upgrade → no corruption

### SC Verification Matrix
- SC-1: _nexus_version table created and populated
- SC-2: Migrations tagged with correct versions, version-gated execution
- SC-3: nx upgrade with all three flags works correctly
- SC-4: nx doctor --check-schema reports correct state
- SC-5: MCP version divergence warning fires
- SC-6: Domain stores delegate to module-level functions
- SC-7: Adding a new Migration() entry is the only step for new features
- SC-8: hooks.json has nx upgrade --auto first in SessionStart
- SC-9: Existing installs bootstrap to PRE_REGISTRY_VERSION

```python
def test_sc9_existing_install_bootstrap(tmp_path):
    db = tmp_path / "memory.db"

    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db))

    conn.commit(); conn.close()
```


Verify valid JSON after edit: `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('nx/hooks/hooks.json'))"`.

### Deliverable 2: MCP main() Version Check (SC-5)

**AUDIT FINDING — SYNCHRONOUS ONLY:** The version check must be synchronous. It runs before `mcp.run()`, outside any async context. Do not use `async def`, `asyncio.run()`, or `await`. A simple synchronous function is correct.

**Both files to modify:**
- src/nexus/mcp/core.py:1151–1156
- src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py:575–580

**Implementation pattern:**
```python
def main():
    from nexus.logging_setup import configure_logging
    configure_logging("mcp")
    _check_version_compatibility()  # synchronous, before mcp.run()
    mcp.run(transport="stdio")

def _check_version_compatibility() -> None:
    """Synchronous version check before MCP startup. Never blocks startup."""
    try:
        from importlib.metadata import version as _pkg_version
        from nexus.commands._helpers import default_db_path
        import sqlite3, structlog
        cli_ver = _pkg_version("conexus")
        db_path = default_db_path()
        if not db_path.exists():
            return
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT value FROM _nexus_version WHERE key='cli_version'"
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()
        if row is None:
            return
        stored_ver = row[0]
        # Parse versions for comparison
        from nexus.db.migrations import _parse_version
        cli_parts = _parse_version(cli_ver)
        stored_parts = _parse_version(stored_ver)
        # Warn if diverges by more than patch (major or minor mismatch)
        if cli_parts[:2] != stored_parts[:2]:
            log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
            log.warning("mcp.version_mismatch",
                        cli_version=cli_ver,
                        stored_version=stored_ver,
                        suggestion="run `nx upgrade` to sync")
    except Exception:
        pass  # Never block MCP startup on version check failure
```

Add the helper function to both core.py and catalog.py (or extract to a shared module if preferred).

### Deliverable 3: nx doctor --check-schema (SC-4)

**Files to modify:**
- src/nexus/health.py — add `check_t2_schema(db_path: Path) -> list[HealthResult]` function
- src/nexus/commands/doctor.py — wire into doctor output

**HealthResult dataclass** (health.py:25–37):

```python
    label: str
    ok: bool
    detail: str = ""
    suggestion: str = ""
```

**Schema check implementation sketch:**
```python
def check_t2_schema(db_path: Path) -> list[HealthResult]:
    results = []
    if not db_path.exists():
        results.append(HealthResult("T2 schema", ok=False, detail="DB not found"))
        return results
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path))
    try:
        # Check _nexus_version vs CLI version
        from importlib.metadata import version as _pkg_version
        cli_ver = _pkg_version("conexus")
        row = conn.execute("SELECT value FROM _nexus_version WHERE key='cli_version'").fetchone()
        if row is None:
            results.append(HealthResult("_nexus_version", ok=False,
                detail="table missing", suggestion="run `nx upgrade`"))
        else:
            stored = row[0]
            from nexus.db.migrations import _parse_version, MIGRATIONS
            pending = [m for m in MIGRATIONS
                       if _parse_version(m.introduced) > _parse_version(stored)
                       and _parse_version(m.introduced) <= _parse_version(cli_ver)]
            if pending:
                results.append(HealthResult("T2 migrations", ok=False,
                    detail=f"{len(pending)} pending",
                    suggestion="run `nx upgrade`"))
            else:
                results.append(HealthResult("T2 migrations", ok=True, detail="up to date"))
        # Check expected columns
        ...
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return results
```

description:
## Phase 3 Implementation: T2Database.__init__() Changes

Modify T2Database.__init__() to use the transient connection path with _upgrade_done fast path.

### Implementation Steps

1. At top of __init__(), check _upgrade_done set for path_key:
   - If present: skip to store construction (zero DB overhead)
   - If absent: proceed to step 2

2. Open transient sqlite3.Connection to path:
   - PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000
   - PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL

3. Call apply_pending(conn, current_version):
   - current_version from importlib.metadata.version("conexus")
   - This creates base tables, bootstraps _nexus_version, runs pending migrations

4. Close transient connection

5. Add path_key to _upgrade_done set

6. Construct domain stores normally (existing code):
   - MemoryStore(path)
   - PlanLibrary(path)
   - CatalogTaxonomy(path, self.memory)
   - Telemetry(path)

### Execution Context

**File to modify:** src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py lines 99–113

**Path canonicalization pattern** (match domain stores):
```python
try:
    path_key = str(path.resolve())
except OSError:
    path_key = str(path)
```
Memory store uses this pattern (memory_store.py:~285). Match it exactly.

**importlib.metadata.version wrapping:**
```python
try:
    from importlib.metadata import version as _pkg_version
    _current_version = _pkg_version("conexus")
except Exception:
    _current_version = "0.0.0"  # dev environment fallback
```

**WAL mode and busy_timeout on transient connection:**
Both are already issued by MemoryStore on its own connection. Setting them on the transient connection ensures the WAL journal file exists before stores open their connections. Match the pattern from memory_store.py (look for `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout`).

**Import from migrations.py:**
```python
from nexus.db.migrations import _upgrade_done, apply_pending
```
This is a top-level import (no circular risk: t2/__init__.py does not export anything that migrations.py imports at module level).

**Complete modified __init__ sketch:**
```python
def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        path_key = str(path.resolve())
    except OSError:
        path_key = str(path)
    if path_key not in _upgrade_done:
        # transient connection for migrations
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
        try:
            conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
            conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            apply_pending(conn, _current_version)
        finally:
            conn.close()
        _upgrade_done.add(path_key)
    # existing store construction
    self.memory = MemoryStore(path)
    self.plans = PlanLibrary(path)
    self.taxonomy = CatalogTaxonomy(path, self.memory)
    self.telemetry = Telemetry(path)
```

**Files to modify:**
- src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py

**Validation:**
```
uv run pytest tests/test_migrations.py tests/test_t2.py tests/test_t2_concurrency.py -v
```

## Phase 1 Implementation: src/nexus/db/migrations.py

Implement the migration registry module that centralizes all T2 schema migrations.

### Deliverables

1. **Dataclasses**: Migration(introduced, name, fn) dataclass
2. **Helpers**: _parse_version(ver) → tuple[int, ...] with try/except ValueError fallback to (0,0,0)
3. **Constants**: PRE_REGISTRY_VERSION = "4.1.2" (last release before registry ships)
   - **Audit note**: PRE_REGISTRY_VERSION = "4.1.2" is correct for current release. If the release ships before this branch merges, bump to the new release version.
4. **Process-level fast path**: _upgrade_done: set[str] — checked before any DB access
5. **Module-level migration functions** — extract from domain stores:
   - migrate_memory_fts(conn) — from MemoryStore._migrate_fts_if_needed (memory_store.py:298–329)
   - migrate_plan_project(conn) — from PlanLibrary._migrate_plans_if_needed (plan_library.py:136–180)
   - migrate_access_tracking(conn) — from MemoryStore._migrate_access_tracking_if_needed (memory_store.py:331–350)
   - migrate_topics(conn) — from CatalogTaxonomy._migrate_topics_if_needed (catalog_taxonomy.py:157–191)
   - migrate_plan_ttl(conn) — from PlanLibrary._migrate_plans_ttl_if_needed (plan_library.py:182–193)
   - migrate_assigned_by(conn) — from CatalogTaxonomy._migrate_assigned_by_if_needed (catalog_taxonomy.py:193–208)
   - migrate_review_columns(conn) — from CatalogTaxonomy._migrate_review_columns_if_needed (catalog_taxonomy.py:210–227)
6. **MIGRATIONS list**: Ordered by introduced version, historically accurate per git tag
7. **apply_pending(conn, current_version)**:
   - Step 1: Execute all base-schema SQL via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (lazy import from stores)
   - Step 2: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _nexus_version
   - Step 3: Bootstrap — detect existing vs fresh install, seed appropriately
   - Step 4: Read last-seen version
   - Step 5: Filter + execute eligible migrations
   - Step 6: Update _nexus_version to current_version

### Circular Import Avoidance
- migrations.py imports base schema SQL from stores inside apply_pending() (lazy, not module-level)
- Store files import individual migrate_* functions inside method bodies (lazy)

### Execution Context

**Exact extraction sources:**

`migrate_memory_fts(conn)` — extract from memory_store.py:298–329. The method uses `sqlite_master` (not PRAGMA) to detect the FTS table. **Do not change this guard** — audit finding confirms sqlite_master is correct for virtual table detection; PRAGMA table_info does not work on FTS5 tables.

`migrate_plan_project(conn)` — extract from plan_library.py:136–180. **Audit note**: This is a compound migration — it includes FTS rebuild + trigger recreation, not just ALTER TABLE. Extract all of it verbatim; do not simplify.

`migrate_access_tracking(conn)` — extract from memory_store.py:331–350. Uses PRAGMA table_info(memory) — correct.

`migrate_topics(conn)` — extract from catalog_taxonomy.py:157–191. Uses `sqlite_master` guard — **do not normalize to PRAGMA**. Audit finding: migrate_topics uses sqlite_master guard, not PRAGMA. Keep as-is.

`migrate_plan_ttl(conn)` — extract from plan_library.py:182–193. Uses PRAGMA table_info(plans).

`migrate_assigned_by(conn)` — extract from catalog_taxonomy.py:193–208. Uses PRAGMA table_info(topic_assignments).

`migrate_review_columns(conn)` — extract from catalog_taxonomy.py:210–227. Uses PRAGMA table_info(topics).

**Threading — apply_pending lock:**
- Add a module-level `_bootstrap_lock = threading.Lock()` in migrations.py
- The bootstrap check (step 3: read + conditionally insert row in _nexus_version) must run under this lock
- **Audit finding**: apply_pending needs its own threading.Lock for bootstrap check race — two concurrent T2Database constructors on same path could both see no row and both insert PRE_REGISTRY_VERSION

**_upgrade_done vs per-domain _migrated_paths:**
- `_upgrade_done: set[str]` is module-level in migrations.py — checked by T2Database before opening any connection
- Per-domain `_migrated_paths` sets (one each in memory_store.py:57, plan_library.py:47, catalog_taxonomy.py:56) must continue to exist
- **Audit finding**: _upgrade_done and per-domain _migrated_paths must coexist — do not remove per-domain sets; they guard standalone store construction

## Audit Correction (from plan-auditor)

The SQL query must filter `WHERE parent_id IS NULL` to exclude child/sub-topics. The existing `CatalogTaxonomy.get_topics()` method (no args) already does this correctly — it returns root topics only. Do NOT use `get_topics_for_collection()` which returns all topics including children. Use direct SQL or `get_topics()` with collection filtering.

## Execution Instructions

1. Create `tests/test_context.py` FIRST (TDD):
   - `test_generate_context_l1_with_topics`: mock CatalogTaxonomy.get_topics(), verify output format
   - `test_generate_context_l1_empty_taxonomy`: no topics → file not written (or empty guard)
   - `test_generate_context_l1_groups_by_prefix`: code/docs/knowledge/rdr grouping from collection field
   - `test_generate_context_l1_top5_per_prefix`: verify limit of 5 topics per prefix by doc_count
   - `test_generate_context_l1_atomic_write`: verify temp file + os.replace pattern
   - `test_refresh_context_l1`: verify convenience wrapper opens T2Database and delegates

2. Implement `src/nexus/context.py`:

   ```python
   # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
   CONTEXT_L1_PATH = Path.home() / ".config" / "nexus" / "context_l1.txt"

   def generate_context_l1(taxonomy: CatalogTaxonomy, *, output_path: Path | None = None) -> Path:
       ...

   def refresh_context_l1(db_path: Path | None = None) -> Path:
       ...
   ```

3. SQL correctness (audit fix):

   The correct query to get root topics only, all collections, ordered by doc_count:
   ```sql
   SELECT collection, label, doc_count
   FROM topics
   WHERE parent_id IS NULL
   ORDER BY doc_count DESC
   ```

   `CatalogTaxonomy.get_topics()` (no `parent_id` arg, line 232 of `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`) already applies `WHERE parent_id IS NULL`. You can call it and filter/group in Python, or issue raw SQL via `taxonomy.conn.execute()` within a `with taxonomy._lock:` block.

4. Grouping and formatting:
   - Group by `collection.split('__')[0]` → `code`, `docs`, `knowledge`, `rdr`
   - Top 5 per prefix by `doc_count`
   - Format:
     ```

       code: GPU Kernel Programming (1294), Latency Benchmarking (1272), JUnit Testing (1202)
       knowledge: Organization Member Services (71), Byzantine Consensus (68)
     ```
   - Target: ≤ 200 tokens total

5. Atomic write pattern:
   ```python
   output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   tmp = output_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
   tmp.write_text(content)
   os.replace(tmp, output_path)
   ```

6. `refresh_context_l1()` opens `T2Database(db_path or default_db_path())` and calls `generate_context_l1(db.taxonomy)`.

7. Logging: use `structlog.get_logger(__name__)` — no `print()` statements.

8. Run tests: `uv run pytest tests/test_context.py -v`

- `src/nexus/context.py` type-checks (all public functions annotated)
- Atomic write: confirm `.tmp` intermediary used, not direct write
- SQL excludes child topics: `parent_id IS NULL` in query

# P3.2 Create PR for RDR-071

**Context**: Create PR for RDR-071 Query Sanitizer implementation.
**RDR**: RDR-071 (accepted). **Epic**: nexus-xyh

**Prerequisites**: nexus-xyh.8 (test suite green)

---

## Execution Instructions

1. Create branch:
   ```
   git checkout -b feature/nexus-xyh-query-sanitizer
   ```

2. Stage all modified/created files:
   ```
   git add src/nexus/filters.py
   git add src/nexus/mcp/core.py
   git add src/nexus/config.py
   git add tests/test_query_sanitizer.py
   ```
   Also add `tests/test_mcp_sanitizer.py` if integration tests were created in a separate file.

3. Commit referencing RDR-071 and bead nexus-xyh (no AI attribution per project conventions):
   ```
   git commit -m "feat(search): add query sanitizer for system prompt contamination (RDR-071)

   - Add sanitize_query() to filters.py: 4-step cascade (passthrough, question
     extraction, tail sentence, tail truncation)
   - Wire sanitizer into MCP search() and query() tools in mcp/core.py
   - Add search.query_sanitizer config default (True) to config.py
   - Port and adapt test suite from mempalace reference implementation

   Refs: nexus-xyh"
   ```

4. Push and create PR:
   ```
   git push -u origin feature/nexus-xyh-query-sanitizer
   gh pr create --title "feat(search): query sanitizer for system prompt contamination (RDR-071)" --body "..."
   ```

5. **PR description must include**:

   ```markdown
   ## Problem
   AI agents prepend system prompts (2000+ chars) to search queries. MiniLM (local mode)
   suffers 5x distance inflation, filtering all results as noise. Voyage AI (cloud) is
   resilient (80% overlap) but not immune. Silent failure — no error, no warning.

   ## Solution
   4-step cascade in `filters.sanitize_query()`, wired into MCP `search()` and `query()`
   tools before queries reach `search_cross_corpus`:
   1. Passthrough (<= 200 chars) — no degradation
   2. Question extraction (last sentence ending with ?) — near-full recovery
   3. Tail sentence extraction — moderate recovery
   4. Tail truncation (last 500 chars) — minimum viable fallback

   ## Success Criteria Validation
   - **SC-1** (local MiniLM >= 60% recall): validated by logic coverage. Unit tests confirm
     correct extraction of query intent. Live measurements (RF-071-4) established algorithm
     effectiveness during research phase.
   - **SC-2** (cloud Voyage >= 95% clean-query overlap): validated by logic coverage. Short
     queries take the passthrough path unchanged. Live measurements (RF-071-3) confirmed
     Voyage resilience.
   - **SC-3** (< 1ms latency): pure Python implementation — regex + string slicing, no LLM,
     no network, no embedding calls. Verified via pytest timing output.
   - **SC-4** (5 contamination patterns): TestContaminationPatterns covers system prompt,
     chain-of-thought, tool preamble, multi-turn context, empty.

   ## Config
   Enabled by default. Disable per-repo: `search.query_sanitizer: false` in `.nexus.yml`.
   CLI paths (`nx search`) are not affected — only MCP tool paths are vulnerable.

   ## Files changed
   - `src/nexus/filters.py` — add `sanitize_query()`, constants, regex patterns
   - `src/nexus/mcp/core.py` — wire sanitizer into `search()` and `query()` tools
   - `src/nexus/config.py` — add `search.query_sanitizer: true` default
   - `tests/test_query_sanitizer.py` — unit + integration tests
   ```

---

## Validation

PR created. CI green.
close_reason: RDR-071 implementation complete. 24 sanitizer tests + 193 full suite pass. Ready for release.

# P1.2 Implement sanitize_query in filters.py

**Context**: Implement the 4-step query sanitizer cascade in nexus. Port from mempalace/mempalace/query_sanitizer.py (~130 lines).
**RDR**: RDR-071 (accepted). **Epic**: nexus-xyh

**Search keywords**: query sanitizer, filters, sentence splitting, regex, structlog

**Prerequisites**: nexus-xyh.1 (tests written first — TDD)

---

## Execution Instructions

1. Read the reference implementation: `/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/mempalace/mempalace/query_sanitizer.py`

2. Append to `/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus/src/nexus/filters.py` (after `parse_where_str`):

   **Constants** (identical to mempalace):
   ```python
   SAFE_QUERY_LENGTH = 200
   MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 500
   MIN_QUERY_LENGTH = 10
   ```

   **Regex patterns** (identical to mempalace):
   ```python
   _SENTENCE_SPLIT = re.compile(r"[.!?。！？\n]+")
   _QUESTION_MARK = re.compile(r'[?？]\s*["\']?\s*$')
   ```

   **Function signature**:
   ```python
   def sanitize_query(raw: str) -> str:
   ```

3. **Key adaptations from mempalace** (these are required — do not skip):

   | Mempalace | Nexus |
   |---|---|
   | Returns `dict` with `clean_query`, `was_sanitized`, etc. | Returns `str` (the clean query string only) |
   | `import logging` + `logger = logging.getLogger("mempalace_mcp")` | `import structlog` + `_log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)` at module level |
   | `logger.warning(...)` when sanitized | `_log.debug(...)` using structured fields |
   | Handles `None` input | No `None` handling (MCP tools type-annotate `query: str`) |

2. Create `tests/test_query_sanitizer.py` with the following test classes:
   - `TestPassthrough` — short queries (<= 200 chars) pass unchanged
   - `TestQuestionExtraction` — queries ending with `?` extracted correctly
   - `TestTailSentence` — last meaningful sentence extraction
   - `TestTailTruncation` — fallback to last 500 chars
   - `TestContaminationPatterns` — 5 patterns: system prompt, chain-of-thought, tool preamble, multi-turn context, empty
   - `TestLengthGuards` — output never exceeds MAX_QUERY_LENGTH

3. Imports for the nexus version:
   ```python
   from nexus.filters import sanitize_query, SAFE_QUERY_LENGTH, MAX_QUERY_LENGTH, MIN_QUERY_LENGTH
   ```

4. Tests should initially FAIL (function not yet implemented in filters.py).

5. Verify tests compile and are discoverable:
   ```
   uv run pytest tests/test_query_sanitizer.py --collect-only
   ```

---

## Critical Adaptation: nexus returns str, not dict

**AUDIT FINDING (nexus-xyh.1)**: The mempalace `sanitize_query` returns a `dict` with keys `clean_query`, `was_sanitized`, `original_length`, `clean_length`, `method`. The nexus version will return a plain `str` (the sanitized query string only).

**Do NOT do search-and-replace on the mempalace test file.** Every assertion that accesses `result["clean_query"]`, `result["was_sanitized"]`, `result["method"]`, etc. must be **fully rewritten** for the str interface. Examples:

| Mempalace (dict) | Nexus (str) |
|---|---|
| `assert result["clean_query"] == "What is Rust?"` | `assert result == "What is Rust?"` |
| `assert result["was_sanitized"] is True` | `assert result != original_query` (or check length) |
| `assert result["method"] == "passthrough"` | `assert result == original_query` (passthrough means unchanged) |
| `assert result["clean_length"] == len(result["clean_query"])` | `assert len(result) <= MAX_QUERY_LENGTH` |

**`TestMetadata` class is vestigial for the str interface** — drop it entirely (the metadata keys don't exist). Replace with `TestLengthConstraints` that checks:
- output never exceeds MAX_QUERY_LENGTH
- passthrough returns identical string
- contaminated queries return shorter string

**For `test_none_query`**: do NOT port — nexus MCP tools type-annotate `query` as `str`, so `None` input is not valid at the nexus API boundary.

---

## Contamination pattern test data

SC-4 requires 5 contamination patterns. Recommended test strings (adapt as needed):

1. **System prompt**: `"You are a helpful assistant with access to tools. Always be concise. " * 30 + "\nWhat is Byzantine fault tolerance?"`
2. **Chain-of-thought**: `"Let me think step by step. First I need to understand... Actually, the key question is: how does PBFT handle view changes?"`
3. **Tool preamble**: `"<tool_result>search returned 0 results</tool_result>\n\nSearch for: distributed consensus algorithms"`
4. **Multi-turn context**: `"User: What is Raft?\nAssistant: Raft is a consensus...\nUser: And how does it compare to PBFT?"`
5. **Empty / whitespace-only**: `""`, `"   "`, `"\n\n"`

---

   - If topic specified:
     - Call `CatalogTaxonomy.get_doc_ids_for_topic(label)` — query `topic_assignments JOIN topics WHERE topics.label = label`
     - Build where filter: `{'id': {'$in': doc_ids}}` (ChromaDB where clause)

   ```python
           "JOIN topics t ON t.id = ta.topic_id WHERE t.label = ?", (label,)
   ```

title: P1.6: Add post_store_hook in mcp_infra.py for incremental assignment
description:
## Context
RDR-070 Phase 1, RF-070-6. Add post_store_hook callback in mcp_infra.py.
Do NOT extend auto_linker.py — it is single-responsibility for links.

This bead depends only on nexus-9k5 (sklearn HDBSCAN engine).

## Design: ChromaDB centroid query for incremental assignment

Incremental assignment path in the hook:
1. Re-embed content with local MiniLM (~1ms)
2. Query `taxonomy__centroids` ChromaDB collection (HNSW/SPANN ANN index)
3. **Unconditional nearest-centroid assignment — no distance threshold (RDR RF-070-7).** Assign to T2 with assigned_by='centroid'. HDBSCAN eliminates manual thresholds; batch discover defines cluster boundaries; incremental assignment maps to nearest existing cluster.
4. Misassignments corrected at next re-discovery (2x corpus growth trigger).
5. No sklearn model loading. No pickle deserialization. Single ChromaDB query.

## Hook execution model
Synchronous, blocking store_put return. ~3ms total (1ms MiniLM + 1ms ANN + 1ms T2).
Follows catalog_auto_link pattern: exceptions caught per-hook, logged, never fail store_put.

## Recovery
If taxonomy__centroids collection is missing (no discover run yet), hook is a no-op — document stored without topic assignment. This is safe and expected before first discover.

## Files to Modify
- `src/nexus/mcp_infra.py` — add hook registration + firing mechanism
- `src/nexus/mcp/core.py` line 394 (`store_put` function) — call fire_post_store_hooks()

- `auto_linker.py`: `src/nexus/catalog/auto_linker.py` — pattern reference for non-fatal hook (try/except + structlog)

1. Write tests FIRST for hook mechanism
2. In mcp_infra.py, add:

   - `register_post_store_hook(fn: Callable[[str, str, str], None]) -> None`

- `sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity`: for nearest-centroid comparison

## Implementation
1. Run `sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=max(5, N//15), store_centers="centroid").fit_predict(embeddings)`
   on a sample of code__ART embeddings (re-embedded with local MiniLM 384d).
2. Generate c-TF-IDF labels via CountVectorizer+TfidfTransformer for each cluster.
3. Manual inspection: do the top-5 terms per cluster reflect recognizable code patterns
   (e.g., "HTTP handlers", "database queries", "test fixtures")?
4. Measure nearest-centroid vs batch agreement:
   - Hold out 10% of embeddings.
   - Run fit_predict on remaining 90%.
   - For each held-out embedding, find nearest centroid via cosine_similarity.
   - Compare assigned topic to what fit_predict would have assigned.
   - Report agreement percentage. If <75%, revisit min_cluster_size or consider UMAP reduction.

## Codebase Patterns
- Test fixtures: `chromadb.EphemeralClient()` for isolation, no API keys needed
- Synthetic test data: use `numpy.random.default_rng(seed=42)` for reproducible vectors
- Integration test marker: `@pytest.mark.integration` if real T3 data needed

## Test Commands
```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k "topic_quality or agreement" -v
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Code chunk topics show recognizable structural patterns in top-5 terms
- [ ] Nearest-centroid vs batch agreement measured and documented
- [ ] If agreement <75%, remediation plan documented
- [ ] No BERTopic dependency — uses sklearn HDBSCAN + ChromaDB centroid query only

## Dependency Constraints
- Blocked by: nexus-9k5 (P1.2 — sklearn HDBSCAN engine must exist to validate against)
- Blocks: nexus-mr0 (P1.8 — review gate)

title: P1.2: Replace catalog_taxonomy.py with sklearn HDBSCAN engine
description:
## Context
RDR-070 Phase 1. Replace the word-frequency Ward clustering in catalog_taxonomy.py with sklearn HDBSCAN.
The existing 520 LOC `cluster_and_persist()` pipeline is deleted. T2 schema (`topics`, `topic_assignments` tables) is retained with new `assigned_by` column.

## Design: sklearn HDBSCAN + ChromaDB centroid ANN
`sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN` replaces BERTopic. Centroids stored in ChromaDB `taxonomy__centroids` collection (not pickle files). c-TF-IDF labels via CountVectorizer+TfidfTransformer. No sentence-transformers, no PyTorch.

## Audit Finding M1 (data model mismatch)
The actual `topic_assignments` schema has `doc_id, topic_id` only. Add only `assigned_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hdbscan'` per RDR-070 gate remediation.

## Audit Finding M4 (constructor retention)
`CatalogTaxonomy.__init__` takes a `MemoryStore` reference via constructor injection. Retain this.

## Files to Modify
- `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py` (lines 85-520) — MAJOR REWRITE
- `src/nexus/taxonomy.py` — update deprecation shim
- `tests/test_taxonomy.py` — rewrite tests for sklearn-based API

## Implementation
1. Write tests FIRST for the new sklearn-based API
2. Delete `cluster_and_persist()` and supporting word-frequency code
3. Schema migration: `ALTER TABLE topic_assignments ADD COLUMN assigned_by TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hdbscan'`
   Values: 'hdbscan' (batch), 'centroid' (incremental), 'manual' (operator), 'auto-matched' (re-discovery)
4. New public methods on CatalogTaxonomy:
   - `discover_topics(collection, embeddings, chroma_client) -> int`
     `sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=max(5, len(embeddings)//15), store_centers="centroid").fit_predict(embeddings)`
     **c-TF-IDF text retrieval**: after fit_predict, retrieve texts from T3 via `collection.get(ids=chunk_ids, include=["documents"])`. Texts held in-memory for label generation only (~5MB for 9K docs).
     `CountVectorizer` + `TfidfTransformer` on per-cluster texts produce topic labels.
     Stores topics in T2. Upserts centroids to `taxonomy__centroids`.
   - `assign_single(collection, embedding, chroma_client) -> int | None`
     `taxonomy__centroids.query(query_embeddings=[emb], n_results=1)`.
     **Unconditional nearest-centroid assignment** — no distance threshold (RDR RF-070-7).
     Misassignments corrected at next re-discovery.
   - `_create_centroid_collection(client)` — `client.get_or_create_collection("taxonomy__centroids", embedding_function=None, metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})`. Do NOT use t3.get_or_create_collection().
5. **All-noise handling**: if HDBSCAN assigns all docs to noise (-1, store_centers returns empty), log warning, skip centroid upsert, return 0 topics.
6. **Batch noise**: docs assigned -1 get no topic_assignments row. `nx taxonomy list` shows "Uncategorized" count.
7. Recovery: centroid collection missing -> assign_single returns None (no-op).
8. Retain get_topics, get_topic_tree, get_topic_docs as-is.
9. No pickle files. No model persistence directory.

## Test Commands
```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -v
uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k "discover or assign_single or all_noise" -v
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] sklearn HDBSCAN discovers topics from MiniLM 384d embeddings
- [ ] c-TF-IDF labels generated from T3 document texts (not metadata)
- [ ] Centroids upserted to taxonomy__centroids with hnsw:space=cosine
- [ ] assign_single uses unconditional nearest-centroid (no threshold)
- [ ] All-noise path handled (0 topics, warning logged)
- [ ] assigned_by column migration applied
- [ ] No BERTopic, no PyTorch, no pickle files
- [ ] Tests pass
design:
## Design Change: sklearn HDBSCAN + ChromaDB centroids (replaces BERTopic)

### Why
BERTopic eagerly imports sentence-transformers + PyTorch (~500MB). sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN
provides the same density-based clustering with zero new heavy deps (scikit-learn is now a
core dep at 30MB). Verified in nexus-86v smoke tests.

### Architecture

**Batch discovery** (discover_topics):
1. sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=N, store_centers="centroid") on MiniLM 384d vectors
2. CountVectorizer + TfidfTransformer for c-TF-IDF topic labels (replaces BERTopic built-in)
3. Persist topics + assignments to T2 SQLite (existing schema, unchanged)
4. Upsert centroids into ChromaDB collection taxonomy__centroids with hnsw:space=cosine
   - metadata: {topic_id, label, collection, doc_count}
   - ChromaDB HNSW (local) / SPANN (cloud) handles ANN indexing automatically

**Incremental assignment** (assign_single):
1. Re-embed new doc with local MiniLM (~1ms)
2. taxonomy__centroids.query(query_embeddings=[emb], n_results=1) -> nearest topic
3. Assign unconditionally to nearest centroid in T2. No distance threshold (RDR RF-070-7). Misassignments corrected at next re-discovery.

**No pickle files.** No .bertopic model dirs. No manual cosine_similarity.
Centroids live in ChromaDB — same persistence/replication story as all other embeddings.

### What changes from the original bead description
- Delete all BERTopic references (import, fit_transform, approximate_predict, model save/load)
- discover_topics() uses SklearnHDBSCAN + CountVectorizer/TfidfTransformer
- assign_single() queries taxonomy__centroids ChromaDB collection, not HDBSCAN approximate_predict
- No get_model_path() or load_model() methods — centroids are in ChromaDB
- No ~/.config/nexus/taxonomy/ directory needed
- model_version column on topics table: still useful for tracking which discover run produced a topic
notes:
## RF-070-11: ChromaDB centroid collection requirements

The taxonomy__centroids collection has 3 requirements that differ from normal T3 collections:

1. **hnsw:space=cosine** — must be set at creation (t3.py:330 only sets hnsw:search_ef).
   MiniLM embeddings are L2-normalized; cosine is the correct metric. Cloud SPANN always
   uses cosine, but local HNSW defaults to L2 without explicit override.
   SPANN params are immutable after creation — get it right the first time.

2. **No VoyageAI EF** — centroids are pre-computed MiniLM 384d vectors, not Voyage.
   _embedding_fn() in t3.py routes by collection prefix. taxonomy__ is not a recognized
   prefix, so either: (a) always pass embeddings= explicitly to upsert/query, or
   (b) register taxonomy__ prefix to use LocalEmbeddingFunction.

3. **Pre-computed embeddings on both read and write** — upsert centroids with
   embeddings= parameter. Query with query_embeddings= parameter. Never let ChromaDB
   invoke an EF for this collection.
close_reason: HDBSCAN engine rewrite complete: discover_topics, assign_single, _create_centroid_collection, assigned_by migration. 23 taxonomy tests + 6 concurrency tests pass.

title: P1.1: Add bertopic dependency + verify minimal install path
description:
## Context
RDR-070 Phase 1, first task. Add bertopic to pyproject.toml dependencies.

## Audit Finding S2 (SEVERITY: S — must address)
BERTopic's minimal install path (no sentence-transformers/PyTorch) is unverified. This bead MUST include a contingency plan:
1. **Happy path**: `bertopic>=0.16` installs cleanly; `fit_transform(docs, embeddings)` works with pre-computed numpy arrays; no PyTorch pulled.
2. **Fallback 1** — if BERTopic's import path unconditionally imports sentence-transformers: try `pip install bertopic --no-deps` then manually install only `hdbscan`, `umap-learn`, `scikit-learn`. Document the minimal dep set.
3. **Fallback 2** — if BERTopic cannot function without sentence-transformers at all: use HDBSCAN directly (`hdbscan>=0.8.38`) + UMAP (`umap-learn>=0.5`). The BERTopic wrapper adds c-TF-IDF topic labeling, but HDBSCAN+UMAP alone can cluster. Topic labels can be derived from top TF-IDF terms manually (the existing `cluster_and_persist()` already does this).
4. **Fallback 3** — pin with `--no-deps` and vendor only the clustering path.

Document which path was taken in a comment at the top of the smoke test.

## Files to Modify
- `pyproject.toml` — line ~30 (dependencies array): add `"bertopic>=0.16"` or the fallback dep set
- `tests/test_taxonomy.py` — add `test_bertopic_smoke` test function

## Codebase Patterns
- Dependencies in pyproject.toml follow alphabetical order in the dependencies array
- Test files use `pytest` + `chromadb.EphemeralClient` for isolation
- Local embedding: `src/nexus/db/local_ef.py` — `LocalEmbeddingFunction` wraps `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` (384d). Use `_TIER0_MODEL` / `_TIER1_MODEL` constants. `_MODEL_DIMS` dict maps model names to dimensions.

## Implementation
1. Add `bertopic>=0.16` to pyproject.toml dependencies array
2. Run `uv sync` to install
3. Write a smoke test that:
   - Imports bertopic
   - Creates a BERTopic model with pre-computed numpy embeddings (no sentence-transformers/PyTorch)
   - Calls fit_transform(docs, embeddings) with synthetic data (50+ docs, 384d random vectors)
   - Verifies topics are assigned
4. If the happy path fails, execute Fallback 1/2/3 in order. Document decision.
5. Record the actual installed dependency tree size (`uv pip tree bertopic`)

## Test Commands
```bash
uv run pytest tests/test_taxonomy.py -k bertopic_smoke -v
uv pip tree bertopic  # verify dep chain
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] bertopic (or fallback) importable after uv sync
- [ ] fit_transform works with pre-computed 384d numpy arrays
- [ ] Contingency path documented if happy path failed
- [ ] Test passes in CI
- [ ] No PyTorch/sentence-transformers in required dep chain

## Dependency Constraints
- No blockers — this is the first bead in the chain
- nexus-9k5 (P1.2) and nexus-ih2 (P1.3) both depend on this completing first
notes:
## Resolution: sklearn replaces BERTopic (no optional extra needed)

BERTopic eagerly imports sentence-transformers at module load, pulling PyTorch
(~373MB) + sentence-transformers as unavoidable transitive deps. Pivoted to
scikit-learn>=1.3 as a core dep instead:

- `sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN` — same density-based clustering, `store_centers="centroid"`
  gives centroids for incremental assignment
- `CountVectorizer` + `TfidfTransformer` — c-TF-IDF topic labels (~10 LOC)
- `cosine_similarity` — nearest-centroid incremental assignment (~3 LOC)
- No UMAP needed (HDBSCAN works directly on 384d MiniLM vectors)

Weight: 30MB (scikit-learn + threadpoolctl) vs. ~500MB (bertopic + torch chain).
scipy + joblib already present as transitive deps. No config gating needed — core dep.

ChromaDB already indexes embeddings via HNSW (local) / SPANN (cloud) — downstream
beads can query T3 for nearest centroid rather than maintaining separate state.

## Tests
3 smoke tests in TestSklearnHdbscanSmoke:
- test_hdbscan_finds_clusters: 60 docs, 384d, >=2 clusters
- test_tfidf_topic_labels: per-cluster top terms from correct domain
- test_incremental_nearest_centroid: new doc assigned to correct cluster
All 21 taxonomy tests pass in 0.29s.

# P1.5: Dogfood — one-week usage + post-mortem

Context: nx — RDR-064 Decision #15. Acceptance criteria per SC-10: ship only with usage evidence. One minimum-week single-operator use followed by an honest post-mortem.

This bead is created per audit correction from plan-auditor. Decision #15 in RDR-064 explicitly requires: "One-week minimum single-operator use, honest post-mortem" before shipping. SC-10 (Success Criterion 10) encodes this as a gate.

## Prerequisites

nexus-gut (Phase 1 code review — go verdict issued)

## Execution

### Week of Usage (Days 1-7)

Run `nx console --port 8765` as the primary observability surface during normal Nexus work. Minimum usage triggers:
- [ ] At least one live agent indexing run observed in Activity Stream
- [ ] At least one T1 session liveness check in Sessions & Health
- [ ] At least one named campaign reviewed in Campaigns & Provenance
- [ ] At least one console start/stop cycle confirming pid file cleanup

Track a daily log of observations (free-form, written to `~/.config/nexus/logs/console-dogfood.log` or similar).

### Post-Mortem (Day 8)

Write a brief post-mortem covering:

1. **What worked** — which panels were actually used, which features were reached for organically
2. **What was missing** — features the operator reached for that don't exist in v0.1
3. **What was confusing** — UX issues, layout surprises, misleading data
4. **What was wrong** — bugs, crashes, data accuracy issues
5. **Decision #15 verdict**: does v0.1 meet the "meaningful operator observability" bar?

### SC-10 Acceptance Criteria

Per RDR-064 SC-10:
- [ ] Minimum one week of real use (not demo runs)
- [ ] Post-mortem written and filed (in `docs/rdr/` or a scratch note)
- [ ] Either: no blocking issues found → close RDR-064 | OR: blocking issues identified → new bead(s) created to address before close

## Deliverable

Post-mortem doc + go/no-go verdict on RDR-064 closure. If no-go, create follow-up beads before closing.

RDR-064 closure (via `/nx:rdr-close rdr-064`)

# P1.4: Panel 3 — Campaigns & Provenance

Context: nx — RDR-064 Phase 1, Panel 3. Answers "what did that agent campaign actually produce?" Landing at `/campaigns`, split into System creators (collapsed) and Named campaigns (expanded).

## Codebase Facts

- **`~/.config/nexus/catalog/links.jsonl`** — 16,412 lines at measurement. Groupby `created_by` in one pass. Field: `created_by`, `link_type`, `source`, `target`, `created_at`, `owner`, `content_type`.
- **Known named campaigns** (from RF-064-12): `rdr-068-research`, `research-campaign-2026-04-08`, `synthesis-gap-analysis`, `claude-session-2026-04-09`, `deep-analyst`, `deep-research-synthesizer`, `720-review`, `user`.
- **System creators** (collapsed by default): `index_hook`, `filepath_extractor`, `auto-linker`.
- **Named campaigns** (expanded by default): everything not in the system creators list.
- **Catalog SQLite** — use for efficient repeat queries when JSONL scan > 500 ms: `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_db.py`. v0.1: re-scan per request; add LRU cache keyed on `links.jsonl` mtime when page load exceeds 500 ms.
- **Phoenix trace tree pattern (RF-064-16)**: hierarchical nesting — campaign row → link batch → individual link. Disclosure triangle + indented children, colored by link type. Use `<details>/<summary>` (Pico native, no JS needed for basic expand/collapse).
- **LangSmith thread grouping pattern (RF-064-16)**: multiple campaigns on the same topic co-located by `created_by` prefix similarity. v0.1: simple groupby `created_by`; semantic clustering deferred.
- **`src/nexus/console/routes/campaigns.py`** — stub created in nexus-aq4. This bead fills it in.
- **Scope model**: `?scope=project|all`. Project scope filters by `owner` derived from cwd at `nx console` launch. All scope shows cross-project activity.

## Prerequisites

nexus-aq4 (console infrastructure). Run `/nx:composition-probe nexus-aq4` and verify PASS before starting.

## Routes to Implement

```
GET /campaigns?scope=...                                      # campaigns landing
GET /campaigns/{created_by}                                   # campaign detail
GET /campaigns/{created_by}/links?scope=...&...filters        # all links for a campaign
GET /campaigns/{created_by}/docs?scope=...                    # all docs registered by campaign
```

## Execution

1. **Write tests first**: `tests/test_campaigns_panel.py`
   ```python
   from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
   from nexus.console.app import create_app

   def test_campaigns_landing_200():
       client = TestClient(create_app())
       resp = client.get("/campaigns?scope=all")
       assert resp.status_code == 200

   def test_campaigns_split_into_system_and_named():
       client = TestClient(create_app())
       resp = client.get("/campaigns?scope=all")
       # Verify two sections exist
       assert "system" in resp.text.lower() or "index_hook" in resp.text.lower()

   def test_campaign_detail_404_for_unknown():
       client = TestClient(create_app())
       resp = client.get("/campaigns/nonexistent-campaign-xyz")
       assert resp.status_code in (200, 404)
   ```
2. Implement JSONL groupby in `src/nexus/console/routes/campaigns.py`:
   ```python
   def _load_campaign_summary(links_path: Path, scope: str, project_owner: str) -> dict:
       """One-pass groupby over links.jsonl. Returns {created_by: CampaignSummary}."""
   ```
   - Single pass over `links.jsonl` lines — collect `{created_by: {count, link_types, content_types, time_range, doc_count_approx}}`
   - LRU cache keyed on `(links_path, mtime, scope)` — invalidate on mtime change
3. Implement `GET /campaigns` route:
   - Separate system creators from named campaigns using a constant set
   - System creators section: `<details>` collapsed by default (Pico `<details open>` only on named section)
   - Named campaigns section: one row per `created_by` with: name | link count | doc count | time range | link types | content types
   - Each row: click → `hx-get="/campaigns/{created_by}"` → right-panel or page navigation
4. Implement `GET /campaigns/{created_by}` detail route:
   - Timeline view (chronological link creation)
   - Link list with Phoenix-style expand/collapse (`<details>/<summary>` per link type batch)
   - Doc list (documents.jsonl filtered by `created_by`)
   - Link-type breakdown (counts per type)
5. Implement `templates/campaigns/index.html`:
   - Two sections using Pico `<details>`: System (collapsed), Named (expanded)
   - Campaign row: lnav-inspired left color border per creator class
   - Scope toggle in top nav (carries through all HTMX `hx-get` calls via URL param)
6. Implement `templates/campaigns/detail.html`:
   - Phoenix trace tree visual: `<details>` nesting for link batches
   - Filter bar: time window, link_type, content_type (same HTMX pattern as Activity Stream)
7. Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_campaigns_panel.py -x`

## Templates to Create/Fill

- `src/nexus/console/templates/campaigns/index.html`
- `src/nexus/console/templates/campaigns/detail.html`
- `src/nexus/console/templates/campaigns/_links.html` — HTMX partial for link list
- `src/nexus/console/templates/campaigns/_docs.html` — HTMX partial for doc list

## Key Design Constraints

- **One-pass groupby** — re-scan per request; add LRU cache on mtime when > 500 ms (expected at 100K+ entries)
- **No CDN** — all assets vendored (already done in nexus-aq4)
- **Scope param threads through all routes** — every `hx-get` includes `?scope={current_scope}`
- **v0.1: no destructive actions** — read-only observation only

## Estimated Effort

2-3 days

## Blocks

nexus-gut (P1 review)
close_reason: Campaigns panel: JSONL groupby, system/named split, detail view with link-type tree, 7 tests pass
