description:
RDR-196 **Phase 1, Step 3 — CLIENT HALF.** Carries the WIRE-CONTRACT LEDGER
DECLARE for the pair. Rides the paired release at `.p1f`.

## ⚠ WIRE-CONTRACT CHANGE — this bead carries the CLIENT HALF of `.p1c`

The `steps[]` array on `POST /v1/telemetry/nx_answer_runs/record` is a wire
contract change. Per the tk070 precedent (`.p6a`/`.p6b`), the pairing is
mechanized through the ledger: **declare this pair in
`docs/wire-contract-pending.md` under `Unshipped` (:44)**, and it moves to
`Shipped` (:48) only at `.p1f`'s paired cut. The release gates refuse an
un-paired client release; the ack is the paired cut itself.

## What ships

1. **Stop writing `cost_usd = 0.0`.** Eight call sites:
   `src/nexus/mcp/core.py` 6538, 6644, 6670, 6738, 6776, 6884, 6995, 7099.
   `_nx_answer_record_run` is at :5785-5814. The run row's `cost_usd` becomes
   the **sum of its step rows**.
2. Client write-through of the `StepRecord` list from `.p1b` to the endpoint.
3. **Capability probe.** Send `steps` only when the engine advertises support;
   otherwise degrade to the run-row-only record with a logged warning — never a
   400. Per the RDR: "a client ahead of its engine degrades ... never a 400".

## The probe is a VACUOUS-GATE RISK — treat it as one

After `.p1f` bumps `REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION`, every local install gets exactly
the pinned engine, so the older-engine branch is unreachable in ordinary
testing and only real during the cloud deploy window. A branch that never runs
is not a fallback; it is untested code that will be wrong when it finally
fires. The test MUST force the branch explicitly (stub the probe to report an
older engine), not wait for ambient conditions (nexus-moht0 doctrine: a sweep
that found nothing to check is a failure, not a pass).

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: decide what the probe reads — engine `/version`
   fields vs a capability list — and whether the client caches the answer per
   process. Note that the public edge has stubbed `/version` before
   (nexus-bwulw, 2026-07-23: three client features shipped green through every
   engine-direct gate and were dead through the edge). Whatever the probe
   reads must be something `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh` asserts
   survives the edge.
2. **TDD, red first**: (a) run + steps written, run `cost_usd` equals the sum
   of the step rows to the cent; (b) probe reports no support -> run row only
   + warning, NO exception, NO 400; (c) probe path itself asserted, not
   assumed.
3. Delete the `cost_usd=0.0` literals at all eight sites. `grep -n "cost_usd=0"
   src/nexus/mcp/core.py` must return nothing.
4. Declare the pair in `docs/wire-contract-pending.md` Unshipped.
5. Telemetry write failure must not fail the answer — the `_warn_telemetry_drop`
   path already exists; assert the run still returns its answer when the step
   write fails.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] `grep -n "cost_usd=0" src/nexus/mcp/core.py` returns NOTHING.
- [ ] A test asserts `run.cost_usd == sum(step.cost_usd)` on a real multi-step
      run against the ENGINE SUBSTRATE, not a mock (the RDR's MVV wording:
      "asserted by a test against the engine substrate, not a mock").
- [ ] The older-engine degradation test FORCES the branch and asserts both the
      run-row-only write and the warning. Demonstrate the branch is taken
      (assert on the warning), do not infer it.
- [ ] A test asserts a step-write failure still returns the answer.
- [ ] `docs/wire-contract-pending.md` Unshipped carries the declare, naming
      both halves' commits.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -n auto` green.

## Depends

`.p1c` (the endpoint must accept `steps` before the client sends it).
notes: Commits cc61d4c31 (client, shared with lme1s) + ledger declare 6bf155e76. Reviews [23091] [23092]; dev notes [23088]. Partial-steps-on-exception folded into .11.
close_reason: Steps write-through behind a /version capability probe (nx_answer_steps_supported), run cost_usd = sum of step costs or None, nine cost_usd=0.0 literals removed, degradation forced in test, step-write failure never fails the answer, integration round trip against the engine. Ledger declared (engine tag TBD, tk070 precedent). Commit on develop.

title: RDR-196 .p1c (Phase 1 Step 3, ENGINE HALF): nx_answer_steps Liquibase changeset at the changelog tail + optional steps[] on the record endpoint, one transaction, tenant-keyed + RLS
description:
RDR-196 **Phase 1, Step 3 — ENGINE HALF.** Rides the paired release at `.p1f`.

## ⚠ ALL DDL THROUGH LIQUIBASE — this is engine DDL, not a client table

Hot rule, no exceptions in code comments: new persistent state goes to PG
through Liquibase via the engine. `nx_answer_steps` is an engine table. There
is no client-side alternative (the RDR's "parallel telemetry table on the
client" alternative was rejected for exactly this reason).

## What ships

- A **NEW changeset file at the changelog TAIL**, `telemetry-00N-nx-answer-steps.xml`
  (next free number in the `telemetry-*` family). It is **NOT an edit of
  `telemetry-001-baseline.xml` changesets 7-8** (:182-216) which own
  `nx_answer_runs` — editing a shipped changeset is a checksum break.
- Table `nx_answer_steps`: tenant-keyed and RLS'd exactly like its parent
  `nx_answer_runs`, FK to the run row. Columns per the RDR's `StepRecord`:
  `{run_id, step_index, operator, source, model, input_tokens, output_tokens,
  cost_usd, elapsed_ms, ok, bundled_steps}`.
- `POST /v1/telemetry/nx_answer_runs/record` (`TelemetryHandler.java` route
  :110, handler :325) accepts an **optional** `steps: [...]` array and writes
  parent + children **in ONE transaction**. Optional is the compatibility
  hinge for `.p1d`'s capability probe.
- The version/capability advertisement `.p1d` probes against.

## Column-type discipline (nexus-cefa1 arc precedent)

Pick types deliberately, not by habit: `source` is a small closed set (llm | sql
| bundle) — constrain it; `cost_usd` is money — do NOT use float if the schema
family uses numeric; `ok` is boolean; `bundled_steps` is an int array or JSON,
not a comma string. The schema type-hygiene arc (nexus-cefa1) retyped 14
columns that were chosen by habit; do not add a 15th.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: settle the FK's ON DELETE behaviour and whether
   `(run_id, step_index)` is the natural PK. A bundle produces ONE record for
   several indices — decide what `step_index` means for it and make the PK
   honest about that. Getting this wrong is a schema change later, which costs
   another engine cut.
2. **TDD, red first**, Java side: a repository/handler test that posting a run
   WITH `steps` writes both, and that a failure inside the child write rolls
   back the parent. Partial-write telemetry is worse than none.
3. A test that posting a run WITHOUT `steps` still succeeds (the degradation
   contract `.p1d` depends on).
4. Tenant isolation test: tenant A cannot read tenant B's step rows. This is
   the standing multi-tenant assertion class; a new tenant-keyed table without
   one is an RLS hole.
5. Register the changeset in the master changelog at the TAIL, before any
   runAlways grants. Pin `EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS` to the files as authored.
6. **Full `./mvnw test`** — the standing rule for any Java schema change; a
   partial run is not evidence (and watch for stale surefire reports inflating
   the count).

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] `git diff` touches a NEW `telemetry-*` file; `telemetry-001-baseline.xml`
      is UNCHANGED (checksum integrity).
- [ ] Rollback tested: the changeset's rollback runs clean and does not leave a
      differently-typed table behind (the `lelhx` P2 class — vectors-004
      rollback recreated per-dim tables as BYTEA).
- [ ] Transaction test proves parent+children roll back together.
- [ ] Run-without-steps test passes (degradation contract).
- [ ] Cross-tenant read returns zero rows.
- [ ] Full `./mvnw test` green on the exact tree, plus
      `scripts/build-gate-jar.sh` re-run.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --candidate-migration` exercises
      the new changeset (mandatory for any changeset riding a cut).

## Depends

`.p1b` (the StepRecord shape must be settled before it becomes a column list —
a shape change after this bead costs an extra engine cut).
notes: Commit e87d2d9c7. Reviews [23072] [23073]; dev notes [23068]. Capability field: nx_answer_steps_supported (boolean, always true).
close_reason: telemetry-007 (2 changesets: table + RLS), FK cascade, PK (run_id, step_index), source CHECK, cost_usd NUMERIC child / DOUBLE parent documented; steps[] optional on the record endpoint in ONE txn; /version nx_answer_steps_supported; RLS canary + cloud gate updated. mvn 2193/0/0. Commit on develop. OPEN ITEM owned by orchestrator: migration-rehearsal --candidate-migration (EXPECT_NEW_CHANGESETS=2) runs in the .p1f battery.

title: RDR-196 .p1b (Phase 1 Step 2): collect one StepRecord per executed step in plans/runner.py — all three completion sites, SQL fast path (Gap 5), one record per bundle
description:
RDR-196 **Phase 1, Step 2**.

## The gap (Gap 1 second half, and Gap 5)

`src/nexus/plans/runner.py` already instruments every step:
`nx_answer_step_start` at :1185-1190, `nx_answer_step_complete` at :1285, :1361
and :1467 — three emission sites, i.e. three code paths a StepRecord must be
produced on, not one. These events carry `elapsed_ms` **to the log file only**,
never to the store, and with no model, tokens, or cost.

Gap 5 rides here too: `operator_filter` / `operator_groupby` /
`operator_aggregate` choose a SQL fast path over `document_aspects` versus a
`claude -p` dispatch via `source="auto"` keyword cues. That is NOMA's
deterministic-vs-stochastic engine choice, made with no cost estimate and
**never recorded as a decision**. Recording `source` per step is what turns it
into a measurable decision instead of an invisible one.

Bundling (`src/nexus/plans/bundle.py`, `dispatch_bundle:732`,
`compose_bundle_prompt:687`) already performs NOMA's *fusion* transformation —
adjacent operators collapsed into one dispatch — heuristically and unrecorded.
The measured consequence (h33x8.6): a 4-operator bundle costs about the same as
a 2-operator bundle; marginal cost of an extra bundled operator is near zero
while the FIXED cost of a round trip is ~50-65s. A bundle must therefore be
ONE record listing its bundled step indices, not N invented per-step records —
inventing per-step costs by dividing the bundle cost would fabricate data and
destroy exactly the finding above.

## Target shape (RDR § Technical Design)

```
StepRecord = {run_id, step_index, operator, source: "llm"|"sql"|"bundle",
              model: str|None, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int,
              cost_usd: float, elapsed_ms: int, ok: bool, bundled_steps: [int]}
```

SQL fast-path steps record `model=None, cost_usd=0` — and `source="sql"`, which
is what makes them distinguishable from a broken LLM step that recorded zero.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: reason through the bundle attribution. 196-R1
   established `modelUsage` is keyed per model, so a multi-turn bundle IS
   attributable per model — decide whether the bundle record carries the
   per-model breakdown or a single roll-up, and say why.
2. **TDD, red first**, in `tests/test_plan_run.py`: a plan run produces one
   StepRecord per executed step; a bundled run produces one record whose
   `bundled_steps` lists the fused indices and whose `source == "bundle"`.
3. Cover ALL THREE `nx_answer_step_complete` sites (:1285, :1361, :1467). A
   test that only exercises one path leaves two silent. Assert the count of
   records equals the count of executed steps for a plan that traverses more
   than one of those paths.
4. Cover the FAILURE path: a step that errors must still produce a record with
   `ok=False` and whatever usage the dispatch reported before failing. A
   telemetry layer that only records successes measures the wrong population —
   this is the same mistake that produced the 45x-wrong docstring figure.
5. Record `source` for the SQL fast-path branches in
   `operator_filter`/`groupby`/`aggregate` (Gap 5).
6. Pass the record list to the run recorder; do NOT yet write to the engine —
   that is `.p1c`/`.p1d`. This bead ends at an in-process list plus the
   structlog fields.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] Red-first tests shown failing pre-change.
- [ ] A test asserts `len(step_records) == executed_step_count` on a plan that
      hits at least two of the three completion sites.
- [ ] A test asserts a bundled dispatch produces exactly ONE record with a
      populated `bundled_steps`, and that no per-step cost was fabricated by
      division.
- [ ] A test asserts a SQL fast-path step records `source == "sql"`,
      `model is None`, `cost_usd == 0` — and is therefore distinguishable from
      a zero-cost LLM step.
- [ ] A test asserts a FAILED step still produces a record with `ok=False`.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -n auto` green.

## Depends

`.p1a` (usage capture is the source of the model/token/cost fields).
notes: Commit 7b86ae96d. Reviews T2 [23056] [23057]; dev notes [23054].
close_reason: StepRecord at all three completion sites + failure paths; bundles one record, cost undivided; SQL fast path source=sql; isolated-path usage captured via ambient ContextVar sink (no operator signature change); multi-dispatch roll-up tested. 426 passed. Commit on develop. Note: model/cost/source are on the in-process StepRecord, not added to the structlog step_complete event.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## AUDIT FOLD R3-prevention (nx_plan_audit 2026-08-20) — the `model` column is load-bearing for Phase 3

Note for whoever implements the StepRecord shape: `model` is not merely descriptive telemetry. **.p3a's budget derivation filters on it** to separate pre-flip (all-strong) from post-flip (tiered) cost populations — the schema-level prevention of the mixed-tier pooling hazard (risk R3). Pooling the two produces a median describing neither, and nothing downstream would surface it.

Consequences for this bead:
- `model` must be recorded accurately per record, from the dispatch envelope's reported id — **not** from what the caller intended to request. 196-R1 established `modelUsage` reports `canonicalModel`; prefer the reported canonical id over the requested alias, since an alias can re-point under the product and would silently invalidate every derivation that filtered on it.
- SQL fast-path steps record `model=None` — already specified, and it is what keeps them out of the model-filtered population by construction.
- For a BUNDLE, the record's model must be attributable. 196-R1 confirmed `modelUsage` is keyed per model, so a multi-turn bundle IS attributable — this is the concrete reason the bead's step-1 decision (per-model breakdown vs single roll-up) matters downstream, not just aesthetically.

**Added VERIFICATION:**
- [ ] A test asserts the recorded `model` equals the envelope's reported canonical id, not the requested alias.

title: RDR-196 .p1a (Phase 1 Step 1): capture cost/usage/model from the claude -p stream-json result envelope in claude_dispatch — dispatch.py discards all of it today
description:
RDR-196 **Phase 1, Step 1** — head of the arc's critical path.

## The gap (Gap 1, first half)

`src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py` parses the `claude -p --output-format
stream-json` event stream at `_parse_stream_json_output` (:361-437) and
**discards every cost/usage field**. Verified by census: there is NO
`total_cost_usd`, `usage`, or `modelUsage` reference anywhere in the module.
`claude_dispatch`'s signature is at :571-578; argv build :676-705.

196-R1 (VERIFIED by spike, T2 `nexus_rdr/196-research-1`) established exactly
what the result event carries:

```
total_cost_usd, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, num_turns,
usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens,
       cache_read_input_tokens},
modelUsage.{<model-id>: {inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens,
                         cacheCreationInputTokens, costUSD, canonicalModel}}
```

`modelUsage` is keyed PER MODEL, which is what makes a bundled multi-turn
dispatch attributable — this matters directly for `.p1b`'s bundle records.
Assistant events additionally carry `message.model` and per-turn `usage`.

NOMA §5.2's point holds here: monetary cost is almost analytic (tokens x
published price) and nexus is throwing the tokens away.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: decide the return shape. The RDR proposes
   `DispatchUsage = {model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, elapsed_ms}`
   and marks the field names **Assumed — verify against the fixture**. Verify
   them; if 196-R1's names differ from the RDR's illustrative sketch, the
   FIXTURE wins and the RDR text gets a correction note.
2. **TDD, red first.** Extend `tests/test_operator_dispatch.py` with a test
   that parses `tests/fixtures/claude_dispatch_stream_json_sample.ndjson` and
   asserts a populated `DispatchUsage` — cost > 0, both token counts > 0, a
   non-empty model id. It must fail on the pre-change tree.
3. Add a **non-vacuity assert on the fixture itself**: a test that the fixture's
   result event actually CONTAINS `total_cost_usd` and `usage`. Without it, a
   future fixture regeneration that drops the fields turns the whole telemetry
   arc into silent zeros and every downstream test still passes.
4. Parse defensively per the RDR's risk register: when a field is absent
   (older/newer CLI), record `None` + a structlog warning — **never 0.0**.
   0.0 is indistinguishable from "free" and is exactly the bug this arc exists
   to fix. Add a test for the absent-field path using a doctored fixture copy.
5. Return usage alongside the parsed JSON without changing `claude_dispatch`'s
   existing return contract for callers that ignore it. 18 call sites across 4
   modules go through this function — run
   `mcp__plugin_sn_serena__jet_brains_find_referencing_symbols` on
   `claude_dispatch` before changing the signature.
6. Do NOT add `--model` here. That is `.p2b`. Keeping the two changes in
   separate commits is what makes the Phase 2 A/B attributable.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] Red-first test shown failing pre-change (paste), passing after.
- [ ] Fixture non-vacuity test exists and FAILS when the cost fields are
      stripped from a copy of the fixture (demonstrate this, do not assert it).
- [ ] Absent-field path yields `None` + a warning, asserted by a test.
      `grep` shows no `cost_usd = 0.0` fallback introduced by this bead.
- [ ] A live (integration-marked) dispatch records a real non-zero cost — the
      fixture alone does not prove the parser sees production shapes.
- [ ] All 18 existing `claude_dispatch` call sites still pass:
      `uv run pytest -n auto` green.

## Depends

`.r4` (error classes disposed) — measuring a pipeline with unresolved
silent-failure classes mixes cost-of-working with cost-of-broken.
notes: Commit 60d119e66. Reviews T2 nexus/review-nexus-nyry9.7 [23017]; dev notes nexus/nyry9.7-dev-notes-2026-08-20. Load-flake reds filed nexus-86xx6.
close_reason: DispatchUsage/ModelUsage + opt-in usage_sink on claude_dispatch; canonicalModel recorded (R3); None never 0.0; fixture non-vacuity demonstrated; RDR correction block added (duration_ms not elapsed_ms). 106 passed in test_operator_dispatch.py; full suite green on quiescent tree modulo load-flake. Commit on develop.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## AUDIT FOLD, critical-path head (nx_plan_audit 2026-08-20)

The `.r4` (nexus-nyry9.4) dependency has been **REMOVED** from this bead. It was avoidable serialization at the head of the arc's critical path.

Reasoning: `.r4`'s value is that the telemetry is not measuring a knowingly-broken pipeline — and that bites at READ time, not at capture time. Capturing usage from the dispatch envelope is correct regardless of whether four historical error classes have been dispositioned. `.p1e` (nexus-nyry9.11) already depends on `.r4`, which is the right place: nothing is interpreted before then.

**Net effect: this bead is now a ROOT and can start immediately, in parallel with all five residuals.** The guarantee is unchanged — no measurement is read or published before `.r4` closes.

title: RDR-196 .r5 (residual): prove or delete every _nx_answer_classify_plan bucket — the single_query fast path was unreachable and retrieval_only is unproven
description:
RDR-196 arc, inherited residual **5 of 5** from the CLOSED bead nexus-h33x8.6
(follow-on defect #3 in T2 [22886]).

## The defect

`_nx_answer_classify_plan` (`src/nexus/mcp/core.py:5708-5734`) returns
`"single_query"` only for a plan with exactly ONE step whose tool is `query`.
That branch calls `query()` directly with NO `claude -p` — `query()` measures
mean ~2.1s, which is the documented sub-second-class fast path.

h33x8.6 enumerated the step shape of all 21 plans in the library: **not one
qualifies.** Every plan ends in an operator. So the advertised fast path was
dead code in practice, and every successful nx_answer call paid the ~11s
`claude -p` floor. Seed retrieval-only plans shipped since
(`conexus/plans/builtin/document-discovery.yml`,
`conexus/plans/builtin/corpus-coverage-check.yml`) were meant to make it
reachable. **Whether they actually do is unverified**, and the sibling
`retrieval_only` classify bucket has not been shown to route anything either.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: state what "reachable" means as a test, not as
   a code reading.
2. Read `_nx_answer_classify_plan` (core.py:5708-5734) and enumerate every
   bucket it can return and the branch each one routes to.
3. For EACH bucket, produce a **live routing test**: an `nx_answer` call whose
   matched plan lands in that bucket and whose execution provably takes that
   branch (assert on a branch-distinguishing observable — e.g. zero `claude -p`
   dispatches for `single_query` — not on wall-clock, which is not a proof).
4. Any bucket for which no such test can be written is DEAD. Delete it. The
   dead-code disposition is delete, not preserve (standing directive: no
   preservation campaigns).
5. Verify the two shipped builtin YAML plans actually classify into the fast
   bucket. If they do not, either fix the plans or record that the fast path
   remains unreachable — do NOT close this bead on the plans' mere existence.
6. Correct the latency figures in the `nx_answer` docstring if `.p1e` has not
   already: `core.py`'s advertised distribution was measured 45x optimistic at
   the fast end (0.7% under 5s, not 32%), because it counted degenerate
   zero-step error rows as successes.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] A test exists per surviving classify bucket, asserting the branch via a
      dispatch-count or equivalent structural observable. Wall-clock assertions
      do not count.
- [ ] `single_query` has a PASSING live test driven by one of the two shipped
      builtin plans, or this bead's close reason states in one line that the
      fast path is still unreachable and why.
- [ ] Every bucket with no test is DELETED from `_nx_answer_classify_plan` in
      this bead's diff; `grep` for its literal returns nothing in `src/`.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -n auto` green.

## Execution notes

- SPAWN a `conexus:developer` subagent; SPAWN `Explore` for the
  classify-bucket call-site census in parallel.
- This bead is cheap and high-visibility; it is a good first `.r*` to run
  alongside `.p1a`.
notes: Commit 262c452ef (shared with .4). Reviews [23030] [23033] [23045]. Silent $var literal pass-through filed as nexus-pucte.
close_reason: Buckets: single_query PROVEN live from a real plan_match on document-discovery.yml (and found broken: it queried the literal $question; fixed via the shared binding helper); needs_operators live; retrieval_only DELETED (0/17 builtins, 0 grown plans, only a hand-built test) so every plan_run gets the budget deadline. 241 passed. Commit on develop.

title: RDR-196 .r4 (residual): dispose of the four live nx_answer_runs error classes (empty tool name, missing dispatch_router, qwen HTTP, no-stdin) before Phase 1 measures the pipeline
description:
RDR-196 arc, inherited residual **4 of 5** from the CLOSED bead nexus-h33x8.6
(follow-on defect #5 in T2 [22886]).

## The defect — four live error classes in production telemetry

`nx_answer_runs` carries real failure rows, on the live store, unexplained:

| error text | occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown tool ''` | 4 |
| `No module named 'nexus.operators.dispatch_router'` | 2 |
| `qwen_dispatch HTTP error: All connection attempts failed` | 3 |
| `claude -p exited 1: Warning: no stdin data received in 3s` | 1 |

The first two are **silent-failure class**: an empty tool name and an
ImportError for a module that does not exist mean a plan step was dispatched
against something the runner could not name or load, and the run recorded a
failure rather than failing loud at the point of breakage.

## Why this gates Phase 1

Phase 1 (`.p1a`-`.p1f`) makes nx_answer's cost and latency observable, and the
whole arc is then judged against that telemetry. Measuring a pipeline whose
known breakages are unresolved produces numbers that silently mix "this is
what it costs" with "this is what it costs when it is broken". Also relevant:
39 of 181 historical rows are DEGENERATE (step_count=0), and it was exactly
that population that produced the 45x-wrong "32% under 5s" docstring figure.
Phase 1's read surface (`.p1e`) must not repeat that mistake, which means the
error classes have to be classified first.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: for each of the four classes, state the
   hypothesis and the cheapest disconfirming evidence.
2. For EACH class, produce one of exactly two dispositions:
   - **LIVE** — reproduce it, fix it, TDD red-first, with the regression test
     named in this bead's close reason; or
   - **DEAD** — prove the code path no longer exists on develop (cite the
     commit that removed it and the grep that returns nothing), and record the
     row as historical.
   "Probably dead" is not a disposition.
3. Specifically for `nexus.operators.dispatch_router`: `grep -rn
   dispatch_router src/ tests/ conexus/` and settle whether any live caller
   still references it.
4. Specifically for `unknown tool ''`: find where a step's tool name can be
   empty in `src/nexus/plans/runner.py` and make that condition fail loud at

title: RDR-196 .r2 (residual): budget_seconds does not cover the inline-planner phase — 40% of a measured run ran outside the caller's budget
description:
RDR-196 arc, inherited residual **2 of 5** from the CLOSED bead nexus-h33x8.6.

## The defect

`budget_seconds` shipped at dab75b819 with a two-shape exhaustion marker
(structured field `budget_exhausted_at_step`, set at `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:6467`
and `:6896`; leading text line emitted at `core.py:6814-6816`). The budget clock
does **not** cover the inline-planner phase. On the measured 2026-08-19 run
(row 382) the inline planner was **29.8s of a 74.3s run — 40.1%** — and none of
it was charged against the caller's budget. A caller asking for
`budget_seconds=30` can therefore burn 30s of planner and then start spending its
budget, returning at ~60s+ with no marker fired.

This is a hole in the SHIPPED time budget, and it is a PRECONDITION for
RDR-196 Phase 3: the USD budget (`.p3c`) must charge the inline planner's
dispatch cost, and it must not be built on top of an accounting boundary that
is already known-wrong on the time axis.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first: decide whether the budget clock starts at
   `nx_answer` entry or at plan-execution entry, and what the caller's
   `budget_seconds` is a promise ABOUT. State the chosen contract in words
   before touching code.
2. **TDD, red first.** Write a test that pins the contract: an `nx_answer` call
   whose plan-match MISSES (forcing the inline planner) with a
   `budget_seconds` smaller than the planner's own elapsed time must return
   the exhaustion marker rather than running the plan. It must fail before the
   fix. A test that passes on the pre-fix tree is not the test.
3. Move the budget clock's origin to `nx_answer` entry (or whatever the
   step-1 contract decides) and charge the plan-match gate + inline-planner
   phase against it.
4. The marker path is UNCHANGED — one emitter, both shapes. Do not add a
   second marker for "exhausted during planning"; the existing
   `budget_exhausted_at_step` carries a step index, so define and document
   what the index is when exhaustion happens BEFORE step 0 (a named sentinel,
   asserted in the test, not an incidental -1).

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] The red-first test exists and is shown failing on the pre-fix tree
      (paste the failure), then passing after.
- [ ] A test asserts the pre-step-0 exhaustion case emits BOTH shapes: the
      structured `budget_exhausted_at_step` field AND the leading text line.
      Asserting only the structured shape reproduces the silent-truncation
      class the RDR calls out.
- [ ] `grep -c` for the exhaustion leading-line literal in `src/` is still 1.
      A second literal means a second marker shape was introduced.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -n auto` green.

## Execution notes

- SPAWN a `conexus:developer` subagent. Do not grind this inline.
- Stacked review is covered by `.rg1`; do not push without it.

Critic's sentinel/step_index cross-ref recorded on nexus-nyry9.8; stale enrichment text corrected in T2 [23008].
close_reason: Budget clock already started at entry; the gap was no deadline check between Step 1 and plan_run. One pre-Step-2 check through the single emitter; sentinel _NX_ANSWER_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_PRE_PLAN=0; literal count 1; 131 passed in test_nx_answer.py; full suite green on quiescent tree modulo load-flake. Commit on develop.

title: Cost-aware nx_answer arc (RDR-196): per-step cost/quality telemetry, per-operator model routing, cost-ranked plan choice
description:
ARC PARENT for RDR-196 (accepted 2026-08-20, gate PASSED T2 [22908]).
RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-196-cost-aware-nx-answer.md
Plan of record: T2 nexus/plan-rdr196-execution-2026-08-20

## What this arc closes

NOMA (Kaoudi & Giurgiu, arXiv 2512.11001; catalog 1.14.51) frames multi-agent
pipelines as a query-optimization problem. nx_answer is the paper's expensive
baseline on every axis except the plan library: one model for every operator, no
per-step cost/latency/quality record, `cost_usd = 0.0` written unconditionally,
`budget_usd` documented as "reserved for future enforcement", and plan_match
ranking on confidence alone.

Five gaps (RDR § Enumerated gaps):
- Gap 1 no per-step cost/latency/model record -> Phase 1
- Gap 2 one model for every operator          -> Phase 2
- Gap 3 cost-blind plan choice, unenforced budget -> Phase 3
- Gap 4 tool-free dispatch loads the whole MCP set -> Phase 0 (LANDED f1ae257d0)
- Gap 5 SQL-vs-LLM engine choice by keyword heuristic, unrecorded -> Phase 1 (recorded)

## Measured baseline this arc is judged against

nexus-h33x8.6 / T2 nexus/nx-answer-capability-analysis-2026-08-19 [22886]:
n=142 executed runs, p50 80.1s, p95 217.1s, p99 316.7s; 0.7% under 5s; operators
70.7% of step time; ~11s irreducible claude -p floor per dispatch; plan-miss tax
~53s at p50. 196-R2 cost spread on one trivial dispatch: default+MCP $1.84 /
strict-empty $0.91 / sonnet $0.34 / haiku $0.07 (~13x tier spread).

## Structure (id-prefix children, as nexus-tk070.pN / nexus-cefa1.N)

- .r1-.r5  inherited residuals from the CLOSED nexus-h33x8.6 (Phase 1 inputs)
- .p1a-.p1f  Phase 1 Measure, incl. the PAIRED ENGINE RELEASE (.p1f)
- .p2a-.p2d  Phase 2 Per-operator model routing, gated on the quality proxy
- .p3a-.p3c  Phase 3 Cost-ranked plan choice + budget
- .p4        Phase 4 CONDITIONAL escalate loop (opens only on a Phase 2 negative)
- .rg1/.rg2/.rg3  stacked reviews at phase boundaries
- .gate      arc-end phase-review-gate

## Fences (RDR § Approach "Out of scope" — do not silently re-enter)

- generative pipeline synthesis (NOMA 5.1)
- continuous Bayesian refinement (NOMA 5.3)
- time/price arbitrage (NOMA 6)
- ANY change to plan-matching semantics -- RDR-100 owns that. .r1 and .r3 are
  DIAGNOSIS-AND-REFERRAL ONLY for exactly this reason.
- any change to operator semantics
- getting below the ~11s claude -p floor (measured impossible on this substrate;
  RDR-196 does not attempt it)

## Delivery

ONE engine cut in the whole arc (.p1f, `nx_answer_steps` DDL) + paired client
release, deploy-first per the 7.13.0 choreography. Phases 2/3/4 are client-only
and ride ordinary releases.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## AUDIT-FOLD FINDING — Phase 0 (Gap 4) is NOT fully landed, contrary to the RDR text

Surfaced by nx_plan_audit F1 during planning, verified 2026-08-20.

RDR-196 § Approach Phase 0 is marked **LANDED (f1ae257d0)**. That commit added `--strict-mcp-config` + empty `--mcp-config` to `claude_dispatch`'s argv. But RDR-196 Gap 4 names FOUR consumers of the overhead: "Every nx_answer step, `nx enrich aspects` extraction, `nx_tidy` and the inline planner".

`src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py:1559` builds its own argv — `["claude", "-p", "--output-format", "json"]` — and never calls `claude_dispatch`. So `nx enrich aspects` still loads the user's entire MCP server set on every extraction, at the ~2x context/cost 196-R2 measured ($1.84 vs $0.91 per dispatch). It also still uses `--output-format json`, the buffering mode h33x8.6 proved makes partial-output capture structurally vacuous.

**Disposition**: owned by .p0b (nexus-nyry9.6), which now carries the scope decision (re-route through claude_dispatch vs parse in place) and the blast-radius note. **The RDR text needs a correction note** so 'Phase 0 LANDED' does not read as covering all four consumers — fold it in at .p0b's close or at the .gate cross-walk, whichever comes first. Flagged here rather than left in the plan prose.

title: Migrate capability_census + routing_log from JSONL files to T2 telemetry tables (PG via engine) — delete file rotation machinery after
description:
Sam directive 2026-08-20 (during the h33x8.3 rotation review): leverage PG instead of flat-file gymnastics. Both JSONL logs move to the T2 telemetry family, riding the NEXT engine cut (DDL through Liquibase — ALL-DDL rule; the cut already queued for taxonomy-013/catalog-033 is the natural vehicle).

PART 1 — capability_census table: one row per session (session_id, ts, per-capability counts, blindspot flag+reason as columns). Writer swap in src/nexus/_session_end_census.py: HTTP via the launcher's existing service path (tier-summary precedent, 2s timeout); service-down = JSONL fallback OR metered drop (decide at design time — the BLINDSPOT-when-unmeasurable semantics must survive either way). SQL retention per the expire_relevance_log pattern. Reader: extend nx census capability to read the table.
PART 2 — routing_events table: routing hooks (conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/_lib.py + sn/ twin) write best-effort with SHORT timeout (~250ms), fire-and-forget semantics, service-down = metered drop via the _check_t2_dropped_writes pattern — the hook's own exit code NEVER depends on the write (fail-open preserved). Hooks are standalone scripts: urllib-level client, no nexus imports. Engine route: POST /v1/telemetry/routing_events (+ batch?). Readers: routing_stats.py aggregate()/escape_events() become SQL (or read-through). NOTE: unlike census, routing writes happen on the permission hot path — measure the added latency before shipping; if the sync POST is felt, batch/spool locally and flush.
PART 3 — after both ship AND the plugin pin advances (hooks are Tier C): DELETE the file-rotation machinery (_rotate_log_if_oversized in all three files, the .1-reader merge in routing_stats), the JSONLs age out. The interim TOCTOU-fixed rotation (nexus-g3jw6 fix) protects files until then — it is NOT wasted work, it guards every install between now and the migration.

Constraints: DDL via Liquibase changesets in the engine; wire shape recorded in docs/wire-contract-pending.md if client half ships before engine half (ledger discipline); avoid the RDR-196 nx_answer_runs write-only mistake — every new table ships WITH a reader surface (S11 doctrine: a writer whose data no surface reads is accumulating cost, not evidence).

title: No structural guard stops a dev-checkout process from writing the PRODUCTION T2/plan library — only 'remember the pytest fixture' defends it (live-write incident 2026-08-19)
description: Evidence (nexus-h33x8.6 comments, critic [22900]): during a1 seed-plan work a developer subagent ran 'uv run python -c ...' importing nexus.plans/nexus.db.t2 OUTSIDE pytest's _pin_t2_substrate autouse fixture; the client auto-discovered the live engine and wrote 2 plan rows (ids 362, 363) into Sam's PRODUCTION plan library on this box (caught via plan_search, deleted via plan_delete). The critic confirmed there is no guard anywhere in the T2 client path against this class: any process in the dev checkout with the default config resolution reaches production. Design question, not a patch: e.g. (a) a dev-checkout marker (repo-local .nexus.yml / env) that makes the client REFUSE writes to an engine whose identity/tenant is the production one unless an explicit NX_ALLOW_PROD_WRITE=1 is set; (b) make the test fixture's pin the default for any process whose cwd is inside a git checkout of nexus; (c) tenant namespacing so dev processes land in a scratch tenant by default. Pick at the design level (no knob reflex); must not wedge Sam's real CLI use from this checkout (he runs the installed nx, not uv run). Related memory: 'NEVER invoke the live nx from a dev session'.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate repro (uv run python -c writing a plan row from the checkout with default config) is refused or redirected with a loud message; the pytest path unchanged; Sam's installed nx unaffected; decision + rationale recorded in T2.

title: nx index repo aborts the whole run (rc=1) on a single unextractable PDF fixture — run_file_loop FIRST_EXCEPTION semantics fail the finalization after 3159/3160 files succeeded
description: Observed 2026-08-19 during the RDR-195 MVV (T2 nexus/rdr-195-mvv-measurements [22899]): indexing laravel/framework (3160 files) through the dev engine, every code file was embedded and durably flushed page-by-page; the LAST file, tests/Integration/Mail/Fixtures/blank_document.pdf (a deliberately blank test fixture), made PyMuPDF raise 'produced empty output' and src/nexus/indexer_utils.py run_file_loop's FIRST_EXCEPTION wait semantics aborted the run's finalization with rc=1. A single unextractable fixture should not fail a repo index: log the file as skipped (loud, counted in the summary, non-zero 'skipped' count surfaced) and finish; reserve rc!=0 for failures that lose data. Distinct from the PDF-extraction QUALITY work in nexus-ov5tc (MinerU heading shredding etc.): this is fail-fast-vs-continue in the file loop. Repro: tests/e2e/rdr195-voyage-mvv.sh <laravel-framework-clone> (INDEX_RC=1 caveat line). Fix at the loop, with a test that one raising file among N leaves the other N-1 indexed and the run exiting 0 with the skip reported (RED first).

title: code_indexer builds context-prefixed embed_texts that the default service-mode path never embeds — engine embeds raw documents, discarding file/class/method context (candidate retrieval-quality regression since RDR-155 P4a)
description: Found in passing by the RDR-195 Phase 1 substantive critique (T2 nexus/substantive-critique-rdr195-phase1-610c27e2e-2026-08-19 [22887]), confirmed 2026-08-19 against develop: src/nexus/code_indexer.py:364-455 builds embed_texts = f'{prefix}\n{chunk text}' ('prefixed texts sent to Voyage AI; raw text stored') and :456-470 only consumes it on the ctx.embed_fn (local/injected) branch. On the DEFAULT service-mode path (_service_mode_stub(), RDR-152 Seam B, nexus-fsquc) embeddings=[[] ...] and HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks ships only documents; the engine (PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal, traced by the critic) embeds raw documents with no prefix. So since RDR-155 P4a the code__ collections' vectors carry NO file-path/class/method context that the prefixing was added to provide ('improved retrieval quality' comment :456). Either (a) the prefix was never load-bearing and the dead construction + comment should be deleted (cheap; measure first), or (b) retrieval quality regressed and the engine path needs an embed-text vs stored-text split (wire-contract change: upsert payload carries embed_text per chunk; catalog/T3 store raw). Decide with a measured recall comparison on a code__ corpus (prefix vs raw) before choosing; nothing to do blindly. Related: RDR-180/RDR-191 chunk identity is sha256(chunk_text) of the RAW text — an embed-text split must not alter chash. Evidence also: the Java engine has no title/metadata prefix on the Voyage request (critic trace).
acceptance_criteria: A measured recall comparison (prefixed vs raw embed text, same code__ corpus, same queries) recorded in T2; then either the dead embed_texts construction is deleted with its comment, or an RDR is opened for the embed-text/stored-text split. No silent choice.

Consequences: (a) apply_hybrid_scoring's min(1,30/chunk_count) file-size penalty finds no chunk_count and factors 1.0 for everything — CLI order is pure distance while the (now-fixed) MCP path penalizes, so end-to-end CLI/MCP parity fails on code__ corpora; (b) the nexus-dxly catalog pass at search_cmd.py:470 reaches the right function with nothing to key on — dead wiring; (c) _display_path never attaches, likely degrading --path scoping (search_cmd.py:393-399). The 7.11.0 parity test (tests/test_mcp_server.py:397) feeds identical fixture lists to both sides so it structurally cannot catch input-construction divergence — extend it or add a live-shaped test. One-arg fix candidate + regression test. Repro: nx search 'session lease resolution tier fallback' --corpus code__1-1__voyage-code-3__v1 -m 5 --json (strict distance order, doc_id None) vs MCP search same args (boost order). Same silent-failure class the 7.11.0 sweep was shipping fixes for.
close_reason: Fixed on develop 29f3c3299 (+ pin repair 4cc1bfa23): one guarded catalog reader hoisted and passed into search_cross_corpus, reused at both downstream sites; --max-file-chunks warns on catalog-unavailable instead of crashing. Proven live before/after on the production store: pre-fix doc_id None + distance order, post-fix doc_id/chunk_count/_display_path attached + boost order matching MCP. Stacked-reviewed (both clean, findings applied: stderr warn, CHANGELOG entry covering all four repaired behaviors, called-once reader pin, warn test). Full suite 13290 passed.

title: Sweep monkeypatch.setattr('nexus.config.nexus_config_dir', ...) out of tests — it leaks into modules first-imported under the patch
description:
Production evidence: v7.11.0 release PR #1467, CI shard 3 (both 3.12 and 3.13) — tests/test_false_clean_diagnostics_service_mode.py:400 patched nexus.config.nexus_config_dir with a lambda; the health run it triggers first-imports nexus.gc_purge_marker (deferred import at nexus/health.py:4596), whose module-level 'from nexus.config import nexus_config_dir' captured the lambda BY VALUE (sys.modules caching makes the binding permanent). Monkeypatch teardown restored nexus.config but not that binding, so every later purge-marker read/write in the serial process resolved to the leaked tmp dir — broke 3 TestGcPurgeMarker tests order-dependently. That site is fixed (setenv) on the release branch.

CORRECTED INVENTORY (substantive-critic verification, T2 [22866] — the original filing undercounted 9 sites/3 files): 29 remaining setattr sites across 7 files — test_credential_persistence_gui_spawn.py x4, test_doctor_cmd.py x1, test_git_hooks.py x2, test_health_index_log.py x1, test_health.py x8, test_mineru_config_drift.py x9, test_upgrade_finish.py x4.

PRIORITY: test_doctor_cmd.py:33 is an AUTOUSE fixture covering all 62 tests in the file, several of which run bare 'nx doctor' via CliRunner — the identical run_health_checks() -> gc_purge_marker chain that leaked. The other 8 originally-tracked sites verified safe (narrow single-check paths, function-local imports immune to by-value capture); the 20 newly-found sites are unassessed.

SOURCE-SIDE (root-cause-complete, cheaper than converting 28 test sites): (a) src/nexus/aspect_worker.py:72 carries the identical module-level 'from nexus.config import nexus_config_dir' vulnerability, reached only via deferred imports (hook_registry.py, indexer.py, aspect_worker_daemon.py, commands/aspects.py) — currently untracked and unfixed; (b) gc_purge_marker.py's module-level import remains exposed beyond the one now-fixed trigger. Convert both to late-binding (import nexus.config; config.nexus_config_dir()).

GUARD: a lint tripwire banning monkeypatch.setattr on nexus.config.nexus_config_dir in tests/ — the env var IS the designed override, read at call time.
close_reason: Superseded: delivered by nexus-78blw (48 sites converted, 7 exempt, ratchet lint).

title: test_ndcg_drift_gate raw-layer leg had a silent env-var redirection bug — likely never produced a real signal
description:
Found + fixed while building nexus-j46lz's boost-layer leg. tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py's seeded_client fixture pins NX_SERVICE_URL/TOKEN via raw os.environ[...]=... at MODULE-fixture-setup time (once, before any test in the module runs). The repo-wide autouse _pin_t2_substrate (tests/conftest.py, function-scoped) then overwrites those same env vars before every test BODY runs, pointing them at the STANDARD shared T2 substrate instead. HttpVectorClient's module-level HTTP helpers (count/list_collections/search — see http_vector_client.py's _resolve_endpoint(), called fresh on every request, unlike HttpTaxonomyStore's RefreshableHttpStoreMixin which pins at construction) therefore silently talk to a DIFFERENT, empty substrate during the actual test body — zero errors, just zero rows back.

Practical effect: test_ndcg_drift_gate (nexus-9kq3h, 'built but never armed, no baseline pinned') would have returned mean_ndcg_at_3=0.0 if anyone had pinned its baseline before this was found — confirmed empirically (I nearly did this myself with NX_NDCG_PIN=1, caught it, deleted the spurious ndcg_baseline.json before committing).

FIXED for the NEW boost-layer leg via a non-autouse _service_env(java_service, monkeypatch) fixture (same pattern as tests/db/test_http_combined_query_integration.py's vec_client) — non-autouse fixtures resolve after autouse ones of the same scope, so its monkeypatch.setenv wins. test_ndcg_drift_gate (the ORIGINAL, pre-existing gate) now ALSO requires this fixture and is presumably fixed too, but its own baseline is still unpinned (out of scope for nexus-j46lz — pinning it is a distinct decision).

Follow-up ask: someone should now run NX_NDCG_PIN=1 uv run pytest tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py::test_ndcg_drift_gate -m integration to pin a REAL (non-zero) baseline for nexus-9kq3h, now that the fixture bug is fixed, and reconsider whether nexus-9kq3h should be resumed/wired into CI.

tests/test_query_descendants_seed_defects.py's _FakeCatalogSpy) -- never
against a real ActiveCatalog, and never with a real (or even fake-but-
service-shaped) T3 in the same test.

was never covered even before), but the deletion removed the ONLY test that

title: Redirect operator glued to a real refspec token defeats push-to-main and release-branch resolution
description:
Found during code-review-expert review of nexus-cr4lp F1 (T2 nexus/guard-evidence-cluster-root-cause-2026-08-18).

_strip_shell_redirections() in conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py
only strips a redirection token when the operator is at the START of its own shlex token (bare
`>`/`2>&1`/etc., or attached-with-operator-FIRST like `2>&1`, `&>file`). It does NOT handle a
redirection operator glued to the END of a real argument with no separating whitespace, e.g.
`git push origin main>foo` -- in REAL bash this pushes to branch "main" with stdout redirected to
a file named "foo", but shlex.split() (used throughout this file, pre-existing limitation) tokenizes
"main>foo" as ONE opaque token that does not match "main" in _PROTECTED.

Verified live (this checkout's own hook file, not a hypothetical):
  git push origin main            -> DENY (correct, nexus-vduer)
  git push origin main>foo 2>&1   -> ALLOW (guard defeated)
run from a checkout tracking origin/main, nexus-scoped repo.

Pre-existing gap, NOT introduced or worsened by cr4lp (pre-fix behavior was equally defeated).
F1's docstring claim "closes LEG A and B1" is accurate for those two specific incident shapes but
the closure is incomplete for this adjacent shape. Affects both _targets_protected (push-to-main,
rule 2) and _push_destination_branches (release-branch exemption resolution, rule 3's helper) since
both call the same _strip_shell_redirections.

Recommend: extend _strip_shell_redirections (or add a companion pass) to also split a token on an
embedded redirection operator not at position 0, e.g. "word>rest" -> keep "word", drop the rest --
or move push-destination resolution to a stricter shell-aware tokenizer.

Not a ship-blocker for nexus-cr4lp/nexus-iwlq4 (pre-existing, not in stated F1-F5/B1-B4 scope).

description:

nexus-wixar added scripts/check_lint_leg_non_vacuity.py + a CI step that fails the `test-lint` job if pytest's own summary shows fewer than 400 executed (passed+failed) tests -- closing the specific mass-skip nexus-wixar found (test-lint's own corpus skipping to 0 via the T2-substrate graceful-skip path).

That fix is correctly SCOPED to test-lint (the bead's own title names only the lint leg) -- not a silent scope reduction. But it leaves the sharded `test` job (`pytest tests/ --splits 4 --group N`, 4-way matrix, the PR's primary required check) and the `pytest-gate` fan-in with NO equivalent protection: `pytest-gate` (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~L788) trusts `needs.test.result == "success"` directly, with no floor on how many tests any given shard actually EXECUTED. Not a ship-blocker for nexus-wixar -- that bead's acceptance bar is the lint leg specifically, met. Filed as the named residue per this repo's own "unfloored legs must be named, not left to attrit silently" convention.

title: looks_like_binary_content misclassifies exactly-8192-byte corrupt files as text (rqsh1 round-2 boundary bug)
design:
nexus-rqsh1 round-2 replaced the strict single-shot
sample.decode("utf-8") with an incremental decoder to fix a false-
positive on valid UTF-8 straddling the 8192-byte sniff-sample cut.
The final= flag is computed as `final = len(sample) < sample_bytes`,
which conflates "the read returned fewer bytes than requested (short
file, definitely EOF)" with "the read returned exactly sample_bytes
bytes" -- the latter is ambiguous: it could mean the file is LARGER
than 8192 bytes (a true truncated prefix, defer judgment -- correct)
OR the file is EXACTLY 8192 bytes (the sample IS the whole file, no
more bytes exist -- must decode strict).

`len(sample) < sample_bytes` is False in both of the exactly-8192-byte
sub-cases, so `final=False` is passed even when sample_bytes==8192 IS
the whole file. Empirically verified (substantive-critic round-2
verification, 2026-08-17): a deterministic 8192-byte file consisting
of 8191 ASCII bytes + a genuinely truncated/corrupt UTF-8 lead byte at
EOF (real corruption, not a sampling artifact -- there are no more
bytes) is classified `looks_like_binary_content() == False`
(misclassified as text).

This is not just a decode nuisance: for `nx index repo`'s
candidate_files/prose_files path, indexed_for_catalog registers every
prose_files entry BEFORE per-file indexing outcome is known (comment
at indexer.py ~4130: "determined by the file LIST not by indexing
OUTCOME"). A misclassified exactly-8192-byte corrupt file therefore
still gets a catalog Document registered, then
prose_indexer.index_prose_file's read_text() raises UnicodeDecodeError,
caught silently (debug log, returns 0 chunks) -- reproducing the exact
chunk_count=0 un-clearable phantom nexus-rqsh1 exists to eliminate, via
this one narrow boundary. Same mechanism applies to the
doc_indexer.index_markdown guard (same function, same boundary) for
`nx index md`/`nx index rdr` on an exactly-8192-byte corrupt .md file --
the guard would fail to raise UnchunkableContentError and registration
would proceed.

Trigger is narrow (file size must be EXACTLY 8192 bytes AND genuinely
corrupt at that exact byte), and untested -- round-2's own test suite
(tests/test_classifier.py::TestLooksLikeBinaryContent) only covers
files strictly larger than 8192 bytes (8264-byte fixtures) and does
not exercise the ==8192 case.

Fix: determine "is this sample the whole file" by comparing to actual
file size (os.stat before/after the read, or reading sample_bytes+1
and checking whether more than sample_bytes bytes came back) rather
than `len(sample) < sample_bytes`.

Context: nx (T1 scratch tags critique2,rqsh1,0vycz; round-1 critique
T1 3217f340; round-2 fix T1 d0124ea6)
close_reason: sample_bytes+1 over-read disambiguates truncation from EOF; all four boundary cells verified empirically by critic; commit 7733b48a9.

title: RUNFENCE: 4 indexing producers call _fence_begin with no paired _fence_fail — a failed upload strands index_state='indexing' forever
description:
Root cause behind nexus-tjf7l (14 docs stranded in index_state='indexing', 7.8.0 shakedown).

Four RUNFENCE producers stamp 'indexing' before upload and have NO failure arm, so a
permanently-failed upload leaves the doc at 'indexing' forever:
  - src/nexus/indexer.py:4409  _fence_begin_many (nx index repo HOT PATH, via
    ChunkBatcher.on_batch_begin -> _fire_flush_grain_begin)
  - src/nexus/indexer.py:2317  per-file PDF fallback
  - src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:280
  - src/nexus/code_indexer.py:511
src/nexus/indexer.py contains ZERO _fence_fail references.

Mechanism (chunk_batcher.py _flush_batch, ~L405-490): on_batch_begin stamps every file
'indexing'; self._flush raises; on_batch_complete is guarded by `if error is None:` and is
skipped; nothing calls fail_index_run. The end-of-run _batcher.failed_files block
(indexer.py ~L4873) logs index_batch_upload_failures and stops.

EVIDENCE (~/.config/nexus/logs/index-ART-8c2e74c0.log, one nx index repo run
2026-08-06 21:47-22:59 PT): 12x chunk_batch_flush_failed with
'POST /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks -> HTTP 504: Gateway Timeout', 12x
indexed_file_upload_failed, tail index_batch_upload_failures count=12. Those 12 ART files
are 12 of the 13 ART docs doctor reported stranded ~255h later. Run ended cleanly (no
interrupt). NOT the doctor's suggested causes (stuck run / rolling-deploy split).

PRECEDENT ALREADY IN TREE: nexus-cotmr closed exactly this for nx store put and MCP
store_put. src/nexus/commands/store.py:138-144 comment: 'stamp failed unconditionally so
the fence does not wedge at indexing with only the 6h doctor sweep as signal.' The four
INDEXING producers were left open.

FIX: client-side only. POST /v1/catalog/index-run/fail already exists
(http_catalog_client.py:938 / CatalogHandler.java:2321 / CatalogRepository.failIndexRun).
No engine change, no tag, no deploy.
  1. chunk_batcher.py: add on_batch_failed(collection, file_contexts, error) alongside
     on_batch_begin/on_batch_complete; fire in _flush_batch's error branch (never-raising,
     same contract). NOT on the bisect path.
  2. indexer.py: _fire_flush_grain_fail next to _fire_flush_grain_begin (~L4380); wire at
     ~L4569.
  3. indexer.py:2317, prose_indexer.py:280, code_indexer.py:511: try/except ->
     _fence_fail -> re-raise, mirroring commands/store.py:137-149.

SAFETY: 'failed' and 'indexing' are identical to the freshness three-way
(doc_indexer.py:436 - both 'definitely stale, no probe'), so a failed doc still always
re-indexes. Nothing gets skipped. _fence_fail already swallows everything incl.
TombstonedDocumentException.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (full reasoning in T1 scratch tag=tjf7l):
 - doctor --fix reset: -> 'failed' is a behavioural no-op; -> NULL/'complete' falls through
   to _manifest_is_fully_present (unconditionally True post-RDR-191 P6) so the doc reads
   FRESH and is SKIPPED - blesses the partial vectors the run log says are there. Silent
   under-work, against the no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness directive.
 - engine sweep: same target-state trap, plus the fence has no heartbeat column (catalog-020
   added state/hash/run_id/started_at only) so it cannot tell in-flight from dead; adding one
   re-introduces lock semantics - the explicit nexus-lcmbp non-goal.

TESTS: tests/db/test_vw594_runfence_coverage.py / tests/test_5xn3k_fence_ordering.py;
copy the shape of tests/test_cotmr_cli_store_fence.py. Non-vacuity: fail_index_run called
with the failing doc_ids when _flush raises, NOT called on the success path, begin-before-
upload / fail-after ordering, and no double-report for succeeding bisect halves.

Context: nx (T1 scratch tag=tjf7l)
close_reason: Four _fence_fail arms landed (commit 7733b48a9); failed uploads stamp 'failed', freshness semantics preserved, no double-report. 3-round stacked review clean.

description:
substantive-critic review of nexus-4ftd7 implementation (2026-08-16, T2 nexus/critique-8fvp2-4ftd7-2026-08-16).

mcp/core.py store_put now accepts agent/session and falls back to NX_AGENT env, then a distinct "mcp" marker (never "nexus-indexer", never empty) -- correct and well-tested for the EXPLICIT-agent and NX_AGENT-env cases (tests/test_mcp_store_put_attribution.py).

But: (1) NX_AGENT is not exported anywhere in the hook/dispatch infrastructure for Agent-tool in-process Task dispatches (grepped conexus/hooks/scripts/*.sh and *.py -- zero hits) -- per RDR-105, Agent-tool subagents share the parent's MCP server process entirely, so there is no per-subagent env to distinguish them short of each subagent explicitly passing agent= on the tool call. (2) The calling convention was updated for memory_put (T2) -- every agent's system prompt's CONTEXT_PROTOCOL section shows `memory_put(..., agent="<role>", ...)` -- but NOT for store_put (T3): the same prompts' T3 write example is `store_put(content=..., collection="knowledge", title=..., tags=...)` with no agent kwarg. Verified directly in this critic's own injected system prompt this session.

Net effect: until the store_put calling convention (agent/skill prompts, _shared/CONTEXT_PROTOCOL.md, orchestration skill) is updated to pass agent="<role>" the same way memory_put's was, two different subagents both writing via store_put with no explicit agent= will both land the same "mcp" marker and still fail search_engine._flag_contradictions's agent_a != agent_b precondition -- the constant-collision problem nexus-4ftd7 was filed to close is recreated one level up for the majority (anonymous) MCP-write population. The one test that drives the precondition end-to-end (test_two_mcp_writers_with_different_agents_satisfy_contradiction_precondition) only covers the explicit-agent case; no test documents or guards the anonymous-vs-anonymous residual gap.

Recommendation: (a) update store_put's usage convention everywhere memory_put's was updated (agent prompts, _shared/CONTEXT_PROTOCOL.md, skills that call store_put) to pass agent="<role>"; (b) add a regression test that asserts two unmarked store_put writes still collide on "mcp" -- documents the known boundary so it isn't mistaken for full coverage later.

Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-8fvp2-4ftd7-2026-08-16.
close_reason: Convention half shipped @ cb14e4fc5 (store_put agent= convention across all 10 agent files + CONTEXT_PROTOCOL + skills, mirroring memory_put). Env-wiring half is INFEASIBLE by architecture, not deferred: RDR-105's shared-MCP-process model means per-dispatch NX_AGENT export cannot reach in-process Agent-tool dispatches (rationale recorded in bead comment by the fix-round developer). Anonymous in-process writes carry the distinct 'mcp' marker; per-role attribution comes from the now-documented explicit agent= convention.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Fix round (developer, post-stacked-review): applied recommendation (a) - the
store_put calling convention now passes agent="<role>" everywhere memory_put's
convention does:
- all 10 agent .md files' Post-flight write-back block (store_put line)
- conexus/agents/_shared/CONTEXT_PROTOCOL.md Storage Tools section
- conexus/skills/nexus/SKILL.md + reference.md (added the missing agent/session
  param rows to the store_put reference table too - they weren't documented at
  all pre-fix)
- conexus/skills/catalog/SKILL.md's store_put example

Recommendation (b) - wiring the SubagentStart hook to export NX_AGENT for
in-process Agent-tool dispatches - is NOT achievable within the current
architecture, not merely unwired: per RDR-105 (docs/architecture.md, also in
this repo's CLAUDE.md), Agent-tool sub-agents run IN-PROCESS, sharing the
parent's single MCP server. A hook script (subagent-start.sh) runs as ITS OWN
separate OS process; anything it exports dies with that process and never
reaches the parent MCP server's env, which is what actually handles the
store_put tool call. There is no per-subagent process boundary to inject an
env var across for this dispatch path - only claude -p subprocesses (which DO
get their own process/env) could receive NX_AGENT this way, and those already
default to their own owned T1/T2 sessions per RDR-105.

Net: the calling-convention fix (a) is the correct and only available lever
for the in-process Agent-tool population; residual risk is exactly "an agent
that forgets to pass agent= explicitly still lands on the mcp marker" - a
prompt-discipline gap, not a wiring gap. Leaving this bead open per relay
protocol (no bead closes in this round) since the fix is a convention-doc
change, not something a test can fully enforce.

title: t2_prefix_scan.py: unbounded per-namespace HTTP fan-out, no cap/cache, untested beyond 2 namespaces
description:
substantive-critic review of nexus-8fvp2 implementation (2026-08-16, T2 nexus/critique-8fvp2-4ftd7-2026-08-16).

_build_output() in conexus/hooks/scripts/t2_prefix_scan.py issues one GET /v1/memory/all per namespace returned by GET /v1/memory/projects, and only stops once total rendered entries hits _HARD_CAP (15) -- a namespace with zero matching entries does not count toward the cap and the loop continues to the next namespace regardless. GET /v1/memory/projects itself is unbounded server-side too (MemoryRepository.getProjectsWithPrefix has no LIMIT -- verified in service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/MemoryRepository.java:445-467).

Worst case: a namespace-heavy, entry-sparse prefix triggers N sequential HTTP round trips (N = number of matching namespaces, unbounded), each individually up to the 3.0s default timeout under a slow-but-alive (not down) engine. No caching exists across invocations -- every SessionStart AND every SubagentStart independently re-runs the full scan, so a parallel agent-fleet dispatch multiplies the cost per spawned agent.

In THIS session's own live SubagentStart injection, only 1-2 namespaces were scanned before the cap hit (nexus / nexus_rdr) -- the happy-path cost is low today. But this is a structural, code-verified worst case, not disproven by one observation, and the test suite (tests/hooks/test_t2_prefix_scan.py) never exercises more than 2 namespaces so the fan-out behavior is unvalidated.

Recommendation: cap the number of namespaces the client will fetch entries for (e.g. namespaces[:5], already DESC-ordered by recency so this loses only the least-relevant namespaces) before entering the fetch loop, and/or add a short-TTL cache (in-process is insufficient since each hook invocation is a fresh subprocess -- would need a small on-disk cache file under NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR with a few-second TTL) shared across sibling SubagentStart invocations in the same session.

Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-8fvp2-4ftd7-2026-08-16.
close_reason: Shipped on develop @ cb14e4fc5. T2 injection repointed to engine HTTP (stdlib-only, client-matching credential precedence incl. config.yml, two-arm loud freshness assert, namespace isolation + cap + budget, AST no-sqlite lint with bypass-probe fixture); store_put actor attribution wired end-to-end with RF-10 test. Stacked review + delta re-review CONFIRMED-FIXED on all findings; 12835 -n auto green. Plugin-surface files ride PENDING_RELEASE.md until the next release ships (injection fix inert in installed sessions until then).

title: t2_prefix_scan._build_output: mid-scan failure on namespace N discards already-fetched output for namespaces 1..N-1
description:
code-review-expert finding on nexus-8fvp2 review (T2 [22743] implementation). conexus/hooks/scripts/t2_prefix_scan.py: main()'s try/except around _build_output(...) (lines 366-370) catches _Unreachable raised from ANY namespace's _get_entries call mid-loop (inside _build_output, lines 260-310) and discards the ENTIRE local 'lines' list built so far, printing only a bare WARNING. A transient failure/timeout on namespace N of several wipes out namespaces 1..N-1's already-successfully-fetched data too, not just namespace N's. This contradicts the design intent demonstrated by the (single-namespace) stale-arm test (test_stale_arm_warns_but_still_shows_entries: 'data is still surfaced, not dropped') — no multi-namespace-partial-failure test exists to catch this asymmetry. Also compounds a related latency concern: _get_namespaces has no cap (server-side MemoryRepository.getProjectsWithPrefix has no LIMIT clause) and _build_output's outer loop only checks the _HARD_CAP break before calling _get_entries for each namespace — namespaces returning zero entries don't count against the cap, so a project with many low/no-content namespace variants triggers one sequential HTTP round-trip per namespace, unbounded, each up to the 3s timeout. Fix: wrap the per-namespace _get_entries call in _build_output with its own try/except so one bad namespace degrades gracefully (skip + note) instead of vetoing the whole render; consider a namespace-count cap independent of _HARD_CAP.

title: t2_prefix_scan NO-SQLITE lint: from-sqlite3-import + non-literal db filename bypass regex
description:
code-review-expert finding on nexus-8fvp2 review (T2 [22743] implementation): tests/hooks/test_t2_prefix_scan.py::test_no_hook_script_reads_memory_db_or_sqlite (lines 466-491) uses two regexes — _MEMORY_DB_LITERAL_RE (matches only the exact literal "memory.db") and _SQLITE_IMPORT_RE (matches only 'import sqlite3', not 'from sqlite3 import X'). Concretely verified (probe script): a hook that does 'from sqlite3 import connect; connect("t2_local_cache.db")' passes this lint clean — it does NOT catch the reintroduction. This defeats the lint's stated purpose (guard the six-week silent-freeze regression class nexus-8fvp2 fixed). Fix: broaden _SQLITE_IMPORT_RE to an unqualified \bsqlite3\b module-name scan (catches 'import sqlite3', 'from sqlite3 import X', 'importlib.import_module("sqlite3")'), and/or broaden the db-literal regex to any '*.db' string literal, not just the exact 'memory.db' spelling.

title: nexus-cy9u7 CRITICAL-1 fix: upsert_chunks now self-retries, so db/reconcile.py's pre-existing _etl_batch_with_breaker(upsert_chunks) call nests 3 undocumented retry layers with un-audited worst-case time
design:
substantive-critique delta round (nexus-cy9u7 rate-brake, 2026-08-16 fix-pass-2). CRITICAL-1's fix wraps `HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks` at the client boundary with `_vector_with_retry` (http_vector_client.py:1539-1543) — correct per round-1's own recommendation ("wrap at the client boundary" over the duck-typed detection gap). But `upsert_chunks` already had a PRE-EXISTING retry layer underneath (`_request`'s own `_GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES` bounded backoff, http_vector_client.py:493,813-846 — 2s/5s/10s, 3 extra attempts, no brake integration, not counted in get_retry_stats()), and db/reconcile.py's verify-fill path (`_verify_fill_one`, L664-670, UNTOUCHED by this diff — confirmed via `git diff`/`git status`) ALREADY wraps `vector_client.upsert_chunks` in `_etl_batch_with_breaker` (retry.py:678-736: `_etl_with_retry` 3 attempts + circuit breaker up to 20 trips of 30s pause each).

Net effect: this fix silently changed what `_etl_batch_with_breaker(vector_client.upsert_chunks, ...)` in db/reconcile.py actually does, from a 2-layer retry (gateway + etl-breaker) to a 3-layer retry (gateway + vector + etl-breaker), each layer with its own attempt count and each now ALSO pausing on the shared brake. Demonstrated concretely by the fix's own test (tests/test_vector_retry.py::test_upsert_chunks_504_no_retry_after_escalating_default_real_server, L539-581): a single `upsert_chunks` call under sustained 504 burns through the gateway layer's 4 attempts BEFORE `_vector_with_retry`'s own retry loop even sees the failure once.

Worst-case wall-clock for ONE verify-fill batch (db/reconcile.py's live production path — reachable from health.py and migration/pg_read.py) under a sustained outage is the PRODUCT of all three layers' bounds, nowhere documented: gateway (up to 4 attempts, 17s fixed) x vector (up to 5-8 attempts, brake-floored up to 60-300s each) x etl (3 attempts) x breaker (up to 20 trips x 30s pause + reset). This can run to HOURS before the breaker's max_trips ceiling finally raises — not the "~2-4 min to ~35 min" worst-case range documented in docs/cli-reference.md L104, which only accounts for a single _vector_with_retry call in isolation.

Not Critical: it does terminate (breaker's max_trips=20 provides an eventual raise, no infinite hang; every write remains idempotent/safe to retry), and this is a maintenance/health-check path, not the hot bulk-index path the incident was about. But it is a real, un-audited behavioral change with zero disclosure anywhere the developer's own worst-case numbers are stated.

Recommendation: either (a) have verify-fill's call site pass an explicit lower max_attempts to _etl_batch_with_breaker/upsert_chunks to avoid the multiplicative blowup, or (b) document the nested-retry compounding explicitly (a "when this write path is itself wrapped by another retry layer, worst-case multiplies" caveat) in retry.py's module docstring, or (c) at minimum verify db/reconcile.py's verify-fill path is not reachable from any user-facing timeout-sensitive flow (confirm health.py callers tolerate multi-hour stalls, or add its own outer bound).
close_reason: Fixed in eb999845b: upsert_chunks retry=False at reconcile.py verify-fill; single retry owner; falsifiable composition tests (429 stimulus)

title: nexus-cy9u7 CRITICAL-2 fix: manifest-write connectivity errors now trip the shared Voyage-rate brake (retry.py:857-872), pausing unrelated T3 vector writes on a local catalog-engine blip unrelated to Voyage RPM
design:
substantive-critique delta round (nexus-cy9u7 rate-brake, 2026-08-16 fix-pass-2). retry.py `_manifest_write_with_retry` (L806-887): CRITICAL-2's "every retryable failure trips the brake" widening was applied uniformly to ALL THREE write wrappers, including manifest-write's plain CONNECTIVITY check (`_is_connectivity_error`, L765-803) — not just its rate-limit signal. Pre-fix rationale for coupling manifest writes into the SAME brake as T3 vector writes was explicitly "the manifest write lands on the same engine that embeds server-side, so it can be paced by the identical per-project rate limit" (L822-829) — that justification applies to a 429/503+Retry-After signal, NOT to a bare httpx.ConnectError/TimeoutError from a flaky LOCAL catalog-engine connection, which has nothing to do with Voyage's RPM budget.

Net effect: a transient local catalog-engine restart/blip during a bulk `nx index repo` run now pauses EVERY T3 vector writer in the process (via the shared RateLimitBrake) for the escalating-default duration (2s, doubling per consecutive trip, capped 60s) — even though the vector-write path itself saw no problem. This is undisclosed in both rate_brake.py's module docstring and docs/cli-reference.md's new paragraph, both of which frame the brake purely in terms of Voyage rate-limiting.

Not Critical (bounded, no livelock — brake always resolves; genuine 4xx still fails fast per test_400_status_error_still_raises_immediately), but a real undisclosed scope-creep from the CRITICAL-2 widening.

Recommendation: either (a) scope manifest-write's brake-tripping to ONLY its rate-limit signal (revert connectivity-triggered trips to a wrapper-local backoff, no shared-brake coupling), or (b) if the coupling is intentional (unify all engine-facing write paths under one pacing signal regardless of failure class), say so explicitly in both rate_brake.py's docstring and cli-reference.md's paragraph.

Evidence: retry.py L822-845 docstring, L855-872 trip call inside `if rate_limit_err is None and not is_connectivity: raise` guard (both classes retried+trip). Verified via test_manifest_write_retry.py::test_connect_error_also_trips_brake_with_escalating_default (passes, confirms the coupling is real and intentional-by-test, just undisclosed in prose).
close_reason: Documented-by-design in eb999845b: manifest connectivity-brake coupling kept; same-engine-process premise verified (shared service_endpoint resolver), disclosure scoped to local in rate_brake.py + cli-reference

title: nx index: bound bulk-index embed request rate under Voyage per-PROJECT RPM limit (4000 RPM voyage-context-3 shared by all workers); today only --concurrency file parallelism exists, no embed-rate cap
description:
From the 2026-08-15 incident (conexus-ddh0; engine half nexus-99r7y): a parallel bulk `nx index` exhausted the Voyage per-PROJECT 4000 RPM budget in seconds; the engine embeds server-side for manifest/write_many, retried 429s past the edge 30s bound, clients saw 5xx. The limit is per PROJECT, so every concurrent worker/session shares it.

Current state (verified develop 2026-08-15): the client has file-level parallelism (indexer_utils.py:1157 ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=concurrency)), a flush pool in chunk_batcher.py (flush_concurrency, ceiling meant to respect the per-collection write quota), and T3 per-collection write semaphores (db/t3.py:407, QUOTAS.MAX_CONCURRENT_WRITES=10). None of these bound EMBED requests per minute across the project; the only mitigation is an operator throttling by hand.

Decide with Hal: (a) client-side token bucket / max-in-flight cap sized to the project RPM (config `voyage_rpm_budget`, default conservative, shared across a run; note it cannot see OTHER concurrent sessions, so it is a per-process bound, honest about that), plus honour 429/Retry-After from the engine (which nexus-99r7y will start passing through) by pausing the run rather than failing files; or (b) declare "operator sizes the job" and document it as a HARD constraint in docs/cli-reference.md nx index (concurrency guidance in RPM terms) rather than leaving it implicit. Either way the answer wants documenting. Search keys: Voyage RPM, 429, Retry-After, chunk_batcher flush_concurrency, indexer_utils concurrency, conexus-ddh0, nexus-99r7y.

title: CceEmbedder 429 backoff not sized for sustained Voyage rate limiting: honour Retry-After / adaptive backoff so bulk manifest/write_many degrades to slow writes instead of edge-timeout 5xx
description:
Observed 2026-08-15 ~22:35-22:55Z on engine-service-v0.1.76 during a bulk nx index run (conexus-ddh0): POST /v1/catalog/manifest/write_many -> CceEmbedder -> Voyage HTTP 429 "exceeded your project Requests Per Minute (RPM) rate limit of 4,000 requests per minute for voyage-context-3" -> event=cce_retry attempt=1 status=429 delay_ms 273-451 (74 events) -> accumulated retries exceed the public edge 30s upstream bound -> 5xx to the client; some 429s outlived the retries and surfaced verbatim via catalog_handler_error op=/manifest/write_many. This was the BULK of the 5xx in that incident (the remaining 4 were nexus-0uuit, an unrelated PG deadlock). DB work per request was 10-25ms (register_many_timing); the engine was idle.

Why: the current CCE backoff (~300-450ms, few attempts) is tuned for an occasional 429, not a minutes-long project-wide ceiling. Under sustained limiting it burns its attempts inside the edge timeout and turns throttling into client-visible failures.

What (engine side): (a) honour the Retry-After header when Voyage sends one; (b) adaptive/longer backoff with jitter for consecutive 429s, bounded so a request either completes or fails fast with a 429/503 + Retry-After of its own well before the 30s edge bound (fail fast and honest beats timing out); (c) surface a metric/log for sustained-429 state. Client side (separate, on conexus-ddh0 / possibly an nx index bead): bound bulk-index concurrency under the per-PROJECT 4000 RPM limit shared by all workers. Test with a stub embedder returning 429 sequences on real engine wiring, not a mock of the retry loop.

Search keys: CceEmbedder, cce_retry, 429, Retry-After, voyage-context-3, write_manifest_many_swept, catalog_handler_error, edge 30s. Related: nexus-0uuit, conexus-ddh0.

title: RDR-194 P7: close-out — census-leg audit, fk_census ground truths extended, cloud-count-3 deploy verify, phase-review-gate, engine cut prep + paired client release
description:
RDR-194 **P7**, close-out. No changesets. Four distinct deliverables; none is
optional and none substitutes for another.

## 1. Census-leg audit, both directions

- **Retired legs are GONE**: `nx doctor --check-dangling-links` (P1) and
  `ChashCensus` leg C1 `dangling.topic_assignments` plus its `:195` "either era"
