title: RDR-191 P5: OWNS the unified chunks->catalog_collections collection FK — new changelog (FK add + new-id VALIDATE + violating-row test), per-dim drop-half moot
description:
**Raised by the Phase 4 scoping inventory (T2 `nexus/rdr-191-p4-scoping-inventory-2026-08-13` [22416], Parts 5.14 and 7.7). No bead currently owns it; the inventory suggested `nexus-o8dil.12`, and it is filed separately because the deliverable is a NEW changelog rather than an edit to `.12`'s create-table changeset.**

`fk-002` carries **three per-dim collection foreign keys**, one on each of `chunks_384 / _768 / _1024`, and `fk-002-validate.xml` carries `sqlCheck` preconditions naming each constraint with `expectedResult=1`.

## Why a new changelog, not an edit

Already-applied changesets are checksum-frozen. `catalog-013:200-206` states the house convention explicitly: recovery on a MARK_RAN or already-applied box is a NEW changeset id, never an in-place edit. So the three per-dim FKs must be dropped and the unified one added by a new changelog appended at the tail, after `fk-002-validate.xml`, the same ordering requirement `nexus-o8dil.13` lints for.

## Related vacuity, same family

`fk-002-7` through `fk-002-11` (and the `fk-003-7..11` mirror) go **permanently vacuous** for the unified table: their `sqlCheck` preconditions name constraints that will no longer exist, so they mark-ran or skip and verify nothing. This is the same shape as `catalog-013-2/-3`, which `nexus-o8dil.13` owns for the CHECK family. The FK family's equivalent is here.

**Correction to record, verified**: `catalog-013:209`'s `expectedResult="5"` is NOT a boot brick under a three-to-one collapse. `catalog-013-2` carries `<preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN">` and has no `runAlways` or `runOnChange`, so a count mismatch makes it mark-ran and skip. The residual risk is the mirror image: permanent vacuity, which a new-id VALIDATE changeset fixes. Do not re-file this as a brick.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A NEW changelog drops the three per-dim collection FKs and adds the unified equivalent on `nexus.chunks`. Appended after `fk-002-validate.xml`.
- [ ] A NEW-id VALIDATE changeset covers the unified FK, so the invariant is actually verified rather than inherited from preconditions that can no longer match. Same convention as `catalog-013:200-206`.
- [ ] A test proves the new VALIDATE changeset FAILS on a deliberately violating row. Demonstrate the failure; a precondition that can only pass is the defect this bead exists to avoid.
- [ ] Stale header prose in `fk-002` and `fk-002-validate.xml`, and the comments at `db.changelog-master.xml:89` and `:96`, are corrected in the same diff.
- [ ] Coordinated with `nexus-o8dil.12` so the unified table exists before this runs, and with `nexus-o8dil.13` so both changelogs land in the correct tail order.

## Context

- Inventory: T2 `nexus/rdr-191-p4-scoping-inventory-2026-08-13` [22416], Parts 5.13, 5.14, 7.6, 7.7.
- Plan: T2 `nexus/plan-rdr-191-phases-2-7` [22217].
- RDR: `docs/rdr/rdr-191-unify-chunk-tables-enable-manifest-fk.md`.

## Standing constraints

- ALL DDL through Liquibase. NEVER DDL in Python.
- TDD: test file before implementation.
- STACKED REVIEW at the phase boundary: `code-review-expert` AND `substantive-critic`. Both run.

title: danglingManifestCountDsl is chash-only (no tenant, no collection) yet enforced as a hard abort gate in RekeyOps and StagingPromoteOps — the 2.2x-undercount shape as an enforcement instrument
description:
Long-known as a census defect (T2 [22298] Finding 3), re-verified UNFIXED at HEAD by the 2026-08-13 census re-verification (T2 [22383]): ChashSqlIdioms.java:402-413 keys three NOT EXISTS on CHASH alone — no tenant_id, no collection predicate — and is enforced as a throwing abort gate at RekeyOps.java:681 and StagingPromoteOps.java:1125. Same shape that understated the 2026-08-11 live census 2.2x (2,951 vs 6,501).

NOT a producer (the real defenses on those paths are the alias-map repoint and resolvable-only promote; verdict in [22383] cell 4). It is a WEAK DETECTOR guarding precision-critical paths: a dangling row whose chash exists under a different tenant/collection reads as clean and the rekey/promote proceeds.

FIX: re-key the counter to (tenant_id, collection, chash) — the same key catalog-025 normalized the manifest to. Java-only. NOTE the prior-record correction in [22383]: nexus-kzso5's 'census re-key' was the CLIENT-side nx catalog verify census (commands/catalog_cmds/integrity.py), NOT this counter; do not assume it was already done.

title: sweepChunks* live-owner guard keeps DELETED_AT.isNull() while mmkqe/wnpet made their surfaces unconditional — Tier-1 protection is not uniformly implemented across independent-deleter surfaces
description:
Found by the GATE-2 census re-verification (T2 [22383], deep-analyst 2026-08-13, develop @ 2b792358a). Class-(b) only — harmless for GATE-2's definition-(a) criterion, but a two-tier-contract inconsistency.

CatalogRepository.java:4877 (sweepChunks family's own live-owner guard, :4870-4878) still filters DELETED_AT.isNull(), i.e. a TOMBSTONED owner's manifest row does NOT protect its chunk from the sweep. Per the definition of record's amendment (T2 [22364] two-tier protection), the sweep is an INDEPENDENT-DELETER surface, the same class as PgVectorRepository.delete (nexus-mmkqe) and gc_expire_quarantine (nexus-wnpet), both of which were made UNCONDITIONAL (Tier 1: tombstoned owner still protects). Tier-1 rule is therefore not uniformly implemented.

Mitigating direction-of-record note: the sweep runs AFTER the manifest DELETE commits (manifest-first at CatalogRepository.java:4080), so on the primary path the rows are already gone and the guard is a backstop for OTHER documents' references — which is exactly where the tombstone-blindness matters (a tombstoned OTHER document's reference does not protect).

FIX: drop the DELETED_AT.isNull() term from the sweep guard, matching mmkqe's shape. Java-only, no DDL. Add/extend a unit test in the PgVectorRepositoryDeleteAntiJoinTest / CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest family pinning tombstoned-referrer protection on the sweep path. Do NOT reconcile the other direction (purge_trash/strandedChunkCount stay grace-window-scoped, Tier 2 — see [22364]).

title: gc_quarantine_orphans guard SELECT and DELETE are two READ COMMITTED statements with NO lock — write-skew can quarantine a chunk a concurrent manifest write just started referencing
description:
Found by the GATE-2 census re-verification (T2 [22383] nexus/rdr-191-gate2-census-cells-post-wave2-2026-08-13, deep-analyst 2026-08-13, develop @ 2b792358a). THE ONE OPEN AXIS blocking a clean GATE-2 item-2 close.

MECHANISM (inferred from statement structure; verified absence of locks): catalog-024's gc_quarantine_orphans runs its manifest-reference guard SELECT (catalog-024:119-128) and its DELETE/move (:159-163) as two separate READ COMMITTED statements. Grep-verified ZERO pg_advisory locks / LOCK TABLE / FOR UPDATE across catalog-024 and catalog-027, and the Java caller adds none (PgVectorRepository.java:2349-2352). A manifest write that lands between the two statements references a chunk the DELETE then removes — the same write-skew class runSweepTransaction closes with an EXCLUSIVE sweep gate (CatalogRepository.java:4661-4676).

NOT the c30ew NULL-collection class, NOT what catalog-027 fixed. Previously unrecorded.

FIX OPTIONS (either closes the cell): (a) concurrency test proving/refuting the window; (b) STRUCTURAL — take the same exclusive sweep gate runSweepTransaction uses, or collapse guard+delete into one DELETE ... RETURNING with the anti-join inline. Option (b) closes it with no test needed. ALL DDL through a new Liquibase changeset (catalog-028+ pattern); never edit shipped catalog-024.

Verdict context: gc_quarantine_orphans is NOT-A-PRODUCER serially; GENUINELY-UNDETERMINED concurrently. This bead is that residue.
close_reason: Fixed in 8b1a8dc88 (catalog-028): gc_quarantine_orphans takes the EXCLUSIVE half of the per-(tenant,collection) advisory sweep gate every manifest writer holds SHARED — both reviewers independently verified all 9 writer paths conflict, window CLOSED not narrowed. Inline NOT EXISTS guard, bounded acquisition (lock_timeout/statement_timeout mirroring acquireSweepGateExclusive, loud mutation-free failure on 55P03), two kill-controlled definition pins, FOURTH-DIM CHECKLIST + o8dil.41 inventory updated. DEPLOYS at the next engine cut (v0.1.75, batched per Hal 2026-08-13) — cloud runs the pre-fix function until then; the race is theoretical, never observed, and its worst case is recoverable quarantine.

title: rnqbw: shared-chunk control test never reaches _retract_manifest_rows_for_chash -- only re-validates the pre-existing ambiguity guard
design:
Found during targeted re-review of nexus-rnqbw (RDR-191 GATE-2 P0 fix).

tests/test_rnqbw_same_call_reap_ordering.py::
test_mcp_store_delete_still_protects_a_chunk_genuinely_shared_with_a_live_document
is documented as a "non-vacuity control" against the retraction fix
"degrading into blanket permission" -- but it constructs its shared-content
twin with content_type="knowledge" and no file_path (via ActiveCatalog.register
with no file_path passed), same as the original note.

resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash's candidate filter is
`entry.content_type == "knowledge" and not entry.file_path` -- both the note
and the twin satisfy it, so resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash finds 2
candidates for the shared chash and returns None (ambiguous) BEFORE
store_delete_catalog_cleanup ever calls _retract_manifest_rows_for_chash.
Traced and confirmed: the retraction helper's own per-document scoping logic
(operating only on entry's own manifest via reader.get_manifest(tumbler_str))
is never exercised by this test at all.

The test's assertions (chunk survives, no false "Deleted:", message mentions
"anti-join-protected") all pass via the PRE-EXISTING ambiguity guard, not via
retraction being correctly scoped. A hypothetical regression that made
_retract_manifest_rows_for_chash retract a chash's manifest row from EVERY
document referencing it (not just entry's own) would sail through this test
undetected, because the ambiguous-resolve short-circuit means retraction
code is never reached in this scenario.

Recommend: register the twin with a different content_type (e.g. "code") or
a non-empty file_path so it falls OUTSIDE resolve_knowledge_doc_for_chash's
candidate filter -- forcing an unambiguous resolve to the note, so
_retract_manifest_rows_for_chash actually runs -- then assert the twin's own
manifest row / chunk_count is untouched by the retraction (in addition to
the existing chunk-survival assertion, which the anti-join provides
independent of retraction scoping).

Reference: T2 nexus/rdr-191-dangling-definition-of-record [22364] amendment;
code-review-expert pass 2026-08-12/13.

title: rnqbw: _retract_manifest_rows_for_chash drops per-row collection, silently repoints surviving rows on a multi-collection manifest
design:
Found during targeted re-review of nexus-rnqbw (RDR-191 GATE-2 P0 fix).

src/nexus/catalog/store_hook.py::_retract_manifest_rows_for_chash builds
`remaining` rows from ManifestRow objects but drops r.collection, then calls
writer.write_manifest(tumbler_str, remaining, collection=entry.physical_collection)
-- a SINGLE collection value stamped on every remaining row.

CatalogRepository#writeManifestRows (service/.../CatalogRepository.java:4081)
deletes ALL manifest rows for docId (no collection filter) then inserts
`rows` all stamped with the one caller-supplied `collection`. So if a
document's manifest ever legitimately spans TWO collections (RDR-191 made
`collection` a PER-ROW field specifically to support this during rekey /
StagingPromoteOps-style migration), retracting one chash via this helper
would silently repoint every surviving row -- even ones that belonged to a
DIFFERENT collection -- to entry.physical_collection.

Currently unreachable in practice: the three live callers
(reap_catalog_manifest_for_chashes, store_delete_catalog_cleanup) only ever
resolve store_put/memory-promote-origin documents (content_type=="knowledge",
no file_path), which are always single-chunk/single-collection by
construction (single_chunk_manifest_metadata + store_put_manifest_direct).
So today `remaining` never has >0 rows with a foreign collection. But the
helper itself carries no assertion/guard enforcing that precondition, so a
future caller (or a future multi-chunk knowledge doc) would hit silent
collection corruption with no test coverage to catch it.

Recommend: either (a) raise loud if any row in `remaining` has
r.collection not in (None, entry.physical_collection) before calling
write_manifest, or (b) document the single-collection-manifest precondition
explicitly in the docstring and add an assertion.

Reference: T2 nexus/rdr-191-dangling-definition-of-record [22364] amendment;
code-review-expert pass 2026-08-12/13.

title: Collection rename does not re-home chash_remap's source_collection/target_collection -- ledger detaches from the renamed name (accepted per RF-186-1, nexus-4nll0)
description:
nexus-4nll0 resolved the design question of whether chash_remap belongs in CatalogRepository.COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES: EXCLUDED from both the re-home (rename) and emptiness (retired-name-revival) halves, per the standing raw-fact classification (RF-186-1: chash_remap is an append-only migration ledger, no verdict surface, audit outlives the collection it describes -- same class as gc_audit's audit-only nature, though NOT gc_audit's re-home treatment, since gc_audit's collection column is not inside its primary key and chash_remap's source_collection is: (tenant_id, source_collection, old_id)).

This is option (b) of nexus-4nll0's three options ("exclude it, accept that rename detaches the remap ledger (file the detach as its own bug)") -- filing that bug now, per that option's own explicit requirement.

CONSEQUENCE: after `nx catalog collection rename X Y` (CatalogRepository#renameCollectionTxn), chash_remap rows with source_collection=X or target_collection=Y remain stamped with the OLD name. RemapRepository's read paths (entriesForCollection / count / membership / clearLeg / sourceCollections), all keyed on SOURCE_COLLECTION, and nexus.remap_membership() will no longer find them under the renamed collection's current name -- the migration ledger silently detaches from a collection that gets renamed after a migration wrote facts about it.

WHY THIS IS ACCEPTED, NOT A DEFECT TO FIX THE SAME WAY: re-homing would rewrite a column inside chash_remap's PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, source_collection, old_id), which can collide 23505 if the target name already holds an entry with the same old_id, and the ledger is a PERMANENT historical record -- rewriting "what collection this migration fact was about" after the fact falsifies the audit trail rather than correcting it.

SCOPE FOR A FIX, IF ONE IS EVER WANTED: NOT a COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES entry (rejected above). Options: (a) leave as pure historical fact, document that a rename orphans old remap queries by name (operators must know the collection's rename history to find its remap facts) -- the do-nothing option; (b) add a name-history side table/view so remap queries can resolve renamed collections by chasing the rename chain; (c) surface the rename in chash_remap's own provenance field rather than rewriting source_collection/target_collection. No option has been chosen -- this bead is tracking scope, not implementation.

Verified: CatalogRepository.java's COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES javadoc (~line 6259-6264) and RemapRepository.java's RF-186-1 no-verdict-surface doc already establish the classification; tests/catalog/test_collection_scoped_tables_schema_parity.py's _DOCUMENTED_EXCLUSIONS carries the PK-collision + permanence reasoning for both chash_remap columns.

title: gc_audit is a write-less audit surface: catalog-018 built the table and both routes, nothing in src/ ever records to it
description:
Found read-only during the nexus-3rr3x / nexus-xehfx legacy-burndown diagnosis, 2026-08-12.

catalog-018-gc-audit.xml (nexus-jqvzk, Hal ruling 2026-07-30) created nexus.gc_audit
explicitly to answer 'what did the GC take on the 21st' — its own header says a
destructive verb whose only trace is its own stdout cannot answer that. The engine
side is complete: table + RLS + both indexes, CatalogRepository.recordGcAudit
(:7944-8000), and both routes wired in CatalogHandler:251-252
(POST /v1/catalog/gc_audit/record, GET /v1/catalog/gc_audit/list).

THE DEFECT: nothing calls the record route. grep across all of src/ for 'gc_audit',
'gcAudit', 'record_gc' finds ZERO client callers — the only hits in src/nexus are
health.py:2207 (a table-name list) and an engine_version.py comment. The audit
table has been deployed since engine-service-v0.1.59 (2026-07-30) and is, as far
as the client is concerned, permanently empty.

WHY IT MATTERS, concretely: during the 3rr3x investigation gc_audit was assumed on
both sides of the relay to be the evidence trail that could settle what happened
to the 2026-08-03 cohort of 11,156 tombstones. It cannot — there is nothing in it.
An audit surface that is believed to exist but records nothing is worse than none,
because investigations route through it and lose time.

SCOPE / what to decide:
1. Which operations SHOULD record? At minimum the destructive ones this table was
   built for: nx t3 gc, catalog purge-trash (both dry-run and execute — the header
   explicitly wants dry-run rows so an operator can diff the preview against the
   run), reconcile-stale's tombstone arms, collection delete, chunk quarantine/expire.
2. Note purge-trash is the sharpest case: nexus-5da44's age-blind chunk sweep will
   delete chunks for EVERY tombstoned doc on the first execute, and today that
   would leave no record of which chashes went.
3. Add a non-vacuity test — a lint or contract test asserting at least one client
   caller of the record route exists, so this cannot regress to write-less again.

Related: nexus-3rr3x (where this was found), nexus-5da44, nexus-jqvzk (origin).

title: nx catalog verify Class C census keys by doc physical_collection — ghost docs produce a phantom empty-collection entry and swallow the real collection's signal
description: src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/integrity.py (_census_lost_and_never_chunked / _class_c_unverifiable_rows, ~lines 717-772) keys client-side manifest-row totals by e.physical_collection, but the shipped RDR-191 contract (CatalogRepository.java ~3530-3547) deliberately decouples the manifest row's stamped collection from the doc's physical_collection. A ghost doc (physical_collection='') with manifest rows now yields a phantom {"collection":"","unverifiable_rows":N} entry in nx catalog verify --json and silently swallows the real collection's coverage signal. Diagnostics-correctness only (Class B damage detection is engine-side, unaffected). Zero test coverage of this path. Fix: key the census by the manifest row's own collection field; add a ghost-doc regression test. RELATED AUDIT (flagged, unverified, same proxy pattern): nx catalog collections / reconcile-stale GC sweeps may also use physical_collection as a proxy for manifest-row collection — audit while in there (manifest_heal.py already verified SAFE, it excludes ghosts). Found by substantive-critic round-3; full evidence T2 nexus/rdr-191-gate2-python-tail-critique-round3-2026-08-12 [22342].
acceptance_criteria: Census keyed by manifest row collection; ghost-doc regression test proves no phantom empty-collection entry and correct per-collection totals; GC-sweep proxy audit recorded (fix or explicit not-affected note).
close_reason: Landed 8c8185af2 with caveats: ghost-touched collections report INCOMPLETE (not full totals) until wire carries row collection (nexus-kzso5); Class B/C round trips not snapshot-consistent (pre-existing race, now visible not silent).

title: StagingPromoteOps: empty-physical_collection manifest skip has zero observability — add manifest_doc_no_collection counter + WARN
description: RDR-191 caller-supplied-collection design: StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant resolves manifest collection solely from the doc's physical_collection; a doc with empty physical_collection produces NO manifest row for its staged chunks. That outcome is currently silent — no counter, no WARN — unlike the sibling 'doc not registered' case which got both (manifest_doc_not_registered, same round). A ghost doc's staged chunks can sit stuck indefinitely with no signal. Add a manifest_doc_no_collection counter + WARN mirroring the not-registered pattern in StagingPromoteOps.java (~line 732 as of 2026-08-12 uncommitted tree). Found by substantive-critic round-2 (T2: nexus/critique-round2-nexus-j862l-test-reconciliation-2026-08-12 [22340]); recommended as a prerequisite to calling RDR-191 Phases 3-6 fully defended.
acceptance_criteria: Empty-physical_collection skip emits WARN + increments a counter; test pins both (non-vacuous: skip path exercised, counter asserted).
close_reason: Counter+WARN landed 7e558969e; 24/24 green; reviewers clean.

title: stop_failure_hook.py mints a new permanent bd-remember key per API failure — unbounded bd prime context pollution
description: conexus/hooks/scripts/stop_failure_hook.py:96 runs 'bd remember "stop-failure-<type>: <details> at <timestamp>"' on every StopFailure event. The embedded timestamp makes every summary a unique key, so the pool grows one permanent entry per API hiccup and bd prime injects all of them into every session's context. Found 2026-08-12: 32 of 36 bd memories were this class (mostly empty-bodied rate_limit/server_error stamps, June-August); all 32 forgotten same day. The hook's own docstring correctly avoids bd create to protect bd ready, but bd remember has the identical pollution problem one layer down. Fix direction: append to a log file (e.g. ~/.config/nexus/logs/stop-failures.log) or update a SINGLE fixed key via bd remember --key stop-failures (last-N or counter form) — never a per-event key. Update tests/hooks/test_stop_failure_hook.py to pin the no-new-key-per-event contract (non-vacuous: two invocations must not produce two keys).
acceptance_criteria: Two hook invocations with different timestamps produce at most one bd memory key (or zero, if log-file route); test pins it; existing behavior of not filing issues preserved.
close_reason: Closed

title: ci.yml's engine-service-build and write-seam gate are NOT required checks either, so their merge-blocking comments are false and cqquo's new guards harden advisory jobs — broader than nexus-hq9na
description:
ci.yml's engine-service-build and write-seam behavioural gate are NOT required checks either, so their comments claiming they block merge are false and every guard hardening them is advisory — broader than nexus-hq9na

## Verified against the live API, twice, by two independent readers

    gh api repos/Hellblazer/nexus/branches/develop/protection --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'
      -> ["pytest-gate"]
    gh api repos/Hellblazer/nexus/branches/main/protection    --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'
      -> ["pytest-gate"]

**"pytest-gate" is the ONLY required check on either branch.** Everything else in
`.github/workflows/**` is advisory at merge, whatever its comments say.

## What that makes false

`nexus-hq9na` (P2, 2026-07-31) already records this for `service-ci.yml`'s `changes`
job. This bead extends it, because at least two MORE sites carry the same false claim:

  - `ci.yml`'s `engine-service-build` — commented as if it gates merge.
  - `ci.yml`'s write-seam behavioural gate — same.
  - `service-ci.yml`'s comments about branch protection referencing its job NAME (the
    reason nobody may rename it) are, on the same evidence, describing a protection
    entry that does not exist.

The rename warning is still worth OBEYING — if these are ever made required, the names
matter, and the cost of obeying is zero. But it should say "must not drift BEFORE these
become required", not "is referenced by branch protection", because the latter is untrue
today and misleads every reader into thinking the job is load-bearing.

## Why this matters more than a stale comment

`nexus-cqquo`'s fix (2026-08-12) added fail-loud guards to 5 dorny consumer sites so a
malformed filter output can no longer silently skip an expensive job. Those guards are
CORRECT and should stay. But on this evidence they currently harden ADVISORY jobs: a
guard that fails a job nothing requires stops nothing at merge. The work is not wasted —
it is a precondition for making these required — but the protective value people will
assume it has does not exist yet.

So this is the second layer of the same class `nexus-moht0` covers. `moht0` is about
gates that pass without checking; this is about gates that check correctly and then are
not consulted.

## The decision this needs (Hal's, not a fix to apply blindly)

Which of these SHOULD be required on develop and/or main? Requiring a check has real
cost — a required check that flakes or that skips wrongly wedges every PR, and this repo
has already been bitten by the pending-forever shape (`service-ci.yml`'s own header
explains why its workflow carries no `paths:` filter: a required check that never
triggers leaves PRs pending FOREVER, not passing).

Candidates, with the tension stated:
  - `engine-service-build` — expensive; making it required is the CI-cost question, not
    just a protection toggle.
  - `service-ci.yml`'s Java suite + its `changes` detector — `hq9na`'s existing point is
    that 1541 engine tests currently gate nothing at merge, and that TWO P0 catalog
    defects (`nexus-u4e20`, `nexus-v6za0`) reached develop behind exactly that gap.
  - the write-seam behavioural gate.

⛔ Do NOT change branch protection as part of a code change. It is repo configuration, it
is not in version control, and flipping it silently changes the merge contract for
everyone. Surface the recommendation; Hal decides.

## Cheap mitigation available now, independent of the decision

Add a test that asserts the live required-check set MATCHES what the workflow comments
claim, so the two cannot drift again silently. That converts this from a thing
rediscovered every few months into a thing that fails loudly the moment it is untrue.
Note it needs network/auth, so it belongs with the integration or a dedicated marker —
NOT in the default unit suite, per the sibling High finding on exactly that mistake.

## Origin

Found during code review of the `nexus-cqquo` fix, verified live by the reviewer and
then independently re-verified. Extends `nexus-hq9na`. Related: `nexus-moht0` (the
vacuous-gate epic), `nexus-cqquo` (the guards this affects).

title: CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest asserts stale pre-nexus-s13u0 fk-001 message shape
description:
Discovered during RDR-191 GATE-2 review follow-up (nexus-o8dil.7 physicalCollectionOf
verified-stamp fix), 2026-08-12. Out of scope for that fix, filed as a new finding.

service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/http/CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest.java (RDR-172
follow-up, nexus-7e057 -- predates RDR-191) has 3 tests asserting the OLD fk-001
SQLException message shape for an unregistered doc_id:
  - manifestWrite_unregisteredDocId_returns409_withSqlstate (line 114)
  - manifestAppend_unregisteredDocId_returns409_withSqlstate (line 129)
  - manifestWriteMany_unregisteredDoc_failedCarriesReasonAndSqlstate (line ~250s)

Each asserts response body contains `"sqlstate":"23503"` and/or
`"reason":"foreign key violation"`. This is now permanently unreachable: nexus-s13u0
redesigned CatalogRepository.physicalCollectionOf to throw DocumentNotFoundException
explicitly ("manifest write refused: document not registered: <id>") instead of relying
on the raw FK violation for the "doc not registered" case, since
catalog_document_chunks.collection went NOT NULL with no sentinel/DEFAULT
(catalog-025-collection-not-null.xml) and the old FK-violation-as-signal mechanism no
longer fires the same way.

Current behavior (post this session's CatalogHandler.java fix, which added a
DocumentNotFoundException -> 409 catch arm): HTTP status 409 now matches the test's
expectation. The body-content assertions (sqlstate/reason strings) do not and cannot
without editing the test to the new message shape.

Fix: update the 3 assertions to check for the new message
("manifest write refused: document not registered: ...") instead of the old
fk-001-era sqlstate/reason fields. Verify the single-doc AND batch (writeManifestMany)
paths both get updated consistently.

Verification command:
  cd service && ./mvnw -q -o test -Dnexus.test.forks=1 -Dtest=CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest

title: StagingPromoteOps' manifest_unresolved counter is INFO-only with zero automated consumers, so a real data-integrity signal reaches nobody — and neither staging counter has a metric or alert path
description:
StagingPromoteOps' `manifest_unresolved` counter is INFO-only with zero automated consumers, so a real data-integrity signal reaches nobody — and neither counter has a metric or alert path

## The finding

`POST /v1/staging/finalize` returns a counts map that includes `manifest_unresolved`
(pre-existing) and, as of `nexus-s13u0`, `manifest_doc_not_registered`. Both are
data-integrity signals: they count manifest rows the finalize could not resolve or
attribute. Established while fixing `nexus-s13u0`:

  - The counters ride in the RAW HTTP RESPONSE BODY of `/v1/staging/finalize`, and in a
    pre-existing UNCONDITIONAL `log.info("event=staging_finalize" ... counts={})` that
    dumps the whole map. At INFO, mixed in with routine success counts, a nonzero
    integrity counter is indistinguishable from normal operation.
  - ZERO AUTOMATED CONSUMERS. `grep` finds no Python caller of `/v1/staging/finalize`
    anywhere in `src/nexus/`. The single E2E script that exercises `finalize()`
    (`tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_guided.sh`) asserts on five specific
    unrelated fields and never reads either key.
  - So the only way a nonzero value reaches a human is a printed JSON blob during a
    manual rehearsal run that nobody is reading for this.

`nexus-s13u0` added `log.warn("event=staging_finalize_doc_not_registered tenant={}
count={}")`, fired only when nonzero, for the NEW key. That closes the immediate gap
for `manifest_doc_not_registered` only.

## What is left, and why it is worth a bead rather than a comment

1. `manifest_unresolved` STILL has the original weakness: INFO-only, no consumer, no
   conditional WARN. It is the older of the two and counts the same class of problem.
   Shipping one key surfaced and its sibling silent is the kind of inconsistency that
   gets rediscovered later as a defect, by someone who reasonably assumes both
   integrity counters behave the same way.
2. NEITHER key has a metric or an alert path. A conditional WARN is actionable only if
   somebody is already reading logs for the right reason. This is the weaker half of
   the project's fail-loud convention: loud enough to find during an investigation, not
   loud enough to start one.

## Why this is not a nitpick

A counter that nobody reads is functionally equivalent to no counter. `nexus-c30ew`'s
whole arc this session turned on instruments that reported clean because they could not
see what they were measuring, and the RDR-191 rationale names that false-clean class
explicitly. This is the same shape one layer out: the instrument WORKS and its output
goes nowhere.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

- A conditional WARN for `manifest_unresolved`, matching what
  `manifest_doc_not_registered` now has — the cheap half, and it makes the two
  consistent.
- Decide deliberately whether either belongs on a metric/alert path, or whether the
  honest answer is that `/v1/staging/finalize` is an operator-invoked route whose JSON
  a human reads at the time, in which case say so in the handler's docstring and stop
  treating log level as the mitigation.
- If a consumer is wanted: the E2E rehearsal script is the obvious first one, since it
  already parses the response and asserts on five other fields. Asserting these two are
  zero would turn both counters into a gate rather than a diary.

## Origin

Found by the `nexus-s13u0` implementation agent while answering whether its new counter
was surfaced anywhere an operator would see it — a question asked because a counter is
strictly weaker than a throw against the fail-loud directive. The sibling's identical
weakness was inherited, not introduced by that change. Detail: T2
`nexus/nexus-s13u0-9kj5j-final-results-2026-08-12` [22320].

title: RDR-191 GATE-2 tripwire: no test covers F8c retraction and F10c still-referenced COOPERATING when a pruned chash is shared with a second live document
description:
The GATE-2 tripwire's Python arm covers the F8c+F10c composition, but only for the case where the pruned chash is referenced by NO other live document. The interesting case, where the client-side retraction and the server-side still-referenced anti-join must COOPERATE on the same call, is untested.

## What is covered today

`tests/test_o8dil7_prune_misclassified_manifest_antijoin_engine.py::test_prune_misclassified_real_engine_no_dangling_manifest_row` drives the full chain on a live engine:

    _prune_misclassified_in_collection (src/nexus/indexer.py:2530)
      -> _guarded_delete
      -> _batched_delete (:2492-2500)
      -> _ServiceCollectionStub.delete (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1295)
      -> real HTTP
      -> real PgVectorRepository.delete

Its fixture is dangling by construction (manifest `collection` denormalized to the RIGHT collection, physical chunk only ever in the WRONG one), so `dangling_after == dangling_before` holds only if F8c's retraction is correct. Genuinely non-vacuous; verified by the critic by hand-tracing the chain rather than reading the docstring.

## The gap

No test covers a chash SHARED by a second LIVE document in the collection being pruned, driven through this Python wrapper.

That is the case where the two halves must agree:
- F8c (client-side) retracts the manifest row for the document being pruned, and
- F10c (server-side) `stillReferenced` must REFUSE the chunk delete because the OTHER live document still references the same chash.

Both must be right, and they must be right about the same rows, in the same call. Either one alone passing proves nothing about the pair. RDR-108's shared-chunk collapse makes identical chunk text in one collection share a single row by design, so this is a normal state, not an exotic one — and `_batched_delete`'s own docstring says the server "reports an int that can legitimately be less than requested (the server's anti-join retains a chash a live document still references)", i.e. the code already anticipates exactly this interaction.

## What a test would catch that the halves cannot

- A retraction that removes the wrong document's manifest row (client half wrong, server half masks it because the chunk survives anyway).
- An anti-join that refuses the delete for the wrong reason, or that stops refusing after a refactor (server half wrong, client half masks it because the count reconciles).
- A count-honesty regression: `_batched_delete` returning `len(ids)` instead of the server's actual deleted count is invisible unless a partial refusal actually occurs, which is precisely this scenario.

## Shape

Seed one collection with two LIVE documents sharing a chash. Prune one of them via `_prune_misclassified_in_collection` against the real engine. Assert:
1. no dangling manifest row afterwards (global, `(tenant_id, collection, chash)`-keyed),
2. the CHUNK SURVIVES, because the second document still references it,
3. the returned delete count reflects the SERVER's actual count, not the requested one.

Assertion 2 is the one the existing test cannot make, and it is the point.

## Scope note

This is a NARROW residual. The critic was explicit it is NOT grounds to reopen GATE-2 acceptance item 3, and it should not be used as one. It is a follow-up.

## Origin

substantive-critic round-2 re-review of the GATE-2 tripwire (2026-08-12), recorded in T2 `nexus/rdr191-gate2-tripwire-critic-round2-2026-08-12` [22301].
close_reason: Covered in 8c75a61a3: test_prune_misclassified_shared_chash_second_live_document_protected drives the F8c retraction + F10c server still-referenced COOPERATING in one call against the real engine — shared chunk survives, doc B's manifest row intact, pruning doc's row retracted, AND the count-honesty assertion (pruned == 0, actual-not-requested) the bead named. Critic verified it is NOT the gy2eh weak-guard shape (real server round-trip traced). Stacked review clean.

title: [bug] the four heavy testcontainers classes wedge or crash under the default forkCount=4, twice on 2026-08-11 — one hung ~46min on a socket to a REAPED container
description:
Running the heavy testcontainers classes together under the default `forkCount=4` (service/pom.xml:98/:269, `reuseForks=true`) wedged or crashed TWICE on 2026-08-11, from two independent sessions. The workaround found was `-Dnexus.test.forks=1`, which is a LOCAL flag. CI runs the default.

## Observed twice, independently

(1) A developer agent's neighbours run hit a forked-VM crash running
    CatalogDeleteCollectionCascadeTest, StagingPromoteOpsIntegrationTest,
    RekeyOpsIntegrationTest and PgVectorRepositoryDeleteAntiJoinTest together.
    Attributed to those four large testcontainers classes contending for Docker
    resources across parallel forks. Resolved by re-running with
    `-Dnexus.test.forks=1`.

(2) A separate run of the same four classes WEDGED rather than crashed, and was
    diagnosed here directly:
      - surefire JVM alive ~46 min after three of the four classes had finished
        in ~25s each
      - `jstack` showed the main thread RUNNABLE in
        `sun.nio.ch.Net.poll` -> `org.postgresql.core.VisibleBufferedInputStream.readMore`,
        i.e. blocked reading a PG socket that never answers
      - `lsof` showed TWO established connections: one to the live pgvector
        container (port 49167) and one to port 49160, a container NOT PRESENT in
        `docker ps`
      - `docker ps` showed TWO testcontainers ryuk instances but only ONE
        non-ryuk container: one session's PG had been reaped while a JVM still
        held a connection to it
      - `pg_stat_activity` on the surviving container showed no activity and no
        blocking chain, confirming the wedge was against the DEAD peer
    A read against a reaped container neither returns nor resets, so the run
    hangs indefinitely rather than failing.

## Why this matters beyond a local annoyance

- CI uses the default `forkCount=4`. Neither observation involved a code defect,
  so this presents as a random red or, worse, a HANG that burns the job's wall
  clock until the runner times out. A hang is the expensive failure mode: it
  produces no useful signal and it consumes the full timeout budget.
- The RDR-191 GATE-2 tripwire adds a FIFTH heavy testcontainers class
  (`RdrO8dil7GlobalManifestAntiJoinTest`), raising contention pressure on exactly
  the set that already failed twice.
- The project deliberately runs NO `rerunFailingTestsCount` (service/pom.xml:252-262,
  "a racy PRODUCT bug would be retried into a green run"). That is the right call,
  and it means an infra-level flake here surfaces as a hard red with no retry,
  training people to re-run by hand. That habit is precisely what the no-blanket-rerun
  directive exists to prevent.

## Ask

1. Establish whether this reproduces on CI hardware or is specific to this
   workstation's Docker (the box also has a known Docker port-forward wedge class,
   T2 `project_docker_port_forwarding_wedges`). Do not assume either way; the two
   observations here are both local.
2. If real, decide the fix deliberately rather than by flag:
   - cap forks for the testcontainers-heavy classes specifically, or
   - make `SharedCluster` resilient to a reaped peer (a socket timeout would convert
     the HANG into a fast, legible failure — arguably worth doing regardless, since
     an indefinite hang is never the right response to a dead container), or
   - serialize that class set.
3. Whatever ships needs to fail FAST rather than hang. The hang, not the crash, is
   the part that cost the most time tonight.

## Note

`-Dnexus.test.forks=1` is a workaround, not a fix, and it is invisible to CI. If it
becomes the accepted answer it belongs in the build configuration where CI reads it,
not in an agent's shell history.

## Origin

Observed during the RDR-191 GATE-2 tripwire work (nexus-o8dil.7). Not caused by
that work; the tripwire only adds to the contended set.

title: [bug] doctor's producer-regression anchor is a RELEASE-TAG time, which the install has no reason to share — a late upgrader gets the same false positive apig6 just fixed, and the check has install-local evidence it ignores
description:
Split out of nexus-apig6 (Hal, 2026-08-11: "part of the fix"), raised by
substantive-critic Significant #1 and code-review-expert focus area 2. Landing
in the SAME change as apig6 — shipping apig6 alone leaves the false positive
fully intact for anyone who upgraded late.

THE DEFECT
apig6 corrected doctor's producer-regression anchor from v7.1.0's tag time to
v7.3.0's. Both are RELEASE-TAG times, and a release tag says when the code
became available, not when this install started running it. An install that
upgraded on 2026-09-15 wrote legitimately-unfenced documents for five weeks
after 2026-08-07; every one of them is dated after the anchor, so doctor
reports each as a producer regression and prescribes re-indexing. That is
apig6's exact false positive displaced onto a later population — same class,
different window, and unbounded in size (it grows with upgrade lateness).

The check already had the evidence it needed and ignored it: the documents
that ARE stamped.

THE FIX — install-local anchor
Every producer was fenced by ONE commit (f55435eb), so a single stamped
document anywhere in the corpus proves this install's client had FULL coverage
at that document's write time. That is a fact about THIS install.

  anchor = earliest indexed_at over documents with a non-null index_state

Documents unstamped BEFORE the anchor were written by a pre-coverage client —
expected, no action. Unstamped AFTER it are genuine regressions.

The release constant survives as a candidate-gathering FLOOR in the walk (no
client can have had coverage before the release existed), which also makes a
skewed/restored pre-release stamp unable to drag the anchor backwards.

THIRD OUTCOME — ambiguity, stated
Zero stamped documents anywhere means nothing establishes this install ever ran
a fenced client; a late upgrader and a broken producer are indistinguishable.
This still WARNS — silence would hide the exact shape the vw594 incident had,
and is pinned live by test_cotmr_cli_store_fence.py::TestAcquireGateJourney
DoctorClean::test_artificially_unfenced_document_still_warns, which caught the
first attempt at this arm when it returned ok=True. The WARN states the
ambiguity, asserts no regression, and prescribes re-indexing ONE document.

ALSO FIXED HERE (substantive-critic Significant #2 + Minor)
- _MAX_RETAINED_UNSTAMPED=50 was defined but the display join hardcoded [:10].
  Replaced by _MAX_NAMED_UNSTAMPED=10 (display) and _MAX_TRACKED_UNSTAMPED=1000
  (retention), both actually used; walk-time truncation is reported explicitly.
- Stale "08-02..08-09" assertion message corrected to the five-day window.

DEAD CODE FOUND BY ITS OWN KILL CONTROL
The anchor first read max(earliest_stamped_dt, _PRODUCER_FENCE_RELEASE_DT).
Removing the max() failed no test — because candidates are already gathered
above the floor during the walk, so an anchor below it cannot change any
outcome. The max() was deleted and the test re-pointed at the walk-level guard,
which does go RED when deleted. The original test was vacuous and passing.

KILL CONTROLS (all run 2026-08-11, each RED for exactly its own tests)
  KC1 anchor -> pure release-tag        => 3 oiu1t tests RED
  KC2 drop max() floor                  => nothing RED (proved it dead)
  KC3 drop walk-level floor guard       => 2 tests RED
  plus apig6's two: wrong anchor date, dropped undated counter

TESTS: 11 in TestDoctorFenceCoverageDistinction, incl. the late upgrader, its
non-vacuity control (same install, one post-baseline doc, must still WARN and
name only that one), zero-stamp ambiguity, and the floor.

SUITES: full unit suite 12524 passed / 37 skipped / 4 xfailed. Affected-suite
sweep 196 passed.

KNOWN LIMIT (not fixed, no evidence it bites): the anchor is corpus-wide, so an
install whose ONLY stamped documents are recent still treats its own older
unstamped writes as pre-coverage. Per-document producer-client-version tracking
would settle it exactly; that is a catalog schema change with no demand.
notes:
ROUND 3 — reviewer findings addressed 2026-08-11 (both reviewers re-run on the
combined diff; both returned a Critical on the SAME assumption).

CRITICAL (confirmed, not adopted on faith): "a single stamp proves full client
coverage" is FALSE. v7.1.0 fenced 4 sites (all PDF/md/DEVONthink ingest); the
rest arrived at v7.3.0, and no catalog field records which producer or client
version stamped a row. An install on v7.1.0/v7.2.x that runs one PDF ingest
establishes an anchor while its repo-index/store_put writes stay legitimately
unfenced. Tracked as nexus-2sa6w (P1, open) with the disposition recorded
there; the content_type-based discriminator was deliberately NOT taken now.
This diff stops asserting the claim: docstring KNOWN LIMIT with the git
derivation, WARN names both explanations, `nx --version` is the first fix
suggestion, and a compound-scenario test pins the non-accusatory wording.

IMPORTANT 1: `legacy` folded `candidates_truncated` into "predate the anchor,
need no action" while the same message admitted they were unattributed. They
are now excluded from `legacy`.

IMPORTANT 2: the `checked > 0` ok=True summary collapsed to "none (N checked)",
dropping the reported_null/undated story — and that is the COMMON branch on a
real corpus, the exact state a downstream install misread as an upstream bug.
It now carries the attributed-legacy and undated counts.

IMPORTANT 3: "no document has EVER been stamped" was reachable-false when
stamps exist but carry unparseable indexed_at. The message now distinguishes
checked == 0 from "none of the N stamped documents has a usable date".

KILL CONTROL 4: restoring the accusatory wording turns 3 tests RED.
TESTS: 12 in TestDoctorFenceCoverageDistinction.
SUITES: full unit 12525 passed / 37 skipped / 4 xfailed; affected sweep 197.
close_reason: Shipped 8aa4c4e9. Anchor = earliest indexed_at over stamped documents (install-local), release date retained as candidate-gathering floor. Third outcome added for the no-baseline case: WARNs stating ambiguity rather than asserting or staying silent (first cut returned ok=True and lost detection; test_cotmr_cli_store_fence's artificially-unfenced control caught it). Round-3 reviewer Criticals addressed by removing the false full-coverage claim; discriminator deferred to nexus-2sa6w P1 open with disposition recorded there. Also fixed: truncated-vs-legacy accounting, checked>0 summary transparency, EVER-stamped overclaim, dead max() floor. 12 tests, 4 kill controls. Full suite 12525 passed.

title: [bug] doctor's producer-regression WARN anchors on _FENCE_RELEASE_DT = v7.1.0 (4-site fence), five days before full producer coverage shipped at v7.3.0 — false-positive on any doc indexed 08-02..08-07, and its fix_suggestion is a full corpus re-embed
description:
FOUND VIA a downstream instance (Steve's box, conexus 7.6.1) reporting 460/462
catalog docs with index_state NULL and concluding "nexus-vw594 is an unpatched
upstream producer bug". vw594 is CLOSED and shipped; the real defect is here.

src/nexus/health.py:4509
    _FENCE_RELEASE_DT = datetime(2026, 8, 2, 22, 26, 0, tzinfo=UTC)   # v7.1.0

_check_stale_indexing_runs uses this to tell two cases apart:
  (a) quiescent fence-aware corpus, nothing indexed since the fence  -> ok=True
  (b) "vw594 signature": a doc indexed AFTER the fence with no stamp -> WARN

The constant is the v7.1.0 tag time, i.e. the CLIENT fence at 4 sites
(commit 4b0c5fb5). vw594's own investigation established those 4 sites
covered ~105/10544 docs; the producers of the other 96% (repo indexer
_batch_flush, store_put, code/prose indexers, memory, MCP) were only fenced
by f55435eb (2026-08-04), which reached the public at v7.5.0
(2026-08-09 22:45:30 UTC).

CONSEQUENCE: every document indexed in the window
    2026-08-02 22:26 UTC  ..  <user's upgrade to >=7.5.0>
was written by a producer that was legitimately unfenced at the time, and
trips branch (b). The emitted text asserts "The fence engine is live; a
producer wrote this document without ever calling index-run begin/complete
(nexus-vw594 coverage gap), not a pre-fence engine" — naming a CLOSED bead as
a live coverage gap — and its sole fix_suggestion is

    nx index <path> --force   (re-index through a fenced producer)

i.e. re-chunk + re-embed the corpus to backfill a metadata column. On the
reporting install that is ~460/462 documents. vw594 ruled NO LEGACY BACKFILL
as a design decision, so this WARN's remedy contradicts the design decision
that produced the state it is warning about.

Corroborating evidence that the fence itself is HEALTHY: 2 of 462 docs on
that install DO carry index_state — consistent with the small number written
since 7.5.0 stamping correctly.

FIX
1. Move _FENCE_RELEASE_DT to the v7.5.0 tag time (2026-08-09T22:45:30Z) —
   the first PUBLIC release in which ALL producers stamp. Update the
   docstring: it currently justifies the v7.1.0 value explicitly, so the
   comment must move at full width, not just the literal.
2. Restate the WARN text: vw594 is closed. A post-7.5.0 unstamped doc is a
   NEW producer regression, not "the vw594 coverage gap".
3. The fix_suggestion must not read as a routine remedy when the population
   is the whole catalog. Either scope it to the named documents or say
   plainly that pre-7.5.0 documents are permanent no-backfill debt and need
   no action.
4. Regression test: a doc with indexed_at between the v7.1.0 and v7.5.0 tag
   times and index_state NULL must NOT produce the vw594-signature WARN; a
   doc after v7.5.0 must.

WHY P2: not data corruption and search/retrieval are unaffected, but this is
a false-positive health finding whose prescribed remedy is an expensive,
design-contradicting corpus re-embed, and it has already caused one
downstream instance to file the state as an open upstream bug.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 (code-review-expert, verified independently via git).

This bead's DESCRIPTION states full producer coverage shipped at v7.5.0 on
2026-08-09T22:45:30Z. THAT IS WRONG, and the first fix attempt faithfully
implemented the wrong number.

Ground truth:
    git tag --contains f55435eb --sort=creatordate | grep '^v' | head -1
        -> v7.3.0
    git log -1 --format=%cI v7.3.0
        -> 2026-08-07T09:00:35-07:00   (= 2026-08-07T16:00:35Z)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor f55435eb v7.2.0
        -> non-zero (v7.2.0, 2026-08-04, does NOT contain it)

CHANGELOG.md's v7.3.0 entry corroborates ("begin-many index-run fence";
"nx store put / nx memory promote join the RUNFENCE choreography"); v7.4.0
and v7.5.0 carry no fence work at all.

PROVENANCE OF THE ERROR: `git tag --contains f55435eb` was run in this
session and its output listed v7.3.0 FIRST. I read past it and wrote v7.5.0
into both this bead and the code. The false-positive window is five days
(08-02..08-07), not a week, and anchoring on v7.5.0 would have silently
absorbed any real regression in the 08-07..08-09 gap into the "legacy, no
action needed" bucket — the same defect class this bead exists to close,
merely narrower and in the safe direction.

Read the DERIVATION block in _PRODUCER_FENCE_RELEASE_DT's docstring, not this
bead's description, for the authoritative number: the docstring carries the
git commands to re-verify it.

SHIPPED FIX (all four description items delivered, plus two review findings):
  1. _FENCE_RELEASE_DT -> _PRODUCER_FENCE_RELEASE_DT = 2026-08-07T16:00:35Z,
     docstring rewritten at full width with the derivation commands and BOTH
     wrong values called out by name (v7.1.0 backward, v7.5.0 forward).
  2. WARN text: names a NEW coverage regression, no longer cites closed
     nexus-vw594 as a live gap.
  3. WARN counts and NAMES only the post-coverage population; appends the
     legacy count with "need no action (no legacy backfill by design)".
     fix_suggestion scoped to the named documents.
  4. Tests: 08-02..08-07 window must not warn; post-08-07 must warn and name
     itself; mixed corpus counts 1 not 6.
  +5 (review): post_fence_names capped at _MAX_RETAINED_UNSTAMPED=50 while
     the count stays exact — the list was unbounded over a 10k-doc walk.
  +6 (review): reported-but-NULL docs with no usable indexed_at are counted
     separately and never claimed to predate coverage.

Kill controls (both run, both RED for exactly their own test):
  A. anchor -> 2026-08-09  => test_regression_just_after_v7_3_0_is_not_absorbed_as_legacy RED
  B. drop undated counter  => test_undated_reported_null_is_not_claimed_as_pre_coverage RED

Suites: 144 passed / 4 deselected across test_health_service_checks.py,
test_cotmr_cli_store_fence.py, db/test_vw594_runfence_coverage.py,
test_engine_version.py.
close_reason: Shipped 8aa4c4e9 on feature/nexus-apig6-fence-anchor. Anchor corrected v7.1.0 -> v7.3.0 (2026-08-07T16:00:35Z, git-derived, docstring carries the derivation commands); WARN scoped/named/non-accusatory; legacy population excused explicitly; fix_suggestion no longer prescribes a corpus re-embed.
