title: Replace the routing-tier ownership PROXY in _t1_clear_if_owned with a real ownership signal (and close the disclosed TOCTOU with it)
description:
`_t1_clear_if_owned` (`src/nexus/hooks.py`, nexus-65a9k) infers T1 scope ownership from the ROUTING TIER (`USE_LEASED` / `USE_INHERITED` / `MINT`). That is a PROXY for ownership, not an ownership signal.

## Why the proxy is load-bearing and fragile

`USE_INHERITED` is treated as "this process owns the scope outright, safe to clear". That is true TODAY only because of discipline in `src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py`:
- `share_t1` is retired and raises;
- `ephemeral` + `grants_tool_access` always mints a fresh, distinct uuid4 session and never forwards the parent's token.

The gate cannot verify any of that. It trusts it.

⛔ A future drift in `dispatch.py` could reopen an equivalent hole silently — and that is EXACTLY the class of drift that caused GH #1454 in the first place: `dispatch.py` forwarding `NX_SESSION_ID` to a child that had no business holding it. The fix for that bug now depends on a different unenforced invariant in the same file.

## Ask

Introduce a real ownership signal rather than inferring one. Sketch (not prescriptive): an explicit `NX_T1_BORROWED` marker set at dispatch time, which the SessionEnd path reads directly, so "am I allowed to delete this scope" is answered by something the dispatcher DECLARED rather than something the resolver INFERRED.

Whatever lands should make the question answerable without reasoning about routing tiers at all.

## Also fold in — the disclosed TOCTOU

The gate re-derives `resolve_t1_routing_tiers()` immediately before `clear()`, which is a SEPARATE call from the one that opened the store. A window exists across the `flagged_entries()` HTTP call and a T2 write. Both reviewers assessed it as narrow and non-blocking for the P0:
- exploitable only if the borrowed-from parent's lease is removed in that exact window;
- it matches an accepted race-window precedent already present in the same function.

But the substantive-critic added a point worth keeping: if a fresh lease goes stale mid-window the decision flips to `MINT`, which is NOT gated, and `clear()` proceeds against a still-parent-bound store. That can violate nexus-d76vc's design, which deliberately PRESERVES a handed-off session's rows via TTL rather than deleting them. So the window is not merely wasted work.

A real ownership signal would close the TOCTOU as a side effect, since there would be nothing to re-derive.

## Scope fence

NOT a P0 and NOT a 7.6.1 blocker. Both stacked reviewers cleared the shipped fix explicitly. This is hardening of a correct fix, not a correction of it.

## Origin

Secondary findings from both reviewers on the nexus-65a9k patch, 2026-08-11. T2: `nexus/nexus-65a9k-code-review-findings` [22279].

title: nx scratch clear reaches the same USE_LEASED path as the GH#1454 data loss — user-confirmed, but confirmation does not establish scope ownership
description:
`nx scratch clear` (`src/nexus/commands/scratch.py` `clear_cmd`) reaches the same `get_t1_database()` -> tier-2 USE_LEASED path that caused the GH #1454 data loss, and can therefore delete a T1 scope owned by a different live process.

## Difference from the P0

`nexus-65a9k` (GH #1454) was AUTOMATIC and silent: a `claude -p` child's SessionEnd hook wiped its parent's scope with no user involvement. This path is USER-INVOKED and confirmed (preview + `click.confirm` unless `--yes`), so a human sees a prompt before anything is deleted. That is why it was deliberately left out of the P0 minimal patch, not because it is safe.

## Why it still matters

The confirmation shows the user WHAT will be deleted, but it does not establish WHOSE scope it is. If `clear_cmd` has borrowed another live session's lease, the preview accurately lists rows that belong to a different conversation and the user confirms deletion of someone else's working memory believing it is their own. The prompt is not a defence against wrong-scope resolution; it is a defence against accidental invocation.

`--yes` removes even that.

## The contract problem

After `nexus-65a9k` lands, `USE_LEASED` means "must not delete" in the SessionEnd hook and "may delete on confirmation" here. Same tier, opposite semantics, in the same codebase. Decide deliberately which it is rather than leaving it split by accident.

## Ask

1. Apply the same ownership gate the P0 introduced (`_t1_clear_if_owned` in `src/nexus/hooks.py`) or its logic, so a borrowed scope is never cleared.
2. If a user genuinely needs to clear a borrowed scope, that should be an explicit, differently-named action, not the default behaviour of `nx scratch clear`.
3. Whatever lands, make the two call sites agree on what `USE_LEASED` permits, and say so in one place rather than two.

## Verify before fixing

Confirm the USE_LEASED path is actually reachable from `clear_cmd` in practice, not just in principle. The P0's implementer flagged this by code inspection and did not demonstrate it. If it turns out unreachable, close this WONTFIX with the reasoning recorded, which is a fine outcome.

## Origin

Flagged by the `nexus-65a9k` implementer while fixing GH #1454, correctly left outside that patch's ownership fence. 2026-08-11.

title: T1 tier-2 can resolve via the machine-wide current_session file, binding a process to a DIFFERENT concurrent conversation's scope
description:
When `read_claude_session_id()` returns empty, `NX_SESSION_ID` is unset and the T1 tier-2 path can resolve via the machine-wide `~/.config/nexus/current_session` file — which our own docs describe as "a machine-wide last-writer-wins file a concurrent session can own."

That means a process can bind to a session identity belonging to a DIFFERENT concurrent conversation.

## Severity, stated precisely

The DATA-LOSS half of this is closed by `nexus-65a9k`'s ownership gate: once the destructive `clear()` only fires on tier-1 `USE_INHERITED`, a tier-2 resolution — however it was reached — can no longer delete anything. Verify that reasoning holds once 65a9k lands rather than assuming it.

What REMAINS after 65a9k is the resolution hazard itself: reads and writes can land in the wrong conversation's scope. That is a correctness and privacy-shaped problem (one conversation's working memory becoming visible or writable to another), not a deletion problem. Filed at P2 on that basis. **If 65a9k's fix turns out not to close the deletion path, raise this immediately** — it becomes a P0 sibling.

## Ask

1. Confirm the deletion path is genuinely closed by 65a9k's gate.
2. Decide whether tier-2 should be allowed to resolve from `current_session` at all for a process that did not write it. The file is a shared mutable global; it is the same design hazard as any such global and will surface again elsewhere.
3. If it must stay, authenticate it — the handoff watcher already establishes a precedent by re-deriving its OWN ancestry (`nexus.session.find_mcp_sibling_pids`) rather than trusting a marker file alone (nexus-d76vc). Mirror that rather than inventing a new mechanism.

## Note on what this bug is NOT

The `frozen-at-spawn` claim for MCP-tool T1 in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md is TRUE and unregressed — verified during the 65a9k diagnosis (`mcp_infra.get_t1()` caches `_t1_instance`, reset only by `reset_t1_for_release()` from the handoff tick). This bead is about the CLI/hook tier-2 path, not about MCP scope drift. Do not "fix" the MCP resolution chain on the strength of this bead.

## Origin

Diagnosis of nexus-65a9k (GH #1454), 2026-08-11.
notes:
## ⛔ 2026-08-11 — THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG. Corrected. Verdict: NOT a P0 sibling.

This bead asserted that nexus-65a9k's fix closes the deletion half because
"clear() only fires on tier-1 USE_INHERITED". **That is factually wrong**, caught
by the substantive-critic on the 65a9k patch and VERIFIED by reading the shipped
gate (`src/nexus/hooks.py` `_t1_clear_if_owned`).

WHAT THE GATE ACTUALLY DOES: it skips clear() on `USE_LEASED` ONLY. Both
`USE_INHERITED` and `MINT` proceed to `t1.clear()`. The docstring says so
outright: "every other decision (USE_INHERITED, or the MINT that produced the
genuinely-bare CLI-dedicated store) is unchanged from before this fix and clears
exactly as it always has."

### Answering this bead's own escalation condition

I wrote: "If 65a9k's fix turns out not to close the deletion path, raise this
immediately — it becomes a P0 sibling." Honest answer, having checked:

**IT DOES NOT BECOME A P0 SIBLING**, but not for the reason originally given.

The reasoning that actually holds: a LIVE process holds a published, refreshed
lease by construction. Binding to a live process's scope therefore resolves as
`USE_LEASED`, which IS gated. So the delete-a-live-process's-working-memory path
— the GH #1454 defect — is closed. The original conclusion was right; its stated
premise was not.

### The residual, which is real and narrower

`MINT` is ungated, and MINT can bind to an EXISTING session id whose lease has
lapsed but whose rows have not yet been TTL-swept. Clearing then deletes rows of
a NON-live session. Two ways that matters:

1. It can violate nexus-d76vc's design, which DELIBERATELY preserves a
   handed-off session's rows via the 24h TTL rather than deleting them (the
   `/clear` and `/resume` case). Deleting them early defeats that choice.
2. A narrow race: a live MCP whose lease refresh lapses momentarily could be
   MINTed over and cleared. Requires the refresh to fail in exactly that window.

Neither is the always-reproducible, silent, live-scope wipe that made 65a9k a P0.

### ALSO UNVERIFIED — a SEPARATE close_session() call site, not covered by 65a9k

`src/nexus/mcp/core.py` (~:1204) constructs a FRESH `HttpScratchStore()` and
calls `close_session()` during MCP teardown, via `_t1_shutdown()`. That is a
process closing its OWN scope at its own shutdown, so it is a different shape
from the child-wipes-parent defect and is NOT ship-blocking for 7.6.1.

But it builds a NEW store rather than using the cached frozen `_t1_instance`,
which means it RE-RESOLVES at teardown. If resolution has drifted by then, it
could close a session that is not its own. INFERRED, not reproduced. Verify
reachability before treating it as benign OR as a defect.

### Ask, revised

1. Decide whether `MINT` should also be gated, or whether clearing a
   lease-less-but-extant session id is intended behaviour. Reconcile with
   nexus-d76vc's TTL-preservation design either way.
2. Verify the `mcp/core.py` teardown call site above.
3. Keep the original tier-2 / `current_session` resolution question — it is
   unchanged and still stands.

Priority stays P2: no live-scope deletion path remains open.

title: Every claude -p operator dispatch triggers a full detached SessionEnd (fork + T1 resolve + T2 expire sweep) on the highest-volume path
description:
Every `claude -p` operator dispatch triggers a FULL detached SessionEnd on the highest-volume path in the system: a double-fork, a T1 routing resolve, and a T2 `expire()` sweep — per operator call.

## Why this is worth fixing on its own

Found while root-causing `nexus-65a9k` (GH #1454), where this machinery deleted a live parent's T1 scope. The ownership gate in that P0 stops the DELETION, but it does not stop the WORK: every `operator_extract` / `operator_rank` / `operator_summarize` / `nx_answer` call still pays a fork plus a T2 expire sweep it has no reason to run.

`nx_answer`'s own docstring reports 100-run production latency where 40% of calls take 30s-2min and 23% take 2-5min, and plan execution fans out one subprocess per operator step. So this is per-step overhead on the slowest, highest-fanout path we have.

## Ask

1. Measure it first. Do not assume it is significant — quantify the fork + resolve + T2 expire cost per dispatch before changing anything. If it is noise against a 30s subprocess, close this WONTFIX with the measurement recorded, which is a perfectly good outcome.
2. If it is material, have the child's SessionEnd detect a nested/ephemeral operator dispatch and skip the flush entirely rather than resolving T1 and sweeping T2 for a process that owns neither.

## Relationship to the P0

Complementary, NOT a substitute. `nexus-65a9k`'s ownership gate is the correctness fix and must land on its own merits. Skipping the flush for nested dispatches is defence in depth plus a performance win. Do not merge the two: a P0 data-loss patch stays minimal.

## Origin

Diagnosis of nexus-65a9k, 2026-08-11. T3: `debug-finding-t1-scratch-wiped-by-operator-dispatch-65a9k-2026-08-11`.

title: test_store_cmd real_http_vector_client fixture leaves _reap_catalog_for_doc_ids able to make a real network call
description:
`tests/test_store_cmd.py`'s `real_http_vector_client` fixture does not mock the catalog reader reached by `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids`, so a test using it can make a REAL, UNCONTROLLED NETWORK CALL.

## Provenance

Found 2026-08-11 by the substantive-critic reviewing the `nexus-o8dil.45` diff. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by that change, which is why it did not block that commit. Surfaced as a single non-reproducible flaky failure; did NOT reproduce across 8 follow-up runs.

## Why this matters more than its flake rate suggests

A unit test that can reach the network is not a unit test, and this repo's unit suite is explicitly built to need no API keys and no network (`InMemoryVectorClient` + bundled ONNX). The consequences are all silent:

- On a developer box with a live cloud-mode install, the call may SUCCEED and the test passes for the wrong reason.
- In CI or offline it fails intermittently and reads as an ordinary flake.
- ⛔ Worst case: this box runs Hal's PRODUCTION cloud-mode install alongside the dev checkout. An uncontrolled catalog read from a test run is a test touching production state. Nothing here indicates a WRITE, but the boundary is the problem, not the current verb.

Low flake rate is what makes it dangerous — 1-in-N failures get re-run rather than investigated.

## Ask

1. Mock the catalog reader in the `real_http_vector_client` fixture so `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids` cannot reach out.
2. Verify by ASSERTION, not by observation: the fix must be proven by a test that fails if the network path is reachable, not by "we ran it 8 times and it passed". This flake already demonstrated that repeated green runs prove nothing here.
3. Consider whether a suite-wide guard belongs here — a fixture or conftest hook that fails loudly on an unexpected outbound connection during unit tests would close this whole class rather than this one instance. Do not build that speculatively; file it separately if the audit shows more instances.

## Scope fence

Test-isolation only. Not a production defect. `_reap_catalog_for_doc_ids`'s own behaviour is not in question.

## Related

- `nexus-3u1i2` — a different pre-existing flake in the same review sweep (xdist order-dependence). Different mechanism; do not merge without proving a shared cause.
- Directive `feedback_check_install_mode_before_diagnosing.md` — why an uncontrolled call from this checkout is specifically hazardous on this box.

title: Four more delete-count over-reporting callers outside o8dil.45's ownership: chunk_quarantine x2, mcp_infra x2
description:
`nexus-o8dil.45` fixed the delete-count over-reporting at the four call sites it owned. FOUR MORE call sites have the identical bug and were deliberately left untouched (out of that bead's declared file ownership).

## The bug class

`_ServiceCollectionStub.delete()` returns the server's actual deleted count. Post-`nexus-o8dil.5`, the engine's anti-join can legitimately delete FEWER chunks than requested (a chunk another live document still references is correctly retained). A caller that discards the return and reports `len(ids)` therefore SILENTLY OVER-REPORTS success on a request the server partially or fully refused.

Violates the standing project directive: no silent fallback for data-correctness problems — FAIL LOUD.

## Unfixed sites (reported by the o8dil.45 implementer, NOT independently re-verified)

- `src/nexus/catalog/chunk_quarantine.py:252` — `quarantine_orphans`
- `src/nexus/catalog/chunk_quarantine.py:299` — `restore_rereferenced`
- `src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:1430` — `_sweep_superseded_vectors`
- `src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:1565` — batch variant of the same

All four discard `_ServiceCollectionStub.delete()`'s return and report `len(ids)` unconditionally.

⚠ VERIFY BEFORE EDITING. Two of `nexus-o8dil.45`'s own claimed sites turned out to be DRIFTED — already fixed by commit 936e05a0 before work began. Line numbers here are as-reported at 2026-08-11 and will drift. Re-verify each site against the current file; if a claim does not match the code, report the discrepancy rather than "fixing" something into existence.

## Why these matter specifically

`chunk_quarantine`'s two arms are GC paths — `gc_restore_rereferenced` / `gc_expire_quarantine` are already implicated in the catalog-drift class (sibling `nexus-uyl70`). A quarantine sweep that reports it reclaimed N chunks when the server protected some of them makes drift diagnosis actively misleading, in exactly the subsystem where drift is currently being chased.

`mcp_infra`'s superseded-vector sweep runs on the MCP server's own lifecycle path, so its over-report lands in operator-facing output.

## Shape

Mirror what `nexus-o8dil.45` landed: capture the actual count, report it instead of the requested size, and decide per site whether `actual < requested` should be reported accurately or additionally WARN. Read the o8dil.45 diff first and follow its per-site reasoning rather than inventing a new contract.

## Scope fence

Count VISIBILITY only. Not manifest-completeness (that is `nexus-o8dil.2`), not the quarantine deregistration gap (that is `nexus-uyl70`).

## Origin

Found by the `nexus-o8dil.45` implementer while verifying that bead's claimed call sites; correctly left unfixed as outside declared file ownership rather than silently widening scope.

title: chash_rekey resolves 'is this local?' two different ways in one rung (credential-resolution vs is_local_mode)
description:
The `chash_rekey` upgrade-ladder rung decides "is this a local box?" TWO DIFFERENT WAYS in one rung. The two predicates can disagree, and nothing reconciles them.

## The two predicates

1. `_locally_actionable` — `src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/rungs/chash_rekey.py:701-728`, wired as `applicable_fn` at :737. Returns `resolve_admin_credentials(None) is not None`, i.e. "can I read pg_credentials" (`src/nexus/db/admin_sql.py:52-80`). This is a CREDENTIAL-RESOLUTION test.

2. The re-provision leg — `src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py:866-869` gates on `nexus.config.is_local_mode()`. This is a CONFIGURED-MODE test.

Both are reached from the same rung: `reprovision_diag_view_best_effort` (`pg_provision.py:857-881`) is the rung's `reprovision_fn` (`chash_rekey.py:696-699`).

## Why it matters

The two answer different questions and can diverge:
- a local-mode box whose pg_credentials are missing/unreadable => `is_local_mode()` true, `_locally_actionable` false;
- a box with readable admin creds but not configured local mode => the inverse.

Divergence means one leg of the rung runs while the other silently skips, with no diagnostic saying so. Per project directive, a correctness-relevant mode decision must not resolve two ways in one component.

Note the credential test in particular conflates capability with mode: "I can read pg_credentials" is evidence about provisioning state, not about deployment mode. Missing pg_credentials is a CORRECT state on a cloud-mode box (see `feedback_check_install_mode_before_diagnosing.md`), so the credential predicate reads a legitimate cloud box as "not locally actionable" for the right answer by accident, not by design.

## Ask

Decide which predicate is authoritative for this rung, use it in both places, and make the other a derived/asserted consistency check rather than an independent decision. If they are genuinely answering different questions, name them differently so the divergence is legible instead of looking like a duplicate.

## Scope fence

This is NOT a request to change what the rung does on any deployment today. It is a request to make the mode decision single-sourced. Behaviour change on any live path needs its own evidence.

## Origin

Found during nexus-o8dil.9's read-only sweep of chash_rekey for RDR-191 Phase 3 (which needed the local/managed split). Recorded in T2 `nexus/rdr-191-cloud-measurements` Part 2 §8. Not an observed failure.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): SUPERSEDED. Evidence: chash_rekey rung DELETED at nexus-lgdel.l1 (commit 5a3dcd16c removes src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/rungs/chash_rekey.py); both predicates gone with it

title: F8c guard scopes chash ownership to doc_ids only — a chash owned by a document OUTSIDE the reclassified set is still deleted, producing a fresh dangling manifest row
description:
Found by nexus-o8dil.6's substantive-critic pass (T2 nexus/rdr-191-o8dil6-substantive-critique-phase2-2026-08-11 [22259]). Discovered-from nexus-o8dil.2. UNCOMMITTED work — fix before the Phase 2 diff is committed.

THE DEFECT. _prune_misclassified_in_collection's new F8c manifest guard (src/nexus/indexer.py, _guarded_delete closure ~2570-2620, call sites ~2718 and ~2764) builds its chash-ownership ground truth ONLY from catalog.get_manifests(doc_ids) — the documents being reclassified in this call.

RDR-108's architecture explicitly allows one chash to be owned by MANY documents (content-addressed dedup: identical chunk text in a collection collapses to ONE row shared by every document containing it). So a document OUTSIDE doc_ids can legitimately reference the exact chash being pruned. _guarded_delete has no visibility into that outside owner: it clears doc_ids' own reference, sees no remaining reference IN ITS OWN VIEW, and deletes the T3 row — leaving the outside document with a manifest row pointing at nothing.

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT A REFINEMENT. This is F10c — the live silent data-loss bug this entire arc began with (nexus-o8dil.5: 'delete document A's chunks destroys a chunk document B still references') — RE-CREATED by the fix for its sibling F8c. It contradicts the fix's own docstring guarantee, and it falsifies GATE-2's 'zero live producers of dangling-manifest rows' bar for producer #6.

THE FIX IS NAMED AND THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS. catalog.docs_for_chashes maps chash -> [doc_id, ...] CATALOG-WIDE and is documented for exactly this hazard at src/nexus/catalog/store_hook.py:62-95. It is unused at this call site. The Java sibling fix (.40 / F8d, CatalogRepository.deleteCollectionTxn step 1b) solved the analogous scoping-asymmetry correctly by scoping COLLECTION-WIDE rather than to a document subset. Python should mirror that shape.

WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT. tests/test_o8dil2_prune_misclassified_manifest_guard.py has 4 tests and NONE has an outside-doc_ids owner case. They were RED-then-GREEN against the bug they were written for and prove nothing about this one. The regression test for this bead MUST seed a chash owned by a document outside the reclassified set and assert that document's manifest row survives intact — and must be shown RED against the current guard.

ALSO IN SCOPE, same call site (critic's Significant #1): the production call site (indexer.py:3999-4001 -> :5049) passes a make_catalog_reader() handle as catalog=, and atomic_manifest_replace (a WRITE) only works because _SharedServiceCatalogHandle.__getattr__ forwards any method with no whitelist. That bypasses factory.py's documented 'mixed sites hold both a reader and a writer' convention, and a writer (_migrate_writer) is ALREADY in scope at that call site, unused. Use the writer. This is latent-break cleanup, not cosmetics: this repo has prior art of a catalog handle refusing operations via a closed whitelist, at which point the forwarding stops working.

NOT IN SCOPE: nexus-o8dil.45 (callers discard the server delete-count) stays separate.
close_reason: PARTIALLY SHIPPED in 831a4e81, deliberately. The catalog_writer threading is kept (routes atomic_manifest_replace through _migrate_writer instead of a reader handle's unwhitelisted __getattr__, now test-distinguished, which nothing did before). The _outside_owned_ids catalog-wide docs_for_chashes pre-check was REMOVED after critique: correctness never depended on it (the server anti-join refuses the delete), its only beneficiary was a progress-bar postfix with no downstream consumer, and this function had already been optimised away from that round-trip class at a measured 226s / ~11% of wall. Paying measured cost for a cosmetic number behind a guarantee that already holds is the wrong trade. This bead's original P0 framing was mine and was wrong on two counts — see the correction comment.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, 2026-08-11 — THIS BEAD AS FILED OVERSTATES THE DEFECT TWICE. Read this before acting on the description.

I filed it from the substantive-critic's Critical without verifying two load-bearing claims. Both are false.

FALSE CLAIM 1: 'F10c re-created by the fix'. The PRE-FIX code called _batched_delete(col, present_ids) and _batched_delete(col, existing['ids']) UNCONDITIONALLY, with no manifest consultation whatsoever (verified from the diff). The new guard therefore STRICTLY SHRINKS the producer set — it protects doc_ids' own owners where nothing protected anyone before. It re-creates nothing. Scoping to doc_ids is PRE-EXISTING, exactly as the parallel code-review-expert pass said (it rated this Low, not Critical).

FALSE CLAIM 2: 'the T3 row is deleted anyway, producing a dangling manifest row'. It is not deleted. Verified by tracing the actual path: _batched_delete -> col.delete -> _ServiceCollectionStub.delete (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1295) -> POST /v1/vectors/store-delete -> VectorHandler.handleStoreDelete -> PgVectorRepository.delete, which since nexus-o8dil.5 (commit 936e05a0) is ANTI-JOIN SCOPED and REFUSES to delete any chunk a live catalog_document_chunks row still references. An outside owner's manifest row is exactly such a reference. The engine backstops the client guard's blind spot. This is what the code reviewer meant by 'eventual consistency holds'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is not P0:
1. The client-side guard is ADVISORY, not authoritative — correctness rests on the engine's anti-join. That is defence-in-depth worth having, not a live data-loss path.
2. The real residual is COUNT DISHONESTY plus pointless work: _batched_delete returns len(batch), the REQUESTED count, so when the engine refuses a refused id is still counted as pruned. That is nexus-o8dil.45's scope, already tracked, not this bead's.
3. Using catalog.docs_for_chashes (catalog-wide) would let the client decide correctly instead of issuing deletes the engine will refuse, and would make  honest at this call site. Still worth doing. NOT urgent, NOT data loss.

PRIORITY: dropping P0 -> P2. GATE-2 IMPACT: this does NOT block nexus-o8dil.7's 'zero live producers of dangling-manifest rows' criterion, because no dangling row is produced. The genuine GATE-2 blockers remain the ones nexus-o8dil.39's audit named: the missing system-wide regression tripwire and the live-corpus census run.

CAVEAT worth keeping: the engine-side protection requires an engine at v0.1.71+. REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION is (0,1,71) and PINNED_SERVICE_TAG derives from it, so every supported install has it — but that is the assumption the client's advisory guard is leaning on, and it should be stated wherever this is documented rather than assumed.

title: 87 SHA-pinned GitHub Actions with no Dependabot — pins rot silently and the publish action's rot only surfaces at release time
description:
2026-08-11: the conexus 7.6.0 publish failed because pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish was pinned at a 2026-02-18 commit whose bundled twine rejects Metadata-Version 2.5 (emitted by hatchling 1.32.0). Cost: a failed release run, two fix PRs (#1449, #1450) and two tag re-points before the artifact published.

MEASURED STATE OF THE REPO:
- 87 'uses:' entries across .github/workflows/*.yml are pinned by 40-char SHA.
- A handful float on tags instead: actions/checkout@v4 AND @v5, actions/cache@v5, astral-sh/setup-uv@v5 AND @v7. The convention is not uniform, and two of those disagree with themselves on version.
- There is NO .github/dependabot.yml. Nothing refreshes any of the 87 pins, ever.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN ACCEPTING: SHA pinning is the correct supply-chain choice (a tag is mutable, a SHA is not) and should be KEPT. The defect is the missing other half — nothing keeps the pins current. The publish action is the worst case in the set because it is exercised exactly once per release, so its rot is discovered at the most expensive possible moment, after the tag is already pushed.

RECOMMENDED FIX: add .github/dependabot.yml with a github-actions ecosystem entry. It preserves immutability while removing the rot, and turns 'discovered at release time' into 'a PR in the backlog'. Do NOT fix by floating the publish action to @release/v1 — that surrenders the immutability guarantee on precisely the action that handles publishing credentials.

WHILE THERE: reconcile the floating stragglers (checkout pinned at both v4 and v5 in the same repo; setup-uv at both v5 and v7).

RELATED TRAP, cost one extra cycle today and belongs in the same review: 'gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/git/ref/tags/<tag> --jq .object.sha' returns the ANNOTATED TAG OBJECT's sha, not the commit. Pinning that sha makes the action's ghcr image unresolvable ('docker: Error response from daemon: manifest unknown'). Dereference it — 'gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/<tag> --jq .sha' or 'git rev-parse <tag>^{}'. If Dependabot lands, it gets this right automatically, which is a further argument for it.
close_reason: DONE, not deferred. .github/dependabot.yml added with a grouped weekly github-actions ecosystem entry (one PR/week, not 87), merged in PR #1451. SHA pinning deliberately KEPT — the fix was the missing refresh half, not the pinning. Also in the same PR: workflow_dispatch on the Release workflow so a CI-side publish failure no longer forces a tag move. Filed and closed within the hour rather than joining the pile; the annotated-tag-vs-commit sha trap is recorded in the dependabot.yml header.

title: build-system.requires = ['hatchling'] is unbounded — a build-backend bump broke the v7.6.0 PyPI publish at the upload gate
description:
2026-08-11: the conexus 7.6.0 Release workflow FAILED at 'Publish to PyPI' with

  InvalidDistribution: Invalid distribution metadata: '2.5' is not a valid metadata version

ROOT CAUSE, verified locally not inferred: hatchling 1.32.0 emits Metadata-Version 2.5 (confirmed by reading METADATA and WHEEL out of the built dist/conexus-7.6.0-py3-none-any.whl: 'Metadata-Version: 2.5', 'Generator: hatchling 1.32.0'). The pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish pin was a 2026-02-18 commit whose bundled twine predates that metadata version. Fixed for now by bumping the pin to v1.14.2 (PR #1449). THE WHEEL WAS ALWAYS VALID — only the uploader was stale.

THE UNDERLYING DEFECT IS THIS BEAD: pyproject.toml's build-system.requires = ['hatchling'] is UNBOUNDED, so the build backend floats and can change the emitted metadata version under us at any time, on a machine we do not control, during a release. Same class as nexus-l2ku5, where an unbounded mcp>=1.0 resolved to a breaking 2.0 fresh from PyPI and killed both MCP servers for four days while every gate ran pinned to the dev venv and saw nothing.

WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT: tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh builds a wheel and installs it, but never runs twine's metadata validation, so the publish step is the FIRST execution of that check in the entire pipeline. A release can be nine-gates green and still fail at upload.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, decide deliberately:
1. Bound build-system.requires (e.g. hatchling>=1.x,<2) so the backend cannot move mid-release. Cheap, and matches the l2ku5 lesson.
2. Add a twine check to a pre-tag gate so metadata validity is exercised before the tag burns a release-workflow run. This is the stronger fix: it closes the whole class rather than this instance, and it belongs with the nexus-moht0 vacuous-gate work in spirit (a gate suite that structurally cannot see the failure mode it is supposed to prevent).

Prefer BOTH. Do not close on the action pin bump alone — that fixed the symptom on one axis and leaves the backend free to move again.
close_reason: Closed

title: nx catalog doctor --collections-drift hangs past 110s instead of failing loud when no storage-service lease exists
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 while sizing the blast radius of nexus-syfes on a live install.

REPRO: with the local storage service stopped ('nx daemon service status' -> 'No storage service lease found — is the service running?'), run:
  timeout 110 nx catalog doctor --collections-drift --json
Result: rc=124 (timed out), zero bytes on stdout, zero bytes on stderr. No error, no message, no partial output.

PROBABLE CAUSE, NOT YET CONFIRMED: the drift check reaches the engine over HTTP with no connect deadline and no pre-flight lease check, so an absent service produces a hang rather than a refusal. CONFIRM THIS BEFORE FIXING — start the service, verify the same invocation completes promptly, then stop it and verify the hang returns. Do not adopt the cause from this description.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND UX: an earlier background invocation of the same command was reported as 'completed (exit code 0)' with an empty output file. A gate that emits nothing and appears to exit clean is indistinguishable from a gate that passed — the exact shape behind the 2026-08-09 vacuous-verification cluster. collections-drift is a release-gating check (it blocked 7.6.0 via the sandbox shakedown), so a silent no-op form of it is a real risk, not a cosmetic one.

FIX SHAPE: fail loud with the same 'no storage service lease found' message the daemon status command already produces, plus a bounded connect timeout. Never a silent empty-clean.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
VERIFIED NOT A RISK TO THE 7.6.0 BATTERY (2026-08-11), so the deferral is evidence-based rather than assumed.

The hang requires a stopped storage service. The sandbox shakedown runs against a live one, and tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh sets 'set -euo pipefail' (:36), so the gate's 'nx catalog doctor --collections-drift | sed' pipeline propagates nx's exit status rather than sed's. Proof it is live: this exact gate FAILED on the nexus-syfes defect with real counts (2 named orphan rows; 6 collections registered vs 4 in T3), which a vacuous check cannot do.

A dead service mid-run would HANG, hitting the harness timeout — it cannot manufacture a false green. The defect is real for interactive CLI use; it does not undermine the release validation.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — THE MECHANISM IN THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION IS FALSE. Do not act on it.

I wrote that the hang occurs 'with the local storage service stopped'. This box has no local storage service by design: the install is CLOUD-MODE by config (nx service probe resolves https://api.conexus-nexus.com even with NX_SERVICE_URL unset in the shell; ~/.config/nexus/activate.sh documents the 2026-07-02 conexus-9gs cutover of T2+T3 to the managed service). 'nx daemon service status' reporting no lease, and pg_credentials being absent, are both CORRECT states for a cloud-mode install — not evidence of an outage. I misread them as a broken local install.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY OBSERVED, with the false framing removed: 'nx catalog doctor --collections-drift --json' against the CLOUD service (api.conexus-nexus.com, release_version 0.1.69) ran past a 110s timeout, rc=124, with zero bytes on both stdout and stderr. An earlier background invocation of the same command was reported as 'completed (exit code 0)' with an empty output file.

That is a more serious observation than the one originally filed, not a lesser one: a release-gating check hanging silently against the production managed service. The probable cause named originally (no pre-flight lease check, no connect deadline) was inferred from the wrong premise and should be re-derived from scratch. Reproduce against the cloud before hypothesising.

title: Nothing deregisters a catalog_collections row when a collection drains to zero chunks via gc_restore_rereferenced or gc_expire_quarantine — same drift signature nexus-syfes closes, different path
description:
Deferred from the stacked review of nexus-syfes (substantive-critic significant #3; not covered by code-review-expert).

nexus-syfes closes the path where a quarantine sibling is REGISTERED without ever receiving rows. The symmetric gap is untouched: a collection that legitimately received rows and later drains back to zero keeps its catalog_collections projection row forever. Two live paths reach it — gc_restore_rereferenced restoring ALL quarantined rows back to the origin (emptying the quarantine sibling), and gc_expire_quarantine hard-deleting all expired rows.

Both produce the identical 'nx catalog doctor --collections-drift' projection_not_in_t3 signature that blocked the 7.6.0 release, so this can re-red the same gate through a door the fix does not cover.

NOT release-blocking for 7.6.0: reaching it requires a full drain, which the sandbox shakedown corpus does not produce (nothing deleted, grace window unexpired). Confirm that claim before relying on it.

Design note before fixing: deregistration is NOT simply symmetric with registration — the collection may still be referenced by catalog_document_chunks manifest rows, topic_assignments, or chash_index, all of which carry FKs to catalog_collections. A drain-to-zero deregistration must anti-join against every referencing table, not just count chunks. See RDR-191 F17 on repairs that reason about one side of a join only.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
VERIFIED NOT REACHABLE IN THE 7.6.0 BATTERY (2026-08-11). The original filing deferred this on an UNVERIFIED assumption; this is the confirmation.

tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh never invokes gc_restore_rereferenced or gc_expire_quarantine — the only occurrence of the string 'quarantine' in the whole harness is a source path at :474 (src/nexus/catalog/chunk_quarantine.py), not a call. No drain-to-zero path executes, so this cannot re-red the collections-drift gate during the release battery.

Still a real defect for production installs where restore/expire do run.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-11 — absorbing nexus-hzysz and nexus-yjfzm, which are the same unit of work seen from different angles: a catalog_collections row that outlives its referent. Whoever builds the deregistration path should handle all three in one change.

FROM nexus-hzysz (P3, closed as folded): TaxonomyRepository.renameCollection (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TaxonomyRepository.java:856) registers newCol unconditionally, then UPDATEs topics/taxonomy_meta/topic_assignments from oldCol. A rename matching zero rows leaves newCol registered with nothing pointing at it. Read-derived, never observed; a rename normally follows a real T3 rename in which newCol legitimately has chunks. Audit finding: the other seven ensureCollectionRegistered call sites in that file are SAFE — each is followed in the same transaction by a write that references the collection.

FROM nexus-yjfzm (P3, closed as folded): rows already minted on boxes that ran published engine-service-v0.1.70 (the defective unconditional registration). Exposure is near-zero — v0.1.70 was never deployed (cloud served 0.1.69 throughout) and never pinned by a release (7.6.0 ships v0.1.71), so it is dev boxes and discarded sandboxes only. The sweep belongs in the same change as the deregistration path rather than as standalone cleanup. Note delete_collection_projection (http_catalog_client.py:2527) is a STUB that only logs — there is no client-side path to remove such a row today, so remediation needs engine-side deletion or direct SQL.

THE COMMON FIX: deregistration is not symmetric with registration. A row may still be referenced by catalog_document_chunks, topic_assignments, or chash_index, all carrying FKs to catalog_collections. Any removal must anti-join every referencing table, not just count chunks (RDR-191 F17: repairs that reason about one side of a join only).

title: [bug] local-index-memory-gate health poll swallows a JSON parse error into print("") — a SILENT FALLBACK on a correctness decision that turned a one-line error into 60s of opaque polling and a verdict accusing a healthy service
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, second failed attempt to run the local-index memory gate.
Source: T2 [22181] `nexus/local-index-memory-gate-run-post-repair`.
**This is the more important of the two gate findings** (the sibling being nexus-cwc8w, the
parse bug). The parse bug is one line; this is a directive violation sitting
inside the gate that was JUST repaired to remove exactly this class.

## Established

`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:666-667`:

    except Exception:
        print("")

A JSON parse failure on the health payload is converted into the empty string,
which is then compared against `"ok"` (`:669`) and silently treated as
"not healthy yet". No line is printed, no counter is bumped, nothing
distinguishes "parsed, service reports degraded" from "could not parse at all".

Consequence, observed on the real run: a **one-line JSON parse error** became
**60 seconds of opaque polling** (30 attempts x 2s sleep) terminating in
`_die "service never became healthy"` (`:679`) — a verdict that **ACCUSED A
HEALTHY SERVICE**. The preserved `health-poll.log` shows all 30 attempts
returned `rc=0` with `"health": "ok"` in the payload. Had the parse failed
loud, diagnosis would have been immediate instead of requiring a separate
investigation session.

A second instance of the same shape is at `:606-607` (the
`_COMBINED_WRITE_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S` introspection probe). That one is arguably
benign — the empty result is explicitly branched on at `:609-618` with a `note`
emitted — but it should be reviewed in the same pass rather than left as a
copy-paste template for the next probe.

## Why this is a directive violation, stated plainly

Standing directive: **no silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems — FAIL
LOUD.** The health decision is correctness-relevant: it gates whether the gate
proceeds at all, and its failure mode is a verdict that blames the wrong
component.

This is a **fresh instance of the success-shaped-emptiness / silent-fallback
class inside the gate that was just repaired to remove that very class.** The
repair (nexus-wbeyi) existed because the old poll could report a DEAD service
as healthy; the repaired poll reports a HEALTHY service as dead, by the same
mechanism — a decision derived from a value that means "I don't know" being
treated as if it meant a definite answer. Fixing the parse (sibling bead) makes
this instance stop firing; it does NOT remove the class from the file.

## Cross-references — the same class, already tracked elsewhere

- nexus-wbeyi (P1, open) — the poll's PREVIOUS false-clean failure, and the
  explicit note that a naive fix would make a dead service read as healthy.
- nexus-epj0b (P2, open) — `auth-login.sh` prints "No credentials found" and
  exits 0; failure indistinguishable from success.
- nexus-poplq (P2, open) — e2e `run.sh` reports "0 passed, 0 failed" exit 0 on
  a scenario mismatch; no executed-work floor.
- nexus-i1oh4 (P2, open) — `cloud-client-path-gate.sh` counts only failures, so
  a leg that never ran prints PASSED.
- nexus-okbr8 (P2, open) — `upgrade-shakeout.sh` step 11 renders a skip as a
  pass inside a journey gate.
- nexus-3znzn (P2, open) — sweep for tests that PIN fail-open behaviour.
- nexus-v2mdd (P1, open) — two fail-open-to-GREEN surfaces degrading together.

## Ask

1. Make the parse failure FAIL LOUD: distinguish "payload unparseable" from
   "service reports not-ok". Unparseable should abort with the raw payload in
   the message, or at minimum print a per-attempt diagnostic naming the parse
   error — never fold into the same empty value as a legitimate degraded
   health state.
2. Review `:606-607` in the same pass and either justify it in-line or apply
   the same treatment.
3. Sweep the rest of this file for other `except Exception:` -> benign-default
   conversions on correctness-relevant decisions and record the verdicts.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a deliberately unparseable payload, the gate FAILS within one attempt
  with a message naming the parse failure — not after 30 attempts, and not
  with a message about the service's health.
- With a legitimately degraded payload (`"health": "db-down"`), the gate still
  polls and still reports the health-based verdict. The two must not collapse.
- **Measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix**: re-introduce the
  silent `print("")` and confirm the new assertion/self-test case goes RED. If
  it stays green, the repair is theatre — which is precisely the finding this
  bead records.
acceptance_criteria: An unparseable payload FAILS within one attempt with a message naming the parse failure; a legitimately degraded payload (health=db-down) still polls and still reports the health-based verdict — the two must not collapse; and the detector is MEASURED against a deliberately broken fix (re-introduce the silent print("") and confirm RED).
close_reason: Health-poll parser extracted as _health_from_status_json: raw_decode scan tolerates log-line-prefixed payloads; unparseable rc=0 payload dies immediately with the named cause (PARSE_ERROR sentinel, never a silent empty). 6 self-test cases; RED/GREEN on both beads. Commit be441d8c2.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Fixed 2026-08-18 (both beads in one edit, same site): the poll's inline json.load/except-print("") replaced by the extracted _health_from_status_json helper.

- cwc8w half: parser scans for the first parseable JSON OBJECT (json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode walk), so a structlog warning line prepended to stdout (nexus-f93r1 product defect, e.g. the gate's own NX_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP override) no longer defeats parsing.
- 9dua3 half: no JSON object anywhere -> loud PARSE_ERROR sentinel; the poll _dies immediately on an rc=0-but-unparseable payload (structural, not transient), naming the cause and STATUS_LOG -- never 60s of opaque polling.

GREEN: --self-test now carries 6 parser cases, all PASS (including the two bead specimens).
RED (pre-fix shape, both specimens): old parser returns '' for BOTH the log-line+JSON payload (healthy service read as not-healthy) and pure garbage (parse failure indistinguishable from degraded) -- reproduced 2026-08-18 with the verbatim pre-fix snippet.

title: [bug] local-index-memory-gate health poll cannot parse a --json payload preceded by a stdout log line — the gate's own cap-override env var makes every payload unparseable, aborting at 3/6 against a healthy service
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, second failed attempt to run the local-index memory gate.
Source: T2 [22181] `nexus/local-index-memory-gate-run-post-repair`.

## Established

`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:662-667` parses the health payload with
a bare `json.load(sys.stdin)`:

    HEALTH="$(printf '%s' "$STATUS_JSON" | "$VENV/bin/python" -c '
    import json, sys
    try:
        print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("health", ""))
    except Exception:
        print("")
    ')"

The payload it is fed is NOT clean JSON. `_nx()` (`:576-587`) sets
`NX_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP="$CAP"` on **every** invocation, which makes
`nx daemon service status --json` prepend a structlog warning line to stdout
(**nexus-f93r1**, the product defect — this bead depends on it). `json.load` raises, the fallback yields
`HEALTH=""`, `"ok"` is never seen, 30 polls burn 60s, and the run dies at
step 3/6 with `_die "service never became healthy"` (`:679`) — against a
service whose own captured payload said `"health": "ok"` in all 30 attempts
(`health-poll.log`: 30 headers, 30 `rc=0`, 30 `"health": "ok"`).

The gate is self-defeating by construction: the warning's own note text names
`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh` as its expected caller.

## Why the previous repair missed it (both mechanisms were in its own UNPROVEN list)

1. The healthy arm was verified only against SYNTHETIC JSON payloads with no
   warning preamble (flagged as UNPROVEN item 3 in the repair note).
2. The dead-service proof passed because `rc != 0` short-circuits at
   `:660` BEFORE the parse ever runs.

So the one path that mattered — real live service, real `--json`, real env var
— is the one path never exercised. Same shape as the pre-repair failure
(nexus-wbeyi): verified everywhere except in situ.

## Relationship to the product defect

This is BLOCKING for the gate but **subsumed if nexus-f93r1's structural fix lands**
(route pre-`configure_logging` emissions to stderr) — with a clean stdout the
existing parse would succeed unchanged. Filed separately because (a) the gate
must not depend on an unshipped product fix to run, and (b) a parser that
assumes a pristine payload is fragile regardless: the nexus-f93r1 class is broader than
this one env var.

## Ask

1. Extract the JSON substring rather than assuming a clean payload
   (`JSONDecoder().raw_decode` from the first `{`, the same remedy applied in
   nexus-uu0vg / nexus-xdt7o), OR consume the payload from a source that
   cannot carry log lines.
2. Pair it with the fail-loud change tracked separately (D8 bead) — extraction
   alone still swallows a genuinely malformed payload.
3. If nexus-f93r1 lands first, keep the hardening anyway and say so in the code
   comment; do not revert to a bare `json.load`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The gate reaches step 4/6 on a real run with `NX_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP`
  set, against a live healthy service. This is the only evidence that counts —
  a synthetic-payload self-test is exactly what failed to catch it twice.
- **Measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix**: feed the poll a
  payload with a prepended log line AND a payload that is genuinely
  unparseable, and confirm the first is accepted while the second FAILS the
  run. A change that makes both pass has re-created the false-clean class this
  gate exists to catch (cf. nexus-wbeyi, where the naive fix would have made a
  DEAD service read as healthy).
acceptance_criteria: The gate reaches step 4/6 on a REAL run with NX_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP set against a live healthy service (synthetic-payload self-tests do not count — they missed it twice); and the detector is MEASURED against a deliberately broken fix: a log-line-prefixed payload is accepted while a genuinely unparseable one FAILS the run.

title: [E] MinerU is asserted by exit code ALONE — extractor=auto can silently route away and still exit 0, nothing asserts which extractor ran, and --check-mineru is called by no gate
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven** that no assertion identifies the extractor. **[NE]** whether
MinerU has actually been silently bypassed in a real release run — never measured, because
nothing records it.

## The claim being audited

AGENTS.md step 6c and `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:199-205` both state that
`release-sandbox.sh shakedown` is "the ONLY gate that exercises MinerU end-to-end through
the production `nx index pdf` path (step 3b of 11)".

## Why the claim is unbacked

- `tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:560-564` (step 3b) passes `extractor="auto"`.
- `src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py:875-896` routes AWAY from MinerU on a `_has_formulas_quick`
  regression or a Docling probe exception, and **still exits 0**.
- Nothing in the shakedown asserts WHICH extractor ran.

So a MinerU outage, a version drift, a server that never started — any of these degrade the
step to a different extractor and the gate reports green. The release then ships on the
belief that MinerU was exercised.

- `nx doctor --check-mineru` EXISTS (`src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:1478-1480`) and the
  shakedown never calls it.
- The pytest counterpart (`tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py:488`
  `test_mineru_path_preserves_formulas`) is deselected everywhere — including from the
  nightly `-m slow` leg (`local-service-gate-nightly.yml:283`).

Net: MinerU end-to-end is asserted by exit code alone, on both the gate path and the pytest
path.

## Prior art — read before starting

nexus-6xkdu (closed P1) removed the `|| true` that made steps 2/3a/3b/4 unable to redden
the run. That was necessary and not sufficient: the steps can now fail, but they cannot
detect a silent extractor substitution because nothing looks at the extractor.

Also relevant: nexus-24oe4 (closed) — "MinerU server pid file proved liveness, not
identity". Same distinction, one layer down.

## Scope

- Assert the extractor identity in step 3b (structured log field, `--extractor mineru`
  explicitly, or a post-hoc assertion on the run record) so a route-away reddens the run.
- Call `nx doctor --check-mineru` in the shakedown and read its rc.
- Decide the fate of `test_mineru_path_preserves_formulas` — see the `-m slow` docs bead;
  it is the single test with no executing runner anywhere in the repo.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix

This bead is NOT done when the gate is changed. It is done when the CHANGED gate has been
SHOWN FAILING against a deliberately broken input, and that demonstration is recorded
(a test fixture, a `--self-test` arm, or a pasted RED transcript pasted into this bead).

1. Construct the break the assertion claims to catch — delete the producer, corrupt the
   value, empty the filter output, skip the leg, plant the regression.
2. Run the gate. It MUST go RED, and the message MUST name the real cause.
3. Repair the break. Run again. It MUST go GREEN.
4. Paste both runs here.

A fix that has only ever been observed green does not count as done.

Rationale (2026-08-10): this session produced a gate that was committed, reviewed and dead
on arrival because nobody ran it, and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after being swept
across 12 sites. The demonstration is the deliverable, not the diff.

---

comments.text:
Fixed 2026-08-18 per the bead's 3-item scope:

title: [E] fresh-install-mvv --published without an explicit version asserts nothing about which version PyPI served; markdown-search literal is satisfied by the store-put doc; 9/9 non-vacuity leg is -s only
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven** for each item; `--published` version-check absence verified
by reading the guard conditions.

`tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh` — the VIRGIN-journey gate (nexus-nolqs), release-battery
step 1b.

## A. `--published` with no explicit version asserts nothing about what PyPI served

This is the documented post-tag SHAKEDOWN form (T2 `nexus/shakedown-playbook` §2 S1) and
the highest-consequence item here.

- `:293` gates the dist-info version comparison on `[ -n "$PUBLISHED_VERSION" ]`.
- `:452-457` only PRINTS the installed version.

So `./tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh --published` (no version) after a publish that
silently did not land will happily validate the PREVIOUS release and print PASSED. The one
gate whose entire job is "did the artifact actually reach PyPI" does not check which
artifact it got.

## B. the markdown-search literal is satisfied by the wrong document

`:377-379` ("search returns the indexed markdown") greps for `fresh-mvv`. The store-put
document's own title is `fresh-mvv-sentinel` (`:322`), which satisfies that substring. The
discriminating literal `fresh-mvv-markdown-note` IS used for the catalog leg at `:370` —
so the right literal exists in the file and the search leg uses the weak one.

## C. the "9/9 non-vacuity" leg is `-s` only

`:439-449` checks `[ -s "$LOGS/$f" ]` over 7-8 files. Every one of them already has a real
content assertion earlier in the script, so this leg adds nothing; and a log containing
only a traceback satisfies `-s`.

## D. dead branch

`:434-437`: with `ALLOWLIST_REGEX` a no-match sentinel (`:427`), any warning exits at
`:432`, so the allowlisted-warning echo at `:434-437` is unreachable.

## E. env asymmetry — the nexus-l2ku5 class is only half-closed

`--published` installs through `_uv_sandboxed` (`:188-196`, `env -i`). The DEFAULT
local-wheel layer does NOT: `:230`, `:236-237` run with the operator's ambient `UV_*` /
`PIP_INDEX_URL` / uv cache. nexus-enfoh (closed) fixed the `--published` half. The
local-wheel half was not in that sweep.

nexus-l2ku5 is the precedent that makes this matter: `mcp>=1.0` unbounded resolved to
`mcp` 2.0.0 fresh from PyPI and killed both MCP servers for four days, while every gate ran
pinned to the dev venv and saw nothing.

## Scope

A is required. B and E are cheap and worth doing in the same pass. C and D are hygiene.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix

This bead is NOT done when the gate is changed. It is done when the CHANGED gate has been
SHOWN FAILING against a deliberately broken input, and that demonstration is recorded
(a test fixture, a `--self-test` arm, or a pasted RED transcript pasted into this bead).

title: [E] scheduled_workflow_watchdog filters on on.schedule and is structurally BLIND to dispatch-only workflows — it cannot see the class it exists to catch
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven structurally.** The filter is the blindness.

## The finding

`scripts/scheduled_workflow_watchdog.py:68-88`, `scheduled_paths()`:

    triggers = doc.get("on", doc.get(True))
    if isinstance(triggers, dict) and "schedule" in triggers:
        out[f".github/workflows/{path.name}"] = path

The watchdog only ever considers workflows that ALREADY carry a `schedule:` block. A
workflow whose NAME promises a weekly cadence but whose `on:` block is
`workflow_dispatch:` only is invisible to it **by construction**.

That is precisely the population the watchdog exists to protect against: the workflows
whose names lie are exactly the ones it cannot see. Three live instances today —
`era-hop-mvv.yml` (nexus-4viey), `guided-upgrade-mvv.yml` (sibling bead), and
`plan-schema-check.yml`'s weaker "on every pull request" claim.

## Credit where due — this module is otherwise the good shape

It already handles the Norway problem (`doc.get(True)`), treats an unparseable workflow as
a finding rather than a skip (`:82`), treats `nothing-to-watch` as a FINDING kind, and has
its own test file. This is a coverage gap in a well-built detector, not a bad detector.

## Scope

Add a fourth finding kind keyed on `name:` vs the `on:` block — e.g. `name-claims-cadence`:

- workflow `name` contains a cadence word (`weekly`, `nightly`, `daily`, `hourly`,
  `on every`, `on ... changes`) but `on:` lacks the corresponding trigger
  (`schedule` / `push` / `pull_request` / `paths`).
- Emit as a finding with the claimed-vs-actual pair in the detail line.

Deliberately keyword-based and therefore approximate — that is fine; a false positive
costs one rename, a false negative costs a journey nobody runs for months.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix

This bead is NOT done when the gate is changed. It is done when the CHANGED gate has been
SHOWN FAILING against a deliberately broken input, and that demonstration is recorded
(a test fixture, a `--self-test` arm, or a pasted RED transcript pasted into this bead).

1. Construct the break the assertion claims to catch — delete the producer, corrupt the
   value, empty the filter output, skip the leg, plant the regression.
2. Run the gate. It MUST go RED, and the message MUST name the real cause.
3. Repair the break. Run again. It MUST go GREEN.
4. Paste both runs here.

A fix that has only ever been observed green does not count as done.

Rationale (2026-08-10): this session produced a gate that was committed, reviewed and dead
on arrival because nobody ran it, and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after being swept
across 12 sites. The demonstration is the deliverable, not the diff.

title: cloud-client-path-gate.sh counts only failures — a leg that silently did not run contributes nothing and the gate prints PASSED
description:
Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §B3. Tagged [E]; re-verified against the tree 2026-08-10.

## THE SHAPE — success-shaped emptiness

One of four instances of a single defect class filed together: **a gate that passes when it did nothing**. A leg that silently did not run contributes nothing to the verdict, so absent work reads as clean work. The pattern matters more than any individual instance — whoever fixes one should fix the shape.

Family: `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh` (this), `tests/e2e/auth-login.sh` (nexus-epj0b), `tests/e2e/run.sh` (nexus-poplq), `tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` (nexus-okbr8). Adjacent prior art: nexus-ogzsz, nexus-eu2sg, nexus-3znzn, nexus-wbeyi, nexus-c7fht.

## This instance

The gate counts ONLY failures. There is no count of legs that RAN.

VERIFIED, exact — `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh`:

    :59   # Exit 0 == CLOUD CLIENT-PATH GATE PASSED (literal sentinel on last line).
    :61   set -euo pipefail
    :66   # Legs accumulate violations instead of fail-fast: a red run is relay
    :67   # evidence, and "which legs are broken" is the payload.
    :68   VIOLATIONS=0
    :69   _leg_fail() { echo "  LEG FAILED: $*" >&2; VIOLATIONS=$((VIOLATIONS + 1)); }
    :70   _fail() { echo "CLOUD CLIENT-PATH GATE FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
    ...
    :175  if [ "$VIOLATIONS" -gt 0 ]; then
    :176      _fail "$VIOLATIONS leg(s) violated — the public edge does not deliver the engine's pinned client contract"
    :177  fi
    :178  echo "CLOUD CLIENT-PATH GATE PASSED"

The accumulate-don't-fail-fast design at :66-69 is deliberate and good — a red run enumerating every broken leg is better relay evidence than a fail-fast. The defect is that the verdict at :175 is a function of VIOLATIONS ALONE. Nothing observes how many legs executed.

Consequence: if a leg is skipped, guarded out, silently swallowed, or removed by an edit, VIOLATIONS stays 0 for that leg and the gate prints PASSED. Zero violations means "no leg reported a violation", which is true both when every leg ran clean and when no leg ran at all. The two are not distinguished anywhere.

This gate is load-bearing: per AGENTS.md it is the ONLY thing that asserts the engine's pinned contracts survive the PUBLIC edge, and it exists because on 2026-07-23 (nexus-bwulw) three client features shipped green through every engine-direct gate while the edge stubbed /version and auth-gated /health. A gate carrying that history must not be able to pass on silence.

## Ask

Add an OBSERVED-VS-EXPECTED leg assert. Generalize the shape already used by `local-service-gate.sh` (counted FLOOR/BUDGET pinned to a dated empirical run):

1. Count legs that RAN (`LEGS_RAN`), not only legs that failed. Each leg increments on entry.
2. Declare the expected leg count as a literal constant with a dated rationale comment.
3. The verdict becomes `VIOLATIONS == 0 AND LEGS_RAN == EXPECTED_LEGS`. A shortfall is a FINDING with its own message, distinct from a violation — "the gate did not run its full battery" is a different fact from "the edge is broken", and the relay needs to tell them apart.
4. Emit the counts on the terminal sentinel line so the result is greppable: e.g. `CLOUD CLIENT-PATH GATE PASSED — legs=N violations=0`.

Note the two legs that already print `ok [C]` / `ok [D]` (`:157`, `:165`) are inside a Python heredoc whose own `sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)` feeds the shell — the leg-ran counter must be incremented on the SHELL side, on entry, so a heredoc that dies before reaching either branch still counts as a leg that failed to complete rather than a leg that quietly did not run.

Related, same class, same script family: T2 [22176] §B3 also notes `release-sandbox.sh` has no assert that its 11 steps ran. That half is out of scope here; file separately if not already covered.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions)

- [ ] `LEGS_RAN` counted on entry per leg; expected count declared as a literal with dated rationale.
- [ ] Verdict requires BOTH zero violations AND the full leg count; shortfall message is distinct from the violation message.
- [ ] Terminal sentinel carries the counts and stays greppable.
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Comment out or short-circuit ONE leg, run the gate, and demonstrate it going RED with the shortfall message (not the violation message). Paste the red output. Then restore and demonstrate green with `legs=N`. Both directions, both pasted.
- [ ] Non-vacuity: demonstrate the gate still goes RED via the ordinary violation path too (a leg that runs and fails), so the new floor has not displaced the original check.

## Rationale for the acceptance bar

2026-08-10 produced a gate committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it; and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after a 12-site sweep. This gate's own origin story (nexus-bwulw) is three features shipping green past every gate that never looked at the right surface. Only an executed red distinguishes the fix from the disease.

title: e2e run.sh: a --scenario mismatch runs nothing and reports 'Results: 0 passed, 0 failed' exit 0 — no executed-work floor
description:
Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §B2. Tagged [E]; re-verified against the tree 2026-08-10.

## THE SHAPE — success-shaped emptiness

One of four instances of a single defect class filed together: **a gate that passes when it did nothing**. A run that executed nothing is indistinguishable from a run that executed everything and passed. The pattern matters more than any individual instance — whoever fixes one should fix the shape.

Family: `tests/e2e/run.sh` (this), `tests/e2e/auth-login.sh` (nexus-epj0b), `tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` (nexus-okbr8), `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh`. Adjacent prior art: nexus-ogzsz, nexus-eu2sg, nexus-3znzn, nexus-wbeyi, nexus-c7fht.

## This instance

A typo'd `--scenario` number produces `Results: 0 passed, 0 failed` and exit 0.

VERIFIED, exact — `tests/e2e/run.sh`:

    :22   ONLY_SCENARIO=""
    :34   --scenario)   ONLY_SCENARIO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    :213  run_scenario() {
    :216      num=$(basename "$file" | cut -d_ -f1)
    :217      if [[ -n "$ONLY_SCENARIO" && "$num" != "$ONLY_SCENARIO" ]]; then
    :218          return 0
    :219      fi
    :227  for scenario_file in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/scenarios/[0-9]*.sh; do
    :228      run_scenario "$scenario_file"
    :229  done
    :232  summary

and `tests/e2e/lib.sh`:

    :11   PASS=0
    :12   FAIL=0
    :13   SKIP=0
    :235  summary() {
    ...       echo " Results: ${PASS} passed, ${FAIL} failed${skip_suffix}"
    :244      [[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]

(T2 [22176] cited `run.sh:217`; :217 is the `if`, :218 is the `return 0`. Substance unaffected.)

Trace: `--scenario 07` when the file is `7_foo.sh` (or any typo, or a renamed/deleted scenario) matches nothing. Every `run_scenario` call returns 0 without sourcing anything. PASS and FAIL both stay at their :11-12 initial 0. `summary`'s verdict is `[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]` — TRUE when FAIL is 0 because nothing ran. The harness prints `Results: 0 passed, 0 failed` and exits 0.

There is no assertion anywhere that `--scenario` matched a real file, and no floor on PASS.

## Ask

1. A `--scenario` value that matches no scenario file must FAIL LOUD (nonzero, named reason listing the available scenario numbers). An unmatched selector is a caller error, not an empty result set.
2. `summary` must require an executed-work floor: `PASS + FAIL + SKIP > 0`, and a zero-total run is a FINDING, not a pass. This is the generalization of the shape and is the half that also covers scenario-glob breakage, a moved `scenarios/` dir, and a `[0-9]*.sh` pattern that stops matching.

Precedent to copy: `expectations.sh` rc contract (0 clean / 1 BLINDSPOT false-clean / 2 real deficit / 3 nothing checkable) — "absence of a ledger is absence of EVIDENCE, not evidence of cleanliness". And `local-service-gate.sh`'s counted FLOOR/BUDGET pinned to a dated empirical run.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions)

- [ ] `./tests/e2e/run.sh --scenario <nonexistent>` exits nonzero with a named reason.
- [ ] `summary` fails on a zero-total run, independently of the selector fix.
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Run with a deliberately bogus `--scenario` value and paste the nonzero exit. Separately, temporarily point the glob at an empty directory and demonstrate `summary` going RED on `PASS=0 FAIL=0`. Both pasted. The zero-total floor must be observed failing, not merely written.
- [ ] Non-vacuity of the fix itself: demonstrate that a VALID `--scenario` still runs exactly one scenario and still passes — a floor that makes the normal path fail is not a fix.

## Rationale for the acceptance bar

2026-08-10 produced a gate committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it; and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after a 12-site sweep. This bead's subject is literally "a run that executed nothing reports success" — the fix must be shown executing something.

title: auth-login.sh prints 'No credentials found' and EXITS 0 — failure is indistinguishable from success to any caller
description:
Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §A4/§B2. Tagged [E]; re-verified against the tree 2026-08-10.

## THE SHAPE — success-shaped emptiness

This is one of four instances of a single defect class filed together: **a gate that passes when it did nothing**. Failure and no-op are indistinguishable to the caller. The pattern matters more than any individual instance — whoever fixes one should fix the shape.

Family (this bead is one of four): `tests/e2e/auth-login.sh` (this), `tests/e2e/run.sh` scenario mismatch, `tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` skip-as-pass (nexus-okbr8), `tests/e2e/cloud-client-path-gate.sh` failure-only counting. Adjacent prior art in the same class: nexus-ogzsz, nexus-eu2sg, nexus-3znzn, nexus-wbeyi, nexus-c7fht.

## This instance

`tests/e2e/auth-login.sh` prints a failure message and exits 0.

VERIFIED, exact:

    :13   set -euo pipefail
    :114  if [[ -f "$AUTH_DIR/.credentials.json" ]]; then
    :115      echo "✓ Credentials saved to tests/e2e/.claude-auth/.credentials.json"
    :116      echo "  Run: ./tests/e2e/run.sh"
    :118  else
    :119      echo "✗ No credentials found — did you complete login and /exit?"
    :120      echo "  Tip: credentials are saved to ~/.claude/.credentials.json inside the container"
    :121  fi        <- LAST LINE OF FILE (121 total)

The `fi` at :121 is EOF. There is no `exit 1` on the failure branch and no trailing exit. The script's status is the status of the last `echo`, which is 0. `set -euo pipefail` at :13 does not help: nothing fails, the script simply reports failure in prose and reports success in its exit code.

(T2 [22176] recorded this as `:117-121`; the failure branch is actually `:119-120` inside the `:114-121` block. Substance unaffected.)

Consequence: any caller, wrapper, CI step or human running `./tests/e2e/auth-login.sh && ...` proceeds as if credentials were obtained. The one legible signal — the ✗ line — is visible only to a human reading stdout at the moment it scrolls past.

## Note on classification

T2 [22176] §B2 raises a live alternative: `auth-login.sh` may be a SETUP HELPER rather than a gate, in which case "nothing says so" is itself the defect. Either resolution is acceptable:
- (a) it is a gate → `exit 1` on the failure branch, plus a greppable terminal sentinel;
- (b) it is a setup helper → say so in its own header, and remove it from any context that treats its exit code as a verdict.
What is not acceptable is the current state, where it looks like a gate, prints like a gate, and cannot fail like one.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions)

- [ ] The no-credentials path exits nonzero (or the script is explicitly reclassified as a helper, in writing, in its own header).
- [ ] If it stays a gate: a greppable terminal sentinel on the success path, and a documented rc contract (each declared nonzero rc appears as a literal `exit N` in the file).
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Run the script in a sandbox with NO `.credentials.json` present and demonstrate a nonzero exit. Paste the `echo $?`. Then run it WITH credentials present and demonstrate 0. Both directions, both pasted. A fix asserted from reading the diff is exactly what this bead is about.

## Rationale for the acceptance bar

2026-08-10 produced a gate that was committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it; and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after being swept across 12 sites. In a bead whose subject is "the exit code disagrees with the prose", accepting a prose claim that the exit code was fixed would be self-parody.
