title: guided-upgrade-mvv is a SECOND workflow named 'weekly' with a dispatch-only trigger, and the x7xjj watchdog is structurally blind to both it and era-hop
description:
Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §A5. Tagged [E]; every claim below independently re-verified against the tree 2026-08-10.

This is the SECOND and THIRD instance of the shape nexus-4viey filed (era-hop), plus a distinct structural defect in the watchdog that was built to catch exactly this. Filed separately from 4viey because the watchdog blindness is its own bug with its own fix.

## Half 1 — a second workflow whose NAME advertises a cadence it does not have

VERIFIED, exact:

- `.github/workflows/era-hop-mvv.yml:1` — `name: Era-spanning upgrade hop (weekly + on ladder-path changes)`
  `:80-81` — the ENTIRE trigger block is `on:` / `workflow_dispatch:`. No schedule, no push, no path filter. (This half is nexus-4viey's subject; repeated here only because the watchdog fix must cover both files.)

- `.github/workflows/guided-upgrade-mvv.yml:1` — `name: Guided-upgrade MVV (weekly + on migration-path changes)`
  `:51-52` — the ENTIRE trigger block is `on:` / `workflow_dispatch:`.

guided-upgrade differs from era-hop in an important way: its body (`:28-51`) DOCUMENTS the dispatch-only state deliberately and correctly — "AUTOMATIC TRIGGERS REMOVED 2026-07-27 (nexus-x7xjj) ... This file stays dispatch-only as a parts-donor; do NOT restore its schedule — the journey it drives is deleted for good."

So for guided-upgrade the ask is NOT to restore a schedule. The ask is that the NAME was never updated to match a deliberate, documented, permanent decision. Line 1 still asserts "weekly + on migration-path changes" while lines 28-51 explain at length why it will never run either way. The prose header and the workflow name disagree, and the name is what shows in the Actions run list.

This is the exact failure mode T2 [22176] §4 names as the reason rationale must have ONE authoritative home: "TWO copies of a rationale is how era-hop-mvv.yml came to be titled 'weekly' while its `on:` block is dispatch-only".

## Half 2 — the watchdog built for this is structurally blind to it

`scripts/scheduled_workflow_watchdog.py` (nexus-x7xjj, CLOSED) exists precisely because scheduled gates fail silently. Its discovery function:

    :68  def scheduled_paths(workflow_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Path]:
    :78      for path in sorted(workflow_dir.glob("*.y*ml")):
    :86          if isinstance(triggers, dict) and "schedule" in triggers:
    :87              out[f".github/workflows/{path.name}"] = path

It sweeps workflows that DECLARE `on.schedule`. A workflow that lost its schedule drops silently out of the swept set — the watchdog cannot distinguish "no longer scheduled" from "never was". Two of the three workflows whose silent failures motivated building it (`era-hop-mvv`, `guided-upgrade-mvv`) are now invisible to it by construction.

The watchdog's own zero-found guard (`:100-108`, "no workflow declares an `on.schedule` trigger... this watchdog stopped recognising them") is good and does not help here: the set is non-empty, it is merely INCOMPLETE. A partial sweep passes clean.

## Ask

1. era-hop-mvv: give it the cadence its name claims, or rename to the truth (nexus-4viey owns this; listed for completeness).
2. guided-upgrade-mvv: RENAME line 1 to match the documented dispatch-only-forever decision. Do not restore its schedule (`:47-49` is explicit).
3. Watchdog: detect NAME-CLAIMS-CADENCE, not only declared schedules. Sweep the union of (a) workflows declaring `on.schedule` and (b) workflows whose `name:` contains a cadence token (weekly / nightly / daily / hourly / monthly / "on changes" / "on * changes") but whose `on:` block lacks the corresponding trigger. Report the mismatch as a FINDING. T2 [22176] §A5 proposes the registry-declared-K3-rows union as an alternative shape; either satisfies this bead as long as the two named files stop being invisible.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions)

- [ ] `guided-upgrade-mvv.yml:1` name no longer claims a cadence the file does not have.
- [ ] The watchdog reports a finding for a dispatch-only workflow whose name claims a cadence, demonstrated on the real `guided-upgrade-mvv.yml` and `era-hop-mvv.yml` BEFORE their names are fixed. Paste the finding output.
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Add a fixture workflow named "... (weekly)" with `on: workflow_dispatch:` only, run the watchdog, and demonstrate it going RED. Then flip the fixture to a real schedule and demonstrate it going green. Paste both. A detector observed only in its passing state is unmeasured.
- [ ] Non-vacuity: the union sweep must still fail on zero-found (the existing `:100-108` guard must survive the change and be shown still firing on an empty fixture dir).

## Rationale for the acceptance bar

2026-08-10 produced a gate committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it; and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after a 12-site sweep. The watchdog here is a second-order case: a detector that was built, shipped, closed (nexus-x7xjj), and then silently stopped covering two of its three original subjects. Only an executed red proves the replacement is different.

Related: nexus-4viey (first instance, era-hop — P1 open), nexus-x7xjj (the watchdog's origin bead, closed), GH #1447, T2 [22176] §A5.
close_reason: Closed

title: CI Cost Discipline is cited as project policy by 4 workflows but has ZERO hits in AGENTS.md — the citations dangle into a personal file
description:
Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §A6 ("findings discovered in passing"). Tagged [E] established; every file:line below independently re-verified against the tree 2026-08-10.

## The defect

Four CI workflows cite the CI Cost Discipline directive as PROJECT policy. The directive is not in the project file. The citations dangle.

VERIFIED:

- `grep -in "cost" AGENTS.md` returns ZERO hits (grep rc=1; AGENTS.md is 219 lines).
- `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md` (`lrwxr-xr-x CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`). So every "CLAUDE.md" citation resolves to AGENTS.md and finds nothing.
- Four citing sites, exact:
  - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:543` — "Deliberately a single small ubuntu job with NO matrix (CI cost discipline, CLAUDE.md)"
  - `.github/workflows/era-hop-mvv.yml:34` — "CI-cost discipline (CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVES): NO native GraalVM build..."
  - `.github/workflows/package-upgrade-mvv.yml:27` — "CI-cost discipline (CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVES): NO native GraalVM build..."
  - `.github/workflows/stranded-redirect-rehearsal.yml:30` — "CI-cost discipline (CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVES): NO native GraalVM build..."

The directive text lives ONLY in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, a user-global personal file. No contributor, no reviewer reading a PR diff, and no CI reader can see it. Four workflows make cost-shape decisions (no matrix, no GraalVM, weekly-not-nightly, ubuntu-only, secret-free) and justify them by pointing at a policy that, from inside the repo, does not exist.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

A cited-but-absent policy READS AS ENFORCED. A reviewer sees "(CI cost discipline, CLAUDE.md)" and treats the constraint as settled and authoritative. Nothing checks it, nothing states it, and a future edit that violates it has nothing to violate. This is the same rot class as the rest of the falsifiability findings: a surface that presents as governed while being ungoverned.

## Ask (either half is acceptable; do one)

1. Land the CI Cost Discipline directive in `AGENTS.md` as a real section, so the four citations resolve. (Preferred — the constraint is genuinely project policy in practice; four workflows already behave as if it is.)
2. OR correct the four citations to point at wherever the directive actually lives, and stop implying project-file authority.

Then, per T2 [22176] §A6, add the standing lint: every `AGENTS.md §` / `CLAUDE.md §` citation under `.github/workflows/` and `tests/e2e/` must resolve to a real heading in the target file.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions)

- [ ] All four citation sites resolve to real text in `AGENTS.md` (or are corrected), demonstrated by a command whose output is pasted into the closing note.
- [ ] The citation lint exists and is wired into an EXECUTING invocation (the `-m lint` bucket, ci.yml:579 — already a required check), not merely committed.
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Add a fixture workflow (or temporarily corrupt one citation) carrying a bogus `AGENTS.md § Nonexistent Heading` reference, run the lint, and demonstrate it going RED. Paste the red output. A lint that has never been observed failing is not evidence.
- [ ] Non-vacuity assert: the lint must FAIL if the citations-found count is zero. Scanning nothing is not the same as finding nothing wrong. (Precedent: `expectations.sh` rc=3, "absence of a ledger is absence of EVIDENCE, not evidence of cleanliness".)

## Rationale for the acceptance bar

2026-08-10 produced a gate that was committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it; and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after being swept across 12 sites. A fix demonstrated going red is the only evidence that distinguishes those outcomes from a real one.

Related: nexus-4viey (era-hop naming drift — the same workflow file, different defect), T2 [22176] §A6.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] local-index-memory-gate calls nx init with no --no-autostart and unredirected stdin — from a TTY it registers an autostart unit pointing at the /tmp install cleanup deletes
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, first real execution of `tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`
(T2 [22174]).

## The defect

    tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:552
        _nx init >"$LOGS/init.log" 2>&1 || { tail -30 "$LOGS/init.log" >&2; _die "nx init failed"; }

No `--yes`, no `--no-autostart`, and stdin is NOT redirected.

Both flags exist:

    src/nexus/commands/init.py:830-844
        --yes           "Accept the service-autostart registration non-interactively (local mode)."
        --no-autostart  "Do not register the service autostart unit; start a session ..."

and the decision point is:

    src/nexus/commands/init.py:296-317  (_decide_autostart)
        if no_autostart: return False
        <non-interactive> -> "[non-interactive: skipping service autostart registration ...]"
        return click.confirm(...)          # interactive, DEFAULT YES

## Why it matters

Non-interactively (CI, `claude -p`, redirected stdin) the gate is safe — `_decide_autostart`
takes the non-interactive branch and declines. That is how the source session's runs
behaved, so this has not yet bitten anyone.

Run from a TTY, `click.confirm` PROMPTS with default yes. An operator hitting Enter
registers a **persistent autostart unit pointing at the gate's isolated /tmp install** —
which the gate's own cleanup then deletes. The result is a launchd/systemd unit on the
user's machine pointing at a path that no longer exists.

That is a standing-directive violation in shape (don't break the live nexus install): the
gate is otherwise scrupulous about isolation — it refuses to run against
`~/.config/nexus`, it verifies the engine's `argv[0]` is the isolated mktemp binary before
any kill (`storage_service_daemon.py:748`), and the source session confirmed no gate
artifact anywhere under `~/.config/nexus`. The autostart unit is the ONE artifact that
would escape that isolation, and it escapes it durably.

Precedent that this is a real failure mode, not a hypothetical: nexus-4e96a (CLOSED P1),
"local-service-gate step 1 (`nx init --service`) auto-starts the pinned release binary,
silently making step 3's launch-artifact selection a no-op" — the same gate-invokes-init
seam producing an unintended persistent side effect.

## Ask

Invoke init explicitly non-interactive and explicitly declining the unit:

    _nx init --no-autostart </dev/null >"$LOGS/init.log" 2>&1 || ...

`--no-autostart` is the load-bearing half (it wins unconditionally at `init.py:305`);
`</dev/null` is belt-and-braces so the run is TTY-independent regardless of future
`_decide_autostart` changes. Do NOT use `--yes` — that ACCEPTS the registration.

Audit the other `_nx` call sites in the gate for the same unredirected-stdin exposure while
here.

## Non-vacuous check

Run the gate from a real TTY and assert that no autostart unit naming the isolated config
dir exists afterwards. Cheapest durable form: after `nx init` returns, assert the gate's
own log contains the non-interactive/declined marker and that no unit file under the
platform autostart location references `$ISOLATED_CONFIG_DIR`. Falsify by temporarily
dropping `--no-autostart` and confirming the assert goes RED when driven from a TTY — if it
stays green, the check is running non-interactively and is vacuous, which is exactly the
condition that hid this.

Related: nexus-97dp4, nexus-4e96a (closed, same seam), and the sibling first-run beads for
the health poll and corpus shape.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: gate now runs _nx init --no-autostart with stdin </dev/null (tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:689; commit a1b64b3cb)

title: [bug] local-index-memory-gate JSON: flushes_at_cap counts both flush families but flushes counts only chunk_flush_complete — flushes_at_cap can exceed flushes
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, first real execution of `tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`
(T2 [22174]). Not yet OBSERVED in output — no JSON line has ever been emitted, because the
gate aborts at step 3/6 (see the health-poll bead). This is a read of the emit path.

## The incoherence

The gate's JSON carries two flush counters computed over DIFFERENT event populations.

`flushes` — ChunkBatcher family ONLY:

    tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:719
        FLUSHES_TOTAL="$(_count_matches_in_log "$RUN_LOG" chunk_flush_complete)"

`flushes_at_cap` — BOTH families:

    tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:133-141  (_cap_bound_count_in_log)
        for v in $(grep -F 'chunk_flush_complete' ... ); do ... n=$((n+1)); done
        for v in $(grep -F 'http_vector_upsert_chunks_request' ... ); do ... n=$((n+1)); done

The legacy per-file paged upload emits `http_vector_upsert_chunks_request` and NO
`chunk_flush_complete`. So on any run where the legacy path binds the cap — which, per the
corpus bead, is the ONLY way this gate's current corpus binds it at all —
`flushes_at_cap > flushes`.

Emitted together on one line at `:246` / `:732-734`:

    {"peak_gb":...,"cap":16,...,"flushes":0,"flushes_at_cap":8,...}

"8 of 0 flushes reached the cap" is nonsense on its face and would mislead anyone reading
the JSON — including a future triage that treats `flushes` as the denominator.

Note `_largest_flush_in_log` (`:121-126`) already merges both families deliberately and
documents why. The bug is that `flushes` alone was NOT given the same treatment, so the two
fields silently disagree about what a "flush" is.

## Ask

Pick one and make both fields honour it:

- (preferred) count BOTH families in `flushes`, matching `flushes_at_cap` and
  `_largest_flush_in_log`; or
- emit them as four fields — `combined_flushes`, `combined_flushes_at_cap`,
  `legacy_pages`, `legacy_pages_at_cap` — which is strictly more useful given the
  combined-vs-legacy path ambiguity that motivates the corpus bead.

Either way, document in the `_emit_json` comment (`:243-246`) which event families each
field counts.

## Non-vacuous check

Extend the existing `--self-test` (which already builds synthetic logs — see the
`fake1.log` / `fake2.log` fixtures at `:275-295`) with a fixture containing ONLY
`http_vector_upsert_chunks_request count=N` events at or above the cap and ZERO
`chunk_flush_complete` events — the legacy-only shape. Assert
`flushes_at_cap <= flushes`. Against today's code that assertion goes RED
(`flushes=0, flushes_at_cap=N`); if it passes before the fix, the fixture is not
exercising the legacy-only path and is itself vacuous.

Related: nexus-97dp4, and the sibling first-run beads for the health poll and the corpus
shape.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: a1b64b3cb repaired the gate incl wizj6: flushes counters made coherent, legacy_pages_at_cap split out (local-index-memory-gate.sh:142-177)

title: Bge768ParityTest + Bge768BatchCompositionTest have no Java-side max-skip/non-vacuity assert — model-absent skip reports surefire 0/0/0/0
design:
Found during substantive-critique of commits 2b0c5908/254e3897/2b3a1635/a7553c88
(engine-embed-path-hardening-design-v0.1.70, W1/W7).

service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/Bge768BatchCompositionTest.java
(added 2b3a1635) and its sibling service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/Bge768ParityTest.java
both skip via JUnit Assumptions.assumeTrue when the bge ONNX model is absent
locally. Neither has a Java-side max-skip / non-vacuity meta-assert. Per the
class's own javadoc: "This test is the GATE for sub-batching (W2/W3) ... and
for ORT SessionOptions tuning (W9)" — i.e. it is the load-bearing precondition
for the rest of the numeric spine.

This directly violates the standing hot rule (global CLAUDE.md § Testing):
"Functional gates are self-provisioning scripts, never ambient machine state.
A gate that skip-passes when its dependency is absent must carry a max-skip /
non-vacuity assert."

The repo already has TWO precedents for exactly this mechanism:
  scripts/assert_rehearsal_ran.py
  scripts/assert_rerank_inference_ran.py (cites the identical hot-rule text
    in its own docstring, gates CrossEncoderRerankerInferenceTest the same
    way Bge768BatchCompositionTest needs)

.github/workflows/service-ci.yml's prime-bge-onnx action DOES provision the
model unconditionally on every push touching service/**, so CI itself is not
currently blind — the exposure is local-only runs and any future CI change
that drops the priming step silently, which would go undetected forever
(surefire reports 0/0/0/0, no failure).

2b3a1635's commit message calls this "a pre-existing gap shared with
Bge768ParityTest, tracked separately" — but no bead existed for it before
this one. Filing per the standing "a finding in prose becomes a bead, unasked"
directive.

Fix: a script mirroring assert_rerank_inference_ran.py's shape — parse the
surefire XML for both classes, fail if testcases==0 or any <skipped> is
present, wire it into service-ci.yml after the mvn test step.

title: T2 [22162] §2.2 derives ADMISSION_WAIT_MS against a 30s client read timeout that no longer exists — the combined-write POST is 600s since 127f2dbc, a 20x error in the input
description:
Found 2026-08-10 during the T2 [22162] correction work. **Second, independent defect in the same
sentence** as the retracted §0.3 premise — see the companion bead on that retraction. Fixing that
one alone leaves `ADMISSION_WAIT_MS` still derived from a stale input.

## The stale assumption

T2 `nexus/engine-embed-path-hardening-design-v0.1.70` (entry 22162) §2.2 justifies its
`ADMISSION_WAIT_MS = 10_000` by requiring the admission wait stay **"well under the client's read
timeout"**, and reasons explicitly against a 30s client budget:

> "Queue-forever hands the outcome to the client's 30s read timeout, which is the ONE path that
> DOES storm (up to 8 POSTs, each a fresh uncancelled embed). Bounded-wait-then-503 converts a
> would-be storm into a single clean failure, which is why `ADMISSION_WAIT_MS` must stay well
> under the client's read timeout."

## The actual timeout (verified in-tree, 2026-08-10)

```
src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:226   _COMBINED_WRITE_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S = 600.0
src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:3095      timeout=_COMBINED_WRITE_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S,
```

600s, not 30s — restored by `127f2dbc` (nexus-y9t08) and refined by `47c5a39a` (nexus-n2w4q,
which narrowed the ReadTimeout handling on this one call and converts it to
`CombinedWriteEmbedTimeoutError`). **§2.2's binding constraint is evaluated against a value 20x
smaller than the real one.**

The design was authored against the pre-fix 30s state and was correct when written. Our own client
work the same day invalidated it.

## Process observation — record this, not just the number

This is **self-inflicted, and it is the exact cross-cut a paired client+engine release is supposed
to catch before shipping**. The engine design took a client constant as an input; the client
release moved that constant; nothing connected the two. The design's own §5 backward-compat table
and §6 release section both reason about a v0.1.70 engine talking to 7.5.0 clients, and neither
notices that the client half moved underneath §2.2 in the same window.

Both defects in this one sentence — the retracted "503 is not retried" premise and this stale
timeout — were invisible for the same structural reason: **the constant was presented as a value
rather than as a function of named inputs.** A reader could not see what it depended on, so
neither dependency was re-checked when it changed. That is the generalizable lesson, and it is why
ask 2 below is not optional polish.

## Ask

1. **Re-derive `ADMISSION_WAIT_MS` against the ACTUAL current read timeout (600s), jointly with
   the §0.3 retraction.** The two corrections must land together: correcting only the retry premise
   leaves a constant sized against a 30s budget; correcting only the timeout leaves it sized on the
   belief that a 503 terminates in one response. Either alone produces a wrong number.
2. **State the derivation explicitly in the design, as a function of its named inputs** — client
   read timeout, gateway-ladder retry count and sleeps, the ChunkBatcher bisect multiplier, and the
   expected saturation drain time. A future change to any of them then has a visible dependent.
3. Note in §2.2 that the 600s budget makes "the engine decides the outcome rather than the client's
   clock" trivially satisfiable at almost any wait value, so the constraint that actually binds is
   now the amplification cost (4 POSTs per flush attempt x `2F-1` attempts), not the client clock.

## Non-vacuous check

Documentation correction, so the check is a read-back after the edit, and it must be a **detector,
not a restatement**:

- `memory_get` T2 [22162] and confirm §2.2 (a) cites 600s with the `http_catalog_client.py:226`
  reference, (b) shows the derivation as a named-input formula, not a bare number, and (c) names
  the commits (`127f2dbc`, `47c5a39a`) that moved the input, so the next reader can tell whether
  it has moved again.
- **The falsification**: take the corrected derivation, substitute the OLD 30s value, and confirm
  it yields a materially different constant. If it does not, the derivation does not actually
  depend on the input it claims to, and the correction is cosmetic.
- A §2.2 that still reads "well under the client's read timeout" with no number attached fails this
  check even if 600s appears elsewhere in the memo.

Related: the companion §0.3 retraction bead (retracted 503-is-not-retried premise, the other wrong
input to this same constant), the ChunkBatcher bisect-multiplier bead (the amplification term that
should replace the client clock as the binding constraint), nexus-y9t08 (`127f2dbc`, restored 600s),
nexus-n2w4q (`47c5a39a`, narrowed the ReadTimeout handling and quantified the 8x storm),
nexus-zu4ma and nexus-0o76a (the engine work the design covers), T2 [22168]
`nexus/engine-w0-503-client-degradation` (the W0 read that surfaced both defects).

title: index: d29244f6 leaves _ETATicker and _PhaseHeartbeat double-firing in the pre-file-loop window — meaningless '0/N files' line interleaves with the in-place heartbeat on stderr
description:
Found 2026-08-10 by code review of commit `d29244f6`, which introduced `_PhaseHeartbeat` (the
nexus-mx22w liveness guarantee) and moved `_ETATicker`'s stop point (the nexus-p7tp3 fix). The two
mechanisms now overlap in a window neither bead anticipated.

## Defect

`d29244f6` correctly stopped killing `_ETATicker` on the first `on_phase` call — in production the
first phase marker ("Registering N catalog entries…") fires **before** the per-file loop starts,
so the old latch killed the ticker within seconds of every run (nexus-p7tp3). The new stop point
is inside `on_file`, at `n >= total` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:631-640`).

The new stop point is inside `on_file`, at `n >= total` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:631-638`).

That fix is right, and it has a side effect: **the ticker is now alive for the entire pre-file-loop
window** — catalog registration, staleness cache construction, everything before the first
`on_file`. During that window `n == 0`, so the ticker's 60s tick renders its first-tick regime
(`_format_eta`, `src/nexus/commands/index.py:232-246`):

```
[eta] 0/N files · 0 chunks · no samples yet · pending
```

That regime is deliberate and correctly guarded against division by zero — but it was designed for
"the first tick before any file completes", meaning early *inside* the file loop. It now fires
during a window where the file loop has not started at all, so it conveys no pace information and
says nothing the phase marker did not already say.

Meanwhile `_PhaseHeartbeat` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:326`) is armed by that same first
`on_phase` call (`:679-681`) and, by design, covers exactly this window: it emits
`  [post] <label> still running (Xs elapsed)` (`:399`) every 10s on a TTY / 30s non-TTY
(`:355`). The class docstring at `:338-344` explicitly claims it "covers every phase, including
the ones the ticker never saw at all" — but it does not claim, and does not have, exclusivity.

**Result:** in any pre-loop phase running longer than 60s, both emit. Two liveness voices for the
same silent window, one of them reporting `0/N files` about a loop that has not begun. On a TTY it
is worse than cosmetic: **both writers share stderr** — `_PhaseHeartbeat` renders in place with a
leading `\r` (`:338-341`, echo lambda at `:612` with `err=True`) while the ticker writes a full
line (`:609`, also `err=True`) — so the ticker's line lands mid-render and corrupts the in-place
update.

The `d29244f6` docstring reasoning that the two are "deliberately separate" is about their
*formats and cadences*, which is sound. It does not address *simultaneity*, which is the defect.

## The commit's own test does not cover it

`tests/test_index_cmd.py:838` `test_eta_ticker_not_stopped_by_first_phase_marker` sets up exactly
the overlap window — `on_start(2)`, then `on_phase(...)`, then `time.sleep(0.06)` before the
first `on_file` — and asserts `"[eta]" in result.output`. But it patches only the ticker's
interval down (`_FastETATicker`, interval 0.02 at `tests/test_index_cmd.py:846-850`);
`_PhaseHeartbeat` is constructed with its REAL interval (10s TTY / 30s non-TTY,
`src/nexus/commands/index.py:610-613`). A 0.06s sleep cannot make the heartbeat fire. **The test
proves the ticker survives a phase marker and never observes the double-fire it creates.**

## Ask

1. Make the two mutually exclusive. The cheapest shape consistent with both parent beads' intent:
   `_PhaseHeartbeat` owns liveness whenever a phase is armed, and `_ETATicker` suppresses its
   emission while `n == 0` (nothing to report) — or, equivalently, the ticker starts emitting only
   at the first `on_file`. Either restores exactly one liveness voice per window without
   reintroducing the p7tp3 bug (the ticker must stay *alive*, it just must not *speak* about a
   loop that has not started). Do not resolve it by re-latching the ticker on `on_phase` — that is
   the p7tp3 regression.
2. Note the TTY interleaving explicitly in whatever comment records the decision, so a later
   change that moves either writer back onto the other's stream is recognisable as a regression.

## Non-vacuous test

- **Overlap leg (the missing one)**: patch BOTH intervals down — `_FastETATicker` as today, and
  `_PhaseHeartbeat(interval=0.02)` via the constructor kwarg it already accepts
  (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:352`). Fire `on_start(N)` then `on_phase(...)`, sleep long enough
  for several ticks of each, then complete the loop. Assert **no `[eta]` line with `0/` appears
  while a phase is armed**, and that at least one `still running` line does — i.e. exactly one
  voice, and it is the right one.
- **Regression guard for p7tp3**: keep `test_eta_ticker_not_stopped_by_first_phase_marker`'s
  property, restated so it still holds under the fix — the ticker must emit `[eta]` once the file
  loop is under way and a phase marker fired earlier in the run. If the fix is "suppress while
  n == 0", this leg is what stops someone from implementing it as "stop on phase".
- **Exact-count leg**: assert the ticker's stop is still called exactly once, at `n >= total`
  (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:871` already does this — confirm it still passes unchanged).
- **Non-vacuity**: revert the mutual-exclusion change and the overlap leg must go RED (both a
  `0/` eta line and a `still running` line present in the same window). Verify by reverting.

Related: nexus-p7tp3 (the ticker stop-point fix this reviews), nexus-mx22w (the heartbeat this
reviews), nexus-c14zi (route `_progress` \r writes through the phase channel and TTY-gate them —
same stream-collision class), nexus-p6kpx (unify the four progress channels behind one
ProgressReporter — the structural fix this defect is an argument for), nexus-uoot1 (mechanize the
no-silent-phase guarantee).

title: T2 [22162] design §0.3 records a FALSE claim as [E]: a 503 IS retried 4x by the inner gateway ladder — retract in place and re-derive ADMISSION_WAIT_MS
description:
Found 2026-08-10 by the W0 client-degradation investigation. Source of record: T2
`nexus/engine-w0-503-client-degradation` (entry 22168), section 0 (HEADLINE). The design being
corrected is T2 `nexus/engine-embed-path-hardening-design-v0.1.70` (entry 22162).

**This is nexus-b32rx's failure class recurring: an inference recorded as established.** The
design tags its claims [E]/[I]/[NE] precisely to prevent this, and this claim carries an [E] it
did not earn.

## The false claim

T2 [22162] §0.3, verbatim heading:

> "### 0.3 A 503 does NOT trigger the client's retry ladder **[E]** — this inverts item 2"

and the load-bearing consequence it derives:

> "the 503 path terminates in one response. Therefore the admission WAIT timeout must be SHORTER
> than the client's read timeout, so the engine decides the outcome rather than the client's
> clock."

## What is actually true (verified by direct read, develop working tree 2026-08-10)

A 503 **is** retried, four times, with a 2/5/10s backoff, by an inner gateway ladder the design
never inspected:

```
src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:490   _GATEWAY_RETRY_SLEEPS = (2.0, 5.0, 10.0)
src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:491   _GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES  = frozenset({502, 503, 504})
src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653
    for i, delay in enumerate((*_GATEWAY_RETRY_SLEEPS, None)):
        try:    return self._request_once(method, path, **kwargs)
        except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
            if exc.response.status_code not in _GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES or delay is None:
                raise
            time.sleep(delay)
```

Present in **both** the T3 client (`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:830-836`) and the
T2/catalog client (`src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653`), so every path a combined
write or a legacy upsert-chunks call can take is affected.

**The design's two cited readings are each individually correct** — it read the two OUTER
classifiers and missed the inner one:

- `src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:150-151` — `_is_retryable_endpoint_error` returns
  `status_code == 401` only. Correct: the self-heal/re-resolve axis does not retry a 503.
- `src/nexus/retry.py:570-575` — `_is_connectivity_error` inspects type / `__cause__` /
  `__context__`, never status. Correct: the outer `_manifest_write_with_retry` does not retry
  a 503.

Both sit **outside** the gateway loop. The correct statement is: a 503 is retried on exactly one
of the three axes — the innermost — for 4 POSTs and 17s of client sleep per flush attempt.
Neither zero, nor the 8-POST ReadTimeout storm.

## Why it matters

`ADMISSION_WAIT_MS = 10_000` (T2 [22162] §2.2) was sized on the premise that a 503 terminates in
one response, with the binding constraint stated as "must stay well under the client's read
timeout". That premise is false, so the constraint is no longer the binding one. The wait is paid
**4x per flush attempt**, and the `ChunkBatcher` bisect multiplies flush attempts by `2F-1` — ~124
POSTs for a 16-file flush (see the companion bisect bead and T2 [22168] §0).

**The design's CONCLUSION survives**: 503 is still the right signal (the client already has a
designed 503 policy on the sibling path — `_TRANSIENT_UPSERT_CODES = {502, 503, 504}` at
`src/nexus/indexer.py:1930` -> defer-to-staleness at `:1967-1983`; and the engine already returns
503 for the analogous DB-pool saturation, `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TenantScope.java:208-211`
-> `HttpUtil.java:172`). Only its stated RATIONALE is wrong. Do not re-open the code choice.

## Ask

1. **Correct §0.3 in T2 [22162] in place, with an explicit retraction.** Do NOT silently edit —
   this repo records corrections (nexus-b32rx precedent; the standing directive against writing
   an inference into a permanent record as fact). Keep the retracted sentence visible, marked as
   retracted, with the reason and the file:line evidence above. Replacement text:
   *a 503 is retried 4x with 2/5/10s backoff by the inner gateway ladder
   (`src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653`), and the ChunkBatcher bisect multiplies that
   by `2F-1`. It is still strictly better than the ReadTimeout path — each retry is rejected
   cheaply at admission rather than starting a fresh uncancelled embed — but it is a bounded
   storm, not a single clean response.*
2. **Re-derive `ADMISSION_WAIT_MS`** (§2.2) against the real multiplier. T2 [22168] §5 argues for
   lowering it to ~1-2s so the client's own 2/5/10 backoff does the waiting (a backoff holds no
   server thread or connection); keeping 10s is defensible only if measurement shows saturation
   reliably drains inside it so the multiplier never materialises. The correct value is [NE] and
   belongs to the W9 measurement — record the direction and the dependency, not a guessed number.
3. **Update §5's backward-compat row.** "new 503 on admission saturation -> [NE] graceful
   degradation" now resolves to: graceful on the batcher path and on the prose/PDF/RDR legacy
   path; NOT graceful on the code-file legacy path (aborts the run — see the companion P1 bead);
   silent on 7.5.0 in the field (exit 0, the pre-nexus-4s1ww shape).
4. **Cross-check the rest of §0's [E] tags for the same defect** — a claim about client behaviour
   derived from reading a classifier is only [E] for that classifier, never for "the client".

## Non-vacuous verification

This is a documentation correction, so the check is a read-back, not a test run: after the edit,
`memory_get` T2 [22162] and confirm (a) the retracted sentence is present and marked retracted,
(b) the replacement names `src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653`, and (c) §2.2 no longer
states a re-derived constant as settled without naming its measurement dependency. A silent
in-place replacement with no retraction marker fails this check even if the new text is correct.

Related: nexus-b32rx (the recurring class this instantiates), nexus-zu4ma and nexus-0o76a (the
engine work the design covers), nexus-lqrec, nexus-n2w4q, nexus-y9t08, nexus-4s1ww.

Evidence: T2 [22162] SS0.3 retracted in place with verbatim-preserved claim, marked RETRACTED, names _refreshable_client.py:649-654; ADMISSION_WAIT_MS flagged re-derive at every derived site; SS5 row retracted — all three of the bead's read-back checks pass

comments.text: PAIRED WITH nexus-4ao66 (P2), filed 2026-08-10: §2.2's ADMISSION_WAIT_MS has a SECOND wrong input independent of this bead's retracted §0.3 premise — it is derived against a 30s client read timeout, but the combined-write POST is _COMBINED_WRITE_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S = 600.0 (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:226, restored by 127f2dbc / refined by 47c5a39a). A 20x error in the input. The two corrections MUST land together: fixing only the retry premise leaves a constant sized against 30s; fixing only the timeout leaves it sized on the belief that a 503 terminates in one response. Either alone produces a wrong number.

title: ChunkBatcher bisects on status-coded gateway transients (502/503/504), multiplying requests against an already-saturated server by 2F-1 — ~124 POSTs and ~29 min per 16-file flush
description:
Found 2026-08-10 by the W0 client-degradation investigation for the v0.1.70 engine embed-path
hardening design. Source of record: T2 `nexus/engine-w0-503-client-degradation` (entry 22168),
section 0 ("the multiplier the design has no model for at all") and section 5.

## Defect

`ChunkBatcher._flush_batch` catches **every** exception type and, for a batch holding >= 2 files,
bisects and retries both halves:

```
src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:449   except Exception as exc:   # broad, type-blind
src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:450       if len(pend.file_counts) >= 2:
src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:464-465       for half in self._split(pend):
                                             self._flush_batch(collection, half)
```

Bisection is the right response to a **payload-attributable** failure (one poisoned file in the
batch): splitting isolates the offender. It is the wrong response to a **server-saturation**
failure. Splitting a batch cannot relieve pressure on a saturated server — it strictly
**multiplies** the number of requests aimed at it. Under a persistent status-coded transient
every node of the binary tree fails, so a flush of F files costs `2F-1` flush attempts.

## Amplification arithmetic (established from in-tree constants)

Each flush attempt is itself retried by the inner gateway ladder:
`_GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES = frozenset({502, 503, 504})`
(`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:491`) with
`_GATEWAY_RETRY_SLEEPS = (2.0, 5.0, 10.0)` (`:490`), looped at
`src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653` — 4 POSTs and 17s of client sleep per attempt.

At F = 16 (the onnx-local cap, `_ONNX_LOCAL_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP_DEFAULT = 16`,
`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:510`), with the v0.1.70 design's proposed
`ADMISSION_WAIT_MS = 10_000`:

| term | value |
|---|---|
| flush attempts (`2F-1`) | 31 |
| POSTs (`x4`) | **124** |
| client backoff sleep (`31 x 17s`) | 527 s |
| server-side admission wait (`124 x 10s`) | 1 240 s |
| **total wall, one flush batch** | **~29 min** |

`flush_concurrency=3` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:4293`), so three of these run at once.
Suppressing the bisect for gateway-transient codes takes the same batch to 4 POSTs and ~57 s.

The wall-clock figures are a worst case computed from established constants, not an observation;
the request-count multiplication itself is structural and does not depend on the timing model.

## Ask

Do **not** bisect on gateway-transient status codes. In `_flush_batch`
(`src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:449`), when the caught exception carries a status in
{502, 503, 504} (`httpx.HTTPStatusError.response.status_code`, or
`VectorServiceError.code` — `src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:951`), skip the bisect and fail
the batch straight to per-file settlement (`error = str(exc)` at
`src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:467`, which already flows to `_failed_files`). Every other exception
class keeps today's bisect behaviour — the change is a narrowing, not a removal.

Reuse `_TRANSIENT_UPSERT_CODES` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:1930`) rather than minting a third copy of
the same frozenset; it and `_GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES` are already the same three codes in two places.

## Non-vacuous test

- **Amplification leg**: a batcher holding 8 files, with `_flush` stubbed to always raise a
  502/503/504-carrying error. Count `_flush` invocations. Assert **exactly 1** (no bisect), and
  that all 8 files land in `failed_files` with the error recorded. Pin the count exactly — a
  `<= 3` style bound would pass on a partially-narrowed implementation.
- **Preserved-behaviour leg**: same fixture, but `_flush` raises a plain `ValueError`. Assert the
  bisect still runs (invocation count `2F-1 = 15`) and per-file attribution is unchanged. Without
  this leg the change is indistinguishable from deleting bisect entirely.
- **Attribution leg**: mixed batch where only ONE file's payload triggers a non-status error —
  assert the healthy files still succeed, i.e. narrowing did not cost the isolation property
  bisect exists for.
- **Non-vacuity**: revert the status-code check and the amplification leg must go RED (15
  invocations instead of 1). Verify by deleting the check, not by reasoning.

## Notes

- This is client-side and independent of any engine tag. It reduces load against a saturated
  engine regardless of whether v0.1.70's admission control ships.
- Distinct from nexus-lqrec (abandoned server-side embeds continuing after a client timeout) and
  nexus-n2w4q (the 8-POST ReadTimeout ladder). Those are the *timeout* axis; this is the
  *status-code* axis, and neither of them models the `2F-1` bisect multiplier at all.

Related: nexus-lqrec, nexus-n2w4q, nexus-y9t08, nexus-0o76a (engine admission control),
nexus-zu4ma, nexus-4s1ww (flush-failure reporting), nexus-33hpq (the cap that sets F).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Cross-ref: nexus-4ao66 (P2) establishes that the design's stated binding constraint for ADMISSION_WAIT_MS — 'well under the client's read timeout' — is now trivially satisfiable, because the combined-write POST budget is 600s (src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:226), not the 30s the design assumed. That makes THIS bead's amplification term (4 POSTs per flush attempt x 2F-1 attempts) the constraint that actually binds the constant. Suppressing bisect on gateway-transient codes therefore does not merely reduce load — it changes what the engine-side constant must be derived against.

title: index: taxonomy_assign_batch_failed is not counted in any run summary
description:
Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), section 6
(adjacent honesty gap found in passing), bead-breakdown item 9.

## Defect

On the evidence run (`nx index repo .` on nexus itself, cloud/voyage, conexus 7.5.0), the log
carried exactly **3 WARNING-level structlog lines**, two of which were
`taxonomy_assign_batch_failed` (HTTP 500) at 10:45:00 and 10:45:03, covering **1254 chunks across
2 batches**. Those chunks' topic assignments were LOST.

**The run reported clean.** Exit 0, `Done.`, and NO summary line mentions the failure. The two
warnings are visible at the default level, but nothing aggregates them, so a user reading the
summary (or a script reading the exit code) has no signal that 1254 chunks are missing their topic
assignments. Topic-scoped search over those chunks is silently incomplete.

This is the same family as nexus-4s1ww / GH #1432: a partial failure of a write path reported as
success by the channels a human or a script would actually check. The no-silent-fallbacks-for-
data-correctness directive applies directly.

## Ask

1. Count `taxonomy_assign_batch_failed` occurrences (and the affected chunk count) during the run.
2. Surface them in the run summary, in the SAME shape the existing flush-failure reporting uses
   (`, N file(s) failed` / `- N ... failed to flush`), so the two honesty gaps read consistently.
3. Decide and record the exit-code policy explicitly. GH #1432 set the precedent that total write
   failure must be non-zero; a partial taxonomy-assignment loss is a weaker case and the decision
   should be made deliberately rather than defaulted. State the chosen policy in the bead's close
   note.

## Non-vacuous test

- Inject a taxonomy-assign batch failure (HTTP 500 from the assign endpoint) and assert the run
  summary names the count of failed batches AND the count of affected chunks. Asserting only "a
  warning was logged" is vacuous: the warning is ALREADY logged today and the run still reports
  clean.
- Assert the clean-run summary does NOT gain a phantom "0 failed" line when nothing failed, if the
  chosen shape is conditional.
- Non-vacuity: remove the counter and the summary assertion goes red while the existing warning-log
  assertion still passes, proving they are independently pinned.
- Pin the new sentence in `tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` alongside the ~50 sentences already
  pinned there, and do not reword any existing one (constraint 5).

## Open question carried from the assessment (section 9, NOT ESTABLISHED)

Whether the 2 HTTP 500s are a transient engine fault or a REPRODUCIBLE batch-size limit
(1254 chunks across 2 batches) is not established. This bead is about the reporting being wrong
regardless of cause. If the investigation shows a reproducible batch-size limit, file that
separately rather than folding it in here.

## Related

- nexus-4s1ww (open, P1) — same family, flush path.
- nexus-gednd (closed) fixed taxonomy-assign failures being swallowed at DEBUG level; they now reach
  WARNING. This bead is the NEXT step: WARNING-visible but summary-invisible.
- nexus-reskd (closed) — taxonomy assign hook silently no-opping on a truthiness gap, same class.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS (binding on ANY change to `nx index` output)

From an exhaustive consumer sweep in T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` section 7.4.
Constraints 1 and 2 break their gate SILENTLY (wrong result, not a red). Read them before writing
a single line of output code.

1. **Never emit a new line matching `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]`.**
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:197-203` counts lines of that shape
   (`grep -cv skipped`) into a TWO-SIDED gate (run1 >= 10, run2 <= 6). A new line of that shape
   makes the gate fail silently wrong, not loudly.
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh:399-401` counts the same shape (>= 3).
   => Put any fraction LATER in the line, behind the `  [post] ` prefix. Correct shape:
   `  [post] Pruning deleted files: collection 1/3, page 42/96 (3m10s elapsed)`.
2. **Never emit `\r` on the non-TTY path.** `tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts
   `"\r" not in result.output`.
3. **Do not touch the `[debug-timing]` block.**
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/aggregate.py:20-21,27` hard-parses the header wording and the
   ordered stage rows and raises `ValueError` on drift.
4. **`Done.` must stay, and stay LAST.** 8 assertion sites across 6 files
   (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:84,103`; `tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py:277`;
   `tests/test_indexer_e2e.py:864,907`; `tests/test_index_taxonomy.py:106`;
   `tests/test_index_reminder.py:192,212`; `tests/test_scenario_journeys.py:411`), two of them
   deliberately on failure paths. Also `tail -5` consumers
   (`tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:528,535,560,568`; `scenarios/03_skills.sh:11`) degrade if new
   trailing lines are appended after the summary. Add nothing after `Done.`.
5. **Do not reword the summary sentences.** `tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` pins ~50 exact
   sentences including em-dashes and `(s)` pluralization; `tests/test_index_cmd.py:514,571-574,588`
   and `tests/test_index_pdf_batch.py:117-118,141,189` likewise.
6. **`[post]` is the SAFE channel to extend.** Nothing asserts on the `[post]` markers;
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/test_aggregate.py:19` fixtures one as noise the parser must
   skip. Nothing in `.github/workflows/**` or `conexus/hooks/**` parses `nx index` output at all.
   This is the single most useful fact for anything in this family.

## Conventions to REUSE, not reinvent (assessment 7.3)

- Completed duration: `({t:.1f}s)`.
- Projection: `~{_fmt_duration(...)} remaining` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2894-2903`: `42s` / `1m30s` / `2h05m`).
- Rate: `{rate*60:.1f} <unit>/min`.
- ETA regimes: `_format_eta` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:216-236`) -> `pending` / `~N min remaining` / `done`.
- Where no denominator exists, say so: `still running (1m12s elapsed)`. Never a fake percentage,
  never a fake ETA.

Source: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159).

title: index: route _progress \r writes through the phase channel and TTY-gate them
description:
Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), section 2
channel 3, proposal a6, bead-breakdown item 7.

## Defect

`nx index` writes progress through FOUR uncoordinated channels (assessment section 2). Channel 3 is
a raw `sys.stderr.write` bound at `src/nexus/indexer.py:969` (`_progress = sys.stderr.write`) and
used at `src/nexus/indexer.py:970, 1364, 1369, 1380, 1442`. It emits `\r` and is **NOT TTY-gated**.

Observed consequence in the non-TTY log of a real run: two logically separate lines mashed into
one, with a structlog event tacked on the end:

```
Catalog: linking 251 new entries...  Catalog: housekeeping...event='...'
```

The `\r` that repaints in place on a TTY is just a literal control character in a redirected log,
so every consumer of that log (and every human reading it) sees a corrupted line.

This also sits in tension with the existing contract elsewhere in the same command:
`tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts `"\r" not in result.output`. The assessment notes
`src/nexus/indexer.py:969` "already violates the spirit of this on stderr" and says to fix it in the
same pass as any other output work.

## Ask (proposal a6, size XS)

1. Route the `src/nexus/indexer.py:969` `_progress` writes through the phase channel
   (`on_phase` / the `[post]` marker path at `src/nexus/commands/index.py:566-578`) instead of
   writing to `sys.stderr` directly.
2. TTY-gate the `\r`: in-place repaint only when `sys.stderr.isatty()`; a plain appended line
   otherwise.

## Non-vacuous test

- Run the command with a non-TTY stderr and assert `"\r" not in` the captured stderr, mirroring the
  existing stdout assertion at `tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` so BOTH streams are pinned.
- Assert the two previously-mashed lines arrive as two SEPARATE lines in the non-TTY capture. A test
  that only greps for the absence of `\r` passes even if the lines are still concatenated by some
  other mechanism.
- Assert the TTY path still repaints (i.e. the gate did not simply delete the feature).
- Non-vacuity: restore the raw write and both assertions go red.

## Related

- nexus-w1stu (open, P3) is the ADJACENT half of the same corrupted line: structlog event lines
  interleaving raw into human CLI progress output, with a proposed fix of routing structlog to the
  per-run log file in CLI contexts. Distinct fix locus (log routing vs. this raw-write channel);
  the observed mashed line is caused by both together. Cross-reference, do not merge.
- The four-channel unification bead (assessment b1) subsumes this one structurally, but this fix is
  XS and should not wait for it.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS (binding on ANY change to `nx index` output)

From an exhaustive consumer sweep in T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` section 7.4.
Constraints 1 and 2 break their gate SILENTLY (wrong result, not a red). Read them before writing
a single line of output code.

title: upgrade_finish.pending_data_rung_callout's CALLER silently swallows a raising default_registry() — the same fail-open-to-silence class v2mdd fixed one frame down, left open one frame up, same file
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 by substantive-critic review of nexus-v2mdd (3e2a5317).

v2mdd fixed TWO fail-open-to-GREEN/silence surfaces:
(1) health.py:_check_pending_rungs' OUTER handler (default_registry()
    construction failing) -> now ok=False, warn=True.
(2) upgrade_finish.py:pending_data_rung_callout's INNER per-rung
    `except Exception: continue` (rung.detect() raising) -> now an
    explicit "status unknown" line.

Both fixes are correct and non-vacuously tested (verified by direct
read: tests/upgrade/test_ladder_surfaces.py::test_doctor_check_is_crash_proof,
tests/test_upgrade_finish.py::test_detect_crash_surfaces_as_unavailable_not_silently_dropped).

## The gap

pending_data_rung_callout() itself (src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:1516-1544)
only wraps rung.detect() in try/except — the `default_registry()` call
that FEEDS the for-loop (:1529, `for rung in default_registry():`) is
NOT wrapped at all inside this function. If default_registry() itself
raises (deferred imports, registry construction — the EXACT failure
class finding (1) fixed in health.py's twin function), the exception
propagates out of pending_data_rung_callout uncaught.

Its only caller, check_version_transition's finish pass
(src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:~1694-1697), catches it:

    try:
        actions = actions + pending_data_rung_callout()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        _log.warning("pending_rung_callout_failed", exc_info=True)

This is the SAME shape v2mdd exists to eliminate: a raising
construction-level failure becomes indistinguishable from "nothing
pending" from the user's point of view — no line is appended to
`actions`, so the `nx upgrade` finish-pass summary a user actually reads
says nothing, and the only trace is a structlog WARNING line most users
never see. This is genuinely NOT covered by v2mdd's stated scope (the
bead's finding (2) named `rung.detect()` raising specifically, not
`default_registry()` raising) — it is a new instance of the identical
class, immediately adjacent to the code v2mdd touched, in the same file,
uncovered by any test (every existing test mocks
`default_registry(return_value=[...])`, none mocks it to raise).

## Mitigating factor

nx doctor's _check_pending_rungs (the OTHER half of v2mdd) now correctly
surfaces the SAME underlying default_registry() failure as a ⚠ warning,
and pending_data_rung_callout's own docstring already states "nx doctor
remains the backstop for full detail either way." So a user who runs
`nx doctor` separately is not left blind. A user who only reads the
`nx upgrade` finish-pass output (the immediate, at-the-point-of-action
surface) is.

## Ask

1. Wrap the `default_registry()` call inside pending_data_rung_callout
   itself (not just its caller) and emit an explicit unavailable line,
   mirroring the per-rung fix already applied — OR wrap it at the
   existing caller (upgrade_finish.py's finish pass) and append an
   explicit "could not check pending data rungs" action line there
   instead of only logging.
2. Test: mock default_registry to raise (`side_effect=RuntimeError(...)`)
   and assert the finish-pass `actions` list contains a user-visible
   line, not silence. Non-vacuity: must go red if the wrap is removed.
3. Flag this as a concrete first hit for nexus-3znzn's planned sweep
   (which would have found this if run against upgrade_finish.py) —
   evidence that the sweep is worth doing promptly, not deferred.

Related: nexus-v2mdd (the sibling fix this gap sits directly next to),
nexus-3znzn (the generalizable sweep this is a live instance of).

title: [perf] taxonomy is ~100% of flush-grain hook cost at production corpus scale (90.1s of 90.2s) — decide whether 7.4.0's 'collapsed to noise' verdict is scale-bound or regressed
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 on a real `nx index repo .` over the nexus repo itself — live
managed/cloud mode (api.conexus-nexus.com, engine v0.1.69, voyage), conexus 7.5.0, no
--force. 1930 files, 1646 skipped unchanged, 284 changed, 3 flushes.

  flush-grain hooks total   90.2s
    taxonomy                90.1s   <-- essentially 100% of it
    manifest                 0.0s
    aspect                   0.1s
  hook lock wait            23.1s (included above)

## Why this needs recording rather than shrugging at

T2 nexus/indexing-perf-assessment-7.4.0 [21715] is the standing measured verdict on the
7.4.0 indexing-perf work (nexus-yu9w5/lns3o, "taxonomy assignment collapsed to ONE POST").
It measured the taxonomy leg at 0.45-0.57s/flush across 86 flushes and concluded the leg
had fallen "from the dominant term (~51% of flush thread-time) to ~0.5s/flush noise".

On this run the taxonomy leg is once again ~the entire flush-grain hook cost. That does
not necessarily contradict [21715] — that memo stated its own caveats explicitly and
honestly (probe corpus 109 files vs production ~1875; probe taxonomy 21 topics vs
production ~581; smaller centroid space server-side) and said those "affect magnitude, not
direction". This bead is about establishing WHICH it is, because the difference matters:

  (a) CORPUS SCALE — the per-POST cost is fine and simply scales with topic count /
      assignment space. Then "taxonomy is solved" is true at probe scale and false at
      production scale, and the conclusion in [21715] must not be reused unqualified.
  (b) REGRESSION — something since 7.4.0 reintroduced per-flush work the yu9w5 change
      removed. Then it is a live perf defect.

NOT ESTABLISHED which. Do not cite [21715]'s "collapsed to noise" line about a
production-scale corpus until this is settled.

## Ask

1. Re-measure the taxonomy leg at PRODUCTION corpus scale with the per-flush split already
   available in the log (`chunk_flush_complete` carries flush_hook_s; the [post] summary
   carries the taxonomy split). One warm run on this repo is enough to get the per-flush
   number.
2. Check the route: [21715] verified the hook actually rode assign_from_chashes by
   asserting ZERO tripwire / get_embeddings / unmatched_chashes / embed_unavailable lines.
   Re-run that same grep. If those lines are back, it is (b) and the route has fallen off
   the batched path — the fastest discriminator available and it costs one grep.
3. Only if the route is clean, treat it as (a) and decide whether per-flush taxonomy
   assignment should be batched further or deferred to end-of-run at large topic counts.

Pruning deleted files cost 547.8s — 87% of the 627.6s post-processing phase — on a run
whose actual write work was 3 flushes / 3.7s. Recorded as a measurement comment on

title: [test-infra] sweep for tests that PIN fail-open behaviour — v2mdd regressed because a 'crash-proof' test asserted ok is True next to a sibling asserting the opposite
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 while fixing nexus-v2mdd. The fix itself is done; this bead is the
GENERALIZABLE half, which is bigger than the two lines it came from.

## What happened

nexus-v2mdd was a REGRESSION of a bug already fixed once. The reason it came back is not
that coverage was missing — it is that coverage was WRONG, and wrong in a way that reads
as right.

tests/upgrade/test_ladder_surfaces.py contained, adjacent to each other:

  test_a_rung_that_cannot_answer_is_pending_not_green   <- pins the INNER per-rung handler
                                                            CORRECTLY (not green)
  test_doctor_check_is_crash_proof                      <- asserted results[0].ok is True
                                                            for the OUTER handler, i.e.
                                                            pinned the FAIL-OPEN BUG

Two tests in one file encoding OPPOSITE contracts for the same property. Anyone auditing
"is the upgrade-ladder health check covered?" sees a file that answers yes.

tests/test_upgrade_finish.py had the same shape: test_detect_crash_degrades_to_no_callout
asserted `pending_data_rung_callout() == []`, i.e. it pinned "a raising detect() silently
produces no warning" as the intended contract.

## The naming failure, which is the transferable lesson

"crash-proof" meant "never crashes nx doctor". The assertion written to enforce it was
`ok is True`. Those are not the same property, and the gap between them is exactly the
fail-open bug. A test named for a SAFETY property (crash-proof, resilient, best-effort,
degrades-gracefully, non-critical) is a prime site for this: the safe-sounding name
licenses an assertion that the check returned SUCCESS, when what was actually wanted is
that it returned WITHOUT RAISING.

## Ask

1. Sweep the suite for tests whose assertions pin fail-open behaviour. Highest-yield
   search: tests whose NAME contains crash_proof / crash-proof / resilient / best_effort /
   degrades / graceful / non_critical / never_fails, and whose body asserts ok is True,
   == [], == {}, is None, or "not raised" on an EXCEPTION path.
2. For each hit, decide which property was actually intended — "does not raise" vs
   "reports success" — and split them if both are wanted. The correct shape already exists
   in-repo as a model: upgrade_ladder/runner.py's pending_rungs converts a failure into
   PENDING-with-reason rather than into silence.
3. Where a test is found pinning fail-open, check whether the production code it pins is
   ALSO wrong (v2mdd's was). The test and the bug travel together.

## Known candidate, NOT fixed, needs a judgment call rather than a sweep

src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py `_uninstall_stray_t2_launchagent`'s applicability probe
(~:1483-1488) does `except Exception: return []` on an existence probe. Its own docstring
documents this as deliberate two-tier discipline mirroring heal_diag_view, so it may be
correct as written — unlike v2mdd's two handlers, which had no such rationale. Decide
explicitly; do not sweep it away either direction.

## Related
nexus-v2mdd (the instance), nexus-hdumg (rung declared verified after its diagnostic
FAILED), nexus-eu2sg (four checks that pass over an empty/unreadable input set),
nexus-2nh4c (vacuous-green lint over health.py and doctor.py — this bead is its test-side
counterpart), nexus-3zu8g (root enabler), RDR-182's never-a-silent-all-clean design.

title: [bug] engine: no admission control and no cancellation on the embed path — abandoned client requests keep burning CPU/memory to completion
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, deep-analyst assessment of the 7.5.0 local-index cluster (T2 [22152]).

The engine accepts embed work without bound and cannot stop it once started.

- No admission control: NexusService.java:393 is unbounded virtual-thread-per-request, so N
  concurrent client POSTs become N concurrent ONNX embeds.
- No cancellation: neither CombinedWriteService.java (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/)
  nor Bge768Embedder.java observes client disconnect or interruption. A client that times out and
  gives up leaves the embed running to completion on the engine.
- No SessionOptions tuning: Bge768Embedder.java:137 sets none, so ORT thread-pool and arena
  behaviour are defaults.

Consequence: engine memory and CPU are a function of what callers happen to send, with no ceiling
the engine itself enforces. This is the same "trusting a caller-supplied size" argument nexus-zu4ma
makes for batch size, one level up — zu4ma bounds the size of ONE request, this bounds how many
requests can be in flight and whether abandoned ones keep burning resources.

Pairs with the 30s-timeout retry bead: retries are only additive load BECAUSE there is no
cancellation and no admission control. Fixing the client timeout removes today's trigger; this
removes the amplifier.

## Ask
Bounded concurrency for the embed path (a semaphore/bulkhead sized from a memory budget), plus
cancellation on client disconnect. Test: assert that N+1 concurrent embed requests do not produce
N+1 concurrent ONNX sessions, and that an aborted request stops server-side work. Non-vacuity:
must go red if the bound is removed.

ENGINE-SIDE — requires an engine-service tag cut (separate release lifecycle).
Related: nexus-zu4ma (per-request bound), nexus-lqrec, nexus-00wsf (engine spins at 100-290% CPU
with zero active PG queries), nexus-ptor7 (synchronous CCE holds a request + Hikari connection).

The in-code comment claiming code files are covered by the batcher (src/nexus/indexer.py:4334-4337) is false: ChunkBatcher.add returns False over the cap (chunk_batcher.py:260) and code_indexer.py:487 falls through to the legacy direct upsert at :515. Latent today, activated by any engine that begins emitting 503. W5 should not ship ahead of that ~3-line client fix. Also filed: nexus-00ez4 (P2, the bisect multiplies 503 rejections by 2F-1) and nexus-a3tko (P2, the design's §0.3 retry claim is false, so ADMISSION_WAIT_MS needs re-deriving). title: [bug] cap=16 silently narrows RDR-181 atomicity: files >16 chunks fall off the combined-write path onto the legacy two-call shape
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, deep-analyst assessment of the 7.5.0 local-index cluster (T2 [22152]).

The 7.5.0 onnx-local cap of 16 (per_collection_chunk_cap, src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py)
interacts with the ChunkBatcher's whole-document routing rule. chunk_batcher.py:250-256 routes
a document to the combined-write path only when the batch carries the WHOLE document (first
chunk at position 0). With the cap at 16, any file producing more than 16 chunks can no longer
fit one flush, so it falls off the batcher onto the LEGACY two-call path.

That path is exactly the non-atomic shape RDR-181 / nexus-kl2z6 replaced: a chunk-upsert POST
followed by a separate manifest-write POST, with the pre-existing window where chunks land and
the manifest does not (or vice versa). The 7.5.0 CHANGELOG documents this window as surviving
only for "continuation-sliced documents ... an oversized file split across flushes" and tracks
it as nexus-7t86z.

The unnoticed part: lowering the cap to 16 MOVES THE BOUNDARY. Files between 17 and 300 chunks
were whole-document (atomic) before the cap and are continuation-sliced (non-atomic) after it.
On a code corpus that is a large fraction of files, not an edge case. Nothing in the 33hpq work
or the CHANGELOG notes that the atomicity guarantee narrowed as a side effect of the memory fix.

## Ask
1. Quantify: on a representative corpus, what fraction of files exceed 16 chunks and therefore
   lost the atomic path? (Cheap to measure from an existing index run's chunk counts.)
2. Decide whether that is acceptable, or whether the combined write needs a multi-flush
   whole-document mode so atomicity is not a function of the memory cap.
3. Either way, the coupling between per_collection_chunk_cap and RDR-181 atomicity should be
   stated where the cap is defined — right now raising or lowering the cap silently changes a
   durability property.

Related: nexus-7t86z (the residual continuation-slice window), nexus-33hpq (closed, the cap),
nexus-b32rx.

title: rehearse_fullstack.sh RF-4 liveness check cannot fail (if pgrep..then ok..else note) and the PASS banner claims liveness it did not confirm
description:
Observed directly 2026-08-09 on a real --fullstack run against 7.5.0 that reported FULL-STACK SHAKEOUT PASSED, exit 0.

## The defect

tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_fullstack.sh:127-132

    note "leased-daemon liveness after nx-mcp teardown (RF-4 check):"
    if pgrep -af "aspect-worker" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      pgrep -af "aspect-worker" | sed ...
      ok "leased aspect-worker daemon SURVIVED nx-mcp teardown (RF-4 ...)"
    else
      note "no live aspect-worker process found post-teardown"
    fi

The else arm is a NOTE, not a bad. The check has exactly two outcomes: PASS, or silence. It cannot fail and therefore cannot detect the regression it exists to detect (RDR-173 RF-4: the extraction host must be process-independent and survive nx-mcp teardown).

## Observed

My run took the ELSE branch — log line: "no live aspect-worker process found post-teardown" — and the run still finished FAILS=0 / exit 0 with the banner:

  FULL-STACK SHAKEOUT PASSED — ... real-container liveness confirmed by P2.5 nexus-8zog5

So the terminal banner ASSERTS liveness was confirmed while the run own output says no live process was found and the check was skipped. The banner is making a claim the run did not establish.

## Contributing cause (independent, also worth fixing)

Dockerfile.fullstack installs: ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release python3 python3-venv python3-pip git. NO procps, therefore NO pgrep. `pgrep ... >/dev/null 2>&1` on a missing binary returns non-zero with the error swallowed, which is indistinguishable from "found no process". So the check may never have been able to run in this image at all — a probe that cannot execute rendering as a soft note.

(Found by the developer agent building the sibling --shakeout-e2e journey, which deliberately uses /proc introspection instead of pgrep for exactly this reason. Verified independently against the Dockerfile and against my own run log.)

## Scope — what is NOT wrong

The substantive assertion of this journey DID fire: the aspect-pipeline drain is asserted properly (document_aspects>0 plus a zero-enqueue-failure tripwire) and that is a real, failable check. The journey is not worthless; one arm of it is theatre and the banner oversells.

## Asks

1. Make the else arm a `bad`, or state explicitly why an absent worker is acceptable. A check whose negative case is a note is not a check.
2. Replace pgrep with /proc introspection (no procps dependency), matching what rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh does. OR add procps to the image and let the check mean something.
3. MEASURE it: kill the aspect-worker deliberately and confirm the repaired check goes RED. An assertion never shown to fail is not an assertion.
4. Fix the banner. It should not claim "liveness confirmed" unless the liveness arm actually passed in THIS run. Consider deriving the banner text from what fired rather than hardcoding it — the banner also still says "vs the 6.0.0 service" on a 7.5.0 run, which is separately stale.

## Note on how this was nearly missed

I reported this run to Hal as PASSED on the strength of its terminal verdict line without inspecting which assertions fired. This is the eighth instance in one week of a green that means less than it appears. Read the assertion list, not the banner.

Related: nexus-acvi7 (combined-write existence-partition unobservable), nexus-dmi67 (cc-validation 27b permanently red), nexus-97dp4 (gate fixture too small to bind), nexus-v2mdd (fail-open-to-green in the upgrade ladder).
