title: cc-validation scenario 27b asserts an Agent-tool `name` parameter that does not exist — a permanently-RED tripwire that shipped guidance tells people to run
description:
Found 2026-08-09 while validating whether tests/cc-validation is still alive (Hal suspected it was pre-7.0 and rotten). It is NOT rotten — see the counter-evidence below. The defect is one scenario.

## Evidence the harness is HEALTHY (do not delete it)

Ran on 7.5.0, live keychain auth, real interactive claude in an isolated HOME on a private tmux socket:
  scenario 01  PASS  plain stdout did NOT inject in interactive
  scenario 12  PASS  subagent-start.sh IS injecting unique hook content
  scenario 26  PASS  routing deny reason + backend-agnostic remedies surfaced to the model
  scenario 27a PASS  SubagentStart fired for sync Task dispatch
  scenario 27c PASS  start-event captured for unnamed background dispatch
  scenario 27b FAIL  x2  <- the subject of this bead
  Totals: 5 passed, 2 failed
Static audit also clean: ZERO references to retired surfaces (no NX_T1_ISOLATED, no Chroma, no guided-upgrade, no SQLite). Newest scenarios are 2026-07-17 (RDR-184 work). The stale-looking 2026-05-31 date on runner.sh is misleading — the scenario set kept being extended.

## The defect

scenario 27b (tests/cc-validation/scenarios/27_subagent_start_payload.sh:85-109) prompts:
  "Use the Agent tool to spawn a background agent: subagent_type=general-purpose, name=startprobeB, run_in_background=true ..."
then asserts:
  :104  agent_id carries the named morphology  a<name>-<hash>
  :108  agent_type == "startprobeB"

THE AGENT TOOL HAS NO `name` PARAMETER. Confirmed two ways: (1) the live Agent tool schema accepts description, prompt, subagent_type, model, isolation, run_in_background — and nothing else; (2) nexus-nu7fo (CLOSED, P1) states it outright — "name-morphology keys on a name the Agent tool has no [parameter for]" — measured at recognized=0 of 10 dispatches across two consecutive sessions.

So 27b asserts a property that CANNOT hold. It is not detecting a payload change; it is permanently red. A test that can never pass is worth exactly as much as a test that can never fail.

## Why it matters beyond one red line

conexus/commands/continuation.md:24 instructs: "Payload-morphology tripwire: after any Claude Code version change, rerun ./tests/cc-validation/runner.sh --scenario 27". That is SHIPPED guidance pointing at a scenario with a permanently-failing arm. The predictable outcome is that operators either chase a phantom regression or learn to discount the tripwire entirely — which then also discards 27a and 27c, the two arms that DO work and DO test real morphology.

## Asks

1. Fix or retire 27b. If a named-dispatch morphology is genuinely wanted, it needs a mechanism that exists; if not, delete the arm and keep 27a/27c.
2. Re-point continuation.md at whatever remains a valid tripwire, so the instruction is executable.
3. MEASURE the repaired tripwire against a deliberately altered payload — a tripwire never shown to fire is not a tripwire.
4. Cross-check nexus-nu7fo: it is CLOSED, but 27b still encodes the fiction nu7fo identified. Closing the analysis did not remove the artifact that depends on it.

## Do NOT delete tests/cc-validation

Hal proposed deleting it as ancient clutter. Counter-evidence above. It is also load-bearing: tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:909 SOURCES its lib for tmux primitives + claude_start, and it is the cited empirical basis for conexus/hooks/scripts/subagent-start.sh and both copies of expectations.sh. Retirement, if ever, comes after a replacement demonstrably covers the same surface.

title: measure local-mode indexing throughput before/after the onnx-local cap — the 7.5.0 release note asserted a slowdown that was never measured
description:
Filed 2026-08-09 by the session that shipped 7.5.0, correcting its own error.

## What went wrong

The shipped 7.5.0 CHANGELOG entry for nexus-33hpq said: "roughly 19x more round trips, so a local nx index repo takes noticeably longer than in 7.4.x". The matching docstring in per_collection_chunk_cap said the path is "measurably slower". Neither was measured.

- The 19x is just the cap ratio (300/16). It is an UPPER BOUND that is only approached on a corpus large enough that flushes actually REACH the cap. The shakedown fixture flushes on file-grain boundaries at 8-15 chunks, so the cap barely binds there at all (see nexus-97dp4).
- "Noticeably longer" had no before/after behind it. There CANNOT be one from the release battery: the cap=300 case WEDGED rather than completing, so there is no baseline duration to compare against.
- The orchestrator also mis-reported the gate as taking "~25 min vs a documented 5-15 min". Actual: 20m38s total (14:46:56 -> 15:07:34), against a documented band of ~5-10 min warm PLUS 10-15 min cold. The run was cold (fresh sandbox, download events present, MinerU ran). It was inside the normal band. No anomaly.

Actual measured numbers from the passing run, for whoever picks this up:
  step 2 (nx index repo): 3m20s for 92 chunks across 8 flushes
  upload time per flush:  1.763 / 4.647 / 4.742 / 4.469 / 4.681 / 5.625 / 1.486 / 1.81 s (~29s total)
  peak engine RSS:        3.03 GB (vs 77.4 GB at cap=300)

## Ask

1. Measure indexing wall-clock at cap=16 vs a higher cap on a corpus LARGE ENOUGH that flushes actually hit the ceiling — the small fixture cannot answer this. Coordinate with nexus-97dp4, which wants exactly such a corpus for a different reason.
2. Either substantiate a throughput cost with real numbers or state plainly that none was observed. Then correct the docstring and CHANGELOG to match.
3. If a real cost exists, that is the input for choosing a cap ABOVE 16 — 16 was deliberately conservative and validated only at 3.03 GB peak, not optimised. Any raise must re-measure peak RSS per the docstring rule.

## Note for the record

The published PyPI/GitHub release notes for 7.5.0 are frozen with the overstated text. The in-repo CHANGELOG has been corrected on develop with a pointer under [Unreleased]. The failure mode here is the same one this session spent the day catching in other work: asserting a magnitude from arithmetic instead of measurement, then writing it into a permanent user-facing record.

Related: nexus-33hpq, nexus-97dp4, nexus-zu4ma, nexus-b32rx.

title: shakedown fixture is too small to be a memory gate — 92 chunks total, cap never binds at 16
description:
Found during the v7.5.0 cut while answering "what is the chunk count of the gate" (Hal). Referenced by a docstring note in src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py (per_collection_chunk_cap).

## Measured

release-sandbox.sh shakedown, step 2 (nx index repo) on the shakedown-fixture:
  36 files -> 92 chunks total, 8 flushes, max flush 15, mean 11.5
  grand total across every log in the gate run: 92 chunks
  collections seen in flush-complete events: code__ only

With the nexus-33hpq cap at 16, NO flush reaches the cap. The largest is 15. The cap never binds.

## Why this matters

1. The gate cannot detect a cap regression. If someone later raises the onnx-local cap from 16 to 64 (or back to 300), this fixture will still flush <=15-chunk batches per file-grain and pass green, while a real corpus reproduces the 77.4 GB blowup. The gate that caught nexus-33hpq only caught it because the corpus was small enough that a near-whole-corpus batch (~92) was ALREADY catastrophic — that was luck, not coverage.
2. It invalidates cap-derived arithmetic. The nexus-33hpq analysis (mine and the implementing agent"s) both keyed the memory model on "a 300-chunk batch". The corpus cannot produce one. The 77.4 GB came from a batch of AT MOST ~92 (bisect events observed at 82 for code, 28 for docs). Any extrapolation anchored on 300 is mis-premised; the docstring has been corrected to say so.

## Asks

1. Give the shakedown (or a dedicated gate) a corpus large enough that flushes actually REACH the configured cap, so the cap boundary is exercised.
2. Add a non-vacuity assert: fail the gate if the largest observed flush is below the configured cap — i.e. prove the run actually tested the ceiling. Without that, a green run means "the cap was never reached", which reads identically to "the cap is safe".
3. Consider asserting peak engine RSS against a budget during the indexing steps. The 77.4 GB blowup was invisible to every assertion in the gate; it was caught only because the service died and a human watched RSS. Nothing in the suite measures memory.
4. Open question, NOT answered: only code__ chunks appear in the passing run"s flush-complete events, though the earlier failing run also showed docs__. Determine whether the docs/rdr/pdf steps route through a different path (doc_indexer rather than ChunkBatcher) or merely log differently — this changes which paths the cap actually governs.

Related: nexus-33hpq (the cap fix), nexus-zu4ma (engine sub-batching), nexus-lqrec (retry storm), nexus-te9fj (stale peak figure).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIRST REAL RUN OF THE FIX, 2026-08-10 — and it reproduced this bead's own defect class.

Source: T2 [22174] `nexus/local-index-memory-gate-first-run-2026-08-10`. The gate written to
close this bead (`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`, commit 3427a030) was executed for
the first time. Recording it here bluntly because this bead exists precisely to stop a
memory gate from being theatre.

## 1. The gate has still never produced a memory measurement

Both runs (`--cap 300` and `--cap 16`, `--rss-ceiling 20`) aborted at step 3/6:
`ERROR: service never became healthy`. `_emit_json` lives at step 6/6 and was never reached.
peak_gb, flushes, flushes_at_cap, killed, wall_s, retries: **all UNMEASURED**.

Consequences for this bead's four asks:

- Ask 1 (corpus large enough that flushes reach the cap) — **NOT DEMONSTRATED.**
- Ask 2 (non-vacuity assert) — the assert EXISTS in code
  (`local-index-memory-gate.sh:225`) but has **never executed**. Its behaviour is
  UNTESTED, not "passed". A gate whose non-vacuity assert has never run is exactly the
  epistemic state this bead was filed about.
- Ask 3 (peak engine RSS against a budget) — the RSS ceiling / SIGKILL path was NEVER
  exercised. Its own author's open question — "does the 1s sampler outrun a blowup" —
  remains NOT ESTABLISHED.
- Ask 4 (why only `code__` chunks appear in flush-complete events) — untouched.

Root cause of the abort filed as **nexus-wbeyi** (P1): the health poll's
`nx ... | grep -qiE ...` under `set -o pipefail` can never return 0, AND the dead-service
message matches its accept pattern via the word "running", so fixing the pipefail bug
naively converts it into a live false-pass. Both halves must land in one change.

## 2. THE FIX FOR THIS BEAD REPRODUCED THIS BEAD'S DEFECT CLASS

This bead is "a memory gate whose ceiling is unreachable". The gate written to fix it has a
ceiling that IS reachable — but only on the wrong code path.

`chunk_batcher.py:255-260` refuses any file whose own chunk count exceeds the cap
(`len(ids) > cap -> return False`) and routes it to the LEGACY per-file paged upload. The
gate's corpus is built entirely from **oversize** files (`local-index-memory-gate.sh:33-35,
572-624`; the header calls it "a single oversize-file trick"). So every file falls off the
combined-write path. A ChunkBatcher flush reaches the cap only by accumulating MULTIPLE
files each <= cap (`chunk_batcher.py:282-297`) — a shape this corpus never produces.
`--corpus-scale N` adds more OVERSIZE files, so it scales the wrong axis and cannot fix it.

The sting: the non-vacuity assert this bead ASKED FOR would have passed anyway, because
`_largest_flush_in_log` (`:121-126`) counts the legacy
`http_vector_upsert_chunks_request count=N` family too. The gate would have reported "the
cap bound N times" while binding it only on the path the 77.4 GB incident did not run — a
green non-vacuity assert over the wrong population. Same shape as this bead, one layer
down. Filed as **nexus-c7fht** (P1).

## Standing residue

Asks 1-4 above are all still open on this bead. It cannot be closed on the existence of the
gate; it can only be closed on a run that emits a JSON line whose `chunk_flush_complete`
events reach the configured cap.

Sibling first-run findings: nexus-wizj6 (P2, `flushes_at_cap` can exceed `flushes`),
nexus-onwn7 (P2, `nx init` interactive autostart prompt), nexus-czcw5 (P3, poll discards
`nx` output). Correction to the nexus-b32rx experiment design filed as a comment there.

title: retry-storm risk: a timed-out embed request may keep running server-side while the client retry starts a second one — smaller batches mean MORE retry opportunities
description:
Raised by substantive-critic during the nexus-33hpq review (2026-08-09). NOT resolved, NOT reproduced — filed so it does not evaporate.

## Hypothesis

The nexus-33hpq symptom log shows ReadTimeout followed by manifest_write_transient_error_retry (attempts 1, 2, 3 with backoff). No synchronization was found in Bge768Embedder.java or CombinedWriteService.java that would cancel or exclude an abandoned in-flight request. So when the client times out and retries, the ORIGINAL server-side embed may still be running, and the retry starts a SECOND one. Under sustained load that compounds: N retries can mean N concurrent forward passes for the same work.

## Why it matters now specifically

The nexus-33hpq client fix lowers the onnx-local upsert cap from 300 to 16 — roughly 19x MORE round trips for the same corpus. If each round trip is an independent opportunity to time out and retry, shrinking the batch could increase total retry pressure even though it decisively reduces per-batch memory.

## Evidence FOR (weak, indirect)

- The retry ladder is visibly present in the nexus-33hpq client log.
- No cancellation/idempotency-guard found on the server embed path (searched, not exhaustively).
- ChunkBatcher runs flush_concurrency=3 (indexer.py), so several requests are in flight by design.

## Evidence AGAINST (measured, on ONE corpus)

The post-fix release-sandbox shakedown at cap=16 PASSED all 11 steps with peak RSS 3.03 GB, zero storage_service_unhealthy events, /livez 200 throughout. On this 36-file fixture the smaller batches did NOT produce a retry storm. That is one corpus at one size, and does NOT rule out the behaviour on a much larger one.

## Ask

1. Determine whether an abandoned (client-timed-out) embed request actually continues server-side, or whether the HTTP layer cancels it. This is a factual question about the engine and should be settled by reading/instrumenting, not argued.
2. If it does continue: consider request-scoped cancellation, or an idempotency/in-flight-dedup key so a retry joins the existing work rather than duplicating it.
3. Add a load-shaped test at a corpus size well beyond the 36-file shakedown fixture, asserting bounded concurrent embeds under induced timeouts.

Related: nexus-33hpq (the cap fix), nexus-zu4ma (engine-side sub-batching), nexus-b32rx (critique findings, incl. the unexplained v7.4.0-vs-v7.5.0 delta).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: RELATED BUT DISTINCT AXIS, filed 2026-08-10 as nexus-00ez4 (P2): this bead and nexus-n2w4q both model the TIMEOUT axis (abandoned server-side embeds, the 8-POST ReadTimeout ladder). Neither models the STATUS-CODE axis: ChunkBatcher._flush_batch (src/nexus/chunk_batcher.py:449) catches Exception type-blind and bisects, so a persistent 502/503/504 costs 2F-1 flush attempts, each carrying the 4-POST gateway ladder (src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py:649-653) — ~124 POSTs for a 16-file flush, aimed at a server whose problem is saturation that splitting cannot relieve. Suppressing bisect for gateway-transient codes is the single highest-leverage client-side change available and is independent of any engine tag.

title: orphaned nexus-service JVMs from deleted agent worktrees survive indefinitely — no sweep covers this class
description:
Found during the v7.5.0 release battery (2026-08-09), while triaging a wedged release-sandbox shakedown.

## Observed

16 live "java -jar .../.claude/worktrees/agent-a131fa8a8184bc71d/service/target/nexus-service-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar" processes, all belonging to a worktree directory that NO LONGER EXISTS on disk (only the then-current agent worktree remained). They had outlived their dispatching agent, their session, and the deletion of their own worktree and jar path. Each held a listening socket on a high port. Machine also carried kern.sysv.shmmni=32 (the documented macOS ceiling this project has hit before).

They had to be killed by hand: 15 died on SIGTERM, 1 needed SIGKILL.

## Why no existing mechanism caught it

scripts/sweep-test-substrates.sh (nexus-ui654) is a thin wrapper around tests._engine_substrate.sweep_stale_substrate_clusters() and is scoped to stale nexus_t2_substrate_pg_* clusters left by finished PYTEST sessions. Run against this box it correctly reported "nothing found -- clean" while all 16 orphans were live: the class it sweeps and the class that leaked are different. Confirmed by running it.

The parent-death watchdog (parent_death_watchdog_armed, storage_service_daemon) covers a service whose SUPERVISOR dies. It evidently does not cover, or did not fire for, this shape.

## Impact

Resource pressure on a shared dev box that runs multiple concurrent E2E gates and PG bundles under a 32-segment shmmni ceiling. This is the SUSPECTED (not proven) contributor to a release-sandbox shakedown wedging mid-run: the sandbox service stopped answering /livez while its PG stayed healthy (service_ok=False livez_answered=False pg_ok=True), the supervisor correctly fired storage_service_stuck_exit at consecutive_unhealthy=4 and exited 3 for an OS restart that never comes in a sandbox, and nx index repo then ground for 16+ minutes on service_endpoint_reresolved_retry. Causation is NOT established -- machine memory was 93% free when measured after the fact. The re-run on a cleaned machine is the discriminator.

## Asks

1. Extend the sweep to engine-service JVMs whose jar path is under a .claude/worktrees/<id>/ directory that no longer exists. That predicate is unambiguous and safe: a jar path that does not resolve cannot belong to a live worktree.
2. Determine why the parent-death watchdog did not reap these. If a worktree agent exits without the supervisor dying, is anything responsible for the child?
3. Consider a dispatch-time or SubagentStop-time sweep so agent-worktree services do not outlive their agent.

## Method note worth keeping

The first census of this used "pgrep -c java || echo 0" and printed 0 while orphans were plainly running: macOS pgrep has NO -c count flag, so the command errored and the || fallback manufactured a clean reading. Use "pgrep -f PATTERN | wc -l" on macOS. This is the same vacuous-measurement shape the 2026-08-09 sweep catalogued.

Related: nexus-ui654 (PG substrate sweep), nexus-mqm5w (filed same day).

title: restart-stale emits a false NEEDS HUMAN whenever stop exits non-zero — rc short-circuits the convergence verify
description:
Found during the v7.5.0 release battery (step 1c, tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh --package-upgrade). PRE-EXISTING, shipped in v7.4.0 — NOT a 7.5.0 regression. Adjudicated DOES-NOT-BLOCK for 7.5.0; fix targets develop AFTER the cut.

## Symptom

nx daemon restart-stale printed "NEEDS HUMAN: the service restart did not report success" even though convergence fully succeeded: restart-stale rc=0, "converged engine" action fired, new stack came up on v0.1.69, +7 Liquibase changesets, service_ready, health ok, post-convergence T1 put/get round-trip passed, pre-upgrade T1 row survived, old pids absent after the restart. A false alarm, not a missed convergence.

## Root cause (primary)

src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:908-915 — _restart_and_verify returns the NEEDS HUMAN early whenever stop.returncode != 0 or start.returncode != 0, BEFORE it ever calls _running_engine(). This is the nexus-4yf4u fallacy with the sign flipped: a returncode proves the commands ran, not that the service came up — and that cuts both ways. In this run the very next branch (:938) would have evaluated TRUE, since after.version == REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION == (0,1,69).

Internal inconsistency confirming the defect: the success branch at :939-947 carries a comment explicitly anticipating this exact case — "an incomplete stop is a real event even when the cycle then went on to converge, and silence here would hide the very condition that used to make this a coin flip". The early return makes that branch unreachable precisely when its comment applies.

## Root cause (secondary — why stop rc=1)

- src/nexus/daemon/service_registry.py:790 pid_alive is a bare os.kill(pid, 0), which CANNOT distinguish a zombie or a process mid-teardown from a live one.
- service_registry.py:815 terminate_pids judges "stubborn" only 0.5s after SIGKILL, on that same predicate.
- service_registry.py:898 sweep -> storage_service_daemon.py:1736 stubborn-survivors warning -> commands/daemon.py:1029-1040 converts stubborn into rc=1 (deliberate, nexus-oyo2g).

Note for future readers: storage_service_daemon.py:1520-1522 documents that the supervisor_exit exit_code=0 line is a BREADCRUMB logged BEFORE sup.stop(), so a clean supervisor_exit does NOT prove the pid had exited. The observed 10.46s gap decomposes as two serial 5.0s teardown windows (_GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT=5.0) plus the 0.5s post-SIGKILL sleep.

## Falsified hypotheses (do not re-litigate)

Zombie-reaping in a reaperless container was investigated and DISPROVED empirically: across three docker shapes on python:3.12-slim with NO --init and PID 1 = a bash script, with the victim double-forked so it reparents to PID 1 (plain foreground killer; killer in command substitution; silent killer in command substitution with bash blocked in a single read), the orphan was reaped in under 1s every time — bash as PID 1 does reap adopted orphans via waitchld/waitpid(-1). A 900MB-RSS orphan also left the process table in 3.8ms, so the 0.5s post-SIGKILL check is not racing teardown. Adding --init to the harness would change nothing.

## Residual (not closed)

The exact reason BOTH pids were still os.kill-visible at +0.5s is not fully settled by the logs. Closing that last inch needs an instrumented re-run capturing /proc/<pid>/stat state characters. That is bead work, not release work.

## Fix direction

Delete the rc-based early return at :908-915; thread the transcript into an rc_note carried on the success line instead. Fail-closed is preserved: a genuinely failed start leaves after.version None and still reaches the final NEEDS HUMAN at the end of the function.

## Test gap that let this ship

tests/test_upgrade_finish.py:558 is the ONLY wiring test for this path and it hardcodes returncode=0. No test in the suite ever feeds stop.returncode != 0, so the early return has never once been measured against a converged outcome. Land a PAIR: (1) positive — rc=1 + converged => NO NEEDS HUMAN (must fail on todays tree); (2) non-vacuity negative — rc=1 + still on the old version => MUST still emit NEEDS HUMAN (must go red if the version comparison is deleted).

## Explicitly NOT the fix

Do NOT widen the grep exclusion at tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_package_upgrade.sh:258. That assert is correctly reporting a real emitted line; the defect is upstream of it.

Analysis: T2 nexus/debug-pkg-upgrade-gate-needs-human-2026-08-09 [22132]. Release-cut state: T2 [22131].

title: the false-portability idiom 'stat -f FMT X 2>/dev/null || stat -c FMT X' appears in 3 more shell files — on GNU it emits a filesystem-info block into the captured output before the fallback fires
description: Sibling occurrences found while fixing the same defect in tests/e2e/lib/expectations_test.sh (nexus-3zu8g, commit 8e5a36d4), which the new gate caught on its first Linux CI run. THE TRAP: on GNU coreutils, stat's -f is a REAL flag ('display filesystem status'), NOT BSD's '-f FORMAT'. So  parses '%Lp' and X as two FILE arguments — it fails on the nonexistent '%Lp' (stderr, suppressed by 2>/dev/null) but SUCCEEDS on X, printing a multi-line 'File: ...' filesystem block to STDOUT, which is NOT suppressed. The compound exit is still non-zero so the || fallback also runs, but the garbage is already inside the captured . Result: a value like 'File: "/path"\n ID: ...\n700' where '700' was expected. REMAINING SITES: (1) tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh:357 (BUNDLE_SIZE) — looks LIVE-BUGGY on Linux, likely the highest value fix; (2) tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh:369 — cosmetic echo only; (3) scripts/rdr152-sandbox/prod-copy.sh:43. FIX: the same explicit uname -s branch used at 8e5a36d4 (_stat_perms helper: Darwin -> stat -f '%Lp', else -> stat -c '%a'), or a shared helper if a common lib exists. VERIFY ON BOTH PLATFORMS — a fix validated only on macOS reproduces the defect. NOTE the general lesson worth carrying beyond stat: 'try the BSD form, fall back on failure' is unsafe whenever the other platform's flag is valid-but-different, because the first attempt can partially succeed and contaminate output before the fallback runs.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: DESCRIPTION REPAIR (orchestrator error, SECOND occurrence today — see nexus-i514o for the first): two code fragments were eaten by unescaped backticks in my bd-create command (bash command substitution inside a double-quoted string), so the description reads "So  parses" and "inside the captured ." with the fragments missing. The two lost fragments, in single quotes this time: the invocation is  stat -f (percent)Lp X 2>/dev/null || stat -c (percent)a X , and the contaminated capture is a  $(...)  command substitution. Nothing else in the description was affected. LESSON, since I now have two instances in one session: never put backticks in a bd description passed through a double-quoted shell string — use single quotes for the whole argument, or a heredoc.

title: credit slots orphaned by a killed hook are never reclaimed within a session, and expectations_census counts ROWS not SLOTS — so the pool decays monotonically and census cannot see the decay
description: The genuine remainder of the nexus-ols6a round (2026-08-09) after the disclosure half was fixed at fc066671. TWO HALVES, both real: (1) NO INTRA-SESSION RECLAIM — a slot claimed by a hook that is then SIGKILLed (routine: hooks.json gives SubagentStop a 10s timeout while the lock budget is 20-60s) is stranded for the life of the session; only expectations_sweep's -mtime +7 ever removes it, which is useless at session scale. So a long session's per-type credit pool decays monotonically as kills accumulate. The fc066671 fix makes each individual decay VISIBLE (a lost claim while rows say credit remains now BLOCKS with cause=credit-slot-orphan instead of silently passing), which is the important half — but the pool still shrinks. (2) CENSUS/GUARD DISAGREEMENT — expectations_census counts ledger ROWS; the orphan is a SYMLINK no audit surface reads. So census reports a clean ledger in exactly the state where the guard is degraded, and an operator reading undeclared=0 gets a weaker assurance than they think. FIX DIRECTION (the real one): teach census to see slots, so the two surfaces agree about the same ledger; optionally a session-scoped reclaim, but NOT a bounded-age check-then-act reap — that reintroduces the TOCTOU shape round 3 correctly removed. NOTE the masking subtlety found while building the orphan test: a hook killed mid-claim orphans its LOCKDIR as well as its slot, so for ~60s subsequent stops block with lock-exhausted and the stale lock MASKS the orphaned slot; the silent-miss window opens only after the 60s reap clears the mask. Related: nexus-7z7rj, nexus-ols6a, nexus-ma5tg, nexus-3zu8g.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING (critic delta on fc066671, MEASURED not reasoned — I wrote 'decays monotonically' and that is too strong). TWO SELF-HEALING PROPERTIES: (1) THE STICKY OVER-BLOCK SELF-CLEARS. With an orphan and credit=2, subsequent agents do block with cause=credit-slot-orphan — but the moment a new EXPECT row of that type arrives (credit 2->3) the next agent claims normally with NO cause. So ONE killed hook costs only the agents arriving between the kill and the next same-type declaration, NOT 'the rest of the session'. The pool does not decay monotonically in any session that keeps dispatching that type — which is the normal case. (2) AN HONEST DRY POOL DOES NOT CRY WOLF: credit=2 with 4 sequential agents gives two credit-backed blocks and two clean does-not-owe returns with no cause — so the new alarm does not fire on legitimate exhaustion. ALSO CORRECTED: NX_EXPECT_LOCK_TRIES=200 is set ONLY inside pytest extra_env — never in production, never in CI env. At the shipped default of 10 tries (~1s) the lockdir-masking window is ~1s, not ~60s, and the 'later stops block with lock-exhausted, safe and disclosed' framing is correct. NET: this bead is still real (census counts ROWS while the orphan is a SYMLINK, so the two surfaces genuinely disagree, and that is the half worth fixing), but its severity is lower than filed and the census-visibility half is now clearly the priority over any reclaim mechanism.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REFRAMING (Hal, 2026-08-09) THAT POINTS AT A BETTER FIX DIRECTION THAN THE ONE FILED: 'this is load handling — the credits ARE the slots.' Correct, and it makes the residual a textbook LEAKED-PERMIT problem rather than a bespoke ledger quirk. The credit pool is a counting semaphore; a claim is a permit; the orphan is a permit leaked by a holder that died. That reclassification matters because the failure modes and remedies of counting semaphores are well understood, and it explains the whole three-round history.

THE ROOT CONSTRAINT, verified on this box: macOS has NO flock(1) binary (util-linux only), so the BASH shellib cannot use a kernel-backed advisory lock at all. Contrast the PYTHON side: nexus/_locking.py wraps fcntl.flock, which AUTO-RELEASES on process death (the kernel closes fds on exit, including SIGKILL) — which is exactly why nexus-ui654's boot semaphore, built the same week on the same 'slots' idea, has NO orphan problem and this one does. Same abstraction, different primitive, and the entire difference is death semantics.

THE CAUSAL CHAIN THAT FOLLOWS: no auto-release -> you need a reap -> a reap needs check-then-act -> check-then-act is stealable (that IS nexus-7z7rj's round-3 root cause: [[ -d ]] / find / rmdir deletes a live holder's lock) -> moving to symlink slots fixed the ceiling but inherited 'no auto-release', which is this bead. Three rounds of narrowing were all downstream of a missing primitive.

FIX DIRECTION SUPERSEDING 'teach census to see slots' (keep that as the cheap interim): give the shell hook a primitive with correct death semantics by DELEGATING the critical section to Python, which already has fcntl.flock via nexus._locking. A flock held only from read-decide through row-append and released after gives all three properties at once — mutual exclusion without a reap (so no stolen-lock class), auto-release on SIGKILL (so no orphan class), and rows remaining the durable debit. Cost is one python fork+exec per stop (~50-100ms) against the hook's 10s budget, which is affordable; measure before adopting. If that is too heavy, the fallback is to keep symlink slots but have the SAME python helper sweep permits whose owner pid is dead at claim time — note that reintroduces check-then-act, so it must be done in one process, not in shell steps.

CROSS-REFERENCE: nexus-ui654 is the worked example of the correct primitive; nexus-7z7rj carries the three-round history; nexus-ma5tg has the identical shape still live in agent-dispatch-expect.sh.

title: chash-rekey verify() blast-radius claim overstates backfill_diag_role_best_effort as unconditional — it only fires on an actual engine version transition
design:
nexus-hdumg review finding (review-hdumg-fix-2026-08-09, code-review-expert),
on commit b85496b8 (worktree agent-ac2e1beee0b2310cf).

The fix's commit message and T2 report (nexus/nexus-hdumg-root-cause-2026-08-09
[22093]) argue the blast radius of the new VERIFY_FAILED behavior is bounded
because "both remedies for an unmeasurable store already run on this same
upgrade path (backfill_diag_role_best_effort for absent credentials,
reprovision_diag_view_best_effort inside this rung's own converge for an
absent view)... the stop costs a re-run, never the store."

Verified in code: reprovision_diag_view_best_effort() is genuinely
UNCONDITIONAL — chash_rekey.py's converge() calls self._reprovision_fn()
every time converge() runs (i.e. every time the rung isn't already
converged-and-recorded).

backfill_diag_role_best_effort() is NOT unconditional. Its only call site
is upgrade_finish.py:611, inside _poison_probe(), which is only reached
from converge_engine(config_dir) at upgrade_finish.py:1159. converge_engine
is only invoked from TWO triggers, both gated on an actual pending ENGINE
VERSION TRANSITION, never on every nx upgrade invocation:

  1. commands/upgrade.py's _converge_preconditions -> preconditions.py's
     converge_preconditions(): engine_converge() only called when
     `engine_status.applicable and not engine_status.converged and
     allow_engine_install` — i.e. only when the engine is NOT already at
     the current version, AND allow_engine_install is True (which itself
     is `not auto_mode and not skip_t3` — so --auto invocations never
     reach it via this path either).
  2. upgrade_finish.check_version_transition() (root `nx` CLI group,
     fires before any subcommand): its own docstring says it "returns None
     when the stamp is current (the overwhelmingly common case)" — i.e.
     also gated on an actual version-stamp mismatch.

So on a box where the engine is ALREADY at its converged/current version
(steady state — the common case for most nx upgrade invocations, not just
the version-transition moment) and nexus_diag credentials are missing for
ANY reason other than "mid version-transition" (lost/corrupted credentials
file, a fresh PG data dir without re-running nx init, a manually revoked
role, etc.), backfill_diag_role_best_effort NEVER RUNS in that invocation.
The chash-rekey rung's own converge() does not call it either (only
reprovision_diag_view_best_effort is wired as reprovision_fn) — verified
via `grep -rn backfill_diag_role_best_effort src/nexus/`: exactly one call
site exists.

Consequence: on such a box, `nx upgrade` (non-auto) will VERIFY_FAILED
with an actionable message pointing at `nx init --service` (confirmed
good UX — this is not a silent brick), but the "costs a re-run, never the
store" framing is incomplete: a passive re-run of `nx upgrade` will NOT
self-heal this specific case, since nothing in that re-run's own call
graph runs the role backfill either (same conditional gate, same absent
transition). The operator must take the MANUAL nx init --service step the
message names, not just "try again". This does not make the fix wrong
(loud+actionable strictly beats the old silent false-pass), but the
blast-radius risk assessment in the commit/report is more optimistic than
the code actually supports for this one remedy.

Recommended low-cost fix: wire backfill_diag_role_best_effort() into
chash_rekey.py's own converge() alongside self._reprovision_fn(), the same
way reprovision_diag_view_best_effort already is — this closes the gap
symmetrically and makes the "costs a re-run" framing accurate for both
remedies, not just one. backfill_diag_role_best_effort() is already
idempotent, best-effort, and zero-arg (src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py:884) —
trivial to call from a second reprovision-style seam.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: DUPLICATE of nexus-ueshf (same finding, filed from the substantive-critic's trace minutes earlier). Your more precise tracing — the version-transition gating, the single call site, and the wire-into-the-rung's-own-converge fix — has been copied onto ueshf, which is the bead of record. Two independent reviewers finding this from different directions is worth noting: it means the commit's framing was misleading enough to catch twice.

title: diag-role backfill is NOT unconditional on the upgrade path: backfill_diag_role_best_effort only runs via converge_engine, gated off under --auto and after the engine has converged — so a broken diag ROLE gets zero automatic remedy on the most common invocation
description: Found by the substantive-critic while verifying nexus-hdumg's blast-radius claim (T2 critique-hdumg-fix-2026-08-09 [22098]), by tracing the call graph rather than trusting the commit message. THE CLAIM under review was that both diag remedies already run on the same upgrade path before verify(), which bounds the impact of hdumg making an unmeasurable rung VERIFY_FAILED. HALF TRUE: reprovision_diag_view_best_effort (the VIEW remedy) is genuinely unconditional, every invocation. But backfill_diag_role_best_effort (the ROLE/credentials remedy) is only reachable via converge_engine(), gated by allow_engine_install = (not auto_mode and not skip_t3) AND (not engine_status.converged). CONSEQUENCE: under --auto — the hook-driven and arguably most common real invocation — it NEVER runs; and even interactively it stops running once the engine has converged, which is exactly the retry the new VERIFY_FAILED error text recommends. So a user whose diag ROLE (not view) is broken, on --auto or on a post-convergence retry, gets ZERO automatic backfill attempts and a hard-stopped ladder. NOT a brick: the error text names nx init --service, which calls _create_roles directly rather than the same best-effort wrapper, so a working escalation exists — which is why the critic still recommended shipping hdumg. FIX DIRECTIONS: either make the role backfill reachable on the --auto/post-convergence path before verify runs, or state plainly in the error text that the automatic role remedy does not run in this mode and name the manual one first. Correct the 'both remedies already run' framing wherever it is recorded before anyone relies on it. Related: nexus-hdumg (the fix this bounds), RDR-182.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: MERGED WITH nexus-o0ndo (filed independently by the code-review-expert minutes later, same finding from a different trace). Keeping this bead; o0ndo closed as dup. THE REVIEWER'S TRACE IS MORE PRECISE THAN THE CRITIC'S — adopt it: backfill_diag_role_best_effort has exactly ONE call site, reached via _poison_probe -> converge_engine, whose TWO triggers (_converge_preconditions and root-level check_version_transition) are BOTH gated on an actual pending ENGINE VERSION TRANSITION. check_version_transition's own docstring says it returns None 'when the stamp is current, the overwhelmingly common case'. The preconditions path ADDITIONALLY skips on --auto. So the gap is wider than the critic's --auto framing: on ANY steady-state box (engine already converged, no version transition pending) with diag credentials broken for a non-transition reason, NOTHING self-heals on a passive re-run — the operator must run nx init --service manually, which the error text does correctly name, so it is not a silent trap. CONCRETE CHEAP FIX (reviewer's, adopt it): wire backfill_diag_role_best_effort into the chash-rekey rung's OWN converge(), symmetric with the existing reprovision_diag_view_best_effort wiring that IS unconditional there. That makes both remedies genuinely run before verify on every invocation, restoring the blast-radius argument as originally stated.

title: expectations: agent-dispatch-expect.sh reap steals a live lock (same TOCTOU class as nexus-7z7rj)
description:
conexus/hooks/scripts/agent-dispatch-expect.sh:137-138 carries the IDENTICAL reap-then-contend pattern nexus-7z7rj root-caused in expectations_owes_report:

    if [[ -d "$LOCKDIR" ]] && [[ -z "$(find "$LOCKDIR" -maxdepth 0 -mmin -1 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
        rmdir "$LOCKDIR" 2>/dev/null
    fi

-d / find / rmdir are three steps; the holder can release and a third writer legitimately re-acquire between them, so the rmdir deletes a LIVE holder's lock and two writers end up in _expect_if_absent's critical section at once. Deterministically reproduced for the owes_report copy with injected scheduling delay (see nexus-7z7rj round 3).

BLAST RADIUS HERE IS DIFFERENT and needs its own analysis before fixing: the CS writes EXPECT rows idempotently, so a steal yields DUPLICATE EXPECT rows. expectations_undeclared/census dedupe EXPECT by dispatch_id ($5) and are therefore protected; expectations_owes_report's awk does NOT dedupe by dispatch_id, so a duplicate inflates that type's credit pool. Direction is over-credit -> more agents classified as owing -> over-block (safe), but it also makes the census and the stop-guard disagree about the same ledger, and CLAUDE.md already warns that an inflated credit pool can mask an undeclared start.

Fix options are the same two as 7z7rj, and 7z7rj's conclusion applies verbatim: safely stealing a name-based lock needs an atomic compare-and-delete that POSIX does not provide. Either (a) never reap and accept a SIGKILL-leaked lock wedging dispatch registration, or (b) make the write idempotent by an atomic primitive so lock correctness stops mattering (the 7z7rj slot-symlink shape). Prefer (b) for symmetry.

Context: nx

title: vacuous-verification family in src/nexus: four checks that pass over an empty or unreadable input set — doctor_search empty-collections, sql_lint empty-segments, storage_boundary_lint unreadable-file and missing-src, reconcile all-over-empty
description:
Batch from the codebase-wide vacuous-verification sweep (full detail + swept-clean negative space in T2 nexus/sweep-vacuous-verification-src-nexus-2026-08-09 [22088]). Same defect class as nexus-hdumg and nexus-v2mdd: the check passes because it examined NOTHING, and nothing distinguishes that from genuinely-clean. Each needs a test proving the vacuous case, which is why these are batched separately from v2mdd's 6-line fixes.
1. src/nexus/doctor_search.py:452 run_check_search — _list_collections() returning [] skips the retrieval probe entirely (guard :437), so any([]) is False and zero-collections-scanned exits 0 identically to all-healthy. Gates nx doctor search exit code 2 + the retrieval_quality JSON. FIX: emit an outcome=error enumerate row when the collection list is empty.
2. src/nexus/remediation/sql_lint.py:123 is_read_only_diagnostic — the aggregate-only loop over _select_segments() is vacuously satisfied when the regex matches nothing, contradicting _select_segments' own fail-closed docstring. Gates the RDR-182 section-5 content boundary in the legacy-grants era (mitigated today by view-era DB grants, so latent not live). FIX: if not segments, return False with a reason.
3. src/nexus/storage_boundary_lint.py:513 _scan_file_full — OSError/UnicodeDecodeError/SyntaxError returns an empty FileScan, indistinguishable from a clean file; LintResult carries no scanned-file counter. AND :694 _iter_py_files — a missing or renamed src/ returns [], so zero files scanned reads as zero violations. Gates the sqlite3.connect / voyageai.Client storage-boundary CI gate — i.e. the gate that enforces the NO-SQLITE hot rule. FIX: scanned-file counter in LintResult with a non-vacuity floor, and surface unreadable files as violations rather than silence.
4. src/nexus/db/reconcile.py:305 MigrationReport.ok — all([]) is True over an empty results tuple, producible by verify_fill_collections :804-833; the verdict is logged at :842. FIX: bool(self.results) and all(...).
Related: nexus-v2mdd (the two HIGH fail-open-to-green surfaces), nexus-hdumg (the rung that started this), RDR-182 never-a-silent-all-clean.

title: migration-rehearsal: no invocation exercises the Phase D daily-driver surface against Voyage
description:
Consequent of nexus-f4apk (the --comprehensive/--stress + --with-cloud incoherence
guard, same commit as nexus-elt26): Phase D/E are deterministic bge-768 LOCAL by
construction (rehearse.sh's own header), --with-cloud boots a voyage-only service,
and the two are now guarded as mutually exclusive in run.sh. That guard is correct
(the alternative was an unguarded HTTP 422 downstream) but it makes the gap
permanent by construction: NO flag combination of tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/
run.sh exercises the T2/T1/T3/catalog/doctor daily-driver surface against a
Voyage-serving engine. --with-cloud alone asserts nothing past Phase A's
install-time checks; --comprehensive/--stress only ever run against onnx-local.

This is exactly the surface a real cloud deploy exercises (T2 conexus/[22073], the
v0.1.69 rehearsal relay that surfaced the whole finding class), so the gap is worth
closing deliberately rather than left implicit. Wanted: a voyage-capable Phase-D
variant — either a new rehearse_comprehensive_cloud.sh entrypoint (mirroring the
--guided/--cold split already in run.sh) or a --with-cloud-aware branch inside
rehearse.sh's existing Phase D that swaps the bge-768 assertions for
voyage-context-3-appropriate ones (collection naming, embedder identity). Sizing:
too large for the elt26/f4apk fix commit (which only adds the guard + documents
the gap in run.sh's header and rehearse.sh's phase table) — this bead is the
follow-up.

Not urgent: Run 3 in the v0.1.69 rehearsal (bare --comprehensive, no --with-cloud)
already proves the daily-driver surface works end-to-end on SOME embedder; what's
missing is proof it also works when the serving embedder is Voyage specifically,
which is the production cloud shape.

title: migration-rehearsal: --comprehensive + --with-cloud is an unguarded incoherent combination (Phase D is bge-768-local, --with-cloud is voyage-only) — and no flag combination exercises Phase D against Voyage at all
description: Reported by conexus from the v0.1.69 rehearsal (relay T2 conexus/[22073], finding 3 + consequent gap). run.sh ALREADY guards the identical class — '--guided and --with-cloud are incoherent (guided seeds local bge-768 targets; cloud is voyage-only); run --guided alone' → exit 2 — but Phase D carries the SAME bge-768-local dependency with NO guard, so --comprehensive --with-cloud arg-parses cleanly and fails downstream at the engine with HTTP 422 (correct engine behavior: cross-model contamination refusal, v0.1.69 not at fault). --stress/Phase E likely wants the same check. CONSEQUENT COVERAGE GAP, the more interesting half: because the voyage leg and the daily-driver leg are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION, NO single invocation exercises Phase D's surface against Voyage — Run 1 boots voyage but asserts nothing past install; Run 3 asserts the full surface on onnx-local. ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED 2026-08-09 (debugger, worktree agent-a3352af28bd817193, commit 3a9aafb3, UNPUSHED). NOT production write loss, NOT engine-side, does NOT belong in the v0.1.69 engine payload.

CAUSE: tests/test_catalog_e2e.py::injected_active was a bare `return` fixture assigning mcp_infra._t3_instance = local_t3 (a T3Database over the in-process InMemoryVectorClient) with no teardown. _t3_instance is a PROCESS-WIDE singleton and doc_indexer._index_document resolves its write handle via mcp_infra.get_t3() in service mode (RDR-152 Seam B) — so that singleton sits on the production CLI write path, not just the MCP tool path. Any injected_active test poisoned its xdist worker; a later `nx index md` in the same process wrote its chunk into an in-memory dict, never reached PG, and the RUNFENCE completion check correctly refused (referenced=1 present=0). The verify side was right every time; the write never happened.

NOT LOAD-SENSITIVE. xdist distributes tests to workers DYNAMICALLY, so which tests share a worker varies per run; load merely correlated. Reproduced deterministically at load_avg 2.85.

FALSIFYING EVIDENCE (all from the already-captured 2026-08-09 06:02 run — this was decidable a day ago): (1) http_vector_upsert_chunks_request (INFO) and upsert_skip_reembed_upsert_outcome (DEBUG) shipped in the SAME commit e52a0907, yet the failing run's COMPLETE, untruncated CLI output carries the outcome line and ZERO http_vector_* lines; (2) branch->outcome spans 89 microseconds while the existing_ids probe in the same process took 2.8ms — no HTTP round trip fits in 89us; (3) probed that the INFO line IS visible under the journey's NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG config, so the absence is real signal, not filtering. The cross-tenant existence-partition / RLS-GUC-bleed hypothesis is FALSIFIED: nothing reached the engine, so no tenant-context question arises. The remaining fork from the 08-08 capture (upsert-never-sent vs acked-but-lost vs landed-then-removed) resolves to UPSERT-NEVER-SENT.

-> 1 failed, 1 passed; identical signature, identical missing chash 606712df69a1..., 55us branch->outcome gap, zero http_vector_* lines.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
EVIDENCE LOOP CLOSED — the "orchestrator-invoked reds 3/3 vs debugger-invoked greens 3/3, environmental delta unexplained" asymmetry (recorded in the 2026-08-09 13:04 comment) reconciles with the worker-colocation root cause. It is a co-location/scheduling question, NOT an environmental delta. Two of the three legs are now hard evidence; the third is honestly partial.

LEG 1 — three of the debugger-invoked greens never collected the poisoning file at all (DETERMINISTIC, hard evidence). From the run table in T2 [21831]: run 3 was `tests/test_scenario_journeys.py -n auto` (journeys alone); run 4 was `tests/db tests/catalog tests/test_scenario_journeys.py -n0` (1458 tests, ONE worker); run 7 was `test_doc_indexer + test_index_cmd + test_indexer_e2e + hooks + 5xn3k + catalog + scenario -n0` (822 tests, ONE worker). Runs 4 and 7 are the strongest APPARENT counter-evidence to this root cause — single-worker runs with hundreds/thousands of preceding tests in one process, exactly the poisoning setup — and they passed. The reason is selection: `tests/catalog/` is a DIRECTORY (test_catalog_conformance.py, test_catalog_protocol_fidelity.py, ...); the poisoning file is `tests/test_catalog_e2e.py`, which is NOT inside it. Verified in the tree. Those runs never collected `injected_active`, so no poison could exist. Not an environmental delta — a selection artifact.

LEG 2 — the full probe-armed greens DID run the poisoning file, and only ONE worker of ~16 was poisoned (MEASURED). Runs 5/6/8 were full `-n auto`, so selection is not the explanation, and test_catalog_e2e.py demonstrably executed: it contributed 71 of run 8's 130 refusal events. Run 8's per-worker probe artifacts SURVIVE at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hal-hildebrand-git-nexus/8469eaba-e90c-4d20-8ddf-9e8afe2cd8e5/scratchpad/refusals-gw*.jsonl. Parsing them by nodeid: ALL SIX `injected_active` tests (test_search_returns_indexed_files, test_search_structured_filter, test_show_returns_full_entry, test_resolve_returns_collections, test_search_then_traverse_links, test_link_creation_via_title) landed on a SINGLE worker, gw5. Workers ran gw0..gw15. So in that green run exactly 1 of ~16 workers was poisoned, and the journeys landed elsewhere. Green is the EXPECTED outcome of that distribution, not evidence against the root cause. Symmetrically, in the 2026-08-09 06:02 red both journeys ran on the SAME worker, gw8 (xdist_worker=gw8 on both failures) — one poisoned worker carrying both.

LEG 3 — why the orchestrator-invoked runs co-located 3/3 is NOT proven, and I will not claim it. Per-worker artifacts exist only for run 8; nothing comparable was captured for the reds, so the actual distribution in those runs is unrecoverable. If co-location were ~1/16 per run as measured in run 8, three consecutive reds would be a ~0.02% coincidence — implausible, so something systematic did differ. The plausible mechanism, consistent with every observation but unproven: xdist's default `--dist load` deals tests to workers dynamically (no `--dist` in addopts), so under heavy load (the reds ran at load_avg 43 on 16 cores) workers progress at very uneven rates and a consecutive block like the six TestMCP tests gets SPREAD across many workers instead of clustering on one, raising the chance a journey's worker was previously poisoned from ~1/16 toward ~6/16. That single mechanism would explain both the load correlation and the invocation asymmetry without any environmental delta. It is CONSISTENT-WITH but NOT PROVEN-BY the surviving evidence.

NOT IMPLICATED: the probe plugin. It changed no code path in the mechanism; run 8 shows it green simply because the poison was confined to gw5. The 13:04 comment's framing of a "debugger-invoked vs orchestrator-invoked environmental delta" is retired — the variable is which worker got the poison, and all three green legs are now accounted for (two deterministically, one by measurement).

Bottom line: nothing in the asymmetry contradicts the root cause, and the two runs that looked most like a refutation (4 and 7) are explained by their selections excluding tests/test_catalog_e2e.py. The residual unknown is only the 3/3 clustering of the reds, which does not bear on the diagnosis or the fix — the fix removes the poison entirely, so co-location stops mattering.

title: test_serialize_false_opts_out_of_the_lock_entirely is vacuous — mutation-confirmed
description:
Found during substantive-critic review of the uncommitted eslkl bundle (2026-08-08), develop @ 6ebee497. Critique: T2 memory nexus/critique-eslkl-bundle-2026-08-08.

tests/test_indexer_concurrency.py::TestLockedHookRegistry::test_serialize_false_opts_out_of_the_lock_entirely is the ONLY test covering LockedHookRegistry's serialize=False opt-out — the exact mechanism production's taxonomy_assign_batch_hook.serialize=False depends on. Falsified by deleting the code (house directive): removed the `if getattr(hook, "serialize", True) is False: return hook(*args, **kwargs)` short-circuit from hook_registry.py's LockedHookRegistry._invoke (i.e. made the opt-out a no-op, every hook always locks) and the test STILL PASSED.

Root cause: the test uses a 2-party threading.Barrier(timeout=5) inside the hook body and asserts `not errors` where errors is only populated if locked.fire_batch(...) itself raises. But HookRegistry.fire_batch has its own per-hook `except Exception: log + persist hook_failures` wrapper that NEVER re-raises. So when the opt-out is broken and both fires serialize, thread 1 enters the hook, blocks on the barrier waiting for a second party that can never arrive (thread 2 is stuck queued on the same lock), and after the 5s barrier timeout thread 1 gets BrokenBarrierError — which fire_batch's own exception handling swallows silently. The test's fire() wrapper never sees an exception either way, so `errors` stays empty whether the hooks ran concurrently (real pass) or serialized-then-silently-failed (should-be-fail, reads as pass). Confirmed both ways empirically.

Fix: assert on an independent, non-swallowed signal that both threads were genuinely inside the hook body concurrently — e.g. a shared counter incremented before `barrier.wait()` and decremented after, asserted to hit 2 via a separate polling thread or Event, or have the hook body write its own thread id to a list under a lock at entry/exit and assert two entries had no non-overlapping window — not a mechanism whose failure path funnels back through hook_registry's swallow-everything per-hook exception handling.
close_reason: Landed in develop 13cd7029; dual-reviewed; suite 12093 green.

title: nexus-11gh6 design gap: StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant:336 is a FIFTH catalog_document_chunks insert site (raw SQL) — outside the sweep-gate enumeration AND test 7d's insertInto() scan pattern
description:
Found by the plan-audit pass on the nexus-11gh6 sweep-gate design (T2 design-11gh6-sweep-write-skew-closure [21768]), develop @ 6ebee497.

The design memo and plan enumerate four insertInto(CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS) writer sites (CatalogRepository.java:3512, 4095, 6461, 6487) and gate them shared. But StagingPromoteOps.finalizeTenant's manifest promote (StagingPromoteOps.java:336) INSERTs into nexus.catalog_document_chunks via RAW SQL. It is not in the memo's §2 mechanism, not in §3's residual list, and the proposed 7d source-scanning tripwire (which greps the typed insertInto pattern) cannot see it — a raw-SQL site silently reopens the gap 7d exists to close.

Worse than a bare enumeration miss: finalizeTenant's canonExists arm (lines 331-344) READS chunks_384/768/1024 to prove content existence, then inserts the manifest row — exactly the read-then-insert shape that races the exclusive sweep (sweep deletes the chunk after canonExists observed it, finalize inserts a now-dangling reference). Mitigations that make this P2 not P1: single-actor migration-era path, per-tenant 'staging:' advisory serialization already present (line 272), and manifest_verify surfaces the dangle as missing>0.

Fix options (either acceptable, per the memo's own exact-scope discipline):
(a) take the sweep gate SHARED at the top of finalizeTenant's txn (before the 'staging:' lock for uniform gate-first ordering) — note the insert spans MANY collections (staging.document_chunks is tenant-wide), so the gate key needs the collection set or a tenant-wide shared key; or
(b) add it to memo §3's explicitly-not-closed list with the purge_trash-style single-actor rationale.
EITHER WAY: test 7d must scan BOTH the typed insertInto(CATALOG_DOCUMENT_CHUNKS pattern AND raw 'INSERT INTO nexus.catalog_document_chunks' in main source, or the tripwire is vacuous against raw-SQL writers.

Blocks the 11gh6 implementation pass only in the sense that the memo/javadoc residual list must name it before 'closes the write-skew' ships (round-1 overclaim lesson, memo §5).

title: sweep TOCTOU: batched fast-branch widens cross-fire race window under NX_INDEX_CONCURRENCY=1 (unlocked flush_concurrency=3)
design:
Found during substantive-critic review of nexus-tgrgs/jk88j/67qsd (T2 nexus/critique-tgrgs-jk88j-67qsd-batch-manifest-sweep-2026-08-08), develop uncommitted @94949df9.

_sweep_superseded_vectors_many's docstring (mcp_infra.py) accepts the cross-FIRE sweep TOCTOU race (design memo T2 nexus/design-eslkl-hook-lock-narrowing §2b) with: "flush-grain fires remain serialized by LockedHookRegistry for now". This is true only when resolve_index_concurrency() > 1 (indexer.py:3593 gates LockedHookRegistry construction on it). ChunkBatcher(flush_concurrency=3) at indexer.py:3881 is UNCONDITIONAL -- 3 flush workers fire the flush-grain hook chain concurrently regardless. Under NX_INDEX_CONCURRENCY=1 (explicitly named "a supported configuration today" in the design memo), the hook registry stays bare/unlocked and the NEW batched fast-branch sweep genuinely widens the pre-existing per-doc race window: the old sequential per-doc loop gave each doc a tight, independent read-write-sweep cycle; the new fast branch reads the WHOLE batch upfront, so any individual doc's window from its own stale read to its own sweep decision now spans the whole batch's write_manifest_many call. Moderate widening (round-trip count drops, but per-batch wall time for the write step likely goes up with doc count) -- not measured.

Recommend: (a) correct the docstring to state the LockedHookRegistry protection is conditional on concurrency>1 and name the exposed configuration explicitly, (b) decide whether to fold this into nexus-eslkl's scope or track separately with a measurement pass (design memo §7 T6's seeded-property-test-at-concurrency-3 shape would validate/bound it), (c) do NOT read the current docstring as proof the cross-fire hazard is fully mitigated for every configuration.

title: flush-grain hook chain serializes globally under LockedHookRegistry — 104s/run of pure lock wait remains after nexus-itpdc
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-08 on 7.4.0 cloud + engine v0.1.68 (perfprobe-740, 109 files / 29 flushes; T2 nexus/flush-tail-investigation-2026-08-08).

nexus-itpdc's root cause was LockedHookRegistry's single mutex, NOT the GIL. Fixed there: zero-match fires (grain with no registered hook) no longer acquire the lock, which took the whole file-grain bucket from 53.9s to 0.0s per run. THIS bead is the RESIDUAL: the NON-empty flush-grain chain still holds one process-wide mutex across its network round trips.

Measured (P4fix, quiet box, post-itpdc-fix): hook_lock_wait_seconds=104.1 against a held critical section of taxonomy 12.8s + manifest 44.0s = 56.8s. Wait is ~1.8x held time — the signature of 3 ChunkBatcher flush workers (flush_concurrency=3) plus 2 file-loop workers (resolve_index_concurrency default) all funnelling through one lock. flush-grain bucket reads 113.2s of which only 56.8s is hook work; the other 56.4s is queueing. That gap is what nexus-jb4pp saw as 'UNSPLIT' and mis-attributed to the missing fence sub-timer (the fence is only 8.5s/run and is now separately reported as flush_fence_seconds).

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER: resolve_index_concurrency's docstring (indexer_utils.py:1021-1026) names this lock as what makes a diverging T2 memory backend safe under concurrency — 'Narrowing the hook lock requires extending this gate.' So narrowing needs the interleaving audit cfc72 deferred, per hook chain (taxonomy assign, manifest write, aspect enqueue), not just a smaller critical section.

DESIGN DIRECTIONS (unranked, needs the audit first):
(a) per-hook-name locks instead of one registry lock — taxonomy and manifest touch disjoint T2/catalog state, so they need not exclude each other;
(b) drop the lock for hooks whose backends are already thread-safe (both are HTTP clients over the engine now — the SQLite hazard the lock was built for died with RDR-158 P4), keeping it only for any hook that declares it needs serialization;
(c) leave the lock but stop calling hooks under it for work that is pure network (release around the round trip).
(b) is likely correct-and-largest but is exactly the audit cfc72 punted; do not ship it on inspection alone.

BLOCKED-ON-DESIGN. Instrumentation to measure any fix already exists: hook_lock_wait_seconds in index_chunk_batch_stats.
close_reason: Landed in develop 13cd7029; dual-reviewed; suite 12093 green.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN READY — interleaving audit DONE 2026-08-08. Full memo: T2 nexus/design-eslkl-hook-lock-narrowing [21731] (permanent).

THREE FINDINGS THAT REORDER THIS WORK:

1. THE HOOK LOCK IS THE OUTER OF THREE NESTED PROCESS-WIDE LOCKS. Every hook's network I/O is already serialized a second time downstream: taxonomy + aspect-enqueue by mcp_infra._service_t2_lock (held across the full write_fn, mcp_infra.py:383), manifest by catalog/factory._service_catalog_lock (held across EVERY op, factory.py:147 and :162). Narrowing only THIS lock relocates ~90s of the measured 104s wait one layer down — the identical timer-relocation signature that proved itpdc was a convoy. Projected wall win from eslkl ALONE: ~13-18s of the 56.8s serialized hook wall, NOT 104s. (104s is thread-seconds of queueing across 3 workers; the critical section is 56.8s and the 3-way-parallel floor is ~19s.)

2. THE AUDIT COLLAPSES TO ONE HAZARD: _sweep_superseded_vectors' client-side read-modify-write over GLOBALLY-SHARED chashes (mcp_infra.py:1181, called :1475). _service_catalog_lock is PER-OP, so the per-doc sequence get_chunk_chashes -> atomic_manifest_replace -> orphaned_chashes -> T3 DELETE -> resync -> complete is NOT atomic. Race: thread A drops shared chash X and deletes it from T3 after reading docs_for_chashes(X)={}, while thread B's manifest (not yet written) is about to reference X. Silent: B's manifest row points at a deleted chunk. Same mechanism is the ONLY cross-chain hazard too (A's sweep deletes X while B's assign_from_chashes probes chunks_<dim> for X -> false unmatched_chashes tripwire). Everything else is provably safe: taxonomy is server-side idempotent (TaxonomyRepository.assignFromChashes, ONE tenantScope txn, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING / GREATEST-wins) and client-serialized by _service_t2_lock regardless; manifest replace is a server-side atomic delete+insert per DISJOINT doc_id (ChunkBatcher is file-atomic); all six run-summary counters carry their own mutexes; CollectionDocumentsCache is per-fire.

3. nexus-67qsd/nexus-jk88j DOMINATE THIS BEAD AND SHOULD LAND FIRST. Folding the sweep into /manifest/write_many's server-side txn cuts manifest held time 44.0s -> ~12s (327 round trips -> 29, ~32s wall) AND removes the sole hazard BY CONSTRUCTION — no client-side read-modify-write left to interleave. After that the remaining narrowing prize is ~12s and needs no safety argument.

THE BLOCKING RATIONALE IS DEAD. resolve_index_concurrency (indexer_utils.py:1010-1062) names a 'diverging T2 memory backend'; that meant service vectors/catalog + direct in-process SQLite T2. storage_backend_for (db/storage_mode.py:127-165) is now a fail-loud VALIDATOR returning StorageBackend.SERVICE unconditionally and hard-erroring on any =sqlite (RDR-158 P3 / nexus-7bomn); t2_index_write's own docstring confirms the direct-SQLite arm is gone. NO supported configuration produces a diverging T2 backend; the gate does NOT need extending. Correct that docstring in whichever change lands the narrowing — the real constraint to name is the manifest sequence.

DECISIVE EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE: (a) flush_concurrency=3 (indexer.py:3881) is UNCONDITIONAL while LockedHookRegistry is gated on _concurrency>1 — so NX_INDEX_CONCURRENCY=1 is a SUPPORTED config in which 3 flush workers fire the flush-grain chain on a BARE registry. The unlocked topology already ships. (b) LockedHookRegistry has exactly ONE construction site (indexer.py:3590); MCP store_put, nx store put/import, memory promote, doc_indexer, pipeline_stages, exporter all use bare registries — the lock is a local mitigation on 1 of ~8 entry points, not a global invariant. (c) The aspect chain ALREADY runs outside the lock on the hot path (nexus-nj4ch, direct t2_index_write at indexer.py:3841 after fire_batch returns), shipped, no corruption.

CORRECTION TO [21723] §1: 'file-loop workers plus flush workers funnel through the lock' should read 3 FLUSH WORKERS. On the batcher path every hook fire (on_batch_begin, on_file_complete, on_batch_complete) happens inside _flush_batch in the pool worker; file-loop concurrency only feeds the batcher faster.

RECOMMENDATION: 67qsd + jk88j FIRST (jk88j's stated order stands: sweep in the fast branch, then whitelist), THEN option (b) per-chain locks — one lock per registered hook, default LOCKED, opt-out via a declared attribute in the batch_grain idiom (taxonomy_assign_batch_hook.serialize=False) so the safety claim sits next to its evidence and new hooks are safe by default. Option (a) per-grain is a NO-OP (both default batch hooks are the same 'flush' grain — a per-grain lock IS this lock, renamed). Do NOT ship 'drop the lock, both backends are HTTP now': true of the transports, FALSE of the manifest sequence.

MUST LAND TOGETHER: eslkl + u2u0n + a NEW BEAD for _service_t2_lock (unfiled — same convoy shape, same CAS fix, becomes the taxonomy chain's serializer at 12.8s/run held). u2u0n's 'eslkl first then re-measure' is wrong on the numbers: EITHER ALONE delivers ~nothing (eslkl relocates onto the catalog lock; u2u0n is invisible because the hook lock pre-serializes).

TEST STRATEGY (deterministic, barrier-based, zero sleeps): T1 hazard-exists falsification (2-party Barrier at the orphan-read/replace seam, must FAIL post-fix); T2 hazard-closed against the engine substrate; T3 lock topology (hold hook A's lock, assert B completes — extends the existing test_zero_match_fires_never_take_the_lock pattern) with a non-vacuity mirror; T4 self-serialization (enter/exit ordinals, no interleaved enter,enter); T5 CAS-eviction correctness parametrized over all three locks; T6 seeded property test, 8 flushes / disjoint doc_ids / overlapping chashes / concurrency 3, invariant 'every manifest chash exists in chunks_<dim>'. Plus a measurement GATE: hook_lock_wait_seconds down AND service_catalog_op_stats lock_wait_s NOT up by the same amount AND wall down — relocation must read as failure.

ENGINE v0.1.69 CANDIDATES: (1) fold the superseded-vector sweep into /manifest/write_many's per-doc transaction, preserving BOTH client guards (shared-chash union + manifest-less-note/live_chunks) and staying fail-open; (2) return swept/kept counts so the CLI summary keeps feeding (39upx hazard 4 — a skip must never be silent). Not engine-side: the three client lock narrowings and the write_manifest_many whitelist add.

UNMEASURED, capture in the before/after pass: aspect_enqueue's held time under _service_t2_lock (_flush_hook_by_name['aspect_enqueue'] exists but is absent from [21723]'s table; est ~3s/run).

WORTH ONE LOG SWEEP before deciding urgency: has the sweep TOCTOU fired in the wild? Loud symptoms are write_manifest_many_complete_refused / index_run_complete_write_failed / superseded_sweep_*.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Related bead filed: nexus-ldab2 (P3) — _service_t2_lock, the THIRD convoy on this path (taxonomy 12.8s/run held + the batched aspect enqueue). Must land in the same change as this bead and nexus-u2u0n; landing any one alone relocates the wait to the next lock down rather than removing it.

title: drift-ledger _in_release_window cannot distinguish tag-absent from fetch-failed
design:
Commit 5c4a0ca8 (tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py) makes
_require_or_skip() defer to _in_release_window() before its
NX_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_DRIFT_CHECK=1 hard-fail raise. _in_release_window()
classifies "release window" purely from local git state: ref ==
v<pyproject-version> AND `git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}` fails to
resolve. That local-resolution probe cannot distinguish "the tag genuinely
does not exist yet" from "the tag exists on origin but this checkout's
fetch step failed to bring it down" -- exactly the ambiguity
NX_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_DRIFT_CHECK exists to eliminate (see the file's own
_REQUIRE_ENV docstring: "if the job's tag-fetch step ever breaks, a skip
would report green having checked nothing").

Practical exposure: develop's pyproject.toml + marketplace.json ref sit at
v<last-released-version> continuously from the post-release back-merge
(release process step 8b) until the NEXT release branch bumps them again --
this is not a rare edge, it is develop's normal resting state between
releases (confirmed empirically: this checkout, on release/v7.4.0, is
literally in the matching ref==v<version>+no-local-tag state right now).
Any transient/broken tag-fetch in .github/workflows/plugin-drift-ledger.yml
during that span will be silently classified "release window: tolerated"
by BOTH the shell fetch step (pre-existing, since the 7.0.0 cut) and now
also by _require_or_skip() (new as of 5c4a0ca8) -- reopening, one level up,
the exact "guard believed live but not checking anything" class this whole
file exists to prevent (2026-07-25 incident in the file's module
docstring).

Before 5c4a0ca8: _require_or_skip() raised unconditionally on any tagless
state under the require flag, regardless of window classification -- noisy
(also raised on the legitimate release-branch window) but safe against this
specific fetch-failure case. After 5c4a0ca8: that unconditional hard-stop
is gone; the one remaining safety net for "fetch broke, tag genuinely
exists" is removed.

Suggested remediation direction: disambiguate via an authoritative check
against the remote (e.g. `git ls-remote --tags origin <ref>`) rather than
local resolution only. If ls-remote confirms the tag does NOT exist
upstream, that is a genuine release window. If ls-remote finds the tag DOES
exist upstream but local resolution still fails, that is a broken/
incomplete fetch and must remain a hard failure under the require flag --
never a silent tolerate. Alternatively (weaker, but cheaper): plumb an
explicit, positively-asserted "release window" signal from the workflow's
own fetch step (which already computed this) into the pytest run via env
var, rather than having Python re-derive the same ambiguous local-only
signal a second time -- though note the shell step has the IDENTICAL
blind spot today (same ref==v\$version fallback with no ls-remote check),
so fixing only the Python side without also fixing the shell step's
`git fetch --depth=1 ... || tolerate` fallback leaves the workflow-level
exposure open.

Secondary, lower-severity finding (same critique): _in_release_window() is
unbounded in time/commits -- a release that stalls between merge-push and
tag-push for days (not the "seconds" the docstring describes) stays
classified in-window indefinitely, during which the real diff-based drift
check (_drifted_paths) is skipped entirely in favor of a weaker "ledger is
empty" proxy. If any plugin-surface-touching PR merges to main during a
multi-day stall, that drift is invisible until the tag finally cuts, at
which point it ships undeclared with nothing having caught it at the
moment it happened.

Full critique on file: substantive-critic run 2026-08-07, commit
5c4a0ca8 on release/v7.4.0. Verdict: not-justified (fix-first) pending
this issue.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: commit 2ebf2eef7 (names nexus-icrwy): release window now CONFIRMED via git ls-remote against origin (test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py:201,237) instead of inferred from local taglessness

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CLOSED (Critical): fetch-failure-masquerade fixed by 2ebf2eef (release/v7.4.0, pushed). _require_or_skip's window branch now authoritatively confirms tag absence upstream via _remote_confirms_tag_absent() (git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v<pyproject-version>) before trusting the window: confirmed-absent -> proceed to ledger-EMPTY contract; confirmed-present -> loud AssertionError naming the broken fetch step (never a window); probe inconclusive -> fail-closed under NX_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_DRIFT_CHECK=1, plain skip locally. Four self-tests pin the quadrant. Verified independently: read full diff, ran tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py in isolation both with and without the require flag (16/16 passed both ways), and ran the live ls-remote probe on this checkout (refs/tags/v7.4.0 -- 0 lines, genuine window, matches expected CI behavior).

REMAINS OPEN on this bead: the Significant finding from my original critique -- _in_release_window() has no time/commit bound, so a tag-cut that stalls for days (not the intended seconds-between-merge-and-tag-push) stays window-classified indefinitely, during which the real diff-based drift check never runs (only the weaker ledger-empty proxy). This commit explicitly defers that residual (see its commit message) rather than fixing it. Downgrading to P2 -- the Critical (silent-green on a broken fetch step) is resolved; what remains is a narrower gap requiring an actual additional main-merge during a multi-day stall, partially mitigated in practice by the release skill's 'tag the merge commit IMMEDIATELY' discipline.

Companion bead nexus-fhgne (P3, code-review-expert finding) tracks the mirrored local-only inference still present in .github/workflows/plugin-drift-ledger.yml's bash fetch-tolerance fallback -- that layer was NOT touched by 2ebf2eef and still conflates tag-absent with fetch-failed at the shell level, same as _in_release_window() itself (which 2ebf2eef also left unchanged -- it works around it via the new upstream-confirmation call in _require_or_skip rather than fixing _in_release_window() directly, which is fine since _require_or_skip is the sole gate all three ledger tests route through).

title: doctor MCP entry-point resolver probes a FOREIGN home's install when the process's own prefix is home-rooted (l2ku5 own-prefix-skip backfires under a relocated HOME)
description: Found at the 7.4.0 cut via the release sandbox: _resolve_mcp_binary (src/nexus/health.py, the l2ku5 layer test) prefers the first PATH hit outside the running process's own sys.prefix. Under a relocated HOME (release sandbox, any chroot-style env), the artifact under test IS the own-prefix hit, so the resolver walked past it and probed the REAL home's live nx-mcp — the doctor verdict then tracked host health/load, observed live as an 8s initialize timeout under gate load while the host binary answered instantly when idle. Fix (7.4.0 release branch): HOME-scoping — when own prefix is under the current $HOME, a PATH hit OUTSIDE $HOME is foreign and is demoted below the own-prefix fallback (never dropped; foreign-only last resort still probes). Dev-box preference and system-wide-install shapes provably unchanged (3 new tests + composition-test HOME pin in tests/test_health_mcp_entrypoints.py).
close_reason: Fixed at 4c17077c: resolver HOME-scoping, foreign hits demoted never dropped; sandbox gate probes its own artifact (verified in the passing shakedown log); /usr/local topology pinned as documented trade-off. Dual-reviewed clean.

title: release-sandbox activate leaks the invoking session id — shakedown step 8 coupled to invoker CLI lease freshness
description: Found at the 7.4.0 cut (2026-08-07): shakedown step 8 (T1 scratch write) died with t1_explicit_session_no_usable_lease naming the ORCHESTRATING Claude session's id. sandbox.sh's generated activate unset CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT but not CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/NX_SESSION_ID, so the virgin CLI inherited an explicit session id and took the fails-loud explicit-id path instead of the bare-invocation CLI-dedicated mint. Product verified CORRECT: with the vars scrubbed, nx scratch put stores rc=0.
