title: design: MCP T1 scope follows the transcript — SessionStart(clear/resume) handoff marker + lifespan re-lease
description:
Hal-requested 2026-08-07, closing the aj564 split-brain window by design rather than discipline.

MODEL CONFIRMED CORRECT: session identity flows through process parentage everywhere (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID env -> CLI per-invocation resolve; MCP spawn env; NX_SESSION_ID forward into claude -p dispatches per 4gby/5daww). The ONE divergence window is a lifetime mismatch: the MCP server is a long-lived child that samples the session id once at spawn and outlives /clear//resume, and the MCP protocol carries no per-request session-id channel — so the running server cannot know the transcript changed. Freeze-at-spawn is the honest response to a missing signal (docs/architecture.md § T1's three scopes; measured split-brain aj564: CLI 2 vs MCP 39 entries same instant).

DESIGN SHAPE (supply the missing signal instead of freezing): the conexus SessionStart hook already fires on matcher startup|resume|clear|compact. On clear/resume it writes a session-handoff marker keyed to the MCP server's identity (pid or lease path: e.g. ~/.config/nexus/t1_handoff.<mcp_pid> containing the NEW transcript session id). The MCP lifespan (which already owns the t1_lease publish/heartbeat loop, daemon/t1_lease.py RDR-149 P4) watches for the marker on its heartbeat tick and RE-LEASES onto the new session id: publish new lease, freeze new scope, drop the old heartbeat.

OWNERSHIP SEMANTICS (decide in design review): entries written under the pre-clear id STRAND under that id and age out via the T1 TTL sweep — arguably correct (they belonged to the pre-/clear conversation). Alternative (migrate old scope's rows to the new id) is rejected-by-default: it merges conversations the user explicitly separated with /clear.

MUST-HOLDS: (1) rn3wo.1 never-share-identity — the handoff marker must be authenticated to the same claude process ancestry (a concurrent session's hook must not be able to re-point another session's MCP server; key on pid + verify ancestry, and the marker lives in the user-private config dir); (2) f7xyq fail-loud semantics unchanged for explicit-id probes; (3) frozen-scope stability for the common no-clear session is unchanged (no re-resolve per call — only on marker); (4) subagent-visible MCP tools follow the parent scope automatically (they use the parent's server).

CONSEQUENCE: MCP and CLI scopes become identical at all times for a given conversation; the 'markers via CLI only' operational rule collapses; docs/architecture.md three-scopes section simplifies to two (session scope + shared bare-CLI scope). Cross-references: nexus-aj564 (measurement), nexus-f7xyq (fail-loud), nexus-ylof9 (parent-lease borrow nuance — re-check its three-case docstring after this lands), project_t1_three_scope_rule memory (retire/rewrite on landing). RDR-worthy if design review says the ownership question needs a decision record.
close_reason: Shipped develop (see commit). Both halves PyPI-side (Tier B): marker writer in nx hook session-start (clear/resume, ancestry-gated to own claude pid), watcher in MCP lifespan (5s tick, atomic claim via os.replace, ancestry+staleness re-verify, off-loop re-lease w/ deadline, pre-init hooks cleared before env swap, no-clobber hardlink reinstate). Strand-and-TTL ownership per design. Reviews: critic 0C/0H w/ empirical MUST-HOLD probes; reviewer 3 rounds (1C+2Imp+1Imp all fixed) -> final CLEAN, independently re-ran 47/47. Follow-ups open: 9l147 reaper, yfh5x dead-code deletion; 1x2di folded.

title: engine: session_tokens has NO scheduled expiry sweep — expired tokens are permanent rows unless explicitly closed
description: Found by the 2026-08-07 nexus-4lkmz/bjltu re-review (code-review-expert, T1 marker 61799ab3): NexusService.java's only scheduled sweep thread (t1-ttl-sweep) calls scratchRepo.sweepTenant — scratch rows only. TokenStore.java has exactly resolveSession/issueSessionToken/closeSession and no batch/scheduled expiry; its docstring says 'session_tokens has no revoked_at (DELETE-on-close + expiry only)'. Auth checks expires_at live, so an expired-but-unclosed token is inert (no security exposure) — but the ROW is never deleted by anything except an explicit close. Any minting process that dies without close (crashed MCP, killed dispatch, machine reboot — e.g. today's) leaks a permanent row. Fix shape: extend the existing t1-ttl-sweep thread to also DELETE FROM session_tokens WHERE expires_at < now() (tenant-scoped like the scratch sweep), or a companion scheduled sweep. ENGINE-SIDE, rides an engine tag (not necessarily the imminent v0.1.68 — low urgency, rows are small; but the sweep is one query on an existing thread). Related: dispatch-side explicit token close is being added under nexus-bjltu; this bead is the backstop for every OTHER minting path.

title: reinstall-tool.sh: fold the MCP-holder dance into the journey — self-aware refusal + --cycle-mcp arm
description:
Friction observed in the live 7.2.0->7.3.0 upgrade (2026-08-07, post-reboot session): a reinstall run from INSIDE a live Claude session always hits the q3xrx holder check, because the session's own nx-mcp + nx-mcp-catalog spawn at session start from the old venv. The sanctioned path today is a two-manual-step dance: kill this session's two MCP server PIDs, reinstall, then the human runs /mcp reconnect (which boots the servers from the NEW venv — the desired end state). --cycle-daemons only cycles the storage daemon, not MCP servers, so it does not help this case. The guards all behaved correctly (refusal loud, PIDs named, no --force, upgrade-finish 'no stale processes', doctor process-freshness green after reconnect) — this is journey friction, not a protection defect.

Fix shape (design-level, fold friction into the journey rather than adding a raw knob):
1. Self-aware refusal: when live_venv_processes() holders are nx-mcp/nx-mcp-catalog whose ancestor is a claude process, the refusal message should say so explicitly and print the exact sequence (kill <pids> && reinstall, then '/mcp' in that Claude session to reconnect on the new venv) instead of the generic three-remedy list.
2. Optional --cycle-mcp arm: kill the MCP-server holders (they are stateless stdio children; Claude Code reconnects on demand via /mcp), install, and remind the operator to /mcp reconnect. Must NOT be the default; the default stays refuse-loud. Composes with --cycle-daemons.
3. Keep the q3xrx invariant untouched: never swap the venv under ANY live holder; --force semantics unchanged.

Evidence: shakedown-2026-08-07-umbrella (T2 21610) MAJOR RE-DIAGNOSES section; this session's transcript (holder refusal exit 3, sanctioned kill, clean reinstall, /mcp reconnect verified live).
close_reason: Shipped develop ae5e2e86. Self-aware refusal (claude-ancestored MCP holder classification, honest multi-session wording) + opt-in --cycle-mcp arm (kills only classified MCP holders, refuses on non-MCP holder or kill survivor, composes with --cycle-daemons, /mcp reminder). q3xrx never-swap invariant, refuse-loud default, --force semantics all unchanged. 9-case stubbed-PATH test harness; survivor-recheck branch mutation-proven covered (both reviewers ran the mutation independently). title: nexus-2t63u follow-up: early physical_collection reconcile creates a mid-run-failure search-invisibility window
description: Empirically verified (critique probe, T2 nexus/nexus-2t63u-critique-2026-08-06 [21567]): a mid-run failure AFTER the early physical_collection reconcile lands (doc_indexer.py's _register_or_lookup_doc_id by_file_path branch) but BEFORE _fence_complete flips physical_collection to the run's target immediately; index_state correctly goes to 'failed', but manifest_verify still reports clean against its own unchanged per-row stamp (the OLD collection). Result: nx catalog show reports the doc living in a collection with ZERO chunks for it; catalog-aware query()/search resolves there and finds nothing, even though the doc's real content is fully live under the OLD collection. Pre-nexus-2t63u this never happened (physical_collection only moved at _catalog_pdf_hook's tail, unreached on a crash/refusal). Recovery requires a successful retry. This is the direct cost of doing the reconcile eagerly, which is structurally required by the engine's current unconditional physical_collection read at manifest-write time -- the deferred engine-side fix (explicit collection param on the manifest-write payload, validated against physical_collection) would eliminate this window entirely. Not a blocker for the Option A stopgap; filed so the window is tracked rather than silently accepted.

title: nexus-cotmr's note-exemption masks the vw594/F2 store_put fence coverage gap it was believed to be excluded from
design:

[21532]) justifies exempting ALL note-shaped (store_put-origin) documents
from health.py::_check_stale_indexing_runs's NULL-index_state WARN on the
premise that "store_put-origin documents NEVER carry index_state
(registered exclusion on nexus-5xn3k, accepted design)... is INTENTIONALLY
outside the RUNFENCE begin/complete choreography" — citing Hal's
2026-08-02 17:02 comment on nexus-39upx verbatim.

THAT CITATION IS STALE. Two days later, commit f55435eb (2026-08-04
20:02:42, "fix(fence): RUNFENCE stamps every producer... store_put
coverage... (nexus-vw594)", already on develop, NOT touched by cotmr's
diff) added explicit RUNFENCE instrumentation to MCP store_put
(src/nexus/mcp/core.py store_put(): _fence_begin before t3.put, _fence_fail
on error, manifest_complete={catalog_doc_id: content_hash} passed to
fire_batch for completion). tests/test_vw594_fence_coverage_gate.py's own
AST-tripwire allowlist labels this "producer 10 (MCP store_put / nx store
put)" and asserts "manifest_complete rides the existing fire_batch call" —
i.e. F2's own documented intent is that store_put DOES participate in
begin->complete, contradicting "intentionally outside the choreography."

Hal's OWN LATER comment (nexus-vw594, 2026-08-05 00:19, "INVESTIGATION
COMPLETE... FIX F1-F4... F2 store_put begin+complete") is more recent
than, and reverses, the 08-02 17:02 ruling cotmr cites. cotmr's T2 record
claims F2 "is superseded by the accepted design; not implemented here" —
this is FACTUALLY WRONG; F2 (begin+fail, at minimum) is implemented and
live on develop.

SEPARATE, VERIFIED-REAL GAP: CLI `nx store put` / `nx memory promote` /
`nx store import` (all routed through hook_registry.py's
fire_store_chains, confirmed via direct read) call NEITHER _fence_begin
NOR pass a manifest_complete= map to fire_batch — genuinely, completely
unfenced, unlike the MCP entry point. This is very likely WHY the
acquire-gate journey (which used CLI store put per the bead's own text)
observed a NULL index_state — not because store_put is categorically
excluded by design, but because F2's coverage claim ("MCP store_put / nx
store put") is true for only half of that label. This is producer-coverage
debt, not accepted design, and it happens to be structurally invisible to
F4's own AST tripwire (fire_store_chains's internal fire_batch call lives
in hook_registry.py, which is in the tripwire's _EXCLUDED_FILES set).

CONSEQUENCE: is_note_shaped's exemption, applied uniformly regardless of
producer, permanently masks BOTH (a) the known CLI producer-coverage gap
now, and (b) any future MCP-path fence-begin/fire_batch failure that
leaves a note at NULL — exactly the failure class the vw594 NULL-signature
WARN exists to catch. "Over-retention is the safe direction" (correct for
the g6k6b GC-sweep precondition, a deletion-safety question) does not
transfer to a DIAGNOSTIC/detection question, where silence is the unsafe
direction.

RECOMMENDATION: either (a) close the CLI producer-coverage gap (wire
fire_store_chains / commands/store.py / commands/memory.py into
begin/complete/fail, completing F2's own stated scope) so a note's NULL
index_state becomes a genuine anomaly signal again, or (b) if the
exemption is kept as a near-term mitigation, correct the T2 record and the
inline code comments in health.py/indexer_utils.py (currently assert a
factually incorrect "accepted design, intentional exclusion" as if
settled) and track the CLI coverage gap as its own explicitly-open bead
so it is not silently forgotten now that the doctor can no longer detect
it.

Evidence trail: git blame src/nexus/mcp/core.py:2622-2691 (f55435eb);
tests/test_vw594_fence_coverage_gate.py lines 161-168; bd show
nexus-vw594 (close reason + comment log); src/nexus/hook_registry.py
fire_store_chains (no manifest_complete kwarg); src/nexus/commands/
store.py, src/nexus/commands/memory.py (no _fence_begin/_fence_fail
calls anywhere).

title: rlkgu tripwire scope excludes db/embed_migrate.py's unguarded per-record index_pdf/index_markdown loop
description:
substantive-critic finding on nexus-rlkgu (T1 cc3d9989).

nexus-rlkgu's scanner (tests/test_rlkgu_per_record_catch_tripwire.py
_SCAN_RELPATHS) only sweeps src/nexus/commands/dt.py and
src/nexus/commands/index.py. That scope was inherited unchanged from
nexus-hb10j's "exhaustive sweep" (T2 21486), which checked
commands/collection.py's reindex loop, indexer_utils.run_file_loop, and
indexer._contain_transient_upsert -- but never checked
src/nexus/db/embed_migrate.py.

src/nexus/db/embed_migrate.py:_default_reindex has a per-source-path
loop (line ~274-282):

    for sp in source_paths:
        ...
        if p.suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
            count = index_pdf(p, corpus=corpus, collection_name=target_name, force=True)
        else:
            count = index_markdown(p, corpus=corpus, collection_name=target_name, force=True)

with ZERO try/except around the individual per-record call -- the exact
"unguarded call" shape the tripwire's own kill control
(test_kill_control_unguarded_call_is_flagged) demonstrates as "the most
extreme version of the gap". The only exception handling is one layer up,
in migrate_collection_safe, wrapping the ENTIRE driver(...) call for the
whole collection: a single ChunkLandingUnverifiedError/IndexRunVerifyRefused
on source N aborts reindexing of every remaining source path too, and the
whole collection migration is marked status="failed" -- discarding partial
progress rather than the dt.py/index.py contract of catch-one-record,
continue-the-batch.

Currently NOT live: grepped the full src/ tree -- migrate_collection_safe,
_default_reindex, and detect_stale_local_collections are referenced
nowhere outside db/embed_migrate.py itself and tests/test_embed_migrate.py.
No CLI command (init.py, upgrade.py, doctor.py) wires them in, despite the
module's own docstring claiming "The CLI wiring (nx init) handles the
preview, confirmation, and reporting" -- RDR-144 (closed) apparently never
shipped that wiring, or it was removed. So this is not exploitable today,
but it is real per-record code calling the exact _TARGET_FUNCS names the
tripwire is meant to police, sitting completely outside its scan scope
with no allowlist acknowledgment (unlike indexer_utils.run_file_loop,
which the hb10j sweep explicitly carved out with a documented reason).

If this module is ever wired into a live command (its own docstring says
it should be), a NexusError raised mid-migration would silently reproduce
the whole-batch-abort bug class nexus-rlkgu exists to prevent, invisible
to both of nexus-rlkgu's gates.

Fix options (pick one): (a) widen _SCAN_RELPATHS to include
db/embed_migrate.py and either wrap the per-record call in
PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS-or-continue (if per-record salvage is
desired here too) or add a reasoned _LOOP_ALLOWLIST entry documenting the
intentional all-or-nothing migration contract; (b) at minimum, correct
db/embed_migrate.py's stale module docstring so it stops claiming CLI
wiring that doesn't exist, and file a follow-up to either wire it or
delete the dead code path (unused != useless, but a stale "this is
already safe" docstring is worse than no docstring).

title: session.items-based censuses (test_mode_declarations_are_explicit) are shard-blind under CI's real pytest-split matrix, not just the lint marker
design:
Verified 2026-08-05 during substantive-critique of nexus-8x4le's revert (which
correctly un-blinded the census from the permanent `-m lint` blind spot).

pytest_split/plugin.py:168 does `items[:] = group.selected` inside
pytest_collection_modifyitems — the EXACT same session.items-mutation
mechanism that -m/-k deselection uses (confirmed empirically: 11733 default
items -> 803 under `-m lint`). CI's actual PR-gating `test` job
(.github/workflows/ci.yml, "pytest (Python X, shard N/4)") invokes
`pytest tests/ --splits 4 --group N`, NOT xdist -n auto.

Empirically confirmed on develop @ 83730d65 + nexus-8x4le's uncommitted diff:
  for g in 1 2 3 4: pytest tests/ --collect-only --splits 4 --group $g
  -> test_mode_declarations_are_explicit lands in group 3 (2796/13101 items)
  -> the du2dw offender (TestCheckChashConformanceReport::
     test_fully_routable_collections_still_render_plain_clean) ALSO lands in
     group 3 -- coincidentally co-located.

This means the census only ever sees ~24% of the corpus (its own shard) under
CI's real matrix job. It caught the du2dw offender THIS TIME because they
happen to share a shard under the current .test_durations.json balancing --
not because whole-session enforcement was actually restored. A future
voyage-token violation landing in shard 1, 2, or 4 (wherever the census
itself isn't) will NOT be caught by the real CI gate, silently.

nexus-8x4le's validation (`-n auto` xdist, 3x, "IDENTICAL session.items")
does NOT reproduce CI's actual invocation shape and therefore does not prove
the fix restores real enforcement -- xdist workers each do full local
collection (session.items unmutated); pytest-split's `--splits/--group`
explicitly shrinks it, same as `-m lint`.

Fix candidates (per the ORIGINAL nexus-8x4le bug description's own list,
never revisited after the tree-drift diagnosis superseded it):
  1. Give this census (and structurally similar session.items-based
     checks, if any exist) a dedicated single non-sharded CI job, the same
     pattern test-lint already uses for the lint bucket.
  2. Aggregate the census via a controller-side pytest_sessionfinish hook
     that pytest-split's grouping cannot shrink (an out-of-band file-based
     merge across the 4 shard processes, or a `pytest-split`-aware skip
     that only runs the census in a job explicitly excluded from
     --splits/--group).
  3. Revert to AST-only filesystem scanning (the option nexus-109's own
     step 4 explicitly scoped OUT) to make it filesystem-based like every
     other lint-bucket census, trading the request.fixturenames-based
     cloud_mode-opt-in precision for shard-safety.

tests/AGENTS.md's corrected rule already gestures at this in the abstract
("If a session.items-based census genuinely needs to run once per PR rather
than once per shard, that is a CI-wiring problem") but does not identify
that this is CURRENTLY TRUE for this exact file under the real CI matrix,
right now, not a hypothetical.
close_reason: CI-red follow-up landed as d5afad74 (round 1: ddd5b7e6). Dedicated test-mode-census job executed and passed on run 31063690597; all 4 shards green (the shard-3/4 port collision cannot recur — partial-view skip fires pre-fixture via tryfirst hook). Third vacuity variant (t2_service_env graceful skip) closed by NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=none + CI-env-shape regression test. tp8yk-era commands/index.py. hb10j fixed the same gap for --dt-content
in dt.py's index_cmd.

The developer declined extraction (the four near-identical catch blocks
across dt.py/index.py have differing return/log shapes: append-to-list
vs raise ClickException, differing structured-log field sets per
exception type) and set an informal "fix at the 4th occurrence"
threshold. Per the standing root-cause-after-3-patches directive
(3+ patches to the same subsystem = step back and find the structural
cause), deferring past occurrence 3 is exactly the reactive pattern
this directive exists to head off.

Diagnosis: the structural cause is NOT "no shared idiom" (full
extraction is genuinely awkward given the differing control-flow shapes
per call site) — it's "new NexusError subclasses keep being introduced
without an audit of every per-record catch site that should absorb
them." Full extraction doesn't close that loop; a cheap mechanical
tripwire does.

Recommended fix: a CI-checked test (grep- or AST-based, mirroring the
"exhaustive inverse-grep for cross-surface wiring" pattern already used
elsewhere in this repo) that asserts every per-record/per-file loop in
src/nexus/commands/dt.py and src/nexus/commands/index.py which calls an
index_*-family function catches BOTH ChunkLandingUnverifiedError and
IndexRunVerifyRefused (or documents, in an explicit allowlist with a
reason, why it does not — e.g. batch loops using a broad `except
Exception` are already safe by construction, single-file commands that
intentionally abort are exempt). Confirmed exhaustive sweep at hb10j
review time found no fifth live occurrence — index.py's --dir batch
loops use `except Exception` (already safe by construction); nx index
repo's run_file_loop has a documented first-exception-aborts contract
(different, intentional shape). The tripwire's job is to catch the
NEXT new NexusError subclass before occurrence 4, not to re-litigate
current call sites.

Scope: src/nexus/commands/dt.py, src/nexus/commands/index.py (the two
files with per-record catch-and-continue loops around index_* calls).
close_reason: Shipped develop (ddd5b7e6 range). PER_RECORD_SURVIVABLE_EXCEPTIONS + two AST gates + registry-driven handler-body coverage; occurrence 4 now fails at introduction time through THREE independent mechanisms (classification gate, registry gate, generic else). Critic round 1 reproduced occurrence-4 through the green gates (cy4oy — binary dispatch) — fixed with total dispatch, independently re-verified round 2. embed_migrate scope acknowledged (a1zv2 open for module disposition).

title: Widen nexus-84a6 json.loads(result.output) tripwire past the literal 'result' variable name
description:
tests/test_cli_runner_output_invariant.py (nexus-84a6) exists specifically to
prevent json.loads(<CliRunner Result>.output) — Click 8.2+ merges stdout+stderr
into .output, so any interleaved warning/log line breaks JSON parsing
non-deterministically. Its regex is anchored to the literal variable name
`result`: `re.compile(r"json\.loads\(\s*result\.output\s*\)")`.

Two live occurrences already slip past it under a different variable name,
today, on develop:
  - tests/test_census.py:392        payload = json.loads(res.output)
  - tests/test_catalog_cli.py:1125  assert "taxonomy" not in json.loads(js.output)

(test_catalog_cli.py:1102, three lines above, correctly uses
`json.loads(result.stdout)` in the same class — proof the tripwire's own
file shows the split between caught and uncaught instances.)

This bug class is exactly what caused the 2026-08-05 CI red fixed alongside
this bead: tests/test_scenario_journeys.py used json.loads(search.output) /
json.loads(wombat_search.output) / etc. (variable names search, code_search,
knowledge_search, wombat_search, octopus_search) — none matched by the
nexus-84a6 regex either, and that guard never fired despite existing
specifically to prevent this failure mode.

Fix: widen the regex to catch any `json.loads(<expr>.output)` (e.g.
`json\.loads\(\s*[\w.]+\.output\s*\)`, retaining the allow-list for its own
docstring mention), OR match on `.output` used anywhere as a json.loads
argument regardless of the receiver name. Then convert the two live
occurrences above to `.stdout`.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t test-suite-compression-P2-reduced-critique
Found during substantive-critic review of the conftest.py/test_scenario_journeys.py
CI-unbreak fix (T1 afaba253, T2 [21471] et al).

Reviews T2 [21485] clean.

title: [dt] --dt-content batch aborts on ChunkLandingUnverifiedError/IndexRunVerifyRefused — _index_dt_content_record except tuple missing the tp8yk exception types
description:
Discovered during substantive-critic adjudication of nexus-2xu6t (T2 nexus/nexus-2xu6t-critique-2026-08-05 [21480]).

src/nexus/commands/dt.py `_index_dt_content_record` (370-448), the
non-file-backed `--dt-content` ingest path, wraps its `index_markdown(...)`
call in `except (RuntimeError, ImportError, OSError)` only (line 445).

`ChunkLandingUnverifiedError` and `IndexRunVerifyRefused` are `NexusError`
subclasses (src/nexus/errors.py:196, 234) — NOT caught by that tuple.

The main `nx dt index` loop's dt-content branch
(`if dt_content_active: ... _index_dt_content_record(...)`, commands/dt.py
~723-736) has no try/except of its own around that call. So either
exception, raised from inside a --dt-content record's index_markdown call,
propagates uncaught out of the entire `for uuid, path in records:` loop —
aborting the WHOLE `nx dt index --dt-content` batch on the first affected
record, and leaving every subsequent record in the batch unprocessed.

This is exactly the nexus-2fyb / nexus-qo84l / nexus-9800y regression class:
tp8yk's commit 2bce3223 added the matching except clauses
(ChunkLandingUnverifiedError, IndexRunVerifyRefused) to the file-backed
`_index_record` call site in the same loop (commands/dt.py 763-809,
collect-and-continue, converts to a failed-record entry) but never touched
`_index_dt_content_record`'s own except tuple.

Fix shape: extend `_index_dt_content_record`'s except tuple to also catch
ChunkLandingUnverifiedError / IndexRunVerifyRefused (log + return False so
the caller's existing `else: skipped += 1` path handles it), OR wrap the
`if dt_content_active: ... _index_dt_content_record(...)` call site in the
main loop with the same per-record try/except the file-backed branch
already has, converting to a `failed` entry with the same wording.

Regression test: monkeypatch index_markdown (inside _index_dt_content_record)
to raise each of the two exception types for one dt-content record among
two, assert BOTH records are processed (collect-and-continue) rather than
the batch aborting after record 1.
close_reason: Shipped develop (wave-1 commit + CHANGELOG follow-up): --dt-content collect-and-continue for both NexusError types, mirroring the file-backed site; 5 red-first tests + exit-code integration; kill control independently re-executed. Recurrence mechanism adjudicated per root-cause-after-3-patches: filed nexus-rlkgu (catch-site tripwire — extraction would not close the loop); exhaustive sweep found no 5th occurrence. Reviews T2 [21486] clean.

title: fresh-install-mvv.sh ALLOWLIST_REGEX for vw594 stale-index-run entry over-matches the UNRELATED stuck-mid-run staleness alarm under the same label
description:
Found during substantive-critic review of nexus-796zn (developer commit b69b26b1).

health.py's _check_stale_indexing_runs (label = "stale index-run fences",
health.py:4031) has TWO independent WARN-worthy branches sharing the SAME
label and CLI-rendered as f"{label}: {detail}" (format_health_for_cli,
health.py:89-91):

  1. reported_null branch (~health.py:4122-4143, the nexus-vw594 coverage-gap
     signature): detail = "N document(s) report index_state but it is NULL
     ... coverage gap ..."
  2. stale branch (~health.py:4151-4165, pre-existing stuck-mid-run alarm):
     detail = "N document(s) stranded in index_state='indexing' beyond {H}h:
     ... check for a stuck run or a rolling deploy ..."

tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh's ALLOWLIST_REGEX entry added by nexus-796zn
is:
  'stale index-run fences: [0-9]+ document'

This matches BOTH branches — both detail strings begin with "N document(s)"
immediately after the shared label prefix. The regex is scoped only by the
label + generic count prefix, not by anything unique to the intended
(reported_null / vw594-floor-gap) branch.

On today's virgin-box MVV run only branch 1 fires (nothing gets stuck
mid-index in a scripted linear journey), so the allowlist entry currently
only ever suppresses the intended case — this is why nexus-796zn's own
"would a third unexpected warning still fail the gate" self-check passed.
But branch 2 is a REAL, unrelated, always-relevant operational alarm (a
stuck index-run / split begin-complete across a rolling deploy) that this
same regex would silently swallow if it ever fired during a run — masking
a genuine defect as the known-benign engine-floor gap. This is exactly the
allowlist-blind-to-unenrolled-member failure class the 2026-08-03 shakedown
playbook (T2 nexus/shakedown-playbook §3.2) names as the reason census-style
checks beat allowlists.

Fix: anchor the regex on text unique to branch 1, e.g.
  'report index_state but it is NULL|coverage gap'
instead of the shared label+count prefix. Update
tests/test_fresh_install_mvv_published_mode.py::
test_doctor_allowlist_stays_in_grep_level_parity_with_health_py to pin the
tightened substring too.

Relay: nexus-796zn (P1). Critique: substantive-critic pass, 2026-08-05.
close_reason: Fixed in this diff: ALLOWLIST_REGEX's stale-index-run-fences alternative anchored to the vw594 branch's distinguishing text ("report index_state but it is NULL") instead of a bare [0-9]+ document pattern that also matched the genuinely-stuck-run alarm branch. New test test_allowlist_regex_matches_vw594_signal_but_not_a_real_stuck_run_alarm proves the anchored regex matches the vw594 line and rejects the stuck-run line; manually confirmed the OLD regex would have matched both.

title: chash_conformance_report SQL non_conformant>0 branch never proven against real Postgres; 'impossible by construction' claim is false
description:
nexus-du2dw / RDR-180. tests/db/test_du2dw_chash_conformance_report_engine.py and
tests/test_health_service_checks.py::TestCheckChashConformanceReport both assert
seeding a genuine non-conformant chash row through the real engine is "impossible

RekeyOpsIntegrationTest.java already has an established, working pattern

catalog_document_chunks chash_octet_check constraints, inserts genuinely

reconstructing exactly the mid-migration poisoned state this new function is

octet_length(chash) <> 32 WHERE clause across chunks_<dim> and the
collection-IN-list-filtered catalog_document_chunks subquery) has NEVER been

check test proves only the fake-reader JSON-shape mapping, never real SQL. A
subtle bug in the stored function (wrong table, wrong predicate, IN-list typo,
off-by-one on the LIMIT 20 sample) would pass every test in this diff.

Fix: add a Java integration test for nexus.chash_conformance_report(dim) using
the same withChecksDropped seeding technique RekeyOpsIntegrationTest already
established, asserting non_conformant and sample_chashes are correct against a
genuinely poisoned row. Also correct the "impossible by construction" docstring
claims in both test files once the seeding path is proven.

title: doc_indexer.py/pipeline_stages.py stale-chunk prune's source_path filter is dead for PDF/markdown (RDR-102 D2 removed the field from chunk metadata)
description:

This where-clause is used by THREE stale-chunk prune sites: _index_document, _index_pdf_incremental, and index_pdf's small-doc branch (all doc_indexer.py), plus pipeline_stages.py's _prune_stale_chunks (called from pipeline_index_pdf, the streaming path).

metadata_schema.make_chunk_metadata() — the SOLE factory every doc_indexer.py/pipeline_stages.py chunk-metadata build routes through ("Indexers should never build chunk metadata dicts by hand") — has NO source_path parameter at all. RDR-102 D2 hard-removed it. So for ANY chunk written via the real PDF/markdown ingest path, this where-clause matches ZERO rows, and stale_ids is always empty at all four sites. Empirically confirmed via a live index_pdf run against the real engine substrate (2026-08-04): metadata for a freshly-indexed PDF chunk carries no source_path key; querying col.get(where={"source_path": ...}) against a document that WAS indexed returns zero rows.

Practical effect: these four prune blocks (including nexus-tp8yk's new D3 union-guard wiring at each of them) are effectively unreachable for fresh PDF/markdown content. The user-visible cross-document dedup/prune protection people actually get on a fresh install comes entirely from mcp_infra._sweep_superseded_vectors (manifest-diff based — compares the document's OWN before/after manifest chash sets, not a source_path query), which correctly fires on every re-index that changes a document's chunk set and already has its own union guard (verified end-to-end: tests/integration/test_tp8yk_manifest_never_outruns_chunks.py::test_union_guard_keeps_shared_chunk_at_the_production_wiring).

Pre-existing (RDR-102 D2), NOT introduced by nexus-tp8yk. Likely still reachable for content code_indexer.py/prose_indexer.py write (those DO still set source_path in chunk metadata directly, bypassing make_chunk_metadata's identity-kwarg removal — indexer.py:3672, prose_indexer.py:83) IF they route through the same _identity_where-based prune functions, or for legacy pre-RDR-102 documents being re-indexed. Scope: audit whether these four prune sites' source_path fallback should be deleted as dead code (harmless either way — never incorrectly deletes, just never finds candidates) or rewired to a working identity key (e.g. doc_id-scoped, mirroring the RDR-108 Phase 3 manifest-authoritative model _sweep_superseded_vectors already uses).

title: utpuw P6a: nx self install — the packaged installer, safe by construction under side-by-side
description:
PHASE 6 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .2 .3 .4 .9.

THE ENABLING INSIGHT: under side-by-side generations a SELF-install is safe by construction — the running nx builds a NEW tree and never mutates its own. That is impossible today and it is what makes this command viable. It also solves the three-caller import-constraint problem (see .9): the machinery ships INSIDE the package as package data (e.g. src/nexus/_install/install_generation.sh), scripts/reinstall-tool.sh (.8) becomes a thin repo wrapper exec-ing the in-repo copy, and 'nx self install' execs the packaged copy from its own untouched generation. ONE implementation, no parity-test duplication.

Bootstrap (virgin box, nothing installed) stays bash-only via the repo script or the documented install path — unchanged from today.

HAZARD TO HONOUR: the script is exec'd from generation N while it builds N+1 and then GCs. GC rule (d) in .6 — never delete the generation hosting the running installer — is what makes this safe; verify it holds with an explicit test here too, not only in .6.

SCOPE FENCE (do not silently widen): this replaces the MECHANISM of 'uv tool upgrade conexus'. It does NOT merge 'uv tool upgrade conexus' + 'nx upgrade' into one self-upgrading command. RDR-143 CA-2 (docs/rdr/rdr-143-plugin-cli-version-lockstep.md:104) deliberately keeps them two commands: binary upgrade vs migration ladder. Merging them is a separate RDR. Note also src/nexus/commands/upgrade.py today never invokes uv/pip at all — it is migration/ladder-only — so the flip/GC logic has NO existing home there and must not be smuggled in.

Extras must be threaded explicitly (there is no receipt to re-derive them from — see .2).

TESTS: self-install from a live generation produces a new generation and flips; the hosting generation survives GC; extras carried forward; both source kinds (directory, registry) work.

title: utpuw P5a: src/nexus/install_layout.py — single Python source of truth, and exact generation-based staleness
description:
PHASE 5 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .1 (contract) and .2 (a real layout to test against).

The Python-side counterpart to the bash installer: resolve tools dir, shim dir, current generation, enumerate generations, read receipts, and answer 'am I stale?'.

STALENESS BECOMES EXACT, replacing an mtime heuristic:
    stale  <=>  Path(sys.prefix) != os.readlink(<tools>/current)
One readlink. No filesystem-clock inference, no false positives, no false negatives. This is ALSO design point 6 of nexus-utpuw (new spawns log, not fail, when their baked version != current) — the tripwire and the staleness detector are THE SAME MECHANISM and must be implemented once, here, not twice.

Today src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:145-168 self_staleness() infers staleness from dist-info mtime, which only works because uv replaces site-packages IN PLACE. Under side-by-side that premise is dead: the old generation's files are never replaced, so the mtime detector would report stale=False forever. That is a deliberate replacement, not a casualty — see .12 for the _stale_host reframe.

- scripts/reinstall-tool.sh: bash, may run with NOTHING installed. Cannot import nexus.

title: utpuw P3: legacy uv-tool install migration — extras bridge, shim takeover, DEFERRED legacy reap
description:
PHASE 3 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .2, .3, .4.

First run of the new installer on a box carrying the legacy 'uv tool install conexus' layout must converge it CLEANLY and — critically — WITHOUT breaking live holders.

THE ORDERING DECISION (the naive order is wrong and would violate the acceptance criterion):
'uv tool uninstall conexus' DELETES $(uv tool dir)/conexus — the exact tree every live holder is running from. That is the nexus-q3xrx hazard verbatim. A migration that uninstalls is a migration that breaks live sessions. THEREFORE: DO NOT UNINSTALL AT MIGRATION TIME.

Required order:
 1. Read uv-receipt.toml ONE LAST TIME -> extract extras -> seed the new generation nexus-install.json. This is the ONLY bridge for the [local] extra (see .2).
 2. Build the new generation side-by-side (legacy tree untouched; holders fine).
 3. Flip current.
 4. Replace ~/.local/bin/{nx,nx-mcp,nx-mcp-catalog,mineru,mineru-api} — currently uv-owned SYMLINKS into the legacy venv — with nexus-owned files, write-temp + mv -f per file.
 5. Register the legacy tree as a pseudo-generation in the GC ledger. It is reaped by a LATER install pass once its holder count reaches zero — NEVER during the migrating run.
Legacy reap is a plain rm -rf of the legacy dir, NOT 'uv tool uninstall' (by then the bin entries are ours and uv would try to remove them by name). After the rm, 'uv tool list' no longer shows conexus, so 'uv tool upgrade conexus' correctly reports not-installed.

ACCEPTED RISK, recorded not hidden: between migration and legacy reap uv still holds a valid receipt, so a stray 'uv tool upgrade conexus' (a human, or a not-yet-rewired SessionStart hook) rebuilds the legacy tree and re-symlinks OVER our shims — a silent revert. Mitigations: (a) the plugin hook rewiring (.15) ships in THIS arc, not later; (b) doctor detects a live uv-managed conexus alongside the generation layout (.11); (c) shim writes are idempotent so re-running repairs it. Our shims are regular FILES where uv writes SYMLINKS, so uv may refuse or force — either way (b) catches it. Do NOT build a lock; this is proportionate.

TESTS: migration from a fabricated legacy layout under tmp HOME — extras survive the bridge; legacy tree still present and byte-identical after migration; shims replaced symlinks with files; a simulated holder on the legacy tree blocks its reap; reap fires on a later pass once holders are gone; the whole migration exits 0 with a live holder present.

title: utpuw P2b: generation GC — keep-last-N, zero-holders, and four never-delete rules
description:
PHASE 2 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .3 (flip/rollback) and .5 (census).

GC pass at install time. Nix model per research finding 6.

NEVER DELETE:
 (a) the generation 'current' points at;
 (b) the PREVIOUS current — rollback for free (.3);
 (c) any generation with a live holder (census, .5);
 (d) the generation hosting the RUNNING INSTALLER. Under 'nx self install' (.14) the installer script is exec'd from its own generation; keep-last-N usually covers this implicitly, but it must be an EXPLICIT rule, not an emergent one.
Keep the last 2-3 generations unconditionally regardless of holders.

NEVER GC THE BASE INTERPRETER (research amendment 4): old generations' pyvenv.cfg home= points at a uv-managed CPython. Deleting or pruning it silently breaks every old generation (pipx#146 / uv#8028 class). We never touch it; .11 adds the doctor check that detects when uv prunes it out from under us.

SCOPE STRICTLY TO tools/ (audit risk #4): ~/.local/share/nexus/ also holds chroma/ (stranded_install.py:113-125) and fastembed_cache/ (config.py:522), documented at mcp/core.py:6402 as user data explicitly NOT removed by uninstall. A GC that walks the parent is a data-loss bug.

TESTS (these are the destructive-path tests — be exhaustive): each never-delete rule individually and in combination; keep-last-N boundary; a gen with a holder that also falls outside keep-last-N is retained; sibling dirs chroma/ and fastembed_cache/ untouched (explicit assertion, both present before and after); GC is a no-op on a fresh single-generation install.

title: utpuw P1c: shim writer — nexus-owned readlink-before-exec files for nx/nx-mcp/nx-mcp-catalog/mineru/mineru-api
description:
PHASE 1 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .1.

Write nexus-owned regular FILES (never symlinks) into $NX_BIN_DIR for an explicit ALLOWLIST of console scripts: nx, nx-mcp, nx-mcp-catalog, mineru, mineru-api. Allowlist, not a glob — <gen>/bin also contains python, pip, activate etc. which must NOT be shimmed. Write a shim only if the target exists in the new generation.

mineru/mineru-api ARE IN SCOPE (audit risk #6): scripts/reinstall-tool.sh:169-183 is the ONLY thing in the repo that symlinks them into ~/.local/bin today. Drop them and 'nx mineru start' regresses via the src/nexus/_mineru_spawn.py:118-153 PATH fallback (path (c)); paths (a) sys.executable-adjacent and (b) ancestor-walk still work inside a gen venv, so the regression is PATH-only and therefore easy to miss.

Writes must be IDEMPOTENT and per-file atomic (write temp + mv -f), because migration (.7) replaces uv-owned symlinks at these exact names and because re-running the installer must repair a reverted shim.

The shim body is fixed by .1's template — readlink before exec, absolute tools path baked, clear error on dangling current.

--- AUDIT FINDING F1 (HIGH, nx_plan_audit 2026-08-04) — FOLDED IN ---
A LITERAL allowlist of five names was WRONG: it omitted nx-session-end-launcher, the project's
FOURTH console script (pyproject [project.scripts]: nx, nx-mcp, nx-mcp-catalog,
nx-session-end-launcher). conexus/hooks/hooks.json:56 invokes it by BARE PATH NAME with no
fallback, so omitting its shim silently kills every SessionEnd flush post-migration. uv symlinks
ALL of a project's own entry points today, which is why this works now and why the omission would
not surface until after the layout moved.

CORRECTED RULE — derive, do not hardcode (same principle as the process markers in .10):
  shim set = (every console script declared by the INSTALLED distribution, read from its
              entry_points metadata in the new generation)

uv's own rule is the first clause; the second is our documented extension (uv does not link
dependency entry points, which is why scripts/reinstall-tool.sh:169-183 exists at all).
This is future-proof against a fifth entry point being added without anyone updating a list.

Still an EXCLUSION list, not a glob: <gen>/bin also holds python, pip, activate etc. which must
never be shimmed.

title: utpuw P1b: atomic current flip — symlink-then-rename, never ln -sfn
description:
PHASE 1 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .1.

Flip $NX_TOOLS_DIR/current to a newly built generation ATOMICALLY.

'ln -sfn' is NOT atomic (unlink + symlink leaves a window where 'current' does not exist; a spawn in that window gets a shim failure). Required form:
  ln -s <abs-gen> <tools>/.current.tmp.$$ && mv -f -h <tools>/.current.tmp.$$ <tools>/current
macOS BSD mv needs -h (operate on the symlink itself, do not follow); GNU is 'mv -T'. Python equivalent os.replace() is acceptable where a Python path exists. Target stored ABSOLUTE.

Include the ROLLBACK flip in this bead: previous-current is recorded (see .6 GC retention), so rollback is one symlink flip and comes free — do not defer it to a later arc.

TESTS: flip under a concurrent reader loop asserting 'current' ALWAYS resolves (no window); assert stored target is absolute; assert a dangling/missing current produces the shim's clear error (exit 70) and not a cryptic exec failure; rollback flip returns to the prior generation.
Context: plan in T2 — mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_get(project="nexus", title="plan-utpuw-versioned-installs"). Prior art: T2 nexus/research-utpuw-versioned-install-prior-art [21426]. Design of record: nexus-utpuw description + both comments.

title: utpuw P1a: generation builder — build venv AT its final versioned path, nexus-owned receipt, extras first-class
description:
PHASE 1 of nexus-utpuw. Depends on .1 (layout contract).

Build a new generation at $NX_TOOLS_DIR/gen-<stamp>/ and write its receipt. Never touches any existing generation — this is what makes the whole design safe under live holders.

MECHANISM (research amendment 2 — do NOT use per-version UV_TOOL_DIR):
  uv venv --python 3.12 <gen>
  uv pip install --python <gen>/bin/python '<spec>'
Rationale: console-script shebangs bake ABSOLUTE paths at install time, so the tree is not relocatable and must be built at its final path. Per-version UV_TOOL_DIR was rejected: the receipt lives inside the env, and uv would also need UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR redirected or it clobbers the shared bin symlinks — the top-level shims must be nexus-owned FILES, never uv-owned symlinks.

DO NOT use 'uv venv --relocatable' — it rewrites shebangs to an exec trick; absolute baked paths are exactly what this design requires.

SPEC CONSTRUCTION: preserve the PEP 508 fixup from scripts/reinstall-tool.sh:157-158 — extras precede a version pin, so 'conexus==X[local]' is INVALID; build 'conexus[local]==X'. Both sources must keep working: local checkout ('.', the dev loop) and registry ('conexus==X.Y.Z').

EXTRAS ARE NOW FIRST-CLASS (audit risk #4): uv-receipt.toml was the ONLY home for extras (reinstall-tool.sh:133-151, upgrade_finish.install_source():525-557). Losing them re-opens the 768->384 embedder-downgrade P0 documented in README.md:80. Extras go in nexus-install.json and are threaded explicitly through every later install; there is no receipt to re-derive them from.

RECORD base_interpreter IN THE RECEIPT: uv venv writes pyvenv.cfg home= pointing at a uv-managed CPython. That interpreter is outside our control ('uv python uninstall' / uv pruning can orphan every old generation — the pipx#146 / uv#8028 class). We cannot prevent it; we must be able to DETECT it (doctor check in .12). Note 'uv venv --python 3.12' may resolve a different patch over time -> base-interpreter proliferation. Benign (each gen references its own) but do not assume a shared base.

TESTS: build into tmp NX_TOOLS_DIR with a stubbed uv (pattern: tests/scripts/test_reinstall_tool_downgrade_guard.py:59-75 _stub_uv); assert gen dir shape, receipt fields, extras round-trip, PEP 508 spec construction for both source kinds, and that NO pre-existing generation is mutated (hash the tree before/after).
Context: plan in T2 — mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_get(project="nexus", title="plan-utpuw-versioned-installs"). Prior art: T2 nexus/research-utpuw-versioned-install-prior-art [21426]. Design of record: nexus-utpuw description + both comments.

entry point and the packaging/resource-resolution around it — it does NOT create the script.

title: utpuw P0: generation layout contract — paths, env overrides, receipt schema, shim template
description:
PHASE 0 of nexus-utpuw (design of record: bead description 5-point design + comment 1 acceptance + comment 2 research amendments; T2 nexus/research-utpuw-versioned-install-prior-art [21426]).

Lock the path algebra + on-disk contract that every later phase depends on. Pure definition + tests, no installer behaviour yet.

CONTRACT
- NX_TOOLS_DIR (default "$HOME/.local/share/nexus/tools") — generation root.
- NX_BIN_DIR   (default "$HOME/.local/bin")               — shim dir.
- Generations: $NX_TOOLS_DIR/gen-<stamp>/ (a real venv, built AT this path).
- Pointer:     $NX_TOOLS_DIR/current -> ABSOLUTE path of a gen dir (plain readlink, NOT readlink -f; -f is macOS >= 12.3 only).
- Receipt:     $NX_TOOLS_DIR/gen-<stamp>/nexus-install.json, nexus-OWNED (replaces uv-receipt.toml as the home of extras).
  {"schema":1,"version":"7.2.0","spec":"conexus[local]==7.2.0",
   "source_kind":"directory"|"registry","source":"/Users/.../git/nexus"|"conexus",
   "extras":["local"],"python":"3.12.8",
   "base_interpreter":"/.../uv/python/cpython-3.12.8-.../bin/python3.12",
   "created_at":"...","installer_schema":1}
- Shim template (readlink-before-exec is MANDATORY, not stylistic — see below).

WHY DEFAULTS MUST BE $HOME-DERIVED (do not hardcode, do not cache):
tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:174-187 and tests/e2e/run.sh:143-148 isolate ONLY by redirecting $HOME. The activation-BEFORE-reinstall ordering fixed in 137d2688 works precisely because uv derives its install location off $HOME. If our defaults stop being $HOME-derived, release-sandbox.sh silently starts clobbering the live install — the regression AGENTS.md:163 warns about.

WHY THE SHIM MUST readlink BEFORE exec (load-bearing CPython fact, research finding 2):
Modules/getpath.py checks for pyvenv.cfg adjacent to the executable AS INVOKED (unresolved) BEFORE realpath; realpath happens later and only feeds base_executable/home search. So exec-ing .../current/bin/nx leaks the "current" component into sys.prefix and sys.path, and a later flip retargets every not-yet-imported module — reproducing the nexus-q3xrx lazy-import failure class exactly. Shim form:
  #!/bin/sh
  NX_GEN="$(readlink "<ABS>/tools/current")" || exit 70
  exec "$NX_GEN/bin/<cmd>" "$@"
Shims bake the ABSOLUTE tools path (HOME-independent once written; a sandbox HOME gets sandbox-pointing shims). Consequence: shims MUST be rewritten when NX_TOOLS_DIR changes; they cannot be shared across sandboxes.

NAMESPACE CARE: $HOME/.local/share/nexus/ ALREADY holds chroma/ (src/nexus/stranded_install.py:113-125) and fastembed_cache/ (src/nexus/config.py:522), documented in src/nexus/mcp/core.py:6402 as user data explicitly NOT removed by uninstall. The tools/ subtree is ours; GC must be scoped strictly to it.

TESTS (TDD, write first)
- Path algebra: defaults resolve off $HOME; NX_TOOLS_DIR/NX_BIN_DIR overrides honoured; no absolute caching.
- Receipt round-trip incl. extras and source_kind.
- Shim template renders readlink-before-exec and contains NO bare exec of the current symlink (a literal negative assertion — this is the regression tripwire for the single subtlest constraint in the design).

Context: mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__memory_get(project="nexus", title="plan-utpuw-versioned-installs"). Use sequential-thinking for the env-override surface. SPAWN sub-agents for parallel work; conserve top-level context.

title: reinstall-tool venv swap: replace in-place --reinstall with side-by-side versioned installs + spawn-time binding
description:
Problem (recurs every dev-loop reinstall): uv tool install --reinstall rebuilds
\$(uv tool dir)/conexus IN PLACE. Every live holder (nx-mcp / nx-mcp-catalog in
every Claude session, storage-service supervisor, in-flight nx runs) suffers
delayed lazy-import failures after the swap (nexus-q3xrx: cacert vanish,
0.0.0 version skew, ModuleNotFoundError). The q3xrx holder guard therefore
refuses whenever ANY Claude session is open — which for Hal is always. The
friction is structural: with in-place swap, 'safe reinstall under live
sessions' is impossible by construction, so the guard can only offer
close-everything / --cycle-daemons / --force.

Design-level fix (nix/homebrew model — immutable versioned trees, atomic flip):
1. Each install lands in a FRESH versioned dir (e.g.
   ~/.local/share/nexus/tools/<stamp>/, via UV_TOOL_DIR=<stamp dir>), never
   touching the tree live processes hold.
2. ~/.local/bin shims (nx, nx-mcp, nx-mcp-catalog, mineru*) become spawn-time
   binders: exec "\$(readlink .../current)/conexus/bin/<cmd>". A process
   resolves 'current' once at spawn and holds that REAL path for life —
   flipping the symlink never changes a running process's venv.
3. Install = build new dir -> atomically repoint 'current'. New spawns get new
   code; live holders keep their intact old tree. No refusal needed at all.
4. GC pass at install time: delete versioned dirs with zero live holders
   (reuse live_venv_processes() per-dir). Old trees linger only while a
   session that spawned from them is still alive.
5. Guard semantics invert: instead of REFUSING under holders, report
   'N sessions still bound to <old-stamp>; they converge on their next MCP
   restart' — the exact model the plugin's SessionStart background upgrade
   already promises ('takes effect on your next session').

Ripple surfaces to audit before implementing (this is why it's a design bead,
not a patch): uv tool receipt/extras preservation (reinstall-tool.sh reads
uv-receipt.toml), uv tool list/upgrade bookkeeping under a non-default
UV_TOOL_DIR, the plugin's background extras-preserving upgrade dispatch,
nx doctor install checks, tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh (sandbox HOME
activation ordering, fixed 137d2688), fresh-install-mvv.sh, and anything
hardcoding \$(uv tool dir)/conexus.

Until this ships, the refusal recurs by design whenever any Claude session is
open; remedies stay: close/kill stale sessions (esp. orphaned --fork-session
holders), --cycle-daemons for nx-owned daemons, --force + restart MCP.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (Hal, 2026-08-04): zero flags, zero steps. Bare 'scripts/reinstall-tool.sh' must ALWAYS succeed under any number of live sessions — no refusal, no --force, no --cycle-daemons, no close-your-sessions instruction. The flags exist only because in-place swap makes safety structurally impossible; under versioned side-by-side installs the refusal path, --force, and --cycle-daemons are DELETED, not kept as escape hatches. Live holders keep their old tree untouched and converge at their next spawn; the only output about them is informational. The downgrade/divergent-source guards (stale-checkout, PyPI-over-dev) are a different failure class and stay.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
WEB RESEARCH COMPLETE (2026-08-04, full findings: T2 nexus/research-utpuw-versioned-install-prior-art [21426]). Prior art VALIDATES versioned-trees+shims+atomic-flip+GC: it is the Nix (profiles/generations), Homebrew (Cellar+opt), Chrome (Omaha side-by-side), rustup/asdf/mise (spawn-time shims) model, and wingu built exactly this for Python venvs under gunicorn (zero-downtime deploys writeup). uv has NO atomic/versioned tool-install story upstream; pipx shares the disease (pipx #146). DESIGN AMENDMENTS from findings:
1. Shim MUST readlink before exec — CPython getpath.py does the pyvenv.cfg lookup on the UNRESOLVED path (symlink resolution happens later and only feeds base_executable/stdlib), so exec'ing .../current/bin/nx directly leaks the 'current' component into sys.prefix+sys.path and reproduces the q3xrx class on flip. Shim form: #!/bin/sh + exec "$(readlink /abs/current)/bin/<cmd>" "$@", with current's target stored ABSOLUTE (plain readlink suffices; readlink -f only macOS>=12.3).
2. Build each venv AT its final versioned path (console-script shebangs bake absolute paths at install; tree is not relocatable). Prefer plain 'uv venv <dir> && uv pip install --python <dir> ...' over per-version UV_TOOL_DIR (receipt lives inside the env; would also need UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR redirected or uv clobbers the shared bin symlinks — top-level shims must be nexus-owned files, never uv-owned symlinks). Extras preservation moves from uv-receipt.toml to a nexus-owned receipt.
3. Flip must be symlink-then-rename, NOT ln -sfn (unlink+symlink window where current doesn't exist). macOS: mv -f -h tmp current, or python os.replace.
4. GC: keep last 2-3 generations unconditionally (free rollback, Chrome delete-after-confirm); never GC the uv-managed BASE interpreter that old venvs' pyvenv.cfg home= points at (pipx#146/uv#8028 class).
5. Simpler alternative seriously evaluated: shiv zipapp (SHA-256-keyed extraction cache = immune by construction) — rejected for now (3 entry points, new distribution artifact, first-run latency); fallback if venv-generation plumbing turns out gnarly.
6. Cheap tripwire: new spawns log (not fail) when their baked version != current.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PLAN COMPLETE + AUDITED (strategic-planner, 2026-08-04).

Plan: T2 nexus/plan-utpuw-versioned-installs [21427]. Audit outcome + corrections: T2 nexus/plan-utpuw-versioned-installs-audit-outcome [21428] — read BOTH, the plan body predates the audit corrections. nx_plan_audit verdict PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; all cited line anchors independently verified; 7 findings all folded into the beads before work starts.

BEADS: nexus-utpuw.1-.25 (20 work + 5 stacked-review gates), 67 dep edges, acyclic. Only .1 is ready; the graph gates everything else. Incidental finding filed as nexus-4com9.

PHASES: P0 layout contract (.1) -> P1 builder/flip/shims (.2-.4) -> RG-A (.21) -> P2 census+GC (.5,.6) and P3 legacy migration (.7) -> RG-B (.22) -> P4 reinstall-tool.sh rewrite (.8, THE ACCEPTANCE BEAD) -> RG-C (.23); P5 Python consumers (.9-.13) and P6 self-install/hook (.14,.15) -> RG-D (.24) -> P7 E2E (.16-.19) -> RG-E (.25) -> P8 docs (.20).

THREE DECISIONS THE BEAD DID NOT SETTLE (full rationale in the plan):
1. Machinery ships as package data src/nexus/_install/install_generation.sh; reinstall-tool.sh and 'nx self install' both exec it. Enabled by: under side-by-side, a SELF-install is safe by construction (the running nx builds a new tree, never mutates its own). Three callers have incompatible import constraints — the plugin hook runs under a BARE python3 and cannot import nexus.
2. Legacy migration must NOT run 'uv tool uninstall' — it deletes the tree live holders are running from (the q3xrx hazard verbatim, and it would violate the zero-flag acceptance criterion). Order: bridge extras out of uv-receipt.toml -> build side-by-side -> flip -> take over uv's ~/.local/bin symlinks -> register legacy as a pseudo-generation, reap on a LATER pass at zero holders via plain rm -rf.
3. _stale_host's mtime premise dying is a FIX, not a casualty: staleness becomes exact (sys.prefix != readlink(current)), and that is THE SAME MECHANISM as design point 6's spawn-time tripwire — implement once, in install_layout.py.

HIGHEST-VALUE AUDIT CATCH (F1, HIGH): the shim allowlist omitted nx-session-end-launcher, the project's FOURTH console script, invoked by bare PATH name at conexus/hooks/hooks.json:56 with no fallback — every SessionEnd flush would have died silently post-migration. Fixed by DERIVING the shim set from the installed distribution's entry_points plus an explicit dependency-script list, rather than lengthening a hardcoded list. Note the pattern: this arc removes one hardcoded-inventory failure class (_PROC_MARKERS) and nearly reintroduced the identical class in the shim list.

THREE SILENT-ROT SURFACES that must ship in THIS arc, not later: upgrade_finish.py:61-65 (hardcoded 'uv/tools/conexus' disables the entire restart-stale pass), health.py:148-201 ('Process freshness' renders SILENT GREEN — the exact failure it exists to prevent), version_lockstep_action.py:200 (SessionStart auto-upgrade becomes a permanent no-op; marker stays stale and the hook re-nudges forever).

CI CANNOT CATCH THIS CLASS: zero uv-tool references in .github/workflows, and fresh-install-mvv.sh installs via plain 'uv pip install' and never touches shims. Hence .16 must be a FAST test that runs by default, not an E2E-only gate.

No RDR up front — the bead description + both comments + the research memo are the design of record. Named escalation trip: if RG-D finds the staleness/marker reframe changes OBSERVABLE upgrade semantics, that becomes an RDR rather than a bead comment.

title: SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest.OLD_TAG rotation is blocked by its own structural preconditions — v0.1.17 pin rots while every rotation candidate ≥v0.1.33 contains catalog-013/014
description: The nexus-7z6s7 rotation policy says advance OLD_TAG to the previously-deployed engine tag when the cloud reference materially advances (now v0.1.65; previously-deployed = v0.1.64). But the rotation is structurally impossible as a mechanical bump: the javadoc's precondition requires the tag's changelog tree to PREDATE the guard-bearing changesets under test (catalog-013-chash-checks-validate, catalog-014-manifest-collection-stamp, both first shipped v0.1.33+), and every plausible rotation candidate now contains them — the data leg's changesetApplied gates would fail loudly (correctly: the hop's assertions go vacuous). The v0.1.64->HEAD hop contains exactly ONE changelog edit (fk-001-catalog-cross-store.xml, +11 lines) and likely zero row-DML-on-FORCE-RLS changesets, so a rotated data leg would have an empty seed-coverage set and no subject. Rotation therefore requires a REDESIGN decision: (a) keep v0.1.17 and re-justify the aged-box claim explicitly (fleet-history argument), (b) rotate and redesign the data leg around whatever the new hop actually exercises (possibly retiring the row-DML leg until a future row-DML changeset ships, with the gm38i lint pinning the empty set), or (c) pick a mid-history tag that still predates catalog-013 with a documented realism rationale. Three-part mechanics per nexus-gm38i (regenerate scripts/gen_rehearsal_hop_manifest.py snapshot, re-derive seed coverage, re-point SEED-COVERAGE block + DECLARED_SEED_COVERAGE) apply AFTER the design pick. Found during 7.2.0 release prep 2026-08-04 (handoff listed the rotation as a release item; it is not mechanically executable). Related: nexus-7z6s7 (policy), nexus-gm38i (lint), nexus-u5dln (data leg).

title: plan-shape/cost tripwire for the tombstone liveness predicates — the M1 whole-manifest-subplan class shipped green through every gate twice
description: msz9i critique Sig-4 disposition (T2 [21411]): no cost or plan-shape gate exists anywhere in the service suite — TombstoneFilterGateTest is name-presence regex only. The whole-manifest hashed-subplan class shipped undetected twice: dcf77fb7's raw-SQL predicate (hybrid, caught days later by a cloud p50 relay) and the jOOQ twin (get/list, 101x-739x on point lookups, caught only by msz9i's review round). Add an EXPLAIN-based tripwire test at the layer that failed: assert the rendered plans for both liveChunksPredicate and liveChunksCondition contain NO whole-relation SubPlan/seq-scan over catalog_document_chunks (or assert estimated cost under a ceiling with headroom) on a representative fixture — a plan-shape assert, not a wall-time assert (deterministic under CI load). Model: HybridSelectiveGateTest already uses plain EXPLAIN for plan-shape dispatch checks — extend the pattern. Accept conexus-side cloud p50 monitoring as the outer guard; this is the inner one.

title: search_topic_scoped_<dim> SQL functions still carry the pre-msz9i two-subquery live_chunks shape — divergent from the Java predicate, same whole-manifest scan
description:
Found during nexus-msz9i's EXPLAIN investigation. catalog-006 changesets 4-6 (search_topic_scoped_384/768/1024), carried forward into catalog-019-tombstone-aware-read-views.xml, embed the ORIGINAL live_chunks predicate verbatim in their SQL function bodies:
  (NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM catalog_document_chunks m WHERE m.tenant_id=c.tenant_id AND m.chash=c.chash)
   OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM catalog_document_chunks m JOIN catalog_documents d ... WHERE ... AND d.deleted_at IS NULL))

nexus-msz9i proved with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) that this shape makes PG build TWO hashed SubPlans, each seq-scanning the ENTIRE catalog_document_chunks manifest once per query — a fixed cost linear in total manifest size — and inflates the plan cost ~160x, which crosses jit_above_cost and adds ~118ms of JIT compile per query. The Java-side predicate (PgVectorRepository.liveChunksPredicate) is being rewritten to the equivalent DEAD-SET form under msz9i.

Two problems left behind:
1. PERF: the topic-scoped search path keeps the expensive shape. Lower volume than hybrid search so not a p50 driver, but the same corpus-scaling cost applies.
2. DRIFT: the SQL functions and the Java predicate now express the same policy in two different (and differently-performing) ways. This is exactly the class of divergence catalog-019 was created to close — its own header documents four views whose predicates had silently disagreed with the rest of the tombstone surface.

Fix shape: a new Liquibase changeset CREATE OR REPLACE-ing the three search_topic_scoped_<dim> functions with the dead-set form (DDL through Liquibase only). Equivalence rests on fk_catalog_chunks_catalog_doc (fk-001-5) being added VALIDATED — see msz9i's T2 entry for the full argument.

Also worth auditing in the same sweep: catalog-007 graph-hop functions and catalog-008 combined-query extensions for the same embedded shape.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DUPLICATE FINDING CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-10 — commenting rather than filing a second bead.

Source: T2 [22176] `nexus/falsifiability-enforcement-design-2026-08-10` §B2 re-derived this finding from scratch. Re-verified against the tree today; adding the exact lines, two facts the original filing did not carry, and an acceptance bar.

## Re-verified, exact — tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh

    :92   _pass() { echo "  ✓ $*"; }
    :93   _step() { echo; echo "── $* ──"; }
    ...
    :363      _pass "mcpb pack produces a $BUNDLE_SIZE-byte bundle (well under 100 KB)"
    :364  else
    :365      _pass "skipped (mcpb/ not present on this branch)"
    :366  fi
    ...
    :369  _step "12/12 PASS"

(T2 [22176] cited `:366-371`; the `_pass "skipped"` is at :365 and the summary `_step` at :369. Substance unaffected — line numbers have drifted since the 2026-08-03 filing.)

## Two facts to add to this bead

1. `_pass()` at :92 renders as `  ✓ <text>`. So the skip is not merely counted as a pass — it is rendered with the SAME success tick as a real pass. There is no visual or greppable distinction at all between step 11 passing and step 11 not existing.

2. **THERE IS NO GREPPABLE PASSED SENTINEL IN THE FILE.** `grep -n "PASSED" tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` returns nothing. The terminal verdict is `_step "12/12 PASS"` at :369, which is unconditional — it is reached whether or not step 11 did anything, and it is not a machine-checkable sentinel any caller can key on. This second half is the more serious of the two and was not in the original filing.

## Classification

This is one of four instances of a single defect class — **success-shaped emptiness: a gate that passes when it did nothing** — filed together today. The pattern matters more than any individual instance; whoever fixes one should fix the shape.

Siblings filed 2026-08-10:
- nexus-epj0b — auth-login.sh prints a failure message and exits 0
- nexus-poplq — run.sh `--scenario` mismatch runs nothing, reports `0 passed, 0 failed`, exits 0
- nexus-i1oh4 — cloud-client-path-gate.sh counts only failures, so an unrun leg prints PASSED

Adjacent prior art in the same class: nexus-ogzsz, nexus-eu2sg, nexus-3znzn, nexus-wbeyi, nexus-c7fht.

## Recommend P3 -> P2

Currently P3. The three siblings above are all P2, and the missing greppable sentinel (fact 2) makes this the same severity: the gate has no machine-checkable verdict at all. Raising is a bd update, outside this pass's write scope — flagging for whoever grooms.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (not suggestions) — adding to the existing asks

- [ ] A skip is reported DISTINCTLY from a pass (its own marker, its own count), or the branch asserts mcpb/ must be present.
- [ ] The terminal verdict becomes a greppable sentinel carrying counts, e.g. `UPGRADE-SHAKEOUT PASSED — steps=12 skipped=0`, and is NOT reached unconditionally.
- [ ] **MEASURE THE DETECTOR AGAINST A DELIBERATELY BROKEN FIX.** Run the shakeout in a sandbox with `mcpb/` deliberately absent and demonstrate the output no longer claims a clean 12/12 — paste it. Then run with `mcpb/` present and demonstrate the real pass and the sentinel. Both directions, both pasted.
- [ ] The original second half of this bead still stands: the header docstring documents only 10 of the 12 steps.

Rationale for the bar: 2026-08-10 produced a gate committed, reviewed, and dead on arrival because nobody ran it, and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after a 12-site sweep. A fix to a false-clean gate that is itself never observed going red is the same failure again.

Only `tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` touched.

## Acceptance criteria disposition

- [x] **A skip is reported DISTINCTLY from a pass.** New `_skip()` helper

      every real check — not an unconditional claim layered on top of the real work.
      `grep -q "UPGRADE-SHAKEOUT PASSED"` is now a valid machine-checkable gate for any
      caller (release skill, CI, etc.).
- [x] **Measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix, both directions.**
      Rather than driving a full 3-5 minute sandboxed `run` twice (mcpb/ present vs.
      absent requires either two different worktree states or moving mcpb/ aside,
      which risks corrupting the shared working tree other sessions are also using —
      out of this pass's scope), the byte-bound half of the detector
      (`_check_mcpb_size`) was extracted into a pure function and demonstrated via the

      transcript pasted on nexus-x8fuq (item E section), reproduced below for this
      bead's own record:

          GREEN (unmodified):
            ✓ RED: near-empty 10B -> TOO_SMALL verdict
            ✓ RED: empty size fails the gate
            ✓ GREEN: 50000B passes the gate
            SELF-TEST PASSED

            ✗ FAIL: RED: near-empty 10B -> TOO_SMALL verdict — expected [TOO_SMALL] got [OK]
            SELF-TEST FAILED — 1 check(s)
            EXIT: 1

      The skip-vs-pass distinction itself (the more serious of this bead's two facts)

      when `mcpb/manifest.json` is absent, and `SKIP_COUNT` is only ever incremented

## Recommend P3 -> P2

Not actioned in this pass (scope was fixing the script, not bead metadata) — flagging
again per the original comment's own recommendation, for whoever grooms.

`bash -n tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` clean. `shellcheck` clean.

title: CI latency: pytest job is 24-30min wall per push — sharding + doc-only fast lane options (decision packet for Hal)
description: Hal 2026-08-03: 'our CI is geologic in latency'. Facts: the pytest (Python 3.12) job runs 24-30min wall per develop push; 18,780 test functions; pytest is 92% of CI compute (project_ci_cost_structure — cadence is the COST lever and batching is already practiced; this bead is about LATENCY). Options, each scored against the CI Cost Discipline directives: (A) SHARD the pytest job across 3-4 matrix runners (pytest-split or --num-shards): wall 30->~8-10min; compute cost ~= same total test-minutes + ~2min setup per shard; per-process execution stays SERIAL so the no-parallel-tests invariant holds within each shard; required-check aggregation needs a fan-in job with job-level skip semantics. (B) DOC-ONLY FAST LANE: dorny paths-filter skips pytest entirely when the diff touches only docs/, conexus/skills/, *.md — job-level skip so branch protection stays satisfied, WITH the mandatory non-vacuity assert (a lane that skip-passes must prove its predicate was evaluated); cost AND latency win, zero correctness risk. (C) AFFECTED-SUBSET tier for interior develop pushes (path->test-subset mapping) with full suite at PR-to-main: biggest latency win, REJECTED-BY-DEFAULT — subset-mapping drift is the layer-test failure class and the release battery is the only other full-suite net. RECOMMENDATION: A+B; revisit C only with a mechanically-derived (not hand-maintained) mapping. RELEASER IS HUMAN and CI cost discipline is DIRECTIVE: Hal picks; do not implement without his selection.

title: expectations_owes_report's CONSUMED settlement has no concurrency guard — same-type parallel background stops can race the read-then-append and violate N-of-type exactness
design:
Wave-1 subagent-reliability-burndown, nexus-hbr4x (tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh:223-264 expectations_owes_report). The CONSUMED-verb settlement is a read (awk scan of the whole ledger file) followed by a conditional append — two separate operations with a race window between them, and NO lock guards it.

Contrast: the sibling EXPECT-write path in the SAME arc (conexus/hooks/scripts/agent-dispatch-expect.sh's _expect_if_absent, guarded by a bounded mkdir LOCKDIR) explicitly protects against exactly this TOCTOU class — precedent nexus-3h0u6, and it has a dedicated concurrency test (tests/hooks/test_agent_dispatch_expect.py::TestIdempotence::test_concurrent_double_registration_writes_one_row, 8-way ThreadPoolExecutor). expectations_owes_report has no analogous lock and no analogous test; tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py::test_consumed_settlement_n_of_type only exercises SEQUENTIAL stops.

CONCRETE RACE: two agents of the same type, each with an unspent background credit unit available, stop within the same window. Both awk passes read credit=N, spent=K (before either appends); both compute verdict "new"; both append their own CONSUMED row. This can inflate `spent` beyond what real STOP order should have allowed, letting a LATER same-type stop see credit<=spent and be waved through earlier than the N-of-type contract promises (under-detection), OR let more than N agents simultaneously believe they owe (over-blocking) depending on which side of the race a given agent lands on.

This is a real production scenario, not hypothetical: parallel same-type agent fleets are an explicitly encouraged dispatch pattern (user CLAUDE.md: "If the user specifies... parallel... single message with multiple tool use content blocks").

RECOMMENDATION: add a bounded lock around the read-then-append in expectations_owes_report (same lockdir pattern as the EXPECT write path), or explicitly document+test the race's bounded impact if a lock is judged unnecessary overhead for a stop-time hook.

title: release battery is ~90min serial when it should be ~25min — parallelize the hermetic sandbox gates (MVV/LSG/PKGUP) and stop pre-running the suites PR CI re-runs as required checks

title: engine: malformed/type-mismatched request bodies return 500 internal-server-error instead of 400 — Jackson parse exceptions miss the 4xx ladder in every handler
description: SHAKEOUT-7.1.1 agent D (2026-08-03, live v0.1.62): POST /v1/catalog/index-run/begin with '{not json at all', POST /v1/vectors/search with '{this is not json}', and type-mismatched {"doc_id":12345,"chunk_count":"banana"} all return 500 {"error":"internal server error"}. Root cause confirmed in source: handlers map IllegalArgumentException -> 400 (VectorHandler.java:189) but Jackson parse/cast exceptions (JsonProcessingException, ClassCastException from tree navigation) fall through to the blanket catch (CatalogHandler.java:257-264, VectorHandler.java:200). No stack-trace leakage (body is the opaque literal) — the defect is CLASSIFICATION: client errors inflate the 5xx rate, mislead incident triage, and wear the retryable shape (clients retry 5xx; a malformed body will never succeed). Well-formed-but-wrong bodies already 400 correctly throughout. Fix shape: catch the Jackson exception family (and cast errors from body navigation) in the shared request-parse path -> 400 typed envelope; regression tests drive each handler with unparseable + type-mismatched bodies asserting 400. bd-searched five phrasings 2026-08-03, uncovered. title: reinstall-tool holder check cannot distinguish live MCP holders from PPID-1 orphans — refusal blocks on processes whose parent died days ago
description:

Hal cycled every Claude session per the refusal's own remedy text and the refusal persisted — because the holders were ORPHANS: PPID 1 (launchd), 22h23m elapsed, parent long dead. Same leaked-worker class as the posix-semaphore-exhaustion accumulator already in the bd memory bank (ungraceful daemon exits leak resource_tracker/spawn pairs).

Fix shape: in the holder scan, classify each holder by PPID. PPID==1 (or PPID no longer exists) => STALE ORPHAN: report it separately ('orphaned worker, parent dead — safe to kill: kill <pid>') and optionally offer/perform the kill under a flag (e.g. --reap-orphans), still refusing on genuinely-parented holders. Keep the hard refusal for live-parented holders (nexus-q3xrx semantics unchanged). Caution: resource_tracker legitimately outlives SOME parents briefly during teardown; require an age threshold (e.g. >5 min) alongside PPID-1 before calling it stale. Test: spawn a fake venv-python child, orphan it, assert the tool classifies it stale and reaps under the flag; assert a live-parented holder still refuses.

Evidence: ps -o pid,ppid,etime on 49235/49236 -> PPID 1, ELAPSED 22:23:53; kill freed the venv; reinstall then proceeded (session 4f5f523d continuation d6cc425d).
notes: SHAKEOUT agent E census (2026-08-03): actual orphan population is 22 resource_tracker+spawn_main pairs at PPID 1 (44 procs; 46 total venv-python PPID-1, ~18GB summed RSS) — 11x the 2 pids this bead recorded. The reap tooling this bead prescribes should sweep the population, not just classify at reinstall time.
