title: possible hang in multi-threaded pipeline resume when WAL is preserved but pipeline row was marked failed (unconfirmed root cause)
description:
Observed 2026-08-02 as a SIDE FINDING while diagnosing nexus-gl99l (the
stale-progress-counter defect) during nexus-5xn3k.7 RUNFENCE gate
construction. NOT independently root-caused — filed as a documented,
reproducible-so-far observation rather than silently dropped.

## Observation

Variant of the nexus-gl99l repro where, instead of letting
`clear_orphan_wal` run for real, it was stubbed to a no-op (leaving the
WAL pages/chunks intact) while `db.mark_failed` ran normally (needed to
avoid PipelineConflictRunning on an immediate same-test retry, since a
'running' row's heartbeat would otherwise read as fresh).

With the WAL genuinely preserved, `chunker_loop`'s resume correctly
found `written_up_to == 200` (all chunks still embedded) and skipped
re-chunking; `uploader_loop` then correctly proceeded to upload the
un-uploaded remainder (the second ~100-chunk batch landed in T3
successfully, confirmed via `http_vector_upsert_chunks count=100` in
the debug log). Immediately after that batch's `hooks.fire_batch` call
reached `manifest_write_batch_hook` -> `get_catalog_writer()` (both
resolved, logged at DEBUG) -> `_manifest_write_loop(...)`, the process
hung indefinitely (>200s, no further log output, no exception).

The batch in question is a CONTINUATION slice (chunk_index 100-199, no
position 0), which takes `append_manifest_chunks`'s code path inside
`_manifest_write_loop`'s per-doc loop (not `atomic_manifest_replace`).

## What's been ruled out

An isolated repro calling `HttpCatalogClient.append_manifest_chunks`
directly (no pipeline/upload machinery, no concurrent threads) after a
prior `atomic_manifest_replace` for the same doc completed in 0.01s —
no hang. So the endpoint itself is not unconditionally slow/broken;
whatever triggers the hang is specific to the concurrent, multi-threaded
pipeline context (extractor/chunker/uploader threads all live,
mid-resume) or to some connection/lock state left over from the FIRST
(interrupted) run.

## Status

Not blocking nexus-5xn3k.7 — the gate's `_reset_pipeline_buffer` helper
(a full `delete_pipeline_data` reset before the recovery run) avoids
this scenario entirely by design, and is the documented, deliberate
scope boundary (pipeline-buffer resume mechanics are out of scope for
the RUNFENCE fence gate). Filed so the observation is not lost;
whoever picks this up should start by reproducing WITHOUT test mocks
(a real multi-batch PDF, real MinerU/docling extraction) to rule out
an artifact of the PDFExtractor/PDFChunker class-level mock combined
with concurrent threads re-entering a patched attribute.

Context: nx

comments.text: ARC-CRITIC framing correction (2026-08-02, do not lose this): glzrn is availability/liveness debt, NOT a silent-success recreation — verified: the hang sits inside _manifest_write_loop BEFORE any completion-stamp code, so the doc stays visibly 'indexing' (loud + covered by the .6 indexing-age doctor axis), never silently promoted. NON-BLOCKING for the RUNFENCE arc close on that basis. BUT the precondition is NOT purely synthetic: pipeline_stages.py:840-846 wraps mark_failed + clear_orphan_wal in one boundary catch, so a transient failure of clear_orphan_wal ITSELF leaves WAL preserved on a failed row — a real, reachable path into this state. Never close this as cannot-happen; root-cause remains unconfirmed.

title: dt.py refusal footer wording can be arithmetically dishonest in a mixed flush-grain/incremental refusal batch
description:
Delta re-verification of nexus-5xn3k.6 (T2 nexus/5xn3k6-critique-2026-08-02, id
21355) after nexus-qo84l was fixed. The qo84l fix is correct (dt.py now catches
IndexRunVerifyRefused and buckets it into `failed`, batch survives). But it
interacts badly with the pre-existing S1 wording fix ("N of the M indexed above
had completion refused"):

_fence_complete() (doc_indexer.py:399-430, unchanged by the qo84l delta) calls
_record_complete_refusal(doc_id) BEFORE re-raising IndexRunVerifyRefused, by
explicit design ("both feed the SAME .6 summary consumer... Recording here
closes that gap"). So a document whose refusal takes the PROPAGATING path
(streaming/incremental, now correctly caught by dt.py's new except clause and
bucketed into `failed`, NOT `indexed`) is STILL added to the global
get_complete_refusals() list.

In a dt.py batch mixing (a) a small document refused via the non-propagating
flush-grain path (chunks>0 returned normally, counted in `indexed`) and (b) a
large document refused via the propagating incremental/streaming path (now
correctly excluded from `indexed`, landed in `failed` instead), the end-of-run
footer:

    f"  WARNING: {len(refused)} of the {indexed} indexed above had "
    f"completion refused..."

counts BOTH types in len(refused) but `indexed` only reflects type (a) — the
claim "N of the M indexed above" can be arithmetically false (N > M) or at
minimum silently includes a failed-bucket doc inside an "indexed above" claim.

Not covered by any test: TestDtIndexRefusalPropagation (the new qo84l test)
mocks nexus.doc_indexer.index_pdf directly, bypassing the real _fence_complete
body entirely, so _record_complete_refusal never fires in those tests and the
footer path is never reached. The pinned 2/1 wording test
(test_refused_subset_wording_is_not_hardcoded_to_one_of_one) only exercises the
homogeneous non-propagating-refusal-type case.

Note: index_repo_cmd's equivalent footer is NOT at risk -- index_repository's
per-file loop only processes code/markdown, which structurally cannot reach
_fence_complete's propagating path (confirmed by call-graph:
_index_pdf_incremental / pipeline_index_pdf are PDF-only). This is specific to
dt.py, which does process PDFs.

Fix options: (a) have the new `except IndexRunVerifyRefused` branch in dt.py
also remove/discount this doc_id from the refused-count shown in the footer
(the per-record failure line already names it via _index_run_refused_message,
so the aggregate footer should report only the REMAINING non-propagating
refusals to keep "of the M indexed above" true), or (b) reword the footer to
not claim a subset relationship at all, e.g. "N document(s) had completion
refused (see per-record failures above for any already counted as failed)".

Found during substantive-critic delta re-verification of nexus-5xn3k.6
(develop, same tree as qo84l). Full write-up: T2 nexus/5xn3k6-critique-2026-08-02
(id 21355) and this bead.
notes: DORMANCY ENDED 2026-08-02: engine-service-v0.1.62 deployed to cloud (edge /version=0.1.62 verified). Fence-aware routes now live in the pinned/cloud path, so the mixed flush-grain/incremental refusal batch this bug describes is REACHABLE in production, not just against a dev jar. Priority unchanged (P2, wording-honesty not data loss).

title: [gate] per-run build nonce as the artifact-identity discriminator for the smoke leg — the fence-route 404 discriminator dies when RUNFENCE ships in a pinned release
description:
From the x81ks code review (2026-08-02). The smoke leg's version check (release_version == GATE_STAMP) is vacuous by construction: the pinned release binary and the freshly-stamped dev jar bake the IDENTICAL version. Today the artifact discriminator is accidental — the RUNFENCE index-run routes 404 on the pinned v0.1.61 binary and 200 on the fresh jar (exactly what caught 4e96a live). That discrimination DIES the moment a pinned release carries the fence routes (imminent: v0.1.62), silently reverting the smoke leg to the vacuity class x81ks exists to kill — the third instance of assertion-passes-because-it-cannot-discriminate in one investigation (tmsnz, 4e96a, this).

Durable fix: stamp a PER-RUN NONCE at build-gate-jar time — e.g. build_ref=<git sha>+<run nonce> written into release.properties by scripts/build-gate-jar.sh (and the gate's own stamp step), exposed by VersionHandler (/version gains the field), asserted by the smoke leg as build_ref == the value THIS run stamped. Only the artifact built by this gate run can ever match a per-run nonce — robust against every future release. Engine half: VersionHandler + release.properties plumbing (batch with the next engine work); script half: build-gate-jar.sh + local-service-gate.sh assert. Until it lands, the gate carries an explicit comment naming step (d) as the interim discriminator with this bead as the revisit trigger (shipped with x81ks).

Cross-refs: nexus-x81ks (parent), nexus-4e96a (the short-circuit this discriminates against), review thread in T1.
close_reason: Shipped in fe2fcaa0 (develop). build_ref per-run nonce: stamped by build-gate-jar.sh + LSG step 2, served by /version only when non-blank (shape-identity preserved), smoke leg asserts served==stamped (jar mode) / ABSENT (native mode). Falsified live: wrong-nonce full-gate run failed loud naming 4e96a, real run 12/12. Dual-reviewed (0 Critical; Important + 2 Significant all fixed in same commit). Discriminator test TestSmokeLegDiscriminatorDoesNotOutliveItsPower green at floor (0,1,62).

title: doctor/rename-collection print 'restore the trashed document(s)' guidance but no CLI/MCP/REST surface exists to do it
description:
Found during substantive-critique of the nexus-e1k14 fix (doctor.py --collections-drift
TOMBSTONED-vs-ABSENT split), 2026-08-02.

Three operator-facing sites tell the operator to restore trashed documents before
proceeding, and all three are equally unactionable:

  - src/nexus/collection_rename.py:91 (rename_collection_data_plane, old TOMBSTONED guard)
  - src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py:295 (rename-collection CLI wrapper,
    same message)
  - src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/doctor.py:357 (collections-drift TOMBSTONED bucket,
    added by the nexus-e1k14 fix)

Verified end to end, not taken on inference:

  - `nx catalog --help` has no restore/untrash/undelete verb.
  - `grep -rn document_restore src/` returns zero hits — no Python surface (CLI or MCP)
    calls it anywhere.
  - `grep -rn documentRestore\|restoreDocument service/src/main/java` returns zero hits —
    no Java repository method or REST handler wraps it either.
  - The PG functions exist (document_trash / document_restore / purge_trash,
    catalog-003-soft-delete.xml, RDR-156 P3) but have NO caller anywhere in the
    codebase — trash and restore are both currently invisible to every operator
    surface (CLI, MCP, REST). There is no way to even TRASH a document through a
    documented path either, so the whole soft-delete lifecycle this text refers to
    is presently a DB-internal capability with no operator door in or out.

Impact: the nexus-e1k14 fix (correctly) stops printing the destructive supersede
recipe against a TOMBSTONED collection, replacing it with "restore the trashed
document(s) ... FIRST". That message is strictly safer than before (no destructive
command is dangled) but gives the operator no path to close the doctor FAIL --
inviting exactly the kind of ad hoc improvisation (hand-written UPDATE ... SET
deleted_at = NULL against production Postgres, or reaching for supersede anyway
out of frustration) the original bug's harm framing was about.

Fix shape: expose document_restore (and probably document_trash) through at least
one of {nx catalog CLI verb, MCP tool, documented direct-SQL incantation with the
correct WHERE/tenant scoping} so the guidance printed by all three sites above
points at something real. Until then, consider softening the three messages to
name the actual mechanism (or explicitly say none exists yet) rather than implying
one does.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
NEW EVIDENCE + A WORKING, MEASURED SOLUTION (2026-08-10). Filed here rather than as a new bead:
this bead already states the problem ("the lint scans request.session.items, so it only fires when
the offending file is co-collected — in practice only on the full develop CI run") and already
proposes the pre-push tripwire as an alternative. This comment supplies the two instances, the
implementation, and the non-vacuity evidence.

RECOMMEND BUMPING P3 -> P2 on the strength of the recurrence count below.

## Two more instances today (the count is now ~8)

Commits `127f2dbc` and `47c5a39a` each ran a targeted, path-scoped battery. Both looked green.
Both introduced offenders that surfaced only on the next whole-session run. The `_MODE_LINT_EXCLUDE`
set already documents roughly six prior entries that got in the same way. This is a repeating,
known-shape failure, not a one-off.

## What the census actually is, and why it is structurally vacuous when narrowed

`tests/test_mode_declarations_are_explicit.py:147` runs `_scan_offenders(request.session.items)`.
`session.items` is only ever what THIS pytest invocation collected, so the census is vacuous by
construction under standalone, `-k`, `-m lint`, or path-scoped selection. `tests/conftest.py`'s
`partial_session_view_reason` (`:352`) already recognises this and SKIPS rather than passing
vacuously — correct, but a skip in the authoring loop is still no signal in the authoring loop.

## What already exists (so this bead is not "nothing is wired")

The CI half is closed. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:608-696` runs a dedicated
`pytest (mode-declarations census)` job — `NX_CENSUS_ONLY_JOB=1 uv run pytest tests/ -q`, no
service jar, `NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=none`, `NX_SCENARIO_SKIP_BUDGET=999` — which skip-marks (never
deselects) everything outside `_CENSUS_ONLY_ALLOWED_MODULES` (`tests/conftest.py:510`) so
`session.items` stays the real corpus. Landed with nexus-vdti6, 2026-08-06.

**The gap this bead names is the LOCAL / PRE-PUSH loop.** That CI job catches an offender after
the push, on develop — which is precisely how `127f2dbc` and `47c5a39a` got in.

## The solution, implemented and measured

A collect-only probe running the identical `_scan_offenders(session.items)` at
`pytest_collection_finish`. It boots NO substrate (no PG, no engine jar, no model) because
collection never resolves fixtures, and it never enters the runtest phase at all.

Working code: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hal-hildebrand-git-nexus/e3ab8eee-f7e9-46d9-b5d5-c1dcd88ff76d/scratchpad/mode_lint_probe.py`
(scratchpad — ephemeral; the ask below is to land it as a committed artifact).
Technique recorded in T2 `nexus/mode-declaration-suite-fix-2026-08-10` [22170].

Measured today: **~40s wall. 12437 items / 4 offenders before the fix; 12438 items / 0 after.**

Note it is strictly CHEAPER than the existing CI job's shape: that job pays collection plus
per-item skip overhead across ~11.7k skip-marked items; the probe pays collection only. Worth
evaluating whether the CI job should adopt the same hook rather than keeping two mechanisms.

## Ask (supersedes this bead's original "candidate class-closer" sketch — the AST-grep leg is no
## longer needed; the probe gets the real census, not an approximation of it)

1. Land the probe as a first-class committed check, not a scratchpad artifact.
2. Wire it where it fires in the authoring loop: a pre-push hook or a fast CI job. This does NOT
   conflict with the repo's CI cost discipline — it is cheap precisely because it collects and
   boots nothing, so it is not an "expensive job" needing a path filter.
3. Generalize deliberately. **Checked 2026-08-10: `_SESSION_ITEMS_CENSUS_TEST_NODEIDS`
   (`tests/conftest.py:413-416`) currently holds exactly ONE nodeid, and
   `_CENSUS_ONLY_ALLOWED_MODULES` (`:510-512`) exactly one module — so there is no second
   `session.items` census today.** The generalization is therefore forward-looking, and the right
   shape is for the probe to READ those registries rather than hardcode `_scan_offenders`; any
   future sibling census then inherits pre-push coverage by registration, which is exactly what the
   registry comment at `:406-412` already asks future authors to do.
4. Non-vacuity is not optional: the probe must be demonstrated to go RED on a deliberately
   introduced offender. Today's 4-then-0 measurement IS that evidence — cite it in the
   implementation, and keep a committed regression that introduces a synthetic offender and asserts
   the probe's non-zero exit. A probe that only ever ran clean would be the same vacuous-pass class
   this whole family exists to eliminate (nexus-vdti6's framing).

Related: nexus-vdti6 (closed — the shard-blindness half and the CI census job), nexus-7i31i (open —
the census job's CI-wiring has no drift guard, the 4th vacuity vector), nexus-th15h (closed — the
exclusion sets had no liveness check), nexus-3znzn (open — sweep for tests that pin fail-open
behaviour), nexus-uoot1 (open — mechanize the no-silent-phase guarantee). Same family throughout: a
guarantee that exists but is not mechanically enforced where it would actually fire.

title: the write_many batch path in _manifest_write_loop never calls _sweep_superseded_vectors — only the per-doc fallback does, so most flush-grain writes stay unswept even after nexus-kgos1
design:
Found during code-review of 43b7932d (nexus-kgos1), diff 76a2f07c..HEAD.

_manifest_write_loop (mcp_infra.py:986) has two branches:
  1. The write_many batch fast-path (callable(cat.write_manifest_many)) —
     the code's own comment calls this the path "multi-doc batches (the
     flush-grain aggregate path)... go through ONE write_many POST when the
     writer supports it" (line 987-991). This is the PRIMARY path for
     ChunkBatcher-driven production writes.
  2. The per-doc fallback loop (404, missing capability, or continuation
     slices) — this is the ONLY place _sweep_superseded_vectors is called
     (mcp_infra.py:1113; grep confirms exactly one call site in the file).

nexus-kgos1 fixed the reader-routing bug so the per-doc path's sweep can
actually delete rows now. But branch 1 (write_many) never invoked the sweep
before this fix and still does not after it — nothing in the write_many
branch computes a `before` set or calls _sweep_superseded_vectors at all.

Net effect: for a modern engine (>= the version that added write_many, no
404 fallback triggered) writing flush-grain batches — the described common
case — a shrink-reindex's superseded T3 rows are STILL never cleaned up
post-kgos1. The sweep only activates for the minority path: 404 fallback,
writer lacking write_manifest_many, or an all-continuation batch.

This doesn't make kgos1 wrong (the per-doc path genuinely was a total
no-op before, now it isn't), but it means the practical blast radius / real
world benefit of "the sweep now deletes rows in production" is narrower
than it may read, and conversely the corpus-wide orphan problem
(nexus-39upx) is only partially remediated by this fix for engines that
exercise write_many normally.

Recommend: either (a) add an equivalent before/after sweep to the
write_many branch (batched _sweep_superseded_vectors call per doc, or a
single batched reverse-lookup across all dropped chashes in the write_many
batch), or (b) explicitly document that write_many-eligible batches are
out of scope for the sweep and file the corpus-wide catch-up sweep
(referenced in nexus-flkdc) as the actual remediation path for those.
close_reason: Fixed at cb5b6000: the write_many fast branch sweeps via _sweep_superseded_vectors_many (batch-wide live union, failure-path prior-manifest protection). Dual-reviewed.

title: consider a single-pass state-machine rewrite of _normalize_mineru_latex — third distinct patch to the same two-pass regex subsystem (repo directive: root-cause after 3+ patches)
description:
Found during substantive-critique of 3a7bc6ac (nexus-cfy5k).

Chronology of patches to src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py's _normalize_mineru_latex /
normalize_latex_spacing subsystem:
  1. closes #1049 (55691515, 217072cc, 2026-06-03) -- spacing normalization
     itself.
  2. 57a392ff (nexus-gtltb) -- $$ display-block pass left delimiters in
     place, desyncing the inline pass's [^$] bracket matching; PROSE between
     formulas got whitespace-stripped instead of formulas.
  3. 3a7bc6ac (nexus-cfy5k, this diff) -- escaped currency \$ was treated as
     a real delimiter for the same reason: neither pass honours backslash
     escaping, so a PAIR of \$ bracketed prose as an inline formula.

Both (2) and (3) are the SAME species of bug: the two-pass
withdraw-then-scan-then-restore regex design treats "everything between two
un-withdrawn $ characters" as math, and each fix has been "add one more
category of $ that must be withdrawn first" (display blocks in the original
design, then \text{...}, now \$). That is an open-ended category, not a
closed one. Plausible NEXT triggers, unaddressed by cfy5k's fix, using the
same mechanism (any construct that puts two un-delimiter $ characters on one
page without an intervening real formula):
  - `$` inside fenced or inline code (shell variables like $HOME, $1, awk
    field refs) -- MinerU passes code blocks through largely verbatim and
    has no reason to escape a shell $.
  - `$` in markdown tables (price columns/rows) that MinerU does NOT escape
    (the \$ escaping cfy5k fixes appears to be MinerU's OWN convention for
    prose currency -- there is no evidence it is applied uniformly inside
    table cells, which MinerU renders through a different code path).
  - `\$$` / `$$\$` boundary collisions where an escaped dollar sits directly
    adjacent to a real display delimiter.

Repo directive (AGENTS.md via ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md): "root-cause after 3+
patches [to the] same subsystem." This is the third.

RECOMMENDATION TO EVALUATE (not prescribing the outcome): replace the
withdraw/restore regex chain with a single left-to-right scan over the
markdown string that tracks explicit state (plain text / backslash-escape /
fenced-code / inline-code / display-math / inline-math / \text{} group) and
emits normalized output in one pass. This is the class of design that
structurally CANNOT desync the way both gtltb and cfy5k did, because there is
no second pass to desync against and no growing withdraw-first allowlist to
maintain. Scope is narrow (MinerU's specific markdown dialect, not general
CommonMark), so this is more likely a ~100-150 line function than a
general-purpose parser -- evaluate against the corpus of live MinerU output
before committing to it; if the actual trigger surface turns out to be just
{display, text, escaped-$} and nothing else ever reproduces, the two-pass
approach may be adequate and this bead should be closed as unwarranted.

Also relevant to nexus-gtltb's closure bar: closing gtltb after only two
known triggers risks a fourth discovery post-close reopening the same
worklist a third time (see nexus-cfy5k's BLOCKS link). Consider requiring a
corpus-wide $ audit (not just the two known trigger shapes) before gtltb
closes, on top of the rescan cfy5k already blocks it for.

title: sweep's reader=None fallback silently reproduces the exact kgos1 defect class at any call site that omits reader= — already exercised, silently, by tests/catalog/test_manifest_write_many.py
description:
Found during substantive-critique of 43b7932d (nexus-kgos1).

_manifest_write_loop / _sweep_superseded_vectors (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:923,
986) both default reader=None and fall back with
    _reader = reader if reader is not None else cat
The ONLY production call site (manifest_write_batch_hook, mcp_infra.py:898)
always threads reader=_gate, so production is fixed. But the fallback means
ANY caller that omits reader= gets the pre-fix behaviour back: reads routed
through whatever `cat` is, which for the real _ServiceCatalogWriter raises
AttributeError on both get_chunk_chashes and docs_for_chashes -- the exact
kgos1 mechanism, now logged (superseded_sweep_before_read_failed) instead of
fully silent, but still a permanent no-op for that call site.

This is not hypothetical: tests/catalog/test_manifest_write_many.py's
TestManifestWriteLoopBatching class calls _manifest_write_loop(cat, by_doc)
with NO reader kwarg, using a plain `_FakeCat` test double that has no
get_chunk_chashes/docs_for_chashes methods at all. Every one of those tests
whose by_doc includes position-0 chunks (most of them) walks into the sweep's
_before read, hits a real AttributeError against _FakeCat, gets caught, and
silently no-ops the sweep for the duration of that test -- the tests only
assert on many_calls/replace_calls/resync_calls, so this doesn't fail them,
but it means that file provides ZERO coverage of the reader-threading fix
kgos1 just landed, despite exercising the same code path the fix touched.

kgos1's own commit message diagnosed this exact pattern in the OLD test
suite ("tests below the layer that fails, proving the function not the
feature") and added test_superseded_vector_sweep.py::
test_sweep_fires_through_the_real_write_only_proxy specifically to close it
for _sweep_superseded_vectors' direct callers. The reader=None default
reopens the identical blind spot one call site removed: nothing prevents a
FUTURE _manifest_write_loop caller (or a refactor of this one) from omitting
reader= and silently reintroducing the no-op sweep, and the existing
test_manifest_write_many.py suite would not catch it because it already
exercises that exact (currently harmless, because unasserted) fallback path.

Recommend: drop the reader=None default (require the caller to pass it
explicitly, raising TypeError on omission) so a missing wire-up fails loudly
at call time instead of degrading to a silent-per-doc no-op; or add an
explicit assertion in test_manifest_write_many.py's _FakeCat that
get_chunk_chashes/docs_for_chashes are never called on it (proving the
fallback path is dead in that suite, not merely unexercised-and-untested).
close_reason: Fixed in 0cf75c78: reader is now keyword-only and REQUIRED on both _manifest_write_loop and _sweep_superseded_vectors, so a missing wire-up raises TypeError at the call instead of degrading to a silent no-op sweep. Pinned by test_reader_is_required_not_defaulted. The two doubles in tests/catalog/test_manifest_write_many.py now carry get_chunk_chashes/docs_for_chashes explicitly, so that file's sweep provably no-ops on an empty before rather than by accident on AttributeError.

title: union guard's docs_for_chashes read has a TOCTOU race against concurrent manifest writes sharing a chash — the newly-activated sweep can delete a T3 row a different in-flight document is about to reference
description:
Found during substantive-critique of 3a7bc6ac/43b7932d (nexus-cfy5k, nexus-kgos1).

_sweep_superseded_vectors (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:923) queries
_reader.docs_for_chashes(dropped) to decide whether a chash this document no
longer references is truly orphaned (no other document's manifest points to
it) before deleting the T3 row. That reverse lookup is a live read against
the catalog's current document_chunks state at the moment it runs — it has no
isolation from a DIFFERENT document's indexing that is concurrently in flight.

RACE: document A drops chash H in a shrink-reindex. Document B, indexing
concurrently, writes a chunk with content that happens to hash to the SAME H
(duplicate/boilerplate text — plausible in an academic-paper corpus: license
blocks, copyright notices, common citation fragments) into T3, but has not
yet reached manifest_write_batch_hook's atomic_manifest_replace /
append_manifest_chunks call for its own doc_id (T3 write and manifest write
are two separate stores with no cross-store transaction). If A's
docs_for_chashes(H) lands in that window, it sees zero references, decides H
is orphaned, and hard-deletes the T3 row — which B's manifest is about to
point to once B's write lands. Net effect: B's document ends up with a
manifest row referencing a chash with no T3 vector, permanently unsearchable
for that chunk, with no error surfaced anywhere (this is the EXACT
"catalog looks clean, T3 is wrong" failure class nexus-39upx exists to fix,
reintroduced through a different door).

This is a LATENT gap in the original nexus-39upx design (76a2f07c) — it could
not fire before because the sweep never executed (nexus-kgos1). Landing
kgos1 activates a hard-delete path against live production T3 data for the
first time ever, and the commit message's safety argument ("the union guard
... over-retains and never over-deletes, so this is safe to land ahead")
only accounts for the KNOWN collection-blindness gap (nexus-flkdc), not this
concurrency gap. The two are independent: flkdc is about scope-of-lookup
(global vs per-collection), this is about time-of-check-to-time-of-use.

No test in tests/test_superseded_vector_sweep.py or
tests/catalog/test_manifest_write_many.py exercises concurrent writers.

Mitigation directions (not prescribing): a short quarantine/grace-period
before a chash is eligible for deletion (skip if the T3 row's write
timestamp is within N minutes), or scope the delete to chashes that have
been absent from ALL manifests for two consecutive sweep passes, or a
per-chash advisory lock during the manifest-replace + sweep sequence.

Severity P2, not P1: does not block landing 43b7932d — the sweep being a
permanent no-op (nexus-39upx) is a strictly worse status quo than a sweep
with a narrow, likely-rare race window. Track and evaluate before the
corpus-wide catch-up sweep (39upx/flkdc remediation) runs at scale, where
concurrent multi-document indexing is most likely.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: nexus-55l58 forensics (2026-08-04): fcx2s is FALSIFIED as the producer of the 188 dangling manifest rows — within each damaged doc, surviving old-only chashes have identical guard-visible reference status to the missing ones (a set-based sweep cannot delete 15 and keep 34), and missing positions form contiguous runs while chash-set differences are position-agnostic. The 188 are partial-population at ingest (nexus-tp8yk), not sweep deletions. The TOCTOU window itself remains real and this bead stays open on its own merits.

title: the expectations ledger's exact-duplicate filter silently collapses N same-type dispatches declared in the same second, reporting them as undeclared — a FALSE positive on the ledger's core signal
description:
Found by probe while declaring three conexus:debugger dispatches in one turn.

MEASURED (repo copy, tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh)
  3 x expectations_expect <sid> conexus:debugger background   -> ROWS expect=1
  same, spaced 1 second apart                                 -> ROWS expect=2
  same, with distinct dispatch_ids                            -> ROWS expect=3
The ledger FILE contains all three rows in every case (verified with od -c); the
collapse is in the reader, not the writer.

MECHANISM
tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh:419
    seen[$0]++ { next }                     # 3h0u6 exact-duplicate rows
The row is  <ts>\tEXPECT\t<name>\t<mode>[\t<dispatch_id>]  and _expectations_ts is
SECOND-granularity. Parallel dispatches — the normal case, since concurrent agents
go out in one message — therefore produce BYTE-IDENTICAL rows and all but one are
dropped before the tally.

The guard is deliberate and its stated reason is sound (a re-registered dispatch
must not inflate the credit pool and mask an undeclared start). It simply cannot
distinguish "the hook registered the same dispatch twice" from "the orchestrator
dispatched three agents of one type in the same second". dispatch_id is exactly the
field that settles it — see :425.

CONSEQUENCE
The AGENT walk consumes one credit per start (:337 credit[t]--), so with expect
collapsed to 1 and 3 starts, 2 are printed as UNDECLARED. Observed live this
session: 5 declared dispatches, ROWS expect=3, CLASSIFIED undeclared=2. Following
the documented convention produces a false compliance failure, in the one tool whose
entire purpose is measuring that compliance. That is the nexus-nu7fo class again:
a signal that cannot be made true by doing the right thing.

THE HOOK IS NOT AFFECTED
conexus/hooks/scripts/agent-dispatch-expect.sh:122 already passes "$DISPATCH_ID",
so the mechanized path (nexus-qc4p1) is correct. Only the HAND-WRITTEN path is
broken — and that is the live path, because the hook loads from the pinned release
tag and is inert until the next plugin release.

FIX, cheapest first
  a) CLAUDE.md and conexus/skills/orchestration/SKILL.md document the 3-arg form
     `expectations_expect "$SESSION_ID" <subagent-type> background`. Document the
     4-arg form with a dispatch_id as the REQUIRED form for hand-written rows.
  b) Better: make the dedupe key (dispatch_id) rather than the whole row when a
     dispatch_id is absent — i.e. only collapse exact duplicates that CARRY the
     same dispatch_id, and let dispatch_id-less rows count individually. That
     restores the documented "N EXPECT rows of a type against N STARTs" contract
     without weakening the re-registration guard, which only ever fires on rows
     that HAVE a dispatch_id anyway (:425 is already dispatch_id-gated).
  c) Or make _expectations_ts sub-second, which fixes the symptom and not the class.

(b) looks correct: :425's re-registration dedupe is already conditioned on
$5 != "", so :419's whole-row filter is doing work only for rows the other guard
deliberately declines to touch.

Both copies must stay byte-identical (tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py):
edit tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh and copy to conexus/, never the reverse.

title: HttpUtil.sendTypedDbError maps only SQLSTATE 23*, so PG's 22021 NUL rejection falls through as an opaque 500 instead of a typed 4xx
description:
Split out of the page_text NUL bead so the diagnosability fix is not lost when the
sanitization fix lands.

service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/HttpUtil.java:76-87 matches only
SQLSTATE `23*` (integrity violations). Postgres rejects NUL in a `text` value with
SQLSTATE 22021, which therefore falls through to the generic path at HttpUtil.java:185
and is emitted as an opaque 500 at http/PipelineHandler.java:104.

CONSEQUENCE
A caller-data problem is reported as a server fault. The client's retry policy keys on
status (500 is correctly not retried, but 502/503/504 are), so the classification also
drives behaviour, not just the log line. Diagnosing the underlying cause took a full
differential scan across the corpus because the response carried nothing.

FIX
Map 22021 (and the adjacent 22* data-exception family, at least 22P05) in
sendTypedDbError to a typed 4xx naming the offending field. Engine-side, so it rides
the engine-service lifecycle.

Even after sanitization lands this is worth fixing: sanitization removes the known
trigger, and the mapping is what makes the NEXT unknown one legible.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Closed at the (0,1,61) floor bump (develop 418fd18e): engine fix shipped in engine-service-v0.1.61, deployed ~2026-08-02T00:15Z, functionally gated green (relay T2 [21347]), gate called by Hal.

title: the glued-prose detector false-positives on LaTeX \phantom{xxxx...} runs, so the gtltb remediation gate can never read clean
description:
The corruption signature used throughout the nexus-gtltb arc is

    regex [A-Za-z]{25,}  AND  the match contains <= 2 uppercase characters

The <=2-capitals discriminator was added to separate glued prose from camelCase and
minified JS, and it does that well. It does not exclude single-character runs.

LaTeX \phantom{xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx} inside a legitimate $$\begin{array}...$$
block is a 25+ character all-lowercase run and matches. Measured: the freshly and
CORRECTLY re-indexed Zoology document (tumbler 1.14.25) reports 3 glued rows, and all
3 are this construct.

CONSEQUENCE
Any remediation gate asserting "glued == 0" will never pass on formula-bearing
documents, so a real residual cannot be distinguished from this artifact — which is
precisely the discrimination the metric exists to provide.

FIX
Exclude runs composed of a single repeated character (and consider excluding matches
occurring inside a $$...$$ span) from the signature. Then re-derive the arc's counts:
every glue number recorded so far carries this false-positive component.

title: the union guard's reverse lookup is collection-blind — docs_for_chashes is global while the delete is collection-scoped, so a duplicate document in another physical collection pins orphans permanently
description:
Split out of nexus-kgos1 so it is not lost when that bead's primary fix lands.

mcp_infra.py:955-957 keeps any chash referenced by a document other than doc_id, and
the ordering is correct (_before read pre-replace, refs read post-replace). The union
guard's SHAPE is right and is falsified by its dedicated test.

The defect is scope: docs_for_chashes is GLOBAL while the delete is scoped to a single
physical collection. A document in a different physical collection therefore pins rows
in this one, and they can never be swept.

LIVE PROOF
knowledge__vector-search__voyage-context-3__v1, sweeping tumbler 1.14.11 (HRNN):
  T3 rows not in this manifest   307
     referenced by NOTHING       146   <- a working sweep deletes these
     referenced by 1.14.19       161   <- kept, and permanently unsweepable

Tumbler 1.14.19 is the SAME PAPER re-registered from
/Users/hal.hildebrand/Downloads/2606.03225v1.pdf under the title "2606.03225v1", with
physical_collection = docs__default__voyage-context-3__v1 — not the collection being
swept.

So even after nexus-kgos1 lands, 161 of those 307 rows survive.

TWO SEPARABLE THINGS
  a) scope the reverse lookup to the collection being swept, AND
  b) the duplicate-document problem itself (same paper registered twice, in two
     physical collections, under two titles) needs its own resolution — a
     cross-collection duplicate audit. Deleting 1.14.19 without that audit would be
     guessing.

title: a third of the catalog is debris: 7,142 documents in 29 collections that do not exist in T3, 5,728 registered-never-populated, 1,798 rooted in deleted worktrees
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 by a live-corpus audit (all 21,686 enumerable documents, 80
referenced collections). Not urgent, but it is a third of the catalog and it
distorts every measurement taken from it.

MEASURED:

 - 12,875 of 21,686 documents (59%) have an EMPTY MANIFEST. Of those:
     7,142 live in 29 collections that DO NOT EXIST in T3 — verified three ways
       (absent from list_collections, collection_exists_raw False, count 0).
       Largest: code__1-32 (3,840 docs, owner root /Users/hal.hildebrand/git —
       the whole git dir), code__1-60 (907), docs__1-48 (822), docs__1-59 (822),
       code__1-3 (588), docs__1-50 (95). Most owner roots are benchmark temp
       dirs like /private/var/folders/.../bench-index-XXXX/benchidx-07041504-w2.
     5,728 are chunk_count=0 AND empty manifest — registered, never populated.
       Honest, but 26% of the catalog.
         5 are DISHONEST: chunk_count > 0 with an empty manifest —
       1.10.4386 (rdr-182, claims 50) and 1.11.227/228/229/230 (claim 1 each).

 - 1,798 documents in rdr__1-1 have source_uri inside .claude/worktrees/, across
   11 distinct ephemeral worktree directories that no longer exist. rdr__1-1
   holds 4,307 docs of which 4,003 have no manifest.

 - 4,108 T3 chunks appear in NO manifest (the reverse direction): code__1-1
   2,807/32,285 (8.7%), code__arcaneum 412/2,363 (17%), knowledge__knowledge
   242/1,451 (17%), docs__1-1 340/4,810, rdr__1-20 151/977.

 - 60 dangling manifest rows across 5 documents, independently confirmed by the
   server's own manifest_orphans(dim=1024) returning 60. Notably 1.14.2 is THIS
   REPO'S OWN FIXTURE — tests/fixtures/tc-sql.pdf, manifest of 56, chunk_count
   claiming 56, ZERO chunks present. That is the nexus-5xn3k class sitting in
   our test data.

COUNTING CAVEAT worth preserving, because it would generate false positives for
anyone repeating this: manifest ROWS legitimately exceed UNIQUE chashes —
identical chunk text collapses to one T3 row by design (CLAUDE.md catalog/T3
split). Zoology is 400 rows / 394 unique / 394 present. Comparing rows to T3
would falsely report 6 missing; corpus-wide that gap is 19,060 rows.

INFERRED, not measured: the dead collections and worktree-rooted registrations
look like accumulated debris from benchmark runs and from indexing inside
worktrees, rather than an active corruption mechanism — the owner roots are temp
and worktree paths. The code path that leaves them behind was not traced.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: every corpus-level measurement is computed over
a catalog where a third of the entries point at nothing. Coverage percentages,
GC alive-sets, drift counts and doctor checks all inherit that. And it interacts
with nexus-hg4er (487 documents the catalog cannot even enumerate) — the true
denominator is unknown in both directions.

DO NOT bulk-delete on the strength of this bead. 1.14.2 is a real fixture whose
chunks went missing (a defect to fix, not debris to sweep), and the 5 dishonest
chunk_count docs need diagnosis before removal. Scope a cleanup only after
nexus-hg4er explains the enumeration gap.

RELATED: nexus-hg4er, nexus-5xn3k (failed index poisons a document),
nexus-jqrtp (gc alive-set), nexus-e1k14 (doctor prints a destructive recipe
against restorable data).
close_reason: salvage-class per clean-slate directive T2 [21548]; the 2026-08-06 execution already did the work (grooming T2 [21595])

title: MinerU formula-PDF text length drifted 60135 -> 59217 with no version change — the locked-exact test caught it, cause not yet isolated
description:
FOUND 2026-08-01 by the 7.0.0 dry run's integration gate.

    tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py::TestFormulaPreservationOnRealPdf
      ::test_mineru_path_preserves_formulas
    AssertionError: extracted text is 59217 chars; locked at 60135. Length drift
    indicates partial extraction, encoding shift, or whitespace handling change.

THE TEST IS WORKING AS DESIGNED - do not "fix" it by re-locking without a cause.
Its docstring (nexus-2fyb, code-review round 2) is explicit that every assertion
is exact BECAUSE inequalities were the original bug shape: "meta_count > 0
shipped formula_count=0 silently; even meta_count >= 5 would pass if MinerU
regressed from 44 to 5, dropping 39 formulas invisibly... The test fails loudly
on ANY drift; a human reviews and either updates the constants (legit upgrade) or
files a bug (regression)." This bead is that review being started, not skipped.

WHAT IS NOT THE CAUSE, checked:
  - extraction_method still "mineru", page_count still 33, and formula_count
    still 44 - the failure is at the LENGTH assert (line 493), which runs AFTER
    those three, so all of them passed. No formulas were lost.
  - MinerU version did not move: uv.lock pins 3.1.11 (entry added 2026-03-31,
    479b3c2e) and 3.1.11 is what is installed. The constant was locked
    2026-05-05 (de5fa429).
  So: same library version, same page count, same formula count, 918 fewer
  characters (-1.5%). That signature is whitespace/encoding, not truncation.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis: MinerU's MODEL WEIGHTS are not
pinned. The test's own docstring notes the first invocation downloads ~2-3 GB
into ~/.cache/huggingface. Those weights carry no version in uv.lock, so an
upstream model update changes extraction output while every pinned dependency
stays identical - which is exactly the observed shape. If that is confirmed, this
is the reproducibility cost of an unpinned upstream artifact and belongs with
nexus-go5ou (the cross-encoder's unpinned HuggingFace fetch), which is the same
class one model over.

NOT RULED OUT: 17 commits touched src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py since the constant
was locked, including an RDR-148 arc (per-page timeout, RLIMIT_AS ceiling,
degrade-to-docling) and the nexus-c7odl/1qdb9 on-demand lifecycle work. A
whitespace-affecting change in our own code is entirely plausible and has not
been excluded. Bisecting the extractor against the fixture would settle it.

HOW TO SETTLE IT, cheapest first:
  1. Diff the actual extracted text against the expectation rather than the
     length alone - 918 chars is small enough to characterise (leading/trailing
     whitespace per page? a stripped header? changed newline handling?). The
     shape of the diff names the cause faster than bisection.
  2. If it is whitespace-only and semantically identical, the correct outcome is
     to re-lock WITH the diff recorded in the commit - the test's own protocol.
  3. If content is missing, it is a regression and the constant must NOT move.

DO NOT re-lock on the basis of "the test is annoying". The whole reason this
assertion is exact is that the previous shape hid a 39-formula loss.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: drift root-caused and re-locked with cause recorded: tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py:428 comment "60135 -> 59573 (nexus-gtltb). 60135 was the RAW pre-normalizer length" — the bead's own protocol (review then re-lock with diff) was followed

title: audit the verbs retired by the SQLite removal — which need an engine port, which are genuinely obsolete
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 alongside nexus-vl8lk, and deliberately separated from it.

The SQLite retirement (RDR-158 P3/P4) left two populations. nexus-vl8lk covers
the dangerous one: doctor checks stubbed to a SILENT PASS. This bead covers the
honest one: verbs retired to a LOUD ERROR.

  nx catalog init                     commands/catalog.py:286
  nx catalog setup                    commands/catalog.py:299
  nx taxonomy backfill-source-collection  commands/taxonomy_cmd.py:2558
  nx aspects gc                       commands/aspects.py:120
  nx aspects gc-fixtures              commands/aspects.py:153
  nx aspects backfill-source-uri      commands/aspects.py:184
  nx aspects gc-pre-rdr096            commands/aspects.py:214

These CANNOT mislead a gate — they refuse and explain why, which is the correct
shape for a capability that no longer has a substrate. So this is not a
correctness bug and is not urgent.

IT IS STILL A CAPABILITY QUESTION. `nx aspects gc` was garbage collection; its
retirement note says the orphan sweep ATTACHed the local SQLite file. The
underlying need (orphaned aspect rows accumulate) does not disappear because the
implementation's substrate did. Same shape for backfill-source-uri, which
repaired a real data defect.

THE AUDIT: for each verb above, decide exactly one of
  (a) PORT - the need is live and the engine can answer it; file the port;
  (b) OBSOLETE - the need died with the substrate (e.g. a fixture-cleanup verb
      for fixtures that no longer exist); then DELETE the verb rather than
      keeping a retired stub in --help forever;
  (c) SUPERSEDED - something else already covers it; name what, in the retirement
      message, so an operator who hits the error is told where to go instead.

Today every one of them says only "retired". None says what replaced it, and (c)
is cheap and useful even where (a) is not affordable.

NOTE ON SCOPE: at least one of these is load-bearing in a release gate right now
- tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh calls the retired `nx catalog setup` and swallows
its error with `|| true`. That specific removal is tracked on nexus-vl8lk since
it pairs with the stubbed check it was feeding.

title: live cloud taxonomy has 50/986 topics with projection assignments but no topic_links row
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 by the 7.0.0 release dry run. Surfaced only because the
release-sandbox smoke gate was fixed to stop swallowing doctor failures
(b3fa96bf) — before that this had been reported inside a gate that exited 0.

    nx doctor --check-taxonomy
    X topic_links drift: 50/986 topic(s) have projection assignments but no
      topic_links row.
      - topic 1097: (unlabelled id=1097)
      - topic 1091: (unlabelled id=1091)
      ... 48 more, all unlabelled ids
    Fix: re-run 'nx taxonomy project --backfill --persist' to rebuild the
    materialized view.

SCOPE — service mode, so this is the SHARED CLOUD taxonomy, not one sandbox's
local state. The sandbox reads the same api.conexus-nexus.com catalog every cloud
user does, so any of them running nx doctor --check-taxonomy sees this.

5% of topics affected. Every one listed renders as '(unlabelled id=N)', which is
itself a signal worth chasing: it suggests these rows lost their label alongside
their topic_links row rather than being ordinary topics that merely missed a
projection pass.

THE DOCUMENTED FIX IS A REBUILD, and that is the question this bead exists to
ask rather than answer: 'nx taxonomy project --backfill --persist' rebuilds the
materialized view, but running it does not explain HOW the drift arose, and a
rebuild that silently re-diverges next week is the same bug with a longer period.
Establish the cause before or alongside the rebuild.

NOT YET INVESTIGATED, stated so nobody reads this as diagnosed: whether the drift
is a one-off from a known incident (a partial projection run, an interrupted
taxonomy pass, a migration) or an ongoing write-path hole. The 5%-and-all-
unlabelled shape favours a discrete event, but that is a guess.

DECISION NEEDED: does a green nx doctor --check-taxonomy gate the release? The
smoke arm now exits non-zero on it, so as of b3fa96bf it DOES, mechanically. If
that is not intended, the gate should say so explicitly rather than the exit code
being decided by which check happens to be listed.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: premise retracted in-bead (stale local SQLite, zero cloud rows); doctor verdict now service-scoped with local census demoted to note (doctor.py:1976-2010; commits 1b5b62750, d0e9173e7) so the gate no longer blocks on the relic

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RETRACTION OF THIS BEAD'S SCOPE — the title and description are WRONG and must not be acted on as written.

I filed this asserting the drift is in the SHARED CLOUD taxonomy and that "any cloud user running nx doctor --check-taxonomy sees this". Both claims are false. Measured by a dispatched investigation, and I have re-verified the decisive fact myself.

nx doctor --check-taxonomy HAS NO SERVICE-MODE BRANCH. _run_check_taxonomy (src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:1926) calls default_db_path() and opens it via _t2_diagnostic_connect (doctor.py:18) as sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro"). On this box that is ~/.config/nexus/memory.db, 248 MB — the FROZEN SQLITE MIGRATION SOURCE. is_local_mode() is False and service_url is https://api.conexus-nexus.com; the check consults neither.

Evidence the rows are not in the cloud:
 - the doctor output reproduces byte-for-byte off that SQLite file (DRIFT COUNT 50, PROJECTION TOTAL 986, same 10 sample ids in order);
 - the cloud has 403 topics; ZERO of the 50 ids exist there — get_topic_by_id returned None for 1062, 1097, 1671, 1676 individually, not merely absent from a bulk list;
 - the local/cloud topic-id intersection is 157, none of them in the 50.

So this is stale local state in a file that is, by design, a read-only migration source. It is not production data and no cloud user is affected.

WHAT THE 50 ACTUALLY ARE. They have no `topics` row at all — the table holds ids 3012-4275 and every one of the 50 is below that floor. They are orphaned topic_ids left by a taxonomy rebuild on 2026-05-13 that restarted the id sequence at 3012 without cascading deletes to topic_assignments or topic_links. 562 topic_ids are orphaned in total; the 50 are just the subset the check's EXISTS guard surfaces (473 others are equally orphaned but happen to appear in topic_links, and 11 live ids are unlinked). Their assignment timestamps stop dead at 2026-05-12 while the table runs to 2026-07-01. They are unlabelled because the LEFT JOIN finds no row — topics.label is TEXT NOT NULL, so a null label is impossible by schema.

The real defect this exposes is filed separately: a doctor check that diagnoses the frozen migration source while the operator runs against the service.

This bead should be closed or re-scoped to the orphan-cleanup question for the local file, if that is even worth doing on a substrate scheduled for deletion.

title: release-sandbox shakedown arm swallows doctor failures with an explicit || true — worse than the smoke arm that was just fixed
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 by the 7.0.0 release dry run, while fixing the sibling defect in
the smoke arm (commit b3fa96bf).

tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:374, the shakedown arm:

    for check in --check-schema --check-plan-library --check-taxonomy; do
        echo "  $check:"
        nx doctor "$check" 2>&1 | tail -5 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
    done

The explicit || true means this arm does not merely fail to PROPAGATE a failure,
it does not DETECT one. The smoke arm at least printed [FAIL]; this prints five
lines of tail and moves on. Two further losses stack on top: tail -5 can truncate
the failure message itself, and with set -o pipefail the || true is what
specifically defeats the status the pipeline would otherwise carry.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY THE SAME FIX. shakedown is an ensemble walk — eleven
numbered stages exercising every nx surface in sequence. Exiting on the first
doctor failure would abandon the remaining stages, which is the wrong trade for a
walk whose value is breadth. It wants a collect-and-summarise at the end, the way
the smoke arm now does, but spanning all stages rather than just this loop.

WORTH NOTING WHILE IN THERE: the same script already treats one check as a
blocker on purpose — :380 'RDR-101 Phase 6: collections-drift is a release
blocker' — so the arm is not uniformly advisory. Whatever shape is chosen should
make the distinction explicit rather than leaving it to whether a given line
happens to carry || true.

SCOPE: shakedown only. The smoke arm is fixed and verified (exits 1, names the
failing checks).
close_reason: superseded: fixed by fe6452a4: release-sandbox doctor step fail-capable (grooming 2026-08-07, T2 [21595], Hal-approved batch)

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Shakedown-playbook drafting detail (T2 [21394] §S6): the swallowing is not confined to the doctor loop this bead was filed on — of the release-sandbox shakedown arm's 11 steps, only steps 5 and 11 can exit non-zero; all four indexing steps end in '|| true'. Until fixed the arm is a state-builder, not a gate; nexus-6xkdu (MinerU coverage) DEPENDS on this arm being a real gate and the two are often conflated.

title: nx doctor tumbler-drift check does one full scan per owner — 65 owners exceeded 2 minutes on a live install
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 while verifying the nexus-k5sdi fix against a live catalog.

_check_next_seq_drift (health.py) loops every owner and calls _highest_child_seq
per owner, each of which scans catalog_documents for that prefix. On the live
install (65 owners, service mode against api.conexus-nexus.com) a script doing
exactly what the check does EXCEEDED A 2-MINUTE TIMEOUT and had to be killed.
Scoped to 2 owners it returned in seconds, so the cost is per-owner and linear.

CONSEQUENCE: nx doctor may hang or take minutes on any populated install. That is
a diagnostic command — the one thing a user runs when something is already wrong,
and the one place a multi-minute stall reads as "doctor is broken too".

NOT YET MEASURED, state it rather than guess: whether the full nx doctor run
actually exceeds a user-visible threshold, since the check may run concurrently
with others or the reader may warm a cache. The 2-minute figure is for an
isolated reproduction of this check's work, not for nx doctor end to end. Measure
before choosing a fix.

CANDIDATE FIXES:
 (a) ask the engine for MAX(child seq) GROUPED BY owner prefix in ONE query
     instead of N — CatalogRepository.highestChildSeq already computes exactly
     this per prefix (:1153) and the group-by form is a small addition;
 (b) have list_owners return the high-water mark alongside next_seq, so the
     check needs no second round trip at all — arguably the right shape, since
     the pair is only ever meaningful together;
 (c) bound the check (sample, or only owners written recently) — cheapest, but
     turns a complete audit into a partial one, which is the wrong trade for a
     check whose whole point is knowing the blast radius.

(b) is preferred: nexus-0ehwe item 3 already added next_seq to the owner
projection for exactly this check, so extending that projection is consistent
with how the observability was built rather than a new mechanism.

RELATED: nexus-k5sdi (the predicate off-by-one in the same check, fixed).
nexus-0ehwe item 5 (the sweep) will want the same grouped query.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: per-owner scan replaced by ONE corpus pass _highest_child_seqs (health.py:5104-5119, comment cites 65 owners x 218s ohxzu measurement)

title: every rename now leaves a retired row in the catalog registry, and list_collections() has no live-only view — consumers that don't branch on superseded_by see a collection that isn't there
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 by the 7.0.0 dry run's integration gate. A test asserting the OLD contract went red; investigating why surfaced the question.

THE CHANGE. nexus-cecqy / nexus-g8z8n (commit 1d854b7a, 2026-07-31 09:22) made renameCollection RETIRE the old name instead of DELETING it — correctly, because deleting threw away the provenance the revive path needs to distinguish 'retired by this very rename' from 'an unrelated collection sharing the name'. The old row now survives carrying superseded_by/superseded_at.

THE CONSEQUENCE NOBODY SIZED. Before this change, a retired row in catalog_collections could ONLY come from an explicit /collections/supersede. Now EVERY rename produces one. The population of retired rows just went from rare-and-deliberate to routine.

AND THERE IS NO LIVE-ONLY VIEW. CatalogRepository.listCollections (:2906) has NO superseded_by predicate — it returns the raw registry projection, ordered by name, and selects SUPERSEDED_BY so callers CAN branch on it. Two catalog consumers do: commands/catalog_cmds/doctor.py:258 and :661. Whether every other consumer does is UNVERIFIED and is the actual question this bead asks.

A consumer that treats each listed row as live now sees, after any rename, a collection that does not exist — with an empty/absent created_at and display_name (observed shape: {'content_type': 'knowledge', 'created_at': '', 'display_name': '', ...}).

NOT A REGRESSION IN THE FIX. The retire is right and should stay; deleting the row was the bug. What is missing is the read-side counterpart: either a live-only accessor, or an audited sweep proving every consumer branches.

SCOPE TO SETTLE:
 - enumerate catalog list_collections() consumers (distinct from T3
   list_collections(), which is the vector surface and unaffected) and check each
   for a superseded_by branch;
 - decide whether listCollections should gain a live-only variant, or whether the
   raw projection stays and the contract is documented at the call sites;
 - if a live-only view is added, the raw one must remain reachable, since doctor
   and the drift tooling need to SEE retired rows.

PINNED MEANWHILE: tests/db/test_i711w_gap_contracts_fresh.py::test_registry_row_moved
now asserts the real post-change contract in both directions — the retired row
survives, carries superseded_by == the new name, and appears in the raw projection.
It previously asserted 'old registry row must be deleted' and had been RED since
09:22 that morning, invisible because the file is integration-marked and CI does not
run it (nexus-5opzu's exact class, caught live).

title: release checklist step 1 boots whatever jar happens to be on disk — a below-floor stamp fails the integration suite mid-cut with 49 ManagedServiceIncompatible errors
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 running the 7.0.0 release checklist as a dry run. Hit it directly.

THE GAP. CLAUDE.md checklist step 1 is:
  'Run unit + integration suite. uv run pytest and uv run pytest -m integration.
   Both must pass — integration is excluded from CI and is your last line of defense.'
Neither invocation says anything about the local service jar. Step 0 (check_engine_release_floor.py) verifies the PIN and the CLOUD engine — not the artifact the local suite actually boots.

WHAT HAPPENS. release.properties release_version is BLANK in source and stamped at build time (CLAUDE.md:135), so a locally-built dev jar carries whatever stamp its build baked, or none. The integration suite boots that jar through the engine substrate. If its stamp is below REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION, the client REFUSES it — correctly, that is the GH #1402 guard working — and the run dies:

  nexus.db.managed_endpoint.ManagedServiceIncompatible: managed nexus service at
  http://127.0.0.1:58420 is release_version '0.1.59', below the minimum this client
  supports (v0.1.60).

MEASURED, not hypothetical: 49 occurrences across one run; roughly 11 of 17 reported failures/errors were this and nothing else. A jar built at 17:49 today was already below a floor bumped at a4830c8f the same evening — the window between a floor bump and a rebuild is HOURS, and a release cut is exactly when the floor has just moved.

WHY IT BITES AT THE WORST MOMENT. The floor bump is itself part of the release arc. So the checklist step most likely to encounter a stale jar is the one run immediately after bumping, with the version already bumped and the release PR open. The failure mode is 49 red tests and no obvious cause, which reads as 'develop is broken' rather than 'rebuild your jar'.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS, one gate over. tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh:215-243 derives the stamp from REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION, compares it to the jar's baked stamp via unzip, rebuilds with the stamp written into release.properties when they differ, and restores the file afterwards (with a signal-safe backstop at :189). It even prints the diagnosis: '[gate] jar stamp <none> != floor 0.1.60 — rebuilding stamped'.

OPTIONS:
 (a) Cheapest — add the stamp-check to checklist step 1 as an explicit preceding
     command, so the human runs it before pytest.
 (b) Better — hoist the stamping block out of local-service-gate.sh into a script
     (scripts/ensure_stamped_jar.sh) that both the gate and the checklist call. The
     logic is already self-contained and already handles restore-on-failure.
 (c) Best — make the engine-substrate fixture itself fail with the REMEDY rather
     than the raw incompatibility, i.e. tests/_engine_substrate.py detects a
     below-floor baked stamp at boot and raises 'rebuild the jar stamped at
     <floor>: <command>'. That turns 49 confusing failures into one actionable
     error, and covers every caller, not just the checklist.

(c) is the same shape as the fail-loud-with-remedy contract ensure_engine already
has for a MISSING jar (tests/_engine_substrate.py:19 'a missing or stale JAR' fails
loud) — the staleness check just does not currently include the version stamp.

P2: no user-facing defect, and the guard that fires is working as designed. This is
release-process friction that costs an hour at the worst possible time.

title: cross-encoder ONNX is the last HuggingFace dependency — anonymous HF fetch at RUNTIME on every local-mode install, while bge and docling are self-hosted
description:
FOUND 2026-07-31 during the 7.0.0 dry run, in answer to a direct question about whether CI downloads come from our mirror. bge-768 and docling do. The cross-encoder does NOT, and it is the only one that reaches HuggingFace from SHIPPED CODE rather than only from CI.

TWO SITES, one of them user-facing:

1. RUNTIME (the one that matters): src/nexus/db/service_crossencoder_model.py:127
     base = f'https://huggingface.co/{CROSSENCODER_REPO}/resolve/{_PINNED_REVISION}'
   fetch_service_crossencoder_onnx() runs on local-mode installs to provision the
   Java-read rerank model. Every fresh local install performs an ANONYMOUS HF fetch
   of a ~91 MB model. It IS digest-verified (sha256 on both model and tokenizer) and
   it fails loud with an actionable message, and the caller treats cross-encoder
   failure as non-fatal (rerank degrades loud rather than blocking boot) — so this
   is an availability and supply-chain-surface issue, not a correctness one.

2. CI: .github/actions/prime-crossencoder-onnx/action.yml:50, same base URL, with
   retry/backoff + sha256. Cached, so it is a cold-cache cost, not per-run.

WHY THIS IS INCONSISTENT WITH THE ESTABLISHED RULE. The repo already decided this
question twice and self-hosted both times:
  - .github/actions/prime-bge-onnx: 'downloads from a SELF-HOSTED GitHub release
    asset (no HuggingFace dependency)' — built because an un-retried anonymous HF
    download (HTTP 429) was the recurring CI flake, 'acute on release PRs to main,
    which structurally cannot restore caches primed on develop.'
  - ci.yml:345 'Fetch docling models from our own mirror' / 'WE HOST THESE. Nothing
    here may reach HuggingFace.' — after HF fetch failures produced ~21 baffling
    extraction_method assertion failures (nexus-cxsbs / nexus-c7gnx).
The cross-encoder is the straggler from both sweeps.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE OTHERS WERE. bge and docling were CI-only exposure. This
one ships: a user on a fresh local install depends on HuggingFace being up,
un-rate-limited, and still serving that pinned revision. A 429 on a release day
degrades rerank for real users, not just a CI run.

PROPOSED FIX, mirroring what already exists: publish model.onnx + tokenizer.json as
a self-hosted GitHub release asset (the ci-assets-bge-768-v1 pattern), repoint both
sites at it, keep the existing sha256 pins verbatim so the artifact is provably the
same bytes. The prime-crossencoder-onnx action then collapses onto the same shape as
prime-bge-onnx.

P2 not P1: digest verification means a compromised or swapped upstream fails closed,
and rerank degradation is non-fatal by design. The exposure is availability plus an
un-owned third-party dependency in the install path.

title: [ci] engine-service-release.yml documents an approval gate the apple-signing environment does not have — no required_reviewers, no wait_timer
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while cutting engine-service-v0.1.60, answering "are we going to be
blocked waiting for a click for the mac signing again?" The answer is no — and the reason
is that the documented gate does not exist.

engine-service-release.yml (~line 96-109) states, as a stated COST of the design:

    # COST, stated so it is not a surprise: every run of this job now waits for
    # one approval, including the linux legs that need no secrets. Approval is
    # per-environment-per-run, so one click releases all three matrix legs.

THE ENVIRONMENT HAS NO APPROVAL GATE. Live config:

    GET repos/Hellblazer/nexus/environments/apple-signing
      protection_rules:            branch_policy ONLY
      required_reviewers:          ABSENT
      wait_timer:                  ABSENT
      deployment_branch_policy:    {protected_branches: false, custom_branch_policies: true}

Confirmed empirically in run 30677487799 (the v0.1.60 cut): both linux legs ran to
`success` UNATTENDED and mac-arm64 proceeded to `in_progress` with nobody clicking
anything. No job ever entered the `waiting` state.

SAME CLASS AS nexus-hq9na, which was fixed earlier the same day: a workflow comment
asserting a control that is not configured. And it overclaims in the DANGEROUS direction —
a reader concludes the Apple signing secrets are reachable only after a human approves,
when in fact the only controls are (a) the deployment branch policy and (b) the signing
STEPS being independently tag-gated, which the comment itself calls "defence in depth
rather than the only control".

TWO POSSIBLE RESOLUTIONS, and it needs a decision rather than a patch:
 (a) THE COMMENT IS WRONG — the approval was considered, documented, and never configured.
     Fix the comment. Arguably correct on the merits: this workflow only fires on a TAG
     PUSH, which is already a deliberate human act, so an approval click is redundant with
     the thing that triggered it. That is also why nobody noticed.
 (b) THE CONFIG IS WRONG — a required reviewer was intended and is missing. Then the
     signing secrets are one branch-policy mistake away from an unattended run, and the
     environment should get a required_reviewers rule.

I lean (a), because the tag push IS the human gate and the comment's own final sentence
argues the policy is defence in depth. But (b) is a security posture question about who
can reach six APPLE_* secrets, and that is not mine to settle.

WORTH NOTING FOR THE COST ARGUMENT EITHER WAY: the comment justifies NOT splitting mac
signing into its own job by weighing it against "an approval click". If there is no click,
that trade was mis-priced — the linux legs are not in fact paying an approval cost, so the
argument for keeping the 20-step job monolithic rests on the post-tag-discovery risk alone.

title: [engine] Main's startup sequence is executed by NO test — three failure handlers and the pgvector router invariant are all unpinned
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while answering "did we actually fix kjjab?" — the answer was "the
mechanism yes, the reporting no", and this is the no.

NOTHING TESTS Main's STARTUP SEQUENCE. Every service test constructs NexusService directly
(e.g. ServiceIntegrationTest.java:65, `new NexusService(0, TOKEN, svcDs)`). Main.main is
invoked by no test in the suite. So everything Main does BEFORE handing off is unpinned:

  - the Liquibase migration call and its catch (:82-:84)
  - root-token seeding and its catch (:100-:113, added by nexus-kjjab)
  - the PoolerModeCheck catch (:168)
  - the vector-backend wiring, incl. the PRODUCTION WIRING INVARIANT recorded on
    nexus-1k8s1 — that PgVectorRepository must take the ROUTER constructor, because the
    plain-Embedder one silently falls back to ONNX for ALL collections and breaks
    cloud-mode routing, "caught only at the first upsert's dim check"

That last one is the point: the file's own comments describe invariants whose violation is
SILENT, and the file has no test. Boot is the one code path every install executes and the
only one no test exercises.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND kjjab. Three of the startup steps are FAILURE HANDLERS. A handler
that is never executed by a test is indistinguishable from one that is wrong: the two
Liquibase/pooler handlers log.error + exit(1), the kjjab one now does too, and nothing
asserts any of them produce a diagnosable failure rather than a bare stack trace. The
original kjjab severity came entirely from this — the defect was ordinary, the
un-diagnosability is what made it P0-ops.

SHAPE OF THE FIX (needs a decision, not obviously one way):
 (a) extract Main's startup into a testable `Bootstrap.run(env, ds)` and pin each failure
     handler's OUTCOME (message contains the remedy; exit code 1), leaving main() a thin
     shell — the standard move, and it makes the handlers assertable without spawning a JVM;
 (b) spawn the real jar as a subprocess against a testcontainer with a deliberately broken
     precondition, and assert exit code + stderr. Heavier and slower, but it tests what
     actually ships, including the exit path itself;
 (c) accept it, and say so explicitly on this bead, so the next person does not rediscover
     the gap from scratch.

(a) covers more for less, but does NOT cover the exit path or the bare-JVM behaviour, which
is where kjjab's severity actually lived. A narrow (b) for one representative handler plus
(a) for the rest is probably the honest combination.

NOT A REGRESSION — this gap predates kjjab. Filed because kjjab's fix ADDED a third
handler to an untested sequence, and closing that bead without recording the gap would have
implied coverage that does not exist.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PARTIALLY CLOSED 2026-07-31, commit 848a531c: tests/test_main_bootstrap_failure.py.
STAYS OPEN — this covers ONE of the four unpinned things named in the description.

WHY IT WAS WRITTEN RATHER THAN LEFT FILED. I filed this bead and moved on, and Hal asked
"did we actually fix the testing of kjjab? or?" The answer was no: I had reported a finding
instead of completing the work. Filing is not fixing. That is the whole reason this bead
has a commit attached to it within an hour of being created.

NOW COVERED — the root-token handler, at the BOOT layer, against the REAL shipped jar:
  test_revoked_root_slot_exits_nonzero_with_a_remedy_not_a_stack_trace
  test_rotating_the_provisioned_token_boots_cleanly

Each spawns `java -jar` against its OWN database (created and dropped per test on the
session substrate's PG, so it never touches the service_tokens rows other tests
authenticate against). It asserts process outcome — exit status and log content — which is
what an extracted Bootstrap.run() could not have covered.

THE FALSIFICATION IS THE INTERESTING PART, and it is worth keeping for whoever pins the
remaining handlers. Reverting Main's handler to the bare call leaves

    assert rc != 0            PASSING     (the exception propagates; the JVM still exits 1)
    assert "root_token_seed_refused" in out   FAILING

So a test that merely asserted "boot failed" would have stayed GREEN through the exact
defect that made nexus-kjjab P0-ops. The severity there was never "it fails" — it was "it
fails un-diagnosably". Any pin for the remaining handlers must discriminate the same way,
or it will be decorative in precisely the case that matters.

STILL UNPINNED, and this bead remains open for them:
  - the Liquibase migration catch (Main.java:82-84)
  - the PoolerModeCheck catch (:168)
  - the pgvector PRODUCTION WIRING INVARIANT (nexus-1k8s1): PgVectorRepository must take
    the ROUTER constructor, because the plain-Embedder one silently falls back to ONNX for
    ALL collections and is "caught only at the first upsert's dim check". This is the one
    with no failure at all to assert on — it needs a positive check that the router is
    wired, not a failure-mode test, and it is the hardest of the four.

The harness now exists, so the remaining three are incremental rather than greenfield.

title: nx_answer has 4 lifetime invocations against a mandate saying ALL analytical questions route through it — treat as a capability/latency defect, NOT a compliance defect
description:
THIS IS A CAPABILITY BEAD, NOT A COMPLIANCE BEAD. Filing it as compliance would be
the wrong fix, and would burn the credibility of the whole nexus-h33x8 program on
its single most visible number.

THE MEASUREMENT: `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__nx_answer` has FOUR lifetime
invocations across 1,606 transcript files in this project. Two from orchestrators,
two from subagents. Meanwhile the guidance layer states, in the SessionStart block
and in using-nx-skills SKILL.md, that "ALL analytical questions go through
nx_answer". So the most emphatic mandate in the guidance layer has a compliance
rate indistinguishable from zero.

WHY THIS IS PROBABLY NOT A DISCIPLINE FAILURE. nx_answer's OWN docstring
advertises its measured latency distribution over 100 production runs:
    32% under 5s | 5% in 5-30s | 40% in 30s-2min | 23% in 2-5min
and notes the plan-MISS path adds another `claude -p` planner subprocess (up to
300s) on top. So 63% of calls block for over 30 seconds and nearly a quarter for
multiple minutes. An agent that greps instead of waiting up to five minutes for a
retrieval answer is making a CORRECT trade. The mandate is not being ignored; it
is being priced.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SEPARATES THE TWO EXPLANATIONS, and it is already in the
epic's data: the SubagentStart preflight lifts plan_search from 12 to 281 and
scratch from 61 to 929 -- the same channel, the same session population, the same
imperative framing. It moves nx_answer from 2 to 2. A delivery channel that
demonstrably works for four sibling capabilities and does nothing for this one is

a3 (dispatch.py stream-json de-vacuation): claude_dispatch now uses --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages instead of plain json. CRITICAL finding beyond original scope: switching only the output-format flag does NOT fix the vacuous timeout drain -- asyncio.subprocess.Process.communicate()'s internal unbounded read(-1) loop buffers into a coroutine-local list and pops bytes out of the StreamReader's own buffer as it goes; when asyncio.wait_for's timeout cancels communicate(), everything already read is discarded with the cancelled frame AND is no longer in the buffer either. title: guidance content: invert using-nx-skills — imperative + triggers lead, routing menu behind progressive disclosure; SessionStart 12,817 -> under 6,000 bytes, with a pre-registered prediction that can fail
description:
DEPENDS ON nexus-h33x8.4 (so this content change, and every later revision, is
Tier B / session-cadence rather than release-cadence) and on nexus-h33x8.1 (so
the effect is measurable). Tier depends on .4 landing first; if .4 slips, this is
Tier C and needs a PENDING_RELEASE.md entry.
