title: [index] first-class sensitivity: --sensitive on capture/index should route, stamp, and exempt documents from every LLM-dispatching surface — today it's all hand-rolled workarounds
description:
Motivated 2026-07-28 by indexing a sensitive business PDF. Everything required was possible,
but ALL of it was operator knowledge rather than product surface:

- **Collection routing as a side-channel**: the only way to keep the document out of LLM
  extraction sweeps was knowing that `docs__default` has aspect extraction intentionally
  disabled (nexus-z70w) and overriding `--collection` with the four-segment name. Nothing marks
  the DOCUMENT as exempt — protection is an accident of which collection it sits in, and a
  future `nx catalog migrate-fallback` / collection reorganization would silently strip it.
- **No sensitivity metadata anywhere**: catalog row, chunk metadata, and search results carry
  no flag. A future session (or agent) retrieving these chunks has no signal that quoting them
  into an artifact/bead/PR is inappropriate.
- **The LLM-dispatch surfaces that must honor such a flag today do not know it exists**:
  `nx enrich aspects` (content → claude CLI), `--validate-sample` (content → operator_verify),
  `nx taxonomy label` / `review --auto` (chunk terms → claude_dispatch), `nx_answer` operator
  steps (chunk content → claude -p), `nx dt index --enrich` (bib fields → CrossRef, an
  EXTERNAL third party). DEVONthink got this right with excludeFromChat — input AND output
  protection at the API layer. Nexus has no analogue.
- **Cloud exposure is undisclosed at index time**: in service mode, indexing uploads chunk text
  + embeddings to the cloud tenant. Fine when chosen; never stated. A `--sensitive` flag is the
  natural place for a one-line "this will be stored in <tenant>" acknowledgment.

## Proposed

1. `--sensitive` on `nx index pdf/md`, `nx dt capture`, `nx dt index`: stamps
   `sensitive=true` into chunk metadata + catalog row (+ DT tag on writeback).
2. Every LLM-dispatching/enriching surface filters on the flag BY DEFAULT: aspects, validation
   sampling, taxonomy label/review dispatches, bib enrichment (external!), operator
   auto-hydration in plan runs. Loud skip lines, not silent.
3. `search`/`query` results carry the flag so downstream consumers (agents especially) can
   apply output discipline; consider a `sensitive:` prefix badge in human-readable output.
4. `nx catalog list --sensitive` / doctor check: sensitive docs sitting in aspect-ELIGIBLE
   collections get flagged (the routing-as-side-channel failure mode above).
5. Docs: state plainly which verbs ship content to which endpoints (cloud tenant, claude CLI,
   CrossRef/S2/OpenAlex) — the disclosure exists today only as tribal knowledge.

Prior art in-repo: DEVONthink MCP's excludeFromChat contract (two-sided protection); nexus-z70w
(aspect-disabled collection) is the mechanism to generalize from collection-granularity to
document-granularity.

title: [test-infra] tripwire: a test that sets NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT without NX_SERVICE_URL silently reads from the session substrate's service
description:
The class has now cost two multi-session misdiagnoses and 14 tests.

MECHANISM. resolve_service_endpoint ranks NX_SERVICE_URL ABOVE the NX_SERVICE_HOST/NX_SERVICE_PORT halves. The session-scoped engine-substrate fixture exports an NX_SERVICE_URL. So a module that spawns its own service and pins only host/port has its env-resolved READS routed to the SESSION's service while its explicitly-constructed clients (base_url=...) WRITE to its own. The result is never an obvious error:
  - if the two services disagree on the bearer -> HTTP 401, which the MCP tool functions and aspect_sql's source='aspects' mode swallow into an empty result with the reason in a field nothing prints (nexus-qvs2h, 9 tests, weeks read as an RLS bug);
  - if they agree on the bearer -> a clean answer about the OTHER tenant: [] and {'owners': 0, 'documents': 0, ...} (nexus-12m77, 5 tests, weeks read as data-visibility).
Both present as 'seeded but invisible', which is the RLS signature, so the investigation goes to tenancy every time.

SECOND HALF OF THE TRAP. Pinning the env in a CLASS-scoped fixture is not enough: conftest's autouse _pin_t2_substrate is FUNCTION-scoped, so it runs after class-scoped setup and overwrites it per test. The 12m77 fix needed BOTH the URL and a move to function scope; each half alone still failed all 5. A tripwire must catch the ordering half too, not just the missing key.

PROPOSED TRIPWIRE (autouse, session or function conftest): when a test's env carries NX_SERVICE_HOST or NX_SERVICE_PORT whose (host, port) does NOT match the host/port of the live NX_SERVICE_URL, fail with an explicit message naming both endpoints. That is precisely the mode-split state and has no legitimate use — a module either drives one service or explicitly opts out. Cheap: string compare per test, no I/O.

LATENT SURFACE, measured 2026-07-28: 21 test files set NX_SERVICE_PORT and never mention NX_SERVICE_URL. All are green today, so this is not a live-bug sweep; the tripwire is what keeps the next one from costing another two sessions.
  tests/test_t1_isolated_service_mode.py, tests/_engine_substrate.py,
  tests/catalog/test_http_catalog_client.py, tests/db/test_embed_parity.py,
  tests/db/test_xnz0o_commands_integration.py, tests/db/test_http_aspects_stores_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_http_telemetry_store_integration.py, tests/db/test_http_scratch_store_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_http_chash_integration.py, tests/db/test_health_service_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_catalog_etl.py, tests/db/test_storage_mode.py,
  tests/db/test_http_plan_library_integration.py, tests/db/test_catalog_consumer_qnp5s_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_coverage_3cwnx_integration.py, tests/db/test_collection_health_dsu5z_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_http_memory_store_integration.py, tests/db/test_http_taxonomy_store_integration.py,
  tests/db/test_mvv_memory_service.py, tests/db/test_http_scratch_store.py, tests/db/test_memory_etl.py

Worked examples of the fixed shape: tests/db/test_http_catalog_integration.py::TestReaderPaths::_point_reader_at_this_modules_service (function-scoped, monkeypatch, sets the URL, evicts the shared client on both sides) and the 11 sites in tests/db/test_l9hd8_aspect_sql_service_integration.py fixed in cd9bc492.

title: [bug] the client ONNX stack is justified by a consumer that was never wired — extract_salient_sentences has zero src/ callers, and RDR-188 cited it to keep cross_encoder alive
description:
FOUND 2026-07-28 while scoping decision 3 (retire the tier-0 local EF), from
Hal's read that this is "residue from the nx_search fallout of reranking on the
client". That read is right in substance; the mechanism turned out to be
different from orphaning, and worse.

THE CHAIN, each link verified:

1. RDR-188 moved rerank server-side. search_engine.py:509-603 — `rerank` requests
   the SERVER's fused rerank stage, honored only when the backend carries
   `supports_server_rerank`.

2. a3a7eaa3 (2026-07-22, nexus-9o6y2.19) "retire client rerank path fully"
   deleted rerank_results / _rerank_local / _RERANK_MODEL, and recorded an
   explicit DESIGN DECISION in its message and in cross_encoder.py's docstring:

     "the module survives BY DESIGN as a salience-only substrate (salience.py's
      extract_salient_sentences is a genuine non-rerank consumer; wholesale
      deletion was the silent-deletion trap the audit flagged)"

3. `extract_salient_sentences` has ZERO callers in src/. The only references
   anywhere are its own definition, its own `__all__` entry, a docstring mention
   in cross_encoder.py added by a3a7eaa3 itself, and two test files
   (test_rdr_109_phase4_salience.py, test_rdr_109_phase5_salience.py).
   `nexus/salience.py` IS imported by search_engine.py:1100 — but only for
   `token_overlap_boost`, which does not touch the cross-encoder.

4. So the module retained as "salience-only" is retained for a salience entry
   point nothing calls. The only live consumer of `nexus.cross_encoder` in src/
   is doctor.py:2284's `cross_encoder_available()` availability probe — a
   diagnostic reporting on a capability no production path uses.

5. And capability-ledger row 47b (T2 [21097]) declares onnxruntime + tokenizers
   first-class "for cross_encoder only" — a dependency pair whose stated sole
   justification is this chain.

NEVER WIRED, NOT UNWIRED — the distinction matters for how to treat it.
`git log -S extract_salient_sentences -- src/` returns exactly two commits:
6ffc060d (2026-05-11, RDR-109 Phase 5) which ADDED the definition, the docstring
and the `__all__` entry and wired no caller; and a3a7eaa3, which added only the
docstring mention. It has never had a production call site. So this is not
rerank-retirement residue in the strict sense — it is a Phase-5 substrate that
shipped unwired, and the rerank retirement then leaned on it as load-bearing.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A DELETE. The standing directive is
"unused != useless — ask before deleting", and a3a7eaa3's own audit flagged
wholesale deletion of cross_encoder as a silent-deletion trap. That caution was
right in general and simply picked the wrong evidence: it validated the
consumer's existence, not its reachability. Nothing here should be deleted on
this bead's say-so. What this bead asks for is a DECISION on a chain that is
currently justified by an empty last link:

  (a) WIRE IT. salience.py's own docstring says extract_salient_sentences "runs
      at index time (or via the ...)" — if that was the RDR-109 Phase 4/5
      intent and it is still wanted, wire it and the justification becomes real.
  (b) RETIRE THE CHAIN. If salience-at-index-time is not wanted, then
      extract_salient_sentences, nexus.cross_encoder, doctor's availability
      probe, and ledger row 47b's onnxruntime+tokenizers declaration all go
      together, and a no-extras client stops shipping an ONNX runtime it never
      invokes.
  (c) KEEP DELIBERATELY, with the reason corrected in cross_encoder.py's
      docstring — "retained unwired for future index-time salience" is a
      defensible position, but it is not what the docstring says today, and the
      next reader will re-derive this.

BEARS DIRECTLY ON DECISION 3 (retire tier-0 local EF). Ledger row 47b is one of
the two things keeping a client-side ONNX stack in the tree; the other is the
tier-0 EF itself. If (b) is chosen, decision 3's remaining surface shrinks to
the two deliberately-offline paths (isolated T1 at db/t1.py:152 and
`nx index --dry-run` at commands/index.py:1356) and nothing else.

METHOD NOTE. This is the same failure shape as nexus-tdkg1.1's method list and
capability-ledger row 46: a written justification naming a consumer, believed
without checking the call graph. Third instance in two sessions. The check that
finds it every time is one grep for callers, excluding the symbol's own module.

title: [taxonomy] review --auto --dry-run does not predict what --auto actually deletes: verdicts are non-deterministic, so the preview is not a safety mechanism for a destructive command
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 on `knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` (26 pending topics, freshly
rebuilt). Ran the documented safe sequence — preview, inspect, apply — back to back, same
collection, same topics, nothing changed in between.

    nx taxonomy review -c <coll> --auto --dry-run
      -> Dry run: 24 accepted, 0 renamed, 2 deleted, 0 merged, 0 skipped
         Deletes: [1426144040] Index and type formalism (273 docs)
                  [1426144055] Mathematical symbol notation (199 docs)

    nx taxonomy review -c <coll> --auto -y
      -> Auto-review complete: 21 accepted, 1 renamed, 3 deleted, 0 merged, 1 skipped
         Deletes: [1426144055] Mathematical symbol notation (199 docs)
                  [1426144048] arXiv language model citations (167 docs)
                  [1426144050] Epsilon-bounded optimization problem theory (95 docs)

**The delete sets barely overlap.** One topic in common. The dry run condemned
"Index and type formalism" — which the real run instead RENAMED (to "Simplex type and index
notation") and kept. The real run deleted two topics the preview said nothing about, destroying
262 doc-assignments the operator never saw proposed.

Cause is structural, not a bug in the diff: `--auto` obtains verdicts from batched
`claude_dispatch`. There is no seed, no caching of the dry-run verdicts, and no re-use of them on
apply — so the two invocations are two independent samples from a stochastic process. `--dry-run`
therefore previews *a* plausible verdict set, not *the* verdict set that will be applied.

## Why this matters more than typical LLM variance

`--dry-run` here is the ONLY safety mechanism on a destructive operation. `--help` documents it as
"Print verdicts without applying any mutations (--auto only)", and pairs it with `-y` ("Skip the
destructive-action confirmation prompt"). The intended workflow is plainly: preview → satisfy
yourself → apply with -y. That workflow is unsound as built. An operator who reviews the preview
and approves it has approved a different set of deletions than the one that runs.

Topic deletion is not trivially reversible: assignments are dropped (461 docs became uncategorized
here), and the only route back is a full `rebuild`, which re-clusters everything and produces yet
another non-identical taxonomy.

## Acceptance

1. **Make the preview authoritative.** Have `--dry-run` persist its verdicts (keyed by topic id +
   a content hash of the topic's terms/label), and have a subsequent `--auto` apply *those*
   verdicts rather than re-sampling. Invalidate if the taxonomy changed in between.
   Alternatively: a single invocation that computes verdicts once, prints them, and prompts —
   removing the two-invocation gap entirely.
2. **If re-sampling is kept, say so.** `--help` must state that `--dry-run` output is indicative
   only and that the applied run may differ, so nobody treats it as an approval artifact.
3. **Show destructive verdicts at apply time and require confirmation of THAT list**, not a
   previously-seen one. Today `-y` blanket-skips the confirmation, so the actual delete list can
   reach the user only after it has already been applied — which is what happened here.
4. Consider `--accept-only` / `--no-destructive`: run the auto-reviewer but restrict it to
   accept+rename, leaving delete/merge for explicit human action. That makes the common case
   ("label and accept these 26 topics") safe by construction.

## Note

The reviewer's judgement was GOOD in both runs — the topics it deleted were genuinely LaTeX/
citation-boilerplate artifacts (independently corroborating nexus-1d5y6), and the rename was an
improvement. This bead is not about verdict quality. It is that a destructive command's preview
does not predict its behaviour.

Full record: T2 `nexus/forensics-2026-07-27-taxonomy-and-aspect-findings`.

title: [dt] --dt-content indexes web-archive boilerplate verbatim: 59% of one CACM article's indexed text is cookie-consent junk, and it outranks the article's own content
description:
`nx dt index --dt-content` writes DEVONthink's AI-extracted text **verbatim** into the
T3-indexed cache file with no cleaning:

    src/nexus/commands/dt.py:410-427
    text = _dt.dt_extract_content(uuid)
    front = f"---\ntitle: {json.dumps(name)}\n---\n\n{text}"
    cache_path.write_text(front, encoding="utf-8")
    count = index_markdown(cache_path, ...)

For web archives that text includes the entire cookie-consent wall, per-cookie tables,
and base64 `data:image/png` URIs.

## Measured on tumbler 1.12.102 (CACM "Formal Reasoning Meets LLMs", DT UUID 00327AAD-…)

- **47,725 of 80,670 chars (59%)** of the indexed document is cookie-consent boilerplate
  and inline base64 image data.
- The article body proper is ~lines 687-846 of a 926-line extraction. Everything before is
  Cookiebot output; everything after is CACM site chrome ("Related Reading", "The Latest
  from CACM").
- 70 chunks were produced; **32 of them match a cookie-tracking query**.
- Retrieval is inverted: a query about *cookie tracking* matches this document at distance
  **0.275**, while a query about *its actual subject* (formal reasoning / theorem proving /
  Lean) matches at **0.394**. The junk is more retrievable than the paper.

## Independent corroboration from the aspect extractor

`scholarly-paper-v1` did not run — the paper-shape detector routed to `general-prose-v1`,
almost certainly because `_PAPER_SHAPE_SIGNALS` finds no Abstract heading under 47KB of
cookie tables. The extractor flagged the problem itself:

    "extraction_caveat": "Source text is a partial web scrape — the leading ~60% is
     cookie-consent boilerplate, and the article body is truncated mid-section with
     figures and citations stripped."
    "confidence": 0.72
    "extractor_name": "general-prose-v1"

So a correctly-typed `content_type=paper` CACM article with a DOI gets prose-grade
extraction because of ingest noise.

## Impact

Every web archive ingested via `--dt-content` is affected. Consequences compound:
1. Retrieval pollution — boilerplate chunks compete with real content collection-wide, and
   cookie/tracking vocabulary is near-identical across ALL such documents, so they cluster
   together and can form spurious topics.
2. Aspect quality — paper-shaped sources get misrouted to the prose extractor.
3. Cost — ~59% of embedding spend on this document was boilerplate.

## Acceptance

1. Strip boilerplate before `index_markdown` on the `--dt-content` path. Minimum viable:
   drop `data:` URIs, and detect/trim a leading cookie-consent block (Cookiebot's output is
   highly regular — "Maximum Storage Duration" / "Type: HTTP Cookie" line pairs).
2. Prefer DEVONthink's own reader/article view when available for `webarchive` records
   rather than the full page text.
3. Emit a boilerplate-ratio warning at ingest when the stripped fraction exceeds a
   threshold, so silent quality loss is visible.
4. Re-index affected records. Identify via chunks matching cookie-consent vocabulary in
   collections carrying `extraction_source=dt_content`.
5. Note the cache file at `catalog/.dt-content/<uuid>.md` is unconditionally rewritten each
   run, so manual cleanup cannot be a workaround — the fix must live in the writer.

Found while integrating 1.12.102 (see nexus-pbawi for the unrelated register wedge hit in
the same session).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## Document 1.12.102 remediated by hand 2026-07-27 (product defect still open)

Sequence, for anyone repeating this on other affected records:

1. Backed up the cache file, then stripped it: kept frontmatter + the article body
   (lines 698-823 of 930) + DOI/issue block; dropped the Cookiebot wall, the CACM site
   chrome, and every `data:image` line. 80,670 -> 28,185 chars (65% removed), 0 cookie
   mentions, 0 data URIs.
2. Re-indexed via `index_markdown(cache_path, corpus="dt", collection_name=...,
   extraction_source="dt_content")` directly — NOT `nx dt index`, which would rewrite the
   cache from DEVONthink and undo step 1.
3. **`index_markdown` does not replace chunks — it ADDS them.** 28 clean chunks were
   written and the manifest moved to them, but the 70 old chunks stayed live in T3.
   Result was strictly worse for a while: cookie chunks still retrievable AND duplicate
   copies of the article (identical text at distances 0.3790 / 0.3801). This is the trap —
   fixing the source file and re-indexing is NOT sufficient.
4. `nx t3 gc` was the wrong instrument: with `--orphan-window 1h` it proposed 17 chunks, and
   hydrating them showed a mixed bag — two belonged to OTHER documents in the collection
   (mesh/AMR content: `\Delta x`, "nodal mass basis for velocity interpolation"). The 30d
   default window exists precisely to protect transient re-index orphans, so windowed GC
   cannot be used for targeted cleanup.
5. `delete_by_source(collection, source_path)` returned **0** — chunks are not addressable by
   the `.dt-content` source_path, and `get_by_id` returns empty metadata in service mode, so
   neither source_path nor title can attribute a chunk. That left content-based attribution
   as the only exact method.
6. Attribution used: hydrate each candidate, normalize whitespace, and test whether a 110-char
   probe from the chunk's midpoint is a substring of the ORIGINAL (pre-clean) file. Exact, no
   false positives possible. Deleted via `delete_by_chunk_ids`:
   - 32 boilerplate-only chunks (cookie tables / base64 PNG, zero article terms)
   - 16 + 3 stale article chunks not in the 28-chash manifest
   - 262 candidate chunks belonging to other documents were correctly left alone
   Iterated until a re-scan over 12 queries returned 0 residual.

Verified after: cookie query no longer matches at all (nearest 0.758 vs threshold 0.65,
was 0.275); no duplicate text in topical results; manifest = 28.

**Implication for acceptance item 4 (re-index affected records): a bulk re-index will NOT
fix this class on its own** — it will double every affected document unless the stale chunks
are deleted first. Any remediation sweep needs a delete-then-index, and needs a supported way
to enumerate a document's live chunks (the catalog's `get_chunk_chashes(doc_id)` works; the
T3-side `delete_by_source` did not).

Residual on this document: the aspect record was extracted from the polluted text — it
routed to `general-prose-v1` (not `scholarly-paper-v1`), confidence 0.72, and carries a now-stale
`extraction_caveat` about cookie boilerplate. Not re-extracted, because `nx enrich aspects` is
collection-wide with no per-document verb and would re-run all 46 records (~$0.45) and churn 45
unrelated rows. A per-document re-extract verb would make this cheap.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## Independent corroboration: unvalidated extraction manufactures spurious TOPICS, not just bad chunks

Rebuilding the taxonomy for `knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` on 2026-07-27
(`nx taxonomy rebuild`, HDBSCAN over 6,113 chunks → 26 topics) surfaced the extraction-noise
problem from a completely independent direction.

**Raw discover-stage topic labels (TF-IDF token triples, before the LLM labelling pass):**

```
octants mathfrak octant        mathcal refinement hat      td memory rowspan
mathbf pmb mathrm              mathcal mathsf elements     pi ell psi
varepsilon mathcal ell         td mesh rowspan             face td prime
```

`mathbf`, `pmb`, `mathrm`, `mathcal`, `mathsf`, `varepsilon` are **raw LaTeX commands**.
`td` / `rowspan` are **raw HTML table markup**. These are clustering as if they were subject
matter — the extractor's markup residue is dense and consistent enough across documents to form
its own semantic neighbourhoods.

Of the 26 resulting topics, roughly three are markup/notation artifacts rather than real subjects:

- "Mathematical symbol notation" (199 docs)
- "Index and type formalism" (273 docs)
- "Memory and retrieval benchmark tables" (422 docs)

That is **~894 chunks (15% of the collection)** whose topic assignment is driven by extraction
residue. The LLM labelling pass makes them *look* legitimate — "Mathematical symbol notation"
reads like a real topic — which makes the pollution harder to spot after the fact, not easier.

### Why this raises the priority of the sanity gate

The existing acceptance items treat extraction noise as a per-document retrieval problem
(§ the CACM cookie boilerplate outranking the article). This shows the blast radius is wider:

1. **Corpus-level.** Noise from many documents aggregates into topics that then compete in
   topic-scoped retrieval (`search --topic`, `search_topic_scoped`) for every query.
2. **Self-concealing.** The labelling pass launders machine-generated garbage into plausible
   English. Post-hoc audit of topic *labels* will not find it — you have to look at the
   pre-labelling token triples or at the member chunks.
3. **Cost.** Discovery embedded 6,113 chunks to cluster; the fraction spent organising markup is
   wasted, and the resulting topics permanently skew the taxonomy until the next rebuild.

Concretely strengthens acceptance item 1 (strip boilerplate) and the proposed post-extraction
sanity gate: a whitespace-ratio / markup-fraction check at ingest would have prevented all three
artifact topics. Suggest additionally: **strip LaTeX command tokens and HTML tag names from the
TF-IDF vocabulary used for topic discovery**, as a cheap defence-in-depth independent of whether
ingest is fixed.

title: rollback procedure has an undocumented ownership precondition — a schema owned by a different role fails at the first DROP
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 by code-review-expert on the nexus-a0m60 review.

THE FORWARD PATH GUARDS FOR THIS EXPLICITLY. staging-001-landing-tables.xml:224-232 skips
grants when pg_get_userbyid(n.nspowner) <> current_user, and its own comment says a bulk
grant 'hard-errors when a replay runs as a non-owner of a schema a prior run's owner
created'.

THE ROLLBACK PATH HAS NO EQUIVALENT GUARD anywhere except staging-4's own inverse.

CONSEQUENCE. In SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest the admin role creates and therefore
owns every schema and table, so this never surfaces. On a real cluster where the schemas
were provisioned by a different role — or by an earlier migration credential — the first
DROP TABLE in the rollback chain fails with 'must be owner of table', and the chain stops
part-way, having already reverted some changesets.

UNTESTABLE IN THE CURRENT HARNESS BY CONSTRUCTION: the container's bootstrap makes the
migration role the owner of everything. Reproducing it needs a fixture where schemas are
created by role A and the rollback runs as role B.

MINIMUM ACTION: document it as a stated precondition of the rollback procedure, alongside
the nexus-9vg5g fresh-init precondition — both belong in the same operator runbook section.
BETTER: a fixture that pins it, since a partially-applied rollback is worse than a refused
one.

title: rollback round-trip only covers full-teardown; PARTIAL release-to-release rollback is untested and has different semantics
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 by code-review-expert on the nexus-a0m60 review.

THE GAP. SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest only ever rolls back to the floor, where
every migration-owned table is dropped and rebuilt. Schema identity is then nearly
guaranteed by construction — a full teardown/rebuild reproduces the schema almost by
definition.

But the incident that motivated the whole arc was a PARTIAL rollback: 'is 0.1.56 still a
supported rollback target for 0.1.57'. That is release-to-release, a handful of changesets
deep, and it has genuinely different semantics.

CONCRETE UNTESTED CASE: rdr180-3..7 are ALTER COLUMN chash TYPE bytea conversions carrying
empty <rollback/>. A rollback to any tag ABOVE rdr180 therefore leaves chash as bytea while
everything around it reverts to the text-era shape. That is exactly the
'parseable, executable, and still wrong' class the test's javadoc claims execution catches,
and it is not covered. Note the octet_length(chash)=32 CHECK renders identically for text
and bytea, so the constraints category does not backstop it either (the columns category
added post-review would, but only if a partial rollback is actually exercised).

FIX DIRECTION: a second @Test that rolls back to a MID-TREE point and asserts both what
reverted and what deliberately did NOT. Alternatively state the scope limit explicitly in
the class javadoc so nobody reads full-teardown coverage as partial-rollback coverage.

COST NOTE: this is a third testcontainer on every service/** PR. Folding the existing two
tests into a @Nested sharing one container (suggested in the same review) would pay for it.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest.java:727 typeHygieneRollback_restoresExactDataAndRoundTripsForward does mid-tree partial rollbacks (stages through catalog-031-1 and catalog-002) asserting revert + round-trip; residual chash/vectors-004 window tracked by open nexus-lelhx

title: the rollback gate decays silently as the empty-<rollback/> set grows — 49 of 208 changesets are already declared irreversible and nothing bounds it
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-27 by substantive-critic on the nexus-a0m60 review.

MEASURED: 49 of 208 changesets carry an empty <rollback/>. Two were added deliberately by
a0m60 (catalog-016-0, vectors-001-1) and disclosed; the other 47 predate it and include
rdr180-1-drop-dependent-views, rdr180-14/15-recreate-*, rdr180-15..19 (function
definitions), rdr187-1/2/3, and all the fk-002/003-validate legs.

WHY IT MATTERS. SchemaRollbackRoundTripIntegrationTest STRUCTURALLY REWARDS growing that
set. A future changeset that creates an index, view, function or policy and declares
<rollback/> passes every assertion in the file: the object survives the rollback (it is
not a table, so tablesInSchema misses it), the forward re-apply is a no-op or CREATE OR
REPLACE, and after == before. The gate gets weaker and nothing says so.

That is the same silent-decay mode the a0m60 design correctly rejected for
rollbackCount(N) — and then reintroduced on a different axis.

FIX DIRECTION: a companion lint in the shape of test_the_rule_is_load_bearing_not_vacuous
— pin the count (or an explicit allowlist) of empty <rollback/> changesets so adding one
is a deliberate, reviewed act rather than a silent weakening. An allowlist is probably
better than a bare count: it forces a one-line justification at the point of addition.

RELATED FRAMING FIX, same finding: the a0m60 commit message says 'roll back EVERYTHING'
and db.changelog-master.xml says 'reverts the entire schema we own'. With 49 declared-
irreversible changesets that overclaims. The accurate statement is: the full table set,
minus a declared-irreversible cohort.

title: pure-static tests boot the engine substrate — a changelog lint cannot run when the changelog changes
notes:
FOUND while adding tests/test_changelog_analyze_lint.py right after the nexus-aqbrk
flip (2026-07-26/27).

SHAPE. tests/conftest.py::_pin_t2_substrate is autouse and, post-flip, routes EVERY
test to the engine substrate — including tests that touch no substrate at all. The
changelog lints (test_changelog_analyze_lint, test_changelog_rls_lint,
test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint) are pure static XML analysis: they parse
files under service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/ and assert on the text. They do
not need PG, a JAR, or a tenant.

WHY IT BITES SPECIFICALLY. The engine substrate refuses to boot on a STALE jar. A jar
goes stale the moment you edit the changelog. So the changelog lints are unrunnable
exactly when you are editing changelogs — the moment you most want them. Observed
three times in one sitting: each changelog edit forced a full `mvn package` before the
lint could even be evaluated, and a failed falsification attempt produced NO output at
all because the test ERRORED rather than FAILED (silently, until the exit code was
read).

NOT A CI PROBLEM. CI's `service-jar` job builds the artifact and the test job downloads
it, so the jar is always fresh there. This is local-dev ergonomics — which is why it is
P2, not higher.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not decided). A marker-based opt-out honoured by _pin_t2_substrate,
e.g. `pytestmark = pytest.mark.no_substrate`, returning before
`request.getfixturevalue("t2_service_env")`. Cheap, and it documents at the test which
tests are substrate-free. Alternatives worth weighing: keying off a path prefix (too
implicit), or making the staleness check lazy so only tests that actually touch the
service pay for it (better, more invasive).

WHATEVER LANDS MUST NOT become a way to silently skip the substrate for tests that DO
need it — NX_T2_SUBSTRATE_EXPECTED=1 exists precisely to stop the engine arm vanishing
into a green run (it is what surfaced the 73 CI errors in PR #1426). An opt-out marker
is a new way to make that vanish, so it needs a census assert: the set of marked tests
should be small, enumerated, and covered by a test that fails if it grows silently.
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): ALREADY-FIXED. Evidence: NX_TEST_T2_SUBSTRATE=none branch in tests/conftest.py (~:1031, nexus-vdti6/wixar) lets pure-static lints run without a fresh jar; non-vacuity guarded by scripts/check_lint_leg_non_vacuity.py + tests/test_wixar_lint_leg_substrate_none.py

title: T3 title collision: a RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER shadows the real VADAOrchestra design sketch, breaking store_get by title
description:
Two T3 documents share the title `research-note-vadaorchestra-borrowables-replanning-catalog-rules-2026-06-25` in `knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1`. One holds the real content; the other holds the literal string `RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER`.

    4be8b2f33c526102940f6e88aadba13900b69175ee37d5fa6b3d9647e7b99cb5  -> "RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER"
    fee7a73e5ad8664375c4d803eb3fe3feceafd74cd44858db25ca0747c7ee4a4a  -> the full design sketch

Both carry identical tags (`research,design-sketch,plan-runner,replanning,catalog-links,datalog,neurosymbolic`) and the same indexed date (2026-06-26).

## Impact

`store_get(doc_id="<the title>")` cannot resolve it — it returns:

    Multiple documents with title '...': 4be8b2f3..., fee7a73e... Pass a 64-char content-hash to disambiguate.

So retrieval by title fails, and a caller picking a hash blind has a coin-flip chance of getting the placeholder and concluding the research was never written. That is what nearly happened on 2026-07-26 while researching RDR-190: the first hash tried returned the placeholder.

Content-addressed dedup cannot catch this — the two documents have genuinely different content, so they are correctly distinct chunks. The collision is at the TITLE layer, which has no uniqueness constraint.

The real content is load-bearing: it is the design sketch behind beads nexus-chr25 (plan-IR `rule` step, bounded recursive closure over `catalog_links`) and nexus-q2wif (bounded replanning loop in `plan_run`). Both beads cite it BY HASH specifically because of this collision, with a warning not to read the other one.

## Scope

Isolated, not a pattern — a full-corpus search for `RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER` across `knowledge` returns exactly one hit (this document). So this is a one-off cleanup, not a systemic write-path defect, unless investigation shows otherwise.

Two questions worth answering before deleting:

1. **How did it happen?** Most likely a `store_put` that wrote a stub first and a second call that wrote the real content under the same title, where the store appends rather than replaces on title collision. If `store_put` is append-on-same-title by design, that is worth knowing — it means any note written twice leaves a shadow. If it is meant to upsert by title, this is a write-path bug and the cleanup is secondary.
2. **Should title be unique per collection?** There is currently no constraint. Adding one is a bigger call than this cleanup; noting it as the underlying design question.

## Fix

Delete the placeholder document by hash (`4be8b2f3...`), leaving the real one. Then update nexus-chr25 and nexus-q2wif to cite by title again instead of by hash-plus-warning, since the ambiguity would be gone.

Do NOT delete by title — that is exactly the operation that cannot disambiguate.

title: Orchestration Gap 1: expectations_expect is unavailable in some sessions, so named background agents ship undeclared and the RDR-184 audit returns empty instead of flagging
description:
FILED PER THE RDR-184 ESCALATION RULE, not as a retro note: "any undeclared background
teammate in a retro -> mechanization bead".

WHAT HAPPENED (session 2026-07-26, nexus-aqbrk substrate port). Two NAMED background
agents were dispatched: `triage-multi` (22 files) and `triage-singles` (24 files). Neither
had an EXPECT row, because `expectations_expect` IS NOT IN THE SESSION'S TOOL LIST. I
checked via ToolSearch before dispatching ("expectations expect census background
teammate") and it returned only TaskStop / TaskOutput / SendMessage / EndConversation. I
proceeded, substituting the directive's SUBSTANCE by hand: unique names, an explicit
completion protocol in each prompt, and shared context seeded to T1 scratch first.

THE AUDIT DOES NOT CATCH THIS, which is the actual defect:

    source tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh
    expectations_undeclared <session_id>   -> (empty)
    expectations_census    <session_id>    -> (empty)

Both return EMPTY, not UNDECLARED. Empty reads identically to "nothing to flag", so a
session that could not declare is indistinguishable from a session with nothing to declare.
The Gap-1 audit is silent in exactly the case it exists to catch, which is the same
false-clean class the port spent today finding in tests (a check that reports OK when its
precondition never held).

TWO THINGS TO FIX, and they are separable:

1. THE AUDIT SHOULD FAIL LOUD ON AN EMPTY CENSUS when the session HAS named background
   dispatches. `expectations_census` already knows the session id; if it can enumerate
   dispatches at all, zero ROWS against >0 named dispatches is a violation, not a pass.
   If it cannot enumerate dispatches independently of EXPECT rows, say so in the output
   ("no rows AND no dispatch source - cannot audit") rather than printing nothing.

2. THE TOOL'S AVAILABILITY IS NOT GUARANTEED. Establish whether `expectations_expect` is
   supposed to be present in every Claude Code session or only where a particular plugin
   is loaded. If the latter, the directive needs a documented fallback (the hand-substituted
   protocol above worked and is auditable from the dispatch prompts) rather than an
   instruction that silently cannot be followed.

NOT A BLOCKER on anything in the 7.0.0 wave. Filed because the escalation rule says a
mechanization bead, and because an audit that cannot distinguish "clean" from "could not
run" will keep reading clean.

GAP 4 (commit-pathspec) BY CONTRAST RAN AND PASSED this session:
    bash tests/e2e/lib/commit_scope_audit.sh 2efd9fee.. tests/ service/ src/nexus/ \
         .github/workflows/ci.yml
    -> 0 FOREIGN FILE(S) across 34 commits, 0 merge commits skipped.
That one works. Model the Gap-1 fix on it.

title: Rationalize content_type: three disjoint vocabularies share one name, and the catalog's is open-ended
description:
Three disjoint vocabularies are all called `content_type`. No two agree, none is authoritative, and the catalog one is open-ended. Surfaced while adding the `bindings` parameter in PR #1425 (nexus-0yrjr), where the question "what is a legal content_type?" turned out to have three different answers.

## The three

1. **`src/nexus/metadata_schema.py:118`** — `CONTENT_TYPES: frozenset = {"code", "pdf", "markdown", "prose"}`. Chunk-metadata validation; `validate_chunk_metadata` raises on anything outside it. Docstring says it "replaces the old overlapping pair (store_type, category)" — so this vocabulary has already been consolidated once.

2. **`src/nexus/corpus.py:20`** — `_CONTENT_TYPES = ("code", "docs", "rdr", "knowledge")`. The RDR-103 collection-name prefix in `<content_type>__<owner_id>__<embedding_model>__v<n>`. Structurally constrained: these become physical collection names.

3. **The catalog `content_type` column** — open-ended, no validation anywhere. Live distribution (full scan of ~1000 catalog rows, 2026-07-26): `code` 802, `prose` 138, `rdr` 59, `blog_post` 1, plus `paper` and `knowledge` observed via catalog search. Grows whenever something is indexed with a new value.

## Overlap

| value | metadata_schema | corpus prefix | catalog |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | yes | yes | yes |
| prose | yes | — | yes |
| rdr | — | yes | yes |
| knowledge | — | yes | yes |
| pdf | yes | — | — |
| markdown | yes | — | — |
| docs | — | yes | — |
| paper | — | — | yes |
| blog_post | — | — | yes |

Only `code` appears in all three.

## Why it bites

`query(content_type=...)` and `search_metadata_scoped(content_type=...)` filter vocabulary **3**. `metadata_schema.validate_chunk_metadata` enforces vocabulary **1**. A caller who reads `CONTENT_TYPES` — the only one that looks canonical, being a module-level exported frozenset — and passes `pdf` or `markdown` to a retrieval filter gets zero rows, silently, because neither value exists in the catalog.

Concretely already wrong in-tree: builtin plan `type-scoped-search`'s own description says "code, paper, rdr, knowledge", which omits `prose` — the SECOND most common catalog value at 138 documents. Anyone following that description to scope a search silently excludes 138 documents. The `TYPED_BINDING_DOMAINS` hint added in PR #1425 originally copied that same wrong list; it was rephrased as open-ended examples rather than a closed set, which is a mitigation, not a fix.

## Why PR #1425 deliberately did NOT validate

`nx_answer(bindings={"content_type": ...})` accepts any value without checking. That was a deliberate call, recorded here so it is not mistaken for an oversight: validating against vocabulary 1 would reject `rdr` and `paper`; validating against vocabulary 2 would reject `prose` and `paper`; validating against a snapshot of vocabulary 3 would reject the next new type someone indexes. There is no set to validate against until this bead is resolved. The consequence is that a caller passing a nonsense `content_type` gets an empty retrieval — an explicit caller choice rather than a system-invented value, which is the improvement, but it is not the end state.

## What resolving this looks like (not yet decided)

- Decide whether the catalog vocabulary SHOULD be closed. If yes, enumerate it, validate at registration, and migrate the strays. If no, say so explicitly and stop shipping error messages and plan descriptions that imply a closed set.
- Decide whether these are genuinely one concept under three names, or three different concepts that should stop sharing the name `content_type` (a chunk's media type, a collection's routing prefix, and a document's kind are arguably not the same thing — if so, RENAMING two of them is the fix, not unifying the values).
- If a closed catalog set emerges, `TYPED_BINDING_DOMAINS` in `src/nexus/plans/schema.py` should read from it rather than carrying a prose hint, and `nx_answer`'s `bindings` should validate against it.

## Related

- nexus-0yrjr / PR #1425 — where this surfaced.
- RDR-103 — owns the collection-name shape (vocabulary 2).
- RDR-189 (draft) — its answer-object-family work would want a real typed-binding schema; this is the same "our types are prose, not types" problem one layer down.

title: 35 integration/stress tests fail on BOTH substrates — pre-existing rot in the integration scope, invisible because default addopts deselects it
description:
FOUND BY the nexus-aqbrk integration-scope triage (2026-07-26). NOT substrate-port debt — these
fail identically on the SQLite arm, so they predate the port and are unrelated to it.

WHY NOBODY HAS SEEN THEM. pyproject.toml addopts is
    -m 'not integration and not slow and not stress'
so the entire 559-test integration/slow/stress scope is deselected from every default `uv run
pytest` run, and CI inherits that. The scope is only exercised deliberately (`-m integration`,
which CLAUDE.md documents as excluded from CI and "your last line of defense" at release time).
This bead is that defense reporting in.

MEASURED, sqlite arm, 2026-07-26:
    uv run pytest tests/ -q -p no:randomly -o addopts="-m 'integration or slow or stress'"
    -> 30 failed, 391 passed, 132 skipped, 6 errors in 490.94s

The 36 failures/errors intersected with the engine arm's 121 give 35 common — this bead.
(The 36th, tests/benchmarks/test_retrieval_drift_gate.py::test_ndcg_drift_gate, is sqlite-ONLY
and is called out separately below.)

THE 35, by file:
   8  tests/stress/test_t2_daemon_stress.py
   5  tests/db/test_http_chash_integration.py
   5  tests/db/test_http_catalog_integration.py
   4  tests/db/test_write_seam_gate_integration.py
   4  tests/db/test_http_combined_query_integration.py
   2  tests/test_integration.py
   2  tests/db/test_indexer_seam_b_integration.py
   1  tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py
   1  tests/db/test_xnz0o_commands_integration.py  (TestNoSQLiteAccess::test_db_property_raises_runtime_error)
   1  tests/db/test_frecency_enehl_integration.py
   1  tests/db/test_coverage_3cwnx_integration.py
   1  tests/db/test_catalog_consumer_qnp5s_integration.py

PLUS ONE ODDITY worth its own look: test_ndcg_drift_gate fails on SQLite but PASSES on the engine
substrate. A retrieval-quality drift gate that only trips on the substrate being retired is either
a stale baseline or a real signal about the local path. Do not assume stale.

TRIAGE NOT YET DONE. These were partitioned by substrate, not diagnosed. Before any fixing, sort
them into: (a) needs credentials/live services not present on this box (.env has CHROMA_API_KEY +
VOYAGE_API_KEY set but the runs did not source it), (b) genuinely rotted since the scope was last
exercised, (c) obsolete tests of retired machinery that should be deleted with their subject.
Category (a) is not a defect and should end in a self-provisioning gate or a skip with a
non-vacuity assert, per the standing rule that gates are scripted, never ambient.

RELEASE RELEVANCE. CLAUDE.md's release checklist step 1 requires `uv run pytest -m integration`
green before a cut. On this box, today, it is not. Whoever cuts 7.0.0 will hit this; better to
know now than at the gate.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
TRIAGE DONE 2026-07-26. The three categories the bead asked for, with the dominant cause PROVEN rather than inferred. 30 failed + 6 errored on the sqlite arm; 35 intersect the engine arm (this bead's set).

=== (a) ENVIRONMENT / HARNESS — NOT ROT: 10 ===

DOMINANT CAUSE, and it is BY DESIGN. 7 tests die on:

  ManagedServiceIncompatible: managed nexus service at http://127.0.0.1:NNNNN
  reported no usable release_version on /version (got None) — a dev/unstamped
  or pre-release engine is older than the minimum this client supports (v0.1.56)

Proven, not guessed: the built jar (service/target/nexus-service-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar)
contains NO release.properties, and the source resource says why in its own comment —

  'Left BLANK in source / on dev + workflow_dispatch builds: VersionHandler then
   reports release_version=null on /version, and an RDR-002 version-pin consumer
   fail-closes — an engine with no stamped release is by definition not a release
   >= the required floor.'

VersionHandler.resolveReleaseVersion() reads ONLY that bundled resource — there is

title: [bug] set_alias is a catalog WRITE that is not on CATALOG_WRITE_OPS — unroutable through the daemon shim, and in service mode it lands on the READER handle
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk auditing the dies-roster (test_catalog_cli.py::TestVerifyCommand::test_verify_excludes_alias_rows).

Catalog.set_alias (catalog.py:1735) mutates: it appends a DocumentAliased event and the projector writes the row (catalog_writes.py:409 -> projector.py:350). HttpCatalogClient.set_alias (http_catalog_client.py:1141) exists too. But "set_alias" is NOT in CATALOG_WRITE_OPS (daemon/catalog_write_shim.py), which has two consequences that pull in opposite directions:

SQLITE MODE: make_catalog_writer() returns a CatalogWriter whose __getattr__ forwards only whitelisted names, so set_alias is not reachable through the writer AT ALL. A caller holding a writer cannot alias. A caller holding a READER can call it — and gets "sqlite3.OperationalError: attempt to write a readonly database", because make_catalog_reader opens mode=ro (RDR-146 P1.2). So on SQLite the operation is simply unreachable through the typed factories; it works only from a directly-constructed writable Catalog.

SERVICE MODE: make_catalog_reader() returns _SharedServiceCatalogHandle, which proxies EVERY attribute to the shared HttpCatalogClient. So reader.set_alias(...) succeeds — a WRITE, through the object the factory calls a reader, bypassing the write whitelist and the daemon single-writer discipline entirely.

So the same call is unreachable-through-the-writer on one substrate and silently-permitted-through-the-reader on the other. Neither is what the RDR-146 typed-factory split was for: the whole point of make_catalog_reader / make_catalog_writer is that the type tells you what you can do.

NOT ESTABLISHED — and this determines the fix, so it needs answering first:
  1. Is set_alias meant to be routable? If yes it belongs in CATALOG_WRITE_OPS, and the daemon dispatch table gains it for free (_build_dispatch_table resolves every whitelisted op as a bound method).
  2. Or is aliasing deliberately an admin/maintenance operation that should go through make_catalog_admin, like the other deep-maintenance verbs?
  3. Separately and more broadly: should _SharedServiceCatalogHandle proxy writes at all? Today it makes "reader" a misnomer in service mode, and any write reachable that way is invisible to the whitelist. A read-only proxy that refuses non-read ops would surface every case of this class at once — there may be others.

(3) is the one worth a sweep regardless of how (1)/(2) land: grep for reader-held mutators.

WORKAROUND meanwhile: tests/_catalog_fixture_ops.unroutable_write_target() returns the service handle in service mode and a directly-constructed writable Catalog on SQLite, so a test can perform the write on either substrate without pretending the factories support it.

title: [question] catalog by_doc_id means two different things on the two substrates — is meta.doc_id still a lookup key, or is the tumbler the only document identity?
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk porting tests/test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py. NOT filed as a bug because which side is right is a CONTRACT question I could not settle from the code.

THE DIVERGENCE. Same method name, two different lookups:

  SQLite  catalog_docs.py:791  by_doc_id(d) -> WHERE json_extract(metadata, '$.doc_id') = d
                               docstring: "Look up catalog entry by T3 doc_id stored in meta.doc_id"
  Service http_catalog_client.py:1075  by_doc_id(d) -> self.resolve(d) -> GET /show?tumbler=d
          engine resolveMany (CatalogRepository:1895) -> WHERE tumbler IN (:docIds)

So on the engine a by_doc_id lookup is a TUMBLER lookup. An entry registered with meta={"doc_id": "doc_abc123"} — which is exactly what the knowledge store hook writes for MCP-stored notes — is unreachable by that key in service mode; by_doc_id returns None with no error.

EVIDENCE FOR EACH SIDE, which is why this is a question:

  FOR the service being right: RDR-108 made the tumbler the document identity, and indexer_utils.py:262 documents the current contract as "by_doc_id keys on the catalog tumbler stored in chunk metadata". search_engine._attach_display_paths feeds resolve_many from chunk metadata doc_id, which under that contract IS a tumbler — so the search path is correct on the engine and the SQLite meta.doc_id lookup is the legacy shape.

  FOR the gap being real: the knowledge hook still writes meta.doc_id, and nothing in service mode can look an entry up by it. If any path resolves a knowledge note from its T3 doc id, that path silently returns nothing on the default substrate.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING:
  1. Is meta.doc_id still a supported lookup key after RDR-108, or is it vestigial data the hook should stop writing?
  2. If supported, the engine needs a metadata->>'doc_id' lookup and by_doc_id must stop aliasing resolve().
  3. If vestigial, the SQLite by_doc_id is the thing that is wrong, and the name should stop suggesting a doc_id lookup — it is by_tumbler.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any production path currently resolves a knowledge entry by meta.doc_id in service mode. The store hook's own idempotency does NOT depend on it (test_idempotent_by_doc_id passes on both substrates, so reconciliation happens by another key). That is the check that would settle the severity.

TEST FALLOUT (3, all asserting the SQLite meta.doc_id semantic):
  test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestByDocId::test_lookup
  test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestByDocId::test_multiple_entries_returns_first
  test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestStorePutHook::test_registers_knowledge_entry

comments.text:
SECOND SITE 2026-07-26 (nexus-aqbrk, commit pending): tests/test_auto_linker.py::TestCatalogAutoLinkIntegration hits the identical divergence, independently of test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py where this bead was filed.

MECHANISM AT THIS SITE: mcp_infra.py::catalog_auto_link(doc_id) locates the just-stored document with cat.by_doc_id(doc_id), where doc_id is a LEGACY meta id ('test-doc-001') written by the store hook as meta={'doc_id': ...} — never a tumbler. So on the service arm resolve() misses, the function logs auto_link_skip_doc_not_in_catalog and returns 0, and NO link is created.

WHY THAT RAISES THE STAKES ON THIS BEAD: this is not only a test-visible divergence. catalog_auto_link is PRODUCTION code on the MCP store_put path. If meta.doc_id is genuinely no longer a lookup key in service mode, then auto-linking from T1 link-context silently creates zero links for every agent-stored document on a migrated install — and the only signal is a DEBUG log line. nexus-a414 already had to make these skips visible once because 'the prior all-DEBUG behaviour silently swallowed every recipe-compliant call that produced zero links'.

I did NOT change production code — which side is right is the contract question this bead exists to settle. The test now asserts AT THE BROKEN VALUE (count == 0, no links) with this bead named, so settling wji11 fails it loudly and points at the assertion to restore.

WHOEVER SETTLES THIS should check the auto-linker path specifically, not just catalog reads: if the answer is 'tumbler is the only identity', then catalog_auto_link needs to be handed a tumbler by its caller rather than a meta id, and that is a production change with user-visible behaviour attached.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
HAL SETTLED THE CONTRACT 2026-07-26: TUMBLER IS THE ONLY DOCUMENT IDENTITY. That matches RDR-108 as stated in AGENTS.md — 'Catalog Documents are graph nodes addressed by tumblers (Document.tumbler); T3 chunks are content-addressed blobs whose natural ID is the FULL sha256(chunk_text)'. So the SERVICE behaviour (resolve by tumbler) is correct and the SQLite meta.doc_id lookup is the legacy one.

THAT TURNS THIS BEAD FROM A QUESTION INTO A DEFECT WITH A CENSUS. by_doc_id has SIX production call sites, and the ones that pass a CHUNK id are already broken on the service arm TODAY — silently, because every one of them treats None as 'not found' rather than 'lookup unsupported':

  1 catalog/store_hook.py:167   reader.by_doc_id(doc_id)   comment says it outright:
      'Dedup by chunk_chroma_id stored in legacy meta.doc_id.'
      SERVICE IMPACT: the dedup NEVER FIRES -> a re-store of identical content
      mints a SECOND catalog Document instead of reusing the existing one.
      This is adjacent to the nexus-b6enc ghost/duplicate-row class.
  2 catalog/store_hook.py:384   reader.by_doc_id(chash_doc_id)  — argument NAMED
      for what it is. The delete path's lookup misses in service mode.
  3 mcp_infra.py:678            the auto-linker. Zero links created for every
      agent-stored document on a migrated install; DEBUG line is the only signal
      (the exact silence nexus-a414 already had to fix once).
  4 commands/store.py:359       loops doc_ids -> by_doc_id for the tombstone reap
  5 commands/collection.py:35   single lookup
  6 search_engine.py:259        legacy per-doc loop (has a resolve_many fast path
      above it, so this is the fallback leg only)

Sites 4-6 need their callers' id PROVENANCE checked before classifying — I traced
1-3 to a chunk/chash id by reading, and did NOT trace 4-6 to a definite source.

WHAT THE FIX SHAPE NOW IS, given the settled contract: pass the TUMBLER, not the
chash. At the auto-link site that is a one-word change — mcp/core.py:2659 already
has BOTH ids in scope (catalog_doc_id = the tumbler from catalog_store_hook_tracked;
doc_id = the chash from t3.put) and passes the wrong one. The dedup site is harder:
it needs a tumbler it does not have yet, so 'dedup by content identity' has to be
re-expressed against something the service can answer (by_source_uri? a chash->doc
manifest lookup?), which is a design decision, not a rename.

I have NOT made any production change. Six sites with user-visible behaviour
attached is not a test-port edit. Recommend this bead is re-typed from question to
bug, re-prioritised (the dedup and auto-link impacts are user-visible on every
migrated install), and scoped as its own arc.

Test-side meanwhile: tests/test_auto_linker.py asserts the CURRENT broken value
with this bead named, so the fix fails it loudly.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
COMPLETE CALL-SITE CENSUS 2026-07-26 (all 6 traced to their id SOURCE, by reading, not inferring). The result changes the shape of the fix: by_doc_id is OVERLOADED — different callers pass DIFFERENT KEY TYPES, and each substrate implements only ONE of them. Neither side is uniformly right; each satisfies a different half of the callers.

=== CLASS A — passes a CHASH (chunk id). Broken on SERVICE. 4 sites ===

 A1 catalog/store_hook.py:167   by_doc_id(doc_id) where doc_id = chunk_chroma_id.
      Comment: 'Dedup by chunk_chroma_id stored in legacy meta.doc_id.'
      SERVICE IMPACT: dedup never fires -> re-storing identical content mints a
      SECOND catalog Document. Adjacent to the nexus-b6enc duplicate-row class.
 A2 catalog/store_hook.py:384   by_doc_id(chash_doc_id) — named for what it is.
      SERVICE IMPACT: the delete path's lookup misses.
 A3 mcp_infra.py:678            the auto-linker; mcp/core.py:2659 passes doc_id
      (= t3.put's return, a chash) while catalog_doc_id (the TUMBLER) is in scope
      two lines up. SERVICE IMPACT: zero links for every agent-stored doc.
 A4 commands/store.py:359       _reap_catalog_for_doc_ids(ids). Both feeders are
      T3 chunk ids: --id -> db.delete_by_id, --title -> db.find_ids_by_title. The
      command's own docstring says 'T3 chunk natural IDs are content-derived (the
      full sha256(text) hexdigest)'.
      SERVICE IMPACT: the post-delete catalog tombstone reap NEVER FIRES — exactly
      the 'eventual consistency surprised users who expected delete to be atomic'
      the function exists to prevent, and a re-break of nexus-kmo9h's intent
      ('the old gate silently skipped the reap on every fresh service-mode box').

=== CLASS B — passes a TUMBLER. Broken on SQLITE, CORRECT on service. 2 sites ===

 B1 commands/collection.py:35 (_doc_id_to_file_path, called from :551). The id is
      meta['doc_id'] or chash_to_doc[chash] — and the manifest's doc_id column IS
      the tumbler ('documents.tumbler -> document_chunks.doc_id', AGENTS.md).
      Post-RDR-108 chunks carry no meta doc_id, so the manifest path is the live
      one. SQLITE IMPACT: json_extract(metadata,'$.doc_id') = <tumbler> never
      matches, so nx collection reindex treats every post-prune chunk as
      sourceless and the safety check always fires. Conservative, but wrong.
 B2 search_engine.py:259 — the legacy per-doc loop, fed by
      _attach_doc_ids_from_catalog, which resolves chash -> manifest doc_id
      (a TUMBLER). EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE: it is the fallback for catalogs
      lacking resolve_many(), and BOTH substrates define it (catalog.py:1912,
      http_catalog_client.py:1078). Dead leg — which is why nobody noticed it is
      SQLite-broken.

=== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX ===

'Make the service support meta.doc_id' would fix Class A and leave Class B broken
on SQLite. 'Tumbler is the only identity' (Hal, settled) is the right call, and it
makes the work: migrate the four Class-A callers off chash keys. A3 is nearly a
one-word change (the tumbler is already in scope). A1 is the hard one — dedup by
CONTENT identity needs a key the service can answer (by_source_uri? a chash->doc
manifest lookup?), which is design, not rename. A2/A4 need the same: a chash->doc
resolution step before the catalog lookup.

Once Class A is migrated, by_doc_id has only tumbler-passing callers and should
collapse into resolve() — at which point the SQLite meta.doc_id branch can go, and
B1/B2 are fixed for free.

CONFIDENCE: A1-A4 and B1 traced to a definite source. B2's key type is traced;
its unreachability is inferred from both substrates defining resolve_many, which
I verified by grep but did not confirm at runtime.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
WORK SCOPED OUT to nexus-5axey (2026-07-26). This bead keeps the CONTRACT RECORD — question asked, and Hal's answer: tumbler is the only document identity, consistent with RDR-108. nexus-5axey carries the 6-site census, the migration plan, and the N>1 decision the dedup needs.

ALSO ANSWERED THERE, since Hal raised it: why NOT a polymorphic by_doc_id accepting either chash or tumbler. Because chash -> document is ONE-TO-MANY (AGENTS.md: 'Identical chunk text in the same collection collapses to one T3 row by design; the manifest preserves position via (doc_id, position) rows pointing at the shared chash'), so a chash cannot back a single-valued accessor. A polymorphic version would need different CARDINALITY per key type — entry vs list — which is a different method, not polymorphism, and would re-create exactly the overload that caused this bug.

The primitive for the chash side already exists on both substrates and is parity-registered: docs_for_chashes(chashes) -> dict[chash, [doc_id, ...]]. Its dict-of-LISTS shape IS the one-to-many relation, and it was hardened once already for shape parity (nexus-h8rf6.3).

Suggest closing this bead once 5axey lands, or keeping it open as the contract citation — Hal's preference.

title: [bug] T2 daemon cannot start when any store is service-backed — _build_dispatch_table's bare getattr trips the fail-loud .conn guard
description:
FOUND BY nexus-aqbrk (RDR-158/155 substrate port), starting a real T2 daemon under the engine substrate.

  src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:747, inside _build_dispatch_table:

    for attr_name in dir(store):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        ...
        candidate = getattr(store, attr_name)      # <- bare, no default

  dir(HttpMemoryStore) includes the RawHandleGuardMixin "conn" property. It does not start with "_", so the loop calls getattr(store, "conn"), the guard raises AttributeError by design, and it propagates out of daemon start():

    AttributeError: HttpMemoryStore is service-backed and has no raw SQLite 'conn'.
      at t2_daemon.py:747 in _build_dispatch_table
      at t2_daemon.py:1088 in start

  "_lock" is spared only because it starts with an underscore.

THE GUARD IS BEHAVING CORRECTLY. _raw_handle_guard's docstring is explicit that it raises AttributeError (never RuntimeError) precisely so hasattr / has_raw_access keep returning False. dir()-driven enumeration therefore has to use the defaulted form — which the very next loop in the same function already does for t2db (getattr(t2db, method_name, None)). The store loop just did not.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and why this is filed rather than patched: what SHOULD the T2 daemon do when its stores are service-backed? It exists to be the SQLite single-writer. Options:
  (a) getattr(..., None) and skip — daemon starts with a dispatch table missing the raw-handle ops. Silent partial function; may be exactly right if the remaining ops are all it needs.
  (b) refuse to start with a clear "T2 daemon is not applicable in service mode" — honest, but breaks any caller that starts it unconditionally.
  (c) never construct it in service mode — moves the decision up to the caller.
(a) is a one-word change and (b)/(c) are behaviour changes. Picking (a) reflexively is how a daemon ends up half-working in a mode nobody tested.

REACHABILITY. Not test-only in principle: any install where a T2 store resolves to SERVICE while something starts the T2 daemon hits this. Whether that combination occurs on a real install today has NOT been established — worth checking before assigning priority. Filed P2 on that uncertainty; raise it if a real path is found.

WORKAROUND IN THE MEANTIME: tests/catalog/test_catalog_factory.py pins NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite for its daemon-routed leg (it tests the local writer, so it needs the local T2 it always assumed).
close_reason: Queue-triage sweep 2026-08-19 (Sam-authorized, 8-agent verify-or-flag fleet, verified against develop @ 33d0c453e): SUPERSEDED. Evidence: src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py no longer exists — T2 daemon retired (nexus-i711w Stage 2B / RDR-158); the _build_dispatch_table code is gone

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REACH IS LARGER THAN THIS BEAD ESTIMATES (nexus-aqbrk, 2026-07-25). Filed with "whether that combination occurs on a real install has NOT been established" and P2 on that uncertainty. In the test world it is not marginal at all: this defect is the bulk of an 89-failure cluster.

Running tests/daemon/ under the engine substrate, before pinning: 89 failed / 582 passed, 327 seconds. The dominant shapes were "daemon did not start" and "daemon did not start within 15 s" — every one of them this bead: T2Daemon.start() -> _build_dispatch_table -> dir(store) + bare getattr -> the fail-loud .conn guard on HttpMemoryStore. The tests were burning their full timeouts waiting for a daemon that could never come up. After pinning the suite to a local T2: 676 passed, 59 seconds. The 268-second difference IS this defect.

That does not settle the production question — the daemon suite constructs the mixed state deliberately, and whether a real install ever has a service-backed store while something starts the T2 daemon is still open. But two things are now firmer:

1. The failure mode is not theoretical or timing-dependent. It is deterministic and total: start() raises, every time, on any service-backed store.
2. It fails SLOWLY from the caller's side. Callers do not see the AttributeError — they see a daemon that never becomes reachable and then a timeout. If this ever fires in production, it will present as "the T2 daemon is hanging", not as "the T2 daemon crashed on a bad getattr", and the traceback naming the cause will be in the daemon's own log rather than in front of whoever is debugging.

(2) is the argument for raising priority even before the production-reachability question is answered: the diagnosis cost is high and the fix (option (a), the defaulted getattr the very next loop in the same function already uses) is one word. The design question this bead correctly refuses to guess at — whether a service-mode T2 daemon should start with a partial table, refuse, or never be constructed — is unchanged and still needs Hal.
