title: SessionStart passive check: warn when the working tree's plugin surface differs from the INSTALLED pinned copy
description:
Raised by the substantive critic on a4fbe2f7 (2026-07-25) as an option that was MISSING from the four I gave Hal on nexus-ut7ek. Recording the omission rather than burying it: the decision surface I enumerated was incomplete, and this alternative is arguably more responsive to the actual problem than the one chosen.

THE GAP IT CLOSES. The ledger (conexus/PENDING_RELEASE.md + tests/test_plugin_release_drift_ledger.py, shipped 156ebfe3) makes inert plugin changes VISIBLE, but only to someone who runs pytest or opens the file. It does not fire at the moment of risk — session start, before any subagent is dispatched. The 2026-07-25 incident was an agent running `git stash -u` believing a guard was live; nothing in the ledger design would have interrupted that.

THE PROPOSAL. A passive, read-only SessionStart check: when cwd is the nexus repo, diff $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT's behavioural surface against the working tree and inject additionalContext — 'N behavioural files in your working tree differ from the pinned plugin you are running'.

WHY IT IS NOT THE REJECTED DOGFOOD OPTION (option 2 on nexus-ut7ek). It re-registers NOTHING and re-executes NOTHING. It emits information. So it does not reproduce nexus-3h0u6 (dual registration -> duplicated START/REPORTED rows -> 2x census inflation), and it does not double the routing-hook latency against the RDR-121 300ms budget. That distinction is the whole reason it deserved to be on the original options list.

PRECEDENT EXISTS: conexus/hooks/scripts/version_lockstep_hook.py already detects plugin/CLI version skew at SessionStart, is documented fail-safe (NEVER wedges synchronous SessionStart, NEVER raises, exit 0), and could host this.

CHICKEN-AND-EGG TO RESOLVE FIRST: the check would itself live in conexus/hooks/, i.e. inside the pinned surface — so it only starts working one release AFTER it ships. Not fatal (it is a one-time cost, same as any hook) but it must be stated in the implementation, or it becomes another believed-live-but-inert guard, which would be the fourth instance of this class in a single day.

STRICTLY ADDITIVE to the ledger, not a replacement: the ledger gates the PR path in CI, this warns at the session path.

title: Stale service JAR silently costs a full suite run: make the freshness check a precondition, not a discipline
description:
Third occurrence in ONE day (2026-07-25). Each costs a full ~13-minute suite run plus the time spent misreading 73 errors as real failures.

MECHANISM. tests/db/_service_fixture.py::jar_freshness_skip_reason compares service/target/nexus-service-1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar mtime against the service/ sources and fails LOUD ("service jar is STALE") — per test, at fixture time, 73 times. That is the right behaviour for a single targeted run. It is the WRONG ergonomics for a full suite: the whole run completes, reports 73 errors, and the operator has to recognise the signature and start over.

OCCURRENCES TODAY:
1. Morning full suite — 73 errors after the asaod merge changed TaxonomyHandler.java. Diagnosed from the handoff note, rebuilt, re-ran.
2. Post-review full suite — same, after the H1 /import_batch fix touched TaxonomyHandler.java + HttpUtil.java.
3. The immediately following run was started WITHOUT rebuilding again and had to be killed mid-flight.

The session handoff document warned about this explicitly in its workflow-lessons section ("ALWAYS check the JAR timestamp before interpreting engine-substrate failures; this cost real time"). It was read at session start and the failure still recurred twice. That is the evidence that a documented discipline is not a mechanism — same conclusion as nexus-1e2eh, one layer down.

FIX SHAPES, cheapest first:
  (a) SESSION-SCOPED PREFLIGHT: a single autouse session fixture (or a conftest hook) that checks JAR freshness ONCE at collection and fails the run immediately with the rebuild command, instead of 73 identical per-test errors 13 minutes later. Turns a wasted run into a 2-second stop.
  (b) AUTO-REBUILD: same check, but shells `mvn -f service/pom.xml package -DskipTests` when stale. Convenient but slow and surprising inside a test run; probably wrong by default, maybe behind NX_AUTOBUILD_JAR=1.
  (c) A pre-push / pre-suite script wrapper that rebuilds when service/ is dirty relative to the JAR.

(a) is the one that matches the actual failure — the information already exists at fixture time, it is just delivered too late and too many times to act on cheaply.

RELATED: nexus-1e2eh (documented procedure rot), nexus-eqxxh (CI has no JAR at all, so these tests SKIP there — meaning CI would not have caught any of this either).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] remediate tool's fail-closed consent audit rests on an always-true hasattr check
description:
Found incidentally by the nexus-at2ff handle-shape sweep, 2026-07-25. NOT FIXED.

src/nexus/mcp/core.py:6326 guards with `if not hasattr(_db.telemetry, "record_consent")`. record_consent is present on BOTH Telemetry (SQLite) and HttpTelemetryStore (service), so the condition is structurally always False and the guarded branch is unreachable.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND DEAD CODE: this is the version-skew guard behind the `remediate` tool FAIL-CLOSED consent-audit claim. That tool documents (RDR-182 P3.2, five-layer contract) that it refuses to release its recovery playbook if the consent audit cannot be written — specifically naming a pre-nexus-ng2sy engine without the consents route as the case it fail-closes on. If the skew check can never fire, the fail-closed guarantee is not enforced by this check; it rests on whatever the call itself raises.

TO ESTABLISH: does HttpTelemetryStore.record_consent RAISE against an engine lacking the consents route (in which case the contract holds via the exception path and only the hasattr is redundant), or does it swallow/return? If it swallows, the tool releases its playbook unaudited — the exact thing the contract says never happens.

That determination decides severity: redundant-guard cleanup (low) vs a broken fail-closed security contract (high). Do NOT close this by deleting the hasattr until the raise-vs-swallow question is answered.

RELATED: RDR-182, nexus-ng2sy, nexus-at2ff sweep.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] plan-cache staleness tier is DEAD in production: mtime probe reads a .path only the SQLite PlanLibrary has
description:
Found by the nexus-at2ff handle-shape sweep, 2026-07-25. DOCUMENTED but NOT FIXED — the code now declares the behaviour instead of misdescribing it; the tier is still inert.

src/nexus/mcp/plan_cache_registry.py:62 does getattr(library, "path", None) and returns 0.0 when absent. PlanLibrary (SQLite) sets .path; HttpPlanLibrary does NOT. populate_from is called with db.plans (mcp/core.py), which IS HttpPlanLibrary in service mode — the production default. So the mtime is ALWAYS 0.0, the staleness comparison at :163-165 can never fire, and the only surviving condition is `not self._populated`.

CONSEQUENCE: the T1 plan-session cache is populated ONCE per MCP process and never refreshed. nexus-qgjr shipped a repopulate-on-change tier that has never functioned in production. A plan edited or added by another process is invisible to a running MCP server for the life of that process.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the docstring described the no-path case as covering "in-memory or test-stub libraries" — framing the ONLY production case as an abstract edge case. Same self-concealing shape as the rest of the at2ff class.

NOT SILENTLY "FIXED": the service backend has no file mtime to read and inventing one would be worse than 0.0. The behaviour is now stated in the docstring plus a debug log line (plan_cache_staleness_unavailable) so it is observable rather than assumed-working.

WHAT A REAL FIX NEEDS: a server-side change so the client has something to compare. Options — an ETag or Last-Modified on the plan-list endpoint; or a cheap monotonic plan-library version/counter the client can poll. Either is an ENGINE change and rides an engine-service tag. Decide whether the staleness tier is worth that, or whether populate-once-per-process is acceptable and nexus-qgjr should be closed as superseded.

RELATED: nexus-qgjr (shipped the tier), nexus-at2ff (the sweep that found it), nexus-cwtwx (the structural blind spot).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED f3b02373 — the tier is now live in production for the first time.

WHY A TTL AND NOT REAL CHANGE DETECTION (investigated, not assumed): the Java plans service was read route by route — save/get/delete/disable/enable/set_scope_tags/list_active/search/list/exists/metrics/import*. NONE returns a cheap change signal: no ETag, no Last-Modified, no version counter. list_active and list return the FULL row set, so polling either costs the same as just repopulating. Adding a signal is an ENGINE change = tag + cross-team deploy relay, which the bead ruled out for today.

So: UNBOUNDED staleness -> BOUNDED staleness, stated plainly in the docstrings rather than dressed up as change detection. Two signals coexist, chosen per library — has .path (SQLite) keeps nexus-qgjr exact mtime detection UNCHANGED; no .path (HttpPlanLibrary, the production default) repopulates at least once per 90s. Constant is named, with its reasoning recorded, on time.monotonic() so NTP/DST cannot perturb the window.

THE SUBTLE PART, easy to get wrong: the branch keys on whether .path EXISTS, not on whether the mtime came back 0.0. A SQLite library whose stat() raises OSError ALSO returns 0.0, and must stay on the mtime branch rather than silently inheriting the TTL. Keying on the return value conflates them.

NOT FLAGGED BY THE BEAD, worth carrying: populate() runs while HOLDING the registry lock, so this turns a once-per-process lock-held expensive operation into a RECURRING one every 90s. With ~17 plans in the live library that is a short stall and the lock discipline is unchanged — but it recurs now, and should be MEASURED rather than assumed if the plan count grows.

Mutation-verified independently of the agent that wrote it, mutation confirmed to land first: collapsing has_mtime_signal to True fails the TTL test exactly as predicted (current_mtime > 0.0 is never true for a path-less library, so staleness never re-fires). Tests drive an HttpPlanLibrary-SHAPED double with no .path — the production shape; a SQLite-shaped test would reproduce the original blind spot. 146 passed on the plan-cache surface.

STILL OPEN, separately: a real server-side change signal (ETag or version counter on a plan-listing route) would replace bounded staleness with exact detection. That is an engine change and needs its own bead if wanted.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP 8a8ce284 — the lock-contention half, flagged by BOTH stacked reviewers on the original fix.

f3b02373 made the populate RECURRING but left it inside `with self._lock:`, and populate does an HTTP round-trip + one ONNX embed per active plan. Every concurrent MCP tool call touching plan matching blocked behind the repopulating thread, for its full duration, once every 90s. Pre-f3b02373 this was once-per-process, which is why the granularity never mattered — making the refresh recurring turned a one-time stall into a permanent rhythm. The critic noted the original commit ADMITTED the risk and attached no test or metric; a disclosed risk with no tripwire is still undefended.

DESIGN DECISION: concurrent arrivals return the STALE-BUT-USABLE cache immediately rather than blocking. The contract is already bounded staleness, so ~90s-old data is exactly what the caller signed up for; blocking would trade a correct-and-instant answer for the same answer delivered late. It also avoids a thundering herd — "wait then repopulate" gives every waiter its own populate the moment the first finishes.

THREE INVARIANTS, each mutation-verified with the mutation confirmed to land first:
- _populating cleared UNCONDITIONALLY (success AND failure). Clearing only on success deadlocks the cache PERMANENTLY — every later caller sees _populating=True and never repopulates. No retry clears it.
- single-flight actually holds (ignoring the flag lets duplicate populates run).
- an epoch guard keeps clear() coherent with an in-flight populate.

The original failure-path behaviour is preserved deliberately: _populated/_mtime/_last_populate_monotonic stay unchanged on failure so the next call retries. That documents a real prior bug where try/finally permanently suppressed populate failures — easy to reintroduce while restructuring around a new finally.

Verified DIRECTLY, not only via tests: with a slow populate in flight, another thread CAN take the registry lock. Without that the change would be cosmetic.

PROVENANCE worth recording: the subagent died on an API error mid-verification and left its OWN mutation C applied in the tree — `self._populating = False  # MUTATION-C: only cleared on success` — i.e. the deadlock above, contradicting the comment three lines higher. Its test caught it. Reverted, remaining mutations completed, grep confirmed no other markers survived. 278 passed on the surface.

title: storage_boundary_lint is blind to handle PROVENANCE: ._client/._client_for allowlisted by FILE, not by which handle arrives — the structural cause of the at2ff class
description:
STRUCTURAL ROOT of the nexus-at2ff bug class. Today that class produced SEVEN confirmed live defects across two independent sweeps, and the lint that exists to prevent exactly this could not see any of them.

THE BLIND SPOT. storage_boundary_lint.CLIENT_FOR_ALLOWLIST_PREFIXES (GH #1373, hard-enforced at baseline 0) allowlists ``._client_for`` by the FILE the call appears in — src/nexus/db/. It says nothing about WHICH HANDLE arrives at that call. So a db/-internal helper invoked from commands/ with a make_t3() handle is invisible to the lint BY CONSTRUCTION. That is exactly src/nexus/db/t3_reidentify.py:145, which made `nx t3 reidentify` error on every collection.

THE CLASS, for the record. Production code assumes an attribute that exists only on a TEST double or a retired implementation:
  - production make_t3() -> HttpVectorClient (no ._client, no ._client_for)
  - T3Database (test facade, injected client) HAS both
Combined with a broad except that reads the resulting AttributeError as an ENVIRONMENT condition ("T3 unavailable — skip"), the failure is invisible: the code silently does nothing while the suite proves it works, because the suite runs the handle shape that has the attribute.

CONFIRMED INSTANCES FIXED 2026-07-25 (a23b2aa3 + the review round): catalog_links.py:195,381; mcp/catalog.py:640; catalog/orphan_backfill.py:130,662; catalog_cmds/orphan_backfill.py:345; db/migrations.py:2705 (an UPGRADE BLOCKER — every collection SKIPPED, then a hard fail outside the loop except, so `nx upgrade` said "will retry" for a retry that could never succeed); db/t3_reidentify.py:145.

THREE TESTS WERE FOUND ENCODING THE BUGGY SHAPE — this is the load-bearing part. tests/test_catalog.py (mock_t3 = MagicMock(); mock_t3._client = t3) and tests/test_projection_quality.py (class _StubT3: self._client = client) both constructed a wrapper that has NEVER existed in production, so they asserted the validation works against the one shape that has the attribute. A test fixture encoding a non-existent handle shape is how this class survives review. Both de-wrapped.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THE CLASS (the decision this bead exists for):
  (a) A Protocol on make_t3() return + mypy enforcement, so a call to an attribute outside the protocol is a type error at the CALL SITE regardless of which file it lives in.
  (b) A DATAFLOW-keyed lint: track handles originating from make_t3()/get_t3() and flag private-attribute access on them, wherever the access appears.
  (c) Accept and rely on review — rejected by evidence: two independent sweeps today, one seeded with the answer, and neither found all instances on the first pass.

(a) is likely cheaper and stronger than (b) and composes with the existing type hints. Needs a call.

RELATED: nexus-at2ff (closed, instance fixes); GH #1373 (the ._client_for hard-enforcement whose allowlist shape is the gap).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CLOSED — tests/test_private_handle_access_census.py (538905c8).

DESIGN DECISIONS, recorded so the next person does not relitigate them:
1. Counts NON-self receivers ONLY. 78 of 85 raw ._client/._client_for matches in src/ are `self._client` — ordinary encapsulation. Counting them would bury the 7 real sites in noise and the census would be abandoned as unusable within a week.
2. Census over DATAFLOW. Five of the nine defects arrived as function PARAMETERS (t3_db._client, db._client_for) and one receiver was named just `db`. Local dataflow analysis would have missed most of them; receiver identity is the wrong thing to chase. The ACT — one object reaching into another private client handle — is what is frozen.
3. Census over Protocol+mypy. The repo has NO mypy (verified: absent from pyproject.toml and all workflows). Introducing it to a 13k-test codebase to close this class is an arc, not a fix. If mypy ever lands, a Protocol on make_t3() return is the stronger check and this census can retire.

Seven surviving sites enumerated, each with the guard that makes it safe (is_service_backed / instance check / T3Database own module). Mutation-verified BOTH ways: reintroducing the original catalog_links bug fails it; a brand-new reach in a census-absent file fails it.

CAVEAT worth knowing: the first mutation attempt silently NO-OPed on a missing anchor and read as "the census has a hole". Every mutation was subsequently verified to land before its result was believed.

title: deployed-engine-version tracker rotted AGAIN, in a new form: canonical nexus/ entry absent, only copy is nexus_active/ at v0.1.41 while cloud runs 0.1.55
description:
RECURRENCE of the exact defect class nexus-dz6b1 / RDR-179 closed. Found 2026-07-25 while cutting engine-service-v0.1.56.

STATE, all verified not inferred:
- Cloud is running 0.1.55 (nx service probe, the live /version handshake — truth, not a cache).
- nexus/deployed-engine-version — the CANONICAL tracker per the shipped design [20277] — DOES NOT EXIST. Both memory_get(project=nexus) and `nx memory get -p nexus` return not-found.
- nexus_active/deployed-engine-version [20742] EXISTS and is the only copy: engine-service-v0.1.41 @ 2026-07-14. That is SIX tags behind live (0.1.41 -> .44 .49 .50 .52 .53 .54 .55).

WHY THIS IS THE SAME BUG WEARING A NEW HAT. The dz6b1 design memo opens: "T2 nexus/deployed-engine-version rotted (sat at v0.1.17 while 0.1.18/19/22 deployed), poisoning a duoak.1 plan-audit." The mechanization shipped `nx service record-deploy`, which guards the VALUE with a live /version read before writing. It writes project="nexus" (service_cmd.py:147-148; tests/test_service_cmd.py:266 pins that). But the operational writes have been landing in project="nexus_active" instead, so:
  (a) the guarded writer and the read-in-practice tracker are in DIFFERENT namespaces, and
  (b) the canonical entry is now absent entirely, so a reader who follows the design finds nothing while a reader who stumbles on nexus_active finds a six-tag-stale answer.

The skill itself documents the surviving hole: "this guards the VALUE (no wrong version can be recorded); it does NOT force the step to run... the original v0.1.17-stale-across-three-deploys incident was an OMISSION, not a fat-finger." That is exactly what recurred. The namespace split is the NEW half and is not documented anywhere.

BLAST RADIUS IS PLANNING, NOT RELEASE — checked, do not re-derive. scripts/check_engine_release_floor.py (the release skill Step 0 blocking gate) reads the LIVE /version via probe_managed_service, NOT the tracker. So no release can be misjudged by this. The design memo states the tracker has ZERO code consumers; its only readers are agents/humans during planning — which is precisely how the v0.1.17 rot poisoned a duoak.1 plan-audit. A planning agent trusting nexus_active today would believe the cloud is 14 tags of engine work behind where it is.

OPEN QUESTION worth answering before fixing: WHY is nexus/deployed-engine-version absent rather than merely stale? record-deploy writes ttl=0 (permanent), so a successful run should have left a permanent row. Either record-deploy has never been run for real (only against the test fake), or the row was written to a T2 substrate that is no longer the one being read (the SQLite->PG migration is in flight, RDR-158/RDR-186). The nexus_active [20742] content CLAIMS "Local: record-deploy written (live /version-verified)" for v0.1.41 — so it was believed to have run. Resolve this before trusting any fix.

FIX SHAPE (not started):
1. After the v0.1.56 deploy lands, run `nx service record-deploy engine-service-v0.1.56 --commit f59449f1 --gate PASSED`. That recreates the canonical entry with a machine-sourced version.
2. Decide ONE namespace and make the other a pointer or delete it. nexus/ is canonical per the shipped design; nexus_active/ is the 22-entry cross-instance relay namespace and is the wrong home for a durable operational tracker.
3. Consider whether the omission vector can finally be closed — the skill notes "cloud-gate writes the tracker on pass" as the real fix, but that is conexus-side and out of this repo.

RELATED: nexus-dz6b1 (the original mechanization), RDR-179, nexus-1e2eh (release-only procedures rot silently — same family: a step nothing forces gets skipped).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
PARTIAL FIX SHIPPED a797dbd4 — the DETECTION half. The bump itself is still owed and is correctly blocked on the conexus deploy of v0.1.56.

What landed:
- scripts/check_engine_release_floor.py gained check_pin_currency() + newest_published_engine(). The gate now fails when a published engine tag is ahead of REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION, naming both versions, the local-install consequence, and the deploy-first ordering. Runs BEFORE the network probe (local + cheap). Fails CLOSED on unreadable/empty tag lists.
- .github/workflows/release.yml checkout gains fetch-tags: true — without it the gate sees zero tags in CI.
- Governance sweep: the banned compatibility-floor clause removed from AGENTS.md, .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/engine-release/SKILL.md. Past-tense incident narrative deliberately kept.
- 14 tests, all mutation-verified, including a banned-doctrine sweep so the clause cannot return, a positive assertion so DELETING the guidance does not pass, and a non-vacuity test that parses the repo real tags.

Two findings worth carrying forward:
1. The six pre-existing gate tests would have gone VACUOUS — check_floor now fails on pin-currency before reaching the cloud probe, so each would still have passed its assertions for the wrong reason. They are pinned to an explicitly-current pin. Any future check inserted EARLIER in a gate has this same hazard.
2. The fail-closed branch caught a real bug on first run: parse_engine_version takes "0.1.56", not "engine-service-v0.1.56", so every tag failed to parse and the gate reported "zero tags visible". Written to pass on an empty list it would have shipped green and useless.

STILL OPEN on this bead (unchanged):
- The tracker namespace split: record-deploy writes project="nexus" (service_cmd.py:147, pinned by tests/test_service_cmd.py:266) while the only live copy is nexus_active/deployed-engine-version at v0.1.41. Canonical nexus/deployed-engine-version is ABSENT.
- The open question of WHY it is absent rather than stale (ttl=0 should be permanent). Running record-deploy for v0.1.56 after the deploy lands is a free live test of exactly this.
- REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION -> (0,1,56) at the next release.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RESOLVED except for the conexus-side omission vector. 2026-07-25.

1. OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED — the write path was never broken. `nx service record-deploy engine-service-v0.1.56 --commit f59449f1 --gate PASSED` wrote nexus/deployed-engine-version [21141] and it reads back immediately via both `nx memory get -p nexus` and search. So the canonical entry absence was an OMISSION, not a substrate/ttl problem — exactly the residual scope the skill documents ("guards the VALUE; does NOT force the step to run"). The [20915] note claiming "record-deploy-DONE" for v0.1.47 on 2026-07-18 was therefore inaccurate or referred to something else.

2. NAMESPACE SPLIT CLOSED. nexus_active/deployed-engine-version [20742] (stale at v0.1.41 since 2026-07-14) overwritten with a SUPERSEDED pointer to the canonical nexus/ entry plus the rot history. One tracker again. Chose a pointer over deletion because nexus_active is the shared cross-instance relay namespace conexus also reads.

3. DETECTION SHIPPED a797dbd4 — check_pin_currency() in check_engine_release_floor.py, the governance sweep, 14 mutation-verified tests.

4. THE ACTUAL BUMP SHIPPED bfd3c25d — REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION (0,1,52) -> (0,1,56), moving PINNED_SERVICE_TAG with it. Both gate directions now green: pin == newest published tag == deployed cloud.

REMAINS OPEN, and it is not ours to close: forcing the step to run at all. The real fix is the cloud gate writing the tracker on pass, which is conexus-side. Until then record-deploy stays a step a human must remember, and this bead class can recur.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CLOSED 2026-07-25. All three parts done: detection shipped (a797dbd4), namespace split closed (nexus_active copy is now a SUPERSEDED pointer), and the bump landed (bfd3c25d, v0.1.52 -> v0.1.56). The remaining omission vector — forcing record-deploy to run at all — is NOT new work: nexus-nx3l5 has owned it since 2026-07-04. Not duplicating it here.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
REOPENED-IN-EFFECT BY nexus-cg13x (2026-07-26) — this bead's ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG.

Closed on: 'record-deploy has never been run for real / the step had simply been OMITTED.
That is the documented residual scope limit of the mechanisation (guards the VALUE; does NOT
force the step to run).'

Actual cause: the step DID run. service_cmd.py:151 wrote the tracker with ttl=0 and the
comment '# permanent operational record'. ttl=0 does not mean permanent — it means EXPIRE
IMMEDIATELY (effective_ttl = 0 * (1 + log(access_count+1)) = 0, so any row older than an
instant is swept). The write succeeded, read back fine, and was deleted before the next
session looked. Both expire() implementations agree, so it was never a substrate issue.

This bead's own OPEN QUESTION had the right instinct — 'WHY is nexus/deployed-engine-version
ABSENT rather than merely stale? record-deploy writes ttl=0 (permanent), so a successful run
should have left a permanent row' — and then answered it with the wrong branch. The
parenthetical '(permanent)' was the assumption that needed testing, and it was the bug.

Evidence it was not an omission: nexus_active [20742] records the 2026-07-25 run as 'wrote
nexus/deployed-engine-version [21141] successfully, readable immediately.' Both true. I then
reproduced the whole cycle today — ran record-deploy, got [21155], read it back on two
surfaces — while the row was already condemned.

LESSON, the transferable part: a 200 plus a row id proves the WRITE, not its DURABILITY, and
an immediate read-back cannot distinguish the two. Every verification this bead and its
predecessors performed was an immediate read-back.

Fixed under nexus-cg13x (caller, the test that pinned the bug, the MCP docstring, tracker
re-recorded with ttl NULL). Engine-side coercion of ttl<=0 -> NULL and the doc propagation
remain open there. Reopen this bead or close it against cg13x as Hal prefers — flagging
rather than reopening unilaterally, since Hal closed it.

title: [bug] 12 db tests fail whenever the shell has cloud creds sourced — suite is not hermetic against an activated env
description:
Repro (clean develop, no local edits):
  source ~/.config/nexus/activate.sh
  uv run pytest tests/db/test_om64x_stale_port_recovery.py tests/db/test_http_telemetry_store.py
  -> 11-12 failed
  env -u NX_SERVICE_URL -u NX_SERVICE_TOKEN -u NX_STORAGE_BACKEND <same command>
  -> 18 passed

Affected: tests/db/test_om64x_stale_port_recovery.py (all TokenStore/ScratchStore recovery
classes) and tests/db/test_http_telemetry_store.py::TestConfigErrors::test_missing_port_raises.

They assume NX_SERVICE_URL / NX_SERVICE_TOKEN / NX_STORAGE_BACKEND are ABSENT. With them set,
service_endpoint.py:424 raises the 'service_url is set but no service_token is resolvable' /
endpoint-resolution error instead of the NX_SERVICE_PORT error under assertion, and the recovery
tests resolve a real endpoint rather than the fixture's.

Why this matters more than a normal flake: sourcing activate.sh is the DOCUMENTED way to get a
working token (and the fix path in nexus-srt1m's new 401 doctor advice points operators straight
at it). So the more correctly a developer configures their shell, the more of the suite fails --
and it fails in a way that reads as a real regression in whatever branch happens to be checked
out. Cost this session: a full clean-worktree bisect against develop to prove 12 failures during
a P4b P3 deletion pass were not mine.

Fix: monkeypatch.delenv the three NX_SERVICE_* vars in these tests' fixtures (or an autouse
fixture scoped to the files that assert on endpoint-resolution failure modes). Related standing
directives: 'pin is_local_mode in cloud-path tests' and 'never export gate-wide NX_SERVICE_URL'.
Consider whether a conftest-level guard belongs here so the class cannot regrow.
close_reason: Fixed in 58148b0b on develop. _isolate_service_endpoint_env autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py delenvs NX_SERVICE_URL/TOKEN/HOST/PORT — two independent leak paths (service_endpoint resolution tier 1, and the service_url entry in config.CREDENTIALS), which is why a two-file patch would not have held. Joined the existing ambient-pollution fixture family; placed before _pin_storage_backend_sqlite so t2_service_env's explicit setenv still wins (autouse fixtures run in definition order). Regression test runs the 4 previously-failing groups in a subprocess with deliberately polluted env — in-process absence assertions would be vacuous on CI. Mutation-verified: disabling the scrub fails all 5. tests/db 1239 passed BOTH with creds set and unset (was 1227/1239); service-mode suites 198 passed; ruff check src/ clean.

title: [bug] doctor reports a 401 as 'Vector service not reachable' and prescribes starting a service that is provably up
description:
Observed 2026-07-25 while harvesting the engine-service-v0.1.55 relay, after the conexus-side bearer-token rotation (conexus-rbht revoked+reissued the token at ~18:01 07-24).

SYMPTOM (real doctor output, same run, three lines apart):
  x Vector service (/v1/vectors): not reachable
    Fix: Start the nexus-service (pgvector backend) and export NX_SERVICE_URL / NX_SERVICE_TOKEN.
  ok Managed/remote service (version): https://api.conexus-nexus.com - release_version 0.1.55

Doctor asserts the service is unreachable AND reachable in one report, and its primary fix is to
start a service that its own next check proves is running. In cloud mode 'start the nexus-service'
is categorically wrong advice - there is no local service to start.

ROOT CAUSE: src/nexus/health.py:_check_vector_service (~line 584) wraps the probe in a bare
'except Exception' and collapses EVERY failure into detail='not reachable'. An HTTP 401 from
_get('/v1/vectors/collections') is an AUTHENTICATION failure, not unreachability. The status code
is present in the exception string (the log line carries 'GET /v1/vectors/stats -> HTTP 401:
Unauthorized') and is discarded.

WHY IT COSTS REAL TIME: the actual cause was a revoked token held by a stale process env. The
prescribed fix sends the operator to service-start / provisioning, i.e. the wrong subsystem
entirely. Verified by direct probe: rotated token -> /v1/vectors/stats 200, /health 200;
pre-rotation token -> 401 on every authenticated route; /version 200 in all cases (it is served
unauthenticated off the DB pool as of v0.1.55).

FIX: discriminate on status in the handler.
  - 401/403 -> detail 'authentication failed (HTTP 401)'; fix = refresh NX_SERVICE_TOKEN and
    restart processes holding the old one (long-lived MCP servers cache env at spawn).
  - connection/DNS/timeout -> keep the existing 'not reachable' + boot-advisory path.
  - other 4xx/5xx -> surface the code rather than laundering it into 'not reachable'.
Fatal=True is right for both, only the detail and fix_suggestions differ.

AGGRAVATING FACTOR worth covering in the same fix: a rotated token does not reach already-running
processes. Long-lived MCP servers and Claude sessions keep 401ing until restarted, while a freshly
sourced shell works - which reads as 'intermittent'. The 401 branch should say so explicitly.
close_reason: Fixed in 3cffd93b on develop. _check_vector_service now discriminates on VectorServiceError.code: 401/403 -> 'authentication failed (HTTP N) - the service is reachable but rejected the token' with a fix that refreshes NX_SERVICE_TOKEN and names the stale-process-env aggravator; other HTTP status -> surfaces the code; transport failure (code None) -> unchanged 'not reachable' + boot advisory. Boot advisory now confined to the transport branch so a stale Liquibase line cannot be scraped while the service is up answering 401. Verified live against api.conexus-nexus.com with an invalid token. Mutation-tested non-vacuous (neutering the discriminator fails exactly the 4 new tests). 366 passed across the doctor/health class; ruff check src/ clean.

title: [bug] pytest leaks long-lived aspect-worker + postgres daemons that survive the run (6 + 3 alive now; 2nd sighting)
description:
SECOND SIGHTING — filing per the trigger recorded on nexus-g37fr (2026-07-23): "killed a leaked pytest postgres (pytest-3095 stranded-install test cluster, tmpdir pruned out from under the live postmaster — fixture leak class worth a bead if seen again)". Seen again 2026-07-24, and worse than the first sighting suggested.

OBSERVED (live, this box, 2026-07-24 during a routine log-health review):
  6 x `nx daemon aspect-worker start --config-dir /private/var/folders/.../pytest-of-hal.hildebrand/pytest-<N>/test_hook_starts_worker_on_fir0/.config/nexus`
  3 x postgres processes rooted in tmpdirs
still RUNNING, from pytest runs that finished. Sample pids/dirs: pytest-3594, pytest-3626, pytest-3627 — their .config/nexus dirs still exist, so these are not the tmpdir-pruned variant of the first sighting; they are simply never stopped.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS:
1. Unbounded accumulation. Every full-suite run that exercises the worker-start hook adds more. They are daemons — nothing reaps them. On a dev box that runs the suite several times a day this grows without limit until a reboot.
2. They are not inert. Each aspect-worker polls on a loop; the leaked ones on THIS box generated the 1,375-entry 401 burst on 2026-07-10 against api.conexus-nexus.com (reclaim_stale, Unauthorized) — leaked test daemons hammering the PRODUCTION cloud endpoint with a stale/absent token. That burst was initially indistinguishable from a live product defect during this review.
3. Diagnostic noise. They make `pgrep aspect-worker` useless for answering "is the real worker running", which is a question doctor and several runbooks ask.

SUSPECTED SOURCE: the test that starts a worker via the session hook (`test_hook_starts_worker_on_fir*` in the name of every leaked process's config dir). Its fixture starts a real detached daemon and never tears it down; `start_new_session=True` means it outlives the pytest process by design.

FIX SHAPE: the fixture that starts a worker must stop it (addfinalizer / yield-fixture teardown that SIGTERMs the pid and waits), and the teardown must be robust to the test failing mid-way. Consider a session-scoped autouse sweep as a backstop: any aspect-worker whose --config-dir is under the pytest tmpdir root gets reaped at session end. Do NOT reach for a global pgrep-and-kill — the standing lesson (2026-07-24) is to verify the parent is actually dead before cleaning up "orphans", and a broad sweep could kill Hal's real worker.

RELATED: nexus-g37fr (first sighting, in a comment), nexus-00wsf (unexplained engine CPU — leaked pollers are a candidate contributor to background load on a dev box, worth excluding before blaming the engine).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED 53f58cb3 — the POSTGRES half. The aspect-worker half shipped earlier; this closes the other one the bead reported (6 workers AND 3 postmasters).

TWO CLASSES, TWO ROOT CAUSES — fixing one did not touch the other:
- aspect-worker leaks on a CLEAN exit (stop_worker stops the in-process thread, not the detached Popen subprocess).
- postgres leaks on an ABNORMAL exit. _engine_substrate.py DOES register atexit teardown, but atexit never runs on SIGKILL / double Ctrl-C / crash — exactly how a long suite gets aborted.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT THE BEAD DID NOT DRAW OUT: a session-END reaper cannot fire when the run is KILLED, and that is the case that leaks. Stranded daemons are only reachable from a LATER session. So a session-START pass over sibling pytest-* roots was added. 21 stale session dirs were present on this box — that is the backlog it drains. One ps for the whole scan, not one per root.

PRECISION: postgres matched on executable BASENAME so pg_ctl (same -D flag) and `postgres: checkpointer` children are not swept up. SIGQUIT not SIGTERM — SIGTERM is postgres SMART shutdown which WAITS for clients and can hang a teardown on a stranded cluster; these clusters are throwaway (fsync=off).

A PRE-EXISTING TEST CAUGHT A BUG IN THE FIX: the first back-compat wrapper filtered by label AFTER reaping, so it would have KILLED every postgres it walked past while reporting none. test_spares_unrelated_processes_that_mention_the_tmp_root asserts on the KILL LIST not the return value, and failed instantly. Filter now gates the kill.

VERIFIED END-TO-END on REAL processes, because this file records the previous reaper passing 100% of fake-ps unit tests while reaping ZERO real daemons (macOS /var -> /private/var). Purpose-compiled binary named postgres: reaped+dead inside the root, UNTOUCHED outside it, matched across a real symlink with both sides in opposite forms. That proof is intentionally not a standing test (needs cc, a spawn/sleep sync, macOS-only symlink leg); driver kept in scratch. 15 fake-ps unit tests pin matching/scoping.

title: Dependency-free engine liveness endpoint + move the health probe off the heartbeat thread (closes the 7f7gb gap; engine half -> v0.1.55)
description:
Split out of nexus-7f7gb (2026-07-24), which shipped the client-side half. That fix is real but BOUNDED BY AN INVARIANT it cannot escape, and this bead is the escape.

THE WALL 7f7gb HIT
GET /health is engine-side dataSource.getConnection() + SELECT 1 (HealthHandler.java) — it takes a HikariCP pool connection, whose own connectionTimeout is 30s. So under pool saturation /health can block up to 30s. To tell "pool busy" from "process wedged" the supervisor's probe would have to outlast that.

It cannot. The probe BLOCKS the supervisor's heartbeat thread, so a tick costs _HEALTH_TIMEOUT + heartbeat interval, and the lease TTL must be >= 3x that (tests/daemon/test_storage_service_daemon.py::test_ttl_exceeds_worst_case_heartbeat_tick). With TTL 15s that caps the probe at exactly 4.0s — which is where 7f7gb left it, at the boundary with ZERO margin. Raising it further makes the supervisor lose its OWN lease mid-probe, trading a spurious restart for a vanished endpoint: the same outage wearing a different hat. Raising the TTL instead widens the post-restart stale-endpoint window (the nexus-om64x trade-off).

So today's restart window is ~16s of total silence, up from ~6s. Better, and still not provably wider than a heavy indexing burst. The 503-vs-timeout distinction 7f7gb shipped is what actually protects the DB-unhappy case; the saturation case is only mitigated.

TWO HALVES, EITHER OF WHICH BREAKS THE WALL

1. ENGINE (rides v0.1.55 per the batching decision on nexus-g37fr): a genuinely dependency-free liveness endpoint — GET /livez returning 200 with NO pool access, no SELECT, no I/O beyond the socket. Then a saturated pool cannot make liveness look dead, and the probe can stay fast because it no longer waits on anything. This is the standard liveness/readiness split: /health stays the READINESS probe (DB included, for doctor and for lease-stamping decisions); /livez becomes the LIVENESS probe (restart authority only).
   Note the same defect exists on /version, which also blocks on getConnection() for its schema fields (found during nexus-4yf4u) — worth fixing in the same pass so no unauthenticated probe endpoint touches the pool.

2. CLIENT: move the health probe OFF the heartbeat thread. If the probe runs asynchronously and the heartbeat reads its last result, the tick stops being bounded by the probe timeout and the TTL invariant stops capping the probe budget. This is worth doing even if the engine half lands, because it removes the coupling permanently rather than making it merely survivable.

RECOMMENDED ORDER: engine /livez first (cheap, rides a tag that is being cut anyway), then repoint the supervisor's RESTART decision at /livez while /health keeps driving lease-stamping. The async probe becomes optional once liveness is free.

ACCEPTANCE
- A saturated pool (indexing burst) never advances the restart counter.
- A genuinely wedged JVM (deadlock, GC spiral) still triggers the OS restart within a bounded window.
- test_ttl_exceeds_worst_case_heartbeat_tick still passes, with MARGIN rather than at the boundary.
- The 7f7gb tri-state tests stay green (503 never restarts).

RELATED: nexus-7f7gb (client half, SHIPPED), nexus-00wsf (engine spins at 100-290% CPU with zero PG queries — plausibly the same saturation story seen from the other side), nexus-g37fr (v0.1.55 batching decision).
close_reason: Client half SHIPPED on develop 44c00100, closing the bead. The engine half (/livez, /version off the pool) has been live since engine-service-v0.1.55 and was unconsumed; the supervisor now drives its RESTART decision off /livez while /health keeps lease-stamping. A beat whose /health goes silent consults /livez first: an answer means SATURATED (counter reset, lease not stamped, TTL ages it out), silence on BOTH means WEDGED (counter advances, exit-for-OS-restart at threshold). _HEALTH_TIMEOUT lowered 4.0 -> 2.0 — safe precisely because a /health timeout now costs a lease stamp rather than a kill — plus _LIVEZ_TIMEOUT 1.0, so the worst tick goes 5.0 -> 4.0 against a 15s TTL: 3s of margin where the bead reported zero. ACCEPTANCE, all four met: a saturated pool never advances the restart counter (test_saturated_pool_silent_health_but_live_livez_never_restarts, mutation-falsified — disabling the consult reproduces storage_service_stuck_exit on a healthy service); a genuine wedge still exits within the same ~16s window (test_wedged_process_both_probes_silent_still_exits); test_ttl_exceeds_worst_case_heartbeat_tick passes WITH margin, and a new companion test asserts the margin is STRICT so the next probe increase fails loudly; the 7f7gb tri-state tests stay green (503 never restarts). Both TTL invariant tests had their FORMULA updated to span both probes — leaving the old expression would have understated the real budget. PLACEMENT: implemented in daemon/storage_service_daemon.py, NOT service_registry.py as the bead text says. Checked against tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py's own asserts: it bans only the deleted addr-file shapes, LeaseRecord and _elect, and explicitly does NOT ban lifecycle verbs in tier consumers. The probe is tier-specific (storage_service is the only tier with HTTP endpoints); the TTL still lives in service_registry.TIER_TTLS. Full suite 11534 / 0; daemon suite 430 including RDR-149 conformance + the lifecycle gate.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SCOPE ADDITION (2026-07-24): add a /links/orphaned route to the engine half of this bead's v0.1.55 payload — see nexus-ysrwi.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE rather than as its own bead: it is the same shape as this bead's /livez work (a small, unauthenticated-or-tenant-scoped read route the client cannot synthesise), it rides the same tag, and it unblocks a doctor check that is otherwise impossible. Bundling avoids a second engine round-trip for one route.

CONTRACT: symmetric with the routes that already exist — CatalogHandler has /manifest/orphans and /docs/orphaned but nothing for links. /links/orphaned returns links whose from_tumbler or to_tumbler resolves to no live document, so the client can render a count and name the offending tumblers.

WHY THE CLIENT CANNOT DO IT: HttpCatalogClient.link_audit() is a stub returning {} ("not supported in initial service-mode implementation"), and the SQLite link_audit reads the frozen legacy store (0 rows post-migration). The only available client-side proxy, chunk_counts_for_docs(), returns docs that HAVE a chunk_count, so a doc with no manifest row would be misreported as a dangling endpoint. False positives are disqualifying for a doctor row.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ENGINE HALF IS ALREADY LIVE — the "engine half -> v0.1.55" in the title is DONE, not pending (checked 2026-07-25 while cutting v0.1.56).

/livez (LivezHandler.java, +55 lines) and /version-off-the-pool (VersionHandler.java, +59) shipped in e3fe1f30, an ancestor of engine-service-v0.1.55, plus ProbeEndpointsTest.java (+170). That tag is DEPLOYED: nx service probe reports release_version 0.1.55 from api.conexus-nexus.com (live handshake, not the tracker). v0.1.56 adds nothing here.

WHAT REMAINS is entirely the client half, and it has NOT started: grep for "livez" across src/nexus/daemon/ returns zero hits in service_registry.py. The supervisor still drives its RESTART decision off /health — the pool-blocking endpoint whose 30s connectionTimeout is the exact wall this bead was filed to escape. So the dependency-free liveness endpoint exists and is serving in production, and nothing consumes it.

Per the bead RECOMMENDED ORDER, the next step is now unblocked: repoint the supervisor RESTART authority at /livez while /health keeps driving lease-stamping. Note the daemon-lifecycle hot rule — that change lands in the SHARED primitive (daemon/service_registry.py + the RDR-149 conformance suite), never one tier copy; tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py enforces it.

No engine tag needed.

title: [bug] GH#1419.3c: nexus-service spins at 100-290% CPU with ZERO active PG queries during/after indexing (engine-side, client-unfixable)
description:
Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 3, the ENGINE half. Split out of nexus-gbt5u (2026-07-24) rather than folded into it: gbt5u's fix is client-side TCP keepalive and cannot touch this.

OBSERVATION (Steve, verbatim): during the indexing session 'nexus-service was also spinning with zero active queries (confirmed via pg_stat_activity before touching anything)'. It 'had to be killed manually'. Concurrent with a client that hung 2+ hours. 100-290% CPU = 1 to 3 cores saturated.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY EXPLAINED
- NOT the nexus-j0nec wedge. That looked identical (engine unresponsive, requests timing out) but root-caused to tests/_engine_substrate.py spawning the engine with stdout=subprocess.PIPE and never draining it: the 64KB pipe fills, the console write blocks holding the PrintStream monitor, every logging thread pins behind it. VERIFIED NOT APPLICABLE in production: storage_service_daemon.py:621 routes stdout AND stderr to a real log file via open_child_log_or_devnull (nexus-ovbr7), never a pipe. The production spawn cannot fill a pipe. Hypothesis excluded, do not re-run it.
- NOT the client-side hang. gbt5u established that as Darwin's monotonic clock pausing during system sleep plus absent TCP keepalive. That explains the CLIENT hanging; it does not explain the SERVER burning cores.

OPEN HYPOTHESES, roughly by fit to '1-3 cores busy, zero PG work':
1. GC death spiral. Multi-threaded GC on an undersized heap saturates exactly 1-3 cores while making no application progress, and issues no queries by construction. NX_SERVICE_MAX_HEAP already exists as an operator knob (its OOM guidance is quoted in upgrade_ladder/provisioning.py's discoverability-gate message), which suggests heap pressure on constrained boxes is a known shape. Steve was running CPU-bound LOCAL embedding concurrently — memory and CPU contention at once.
2. Abandoned-request handling. The client timed out and went away; a server-side thread continues or spins on a dead connection. Note the ordering fits: Steve saw 1-3 retries per repo from transient timeouts BEFORE the long hang, so abandoned requests were definitely being produced.
3. A genuine busy-wait / spin loop in a request or background path (embedding queue, aspect worker, connection pool eviction).
4. Watchdog interaction: Issue 3b (nexus-7f7gb) has the storage-service watchdog cycling the service after 3 failed health checks under legitimate load. A cycle landing mid-work could leave a spinning remnant, or the spin could be what fails the health checks. These two beads should be read together.

DIAGNOSTICS TO RUN WHEN REPRODUCED (none require a fix first)
- jcmd <pid> Thread.print (or jstack) while spinning — names the hot threads immediately and separates GC from an application spin.
- jcmd <pid> GC.heap_info + -Xlog:gc for the GC hypothesis; a death spiral shows near-100% time in GC with no heap recovered.
- top -H -pid <pid> to confirm whether the CPU is in a few named threads (app spin) or many (GC).
- Correlate against pg_stat_activity being empty (Steve already established this) and the service log for the same window.

REPRODUCTION PATH: index a large repo in local mode with local embedding on a memory-constrained box, ideally with a client timeout/abandon in the middle. The 4yf4u lesson applies here too — reproduce under instrumentation before claiming a mechanism; the last engine-wedge investigation named the wrong subsystem for a while because the symptom pointed at the engine and the cause was in what owned its stdio.

RELATED: nexus-gbt5u (client half, FIXED), nexus-7f7gb (Issue 3b watchdog cycling under load), nexus-29kr0 (Steve reindex forensics).

title: Promote engine convergence to a real ladder rung (RDR-185 successor; decides upgrade_ladder/provisioning.py's fate) — RDR candidate
description:
DEFERRED OUT OF nexus-4yf4u (Hal decision D1, 2026-07-24): 4yf4u fixed restart-stale's engine convergence IN PLACE. Promoting convergence to a ladder rung was the acknowledged right end state but is not a P1 bug fix — it needs a rung contract for NON-DATA (binary) convergence and it collides with a standing P2 decision. Filed so the deferral is tracked rather than lost.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT END STATE
restart-stale owns a BESPOKE engine-convergence mechanism that sits outside the ladder. nexus-4yf4u's own bead text names this the design smell: 'escalate to the ladder's engine-binary rung (RDR-185 convergence territory — the ladder is the standing mechanism; restart-stale bypassing it is the design smell)'. 4yf4u dispositioned the FAIL-LOUD half of that sentence and explicitly deferred the ESCALATE half — this bead is that half.

THE STRUCTURAL WIN (the real argument, not tidiness)
RDR-185 Gap-4's binding pin is tests/upgrade/test_gap4_two_mechanisms.py::test_rung_convergence_is_re_derived_live_never_cached: a rung answers 'am I converged?' from the LIVE world every time; the banned form is a persisted freestanding verdict (cache file / second table / marker). detect_engine_convergence answers exactly that question from the install-provenance SIDECAR — a cache file — and the Gap-4 pin never caught it because the pin AST-scans RUNGS and this leg is not one. Promoting it makes the existing Gap-4 pin cover engine convergence BY CONSTRUCTION instead of by a hand-written test that the next refactor can drift away from. That is the payoff; the tidiness is incidental.

THE TENSION TO RESOLVE (why it is not mechanical)
upgrade_ladder/provisioning.py::establish_verified_service begins with provision_and_serve — full 'nx init --service' reuse, i.e. ACQUISITION. But the P2 consumption decision (recorded in that module's docstring) is that the upgrade path NEVER provisions: nx init owns acquisition, and a stranded pre-PG install gets the stranded-install redirect. So a rung cannot simply call establish_verified_service. The design work is: what does a binary-convergence rung's detect/converge/verify contract look like when it must converge an install that ALREADY EXISTS, without acquiring one? Most likely the health-gate -> version-pin -> discoverability SPINE is reusable while provision_and_serve is not.

IT DECIDES ANOTHER MODULE'S FATE (the deadline)
src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/provisioning.py is TEST-CONSUMED ONLY. Its docstring previously justified itself as 'the intended material for nexus-4yf4u' and said to revisit if 4yf4u landed elsewhere. It DID land elsewhere (4yf4u uses binary_lifecycle.fetch_service_version + engine_version.parse_engine_version, because verify_service_version is a fail-closed >= BOOLEAN that never surfaces the observed version the operator lines need). The docstring was updated 2026-07-24 to record that its 4yf4u rationale lapsed. Its ONLY remaining live candidate consumer is THIS bead. So:
  - if this lands  -> provisioning.py gets a genuine production consumer at last;
  - if this is declined -> provisioning.py has NO consumer and should be DELETED rather than kept on a lapsed rationale (deleting it is still a decision, not a cleanup: it is a Hal-locked RDR-155 P4b P0e D-C rehome).
That coupling gives this bead a real deadline: it should be answered BEFORE the 7.0.0 wave's P3 revisits upgrade_finish/provisioning, or P3 will face the same undecided module again.

RDR CANDIDATE
This is an architecture decision (new rung contract class + interaction with a locked P2 acquisition decision), not a task. Recommend /conexus:rdr-create as an RDR-185 successor rather than implementing straight from this bead.

INPUTS
- Design memo: T2 nexus/design-4yf4u-restart-stale-convergence.md [21124] (Non-goals section records this deferral).
- src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py: detect_engine_convergence / _running_engine / _restart_and_verify / converge_engine (the code a rung would absorb).
- src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/provisioning.py docstring (the lapsed-rationale record).
- RDR-185 (closed): docs/rdr/rdr-185-single-ladder-convergent-upgrade.md Gap 4; T2 nexus_rdr/185.

title: Orchestration Gap-1 guard is blind to prompt-named background dispatches (4 starts / 0 EXPECT rows, census undeclared=0 false-clean)
close_reason: superseded: false-clean half closed by suuja rc=1 BLINDSPOT signal (grooming 2026-08-07, T2 [21595], Hal-approved batch)

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SECOND EVIDENCE SET (2026-07-24 session, RDR-184 retro). Census is EMPTY, not "undeclared>0" — the false-clean this bead describes, reproduced with a different root cause than the first sighting.

DISPATCHES THIS SESSION: 3 named background agents (CRE-4YF4U-A code-review-expert; CRITIC-4YF4U-B substantive-critic, killed; CRITIC-4YF4U-C substantive-critic rerun). All three carried unique names in the prompt text per the Gap-1 convention.

EXPECT ROWS FILED: ZERO. Not an oversight — the mechanism is ABSENT in this session. `mcp__plugin_conexus_nexus__expectations_expect` does not exist in the tool list, and `nx expectations` is not a CLI command ("Error: No such command 'expectations'"). The orchestrator cannot declare even when it intends to.

RETRO RESULT: `expectations_undeclared <sid>` and `expectations_census <sid>` both return EMPTY. So a session with 3 undeclared named dispatches produces a census indistinguishable from a session with none.

CONSEQUENCE BEYOND THE CENSUS (new, worth folding into this bead's scope): the SubagentStop guard's decision table is `agent not listed -> exit 0`, and ground truth for "owes a report" is the expectations file. With no EXPECT rows, the stop guard was INERT for all three agents despite NX_ORCH_STOP_GUARD defaulting to block. So the blindness is not only a reporting gap; it silently disables the guard itself for every dispatch made without a declaration mechanism.

SUGGESTS the fix has two halves: (1) make the census distinguish "no rows because nothing was dispatched" from "no rows because nothing could be declared"; (2) ensure a declaration path EXISTS in every session shape that can dispatch agents, or have the stop guard fail loud when it sees a named dispatch with no ledger at all.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SECOND CONFIRMED REPRODUCTION, 2026-07-25 session f44c0c50. Census output verbatim:

  ROWS       expect=0 start=6 reported=0 blocked=0 wouldblock=0
  CLASSIFIED reported=0 blocked_resolved=0 (immediate=0 later=0) blocked_unresolved=0 wouldblock=0 no_terminal=0 undeclared=0 no_start=0 expected_no_start=0

SIX background Agent dispatches, ZERO EXPECT rows, and CLASSIFIED reports undeclared=0. That is the false-clean this bead names, now at 6 starts rather than the original 4 — the guard scales its blindness with the fan-out.

The dispatches were: code-review-expert (python diff), substantive-critic, code-review-expert (java/service scope), test-validator, deep-analyst (handle-shape sweep), debugger (suite runtime). All六 were prompt-named background agents launched via the Agent tool without a prior expectations_expect row. Every one returned useful findings (1 Critical, 3 High, 3 confirmed defects), so this is not a case of the dispatches being unimportant — it is the census being unable to see the most productive agent round of the session.

ORCHESTRATOR ERROR ALSO WORTH RECORDING: the RDR-184 Gap-1 convention (UNIQUE name + EXPECT row BEFORE the Agent call) was not followed. So this reproduction is a compound of the guard blindness AND the operator skipping the declaration. The escalation contract says any undeclared background teammate in a retro is a mechanization trigger; that mechanization is this bead. Not filing a duplicate.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: nothing in-session. The census is the only check, and it reported clean. A guard that reports undeclared=0 when expect=0 and start=6 is worse than no guard, because it converts "nobody declared anything" into a passing signal — the same false-clean class as nexus-ingey/k0luu fixed in this same session on the diagnostics side.

title: GH#1419.2: daemon service uninstall race — launchd respawns postgres in the stop-to-remove-autostart window
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 2. nx daemon service uninstall --autostart removed the LaunchAgent but a postgres launchd spawned in the gap survived and needed manual kill. Fix: order remove-autostart-unit BEFORE/atomically-with stop, then verify no surviving postgres before reporting success (fail loud otherwise). Daemon-lifecycle rule applies: fix in the shared primitive service_registry.py + RDR-149 conformance suite, never one tier's copy.
close_reason:
SHIPPED develop 6907e239 (2026-07-24). GH #1419 Issue 2.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, recorded so it is not re-derived. It said the uninstall sequence has a race window (launchd respawning postgres between stop and remove-autostart) and asked to reorder them. There is no such window: uninstall_autostart ALREADY deactivates (launchctl bootout / systemctl disable) BEFORE unlinking the unit file, and the command never stops anything at all — it is documented as removing the autostart entry only, and `nx daemon service stop` leaves Postgres running BY DESIGN ("it is independently managed", daemon.py's own message).

ACTUAL DEFECT: silence. Uninstall printed a bare "Removed <path>" while a supervisor and a Postgres cluster could both still be live, and named neither. "Uninstalled" reads as "gone", which is how Steve ended up hunting a postgres process by hand.

SHIPPED: the shared primitive (installer.uninstall_autostart) now returns SURVIVORS and both tiers' CLI wrappers print them — the storage service with its supervisor pid and `nx daemon service stop`, Postgres with its port and `nx daemon service stop --with-pg`. Liveness via the RDR-149 ServiceRegistry lease, never a bespoke ps sweep (test_lifecycle_gate.py exists to stop exactly that). Probe scoped BY TIER so a t2 uninstall cannot misattribute the storage service as its survivor. Landed in the shared primitive, not the service command, per the standing daemon-lifecycle rule.

JUDGMENT CALL FOR HAL TO OVERRIDE IF WANTED: exit code stays 0. The bead said "fail loud otherwise"; this is loud (stderr, with the exact commands) but not a failure — the uninstall succeeded at what it claims, and a surviving Postgres is documented behaviour on the stop path too. Exiting non-zero would break scripted teardown for an outcome the product considers correct. Say the word and it becomes non-zero when survivors exist.

TESTS: 13, each RED first. Three bind a REAL listener on port 0 instead of stubbing the probe — a detector that never detects would otherwise pass every reporting test while reporting "nothing survived" on a box where postgres is alive, i.e. the exact bug.

VERIFICATION: 664 daemon tests pass, lifecycle gate + RDR-149 conformance green (78), ruff clean. Probe run against this box's real config dir returns empty, correctly — it is cloud-mode with no local service or PG.

RESIDUAL, not fixed (out of scope, worth knowing): a FAILED launchctl bootout is still downgraded to a warning and the unit file removed anyway, which can leave a job loaded in launchd with no unit file left to remove it by. The new survivor report makes that state visible rather than silent, which is the practical mitigation; a real fix would refuse to unlink on bootout failure. File separately if that shape is ever seen in the field.

title: GH#1419.9: no supported export/import for catalog links + store_put-only knowledge content across reinstall
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 9. Full reinstall is a supported recovery path (fixed Issue 1) but carrying the link graph + knowledge-only content across one required ad hoc SQL against a scratch cluster, matching links by title with file_path disambiguation (tumblers not stable across reindex). Ask: nx catalog export-links / import-links keyed on stable identity (title+file_path), and nx knowledge export for store_put-origin content. Overlaps existing .nxexp exporter — evaluate extending it rather than a new verb (no-knob-reflex: fold into the journey).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
TRIAGE 2026-07-24 (Hal: "let's not forget xn3fr"). NOT STARTED — deliberately. This is the only one of the three remaining GH #1419 beads that is genuinely FEATURE work rather than a fix, and the bead's own suggested shape may be wrong.

THE STRUCTURAL MISMATCH: the bead says "overlaps existing .nxexp exporter — evaluate extending it rather than a new verb (no-knob-reflex: fold into the journey)". Folding is the right instinct, but exporter.export_collection() exports ONE COLLECTION's chunks and embeddings. The two things this bead needs to carry are not collection-scoped:
  - catalog LINKS are catalog-level and CROSS-collection (a link routinely joins tumblers in different collections);
  - store_put-origin knowledge has identity title+file_path, which is likewise not a collection property.
So hanging a cross-collection graph off a per-collection export changes what .nxexp IS, rather than extending it. That is a design decision, not an implementation detail — which is why this needs a design pass and not a patch.

THE UNDERLYING NEED IS REAL AND CONFIRMED: full reinstall is now a supported recovery path (nexus-4yf4u shipped), so "reinstall" is advice we give. But carrying the link graph across a reinstall currently requires ad hoc SQL against a scratch cluster, matching links by title with file_path disambiguation because tumblers are NOT stable across reindex. We are recommending a recovery path whose data-preservation story is "write your own SQL".

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS for that pass:
1. Does the link graph belong in .nxexp at all, or in a separate catalog-level export (nx catalog export-links) whose scope is the catalog rather than a collection?
2. What is the stable identity contract across a reindex? The bead proposes title+file_path. Is that sufficient for knowledge docs with no file_path (store_put-origin — exactly the nexus-b6enc population)?
3. Does this interact with the 7.0.0 wave? The catalog is PG-resident now, so an exporter that reads the catalog reads the engine, not SQLite. Check against the P3 partition before designing.

RECOMMENDATION: take this through /conexus:brainstorming-gate when it comes up, not as a bug fix. Priority stays P2; it is a real gap in a recovery path we now actively recommend, but nothing is broken today that it would fix.

title: GH#1419.7: dangling catalog_links rows (target tumbler has no document) — no write-time cleanup, no doctor check
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 7. 5 of 52 backed-up links pointed at tumblers with no document anywhere in the same pg_dump — orphans from document deletion without link cleanup. Add: doctor integrity check for catalog_links with unresolvable endpoints + delete-time link cleanup (or FK with ON DELETE). Direct evidence for nexus-tk070 (post-deletion FK census, Hal-gated) — this is exactly the enforce-or-check relationship class tk070 will enumerate; do not start tk070 itself.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DOCTOR-HALF SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-07-24). I triaged this as "client-side, cheap, actionable now". That was WRONG. There is no primitive on the service path to build the check on, and every available proxy false-positives.

WHAT I FOUND
1. Catalog.link_audit() already computes an `orphaned` list — but catalog_links.py implements it as raw SQL against the SQLite `links` table, i.e. the FROZEN legacy store (see nexus-aoqnb: the live-path .catalog.db holds 0 rows on a migrated box). Running it there reports zero orphans forever.
2. HttpCatalogClient.link_audit() — the SERVICE path, i.e. every post-migration box — is a stub: `return {}  # not supported in initial service-mode implementation`. A doctor check reading result.get("orphaned", []) would therefore render "0 orphans, clean" on every install. That is the exact kmo9h false-clean class ("never render couldn't-check as checked-clean").
3. The obvious client-side workaround does not hold either: link_query() can page all links, but the batch existence primitive available is chunk_counts_for_docs(), which returns "docs that HAVE a chunk_count". A document with no manifest row is ABSENT from that map and would be reported as a dangling endpoint. False positives are the worst outcome for a doctor row — a check that cries wolf gets ignored, which is how a real one gets missed.
4. Engine-side there is no links equivalent: CatalogHandler routes include /manifest/orphans and /docs/orphaned but nothing for links.

WHAT THIS MAKES THE RIGHT SHAPE
Point 4 is also the good news: the engine already has TWO sibling orphan routes, so the missing one is obvious in form — a /links/orphaned route symmetric with /docs/orphaned, returning links whose from_tumbler or to_tumbler resolves to no live document. Small, and it makes the doctor check trivial (call it, render the count, name the tumblers).

REVISED DISPOSITION: the doctor half is BLOCKED on that engine route, so it belongs in the v0.1.55 batch alongside the other engine work (decision recorded on nexus-g37fr), not in a client-only pass. The FK/ON-DELETE half remains blocked on nexus-tk070 (Hal-gated, do-not-start), so BOTH halves of this bead are now engine-side. Nothing client-only remains.

STRUCTURAL NOTE for tk070 when it runs: catalog_links in catalog-001-baseline.xml carries a PK (tenant_id, id) and a UNIQUE (tenant_id, from_tumbler, to_tumbler, link_type) but NO foreign key to documents. Dangling links are not a fluke — nothing structurally prevents them. That is a concrete row for the FK census.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DETECTION FIXED 42ce8872. PREVENTION DEFERRED to nexus-tk070 (needs an engine change).

GROUND TRUTH, taken before any code: 277 dangling rows on the LIVE store (engine v0.1.56, service mode). Steves postmortem sampled 5 of 52 — the corpus has grown, and 277 vs "a few stale edges" invites a different response.

THE EXACT PATH THAT CREATES THEM, which matters more than the check: CatalogRepository.java:2146-2195 `deleteCollectionTxn`, reached via delete_collection() -> POST /v1/catalog/collections/delete. Step 6 (line 2190) HARD-deletes catalog_documents scoped to a physical_collection — the codes own comment calls it "the ONLY production HARD delete of document rows" — and NO step removes catalog_links referencing those tumblers. A cross-collection link (implements from code__* to rdr__*) survives when either endpoints collection is deleted.

RULED OUT rather than assumed: per-document soft-delete does NOT cause this. orphanedLinks() tests row PRESENCE, not deleted_at, so a tombstoned doc does not orphan its links.

ALREADY HALF-PRESENT: the engine route (orphanedLinks + /v1/catalog/links/orphaned, commit e3fe1f30) was already on develop from a prior pass — only the Python client method was missing. Client half met an engine half that had been sitting unused.

title: GH#1419.3b: storage-service watchdog cycles nexus-service under legitimate indexing load (3 failed health checks = restart)
description: Steve postmortem GH #1419 Issue 3 second half. Watchdog observed cycling the service after 3 consecutive failed health checks caused purely by CPU-bound local-embedding load, not failure — a client mid-batch loses its connection. Health probe should distinguish saturated-but-progressing from hung (e.g. longer probe timeout, load-aware backoff, or liveness endpoint that doesn't compete with embed workers).
close_reason:
SHIPPED develop cf426cdc (2026-07-24). GH #1419 Issue 3b.

MECHANISM (verified both sides): GET /health is dataSource.getConnection() + SELECT 1 (HealthHandler.java) — it takes a HikariCP pool connection. The supervisor probed it with a 2s timeout and exited for an OS restart after 3 consecutive failures at 1s: a 3-SECOND grace window. Under indexing load the pool is contended, /health blocks past 2s, the counter fills, the service restarts, in-flight clients are severed, they retry, load rises. Self-amplifying, and caused by the probe that decides whether to KILL the service competing for the resource saturation exhausts.

DEEPER DEFECT FIXED: _service_healthy returned a bare bool, collapsing "answered 503" and "did not answer at all" into one False. Opposite evidence. A 503 proves the process is ALIVE; restarting cannot fix a down DB and does sever clients. Probe is now tri-state (HealthProbe OK/UNREADY/UNKNOWN); only UNKNOWN advances the restart counter. UNREADY resets it, declines to stamp the lease, and logs. _service_healthy survives as a bool for the STARTUP gate where the distinction is genuinely irrelevant.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, stated plainly: widening the probe budget hits a hard invariant — the probe BLOCKS the heartbeat thread, so tick = _HEALTH_TIMEOUT + heartbeat interval and lease TTL must be >= 3x that (test_ttl_exceeds_worst_case_heartbeat_tick). TTL 15s caps the probe at EXACTLY 4.0s. My first attempt at 20s tripped that test — the supervisor would have lost its own lease mid-probe, trading a spurious restart for a vanished endpoint. Final: 4.0s x 4 beats = ~16s of silence before restart (was ~6s), sitting at the invariant boundary with ZERO margin. A pool with a 30s connectionTimeout can still outlast a 4s probe, so the SATURATION case is mitigated, not solved. The 503-vs-timeout distinction is what genuinely protects the DB-unhappy case.

FOLLOW-UP: nexus-hubc0 — dependency-free engine /livez (no pool access) plus moving the probe off the heartbeat thread; engine half batched into v0.1.55 per the g37fr decision. That is what actually breaks the wall. Also noted there: /version has the same defect (blocks on getConnection for schema fields, found during nexus-4yf4u), so no unauthenticated probe endpoint should touch the pool.

TESTS: 9 new, each RED first, driving a REAL loopback server on port 0 with a switchable status rather than stubbing the probe — a classifier that never classifies would otherwise pass every reporting assertion. Two existing heartbeat tests re-pointed to the tri-state seam; the eight startup-gate stubs keep the boolean deliberately.

VERIFICATION: 676 daemon tests pass, ruff clean.

title: expectations_census: BLOCKED/REPORTED rows with no matching START row are invisible to per-agent AGENT/CLASSIFIED output
design:
Found during substantive-critique of the nexus-hybv1 fix (subagent-stop.sh
post-block resolution stamp + expectations_census).

expectations_census's per-agent AGENT lines and CLASSIFIED tallies are
keyed off the `order[]`/`name[]` arrays, which are populated ONLY by
matching START rows (the "a<name>-<hash>" morphology). term[] (REPORTED/
BLOCKED/WOULDBLOCK classification) is populated independently, keyed by
agent_id from the verb rows themselves, with no dependency on START.

Consequence: a BLOCKED (or REPORTED/WOULDBLOCK) row for an agent_id that
never got a matching START row -- e.g. because the SubagentStart hook
failed to fire, raced, or is disabled independently of SubagentStop (the
two are separate hook registrations; expectations_start's own docstring
calls START "non-load-bearing backfill", i.e. already known to be
best-effort) -- is silently ABSENT from both the AGENT rows and the
CLASSIFIED summary, while still incrementing the raw ROWS tally
(rows["blocked"]++).

Reproduced directly (session with EXPECT + BLOCKED but no START row for
that agent_id):
  ROWS       expect=1 start=0 reported=0 blocked=1 wouldblock=0
  CLASSIFIED reported=0 blocked_resolved=0 blocked_unresolved=0 wouldblock=0 no_terminal=0 undeclared=0 expected_no_start=1

The BLOCKED event is reported as `blocked_unresolved=0` -- exactly the
bfbfa2fe failure class (a real BLOCKED miscounted as 0) this bead's own
forensic basis was built to catch, reintroduced through a different
mechanism (START-row dependency) that the fix didn't anticipate. The
"EXPECTED_NO_START ghostworker" line that appears instead conflates
"never dispatched" with "dispatched, blocked, but our own START
instrumentation missed it" -- two very different signals for SC
interpretation.

FIX: derive order[]/name[] from the union of {START rows} union
{BLOCKED/REPORTED/WOULDBLOCK rows lacking a matching START}, so no
agent's terminal state can vanish from classification purely because its
bookkeeping START write failed. At minimum, assert ROWS blocked+reported+wouldblock
totals are >= sum of the corresponding CLASSIFIED buckets as a self-check
in the test suite, so a future silent drop reintroduces a test failure
rather than a silent gap.

Also flagged in the same critique, lower severity:
- _stamp_resolution_if_reported has no idempotency guard: every
  subsequent Stop of an already-BLOCKED_RESOLVED multi-round agent
  (verified empirically) appends another REPORTED row unconditionally,
  inflating ROWS reported= without bound (CLASSIFIED stays correct,
  since it's deduped per agent_id via order[]). Recommend skip-stamping
  once a REPORTED row already exists for the agent_id.
- BLOCKED_RESOLVED conflates "the guard's own round-trip caused the
  report" (stop_hook_active=true path) with "some unrelated later Stop
  found a report already in the transcript" (the already_blocked/
  non-active path) -- both write an identical REPORTED row today. Since
  the round-1-block-then-round-2-idle case (Gap-1's core scenario)
  remains entirely unenforced and unmeasured by design, a late
  incidental SendMessage in round 5 retroactively paints rounds 2-4's
  silent idling as "guard success" in the ledger. Recommend the two
  call sites stamp distinguishable verbs (or a resolved_via field) so
  census consumers can separate strong causal evidence (immediate
  round-trip) from weak (later, possibly-unrelated report).
close_reason: Fixed in the same working tree before commit (review round on nexus-hybv1): expectations_census now seeds the per-agent list from the union of START rows AND terminal verbs (BLOCKED/REPORTED/WOULDBLOCK) — a BLOCKED with no START row prints as 'AGENT <id> - BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED no-start' and counts in CLASSIFIED (no_start counter added). Regression fixture: anoshow-x-cccc in tests/e2e/lib/expectations_test.sh Test 13. Also fixed from the same review round: REPORTED-then-BLOCKED last-state-wins (sticky-REPORTED masking), duplicate-stamp guard (expectations_last_terminal), immediate/later resolution-strength split.

title: Local-mode first-store 422 when VOYAGE_API_KEY is exported: init saves bge-768 client config while supervisor plumbs the key into NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY and the engine flips voyage-only
description: Found during the 6.15.0 post-release shakeout (fresh PyPI install, HOME-isolated sandbox, mac-arm64, engine v0.1.51). title: remediate chash-poison playbook steers rollback-first on a serving store — no ladder-aware branch (GH #1414 follow-up)
description:
Observed live 2026-07-21: Steve Harris's agent (GH #1414 reporter), following the remediate/forensics chash-poison playbook verbatim, proposed running 'nx storage migrate vectors --rollback' as step 1 on a store that was serving fine on engine v0.1.49 with ~29k width-non-conformant rows — a condition the upgrade ladder heals in place (substrate-etl re-index of 2 named collections + chash-rekey rung from stored text).

The playbook (src/nexus/remediation/playbook.py, _chash_poison) prescribes rollback -> re-index -> guided-upgrade unconditionally. It has no branch for the RDR-185 ladder path, while docs/migration-runbook.md itself says 'the remedy for a block on that path is to run nx upgrade, not to re-index' and marks §8.1's re-index step OPTIONAL under the ladder. The playbook's premise ('a new engine would crash-loop on boot') is also the nexus-joima over-claim — v0.1.49+ tolerates the rows (VALIDATE now 3-of-5 by decision).

Net effect: the product's own guided-remediation surface steers autonomous agents toward the maximum-disruption recovery (full pgvector rollback, reverting serving to Chroma) for the ORDINARY post-6.14.0 upgrade-ladder condition. Steve's agent did ask before executing — a less careful one would not have.

Fix shape (design fork, ask Hal): playbook should discriminate on live store state it already has (StoreState) — if the engine currently serving >= tolerant version AND ladder rungs are pending, the playbook is 're-index the named collections, nx upgrade, hold engine upgrades until doctor clears' with rollback reserved for the true GH #1390 crash-loop/blocked-boot class. Depends on nexus-joima's verification verdict.

Related: nexus-joima (over-claiming warning), nexus-pgdcv (fail-open converge gate), nexus-g6vb4 (stale MCP host).
