title: Per-chunk delete leaks chash_index pointers — every deletion path, engine choke point candidate (blocks uu4ue DELETE)
description:
Found by nexus-uu4ue ATTRIBUTE part 1 (2026-07-20). PgVectorRepository.delete (service .../vectors/PgVectorRepository.java:2008) deletes chunk rows only; NO caller anywhere pairs it with chash_index cleanup, and the GC/quarantine pipeline (indexer.py _prune_deleted_files, _prune_misclassified, pipeline_stages.py PDF stale prune, chunk_quarantine.py expire) never touches chash_index. Only collection-wide delete_collection cleans pointers; the catalog_spans.py:367 self-heal is collection-level and lazy. Net: pointer rows are written on every upsert, deleted on almost no delete — the 292,230 cloud orphans are this leak's integral, and it is STILL OPEN on every store, local included.

DESIGN FORK (Hal's call before implementing):
(a) ENGINE choke point — PgVectorRepository.delete's key (collection, chash IN ids) is exactly chash_index's natural key (chash, physical_collection); delete pointer rows in the SAME transaction. Single point, covers every caller including future ones (the nexus-q6830 lesson: N callers opting in is the failure class). Also decide: should the quarantine MOVE (copy-then-delete from live) repoint the chash_index row to the quarantine collection instead of leaving it aimed at live?
(b) Caller-side pairing — 4+ Python sites each remember to clean up. Rejected shape unless there is an engine-side reason (a) cannot work.
Manifest cleanup stays a caller obligation either way (doc-keyed, already documented as application-enforced FK, T2 nexus_rdr/155-manifest-fk-decision).

ORDERING: this must land (engine tag + deploy, second release lifecycle) BEFORE nexus-uu4ue step (2) DELETE, or the deletion envelope chases a moving target. Attribution queries relayed to conexus as [20992]; their Q3 answer (dangling rows newer than 2026-07-06) is the live falsification of whether the leak is measurably active on the cloud store.
close_reason: MOOTED by RDR-187 acceptance (2026-07-20, gate PASSED): the design-level fix is to DROP chash_index entirely, not to add pointer cleanup to the delete transaction. The leak class cannot exist without the table. This bead's analysis (the five-path leak inventory, the choke-point argument) is preserved in RDR-187's Gap 2 and Verified Ground; if RDR-187 is ever rejected or abandoned, reopen this bead — its choke-point design is the fallback.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: HOLD — do not implement. RDR-187 (draft, docs/rdr/rdr-187-retire-chash-index-router-table.md) supersedes this fix at the design level: drop chash_index entirely rather than maintain the derived copy. This bead moots on RDR-187 acceptance (the leak class cannot exist without the table). If RDR-187 is rejected, this bead's choke-point design is the fallback and the analysis here stands.

title: VERIFY: is the chash-poison 'engine upgrade will crash-loop' warning still true, and does it cite a CLOSED issue? (GH #1414)
description:
Hypothesis from Steve Harris's GH #1414 transcript, NOT asserted — needs checking before we change any text.

health.py:2431 tells the user 'Do NOT upgrade the engine binary until remediated' and predicts a crash-loop on catalog-013-3's VALIDATE CONSTRAINT. Steve's box upgraded 0.1.35 -> 0.1.49 with 35477 width-non-conformant rows present, and the service came up and served fine. Since RDR-180 made VALIDATE 3-of-5 BY DECISION (catalog_document_chunks and chash_index stay NOT VALID over pre-existing orphans), the prediction may no longer hold for current engines.

If it does not hold, we are telling users not to do something the shipped engine tolerates — a false gate that will get ignored, which is worse than no gate. If it DOES still hold, Steve got lucky and we should understand why.

Second, smaller: the warning cites GH #1390 by number, and #1390 is CLOSED. Either the reference should move to the live tracking item or the text should stop pointing users at a closed issue.

Check against catalog-013-3's current changeset + the RDR-180 amnesty semantics before editing any string.
close_reason: Verified + shipped: crash-loop claim disproven for v0.1.48+ (T2 [21022]); all surfaces narrowed and GH #1390 citation contextualized as closed in 5e2a9730

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
VERIFY VERDICT 2026-07-21: the crash-loop claim is FALSE for v0.1.48+ engines (the RDR-180 bytea era), for the poison class the probe detects. Mechanically verified:
1. rdr180-2 DROPS the char len_checks; rdr180-11 adds the octet checks NOT VALID with the header comment 'VALIDATE is the client rung's post-rekey act via the admin connection -- deliberately NOT a boot changeset'. grep confirms ZERO 'VALIDATE CONSTRAINT *octet*' statements anywhere in the changelog.
2. catalog-013-3 VALIDATEs only the CHAR-era len checks (length(chash)=32), existence-gated per constraint, and freezes after first success. Legacy 32-hex ids have length()=32 -> they PASS. Steve's 0.1.35->0.1.49 boot: 013-3 passed, rdr180 converted rows to 16-byte bytea, octet checks landed NOT VALID -> serves fine. NOT luck -- by design.
3. Residual TRUE class (narrow): pre-v0.1.48 char-era box with rows genuinely violating length()=32 (e.g. 64-char strays OUTSIDE chash_index -- 013-0/1b normalized chash_index only) hitting 013-3's first run with the constraint present -> crash-loop real. Warning must be conditioned on this class, not asserted universally.
4. GH #1390 confirmed CLOSED 2026-07-10 (gh issue view). Citation must move to the runbook/live ref.
5. THIRD defect: health.py fix_suggestions steer to runbook 8.1 rollback-first -- same mis-steer as nexus-o513u. health.py:2431 detail text + fix_suggestions + playbook _chash_poison + _chash_poison_forensics interpret step all inherit the same false premise; fix together (fold text edits into o513u scope). Full verdict: T2 nexus/joima-verdict-crash-loop-overclaim-2026-07-21 [21022].

title: converge_engine's poison gate fails open on the ORDINARY ordering — doctor converges the engine before the service is up (GH #1414)
description:
Steve Harris, GH #1414 transcript. upgrade_finish.py:471-503 _poison_playbook() returns None when the probe cannot run (PG down, not service mode, any error) — documented and deliberate: 'it must never block a legitimate convergence'. In Steve's run the FIRST nx doctor converged the engine 0.1.35 -> 0.1.49 and restarted the storage service; the poison condition (35477 non-conformant rows) only surfaced in a LATER doctor, after nx init --service brought the service up so the probe could run. The engine had already been swapped.

The fail-open is defensible in isolation. What this transcript shows is that 'probe cannot run because the service is not up yet' is the ORDINARY ordering on a box being converged, not a rare edge — so the gate is absent exactly when convergence is most likely to happen. Assess: can the gate distinguish 'probe unavailable' from 'probe says clean', and defer convergence (with a loud line) rather than proceeding blind, when the store is service-mode but unreachable? Do NOT convert this into a hard block that bricks legitimate convergences — the existing comment is load-bearing.
close_reason: Shipped fc24123c: tri-state PoisonProbe (poisoned/clean/unknown); converge_engine DEFERS loudly on unknown (verified path nx doctor/restart-stale leads; install-binary named only for will-not-boot); install-binary gate migrated to the same probe with warn-UNVERIFIED-and-proceed on unknown (round-2 critic HIGH-1); CHASH_CONFORMANCE_LABEL shared constant (MEDIUM-1); no passive-retry promise (MEDIUM-2); truncation + creds-absent-warn arms tested. Stacked reviewers both rounds; deferral branch mutation-verified. Never-brick constraint held: nx init never routes through converge_engine (reviewer-verified); doctor backstop confirmed adequate.

title: MCP host cannot self-detect staleness after in-place uv tool upgrade — opaque ImportError (GH #1414)
description:
Steve Harris, GH #1414 suggestion 1+2. After 'uv tool upgrade conexus' replaced site-packages under a live nx-mcp process, a deferred import (nexus/db/t2/__init__.py's 'from nexus.db.t2.http_memory_store import HttpMemoryStore', deferred for circular-dep avoidance) fired for the first time on a memory_get call. It read the NEW http_memory_store off disk, which imports DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT_BUDGET_S from nexus.db.service_endpoint — already in sys.modules as the OLD module object. Result: ImportError for a name that demonstrably exists in the file on disk, and imports fine in a fresh interpreter. Mixed old/new module graph.

STRUCTURAL CAUSE OF THE DIAGNOSTIC GAP: src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:197 in enumerate_processes skips 'pid == me'. detect_stale_processes() therefore cannot, by construction, see the process calling it. Correct for nx doctor (don't report yourself); it means the primitive that diagnoses this can never be pointed at the process suffering from it. nx doctor named his exact two pids (92783/92784) from a separate terminal, but nothing in the failing tool call pointed there.

Fix shape (design fork, ask Hal before building): a self_is_stale() helper — same install_mtime_and_version() comparison applied to our own start time — consumed by the MCP host. Open questions: check at startup, per tool call, or only when decorating an exception? Refuse loudly vs warn? No new verb, no knob.

Related: nexus-y3wuu (same class — a diagnostic that exists and silently does not apply).
close_reason: Decorate+warn shipped in 188cbe45: SelfStaleness/self_staleness + _stale_host hook on BOTH MCP servers (core + catalog, critic HIGH-1). Never refuses. GH #1414 issue itself stays OPEN until this reaches a PyPI release.

Never refuses.

title: operator dispatch discards stdout on non-zero claude -p exit — 'exited 1:' with no diagnosis (GH #1414)
description:
Steve Harris, GH #1414 suggestion 3. src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py:342-346 builds the OperatorError message from stderr ONLY. claude -p --output-format json reports errors on STDOUT, so a non-zero exit with a real diagnostic surfaces as literally 'claude -p exited 1:' with an empty snippet — which is what nx_plan_audit gave him, twice, with nothing in ~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log either.

The same function already knows better: the asyncio.TimeoutError branch (~line 333-339) drains BOTH pipes and persists them via _persist_timeout_log, with a comment (nexus-1at5) that discarding the output makes the next debugging session start from zero. The non-zero-exit branch never got the same treatment. Fix is to include stdout in the error (and consider the same persist-to-log path when both streams are non-trivial), so the failure is diagnosable regardless of which stream claude used.

Note this is INDEPENDENT of the stale-process root cause in that issue: whatever made claude -p fail, the error surface should have carried its output.
close_reason:
Shipped as 5f967f65 on develop. Full suite 14184 passed / 0 failed.

Both halves of the bead's sketch are addressed, though the second differently than sketched: the error now reports whichever stream carried text (with an explicit sentinel when the subprocess was silent), and a structlog operator_dispatch_failed event at the choke point gives every one of the 17 call sites a record — rather than the per-call-site persist the bead originally imagined.

Deliberately NOT claimed as nexus-1at5 parity. That branch writes a dedicated uncapped per-incident file and names its path in the exception; this writes a capped event into the shared 10MB x 5 rotating mcp.log with no pointer back. And durability is a property of the CALLING process's logging mode, not the choke point: the 15 mcp-mode sites get the file handler, the 2 taxonomy CLI sites get stderr only. Residuals tracked as nexus-ri56e (addressability, retention, CLI coverage — with the warning not to port _persist_timeout_log literally, since its no-cleanup design is only safe because timeouts are rare) and nexus-l1qpj (per-failure stderr volume in the taxonomy batches, untested).

Stacked review earned its keep four times across two rounds, none visible to a green suite: the nexus-1at5 overclaim, the mcp.log gap being systemic rather than nx_plan_audit-only (13 of 17 sites bare, 3 with no covered path), silent truncation of the log field (the same 'silence must read as silence' principle this diff designed into the exception, missing one field over), and a code comment left contradicting its own corrected commit message. Three independent enumerations of the call sites gave 12/17/17 — the first was an inherited partial list presented as traced, which is the exact sampling-as-inventory failure nexus-ou4tb is open over.

Root cause of the GH #1414 failure itself is untouched and remains open as nexus-g6vb4 (MCP host cannot self-detect staleness after an in-place uv tool upgrade; upgrade_finish.py:197 excludes pid == me by construction).

title: nx forensics/chash-poison probe is LOCAL-ONLY by design — say so instead of reporting 'no nexus_diag credentials'
description:
Hal decision 2026-07-20, answering conexus round-22 ASK (T2 conexus [20987]): option (b). The client-side diagnostic path (nx forensics, the RDR-182 pre-upgrade chash-poison probe) is local-only BY DESIGN. We are NOT adding remote reachability — no host/dbname/sslmode in DiagCredentials, no credential resolution outside the local bundle.

What remains is an honesty fix, not a capability: today src/nexus/db/diag_connection.py resolve_diag_credentials() returns port/user/password and never sets host or dbname, so they fall to the DiagCredentials defaults (host=127.0.0.1, dbname=nexus), and the path shells to a local psql reading the local bundle pg_credentials file. On a managed/BYO deployment the probe can therefore only ever report 'no nexus_diag credentials', which an operator cannot distinguish from 'not provisioned'. conexus read our source to find this out; it cost them real time.

Scope: (1) when not is_local_mode(), refuse with an explicit local-only-by-design message naming the contract, rather than a missing-credentials message; (2) state the contract in the diag_connection module docstring and wherever nx forensics is documented, so the next reader does not infer a gap; (3) no new verb, no knob.

Related: nexus-tcqah owns the diag view provisioning/ownership design. RDR-182 owns the probe. conexus is recording (b) as the intended contract on their side and has corrected their bead's acceptance criterion accordingly.
close_reason: Shipped: live_store_detail refuses with LOCAL-ONLY-by-design contract when not is_local_mode() (zero resolution work on refusal, test-pinned); module + DiagCredentials docstrings state the contract (remote fields = contract change requiring Hal decision); cli-reference nx forensics + configuration.md BYO-role docs updated. No new verb, no knob. Commit follows with the cluster batch.

title: Census counting method under-reports BLOCKED events — a real block recorded as BLOCKED=0
description:
Found 2026-07-20 while checking whether the nexus-3h0u6 row-doubling had corrupted the .11 census.

THE DISCREPANCY. The 2026-07-19 session bfbfa2fe is recorded as a supplementary census row in a comment on nexus-ccs9v.11, reporting: 'EXPECT=2 (reviewer-1010, critic-1010), REPORTED=2, BLOCKED=0, WOULDBLOCK=0'.

The actual expectations file for that session (~/.local/state/nexus/orchestration/bfbfa2fe-*.expectations) contains:

  15:27:17  START     areviewer-1010-1b8b89048ae224ed
  15:27:31  START     acritic-1010-efef627874d62606
  15:33:49  BLOCKED   acritic-1010-efef627874d62606     <-- recorded as BLOCKED=0
  15:34:12  REPORTED  areviewer-1010-1b8b89048ae224ed

(every hook-written row appears twice — the nexus-3h0u6 doubling, fixed in 99da8fde. Deduplicated above for readability.)

critic-1010 was BLOCKED and has NO REPORTED row at all: START, BLOCKED, nothing else. The census recorded BLOCKED=0.

WHY IT MATTERS. nexus-ccs9v.11 exists specifically to measure the guard's false-block rate, and nexus-ccs9v.15's default-ON flip was gated on that measurement. A BLOCKED event counted as zero is exactly the error class the census was built to detect. The block here may well have been LEGITIMATE (an agent that genuinely stopped without reporting) — but legitimate-and-miscounted is indistinguishable from false-and-miscounted in the recorded data, and the recorded data says it did not happen.

SCOPE — what is NOT affected. nexus-ccs9v.11 itself is closed on session 94a4c63c (2026-07-18), whose file I checked directly: rows are NOT doubled and the census matches (EXPECT=3 START=3 REPORTED=3 BLOCKED=0). That measurement stands. This is about the counting METHOD, which the still-open nexus-ccs9v.19 will reuse.

LIKELY CAUSE (unverified): the counts appear to have been taken per-agent rather than per-row, which is a reasonable way to cope with the doubled rows but silently drops a BLOCKED that has no matching REPORTED. Whatever the cause, the method produced a number that contradicts the file.

TO FIX:
1. Re-derive the bfbfa2fe census from the file and correct the comment on nexus-ccs9v.11, including whether that block was false or legitimate (cross-check the session transcript for whether critic-1010 reported after being blocked).
2. Write the census down as a SCRIPT, not a hand count, so .19 and any later measurement cannot drift from the file the same way. tests/e2e/lib/expectations.sh already has expectations_sweep/expectations_undeclared to build on.
3. Re-check whether .15's default-ON acceptance is affected. Probably not — .11 closed on clean 07-18 data — but it should be an explicit answer, not an assumption.
close_reason: All 3 fix items + the 07-21 complement delivered. (1) bfbfa2fe re-derived by script + .11 comment corrected: EXPECT=2 START=2 REPORTED=1 BLOCKED=1; block LEGITIMATE and RESOLVED (critic-1010's only SendMessage 26s post-block). (2) Census is now a SCRIPT: expectations_census in expectations.sh (both copies, synced) — dedups 3h0u6-doubled rows, classifies per-agent terminal state (REPORTED/BLOCKED_RESOLVED/BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED/WOULDBLOCK/NO_TERMINAL/undeclared/expected_no_start); 9 new shell tests + fixture reproducing the exact bfbfa2fe shape. (3) .15 default-ON acceptance EXPLICITLY unaffected: .11 closed on 94a4c63c, script-re-verified 7/7 REPORTED BLOCKED=0; population-wide, all 18 BLOCKED events across all 17 ledgers were legitimate AND resolved 15-30s post-block (transcript-verified) — false-block rate remains 0, so the flip's evidence base is STRONGER than at acceptance. ROOT CAUSE of the 07-21 'over-report' complement: not channel-sensitivity — the once-guard exits (stop_hook_active + already_blocked) recorded NOTHING post-block, so a resolved block was ledger-identical to a dead agent, and later rounds of a once-blocked agent (gh1414-critic r2/r3) left no trace. FIXED: subagent-stop.sh now stamps a REPORTED resolution row from both exits (fail-open, never re-blocks); 7 new pytest cases, mutation-falsified.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Complement evidence 2026-07-21 (session b819e8f3): census OVER-reports BLOCKED, not just under. Ledger: EXPECT=11 START=7 REPORTED=3 BLOCKED=6 WOULDBLOCK=0. All 6 BLOCKED rows (gh1414-critic, gh1414-arc-critic, all 4 docs-auditor-*) were agents that DELIVERED complete findings to main via SendMessage; only gh1414-code-reviewer's hand-backs registered REPORTED (3/3 rounds). The guard's REPORTED detection appears path-sensitive: one delivery channel classifies REPORTED, the other BLOCKED. Fix scope: classify by delivery outcome, not channel.

title: Orchestration hook coverage silently absent if the installed conexus plugin predates the hook registrations
description:
Found by substantive-critic reviewing nexus-3h0u6 (99da8fde), 2026-07-20.

3h0u6 removed the .claude/settings.json registration of subagent-start-stamp.sh / subagent-stop.sh, leaving conexus/hooks/hooks.json as the single surface. Correct for the doubling, but it removes the ONLY fallback.

THE GAP: anyone whose installed conexus plugin is pinned to a tag predating the hook entries (they landed ~78bb02b6 / d613f2e7, both ancestors of v6.14.0) now gets ZERO orchestration-hook coverage — not doubled, not single, silently absent. No EXPECT/START/REPORTED rows, no stop guard, no signal. That defeats nexus-ccs9v.15's default-on live-block directive entirely for those installs.

Strictly worse than the bug fixed: doubling was a census data-quality nuisance; silent absence is no coverage at all.

Note the repo's own state makes this concrete rather than hypothetical: develop's pyproject is 6.11.0 and marketplace.json pins v6.11.0, while the hooks shipped in the v6.14.0 lineage on main. The release rule (source.ref points only at immutable release tags) means an install can legitimately sit on an older pin.

test_orchestration_hooks_are_registered_exactly_once only inspects the two static JSON files in this tree — it cannot see the operator's installed plugin version, and nothing else checks it.

FIX SHAPE (the critic's suggestion, and it avoids re-adding the redundant registration): a version-floor check that compares the INSTALLED conexus plugin version against the floor that first carried both hook entries, surfaced via nx doctor or a SessionStart warning. Detection, not duplication.

Do NOT fix by restoring the .claude/settings.json entries — that reinstates the doubling and re-corrupts the nexus-ccs9v.11 census.
close_reason: Doctor check shipped: _check_orchestration_hook_floor (health.py) reads installed_plugins.json, warns when the newest installed conexus plugin < v6.14.0 (_ORCH_HOOKS_PLUGIN_FLOOR, floor rationale in the constant's docstring) with /plugin update conexus as the fix. CLI-side by necessity — a pre-floor plugin's own hooks.json predates any warning hook (the fix-shape reasoning in the bead: detection, not duplication; .claude/settings.json entries NOT restored). 12 tests (v2 schema, marketplace suffixes, newest-wins, fail-open on missing/malformed/unparseable); live-verified on this box. Docs: cli-reference doctor section. Commit on develop.

  START    ab878d-critic-1f159...              <- written TWICE
  START    ab878d-critic-1f159...
  REPORTED ab878d-critic-1f159...              <- written TWICE
  REPORTED ab878d-critic-1f159...
  ... every subsequent REPORTED likewise doubled

Every hook-written row is duplicated. EXPECT rows, which the orchestrator writes by sourcing the shellib directly, are single. So the doubling is in hook dispatch, not in _expectations_append.

ROOT CAUSE. subagent-start-stamp.sh and subagent-stop.sh are each registered in TWO places and both fire:
  - conexus/hooks/hooks.json:103,115  (via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT)
  - .claude/settings.json:9,21        (via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)

WHY IT MATTERS. nexus-ccs9v.11 is the census bead: it exists to count EXPECT x START x REPORTED x WOULDBLOCK rows from a real multi-agent repo session and decide whether the guard is behaving. Its raw material is currently inflated 2x for every hook-written row while EXPECT stays 1x, so any EXPECT-vs-REPORTED ratio computed from it is wrong by construction. nexus-ccs9v.15's bead-close rides on .11. A census run against doubled data would either read as a systematic anomaly or, worse, be silently normalized.

SECOND-ORDER. The two registrations are not equivalent: .claude/settings.json wraps the call with NX_ORCH_STOP_GUARD="${NX_ORCH_STOP_GUARD:-block}"; the plugin copy passes no env at all. The script's own default is also block (line 49, MODE="${NX_ORCH_STOP_GUARD:-block}") so both currently land on block and behaviour happens to agree — but that is coincidence, not design, and a future change to either default would make the two invocations disagree with each other within a single event.

FIX SHAPE. Pick ONE registration surface and delete the other. The .15 flip deliberately put the default-on wiring in .claude/settings.json so repo sessions run live-block; if that is the intended surface, the plugin's hooks.json entries should go (or vice versa). Then re-verify a real multi-agent session produces exactly one row per event before .11 runs its census.

DO NOT just dedupe rows at read time in the census — that hides a double-dispatch that also means the stop guard's block decision is evaluated twice per subagent stop.
close_reason: Closed

title: PG bundle extract marker is version-blind — a bundle major/minor change would never install
description: VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY 2026-07-20: nexus/db/pg_bundle.py's extraction marker (.nx_bundle_extracted) is an EMPTY file carrying no version. is_bundle_extracted() returns True on any complete prior tree, so extract_bundle() handed a DIFFERENT archive returns the OLD bin dir and leaves the OLD binaries in place (probe: seeded a fake old tree + marker, passed a new archive, binaries unchanged and 'pg_bundle_already_extracted' logged). Latent, not yet biting: PG_VERSION in engine-service-release.yml has been 17.5 for the whole history, so no bundle version change has ever shipped. The moment it does (17.5 -> 18.x, or a security patch bump), every existing install silently keeps the old PostgreSQL binaries. FIX SHAPE: stamp the marker with the bundle version (or reuse the nexus-pg.meta.json tag/sha already written by binary_install) and re-extract on mismatch. NOTE the harder half: a data directory created by PG N cannot be started by PG N+1 binaries, so a real major bump additionally needs pg_upgrade or dump/restore — that part is RDR-scale and is NOT this bead. Related evidence: an install carrying a v0.1.17-era archive alongside a PG16 cluster dir from the pre-bundle host-PG era.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ATTRIBUTE step, part 1 of 2 (2026-07-20, post-v0.1.50 deploy): WRITE-PATH LEAK ANALYSIS — the answer is YES, THE PATHS STILL LEAK, all of them. The debt regrows under any chunk-deleting workload. Verified inventory, file:line:

L1 (the root): PgVectorRepository.delete (service .../vectors/PgVectorRepository.java:2008) deletes CHUNK ROWS ONLY. The manifest obligation is explicitly punted to callers as an application-enforced FK (T2 nexus_rdr/155-manifest-fk-decision); chash_index is not even MENTIONED — no cleanup, no documented caller obligation, nothing. Every per-chunk delete in the system flows through here.

L2: PDF stale-chunk prune (pipeline_stages.py ~1048): col.delete(ids) in 300-batches, no chash_index, no manifest.

L3: misclassified-chunk prune (indexer.py _batched_delete callers ~2160-2225, both manifest-keyed and doc_id-keyed legs): chunk rows only.

L4: deleted-files GC (indexer.py _prune_deleted_files -> chunk_quarantine.py): quarantine_orphans copies to a quarantine-prefix collection then deletes from live (:176) — pointer survives, and chash still resolves in the chunks table so it is NOT yet census-dangling; expire_quarantine (:296) hard-deletes after the grace window — THAT is the moment the chash_index row goes dangling. grep chash_index chunk_quarantine.py = zero hits.

L5: upsert-supersede: re-index UPSERT-on-(doc_id,position) repoints the manifest slot to the new chash; the OLD chash's chunk row survives until L4 GCs it, then its pointer dangles.

THE ONLY CLEANUP THAT EXISTS: (a) collection-wide delete_collection (clean, but only fires on whole-collection removal); (b) a lazy self-heal in catalog_spans.py:367 whose staleness test is COLLECTION-level (row collection not in live collections) — a pointer into a LIVE collection whose chunk is gone is never healed by anything, and it only fires when a span resolution happens to look up that exact chash.

MECHANISM SUMMARY: chash_index rows are written on every chunk upsert and deleted on (almost) no chunk delete. The 292,230 orphans are the integral of L2-L5 over the store's lifetime. The created_at window ending 2026-07-06 is NOT evidence the leak stopped — content writes stopped then (window closed).

CANDIDATE FIX (design fork for Hal, NOT decided): PgVectorRepository.delete's key (collection, chash IN ids) is exactly chash_index's natural key (chash, physical_collection) — delete the pointer rows in the SAME transaction, engine-side, single choke point (same lesson as nexus-q6830: N callers each remembering to opt in is the failure class). Manifest stays a caller obligation (doc-keyed, already documented). Alternative: caller-side pairing, which requires 4+ Python sites to each remember. Leak fix must land BEFORE the DELETE step or the envelope is chasing a moving target.

LIFECYCLE: PyPI (client).
D4: _nexus_t3_steps (commands/upgrade.py:687, created inline mid-command) is upgrade bookkeeping registered in no migration registry — RDR-158 P4 would silently drop it. Subsume into the ladder mechanism (P2 ladder_completions / in-process holder) rather than carry a standalone inline table.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN (2026-07-18, orchestrator — pinned pre-implementation; the tree is frozen for the .7/.8/.12 landing and .15 touches commands/upgrade.py which is in .12's commit set, so .15 lands as the NEXT commit after):
SUBSUMPTION SHAPE: T3-step completion becomes ledger records in the SAME CompletionLedger the ladder uses (DeferredLadderLedger + InProcessCompletionHolder → PG nexus.ladder_completions), keyed rung_name = 't3-step:<introduced>:<name>' (namespaced; can never collide with real rungs; ignored by derive_ladder_position by construction — pinned by test_rows_outside_the_order_are_ignored, position only consults the canonical ORDER).
- READ: done_set = names with the t3-step: prefix from holder.verified_rungs(). WRITE: holder.record_verified(key, package_version=current, detail=step.name) after the step succeeds; flush at block end (same RF-186-2 class: a lost record costs one redundant re-run of an idempotent step — T3_UPGRADES currently holds exactly ONE step, the 4.2.0 backfill_projection; VERIFY its idempotency in the TDD, it is the whole risk surface).

- CENSUS: tests/test_no_new_sqlite.py commands/upgrade.py DDL entry (1, the stray) drops in the SAME commit; check the ALTER entry (3) — only lower what the deletion removes. Falsify per the bead: leave the inline CREATE → census fails to shrink.
- ENGINE DEPENDENCY: none new — rides the same /v1/ladder surface as .12 (engine >= v0.1.46).

title: nx doctor false-flags Chroma Cloud creds on a migrated service-mode install (✗ when present as shell-env-only AND ✗ when absent → EXIT 1)
description:
Surfaced during Hal's 6.12.0 post-restart validation 2026-07-17. Third member of the retired-Chroma-machinery-nags-a-migrated-install cluster (with nexus-dv708 dead-cloud-leg hard-fail + nexus-tidtd count-equality convergence flaw).

nx doctor treats Chroma Cloud creds (CHROMA_API_KEY/CHROMA_DATABASE/CHROMA_TENANT) as EXPECTED, so a migrated service-mode install (T3 mode: cloud via the conexus service; Chroma is only the retired rollback source) gets a no-win result:
- WITH the creds present in shell env: ✗ 'Credential persistence (GUI spawn): N credentials in shell env only ... GUI-spawned consumers will misdetect cloud mode as local mode'.
- WITHOUT them (clean terminal): ✗ 'ChromaDB (CHROMA_API_KEY): not set', ✗ 'ChromaDB (CHROMA_DATABASE): not set' -> nx doctor EXIT=1.

Neither reflects a real problem: the install is healthy (migration reports clean, total_failed=0, verification=verified; service reachable at release_version 0.1.44; Voyage set). The Chroma-cred checks predate the move-to-service and should be conditional on Chroma actually being an active backend, not required unconditionally.

BLAST RADIUS: single install (Hal; only Chroma-era service install). Cosmetic, but the absent-cred path makes nx doctor exit 1 in a clean terminal, which any automation keying on doctor exit code would misread as unhealthy.

FIX (with the RDR-185 follow-up, alongside dv708/tidtd): make the Chroma-cred doctor checks conditional on the install actually being in / needing Chroma-cloud mode. A migrated service-mode install (has service_url + service_token + voyage_api_key, migration verified) should not be flagged for absent OR shell-env-only Chroma creds. Verify against Hal's install: nx doctor should exit 0 with no Chroma-cred ✗ once the checks are service-mode-aware.

Cluster: nexus-dv708 (P2), nexus-tidtd (P1). Operational state today: NX_MIGRATION_NOTICE=0 in Hal's ~/.zshrc unblocks nx upgrade; nx doctor still shows these cosmetic ✗ marks (this bead).
close_reason: Fixed as bf3ddae6 on develop (one pass with c7aj3 per the pinned fix shape): doctor cred lines informational always (exit-1 false-positive gone) AND the shell-env-only false-flag premise-gated in _check_credential_persistence (service_url persisted = mode anchored; verified silent on the real repro config, mutation-verified). Tradeoff for pre-migration installs disclosed in-code + on c7aj3.

title: substrate-etl detect() hard-fails when a configured Chroma Cloud read leg has DEAD creds (open_read_legs only degrades on half-configured, not on auth failure)
description:
REGRESSION surfaced on 6.12.0 nx upgrade (Hal's live cloud install, 2026-07-17). Chain: substrate_etl.detect() -> _plan() -> _classify() -> detect_pending_migration_memoized() -> open_read_legs() -> open_cloud_read_client() -> chromadb.CloudClient() -> get_user_identity() -> ChromaError: Permission denied (revoked Chroma Cloud creds) -> propagates -> runner maps detect() exception to RungOutcome.FAILED (hard edge) -> 'nx upgrade did not converge', exit nonzero.

Root cause: src/nexus/migration/detection.py open_read_legs() cloud branch catches ONLY RuntimeError (the half-configured/missing-creds sentinel from open_cloud_read_client). A configured-but-DEAD cloud leg (creds present in env/config but revoked) raises ChromaError (auth) or a connection error, which is NOT caught -> propagates -> hard-fail.

BLAST RADIUS: single user. Trigger requires chroma_database + chroma_api_key BOTH configured (else RuntimeError -> cloud=None, already handled) AND the creds fail to auth. Only Chroma Cloud installs have those creds; Hal is the only Chroma Cloud install ever (all others local/greenfield-managed). Confirmed not a general regression; NOT patch-worthy on its own.

FIX (small, defensive, aligned with the retired-Chroma-Cloud decree): broaden open_read_legs' cloud except to also degrade a configured-but-unreachable/unauthorized cloud leg to cloud=None with a LOUD warning (mirror _default_prior_collections' 'degrade loud, do not crash the trigger' pattern). A dead/revoked cloud leg is functionally 'no cloud source to migrate' — the retired managed-migration path. Do NOT swallow silently; WARNING naming the leg + error. Add a test: configured-but-CloudClient-raises-ChromaError -> cloud=None, not raise. Rides the next normal release; no emergency patch (population of one + trivial workaround: clear the dead creds).

WORKAROUND for Hal now: clear the stale Chroma Cloud creds (env CHROMA_API_KEY/DATABASE/TENANT + config.yml credentials.chroma_*), then nx upgrade -> cloud leg reads unconfigured -> RuntimeError -> cloud=None -> converges.
close_reason: Closed

title: TOCTOU race in get_http_vector_client's fast-path cached-probe check can raise TypeError instead of ManagedServiceError
design:
Found during substantive-critique of the uncommitted nexus-5t1jp diff
(src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py, tests/db/test_http_vector_client_version_gate.py).

BUG: the unguarded fast-path check at the top of get_http_vector_client():

    if cloud_mode and _cached_probe_error_binding():
        _reraise_cached_probe_error(_version_probe_error)

reads the module global `_version_probe_error` TWICE — once inside
_cached_probe_error_binding() (which validates the cached error is still
authoritative) and once again on the next line to pass to
_reraise_cached_probe_error(). Before nexus-5t1jp, `_version_probe_error`
was write-once in production (None -> error, never back to None outside
reset_http_vector_client_for_tests, which is test-only) — the surrounding
comment at http_vector_client.py:1970-1975 explicitly documents this
as the reason the unguarded read is safe ("Only the WRITE path ... holds
the lock. Cleared by reset_http_vector_client_for_tests").

nexus-5t1jp's healing feature adds a THIRD, PRODUCTION write path: inside
get_http_vector_client()'s locked section, an expired UNREACHABLE-class
cache is cleared (_version_probe_error = None) before re-probing. That
comment's invariant is now false, but the comment was not updated and the
fast-path read was not made race-safe.

RACE: Thread A evaluates _cached_probe_error_binding() and gets True
(window not yet expired at A's read). Before A's next statement executes,
thread B (already inside the lock, deciding independently that the window
HAS expired) clears _version_probe_error to None and starts a fresh probe.
If A's next statement (_version_probe_error read for the reraise call)
executes in this gap, it sees None and calls
_reraise_cached_probe_error(None), i.e. `raise type(None)(str(None))` ->
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable — not a ManagedServiceError.
This breaks every caller's `except ManagedServiceError` / `except
RuntimeError` handling (e.g. nexus.commands.store._t3's `except
RuntimeError as exc: raise click.ClickException(...)`), producing a raw
uncaught TypeError instead of a clean fail-loud error.

Exposure is real, not just theoretical: FastMCP (src/nexus/mcp/core.py,
`mcp = FastMCP("nexus", lifespan=_t1_chroma_lifespan)`) dispatches sync
tool functions off-thread, so concurrent T3 tool calls genuinely run on
different threads in the same long-running MCP server process — exactly
the population nexus-5t1jp targets. The race window is narrow (needs two
threads straddling the exact _PROBE_UNREACHABLE_RETRY_S boundary with a
GIL preemption landing in a 1-statement gap) but is a genuine new hazard
this diff introduces; it did not exist when the cache was write-once.

FIX: close the TOCTOU window by reading _version_probe_error exactly
once per decision point. Simplest shape: have _cached_probe_error_binding
return the validated Exception (or None) instead of a bool, so the caller
reraises the SAME snapshot it validated:

    cached = _cached_probe_error_binding()  # returns Exception | None
    if cloud_mode and cached is not None:
        _reraise_cached_probe_error(cached)

Also update the stale comment at http_vector_client.py:1970-1975 to
acknowledge the new production write path (the healing-clear), not just
reset_http_vector_client_for_tests.

SEPARATE, LOWER-SEVERITY FINDING same diff: reset_http_vector_client_for_tests()
adds `global _version_probe_failed_at` but never assigns to it — an
incomplete reset relative to its own docstring ("reset ... the cloud
version-probe cache"). Currently masked/dead (every write to
_version_probe_error is always paired with a fresh
_version_probe_failed_at stamp, and reads of _version_probe_failed_at are
always gated behind `_version_probe_error is not None`), but it's a latent
trap for future refactors. Fix: add `_version_probe_failed_at = None` to
the reset body.

Also: tests/db/test_http_vector_client_version_gate.py's MODULE docstring
(lines 3-12) still claims "a failure is cached and re-raised verbatim on
every subsequent call (never re-probed)" -- no longer true for the
UNREACHABLE class post-5t1jp. Needs a one-line update noting the bounded
retry window, so a reader of just the module docstring isn't misled.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Cloud-mode T3 probe failure is cached for the process lifetime — no re-probe when the managed service comes back (brw1s's disease one layer down)
description:
Found by the substantive-critic during the nexus-brw1s review (2026-07-17), verified independently beforehand: the SAME cached-forever pathology brw1s fixed for T1, one layer down, in cloud mode only.

THE PATH: get_http_vector_client (http_vector_client.py ~2080-2120) runs probe_managed_service() once per process in cloud mode (service_url set => not is_local_mode()). On failure the error is stored in module-global _version_probe_error and EVERY subsequent call re-raises a fresh copy — by design ("re-probing a state we already know"), with NO production re-probe path; reset_http_vector_client_for_tests is test-only.

CONSEQUENCE: a cloud-mode session whose managed service is down at the FIRST T3 tool call has search/query/store cached-failed for the REST OF THE SESSION — even after the service comes back. That is exactly the disease brw1s cured for T1 (a transient outage cached for the process lifetime), and unlike T1 it does not self-heal on service arrival. The T1 mint path heals precisely because resolve_service_endpoint caches no negative (verified: service_endpoint.py 357-410; the _has_ever_resolved_lease global is positive-only).

POPULATION: cloud-mode sessions only (operator's own; local mode skips the probe entirely — verified against the GH #1405 field shape). NOT mooted by the migration decree: this is the LIVE managed SERVING path.

FIX DIRECTION: drop the cached _version_probe_error for the UNREACHABLE class specifically (ManagedServiceUnreachable) so connectivity failures re-probe on next call, while keeping the cache for INCOMPATIBLE (below-floor engine — genuinely stable within a process, and the original nexus-b6qlf rationale). The nexus-b6qlf traceback-accumulation concern (why the cache exists) applies to re-RAISING the same instance, not to re-probing; a bounded re-probe (e.g. not more than once per N seconds) also satisfies it.

CROSS-REF: nexus-brw1s's deferral wording was narrowed to name this bead rather than claim "every non-T1 tool is unaffected" universally (false in cloud mode until this closes).
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Mislabel-on-voyage-service fails mid-flight with HTTP 422 instead of a pregate diagnosis (seed_legacy's untracked 'tracked separately')
description:
Found while verifying the eb8edd73 mislabel fix (RDR-185 P5, 2026-07-17). seed_legacy.py:428 says this is "tracked separately" — no bead matches any search for it. Filing so the claim is true.

THE SHAPE: a measured-768 mislabel (voyage-NAMED collection whose stored vectors are local ONNX 768) on a VOYAGE-MODE (cloud) service. remap_target_model returns the ONNX model UNCONDITIONALLY for measured-768 content — correct, vectors that were never voyage must never bill a voyage re-embed — so the leg's target is always the bge-768 name. A voyage-only service has no bge embedder and refuses the upsert with HTTP 422, failing the leg MID-FLIGHT (empirical: the first with-cloud run post-itme7, 2026-07-13; seed_legacy.py:420-428 records it and stopped seeding _MISLABEL on --with-cloud because of it).

NOTE the codebase contradiction while here: detection.py:321 claims "bge is wired in both deployment modes per wired_models; the deployed engine's /version smoke lists it" — the seeder's empirical 422 says a voyage-mode service has NO bge embedder. Both cannot be true; whoever picks this up should establish ground truth against the deployed engine first (the critic's eb8edd73 review read Main.java:105-140 and EmbedderRouter — start there).

WHY IT MATTERS MORE SINCE eb8edd73: the mislabel fix routes measured-768 collections to the bge target in BOTH modes now (previously the keyed branch skipped them as "conformant" — silently broken recall). So on a cloud install, a mislabeled collection moves from silently-skipped to loud-mid-flight-422. Loud beats silent, but the 422 arrives MID-WALK with a transport error, not up front with a diagnosis.

FIX DIRECTION (the seeder's own suggestion): the pregate should block it up front with a real diagnostic ("collection X's vectors are local ONNX but this deployment serves only voyage — re-index from source, or migrate via a local service") rather than a mid-flight HTTP 422. Plan-time is the right altitude: is_measured_dim_override already identifies the shape at classification.

NO LIVE GATE: --era-hop/--with-cloud are structurally incoherent (seed_legacy.py:347-351), so no container leg can currently seed this. Unit-level: plan the shape with a voyage-only wired set and assert the pregate surfaces it.
close_reason: MOOTED under the same population decree that closed nexus-bmiq9 (Hal, 2026-07-17: 'we're done with chromadb cloud migration... no one has that but us and we're fine and dandy'). This bead's trigger requires a VOYAGE-KEYED migration shape — voyage-named collections and/or a Voyage key making the remap target billable. That population is exactly one install (Hal's), and its migration completed 2026-06. Everyone else is all-local bge/minilm with no key: no billed leg is ever planned and this path is unreachable. title: [bug] A consent-deferred rung is invisible on --auto, and doctor's remedy is the verb that deferred
description:
Found by the substantive-critic in RDR-185 P5 r4, carried in r5, previously unfiled.

That is the impossible-remedy shape RDR-185 exists to end, and this repo already settled the principle 90 lines away in the same file: health.py's _check_legacy_id_census (bead nexus-mq42b) names the remedy that ACTUALLY works for a collection the upgrade cannot converge, precisely because "the row's silence reads as 'the upgrade will handle it'". title: [bug] nx upgrade --auto never reaches the cost gate: an explicit unattended declaration loses to the isatty proxy
description:
Found by the substantive-critic in RDR-185 P5 r5 (c8346c6f review).

`nx upgrade --auto` is the command's EXPLICIT declaration that nobody is watching — it is the SessionStart hook surface. That declaration is discarded before it can reach the consent gate:

  * registry.py builds SubstrateEtlRung() with NO arguments, so cost_gate_fn is the default.
  * _default_cost_gate(plan) takes only `plan`.
  * auto_mode stops at _run_ladder and is never threaded further.

So the gate falls back to guessing with _has_terminal() (sys.stdin.isatty()) when ground truth is one parameter away. With an inherited tty, `nx upgrade --auto` PROMPTS — the exact "silent hang on a click.confirm no hook can answer" that upgrade()'s own docstring says --yes exists to prevent.

WHY IT IS NOT LIVE TODAY: conexus/hooks/hooks.json:9 is `nx upgrade --auto 2>/dev/null || ...` and Claude Code pipes JSON to hook stdin, so stdin is not a tty and the proxy agrees with the truth. It does not hold for a wrapper that allocates a tty, a `--auto` typed in a terminal, or any future caller. The proxy is a guess that happens to be right on the one surface anyone checked.

FIX: pass auto_mode into the rung's cost gate so the explicit declaration beats the proxy. A caller that SAYS it is unattended must be believed over an inference about its file descriptors. _has_terminal() then remains the fallback for callers that say nothing.

NOTE the ordering that makes this safe today: _default_cost_gate checks assume_yes() BEFORE _has_terminal(), so a hook that sets NX_ASSUME_YES converges regardless of tty. That order is pinned by test_standing_consent_lets_a_billed_walk_converge_unattended (its first draft forced a terminal and left the order unpinned — the sixth vacuous pin of the arc).

title: [bug] A mislabeled voyage collection can bill on a pure re-id leg — billed means 'might bill', not 'will bill'
description:
Found by the code reviewer in RDR-185 P5 r3, then RE-OPENED by the substantive-critic in r4 after the first attempt at fixing it broke SC-1.

THE PATH: a re-id-only leg (needs_reembed=False) passes stored vectors through. _provenance_scrub drops the vector of any chunk whose recorded embedding_model disagrees with the target's declared model segment (the nexus-bfdri mismatch-only rule, working as designed). run_batched_etl attaches embeddings only if EVERY chunk in the batch has one — so ONE mismatched chunk sends embeddings=None for the whole batch and the service re-embeds all of it. If the target declares a Voyage model, that is BILLED, with needs_reembed False the entire time and therefore no consent prompt.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED BY WIDENING: the r3 fix set billed = (target's declared model is a voyage model), for every leg. That reads TRUE for any voyage-declared collection carrying legacy ids — because a pure re-id leg's target IS its source name. That is SC-1's motivating install (the 18-collection 2026-07-16 work instance) and precisely the leg SC-2 promises costs nothing ("Zero re-embedding and zero source-file requirements for pure id-scheme conformance"). Combined with r4's "no terminal declines" rule, that install stopped converging at all and reported exit 0 while doing it — a silent permanent non-convergence on the RDR's flagship shape. Reverted to `needs_reembed and _leg_can_bill(target)`.

So the residual is back, narrowed: a MISLABELED voyage-declared collection (recorded provenance != its own name) with legacy ids can bill without asking.

THE MISSING INPUT: whether a collection's recorded provenance disagrees with its name is a PLAN-TIME question, and nothing answers it today. CollectionClassification carries model (from the NAME) and measured_dim — but measured_dim is not probed for legacy collections (legacy_ids suppresses should_probe_dim), so is_measured_dim_override is always False for exactly the population in question.

FIX DIRECTION (critic's): resolve provenance at classification time — sample the recorded embedding_model and compare it against the declared segment, the same comparison _provenance_scrub makes per chunk. Then LegPlan.billed means WILL bill rather than MIGHT bill: the ask survives intact for genuine re-embeds, and SC-1's pure re-id converges unattended with nothing to consent to. Reuse the scrub's own test (_declared_model) rather than re-deriving it — that drift is what produced nexus-j5diu.

SCOPE NOTE: this is the ONLY case where billed is wrong, and it is wrong in the silent-bill direction, which is why it must not be left indefinitely. It is narrow (the bfdri mislabel class) but it is real money without consent.

NO LIVE GATE: the era-hop is local bge-768, so no billed leg is ever planned. See nexus-3vhqk for the dummy-key leg that would gate this whole class.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Code review of c8346c6f (2026-07-17) — reachability CONFIRMED in the real ETL, plus a cheaper hardening than this bead scopes.

REACHABILITY, from source: vector_etl.py:658-684 (and :862, the resume path) gates on

    if all(c.get("embedding") is not None and _provenance_ok(c) for c in batch):

ONE mis-provenanced chunk sends embeddings=None for the WHOLE batch -> the server re-embeds it -> billed. Reachable shape: a voyage-keyed install with a mislabeled (nexus-bfdri) collection carrying legacy ids -> needs_reembed=False -> billed=False -> the consent gate is never asked -> Voyage billed with no consent. The only mitigation today is a post-hoc _log.warning at :677.

THE REVIEWERS POINT, which reframes the fix: the ETL already DISCOVERS "this batch will bill" at :665 — and merely warns about it. So the full plan-time provenance probe this bead describes is not the only route, and not the cheapest. Making that discovery a DECISION (refuse, or defer without consent) closes the hole AT THE POINT OF HARM, in the code that already knows. Plan-time provenance is the better long-term answer (it lets the prompt be accurate before any work starts); the :665 guard is the smaller one that stops the silent spend now.

Weigh both when this is picked up. Do not just port the plan-time probe because this bead said so.

TRADE ACCEPTED FOR NOW (both reviewers agree it is defensible): the alternative — the widened predicate — demonstrably broke SC-1s flagship shape (a pure re-id deferring forever at exit 0) and was strictly worse. This is billing, not data-correctness, and it is logged. But "logged" is not "consented", and the standing directive on silent fallbacks means this should not sit indefinitely.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DEMOTED from sole defense to optimization by edaa8401 (2026-07-17).

The silent bill is now REFUSED at the drop site: _provenance_scrub raises UnconsentedReembed when a drop would fall on a billed-target passthrough leg, gated on standing consent (nx upgrade --yes / NX_ASSUME_YES still authorizes it). The critic's point stands and was the whole unlock — this bead's own argument (that 'will this bill' needs provenance the PLAN cannot see) is TRUE at plan time and FALSE at the drop site, where declared, prov, and the fact of the drop are all in hand, and where the scrub runs only on legs whose plan promised billed=False.

So the money is no longer spent silently: a mislabeled voyage collection now FAILS the walk loudly, naming the collection and the two ways through (authorize with --yes, or re-index so content and name agree). Nothing billed, nothing recorded.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOW: the optimization. Plan-time provenance would let the product ASK ONCE, up front, with an accurate prompt — instead of failing mid-ETL after the walk has already done work. Strictly better UX, no longer a correctness hole. Reprioritized accordingly; it is no longer 'real money without consent'.

Pins (all falsified by re-breaking): tests/upgrade/test_substrate_leg.py::test_mis_provenanced_vector_into_a_BILLED_target_refuses (fires on the silent bill), ::test_standing_consent_allows_the_billed_fallback (consent is honoured), ::test_mis_provenanced_vector_falls_back_to_reembed_when_it_is_free (stays quiet on healthy bge installs).

NOTE the test that had to be rewritten: test_mis_provenanced_vector_falls_back_to_reembed asserted the silent bill and called it 'correctness over cost'. It was pinning the defect.

title: [task] The rung's billed-consent prompt has no dollar estimate (cewad's render_cost_confirmation is on the demoted verb)
description:
Found by the substantive-critic during RDR-185 P5 (nexus-k1m2f review).

nexus-cewad shipped an ESTIMATE-AND-CONFIRM gate: migrate_cmd._confirm_voyage_cost calls render_cost_confirmation(preview) to show the projected token spend, then asks. The substrate rung's _default_cost_gate is a REIMPLEMENTATION that asks a bare "This upgrade re-embeds collections with a billed Voyage model. Proceed?" with NO estimate.

Consenting to an unquantified bill is a materially weaker decision than the one cewad shipped, and arguably not informed consent. Its docstring used to claim it was "the EXISTING gate, unchanged" — corrected in P5 to say plainly what it is.

WHY NOT FIXED IN P5: render_cost_confirmation takes a DryRunPreview, which the rung does not build (it plans SubstratePlan legs). Composing them means teaching the rung to build a preview, or factoring the estimator out of the preview shape. Real work, outside a census bead's change.

FIX DIRECTION: one gate, one estimate, one bypass — the same compose-don't-re-derive argument source_progress's docstring makes. Either _default_cost_gate calls _confirm_voyage_cost (it carries assume_yes too), or extract the estimator so both share it. NOTE: RDR-155 P4b deletes the migration module, so a shared estimator must not live only there.

CONTEXT: P5 added NX_ASSUME_YES / nx upgrade --yes (the unattended channel SC-1 needs) and amended RDR-185 Constraints to enumerate billed re-embed as the third genuine decision. The estimate is the remaining half.
close_reason: Duplicate of nexus-byosf — the first bd create succeeded but printed no output, so I filed it twice. byosf is the survivor.

title: Eager CLI upgrade with atomic venv flip — stop coupling the engine download to a safe-swap window (RDR-143 follow-on)
description:
Hal, 2026-07-16 (6.11.0 upgrade observation): downloading the full stack regardless of mode is fine — DELAYING it, when it's the engine of the product, is weird. Root cause: uv tool uses ONE in-place venv, so upgrade == rewrite-under-live-holders; the RDR-143 lockstep hook therefore defers dispatch/effect to session boundaries, coupling the (large, ~GB with mineru[pipeline]/docling) download to the swap-safety window. The plugin updates instantly at reload while the CLI trails by a session.

Proposed shape: version-suffixed venvs + atomic symlink flip. On skew detection (SessionStart/resume hook, or plugin-reload), eagerly build the NEW venv in background (live processes keep old inodes, untouched); flip the symlink on completion; new processes pick up the new version immediately. Kills: the deferred-effect window, the live-holder refusal class (reinstall-tool --force footgun), and the sit-down-to-work download. Needs: uv tool layout compatibility check (uv may not support suffixed tool dirs — may need uv venv + manual shim management, or uv tool install --force into a staging dir then rename), PATH shim stability, doctor process-freshness interplay (old processes legitimately old until restart — existing check already handles), rollback = flip symlink back. Distribution-design adjacent to RDR-157/RDR-143; likely wants a small RDR if the uv-layout investigation says non-trivial.

reverted to pre-diff (no np.errstate suppression), the test STILL PASSES —
pytest's warning capture shows the RuntimeWarnings (divide by zero, overflow,
invalid value in matmul, x2 call sites) firing exactly as the fix's docstring
describes, but the test only asserts on structured-log event names
("clustering_minibatch_kmeans" present, "clustering_nonfinite_embeddings"
absent), which hold true identically whether or not the np.errstate
suppression exists. The "nonfinite" sibling test in the same file DOES
discriminate correctly (fails pre-diff, per the same stash check).

Net effect: the core mechanism of the fix (suppressing spurious
macOS-Accelerate RuntimeWarnings on provably-finite input) has zero
regression protection. A future refactor could silently drop the
np.errstate block and no test would catch it.

Fix: add an assertion to the finite-input test that actually exercises the
warning channel, e.g. `with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("error"); tc._cluster(...)`
(or pytest.warns(None) / recwarn fixture) asserting no RuntimeWarning
escapes on the finite path. Consider also asserting
`not np.isnan(centroids).any()` post-fit as a lightweight guard against a
genuine 0/0-produced NaN being silently masked by invalid="ignore" on
finite-but-degenerate input (e.g. duplicate/zero-norm rows) — isfinite()
gates on NaN/Inf only, not on degeneracy, so a real divide-by-zero from
degenerate finite input would now be silently swallowed with no signal.

title: taxonomy discover: check the existing-topics guard BEFORE fetch+cluster — every index run wastes the full discover cost as a designed no-op
description:
Found 2026-07-15 chasing the g7ubw verify. Non-force discover_topics returns 0 when topics already exist (both backends: HttpTaxonomyStore /topics/persist_discovered guard; CatalogTaxonomy.discover_topics docstring 'use rebuild_taxonomy to re-discover'). But the guard fires at PERSIST time — AFTER _fetch_service_vectors has fetched every chunk text (113 pages for code__1-1) + every embedding (94 batches post-g7ubw) and clustered 28k x 1024 (MiniBatchKMeans). Today's index run spent 300.3s on the taxonomy pass and created 0 topics across all three collections — all had existing topics; every collection was a full-cost no-op. This has been true of EVERY changed index run since the guard existed; topic freshness actually comes from flush-grain incremental assign_batch, and full refresh only via rebuild/--force.

Fix: in discover_for_collection (taxonomy_cmd.py), non-force path: probe taxonomy.get_topics_for_collection(collection_name) FIRST; non-empty -> log + echo 'topics exist (use nx taxonomy rebuild to re-discover)' + return 0. Probe failure falls through to the normal path (persist guard remains the atomic backstop for races). Saves the entire fetch+cluster on every index run for topic-bearing collections; zero semantic change (same return, same persisted state).

Related: nexus-tevzq (per-collection zero-change gate — complementary, gates even the probe), nexus-ou9uw (threshold refresh = the eventual real re-discover policy), nexus-du6d0 (staleness observability).

title: T1 CLI path: add total wall-clock budget + user-facing slow-path message (mint->list/get retry stack can compound silently)
description: From the nexus-cfgo9 --package-upgrade rehearsal diagnosis (2026-07-15). The T1 CLI dedicated-session path (nx scratch get et al) is three sequential HTTP round-trips (HttpTokenStore.start_session mint -> /v1/t1/list for id-resolution -> /v1/t1/get), each with a 30s httpx timeout, PLUS connect-retry-once, 401-retry-once, and an outer self-heal-remint-and-retry-once wrapper (_CliDedicatedScratchStore._call) — bounded per-call but the stack compounds to a theoretical ~150-300s total with ZERO user-facing output while it grinds. Observed in the field-shaped rehearsal: one probe exceeded 20s (intermittent — identical scenario re-ran at 0.00s; NOT engine-version-tied; root-cause candidates: token-rotation UPSERT row-lock contention, network jitter, cold start — not pinned down). Fix: client-side total-time budget across the whole op + a clear message when slow ('T1 service slow/unreachable — check nx doctor / engine convergence'), never a silent multi-minute grind. Evidence: diagnostic split-probe timings in the cfgo9 arc; static trace found no unbounded call (flock sites are local-only).
close_reason: Shipped 29d79a2b + fold 7294d4b1: wall-clock budget (NX_T1_CLI_BUDGET_S, default 60s, documented) covers the WHOLE invocation per the bead text — construction-time mint/borrow (bounded-poll lock acquire, mint-start gate) + both self-heal legs (pre-remint AND post-remint gates). Contract: budget bounds leg STARTS; in-flight legs bounded by their own httpx timeouts (worst case ~budget + one leg, never a multi-leg stack — this is the honest limit of client-side bounding without thread-based aborts, recorded here explicitly). Slow-path warning at 5s (structlog->stderr, user-visible). Both reviewers' budget findings folded; enforcement proven by intermediate-budget binding tests.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic (2026-07-23, commit 29d79a2b review): CRITICAL gap against this bead's own spec — "client-side total-time budget across the WHOLE op" is not what shipped.

Evidence (src/nexus/db/t1.py):
- The NX_T1_CLI_BUDGET_S check lives ONLY inside _CliDedicatedScratchStore._call's `except RuntimeError` branch (line ~1420), gating whether the POST-401 remint+retry leg runs. `start = time.monotonic()` is set at the top of _call, so it only ever measures the FIRST attempt of ONE op call plus (conditionally) the remint+retry.
- get_t1_database()'s tier-3 construction path now calls _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow(dedicated_id, config_dir, ...) BEFORE any _CliDedicatedScratchStore even exists (line ~1589). That call: (a) blocks on `fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` with NO timeout — unbounded if a sibling bare-CLI process holds the lock while its own mint call is slow; (b) on the mint path calls mint_t1_session_token -> HttpTokenStore.start_session, itself a 30s-timeout POST with its own internal connect-retry (i.e. up to ~60s). NONE of this is covered by NX_T1_CLI_BUDGET_S, and a failure here raises a raw wrapped RuntimeError ("T1 CLI-dedicated session mint failed...") — NOT the crafted "T1 service slow/unreachable — check nx doctor" remedy text this bead asks for.
- Even within _call, the FIRST attempt (getattr(self._store, name)(*args, **kwargs)) is itself unbounded by the budget — HttpScratchStore._post/_post_raw has its OWN internal connect-retry-once and token-refresh-retry-once (30s timeout each, so up to ~60s), and the budget check only fires AFTER that whole first attempt already completes and raises a 401. A slow-but-not-401 first attempt (e.g. server up but loaded) is never budget-gated at all — it just runs to completion, however long that takes, with only a post-hoc 5s slow-notice log line once it's already done.
- Test coverage (tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py::TestCliOpBudget) only exercises the post-401 remint-retry gate; there is no test that the CONSTRUCTION-time mint/borrow, or a non-401 slow first attempt, are bounded by NX_T1_CLI_BUDGET_S — because they aren't.

Net effect: the exact field-shaped failure this bead was opened to fix (>20s probe, theoretical 150-300s from the cfgo9 rehearsal) is only partially closed. The scenario where the FIRST leg itself is slow (not the outer self-heal compounding) is un-touched — the "never a silent multi-minute grind" promise does not hold for that path.

Recommendation before closing by875: either (a) move the budget check to wrap the WHOLE op including the construction-time mint/borrow (e.g. thread a deadline through _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow and pass an httpx timeout override derived from remaining budget into the HTTP clients), or (b) explicitly narrow the bead's scope to "bound the self-heal retry compounding only" and record that as a deliberate, documented scope reduction (with a follow-on bead for the construction-time/first-leg gap) rather than closing silently as if "whole op" was delivered.

Secondary (Significant, not blocking): read_t1_session_lease's freshness check is a bare `time.time() >= expires_at` with no margin — a borrow can hand back a token with sub-second remaining TTL. The 401 self-heal in _call generically recovers from this, so it's not a correctness bug, but it does mean jc33g's latency win (1.09s -> 0.75s) can regress to a self-heal round-trip on unlucky timing. Consider a small margin (e.g. treat <5s remaining as stale) to reduce that churn.

Tertiary (Minor): NX_T1_CLI_BUDGET_S is a new user-tunable env var with zero documentation (not in docs/cli-reference.md or any env-var reference) — only discoverable by reading the error message or source.
