title: Upgrade leaves MinerU cold: no warm-start when server absent at upgrade time (field report 2026-07-15)
description:
Field report (Hal's work instance, same box as GH #1402, conexus 6.9.0 upgrade): MinerU server was not started as part of the upgrade and had to be started manually.

Code confirms the gap: upgrade_finish.py's restart-stale sweep only CYCLES a MinerU process it finds RUNNING (stale pid -> nx mineru stop/start, spawn-policy gated). A MinerU that is absent at upgrade time (or killed before the sweep) is never started — the design defers to lazy ensure_mineru_running() at first PDF extraction (pdf_extractor.py:949-960). That interacts badly with GH #1047 (cold-start ~180s, hard-fail on math-heavy first extraction): the first post-upgrade PDF job eats the cold-start penalty or fails, presenting as 'upgrade didn't start MinerU'.

Proposed: upgrade_finish (and/or nx doctor) should warm-start MinerU when (a) spawn policy allows, (b) binary present, (c) no live server — i.e. treat warm-MinerU as part of post-upgrade steady state, not just cycle-if-running. Respect pdf.mineru_autostart=false as out-of-band-managed (existing posture).

Related: nexus-4yohu (RDR-149 lease membership — the durable fix putting MinerU under real supervisor lifecycle), nexus-1qdb9 (spawn-guard docs, commit 8829b0f9), GH #1047 (cold-start timeout). Need from the field box if pursuing root-cause detail: whether MinerU was running pre-upgrade and which upgrade path ran (guided-upgrade vs reinstall+init).
close_reason: WONTFIX per Hal 2026-07-15: current behavior is correct — upgrades cycle a running MinerU but never cold-start an absent one; on-demand spawn at first PDF extraction is the design. Documented the expectation + nx mineru start pre-warm in docs/cli-reference.md § nx mineru (commit on develop). Durable lifecycle work remains nexus-4yohu.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Field follow-up (Hal, 2026-07-15): not certain, but MinerU is SUSPECTED to have not been running pre-upgrade. That points at the lazy-start design gap as filed (absent server never warmed by upgrade_finish), not a kill-without-restart regression in the restart-stale sweep. Scope stands: add warm-start to post-upgrade steady state (policy-gated), keep nexus-4yohu as the durable lifecycle fix.

title: Backfill catalog Document bib_* fields from chunk-level bib metadata
description:
# Plan: surface bib metadata on catalog Document rows (nexus-9l2lg)

Single phase, one PR, branch `feature/nexus-9l2lg-catalog-bib-columns` off `develop`.
Design authority: T2 `nexus/design-catalog-bib-columns.md` (approved 2026-07-15).
Divergence-class precedent: T3 `insight-developer-dual-backend-meta-merge-semantics-divergence`.

`nx_plan_audit` verdict: **APPROVED_WITH_CORRECTIONS** (2026-07-15). All corrections
folded into this version: (major) `descendants()` bib_* parity gap added to Task 1;
(minor) design test item 6 (catalog_search bib surfacing) added as Task 6b; (minor)
Task 3's meta-removal pin widened to cover the backend-id keys, not just venue/
citation_count. Audit independently re-verified every load-bearing file:line claim
against the live codebase and confirmed the Task 5 defer decision as defensible (the
projector genuinely doesn't clobber today; the design's own "if it clobbers, fix
in-scope" condition doesn't trigger). Line-reference drift of ~5 lines in enrich.py/
projector.py noted as cosmetic, not corrected (re-verify exact lines at implementation
time regardless — file line numbers drift as this plan sits in the queue).

Engine: NO changes. `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/CatalogRepository.java`
already persists+returns all 8 `bib_*` columns (`UPDATABLE_DOC_COLUMNS` L708-713,
`documentFields()`/`docRowFromRecord()` L3052-3097) — confirmed by direct read, not
assumed. The gap is entirely Python-side (writer omission + reader truncation).

## Pre-existing scope discovery (not in the original design doc — verified by reading code)

`CatalogEntry` (src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:424-478) only declares 4 of the 8 `bib_*`
columns (`bib_year`, `bib_authors`, `bib_venue`, `bib_citation_count` — added nexus-rzqto).
It is MISSING `bib_semantic_scholar_id` / `bib_openalex_id` / `bib_doi` / `bib_enriched_at`.
Both readers that populate it (`catalog_docs.py::resolve()` SQL, and
`http_catalog_client.py::_to_entry()`) only project those same 4 columns, even though the
HTTP engine already returns all 8 on `/show`. This must be fixed FIRST (Task 1) — the
clobber-preserving carry-through in Task 2 needs `entry.bib_semantic_scholar_id` etc. to
exist and be populated, or it silently reverts those 4 columns to their defaults on every
`update()` call that doesn't explicitly re-supply them.

## Task 1 — RED/GREEN: extend CatalogEntry + both readers to carry all 8 bib_* columns

Files:
- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py` — `CatalogEntry` dataclass (L424-455): add
  `bib_semantic_scholar_id: str = ""`, `bib_openalex_id: str = ""`, `bib_doi: str = ""`,
  `bib_enriched_at: str = ""`. Extend `to_dict()` (L457-478) with the same 4 keys.
- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py` — `_DocumentOps.resolve()` (L95-138): extend the
  `SELECT` (L107-111) to add `bib_semantic_scholar_id, bib_openalex_id, bib_doi,
  bib_enriched_at` and the `CatalogEntry(...)` call (L117-138) to read `row[19..22]`.
  Leave `list_by_collection()` (L140-192) alone — it doesn't even select the existing 4
  bib columns today; that's a pre-existing, unrelated gap (note in "Out of scope" below,
  do not fix here).
- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py` — `_DocumentOps.descendants()` (L469-514) — **added
  per nx_plan_audit finding (major)**: its own docstring (L475-479) claims "the full
  `bib_*` field set present" as a `nexus-u26b4` return-shape-parity contract with
  `HttpCatalogClient.descendants()`, but the `SELECT` (L484-489) and returned dict
  (L492-514) only project the 4 pre-existing bib columns — the docstring's claim is
  ALREADY FALSE today, and stays false (worse: newly inconsistent with Task 1's other two
  readers) if left untouched. `HttpCatalogClient.descendants()` (http_catalog_client.py
  L1072-1076) calls `/list` and returns the server's dicts verbatim, which already carry
  all 8 fields (confirmed) — so the parity gap is 100% local-side. Extend the `SELECT` and
  the returned dict literal with the same 4 new `bib_*` keys used above.
- `src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py` — `_to_entry()` (L171-199): add
  `bib_semantic_scholar_id=d.get("bib_semantic_scholar_id") or ""`,
  `bib_openalex_id=d.get("bib_openalex_id") or ""`, `bib_doi=d.get("bib_doi") or ""`,
  `bib_enriched_at=d.get("bib_enriched_at") or ""`. The wire dict already carries these
  (confirmed: `CatalogRepository.docRowFromRecord` L3090-3097) — this is a pure mapping
  fix, no server change.

TDD — new file `tests/test_catalog_bib_columns.py` (new home; existing catalog test files
are 400-1670 lines each and none is the right owner for "all 8 bib columns round-trip"):
- RED `test_catalog_entry_dataclass_has_all_eight_bib_fields` — instantiate
  `CatalogEntry(..., bib_semantic_scholar_id="x", bib_openalex_id="y", bib_doi="z",
  bib_enriched_at="w")` and assert the 4 new attributes + the 4 existing ones all exist
  and round-trip through `to_dict()`.
- RED `test_local_resolve_surfaces_all_eight_bib_columns` — real local `Catalog` (tmp_path),
  register a doc, direct-SQL `UPDATE documents SET bib_semantic_scholar_id=?,
  bib_openalex_id=?, bib_doi=?, bib_enriched_at=? WHERE tumbler=?` (bootstraps the 4 new
  columns before Task 2's writer exists), call `cat.resolve(tumbler)`, assert all 8 fields
  exactly.
- RED `test_descendants_surfaces_all_eight_bib_columns` — same bootstrap-via-direct-SQL
  pattern, call `cat.descendants(prefix)`, assert the returned dict carries all 8 `bib_*`
  keys with exact values (closes the nexus-u26b4 parity gap the audit flagged).
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_bib_columns.py -v`

## Task 2 — RED/GREEN: `_WriteOps.update()` carries bib_* through (local, non-event-sourced path)

File: `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_writes.py`, `update()` (L401-602).
- `rec_dict` construction (L409-446): add 8 keys seeded from `entry.bib_year`,
  `entry.bib_authors`, `entry.bib_venue`, `entry.bib_citation_count`,
  `entry.bib_semantic_scholar_id`, `entry.bib_openalex_id`, `entry.bib_doi`,
  `entry.bib_enriched_at` (Task 1 makes these exist). No change needed to the
  `rec_dict.update(fields)` merge at L452 — `fields` is already `**fields: object`, so
  caller-supplied `bib_year=...` etc. already override the carried-forward defaults
  generically.
- `INSERT INTO documents (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(tumbler) DO UPDATE SET ...`
  (L572-598): add the 8 `bib_*` columns to the column list, `?` placeholders, bound values
  from `rec_dict`, and the `ON CONFLICT` `SET` clause (`bib_year=excluded.bib_year`, etc.).
- Replace the stale comment at L561-571 (references a "BibliographicEnriched event
  handler" that was never built) with accurate documentation: clobber protection is now
  carry-through (unset callers preserve current values; explicit `bib_*` kwargs override),
  not omission.
- Leave the event-sourced branch (L536-547) untouched — see Task 5 (decision task).

TDD — `tests/test_catalog_bib_columns.py` (same file as Task 1):
- RED `test_update_without_bib_kwargs_preserves_existing_bib_columns` — register, call
  `cat.update(t, bib_year=2020, bib_authors="A", bib_venue="V", bib_citation_count=5,
  bib_semantic_scholar_id="ss1", bib_openalex_id="W1", bib_doi="10.1/x",
  bib_enriched_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")`, then `cat.update(t, chunk_count=9)` (no bib
  kwargs) — resolve and assert all 8 bib fields are UNCHANGED from the first call (exact
  equality, not just non-empty). This is the regression this code originally feared.
- RED `test_update_with_bib_kwargs_sets_all_eight_columns_exactly` — single `update()` call
  setting all 8, resolve, assert exact equality on all 8.
- RED `test_update_bib_fields_survive_jsonl_append_and_replay_filter` — after a bib-carrying
  `update()`, call `nexus.catalog.tumbler.read_documents(cat._documents_path)` (or the
  project's equivalent JSONL replay entry point) and assert it does NOT raise. `DocumentRecord`
  (tumbler.py:151-179) has no `bib_*` fields; `_filter_fields(DocumentRecord, obj)`
  (tumbler.py:242) silently drops unknown keys on reconstruction — this test pins that the
  drop is silent, not a crash, now that `rec_dict` (and therefore the JSONL row) carries the
  new keys.
- RED `test_update_bib_columns_on_fresh_and_migrated_schema` — two `CatalogDB` instances:
  (a) freshly created (bib columns present via `CREATE TABLE`, `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog.py`
  L163-170) and (b) simulate a legacy pre-bib DB (create `documents` without the 8 `bib_*`
  columns, then open through the real migration path so the `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`
  guards at L503-517 run) — call `_WriteOps.update(..., bib_year=...)` against both, assert
  success + correct `resolve()` readback on both. This is the "confirm upsert works on both
  fresh and migrated DBs" criterion from the design.
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_bib_columns.py -v`

## Task 3 — RED/GREEN: `_enrich_apply` writes bib_* as top-level columns, not meta JSON

File: `src/nexus/commands/enrich.py`, `_enrich_apply()` (L666-793).
- Replace the `meta_update` dict's `venue` / `citation_count` entries (L741-743) and the
  backend-id entries (L752-757) with top-level `writer.update()` kwargs: `bib_year=`,
  `bib_authors=`, `bib_venue=`, `bib_citation_count=`, `bib_enriched_at=<UTC now ISO>`, plus
  `bib_openalex_id=`/`bib_doi=` (openalex branch) or `bib_semantic_scholar_id=` (s2/default
  branch). Per the approved design: drop `venue`/`citation_count` from `meta` entirely
  (YAGNI on dual storage — nothing reads them back out of `meta`, confirmed by grep before
  removing). Keep `references` in `meta_update` (still meta-only, no catalog column for it).
  Keep the existing top-level `author=`/`year=` kwargs unchanged.
- `_catalog_enrich_hook` docstring (L612-635) and the `writer.update(...)` call (L764-770):
  update to describe the new column-level contract.

TDD — extend `tests/test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestEnrichHook` (existing file/class,
reuses the existing `_make_catalog` helper — do not create a new file for this one, it's a
direct sibling of `test_updates_catalog_metadata`):
- RED `test_updates_catalog_bib_columns_s2_backend` — call `_catalog_enrich_hook` with a
  `bib_meta` dict carrying `year`/`venue`/`authors`/`citation_count`/`semantic_scholar_id`,
  resolve, assert `bib_year`/`bib_venue`/`bib_authors`/`bib_citation_count`/
  `bib_semantic_scholar_id` match exactly and `bib_enriched_at` is a non-empty ISO string.
- RED `test_updates_catalog_bib_columns_openalex_backend` — same with `backend="openalex"`,
  `bib_meta` carrying `openalex_id` + `doi`; assert `bib_openalex_id`/`bib_doi` set and
  `bib_semantic_scholar_id == ""`.
- RED `test_meta_no_longer_carries_venue_or_citation_count` — after enrich (both s2 and
  openalex backend variants), assert `entry.meta` has no `"venue"` / `"citation_count"`
  keys AND no `"bib_semantic_scholar_id"` / `"bib_openalex_id"` / `"bib_doi"` keys (pins
  the YAGNI removal for the backend-id meta keys too, not just venue/citation_count —
  widened per nx_plan_audit finding: the original pin only covered 2 of the 5 relocated
  keys, so a partial regression on the id fields would have slipped through green).
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_knowledge_hook.py::TestEnrichHook -v`

## Task 4 — RED/GREEN: `nx enrich bib --backfill-catalog`

File: `src/nexus/commands/enrich.py`:
- `enrich_bib()` CLI (L127-175): add
  `@click.option("--backfill-catalog", is_flag=True, help="Re-drive the catalog bib_* "
  "write from already-enriched T3 chunk metadata; no external API calls. Idempotent.")`
  and an early branch: `if backfill_catalog: _backfill_catalog_from_chunks(collection); return`
  (before any backend resolution / network setup at L184-205).
- New function `_backfill_catalog_from_chunks(collection: str) -> tuple[int, int]`
  (titles backfilled, chunks scanned), placed near `run_bib_enrichment` (~L178): paginate
  `col.get(include=["metadatas"], limit=300, offset=...)` respecting the 300-record T3
  page cap (AGENTS.md quota table), select chunks where `bib_year` truthy OR either id field
  (`bib_semantic_scholar_id`/`bib_openalex_id`) is non-empty (mirrors the existing
  `already_enriched` detection at L226-229), group by `title` + collect `source_path`s
  (mirrors L211-239's `title_to_ids`/`title_to_source_paths`), reconstruct a `bib` dict per
  title straight from ONE representative chunk's own `bib_*` metadata keys (no re-lookup),
  infer `backend` from which id field is populated (`"openalex"` if `bib_openalex_id`,
  else `"s2"`), call `_catalog_enrich_hook(title=title, bib_meta=bib, collection_name=
  collection, backend=backend, source_paths=sorted(source_paths))`. Zero imports of
  `nexus.bib_enricher*` — no network path reachable from this function.
- Update `enrich_bib()`'s docstring (L163-174) to document the new flag.

TDD — extend `tests/test_enrich_command.py`:
- RED `test_backfill_catalog_populates_bib_columns_from_enriched_chunks` — seed a T3
  collection with chunks carrying `bib_year`/`bib_venue`/`bib_authors`/
  `bib_citation_count`/`bib_semantic_scholar_id` + `source_path` metadata (simulating prior
  live enrichment) and a matching catalog row with blank `bib_*`; run `enrich_bib` with
  `--backfill-catalog`; assert the catalog row's 5 fields now match the chunk metadata
  exactly (`==`, not `>=` — repo convention for fixture regression tests).
- RED `test_backfill_catalog_idempotent_second_run` — run twice; assert the SECOND run's
  reported title-count == 0 new writes (already-current — pick this exact contract, not
  "same as first run") AND assert catalog `bib_*` values are byte-identical before/after
  the second run.
- RED `test_backfill_catalog_skips_non_enriched_chunks` — one collection with an enriched
  title and a non-enriched title; assert only the enriched title's catalog row changes;
  the non-enriched title's row stays at column defaults (`0`/`""`).
- RED `test_backfill_catalog_makes_zero_external_calls` — `monkeypatch` both
  `nexus.bib_enricher.enrich` and `nexus.bib_enricher_openalex.enrich` with a `Mock`
  that raises `AssertionError` if called; run `--backfill-catalog`; assert no exception
  (proves neither backend was ever imported/invoked).
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_enrich_command.py -k backfill_catalog -v`

## Task 5 — DECISION TASK (mandatory, explicit branch): event-sourced projector clobber check

This is the "projector-clobber check" the relay requires as an explicit task with a
decision branch. Investigation already done during planning; the task is to encode the
finding as a regression-pinning test + accurate comments, and make (not silently skip)
the scope call.

**Finding**: `Projector._v0_document_registered` (`src/nexus/catalog/projector.py`
L220-276) intentionally omits `bib_*` from both its `INSERT` column list and its
`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET` clause (comment at L230-236, same phantom
"BibliographicEnriched event handler" reference as the pre-fix `catalog_writes.py`
comment). `DocumentRegisteredPayload` (`src/nexus/catalog/events.py` L238-276) has NO
`bib_*` fields at all — so under `NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=1`, Task 2's `_WriteOps.update()`
event-sourced branch (L536-547, deliberately left untouched by Task 2) cannot persist
`bib_*` even if asked to: the payload has nowhere to put the values and the projector's
SQL has no column to write them into. This is NOT a clobber today (bib columns are simply
never touched by this path) — but naively "fixing" it by adding `bib_*` to the payload +
projector SET clause WOULD introduce a NEW clobber: three other call sites emit
`DocumentRegisteredPayload` for EXISTING rows without any `bib_*` awareness —
`rename_collection` (`catalog_writes.py` L604-731, two emission sites: the per-row
event-sourced loop and the shadow-emit loop) and `_update_document_collection_locked`
(`catalog_writes.py` L91-175, used by both `update_document_collection` and
`update_documents_collection_batch`). None of their `SELECT`s fetch the `bib_*` columns,
so once the projector honors `bib_*` in its `SET` clause, a plain `nx collection rename`
or `update_documents_collection_batch` call under event-sourced mode would silently reset
every renamed/re-collectioned row's `bib_*` back to `0`/`""` — a strictly worse bug than
the one being fixed.

**Decision (this PR): defer.** Event-sourced mode is opt-in (`NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED`,
documented in-code as "Phase 3 PR β" / not the default path) and the approved design's
Decision section only specifies the non-event-sourced `INSERT...ON CONFLICT` path (Task 2)
— it does not mention `DocumentRegisteredPayload`. Extending event-sourced bib support
correctly requires auditing and fixing 3 additional emission sites, which is a separable
unit of work. Do NOT modify `events.py` or `projector.py` SQL in this PR.

Concrete steps:
1. Fix the stale comment at `projector.py` L230-236 to state accurately: `bib_*` is
   intentionally unsupported under event-sourced mode pending a follow-up (cite the bead
   filed in step 3), not "handled by a BibliographicEnriched event handler" (never built).
2. Add a regression-pinning test to `tests/test_catalog_event_sourced_mutators.py`,
   `TestUpdateEventSourced` class: RED `test_event_sourced_update_bib_kwargs_do_not_crash_but_do_not_persist`
   — `monkeypatch.setenv("NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED", "1")`, `cat.update(t, bib_year=2020,
   bib_authors="X")` must not raise, and `cat.resolve(t).bib_year == 0` (documents the
   current, deliberately-deferred behavior so a future silent change is caught).
3. File a follow-up bead: "Extend event-sourced Catalog update() to persist bib_* columns
   (audit rename_collection + update_document_collection_locked emission sites for
   carry-forward, then extend DocumentRegisteredPayload + projector SET clause)" — `relates`
   link to nexus-9l2lg, priority P3, no blocking dependency on this PR's beads.
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_catalog_event_sourced_mutators.py::TestUpdateEventSourced -v`

## Task 6 — Dual-backend parity test (local Catalog vs HttpCatalogClient) — MANDATORY

Precedent + fixture reuse: `tests/test_bib_enricher_write_back_service_mode.py` already
has a real-`HttpCatalogClient`-over-stateful-fake-server harness built for exactly this
divergence class (its own docstring documents a PRIOR live bug found this way — the
meta-merge semantics drift, nexus-ke45f). Extend this file rather than creating a new one.

- Inspect the fake server's `_State` / `/update` / `/show` handlers first: if they already
  merge/return arbitrary `fields` dicts generically, no handler change is needed (the 8
  `bib_*` keys just flow through); if the handler enumerates known fields explicitly,
  extend it to carry all 8 `bib_*` columns, mirroring the real
  `CatalogRepository.UPDATABLE_DOC_COLUMNS` (L708-713) and `docRowFromRecord` (L3062-3098)
  shape.
- New test class `TestBibColumnDualBackendParity`:
  RED `test_local_and_service_backends_produce_identical_bib_columns_after_enrich_apply` —
  build (a) a real local `Catalog` (tmp_path) reader+writer pair and (b) the existing
  fake-server-backed `HttpCatalogClient` reader+writer pair; register the SAME document
  (same title/file_path) into both; call `_enrich_apply(reader, writer, ..., bib_meta=
  SAME_DICT, backend="s2", ...)` against both independently; resolve from both; assert the
  two resulting 8-field `bib_*` tuples are IDENTICAL. This is the standing regression guard
  the T3 insight (`insight-developer-dual-backend-meta-merge-semantics-divergence`) calls
  for — a "drop-in" method identical in name/signature across backends silently diverging
  in semantics is exactly this repo's recurring bug class.
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_bib_enricher_write_back_service_mode.py::TestBibColumnDualBackendParity -v`

## Task 6b — catalog_search surfaces bib_year/bib_citation_count after enrich (design item 6)

Added per nx_plan_audit finding (minor): the approved design's 6th test item

title: T1 borrow path is rotation-fragile: borrower caches the token string once; owner's 30-min re-mint rotates it server-side -> borrower 401s for the rest of its life (should re-read the republished lease on 401)
description: Live incident 2026-07-14, session 24c01b46 (investigated after the MCP scratch tool 401'd all afternoon). Timeline from mcp.log: 08:23 an MCP incarnation of the session minted the T1 service token (t1_session_isolation_minted) and began the nexus-ngcpo refresh loop (server TTL 1h -> re-mint every 30min); 09:19 the session was RESUMED in a second terminal — the fresh MCP found the owner's lease fresh and took the borrow path (t1_session_inherited_no_mint), caching the token string in memory ONCE, by design never refreshing and never re-reading the lease; 09:23 the elder incarnation's next refresh tick re-minted — HttpTokenStore.start_session is ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, so the server-side token ROTATED — and the borrower's cached string stopped resolving. Every MCP-side T1 call 401'd from then on ('cannot re-mint mid-conversation'), while the CLI (self-healing dedicated store) worked fine, masking the damage. ANY two concurrent MCPs sharing a session id reproduce this: same-session double-resume, an elder incarnation surviving in another terminal (this case — pids on another tty), SessionStart-hook overlap. FIX: the borrower does not need to MINT (the ngcpo ownership rule stands) — it needs to RE-READ: the owner republishes the lease file with the fresh token at every rotation, so on a SESSION_UNAUTHORIZED_MARKER 401 the MCP-path HttpScratchStore should re-read read_t1_session_lease(session_id) and retry once (the exact self-heal _CliDedicatedScratchStore already has). Also update the 401 error text: 'reconnect' is not the only remedy once re-read exists. Related: nexus-ngcpo (introduced the owner refresh loop + lease republish this fix rides on).
close_reason: Shipped ace1dda0 + cff2687f: on 401 HttpScratchStore re-reads the owner-republished session lease under a refresh lock (sent-token double-check heals the losing thread of concurrent 401s), adopts a differing token (headers + client rebuild + NX_T1_SESSION and defensive NX_T1_SESSION_ID export), retries once; never mints (ngcpo single-minter rule intact). 401 guidance updated at both surfaces; the stale 'accepted residual' commentary in mcp/core.py corrected with the incident's real premises; the heal's own failure path logs. 8 regression tests (rotation heal, no-lease, unchanged, expired, concurrency-shape via sent-token, env hygiene). Full suite green.

title: nx catalog doctor --collections-drift will false-positive on every populated quarantine__ collection
description: Critique of 4cb743be (nexus-xukbj). _run_t3_vs_catalog() in commands/catalog_cmds/doctor.py classifies any T3 collection with chunks but zero catalog documents as a t3_orphan drift finding; its only exclusion list is _BYPASS_SCHEMA_PREFIXES = ('taxonomy__',) in db/t3.py. quarantine__* collections are, by design, never catalog-registered, and after this commit they are the NORMAL, expected steady-state output of every GC pass with orphans. Any populated quarantine collection will therefore be permanently misreported as drift, corrupting the doctor's 'PASS when all three lists are empty' contract. This is especially self-defeating because expire_quarantine's own floor-refusal warning tells operators to verify with 'nx catalog doctor --t3-vs-catalog' — a check that will already be red from the quarantine collections themselves. Fix: add 'quarantine__' to the bypass/exclusion list used by the collections-drift check (and confirm _BYPASS_SCHEMA_PREFIXES is the right shared mechanism vs a dedicated quarantine-aware skip).

title: Chunk quarantine (soft delete): GC moves orphans to a prefix-excluded sibling collection; hard-delete after grace; auto-restore on re-reference
description: Follow-on to nexus-mr89x (floor shipped in 6.7.1, deliberately conservative). A git pull/refactor changing >NX_GC_FLOOR_FRACTION (0.25) of a repo's content produces supersede-orphans above the floor -> sweep refused with a warning, repeatedly, until NX_GC_FORCE=1 — a nag + orphan accumulation on a normal large update. Precision fix: orphans whose chash was UNREFERENCED BY THIS RUN'S OWN manifest upserts are provably dead (atomic_manifest_replace just replaced their rows in the same run — the indexer can carry the set of replaced-away chashes from the manifest hook to the GC); only GAP-class orphans (unreferenced with NO same-run supersede evidence) should count against the floor. Keeps the mr89x protection intact for the dangerous class while making mass updates sweep cleanly. Evidence threshold per no-preventive-scope: implement when the first real refusal-on-legit-update lands OR fold into the next indexer arc — the refusal is loud, so occurrences will be visible.
close_reason: Shipped 4cb743be + c1fb3d43: chunk quarantine (soft delete). Orphan GC moves orphans to per-origin quarantine-<type>__ siblings (prefix excluded from all search corpora by construction), embeddings intact via copy-then-delete; restore-on-re-reference (before the empty-collection continue); expiry after NX_GC_QUARANTINE_DAYS=14 is the only hard delete, guarded by the origin-filtered mr89x floor. The recurring per-sweep refusal warning is GONE — mass git-pull supersede churn quarantines silently and expires quietly. Stacked review (3+2 Criticals incl. DOA-in-both-modes name-conformance/service-upsert bugs my permissive mocks masked) all actioned: strict=False creation, upsert_chunks_with_embeddings service path, get_embeddings alignment guard, doctor/ETL/legacy-gc exclusions. Realistic collision regression (shared chash across docs__/rdr__ same owner). Full pytest 13136 green. First concrete RDR-156 soft-delete piece (noted for nexus-70r3c).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: DESIGN LOCKED (Hal picked option C, 2026-07-14). Mechanism: quarantine = MOVE orphan chunks to quarantine__<owner>__<model>__v<n> (conformant 4-part shape; the quarantine prefix is in NO search corpus -> exclusion by construction, no filters, no metadata-update primitive needed). Embeddings copy over (local: col.get include embeddings/metadatas/documents; service: stub.get + HttpVectorClient.get_embeddings, write via upsert_chunks_with_embeddings — the ETL-proven path). quarantined_at + origin_collection stamped in metadata AT ADD TIME. Flow in _prune_deleted_files per collection: (1) RESTORE pass — quarantined chashes now referenced again copy back to origin + delete from quarantine (idempotent chash-keyed upsert); (2) QUARANTINE pass — current orphans move (NO floor here: recoverable, so the mr89x per-sweep refusal + NX_GC_FORCE nag DISAPPEARS); (3) EXPIRY pass — quarantine rows older than NX_GC_QUARANTINE_DAYS (default 14) hard-delete, and the mr89x floor applies HERE only (mass hard-delete after a full grace window of persisting defect = the only remaining loud case). Doctor: quarantine counts line. Docs: cli-reference GC section. Supersedes the option-A precision fix (same-run supersede tracking unnecessary — supersede-orphans quarantine silently and expire). First concrete piece of the RDR-156 soft-delete theme (note on nexus-70r3c epic when closing).

title: Run the GC A/B (tests/e2e/gc-ab/run-ab.sh): serial vs G1 runtime GC for the linux engine binary
description: Harness shipped in 4bee0cfb (pom knob native.image.gc + run-ab.sh + load_driver.py); run DEFERRED by Hal 2026-07-13 until the release ships. ~15 min on the 32GB Docker VM; needs a quiet VM (no concurrent rehearsals) for clean latency numbers. Decision it feeds: whether the cloud engine's linux binary switches to --gc=G1 (mac stays serial regardless — G1 is linux-only).
close_reason: Ran 2026-07-14 (harness tests/e2e/gc-ab, shipped 4bee0cfb). DEFINITIVE result at the build step: GraalVM COMMUNITY (our entire toolchain — rehearsal container container-registry.oracle.com/graalvm/native-image-community:25 AND the release workflow) does not ship the G1 native-image collector at all: --gc accepts only 'epsilon' and 'serial'. G1-in-native-image is an Oracle GraalVM (GFTC-licensed) feature, and even there linux-only. So the question 'switch the cloud engine to --gc=G1 for throughput' is answered: NOT AVAILABLE without migrating the whole build pipeline to Oracle GraalVM — a toolchain + licensing decision, not a flag. Serial remains the only real choice on CE (epsilon = no GC, unsuitable for a long-running service). The serial baseline built clean (216M, -Ob) proving the harness; it stays in-tree (pom knob native.image.gc + run-ab.sh) for the day the toolchain question reopens. No throughput data was needed — the door is closed upstream.

title: Rehearsal legs rebuild the Docker image from scratch every run (~19 min/leg): fresh-staged COPY mtimes bust the layer cache
description: Evidence 2026-07-13: three consecutive legs (--guided x2, --shakeout) each spent 18m33s/19m54s/19m+ in docker build; buildx history shows 0% cache. run.sh stages a fresh tmp context per leg, so COPY conexus-*.whl (and the flattened jar/native binary) get new mtimes and bust every downstream layer (pip install, PG bundle). Options: stage with fixed mtimes (touch -t epoch), COPY --link, order the wheel COPY after the heavy layers (already partially done for bge), or a persistent named build context. Not release-gating; pure wall-clock waste in the pre-tag gate.
close_reason: Fixed by 3a5102bd (develop, 2026-07-21) + host GC budget raise. Corrected root cause (instrumented 6-build investigation): NOT staged-COPY mtimes (BuildKit COPY cache is content-based — the requirements COPY cache-hits across fresh mktemp stages) but (a) the wheel's BYTES churn every uv build (embedded mtimes INSIDE the wheel), and the dep-install layer was keyed on the wheel, re-running its 430s closure install every build; (b) the 4.7GB dep layer was being LRU-evicted between same-day builds by Docker Desktop's 20GB defaultKeepStorage (usage was 32GB) and run.sh's own prune --reserved-space 12GB. Fix: lock-keyed requirements.txt dep layer + --no-deps wheel layer with uv pip check guard (Dockerfile/.cold/.fullstack); prune budgets 10/12GB -> 40/40GB; defaultKeepStorage 20GB -> 80GB (Hal authorized). Measured: build 6:31 -> 2:15 on layer hit (deps 295s -> 0s); shakeout image build 10.6s on full cache. Fidelity tradeoff (no live PyPI re-resolve in the three legs) documented as accepted in the Dockerfile — coverage lives in --package-upgrade/--era-hop by design. Gates: 6/6 builds green, CANDIDATE SHAKEOUT PASSED on the split image, stacked reviews clean.

title: verify-fill relevance_log watermark: days=90 coupling unenforced + tenant-blind cache key
design:
Two Significant findings from critique of commit 68509ac8 (nexus-24p05).

1. days=90 COUPLING NOT ENFORCED: three independently hand-typed literal
   `90`s must agree for the disjointness proof to hold:
   - src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py:1274 T2Database.expire(relevance_log_days=90)
   - src/nexus/db/t2/telemetry.py:404 Telemetry.expire_relevance_log(days=90)
   - src/nexus/migration/verify_fill_watermark.py:81
     RETENTION_HORIZON_TABLES = {"relevance_log": 90}
   No shared constant, no cross-file test asserts equality. Today's only
   production caller (hooks.py:165 -> db.expire() default) and the CLI
   (commands/memory.py:257, hardcoded days=90) both happen to agree, but
   nothing prevents future drift -- and this project has already been
   burned by exactly this failure class once (see engine_version.py's
   docstring re: nexus-b6qlf, "two separately hand-typed constants that
   silently drifted apart"). A caller sweeping with days=30 while the
   horizon stays pinned at 90 would let the sweep delete rows the fill
   still probes -> resurrect returns.

2. TENANT-BLIND WATERMARK CACHE KEY: verify_fill_watermark._key(url, table)
   = f"{service_url}|{table}" has NO tenant dimension (inherited from
   te885.10, not introduced by 68509ac8). But the data compared against
   it IS tenant-scoped: ServiceCountSource.counts() is "tenant-scoped
   counts under the service role" (orchestrator.py:101), and the NEW
   retention_marker this commit adds is explicitly per-tenant
   (TelemetryRepository.getRetentionMarkers(tenant, relations),
   tenantScope.withTenant). If the same local watermark file
   (~/.config/nexus/migration/verify_fill_watermarks.json) is ever
   consulted across two different tenants hitting the same service_url
   (plausible in this RLS-multi-tenant architecture -- shared cloud
   engine, per-operator bearer tokens), tenant B's fill run can TRUST a
   watermark recorded from tenant A's count/marker values by coincidental
   numeric pass, silently skipping probes below a rowid floor that was
   never verified against tenant B's own data. Not discussed anywhere in
   the commit despite threading a new tenant-scoped signal through this
   exact cache.

Related: nexus-ots8o (Critical, same commit -- permanent blindness +
false "parity" after cutover+90d). Full findings in T2 memory
project=nexus title critique-68509ac8-nexus-24p05-y92yf.
close_reason: Fixed in the follow-up commit: RELEVANCE_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS single-sources the horizon across the sweep default, T2Database.expire, the memory-command caller, and RETENTION_HORIZON_TABLES with a signature-introspection coupling test; the watermark cache key gains the tenant dimension (service_url, tenant, table) with a tenant-isolation test - tenant B can never trust a floor recorded against tenant A's counts/markers.

title: HttpAspectQueue.claim_next/claim_batch/mark_retry are not idempotent — mixin's blanket gateway-retry-is-safe claim is false for these
description:
Found while critiquing nexus-1ytp6's gateway-retry-axis fix (substantive-critic, 2026-07-13).

RefreshableHttpStoreMixin._once_with_gateway_retry's docstring claims: "Every mixin caller issues idempotent requests (upserts/reads/deletes keyed by natural id), so bounded retry is safe." This is FALSE for at least two HttpAspectQueue (src/nexus/db/t2/http_aspect_queue.py) operations, both of which now inherit the 502/503/504 bounded-backoff retry via the mixin:

1. claim_next() / claim_batch() (lines 217-241): SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + mark in_progress. This is a state-mutating CLAIM, not a natural-id-keyed upsert. If the server commits the claim (row now in_progress) but the gateway drops the response (502/503 mid-delivery), the mixin's retry re-issues claim_next — which will SKIP the now-in_progress row (no longer 'pending') and claim a DIFFERENT row instead. The originally-claimed row is silently orphaned: no worker holds it, and it sits in_progress until reclaim_stale()'s timeout eventually resets it. Not permanent data loss, but a silent processing delay the "idempotent, so retry is safe" framing does not account for.

2. mark_retry() (lines 274-286): increments retry_count server-side. A lost-response retry after a successful server-side increment double-increments retry_count — a genuine non-idempotent double-apply, not just a delay. If retry_count gates a max-retry give-up threshold, this could prematurely exhaust a row's retry budget under a gateway-transient condition that had nothing to do with the row's own processing.

Compare: http_vector_client (the reference this axis was ported from) has no job-queue-shaped operations (claim/increment) — every one of its callers genuinely is upsert/read/delete keyed by natural id, so the reference's blanket idempotency claim is actually true for its own caller set. Porting the SAME blanket claim onto the mixin without auditing whether it holds for job-queue-shaped adopters (HttpAspectQueue specifically) carries the claim further than the evidence supports.

Also worth server-side verification (not confirmed, flagged as open question): http_memory_store.put_or_merge()'s Jaccard-scan-then-conditional-merge-or-insert — whether a retry after a lost-response INSERT would correctly find and merge into the just-inserted row (idempotent) or double-insert a near-duplicate (not idempotent). Needs Java-side inspection to resolve either way.

Fix shape: either (a) narrow the gateway-retry axis to exclude claim_next/claim_batch/mark_retry (opt each store's non-idempotent operations out of _once_with_gateway_retry), or (b) make the operations idempotent server-side (e.g. client-supplied idempotency token), or (c) at minimum correct the mixin's docstring to stop claiming universal idempotency and document the known exceptions with their accepted risk (claim: bounded delay via reclaim_stale; mark_retry: bounded premature-exhaustion risk).
close_reason: Closed

title: RefreshableHttpStoreMixin classifier omits httpx.CloseError — same NetworkError family as the just-added ReadError/WriteError/ConnectError, undocumented
description:
Follow-on to nexus-1ytp6's decision-surface audit, discovered while critiquing that bead's own fix (substantive-critic, 2026-07-13).

src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py's _is_retryable_endpoint_error (69-115) and _send's except tuple (391-419) were updated by nexus-1ytp6 to add ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout/WriteError, with PoolTimeout deliberately and explicitly excluded (documented + test_pool_timeout_is_not_retryable).

Verified directly against the actual httpx 0.28.1 exception MRO (not assumed):

  TransportError
    TimeoutException: ConnectTimeout(✓handled) ReadTimeout(✓handled) WriteTimeout(✓handled) PoolTimeout(✓excluded+documented+tested)
    NetworkError:     ReadError(✓handled) WriteError(✓handled) ConnectError(✓handled) CloseError(MISSING — not handled, not mentioned, not tested)
    ProxyError (MISSING — not handled, not mentioned, not tested)
    UnsupportedProtocol (legitimately out of scope — config error)
    ProtocolError: LocalProtocolError(legitimately out of scope — our own bug) RemoteProtocolError(✓handled)

httpx.CloseError ("Failed to close a connection") is a direct NetworkError sibling of ReadError/WriteError/ConnectError — same family, same restart-window rationale the docstring already gives for those three (TCP RST / socket-close failure during a supervisor SIGTERM). It is silently absent from both the classifier's isinstance tuple and _send's except tuple, and is not mentioned anywhere in the 498-line file (grep-verified) — unlike PoolTimeout/LocalProtocolError, which ARE explicitly reasoned about as deliberate exclusions.

This is the identical defect class nexus-1ytp6 was filed to close (an enumerable httpx sibling silently missing from the classifier), recurring inside the fix itself.

httpx.ProxyError is also unaddressed and undocumented — less clearly restart-window-shaped than CloseError, but likewise has zero decision-surface documentation (no "deliberately excluded because X" note), so it cannot be distinguished from an oversight.

Fix shape: add CloseError to both tuples with a docstring entry paralleling ReadError/WriteError/ConnectError; add ProxyError with a decision (retryable or explicitly-excluded-because) and a test either way; add classifier unit tests for both mirroring test_read_error_is_retryable / test_pool_timeout_is_not_retryable.
close_reason: CloseError added to both classifier and _send except tuple with docstring rationale + test; ProxyError explicitly excluded with rationale + pinning test; remaining taxonomy members documented out-of-scope-by-kind. Commit 3120fb2b.

title: HttpTaxonomyStore pins its child HttpCentroidStore (explicit base_url+token) — mixin self-heal permanently dead for all centroid ops in production
description:
Defect-class audit finding (2026-07-12, group D of the decision-surface audit; missed by 2 stacked-review rounds on batch A + the final sweep-wide gate).

src/nexus/db/t2/http_taxonomy_store.py:142-144: the lazy _centroid property constructs HttpCentroidStore(base_url=self._base_url, tenant=self._tenant, _token=self._token) — explicit non-None base_url AND token. RefreshableHttpStoreMixin.__init__ marks both as pinned; _invalidate_and_reresolve (_refreshable_client.py:316-323) raises RuntimeError('cannot self-heal — both base_url and token were explicitly pinned') when both are pinned. Consequence: on any supervisor restart (port churn) or token rotation while a live HttpTaxonomyStore exists, the parent's own calls self-heal fine but EVERY centroid-backed operation (assign_single, compute_assignments, compute_cross_links, project_against, discover_topics' centroid upsert) raises RuntimeError on the first retryable failure for the remaining life of the instance — the property caches the child once and never rebuilds it.

Grep-verified: this is the ONLY production construction site of HttpCentroidStore in the repo, so the mixin's self-heal for that class is exercised exclusively by test-only no-arg construction — dead code in production. Not a regression vs pre-adoption (that path had zero self-heal before either), but it directly undercuts the f2qvx epic's closure claim ('across all 10 target classes').

Fix shape: construct the child unpinned (HttpCentroidStore(tenant=self._tenant)) and let it resolve its own endpoint/token via the mixin — OR propagate the parent's re-resolution into the child (rebuild the cached child on parent invalidation). First option is simpler and matches every other store's construction convention. Add a self-heal test that exercises a taxonomy->centroid operation through a token rotation (the existing test_http_centroid_store_selfheal.py only tests direct no-arg construction).

Fail-loud (RuntimeError), not silent data corruption — but defeats a specifically-claimed production benefit on every credential-staleness event for this class. T2 record: nexus/f2qvx-group-d-defect-class-audit-centroid-pinning.
close_reason: HttpTaxonomyStore._centroid now propagates parent pin state per half instead of hard-pinning both; all 4 pin combinations tested; production centroid self-heal restored. Commit 3120fb2b.

title: RefreshableHttpStoreMixin drops http_vector_client's 502/503/504 gateway-retry axis and misses ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout in the retryable classifier
description:
Defect-class audit finding (2026-07-12, groups C of the decision-surface audit; both missed by the arc's 5+ stacked review rounds).

Finding 1 (decision-surface undercoverage): src/nexus/db/t2/_refreshable_client.py (_is_retryable_endpoint_error ~69-115, _send ~363-391) ports http_vector_client's endpoint-invalidate-and-retry-once axis but silently DROPS its second, orthogonal retry axis: _GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES = {502, 503, 504} with bounded backoff (2.0/5.0/10.0s, src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:246-347). Not documented as deliberate anywhere (design doc nexus/design-bikit-refreshable-http-store-mixin.md cites the other helpers by line but never mentions the gateway axis). T2 and T3 resolve the SAME managed endpoint via resolve_service_endpoint, and http_vector_client's own comment documents a live production 504 on that service (2026-07-04) — during a redeploy window a T2 write via the mixin gets a proxy 502/503 and fails immediately with zero retry while the T3 client hitting the identical condition retries and succeeds. Test suite has test_500_is_not_retryable but no 502/503/504 case.

Finding 2 (input-domain narrower than reality): same classifier lists ConnectError, ConnectTimeout, ReadError, RemoteProtocolError but omits httpx.ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout — direct MRO siblings under httpx.TimeoutException, NOT subclasses of ReadError. This is the identical non-subclass relationship that justified explicitly adding ConnectTimeout alongside ConnectError in a prior review round (docstring ~78-92, nexus-bikit.3) — the same reasoning applied one level over was stopped short. Restart-window hang (proxy/LB not propagating backend RST, or JVM shutdown drain leaving socket open) manifests as ReadTimeout and propagates as a hard failure instead of getting the one self-heal retry every other restart-window signature gets. Classifier test file has one test per handled type; none for ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout.

Fix shape: (1) add the gateway-retry axis (mirror _GATEWAY_RETRY_CODES + bounded sleeps, or extract shared constants from http_vector_client), (2) add ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout to both the classifier and _send's except tuple, (3) one classifier test per newly handled type + a 502-retry test. Both fixes multiply across all 10+ adopted Http*Store classes.
close_reason: Gateway-transient 502/503/504 retry axis ported from http_vector_client (constants imported, parity-test pinned); ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout/WriteError/CloseError added to classifier + _send tuple; PoolTimeout/ProxyError deliberately excluded with pinning tests. Stacked review 2 rounds clean. Commit 3120fb2b.

title: TDD green: _t1_session_mint_lock_path helper + Branch-0 lock-guarded double-check-then-mint-or-borrow
description:
Make the nexus-jwqjm.1 tests pass. Implementation shape is LOCKED in nexus/design-jwqjm-t1-mint-race-flock.md step 2 -- follow it exactly.

STEP A -- new helper in src/nexus/db/t1.py, placed alongside _t1_session_lease_path (~line 901):
def _t1_session_mint_lock_path(session_id: str, config_dir: Path) -> Path:
    return config_dir / f't1_mint_{session_id}.lock'
Mirror the naming/style of _t1_session_lease_path and _CLI_DEDICATED_SESSION_FILENAME's .lock convention.

STEP B -- src/nexus/mcp/core.py _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch-0 MINT arm (the  block at ~the 'from nexus.db.t1 import mint_t1_session_token' line, where _t1_session_id is truthy). BEFORE calling mint_t1_session_token:
  1. os.open(str(_t1_session_mint_lock_path(_t1_session_id, config_dir)), os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREAT, 0o600); fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX) (blocking). config_dir = nexus_config_dir() (already imported in this branch).
  2. Under the lock, re-check read_t1_session_lease(_t1_session_id, config_dir):
     - FRESH NOW (a concurrent recoverer won while we blocked): treat IDENTICALLY to the existing USE_LEASED early-return -- set os.environ['NX_T1_SESSION']=borrowed_token, os.environ['NX_T1_SESSION_ID']=_t1_session_id, log 't1_session_leased_after_mint_race', release lock + close fd, then . NO _OWNED_T1_SESSION, NO refresh task, NO ownership teardown -- exactly like the USE_LEASED branch which does not enter the big try:yield/finally block. IMPORTANT: release the flock and close the fd BEFORE yielding (do not hold the lock across the yield for the whole session lifetime).
     - STILL STALE: mint_t1_session_token + publish_t1_session_lease WHILE HOLDING the lock, then release lock + close fd, then proceed to today's path (_OWNED_T1_SESSION, refresh task, enter try:yield/finally).
  3. try/finally around the lock lifetime so the flock ALWAYS releases (fcntl.LOCK_UN) and the fd ALWAYS closes -- including on mint failure. The existing fail-loud RuntimeError (structlog t1_session_mint_failed + Phase-E remedy sentence re-wrap) MUST still propagate unchanged: wrap ONLY the lock lifetime, do NOT swallow or alter the mint-failure exception handling.

STEP C -- lifecycle gate (REQUIRED, do not skip): the new fcntl.flock acquire in src/nexus/mcp/core.py lands in a module NOT on _FLOCK_ALLOWED_MODULES (tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py:112). test_flock_acquire_sites_are_allowlisted scans every non-allowlisted module and flags any fcntl.flock( line lacking the inline token '# lifecycle-gate-allow:'. Put that token as an inline comment ON the acquire line with a short reason, EXACTLY as _cli_dedicated_session_id does in t1.py:835 ('# lifecycle-gate-allow: ...'). This is a one-shot per-session mint mutex, NOT a lifecycle election, so the inline-token justification (not routing through ServiceRegistry._elect) is correct. Do NOT add mcp/core.py to _FLOCK_ALLOWED_MODULES -- the inline token is the lighter, precedented choice. (A prior identical regression on the t1.py flock addition is recorded in T1 scratch 2b9d5dda.)

NON-GOALS (confirm each stays untouched):
- resolve_t1_routing_tiers is NOT modified (design non-goal -- tier 1/2 separation preserved; it never mints).
- get_t1_database()'s CLI/detached MINT path (_cli_dedicated_session_id / _CliDedicatedScratchStore) is NOT touched (out of scope -- different mint target; the CLI-dedicated identity is disjoint by design).
- The USE_INHERITED and USE_LEASED early branches at the top of Branch 0 are unchanged.

CLOSING: uv run pytest tests/db/test_t1_mint_race.py tests/db/test_t1_cli_dedicated_session.py tests/test_t1_discovery.py tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py -x  must be green, then FULL unit suite: uv run pytest  (no API keys needed; EphemeralClient + bundled ONNX). Full-suite-green is a hard closing criterion.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t design-jwqjm-t1-mint-race-flock.md . Use mcp__plugin_sn_serena__jet_brains_find_symbol for _t1_chroma_lifespan navigation and insert_after_symbol / replace patterns for the edit. Use sequentialthinking for the control-flow insertion since the early-return-vs-fallthrough split is subtle.
notes:
CORRECTION (two fragments were shell-stripped from the description): STEP B line "(the  block at ~the from nexus.db.t1 import mint_t1_session_token line" should read "(the ELSE block -- the arm where _t1_session_id is truthy -- at ~the from nexus.db.t1 import mint_t1_session_token line". STEP B FRESH-NOW bullet "release lock + close fd, then . NO _OWNED_T1_SESSION" should read "release lock + close fd, then YIELD then RETURN (yield; return). NO _OWNED_T1_SESSION". No other text was affected.
nx_plan_audit MEDIUM (fold in): extract the flock-guarded critical section into a SYNC helper the async generator calls -- do NOT leave the whole mint-or-borrow inline in the async generator. Semantics are byte-identical to the locked design; this only adds the testable seam (and avoids racing an async generator + asyncio.create_task across threads).

Shape: def _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow(session_id: str, config_dir: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]  returning (token, minted). Body = the flock EX open + try/finally(LOCK_UN + close) wrapping: double-check read_t1_session_lease(session_id, config_dir); if FRESH -> return (leased_token, False); else mint_t1_session_token(...) + publish_t1_session_lease(...) under the lock -> return (minted_token, True). Mint failure: let the RuntimeError propagate out of the helper (finally still releases the lock) -- the Branch-0 caller keeps its existing structlog t1_session_mint_failed + Phase-E remedy re-wrap unchanged. The lifecycle-gate-allow inline token goes on the flock line INSIDE this helper. Put the helper in src/nexus/db/t1.py (next to _t1_session_mint_lock_path) so tests import it without importing mcp/core, OR in mcp/core.py if config_dir/import cleanliness favors it -- developer call, but t1.py keeps the flock+lifecycle-gate story in one module.

Branch-0 MINT else-arm then becomes: token, minted = _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow(_t1_session_id, config_dir) inside the existing try/except (re-wrap on RuntimeError as today); set NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID from token in BOTH cases; if not minted -> log t1_session_leased_after_mint_race, yield; return (no _OWNED_T1_SESSION, no refresh task); if minted -> set _OWNED_T1_SESSION, start _t1_session_refresh_loop task, enter the existing try:yield/finally. The refresh task (asyncio.create_task) STAYS in the async generator -- only the sync flock section is extracted.

title: Add non-pinned persistent-connection-refused test for RefreshableHttpStoreMixin
design:
Found during substantive-critic review of nexus-f2qvx.1 (batch A: taxonomy/telemetry/centroid/plan_library mixin adoption).

Gap: no test anywhere in tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py or any per-store selfheal test proves the "f2qvx half" (connection-refused/reset) retry-EXHAUSTED path for a NON-pinned instance -- i.e. server permanently unreachable, base_url/token resolved via env (not test-pinned), first attempt fails, retry also fails, original httpx.ConnectError/ConnectionRefusedError propagates untouched (not swallowed, not looped).

The 401 sibling of this IS covered: test_persistent_401_retries_exactly_once_then_raises (tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py:286) proves the genuinely-bad-credential retry-exhausted case with an exact _REQUEST_COUNT==2 assertion and a message-content check.

nexus-f2qvx.1's own diff removed the one test that used to approximate proof-of-connection-error-propagation for this class of failure: tests/db/test_http_telemetry_store_probe_ids.py::test_probe_ids_fail_closed_propagates_transport_error used to assert `pytest.raises(httpx.ConnectError)` against a MockTransport that always raises ConnectError. Post-mixin-adoption that test's fixture (_store_with_transport) pins BOTH base_url and _token, so RefreshableHttpStoreMixin._invalidate_and_reresolve refuses to retry (raises RuntimeError "cannot self-heal" instead) -- a DIFFERENT code path than the one the test used to exercise. The developer correctly broadened the assertion to `pytest.raises(Exception)` to keep the test passing (a legitimate adaptation to the locked pinned-refusal contract), but nothing was added to replace the lost connection-error-propagation proof.

Fix: add one test (mirrors test_persistent_401_retries_exactly_once_then_raises's shape) to tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py's shared harness: server permanently down (or a handler that always raises ConnectionRefusedError-equivalent), store constructed WITHOUT base_url/_token pins (env-resolved), assert exactly 2 request attempts and that the original connection-class exception (or a wrapped equivalent) propagates on the second failure. Closes the gap once for every current and future adopter rather than per-store.

Secondary, lower-priority cleanup noted in the same review: tests/db/test_http_plan_library.py::TestAuthErrors::test_wrong_token_raises and tests/db/test_http_telemetry_store.py::TestLogRelevance::test_log_sends_auth_headers both loosened from `pytest.raises(Exception, match="401")` to bare `pytest.raises(Exception)`. The resulting exception is actually deterministic (RuntimeError, matching "cannot self-heal", per RefreshableHttpStoreMixin._invalidate_and_reresolve's fully-pinned branch) and is already the asserted contract at the mixin level (tests/db/test_refreshable_client.py::TestPinnedEndpointNeverSilentlyRepointed). Tightening these two to `pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="cannot self-heal")` would restore precision at zero brittleness cost (it's the mixin's own locked, tested contract, not an incidental wording detail).

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t f2qvx.1-critique-2026-07-12 (full critique)

Found by the 2026-07-13 bead-hygiene scour.

title: http_memory_store.find_overlapping_memories: bare OSError can leak past except (ValueError, httpx.HTTPError)
description:
code-review-expert flagged during nexus-bikit.5's Phase-1 gate review (2026-07-12): src/nexus/db/t2/http_memory_store.py:419-422, find_overlapping_memories's large-project branch catches `except (ValueError, httpx.HTTPError):` around self.search(...) to degrade gracefully on failure.

RefreshableHttpStoreMixin's _is_retryable_endpoint_error docstring (_refreshable_client.py) explicitly anticipates a defensive-fallback case where a bare ConnectionRefusedError/ConnectionResetError (builtin OSError subclasses, NOT httpx.HTTPError) can leak through _send's second, uncaught retry attempt. If that fires inside find_overlapping_memories, it escapes this best-effort continue-on-failure branch and crashes instead of degrading gracefully.

Narrow: only fires if a lower transport layer raises a raw OS error instead of httpx's wrapped type on the SECOND (post-retry) attempt. Non-blocking for the bikit.5 gate (both code-review-expert and substantive-critic returned clean overall), but real given the mixin itself documents the possibility -- flagged explicitly rather than left as a code comment.

Fix: widen the except tuple in find_overlapping_memories to also catch (ConnectionRefusedError, ConnectionResetError), or catch OSError broadly if no other narrower type is more correct. Also relevant to the nexus-f2qvx.* adoption sweep -- worth checking whether any of the other 8 stores have a similar best-effort continue-on-failure branch with the same narrow except tuple.

Also noted (Low, doc-gap, same review): _invalidate_and_reresolve mutates self._base_url/self._token on a shared instance with no locking, unlike T3's HttpVectorClient which uses a module-level _endpoint_lock. Probably fine given the per-instance usage pattern here, but worth a doc note before f2qvx copies this mixin onto 8 more store classes whose concurrency patterns aren't yet known.
close_reason: Fixed in 0a8f8759: find_overlapping_memories large-project branch catches OSError alongside ValueError/httpx.HTTPError, with a regression test (monkeypatched _ALL_PAIRS_MAX_ENTRIES=1 + ConnectionResetError search) proving the scan degrades instead of crashing.

description:
nexus-97oz3 closed a routing-correctness x backend-correctness gap for T1 specifically: native-smoke.sh now exercises nexus.db.t1.get_t1_database() (mint+put+get+search+list) against the real compiled native binary, not just raw curl against /v1/t1/*.
