title: Two simultaneous stale-lease recoverers for the same T1 session_id both mint, causing persistent 401 churn
description:
code-review-expert review of nexus-ngcpo's fix (2026-07-12) found: when a lease's original owner has died, read_t1_session_lease correctly returns None (stale), and the resolver falls into the mint branch (src/nexus/mcp/core.py _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch 0), which mints fresh AND claims ownership (_OWNED_T1_SESSION, starts _t1_session_refresh_loop). If TWO processes independently resolve the same session_id and both observe the lease as stale at close to the same moment, BOTH mint, BOTH set _OWNED_T1_SESSION, BOTH start their own refresh loop for the identical session id.

Verified server-side consequence (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TokenStore.java issueSessionToken, ~line 502-525): ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, session_id) DO UPDATE ... SET session_token_hash = ... -- re-minting hard-rotates the row, immediately invalidating whatever token was previously live. Two competing owners therefore don't just race once: each one's periodic refresh (every ~half the token TTL) keeps invalidating the other's freshly-minted token going forward, producing PERSISTENT INTERMITTENT 401 churn for the lifetime of both processes rather than a one-time self-correcting race.

The existing code comments (core.py, Branch-0 self-check) explicitly reason about the fresh-lease borrow-vs-owner race but do not address two simultaneous RECOVERERS of a STALE lease. No test in the nexus-ngcpo diff exercises >1 concurrent recoverer. The project's own T1 sub-agent contract documents nested-MCP-subprocess and detached-SessionEnd-hook as real borrower shapes, so this scenario is reachable, if narrow (requires two processes to both observe staleness within the same short window).

Not a merge blocker for nexus-ngcpo per the reviewing agent's own assessment (narrow timing window, degrades to periodic 401s with an ALREADY-actionable error message via the SESSION_UNAUTHORIZED_MARKER wiring in _mcp_tool_error, not silent data loss or a security hole) -- but should be tracked rather than silently accepted, since this project's convention is to document known residuals explicitly rather than let them go unrecorded.

Candidate fix directions (not yet designed): (a) a file-lock/CAS around the stale-lease-detected-therefore-mint transition, similar to _cli_dedicated_session_id's existing fcntl.flock election pattern; (b) a short random jitter on the refresh interval to reduce (not eliminate) the collision window; (c) accept the narrow window as-is and just ensure the 401 error path stays actionable (already true). Investigate which is proportionate to the actual risk before implementing.
close_reason: Flock-guarded mint-or-borrow closes the simultaneous stale-lease recoverer race (GH-adjacent 401-churn class). All 3 child beads closed. Refresh-loop residual tracked as nexus-ltwu4. Commit a4a6c90f.

title: T1 CLI-dedicated tier unconditionally re-mints on every bare-CLI invocation (doubles measured latency)
description:
Holistic critique of the T1 service cutover found: get_t1_database()'s tier-3 path (src/nexus/db/t1.py ~1133-1144) always calls HttpTokenStore().start_session(dedicated_id) -- the cached file only holds the session ID, never the TOKEN -- so every fresh bare-CLI process pays a full mint round trip in addition to the actual op round trip, with no check of whether an existing token would still be valid.

A single 'nx scratch put' from a plain terminal against the cloud pays roughly DOUBLE the per-op latency figure the session's own benchmark tabulated (T2 nexus/t1-latency-benchmark-2026-07-11: ~100ms measured PER OP, not including this unmeasured mint round trip that precedes every op on this path).

RECOMMENDATION: cache the token locally with its expiry (0600, alongside the existing id file) and only re-mint when actually near-expiry or on a 401, rather than unconditionally on every process start. Natural to bundle with nexus-ngcpo's lease-freshness fix since both need the same 'check expiry before trusting a cached token' primitive.
close_reason: Shipped 29d79a2b + fold 7294d4b1: CLI-dedicated token rides the freshness-checked published lease (borrow-not-remint, flock-serialized, self-heal republishes) + 5s freshness margin so near-expiry leases are never borrowed. Live: 1.09s->0.75s warm. Stacked-reviewed; critic's TTL-margin Significant folded.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
substantive-critic (2026-07-23, commit 29d79a2b review): two observations, neither blocking closure on its own.

1. read_t1_session_lease's freshness check (src/nexus/db/t1.py ~line 995) is a hard `time.time() >= expires_at` with no safety margin. _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow's borrow path can therefore hand a fresh-CLI-process a token with only sub-second remaining TTL, which then 401s on its very first op. Functionally safe (the by875 401 self-heal in _CliDedicatedScratchStore._call generically recovers via remint+retry), but it partially erodes this bead's own latency win on unlucky timing (mint avoided, but the op still pays a full self-heal round trip). Cross-referenced on nexus-by875 as a Significant finding — consider a small margin (e.g. <5s remaining treated as stale) if this shows up in the field.

2. Verified as SAFE (no finding): the CLI-dedicated dedicated_id lease file (t1_session_lease.<dedicated_id>) is a distinct identity from any live-MCP session's lease file, so session_end_flush()'s resolve_active_session_id()-based lookup cannot collide with this cache. No cross-contamination between the two lease namespaces found.

The more material gap from this same commit — the by875 wall-clock budget only covering the post-401 leg, not the construction-time _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow call this bead's tier-3 path now routes through — is filed on nexus-by875, not here, since it's that bead's spec being under-delivered.

title: T1 routing-correctness and backend-correctness never proven together against the real native artifact
description:
Holistic critique of the T1 service cutover found the test seam that let nexus-opr9m (the native-image jOOQ reflection bug -- T1 reads 500'd on the compiled native binary while working fine on the JVM) ship silently remains open, even though that specific bug is now fixed.

tests/db/test_http_scratch_store_integration.py builds and runs against a JVM jar (mvn -f service/pom.xml package -DskipTests) -- and the T1 cutover design doc's own root-cause section states the reflection bug 'came back clean on the JVM (reflection always succeeds there)', meaning this integration test structurally CANNOT catch the class of bug nexus-opr9m fixed. service/native-smoke.sh's T1 section (which DOES catch it) drives /v1/t1/* via raw curl, entirely bypassing Python's get_t1_database() three-tier routing, HttpTokenStore.start_session() minting, and HttpScratchStore's client code.

So: routing-correctness is tested (against a JVM backend that can mask native-only bugs) and backend-correctness is tested (via bypass-curl that skips all the Python routing logic) but the two have never been proven TOGETHER against the actual production artifact (a compiled native binary reached through the real Python client code). Also noted for context, not introduced by this arc: mac-arm64 native builds ship entirely unsmoked by native-smoke.sh (pre-existing gap).

RECOMMENDATION: either extend native-smoke.sh to shell out through the actual nx CLI (or a minimal script using get_t1_database()) against the native binary, or extend the integration test to optionally target a native-built artifact when available.

Full record: T2 nexus/critique-t1-service-cutover-holistic-2026-07-11.
close_reason: Shipped commit c3a8f249 on develop (native-smoke.sh + engine-service-release.yml together). native-smoke.sh gained a T1-via-real-Python-client section (mint+put+get+search+list through nexus.db.t1.get_t1_database() against the already-running native binary), closing the seam that let nexus-opr9m ship silently -- routing-correctness and backend-correctness now proven together against the actual production artifact through the actual production client code, for T1. CI wiring for this to actually execute in engine-service-release.yml (not just local dev runs) shipped in the same commit, tracked/closed as nexus-l8ybx. Scoped to T1 only per this bead's own title -- the identical gap remains open for memory/plans/taxonomy/chash's own real Python HTTP clients (src/nexus/db/t2/http_memory_store.py and siblings), tracked as a new follow-up bead rather than bundled into this fix.

title: T1 CLI-dedicated and MCP Branch-0 session routing are duplicated logic held in sync only by prose, no shared invariant
description:
Holistic critique of the T1 service cutover (nexus-rn3wo.1) found: get_t1_database()'s three-tier routing (src/nexus/db/t1.py ~1041-1146) and _t1_chroma_lifespan Branch 0's three mint-guards (src/nexus/mcp/core.py ~379-524) share low-level primitives (read/publish/clear_t1_session_lease, resolve_active_session_id) but the BRANCHING DECISION ITSELF -- which env var wins, in what order, when to mint vs borrow a lease vs fall back -- is two independently hand-written control flows. They are kept 'in sync' only by cross-referencing comments and the T2 design doc's prose (nexus/design-t1-service-local-cutover-2026-07-11.md), not by any shared function or test that would fail if one diverges from the other structurally.

A future change to lease semantics (TTL, file format, tenant scoping -- see nexus-ngcpo, nexus-36q84) in one file is not mechanically forced to update the other; drift would be silent until it manifests as a bug, exactly the pattern that produced remediation rounds 2-4 of the original nexus-rn3wo.1 arc (each round found a NEW bug the prior fix hadn't anticipated).

RECOMMENDATION: extract the shared decision sequence into one function (e.g. resolve_t1_routing_decision(has_inherited_env, resolved_session_id, config_dir) -> RoutingDecision) called by both get_t1_database() and Branch 0, or at minimum add a structural test asserting both modules consult the lease-file path constant and check ordering identically, so a manual edit to one without the other fails loudly instead of silently.

Full record: T2 nexus/t1-cli-mcp-dual-entry-point-critique-2026-07-12.md.
close_reason: Extracted resolve_t1_routing_tiers() (tiers 1-2: inherited-token-wins, then borrow-a-fresh-lease) unifying get_t1_database() and mcp.core's Branch 0, replacing two independently-hand-written control flows kept in sync only by cross-referencing comments. Round 1 stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic) found and fixed a has_inherited widening bug (token-only vs 'either var'), plus flagged tier-3 mint+exception-translation was ALSO duplicated 3x. Round 2: extracted mint_t1_session_token() as the shared mint mechanic, wired all three call sites (get_t1_database's CLI-dedicated mint, _CliDedicatedScratchStore._remint, mcp.core Branch 0's session mint); Branch 0 keeps its own wrap for extra structlog logging + Phase-E remedy sentence. Round-2 stacked review found 2 Significant (doubled-mint message in the re-mint context string; MINT-leg structural test satisfiable by pre-existing comments alone rather than real dispatch) and 2 Medium (run-on punctuation in Branch 0's remedy sentence; zero test coverage on Branch 0's mint-failure path) -- all four fixed: message template now takes the verb from context verbatim (no auto-appended 'mint failed'), structural test scoped to post-USE_LEASED-dispatch source requiring an actual mint_t1_session_token( call, punctuation fixed, new Branch-0 mint-failure test added. Full suite green (12798 passed, 0 failed) after fixes. Committed 4279f70b on develop.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Update (2026-07-12): nexus-ngcpo's fix (T1 session token refresh/lease-freshness/ownership-recovery) landed and, per its own review, WIDENED this asymmetry rather than narrowing it. Branch 0 (mcp/core.py) now has materially more branching logic (borrow-if-fresh / recover-by-remint-for-same-id-if-stale, plus a whole periodic refresh task) that tier-3's CLI path (get_t1_database() in t1.py) does not mirror at all -- tier-3 only ever borrows-if-fresh or falls through to a wholly different (CLI-dedicated) identity, with no refresh loop and no stale-lease recovery via remint. This was correctly left out of nexus-ngcpo's scope (per its relay), but whoever picks up this bead next should know the current asymmetry is LARGER than when this bead was originally filed, not smaller.

title: Testcontainers Postgres SSL-handshake-at-startup flake during full mvn suite
description: Two consecutive full 'mvn test' runs (2026-07-11, ~15:00 PDT) each had exactly one unrelated test class fail with the SAME error signature: java.sql.SQLException: Could not create new connection -> PSQLException: An error occurred while setting up the SSL connection, thrown from JdbcDatabaseContainer.createConnection at container startup, timing out around 123-124s. Run 1: dev.nexus.service.http.AspectHandlerEnqueueErrorTest. Run 2: dev.nexus.service.CatalogDeleteCollectionCascadeTest. Neither test touches the code under change in that session (SchemaMigrator.java chash preflight). Both pass cleanly and quickly in isolation (8/8 in 8s, and equivalent). docker ps -a showed 0 running containers at rest (Ryuk cleanup working, no leak/buildup). Docker Desktop is configured with only 7.65GiB memory for 16 CPUs. Load average was moderate (2.5-6.2), not extreme. Distinct unrelated test classes failing with the identical infra-level error across separate full-suite runs, both clean in isolation, strongly indicates transient Docker/testcontainers resource contention during long sequential full-suite runs (each integration test class starts + tears down its own Postgres container; forkCount defaults to 1/sequential per pom.xml, so it is not intra-run parallelism -- more likely accumulated Docker daemon-level pressure or a flaky SSL handshake under momentary load). Same general flake CLASS as the earlier-diagnosed ChashVectorConcurrencyTest 503 issue (nexus-xqrq0, already fixed with retry-on-503) but a DIFFERENT mechanism (container-startup SSL handshake vs HTTP pool-exhaustion) and not yet root-caused or mitigated. Candidate fixes: (1) bump Docker Desktop memory allocation (machine config, not code); (2) add a startup connection-retry/backoff wrapper around JdbcDatabaseContainer.createConnection in the shared test base class, mirroring the ChashVectorConcurrencyTest postWithRetryOn503 pattern; (3) investigate whether testcontainers own container-reuse settings could reduce PG container churn across the suite. Not investigated further this session -- two full-suite reruns plus isolated confirmation was enough evidence to attribute this run failures to environment, not the SchemaMigrator commit (0bd39bdc), but the underlying flake class itself remains unfixed and will keep costing full-suite reruns until addressed.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Shipped c5d2a310 + 6de6bd90: mechanism fix only — sslmode=disable + withStartupAttempts(3) in PgContainerHelper.newContainer(); NO blanket surefire reruns (Hal directive). Dead connect() retry helper dropped in review fold (no callers). RESIDUAL: flake was low-frequency, so confirmation is statistical — if the SSL-handshake startup flake reappears in CI, reopen and instrument the container logs.

title: [bug] guided-upgrade retry re-runs already-succeeded collections from scratch + repeated passthrough_fallback_reembed warnings on one collection
description:
NARROWED 2026-07-11: originally filed against a 'vector_etl_count_mismatch (source=400 target=675)' symptom from GH #1381's final unreplied comment. That symptom is ALREADY FIXED by nexus-5b9v0 (closed 2026-07-10T01:03, commit 3d62de3e/994a8060) — root-caused to a cross-model-remap target-name collision, now hard-blocked pre-flight by TargetNameCollisionBlocked in driver.py before any write occurs. nexus-p9vqa (closed 2026-07-10) additionally shipped 'nx migration-audit' to retroactively detect pre-guard silent merges on already-migrated targets. This bead does NOT block RDR-155 P4b on that basis.

Two genuinely-unaddressed observations remain from the same GH #1381 transcript, narrowed to just these:

1. NON-RESUMABLE RETRY: after a migration run blocked partway through (T2 total_failed=16), a bare re-run (without nx migration --clear-state) re-migrated two ALREADY-SUCCEEDED collections from scratch (code__1-1__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1: 1620 chunks/461s; code__1-3__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1: 275 chunks/78s) before reaching new work — roughly 9 minutes of wasted re-work. No skip-if-already-migrated check at the per-collection level on retry.

2. REPEATED passthrough_fallback_reembed WARNINGS: the same collection (code__1-1__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1) logged 'vector_etl_passthrough_fallback_reembed' (provenance_mismatch=300, then batch_size=300 repeated 5x, then batch_size=120) 6 times before completing — unclear whether this is expected batch-chunking behavior (6 batches of ~300 to cover 1620 chunks, which would be normal and not a bug) or genuine redundant retry. Needs a source read of the passthrough-reembed batching loop to determine which.

Neither blocks the count-mismatch/collision correctness question (resolved). Downgraded from P1 (data-correctness blocker) to P2 (reliability/UX gap) — worth fixing before further real-user exposure to guided-upgrade, but not a P4b-deletion blocker on its own. Reference: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/1381
close_reason: Fixed by RDR-185 on the surface users actually take, and demoted on the other. The narrowed complaint (a bare re-run re-migrates already-succeeded collections from scratch, ~9min wasted) is exactly what the substrate rung's drop_converged_legs (nexus-mapbc terminal state: per-collection skip when the TARGET holds the source's rows) + the rung-keyed watermark resume (RDR-178 seam) eliminate on the Service mode: the local SQLite/Chroma tiers are an immutable migration source — no local schema migration to run. ladder path. The guided-upgrade VERB retains its old retry behavior but was demoted at RDR-185 P4.1 (hidden, dies at RDR-155 P4b); the one-verb story routes every retry through the fixed path. The repeated passthrough_fallback_reembed warning half is the nexus-bfdri mislabel class, now REFUSED loudly on billed targets (UnconsentedReembed) rather than warned per-batch.

title: nx catalog doctor --name-vs-embed-dim crashes in service/cloud mode
description:
_run_name_vs_embed_dim (src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/doctor.py:1058)
does 'client = t3_db._client' unconditionally. In service/cloud mode
t3_db is an HttpVectorClient, which has no _client attribute (that's
the local chromadb.PersistentClient/CloudClient shape) -- raises
AttributeError immediately, no traceback caught.

Repro on a fully-migrated cloud-mode install (T3 mode: cloud,
release_version 0.1.37):

    nx catalog doctor --name-vs-embed-dim --json

Traceback:
    File ".../catalog_cmds/doctor.py", line 480, in doctor_cmd
        report = _run_name_vs_embed_dim()
    File ".../catalog_cmds/doctor.py", line 1058, in _run_name_vs_embed_dim
        client = t3_db._client  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    AttributeError: 'HttpVectorClient' object has no attribute '_client'

Since RDR-155 made pgvector/service mode the primary T3 backend, this
diagnostic -- the one specifically meant to catch the nexus-a4h7b
mislabeled-collection bug class -- is unusable for the majority of
current installs. Needs either an HttpVectorClient-native sampling
path or a clean "not supported in service mode" guard instead of an
unhandled AttributeError.

Found while drafting an external recovery runbook (gist) for two
broken installs; the runbook has been written to skip this check with
a note rather than block on it.
notes: Fixed in PR #1392 (branch fix/t2-ensure-running-service-mode-skip, commit c9b5cdb2). Switched to t3_db.get_collection()+get_embeddings() dual-mode-safe surface instead of t3_db._client. 2 new regression tests, 9/9 passing.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1392 (merged 7f50e1c4)

title: Aspect-worker reclaim_stale client never evicts on auth failure (401 loop)
description:
aspect_worker_daemon.py's reclaim loop holds self._reclaim_queue as a
long-lived client constructed once at daemon startup (line ~202, via
self._queue_factory()) and calls queue.reclaim_stale(...) directly
(line ~234). Unlike claim_batch (routed through t2_index_write ->
_service_t2_write_locked in mcp_infra.py, which reactively evicts the
process-lifetime T2Database singleton on ANY exception so the next
call re-resolves credentials), reclaim_stale's except block (line
~240) only logs and keeps the loop alive with the SAME stale client.

Observed impact (2026-07-10): config.yml's service_token was rotated
at 02:24 local. The long-running aspect-worker daemon (pid 52927,
started the prior day) kept calling reclaim_stale with the old cached
token, hitting HTTP 401 every ~30s continuously for over 23 hours
(1394+ reclaim_failed events in aspect_worker_daemon.log) until
manually killed and restarted. claim_batch's self-healing path did
not save it either, since reclaim_stale runs on its own timer/client
independent of the claim loop.

Fix: give self._reclaim_queue the same reactive-eviction treatment as
_service_t2_db in mcp_infra.py -- on exception, discard and rebuild
the queue client (via self._queue_factory()) before the next reclaim
attempt, so a token rotation self-heals within one cycle (~30s)
instead of requiring a manual daemon restart.

Cross-checked all other live nx-mcp sessions via the shared mcp.log
for the same rotation window: exactly one transient 401 (a
best-effort chash dual-write), self-healed via the existing
_service_t2_write_locked eviction, nothing since. This bead is scoped
to the aspect-worker's reclaim_stale path specifically, not a general
credential problem.

Files: src/nexus/daemon/aspect_worker_daemon.py (~lines 156-240,
_reclaim_queue construction and reclaim loop)
notes: Fixed in PR #1392 (branch fix/t2-ensure-running-service-mode-skip, commit c9b5cdb2). _reclaim_once now rebuilds the queue handle on demand whenever self._reclaim_queue is None, mirroring mcp_infra's _service_t2_write_locked eviction pattern. 1 new regression test, 6/6 passing.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1392 (merged 7f50e1c4)

title: RDR-182 P4.2: nx remediate <topic> CLI (per-invocation confirm + consent record)
description:
Guided recovery from the CLI. A human types the command (implicit consent) AND confirms per-invocation for the mutate step.

Build: nx remediate <topic> printing the guided-recovery Playbook, with a per-invocation confirm via the _confirm_voyage_cost pattern (click.confirm, aborts non-interactive). On confirmed mutate, write a consent record via P1.2. Full clickable URLs; hard do-NOTs front-and-center.

TDD: test FIRST — non-interactive aborts (no mutate); declined confirm does not run and leaves the runbook URL on screen; accepted confirm records consent. Exact assertions. docs/cli-reference.md entry.

Acceptance: per-invocation confirm gates the mutate; consent recorded on accept; declining is safe; display of the playbook itself is ungated.
notes:
FOUNDATIONS REVIEW NOTES (2026-07-12): (1) record_consent is write-only — P4.2's per-invocation confirm + consent record likely wants a read surface (list_consents/has_consent) for 'what did I consent to and when'; add it here if needed (Telemetry + contract update; service-mode parity rides nexus-ng2sy). (2) Consent scope strings are unvalidated free text — introduce a shared scope builder (f'{verb}:{topic}' tied to the playbook topics registry + a {forensics,remediate} verb enum) so the audit trail cannot fragment on typos.
P3 CRITIQUE ASSIGNMENT (critic-p3 Medium, 2026-07-12): consent REVOCATION is unimplemented — nothing writes granted=False. This bead (or a P5 sibling) MUST wire the revoke-write: 'nx config set claude_assisted_remediation.enabled false' (and any CLI disable surface) writes record_consent(scope, ts, granted=False), honoring the migration docstring's promise that the audit trail retains revoke events. Use nexus.remediation.consent_scope(verb, topic) — the shared validated builder P3.2 introduced (do NOT hand-interpolate scope strings). Read surface (list_consents/has_consent) also still owed here. RDR-182 Test Plan lists 'consent is recorded and revocable' as in-scope — P5 gates on it.
close_reason: nx remediate <topic> shipped: describe -> per-invocation click.confirm (defaults NO, aborts on EOF, no --yes) gates the RELEASE; accepted confirm audit-records FAIL-CLOSED before the playbook prints (same 5-layer contract as the MCP tool). Revocation-write DELIVERED (the P3 critique obligation): nx config set of the flag writes a grant/revoke row (FLAG_CONSENT_SCOPE, best-effort — flag write never blocks on audit); read surface Telemetry.list_consents wired to nx remediate --history. Live-diag leg gated per A5. consent_scope validated builder. Double-APPROVE. Commit 7de1e579.

Display-only guidance. Per the consent taxonomy (RDR-182 Gap 3) this needs NO gate — printing text the operator chooses to copy IS the consent act; gating it would be over-friction and inconsistent with the shipped install-binary paste-to-Claude prompt.

title: RDR-182 P2.2: pre-emission statement allow-list lint over emitted diagnostics
description:
Guarantees emitted diagnostic SQL is read-only before it ever reaches an agent.

Reuse pattern: _DML_TARGET_RE classification from tests/test_changelog_rls_lint.py — apply the same read-only classification as a pre-emission lint over any SQL the Playbook emitter emits for a diagnostic (forensics) topic.

TDD: test FIRST — a diagnostic playbook containing any mutating statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE) FAILS the lint; a pure SELECT/system-catalog playbook passes; emitted diagnostics reference only schema/metadata objects (databasechangelog, pg_constraint, counts) never row/document/note content. Exact assertions.

Acceptance: lint wired into the emitter path for diagnostic topics; mutating diagnostic content is impossible-by-construction; no store CONTENT object referenced.
notes: AUDIT (nx_plan_audit): NOT a mechanical reuse. _DML_TARGET_RE is a test-only regex today; adapting it into a pre-emission runtime lint over emitter output (classify SELECT/system-catalog vs mutating, decide fail-closed behavior, wire into the emitter path for diagnostic topics) is design work. Confirm the classifier covers CTEs/DO-blocks/functions, not just leading-keyword match.
close_reason: Read-only lint shipped: nexus.remediation.sql_lint (is_read_only_diagnostic + assert_read_only_diagnostics + DiagnosticSqlViolation), wired into emit_playbook via the new Playbook.diagnostic_sql field — mutating diagnostics impossible-by-construction on every surface. Allowlist fail-closed; covers CTE-smuggled DML, DO blocks, SELECT INTO, locking reads, session keywords; store tables aggregate-only (count yes, content never). 16 tests; the audit note's CTE/DO concern explicitly covered. title: nx forensics / nx remediate: first-class commands that emit agent-runnable diagnostic+recovery prompts (with clickable URLs) for a Claude instance to execute
description:
Hal's idea (2026-07-10), generalizing the GH #1390 relay pattern: instead of hand-authoring /tmp relay prompts and pointing users at doc sections, ship PRODUCT commands that guide the Claude instance running them through diagnosis and recovery. First instance already live: nx daemon service install-binary's chash-poison gate (17f3f986) emits a full clickable GitHub runbook URL + a ready-to-paste 'give this to your Claude' prompt. Generalize into a surface:
- nx forensics <topic> (e.g. chash-poison, migration-divergence): emits the read-only diagnostic script/prompt (the GH#1390 forensic SQL bundle is the template — see the three /tmp relay prompts I authored) for a Claude to run and interpret. Read-only, safe-by-construction, structured deliverable.
- nx remediate <topic>: emits the guided recovery playbook prompt (runbook §8.1 style) with the exact commands, sequenced, and the hard do-NOTs.
Design notes: full clickable https URLs everywhere (terminals autolink); prompts must be self-contained (context + hard READ-ONLY/do-not constraints + steps + deliverable + 'box gone' escape), exactly like the forensic relays; pin URLs to main (releases promote develop->main); consider a shared prompt-emitter helper so error surfaces (gates, doctor, guided-upgrade blocks) all reference the same generated prompts. RDR-worthy if it grows beyond a couple of topics. Provenance: the GH#1390 three-round forensic relay + the install-gate paste-to-Claude prompt proved the pattern works end-to-end with a remote operator's Claude.
notes:
ELEVATED to strategic epic (Hal, 2026-07-10): 'assume users have Claude and bake that into update/upgrade, seamless + secure + compliant + privacy-protecting.' Full framing + the HARD security/privacy/compliance requirements: T2 nexus/strategic-claude-assisted-upgrade-2026-07-10. This is RDR-scale + brainstorming-gate-required — the nx forensics/remediate commands are the TACTICAL surface under a broader 'Claude-assisted upgrade' RDR to be created. Locked constraints the RDR must honor: diagnostics READ-ONLY by construction; nothing leaves the box (schema/metadata only, never note content); consent + auditability; the product EMITS guidance, the user's Claude EXECUTES locally with the user's own creds (product never runs their Claude nor receives their data); the safe path must be the easy path (kill the drop-the-constraint reflex).
Parent RDR scaffolded: RDR-182 (docs/rdr/rdr-182-claude-assisted-upgrade-remediation.md, status draft, T2 nexus_rdr/182, commit c7fb3ca6). ykzbj is the tactical command surface (nx forensics/nx remediate) under RDR-182's strategic scope. Opt-in (default-off) + Claude Desktop (RDR-126) integration are first-class RDR requirements. Next lifecycle: /conexus:rdr-research -> rdr-gate -> rdr-accept before implementing (brainstorming-gate).
RDR-182 PLAN (2026-07-10, strategic-planner): 20 child beads .1-.21 (.4 deleted). Phase 0 GATING spike .1 (A4 tool-boundary opt-in refusal) blocks ALL impl. Phases: P1 foundations(.5 config default-off/.6 consent-audit/.7 Playbook emitter) -> P2 trust boundary(.8 nexus_diag role/.9 stmt lint) -> [.21 foundations stacked review] -> P3 MCP tools(.10 forensics/.11 remediate 5-layer) -> [.12/.13 stacked review] -> P4 CLI(.14 forensics display-only ungated/.15 remediate consented) -> [.16 review] -> P5 MVV(.17 safety-property/.18 e2e no-content-read) -> [.19 final review/.20 test-validation]. ENGINE DEPENDENCY: nexus-c4143 (SchemaMigrator fail-clean) is a SEPARATE engine-cut track, referenced not folded. Plan in T2 nexus/plan-rdr182.md.
close_reason: RDR-182 COMPLETE + CLOSED (2026-07-13). All 20 phase sub-beads P0-P5 closed. Shipped: opt-in gate (default-off, global-config-only, A4), consent audit (grant/revoke + read surface), shared playbook emitter, fail-closed read-only SQL lint, nexus_diag SELECT-only+BYPASSRLS role + single connection choke point, MCP forensics/remediate tools, nx forensics/nx remediate CLI, both MVV proofs. Every phase stacked-reviewed; final holistic review (review-final + critic-final APPROVE, test-validator validated) verified all 5 Gaps delivered + taxonomy amendments A5/H1 consistent across code/docs/tests. Full suite 13056 green. RDR frontmatter closed (f671fc63). --force past the 1 open DEFERRED residual (tracked follow-ups, not missed phase work): ng2sy P0 (service-mode parity), vounk P1 (health.py probe rewire), s4a98 P1 (enable-command crash), 9bufb P2 (content-scoping views), wnp3c P2 (3 remaining topics). Commits 96f96c10..f671fc63.

title: Boxes that migrated nonconforming chashes pre-guard will crash-loop catalog-013-3's VALIDATE on the next engine upgrade (canon-chat box: PREDICTED on v0.1.37)
description: Follow-on from the GH#1390 forensic (nexus-4m6i0.11). The canon-chat box completed its Chroma->pgvector migration only AFTER an agent dropped the chash checks — so chunks_768 (and possibly chash_index via client dual-write) likely now HOLD 16/18-char chash rows, and chunks_768_chash_len_check was re-added NOT VALID post-migration (mechanism unclear — minor loose end). PREDICTION: on upgrade to v0.1.37+, catalog-013-2 MARK_RANs (2-of-5 precondition) but catalog-013-3 VALIDATEs the two PRESENT constraints (chunks_768, chash_index); if any row violates, VALIDATE raises -> 013-3 has no guard against VIOLATING ROWS (only against MISSING constraints) -> unrecorded failure -> crash loop every boot: ms57z UX, new cause. Fail-loud on malformed data is the DESIGNED posture (catalog-013 header), but crash-LOOP is not a remedy. Scope: (a) decide guidance vs changeset (a 013-4 normalization can't recompute sha256(chunk_text) without pgcrypto — likely guided remediation doc + nx doctor probe instead: SELECT count(*) FROM chunks_<dim> WHERE length(chash)<>32); (b) warn the canon-chat box operator BEFORE their next engine upgrade (manual remediation: normalize/delete nonconforming rows or re-migrate after nexus-<B1> lands); (c) general population = any box that migrated a legacy-id store pre-guard with constraints dropped or absent. Depends on the B1 ETL fix for clean re-migration.
close_reason: Conexus-side FIXED (develop b2f5fc0c). nx doctor _check_migration_state gains a service-mode-gated chash-conformance probe: counts non-32-char rows across chunks_384/768/1024 + chash_index + catalog_document_chunks and emits a 'Chunk chash conformance' WARNING (never fatal — the box serves fine now) with do-not-upgrade / do-not-drop-constraints / runbook-§8.1 remediation; psql failure degrades to a non-fatal warn (no false alarm). runbook §8.1 = the full recovery playbook (rollback -> re-index -> re-migrate -> only then upgrade) and points back at the probe. sot7v prevents NEW boxes reaching this state; this detects+recovers boxes already in it. DEFERRED (explicit, not lost): engine-side hardening of catalog-013-3 to tolerate VIOLATING rows via a pre-VALIDATE guarded skip-loud — NOT shipped because it softens the fail-loud-on-bad-data posture (a design decision, needs a deliberate engine cut, and the proactive doctor warn now covers the practical risk). ⚠ OPERATOR ACTION for Hal: the GH#1390 canon-chat box (hhildebrand) is the one known affected instance — do NOT upgrade its engine past v0.1.29 until its legacy-id collections are re-migrated per §8.1. 686 health+migration tests green.

title: No harness installs a REAL published old conexus wheel, writes data with it, then upgrades — the deepest 5.x-journey coverage gap
description: 360-sweep Dimension D gap 3 (2026-07-10, NEW). Every 'aged' fixture in the repo is CURRENT code hand-building old-shaped state (seed_legacy.py, seed_gated.py) or an old ENGINE binary (cold rehearsal) — nothing reproduces 'an actual published 5.x release wrote this store'. That distinction is exactly where hand-built fixtures drift from reality (the epic nexus-4m6i0's thesis). Sketch: isolated venv + pip install conexus==5.4.5 (pinned old wheel), drive its real write path (nx store put / nx index on a tiny corpus, local mode), then swap to the current wheel and run nx guided-upgrade against a disposable service; assert classification/migration/verify outcomes exactly. Self-provisioning script under tests/e2e/, manual-dispatch CI at most (CI cost discipline). Cost: HIGH. Audit record: T2 nexus/360-sweep-dimension-D-upgrade-coverage-audit-2026-07-10.
close_reason: Grooming close (Hal, 2026-07-17). Largely superseded by the RDR-185 P4.3 era-hop, which now does most of what this bead sketched: pip-installs the REAL published conexus==6.0.0 wheel from PyPI, provisions with ITS real nx init --service (era engine bundle included), then swaps to the current tree and converges via nx upgrade alone, unattended, with exact re-id assertions. HONEST RESIDUAL, uncovered by choice: the store content is still seed_legacy.py hand-built (necessarily, for pre-RDR-108 id shapes no released wheel can write) rather than written by the old wheel's own write path — the hand-built-fixture-drift thesis stands but its remaining surface is small. The bead's own sketch drives nx guided-upgrade (demoted at P4.1, dies at RDR-155 P4b) and self-rates cost HIGH. Reopen if a real 5.x-written-store defect class ever surfaces that the era-hop misses.

title: Elevate the server-side CCE embed concurrency + Voyage rate-governor research memo to an RDR
description: 360-sweep Dimension C findings F1+F2 (2026-07-10). CceEmbedder.java:110-138 embeds N prose chunks as N SEQUENTIAL Voyage round-trips (per-text calls are semantically required for CCE cross-doc isolation; sequential-vs-concurrent is not) — the dominant knowledge/docs/rdr indexing latency. There is NO proactive Voyage rate governor: only reactive 429 retry (3x/500ms), so concurrent upserts can 429-storm and whole-call retries re-embed text that would have succeeded under a governor (the $ tail). Client-side paging was already tried and CLOSED as ineffective (nexus-o1mbu) — the bottleneck is server-side. Research memo exists: T2 nexus/research-server-side-embed-reduction-2026-07-05. This bead: run /conexus:rdr-create to elevate that memo into an RDR (bounded concurrency per-text embeds + 300-RPM governor), THEN decompose. Include Dimension C's F4 note in RDR scope: verify Voyage per-REQUEST token accounting (no 32k-request guard exists on the pg upsert path; 300-chunk batches run fine so per-input 32k is likely the only constraint — verify, don't assume).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: GROOM 2026-07-22 cross-link: RDR-188 (accepted) formalized the REACTIVE-only posture and created nexus-rb67a as the accepted proactive-governor debt bead — the rerank stage inherits VoyageEmbedder's retry shape by locked decision. title: search() re-embeds the query on every pagination page — P pages = P query embeds where 1 vector suffices
description: 360-sweep Dimension C finding F3 (2026-07-10, NEW). mcp/core.py:1019-1056: paged search computes fetch_n = offset + limit and re-issues the full stateless /v1/vectors/search per page; the server embeds the query on each call. P page-turns of the same query = P Voyage/local query embeds (plus growing re-fetch amplification: page 3 re-fetches pages 1-2's rows). Low per-embed cost (query <= 256 chars) but pure waste. Fix direction: session-scoped (query, model)->vector cache on the client, or embed-once + true server-side paging. Audit record: T3 analysis-deep-embedding-call-efficiency-2026-07-10.
close_reason: Shipped on develop: 2-page lookahead + single-entry 120s TTL cache in the MCP search tool; one embed per page-turn burst, amplification gone. Mutation-verified, 122 green. True server-side paging (engine offset support) remains a possible future engine-side upgrade but the client cache removes the observed waste.

title: migration-audit: cloud Chroma leg auth failure surfaces as raw traceback; no explicit --legs narrowing for a retired cloud source
description: Dogfood run on Hal's live store (2026-07-10, first real-store execution of nexus-p9vqa's nx migration-audit): open_cloud_read_client raised chromadb ChromaError 'Permission denied' (ChromaCloud creds present but rejected — account possibly retired post-cutover). Two defects: (1) the CLI only wraps RuntimeError, so the ChromaError escapes as a raw traceback (code-review-expert Low 2 on nexus-p9vqa, now dogfood-evidenced); (2) there is no way to audit the still-available LOCAL leg when the cloud leg is permanently gone — the audit needs an explicit --legs local|cloud|both narrowing that is LOUD about partial scope (a silently-partial audit reporting clean would be a false clean, the exact class this tool exists to prevent). Wider implication to surface: if the ChromaCloud account is retired, the CLOUD Chroma migration source no longer exists as a rollback/audit target regardless of the RDR-155 deprecation window.
close_reason: Shipped (develop 6f2a55e5): --legs both|local|cloud with loud partial-scope disclosure (render banner + JSON partial_scope/audited_legs + documented exit-code caveat), actionable RuntimeError wrapping for rejected-credential leg opens (closes the already-opened local leg first — review High), zero-open-legs hard error (deleted source never reads clean). Reviews: code-review-expert 0 Critical (High leak fixed + regression test), substantive-critic 2 Significant both remediated (exit-code caveat documented per option a; --legs cloud symmetric coverage added). Dogfooded on Hal's live store: --legs local ran clean-of-merges (3 never-materialized stale 1-2188 collision pairs flagged for cleanup). 655 migration tests green.

title: Rehearsal seed-coverage manifest: single-file JSON edit can silently defeat the exact-match gate
design: Critique of nexus-gm38i uncommitted work (tests/test_rehearsal_seed_coverage_lint.py, scripts/gen_rehearsal_hop_manifest.py, tests/data/rehearsal_old_tag_changesets.json). tests/data/rehearsal_old_tag_changesets.json is verified only by (1) tag string equality to Java OLD_TAG and (2) len(changesets) >= 100. Neither guard verifies the manifest's CONTENT against the actual git tree at OLD_TAG. A single fabricated or copied-forward (id, author) tuple added to the committed manifest's changesets list -- claiming a real future-hop FORCE-RLS row-DML changeset already existed at OLD_TAG -- silently removes it from the derived hop set (hop = derived(HEAD) - old_tag_changesets) with ZERO change to DECLARED_SEED_COVERAGE or any Java file. All tests pass; a reviewer scanning for 'did the declaration change' (the documented tripwire) sees nothing. Empirically confirmed in-process (no repo files modified): tampering old_tag_changesets with one fabricated tuple reproduces the untouched 3-member DECLARED_SEED_COVERAGE exactly, defeating the gate. Fix candidates: (a) verify manifest content via a checksum/hash of the sorted (id,author,file) tuples embedded at generation time and cross-checked, or (b) re-derive the manifest against a shallow git-fetch of OLD_TAG at CI time (reintroduces the network dependency the design deliberately avoided -- tradeoff), or (c) at minimum, assert every manifest entry's changeset id/author pair is NOT independently derivable as a HEAD-only addition by cross-referencing file provenance. See T2 nexus/critique-nexus-gm38i-rehearsal-seed-coverage-lint.md for full critique.
close_reason: Remediated: manifest now carries a sha256 integrity hash (manifest_integrity, computed only by scripts/gen_rehearsal_hop_manifest.py from git truth) recomputed and asserted by load_manifest() on every run, plus (id,author) uniqueness. Re-verified the exact reproduced attack (fabricated tuple appended, no hash recompute) now fails loud with 'integrity check' error. Residual (accepted, documented in both docstrings): deliberate hand-forgery by recomputing the hash with the same shared manifest_integrity() function still succeeds silently -- reproduced and confirmed this matches the explicitly documented/accepted scope (same intent as editing the lint's own assertions), not an undisclosed gap. Regression test tests/test_manifest_tamper_fails_integrity passes. 71 lint tests green, ruff clean. Full re-verification: T2 nexus/critique-nexus-gm38i-remediation-reverify.md

title: AST factory-construction lint has no import-alias resolution (HttpVectorClient bypass)
description:
tests/test_http_vector_client_factory_lint.py's _ConstructionVisitor.visit_Call matches only the LITERAL callee name/attr 'HttpVectorClient' (ast.Name.id or ast.Attribute.attr). It does not resolve import aliases the way its sibling lint in the same codebase (src/nexus/storage_boundary_lint.py's _collect_constructor_aliases, used for T2Database/T3Database/Catalog) does.

Empirically verified (ran analyze() against two synthetic fixtures under the real scan_constructions()/analyze() functions): both 'from nexus.db.http_vector_client import HttpVectorClient as HVC; HVC()' and 'X = m.HttpVectorClient; X()' produce ZERO violations -- a bare, ungated construction that is invisible to the lint. This is a plausible ACCIDENTAL evasion, not just adversarial: the codebase's own deferred-import convention already uses 'import X as Y' pervasively for circular-dependency avoidance (see the very functions the .3/.4 tests exercise, e.g. 'from nexus.db.http_vector_client import _resolve_endpoint, get_http_vector_client').

Fix: port _collect_constructor_aliases (or equivalent ImportFrom-alias tracking) from storage_boundary_lint.py into the factory lint's _ConstructionVisitor, and add a synthetic mechanism test pinning the aliased-import case (mirroring test_attribute_form_construction_is_flagged, which covers module-attribute form but not renamed-import form).

Context: nx (substantive-critic review of nexus-4m6i0.4), Significant not Critical -- narrower/less likely than the structlog leak (nexus-dizod) but a real, verified gap in the lint's exhaustiveness claim.
close_reason: Shipped in 534d2281 on develop: connection-path integration tests (real CLI->factory->probe->httpx graph, mutation-verified against the probe being un-wired) + AST factory lint with from-import alias resolution. Review Critical nexus-dizod (structlog leaking the pre-rewrite contradictory remedy to stderr) fixed at the log site and pinned by a whole-output assertion, mutation-verified. title: catalog-013-2 MARK_RAN permanently freezes precondition re-evaluation — no self-heal if a missing constraint is later added out-of-band
design:
Context: nx. Root: substantive-critic round-2 review of nexus-boz39's fix (service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml, catalog-013-2's <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN">).

Verified against liquibase-core 4.29.0 source (extracted sources jar, cross-checked ChangeSet.java, SqlPrecondition.java, MarkChangeSetRanGenerator.java, StandardChangeLogHistoryService.java, ShouldRunChangeSetFilter.java):

1. MARK_RAN writes a permanent DATABASECHANGELOG row (EXECTYPE=MARK_RAN) on the FIRST boot where the precondition's 5-constraint count check fails (verified: SqlPrecondition.check() does plain string equality, so ANY count != 5 -- 0,1,2,3,4 -- triggers it uniformly, not just the empty-vs-full binary case).
2. StandardChangeLogHistoryService.queryDatabaseChangeLogTable does `SELECT *` with no EXECTYPE filter, and getRanChangeSets() builds a RanChangeSet for every row including MARK_RAN ones.
3. ShouldRunChangeSetFilter.accepts() treats ANY existing matching DATABASECHANGELOG row (any exectype) as "already ran" and permanently excludes the changeset from ever being reconsidered -- UNLESS the changeset has runAlways/runOnChange, which catalog-013-2 and catalog-013-3 do not.

Net effect: once a box hits the MARK_RAN path (or once catalog-013-3 runs at all, recording EXECUTED), BOTH changesets are frozen forever on that box -- the precondition is not "rechecked quietly every boot," it is NEVER invoked again. This is materially better than round-1's failOnError=false (no more per-boot retry cost or SEVERE spam) but it trades away round-1's incidental self-healing property: round-1's crash-loop / soft-fail-loop would keep retrying every boot until the missing constraint was fixed (by any means), at which point the very next boot would succeed and record EXECUTED with the constraint genuinely validated. Round-2's MARK_RAN can never do that -- if the missing constraint is later added out-of-band (mirroring this whole incident's own root-cause pattern: an unexplained, out-of-band divergence), on a box already MARK_RAN'd, that constraint will sit permanently NOT VALID/unproven with zero further Liquibase attempt to validate it, silently.

Bounded blast radius: this is the SAME "unproven old rows" risk class the file's own header (nexus-e0hd2) already accepts as tolerable pre-audit-fix, not a new one; and the codebase's own established remediation precedent (013-1b, 013-3: ship a NEW changeset id to redo a fix rather than rely on an old changeset re-triggering) is consistent with "the correct recovery from a genuinely-missing constraint is a new changeset, not silent DDL." Non-blocking for nexus-boz39's specific scope (crash-loop + log-spam both are genuinely closed, verified).

Recommendation: document this residual explicitly in catalog-013-2/013-3's header comment (this file already documents every other subtlety at this level of rigor) and/or treat "constraint later restored out-of-band" as requiring a new changeset (catalog-013-4 style) rather than assuming Liquibase will notice on its own.

Full verification trail: T2 nexus/critique-nexus-4m6i0.1-catalog-013-round2-mark-ran-critique.md
close_reason: Documented (f5696646 on develop). MARK_RAN freeze semantics written where authors hit them: authoritative nexus-4m6i0.12 block in catalog-013-chash-checks-validate.xml (013-2) + freeze note on 013-3 (EXECUTED freezes identically), pointer notes in fk-002/fk-003-validate.xml covering all ten guarded VALIDATEs, and the recovery CONVENTION (frozen divergence -> NEW changeset id, catalog-013-1b/013-3 precedent; never in-place edit, never assume Liquibase re-notices) in test_changelog_validate_precondition_lint.py's docstring (always-on CI home). All edits XML-comment/docstring only; checksum-neutrality re-proven via SchemaUpgradeRehearsalIntegrationTest old-to-HEAD hop (2/2 green) + both changelog lints (55 passed).

title: [bug] query() service-mode catalog-routing branch bypasses nexus-3l6gz's _group_collections_by_model — same multi-model empty-result defect
description:
Critique of the uncommitted nexus-3l6gz fix (substantive-critic, 2026-07-09) found a sibling instance of the exact same defect the fix addresses.

nexus-3l6gz fixed search_metadata_scoped and search_graph_hop (the two standalone MCP tools) by adding _group_collections_by_model() (src/nexus/mcp/core.py) and looping one combined-query call per embedding-model group instead of one mixed-model call.

query()'s SERVICE-MODE BRANCH (src/nexus/mcp/core.py lines ~1610-1811, nested inside `if has_catalog_params:` i.e. author/content_type/follow_links/subtree given) calls t3.search_metadata_scoped(...) and t3.search_graph_hop(...) DIRECTLY on the raw `target = _resolve_corpus_target(corpus, t3)` list — three call sites (~1683, 1692, 1701) — with NO grouping by embedding model. This is the exact anti-pattern the RCA (T3 doc: debug-search_graph_hop-multimodel-corpus-empty-nexus-3l6gz) diagnosed.

Repro shape: query(question=..., corpus="all", author="X") or query(question=..., corpus="code,docs", content_type="code") in service mode — target spans >1 embedding model (voyage-code-3 vs voyage-context-3) — the branch embeds the query once with the first collection's model and silently drops/mis-ranks the other model's chunks, reproducing the same 'No documents found' / incomplete-result symptom nexus-3l6gz fixed for the other two tools.

query() is documented as the canonical entry point for analytical questions (conexus:query skill) and its own docstring documents both `corpus="all"` and the catalog params as supported, so this is a live, reachable combination, not hypothetical.

Fix: extend _group_collections_by_model() to the three t3.search_metadata_scoped/search_graph_hop call sites inside query()'s service-mode branch (mirror the loop-and-merge shape already applied to the standalone tools). Add regression tests analogous to tests/test_combined_query_multimodel_bug.py but targeting query() with has_catalog_params=True and a multi-model corpus.

Also flagged (Significant, not blocking): neither search_metadata_scoped's nor search_graph_hop's docstring documents (a) the new per-model-group round-trip / all-or-nothing partial-failure semantics, or (b) that the cross-group merge sorts by raw cosine distance across DIFFERENT embedding-model spaces (not a rigorously comparable metric) — search_topic_scoped's docstring sets precedent for documenting this class of caveat.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] search_graph_hop MCP: multi-prefix corpus spanning embedding models returns empty when one model-group has no hits — single-corpus works
description: Found during 6.5.1 post-reinstall verification (2026-07-09, engine v0.1.35, live tenant). REPRO: search_graph_hop(seeds=['1.9.80'], corpus='code', depth=2) → 1 row (1.9.3, dist 0.5632). Same call with corpus='code,docs' → 'No documents found', despite collection_list showing both code__1-9__voyage-code-3__v1 and docs__1-9__voyage-context-3__v1, and explicit corpus='code__1-9__voyage-code-3__v1,docs__1-9__voyage-context-3__v1' also returning the row. Hypothesis: the MCP layer groups resolved collections by embedding model (voyage-code-3 vs voyage-context-3 — the query must be embedded per model), calls the SQL function per group, and the merge mishandles the case where one group is empty (docs group legitimately empty here: the only docs-collection doc reachable is the seed itself) — dropping the non-empty group's rows. LATENT until now: combined queries returned zero on all live data until v0.1.35 (nexus-x6kdz), so multi-corpus graph-hop was never live-exercised. Workaround: single corpus prefix or explicit collection names. Check the sibling tools (search_metadata_scoped multi-model corpus) for the same merge shape. Client-side (src/nexus/mcp/core.py corpus resolution/merge) — fix rides a PyPI release, no engine change expected.
close_reason: Fixed in develop 36c088a0. Root cause (bead hypothesis REFUTED): no per-embedding-model grouping existed anywhere — the service guards only vector dimension, both voyage models are 1024-dim, so mixed corpus lists passed the guard and the query embedded with only the first collection's model, ranking one vector across incompatible embedding spaces. Fix: _group_collections_by_model + _grouped_combined_query in src/nexus/mcp/core.py — one client call per model group, None-safe global distance sort, dedup, post-merge truncation — applied to ALL FIVE call sites (search_metadata_scoped, search_graph_hop, and query()'s three service-mode sites; the latter found by critic inverse-grep, tracked+closed as nexus-hg745). search_topic_scoped confirmed immune. 12 regression tests (repro, no-mixed-call contract, cross-group merge/ordering, query() branches, partial-failure all-or-nothing); adjacent suite 86 green. Both stacked reviewers clean after one fix round each. Semantics documented: all-or-nothing partial failure; cross-model distance non-comparability caveat. Engine-side fail-loud guard: nexus-9y5om (open, rides next engine tag). NOTE: live MCP runs the installed 6.5.1 wheel — the live repro (seeds=['1.9.80'], corpus='code,docs') becomes verifiable through the MCP surface after the next PyPI release + reinstall; unit fake mirrors the proven server semantics in the interim.

Context: nx

RDR-130/#1007 switched conexus/commands/{rdr-show,rdr-gate,rdr-accept,rdr-research,rdr-audit}.md
from `"$ARGUMENTS"` to `'$ARGUMENTS'` in the preamble backtick line, on the premise
(commit 27bc9a8c) that "args are load-bearing but are shell-safe ID/keyword/flag
tokens... immune to every metacharacter except a literal apostrophe, which cannot
occur in those tokens."

That premise is FALSE for rdr-research specifically: its `add <id> <text>` subcommand
is designed to accept free-form research-finding prose (see conexus/commands/rdr-research.md
description: "Add, track, or verify structured research findings"). A user's apostrophe
in prose ("tenant's", "engine's own") reproduces the original (eval):1: unmatched ' crash,
because Claude Code textually splices $ARGUMENTS into the !`...` line BEFORE any shell
quoting/escaping can run -- there is no way to safely single-quote a string containing an
embedded apostrophe via pure textual substitution (would need '\''-style escaping, which
Claude Code's substitution does not perform).

tests/test_command_shell_quoting_e2e.py documents this as an accepted boundary
("Their one boundary -- a literal apostrophe -- is documented in the command bodies;
token-only args cannot contain one") but conexus/commands/rdr-research.md's body does NOT
actually document this constraint to users, and the constraint is violated by the command's
own designed use case.

Candidate fixes (need design work, not a quick quote-style flip):
1. Drop $ARGUMENTS from the preamble shell line entirely (matching the 18 "dropped-arg"
   commands) and give up the auto-preload-by-ID feature for rdr-research, OR
2. Have the preamble handler take the RDR ID via a separate, explicitly-safe channel
   (e.g. a dedicated flag Claude Code doesn't textually splice raw prose into), OR
3. Document the constraint prominently in rdr-research.md AND make the crash a graceful,
   understandable error (currently "(eval):1: unmatched '" is unintelligible to a user).

Found during a 2026-07-08 substantive-critic review (T2 nexus title:
critique-rdr-research-quoting-incident-2026-07-08) of an AI assistant's reverted mistake:
the assistant "fixed" the apostrophe crash by flipping to "$ARGUMENTS" (double-quote),
which passed a naive smoke test but reintroduced the exact shell-injection hole #1007
closed, and was caught only by tests/test_command_shell_quoting_e2e.py's
test_inventory_is_sane hard assertion after a user challenge. The revert restored the
single-quoted (injection-safe, apostrophe-crash-prone) state -- this bead tracks fixing
the underlying crash-on-apostrophe gap properly rather than leaving it as a known landmine.
close_reason: Duplicate of nexus-ybvyo (same root cause: single-quoted ARGUMENTS preamble breaks on apostrophes; this was the rdr-research re-report 5 days later). Merged - ybvyo carries the fix; bug still live at conexus/commands/rdr-research.md:8 at merge time.

title: nx upgrade / nx doctor: substrate-migration bridge pointer — detect pending Chroma→pgvector cutover and point at nx guided-upgrade
description: Two upgrade commands confused users (Hal, 2026-07-08): nx upgrade (routine in-place schema migrations, hook-invoked with --auto) and nx guided-upgrade (one-time substrate cutover). Nothing bridges them: a user with a pending substrate migration runs nx upgrade, sees 'migrations complete', and gets zero pointer to the real next step. Fix: nx upgrade runs detect_pending_migration best-effort in INTERACTIVE mode (never in --auto hook mode — keep hooks fast and silent) and prints a loud banner pointing at nx guided-upgrade (interactive, cost preview first). Same pointer as an nx doctor check. Auto-DETECT without auto-EXECUTE: the cutover keeps its consent gate (--yes, cost preview, provisions PG, may bill re-embeds). Dies naturally with RDR-155 P4b (which deletes guided-upgrade + the migration module). Client-side only; ships in 6.4.1.
close_reason: Shipped in 6a70282a on develop. Four surfaces point a pending Chroma→pgvector cutover at nx guided-upgrade: interactive nx upgrade banner + TTY chain-offer, nx doctor banner, both endpoint-not-resolvable errors, SessionStart hook context line. Gate = legacy dir + ABSENCE of real-service evidence (service_url / HOST-PORT env / pg_credentials / lease) — NOT storage_backend_for, whose SERVICE hard default would have darkened everything for the vanilla 5.x upgrader (review CRITICAL, caught by both reviewers, fixed + locked under the real unpatched default). title: taxonomy discover 409s on re-discovery instead of updating persisted topics (service mode)
description:
Observed on the same work-instance nx index run, collection
docs__1-56__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1 (45 chunks, 768d, service-mode clustering):

  event='taxonomy_discover_failed' ...
  httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '409 Conflict' for url
  'http://127.0.0.1:54963/v1/taxonomy/topics/persist_discovered'
  Taxonomy: discover FAILED for docs__1-56__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1
  (HTTPStatusError) - run `nx taxonomy discover` to retry

Call chain: commands/index.py run_collection_postprocessing -> _discover_taxonomy
-> taxonomy_cmd.py discover_for_collection -> _discover_via_service ->
db/t2/http_taxonomy_store.py HttpTaxonomyStore.discover_topics ->
persist_discovered_topics -> POST /topics/persist_discovered -> resp.raise_for_status().

409 strongly suggests the engine's persist_discovered handler treats a second
discovery on a collection that already has persisted topics as a conflict
(probably a unique constraint on (collection, topic_label) or similar) instead
of upserting/replacing. The CLI's own error message ("run `nx taxonomy discover`
to retry") implies the intended UX is idempotent re-discovery, but every retry
will hit the same 409 since nothing about the state changed - a collection that
has ever had topics discovered can seemingly never re-discover in service mode.

Needs: (1) confirm the engine-side persist_discovered SQL/logic to see whether
it's insert-only vs. upsert, (2) decide the right semantics - does re-discover
mean replace the topic set, or merge, and (3) fix the 409 to either succeed
(desired case) or fail with a clear message instead of the generic
HTTPStatusError bubbling up as "discover FAILED".
close_reason: Fixed end-to-end, live in production. Root cause: TOCTOU race on the unlocked existing-topics guard (two concurrent persist_discovered both count 0, both insert, loser 23505 -> typed 409) — NOT version skew (handler byte-identical v0.1.14..develop) and NOT plain re-discovery (guard skips that). Engine fix (03eb2ba2, shipped engine-service-v0.1.32): per-(tenant,collection) pg_advisory_xact_lock + SET LOCAL lock_timeout=5s in persist_discovered/rebuild/split; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING belt + existing-id reuse on discover AND rebuild root inserts. Client fix: persist_discovered_topics treats a 23505-scoped 409 as benign skip (pre-fix engines); non-23505/non-409 propagate. v0.1.32 deployed to api.conexus-nexus.com + STEP-6 GREEN first attempt (conexus-confirmed [20412]: /version 0.1.32 through the edge, voyage parity ~4e-7, recall@20 13/13, latencies in bound; rollback 0.1.31 on file). Stacked reviews clean (reviewer: approve; critic HIGH + 2 Medium all addressed in-arc). Full mvn 1180/1180; two red suite runs en route were kill-orphaned-testcontainer environment noise (clean-env run green). NOTE: bead was claimed by the work instance (hal.hildebrand) which filed it; fix executed on this instance at Hal's direction.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (debugger, 2026-07-07): TOCTOU race, NOT version skew and NOT plain re-discovery. persistDiscoveredTopics' skip-existing guard is a plain unlocked SELECT COUNT in the withTenant txn (TenantScope.java:215-223 confirms one txn); the root TOPICS insert (TaxonomyRepository.java:1698-1705) has NO onConflict (assignments do). Two concurrent persist_discovered calls for the same (tenant,collection) both count 0 under READ COMMITTED, both insert the same deduped root label, second gets 23505 -> sendTypedDbError class-23 -> 409 (TaxonomyHandler.java:191). Handler+guard+index byte-identical v0.1.14..develop (skew ruled out). Trigger vector: two service clients discovering concurrently (overlapping nx invocation or the live MCP server issuing discovery during nx index postproc). persistRebuildTopics (L1600) + persistSplit share the vulnerable shape. Client UX bug on top: http_taxonomy_store._post has no 409 handling -> generic HTTPStatusError -> misleading 'retry' hint (retry against settled state actually SUCCEEDS-as-skip via the guard, so the hint is wrong only for the race window).

title: get-all-metadata 404 fails open to empty staleness cache instead of documented per-file fallback
description:
Observed on a work-instance nx index run against a local nx-service (path
/Users/hhildebrand/, engine served on http://127.0.0.1:54963). build_staleness_cache
hit HTTP 404 on POST /v1/vectors/get-all-metadata:

  event='build_staleness_cache_paginated_get_failed' ... exception='...
  urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404: Not Found ...
  nexus.db.http_vector_client.VectorServiceError: POST /v1/vectors/get-all-metadata -> HTTP 404: not found'
  [post] Staleness caches built - code: 0 docs, docs: 0 docs, rdr: 0 docs (0.0s)

get-all-metadata was added in engine-service-v0.1.30 (CHANGELOG 6.3.5) specifically
to collapse the paginated staleness-cache build from ~110s to ~9s on a 1,700-file
repo. The 404 means that instance's local engine-service predates v0.1.30.

The bug: the client's failure path doesn't match the documented behavior.
CHANGELOG 6.3.5 says "older engines fall back to the previous per-file behavior"
- but the observed behavior is a warning followed by an EMPTY cache (0 docs
across code/docs/rdr), not a per-file fallback. An empty staleness cache means
every file in the next `nx index repo` run is treated as new/changed, i.e. every
run on that instance silently becomes a full re-embed until the engine is
upgraded to >= v0.1.30 - no error surfaces to the operator beyond a warning-level
log line buried in index output.

Root cause to confirm: src/nexus/indexer_utils.py build_staleness_cache /
_get_all_metadata, and nexus/db/http_vector_client.py get_all_metadata - check
whether there's supposed to be a per-collection paginated-get fallback on 404
that never fires, or whether that fallback path was removed/never implemented
when get-all-metadata shipped in 6.3.5.

Fix should either: (a) implement the actual per-file/paginated fallback so a
pre-0.1.30 engine still gets correct staleness results, or (b) if that fallback
is deliberately not worth maintaining, at minimum surface this as a loud
WARN/ERROR to the operator (not just a structlog warning line) recommending
an engine upgrade, since silent full-re-embed has real Voyage cost implications.
close_reason: Duplicate of nexus-441p5 (same finding filed independently from both instances today, 2026-07-07). Fix is in flight on 441p5: fast path gets its own try; on failure WARN (404 => engine-upgrade hint) and fall back to the paginated sweep; empty cache only when BOTH paths fail. Test test_build_falls_back_to_paginated_when_get_all_metadata_fails rewritten to assert the documented contract (it previously locked in the empty-cache regression).

title: Undefended interaction: data-scoped (and tenant/root) bearers can mint uncapped-TTL session tokens via /v1/sessions/start
description:
Gate-B critique (nexus-x1h07 Phase 4-5). SessionTokenHandler.handleStart (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/SessionTokenHandler.java) has NO TTL ceiling at all -- ttl_seconds from the body is accepted verbatim (only <=0 is rejected), unlike DataTokenHandler's new env-tunable, no-silent-clamp ceiling. SessionTokenHandler also has no scope check whatsoever, and AuthFilter's new mint-path restriction only confines scope=mint; a scope=data bearer (the new short-TTL, one-tenant, revocable-via-its-mint-credential credential class this feature exists to create) passes straight through to /v1/sessions/start same as a plain tenant token.

Net effect: a data token -- capped at <=3600s by design -- can, before it expires, request an attacker-chosen (effectively unbounded) TTL session_tokens row for its own tenant. This does NOT escalate privilege in the way it first appears: a session token cannot be presented alone as the primary Authorization bearer (it lives in a separate session_tokens table, checked only via the secondary X-Nexus-T1-Session header, and always requires an independently-valid primary bearer for the same tenant on every request -- confirmed by reading AuthFilter's Decision 1 vs Decision 2 resolution order). So this is NOT the "credential outlives its own revocation" hole it might look like at first glance.

What IS real: (a) an unboundedly-long-lived session-tenant binding row persists in session_tokens indefinitely (DB bloat / no natural cleanup beyond explicit /v1/sessions/close), untouched by revoking the mint credential; (b) this is a pre-existing gap in SessionTokenHandler (not introduced by this diff) that the nexus-868dq/x1h07 design and plan never mention when reasoning about "full data-path authority for its tenant" (design item 6) -- no test in DataTokenHandlerTest or elsewhere exercises a data token calling /v1/sessions/start; (c) it creates a TTL-discipline asymmetry: one new route enforces a careful env-tunable ceiling with explicit no-clamp semantics, an adjacent route reachable by the same new restricted credential class has none.

This is exactly the class of "undefended interaction" that should go through the bus (conexus RDR-005) rather than being accepted by omission, per the project's own "any deviation goes through the bus BEFORE code lands" discipline for this arc. Recommend: either apply the same ttl_seconds ceiling policy to SessionTokenHandler generally, or explicitly decide (and document) that scope=data bearers are out of scope for /v1/sessions/start and enforce it, or explicitly accept the current behavior in writing.

Found during: substantive-critic Gate-B review of nexus-x1h07 Phases 4-5.
close_reason: conexus ACK received 2026-07-07 ([20416]): the shipped conservative default (data-scoped bearers' /v1/sessions/start defaults to the data ceiling, 400 above it) is ACCEPTED as-is. Their EdgeProxyHandler never calls /v1/sessions/start — the JIT data-token flow uses the mint credential directly as the upstream bearer, so the default is never exercised on their side. No engine change needed. Last open residual of the RDR-005 A1 arc (868dq/x1h07): the arc is now residual-free end to end.

title: Extract owns_process short-circuit into shared daemon-lifecycle primitive (GH #1369 follow-up)
description:
GH #1369 fixed a real bug (storage_service + T3 supervisors exiting non-zero on a
healthy 'already running' short-circuit, causing launchd/systemd respawn loops +
port churn) by adding an `owns_process` property + an early-exit-0 check
independently to BOTH src/nexus/daemon/storage_service_daemon.py and
src/nexus/daemon/t3_daemon.py.

This is functionally correct (verified: 87 passed / 1 skipped across the touched
daemon test files) but violates the standing gate in src/nexus/daemon/AGENTS.md:
"Any future lifecycle fix lands in the shared primitive (service_registry.py)
plus the cross-tier conformance suite (test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py) —
NEVER in one tier's copy." Both StorageServiceSupervisor and T3Supervisor already
compose the shared ServiceSupervisor primitive (service_registry.py); the
owns_process concept (and the standard "start(); if not owns_process: log+stop+
exit 0; else heartbeat loop" skeleton) should be factored into that primitive
(or a small shared mixin/base) instead of hand-duplicated a second time.

Also: tests/daemon/test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py's EXPECTATIONS matrix
(which already tracks "storage_service" as a first-class tier alongside t1/t2/t3/
aspect_worker) was NOT updated with a property for this behavior, despite
RDR-175's own frontmatter related_tests field naming that file. Add a property
(e.g. "unowned_no_heartbeat_exit_zero") asserted pass for storage_service + t3,
with a documented GAP/SPEC cell for t1 (MCP-lifespan-owned, N/A) and t2 (uses a
different spawn-lock+poll-for-winner mechanism, already correct via
T2SpawnLockLost handling — worth a cross-reference note, not a copy of this
exact shape) and aspect_worker (no discover-first short-circuit branch exists;
confirm N/A).

Consider also whether tests/daemon/test_lifecycle_gate.py needs a structural
rule (parallel to test_lease_record_defined_only_in_primitive) that fails CI if
an 'owns_process'-shaped property is defined in more than one tier consumer
file without a shared source.

Non-blocking: GH #1369 itself is fine to close as-is (fix is correct + tested);
this is the deferred shared-primitive-extraction + conformance-suite follow-up.
close_reason: Extracted exit_if_process_unowned + SupervisedResource Protocol into src/nexus/daemon/service_registry.py; both storage_service_daemon.py and t3_daemon.py now call the shared helper instead of hand-duplicating the owns_process short-circuit skeleton. Added mechanical lifecycle-gate tests (test_lifecycle_gate.py): exit_if_process_unowned defined only in the primitive, every owns_process consumer calls it, allowlist non-vacuous. Also closed the test-asymmetry gap: added test_not_owning_process_never_calls_heartbeat_once to test_t3_supervisor.py mirroring storage's precise heartbeat_calls==0 pin. Full suite green: 12306 passed. Deferred the EXPECTATIONS-matrix integration in test_rdr149_lifecycle_conformance.py (harness abstraction there models lease records, not process ownership -- would need real design work, not a quick property add); the mechanical gate tests in test_lifecycle_gate.py cover the same drift-prevention intent more proportionately for this specific bug shape.

title: Batch aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook across the 8 fire_document call sites (mirrors register_many/update_many/delete_many/get_all_metadata pattern)
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Found during nexus-duoak's staleness-cache/chunk-batching shakeout, 2026-07-06. The chunk-batching 'file-grain' hook time (34.7s of a ~628s pipeline in this repo's own shakeout) is dominated by aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook's per-document T2 queue INSERT (~250 real inserts for RDR/docs/knowledge files; code files early-return no-op via select_config()==None). manifest_write_batch_hook/taxonomy_assign_batch_hook/chash_dual_write_batch_hook were ALL already promoted to flush-grain (nexus-u2kwq) -- this is the one remaining per-file round trip in the hot indexing path.

Same architectural fix as register_many/update_many/delete_many (catalog) and get_all_metadata (vectors) this session: add HttpAspectQueue.enqueue_many() (Java repo method + endpoint, Python client), mirroring the exact established pattern.

NOT a same-session bolt-on though -- unlike those fixes (each touched exactly ONE call site), aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook is fired via HookRegistry.fire_document() from 8 DISTINCT call sites: code_indexer.py:537, prose_indexer.py:292, doc_indexer.py:844/1501/1566, pipeline_stages.py:858, indexer.py:1868/2938 (the bulk-index closure this shakeout profiled), PLUS mcp/core.py:2123 (MCP store_put -- single-document, must stay non-batched, must NOT be touched).

Design needs to answer:
1. Which of the 8 call sites represent the SAME logical bulk-index run (candidates for batching) vs standalone single-doc calls (store_put) that must be left alone.
2. How the flush-grain aggregation (already proven for manifest/taxonomy/chash in indexer.py's _fire_flush_grain_hooks, keyed on _file_contexts) generalizes to the OTHER per-file-type indexer modules (code_indexer/prose_indexer/doc_indexer/pipeline_stages) if they're in scope -- do they have an equivalent flush/batch boundary, or only indexer.py's ChunkBatcher does?
3. aspect_extraction_enqueue_hook's documented content-sourcing contract (MCP store_put passes full content; CLI passes empty + falls back to disk read) must survive batching -- easy to accidentally break across 4+ modified call sites.
4. select_config(collection) is None gating (code__ collections skip entirely) must still short-circuit BEFORE accumulating a row, not after (avoid enqueueing dead rows).

Instrumentation added this session (indexer.py's _hook_seconds now splits file-grain into file_batch/file_single/file_document sub-timers, surfaced in the 'Chunk batching:' phase line) -- use it to re-measure the actual win once implemented.
