title: Structured logging on the ~22 read-path MCP Error:{e} returns + fix chunking.py:172 printf-in-structlog bug
description: F7. MCP read-path tools (mcp/core.py search/query/collection_list/store_get) end 'except Exception as e: return f"Error: {e}"' with no server-side log — a dead service yields the agent a raw ConnectionRefusedError repr, nothing logged (~22 sites in mcp/). Separately, chunking.py:172 _log.warning('Semantic chunking failed (%s); ...', exc) uses printf interpolation which structlog does NOT apply, so exc is dropped from the rendered event. FIX: add structlog calls + actionable remediation to the read-path error returns; convert the chunking.py:172 %s to a structured field.
notes:
## F7. Structured logging on MCP read-path error returns + fix the printf-in-structlog bug

### What's wrong
Two distinct defects, both swallowing diagnostic information:

1. **Silent read-path error returns (~22 sites in `src/nexus/mcp/core.py`).** MCP tool handlers end with `except Exception as e: return f"Error: {e}"` and emit **no server-side log**. When the backing service is dead, the agent receives a raw `ConnectionRefusedError` repr with zero actionable remediation, and nothing is recorded server-side for diagnosis. Confirmed 22 occurrences at lines: 987, 1139, 1209, 1308, 1843, 1988, 2045, 2228, 2297, 2404, 2464, 2487, 2526, 2631, 2749, 2788, 2807, 2864, 2907, 2930, 2970, 2998. The bead names the read-path tools specifically (`search`/`query`/`collection_list`/`store_get`) — these are the priority sites; the remaining handlers in the same file share the identical anti-pattern and should be converted in the same pass for consistency.

2. **printf-in-structlog bug — `src/nexus/md_chunker.py:172`** (the bead's "chunking.py:172" is a misnomer; there is no `chunking.py` — the file is `md_chunker.py`):
   ```python
   _log.warning("Semantic chunking failed (%s); falling back to naive.", exc)
   ```
   structlog does **not** apply printf `%s` interpolation, so `exc` is dropped from the rendered event entirely — the warning fires but never shows what failed. Convert to a structured field:
   ```python
   _log.warning("semantic_chunking_failed_fallback_naive", error=str(exc), exc_info=exc)
   ```

### Approach
- **md_chunker.py:172** — single-line fix. Module already has `_log = structlog.get_logger()` (line 14). Replace the `%s` interpolation with a structured `error=` field (and optionally `exc_info=exc` for the traceback). This is the cheap, isolated win — do it first.
- **mcp/core.py error returns** — `core.py` already has module-level `_log = structlog.get_logger()` available (multiple named loggers exist in-file, e.g. line 108 `_hb_log`). For each read-path handler, before `return`, add a structured log of the exception (`_log.error("mcp_<tool>_failed", error=str(e), exc_info=e)` or similar event-name-per-tool), and enrich the returned string with **actionable remediation** rather than a bare repr — e.g. detect connection failures and return guidance like "T3 service unreachable — is the daemon running? Try `nx doctor`." Keep the return-a-string contract (these are MCP tool returns, not raises).
- Match the existing structured-logging idiom in the file: event name as the first positional string (snake_case), context as kwargs. **Never** reintroduce `%s`/`.format`/f-string interpolation into the log message itself.

### Constraints / gotchas
- **Structured logging only** (project rule): `_log.event("event_name", **fields)`. The `%s` form is exactly the bug being fixed — do not propagate it.
- These `core.py` returns are MCP **tool return values** (strings handed back to the agent), not exceptions to re-raise. Preserve that — log *and* return.
- Don't leak full tracebacks into the agent-facing return string; put `exc_info` in the log, put a concise remediation hint in the return.
- TDD: assert the logger is called on the error path (capture via structlog's testing capture / a caplog-style fixture) and assert the returned string contains the remediation hint. For md_chunker, assert the rendered event carries the error field (non-vacuous: check the value, not just that a warning fired).

title: Commit a [tool.ruff] config enforcing event-name-snake-case, no-print-in-library, audited BLE001
description: F7. No committed ruff config (zero [tool.ruff], no .ruff.toml), yet 73 noqa:BLE001 + 284 noqa:PLC0415 are version-controlled but unenforced in-tree — the structlog-only/no-print discipline holds only by convention. FIX: commit a [tool.ruff] ruleset (snake_case event names, no print() in library code, audited broad-except), wire into CI. Surfaces (and gates) the print()s in pdf_extractor.py:85, plans/loader.py:312/314, catalog_taxonomy.py:2243, migrations.py:2268-2329, t2/__init__.py:643.
notes:
## Commit a `[tool.ruff]` config enforcing the structlog-only / no-print discipline (epic nexus-whh61, F7)

### Verified state of the world (branch `feature/arch-docs-staleness`)
- **No ruff config anywhere**: zero `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml`, no `.ruff.toml`/`ruff.toml`. Confirmed.
- **ruff is not even a dev dependency** — `[dependency-groups].dev` (pyproject.toml:192–198) lists only pytest/pytest-asyncio/pytest-cov/syrupy/twine. Adding the config requires also adding `ruff` to the dev group so CI can run it.
- **noqa codes are real and version-controlled but inert**: 73 `# noqa: BLE001` (broad-except) and 284 `# noqa: PLC0415` (import-not-at-top) across `src/`. Without a committed ruleset these are dead annotations — they suppress nothing because nothing enforces them.
- **CI has no lint job**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only pytest (matrix 3.12/3.13). No ruff/flake8/pylint step exists anywhere under `.github/`. Wiring means adding a job (or step) to ci.yml.

### print() inventory (re-verify before gating — most are intentional stderr)
The bead's cited lines are accurate but note the path correction and intent:
- `src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py:85` — `print(msg, file=sys.stderr)`, **already deliberately gated** behind `NEXUS_PDF_PROGRESS_QUIET` with a docstring (lines 75–85) explaining it replaced a no-print violation. A `T20`/print rule will flag it; it needs a justified per-line `# noqa: T201` or routing through a sanctioned helper, not deletion.
- `src/nexus/plans/loader.py:312,314` — schema-validation errors to stderr.
- **`src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py:2243`** (bead said `catalog_taxonomy.py:2243` — actual path is `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py`), `print(f"  {msg}", file=sys.stderr)`.
- `src/nexus/db/migrations.py:2268,2298,2308,2312,2315` — migration progress to stderr.
- `src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py:643` — print to stderr.

**Key nuance for the implementer:** nearly all of these are `file=sys.stderr` progress/diagnostic output, not stray debug prints. The project rule (CLAUDE.md "Hot rules") is *no `print()` in library code; CLI commands use `click.echo()`*. So the ruff adoption must decide per-site: convert library-internal progress to `structlog` (pdf_extractor already shows the pattern: `_log.info(...)` + gated stderr), or move user-facing CLI output to `click.echo()`. Do not blanket-noqa all of them — that recreates the "unenforced by convention" problem the bead is fixing.

### Suggested ruff ruleset (calibrate to existing noqa codes so the tree stays green)
- **Event-name snake_case**: ruff has no built-in structlog event-name rule. Options: (a) `flake8-logging` (`LOG`) rules for logging hygiene, or (b) a custom check — but ruff cannot assert "first positional arg to `_log.info` is snake_case". This sub-goal likely needs `flake8-logging-format`/`LOG` rules plus a targeted test, OR explicit scope-narrowing in the bead. **Flag to user**: the literal "event-name-snake-case" enforcement may not be expressible as a stock ruff rule; confirm scope.
- **No print in library**: `flake8-print` → rule code `T20` (`T201` print, `T203` pprint). Select `T20`, then exempt CLI command modules (`src/nexus/commands/**`) via `[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]` since those legitimately use click.echo but may have prints.
- **Audited broad-except**: `BLE001` (flake8-blind-except). Enabling it makes the 73 existing `# noqa: BLE001` live and required — good. New broad excepts then fail CI unless audited+annotated.
- `PLC0415` (import-outside-top-level) is already noqa'd 284×; enabling pylint convention `PLC` (or just leaving these as accepted) keeps them green. Decide whether to enforce or `ignore` PLC0415 globally given the 284 deliberate lazy-imports.

### Adoption sequence (avoid a red CI on commit)
1. Add `ruff` to `[dependency-groups].dev`; refresh `uv.lock` (`uv sync`).
2. Add `[tool.ruff]` / `[tool.ruff.lint]` with `select = [...]` for the chosen codes; add `per-file-ignores` for CLI modules.
3. Run `uv run ruff check src/` — triage each new finding: convert print→structlog/click.echo, or add justified `# noqa: <code> — reason`.
4. Add a `ruff` step/job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (mirror the pytest job's `uv sync --group dev` setup) so it gates PRs to develop/main.
5. **PR targets `develop`, not main** (project rule).

title: chash_index.dual_write silently drops routing rows on WAL-busy (catches Exception, warns, never re-raises)
description: F4. chash_index.py:428-436 dual_write catches Exception, logs a warning, never re-raises; upsert_many (:169-209) is all-or-nothing, so one WAL-busy failure drops a whole source's chash routing rows, later forcing the catalog_spans.py fallback_chash_scan over every T3 collection. FIX: decide a re-raise/retry policy (route through the daemon retry like other writes) so routing rows aren't silently lost on contention.
notes:
## F4: `chash_index` dual-write silently drops routing rows on WAL-busy

### Problem
`dual_write_chash_index` (`src/nexus/db/t2/chash_index.py:380-436`) is best-effort: it wraps the `upsert_many` call in a `try/except Exception` that logs `chash_index_dual_write_failed` at **warning** level and never re-raises (`:428-436`). Because `ChashIndex.upsert_many` (`:169-209`) is intentionally **all-or-nothing** (one `executemany` + `commit`, full rollback on failure), a single `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked/busy` drops a whole source's chash routing rows. The cost surfaces later: `Catalog.resolve_chash` finds no live row and `catalog_spans.fallback_chash_scan` (`src/nexus/catalog/catalog_spans.py:124`) runs a 30-second-bounded **parallel scan over every T3 collection** to recover the span. The docstring frames missing rows as "a performance hit, not a correctness hit" — that is the assumption to revisit.

### Important: partial mitigation already exists (don't duplicate it)
The **batch-hook caller path is already hardened**. `chash_dual_write_batch_hook` (`src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:872-915`) routes the write through `t2_index_write` (`:315`) so the daemon (`T2Client`) holds memory.db's single WAL-writer slot instead of the indexer, and on a `locked`/`busy` failure it calls `nexus.dropped_writes.record_drop(...)` (`:902-914`) so the drop becomes a metered number `nx doctor` surfaces (RDR-129 Gap 4 / nexus-uq8a4). So the indexing hot path is *daemon-routed + metered* today.

### Where the gap actually remains
1. **The inner helper still swallows.** Even with daemon routing, the `except Exception` in `dual_write_chash_index` (`:430`) catches *inside* `write_fn`, so the daemon path's outer `locked/busy` detection in `mcp_infra` only fires because `t2_index_write` probes reachability up-front (see its docstring `:336-345`) — NOT because the inner helper surfaced anything. Any non-reachability WAL-busy (daemon is up but the batch still hits `busy`) is swallowed by `:430` and never reaches `record_drop`.
2. **The `collection.py` backfill caller is NOT routed or metered.** `backfill_chunk_text_hash` calls `dual_write_chash_index(chash_index, coll_name, t2_ids, t2_metas)` directly (`src/nexus/commands/collection.py:744`) — no `t2_index_write`, no `record_drop`. A WAL-busy here is a pure silent drop, exactly the failure mode F4 describes.

### Fix direction
Decide a re-raise/retry policy consistent with the RDR-128/129 single-writer model (sibling bead nexus-1krqx — single-writer fail-loud / daemon-retry). Options to weigh:
- Add a bounded inner retry (matching the `sqlite3.OperationalError` backoff pattern in `src/nexus/db/t2/memory_etl.py:123,172`) inside `upsert_many` or the helper, so transient WAL contention self-heals rather than dropping.
- Distinguish lock/busy failures from other exceptions in `dual_write_chash_index` and route lock/busy through `record_drop` from the helper itself (so *every* caller is metered, not just the batch hook), or re-raise so the caller decides.
- Route the `collection.py:744` backfill caller through `t2_index_write` so it inherits daemon routing + metering parity with the indexing hook.

Keep the helper's "never abort a successful T3 write" contract (`:399-404`) — the goal is no *silent* loss, not making T3 writes fail on T2 contention.

title: nx doctor: attribute the WAL writer-lock holder and aspect-worker-owning MCP PID
description: F4 (operability). doctor.py aspect-queue check reports depth/status/oldest but enumerates no MCP PID, no worker-thread owner, no WAL-lock holder — so an operator hitting the known orphan-MCP WAL-contention problem has no signal to find the culprit. FIX: add a doctor check that attributes the SQLite WAL writer-lock holder / aspect-worker-owning MCP PID.
notes:
## nx doctor: attribute the WAL writer-lock holder + aspect-worker-owning MCP PID

**Goal (F4 operability):** When an operator hits the known orphan-MCP WAL-contention problem (`database is locked` from stale aspect-workers in long-lived/orphan nx-mcp processes contending on the T2 SQLite WAL), `nx doctor` currently gives no signal to find the culprit. Add a doctor check that *attributes* the contention: enumerate the live aspect-worker-owning MCP PIDs and identify the WAL writer-lock holder, so the operator can `kill -9` the orphan rather than guess.

### Where the signal already lives
The attribution data is **already on disk** — this is wiring, not new infrastructure:

- **Worker-PID advertisement:** Each nx-mcp that starts an `AspectExtractionWorker` writes a lock file `<nexus_config_dir>/locks/aspect_worker.<pid>` (`aspect_worker._write_worker_lock`, `_worker_lock_path`, `src/nexus/aspect_worker.py:560-628`). The PID suffix *is* the owning MCP PID. `_sweep_dead_worker_locks` (line 576) already demonstrates the liveness-check idiom: parse the PID from the filename, `os.kill(pid, 0)` → alive/`ProcessLookupError`=dead/`PermissionError`=alive-other-user. Reuse this exact pattern to enumerate **live** worker-owning PIDs.
- **The check to extend:** `_run_check_aspect_queue()` in `src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:603-687`. It already reports depth/per-status/oldest/failed-rows but emits **no PID, no worker-owner, no WAL-lock holder**. Add the attribution output here (or a sibling `_run_*` helper wired the same way), and register a flag mirroring the existing `--check-aspect-queue` plumbing at `doctor.py:1216-1217` (option decl) and `doctor.py:1311-1312` (dispatch in the command body).

### Implementation notes / suggested approach
1. **Enumerate worker-owning MCP PIDs:** glob `<config_dir>/locks/aspect_worker.*`, parse PID, filter to live PIDs via the `os.kill(pid, 0)` idiom (copy semantics from `_sweep_dead_worker_locks`). Report each live PID; flag dead-but-present lock files as stale leftovers (these correlate with crashed/`-9`'d orphans). More than one live worker PID = the multi-worker contention condition itself — surface it explicitly.
2. **Attribute the WAL writer-lock holder:** SQLite does not expose the WAL writer-lock holder via SQL. Attribute it by finding which live processes hold the T2 db file open. Options, in order of portability preference: (a) `psutil.Process(pid).open_files()` cross-referenced against `default_db_path()` and its `-wal`/`-shm` siblings (psutil is the cleanest, check it's an available dep first); (b) fall back to `lsof <db>` parsing if psutil is absent. Cross-reference the holder PIDs against the worker-lock PID set so output reads "PID N holds the T2 WAL and owns aspect-worker lock". Keep it **read-only and daemon-offline-safe** — see the `epsilon-allow` comment at `doctor.py:621`; this diagnostic must work when the daemon is down. Never block on the lock.
3. **Output contract:** human-readable `click.echo` lines consistent with the surrounding aspect-queue output (it is a CLI diagnostic, not library code — `click.echo`, never `print`/structured log here). State PID, role (worker-owner / WAL-holder / both), and liveness.

### Domain context
- `aspect_worker` runs *inside* nx-mcp processes with their own SQLite connections; a worker code fix only goes live when the **hosting** nx-mcp restarts (not on daemon restart). Orphan/long-lived MCPs keep stale workers contending — this is the documented WAL-contention root (nexus-aigkb × v4m7y × kg8sj; see memory `project_daemon_restart_not_worker_fix`). Single-writer hardening landed via RDR-128/129 (daemon write-path) but orphan MCPs predating/bypassing the daemon are exactly what this check makes visible.
- Parent epic `nexus-whh61` (synthetic-aperture remediation) — observability/process-debt bucket.
close_reason: Obsoleted by RDR-152 T2→Postgres migration. The WAL writer-lock contention this check attributes is a SQLite-only failure class (orphan nx-mcp aspect-workers fighting memory.db's single-writer slot). Under the Java/PG service backend (NX_STORAGE_BACKEND_MEMORY=service) T2 is MVCC Postgres — no WAL writer lock, the contention cannot occur. The check would only help the legacy local-SQLite path (a substrate on its way out) and would mislead on PG-backed deployments. Owner decision 2026-06-23: drop, ship yttqr alone. yttqr (backend-agnostic logging fixes) shipped separately.

title: Remove cargo-cult ChromaDB-quota comments/validators on the pgvector write path; document server-enforced dedup
description: F1 residue (Low->tracked P2). After the Java audit, the 300-record/16384-byte 'quotas' are ChromaDB-Cloud limits inapplicable to Postgres; server dedups in PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal. http_vector_client.py:1015-1021 update_chunks batches 'to match the service quota' that the live backend does not have, while upsert_chunks (:512-550) does not batch — confusing asymmetry. FIX: remove/relabel the cargo-cult quota comments on the service path, document that dedup+conflict-merge is server-enforced, keep chroma_quotas.py scoped to the retired Chroma migration source only.
notes:
## What & why

Remove cargo-cult ChromaDB-Cloud quota comments/`QUOTAS` references on the **pgvector (service) write path** and document that dedup + conflict-merge is **server-enforced**. The 300-record / 16384-byte "quotas" are ChromaDB-Cloud free-tier limits (`src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py`, RDR-005, sourced from `docs.trychroma.com/cloud/quotas-limits`). They are inapplicable to the Postgres/pgvector backend that the service now uses. `chroma_quotas.py` must stay scoped ONLY to the retired Chroma migration source.

## Ground truth from the code

**Server already dedups + merges (no client batching needed for correctness).** `PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal` (`service/src/main/java/.../vectors/PgVectorRepository.java:268`) does first-wins in-batch dedup (`seen` HashSet, lines 287–314, emits `event=upsert_dedup_collapsed`) and cross-batch `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` merge of `chunk_text`/`embedding`/`metadata` (documented lines 204–206). There is NO 300-record or 16KB-byte limit on the PG path. Javadoc at lines 200–216 is the authoritative contract; contract suite `PgVectorRepositoryContractTest.java:384` ("Contract 3: upsert semantics — stored vector, first-wins dedup, in-place") pins it.

**The confusing asymmetry (the actual defect to fix):**
- `update_chunks` (`http_vector_client.py:1000`) batches at `QUOTAS.MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE` (300) with comment "to match the service's quota validator" — the live PG backend has no such validator. (`http_vector_client.py:1015-1021`)
- `upsert_chunks` (`http_vector_client.py:~480-550`) sends ALL ids in a single `_post("/v1/vectors/upsert-chunks", ...)` with no batching (lines 532-545). So the two metadata/vector write paths to the same service disagree on whether a 300-cap exists.

**Other service-path `QUOTAS` references to evaluate (don't blanket-delete — some are legitimate pagination):**
- `http_vector_client.py:1112-1114` (`page_limit`) and `1165-1172` (delete batch) — these guard the service's own GET/DELETE paging, not a Chroma write quota; relabel rather than remove if the service endpoints genuinely paginate.
- `exporter.py:211,372` (`page_size = QUOTAS.MAX_RECORDS_PER_WRITE`) — export read-paging; assess separately, likely out of scope (export still reads from Chroma migration source).

## Suggested fix shape

1. In `update_chunks` (1006-1017): drop/relabel the "to match the service's quota validator" comment. If 300-batching is kept purely as a request-size pragmatic chunking (not a quota), say so explicitly; otherwise remove the loop to match `upsert_chunks`' single-POST shape and kill the asymmetry. Decide ONE convention for both methods.
2. Add a short docstring note on the service write path that dedup + conflict-merge is **server-enforced in `PgVectorRepository.upsertChunksInternal`** — clients need not pre-dedup or quota-check.
3. Leave `chroma_quotas.py` unchanged but verify its module docstring scopes it to the retired Chroma migration source only (currently says "Single source of truth for all ChromaDB Cloud limits" — narrow that wording).
4. Coordinate with related bead **nexus-h29w1** (CI gate asserting server-side dedup/quota against `HttpVectorClient`) — that gate is what prevents the cargo-cult from creeping back.

This is F1 residue, Low→tracked P2, parent epic nexus-whh61 (synthetic-aperture remediation). Pure comment/doc cleanup + possible removal of a no-op batching loop; no behavioral change to the wire protocol intended.

## Key files

- `src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py`
- `src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py`
- `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/PgVectorRepository.java`
- `src/nexus/exporter.py`
- `tests/test_http_vector_client.py`
- `tests/test_http_vector_client_parity.py`
- `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/PgVectorRepositoryContractTest.java`

title: RDR-166: same-model vector passthrough — skip the Voyage re-embed when source_model == target_model
description: A same-model managed migration (e.g. voyage-context-3 -> voyage-context-3) currently RE-EMBEDS every chunk server-side and bills the operator's Voyage key, even though the stored vectors are already correct and identical. Root cause: Seam B made the JVM service the sole embedding authority (embed-on-write) to prevent cross-model contamination (RDR-109), but it overshoots — there is NO vector-supplied ingestion path. The only endpoint is /v1/vectors/upsert-chunks (embeds server-side); upsert_chunks_with_embeddings is a deliberate no-op wrapper that discards caller embeddings (http_vector_client.py:523); iter_collection_chunks deliberately does not fetch source vectors (chroma_read.py:115). Re-embed is REQUIRED for the cross-model case (minilm->voyage) but pure waste for same-model. Fix: a vector-PASSTHROUGH path that copies stored vectors when source_model == target_model, making the migration genuinely $0 instead of merely cost-confirmed. Needs: (1) a service endpoint that accepts precomputed vectors; (2) the read leg to fetch vectors in the same-model case; (3) a model-VERSION guard so passthrough only fires when the embedder is provably identical (handles the RDR-109 contamination concern with a guard, not a blanket re-embed). Interim mitigation = the nexus-cewad cost guardrail (warn+confirm), which stays useful for the unavoidable cross-model case. Spans nexus client + Java engine-service (cross-repo) — coordinate with conexus. Surfaced by Hal during cewad review 2026-06-22: 'why? there is no need to re-embed.'
design: Passthrough fires iff source collection's embedding model == target service's wired model for that collection AND the model version/provider is pinned-identical. Otherwise fall through to the existing server-side re-embed (cross-model or version-skew). Update build_dry_run_preview billed_voyage_tokens to EXCLUDE same-model groups once passthrough lands (they become free) — today they are correctly counted as billed because the re-embed is real.

title: inline-provisioned storage supervisor lease can stall after first publish (15s TTL) — lease-discovery consumers race expiry
description: Secondary finding from nexus-qvemn debug (T2 nexus/qvemn-debug-2026-06-22) + qvemn substantive-critic Sig-2. The inline-provisioned (--foreground/detached) storage supervisor published its lease ONCE at t=0 (event=storage_service_lease_published) and emitted NO further heartbeat events in the following ~19s window; the lease (storage_service TTL=15s, service_registry.py:77) aged out and discover() reaped it, returning (None,None). nexus-qvemn worked around this for guided-upgrade by pinning NX_SERVICE_HOST/PORT into env so the migration legs bypass lease discovery — but ANY OTHER consumer that relies on lease discovery after ~15s against a freshly inline-provisioned supervisor still races the same expiry (e.g. standalone nx migrate-to-service with inline provision, a long-running MCP worker, HttpVectorClient lease fallback). Same bug CLASS as nexus-qke1e (already fixed once → recurrence). Why the heartbeat stalled is undetermined from the log alone (debugger's 0.25 uncertainty).
design: Determine why the detached inline supervisor does not re-stamp its lease post-publish. Candidate areas: src/nexus/daemon/storage_service_daemon.py heartbeat/re-stamp loop, the --foreground/detached spawn path, service_registry.py TTL vs re-stamp interval. Either (a) ensure the inline supervisor re-stamps within < TTL, or (b) gate establish_verified_service readiness on a discover() poll (not just /health) so a non-discoverable lease fails fast. Add a controlled test asserting a detached inline supervisor re-stamps its lease within ~10s of publish.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of the post-publish heartbeat stall identified; inline supervisor keeps its lease fresh (re-stamp < TTL) OR readiness gates on discoverability; regression test for lease freshness after inline provision. Cross-ref nexus-qke1e.
close_reason: Closed

title: guided-upgrade hardcodes cross-model remap target to bge-768 regardless of embedding mode (mixed local-legacy → voyage-mode migrant blocked)
description: Surfaced by the migration-rehearsal --guided --with-cloud shakeout 2026-06-22. driver.py:181 builds the cross-model target map as cross_model_target_name(c.collection, _ONNX_MODEL) where _ONNX_MODEL='bge-base-en-v15-768' (detection.py:59) — unconditionally bge-768, with no embedding-mode awareness. Those bge-768 targets are then passed to BOTH legs incl. migrate_cloud (driver _run_leg 'cloud'). Consequence: a deployment in voyage (cloud) mode that has legacy minilm-l6-v2-384 collections to cross-model-remap cannot migrate them — the service's pebfx.2 fail-loud guard correctly refuses with HTTP 422 'embedding mode voyage has no embedder for model bge-base-en-v15-768', migration BLOCKED 0/N, sentinel migrated-failed, reads degraded-LOUD. Pure-cloud users (voyage-context-3 collections, byte-for-byte migrate) are unaffected; pure-local users (bge-768 target, ONNX mode) are unaffected. The exposed scenario is the MIXED migrant: ran local (minilm-384) then migrates onto a voyage-mode service — target should derive voyage-context-3, not bge-768. NOTE: the fail-loud guard behaved correctly (no silent wrong-model vectors). NOTE: the harness also should reject --guided + --with-cloud (incoherent: --guided seeds local-ONNX targets) the way it rejects --cold + --guided.
design: Make the cross-model remap target embedding-mode-aware: in voyage mode derive voyage-context-3 (the cloud target), in local mode derive bge-768. Decide product scope first: is the mixed local→cloud-mode migrant in scope for release N, or explicitly unsupported (block with a clear diagnostic)? If unsupported, the fix is a loud pre-gate refusal in the driver, not silent. Also add a run.sh guard rejecting --guided + --with-cloud.
acceptance_criteria: Driver derives the cross-model target from the live embedding mode (or blocks the mixed scenario with a clear diagnostic). migration-rehearsal exercises the coherent cloud cross-model path (or asserts the documented block). run.sh rejects --guided + --with-cloud.
notes: CLOUD-SCOPE ANSWERED 2026-06-22 (conexus STEP-6 reply [4461], v0.1.7 test-deploy): NOT a cloud release-N blocker. RLS-aware per-tenant probe of api.conexus-nexus.com: real tenant 'nexus'=0 vectors (pre-cutover); gate corpus=116,489 voyage-context-3 + ONE chunks_384 row which is a seam TEST FIXTURE (knowledge__seam-b-test__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1). title: Rename REST endpoint: new_name collision silently triggers RDR-162 cross-model COPY branch (needs cross_model caller signal / 409)
description: substantive-critic Significant on PR #1281 (nexus-hz785). CatalogRepository.renameCollection has a targetExists branch (RDR-162 cross-model COPY): when new_name is already a registered collection it repoints catalog_documents.physical_collection ONLY, leaves both registry rows, and returns a map with just the catalog_documents key — chunks/taxonomy/aspects are NOT moved. This is intentional for the bge-768 cross-model migrate path. BUT the service has no caller signal distinguishing intentional cross-model COPY from an accidental new_name collision: a direct REST / HttpCatalogClient caller that mistypes (or reuses) new_name gets a 200 with a suspiciously short response and a silent PARTIAL rename. Guarded today ONLY by the Python shim collection_rename.py:71-74 (collection_exists(new) -> ClickException); any non-shim caller bypasses it.
design: Cannot simply 409 on collectionExists(new_name) — that breaks the legitimate RDR-162 cross-model branch (CatalogRenameCollectionTest @Order 50). Add an explicit caller signal: handleCollectionRename reads a 'cross_model: true' body flag (default false). If new_name exists AND !cross_model -> 409 Conflict 'target collection already exists'. If cross_model -> current RDR-162 repoint branch. Thread the flag through HttpCatalogClient.rename_collection_cascade so the bge-768 migrate path sets it; the Python shim's existing guard becomes the default-false behavior server-side. Add CatalogHandlerRenameTest cases: 409 on plain collision, 200 repoint on cross_model=true.
acceptance_criteria: Plain rename to an existing new_name -> 409 (not silent 200 partial). cross_model=true preserves the RDR-162 repoint branch (group-12/@Order-50 still green). HttpCatalogClient threads the flag; migrate path sets it. Tests cover both branches from the REST layer.
close_reason: 409 collision guard + cross_model flag shipped in PR #1282 (squash to develop); stacked review clean, 4 added tests close the 409-propagation gap

title: Service-mode per-document hard-purge must clean topic_assignments (no fk-001 FK)

title: RDR-164 P1: Collection-registry backfill + FK validation (backfill MUST precede VALIDATE)
description:
Register every referenced collection in catalog_collections (mirror fk-002-0-backfill-stubs), then VALIDATE the five existing NOT VALID ON DELETE RESTRICT FKs (chunks_{384,768,1024}, chash_index, topic_assignments) and ADD ON DELETE RESTRICT FKs to the remaining FK-eligible collection-level tables (document_aspects, aspect_extraction_queue, topics, taxonomy_meta, document_highlights). BACKFILL MUST PRECEDE VALIDATION (CA-2: NOT VALID constraints mean bulk rows are unvalidated; validating before backfill fails on orphans). NO FK on relevance_log/search_telemetry/hook_failures.

BACKFILL POLICY (Q5, register-then-reconcile, fail-loud on ambiguity, RDR-153 migration-data-quality discipline): for each distinct (tenant_id, collection) referenced by a lifecycle table but absent from catalog_collections — (a) maps to live data (chunks/projection exist) -> STUB-REGISTER; (b) genuinely orphaned (no chunks/projection/live collection) -> DELETE rows WITH A LOGGED COUNT (these are the orphans the RDR exists to remove; no silent drop); (c) AMBIGUOUS (renamed/tombstoned name mapping to >1 registry entry) -> FAIL LOUD with a structured migration issue, require operator resolution, NEVER guess.

Liquibase changelog + migration rehearsal (RDR-153). Composite (tenant_id, col) FKs keep cascade tenant-safe. TDD: exact-count assertions on backfill outcomes (stub-registered N, deleted-orphan M, fail-loud on synthetic ambiguous fixture). Local sqlite mode: this is the in-PG FK spine — local path is unaffected by FK adds but its parallel client cascade must still pass the unit suite. JAVA schema -> FULL mvn suite (Java CI advisory). description:

title: Translate range where-operators ($gte/$lte/$gt/$lt) on the RDR-152 vector bridge

Decide text-vs-numeric semantics deliberately; add Testcontainers cases for numeric (year), lexical edge ('9' vs '10'), and non-numeric-metadata rows. Also covers the compound $and/$or deferral from 05bfd if scoped in.

title: Taxonomy assign hook silently no-ops on service-mode PDF ingest (truthiness gap: [[],..] passes 'if not svc_embeddings')
description: SHAKEOUT 2026-06-20 (stacked-review of nexus-9n1u3, critic Sig-3 / code-review L2). Pre-existing, affects BOTH batch (doc_indexer.py:1416 passes [[]]*N) and now streaming (nexus-9n1u3) PDF ingest in service mode. In src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:~693-694 taxonomy_assign_batch_hook does 'svc_embeddings = embeddings; if not svc_embeddings: <re-fetch via get_embeddings>'. When the caller passes [[], [], ...] (server-side-embed placeholder), the OUTER list is non-empty so 'if not svc_embeddings' is FALSE — the re-fetch path is skipped and compute_assignments is called with zero-dimensional vectors (N,0), which hits the dim-mismatch short-circuit at http_taxonomy_store.py:~586 and returns [] -> taxonomy assignment silently produces NOTHING for service-mode PDFs. FIX: change the guard to 'if not any(svc_embeddings):' (inner-emptiness check) so zero-dim placeholders trigger the get_embeddings re-fetch from the service. Add a test calling taxonomy_assign_batch_hook with embeddings=[[],[]] in service mode asserting it re-fetches (or short-circuits cleanly). Related: nexus-gmiaf.21+. Needs confirmation against live service taxonomy.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1269 (fix/service-mode-followups → develop). Stacked review clean, live-verified.

title: catalog_links MCP tool always errors in service mode (singular link_type kwarg + unconditional .to_dict())
description: SHAKEOUT 2026-06-20 (Track A audit #5 Medium + #8 Low). The 'links' MCP tool (nexus-catalog server) always errors in service mode. (#8) lines 443-446 call .to_dict() unconditionally on graph nodes/edges that are plain dicts returned by /traverse in service mode (http_catalog_client.py:930) -> AttributeError once #5 is fixed. NOT covered by nexus-0cy4b (that is the catalog INDEXING ensure_owner_for_repo defect). Residual-risk: verify the live /traverse node/edge JSON shape after this lands. Adversarially verified real.

title: nx scratch raw traceback in service mode (NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service routes CLI T1 to MCP-only HttpScratchStore)
description: SHAKEOUT 2026-06-20 (Track B-2 live finding, Medium). With NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service exported (which nx init --service instructs users to do, init.py:560), storage_backend_for('t1') returns SERVICE (global env overrides T1's SQLite hard-default special-case in storage_mode.py:178). get_t1_database() (src/nexus/db/t1.py:790-793) then returns HttpScratchStore(), whose __init__ calls resolve_service_config() and raises a RAW uncaught RuntimeError traceback ('nexus-service endpoint is not resolvable') on any CLI nx scratch put/list/get. But storage_mode.py:178 itself documents service-T1 as 'MCP-context-only (HttpScratchStore needs a minted session the CLI does not provision)'. So a documented service-mode setup makes nx scratch crash ugly. Compare the DEFAULT (no global flag) path which gives a CLEAN actionable error ('set NX_T1_ISOLATED=1 for ephemeral scratch'). FIX: in get_t1_database() or scratch.py, when service-T1 is selected but no session/endpoint resolves, fall back to the clean NX_T1_ISOLATED guidance (or to local T1) instead of letting HttpScratchStore's raw RuntimeError escape. Repro: NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR=tmp NX_LOCAL=1 NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=service uv run nx scratch put 'x'.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1269 (fix/service-mode-followups → develop). Stacked review clean, live-verified.

title: Service-mode telemetry READ-side parity: nx tier-status + doctor --check-tier-discipline report 0 from local SQLite
description: SHAKEOUT 2026-06-20 (Track A audit #4 Medium + #7 Low). The nexus-pyzk7 fix routed tier_writes/nx_answer_runs WRITES to the service (Postgres), but the READ/diagnostic side still reads local SQLite, so both surfaces silently report zero activity in service mode. (1) src/nexus/commands/tier_status.py:172 — sqlite3.connect(db_path) reads tier_writes from local SQLite (epsilon-allowed 'must operate when daemon offline'); service writes are in PG -> reports 0 writes (silent wrong-result). (2) src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:719 — --check-tier-discipline reads the same local table -> false-clean, never exits non-zero. FIX (one bead): branch the read on storage_backend_for('t2'); add GET /v1/telemetry/tier_writes read endpoint to HttpTelemetryStore (mirrors existing record/import); keep raw-SQLite only for the SQLITE backend. For doctor, when SERVICE + empty local table emit 'service-backed telemetry — local inspection N/A' instead of 'no writes seen'. This is the read-side half of nexus-pyzk7.
close_reason: Bug fixed in PR #1269: nx tier-status + nx doctor now emit honest 'service-backed; local inspection N/A' in service mode (was silently reading empty local SQLite). Full service-side read parity (GET /v1/telemetry/tier_writes) deferred to nexus-59wjj.

description: Surfaced by the 2026-06-20 full CLI live smoke (after the embed-token fix, indexing reached post-processing). indexer.stamp_collection_version calls col.modify(metadata=...) — a Chroma collection method the _ServiceCollectionStub (service-backed T3) does not expose -> AttributeError aborts nx index repo at the 'Stamping pipeline version' post step. title: Service+local mode: nx index names code__ collections with minilm-384 token but the service embeds bge-768 -> 422
description: Surfaced by the 2026-06-20 live CLI smoke (after the catalog owner-upsert gap was fixed, indexing reached vector upsert). In service mode with NX_LOCAL=1, nx init --service records local.embed_model=BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 and the service embeds onnx-local bge-768, but nx index repo builds the collection name with the client's fastembed-tier token 'minilm-l6-v2-384' (e.g. code__corpus-HASH__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1). The service refuses: HTTP 422 'no embedder for model minilm-l6-v2-384 ... Available models: [bge-base-en-v15-768]'. NX_LOCAL_EMBED_MODEL=BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 did NOT change the collection token, so the code-indexer's model-token resolution for service+local collection naming does not honor the recorded/overridden local model -> defaults to minilm-384 (likely because the [local]/fastembed extra is not importable in the dev tree, so _resolve_local_model falls back to tier-0). Fix: in service mode the collection embedding-model token must follow the SERVICE's embedder (query /version embedding_models = bge-768), not the client's fastembed availability. Files: code_indexer.py collection-name/model-token resolution; the local-model resolver; possibly mcp_infra/make_t3 collection naming. Blocks full CLI nx index repo in service+local mode (the 6.0 default). NOTE: taxonomy discover/split/project were verified live by seeding bge-768 vectors directly (nexus-7ydks/9pqoj); this only blocks the CLI index path.
notes: FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-06-20 (PR #1260): effective_embedding_model_for_writes now follows the service embedder (bge-768) in local+service-vector mode instead of the client fastembed tier. Live CLI smoke: nx index repo embeds + upserts to a code__...__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1 collection (no more 422). +2 regression tests.

title: Service-mode catalog indexing broken: HttpCatalogClient.ensure_owner_for_repo signature + Java upsertOwner null tumbler_prefix
description:
Live taxonomy smoke 2026-06-20 (nx index repo against the JAR-launched pgvector service) surfaced two pre-existing service-mode catalog-index defects:

(1) [FIXED] HttpCatalogClient.ensure_owner_for_repo made 'repo' keyword-only (def ...(self, *, repo: ...)), but the canonical Catalog.ensure_owner_for_repo (catalog.py:1193) and the caller (commands/index.py:86 -> self._writer.ensure_owner_for_repo(repo)) pass it POSITIONALLY -> 'takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given'. Fix: make 'repo' positional-or-keyword to match the protocol.

(2) [OPEN, BLOCKER, needs Java] After (1), POST /v1/catalog/owners/upsert returns 500: 'null value in column tumbler_prefix of relation catalog_owners violates not-null constraint' (CatalogRepository.upsertOwner CatalogRepository.java:243 / CatalogHandler.handleOwnerUpsert:553). The Python client (http_catalog_client.ensure_owner_for_repo) sends no tumbler_prefix and expects the SERVER to assign one ('Otherwise the server assigns a prefix; we query it back'), but the Java upsertOwner inserts NULL and the column is NOT NULL. Needs a service-side fix: assign the owner tumbler_prefix server-side when absent (mirror the SQLite Catalog's prefix allocation), then rebuild the engine-service JAR/binary. Until then, nx index repo in service mode (the 6.0 default) cannot register owners = indexing blocked. NOTE: taxonomy discover/split/project do NOT need the catalog and were smoked live by seeding vectors directly (nexus-7ydks/9pqoj).
notes: | FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-06-20 (PR #1259): (1) Python HttpCatalogClient.ensure_owner_for_repo repo positional + now computes/sends repo_hash via _repo_identity_with_main (idempotent, mirrors canonical); (2) Java CatalogRepository.upsertOwner allocates tumbler_prefix server-side (reuse by repo_hash else 1.{MAX+1}) - CatalogRepositoryTest 86/86 incl. new owner_serverSideAllocatesPrefix_whenAbsent against real Testcontainers PG. Live CLI smoke (JAR-launched service): nx index repo now PASSES owner registration cleanly (was 500 on /owners/upsert). Catalog gap CLOSED. Indexing then hits a SEPARATE, newly-filed bug (service+local collection model-token = minilm-384 vs service bge-768 -> 422), tracked in the new bead - NOT this bead. Requires JAR/binary rebuild + the publish pipeline to ship the Java half to released builds.
close_reason: Code shipped to develop (Python 6d65c196 + Java CatalogRepository.upsertOwner server-side tumbler_prefix allocation, CatalogRepositoryTest 86/86). Live-verified owner registration. Remaining 'JAR/binary rebuild to ship Java half to released builds' is the luxe6 release-distribution gate, not separate code work.

title: Explicit-opt-in JAR launch for nx daemon service (dev/test alternative to the native binary; amends RDR-161)
description: RDR-161 made the cosign-signed native binary the SOLE launch artifact and expunged the java -jar path. That blocks local dev/test on hosts without a darwin native binary (e.g. live taxonomy smoke 2026-06-20: JAR built, no darwin native binary, nx daemon service start cannot launch). Amend: StorageServiceSupervisor accepts an EXPLICIT, opt-in JAR via NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR (and/or nx daemon service start --jar PATH). Native binary stays the default and the only production path. NO auto-discovery, NO silent fallback (preserves RDR-161's 'never silently mask a missing native binary' supply-chain intent). The JAR launch is LOUDLY logged ('unverified dev/test artifact, not the signed native binary') and shown in nx daemon service status as artifact=jar (unverified). Launch: [java, -Xmx?, -jar, jar] with a java-on-PATH guard (fail loud with remedy). Files: src/nexus/daemon/storage_service_daemon.py (_find_service_jar, _spawn_service argv branch, status provenance), commands/daemon.py (optional --jar), docs (RDR-161 amendment note, storage_service_daemon docstring, migration-runbook 'sole artifact' claim). Verification: enables the deferred discover/split/project live smoke (nexus-7ydks/9pqoj).
notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-06-20, PR #1258 -> develop. NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR explicit opt-in: _resolve_launch_artifact + _spawn_service argv branch (java -jar) + java-on-PATH guard; loud verified=False log + launch_kind on spawn record; native stays sole production/verified path; no auto-discovery/silent-fallback. RDR-161 native-only gate updated to amended policy (expunged dual-mode forbidden everywhere; opt-in launch confined to storage_service_daemon.py). RDR-161 amendment note + migration-runbook updated. Tests: tests/daemon/test_jar_launch_opt_in.py (10) + gate/daemon suites green. UNBLOCKS the full discover/split/project live smoke (nexus-7ydks/9pqoj) — best run once #1257/#1258 land on develop so all pieces are co-located + an isolated PG is provisioned.
close_reason: Bead's own notes say IMPLEMENTED 2026-06-20, PR #1258. Confirmed: tests/daemon/test_jar_launch_opt_in.py exists. Done work left open. Grooming-pass verification (2026-07-12).

title: nx taxonomy review delete/merge leaks centroids (pre-existing; worse in service mode)
description: substantive-critic finding on nexus-9pqoj (2026-06-20). review_cmd's delete (action=d) and merge (action=m) call db.taxonomy.delete_topic / merge_topics via t2_index_write but never clean up the topic's centroid. Pre-existing in raw mode (the taxonomy__centroids chroma collection keeps the orphan); in service mode the orphan stays in the pgvector centroid store and keeps attracting chunks in project_against / assign_single until the next full rebuild = persistent ghost assignments to deleted topics. Fix: make HttpTaxonomyStore.delete_topic / merge_topics (and the CatalogTaxonomy equivalents) delete their own port/chroma centroid via self._centroid.delete_ids(collection, [topic_id]) rather than the Chroma-era 'caller handles centroid' contract. Files: src/nexus/commands/taxonomy_cmd.py review_cmd (~917,922); src/nexus/db/t2/http_taxonomy_store.py delete_topic (285-306) + merge_topics (309-328).
close_reason: Service-mode fix shipped in PR #1271 (merged 11:16 UTC): HttpTaxonomyStore.delete_topic/merge_topics self-clean the centroid via self._centroid.delete_ids. Local CatalogTaxonomy leg → nexus-5kl1b. Broader cascade-consolidation pattern → RDR-164.

title: Wire nx taxonomy split / project + auto cross-collection projection through the service (nexus-7ydks follow-on)
description:
Split out from nexus-7ydks (which wired discover/rebuild/assignment to the pgvector service). These three taxonomy paths are still raw-Chroma-only and refuse cleanly on a service-backed handle via _reject_service_backed_handle:

1. `nx taxonomy split` (split_cmd in src/nexus/commands/taxonomy_cmd.py): uses CatalogTaxonomy.compute_split + raw chroma centroid reads/writes. Port to HttpTaxonomyStore.split_topic (already a drop-in) + service centroid endpoints.
2. `nx taxonomy project` (project_cmd): uses project_against with a raw chroma client. Port to HttpTaxonomyStore.project_against (drop-in exists).
3. The automatic cross-collection projection pass in discover_cmd --all (taxonomy_cmd.py) and run_collection_postprocessing (src/nexus/commands/index.py:~789, db.taxonomy.project_against(..., t3._client)): currently skipped LOUDLY in service mode (nexus-7ydks). Wire it to the service project path so --all does full discover+project again.

Pattern is established by nexus-7ydks: branch on _has_raw_access(taxonomy); service path fetches vectors via t3.get_embeddings + paginated stub and persists through the HttpTaxonomyStore drop-in (centroids via the /v1/taxonomy/centroids HTTP route); retire the _reject_service_backed_handle guards on these paths in tandem. The store-side orchestrators (split_topic, project_against, compute_split) already exist and were verified by the nexus-1di3r store-parity arc. Add unit tests mirroring tests/test_taxonomy_service_wiring.py + a live-service smoke.
notes: Parent epic: nexus-gmiaf (RDR-152). Split out from nexus-7ydks 2026-06-20 at user request. nexus-7ydks shipped discover/rebuild/assignment on the service (PR #1256); this carries the remaining split/project/projection-pass port. | SCOPING FINDING 2026-06-20: bigger than 'wire the CLI'. Unlike discover_topics (which takes embeddings as a param, so 7ydks only changed the CLI fetch), HttpTaxonomyStore.split_topic and project_against STILL take a chroma_client and read chunk texts/embeddings through it (chroma_client.get_collection().get(...)) — they are explicitly 'HYBRID: centroids via the port, source chunk reads stay on chroma'. So 9pqoj must ALSO change the store internals (src/nexus/db/t2/http_taxonomy_store.py) to fetch chunks via the service: split_topic should pull the topic's stored vectors via t3.get_embeddings (NOT MiniLM-384 re-embed, which the raw path does — re-embedding would put child centroids in the wrong space vs the bge-768/voyage parent centroids); project_against should pull SOURCE chunk embeddings via get_embeddings instead of get(include=['embeddings']). Plus the CLI wiring + removing the _reject guards + the auto projection pass in discover_cmd --all / index.py. Depends on nexus-7ydks landing (#1256) since it builds on _fetch_service_vectors / _require_supported_taxonomy_backend. | LIVE SMOKE 2026-06-20 (PARTIAL): rebuilt fresh JAR (mvn -f service/pom.xml package -DskipTests); 24/24 tests/db/test_http_taxonomy_store_integration.py pass against live JAR+PG16 — verifies the PERSIST half (centroid port upsert/delete_ids/query, assign_topic, merge_topics, persist_*, ETL) over real HTTP->JAR->Postgres. NOT YET live-verified: the full CLI clustering path (get_embeddings fetch -> compute -> centroid persist) end-to-end — BLOCKED on this darwin host because service/target/nexus-service is an ELF aarch64 Linux binary and RDR-161 retired the java-jar CLI launch path, so `nx daemon service start` has no darwin native binary. Clustering math is pure-Python unit-tested. Remaining smoke needs either a darwin native engine-service binary OR a Linux env OR a fixture-based discover/split/project integration test that seeds bge-768 vectors via the vector endpoint (avoids the voyage 422 embedding-mode gate). Frecency 422 in the vector integration suite is environmental (voyage-collection vs onnx-local service), unrelated to this work. | LIVE SMOKE DONE 2026-06-20: ran end-to-end against a real JAR-launched pgvector service (via the NEXUS_SERVICE_JAR amendment + isolated NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR; nx init --service launched the service from the JAR on darwin). Seeded 10 bge-768 chunks via the vector endpoint, then: DISCOVER (7ydks) -> 2 topics correctly clustered (get_embeddings (10,768) live, _discover_via_service ran, HttpTaxonomyStore persist + centroid port); SPLIT (9pqoj) -> 2 children (_svc_fetch_by_ids -> compute_split -> persist_split -> centroid port, live); PROJECT (9pqoj) -> matched_topics returned, incomplete_fetch=False (S1 flag verified). Catalog/index CLI path was bypassed (2 pre-existing service-mode catalog bugs surfaced, tracked nexus-0cy4b) - taxonomy needs no catalog. The deferred 'live end-to-end verification' item is now CLOSED.
close_reason: Shipped + merged to develop. split/project/auto-cross-collection-projection ported to pgvector service (commits f0c39abf, d647f711; merge 45515805). taxonomy_cmd.py split_cmd:1064 + project_cmd:1680 service-wired; index.py:792 auto-projection wired; http_taxonomy_store.py _svc_fetch_by_ids:928 fetches source vectors via service (the scoping-finding store-internals change). tests/test_taxonomy_service_wiring.py green (11). Live-smoke DONE 2026-06-20 (split->2 children, project->matched_topics, incomplete_fetch=False). Stranded in_progress; closing as shipped.

title: Managed-cloud Desktop (.mcpb) auth: NX_SERVICE_TOKEN is env-only but the .mcpb does not read shell env
description: Surfaced by the release-N doc audit (nexus-ooaut). resolve_managed_endpoint (managed_endpoint.py) reads NX_SERVICE_URL/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN from os.environ ONLY (not config.yml via get_credential). The Claude Desktop .mcpb is a GUI subprocess that does NOT inherit the shell env (the long-documented Desktop cred footgun). So a managed-cloud Desktop user has no documented/working path to supply the service token: env-only resolution + no shell-env inheritance + no config.yml fallback for the token. The error message in resolve_managed_endpoint even says 'Set it with nx config set' but the code never reads config.yml for it. EITHER (a) wire a config.yml fallback for NX_SERVICE_URL/TOKEN (mirror get_credential), OR (b) document the real persistence mechanism for the .mcpb. Local installs are fine (token in pg_credentials + lease discovery). Conexus RDR-001 (managed multitenant) adjacent. Blocks an accurate desktop-deployment.md managed-cloud section.

title: RDR-161 PG bundle binaries lack RPATH — not self-contained on a minimal base (libpq.so.5 not found)
description: nexus-4mm24 cold-acquire test caught it: on minimal debian:trixie-slim (no system libpq), the relocatable PG bundle's bin/ binaries (initdb/pg_ctl/postgres/pg_config) FAIL with 'libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file' (exit 127). Diagnosis: libpq.so.5 IS in <bundle>/lib, but the binaries carry NO RPATH/RUNPATH (readelf -d shows none), so the loader can't find the bundle's own libs; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<bundle>/lib fixes it. SHIPS-NOW consumer guard already landed in pg_provision._bundle_lib_env (sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH for all bundled-PG subprocess invocations — initdb/pg_ctl/postgres-inherited/pg_config). DURABLE ROOT-CAUSE FIX (this bead): scripts/build_pg_bundle.sh should patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN/../lib' on the bin/ binaries (and $ORIGIN on lib/*.so for inter-lib deps) so the bundle is truly self-contained regardless of consumer env. Requires re-cutting + republishing nexus-pg-*.txz on the next engine-service tag. Until then the consumer guard covers nx's own provisioning. This is a real fresh-user defect (luxe6 install-collapse class), not just a test artifact.
notes: RESTART-PATH SCOPE (substantive-critic, 2026-06-19): the ships-now consumer guard (pg_provision._bundle_lib_env in _run/_pg_config_value) covers nx-MANAGED PG lifecycle ONLY: nx init --service provisioning, and daemon restarts (storage_service_daemon._ensure_pg_running -> _start_cluster -> _run). It does NOT cover out-of-band postgres restarts: OS autostart (systemd/launchd), manual pg_ctl/postgres invocation, or a postgres self-restart after a crash inside pg_ctl supervision (the child re-inherits from a pg_ctl process that no longer carries LD_LIBRARY_PATH). The RPATH fix (this bead) is the ONLY thing that closes those paths. Release-N gating: NOT blocking IF nx manages the full PG lifecycle and manual pg_ctl is unsupported (current state — no OS-autostart in the nx install path). If conexus deploy adds OS-autostart of the bundled PG, iytd3 becomes release-blocking. Decide with this evidence.

title: MinerU: memory guard + per-page timeout before subprocess spawn (OOM-cascade resilience)
description: MinerU extraction relies entirely on the OS OOM killer: no memory limit (ulimit/cgroup) is set before spawning the extraction subprocess (pdf_extractor.py ~970-986), and there is only a batch-level 180s timeout (~:997), no per-page timeout. Large formula-dense PDFs OOM unpredictably mid-batch; the -9 SIGKILL then triggers a 1-page retry that can OOM again, cascading 3-5x before resolution. Add an explicit memory guard (ulimit/RLIMIT_AS or cgroup) before subprocess spawn and a per-page timeout within the batch loop, with adaptive batch-size reduction (batch//2) before falling to 1-page.
design: Extend the subprocess path in pdf_extractor.py (RDR-044 fallback chain). Use resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS) in the child preexec, or a cgroup if available. Per-page timeout wraps the page loop. Keep docling->PyMuPDF fallback intact. Coordinate with nexus-m26oq so the degrade-to-docling and the memory-guard land coherently (same subprocess path).
acceptance_criteria: Subprocess spawns with an explicit memory ceiling (configurable, sane default); exceeding it raises a catchable MemoryError-class failure rather than an opaque OS -9. A page exceeding the per-page timeout is isolated, not a whole-batch kill. OOM on a multi-page batch retries at batch//2 before 1-page. Test simulates a memory-runaway/timeout page and asserts isolation + bounded cascade. Complements nexus-m26oq (per-page degrade-to-docling).
notes:
Files: src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py (subprocess spawn ~954-1020, retry ~655-685, timeout ~997), src/nexus/commands/mineru.py, src/nexus/_mineru_pid.py. Sibling: nexus-m26oq (per-page -9 -> docling degrade). No API keys needed to test (synthetic OOM/timeout fixture).

CONFLICT: depends on m26oq — both edit _mineru_run_subprocess/_extract_with_mineru; land m26oq first or shared branch.

TIMEOUT: proc.wait(timeout=180) ~:996-1004, ONLY timeout, hardcoded batch-level; TimeoutExpired -> _killpg_safe + RuntimeError. EXIT: ~:1005-1017 returncode!=0 -> RuntimeError; -9 OOM lands here as opaque RuntimeError (the case to convert to catchable distinguishable error). _mineru_run_isolated :929-954 dispatch (server -> subprocess; server httpx crashes funnel to subprocess).
OOM RETRY/BATCH LOOP: _extract_with_mineru ~:620-721; batch_size=get_mineru_page_batch() (config, default 1), batches :623-634. 1-page retry except RuntimeError :655-685 (covers -9 + server fallback): span<=1 re-raise else per-page loop. INSERTION POINT for adaptive batch//2: between batch-failed and 1-page drop. Per-page timeout: thread budget into _mineru_run_subprocess (replace bare timeout=180; pass explicit timeout when end-start==1).
DOCLING FALLBACK (keep, RDR-044): extract() :334-457; auto: _has_formulas_quick ~:384 -> Docling probe enriched=False ~:390 -> <5 formulas Docling wins else MinerU :420-457; MinerU except :440-457 re-raises loud RuntimeError. m26oq changes this seam to degrade-to-docling — coordinate so the memory-ceiling error is the catchable type m26oq keys on. _extract_with_docling :486; _extract_normalized PyMuPDF terminal ~:394. CAVEAT: RLIMIT_AS caps VIRTUAL space; torch maps large arenas -> size generously or prefer cgroup v2 memory.max on Linux. macOS has NO cgroups + RLIMIT_AS unreliable for torch -> GATE rlimit behind platform/env check, keep OS-OOM-killer fallback on darwin (tests: darwin dev / Linux CI). (2) per-page timeout param. (3) batch//2 step at :655-685.

title: hybridSearch collapses on selective text gates — needs text-first two-phase plan (mirrored from conexus-1az)
description:
Mirrored from conexus-1az (found by conexus xr7.8.9 production go-live gate, 2026-06-12, cloud corpus 116k chunks_1024).

PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch runs ONE query: HNSW ORDER BY embedding + iterative_scan=relaxed_order with the text gate as a scan filter. For SELECTIVE gates this collapses: 'migration protocol' over code__1-33+1-28 has exactly 6 text-gate matches; they rank deeper than hnsw.max_scan_tuples (20k default) from the query vector, so the endpoint returns 0 rows. Budget sweep (Crunchy): 40k->4 rows/34s, 80k->6/95s, 200k->6/140s — full recall ~95s, past every HTTP timeout. A text-index-first plan (GIN bitmap on chunk_tsv/trgm, then order the gated set by distance) answers in ms (bare text-gate COUNT is instant). Same query against the LOCAL engine returns 6 at default budget by HNSW-insertion-order luck — which is how the cross-deployment gate caught it.

Fix belongs in PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch (two-phase or planner-aware dispatch on gate selectivity). Cloud DB already has GRANT SET ON PARAMETER hnsw.max_scan_tuples/iterative_scan TO nexus_svc for SET LOCAL experiments.

AC: hybrid-search returns the complete text-gate-matched top-k for selective gates (pathological case: 6/6) within interactive latency (<2s) at default GUCs, on both local and cloud deployments.

Source of truth: conexus-1az. Should land before/with luxe6 release N.
notes: INVESTIGATION 2026-06-19 (nexus instance): the text-first two-phase plan this bug asks for is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED on develop and regression-green. Timeline proves it: conexus-1az found the collapse 2026-06-12 on the PRE-FIX cloud deployment; the fix nexus-lcogi 'selectivity-aware text-first plan for hybridSearch collapse' landed 2026-06-14 (30515ab1), refined by nexus-x7z7l single-gate-eval 2026-06-17 (4cd6bbfe). Current PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch selective branch (lines ~658-727): bounded GIN-indexed chash fetch (LIMIT SELECTIVE_GATE_MAX+1=5001), and for matches<=5000 ranks via chash IN (...) PK filter with NO HNSW scan -> unstarvable by hnsw.max_scan_tuples. HybridSelectiveGateTest reproduces the exact pathological topology (targets FARTHEST from query vector but carrying the rare token) + EXPLAIN structural proof (rank never touches HNSW index) + behavioral completeness. Ran on develop 2026-06-19: Tests run 5, Failures 0. AC DISPOSITION: local/container half MET (regression green). Cloud production-scale (>20k rows) half UNVERIFIED — container fixture cannot faithfully force the >20k collapse (PG seqscans cheaply at small scale; test defers scale-recall to conexus xr7.8.9 gate). The fixed code has NEVER been re-gated at cloud scale (06-12 gate predated it). REMAINING WORK IS NOT ENGINE CODE: deploy engine-service(lcogi+x7z7l) to cloud + re-run the selective-gate recall check via the conexus xr7.8.9 gate harness. Gated by physical cutover conexus-xr7.8 (freeze-gated). Leaving OPEN pending that cloud re-gate.

Remaining work is a CLOUD RE-GATE (conexus xr7.8.9 harness vs >20k prod corpus w/ engine-service>=v0.1.5 at cutover), tracked conexus-side as conexus-1az. Not engine work.

title: Client-side supervisor re-spawn backstop: re-establish a dead storage-service supervisor instead of hard-failing on a missing lease
description: Debugger (nexus-lz3f2 root-cause) flagged a genuine product gap: the storage-service supervisor is a single point of failure with no client-side liveness backstop. When it dies (OOM/kill-9) and no OS unit (launchd/systemd) restarts it, the lease ages out and clients (nx migrate-to-service, T2/T3 resolution) HARD-FAIL with 'endpoint is not resolvable' — discover_lease() returns (None,None) and never calls ensure_storage_supervisor (the existing re-spawn primitive, commands/daemon.py:1495). DESIGN NUANCE (do not implement naively): if the supervisor died but the JVM service process is STILL alive, a bare ensure_storage_supervisor would spawn a SECOND JVM (sup.start() discover()=None -> _spawn_service new port) -> double-JVM -> worse memory pressure (cascading OOM in constrained hosts). The correct fix ADOPTS the existing live service (re-attach the supervisor to the running pid/port + republish the lease) rather than spawning a new one; only spawn fresh if the service is genuinely dead. Gate to migrate/init surfaces (not every read path), flock-guarded. nexus-lz3f2 (TTL margin + heap bound, commit a2456e51) addresses the OOM TRIGGER; this is the deeper SPOF backstop. Production note: on a unit-managed host the OS restarts the supervisor (run_storage_supervisor returns non-zero) — this backstop covers non-unit environments (containers, bare installs).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Scope clarified by the nexus-f9y78 fix + its stacked review (2026-06-29). f9y78 closed criterion (b) for the guided-upgrade consumer ONLY (establish_verified_service gates readiness on service_endpoint.discover_lease, fail-fast). The GENERAL class this bead tracks remains open: standalone nx migrate-to-service (migrate_cmd _resolve_endpoint), HttpVectorClient._resolve_endpoint, and long-running MCP workers all resolve via service_endpoint.resolve_service_config/discover_lease with NO re-spawn, so they still race a stale lease from an OOM-killed inline supervisor. CRITICAL design constraint (substantive-critic SIG-1): the re-spawn backstop MUST adopt the live JVM, not bare-spawn — in the f9y78 scenario discover() returns None (lease aged out) while the JVM is still serving, so a naive ensure_storage_supervisor call spawns a SECOND JVM (the dead-pid guard only fires when existing is not None) -> double-JVM -> cascading OOM. Correct fix: at the resolver layer (discover_lease/resolve_service_config), on (None,None) probe /health; if the service answers, re-attach/republish the lease for the live pid rather than spawn; only spawn fresh if /health also fails. Also fold in the NX_SERVICE_MAX_HEAP default-on-inline-path mitigation (OOM prevention) — f9y78 added the heap hint to the guided-upgrade error + cli-reference docs but did NOT arm it by default.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: RESOLVE-ATTEMPT FINDING (2026-06-29): the kill-then-respawn-with-durable-pid+port-file design CONFLICTS with the RDR-149 lifecycle gate. test_lifecycle_gate.py:25-27 explicitly bans 'a pid-keyed addr file' and 'per-tier orphan sweep' — liveness is lease TTL freshness by design. A durable pid/port recovery file + orphan-reap is exactly that pattern. So the backstop needs an RDR-149-ALIGNED design, not the naive pid-file approach. Candidate aligned approaches: (a) make the orphaned JVM DIE WITH ITS SUPERVISOR (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux / equivalent) so a dead supervisor leaves NO orphan — then ensure_storage_supervisor heal-on-next-use (RDR-174) works with no double-JVM and no pid-file; (b) OS-init watchdog (RDR-175) already covers the autostart path; the gap is only the non-autostart inline path. Hal's port-persistence insight is sound mechanically but the persisted-pid-file form is gate-prohibited; the parent-death-signal form achieves the same goal (no recoverable-orphan needed because there's no orphan) within the RDR-149 model. RECOMMEND: this needs a small focused design (brainstorming-gate or mini-RDR), not a one-shot build. f9y78 fail-fast already covers the guided-upgrade consumer.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: LINUX CLASS CLOSED by the PR_SET_PDEATHSIG fix (commit on develop 2026-06-29): the JVM now dies with its supervisor, so on Linux a dead/OOM-killed supervisor leaves NO orphaned-but-serving JVM — no double-JVM hazard, and discover_lease consumers see a clean connection-refused instead of a stale-lease race. The adopt-live-service / resolver-layer heal this bead originally scoped is now MOOT on Linux (no orphan to adopt or route around). REMAINING SCOPE (keep open, low priority): macOS WITHOUT autostart — PR_SET_PDEATHSIG has no equiv, so an OOM orphan can still linger (port-less, lease-less zombie under launchd; full hazard on --foreground/no-launchd). The macOS OOM-in-prod combination (no-launchd + memory pressure) is unusual. If/when addressed, the fix is the resolver-layer ensure_storage_supervisor heal for discover_lease callers (HttpVectorClient, http_catalog_client) gated to migrate/init surfaces — NOT a pid-file (RDR-149 gate). Stacked review of the pdeathsig fix: 0 Critical/High; MEDIUM-1 (subreaper-agnostic race guard via _SUPERVISOR_PID) + MEDIUM-2 (prctl-failure os.write notice) applied.

title: Support operator-form ($ne/$in/...) where-filters on the RDR-152 bridge vector routes
description:
Consumer-driven (conductus-RDR-001 P0). The raw bridge /v1/vectors/search (and /query, /get) only translate PLAIN-EQUALITY where predicates: PgVectorRepository.search builds `metadata->>key = value` per entry, ANDed (verified @ ed37fe09; getWhere doc explicitly: 'Chroma operator-form filters ($and,$gte,...) are NOT translated', nexus-1k8s1). Two problems for foreign/editor clients that only have the raw bridge (not the nx MCP search layer which DOES support operators like section_type!=references):

1. No EXCLUSION possible: a thin client cannot express section_type != references to drop reference-section noise from vector results. The nx MCP/CLI search supports where='section_type!=references' above the bridge; the raw endpoint does not.
2. ACTIVE FOOTGUN: sending where={'section_type':{'$ne':'references'}} is not rejected — the handler does String.valueOf(map) -> binds metadata->>'section_type' = '{$ne=references}', matching nothing, SILENTLY returning zero hits. No 400, no error. A consumer following the (now-corrected) Chroma-shaped contract comment gets silent empty results.

ASK: translate at least the common Chroma operator-form on the bridge vector where-filter ($ne, $in, $nin, $and, $or; $gte/$lte already used by aspect paths). Minimum viable: $ne + $in so exclusion works. Alternatively, if operator-form stays unsupported by design, REJECT operator-shaped where values with a 400 (don't silently match-nothing) so clients fail loud.

CONSUMER IMPACT: conductus-dzx.7 (default-drop references-section chunks from vault search) is BLOCKED on this — the conductus thin client deliberately won't hand-roll server-side semantic filtering (RDR-001: depends only on the public bridge contract). Conductus shipped a corrected contract comment warning against the $ne footgun in the meantime.
notes: ext-ref conductus-RDR-001 / conductus-dzx.7. Filed from conductus session 2026-06-18. See conductus T2 dzx7-where-operator-finding.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1270 (feature/nexus-05bfd-where-operators → develop, merged 05:44 UTC). appendWherePredicate translator ($eq/$ne/$in/$nin) on all 3 bridge where-sites; fail-loud 400 for unsupported shapes. 99 Java tests green (unit+repo+hybrid+serving incl HTTP-wire 400). Stacked review clean. Range operators deferred to nexus-4l80g.

title: Fine-grain / author-anchored spans (sub-chunk, heading/block alignment) for catalog links
description: Owner wants finer-grain spanning in nexus generally; surfaced by Conductus (Hellblazer/conductus RDR-001 OQ-3). Today catalog spans are chash: CHUNK identities. Obsidian sub-document refs ([[Note#Heading]], [[Note^blockid]]) are author-controlled anchors whose boundaries do not align with nexus chunk boundaries, so block-refs cannot map faithfully to chash spans. A fine-grain span model (sub-chunk char ranges anchored to content, or stable author-supplied anchors) would let Conductus map heading/block refs to precise catalog spans instead of approximating to the containing chunk. Independently useful for any precise-quotation / passage-pinning use case (RDR catalog 'quotes' links).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog supports a content-stable sub-chunk span (e.g. chash:<hash>:<start>-<end> already exists for positional-in-chunk; extend to survive re-chunking and/or accept an externally-supplied stable anchor id). Conductus can pin a heading/block-level passage to a precise span that survives re-indexing. Back-reference to conductus RDR-001 OQ-3 retained.

title: Expose composed-retrieval (nx_answer) route on the RDR-152 bridge for editor/plugin consumers
description: [njrcn-relay 2026-06-25 r3 constraint] Composed-retrieval bridge route MUST NOT be synchronous-unbounded on the conexus edge proxy: the CP EdgeProxyHandler is a bounded-thread (default 16) synchronous relay behind an ALB ~60s idle; nx_answer composition is 30s-5min → a sync /v1 composed call would starve the data path (503s) + exceed ALB/client timeout. Design: ASYNC submit→poll (like nx_answer structured runs) OR hard server-side timeout < ALB idle; tenant-scoped plan-cache (plan_match/plan_search per tenant) for the fast path (bounds typical, not worst-case); if a sync variant exists, isolate it on a SEPARATE smaller concurrency budget from the /v1 data path + hard timeout. Shared interest: conexus (edge proxy) + conductus (ask-your-vault/fact-linter) + nexus. Co-design with conexus. Source: nexus/nexus-to-conexus-conductus-relay-2026-06-25-r3, conexus A3.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge exposes a composed-retrieval endpoint (e.g. POST /v1/answer) returning a composed, cited answer equivalent to the MCP nx_answer tool, under the same token+tenant AuthFilter. Conductus can render composed answers without shelling out to conexus. Back-reference to conductus RDR-001 retained.
notes: REFERENCE-DESIGN INPUT from conductus (2026-06-18, docs/design/nexus-ai-leverage-and-nx_answer.md). Conductus is building a SHALLOW client-composed 'Ask your vault' (LocalComposedProvider: bridge retrieval + BYO/local LLM generation) that ships independent of this route — it serves as a working prototype of what an editor-facing composed answer should look like. When shaping the composed route, please consider editor-client needs: (1) STREAMING response (token/chunk stream, not just a final blob) for responsive UX; (2) a CITATION PAYLOAD on the answer (per-claim source refs with chunk_text_hash + source_path + title) so a client can render [[wikilinks]]/external citations; (3) SCOPE params (collections, catalog subtree, follow_links depth) so the client controls cross-corpus reach; (4) KEEP retrieval primitives and the composed route SEPARATE — editor clients often want retrieval-only (related-notes, no generation) and should not be forced to take server-side generation. The healthy shape is 'strong retrieval primitives AND an optional composed route', not one-or-the-other. Conductus will add a BridgeComposedProvider (thin delegation) once this lands.

title: RDR-161: wire PG-bundle auto-acquire into nx init --service (before _provision_postgres_step)
description: Discovered in RDR-161 P2 stacked review (substantive-critic S1, 2026-06-18). P1 wired the native BINARY into nx init --service (_ensure_service_binary_step), but the PG bundle is NOT auto-acquired by init: _provision_postgres_step -> _select_bundled_pg only LOOKS for an already-placed bundle at <config_dir>/service/ (it does not download). Asymmetry: binary auto-acquired, bundle not -> the §Consequences 'pip install + nx init --service is a survivable local install' promise is unmet for a fresh machine (user must run 'nx daemon service install-binary TAG' first, then re-run init). FIX: acquire the PG bundle (install_pg_bundle, tag via resolve_service_tag) in init_cmd's --service path BEFORE _provision_postgres_step so _select_bundled_pg finds it. Note ordering: PG acquire must precede PG provisioning; current order is provision->embedder->binary. NOTE: inert until PINNED_SERVICE_TAG is set (same gate as the binary auto-acquire), so not user-visible today. Not a P2 §Approach bullet -> deferred from P2, not a silent scope reduction. Context: RDR-161 §Approach, §Consequences; T2 nexus/rdr-161-p2-* review.

title: Hybrid search: evaluate the text gate ONCE (selective + non-selective) via bounded chash fetch + rank-by-chash — kills the double <% trigram heap-recheck
description: conexus-qsa hybrid p95 latency investigation (2026-06-17) found the deployed RDR-155 P3 lcogi dispatch evaluates the text gate TWICE on the non-selective (code/fanout, >5000 matches) path: a full count(*) plan-probe PLUS the ranked-scan filter. PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch:668-681. For the code corpus (~28k gate matches) the count(*) alone scans all matches before any ranking. The count is only needed to pick selective-vs-HNSW plan; a bounded 'SELECT 1 FROM table WHERE <gate> LIMIT selectiveGateMax+1' existence probe gives the same dispatch decision without the full scan. P5.2 RRF (RDR-156, unbuilt) was meant to remove this; this is the cheap interim win, no cutover. GATED ON conexus EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) result — if the dominant cost is the gin_trgm_ops <% leg (possible missing/invalid trgm index on cloud code collections), that is a cloud-DB index issue, not this. title: Native-image CI build perf: -Ob quick-build for PR/smoke + ParallelGC + tunable builder heap (and larger-runner follow-on)
description: Triaged from the v0.1.x engine-service builds (2026-06-17): native-image build is 6m23s with Peak RSS 7.86GB (> ubuntu-latest's 7GB) and CPU load 3.72 (> 2 vCPU) -> memory over-commit + GC thrash (40.9s/3054 GCs on the good run; a 61%-of-stage GC-warning spike observed). Implemented now: (2) parameterized optimization level (native.image.opt, default -O2 for release artifacts; CI PR-trip-wire + smoke builds pass -Dnative.image.opt=-Ob quick-build = ~half the time + lower memory); (3) -J-XX:+UseParallelGC (faster builder GC on all cores) + parameterized -J-Xmx (native.image.maxheap, default 5632m ~= 80% of 7GB, single knob to raise on a larger runner). DEFERRED (1) (owner cost/availability decision): move linux native builds to a larger GitHub-hosted runner (4-8 core / 16-32GB) — the decisive fix for both the RSS>RAM thrash and the CPU starvation; when it lands, bump native.image.maxheap accordingly. Files: service/pom.xml native profile, .github/workflows/ci.yml (PR native steps).
close_reason: Shipped PR #1232: -Ob quick-build on PR native gates (trip-wire + service-ci smoke), ParallelGC + tunable -Xmx. Empirical: PR-trip-wire native build 6m23s-baseline -> 3m54s job (~half), GC thrash gone. Release stays -O2. Larger-runner (1) remains owner-deferred (one-knob bump of native.image.maxheap).

title: nx doctor: suppress local_embedder_advisory for service-mode installs

description: Follow-up from RDR-160 P3 review (substantive-critic Obs-3). service_bge_model_present() exists and is tested but nothing calls it in nx doctor. A local --service install with a missing/truncated bge model gets no proactive health warning until the JVM boots and fails with an opaque onnxruntime error (the Bge768Embedder fail-loud preflight catches missing-file at boot, but doctor should surface it earlier). Wire a doctor check GATED on service-backend + local mode: if not service_bge_model_present() then warn/fatal with the "nx init --service" remedy plus the expected path. Must NOT fire for non-service local installs (the Python fastembed path does not need the Java-read file) or for cloud mode. Parallels the managed-endpoint probe deferral nexus-o6fch.
close_reason: Merged to develop via PR #1204. nx doctor _check_service_bge_model surfaces a missing/incomplete service bge-768 model (soft warn, service+local gated). Follow-up nexus-ybw87 (local_embedder_advisory service-mode suppression).
