title: Decide: does VoyageEmbedder in the LOCAL Java service violate the 'service makes no remote calls' invariant?
description: Surfaced 2026-06-15 during the RDR-157 cloud topology correction (see T2 nexus_rdr/157-P3.3-topology-correction-and-move-to-rdr001). The locked invariant is: the local Java service connects ONLY to LOCAL Postgres over JDBC and makes NO outbound HTTP; only the nx CLI + local MCP server make remote HTTP calls. BUT today the local Java service CAN make an outbound HTTPS call to the Voyage AI REST API: EmbedderRouter (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/EmbedderRouter.java) routes voyage-* collections to VoyageEmbedder when NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is set (Main.java:100-130), independent of the local-vs-cloud distribution. So 'local stack + Voyage embeddings' works functionally (local pgvector storage, Voyage REST embedding) but means the local service reaches the network. DECISION NEEDED: (a) accept VoyageEmbedder as a sanctioned third-party-API exception to the invariant (the invariant is really about client<->service<->PG topology + control-plane HTTP, not third-party embedding APIs), and document it; OR (b) hold the invariant strictly and move local-mode embedding to the client (CLI/MCP embeds via Voyage, hands vectors to the service) so the service never touches the network. Affects RDR-157 (local distribution) framing and conexus RDR-001 (cloud) boundary. No code change until decided.
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision (a or b) recorded in the RDR-157 and/or RDR-001 record; if (b), a follow-on implementation bead is filed; if (a), the invariant's wording is amended to carve out third-party embedding APIs.
notes: DECIDED 2026-06-15 (owner): ACCEPT VoyageEmbedder as a sanctioned exception to the 'local service makes no remote calls' invariant. Rationale: a third-party EMBEDDING API call is categorically different from the client<->service<->PG topology + control-plane HTTP the invariant governs; local stack + NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY (voyage-* collections embedded via Voyage REST, vectors stored in LOCAL pgvector) stays supported. NO action now. DEFERRED enforcement (later): (1) amend the invariant wording to carve out third-party embedding APIs explicitly; (2) ensure the carve-out is BOUNDED — only embedding APIs, not arbitrary service-side network egress (a guard/test so a future contributor cannot smuggle other outbound calls under this exception). Revisit when RDR-157 local + RDR-001 cloud service delivery lands.

title: RDR-157: mac-arm64 native service binary ships UNSMOKED — add macOS native-serving regression coverage
description: Post-f6j31 the mac-arm64 native nexus-service binary is build+published in engine-service-release.yml but smoke:false (GH macOS runners have no Docker for native-smoke.sh). Cited backstops (mac-arm64 CA-3 PG gate + lp2qo spike) do NOT execute the service binary; CA-3 tests pg_provision+pgvector, lp2qo was a one-time local run. substantive-critic O-B on PR #1197: every engine-service-v* release publishes an unsmoked mac binary with no per-build regression detection (e.g. macOS-linker GraalVM reachability, JNI/ONNX load path, deployment-target). Need a Docker-capable/self-hosted mac runner or an alternate macOS smoke. P3/P4 coverage gap.

title: RDR-157: engine-service-build PR job is advisory (non-required) — decide whether to promote to required
description: The engine-service-build trip-wire (ci.yml) is path-gated to service/** but NOT a required check, so a red result does not block merge (auto-merge gates on required checks only). substantive-critic S2 on PR #1197: this converts 'zero visibility' to 'visible but ignorable'. Decision needed: (a) make it required, accepting ~40min native build on every service/** PR + a branch-protection update; or (b) keep advisory and accept that a service regression can merge to develop and surface at the next engine-service-v* tag. Tracked so the posture is a known risk, not a claimed closure.

title: RDR-157: mac-arm64 native nexus-service binary build (GH macOS has no Docker for jOOQ codegen)
description: The engine-service-release.yml publish matrix covers linux-amd64 + linux-arm64. mac-arm64 is deferred: -Pnative runs jOOQ codegen via testcontainers-jooq-codegen-maven-plugin (generate-sources, boots a pgvector container), but GitHub-hosted macOS runners have NO Docker. So the native SERVICE binary can't build on a GH macos-14 runner. (The mac-arm64 CA-3 gate already passes — it builds PG+pgvector from source, no jOOQ codegen.) Options: (a) decouple jOOQ codegen — pre-generate sources on linux, pass as an artifact, build native on mac without codegen (pom refactor, nexus-ykrhb territory); (b) self-hosted mac runner with Docker; (c) colima on the GH macos runner (slow). Needed for the mac-arm64 LOCAL distribution. Surfaced building the desktop native-binary matrix 2026-06-15.
acceptance_criteria: mac-arm64 native nexus-service binary built + attached to the engine-service-v* release (sha256), via codegen-decoupling or a Docker-capable mac runner.
close_reason: jOOQ codegen decoupled (#1195). -Pprebuilt-jooq unbinds testcontainers codegen; a linux jooq-codegen job generates once + uploads the jooq-sources artifact, native build jobs consume it (no Docker). mac-arm64 native binary now builds on macos-14 — verified green via workflow_dispatch (all 3 targets incl mac built; codegen job green). mac build-only (smoke needs Docker; covered by mac CA-3 + lp2qo). Unblocks the full 3-target publish matrix (nexus-vwvv5.6).

title: RDR-157 N+1: cosign/Sigstore signing for published native nexus-service binary
description: RDR-157 Open Q4. PUBLISHER HALF: engine-service-release.yml signs each engine-service-v* native binary with keyless cosign (OIDC->Fulcio, Rekor bundle), self-verifies before upload, and publishes asset.cosign.bundle + a verify command in the release notes. Native binary runs with DB creds in conexus cloud + is opaque to static inspection, so detached signing matters more than for a JAR. CONSUMER HALF (conexus deploy verifies before docker run + ECR_PUSH.md) is split out to nexus-1jt17 under the RDR-001 consumer epic nexus-w5v8j: a published-but-unchecked signature is no protection until that lands. Surfaced by substantive-critic of PR #1189; scope-split surfaced by substantive-critic of the signing PR.
acceptance_criteria: engine-service-v* release assets carry a cosign/Sigstore signature; conexus deploy verifies it before use; documented in the release notes + ECR_PUSH.md.
close_reason: publisher half shipped in PR #1213 (keyless cosign signing of engine-service release assets); consumer-half verification tracked under nexus-1jt17 (conexus RDR-001)

title: Service install (minilm-384) boot-fails: Java OnnxEmbedder has no model — nothing fetches all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX on a fresh service install
description: Surfaced by tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal Phase A. In service mode the Java service eagerly constructs OnnxEmbedder at boot, loading ~/.cache/chroma/onnx_models/all-MiniLM-L6-v2/onnx/model.onnx. On a fresh 'nx init --service --embedder minilm-384' install nothing downloads that model: init's only warmup (_warmup_bge in src/nexus/commands/init.py) covers bge-768, and chromadb's Python ONNXMiniLM_L6_V2 (which fetches the model to that cache path on first instantiation) is never invoked because embedding now happens server-side in Java. Result: 'nx daemon service start' → JAR exits code 1 with OrtException ORT_NO_SUCHFILE 'model.onnx ... File doesnt exist'. Schema migration (102 changesets) and token seed both succeed first, so it is purely the embedder model. Fix options: (a) warm the minilm ONNX cache during 'nx init --service' (mirror _warmup_bge for the minilm branch); (b) have the Java OnnxEmbedder download the model if absent; (c) bundle the model with the service JAR. Part of the pebfx install story (nexus-luxe6). bge-768 service installs likely hit the analogous gap unless _warmup_bge runs in the --service path — verify.
notes: FINDING 2026-06-15 (owner clarification): local-mode T3 default should be bge-768; MiniLM-384 is STRICTLY for T1. But the Java service has NO bge embedder — OnnxEmbedder (MiniLM-384) is its only local embedder and EmbedderRouter local-mode wires it for ALL collections (verified; MiniLM-384 since RDR-152 gmiaf.20; RDR-155 noted 'MiniLM 384 or bge-base' but shipped MiniLM). So local T3 has ALWAYS embedded with MiniLM-384, inconsistent with nx init offering bge-768 as the recommended local embedder. The boot-failure (this bead) is a symptom; the root is the service uses the wrong local embedder. CORRECT FIX is RDR-scale: new Java BgeOnnxEmbedder (bge CLS-pool + L2-normalize + query-instruction prefix, != MiniLM mean-pool) + embedding-parity gate vs Python fastembed reference (precedent: gmiaf.21 CCE/Voyage parity) + EmbedderRouter local default -> bge-768 + warmup fetches bge ONNX in a Java-loadable form + route to chunks_768. The CLI-fetches/service-reads warmup mechanism prototyped here (feature/nexus-jrrve-service-model-fetch, NOT committed) is reusable for bge. PENDING owner decision: new RDR vs re-scope. PG bundle (#1200) + this are independent; #1200 CI green.
close_reason: SUBSUMED by RDR-160 (epic nexus-ap4ok). The 'fresh service install boot-fails, nothing fetches the ONNX' bug is resolved: nx init --service now fetches the STANDARD bge-768 ONNX (service_bge_model.py) to the Java-read path, Bge768Embedder fail-loud-preflights with a remedy if absent, and the service embeds with bge-768 (not MiniLM). minilm-384 is non-operative for the service path (advisory). Greenfield per RDR Decision 6.

title: Docker full-stack migration dress-rehearsal harness (soup-to-nuts: install→provision→seed→migrate→validate→rollback)
description: The middle rung between the hermetic Python migration E2E (tests/migration/test_e2e_oracle.py — logic only, in-process destination) and the live conexus cloud cutover (xr7.8). A Docker-based harness that, in an ephemeral box, runs the FULL operator path: clean install of the develop wheel → nx init --service (provision PG16 + pgvector + the service JAR + JRE) → seed Chroma (PersistentClient) + SQLite T2 with sample data → nx upgrade (guided Chroma→service migration, RDR-159) → assert parity (chunk counts + a search round-trips through the running pgvector service) → forced rollback → assert Chroma intact. Both legs: ONNX/local (secret-free) AND Voyage/cloud (keys from .env). Purpose: catch install/provisioning/ETL bugs (the class that cost ~40min on the 2026-06-10 prod run) locally BEFORE the user-authorized prod freeze session. Sibling-container (Testcontainers-style) from host docker; NOT DinD. Origin: release-readiness probe 2026-06-14.
close_reason: Built + landed in PR #1184. tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/ (Dockerfile, run.sh, rehearse.sh, seed_legacy.py). Both legs green soup-to-nuts: ONNX-local + Voyage cloud. Surfaced+fixed nexus-6laob (Debian socket bug); surfaced nexus-jrrve (ONNX model not fetched on service install).

title: nx index repo --since-head: git-diff-driven incremental indexing (avoid full-repo walk + full-collection staleness pull per commit)
description:
PROBLEM. The git post-commit/post-merge/post-rewrite hooks (now removed — see below) ran 'nx index repo $REPO_TOP' on every commit. index_repository() is repo-scoped with no changed-files input, so each run pays a fixed cost regardless of what changed: (1) build_staleness_cache pulls EVERY chunk of code__/docs__/rdr__ from T3 (ceil(N/300) round-trips per collection), (2) walks every file in the repo (1240 for nexus) hashing each against the cache (the 'skipped (0.0s)' spam), (3) runs an RDR post-pass over all 209 RDRs (~70s 'rdr: 0 indexed, 209 current' even on a no-op), (4) prunes deleted files via the full-tree walk. Embedding is already incremental (unchanged chunks skip), but the SCAFFOLDING is not — ~70s+ fixed tax per commit. This made hook-driven indexing too expensive; the hooks were removed across 10 repos (2026-06-14), trading auto-freshness for manual 'nx index repo'.

ENABLER (already present). index_repository() writes owners.head_hash every successful run (_set_owner_head_hash) — the system already records which git commit was last fully indexed. Git knows exactly what changed. Those two facts make true granularity straightforward.

PROPOSED. Add 'nx index repo --since-head' (and/or index_repository(repo, since_head=True) / a paths= param): diff 'git diff --name-status <owners.head_hash> HEAD' to get the delta, then process ONLY that delta — targeted staleness lookup by source_uri for just those files (NOT a full-collection pull), embed A/M files, prune D files' chunks, re-point R (renames). Fall back to a full walk when head_hash is missing (first run), unreachable (history rewrite/shallow), or the diff fails. Hook stays trivial: 'nx index repo "$REPO_TOP" --since-head'. After this, a one-file commit reads one file, does one targeted staleness lookup, embeds one file's chunks — no full pull, no 70s RDR pass, no 1240-file walk.
design:
ENTRY: src/nexus/commands/index.py index_repo_cmd (@index.command 'repo') gains --since-head flag; src/nexus/indexer.py index_repository() gains since_head: bool (or changed_paths: list[(status,path)] | None). 
DELTA SOURCE: git diff --name-status <owners.head_hash> HEAD (read head_hash via the owner/catalog record the indexer already maintains; --name-status yields A/M/D/R so deletes+renames are handled, unlike --name-only). 
TARGETED STALENESS (the core change): instead of build_staleness_cache pulling the whole collection (nexus.indexer_utils.build_staleness_cache → _paginated_get over all chunks), add a path-scoped lookup that queries existing chunks by source_uri/source_key for ONLY the changed files (catalog: source_uri → doc → document_chunks → chash). Reuse check_staleness semantics on that small set. 
DELETION/RENAME: D → prune that file's chunks (the existing deleted-file prune at indexer.py ~line 891 currently relies on the full walk; the delta path must prune per-D-path explicitly). R → treat as D(old)+A(new) or re-point source_uri. 
FALLBACK: head_hash absent/unreachable/shallow/diff-error → full index_repository (current behavior). Log which path was taken. 
HOOK: the granular hook calls 'nx index repo --since-head'; keep the pgrep + flock guards. 
EDGE CASES: worktrees (head_hash is per-owner; existing worktree-identity code handles it), first run, force/--force still does full, frecency_only unaffected. 
NON-GOAL: do NOT change the default 'nx index repo' (full walk) behavior — --since-head is opt-in; the hook adopts it.
RELATED: the per-collection full-pull staleness (build_staleness_cache) is itself worth a targeted variant for this path. Tier-1 stopgap (hook routes changed RDR→'nx index rdr <file>', prose→'nx index md <file>', code→full repo only when code changed) needs NO code change and can ship first; the file-scoped rdr/md subcommands already exist (index rdr docstring: single-file is 'the preferred form when only one changed').
acceptance_criteria: (1) 'nx index repo --since-head' on a repo with a valid owners.head_hash processes ONLY files changed in head_hash..HEAD: a 1-file commit embeds 1 file, does NOT pull the full collection, does NOT run the 209-RDR pass unless an RDR changed. (2) Deleted files (status D) have their chunks pruned; renamed (R) re-pointed; added/modified (A/M) embedded. (3) Missing/unreachable head_hash (first run, shallow, rewritten history) falls back to a full walk with a log line stating which path ran. (4) Default 'nx index repo' (no flag) behavior unchanged (regression: existing index tests green). (5) owners.head_hash is advanced to HEAD after a successful --since-head run. (6) Benchmark: --since-head on a 1-file change is >10x faster than full 'nx index repo' on the nexus corpus (the 70s RDR no-op pass is gone). (7) TDD: tests cover delta computation, A/M/D/R handling, targeted staleness (no full-collection pull), and fallback.
notes: Context: filed 2026-06-14 after removing the nx-index git hooks from 10 repos (arcaneum/ART/BFDB/Delos/Kramer/Luciferase/nexus/scheme-evolution-research/t8code/WoWAddonDevGuide) because the full-repo reindex per commit was too expensive (Luciferase was mid a ~19h full re-embed at 32s/file; nexus paid ~70s/commit on a no-op RDR pass). Removing hooks traded auto-freshness for manual 'nx index repo'. This bead restores cheap auto-freshness. Research findings (this session): index_repository is repo-scoped; staleness = full-collection chunk pull into an in-memory cache + per-file lookup; head_hash already tracked per owner; deletion-prune currently depends on the full walk; file-scoped rdr/md subcommands already exist but code has none. Tier-1 hook stopgap (no code change) can ship independently. When this lands, re-installing a granular hook is a separate follow-up.
close_reason: Shipped b3843572. --since-head on nx index repo: worktree-inclusive git delta from owners.head_hash (new reader _get_owner_head_hash + _git_changed_since with A/M/D/T/R/C parsing, U/mid-merge = fallback); delta walk filter; empty staleness caches (per-file path guards no-op edits); explicit doc deletion for D/R-old (git rename detection reused) + manifest-driven chunk sweep; ALL full-tree passes gated off under the partial walk incl. the housekeeping miss-count sweep (mass-delete hazard, structurally pinned), misclassified prune, quarantine, rg cache rebuild; loud fallback on any doubt; --force wins. Empty delta = sub-second no-op. 10 new tests, 129 green, docs row added. NOTE for the hook re-enable decision (Hal's call, separate): the hooks removed 2026-06-14 can now run 'nx index repo $REPO_TOP --since-head' cheaply.

title: HybridParityIntegrationTest bit-rotted: missing catalog_collections grant + sub-32-char chash ids
description: The @integration HybridParityIntegrationTest (RDR-155 P3.1, nexus-sbvg0) no longer runs — two pre-existing fixture-rot issues hidden because @integration is CI-excluded: (1) @BeforeAll grants chunks_384 but not catalog_collections, so upsertChunks()->ensureCollectionRegistered() fails 'permission denied for table catalog_collections'; (2) after fixing the grant, the fixture chash ids ('par-t1' etc., 5 chars) violate the later-added chunks_384_chash_len_check (length=32). Also needs the chroma CLI on PATH (dual-leg Chroma+pgvector parity). Fix: grant catalog_collections SELECT,INSERT; pad fixture chash ids to 32 chars (sha256Hex32-style). Discovered while verifying nexus-lcogi (the lcogi hybridSearch fix is SELECT-only and validated by PgVectorHybridSearchContractTest + the new HybridSelectiveGateTest; this parity test is a separate rot). Likely sibling to nexus-i055u (DualRunHarness @BeforeAll rot in minilm-only env).
close_reason: Duplicate of nexus-luofb — already fixed by PR #1236 (commit 3dd10338, 2026-06-17): catalog_collections SELECT,INSERT grant added (line 218) and fixture chash ids padded to 32 chars via chash() helper (line 122-128). Both fixes this bead describes are in. Remaining chroma-CLI requirement is an @integration env dep (findChromaBinary), not a code bug.

title: Verify tenant RLS isolation holds under transaction-mode connection pooling (PgBouncer)
description: From conexus-cmt (RDR-001). The engine's tenant isolation relies on SET LOCAL <tenant GUC> inside each transaction; its leak-safety under a REAL connection pool (PgBouncer, as in Crunchy Standard / production) has never been regression-tested. Need: prove the engine (a) functions correctly under transaction-mode PgBouncer (no reliance on session-scoped features that txn-mode pooling breaks — prepared statements, session SET, advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY), and (b) does NOT bleed tenant context across a reused pooled server connection. Test shape: two sequential requests from different tenants over a pool constrained to one server connection; assert request 2 cannot see request 1's rows. The conexus-side CP equivalent is already covered (conexus-8ow GucLeakTripwire); this is the engine-side analog over the nexus.tenant RLS path.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test proves: engine operates correctly under transaction-mode PgBouncer, AND tenant context does not bleed across a reused pooled connection (cross-tenant row visibility = 0). Mirrors conexus-cmt.
close_reason: Work shipped via merged PRs #1228/#1227/#1226; stale in_progress from cleared session

title: Emit per-request (tenant_id, tokens) usage for downstream metering ingestion
description: From conexus-xr7.6.3 (RDR-001 Phase 6 metering, forward bead). The conexus control-plane has built+tested the ENTIRE consumer-side token INGESTION path (conexus_svc-writable, aggregates into usage_counter.tokens) but has nothing to ingest: the engine must emit, per request it serves, the per-tenant token-usage count. The emitter lives in the engine. Without it, per-tenant token metering is consumer-side-complete but NOT end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: The engine emits per-request (tenant_id, tokens) usage (header or structured channel) that a downstream consumer can aggregate. Verified end-to-end: conexus_svc ingestion rolls engine-emitted counts into usage_counter.tokens. Unblocks conexus-xr7.6.3.
close_reason: Merged to develop via PR #1180. Engine emits X-Nexus-Usage-Tokens per-request header (Voyage usage.total_tokens / CCE accumulated / ONNX→0 local). Token count threaded via explicit return values (Tokened<T> + *WithTokens), NOT a ThreadLocal (round-1 critic Critical). Header contract pinned to a constant + format test. Stacked review 2 rounds: justified, 0 Critical/0 Significant. /embed parity gate unchanged. Engine-side only; conexus EdgeProxyHandler ingest is conexus-xr7.6.3 (design on bead). Retry-undercount documented (billing-safe direction).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
DESIGN (research 2026-06-14). CONTRACT: engine sets response header 'X-Nexus-Usage-Tokens: <int>'; conexus EdgeProxyHandler reads it post-upstream, calls MeteringService.recordTokenUsage(UUID tenant, long tokens) [ALREADY EXISTS + tested, conexus], then STRIPS the header from the client relay. Response-header is the channel (no log scrape, no engine-side table write).

ENGINE SIDE (nexus repo = THIS bead's scope): Voyage usage.total_tokens is parsed-then-DISCARDED (VoyageEmbedder.sortedData reads only data[]); CCE same per-text (sum N calls); ONNX has tokenizer ids length (encodings[i].getIds().length) free in embedBatch. PLAN: (1) new record EmbedResult(List<float[]> embeddings, long tokens); (2) VoyageEmbedder/CceEmbedder/OnnxEmbedder gain embedWithUsage() capturing usage.total_tokens (Embedder iface default delegates embed() with 0); (3) EmbedderRouter.embedForCollectionWithUsage / embedOneForCollectionWithUsage; (4) VectorHandler: each embedding endpoint (/search,/query,/hybrid-search,/search-metadata-scoped,/search-topic-scoped,/upsert-chunks,/store-put,/embed) calls *WithUsage, then ex.getResponseHeaders().set('X-Nexus-Usage-Tokens', tokens) when tokens>0, BEFORE HttpUtil.send. Tenant already resolved (RequestContext.tenant via AuthFilter). Edge cases: 0 tokens (dedup-collapse/cache) → omit header; errors (500) → no header → no charge; multi-collection → one query embed; ONNX local → emit real tokenizer count (keeps billing coherent). TDD: VectorHandlerTokenUsageTest (stub router returns EmbedResult tokens=73; assert header on /search+/upsert, ABSENT on /store-list + on 500 + on 0-token).

CONEXUS SIDE (conexus-xr7.6.3, NOT this bead — relay): EdgeProxyHandler gains svcMetering (conexus_svc MeteringService) injection; after httpClient.send reads upstreamResp.headers().firstValue('x-nexus-usage-tokens'), calls recordTokenUsage in try/catch (metering never fails a request), adds 'x-nexus-usage-tokens' to the header-strip exclusion list (line ~579). EdgeProxyHandlerTokenIngestionIT verifies usage_counter.tokens rolls up + header not client-visible. ControlPlaneServer.main wires svcDsl-backed MeteringService.

title: Support a mint-scoped (non-root) service token so consumers needn't carry root admin authority
description: From conexus-c0x (RDR-001 security hardening). The conexus edge (internet-facing) currently must hold the engine ROOT service_token (CONEXUS_ENGINE_ADMIN_TOKEN) to mint per-tenant tokens, because the engine admin API only accepts the root token. An edge compromise therefore yields full engine-admin authority. The engine should support a SCOPED token type (e.g. mint-only, no tenant-delete/admin) so a consumer can be issued least-privilege credentials. Until this exists, conexus-c0x cannot issue the edge a non-admin token (its core fix) and falls back to marginal secret-resource-policy defense-in-depth.
acceptance_criteria: The engine admin API can issue/accept a scoped token that permits per-tenant token minting but NOT engine-admin operations (tenant delete, global admin). A consumer (conexus edge) can authenticate with it for mint, and an admin-scope operation with it is rejected. Unblocks conexus-c0x.

Scoped tokens per RDR-005 pins; mint issuance operator-only via nx service token issue --scope mint. AC met: mint-scoped credential mints per-tenant tokens (data tokens via x1h07's endpoint), rejected on all admin ops. conexus edge provisioning (their conexus-8ub8 remainder) in progress their side. record-deploy verified live.

# Plan: scoped service tokens + data-token mint (nexus-868dq + nexus-x1h07)

One `service/` arc, one engine cut. Design is locked (T2 `nexus/design-868dq-x1h07-scoped-tokens-data-mint.md` [20380]); acceptance criteria are the conexus RDR-005 pins (T2 `conexus/conexus-to-nexus-rdr005-x1h07-pins-2026-06-26` [5758]). This plan is the work breakdown only — no design re-litigation.

## Grounding (as-read, 2026-07-07)

- `service_tokens` currently has NO scope column; privilege is a single `isRoot` bit derived from `label == 'bootstrap-legacy-token'` (`TokenStore.ROOT_TOKEN_LABEL`).
- `TokenStore.ServiceToken(tenantId, expiresAt, isRoot)`, `TokenCache.Resolved(tenantId, isRoot)`, `RequestContext.Principal(tenant, session, mintedSession, isOperator)` — all 4-or-fewer-field records that ripple through `AuthFilter` → every handler.
- `RequestContext.Principal(...)` is constructed positionally in **7 places**: `AuthFilter.java` (production) + 6 test files (`CatalogHandlerImportEmptyBodyTest`, `CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest`, `AspectHandlerEnqueueErrorTest`, `TaxonomyHandlerAssignFkTest`, `MigrationHandlerIngestCloudTest`, `CatalogHandlerUpdateManyDeleteManyTest`), all with the current 4-arg shape. Adding fields breaks all 7 call sites — Phase 2 must fix them in the same commit or the build doesn't compile.
- `TokenStore.issueToken(tenant, label, ttl)` has exactly 2 callers (`TokenAdminHandler` x2, `TokenBoundaryAdversarialTest` x2) — safe to keep as a delegating overload.
- `rotateTokens` hardcodes the new row's label to `"rotated"` and writes no scope — after Phase 1 ships, this SILENTLY DOWNGRADES a rotated mint-scope token to `scope='tenant'` (schema default). This is a correctness gap I found reading the code, not in the design memo's numbered list — flagged as an explicit added task (2.5), not silent scope creep.
- jOOQ codegen (`testcontainers-jooq-codegen-maven-plugin`, `generate-sources` phase) auto-regenerates `SERVICE_TOKENS` from the Liquibase changelog on every Maven build — no manual codegen step.
- Existing hermetic test pattern (`TokenAdminHandlerTest`, `ServiceTokenSchemaLiquibaseTest`): Testcontainers PostgreSQL, real Liquibase migration, real `NexusService`, `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)`. New tests follow this.
- CLI: `src/nexus/commands/service_cmd.py` (`nx service token issue/rotate/revoke/list`), backed by `src/nexus/db/t2/http_token_store.py` (`HttpTokenStore`), unit-tested in `tests/test_service_cmd.py` (`_FakeStore` pattern).

## Plan-author decisions (called out for audit — not literal design-memo bullets)

1. **AuthFilter centralizes the mint-scope path restriction** (design item 4's "no data-path tenant authority"): a `scope=mint` bearer is rejected with 403 for any path other than `/v1/data-tokens/*`, enforced in `AuthFilter` itself (one choke point), matching the existing nexus-45ykb wildcard-rejection pattern. `TokenAdminHandler`'s own scope guard and `DataTokenHandler`'s own scope guard are defense-in-depth layer 2, mirroring the existing nexus-e4130 layered-authorization style.
2. **`rotateTokens` becomes scope-preserving** (Task 2.5) — not in the design memo, but required for internal consistency: without it, rotating a mint-scope token silently strips its mint privilege.
3. **`TokenInfo`/`nx service token list` gains a `scope` column** — small operability addition (an operator can't safely choose a revoke target without seeing which rows are mint/data-scoped); flagged explicitly as a bounded, low-risk addition, not gold-plating.
4. **`/v1/data-tokens/mint` accepts ONLY `scope=mint` callers** (not root) — reads design item 4 ("accepted ONLY by ... mint") literally. If Hal wants root to also bypass this, that's a follow-up, not assumed here.

## Env vars introduced (exactly 4, per relay constraint: "TTL ceiling; the three rate-limit bounds")

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `NX_DATA_TOKEN_TTL_CEILING_SECONDS` | 3600 | max `ttl_seconds` a mint caller may request; over-ceiling is HTTP 400, never clamped |
| `NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_BURST` | 5 | per-(credential,tenant) bucket capacity |
| `NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE` | 1 | per-(credential,tenant) refill rate |
| `NX_MINT_RATE_GLOBAL_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE` | 10 | per-credential global bucket capacity AND refill rate (no separate global burst knob) |

TTL default (300s) is NOT env-overridable (relay scoped only the ceiling; a body-supplied `ttl_seconds` already covers the "want something other than 300s" case up to the ceiling).

---

## Phase 1 — Schema: `service-tokens-003` scope column

**Task 1.1 (test-first).** Extend `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/ServiceTokenSchemaLiquibaseTest.java`: add `"scope"` to the expected `SERVICE_TOKEN_COLUMNS` set; add `scopeColumnHasCheckConstraint()` (insert each of root/tenant/mint/data succeeds; insert `'bogus'` throws `SQLException` on the CHECK); add `bootstrapRootTokenBackfilledToRootScope()` (seed a root-labelled row via raw SQL pre-migration order — actually: run full migration, assert any pre-existing `bootstrap-legacy-token` row, if present, has `scope='root'`; simplest: seed a root-labelled row via direct INSERT *before* changelog-003 would run isn't possible since Liquibase runs the whole chain atomically in test setup — instead assert the changeset's backfill UPDATE statement is idempotent by re-running `Liquibase.update()` twice and asserting no error, then separately unit-assert via `TokenStore` in Phase 2 that `ensureBootstrapToken` sets scope='root').
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=ServiceTokenSchemaLiquibaseTest` — must FAIL (no scope column yet, no check constraint).

**Task 1.2.** Create `service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/service-tokens-003-scope-column.xml`:
```sql
ALTER TABLE nexus.service_tokens ADD COLUMN scope TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'tenant';
ALTER TABLE nexus.service_tokens ADD CONSTRAINT chk_service_tokens_scope
    CHECK (scope IN ('root','tenant','mint','data'));
UPDATE nexus.service_tokens SET scope = 'root' WHERE label = 'bootstrap-legacy-token';
```
Rollback: drop constraint, drop column. Register `<include file="db/changelog/service-tokens-003-scope-column.xml"/>` in `service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/db.changelog-master.xml` immediately after the `service-tokens-002` include (line ~57).
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=ServiceTokenSchemaLiquibaseTest` — must PASS.
**Deps:** none. **Success:** schema test green; jOOQ `SERVICE_TOKENS.SCOPE` field exists after next `./mvnw compile` (verify via `grep -r "SCOPE" service/target/generated-sources/jooq/dev/nexus/service/jooq/nexus/tables/ServiceTokens.java`).

---

## Phase 2 — Domain model: scope through TokenStore / TokenCache / RequestContext / AuthFilter

**Task 2.1 (test-first).** Add failing tests to `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/TokenBoundaryAdversarialTest.java` (or a focused new file `TokenScopeResolutionTest.java` if that file is already large — check line count first; if >600 lines, use a new file alongside it): `lookupServiceToken` returns the row's `scope`; `issueToken(tenant, label, ttl, scope)` rejects `scope` not in `{root,tenant,mint,data}` (`IllegalArgumentException`); `ensureBootstrapToken` inserts with `scope='root'`.
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=TokenScopeResolutionTest` (or the chosen file) — FAIL.

**Task 2.2.** Edit `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TokenStore.java`:
- `ServiceToken` record gains `String scope`; `lookupServiceToken` selects `SERVICE_TOKENS.SCOPE`; `isRoot` now derived as `SCOPE_ROOT.equals(scope)` (not label — per design "isRoot := scope=='root'").
- New constants `SCOPE_ROOT="root"`, `SCOPE_TENANT="tenant"`, `SCOPE_MINT="mint"`, `SCOPE_DATA="data"`.
- New 4-arg `issueToken(String tenant, String label, Long ttlSeconds, String scope)` validating scope membership; existing 3-arg `issueToken(tenant, label, ttl)` becomes a delegating overload passing `SCOPE_TENANT` (zero behavior change for the 2 existing callers).
- `ensureBootstrapToken` inserts `SERVICE_TOKENS.SCOPE` = `SCOPE_ROOT` explicitly (don't rely on the column default, since a future default change must not silently affect root provisioning).
- New `TokenInfo` field `scope`; `listTokens` selects and returns it.
Run: `-Dtest=TokenScopeResolutionTest` — PASS.

**Task 2.3 (test-first).** Extend `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/AuthFilterTest.java`: `Resolved`/`Principal` carry scope through; a `scope=data` token resolves `isOperator=false` and exposes `scope="data"`.
Edit `TokenCache.java`: `Entry` gains `scope`; `Resolved(String tenantId, boolean isRoot, String scope)`.
Edit `RequestContext.java`: `Principal` gains `String scope, String credentialHash` (6-arg record now); new static accessors `RequestContext.scope()` and `RequestContext.credentialHash()`.
Edit `AuthFilter.java`: thread `resolved.get().scope()` and the already-computed `TokenHashing.sha256Hex(rawToken)` into the new `Principal(...)` call.
**Task 2.4 (mechanical, same commit).** Fix all 6 test call sites of `new RequestContext.Principal(TENANT, null, false, false)` → add `, "tenant", "test-credential-hash"` (or equivalent) in: `CatalogHandlerImportEmptyBodyTest.java:154`, `CatalogHandlerManifestFkTest.java:155`, `AspectHandlerEnqueueErrorTest.java:212`, `TaxonomyHandlerAssignFkTest.java:145`, `MigrationHandlerIngestCloudTest.java:442`, `CatalogHandlerUpdateManyDeleteManyTest.java:185`.
**Task 2.4b.** Add the AuthFilter mint-path-restriction guard (plan-author decision 1): after resolving `scope`, if `"mint".equals(scope)` and the request path does not start with `/v1/data-tokens/`, reject with 403 (`"mint_scope_data_path_forbidden"`). Add tests to `AuthFilterTest.java`: mint-scope + `/v1/memory` → 403; mint-scope + `/v1/data-tokens/mint` → passes through to the handler.
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=AuthFilterTest` — PASS. Full compile check: `cd service && ./mvnw test-compile` (catches any remaining `Principal(` call sites).

**Task 2.5 (test-first, the found gap).** Add to `TokenBoundaryAdversarialTest.java` (or the new scope-resolution test file): `rotateTokens` on a tenant whose only live token has `scope='mint'` issues a new token that ALSO has `scope='mint'`, not the schema default `'tenant'`.
Edit `TokenStore.rotateTokens`: change the `expired` SELECT to also fetch `SERVICE_TOKENS.SCOPE`; carry the first fetched live token's scope into the new row's INSERT (fallback `SCOPE_TENANT` when no live tokens existed, matching current no-live-token behavior). Document as best-effort (correct for the intended one-scope-per-tenant-row usage; a tenant with deliberately mixed scopes on rotate is out of scope here).
Run: full `-Dtest` for the modified test file — PASS.

**Deps:** Phase 1. **Success:** `./mvnw test -pl service` green for all Phase 1-2 test files; `git grep "new RequestContext.Principal("` shows zero 4-arg call sites left.

---

## Phase 3 — TokenAdminHandler: scoped issuance + cross-scope lockout

**Task 3.1 (test-first).** Extend `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/TokenAdminHandlerTest.java`:
- `handleIssue` with body `{tenant, scope:"mint"}` from a non-operator bearer → 403.
- Same from the operator (root) bearer → 200, and the resulting row has `scope='mint'` (verify via a follow-up `list` call or direct SQL).
- `handleIssue` with `scope:"data"` or `scope:"root"` (any caller, including operator) → 400 (`"invalid scope for issue: ..."`) — data/root scope may not be minted through this endpoint.
- A bearer whose OWN scope is `mint` calling ANY `TokenAdminHandler` route (`/v1/service-tokens/list`, `/v1/service-tokens/issue`, `/v1/tenants/create`) → 403, even though `AuthFilter`'s Task 2.4b guard already blocks it at the filter layer — this test proves handler-level defense-in-depth independently (construct the request bypassing... actually since AuthFilter blocks first in the real service, assert via a targeted unit test that calls `TokenAdminHandler.handle(...)` directly with `RequestContext` pre-seeded to `scope=mint` — mirrors the existing direct-handler-unit-test style already used elsewhere in this file if present, else falls back to the full HTTP path returning 403 for either reason).
- Same for `scope=data`.
Run: `-Dtest=TokenAdminHandlerTest` — FAIL.

**Task 3.2.** Edit `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/TokenAdminHandler.java`:
- Top of `handle()`: if `"mint".equals(RequestContext.scope()) || "data".equals(RequestContext.scope())` → 403 (`"scope_forbidden_on_admin_surface"`), before the path switch.
- `handleIssue`: read optional body `"scope"`; if absent default `TokenStore.SCOPE_TENANT` (unchanged behavior); if present and equals `SCOPE_MINT`, require `requireOperator(ex)` (403 otherwise, reuse existing helper); if present and NOT in `{tenant, mint}` → throw `IllegalArgumentException` (→ 400 via existing catch block).
- `handleList` row map: add `row.put("scope", t.scope());`.
Run: `-Dtest=TokenAdminHandlerTest` — PASS.

**Deps:** Phase 2. **Success:** `TokenAdminHandlerTest` green; `git grep -n "scope" service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/TokenAdminHandler.java` shows the guard + issue validation + list column.

### >>> REVIEW GATE A (mandatory, dispatch both) <<<
`code-review-expert` then `substantive-critic` on the combined Phase 1-3 diff (schema + TokenStore/TokenCache/RequestContext/AuthFilter/TokenAdminHandler). Brief the critic with this plan's "Plan-author decisions" section — it should pressure-test: does `isRoot` deriving from `scope` (not `label`) actually preserve every existing root-token test's assumption? Does the rotate-scope-preservation fallback correctly handle a tenant with zero live tokens? Is the AuthFilter mint-path prefix check (`startsWith("/v1/data-tokens/")`) exact-prefix-safe against a crafted path like `/v1/data-tokens-evil`? Fix Critical/High, re-run `./mvnw test -pl service` before proceeding.

---

## Phase 4 — `DataTokenHandler`: `POST /v1/data-tokens/mint`

**Task 4.1 (test-first).** New file `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/DataTokenHandlerTest.java`, hermetic Testcontainers pattern (mirror `TokenAdminHandlerTest`'s `@BeforeAll startAll()` boilerplate: `PgContainerHelper.start()`, `nexus_svc` role, full Liquibase, seed root token, real `NexusService`). Cases:
- Seed a `scope=mint` token (issue via `/v1/service-tokens/issue` as operator). Call `/v1/data-tokens/mint` with `{tenant:"acme"}` as that bearer → 200, body has `data_token` + `expires_in_seconds:300` (default).
- Cross-tenant mint: the mint token is itself bound to `tenant_id="conexus-edge"` (or whatever tenant it was issued against); minting a data token for `{tenant:"acme"}` still succeeds (design item 5's "cross-tenant mint allowed").
- `{tenant:"acme", ttl_seconds:7200}` (over default ceiling 3600) → 400, no token minted.
- `{tenant:"acme", ttl_seconds:1800}` → 200, `expires_in_seconds:1800`.
- Missing `tenant` → 400.
- Wildcard tenant `"*"` → 400 (via existing `rejectWildcard`).
- A `scope=tenant` bearer, a `scope=data` bearer, and the root bearer ALL get 403 calling this endpoint (plan-author decision 4: ONLY `scope=mint` is accepted).
- The minted `data_token`, presented as a bearer against `/v1/memory` (or any ordinary data route) for its tenant, resolves and succeeds — proves "full data-path authority for its tenant" (design item 6).
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=DataTokenHandlerTest` — FAIL (class doesn't exist yet — expect compile error first, which is the correct TDD red state for a new class).

**Task 4.2.** New file `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/DataTokenHandler.java`:
```java
public final class DataTokenHandler implements HttpHandler {
    static final long DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = 300L;
    private final TokenStore store;
    private final MintRateLimiter rateLimiter;   // Phase 5, may be a no-op limiter here (see Task 5 ordering note)
    private final Clock clock;
    private final long ttlCeilingSeconds;

    public DataTokenHandler(TokenStore store, MintRateLimiter rateLimiter, Clock clock, long ttlCeilingSeconds) {...}
    public static DataTokenHandler fromEnv(TokenStore store, Clock clock) {...}  // reads NX_DATA_TOKEN_TTL_CEILING_SECONDS

    // handle(): route POST /v1/data-tokens/mint only, 404 else, 405 non-POST
    // handleMint(): require RequestContext.scope() == "mint" (403 else);
    //   read+validate tenant (required, non-wildcard) and ttl_seconds (default 300, > ceiling -> 400, <=0 -> 400);
    //   rateLimiter.tryAcquire(RequestContext.credentialHash(), tenant) -> false => 429;
    //   store.issueToken(tenant, "data-token", ttlSeconds, TokenStore.SCOPE_DATA);
    //   respond {data_token, expires_in_seconds}
}
```
Wire in `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/NexusService.java`: after the `sessionsCtx` block (~line 296), add
```java
var dataTokenCtx = server.createContext("/v1/data-tokens",
        DataTokenHandler.fromEnv(tokenStore, java.time.Clock.systemUTC()));
dataTokenCtx.getFilters().addAll(authFilter);
```
Run: `-Dtest=DataTokenHandlerTest` — PASS (rate-limit cases stubbed/deferred to Phase 5; construct with a generous/no-op limiter for this phase's tests, e.g. `new MintRateLimiter(clock, Integer.MAX_VALUE, Integer.MAX_VALUE, Integer.MAX_VALUE)` until Phase 5 lands the real class — **note:** this means `MintRateLimiter`'s class shell must exist before Task 4.2 compiles; either build Phase 5's class first as a thin shell then fill it in Phase 5, or reorder so 4.2 and 5.1/5.2 land together. Recommended: do Phase 5 (Task 5.1-5.2 only, the class itself) immediately before Task 4.2, then Task 4.2, then Phase 5's remaining rate-limit-specific tests (5.3) — see reordering note below.)

**Deps:** Phase 3 (needs `RequestContext.scope()`/`credentialHash()`, `TokenStore.SCOPE_DATA`, `NexusService` wiring point after sessions). **Success:** `DataTokenHandlerTest` green, `NexusService` route registered, `/v1/data-tokens/mint` reachable via a real jar smoke (`mvn -f service/pom.xml package -DskipTests` then curl — sanity only, not a gate).

---

## Phase 5 — Rate limiting on the mint endpoint

**Reordering note:** build the `MintRateLimiter` class (Task 5.1) BEFORE Task 4.2 so `DataTokenHandler` can depend on the real type from the start; the rate-limit-specific *behavioral* tests (Task 5.3, the 429/bucket-refund cases) land after Task 4.2 since they need `DataTokenHandler` wired to exercise via HTTP. Sequence: 5.1 → 5.2 → 4.1 → 4.2 → 5.3.

**Task 5.1 (test-first).** New file `service/src/test/java/dev/nexus/service/http/MintRateLimiterTest.java` (pure unit test, no Postgres — plain `MutableClock` inner class mirroring `AuthFilterTest`'s pattern, no shared utility extracted per existing per-file-fake convention). Cases:
- `tryAcquire` succeeds up to `tenantBurst` times immediately for one `(credential,tenant)`, then fails on the next call at the same instant.
- After advancing the clock by `60s / tenantSustainedPerMinute`, one more token is available.
- A DIFFERENT tenant with the SAME credential has its own independent tenant bucket (not exhausted by the first tenant's calls) but shares the SAME global bucket (so hammering N different tenants with one credential still hits the global cap).
- Global bucket: after `globalSustainedPerMinute` total acquisitions across ANY mix of tenants for one credential, the next call fails even though each individual tenant bucket still has headroom.
- Refund-on-partial-failure: when the tenant bucket succeeds but the global bucket is exhausted, `tryAcquire` returns `false` AND a subsequent call (same instant, same tenant) still sees the tenant bucket's token available (i.e., the tenant-side consumption was rolled back, not leaked) — this is the specific correctness property called out in the design decisions above.
- `fromEnv` reads `NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_BURST` / `NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE` / `NX_MINT_RATE_GLOBAL_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE`, defaulting to 5/1/10 when unset (use a small env-injection seam — a package-private overload taking a `Map<String,String>` or `Function<String,String>` env lookup, NOT `System.getenv` directly, so the test doesn't need real env mutation).
Run: `cd service && ./mvnw test -Dtest=MintRateLimiterTest` — FAIL (class doesn't exist).

**Task 5.2.** New file `service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/http/MintRateLimiter.java`: token-bucket per `(credentialHash, tenant)` keyed in a `ConcurrentHashMap`, plus one global bucket per `credentialHash`. `tryAcquire(String credentialHash, String tenant)`: consume tenant bucket first; on tenant success, consume global bucket; on global failure, refund the tenant bucket and return false; on tenant failure, return false without touching global. Buckets refill lazily on access based on elapsed time from the injected `Clock` (mirrors `TokenCache`'s clock-driven-not-scheduled-thread style). `fromEnv(Clock)` factory using `System.getenv`, delegating to the env-injectable package-private constructor for testability.
Run: `-Dtest=MintRateLimiterTest` — PASS.

**Task 5.3 (test-first, after 4.2 lands).** Extend `DataTokenHandlerTest.java`: a `scope=mint` bearer minting for the same `(credential,tenant)` more than `NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_BURST` (construct the test service with an explicit small `MintRateLimiter`, e.g. burst=2, injected via the non-`fromEnv` `NexusService` path — check whether `NexusService`'s constructor needs a test-only seam for this, or whether the test constructs `DataTokenHandler` directly against a live `TokenStore` rather than through `NexusService`'s auto-wiring; prefer the latter to avoid widening `NexusService`'s constructor surface) hits 429 on the 3rd call within the same instant; after advancing past the refill window, succeeds again.
Run: `-Dtest=DataTokenHandlerTest` — PASS.

**Deps:** 5.1/5.2 before 4.2; 5.3 after 4.2. **Success:** `MintRateLimiterTest` + `DataTokenHandlerTest` (rate-limit cases) green.

### >>> REVIEW GATE B (mandatory, dispatch both) <<<
`code-review-expert` then `substantive-critic` on the combined Phase 4-5 diff (`DataTokenHandler`, `MintRateLimiter`, `NexusService` wiring). This is the highest-risk batch (new network-reachable mint surface + new in-memory security control). Critic should specifically pressure-test: is the refund-on-partial-failure race-safe under the virtual-thread-per-request executor (two concurrent requests for the same credential+tenant racing tryAcquire)? Does a restart of the single engine instance reset rate-limit state to zero (acceptable per design's "single-instance engine => in-memory correct," but confirm no HA/multi-instance deployment currently exists that would silently multiply the effective limit)? Is the 400-vs-429-vs-403 status-code precedence order correct (e.g., does an over-ceiling TTL check happen before or after the rate-limit consume — should be BEFORE, so a malformed request doesn't consume a rate-limit token)? Fix Critical/High, re-run `./mvnw test -pl service` before proceeding.

---

## Phase 6 — CLI: `nx service token issue --scope mint`

**Task 6.1 (test-first).** Extend `tests/test_service_cmd.py`: `_FakeStore.issue_token` gains a `scope: str | None = None` param recording it; new test `test_issue_passes_scope_flag` invokes `nx service token issue --tenant t1 --scope mint` and asserts the fake store received `scope="mint"`; new test `test_issue_omits_scope_by_default` asserts `scope=None` when the flag isn't passed (preserves current default-'tenant' server behavior).
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_service_cmd.py -k scope` — FAIL.

**Task 6.2.** Edit `src/nexus/db/t2/http_token_store.py`: `issue_token(self, tenant, label=None, ttl_seconds=None, scope=None)` — add `"scope"` to the body dict only when not `None`.
Edit `src/nexus/commands/service_cmd.py`: add `--scope` option to `issue` (`type=click.Choice(["tenant", "mint"]), default=None`), pass through to `store.issue_token(tenant, label, ttl_seconds, scope)`.
Run: `uv run pytest tests/test_service_cmd.py -k scope` — PASS. Then `uv run pytest tests/test_service_cmd.py` (full file) — PASS (no regression).

**Task 6.3 (e2e, test-first).** New file `tests/db/test_data_token_mint_e2e.py` using the `_service_fixture.py` pattern (`jar_freshness_skip_reason`, `create_tenant_token`-style helpers): boot the real jar (skip loudly if stale/missing per existing convention), issue a `scope=mint` token via `nx service token issue --scope mint` (or the raw HTTP client directly — prefer the CLI path since it's the actual consumer surface), POST `/v1/data-tokens/mint`, assert 200 + the returned data token works against an ordinary route for its tenant. Non-vacuity: assert the response actually contains a token string of nonzero length AND that a follow-up authenticated call with it succeeds (not just "the mint call returned 200").
Run: `NEXUS_ENABLE_INTEGRATION=1 uv run pytest -m integration tests/db/test_data_token_mint_e2e.py` (requires the rebuilt jar — run `mvn -f service/pom.xml package -DskipTests` first if `jar_freshness_skip_reason` reports stale).

**Deps:** Phase 4 (endpoint must exist). **Success:** `test_service_cmd.py` full file green; e2e test green against a freshly built jar.

title: Tombstoned-vs-absent ambiguity: raw existence probe for rename/indexer/corpus collection_exists callers
description: RDR-156 P3 critic finding (gate bead nexus-70r3c.13). collection_exists() now reads the tombstone-filtered collection_vector_stats view (Decision 6 live semantics): a collection whose every chunk belongs to trashed documents reads as absent. Affected probes that need to distinguish 'tombstoned' from 'truly absent': collection_rename.py rename_collection_data_plane (reports 'not found' when the answer is 'trashed — restore first'), indexer.py:546-554 RDR-103 rename probes (trash-then-reindex would create a duplicate fresh collection beside the tombstoned one), corpus.py:402-419 name-resolution probes (silently skip tombstoned candidates). Fix shape: collection_exists_raw(name) on HttpVectorClient (or an include_tombstoned flag on /v1/vectors/collections which already lists raw DISTINCT names) + repoint the three probe sites + tests covering the trash-then-rename and trash-then-reindex paths. Cannot materialize until trash verbs ship and catalog-005 JAR is deployed (no deleted_at rows exist before then); doc notes at collection_rename.py mark the caveat in the meantime.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIXED cad6408a.

ONE CALLER WAS PROVABLY WRONG, not merely unclear: rename_collection_data_plane guarded its TARGET with `if t3_db.collection_exists(new)`, so a TOMBSTONED target read as FREE TO CLAIM. That rename path has no cross_model escape valve, so claiming it would land live data on top of dead rows sharing one name. Real corruption was defended in practice ONLY by the engine 409 — which is registry-based (catalog_collections), not chunk-based, i.e. a guard in a different layer checking a different thing. The Python false negative just produced a worse error path. Now refused unless truly ABSENT.

THE BEAD CAVEAT WAS STALE: "cannot materialize until trash verbs ship and catalog-005 JAR is deployed" — both HAD shipped. Tombstoning sets catalog_documents.deleted_at and never touches chunks_384/768/1024 (purge is separate and later), so the raw GET /v1/vectors/collections listing still names a tombstoned collection while collection_vector_stats does not. That raw listing IS the probe; NO engine change was needed.

OTHER CALLERS AUDITED ONE BY ONE, not swept:
- rename `old`: needed the distinction for its MESSAGE ("not found" hides "restore the trashed docs first").
- indexer RDR-103: wants LIVE semantics, correct as-is. NOT a collision bug — an ORPHAN-DEBT one: a tombstoned legacy candidate silently fell to "greenfield" and stayed un-migrated with no trace. Observability only.
- corpus resolution: wants LIVE semantics, not a bug at all; only the silence was worth fixing.

THREE STATES NOT A BOOLEAN FLAG: a raw=True param does not tell a reader which semantics was intended; PRESENT/TOMBSTONED/ABSENT does.

THE SUBTLE PART — the dispatch is isinstance, deliberately. A duck-typed hasattr check would silently succeed against MagicMock (auto-vivifies ANY attribute), handing back a bare Mock instead of a real state and corrupting every guard branching on it. The rename suite is full of such doubles — which is also why every existing rename test passed UNMODIFIED, the evidence the shim is inert for non-HTTP backends rather than merely untested. T3Database is exempt by construction (raw physical check, no tombstone concept).

Mutation-verified independently of the authoring agent, each mutation confirmed to land: reverting the `new` guard to PRESENT-only fails test_new_tombstoned_is_not_free_to_claim; duck-typing the dispatch fails the MagicMock trap test + 2 others.

31 new tests. Change-class sweep: 3773 passed, 0 failed. That sweep FIRST showed 4 failures + 13 errors, all of which were a STALE SERVICE JAR — caught by the session-start banner (nexus-zryqm) rather than misread as regressions.

title: Test-isolation leak: full unit suite SIGTERMs the production uid-scoped T2 daemon
description: Evidence (2026-06-11): production t2_daemon.log records t2_daemon_stop_requested signal_received=True at 13:28:08Z followed by t2_daemon_stopped — inside a full 'uv run pytest' window (13:24-13:36Z) on the dev machine. No operator sent that signal. Some test (suspects: daemon lifecycle suites or tests/_daemon_leak_guard.py reaper, cf. analysis-deep-orphan-resource-leak-nexus-t2-2026-06-05 'reaper format blindness') signals the REAL uid-scoped daemon instead of a tmp-config-dir one. Consequence: every full-suite run silently kills the developer's production T2 daemon; MCP clients then hit 'database is locked' / 'No T2 daemon discovery resolved' until ensure-running. Repro: note production t2 pid, run full suite, observe stop_requested in ~/.config/nexus/logs/t2_daemon.log. Fix direction: the offending test/guard must scope kills to pids it spawned (or to config-dir-derived discovery), never the uid-global daemon.
notes:
Second data point (2026-06-11 13:46Z): a FRESH daemon spawned by 'nx daemon t2 ensure-running' (pid 81212, started 13:46:28) received SIGTERM at 13:46:30 — 1.5s after start, AFTER the full-suite window ended (13:36Z). So the killer is not (only) my pytest run; something else on the box is signalling uid-scoped T2 daemons (suspect: the other Claude instance's RDR-151 daemon-arc test activity, or a stale reaper). Subsequent ensure-running at ~13:50Z converged and stayed up. The t2_daemon.log breadcrumbs (signal_received=True) are what made both kills visible — same observability pattern nexus-ovbr7 just extended to storage-service/t3.

3rd+4th data points (2026-06-11 19:14-19:16Z): freshly-spawned storage-service JAR pid 17473 SIGTERM'd (exit 143) BEFORE /health ready (supervisor crash backstop captured the full traceback — observability win), AND the T2 daemon stopped at 19:16:44 in the same window. Both coincide with the other instance resuming activity. Suspect list now firmly: a session-start/test-run cleanup sweep in a sibling instance reaping uid-scoped daemons as 'orphans' (tests/_daemon_leak_guard.py reaper-format-blindness class per analysis-deep-orphan-resource-leak-nexus-t2-2026-06-05). The kill signature is consistent: SIGTERM to JUST-SPAWNED daemons (1.5s-4s after start).

MECHANISM DECODED (2026-06-11 20:55Z, 5th data point): supervisor log shows the full kill shape — clean supervisor_exit stop_requested=True at 13:55:31, NEW supervisor started 13:55:36 (not by this session), its 2.5s-old JAR SIGTERM'd (exit 143) mid-startup at 13:55:39. That is TWO ACTORS RACING stop/start cycles on the shared singleton service: the sibling instance bounces (stop, start, stop again) while this session operates. NOT a test reaper for the service kills (tests/_daemon_leak_guard.py is correctly tmp-config-scoped + cmdline-guarded; tests/db/test_service_endpoint_discovery.py is isolated). The earlier T2-daemon kills during full-suite windows may still have a separate test-leak mechanism — keep both hypotheses but the service-bounce class is now proven. FIX SHAPE: sibling instances must use ensure-running semantics for routine ops (non-foreground 'service start' is already idempotent — no-ops on a live lease); explicit stop+start cycles on shared singletons need cross-instance coordination, or the supervisor needs a start-grace period where a stop request queues instead of killing a mid-startup JAR.

title: RDR-156: Vector-Store Capability Leverage — schema-enforced integrity, soft delete, combined-query unification over RDR-155 pgvector chunk tables
description:
Same deliberate capability-selection pass RDR-154 made over the RDR-152 schema, scoped to the RDR-155 vector tables (nexus.chunks_384/768/1024) — unaudited new scope (RDR-154 gate predates vectors-001). Co-residence of vectors + governing metadata in one Postgres makes combined queries possible and integrity schema-enforceable. Discipline: declarative FK > function > view > trigger-only-if-app-unfixable; ZERO new triggers in this RDR. Six phases P0-P5, sequential; gate per phase folds /conexus:phase-review-gate + stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic + test-validator).

KEY CROSS-RDR SEQUENCING: (1) P0 VALIDATE CONSTRAINT changeset is a SEPARATE bead world-blocked on RDR-153 data migration (epic nexus-dfwh0) completing with summary.total_failed==0 — bead-ready, HOLD, mirrors RDR-155 P4b. (2) P1 soft delete lands BEFORE the view set so P2/P3 views ship tombstone-filtered from day one. (3) P5 hybrid_search world-blocked on conexus xr7.8.9 parity go-live gate (external — NOT a nexus bead). (4) RDR-154's 16 beads (nexus-4ft44) are unstarted siblings on the same schema — note potential changeset-ordering coordination, do NOT merge the arcs.

Verified live constraints (T2 nexus_rdr/156-research-findings, PG16+pgvector 0.8.2, 98k chunks): query vector MUST be a function argument not join-sourced (2ms vs 340ms HNSW vs seq); narrow-collection filtered HNSW silently under-returns at hnsw.max_scan_tuples ceiling (2 of LIMIT 10) — combined-query parity fixtures MUST include a narrow-collection exact-recall ==N assertion. RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-156-vector-store-capability-leverage.md (accepted 2026-06-10, gate PASSED 0C/0S). On acceptance RDR-106 flips superseded-by: RDR-156.

title: JAR lifecycle for installed users: well-known JAR location + 'nx daemon service install-jar' + /version endpoint with app+schema version handshake
description: (a) JAR auto-discovery resolves service/target relative to the INSTALLED package root (uv tools dir) — impossible for pip/uv-installed users (hit 2026-06-10, workaround --jar). Design: well-known location ~/.config/nexus/service/nexus-service.jar; 'nx daemon service install-jar <path|--from-repo>' copies a built JAR there and records provenance (version, sha256, build date) in a sidecar; supervisor discovery order = --jar > well-known location > repo-relative (dev convenience) > fail with actionable build instructions. (b) VERSION SKEW (simulated, not hit): no handshake exists between nx client, JAR app version, and Liquibase schema version. Old JAR + newer schema (or new JAR self-applying Liquibase while older JAR instances run) fails undiagnosably. Service /version endpoint returns {app_version, schema_changelog_id}; nx clients log/warn on mismatch with the installed nx version; supervisor refuses to start a JAR older than the schema it would connect to. title: nx daemon service start: three first-run operational failures (jar discovery, devnull logs, missing CREATE EXTENSION in init --service)
description: Found during the RDR-155 production migration run (2026-06-10), first-ever production start of the storage service via installed nx 5.10.6. Three distinct defects, each of which made the next one harder to diagnose: (1) JAR auto-discovery resolves service/target relative to the INSTALLED package root (~/.local/share/uv/tools/conexus/lib/python3.12/service/target) instead of a repo root or cwd — installed-tool users can never auto-discover; --jar is mandatory in practice. (2) StorageServiceSupervisor._spawn_service sends JAR stdout/stderr to subprocess.DEVNULL — when the JVM exits pre-/health the only message is 'exited with code 1, check service logs' but there ARE no service logs; should tee to ~/.config/nexus/logs/storage_service.log. (3) nx init --service provisions cluster+db+roles but does NOT run CREATE EXTENSION vector as the cluster superuser; the service's Liquibase vectors-001 then fails with 'permission denied to create extension' because nexus_admin is not superuser. Manual fix applied: psql -p 53649 -d nexus -c 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector'. init --service should create the extension at provision time (it owns the only superuser context). Also: the 60s readiness timeout in background mode swallows all three errors — only --foreground surfaces them.
notes:
4th defect found same run (2026-06-10): supervisor does not plumb the Voyage API key — Java service reads NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY and SILENTLY falls back to local ONNX MiniLM (384-dim) when absent (Main.java:111, 'Voyage when NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is present, ONNX otherwise/fallback'). On the migration run this produced HTTP 400 dim-mismatch failures for every voyage-* collection (PgVectorRepository MODEL_DIMS guard caught it — zero contaminated rows, fail-loud worked). But the SILENT fallback itself violates the no-silent-fallbacks-for-correctness rule: a same-dim wrong-model case would NOT be caught by the dim guard. nx daemon service start should (a) source the Voyage key from nexus config/.env and pass it to the JAR, (b) the service should log loudly (or refuse voyage-token collections) when running in ONNX-fallback mode. Workaround used: export NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY from repo .env before nx daemon service start.

4th silent death (2026-06-11 ~05:30 PT): supervisor+JAR found dead with lease file gone between session handoff (~04:30, verified live) and 05:35; PG survived (18h uptime). No supervisor log dir exists under ~/.config/nexus/ — death cause undiagnosable, again. Recovery this time also surfaced the JAR-provenance gap: previous session ran from a repo-target build, never installed to the well-known location, so 'nx daemon service start' failed with no-JAR after the death. Fixed by rebuilding from develop + install-jar (sha256 4fb17bb810ac59b0…, 65 changesets); well-known location now populated so restarts are self-contained.

Item 2 (supervisor DEVNULLs JAR logs) FIXED by nexus-ovbr7 / PR #1163 (2026-06-11): jar -> logs/storage_service_jar.log, supervisor -> logs/storage_service.log breadcrumbs + crash backstop, detached spawn -> storage_service.crash.log, exit codes logged, status surfaces paths. Remaining items here: jar discovery UX (largely addressed by pebfx.4 install-jar) and missing CREATE EXTENSION in init --service.

title: [bug] CCE embed-parity: corpus[1] cosine 0.999995 drifts past the 1e-9 bit-exact threshold (Seam B)
description: tests/db/test_embed_parity.py::test_cce_parity fails: CCE (voyage-context-3 contextualized) corpus[1] cosine=0.9999950 (diff 5e-06, float32_bit_exact=False, max_ulp_diff=13.7M) vs threshold 1e-9. corpus[0] is bit-exact (1.0). The drift is ORDERS below the test's own named CCE failure modes (input_type mismatch ~0.95, truncation omission ~0.99995, batch-context contamination ~0.9996), so it is NOT a semantic wiring bug — likely float32(JVM)-vs-float64(Python) serialization on one batched text, or Voyage CCE API non-determinism across the two separate API calls (Python chromadb vs JVM CceEmbedder). PRE-EXISTING (no session change touches CceEmbedder/EmbedderRouter); previously MASKED because the fixture under-provisioned svc_parity so the service crashed at startup-migration before reaching the assertion (fixed: GRANT CREATE on public/nexus/db). RDR-152 Phase 3 Seam B. Decide: relax the CCE-only threshold to a calibrated tolerance, or root-cause the per-text drift (compare raw JVM vs Python CCE vectors for corpus[1], check batch ordering/float serialization). ONNX + Voyage-standard parity are bit-exact (cosine 1.0).
close_reason: ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (PR #1144). Decisive: voyage-context-3 CCE is non-deterministic across network sessions — same text embedded 4x drifts 2.6e-4..3.7e-4 cosine (empirical). The JVM CceEmbedder is correct (identical API/params to Python _cce_embed); the 1e-9 bit-exact threshold is unattainable for CCE because API call-to-call variance exceeds it (and exceeds the named truncation/contamination failure modes). Fix: CCE-only cosine_threshold=1e-3 (clears the 3.7e-4 noise floor with margin, still catches gross wiring ≈0.95), drop bit-exact ULP gate for CCE. voyage-code-3 standard path verified deterministic (4 calls bit-exact); earlier flake was transient. All 4 parity tests green. Optional follow-up: replace output-vector comparison with request-level structural assertions (model/input_type/truncation/batching) so fine drift below the API noise floor is verified deterministically.

title: aspect --validate-sample feeds operator_verify raw file bytes, not indexed chunk text → false negatives on PDFs (esp. OCR'd/scanned)
description:
nx enrich aspects --validate-sample samples N% of freshly-extracted AspectRecords and runs operator_verify(claim=aspects, evidence=document text) to catch hallucination. But the evidence it passes is wrong: it reads the raw source file off disk and hands those bytes to the verifier. For PDFs (FlateDecode-compressed content streams; for scanned docs, CCITTFax image objects + an invisible OCR text layer) read_text() yields binary/object-structure garbage, NOT the extracted prose. The aspect EXTRACTOR, by contrast, consumes the indexed T3 chunk text (Docling/MinerU/OCR output reassembled via the catalog document_chunks manifest). So the validator verifies the claim against different evidence than the extractor saw, producing spurious disagreements while the extraction is actually correct.

DISCOVERED 2026-06-09 during 'nx enrich aspects knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1' (39 extracted, 1 validation disagreement). The flagged doc — 'POINTERLESS IMPLEMENTATION OF HIERARCHICAL SIMPLICIAL MESHES…' (ABBYY FineReader 8.0 OCR'd scan) — had a CORRECT, well-grounded extraction (verified: T3 chunks contain 'Maubach simplex bisection', the permutation formula, barycentric-coordinate search; the 708MB-vs-222MB and 6072-vs-14492 figures trace to real chunk text). operator_verify's own reason admits it only saw 'CCITTFaxDecode image' + 'FlateDecode Form XObjects' + 'XMP metadata' — i.e. it inspected the raw PDF binary, not the OCR text layer. False negative.

IMPACT: the --validate-sample signal is unreliable for any PDF-sourced collection (DEVONthink imports, knowledge__*-papers). Born-digital PDFs may occasionally pass only because stray plaintext metadata happens to ground enough of the claim; scanned/OCR'd PDFs reliably false-fail. This validator runs on the same path nexus-lxy5n's 'nx dt index --aspects' would invoke.
design: Evidence for operator_verify must come from the SAME source the extractor used: the indexed T3 chunk text reassembled via the catalog document_chunks manifest (the _doc_id_resolver / chunk-reassembly reader at src/nexus/commands/enrich.py:30-69, also used by the aspect extractor), NOT Path(source_path).read_text(). Replace the read_text() block at enrich.py:1326-1330 in _run_validation_sample with a call that hydrates the document's chunks (store_get_many over the manifest chashes, position-ordered) and concatenates them, then truncate to the existing [:50000] cap. Keep the OSError->errored branch but it should now key off 'no chunks for this doc' (empty reassembly) rather than file-read failure.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Validator evidence is the reassembled indexed chunk text, not raw file bytes. (b) Regression test: an OCR'd/scanned-style PDF fixture whose on-disk bytes are non-textual but whose indexed chunks contain the prose → operator_verify receives the prose and the correct extraction VERIFIES (no false disagreement). (c) A genuinely-hallucinated aspect (claim text absent from chunks) still produces a disagreement (true positive preserved). (d) A doc with zero indexed chunks routes to the errored/skip branch, not a silent pass. Deterministic: fixture catalog + EphemeralClient, stub operator_verify's claude_dispatch.
close_reason: validate-sample now verifies against reassembled T3 chunk text via read_indexed_text (same evidence the extractor saw), not raw file bytes; no raw-bytes fallback; all-errored surfaced loudly. Commit 9817836f.

title: nx_answer plan-miss: inject retrieved plans as few-shot examples into inline planner (CacheRAG R1)
description: On a plan MISS, nx_answer's inline planner prompt is zero-shot. CacheRAG (Sun & Chen, HKUST) shows that injecting top-k similar historical plans as few-shot examples into the LLM planner is the single highest-leverage cache mechanism (ablation: ~4.3% accuracy / ~5.5% truthfulness lift from this alone). Nexus already stores successful plans and can retrieve them by similarity (plan_match); it simply never feeds them to the planner on a miss. This bead closes that gap.
design: Add a low-threshold (~0.25, below the 0.40 execution gate) plan_match call inside the plan-miss path, and append the matched plan_json(s) to the inline planner prompt as structural few-shot examples. Goal is structural guidance (which tools exist, how steps chain), not identity matching - hence the lower threshold than execution.
acceptance_criteria: On plan-miss, the inline planner prompt contains 1-2 retrieved similar plans as examples when any clear the few-shot threshold; zero matches degrades gracefully to today's zero-shot prompt; prompt growth is bounded (n<=2, plan_json truncated). Tests cover: (a) miss-with-matches injects examples, (b) miss-with-no-matches falls back to zero-shot unchanged, (c) prompt-length bound enforced.
notes:
## CacheRAG R1 — few-shot plan injection on plan-miss

Source: research synthesis "CacheRAG vs nexus plan-library" (T3 `knowledge`).
Paper: knowledge__dt-papers, "CacheRAG: A Semantic Caching System for RAG in KGQA"
(Sun & Chen, HKUST). Mechanism = §4.2 "cache retrieval module provides useful examples".

### What CacheRAG does that we don't
CacheRAG injects top-k similar historical plans as FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES into the LLM
planner on every query, including misses. Ablation ("w/o cache"): -4.3% accuracy,
-5.5% truthfulness. We do cache-execute (plan hit) but our plan-MISS planner is
zero-shot.

### Exact code geography (verified 2026-06-09)
- Gate + match call: src/nexus/mcp/core.py:3936-3949
  `_plan_match(question, library=db.plans, cache=cache, dimensions=..., 
   scope_preference=scope, min_confidence=effective_min_confidence, n=5)`
  Default gate threshold _PLAN_MATCH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (=0.40, matcher.py:236).
- Hit test: core.py:3953-3955 `_nx_answer_match_is_hit(matches[0].confidence, ...)`.
- Miss path: core.py:3956-3962 calls `_nx_answer_plan_miss(question, scope=, max_steps=)`.
- Planner prompt assembly: `_nx_answer_plan_miss`, core.py:3616-3657. The prompt today =
  decompose-instruction + corpus_hint + corpus_names_hint + _PLANNER_TOOL_REFERENCE
  (core.py:3259) + output-format line. NO plan examples anywhere.
- Matcher filters below threshold: matcher.py:312 `if confidence < min_confidence: continue`.

### KEY SUBTLETY — why "just reuse the matches we already have" doesn't work
The gate's plan_match at core.py:3940 already passes min_confidence=0.40, and
matcher.py:312 drops everything below that. So when we reach the miss path, `matches`
is empty (or contains only sub-threshold entries that failed the hit test). The
0.25-0.40 "structurally similar but not identical" band that makes the BEST few-shot
material has already been filtered OUT. Two clean options:

  Option A (preferred): in the miss branch, do a SECOND plan_match with a lower
  few-shot threshold (~0.25, < the 0.40 exec gate), n=3, reusing the same `cache`
  and `db.plans` (still in scope via _t2_ctx). Pass results into _nx_answer_plan_miss.
  Rationale: keeps the exec gate strict (0.40) while sourcing loose structural
  examples separately. Matches CacheRAG's "moderate-similarity → few-shot" tier.

  Option B: lower the single match call's min_confidence to ~0.25 and gate the HIT
  decision separately on matches[0].confidence >= 0.40. One match call, but couples
  two concerns (exec gate vs few-shot floor) and changes existing match_metrics
  semantics + telemetry. Riskier; only if perf of a 2nd match matters (it shouldn't —
  T1 cosine cache, sub-ms).

Go with A unless profiling says otherwise.

### Implementation sketch (Option A)
1. Add `few_shot_plans: list[Match] | None = None` param to `_nx_answer_plan_miss`.
2. In the miss branch (core.py ~3961), before calling, run:
     fewshot = _plan_match(question, library=db.plans, cache=cache,
                           dimensions=dimensions, scope_preference=scope,
                           min_confidence=_PLAN_FEWSHOT_MIN_CONFIDENCE, n=3)
   (need _t2_ctx open here; the existing miss branch is OUTSIDE the `with` block at
   3938 — reopen or restructure so cache/db are available. Check scope carefully.)
3. In _nx_answer_plan_miss, if few_shot_plans: build an examples block from each
   match's stored plan_json (Match carries the plan; confirm field name on the Match
   dataclass, nexus.plans.match.Match). Append between corpus_names_hint and
   _PLANNER_TOOL_REFERENCE.
4. BOUND the prompt: n<=2 actually injected, truncate each plan_json to ~400 chars,
   strip outcome_notes. Few-shot is structural guidance, not a transcript.
5. Zero matches → omit the block entirely → today's exact zero-shot prompt (no regression).

### New constant
`_PLAN_FEWSHOT_MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.25` near _PLAN_MATCH_MIN_CONFIDENCE in core.py.

### Tests (tests/mcp/ — find the existing nx_answer/plan-miss test module first)
- miss WITH sub-threshold matches in [0.25,0.40) → planner prompt contains example block.
- miss WITH no matches >=0.25 → prompt byte-identical to current zero-shot (lock with ==).
- prompt-length bound: >2 candidates → exactly 2 injected; long plan_json truncated to cap.
- exec gate unchanged: a >=0.40 match still HITS and never reaches the planner.
  (Guards against Option-A regressions to the gate.)
Deterministic: seed/stub claude_dispatch; assert on the PROMPT passed to it, not on
model output. plan_match is local T1 cosine — no network.

### Scope / non-goals
- R2 (MMR diversity over the few-shot set) and R3 (auto-infer dimensions at match time)
  are SEPARATE follow-on beads. This bead is just the injection. Don't pull them in.
- Do NOT add answer-level caching (synthesis R4 — wrong for an evolving KB).

### Effort
~15-25 LOC core + ~4 tests. Single file (core.py) + one test file. No schema, no migration.
close_reason: On plan miss, nx_answer injects the gate's near-miss matches as few-shot exemplars into the inline planner (CacheRAG R1). _format_plan_few_shot: <=3 steps-only examples, cosine floor >=0.25, FTS5 excluded, description sanitized, examples-before-question. Stacked review: similarity-floor + injection-sanitization + ordering-test added. Full suite green 11361. Commit 27337222.

title: phase-review-gate: recognise '## Implementation Plan' (and synonyms), not only '### Approach'
description:
The phase-review-gate preamble (nx rdr preamble phase-review-gate -- <id> --phase <N>) hard-requires a §Approach heading to cross-walk phase items against closing beads. Matcher lives in src/nexus/commands/rdr.py. RDRs that structure phased work under '## Implementation Plan' (e.g. conexus RDR-001) make the gate error out with 'No ### Approach section found in this RDR', so the gate cannot run at the phase boundary and the cross-walk must be done by hand — defeating the silent-scope-reduction guard the gate exists to provide.

Repro: nx rdr preamble phase-review-gate -- rdr-001 --phase 7 against an RDR whose phase items live under '## Implementation Plan' -> ERROR No ### Approach section found.

Fix options (decide in nexus): (a) widen the heading matcher to also accept 'Implementation Plan' and likely synonyms ('Plan', 'Phases'), at any heading level (## or ###); (b) make the recognised heading configurable; (c) normalise RDR templates to a canonical heading and lint for it. Lowest-friction is (a) — accept a small set of phase-structure headings case-insensitively at ## or ### level. Add a regression test in tests/test_rdr_preamble.py covering an '## Implementation Plan' RDR for both Pass 1 (enumerate) and Pass 2 (validate evidence).

Context: surfaced closing conexus RDR-001 Phase 7 (conexus-xr7.7) 2026-06-08; cross-walk was done manually instead. Cross-repo report — filed from conexus session.
close_reason: Widened phase-review-gate heading matcher to accept Approach/Implementation Plan/Phases/Plan at ##/###/#### case-insensitively; bare Plan whole-heading-anchored. Commit c32b7a25.

title: RDR-152: prod-copy.sh count verification silently SKIPs (psql not found via sandbox_helper) — hollow 'all passed'
description: prod-copy.sh resolves PSQL_BIN via 'uv run python sandbox_helper.py pg-bin psql' which returned empty, so every verify_pg_count_* printed 'SKIP <table> (psql not found)' and the run reported 'All verifications passed' with exit 0 despite never checking a single T2 table count against prod. comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
UPSTREAM RE-CHECK 2026-06-12: the blocking premise is now STALE.

The bead was filed (2026-06-07) on "currently only 3.18.2 in community repo".
The oracle/graalvm-reachability-metadata repo now carries an org.jooq/jooq
metadata-version 3.20.0 entry with tested-versions 3.20.0 -> 3.21.5, which

class-init NPE (DefaultDataType static-init under --initialize-at-run-time=org.jooq
cascading to a LocatorImpl heap error), not a missing-reflection error.
Reachability metadata registers reflection/resources; it does not by itself change
class-initialization-time partial-evaluation. So the metadata clears the upstream
gate but a native-image build spike is still required to confirm it resolves the
NPE (it may still need a Substitution/Feature or an explicit
--initialize-at-build-time exclusion for the jOOQ DataType statics).

(jlink ships per RDR-152 decision 5). Recommend: time-box a native-image build

SPIKE RESULT (2026-06-12): the jOOQ DefaultDataType blocker is RESOLVED.

Changes (branch spike/nexus-lp2qo-jooq-graal-metadata, service/pom.xml):
- native-build-tools 0.10.4 -> 1.1.2 (bundles org.jooq/jooq/3.20.0
