- Toolchain: the 3.20.0 metadata uses GraalVM's unified reachability-metadata
  SCHEMA, which GraalVM 25.0.1 rejects ("your installation does not provide
  reachability-metadata schema"). Installed Oracle GraalVM 25.0.3 and pointed
  BOTH GRAALVM_HOME and JAVA_HOME at it (the native-maven-plugin detects via
  GRAALVM_HOME, which the session pinned to 25.0.1 — that was a false-negative
  on the first 25.0.3 attempt).

EVIDENCE: with 25.0.3 + 3.20.0 metadata, native-image runs the full analysis
([2/8] Performing analysis ... [7/8] Laying out methods) with NO DefaultDataType
heap error and NO jOOQ NPE. The original build-time LocatorImpl heap error is
gone. jOOQ is no longer the blocker.

NEW blocker (different class, general native bring-up, NOT jOOQ):
[7/8] Error: Type not found during analysis:
liquibase.integration.commandline.LiquibaseCommandLine.
Mechanism mirrors the old jooq issue: the 1.1.2 community metadata bundle now
registers liquibase-core reflection (incl. the CLI class), but picocli is an
optional dep of liquibase-core and is NOT on our runtime classpath, so
LiquibaseCommandLine (picocli-typed fields) fails to link. The service uses
liquibase via the Java API (SchemaMigrator), not the CLI. Fix options: add
info.picocli:picocli as a dep (canonical), or exclude liquibase-core from the
metadata repo (mirrors the prior jooq exclusion). Trying picocli next.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SPIKE COMPLETE (2026-06-12) — VERDICT: the parked jOOQ blocker is RESOLVED;
native-image now stops on general service bring-up (liquibase runtime reflection),
NOT on jOOQ. Stopping the spike here: question answered.

== PRIMARY FINDING (the reason this bead existed) ==
jOOQ 3.20.11 DefaultDataType build-time heap/static-init NPE is GONE. With:
  - native-build-tools 0.10.4 -> 1.1.2 (bundles org.jooq/jooq/3.20.0
    reachability-metadata.json, tested 3.20.0-3.21.5 -> covers 3.20.11),
  - jOOQ un-excluded from <metadataRepository>, --initialize-at-run-time=org.jooq
    workaround removed,
  - GraalVM 25.0.1 -> 25.0.3 (the 3.20.0 metadata uses the unified
    reachability-metadata SCHEMA that 25.0.1 rejects; plugin detects GraalVM via
    GRAALVM_HOME, which the shell pinned to 25.0.1 — must set BOTH GRAALVM_HOME
    and JAVA_HOME to 25.0.3),
native-image completes the FULL [1/8..8/8] pipeline and produces a 127MB arm64
binary. At runtime the binary boots, Hikari connects, jOOQ classes initialize
with NO DefaultDataType NPE. jOOQ is conclusively no longer the blocker.

== REMAINING BLOCKERS (general native bring-up, each a DIFFERENT class) ==
Peeled in order, all post-jOOQ:
1. LiquibaseCommandLine "Type not found" — FIXED by adding info.picocli:picocli
   (optional dep of liquibase-core; community metadata forces the CLI class
   reachable). 
2. db/changelog/*.xml not bundled — FIXED: resource-config pattern
   db/changelog/.*\.xml.
3. liquibase XSDs not bundled (blocked remote lookup, secureParsing=true) —
   FIXED: resource-config pattern www.liquibase.org/xml/ns/dbchangelog/.*\.xsd.
4. *** CURRENT WALL *** MissingReflectionRegistrationError invoking
   liquibase.change.AbstractSQLChange.setSplitStatements. The community
   liquibase-core/4.27.0 metadata IS applied (confirmed in
   -H:ConfigurationFileDirectories) and DOES name setSplitStatements, but the
   runtime INVOKE still fails — registration is for lookup on subclasses, not
   invoke on the declaring AbstractSQLChange. This is the known-hard liquibase-
   on-native reflection-completeness gap. Pinning liquibase 4.29.2 -> 4.29.0
   (an exact tested-version) did NOT clear it.

== RECOMMENDED PATH (own scoped bead, not this spike) ==
Two viable routes for #4:
  A. native-image TRACING AGENT: run the service on the JVM under
     -agentlib:native-image-agent=config-merge-dir=... against a representative
     migrate+query+embed workload, capture exact reflection/resource/proxy
     metadata, commit it, rebuild. Exhaustive; also captures any onnxruntime /
     djl-tokenizers / HTTP gaps in one pass. This is the canonical fix.
  B. ARCHITECTURAL: do NOT run liquibase inside the native image. Migrations
     already run fine on the jlink/JVM leg; a native serving binary could skip
     embedded SchemaMigrator (migrate via jlink or a separate `migrate` step)
     and only serve the jOOQ query path — the part now proven native-clean.
     Smaller native surface, sidesteps liquibase-native entirely.

== PREREQUISITES this spike surfaced (beyond the bead's assumptions) ==
- GraalVM 25.0.3+ REQUIRED (25.0.1 rejects the new metadata schema). CI's
  Linux native job (S0.4 C2, still unbuilt) must provision 25.0.3+.
- The build is macOS/arm64 here; prod native is Linux — re-verify on Linux.

jlink remains the shipping path (RDR-152 decision 5). native-image is still
opt-in (-Pnative) and NOT mergeable until #4 + a Linux CI job land. Spike work
preserved on branch spike/nexus-lp2qo-jooq-graal-metadata (NOT merged).

title: reinstall-tool.sh: guard against installing a tree version older than the T2 DB stamp
description: Bare scripts/reinstall-tool.sh defaults to SOURCE=. (local tree). If the tree's pyproject version trails the version stamped in memory.db (_nexus_version.cli_version), the install silently downgrades the client below the DB schema stamp and the T2 daemon fail-closes on the RDR-120/149 handshake. This was the mechanism behind a live T2 lockout (client 5.10.5 vs DB-stamp 5.10.6, and the symmetric 5.10.3-tree trap). Add a preflight downgrade guard: when SOURCE=. and pyproject version < DB stamp, refuse with remediation (install from PyPI, or bump the tree). PyPI installs unaffected; equal/newer versions pass.
close_reason: declined — no downgrade guard wanted

title: Structurally enforce single-writer: audit all write paths go via the daemon + nx CLI never opens a direct DB connection (Bedrock-style; from web research)
description: From web research (T3: research-sqlite-daemon-concurrency-architectures-2026-06-05). nexus is Bedrock-shaped but enforces single-writer by CONVENTION; Bedrock disabled POSIX locks to enforce structurally. The recurring database-is-locked bug class (aspect_worker w/ own conns; multi-daemon T2-write cascade nexus-x47yx) is incomplete daemon-fronting. SCOPE: (1) audit every SQLite write path in the codebase and confirm it routes through the T2 daemon, not a direct connection; (2) ensure one-shot nx CLI invocations never open a direct write connection (busy_timeout is per-process — a CLI one-shot gets no protection); (3) add a loud guard/test that fails if a non-daemon process opens the DB for write. Related: RDR-151 (epic nexus-5kcsq), RDR-149 service_registry primitive, nexus-xmohw root cause, nexus-x47yx. COORDINATE: do not claim in parallel with in-flight nexus-8voni/nexus-th4dh; this is follow-on architectural hardening, sequence after Phase 1 peg fix.
close_reason: Superseded by RDR-152 (Postgres + Java service retires the SQLite single-writer daemon these patch; see nexus-u2vmv). RDR-151 patches a subsystem being deleted — closing as superseded rather than gating a dead RDR. Per user 2026-06-13.

title: RDR-151 P2.1: cooperative bounded write retry/backoff replacing SQLite default busy-handler spin (Gap 5)
description:
RDR-151 Phase 2, Gap 5 / RC-beta (the database-is-locked burn). Capture B showed a thread-pool thread parked in sqlite3BtreeBeginTrans -> btreeInvokeBusyHandler -> sqlite3OsSleep (a write that could not acquire the WAL writer lock) while a second thread queued on the store's Python rlock. Cleared within 3s (transient, not deadlock). reclaim_stale bounds its own retry (3 attempts, sleeps (0.1,0.5), aspect_extraction_queue.py:489-491), but SERVE-PATH writes fall back on SQLite's DEFAULT busy handler, which SPINS in OsSleep rather than yielding. This is the intra-daemon source of T2ClientError(database is locked) (nexus-00en9), amplified when Gaps 3/4 let a second daemon coexist.

LINEAGE: this is the RDR-129 P3 / B3 deferral (nexus-izpcb — the single internal write lock that would make serving genuinely contention-free). RDR-129 shipped B1 (busy_timeout 5000->30000) + B2 (bounded dispatch retry) but DEFERRED B3. Gap 5 is that deferred item now observationally confirmed firing in production. NOT a contradiction of RDR-129-as-closed.

FIX DIRECTION (RDR §Decision item 4): replace serve-path reliance on SQLite's spinning default busy handler with a COOPERATIVE bounded retry+backoff (mirroring reclaim_stale's pattern), OR a single serialized in-daemon writer (one connection, one queue). RDR §Open Questions asks whether the single serialized writer is the right long-term answer — make this design call with sequentialthinking; the cooperative-retry is the lower-risk landing if the serialized-writer is larger than Phase 2 warrants.

RF-4 (RDR §Research Findings, OPEN): WHICH write stalls is not yet known (sample cannot yield SQL text). Add a transient op-label log at the _invoke_with_lock_retry dispatch site (t2_daemon.py:1343-1377) under a controlled restart to discriminate serve-path write vs 30s reclaim vs stored_schema_version connection; then REMOVE the log (RDR §Approach Phase 2).

FILES: src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py _invoke_with_lock_retry (1343-1377); src/nexus/db/t2/ store write paths.

TDD: test-first, EXACT-COUNT regression test (RDR §Approach Phase 2: 'Exact-count regression tests for each'). Assert retry attempt count, backoff bounds, and no unbounded spin under simulated WAL writer-lock contention. Use mem:feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression.

Cross-ref: nexus-izpcb (RDR-129 B3) lineage bead. Context: RDR-151 §Decision item 4, §Research Findings RF-4/RF-5, §Open Questions.
notes: ANCHOR CORRECTED by audit+enrich (2026-06-05): the original anchor _invoke_with_lock_retry (t2_daemon.py:1343-1377) is WRONG — that is already the RDR-129 B2 cooperative async retry wrapper. ROOT CAUSE of RC-beta (capture B btreeInvokeBusyHandler->sqlite3OsSleep): PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000 (30s in-C) set at the per-store connection-open sites makes SQLite spin-sleep INSIDE the C extension on the dispatch thread, defeating the Python cooperative retry layered above it. FIX: drop the long in-C busy_timeout (toward 0/small) so SQLITE_BUSY fails fast to the Python async retry instead of spin-sleeping in C. Target sites: src/nexus/db/t2/_tuning.py:19 (SERVING_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=30000); __init__.py:224/484/594; memory_store.py:264-270; telemetry.py:130; document_aspects.py:203; catalog.py:333; catalog_taxonomy.py:243; document_highlights.py:100; aspect_extraction_queue.py:182-191. memory_store.py:407/548 already demos the fast-fail pattern (_ACCESS_TRACK_BUSY_MS). title: T3 supervisor stop() never calls mark_shutting_down → zero-daemon window analog of T2 RDR-151 Gap 3
description: T3Supervisor.stop() (src/nexus/daemon/t3_daemon.py:445) calls self._registry.relinquish(rec) but never self._registry.mark_shutting_down(rec). mark_shutting_down exists (service_registry.py:328) and is ONLY called from t1_lease.py:277 — neither T2 (RDR-151 Gap 3) nor T3 calls it. This is the structural analog of RDR-151 Gap 3 for the T3 tier: during stop()'s drain the lease still reads 'live' (TTL 3.0s) while the supervisor tears down, so a concurrent ensure-running can resolve an apparently-live endpoint, fail to connect, and treat it as a crash. T3 supervisor is synchronous (time.sleep loop, run_t3_supervisor t3_daemon.py:480-516), not asyncio, so the window may be narrower than T2's, but the gap is the same. RDR-149 (closed) owns the shared lifecycle primitive but never scoped mark_shutting_down specifically, so this T3 gap is currently unowned. Surfaced by the RDR-151 substantive-critic (2026-06-05). Fix T2 in RDR-151 Gap 3; fix T3 here (or fold the mark_shutting_down call into a shared supervisor stop path so all tiers get it, honoring the RDR-149 'lands in the shared primitive' invariant).

title: T2 daemon stop() doesn't mark_shutting_down + doesn't force-close client transports → ensure-running-during-drain zero-daemon window + every stop takes full socket-teardown timeout
description:
Found during 5.10.1 local shakeout 2026-06-05. Two coupled stop()-path hygiene gaps (both pre-existing, NOT 5.10.1 regressions; 64w50-adjacent):

1. ensure-running-during-drain zero-daemon window: T2Daemon.stop() (src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py) does NOT call ServiceRegistry.mark_shutting_down (the method exists at service_registry.py:328 but is unused). So during the bounded ~5s socket-teardown drain after SIGTERM, the lease stays FRESH. A concurrent 'nx daemon t2 ensure-running' calls _running_daemon()->find_t2_daemon, sees the fresh lease, prints 'T2 daemon already running' and DECLINES to spawn. The draining daemon then exits -> ZERO daemons until the next ensure-running. Reproduced live: stop then immediate ensure-running -> 0 daemons. Distinct from nexus-64w50 (spawn-loser-quits); this is decline-to-spawn-against-a-dying-incumbent. Fix: call mark_shutting_down early in stop() (on SIGTERM receipt) so discover()/find_t2_daemon returns None for a shutting-down daemon and ensure-running spawns a replacement immediately.

2. socket_close_timeout fires on EVERY stop: stop() server.close()+wait_closed() always hits _GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT (5s, nexus-saigj) because a long-lived idle MCP client connection never closes on its own. saigj correctly BOUNDS it (no hang), but every stop now costs a full 5s and emits a dispatch_failed reclaim_stale 'closed database' race from an in-flight client RPC. Fix: force-close client transports (abort writers) in stop() before/alongside wait_closed so teardown is prompt and clients see a clean disconnect.

Both improve restart latency + close the residual zero-daemon window the 5.10.1 64w50 fix doesn't cover (64w50 = spawn path; this = stop/ensure-running path). Recommend pairing with nexus-hcw0g (reaper) as a daemon-lifecycle hardening follow-on.
notes: LIVE on 5.10.2 (Desktop update shakeout 2026-06-05): this causes ACTUAL T2 WRITE FAILURES, not just CPU waste. Observed: 2 daemons coexisting (stuck 40-min incumbent 30170 + churning peg 29269); ensure-running spawned replacements (11862->29269) every few min because the incumbent was slow-to-hello, each new daemon pegging ~99% CPU. While 2 daemons contended on memory.db, every 'nx memory put' failed with T2ClientError: memory.put: OperationalError: database is locked (unhandled -> raw CLI traceback). Log shows the x47yx signature: t2_daemon_socket_close_timeout(uds,5.0s) + taxonomy.persist_assignments dispatch_failed mid-drain. Manual sweep (kill both, start one) restored T2 writes. Severity should be P1: T2 is the cross-process shared bus and it is unreliable whenever this fires.

The stop()/ensure-running hygiene gaps are on the SQLite single-writer T2 daemon path. 6.0.0 hard-defaults to service mode where t2_index_write short-circuits to the service-backed T2Database and the daemon is not the write arbiter; the daemon code is the rollback target slated for full deletion by gmiaf.24 (RDR-152 P4.1). title: test_t2_multistack_race leaks orphan t2 daemons + /tmp config dirs (reaper is single-shot, single-pid)
description:
Found during 2026-06-05 shakeout sweep: 134 orphaned 'nx daemon t2 start --config-dir /tmp/nxt2race-*' processes (reparented to init, aged up to 18h) + 186 leaked /tmp/nxt2race-* dirs accumulated on the dev box. Manually reaped.

Root cause: tests/_daemon_leak_guard.py reap_tmp_daemons() is (a) single-shot — reads ONE pid from the discovery file and kills it once, no loop; (b) discovery-file-pid-only — misses any daemon whose pid isn't the one currently recorded (multistack starts several; only the converged winner is in the discovery file, losers/predecessors are missed); (c) vulnerable to respawn-after-reap now that nexus-64w50's spawn-loss retry (PR #1126) lets a spawn-loser re-acquire a freed lock for ~30s — a loser mid-retry when the reaper kills the winner becomes a new survivor the single-shot reaper already passed.

Live orphan daemons re-assert their discovery files (RDR-140 reassert loop), so rm of the /tmp dir doesn't stick until the daemon is killed first.

Fix: make reap_tmp_daemons match by config-dir substring in the process cmdline (catch ALL daemons on that /tmp dir, not just the discovery-file pid) AND loop TERM->KILL until no matching process remains for a quiet interval (defeat respawn-after-reap). The multistack test is the primary guard for daemon single-writer behavior; a reaper my own 64w50 fix can defeat could mask future regressions. NOT a release gate (test passes; CI runners are ephemeral) but should fast-follow 5.10.1.

title: RDR-149 lease takeover sends stop_requested but leaves a gap with no replacement daemon
description:
Observed live 2026-06-05 on conexus 5.10.0.

SYMPTOM: daemon pid 50782 (started 08:01:11) received `t2_daemon_stop_requested signal_received=True` at 08:06:49, shut down gracefully by 08:07:50, and NOTHING started a replacement. Left zero T2 daemons + no discovery file until a manual `ensure-running`. The crash-loop guard was NOT tripped (t2_crashloop.json: 1 timestamp, tripped_logged=false) — so this is not a crash loop; it is a clean takeover-stop that orphaned the service.

CONTEXT: this is RDR-149 lease-handoff behavior. When a new owner claims the lease (or an ensure-running caller decides the incumbent is stale — plausibly because 50782 was pegged on reclaim_stale and slow to answer hello(); see sibling bead), it requests the incumbent to stop. But the stop was not paired with a successful replacement start, leaving a window (here, indefinite until manual intervention) with no daemon.

EXPECTED: takeover must be atomic/ordered — a replacement daemon should be confirmed-live (lease acquired + reachable) BEFORE the incumbent is told to stop, OR the stopping incumbent should only exit once a successor holds the lease. A stop-without-successor should never leave zero daemons.

FIX DIRECTIONS: in the RDR-149 service_registry handoff path, gate the incumbent's stop on successor liveness (start-then-stop, not stop-then-hope); or have ensure-running re-spawn after a takeover-stop it initiated. Also: don't declare a busy-but-alive daemon stale (couple with the reclaim_stale backoff fix so a pegged daemon still answers hello()).

title: T2 daemon pegs a core on aspect_queue.reclaim_stale lock contention after restart
description:
Observed live 2026-06-05 on conexus 5.10.0 (daemon pid 50782, post-sweep restart).

SYMPTOM: a freshly-restarted T2 daemon pegged a core at ~99% CPU for 5+ min; 163 of the last 200 t2_daemon.log lines were `database is locked`. CPU was bursty (84% -> 24% on consecutive samples), not a hard hang — it was busy-retrying lock acquisition, not log-spamming (+0 log lines/4s).

ROOT: the dominant locking op is `aspect_queue.reclaim_stale` (71 of recent lock events). The daemon (50782) was the SOLE holder of memory.db/-wal per lsof, yet logging constant `database is locked` — i.e. internal contention between the daemon's own threads (6 threads: main loop + aspect_worker + expire + heartbeat) AND/OR the 4 live nx-mcp processes each polling reclaim_stale against the same memory.db. This is the known aspect-worker WAL contention (T2 memory: project_daemon_restart_not_worker_fix). Distinct from the RDR-149 multiplicity fix, which is working.

TRIGGER: restart while a backlog of stale aspect-queue rows exists + multiple aspect-worker pollers + concurrent `nx index repo` runs. The peg self-recovered (drained to 0% once backlog cleared) but it (a) wastes a core and (b) made the daemon slow-to-hello, contributing to a takeover-stop (see sibling bead).

FIX DIRECTIONS: exponential backoff (not tight retry) on reclaim_stale lock failure; raise busy_timeout; serialize reclaim_stale to a single owner (daemon-only, not per-nx-mcp poller); or batch/throttle reclaim polling. Consider whether reclaim_stale should run at all in nx-mcp aspect_workers now that persist routes through the daemon (RDR-129/zir76).

title: T1 cold-start Bash-sibling discoverability sliver (RDR-149 P4 known limitation)
description: RDR-149 P4 keys T1 on session-id. In the cold-start sliver before the SessionStart hook writes ~/.config/nexus/current_session (and with no NX_SESSION_ID in env), a bare Claude-Code-spawned Bash sibling (hook, nx scratch, nx doctor) resolves no session-id and gets a loud retryable T1ServerNotFoundError (Path D) instead of discovering the transient server_pid-keyed lease. The owner (_t1_state) and MCP-dispatched subprocesses (env Path A) are unaffected. This is the accepted tradeoff of session-id keying over the unreliable find_immediate_claude_pid PPID-walk (RDR Gap 2): closing it via a transient-lease scan would risk cross-session mis-binding (two concurrent Claude sessions both mid-cold-start), which the RDR rejected. Surfaced by substantive-critic on commit dbaa8974. Decision (B1): accept + document + honest test, tracked here. Re-evaluate only if a real hook is observed failing in the sliver; possible mitigation is ensuring the session-id hook writes current_session before any other SessionStart hook runs nx.

title: nx collection prune for orphaned dimension-mismatched collections + quieter search logging
description:

GH #1113 (2026-06-04). Adjacent to nexus-1714 (doctor legacy-metadata check) but distinct: this needs a prune verb + log-noise downgrade. Specific orphan: knowledge__shakedown-scratch__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1 (1 chunk, 384d, prior shakeout leftover).

close_reason: Shipped 663888e2 on develop. AC1: nx collection prune (fail-safe list-by-default, --yes deletes via the delete cascade, --dry-run wins, unresolved active-embedder probe never guesses). title: CI/release hermeticity: docling PDF tests fetch HF model at test time, flaking releases
description: The v5.8.0 release workflow failed twice on transient HuggingFace docling-model fetch (LocalEntryNotFoundError -> silent pymupdf fallback -> 21 'extraction_method == docling' assertion failures), then passed on the 3rd run. Root cause: tests/test_pdf_extractor_integration.py and tests/test_pdf_subsystem.py assert docling was used but are NOT marked @pytest.mark.integration, so they run in the default 'pytest tests/' that gates both ci.yml and release.yml. Neither workflow caches the HF/docling model (~/.cache/huggingface) — only ChromaDB ONNX + uv wheels. So the docling model is re-fetched from HF every run; when HF is flaky/rate-limiting the release goes red. Fix options: (a) mark these PDF tests @pytest.mark.integration so they stop gating CI/release (they are integration by nature — network model), and/or (b) add an actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.cache/huggingface keyed on the docling model version in both ci.yml and release.yml. Prefer (a)+(b). This is a standing release reliability hazard, surfaced during the conexus 5.8.0 cut.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-144 P4 follow-up: redirect/clean catalog entries after 384->768 migration
description: embed_migrate migration reindexes into the new 768 target (new catalog entries) and deletes the old 384 physical collection, but never removes/redirects the OLD catalog Document entries pointing at the deleted collection. Result: ghost catalog records that nx doctor / orphan tooling will flag. Consider Catalog.rename_collection or explicit old-entry cleanup. Identified in P4 substantive critique (O1). Not data loss; catalog integrity.
close_reason: Fixed: extracted canonical delete cascade into src/nexus/db/collection_purge.py (purge_collection_cascade); migration + delete_cmd both route the old-collection delete through it, so no orphan catalog/taxonomy/chash/pipeline rows. Cascade-failure visibility regression (both reviewers flagged) fixed via CascadeCounts.failures surfaced to stderr (delete_cmd) + outcome.reason (migration). substantive-critic re-verify justified/0-sig; test-validator PASS (5 tests across 3 caller surfaces; 51-test cascade regression green). Commits c3704cb3 + fa97b83e.

title: RDR-144 P4 follow-up: harden reindex verification against empty-file count inflation
description: embed_migrate._default_reindex increments indexed unconditionally per existing source file, even when index_pdf/index_markdown produce zero chunks (empty/silently-broken file). Verification (indexed>=expected_sources AND after>0) then passes and the old collection is deleted, losing the original chunks from that file. Fix needs index_* to report chunks-written so indexed counts only content-producing sources, OR a content-count floor. Identified in P4 stacked review (S2). Lower-probability (file non-empty at original index, empty now) but irreversible.
close_reason: Fixed: _default_reindex now counts only content-producing sources (index_markdown/index_pdf chunk-count return; batch_index_markdowns 'indexed' status), so a zero-chunk/empty source can't inflate the verification and trigger a data-losing delete. Stacked review: code-review approved, substantive-critic justified. test-validator PASS (3 exact-count tests, docs + rdr branches). Commits c3704cb3 + fa97b83e.

description:

SCOPE:
- Reuse health._check_t3_local dimension probe (health.py:258-309, the #1061 E1 check) — already dimension-based, covers local->local 384->768. Detect old 384 collections under 768 EF.

- SAFETY PROTOCOL (gate-locked, ordered, no shortcuts): (1) dry-run preview of what would change; (2) double-confirm before any destructive op; (3) reindex-first into the new 768 collections; (4) delete the old 384 collections ONLY after verifying the reindex succeeded. NEVER delete-before-reindex. On mid-reindex failure: old data must still exist (no data loss).

TDD: test FIRST. existing-384 -> cleanup/reindex OFFERED (not silent orphan); reindex-failure-midway -> old collections still present (no loss); dry-run -> no mutation; delete only fires after verified reindex.

title: RDR-144 P3: extra-add (editable-safe) + bge model pre-fetch with offline-safe warmup
description:
Phase 3. Two coupled pieces hosted by the nx init verb (P2).

(A) EXTRA-ADD, EDITABLE-SAFE (CA-2): gate on presence of \$(uv tool dir)/conexus/uv-receipt.toml.
  - Present (uv-tool install) -> shell reinstall-tool.sh-style: uv tool install --reinstall --from SOURCE[local] (preserve extras). receipt + directory key = local-source install, safe.
  - ABSENT (uv sync dev/editable tree has none) -> do NOT auto-reinstall; print manual instruction (pip install conexus[local]). This rules out the clobber-a-dev-tree hazard.

(B) MODEL PRE-FETCH (CA-1): warmup-embed to fetch bge via _init_ef() (P1 — into the STABLE XDG cache, not \$TMPDIR), with a visible progress bar. CRITICAL: wrap warmup in try/except Exception — offline/cache-miss is a fastembed logger.error + None return -> None-deref crash (Refinement B); convert to an ACTIONABLE message pointing at the cache path. Never a crash, never a wedged first search. MinerU commands/mineru.py:243 is the UX precedent.

TDD: test FIRST. fresh-local -> bge provisioned + warmup fetch (mock fastembed); cloud -> no fastembed touched; offline -> graceful actionable message NOT crash/hang; editable tree (no uv-receipt.toml) -> manual instruction printed, NO reinstall shelled.

DEPENDS ON P1 (stable cache) + P2 (verb host). Context: RDR-144 §Implementation Plan Extra-add + Model pre-fetch; nexus_rdr/144-research-CA1-CA4 (CA-1 Refinement B, CA-2). description: Deep-review (2026-05-31) confirmed a REACHABLE single-writer violation NOT closed by RDR-140 (flagged in RDR-140 Trade-offs as candidate-in-scope, then put in RDR-128 P3 scope; no dedicated bead until now). t2_index_write (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:195) catches T2SchemaVersionMismatchError AND T2DaemonNotReachableError and degrades to a DIRECT T2Database writer (mcp_infra.py:218), bypassing the daemon spawn lock. Reachable in production WITHOUT nx upgrade: a stale-version daemon (holds the spawn lock, serving) + a current-code client (post-reinstall, e.g. 5.4.5) -> database.hello() raises T2SchemaVersionMismatchError -> client opens writer B against the same memory.db => TWO live writers. WAL prevents corruption (byte-level writer lock; new-code-vs-old-schema errors loud rather than corrupts) but it is a single-writer-invariant violation during the post-upgrade / version-skew convergence window — exactly the window with the most churn. RDR-140's P2 version-cycle NARROWS but does not close it. DECISION NEEDED: close (route the fallback through the daemon / wait briefly for version-convergence before opening a direct writer) vs accept-and-document (WAL keeps it non-corrupting). Likely an RDR-128 P3 successor RDR. Source: deep-analyst single-writer e2e + substantive-critic, T2 nexus/rdr140-deep-review-spirit-2026-05-31, nexus/rdr140-single-writer-e2e-analysis-2026-05-31.

title: RDR-140 follow-up: extend crash-loop guard to the launchd/systemd 'nx daemon t2 start' path (Option A)
description: P4 (RDR-140) scoped the crash-loop guard to the ensure-running-driven respawn path only. launchd (KeepAlive=true) and systemd (Restart=on-failure) run 'nx daemon t2 start' DIRECTLY and never consult the t2_crashloop.json sentinel, so a hard-failing autostart daemon is rate-limited only by ThrottleInterval/RestartSec. Option A: have run_t2_daemon / t2_start_cmd check the same sentinel and exit-fast (log once) when tripped. Behavioral — refusal-loop semantics and operator-manual-recovery (start refusing to start) need design; likely its own RDR. Source: critic P4.4 Critical, T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-gate.
design:
## Option A: guard the launchd/systemd start path

SITE: src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:1332 run_t2_daemon (the entry the supervisor runs) and/or src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:525 t2_start_cmd.

PROBLEM: the crash-loop guard lives only in t2_ensure_running_cmd (commands/daemon.py:1107-1127). The autostart units run 'nx daemon t2 start' DIRECTLY:
- conexus/daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist:26 ProgramArguments -> 'daemon t2 start', :47 KeepAlive=<true/> (respawns on ANY exit).
- conexus/daemon/nexus-t2.service ExecStart -> 'daemon t2 start', Restart=on-failure.
Neither consults t2_crashloop.json, so a hard-failing autostart daemon is throttled only by launchd ThrottleInterval / systemd RestartSec.

REUSE the existing guard seam (commands/daemon.py:798-865): _crashloop_sentinel_path / _read_crashloop / _record_restart / _crashloop_tripped / _reset_crashloop, constants _CRASHLOOP_WINDOW_S / _CRASHLOOP_MAX_RESTARTS. run_t2_daemon would: record a start; if tripped, _log.error once + exit fast WITHOUT constructing T2Database (A1!) and WITHOUT a traceback; reset on a clean long-lived run.

DESIGN OPEN QUESTIONS (why this is its own bead, not contained P4):
- Under KeepAlive=true, exit-fast still respawns every ThrottleInterval -> a refusal-loop, not a fix. Need to decide: exit 0 (clean, but KeepAlive=true ignores) vs leave to ThrottleInterval vs add launchd ExitTimeOut/throttle tuning vs a sentinel-driven backoff.
- An operator manually running 'nx daemon t2 start' to RECOVER must not be refused by a stale tripped guard -> recovery semantics.
- 'reset on healthy run' needs a definition of healthy (survived N seconds) since start() has no reachability poll like ensure-running.
Likely warrants a short RDR. ACCEPTANCE: launchd/systemd respawn of a hard-failing daemon is bounded (log-once + bounded retry), operator recovery path preserved, A1 single-writer untouched, autostart integration test or documented manual verification.

Source: critic P4.4 Critical; T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-gate.
notes:
DEEP-REVIEW (2026-05-31) addendum: there is a CHEAPER partial mitigation distinct from the full guard-in-start. The unit templates currently have NO application/supervisor burst cap: conexus/daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist has KeepAlive=<true/> + ExitTimeOut but NO ThrottleInterval; conexus/daemon/nexus-t2.service has RestartSec=5s but NO StartLimitBurst/StartLimitIntervalSec. So a hard-failing autostart daemon respawns at launchd's ~10s default / systemd's 5s indefinitely. Sub-option A0 (one-line, low-risk, no refusal-loop semantics): add ThrottleInterval (e.g. 30) to the plist and StartLimitBurst + StartLimitIntervalSec to the service -> a supervisor-level burst cap. Note: the rdr140-p4-gate memo CLAIMED 'launchd/systemd bounded by ThrottleInterval/RestartSec' but ThrottleInterval was never set — A0 makes that claim true. Full Option A (sentinel check in run_t2_daemon/t2_start_cmd) remains the complete fix. Source: deep-review agents 3+4, T2 nexus/rdr140-deep-review-spirit-2026-05-31.
LIVE CONFIRMATION 2026-06-02 (chat-surface shakeout): two T2 daemons bound to ~/.config/nexus (pid 85769 incumbent + a newcomer crash-looping: observed PID change 34541->45732 in ~90s, pegged 74-100% CPU). mcp.log: 'ensure-running timed out after 15s' + 't2_index_write_daemon_unreachable_but_alive ... did not respond to hello(); writes degraded to direct'. This is the exact failure this bead's crash-loop guard targets. Manually cleared by killing both; single clean daemon respawned (pid 50701, healthy). The 'nx daemon t2 start' path has no guard against a second daemon spinning when one is already bound.
MECHANISM (from t2_daemon.log 2026-06-02 20:46-21:00): the thrash is NOT just duplicate daemons — it's a respawn feedback loop. A freshly-started daemon does a hot startup burst (aspect_queue drain + expire), pegging a core (observed 69-100% CPU) for tens of seconds. During that burst it fails hello(), so the next ensure-running caller declares it dead and respawns it -> stop_requested(signal_received=True) -> new pid, repeat. Observed lineage: 50701(20:52)->65125(20:57)->68122(20:58, started from the git/.venv install)->74830(21:00), restarting every 1-5min, with 'database is locked' on aspect_queue.reclaim_stale + expire_relevance_log while orphaned nx-mcp aspect_workers wrote memory.db directly (degraded-to-direct). It self-settled once orphan-MCP contention dropped (manual kills 5->3 nx-mcp) and one daemon got a clean window: 74830 drained, went to 0% CPU, no restarts for 2min+. IMPLICATION: a duplicate-daemon guard alone is insufficient — ensure-running's liveness probe must distinguish 'busy/starting (alive)' from 'dead' (check process-alive/pidfile before respawn, or grant a startup grace period), else it respawns a healthy-but-busy singleton. Manual kills do NOT durably fix this; needs the guard + liveness-probe fix.

title: MinerU MFR memory-runaway: per-page -9 should optionally degrade to docling, not fail whole doc
description: Root-caused 2026-05-30 from the RDR-139 demo (arXiv:2605.13379). A single page (page 31) reproducibly OOM/jetsam-SIGKILLs (-9) MinerU's formula-recognition (MFR) model, even on an idle machine with 92% RAM free and run in isolation — so it's page-content-specific (a formula MFR can't bound), not transient pressure, not a wrapper timeout, not a nexus rlimit. batch_size is already at the 1-page floor (pdf_extractor.py _extract_with_mineru), so the existing OOM mitigation (shrink batch) has no headroom and span<=1 re-raises immediately -> whole-doc failure. Proposal: when a SINGLE-page MinerU subprocess returns -9, optionally fall back THAT page to docling (formula-stripped) and continue, instead of failing the whole document. Keep it opt-in (e.g. --on-formula-oom=docling|fail, default fail) to preserve the no-silent-fallback-for-formulas guarantee by default. Pairs with nexus-pxxyn (thread --extractor through nx dt). Evidence: re-run of _mineru_run_isolated(p,30,31) failed identically; pymupdf shows page 31 is visually unremarkable (38 drawings, 5637 chars).
notes: RDR-148 CONSOLIDATION (2026-06-24): this bead is now Gap 5 of RDR-148 (MinerU subprocess-resilience). Design home: docs/rdr/rdr-148-mineru-endpoint-discovery-and-subprocess-resilience.md. Relevancy review confirmed PDF extraction stays client-side (RDR-152) so this is NOT obsoleted by PG/pgvector/native work. Implementation: MineruMemoryError(RuntimeError) maps -9/SIGKILL exit; on_formula_oom={fail|docling} threads through extract()->_extract_with_mineru; single-page MineruMemoryError + docling mode degrades that page (default fail). Shares the catchable error type with yrlbd (Gap 6). GATED on RDR-148 accept. Original root-cause evidence (arXiv:2605.13379 page 31 -9, re-validated 2026-05-31 in isolation) still valid.

title: nx enrich aspects bypasses t2_index_write — crashes on any concurrent T2 writer
description:
## Symptom

`nx enrich aspects <collection>` crashes mid-batch with:

```
sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked
```

The crash is **fatal to the whole batch** — papers extracted up to the crash point are kept, but extraction stops. No retry. Subsequent batches that retry have to start over from the first un-extracted paper (idempotent skip works there, but only if the earlier records actually persisted).

Observed today (2026-05-28) twice in the same session during a Luciferase Pyramid SFC RDR research run on `knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` (37 papers):

- **v1**: crashed at paper 6/37 (concurrent `nx enrich bib` was the contender)
- **v2**: crashed at paper 12/37 (concurrent deep-research-synthesizer subagent doing T2 writes was the contender)

Both crashes had identical tracebacks ending at `db.document_aspects.upsert(record)` in `enrich.py:1021`.

## Root cause

`commands/enrich.py:1021`:

```python
db.document_aspects.upsert(record)
```

This is a **direct SQLite write** that bypasses `t2_index_write` (the routing wrapper that probes the T2 daemon and falls back to direct writes). And `db/t2/document_aspects.py:520` has no retry-on-busy logic — it just calls `self.conn.execute(...)` + `self.conn.commit()` and propagates `OperationalError`.

This violates the RDR-128 design intent (every T2 write should route through `t2_index_write` so the daemon's single-writer-serialization handles contention). The aspects-extraction code path was apparently overlooked.

## Why it bites

`memory.db` is a single shared SQLite file in WAL mode. Concurrent writers are common:

- the `nx enrich bib` codepath (writes `bib_*` fields to chunks)
- the indexer codepath (`nx dt index`, `nx index pdf`) routing through `t2_index_write`
- subagent tool calls that write to T2 (the `mcp_infra.t2_index_write` route, or direct `memory_put` etc.)
- the T2 daemon itself if anyone is connecting through it
- the aspect_worker's own `aspect_queue.enqueue` calls during hook firing

Any of those overlapping with `nx enrich aspects` triggers the crash. In practice this means the command is unsafe to run while ANY other nx operation is touching memory.db.

## Proposed fix

Two options, each independently valuable:

**Option A — route through t2_index_write** (canonical fix per RDR-128):

```python
# enrich.py:1021 (replace)
from nexus.mcp_infra import t2_index_write
t2_index_write(lambda db: db.document_aspects.upsert(record))
```

This serializes the write via the T2 daemon when available, eliminating the lock conflict (the daemon's `_writer_lock` is the single point of contention). Falls back to direct write if the daemon is down — same as today, but with the `t2_index_write_daemon_unreachable_fallback` warning surface.

**Option B — retry-on-busy at the storage layer** (defense in depth):

In `db/t2/document_aspects.py:520`, wrap the `conn.execute` + `conn.commit` in a retry loop:

```python
for attempt in range(5):  # ~ 7 seconds total at 100-200-400-800-1600 ms
    try:
        with self._lock:
            self.conn.execute(...)
            self.conn.commit()
        break
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
        if "locked" not in str(e) or attempt == 4:
            raise
        time.sleep(0.1 * (2 ** attempt))
```

This catches the transient lock and gives concurrent writers a chance to release. SQLite docs recommend `PRAGMA busy_timeout` for the same effect — setting `conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")` at connection open does this at the C level (cleaner than Python-level retry).

**Recommended**: Both. (A) fixes the architectural violation, (B) hardens the storage layer for any other code paths that might also bypass `t2_index_write`.

## Repro

1. Open two shells.
2. Shell 1: `nx enrich aspects <collection-with-30+-papers>` (will take a while)
3. Shell 2: `nx enrich bib <same-collection>` (or anything else that writes to memory.db)
4. Watch shell 1 crash at some paper N/M with `database is locked`

## Acceptance

- After fix, `nx enrich aspects` survives concurrent T2 writers (test with concurrent `nx enrich bib` and concurrent `nx dt index`).
- Existing aspects records continue to upsert correctly.
- No regression in single-writer throughput.

## Source incident

2026-05-28 ~17:34 UTC during Luciferase RDR-010 research synthesis. Logs:
- `/tmp/enrich-aspects.log` (v1 crash at 6/37)
- `/tmp/enrich-aspects-v2.log` (v2 crash at 12/37)

Both crashes have identical traceback ending at `enrich.py:1021 db.document_aspects.upsert(record)`.

## Related

- nexus-kmvf2 (T2 daemon launchd KeepAlive / orphan-spawn pattern) — orthogonal but same family of "T2 contention" issues
- nexus-op10y (race window during predecessor-reap) — also T2 contention
- RDR-128 (the design that's being violated by enrich.py:1021)

The accumulating pattern of T2 contention bugs (kmvf2, op10y, this one) suggests a broader audit: grep for any direct `T2Database` usage that bypasses `t2_index_write`. Aspect extraction is one culprit; there may be others.
acceptance_criteria: nx enrich aspects survives concurrent T2 writers without crashing; tested with concurrent nx enrich bib AND concurrent nx dt index
notes: Identical crash twice today during one session. Two-line fix at enrich.py:1021 (route through t2_index_write). Broader audit recommended — any direct T2Database calls that bypass t2_index_write are candidates for the same bug.
close_reason: Routed aspect persist through t2_index_write->complete_aspect (commit on develop). Reads stay direct (WAL-safe); write is daemon-serialized. Test added.

title: T2 daemon launchd KeepAlive too narrow (Crashed-only) — clean exits leave daemon down
description:
## Symptom

T2 daemon (PID 63899 today) was not running at session start despite ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.t2.plist being installed. nx dt index hit t2_index_write_daemon_unreachable_fallback for ~5 minutes before the daemon came back up (likely via demand-spawn from the indexer recovery path, not launchd). Once a run flips its writes to the fallback path, it does NOT re-probe and stays on fallback for the rest of the run, even after the daemon recovers.

## Root cause

com.nexus.t2.plist sets:

    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
        <key>Crashed</key>
        <true/>
    </dict>

This restarts the daemon only on a non-zero-exit *crash*. Clean exits — SIGTERM from `nx daemon t2 stop`, the macOS shutdown sequence, log-rotation watchdogs, or an orderly OS sleep cycle that terminates the process group — set `last exit code = 0` and launchd does NOT restart. Observed today:

- `launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.nexus.t2` → `state = not running, last exit code = 0`
- `~/Library/Logs/nexus-t2.log` mtime is 2026-05-22 14:46 → last launchd-managed start was ~5 days ago
- Today's PID 63899 started 14:46:43 UTC was launched outside launchd (not in launchd's process group; launchctl still reports `not running`)

## Repro

1. `nx daemon t2 stop` (clean SIGTERM)
2. Wait — launchd will NOT restart
3. Run any tier-write client (`nx dt index`, agent memory_put, etc.)
4. Observe `t2_index_write_daemon_unreachable_fallback` warnings until something demand-spawns the daemon
5. `launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.nexus.t2` will still show `not running` even after recovery, because the recovery process isn't owned by launchd

## Proposed fix

Widen the launchd KeepAlive policy. Two options:

**Option A (simple, recommended)**: Replace `KeepAlive={Crashed: true}` with `KeepAlive=<true/>` (always-keep-alive). This is the canonical macOS pattern for daemons that should be persistent regardless of exit reason. Pair with `ExitTimeOut=20` so a stuck shutdown doesn't keep launchd looping too aggressively.

**Option B (finer-grained)**: `KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit: false, Crashed: true}`. Restarts on crashes AND on any unexpected clean exit. Reads the same in practice but documents intent.

Either way, the install path (`nx daemon t2 install --autostart`) needs the updated plist template.

## Secondary issue (separate concern, mention in bead but don't fix here)

The indexer client caches its write-path decision at startup. If the daemon comes up mid-run, the indexer should re-probe (e.g., on next write attempt, retry once before falling back). Today's behavior: 1st write fails → entire run goes via fallback even after daemon recovery. File a follow-up bead if RDR-120 owners want to fix that separately.

## Acceptance

- Plist template (in repo) updated to KeepAlive=true OR {SuccessfulExit: false, Crashed: true}
- `nx daemon t2 install --autostart` re-renders the plist with the new policy
- Manual repro: `nx daemon t2 stop` → daemon auto-restarts within launchd's KeepAlive interval (typically 10s)
- Documentation note (`nx daemon t2 install --help` or supervisor README) flags that the daemon now restarts on every exit, not just crashes

## Source incident

2026-05-28 ~14:46 UTC during a Luciferase pyramid-SFC foundation-paper bulk index. Indexer log: /tmp/dt-foundation-index.log (v1, hit fallback) → /tmp/dt-foundation-index-v2.log (v2, clean daemon path after manual restart). User asked "why is the t2 daemon down?" — root cause traced to KeepAlive policy.
acceptance_criteria: Plist KeepAlive widened; nx daemon t2 stop triggers launchd auto-restart within ~10s; install command renders the new policy
notes:
## CORRECTED ROOT-CAUSE — 2026-05-28 15:08 UTC

Two earlier notes here were partly wrong. This is the authoritative version.

### Retractions

- ✗ "spawn-lock not enforced" — WRONG. `nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:236` defines `_SPAWN_LOCK_FILE`, `:248 _spawn_lock_path_for_db()` is per-db, and `:635 self._acquire_spawn_lock()` runs via `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` (see `nexus/_locking.py:74,120`). The lock IS enforced.
- ✗ "3 leaked daemons on the same config_dir" — WRONG. lsof on PIDs 61656/62412/47747 shows config_dir from FD path:
  - PID 47747 → `~/.config/nexus/memory.db` (current, started 08:01:51 PT)
  - PID 61656 → `~/nexus-sandbox/.config/nexus/memory.db` (separate install, leaked)
  - PID 62412 → `~/nexus-sandbox/.config/nexus/memory.db` (separate install, leaked)
  So there's exactly ONE daemon per config_dir for the main install. The `~/nexus-sandbox/` install has TWO leaked daemons, which IS a real leak but in a different config_dir.

### Confirmed findings

1. **launchd KeepAlive=Crashed-only** is real and still concerning. `launchctl print gui/501/com.nexus.t2`:
   - `state = not running`
   - `runs = 1`
   - `last exit code = 0`
   The single launchd-managed run was 2026-05-22 14:46 (per `~/Library/Logs/nexus-t2.log` mtime + 3 "T2 daemon starting" entries). That instance exited cleanly some time after. Narrow KeepAlive didn't re-spawn.

2. **The plugin runs orphan-spawn on every SessionStart** — current daemon (PID 47747) is parented to launchd (PPID=1) but NOT in launchd's job system. Source: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/nexus-plugins/conexus/5.1.2/.claude-plugin/hooks.json` SessionStart matcher `"startup|resume|clear|compact"` invokes:

       nx daemon t2 ensure-running --quiet --timeout=5 2>/dev/null || true

   Implementation: `nexus/mcp/_first_run.py:147` and `nexus/commands/daemon.py:733 @t2_group.command("ensure-running")`. Result: every session start (or resume/clear/compact) re-probes the daemon and spawns one if needed. The orphan-spawned process is reparented to launchd but launchd considers the *job label* `com.nexus.t2` down.

3. **Predecessor-reap pattern** — `nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:943 _reap_predecessor()` SIGTERMs (`:955`) and SIGKILL-escalates (`:970`) any existing daemon when a new one starts and grabs the lock. This is by design (version skew handling, see `:698-702`) — but in practice each `ensure-running` reaps the prior daemon, which is why PIDs 63899 → 11457 → 47747 cycled today across ~17 minutes of indexing.

### Lifecycle that produced today's incident

1. Some time after 2026-05-23, the launchd-managed daemon exited cleanly. `KeepAlive=Crashed=true` didn't restart it. From that point on, only `ensure-running` brings a daemon up.
2. Today's session start fired SessionStart hook → `nx daemon t2 ensure-running` → spawned PID 63899 (or similar) at 14:46:43 UTC.
3. During the bulk index run, additional SessionStart-class events (subagent boundaries? resume? something) fired further `ensure-running` calls. Version-aware `ensure-running` may be a no-op normally but here it apparently spawned NEW daemons that REAPED the predecessor each time, producing the observed PID 63899 → 11457 → 47747 cycle.
4. Every reap creates a ~1s window where the socket is rebound — `t2_index_write` probes during that window fail and the write degrades to direct SQLite.

### Recommended fix sequence

**Primary**: Investigate **why mid-session `ensure-running` re-spawns** instead of no-op'ing on a healthy daemon. Possible culprits:
- Version-aware compare is too strict (e.g. uses uv tool revision string that changes across hook invocations)
- The predecessor-reap fires unconditionally instead of only-on-version-mismatch
- Each subagent spawned via `Task` runs SessionStart→ensure-running and races

Source pointers: `nexus/commands/daemon.py:670-733` `_PREDECESSOR_REAP_TIMEOUT` + `ensure-running` command body; `nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py:698-702 _release_spawn_lock` comments about the "co-dependent ensure-running interlock"; `nexus/mcp/_first_run.py:89-152`.

**Secondary (this bead's original concern)**: widen `KeepAlive` so the launchd-managed daemon ACTUALLY persists across clean exits, OS sleep, etc. — independent of `ensure-running`. Replace `KeepAlive={Crashed: true}` with either `KeepAlive=<true/>` or `KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit: false, Crashed: true}` in `daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist` (template in plugin: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/nexus-plugins/conexus/5.1.2/daemon/com.nexus.t2.plist`; installer: `nx daemon t2 install --autostart`).

**Tertiary**: clean up the `~/nexus-sandbox/.config/nexus/` config dir which has 2 leaked daemons (PIDs 61656, 62412 from yesterday + this morning). Probably stale sandbox testing artifacts; deserve their own kill + investigation.

### Forensic snapshot

Full snapshot of process state, lock state, lsof output: `/tmp/t2-daemon-forensics-2026-05-28.txt` (24K, 285 lines). Indexer logs: `/tmp/dt-foundation-index.log` (v1) and `/tmp/dt-foundation-index-v2.log` (v2). 7 fallbacks in v1 (all within startup window before daemon ready), 8 in v2 (spread across the run, each at paper-completion boundaries).
close_reason: Widened launchd KeepAlive to always-on <true/> + ExitTimeOut=20 in com.nexus.t2.plist (Option A). Test asserts the policy. Secondary indexer-reprobe issue tracked as nexus-op10y.

title: Phase 5.1: Decide Phase 5 migration trigger - upgrade step / first index / dedicated verb (RDR-137 OQ-8)
description:
RDR-137 OQ-8 (gate critique 2026-05-28). The success criterion says 'first session start following the migration' but SessionStart is not a migration trigger today. Pick among:

OPTIONS:
- (a) `nx upgrade` step (runs once at version-bump install; user-visible).
- (b) First `nx index repo` post-upgrade (lazy; risk: never runs if user doesn't reindex).
- (c) Dedicated `nx catalog migrate-repos` verb (explicit; user opt-in but requires docs/discoverability).
- (d) Combine: `nx upgrade` runs it; `nx catalog migrate-repos` available for manual re-run.

DELIVERABLE:
- Decision recorded in T2 (`nexus_rdr/137-phase-5-migration-trigger`).
- RDR §Success Criteria updated to match the chosen trigger (replace 'first session start' wording).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Decision documented with rationale.
- Phase 5.2 implementation gated on this bead being closed.

DEPENDS ON: Phase 4.3 (writer cutover proven via fixture test — migration design needs to know writer behavior is solid).
notes: Decision recorded 2026-05-28: Phase 5 migration trigger is the existing 'nx upgrade' verb (idempotent step). Rationale: 'nx index repo' fires the catalog hook on every commit which would re-run the migration unnecessarily; a dedicated 'nx catalog migrate-repos' verb adds a learn-it-first cost. 'nx upgrade' is the existing one-shot ceremony users run on version bumps and is idempotent by design. Implementation lives in nexus-tts0d.19.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 4.1: Orphan owner cleanup - alias catalog owner 1.22 (qmrr-zm2n) to 1.1 nexus (RDR-137)
description:
RDR-137 Phase 4 one-time data correction. Per A4 verdict, owner `1.22` (qmrr-zm2n) is a pre-RDR-103 historical artifact from when callers used raw worktree-path hashes for repo_hash. A new indexing run from either path now resolves to owner `1.1` (nexus) because nexus-nzyrh (PR #997) fixed the `repo_root` write path. Sweep the existing wrong-`repo_root` rows.

WORK:
- Sweep query: find owners whose `_repo_identity(owner.repo_root)` resolves to a different primary owner's hash.
- For each orphan: alias documents/collections to the primary owner; delete (or tombstone) the orphan owner row.
- Make this a re-runnable `nx catalog dedupe-orphan-owners` subcommand (idempotent).
- Canonical `repo_root` for the merged owner is the main repo path (matters because `resolve_path` uses it as the base for relative file paths).

ACCEPTANCE:

- Local live evidence: owner 1.22 → 1.1 alias verified post-run.

- Reference: rdr-137 §Critical Assumptions A4, §Approach Phase 4.

DEPENDS ON: Phase 3.10 (Phase 3 closeout — wait for read-path cutovers to land first, so any post-sweep regression has a clean read substrate).

title: ensure_owner_for_repo writes raw input path as repo_root, not _repo_identity-derived main_repo (worktree-first-run contamination)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-28 by RDR-137 gate critique. Pre-existing bug independent of RDR-137 migration.

`_repo_identity` (registry.py:17-48) computes `main_repo` internally (via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) for worktree stability — both main and worktree paths derive the same `(name, hash8)` tuple. The dedup IS correct for repo_hash. BUT:

- `ensure_owner_for_repo` (catalog.py:1022) writes `repo_root=str(repo)` — the raw input path argument, NOT the `main_repo` that `_repo_identity` computed internally.
- `_catalog_hook` (catalog.py:640) has the same defect.

Consequence: when `nx index repo` runs FIRST from a worktree path (e.g. `.claude/worktrees/qmrr-zm2n`) and no owner exists yet, the stored `repo_root` is the transient worktree path. After worktree deletion, `resolve_path` produces broken paths for all relative-path documents in that owner.

Live evidence: owner 1.22 (qmrr-zm2n) in the catalog has `repo_root=/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus/.claude/worktrees/qmrr-zm2n` — the worktree path, even though `_repo_identity` would now resolve both worktree and main to the same hash that maps to owner 1.1.

FIX:
- Change `_repo_identity` signature from `(name, hash8)` → `(name, hash8, main_repo_path)`.
- Thread `main_repo_path` through `ensure_owner_for_repo` and `_catalog_hook` to write `repo_root=main_repo_path` instead of `str(repo)`.
- Update all call sites that unpack the 2-tuple.

VERIFICATION:
- New test: indexing a worktree-only repo writes the main repo path as `repo_root`, not the worktree path.
- Locally: alias owner 1.22 → owner 1.1 (one-off data correction) and verify the orphan is gone.
close_reason: Closed

title: Catalog registers phantom docs__1-2188 to nexus repo but not real docs__1-1 (followup from nexus-9iw41)
description:
During the 2026-05-28 fix of nexus-9iw41 (Knowledge Map duplicates), surfaced:

`_repo_collections(nexus)` returns 3 collections: `docs__1-2188__voyage-context-3__v1` (the phantom collection, 815 garbage root topics, now deleted), `rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1`, plus one other. It does NOT return `docs__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1` — the REAL nexus docs collection (88 root topics, 3190 chunks).

Effect: Knowledge Map docs side is now empty for nexus repo post-fix (pre-fix it showed phantom data). The phantom-data-shows situation was strictly worse, but the underlying issue is that catalog repo→collection registration is wrong.

INVESTIGATE:
- How did the phantom get registered to nexus repo? Look for the writer code path that creates repo→collection mappings (likely `nexus.context._repo_collections` source data, possibly `catalog` table).
- Why isn't `docs__1-1` registered to nexus? It might be registered to a different repo (e.g. parent dir), or the registration logic uses the wrong key.
- The 'one other' collection that came back is probably `code__1-1` — confirm.

FIX:
- Add `docs__1-1` (and any other legitimate nexus collections) to the nexus repo's catalog registration.
- Remove the phantom `docs__1-2188` registration (the collection has no chunks and no topics — pure stub).
- Add a defensive lint / nx doctor check: a collection registered to a repo but absent from T3 chroma is suspect.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `_repo_collections(nexus)` returns `{code__1-1, docs__1-1, rdr__1-1, ...}` (real collections, no phantoms).
- Post-fix, Knowledge Map docs side shows real top-5 from `docs__1-1`: 'Plan search scope (775), Phase plan Python (624), Project knowledge findings (596), RDR research gate docs (590), Orphan doc_id reindex (580)' (or current top-5 by doc_count).
close_reason: Superseded: data source is being eliminated (see new bead for repos.json elimination). The patch-edit of repos.json that this bead would have implemented is wrong direction — repos.json itself is the bug. The Knowledge Map docs-empty effect persists until the elimination ships; that's an acceptable cost vs adding another patch-layer to the dying data source.
