title: nx_answer degrades to summarizing SessionStart hook context on empty/weak retrieval
description:
OBSERVED 2026-05-27: asked nx_answer a scoped analytical question about RDR-070; it returned a tidy summary of the SessionStart HOOK PAYLOAD (using-nx-skills rules, the three storage tiers, beads task-tracker, ~80 deferred tools, the skill catalog) instead of anything from the rdr/code/docs corpora. The model answered 'describe my environment' instead of the actual question.

ROOT CAUSE (two compounding factors):
1. nx_answer operators dispatch as 'claude -p' subprocesses, and those subprocesses fire THIS project's SessionStart hooks (bd prime, using-nx-skills, nx capabilities, etc.) — ~13KB of ambient context injected into the operator's window. When the retrieval step returns little/nothing, the model latches onto the most salient thing it sees (the hook dump) and summarizes THAT. Classic 'model summarized its own ambient context' failure.
2. Empty/weak retrieval was the trigger. Likely contributor: a malformed scope argument (scope='rdr,code,docs' — a comma list; scope expects a single corpus prefix or catalog subtree like 'knowledge' or '1.2'). Bad scope -> retrieval filtered to ~nothing -> fallback-to-summarizing-hooks.

WHY IT MATTERS: nx_answer is the canonical analytical-query entry point (the /conexus:query skill funnels all how/why/compare/tradeoffs questions here). Silently returning a confident-sounding but completely-off-topic answer is worse than failing — the caller has no signal the retrieval was empty.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick during design):
- Empty-retrieval guard: when the retrieval steps yield no/low evidence, nx_answer must return an explicit 'no matching evidence found for <question> in <scope>' rather than letting the operator synthesize from ambient context.
- Suppress SessionStart hooks in operator 'claude -p' subprocesses: ephemeral operators (ephemeral=True per the T1 sub-agent contract, RDR-105) are not interactive sessions; the SessionStart hook dump is pure noise + token cost + this pollution vector. Consider a CLAUDE_DISABLE_SESSIONSTART-style env or running operators with hooks off.
- Scope validation: normalize/validate the scope param; warn (or hard-error) on an unparseable scope instead of silently retrieving nothing.

REPRO: nx_answer(question='...RDR-070...', scope='rdr,code,docs') in the nexus repo with SessionStart hooks active. Logs: ~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log (nx_answer emits per-step nx_answer_step_start/complete events per its docstring) — check whether the plan matched, what scope resolved to, and whether retrieval returned 0.
Related: RDR-105 (T1/operator ephemeral contract), RDR-080 (nx_answer).
close_reason: Scope normalization (comma-list -> unscoped + warning) + empty-retrieval guard (explicit no-match instead of ambient-context synthesis). Both pure helpers, 11 unit tests. Hook-suppression candidate left for a follow-up if needed.

title: nx index: --incremental (chash-compare, re-embed only changed files)
description:
MemForest leverage idea #3 (synthesis T3 research-memforest-nexus-leverage-2026-05-27; tumbler 1.14.4).

MemForest: 'memory state is separated from derived access artifacts — summaries, embeddings, index rows can be regenerated selectively.' Re-index cost should scale with actual change, not corpus size.

nexus today: nx index pdf/repo re-index full. The RDR-108 Phase 3 document_chunks manifest (PR #618, fd09a7f4) now tracks which sha256 chashes compose each catalog Document — the infrastructure for incremental already exists.

SCOPE: add --incremental to index commands: (1) read existing document_chunks manifest, (2) sha256 each source file, (3) skip files whose chashes are unchanged, (4) re-embed only changed files. ~100 lines of comparison logic.

RISK: chash matches CONTENT, not embedding-model version. Pair with --force-reembed for model-version changes where chash is identical but the embedding is stale.
notes:
ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — closing as done, no code needed. Grounding against 5.2.0 source shows incremental, content-hash + model-aware re-indexing is the DEFAULT behavior, with --force as the opt-OUT:
- doc_indexer.py:627-641 (PDF/markdown/prose paths): looks up the existing chunk by identity, skips (return 0) when stored_hash == content_hash AND stored_model == target_model unless force=True.
- indexer.py:1317 (code repo path): 'if not force and check_staleness(col, file, content_hash_hex, target_model, ...)' — same content-hash + model gate.
So 'nx index --dir' / 'nx index repo' already re-embed only changed/new files, and a model change already triggers re-embed (the skip requires BOTH hash and model match). A --incremental flag would be a redundant alias for the existing default. The bead (MemForest synthesis idea #3) was based on the synthesis's incorrect premise that full re-index was required.
close_reason: Closed

title: nx_answer: two-phase recall (collection prefilter -> chunk browse)
description:
MemForest leverage idea #2 (synthesis T3 research-memforest-nexus-leverage-2026-05-27; tumbler 1.14.4). Fold into RDR-070 taxonomy work.

MemForest recalls WHICH MemTrees are relevant first (coarse embedding over root summaries), then descends coarse->fine. Ablation: neither flat top-k alone nor root-only alone suffices.

nexus today: search_cross_corpus (src/nexus/search_engine.py) queries ALL collections simultaneously (~290k chunks, no pre-filter).

SCOPE: add a collection_prefilter step. Embed the query, cosine-compare against per-collection summary embeddings (RDR-070 BERTopic topic labels per collection are a natural 'root summary'), select top-M collections (default 5), then run the full chunk query only in those M. O(|collections|) dot products + targeted per-collection queries.

WHY under RDR-070: collection summaries are a byproduct of 'nx taxonomy discover' — RDR-070 makes this nearly free.

RISK: cross-cutting queries ('how does T2 handle concurrency?') may wrongly exclude relevant collections. Needs an 'all' escape hatch bypassing the prefilter. Ship opt-in first.
notes: Promoted to RDR-134 (RDR-070 Phase 5: Taxonomy-Aware Recall in nx_answer). On grounding against real code, two-phase recall is not bead-sized: it means teaching nx_answer to read the taxonomy RDR-070 already built (per-topic centroids in taxonomy__centroids, topic_assignments, top_topics_for_collection, project_against) and deciding prefilter granularity (per-topic centroids EXIST; per-collection summaries do NOT). Retrieval-hot-path design with a real fork = RDR-070's natural Phase 5. See RDR-134.
close_reason: Closed

title: memory_put: canonical-fact merge at write time (Jaccard gate, opt-in)
description:
MemForest leverage idea #1 (synthesis: T3 research-memforest-nexus-leverage-2026-05-27; paper tumbler 1.14.4).

MemForest normalizes extracted outputs into CANONICAL FACTS before insert, so new evidence merges into existing state without full rewrites (prevents 'Bob lives in NY' then 'Bob moved to Miami' accumulation).

nexus today: memory_put (src/nexus/mcp/core.py ~1724) is a blind upsert by (project, title). The overlap/Jaccard logic (find_overlapping_memories) already exists but ONLY in the reactive memory_consolidate tool agents must remember to call. Over a long project arc (e.g. RDR-112, 20+ sessions) T2 accumulates dozens of overlapping entries; SubagentStart context injection then carries redundant state.

SCOPE: add an opt-in canonical_merge mode to memory_put. Before writing, FTS5-query existing project entries for token overlap vs new content; if Jaccard > threshold (default 0.5), MERGE rather than insert. Reuse the existing Jaccard logic in memory_store.py. ~50 lines (write-path gate).

RISK: pure-Jaccard misses paraphrastic dupes and can false-positive distinct entries. Keep LLM-assisted merge (MemForest's actual mechanism, more accurate) as an opt-in flag to protect memory_put write latency. Ship pure-Jaccard opt-in first.
close_reason: Closed

title: Evaluate DEVONthink MCP integration (official + dvcrn) for nexus ingestion + knowledge-graph linking
description:
DEVONthink shipped a built-in MCP server (DEVONtechnologies blog 2026-05-26; macOS Sequoia+; Settings > AI > MCP; providers: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex, Hermes Agent). Capabilities: read/summarize records, create/update documents, move between groups, add tags/annotations. Privacy: 'Redact sensitive content' + 'Exclude from Chat & MCP' per-item/db. Community alternative: dvcrn/mcp-server-devonthink (stdio, Node/npx, JXA bridge) exposes 16 tools: is_running, create_record, delete_record, move_record, get_record_properties, search, lookup_record, create_from_url, get_open_databases, list_group_content, get_record_content, rename_record, add_tags, remove_tags, classify (DT AI classification proposals), compare (hybrid similarity).

EVALUATION QUESTIONS:
  1. Resolver/selector layer: nexus.devonthink currently bridges via osascript (subprocess per call). The MCP servers wrap the same JXA/AppleScript surface. Is there value in nexus CONSUMING a DT MCP server instead of raw osascript? (Pro: richer tools, classify/compare; Con: extra process, MCP client plumbing, the osascript path already works and is sync-friendly for CLI.) Likely: keep osascript for selectors, ADD MCP for the AI tools (classify/compare).
  2. Knowledge-graph linking (ties to nexus-lxy5n): DT's classify + compare + native 'See Also' give topical neighbours. nexus auto-linker (nx catalog generate-links) is metadata-only (citations + RDR filepath) and produced NOTHING for the MemForest paper (no bib match). DT compare/classify could supply semantic relates-edge candidates for the incorporation pipeline. Prototype: on dt index, call compare for the record, map DT neighbours to catalog tumblers, create relates links.
  3. Bidirectional sync: after nexus incorporates + extracts aspects, write back to DT via add_tags / annotations (e.g. tag 'nx-indexed', tumbler, extracted aspect keywords) so DT and nexus stay coherent. get_record_content could also bypass the Files.noindex path-resolution for records that are not file-backed (web clips, RTF, formatted notes).
  4. create_from_url: DT can ingest a URL into a record; nexus could drive 'capture URL -> DT record -> nexus index' in one flow.

DELIVERABLE: a recommendation (osascript vs MCP per layer) + a thin spike wiring compare/classify into the linking step. If scope grows (bidirectional sync contract, MCP client lifecycle, privacy-redaction interplay), promote to an RDR. Related: nexus-lxy5n (incorporation pipeline), RDR-099 (closed, osascript selectors).
close_reason: EVALUATED. Recommendation recorded in T2 nexus/gjz52-devonthink-mcp-eval-2026-05-28: KEEP osascript for selectors (no MCP migration); Layer-2 compare/classify semantic linking + Layer-3 bidirectional sync both require consuming a DT MCP server (client lifecycle + privacy interplay) -> RDR-scale per the bead's own escalation clause. Spike+sync promoted to a new RDR-promotion bead (entangled with nexus-lxy5n).

title: nx dt index: run full incorporation pipeline (bib enrich + aspects + auto-link) end-to-end
description:
GOAL: `nx dt index --uuid <UUID>` (and all selector variants) should incorporate a DEVONthink record into the knowledge graph END-TO-END in one operation, not stop at index+stamp.

MOTIVATION (2026-05-27, indexing x-devonthink-item://886082AB-... = MemForest paper): doing the full 'index it, incorporate it, extract aspects, do all the linking and knowledge-graph integration' required a manual multi-step dance:
  1. nx dt index (or nx index pdf) -> indexes chunks + stamps DT URI
  2. nx catalog update --source-uri / --meta -> stamp devonthink_uri (only if dt index stamp didn't fire)
  3. nx enrich <collection> -> bibliographic metadata (Semantic Scholar)
  4. nx enrich aspects <collection> -> scholarly-paper-v1 aspect extraction
  5. catalog auto-linking / cites/relates links into the knowledge graph -> entirely manual today

CURRENT STATE: nx dt index (RDR-099 P2, src/nexus/commands/dt.py) does: selector-resolve -> route to knowledge__<corpus>-papers -> nx index pdf|md -> stamp DT URI on catalog entry. It does NOT trigger bib enrichment, aspect extraction, or graph linking. Those are separate manual commands.

SCOPE:
  - Add pipeline-stage flags to nx dt index: --enrich (bib), --aspects, --link (catalog auto-linker), and a --full / --incorporate convenience that runs all stages. Decide sane defaults (likely: --enrich + --aspects on by default for paper-shaped collections; --link opt-in until auto-linker precision is trusted).
  - aspect extraction must be reliable: today the ingest hook enqueues to aspect_extraction_queue, but the queue is WAL-contended (orphan nx-mcp workers -> 'database is locked' failures; stale in_progress claims). The synchronous nx enrich aspects path (extract_aspects direct call) is the reliable one. nx dt index --aspects should use the synchronous path, OR ensure a healthy drain.
  - knowledge-graph linking: after incorporation, run the catalog auto-linker so the new doc gets cites/relates/implements edges to peer docs (e.g. MemForest <-> other agent-memory papers in dt-papers).

FOOTGUN found while doing this manually (worth a separate fix or fold in here): nx enrich aspects requires the FULL versioned collection name (knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1). Passing the bare normalized name (knowledge__dt-papers) that nx index pdf/dt index ACCEPT silently prints 'No documents to process' because catalog.list_by_collection does exact-match on physical_collection. enrich aspects should normalize/resolve the bare name like the index commands do, or warn on no-match instead of silent empty.

DESIGN INPUT: DEVONthink shipped a built-in MCP server (DEVONtechnologies, 2026-05-26; macOS Sequoia+, Settings>AI>MCP) and there is a community server dvcrn/mcp-server-devonthink (16 JXA tools: search/lookup/create_record/classify/compare/add_tags/get_record_content/...). The incorporation pipeline could consume DT's classify/compare tools for graph-linking suggestions, and DT-side tagging could be written back after incorporation (bidirectional sync). Evaluate MCP-vs-osascript for the resolver/selector layer. See separate research bead.

SUBSTRATE: RDR-099 (closed) shipped selectors + dt index + DT URI stamp. This extends it. May warrant its own RDR if the MCP integration + bidirectional sync expands scope.
notes:
## Grounded enrichment (2026-06-09) — scope has SHRUNK; RDR-139 shipped most of it

Verified against live code + a real run while indexing the CacheRAG paper
(x-devonthink-item://65097F07-… → knowledge__dt-papers). Two corrections to the
original description below.

### CORRECTION 1 — most pipeline stages already shipped via RDR-139
`nx dt index` (src/nexus/commands/dt.py:442 `index_cmd`) ALREADY has these flags
(RDR-139 Layers C/D/E/F, post-dating this bead's 2026-05-27 filing):
  - `--enrich`        bib gap-fill (DT-CrossRef), dt.py:535; calls
                      run_bib_enrichment(coll, source="dt") at dt.py:743-747.
  - `--link-semantic` 'relates' edges to DT similarity/explicit-link neighbours (Layer B), dt.py:509.
  - `--writeback`     stamp nx identity back onto the DT record (Layer F), dt.py:521.
  - `--highlights`    ingest DT highlights/mentions into document_highlights (Layer E), dt.py:562.
  - `--dt-content`    index non-file-backed records from DT AI-text (Layer D), dt.py:548.
So bib-enrich + linking + writeback are DONE. Do NOT re-scope them.

### CORRECTION 2 — catalog Documents ARE created by the index path
Original motivation implied aspects were blocked by missing catalog entries. NOT true.
`nx enrich aspects knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1 --dry-run` reports
**41 catalog documents** (extractor=scholarly-paper-v1, version=claude-haiku-4-5,
~$0.40). The dt-papers PDFs are properly cataloged with document_chunks manifests.
(The misleading signal: `catalog_resolve(corpus="knowledge__dt-papers")` returns []
because resolve filters the catalog `corpus` FIELD — empty on these rows — not
physical_collection. A red herring; ignore catalog_resolve for this check, use
`cat.list_by_collection(<full_name>)`.)

### REMAINING REAL SCOPE (what's actually left)

**1. Add `--aspects` to `nx dt index` [ABSENT — the core gap].**
   dt.py index_cmd has NO --aspects flag and never calls extract_aspects
   (grep: only run_bib_enrichment is wired). Aspect extraction is still a separate
   manual `nx enrich aspects` step. Add `--aspects` that runs the SYNCHRONOUS
   extract_aspects path (the reliable one), NOT the WAL-contended
   aspect_extraction_queue (orphan nx-mcp workers → 'database is locked'; see
   mem:project_daemon_restart_not_worker_fix). The synchronous batch driver already
   exists in src/nexus/commands/enrich.py (the `aspects` command body around the
   _collect entries helper at enrich.py:~915-950 and the per-doc extract loop). Factor
   a reusable `run_aspect_extraction(collection, ...)` out of that command and call it
   from both the CLI command and dt index --aspects (mirror how --enrich reuses
   run_bib_enrichment at dt.py:747). Pass the FULL versioned collection name that
   dt index already resolved for the index step — do NOT pass the bare name (see #3).

**2. Add `--full` / `--incorporate` convenience [ABSENT].**
   One flag that turns on --enrich + --aspects (+ --link-semantic?). Decide defaults:
   recommend --enrich + --aspects ON under --full for paper-shaped (knowledge__*-papers)
   collections; keep --link-semantic opt-in until auto-linker precision is trusted.
   Gate aspect/bib stages to paper-shaped collections only — docs__* aspect extraction
   is intentionally disabled (nexus-z70w); knowledge__*-papers is the aspect-eligible
   route (dt.py corpus help at dt.py:489-501).

**3. Fix the silent-empty footgun on `nx enrich aspects` [ABSENT — small, high-value].**
   `nx enrich aspects` requires the FULL versioned name. Passing the bare normalized
   name (knowledge__dt-papers) that `nx index pdf` / `nx dt index` ACCEPT prints
   "No documents to process in '<name>'." and exits 0 — a silent miss.
   - Root: enrich.py:935 `cat.list_by_collection(collection)` does EXACT match on
     physical_collection; bare name never matches the versioned row →
     enrich.py:880 echoes the empty message.
   - Fix: before list_by_collection, normalize/resolve the bare name to the versioned
     physical collection the same way the index commands do (find the normalizer used
     by `nx index pdf` — the --collection help at index pdf says "Bare names … are
     auto-normalized to knowledge__<name>"; reuse that + append the
     __<embedding_model>__v<n> suffix by resolving against existing collections, e.g.
     via collection_list / the chroma client). MINIMUM viable: when 0 entries match
     AND the passed name has no `__…__v` suffix, look up candidate versioned
     collections sharing the bare prefix and either auto-select the unique match or
     emit a LOUD warning naming the full name to use — never a silent exit-0.
   - This is a no-silent-fallback-for-correctness issue (mem:feedback_no_silent_fallbacks_for_correctness):
     a data-completeness command must not report success-shaped output on a name miss.

### TESTS
- dt index --aspects: stub extract_aspects; assert it's invoked once per indexed doc
  with the full versioned collection; assert NOT invoked without the flag.
- dt index --full: asserts enrich + aspects stages both fire for a knowledge__*-papers
  collection; neither bib nor aspects fire for a docs__* collection (nexus-z70w guard).
- footgun: `enrich aspects <bare>` with a populated versioned collection → either
  processes the resolved collection OR exits NON-zero / warns loudly; lock that it is
  NOT a silent exit-0 with the empty message. Add a positive case (full name → 41-style
  non-empty entry list via a fixture catalog).
- Deterministic: fixture catalog + EphemeralClient; no network; stub claude_dispatch in
  the aspect extractor so cost=0.

### EFFORT
Medium. #1 is the bulk (factor out run_aspect_extraction + wire flag, ~40-60 LOC +
tests). #2 thin convenience layer. #3 small but touches a shared resolver. Single arc,
one branch, one PR. May NOT need its own RDR now that RDR-139 absorbed the linking/
writeback scope — this is a focused 3-part follow-on. Confirm with Hal whether #3
(footgun) should split into its own tiny bead since it's independently shippable.

### IMMEDIATE UNBLOCK (independent of this bead)
The original "enrich aspects knowledge__dt-papers" request works TODAY with the full name:
  nx enrich aspects knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1
41 docs, ~$0.40, 1 skip (holke-knapp-burstedde-2019-ghost.pdf: empty source).

### RELATED: nexus-vwns1
nx dt index --aspects (scope item #1 above) will invoke nx enrich aspects' --validate-sample
path, which has a verifier-evidence bug (feeds raw file bytes to operator_verify instead of
indexed chunk text → false negatives on PDFs). Not a hard blocker, but land nexus-vwns1
first or the --aspects validation signal will be noisy on DEVONthink PDF sources.

title: Phase-review gate: P2 single-daemon enforcement + B1 (RDR-129) — cross-walk §Validation/§Test-Plan against kwqhd+exa2p+qi1zb
description:
RDR-129 P2 phase-review gate. Before P3 (conditional internal serialization, nexus-izpcb) may be evaluated, cross-walk RDR-129 §Validation and §Test Plan against the three closing P2 beads (nexus-kwqhd, nexus-exa2p, nexus-qi1zb). MANDATORY review step per RDR-129 §Implementation Plan ('Phase gate at each boundary: cross-walk §Validation against the closing beads') and the project's phase-review-gate discipline (feedback_phase_closeout_scope_audit). Use the /conexus:phase-review-gate skill.

Validation items to confirm closed (RDR-129 §Validation + §Test Plan):
1. Under a version transition or forced double-spawn, the system always converges to EXACTLY ONE daemon for the db — never zero (the A2 PID-liveness-interlock zero-daemon case the gate flagged as Significant #1), never two. Drive the stop()->defer-release->ensure-running respawn sequence and assert convergence to one.
2. The side-orphan sweep (nexus-exa2p / A1): manufacture a lockless live predecessor + a same-db side daemon and assert a starting daemon reduces to exactly one. Cover the macOS lsof portability case explicitly if the enumeration mechanism is lsof-based (its output is not POSIX-standardized); /proc/<pid>/fd on Linux.
3. nx doctor reports daemon multiplicity (A3) as a HARD error with offending pids when two daemons are forced.
4. Deterministic multi-writer load test (N concurrent routed writers across >=2 stores vs one daemon): zero UNRECOVERED drops after B1+B2 (B2-retried-and-succeeded writes do not count). If drops persist -> P3 (izpcb / B3) is triggered; if zero -> P3 may be skipped.
5. B1 prerequisite audited: the T2Client per-call RPC timeout EXCEEDS the 30s serving busy_timeout, so a daemon-side 30s wait does not surface to callers as an RPC-timeout error of a different type than 'database is locked'.
6. tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_startup_invariant.py extended for the sweep + the version-cycle case; full unit suite green.

This gate bead is NOT a 6th facet bead — it is the mandated phase-review-gate type. It blocks nexus-izpcb so P3 cannot start until the P2 cross-walk passes (and decides whether P3 fires at all).

P3 is CONDITIONAL: this gate's load-test item #4 decides whether izpcb (B3) is needed — if B1+B2 produce zero unrecovered drops, P3 may be closed without implementation.

title: T2 daemon predecessor-reap misses side-orphans not named in the addr file
description:
Follow-up to nexus-070e2 / PR #978 (the RDR-128 single-writer reap). _reap_predecessor_daemon() only reaps the SINGLE pid named in the t2_addr discovery file at takeover. A 'side orphan' that started AFTER the canonical daemon (so it was never written to the addr file) is not caught.

Observed live during the 5.1.5 prod shakeout: two daemons coexisted — pid 99075 (canonical, in addr file) + pid 1989 (side-orphan, started ~31s later, never canonical). A new daemon's reap would target 99075 (addr-file pid), not 1989, so 1989 had to be killed manually. The primary takeover case (new daemon reaps the addr-file predecessor) IS covered + proven; this is the residual multi/side-orphan gap.

Fix direction: on daemon start (after _acquire_spawn_lock, before T2Database opens) and/or in T2 daemon already running., enumerate ALL live processes whose cmdline is a t2 daemon FOR THIS db path and reap every one that is not self — not just the addr-file pid. Reuse _pid_is_alive + _is_t2_daemon_process; add SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation per process.

DESIGN CARE (do not skip): the sweep MUST be scoped to the SAME db/config_dir — a host may legitimately run separate t2 daemons for different config_dirs. But the cmdline is identical ('nx daemon t2 start', default config_dir) so cmdline alone can't distinguish db paths. Need a reliable per-db signal: e.g. match the daemon's open fd on the db file (lsof/proc), or have the daemon advertise its db_path (cmdline arg / proctitle / a per-db pid registry), then sweep only same-db daemons. Keep the PID-reuse guard. The db-path-scoped spawn lock (_spawn_lock_path_for_db) already defines per-db identity — lean on that.

Refs: nexus-070e2, PR #978, RDR-128 single-writer. Found: 5.1.5 prod shakeout 2026-05-27.
notes: IMPL 2026-05-27 (commit 977a2acc, PR #983). A1 same-db open-fd sweep in _reap_predecessor_daemon (+_reap_one_daemon, +_enumerate_t2_daemon_pids_for_db: /proc on linux, lsof on darwin, short-circuits when db absent). A3 ALSO HERE (doctor _check_t2_daemon_singleton, hard fatal, names pids) built on the shared enumeration — kwqhd does NOT carry A3. Phase gate: A3 covered by exa2p, not deferred. Narrow suite 56 green.
close_reason: Closed

title: T2 daemon spawn-lock does not prevent duplicate daemons (single-writer invariant violated)
description: LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-05-26 (5.1.2 shakeout): 6 nx daemon t2 start processes were running concurrently against the same config_dir and memory.db, all ppid==1, only one canonical per the t2_addr discovery file. RDR-120 spawn-lock (fcntl.flock on config_dir/t2_spawn.lock plus a db_path.spawn_lock sibling) is supposed to enforce one-daemon-per-config_dir, but duplicates coexisted. The orphans each held a T2 SQLite connection and were a dominant WAL-contention source behind the FTS5 lock seen in nx doctor; reaping them restored T2 integrity. Root-cause candidates: flock released or not acquired on the orphan path; supervisor restart spawning a new daemon while the old orphan lingers ppid==1 without holding the lock; or the lock check racing. This violates RDR-128 single-writer in practice. Needs: investigate why flock did not block the 2nd..6th daemon, enforce single-writer at start, and detect/reap orphaned daemons (relates nexus-9h1s reaper, nexus-qi1zb contention).
acceptance_criteria: Only one t2_daemon can run per config_dir/db; a duplicate start fails loud or no-ops via the spawn-lock; orphaned daemons (ppid==1, not the discovery target) are detected and reaped by nx doctor or a sweep; a test simulates a held lock and asserts the second start is refused.
notes: IMPL 2026-05-27 (commit bb416f13, PR #984, branch feature/nexus-kwqhd-spawn-lock-defer). A2 = (1) stop() defer spawn-lock release to OS-on-exit + (2) ensure-running cycle-wait polls PID liveness (_predecessor_alive = _pid_is_alive + _is_t2_daemon_process guard) not discovery file, abort-if-alive-at-timeout (_T2_CYCLE_EXIT_TIMEOUT). A3 (doctor multiplicity) is NOT here — it landed in exa2p/#983 (shared enumeration helper); do not double-implement. RF-A1 honoured: lock already version-stable, fix is defer-release only. Contract inversion: stop() now HOLDS the lock; test_spawn_lock_held_until_release_not_just_stop pins it. Full daemon suite green (117).
close_reason: Closed

title: search/query silently drop above-threshold matches on rare-token queries; surface the cut
description: Surfaced by the 5.1.0 desktop-chat shakeout (T2 memory: nexus/shakeout-510-issues, issue 2). A T3 chunk indexed seconds earlier is NOT returned by search when the query contains a rare/OOV token (e.g. 'zephyranth-510 shakeout probe' -> 'No results'), even though the chunk contains that exact token; the documented threshold=2.0 override (RDR-087 Phase 1.1) recovers it at distance 0.5515. Same on document-level query. HYPOTHESIS (from reporter): the query embedding is dominated by the OOV/hash-bucketed token, landing far from any chunk; the per-collection default threshold then drops the otherwise-reasonable 0.55 match. The deeper problem is the SILENT failure: caller sees 'No results' with no hint a 0.55 candidate existed. SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (from reporter): (1) on zero hits, footer the best-rejected distance + which threshold blocked it (e.g. 'top candidate dropped at distance 0.55, threshold 0.X — re-run with threshold=2.0'); (2) auto-relax once on empty and return rejected matches under a clear below-threshold banner; (3) document the rare-token failure mode in the search tool description. Pre-existing (RDR-087 threshold class, not a 5.1.0 regression). Severity: medium-high (queries with novel identifiers — ticket IDs, codenames, error fingerprints — silently return nothing). Model: voyage-context-3, collection knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1.
close_reason: Closed

title: memory_consolidate find-overlaps misses real overlaps: FTS AND-of-first-3-words candidate retrieval kills recall
description: Surfaced by the 5.1.0 desktop-chat shakeout (T2 memory: nexus/shakeout-510-issues, issue 1). Two entries sharing the distinctive token 'zephyranth-510' (+ probe/shakeout/T2) are not detected as overlapping even at min_similarity=0.1. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading src/nexus/db/t2/memory_store.py:739 find_overlapping_memories): for each entry e1 it builds an FTS5 candidate query from e1's FIRST 3 non-stopword (len>2) content words AND'd together (e.g. 'probe entry'), runs self.search(snippet), and only computes Jaccard against those FTS candidates. An overlapping entry that does not contain those specific positional first-words is never retrieved as a candidate, so its Jaccard is never computed. In the repro, alpha's snippet is 'probe entry' but beta lacks 'entry' -> beta excluded -> empty. The most distinctive shared token (zephyranth-510) is at the END of alpha's content and is never used for retrieval. The code comment itself admits 'AND-of-terms means too many words kills recall'. Compounded by len(w)>2 dropping short distinctive tokens like 'T2'. FIX OPTIONS: (a) for small projects (<=N entries) compute all-pairs Jaccard directly, skipping the FTS prefilter; (b) build the candidate query from the rarest/most-distinctive tokens (or OR-of-terms) rather than positional first-3 AND'd; (c) lower the len>2 floor or keep hyphenated tokens. Pre-existing (RDR-061 E6, not a 5.1.0 regression). Severity: medium (silent empty -> duplicate/stale entries accumulate unnoticed).
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
REOPEN CANDIDATE / partial-close note, found in the release-gate vacuity audit at develop a7553c88 (T2 nexus/release-gate-vacuity-audit-2026-08-10 [22175]).

This bead's problem (2) was 'the gate is NOT in the release skill checklist'. It reached .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md (step 6b, :186). It NEVER reached AGENTS.md: 'grep -c upgrade-shakeout AGENTS.md' returns 0 today, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md — the file an agent auto-loads and follows by default. docs/contributing.md also omits it.

So the leg is in one of three checklists. AGENTS.md § Cutting a release additionally omits local-service-gate.sh and run.sh --package-upgrade (both grep 0) and prescribes bare 'uv run pytest -m integration', which docs/contributing.md:258-262 explicitly calls insufficient.

Filed as nexus-17yxc (P3) with the full three-way divergence table. Also relevant: this bead's 2026-05-25 note of the '11/11 green' claim in docs/desktop-deployment.md — the script now reports 12/12, so that string has survived a correction cycle (filed as nexus-ofpqq).

title: T2 daemon serving-path: internal cross-store WAL contention drops best-effort chash writes under heavy concurrent indexing
description: Surfaced by the RDR-128 5.1.0 live shakeout (2026-05-25). Under two concurrent full-repo indexes (nexus + a launchd Luciferase job) routing all writes through the single T2 daemon, the daemon's OWN dispatch of chash_index.upsert_many hit 'database is locked' 5 times in ~8 min. lsof confirmed ONLY the daemon (pid 46412) had memory.db open, so this is NOT cross-process contention (RDR-128 eliminated that) — it is the daemon's per-store connections (RDR-063 one-connection-per-store) contending with EACH OTHER on SQLite's single WAL writer lock, exceeding the per-store busy_timeout=5000. The failing op is the best-effort chash dual-write, so the rows are swallowed/dropped (chash_index is a rebuildable lookup cache → recoverable via backfill), but it contradicts architecture.md's claim that busy_timeout=5000 absorbs cross-domain contention so 'callers do not see OperationalError: database is locked'. RDR-128 added busy_timeout=30000+retry to the BOOTSTRAP migration only, NOT to the serving dispatch. Fix options: (a) raise the daemon serving connections' busy_timeout; (b) add bounded retry to the daemon serving dispatch on 'database is locked'; (c) serialize the daemon's own cross-store writes behind one internal write lock. The daemon did NOT crash (stable throughout) — this is a completeness/robustness gap, not the crash-loop class. Candidate for an RDR if it recurs or chash completeness matters. Evidence: ~/.config/nexus/logs/t2_daemon.log, timestamps 2026-05-26T03:02-03:03Z.
notes:
LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-05-26 (5.1.2 shakeout): nx doctor T2 integrity check reports FTS5 database is locked while an nx index repo run (separate CLI process, --on-locked=skip) actively writes T2. Two independent CLI processes each hold their own T2 connection and contend; busy_timeout=5000 expires. Confirms gap 3 (per-store/per-process connections contend unmanaged) and gap 2 (silent best-effort drops: the indexer --on-locked=skip is already dropping writes). Orphan-process sweep (25 stale mcp-inject/tail/chroma reaped) did NOT clear the lock, proving the writer is the legitimate active index, not accumulation. Note: this is multi-PROCESS contention (index vs doctor), which RDR-128 single-writer was meant to funnel through one daemon but CLI paths open T2 directly. RDR-129 busy_timeout+retry+serialization would reduce frequency but not fully eliminate without single-writer routing of CLI writes. See sibling doctor-reporting bead.
RDR-129 PHASING (strategic-planner 2026-05-27): this bead is assigned WHOLE to P2 (hard single-daemon enforcement + B1), NOT split across P1/P2. Rationale: the RDR splits Layer B solutions B1 (raise serving busy_timeout 5000->30000) into P2 and B2 (bounded lock-retry on serving dispatch) into P1, but both are the same busy_timeout+retry work on the serving _dispatch (t2_daemon.py:708) and cannot be split across phases without splitting the bead. The BINDING constraint is the gate finding (Significant #2): B1 must NOT ship pre-P2 — a 30s blocking wait under multi-daemon coexistence (Layer A unfixed) holds an asyncio.to_thread pool thread for 30s and N coexisting daemons each saturating their pool stalls RPC dispatch. So B1 ships PAIRED WITH P2 enforcement. B2 (the bounded retry) co-locates here with B1. The immediate-relief P1 win is preserved by uq8a4 (B4 doctor soft-WARN + drop counter), which ships in P1. DEPENDS ON nexus-kwqhd + nexus-exa2p (single-daemon enforcement must land before the busy_timeout raise runs). B1 PREREQUISITE: audit the T2Client per-call RPC timeout exceeds 30s (RDR-129 B1 (a)).
close_reason: Closed

description:

title: RDR-128 P3: close the invariant (remaining writers -> irreducible lint set)
description:
RDR-128 Phase 3 — close the invariant. Route or lock-discipline the REMAINING direct
writers and drive BOTH storage_boundary_lint populations to the documented-irreducible
set. This is the phase the quantitative acceptance criterion gates on.

## Context
- RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-128-t2-single-writer-enforcement.md (Proposed Solution 1+5; P3;
  Validation quantitative criterion).
- Memory: nx memory get -p nexus -t daemon-restart-not-worker-fix (aspect_worker opens
  its own short-lived SQLite connection inside every nx-mcp process).
- Remaining direct writers to route/lock (from RF-1): aspect_worker; operator/CLI
  T2Database() sites in enrich.py, operators/aspect_sql.py, mcp_infra.py,
  merge_candidates.py, and the collection_* modules; nx repair plans; nx aspects
  repair verbs. Plus nx doctor's multiple read-only diagnostic connections (reduce).
- Use Serena: find_referencing_symbols on T2Database to enumerate every remaining
  construction site precisely; search_for_pattern "epsilon-allow" for raw-connect sites.

## Prerequisites
- Depends on: P2 nexus-sbxbe.3 (bootstrap lock discipline must exist before the
  remaining writers can adopt route-or-lock). Parent: epic nexus-sbxbe.
- Required state: P0 baseline recorded; P1 indexer routed; P2 lock available.

## Execution (TDD — tests FIRST)
Use sequential-thinking to triage each remaining site: route-through-daemon vs
take-the-migration/advisory-lock vs convert-to-documented-irreducible-exemption.
  - TEST FIRST: concurrency test — N simulated writers (indexer + upgrade + worker)
    against ONE daemon, assert NO `database is locked` surfaces to any caller.
  - TEST FIRST: regression guard (lint or test over epsilon-allow + construction
    sites) asserting no NEW code path opens memory.db directly without the
    routing/lock helper; lock the irreducible counts as EXACT `== N` assertions.
  - IMPL: route aspect_worker writes through the daemon; route/lock the operator/CLI
    T2Database() sites (enrich.py, aspect_sql.py, mcp_infra.py, merge_candidates.py,
    collection_*); reduce nx doctor reader connections. For each genuinely-irreducible
    site (bootstrap chicken-and-egg), keep a documented lock-discipline exemption.
  - DRIVE both lint populations (raw-connect baseline 20, construction baseline 53)
    to the documented-irreducible set via nx doctor --check-storage-boundary.

## Validation (before close — MANDATORY review gate + EPIC acceptance)
- code-review-expert review per routing batch.
- test-validator pass on the N-writer concurrency + regression-guard tests.
- EPIC ACCEPTANCE verification: run a full release cycle (post-commit indexer fires +
  upgrade + daemon restart) and confirm ZERO `database is locked` daemon incidents
  (qualitative); confirm both lint populations at irreducible set (quantitative).
  Phase-review-gate cross-walk RDR Proposed-Solution items 1+5 against the closing work.

## Parallelization
The independent T2Database() module sites parallelize well — SPAWN parallel agents,
one per module cluster (enrich / aspect_sql / mcp_infra / merge_candidates / collection_*).
Sub-agents may spawn children for intensive multi-file routing.

## Continuation state
Update epic nexus-sbxbe with final irreducible counts + the release-cycle acceptance
evidence. This bead's close should accompany the epic close.
acceptance_criteria: aspect_worker + operator/CLI T2Database() sites (enrich.py/aspect_sql.py/mcp_infra.py/merge_candidates.py/collection_*) routed or lock-disciplined; nx doctor reader connections reduced; BOTH lint populations driven to documented-irreducible set (every remaining exemption carries a lock-discipline justification); N-writer concurrency test passes; full release cycle runs with ZERO database-is-locked daemon incidents; code review + test-validation pass

title: Daemon lifecycle control: version-aware ensure-running + nx doctor skew check
description: The T2 daemon's code version is frozen at process start; an upgrade (uv tool upgrade / reinstall) leaves a stale daemon running old code until a manual 'nx daemon t2 stop && ensure-running'. Surfaced repeatedly during v5.0.2/5.0.3: aspect_worker WAL fix inactive until restart, version-string skew (daemon 5.0.2 vs tool 5.0.3), and (pre-n8sbw) silent. Targeted fix (fork 2, no RDR per user 2026-05-25): (1) nx doctor reports daemon_version vs installed-tool-version skew like it does plugin-name drift; (2) ensure-running becomes version-aware: when the running daemon's version != installed tool version, it gracefully cycles it (SIGTERM drains in-flight via stop() wait_closed, then respawn) so the existing session-start auto-call self-heals. Risk accepted/mitigated: graceful stop drains connections; skew window is small (first ensure-running after upgrade). Builds on n8sbw observability.
notes: SHIPPING control (2026-05-25): version-aware ensure-running primitive + wired into nx upgrade (post-success nudge) + scripts/reinstall-tool.sh + plugin/mcpb already call it at session start = restart-on-install across all paths. Tests: 2 ensure-running (stale-cycle/current-no-cycle) + 2 upgrade-nudge + autouse isolation fixture. DEFERRED to fast-follow: nx doctor skew-check (visibility only; doctor_cmd is a 2000-line surface, kept this PR tight on the control). Doctor check is the safety net for the bare 'uv tool upgrade conexus' path that bypasses nx upgrade.

title: _parse_json_payload in test_phase5_doc_cite tolerates leading but not trailing log lines (flaky on merged stdout/stderr)

title: T2 daemon dies leaving stale socket + no discovery file; daemon runs silent (stdout/stderr=DEVNULL) so death is undiagnosable
description:
During v5.0.2 post-release shakedown 2026-05-24: ran 'nx daemon t2 stop && nx daemon t2 start' inside a run_in_background Bash task. The new daemon (pid 68629, 5.0.2) appeared healthy via 'nx daemon t2 status' and 'nx doctor' (T2 integrity PRAGMA ok), but it NEVER wrote its client discovery file ~/.config/nexus/t2_addr.<uid> (501), and ~45min later the process died. Result: all CLI T2/T1 clients (nx memory, nx scratch) failed with T2DaemonNotReachableError 'No t2 daemon discovery resolved' even though status could still see a (dying) daemon via the socket/pidfile. A subsequent clean FOREGROUND 'nx daemon t2 start' (pid 3544) wrote t2_addr.501 correctly and stayed up; T2 write/read/get then worked.

Hypothesis: daemon double-fork/detach races with, or is interrupted by, the launching shell's teardown when started from an ephemeral/backgrounded shell — leaving it half-initialized (UDS socket created at ~/.config/nexus/sockets/t2.sock, but discovery file not written) and prone to dying. status reads the socket/pidfile so it masks the missing discovery file.

Repro (suspected): start daemon from a short-lived background shell vs a foreground call; compare presence of t2_addr.<uid> and survival. Fix direction: ensure discovery-file write completes (and is fsync'd) as part of daemonization BEFORE the launcher returns, and/or make status/doctor flag 'socket present but no discovery file' as degraded rather than healthy. Not necessarily a 5.0.2 regression — surfaced during 5.0.2 shakedown.
design:
INVESTIGATION 2026-05-24 (corrects the original hypothesis).

ORIGINAL TITLE IS WRONG: the daemon did NOT come up without a discovery file.
Proof: `nx daemon t2 status` (commands/daemon.py:613-637) reads t2_addr.<uid>
DIRECTLY off disk and exits 1 if absent. It successfully printed pid=68629,
daemon_version=5.0.2, tcp_port repeatedly — so the discovery file WAS written
at startup (t2_daemon.py:506-514) even though the daemon was launched from a
backgrounded shell. The file existed through status + doctor, then vanished.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: 68629 wrote its discovery file at ~21:05, served
status/doctor, then died abnormally. Its death left {discovery file REMOVED,
UDS socket REMAINING}.

WHY THAT ASYMMETRY (the mechanism): T2Daemon.stop() (t2_daemon.py:535-558)
unlinks the discovery file (line 547) BEFORE the UDS socket file (549-550).
- Clean stop() removes BOTH.
- Pure SIGKILL removes NEITHER (would leave the discovery file behind).
- A stop() that BEGINS (SIGTERM -> run_until_signal -> stop()) but is
  interrupted/killed after line 547 and before 550 leaves exactly the observed
  {no discovery, stale socket}. So the daemon was mid-graceful-shutdown when it
  was hard-killed or crashed.

TRIGGER: UNDETERMINED and currently UNDETERMINABLE. Sweeps are exonerated:
sweep_orphan_t1_chromadbs (session.py:460) requires BOTH "chroma run" AND
"nx_t1_" in the command (session.py:_parse_orphan_t1_chromadb_candidates),
and sweep_orphan_resource_trackers requires "multiprocessing". The daemon
command is `nx daemon t2 start` -> matches none. No code path intentionally
SIGTERM/SIGKILLs the T2 daemon except the explicit `nx daemon t2 stop`
(daemon.py:558-600, SIGTERM-only), which ran only once and on the PRIOR
daemon (21381), not 68629. Spawn lock is flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) held for
lifetime (t2_daemon.py:486->557), so a racing second start could not collide
while 68629 held it.

ROOT BLOCKER (the real actionable core): the T2 daemon is spawned with
stdout/stderr/stdin = subprocess.DEVNULL (commands/daemon.py:716-720) and has
NO file log sink. Confirmed live: lsof on the running daemon shows fd0->/dev/null
and zero .log files open. So t2_daemon_started/stopped/dispatch_failed and any
crash traceback are discarded; daemon.log is 0 bytes. The death cause is
invisible BECAUSE the daemon is silent.

DECOMPOSES INTO 3 FIXES:
1. (PRIORITY / enabler) Give the daemon a real log sink: route stdout/stderr to
   a rotating ~/.config/nexus/logs/t2_daemon.log (or configure structlog to a
   file FD that survives the Popen). Without this, every future daemon death is
   undiagnosable. This is the prerequisite to ever finding the trigger.
2. Crash-safe cleanup ordering: unlink the UDS socket BEFORE (or atomically
   with) the discovery file in stop(), and/or register an atexit + signal-safe
   handler that removes BOTH. Currently an interrupted stop() strands the socket.
3. Stale-state robustness: on startup/ensure-running, treat a UDS socket whose
   discovery file is absent (or whose recorded pid is dead) as reapable; and make
   `nx daemon t2 status` probe socket/pid liveness rather than trusting the file
   alone, so "dead daemon, stale socket" is detectable.

REPRO NOTE: not safely reproducible on the shared substrate without disrupting
live sessions; fix #1 first, then the trigger becomes observable on recurrence.
notes: PR #953 (-> develop) implements fix #1 (daemon file logging) + fix #3 (status pid-liveness) + bonus: __main__ guard for python -m nexus.cli (fixes silent _resolve_nx_bin fallback). Fix #2 (stop() socket/discovery unlink ordering) deemed benign and OUT OF SCOPE: residual stale socket is unlinked by next _bind_uds, and ensure-running already self-heals stale discovery via pid probe. Full suite green (7592). Bead closes when #953 merges.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #953 (merged to develop 1ad87492): daemon file logging + status pid-liveness + python -m nexus.cli __main__ guard. fix #2 (stop ordering) deemed benign/out-of-scope. Full suite green.

title: conexus !{ } command blocks using a Python heredoc emit raw source instead of executing (rdr-create + 8 other RDR-lifecycle commands)
description:
conexus slash commands whose `!{ }` bash-execution block wraps a Python heredoc (`python3 << 'PYEOF' ... PYEOF`) are emitted into the prompt as raw source instead of being executed with stdout inlined. The discovery/context header those blocks are meant to produce never renders.

## Symptom

Running `/conexus:rdr-create` (observed in repo `Luciferase`), the leading `!{ ... }` discovery block — which should print a rendered header (`**Repo:** ... **RDR directory:** ...`, `**Next ID:** RDR-004`, the existing-RDR table, and active beads) — instead came back as the literal Python source of the block. None of its computed output appeared. The model fell back to deriving the values manually (scanned docs/rdr, found RDR-001/002/003, next = RDR-004), so the run still succeeded; this is graceful degradation, not a hard failure.

## Root-cause evidence (the discriminating factor)

Compared all 25 conexus commands that contain a `!{ }` block in `commands/conexus/5.0.1/`:

- Commands that DO render (e.g. `review-code.md`, `analyze-code.md`, `nx-preflight.md`, `continuation.md`) build their block from `echo`/inline shell or `python3 -c "..."` — **0 heredoc markers**.
- Commands that emit raw source build their block from a Python heredoc `python3 << 'PYEOF' ... PYEOF` — **1 heredoc marker**.

The user confirmed the `review-code` (echo-based) block rendered correctly in the SAME session in which `rdr-create` (heredoc-based) did not — so the difference is the heredoc form, not a session/permission fluke. Note: none of the 25 commands declare `allowed-tools` frontmatter, so that is NOT the discriminator (echo-based blocks render without it).

## Affected commands (heredoc form — all predicted broken)

`rdr-create.md`, `rdr-list.md`, `rdr-show.md`, `rdr-gate.md`, `rdr-accept.md`, `rdr-audit.md`, `rdr-close.md`, `rdr-research.md`, `phase-review-gate.md`

This is the whole RDR-lifecycle discovery-header family — a systematic class, not a one-off.

## Hypothesis

The slash-command `!{ ... }` extractor/runner does not correctly handle a multi-line heredoc inside the braces (likely the `PYEOF` delimiter or the `<<` interacts badly with brace/line parsing), so the runner declines to execute and passes the literal block through into the rendered prompt. Specific form in `rdr-create.md:7-183`:

```
!{
NEXUS_RDR_ARGS="${ARGUMENTS:-}" python3 << 'PYEOF'
...
PYEOF
}
```

Unconfirmed whether the block fails to launch vs. runs-but-output-swallowed — only the symptom (raw source inlined) was observed; cannot probe the harness runner directly.

## Impact

Non-blocking. The discovery output is convenience (re-derivable), and the skill body (`skills/rdr-create/SKILL.md`) already specifies the manual derivation steps as the fallback. But it degrades UX across the entire RDR command family and the failure is silent (raw source dumped into the prompt).

## Suggested fix (in this repo)

Refactor the 9 heredoc-form commands to avoid the heredoc inside `!{ }` — either move the Python to `python3 -c "..."` (matches the working pattern; note `SKILL.md` Step 0 already uses `-c`), or extract to a `resources/` script invoked as `python3 $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/resources/.../discovery.py`. Independently worth confirming upstream whether Claude Code's `!{ }` bash-exec is documented to support heredocs at all; if not, this is a plugin-side constraint to encode in the command-authoring guidance.
design: Refactor heredoc-form !{ } blocks to python3 -c or extracted resources/ scripts (matches the working echo/-c pattern). Verify upstream whether Claude Code !{ } bash-exec supports heredocs; encode result in command-authoring guidance.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 heredoc-form commands render their discovery block (not raw source) when invoked; OR commands refactored off the heredoc form. review-code-style (non-heredoc) blocks continue to render.
close_reason: Closed

title: T1 chromadb servers leak across Claude Code sessions (SessionEnd not reaping)
description:
## Symptom

After ~3 days of normal Claude Code use, 4 orphaned ChromaDB server
processes accumulated, parented to launchd (pid 1):

  PID    AGE       COMMAND
  13170  1d 6h     chroma run --port 49994 --path /tmp/nx_t1_0x97x9j3
  43187  3d 21h    chroma run --port 57057 --path /tmp/nx_t1_0dcn2pnx
  58029  1d 11h    chroma run --port 56579 --path /tmp/nx_t1_ld3m5iv9
  64209  3d 1h     chroma run --port 62227 --path /tmp/nx_t1_wbfyvvau

Each holds open file descriptors, a TCP port, and a /tmp/nx_t1_* dir.
No live consumer; the originating Claude Code sessions ended long ago.

## Diagnosis

T1 (per-session ChromaDB scratch) is started by the SessionStart hook
and supposed to be stopped by the SessionEnd hook. The SessionEnd hook
exists but apparently doesn't always fire OR doesn't always reap the
spawned chromadb. Possible failure modes:

- Claude Code crashes (no clean exit, hook never runs)
- macOS forces a logout while sessions are still running
- The chromadb subprocess is parented to launchd before SessionEnd
  fires (a launchd reparenting quirk on macOS)
- SessionEnd hook script has a bug that doesn't propagate to the
  chromadb child

When the originating Claude Code session is gone, the chromadb is
orphaned. Nothing reaps it. It runs until the host reboots or the
user kills it manually.

## Impact

- Resource leak: file descriptors, TCP ports (49994, 56579, 57057,
  62227 in this snapshot), tmpfs space under /tmp/nx_t1_*
- Process table pressure (modest; chromadb is ~50 MB resident)
- Cosmetic noise in `ps`, `lsof`

## Fix paths

1. **Reaper on SessionStart**: when a new Claude Code session starts,
   scan for orphaned nx_t1_* chromadbs (parented to launchd) and kill
   them. The /tmp dir name carries the entropy, so false positives
   are unlikely.

2. **Idle-timeout in the chromadb spawn**: if the T1 chromadb hasn't
   received a connection in N minutes, self-terminate. Requires
   wrapper around chromadb's start.

3. **Liveness-check on the parent Claude Code PID**: the chromadb
   could poll for its parent's existence and exit when the parent is
   gone. Adds a thread to chromadb's process; messier.

Option 1 is the cleanest. SessionStart already runs hook code; adding
an orphan sweep there is ~20 LOC.

## Recovery (manual, until fix lands)

  for pid in $(pgrep -f 'chroma run.*nx_t1_'); do
    if [ "$(ps -p $pid -o ppid= | tr -d ' ')" = "1" ]; then
      kill $pid
    fi
  done

## Related

title: aspect_worker.reclaim_stale collides with concurrent T2 writers under WAL
description:
## Symptom

`nx-mcp` startup logs (`~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log`) show clusters
of `aspect_worker_claim_failed` warnings:

    sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked
      File "nexus/aspect_worker.py", line 268, in _run_loop
        t2.aspect_queue.reclaim_stale(timeout_seconds=...)
      File "nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py", line 457
        cur = self.conn.execute(...)

Frequency: ~5-15 events/hour during normal use. Clusters of 2-3
events within milliseconds of each other (clear "multiple writers
racing for same lock" pattern).

## Diagnosis

`AspectExtractionQueue.__init__` (db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py:150-153)
opens its own dedicated `sqlite3.connect(memory.db)` with
`busy_timeout=5000` (5 seconds). It is one of nine T2 stores that
do so:

    src/nexus/db/t2/__init__.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/catalog.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/chash_index.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/plan_library.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/memory_store.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/document_aspects.py
    src/nexus/db/t2/telemetry.py

Under WAL mode, SQLite allows exactly one writer across all
connections. Other connections that hit ERROR_BUSY back off and
retry until `busy_timeout` elapses. If the writer slot is held
for >5s by another store (e.g. a large MemoryStore put under
parallel indexing), `reclaim_stale` returns `database is locked`
rather than blocking further.

Two contending paths inside the T2 daemon process:

1. The aspect_worker's daemon thread doing periodic `reclaim_stale`
   UPDATEs.
2. Any RPC handler writing through another T2 store (`memory_put`,
   `plan_save`, etc.) holding the writer slot.

This is not a correctness bug — the operation just retries on the
next poll. But the warnings are noisy and worsen under load.

## Suggested fix paths (any one suffices)

1. **Cheap**: bump `aspect_queue` `busy_timeout` from 5s to 30s.
   Reduces noise without changing architecture. ~1-line change.

2. **Right**: route aspect_queue writes through a shared per-daemon
   writer (single sqlite3.Connection with serialization), so
   intra-daemon stores no longer contend on the WAL writer slot.
   Bigger change; touches T2 facade structure.

3. **Belt-and-suspenders**: add retry-with-backoff inside
   `reclaim_stale` to absorb transient ERROR_BUSY beyond
   busy_timeout. ~10 lines.

## Reproduction

Run `nx-mcp` with a busy aspect_extraction_queue (re-index some
PDFs into `knowledge__*`). Watch `~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log`
for `aspect_worker_claim_failed`.

## Not blocking; impact

- No data loss; work item stays `pending` and is reclaimed next pass
- No user-visible behaviour change
- Warning-level noise only

title: PreToolUse hook phase_review_close_requires_gate false-positives on implementation beads
description:
GH issue #931. Hook nx/hooks/scripts/routing/phase_review_close_requires_gate.py line 168 uses a substring trigger _TRIGGER_RE = r'\b(phase|review)\b' over the full 'bd show' output. With fail_closed:true this denies bd close on any implementation bead in a phased RDR plan whose description, parent epic, or rationale mentions 'phase' or 'review' (which is most of them).

Repro: Luciferase-hic, an implementation bead under RDR-003 Phase 0 with title 'Phase 0 Step 0: Resolve spatial-level question...'. Close attempt is denied; the redirect /nx:phase-review-gate 003 --phase 0 is the wrong action because this bead is the implementation, not the gate (gate is the sibling Luciferase-ma7.1).

Fix candidates from issue body:
1. Label-based: trigger requires a 'phase-review' label on the bead. Cleanest but needs data migration for existing gate beads.
2. Title-prefix: trigger requires bead title to match 'Phase N review gate' OR contain 'phase-review-gate' (the slash command literal). Zero migration; matches existing convention used by Luciferase-ma7.1 and nx phase-review-gate beads in nexus.
3. Explicit metadata field: bead description must declare 'phase_review: true'. Follows RDR-001 commitment-metadata pattern.

Recommend (2) for immediate ship; consider (1) or (3) later if convention coverage is incomplete.

Workaround: append '# routing-allow: <reason>' to the bd close command (>=8 chars). Already documented in the Luciferase RDR-003 arc.

Refs: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/931
close_reason: Fixed via PR #932 (commit on develop). Tightened phase_review_close_requires_gate trigger to match only bead titles with 'Phase N review gate' or 'PN phase-review-gate' patterns; full regression test added covering the 4 false-positive cases from GH #931.

title: CLI memory/plan/tier_status commands: route through T2Client when daemon reachable
description:
RDR-120 follow-up — gap surfaced by nexus-cm0az smoke 2026-05-22.

The P4 cutover (nexus-2ngox) migrated nexus.mcp_infra.check_version_compatibility to T2Client but **left the CLI's user-facing memory / plan / tier_status commands on T2Database direct-open** with epsilon-allow annotations. The lint count went to 0 but the runtime behaviour is:

- Host CLI Claude: T2Database opens ~/.config/nexus/memory.db locally. Works.
- Container CLI (with conexus installed, NX_T2_ADDR pointing at host daemon): T2Database opens **container-local** /root/.config/nexus/memory.db. **Daemon never touched.** Container state diverges from host state.
- MCP server (nx-mcp on host): also uses T2Database direct. This is fine because nx-mcp is the same process on the host as everyone else's daemon-arbitrated state.

Real-world manifestation (cm0az smoke):
- Host T2 daemon running on 127.0.0.1:49177, host's memory.db has row IDs in the 1400+ range.
- Container `nx memory put -p nexus_rdr -t container-pypi-smoke-1 ...` → "Stored: nexus_rdr/container-pypi-smoke-1 (id=1)" → fresh container-local DB. Daemon never saw the write.
- Host `nx memory get nexus_rdr/container-pypi-smoke-1` → "entry not found". Confirmed split state.

Scope:
1. `nx memory put / get / search / list / delete / expire / promote` — migrate the T2Database direct-open path to use T2Client when `storage_mode() == "daemon"` AND a daemon is reachable. Fall back to T2Database direct-open (with operator-warning) when no daemon is reachable, OR fail-loud (matching the T3 `nx daemon t3 start` operator surface).
2. `nx plan repair *` — same migration. Currently epsilon-allowed as "operator-invoked maintenance".
3. `nx tier-status` — read-only diagnostic. Could stay direct-open OR migrate for consistency. Decide at impl time.
4. `nx _session_end_launcher` — best-effort; documented as "must not block on daemon availability". Stay direct-open.
5. `nx doctor` (multiple sites) — diagnostic; documented as "must operate when daemon offline". Stay direct-open.
6. `nx upgrade` — chicken-and-egg substrate bootstrap. Stay direct-open.
7. `nx health` PRAGMA integrity_check — daemon-offline diagnostic. Stay direct-open.

So the operator/debug paths legitimately stay direct-open. The user-facing CLI commands (memory + plan repair) need the daemon route.

Implications for the container story:
- Once this lands, `nx memory put` in a Docker container (with conexus installed + NX_T2_ADDR set to host daemon) will route correctly to the host's daemon and share state with host CLI.
- Cowork is unaffected — Cowork uses MCP transport, not the CLI. nx-mcp on the host is already the integration point.

Acceptance:
- nx memory put / get / search / list / delete / expire / promote round-trip through the daemon when daemon mode + daemon reachable.
- Container smoke (nexus-cm0az re-run after this): container `nx memory put` → host `nx memory get` round-trip OK.
- Tests: existing memory tests keep working by either (a) the conftest spawning a test-mode daemon, OR (b) the test injecting a T2Client-stub, OR (c) the CLI commands accepting an `--inline` flag for explicit direct-open testing.

Out of scope:
- Operator/debug paths stay direct-open with their epsilon-allow tokens (legitimate).
- Plan / catalog / aspects / chash_index domain stores have their own migration question; this bead is memory + plan-repair only.

title: Operator doc: container-integration with host nexus daemons
description:
RDR-120 follow-up (post-P6 critique): container operators have no documentation explaining how to make a container's nexus instance talk to the host's daemons. This is the gap between "substrate ships" and "Claude Co-Work claim".

Scope: add a section (or new doc) covering container integration.

Suggested location:
- `docs/architecture.md` § "Container integration" subsection,
  OR a dedicated `docs/container-integration.md` linked from
  `docs/architecture.md` and the top-level README.

Required content (driven by the MVV beads' outcomes):

1. The three connection paths, when to use each:
   a. TCP loopback + `--network=host` (simplest; trades network
      namespace isolation).
   b. UDS socket mount + `--user $(id -u)` (best when network
      isolation is wanted; needs UID matching).
   c. Operator-side forward (`socat` / `ssh -L`) — fallback for
      environments where neither (a) nor (b) is acceptable.
2. The exact env-var incantations for each path
   (`NX_T2_ADDR`, `NX_T2_SOCK`, `NX_T3_ADDR`).
3. Discovery-file resolution: when to mount `~/.config/nexus/`
   vs when to rely on env vars.
4. T1 isolation across containers: containers do NOT share T1
   with each other or the host. Cross-container shared state
   must use T2 (`nx memory put` / `nx memory get`).
5. Why non-loopback TCP is off the table (banlist + auth-design
   gap) — informational, not actionable.
6. Diagnostic recipe: `nx daemon t2 status` from inside the
   container; expected output; common failure modes
   (EACCES on UID mismatch, ECONNREFUSED on missing port).

Depends on nexus-wkyt7 + nexus-3d1ph (the doc cites their
MVV-validated incantations rather than inventing fresh ones).

Acceptance:
- Doc landed under `docs/`.
- Each of the three connection paths has a runnable example.
- Cross-referenced from `docs/architecture.md` § daemon model.

title: Container MVV: TCP loopback path — claude CLI in container shares T2/T3 with host
description:
RDR-120 follow-up (post-P6 critique): structurally we enabled cross-process daemon access; we never validated the container→host scenario the substrate split was implicitly motivated by (Claude Co-Work in a container talking to host nexus).

Scope: MVV the TCP-loopback container connection path.

Setup:
- Host: `nx daemon t2 start` + `nx daemon t3 start`. Capture the
  TCP port from `nx daemon t2 status` and `nx daemon t3 status`.
- Container (Docker / Podman): run with `--network=host` and the
  appropriate env vars pointing at the host's daemons:
    -e NX_T2_ADDR=127.0.0.1:<t2_tcp_port>
    -e NX_T3_ADDR=127.0.0.1:<t3_tcp_port>
    -e NX_PYTEST_DAEMON_MODE=1   # if running tests
  Container can also mount `~/.config/nexus/` read-only as a
  fallback for discovery-file resolution; not strictly needed
  when env vars are explicit.

MVV steps:
1. Host: `nx memory put nexus_rdr container-mvv-1 "container-wrote-this" --tags=mvv`
2. Container: `nx memory get nexus_rdr container-mvv-1` — verify
   the row round-trips.
3. Container: `nx memory put nexus_rdr container-mvv-2 "host-reads-this"`
4. Host: `nx memory get nexus_rdr container-mvv-2` — verify
   bidirectional visibility.
5. Record timings, schema-version-handshake outcomes, and any
   errors observed. Stress: 10 sequential read+write cycles
   from a tight container-side loop.

Acceptance:
- Round-trip clean in both directions.
- T2 handshake (database.hello) succeeds with no
  DeprecationWarning fire and no schema-version mismatch.
- T2 receipt 120-container-mvv-tcp-receipt with timings and
  exact incantation.

Out of scope (separate beads):
- UDS socket path (companion bead).
- Operator-facing documentation (companion bead).
- Non-loopback TCP (not enabled; banlist).

title: phase-review-gate skill: recognize phase-block sub-bullets as items (RDR-120 follow-on)
description:

title: Build stable test fixtures for knowledge__hybridrag and knowledge__delos corpora (replace prod dependency)
description:
Two integration test files currently fail with 'corpus returned 0 hits' because they depend on production-only corpora that no longer exist:

- tests/test_hybrid_plan_factual_qa.py: requires knowledge__hybridrag (5 fixtures: fx-1 through fx-5). Documented in the file's docstring as 'The harness assumes knowledge__hybridrag has been indexed and catalog-linked locally before running.'
- tests/integration/test_rdr_093_groupby_aggregate_pipelines.py: requires knowledge__delos for the MVV BFT/consensus query. Two tests fail: test_search_filter_groupby_aggregate_end_to_end and test_aggregate_summaries_reference_inline_body_content.

Status confirmed 2026-05-20 during 4.33.0 release prep: nx collection list shows no knowledge__delos and no knowledge__hybridrag locally; the prod corpora these tests reference are gone. Tests have been silently failing on this dependency for some time; they passed the v4.32.14 release because nobody re-ran -m integration before tagging.

Work:
1. Decide on a small, stable, checked-in fixture corpus shape for each (a handful of representative chunks each, small enough to commit or to seed deterministically at test setup).
2. Add a conftest fixture or session-scoped setup that indexes the fixture corpus into a deterministic collection name before the tests run.
3. Update the tests' TARGET_COLLECTION constants to the new fixture collection name.
4. Add a skip-when-missing guard so a developer without the fixture indexed gets 'skipped: fixture corpus not present' instead of 'returned 0 hits'.

Surface as the corpus-fixture-vs-prod-dependency lesson: integration tests should never depend on a live external corpus the maintainers cannot reproduce on demand.
notes:
REASSESSED 2026-05-28: step 4 (skip-when-missing guard) is ALREADY DONE. Both test files skip cleanly when the corpus is absent — verified: 'uv run pytest <both> -m integration' -> 18 skipped, 1 passed, 0 FAILED. test_hybrid_plan_factual_qa.py has _corpus_indexed + requires_full_stack/requires_t3_only skipif markers; test_rdr_093...py has _skip_without_live_deps fixture calling _corpus_indexed(DELOS_COLLECTION) with pytest.skip. The bead's premise ('fail with 0 hits', 'silently failing') is STALE — the silent-failure-at-release problem the bead was really about is resolved; missing corpus -> graceful skip with an actionable message, not a hard fail.

REMAINING SCOPE (steps 1-3 only): build a small, checked-in, deterministic fixture corpus for knowledge__hybridrag (5 fixtures fx-1..fx-5) + knowledge__delos so the tests actively PASS instead of skip (restores lost active coverage). Requires an embedding-function decision: MiniLM-local (no API, deterministic, but different neighbours than voyage so fixture ground-truth must be EF-robust) vs voyage-CCE (matches prod retrieval but needs API keys + >=2 chunks). Medium task, lower urgency than originally framed since the failure mode is already contained. Recommend pairing the EF decision with whoever owns the hybrid-plan / RDR-093 retrieval-quality validation.

title: setup_cmd split-store race when daemon comes up between Catalog.init and open_catalog
description:
RDR-112 6shq chak review surfaced a narrow race in setup_cmd (commands/catalog.py:244-260): if NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon and the daemon is DOWN at line 244 (Catalog.init time) but UP by line 260 (open_catalog call), the bootstrap creates a fallback direct-mode CatalogDB at .catalog.db while subsequent ops write to the daemon's memory.db — recreating exactly the split-store residue that 6shq.5 set out to prevent.

The chak gate folded in bootstrap_fallback_active=True on the fallback Catalog (catalog.py:831 area) so the degraded state is now machine-detectable, but setup_cmd does not yet check the flag. Two options for the fix:

(a) setup_cmd should pass the catalog instance returned by Catalog.init to its downstream calls (avoid the second open_catalog), so the second open's mode mismatch cannot occur.

(b) setup_cmd should check cat.bootstrap_fallback_active after Catalog.init and either retry open_catalog OR raise a ClickException with 'daemon came up mid-bootstrap; rerun setup' guidance.

Option (a) is simpler structurally but requires audit of every consumer of Catalog.init's return value (currently init_cmd discards it). Option (b) is local but adds operator burden.

Out of scope for chak: chak is the close-out review gate, not new feature scope. Filing as P2.

title: RDR-112 follow-up - add parameter binding to T2 daemon exec_raw RPC
description:
Surfaced during nexus-cj1a Phase 4 review gate (2026-05-18).

## Symptom

`src/nexus/daemon/introspection.py:exec_raw(sql: str)` accepts only a raw SQL string. The daemon-side connection is opened with `mode=ro` so writes are blocked, but the RPC has no parameter-binding interface — callers must interpolate values into the SQL string.

The pac1 fix in `commands/doctor.py:_run_check_tier_discipline` works around this by quote-escaping `session_id` inline (`"'" + session_id.replace("'", "''") + "'"`). Today the input is bounded (UUID-shaped, not adversarial). The pattern is now in the codebase as the canonical idiom for exec_raw with variable inputs.

## Risk

Phase 5+ admin checks that need exec_raw with user-supplied input (collection name, title, tag value) will copy this quoting pattern onto less-trusted strings. Server-side `mode=ro` prevents writes but does not prevent information disclosure or unexpected query behaviour from malformed SQL on a read-only handle.

## Recommendation

Add `params: dict[str, Any] | None = None` to `IntrospectionService.exec_raw`. Pass through to `sqlite3.connect().execute(sql, params)`. Update the doctor.py tier-discipline call to use `WHERE session_id = :session_id` with `params={"session_id": session_id}`.

## Files

- `src/nexus/daemon/introspection.py` — exec_raw signature + impl
- `src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py` — `call('exec_raw', {'sql': ..., 'params': ...})` plumbing (probably already supports arbitrary args dicts)
- `src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:_run_check_tier_discipline` — drop the inline quote escape; use parameter binding
- `tests/daemon/test_t2_client_facade.py` — round-trip test for exec_raw with params

## Filed by

nexus-cj1a Phase 4 review gate, substantive-critic Significant #2.
close_reason: RDRs 110-118 scrapped 2026-05-19 (commit 2bc112a6). Bead orphaned.

title: RDR-112 follow-up — daemon-mode RPC enablement for document_aspects + dataclass-arg ops
description:
Surfaced during nexus-yfqv (P4.2) audit.

## Symptom

`nx enrich aspects-show`, `nx enrich info`, `nx enrich delete`, and aspect upserts via `nx enrich aspects` fail under `NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon` with `T2DaemonError: unknown RPC op: 'document_aspects.<method>'`.

## Root cause

`src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py` `_RPC_DENY_OPS` (lines 246-257) blocks:

- `document_aspects.upsert` (accepts AspectRecord dataclass arg)
- `document_aspects.get` (denied; reason TBD — return type is dataclass but encoder tags it)
- `document_aspects.get_by_doc_id` (same as get)
- `catalog.transaction` / `catalog.bulk_load_documents` (contextmanagers)

The comment names the rationale: "Methods whose signature accepts a dataclass instance cannot round-trip JSON until a typed-arg reconstructor lands. Re-enable as the reconstructor adds coverage."

## Why not yfqv

The yfqv flip (make_t3 → get_t3 inside enrich bib) was contained. The deny-list gap is substrate scope — needs:

1. A typed-arg reconstructor (encoder→decoder roundtrip for AspectRecord) on the daemon side.
2. Tests that exercise the dataclass-arg ops via T2Client → daemon.
3. Re-evaluation of why `get` and `get_by_doc_id` are denied (return-only paths should already work given `AspectRecord` is in `_ALLOWED_DATACLASS_TYPES`).

## Files

- `src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py` `_RPC_DENY_OPS` — remove ops as coverage lands.
- `src/nexus/daemon/_codec.py` (or equivalent) — typed-arg decoder.
- `tests/daemon/test_t2_client_facade.py` — add round-trip coverage for AspectRecord/QueueRow/etc.
- `tests/commands/test_enrich_daemon_mode.py` — once deny lifts, replace the `TestStoreProxyHygiene` unit pin with an end-to-end `aspects-show` test (the test author left a stub in the yfqv commit's diff message).

## Related

- Pre-yfqv `enrich aspects-show` called `db.document_aspects._has_doc_id_pk()` — a private method that `_StoreProxy` skipped at dispatch build, so the call AttributeError'd under daemon mode. yfqv refactored to chained `get_by_doc_id or get(...)`; both ops are public-name proxied but still hit the deny list above. Refactor lands in `feature/nexus-yfqv-cli-port-search-enrich` (PR forthcoming).

## Acceptance

- All deny-list ops moved out of `_RPC_DENY_OPS`.
- `nx enrich aspects-show <tumbler>` works under `NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon`.
- `nx enrich aspects <collection>` (full extraction) works under daemon mode.
- Replacement integration test in `test_enrich_daemon_mode.py` covers aspects-show.

title: RDR-112 P1.5.4 — nx daemon t3 install/uninstall (launchd/systemd autostart unit, mirrors T2 install)
description:
## Context

Phase 1.5 of RDR-112 (epic nexus-8hy6). T2 has `nx daemon t2 install` + `uninstall` at src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:896/1025 — generates a launchd plist (macOS) or systemd user unit (Linux) so the daemon survives reboot. T3 needs the same so production deployments have parity. Priority P2 (lower than impl beads) because nexus-hpxl doesn't require autostart — manual `nx daemon t3 start` is sufficient for the MCP flip. Ship for operational completeness.

## Acceptance

- `nx daemon t3 install [--config-dir ...]` — generates and registers an autostart unit:
  - macOS: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.nexus.t3-daemon.plist` (loaded via `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid>`).
  - Linux: `~/.config/systemd/user/nexus-t3-daemon.service` (enabled via `systemctl --user enable`).
  - Unit invokes `nx daemon t3 start --foreground --announce-stdout` so the OS supervisor captures lifecycle.
  - Pins `NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR` via the unit environment (mirrors nexus-mcr9 fix for T2).
- `nx daemon t3 uninstall [--config-dir ...]` — unloads + removes the unit file. Idempotent.
- `nx daemon t3 doctor [--config-dir ...]` (optional, mirrors T2 doctor_cmd at daemon.py:233) — surfaces install state, last-launch result, common failure modes.
- TDD: tests in `tests/daemon/test_t3_install.py` cover:
  - (a) macOS install creates plist with expected ProgramArguments + EnvironmentVariables.
  - (b) Linux install creates systemd unit with expected ExecStart + Environment lines.
  - (c) uninstall removes the unit file and is idempotent (second call no-ops).
  - (d) install detects an existing unit and refuses (with --force override).
- Code review MANDATORY after impl.

## Dependencies

- Depends on nexus-s3dm (P1.5.1) — the install unit invokes `nx daemon t3 start --foreground`.

## Files

- `src/nexus/commands/daemon.py` — add `install_cmd` and `uninstall_cmd` under `t3_group`, copying the structure from t2_group's equivalents (daemon.py:896-1100).
- `tests/daemon/test_t3_install.py` (new)

## Reminders

- T2's install/uninstall implementation is the template — read daemon.py:896-1100 first; the plist + systemd unit shapes are battle-tested.
- Sequential thinking for the `NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR` env passdown (RDR-112 P0-gate CONTRACT, nexus-mcr9 — same pattern applies to T3).
- SPAWN code-review-expert in parallel with test-validator after impl.

## Out of scope

- Cross-platform peer-cred (T2's RDR-113 work, nexus-dsxd) — T3 is TCP-only loopback, peer-cred N/A.

Tests written FIRST: (a) install --autostart writes correct plist/unit file (compare against T2 plist template at daemon.py:896-1100), (b) the autostart unit invokes 'nx daemon t3 start' with the right working directory + env, (c) uninstall removes file cleanly and stops a running daemon.

title: DR-5: Cross-subspace spurious-wake characteristic undocumented
description:
**NOTABLE.** From the 360° architectural review.

## Issue

`blocking_take` poll wakes on ANY `data_version` increment across all subspaces, acquires service lock per wake, calls take() (which holds the shared connection lock for the chroma + SQL query). On high cross-subspace write rates, N concurrent blocking_take callers each speculatively acquire the lock per-commit, multiplying contention linearly.

The direct-mode `_DataVersionWatcher` has the same characteristic (subspace-blind), so this is an accepted v1 trade-off — but it's NOT documented in the service docstring.

## Fix

Add a comment to `TuplespaceService.blocking_take` noting:
- Cross-subspace spurious-wake characteristic
- Scaling: O(N × commit_rate) lock acquisitions
- v2 path: per-subspace threading.Event (see HR-1 backlog)

No code change.
close_reason: shipped via Bundle DR

title: TR-1: test_start_skips_announce_when_disabled doesn't exercise the production gate
description:
**NOTABLE (contract gap).** From the 360° test review.

## Bug

`tests/daemon/test_cockpit_boundary_bundle_c.py:244` test does NOT call `start()`. It manually evaluates `if daemon._announce_stdout_enabled: daemon._announce_stdout()` and asserts `called["n"] == 0`. A future regression that accidentally removes the `if` condition from start() would not be caught.
