title: HR-3: blocking_take data_version polling is vestigial machinery
description:
**NOTABLE.** From the 360° line-level code review.

## Issue

`tuplespace_service.py:230-321` blocking_take loop polls `take()` every 10ms unconditionally. When `current_version == last_version` the `continue` sends control back to the top of `while True`, which calls `take()` again; when the version changes, it falls through to the same top-of-loop `take()` call. The version state only updates `last_version` — it does not gate or defer the retry.

The docstring + module comment describe the mechanism as 'wakes on PRAGMA data_version increments' — implies event-driven behaviour. The actual behaviour is a fixed 10ms poll regardless of commits.

## Impact

Functionally correct (10ms cadence meets the CA-5 latency budget). But the data_version overhead is unnecessary machinery in the daemon-side path. The direct-mode `_DataVersionWatcher` uses it correctly (single threading.Event that fires on commit); the daemon-side equivalent just polls.

## Fix

Either:
(a) Remove the data_version tracking; simplify to a pure 10ms poll loop.
(b) Make the wait actually wait — sleep until data_version changes OR deadline fires, using PRAGMA data_version as an event source.

Recommend (a): simplest, matches actual behaviour. Update docstring.

title: events table query uses GLOB '*' defeating idx_events_subspace_rowid
description:
Architectural S4: bindings.py:_fetch_event_batch issues 'WHERE subspace GLOB ? AND rowid > ?' with default subspace_glob='*'. SQLite cannot use B-tree prefix scan when GLOB pattern starts with wildcard. idx_events_subspace_rowid unused; full-table scan per _tick. Negligible at current volume; degrades linearly. No retention on events table itself.

Fix: when glob is '*' use 'WHERE rowid > ?' (no subspace predicate). When glob has prefix-no-wildcard like 'tasks/*' use 'WHERE subspace >= ? AND subspace < ? AND rowid > ?' (range scan). Plus: add events table retention to retention sweeper.

title: _t2_decode: deny unknown __dataclass__ payloads

Once the retention sweeper ships, the row could expire on the first fire's timestamp despite recent activity. Fix: INSERT ... title: hook-bridge: subspace registration ordering hazard — bridge fires before nexus-78mh registers schemas with daemon
description: The seven hook-event YAMLs ship in nx/tuplespace/builtin/hooks/. They are loaded by _load_registry_with_hooks at bridge invocation time (direct mode). But they are NOT registered with the daemon subspace registry until nexus-78mh (CA-9 coordination) runs. If a bridge fires BEFORE nexus-78mh completes: direct mode succeeds (local registry has the schemas); daemon mode (nexus-pce1.6 future path) would fail with UnknownSubspaceError. This is a sequencing hazard for the Phase 3 daemon-mode cutover. Document the ordering requirement explicitly in both nexus-78mh and the bridge code, and add a guard in _emit_direct_auto that catches UnknownSubspaceError and logs a structured warning (not exception) with remediation hint. title: hook-bridge: test fixture uses embed_from:content while production YAMLs use embed_from:match_text — _emit_direct_auto path untested
description: The hook_registry fixture (tests/cockpit/test_hook_bridge.py) writes inline YAMLs with embed_from: content. Production YAMLs (nx/tuplespace/builtin/hooks/*.yml) all use embed_from: match_text. The emit() tests inject conn+index+registry, bypassing _emit_direct_auto entirely. Result: (1) no test exercises the actual production schema loading path (_load_registry_with_hooks with subdirs=(hooks,)); (2) no test verifies the embed_from=match_text path against real schema; (3) the fallback match_text or content in _resolve_embed_text is exercised differently. Add: test that loads production YAMLs directly via _load_registry_with_hooks and asserts embed_from=match_text, plus an integration test of _emit_direct_auto with a tmp nexus config dir. Context: post-merge audit of nexus-y0nb (PR #784)

title: hook-bridge: _emit_direct_auto opens PersistentClient on every hook invocation — timeout hazard for high-frequency hooks
description: PostToolUse fires on every Bash/Read/Write/Edit call. _emit_direct_auto opens chromadb.PersistentClient + open_tuples_db + loads registry from YAML on each invocation. ChromaDB PersistentClient init is 200-500ms on warm Python, heavier cold. With a 5s hook timeout, a slow disk or concurrent chroma write could cause the hook to be killed mid-write, leaving tuples.db in a partially committed state (SQLite WAL mitigates but does not eliminate). Also: no SIGTERM handler means interrupted writes on timeout. Fix options: (a) module-level singleton with lazy init + lock, (b) registry + conn cached via module state, (c) keep as-is but document and monitor. Context: post-merge audit of nexus-y0nb (PR #784)
close_reason: shipped via commit 5de3f641 + b3199c5e (RDR-112 cutover) — module-level singleton client; later subsumed by daemon-mode preferring T2Client RPC. Hot path no longer opens PersistentClient per invocation. Audited 2026-05-17.

title: hook-bridge: Stop/StopFailure and SessionStart/SessionEnd lack variant dimension discriminator
description: Both Stop+StopFailure map to assistant_turn_ended; both SessionStart+SessionEnd map to session_lifecycle. Neither pair writes a 'variant' or 'event_type' dimension, so downstream consumers cannot filter by hook event type. _build_dimensions ignores hook_type for these cases. match_text contains the literal hook_type string but that is not a queryable dimension. Fix: add an event_type required dimension to both subspace YAMLs and populate it from hook_type in _build_dimensions. Context: post-merge audit of nexus-y0nb (PR #784)

title: RDR-112 Phase 3 — MCP tuplespace_* tools route through T2Client under NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the Track D Phase 1 review and confirmed via live smoke. Under \`NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon\`, \`mcp/core.py\` \`_get_tuplespace()\` returns \`{conn: None, index: None}\`. The eight MCP tuplespace_* tools (\`tuplespace_out\`, \`tuplespace_read\`, \`tuplespace_take\`, \`tuplespace_ack\`, \`tuplespace_nack\`, \`tuplespace_list_subspaces\`, \`tuplespace_subspace_schema\`, \`tuplespace_subspace_stats\`) then call \`api.out(conn=None, index=None, ...)\` which raises \`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'execute'\` on the first conn.execute() inside api.

This is genuinely Phase-3 work: the routing pattern depends on the full T2 daemon surface (now stable) and likely on whatever Phase 2 (nexus-7ejx CatalogDB collapse) does to the dispatch table.

## Scope

Add new daemon-side RPCs for the eight tuplespace operations, wrap the existing api functions server-side, and have mcp/core.py dispatch to T2Client.call when storage_mode == "daemon".

## Acceptance

- Daemon-side: register 8 new ops in t2_daemon.py dispatch table:
  - tuplespace.out
  - tuplespace.read
  - tuplespace.take
  - tuplespace.ack
  - tuplespace.nack
  - tuplespace.list_subspaces
  - tuplespace.subspace_schema
  - tuplespace.subspace_stats
  
  Each wraps the corresponding api function with a daemon-owned (conn, index) pair.

- mcp/core.py: when NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon, MCP tools dispatch via T2Client.call("tuplespace.<verb>", args) instead of calling api.<verb> directly. Direct-mode path unchanged.

- T2Client.tuplespace.out/read/take/... store-proxy attribute exposed so callers can use the typed accessor instead of bare client.call().

- Tests: same surface coverage as the direct-mode api tests, but driven through the daemon. Reuse test_api.py patterns; new test_tuplespace_daemon_routing.py runs the 8 ops via T2Client against a real daemon.

- Live smoke: start daemon, set NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon, call tuplespace_out + tuplespace_read via the MCP tools. Both succeed.

## Coordination

- BLOCKED on Phase 2 (nexus-7ejx CatalogDB collapse) — the dispatch table shape may change. Do not start until Phase 2 lands.
- Phase 3 cutover (nexus-507q NX_STORAGE_MODE default direct -> daemon) depends on this bead.

## Files

- src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py — dispatch entries
- src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py — tuplespace proxy
- src/nexus/mcp/core.py — daemon-mode dispatch
- src/nexus/tuplespace/api.py — minor refactor if signatures need adjustment
- tests/daemon/test_tuplespace_daemon_routing.py (new)
close_reason: RDRs 110-118 scrapped 2026-05-19 (commit 2bc112a6). Bead orphaned.

title: CI flake — tests/test_migrations.py concurrency tests fail intermittently on Linux
description:
## Context

Two tests in tests/test_migrations.py fail intermittently on Linux CI runners:

- test_concurrent_apply_pending_runs_once — assert 2 == 1 (failed CI run 25895886398, 2026-05-15 01:50:47 on x98k branch; same code passed on develop run 25895889296 at 01:50:53)
- test_run_if_needed_fast_path_second_call — Expected 'apply_pending' to not have been called. Called 1 times. (failed CI run 25894819239 on develop, 2026-05-15 01:14:16)

Both are concurrency-related: they assert that the migration lock (_upgrade_lock) + cache (_upgrade_done set) prevent double-apply across threads. Failures suggest a latent race: when thread 1 enters the lock, calls bootstrap_version, releases the lock, then adds path_key to _upgrade_done — there is a window where bootstrap_version has run but the cache add hasn't, so thread 2 acquiring next still sees an empty cache and runs bootstrap again.

The test passes locally and on many CI runs; Phase 1 RDR-112 work (run_daemon_migrations, migrate_tuples_*, migrate_subspace_registry_table) exercises the migration surface much more heavily and is exposing the race more often. It is NOT a Phase 1 regression — the bug is in apply_pending's lock scope.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce locally with stress (loop the failing test N times under load).
- Fix: move _upgrade_done.add(path_key) inside the same critical section as the bootstrap_version call. Currently the assumption is "we add to the set under the lock" but verify by reading src/nexus/db/migrations.py apply_pending.
- Alternative fix path: use a per-path lock instead of a global one — eliminates the race for distinct paths.
- Tests must pass 50 consecutive runs of the affected test files under the existing concurrency.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring the entire migration system. Surgical fix only.
- Phase 1 RDR-112 daemon work — that surface is not introducing this bug.

## Files

- src/nexus/db/migrations.py (apply_pending lock scope)
- tests/test_migrations.py (TestApplyPending::test_concurrent_apply_pending_runs_once, TestT2DatabaseIntegration::test_run_if_needed_fast_path_second_call)
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-112 m4gm follow-up — denormalize subspace into tuple_claim_log (eliminate COALESCE empty-subspace silent-drop)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by code review of PR #771 (nexus-m4gm, EventStream RPC). The \`trg_claim_log_event\` trigger uses \`COALESCE((SELECT subspace FROM tuples WHERE id = NEW.tuple_id), '')\` to handle the case where a tuple is hard-deleted before its nack log entry is committed (e.g., 30-day retention sweep races a slow nack).

The empty-string fallback emits an event with \`subspace=''\` into the \`events\` table. No subscriber's GLOB pattern (e.g., \`"tuples/foo*"\`) matches an empty string, so the nack event is silently invisible to all subspace-filtered subscribers — even though it lives in the events table.

## Acceptance

Pick ONE of these two paths:

**(a) Denormalize subspace into \`tuple_claim_log\`** — add a \`subspace TEXT\` column to tuple_claim_log, populate at INSERT time from \`api.py\` claim/ack/nack code paths. Update \`trg_claim_log_event\` trigger to use \`NEW.subspace\` directly (no JOIN, no COALESCE). Migration step in \`run_daemon_migrations\`. Idempotent.

**(b) Subscriber-side filter** — in \`event_stream.handle_event_stream\`, reject events with \`subspace = ''\` as noise + emit a structured warning log. Document the trade-off in store.py.

Path (a) is correct and surfaces the events to subscribers. Path (b) is the easier ship and acknowledges the drop. Prefer (a) unless schema/migration cost rules it out.

## Tests

- Acquire a tuple, hard-delete its row from \`tuples\` (simulating retention sweep), THEN write the nack into \`tuple_claim_log\`. Subscribe to that subspace's GLOB. Assert the nack event is delivered.
- Under path (a): a regression test that confirms \`tuple_claim_log.subspace\` matches \`tuples.subspace\` for normal claim/ack flows.

## Files

- \`src/nexus/tuplespace/store.py\` (DDL + trigger)
- \`src/nexus/tuplespace/api.py\` (claim/ack/nack write paths under path a)
- \`src/nexus/db/migrations.py\` (upgrade migration under path a)
- \`tests/daemon/test_event_stream.py\` (regression test)
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-112 follow-up — dataclass-arg RPC reconstructor (re-enables document_aspects.upsert/get/get_by_doc_id)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by code review of PR #768 (nexus-qy0u). `document_aspects.upsert(record: AspectRecord)`, `document_aspects.get(...) -> AspectRecord | None`, and `document_aspects.get_by_doc_id(...) -> AspectRecord | None` cannot round-trip JSON: the daemon's `_t2_decode` returns plain dicts for dataclass-tagged frames (by design), so `fn(record={...dict})` raises `TypeError` against a method expecting `AspectRecord`. The three ops are currently in `_RPC_DENY_OPS` in `t2_daemon.py`.

Re-enabling them needs a typed-arg reconstructor that:

1. At dispatch-table build time, inspects each method's parameter type hints.
2. Identifies dataclass-typed parameters.
3. On call, when the wire frame's `__dataclass__` tag matches a registered dataclass, reconstructs the instance before invoking the method.
4. On the return path, encodes dataclass return values as `{__dataclass__: cls, fields: {...}}` (already done) AND on the client side, reconstructs to the dataclass instance instead of leaving as `dict`.

## Acceptance

- Server-side: `_build_dispatch_table` reads `inspect.signature(method).parameters` and for each parameter whose annotation is a dataclass (or `dataclass | None`), records the type. On call, decode the arg from the `__dataclass__` tag and instantiate before invoking.
- Client-side: `T2Client` proxy method introspects the return-type annotation; if dataclass, reconstructs from `{__dataclass__: ..., fields: ...}` on receive.
- Remove the three entries from `_RPC_DENY_OPS` in `t2_daemon.py`.
- Tests: extend `TestDocumentAspectsStore` (currently in `test_t2_client_parity.py`) with round-trip tests for `upsert`, `get`, `get_by_doc_id`.
- Tests: round-trip preserves type identity — `isinstance(client.document_aspects.get(...), AspectRecord)` returns True.
- A negative test confirms an unknown dataclass tag (registered server-side but not client-side) raises a clear error rather than silently returning a dict.

## Files

- `src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py` (dispatch-table build + arg reconstruction)
- `src/nexus/daemon/t2_client.py` (return-value reconstruction in `_StoreProxy._call`)
- `tests/daemon/test_t2_client_parity.py` (re-enable + add upsert/get coverage)

## Security note

The reconstructor must NOT use `eval`, `pickle`, or any other arbitrary-class-instantiation primitive. Restrict to dataclasses registered at startup via an explicit module-level allowlist (e.g. `_RPC_DATACLASSES: dict[str, type] = {"AspectRecord": AspectRecord, ...}`). The dispatch-table builder validates each method's dataclass parameters are in the allowlist; methods referencing unlisted dataclasses raise at startup, not at first call.

## Out of scope

- Generalising to non-dataclass typed args (e.g. `Pydantic.BaseModel`). Dataclasses only for v1.
close_reason: RDRs 110-118 scrapped 2026-05-19 (commit 2bc112a6). Bead orphaned.

title: RDR-112 follow-up — taxonomy RPC write-path test coverage (3/59 ops exercised)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by code review of PR #768 (nexus-qy0u, T2 domain-store RPCs). Taxonomy is the largest RPC namespace at 59 ops — 39% of the 150-op surface — but only 3 read-only ops are exercised by tests (`get_all_topics`, `get_distinct_collections`, both on a fresh empty DB; plus rename_collection_cascade no-op).

Methods like `assign_topic`, `delete_topic`, `compute_icf_map`, `detect_hubs`, `update_topic_label`, and the entire write-path of the taxonomy store have zero RPC parity coverage. Phase 3 of RDR-112 will flip taxonomy call-sites to the daemon path via T2Client — if a wire-format bug exists in any write-path method, it will land in production undetected.

## Acceptance

- Identify the taxonomy write-path methods most likely to be Phase-3-critical (start with: `assign_topic`, `delete_topic`, `update_topic_label`, `compute_icf_map`, `detect_hubs`).
- For each, add a parametrized RPC parity test: build identical fixture state in two T2Database instances (one direct, one daemon-fronted), run the method, assert outputs match.
- Reach at least 50% method coverage on the taxonomy namespace (30 of 59 ops).
- Tests live in `tests/daemon/test_t2_client_parity.py` extending the existing `TestTaxonomyStore` class.

## Files

- `tests/daemon/test_t2_client_parity.py`
- `src/nexus/db/taxonomy.py` (reference only — don't modify)

## Out of scope

- New taxonomy features
- Refactoring the taxonomy store
- Coverage of `document_aspects.upsert/get/get_by_doc_id` (separate follow-up — typed-arg reconstructor)

## Notes

Use `inspect.getmembers(t2db.taxonomy, predicate=inspect.ismethod)` to enumerate the surface. Skip underscore-prefixed and `close`. Prioritize methods that mutate state — read-only methods on empty fixtures don't catch wire-format bugs.

title: RDR-112/113 — Gate admin RPCs to UDS only (thread is_uds through dispatcher)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the 2026-05-14 360-review. The shipped t2_daemon.py (PR #766) routes all RPC ops through a single `_handle_connection` path with no transport-type discrimination. The `is_uds` flag is not threaded through to the RPC dispatcher.

This means admin RPCs (highest blast radius: `subspace_add`, `apply_pending_migrations`, `import`) will be reachable over loopback TCP. RDR-113 host-trust model (TCP is loopback-only but admin ops should still require UDS + peer-cred) is not enforced for admin ops.

nexus-niun's RDR-113 audit will surface this gap; this bead provides a home for the fix.

## Acceptance

- `_handle_connection` and the RPC dispatcher accept and propagate an `is_uds: bool` flag derived from `writer.transport.get_extra_info('socket').family == socket.AF_UNIX`.
- A set of admin op names (`subspace_add`, `apply_pending_migrations`, `import`, plus any future admin op) is declared at module level (e.g. `_ADMIN_OPS: frozenset[str]`).
- Dispatcher rejects admin ops on TCP with `{error: {type: 'PermissionDenied', message: 'admin op <name> requires UDS transport'}}`.
- TDD: tests covering (a) admin op succeeds over UDS, (b) same admin op rejected over TCP with expected error frame, (c) non-admin op succeeds over both transports.

title: RDR-112 P1.x — daemon-health probe at cli.main when NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon
description:
Phase-1 leaf surfaced by the round-3 comprehensive review (2026-05-13, foundational analyst).

The uqqy round-3 fix added a NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon early-return guard at cli.main, deferring migration responsibility to the daemon's startup runner (nexus-w0et). The guard is correct, but if a user sets NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon with no daemon actually running, the migration step silently skips. Downstream RPC will fail loudly when the first T2 op is attempted — not corrupting, but the failure happens late and the user doesn't get a clean "daemon not reachable" message at CLI entry.

Acceptance:
- Add a daemon-reachability probe at cli.main when NX_STORAGE_MODE=daemon. Plausible implementations:
  (a) Read the daemon address from $NX_T2_ADDR or the discovery file (~/.config/nexus/sockets/...), open a UDS connection, send a no-op ping RPC, close. ~50ms in the happy path.
  (b) Stat the discovery file's existence as a cheap pre-check before the RPC roundtrip.
- On failure: emit a structured warning + TTY-gated stderr alert pointing at `nx daemon status` (or whatever the diagnostic command becomes).
- Test: simulate daemon-mode + no daemon; assert cli.main produces the alert and doesn't crash.

Depends on:
- nexus-w0et (daemon startup runner) — defines the discovery-file layout the probe reads.
- nexus-61x6 (daemon scaffold + UDS transport) — provides the RPC surface to ping.

Don't claim until those are at least scaffolded.

description:
## Context

title: RDR-111 P2.3 — X.3 cross-RDR coordination: failure-category demux contract with RDR-112 nexus-m4gm
description:

  - `event.category=data` + tool_call raises → action failure (cursor advances, counter++)
  - `event.category=data` + transport drops → substrate failure (no cursor advance, reconnect with backoff)

  - `event.category=substrate` → not dispatched, log only

title: RDR-113 P3 — SECURITY.md documenting v1 host-trust boundary + forward-reference to future cross-host auth RDR
description:
## Context

Parent epic: nexus-07z0 (RDR-113). RDR-113 commits to a written threat model with explicit non-goals. The RDR file itself documents this, but a project-level `SECURITY.md` surfaces the boundary for users / packagers / reviewers who don't read RDRs.

## Acceptance

- New `SECURITY.md` at repo root with the following sections:
  - **Trust Boundary (v1)**: nexus daemons are designed for single-user host trust. The daemon owner and the connecting client must share a UID. Lifted verbatim or condensed from RDR-113 §Approach §1-§3.
  - **Threats Addressed**: second-user-on-same-host attach, TCP listener escape to network — both blocked. Verbatim from RDR-113 §Threat Model.
  - **Threats NOT Addressed (Accepted Risk)**: same-user malicious process, compromised parent process injecting env vars, cross-host attacks. Verbatim from RDR-113 §Threat Model + §Approach §5.
  - **Forward Reference**: token-based auth lands in a future RDR when the threat model expands (cross-host / multi-user / federated). Until then, the host-local v1 path is the supported deployment.
  - **Reporting**: how to disclose a security issue (private email or GitHub security advisory).
- README.md gets a short \"Security\" subsection linking to SECURITY.md.
- No prose duplication of the RDR — SECURITY.md is the user-facing summary; the RDR is the design record.
- No em-dashes per project style.

## Files

- `SECURITY.md` (new)
- `README.md` — add a one-paragraph \"Security\" subsection linking to SECURITY.md.

## Reminders

- This is a documentation bead — no code review needed, but a substantive-critic pass is useful: dispatch substantive-critic on the draft to catch over-claiming.
- The RDR file is the source of truth. If SECURITY.md and the RDR conflict at any time, the RDR wins; SECURITY.md is the synopsis.
- Project preference: no em-dashes in prose (see MEMORY.md `feedback_no_em_dashes`).

title: RDR-110 P3.2 — Cross-RDR: peer-cred enforcement on daemon RPCs touching mailbox/<agent> (RDR-113)
description:
## Context

This is RDR-110's side of the contract: confirm that the daemon's RPC handlers for tuple-space operations on agent-private subspaces (mailbox in particular) honor RDR-113.

## Acceptance

- Audit the daemon RPC handlers for `tuplespace_out`, `tuplespace_read`, `tuplespace_take`, `tuplespace_ack`, `tuplespace_nack` against RDR-113 §Proposed Solution. Confirm:
  - UDS bind discipline (`os.chmod(0o600)` after bind, before listen).
  - Peer-cred check at `accept()` — connecting process UID matches daemon's UID.
  - TCP listeners (if any) loopback-only (`127.0.0.1` or `::1`).
- Integration test: simulate a connection from a different UID (via test fixture) — daemon refuses.
- Documented in `docs/architecture.md` tuplespace section that `mailbox/<agent>` and other agent-private subspaces inherit RDR-113 trust model — no application-layer auth in v1.

## Coordination

- **Cross-bead dependency**: RDR-112 nexus-niun (RDR-113 enforcement audit on daemon RPCs). This RDR-110 bead is the tuple-space-specific check; nexus-niun is the broader daemon audit. Coordinate so both audits use the same harness.

description:
## Context

- Validation rules (from RDR-110 §Subspace registry): name regex, schema-version, field-shape constraints, reserved-prefix checks (`tuples/*` reserved, `daemon/*` reserved).
- Handshake digest: daemon computes a sha256 over the sorted subspace-name → schema-digest map and advertises it on connect. `T2Client` may compare against a cached digest and warn-or-refuse on mismatch.
- CLI: `nx daemon t2 subspace add <yaml>` invokes the admin RPC. Trust gate: admin RPCs require either UDS connection (host-trust per RDR-113) or a future token (deferred).
- TDD: tests cover (a) valid YAML registers and emits event, (b) reserved-prefix collision rejected, (c) duplicate name rejected, (d) digest advertised on next handshake reflects the new registry, (e) RDR-111's seven YAMLs all parse and register cleanly (fixture).
- Code review MANDATORY after impl.

## Coordination

- **RDR-111 CA-9**: this bead is the contract realization point. RDR-111 ships its seven hook-event subspace YAMLs and they install via `nx daemon t2 subspace add` in RDR-111's planning chain. Reference them as a test fixture if available; otherwise stub the seven names and shapes from the RDR.

## Files

- `src/nexus/daemon/t2_daemon.py` — handler + admin gate
- `src/nexus/daemon/subspace_registry.py` (new) — validator + persister
- `src/nexus/commands/daemon.py` — `nx daemon t2 subspace add` subcommand
- `tests/daemon/test_subspace_registry.py` (new)

title: RDR frontmatter flow sequences with unquoted '#'-prefixed refs silently fail YAML parsing
description:
## Symptom

A natural and common pattern in RDR frontmatter — listing PR / issue / bead references in a YAML flow sequence — produces invalid YAML when the refs use `#NNN` syntax without quotes:

```yaml
references:
  prs: [#381, #382, #383, #385, #386, #388, #389]
status: post-mortem
```

YAML 1.1 / 1.2 treats `#` as comment-start at any position where a token doesn't already start. The scanner reads `[`, then `#381, ...` as a comment that consumes the rest of the line including the closing `]`. The flow sequence never closes; the parser runs into the end of the frontmatter looking for `,` or `]`.

Concrete error:

```
yaml.scanner.ScannerError: while parsing a flow sequence
expected ',' or ']', but got '<stream end>'
```

This bites a fresh writer immediately and silently — the YAML "looks right" by eye, and the broken interpretation isn't visible until a downstream consumer chokes.

## Reproduction

```bash
cat > /tmp/repro.yaml <<'EOF'
prs: [#381, #382]
status: x
EOF
python3 -c 'import yaml; print(yaml.safe_load(open("/tmp/repro.yaml")))'
# → yaml.scanner.ScannerError: while parsing a flow sequence ...
```

## Why it matters

- The author's eye sees a perfectly valid list of PR references — the standard `#NNN` GitHub shorthand.
- YAML semantics disagree silently — no inline indication that the line is malformed.
- The downstream consumer (nexus indexer's RDR post-pass) currently hangs on this case rather than continuing past the malformed file (see related bead: indexer-skip-on-frontmatter-parse-failure).
- Pattern is broadly applicable — issues (`#nnn`), beads (`#bead-id`), PRs (`#nnn`), commits all naturally use `#`-prefix references.
- At time of filing this is rare in the corpus (grep `'prs: \[#'` across `docs/rdr/` returned exactly one file) but the trap is general; every new post-mortem or RDR that wants to cite PRs runs the same risk.

## Fix options

(a) **Documentation / template.** Update `docs/rdr/AGENTS.md` (or the RDR template) to require quoting `#`-prefixed refs in flow sequences, with one good and one bad example side-by-side. Cheapest; relies on author discipline.

(b) **Convention switch to block sequences.** Adopt block-form sequences for ref lists in RDR frontmatter:

```yaml
references:
  prs:
    - "#381"
    - "#382"
```

Wider lines, but unambiguous and audit-friendly when diffs land per-ref. Block-form values inside a list don't trigger the `#`-as-comment scanner state in the same way (the leading `- ` puts the scanner in a different state before `#` appears).

(c) **Pre-process in the indexer.** The frontmatter parser used by the indexer could pre-process YAML text to escape `#`-prefixed tokens inside flow sequences before handing to `yaml.safe_load`. Brittle (regex-shaped, has to understand flow-sequence boundaries) but transparent to authors and retrofits cleanly.

(d) **Pre-validate at RDR creation.** The RDR creation skill (`/nx:rdr-create`) or a `nx rdr lint` subcommand could validate frontmatter at write time and reject patterns that won't parse. Catches the bug at the source, not at index time. Naturally pairs with (a).

(e) **Custom YAML loader.** Switch to ruamel.yaml or a YAML 1.2 dialect with different comment-scanning semantics. Non-standard, likely worse than (a)/(b)/(d) — increases dependency surface for a narrow win.

## Recommendation

Combine (a) and (d). Document the quoting / block convention in `docs/rdr/AGENTS.md` with explicit good/bad examples; add a lint step at RDR creation that surfaces flow-sequence-with-`#`-refs as a hard error before the file is committed. (b) as a stylistic convention is fine if the project wants block-form everywhere, but requires migrating existing RDR frontmatter (small task today, larger task if the corpus grows).

Avoid (c) and (e) — they make the framework more complicated to handle a hazard that's better caught at the source.

## Acceptance criteria

- Convention documented in `docs/rdr/AGENTS.md` (or wherever RDR authoring is gated) with a paired good/bad example.
- A pre-write check (lint step in `/nx:rdr-create` or `nx rdr lint`) catches `'\\bprs:\\s*\\[#'`-class patterns and surfaces the hazard as a hard error with the fix suggestion inline.
- Existing offenders fixed. As of 2026-05-13 the grep `prs: \[#` across `docs/rdr/` returned exactly one file (`docs/rdr/post-mortem/nexus-3e4s-catalog-t3-drift.md`); spot-check before merge in case more landed.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the downstream hang — that's the sibling bead (`indexer-skip-on-frontmatter-parse-failure`). Graceful degradation is a separate concern from preventing the situation.

## Refs

- Encountered: operator session 2026-05-13.
- Specific instance: `docs/rdr/post-mortem/nexus-3e4s-catalog-t3-drift.md` line 7.
- Related bead: indexer-skip-on-frontmatter-parse-failure (the hang this pattern triggers downstream).
acceptance_criteria: Convention documented in docs/rdr/AGENTS.md with paired good/bad examples. Pre-write check (lint step in /nx:rdr-create or 'nx rdr lint') catches 'prs: [#…'-class patterns and surfaces the hazard as a hard error with inline fix suggestion. Existing offenders fixed (grep 'prs: \[#' across docs/rdr/ as the floor check).

title: Indexer hangs on YAML frontmatter parse failure during RDR post-pass; should skip and continue
description:
## Symptom

During `nx index repo .`, the main indexing pass completes (e.g. 783/783 files at 100%), but the `[post] Discovering and indexing RDR markdown files…` post-pass hangs indefinitely after emitting:

```
event='frontmatter_parse_failed' timestamp='2026-05-13T01:44:21.963616Z' level='warning'
    error='while parsing a flow sequence
      in "<unicode string>", line 6, column 8:
          prs: [#381, #382, #383, #385, #386, # ...
               ^
    expected '','' or '']'', but got ''<stream end>''
      in "<unicode string>", line 7, column 20:
        status: post-mortem
                           ^'
```

The CLI never returns. CPU drops to near-zero (state `S+`); no further log output. Killing the PID is the only recovery.

## Reproduction

1. Place a markdown file under `docs/rdr/**/` with malformed YAML frontmatter. Easiest seed is a flow sequence containing unquoted `#`-prefixed refs:

```yaml
---
title: "..."
references:
  prs: [#381, #382, #383]
  status: post-mortem
---
```

YAML parses `#381 ...` as a comment, eating the `]`; the flow sequence runs off the end of the frontmatter.

2. `cd <your-repo> && nx index repo .`
3. After the main 100% pass, the post-pass logs the parse warning once, then hangs. No subsequent log output. The process stays in `S+`.

Empirical: 2026-05-13 on `feature/silent-migration-noop` at conexus 4.32.11. The single offending RDR was `docs/rdr/post-mortem/nexus-3e4s-catalog-t3-drift.md` line 7. Quoting the refs (`prs: ["#381", "#382", ...]`) made YAML parse cleanly; until that fix the indexer would have continued hanging on every re-run.

## Expected behavior

Parse failure on one RDR should:

1. Log the warning with the offending **file path** (currently it logs only `<unicode string>` because PyYAML's default name string isn't being overridden; the indexer knows the path but isn't passing it).
2. Skip that single RDR.
3. Continue with remaining RDRs.
4. Surface the skipped count + paths in the post-pass summary so a follow-up `nx rdr lint` (or manual inspection) can find them.

## Where to look

Search `src/nexus/indexer.py` and `src/nexus/commands/index.py` for `frontmatter_parse_failed` to find the warning emit site. Whatever the surrounding control flow is, it should be a per-RDR `try ... except yaml.YAMLError: log_with_path; continue` loop. The hang is downstream of the warning — possibilities ordered by likelihood:

- An async / concurrent.futures task whose exception was swallowed but the awaiter never wakes (most common cause of "log a warning then hang silently").
- A lock or semaphore held across the iteration; the parse-fail branch never releases it.
- Worker process(es) that crash silently; the orchestrator waits forever for join.
- Single-flight retry with an unbounded backoff that the warning didn't break.

A regression test should feed a known-malformed-frontmatter RDR into the post-pass under a wall-clock bound (e.g. 30s) and assert (a) the indexer completes, (b) the skipped file count is surfaced.

## Out of scope

- Fixing the YAML pattern itself — that's the sibling bead (`#`-prefixed refs in flow sequences). This bead is about graceful degradation regardless of the parse-failure cause; the next class of malformed frontmatter (e.g. truncated `---` delimiters, BOM noise) will hit the same hang.

## Refs

- Symptom log captured in operator session 2026-05-13 01:44:21Z.
- Offending fixture: `docs/rdr/post-mortem/nexus-3e4s-catalog-t3-drift.md` (single line — operator quoted the refs; uncommitted at time of bead filing).
- Affected install: conexus 4.32.11, branch `feature/silent-migration-noop`.
- Related bead: rdr-frontmatter-yaml-hash-hazard (the surface pattern that produced this hang).
acceptance_criteria: Malformed YAML frontmatter on a single RDR does NOT hang the indexer. Warning log includes the offending file path (not just '<unicode string>'). Post-pass summary reports skipped RDRs (count + paths) at the end. Pytest regression test feeds a known-malformed frontmatter and asserts the indexer completes within 30-60s wall-clock.
close_reason: Closed

title: catalog doctor replay-equality false-positive on documents.chunk_count
description:
nx catalog doctor --replay-equality reports a documents-table content diff where live SQLite has chunk_count=N (typically 1) and the in-memory event-replay projection has chunk_count=0, on the same doc rows. Observed 2026-05-12 on prod catalog after a clean event-sourced rebuild: collections projection matches (194/194) but documents diff persists.

Root cause: document_chunks is populated by manifest_write_batch_hook (post-store side-effect), not by event-log events. Live SQLite's documents.chunk_count is then set by Catalog.resync_chunk_count_cache(doc_id) which runs OUTSIDE the event log. The projector's in-memory replay (catalog.projector.apply_many) has no document_chunks table to derive from — its post-replay UPDATE re-derive sees zero manifest rows and keeps register-time chunk_count (often 0).

This is not real drift. The boundary between event-sourced columns (documents.tumbler/title/etc) and hook-derived columns (documents.chunk_count) means equality-check assumptions don't hold for chunk_count.

Fix options:
1. Exclude chunk_count from the replay-equality column comparison (simplest; documents the boundary).
2. Have the projector replay also apply document_chunks events from a separate manifest_events.jsonl (event-source the manifest writes — large refactor).
3. Re-derive chunk_count on the in-memory replay side too, but require the doctor to load document_chunks from disk into the in-memory cat first (cross-store coupling).

Option 1 is the cheap and correct fix: the column is intentionally non-event-sourced. Add an excluded_columns set to the comparison in nexus.catalog.doctor's replay-equality check.

Related: nexus-lf8f (post-replay chunk_count re-derive added in projector — only handles docs that DO have manifest rows; the false-positive is for docs that DON'T).
notes:
2026-05-12 follow-up: a second false-positive class observed in production. SQL DELETE on the collections projection (e.g. to clean stale projection rows that have no supersede target — model/owner is gone, can't point to anything) leaves the live SQLite count below the event-log replay count. The replay can't reconstruct the deletion because the catalog has no CollectionDeleted event type — only CollectionSuperseded(target).

Fix should generalize to cover both classes: documents.chunk_count and collections projection-only deletes. Options:
- Exclude both from replay-equality comparison with a documented rationale.
- Introduce a CollectionDeleted event so SQL deletes can round-trip through the event log.
- Provide an admin verb 'nx catalog drop-stale-projection' that emits a synthetic supersede-to-tombstone event.
close_reason: Shipped in v4.32.11 (PR #722 merged + tag pushed 2026-05-12). Sandbox shakeout (fresh + index ext-apps + delete-collection cycle) now passes all 6 doctor checks at every stage.

title: P2: retry backoff has no jitter — thundering-herd risk under sustained rate-limit
description: Tier-6. retry.py:130-145, 212-228 use pure doubling backoff (2s,4s,8s cap 30s; 1s,2s,4s cap 10s). Multiple concurrent indexing workers retrying after a rate-limit produce synchronized retries against Voyage AI / ChromaDB Cloud, amplifying the rate-limit. Fix: delay *= (1 + random.random() * 0.2) before each sleep.
acceptance_criteria: Both time.sleep() calls in retry.py use a jittered value (delay * factor); factor contains a random component; tests remain deterministic via monkeypatching
notes:
## Enrichment (2026-05-12)

### Fix
src/nexus/retry.py:144 and :227 — add ±20% jitter to the sleep value before each time.sleep(delay):

    sleep_for = delay * (1 + random.random() * 0.2)
    time.sleep(sleep_for)

Do NOT mutate the doubling schedule — only randomize the actual sleep value. Keep delay itself deterministic so the cap math is unchanged. Log the jittered value (not base delay) in the warn line.

### Affected wrappers
- _chroma_with_retry (lines 119-145): delay starts 2.0s, cap 30s
- _voyage_with_retry (lines 197-228): delay starts 1.0s, cap 10s

Both see concurrent indexing pool callers; both target rate-limited remote services.

### Test determinism
Monkeypatch random.random → 0 (or seed random) in retry tests to keep assertions stable. Per project policy: deterministic seeded randomness.

title: P2: fire_post_document_hooks fragile TypeError back-compat (apply batch chain pattern)
description: Tier-2 design finding. mcp_infra.py:1017-1023 uses try/except TypeError retry pattern; batch chain already moved to inspect.signature at registration (mcp_infra.py:482-507). ## Enrichment (2026-05-12)

### Problem
`fire_post_document_hooks` (src/nexus/mcp_infra.py:989-1023) uses a fragile try/except TypeError to fall back to the legacy 3-arg signature when a registered hook doesn't accept the `doc_id` keyword. Any unrelated `TypeError` raised inside the hook body (e.g., `int(None)`, bad string formatting) is caught by the outer `except TypeError`, silently retried with the legacy signature — masking real bugs and corrupting hook semantics.

- In `register_post_document_hook`, inspect the callable's signature once: classify as doc_id-capable when `"doc_id" in params` OR a `VAR_KEYWORD` (`**kwargs`) is present.
- In `fire_post_document_hooks`, branch on `id(hook) in _post_document_hooks_with_doc_id` — no try/except TypeError back-compat retry.
- Let the outer `except Exception` handle real hook failures faithfully.

### Key files
- src/nexus/mcp_infra.py lines 476-520 (batch-chain registration reference), 989-1023 (fragile retry to fix)
- tests/test_post_document_hooks.py (new contract tests)

2. Register a `**kwargs` hook — verify it receives `doc_id` kwarg.
3. Register a hook that declares `doc_id` — verify passthrough.

title: MinerU config drift: _restart_mineru_server writes ephemeral port to persistent config
description:
## Problem

``pdf_extractor._restart_mineru_server`` calls ``_find_free_port()`` to pick a port, spawns ``mineru-api`` on it, then writes the port to ``~/.config/nexus/config.yml`` via ``set_config_value``. The server is **ephemeral** (lives only as long as the spawning shell / process tree), but the config write is **persistent**.

Failure sequence:

1. Day 1: MinerU server crashes mid-PDF run.
2. ``_restart_mineru_server`` fires, picks port (say 49353), spawns ``mineru-api --port 49353``, writes ``mineru_server_url: http://127.0.0.1:49353`` to config.yml. Run completes.
3. Day 2 (after reboot or process tree cleanup): server is dead. Config still says 49353.
4. Next ``nx index pdf`` on a math-heavy paper: probes 49353, gets ConnectError, falls through to in-process subprocess, OOM-kills on page 23+.

Caught during 4.32.1 shakeout — Hal's config had ``mineru_server_url: http://127.0.0.1:49353`` from a long-dead restart cycle. The doctor + warn-on-fallback fixes (nexus-h1jk, PR #693) make this visible but don't prevent it.

## Fix candidates

A. **Stop writing to persistent config.** Use the PID file at ``~/.config/nexus/mineru.pid`` as the source of truth for the live port; pdf_extractor reads it at startup. Config holds a DEFAULT (e.g. ``8010``) that pdf_extractor falls back to when no PID file is present. Restart updates PID file only.

B. **Validate config on startup.** ``get_mineru_server_url`` cross-checks the configured URL against the PID file's ``port``; on mismatch (or stale PID), revert to default before returning. Operator never sees a stale URL.

C. **MCP supervisor.** Long-lived nexus MCP owns the MinerU server lifecycle. Spawns on startup, restarts on crash, tears down on MCP shutdown. Doesn't write to config — uses MCP-process-scoped state.

D. **launchctl user service.** OS-level daemon. Most robust; needs platform-specific work (macOS launchctl, Linux systemd). Out of scope for a single bug fix.

## Recommended path

A + B together: stop writing config, treat PID file as source of truth, fall back to default port when no live process. Minimal blast radius; preserves the existing ``nx mineru start/stop`` UX. Hold C/D for a later RDR if the substrate needs it.

## Out of scope (for this bead)

- MinerU OOM under formula extraction itself (separate issue — server mode mitigates it but doesn't fix the underlying memory accumulation in MinerU's pipeline).
- Auto-spawn-on-cache-miss from pdf_extractor (UX decision: warm-up takes 10-30s).

## Refs

- nexus-h1jk (the visibility fix, PR #693).
- src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py:_restart_mineru_server (the offending config write).
- src/nexus/commands/mineru.py:_pid_file_path (the existing PID file infrastructure).
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-109 Phase 2 fallout: test_indexer_e2e cloud-cred mock pattern incompatible with local-T3
description:
Two integration tests in tests/test_indexer_e2e.py fail after RDR-109 Phase 2 (#682):

- test_smart_index_staleness_check: re-index added 1 chunk (6 -> 7).
- test_migration_moves_prose_from_code_to_docs: seeded misclassified chunk not pruned.

Root cause: the shared ``_index`` helper at tests/test_indexer_e2e.py:153 patches ``nexus.config.get_credential`` to return "test-key" for ALL keys. That forces ``is_local_mode()`` to return False because both ``chroma_api_key`` and ``voyage_api_key`` resolve truthy. The indexer then writes voyage-named collections (e.g. ``docs__nexus-rich0-...__voyage-context-3__v1``).

But these tests pass the ``local_t3`` fixture (``T3Database(local_mode=True)``). So writes go through ``T3Database._build_embedding_fn`` with ``local_mode=True`` against a voyage-named collection — which is the exact case Phase 2 closes by raising ``IncompatibleCollectionError`` (inverse-RDR-059 hazard).

The 84/86 other integration tests in this file pass because they either:
- Don't re-index (so the staleness/prune paths aren't exercised);
- Or assert collection-shape / fixture seeding that doesn't trip the dispatch boundary.

## Fix options

A. Remove the cloud-cred mock from ``_index`` and let local_t3 fixtures be genuinely local-mode (collection names use the local token). Will rename many tests' expected collection names.

B. Replace ``local_t3`` with ``cloud_mode`` + a cloud-shaped T3 fixture for tests using the mock pattern. Preserves voyage naming.

C. Per-test override: in the 2 failing tests, manually monkeypatch ``nexus.config.is_local_mode`` so the indexer uses local naming consistently with the local_t3 backend.

Option C is the smallest diff; A is the cleanest long-term fix.

## Caveat

Tests fail on develop tip after 4.32.0 release prep (commit 31e9aa36). Unit suite is fully green. Sandbox smoke passes. Production behavior is correct; this is test-mock pattern drift.

## Refs

- PR #682 (Phase 2): introduced IncompatibleCollectionError + bidirectional EF dispatch.
- tests/test_indexer_e2e.py: ``_index`` helper at line 153.
- Failing tests: ``test_smart_index_staleness_check`` (line 476), ``test_migration_moves_prose_from_code_to_docs`` (line 500).
notes:
2026-05-11 post-4.32.1 investigation:

Attempted fix C (patch is_local_mode in _index) didn't help — the test_indexer_e2e local_t3 fixture is defined locally (line 85, NOT the conftest version) as ``T3Database(_client=..., _ef_override=...)`` without ``local_mode=True``. So _local_mode is False; aligning is_local_mode to that doesn't change which branch fires.

The EF override sidesteps _build_embedding_fn entirely, so RDR-109 Phase 2's bidirectional dispatch CAN'T be the proximate cause. Something else broke between 4.31.x and 4.32.0 for the re-index staleness paths.

Standalone reproduction of `_index` -> auth error — the test relies on the autouse mock_voyage_client (test file lines 99-119) to fake Voyage embed responses. The reproduction surface is fragile; needs a focused debug session against the mock plumbing.

Recommendation: pick this up under /nx:debug with the actual failing test running locally, instrument `check_staleness` and the chunk write paths to identify what's being written on run 1 vs detected on run 2. Not a single-line fix.

Worktree /tmp/nexus-7kf7 left clean (reverted patch).

Two indexer bugs from RDR-108 Phase 3 fallout: _index_pdf_file did not thread staleness_cache (Bug 1); _prune_misclassified_in_collection catalog-present branch dropped the doc_id-keyed where filter (Bug 2). Both fixes verified; nexus-f3tyz filed for the macOS symlink follow-on.

title: RDR-109 Phase 4: Calibration — seed queries + held-out QA + boost-weight sweep [0.0..0.15]
description:
RDR-109 Phase 4 — measurement work for nexus-2wc1. RDR file: /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus/docs/rdr/rdr-109-honest-naming-and-cross-encoder-salience.md (lines 242-251).

## Depends on

- RDR-109 Phase 3 (nexus-n3qu.3) — needs the cross-encoder substrate to score pairs.

## Steps

1. Curate seed-query set per content_type:
   - `papers` (knowledge__rag-papers, knowledge__hybridrag, etc.) — 3-5 generic seed queries about paper salience.
   - `code` (code__*) — 3-5 generic seed queries about API/function salience.
   - `prose` (docs__) — 3-5 generic seed queries about doc concept salience.
   - `rdr` (rdr__) — 3-5 generic seed queries about decision/rationale salience.
   - Document seed queries in `data/calibration/rdr-109/seed_queries_<content_type>.json`.
2. Build held-out QA set: ≥30 questions per content_type with known-good chunks.
   - Hand-curate against existing collections (knowledge__hybridrag, knowledge__rag-papers as seed corpora).
   - Format: `{question, expected_chunk_chash, content_type}` JSONL.
   - Store at `data/calibration/rdr-109/qa_<content_type>.jsonl`.
3. Implement calibration harness:
   - For each content_type: index a copy of the corpus with each candidate boost weight in `[0.0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.075, 0.10, 0.15]`.
   - Run held-out questions through `search_cross_corpus` for each weight.
   - Measure top-5 hit rate (expected_chunk_chash in top-5 results).
4. Pick boost weight that maximizes hit rate WITHOUT regressing any baseline-passing query (no Pareto regression).
5. Document chosen weight + per-content-type measurements in:
   - RDR-109 revisions section.
   - `data/calibration/rdr-109/results.md`.
6. Stash calibration artefacts (seed queries, QA set, results) in nx T2 memory under project nexus, title `rdr-109-calibration-results.md`.

## Files

- `data/calibration/rdr-109/seed_queries_*.json` (new).
- `data/calibration/rdr-109/qa_*.jsonl` (new).
- `data/calibration/rdr-109/results.md` (new).
- `scripts/rdr-109-calibrate.py` (new harness).
- Tests: deterministic regression test that re-runs a small QA subset against the chosen weight.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Seed-query sets curated for all 4 content_types (papers/code/prose/rdr).
- [ ] Held-out QA set has ≥30 questions per content_type with verified expected chashes.
- [ ] Boost-weight sweep results table published; chosen weight justified by hit-rate + Pareto non-regression.
- [ ] Calibration artefacts stashed in nx T2 memory (project=nexus, title=rdr-109-calibration-results.md).
- [ ] Reproducible: `python scripts/rdr-109-calibrate.py` re-derives the chosen weight from data/calibration/.
- [ ] If NO weight passes Pareto non-regression: surface to user (RDR-109 revisions) + propose Phase 5 deferral or RDR-109 split per RDR coupling note (lines 290-293).

## Execution

- Use sequential-thinking MCP for QA set design (representativeness + held-out discipline).
- Use nx_answer for prior calibration approaches in RAG / IR literature (knowledge__rag-papers + knowledge__hybridrag).
- Calibration is potentially 2-3 days of experiment time (per critic finding #5 in T1 scratch 285160f5) — Phase 2's close gate intentionally does NOT depend on this.

## Context pointers

title: AST chunker produces mid-identifier fragments in large code files (split through identifiers)
description:
## Source

Split out from nexus-fh3j after a 2026-05-10 empirical reclassification of micro-chunks.

## Symptom

The AST chunker (``code_indexer`` / tree-sitter path) produces chunks that START mid-identifier in some code collections. Sample fragments observed in ``code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1`` (the ART Java repo):

- ``tected CanonicalLaminarCircuitGPU(CanonicalParameters params, OrientingAdapter o`` -- ``protected`` split
- ``ivate void initializeMetalKernels() throws Exception {`` -- ``private`` split
- ``e float executeIterationBatched(int dimension, int groupingDim) throws Exception`` -- some prefix split
- ``ngResult processGPUIterationLoop(float[] input) throws Exception {`` -- some prefix split
- ``ount >= minStableIterations) {\n // Re`` -- ``count`` split
- ``xL6 >= minL6Threshold) {\n /`` -- ``maxL6`` (or similar) split
- ``f (iter % 10 =`` -- ``if`` split

All fragments end mid-token too. They look like the chunker fell through to a character-offset boundary that doesn't align with identifier boundaries.

## Scope

The fh3j re-audit (1,228 micro-chunks across all prod collections) found 23.9% of micro-chunks are this broken-split class. ALL of them came from ONE collection: ``code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1``. Other code collections (``code__1-2188``, ``code__1-7``, ``code__Delos-*``, ``code__Kramer-*``) had ZERO broken-split samples in the audit.

This is a code-path-specific bug, not a general chunker regression.

## Hypotheses (to verify in the fix)

1. **Large-source-file fall-through**: the AST chunker has a per-file size limit; files past N bytes fall through to character-offset chunking. Java codebases like ART tend to have very large class files (the ART CanonicalLaminarCircuitGPU.java sample is 100k+ lines).

2. **Tree-sitter Java grammar quirk**: a particular AST node shape in the Java grammar yields a chunk-boundary inside an identifier. Less likely; tree-sitter respects token boundaries by construction.

3. **Streaming-pipeline edge case**: the streaming chunker's batch boundary aligns to a fixed byte offset that doesn't respect identifier boundaries. Most likely if the chunker is processing in fixed-size windows.

## Acceptance

- Identify the code path producing mid-identifier splits in ``code__1-2153``.
- Fix the chunker to respect identifier boundaries (either align splits to AST node boundaries or, for the fallback path, skip ahead to the next whitespace).
- Add a regression test that asserts: for a synthetic large Java file, no chunk starts or ends with a partial-identifier signature (lowercase letter at the chunk boundary that could be the middle of a word).
- Re-run the fh3j audit pattern on prod after the fix; expect the broken-split count to drop to zero.

## Refs

- Parent: nexus-fh3j (closed 2026-05-10 after empirical reclassification).
- Audit script: see fh3j notes for the inline Python that classified 1,228 micro-chunks into 76% valid (headers, declarations, sentences) vs 24% broken (mid-identifier fragments).
- Affected source: ``src/nexus/index/ast_chunker.py`` (or wherever the Java AST chunker lives) + the streaming-pipeline batch boundary logic.
- Affected collection: ``code__1-2153__voyage-code-3__v1``.

## Priority rationale

P2: the broken chunks ARE wasted Voyage budget (~24% of micro-chunks, concentrated in one repo) but they don't actively break correctness. Search results pollute slightly with fragment hits; ranking de-prioritizes them naturally. Worth fixing before re-indexing the affected repo or onboarding similar large-Java codebases.
close_reason: Closed

title: P2: synthesizer.py:682 legacy_chunk_index fallback returns 0 → undefined ordering (RDR-108 Phase 4 review S4)
description:
## Source

src/nexus/catalog/synthesizer.py:682:
\`legacy_chunk_index = int(meta.get(\"chunk_index\", 0) or 0)\`

- Test: synthesize a multi-chunk doc post-Phase-3, verify chunks are in original order.

title: P2: collection_gc_cmd raw traceback on SQLite errors (RDR-108 Phase 4 review CR-M2)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay code-review-expert agent a84fe98ab87acc2b2.

## Problem
src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:5471 collection_gc_cmd queries cat._db.execute(...) without try/except. Any SQLite error (locked DB, schema mismatch, FS issue) surfaces as a raw traceback to the operator. The T3 path in the same function has proper error handling; the cat path doesn't.

## Fix
Wrap in try/except matching the T3 pattern:
\`\`\`python
try:
    doc_collection_rows = cat._db.execute(...).fetchall()
except sqlite3.Error as exc:
    click.echo(f\"Failed to query catalog: {exc}\", err=True)
    raise SystemExit(1)
\`\`\`

## Acceptance
- Error path mirrors the T3 path.
- Regression test: with a corrupted catalog DB, the verb exits with a clean message, not a traceback.
close_reason: Closed

title: P2: ThreadPoolExecutor thread leak in t3.py list_collections (RDR-108 Phase 4 review CR-M1)
description:
## Source

## Problem
src/nexus/db/t3.py:930-938 list_collections uses \`executor.shutdown(wait=False)\` before the result generator is consumed. If the for-loop exits early (exception, break), worker threads leak.

## Fix
Use \`with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=...) as executor:\` so __exit__ runs shutdown(wait=True). Move the result accumulation inside the with-block.

## Acceptance
- ThreadPoolExecutor wrapped in \`with\`.
- No regression in list_collections behavior.

ks40 fixed three indexer paths (_prune_deleted_files, _prune_misclassified, _run_index_frecency_only) to use get_collection (not get_or_create_collection) so they don't speculatively create empty zombie T3 collections. But src/nexus/collection_audit.py:394 (compute_chash_coverage missing-sample probe) still calls get_or_create_collection. Same leak pattern, different code path. The ks40 prevention is incomplete here.

## Fix
Apply the same get_collection + try/except _ChromaNotFoundError pattern. If the collection doesn't exist, the audit can't read from it; return ChashCoverage(total_chunks=None, ...) or skip.

## Acceptance
- collection_audit.py uses get_collection.
- Regression test: compute_chash_coverage on a non-existent collection does NOT create it.

title: P2: docs_for_chashes vs chashes_for_collection normalization contract divergence (RDR-108 Phase 4 review S2)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay substantive-critic agent a55f4d22df1ba44b9.

## Problem
src/nexus/catalog/catalog_writes.py:
- chashes_for_collection (line 886) normalizes to 32-char via \`substr(chash,1,32)\` and returns chash[:32].
- docs_for_chashes (line 920) does literal \`WHERE chash IN (?)\` and returns full chash keys.

The manifest write hook stores full 64-char chunk_text_hash. Current callers (mcp/core.py:862) pass 64-char and round-trip works. But D1 says natural ID is chash[:32]; any future caller following D1 conventions will silently get empty results.

## Fix
Normalize docs_for_chashes the same way chashes_for_collection does:
\`\`\`python
WHERE substr(chash,1,32) IN (...)
\`\`\`
Return keys as chash[:32]. Update mcp/core.py and any other caller to look up via chash[:32].

## Refs
- nexus-rehf (D-H1+H2 fix) depends on this — the shared _attach_doc_ids_from_catalog helper uses docs_for_chashes with chash[:32] keys.
close_reason: Closed

title: P2: chash_reconcile_cmd missing isinstance(c, str) guard (RDR-108 Phase 4 review CR-H1)
description:
## Source
nexus-izay code-review-expert agent a84fe98ab87acc2b2.

## Problem
src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:5336 (chash_reconcile_cmd):
\`live_collections = {c.name for c in t3._client.list_collections()}\`

Every other call site in the codebase guards: \`name = c if isinstance(c, str) else c.name\`. ChromaDB versions vary on whether list_collections returns Collection objects or strings; without the guard this raises AttributeError on string-returning versions.

## Fix
\`\`\`python
live_collections = {
    (c if isinstance(c, str) else c.name)
    for c in t3._client.list_collections()
}
\`\`\`

Plus a regression test that mocks list_collections to return strings and verifies chash-reconcile completes.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit: every T3 write call site must traverse all normalization layers (collection name + embedding model + catalog projection)
description:
## Problem class

Multiple T3-related decisions are made by independent layers:

1. **Collection name canonicalization** — \`corpus.t3_collection_name()\`
   takes a user-facing arg (\`knowledge\` or \`knowledge__art\`) and
   returns the on-disk collection name. Bare names get the prefix
   added; double-underscore names pass through.

2. **Catalog-aware vs legacy resolution** — \`indexer._repo_collection_or_legacy()\`
   queries the catalog for a conformant 4-segment name when the
   catalog is initialized; falls back to legacy
   \`<basename>-<hash8>\` shape otherwise.

3. **Embedding model selection** — \`corpus.index_model_for_collection()\`
   dispatches the model (\`voyage-code-3\`, \`voyage-context-3\`,
   etc.) by inspecting the collection-name prefix. A name that
   doesn't match any expected prefix may silently fall back to a
   default model OR to a non-CCE pipeline, depending on caller.

4. **Catalog projection registration** — \`Catalog.register_collection()\`
   inserts a row into the \`collections\` projection table so the
   doctor's \`--collections-drift\` check can verify T3 -> catalog
   coverage. Missing this step at write time creates the
   \"unregistered T3 collection\" pattern flagged by ks40.

Each layer is independently correct. The bug class is **callers
that skip one layer**:

- **2026-03-23 postmortem (c29bd7ff)**: \`nx index pdf --collection\`
  skipped \`t3_collection_name()\` -> bare \`knowledge\` collection
  created -> bare prefix didn't match the CCE branch in
  \`index_model_for_collection\` -> 10,036 chunks embedded with the
  wrong model into an unsearchable name. Fixed at the single call
  site (e54bdc87).

- **nexus-ks40 (today)**: three \`indexer.py\` paths called
  \`db.get_or_create_collection\` for read purposes -> empty zombie
  T3 collections under a name the catalog never registered ->
  doctor flagged \"T3 collections without projection rows\" forever.
  Fixed at the call sites by switching to \`get_collection\`.

Both are pattern-instance fixes. Neither is structural prevention.

## Why this matters

The next bug of this class is one new write-path call site away.
\`grep -rn \"get_or_create_collection\\|get_collection\\|create_collection\"
src/nexus/\` returns 30+ sites. Each is an opportunity to skip a
normalization layer; CI does not catch the skip.

## Proposed scope

A. **Inventory.** Walk every T3 write call site:
   - \`get_or_create_collection\`
   - \`create_collection\`
   - \`upsert_chunks\` / \`upsert_chunks_with_embeddings\`
   - \`put\`
   - \`update_chunks\`
   For each, document which normalization layers it depends on
   (name canonicalization, embedding model match, catalog
   projection write).

B. **Per-site audit.** For each site, verify:
   - Collection name passes through \`t3_collection_name()\` OR is
     known-conformant (e.g., the indexer's catalog-aware resolver).
   - Embedding model used matches what \`index_model_for_collection()\`
     would return for the chosen name (no silent fallback).
   - Catalog projection registration happens at or before first
     write (so the doctor can find the row).

C. **Structural test.** Add a test that fails when a new T3 write
   call site is added without the funnel. Options:
   - AST scan of \`src/nexus/\` for \`*.upsert(\` /
     \`get_or_create_collection(\` and require each match to be in
     a known allow-list OR carry a comment marker (\`# normalized:
     <layer>\`).
   - Or: a contract-style test that imports the indexer / put /
     other write entry points and asserts they call
     \`t3_collection_name\` (or equivalent) before the T3 call.

D. **Doctor coverage.** Extend \`nx catalog doctor\` with a check
   that surfaces \"T3 collections whose name doesn't match any
   embedding-model-prefix rule\" as a separate failure mode (today
   they'd just look like \"unregistered T3 collections\").

## Acceptance

- A documented inventory of all T3 write call sites and the
  normalization layers each one traverses.
- At least one structural test that would have caught both
  c29bd7ff (bare-name -> wrong embed) AND ks40 (read-path
  speculative create).
- Doctor surfaces wrong-prefix collections distinctly from
  unregistered-but-conformant ones.

## Refs

- 2026-03-23 postmortem: \`docs/postmortem/2026-03-23-pdf-index-collection-mismatch.md\`
  (commit c29bd7ff). 10,036 chunks under wrong embedding model.
- nexus-ks40 (this session): zombie 0-chunk collections from
  read-path speculative creation. 13 swept in prod.
- Adjacent fixed-ish issues: GH #535 / #545 / #563 (bare-prefix
  resolver follow-ups), GH #551 (slug derivation conformant suffix
  budget), GH #336 (silent 0 chunks when api_key unset).
- Affected modules: \`src/nexus/corpus.py\`, \`src/nexus/indexer.py\`,
  \`src/nexus/doc_indexer.py\`, \`src/nexus/code_indexer.py\`,
  \`src/nexus/prose_indexer.py\`, \`src/nexus/db/t3.py\`,
  \`src/nexus/commands/index.py\`, \`src/nexus/commands/store.py\`,
  \`src/nexus/commands/catalog.py\`, \`src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py\`.

## Priority rationale

P2: not a live data-loss bug today (the two known instances are
fixed). But the bug class keeps recurring and the blast radius
when it happens is large (lost chunks, wrong embeddings,
silently-broken search). Structural prevention here is cheaper
than the next postmortem.
notes:
2026-05-10 audit complete. Explore agent walked all 17 confirmed T3 write call sites (excluding read-only and bypass-schema sites). Findings:

| Site | L1 | L2 | L3 | L4 | Gap analysis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pipeline_stages.py:645, 733 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | None (L4 via _catalog_hooks post-store) |
| doc_indexer.py:616, 856, 1154 | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | L2 not needed: name synthesized via canonical_embedding_model is conformant by construction |
| aspect_extractor.py:756 | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | L1+L2 skip, BUT in deprecated code (RDR-096 Phase 5 removal target). Low value to fix now. |
| collection_health.py:152, 286, collection_audit.py:163 | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | Read-only after the post-ks40 get_or_create→get_collection sweeps; remaining writes confirmed test-only |
| indexer.py:2084, 2085, 2347 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | None (L4 via _catalog_hooks) |
| plans/session_cache.py:61 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Hardcoded PLANS_COLLECTION (conformant); L4 N/A for plans tier |
| catalog/catalog_spans.py:411 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Catalog-derived name (already canonical); L4 already done |
| catalog/consolidation.py:55, 67 | ✓ | mixed | ✓ | ✗ | :55 synthetic-conformant, L2 not needed; :67 catalog-derived |
| mcp/core.py:1042 | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | L2 skip: t3_collection_name produces conformant name; L2 catalog-fallback not needed |

CONCLUSION: zero ACTIONABLE gaps in current production write paths. The 4 sites that nominally skip L2 do so because their inputs are synthetic-conformant (don't need catalog fallback for legacy names). The aspect_extractor.py:756 L1+L2 skip is in deprecated code slated for removal in RDR-096 Phase 5. The L4 (catalog projection registration) is correctly done via _catalog_hooks post-store hook system, not at the write call sites directly.

Audit-pattern docs added to bead notes for the 2026-03-23 postmortem class. The single-call-site bug (e54bdc87 / nx index pdf --collection) was an L1 skip; today no L1 skips exist in active code paths.

Closing as "audit complete; no follow-up beads needed". Re-open if a future call-site addition or a refactor introduces a new gap.
close_reason: Closed

title: catalog doctor --collections-drift: zombie 0-chunk projections accumulate from shakedown / worktree runs
description:
## Problem

\`nx catalog doctor --collections-drift\` (the release gate at shakedown step 11/11) fails on develop's HOME catalog with:

\`\`\`
Projection rows whose T3 collection is gone and not superseded (1):
  rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1
Remediate: register a target collection and supersede manually:
  python -c \"from nexus.catalog.catalog import Catalog; ...\"
\`\`\`

Inspecting T3 directly: \`rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1\` exists in T3 with **0 chunks**. The doctor's \"T3 collection is gone\" check apparently treats 0-chunk collections as gone (or the live-collection probe excludes empty ones). Either way the gate trips.

Plus the doctor lists 7+ \"T3 collections not registered in catalog\":
- \`rdr__1-3__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`rdr__agent-a67910286cac6d33c-292af502__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`rdr__agent-aa30ae10a97c4fe8b-19de5153__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`rdr__agent-ae11e6fda7c3c970d-dc46e126__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`rdr__nexus-rich0-1bfccdf0__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`rdr__nexus-rich0-e5337bfd__voyage-context-3__v1\` (0 chunks)
- \`docs__shakedown_4_16_1\`
- \`docs__stale\`

These are zombie collections accumulated from:
- Past shakedown runs (rdr__1-1, rdr__1-3 — owner-numbered names from the test repo's catalog registration).
- Past worktree runs (rdr__agent-* names — auto-derived from worktree-agent-<hash> branches that have since been deleted; see prior local cleanup).
- Pre-RDR-103 dev runs (rdr__nexus-rich0-* — legacy basename-hash naming).

Same drift class also affects prod for \`docs__art-architecture\` (pre-existing).

## Why this matters

The collections-drift gate is a release blocker (\`exit 1\`). Until cleaned, the release-sandbox shakedown can never reach 11/11 PASS, which means we can't tag a release without manually overriding or remediating per the doctor's instructions.

## Not a regression

The drift state predates this session's merges (#624 + #506 + #630 + #635 + #636). The Phase 4+5 bundle exercised the full indexer pipeline (steps 1-10 of the shakedown all PASS), proving no functional regression. The drift is accumulated state hygiene that the bundle's new gates surface, not corrupt.

## Investigation hints

Two distinct bugs to consider:

1. **0-chunk collection misclassified as \"gone\"**: when \`nx index rdr\` registers the conformant rdr__1-1 in catalog but \`batch_index_markdowns\` doesn't actually write any chunks (e.g. all .md files were skipped via staleness, OR the collection got created earlier as part of catalog naming registration before any indexing happened), T3 ends up with an empty collection and the catalog has a row. The doctor probably checks \`col.count() > 0\` instead of \`col exists\` — should distinguish \"empty collection\" from \"absent collection\" before flagging drift.

2. **Catalog-T3 naming asymmetry leaks**: \`_repo_collection_or_legacy()\` falls back to legacy \`<basename>-<hash8>\` naming when the catalog isn't yet initialized, and to conformant \`1-N\` naming after the catalog assigns owner numbers. If \`nx index repo\` runs both code paths in different states (or if the catalog's owner number assignment slips between calls), T3 ends up with collections under one name and the catalog projection under another. The pile of zombie rdr__nexus-rich0-* + rdr__agent-* + rdr__1-3 is the historical ledger of these slips.

## Acceptance

- \`nx catalog doctor --collections-drift\` exits 0 on a clean local HOME after running the shakedown end-to-end.
- Either:
  (a) The doctor's check distinguishes \"empty\" from \"absent\" so empty rdr__ collections from a no-op index aren't flagged.
  (b) Or the indexer never registers a catalog projection for an empty collection (fold register-collection into the actual write path instead of pre-registering at name-resolution time).
  (c) Or a sweep verb is added (\`nx catalog gc --empty-projections\` or similar) so operators can clean zombie state in one command.

## Refs

- Surfaced by: \`./tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh shakedown\` step 11/11 (2026-05-10).
- Same drift class in prod (\`docs__art-architecture\`).
- Adjacent code: \`src/nexus/indexer.py:_discover_and_index_rdrs\`, \`src/nexus/indexer.py:_repo_collection_or_legacy\`, \`src/nexus/catalog/synthesizer.py\`, the \`nx catalog doctor --collections-drift\` implementation in \`src/nexus/commands/catalog.py\`.
close_reason: Closed

title: indexer test fixtures: add realistic-duplicate chunk content cases (boilerplate, license headers)
description:
## Problem

The original nexus-kmb6 test suite (indexer write-path retargeting to content-derived IDs) used distinct chunk content per test fixture. The within-batch duplicate-content scenario (real-world: boilerplate copyright headers across files, license blurbs in each file, stock paragraphs) was never exercised. Result: nexus-1ljk (DuplicateIDError) shipped to prod and surfaced when the operator re-indexed a real repo.

## Fix

Add fixtures with intentionally-identical chunk content across multiple files:
- Two .py files in the same code__ collection that share an identical block of N consecutive lines (chunked the same way).
- Two .md files in the same docs__ collection sharing an identical paragraph.
- A PDF with two pages whose chunked text happens to overlap.

Run the full indexer pipeline + assert no crash and the right collapse semantic.

## Test gap acknowledgement

The Phase 4 review surfaced this gap retroactively. The pattern is broadly applicable: any time a code path assumes value uniqueness, the test fixtures should EXPLICITLY exercise the duplicate case rather than incidentally avoid it.

## Refs
- nexus-1ljk: the bug this would have caught
- nexus-2exh review caveat (test fixture realism gap)
notes: Tests added in tests/test_indexer_duplicate_content.py: 4 scenarios covering cross-file (2 .py duplicates; 2 .md sharing a paragraph) and within-batch (1 .md repeated paragraph; PDF with chunker stub yielding duplicates). Within-batch tests verified to fail when nexus-1ljk dedup is reverted.
close_reason: Closed

title: nx catalog chash-reconcile: bulk-sweep stale chash_index rows pointing at deleted T3 collections
description:
## Symptom

RDR-108 Phase 5 verification probe (2026-05-10) found:

\`\`\`
chash_index distinct: 1824
T3 collection count:  153
In chash_index but NOT in T3 (ghosts): 1682
In T3 but NOT in chash_index:          11
\`\`\`

Sample ghost rows point at collections like \`code__catalog-e2e0-*\`
(test fixture leakage), \`code__1-1__voyage-code-3__v1\` (legacy
RDR-101 test names), and other collections that have since been
deleted from T3.

\`Catalog.resolve_chash\` self-heals on access (drops the stale row
when it tries to look up a chash and the collection is missing in
T3), but that's a per-access correction, not a sweep.

## Background

This was the original symptom that motivated bead \`nexus-mmf5\` in
the 2026-05-08 prod shakeout. \`nexus-mmf5\` was later repurposed
(2026-05-09) to drop the \`chunk_chroma_id\` column entirely — a
structural fix downstream of RDR-108 D1. The drift cleanup verb was
explicitly deferred as out-of-scope.

This bead picks up the deferred work.

## Fix

Add two CLI verbs:

1. \`nx catalog chash-audit\` — read-only report. Lists chash_index
   rows whose \`physical_collection\` is not in
   \`client.list_collections()\`. Counts ghost rows per
   collection-name pattern (e.g. test-fixture prefixes vs legacy
   conformant names).

2. \`nx catalog chash-reconcile [--dry-run] [--apply]\` — bulk
   delete the stale rows. Either \`--dry-run\` (report only) or
   \`--apply\` (actually delete). Prefer batch DELETE
   (\`DELETE FROM chash_index WHERE physical_collection = ?\`)
   per ghost-collection so the existing
   \`idx_chash_index_collection\` index drives the operation.

## Out of scope

Reverse direction: 11 T3 collections that lack chash_index rows.
Filed separately if needed; these are likely test/local-mode
collections rather than missing-coverage in chash_index. Spot
check during chash-audit.

## Affected files

- \`src/nexus/commands/catalog.py\` — new \`chash-audit\` and
  \`chash-reconcile\` subcommands.
- New: \`tests/test_chash_reconcile.py\`.

## Refs

- nexus-mmf5 original bead description (drift symptom + reconcile
  sketch); the column-drop work shipped, the reconcile work was
  deferred to here.
- 2026-05-10 Phase 5 verification probe (T2 memory: rdr-108-phase5-verification-probes).

title: RDR-108 Phase 5 follow-up: parallel-across-collections in nx t3 reidentify
description:
## Problem

The migration verb at \`src/nexus/commands/t3.py:gc_cmd:reidentify_cmd\`
processes collections serially. For 150 collections * ~1900 round-trips
across all passes at ~200ms ChromaDB Cloud latency, the operator waits
~10-30 min for the dry-run alone before deciding whether to fire
\`--no-dry-run\` (which adds the upsert + delete passes).

Within a collection, batching is already at the quota max (300/op)
and the two-pass design is correctness-preserving (sidesteps offset
instability during in-loop upserts). Cross-collection state is
independent: each collection has its own ID namespace and the
ChashIndex / catalog updates are per-doc-id keyed.

## Fix

Wrap the \`for coll_name in collections_to_process\` loop in
\`concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N)\`. Default
\`max_workers=4\`; expose via \`--max-workers N\` CLI flag.

Aggregation: each thread returns its \`ReidentifyResult\` independently;
main thread aggregates totals + errors after \`as_completed\`.

Output: per-collection lines may interleave on stderr; that's
acceptable. Print "[DONE i/N]" rather than "[i/N] processing" so the
order reflects completion order, not start order.

## Affected files
- \`src/nexus/commands/t3.py:reidentify_cmd\` (~759-897)
- \`tests/test_t3_reidentify.py\` (TestReidentifyCLI: add a parallel-execution test)

## Out of scope
- Within-collection pipelining (riskier, modest additional gain).
- Two-pass merge (would require a separate ID-snapshot mechanism).

## Refs
- RDR-108 Phase 5 nexus-b5mh prerequisite (operator runs reidentify
  against prod before zero-stale verification).
close_reason: Closed

title: P2: RDR-108 Phase 1 remediation T-E: defensive coding + operator UX
description:
RDR-108 Phase 1 multi-lens review surfaced defensive-coding gaps and operator-UX rough edges.

## Findings to address

K10 (code-quality S-1): bare except in manifest_backfill.py:161
- Intent is "T3 collection not found" but bare except swallows quota errors, transient network errors, auth failures
- Other nexus T3 callers use `except _ChromaNotFoundError` (chromadb.errors)
- Fix: `except _ChromaNotFoundError:` specifically, let other exceptions propagate

S-2 (code-quality): BackfillResult.docs_skipped_no_t3 declared but never incremented
- manifest_backfill.py:67 — field exists for distinguishing "T3 collection missing" from "doc has zero chunks"
- Currently both produce identical behavior (docs_processed += 1, empty manifest written)
- Fix: increment docs_skipped_no_t3 when col is None; surface in CLI output

OBS-2 (migration): no user-facing "migrating database..." UX
- T2Database.__init__ runs apply_pending silently
- First post-upgrade `nx <anything>` taking 3s looks like a hang
- Fix: emit click.echo or stderr warning at migration start with "Migrating <table> ..." progress

SIG-6 (migration): nx t3 backfill-manifest has no progress / no resumability / no Ctrl-C safety
- 290k chunks at 300/page = ~967 GETs taking 100-300s
- No output during run; Ctrl-C mid-flight leaves partial state
- Fix: add progress reporting (chunks_processed / total estimate, periodic stderr); --resume flag; signal handler for SIGINT to flush in-flight transaction cleanly
