title: P2: heuristic auto-linker over-emits — top RDRs have 562-660 inbound 'implements-heuristic' edges
description:
## Symptom

Catalog link graph (`memory.db.links` mirrored to `~/.config/nexus/catalog/.catalog.db.links`) has 23,582 edges. The `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500` cap (`src/nexus/catalog/catalog_links.py:62`) fires correctly during BFS traversal, but the underlying density skew suggests heuristic auto-linkers are over-emitting low-precision edges.

## Probe evidence (2026-05-08)

Edge composition by link_type:
- `implements-heuristic`: 15,490 (66%, source: `index_hook`)
- `implements`: 6,557 (28%, source: `filepath_extractor`)
- `cites`: 1,411 (6%, source: `art-corpus-cite-scan` / `bib_enricher`)
- `relates`, `contains`, `supersedes`, `describes`: 124 (0.5%, hand-curated)

Top-10 in-degree (cap-triggering tumblers — at depth 1 BFS, just inbound neighbors exceed 500):
- 1.1.653 / 1.1.668: rdr-063-t2-domain-split.md → **660 in** (each)
- 1.13.2 / 1.13.3: Portal Routing / Subdomain Lifecycle → 659 in (each)
- 1.17.24: AST Chunk Line Range Bug → 562 in
- 1.17.18 / 1.17.22: Knowledge Base Retrieval Quality → 461 in (each)
- 1.11.52 / 1.11.72: Items-in-Positions / Grossberg-Language → 460 in (each)

Top-4 out-degree (all RDRs that auto-link to many code chunks):
- 1.17.14 (T1 Scratch RDR-010): 133 out
- 1.17.21 (ChromaDB Cloud Quota RDR-005): 127 out
- 1.17.28 (ChromaDB Transient HTTP Retry RDR-019): 127 out
- 1.17.63 (T1 Scratch Inter-Agent Context RDR-041): 126 out

Out-degree histogram:
- 1: 352 tumblers
- 2-5: 1,572 tumblers
- 6-10: 272 tumblers
- 11-50: 630 tumblers
- 51-100: 1 tumbler
- 101-500: 4 tumblers
- 500+: 0 tumblers

## Diagnosis

The cap (500) is a reasonable design value for interactive graph traversal — a node with >500 first-degree neighbors isn't visually useful. The cap is firing **correctly**, not too low.

The actual issue is upstream: `index_hook` emits an `implements-heuristic` edge whenever a code chunk's auto-extracted symbols match an RDR's terminology heuristic. For high-traffic RDRs about generic infrastructure (rdr-063 t2-domain-split, AST chunking, code search recall, T1 scratch), this matches HUNDREDS of code chunks, most of which only weakly relate.

Result:
- BFS from a high-traffic RDR caps out instantly at 500 nodes
- Most of those 500 are noise (chunks that mention "scratch" or "T1" generically)
- The ~6% of hand-curated edges (`cites`, `relates`, `contains`) get drowned in the heuristic flood

## Fix options

Three independent levers:

### (a) Filter `implements-heuristic` at retrieval time

Default `Catalog.graph()` and `graph_many()` to `link_types=["cites", "relates", "contains", "supersedes", "describes", "implements"]` — i.e., everything EXCEPT `implements-heuristic`. Add an explicit `include_heuristic=True` flag for callers who want the noise.

Cost: one-line filter at the public API boundary. Doesn't touch existing data.

### (b) Confidence-score the heuristic edges

Add a `confidence: REAL DEFAULT 1.0` column to `links`. `index_hook` writes confidence based on its scoring (e.g., n-gram overlap depth, exact-match ratio). Default-filter retrieval to confidence >= 0.5.

Cost: schema migration + index_hook scorer + retrieval default filter.

### (c) Throttle `index_hook` at write time

Cap each (from_tumbler) at N out-degree per source. If `index_hook` would write the 51st edge from this RDR, drop the lowest-confidence existing edges first or skip the new one.

Cost: per-write logic, but bounds the graph size at ingest.

Recommendation: (a) for immediate relief (no migration), (b) for proper signal/noise separation if the heuristic edges have value, (c) only if (a)+(b) don't suffice.

## Out of scope

- The cap itself (`_MAX_GRAPH_NODES=500`). Don't raise it; the issue is upstream noise.
- Hand-curated edges. Healthy at 6% of total.

## Affected files

- `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_links.py:821-898` (graph) and `:900-...` (graph_many) — add the filter
- Wherever `index_hook` lives (probably `src/nexus/catalog/post_store_hooks.py` or similar) — emission site
- Tests: `tests/test_catalog_links.py` — add coverage for the filter
- Verb: `nx catalog graph` should default to no-heuristic; `--include-heuristic` opt-in.

## Refs

- 2026-05-08 prod-shakeout graph_node_limit probe (this bead)
- `_MAX_GRAPH_NODES`/`_MAX_GRAPH_DEPTH`: `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_links.py:61-62`
- Emit site: `src/nexus/catalog/catalog_links.py:856-859` ("graph_node_limit" warning)

title: P2: 125 document_aspects rows committed with NULL or zero confidence (16.6%)
description:
## Symptom

Of 753 RDR-089 aspect extractions in `memory.db.document_aspects`:

- **53 rows have `confidence IS NULL`**
- **72 rows have `confidence = 0`**

Total: 125 (16.6%) low-quality extractions persisted to the table.

A NULL or zero confidence is a signal the extractor failed, was uncertain, or returned a degraded result. The current code path commits these rows anyway, which means downstream consumers (`nx aspects show`, retrieval ranking, telemetry) treat them as authoritative.

## Probe evidence (2026-05-08)

```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM document_aspects WHERE confidence IS NULL;  -- 53
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM document_aspects WHERE confidence = 0;       -- 72
SELECT MIN(confidence), MAX(confidence), AVG(confidence) FROM document_aspects WHERE confidence IS NOT NULL;
-- min=0.000  max=1.000  avg=0.823
```

## Hypothesis

Two extractors are active:

- `scholarly-paper-v1` (385 rows, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) — the LLM-driven extractor, can return any confidence in [0,1]
- `rdr-frontmatter-v1` (368 rows) — deterministic; should always return confidence=1.0

The 125 zero/NULL rows are likely all from `scholarly-paper-v1` where the LLM returned a low-quality response and the extraction wrapper either parsed `null`/`0.0` from the JSON or failed to parse and defaulted to NULL.

(Hypothesis to verify in implementation: split confidence stats by extractor_name.)

## Fix options

(a) **Fail-loud on commit** — raise/skip when confidence < threshold (e.g. 0.3). Re-queue for retry with a different prompt or model. Mirrors RDR-089's no-silent-fallback ethos (project memory entry: "no silent fallbacks for data-correctness problems").

(b) **Mark and hide** — keep the row but add a `quality_status` column (`accepted` / `low_confidence` / `failed`); default-filter retrieval. Mirrors the soft-delete pattern from RDR-107.

(c) **Just reject and log** — don't persist the row at all; structured-log the failure for telemetry; let the queue retry.

Option (a) or (c) is closer to the project's "no silent fallback" disposition. Option (b) is closer to the Xanadu/RDR-107 pattern. User direction needed.

## Affected files

- src/nexus/aspects/extractor.py (or wherever the extraction wrapper lives)
- src/nexus/db/t2/aspects.py — write path
- New: tests/test_aspects_low_confidence.py

## Refs

- 2026-05-08 prod-shakeout aspect probe
- RDR-089 (structured aspects)
- project memory: feedback_no_silent_fallbacks_for_correctness.md
close_reason: Closed

title: P2: CLAUDE.md 3-clause expire-guard SQL rule is stale (expires_at was removed Phase 5c)
description:
## Symptom

CLAUDE.md "Hot rules" carries an expire-guard SQL invariant that no longer applies:

> **T3 expire-guard SQL must be three-clause.** `ttl_days > 0 AND expires_at != "" AND expires_at < now`. The `!= ""` clause is mandatory: permanent rows have `expires_at=""` which sorts before ISO timestamps and would be wrongly deleted by a two-clause guard.

This rule is from the era when T3 chunks had an `expires_at` column. RDR-101 Phase 5c removed it. Current code (verified 2026-05-08):

- `src/nexus/metadata_schema.py:95-99`:

  ```
  # Lifecycle / scoring (5) — `expires_at` removed; expiry is
  # derived from `indexed_at + ttl_days` Python-side. ``ttl_days=0``
  ```

- `src/nexus/db/t3.py:986-988`:

  ```python
  # ttl_days > 0 (eliminates permanent entries) then check
  # indexed_at + ttl_days Python-side via is_expired().
  ttl_where: dict = {"ttl_days": {"$gt": 0}}
  ```

- `src/nexus/metadata_schema.py:359-369` (the helper that replaced the SQL):

  ```python
  # ── Expiry helper (replaces the dropped ``expires_at`` field) ──
  # Replaces the previous ``where=expires_at < now`` filter. Computes
  # expiry from ``indexed_at + ttl_days`` Python-side. ``ttl_days == 0``
  ```

## Probe evidence (2026-05-08)

Across all 150 T3 collections (290,662 chunks):

- 228,334 (78.56%) permanent (`expires_at=''`, `ttl_days=0`) — healthy
- 12 chunks with `ttl_days>0` and empty `expires_at` (Python-side TTL) — valid post-Phase-5c shape
- 19 chunks with legacy `expires_at` populated AND `ttl_days>0` — pre-Phase-5c residue, harmless
- 62,297 (21.43%) with neither field (pre-fields chunks) — code reads `meta.get("ttl_days", 0)` so default-handled
- 0 expired-but-alive (no TTL bypass)

## Fix

CLAUDE.md update — replace the stale 3-clause rule with the current invariant:

> **T3 TTL is computed Python-side, not in SQL.** Schema columns: `ttl_days` (default 0 = permanent) and `indexed_at` (ISO8601). Expiry filter pattern: `where={"ttl_days": {"$gt": 0}}` to skip permanent rows, then `nexus.metadata_schema.is_expired(meta)` Python-side to evaluate. The legacy `expires_at` column was removed in RDR-101 Phase 5c; do not reference it in new code.

## Affected files

- CLAUDE.md (also docs/architecture.md if it carries the same rule — TODO verify)

## Tests

- `grep -rn "expires_at" CLAUDE.md docs/architecture.md docs/cli-reference.md` should return 0 hits after the fix.
- `grep -rn "expires_at < now\|three-clause" docs/` should return 0 hits.

## Refs

- RDR-101 Phase 5c (removed expires_at)
- 2026-05-08 prod-shakeout TTL probe — confirmed Python-side TTL works as designed; no actual data hazard.
close_reason: Closed

title: investigate: catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage FAIL (taxonomy__centroids 2014 orphans)
description: 2026-05-08 prod probe: nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage flags three 100%-orphan-ratio collections: knowledge__rdr (4 orphans), knowledge__scratch (1), taxonomy__centroids (2014). Remediation hint says retired post Phase 5b - re-index. But taxonomy__centroids is BERTopic-generated (RDR-070), not user-indexed. Hypotheses: (1) doctor's t3-doc-id-coverage check should EXCLUDE taxonomy__* and knowledge__scratch from orphan count (false positive class - centroids are embedding-space anchors, not docs); (2) knowledge__rdr 4 chunks are stale MCP store_put traffic without doc_id propagation; (3) knowledge__scratch 1 chunk is ephemeral. Action: read-only investigation first; either fix the audit's exclusion list or repair the underlying chunks; do NOT delete taxonomy__centroids - it's the BERTopic anchor set for RDR-070 search-time topic boosting. Refs: src/nexus/commands/catalog.py doctor_cmd --t3-doc-id-coverage, docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-orphan-recovery.md, docs/rdr/rdr-070-*.
notes:
2026-05-08 deep probe — confirmed taxonomy__centroids is a false positive class

Sampled taxonomy__centroids chunks via chromadb.CloudClient: chunks have metadata schema {collection, doc_count, label, topic_id} - completely different from document chunks. Example: {'collection':'code__arcaneum-2ad2825c', 'label':'output_json click json', 'doc_count':8, 'topic_id':301}. These are BERTopic centroid embeddings, not document chunks. They reference the SOURCE collection (code__arcaneum-2ad2825c) they were derived from.

The doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage check (src/nexus/commands/catalog.py) treats absence of doc_id as orphan-ness. For taxonomy__* it should special-case: these chunks intentionally have no doc_id (they're not documents). Same for any future centroid/embedding-anchor collections.

Recommended fix: doctor's t3-doc-id-coverage should skip collections matching prefix taxonomy__* (or check for the {topic_id, label} schema as the centroid signal). Add a config-driven exclude list.

ALSO check if knowledge__rdr (4 orphans) and knowledge__scratch (1 orphan) are real or false positives — sample those too in the same investigation.

- src/nexus/commands/catalog.py doctor_cmd --t3-doc-id-coverage check

description:

Verified: zero fixture-cache files have been written to ~/.config/nexus/ since the fixture landed.

## Risk

The 1,707 historical files were a one-time manual cleanup (already done 2026-05-08). Future leakage is prevented by the autouse fixture, but only for tests that USE that fixture. A test that explicitly `monkeypatch.delenv("NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR")` or that bypasses the fixture entirely (e.g. spawns a subprocess that re-resolves nexus_config_dir() against the real ~/.config/nexus/) could re-introduce the leak silently.

## Proposal

Add a session-scoped `pytest_sessionfinish` hook that:

1. Captures the set of *.cache files in ~/.config/nexus/ at session START.
2. At session FINISH, computes the delta.
3. If any new cache files match a test-fixture prefix list (`nexus-rich0`, `nexus-mini0`, `code-repo`, `prose-repo`, `pdf-repo`, `stage-b-repo`, `sentinel-repo`, `test-repo`, `nx-shakeout-`), FAIL the session with a clear error pointing to the offending test.

This catches:
- Tests that explicitly bypass _isolate_config_dir (e.g. via monkeypatch.delenv).
- Tests that spawn subprocesses without inheriting NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR.
- New fixture names whose prefix isn't on the allowlist (in which case the test author updates the list).

Implementation cost: ~30 LOC in tests/conftest.py.

## References

- nexus-mrmq (PR #601): the autouse `_isolate_config_dir` fixture that prevents ongoing leakage
- src/nexus/indexer.py:1810: cache write site
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-105 P5.2: NEXUS_SKIP_T1 honored alongside NX_T1_ISOLATED with deprecation warning
description:

title: RDR-105 P4.4: Add periodic orphan-reaper at MCP startup (~10 LOC)
description:
Sub-task of P4 (nexus-jnx7). Add a periodic best-effort GC sweep at top-level MCP startup. Replaces watchdog's orphan-reap responsibility (reaped in P4.1).

Implementation (~10 LOC at MCP top-level startup):
  for path in (Path.home() / '.config' / 'nexus').glob('t1_addr.*'):
      try:
          pid = int(path.name.removeprefix('t1_addr.'))
      except ValueError:
          continue
      if not _is_pid_alive(pid):  # retained from P4.2
          path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

Properties:
- Best-effort. Not load-bearing. A missed reap leaks ~50 MB chroma + ~100 bytes file until next sweep.
- Runs only at MCP top-level startup (not periodic in-process — keeps it dead simple).
- Reuses _is_pid_alive primitive retained from session.py.
- Independent of the existing sweep_orphan_tmpdirs (which handles nx_t1_* tmpdir cleanup, also retained, unchanged).

Note PID-reuse edge case (per RDR §'Remaining low-stakes residuals'): a claude_pid from a long-dead session could be reused on Linux (PIDs wrap at 4,194,304). Reaper would skip cleanup of the genuine orphan (its PID looks alive, even though the alive process isn't Claude). Low-stakes; reaper is best-effort; orphan eventually gets reaped when its (reused) PID dies. No mitigation required, but worth a code comment.

TDD: tmp_path fixture creating fake t1_addr.<pid> files for live + dead pids; assert reaper unlinks the dead-pid files only.

See RDR-105 §'Code changes (additions)' last bullet, §'Remaining low-stakes residuals'.
close_reason: Deleted in P4 along with the multi-writer coordination layer.

title: MCP server's chroma spawn / .session write is failing silently; CLI cannot find record
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-06 during validation of GH #567 fix. Local Claude session shows:
- ~/.config/nexus/current_session points at UUID 902900b0-...
- ~/.config/nexus/sessions/ is empty (no .session file)
- MCP tools work in-conversation because the server uses an in-process EphemeralClient
- CLI nx scratch raises T1ServerNotFoundError (correct post-#567 behavior)

Architecture INTENT (RDR-094 + nx-mcp ownership): the FastMCP lifespan calls _t1_chroma_init_if_owner which spawns chroma via start_t1_server() and writes the .session record via write_session_record_by_id. CLI tools find that record and connect via HttpClient → cross-process shared T1.

Architecture REALITY today: the start_t1_server() call is wrapped in a broad try/except at src/nexus/mcp/core.py:163-171 that swallows ANY exception with just a structlog.warning('t1_chroma_spawn_failed'). When this fires, _OWNED_CHROMA stays empty, no .session is written, and CLI tools have nothing to connect to. The MCP server keeps running with its per-process EphemeralClient.

GH #567's PR #569 makes the CLI fail loud on this state. The remaining work is to address WHY start_t1_server() is failing in the first place (or why _t1_chroma_init_if_owner isn't running its happy path) so the .session file lands and CLI cross-process sharing works as designed.

Investigation steps:
1. Tail ~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log for 't1_chroma_spawn_failed' events to see the actual exception.
2. Check whether start_t1_server() returns successfully but _OWNED_CHROMA doesn't update (race / branch issue).
3. Check whether SessionStart fires write_claude_session_id before or after the MCP lifespan, and whether the timing matters.

Fix candidates:
- Surface the spawn failure more loudly (raise instead of swallow) so the operator sees the immediate cause.
- Investigate why chroma fails to start in this environment.
- Possibly: have the MCP server's lifespan retry the spawn or fall back to a port-based chroma rather than tmpdir-based.

Filed as follow-up to GH #567 / PR #569. The CLI's loud-failure shipped first because silent data loss was the headline bug; making the .session file land is the structural fix.

title: CI py3.12 sqlite-multiconn flake: tests with multiple short-lived sqlite3 connections fail intermittently on Linux runner only
description:
During 4.26.2 release polling (PR #536), CI Python 3.12 hit two unrelated test flakes back-to-back, both pass locally on macOS:

1. tests/test_doc_indexer.py::test_preflight_registration_idempotent_on_staleness_skip — 'assert n2 == 0' (idempotency violation; second insert added rows it should not)
2. tests/test_console_health_aspect_queue.py::test_mixed_statuses_aggregate_correctly — 'assert 4 == 5' (missed one of five just-inserted rows)

Common shape:
- Multiple short-lived sqlite3 connections opened in fixture/helper functions (open → INSERT → commit → close)
- Subsequent connection reads expecting full visibility of prior writes
- Linux GH runner Python 3.12 only (system sqlite 3.37, ext4)
- Linux Python 3.13 passes (deadsnakes Python ships newer sqlite3)
- macOS local Python 3.12 passes (APFS + newer SQLite)

Hypothesis: fsync/commit-visibility window between connection close and next connection's read isn't reliably covered by the older sqlite3.37's default 'delete' journal mode on a busy CI ext4 disk. Flake floor probably high single digits %.

Fix options (preferred order):
1. Convert helpers to T2Database which already does WAL + busy_timeout
2. Keep one persistent sqlite3 connection per test fixture (open once, reuse)
3. Add 'PRAGMA synchronous=FULL' + 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint' on test connections

Prefer #1 since it removes the helper duplication.
close_reason: Closed

title: 4.26.2: backfill source_uri on document_aspects rows where NULL/empty (ocu9.11 prerequisite)
description:
Live audit on production document_aspects 2026-05-06 (memory: ocu9_11_audit_empirical_findings):

  total_rows:                 579
  null_or_empty source_uri:    61 (10.5%)
  null source_path:             0

The bead nexus-ocu9 (RDR-096 Phase 2) backfilled source_uri across 5471 paths at 99.98% round-trip clean (research-2). The 61 NULL/empty rows we're seeing now likely came from one of:
  - pre-4.23.0 rows the backfill missed
  - writer paths that landed AFTER the backfill but BEFORE the v4.23.0 structural enforcement (RDR-102 Phase B / commit 83ac62c7)
  - test pollution writing direct to production memory.db

## Why this is a 4.26.2 bite, not 4.27.0

ocu9.11 (4.27.0) ships the DROP COLUMN migration. The bead spec says pre-migration audit BLOCKS if any source_uri NULL row exists. With 10.5% prevalence the audit blocks the migration entirely on first run.

Two options:
  A. Strict audit blocks 4.27.0 migration; user manually triages 61 rows
  B. Auto-coalesce in 4.27.0 migration's INSERT...SELECT (using COALESCE(source_uri, 'file://' || source_path))

Both work, but a third option is cleaner: backfill the 61 rows in 4.26.2 ahead of 4.27.0 so the strict-audit version of ocu9.11 runs cleanly. 10 minutes of work, zero risk — just an UPDATE.

## Scope

1. Add migration in src/nexus/db/migrations.py:
   - migrate_backfill_document_aspects_source_uri
   - Idempotent: only updates rows where source_uri IS NULL OR source_uri = ''
   - SQL:
     UPDATE document_aspects
        SET source_uri = 'file://' || source_path
      WHERE (source_uri IS NULL OR source_uri = '')
        AND source_path IS NOT NULL
        AND source_path != ''
   - Log structured 'document_aspects_source_uri_backfilled' with row count.
   - Register in MIGRATIONS list at version 4.26.2.

2. Test in tests/test_migrations.py:
   - Fixture: insert 3 rows: 1 with source_uri set, 1 with source_uri NULL, 1 with both empty.
   - Apply migration.
   - Assert: NULL row gets file://+source_path. Set row unchanged. Both-empty row unchanged.

## Acceptance

- 4.26.2 release ships the backfill
- Production audit returns 0 NULL/empty source_uri rows
- 4.27.0's ocu9.11 strict-audit migration then runs cleanly without triage backlog

## Why not just do A or B in 4.27.0

Option A surfaces 61 rows of triage backlog at the worst moment (release-prep flow blocks). Option B is silent — no structured audit signal, no operator visibility into what got coalesced. The 4.26.2 backfill turns the data-quality issue into a one-time observable migration with a row count, which is a better posture for a column-drop release that's already breaking external SQL consumers.

Files: src/nexus/db/migrations.py, tests/test_migrations.py.

Bead: filed 2026-05-06 to ship in 4.26.2 patch ahead of 4.27.0 ocu9.11 migration.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 1B: nx tier-status CLI + SessionEnd tier-write summary hook
description:
Phase 1B follow-up to Phase 1A (nexus-???; the tier_writes telemetry table + recording wires up first).

## Why

Phase 1A captures tier writes to T2. Phase 1B surfaces them to the user.

## Scope

1. **`nx tier-status` CLI** at src/nexus/commands/tier_status.py:
   - Default: summary of CURRENT session (from NX_SESSION_ID env or t1 watchdog state).
   - --session <id>: specific session.
   - --last N: aggregate last N sessions.
   - --json: structured output for downstream tooling.
   - --since <iso>: window override.
   Output columns: tool, tier, agent (or '<none>'), count.

2. **`nx doctor --check-tier-discipline`**: audit current session — flag if:
   - Session > 30 minutes wall-clock with zero memory_put / store_put / plan_save calls
   - More than 10 raw `search` calls without a `nx_answer` call (suggests 'compose, don't search raw' was missed)
   - More than 5 `Read` of project files without a `memory_search` (suggests pre-flight skip)
   Heuristic only. Returns warning, not error. Does not block.

3. **SessionEnd hook tier-write summary**: append a structured summary to nx-session-end-launcher output. Format:
   ```
   tier writes this session: T1=N (scratch), T2=M (memory) + K (plans), T3=P (store)
   ```
   Suppressed if all zero AND session < 5 min wall-clock (transactional sessions don't need a noise summary).

## Out of scope

- READ-side recording. Heuristics in --check-tier-discipline use existing tool-call evidence (transcript scan).
- Per-agent attribution. Blocked on nexus-9clx.
- Push notifications / persistent leaderboards.

## Acceptance

title: aspect_extraction_queue.reclaim_stale: timestamp format mismatch — SQL comparison silently fails, dead-worker orphans never reclaimed
description:
Found during 4.25.3 shakeout drain validation 2026-05-06.

src/nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py:416 — reclaim_stale runs:
```sql
UPDATE aspect_extraction_queue
SET status = 'pending', last_attempt_at = NULL
WHERE status = 'in_progress'
  AND last_attempt_at < datetime('now', '-300 seconds')
```

Format mismatch:
- last_attempt_at stored as: '2026-05-06T03:01:51.332866+00:00' (ISO 8601, T separator, +00:00 suffix)
- datetime('now', '-300 seconds') returns: '2026-05-06 10:01:54' (space separator, no timezone, no fractional)

String comparison: 'T' (0x54) > ' ' (0x20). Orphan timestamps sort AFTER cutoff for ALL in_progress rows of this format. Reclaim therefore matches ZERO rows, regardless of staleness.

Repro on this DB right now:
```
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM aspect_extraction_queue
WHERE status='in_progress'
  AND last_attempt_at < datetime('now', '-300 seconds');     -- returns 0
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM aspect_extraction_queue
WHERE status='in_progress'
  AND datetime(last_attempt_at) < datetime('now', '-300 seconds');  -- returns 5
```

Effect: when a worker dies after claiming rows, those rows are orphaned forever. The 5 orphans from 03:01:51 UTC sat in_progress for 7+ hours despite the 300s reclaim timeout.

Acceptance:
- reclaim_stale wraps last_attempt_at in datetime() to normalize (or stores last_attempt_at in matching format)
- Test added: enqueue + manually set status=in_progress + last_attempt_at to a stale ISO 8601 timestamp; reclaim_stale should return 1, row should be back to status=pending
- Existing test test_reclaim_stale_resets_old_rows must still pass

Out of scope: backfilling existing schema (the column is already TEXT, no migration needed; just normalize the comparison).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #523 (squashed 58634990); shipped in conexus 4.25.4

title: catalog MCP: list/resolve contract issues found in 4.25.3 shakeout
description:
Two anomalies found exercising the nexus-catalog MCP server in 4.25.3 (2026-05-05):

## 1. catalog_list does not surface document-level entries by content_type
Calling `catalog_list(content_type="rdr")` returns []  even though `catalog_stats` reports 2,270 documents of type 'rdr' and `catalog_search(content_type="rdr")` returns RDR documents fine. catalog_list with no filter returns owner-level catalog rows (tumblers 1.2.1, 1.3.1 etc — one per repo+content_type combination). Filter behaviour is opaque: either it filters owner-level rows on the type field (which is rarely 'rdr') and so returns empty, or there's a real bug. Either way the user-facing semantics don't match the type-breakdown that catalog_stats publishes.

Repro:
```
catalog_stats() → {'by_type': {'rdr': 2270, ...}}
catalog_list(content_type='rdr', limit=5) → []
catalog_search(content_type='rdr', query='RDR-101', limit=3) → 3 RDR entries
```

Fix: either (a) make catalog_list surface document-level entries with the same semantics as catalog_search, or (b) document explicitly that catalog_list is owner-scoped only and add a docstring example.

## 2. catalog_resolve raises ValueError on dashed owner_id
`catalog_resolve(corpus='code', owner='1-2188')` → `Error: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '1-2188'`. The owner format coming out of `nx doctor` is dashed strings ('1-2188', '1-2153', 'Luciferase-f2d57dbc'). The resolve handler is treating owner as numeric. Either:
- The MCP arg schema should reject non-numeric early with a typed error (not bare ValueError leaked from int())
- Or it should accept the dashed string format that doctor publishes

The bare ValueError is the immediate UX bug. The schema mismatch is the deeper question.

## Why this matters
catalog_resolve is the documented entry point for going from semantic identity → physical_collection name. Catalog/skills tutorials in the plugin say to use it. If the most natural input format (the format doctor displays) raises ValueError, downstream skills calling resolve programmatically will silently break.

## Acceptance
- catalog_resolve fails with a typed validation error (not bare ValueError) when owner format is wrong, with a hint at the expected format
- catalog_list docstring clarifies owner-scoped vs document-scoped semantics, OR catalog_list grows a way to enumerate documents by content_type to match catalog_stats counts

Surfaced during 4.25.3 live shakeout (bd memory: shakeout-4.25.3-2026-05-05).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #533. catalog_list now filters content_type in SQL (pagination correct); catalog_resolve emits typed error pointing at dotted-tumbler form instead of leaking int() ValueError.

title: nx_answer plan-miss path needs progress visibility — silent claude -p chain feels like a hang
description:
On a plan-match miss, nx_answer (src/nexus/mcp/core.py:2952-3031) spawns a claude -p subprocess for the inline planner (300s timeout, 1-shot retry at 150s) then chains a claude -p per operator step (300s each). Worst case 4-step plan = ~25min wall-clock. From the MCP caller's seat with zero progress visibility, indistinguishable from a hang.

Confirmed in 4.25.3 live shakeout 2026-05-05: nx_answer call against a cold-miss verb-shaped question was indistinguishable from a hang and got cancelled.

This is a UX/observability bug, not a runtime correctness bug. The structural latency is fine if and only if the caller can see progress.

Acceptance:
- Per-step structured log emit (nx_answer_step_start / nx_answer_step_complete) with step index, tool name, elapsed wall-clock
- Some caller-surfaceable progress signal (incremental return? callback? at minimum a stderr line per step from the MCP server so the parent Claude Code can render it)
- Document the worst-case latency in the nx_answer docstring so callers do not assume sub-second

Related:
- nexus-wr5o (1-shot retry on OperatorOutputError — already shipped)
- nexus-l0yh (graceful OperatorError fallback)

Not in scope: making the plan-miss path fast (separate problem — needs better plan library coverage; see plans-triage in 2026-05-05 shakeout notes).
notes:

title: nx_answer inline planner: add 1-shot retry on OperatorOutputError (transient JSON parse failures)
description:
## Symptom

During the conexus 4.25.2 hooks/agents shakeout (2026-05-05), a dispatched nx:codebase-deep-analyzer agent reported in its tool-sequence summary:

> "nx_answer hit an inline planner JSON parse error and returned no result"

The error string surfaced to the agent matches the message produced by:

- `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:3247-3250` -> "No matching plan found and inline planner failed: {reason}"
- `src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py:153-156` -> "claude -p output is not valid JSON: {exc} - got: {raw[:200]}"

So the failure path is: `_nx_answer_plan_miss` -> `claude_dispatch` -> `claude -p` returns malformed JSON despite `--output-format json --json-schema` -> `OperatorOutputError` raised -> caught by `nx_answer` -> string error surfaced to caller.

## Why it warrants a fix

The on-disk plumbing is already correct: timeout, schema enforcement, and structured error surfacing all work. The remaining gap is **retry**: `OperatorOutputError` from `claude -p` is plausibly transient (model output drift, partial stream, structured_output null on first attempt then valid on retry), but the current code path raises on first failure with no second attempt.

Single-shot retries are appropriate when:

- The error class is plausibly transient (JSONDecodeError or null structured_output, not OperatorError or OperatorTimeoutError).
- Cost ceiling stays bounded (one extra `claude -p` call worst case).
- Caller experience improves materially: shakeout report would have been "succeeded after 1 retry" instead of "returned no result".

## Repro

Not deterministically reproducible (transient model output). Inferred from the shakeout transcript. The fix is observability + resilience, not a known-bad input fix.

## Proposed fix

In `_nx_answer_plan_miss` (mcp/core.py:2937), wrap the `claude_dispatch` call in a 2-iteration loop:

- Attempt 1: 300s timeout (current).
- Attempt 2 (only on `OperatorOutputError`): 150s timeout. Halved so one hang doesn't double total wall time.
- `OperatorError` and `OperatorTimeoutError` do NOT retry — those are not transient.
- WARN log on first failure with the error string + attempt number, so future runs surface in observability.

## Acceptance

- Test: `_nx_answer_plan_miss` with mock `claude_dispatch` that raises `OperatorOutputError` once then returns valid payload -> succeeds on second attempt, returns the parsed Match.
- Test: mock raises `OperatorOutputError` twice -> raises after second attempt with the second exception.
- Test: mock raises `OperatorError` (non-zero exit) -> raises immediately, no retry.

## Originating context

Conexus 4.25.2 shakeout, 2026-05-05. Surfaced in the same dispatch that produced nexus-a414 (catalog_search empty tumblers + auto-linker silent swallow). Both are observability gaps in the otherwise-working RDR-080 retrieval layer.
close_reason: Already shipped via PR #519/#520/#521 era — code at src/nexus/mcp/core.py:3108-3131 (1-shot retry on OperatorOutputError, 300s→150s halved timeout, OperatorError/Timeout not retried). 5 tests at tests/test_nx_answer.py:1856-1920 (TestNxAnswerPlannerRetry) confirm: succeeds-on-second-attempt, exhausted-raises-second-error, no-retry-for-operator-error, no-retry-for-timeout-error, first-attempt-success-no-retry. All 5 green 2026-05-06.

title: Restore T1/T2/T3 + nx_answer signal in startup hooks (over-corrected by trim e2fc2408)
description:
## Finding

The April 25 startup-hook trim (commit e2fc2408 / PR #320) removed verbose tool-doc prose to save ~1100 tok/session + ~360 tok/dispatch — a real win — but over-corrected by also stripping behavior-driving content. Telemetry mined from 795 session transcripts (505 pre-trim, 290 post-trim, 10-day windows on each side) shows the regression is concentrated in composed-retrieval tools:

| Tool | Pre-trim per-session rate | Post-trim per-session rate | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nx_answer` | 4.6% | 1.0% | **-78%** |
| `plan_search` | 3.4% | 0.3% | **-90%** |
| `catalog_search` | 2.4% | 0% | **-100%** |
| `store_put` | 0.4% | 0% | -100% |
| `store_list` | 0.4% | 0% | -100% |
| `search` (T3) | 5.1% | 5.9% | +16% |
| `scratch` (T1) | 3.2% | 7.2% | +125% |
| `memory_put` (T2) | 9.9% | 20% | +102% |

T1 / T2 / raw `search` actually went up — they were not the regression. The collapse is specifically in:
- Composed retrieval (`nx_answer`, `query`)
- Plan reuse (`plan_search` / `plan_save`)
- Catalog metadata + auto-linking (`catalog_search`, `store_put`)

These tools shared a property: their pre-trim prose included **examples + reasoning + recipes** that the trim collapsed to bare tool names.

## Hypothesis (validated against the diff)

What got cut and was load-bearing:
- The **3 specific phrasings** for routing analytical questions to `nx_answer` ("how does X work", "tradeoffs in Y", "compare X across projects").
- The **"ALL analytical questions go through nx_answer"** imperative section header (softened to a parenthetical).
- The **verb-shape paragraph with reasoning** ("composed retrieval strictly more useful than raw chunks").
- The **AUTO-LINK 3-step recipe** in subagent-start.sh (`scratch put (link-context) → catalog_search → store_put`) which connected three tools into one workflow.
- The **tier "check before X" cues** ("check before researching", "before project work", "before duplicating sibling work").

What got cut correctly:
- `<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>` 1%-chance preamble (shouting, no signal).
- "The Rule" duplicate.
- "Skill Priority" / "Skill Types" / "User Instructions" tail (meta with no decision content).
- Multi-line tool param signatures with 3-5 example calls each (one-liners are sufficient).
- 7 of the 12 Red Flags (skill-meta noise).

## Strategy

Surgical restoration: bring back the **examples + reasoning + recipes**, leave the bloat-removal in place. Net cost: ~+2000 chars across both files vs current; still ~5800 chars lighter than pre-trim.

Specifically:
1. SKILL.md: restore "ALL analytical questions go through `nx_answer`" with verb-shape paragraph; restore tier "when to check" cues; restore 3 specific search→nx_answer phrasings in Common Mistakes; add 5 tool-skipping Red Flags (down from 12).
2. subagent-start.sh: add tier "when to check" cues in NX_TIERS heredoc; add Verb-shape question routing line in NX_T3; restore AUTO-LINK as a discrete 3-step recipe heredoc.

## Constraints honored

- Heredoc bodies kept under 500 bytes each (bash 5.3 deadlock guard).
- All three `SKIP_*` classification branches still work.
- Plugin-structure tests + hook tests stay green.

## Verification

- Sandbox-tested under bash 3.2 (Apple system) and bash 5.3 (homebrew); no deadlock; exit 0.
- All 3 restoration blocks emit correctly under empty-stdin and stress-task stdin.
- `tests/test_plugin_structure.py` (576 tests), `tests/test_hooks.py` (16), `tests/test_hook_drift_guard.py` (10), `tests/test_hook_cli.py` (6), `tests/test_context.py` (12) — all green.

The using-nx-skills SKILL.md restored the imperative 'ALL analytical questions go through nx_answer' header, the verb-shape phrasings paragraph, the 3 search→nx_answer corrections in Common Mistakes, and the 5 Red Flags. The subagent-start.sh restored tier 'check before X' cues in NX_TIERS, the verb-shape question routing line in NX_T3, and the AUTO-LINK 3-step recipe in NX_AUTOLINK. title: Catalog rebuild dispatch caps incremental at ~850ms via _event_log_covers_legacy O(N) scan
description:
## Finding

RDR-104 (PR #517 / nexus-plpv) implements incremental catalog projection rebuild and claims:

> "Steady-state Catalog() construction after a single write becomes <100 ms (vs. the prior ~4 s on a 452K-event log)"

Live shakeout on conexus 4.25.0 against the production catalog (~/.config/nexus/catalog, 460,831 events / 244 MB events.jsonl) measures **~850 ms**, not <100 ms. The 4.25.0 RDR-104 dispatch logic itself is correct — the bottleneck is `_event_log_covers_legacy()` which predates RDR-104.

## Measurements

- Empty-delta with NO mtime change (rebuild dispatch skipped entirely): **0.5–1.5 ms** ✓
- Empty-delta INSIDE rebuild dispatch (mtime ticks, no new events): **~850 ms** ⚠️
- Incremental dispatch (mtime ticks, +1 new event): **~860 ms** ⚠️
- `_event_log_covers_legacy()` in isolation on this catalog: **838 ms cold / 833 ms warm**

## Root cause

`src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:997` calls `_event_log_covers_legacy()` unconditionally on every rebuild dispatch, before the empty-delta / bootstrap / invalidated / incremental sub-branches. The function (line 1283) does:

1. Full O(N) line scan + json.loads of `documents.jsonl` (16 MB, ~70K lines)
2. Full O(N) line scan + json.loads of `events.jsonl` (244 MB, 460,831 lines)

On a 460K-event catalog this is ~838 ms — dominated by Python's json.loads on the events file.

## Why it matters

The MCP server instantiates one Catalog() per tool call (per `src/nexus/catalog/__init__.py:32` docstring). After every write event, the next tool call falls into the rebuild path. The new floor for post-write MCP latency is ~850 ms, not the 100 ms RDR-104 advertised.

The RDR-104 incremental dispatch is correct — synthetic-event test confirmed (doc lands in projection, marker advances to new EOF atomically, header hash preserved). The dispatch logic is just gated by an O(N) guardrail that runs first.

## Possible remediations

1. **Skip the guardrail when the marker is established.** The bootstrap-fallback risk only applies before the first incremental rebuild succeeds; once `_meta.last_applied_event_offset` is non-null, the legacy-coverage check is unnecessary. Cheapest fix.
2. **Cache the guardrail result keyed on (events.jsonl mtime, documents.jsonl mtime).** If neither file changed since the last covers_legacy() return value, reuse it.
3. **Replace the O(N) scan with a streaming counter that exits early once the threshold is met.** Net registrations only need to exceed `int(legacy_doc_count * 0.95)` — once that count is reached, return True without finishing the file.

## Reproduction

```python
SHAKE=/tmp/shake-$$
mkdir -p $SHAKE/catalog
cp ~/.config/nexus/catalog/{events,documents,links,owners}.jsonl $SHAKE/catalog/
cp ~/.config/nexus/catalog/.catalog.db $SHAKE/catalog/
SHAKE=$SHAKE uv run python <<'PY'
import os, time
from pathlib import Path
from nexus.catalog import Catalog
cdir = Path(os.environ['SHAKE']) / 'catalog'
c = Catalog(catalog_dir=cdir, db_path=cdir/'.catalog.db')
t0 = time.perf_counter()
c._event_log_covers_legacy()
print(f"covers_legacy: {(time.perf_counter()-t0)*1000:.0f} ms")
PY
```

## References

- RDR-104 PR: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/pull/517
- Epic nexus-plpv (closed)
- Source: `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:997` (call site), `:1283` (function body)
close_reason: Closed

title: pdf_extractor: page_boundaries uniform char distribution gives wrong page_number for MinerU chunks
description:
In _mineru_build_result (pdf_extractor.py around line 800-809), page_boundaries is computed via 'chars_per_page = total_len / page_count', distributing characters uniformly across pages regardless of actual content. The chunker (pdf_chunker.py:211) reads page_boundaries to assign page_number to every chunk. For real PDFs with uneven content (figures, tables, full-page formulas), chunks get tagged with wrong page numbers — a theorem on page 8 can be tagged as page 2 in search results.

Pre-existing bug, NOT introduced by nexus-2fyb. Surfaced during the multi-reviewer audit on PR #509 because every MinerU-extracted PDF hits this code path. Fix requires plumbing per-page markdown lengths from _extract_with_mineru's batch loop into _mineru_build_result and using actual character offsets.

Affects: any user inspecting page_number metadata in T3 chunks for MinerU-extracted PDFs.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed. _extract_with_mineru collects per_page_lengths (line 540) and threads them into _mineru_build_result (line 903 takes per_page_lengths param); page_boundaries built from per-page actual offsets.

title: indexer: stamp pipeline_version on every successful index, not just --force
description: The current stamp gate at src/nexus/indexer.py:1995 is 'if force:'. This is wrong: --force does not change WHICH pipeline produces embeddings, it only bypasses the file-level staleness check. Embeddings written by an incremental 'nx index repo .' use the same v4 pipeline as a --force run; refusing to stamp them is a category error. The user-visible consequence: nx doctor reports 'no version stamp (index with --force to stamp)' against collections that ARE current, and the suggested remediation re-pays for 4-5K files of Voyage embedding to repair a state that should not exist. Fix: stamp on every successful index_repository run, regardless of force. This is safe because: (a) the indexer always uses the current pipeline for any chunks it writes; (b) if no chunks were written (everything skipped as current), the stamp is still correct; (c) if the run failed mid-flight, the stamp is not written (current behaviour for force runs too).
close_reason: Already shipped via PR #508 (commit 9562280d, 2026-05-04). title: [bug] nx store list auto-promotes 2-segment --collection but nx search does not, splitting operator view of legacy collections
description:
Found during post-nexus-7vuw scenario sweep on warm-sandbox 2026-05-04: nx store list --collection knowledge__art and nx search --corpus knowledge__art resolve the user-typed 2-segment name through DIFFERENT paths, so the same operator input returns different collections.

# Reproducer

```bash
# In warm sandbox / local mode:
# 1. Pre-create a legacy 2-segment collection with seed data.
python3 -c "
from nexus.db import make_t3
db = make_t3()
col = db.get_or_create_collection('knowledge__art', strict=False)
col.add(ids=['legacy-1'], documents=['Legacy ART data'],
        metadatas=[{'title':'art-overview','tags':'art','category':'knowledge',
                    'session_id':'','source_agent':'manual','store_type':'knowledge',
                    'indexed_at':'2026-04-01T00:00:00+00:00'}])
"

# 2. Operator types short form to LIST:
nx store list --collection knowledge__art
# Output: 'No entries in knowledge__art__voyage-context-3__v1 at offset 0.'
# (auto-promoted; legacy collection invisible)

# 3. Operator types short form to SEARCH:
nx search 'adaptive resonance' --corpus knowledge__art -m 5
# Output: returns the legacy chunk
# (NOT auto-promoted; legacy hit directly)
```

# Root cause

Two different routing rules for user-typed collection arguments:

- nx store list calls nexus.corpus.t3_collection_name(user_arg)
  which auto-promotes 2-segment input (knowledge__art) to the
  RDR-103 conformant 4-segment shape
  (knowledge__art__voyage-context-3__v1). When the legacy 2-segment
  collection actually exists in T3 and the conformant doesn't, the
  list returns nothing.

- nx search (and the MCP search tool) at
  src/nexus/mcp/core.py:466-467 treats any --corpus value
  containing __ as fully qualified and uses it as-is, with no
  auto-promotion. So legacy 2-segment names hit the existing T3
  collection directly.

# Why this matters

Operators with pre-existing legacy collections (the user's project
memory mentions knowledge__delos and similar) see inconsistent
behavior:

- Search continues to find their data.
- List + put silently look at a different (empty) conformant
  collection.

This violates least surprise — the same --collection knowledge__X
input must resolve to the same collection across all tools, OR the
conformant grammar must be enforced uniformly with a clear migration
verb that operators run once.

# Resolution options

A) Make nx search auto-promote 2-segment --corpus values to
   conformant via t3_collection_name (matches nx store list).
   Pre-existing legacy collections become invisible to --corpus
   knowledge__X; operators must use the bare prefix
   --corpus knowledge (which DOES fan out across all matching
   collections including legacy 2-segment) or run a one-shot
   migration.

B) Make nx store list and nx store put skip the auto-promote
   when the legacy 2-segment name exists in T3 (read-side
   grandfathering at the user-facing CLI layer too, not just at
   T3Database.get_or_create_collection).

C) Hard-cut: emit a deprecation warning when --collection /
   --corpus matches the 2-segment shape; require operators to
   either type the full conformant name or run
   nx catalog backfill-collections to migrate.

(A) is the simplest fix and aligns with RDR-103's stated policy:
short forms are operator conveniences that auto-promote; legacy
data is reachable via prefix-expansion or explicit conformant name.
But it does break search-by-short-name on legacy collections, which
operators currently rely on.

# Test surface

- Unit test in tests/test_mcp_server.py or
  tests/test_search_cmd.py: search(corpus='knowledge__art')
  resolves to the same target collection as
  store_list(collection='knowledge__art'). Today they diverge.

- Integration: round-trip a single store_put then both store_list
  and search with the same --collection / --corpus short
  form must surface the document.

# Dependencies

Surfaced by RDR-103 Phase 5's t3_collection_name auto-promotion
landing in store_put / store_list paths (PR #491) without an
equivalent change in the search corpus resolver. Pre-Phase-5 both
paths used the user input verbatim and were consistent.

# Acceptance

- A single decision recorded for the routing rule (option A, B, or C
  above) with one-line rationale.
- Unit test pinning the round-trip invariant.
- nx store list --collection X and nx search --corpus X
  return the same collection target for any X.
notes: Discovered during nexus-7vuw scenario validation 2026-05-04. Warm-sandbox repro at /tmp/warm-sandbox-index.log. Local-mode T3 was used; the same routing inconsistency exists in cloud mode because the divergence is at the CLI input-resolution layer, not the T3 backend.
close_reason: Fixed: t3_collection_name now optionally probes T3 and grandfathers existing legacy 2-segment collection ahead of auto-promoted conformant target. Read+write CLI surfaces (store_put/get/list/delete + search corpus router for __ values + memory promote) all converge on the same physical collection for the same user input. nx index commands intentionally skip the probe to avoid an eager credential dependency. PR #495 merged to develop. CI green Python 3.12 + 3.13 round-2; sandbox repro shows pre-existing legacy now grandfathered correctly.

title: [bug] Phase 5 produces split RDR collections: path-derived synth vs catalog-tumbler owner
description:
Sandbox shakedown after RDR-103 Phase 5 (PR #491 + PR #492 + PR #493 merged 2026-05-04) surfaced two distinct rdr__ collections for the same repository in the same session:

- `rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1` (4326 chunks) — owner segment is the catalog tumbler ("1.1" → "1-1").
- `rdr__nexus-571b8edd__voyage-context-3__v1` (3926 chunks) — owner segment is the path-derived `<basename>-<hash8>` synthesis fallback.

Both names are RDR-103 conformant (4-segment, voyage-context-3, v1). The strict-naming guard accepts both. The split is silent — there is no error, just two collections that operators (and downstream tools like nx search / nx catalog doctor) have to know about.

# Reproducer

```bash
./tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh reset
./tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh shakedown
# Look at step 5 (greenfield acceptance) collection list.
```

The shakedown's collection table at step 5 shows both rdr collections coexisting, populated by different code paths:

- Step 2 `nx index repo /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus` (integrated path) writes RDR chunks into one of these.
- Step 4 `nx index rdr` (standalone path) writes RDR chunks into the other.

# Root cause hypothesis

Two indexing entry points produce different owner_id segments for the same `(repo, content_type=rdr)` pair:

1. `nx index repo` — `_run_index` calls `_catalog_hook` which registers an owner (tumbler 1.1 here). Subsequent name resolution via `_repo_collection_or_legacy` AND/OR `_migrate_legacy_collections` produces the tumbler-based conformant name `rdr__1-1__voyage-context-3__v1`.
2. `nx index rdr` (`commands/index.py:909-912`) calls `_repo_collection_or_legacy(repo_root, "rdr")` directly without `_catalog_hook`. If the catalog owner is registered, this returns the tumbler-based name. If the owner is NOT registered for this repo_hash at this point, it falls through to `_conformant_name_for_repo` which synthesises the path-derived `rdr__<basename>-<hash8>__voyage-context-3__v1`.

Open question: WHY do these two flows produce different names in the same session when both should see the same owner row after step 2 registers it? Possibilities:
- A timing window in `_run_index` where `_repo_collection_or_legacy` (line 1715-1726) runs BEFORE `_catalog_hook` (line 1737) registers the owner. First-pass writes go to path-derived synth; the operator now has rdr__nexus-571b8edd. Subsequent passes by the migration helper compute a DIFFERENT conformant target (tumbler-based) and write to a NEW collection because the path-derived synth doesn't match the legacy 2-segment shape that `_legacy_collection_name` checks for.
- `_migrate_legacy_collections` decision tree case 4 (neither legacy nor conformant present from its perspective) creates a fresh conformant collection at the tumbler-derived target, ignoring the existing path-derived collection.
- Something else in the order of operations.

# Why this matters

- Operator surprise: `nx search corpus=rdr` returns results from one collection, not both. Cross-collection traversal sees a fragment.
- Storage waste: identical RDR chunks live in two collections; embedding budget paid twice.
- Catalog-doctor drift: `collections-drift` would surface the two rdr__ collections as siblings when only one should exist.
- Operator workflow: someone who normally runs `nx index rdr <path>` for fast RDR-only refresh sees one collection; someone who runs the full `nx index repo` pass sees a second collection. They don't see the same data.

# Acceptance

- A single `(repo, content_type=rdr)` pair maps to exactly one conformant collection, regardless of entry point (`nx index repo` integrated vs `nx index rdr` standalone).
- The fix decision is which owner_id to canonicalise on:
  (a) Catalog tumbler (e.g. `1-1`) — requires `nx index rdr` to either register the owner first OR fail loudly when no catalog owner exists.
  (b) Path-derived (e.g. `nexus-571b8edd`) — requires the catalog-aware path to skip the tumbler lookup for fallback consistency.
  (c) Some normalised form that both paths converge on.

Per RDR-103's intent, the catalog tumbler is the canonical owner. So (a) is the principled answer: `nx index rdr` should ensure the catalog owner exists before resolving the collection name (calling `Catalog.ensure_owner_for_repo` would do it — same helper `_catalog_hook` is supposed to use).

# Test surface

- New regression test: greenfield `nx index repo` then `nx index rdr` should land RDR chunks in EXACTLY ONE conformant rdr__ collection. Counts should match.
- Repro at the unit level: drive `_repo_collection_or_legacy` with both fresh-catalog and post-_catalog_hook states; assert it returns the tumbler-based name in both, not the path-derived fallback.
- Sandbox-level smoke: `./tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh shakedown` should show ONE rdr__ collection in the step 5 table, not two.

# Dependencies

Surfaced by the RDR-103 epic (`nexus-yqnr`) at close. Pre-existing design split that the Phase 5 strict-flip + conformant-fallback synthesis made visible. No blocker for the epic close (the epic shipped); this is a clean-up follow-up.
notes: Discovered during release-sandbox shakedown 2026-05-04 after PR #491 (Phase 5) and PR #492 (Phase 6 docs) merged. Shakedown output preserved at /tmp/sandbox-shakedown.log. Both collections are conformant per the strict-naming guard, so this is a UX / consistency bug, not a correctness gap.
close_reason: Fixed: dropped UNIQUE(name) constraint on owners (replaced with composite UNIQUE(name, owner_type)); extended _migrate_legacy_collections to also detect Phase-5 path-derived 4-segment synth shape. PR #494 merged to develop. Sandbox shakedown 10/10 green; bug repro gone (single rdr collection instead of split).

title: RDR-103 Phase 5: strict-flip default + flag drop + remove legacy registry helpers
description:
RDR-103 Phase 5. RDR file: `docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md` § Phase 5.

**Supersedes nexus-2r71** (one-to-one — see epic for "supersedes jointly with" vocabulary applied elsewhere) — that bead's scope (flip strict_collection_naming default to True, irreversible) is fully absorbed here. Once this bead closes, close `nexus-2r71` with reason "superseded by nexus-yqnr.7 under RDR-103 catalog-as-naming-authority refactor".

The original `nexus-2r71` plan was a 30-site flag-threading exercise. RDR-103 collapsed that to a 5-line patch — the helper (`CollectionName.render`) emits conformant by construction, so no caller-side opt-out is needed. The flag becomes a defensive backstop, not a contract surface.

# Scope

1. Flip `T3Database.strict_collection_naming` default to `True` (irreversible). Implementation surface: `src/nexus/db/t3.py:582-588` reads `[catalog].strict_collection_naming` from config with a `False` default; flip the default to `True` and adjust the surrounding logic. Operators on legacy mode will get a clear `ValueError` (see `src/nexus/db/t3.py:596-602`) pointing at conformant naming docs if any non-conformant write attempt remains.

2. Audit the surface-area for any remaining direct callers that pass non-conformant strings. Per RDR-103, these should already be eliminated by Phase 3, but verify:
   - `grep -rn 'get_or_create_collection.*code__\|docs__\|rdr__\|knowledge__' src/ nx/ tests/` should show only conformant 4-segment shapes (or `CollectionName(...).render()` calls).
   - Any test that mocks `get_or_create_collection` with a hand-rolled legacy string needs updating.
   - Verify Phase 3a's `RepoRegistry.add` migration landed cleanly (no fallback path to the legacy helpers should remain by this point).

3. Drop the `strict_collection_naming` flag in a follow-up commit (single PR, two commits OK). The flag's purpose was to enable opt-in; now it's permanently on.

4. Remove the DEFINITIONS of legacy registry helpers from `src/nexus/registry.py:64-91` — `_collection_name`, `_docs_collection_name`, `_rdr_collection_name` should no longer exist. Phase 3a removed their write-path USES; Phase 4 imported them transiently for the migration path; Phase 5 (this bead) removes the definitions and Phase 4's transient imports together.

   **Pre-deletion checklist**: confirm no lingering import via `grep -rn '_collection_name\|_docs_collection_name\|_rdr_collection_name' src/ nx/ tests/`. Hits should be limited to test assertions of the conformant equivalents (no production code import, no `RepoRegistry.add` fallback).

# Tests

- All existing tests (after Phase 3a's sweep) still green.
- New regression: `T3Database.get_or_create_collection("code__nexus-XXXXXXXX")` (legacy 2-segment) raises `ValueError` (or whatever the strict-flip raises). Pattern after `tests/test_t3_strict_collection_naming.py`.
- Test ensuring no module imports `_collection_name` family after this bead lands.

# Acceptance

- `T3Database.strict_collection_naming` default is `True`.
- Flag exists in code (final-removal commit may or may not be in this bead — it's listed as a follow-up in the RDR; either way OK so long as the flip lands).
- Legacy registry helper DEFINITIONS gone from `src/nexus/registry.py`.
- Phase 4's transient imports removed alongside.
- `pytest tests/` green.
- `nx catalog doctor --collections-drift` exits 0 cleanly on a fresh greenfield AND on a legacy-migrated catalog (post Phase 4).
- **Pause-for-review checkpoint (acceptance criterion, NOT narrative)**: this bead MUST NOT close until the user has explicitly acknowledged the irreversible flip in a review of the diff (per CLAUDE.md `feedback_gate_accept_pause`). Implementer ships the diff, requests user review, waits for explicit approval, THEN closes the bead. Auto-close prohibited.

# Reminders

- TDD for the flip: write the regression test first, then flip the default.
- `code-review-expert` via `/nx:review-code` before complete — irreversible flips warrant a fresh pair of eyes.
- `/nx:test-validate` after review.
- This is a release-shaping change. Per CLAUDE.md `feedback_release_discipline`: full unit + integration suite must run before any release containing this bead. Implementer responsibility before tagging.

# Pinned decisions referenced

(All four indirectly — the flip is what makes the conformant-naming contract enforceable rather than aspirational.)

# Dependencies

Depends on Phase 3 review (`nexus-yqnr.5`) — the flip cannot ship until indexers actually emit conformant names. Also depends on Phase 4 (`nexus-yqnr.6`) — operators with legacy collections need the upgrade path before strict mode rejects writes.
notes:
Phase 3-review (second pass, 2026-05-03) raised two Phase-5-scope items to fold in:

1. context.py:69 constructs `f"rdr__{suffix}"` inline by lifting the suffix from the registry value. Post-Phase-4 the registry is conformant, so the suffix becomes `<owner>__voyage-context-3__v1` and the reconstruction `rdr__<owner>__voyage-context-3__v1` is the conformant shape (works correctly). For unmigrated repos still on the legacy 2-segment registry shape, the reconstruction is `rdr__<basename>-<hash8>` (legacy). Phase 5 should replace this with `Catalog.collection_for_repo(repo, "rdr").render()` once the legacy registry helpers are removed.

2. `_catalog_hook` (indexer.py around line 318-326) does inline owner lookup-or-register that exactly mirrors the new `Catalog.ensure_owner_for_repo` extracted in Phase 4. Phase 5 should fold the inline pattern into a call to `ensure_owner_for_repo` so there is one canonical owner-registration path.

T3Database.get_or_create_collection default is unconditional strict; legacy registry helpers gone; fallback paths synthesise conformant names; t3_collection_name auto-promotes user input. CI green on Python 3.12 + 3.13.

title: RDR-103 Phase 4: migration on first index (legacy-to-conformant rename in _catalog_hook_repo)
description:
RDR-103 Phase 4. RDR file: `docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md` § Phase 4 + § Migration path.

# Scope

In `_catalog_hook` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:243`) — NOT `_catalog_hook_repo` as the RDR shorthand text implies. Wire the legacy-to-conformant rename:

1. Compute conformant target via `cat.collection_for(content_type, repo_owner, current_model)`. **`current_model` is the indexer's CURRENT canonical model for the content-type prefix** — NOT parsed from the legacy collection name. (Pinned decision #1.)

2. Look up the legacy name via the existing repo registry helpers (`registry._collection_name`, `_docs_collection_name`, `_rdr_collection_name`). NOTE: Phase 3a removes USES of these helpers from runtime write paths; this Phase 4 keeps them as a one-shot migration utility imported only from `_catalog_hook`. Phase 5 removes the DEFINITIONS as the final step. The helpers MUST survive through Phase 4 — do not drop them in Phase 3a.

3. Decision tree:
   - Legacy in T3, conformant absent → invoke `Catalog.rename_collection(legacy, conformant)`. Print one-line operator message: `Upgraded legacy collection X to Y.`
   - Conformant present, legacy absent → steady state. No message. Index proceeds against conformant.
   - Both present → conformant created by prior partial run. Skip rename, index against conformant; legacy left for operator cleanup via existing tools.

The migration is one-shot per repo per content-type. Legacy-absent in T3 is the sufficient idempotency signal; on subsequent indexes, step 3.case-2 fires with no message.

# Tests (TDD)

`tests/test_collection_name_migration.py` (new):
- Greenfield-with-legacy: rename happens once, message emitted once.
- Re-index after migration: no rename, no message (idempotency lock).
- Partial state both-exist: skip rename, index against conformant, legacy untouched.
- Verify the rename uses `Catalog.rename_collection` (not `update_documents_collection_batch`) — must be 1:1 atomic, not 1:N retarget.

`tests/test_repo_identity_stability.py` (new or extension):
- Two `_repo_identity` calls against the same path return the same hash.
- `--git-common-dir` resolution: worktree resolves to main repo's hash.

# Acceptance

- `pytest tests/test_collection_name_migration.py tests/test_repo_identity_stability.py -q` green.
- Operator running `nx index repo` against a legacy-collection catalog sees the upgrade message exactly once per repo per content-type.
- Subsequent runs show no message.

# Reminders

- Sequential thinking for the partial-state recovery path. The "both exist" case is the real-world failure mode (interrupted prior run); it must not double-rename.
- TDD: lock the idempotency assertion BEFORE wiring `_catalog_hook`.
- `code-review-expert` via `/nx:review-code` before complete.
- `/nx:test-validate` after review.

# Pinned decisions referenced

#1 — migration uses indexer's CURRENT canonical model.

# Dependencies

Depends on Phase 1 (`CollectionName`), Phase 2 (`Catalog.collection_for`), AND Phase 3a (`nexus-yqnr.3`). Both Phase 3a and Phase 4 modify `src/nexus/indexer.py`; running them in parallel guarantees merge conflicts and Phase 4's migration logic only makes sense after Phase 3a's rewrite has landed.

title: RDR-103 Phase 3b: plugin-layer indexers (rdr_hook.py + rdr-close skill knowledge_postmortem collapse)
description:

title: RDR-103 Phase 3a: indexer family rewrite (registry + indexer + doc_indexer + pipeline_stages + commands/index)
description:

**Supersedes nexus-qpet.4** (jointly with nexus-yqnr.4) — that bead's scope (rewrite indexer family for conformant names) is fully absorbed by Phase 3a + 3b. title: [epic] RDR-103: Catalog as Collection-Name Authority
description:
Tracking epic for RDR-103 (`docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md`), accepted 2026-05-03.

RDR-103 consolidates collection-naming authority in the catalog: the collection name becomes a formal tuple `(content_type, owner_id, embedding_model, model_version)` rendered to `<content_type>__<owner_id>__<embedding_model>__v<n>`. The indexer asks the catalog for a collection rather than constructing one and asking the catalog to record it. Strict-naming collapses from a 30-site flag-threading exercise to a property of a single helper.

# Pinned decisions (do NOT re-litigate)

These were settled during the RDR gate (2026-05-03). Implementer beads must reference these and refrain from re-opening:

1. Migration uses indexer's CURRENT canonical model, NOT the model parsed from the legacy collection name. Sidesteps unknown legacy models (e.g. pre-canonical-set `voyage-3`).
2. Model-name change is not a version bump. New tuple naturally lands in `v1`. Operator runs `nx catalog supersede-collection` for the old collection.
3. `knowledge__rdr_postmortem__{repo}` collapses into the conformant `knowledge__<owner_id>__<model>__v1` shape; `rdr_postmortem` semantic encoded at the document level via `category`.
4. `CollectionName.parse` raises on legacy/unknown shapes. Generic callers gate with `is_conformant_collection_name` first.

# Vocabulary: "supersedes jointly with"

Two child beads (`nexus-yqnr.3` and `nexus-yqnr.4`) jointly absorb the scope of the deferred `nexus-qpet.4`. Neither absorber alone is sufficient — both must close before the predecessor can close. The pattern reads as: "X is superseded jointly by Y AND Z; close X only after BOTH Y and Z close." This vocabulary is novel to this epic; future readers should interpret it strictly (joint, not disjunctive). The single non-joint absorption is `nexus-yqnr.7` superseding `nexus-2r71` (one-to-one).

# Existing primitives the implementation must reuse (not rebuild)

- `Catalog.rename_collection` (atomic T3-then-catalog rename, `tests/test_catalog_rename_collection.py` 14 cases).
- `Catalog.update_documents_collection_batch` (single-flock per-doc re-point).
- `collections.superseded_by` column.
- `_owner_segment_for_tumbler` at `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:606` (to be promoted to a public helper in Phase 2).
- `Catalog.owner_for_repo` at `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:1093`.
- `is_conformant_collection_name` / `parse_conformant_collection_name` at `src/nexus/corpus.py:54,75`.

# Bead absorption

Two existing beads in `nexus-qpet` get absorbed into this epic's phase work and should be closed-as-superseded once the absorbing work is done:
- `nexus-qpet.4` (indexer rewrite) is absorbed JOINTLY into Phase 3 (`nexus-yqnr.3` + `nexus-yqnr.4`). Close only after BOTH absorbers complete.
- `nexus-2r71` (strict-flip + flag drop) is absorbed into Phase 5 (`nexus-yqnr.7`). One-to-one supersedure.

# Closure criterion

All phase beads closed AND `nx catalog doctor --collections-drift` exits 0 cleanly on a fresh greenfield index AND `nexus-qpet.4` + `nexus-2r71` closed-as-superseded.

# Branch

`feature/rdr-101-remediation` (PR #491). Phase 1+2 may proceed in this branch; Phases 3-6 should likely be a fresh branch off whatever lands first.

title: RDR-101 Phase 5 follow-up: no-catalog prune path zero-matches new chunks
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review of Phase 5 (2026-05-03).

Three prune call sites in src/nexus/doc_indexer.py (lines 663, 805, 1274) call _identity_where(path, corpus) without content_hash. That falls through to {'source_path': file_path} when no catalog doc_id is found. Phase 5c removed source_path from new chunk metadata, so this where= filter matches zero chunks for any chunk indexed after Phase 5c.

Stale chunks from a re-index of a truncated file are silently NOT pruned in the no-catalog code path. Distinct from the staleness-skip path which correctly uses content_hash (commit 80071934).

Impact: users running nx index without a catalog (local-mode, air-gapped, first-run before catalog setup) accumulate stale chunks from prior versions of re-indexed files indefinitely. Chunk count bloat, outdated search results.

Resolution: add a prune_by_chunk_id mode that accepts a set of current chunk IDs and deletes the complement using col.delete(ids=stale_ids), bypassing the where= entirely. The current_ids_set is already in scope at the prune call sites.

Priority P2 (real bug, but limited to no-catalog code path).

title: RDR-101 follow-up: GC alive-set forward-proof for UUID7 doc_ids
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review of Phase 6 (2026-05-03, substantive critic CRITICAL-1).

Today GC's alive-set is built from CatalogEntry.tumbler (e.g. '1.1.1') and matched against T3 chunk metadata.doc_id. Verified: indexer._doc_id_resolver returns str(tumbler) so chunks today carry tumblers as doc_id. Intersection works.

Forward concern: if a future Phase ships UUID7 doc_ids in T3 chunk metadata (per RDR-101's eventual native-write design), alive_str would still contain tumblers and chunks would carry UUID7s. Empty intersection means GC sweeps every alive doc's chunks after the orphan window. Silent mass-deletion with a 30-day delay.

Tests in test_t3_gc.py all seed doc_id as tumbler ('1.1.1'); they share the assumption and would not catch the regression.

Mitigation paths:
1. Add a CatalogDB.doc_ids_for_collection(coll) that returns BOTH tumbler and any UUID7 doc_id column when the schema has one; GC's alive_str unions them.
2. Add a schema-version sentinel in collections projection; GC asserts schema version matches what its alive-set query knows.
3. Add a UUID7-shaped test that fails today and locks down the contract.

Priority P2 (forward-proofing only; no current bug).

title: t3-backfill-doc-id (and adjacent maintenance verbs) hang indefinitely on Chroma cloud connection close — missing per-request timeout
description:
## Why

`nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id` hung indefinitely on collection 9/46 (`code__ART-8c2e74c0`, 63077 chunks, 91% complete) during a real recovery run on 2026-05-03.

Forensic state at hang:

- Process state: `S+` (sleeping in foreground), 0.0% CPU sustained for 10+ minutes
- Two TCP sockets to ChromaDB Cloud (`ec2-52-86-129-243.compute-1.amazonaws.com:https`):
  - One ESTABLISHED
  - One in **CLOSE_WAIT** — Chroma server-side closed the connection but the Python client never received/processed the close
- No catalog lock held
- Process gracefully terminated on SIGTERM; SIGKILL not needed

`CLOSE_WAIT` on the client side with no read activity is the textbook signature of a request waiting for response data on a socket the server has already terminated, with no client-side timeout configured to break the wait.

## Reproducer

Not deterministically reproducible from the same starting state — a retry against `code__ART-8c2e74c0` immediately after the kill completed successfully in 36 seconds. The original run had been processing in 5-second-throttled progress bursts (~30 batches/burst, 1800 chunks/sec) before stalling at batch 191/210. Suggests a transient Chroma cloud-side issue (rate limit close, load balancer reset, network hiccup) that the client cannot recover from absent a timeout.

## Root cause hypothesis

Per `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:4225+` the t3-backfill loop calls `col.get(ids=batch_ids, include=["metadatas"])` and `col.update(...)` without a per-request timeout. The ChromaDB HTTP client (`chromadb` package) does not impose a default request-level timeout for these operations. When the server-side connection drops mid-request, Python's underlying `httpx` / `requests` socket read blocks forever.

The verb has retry/bisect logic (per nexus-o6aa.9.18 + .19) for **failed** batch operations, but a request that hangs without raising never enters the retry path. Failure-to-recover gap.

## Acceptance

- All ChromaDB operations in the t3-backfill verb (and adjacent maintenance verbs that walk many collections — `prune-deprecated-keys`, `synthesize-log --chunks`, `repair-orphan-chunks`, `verify`) carry a per-request timeout (suggest 60s default, configurable).
- On timeout the existing retry/bisect path runs (counts the timeout as a batch failure).
- Add a regression test: monkey-patch `col.get` to sleep indefinitely; assert the verb completes within timeout * retries seconds rather than hanging.
- Doc note in CHANGELOG: long-running maintenance verbs now bound by per-request timeout.

## Workaround (current)

External timeout on the verb invocation:

```bash
timeout 600 nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id --collection <name>
```

Or run with `--collection` per-collection (the verb idempotently resumes), giving the operator a hang-checkpoint.

## Scope

Probably touches 1–3 files: a thin wrapper around `t3._client.get_collection(...).get/update/...` calls, or per-call timeout kwargs.  Not architectural; small fix with high operator value.

## References

- Recovery session 2026-05-03 — observed hang during 138K → 53K orphan recovery on production catalog.
- `nexus-o6aa.9.18` — per-chunk retry path

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
FIX shipped on integration/rdr-102-phase4 + develop, 2026-05-03.

Approach: best-practice override rather than per-call wrapping. Verified upstream that chromadb has no documented timeout knob — `Settings.chroma_query_request_timeout_seconds` exists but never reaches the httpx.Client; the Cookbook docs and the source both treat the hardcoded `timeout=None` as the only path. Wrapping every `col.get/col.update` call site externally would have been ~30 LOC of churn across catalog.py + synthesizer.py with no upstream-fix transition path.

Patch: `src/nexus/db/t3.py` adds `_apply_chroma_http_timeout(client)` called once at the end of `T3Database.__init__`. Defaults: `httpx.Timeout(connect=10, read=120, write=60, pool=10)`. Defensive on shape — only touches clients that expose `_server._session` (CloudClient + HttpClient via FastAPI backend); PersistentClient/EphemeralClient skipped.

After the override, a stalled chroma read raises `httpx.ReadTimeout`, which `_is_retryable_chroma_error` already classifies as retryable (it's a `httpx.TransportError`). The existing `_chroma_with_retry` helper consumes that via the standard retryable path — no changes to retry.py or to the maintenance verbs needed.

Tests in tests/test_chroma_retry.py::TestChromadbTimeoutPatch:
- test_cloud_client_timeout_is_finite — asserts override fires, timeout != httpx.Timeout(None)
- test_local_persistent_client_unaffected — defensive hasattr path doesn't break local mode
- test_slow_chroma_op_now_raises_readtimeout — end-to-end retry guard (3 ReadTimeouts → "ok" via retry)

Removable once chromadb exposes a real `Settings.chroma_http_request_timeout_seconds` field — track upstream chroma-core/chroma. Comment + constants flagged in the t3.py patch.

Drive-by repairs (out of jgjw scope but unblock phase4-to-main): 3 tests in test_t3.py asserted source_path round-trips through upsert/update calls; RDR-102 Phase B drops it from ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL, so the assertions are inverted to `source_path not in written`.

Acceptance status:
- ✓ Per-request timeout in place (CloudClient/HttpClient).
- ✓ Existing retry/bisect path runs on timeout (httpx.ReadTimeout is retryable).
- ✓ Regression test exists (slow-op simulation).
- (Pending release) CHANGELOG note for "long-running maintenance verbs now bound by per-request timeout."

title: Delete RDR-101 transitional catalog verbs after Phase 5b ships
description:
## Why

Five `nx catalog` subverbs exist to fix the RDR-101 schema-vs-write divergence: `migrate`, `synthesize-log`, `t3-backfill-doc-id`, `prune-deprecated-keys`, `repair-orphan-chunks`. They are one-time transitional tooling — operators run them once to bring legacy state up to current schema, then never again.

The bead `nexus-x783` (Rotoroot) calls this out as part of CLI surface bloat. After RDR-101 Phase 5 ships (Phase 5a opt-in flag → Phase 5b default-on flip → Phase 5c final schema removal), these verbs have no work left to do.

This bead is the cleanup pass: delete the verbs, the underlying code paths, the tests, and the doc references. Pure subtraction.

## Scope

- Delete `@catalog.command(...)` definitions for the 5 verbs in `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py`.
- Delete supporting helpers that have no other callers: `_PRUNE_DEPRECATED_KEYS`, `_synthesize_collection_chunks` (if exclusive to synthesize-log), `_backfill_doc_id_for_collection`, `_repair_orphan_chunks`, etc. Trace each helper's callgraph; keep anything still in use by indexer / catalog hooks.
- Delete tests: `test_catalog_prune_deprecated_keys.py`, `test_catalog_synthesize_log.py`, `test_catalog_t3_backfill.py`, `test_catalog_t3_backfill_partial_failure.py`, `test_catalog_repair_orphan_chunks.py`, `test_catalog_migrate.py`, plus any test files the verbs depend on.
- Delete migration docs: `docs/migration/rdr-101.md` reference can stay (historical) but `docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-orphan-recovery.md` and adjacent how-tos can compress into a single "RDR-101 transition (closed)" entry.
- Delete the doctor's "Run nx catalog migrate ..." remediation hint paths.
- Update `docs/cli-reference.md` and `nx catalog --help` text.

## Acceptance

- `nx catalog --help` no longer lists the 5 verbs.
- The catalog subverb count drops from 40 to ≤35 (this bead alone).
- `grep -r "_PRUNE_DEPRECATED_KEYS\|synthesize_log\|t3_backfill_doc_id\|repair_orphan_chunks" src/ tests/` returns 0 hits.
- All other tests still pass; no regressions in indexer / doctor / catalog read paths.
- Greenfield smoke (`tests/test_indexer_e2e.py::test_greenfield_index_writes_no_deprecated_keys` + `release-sandbox.sh shakedown` step 5) still passes — the regression guards remain even though the verbs they reference are gone (the guards check chunk metadata directly, not via the verb).

## Blockers

This bead **cannot start** until:

- `nexus-o6aa.12` (Phase 5b — flip `[catalog].event_sourced` default to true) is merged.
- One release after Phase 5b ships (gives operators a window to migrate before the verbs disappear).

## Out of scope

- Reorganizing top-level CLI groups (Rotoroot territory — `nexus-x783` / RDR-103).
- Collapsing other catalog subverbs (cousin synonyms, diagnostic fragmentation — separate bead).
- Identity unification (Rotoroot territory).

## References

- Bead `nexus-x783` — Rotoroot, the architectural superset.
- Bead `nexus-o6aa.12` — Phase 5b, the prerequisite.
- RDR-101 — Event-sourced catalog migration (the work these verbs supported).

Develop tip has the test deletions but the verbs are still in catalog.py. Rolling forward in feature/nexus-o6aa-14-phase6-release-gate which carries the missing changes locally.
