title: Skip taxonomy__centroids in chunk_text_hash backfill
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

Problem: `nx collection backfill-hash --all` and `nx catalog backfill` walk every collection and call `coll.get(include=['documents', 'metadatas'])` on each chunk. The `taxonomy__centroids` collection stores embeddings + label metadata only — no document text — so every centroid row triggers a warning emit (`backfill_chunk_text_hash_none_doc`). With 187 centroids per project this floods stderr with no actionable signal.

Fix: filter `taxonomy__centroids` out of the backfill collection enumeration in `src/nexus/commands/collection.py:600` and the analogous catalog backfill site at `commands/catalog.py:2730`. Centroids are derivative — they have no source document to hash and aren't link-target candidates either, so backfilling them yields nothing useful.

Acceptance:
- `nx collection backfill-hash --all` against a tenant with taxonomy populated emits zero `backfill_chunk_text_hash_none_doc` warnings.
- Existing per-collection `nx collection backfill-hash taxonomy__centroids` (explicit name) still works as before — only the `--all` and catalog-driven paths skip.

title: Synthesizer title-prefix file_path resolution — recover ~85K code-chunk orphans without re-embedding
description:
RDR-102 Phase D + post-close investigation surfaced that ~138K orphans
remain in production T3 after synthesize-log. Distribution by collection:

- code__claude-code-7dbc4de3: 30,483 (22%)
- code__Luciferase-f2d57dbc: 28,066 (20%)
- knowledge__knowledge: 11,908 (9%)
- docs__default: 9,479 (7%)
- code__Kramer-2c1f322c: 6,876 (5%)
- code__nexus-571b8edd: 5,123 (4%)
- code__arcaneum-2ad2825c: 4,964 (4%)
- (... long tail across 119 collections, ~138K total)

Root cause: prune-deprecated-keys (PR #480, pre-RDR-102) stripped
source_path from chunks. Phase A pre-flight register hadn't shipped
yet so doc_id was never written. Result: chunks have neither identity
field. Title fallback fails because chunk title is '<relpath>:<line-
range>' (e.g. 'mcp-server/src/index.ts:1-24') while catalog Document
title is just the filename (e.g. 'index.ts').

Fix: extend _synthesize_collection_chunks to add a title-prefix
resolution path — split chunk title on ':', take the prefix as a
candidate relative file_path, look it up in a NEW file_path_to_doc_id
reverse map built from DocumentRegisteredPayload.file_path entries.

Concretely, current synthesizer priority order:
  0. chunk's own meta['doc_id'] (Phase A propagation)
  1. source_uri match (chunks with source_path)
  2. title exact match (CHROMA_IDENTITY_FIELD pattern)
  3. live_doc_lookup content_hash match (--prefer-live-catalog)
  4. orphan

NEW priority 2.5 (between title-exact and content-hash-recovery):
  - if chunk title contains ':', take prefix before ':' as relpath
  - look up relpath in file_path_to_doc_id reverse map
  - if found → use that doc_id, not orphan

Expected impact: ~85K of 138K orphans recovered (the code__ majority).
Some docs__ collections may also benefit if they use the same title
format. Knowledge / standalone PDF orphans not affected (different
title format).

Acceptance criteria:
- New synthesize_t3_chunks unit test asserts a chunk with title
  '<relpath>:<line-range>' resolves to the matching catalog Document
  via file_path
- Existing synthesizer tests still pass (priority chain unchanged for
  non-title-prefix chunks)
- Optional measurement: run synthesize-log against live production
  catalog post-fix, confirm orphan count drops from 138,563 to ~50K

Refs: RDR-102 (closed) post-close investigation, RDR-101 epic Phase
4 follow-up enhancements (alongside nexus-o6aa.9.17/.18/.19)
close_reason: Shipped on feature/synthesizer-title-prefix-orphan-recovery (commit 36cbb1b7). Production-validated: combined with manual bulk-registration of 5,026 per-file Documents for orphan repos, recovered 85,290 chunks (61.55% of the 138,563 baseline) without re-embedding. Doctor coverage went from 138,563 → 53,273 orphans (43.75% → 16.82% global ratio). 3 unit tests in TestTitlePrefixFilePathRecovery pass; 39 tests in adjacent regression sweep pass. Branch ready for PR.

title: RDR-102 Phase D: write-then-verify gate + orphan-recovery smoke (closes nexus-o6aa.10)
description:
RDR-102 Phase D — final validation bead. Depends on Phase A impl (nexus-uusi), Phase A3 (nexus-4uv5), and Phase B impl (nexus-ejs4). NOT a hard dependency on Phase C, but D5 step 4 (orphan ratio drops measurably) is cleanly observable only with Phase C's orphan_ratio JSON field — see CORRECTION below. NO new code — runs the structural gate per RDR D4 and the orphan-recovery smoke per D5.

## CORRECTION (post-plan-audit 2026-05-02)

Phase D step-4 acceptance ("orphan ratio drops measurably") is cleanly observable in JSON only after Phase C lands (which adds t3_doc_id_coverage.orphan_ratio). Before Phase C: operator reads the manual chunk count vs events.jsonl orphan-event count to compute the ratio by hand. After Phase C: jq '.t3_doc_id_coverage.per_coll["knowledge__delos"].orphan_ratio' returns the value directly.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATION: validation can technically run with C still in flight, but the smoke is materially easier to verify when C has landed. Recommended ordering: do not run Phase D smoke until BOTH (a) Phase A+B impl have merged AND (b) Phase C impl has merged. If schedule pressure forces D before C, the validator computes orphan ratio manually from events.jsonl + col.count.

## Phase D gate (write-then-verify, on a fresh collection)

Per RDR D5 + R5 critique: the first draft's gate ("post-sweep dry-run prune returns zero") was satisfiable trivially (prune everything first, run dry-run, get zero, declare done — exactly the failure shape that produced the original tautological PASS). The actual gate is **index a fresh file through each fixed path, then verify the resulting chunks carry no source_path AND populate doc_id**.

```bash
# Set up: fresh collections so we measure writers, not pre-prune residue
TS=$(date +%s)

# Write through each fixed path
nx index pdf <test-paper.pdf>     --collection knowledge__rdr102-gate-$TS
nx index md  <test-md-file.md>    --corpus rdr102-gate-$TS
nx index rdr <test-rdr.md>        # standalone path (uses batch_index_markdowns)
nx index repo <test-repo>         # exercises code_indexer + prose_indexer + pipeline_stages

# Verify no writer leaked source_path
for COLL in knowledge__rdr102-gate-$TS docs__rdr102-gate-$TS code__rdr102-gate-$TS rdr__rdr102-gate-$TS; do
  nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys --dry-run --collection "$COLL"
  # Required: 'chunks_updated: 0' for source_path on every collection
done

# Verify doc_id is populated on the same fresh writes
nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage  # all four collections at 100% (no orphans by construction)
```

## D5 orphan-recovery smoke

Run the three-command procedure on one previously-orphan collection (e.g., knowledge__delos):

```bash
# Backup catalog before destructive recovery
cp -a .catalog .catalog.pre-rdr102-d5

# Capture baseline (use Phase-C JSON if available; manual count if not)
nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage --json | jq '.t3_doc_id_coverage.per_coll["knowledge__delos"].orphan_ratio'

# Run recovery
nx catalog synthesize-log --prefer-live-catalog --collection knowledge__delos
nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id --collection knowledge__delos

# Capture after-state
nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage --json | jq '.t3_doc_id_coverage.per_coll["knowledge__delos"].orphan_ratio'

# Assert: orphan ratio dropped measurably (knowledge__delos has known orphan content)
```

## Test suite gates

1. uv run pytest — full unit suite green
2. uv run pytest -m integration — integration suite green
3. Write-then-verify gate (above)
4. Orphan-recovery smoke (above)

## Acceptance — closes nexus-o6aa.10 for real

After 1-4 pass:
- Update bead nexus-o6aa.10 status to closed
- Note in close reason: "RDR-102 Phase 4 closeout complete; Phase 5a (nexus-o6aa.11) unblocked by Phase B+D"
- File completion summary in nx memory: mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__memory_put(content="...", project="nexus", title="rdr-102-completion-state.md")

## Out of scope (Phase 5)

- Phase 5a opt-in flag [catalog].event_sourced (nexus-o6aa.11)
- Phase 5b legacy-surface drops (e.g., source_path readers in stale-detection fallback shape)
- Reindexing the 309,681 orphan chunks beyond this smoke test (operators run the documented procedure post-merge per D5)

## Context

- Recovery doc: docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-orphan-recovery.md (shipped by nexus-4uv5)
- Audit: docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-audit-2026-05-02.md

## Reminders

- DO NOT close nexus-o6aa.10 unless ALL four gates pass — the original RDR-101 Phase 4 close was tautological precisely because the gate was satisfied on a slice
- The write-then-verify smoke CANNOT be skipped — it is the structural PASS gate that proves writer correctness

title: RDR-102 Phase B impl: drop source_path from schema + 6 writer call sites
description:
RDR-102 Phase B — implementation bead. Depends on test bead nexus-dqwf, which depends on Phase A impl (nexus-uusi). Hard-remove source_path from the chunk-write path.

## CORRECTION (post-plan-audit 2026-05-02)

base_meta dict at src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:851 carries a now-dead source_path key — Phase B drops it opportunistically as part of this bead (it is not a write-side site that hits make_chunk_metadata; it is a defensive base dict that no longer needs source_path once the schema removes it). Verify at edit time: if removing the key from base_meta changes any test outcome, that test should be updated as part of this bead.

## Files (per RDR-102 RF-4 verified inventory — DO NOT INVENT FILES)

- src/nexus/metadata_schema.py
  - Remove "source_path" from ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL (line ~52 — currently 32 keys; drops to 31, restores Chroma 32-key cap headroom per RF-5)
  - REMOVE source_path PARAMETER from make_chunk_metadata() signature (line ~285) — HARD DELETE per D2, NOT deprecated kwarg per A3 rejection
  - Update MAX_SAFE_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS comment if it referenced source_path

- src/nexus/code_indexer.py:402 — drop source_path=str(file_path) from make_chunk_metadata call
- src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:103 — drop source_path=str(file_path) (branch A)
- src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:183 — drop source_path=str(file_path) (branch B)
- src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:145 — drop source_path=pdf_path (PDF-in-repo writer; was MISSING from original draft per critic-corrected inventory)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:794 — drop source_path=str(pdf_path) (_pdf_chunks)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:874 — drop source_path=sp (_markdown_chunks)
- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:851 — drop dead source_path from base_meta dict (audit-found opportunistic cleanup)

## D2 hard-remove rationale (Alternative A3 rejection)

The first RDR draft proposed keeping source_path as a deprecated no-op kwarg "for back-compat with external consumers." description:

- _markdown_chunks is around src/nexus/doc_indexer.py (function entry; line 874 is Phase B's source_path drop site within it)

This bead modifies the FUNCTION ENTRY POINTS to accept a new doc_id kwarg; the chunk-write line within each function (the make_chunk_metadata call) gains a doc_id=doc_id argument. Phase B (nexus-ejs4) drops the source_path argument from those same call sites.

## Files (per RDR-102 RF-4 verified inventory)

- src/nexus/doc_indexer.py
  - NEW helper: _register_or_lookup_doc_id() (tumbler-based)
  - _pdf_chunks() entry point (~line 714) accepts new doc_id kwarg → passes to make_chunk_metadata at line 794
  - _markdown_chunks() entry point accepts new doc_id kwarg → passes to make_chunk_metadata at line 874
  - _index_document() registers Document upfront, threads doc_id to _markdown_chunks
  - index_pdf() registers Document upfront, threads doc_id to _pdf_chunks
  - _lookup_existing_doc_id() becomes the read-only path used by post-hook chain

- src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py

  - _catalog_pdf_hook becomes idempotent for already-registered case
  - Chunk-write site at line 145 gains doc_id=doc_id passthrough (Phase B drops source_path from same call)

## Decision (D1) restatement

Mirror src/nexus/indexer.py:run:
1. Open catalog (graceful no-op when absent — preserve no-catalog ingest contract)
2. Resolve owner for corpus
3. Look up Document by (owner, file_path); if found use its tumbler; if not register fresh
4. Pass resolved doc_id to chunkers via new kwarg
5. Chunkers pass to make_chunk_metadata(..., doc_id=doc_id)

The post-store fire_post_document_hooks chain stays in place — it triggers aspect-extraction enqueue, not chunk metadata.

## Idempotency invariant (R1)

Catalog.register() (catalog.py:1218-1234) returns existing tumbler without writing event when by_file_path(owner, file_path) finds an existing row. Re-running nx index pdf foo.pdf produces zero new events.jsonl lines once foo.pdf is registered. Test bead nexus-5iid asserts this via test_preflight_registration_idempotent_on_staleness_skip.

## Edge case

A first-time index then skipped by staleness check (rare: identical content_hash already present from different source path) emits DocumentRegistered with no companion ChunkIndexed events. This is valid — Document is canonically tracked. Doctor must NOT flag this as drift; replay equality unaffected.

title: Phase 4: doc_indexer paths (nx index pdf/md/rdr standalone) don't write doc_id, regress source_path
description:
Empirical audit 2026-05-02 confirmed three doc_indexer paths fail to wire doc_id at chunk-write time:

1. nx index pdf → doc_indexer.index_pdf
2. nx index md → doc_indexer.index_markdown → _index_document
3. nx index rdr (standalone) → batch_index_markdowns → _index_document

The bug pattern is identical across all three:
- Chunk metadata is built via make_chunk_metadata() WITHOUT passing doc_id
- Catalog hook (_catalog_pdf_hook / _catalog_markdown_hook) fires AFTER the upsert
- Result: chunks land in T3 with no doc_id field

Existing chunks survive doc_id loss only because ChromaDB upsert MERGES metadata
(verified: upsert with metadatas=[{a: 99}] on existing {a: 1, b: 2} yields
{a: 99, b: 2}). New chunks (or chunks indexed for the first time on these paths)
have no doc_id at all.

Additional regression on the same paths: source_path is rewritten on every
reindex because make_chunk_metadata always writes it (ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL still
includes source_path). The prune verb removes it; the next reindex puts it back.

Reproducer (PDF):
1. nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys
2. nx index pdf <any-paper.pdf> --collection knowledge__delos
3. col.get(...): source_path is back, doc_id is missing

Reproducer (markdown):
1. nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys
2. nx index md <some-md-file.md> --corpus <corpus> --force
3. col.get(...): source_path is back, doc_id is missing
   (verified empirically with /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus/README.md indexed
    at 2026-05-02T16:47:17 — has source_path, no doc_id)

Why nx index repo works:
- indexer.py:run calls _catalog_hook() UPFRONT
- Builds file_to_doc_id: dict[Path, str]
- Passes as doc_id_resolver to code_indexer / prose_indexer / _index_pdf_file
- These pass doc_id to make_chunk_metadata at chunk-write time

Fix scope:

- Pass doc_id to _pdf_chunks() and _markdown_chunks()
- _pdf_chunks (line ~787) and _markdown_chunks (line ~872) accept doc_id parameter

See docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-audit-2026-05-02.md for full audit table.

title: Phase 4 sub-task: nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys verb
description:
The verb that mechanically clears the deferred-class population identified by the .9.18/.9.19 backfill rerun. Each over-cap chunk on Hal's catalog has 35–36 metadata keys; dropping the six legacy keys (`source_path`, `title`, `git_branch`, `git_commit_hash`, `git_project_name`, `git_remote_url`) brings them to 29–30 keys, leaving room for `doc_id`.

Behaviour:
- `nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys` walks every collection in T3 and rewrites every chunk's metadata to drop the deprecated keys.
- Idempotent: chunks that already lack the keys are no-ops.
- Same `--dry-run`/`--json`/`--resume` flags as `t3-backfill-doc-id` (consistent operator surface).
- Bisect-on-failure path mirrors `.9.19` for symmetry against Cloud T3 quotas.

GATING: must NOT run before .10.2 audit completes AND every reader from the audit migrates to doc_id lookups. Pre-gate, the verb's own machinery exists but the CLI entry point is hidden behind a `--i-have-completed-the-reader-migration` flag (or a feature gate keyed off a new `[catalog].readers_migrated_to_doc_id = true` config). Operator-runs once after .10's reader work lands.

Acceptance:
- Verb implemented + unit-tested (synthetic chunks with the six keys → empty post-prune).
- Test against a sandbox catalog containing the over-cap shape: prune drops the chunks to ≤30 keys, follow-up `t3-backfill-doc-id` lands cleanly.
- Documented in `docs/migration/rdr-101.md` as the post-migration cleanup step.
- Operator-facing safety message printed when run pre-reader-migration.

Out of scope:
- Removing the keys from `ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL` in `metadata_schema.py` — that's `.13` (Phase 5c, irreversible schema removal).
- Plugin-marketplace soak before the prune (telemetry path dropped per epic-level decision).

Estimated work: a few hundred lines in `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py` + tests; bulk of complexity is the gating + the bisect symmetry.
close_reason: Closed by PR #480. nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys verb shipped: drops 5 keys (source_path + 4 git_*), preserves title (audit Category C). Two pre-flight gates: --i-have-completed-the-reader-migration and t3-doc-id-coverage = 100%. ChromaDB merge-vs-replace handled via {key: None} deletion patches. 9 tests pass; 991 wider tests pass. Documented in docs/migration/rdr-101.md. Live operator workflow remains: dry-run + per-collection prune + t3-backfill-doc-id --resume to drain the deferred class on Hal's catalog.

title: fix(t3): import path creates taxonomy__* collections with wrong distance metric (L2 instead of cosine)
description:
Surfaced during nexus-o6aa.9.16 CI investigation (2026-05-01).

**The bug:** `nx store import file.nxexp` for a `taxonomy__*` collection routes through `T3Database.upsert_chunks_with_embeddings` → `T3Database.get_or_create_collection`, which injects an embedding_function and defaults to L2 distance. Production taxonomy code (`catalog_taxonomy._create_centroid_collection`) correctly uses `hnsw:space=cosine` + `embedding_function=None`. After import, the collection exists with WRONG distance metric — cosine similarity queries return out-of-range values (e.g. -2.6 with cosine bounds [-1, 1]).

**How surfaced:** my `.9.16` test in `tests/test_exporter.py::test_round_trip_preserves_taxonomy_metadata` initially seeded `taxonomy__centroids` via `T3Database.get_or_create_collection`. ChromaDB's process-wide collection state then polluted `tests/test_projection_quality.py` similarity assertions when both files ran in the same process. Documented warning in `src/nexus/db/t2/catalog_taxonomy.py:1607`: "Do NOT use t3.get_or_create_collection() — it injects the wrong EF + L2."

**Fixed in test (.9.16):** seed via `ephemeral_db._client.get_or_create_collection(...)` directly with `hnsw:space=cosine`. CI green.

**Not fixed in production:** the `nx store import` path still routes through `T3Database.get_or_create_collection`. Real-world `.nxexp` round-trip for taxonomy collections silently creates an L2 collection — metadata round-trips correctly (per .9.16 fix) but distance metric is wrong, breaking any subsequent `assign_single`/`assign_batch` query against the imported centroids.

**Two ways to fix:**

1. **Extend `_bypass_canonical_schema` to also override collection-creation params.** When `_BYPASS_SCHEMA_PREFIXES` matches, `upsert_chunks_with_embeddings` calls `self._client.get_or_create_collection(name, embedding_function=None, metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})` directly instead of `self.get_or_create_collection(name)`. Cleanest if all taxonomy collections want the same shape.

2. **Per-collection-type creation policy.** A registry mapping collection prefix → `(embedding_function, metadata)` consulted at creation time. More general, supports future special collections that may want different shapes (L2 + custom EF, etc.).

Recommend Option 1 for this fix; Option 2 if more programmatic-vector collections appear and start needing divergent creation params.

**Test contract:** seed a taxonomy__centroids collection with cosine metric, export, import via `nx store import` (production path), query the imported collection, assert similarity ∈ [-1, 1]. End-to-end faithful round-trip.

**Out of scope:**
- Renaming or deprecating `T3Database.get_or_create_collection` for cloud-mode callers (broader refactor; the production warning is enough until then).
- Any other "vector-only" collection that may need different creation params (e.g. RDR-070 future centroid collections).

**Real-world urgency:** medium. Any operator who exports + restores a taxonomy collection today would silently lose taxonomy queries against that collection. Current production catalogs do not yet exercise this path (no one has imported a taxonomy backup), but the .nxexp format claims to be a faithful portable backup — and isn't, for taxonomy collections, until this lands.

**Follows from:** `nexus-o6aa.9.16` (taxonomy keys stripped on import — fixed; this is the deeper layer underneath).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #468. T3Database.get_or_create_collection now branches on _bypass_canonical_schema and creates taxonomy__* collections with embedding_function=None + metadata={'hnsw:space': 'cosine'} regardless of local_mode. Test test_round_trip_preserves_taxonomy_distance_metric regression-locks the fix; pre-fix it fails with restored.metadata=None. Production warning at catalog_taxonomy._create_centroid_collection updated. 238 related tests pass.

title: perf(catalog): t3-backfill batch-bisect on quota failure (O(log N) vs O(N) per failed batch)
description:
Real-data finding from Hal's live migration rerun (2026-05-01): the .9.18 per-chunk retry path takes 30+ minutes of wall clock against Cloud T3 because each chunk in a failed batch triggers a separate API round-trip. 105 failed batches x 300 chunks = 31,500 individual col.update calls at ~50-100ms each = 26-52 minutes.

Most of that work is wasted: the over-cap chunks are concentrated. A halving strategy would isolate them in O(log N) calls per batch.

Algorithm:

  Batch of 300 -> split into [150, 150]
  Try [150]; if fails, split into [75, 75]; etc.
  Stop subdividing when len == 1 -- that is the genuinely-failing chunk.

Worst case (one over-cap chunk per batch): log2(300) = ~9 retries instead of 300. 30x speedup on the per-chunk retry phase.

Best case (over-cap chunks clustered): even fewer retries because halves can succeed wholesale.

Implementation sketch: replace the current per-chunk retry loop in t3_backfill_doc_id_cmd with a recursive bisect helper. Single-chunk failures classify the same way (deferred vs errors) as the .9.18 path. Add a max-recursion safety bound.

Test:
- Synthetic batch of 300 with 1 over-cap chunk in middle.
- Pre-fix per-chunk retry: 300 col.update calls.
- Post-fix bisect: ~9 col.update calls, 1 deferred record at the end.
- WITH TEETH: assert call count delta.

Out of scope:
- Tuning the recursion depth cap.
- Skipping the bisect for collections known to be all-clean.

Discovered live during Hal's .9.18 rerun (2026-05-01). The rerun was running for 30+ min on the per-chunk retry phase against ~9k over-cap chunks scattered across 105 batches.
acceptance_criteria: Batch failures recurse-and-halve before degrading to per-chunk. Test asserts ~log2(N) col.update calls in the worst case (one over-cap chunk per batch). Existing .9.18 tests still pass; deferred-class semantics preserved.
close_reason: Superseded by nexus-iftc (PR #497). The t3-backfill verb was deleted; batch-bisect optimization on quota failure is no longer relevant.

title: feat(catalog): nx catalog migrate progress output (synthesize-log + t3-backfill silent for minutes)
description:
Live migration on a 14k-document / 312k-chunk catalog produces no progress output for ~minutes between the orchestration echo lines. Real Hal-experience finding: started 'nx catalog migrate' against ~/.config/nexus/catalog and was left guessing whether the process was alive vs hung.

Sequence today:
1. migrate echoes '==> nx catalog synthesize-log --force --chunks'
2. synthesize-log walks owners/documents/links/chunks JSONL silently. EventLog.append_many writes the whole event batch in one go (~150 MB for the live catalog). No incremental output.
3. migrate echoes '==> nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id'
4. t3-backfill iterates collections, reads metadata in 300-id batches, calls col.update. No per-collection or per-batch progress.
5. migrate echoes '==> sync live SQLite to events.jsonl'
6. migrate echoes '==> nx catalog doctor ...'
7. doctor finally emits its table-by-table comparison output.

Between step 1 and step 7 there can be 5-10 minutes of silence on a moderate catalog and 30+ minutes on a large one. Operators have no signal that progress is happening.

Three places to add progress:

A. synthesize-log
   - Inside synthesize_from_jsonl (and the chunks variant): print 'synthesized N owners / M documents / K links / P chunks' every N records (configurable; default every 1000).
   - At the end: 'wrote E events to events.jsonl in T seconds'.

B. t3-backfill-doc-id
   - Per collection: '[c/C] processing <coll_name>: N chunks expected'.
   - Per batch: '[b/B] batch updated, K chunks updated, R remaining'. Or just dot-progress.
   - At the end: existing summary stays.

C. migrate orchestrator
   - Time each step; print elapsed.
   - Show estimated-remaining when sandbox baseline data is available.

Implementation notes:
- Use click.echo to stderr (or click.progressbar for a real bar).
- Suppress under --json mode (machine consumers don't want progress noise).
- Suppress in non-TTY contexts? Optional — could be worth it for clean log capture.
- Consider tqdm if it's already a dep; otherwise plain echo lines.

Test:
- Functional: existing migrate / synthesize-log / t3-backfill tests still pass.
- Smoke: run migrate against a multi-document fixture; confirm progress lines fire and end-of-stage summaries appear.

Out of scope:
- Real-time event-source rebuild progress (migrate's sync step is fast, doesn't need progress).
- Configurable verbosity beyond a basic --quiet flag if any.

This is a quality-of-life feature, not a correctness fix. Surfaced live during the operator's first real migration run.
acceptance_criteria: synthesize-log --force emits per-section progress (owners / docs / links / chunks every N records). t3-backfill-doc-id emits per-collection progress. migrate orchestrator echoes step timings. JSON mode suppresses progress. Existing tests still pass.
close_reason: Superseded by nexus-iftc (PR #497). The nx catalog migrate verb (silent for minutes during synthesize-log + t3-backfill stages) was deleted; progress visibility is no longer relevant.

title: fix(catalog): nx store import crashes on vector-only collections (taxonomy centroids, document=None)
description:
Surfaced by .9.10 sandbox e2e validation against Hal's real T3: nx store import on taxonomy__centroids fails with 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'encode'.

Root cause (debugger agent, 2026-05-01):
- src/nexus/db/t3.py:380-404 _write_batch called doc.encode() unconditionally.
- Vector-only collections (RDR-089 taxonomy centroids) round-trip document=None — they're embedding-only entries.
- All 2014 records in taxonomy__centroids have document=None; export side passes them through fine but import crashes.

Fix (two-layer defense):
1. src/nexus/exporter.py:339 — coerce record['document'] or '' at import site.
2. src/nexus/db/t3.py:380-410 — _doc_bytes() helper returns 0 for None; replace inline doc.encode() calls.

Regression test in tests/test_exporter.py::TestVectorOnlyImport (2 tests, all-None and mixed). All 51 exporter tests pass.

Confirmed: re-running the failing import on Hal's sandbox now succeeds — 'Imported 2014 records into taxonomy__centroids (0.5s)'.

Out-of-scope follow-up (separate bead worth filing): canonical metadata schema funnel (_normalize_for_write) strips taxonomy-specific keys (topic_id, label, doc_count) on import. Import roundtrips data shape but drops taxonomy enrichment. Consider whitelisting taxonomy keys for taxonomy__* collections in metadata_schema.py.
acceptance_criteria: nx store import succeeds on a .nxexp file with all-None document fields. Mixed (some None, some text) also imports cleanly. Existing exporter tests still pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(catalog): Catalog.update() coerce None metadata to {} (perpetuating null source)
description:
Catalog.update() at src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:1909 writes:

    json.dumps(rec_dict["meta"])

without the or {} coercion that Catalog.register() at line 1335 applies. When rec_dict['meta'] is None — which happens when Catalog.resolve() reads back a row whose metadata column already holds the literal string 'null' — json.dumps(None) produces 'null', perpetuating the null shape on every subsequent update().

Found while preparing Hal's catalog for RDR-101 migration: 11 rows of 8,163 (0.13%) carry metadata='null' in SQLite. They map 1:1 to "meta": null lines in documents.jsonl. The rows span 2026-04-08 → 2026-04-27 — intermittent.

Functional impact: zero (both shapes decode to no metadata). But:
1. doctor --replay-equality reports FAIL on these rows (synthesizer emits meta={} via the dataclass default_factory; projection writes '{}'; live SQLite has 'null').
2. The shape is self-perpetuating — every update() on a null-meta row writes null again.
3. Future synthesize-log + replay would normalize, but only as a side effect of migration, not as a fix to the underlying bug.

Fix: 1-line change at line 1909 from json.dumps(rec_dict['meta']) to json.dumps(rec_dict['meta'] or {}).

Test: register a doc, force metadata='null' via direct SQL (with epsilon-allow), call cat.update(...) on the doc, assert SQLite column is now '{}' not 'null'.
acceptance_criteria: 1-line fix in src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:1909. Regression test in tests/test_catalog.py asserts the round-trip heals null → {}. Existing tests still pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-101 Phase 3 follow-up E: extended e2e validation — scaled catalog + Chroma cloud + partial-failure + MCP
description:
Four marketplace-grade validation gaps not covered by .9.10's harness (small-scale, embedded-Chroma only). Required before declaring this safe for operators beyond Hal's machine.

## Gaps

1. **Scaled catalog soak.** Current harness uses 3 docs. Index 500–1000 docs in step 2; run migrate; measure synthesize-log + t3-backfill latency; verify replay-equality at scale. Validates the linear-scaling claim for _check_bootstrap_status and _event_log_covers_legacy. Probably reuses scripts/validate/lib.sh's seed corpus or hand-generates docs in a tight loop.

2. **Real Chroma Cloud T3 backfill.** Current harness uses NX_LOCAL=1 embedded persistent Chroma. Stand up a throwaway Chroma Cloud tenant (or tenant scoped to a test database), seed a hundred chunks, run nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id, measure latency, verify metadata round-trip via direct ChromaDB API. Validates the cloud-side write semantics not exercised by the embedded client.

3. **Partial-failure injection.** Wrap t3-backfill-doc-id with a fault injector that 5xx's intermittently (e.g. monkeypatch ChromaDB client.update to raise on every Nth call). Confirm idempotent re-run recovers; doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage --strict-not-in-t3 surfaces the in-progress orphans correctly until completion. Validates the recovery story documented in docs/migration/rdr-101.md but not exercised end-to-end.

4. **MCP integration smoke test.** Spin up the MCP server with NEXUS_CATALOG_PATH pointing at a fallback-active sandbox catalog. Invoke a catalog tool (e.g. mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__search). Confirm:
   - structlog warning fires (logged but not displayed to operator).
   - No spurious stderr noise (TTY gating suppresses the human prompt in non-TTY MCP context).
   - Tool invocation completes successfully.

## Out of scope

- Multi-host migration scenarios.
- Stress test (sustained mutation rate over multi-hour windows).
- Plugin marketplace simulation (no real third-party plugins exist yet).

## Deliverable

Either:
- Extend scripts/validate/rdr-101-migration-e2e.sh with new steps 10-13, or
- New harness scripts/validate/rdr-101-migration-e2e-scaled.sh (separate run because Chroma Cloud needs credentials and longer wall-clock).

title: Phase 3 PR ε: lint gate forbidding direct catalog writes outside projector module
description:
RDR-101 Phase 3 PR ε: Audit external `cat._db.execute()` callers; install a lint gate that prevents direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/REPLACE/CREATE/DROP/ALTER against catalog SQLite from any consumer outside the catalog module.

## Why now

Stage B (PRs #438–#445, beads nexus-fecd / nexus-t6p0 / nexus-6qy0 / nexus-n1uo / nexus-ds8e / nexus-y3um / nexus-ai9d) closed the live-write coverage gap end-to-end: every indexer write path (prose, code, PDF, CLI `nx store put`, MCP `store_put`) writes the catalog tumbler as `doc_id` at chunk-write time. With Stage B in place, the only remaining consumers that could perturb catalog SQLite outside the projector should be retired or fenced off.

PR ζ (flip `NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=1` default) depends on ε: until direct writes are forbidden, ζ would silently expose any unaudited direct-write caller and corrupt catalog state under event-sourced mode.

## Audit results (2026-05-01)

Prohibition scope per parent bead nexus-o6aa.9 + handoff brief: "no call site outside the projector module". The handoff brief clarifies (line 87): "anything in the catalog module is presumably allowed to mutate `_db` (it IS the projector). The prohibition applies to consumers OUTSIDE the catalog module" — i.e., the lint gate scope is `src/nexus/` minus `src/nexus/catalog/`.

Survey commands:
```bash
grep -rn "cat\._db\.execute\|self\._db\.execute\|catalog\._db\.execute" src/nexus/
grep -rn "_db\.execute" scripts/
grep -rn "cat\._db\.execute" tests/ | grep -iE "INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|REPLACE"
```

### Production code OUTSIDE `src/nexus/catalog/` — all SELECT (read), zero direct writes

| File:line | Pattern | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:488` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:1114` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/health.py:704,705` | `SELECT count(*) FROM ...` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/scoring.py:232,244` | `rows = catalog._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py:91,182,459` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:844, 1183, 1307, 1312, 1765, 1785, 2089, 2503` | `rows/row = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/commands/store.py:165` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/commands/enrich.py:426, 443` | `rows/row = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/commands/dt.py:155` | `row = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:1019` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |
| `scripts/migrate_art_papers.py:219` | `rows = cat._db.execute(...)` | SELECT — allowed |

**Result: zero direct writes outside `src/nexus/catalog/` in production. Picture is clean.**

### INSIDE `src/nexus/catalog/` (presumed allowed; out of ε scope)

- `projector.py` — 7 writes (the projector itself).
- `catalog.py` — many writes; spot-checked at line 2519 (DELETE FROM links), it sits inside `else:` of `if self._event_sourced_enabled:` — legacy path bypassed under ES mode.
- `dedupe.py:278, 283, 284` — direct DELETE FROM links/documents/owners. Not gated by ES check today. Worth flagging for follow-up (bead noted in OPEN QUESTIONS below) but out of ε scope per the brief's interpretation.

### Tests (case-by-case)

| File:line | Pattern | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_catalog.py:361` | `UPDATE documents SET alias_of = ?` | Intentional invariant-violation fixture (force alias cycle for the cycle-walker test). Allowlist with `# epsilon-allow:` comment + reason. |
| `tests/test_catalog.py:656` | `UPDATE links SET created_at = '2020-01-01...'` | Intentional time-travel fixture (force a stale span for `link_audit()`). Allowlist as above. |

Either allowlist these two with explicit comments, or expose a tiny test-only helper on Catalog (e.g. `_force_alias_for_test`, `_force_link_created_at_for_test`) and rewrite. Allowlist is the simpler choice.

### Scripts

- `scripts/migrate_art_papers.py:219` — SELECT only. No writes. No action.

## Deliverables

1. **Lint gate test** (`tests/test_no_direct_catalog_writes_outside_projector.py`):
   - AST-walk every `.py` file under `src/nexus/` and `scripts/`.
   - For each `_db.execute(...)` call (or any catalog `_db` mutation method), parse the first SQL keyword from the literal string argument.
   - Fail when keyword is INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / REPLACE / CREATE / DROP / ALTER and file is outside `src/nexus/catalog/`.
   - Pattern reference: `tests/test_hook_drift_guard.py` already AST-walks for fire-site invariants — use it as the template.
   - Also walk `tests/` with explicit allowlist for the two known fixture sites (file:line keyed).
   - WITH TEETH comment naming the regression: "guards RDR-101 Phase 3 irreversibility window — once ζ flips ES default ON, any direct write outside the projector silently desyncs SQLite from the event log; doctor's replay-equality signal then becomes meaningless."
   - Verify the test FAILS today by temporarily inserting a violating line and re-running.

2. **Test allowlist comments**: add `# epsilon-allow: <reason>` (matching the lint-gate's allowlist token) to `tests/test_catalog.py:361` and `:656`.

3. **Documentation**: short prohibition note in `src/nexus/catalog/AGENTS.md` (or create one) pointing at the lint gate. Note the legacy-path exception inside `catalog.py` and `dedupe.py` is in-module-only.

4. **Optional follow-up bead**: open a separate bead (not part of this PR) to thread `dedupe.py`'s 3 direct DELETEs through the projector under ES mode. They aren't currently gated; under ζ they would write SQLite without emitting events, breaking replay-equality on dedupe runs.

## Acceptance criteria (from parent nexus-o6aa.9)

- All existing tests pass with the new write path (no regression).
- Integration test (already exists from Stage B.6): event log replay produces same SQLite state.
- Lint gate test passes — and FAILS deterministically when a violating call is inserted into a non-catalog/ src file.
- Doctor passes (`nx catalog doctor --replay-equality --t3-doc-id-coverage --strict-not-in-t3`) on a non-trivial workload.

## Branch / merge

- Branch: `feature/<this-bead-id>-rdr-101-phase3-epsilon-no-direct-catalog-writes`
- PR per bead, squash-merge with `--delete-branch`.
- After merge, ζ (default flip) becomes unblocked.

## Open questions (carry to follow-up beads, not blocking ε)

1. `src/nexus/catalog/dedupe.py:278/283/284` direct DELETEs are not behind an `is_event_sourced()` gate. Under ζ this would silently desync. Decision: ship a follow-up bead to either gate them or rewrite via projector helpers. NOT part of ε.
2. RDR-089 aspect rows: if Phase 3+ projects `DocumentEnriched` v: 1 events into Aspect rows, the lint gate must not interfere. Coordinate timing with RDR-089.

## Reference

- Handoff brief: `/tmp/rdr-101-phase3-epsilon-zeta-continuation.md`
- Parent: nexus-o6aa.9 (Phase 3 sub-task umbrella)
- Predecessors (Stage B chain): nexus-fecd → nexus-t6p0 → nexus-6qy0 → nexus-n1uo → nexus-ds8e → nexus-y3um → nexus-ai9d
- Successor: ζ (NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED default flip — separate bead, depends on this one)

Lint gate test passes on current main. tests/test_catalog.py:361 and :656 carry epsilon-allow comments matching the gate's allowlist token. CONTRIBUTING or src/nexus/catalog/AGENTS.md documents the prohibition. Full test suite green (~6224 passed baseline). Doctor passes on non-trivial workload after merge.

title: Skip integration tests by default + pin bash to /bin/bash in subagent hook tests
description:
Two unrelated bugs surfaced while running the full pytest suite locally:

1. tests/integration/* hit real Voyage/Chroma APIs in retry loops, hanging pytest indefinitely (239+ CLOSE_WAIT TCP sockets). They're marked with pytestmark=pytest.mark.integration and the file docstring says 'Skipped by default. Run with: -m integration', but pyproject.toml does NOT have addopts='-m not integration' to deselect them. Result: pytest tests/ runs the integration suite without credentials, hangs forever.

2. tests/test_context.py::TestSubagentHookInjection::test_hook_emits_knowledge_map (and 2 siblings) call subprocess.run(['bash', subagent-start.sh], ...). PATH lookup on Hal's machine resolves to /opt/homebrew/bin/bash (5.3.9), which has a heredoc deadlock bug: the forked child writes the heredoc body to a pipe before exec-ing cat, so when the body exceeds the pipe buffer (~500 bytes), write() blocks with no reader. Tests time out at 10s. /bin/bash (3.2.57, system) doesn't have the bug.

Note: bug 2 ALSO affects production Claude Code subagent dispatches — orphan subagent-start.sh processes accumulate in user's ps from real agent runs that hit the same deadlock. The deeper fix (split the NXTOOLS heredoc, or pin hook launcher to /bin/bash) is out of scope for this bead.

Fix:
- pyproject.toml: add addopts='-m not integration' so pytest tests/ honors the documented default
- tests/test_context.py: pin to /bin/bash in the four subprocess.run([...]) calls
notes:
PR #440 opened. https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/pull/440

Resolution:
1. pyproject.toml: addopts='-m not integration and not slow' — pytest tests/ now skips network-bound integration tests by default (honours docstring intent).
2. tests/test_context.py: pinned to /bin/bash to dodge homebrew bash 5.3.9 heredoc deadlock.
3. nx/hooks/scripts/subagent-start.sh: split NXTOOLS (1786->279+362), CATALOG (1192->337+311), OPERATORS (634->248). Total: 3612->1537 bytes (57% reduction). All chunks now under 500-byte bash 5.3 deadlock threshold; hook runs in 1.3s (was: indefinite deadlock).

Production impact: orphan subagent-start.sh processes in ps from real Claude Code agent dispatches will stop accumulating. Subagent context budget recovers ~2KB.

Full pytest: 6224 passed / 33 skipped / 61 deselected in 9:45 (was: hang at 27-34% indefinitely).
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 3 PR β: extend NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED to update/delete/set_alias/link/unlink/rename_collection
description:
RDR-101 Phase 3 sub-PR β. Extends the event-sourced gate from PR α (register_owner + register) to all remaining catalog mutators: update, delete_document, set_alias, link, unlink/bulk_unlink, rename_collection. Pattern matches PR α: when gate ON, emit event to events.jsonl FIRST, project to SQLite via Projector.apply, then append to legacy JSONL for back-compat. When OFF, legacy direct-write path unchanged.

Test gate: with NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=1, a sequence of all catalog mutations produces a SQLite state byte-equal to the same sequence under the legacy path (modulo timestamps). Replay of events.jsonl through a fresh CatalogDB matches the live state.

title: Phase 3 PR α: Catalog.register routes through event log when NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED=1
description:
RDR-101 Phase 3 sub-PR α. Adds NEXUS_EVENT_SOURCED gate (default OFF) that, when on, routes Catalog.register() through a new internal path: emit DocumentRegistered event to events.jsonl FIRST, then apply via the projector to write SQLite, then append to legacy documents.jsonl for back-compat (Phase 5 deprecates legacy JSONL).

When OFF: existing behavior unchanged (Catalog.register writes SQLite + JSONL directly + shadow-emits).

Test gate: with flag ON, a sequence of register() calls produces a SQLite state byte-equal to the same sequence under the legacy path. Replay of events.jsonl through a fresh CatalogDB also matches.

Subsequent PRs (β/γ/δ/ε) extend the gate to update / delete_document / link / unlink / set_alias and migrate external callers off direct cat._db.execute mutations. The IRREVERSIBILITY WINDOW does NOT start until the gate flips on by default — that's later in Phase 3.

title: Phase 2 PR ε: nx catalog repair-orphan-chunks verb
description:
RDR-101 Phase 2 sub-PR ε. Operator-facing fixup for orphan chunks the synthesizer (PR β) could not resolve to a document. Provides --list to enumerate orphans (chunk_id, coll_id, chash) and --assign chunk_id:doc_id (repeatable) to append a corrective ChunkIndexed event with the resolved doc_id, which the projector applies idempotently and which the doctor coverage check (PR δ) then sees as resolved.

Verb: nx catalog repair-orphan-chunks [--list | --assign CHUNK_ID:DOC_ID ...] [--collection X] [--json]

Behavior:
- --list (default): walk events.jsonl, print orphan ChunkIndexed events.
- --assign CHUNK_ID:DOC_ID: repeatable. Each pair appends a corrective ChunkIndexed event marked synthesized_orphan=False with the assigned doc_id. The original orphan event stays in the log; replay applies last-event-wins.
- --collection X: scope listing/assignment to one collection.
- --json: structured payload.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2 PR δ: nx catalog doctor --t3-doc-id-coverage flag
description: RDR-101 Phase 2 sub-PR δ. Adds a --t3-doc-id-coverage flag to nx catalog doctor that walks every T3 collection and reports per-collection coverage of the doc_id metadata key. PASS = every non-orphan chunk in every collection carries a doc_id matching what the event log claims. The verb is read-only (no T3 writes); operators run it after t3-backfill-doc-id to confirm Phase 2 is complete on a host.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2 PR γ: nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id verb
description:
RDR-101 Phase 2 sub-PR γ. Reads events.jsonl ChunkIndexed events (synthesized by PR β) and propagates the resolved doc_id into the corresponding T3 chunk metadata via ChromaDB.update(ids=[chunk_id], metadatas=[{..existing, doc_id: X}]). Idempotent — re-running on chunks already carrying the right doc_id is a no-op. Orphan chunks (synthesized_orphan=True) are skipped, surfaced in the report.

Verb: nx catalog t3-backfill-doc-id [--dry-run] [--collection X] [--json]
- Default: walk every collection in the event log, update T3 chunks per ChunkIndexed event, report counts.
- --dry-run: walk + report without calling ChromaDB.update.
- --collection X: scope to one collection (operator can run per-collection during a long backfill).
- --json: structured payload {dry_run, collections_processed, chunks_updated, chunks_skipped, orphans_skipped, errors}.

title: Phase 2 PR β: synthesize ChunkIndexed events from T3 (extends synthesize-log --chunks)
description:
RDR-101 Phase 2 sub-PR β. Extends nx catalog synthesize-log with a --chunks flag that walks T3 collections via ChromaDB and emits one ChunkIndexed event per chunk with doc_id resolved from source_path → catalog source_uri → tumbler → doc_id (the mapping the document phase just minted).

title: Phase 2 PR α: nx catalog synthesize-log verb (persist event log from existing JSONL)

Adds an operator verb that reads owners.jsonl + documents.jsonl + links.jsonl, runs synthesize_from_jsonl, mints UUID7 doc_ids per RDR-101 §Migration / Phase 1, and writes the events to events.jsonl on disk. title: Phase 1 PR F: shadow-write path (gated, opt-in)
description:
RDR-101 Phase 1 sub-PR F. Adds shadow-emit of v: 0 events alongside the existing JSONL+SQLite writes in Catalog. Gated behind NEXUS_EVENT_LOG_SHADOW env var (default OFF). When OFF, no events emitted, no behavior change. When ON, every Catalog mutation appends a typed event to events.jsonl in addition to the existing writes; the events.jsonl can then be replayed through the Phase 1 projector to reproduce the SQLite state (round-trip).

Choices made (gated approach per user direction 2026-05-01):
- Default OFF: NEXUS_EVENT_LOG_SHADOW=0 (or unset). Opt-in via env var.
- Shadow emit uses v: 0 schema so the existing Phase 1 projector handlers apply unchanged (Phase 3 introduces v: 1 native-write semantics).
- doc_id field on emitted events stands in as the tumbler for Phase 1 (same as the synthesizer); Phase 2 backfill mints a fresh UUID7.
- Events appended to events.jsonl using the same dir-flock the existing _append_jsonl call sites already hold — no second lock acquisition, no deadlock.

Write sites covered (each gets one self._emit_shadow_event call after the existing JSONL+SQLite writes):
- register_owner → OwnerRegistered
- register → DocumentRegistered
- update → DocumentRenamed (when source_uri changed) or DocumentEnriched (when meta/bib changed)
- delete_document → DocumentDeleted
- set_alias → DocumentAliased
- link → LinkCreated
- delete_link → LinkDeleted

Tests:
- Gate OFF: no events.jsonl content after register/update/delete (default behavior).
- Gate ON: each write site emits the corresponding typed event with the right payload.
- Round-trip: with gate ON, drive a sequence of catalog mutations, then replay events.jsonl through the projector against a fresh CatalogDB → byte-equal to the live db.
- Env-var parsing: 1/true/yes/on → on; 0/false/no/off/unset/empty → off.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 1 PR D: Frecency projection schema + Document bib columns
description:

Choices made (simpler path per user direction 2026-05-01):

Schemas:

No domain store methods yet — Phase 5 fills them in when frecency relocates from T3 metadata. Phase 1 only ships the empty schema.

title: Phase 1 PR B: events → SQLite projector + JSONL synthesizer + replay-equality test
description:
RDR-101 Phase 1 sub-PR B. Implements the projector that maps events to the existing catalog SQLite schema (owners, documents, links — pre-Phase-5 columns), plus the JSONL → v:0 events synthesizer that lets us drive the projector from an existing catalog state for replay-equality testing.

Scope:
- src/nexus/catalog/projector.py (NEW): Projector class. apply(event) dispatches on (type, v) and writes the existing-schema SQLite rows. Idempotent (INSERT OR REPLACE for documents, INSERT OR IGNORE for links). Sub-cases for v:0 (tombstones, aliases, empty source_uri title fallback) per RF-101-2.
- src/nexus/catalog/synthesizer.py (NEW): synthesize_from_jsonl(catalog_dir) -> Iterator[Event]. Reads owners.jsonl, documents.jsonl, links.jsonl in order; emits v:0 events that preserve enough of each row to round-trip through the projector to a byte-equal SQLite state.

No production write path changes. doc_id values from the events are not yet written to SQLite (Phase 1 targets the existing schema; doc_id columns land in Phase 3+).

title: Phase 6 sub-task: nx t3 gc verb (sole ChunkOrphaned emitter)
description:
RDR-101 Phase 6 deliverable surfaced by plan audit 2026-04-30. RF-101-3 (T2 nexus_rdr/101-research-3) designates 'nx t3 gc' as the sole emitter of ChunkOrphaned events; no other code path may delete T3 chunks directly post-Phase-3. Without this verb implemented, the orphan-window GC (default 30 days) has no mechanism and the catalog-side DocumentDeleted tombstone never translates to physical chunk removal in T3.

Source files:
- src/nexus/commands/t3.py (NEW: gc subcommand under existing nx t3 group)
- src/nexus/db/t3.py (extend T3Database.delete_by_source -> delete_by_chunk_ids)
- src/nexus/catalog/events.py (Phase 1) — ChunkOrphaned event schema reference
- src/nexus/catalog/event_log.py (Phase 1) — emitter for ChunkOrphaned

Spec (from RDR-101 §Read paths / 'Re-index unchanged file' + RF-101-3):
1. Reads catalog projection: which doc_id values are alive in collection X
2. Reads T3: per chunk, get (chunk_id, doc_id, indexed_at)
3. Diffs: chunk_id values whose doc_id is no longer alive AND indexed_at predates the orphan window (default 30 days)
4. Per orphan chunk: emit ChunkOrphaned(chunk_id, reason) event THEN call delete_by_chunk_ids(collection, [chunk_id]). STRICT ORDER: event before delete, so a crash mid-GC leaves the log consistent with T3 (event present + delete failed = next gc retries)
5. Always offers --dry-run first; --yes to skip confirm

Acceptance criteria:
- nx t3 gc --collection X --orphan-window 30d --dry-run prints orphan candidates with no T3 mutation
- Without --dry-run, GC emits one ChunkOrphaned event per chunk before delete; verified via doctor replay-equality
- Operators cannot delete T3 chunks any other way (Phase 6 enforcement)
- Default window 30 days documented; configurable per invocation

RDR reference: RDR-101 §Resolved Open Questions / RF-101-3 / 'GC keys on chunk_id, not chash'.
T2 RF reference: nexus_rdr/101-research-3 (DocumentDeleted = scheduled GC keyed by chunk_id, ChunkOrphaned only emitted by gc verb).
Cited code: src/nexus/db/t3.py:989-1002 (existing delete_by_source as the per-source primitive to extend).
close_reason: Shipped on feature/rdr-101-phase-6-t3-gc commit 1db804f4. T3Database additions: list_chunks_with_metadata + delete_by_chunk_ids. CLI: nx t3 gc with --orphan-window (default 30d) and --dry-run/--no-dry-run + --yes. Strict event-before-delete order per RF-101-3. 12 unit tests; 213 related tests pass.

title: Phase 6: Enforcement (doctor as release gate, collection invariants, fallback migration)
description:
RDR-101 Phase 6: nx catalog doctor becomes the canonical drift check (cron / pre-commit / release-gated). Collection naming validation enforced at create time. Default fallback collections migrated, not deleted.

Source files:
- src/nexus/commands/catalog.py (nx catalog doctor: report drift as release blocker; nx catalog rename-collection; nx catalog migrate-fallback --dry-run)
- src/nexus/catalog/catalog_db.py (Collection.legacy_grandfathered column + write-time validation)
- src/nexus/db/t3.py (collection naming validation at CollectionCreated time)
- ci/ or .github/workflows/ (wire nx catalog doctor into release shakedown)

Tasks:
- nx catalog doctor: drift is a release blocker; integrate into release shakedown (cron, pre-commit, or release pipeline)
- Collection naming validation: reject non-conforming names AT CREATE TIME ONLY. Enforce <content_type>__<owner_id>__<embedding_model>@<model_version>
- Existing legacy collections (code__ART-8c2e74c0, docs__nexus-571b8edd, knowledge__knowledge, docs__default, etc.): grandfathered with Collection.legacy_grandfathered = TRUE (resolves substantive critique S1)
- Opt-in rename: nx catalog rename-collection <old> <new> emits CollectionSuperseded event + triggers background Chroma re-create + re-embed job
- Failing-loud at READ time on legacy names is REJECTED as operationally hostile
- Schema-encoded invariants (one owner per collection, one content_type, one embedding_model) enforced at write time on NEW collections only
- Fallback collection migration: nx catalog migrate-fallback --dry-run walks each fallback collection's documents, proposes target collection per document. Operator reviews + applies. Per-document DocumentRenamed (same owner) or DocumentDeleted + DocumentRegistered (cross-owner) events execute the migration. Fallback collections deprecated only after they go to zero rows; never silently nuked.

Test gate (acceptance criteria):
- Doctor exits non-zero on drift; release pipeline blocks
- New collection with non-conforming name at create time is rejected
- Existing legacy collection continues to read/write without error (grandfathered)
- nx catalog rename-collection produces CollectionSuperseded event + background re-embed completes
- nx catalog migrate-fallback --dry-run on docs__default and knowledge__knowledge produces a valid migration proposal; apply produces correct events

RDR reference: RDR-101 §Implementation Plan / Phase 6 + §Migration / Phase 6 (resolves substantive critique S1 + the fallback-collection silent-nuke risk).
close_reason: Done. PR #497 merged to develop. Phase 6 release-pipeline gate is now wired: nx catalog doctor --collections-drift runs WITHOUT || true at shakedown step 11/11, preceded by backfill-collections --no-dry-run so the gate validates the full create-register-check sequence. Greenfield shakedown 11/11 [done] confirmed. Backfill / drift-check asymmetry on taxonomy__* collections also fixed (backfill now applies the same _BYPASS_SCHEMA_PREFIXES filter as the drift check).

title: Phase 0: chunk_id generation rule (UUID7 vs deterministic digest)
description:
RDR-101 Phase 0 deliverable: pin the chunk_id generation rule before Phase 1 lands.

Background: RDR-101 makes chunk_id the Chroma natural ID (PK), distinct from chash (which is now non-unique-indexed for span resolution). We need to decide HOW chunk_id is generated. Two candidates with concrete tradeoffs:

A. UUID7 fresh at ChunkIndexed time. Opaque, sortable by time, decoupled from content. Parallel with doc_id design (RF-101-1, T2 nexus_rdr/101-research-1). Simplest projector logic.

B. Deterministic digest of (doc_id, position) — e.g. sha256(doc_id || position)[:16]. Reproducible across re-runs, encodes structure, lets disaster recovery rebuild chunk_id without storing it. Brittle if position numbering ever shifts.

Source files (CORRECTED via plan audit 2026-04-30):
- src/nexus/db/t3.py (chunk write paths: indexer.py:987-1000, t3.py:135-143, t3.py:427-439 — anywhere ChromaDB.add() / upsert() ids= argument is constructed)
- src/nexus/indexer.py (catalog hook calls into T3 with the ids it generated)
- src/nexus/db/t2/chash_index.py (chash_index references the chunk_id; backfill paths must produce values consistent with the new rule)
- NOT src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py — chunk_id is T3-side, not catalog-side

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision documented in RDR-101 §Read paths / 'Index a file' step 4 (currently says 'UUID7 or deterministic digest; Phase 0 picks one')
- New module src/nexus/catalog/events.py (Phase 1) gains a chunk_id factory that emits the chosen scheme
- Test that chunk_id is unique within a (doc_id, coll_id) pair AND survives re-index unchanged when doc + content unchanged
- If B: defensive cite of position-numbering invariant — what code paths today might re-number?

title: bib enrichment poisons metadata via citation-DOI on preprints without their own DOI
description:
v4.21.0 shakeout (2026-04-30): nx enrich bib --source openalex on knowledge__rag-papers (CacheRAG paper, an arXiv preprint with no published DOI) extracted DOI 10.1145/3742872 from a citation in the references section, looked it up via OpenAlex, and stamped the wrong paper's metadata across all 174 chunks (wrong authors: 'Karam S. Chatha, Rolf Ernst, Anand Raghunathan, Ravishankar Iyer' from an embedded-systems paper W2912099628; wrong year 2025; wrong venue; wrong citation count).

Root cause: the DOI/arXiv-aware lookup (PR #394/#395/#396) scans all chunks of a document for identifiers. The labeled-preference rule (prefer 'DOI: 10.x/y' over bare '10.x/y') only operates WITHIN a chunk, not across the document. When a paper has no DOI in its own front matter but has citations with DOIs (which is the entire reference list of any academic paper), the citation DOI wins.

Reproducibility:
  uv run python -c "from nexus.bib_extractor import extract_doi; from nexus.db import make_t3; ..."
  Or: nx enrich bib knowledge__rag-papers --source openalex --delay 0.5 --limit 1 (idempotent guard skips already-enriched, but on a fresh collection this reproduces).

Mitigation options (in order of preference):
1. Title validation post-lookup — compare OpenAlex returned title against source_title; reject if similarity < threshold. Safest, smallest blast radius.
2. Restrict DOI extraction to early chunks (e.g., first 3 pages) — front-matter DOIs are the paper's; deep-body DOIs are citations. Heuristic but cheap.
3. Skip DOI extraction in chunks with section_type='references' (per RDR-055). Requires section_type to be populated.
4. Require labeled DOI document-wide (skip bare DOIs entirely if no labeled DOI is found anywhere). Strictest; will under-enrich legitimate papers whose authors used bare 'doi:' formatting.

Acceptance: a regression test fixture with a paper that has citations but no own DOI passes through bib enrichment without being stamped with a citation-DOI's metadata. The fixture should be a real-world preprint shape (CacheRAG would be the canonical example).
acceptance_criteria: A bib enrichment run on a preprint that has DOI citations in its references section (canonical fixture: a CacheRAG-shaped paper) does NOT stamp the citation's paper metadata. Either (a) leaves bib_* fields empty, (b) falls back to fuzzy title search of the source's own title, or (c) rejects a low-similarity title-match and logs a structured warning.
notes: Surfaced in v4.21.0 live shakeout. The 174 contaminated chunks in knowledge__rag-papers need to be cleaned (col.update with empty bib_* values) before any retrieval or re-enrichment is attempted. Filed as P2 not P1 because the contamination is bounded (one collection, one document) and the failure mode is observable when title-vs-bib_authors are inspected — but it WILL silently corrupt larger enrichment runs over preprint corpora.
close_reason: Shipped in v4.21.1 (commit 11358c9c, tag v4.21.1, PR #402)

title: OperatorError handling in plan runner: graceful fallback instead of unhandled error
description: RDR-100 research (T2: nexus_rdr/100-research-1) found that 2 of 73 recent nx_answer_runs surface unhandled OperatorError ('missing required argument') from plan steps. Today the error propagates up to the caller, who sees a stack trace instead of a useful result. The fix is small: catch OperatorError at the per-step boundary in src/nexus/plans/runner.py, log it with structured context (step_idx, operator name, plan_id), and either (a) skip the step and continue with whatever the previous steps produced, or (b) abort the plan and return a structured error envelope to the caller. Decision (a) vs (b) depends on whether the step is on the critical path — if step N depends on step N-1's output, skipping step N's failure is wrong. Likely shape: add a 'step_failure_strategy' on the plan ('skip' default for retrieval-only plans, 'abort' for operator chains) and surface the failure in the run telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: A plan step that raises OperatorError no longer propagates an unhandled exception to nx_answer's caller. Instead: (1) the failure is logged to nx_answer_runs with the step index and operator name, (2) the caller receives a structured envelope indicating which step failed and what (if anything) was produced before the failure, and (3) at least one new test in tests/test_plan_runner.py exercises the path (operator step raises OperatorError mid-plan).
notes: Surfaced from RDR-100 empirical research 2026-04-30. The 2 observed failures had message 'missing required argument', suggesting either a plan schema bug or a runtime arg-passing bug. Investigate the actual messages from the two failing runs (nx_answer_runs telemetry) before settling on the fix shape — the 'missing required argument' phrasing might point at the inputs-translation code in runner.py:768 (nexus-yis0).
close_reason: Closed

description:
aspect_extractor populates document_aspects in T2 with structured fields (problem_formulation, proposed_method, experimental_datasets, experimental_baselines, experimental_results, extras, confidence). The only way to read them today is raw SQL against ~/.config/nexus/memory.db.

title: nx dt index: route PDFs to knowledge__ by default, not docs__
description:
nx dt index --uuid <X> currently dispatches PDFs through index_pdf with the default corpus 'default', which lands them in docs__default. Three problems with this default:

1. Paper-shaped PDFs from DEVONthink belong in knowledge__<X> collections, where scholarly-paper-v1 aspect extraction can run. After nexus-z70w (PR #393) docs__ collections deliberately don't route to any aspect extractor at all, so paper PDFs ingested via the default path get stranded with no aspect data.

2. docs__default is a generic catchall already mixed with random PDF drops, repo docs, and arXiv-shaped paper drops. New paper PDFs add to the soup rather than landing in a curated home.

3. Operators have to remember --collection knowledge__<X> on every nx dt index call to get aspect-eligible placement. Easy to forget; we just hit this with the CacheRAG paper today (had to migrate manually post-ingest, mirroring nexus-olg5).

Live evidence (CacheRAG paper, 2026-04-30):
- nx dt index --uuid B24CA96B-... -> docs__default
- Aspect extraction refused (post-#393): docs__ has no extractor
- Migrated manually to knowledge__rag-papers via inline Python (174 chunks, metadata-only chunk move + cat.update)
- Then aspects + topics worked. Bib partial (OpenAlex coverage gap, not a routing issue).

Design options:

A. Auto-detect by extension at dispatch time:
   - PDFs (paper-shaped) -> knowledge__dt-papers (or knowledge__<corpus>-papers when --corpus is set)
   - Markdown / notes -> docs__dt-notes (or docs__<corpus>)

B. Explicit defaults:
   - --collection becomes required (no default) — operator must pick
   - OR default to knowledge__dt-papers for ALL nx dt index PDFs

C. Add --as-paper / --as-note shorthand:
   - --as-paper -> knowledge__<corpus>-papers
   - --as-note -> docs__<corpus>
   - --collection X always wins

Lean: option A. The dispatcher already picks index_pdf vs index_markdown by extension; extending to also pick the COLLECTION by extension is a small change with the right semantics. Operators who want a different home pass --collection.

Out of scope:
- Auto-aspect-extract on ingest (post-store hook fires only for collections with registered extractors anyway; the routing fix is sufficient)
- Migrating existing docs__default paper PDFs (separate cleanup; nx catalog audit-membership could find them by source_uri shape)

Test recipe:
- nx dt index --uuid PAPER -> knowledge__dt-papers (PDF default)
- nx dt index --uuid NOTE -> docs__dt-notes (markdown default)
- nx dt index --uuid X --collection custom__y -> custom__y (override wins)
- nx dt index --uuid X --corpus myproject -> knowledge__myproject-papers (PDF) or docs__myproject (markdown)
notes: Surfaced 2026-04-30 right after the CacheRAG dt-index test. Migration done manually via inline Python; would be unnecessary if the default routing put paper PDFs in knowledge__ from the start.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #397. nx dt index --uuid X without --collection now routes PDFs to knowledge__<corpus>-papers and markdown to docs__<corpus>. Default --corpus is 'dt'. 90 dt-related tests pass; live verified the help reflects new defaults.

title: Guardrail: docs__ collections should not auto-route to scholarly-paper-v1
description:
The aspect_extractor _REGISTRY currently maps:
- knowledge__* -> scholarly-paper-v1 (Claude Haiku, paper-shaped output)
- rdr__* -> rdr-frontmatter-v1 (deterministic markdown frontmatter parser)
- docs__* -> scholarly-paper-v1 (PROBLEMATIC)

The docs__ registration assumes the collection contains research papers, but in practice docs__<repo> collections are populated by 'nx index repo' which sweeps any prose file in the repo: markdown documentation, code-comment exports, .dict text dictionaries, .jsonl test fixtures, etc. None of these are paper-shaped content.

Live evidence (ART, 2026-04-30):
- 287 aspect rows extracted on docs__ART-8c2e74c0 against repo CLAUDE.md, README.md, BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md, cmudict.dict, jsonl test fixtures.
- 286 of 287 'populated' with problem_formulation/proposed_method/datasets/baselines/results - hallucinated structure for non-paper content.
- 1 in cost (363 docs * .01 Haiku per the original docs__ART enrichment) wasted on hallucinated extractions.

Since the actual papers in any repo go through 'nx index pdf' into knowledge__<repo>-papers (post-nexus-olg5 split convention), docs__ should never need scholarly-paper-v1.

Two-layer fix:
1. Drop docs__ from _REGISTRY. nx enrich aspects docs__<X> would short-circuit at select_config returning None, same as code__ today.
2. Post-store hook gate: when a doc lands in docs__, skip the aspect extraction chain even if a hook fires (defense in depth — registry change is the primary fix).

Migration impact:
- Existing docs__ aspect rows are noise; users SHOULD clear them. Document the cleanup query in CHANGELOG.
- No tooling change for users who legitimately want paper-shaped extraction on a docs__ collection (rare; can use --collection knowledge__<X> at index time).

Out of scope:
- Building a separate 'doc-summary-v1' extractor for non-paper prose. That's a different feature; aspects are paper-shaped by design.

Test recipe:
- nx enrich aspects docs__<test_coll> should print 'No extractor config registered' (same shape as code__<X> today)
- aspect_extractor.select_config('docs__myproj') should return None
- Existing knowledge__/rdr__ flows unaffected
notes: Surfaced 2026-04-30 during ART corpus audit. nx enrich aspects ran on docs__ART (mixed PDF + repo docs) before the nexus-olg5 split and produced 287 hallucinated aspect rows on non-paper content. Cleared via direct DELETE; this bead prevents reaccumulation.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #393. docs__ removed from aspect_extractor _REGISTRY; nx enrich aspects docs__<X> now refuses with redirect note. 189 tests pass.

title: DOI/arXiv-aware bib enrichment: extract identifier from PDF text before title fallback
description:
Current nx enrich bib resolves papers via title-search against OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar. Title is read from chunk metadata (set at index time or rewritten via derive_title from filename). Both sources are unreliable:

- Filename slugs are short/ambiguous: 'mfaz.pdf' matched a 1996 Developmental Brain Research paper at OpenAlex; 'Aging Bloom Filter...' matched a Nature Reviews Drug Discovery paper. The mechanism worked but the identity was wrong.
- PDF metadata Title field is often empty, the LaTeX template default, or 'Microsoft Word - X.docx'. Not reliable.
- Docling-extracted page-1 heading often grabs section labels like 'Concise Papers' rather than the actual title.

Better signals, in order of reliability:
1. DOI in PDF body text. Regex: 10\.\d{4,9}/[^\s]+ . OpenAlex direct lookup: GET /works/doi:10.x/y. Unambiguous.
2. arXiv ID in filename (2503.07641.pdf) or first chunk text. Direct lookup: /works/arxiv:2503.07641 .
3. Title-search fallback (current behavior).

Implementation:
1. New helper nexus/bib_extractor.py with extract_doi(text) and extract_arxiv_id(text).
2. nx enrich bib reads first chunk per source_path, scans for DOI / arXiv ID before falling through to title search.
3. bib_enricher_openalex.enrich_by_doi(doi) and enrich_by_arxiv_id(arxiv_id) helpers.
4. Tests covering happy path, multiple DOIs (use first), no-DOI, DOI-not-in-OpenAlex, and the title-search fallback.

Surfaced 2026-04-30 right after running enrich on knowledge__delos via OpenAlex. 15/15 papers got matches but at least 2-3 were demonstrably wrong via fuzzy title matching. The mechanism (catalog hook propagation post-nexus-tv22) worked; the identity resolution is the bottleneck.

Definition of done:
- nx enrich bib uses DOI/arXiv-first lookup when available
- Wrong-paper matches drop to <5% on collections with academic PDFs
- Existing collections can be re-enriched cleanly: clear bib_* fields, re-run, get correct matches
- Tests cover the regex extractors AND the OpenAlex by-DOI/by-arxiv lookups

Out of scope:
- Re-extracting titles from PDF first-page font analysis (more reliable than current page-1 heading but heavier; punt unless DOI/arXiv route insufficient)
notes: The chunks have document text already in T3 — no re-extraction needed for DOI scanning. First chunk (chunk_index=0) usually contains the abstract + DOI.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #394. nx enrich bib (OpenAlex backend) tries DOI then arXiv ID before fuzzy title search. Direct ID lookups via /works/doi: and /works/arxiv: endpoints. 141 tests pass.

title: catalog enrich hook falls back to first row when title doesn't match (causes 75x duplicate update)
description:
_catalog_enrich_hook in src/nexus/commands/enrich.py matches by (physical_collection, title) exact-match. When the title doesn't match (chunk titles got rewritten via derive_title to paper-shaped names while catalog row titles retained file_path-shaped placeholders like 'docs/papers/X.pdf:page-1'), it falls back to LIMIT 1 with no other filter:

    row = cat._db.execute(
        'SELECT tumbler FROM documents WHERE physical_collection = ? LIMIT 1',
        (collection_name,),
    ).fetchone()

This picks the same first row for every title, causing all 75 enrich calls to clobber the same single catalog entry rather than each finding their own.

Surfaced 2026-04-30 during nexus-olg5 (ART papers split): bib enrichment correctly tagged 9,518 chunks with bib_openalex_id but only 1 of 78 catalog rows propagated.

Fix: the fallback should match by source_path (which is unique and doesn't drift across title-rewrites) instead of by collection-only. The chunk metadata always carries source_path; the bib_meta dict could be extended to include source_path so the hook can look it up.

Workaround: use a side script to propagate from chunks (by source_path -> catalog row) post-enrich. Used today on knowledge__art-papers.

Test recipe:
- Two catalog rows in same physical_collection, different file_paths
- Enrich chunk with title-X (matches no catalog title)
- Confirm: hook does NOT clobber an unrelated catalog row
notes: Surfaced during nexus-olg5 ART migration. The propagation workaround (chunk source_path -> catalog cat.update) is fine for one-off but the underlying hook needs fixing so future bib enrichment runs don't silently clobber catalog rows.
close_reason: Catalog enrich hook now matches by source_path, drops the LIMIT-1 fallback that caused 74/75 ART rows to clobber the same first row. References list propagates correctly. 207 tests pass. Shipped in PR #392.

title: Split docs__ART-8c2e74c0: extract 78 PDFs into knowledge__art-papers
description:
docs__ART-8c2e74c0 currently mixes 78 PDF papers (9,996 chunks under docs/papers/) with 287 non-paper files (markdown docs, .dict, .jsonl, .dot - 5,794 chunks). The mixing causes:

1. nx enrich bib walks all 8,593 unique titles even though only ~78 are real paper titles. The other 8,515 are :chunk-N placeholders from prose ingest. Most lookups are fruitless.
2. Aspect extraction conflates two different document types under one collection.
3. Citation links (when generated) would mix doc-mention links with paper-cites links.

Goal: cleanly separate the 78 papers into knowledge__art-papers (paper-shaped collection with proper title metadata), leaving docs__ART for actual repo docs.

Plan (non-destructive, verifiable per step):
1. nx index pdf --dir /Users/hal.hildebrand/git/ART/docs/papers/ --collection knowledge__art-papers
   - Re-index the 78 PDFs with proper title/author/section metadata via _pdf_chunks
   - Voyage embedding cost: ~10k chunks × ~512 tokens × .18/1M = ~/2
   - Auto-registers catalog rows under a curator owner
2. nx enrich bib knowledge__art-papers --source openalex
   - 78 lookups (vs the failed 8,593 attempt). OpenAlex polite pool. Free.
3. nx enrich aspects knowledge__art-papers
   - 78 papers × .01 Haiku = ~/0.78
4. Verify the new collection (sample a few entries, confirm titles + bib metadata are paper-shaped).
5. Delete PDF chunks from docs__ART (using existing nx collection delete or a more surgical chunk-level delete by source_path prefix).
6. Drop the 78 PDF catalog rows from docs__ART (catalog delete or audit-membership style purge).

Step 5+6 are the destructive steps; require explicit user confirmation after step 4 verifies success.

Out of scope:
- Migrating the existing 363 aspect rows in T2 (under docs__ART collection name) - those would need a SQL UPDATE to re-point at knowledge__art-papers, OR be deleted and re-extracted in step 3. Step 3 with no migration ALSO costs /0.78 (the 78 PDFs would extract again under the new collection); same dollar cost as migration but cleaner provenance.

Definition of done:
- knowledge__art-papers exists with 78 PDF docs, all with paper-shaped titles + bib metadata
- aspects extracted for all 78 with non-null fields
- docs__ART contains only the 287 non-paper files
- nx enrich bib knowledge__art-papers can be re-run without errors
- catalog audit-membership knowledge__art-papers shows single-home (no contamination)
notes:
Revised plan: NO re-indexing, NO re-embedding, NO re-extraction. Migration is metadata-only.

1. Create knowledge__art-papers collection in T3.
2. Read 9,996 PDF chunks from docs__ART (ids + embeddings + documents + metadatas) where source_path startswith /docs/papers/.
3. Rewrite each chunk's metadata: set title=derive_title(filename) instead of 'X.pdf:page-N' placeholder; set category='paper'; preserve everything else.
4. add() chunks to knowledge__art-papers with the SAME ids, embeddings, documents, fixed metadata. ChromaDB accepts pre-computed embeddings via add(embeddings=...) — no Voyage call.
5. delete(ids=...) from docs__ART.
6. Update T2 aspect rows: UPDATE document_aspects SET collection='knowledge__art-papers' WHERE source_path LIKE '%/docs/papers/%'. Existing 78-ish rows persist with their extraction data.
7. Update catalog: update physical_collection on the 78 PDF rows from docs__ART-8c2e74c0 to knowledge__art-papers.

Total cost: 
Total time: ~5 min for the chunk migration, ~1 min for SQL updates, ~5 min for verification.

Verification: nx catalog audit-membership knowledge__art-papers should show 1 home (/git/ART), 78 entries, and bib enrichment via OpenAlex should find paper-shaped titles to look up.
close_reason: ART papers split shipped: 78 PDFs migrated from docs__ART to knowledge__art-papers via metadata-only chunk move (no Voyage cost). 78 catalog rows + 77 aspects + 75 bib + 74 references + 52 internal cites links. PR #391 records the migration script.

title: OpenAlex bib enricher backend (drop-in for Semantic Scholar; no API key needed)
description:
Semantic Scholar requires a corporate/academic email; Hal's personal email was rejected at API key request. OpenAlex provides equivalent coverage (200M+ papers, year/venue/authors/cited-by/DOI) with no key requirement. Add OpenAlex as a second bib enrichment backend so docs__ART and other paper collections can get bibliographic enrichment + citation links without a Semantic Scholar key.

Scope:
- New module: src/nexus/bib_enricher_openalex.py mirroring bib_enricher.py shape (enrich(title) -> dict with year/venue/authors/citation_count/doi/openalex_id).

- HTTP: use httpx.Client with mailto query param for OpenAlex 'polite pool' (Hal's email). No key.

- Tests: mocked httpx responses covering success, no-match, rate-limit retry, network error, malformed payload.

Out of scope:

- arXiv-specific lookup (covered by OpenAlex's broad coverage).
- Local PDF reference parsing (filed separately if Hal wants the offline-only pillar).

Definition of done:
- nx enrich bib docs__ART-8c2e74c0 --source openalex enriches papers without an API key
- Existing nx enrich bib docs__ART-8c2e74c0 (default s2) still works when S2_API_KEY is set
- Auto-fallback: when --source not specified and S2_API_KEY is empty, default to openalex
- nx catalog generate-links --citations creates cites links from OpenAlex-enriched bib metadata
