title: extract_aspects: relative-vs-absolute path mismatch on docs__ collections after per-file recovery
description:
After nexus-p03z's --from-t3 recovery, docs__<repo> catalog rows have relative file_path (anchored to repo_root via nexus-3e4s guard). T3 chunks carry absolute source_path. extract_aspects builds chroma://<col>/{file_path} and the chroma reader matches by source_path — relative vs absolute → no match → 'empty' skip.

Live repro 2026-04-30 against ART:
nx enrich aspects docs__ART-8c2e74c0 --dry-run
365 document(s) (scholarly-paper-v1, Haiku ~.65)
Planned skips: 365 of 365 document(s) would skip on read failure

Same shape as the original ART-lhk1 finding (which we previously diagnosed as cross-project contamination, hidden by the bare 'empty' reason). The contamination was real and is now cleaned. This residual is a different bug: the reader's identity-field lookup needs to handle the relative-path-in-catalog vs absolute-path-in-chunks split that the nexus-3e4s anchor guard introduced.

Fix options:
1. extract_aspects (and _dry_run_predict_skips) resolve the catalog file_path against the owner's repo_root before building the chroma URI. This is the cleanest fix and matches what nexus-3e4s did at register time.
2. The chroma reader tries both forms (relative + abspath-against-cwd) before giving up.
3. The chroma reader is identity-field-aware enough to also match by basename/suffix when an exact source_path miss occurs (more permissive but riskier).

Lean: option 1. Would need a Catalog helper that resolves file_path -> absolute via owner.repo_root, then plumb that into extract_aspects' chroma:// URI construction.

rdr__ART-8c2e74c0 (105 docs) extracted cleanly because extract_aspects' chroma:// URI for the rdr-frontmatter-v1 path doesn't need to match T3 chunks — the parser_fn reads directly from the source file. So this bug only bites scholarly-paper-v1 (knowledge__ and docs__ prefixes).

Severity: P2. Doesn't block the original ART-lhk1 fix (rdr__ART worked). Blocks aspect extraction on docs__<repo> collections going forward.
notes: Surfaced 2026-04-30 right after nexus-p03z PR #388 was opened. Test recipe: register a docs__<repo> catalog row with relative file_path, T3 chunk with abspath source_path under the repo, run enrich aspects, assert it does NOT report 'empty' skip.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #389. extract_aspects gains lookup_path param so chroma reader matches absolute source_path in chunks even when catalog file_path is relative (the post-#388 anchor state). Live verified: docs__ART-8c2e74c0 dry-run flips from 365/365 empty -> all readable. 167 tests pass.

title: [bug] nx catalog backfill: crash + missing T3-metadata per-file recovery for repo-owned collections
description:
`nx catalog backfill` (real, not dry-run) crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'encode'` at `src/nexus/commands/collection.py:490` in `_backfill_chunk_text_hash` because some T3 chunk has `documents[i] is None`. Crash happens BEFORE any catalog registrations can be written, so backfill is effectively unusable on the live catalog.

Repro: `nx catalog backfill` against the host catalog. Dry-run completes fine (it skips the backfill_chunk_text_hash phase).

Surfaced during nexus-3e4s remediation (we wanted backfill to recover orphaned chunks). Pre-existing bug, not caused by 4.20.0 changes.

Fix: `_backfill_chunk_text_hash` should skip rows where `doc is None` (perhaps log a warning + count, then continue). One-line guard.
notes:
## Two issues, not one — split when fixing

### Issue 1 (the crash): _backfill_chunk_text_hash NoneType
One-line guard: `if doc is None: continue` at src/nexus/commands/collection.py:490.
Until then, `nx catalog backfill` is unusable on the live host catalog.

### Issue 2 (the design gap surfaced during nexus-3e4s remediation):
For repo-owned `docs__<repo>` and `code__<repo>` collections, the per-file
catalog rows can be reconstructed from T3 chunk metadata WITHOUT
re-indexing. Today backfill cannot do this — `_backfill_repos` claims the
collection (registers a single summary row) and `_backfill_papers`
excludes claimed collections, so per-file recovery falls through.

Proven pattern (executed on docs__ART-8c2e74c0 + code__ART-8c2e74c0
during nexus-3e4s cleanup, 2026-04-29):
1. `t3.get_collection(coll).get(include=['metadatas'], limit=300, ...)` —
   paginate at 300 (Chroma Cloud cap).
2. Group chunks by `metadata['source_path']`.
3. For each unique source_path, register a catalog row under the repo
   owner (cat.owner_for_repo(hash)) with file_path = relative-to-
   repo_root. The 4.20.0 register-time guard auto-anchors source_uri.
4. T3 metadata has correct source_path (was always anchored on the
   indexed repo at index time — only the deleted catalog rows had
   the wrong URI). Recovery is by-construction correct.

Live results (cost: ~50s T3 reads, $0 embedding):
- docs__ART-8c2e74c0: 1 row → 365 rows (recovered 364 from 15,790 chunks)
- code__ART-8c2e74c0: 4,182 rows → 4,397 rows; chunk_count 0 → populated
  for all 4,397 from 63,077 T3 chunks.

Suggested API:
- `nx catalog backfill --from-t3 [<COLLECTION>|--all-repo-collections]`
  for explicit recovery, OR
- Have `_backfill_repos` recurse into per-file recovery for each repo's
  docs__/code__ collections via the same T3-metadata pattern.

Add a regression test that:
- Deletes per-file rows from a docs__<repo> fixture
- Runs backfill (the new path)
- Asserts rows are recovered with correct source_uri attribution
close_reason: Both issues shipped: #386 (Issue 1 None-doc crash guard) and #388 (Issue 2 --from-t3 per-file recovery). 162 tests pass. Verified live on ART catalog: rdr/docs/code__ART now have correctly-attributed catalog rows. Follow-up nexus-v9az filed for the relative-vs-absolute path mismatch surfaced in docs__ART aspect extraction.

title: Investigate nx enrich aspects 'empty' false-positives + count mismatch on rdr__ collections (ART-lhk1)
description:
Reported from ART project KB triage 2026-04-29 against nexus 4.19.2. Affected: rdr__ART-8c2e74c0 (245 documents per 'nx enrich aspects --dry-run', 140 skipped as 'empty').

Symptoms:

title: fix(doctor): nx doctor --check-taxonomy hangs on real-size catalogs (quadratic SQL)
description: The drift query in _run_check_taxonomy uses NOT EXISTS with an OR clause (tl.from_topic_id = ta.topic_id OR tl.to_topic_id = ta.topic_id) that defeats SQLite's index planner — each outer row triggers a covering scan of topic_links. On Hal's local DB (526k topic_assignments × 13k topic_links = ~7B row comparisons), the check times out at 30s with no output. Found via post-release v4.19.0 live shakeout. Restructure with NOT IN (SELECT from_topic_id UNION SELECT to_topic_id) so topic_links is scanned once into a hash set; query drops from >30s to 0.42s.
close_reason: Fixed in v4.19.1 (PR #375 merged 53d5e0c). NOT EXISTS with OR restructured to NOT IN (UNION). 30s+ → 0.42s on real-size catalog; all 6 TestDoctorCheckTaxonomy tests pass.

description:

Module contents:
- @click.group('dt') with help 'DEVONthink integration verbs (macOS only)'
- @dt.command('index') with mutually-exclusive selector flags:
  * --selection (flag, no arg)
  * --group <path>
  * --tag <name>
  * --smart-group <name>
  * --uuid <UUID> (multiple=True for batch)
- Plus passthrough: --database <name>, --collection <name>, --corpus <name>, --dry-run
- Internal pipeline (single function, all selectors share):
  1. _is_darwin() check — exit 1 with macOS-only message if not darwin (skipped under env var NEXUS_DT_FORCE for fake-helper tests on Linux)

  4. For each (uuid, path):

     - source_uri = f'x-devonthink-item://{uuid}'
     - if ext == '.pdf': dispatch nx index pdf <path> --source-uri <uri> [--collection ...] [--corpus ...]
     - elif ext == '.md': dispatch nx index md <path> --source-uri <uri> [--collection ...] [--corpus ...]
     - else: structlog.warning('skip_unsupported_extension', path=path, ext=ext)
  5. Summarize: 'Indexed N records (M skipped)' to stdout
- Register in src/nexus/cli.py: cli.add_command(dt_module.dt)
- Export from src/nexus/commands/__init__.py if pattern matches other commands

Dispatch mechanism:
- Prefer direct function call into the index module (e.g., nexus.commands.index.index_pdf_impl(path, source_uri=uri, collection=...)) over subprocess invocation — keeps the call within the same process, lets exception propagation work, reuses the open T2/T3 connections.

title: [bug] nx index pdf with --extractor docling silently exits at 0 chunks on PDFs >~50MB
description:
Repro: 71MB PDF (DEVONthink 4.2.2 user manual, 378 pages, Apache FOP-produced). 

Auto-extractor: routes to MinerU when 8 formulas detected, MinerU stalls at page 27/378 and the process dies with no error.

--extractor docling --force: Docling logs "extracting dt-422.pdf…" then exits silently. Only output:
  /Users/.../python3.12/multiprocessing/resource_tracker.py:279: UserWarning: resource_tracker: There appear to be 1 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown
No traceback, no chunk count, no error code.

A 7.3MB PDF (Take Control of DEVONthink 4) on the same Mac, same `nx index pdf --collection knowledge__devonthink` invocation, indexed cleanly to 402 chunks.

Workaround: split with `pdftocairo -pdf -f F -l L` into halves; both halves indexed (400 + 406 = 806 chunks). User now has two catalog entries (1.653.81, 1.653.82) instead of one. Far from ideal — the catalog should know they are halves of the same DT-managed document.

The ~50MB threshold is approximate (we did not bisect). Hypotheses: Docling memory blow-up on large PDFs; per-page model inference timeout / batching break; or some interaction between the streaming-pipeline chunking and Docling subprocess lifecycle.

Acceptance: nx index pdf on a 60-100MB PDF either (a) succeeds, or (b) exits non-zero with an actionable error naming the failure mode (OOM, timeout, etc.), instead of silent 0-chunk success.

Surfaced during RDR-099 research-phase dogfooding (2026-04-28).
notes:
Three load-bearing guards added against silent zero-chunk indexing:
1. _extract_normalized (PyMuPDF fallback) raises RuntimeError on empty text — symmetry with _extract_with_docling
2. _pdf_chunks (batch path) raises RuntimeError when extracted text is non-empty but chunker returns []
3. chunker_loop (streaming path, _STREAMING_THRESHOLD=0 means default for all PDFs) raises on is_final + non-empty text + zero chunks
All errors include actionable mitigation: rerun with --extractor mineru or file a bug. CLI surfaces via existing try/except in commands/index.py:616. 233 unit tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1.4+P1.5: integration tests for abstract-themes plan + match-text hygiene
description:
Parent epic: nexus-5gby (RDR-098 P1 remaining)

Branch: feature/parity-batch-running (PR #362) — commit directly, no new PR.
File: tests/test_abstract_themes_plan_integration.py (NEW — sibling to the
existing tests/test_abstract_themes_plan.py which holds the routing/structural
pins; do NOT collapse the two, the integration file is @pytest.mark.integration
gated and slow, the existing file is fast unit-shape).

## Scope

### P1.4 — Integration test harness (primary)
- 10 abstract-question fixtures over docs__art-grossberg-papers (primary,
  46 topics) + knowledge__delos (secondary, 25+ topics). Suggested split:
  6 over Grossberg, 4 over delos so both corpora get coverage.
- Each fixture: dict {question: str, corpus: str, dominant_themes: list[str]}
  where dominant_themes is 3–5 topic-label substrings expected to appear in
  the aggregate output. Consider tuple-of-alternates form
  (e.g. [("ART", "adaptive resonance theory"), ...]) to reduce paraphrase
  fragility on the 80% substring gate.
- Fixture authoring discipline: pull dominant_themes from the actual
  BERTopic labels for the corpus — query nx taxonomy or the
  catalog_taxonomy table directly — so the assertion grounds in real
  centroids, not invented strings.
- Per fixture: run abstract-themes plan via plan_run, then run a baseline
  plan (flat search + operator_generate(template=summary), inline-built)
  for diff. Record both inputs and outputs to T2 telemetry via the
  existing telemetry hook (search_engine.py records relevance; for plan
  outputs use Telemetry domain store directly — see db/t2/telemetry.py).
- Asserts:
  (a) plan completes without error
  (b) aggregate output covers >= 80% of declared dominant_themes
      (i.e., >= ceil(0.8 * len(dominant_themes)) substring matches in the
      final summarize output)
  (c) baseline-plan delta recorded as informational (NOT gated; log the
      coverage delta to test stdout / structured log)

### Critical sub-assertion — RF-2 verification (Open Question 7)
For each fixture, after plan_run completes, inspect the PlanResult's
steps attribute directly. PlanResult is a dataclass at
src/nexus/plans/runner.py:211 with a steps list[dict] field — NO
return_intermediate_steps kwarg exists; just access result.steps[1]
for the groupby step output (steps are 0-indexed; step 0 is search,
step 1 is groupby for this plan). Capture the returned group keys
from steps[1]. Assert:
- The returned group keys are a subset of the actual BERTopic topic
  labels for the corpus (query taxonomy table for ground truth set).
- If a fixture's groupby returns a key NOT in the BERTopic label set,
  the test FAILS with an explicit message identifying the invented
  label — this falsifies RF-2's Assumed claim.

If the assertion fails empirically (LLM-groupby invents groupings),
the contingent fix is to update nx/plans/builtin/abstract-themes.yml
groupby step args from key: topic to key: _topic_label (this is a
natural-language LLM-prompt hint that nudges the partitioner toward
grounding in the materialized _topic_label metadata field — the SQL
fast path does NOT apply because _topic_label is a search_engine.py
metadata key, not a document_aspects column). Do NOT pre-emptively
change the plan; let the test drive the fix. Document the fix path
and the prompt-hint-vs-SQL-config distinction in a code comment near
the assertion.

### P1.5 — Match-text hygiene (in same file, separate test class)
- 3 factual-question fixtures (e.g., "what year did Grossberg publish ART2",
  "who co-authored the 1976 ART paper", "what is the hash size in
  ChashIndex").
- For each: call plan_match (via mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__plan_match or the
  underlying plans.matcher.match_plan API) with verb=query and assert that
  abstract-themes is NOT the top match. Two valid outcomes:
    - confidence below threshold for abstract-themes (matcher rejects), OR
    - another verb=query plan (research-default, analyze-default) wins.
- Note in test docstring: hybrid-factual-lookup is verb=lookup so it
  passes the dimension filter on a disjoint path — collision check is
  scoped to verb=query siblings only.

## Test mechanics
- Mark all tests @pytest.mark.integration (gates on live API access).
- Use module-scoped fixture for plan loader + matcher singletons.
- Reuse existing T3 collection setup conventions from
  tests/integration/ (look at test_search_e2e.py or similar for the
  pattern). Do NOT spin up a new collection — these corpora already
  exist locally.
- LLM-judge rubric: document a 5-criterion rubric in module docstring
  (relevance, coverage, coherence, faithfulness, conciseness) but
  DO NOT call an LLM for grading in the gated assertions. The rubric
  is for future opt-in evaluation; substring coverage is the gate.

## Execution instructions
1. Use mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking to design
   fixture set and confirm dominant_themes grounding before writing code.
2. Search nx T3:
   mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__search(query="abstract themes plan template
   integration test", corpus="knowledge", limit=5)
   mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__search(query="plan_run integration test pattern",
   corpus="code", limit=5)
3. Read existing tests/test_abstract_themes_plan.py to align style.
4. TDD: write fixtures + assertions first; run with -m integration to
   confirm they fail; then complete telemetry recording.
5. Run targeted: uv run pytest tests/test_abstract_themes_plan_integration.py
   -m integration -v
6. Run full unit shape: uv run pytest tests/test_abstract_themes_plan.py
   to confirm no regression on the routing pins.
7. Update T1 scratch tag rdr-098 with empirical RF-2 result before close.

## Validation
- Targeted test passes with @pytest.mark.integration enabled.
- Existing routing/structural tests unchanged + still passing.
- If RF-2 verification fails: ship plan fix in same commit; reference
  Open Question 7 resolution in commit body.
- Commit message references nexus-5gby and RDR-098.

## Continuation state
Update mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__memory_put(project="nexus",
title="rdr-098-integration-state.md", content=...) with: fixture list,
empirical RF-2 outcome, and any plan adjustments after the run.

title: store_get_many: per-stream slice budgets enforced at runner level
description:
RDR-097 P1.0 — Phase 1 prerequisite (promoted from follow-up bead during the planning-chain audit on 2026-04-28).

## Why this is now P1, not a follow-up

The planning-chain audit caught that RDR-097's earlier "plan-author convention" reframe didn't actually work: the runner's binding-substitution language only resolves whole-token `$var` and `$stepN.field` references; a Python-style `$step1.ids[:vector_budget_chunks]` slice expression would pass through as a literal bogus ID. The audit's own suggested fallback (scalar `limit` arg on `store_get_many`) also doesn't exist — `store_get_many` at `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:1006` accepts only `ids`, `collections`, `max_chars_per_doc`, `structured`. Neither path supports per-stream budgeting today.

Per-stream budgeting is core to addressing Gap 4 of RDR-097 (HybridRAG's documented context-precision tradeoff). Pulling this bead into Phase 1 keeps Gap 4 addressed in the same PR rather than deferring all of Gap 4 to a future phase.

## Scope

Add `limit_per_source: int | list[int] | None = None` to `store_get_many(ids, collections, ...)` at `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:1006`.

Semantics:
- `None` (default): no truncation, current behavior preserved.
- `int`: truncate the IDs list to that many entries before hydrating (single-stream form — used by P1.2 traverse-then-generate).
- `list[int]`: when `ids` is shaped as parallel lists (one list per source), truncate each list to its corresponding limit (multi-stream form — used by P1.1 hybrid-factual-lookup). Length must match `len(ids)`; otherwise raise `ValueError`.

Symmetric with the existing list-shaped `ids`/`collections` contract.

## Acceptance

- `store_get_many(ids=[$a, $b], collections=[...], limit_per_source=[6, 4])` truncates `$a` to first 6 and `$b` to first 4 before hydrating.
- `store_get_many(ids=$x, limit_per_source=4)` truncates `$x` to first 4.
- `store_get_many(ids=[$a, $b], limit_per_source=[6])` raises ValueError (length mismatch).
- RDR-097's `hybrid-factual-lookup.yml` (nexus-vej3) and `traverse-then-generate.yml` (nexus-ddm0) use `limit_per_source` for the per-stream cap mechanism.
- Test: parametrized case in `tests/test_store_get_many.py` (the existing test file for this MCP tool) covering single-int, parallel-list, and length-mismatch error.

## Blocks

- nexus-vej3 (P1.1 hybrid-factual-lookup YAML) — needs the arg to exist before YAML can reference it
- nexus-ddm0 (P1.2 traverse-then-generate YAML) — same

## Provenance

Filed initially during RDR-097 substantive-critic gate review as a future-shape bead. Promoted to P1 prerequisite after `nx_plan_audit` flagged the YAML-slice reframe as non-viable (audit verdict captured in T2 entry `nexus_rdr/097-gate-latest`).
notes:
## Implementation Context (from nx_enrich_beads on 2026-04-28)

**Target signature** at `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:1006`:

```python
@mcp.tool()
def store_get_many(
    ids: str | list,                          # may now be list[list[str]] for parallel-list form
    collections: str | list = "knowledge",
    *,
    max_chars_per_doc: int = 4000,
    structured: bool = False,
    limit_per_source: int | list[int] | None = None,   # NEW
) -> str | dict: ...
```

### Three input shapes

1. **None** — preserve current behavior. No truncation.
2. **int** (single-stream) — apply `id_list = id_list[:limit_per_source]` after normalization at `core.py:1024-1028`, before hydration loop at `core.py:1046`. Consumer: nexus-ddm0 P1.2.
3. **list[int]** (parallel-list) — `ids` is `list[list[str]]`. Truncate each `ids[i]` to `limit_per_source[i]`, flatten, run hydration. Length must match `len(ids)` — `ValueError` on mismatch (stricter than the existing collections-broadcast behavior at `core.py:1047-1050`).

When `ids` is parallel-list, decide whether `collections` continues to broadcast when shorter or also requires strict alignment. Document the choice.

### TDD-first ordering (audit O3)

Lock semantics in `tests/test_store_get_many.py` (existing) BEFORE touching core.py:1006:

- `test_limit_per_source_none_preserves_default` — N=10 IDs, all returned (regression guard)
- `test_limit_per_source_int_truncates_single_stream` — N=20, limit=5, assert no T3 calls for IDs 6..20
- `test_limit_per_source_list_truncates_parallel_streams` — `ids=[[a1..a4],[b1..b3]]`, `limit=[2,1]`, document whether interleave or stream-major flatten
- `test_limit_per_source_list_length_mismatch_raises_valueerror` — verify message includes both lengths
- `test_limit_per_source_int_with_parallel_ids_form` — decide: error, or broadcast-across-streams?
- `test_parallel_form_collections_alignment` — pin whether parallel `ids` requires parallel `collections`
- `test_limit_per_source_zero` and `test_limit_per_source_negative` — edge cases

### Reality check on consumers (audit O1)

`nexus-vej3` issues TWO scalar calls (`limit_per_source=$vector_budget_chunks` and `limit_per_source=$graph_budget_chunks`), not one parallel-list call. **Neither downstream plan currently consumes the parallel-`list[int]` form.** Implementing it for contract symmetry and future plans, not for an active caller. Note this in the docstring so future maintainers don't expect to find one.

### Out of scope

- `src/nexus/plans/runner.py` binding-substitution language NOT touched. The kwarg path was chosen specifically because slice expressions like `$step1.ids[:vector_budget_chunks]` would pass through as literal bogus IDs.
- `_hydrate_operator_args` auto-hydration branch (`runner.py:645-700`) NOT touched — the new kwarg only flows through explicit `store_get_many` plan steps.
- `_OPERATOR_MAX_INPUTS` cap behavior unchanged.

### Docstring

Extend `core.py:1013-1022` with the new arg semantics and the length-mismatch error contract.

Adds limit_per_source kwarg to store_get_many: int truncates single-stream, list[int] truncates parallel-stream + flattens, None preserves default. Parallel-stream ids form is a new input shape; per-stream collection routing when collections list-length matches outer ids length. Out-of-scope branches (runner binding-substitution, _hydrate_operator_args, _OPERATOR_MAX_INPUTS) untouched. 10 new tests + 253 wider plan/MCP suite green. Unblocks nexus-vej3 and nexus-ddm0.

title: MCP server plan-cache invalidation when plan library mutates
description:
The MCP server caches the plan library at first use via `mcp_infra.get_t1_plan_cache(populate_from=db.plans)` — a per-session cache populated lazily. Once built, it is not invalidated when the underlying T2 `plans` table mutates.

Symptoms observed during nexus-ldnp impl:
1. Re-seed a builtin (`abstract-themes.yml` description tweak) → SQL update succeeds → MCP `nx_answer` continues to dispatch the OLD description's match scores until the MCP server is bounced.
2. Add a new builtin → MCP `plan_match` doesn't see it until restart.
3. `nx_answer` invocations ran the inline planner instead of the matched plan because the cache was stale; debugging required reaching into Python.

## Scope

Three viable invalidation triggers; the right one depends on freshness vs. cost tradeoff:

1. **mtime-guarded refresh on each plan_match** — pattern already used by Catalog (see `_last_consistency_mtime` in `src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py`). Cheap when nothing changed; rebuilds cache when SQLite write timestamp moves. Recommended.

2. **TTL-based refresh** — invalidate every N seconds. Simpler but loses freshness during the window.

3. **Explicit invalidate hook on plan writes** — `PlanLibrary.save_plan()`, `delete_plan()`, etc. fire a callback. Tightest coupling to write paths; needs registration plumbing.

## Acceptance

- `nx plan reseed` (from companion bead) updates a builtin description → next `nx_answer` call sees the new description in matcher logs WITHOUT MCP restart.
- New builtin added → next `nx_answer` call can match against it.
- Performance: matcher latency overhead under 10ms in the steady-state cache-hit path.

## Companion to

- nexus-XXXX (plan admin CLI bead) — `nx plan reseed` is mostly useless if MCP doesn't pick up the rewrite.
close_reason: Fixed via mtime-guarded refresh in mcp_infra.get_t1_plan_cache. Pattern mirrors Catalog._last_consistency_mtime. PlanLibrary.path is new public attr; _plan_cache_mtime tracks populate-time mtime; populate fires when current mtime advances. Test stubs without .path fall back to populate-once. 5 new tests + 110 MCP + 172 plan-stack tests green. PR #344. Once merged, RDR-097 P1.5 harness can drop its reset_plan_cache_for_tests workaround.

title: nx plan admin CLI: list/show/delete/disable plans, with origin tracking
description:
The plan library has no admin CLI. To inspect, debug, or clean up plans today you write SQL against T2 directly. This bit me on nexus-ldnp impl: an inline-planner-grown plan (id 70 with strategy=main-themes-grossberg-papers-cognitive) shadowed the new abstract-themes builtin during testing, and the only way to clear it was raw SQL.

## What's missing

The plan library distinguishes three origins by behavior but not by surface:
1. **Seeded builtins** — `nx/plans/builtin/*.yml`, owned by the codebase
2. **Auto-grown** — created by `_nx_answer_plan_grow` when the inline planner produces a successful plan; persisted for reuse but invisible in any tool
3. **User/skill-created** — written via plan_save MCP tool

Today they're indistinguishable in T2. There's no `origin` column. There's no CLI to list, inspect, or delete them.

## Scope

Add `nx plan` command group to `src/nexus/commands/`:

- `nx plan list [--scope=global|personal] [--origin=builtin|grown|user] [--name <pat>]`
  - Tabulate id, name, scope, verb, strategy, use_count, last_used, origin
  - Origin inferred from heuristics until P2 lands proper column: tags startswith "builtin-template" → builtin; scope=personal AND no tags → grown; else user
- `nx plan show <id|name>` — full plan_json, dimensions, bindings, run history
- `nx plan delete <id|name> [-y]` — confirmation prompt, deletes one row + cascades any FK refs
- `nx plan disable <id> [--reason=...]` — soft-disable: matcher skips but row preserved (new column `disabled_at`)
- `nx plan reseed [--force]` — re-run `load_all_tiers`; with `--force`, deletes all builtins first to pick up description changes

## Phase 2 (separate bead)

Add an explicit `origin` column to `plans` table: `'builtin' | 'grown' | 'user'`. Migrate existing rows via heuristic. Wire `_nx_answer_plan_grow` and `plan_save` to set origin. This makes `--origin` filter exact rather than heuristic.

## Why P2 priority

Routine tasks (debugging plan match, cleaning up post-test residue, characterizing what's in the library) currently require Python+SQL. This is exactly the kind of admin gap that makes a tool feel low-trust.
close_reason: nx plan list/show/delete/reseed shipped on PR #345. Closes the routine-ops gap (raw-SQL workaround during nexus-ldnp impl). 4 new subcommands + origin classification heuristic + PlanLibrary.delete_plan. 13 new tests + 340 regression tests green. 'disable' subcommand and Phase 2 'origin' column deferred per bead.

title: nx store put CLI ghosts chunks: catalog row written, chroma index missing
description:
## Problem

`nx store put` (CLI) and `mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__store_put` (MCP tool) are documented as the same operation but diverge on outcome:

- **CLI `nx store put`** writes catalog metadata only. The chunk does NOT land in the chroma collection index. The catalog row appears in `nx store list`; the document is unfindable via `nx search`, MCP `search`, or MCP `query`. CLI returns `Stored: <id> -> <collection>` and exits 0 — silent corruption.
- **MCP `store_put`** works correctly. Same content, same title, same tags, same collection — chunk lands in chroma, immediately searchable.

## Why it matters

- CLI is the natural ingestion path for shell-driven workflows, batch ingest scripts, CI hooks
- Silent failure mode: users add docs they can't find, re-add, storage grows, index doesn't
- `nx collection audit` and `nx collection health` do not flag the discrepancy (both report `chunk_count` matching `nx store list` even when search returns one fewer)
- Compounds with #331/#332/#333 — anything assuming `document_aspects` or operator SQL fast paths align with searchable content gets misleading results
- Compounds with RDR-096 chroma reader — ghosted docs return `ReadFail(empty)` from the URI reader even when the URI is correct; the architectural fix absorbs the symptom but the upstream root cause is still emitting ghosts

## Repro

```bash
echo "# Test\nBody about ChatGPT MCP install with OAuth client IDs and Cognito callbacks." > /tmp/test.md
nx store put /tmp/test.md --collection knowledge --title "ghost-repro-$(date +%s)" --tags "test"
# CLI: "Stored: <id> -> knowledge__knowledge", exit 0
nx store list --collection knowledge | grep ghost-repro     # row present
nx search "ChatGPT MCP install OAuth Cognito" --corpus knowledge -m 25
# ghost-repro doc is missing from results
```

Then via MCP `store_put` with identical content, title, tags → identical id, AND it shows up in search.

## Tracker

- GitHub issue: https://github.com/Hellblazer/nexus/issues/335
- Diagnostic precedent doc: `diagnostic-chroma-ghost-test-2026-04-22` in `knowledge__knowledge`
- Related: #331/#332/#333 (silent-corruption family), RDR-096 (catalog↔T3 reader contract)
design:
Likely site of bug: `src/nexus/commands/store.py` (CLI `nx store put`) calls a different upsert wrapper than `src/nexus/mcp/core.py:store_put`. Diff the two entry points; identify the missing `coll.add_documents` / `T3Database.upsert_chunks` call. Converge both on the MCP code path, OR factor the shared logic into a single helper invoked from both surfaces.

The verify-chunk-queryable round-trip is a small additional cost per ingest (one `coll.get` after the upsert). Probably acceptable; gate on benchmark if not.

The `--verify-chroma` audit mode is its own work item — file as separate bead and link as related.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Audit the CLI `store put` code path against MCP `store_put` path; converge on a single shared upsert function that does catalog write + chroma index in one transaction.
2. After upsert, the success path verifies the chunk is queryable (round-trip lookup) before declaring success. On failure: rollback catalog row, exit non-zero, log diagnostic event.
3. Integration test: write via CLI, confirm via search round-trip in same test (no mocks at the storage boundary per project convention).
4. `nx collection audit --verify-chroma` mode that detects catalog↔chroma drift directly (cross-check `chunk_id` set in chroma against catalog) — this is the broader sibling of (2) and may land in a related bead under the RDR-090 catalog-prune-stale arc.
notes: Related to RDR-090 P1.5 (nx catalog prune-stale / RDR-prefix mode, bead nexus-zg4c) — that work also addresses catalog↔T3 drift, but at the cleanup boundary not the write boundary. The two are complementary.
close_reason: Closed

title: aspect_extractor: source content from T3 (and pass prompt via stdin)
description:
Two stacked bugs surfaced when running `nx enrich aspects knowledge__hybridrag` against the SAGE paper (arxiv 2604.15583, knowledge__hybridrag, tumbler 1.653.77, 134 chunks):

## Bug 1 — content sourced from disk instead of T3 (PRIMARY)

The Claude-CLI scholarly-paper-v1 extractor reads the document body from `source_path` (filesystem) when content isn't passed in. For the `nx enrich aspects` path this is wrong twice over:

1. **The catalog stores basenames, not abspaths**, so `open('2604.15583.pdf')` resolves against the cwd of the `nx` process, not the original ingest directory. Three docs in this collection failed with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<basename>'` even when the file was on disk a tab away.
2. **T3 already has the document text** — we just indexed it into 134 chunks. The extractor walking back to the original PDF re-introduces a second source-of-truth, requires re-running PDF extraction (Docling/MinerU) for output that may differ from what's in T3, and binds aspects extraction to the ingest-time filesystem layout.

The clean fix is to source the document body from T3: `coll.get(where={"source_path": file_path})` → sort by chunk index → join. This makes catalog file_path values irrelevant for the aspects path, removes the cwd dependency, and aligns aspects with the same text the search/query path actually retrieves over.

(Bug 2 below is still real but lives downstream of this fix.)

## Bug 2 — subprocess argv exceeds ARG_MAX

Even after T3-sourcing, the extractor invokes:
`subprocess.run(["claude", "-p", prompt, "--output-format", "json"])`

with the entire prompt — including the full document body — as a CLI argument. macOS ARG_MAX is ~256 KB and counts argv plus env. SAGE (~14 pages of dense text) overflows; the OS rejects exec with `Errno 7: Argument list too long`. Caught as `_HardFailure("subprocess exec failed: ...")`, retries exhausted, null-fields persisted with no useful diagnostic.

**Sites**:
- src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py:1057 (`_invoke_once`, single-doc)
- src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py:902 (`_invoke_once_batch`, batched-per-N)

Pipe the prompt via stdin (`claude -p --prompt-stdin` or stdin-only).

## Repro

```
nx index pdf ~/Downloads/arxiv-papers/2604.15583.pdf --collection knowledge__hybridrag
nx enrich aspects knowledge__hybridrag
# → all 3 docs fail; SAGE specifically with 'Argument list too long' even after cd
```

## Constraint

Do NOT land on `feature/nexus-b9g1-rdr-089-aspect-extraction` — that branch is the closed Phase F arc; this fix lands on its own `feature/<bead-id>-aspect-extractor-t3-source` branch.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] _invoke_once and _invoke_once_batch source document body from T3 (coll.get + chunk-index sort + join), not source_path
- [ ] source_path becomes a fallback only when no T3 chunks resolve (defensive)
- [ ] _invoke_once and _invoke_once_batch pass prompt via stdin, never argv
- [ ] Unit test: subprocess.run argv stays under 4 KB regardless of doc length
- [ ] Unit test: extractor succeeds when source_path doesn't exist on disk but T3 has chunks
- [ ] Re-run nx enrich aspects knowledge__hybridrag --re-extract → SAGE (tumbler 1.653.77) gets a non-null AspectRecord
notes:
Implementing fixes on RDR-089 branch (active aspect-extraction work). Changes landed:

1. PDFChunker (src/nexus/pdf_chunker.py): heading detection (markdown + numbered + bare) → tags every chunk with section_type/section_title via classify_section_type.
2. doc_indexer + pipeline_stages: forward chunker section metadata instead of hardcoded ''.
3. Code indexer (code_indexer.py): adds chunk_start_char/chunk_end_char (computed from line offsets).
4. Prose indexer line-fallback: adds char offsets + section_type/title via _extract_headings reuse.
5. aspect_extractor: new _source_content_from_t3() helper that reassembles document text from T3 chunks, filters to scholarly sections (abstract/introduction/methods/results/discussion/conclusion), caps at 80KB. extract_aspects sources from T3 first, falls back to disk only on T3 miss.
6. aspect_extractor _invoke_once + _invoke_once_batch: prompt now stdin-fed (input=prompt), not argv. ARG_MAX no longer reachable.
7. aspect_worker batch path: same T3-source-then-disk precedence.
8. PDF catalog hook (pipeline_stages._catalog_pdf_hook): file_path now stored as absolute path, not basename — readers no longer depend on cwd.

All test changes:
- tests/test_pdf_chunker.py: 7 new tests for heading detection + section_type tagging.
- tests/test_aspect_extractor.py: argv-shape assertions migrated to kwargs['input']; new test for T3-source path; new test that argv stays bounded regardless of content size.

12/12 PDF chunker tests pass. 30/30 aspect_extractor tests pass. Wider suite running.

title: RDR-089 P2.2: nx enrich aspects CLI (--dry-run / --validate-sample / --re-extract)
description:
Phase 2 / Step 2 — batch CLI for pre-existing collections.

RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-089-structured-aspect-extraction-at-ingest.md (Phase 2, Step 2)
Parent epic: nexus-b9g1
Depends on: nexus-b0e1 (T2 store) + nexus-xo79 (extractor) + nexus-x8x1 (hook + registration shipped — needed for the test surface)

Add subcommand to src/nexus/commands/enrich.py: `nx enrich aspects <collection>` — batch extraction over an existing collection. Iterates documents via the catalog (catalog.list_by_collection — returns ONE entry per source document, NOT per chunk), calls extract_aspects DIRECTLY (bypassing the hook to avoid double-work on docs that already triggered hook-time extraction), upserts to T2.

Flags:

  --dry-run
    Reports document count + cost estimate (papers × ~$0.01 Haiku per call). NO API calls. NO T2 writes.

  --validate-sample N
    After extraction, run operator_check on N% of newly-extracted papers (default 5).
    Call shape:
      operator_check(
        claim=json.dumps(extracted_aspects),
        evidence=raw_document_text,
        timeout=60,
      )
    The extracted aspect record is the CLAIM; the source document is the EVIDENCE.
    Disagreements (operator returns verified=false with rationale) → emit to a `validation_failures.jsonl` file in the corpus directory (path: derive from the catalog entry's source dir or default to ./).
    See RDR Failure Modes / Silent — this is the detection mechanism for hallucinated extractions; the self-reported confidence field is NOT the gate.

  --re-extract --extractor-version <v>
    Re-run on rows whose model_version < v (uses document_aspects.list_by_extractor_version from P1.1).
    Supports incremental schema rollouts — when a new aspect field promotes from extras to a fixed column and the extractor prompt is updated, bump the version and re-extract over the affected collection only.

  --list (Day 2 ops, optional in this bead but cheap to add): list source_paths with extracted aspects in <collection>.
  --info <source_path>: show the AspectRecord JSON for one document.
  --delete <source_path>: remove the aspect row for one document.

Constraints (load-bearing — do not relax):
  - The CLI bypasses the hook. Reason: documents already in the collection (indexed before P2.1 ships, or re-extraction passes) need a path that does not double-fire when ingest re-runs them. Calling extract_aspects directly + upsert is the correct surface.
  - Iterates via the CATALOG, not via T3 query. The catalog returns one entry per source document; T3 returns chunks. Aspects are document-grain.
  - --dry-run must NEVER call subprocess.run. Cost estimate is documents × per-call cost constant (define per RDR Trade-offs: ~$0.01/paper).
  - --validate-sample default is 5 (5%) — but if the P1.3 spike showed poor field stability, raise to 20% per the spike's verdict (cross-reference nexus-8t3k close note).
  - validation_failures.jsonl is one line per failure: {source_path, extracted_aspects, operator_check_rationale, timestamp}.
  - --re-extract is INCREMENTAL by version; do not re-extract rows whose model_version >= the requested version (would be wasteful and idempotent at the row level but expensive at the wallet level).

Out of scope for this bead (deferred per RDR Open Questions):
  - Batch-Haiku-per-call (one prompt extracts N papers). Phase 4 if measurement warrants.
  - extras → fixed-column promotion workflow. The CLI flag is wired here but the policy decision (which fields graduate, who decides, version-bump semantics) is a separate operations RDR.

TDD: extend tests/commands/test_enrich.py with --dry-run cost estimation, --validate-sample sample-size selection, --re-extract version-filter behavior (mock the extractor; assert subprocess.run is called only for rows < target version).

description:
Establishes tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh as the standing pre-merge gate for any PR that touches the deployment surface. Companion: tests/e2e/release-sandbox.md operator manual; CLAUDE.md '## Sandbox Testing' section.

Trigger globs (any change to these files MUST run release-sandbox.sh smoke before merge):
  - pyproject.toml, uv.lock
  - src/nexus/db/migrations.py
  - src/nexus/mcp/**
  - nx/**
  - .claude-plugin/**

  - src/nexus/commands/upgrade.py

Pass criteria: smoke exits clean, all nx doctor --check-* surfaces green (with the documented fresh-sandbox exception for --check-plan-library when nx catalog setup has not run).

Fail criteria: any check exits non-zero. Open a fix-it commit on the same PR (or a separate hotfix PR). Do not merge intending to fix on main — the gap was visible in the sandbox, fix in the sandbox.

Why this exists: editable installs (uv sync) and wheel installs (uv tool install) resolve package data and version-gated migrations differently. Reviewers see the editable shape; users get the wheel shape. Bugs that pass pytest and ship broken usually live in that gap. RDR-095 closure surfaced this risk pattern: 5275 unit tests passed but the wheel-install MCP path was never exercised — the kind of gap release-sandbox.sh smoke catches in ~2 min.

  - Auto-bead on PR open that nudges the author when triggers fire

title: nx hook session-start hangs forever when stdin is not closed (CLI / pipeline case)
description:
The nx hook session-start CLI subcommand calls sys.stdin.read() unconditionally to parse the JSON payload Claude Code pipes in. When stdin is open but no data arrives (any non-Claude-Code invocation: shell pipeline, ad-hoc CLI run with no piped input, test harness), the call blocks indefinitely.

Discovered: a stuck zsh shell from this session was traced to PID 9447 = python3 nx hook session-start spawned by 'nx hook session-start | wc -lc' — the wc never received output because nx never returned. STAT was 'S' (sleeping on read). After ~20 minutes still alive. Killed manually.

In production the 10s timeout in nx/hooks/hooks.json bounds the SessionStart entry, so the hook chain remains usable, but the CLI surface is broken for any out-of-band invocation. Likely affects nx-validation/E2E-style harnesses that exercise the hook directly.

Repro:
  nx hook session-start | wc -lc   # hangs forever; ^C to escape
  echo '{}' | nx hook session-start  # returns immediately (correct)

Source: src/nexus/commands/hook.py:26 (session_start_cmd) — bare sys.stdin.read() with no timeout / TTY check.

Fix candidates:
  (1) sys.stdin.isatty() guard → skip read() when interactive
  (2) select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0.1) with empty fallback
  (3) read with explicit Claude-Code 30s budget that maps to the hooks.json timeout

Same hazard probably applies to other 'nx hook *' subcommands that read stdin.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-095 P3.1 — Update nx taxonomy status to render batch-shape failures

title: RDR-095 P2.3 — Drift guard: assert no direct imports of batch hooks outside mcp_infra.py
description:
Phase 2, Step 3 (promoted from Phase 3 per RDR-095 §Implementation Plan
§Prerequisites bullet 3 — wire BEFORE migration completes, not after).

Add a static-check unit test that asserts no production source file outside
src/nexus/mcp_infra.py imports or references taxonomy_assign_batch_hook or
chash_dual_write_batch_hook directly. This is the load-bearing guard against
the same debt re-accreting in future enrichments.

Deliverable (one new test in tests/test_mcp_infra.py or a new
tests/test_hook_drift_guard.py):

    def test_batch_hooks_not_called_outside_mcp_infra():
        \"\"\"RDR-095 drift guard: registered batch hooks must only be
        referenced inside mcp_infra.py. Every other module fires through
        fire_post_store_batch_hooks.\"\"\"
        import pathlib, re
        repo_root = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent / "src" / "nexus"
        offenders = []
        pat = re.compile(r"taxonomy_assign_batch_hook|chash_dual_write_batch_hook")
        for py in repo_root.rglob("*.py"):
            if py.name == "mcp_infra.py":
                continue
            text = py.read_text()
            if pat.search(text):
                # Allow registration line in mcp/core.py — explicitly:
                if py.name == "core.py" and "register_post_store_batch_hook" in text:
                    continue
                offenders.append(str(py.relative_to(repo_root.parent.parent)))
        assert not offenders, (
            f"RDR-095 drift guard: batch hooks referenced outside "
            f"mcp_infra.py and the single registration site in "
            f"mcp/core.py: {offenders}"
        )

Acceptance criteria (per RDR-095 §Test Plan, drift-guard scenario):
  - The test runs and PASSES after P2.1 + P2.2 + this bead land.
  - The test FAILS if a hypothetical future commit imports either hook in
    a third file. (Verify: temporarily add an import to indexer.py; run
    test; observe FAIL; revert.)
  - Allowance is explicit and narrow: ONLY mcp_infra.py (definitions) and
    mcp/core.py (the single registration site).
  - Test docstring cites RDR-095.

Implementation notes:
  - Use plain ast.parse + walk for ImportFrom rather than regex if a more
    semantic check is preferred. Regex is acceptable per the RDR §Risks
    bullet 3 ("static check (grep-based, in tests/ or scripts/checks/)").
  - Skip __pycache__, *.pyc, .ruff_cache, etc. (rglob *.py handles this naturally).
  - Mark the test with no special pytest marker — it should run in the default
    fast suite so CI catches drift on every commit.

Edge cases to handle:
  - If a docstring or comment in some other file mentions the hook name,
    the regex check flags it. Decide: (a) restrict to ImportFrom AST nodes
    (clean) or (b) accept the false positive and update the test to allowlist
    benign mentions. Recommend (a): use ast.NodeVisitor to scan only
    `from nexus.mcp_infra import …` and direct attribute access
    `mcp_infra.<name>`.

Do NOT:
  - Add allowlist entries for additional files (the whole point is the
    guard catches new offenders).
  - Move the registration line out of mcp/core.py.

Execution notes:
  - Run only the new test post-implementation:
      uv run pytest tests/test_mcp_infra.py::test_batch_hooks_not_called_outside_mcp_infra -v
  - Use mcp__plugin_nx_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking when designing
    the AST walk if you choose option (a) above.

Files to modify:
  - tests/test_mcp_infra.py (add one new test) OR
  - tests/test_hook_drift_guard.py (new file with the single test).
    Either is acceptable — pick the same file scope as the rest of P1.3.

Depends on: P2.1 (the new names must exist) AND P2.2 (the seven sites must
be converted; otherwise this test fails immediately on the existing call sites).

Validation:
  - P2.R review checkpoint includes this guard's correctness review.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-094 Phase I: Add stdio_pipe_break phase to spike harness
description:
Spike A's four phases (clean / mcp_sigkill / mcp_oom / claude_crash) did not exercise a fifth failure mode observed in the wild on 2026-04-25: nx-mcp died with NO mcp_server_crashed AND NO mcp_server_stopping event. atexit didn't run, signal handlers didn't run. Likely cause: stdio pipe break from Claude Code's MCP client (e.g. MCP client SIGKILL'd the server without delivering SIGTERM, or the stdio buffer broke during a tool response).

The fifth failure mode bypasses our entire belt-and-braces:
- Lifespan finally: requires anyio handler (not on stdio).
- Signal handler: requires SIGTERM/SIGINT delivery.
- atexit: requires clean Python exit (not on signal-killed).

If this mode is reachable in normal operation, it's a serious gap in RDR-094's coverage claims. Need to (a) reproduce it, (b) measure whether the watchdog's --mcp-pid trigger catches it at all, (c) update CA-1's evidence to acknowledge this fifth mode.

Implementation:
- Add a phase to scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_lifecycle.py: 'stdio_pipe_break' that closes nx-mcp's stdin abruptly (subprocess.Popen.stdin.close()) without sending any signal.
- 10 runs. Expected cleanup: watchdog --mcp-pid trigger within 5s.
- If watchdog doesn't fire (mcp_pid still alive in some weird half-dead state), file a follow-up bead for harder kill detection.

Reference: forensic timeline in mcp.log on 2026-04-25 between 19:45 and 20:10 — nx-mcp pid 94433 went silent for ~25 minutes without any lifecycle event, then user manually reconnected via /mcp.

Files:
- scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_lifecycle.py (new phase)
- T2 nexus_rdr/094-spike-a-lifecycle: append updated 50-run results

Acceptance:
- 10 stdio_pipe_break runs with cleanup_path = watchdog_mcp at 100%
- If less than 100%, file a code follow-up bead for the gap

- Test: unit test that exercises main() with mocked _is_alive transitions and asserts the right event sequence in a tmpdir mcp.log path (use NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR override).

title: Phase D: Spike B — subagent T1 sharing race verification
description:
## Summary
Verify that moving chroma spawn from the SessionStart hook to MCP-server startup does not regress subagent T1 sharing. Specifically, rule out the race described in RDR §Critical Assumptions CA-2: a subagent dispatched within milliseconds of top-level MCP startup may observe NX_SESSION_ID set but find the parent's session record not yet written, causing a silent EphemeralClient downgrade.

## Spike Protocol (from RDR §Critical Assumptions CA-2)
- Dispatch a subagent within milliseconds of top-level MCP startup (before write_session_record_by_id completes)
- Assert the subagent's T1 client connects to the parent's chroma (not a fresh EphemeralClient)
- Run at least 10 cycles across varying timing delays (0ms, 5ms, 50ms, 200ms)
- Record path attribution per cycle: connected_to_parent vs ephemeral_downgrade

## Deliverable
A new spike script: scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_b_subagent_race.py
Modeled on scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_lifecycle.py structure.
Results in: scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_b_results.jsonl

## Outcome Paths
### Race not reproducible (expected)
- Persist findings to T2 nexus_rdr/094-spike-b-subagent-race
- Mark CA-2 as VERIFIED in RDR-094
- Unblocks Phase E + Phase F

### Race reproducible
- File a follow-up task: add retry-with-backoff to _resolve_top_level_session_id in src/nexus/db/t1.py
- Implement the retry (backoff: 50ms, 100ms, 200ms, max 3 attempts)
- Re-run spike to confirm race eliminated
- Phase E + Phase F block until retry lands and spike re-passes

## Files

title: session-end-detach forks too late — Python 2s cold start races SIGTERM
description:
The 4.10.3 double-fork defense (src/nexus/commands/hook.py::session_end_detach_cmd) forks AFTER Click has parsed argv and after all nexus modules have imported. Measured cold-start time: 2.0s on this install (Python + Click + nexus.hooks + nexus.db + ...). Hook timeout is 5s, so in theory fine — but Claude Code's shutdown SIGTERM is delivered to the hook's process group faster than 2s on this machine, so the first fork never runs and 'Hook cancelled' appears instead.

Evidence:
  * time /Users/hal.hildebrand/.local/share/uv/tools/conexus/bin/nx hook session-end-detach -> 2.005s total to return exit 0 (Python startup dominates)
  * time python3 -c 'import os; p=os.fork(); p==0 or os._exit(0); os.setsid(); os.execvp("nx", ["nx", "hook", "session-end"])' -> 0.017s total (17ms — fork-first wins)

User-facing impact: bounded. The 4.11.0 uuid_mismatch + anchor_dead sweep in sweep_stale_sessions picks up the orphans at next SessionStart, so the leak is caught within seconds of reopening Claude Code. But the 'Hook cancelled' error message appears on every session close, and graceful cleanup (flush scratch to T2, expire memory entries) is skipped because the grandchild never runs.

Fix shape:
  * Add src/nexus/_session_end_launcher.py with a __main__ guard that does os.fork() + os.setsid() + os.fork() + dup2(/dev/null) BEFORE importing nexus modules. Then in the grandchild, import nexus.hooks and call session_end().
  * Update nx/hooks/hooks.json SessionEnd command from 'nx hook session-end-detach || true' to 'python3 -m nexus._session_end_launcher || true'.
  * Keep session_end_detach_cmd as a backward-compat alias that just calls the launcher, for any external invocations.

Net effect: hook returns to Claude Code in ~17ms instead of 2s, well inside any shutdown SIGTERM window. Grandchild does its expensive imports and cleanup detached.
acceptance_criteria: time python3 -m nexus._session_end_launcher completes under 100ms on a cold cache; hooks.json SessionEnd command updated; graceful cleanup actually runs (chroma stopped cleanly, scratch flushed, session file removed) instead of relying on the next SessionStart sweep; 'Hook cancelled' message stops appearing at session close.
notes: Discovered live 2026-04-24 post-4.11.0 release. Sweep fallback still works (current state: only one chroma, no stale session files), but the error message is noise and the flush-scratch-to-T2 step is being skipped.
close_reason: Fork-first launcher landed on PR #279, tagged v4.11.1. Measured 256ms cold-cache return time (vs 2005ms for nx hook session-end-detach, 8x faster). hooks.json chained to prefer launcher + fallback to old detach for mixed-version installs. 5054 tests green, 0 failed. Reinstalled locally; nx-session-end-launcher on PATH, verified 301ms total including head pipe.

title: T1 chroma not GC'd on session UUID rollover within a live Claude process
description:
Follow-up to nexus-99jb (4.10.3 T1 chroma lifecycle defense-in-depth). The three-layer GC covers (1) graceful SessionEnd, (2) watchdog reaping after parent-claude death, (3) liveness-based sweep_stale_sessions. But it does NOT cover session-UUID rollover within a single living Claude process: when /clear or /resume rolls the conversation UUID, the old session's chroma stays alive because claude_root_pid and server_pid are both still live; sweep_stale_sessions has no trigger for 'same claude process, different current session UUID'. Bounded leak (24h age threshold eventually catches it) but not fully closed.

Reproduction: open claude, let T1 chroma spin up; /clear; check ps — old chroma remains, pointing at the same claude_root_pid as the new one. current_session flat file is updated but sweep_stale_sessions doesn't consult it.

Fix: add a fourth reap trigger in sweep_stale_sessions (src/nexus/session.py:209) — when the record's session_id differs from the current_session pointer AND claude_root_pid is alive, mark as stale. SessionStart fires on /clear so the sweep will catch it at the next conversation boundary. Tests: cover the trigger, and cover the non-reap case where claude_root_pid is dead and uuid also differs (that path is handled by anchor_dead, not uuid_stale).

Verified live (2026-04-24): this claude session (pid 83742) has chroma 83904 for stale uuid 0fcbd98f-... still running from yesterday's /resume start, and chroma 240 for current uuid b3e1052f-... Both anchored to same claude pid; sweep won't reap either.
acceptance_criteria: sweep_stale_sessions reaps records whose session_id differs from read_claude_session_id() when claude_root_pid is alive; existing age/server_dead/anchor_dead triggers preserved; structured log 'sweep_reaped_session' carries reason='uuid_mismatch'; tests cover (a) uuid_mismatch + live claude → reap, (b) uuid_match + live claude → keep, (c) no current_session pointer → behave as pre-change, (d) mixed scenarios still honor existing triggers
notes: Scope: src/nexus/session.py:209-286, tests/test_session.py or similar. ~15 lines impl + 4 tests. Bounded leak severity (24h age cap + graceful SessionEnd path), so P2. Surfaced from Hal's 2026-04-24 asking about the leak state post-4.10.3.
close_reason: Landed on PR #278 (commit 9fe81ee). Fourth reap trigger 'uuid_mismatch' added to sweep_stale_sessions: when record.session_id != current_session pointer AND claude_root_pid alive AND anchor not dead, reap. Specificity preserved in structured log — age/server_dead/anchor_dead still win when multiple triggers apply. Compact events unaffected (compaction keeps UUID). 4 new tests; 66 tests green across session + hooks surface. Live evidence: 2 chroma processes for this claude pid confirmed the leak; fix closes the last gap in the 4.10.3 three-layer defense.

title: SessionEnd hook recurring cancellation leaks T1 chroma servers (103 stale processes / 183 tmpdirs observed)
description:
The nx hook session-end SessionEnd hook registered at nx/hooks/hooks.json:35-46 is either hitting its 10s timeout or getting SIGKILLed by Claude Code's own shutdown deadline before it can run src/nexus/hooks.py::session_end's cleanup. Per-session T1 ChromaDB HTTP servers never get stopped, tmpdirs never get removed, and session records in ~/.config/nexus/sessions/ never get deleted. On 2026-04-23 the reference install had 103 live orphaned chroma processes (oldest 33h+) and 183 leftover tmpdirs in /var/folders/.../T/nx_t1_*, only 2 of which were attached to a currently-running Claude Code session.

Message format on abort: 'SessionEnd hook [nx hook session-end || true] failed: Hook cancelled'. The '|| true' safety valve never executes because Claude Code kills the subprocess, not the shell.

Likely causes (pick after instrumentation):
1. T2.expire() on a loaded production memory.db (105MB+ on the reference install) taking >10s
2. T1 flagged_entries scan + clear on a session with many scratch entries
3. stop_t1_server(pid) blocking on TERM/KILL cycle when the chroma process is busy
4. Claude Code's global shutdown deadline cutting the 10s timeout short

Forensics retained at /tmp/nxt1-forensics/ (forensics.txt, live_pids.txt, preserve.txt, kill.txt — the reap evidence). Reap command that was safe: for each session file in ~/.config/nexus/sessions/*.session extract server_pid; preserve those; SIGTERM every other nx_t1_* chroma PID; delete stale session files + tmpdirs.

Proposed fix directions (need /nx:brainstorming-gate before implementation):
- Split the hook into a fast 'signal shutdown' path that returns in <1s and a detached subprocess for the T1 server teardown
- Bump timeout to 30s and add a keepalive heartbeat so the hook can report progress
- Add a reaper invocation to SessionStart that kills any nx_t1_* chroma process whose server_pid does not appear in the live session records (orphan garbage collection)
- Add an 'nx doctor --reap-orphans' command for manual cleanup
acceptance_criteria: After an interactive /plugin reload or natural session close, zero new orphaned nx_t1_* chroma processes accumulate. A monitoring test that spawns and closes 10 mock sessions sees 0 orphans remaining. SessionStart runs an orphan reaper as a belt-and-braces safety net.
notes:
Web research 2026-04-23: confirmed upstream bug #41577 (closed as dup of #24206, will-not-fix). SessionEnd is killed before it completes; timeout is ignored. Also #17885: SessionEnd doesn't fire on /exit. Recipe is defense in depth — fix implementing layers 1+2+3:

LAYER 1 (primary): self-watchdog sidecar — chroma stays in its own setsid() group (preserving worker semaphore cleanup from beads nexus-dc57/ze2a) and a tiny detached Python sidecar watches the Claude Code root PID via os.kill(pid, 0) every 5s. On ProcessLookupError sends graceful SIGTERM to chroma via existing stop_t1_server(). Independent of hooks firing at all.

LAYER 2: detached SessionEnd — nx hook session-end-detach double-forks + exits in <50ms so Claude Code's shutdown kill misses it. The grandchild completes the existing session_end() cleanup synchronously. Fires faster than watchdog's 5s poll when the hook does run.

LAYER 3: aggressive sweep on SessionStart — extend sweep_stale_sessions() to reap records whose server_pid is no longer alive regardless of age (today only 24h+ get reaped; that's why 103 accumulated). Belt-and-braces.

Live evidence gathered 2026-04-23 and preserved at /tmp/nxt1-forensics/: forensics.txt (103 ps entries), live_pids.txt, preserve.txt, kill.txt.

title: seed_loader required_bindings fix benefits only new seeds, not existing rows
description: The nexus-80tk fix merges required_bindings/optional_bindings into plan_json at save_plan time. But the seeder short-circuits via get_plan_by_dimensions when a row with the same (project, dimensions) already exists — so rows seeded before 4.10.1 (the entire live deployment up to today) keep the old plan_json with no binding declarations, and _validate_bindings still finds an empty required_bindings list for them. Symptom: calling nx_answer against the pre-existing analyze-default row still leaks unresolved $area / $criterion into the bundle prompt even post-4.10.1 upgrade. Fix options: (a) migration that re-reads every builtin YAML and patches required_bindings/optional_bindings into the matching DB row's plan_json; (b) bump seed_loader to upsert-on-missing-bindings even when dimensions match; (c) one-shot delete-and-reseed for rows in the global tier whose tags identify them as builtin. Option (a) is safest because it's migration-scoped and idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: After nx upgrade, running nx_answer against analyze-default without area/criterion bindings raises PlanRunBindingError upfront instead of bundling unfilled $vars. Regression test seeds a plan with the old (no-binding) plan_json shape, runs the migration, and asserts bindings are backfilled.
close_reason: Closed

title: operator_summarize/rank/compare/generate 'inputs' arg not renamed when step pre-hydrated
description: _hydrate_operator_args only runs the inputs→{content,context,items} translation when the step args contain an 'ids' key (the auto-hydration trigger). Plan 57 find-by-author has a prior store_get_many step that already materializes content; its summarize step then passes 'inputs: $step2.contents' which resolves to the contents list. Since 'ids' isn't in args, the translation skips, inputs passes through, the unknown-kwarg drop strips it, and operator_summarize fires with no content → TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'content'. Same pattern breaks any isolated summarize/rank/compare/generate whose inputs come from an explicit hydration step rather than the auto-hydration path. Bundled operator chains don't hit it because the bundle prompt composer uses a different arg-presentation path. Fix: extend _hydrate_operator_args to also rename inputs→{content|context|items} based on resolved_tool when 'ids' is absent but 'inputs' is present.
acceptance_criteria: find-by-author plan executes end-to-end against a real author in T3 and returns a summary; a regression test seeds a 3-step plan with explicit store_get_many + summarize and asserts successful execution through _default_dispatcher.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ship nx/plans/*.yml as conexus wheel package data
description:
RDR-092 validation run surfaced a pre-existing deployment gap: the conexus wheel at pyproject.toml [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages only src/nexus, so installed CLIs (uv tool install etc.) cannot find nx/plans/builtin/*.yml from their site-packages. _seed_plan_templates's plugin_root = __file__.resolve().parent^4 / 'nx' points into site-packages where the directory never exists.

Phase 0c's fail-loud guard surfaced the issue in production; the immediate fix on commit-pending-PR #266-followup prefers <repo_root>/nx when run from a repo checkout, but that only covers dev + running-from-checkout flows.

The proper fix ships the plugin YAMLs as wheel package data so installed CLIs can read them via importlib.resources.files('nexus') traversal:

1. Update pyproject.toml:
   - Add nx/ and nx/plans/ to [tool.hatch.build.force-include] (or copy YAMLs into src/nexus/_plans_builtin/ at build time).
   - Or restructure so plan YAMLs live under src/nexus/plans/builtin/ and ship naturally with the wheel.

2. Update _seed_plan_templates to resolve plugin_root via importlib.resources instead of filesystem traversal.

3. Verify behavior:
   - Fresh uv tool install of conexus
   - nx catalog setup from any working directory
   - doctor --check-plan-library reports global builtin count >= 9

Coordination: the nx/ tree also carries agents, skills, commands, hooks — all consumed by Claude Code, which reads them FROM the repo at plugin-install time, NOT from the Python wheel. So moving YAMLs under src/nexus/ would split the plugin surface. Preferable path is force-include of nx/plans/*.yml into the wheel while keeping the Claude Code plugin structure intact at the repo level. Test this carefully — pyproject force-include semantics vary.
close_reason: Merged via PR #267. nx/plans/ now ships as wheel package data via hatch force-include (nx/plans -> nexus/_resources/plans). importlib.resources resolution works from any cwd; 'nx catalog setup' and 'nx doctor --check-plan-library' verified from /tmp (non-repo cwd) via installed CLI.

title: RDR-092 S-2 follow-up: dedup _synthesize_match_text across session_cache + plan_library
description:
Code-review S-2 finding from PR #262 + PR #263 review. Both PRs ship a _synthesize_match_text helper: session_cache uses a dict signature, plan_library uses explicit kwargs. Behaviorally identical today but duplicate code is a maintenance hazard for any future change to the hybrid shape.

Fix after both #262 and #263 merge:
1. Delete the session_cache.py implementation
2. Add a thin delegator that calls plan_library._synthesize_match_text with row dict unpacking:

   def _synthesize_match_text(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
       from nexus.db.t2.plan_library import _synthesize_match_text as _lib
       return _lib(
           description=row.get('query'),
           verb=row.get('verb'),
           name=row.get('name'),
           scope=row.get('scope'),
       )

3. Keep session_cache.py's public __all__ unchanged so any external imports still work.
4. Run tests/test_plan_session_cache_match_text.py + tests/test_plan_library.py; both suites should pass byte-for-byte.

Blocking: PR #262 and PR #263 must both merge to main first.
close_reason: Resolved inline on PR #266. Both Phase 1 (session_cache) and Phase 3 (plan_library) live on the same combined branch, so the cross-module refactor no longer has a merge-ordering constraint. session_cache._synthesize_match_text is now a thin adapter that unpacks the row dict into kwargs and calls plan_library._synthesize_match_text (the single source of truth). See commit on feature/rdr-092-full-implementation.

    def _synthesize_match_text(row: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        query = (row.get("query") or "").strip()

title: taxonomy projection: unify targets, warn on missing, refresh links after persist
description:
Fixes GitHub issues #238 + #239 + #240. Shared theme: taxonomy subsystem has several invariant-mismatches where subsystems disagree.

## #238 single-source vs backfill target-set disagreement

Root cause: project_cmd tries list_sibling_collections first (same-repo different-prefix collections), falls back to get_distinct_collections only when siblings is empty. Backfill always uses get_distinct_collections. For multi-repo multi-docs__ setups, siblings-first silently narrows the target set vs backfill.

Fix: drop the sibling-first heuristic in project_cmd. Always default to get_distinct_collections minus source. Users who want scoped targets use --against explicitly. Single-source and backfill now agree on the default target set.

## #239 status doesn't warn on zero projection

Root cause: status_cmd displays topic counts + review state but not projection assignments. After discover, a collection has topics (green-looking) but zero cross-collection projection data. User discovers the gap only via audit -c.

Fix: status_cmd now queries projection-assignment count per collection. Collections with 0 projection display 'no projection' inline, and an Action hint appears at end when any collection needs projection.

## #240 links view stale after project --persist

Root cause: topic_links table is written at discover time (_discover_cross_links, centroid-similarity pairs) and via links --refresh (compute_topic_links, catalog-derived). project --persist writes to topic_assignments but NOT to topic_links. links_cmd reads topic_links (stale), hubs_cmd reads live from topic_assignments (correct).

Fix: add CatalogTaxonomy.refresh_projection_links() that aggregates per-chunk projection assignments into topic pairs and upserts to topic_links with link_type='projection' merged into any existing types. Call at end of _persist_assignments (single path) and end of _run_backfill.

## Tests

- project_cmd single-source default targets == backfill target set (no siblings preference)
- status_cmd shows 'no projection' hint when collection has topics but zero projection
- refresh_projection_links upserts correctly-aggregated pairs and merges link_types

title: taxonomy: label includes split children; list shows collection; project help stale
description:
Fixes GitHub issues #243 + #241 on the nexus repo.

## #243 root cause

label_cmd calls get_topics() which returns ONLY root topics (parent_id IS NULL). Split sub-topics have parent_id=<parent>, so get_topics() hides them. label_cmd's early-exit check computes pending over the ROOT-only topic set. When all roots are accepted and only split children are pending, target=[] and the command bails with 'No topics to label', even though status correctly reports the 8 pending children.

Same bug on the --all path in relabel_topics: without collection, it uses get_topics() for the relabel_all=True branch.

## #241 items

1. list shows no collection column for topics. _print_tree prints 'label (N docs)' without the collection. Add [collection] prefix for root nodes (depth=0), consistent with hubs / links views.
2. project --help has a stale 'Threshold resolution → 0.70' line. Actual runtime default is per-prefix (0.70 code, 0.50 knowledge, 0.55 docs/rdr). Replace the stale line.
3. label auto-accepts topics (rename_topic sets review_status='accepted' as a side effect). This conflicts with the status action-prompt 'Run `nx taxonomy review`'. The rename_topic behavior is correct for review's interactive rename path; it is wrong for the batch LLM label path. Add update_topic_label (label only, no status transition) and make relabel_topics use it. After fix: label leaves topics pending, review transitions them to accepted.

## Fix

- catalog_taxonomy.py: add get_all_topics(collection='') returning root+children; add update_topic_label(topic_id, new_label)
- taxonomy_cmd.py: rewrite label_cmd early-exit to use get_unreviewed_topics (default) or get_all_topics (--all); _print_tree shows [collection] at root; project docstring cleanup
- taxonomy_cmd.py relabel_topics: replace get_topics()/rename_topic with get_all_topics()/update_topic_label
- tests: split → label sees children; label leaves review_status=pending; _print_tree includes collection at root

No migration. Pure CLI + query-layer fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: plan 51 author='arcaneum' catalog filter returns zero
description:
Grown plan 51 in the live library has its query step filter on:
  author='arcaneum', content_type='rdr'

Every RDR document in the catalog has author='' (empty). The
author field is never populated for indexed RDRs. Filter returns
zero, downstream extract gets empty input, generate honestly
reports 'nothing to synthesize'.

## Likely cause

Inline planner (_nx_answer_plan_miss) built this plan JSON and
hallucinated a non-existent author value. Either:
  (a) planner prompt doesn't tell it that author is commonly empty
      for RDR documents in this catalog, or
  (b) planner should prefer corpus=<collection> over catalog filters
      when the target is a specific project's RDRs.

## Investigation paths

- Check how _nx_answer_plan_miss composes its prompt: what hints
  does it give the planner about available metadata columns?
- Decide: is author= a useful filter for RDRs at all? If not, maybe
  the planner prompt should bias toward corpus=<name>.
- Audit other grown plans (bd list matching tags ad-hoc,grown) for
  the same broken filter.

## Workaround

Plan 52 (arcaneum-scoped) works: uses corpus='rdr__arcaneum-2ad2825c'
directly, bypassing the author filter. Plans that name a specific
collection are robust; plans that rely on catalog metadata filters
need the catalog to carry the filtered column.
close_reason: Closed

title: operator_compare: two-sided items_a/items_b for cross-corpus DAGs
description:
## Context

Cross-corpus composition is a post-5 claim ('how does Arcaneum talk about X vs
how does Nexus talk about X'). Running it surfaced two real gaps:

1. operator_compare takes a single `items` list. The AgenticScholar operator
   spec describes compare as inherently two-sided (A vs B), but the current
   implementation only supports one-sided (comparison WITHIN a set).
2. To get two-sided compare today, authors embed \$step6.extractions inside
   the focus prompt string — which doesn't substitute per the no-inline-
   interpolation rule. Compare then falls back to its training-data knowledge
   of one of the sides, producing partially-hallucinated output.

## Fix

Extend `operator_compare` (src/nexus/mcp/core.py) with optional kwargs:
  - items_a, items_b: two sets to compare
  - label_a, label_b: human labels (default 'A'/'B')

Two-sided branch fires when both items_a and items_b are non-empty. Prompt
becomes 'Compare set {label_a} vs set {label_b}...'. One-sided behavior with
only `items` preserved unchanged.

Also JSON-serialize list/dict values in items/items_a/items_b before prompt
interpolation — currently a list passed in stringifies with Python repr
(single quotes, ugly). json.dumps is cleaner for the LLM.

## Bonus finding to file separately

Plan 51 (grown plan for Arcaneum tradeoffs) has `author='arcaneum'` as a
catalog filter in its query step. Every RDR in the catalog has author=''
(empty), so plan 51 returns zero results and falls into the 'nothing
extracted' generate branch. Inline-planner hallucinated a filter column
that isn't populated. Separate bead.

## Files

- src/nexus/mcp/core.py — operator_compare signature + prompt
- tests/test_operators.py — one-sided regression + two-sided test
- docs/plan-authoring-guide.md — compare two-sided pattern
close_reason: Closed
