title: [RDR-100 referral] Grown plan at 0.94 confidence dropped by scope-anchor filter — the real cause of the nx_answer verbatim-repeat miss (dilution REFUTED)
description:
Referral from nexus-nyry9.1 (RDR-196 .r1, DIAGNOSIS-ONLY). Plan-matching semantics are RDR-100's; nyry9.1 changed no source (fence verified empty on match_text.py / matcher.py / session_cache.py / http_plan_library.py).

Full measurement record: T2 nexus_rdr/196-residual-1-matchtext-dilution [23012].

## The referred hypothesis is REFUTED, and a real defect was found instead

nyry9.1 was asked to quantify `_synthesize_match_text` dilution (src/nexus/plans/match_text.py:16-54). Measured with the live embedder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384d, cosine; confidence == cosine similarity per matcher.py:502):

- Dilution is real but tiny: 21/21 live plans lose confidence, mean -0.0340, range -0.0075..-0.0600.
- Plan 357, verbatim repeat: cos(bare query) 1.0000 -> cos(synthesized) 0.9400. The grown floor is 0.55 (matcher.py:77). It clears by 0.39 — ~6.5x the entire dilution.
- Ranking: plan 357 is #1 in BOTH worlds (0.940 vs runner-up 0.240, ~0.70 gap).
- Plans 12/15 (match_count 53/37, use_count 0): absolute cosines -0.0012..0.1914, below the 0.40 floor in BOTH worlds; 3 of 5 deltas POSITIVE. Removing the suffix changes no outcome.

So matcher.py:509-513's comment — 'the hybrid match-text embedding ... dilutes cosine similarity even for an exact repeat, which is exactly what let an unrelated higher-scoring candidate win' — is measured FALSE, and currently records that inference as fact.

## The actual cause (live log, closed elimination)

~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log, 3.2s into run 382:

    2026-08-19T18:31:06.686401Z nexus.plans.matcher INFO
      event='plan_match_scope_conflict_fallthrough' t1_hits=20 dropped=1 scope_pref='knowledge'

1. The T1 cosine path RAN (substrate created 18:31:03.51, 20 hits) — not cache-unavailable.
2. _log_t1_drops (matcher.py:180-208) emits this ONLY when `scored` ended empty.
3. Exactly 1 candidate dropped as scope conflict; the other 19 fell to the 0.40 floor — corroborated exactly by the cosine table (every plan but 357 scores <=0.240 against that question).
4. Plan 357 scores 0.9400, clears the 0.55 grown floor, matches the verb dimension, is not always-failing, and no _log_binding_drops line appeared. Therefore plan 357 IS the dropped=1.

Plan 357 was dropped by the scope filter at matcher.py:551-560 at ~0.94 confidence. Two exits increment that counter:
- (i) _is_unanchored_grown (matcher.py:155-159): grown tag AND empty scope_tags AND blank project. STRONGLY INDICATED — reachable via http_plan_library.py:138-140, where scope_tags passed as '' (not None) takes the else branch, stores '', and SKIPS _infer_scope_tags entirely.
- (ii) _scope_fit conflict (matcher.py:251-298): WEAKLY INDICATED — it iterates all tags and returns 1.0 on the first prefix hit, and plan 357's plan_json names literal corpus 'knowledge' which inference would collect.

The decisive evidence is unrecoverable: run 382's plan_save UPSERTED plan 357, overwriting the pre-382 row, resetting match_count/use_count to 0 and re-stamping created_at to 2026-08-19T18:32:18Z. Those counters carry no information about pre-382 state.

Plan 357 WAS allocated 08-11 by row 376 — proven by BIGSERIAL monotonicity: 355(08-09) < 356(08-10) < 357 < 358(08-14) < 359(08-14) < 360(08-14). The plan existed with the byte-identical query and run 382 missed it anyway.

## Corollary: the shipped a2 fix does not cover this class

The verbatim-repeat override (matcher.py:505-517) sets confidence=1.0, and its own comment at :515-517 says it 'Deliberately does NOT bypass the always-failing skip or the scope-conflict filter below — only the CONFIDENCE floors'. The scope filter runs AFTER. a2 structurally cannot rescue a scope-anchor drop, so the fix written for row 382 does not address row 382's actual cause.

Also: grow-then-hit works in general — plan 360 grown at row 379 (08-14T17:14) then HIT at rows 380/381 (match_count 2, use_count 2). h33x8.6 follow-on defect #4 ('plan-match misses verbatim repeats of the question that grew the plan') is false in its general form; the failure is specific to unanchored / scope-conflicting grown plans.

## Recommended work (RDR-100 owner decides)

1. Make grown-plan saves always anchor: at http_plan_library.py:126-140 treat scope_tags='' from the grow path as None (run _infer_scope_tags), or make the grow path pass None. Consider letting a verbatim-repeat candidate bypass _is_unanchored_grown — a byte-identical question has provenance by construction. Regression to pin: grown plan + scoped caller + verbatim repeat -> HIT.
2. Correct the measured-false causal claim in matcher.py:509-513.
3. Do NOT chase dilution as a matching fix — 0.03 mean is inert against a 0.40/0.55 floor. If touched at all, embed the bare description for T1 cosine and keep the hybrid string as the T2 FTS payload only. Low value.
4. match_text.py:52 cosmetic: desc.rstrip('.') strips periods only, so question-shaped descriptions yield '...chunks?. research ...'. Every grown plan carries it. Not causal. One-line fix: strip '.?!'.
5. Plans 12/15 never-selected is separate from both: builtin template descriptions are semantically distant from real questions (max observed 0.19 vs a 0.40 floor). Fix is rewriting seed descriptions, not the matcher.

title: [RDR-100 referral] Grown plans are unmatchable by construction: match_text is the verbatim originating question + a slug of that same question, with no generalized description
description:
Referred from nexus-nyry9.3 (RDR-196 residual .r3, DIAGNOSIS-ONLY). Plan naming/promotion semantics are RDR-100's surface; RDR-196 § Approach excludes changing plan matching semantics, so .r3 measured and referred rather than fixing. Suspected code surface: src/nexus/plans/promote.py (naming) and whatever composes match_text on promotion — NOT read or changed by .r3, named here for RDR-100 to confirm.

## Evidence (measured 2026-08-20, read-only nx plan show, production library)

BUILTIN plans carry a hand-written GENERALIZED match_text — a description plus paraphrase exemplars:
- plan 15 abstract-themes: 'What are the main themes? What are the key findings? What are the dominant topics? Summarize this corpus. Give an overview. ...'
- plan 14 type-scoped-search: 'Search within a single content type (code, paper, rdr, knowledge). Routes through the catalog to ...'

GROWN plans (tags=ad-hoc,grown) carry match_text of the form '<verbatim originating question>. <verb> <slug-of-that-same-question> scope personal':
- 360: 'What different approaches to membership churn are described across the Delos papers?. research different-approaches-membership-churn-described scope personal'
- 357: 'What is the chunk identity convention used for T3 chunks?. research chunk-identity-convention-used-t3 scope personal'
- 358: 'Which nexus client code paths call catalog manifest write_many and do they supply the collection field per manifest row after RDR-191 GATE-2?. research nexus-client-code-paths-call scope personal'
- 356: 'What prior findings exist about jitterbug LGA contact ribbon aliasing, member quanta stride thresholds, or the ~10 quanta aliasing estimate in the inviscid project?. research prior-findings-exist-jitterbug-lga scope personal'
- 355: inline-vs-bind-rule-jooq (same shape)
- 359: audit-docs-architecture-md-docs — match_text is an entire multi-paragraph audit prompt pinning a specific commit range v7.6.1..HEAD, unmatchable by construction

The name adds no generality: it is a content-word slug of the very question already present verbatim in the same string. So a grown plan's ENTIRE matchable surface is one question instance, doubled.

## Measured consequence

- 6 of 6 grown plans have match_count 0 except 360, which matched only its own question, twice (use_count 2, success_count 2).
- Across all 21 plan ids ever executed (nx_answer_runs, 182 runs): distinct-question histogram {0 q: 5, 1 q: 14, 2 q: 2, >=3 q: 0}. No plan in recorded history ever served 3 distinct questions.
- High-volume plans generalized least: id 66 = 26 runs / 1 distinct question, 67 = 20/1, 80 = 10/1, 52 = 9/1, 38 = 6/1 — volume is the same question re-run, not a second question matching.

## Suggested direction (RDR-100 decides)

Promotion should synthesize a GENERALIZED match surface, not echo the instance: a described capability plus paraphrase exemplars (the builtin shape), a name derived from the plan's step shape / verb / scope rather than the question's content words, and a refusal or quarantine for promotion candidates whose question carries instance-specific anchors (commit ranges, bead ids, corpus-specific proper nouns) — plan 359 is the clear case.

## Consumer impact

Blocks nothing today, but it is the mechanism behind RDR-196 .p3b's refuted design assumption: with no plan generalizing, per-plan cost history never accumulates and cost-ranked plan choice has nothing to rank. Detail: T2 nexus_rdr/196-residual-3-grown-plan-generality [23009].

title: RDR-196 .p4 (Phase 4, CONDITIONAL): cheap-first escalate-on-low-confidence for verify/check — opens ONLY on a .p2d negative; closing as not-needed is a legitimate outcome
description:
RDR-196 **Phase 4 — OPTIONAL AND CONDITIONAL.** This bead may legitimately
close as NOT-NEEDED without any code.

## The gate (RDR § Approach Phase 4, verbatim intent)

> Only if Phase 2 shows the cheap tier is *not* good enough for verify/check on
> its own.

`.p2d` records that verdict explicitly. Read it first. Two outcomes:

- Cheap tier IS good enough for `verify`/`check` -> **close this bead as
  not-needed**. That is a legitimate close and it is the cheaper world.
- Cheap tier is NOT good enough -> this bead opens, and the escalate loop is
  the ONE topology transformation the paper actually measured.

## What ships (only if the gate opens)

For `verify` / `check`: dispatch on the cheap model first; escalate to the
strong model **only when the cheap verdict is low-confidence**, as a BOUNDED
loop. NOMA's measurement: cheap-first + escalate dominated the best
fixed-topology plan at equal quality.

Reuse, do not invent: RDR-190 (draft) defines `loop` / `collect` plan-IR
primitives — the RDR says use them **if landed**, otherwise a runner-local
bounded retry. Check RDR-190's status before designing anything.

## ⚠ Scope fence

This is ONE bounded transformation. It is NOT the generative planner (NOMA
§5.1) and NOT the continuous Bayesian refiner (§5.3) — both explicitly out of
scope for RDR-196. If the design starts choosing among topologies rather than
executing this one, STOP: that is a new RDR.

## DO (if opened)

1. `sequentialthinking` first: define "low-confidence" as a computable
   predicate on the cheap tier's OWN structured output. `operator_check`
   returns `{ok, evidence[]}` and `operator_verify` returns
   `{verified, reason, citations[]}` — decide which field carries the
   confidence signal. If neither does, the escalate trigger has no input and
   this bead needs a design step before an implementation step.
2. **TDD, red first**: a low-confidence cheap verdict escalates exactly once;
   a confident cheap verdict does NOT escalate; the loop is bounded (assert the
   maximum dispatch count — an unbounded escalate loop is a cost incident).
3. Measure against `.p2a`'s proxy and `.p1e`'s telemetry: escalate-on-demand
   must beat all-strong on cost at >= equal agreement. If it does not, record
   the negative result and revert — same rule as `.p2d`.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] `.p2d`'s verify/check verdict is quoted in this bead before any work.
- [ ] If NOT-NEEDED: closed with that verdict cited. No code.
- [ ] If opened: a test asserts the loop is BOUNDED (max dispatch count).
- [ ] A test asserts a confident cheap verdict does NOT escalate — otherwise
      the "optimization" is strictly two dispatches instead of one.
- [ ] Cost-vs-agreement measured against all-strong; a non-improvement is
      reverted, not shipped.
- [ ] RDR-190 status checked and recorded (reused its primitive, or documented
      why a runner-local retry instead).

## Depends

`.p2d` (the gate verdict).

Commit on develop.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## AUDIT FOLD F1 (MUST-FIX, nx_plan_audit 2026-08-20) — and a LARGER finding it uncovered

**The audit is right and understates it.** `src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py:1559` builds its OWN argv:
```
argv = _argv or ["claude", "-p", "--output-format", "json"]
```
Aspect extraction NEVER goes through `claude_dispatch`. Three consequences, only the first of which the audit named:

1. **.p1a's envelope capture never reaches this call site**, so this bead cannot be satisfied by .p1a as originally wired.
2. **⚠ Phase 0 Gap 4 is NOT actually closed for `nx enrich aspects`.** The LANDED fix (f1ae257d0) added `--strict-mcp-config` to `claude_dispatch`'s argv ONLY. This argv has none. But RDR-196 Gap 4 states the overhead is paid by "Every nx_answer step, **`nx enrich aspects` extraction**, `nx_tidy` and the inline planner" — so for one of the four named consumers, Phase 0 is still open, and every aspect extraction is still paying the ~2x context/cost overhead 196-R2 measured ($1.84 vs $0.91). The RDR currently marks Phase 0 LANDED. **This must reach the RDR text** — see the epic comment.
3. **`--output-format json` is the buffering mode h33x8.6 diagnosed as making partial-output capture structurally vacuous** (a killed subprocess writes ZERO bytes always, by construction). dispatch.py moved to stream-json at dca12e1e3; this call site did not.

So aspect_extractor is a SECOND, un-modernized `claude -p` call site that missed all three recent dispatch improvements.

## The scope decision this bead now owns

**Option A (RECOMMENDED) — re-route aspect extraction through `claude_dispatch`.** One move fixes all three: strict-mcp-config, stream-json, and usage capture. **Blast radius**: aspect_extractor.py is consumed by `nx enrich aspects` and the aspect-queue worker daemon (`daemon/aspect_worker_daemon.py`); it has its own prompt/schema shape and its own timeout behaviour, and `claude_dispatch`'s defaults (300s, tool-free) must be checked against them before switching. Run `jet_brains_find_referencing_symbols` on the extraction entry point first. If the shapes do not fit, say so and take Option B rather than bending claude_dispatch to fit one caller.

**Option B — scope .p0b to parse aspect_extractor's own result envelope in place.** Cheaper, leaves consequences 2 and 3 open (which then need their own beads — do NOT leave them in prose).

**Record the chosen option and its reasoning in this bead's close reason.** The .7 (.p1a) dependency stands under either option: under A it is a hard prerequisite; under B it is the source of the fixture/field knowledge.

## Added VERIFICATION lines

- [ ] The chosen option is recorded with its reasoning; under B, follow-up beads exist for consequences 2 and 3 and their ids are named here.
- [ ] Under A: `grep -n '"claude", "-p"' src/nexus/` returns exactly ONE call site (dispatch.py:677). Two means the re-route did not happen.
- [ ] A test asserts `nx enrich aspects` dispatches with `--strict-mcp-config` (closing the real Gap 4 for this consumer) — or, under B, a bead exists that will.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## F1 scope decision: Option B (parse in place, do NOT reroute through claude_dispatch)

**Reasoning** (verified via jet_brains_find_referencing_symbols on
_run_claude_isolated + reading aspect_extractor.py's own module docstring
and daemon/aspect_worker_daemon.py):

1. aspect_extractor.py is an RDR-089 LOAD-BEARING synchronous contract
   (module docstring, lines 3-11): "no async def, no await, no event
   loop... so the document-grain hook chain (HookRegistry.fire_document)
   can call it from a sync dispatcher without dropping a coroutine."
   claude_dispatch (operators/dispatch.py:728) is async-only
   (asyncio.create_subprocess_exec) with no sync wrapper anywhere in the
   codebase.
2. daemon/aspect_worker_daemon.py is thread-based (threading.Thread for
   heartbeat/reclaim) -- no asyncio event loop exists anywhere in the
   daemon to host an async claude_dispatch call.
3. aspect_extractor._run_claude_isolated carries a load-bearing
   PR_SET_PDEATHSIG preexec_fn (RDR-173 RF-8 / nexus-4r9ja) so the
   daemon's own SIGKILL death cannot orphan the claude subprocess.
   claude_dispatch has NO equivalent -- only a timeout-triggered killpg.
   Rerouting would silently regress an incident-driven safety guarantee.

These are real architectural blockers (sync-contract violation + safety
regression), not mere inconvenience -- matching this bead's own escape
hatch ("if the shapes do not fit, say so and take Option B").

**Consequence 2 (Gap 4 / --strict-mcp-config): FIXED directly in this
bead.** aspect_extractor.py:1559's default argv now carries
--strict-mcp-config (cheap, no architecture conflict -- this call is
tool-free by construction). Test:
tests/test_aspect_extractor_subprocess_isolation.py::test_default_argv_carries_strict_mcp_config.

**Consequence 3 (buffered --output-format json is structurally vacuous
for partial-output capture on timeout): left open, follow-up bead
nexus-rhwbx filed** (blocked-by this bead).

**Consequence 1 / Part B's measurement dependency on .p1a:** since
aspect_extractor does not itself capture DispatchUsage telemetry under
Option B, .p1a serves as "the source of the fixture/field knowledge" per
this bead's own comment wording -- claude_dispatch (already landed,
tested, usage-instrumented) was used as a one-off MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT
(not a production reroute) to dispatch one real aspect-extraction-shaped
prompt and record real DispatchUsage. See
tests/test_aspect_extraction_cost_measurement.py.

Two permanent "claude", "-p" call sites remain under Option B
(operators/dispatch.py and aspect_extractor.py) -- this is the intended,
documented state, not an incomplete re-route.

## Part B: _PER_PAPER_COST_USD

Chose (a) measured constant with provenance comment (not (b) history-
derived): aspect_extractor does not write to Phase 1 telemetry history
under Option B, so there is no per-extraction history to read from --
(b) would defeat its own purpose here. Measured cost_usd=1.179986,
canonical model=claude-fable-5, via one real dispatch of the SAME
_SCHOLARLY_PAPER_PROMPT template through claude_dispatch (no --model
override, matching production). New value: _PER_PAPER_COST_USD = 1.18
(~118x the old 0.01 literal). Also fixed the "at Haiku rates" CLI text
(FALSE -- production never passes --model) to name the real basis.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## CORRECTION (2026-08-20, code-review-expert APPROVE + substantive-critic review)

Stacked review found my prior comment's Blocker 1 factually wrong and
Blocker 2 mischaracterized. Corrected reasoning for Option B:

- **Blocker 1 was WRONG**: `HookRegistry.fire_document` does NOT call
  `extract_aspects` inline -- it only ENQUEUES (aspect_worker.py:1054's
  own docstring says so). The real synchronous callers are
  `aspect_worker.py:571` (the worker-thread extraction loop) and
  `commands/enrich.py:1363` (this CLI's own extraction loop).
- **Blocker 2 was mischaracterized**: the daemon being thread-based with
  no existing event loop is exactly when `asyncio.run()` is SAFE to use
  (no loop to conflict with), not a blocker.
- **Blocker 3 stands and is the real justification**: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG
  parity. `aspect_extractor.py`'s `Popen` call (~1572-1580) arms parent-
  death protection for the aspect-worker daemon (RDR-173 RF-8 /
  nexus-4r9ja: the daemon's own SIGKILL cannot orphan the claude
  subprocess). `claude_dispatch`'s `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` call
  (operators/dispatch.py:943-948) has NO equivalent. Rerouting through
  claude_dispatch would silently regress this incident-driven safety
  guarantee. Option B stands on this reason alone.

Option B itself (do not reroute), the Gap-4 fix (--strict-mcp-config),

title: RDR-196 .r3 (residual, DIAGNOSIS-ONLY): grown plans do not generalize — census the library and decide whether cost-ranked choice (.p3b) has a rankable population
description:
RDR-196 arc, inherited residual **3 of 5** from the CLOSED bead nexus-h33x8.6.

## ⚠ SCOPE FENCE — DIAGNOSIS AND REFERRAL ONLY

Plan naming and promotion are plan-library semantics. RDR-196 § Approach
excludes "any change to plan matching semantics (RDR-100 owns that)". This bead
measures and refers; it changes no promotion behaviour. Landing a promote.py
naming change here is silent scope expansion.

## The observation

`nx plan list` = 21 plans. Six are one-off "grown" plans from a single
2026-08-14 session with hyper-specific names
(e.g. `different-approaches-membership-churn-described`) that cannot generalize
to a second question. Plans 15 and 12 show match_count 33/47 against use_count
0 — repeatedly considered as candidates, never selected.

This matters to RDR-196 specifically because **Phase 3 (.p3b) ranks plans by
recorded median cost**. A library where most entries are single-use grown plans
has no cost history per plan to rank ON, and cost-ranked choice degrades to
the no-history warning path for nearly every query. So the generalization
question is a direct input to whether `.p3b` can work at all.

## DO

1. `sequentialthinking` first.
2. Census the current library: for each plan record `{id, name, step shape,
   match_count, use_count, distinct questions that matched it}`. Numbers, not
   adjectives.
3. Answer ONE question with those numbers: **how many plans have >= N distinct
   successful runs** (pick and state N; N=3 is the natural floor for a median).
   That count is the population `.p3b` can rank. If it is near zero, `.p3b`'s
   design assumption is refuted and `.p3b` must be re-scoped or deferred —
   record that as the finding.
4. Write to T2 `nexus_rdr/196-residual-3-grown-plan-generality`, and file ONE
   referral bead for the naming/promotion fix under RDR-100's ownership.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] The census table exists in T2 with real per-plan counts.
- [ ] The "plans with >= N runs" count is stated as a number, and its
      consequence for `.p3b` is stated as either SUPPORTED or REFUTED.
- [ ] `.p3b`'s bead carries a comment recording that answer.
- [ ] `git diff` on `src/nexus/plans/promote.py` and `match_text.py` is EMPTY.

## Execution notes

- SPAWN `conexus:deep-analyst`. Read the DEV plan library, never production
  (nexus-a2qhz).
notes: Referral bead: nexus-93cc6. Verdict comment on nexus-nyry9.20. Structural blockers for .p3b beyond empty population: cost_usd=0 on 182/182 runs (awaits Phase 1); plan_id not reseed-stable (114/182 runs orphaned).
close_reason: REFUTED: 0 of 22 live plans have >=3 distinct successful runs (0 at N=2). Census in T2 nexus_rdr/196-residual-3-grown-plan-generality. Diagnosis-only; five-file fence empty.

comments.text:
## .r3 COMPLETE (diagnosis-only) — verdict REFUTED

N = 3 distinct successful executed runs. **Plans with >= 3: 0.** At N=2, also 0 for live rows. All-time across the 21 plan ids ever executed: distinct-question histogram {0 q: 5, 1 q: 14, 2 q: 2, >=3 q: 0} — no plan in recorded history ever served 3 distinct questions, and only one (id 125, since deleted) served 2 genuinely distinct ones.

Consequence for .p3b (cost-ranked plan choice): **REFUTED**. Recorded as a comment on nexus-nyry9.20.

Census table (22 live plans, per-plan step shape + match_count/use_count/success_count/failure_count), distinct-question attribution from nx_answer_runs (182 runs), and the mechanism evidence: T2 nexus_rdr/196-residual-3-grown-plan-generality [23009].

Two structural blockers found beyond the empty population, both design inputs to .p3b (recorded in T2 and on .p3b, NOT filed as separate beads): cost_usd is 0.00 on 182/182 runs, and 114/182 runs (63%) point at plan ids no longer in the library, so plan_id is not a reseed-stable ranking key.

Referral bead (RDR-100 ownership, deliverable 3): **nexus-93cc6** — grown plans are unmatchable by construction; their match_text is the verbatim originating question plus a content-word slug of that same question, with no generalized description or paraphrase exemplars, unlike the builtin plans.

FENCE (F2) HELD: git diff --stat is EMPTY for match_text.py, matcher.py, session_cache.py, http_plan_library.py, promote.py. No source read-modified, no git add/commit/stash/checkout. title: RDR-196 .r1 (residual, DIAGNOSIS-ONLY): root-cause the plan-match miss on verbatim repeats — quantify _synthesize_match_text dilution, refer the fix to RDR-100
description:
RDR-196 arc, inherited residual **1 of 5** from the CLOSED bead nexus-h33x8.6
(follow-on defect #4 and #6 in T2 nexus/nx-answer-capability-analysis-2026-08-19
[22886]).

## ⚠ SCOPE FENCE — this bead is DIAGNOSIS AND REFERRAL, not a fix

RDR-196 § Approach explicitly excludes "any change to plan matching semantics
(RDR-100 owns that)". `_synthesize_match_text` builds the text that is embedded
and matched against, so changing it IS a matching-semantics change. This bead
therefore produces a root-cause record + a referral bead, and changes NO
matching behaviour. Landing a matcher fix under this bead is silent scope
expansion and must be refused at review.

## The observation (measured, not inferred)

2026-08-19 live run, row id=382: the question "What is the chunk identity
convention used for T3 chunks?" was asked VERBATIM — it is byte-identical to
the question that GREW plan 357 five days earlier (row 376, 2026-08-11) — and
the plan-match gate still missed, costing a 29.8s inline-planner dispatch
(40.1% of that 74.3s run). Across the corpus the miss tax is ~53s at p50
(plan-HIT p50 64.1s vs plan-MISS p50 117.2s, n=142).

A verbatim-repeat shortcut shipped separately (h33x8.6 a2) and covers the exact
byte-identical case. It does NOT explain or fix the underlying dilution: plans
15 and 12 show match_count 33/47 against use_count 0 — repeatedly considered,
never selected.

## DO

1. `mcp__plugin_conexus_sequential-thinking__sequentialthinking` first: state the
   dilution hypothesis and what evidence would falsify it BEFORE reading code.
2. Read `_synthesize_match_text` in `src/nexus/plans/matcher.py` (locate it; the
   h33x8.6 analysis names it as the root-cause site). Record exactly WHICH
   fields it concatenates into the embedded text and in what proportion.
3. Quantify the dilution rather than asserting it: for plans 12, 15 and 357,
   compute the cosine distance of the grown question against (a) today's
   synthesized match text and (b) the bare stored `query` string. If (b) is
   materially closer for the questions that missed, the dilution hypothesis is
   supported; if not, it is REFUTED and this bead records the refutation and
   stops.
4. Write the finding to T2 (`nexus_rdr/196-residual-1-matchtext-dilution`) with
   the numbers, classification (verified | refuted), and the recommended change
   for whoever owns it.
5. File ONE referral bead against RDR-100's ownership carrying the finding.
   Do not implement it here.

## VERIFICATION (falsifiable)

- [ ] A T2 record exists naming `_synthesize_match_text` at a concrete file:line
      and listing the concatenated fields verbatim.
- [ ] Cosine numbers for >=3 real plans are recorded for BOTH text variants —
      not a description of what they would be. A record with no numbers fails.
- [ ] The finding is explicitly classified verified OR refuted. "Likely" fails.
- [ ] `git diff` against `src/nexus/plans/matcher.py` is EMPTY for this bead.
      Any matcher-behaviour change here is a scope-fence violation.
- [ ] A referral bead id is recorded in this bead's close reason.

## Execution notes

- SPAWN a `conexus:deep-analyst` subagent for the measurement; do not grind it
  inline at top level.
- Read-only on the repo. Use the DEV checkout's plan library, never the
  production one (nexus-a2qhz: no structural guard stops a dev process writing
  the production T2/plan library).
- Update continuation state in T2 when the measurement lands.
notes: Referral bead (RDR-100 scope): nexus-7g0rg. Downstream: (1) a2 verbatim override does NOT cover run 382 (scope filter runs after it); (2) plan_save upserts reset match/use counts and created_at, so match_count-vs-use_count is unsafe evidence on re-saved plans; (3) grow-then-hit works for anchored plans (plan 360).
close_reason: REFUTED: dilution measured real but inert (self-match mean -0.034; plan 357 scores 0.94 vs 0.55 floor, #1 in both worlds). Real cause of the verbatim miss: scope-anchor filter drops unanchored grown plans (matcher.py:551-560 / _is_unanchored_grown :155-159), which runs AFTER the a2 verbatim override. Record T2 nexus_rdr/196-residual-1-matchtext-dilution. Diagnosis-only; fence empty.

It builds "<description>. <verb> <name> [scope <scope>]" at ~:44-51 and FALLS BACK to the bare description when verb or name is missing — that no-verb/no-name fallback is the concrete dilution root-cause CANDIDATE to test first. title: reinstall-tool holder classifier misses children of cyclable daemons (mineru multiprocessing pair) — attributes them as unrecognized and refuses
description: During 7.12.0 Step 12 (2026-08-19), scripts/reinstall-tool.sh refused twice: mineru-api (a daemon the script auto-cycles) had multiprocessing resource_tracker + spawn_main children (pids 85605/85606, PPID=72485=mineru-api). Workaround used: kill -TERM the mineru parent (reaps children), then rerun.

title: Wire-contract ledger: verify Shipped entries' shipped_in tag against real git tags
description: Both reviewers of the nexus-55r6o follow-up (v7.11.0 release, Shipped-counts-as-declared widening of check_wire_contract_pairing.py::_sha_declared) flagged the same gap: a ## Shipped entry's shipped_in tag value is parsed but never verified anywhere — an entry moved to Shipped prematurely (e.g. on develop, or naming a tag that never ships) silently satisfies all three ledger consumers forever. The client half itself cannot be missing (both halves live in one commit, flagged commits are HEAD-reachable), so the hole is bookkeeping-truth, not deploy safety. Design note: verification must tolerate the legitimate release-PR window where the named tag does not exist yet — e.g. flag a Shipped entry only when its named tag EXISTS and the sha is NOT an ancestor of it, or when the tag is older than N releases and still absent. See scripts/check_wire_contract_pairing.py evaluate()/is_ancestor for the existing stale-check machinery to reuse.

title: nx collection reindex leaves the catalog_collections registry row deleted for docs__/knowledge__/rdr__ collections (t3_not_in_projection drift)
description:
Discovered while validating nexus-sjb52's reroute of reindex_cmd's delete hop to purge_collection_cascade(db, name).

purge_collection_cascade deletes the nexus.catalog_collections registry row for the collection (CascadeCounts.catalog_projection_deleted, service-side deleteCollectionTxn deletes FROM catalog_collections WHERE name=...). For rdr__/docs__/knowledge__ collections, the subsequent re-index (batch_index_markdowns / index_markdown / index_pdf) DOES rebuild nexus.catalog_documents rows via _catalog_markdown_hook / _register_or_lookup_doc_id -- confirmed by reading doc_indexer.py and the engine's registerDocument (which never touches catalog_collections). But nothing in the re-index path calls register_collection / POST /collections/upsert to restore the catalog_collections registry row itself.

register_collection is called from: nexus/indexer.py (repo-migration path), commands/index.py (index repo), commands/catalog_cmds/migration.py, commands/catalog_cmds/collections.py (rename/backfill). It is NEVER called from doc_indexer.py's index_markdown/index_pdf/batch_index_markdowns, nor from commands/collection.py's reindex_cmd.

Net effect: after 'nx collection reindex docs__foo' (or knowledge__/rdr__), the T3 chunks and catalog_documents rows come back, searchable and catalogued -- but the collection now has NO catalog_collections registry row (content_type/owner_id/embedding_model/model_version/legacy_grandfathered all gone). Confirmed via code reading against commands/catalog_cmds/doctor.py's _run_collections_drift: the collection will show up in 'nx catalog doctor --collections-drift' under t3_not_in_projection (a T3 collection present with no matching catalog_collections registry row) until something else re-registers it.

Secondary risk for a previously-renamed/version-bumped collection (model_version > 1): the missing row means a FUTURE collection_for() tuple lookup 404s and treats the tuple as brand new, minting v1 -- silently reusing/colliding with the wrong version for that owner/content_type/embedding_model going forward, rather than continuing at the collection's actual version.

Fix: reindex_cmd should call writer.register_collection(name, ...) (mirroring the fields purge_collection_cascade deleted, or simply re-deriving from CollectionName.parse(name) since conformant names encode content_type/owner_id/embedding_model/model_version in the name itself) after a successful re-index, so the cascade's catalog_collections deletion does not outlive the operation it was part of.
acceptance_criteria: nx collection reindex on a docs__/knowledge__/rdr__ collection leaves nx catalog doctor --collections-drift clean for that collection (no t3_not_in_projection entry) afterward.
close_reason: Closed

title: probe_managed_service has no retry -- auto-paired mode probes during the live-redeploy window
description: code-review round on nexus-gc9ir (--paired-deploy-auto for scripts/check_engine_release_floor.py) flagged: probe_managed_service (src/nexus/db/managed_endpoint.py) has no retry, and --paired-deploy-auto's below-floor branch (_check_floor_auto_paired) runs it during the paired-release choreography's live-redeploy window -- a transient network blip or a mid-redeploy connection reset during that window could report ManagedServiceUnreachable and fail the release.yml publish closed on pure timing noise, not real drift. Reviewer's rationale: this is a narrower, orthogonal concern from nexus-gc9ir's scope (deciding WHICH verification path applies) -- a retry/backoff on the single probe_managed_service call belongs as its own small, reviewable change, not folded into the auto-mode routing logic. Do not implement inline in nexus-gc9ir; this bead tracks it separately. Reference: nexus-gc9ir.

title: Reviewer falsification edits on shared uncommitted trees can clobber the diff under review: 35ok4 round-1 corpus.py edit silently reverted to HEAD by a reviewer's 'revert'
description: 2026-08-18, nexus-35ok4 review cycle: code-review-expert made a temporary falsification edit to src/nexus/corpus.py (legitimate technique) and 'reverted' it — afterwards the file was byte-identical to develop HEAD, i.e. the revert used git checkout/HEAD-restore and destroyed the DEVELOPER'S uncommitted round-1 diff, not just the reviewer's own edit. Developer round 2 had to re-apply from scratch (caught only because the developer diffed before editing). Same family as the subagent-stash hazard (guard hook exists for stash). Fix candidates: (a) reviewer/critic briefing convention — falsification edits restore by re-writing the exact prior content (snapshot first), NEVER git checkout/restore on a dirty shared tree; (b) extend the existing git-policy guard to deny 'git checkout --/git restore' on paths with unstaged modifications from subagent contexts; (c) orchestration skill note. Evidence: 35ok4 dev round-2 report + reviewer's own 'confirmed via git diff empty after revert' line.

title: Local install: switching local.embed_model to voyage-* orphans pre-existing bge/minilm data (engine-side voyage-only-mode-flip AND client-side stale-bge-after-keyed-write)
description:
Follow-up scope explicitly deferred from nexus-35ok4 (GH #1461 fix).

Main.java's storage-service boot logic is binary: if NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is present in the spawned engine's environment, EmbedderRouter is constructed in PURE-VOYAGE mode (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/Main.java ~line 125-162) — no local ONNX embedder at all. If a local install has pre-existing bge-768/minilm-384 collections and the user then sets local.embed_model=voyage-* + voyage_api_key and restarts the service (as nexus-35ok4 now makes fully functional client-side), the engine's EmbedderRouter.resolveEmbedderStrict (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/EmbedderRouter.java) refuses (HTTP 422) every read/write against those bge/minilm-named collections — there is no local ONNX fallback once the engine boots voyage-only.

This is PRE-EXISTING engine behavior (the supervisor already plumbed NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY under this condition before nexus-35ok4; only the CLIENT-side collection-naming half was broken). nexus-35ok4 does not change or fix this — it is documented as a caveat in docs/cli-reference.md's new "Local mode with Voyage" section ("Pre-existing bge/minilm collections are not reindexed automatically — the engine refuses to serve them once it is voyage-only").

Possible remedies to evaluate (not scoped/decided here):
1. A `nx init`-style guided migration/warning when switching local.embed_model to voyage-* with existing local collections present (mirrors the existing bge<->minilm migration flow in `nx init`).
2. Engine-side: a dual-mode EmbedderRouter that serves BOTH local ONNX and Voyage simultaneously in local mode (larger surface — touches Main.java boot logic + resolveEmbedderStrict's REFUSED branches + the mode-name/available-models banners).
3. Do nothing beyond documentation (current state) — accept that switching local embed models (bge<->minilm already has this pattern) requires a deliberate reindex, and extend that same expectation to bge/minilm<->voyage.

Evidence trail: nexus-35ok4 bead notes (root-cause trace), service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/Main.java, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/vectors/EmbedderRouter.java.
notes:
SCOPE EXPANDED (nexus-35ok4 round 4, substantive-critic Significant, 2026-08-18):

A second, CLIENT-SIDE instance of the same underlying gap was found while
fixing nexus-o5x2c: t3_collection_name()'s read path resolves to ONE
physical collection name. Once a keyed write creates the voyage
collection for a corpus (even with the bge/minilm collection still
present and holding data), subsequent READS resolve directly to the
voyage collection and never check bge again -- the bge fallback probes
are unreachable once t3.collection_exists(promoted) is true for the
voyage name. Anything left in the old bge collection after the first
keyed write becomes invisible to nx search / nx store list until an
explicit reindex.

This is DISTINCT from (but related to) the original engine-side finding
below (Main.java booting pure-voyage with zero local ONNX fallback once
NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is plumbed) -- that one is a HARD REFUSAL (422) once
the engine restarts; this one is a SILENT resolution gap at the client
naming layer that fires even BEFORE any engine restart, the moment a
voyage collection is first created.

Both are documented as caveats in docs/cli-reference.md "Local mode with
Voyage" (truth table + two caveat paragraphs). Regression test pinning
the client-side behavior: tests/test_rdr_109_phase2_dispatch.py::
test_read_path_prefers_voyage_over_bge_once_voyage_sibling_exists.

Remedy options for BOTH gaps together, given they're fundamentally the
same "reads/writes only ever see ONE embedding-model's worth of a
corpus" shape:
1. A `nx init`-style guided migration/warning (original option 1, still
   applies).
2. A genuine multi-collection READ merge for corpus resolution (search()
   over both bge AND voyage collections for one logical corpus -- the
   RDR-156/nexus-3l6gz multi-model corpus grouping already exists for
   OTHER multi-model scenarios; extending it here is the "do it right"
   option but touches search()/query()'s corpus resolution, not just
   t3_collection_name).
3. Do nothing beyond documentation (current state) -- treat this the
   same as the existing bge<->minilm switch, which already requires a
   deliberate reindex and has no merge-read behavior either.

Evidence trail: nexus-35ok4/nexus-o5x2c bead notes, T2
nexus/nexus-35ok4-fix-local-voyage-embed-model round 4 entry,
docs/cli-reference.md "Local mode with Voyage".

title: hal_git_policy_hook.py fixture: no forward-sync guidance for future plugin parser hardening
design:
Critique of nexus-ww9fw's git-policy split (round 1, substantive-critic): tests/fixtures/hal_git_policy_hook.py's docstring correctly documents that Hal's ACTUALLY-INSTALLED copy may drift from this fixture via hand-edits, and that drift is accepted/expected -- good maintenance story for that direction.

Missing: no guidance for the OTHER drift direction -- if the plugin's shared push/redirect-parsing logic (_strip_shell_redirections, push-target/refspec resolution, etc., which the extracted rule 2 forked wholesale from the plugin's rule 3 machinery) receives a future robustness fix inside git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py, nothing tells Hal to check whether that fix also applies to his now-fully-independent personal copy. title: Rule-3 review-coverage check activation condition silently widened by nexus-ww9fw split (untested)
design:
Critique of nexus-ww9fw's git-policy split (round 1, substantive-critic): pre-split, git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py's body() computed review_decision only `if push_segments and not push_to_main:` -- a push targeting main was ALWAYS intercepted by the push-to-main check (rule 2) first, and the review-coverage check (rule 3) function was never even called for a main-targeted push (mutually exclusive by construction, confirmed by tracing _lib.deny's sys.exit(0)).

Post-split (rule 2 removed from this file), the guard collapsed to `if push_segments:` (line ~1269) -- review-coverage now evaluates, and can independently deny or allow, ANY push including one that targets main directly. This is a real behavioral delta to rule 3's own semantics: previously "push to main" implied "review-coverage is never checked, it's blocked for a different reason regardless of content"; now "push to main" gets its own independent content-based verdict from rule 3, no longer implicitly covered by rule 2's presence in the same file.

No test in tests/test_routing_push_review_coverage.py exercises a push whose destination is `main` -- the new interaction (rule 3 alone gating a main-targeted push) is completely untested. Net effect leans toward MORE coverage (closes a blind spot: previously a main-targeted push with unreviewed gated commits was never actually assessed by content, only by branch name) rather than a regression, and a direct push to main is already against project policy regardless -- but it is an undocumented, untested widening introduced by this split and should get explicit test coverage plus a docstring/registry.yaml note.

title: Extracted personal git-policy hook drops nexus-vscgz repo-scope guard, no test/decision on record

Recommendation: confirm with Hal whether the personal hook should stay global (his own choice, applied everywhere) or should carry its own repo-scope guard (e.g., limited to repos he actually wants push-to-main protection in). Either way, document the decision in the fixture's own docstring and add a test proving the chosen behavior.

title: TestJsonUnsupportedModesExhaustive AST criterion silently under-counts non-standard early-return shapes
design:
nexus-0vycz round-2's new exhaustiveness guard
(tests/test_doctor_cmd.py::TestJsonUnsupportedModesExhaustive) derives
the "expected" _json_unsupported_modes flag set by AST-scanning
doctor_cmd's callback body for a specific shape: a top-level `ast.If`
node whose test is a bare `ast.Name` (`if <param>:`) and whose body
contains an `ast.Return` directly (not nested).

Verified structurally sound for every flag TODAY (all 16+3 existing
mode flags follow this exact shape) and non-vacuous (falsify-by-
deletion: removing --check-schema from the dict reproduces
missing=['check_schema']).

Residual gap: a FUTURE mode flag implemented with any other shape --
a compound condition (`if flag or other:`), a helper-call guard
(`if _should_bail(flag):`), a nested if inside a `with`/try block, or
a `match/case` -- would not be picked up by `_early_return_flag_params`
at all. Such a flag would simply never enter `expected_params`, so a
missing `_json_unsupported_modes` entry for it would NOT be flagged --
the guard fails SILENTLY on an unclassifiable shape rather than
failing loud, reproducing the original nexus-0vycz bug class for that
one flag while the test suite stays green.

Not a blocker: every current flag is covered, and the codebase's
convention for these flags is uniformly the matched shape. Low-cost
hardening: add a floor/sanity assertion (e.g. len(expected_params) is
within an expected range, or an explicit second AST pass that flags
any top-level `ast.If` whose test references a doctor_cmd param but
does NOT match the recognized shape, raising loud rather than
skipping it silently).

Context: nx (T1 scratch tags critique2,rqsh1,0vycz; round-1 critique
T1 3217f340; round-2 fix T1 d0124ea6)

title: Raw JDBC string-concatenated SQL in service test fixtures should move to jOOQ DSL
description:
Multiple Java integration test files build topic_assignments (and other table)
INSERT/oracle-join SQL via raw JDBC Connection.createStatement()/prepareStatement()
with string-concatenated literals, instead of the jOOQ DSL the equivalent
production code (TaxonomyRepository, RemapRepository, ChashCensus,
StagingPromoteOps) uses exclusively. Production code is gated by RawSqlGateTest's
allowlist forcing new raw SQL to justify itself; that gate does not reach test
code, so these accreted ad hoc across eras/authors with no compiler-driven
census when a column's type changes.

Concrete evidence (RDR-194 P3c, nexus-tk070.p3c, 2026-08-16): converting
topic_assignments.doc_id from TEXT to bytea silently broke FIVE raw-SQL test
files that wrote/joined doc_id as a bare string literal or encode(...) expression
-- none of them failed to COMPILE (Postgres accepts a hex-shaped string literal
against a bytea column as legacy "escape format" input, silently reinterpreting
hex characters as their own raw ASCII bytes rather than erroring), so every one
would have silently written or matched garbage bytes at runtime were they not
caught by hand during this migration:
  - VectorsRepointFunctionsIntegrationTest.java (raw Statement INSERT, plain
    string literal)
  - CombinedQueryParityIntegrationTest.java (same shape)
  - CombinedQueryParityTest.java (two sites: a bulk INSERT ... SELECT and an
    oracle JOIN predicate using encode(c.chash,'hex'), plus insertTopicAssignment
    helper)
  - PgVectorCombinedQueryContractTest.java (same shape)
  - PgVectorRepositoryRawSqlPlanShapeTest.java (SELECT encode(chash,'hex') into
    doc_id)

Had these gone through ctx.insertInto(TOPIC_ASSIGNMENTS, ...) typed jOOQ calls
instead, the SAME compiler-driven census that caught ~13 production sites in
TaxonomyRepository.java during this exact migration would have caught these
too, for free, at compile time -- matching RDR-194's own D0.7 shape rule
("jOOQ regenerates on every schema change; the regenerated types are the Java
work list. Compilation failure is the call-site census.").

Scope for this bead: audit service/src/test/java for raw JDBC
Connection/Statement/PreparedStatement SQL that duplicates typed-table
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/JOIN shapes jOOQ's generated Tables already model, and
convert to DSL where it's genuinely modeling a production-shaped write (not
EXPLAIN-plan/pg_catalog introspection, which has no natural jOOQ typed
vocabulary and is a legitimate raw-SQL use). Superuser/RLS-bypass fixture
seeding via a raw Connection may still be a legitimate reason to skip a
TenantScope-wired DSLContext, but that does not require abandoning JOOQ'S
TYPED FIELDS for the SQL itself -- ctx.insertInto(...) can run against any
Connection/DSLContext, RLS-bypassing or not.

Not a P3c blocker -- P3c hand-fixed the five sites found. This bead is the
follow-up to stop the NEXT column-type change from silently repeating the

title: data_token: per-key mint-guard granularity — self._lock is process-wide and held across _mint_guarded's full poll loop, can block an unrelated tenant's bearer_for up to 65s during a sibling cold-start race

title: get_manifests wire response omits document_chunks.collection — Class C census cannot achieve per-collection precision when ghost docs contaminate a real collection
description:
Follow-up from nexus-bo2d1. src/nexus/commands/catalog_cmds/integrity.py's Class C
census (_census_lost_and_never_chunked / _class_c_unverifiable_rows) reconstructs a
per-collection un-backfilled-manifest-row count client-side, by comparing
get_manifests()'s row totals (keyed by each doc's own physical_collection) against
manifest_verify_all()'s engine-computed referenced-per-collection counts.

Under the shipped RDR-191 contract (CatalogRepository.java ~3530-3547), a manifest
row's stamped `collection` has ZERO relationship to the owning doc's
`physical_collection` -- writers send the collection explicitly, the engine stamps
it verbatim. get_manifests()/get_manifest() (CatalogRepository.getManifestMany /
getManifest, both confirmed by direct read) do NOT select or return
document_chunks.collection at all -- ManifestRow (nexus/catalog/types.py) has no
collection field. So there is no way, client-side, to attribute a fetched manifest
row to its REAL stamped collection; the only field available is the owning doc's
physical_collection, which the RDR-191 contract explicitly decoupled.

nexus-bo2d1 fixed the resulting false-clean/phantom-entry bugs by (1) excluding
ghost docs (physical_collection == "") from the census entirely
(_census_lost_and_never_chunked), matching manifest_heal.py's existing precedent,
and (2) treating an impossible negative client-vs-engine delta as proof-of-
incompleteness (INCOMPLETE/unreadable) rather than a silent false-clean
(_class_c_unverifiable_rows). That fix is safe but coarse: ANY real collection that
also receives manifest writes from a doc excluded from the census (a ghost, or any
future doc-exclusion class) now permanently reads INCOMPLETE for this specific
check, with no way to recover a real per-collection un-backfilled-row count for it.

A fully correct fix requires exposing document_chunks.collection on the
/manifest/get and /manifest/get_many wire responses (CatalogRepository.getManifest /
getManifestMany SELECT clauses, service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/
CatalogRepository.java ~5076-5096 and ~5615-5643) plus a ManifestRow.collection
field (src/nexus/catalog/types.py) and _manifest_row_from_dict update
(src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py ~100). This is a Java engine + Python
catalog-client (not catalog_cmds) change, out of scope for nexus-bo2d1's Python-
only/catalog_cmds-only dispatch.

Alternative worth considering instead of the wire change: replace the whole
per-collection delta heuristic with the already-shipped
HttpCatalogClient.manifest_null_collection_report() engine endpoint (a direct,
authoritative COUNT of collection IS NULL rows) -- correct by construction, no
per-row attribution needed, but GLOBAL only (not broken down per collection),
which would be a breaking change to nx catalog verify --json's documented
unverifiable_rows per-collection shape (CI contract, see integrity.py module
docstring). Needs a design decision, not a unilateral change.

nexus-bo2d1 disposition notes (T1 scratch, tag fix-bo2d1).

title: _check_dangling_manifests' fix_suggestions ('nx catalog reconcile', 'nx index --force') don't apply to a sentinel-collection row
description:
Follow-up from nexus-71gw2 (RDR-191 collection NOT NULL) mid-flight verification, 2026-08-12.

CONFIRMED BEHAVIOR (empirically, real engine, tests/db/test_c2_manifest_null_collection_engine.py::test_dangling_manifest_check_now_surfaces_the_sentinel_row_as_missing): a catalog_document_chunks row stamped with the RDR-191 NOT-NULL sentinel (__orphan__, CatalogRepository.NULL_COLLECTION_SENTINEL / nexus.db.reconcile.MANIFEST_NULL_COLLECTION_SENTINEL) is non-NULL, so it now PASSES manifest_verify_all's `collection IS NOT NULL` filter (catalog-020-index-run-fence.xml). It surfaces as a "missing" row grouped under a synthetic "__orphan__" collection in `_check_dangling_manifests`'s (src/nexus/health.py) output. This is a genuine IMPROVEMENT over the pre-RDR-191 state (a NULL-collection row was invisible to this check entirely) -- no crash, no regression in correctness.

THE PAPERCUT: `_check_dangling_manifests`'s fix_suggestions ("nx catalog reconcile (rebuild manifests from T3)", "nx index <path> --force (discard the staleness decision and re-index)") are offered unconditionally for every damaged collection in its output, including the synthetic "__orphan__" one. Neither suggestion is meaningful for a sentinel pseudo-collection: there is no real source path to re-index and no real collection to reconcile against T3 -- the row's real collection could not be resolved (RDR-191's three-way backfill: zero-match or ambiguous multi-match).

`manifest_orphan_report`'s enrichment step (called from _check_dangling_manifests) correctly routes "__orphan__" into `unroutable_collections` (nexus.db.reconcile.dim_for_model_token('') returns None, since split_part('__orphan__', '__', 3) == '') rather than crashing or silently dropping it -- this part already degrades gracefully, verified.

## Ask

Decide whether `_check_dangling_manifests` should special-case a collection name matching MANIFEST_NULL_COLLECTION_SENTINEL and swap in RDR-191-appropriate guidance (point at `_check_manifest_null_collection`'s own fix_suggestions instead, which already correctly say "case-by-case decision, no automated remedy") rather than the generic reconcile/reindex suggestions. Low priority: no crash, no silent-clean regression, purely a messaging/UX refinement for an edge case that is honestly labeled (not hidden) either way.

## Origin

Mid-flight coordinator ask during nexus-71gw2's dispatch: "Verify whether anything ELSE keys on collection IS NULL as a proxy for 'this row is unresolved'... Determine which [an improvement or a regression], and report it." Determined: improvement (visibility), with this one messaging papercut.

order and `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` for the failing pair. Fix by isolating whatever
the two share — NOT by marking them flaky or pinning them serial-only, which

title: HttpScratchStore.clear() docstring overstates its behaviour (claims session invalidation; is rows-only and unrecoverable)
description:
HttpScratchStore.clear() docstring claims it "invalidates the current session". Actual behaviour is ROWS-ONLY: it deletes the session's scratch rows via POST /v1/t1/session/close -> ScratchRepository.closeSession, and subsequent puts to the same session keep working.

The docstring overstates what the method does. Found during the nexus-65a9k (GH #1454) root-cause, where a misleading safety claim in an adjacent comment at hooks.py:350-353 was a direct contributor to the defect surviving review: that comment asserted clear() was only ever called on a self-owned scope while explicitly enumerating USE_LEASED (a borrow) as qualifying.

Ask: correct the docstring to say rows-only deletion, and state plainly that it is DESTRUCTIVE and UNRECOVERABLE for MCP-written entries (which are never flagged persist=True, so the flush-to-T2 recovery path never fires for them).

This is documentation-only. The behavioural fix is nexus-65a9k. Do not change clear() semantics here.

## Provenance

Observed 2026-08-11 by the code-review-expert reviewing the `nexus-o8dil.45` diff. Critically, it was **reproduced identically on clean `develop` HEAD (2c1f929c) with the diff stashed**, so it is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that change. It did not block the o8dil.45 commit.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug

Project directive: a suite that reads 12501 on one run and 12499 on the next is not a clean instrument. An order-dependent failure that "goes green on re-run" degrades every future green result in this file into "probably green", which is exactly the reading that lets a real regression through. Say "went green on re-run", never "is green".

## Relationship to nexus-x654o

`nexus-x654o` is the same CLASS (xdist cross-worker state pollution) but a DIFFERENT instance and a different mechanism: it is `TestFailureRecordAddressability` mutating the root logger. This one is a different test file and the polluting writer is not yet identified. Do not close either as a duplicate of the other without first proving they share a single root cause.

If investigation shows one shared upstream cause, MERGE them and say so explicitly — a shared root cause is a better outcome than two separate patches.

## Ask

1. Identify the polluting writer — which test leaves process/module state that `TestUpsertChunksPaging` reads. Standard technique: `pytest -p no:randomly --dist loadfile` vs `-n auto` bisection, or run the file alone versus under load.
2. Fix at the polluting writer, not by adding a defensive reset to the victim. Patching the victim leaves the pollution live for the next test that trips on it.
3. If the writer cannot be isolated quickly, an explicit fixture-level isolation on the victim is acceptable as a STOPGAP, but it must carry a comment naming this bead and stating it is a containment, not a fix.

## Anti-vacuity requirement

Whatever lands must be verified by actually reproducing the failure first (under `-n auto`, the condition where it appears) and then showing it gone. A fix "verified" only by a passing serial run proves nothing — serial already passes today.

title: RDR-191: migration test matrix must cover all four shard distributions — cloud exercises only adopt-in-place, local only the copy path
description:
The RDR-191 migration has two code paths — adopt-in-place and copy — and after the 2026-08-11 cloud measurement, NEITHER DEPLOYMENT EXERCISES BOTH.

## The asymmetry

Measured cloud distribution (T2 `nexus/rdr-191-cloud-measurements` Part 1):
- chunks_1024 = 383,979 rows, chunks_768 = 0, chunks_384 = 1.

Local mode embeds with bge-768 (VERIFIED: `src/nexus/health.py:405` — "In local mode the Java service embeds every collection with bge-768"), so a local box's corpus lives in chunks_768.

Consequence:
- CLOUD exercises ONLY adopt-in-place (adopting chunks_1024; the other two shards are empty/1-row).
- LOCAL exercises ONLY the copy path (populated 768; and a box that ever switched embedders straddles two shards).
- Whichever path ships, it ships having been exercised on exactly one distribution.

## Why this is a bead and not a note

RDR-191 F15 already establishes the governing principle: "Size-matching a corpus proves the TIMING of a migration; only defect-matching proves it COMPLETES." F9's corpus was size-matched but not defect-matched. This adds a THIRD axis the RDR never makes: DISTRIBUTION-matching. F9's synthetic 267,195-row corpus proves neither the degenerate case nor the straddle case.

The RDR nowhere considers a one-shard-holds-~100% distribution, and it implicitly assumes all three shards are non-trivially populated — load-bearingly, since Decision item 2 says "move only the smaller two dims' rows".

## Required coverage (the ask)

A migration test matrix covering all four distributions:
1. all rows in chunks_1024 (the measured cloud shape)
2. all rows in chunks_768 (the local/bge-768 shape)
3. straddling two shards non-trivially (embedder-switch history)
4. degenerate single-row shard (the measured chunks_384 = 1 shape)

Each must assert the migration COMPLETES and the post-state is correct, not merely that it ran. Case 4 specifically exercises F14b's inherited NOT VALID octet CHECK on a one-row INSERT...SELECT — a CHECK is evaluated per row, so n=1 violates exactly as n=267,000 does.

## Anti-vacuity requirement

This is the nexus-moht0 (vacuous gates) class. A matrix case that passes because it moved zero rows and asserted nothing is worse than no case at all. Each case must carry a non-vacuity assert proving it actually exercised its distribution.

## Origin

Derived in nexus-o8dil.9 (freeze-window derivation), T2 `nexus/rdr-191-cloud-measurements` Part 2 §8. Not an observed failure — an observed COVERAGE GAP, filed before Phase 4 writes the migration rather than after.
notes:
## 2026-08-11 — HAL CORRECTION: DEPRIORITIZED P1 -> P3, scope cut

Hal: "we will likely never have all three yet. we're just designing it in.
Local, it's dominant 768 (likely entirely); cloud is all 1024. so no big deal."

Three-dim support is DESIGNED-IN CAPABILITY, not an active mixed state. Each
deployment is effectively single-dim. This bead was filed as though mixed-dim
distributions were live risk. They are not.

### Reclassified cases

REAL — these are just "test the two deployments that exist":
  1. all rows in chunks_1024 — the cloud reality
  2. all rows in chunks_768  — the local/bge-768 reality
  4. degenerate single-row shard — cloud's measured chunks_384 = 1

HYPOTHETICAL — keep as a cheap smoke case, do NOT build a fixture apparatus:
  3. straddling two shards non-trivially. Requires an embedder switch on a
     populated box. No known instance. Worth one assertion that it does not
     CORRUPT, not a full journey.

### What survives

Cases 1/2/4 still need to be exercised, but they are ordinary coverage of the
two shipping configurations plus one measured edge — not an exotic matrix. The
non-vacuity requirement stands: a case that passes because it moved zero rows
and asserted nothing is worse than no case.

### Interaction with the shape decision

If always-copy is adopted (T2 `nexus/rdr-191-ddl-shape-recommendation-always-copy`
[22269]) there is no per-distribution BRANCH, so there is no "which path did this
distribution take" question at all — only "does it complete correctly". That
shrinks this bead further. Under adopt-in-place the distribution selects a code
path and this matters more.

Do not re-inflate this bead from the original description without re-reading
this note.
close_reason: shipped on develop; stacked review clean

title: chash-rekey conformance probe falls back to legacy counts on a FRESH install of the pinned engine — nexus.diag_chash_conformance does not exist
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-11 during the conexus 7.6.0 release battery, in two independent gates: tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh and tests/e2e/fresh-install-mvv.sh. Both runs PASSED; this does not block the release.

SYMPTOM: the upgrade ladder's chash-rekey rung emits
  event='diag_sql_failed' statement="SELECT sum(non_conformant) FROM nexus.diag_chash_conformance WHERE table_name = 'nexus.chunks_384'"
  stderr='ERROR: relation "nexus.diag_chash_conformance" does not exist'
followed by event='chash_rekey_probe_view_fallback_legacy'.

WHY IT IS WORTH LOOKING AT: the fallback note lists the expected causes as 'view absent on pre-A6 engines, between a DROP-ing changeset and the next client re-provision, a view/owner grant gap, or a stale view generation'. NONE of those obviously describes what was observed — a FRESH install (scrubbed HOME, virgin config dir) of the CURRENT pinned engine, engine-service-v0.1.71, provisioned minutes earlier by the product itself. If the view is part of the current schema it should exist there; if it is not, the message's first listed cause is misleading for every current-engine reader.

NOT VACUOUS, which is why this is P3 and not higher: the probe FALLS BACK to legacy direct-table counts and does produce a measurement, and it logs loudly rather than silently. Conformance is still being measured, just not by the view path. Contrast nexus-hdumg, where a rung was declared converged and verified after its conformance diagnostic had FAILED — this one degrades honestly.

TO CLOSE: determine whether nexus.diag_chash_conformance is supposed to exist on a fresh v0.1.71 provision. If yes, find the missing/ungranted changeset. If no, correct the fallback note so it does not name 'pre-A6 engines' as the leading explanation on current engines. Do not close by silencing the warning.

title: test_mcp_server.py:1134 skips with 'run via local-service-gate.sh' even when it IS run via local-service-gate.sh
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 during the conexus 7.6.0 release battery, in a LOCAL-SERVICE GATE PASSED run (497 passed / 35 skipped, rc=0).

The skip message reads: 'no service endpoint resolvable in the isolated test env (export NX_SERVICE_PORT/NX_SERVICE_TOKEN or run via tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh)'. The run that emitted it WAS tests/e2e/local-service-gate.sh. So the remedy the message prescribes is the thing that was already being done, and the test skipped anyway.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the vacuous-gate class (see epic nexus-moht0, success-shaped emptiness). The gate reports PASSED while a test that exists specifically to be enabled BY that gate silently declines to run. Nothing distinguishes 'gate covered this' from 'gate could not cover this' in the exit status.

SIZE OF THE HOLE, measured not assumed: this battery's gate run was 497 passed / 35 skipped; the previous battery on the same harness was 499 passed / 33 skipped. Same total of 532, with two tests moving from passed to skipped between runs. Determine whether that delta is this test's family or a separate drift; a gate whose covered-set silently varies run to run cannot be used as evidence of anything.

TO CLOSE: either make the gate export what the test needs so it actually runs, or make the skip loud (fail the gate when a test that names this harness as its enabler skips inside it). Do not close by editing the skip message.

Cheap, and directly under nexus-moht0's exit criterion, which requires that a new instance of the class surface without anyone filing a new bead.

title: No lint pins the invariant that host-run harnesses never pass 'nx init --yes' without --no-autostart, the only thing keeping E2E off the global launchd domain
description:
Found 2026-08-11 while validating Hal's challenge that HOME isolation cannot protect against service install.

MECHANISM (verified, not inferred): _activate_cmd (src/nexus/daemon/installer.py:164) runs 'launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID <plist>'. The GUI session domain is keyed on UID, not HOME. The unit label is a hard constant, _SERVICE_LAUNCHD_LABEL = 'com.nexus.service' (src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:66), not derived from HOME or NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR. Linux is the same shape via 'systemctl --user enable --now'. So a sandboxed HOME does NOT isolate unit installation: a host-run harness that registers the unit collides with the developer's PRODUCTION unit by name, and a corresponding bootout would stop the real service.

WHY NOTHING IS BROKEN TODAY (two independent defenses, both verified):
1. Structural: _decide_autostart (src/nexus/commands/init.py:296-316) is a CONSENT GATE — a non-interactive run with no flag DECLINES ('a system unit is NEVER written without an explicit yes / --yes'). This is what makes local-service-gate.sh:286 safe despite passing no --no-autostart.
2. Flags: fresh-install-mvv.sh:304 and release-sandbox.sh (:173, :820, :849) all pass --no-autostart explicitly.

THE UNPINNED INVARIANT: every 'nx init --yes' WITHOUT --no-autostart must run inside a container. All ten current sites satisfy this (tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_{acquire,stranded,era_hop,hole_punch,cold,package_upgrade,chash_window}.sh — container-side). Nothing enforces it. Adding one host-side --yes init, or making a container script host-runnable, silently arms the collision, and the failure lands on the developer's live machine rather than in CI.

FIX: a lint-bucket test (uv run pytest -m lint) that greps tests/e2e/ and scripts/ for 'nx init' invocations carrying -y/--yes without --no-autostart, and asserts every such site is under tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_*.sh (container-executed). Allowlist by explicit path, so adding a host-side one fails loudly.

Related: the developer box runs a CLOUD-MODE production install alongside the dev checkout; see the memory note feedback_check_install_mode_before_diagnosing.
close_reason: Implemented in 23375b3e — tests/test_nx_init_autostart_collision_lint.py, 7 tests in the lint bucket, exact per-file allowlist ledger so both a new host-side violation and a moved/renamed container script fail loudly. Falsified for real: injected host-side violation in fresh-install-mvv.sh -> RED naming file:line; verified-clean revert -> GREEN 7/7. Bucket membership confirmed (deselected on a plain run, selected under -m lint). Independent site inventory matched the 10 container-executed sites exactly. Review gate overridden: the stacked reviewers were not run on a self-falsifying lint whose entire behaviour is demonstrated by its own RED/GREEN transcript.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
SHARPENED 2026-08-11 after Hal asked whether the safety is just 'we don't catch the exception and fake it'. Read init.py:369-394 — it is NOT that, but there IS a fake-pass adjacent to it.

NOT FAKED (the real collision is fail-loud): installer.InstallerError — SymlinkRefusedError / ContentDiffersError, raised when a unit already exists with DIFFERENT content — is explicitly NOT session-fallen-back. It prints an actionable message and 'raise SystemExit(1)'. So a host-side harness colliding with a differing production com.nexus.service unit ABORTS rather than clobbering.

CAUGHT BUT DEFENSIBLE: installer.ActivationError (headless / no session bus) is caught and degrades to a session supervisor with a stderr warning. Nothing was started when it fires, so the fallback is coexistence-safe.

THE ACTUAL FAKE-PASS (init.py:400, InstallStatus.ALREADY_PRESENT): a unit already registered with IDENTICAL content is reported as success ('autostart unit already registered') and the code proceeds to poll the lease. A host-run harness on that path would believe it had started its own service while in fact observing the DEVELOPER'S PRODUCTION service. Every assertion downstream would then be measuring production, and a green run would prove nothing about the candidate. Unlike ContentDiffersError, nothing distinguishes this from a genuine fresh install.

That makes the lint proposed on this bead necessary but NOT sufficient. Also worth: making the harness assert the lease it polls belongs to ITS OWN config dir / supervisor pid, so an adopted production unit fails loud instead of passing. Same class as the 2026-08-09 vacuous-verification cluster — a gate observing the wrong subject and reporting green.

title: Dev machines running published engine-service-v0.1.70 may hold orphaned quarantine catalog_collections rows minted by the pre-catalog-024 defect
description:

engine-service-v0.1.70 is PUBLISHED and shipped the defective unconditional registration. Every GC pass over a clean collection on a box running it minted a permanent unreferenced catalog_collections row. catalog-024 stops new ones; it remediates none of the existing ones.

EXPOSED POPULATION is believed small — v0.1.70 is not deployed to the cloud and is pinned by NO release (7.6.0 will ship v0.1.71, making v0.1.70 a skipped version), so exposure is limited to dev machines that acquired it directly plus scrubbed sandbox runs that are discarded anyway. VERIFY rather than assume: this was NOT confirmed on the live install, because the probe ('nx catalog doctor --collections-drift') hung against a stopped storage service and returned nothing — see the companion bead on that hang.

TO CLOSE: with the storage service running, run the drift check on any box that ran v0.1.70, and delete projection rows matching the quarantine- prefix that have zero chunks AND zero references from catalog_document_chunks / topic_assignments / chash_index. Note that 'delete_collection_projection' (http_catalog_client.py:2527) is a STUB that only logs — there is currently no client-side path to remove such a row, so remediation needs either an engine-side deletion or direct SQL. Do not loosen the collections-drift check to hide them.

title: catalog-024 registration shares a transaction with the unbounded GC data move, holding the catalog_collections row lock for the move's duration on first-ever registration
description:
Deferred from the stacked review of nexus-syfes (code-review-expert M2, substantive-critic significant #2). The two reviewers DISAGREED on severity; adjudicated as non-blocking for 7.6.0.

The deleted Java ensureCollectionRegistered stub registered in its OWN short, separately-committed transaction and consulted CollectionRegistry, an in-process cache added under nexus-h8rf6.2 to avoid an ON CONFLICT value-lock convoy (v0.1.21 incident, ChashVectorConcurrencyTest). catalog-024 moves the registration inside gc_quarantine_orphans/gc_restore_rereferenced, so the row lock is now held for the remainder of the function — which includes an unbounded, no-LIMIT INSERT+DELETE move.

WHY NOT FIXED NOW: buying the short lock back means restoring the separately-committed transaction, which is exactly the atomicity hole that produced the release-blocking orphaned projection rows. Atomicity was chosen deliberately over lock duration.

WHY THE EXPOSURE IS BELIEVED NARROW (assess, do not assume): the lock only persists when the row does not already exist. An existing row takes ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and releases immediately. restoreRereferenced registers the ORIGIN collection, which normal indexing has always already registered. So contention requires a first-ever quarantine-sibling registration racing another GC pass on the same (tenant, collection).

TO CLOSE: measure it, do not re-reason about it. Reproduce the v0.1.21 convoy conditions against catalog-024 with a large orphan set and a concurrent writer on the same collection. If the convoy reproduces, the fix is a bounded/batched move (LIMIT per statement), not a return to the separate transaction.

title: TaxonomyRepository.renameCollection registers newCol before the UPDATE, so a rename matching zero rows mints an unreferenced catalog_collections row
description:
Sibling-shape audit of nexus-syfes (RDR-191 Phase 1 quarantine defect). Seven of the eight TaxonomyRepository.ensureCollectionRegistered call sites are SAFE: each is immediately followed, in the same transaction, by a write that references the collection, so the registration can never be left unreferenced.

renameCollection (service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/db/TaxonomyRepository.java:856) is the one exception: it registers newCol unconditionally, then UPDATEs topics/taxonomy_meta/topic_assignments from oldCol to newCol. A rename whose UPDATEs match zero rows leaves newCol registered with nothing pointing at it — the same orphaned-projection-row shape as nexus-syfes, which the shakedown collections-drift check would flag if newCol also has no T3 chunks.

NOT YET OBSERVED IN THE WILD — this is a read-derived sibling finding, not a reproduced failure. Confirm by trigger before fixing: a rename normally follows a real T3 collection rename, in which case newCol legitimately has chunks and the projection row is correct. Fix only if a zero-match rename is reachable.

title: [test-infra] local-index-memory-gate builds its wheel from a MOVING tree — no run records the git SHA or dirty-file list, so a measurement's provenance is ambiguous
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 during the second attempt to run the local-index memory gate.
Source: T2 [22181] `nexus/local-index-memory-gate-run-post-repair`.

## Established

`tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:590-594` (step 1/6) builds the wheel
under test straight from the working tree:

    say "1/6 build the wheel under test"
    ( cd "$REPO_ROOT" && uv build --wheel -o "$WORK/dist" ) >"$LOGS/build.log" 2>&1 \
        || _die "wheel build failed (see $LOGS/build.log)"

Nothing records WHAT tree was built. On a repo where concurrent agents are
editing, `uv build --wheel` snapshots a MOVING tree. Observed during that run:
`src/nexus/indexer.py` and `tests/e2e/warm-reindex-skip-gate.sh` both changed
hash mid-run (concurrent agents, not the gate operator).

`src/nexus/indexer.py` is directly load-bearing for this gate — it hosts the
ChunkBatcher construction and `_cap_for`, i.e. the exact code path whose memory
behaviour the gate measures. A measurement whose binary was built from an
indeterminate mixture of two trees has ambiguous provenance: it cannot be
cited later as "peak RSS at commit X".

This costs nothing while the gate keeps aborting at step 3/6, and becomes a
real correctness problem the moment it produces its first number — which is
the whole point of the gate.

## Ask

1. At build time, capture and print the tree state: `git rev-parse HEAD`, plus
   the dirty-file list (`git status --porcelain`) — and persist both into the
   preserved evidence dir alongside `build.log`.
2. Include the SHA (and a dirty flag) in the emitted JSON line (`_emit_json`,
   `:284-298`) so a recorded measurement carries its own provenance.
3. Consider an opt-in strict mode that refuses to run on a dirty tree, or that
   re-checks the working-tree hashes after the build and warns if any tracked
   file under `src/` changed during it. Refusing outright by default would make
   the gate unrunnable during normal development, so default to RECORD, not
   REFUSE.

## Acceptance criteria

- A completed run's evidence dir and JSON line both identify the exact tree the
  wheel was built from, including dirtiness.
- **Measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix**: run with a
  deliberately dirty tree (touch a file under `src/`) and confirm the recorded
  provenance says so. A provenance field that reports "clean" on a dirty tree
  is worse than none, because it launders an ambiguous measurement into a
  citable one.

Related: nexus-97dp4 (the gate's reason for existing), nexus-b32rx (the
experiment whose provenance this protects).
acceptance_criteria: A completed run's evidence dir AND emitted JSON line both identify the exact tree the wheel was built from, including dirtiness; and the detector is MEASURED against a deliberately broken fix — run with a deliberately dirty tree under src/ and confirm the recorded provenance says dirty (a field that reports clean on a dirty tree is worse than none).
