title: [E] docs/desktop-deployment.md claims 11/11 for upgrade-shakeout which now reports 12/12, with inconsistent x/10 vs x/12 step labels in the script
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven** by direct comparison. Low severity, real drift.

## The finding

`docs/desktop-deployment.md` calls `tests/e2e/upgrade-shakeout.sh` "the gate before any
release" and states **11/11 green** as the passing condition.

The script's banner now reports **12/12**, and its step labels are internally inconsistent
— some read `x/10`, some `x/12` (e.g. `:245`'s neighbourhood uses `7/12`).

## Why a step count is worth a bead

A gate whose documented passing condition is a count that no longer matches is a gate an
operator cannot verify passed. "11/11 green" against a 12-step script reads as a FAILURE to
a careful reader and as a PASS to a careless one, and neither reading is the truth.

nexus-a3nqp (closed P2) is the prior bead on this doc/script pair and notes the same
"11/11 green" claim from 2026-05-25 — so this string has now survived at least one
correction cycle.

## Scope

- Reconcile `docs/desktop-deployment.md` with the script's actual step count.
- Fix the script's own `x/10` vs `x/12` label inconsistency.
- Better: make the doc reference the banner string rather than a hardcoded count, so it
  cannot drift again.

Related, same script: nexus-okbr8 (open P3, step 11 renders a skip as a pass) and the
sibling bead on this script's four vacuous steps.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix

This bead is NOT done when the gate is changed. It is done when the CHANGED gate has been
SHOWN FAILING against a deliberately broken input, and that demonstration is recorded
(a test fixture, a `--self-test` arm, or a pasted RED transcript pasted into this bead).

1. Construct the break the assertion claims to catch — delete the producer, corrupt the
   value, empty the filter output, skip the leg, plant the regression.
2. Run the gate. It MUST go RED, and the message MUST name the real cause.
3. Repair the break. Run again. It MUST go GREEN.
4. Paste both runs here.

A fix that has only ever been observed green does not count as done.

Rationale (2026-08-10): this session produced a gate that was committed, reviewed and dead
on arrival because nobody ran it, and a P1 class that recurred 72 hours after being swept
across 12 sites. The demonstration is the deliverable, not the diff.

title: [E] scheduled_workflow_watchdog exits 1 on an unparseable workflow or GH API 500, which the workflow maps to findings=1 and posts an EMPTY issue instead of the rc=2 broken-watchdog path
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven** by reading both the script's exit paths and the workflow's
mapping of them.

## The finding

`scripts/scheduled_workflow_watchdog.py` has a deliberate rc contract: rc=2 means
BROKEN WATCHDOG (a distinct, loud outcome), rc=1 means findings exist.

But two error paths exit 1 instead of 2:

- `:82` — an unparseable workflow raises `SystemExit(f"{path}: unparseable workflow: ...")`,
  which is rc=1.
- `:214` — a GH API 500 takes the same path.

`.github/workflows/scheduled-failure-watch.yml:65-71` maps rc=1 to "findings=1" and posts
an issue built from the findings markdown. On these two paths there ARE no findings, so it
posts an issue with an EMPTY body — losing the diagnostic entirely and, worse, presenting a
broken watchdog as a routine findings report.

## Why this is P3 and not higher

The watchdog is otherwise the best-built detector in this repo (three failure modes,
`nothing-to-watch` treated as a finding, the `on:`-parses-as-True Norway guard, its own
test file). This is a narrow rc-mapping bug on the error paths, not a design fault.

But it is the same shape the module exists to prevent: a broken detector reporting as a
functioning one.

## Scope

Route both error paths to rc=2, or have the workflow refuse to post an issue with an empty
body and escalate instead. Then feed it a deliberately unparseable workflow and show the
broken-watchdog path firing rather than an empty issue.

title: [E] nx doctor --check-taxonomy and --check-schema each have an exit-0 degraded branch reachable from BOTH release-sandbox modes (caveat: --check-schema's N/A is vl8lk-intentional)
description:
EVIDENCE CLASS: **[E] proven** that both branches exist and exit 0.
**IMPORTANT CAVEAT below** — one of the two may be intentional; verify before "fixing".

## A. `--check-taxonomy` has a fully green degraded path

`src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:2170-2183`: a broad `except Exception` falls through to a
SQLite census that the code itself explicitly demotes to "never decides the exit code"
(`:2151`). On a fresh HOME it returns "T2 database not found — nothing to check." with
rc 0 (`:2224-2226`).

Both release-sandbox modes call it.

## B. `--check-schema` has an exit-0 "N/A" branch

`doctor.py:102-107`: when the endpoint withholds the fingerprint, the check reports N/A and
exits 0.

## CAVEAT — verify intent before changing B

nexus-vl8lk (closed P1) DELIBERATELY built this branch. Its close reason reads:

> --check-schema: shared /version fingerprint probe, exit 2 unreachable / 1 schema_error
> or zero changesets / 0 OK or **honest N/A**.

So the N/A-exit-0 branch is a designed outcome, not an oversight. The audit's finding is
therefore narrower than "this is a bug": the real question is whether a RELEASE GATE
context should accept an honest N/A as a pass. In interactive `nx doctor` it clearly
should. In `release-sandbox.sh`, where the whole point is to prove the substrate is
present and correct, an N/A is indistinguishable from a pass and that is the gap.

Do NOT simply make the N/A fatal — that would regress vl8lk. The right shape is probably a
strict/gate mode, or a release-sandbox-side assertion that the check reported OK rather
than N/A.

## A is less ambiguous

nexus-ypori (closed) gave `--check-taxonomy` an engine path precisely so it would stop
diagnosing the frozen SQLite migration source. The `except Exception` fallback to that
same demoted SQLite census is the residue of the thing ypori removed.

## Scope

- A: narrow the `except Exception`, and make the fresh-HOME/unreachable case distinguish
  "nothing to check because nothing exists" from "could not check".
- B: add a gate-context strictness so release-sandbox cannot read N/A as proof, WITHOUT
  regressing vl8lk's honest-N/A design for interactive use.

description:

| leg | CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md | docs/contributing.md | .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit suite | yes | yes | yes |

| `release-sandbox shakedown` | yes (6c) | yes (7c) | yes (6c) |
| `check_engine_release_floor` | yes (0) | yes (0) | yes (0) |

VERIFIED at a7553c88:
`grep -c` in AGENTS.md returns **0** for each of `upgrade-shakeout`, `local-service-gate`,
and `package-upgrade`.

`docs/contributing.md:258-262` is explicit about the leg AGENTS.md prescribes:

> Bare `uv run pytest -m integration` is not enough on its own: the local-service
> round-trip family self-provisions inside `local-service-gate.sh` and otherwise
> skip-gates silently on an absent service (the 74/516 ambient-degradation class the gate

`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md` and is the auto-loaded file an agent follows BY

and runs one leg the other two documents call insufficient. The release checklist IS the

`docs/contributing.md:264-265` already points at the skill as "the authoritative,

Reconcile AGENTS.md § Cutting a release with SKILL.md (the authority), or reduce it to a
pointer at SKILL.md so it cannot drift again. Remove or qualify the bare `-m integration`

title: [bug] local-index-memory-gate health poll discards nx output — a poll failure leaves no evidence in the preserved tree
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, first real execution of `tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh`
(T2 [22174]).

## The defect

    tests/e2e/local-index-memory-gate.sh:553-558
        healthy=0
        for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            _nx daemon service status 2>&1 | grep -qiE "health.*ok|healthy|serving|running" \
                && { healthy=1; break; }
            sleep 2
        done
        [ "$healthy" = 1 ] || _die "service never became healthy"

`grep -q` writes nothing and the pipeline's stdout goes nowhere. When the poll fails, the
gate dies with `service never became healthy` and **no record of what `nx` actually said**
across 30 attempts / 60 seconds.

The step immediately above it does this correctly —
`:552` tails `init.log` to stderr before `_die`. The poll is the odd one out.

## Cost paid

This directly extended the source session's root-cause hunt. The gate's own output was
consistent with "the service is genuinely unhealthy"; establishing that the service was in
fact healthy the whole time required standing up a SEPARATE concurrent observer process
running the same command out-of-band (which logged
`nx_rc=0 | status: live  health: ok  pg: up` continuously through the failing window) and
separately reading `storage_service.log` for `storage_service_ready` +
`storage_service_lease_published`. None of that would have been needed had the last poll
attempt's stdout and rc been preserved.

Note the gate DOES preserve evidence well elsewhere — it prints
`EVIDENCE PRESERVED: /tmp/local-index-memory-gate-XXXXXX (logs: .../logs)` on failure. The
poll simply never writes anything into that tree.

## Ask

Capture the poll's output and per-attempt rc into `$LOGS/` (e.g. `service-status-poll.log`,
appended each attempt with attempt number and rc), and tail the last attempt to stderr
before `_die`, mirroring the `nx init` handling at `:552`. Keep it inside the preserved
evidence tree so it survives with the rest.

Recording the rc separately from the matched/not-matched decision is the load-bearing part:
in the defect this bead was found alongside, `nx` exited non-zero while grep matched, and
that discrepancy is invisible unless both are logged.

Best fixed in the same change as the health-poll rewrite, since that rewrite replaces these
exact lines — but it is a distinct property (diagnosability vs correctness) and should
survive as its own acceptance criterion rather than being assumed to come for free.

## Non-vacuous check

Force the poll to fail (stop the service before the poll, or point it at a dead endpoint)
and assert that the preserved evidence directory contains the poll log AND that the log

title: index: col.count() denominator guard admits negative ints — renders 'page k/-1' instead of degrading to page-only
description:
Found 2026-08-10 by code review of the `nx index repo` output-UX work (the nexus-fx5oe page-progress
denominator).

## Defect

`_prune_deleted_files`'s page-progress denominator guard
(`src/nexus/indexer.py:2818-2834`) validates the `col.count()` result with an `isinstance` check
and nothing else:

```python
_count = col.count()
# isinstance guard, not just a bare try/except: a permissive
# test double (MagicMock ...) would otherwise leak a Mock repr ...
if isinstance(_count, int):
    _total_pages = (
        -(-_count // _CHROMA_PAGE_SIZE) if _count else 0
    )
```

The guard's stated purpose — reject a non-numeric test double before it reaches the
operator-visible phase message — is met. But `isinstance(_count, int)` also admits **negative**
ints. A negative count yields a negative `_total_pages` (`-(-(-1) // 300)` = `-1`), and the phase
line renders `page k/-1` instead of degrading to page-only numbering, which is what every other
failure mode in this block does.

Likelihood is low: `COUNT(*)` cannot be negative, and `col.count()`
(`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1150`) reads it from the service. The realistic sources are a
corrupted/garbage response and a test double configured with a negative return. The fix is one
line and makes the guard say what it means.

## Ask

Tighten the guard to `isinstance(_count, int) and _count >= 0`. Everything else in the block is
already correct — the `if _count else 0` arm handles the empty-collection case, and the
surrounding `except Exception` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2834`) already degrades to page-only for
every other failure.

While there: keep the existing comment's explanation of *why* it is an isinstance check rather
than a bare try/except, and extend it to say why the lower bound is there too. The comment is
load-bearing (it documents a real MagicMock hazard) and a later reader trimming "redundant"
conditions is exactly the failure this guard exists to prevent.

## Non-vacuous test

- Call the pruning path with a collection stub whose `count()` returns `-1`, with an `on_phase`
  callback subscribed. Assert **no emitted phase line contains a negative denominator** and that
  the rendering falls back to page-only (the same output shape as the `count()`-raises case).
  Assert on the emitted string, not on `_total_pages` — a test on the internal alone would pass an
  implementation that clamps the value but still formats a `/0`.
- Keep a positive-path leg (`count()` returns 900 -> `page k/3`) so the guard's tightening cannot
  be implemented by disabling the denominator entirely.
- **Non-vacuity**: drop the `>= 0` clause and the negative-count leg must go RED (`page 1/-1`
  appears). Verify by dropping it.

Related: nexus-fx5oe (the page-progress feature this guard belongs to), nexus-paqm8
(prune-misclassified sweep progress — same rendering surface), nexus-uoot1, nexus-p6kpx.
close_reason: Fixed and tested in commit a7553c88; verified by substantive-critic review (T2 22173).

title: index: files deferred by _contain_transient_upsert are invisible to chunk_flush_failed_files — run exits 0 with files unindexed and 'deferred' reads as 'fine'
description:
Found 2026-08-10 by the W0 client-degradation investigation. Source of record: T2
`nexus/engine-w0-503-client-degradation` (entry 22168), section 3 gap 1.

## Defect

`chunk_flush_failed_files` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:4772`) is `len(_batch_failures)`, sourced
exclusively from `ChunkBatcher.failed_files`. Its own docstring comment
(`src/nexus/indexer.py:4765-4771`) says so: "post bisect-retry survivors only, see
chunk_batcher.py". `src/nexus/commands/index.py` turns a non-zero count into a stdout warning and
a non-zero exit — the nexus-4s1ww / GH #1432 fix.

Files deferred by `_contain_transient_upsert` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:1967-1983`) never touch that
counter. On a transient 502/503/504 (`_TRANSIENT_UPSERT_CODES`, `src/nexus/indexer.py:1930`) the
helper logs `index_file_transient_upsert_deferred` and **returns 0**. Zero chunks landed for that
file, and:

- it contributes nothing to `chunk_flush_failed_files`;
- it is indistinguishable from a legitimately-skipped (unchanged) file in the counts;
- the run exits **0** and prints "Done.".

So a run where every prose/PDF/RDR file was deferred by a saturated engine reports clean success
on both channels a human or a script would check — the same shape nexus-4s1ww exists to close,
arriving through a different door.

Reachable today from all three wrapped loops: `_index_one_prose`
(`src/nexus/indexer.py:4338`), `_index_one_pdf` (`:4374`), `_index_one_rdr` (`:4442`). If the
companion P1 bead lands, the code loop joins them.

## Why it is not simply a bug

Deferral is deliberate and correct as a *recovery* strategy: the file stays stale and is retried
on the next run (nexus-7yfe6's design). The defect is in *reporting* — "deferred" currently reads
as "fine". A user who never runs the index again is left with a file that is silently unindexed
and a clean exit code that says otherwise.

## Ask — a decision first, then the change it implies

Decide whether deferrals should be surfaced in the run summary, and at what strength. The options
are genuinely different products, so this needs a call rather than a default:

1. **Informational only** — a stdout line, e.g. `Deferred: N files hit a transient service error
   and will retry on the next run.` Exit code stays 0. Preserves "deferral is not failure" while
   removing the silence.
2. **Informational + a distinct exit code** — non-zero only when deferrals > 0 AND the run is
   non-interactive/scripted, so CI notices.
3. **Fold into `chunk_flush_failed_files`** — simplest, but wrong: it would conflate "permanently
   failed, zero chunks, no automatic retry" with "deferred, will self-heal", and would make
   nexus-4s1ww's exit code fire on a self-healing condition. Recommend against; recorded so the
   option is visibly rejected rather than silently unconsidered.

Whichever is chosen, the plumbing is the same shape: `_contain_transient_upsert` needs to record
the deferred path (a counter or a set, alongside `_quality_gate_failed` / `_batch_failures`),
`index_repository`'s return dict needs a `transient_deferred_files` key next to
`chunk_flush_failed_files` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:4772`), and `src/nexus/commands/index.py` needs
to render it.

## Non-vacuous test

- Drive a run where one prose file's index call raises `VectorServiceError(code=503)`. Assert the
  returned dict reports the deferral (`transient_deferred_files == 1`) AND that the deferral text
  appears in the command's stdout. Asserting only the dict key would prove the counter, not the
  user-visible behaviour that is the whole point.
- Assert `chunk_flush_failed_files` stays 0 in that run — the two conditions must remain
  distinguishable (this is the assertion that pins the option-3 rejection).
- If option 2 is chosen, assert the exit code in both directions: deferrals > 0 -> non-zero,
  deferrals == 0 -> 0.
- **Non-vacuity**: remove the counter increment inside `_contain_transient_upsert` and the
  stdout assertion must go RED. Verify by deleting it.

Related: nexus-4s1ww (GH #1432, the flush-failure exit code this sits beside), nexus-rhwg5 (GH
#1432 ask 3, flush progress), nexus-7yfe6 (introduced the deferral behaviour), nexus-okz5t
(closed: escalating a file that transient-504s every run — the adjacent "deferred forever"
problem), and the companion P1 bead wrapping `_index_one_code`.

title: index: mechanize the no-silent-phase guarantee
description:
Source of record: T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` (entry 22159), proposal b3,
bead-breakdown item 11. STRUCTURAL. Depends on the heartbeat and counter beads landing first.

## Problem

The liveness guarantee proposed in the assessment ("no phase may exceed N seconds without producing
output") is, as designed, a matter of DISCIPLINE. Every new post-processing phase added to
`src/nexus/indexer.py` must remember to arm the heartbeat or emit a counter. There are already
~20 `[post]` emitter sites (assessment section 2 channel 2), and the history says discipline does
not hold:

- nexus-uizok (closed) added phase markers for the drain, and its own description notes that the
  stretch BEFORE the prune phase was missed even though the same ambiguity was named in a comment
  three lines away.
- nexus-vatx (closed) shipped a 60s ETA ticker for exactly this class; it has been dead on every
  run since (latch bug, sibling bead) and nothing noticed for months.
- The 2026-08-10 assessment then found 627.6s of post-processing behind 16 lines.

Three independent attempts, three silent regressions. This is the case for mechanization.

## Ask (proposal b3, size M)

1. A phase REGISTRY: each phase declares a cost class and an optional denominator provider.
2. A test that asserts EVERY registered phase either reports progress (has a denominator provider
   and emits) or is heartbeat-covered. A phase that is neither fails the test at authoring time
   rather than in a user's 14-minute run.

## Non-vacuity is the whole point of this bead

The failure mode for a guarantee-mechanizing test is that it enumerates an ALLOWLIST which quietly
goes stale and ends up scanning nothing. This project has that scar tissue: nexus-th15h (mode-lint
exclusion sets with no liveness check: 21/58 nodeids and 4/73 files were dead) and nexus-ogzsz (a
liveness check that cannot fail). Requirements for this test:

- **Enumerate from the CODE, not from a hand-maintained list.** Discover phases by walking the
  registry / emitter sites, so a new phase is in scope the moment it exists.
- **Assert non-emptiness with a floor.** If the discovered phase count is below the known count,
  FAIL. A scan that finds zero phases must be a red, never a green.
- **Measure the detector against a deliberately broken fix.** Add a phase that is silent by
  construction and prove the test goes red. A guarantee test that has never been shown to fail is
  the same false-comfort shape it exists to prevent.
- Assert every emitted phase line honours the output constraints below, so the mechanization also
  guards the gate-breaking shapes rather than just the silence.

## Sequencing

Land AFTER the heartbeat bead (a1) and the two counter beads (a3, a4). This bead mechanizes a
guarantee; the guarantee has to exist and be satisfied first, or the test lands red or, worse,
lands allowlisted.

## HARD CONSTRAINTS (binding on ANY change to `nx index` output)

From an exhaustive consumer sweep in T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10` section 7.4.
Constraints 1 and 2 break their gate SILENTLY (wrong result, not a red). Read them before writing
a single line of output code.

1. **Never emit a new line matching `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]`.**
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:197-203` counts lines of that shape
   (`grep -cv skipped`) into a TWO-SIDED gate (run1 >= 10, run2 <= 6). A new line of that shape
   makes the gate fail silently wrong, not loudly.
   `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh:399-401` counts the same shape (>= 3).
   => Put any fraction LATER in the line, behind the `  [post] ` prefix. Correct shape:
   `  [post] Pruning deleted files: collection 1/3, page 42/96 (3m10s elapsed)`.
2. **Never emit `\r` on the non-TTY path.** `tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts
   `"\r" not in result.output`.
3. **Do not touch the `[debug-timing]` block.**
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/aggregate.py:20-21,27` hard-parses the header wording and the
   ordered stage rows and raises `ValueError` on drift.
4. **`Done.` must stay, and stay LAST.** 8 assertion sites across 6 files
   (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:84,103`; `tests/test_4s1ww_chunk_flush_failure_reporting.py:277`;
   `tests/test_indexer_e2e.py:864,907`; `tests/test_index_taxonomy.py:106`;
   `tests/test_index_reminder.py:192,212`; `tests/test_scenario_journeys.py:411`), two of them
   deliberately on failure paths. Also `tail -5` consumers
   (`tests/e2e/release-sandbox.sh:528,535,560,568`; `scenarios/03_skills.sh:11`) degrade if new
   trailing lines are appended after the summary. Add nothing after `Done.`.
5. **Do not reword the summary sentences.** `tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` pins ~50 exact
   sentences including em-dashes and `(s)` pluralization; `tests/test_index_cmd.py:514,571-574,588`
   and `tests/test_index_pdf_batch.py:117-118,141,189` likewise.
6. **`[post]` is the SAFE channel to extend.** Nothing asserts on the `[post]` markers;
   `tests/e2e/index-throughput-bench/test_aggregate.py:19` fixtures one as noise the parser must
   skip. Nothing in `.github/workflows/**` or `conexus/hooks/**` parses `nx index` output at all.
   This is the single most useful fact for anything in this family.

## Conventions to REUSE, not reinvent (assessment 7.3)

- Completed duration: `({t:.1f}s)`.
- Projection: `~{_fmt_duration(...)} remaining` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:2894-2903`: `42s` / `1m30s` / `2h05m`).
- Rate: `{rate*60:.1f} <unit>/min`.
- ETA regimes: `_format_eta` (`src/nexus/commands/index.py:216-236`) -> `pending` / `~N min remaining` / `done`.
- Where no denominator exists, say so: `still running (1m12s elapsed)`. Never a fake percentage,
  never a fake ETA.

description:

2. **`[post]` markers** `src/nexus/commands/index.py:566-578` (`on_phase`) ->

3. **Raw `sys.stderr.write` with `\r`** `src/nexus/indexer.py:969`, used at 970, 1364, 1369, 1380,

4. **A second, nested tqdm** `src/nexus/indexer.py:2657-2662` inside `_prune_misclassified`,

title: [bug] per_collection_chunk_cap fails OPEN to 300 — a failed embedding-mode probe silently restores the pre-fix blowup cap with no log line
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10, deep-analyst assessment of the 7.5.0 local-index cluster (T2 [22152]).

src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:638-649 — per_collection_chunk_cap's probe returns None on any
failure, and None falls through to the default of 300 for code__ collections. That default is the
exact value the 7.5.0 onnx-local work identified as the blowup trigger.

So a probe failure does not degrade to the SAFE value, it degrades to the DANGEROUS one: a
transient error while determining "is this an onnx-local engine that needs the small cap?" silently
restores pre-fix behaviour, and nothing in the logs distinguishes "probed, engine is cloud/Voyage,
300 is correct" from "probe failed, guessed 300".

This is the no-silent-fallback-for-correctness class: the fallback direction is wrong, and the
fallback is unobservable.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this occurs in practice. No log evidence of a probe failure has been
collected. Establishing it is part of the work — if it never fires, the fix is still correct but
the priority stays low.

## Ask
1. Fail toward the safe cap, not the unsafe one, when the probe cannot determine the embedding mode.
2. Emit a structured line when the probe fails, so the guess is visible rather than silent.
3. Test pins the failure branch specifically (probe raises -> cap is the small one, and a warning
   is emitted). Non-vacuity: red if the branch reverts to 300.

Related: nexus-33hpq (closed, the cap), nexus-b32rx, nexus-v2mdd (same fail-open-to-green class).

per_collection_chunk_cap's docstring (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:557-564) and the CHANGELOG [7.5.0] Fixed entry for nexus-33hpq both state the cap=16 measurement as '2.15 GB peak'. That number was superseded before this critique: a subsequent full end-to-end re-run of the 36-file repro (continuous external RSS sampling across the whole release-gate battery, SHAKEDOWN PASSED 11/11) recorded a FINAL peak of 3.03 GB — the 2.15 GB figure in the docstring is a mid-run sample, not the actual peak, and is ~41% below the best-available number.

Doesn't change the safety conclusion (3.03 GB is still far below any headroom concern, and the docstring no longer makes a specific machine-RAM claim after the nexus-b32rx round-1 fix removed the unbacked '16 GB laptop' framing). But it is exactly the class of issue nexus-b32rx finding 1 was about — a permanent record (docstring + CHANGELOG, both) citing a specific measured number that isn't the best-available evidence, discovered in the same review cycle where the record was corrected for a different accuracy problem.

title: migration-rehearsal COLD_TAG carries a comment saying "do not bump at the next floor bump" while a live test fails the release unless it IS bumped
description: Hit during the 7.5.0 cut (2026-08-09). tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh COLD_TAG has an in-line comment ending "Bumping it further is a no-op; do not fix it at the next floor bump." But tests/test_engine_version.py::TestDownstreamConsumersTrackTheFloor::test_cold_rehearsal_tag_is_at_least_the_floor asserts COLD_TAG >= REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION and HARD-FAILS the release battery otherwise (it cites the 2026-07-12 incident where a floor bump left COLD_TAG two tags behind while --cold was still live). A conexus relay repeated the comments guidance to me verbatim as "the older standing bump-COLD_TAG pending item is stale guidance", so the contradiction has already propagated into cross-instance advice. RESOLUTION TAKEN AT THE CUT: bumped COLD_TAG to v0.1.69. It is functionally a no-op (--cold was retired at RDR-155 P4b and the branch is unreachable; --acquire supplies its own mandatory NEXUS_SERVICE_TAG), it satisfies the live gate, and it matches the SAME comments own closing rationale that "a future un-retirement of --cold would want this constant already tracking the floor" — which is itself an argument FOR keeping it in sync, so the comment contradicts itself as well as the test. DECIDE ONE WAY: either (a) delete the do-not-bump sentence and keep the test, making float-with-the-floor the rule, or (b) retire the test alongside the retired --cold path and let the constant freeze. Do not leave a comment and a gate giving opposite instructions — the next person hits the same 10-minute detour mid-release. Related: nexus-b6qlf (one-source-of-truth for engine constants), RDR-155 P4b.

title: expectations type_enc collision (a:b vs literal a__b) is now correctness-bearing, not merely cosmetic — it keys credit slots, not just lockdir names
description: Minor 2 from the nexus-7z7rj round-3 review ([22112]), confirmed genuinely separate. The ':'->'__' encoding used to derive per-type identifiers means a subagent type literally containing '__' collides with one containing ':'. This was cosmetic when it only named a lockdir; since the round-3 fix keys CREDIT SLOTS by the same encoding, a collision now merges two types' credit pools — one type can consume another's credit, producing both spurious blocks and spurious passes across the pair. No live collision is known today (current subagent types do not contain '__'), which is why this is P3 rather than higher, but the failure is silent if one ever appears. FIX: use an unambiguous encoding (hash, or escape the escape character). Related: nexus-7z7rj, nexus-ols6a.

title: expectations self-recovery scan starts at spent+1, so a re-entering agent whose orphaned slot sits at an index <= spent burns a second credit unit
description: Minor 1 from the nexus-7z7rj round-3 review ([22112]), confirmed by the developer as genuinely separate and not addressed at fc066671. The crash-recovery readlink walk begins at spent+1, so it cannot find an agent's own previously-claimed slot once spent has advanced past that index — the re-entering agent claims a SECOND slot, burning another unit of credit for the same dispatch. Compounds the pool decay tracked in the sibling bead. FIX: start the self-recovery scan at index 1 rather than spent+1 (the walk is bounded by credit, so the cost is trivial). Related: nexus-7z7rj, nexus-ols6a.

title: expectations.sh round-3 residuals: false sweep rationale, unguarded ${vfields[0]} under set -u, missing EXPECT dedupe in owes_report
description:
CRITIQUE FINDINGS (substantive-critic, 2026-08-09) on nexus-7z7rj round 3 (a7cc2752 +
6ae85883). Full critique: T2 nexus/critique-7z7rj-round3-2026-08-09 [22111].
Sibling of the P1 nexus-ols6a. All three are small and independent.

1. FALSE SWEEP RATIONALE (correct the comment). expectations_sweep's new slot-reap
   comment claims "deleting a slot whose ledger still exists is impossible here because
   the ledger's own mtime gates only its own removal (a slot older than 7 days belongs
   to a session that has been idle at least that long)". Empirically false: a symlink's
   mtime is its creation time and never refreshes, while the ledger's mtime refreshes on
   every append. Probed - `find . -name '*.credit.*' -type l -mtime +7` matched a live
   session's slot while `find . -name '*.expectations' -type f -mtime +7` did not match
   its fresh ledger. Consequence is benign and self-healing (reconciliation rebuilds
   slots 1..spent, and the `credit > spent` gate still caps rows at credit), so this is
   a comment/rationale correction, not a behaviour fix. It matters because round 3's
   whole thesis is that prior rounds' stated invariants were false.

2. UNGUARDED ARRAY DEREF UNDER set -u (one token). expectations_owes_report line ~639:
   `verdict="${vfields[0]}"`. Probed: `IFS=$'\t' read -r -a f <<<""` yields a 0-element
   array and `${f[0]}` under `set -u` is a fatal unbound-variable. Reachable only when
   awk dies (the file is `-r` guarded), and subagent-stop.sh does not set -u - but
   tests/e2e/lib/expectations_test.sh does, and that is exactly the suite 6ae85883 just
   rescued from a two-day set -u blackout. Pre-fix an empty verdict fell benignly to
   `*) return 1`. Use `${vfields[0]:-}`.

3. MISSING EXPECT DEDUPE IN owes_report (closes nexus-ma5tg's real blast radius).
   owes_report's awk counts `$2=="EXPECT" && $3==ty` with NO dispatch_id dedupe, while
   expectations_undeclared and expectations_census DO dedupe on `$5`. So the live guard
   and the retro audit compute DIFFERENT credit for the same ledger. Adding
   `$2=="EXPECT" && $5!="" && ($5 in dseen) {next}` / `$2=="EXPECT" {if ($5!="")
   dseen[$5]=1; ...}` - the idiom already present ~200 lines away in the same file -
   removes owes_report's exposure to the duplicate-EXPECT class entirely, leaving
   nexus-ma5tg (the identical reap TOCTOU in agent-dispatch-expect.sh:137-138) as a
   census-cosmetics bug rather than a cross-surface disagreement.
   NOTE for whoever picks up ma5tg: its direction is a spurious CREDIT (surplus), not a
   spurious DEBIT, so it produces over-blocking only and has NO deferred-miss analogue -
   verified. That is why deferring it is honest, unlike 7z7rj.

4. DOCSTRING OVERCLAIM (minor). _expectations_claim_credit says readlink "audits who
   holds each unit". Slot index equals row position only when claims and appends
   interleave in the same order, which is not guaranteed. Count-wise harmless; the
   audit claim should be softened.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
RE-REVIEW 2026-08-09 (substantive-critic) against fc066671. Items 1-3 of this bead are
LANDED and verified: sweep rationale corrected to name reconciliation as the actual
safety reason; ${vfields[0]:-} guarded; EXPECT dispatch_id dedupe added to owes_report's
awk (which also closes nexus-ma5tg's owes_report blast radius). Item 4 (docstring
overclaim) is still open, and two new small findings replace the closed ones. Re-scope
this bead to the following three:

4. DOCSTRING OVERCLAIM (unchanged). _expectations_claim_credit still says readlink
   "audits who holds each unit". Slot index equals row position only when claims and
   appends interleave in the same order, which is not guaranteed. Count-wise harmless;
   soften the audit claim.

5. NEW - THE credit-slot-orphan CAUSE STATES AN INFERENCE AS FACT. The stderr message
   and the resulting BLOCKED ledger row assert "so a claimant was killed between its slot
   claim and its CONSUMED row". Measured against fc066671: the cause ALSO fires,
   deterministically, when a legitimate WINNER stalls longer than the 0.1s recheck
   spacing between its `ln -s` and its append while a concurrent racer loses the claim -
   12/12 false-orphan at a 0.5s appender stall, 0/12 at 0.05s. That is the intended,
   safe, disclosed direction (no slot burned, no row written, non-persistent), so this is
   not a defect in the DETECTOR - it is a defect in the WORDING, which goes into a
   permanent ledger row an operator will later use for forensics. Reword to "a claimant
   claimed a slot and never recorded it (killed mid-window, or stalled past the
   recheck)". Directly implicates the standing directive about never writing an inference
   into the permanent record as fact.

6. NEW - THE LOCK-TRIES CLAMP IS 6x THE HOOK TIMEOUT. NX_EXPECT_LOCK_TRIES clamps at 600
   (60s) while conexus/hooks/hooks.json gives SubagentStop a 10s timeout. Verified that
   200 is set ONLY inside pytest extra_env - never in production, never in CI env - so
   the shipped default of 10 tries (~1s) is comfortably inside the timeout and the
   round-2 lock-exhausted disclosure works as designed. But any operator who raises the
   knob above ~100 converts a DISCLOSED lock-exhausted block into a hook SIGKILLed
   mid-loop, i.e. an undisclosed unguarded stop - the exact failure mode the knob was
   added (nexus-4b8sz) to mitigate. Derive the clamp from the hook timeout rather than an
   independent literal 600, or refuse/warn above the timeout-derived ceiling.

title: gap4 census gate cannot distinguish a docstring mention from a real call: naming converge_engine in prose reddens test_engine_mechanism_callers_are_allowlisted, pressuring contributors to allowlist non-callers and blunt the census
description: Surfaced by the nexus-hdumg correction round (2026-08-09). tests/.../test_gap4_two_mechanisms.py::test_engine_mechanism_callers_are_allowlisted text-scans src/nexus/** skipping only # comments, so a DOCSTRING that names converge_engine in explanatory prose reads as a call site and reddens the gate. In this instance the developer correctly rewrote the docstring to describe the finisher without symbol names and left a GOTCHA note, but that only works if the next person also knows not to reach for the allowlist. FIX DIRECTIONS: make the scan docstring-aware (skip string literals / use AST rather than text), or split the allowlist into real-callers vs prose-mentions so an exemption cannot silently grant call-site permission. Same class as the sanction-shrink work in nexus-4okz4 (a gate whose false positives train people to weaken it). Related: nexus-hdumg, T2 [22093] GOTCHA note.

title: test_lock_tries_clamped_to_ceiling is load-sensitive by construction: 600 fork+execs inside a fixed 30s subprocess timeout
description:
tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py::TestBlockMode::test_lock_tries_clamped_to_ceiling shadows sleep with a no-op script on PATH and then makes the hook spin its FULL clamped budget — 600 loop iterations, each forking+execing the fake sleep — inside _run_hook's fixed 30s subprocess timeout. On a saturated box those 600 fork+execs can exceed 30s and the test fails on timeout with nothing wrong in the code under test.

OBSERVED 2026-08-09: a sibling agent's full suite (disjoint diff: upgrade_ladder + chash_tables) failed on exactly this test and nothing else, while this box was carrying a background maven build plus concurrent 8-12 process stress bursts. Not shared-state corruption — the hook's ledger/lock state is per-session and tmp_path-scoped in tests (verified) — purely machine load.

This is the same 'passes 95% of the time' shape the nexus-7z7rj arc has been trying to get out of this module: the test's non-vacuity depends on a wall-clock race rather than on the property. Options: (a) assert the clamp without executing the loop (the observable is the printed '(600 tries)' count — a much smaller budget with a separately-asserted clamp computation would prove the same thing), (b) raise the subprocess timeout well clear of any plausible load, or (c) drive the clamp arithmetic directly rather than through a full hook invocation. Prefer (a) or (c).

Context: nx

title: test_contains_scratch_section_when_entries_exist is load-sensitive: post_compact_hook.sh must finish inside a fixed 15s subprocess timeout
description:
Observed 2026-08-09 during the nexus-hdumg full suite (uv run pytest -n auto, worktree agent-ac2e1beee0b2310cf).

SYMPTOM: subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Popen returncode -9 (SIGKILL), orig_timeout=15, raised from tests/hooks/test_post_compact_hook.py:32 _run_hook -> bash conexus/hooks/scripts/post_compact_hook.sh. No assertion was ever evaluated.

CLASS: identical to nexus-i514o / nexus-623af (test_lock_tries_clamped_to_ceiling), but a DIFFERENT test and a DIFFERENT script, so it is not covered by those beads. post_compact_hook.sh shells nx (T1 scratch read over HTTP to the engine) inside a fixed 15s cap; under -n auto with concurrent load (a sibling agent was running a maven gate-jar build plus stress bursts) the cap is exceeded.

EVIDENCE it is not a code defect:
- standalone: tests/hooks/test_post_compact_hook.py + tests/hooks/test_subagent_stop_hook.py together = 59 passed in 29.93s
- the concurrent hdumg diff touches only upgrade_ladder/{protocol,runner,rungs/chash_rekey}.py + db/{chash_tables,pg_provision}.py; git diff --stat -- conexus/hooks/ tests/hooks/ is EMPTY
- the two reds in that run landed on different xdist workers (gw10, gw11), so it is box-wide starvation, not one wedged worker

FIX SHAPE (same as i514o): either raise the cap, or make the assertion not require the hook to complete a full live-substrate round trip under a fixed wall clock. A fixed short wall-clock budget around a bash+CLI+HTTP round trip is not a safe assertion vehicle on a shared dev box.

SWEEP NOTE: worth auditing every tests/hooks/*.py subprocess.run(timeout=N) for the same shape rather than raising them one red at a time.

title: test-substrate: initdb/pg_ctl-start/sidecar-write inside the boot semaphore have no try/except — a controlled failure leaks pgdata with no time bound
description: Found by the substantive-critic during the nexus-ui654 round-2b delta ([22051] Part 4). PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by ui654: the original pre-ui654 code had the identical unwrapped initdb call. Inside _boot_semaphore_slot()'s with-block, initdb / pg_ctl start / the first sidecar write are unwrapped, so a CONTROLLED failure (exception, not a kill) leaves the pgdata dir behind with no reaper coverage until the placeholder sidecar exists — i.e. an initdb failure leaks an un-sidecarred dir permanently. Note the dominant real-world failure mode (hard SIGKILL of the worker) is unaffected either way and is already honestly described in the docstring as the residual. FIX: wrap the semaphore-held subprocess calls in the try/except-cleanup pattern _kill_pg() already demonstrates downstream (shutil.rmtree the partial pgdata on failure, re-raise). Cheap. Related: nexus-ui654 (closed), nexus-shn9o (substrate reuse), nexus-lgdy1 (the sidecar/reap mechanism).

title: test-substrate: per-session PG reuse across xdist workers (yhmav template-clone analogue)
description:
Follow-up from nexus-ui654: one PG substrate boot per xdist WORKER process (not per session) is the root topology behind the concurrency-window shm exhaustion nexus-ui654's semaphore mitigates. A deeper fix would reuse ONE PG cluster per pytest SESSION with per-worker databases/tenants -- the yhmav template-clone analogue (tests/db/PgContainerHelper-style per-fork container reuse already used by the JAVA suite) applied to the Python engine substrate.

Topology evidence (nexus-ui654 investigation, T2 nexus/nexus-ui654-fix-2026-08-09 [22049]): tests/_engine_substrate.py:65-67's _state/_lock are MODULE-LEVEL globals -- under pytest -n auto every xdist worker is a separate process with its own module import, so ensure_engine()/_boot() run once per WORKER, not once per SESSION. The file's own pre-existing _WORKER_SHARD_WIDTH comment (~lines 90-105) already documents this: 'every worker is a SEPARATE process that independently calls _boot()'. This is why N concurrent sessions x M workers-per-session produced 17-31 stale dirs, not just N.

NOT 90% there already: there is no shared-state primitive at all today -- no lockfile registry, no port-coordination beyond the existing disjoint low-range port sharding (_worker_shard_range). A real implementation needs: (1) a cross-process leader-election so exactly one worker per session boots the shared PG (the others wait/attach), (2) per-worker DATABASES (not just tenants) inside that one PG so xdist workers stay isolated from each other's schema-level operations, (3) session-end teardown coordination (last worker out tears down, not first worker to finish).

Scope: bigger architectural change than nexus-ui654's semaphore (which bounds concurrent BOOTS, not the boot COUNT). File as its own tracked unit of work; do not fold into nexus-ui654's semaphore fix.

title: T3 singleton leak: AST lint checks reset-call syntax, not reset behavior — add a behavioral regression test
design:
nexus-gtl01 review finding (review-gtl01-fix-2026-08-09, code-review-expert),
on commit 3a9aafb3 (tests/test_t3_singleton_leak_lint.py).

The new lint mechanizes ONE regression class well: a fixture that seeds
mcp_infra._t3_instance (or calls inject_t3/_inject_t3) and never calls a
reset (_reset_singletons/reset_singletons, or inject_t3(None)) after its
yield. Verified independently during review: it scans all 715 tests/test_*.py
files (non-vacuous), and correctly flags the exact pre-fix injected_active
fixture when re-parsed from `git show HEAD^:tests/test_catalog_e2e.py`.

Gap: the lint is purely syntactic — it checks that a call to
_reset_singletons()/reset_singletons() (or an explicit `= None`/`inject_t3(None)`)
TEXTUALLY APPEARS after the yield. It does not check that the reset call
actually clears _t3_instance at runtime. If `mcp_infra.reset_singletons()`
itself later regressed to no longer touch `_t3_instance` (e.g. an
accidental refactor of the `global _t1_instance, _t1_isolated, _t3_instance,
...` line), every fixture using the documented pattern would still pass this
lint while the original nexus-gtl01 leak silently came back.

There is no dedicated behavioral test pinning "reset_singletons() clears
_t3_instance to None" (test_mcp_infra_t1_reset.py pins the narrower
reset_t1_for_release() contract explicitly excluding T3; no T3-equivalent
exists). The pre-fix deterministic two-test-ordering repro (documented in
T2 nexus/gtl01-root-cause-2026-08-09 [22027] and the commit message) is not
preserved as a committed regression test — it exists only as a report/commit
narrative, reproducible manually via:
  uv run pytest 'tests/test_catalog_e2e.py::TestMCP::test_search_returns_indexed_files' \
                'tests/test_scenario_journeys.py::test_index_md_creates_doc_level_content_with_catalog_registration' -q

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: SECOND OCCURRENCE + PRECISE MECHANISM 2026-08-09 (was filed 08-08 from run [21831]; recurred today in a concurrent-agent session and got fully diagnosed). FAILURE MODE, which is the load-bearing evidence: it is NOT an assertion failure — it is subprocess.TimeoutExpired, Popen returncode -9 (SIGKILL), orig_timeout=30, raised inside _run_hook's subprocess.run(..., timeout=30). The clamp value is never evaluated at all, so a red here says nothing about the property under test. WHY IT IS STRUCTURALLY LOAD-SENSITIVE: the test sets NX_EXPECT_LOCK_TRIES=999999 (clamped to 600) and shadows the sleep binary with a no-op on PATH so the 600-iteration bash retry loop runs its full count without wall-clock cost — but each iteration still forks+execs the shadow, and ~600 fork+execs that cost about a second idle have no headroom against a fixed 30s cap on a saturated box. Today's trigger: a full -n auto suite in one worktree while a sibling agent ran a maven gate-jar build plus 60x8 concurrent stress bursts. HONEST LIMIT on attribution (recorded by the affected debugger): general machine load and sibling-specific load produce the IDENTICAL failure mode, so sibling causation is not proven — shared-machine contention on a timing-sensitive test is the accurate statement. COORDINATION LESSON worth keeping: separate worktrees isolate the TREE, not /tmp, absolute-path lock dirs, or CPU; this test is the canary because it is the one that budgets a fixed 30s wall clock against a 600-iteration subprocess loop. FIX DIRECTIONS (unchanged, now better motivated): assert the clamp VALUE rather than requiring all 600 iterations to execute; or scale/remove the subprocess timeout for this test; or replace the fork+exec sleep shadow with a non-forking stub. Duplicate nexus-i514o closed in favor of this bead.

'Popen: returncode: -9', stdout_seq=[], stderr_seq=[], subprocess.TimeoutExpired after 30 seconds. No assertion reached => cannot be a behavioural regression.
2. STANDALONE: 1 passed in 3.38s (~10x headroom under the 30s subprocess timeout).
3. UNDER DELIBERATE LOAD (14 CPU hogs + fork storm): FAILED, TimeoutExpired, 30.33s — reproduced ON DEMAND. A partially-loaded run landed at 26.08s, passing but barely, which is the margin this test actually runs on.

title: Engine suite wall-clock: evaluate surefire forkCount parallelization (17-18 min full run, mostly testcontainers-PG-bound)
description:
Hal idea 2026-08-08 (during the 11gh6 landing wait). Full ./mvnw test = ~17:36 for 1895 tests, dominated by testcontainers PostgreSQL integration classes — largely I/O-bound, prime forking candidate.

Approach sketch (payoff order):
1. surefire forkCount=3-4 with reuseForks: per-fork JVM + per-fork testcontainers PG (random ports, isolation by construction). Est. 17min -> 5-7min at the cost of RAM (one PG + JVM per fork).
2. testcontainers.reuse.enable to amortize container startup.
3. Do NOT pursue intra-JVM JUnit 5 parallelism: @Order-annotated classes (CatalogManifestSweepRepositoryTest etc.) encode intra-class sequencing and static container fields contend; fork-granularity sidesteps the whole audit.

PRE-WORK REQUIRED: audit for tests assuming a quiescent DB they didn't provision — the 11gh6 gate tests (external-connection advisory-lock holders, Order 20-25 block tests) deliberately violate that assumption and MUST stay fork-isolated from anything sharing their container. Also verify the lifecycle-conformance suite (tests/daemon parity on the Python side) doesn't read surefire report counts that forking would restructure (see project_surefire_stale_reports memory: stale surefire reports already inflate counts).

CI angle: the PR-gated service-ci job pays this wall too — but weigh vs CI cost discipline (parallel forks on hosted runners = same core budget; the win is local dev + release-battery latency, not CI dollars).

title: _service_t2_lock is held across the network round trip — the THIRD convoy in the flush-grain hook chain, unfiled until now
description:
Found by the nexus-eslkl interleaving audit, 2026-08-08 (T2 nexus/design-eslkl-hook-lock-narrowing [21731]).

mcp_infra._service_t2_lock (declared mcp_infra.py:123, acquired :383 in t2_index_write, rationale docstring :119-123) is held for the FULL duration of every T2 write — network round trip included — exactly like catalog/factory._service_catalog_lock (nexus-u2u0n) and for the identical stated reason: 'a concurrent caller can never close() the instance while another thread is still inside write_fn(db)'.

It is the third of THREE nested process-wide locks on the flush-grain hook path:
  LockedHookRegistry (nexus-eslkl)
    -> _service_t2_lock        (taxonomy_assign_batch_hook, batched aspect enqueue)
    -> _service_catalog_lock   (manifest_write_batch_hook)  [nexus-u2u0n]

MEASURED HELD TIME: taxonomy 12.8s/run on the perfprobe-740 workload (109 files / 29 flushes), plus the batched aspect enqueue (unmeasured — _flush_hook_by_name['aspect_enqueue'] exists but is absent from T2 [21723]'s table; est ~3s/run at 29 enqueue_many calls x the ~0.11s round-trip floor). NOT contended today for the same unflattering reason u2u0n gives for the catalog lock: LockedHookRegistry upstream pre-serializes the hook chains, so T2 traffic arrives pre-serialized and this lock never has to block. Narrow eslkl and this becomes a ceiling, with no measurement showing it until then.

THE CRITICAL SECTION IS OVER-BROAD ON ITS OWN TERMS, same as u2u0n. The stated purpose is protecting the CLIENT SWAP (error-triggered eviction of the cached T2Database when a rotated storage_service lease is baked into its Http*Store clients), not the call. _service_t2_write_locked already does the eviction correctly; it just does not do the compare-and-swap identity check that would make a narrow section safe. Direction, identical in shape to u2u0n's: resolve the T2Database under the lock, RELEASE, run write_fn, and on failure re-acquire and evict only if _service_t2_db is still the same instance.

SAFETY NOTE (from the eslkl audit): narrowing this one is LOW risk. Both consumers are idempotent server-side — TaxonomyRepository.assignFromChashes runs in ONE tenantScope transaction with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (own pass) / GREATEST-wins (cross pass), and aspect_queue.enqueue_many is a queue insert the worker claims idempotently. Unlike the catalog side there is no multi-op client-side read-modify-write sequence to interleave.

MUST LAND WITH nexus-eslkl AND nexus-u2u0n as ONE change. Landing any one of the three alone produces a measurement that looks like a win in its own timer and moves nothing — the wait relocates to the next lock down (the itpdc relocation signature, one layer further). Sequence the whole bundle AFTER nexus-67qsd/nexus-jk88j, which cut the manifest critical section 44.0s -> ~12s and remove the sole interleaving hazard by construction.

MEASUREMENT GATE for the bundle: hook_lock_wait_seconds down AND service_catalog_op_stats()[*].lock_wait_s NOT up by the same amount AND wall down. Add an equivalent per-op stat for this lock (mirroring catalog/factory.service_catalog_op_stats, and timing the acquisition on BOTH sides if a getattr-style seam is introduced — see u2u0n's instrumentation-trap warning).

title: _service_catalog_lock is held across the network round trip — latent second convoy, becomes the bottleneck the moment nexus-eslkl narrows the first
description:
Found while attributing nexus-jb4pp, 2026-08-08 (T2 nexus/flush-tail-investigation-2026-08-08).

catalog/factory.py _SharedServiceCatalogHandle holds the module-global _service_catalog_lock for the FULL duration of every forwarded call — network round trip included — in BOTH __getattr__ (attribute resolution) and _call. So every catalog operation in the process (manifest write, RUNFENCE begin_index_run_many, registration, reads) is strictly serialized against every other, across all indexing workers.

MEASURED TODAY: NOT currently contended — per-op lock_wait is 0.0-0.9s per run. The reason is unflattering rather than reassuring: LockedHookRegistry upstream (nexus-eslkl) already serializes the hook chains, so catalog traffic arrives pre-serialized and this lock never has to block. Fix eslkl and this becomes the immediate next ceiling, with the same convoy shape and no measurement showing it until then.

The critical section is over-broad on its own terms. Its stated purpose (factory.py:41-56) is that "a concurrent caller's eviction-on-error can never race a call in flight". Eviction only needs to protect the CLIENT SWAP, not the call: the code already does the compare-and-swap correctly (the "is current" identity check), and that check is exactly what makes a narrow critical section safe. Direction: resolve the client under the lock, RELEASE, make the call, and on failure re-acquire and evict only if the shared slot still holds the same instance.

CAUTION for whoever takes this: instrumenting only _call reads a near-zero wait while threads are demonstrably serializing — the queueing happens in __getattr__. A timer on the wrong side of this convoy reports "no contention" with total confidence (cost one probe pass to catch). service_catalog_op_stats() (added with jb4pp) now times BOTH acquisitions; keep it that way.

Sequence: nexus-eslkl first, then re-measure with service_catalog_op_stats before doing anything here.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
Design memo for the blocking bead is done: T2 nexus/design-eslkl-hook-lock-narrowing [21731]. THREE amendments to this bead:

(a) SEQUENCING IS WRONG. 'nexus-eslkl first, then re-measure' — on the numbers EITHER ALONE delivers ~nothing. eslkl alone relocates ~90s of the 104s hook-lock wait onto THIS lock (the same timer-relocation signature that proved itpdc was a convoy); u2u0n alone stays invisible because the hook lock upstream keeps pre-serializing. They must land TOGETHER, as one change with one measurement pass.

(b) A THIRD LOCK OF THE IDENTICAL SHAPE IS UNFILED: mcp_infra._service_t2_lock (declared :123, held :383, docstring :119-123). Held across the FULL network round trip for the same 'a concurrent caller can never close() an in-flight instance' reason, takes the same CAS fix (resolve under lock, release, call, re-acquire and evict only if the shared slot still holds the same instance), and is uncontended today for the same unflattering reason this bead gives. It serializes taxonomy_assign_batch_hook (12.8s/run held) and the batched aspect enqueue. Becomes the ceiling right after this one. NEEDS A BEAD.

(c) 'Does the catalog writer need finer locking, or is it thread-safe per-op?' — TWO-PART ANSWER. The TRANSPORT needs none: HttpCatalogClient owns pooled httpx.Client connections (thread-safe) and the engine serializes per-row, so the CAS-narrowing sketched in this bead's description is sound exactly as written. What is NOT safe is the multi-op SEQUENCE in _manifest_write_loop (mcp_infra.py:1430-1490): get_chunk_chashes -> atomic_manifest_replace -> orphaned_chashes -> T3 DELETE -> resync -> complete_index_run, six separately-locked ops with a real TOCTOU in the middle (a concurrent doc's manifest can reference a chash this thread's sweep just proved orphaned and deleted). So narrowing this lock is safe for the transport and UNSAFE for the manifest hook unless nexus-jk88j lands first (sweep folded into /manifest/write_many's server-side transaction) or the manifest chain keeps a per-chain lock.

The instrumentation-trap warning in this bead's description is CORRECT and already honoured — _SharedServiceCatalogHandle queues in BOTH __getattr__ (factory.py:147) and _call (:162), and service_catalog_op_stats() times both. Keep it that way.

title: repo-scope guard: OR fix widens marker-check to false-positive foreign repos vendoring conexus/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
description:
Context: nx (round-2 closure verification of nexus-w3apo, substantive-critic).

_repo_scope_is_nexus (conexus/hooks/scripts/routing/git_add_all_redirects_to_explicit_paths.py)
was fixed from fallback-only to OR semantics (Signal A basename==nexus OR Signal B
marker-file-present), correctly closing nexus-w3apo (a genuine nexus checkout with a
renamed/local origin was silently losing the vduer guard).

The OR fix has a side effect not covered by the "Known, accepted residual risks"
docstring paragraph nor by any test: Signal B (the conexus/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
marker check) now runs for EVERY push whose origin doesn't resolve to literally
"nexus" -- previously it ran only when Signal A was undeterminable (missing/unreadable
origin). Empirically reproduced (scratch repos, not the nexus tree): a foreign repo
with a real, resolvable, non-nexus origin that happens to have a
conexus/.claude-plugin/plugin.json file at its toplevel (e.g. vendored/subtree'd, or a
plugin repo hosting a plugin literally named "conexus") is now misclassified as nexus
and gets rules 2 (push-to-main) + 3 (review-coverage) applied -- pre-fix, the same repo
was correctly treated as foreign (Signal A resolved determinately, Signal B never ran).

Severity: Significant, not Critical -- fails LOUD (a visible deny with the existing
`# routing-allow:` escape), not silent, and is the same class of risk the docstring
already accepts for the "unrelated repo literally named nexus" case; it just wasn't
written down for this new instance the OR fix introduces.

Fix direction: (1) add one sentence to the module docstring's "Known, accepted residual
risks" paragraph naming this case explicitly; (2) optionally add a regression test
(foreign repo, real non-nexus origin, WITH a vendored marker file) documenting the
accepted trade-off rather than leaving it silently uncovered -- the existing
foreign_repo_on fixture explicitly asserts NO marker exists, so this shape has zero
test coverage today.

title: core.py: bare _FastMCPSettings.model_rebuild() couples nx-mcp startup to unexported mcp SDK internal
description:
Review finding (nexus-20iee implementation, batch-B review 2026-08-07).

src/nexus/mcp/core.py:19 imports Settings from the PRIVATE submodule
mcp.server.fastmcp.server (not exported via mcp.server.fastmcp's __all__ =
["FastMCP", "Context", "Image", "Audio", "Icon"]), then calls
_FastMCPSettings.model_rebuild() bare (no try/except) at module level,
line 1330, right before `mcp = FastMCP(...)`.

Verified safe TODAY (dev pin pydantic-settings 2.13.1: import + call
succeed with no error; ruff clean). But this is now a hard import-time
dependency of nx-mcp's OWN entry point (nx-mcp = "nexus.mcp.core:main")
on an unexported third-party internal. If a future mcp SDK release
renames/moves Settings, restructures the lifespan forward-ref pattern,
or otherwise makes model_rebuild() raise, nexus.mcp.core fails to
import at all -- crashing nx-mcp startup (and transitively nx-mcp-catalog
too, since nexus/mcp/__init__.py imports core before catalog). The
entire point of nexus-20iee is cosmetic (silencing
IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning); turning it into a startup-crashing
dependency is a disproportionate failure mode.

Recommend: wrap the import + model_rebuild() call in try/except Exception
with a structlog debug-level log, so a future SDK break degrades to
"warning still shown" rather than "server won't start."

Secondary, lower-severity note: the fix's coverage of nx-mcp-catalog
(src/nexus/mcp/catalog.py:21, separate console-script/process) depends
entirely on incidental import ordering in src/nexus/mcp/__init__.py
(core imported at line 3, catalog at line 41) -- verified empirically
this DOES work (Python fully executes a package's __init__.py before any
submodule), but nothing documents the dependency, and a future reorder
of those two import blocks would silently reintroduce the warning for
nx-mcp-catalog only, uncaught by the new regression test (which only
imports nexus.mcp.core directly).
close_reason: Folded into 599e4980: both the unexported-internal import AND the rebuild are guarded; failure degrades to structlog debug, never kills startup. (nexus-3hc9z filed by the other reviewer covers the same finding — closing both.)

title: No reaper for orphaned t1_handoff.<mcp_pid> marker files (nexus-d76vc follow-up)
design: nexus-d76vc's SessionStart hook writes ~/.config/nexus/t1_handoff.<mcp_pid> on /clear|/resume; the MCP lifespan's handoff watcher normally consumes+deletes it within one 5s tick. If the target MCP process dies (crash/OOM/SIGKILL) in the window between the marker being written and its next tick, the marker is NEVER consumed and persists on disk indefinitely -- confirmed by grep: none of the three existing stale-file scanners (nx doctor --check-t1, health._check_orphan_t1, console/watchers.py scan_sessions_sync) recognize the t1_handoff.* prefix (they only glob the older t1_addr.* lease format), and no other sweep touches it either. Functionally safe (the _T1_SERVER_START_TIME staleness check in mcp/core.py's _t1_handoff_tick prevents a future process incarnation from ever misapplying a stale marker even after pid reuse), but it is unbounded disk litter in a codebase that already built dedicated reaping machinery for the equivalent t1_addr.* problem. Add a doctor/health check (or fold into the existing t1_addr.* sweep) that ages out t1_handoff.* files older than some bound (e.g. a few minutes) with no live owning process.
close_reason: Shipped develop ff744321: _check_orphan_t1_handoff in health.py — both marker variants (claimed. checked first), dead-pid-only reap, EPERM=alive, fail-safe on malformed, PID-reuse tradeoff documented. title: operators/dispatch.py: tool-granted mint failure silently falls back to borrowing the parent's live T1 session, contradicting the documented T1UnavailableThisProcessError claim
design:
nexus-4lkmz / nexus-bjltu re-review finding (substantive-critic, focused re-review of the fix round, 2026-08-07).

Scope: only the 2/17 claude_dispatch call sites that grant tool access
(nx_enrich_beads, nx_plan_audit via `_subprocess_tool_grant()` in
mcp/core.py, which allowlists the WHOLE `mcp__nexus` prefix — including
scratch/scratch_manage, not just search/query).

dispatch.py's `_build_dispatch_env(ephemeral=True, grants_tool_access=True)`
mint-failure handling (lines ~195-209) logs a warning and leaves
NX_T1_SESSION/NX_T1_SESSION_ID UNSET. The code comment and T2 implementation
notes claim: "the subprocess's own nested MCP ... resolves no session id,
takes mcp.core._t1_lifespan Branch 0's 'no resolvable session' path, and
raises T1UnavailableThisProcessError on its own first T1-touching call."

This claim is only true when the PARENT has no live published T1 lease.
`claude_dispatch` unconditionally forwards NX_SESSION_ID = the parent's
conversation UUID (pre-existing nexus-4gby/5daww mechanism, line ~221-222,
applies regardless of grants_tool_access or mint success). Empirically
verified (probe against `resolve_t1_routing_tiers` + a real published
lease file via `publish_t1_session_lease`): when the parent MCP is alive
and has already completed its own Branch-0 mint (the common case for any
live session dispatching an enrich/audit operator call), a lease file
exists for the parent's session id. The nested MCP inside the tool-granted
subprocess resolves NX_SESSION_ID -> the parent's id -> finds the live
lease -> takes T1RoutingAction.USE_LEASED and BORROWS the parent's own
session token, never reaching the "no resolvable session" branch at all.

Severity assessment: NOT a rn3wo.1 violation — the borrowed identity is
the dispatch's OWN ancestor's already-legitimate session (the accepted,
designed-for USE_LEASED borrowing mechanism), not the unrelated
bare-CLI CLI-dedicated identity rn3wo.1 specifically guards against. But
it IS a documentation/design-intent accuracy gap: "own minted session per
dispatch, T1UnavailableThisProcessError on mint failure" does not hold in
this composed scenario — the subprocess silently shares the parent's
session instead, untested end-to-end (only `_build_dispatch_env` is
tested in isolation; no test exercises the composed nested-MCP
consequence).

Recommendation: either (a) update the docstring/comments in dispatch.py
and AGENTS.md to accurately describe the lease-fallback possibility for
the 2 tool-granted call sites, or (b) if the borrowed-session outcome is
undesirable (e.g. it could surface the subprocess's scratch writes inside
the parent's own `nx scratch list` unexpectedly), strip/block NX_SESSION_ID
forwarding specifically on the mint-failure path so the subprocess
genuinely reaches T1UnavailableThisProcessError as documented. Low
priority — not a security regression, narrow scope (2/17 call sites x
mint-failure x live-parent-lease), likely benign outcome in practice.

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t nexus-4lkmz-implementation-notes.md;
probe reproduced at /tmp/probe_lease_fallback.py (session-local scratchpad,
not committed).

title: tests/test_indexer_utils_repo.py::test_index_pdf_resolves_path fails standalone — cloud-mode flip without endpoint isolation leaks into ambient local service config
description:
Found while re-running the full uv run pytest -n auto suite during nexus-2t63u round 2
(unrelated implementation work). NOT caused by nexus-2t63u — verified below.

test_indexer_utils_repo.py::test_index_pdf_resolves_path fails even run standalone
(`uv run pytest tests/test_indexer_utils_repo.py::test_index_pdf_resolves_path`):

  nexus.db.managed_endpoint.ManagedServiceIncompatible: The managed nexus service is
  running an engine older than this client requires... managed nexus service at
  http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port> reported no usable release_version on /version
  (got None) — a dev/unstamped or pre-release engine is older than the minimum this
  client supports (v0.1.65).

Root cause (traced): the test does `monkeypatch.setattr("nexus.config.is_local_mode",
lambda: False)` to simulate cloud mode, and mocks `nexus.doc_indexer.make_t3` — but
`index_pdf`'s actual t3-resolution branch (doc_indexer.py ~2160-2168) only calls
`make_t3()` when `is_vector_service_mode()` is False; in the test's simulated cloud mode
it instead calls `nexus.mcp_infra.get_t3()`, which the test never mocks. That function
resolves a REAL service endpoint (self-provisioned per-test-session local engine
substrate, or worse, an ambient local install config) and runs the cloud-mode
compatibility probe against it for real, which fails because that substrate isn't a
stamped release build.

Confirmed unrelated to nexus-2t63u: this failure occurs BEFORE the test ever reaches
`_register_or_lookup_doc_id` (which the test monkeypatches away entirely and which is
the only function nexus-2t63u touched in doc_indexer.py) or any other function touched
by that bead's diff (commands/index.py, mcp_infra.py's additive-only counter block,
commands/_helpers.py). `git diff --stat` against src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py,
src/nexus/db/managed_endpoint.py, src/nexus/config.py shows zero changes from that work.

Likely fix direction: the test needs to either mock `nexus.mcp_infra.get_t3` directly
(matching what index_pdf actually calls in simulated-cloud-mode), or mock
`nexus.db.http_vector_client.is_vector_service_mode` to False so `make_t3()` (the
function it already mocks) is the one actually reached. Needs investigation into why
it apparently passed in a recent baseline run (11997 passed / 1 failed, only
test_mode_declarations_are_explicit) and failed in a later run — worker-order /
per-process singleton caching in get_http_vector_client() (module-global
_vector_client_instance / _version_probe_done, cached forever for the INCOMPATIBLE
class per its own docstring) is suspected but not confirmed; low priority since the
underlying test-isolation gap (not mocking the code path actually taken) is real
regardless of the flake mechanism.

Consolidating on sr6ov.

DIAGNOSIS (2026-08-05, developer dispatch): the census's original xdist-flake
hypothesis (partition-blindness or item-ordering divergence across -n auto

offender lists between a serial run and an -n 2 run, both before and after
the fix below, repeated 3x under -n auto. xdist workers each perform full
local collection and the controller cross-checks agreement; a genuine
mismatch aborts loudly, not as a subtle test failure.

The real cause of "passes serially, fails under -n auto" earlier today: the
TREE changed mid-session. Commit dbd2cb46 (08:59:44, nexus-du2dw) landed a
genuine unaddressed RDR-109 violation in
tests/test_health_service_checks.py::TestCheckChashConformanceReport::
test_fully_routable_collections_still_render_plain_clean (a
"code__y__voyage-code-3__v1" collection-name literal, no cloud_mode,
unexcluded) shortly after 37a53f3c (08:08:13) introduced the -n auto dev
loop. Any full-default-loop run (serial OR parallel) after dbd2cb46 would
deterministically fail; any before it would deterministically pass.

A prior fix attempt (3d9f07ad, unrelated P1d commit) reclassified this file
into the lint bucket on the "whole-repo censuses are xdist-unsafe" reading
of tests/AGENTS.md's lint-bucket rule. That was WRONG for this specific
test: unlike every other lint-bucket census (which walks the filesystem via
rglob), this one reads request.session.items, which -m/-k deselection
mutates in place (confirmed: 11733 default items collapse to 803 under
-m lint). Once lint-marked, CI's test-lint job (pytest -m lint) could
never again see the dbd2cb46 offender or any future one outside the lint
bucket -- a silent, permanent blind spot for RDR-109 Phase 1 enforcement.

FIX applied: reverted the lint-marker reclassification (file stays in the
default loop, where it is empirically xdist-safe), added the
dbd2cb46/nexus-du2dw offender to _MODE_LINT_EXCLUDE_NODEIDS with the
standard "string-literal-as-name" rationale + ratchet bump (35 -> 36), and
corrected tests/AGENTS.md's lint-bucket rule to distinguish
filesystem-scanned censuses (lint-bucket-safe) from session.items-scanned
ones (not). Full -n auto suite green (11692 passed, 0 failed) and the
lint bucket green (691 passed, 0 failed) on the current tree.

    meta_where = _identity_where(str(pdf_path), corpus)   # no content_hash -> {"source_path": pdf_path}
    ...
    batch = _vector_with_retry(col.get, where=meta_where, include=["metadatas"], ...)
    all_meta.extend(batch.get("metadatas", []))
    ...
    return {
        "chunks": count,
        "pages": sorted({m.get("page_number", 0) for m in all_meta}),
        "title": all_meta[0].get("title", "") if all_meta else "",
        "author": all_meta[0].get("source_author", "") if all_meta else "",
    }

RDR-102 D2 (2026-05-02, commit 83ac62c7) removed source_path from make_chunk_metadata
entirely, so every chunk written by the streaming PDF path carries no source_path
metadata. This where-clause therefore always matches zero rows in production, so
all_meta is always empty, and index_pdf(..., return_metadata=True) on a >=_STREAMING_THRESHOLD-page
PDF ALWAYS returns pages=[], title="", author="" -- silently wrong metadata, not an
error.

This is the same root cause as nexus-tbkk1 (the dead source_path fallback in
_identity_where) but a DIFFERENT symptom -- a metadata READ for the return value, not
a stale-chunk PRUNE -- so it was kept out of nexus-tbkk1's scope (that bead is
specifically about the four stale-chunk prune sites, all of which were deleted as
dead code; this read site is _identity_where's one remaining caller and was
deliberately left untouched pending its own fix).

Candidate fix: query metadata via the chunk ids actually just upserted (col.get(ids=...))
instead of a where-filter, mirroring how the small-doc branch already has ids/metadatas_list
in hand without a second T3 round trip -- or thread the already-known metadata through from
pipeline_index_pdf's return value instead of re-querying T3 at all.

Verification: nx index pdf <big-pdf> --collection ... via MCP/CLI with return_metadata path
exercised (or a unit test mocking the streaming branch) should show non-empty pages/title/author
after the fix; today it silently returns empty values.

title: hybridSearch evaluates the live_chunks predicate TWICE on the selective branch — redundant on the rank query
description:
Found during nexus-msz9i's EXPLAIN investigation; deliberately NOT applied there to keep that fix minimal.

PgVectorRepository.hybridSearch folds the live_chunks predicate into 'scope' (the comment at the append site says this is so all three read sites inherit it 'by construction'). But 'gate' is derived FROM 'scope', and the selective branch's rank query also reads scopeSql — so on the selective path the predicate is evaluated TWICE per call: once in the bounded gate probe (up to SELECTIVE_GATE_MAX+1 = 5001 rows) and again in the chash-IN rank query (up to 5000 rows).

The second evaluation is REDUNDANT. liveChunksPredicate references only alias.tenant_id and alias.chash — it is collection-independent, i.e. liveness is a pure function of (tenant_id, chash). Every chash in the rank query's IN-list came out of the gate, which already applied the predicate. So any row the rank query can return is already known live.

This is the same reasoning the surrounding comment already uses to justify NOT re-applying the text gate on the rank query ('the gate's matching chashes already satisfy it, so the expensive <% trigram heap-recheck runs ONCE'). The metadata where-predicates ARE correctly kept, because those are not chash-determined (two same-text rows in different collections share a chash) — liveness is.

Fix: move the append from 'scope' to 'gate'. The HNSW-first branch reads gateSql so it keeps the filter; the gate probe keeps it; only the rank query drops it. No bind-list impact (liveChunksPredicate takes no parameters, and gateBinds is copied from scopeBinds before the text-signal binds are added).

Why deferred rather than folded into msz9i: it changes WHICH read sites carry the tombstone filter. That is nexus-3ck2g-class territory — the bead whose whole point was that a read site silently lacking the filter is a data-correctness bug — so it deserves its own review round and its own argument on the record, not a quiet ride-along in a perf fix. msz9i's dead-set rewrite already restores the pre-dcf77fb7 plan shape, so this is now an optimization, not a regression fix.

Guard to add with it: a test proving a tombstoned document's chunk is still absent from hybridSearch results via the SELECTIVE branch specifically (PgVectorTombstoneFilterTest has hybrid coverage; HybridSelectiveGateTest can pin selectiveGateMax to force the branch).

title: MinerU server dies silently mid-MFR-batch (memory kill), leaves stale pidfile, pipeline degrades to per-page spawn with only a doctor-level signal
description: Observed 2026-08-02 during the gtltb fleet (log ~/.config/nexus/logs/mineru_server.log). Two server generations died at 'MFR Predict 0/65' with zero error output: the 20:14 manual start, then the election-respawned PID 81417 (the mineru_elect self-heal WORKED, then its replacement died identically at 21:05). Mechanism: MinerU misreads unified memory ('GPU Memory: 8192 GB') and picks Batch Ratio 16, so a 2-page window with ~65 formulas blows memory in the MFR model and macOS kills the process silently. Consequences: (a) stale pidfile (status correctly reports it); (b) the indexing pipeline silently falls back to in-process per-page subprocess extraction — correct output, but per-page model reloads (bursty GPU, slow) and the OOM-risk path doctor warns about; (c) no runtime signal that degradation happened. Fix directions: cap MFR batch size / formula-count per window on macOS unified memory (the misread 8192GB is the root of the bad ratio); have the server-death fallback log LOUD (structlog warning per doc, not just doctor); consider re-election retry with backoff instead of one-shot.

comments.text: ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (develop): _server_env passed MINERU_VIRTUAL_VRAM_SIZE=8192, and mineru get_vram() reads that value RAW IN GB (auto-detect paths convert bytes->GB; ratio ladder >=8->4 >=16->8 higher->16) — so every server ran at ratio 16 and was memory-killed mid MFR batch. The election/rediscovery machinery was blameless and worked as designed; it just kept spawning doomed servers. Fixed to 8 (GB, ratio 4) with a unit tripwire test (1<=v<=64) in test_mineru_config_drift.py. Live server restarted from the fixed checkout (PID 99485, env verified). title: nx index --force deletes T3 chunks before extraction, but when extraction fails the delete silently no-ops and 86 stale chunks survive — --force neither forced nor cleaned
description:
Observed on nexus-gtltb remediation doc 3 ("Short term memory in echo state networks")
after its /v1/pipeline/pages 500.

Despite `--force`, which is documented to delete existing T3 chunks before
re-extraction, 86 rows survived for that content_hash — 39 of them still carrying the
glued-prose corruption the remediation exists to remove. The document is un-remediated
rather than damaged, so there is no data loss, but the flag did not do what it says.

Two things to establish before fixing:
  a) whether the delete ran and no-opped, or never ran because extraction failed first
  b) whether the intended semantics are delete-then-write (leaving a window where the
     document has no chunks) or write-then-swap

(b) is the real question. Delete-first is only safe if failure restores; if the answer
is write-then-swap then --force should not be deleting up front at all, and the
surviving 86 rows are the correct outcome of a failed run rather than a bug.

Filed at P3 because it is a correctness-of-flag issue with no data loss, but it should
be resolved before the gtltb remediation re-runs, since the remediation's whole premise
is that --force replaces corrupted chunks.
