comments.text:
MEASURED COST, 2026-08-08 (nexus-jb4pp investigation; T2 nexus/flush-tail-investigation-2026-08-08).

This bead was filed on code reading and priced at P3. It now has a number, and the number argues for P2.

Probe: perfprobe-740 (109 files, 2074 chunks, 29 flushes), conexus 7.4.0, cloud mode, engine v0.1.68, quiet box, `nx index repo --force`. New per-op catalog instrumentation (catalog/factory.py service_catalog_op_stats) attributes the dead path directly:

  op                        calls   call_s   s/call
  get_chunk_chashes          109     10.6    0.097   <- 39upx sweep "before" read, per FILE
  atomic_manifest_replace    109     14.4    0.132   <- the fallback write, per FILE
  resync_chunk_count_cache   109     10.9    0.100   <- per FILE (write_many folds this in server-side)
  ---------------------------------------------------
  subtotal                   327     35.9

against flush_manifest_seconds = 44.0 for the whole hook. So the dead-path fallback is 82% of the manifest leg, and manifest is the largest flush-grain leg on 7.4.0 (3-4x taxonomy).

WHAT THE COST ACTUALLY IS — round-trip COUNT, not payload and not server work. Control from the same run: begin_index_run_many (a properly batched per-flush write) is 29 calls / 3.3s = 0.114 s/call. Every catalog op in the run costs 0.10-0.13s regardless of what it does, i.e. essentially the cloud round-trip floor; server processing is the ~0.02s residue. The fallback runs 327 round trips where the design intends 29.

Projected win once jk88j unblocks this: 35.9s -> ~3.8s per run on 109 files (~0.3s/file, scaling linearly with file count). On the 1875-file nexus tree that is minutes.

Also corrects a premise carried in nexus-jb4pp's own description ("write_manifest_many is one POST per flush already"): it is not, and has never been, in service mode.

Order stands as jk88j says: sweep in the fast branch FIRST, then whitelist. Do not reorder for the perf number above.

   3 uses of `pytest.mark.cloud_mode`                                  -> the
     MARKER. Actually deselected.

NEITHER USAGE IS WRONG. usefixtures is the right tool for setup and the marker is
the right tool for selection; both are being used correctly. The problem is
purely that the shared name makes `cloud_mode` in a pytestmark line ambiguous —
a reader (or an author reaching for "mark this cloud-only") cannot tell which
behaviour they are getting, and the two differ completely.

MITIGATION THAT ALREADY EXISTS, worth knowing before touching this:
local-service-gate.sh:320-333 asserts CLOUD_MODE_EXPECTED=3 exactly, so a
conversion in either direction trips the gate rather than silently changing
coverage. That is why this is P3 and not higher — the count guard makes the
dangerous transition observable.

OPTIONS: rename one of them (the fixture to `cloud_mode_env`, say), or leave it
and document the distinction at both definition sites. Renaming touches 20 files;
documenting costs two comments. I did not pick.

title: event-triggered surfacing: gate on census evidence before building — ONE high-precision trigger or none (Tier C, dormant; hot-path and RDR-121 rule-cap costs stated)
description:
TIER C (a NEW hooks.json PreToolUse/PostToolUse entry) -- fully dormant until the
next plugin release. GATED: do not start until nexus-h33x8.1's census reports the
trigger's real rate. This is deliberately the LAST child, and it may be correct to
never build it.

THE IDEA (direction 2 as proposed): a failing test is the moment to surface
/conexus:debug, via PostToolUse -- not 12KB at session start, hours before any
failure exists. The principle is sound and matches the epic's own proximity
finding (the SubagentStart channel works because it is close to the task).

WHY IT IS RANKED LAST DESPITE BEING SOUND -- four costs the proposal understates:
 1. DORMANT BY CONSTRUCTION. A new hooks.json entry is Tier C. Unlike .1/.2/.3
    there is no PyPI channel for a matcher that does not yet exist, so this is
    inert for a full release cycle from the day it merges.
 2. HOT PATH. Bash is 58,640 calls across the corpus (30,439 orchestrator +
    28,201 subagent). A PostToolUse hook on Bash pays a subprocess spawn on every
    single one. Compare RDR-121/125, which caps PreToolUse:Bash ROUTING RULES at
    FOUR cross-plugin for exactly this reason, with a <300ms p95 cumulative
    budget; four are already registered (registry.yaml). The cap is on rule
    COUNT, and adding a fifth requires consolidation or a successor-RDR budget
    revision -- that is a decision this bead does not get to make unilaterally.
 3. FALSE POSITIVES. "A test failed" must be inferred from arbitrary command
    output. pytest, mvn, shell scripts and E2E gates all fail differently, and a
    non-zero exit is routinely expected (greps that find nothing, probes, `|| true`).
    A trigger that fires wrongly will be tuned out within a week and will take the
    census's credibility with it.
 4. THE PREMISE IS UNMEASURED. Nobody has counted how often a genuine test
    failure occurs without /conexus:debug following. That number comes from .1.
    If it is rare, this hook is pure cost.

THEREFORE, SCOPE: ONE trigger, highest precision available, or nothing.
Recommended candidate: `uv run pytest` exiting non-zero in the orchestrator
context -- a single tool, a single runner, an unambiguous exit convention. Not a
family of triggers, not a generic failure detector.

BUILD ORDER (each step can kill the bead, which is the point):
 a. From .1's census: count sessions with >=1 failing-pytest Bash call and ZERO
    subsequent Skill invocation. If that is low, CLOSE THIS BEAD AS NOT WORTH
    BUILDING and record the number. That is a successful outcome.
 b. If high: prototype the detector OFFLINE over existing transcripts and measure
    its precision/recall against hand-labelled cases. No hook yet.
 c. Only if offline precision is high does a hook get written; and it must be
    weighed against the RDR-121 rule budget explicitly, in writing.

=== VERIFICATION ===
1. STEP (a)'s NUMBER IS RECORDED regardless of outcome. A bead that closes
   "not worth building" WITH the number is a success; one that closes silently is
   the failure mode this epic exists to fix.
2. If built: offline precision/recall on hand-labelled transcript cases, stated
   as numbers, measured BEFORE any hook ships. A detector whose accuracy is
   unmeasured is exactly the "guidance nobody can verify" pattern in a new costume.
3. If built: a measured latency delta on the Bash path, checked against the
   RDR-121 <300ms p95 cumulative budget, plus an explicit statement of where the
   rule sits against the FOUR-rule cap.
4. If built: PENDING_RELEASE.md entry, and DO NOT CLOSE ON MERGE -- Tier C is
   inert until released.

(grep_for_symbols_redirects_to_serena). So this bead's arithmetic — "four are already

WHERE IT BREAKS: the cap, the registry schema (`matcher: Bash` means PreToolUse:Bash), and

 3. THERE IS NO PostToolUse REGISTRY OR LINT AT ALL. Today's only PostToolUse entry is

title: [catalog] rename identity guard lives ONLY in CatalogHandler — renameCollectionTxn re-checks emptiness but never re-checks superseded_by identity
description:
Found in round-2 substantive-critique of nexus-v6za0/nexus-20890 (commits 6fb31f1d,
9e89bdb4, 9a87d657), 2026-07-31.

CatalogRepository.renameCollectionTxn (CatalogRepository.java ~2990-3025) re-derives and
re-checks EMPTINESS inside the transaction's own snapshot before taking the canonical
branch (the CollectionMergeRefused guard at line ~3021), and the javadoc explicitly
defends this as protection against the TOCTOU between a caller's pre-check and the txn.

It does NOT re-check IDENTITY (superseded_by == oldName). That half is enforced ONLY in
CatalogHandler.handleCollectionRename (~line 1200-1211), via repo.collectionIsEmpty(tenant,
newName) called in a SEPARATE tenantScope.withTenant(...) invocation — a different
connection/transaction than the one renameCollectionTxn itself opens moments later. The
repo's own javadoc on the upsert step admits this directly: "CatalogHandler now gates the
revive on the tombstone's identity... but do not restore the stronger claim — this
transaction is not itself the thing enforcing it."

Two consequences:
 1. TOCTOU: a concurrent POST /collections/supersede that changes newName's superseded_by
    between the handler's precheck and the txn's execution is invisible to the txn — it
    only re-verifies emptiness, not identity, at the point of use. An empty tombstone
    that pointed elsewhere at precheck time but was NOT the rename source can still be
    silently revived, erasing its true supersession unaudited — the exact hazard the
    identity guard exists to prevent, reached via a race window instead of the sequential
    logic error the last three rounds fixed.
 2. Any FUTURE caller of CatalogRepository.renameCollection() that does not replicate
    CatalogHandler's identity pre-check (a batch job, a CLI-direct path, a gRPC handler)
    gets ONLY the emptiness protection. It can revive/erase an unrelated supersession
    chain with no exception, no audit trail, as long as the target happens to be empty.

Related but distinct from nexus-mijr4 (which is now stale in its specifics — it names
liveCollectionExists, which was removed and inlined by 6fb31f1d; both call sites now read
getCollection()+superseded_by directly). mijr4's THESIS is what recurred here: "change one,
change both" enforced by comment only, no structural device. Consider closing mijr4 as
superseded-in-form and folding its ask into this bead, or scoping both under one
"pin rename/supersede invariants structurally, not by comment" fix.

Fix shape: either (a) move the identity check into renameCollectionTxn itself, reading
superseded_by from the same ctx used for the emptiness recheck (removes the TOCTOU and
makes the repo method self-defending regardless of caller), or (b) make CollectionMergeRefused
carry the identity condition too and throw it from inside the txn when !identityOk, so the
repository — not just one of its callers — is the thing enforcing both halves.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
ADJUDICATED 2026-07-31, same day it was filed. The two reviewers disagreed about this and
I verified the mechanism myself rather than picking a side.

THE RACE IS DISPROVEN. This bead's premise is that the handler's identity check
(superseded_by == oldName) can go stale before renameCollectionTxn acts, because the two
run in separate transactions. That would require a concurrent writer to move
superseded_by to a THIRD value in the window. No writer can:

  supersedeCollection carries its precondition IN THE WHERE CLAUSE --
    .and(SUPERSEDED_BY.eq("").or(SUPERSEDED_BY.eq(supersededBy)))
  (CatalogRepository.java ~2796, added for nexus-cecqy). That is a DB-level
  compare-and-swap, not a Java check-then-write. A concurrent supersede of the same row
  to a DIFFERENT target matches ZERO rows and the handler's rowcount check reports it;
  a supersede to the SAME target is idempotent.

So once the handler reads superseded_by == oldName, that value cannot change underneath
the rename. The asymmetry (the txn re-checks EMPTINESS but not IDENTITY) is correct, and
it is correct for a reason that lives in a different method -- which is why nobody could
see it from the gate. Emptiness is a fact about rows in OTHER tables that nothing
serialises, so it must be re-measured in the acting snapshot; identity is a fact about
one column that is CAS-protected at the point of write.

That reasoning is now written at the gate itself (commit on develop 2026-07-31), so the
next reader does not have to re-derive it. Documenting it was the code reviewer's actual
recommendation once it withdrew the race.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY THIS STAYS OPEN AT LOW PRIORITY. The residual is not a race, it is
a LAYERING fact: renameCollection() is protected by a precondition enforced in
handleCollectionRename and by a CAS in supersedeCollection. The repository method is not
self-defending. Today that is fine -- there is exactly one caller. It stops being fine
the moment a second, non-HTTP caller appears (a CLI path, a migration step, a scheduled
repair), which would get the emptiness half and none of the identity half, silently.

DOWNGRADE to P3 and reframe: this is not "fix a TOCTOU". It is "decide whether the repo
layer must be self-defending, or whether one-caller-plus-a-comment is the accepted
contract". If nexus-3jntg (the retired_reason discriminator) is ever done, it dissolves
this entirely -- the identity question becomes a single column read that the txn can do
for free, and the asymmetry disappears.

Note for the record: the reviewer that raised this was RIGHT to raise it. The mechanism
that makes it safe is three method-hops away and undocumented at the point of use. That
is exactly the shape that made attempts 1 and 2 possible.

title: two unrelated 'tombstone' concepts (T3 trashed-doc vs catalog superseded) are conflated in operator-facing rename errors
description:
Found by the re-review of 1232585d, 2026-07-31 (terminology hazard, surfaced while
tracing the rename guards).

The codebase now carries TWO UNRELATED "tombstone" concepts:
  - the T3 trashed-document tombstone (CollectionState.TOMBSTONED, meaning every chunk
    belongs to a trashed document)
  - the catalog-registry superseded tombstone (catalog_collections.superseded_by != '')

The CLI uses the FIRST to guard an operation whose engine semantics turn on the SECOND:
both rename verbs pre-flight probe_collection_state (T3 chunk presence,
src/nexus/db/collection_state.py), which never consults superseded_by — while emitting
operator-facing text ("is tombstoned (every chunk belongs to a trashed document)") that
describes the wrong one.

This conflation is a contributing cause of nexus-v6za0 (the P0 merge) and nexus-c29vr:
in both, a client-side T3-presence check was the only thing standing between a caller
and an engine-side registry corruption, and it reads a different notion of "gone".

Probably wants a rename of one of the two terms plus an audit of every operator-facing
message that says "tombstone".

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
CENSUS COMPLETE, 2026-07-31. The bead's framing needs amending, and the census spawned
three code/doc beads that are NOT terminology.

## THE BEAD NAMED TWO SENSES. THERE ARE FIVE.

  A  Document soft-delete tombstone      catalog_documents.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
     (RDR-106/catalog-003). ~90 of 120 service/src/main hits, ~200 of 281 engine-test
     hits. THE DOMINANT USAGE.
  B  T3 collection-state TOMBSTONED      DERIVED FROM A: every chunk under the name
     belongs to an A-tombstoned doc. CollectionState.TOMBSTONED, collection_state.py.
  C  Catalog-registry superseded         catalog_collections.superseded_by != ''.
  D  JSONL delete-marker                 DEAD SURFACE — local catalog removed by
     nexus-i711w, still documented as live procedure. Now nexus-g0glp.
  E  "code tombstone" comment convention ~45 sites. Harmless, but it defeats
     grep-based auditing of the other four.

The bead treated B as primitive. It is DERIVED from A, and A — not B — is the majority
usage and where the engine's operator-facing strings sit. Any rename touching only B
leaves the A/C collision intact.

## NAMING RECOMMENDATION: RENAME C, KEEP "tombstone" FOR A/B.

Not a rename at all — DELETING A SYNONYM. Sense C already has a complete, deployed
vocabulary: the column is superseded_by, the verb is supersede_collection, and THREE of
the four operator-facing C messages in CatalogHandler already say "retired (superseded
by X)". "Tombstone" is a redundant second word layered on top.

  "superseded tombstone" -> "retired registry row"
  "tombstoned name"      -> "retired name"
  "revive a tombstone"   -> "revive a retired name"

BLAST RADIUS: ZERO compatibility surface. Verified explicitly —
  - persisted columns: none contain "tombstone" (all 16 changelogs checked)
  - persisted enum values: none. CollectionState.TOMBSTONED is sense B, not renamed,
    and its .value is NEVER serialized (no .value/str() use anywhere in src/)
  - JSON wire keys: none. Rename-cascade count keys are catalog_collections_superseded
    / _inserted; supersede keys are name/superseded_by/superseded_at
  - HTTP error bodies: ONE string, CatalogHandler.java:1191 ("it cannot revive a
    tombstone"). No test asserts that substring.
  - internal identifiers: ZERO. Sense C's entire footprint is comments, docstrings and
    prose — 11 text sites.

Also note the two CLI rename-refusal assertions
(test_catalog_rename_collection_tombstone_probe.py:81,
test_collection_rename_tombstone_probe.py:111) assert `"tombstoned" in msg or "trash"
in msg` — an OR, so the B-sense strings can drop the word without touching them.

## THE THREE CODE/DOC BEADS THE CENSUS SPAWNED (filed, not left in prose)

  nexus-e1k14  P1  doctor --collections-drift prints a SUPERSEDE recipe against
                   restorable trashed data. THE ONLY DESTRUCTIVE ONE. Detection reads
                   the B notion of "gone", remedy acts on C, and the word "tombstone"
                   appears nowhere in the path — which is why it is the worst site.
                   VERIFIED end to end against catalog-005's view semantics.
  nexus-uloao  P2  rename_collection_cmd guards SOURCE on C and TARGET on B. The target
                   is exactly where v6za0 happened; it is safe today only by accident.
  nexus-g0glp  P3  sense-D doc rot: delete, do not reword.

## CROSS-LINK

nexus-mijr4 is the same root (a notion of "gone" restated rather than shared) on a
different pair: the engine's own two C-readers (CatalogHandler's tgtLive vs
renameCollectionTxn's liveTargetExists) are held in agreement by a comment. That is
C-vs-C so it is out of scope here, but the two beads should move together.

   DIFFERENT-target race. Two concurrent supersedes to the SAME Y both read
   superseded_by = '' (guard 2's early-200 return is not reached), both call the repo,
   and the loser's UPDATE matches via the .or() disjunct and RE-STAMPS
   superseded_at = now(). The serial path deliberately avoids exactly this —
   CatalogHandler.java:1058-1060: "re-stamping superseded_at would move the
   supersession's recorded instant every time the operation is retried". So the
   invariant the handler protects serially is unprotected concurrently, on the very
   statement just hardened. superseded_at is the audit instant nexus-g8z8n guard 4
   exists to make trustworthy.

2. THE NEW 409 ASSERTS A CAUSE IT DID NOT OBSERVE. CatalogHandler.java:1069-1081 states
   unconditionally that zero rows means "was superseded to a different target
   concurrently". At least one other cause yields zero: POST /v1/catalog/collections/delete
   hard-deletes the registry row (CatalogRepository.java:2751), and a concurrent delete
   between guard 1's getCollection and this UPDATE also matches nothing — where the
   correct answer is 404 row-gone, not a 409 naming a supersession that never happened.
   Tenant/RLS is NOT a source of spurious zeros (getCollection is tenant-scoped
   identically, so an invisible row 404s at guard 1 first).

   Asserting a specific concurrent cause the code did not observe is the same honesty
   failure the surrounding comments criticise elsewhere.

FIX: re-read the row on zero rowcount and report what is actually true, or word the
error to name both possibilities.

ALSO OWED: the TOCTOU fix shipped with ZERO tests. Nothing pins the new WHERE conjunct
and nothing pins the updated == 0 -> 409. Both repo-level callers
(CatalogRepositoryTest.java:1104 and :1125) supersede a LIVE row and still return 1.
Delete both additions and the suite stays green — so 1232585d's "mutation-verified"
claim is scoped to the rename guard ONLY. Cheap non-vacuous pin: repo-level
assertThat(repo.supersedeCollection(T, X, Z, "")).isEqualTo(0) after X was superseded
to Y.

title: T2 latency-gate constants are fitted to five runs on one dev box — never measured on a CI runner, where the gate actually fires
description:
Raised by critic-arc-0731 reviewing commit b2980b26 (the nexus-3m01p fix). Filed rather
than left as a review comment on a closed bead.

nexus-3m01p replaced a bare ratio assertion in
tests/test_t2_concurrency.py::test_memory_get_under_concurrent_write_load with two
constants:

    _BASELINE_FLOOR_MS   = 1.0   # floors the ratio's denominator
    _LOAD_P95_CEILING_MS = 50.0  # absolute starvation ceiling

Both were derived from FIVE runs on ONE machine (a dev box, quiet, in one session):
baseline_p95 1.70-2.18ms, load_p95 1.77-2.08ms, plus the single loaded-box observation
that triggered the bead (baseline 0.58ms / load 1.85ms). That is enough to establish the
FAILURE MODE — the denominator was the problem, not the measurement — and the fix is
correct in shape. It is thin evidence for the specific numbers.

THE CRITIC'S POINT, which is fair: the constants were fitted to the observed failure, not
derived from the environment they must survive. Neither was ever measured on a CI runner,
which is where this test actually gates, and where this repo has documented contention
confounds (T2 project_docker_port_forwarding_wedges; the CI-cost notes on runner load).

TWO CONCRETE RISKS:
  - A genuinely FASTER box produces baselines the 1.0ms floor over-corrects for. The floor
    then masks a real relative regression: at baseline 0.4ms the ratio is computed against
    1.0ms, so a load_p95 of 2.9ms reads as 2.9x and passes when the true ratio is 7x.
  - The 50ms ceiling has never been checked against CI's actual load profile. If a
    contended runner routinely reaches 20-30ms it is closer than the "~24x headroom"
    claim suggests, and the first spurious failure will be read as a real regression.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: collect baseline_p95 / load_p95 / load_p99 from ~20 CI runs (the
test already prints all three on one line, prefixed "[rdr-063 under-load]", so this is a
log scrape, not new instrumentation), then set the floor at roughly the 5th percentile of
observed baselines and the ceiling from the observed load_p99 distribution rather than
from a single machine's maximum.

NOT URGENT. The gate is strictly better than what it replaced (which failed on a run where
nothing was slow), and both assertions are mutation-verified. This is about whether the
numbers survive contact with the environment that runs them.

title: nx t3 gc requires -c but retirement docs/error message show it as optional; no all-collections sweep replaces retired nx t3 prune-stale's default scan
design:
Context: nx

Verified 2026-07-31 while critiquing commit 19801b9e (nexus-bm8dd) on develop.

`nx t3 prune-stale` (retired in 19801b9e) had `--collection/-c` with
`default=""` and help text "Omit to scan every T3 collection" — it
iterated every non-quarantine collection when -c was not passed
(src/nexus/commands/t3.py, pre-19801b9e).

Its replacement, `nx t3 gc`, has `--collection/-c` as `required=True`
(src/nexus/commands/t3.py:210-216, unchanged by this session — predates
19801b9e) with help "Required (orphan diff is per-collection)". There is
no all-collections mode.

The retirement's ClickException message (t3.py, prune_stale_cmd) and the
matching docs/cli-reference.md update both print:

    nx t3 gc [-c COLLECTION] --no-dry-run --yes

using brackets that imply -c is optional. Running this literally
(`nx t3 gc --no-dry-run --yes`) fails immediately with Click's "Missing
option '--collection' / '-c'". An operator who used to run
`nx t3 prune-stale` with no args to sweep every collection in one command
now has no single-command equivalent — they must enumerate collections
themselves and loop `nx t3 gc -c X` per collection, and the retirement's
own guidance does not say so; it shows a syntax that will not run.

The commit message's claim that the catalog-native pipeline "does
strictly more" is true per-collection, but the one-command sweep-
everything capability the retired verb had is not actually replaced,
and the migration instructions test-covered
(tests/test_t3_prune_stale.py::test_prune_stale_message_names_the_cause_and_the_replacement)
only assert substring presence ("nx t3 gc" in output), not that the shown
invocation actually runs.

FIX SHAPE: either drop the brackets around -c in the docs/error message
(mark it required), or give `nx t3 gc` a real all-collections mode and
keep the docs as-is.
close_reason:
FIXED on develop, commit 1232585d.

Both halves were real and both were mine (19801b9e):

1. The retirement message and docs/cli-reference.md printed `nx t3 gc [-c COLLECTION]`.
   `-c` is required=True ("Collection to GC. Required (orphan diff is per-collection)"),
   so an operator copying the printed remediation gets Click's "Missing option:
   '--collection' / '-c'". Verified by running it.
2. The "does strictly more" claim was false in one dimension: the retired
   `nx t3 prune-stale` swept every non-quarantine collection when -c was omitted;
   `nx t3 gc` has no such mode. `nx catalog prune-stale` does take all collections, so
   only the GC half needs looping — but the one-command sweep is genuinely gone.

Both now show the real syntax, state the gap explicitly rather than implying parity, and
give the enumeration loop. The test that only asserted `"nx t3 gc" in result.output` — a
substring check that could not have caught a wrong invocation — is unchanged, because the
right pin here is that the printed command RUNS, which needs a live T3 and belongs with
whatever gate covers that.

LEFT OPEN AS A QUESTION, deliberately not decided here: should `nx t3 gc` gain an
all-collections mode? It is a DESTRUCTIVE verb and its -c is required by design (the orphan
diff is per-collection), so adding a sweep-everything mode is a design decision about blast
radius, not a docs fix. Reopen or file a successor if the loop proves too awkward in
practice.

title: [dt] capture failure modes: --type pdf yields a .webloc that indexing skips (exit 0), --doi misses OA copies (incl. Scientific Reports), and an index-stage 500 dumps a raw traceback leaving a captured-but-unindexed record
description:
One batch of 5 captures, 2026-07-27; four distinct failure modes. All reproduced below verbatim.

## 1. URL capture with --type pdf produced a .webloc bookmark; pipeline then skipped it; nothing failed

    nx dt capture "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.04962" --type pdf --collection knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1
    Captured https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.04962 -> DEVONthink record A178592A-…
    event='dt_skip_unsupported_extension' … path='…/Files.noindex/webloc/8/1808.04962.webloc' ext='.webloc'
    Indexed 0 record(s) (1 skipped, 0 semantically linked, 0 written back to DT).

The user asked for a PDF; DT created a bookmark (likely the arXiv redirect defeating DT's
create-PDF-from-URL); the index stage skipped it with a warning; overall flow reports "Captured"
and exits without error. Junk record left in DT (trashed by hand). Acceptance: when --type pdf is
requested and the resulting record is not file-backed PDF, FAIL loudly (capture's own contract:
"reports DT-required and exits NON-ZERO" — same spirit should apply to type mismatch), and don't
leave the record silently.

## 2. --doi reports "no open-access PDF" for a fully-OA Scientific Reports article

    nx dt capture --doi 10.1038/srep00514 --contact-email <set>
    Error: capture failed for doi:10.1038/srep00514 (no open-access PDF found for this DOI)

srep00514 (Dambre 2012) is Scientific Reports — gold OA since 2012; the PDF is one GET at
nature.com/articles/srep00514.pdf (verified: fetched directly, %PDF magic, 517KB). Either the
Unpaywall integration is misquerying or its response handling is wrong. At minimum the error
should distinguish "Unpaywall answered: no OA location" from "Unpaywall lookup failed", and log
the raw response. (Second miss in the same batch: 10.1162/089976602760407955 — that one is
plausibly correct per Unpaywall data since the OA copy is an institutional page (tugraz), but
srep00514 is not a data gap.)

## 3. Capture succeeded, index stage 500s with a raw traceback — record left captured-but-unindexed

    nx dt capture "https://www.ai.rug.nl/minds/uploads/STMEchoStatesTechRep.pdf" --type pdf …
    (record 9B1951FD-… "Short term memory in echo state networks" created as PDF+Text)
    httpx.HTTPStatusError: HttpPipelineDB./v1/pipeline/pages failed: HTTP 500: internal server error
    (raw traceback to console)

Recoverable via `nx dt index --uuid 9B1951FD…` (used), but: (a) raw traceback instead of a clean
"captured OK, indexing failed, re-run with: …" message; (b) relates to the nexus-5xn3k class —
whatever /v1/pipeline/pages wrote before the 500 is unaccounted for; the post-index verification
recipe applies. Server-side: what 500'd on a 60-page PDF POST?

## Workaround that works (for the runbook)

curl the PDF directly (browser UA), verify %PDF magic, then `nx dt capture --file <path>` — file
captures skip both the DT web-capture and Unpaywall layers. All four round-1 failures recovered
this way in one pass.

Related: nexus-mok9x (dt-content quality), nexus-5xn3k (partial-index accounting).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## Round-2 outcomes + two more findings

**Recovery status: all 5 papers indexed and content-verified.** curl (browser UA) → %PDF magic
check → `capture --file` worked where URL/DOI capture failed; two documents additionally needed
the purge + `index_pdf(force=True)` drill from nexus-16f77/5xn3k.

**Finding A — the /v1/pipeline/pages 500 is reproducible and document-correlated.** Across 9
index attempts in this batch it fired on Dambre (srep00514, 7pp Nature 2012) and Jaeger (GMD-152,
60pp, 2002-era PDF) — Jaeger TWICE (URL-capture run and dt-index rerun) — while Tanaka (64pp),
Maass (30pp, also 2002-era), and Shen (16pp) passed through the same path cleanly in the same
minutes. Fails BEFORE extraction (no MinerU lines). Not ordering (Maass succeeded between the two
failures), not size, not age. Both eventual successes came via direct `index_pdf()`, which
bypasses whatever layer posts /v1/pipeline/pages. Server logs for those 500s are the next
diagnostic step.

**Finding B — the 5xn3k staleness poisoning reproduced a 3rd and 4th time, with a new wrinkle:**
after the pipeline-500 partial writes, plain `index_pdf()` returned 0 chunks for both documents,
while `col.get(where={"content_hash": h})` AND `where={"doc_id": tumbler}` both returned **zero
rows** — the purge step found nothing to purge, yet the staleness probe still short-circuited.
Whatever chunks the probe sees are invisible to both audit keys. `force=True` alone cleared it
(Dambre 82, Jaeger 234 chunks, verified by content markers).

**Finding C — `force=True`'s own orphan cleanup is broken in service mode:**

    force_t3_orphan_cleanup_failed ... error="_ServiceCollectionStub.delete() got an
    unexpected keyword argument 'where'"

Same local-Chroma-API-on-HTTP-client family as ids_for_source / delete_by_source /
orphan_backfill.py:130. Means --force (nexus-16f77) currently cannot honor its delete-before-
reindex contract in service mode — cross-filed there.

**Finding D — DT record rename MOVES the underlying file; catalog file_path goes stale.**
Renaming captured records to proper titles (from filename-titles like "tanaka-1808.04962")
renamed Files.noindex/<dir>/<file>.pdf on disk. Catalog file_path then pointed at a nonexistent
file until manually re-upserted. Two implications: (a) capture --file should set the record
title from PDF metadata/first page, not the filename, so nobody needs to rename; (b) anything
verifying "file_path exists" (prune-stale!) would have reaped these three healthy documents.

title: [taxonomy] strip LaTeX command tokens and HTML tag names from the topic-discovery vocabulary — markup residue currently clusters as subject matter
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 rebuilding `knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1` (HDBSCAN, 6,113
chunks → 26 topics).

Pre-labelling TF-IDF token triples:

```
octants mathfrak octant     mathcal refinement hat     td memory rowspan
mathbf pmb mathrm           mathcal mathsf elements    pi ell psi
varepsilon mathcal ell      td mesh rowspan            face td prime
```

`mathbf`, `pmb`, `mathrm`, `mathcal`, `mathsf`, `varepsilon` are LaTeX commands. `td` and
`rowspan` are HTML table markup. They are dense and consistent enough across documents to form
their own clusters.

**~3 of 26 topics (≈894 chunks, 15% of the collection) are markup artifacts**, not subjects:
"Mathematical symbol notation" (199), "Index and type formalism" (273), "Memory and retrieval
benchmark tables" (422).

**`nx taxonomy label` conceals it.** The LLM labelling pass renders `mathbf pmb mathrm` as
"Mathematical symbol notation" — indistinguishable from a real topic in the topic list. Post-hoc
audit of labels will not surface this; you have to read the pre-labelling triples or the member
chunks.

Cost: these topics permanently compete in topic-scoped retrieval (`search --topic`,
`search_topic_scoped`) until the next rebuild, and the embedding spend to cluster markup is wasted.

## Proposed

Add a stop-list to the vocabulary used for topic discovery / label seeding:
- common LaTeX command tokens (`math*`, `pmb`, `varepsilon`, `ell`, `frac`, `mathrm`, `mathsf`,
  `mathfrak`, `mathcal`, `mathbf`, …)
- HTML tag/attribute names (`td`, `tr`, `rowspan`, `colspan`, `img`, `src`, …)

Cheap, self-contained, and **independent of whether ingest-side extraction is ever fixed**
(nexus-mok9x) — worth having as defence-in-depth either way, since any future extractor change
still cannot retroactively clean already-indexed corpora.

Full record: T2 `nexus/forensics-2026-07-27-taxonomy-and-aspect-findings`.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
## Independent corroboration from `nx taxonomy review --auto` (2026-07-27)

The LLM auto-reviewer, with no knowledge of this bead's analysis, condemned the same class of
topics and reached for the same word:

    [1426144055] Mathematical symbol notation (199 docs)
        "Pure LaTeX glyph pollution (pi/ell/psi/bf/mathbf) with no subject anchor"
    [1426144050] Epsilon-bounded optimization problem theory (95 docs)
        "Math-markup cluster (varepsilon/mathcal/ell/boldsymbol); only content term is generic
         'problem', label over-reads the notation"
    [1426144048] arXiv language model citations (167 docs)
        "Reference-list boilerplate — clustered on arxiv/year/surname citation formatting,
         not a subject"

Two points this adds:

1. **A third residue class beyond LaTeX and HTML: reference-list boilerplate.** `arxiv`, years,
   and author surnames from bibliographies cluster into a pseudo-topic the same way markup does.
   The proposed stop-list should therefore also consider suppressing citation-format tokens, or —
   better — excluding `section_type=references` chunks from topic discovery entirely (the
   `search` tool already supports `where="section_type!=references"`, so the classification
   exists).

2. **Correction to this bead's estimate.** It claimed ~3 artifact topics including "Memory and
   retrieval benchmark tables" (422 docs). The reviewer ACCEPTED that one, and on reflection it is
   right — benchmark tables are a genuine subject in memory-systems papers, not markup residue.
   Confirmed artifacts were the LaTeX ones plus the citation cluster. Net effect on the ~15%
   figure is roughly unchanged (461 docs deleted vs the ~894 estimated), but the composition
   differs.

Also note the reviewer RENAMED rather than deleted "Index and type formalism" → "Simplex type and
index notation" (273 docs), judging it a real subject whose label had over-read the notation. So
the boundary between "markup artifact" and "real topic with a bad label" is genuinely fuzzy and
worth a human pass, which is an argument for the `--accept-only` mode proposed on nexus-afnht.

The aspect extractor nonetheless routed to **`general-prose-v1`**, not `scholarly-paper-v1`.

Cause: routing keys on TEXT shape (`_PAPER_SHAPE_SIGNALS` in `src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py` —
an "Abstract" heading and similar markers). CACM's *web* rendering of a peer-reviewed article has
no Abstract section, so it reads as prose regardless of catalog identity.

Consequence: the record loses the scholarly-paper fields. Compare the two documents ingested in
the same session:

| | CACM (general-prose-v1) | Zoology (scholarly-paper-v1) |
|---|---|---|
| experimental_datasets | `[]` | 3 entries |
| experimental_baselines | `[]` | 9 entries |
| experimental_results | narrative prose | structured |
| confidence | 0.87 | — |

Both are peer-reviewed papers. Only the one whose text happens to carry an Abstract heading got
paper-grade extraction.

Note this is NOT the same as the false-positive direction the extractor deliberately guards
(`test_technical_note_with_list_and_year_stays_prose` — a design note must not be promoted to the
paper extractor on weak signals). That guard is correct and should stay. This is the false-NEGATIVE
direction, and there is a strong non-textual signal available that the guard does not consult.

## Suggested fix

Let catalog identity promote when it is unambiguous: `content_type == "paper"` AND a non-empty
`bib_doi` (a registered DOI is hard evidence, not a heuristic) → use `scholarly-paper-v1` even if
`_PAPER_SHAPE_SIGNALS` does not fire. Keep the text-shape path as the default for documents with
no catalog bibliographic identity, so the existing false-positive guard is untouched.

Low priority — the prose record is usable and scored 0.87 confidence. But it silently costs the
structured fields that make `operator_filter` / `groupby` / `aggregate` SQL fast paths work over
`document_aspects`, so the loss compounds for any analytic query over the corpus.

Found alongside nexus-mok9x (extraction quality) — same document, independent defect. Full record:
T2 `nexus/forensics-2026-07-27-taxonomy-and-aspect-findings`.

title: plan_match's scope_conflict / always_failing drop counters are invisible when a runnable candidate wins
description:
`plan_match`'s two pre-existing drop counters are reported only on the fallthrough path, so the drop is invisible whenever a runnable candidate wins — which is the common case.

## The gap

In `src/nexus/plans/matcher.py`, the T1 cosine path accumulates `scope_conflict_drops` and `always_failing_drops`, then:

```python
if scored:
    ...
    return matches          # <-- early return, common case
# only reached when scored is EMPTY:
if hits and scope_conflict_drops > 0:
    _log.debug("plan_match_scope_conflict_fallthrough", ...)
if always_failing_drops:
    _log.debug("plan_match_always_failing_dropped", ...)
```

Both records fire only when EVERY candidate was dropped. When one candidate is dropped for a scope conflict (or for being always-failing) and another survives to be returned, the drop is discarded unlogged.

## Why it matters

The `scope_conflict_fallthrough` record was added by RDR-091 code-review finding I-4 specifically so "operators can see when scope_preference is silently degrading matches". It does not do that in the winning-sibling case — precisely the case where a degraded (rather than absent) match is the outcome an operator would want to understand.

## Second, independent problem: the level

Both records are `_log.debug`. `_resolve_level` (`src/nexus/logging_setup.py:36`) defaults MCP mode to INFO and CLI to WARNING, with DEBUG reachable only via `verbose=True` or `NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`. So even on the fallthrough path where they DO fire, they never reach a log in normal operation. The observability is theoretical in both directions.

## Provenance

Found during the code-review-expert / substantive-critic pass on PR #1425 (nexus-0yrjr). The new `plan_match_unrunnable_binding_dropped` record introduced by that PR had the identical early-return gap — it was copied from this pattern — and was fixed there (nexus-eedj4) by draining before the early return and emitting at INFO. These two pre-existing counters were left untouched as out-of-diff scope; the critic flagged that leaving them is defensible but that they share the defect.

## Fix shape

Mirrors what nexus-eedj4 did: drain/report before the `if scored:` early return, not only after it, and reconsider DEBUG vs INFO given `_resolve_level`'s defaults. The binding-drop helper `_log_binding_drops` in the same file is now the worked example, including the drain-on-emit that stops a single drop being double-reported when the T1 path falls through to FTS5.

## Test note

The regression that catches this shape is `test_a_satisfiable_plan_still_wins_when_a_sibling_is_dropped` in `tests/test_plan_match_binding_satisfiability.py` — a sibling-wins scenario asserting on `capture_logs()`. Any fix here wants the equivalent for the scope-conflict and always-failing cases; the existing tests for those assert on returned plan_ids only, which is why the gap survived.
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-26 in PR #1425 (branch feature/rdr-189-190-target-definition-plan-ir), folded in as a declared scope addition rather than a separate PR — same function, adjacent lines, one CI cycle.

Both records moved into a new _log_t1_drops helper, called before either exit alongside _log_binding_drops, and promoted DEBUG -> INFO (as DEBUG they never reached a log under _resolve_level's MCP=INFO / CLI=WARNING defaults, so they were unobservable even on the fallthrough path where they did fire).

Two tests added on the winning-sibling path — neither record had ANY test asserting it before. Mutation-verified: removing the drains fails exactly those two plus the nexus-eedj4 binding-drop regression.

FIXTURE GOTCHA for anyone extending these: an agnostic plan (empty scope_tags) does NOT survive a real scope_preference in this harness, contrary to what _scope_fit's docstring implies about agnostic being neutral-and-kept. The test pins the winner with an explicit matching scope_tags instead. Worth a look if someone is auditing _scope_fit — I did not chase it, since it was outside this fix.

Closes on PR #1425 merge.
The 'agnostic plan does not survive a scope_preference' fixture gotcha recorded above turned out to be a REAL BUG, not a harness quirk — filed separately after Hal flagged it. The fixture was accidentally reproducing it: save_plan's #1069 project-column fallback stored a bare project name as scope_tags, and _scope_fit prefix-matches collection-name shape, so the tag can never match and the plan is dropped. _scope_fit itself is correct; agnostic (scope_tags='') does survive, returning 0.0. See the new bead.

title: Bounded replanning loop in plan_run (VADAOrchestra borrowable A) — HELD pending plan reuse rising
description:
Design sketch already exists. This bead is the tracked pointer — bd search found nothing for it as of 2026-07-26.

SOURCE: T3 note 'research-note-vadaorchestra-borrowables-replanning-catalog-rules-2026-06-25', knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1, content hash fee7a73e5ad8664375c4d803eb3fe3feceafd74cd44858db25ca0747c7ee4a4a (the same-titled 4be8b2f3... doc is an empty RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER — do not read that one).

THE GAP (verified): plan_run (src/nexus/plans/runner.py:1021) loads the plan once (:1070-1071), walks steps in a single pass, and returns a frozen PlanResult (:1348; dataclass :212 = {steps, final}). The plan is chosen once at the top — library plan via plan-match, or a grown plan from the inline planner — and after that nothing inspects intermediate results in a way that can change the remaining plan. The grown-plan path adapts BEFORE execution, never during.

SHAPE: wrap the existing straight-through executor in an outer replan controller. Run to completion, then ask a cheap gate whether findings warrant appending stages. Inner executor (today's for-loop, factored out as _run_steps(steps, prior)) is UNCHANGED — this is additive.

TERMINATION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT HEURISTIC — this is what makes it safe to ship. Two guards, both from VADAOrchestra: a max_rounds cap, and a (tool, frozenset(params)) no-repeat set. Termination does not depend on the LLM deciding to stop.

CHEAP NON-LLM TRIGGER: operator_aggregate's SQL fast path already computes count / count-distinct / avg-min-max over document_aspects. A cardinality probe ('retrieval returned 1,200 candidates; the plan only ranks top-10') is a strong trigger for 'append a filter/groupby stage before answering' without spending a reasoning call to decide.

*** WHY THIS IS HELD (P3, not P2) ***
It adds an LLM round-trip PER RUN on a path where nx_answer's own docstring reports 23% of runs already take 2-5 minutes, and where measured plan reuse is ~0 (RDR-189 R8; nexus-sbl4m). Adaptive replanning makes each run slower and costlier with no amortization to recover it. Parmar's break-even argument (K* ~= 0.04 executions, arXiv:2605.00827v1) is the whole economic case for investing in richer plan execution, and it needs K > 0. Revisit when reuse rises — same gate as RDR-190's blocking open question.

CONTENDED SURFACE: PlanResult (runner.py:212, currently {steps, final}) is now wanted by THREE drafts — RDR-189 P4 (preservation trace), RDR-190 P2 (loop provenance), and this (a rounds field). Whoever lands first should expect the other two.

TOUCHES: factor runner.py's step loop into _run_steps (pure refactor, no behavior change); add rounds to PlanResult and the nx_answer_runs T2 row; new _replan_gate as one claude -p call with a tight JSON schema {stop: bool, appended_steps: [...]}, reusing the inline-planner dispatch path.

OPEN: default max_rounds (2-3 likely; make it a plan-level dimension so library plans opt in); cost gate must be OFF by default, enabled by a plan dimension or a cardinality threshold, never unconditional; whether a successful adaptive run should persist its appended steps back via plan_save — turning the run into a richer reusable library plan, which is VADAOrchestra's 'trace becomes a deterministic plan'.

SCOPE NOTE: makes plan_run stateful and overlaps the grown-plan path. The note's own read is that this warrants a FULL RDR (not a memo) to scope the persistence-back-to-plan_save question before any code.

title: Plan-IR `rule` step: bounded recursive closure over catalog_links (VADAOrchestra borrowable B)
description:
Design sketch already exists and is complete enough to implement from. This bead is the tracked pointer — bd search found nothing for it as of 2026-07-26, so it was invisible to bd ready.

SOURCE: T3 note 'research-note-vadaorchestra-borrowables-replanning-catalog-rules-2026-06-25', collection knowledge__knowledge__voyage-context-3__v1, content hash fee7a73e5ad8664375c4d803eb3fe3feceafd74cd44858db25ca0747c7ee4a4a. NOTE: two documents share that title; the OTHER one (4be8b2f33c526102940f6e88aadba13900b69175ee37d5fa6b3d9647e7b99cb5) contains only the literal string RESEARCH_NOTE_PLACEHOLDER. Use the hash above.

THE GAP: RDR-078 (closed) shipped `traverse` as a plan operator — typed-edge BFS, fixed depth, single relation, SC-16 validated (a step declares either link_types or a purpose alias, plus depth). Expressing 'everything upstream of this RDR through any mix of cites/implements/supersedes, then aggregated by author' requires hand-chaining multiple traverse steps at fixed depths. It cannot be stated as one recursive relation.

WHY catalog_links IS THE RIGHT SUBSTRATE: (from_tumbler, to_tumbler, link_type, from_span, to_span, created_by, metadata), ~16,500 edges, typed and exact and effectively closed-world — nexus's closest analogue to a Warded Datalog+- knowledge graph. Rules are sound here in a way they are NOT on the T3 vector layer, where a 0.36-distance chunk is not a logical fact. That line is load-bearing: assert only exact typed catalog facts as rule atoms.

SHAPE: a new `rule` plan step, sibling to `traverse`, compiling a declared recursive relation into a single PG WITH RECURSIVE CTE. Not a Datalog engine. Bounded transitive closure over a typed-edge predicate, returning the standard retrieval step-output contract {tumblers, ids, collections} so it composes with downstream groupby / aggregate / filter — giving the full traverse -> aggregate -> threshold pipeline in one declared step.

TERMINATION BY CONSTRUCTION: depth < :max_depth plus UNION (set semantics dedups cycles) halts even on cyclic link graphs. SQL analogue of the PTIME guarantee; no chase needed.

TOUCHES: src/nexus/plans/schema.py (extend _TRAVERSAL_TOOLS at :99, add a validation rule mirroring SC-16); a rule_json -> WITH RECURSIVE compiler in the catalog module executed through the service-backed catalog reader; register in _NON_EMBEDDING_TOOLS (runner.py:241) like traverse, since it operates on tumblers not embeddings.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (from the note): transitive closure over a typed-edge predicate plus an optional attribute filter, NOTHING MORE. Resist negation, existentials, multi-predicate joins — that path reimplements a Datalog engine ('the theorem-prover tax').

RELATION TO RDR-190: `rule` is a third plan-IR primitive. RDR-190 deliberately scoped to two (loop, collect) and warned about JSON DSLs drifting into accidental programming languages. Keep this SEPARATE rather than folding it into RDR-190, so that discipline stays visible.

OPEN: how much Datalog to expose; who authors rules (human-authored library plans first, like traverse, then measure before considering synthesis); document- vs span-granularity (document first — catalog_links carries chash-addressed from_span/to_span, spans are a later refinement).

title: nx doctor should label .catalog.db as a frozen migration source (aoqnb item 2, not covered by the refusal)
description:
Carved out of nexus-aoqnb rather than left inside it as an unfinished item — the bead was closed for its item (1), and an unfinished item inside a closed bead is exactly how scope goes quiet.

WHAT WAS DONE (46bedcc5, aoqnb item 1): make_catalog_admin now REFUSES in service mode, so the two mutating verbs (`nx catalog dedupe-owners --apply`, `nx catalog undelete`) can no longer write the frozen .catalog.db. The refusal message names the file as a frozen migration source at the moment someone tries to mutate it.

WHAT IS NOT DONE (item 2): a PASSIVE doctor line. The bead asked that "nx doctor must explicitly label catalog.db as frozen migration-source, not a live mirror, so recovery procedures do not trust it". The refusal only fires when someone attempts a mutation; it does nothing for the operator who is INSPECTING before a restore, which is precisely the moment the bead was worried about — the 532-docs/13-links file looks plausible and a recovery procedure reaches for it first.

SHAPE: a doctor check that, in service mode, reports .catalog.db present + its row counts + an explicit "FROZEN migration source, not a live mirror; the authoritative catalog is in Postgres" label. Ideally alongside the PG counts so the divergence is visible rather than inferred — that is what would have made the GH #1419.4 discovery immediate instead of forensic.

CAUTION drawn from today: the surrounding doctor checks are the false-clean family (nexus-ingey/k0luu/cv6jp). Do not add a check that reads the frozen file and reports it as health. It must be labelled, not counted as a passing signal, and if the PG side is unreachable it must say UNKNOWN rather than showing only the local number.

title: [bug] HttpCatalogClient._db raises RuntimeError, not AttributeError — breaks the raw-handle guard contract for any hasattr caller
description:
Latent, found by the nexus-at2ff handle-shape sweep 2026-07-25. NOT FIXED. No live caller today, so this is a trap rather than a defect.

src/nexus/db/t2/_raw_handle_guard.py:9-12 states the contract explicitly: the guard properties raise AttributeError and NEVER RuntimeError, because "a RuntimeError would propagate through hasattr and break the guard contract". hasattr() only swallows AttributeError; anything else propagates.

src/nexus/catalog/http_catalog_client.py:253-266 raises RuntimeError from ._db.

CONSEQUENCE IF ANYONE ADDS hasattr(cat, "_db") OR has_raw_access(cat): instead of returning False and taking the service-mode branch, it CRASHES in service mode. The guard idiom that exists precisely to make these checks safe would become the thing that breaks.

Verified there is no live hasattr(cat, "_db") today, which is why this is P3 and latent rather than a live bug. But the whole point of a guard contract is that callers can rely on it without re-checking each implementation.

FIX: raise AttributeError from HttpCatalogClient._db with the same actionable message shape as RawHandleGuardMixin._raise (name the missing handle, point at the routed alternative), or make it use the mixin directly. Add a test asserting hasattr(HttpCatalogClient_instance, "_db") is False — that is the contract, and nothing currently pins it.

WORTH GENERALISING: a test that every service-backed store guard raises AttributeError (not RuntimeError) would close this for all of them at once, and is cheap.

title: No integration test proves a genuine grant fault still returns 500 through the full taxonomy handler stack
description:
From the nexus-asaod stacked review (finding M2), 2026-07-25. NOT FIXED — recorded rather than dropped.

The asaod fix rests on a discrimination: SQLSTATE 42501 + the RLS message => 409 (caller conflict), while a 42501 from a GENUINE grant/role fault must keep surfacing as 500 (a deployment error the operator must see). That discrimination is proven ONLY at the unit level: rlsDetector_requiresBothTheSqlstateAndTheRlsMessage constructs a synthetic SQLException("...permission denied...", "42501") and calls HttpUtil.isRlsRowRejection directly.

Today the "deployment fault stays a 500" guarantee is verified at the classifier input boundary only.

NOT A REGRESSION IN asaod: the sibling suite TaxonomyHandlerAssignFkTest has the identical gap for the class-23 arm, so this is a convention-level hole in how these handler suites are written, not something asaod introduced. Filed separately for that reason.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING: a mislabelled 409 tells an operator their deployment is healthy when their role grants are broken — the same false-clean class the day was spent removing, wearing an HTTP status code.

title: Doctrine-ban tests are gameable by paraphrase: banned-phrase grep protects against literal recurrence only
description:
Demonstrated by the test-validator on the day diff, 2026-07-25. NOT FIXED.

tests/test_engine_release_skill_parity.py enforces the one-engine-identity directive with two greps: _BANNED_DOCTRINE (four historically-observed phrasings) and _REQUIRED_DOCTRINE (a positive phrase that must be present). Both lists were hand-written by the same session that wrote the replacement prose — marking its own homework.

THE VALIDATOR BUILT A WORKING BYPASS:
  "This project follows the ONE engine identity model for releases. In practice,
   REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION should be treated as a lower bound: bump it only when a
   shipped feature genuinely needs the newer engine, and leave it alone otherwise..."
That reintroduces the exact banned carve-out semantics in different words, while containing "ONE engine identity" verbatim. Both tests PASS on it.

HONEST ASSESSMENT OF WHAT THE TESTS ARE WORTH: they do catch literal recurrence of the four phrasings that ACTUALLY occurred, four times, which is the observed failure mode — a checklist copy-pasted forward carrying its old wording. That is not nothing. What they do not do is survive a rewrite, and the file docstring implies durability it does not have.

OPTIONS:
  (a) Accept as a regression pin for the specific incident language, and say so in the docstring rather than implying general protection. Cheapest, honest.
  (b) Invert the check: assert the doc states the rule POSITIVELY and unconditionally, and ban conditional-bump language patterns (only when / only if / unless / lower bound / minimum) NEAR REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION. Catches paraphrase; more false-positive risk on legitimate prose.
  (c) Semantic check via an LLM assertion in CI. Rejected on cost/flakiness unless someone argues for it.

Recommend (a) plus the narrow half of (b) — banning conditional-bump connectives within N lines of REQUIRED_ENGINE_VERSION is cheap and targets the actual semantic being smuggled back in.

title: Rate-limit the /v1/taxonomy/import* routes: the 409 id-conflict response is an unthrottled cross-tenant id-existence oracle
description:
ACCEPTED-RISK FOLLOW-UP from the nexus-asaod stacked review (2026-07-25, finding M1). The risk itself is accepted and recorded in code at TaxonomyHandler.java next to the 409 branch; this bead is the OPTIONAL hardening Hal asked to be filed rather than done now.

THE ORACLE. nexus.topics has a GLOBAL BIGSERIAL primary key — RLS scopes ROWS, not the id space. So POST /v1/taxonomy/import/topic {"id": N} returns 200 when N is free and 409 when another tenant already holds it. An authenticated tenant can therefore probe whether an arbitrary id is claimed SOMEWHERE in the system, with no read access to the holder data.

WHAT LEAKS: existence only. Not the holding tenant, not the label, not any row content — the 409 body is "supplied id is not available in this tenant" and the log line carries tenant+op with no id (verified; there is a test asserting the body does not contain the other tenant). Probed at scale it reveals approximately how densely the global id space is populated, i.e. rough total topic count and allocation pattern across tenants.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3:
- The route requires Bearer auth AND a tenant header; not anonymous.
- It is a fidelity-ETL/migration path, not a hot API.
- Ids are normally each tenant own prior sequential rowids, so collisions arise by accident rather than adversarial choice.
- Content confidentiality is intact; this is a cardinality/allocation-pattern leak.

WHY IT IS NOT ZERO: AuthFilter has NO rate limiting on this route (confirmed in review), so enumeration is unthrottled. A determined tenant can sweep the id space at whatever rate the service will serve.

SCOPE IF DONE: per-tenant rate limiting on /v1/taxonomy/import/* and /import_batch. Design caution — ETL bursts are exactly the traffic shape a naive limiter punishes: the 190k-row dogfood import is the legitimate heavy user of these very routes, so a limiter tuned to stop enumeration must not break the bulk migration path. Consider limiting on 409-RESPONSES specifically rather than on request volume: a caller generating many conflicts is the signature of probing, while a legitimate ETL generates few.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not re-proposed: remove the oracle at source with a composite (tenant_id, id) key. That deletes the whole class — no cross-tenant collision, no RLS refusal, no 409, no oracle. It was already considered and rejected because topics_parent_fk is SELF-REFERENTIAL, so a composite key forces every parent_id to carry a tenant too. The global BIGSERIAL is a deliberate design choice (recorded 2026-07-25), not an oversight.

title: claude_dispatch failure record: addressability + retention + the CLI paths it does not cover
description:
Follow-up to nexus-q6830, from both stacked reviewers on 62aa53db. The structlog 'operator_dispatch_failed' event covers all 17 call sites mechanically, but DURABILITY is a property of the calling process's logging mode, and the record falls short of nexus-1at5's precedent on three axes:

1. ADDRESSABILITY. The timeout branch names its artifact IN the exception ('...logged to {log_path}'), so a debugger holding only the exception has a pointer. The failure branch gives none — finding the record requires already knowing to grep 'operator_dispatch_failed'.
2. RETENTION. _persist_timeout_log writes a dedicated per-incident file with no rotation. The WARNING lands in the shared mcp.log at 10MB x 5 backups, so a busy server can roll it out of the retained window before anyone looks.
3. CLI COVERAGE. mode='cli' returns from logging_setup before any file handler attaches (logging_setup.py:142-143), so nx taxonomy discover / review --auto get stderr only — no persisted record at all.

DO NOT just copy _persist_timeout_log. The reviewer recommended mirroring it exactly; that helper has NO cleanup and accumulates forever, which is fine for RARE timeouts and wrong here — a fail-open batch can produce dozens of failures in one run (the q6830 commit's own example is 'claude -p dying forty times'), so file-per-failure would be unbounded. Whatever lands needs a retention story the timeout path never needed. Options to weigh: one artifact per RUN rather than per failure; a path back-reference in the exception; or wiring open_run_log into the two taxonomy commands so CLI runs get a file at all.

title: subagent-start-stamp mkdir lock has no staleness detection and no signal when it degrades
description:
Found by code-review-expert reviewing nexus-3h0u6 (99da8fde), 2026-07-20. LOW.

The mkdir-based lock in conexus/hooks/scripts/subagent-start-stamp.sh has no staleness detection. If a holder is killed between the mkdir and the rmdir (OOM-kill, host crash), the lockdir leaks for the rest of the session. Every subsequent invocation for that session then burns the full ~1s retry budget failing to acquire, falls through to the unprotected fail-open path, and silently re-admits the exact TOCTOU race the fix closed — with ZERO diagnostic signal, since nothing is logged when acquisition fails.

Impact is bounded: worst case reverts to the documented pre-fix behavior (a possible duplicate row), never a missing row, and the crash window is one file read plus one append wide. The rmdir itself is correctly guarded ([[ -n $_held ]]) so this is a leak/inertness issue, not a steal-someone-elses-lock bug.

What is actually wrong is the CLAIM: the in-code comment says 'the guard now actually holds under concurrency', which silently becomes false after any such crash.

FIX SHAPE: either a lockdir-age check (treat older than N seconds as stale and reclaim) or, at minimum, a stderr note on failure-to-acquire so the degradation is observable rather than silent. The second alone would satisfy the no-silent-fallback directive, which is the part that actually matters here.

title: PG bundle identity could reuse the verified sha256 from nexus-pg.meta.json instead of size+mtime
description:
Found by code-review-expert reviewing nexus-xzop6 (e97aa987), 2026-07-20. LOW.

_archive_identity() keys the extraction marker on name+size+mtime_ns. The docstring justifies skipping a digest on cost grounds (bundles are hundreds of MB, this is the provisioning path) and that reasoning holds in isolation.

But binary_install.py ALREADY computes and stores a verified sha256 in the nexus-pg.meta.json sidecar (_PG_SIDECAR_NAME) for any downloaded bundle. Reusing that value when the sidecar is present would be strictly stronger than size+mtime at zero extra hashing cost — no new digest computation, just reading a value already written and already verified at download time.

Only the ship-alongside / NEXUS_PG_BUNDLE-override case (no sidecar) would need the size+mtime fallback.

Practical relevance: mtime is not preserved uniformly across install mechanisms. A package manager or copy that preserves mtime on a genuinely different archive of identical size would defeat the current check; a copy that resets mtime would cause a spurious (harmless, now non-destructive) re-extract.

Not urgent — the current check catches the real scenario (an upgrade drops a new .txz) and the re-extract path is now safe (extract-then-swap, badc783a).

title: Ladder runner flattens the rekey could-not-tell taxonomy into RungOutcome.FAILED
description:
Found by substantive-critic during nexus-b878d review (2026-07-20).

HttpRemapStore.rekey now raises three distinct types: RekeyJobFailedError (known-failed), RekeyJobTimeoutError (could-not-tell, may yet commit) and RekeyJobLostError (could-not-tell, engine restarted, store state unknown, idempotent re-run is the recovery).

But src/nexus/upgrade_ladder/runner.py wraps rung.converge() in a blanket 'except Exception -> RungOutcome.FAILED'. All three land identically; only the message text in detail= distinguishes them. The taxonomy currently has no behavioral consumer.

That is acceptable today (loud failure, no silent success, and the ladder is operator-driven inside a freeze window) but it means an operator hitting the LOST case sees a hard rung FAILED for a condition whose correct response is 'just re-run it, it is idempotent'.

Decide: either the ladder protocol grows a could-not-tell/retryable outcome distinct from FAILED, or the chash-rekey rung catches RekeyJobLostError and self-retries once before giving up. The first is an RDR-142-trichotomy-adjacent protocol change and should not be done casually; the second is local and cheap.

NOT started under b878d: expanding rung-outcome semantics is a design decision, not review cleanup (no-preventive-scope-beyond-evidence).

title: nx daemon t2 status: honest service-mode message masked by a stale pre-service-mode discovery file
description: Follow-up from nexus-c0vby code review (critic round 1, non-blocking minor). t2_status_cmd's service-mode branch (added in nexus-c0vby, GH #1405 defect 2) only fires when the T2 discovery file is ABSENT. A box that ran local mode before switching to service mode can have a STALE discovery file left over from the old local T2 daemon (last real run before the switch); on such a box, 'nx daemon t2 status' still finds the old discovery file, skips the service-mode branch entirely, and prints the OLD PID's status (correctly reporting it as stale-if-dead via the existing liveness probe, but the MESSAGE framing is 'stale discovery, is the daemon running?' rather than the new 'service mode -- T2 daemon intentionally not running' framing) -- misleading on a service-mode box. Fix: check service-mode FIRST (before the discovery-file-exists branch), or fold the service-mode framing into the stale-pid message too. Needs a test: service mode + a discovery file present (any liveness state) -> service-mode-aware message, not the plain stale/running framing.

title: Dependency-free /proc-based process enumeration on Linux (ps as the macOS path)
description: Promised follow-up from nexus-cfgo9 (Hal-relayed directive 2026-07-15 16:32 comment; critic2 caught that it was never filed). Current fix: enumerate_processes (src/nexus/upgrade_finish.py:151-176) catches FileNotFoundError on a missing ps binary and raises an actionable RuntimeError; callers degrade that leg loudly. Stronger fix: enumerate via /proc directly on Linux (no subprocess dependency — /proc/<pid>/stat + /proc/uptime for etime-equivalent), keep ps for macOS. Preserves the fail-loud invariant (empty read must never look like zero processes — see TestFailLoud). Motivation: minimal container images (debian-slim etc.) lack procps; the --package-upgrade rehearsal leg deliberately runs ps-less to keep this class honest.

title: Add Python regression test for atomic_manifest_replace indexed_at stamping (positive + empty-clear-no-stamp)
description:
nexus-p5qk8 follow-up. During substantive-critic review of the working-tree
diff for nexus-8gue1/nexus-p5qk8 (GH #1397, engine-service-v0.1.42
candidate), _WriteOps.atomic_manifest_replace (src/nexus/catalog/catalog_writes.py)
was found to stamp indexed_at unconditionally, including on
atomic_manifest_replace(doc_id, []) -- a documented, tested "clear"
operation (test_replace_empty_chunks_clears_and_zeros_count in
tests/test_catalog_manifest_backfill.py). This broke the "a clear is not
an indexing event" principle write_manifest/append_manifest_chunks
correctly implement, and diverged from the Java side (writeManifestRows
already guards `if (!rows.isEmpty())`).

The bug was fixed live during the review session (catalog_writes.py now
splits `if chunks: ... else: ...` so indexed_at only stamps on a real
write, chunk_count still re-derives to 0 on empty clear either way) --
verified empirically before/after the fix landed.

BUT: no Python regression test exists for atomic_manifest_replace's
indexed_at behavior, neither the positive case (stamps on real write) nor
the negative case (empty-clear does NOT stamp). The Java suite covers the
equivalent via CatalogFtsFilenameSearchTest.manifest_replace_refreshes_indexed_at_but_empty_replace_does_not
(against CatalogRepository.writeManifest); Python has no parallel.

Given atomic_manifest_replace is the PRIMARY per-document write path
(mcp_infra.py's shrink-reindex hook calls it directly) and just had
exactly this asymmetry bug, add tests mirroring
TestManifestWritesRefreshIndexedAt in tests/test_catalog_manifest_read_api.py:
  - atomic_manifest_replace([...]) stamps indexed_at
  - atomic_manifest_replace([]) does NOT stamp indexed_at (chunk_count
    still re-derives to 0)

Context: nx memory get -p nexus -t critique-nexus-8gue1-p5qk8-catalog-fts-filename-tokens

title: quarantine__ collections unhandled by migration ETL default enumeration and legacy nx t3 gc
description: Critique of 4cb743be (nexus-xukbj), Significant (non-blocking) findings. (2) the legacy 'nx t3 gc' path (commands/t3.py gc_cmd) enumerates t3_db.list_collections() with zero quarantine-prefix awareness (no 'quarantine' string appears anywhere in t3.py) — since quarantine collections are deliberately catalog-unregistered, this older, independent orphan-detection code path could target quarantine contents with its own rules, potentially hard-deleting them outside the 14-day grace window and bypassing the relocated mr89x floor entirely. title: T1 periodic refresh loop bypasses jwqjm's mint-race flock — narrower residual race remains
description:
substantive-critic finding (nexus-jwqjm.3 round 1, Significant, not blocking): _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow (src/nexus/db/t1.py) closes the reported simultaneous-STARTUP mint race, but nexus.mcp.core._t1_session_refresh_loop's own PERIODIC re-mint (~L265-294) calls HttpTokenStore().start_session() directly, unlocked, on its own half-TTL schedule.

Residual mechanism: under a narrow compound timing window, an owner that misses nearly all refreshes for ~half a TTL (~12h on the 24h default) and then fires a very late refresh at the same moment a NEW process independently concludes the lease is stale and wins the flock can still reach the same 'two independently-refreshing owners rotate each other's token' persistent-churn state nexus-jwqjm described -- just via a different trigger (delayed-owner-refresh colliding with a new recoverer) instead of simultaneous startup.

Fix directions (not yet designed): (a) route the refresh loop's re-mint through the same lock/lease-double-check as _lock_guarded_mint_or_borrow -- non-trivial: a refresh that discovers a FRESHER lease already published by a new recoverer would need to 'surprise borrow' mid-refresh, updating this process's own live env/auth state, which is genuinely new behavior beyond a simple lock wrap. (b) accept as a documented residual (current choice) since it requires a much narrower compound timing window than the original bug and degrades to the same already-actionable 401 path.

Not release-blocking. Revisit if this pattern is ever observed in the field (unlike the original bug, which was found by code review, not a field report).

title: nexus_config_dir() should normalize NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR to absolute at the source
description:
Deferred from nexus-oj1hn (T1 orphan-tmpdir liveness sweep, GH #1151) review round 2, substantive-critic finding.

nexus_config_dir() (src/nexus/config.py ~408-424) returns Path(os.environ["NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR"]) verbatim when the override is set, with zero validation or normalization that it is absolute. The module's own docstring documents this env var as user-facing ("sandbox runs, tests, and multi-profile installs can redirect... with one environment variable"), so a relative override is not purely hypothetical.

This surfaced because src/nexus/session.py's _sweep_one_tmpdir_root now compares os.path.abspath(str(d)) against a live_paths set (nexus-oj1hn's fix) -- but os.path.abspath() resolves against the CALLING PROCESS's cwd, not a fixed reference point. sweep_orphan_tmpdirs genuinely runs from two separate processes in production: `nx doctor --reap-tmpdirs` (a freshly launched CLI, operator's cwd) and the long-lived MCP daemon that originally called start_t1_server (Claude Code's spawn-time cwd). If NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR were ever relative, each process's os.path.abspath could resolve it differently, silently defeating the liveness match and reproducing GH #1151 under that precondition.

No current call site sets a relative NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR (verified both review rounds of nexus-oj1hn) -- narrow, accepted residual risk, not blocking. The permanent fix: normalize inside nexus_config_dir() itself (os.path.abspath() or Path.resolve(), single source of truth for every caller) rather than requiring every downstream comparison site to independently re-derive convergent behavior -- this is the second time this exact axis (relative-config_dir handling) has surfaced a gap.

Add a regression test proving cross-process/cross-cwd convergence once fixed (two different monkeypatched cwds computing nexus_config_dir() with the same relative NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR must yield the same absolute path).

title: Catalog references 29 T3 collections that no longer exist (historical reindex churn)
description:
Found via `nx catalog doctor --t3-vs-catalog` post-6.6.1 (that check was
previously silently false-passing due to the nexus-pyv0e/nexus-64np7
_client reach-through bug; fixed in 6.6.1, now correctly firing loud).

29 catalog documents reference physical_collection values that don't
exist in T3 at all (docs_pointing_at_missing_t3). Traced every owner
behind them -- four distinct root causes, confirmed with Hal:

1. Deleted/consolidated owners (5 collections: 1.17, 1.2153, 1.2156,
   1.2202, 1.60): owner row no longer exists in the `owners` table at
   all (dedupe-owners / nexus-tmbh consolidated it into a canonical
   owner), but the update never cascaded to documents.physical_collection
   on the orphaned rows. Real structural gap: dedupe-owners doesn't
   rewrite physical_collection on the documents it's walking away from.

2. Real, still-tracked repos with vanished T3 data: Delos (1.3), Kramer
   (1.5), scheme-evolution-research (1.7), BFDB (1.4, legacy 2-segment
   name predating RDR-101/103). Owner registration is intact, repos are
   real and current on disk, but T3 has no matching collection. Per Hal:
   caused by "the massive problems and indexing/reindexing we have done
   over the months" -- historical churn, not a new bug.

3. Accidental parent-directory index (1.32): owner literally named
   "git", repo_root = ~/git (the parent of ALL of Hal's repos), sweeping
   in unrelated content (a Java "3dviewer" project). Confirmed by Hal:
   `nx index repo ~/git` was run by mistake. Guard against this shipped
   same session (nexus-git-guard, see commit) -- nx index repo now
   refuses a PATH with no .git. This bead is about the STALE DATA left
   behind by the mistake, not the guard itself (already fixed).

4. Ephemeral benchmark probe (1.19 "rich"): repo_root is a
   /var/folders/.../probe-rich-* temp dir from a prior benchmarking
   session. Expected transient garbage.

No first-class remediation command handles this direction today --
`nx catalog collection-gc` only sweeps the OPPOSITE case (orphaned T3
collections with no catalog projection), not orphaned catalog
references pointing at missing T3.

Candidate follow-ups (not decided, needs Hal's call):
- Re-index Delos/Kramer/scheme-evolution-research/BFDB to regenerate
  the missing T3 collections (category 2).
- Delete/supersede the catalog document rows for the "git" (1.32) and
  "rich" (1.19) owners -- both are mistakes/ephemera, not real content
  worth recovering (categories 3/4).
- Fix dedupe-owners to cascade physical_collection updates (or at
  minimum flag/supersede orphaned document rows) when consolidating an
  owner (category 1) -- the actual structural bug.

Full owner-by-owner trace available in this session's conversation if
needed for the follow-up work.

title: Purge AGPL runtime deps from the commercial-license path: swap PyMuPDF -> pypdfium2, isolate MinerU behind a process boundary
description:
Follow-on from the dual-licensing change (commit a7f4dc8a, LICENSING.md) and the Bito-vs-nexus gap analysis v3.1 (T3 knowledge__knowledge, 2026-07-10).

## Why
nexus is now dual-licensed (AGPL-3.0-or-later + commercial option), but two HARD runtime deps are themselves AGPL-3.0 and are explicitly NOT covered by a nexus commercial license (LICENSING.md dependency note):
- pymupdf >= 1.26.6 (Artifex; aggressive dual-license enforcement posture)
- mineru[pipeline] (opendatalab; no commercial option)

Dependency scanners (Snyk/FOSSA/Black Duck) flag AGPL transitives as critical regardless of the top-level license, so a commercial licensee installing conexus still imports AGPL wheels into their environment. That undercuts the commercial pitch: the scanner-level antibody survives the license change.

## Scope
1. PyMuPDF -> pypdfium2 (Apache-2.0/BSD-3, PDFium-based). PyMuPDF is the third leg of the extraction routing (Docling -> MinerU -> PyMuPDF, RDR-044 auto-detect) plus any page-render/metadata call sites. Inventory all fitz imports; port; benchmark extraction parity on the existing PDF fixture corpus before removing the dep.
2. MinerU isolation. CONSTRAINT (nexus-2fyb, locked): demoting mineru to an optional extra caused weeks of silent formula loss; default-on install is the locked decision for the personal install path. The isolation therefore has to preserve default-on UX while making the AGPL boundary clean for commercial consumers — candidate shapes: (a) subprocess boundary (mineru already drives do_parse via its own model stack; a CLI/subprocess seam keeps the AGPL work in a separate process and arguably outside the combined work), (b) split distribution: conexus core wheel without mineru + a conexus[formula] meta-extra that the default installer (nx init / install docs) always provisions, so fresh personal installs keep formula extraction while the base wheel scans clean. Decide via short RDR or design memo; do NOT silently regress formula-aware extraction.
3. Verify: fresh-install scan (pip-licenses or scancode) of the base wheel shows zero AGPL transitives; PDF extraction E2E suite green including formula fixtures; docs updated (LICENSING.md dependency note shrinks or gains 'resolved' status).

## Acceptance
- No fitz/pymupdf import in src/ (inverse-grep clean); pypdfium2 parity validated on fixture corpus with exact assertions.
- MinerU either process-isolated or split-distributed with the default-on guarantee intact (nexus-2fyb must not regress).
- License scan of base wheel: zero AGPL entries.
notes: DECISION (2026-07-12, Hal): not urgent -- no commercial prospects currently blocked on the AGPL scanner objection. Lowered P2->P3; revisit when a real commercial conversation hits it.
