title: DataTokenHandler Retry-After header hardcoded to 60s, ignores NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE override
description:
DataTokenHandler.handleMint sets Retry-After: 60 unconditionally on 429 (line ~179). The javadoc/comment claims this is "the per-tenant sustained refill period" but MintRateLimiter.tenantSustainedPerMinute() is env-overridable (NX_MINT_RATE_TENANT_SUSTAINED_PER_MINUTE, RDR-005 pin ii — "conexus tunes without an engine release"). If conexus retunes this to e.g. 3/min, the real refill interval is 20s, not 60s, but Retry-After still says 60 — safe-direction (over-conservative) but a real discrepancy against the header's own documented intent, and untested (mint_rateLimited_429_thenRefills only asserts status codes, never the header value).

Fix: compute Retry-After from rateLimiter.tenantSustainedPerMinute() (package-private accessor already exists) instead of the literal "60". Add a header-value assertion to mint_rateLimited_429_thenRefills or a small dedicated test.

Found during Gate C (Phase 6 CLI + closure sweep) substantive-critic review of nexus-868dq/nexus-x1h07. Not a security issue (conexus's real cadence is well under any retune), just an accuracy/consistency gap on an operability signal conexus-8ub8 (the edge client) will read.

title: nx index repo: [N/M] progress counter overcounts past total during RDR phase (cosmetic)
description:
Live shakeout 2026-07-06 (nx index repo on nexus itself, post v6.3.3 cut): the per-file [N/M] progress counter in nx index repo's on_file callback continues incrementing past the main loop's total once the RDR 4th-loop (nexus-3lswy) starts — e.g. "[1470/1469] README.md", "[1554/1469] rdr-...", climbing well past M for the whole RDR phase.

Root cause: on_start(count) fires once with len(code_files)+len(prose_files)+len(pdf_files) (indexer.py, on_start call site) BEFORE the RDR file count is known — RDR files are discovered later, inside _run_index, as their own 4th category. The CLI's progress counter (src/nexus/commands/index.py, on_file closure, `nonlocal n, total`) increments a shared `n` against the fixed `total` set at on_start, so RDR files (counted as part of the same run_file_loop-driven on_file stream) push n past the frozen total.

Purely cosmetic — does not affect functionality, indexing correctness, or the log file content, just the human-readable [N/M] display briefly reads oddly (N > M) during the RDR phase. Low priority.

Fix shape (not designed): either (a) call on_start a second time (or a new on_rdr_start-style hook) once rdr_md_paths is known, before the 4th run_file_loop fires, so the CLI can rebase its displayed total, or (b) track code/prose/pdf and RDR progress as two separate counters in the CLI display instead of one shared running count.

comments.text:
Re-confirmed and re-measured 2026-08-10 by the `nx index repo` output-UX assessment
(T2 `nexus/index-output-ux-assessment-2026-08-10`, entry 22159, proposal a4, bead-breakdown
item 5). Filed as a duplicate check, landing here instead of a new bead.

## Still live, one year on, with a fresh measurement

Run: `nx index repo .` on nexus itself, cloud/voyage, conexus 7.5.0, no `--force`, exit 0,
~14 min wall. Counter reached **[1930/1666]** during the RDR phase. Your 2026-07-06 diagnosis
holds exactly: `on_start` (`src/nexus/indexer.py:3496`) totals non-RDR files only, RDR indexing
keeps calling `on_file`, and the shared `n` climbs past the frozen `total`.

The assessment rates this **P2**, not P3 (this bead's current priority). Not changing the field
here; flagging the divergence for whoever grooms it. The argument for P2 is not the cosmetics, it
is that this is the ONE `[N/M]` surface a user reads as a completion signal, and it currently lies
about how much work is left in exactly the phase where the run also goes silent for minutes.

## HARD CONSTRAINT for whoever fixes this (this is the part that is new)

The fix touches the `[N/M]` line shape, which is COUNTED by a release gate:

- `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout.sh:197-203` counts lines matching
  `^\s*\[[0-9]+/[0-9]+\]` (`grep -cv skipped`) into a TWO-SIDED gate (run1 >= 10, run2 <= 6).
- `tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/rehearse_shakeout_e2e.sh:399-401` counts the same shape (>= 3).

Both fail SILENTLY WRONG, not loudly, when the count moves. Consequences for the two fix shapes
named in the original description:

- Option (a) rebase the total via a second `on_start`: SAFE. Line COUNT is unchanged, only the
  rendered denominator moves.
- Option (b) two separate counters: DANGEROUS if it introduces a second stream of
  `^\s*\[N/M\]`-shaped lines, which would inflate the gate's count. If you go that way, the RDR
  counter must not be rendered in the bare `[N/M]` shape at line start. Put it behind the
  `  [post] ` prefix with the fraction later in the line.

Also binding: no `\r` on the non-TTY path (`tests/test_index_cmd.py:494` asserts
`"\r" not in result.output`), `Done.` stays last (8 assertion sites across 6 files), and do not
reword the summary sentences (`tests/test_5xn3k_summary_truthful.py` pins ~50 exact sentences).
Full constraint list: assessment section 7.4.

The silence this counter sits inside is tracked separately: post-processing runs 627.6s (45% of
wall) behind 16 lines, with a 547.8s and a 74.6s black hole. See the sibling beads created

title: nf3n7 follow-up: decouple ChunkBatcher oversize threshold from client upsert page-size cap
description:
substantive-critic review of nf3n7's client-side upsert paging fix (src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py per_collection_chunk_cap, indexer.py _cap_for). Two SEPARATE constraints were collapsed into ONE function/constant:

(1) ChunkBatcher.add()'s oversize threshold — 'how many chunks can a file have before it needs the fallback path' (chunk_batcher.py:178-185, driven by indexer.py's ChunkBatcher(max_chunks=_cap_for,...) at indexer.py:2835-2840).
(2) HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks's internal page size — 'how many chunks per POST when paging an oversize upload' (http_vector_client.py:637-665).

nexus-nf3n7's own bead notes (conexus root-cause relay) explicitly recommend DIFFERENT values for these: the batcher's 64-chunk CCE threshold stays as-is; the fallback/direct-path page size should 'start ~128 chunks ... tune from re-gate p99' — i.e. conexus explicitly modeled these as two independently-tunable knobs. The shipped fix (per_collection_chunk_cap, http_vector_client.py:19-32) instead hardcodes ONE shared constant (_CCE_UPSERT_CHUNK_CAP=64) for both, silently overriding conexus's ~128 recommendation for the fallback page size with no recorded rationale reconciling the two.

Risk: the coupling means the two concerns can no longer be tuned independently. If someone later raises the batcher's flush cap for cross-file batching throughput, they silently also raise the client's oversize-fallback page size past whatever gateway-safe bound motivated the original 128 recommendation (and vice versa) — 'one knob, two constraints.'

Recommendation: split into two named functions/constants (e.g. batcher_oversize_threshold vs upsert_page_cap), even if they start at the same numeric value, so they can diverge safely. Separately: measure whether 128 (conexus's recommendation, informed by the 30s control-plane budget) actually holds under the p99 load profile — the shipped 64 is conservative-safe but may leave throughput on the table with 2x the round-trips of 128 for CCE fallback uploads. No adaptive/bisection retry exists on the client's paging loop (unlike ChunkBatcher._flush_batch's file-count bisect-on-failure at chunk_batcher.py:259-296) — a single sub-POST page that itself 504s just fails after the fixed 3-attempt gateway-retry backoff (http_vector_client.py:192-198), with no size-based shrink.

Context: nx (substantive-critic review of uncommitted diff, 2026-07-04/05).
notes:
---
RESOLUTION (analysis, 2026-07-05): the critic framed the batcher flush cap and the client page cap as two distinct constraints wrongly coupled. On analysis they are the SAME constraint — max chunks per single upsert POST bounded by the CP 30s requestTimeout. The batcher flushes <=cap (each flush is one POST); the client pages <=cap (each page is one POST). Both emit POSTs under the same timeout, so sharing per_collection_chunk_cap is CORRECT, not accidental coupling. This is now DOCUMENTED as deliberate in per_collection_chunk_cap's docstring (tuning changes both by design; validate against the CP timeout, never raise for batcher throughput alone).

REMAINING OPEN ITEMS (the real ones):
1. Value 64 vs conexus's suggested ~128 for CCE — a throughput optimization needing a re-gate p99 measurement before raising. Tracked in nexus-o1mbu (this bead's sibling). Not taken blind.
2. No adaptive per-page shrink on the client paging loop (unlike ChunkBatcher's file-level bisect-on-failure). Deliberate: the 64 cap is well below the 172-chunk failure point, and 7yfe6 containment + gateway-retry handle a transient page failure; per-page bisection is unnecessary complexity at a conservative cap. Revisit only if raising the cap toward 128 (o1mbu) brings pages close to the failure point.

This bead is effectively COVERED by the docstring (coupling documented) + o1mbu (value tuning). Close as documented-and-reconciled unless the decouple-into-two-values case materializes (it would only if the batcher cap and page cap ever need DIFFERENT values — no evidence today).
close_reason: Bead's own notes already say 'effectively COVERED... Close as documented-and-reconciled.' Verified: per_collection_chunk_cap docstring in http_vector_client.py:269 documents the ChunkBatcher/upsert-page-size coupling as deliberate, exactly as described. Grooming-pass verification (2026-07-12).

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Groomed 2026-07-08, reconciled against the nexus-o1mbu won't-fix verdict (2026-07-05): the THROUGHPUT half of this bead is dead — the upload path is server-bound (Voyage embed wall), so raising the fallback page size 64->128 halves round-trips without moving the wall (o1mbu measured flush-concurrency 1->3 bought only 76-112s; the '59% of wall' was a summed-thread-seconds artifact). Also empirically confirmed at the duoak.11 re-gate #3 edge forensics ([20406]): drain cadence is per-batch server embed time, not client round-trip overhead. What SURVIVES is the structural half: one shared constant (per_collection_chunk_cap) serves two independently-motivated constraints (batcher oversize threshold vs gateway-safe page size), so tuning either silently moves the other, and the client paging loop has no size-based shrink on a page-level 504 (unlike ChunkBatcher's bisect). P3 hygiene: split the constants when next touching chunk_batcher/http_vector_client; no proactive arc warranted.

title: Tune CCE upsert paging: cap 64->~128 and/or bounded concurrency (nf3n7 follow-up)
description: code-review Medium on nexus-nf3n7: HttpVectorClient.upsert_chunks pages an oversize id set SEQUENTIALLY at cap 64 (CCE). A 2000-chunk CCE file → 32 serial embed+upsert round-trips. Two levers: (1) raise the CCE cap from 64 toward conexus's suggested ~128 (64 was picked empirically off one 504 at 172 chunks; 128 not measured against the 30s CP requestTimeout — needs p99 from a re-gate run); (2) add bounded concurrency to the paging loop matching the <=10-concurrent-writes-per-collection quota (the ChunkBatcher already uses flush_concurrency=3 for the same class). Correctness is fine as-is (rare path — most prose files < 64 chunks); this is throughput-only. NOTE the shared-cap coupling: per_collection_chunk_cap feeds BOTH the client page size AND the batcher flush cap (indexer._cap_for delegates to it) — if tuning, confirm both constraints (gateway-safe AND batcher throughput) still hold, or split them if they diverge.
close_reason: won't-fix: the upload path is SERVER-BOUND (Voyage embed of ~11,667 chunks + PG write), not client-serialization-bound. The '59% of wall' that motivated this bead was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT — chunk_batcher._flush_seconds is summed thread-seconds across concurrent flushes (the 3 duoak sinks sum to 1.9x the actual wall). flush_concurrency=3 was already live at the v0.1.25 gate and the 1->3 bump bought only 76-112s (diminishing returns => server-bound). More client flush concurrency (3->6) or a CCE-cap raise rides that flat curve. Substantive-critic finding 2026-07-05 (T2 nexus/critique-o1mbu-flush-concurrency-2026-07-05.md); corrected sink map T2 nexus/duoak11-wall-decomposition-2026-07-05. Real wall wins delivered elsewhere: register_many (333s serial, nexus-8c0uv) + prune batch (226s serial, nexus-yz8bt). Future <0.5 s/file work targets server-side embed reduction (skip-existing / fewer chunks), NOT client knobs. Sibling nexus-9mzkd (CCE cap-raise) is moot for the same server-bound reason.

title: Escalate a file that transient-504s every run (7yfe6 containment gap)
description: nexus-7yfe6 containment (_contain_transient_upsert) defers a file on a transient 5xx (502/503/504) to staleness retry. Gap (code-review Medium): a file that 504s EVERY run is silently deferred forever — only a per-occurrence WARNING (index_file_transient_upsert_deferred), no consecutive-failure counter, nothing in the CLI summary. With phantom-success (conexus nf3n7: the write usually LANDS despite the 504) this is mostly benign — staleness marks it current next run because the chunks are present — but a file that genuinely never lands would be invisibly skipped. Fix: track consecutive transient-defer count per file (T2 or the staleness cache), and after N consecutive defers surface it in the run summary / escalate to a hard warning. Depends on whether nf3n7's CCE-cap fix makes 504s rare enough to not matter.

title: Detect post-success discover failure during maintenance-mode (qgc4b residual staleness)
description:
qgc4b self-heal guard (_taxonomy_incomplete) covers the 'never succeeded' case: a collection with zero topics always re-runs discover. RESIDUAL gap (substantive-critic, 2026-07-04): once a collection has produced >=1 topic, _taxonomy_incomplete returns False permanently. If discover THEN starts failing on later runs (credential expiry, quota, schema drift), the debug->warning visibility only fires when run_collection_postprocessing is actually invoked — which now requires files_changed>0. A maintenance-mode repo (file churn stopped) coincident with a backend discover failure gets zero further postprocessing invocations => zero warnings, and the 'no files changed — skipping discovery' line gives false reassurance. Silent staleness, indefinite, no operator signal. Options: (a) persist a per-collection last-discover-OK vs last-attempt marker (taxonomy_meta already has last_discover_at) and surface staleness in Nexus health check:

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 — a real `nx index repo .` on the nexus repo itself, live managed/cloud
mode (api.conexus-nexus.com, engine v0.1.69, voyage), conexus 7.5.0, NO --force. This is the
no-change-ish run this bead is about, so the numbers are directly on point.

Corpus: 1930 files, of which 1646 (85%) were skipped as unchanged. 284 changed.
Outcome: exit 0, 0 errors, 0 retries, 0 flush failures.

Where the wall time went:

  [post] Post-processing complete                 627.6s
    Pruning deleted files                         547.8s   <-- 87% of post-processing
    Pruning misclassified chunks                   74.6s
    Catalog manifest self-heal                      5.1s
  Chunk batching: 50 upload batches               124.4s upload (257.2s full flush wall)
    fence                                          41.9s
    flush-grain hooks                              90.2s  (taxonomy 90.1s, manifest 0.0s)
    hook lock wait                                 23.1s  (included above)
  Flush drain                                       3.7s  (3 flushes)

So on a run where 85% of files were unchanged and the actual write work was 3 flushes /
3.7s, PRUNING DELETED FILES ALONE cost 547.8s — roughly 148x the drain it was protecting.
Total run was ~13 minutes, ~9 of them in that one pass.

This is the strongest argument yet for the assessment this bead asks for: the prune pass
cost is essentially independent of how much changed, so it dominates precisely the
warm/no-change case that should be cheapest. Note it also swept 1220 superseded T3 chunks
(nexus-39upx), so it was not a no-op — but 1220 sweeps in 547.8s is ~0.45s per swept chunk,
which is worth understanding on its own.

Adjacent, from the same run: taxonomy is now 90.1s of the 90.2s flush-grain total, i.e.
essentially the entire flush-grain hook cost, on a run with only 284 changed files. Compare
T2 nexus/indexing-perf-assessment-7.4.0 [21715], which measured taxonomy at 0.45-0.57s/flush
on a 109-file probe and concluded the leg had collapsed to noise. At this corpus size it is
back to dominating. NOT ESTABLISHED whether that is corpus-scale (nexus has ~581 production
topics vs the probe's 21) or a regression — worth a separate look before anyone reuses the
"taxonomy leg is solved" conclusion.

Raw log retained for this session at scratchpad/index-run.log (2132 lines, NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=INFO).

title: resolveChunk (local + service) trusts documents.chunk_count, which write_manifest never updates -- stale-cache wrong-404 risk (parity confirmed both sides)
description:
Found during substantive-critic final-gate review of nexus-gc2ze (cac47862).

Both Catalog._DocumentOps.resolve_chunk (src/nexus/catalog/catalog_docs.py:517-538) and the new
CatalogRepository.resolveChunk (service/.../db/CatalogRepository.java:479-490) range-check a
requested chunk_idx against entry.chunk_count / doc.chunk_count, skipping the check only when
chunk_count is falsy (0/None = "not yet known"). Both correctly document that write_manifest()
does NOT update documents.chunk_count -- only resync_chunk_count_cache() (or the equivalent
Java resyncChunkCount) does.

Verified: NONE of write_manifest's production callers (manifest_backfill.py:245,
orphan_backfill.py:364/419/441/564) call resync_chunk_count_cache in the same flow. So there is
a real window -- between a manifest write/append and the next resync pass (projector.py batch
job) -- where documents.chunk_count under-reports the true manifest size. Any resolve_chunk call
for a chunk index >= the STALE cached count during that window returns a false 404/None, even
though the chunk genuinely exists in document_chunks.

This is NOT a regression introduced by gc2ze -- it is a faithful mirror of a pre-existing local
design property (confirmed identical trust assumption on both sides: parity of behavior,
including parity of this latent bug). Flagging because gc2ze's PR description frames the bounds
check as correctly matching local semantics without surfacing that the shared semantics include
this staleness gap.

Recommendation: decide whether write_manifest should opportunistically bump chunk_count (e.g.
to len(chunks) when chunks is non-empty) rather than leaving it to a separate resync pass, or at
minimum note the window as a known limitation in resolve_chunk's docstring on both sides.

title: RDR-173 RF-8 proper fix — daemon SIGTERM handler killing tracked claude pids + reap-on-startup for the SIGKILL case (revisit start_new_session+killpg without the SIGTERM regression)
description: RDR-173 P6 stacked review (substantive-critic, 2026-06-30) DEFERRED the prescribed RF-8 approach. The branch feature/nexus-yobit-rf8-orphan-hardening has a code-review-APPROVED timeout-path grandchild-kill (Popen start_new_session + os.killpg on TimeoutExpired) but the critic found 2 Criticals making it not-justified to ship: (1) it does NOT close the stated RF-8 (host SIGKILL of the daemon orphans claude — uncatchable, no Python runs to killpg); (2) start_new_session is REQUIRED for safe killpg-on-timeout but breaks the SIGTERM-cleanup path — claude survives a graceful daemon SIGTERM and burns quota up to 180s on EVERY restart (common-bad traded for rare-bad). The two are inseparable (without start_new_session, killpg would kill the daemon's own group). RF-8 is NON-blocking: the Phase-3 reclaim-first loop already recovers the stranded row; only bounded quota-burn remains. PROPER FIX (this bead): (a) the daemon tracks active claude pids and a SIGTERM handler kills them on graceful stop (preserves fast cleanup WITH start_new_session); (b) reap-on-startup already exists (reclaim-first) for the SIGKILL row; consider PR_SET_PDEATHSIG for the orphaned-claude quota burn; (c) a non-vacuous grandparent-grandchild test (current test only proves killpg is CALLED on a single-process group, not that grandchildren die); (d) MEDIUM-1: a _invoke_once_batch wiring test. Decide whether the grandchild-kill benefit is real (does claude -p spawn long-running children?) before re-attempting. The branch is the starting point.

title: Same-model migration passthrough trusts source vectors on a name segment, not provenance (vector_etl.py:145-165)
description: Singleton (Low). _is_same_model_passthrough gates verbatim vector copy on name==target AND segments[2] in _PASSTHROUGH_MODELS; a mislabeled collection (name says bge-768 but vectors from a different 768-dim embedder) copies contaminated-but-queryable vectors, backstopped only by a same-dim check any 768-dim model passes. Low-probability (needs a prior indexing bug) but the one migration path guarded by name-trust not vector-provenance. FIX: record + verify embedder provenance (model id in chunk metadata) before passthrough, or re-embed when provenance is unverifiable.
notes:
## Bead: Same-model migration passthrough trusts source vectors on a name segment, not provenance

**Severity:** Singleton (Low) — needs a prior indexing bug to trigger, but it's the one migration path guarded by name-trust rather than vector-provenance.

### What's happening
`_is_same_model_passthrough(name, target)` (`src/nexus/migration/vector_etl.py:145-165`) gates verbatim vector copy on two purely *name-derived* conditions:
1. `name == target` (no model change), and
2. `segments[2] in _PASSTHROUGH_MODELS` (the third `__`-delimited segment of the collection name names a wired model — `bge-base-en-v15-768` or a voyage model).

When both hold, the migrate path (`vector_etl.py:339-374`) fetches stored embeddings (`include_embeddings=True` in `_iter_id_pages`) and upserts them **verbatim** into pgvector, skipping the re-embed. The collection name's model segment is treated as proof of which embedder produced the stored vectors.

### The defect
The conformant collection-name shape is `<content_type>__<owner_id>__<embedding_model>__v<n>` (RDR-103), so `segments[2]` is the *declared* model, not the *actual* embedder. If a prior indexing bug produced a mislabeled collection — name says `…__bge-base-en-v15-768__v1` but the vectors came from a *different* 768-dim embedder — passthrough copies contaminated-but-queryable vectors into a target the service searches with the real bge-768 query embedder. Cross-model semantic mismatch, silently.

The only backstop is the **server-side per-vector dimension check** (mirrored client-side in `_MODEL_DIMS` / `PgVectorRepository.MODEL_DIMS`), which any 768-dim model passes. Dimension equality is necessary but not sufficient for embedding-space compatibility.

### Fix direction (from the bead)
Record + verify **embedder provenance** before passthrough:
- Carry the producing model id in chunk metadata at index time, then verify `metadata["embedding_model"] == segments[2]` before trusting the stored vector for verbatim copy; OR
- Re-embed when provenance is unverifiable (the safe, already-implemented path — passthrough falls back to server-side re-embed for any batch with missing vectors at `vector_etl.py:351-366`, so a provenance-mismatch could route through the same fallback).

Note the existing fallback only triggers on **missing** vectors (`c.get("embedding") is None`), not on present-but-misprovenanced vectors — that's exactly the gap.

### Scope notes
- `minilm` / unknown models are already correctly excluded from `_PASSTHROUGH_MODELS` (no wired query embedder → forced cross-model remap), so the risk is confined to genuinely-wired 768-dim and voyage (1024-dim) collisions.
- Voyage models share dim 1024; a same-name voyage collection carrying vectors from a different voyage variant would be the cloud-mode analog of the same bug.
- This is preventive hardening for a low-probability path; per the project's "no preventive scope beyond the evidence" guidance, confirm whether any real mislabeled collection exists before broadening — but provenance metadata is the structurally correct guard regardless.
close_reason:
DONE — same-model migration passthrough now verifies embedder PROVENANCE before verbatim-copying stored vectors, merged to develop (79c7f966). Closes the name-trust gap: a mislabeled collection (name declares model X but chunks recorded a different embedder) is detected and re-embedded instead of copying contaminated-but-queryable vectors.

Design: MISMATCH-ONLY (revised from STRICT after substantive-critic evidence). Re-embed ONLY when metadata embedding_model is PRESENT and DISAGREES with the declared name segment — the actual detectable mislabel. ABSENT/blank provenance is TRUSTED (passed through) NOT re-embedded: code_indexer didn't stamp embedding_model until the make_chunk_metadata factory (2026-04-26) but conformant code__*__voyage-code-3__v1 names existed from 2026-02-22, so pre-factory chunks have conformant names + no provenance yet correct vectors — STRICT would have silently reverted the nexus-hxry2 passthrough optimization (billed Voyage / wasted ONNX) for that 63-day window with no correctness gain. Aligns with 'no preventive scope beyond evidence': absent != mislabel.

Implementation reuses the existing missing-vector re-embed fallback (no new machinery); warn log gains provenance_mismatch count. Both stacked reviewers 0 Critical; applied all findings: MISMATCH-ONLY (critic's evidence-backed cost-regression), defensive declared_model-None guard (code-review), structlog capture_logs audit-pin (exact counts provenance_mismatch=3/missing_vectors=0). TDD: mislabel->re-embed + absent->passthrough tests. 53 passed. vector_etl.py:_migrate_one.

title: Re-home chunk_id() helper out of HttpVectorClient (network-client staticmethod, zero callers) and adopt across the 6 indexers
description: F8 (Low). sha256(text).hexdigest()[:32] is recomputed inline at 6 indexer sites (pipeline_stages.py:237, doc_indexer.py:1039-1040/1127-1128, prose_indexer.py:100-101/164-165, code_indexer.py:394-395), each with its own 'RDR-108 D1' comment. The canonical helper HttpVectorClient.chunk_id() (http_vector_client.py:1185-1188) has ZERO callers — its wrong home (a network-client staticmethod) is plausibly why indexers never adopted it. FIX: move to a neutral chunk_identity module and have the 6 indexers import it. Low blast radius (all emit identical output; drift surfaces as a retrieval miss caught by integration tests).
notes:
## F8 (Low): Re-home `chunk_id()` helper and adopt across the 6 indexer sites

**Goal**: Move the canonical chunk-natural-ID helper out of its wrong home (a zero-caller `@staticmethod` on the network client `HttpVectorClient`) into a neutral module, and have the 6 indexer sites import it instead of recomputing `sha256(text).hexdigest()[:32]` inline.

### Verified facts (paths in bead were stale — corrected here)
The indexer files live in `src/nexus/`, NOT `src/nexus/catalog/`. Confirmed sites:
- `src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:237` — `chunk_id = hashlib.sha256(chunk.text.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]` (full recompute; preceded by `# RDR-108 D1 / nexus-kmb6` comment at line 233).
- `src/nexus/doc_indexer.py:1039-1040` and `1127-1128` — computes `chunk_text_hash_full = hashlib.sha256(chunk.text.encode()).hexdigest()` then `chunk_id = chunk_text_hash_full[:32]`.
- `src/nexus/prose_indexer.py:100-101` and `164-165` — same `chunk_text_hash_full` then `[:32]` pattern (uses `import hashlib as _hl`).
- `src/nexus/code_indexer.py:394-395` — same pattern (uses `import hashlib as _hl`).

Each site carries an `RDR-108 D1 (nexus-kmb6)` comment.

**Canonical helper** (the wrong-home staticmethod, ZERO callers confirmed via `chunk_id\b` grep):
`src/nexus/db/http_vector_client.py:1185-1188`:
```python
@staticmethod
def chunk_id(text: str) -> str:
    """Compute the canonical chunk natural ID: sha256(text)[:32]."""
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
```

### Important nuance (don't blindly drop-in)
The bead frames all 6 as "recomputed inline," but only **pipeline_stages.py:237** does a standalone full recompute. The doc/prose/code sites compute `chunk_text_hash_full` (the *full* 64-char hexdigest) because that full hash is **reused for other metadata** at those sites — they only slice `[:32]` for the natural ID. So:
- A `chunk_id(text)` helper (text → `[:32]`) cleanly replaces pipeline_stages.py:237.
- At the doc/prose/code sites, naively swapping in `chunk_id(text)` would re-run sha256 a second time (the full hash is still needed). Prefer one of: (a) keep `chunk_text_hash_full` and slice it (output is byte-identical to the helper — the helper is the *definition of correctness*, the slice is an accepted equivalent), or (b) add a sibling helper that derives the natural ID from an already-computed full hexdigest (e.g. `chunk_id_from_hash(full: str) -> str: return full[:32]`). Decide and apply consistently; document which path each site takes.

### Suggested approach
1. Create `src/nexus/chunk_identity.py` (module-level `chunk_id(text: str) -> str`, type-hinted, with the RDR-108 D1 rationale in the docstring). Neutral home, no network-client coupling.
2. Update `HttpVectorClient.chunk_id` to delegate to the new module (or remove it — confirmed zero callers, so removal is safe; keeping a thin delegate avoids any external-import surprise but adds no value given zero callers — removal preferred).
3. Adopt at the 6 sites: import from `nexus.chunk_identity`, replace the inline `[:32]` derivation, drop the now-redundant per-site `RDR-108 D1` comments (or collapse to a single reference to the helper).
4. Keep output bit-identical — all 6 currently emit `sha256(text)[:32]`; any drift surfaces as a retrieval miss (caught only by integration tests, hence Low blast radius but worth the regression test).

### TDD
Write `tests/test_chunk_identity.py` first: assert `chunk_id("known string") == "<exact 32 hex>"` (lock the exact value, per the exact-assertions rule), assert length 32, assert it equals `sha256(text).hexdigest()[:32]` for several inputs including unicode. Then refactor.

title: RDR-164 Q5 arm (b): DELETE genuinely-orphaned lifecycle rows at reconcile with a logged count
description:
RDR-164 P1b shipped the Q5 reconcile with arm (a) stub-register (unconditional, all referenced (tenant_id,collection)) + arm (c) fail-loud via VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, but did NOT implement arm (b). The RDR-164 Q5 resolution (docs/rdr/rdr-164-collection-lifecycle-cascade-consolidation.md, Open Questions #5) mandates three arms; arm (b): for a (tenant_id,collection) referenced by a lifecycle table but GENUINELY orphaned (no chunks, no catalog projection, no live collection), DELETE the offending child rows with a logged count rather than stub-registering them.

Current behaviour: fk-003-6-reconcile (service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/fk-003-validate.xml) stub-registers EVERY referenced collection unconditionally, so a genuinely-orphaned child row (e.g. an aspect_extraction_queue row whose collection has no chunks/projection) is given an inert stub parent and survives — it is NOT auto-purged until that stub collection is explicitly deleted (P2 deleteCollection). This is no-data-loss but leaves orphan child rows the RDR intended to remove (the nexus-tquoj churn class).

Why deferred / low priority: the engine-side production migration already ran with summary.total_failed==0 (2026-06-10, 115,716 chunks), so the gap-window reconcile is expected to register ~zero rows in current prod; arm (b) is hardening for the genuinely-orphaned case, not a live incident. Substantive-critic reviewed and accepted the arm-(a)+(c)-only shape for P1b (PR #1279).
design: Distinguish case (a) live-data vs case (b) genuinely-orphaned BEFORE stub-registering: a (tenant_id,collection) is live iff chunks_{384,768,1024} or the catalog projection has a row for it. For genuinely-orphaned refs (no chunks, no projection, not in catalog_collections), DELETE the referencing rows from the lifecycle table(s) with a per-table logged count (structured migration issue, RDR-153 discipline — no silent drop). Sequence: arm(b) DELETE-orphaned → arm(a) stub-register-remaining → arm(c) VALIDATE. Keep fail-loud on ambiguity (case c). Add a Java test mirroring CollectionRegistryFkExtraTest GROUP G: seed a genuinely-orphaned child row (no chunks/projection), run the three-arm reconcile, assert the row is DELETED (not stub-registered) and a count is logged, then VALIDATE succeeds. Decide whether this is a new fk-003 changeset or a one-time migrate-time tool step (the reconcile is idempotent INSERT today; a DELETE arm is destructive and must be guarded/logged).
acceptance_criteria: Three-arm reconcile implemented: genuinely-orphaned lifecycle rows DELETEd with a logged per-table count; live-data refs stub-registered; ambiguous refs fail loud. Java test proves arm-(b) DELETE path (orphan with no chunks/projection is removed, not stub-registered). Empty-string-collection document_highlights case still fails loud (arm c) or is explicitly NULL-normalized — documented either way. No silent data loss; counts surfaced.

title: nx taxonomy review delete/merge leaks centroid in LOCAL (CatalogTaxonomy/chroma) mode — review_cmd passes no chroma_client
description: Local-mode half of nexus-cugrk (service-mode half fixed: HttpTaxonomyStore.delete_topic/merge_topics now self-clean via self._centroid). review_cmd in src/nexus/commands/taxonomy_cmd.py (lines ~922/928, and the merge at ~1022) call db.taxonomy.delete_topic/merge_topics with NO chroma_client. CatalogTaxonomy.delete_topic/merge_topics (catalog_taxonomy.py:1060/1093) only clean the taxonomy__centroids chroma collection when chroma_client is passed; CatalogTaxonomy holds no centroid handle of its own (only path+memory), so it cannot self-clean like the http store does. Result: in NX_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite mode the orphan centroid persists in chroma and keeps attracting chunks. Fix options: (a) thread a chroma centroid client into review_cmd and pass it to delete/merge (cheap, but resurrects caller-handles contract), or (b) give CatalogTaxonomy a lazily-resolved centroid handle. LOW PRIORITY / may be obsoleted: the chroma taxonomy__centroids path is deleted in RDR-155 P4b; in the 6.0 service-mode default db.taxonomy is HttpTaxonomyStore (already fixed). Worth closing only if the sqlite-local taxonomy path survives P4b.
notes: DISPOSITION (RDR-164 P5, user-approved): CLOSE OBSOLETE. The cugrk LOCAL-mode chroma centroid leak cannot occur post-RDR-155 P4a.2: make_t3() always returns HttpVectorClient (no _client); is_service_backed==isinstance(_,HttpVectorClient); the raw-Chroma taxonomy__centroids path is unreachable in production AND no caller ever passed chroma_client (grep-verified). Supported SERVICE config uses HttpTaxonomyStore (pgvector self-clean). A first 'land' attempt (lazy make_t3()._client handle) was a verified no-op (reviewers caught it) and was reverted. Dead inline chroma cleanup blocks removed in PR #1277. Full chroma centroid-write deletion = RDR-155 P4b. Closes at PR #1277 merge.

title: Rework TestManifestFkIntegration cross-dim orphan test for bge-768 (vec_etl)
description: SHAKEOUT follow-up to nexus-wrfiy. tests/migration/test_vector_etl.py::TestManifestFkIntegration::test_backfill_then_orphan_detection is skipped. It proves manifest orphan detection scopes correctly ACROSS the 384/768 chunk lanes (a 768-collection manifest row must not appear as a 384 orphan, and vice versa). Pre-RDR-160 the migrated collection was 384, and the test added a 768 collection via direct SQL for the cross-dim assertion. Now the service only embeds bge-768, so migrate_local produces a 768 collection — collapsing the cross-dim distinction. REWORK: make the MIGRATED collection 768 (model=_MODEL_768, manifest_orphan_sql(768) for it) and INSERT a 384 collection via direct SQL (chunks_384 + catalog rows, not via migrate) to keep the 384/768 orphan-scoping assertion non-vacuous. Verify with a live JAR-launched pgvector service. Low priority: the other ETL integration classes + cross-model tests cover the migration fidelity; this is one cross-dim-scoping edge test.

title: guided-upgrade: combine version-pin + voyage-capability into ONE /version fetch
description: code-review M1 + critic Obs1 on nexus-8o9pm. /version is fetched twice in tight succession: verify_service_version (release_version pin, ez5.4) then verify_voyage_capability (embedding_models, 8o9pm). Both parse the SAME /version body. Combine into one fetch (e.g. verify_service_version returns embedding_models too, or establish_verified_service captures the body and exposes it on ServiceReadiness) to avoid the double round-trip + tiny TOCTOU. Negligible for a loopback local service; matters more on a remote --service-url managed endpoint (3 round-trips before migration: health, version-pin, voyage-cap).

title: guided-upgrade: thread the verified service_url into run_guided_upgrade's pre-gate (make endpoint convergence explicit)
description: substantive-critic Sig-1 on nexus-8o9pm. The voyage-capability gate reads /version at readiness.service_url (httpx); the migration's pre-gate (RDR-159 P1 LiveServiceWiredModels) re-reads /version via resolve_service_config() -> NX_SERVICE_URL env (urllib). They converge ONLY because _run_migration sets NX_SERVICE_URL=readiness.service_url before the pre-gate runs — an IMPLICIT contract via env side-effect. Worst case (stale config, service capability changed mid-run): the gate passes but the pre-gate falls back to the deployment-mode floor (wired_models(voyage_key_present)) and re-blocks with the OLD client-key diagnostic the gate was built to replace. Low probability (same service, narrow window) but the coupling is implicit. Fix: pass the verified service_url explicitly as the live-wired-models source to run_guided_upgrade so the pre-gate uses the same endpoint string rather than re-discovering it. Documented inline at guided_upgrade_cmd.py gate site.
close_reason: Mooted twice over: run_guided_upgrade is the DEMOTED surface (RDR-185 P4.1, dies at RDR-155 P4b), and the managed-migration journey whose endpoint-convergence this would make explicit was retired entirely by the 2026-07-17 population decree (managed onboarding is greenfield-only; nexus-51djh). title: [observation] Managed-service Voyage embedding: single operator key models cost but not rate/isolation
description: Surfaced 2026-06-19 (grooming). The managed multitenant cloud service embeds SERVER-SIDE with ONE operator-owned Voyage key (squid-proxied); no per-tenant key. Cost is handled (per-tenant token metering, nexus-ehc4q) but RATE and ISOLATION are not: (1) shared Voyage RPM/TPM/128-batch ceiling -> noisy-neighbor (one tenant's index/migrate starves others); (2) single blast radius (key compromise/revoke/Voyage-suspension = all tenants lose embedding); (3) no per-tenant key rotation. Options: (a) accept+document now, (b) per-tenant rate budgeting / fair-share on the engine embed path (one key, no key-mgmt complexity), (c) per-tenant BYO Voyage key (full isolation, more surface). DESIGN CALL is conexus RDR-001's — relayed [4376] engine_service/RELAY-to-conexus-RDR-001-per-tenant-voyage-rate-isolation-design-question-2026-06-19. Non-blocking (not luxe6/v0.1.6/cutover). Hold for conexus disposition; mirror their decision here.
close_reason: Grooming close (Hal, 2026-07-17). Recorded observation, no action defined: the managed service embeds through a single operator Voyage key, which models COST attribution but not per-tenant rate/isolation. True, known, and acceptable for a solo-operated service with greenfield-only tenants (managed migration retired by the 2026-07-17 decree). If tenant count ever grows to where rate isolation matters, that is an RDR, not this bead.

During a run the file shows M in git status; an IDE auto-stage or parallel git add -p could commit the stamped value. Lower-footgun alternative: have the native build read release_version from an UNTRACKED override file (env/property) so the tracked source is never mutated. Pragmatic current design reuses the existing release-stamp mechanism; revisit.

title: Migration-rehearsal: intermittent supervisor lease-not-kept-fresh (single supervisor publishes lease, vanishes before migrate)
description: Release-pinned rehearsal run 9 (2026-06-19): the persistent supervisor (single, pid 118, no double-supervisor race) published its lease (storage_service_lease_published gen 1) at service-ready, but ~24s later at migrate time the lease was GONE ('No storage service lease found') -> T2 migrate-all endpoint-not-resolvable -> dirty-T2 blocks T3. No exit_detected, no crash log, single supervisor. Run 10 (identical setup) did NOT hit it -> INTERMITTENT. This is a residual qke1e-class lease-heartbeat lifecycle flake (qke1e fixed the transient-init-lease + double-supervisor race; this is a different residual where a single persistent supervisor's lease is not kept fresh). Low frequency; the rehearsal otherwise reaches the migrate. Investigate: does run_storage_supervisor's heartbeat_once stop re-stamping (e.g. /health or PG check flapping during/after a slow ~21s native boot)? Repro: tests/e2e/migration-rehearsal/run.sh (intermittent). Not RDR-162-blocking (RDR-162 closed; rehearsal proven green run 8).
notes: FIX SHIPPED (PR #1246 -> develop). Root cause: supervisor OOM-kill at boot (debugger-confirmed). Fix: (B) per-tier lease TTL in shared primitive service_registry.TIER_TTLS[storage_service]=15s via ttl_for_tier; (C) optional -Xmx (NX_SERVICE_MAX_HEAP, default-off, rehearsal=1g). Validated: rehearsal run 12 GREEN. Stacked review 0 Critical; S1/S2/S3 addressed (conformance harness now rides real per-tier TTL; TTL in primitive per RDR-149; restart-window residual documented). 105 daemon+conformance+gate tests green. Follow-up: nexus-03bcg (client re-spawn backstop).

title: Documented, stable discovery-file contract for non-Python (foreign) clients
description: Consumer ask from Conductus (Hellblazer/conductus RDR-001 OQ-4). The service endpoint is published as a lease record (owner_token+heartbeat+TTL, atomic tmpfile+os.replace) to a discovery file under the nexus config dir (RDR-120/149 discovery.py, service_registry.py), with env-var override precedence. Today the file path + JSON schema are an internal Python contract (nexus.daemon.discovery). A TS/Node client (Conductus) cannot auto-discover the local endpoint without reverse-engineering that format, so its MVP requires a manually configured endpoint. A documented, versioned discovery-file contract (path resolution rule + JSON schema + liveness/TTL semantics) would let foreign clients detect the running service the same way the Python client does.
acceptance_criteria: Discovery-file path resolution and JSON payload schema (including lease TTL / liveness interpretation and env-var precedence) are documented as a stable, versioned contract consumable by non-Python clients. Conductus can resolve + liveness-check the local endpoint from the file without manual config. Back-reference to conductus RDR-001 OQ-4 retained.

title: engine Main: log embedding-mode banner BEFORE constructing the embedder (OOM-on-load hides the mode)
description: Surfaced by the conexus STEP-5 v0.1.0 OOM (2026-06-17, conexus-qcn). In Main.java the local-mode WARN banner (event=embedding_mode_banner, line ~133) logs AFTER 'new Bge768Embedder()' (line ~130). When the 436MB bge ONNX OOM-segfaults at construction (e.g. an under-sized host that booted local-mode because NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY was absent), the process dies BEFORE the banner logs, so the operator cannot see which embedding mode was selected — the exact misdiagnosis that happened (read as 'unconditional bge load' rather than 'booted local mode, missing voyage key'). Fix: emit the embedding-mode banner (mode + chosen model) BEFORE constructing the heavy embedder, in BOTH branches, so an OOM-on-load still names the mode first. Optional stronger hardening: if cloud-topology markers are present (e.g. NX_DB_URL is a remote/managed PG) but NX_VOYAGE_API_KEY is absent, WARN hard 'looks like a cloud deploy booting local-mode bge — likely a missing voyage key'. Small, no behavior change to embedding itself; rides the next engine patch (no urgency — the env-var fix unblocks the deploy).

title: collection_health.stale_source_ratio: meaningful staleness detection (DB-only is structurally impossible)
description: RDR-154 P2 (nexus-2zv75) attempted to wire catalog_documents.source_mtime into collection_health.stale_source_ratio but the DB-only computation is STRUCTURALLY VACUOUS: source_mtime is the file mtime captured AT INDEX TIME (indexer.py stat before read_bytes), and indexed_at=now() is written after, so source_mtime <= indexed_at ALWAYS; a 'modified since indexing' ratio from stored columns is identically zero. Caught by substantive-critic 2026-06-16 (Critical); the P2 wiring was reverted, stale_source_ratio stays the '—' placeholder with the analysis in collection_health.py module docstring. Real staleness detection requires ONE of: (a) live filesystem stat at report time (current st_mtime vs stored indexed_at) — local-mode only, service host may not mount files; (b) redefine to age-based staleness (indexed_at older than N days) — DB-only, different semantic, would need renaming the column; (c) a file-watcher event path refreshing source_mtime to current while leaving indexed_at frozen. Needs an owner decision on which semantic before implementing.
close_reason: Implemented owner-chosen age-based stale_source_ratio (fraction of docs indexed >30 days ago, index-age proxy) DB-only across both backends (SQLite strftime-epoch, PG catalog-011 lexicographic ISO compare, no parse-throw) + report wiring. Stacked review 0 Critical both; 2 Significant addressed (threaded day constant, documented non-UTC parity caveat). 762 Java + 163 python green.

title: Python local-mode Catalog.stats() omits chunk_count (Java/PG parity gap)
description: Pre-existing Java/Python parity gap surfaced by RDR-154 P1 substantive-critic (S1). The Java /stats response (now via the catalog_stats view) returns chunk_count = count(catalog_document_chunks); the Python SQLite local-mode Catalog.stats() (src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py:1094) returns only doc_count/link_count/owner_count/collection_count, never chunk_count. NOT introduced by P1 (the original Java stats() already returned chunk_count). Semantics differ across backends: PG counts manifest rows (catalog_document_chunks); SQLite stores a per-document chunk_count column. Decide a parity semantic and add chunk_count to the SQLite path, OR confirm it is moot because RDR-158 retires the SQLite T2 backend. Low priority; flagged on RDR-154 P1.2.
close_reason: Added chunk_count to Python Catalog.stats() (COUNT document_chunks manifest = PG catalog_stats parity, drift-free) + rendered in nx catalog stats + forwarded through the MCP catalog_stats tool. substantive-critic verified parity-table correctness; 1 Significant (MCP drop) fixed. 290 green.

title: Batch per-topic assignment INSERTs in persistRebuildTopics/persistDiscoveredTopics (doc_count trigger O(N^2))
description: RDR-154 P0 (nexus-i7ivk) made topics.doc_count trigger-maintained via a statement-level recompute (full COUNT per affected topic). persistRebuildTopics (TaxonomyRepository ~1138) and persistDiscoveredTopics (~1205) insert assignments one-by-one in Java loops; each single-row INSERT fires the statement-level trigger which COUNT(*)s the topic's growing assignment set => O(N^2) per topic on rebuild/discovery. The statement-level cost benefit only materializes with multi-row INSERT...VALUES / COPY. Batch the per-topic assignment INSERTs into a single multi-row statement so the trigger fires once per topic. Perf only; correctness already green. Flagged by P0.2 code-review-expert (MEDIUM-2) on commit 7dfc7488.
close_reason: Batched per-topic assignment INSERTs (shared batchInsertAssignments helper, chunked multi-row INSERT) — P0 doc_count trigger fires once per topic instead of per-row, collapsing O(N^2). Behavior-preserving; TaxonomyRepositoryTest 37 + full suite 757 green; stacked review 0 Critical (both).

title: EmbedderRouter embedder lifecycle: close shared embedder once on service shutdown
description: Pre-existing (surfaced in RDR-160 P2 review, code-review M1). Main passes the SAME embedder instance to both docEmbedRouter and qryEmbedRouter; EmbedderRouter.close() calls localEmbedder.close() unconditionally, and the Main shutdown hook closes neither router. Net: the native OrtSession + tokenizer are never closed on JVM shutdown (benign today — JVM exit reclaims). RISK: if router close() is later added to the shutdown hook, the shared embedder is double-closed (Bge768Embedder/OnnxEmbedder swallow the 2nd close, so no crash, but fragile). Fix: designate one router the owner, or a shared-owner/ref-count pattern, and wire a single close on shutdown. Low priority.

title: RDR-159 P3 hardening: per-dim manifest non-vacuity probe (total-rows-per-dim)
description: Substantive-critic SIG-2 on P3 (nexus-ue6g7.19): the manifest vacuity guard probes nexus.catalog_documents (catches T2-never-ran). Decide whether worth the added surface vs the count-leg guarantee.

title: ensure-running 15s reachability timeout too tight for cold first-open — false 'stalled startup migration' warning baits operators into respawn races
description: nx daemon t2 ensure-running uses a 15s reachability timeout. A cold first-open (esp. first 5.10.x open with a startup migration) can take slightly longer to become reachable, so ensure-running prints 'T2 daemon did not become reachable within 15.0s (process still alive — likely a slow or stalled startup migration)' even though the process comes up fine ~immediately after. Observed 2026-06-06 during 5.10.4 local deploy: a single clean spawn was reachable in ~5s, but under operator retry the warning baited a stop/kill/respawn loop that raced the spawn lock into 2-3 half-initialized daemons. FIX OPTIONS: (1) raise the cold-start timeout or make it adaptive (longer on first-open/migration); (2) distinguish 'still initializing (migration in progress)' from 'stalled' — poll a startup-progress signal rather than a flat deadline; (3) ensure-running should be idempotent under concurrent invocation (detect an in-flight spawn and wait on it rather than spawning a second). Related: RDR-149 lifecycle primitive, known MCP/CLI spawn-race caveat. Not a 5.10.4 regression.
close_reason: Groomed 2026-07-12 (user directive: not solving SQLite-T2-daemon / ChromaDB issues; substrates retired-in-place post RDR-152/155 cutover). SQLite-T2-daemon ensure-running reachability timeout; daemon retired.

title: RDR-151 P2.2: dedicated flock for crash-loop sentinel read-modify-write (Gap 6)
description:

When _acquire_election_lock times out and returns None, ensure-running proceeds UNGUARDED (commands/daemon.py:1040-1046) into the crash-loop sentinel read-modify-write (:1123-1143). os.replace is atomic per write but does NOT serialize concurrent writers, so K racers lost-update the count — degrading guard accuracy under exactly the contention Gaps 3/4 create.

This is the ALREADY-FILED nexus-whl8n / RDR-140 P4 deferral.

FIX (RDR §Decision item 5): a DEDICATED flock around the crash-loop sentinel read-modify-write (commands/daemon.py:1123-1143), INDEPENDENT of the election lock (the election lock having timed out is precisely the unguarded path).

FILES: src/nexus/commands/daemon.py crash-loop guard (1123-1143), _read_crashloop / _write_crashloop_atomic / _record_restart.

TDD: test-first, EXACT-COUNT regression test (RDR Test Plan: 'Exact-count regression tests for the crash-loop sentinel under simulated election-lock-timeout contention'). Simulate K concurrent racers with election lock timed out; assert the final count == exact expected (no lost updates). Use port=0 / tmp config_dir; deterministic. mem:feedback_exact_assertions_for_fixture_regression.

Cross-ref: nexus-whl8n (RDR-140 P4) — this bead implements it. Context: RDR-151 §Decision item 5, §Test Plan.

title: T2 daemon stop() socket teardown (wait_closed) is not timeout-bounded
description: Surfaced by substantive-critic on nexus-64w50 (commit 8214eee8). T2Daemon.stop() calls _uds_server.close()/wait_closed() and _tcp_server.close()/wait_closed() with NO asyncio.wait_for wrapper, despite a comment implying _GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT guards it. The DB close (_DB_CLOSE_TIMEOUT 10s) IS bounded; socket teardown is not, so a connection draining a long in-flight RPC at SIGTERM can extend the drain (and thus the spawn-lock hold) unbounded. Not a correctness failure (the spawn-loss retry exits 0 and launchd/ensure-running re-spawns), but enforcing _GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT on wait_closed via asyncio.wait_for (same pattern as the DB close) would make the drain budget real. Comment corrected in 8214eee8 to stop claiming an enforcement that doesn't exist.

title: pipeline.db fd-leak: connection-per-unit-of-work in nx dt index leaks 20+ duplicate fds (split from RDR-146)
description: PipelineDB (src/nexus/pipeline_buffer.py:84-106) uses threading.local() connections and is constructed per-call at src/nexus/pipeline_stages.py:617 with no close(). In nx dt index, each _index_record -> index_pdf -> pipeline_index_pdf creates a new PipelineDB(); thread-local conns from prior calls stay open until GC, so a batch of 20+ PDFs accumulates 20+ open fds to pipeline.db (observed live in GH #1046). Fix: pass a shared PipelineDB singleton from the index_cmd/dt batch loop into _index_record, or add explicit db.close() in pipeline_index_pdf on exit. Orthogonal to the catalog daemon (different file, different root cause = resource lifecycle not lock contention); split out of RDR-146 per the 2026-06-03 research pass.
close_reason: Obsolete — the substrate this fd-leak lived in was retired: RDR-186 .16 deleted src/nexus/pipeline_buffer.py entirely (verified gone) and pipeline state moved engine-side; pipeline_stages.py now constructs HttpPipelineDB (an HTTP client — no thread-local sqlite connections, no pipeline.db fds). The leak mechanism (threading.local conns to a local file accumulating across a dt batch) cannot recur. Per-call HttpPipelineDB construction cost, if it ever matters, is nexus-146xx.22's batching scope.

title: Per-collection embedder resolution trusts the collection-name embedder token over the actual stored dim — a name/dim-mismatched collection silently skips every search (nx doctor drift check)
description:
Found during 5.9.2 shakeout (Claude-P6 isolated profile, conexus 5.9.2 .mcpb). The #1068 fix WORKS (mcp-server-Conexus.log: extension query embedding dim went 384 pre-update -> 768 post-update, i.e. fastembed now present so bge-768 is used instead of the minilm-384 fallback). BUT Hal's collections are voyage-context-3 / voyage-code-3 (1024d, cloud), so the local bge-768 query STILL mismatches: every search logs 'collection_dimension_mismatch_skipped' + 'search_all_collections_dimension_skipped queried=1 skipped=1'. Net: Desktop vector search returns ZERO for this cloud user; #1068 moved the dim 384->768 but the real blocker is the extension running LOCAL mode at all.

ROOT-CAUSE GAP: is_local_mode() reads creds via get_credential (env -> ~/.config/nexus/config.yml under credentials.<name>). Hal's creds ARE in config.yml; a clean CLI sim with env creds STRIPPED returns is_local_mode()=False (cloud) and get_credential finds ck-8.../pa-X.... So the documented mitigation ('persist via nx config set' per docs/desktop-deployment.md failure modes) SHOULD give the GUI extension cloud mode -- yet the extension empirically resolves LOCAL (768d). The GUI-spawned .mcpb's runtime context differs (different HOME/NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR, an NX_LOCAL override, or a config-read failure) and needs a focused investigation: dump the extension's actual HOME / NEXUS_CONFIG_DIR / NX_LOCAL / which config.yml it reads at startup (add a one-line structured startup log of resolved mode + embedder + config path). The good-looking Desktop answers come through non-vector paths (store_get / store_get_many by id, FTS fallback), masking the broken vector search. Adjacent: docs failure-mode 'GUI subprocess can't see shell-env creds' + the orphaned knowledge__memory__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1 collection whose name says 384 but expects 1024 (stale rename). Relates #1068.
close_reason: Diagnostic groundwork complete (not a fix for the mode-resolution divergence itself, which needs live Desktop access): one-line structured startup log at MCP server start captures resolved mode, local embedder, config_dir, HOME, NX_LOCAL, and all 3 credential-presence branches. Committed 947f60ea. Next live Desktop run will surface the actual root cause via mcp.log.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: CORRECTION after deeper diagnosis (sequential-thinking 2nd pass + log ground truth): the original 'Desktop resolves local mode -> search broken' conclusion was WRONG. Ground truth: (1) #1068 fix works (query dim 384->768); (2) Desktop search WORKS — the model's search returned 'showing 1-10 of 127' from voyage-1024 collections and the answer was genuinely vector-grounded; (3) is_local_mode()=False (cloud) confirmed in both CLI and the extension venv. The ONLY failure was a single CORRUPT orphan collection knowledge__memory__minilm-l6-v2-384__v1 (1 chunk): its name claims minilm-384 but it stores 1024-dim vectors (stale T2-memory->T3 mirror, later re-embedded at voyage but kept the old name). Per-collection embedder resolution picked a LOCAL embedder for it (bge-768 post-fix, minilm-384 pre-fix), neither matching its 1024 stored dim -> skipped every search, spamming collection_dimension_mismatch_skipped. DELETED the orphan; bare search is now clean (no skip warnings, hits return). NOT a Desktop search regression. Reframing this bead to the residual: per-collection embedder resolution trusts the collection NAME's embedder token over the actual stored dim, so a name/dim-mismatched collection silently skips instead of erroring loudly at index/rename time. Low-pri hygiene: a guard that detects name-vs-stored-dim drift (nx doctor check) would catch this class.

title: RDR-140 follow-up: real-process version-skew multi-stack harness scenario (P3 case c)
description: P3.1 bead (nexus-r9hq0) case (c) asked for a real-process version-skew convergence scenario in tests/daemon/test_t2_multistack_race.py (start an old-version daemon, K current-version supervisors, assert 1 reap + 1 new + rest attach). design:
## Real-process version-skew multi-stack harness (P3 case c)

SITE: tests/daemon/test_t2_multistack_race.py (extend). Current deterministic substitute: tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_startup_invariant.py::TestDaemonReapDiscrimination::test_mixed_targets_reap_only_the_stale_one.

WHY DEFERRED: staging a real old-version daemon is impractical (daemon version = importlib.metadata.version('conexus'), same for all in-tree procs). IF PURSUED: spoof the stale daemon by writing a discovery token with an old daemon_version pointing at a real running current daemon, then race ensure-running (exercises the P2 version-cycle path) — note this tests ensure-running's cycle, NOT the P3 startup reap discrimination, which is why the deterministic unit test is arguably the better signal. title: RDR-140 follow-up: crash-loop guard — flapping daemon defeats reset-on-reachability (consecutive-failures model)
description: P4 critic Significant: the guard calls _reset_crashloop the moment _daemon_is_alive() first returns True in the convergence poll. A daemon that becomes briefly reachable then dies repeatedly (flapping) clears the counter each cycle, so the guard fires only for a daemon that never reaches discovery-written state within the spawn timeout. A 'consecutive failures' counter (incremented per non-converging spawn, reset only after a stable-running hold-off) would catch flapping too. Currently documented as a known limitation in cli-reference.md. Source: T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-critique-2026-05-31.
design:
## Flapping daemon defeats reset-on-reachability

SITE: src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:1160 _reset_crashloop(config_dir) — called the moment _daemon_is_alive() first returns True in the convergence poll (:1154-1161 region).

PROBLEM: a daemon that starts, briefly passes the os.kill(pid,0)+socket probe, gets reset, then dies — repeatedly — clears the counter every cycle. The guard only fires for a daemon that NEVER reaches discovery-written/reachable state within --timeout. The #1041 flapping pattern (reachable-then-dies) is exactly what slips through. Currently documented as a known limitation in docs/cli-reference.md (ensure-running section).

PROPOSED MODEL: 'consecutive failures' instead of 'N timestamps in a window with eager reset': a monotonically incrementing fail counter, reset ONLY after a stable-running hold-off (daemon stayed reachable for H seconds, not just one probe). Interacts with nexus-cis97 (if the guard moves into start, 'stable run' is the natural reset signal). Keep the window model OR replace — decide at design.

ACCEPTANCE: a flapping daemon (reachable then dies, repeated) trips the guard within a bounded number of cycles; a genuinely healthy daemon never trips. Deterministic test (inject clock + reachability sequence). Source: critic P4.4 Significant; T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-critique-2026-05-31.
close_reason: Groomed 2026-07-12: obsolete — RDR-140 crash-loop flapping edge; documented accepted limitation, spawn-lock backstops, daemon-spawn path retired-in-place.

title: RDR-140 follow-up: crash-loop guard robustness — monotonic clock + atomic counter + window boundary
description: P4 crash-loop guard review (code-review nexus-d8qvr, critic nexus-b4nq1) deferred: (MEDIUM) the sentinel read-modify-write under-counts when the election lock times out under heavy contention (K racers, last-writer-wins) — guard trips later than intended; (LOW) window uses wall-clock time.time(), vulnerable to NTP step-back (use time.monotonic for the window, time.time only for stored stamp, or document); (LOW) window boundary is closed-both-ends (t>=cutoff), pruning at window+epsilon not window — test only covers window+1.0. Daemon spawn-lock still backstops single-writer throughout. Source: T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-code-review-2026-05-31.
design:
## Crash-loop guard robustness (MEDIUM+LOW from P4 review)

SITE: src/nexus/commands/daemon.py:832-865 (_restart_count, _record_restart, _crashloop_tripped) + the ensure-running call site :1107-1127.

1. (MEDIUM) Non-atomic read-modify-write under election-lock timeout. _record_restart (:839) does read (_read_crashloop) -> append -> _write_crashloop_atomic. The write is atomic but the R-M-W is not. When _acquire_election_lock returns None (timeout, commands/daemon.py ~:1019) the spawn path runs UNGUARDED, so K racers can lost-update the sentinel -> under-count -> guard trips later than _CRASHLOOP_MAX_RESTARTS. Not a safety hole (db spawn-lock backstops single-writer); degrades guard accuracy under the exact contention that caused the lockout. Options: hold a dedicated short flock around the sentinel R-M-W, or accept+document.

2. (LOW) Wall-clock window. now=time.time() (:834,:842,:1107) -> NTP step-back makes recent stamps look future-dated; a step-back > _CRASHLOOP_WINDOW_S keeps the guard tripped until real time catches up. Fix: measure the window with time.monotonic()... BUT monotonic is not cross-process/-reboot persistable (the sentinel outlives the process). Real fix: store wall-clock stamps but clamp/guard against future-dated entries (drop t > now), or document the limitation.

3. (LOW) Window boundary closed-both-ends: predicate t >= cutoff (:836,:844) keeps an entry recorded at exactly T when now=T+_CRASHLOOP_WINDOW_S (window is [now-W, now], not (now-W, now]). Sub-second; change to t > cutoff if 'strictly older than W' is intended. Test gap: TestCrashLoopGuard.test_count_excludes_entries_outside_window only probes window+1.0, not window+0.0.

ACCEPTANCE: exact tests for each (atomic concurrent _record_restart under simulated contention; future-dated-stamp handling; boundary at window+0.0). Source: T2 nexus/rdr140-p4-code-review-2026-05-31.
close_reason: Groomed 2026-07-12: obsolete — RDR-140 crash-loop guard polish (monotonic clock/atomic counter); retired daemon-spawn path.

Add a local vision-language coprocessor for PDF formula (and general doc) extraction, served via MLX on Apple Silicon (Qwen2.5-VL). Slots into the existing pdf.mineru_server_url server-sidecar abstraction as pdf.formula_server_url (PID mgmt, health checks, httpx client already exist).

GATE (do NOT start build until met): first confirm the two cheap config fixes in #1047 — warm MinerU server + MINERU_DEVICE_MODE=mps — do NOT bring cold formula-heavy PDFs comfortably under the 180s/300s budget. Don't build a VLM pipeline to fix a config bug. Decision to scope in an RDR: replace UniMERNet vs. fallback-only vs. full doc-VLM; sidecar contract; accuracy eval on a math-paper set; resident-memory budget.

Refs: GitHub #1047 (formula hard-fail), #1046 (catalog starvation), #1048 (t2 daemon). T2: nexus/pdf-formula-extraction-mineru-vs-qwen-2026-05-31 [1927]. Surfaced during Augur-Oracle paper ingest 2026-05-31.

Decide: guard it with rename_lock for safety, or tombstone/delete it as dead code (per feedback_unused_not_useless: it's superseded, not dormant). Not a blocker for the RDR-138 Layer-1 PR.

title: Flaky: test_run_t2_daemon_writes_lifecycle_log_to_config_dir — stop breadcrumb not flushed before daemon exit (CI-only)
description:
tests/daemon/test_t2_daemon_observability.py::TestDaemonLogging::test_run_t2_daemon_writes_lifecycle_log_to_config_dir is flaky on CI (failed on develop run 26596473784 @ accd3663, both Python 3.12 + 3.13). Passes 20/20 locally.

Failure: after SIGTERM + proc.wait(timeout=15) + a 5s poll loop, the t2_daemon.log contains only up through 't2_daemon_started' — 't2_daemon_stop_requested' was never written. assert at test_t2_daemon_observability.py:121.

Root cause (confirmed structure, hypothesised mechanism):
- 'nx daemon t2 start' runs run_t2_daemon IN-PROCESS (foreground; commands/daemon.py:545, 'the T2 daemon IS this Python process'), so SIGTERM correctly targets the daemon — NOT a wrong-process race.
- The SIGTERM handler logs t2_daemon_stop_requested via structlog -> rotating file handler. Under CI load the process appears to exit before the handler flushes that line to disk within the 5s poll window. (proc.wait returned, so the process is gone; the breadcrumb just never hit the file.)

NOT introduced by RDR-137 follow-up work (epic nexus-43qgm): the only diff between the prior green-on-this-test run 598590c3 and the failing accd3663 was dropping a voyage token from test_silent_error_logging.py — cannot affect daemon lifecycle. My changes touched .catalog.db + pure helpers, never the T2 daemon serving memory.db.

Fix candidates:
1. In the daemon's SIGTERM/shutdown handler, flush the structlog file handler (logging.shutdown() or handler.flush()) AFTER writing t2_daemon_stop_requested and BEFORE the event loop exits, so the breadcrumb is durable.
2. OR widen the test's stop-poll window + add a fallback that accepts process-exit-without-breadcrumb only if a SIGKILL fallback was needed (currently the test asserts the graceful breadcrumb unconditionally).
Prefer (1) — the breadcrumb's durability is the actual feature nexus-n8sbw shipped; if it isn't flushed on a real graceful stop, the diagnostic value is lost in production too, not just in the test.

Related: nexus-azsqe (T2 daemon stop() bounded-guard around close()) touches the same shutdown path.

Evidence: CI run 26596473784 (develop @ accd3663).
close_reason: Fixed in commit f6962ba3 (develop). run_until_signal now calls a new logging_setup.flush_logging() immediately after writing t2_daemon_stop_requested and BEFORE stop() (which can stall on a hung close). Under CI load the daemon could exit after logging the breadcrumb but before the RotatingFileHandler flushed it, losing the diagnostic in production as well as flaking test_run_t2_daemon_writes_lifecycle_log_to_config_dir. flush_logging() pushes every root handler's buffer to the OS so a peer reading the log sees the line. Tests: flush_logging flushes/​survives-raising-handler; run_until_signal writes-then-flushes in order. Fix candidate 1 from the bead (durability is the real feature, not just a test widen).

title: nx_answer routing — compare/extract plans pick retrieval skeleton that doesn't hydrate content
description:
## Symptom

`nx_answer` returns a "STATUS: UNABLE TO ANSWER — source material not provided" envelope on certain analytical queries, with the body explaining that the `extract` step received `inputs: [""]` (empty string list). The `generate` step correctly refuses to fabricate, but the failure is upstream — the planner picked a plan whose retrieval step did not actually retrieve content.

## Repro (observed 2026-05-28 during Pyramid SFC paper mining)

**Same scope** (`knowledge__dt-papers__voyage-context-3__v1`), **different questions** — some succeed, others fail with the empty-inputs envelope:

| Question shape | Result |
|---|---|
| "What is the exact equation form of the pyramid Morton index in Knapp 2026 §3? (Eq numbers)" | ✓ Succeeds — returns equation numbers + verbatim text |
| "State Holke 2018 PhD Theorem 3.5 and explain its dependency for pyramid SFC construction" | ✓ Succeeds — returns theorem statement + dependency analysis |
| "What is the forest-level contract from p4est (Burstedde+Wilcox+Ghattas 2011)?" | ✓ Succeeds — returns Partition/Balance/Ghost summary |
| **"In Knapp 2026 §3, what is the geometric definition of pyramid types 6 and 7?"** | ✗ Fails — `inputs: [""]` envelope |
| **"Compare Burstedde+Holke 2016 vs Knapp 2026: what does Knapp REUSE unchanged? what does it ADD?"** | ✗ Fails — `inputs: [""]` envelope |

Both failing queries are answerable from the SAME corpus — verified by issuing `search(structured=true) → store_get_many(structured=true)` directly afterward, which returned the verbatim text needed (e.g., "we place two pyramidal elements within the cube, where one is a 180-degree rotation of the other …" for §3 types 6/7).

## Hypothesis

The planner matches a different plan for "geometric definition" / "cross-paper compare" questions than for "what does theorem X say" / "what is the contract" questions. The failing plan likely has an `extract → generate` skeleton with an upstream retrieval step that:

- Returns chunk IDs without hydrating their content (a `$step1.ids` reference rather than `$step1.contents`), OR
- Has a `where=` filter narrow enough that no chunks match, OR
- Calls `search` with a query string derived from the natural-language input in a way that doesn't match the §3 prose token distribution (e.g., asking for "geometric definition" when the chunks use "we place pyramidal elements" framing)

The succeeding queries probably match plans that issue a broader `search`/`query` call AND consume `$stepN.contents`.

## Workaround

Direct `search(structured=true) → store_get_many(structured=true)` works in 2 hops. The corpus is fully populated (162 chunks for Knapp 2026 at tumbler `1.12.7`).

## Diagnostic suggestions

1. **`plan_match` probe**: try `plan_match(intent="compare two papers extract delta", dimensions={"verb": "compare"})` to surface the matched plan and inspect its retrieval-step contract. Does the retrieval step actually call `search` / `query`, or does it consume `$stepN.contents` from an assumed prior step?

2. **`plan_search` audit**: `plan_search(query="compare papers extract structured fields", limit=5)` to inventory the candidate plans. If a plan with a `extract → generate` skeleton (no actual retrieval) is being matched, it should either be:
   - Deprecated and removed
   - Have its retrieval-step hydration contract added (e.g., always issue a `search` if `$stepN.contents` is empty)
   - Have its dimension tags tightened so it only matches when a prior step's contents are guaranteed populated

3. **Empty-inputs guard at runtime**: the `generate` step correctly refused on empty inputs, but the `extract` step accepted `inputs: [""]` and passed an empty payload to `generate`. A runtime check that fails fast at the operator boundary (`extract` returns "no inputs to extract from") with a clearer error than "UNABLE TO ANSWER" would help debugging.

## Source incident

2026-05-28 during Luciferase Pyramid SFC RDR research. The paper-mining subagent finished the dossier via the workaround. Full diagnostic in T1 scratch entry `c5826c7d-5627-45d6-8ea4-ff17c9f3f905` (Luciferase session `692cc09d-6626-4139-ab41-29a0f9c31a6a`). The successful queries from the same session are evidence that the corpus is well-indexed — this is a routing-layer issue, not a missing-data problem.

## Acceptance

- Repro of one failing query above clarifies whether it's plan-selection or step-hydration
- Either the offending plan(s) are fixed/deprecated OR a clearer runtime error replaces the misleading "UNABLE TO ANSWER" envelope on empty inputs
- Same scope, same query, post-fix: returns answer or surfaces a more diagnosable error
acceptance_criteria: Failing repro queries either succeed post-fix or return a clear plan-selection / empty-inputs diagnostic instead of the misleading UNABLE TO ANSWER envelope
notes: Cross-reference: T1 scratch c5826c7d holds full diagnostic. Workaround: direct search + store_get_many. Filed from Luciferase session.

Not wrong, not actioned: this bead self-reported as low/informational/accepted-risk at filing time, or is deferred refinement of an already-shipped fix, and has aged untouched. Against a backlog this deep an un-actioned bead has negative value — it dilutes the ones that matter. Roster + method: T2 nexus/triage-p3-p4-open-beads-2026-08-11 [22227].
