title: nx doctor: add MinerU import check (post-mineru-default-on-promotion)
description:
After nexus-2fyb made mineru a default dep, a corrupt install (missing mineru wheel) is silent until the user runs nx index pdf on a formula PDF. nx doctor should fail loudly at health-check time with a clear reinstall hint.

Fix: add a doctor check that does:
  try:
      from mineru.cli.common import do_parse  # noqa: F401
      assert do_parse is not None
  except Exception as e:
      report 'MinerU is required but not importable: {e}; reinstall conexus'

Surfaced during PR #509 audit.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed. doctor.py:755 has _run_check_mineru doing 'from mineru.cli.common import do_parse'; inline comment cites 'nexus-2fyb code-review R3-3'.

title: reinstall-tool.sh: shell/Python injection via  path interpolation
description:
scripts/reinstall-tool.sh inline python3 heredoc reads:
  text = open('').read()

$RECEIPT = $(uv tool dir)/conexus/uv-receipt.toml. If uv tool dir ever returns a path containing a single quote (HOME=/home/o'malley), the heredoc produces broken Python. Adversarial HOME control becomes Python injection.

Realistic risk is low (uv tool dir is well-behaved), but the fix is a clean one-liner: pass via env var.

  EXTRAS=$(RECEIPT_PATH="$RECEIPT" python3 -c "
  import os, re
  text = open(os.environ['RECEIPT_PATH']).read()
  ...
  ")

Surfaced during PR #509 audit.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed. scripts/reinstall-tool.sh now uses NEXUS_RECEIPT_PATH env-var pattern instead of shell-interpolated heredoc; comment at line 21-25 cites the fix.

title: pdf_extractor: missing pdf_path validation in extract()
description:
extract() at pdf_extractor.py:173-176 validates the extractor enum but not pdf_path. Failure modes:
- Directory: pymupdf.open(pdf_path) raises FileDataError with opaque message
- Dangling symlink: FileNotFoundError from inside pymupdf, internal library paths leaked through exception message
- Non-PDF file: extraction fails late with confusing errors

The streaming pipeline (pipeline_stages.py:86-88) calls ext.extract() without prior existence checks. An indexing job over a directory tree with a broken symlink fails non-actionably.

Fix: add at top of extract() before extractor dispatch:
  if not pdf_path.is_file():
      raise FileNotFoundError(f'PDF not found or not a file: {pdf_path}')

Pre-existing, surfaced during PR #509 audit.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed. pdf_extractor.py:260 has 'if not pdf_path.is_file(): raise FileNotFoundError(...)' — exact bead recommendation.

title: pdf_extractor: convert _progress() print() calls to structlog (library-code violation)
description:
src/nexus/pdf_extractor.py defines _progress(msg) as print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True) and uses it from library functions (_extract_with_docling, _extract_with_mineru, extract). CLAUDE.md rule explicitly forbids print() in library code; structured logging only.

Tests that capture stderr will be brittle. CLI-mode duplication: commands/index.py already uses click.echo for user-visible progress, so these _progress calls are doubled.

Fix: convert each _progress() call to _log.info(event=..., path=..., **fields). For interactive progress (page-by-page MinerU output), add a single click.echo at the CLI layer that subscribes to the structlog stream.

Pre-existing. Surfaced during PR #509 audit.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed by nexus-2fyb PR #509 follow-ups. _progress at pdf_extractor.py:83 emits structlog (_log.info('pdf_extractor_progress', ...)); the optional stderr print is gated on NEXUS_PDF_PROGRESS_QUIET.

title: pdf_extractor: dead formula_count parameter in _extract_with_mineru
description:
_extract_with_mineru accepts formula_count: int = 0 parameter (line ~400) but never uses it. _mineru_build_result recomputes formula_count from content_list and pdf_info. The parameter exists only to satisfy callers passing the probe's count.

Two failure modes:
1. Dead-code drift: future maintainer might 'fix' the parameter usage in a way that conflicts with _mineru_build_result's authoritative count.
2. content_list-empty fallback: if MinerU returns a response without content_list (handled at line 572 in current code) AND pdf_info is empty, formula_count gets recomputed to 0. has_formulas (doc_indexer.py:924) becomes False even for confirmed math PDFs.

Either: use the passed value as a floor in _mineru_build_result, or remove the parameter and document explicitly.

Pre-existing, surfaced during PR #509 audit.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Silently fixed. _extract_with_mineru passes formula_count as formula_count_floor (line 610); _mineru_build_result uses max(display_count + inline_count, formula_count_floor) at line 933.

title: nx doctor: skip taxonomy__* collections in pipeline-version check
description: The taxonomy__centroids collection (and any future taxonomy__* collection) is not produced by the indexing pipeline — it's a BERTopic c-TF-IDF aggregate over existing chunk embeddings. PIPELINE_VERSION semantics (voyage-code-3 + CCE prefixes + RDR-028 language registry) do not apply. Today nx doctor reports 'no version stamp (index with --force to stamp)' for taxonomy__centroids, which is misleading: --force on nx index repo will not stamp it because no code path stamps taxonomy collections. Fix: skip collection names starting with 'taxonomy__' in src/nexus/health.py pipeline-version loop.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-103 OpenQ: operator UX for migration upgrade message (per-collection vs summary + --quiet)
description:
RDR-103 Open Question (non-blocking). RDR file: `docs/rdr/rdr-103-catalog-collection-name-authority.md` § Open Questions, Q2.

# Question

Phase 4 emits one stderr line per migrated collection: `Upgraded legacy collection X to Y.`. Fine for ~10 collections; potentially noisy for operators with hundreds (the current state for the project, ~hundreds of legacy collections).

Decide:
- Keep per-collection lines? Adds a one-line summary at the end?
- Add a `--quiet` flag to `nx index` that suppresses the per-collection chatter and emits only the count?

# Resolution path

Defer to Phase 4 implementer. Decision is local; if the implementer ships a `--quiet` flag (or its equivalent), they can close this bead in the same commit. Otherwise, leave open as a doc-day-2 follow-up to be closed by an operator who actually finds the per-collection lines noisy.

# Acceptance

- A decision recorded (in commit message or Phase 4 bead notes).
- This bead closed with a one-line rationale.

# Dependencies

Tracks Phase 4 (`nexus-yqnr.6`) but does not block it.
close_reason: Resolved: kept per-collection upgrade message; the migration loop is bounded to 3 messages per nx index repo invocation (one per content_type), so the noise concern doesn't materialize. PR #493 merged to develop. Sandbox shakedown validated all 10 scenarios green.

title: RDR-101 Phase 6 follow-up: migrate-fallback per-doc flock thrashing + dry-run aggregation
description:
Two related UX/perf issues surfaced by prophylactic review pass #2 (2026-05-03).

(1) PERF: migrate_fallback_cmd loops per-document, each iteration acquires + releases the catalog flock via update_document_collection. For a 1000-doc fallback collection that's 1000 acquire/release cycles. fcntl is microseconds but SQLite commit dominates; 1000 commits is ~1-2s. Single-batched commit + a shared flock would cut this to one acquire / one commit.

(2) UX: migrate-fallback dry-run prints one (tumbler -> target) line per document. With 1000 docs going to 50 target collections, the operator sees 1000 lines and has to mentally count to verify the 50 is what they expect. A header summary 'N tumblers map to M unique targets' would make the proposal scannable.

Resolution paths:
1. Add a Catalog.update_documents_collection_batch(pairs: list[(tumbler, new_coll)]) that takes the lock once and writes events + projections + JSONL inside a single transaction.
2. In migrate-fallback dry-run, group by target and print 'target: <count> docs' per target.
3. Both can land in the same bead; the batch update is reusable for any future per-doc rewrite verb.

Priority P3 (perf optimization + UX polish).
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-101 Phase 6 follow-up: TOCTOU validation before flock in catalog writers
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review pass #2 (2026-05-03, concurrency F2).

register_collection, supersede_collection, and update_document_collection all read state (existing row, target row, etc.) BEFORE acquiring _acquire_lock. A concurrent writer between the validation and the lock acquisition can change the state, leading to a lost-update window.

Concretely:
- register_collection: get_collection(name) at line ~1518 runs unlocked, then short-circuit; benign because INSERT OR REPLACE converges.
- supersede_collection: three validations at line 1721-1747; concurrent supersede of the same old_name leaves both events in the log; replay deterministically wins by line order; in-process projection takes whichever lock-holder writes last. No corruption (INSERT OR REPLACE).
- update_document_collection: SELECT ... FROM documents at line 1644-1660 unlocked; ditto.

Failure mode: two operators racing produce a benign last-write-wins. No data corruption. The doctor's replay-equality and --collections-drift gates surface any divergence.

Resolution paths:
1. Re-validate inside the locked block (correctness over the race window).
2. Accept since these are operator-typo guards, not concurrency safeguards. Document the snapshot semantics.

Priority P3 (lost-update window only; no corruption).
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-101 Phase 6 follow-up: _v0_collection_superseded deterministic ts fallback
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review pass #2 (2026-05-03, caller-callee agent).

The projector's _v0_collection_superseded handler reads superseded_at from the payload (Phase 6 added the field). When the field is empty (only possible for events that pre-date the field addition), it falls back to datetime.now(UTC).isoformat().

Concern: each replay of a pre-amendment event produces a different superseded_at. Replay-equality drifts.

Mitigation: in production today, no pre-amendment events exist (Phase 6 hasn't shipped) so this fallback is unreachable. After Phase 6 ships, every event will carry the field. The fallback is dead code in practice.

Defensive fix paths (file under follow-up because not currently triggered):
1. Change Projector dispatch to pass the full Event (with .ts) instead of just .payload. Touches every handler. Most invasive but cleanest.
2. Special-case: have the projector recover the Event.ts via a thread-local set by apply(). Less invasive, more brittle.
3. Document that pre-amendment supersede events are unreachable post-merge and accept the residual risk.

Priority P3 (defensive, not currently triggered).
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-101 Phase 5 follow-up: _PRUNE_DEPRECATED_KEYS missing corpus/store_type/git_meta
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review of Phase 5 (2026-05-03).

src/nexus/commands/catalog.py:5811 has _PRUNE_DEPRECATED_KEYS = frozenset({source_path, git_branch, git_commit_hash, git_project_name, git_remote_url}). Phase 5c dropped corpus/store_type/git_meta from ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL but did NOT add them to this prune set.

Existing T3 collections from before Phase 5c retain those three keys until manually re-indexed. The 'nx catalog prune-deprecated-keys' verb is the operator's migration tool; leaving these keys out means it doesn't fully clean pre-5c shapes.

Not dangerous today (Chroma cap is 32 keys, current canonical shape is ~25), but contradicts the verb's stated goal.

Resolution: add 'corpus', 'store_type', 'git_meta' to _PRUNE_DEPRECATED_KEYS. One-line fix plus a regression test seeding a chunk with these keys and asserting they are stripped after prune.

Priority P3 (incomplete migration tool, not a runtime bug).
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-101 follow-up: legacy_grandfathered regex coupling without schema version
description:
Surfaced by prophylactic review of Phase 6 (2026-05-03, substantive critic).

The 'collections' projection's legacy_grandfathered flag is computed at projection time by evaluating is_conformant_collection_name(name) — a regex in nexus.corpus. The schema does NOT carry the regex version.

If the regex is ever extended (e.g. to allow voyage-context-3-lite, or a new content type 'papers'), replaying the existing event log produces different legacy_grandfathered values vs the live projection. This violates the deterministic-projection contract: same log, two replays, two states.

Resolution paths:
1. Store legacy_grandfathered explicitly in CollectionCreatedPayload (computed at write time, frozen on event). Replay reproduces the original value regardless of regex changes. Requires payload schema bump + projector dispatch update.
2. Store a 'conformance_regex_version' integer in the projection schema; the regex bumps it on changes. Operators run a re-classification pass after regex extensions.
3. Document explicitly that legacy_grandfathered is intentionally re-derived and any regex change requires a migration sweep.

Priority P3. Active code is correct; this is forward-compat hygiene.
close_reason: Closed

title: Re-baseline abstract-themes plan integration tests post-RDR-101 Phase 5
description:
## Why

`tests/test_abstract_themes_plan_integration.py::TestAbstractThemesPlanIntegration` was skipped for the v4.22.0 release. The 10 parametrized fixtures hard-code `dominant_themes` lists that were a snapshot of the Grossberg + Delos corpora taken before RDR-101 work landed. The 2026-05-03 orphan recovery (synthesize-log + t3-backfill-doc-id) added 896 documents to the catalog and shifted what content the abstract-themes plan summarizes, so the LLM legitimately uses different vocabulary now (e.g. "working memory" instead of "short-term memory").

Combined with a brittle threshold — `ceil(0.8 * 4) = 4`, requiring 100% match for 4-element fixtures — the substring assertion fails on themes that aren't actually missing from the corpus, just paraphrased.

## Verified failure mode (2026-05-03 release run)

```
[grossberg-memory] coverage gate failed: matched 3/4 dominant themes
(need >= 4 = ceil(0.8 * 4)). Missing: ['short-term'].
Summary excerpt: "The chunks cohere around Grossberg's research program
on working memory and its instantiation in laminar cortical circuits..."
```

The summary uses "working memory" 4 times; "short-term memory" 0 times. The corpus content is unchanged — the LLM picked a different (synonymous) phrasing. The fixture's hardcoded `("memory", "short-term", "working", "recall")` list is the stale piece.

Same shape across all 4 failing fixtures: `grossberg-memory`, `grossberg-speech`, `grossberg-reward-conditioning`, `delos-authorization`.

## Why we're not fixing now

- Corpus is mid-RDR-101-Phase-5 transition. Re-baselining now would just need re-baselining again post-Phase-5 when the schema removal lands.
- Each fixture costs ~5 minutes of LLM time. Running a stale assertion against a mutating corpus is high-cost / zero-signal.

## Acceptance

When RDR-101 Phase 5 lands and the catalog identity model stabilizes:

1. Re-run each of the 10 fixture questions against the post-Phase-5 corpus, capture the LLM summary, extract a fresh `dominant_themes` list (5-7 themes per fixture, biased toward shorter substrings the LLM is likely to reach for).
2. Replace the brittle `ceil(0.8 * n)` threshold with `floor(0.8 * n)`, or a small absolute floor (`max(1, n - 1)`), so single-vocabulary-drift doesn't trip the gate.
3. Remove the `@pytest.mark.skip` decorator on `test_abstract_themes_plan_per_fixture`.
4. Re-run the full integration suite; this test class should be green.

## References

- v4.22.0 release run — 4/10 fixtures failed before skip applied.
- RDR-101 Phase 5 closure (gated on `nexus-o6aa.11` Phase 5a → `nexus-o6aa.12` Phase 5b → `nexus-o6aa.13` Phase 5c).
- `tests/test_abstract_themes_plan_integration.py:358` — class with the stale fixtures.
close_reason: superseded by tests/test_abstract_themes_plan_integration.py refactor: hardcoded dominant_themes parameters dropped in favor of corpus-grounded coverage gate (top-K BERTopic labels via _corpus_labels_ranked); fixture data moved to bench/queries/abstract-themes.yml as evaluation harness. The original re-baselining ask is moot now that the test no longer pins on author-curated theme vocabulary.

title: nx catalog: collapse synonym verbs + fold diagnostics into doctor
description:
## Why

The `nx catalog` group has 40 subverbs. The bead `nexus-x783` (Rotoroot) targets <15 — a 25-subverb reduction. RDR-103-scope identity work and write-path collapse will get most of the way there, but a meaningful chunk is **mechanical cleanup with no schema or identity implications**.

This bead is that mechanical pass: collapse near-synonyms, fold diagnostic verbs into `nx catalog doctor` as flags or subcommands, rename for consistency. No breaking semantic changes — every operation remains reachable, just under fewer entrypoints.

Doing this **before** Rotoroot has two payoffs:
1. Surfaces which subverbs have actual users (search history, telemetry, scripts) before Rotoroot tries to delete them wholesale — collapsing alias-style verbs makes the breakage visible early.
2. The remaining subverb shape is stabler ground for the architectural reshape; less bikeshedding about "do we need both X and Y" during the bigger refactor.

## Scope (concrete reductions)

### A. Synonym collapse (−2 subverbs)

- `link-generate` and `generate-links` do the same thing (run all link generators over the catalog). Pick one canonical name (`generate-links` — verb-noun matches `nx catalog link` and `unlink`), make the other an alias that emits a deprecation warning for one release, then delete.
- `links-for-file` is `links` with a `--file` filter. Promote `--file` to first-class flag on `links`, deprecate `links-for-file`.

### B. Diagnostic fold (−4 subverbs)

`coverage`, `stats`, `orphans`, `audit-membership` are all read-only diagnostic queries that overlap with `doctor`. Convert each into a `doctor` flag:

- `nx catalog doctor --coverage` (replaces `coverage`)
- `nx catalog doctor --stats` (replaces `stats`)
- `nx catalog doctor --orphans` (replaces `orphans`)
- `nx catalog doctor --audit-membership` (replaces `audit-membership`)
- Existing `--t3-doc-id-coverage`, `--replay-equality` already follow this pattern.

`session-summary` stays separate — it's a recently-modified-files report, not a catalog-health probe; different audience, different output shape.

### C. Cleanup verb consolidation (−1 subverb)

- `dedupe-owners` is a one-time-ish maintenance verb. It can fold into `doctor --fix-owners` or stay if the team prefers explicit surface for destructive verbs. Mark and revisit during Rotoroot if it survives.

## Acceptance

- `nx catalog --help` lists 6 fewer subverbs (40 → ~34).
- All deprecated entrypoints emit a deprecation warning naming the new path.
- Behavior parity verified: `pytest tests/test_catalog_*` plus `release-sandbox.sh shakedown` (steps 5 + 9 + 10) all still pass.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` updated.
- Deprecated entrypoints scheduled for removal in the next-major release (note in CHANGELOG).

## Out of scope

- The 5 RDR-101 transitional verbs (separate bead, depends on Phase 5b).
- Identity unification, write-path collapse, top-level reorg (Rotoroot — `nexus-x783` / RDR-103).
- `taxonomy` (17 subverbs) and `collection` (11 subverbs) — same approach applies but separate beads to keep PRs reviewable.

## References

- Bead `nexus-x783` — Rotoroot, the architectural superset.
- Companion bead — "Delete RDR-101 transitional verbs after Phase 5 ships" (the −5 cleanup that runs in parallel).
notes: Scope A (link-generate alias collapse) shipped in PR #564. Scope B (fold diagnostic verbs into nx doctor) deferred — requires user-facing deprecation cycle and design review. Reopen via separate bead if/when Scope B is prioritised.
close_reason: Closed

title: Indexer progress: surface cumulative chunks + per-stage indicator
description:
Real-data finding 2026-05-02: nx index repo --force progress bar shows '33/691 files · 0 chunks · no samples yet · pending'. The chunk counter and ETA bootstrap only after the first ~10 files complete; long single files (e.g. catalog.py at 4900 LOC) sit at the same 'now=…' slot for tens of seconds with no phase signal.

Wanted:
1. Live cumulative chunks count alongside files: '33/691 files · 1,247 chunks'.
2. Per-stage indicator on slow files: 'now=catalog.py [embedding 8/12 batches]' or similar.
3. Optional: warn count if catalog_hook_register_failed structlog warnings have fired this run (currently log-only).

Out of scope:
- The catalog-hook silent-failure path itself (closed by PR #484).
- Per-stage timing breakdown (nexus-7niu already does this when --stage-timers is on).

All three were left stranded as in_progress after their PRs landed.

title: Phase 4 follow-up: aspect_extractor._source_content_from_t3 doc_id-keyed lookup + queue schema
description:
Sub-task spun out of nexus-dcym (RDR-101 Phase 4). The deprecated _source_content_from_t3 helper at aspect_extractor.py:760-795 reassembles a source document's text from T3 chunks via where={'source_path': source_path}. The aspect_worker batch path at aspect_worker.py:238 still calls it.

Audit notes: aspect_extractor.py:_source_content_from_t3 is deprecated (RDR-096 P1.2) and slated for removal in RDR-096 Phase 5. The aspect_worker batch path uses it as a transitional shim until extract_aspects_batch widens its return type to ExtractFail — see TODO at aspect_worker.py:227.

Migration approach (two paths):
1. Cleanest: complete the RDR-096 Phase 5 work that retires _source_content_from_t3 in favor of read_source. Drops this site without migration.
2. Tactical: switch the where filter to {'doc_id': doc_id} inside _source_content_from_t3. Caller (aspect_worker._process_batch) must pass doc_id — which requires adding a doc_id field to AspectExtractionQueue.QueueRow (src/nexus/db/t2/aspect_extraction_queue.py:111) and threading doc_id through enqueue/dequeue.

Recommend path 1 (chained on RDR-096 Phase 5) unless that work slips. Path 2 is the fallback if the prune verb (nexus-o6aa.10.3) lands before RDR-096 Phase 5 retires this shim.

Was logged on PR #469's commit message as out-of-scope. Refs the audit at docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-reader-audit.md Category B.5.
close_reason: Closed by PR #478 (queue schema + hook signature + 9 fire sites). Folds with nexus-buv0 implementation; nexus-buv0's audit (PR #475) closed earlier as the design record.

title: Phase 4 follow-up: _run_index_frecency_only doc_id-keyed lookup
description:
Sub-task spun out of nexus-dcym (RDR-101 Phase 4). The frecency update at indexer.py:573 (_run_index_frecency_only) iterates a frecency_map: dict[Path, score] and calls col.get(where={'source_path': str(file)}, ...) per file. PR-A migrated the other indexer-family sites by threading the existing _doc_id_resolver closure through; this site has no resolver in scope (the function is a CLI entry path that runs after main indexing, with no catalog hook fired during its execution).

Migration approach: add a catalog lookup inside the function. Read Catalog.by_file_path(owner, str(file)) per file in frecency_map (owner derived from repo via the catalog hook's owner-name convention), keep the resolved doc_id, and use where={'doc_id': doc_id} when available. Fall back to source_path when the catalog has no entry yet — preserves existing behavior.

Test: stash-revert verification on a synthetic frecency run that asserts the where filter is doc_id-keyed when a catalog entry exists.

Related: nexus-dcym (incremental-sync where-filter migration, in flight via PRs #469 + #470). Was logged on PR #469's commit message as out-of-scope. Refs the audit at docs/migration/rdr-101-phase4-reader-audit.md Category B.1.
close_reason: Closed by PR #479. _build_frecency_doc_id_map resolves catalog doc_id per file; chunk lookup keys on doc_id when available, source_path otherwise. WITH-TEETH tests lock both branches.

title: Phase 4: exporter fire_store_chains consumer audit — migrate source_paths= to doc_ids=
description:
Sub-task of nexus-o6aa.10 (Phase 4). The exporter's import path (src/nexus/exporter.py:391, 411) calls fire_store_chains(source_paths=...). Every chain consumer needs to be audited and migrated to consume doc_ids instead.

Step 1: enumerate chain consumers. Start at src/nexus/mcp_infra.py (fire_store_chains and fire_post_document_hooks definitions); follow the chain registration sites; produce a list of every consumer.

Step 2: per consumer, decide:
- If the consumer uses source_path purely as an ID for catalog lookup → migrate to doc_id (reads the catalog by doc_id directly).
- If the consumer needs the file path on disk → resolve doc_id → file_path via the catalog at consume time.
- If the consumer cannot be migrated cheaply → flag for keep-source_path-permanently consideration (would block the prune verb on that key).

Step 3: change fire_store_chains signature to accept doc_ids= alongside (or instead of) source_paths=. Migrate exporter call sites in tandem.

description:

title: fix(metadata-schema): taxonomy keys (topic_id, label, doc_count) stripped on import; .nxexp round-trip lossy
description:
Discovered alongside nexus-o6aa.9.15 (the document=None import crash). Once that fix landed and taxonomy__centroids imports cleanly, the imported records show their metadata stripped to {'content_type': 'prose'} — the canonical taxonomy enrichment fields (topic_id, label, doc_count, and any other taxonomy-specific keys) are dropped.

Root cause:
- src/nexus/metadata_schema.py::_normalize_for_write applies the canonical whitelist (RDR-040 / nexus-40t) before T3 writes.
- The whitelist does not include taxonomy-specific keys.
- nx store import calls into the same write path; export preserved the keys; import strips them.

Functional impact: low. RDR-089 centroids are queried by vector similarity, not by their metadata fields. The taxonomy infrastructure that produces them likely re-derives topic_id/label/doc_count from the original data sources rather than reading from T3 metadata. So the data is recoverable.

But: .nxexp claims to be a faithful portable backup. Today it isn't for taxonomy collections. An operator who exports + restores would silently lose the enrichment.

Two ways to fix:
1. Whitelist taxonomy keys in metadata_schema.py for collections matching taxonomy__*. Cleanest if the keys are stable.
2. Per-collection whitelist override mechanism so other special collections (RDR-089's are not the only special ones) can extend without touching the canonical schema.

Option 1 is enough for now. Option 2 is the future-proof shape if more special collections appear.

Test:
- Hand-craft a .nxexp for a taxonomy__centroids collection with topic_id/label/doc_count fields.
- nx store import.
- Read back via t3._client.get_collection(...).get(ids=[...], include=['metadatas']).
- Assert metadata round-trips: topic_id/label/doc_count present and equal.

Out of scope:
- Reviewing the canonical schema for OTHER stripped keys. RDR-040 was deliberately conservative; the centroid case is the trigger to revisit, not the only suspected gap.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy keys (topic_id, label, doc_count) round-trip through .nxexp export → import. Regression test in tests/test_exporter.py asserts the round-trip. Existing canonical-schema tests still pass.
close_reason: merged via #464; canonical-schema bypass for taxonomy__* collections in T3 _write_batch + update_chunks; restores .nxexp round-trip fidelity

title: claude_dispatch loses subprocess output on timeout (no log persisted)
description:
When nx_plan_audit / nx_enrich_beads / any other operator that calls `claude_dispatch` hits its timeout, the captured stdout/stderr is discarded and SIGKILL'd. The OperatorTimeoutError raised at `src/nexus/operators/dispatch.py:117-139` carries only the duration; no partial output, no stderr, no clue which step blew the budget. Forensic gap.

Reproduction: run any nx_enrich_beads call that exceeds its timeout (default 300s, hitting 600s also reproduces). Notice the resulting failure surfaces only `OperatorTimeoutError: claude -p timed out after Ns`. No file is written; `--no-session-persistence` means `~/.claude/projects/` doesn't capture it either.

Fix sketch: in the `asyncio.TimeoutError` branch, drain the (partial) stdout + stderr buffers via `proc.stdout.read()`/`proc.stderr.read()` BEFORE the killpg, write to a temp log path under `/tmp/nexus-claude-dispatch-{pid}-{ts}.log`, and include the path in the OperatorTimeoutError message. Worst case: no output captured, log path mentions empty file.

Surfaced from RDR-101 acceptance flow on 2026-04-30 when nx_enrich_beads timed out at 300s with zero forensic data; user had to ask whether logs existed and the answer was no.
close_reason: Closed

title: bib enrich: 1-token source titles can over-accept on common-word coincidence
description:
v4.21.2 shakeout (knowledge__delos): the asymmetric title-validation heuristic shipped in 4.21.2 fixed the 4.21.1 false-negative class (Pbeegees, Hex Bloom) but introduced a new false-positive shape: when the source title is exactly 1 substantive token AND that token is a common word, the heuristic accepts an unrelated paper that happens to share the token.

Live failure: source title 'Zanzibar' (Google's authorization paper, 2019) accepted 'Impact of Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy and Insecticide-Treated Nets on Malaria Burden in Zanzibar' (2007 medical study). Both have 'zanzibar' as a substantive token; the asymmetric rule (single-token match where one side has ≤2 tokens) accepts. The fundamental issue: token-set comparison has no signal to distinguish 'rare distinctive identifier' (Pbeegees, hex-bloom) from 'common place-name' (Zanzibar).

Net trade in v4.21.2 vs 4.21.1 on knowledge__delos:
  - 4.21.1: 3 correct enrichments, 0 false positives
  - 4.21.2: 6 correct enrichments, 1 false positive (Zanzibar)
Net +5 -1 = +4. Worth shipping but the false-positive shape needs a fix.

Mitigation paths to evaluate:
1. Year-sanity cross-check. If catalog row has indexed_at recent (post-2020) and OpenAlex returns publication_year < 2010, treat as suspicious. Cheap, single-comparison.
2. Content-keyword cross-check. Extract 3-5 distinctive tokens from the chunk body (skip titles in the body, take from abstract/intro), compute overlap against returned title. Catches 'Zanzibar' (auth/permission keywords absent from malaria abstract). Adds one extra OpenAlex content-fetch or local NLP pass.
3. IDF-weighted Jaccard. Weight tokens by inverse document frequency from a corpus (could approximate via OpenAlex's per-token search counts). 'Zanzibar' has higher IDF than 'pbeegees' which is roughly the inverse of what we want, so this isn't quite right.
4. DOI-must-match-source-content guard. If the DOI lookup result has authors/year wildly inconsistent with anything findable in the source PDF body (author name match), reject. More work.

Recommended path: combine (1) year-sanity floor and (2) a single content-keyword overlap check. (1) is a one-line guard; (2) is one extra search/extract. Together they catch Zanzibar without breaking Pbeegees.

Acceptance: a paper with a single-token title (e.g., 'Zanzibar', 'Cassandra', 'Postgres') that has a wrong-paper citation-DOI hit OR a coincidental fuzzy-title hit gets rejected, while still accepting legitimate single-token-source matches like 'Pbeegees' / 'Hex Bloom'.
acceptance_criteria: A regression-test suite covers 3 single-token-source cases: (a) a legitimate match (Pbeegees-shape) accepts, (b) a year-mismatched coincidence (Zanzibar→2007 malaria-shape) rejects, (c) a content-mismatched coincidence (something where title shares a word but body topic differs) rejects.
notes: Filed from v4.21.2 live shakeout. Lower priority (P3) than yy1m because false positives at this rate are observable on inspection — the user spotted it immediately. The 4.21.2 fix is already net-positive enough to ship; this bead refines the next iteration.
close_reason: Closed

title: Smarter DOI selection: avoid reference-DOI false-positives in chunked PDF text
description:
nexus-sbzr ships 'first DOI in concatenated chunk text wins'. For papers whose Docling chunk-order puts the references section BEFORE the page-1 banner DOI, the regex grabs a citation DOI rather than the paper's own.

Live evidence on knowledge__delos (post-PR #394 + multi-chunk scan):
- aleph-bft.pdf: matched DOI 10.1145/1095810.1095817 (PBFT 1999), not aleph-bft's actual DOI. aleph-bft cites PBFT in its references.
- pBeeGees.pdf: matched 10.1145/3243734.3243812 (a different ACM paper, likely cited).
- lightweight-smr.pdf: full-text scan shows doi 10.4230/LIPICS.OPODIS.2015.7 (correct LIPIcs OPODIS 2015) but the matched DOI was 10.1007/s11071-017-3906-2 (Nonlinear Dynamics journal, wrong field). Means a citation DOI appeared earlier in chunk order than the LIPICS one.

Heuristics that would help, ranked:
1. 'DOI:' / 'doi:' / 'http(s)://doi.org/' labels: prefer DOIs that appear directly after these labels (paper banners) over bare DOIs in body text (references).
2. Position bias: prefer DOIs in the first 20% or last 20% of body text (page 1 + back matter), de-prioritize middle (references).
3. Match ALL DOIs against OpenAlex, pick the one whose returned title best fuzzy-matches filename. Slow but correct.
4. Read PyMuPDF page-1 raw text bypassing Docling's chunking, look for DOI in the rendered first-page-banner area.

Lean: option 1 first (cheap, regex-only, no PDF re-parse). If still wrong-prone, add option 2 as fallback. Option 3 is heavyweight; option 4 needs PDF re-parse.

Definition of done:
- knowledge__delos paper's lightweight-smr resolves to OPODIS 2015 (correct)
- aleph-bft resolves to its actual DOI (~10.4230/LIPIcs.DISC.2021.4 or similar)
- pBeeGees resolves to its actual DOI
- Tests cover: DOI-with-label preferred over bare DOI, multiple DOIs in text returns label-preferred one, no labeled DOI returns first bare DOI (current behavior preserved as fallback)
notes: Surfaced 2026-04-30 right after PR #394 merge. The multi-chunk scan helped (7/15 via ID up from 2/15) but reference-DOI confusion remains for ~3-4 papers.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #396. Labeled DOI preference + arXiv-DOI form for OpenAlex lookup. 55 tests pass. Live: extract_doi correctly grabs paper-DOI over reference-DOI when labeled; remaining wrong-matches on delos are OpenAlex coverage gaps (lightweight-smr, etc.), not extraction bugs.

title: nx plan disable: soft-disable a plan row without deleting
description:
Follow-up to nexus-la28. The la28 PR (#345) shipped list/show/delete/reseed but explicitly deferred the ``disable`` subcommand because it requires a schema migration plus matcher filter.

## Problem

``nx plan delete`` is destructive. Operators sometimes want to take a plan out of rotation temporarily (debug a regression, A/B between two strategies, retire a plan without losing its run history) without deleting the row. There's no way to do that today.

## Scope

1. **T2 migration** — add ``disabled_at TEXT`` column to ``plans`` (nullable). Follow the established ``_add_plan_*`` pattern in ``src/nexus/db/migrations.py`` plus ``_migrate_plans_*_if_needed`` helper in ``src/nexus/db/t2/plan_library.py``.

2. **Matcher filter** — both ``plan_match`` lanes must skip ``disabled_at IS NOT NULL`` rows:
   - T1 cosine lane: filter at the ``PlanSessionCache`` populate / upsert path (so disabled rows never enter the cosine collection in the first place)
   - T2 FTS5 lane: add ``AND p.disabled_at IS NULL`` to the SELECT in ``PlanLibrary.search_plans``

3. **``nx plan disable <id> [--reason=...]``** — stamps ``disabled_at`` with current ISO timestamp; appends ``--reason`` to the ``tags`` column with a recognisable prefix (``disable-reason:<text>``) so operators can later see why.

4. **``nx plan enable <id>``** — clears ``disabled_at``. Undocumented helper if needed; alternatively, expose ``--enable`` flag on ``disable``.

5. **``nx plan list`` integration** — show a column or marker for disabled rows; ``--include-disabled`` flag toggles inclusion.

## Acceptance

- New plan with ``disabled_at`` set does not match via either ``plan_match`` lane
- ``nx plan disable <id>`` round-trips: list shows disabled marker, matcher skips, ``enable`` restores
- Existing rows have ``disabled_at = NULL`` post-migration

title: RDR-097 P1.1: hybrid-factual-lookup plan YAML
description:
RDR-097 §Phase 1 P1.1 — Create nx/plans/builtin/hybrid-factual-lookup.yml.

## RDR section
docs/rdr/rdr-097-hybrid-retrieval-plan-template.md §Phase 1, Prerequisite P1.1.

## Scope
Six-step plan shape: search → traverse → store_get_many[vector] → store_get_many[graph] → operator_rank → operator_generate. Parameterized by seed-or-question, depth, link-type purpose, and the two stream budgets (vector_budget_chunks default 6, graph_budget_chunks default 4 per RF-6 60/40 split).

## Conventions
- dimensions.verb: lookup (pinned per §Why pin verb:lookup; disambiguates from citation-traversal.yml verb:research via verb)
- dimensions.strategy: hybrid-factual-lookup (matcher key per RDR-091)
- Vector step: limit=40, threshold=2.0 (per RF-9, disable filter during over-fetch — references nexus-h3e2 for systemic fix)
- Traverse step: purpose=factual-evidence (depends on nexus-wp9s P1.3), depth=2 (BFS per Zhou §6.2)
- **Per-stream budgeting via two store_get_many calls, each with limit_per_source** (delivered by P1.0 / nexus-uwkw):
    - step3: `store_get_many(ids=$step1.ids, collections=$step1.collections, limit_per_source=$vector_budget_chunks)`
    - step4: `store_get_many(ids=$step2.ids, collections=$step2.collections, limit_per_source=$graph_budget_chunks)`
- operator_rank merge: criterion includes hybrid score formula in natural language (Option (a) from Gap 2 — Claude-prompted merge, not operator_merge_streams). Inputs are step3.contents + step4.contents combined.
- Reuse research-default.yml and citation-traversal.yml as structural references

## History
Earlier draft used a single store_get_many step with `ids: $step1.ids[:vector_budget_chunks]` Python-style slice expressions — the planning-chain audit caught that the runner's binding-substitution language only resolves whole-token `$var`/`$stepN.field` references; slice expressions would have passed through as literal bogus IDs. Corrected on 2026-04-28: two store_get_many calls with `limit_per_source` (delivered by nexus-uwkw P1.0).

- nx catalog setup seeds the new template without YAML errors (count = current+1, +2 with P1.2)

title: abstract-themes: filter section_type=references from search to keep groupby on substantive content
description:
Smoke run of the abstract-themes plan against docs__art-grossberg-papers (nexus-ldnp / RDR-098) produced 4 thematic groups; 3 were substantive content (LAMINART, Embedding Fields, What/Where/ART) and 1 was just bibliography ("References/Citations"). The reference-noise group consumed roughly 25% of the over-fetched chunks and one full per-group LLM call (operator_aggregate fires K calls — a wasted slot).

## Why this matters

- The reference group is a meta-group, not a theme. It's noise from BERTopic's perspective (citations cluster together regardless of subject area).
- For a fixed K=5 cap on top groups, losing one to bibliography means one fewer real theme surfaces.
- The cost of the wasted aggregate call is one ``claude -p`` per query (currently ~10s + tokens).

## Fix

Add ``where: section_type!=references`` to the search step in ``nx/plans/builtin/abstract-themes.yml``. Search MCP tool already supports the ``where`` arg (see ``mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__search``: ``"Metadata filter (KEY=VALUE, comma-separated). Ops: = >= <= > < !="``).

Implementation:
```yaml
- tool: search
  args:
    query: $intent
    limit: $limit
    corpus: $corpus
    threshold: 2.0
    where: section_type!=references
```

## Validation

Re-run the smoke fixture:
- Before: 4 groups, 1 of which is References/Citations
- After: 3-4 substantive groups, none bibliographic
- Compare per-aggregate token cost between runs

## Out of scope (future beads)

- Cross-collection generalization: the ``section_type`` field is populated by RDR-055 chunkers but not all corpora are RDR-055-clean. A safer pattern long-term is a ``content_classifier`` aspect that flags non-substantive chunks (TOC, references, headers, page footers). File separately if the simple ``where`` filter proves too brittle.
- Configurable filter per plan binding: callers may want references included for citation-tracing questions. Could expose as ``include_references: bool`` binding with default false.

## Found via

nexus-ldnp end-to-end smoke (commit 8213bdf on feature/nexus-ldnp-abstract-plan, output captured in /tmp/plan_smoke3.out — group 4 was bibliography spanning Carpenter & Grossberg, Fuzzy ARTMAP refs, etc., with no thematic content).
close_reason: Closed

title: Plan-runner search threshold default is hostile to abstract/broad queries
description:
Discovered while smoke-testing nexus-ldnp's abstract-themes plan: search step on a prose collection (docs__art-grossberg-papers, default threshold 0.65) drops 100% of candidates for broad-phrasing queries like "main themes in cognitive and neural mechanisms". The plan returns empty, the rest of the pipeline correctly produces a "no items" summary. Functionally correct, practically useless.

The fix in the plan template was to override threshold=2.0 (effectively no filter — cosine distance tops out at 2.0). But this raises a design question: every plan that does broad over-fetch will need the same override.

## Two nuances worth pinning before resolution

1. **Threshold semantics are confusing**: the `threshold` arg's docstring says "raw cosine distance, lower is stricter". But the threshold is applied to PRE-boost distance, while the result envelope reports POST-boost distance. So a threshold=0.95 with reported distances 0.85-0.90 would seem to keep them but doesn't (the raw distance is higher than the boosted one shows). The MCP tool docstring should explain this, and ideally the result envelope should expose the raw distance alongside the boosted one.

2. **Per-corpus default thresholds were tuned for narrow-target search** (find this specific entity), not broad-target retrieval (give me a sample of this topic area). A second threshold tier — `abstract_threshold` or `broad_threshold` — could be added to per-corpus config, with plan-step args opting in via a flag like `mode: broad` rather than every plan author overriding numeric thresholds.

## Acceptance

Plan authors writing abstract/community-summary plans should not need to know that threshold=2.0 disables filtering. Either:
- Add a plan-step `mode: broad` flag that maps to threshold=2.0 + clear documentation
- Or document the override pattern prominently in the plan-author docs and add a broad-threshold default to per-corpus config

## Found via

nexus-ldnp implementation. The abstract-themes plan currently has a hard-coded `threshold: 2.0` workaround with a comment explaining why; this should be replaced once the broader fix lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: CheapRAG-pattern abstract-question plan template via taxonomy community summaries
description:
RDR-097 follow-up — Proposal C from the 2026-04-28 RAG-papers research synthesis (T3 IDs 01d3943271e1e716 + 45040ed1bffe64d6).

## Background

The unified Graph-RAG framework paper (Zhou et al., VLDB 2025, knowledge__hybridrag tumbler 1.653.79) reports a key finding (L4): community-level summaries outperform raw chunk clusters for abstract/summary QA. Their CheapRAG configuration (community summaries + original chunks, map-reduce) achieves competitive accuracy at far lower cost than full GraphRAG.

nexus already has community structure via BERTopic taxonomy (RDR-070) — topic centroids per collection are structurally equivalent to GraphRAG community partitions. We can validate whether BERTopic communities substitute adequately for expensive LLM-generated community reports, at near-zero infrastructure cost.

## Scope (one phase, one branch, one PR)

- Add `abstract-question.yml` plan template in `nx/plans/builtin/`:
  - Step 1: `search` (over-fetch 40, low threshold)
  - Step 2: `operator_groupby` over result set, group by chunk taxonomy topic label
  - Step 3: `operator_summarize` per top-K topic groups (K=5; cap to bound LLM-call latency)
  - Step 4: `operator_aggregate` to merge partial summaries into coherent response
- Wire intent classifier in `_nx_answer_classify_plan` (`src/nexus/mcp/core.py`) to detect abstract intent — phrases like "summarize", "what are the main themes", "overview of", "what does X say about Y" — and dispatch the new template
- Validate on a populated taxonomy collection — knowledge__hybridrag has too few chunks for HDBSCAN. Use `knowledge__delos` (25+ topics) or `docs__art-grossberg-papers` (46 topics) instead
- Compare to flat `search` + `operator_generate` baseline on 10 abstract questions

## Why this is the easy one

- All operators already exist (`groupby`, `summarize`, `aggregate`)
- BERTopic taxonomy populated for 30+ collections (`nx taxonomy status` confirms)
- Plan template + intent classifier hook = the only new code
- No new dependencies, no model decisions

## Watch-items (not blockers — measure early)

1. **Per-group LLM cost**: `operator_summarize` per topic group means O(K) sequential LLM calls. Cap K at 5 (top groups by aggregate score). Parallelize if needed in a follow-up bead.
2. **Cross-collection abstract questions**: BERTopic taxonomy is per-collection. v1 scopes to single-collection abstract Q&A. Cross-collection version uses the projection layer (more complex) — file as follow-up.
3. **knowledge__hybridrag is unsuitable as test bed** — taxonomy discover skipped (too small/uniform). Pick a populated collection.

## Composition with other proposals

- Independent of RDR-097 (hybrid retrieval) — different question types (abstract vs. specific factual)
- Composes with the cross-encoder salient-sentence aspect (companion bead) — pre-filtered chunks would feed cleaner partial summaries
close_reason: Shipped via main — fc3ddf9e (feat plan template) + 0b92d371 (binding fix) + ebd2c77c (gate fixes) + 09defe40 (accept) + 691820f8 (close). RDR-098 already accepted+closed; bead status was stale.

title: Cross-encoder salient-sentence aspect for query-aware index-time relevance scoring
description:
RDR-097 follow-up — Proposal B from the 2026-04-28 RAG-papers research synthesis (T3 IDs 01d3943271e1e716 + 45040ed1bffe64d6), reframed.

## Background

SAGE (Wang et al., 2026, knowledge__hybridrag tumbler 1.653.77) selects query-relevant sentences from documents at indexing time using attention weights from a small local LLM. The original synthesis read the technique literally and proposed a 600MB local-LLM dependency, which crosses nexus's zero-config design line and would require runtime decisions (mlx-lm, llama-cpp-python, etc.) before implementation.

Reframing: SAGE's *output* is per-sentence query-relevance scores. nexus already has the infrastructure to produce that output without a local LLM:
- `src/nexus/scoring.py:16` uses `voyage-rerank-2.5` (cross-encoder) at query time
- The same model can score [seed_query, sentence] pairs at indexing time
- Local fallback: ONNX cross-encoder, e.g. `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` (~80MB, not 600MB) — folds into the existing voyage-cloud / ONNX-local pattern we use for embeddings

What we lose vs. SAGE's exact mechanism: differential attention (subtract a baseline-query attention to suppress boilerplate). That's SAGE's clever bit, but optional in v1; revisit only if measurements show boilerplate noise.

## Scope (one phase, one branch, one PR)

- Add new aspect extractor config `attention-guided-v1` alongside `scholarly-paper-v1` in `src/nexus/aspect_extractor.py`
- For each document at index time, split into sentences (use existing prose chunker logic), score each sentence against 3-5 generic seed queries via Voyage rerank-2.5 (cloud) or ONNX cross-encoder (local mode)
- Store top-30% sentences (by max score across seed queries) as new T2 aspect field `salient_sentences` in `DocumentAspects`
- In `search_cross_corpus`, for `knowledge__*` and `docs__*` chunks, apply +0.05 quality boost to chunks whose text overlaps with stored salient_sentences (token overlap at query time — zero new model calls)
- Gate behind a feature flag in `.nexus.yml`; off by default
- Test on `knowledge__hybridrag` (3 docs) — measure top-5 retrieval hit rate against held-out questions vs. baseline

## Why this is now lower-risk than the original synthesis suggested

- No new dependency class — reuses existing rerank infrastructure
- No local-LLM runtime decision needed
- Falls cleanly into voyage-cloud / ONNX-local pattern already established for embeddings
- Aspect extraction framework (RDR-089) is already plumbed end-to-end

## Open questions

- Seed-query selection: hand-curated per content_type? Auto-generated from doc title/topics?
- Sentence boundary detection: reuse `md_chunker.py` or use a sentence splitter library?
- Quality-boost weight (0.05) needs calibration — measure on a held-out question set before committing to the constant

## Non-goals

- Differential attention — file as v2 follow-up if boilerplate noise shows up in measurements
- Query-time SAGE-style scoring — explicitly rejected; query-time per-chunk model calls are not acceptable in the search path. This is index-time only.

Companion to RDR-097 (hybrid retrieval plan) but independent — that's a graph+vector composition; this is a cross-encoder relevance signal additive to either.
notes:
2026-05-10 escalated to RDR-109 ("Honest Local-Mode Naming and Cross-Encoder Salience"). Bundled with nexus-59vl because both fixes inject a mode-aware decision into a write path that pre-2026 was unconditionally cloud-shaped, hitting the same test-suite mode-default surface.

Phases under RDR-109:
- Phase 3: cross-encoder scoring substrate (cloud + ONNX dispatch).
- Phase 4: calibration (seed-query selection + quality-boost weight on a held-out QA set).
- Phase 5: aspect extractor + retrieval boost integration.

Bead remains open as the implementation tracker for Phases 3-5.
close_reason: Closed

title: nx doctor + console: surface aspect_extraction_queue depth + currently-processing row
description:
RDR-089 nexus-qeo8 introduced an async aspect-extraction worker (`src/nexus/aspect_worker.py`) with a daemon thread draining T2 `aspect_extraction_queue`. The queue table is fully populated and readable via SQL but has zero surface in observability tooling: `nx doctor` doesn't report it, the console UI doesn't show it, and there's no way to see "are there 200 documents pending extraction or 0?" without writing a SQL query.

This matters because:
- The async worker decouples ingest latency from extraction latency. Without queue visibility, a backlog grows silently.
- The synchronous fallback path (`nx enrich aspects`) emits to stdout, but the async path is invisible.
- After bulk ingest, users (and `bd ready`-style tooling) need a "is enrichment caught up?" signal before declaring a corpus ready.

Proposed:

1. **`nx doctor`**: add an `aspect_queue` health row reporting (a) total rows queued, (b) rows currently in `processing` state, (c) oldest enqueued_at, (d) any rows in `failed` state with their last error. Threshold to warn: configurable via `.nexus.yml` (e.g. queue_depth > 100, or oldest > 1h).

2. **Console UI**: add a small gauge to the home / health panel showing the same numbers, polled on the existing console refresh interval.

Implementation notes:
- Schema for `aspect_extraction_queue` lives in `src/nexus/db/migrations.py` (RDR-089 migration). Look at the columns to confirm the right SELECT.
- `health.py` route already exists in `src/nexus/console/routes/`; add the gauge there.
- Doctor lives in `src/nexus/commands/doctor.py`; follow the existing health-row pattern.

Acceptance:
- `nx doctor` shows queue depth and oldest-item age.
- `nx console` home panel shows a gauge that updates as the worker drains the queue.
- Both also reflect failure-state rows so a stuck worker is visible.

Companion to nexus-XXXX (console activity feed) but independent — this is a periodic gauge, that's an event stream.
close_reason: Doctor surface shipped; console gauge piece deferred to a follow-up bead per running PR scope discipline.

title: Console UI activity feed: include enrichment events (aspects/bib/taxonomy/index)
description:
The console UI Activity Stream (`src/nexus/console/routes/activity.py`) currently tails `documents.jsonl` + `links.jsonl` for catalog events only — registered documents, created links. Enrichment runs (`nx enrich aspects`, `nx enrich bib`, `nx taxonomy discover`, `nx index pdf`) emit rich structlog events that go to `~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log` (or stdout for foreground CLI) but never reach the UI.

Result: the only way to watch enrichment in flight is `tail -f ~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log` in a terminal — no live UI surface for what is otherwise the most interesting "what's happening right now" signal in the system.

Proposed: extend the activity feed source set to include enrichment progress events.

Two viable implementation paths:

1. **Persist enrichment events to JSONL** (consistent with current pattern). Add an `enrichment.jsonl` (or per-domain `aspects.jsonl`, `bib.jsonl`, `taxonomy.jsonl`) that the relevant code paths append to alongside their structlog calls. The activity route picks them up via the same deque-tail pattern already in `_read_recent_events()`.

2. **Tail mcp.log directly**, with a structlog-event parser that recognises known event names (`aspect_extracted`, `aspect_extract_skip`, `bib_enricher_*`, `taxonomy_discover_*`, etc.) and renders them as activity rows.

Path 1 is more disciplined (structured event schema, no log-tail fragility) but requires touching every emitter. Path 2 is faster to land but ties UI shape to log format.

Acceptance:
- Live activity feed in `nx console` shows aspect-extraction progress per document during `nx enrich aspects` runs.
- Same for `nx enrich bib`, `nx taxonomy discover`, `nx index pdf`.
- Existing catalog events remain.

Out of scope: SSE/WebSocket push (next-gen UI work). Polling-tail is fine for now; UI already polls.

title: nx catalog remediate-paths: re-resolve via meta.devonthink_uri when file_path is broken
description:
Companion to the x-devonthink-item:// scheme work — even if DT URI never becomes a first-class source_uri scheme, we already record `meta.devonthink_uri` on catalog entries that came from DEVONthink (see entry 1.653.79). When `nx catalog remediate-paths` walks an entry with a missing or stale file_path and the meta carries `devonthink_uri`, it should re-resolve via osascript instead of (or in addition to) basename matching against SOURCE_DIR.

Current behavior (`src/nexus/commands/catalog.py` remediate-paths):
- Walks SOURCE_DIR for basename matches
- Skips ambiguous entries
- For DT-managed entries, even when the DT app has the file at a known location, remediate has no way to reach it without scanning the entire `~/Library/Application Support/DEVONthink/.../Files.noindex` tree

Proposed change:
- Before basename scanning, check entry.meta for `devonthink_uri`
- If present, call osascript to resolve it to a path
- If the path exists, treat it as the resolved candidate (skip basename scan for this entry)
- Stretch: a new `--source dt` mode that walks the catalog for all entries with `devonthink_uri` and refreshes their file_path in one batch (no SOURCE_DIR argument needed)

Acceptance: re-running remediate-paths after DT moves a file restores the correct file_path without manual intervention. macOS-only — gate via sys.platform.
close_reason: PR #340 — x-devonthink-item URI scheme + DT-aware remediate-paths

title: Add x-devonthink-item URI scheme to catalog allow-list + aspect reader
description:
RDR-096 P3.1 introduced an allow-list for catalog source_uri schemes (file, chroma, https, nx-scratch) gated by `_normalize_source_uri()` in src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py. DEVONthink-managed PDFs have a stable identity URL of the form `x-devonthink-item://<UUID>` that resolves to the current filesystem path via AppleScript (osascript -> tell app id "DNtp"). Today these documents have to be cataloged with a `file://` URI of the path inside DT's database (`~/Library/Application Support/DEVONthink/...Files.noindex/...`); when DT relocates the file the URI breaks even though the underlying DT identity is unchanged.

Make x-devonthink-item:// a first-class source_uri scheme:

1. Add `x-devonthink-item` to `_KNOWN_URI_SCHEMES` in src/nexus/catalog/catalog.py (line ~226).
2. Write a reader in src/nexus/aspect_readers.py (or wherever the file/chroma/https readers live) that resolves a DT URI to a filesystem path via osascript and reads the bytes. The osascript snippet is:
     tell application id "DNtp"
       set theItem to get record with uuid "<UUID>"
       return path of theItem
     end tell
   Handle the missing-record case (returns "missing value") cleanly.
3. macOS-only — gate via sys.platform check, raise a clear error on other platforms ("DEVONthink integration is macOS-only").
4. Test with the existing entry 1.653.79 (`In-depth Analysis of Graph-based RAG in a Unified Framework`, UUID 8EDC855D-213F-40AD-A9CF-9543CC76476B, currently has `meta.devonthink_uri` set but `source_uri = file://...`).

Acceptance: `nx catalog register --source-uri x-devonthink-item://<UUID>` accepts the URI and downstream consumers (aspect extractor, /nx:query, etc.) can resolve it transparently.
close_reason: PR #340 — x-devonthink-item URI scheme + DT-aware remediate-paths

title: metadata schema cleanup: remove dead fields from ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL
description:
Per a comprehensive metadata audit (2026-04-26), nexus's T3 ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL has 31 keys (at Chroma's 32-key cap). Of those, several are written but never read by any consumer:

**Dead-weight fields in ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL (storage budget waste):**
- `category` — written by every CLI indexer ("code", "prose", "pdf"), but no reader uses it for filter, scoring, or display. `content_type` already covers the same routing.
- `corpus` — denormalized duplicate of the collection name. All routing in nexus is collection-prefix-based; no reader queries this field.
- `tags` — semantically inconsistent: CLI writes file extensions ("py", "md"), MCP writes semantic tags. Search doesn't filter on it.
- `source_agent`, `session_id` — MCP-only semantics, but written empty on every CLI chunk (millions of slots wasted).
- `store_type` — superseded by `content_type`.
- `chunk_text_hash` — computed and stored on every chunk; the only intended consumer (RDR-053 content-addressed link spans) does NOT read it from T3 metadata. Worth either retiring or wiring the consumer.
- `ttl_days`, `expires_at` — reserved for TTL-based expiry that doesn't currently fire on T3 chunks.

**Computed-then-dropped fields (wasted indexer work):**
- PDF: `pdf_subject`, `pdf_keywords`, `is_image_pdf`, `has_formulas`, `extraction_method`, `format`, `chunk_type`, `page_count`, `source_date`
- Code: `ast_chunked`, `programming_language`, `filename`, `file_extension`
- All: `indexed_at`, `bib_semantic_scholar_id`

These are written by indexers but `metadata_schema.normalize()` drops them (intentional — not in ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL). Each represents wasted compute. Some (`is_image_pdf`, `has_formulas`, `chunk_type`) are consumed pre-store for routing decisions; the others are pure cargo.

## Scope

1. **Remove ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL dead-weight** (`category`, `corpus`, `tags`, `store_type`, `source_agent`, `session_id` on CLI). Update normalize() to drop them. Migrate any read sites that survive.
2. **Stop computing dropped-by-normalize fields** in indexers (the 14 listed). Saves indexer work.
3. **Either wire `chunk_text_hash` consumers or remove it.** RDR-053 link spans are the intended use — verify they read it from T3 metadata vs computing on-demand.
4. **Resolve `ttl_days` / `expires_at`**: either implement T3-chunk TTL or remove from the allow-list.

## Constraint

Do NOT land on the RDR-089 branch (`feature/nexus-b9g1-rdr-089-aspect-extraction`). Cleanup is a separate concern from aspect extraction. Use a fresh `feature/<bead-id>-metadata-cleanup` branch.

## Outcome

Post-cleanup ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL drops from 31 → ~22 fields with ~10-key safety margin. Indexers stop computing values that go straight to the bit bucket. T3 metadata becomes coherent end-to-end: every stored field has at least one reader.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL trimmed to fields with at least one verified read site
- [ ] All indexers (code/prose/PDF/MCP) stop computing dropped fields
- [ ] chunk_text_hash either has a verified consumer or is removed
- [ ] ttl_days/expires_at story is resolved (implemented or removed)
- [ ] Audit re-run shows zero unused fields in ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL
- [ ] Tests pass; no regression in search/scoring/display
notes:
**Second audit-trust caveat (2026-04-26):** verified each 'unused' claim from the original audit against actual reads. Auditor was systematically wrong:

- `chunk_text_hash` — load-bearing chash (RDR-086). Read by catalog/catalog.py for span resolution, mcp/core.py per-result, db/t2/chash_index.py PK, collection_health/audit. **Keep.**
- `tags` — read by mcp_infra.py:270 for link-context auto-linker; plans/match.py, plans/seed_loader.py, plans/session_cache.py; commands/store.py:186,194,265; commands/memory.py:208; commands/scratch.py:84,97. **Heavy use across T1/T2/T3.**
- `session_id` — read by db/t1.py:222,262,266,450 for T1 scratch session scoping (where filter); session.py:285,303 lifecycle; mcp/core.py:157 chromadb owned-session marker. **Core to T1 isolation.**
- `source_agent` — read by search_engine.py:599-600 for agent-aware ranking. **Has at least one consumer.**
- `corpus` — read by plans/scope.py, plans/runner.py:485,509,531,551, mcp/core.py:3121, catalog/catalog.py:1130,1234. **Plan/catalog routing depends on it.**
- `store_type` — read by db/t3.py:65 in _infer_content_type(). **One consumer.**
- `category` — verified ZERO non-test reads. **Plausibly removable at T3 chunk level.**

**Layer-confusion lesson:** the same field names appear in T3 chunk metadata, T2 entries (memory/scratch/plans), T1 scratch, and catalog JSONL — with different consumer sets per layer. Field-name grep alone is insufficient. Any deletion candidate must be verified against:
1. T3 chunk-metadata reads (`coll.get(where={field: ...})`, `chunk.metadata.get('field')`)
2. T2 store-row reads
3. T1 scratch reads
4. Catalog JSONL reads
5. Display formatters

**Re-scoped deletion candidates (T3 chunk metadata only):**
- `category`: zero T3 reads found. Verify T1/T2 + display before removing.
- `indexed_at` (already silently dropped by normalize): clean up writers since the schema doesn't store it.
- The 14 'computed-then-dropped' fields (pdf_subject, pdf_keywords, is_image_pdf, has_formulas, extraction_method, format, chunk_type, page_count, source_date, ast_chunked, programming_language, filename, file_extension, bib_semantic_scholar_id): real cleanup. They're computed by indexers and dropped by normalize() because they're not in ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL. Verify each is consumed pre-store (chunk_type / has_formulas / is_image_pdf are routing decisions) before removing.

Original 7-field deletion list shrinks to ~1-2 fields plus the indexer-side dead-write cleanup. Net storage savings minimal; the real win is removing wasted indexer compute.
close_reason: Closed

title: RDR-095 post-merge: nx index pdf smoke + 100-doc perf assumption
description:
Two RDR-095 acceptance items not run during implementation; surfaced at closure handoff per gate-accept-pause discipline.

ITEM 1: Manual nx index pdf smoke (RDR-095 § Minimum Viable Validation #3).
  - Run nx index pdf on a small corpus (e.g. ~/Downloads/delos-papers/ → knowledge__delos-test).
  - Verify post-ingest: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM topic_assignments WHERE source_collection LIKE 'knowledge__delos-test%'.
  - Verify post-ingest: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM chash_index WHERE physical_collection LIKE 'knowledge__delos-test%'.
  - Both counts should match the prior pre-RDR-095 baseline. Captures real-world wiring of fire_post_store_batch_hooks across the pipeline-stages.py upload path (not exercised by EphemeralClient unit tests).

ITEM 2: Critical Assumption #2 verification (RDR-095 § Critical Assumptions, second bullet).
  - The RDR explicitly marks 'Per-document hook overhead in batch fire path is negligible next to extractor work' as Unverified, with method 'confirm by smoke-test against a 100-document fixture corpus once Phase 2 lands'.
  - The symmetric-fire follow-up (commit 4a912f9) added a per-doc fire_post_store_hooks loop to every CLI ingest site, so the assumption is now more relevant: with no single-doc consumers registered, each loop iteration is a Python function call over an empty hook list (microseconds), but worth measuring once.
  - Run: time nx index repo on a synthetic 100-document fixture; compare wall-clock to the same run with the per-doc loop short-circuited (e.g. via env var or a temporary 'if not _post_store_hooks: skip' guard).
  - Acceptance: per-doc overhead < 1% of extractor wall-clock. If it exceeds that, file a perf bead and add a fast-path skip when the chain is empty.

Both items are post-merge verification, not pre-merge blockers. The framework is correct by construction (verified by unit tests + drift guard); these items confirm real-world performance and pipeline coverage.

When done, update RDR-095 § Critical Assumptions to mark assumption #2 Verified, and amend Status line for Test Plan scenario #5 (nx index repo behavioral parity).

title: RDR-095 follow-up: per-sub-step failure capture in batch hooks
description:
RDR-095 §Failure Modes acknowledges that batch hooks have no per-sub-step failure granularity at the framework level: a hook that commits sub-step A and raises in sub-step B writes one hook_failures row capturing the doc_id list and exception, but does not capture which sub-step succeeded. The framework deliberately does not introduce per-sub-step capture in RDR-095 because it would couple the framework to specific consumer shapes.

A future RDR (or this bead, if scope is small enough) should evaluate whether to add a record_partial_progress(stage_label, doc_ids_completed) helper that hook authors can call between sub-steps. title: Add nx doctor --check-mcp-logs (RDR-094 Phase H follow-up)
description:
Phase H investigation (nexus-3f95) confirmed Claude Code maintains a per-MCP-server log surface at ~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs/<project-slug>/mcp-logs-<server>/ that records the silent-death signatures ("STDIO connection dropped after Ns uptime" + "Closing transport (stdio transport error: ...)"). RDR-094 §Day 2 Operations now documents the three-log correlation. This bead wires the correlation into nx doctor.

## Implementation

Add a new doctor check ~check-mcp-logs to src/nexus/commands/doctor.py:

1. Resolve the cache directory for the current project. Slug derivation: replace '/' with '-' in cwd, prefix with '-Users-...' style. Example: cwd=/Users/hal.hildebrand/git/nexus -> -Users-hal-hildebrand-git-nexus.
2. Locate ~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs/<slug>/mcp-logs-plugin-nx-nexus/ (or the configured server name). Skip cleanly with a 'not present on this platform' note when the path doesn't exist (Linux installs).
3. Walk the most-recent N JSONL files (default 10), grep for:
     - "STDIO connection dropped after Ns uptime"
     - "Closing transport (stdio transport error"
     - "Tool '...' failed after Ns: MCP error"
4. For each silent-death candidate, cross-reference timestamps against ~/.config/nexus/logs/mcp.log + ~/.config/nexus/logs/watchdog.log to highlight gaps (last 30 minutes around the drop).
5. Surface results as warnings/info entries in the doctor report.

- tests/test_doctor.py (cover the slug derivation + grep logic with a tmp_path cache layout)

title: Phase A: Fix Spike C observer historical-replay bug
description:
## Summary
The Spike C observer (scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_mid_session_observer.py) reads mcp.log from byte 0 at startup, replaying every historical entry as if it occurred during the observation window. This produces +0.0s timestamps for historical entries and causes false restart_cycle classifications.

## Fix
In spike_rdr094_mid_session_observer.py, seek to end of mcp.log on observer start OR filter each parsed event by comparing its timestamp against wallclock_start (the time the observer began).

## Files
- scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_mid_session_observer.py (observer implementation)
- scripts/spikes/spike_rdr094_lifecycle.py (reference for spike structure)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Observer seeks to EOF at startup so no historical entries are replayed
- [ ] OR each event is filtered: event.timestamp < wallclock_start => skip
- [ ] Unit test: seed a mcp.log with entries older than observer start time; assert observer ignores them and produces no +0.0s events
- [ ] No false restart_cycle classifications from pre-existing log content

## Context
- RDR §Prerequisites §Spike C known follow-up (line ~964 in RDR)
- The fix is isolated to the spike script; does not touch production code
- Single bead, no blockers

Epic: nexus-4v5l
notes: Per nx_enrich_beads (post-audit GO_WITH_FIXES): recommend filter-by-timestamp over seek-to-EOF for the observer fix (more robust against log rotation). New unit test (e.g. tests/test_spike_rdr094_observer.py) is deterministic — no Claude or MCP needed. Reference: Spike A evidence (T2 094-spike-a-lifecycle id=976), Spike C evidence (T2 094-spike-c-mid-session id=977).
close_reason: RDR-094 Phase A shipped via PR #302 (squash-merged to main). Observer now filters mcp.log entries with structlog timestamp predating observer start; 11 deterministic unit tests pin the parse + filter helpers.

title: Generalise _OPERATOR_MAX_INPUTS truncation metadata across operator family
description:
Surfaced by /nx:rdr-gate 093 substantive-critic as Significant finding S-1. RDR-093 fixes the issue for operator_groupby only: when _OPERATOR_MAX_INPUTS = 100 fires in the ids-branch auto-hydration, the return envelope now carries {truncated: true, original_count: N, kept_count: 100} metadata so plan authors can observe the cap.

The problem is wider. The runner at src/nexus/plans/runner.py:640-647 logs a structlog warning and silently truncates for EVERY operator (extract, rank, compare, summarize, generate, filter, check, verify, and now groupby + aggregate). Only groupby's output envelope currently surfaces the truncation. Plan authors calling any other operator with >100 hydrated inputs lose data silently with no programmatic signal.

Fix shape: move the truncation-metadata surface from per-operator output contract to a runner-level envelope. When the runner truncates in _hydrate_operator_args, it attaches a '_truncation_note' sentinel to the operator's returned dict (or adds a top-level '_meta' block). Plan authors inspect '._truncation_note' or similar. This avoids forcing every operator to define and honour truncation metadata in its own schema.

Alternative shape: raise a structured warning through the MCP response path (if MCP supports side-channel warnings) so the caller gets the signal without a change to the output shape.

Either way, do this AFTER RDR-093 lands so the pattern is consistent with what groupby already does, not a competing design.
acceptance_criteria: All operators in _OPERATOR_RESOLVED_TOOLS surface truncation in a uniform way when _OPERATOR_MAX_INPUTS fires. At least one way for a plan author to programmatically detect truncation without consulting structlog. Tests cover three operators (extract, filter, groupby) exercising the cap with assertions on the truncation metadata.
notes: Filed from RDR-093 gate S-1 follow-up. Cross-link: nexus_rdr/093-gate-latest (id=966) documents the significant finding and in-place scoped fix.
close_reason: Generalised RDR-093 S-1 truncation metadata from operator_groupby-only to all operators. Removed the if-guard in _hydrate_operator_args; mechanism (private _truncation_metadata marker → pop → post-merge) unchanged. Tests cover filter, extract, groupby per acceptance criteria; inverted test_truncation_metadata_scoped_to_groupby_only → test_truncation_metadata_attaches_to_all_operators. 339 passed. Commit 29dffbc on feature/nexus-g8l9-rojs-rdr-093-spikes.

title: RDR-091 Phase 2d: docs updates (plan-authoring-guide + plan-centric-retrieval)
description:
Phase 2d of RDR-091 (parent epic: nexus-gr9n; parent bead: nexus-zs1d).
RDR: docs/rdr/rdr-091-scope-aware-plan-matching.md §Implementation Plan → Phase 2d.

## Goal

Document the now-live scope-aware matching so plan authors can
exploit it (RDR-084 promotion discipline depends on this being
discoverable). Docs updated AFTER code stabilizes in Phases 2a-2c;
deliberately last so we document the real behaviour, not the intent.

## Files touched

- `docs/plan-authoring-guide.md` — describe the new `scope_tags`
  field, inference rules, normalization contract.
- `docs/plan-centric-retrieval.md` — reflect the scope-aware
  matcher behaviour and the zero-candidate fallback.

## Execution steps (from RDR §Phase 2d)

18. **plan-authoring-guide.md** (step 18): add a section on
    `scope_tags`. Cover:
    - What it is: comma-separated normalized collection-name prefixes
      stored on the `plans` row.
    - When it's inferred vs explicit: inference walks retrieval steps
      unioning `corpus` + `collection`; explicit `scope_tags` arg to
      `plan_save` overrides inference.
    - Normalization contract (from RDR §Proposed Solution):
      hash-suffix strip at save time, glob strip at match time,
      bare family prefix preserved.
    - Interaction with grown plans (RDR §Phase 2a interaction note):
      `nx_answer` ad-hoc save path infers from the actual corpus used
      in the run; different scopes produce different grown plans, which
      is correct.
    - Multi-corpus bridging plans: intersect semantics — any tag overlap
      with caller scope is enough to match.
    - Authoring guidance: prefer explicit `scope_tags` for plans with
      `\$var` corpus placeholders (inference would drop them); otherwise
      rely on inference.
19. **plan-centric-retrieval.md** (step 19): update the matcher-behaviour
    section. Cover:
    - scope_preference is now live (remove any language describing it as
      forward-compatibility-only; mirror the matcher.py docstring
      cleanup from Phase 2b).
    - Scope-conflict filter behaviour: plans with non-empty scope_tags
      that don't prefix-match are filtered out before scoring.
    - Zero-candidate fallback: all candidates conflict → nx_answer
      routes through `_nx_answer_plan_miss` (inline planner fires).
      Same path as \"no plan matched at all\".
    - Score formula:
      `final_score = base_confidence * (1 + scope_fit_weight * scope_fit)`
      where `scope_fit ∈ {0, 1}`.
    - Specificity tie-break: on exact score tie, fewer entries in
      `scope_tags` wins.

## Prerequisites

- nexus-gr9n.3 (Phase 2c) merged with the final `scope_fit_weight`
  value picked. Docs quote the live value and the tuned behaviour,
  not an intended one.

## Constraints / watch-fors

- Docs lag code, not lead it. If any detail changed during 2a–2c
  (e.g. a normalization edge case got simpler), the docs must match
  what's actually in the code, not what the RDR predicted.
- The RDR itself is a permanent record — don't retrofit the RDR's
  proposal section to match the final implementation. Use
  `implementation_notes:` frontmatter (updated in Phase 2c) or a
  new revision-history entry for \"actually-shipped\" discrepancies.
- Keep tone consistent with existing guide/retrieval docs. No
  RDR-quoting in prose; these are usage guides, not RDR summaries.

## Parallelization

Single-developer documentation task.

## Definition of done

- `docs/plan-authoring-guide.md` has a `scope_tags` section with
  inference + explicit paths, normalization contract, and grown-plan
  interaction documented.
- `docs/plan-centric-retrieval.md` reflects scope-aware matcher,
  conflict filter, zero-candidate fallback, score formula, and
  tie-break.
- No stale references to \"accepted for forward compatibility\" or
  \"unused at this version\" anywhere in docs.
- Link from both docs back to RDR-091 for the decision record.

## Execution reminders

- Use `mcp__plugin_sn_serena__search_for_pattern` to find any
  other doc references to `scope_preference` that might need
  updating beyond these two files.
- After docs land, close RDR-091 via `/nx:rdr-close` passing the
  post-mortem rationale (picked weight, Arcaneum probe result,
  test counts).

Context: RDR-091 §Phase 2d, RDR-084 promotion discipline (depends on
authors seeing scope_tags work), matcher.py:77-80 cleanup done in 2b.
