title: nx collection health: chunk_count=0 for most collections (catalog drift vs T3 reality)
description:
Surfaced during the live 4.8.0 shakeout 2026-04-18.

## Symptom

`nx collection health --format=json` against the production cloud reports `chunk_count: 0` for 129 / 143 collections, even though `nx collection list` shows the same collections with real chunk counts from T3 (e.g. `code__ART-8c2e74c0` = 63077 chunks in `list` but 0 in `health`).

Concretely: on the 4.8.0 install against the user's production tenant:

    nx collection list   # code__ART-8c2e74c0  63077 chunks
    nx collection health --format=json \
      | python3 -c 'import json, sys; d = json.load(sys.stdin); r = [x for x in d["collections"] if x["name"] == "code__ART-8c2e74c0"][0]; print(r["chunk_count"])'
    # 0

## Root cause

`src/nexus/collection_health.py:101` sums `catalog.documents.chunk_count`:

    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(chunk_count), 0), MAX(indexed_at)
    FROM catalog_documents
    WHERE physical_collection = ?

The catalog's `chunk_count` column drifts from the T3 ChromaDB reality whenever:
- A collection was created before `chunk_count` was added to the catalog schema
- A collection was populated via a path that doesn't update `catalog.documents.chunk_count` (direct `store_put`, cloud-side operations, bulk imports)
- `nx catalog setup` has not been run on a tenant that existed before the catalog was introduced

The `list` command uses T3's live `col.count()`, so the two numbers are independent sources of truth.

## Not a 4.8.0 regression

`nx collection health` was introduced in PR #194 (nexus-yi4b.3.4) as part of v4.7.0. The catalog-sourced `chunk_count` has been the behavior since then. The 2026-04-18 v4.8.0 release (nexus-c2op, commit bb29245) added the `chash_index_coverage` column but did not change how `chunk_count` is sourced.

## Proposed fix

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

1. **Always query T3 for `chunk_count`**, not the catalog. A single `col.count()` per collection is cheap (one round-trip per collection). Keeps the `health` report's numbers in sync with `list` by construction.

2. **Backfill the catalog's `chunk_count`** via an opt-in `nx catalog sync-chunk-counts` command that iterates every registered collection, calls `col.count()`, and updates `catalog.documents.chunk_count`. Leaves the `health` query as a fast SQL SUM but requires periodic re-sync.

Option 1 is the correct one for a user-facing health report — the operator wants ground truth, not a cache. Option 2 is complementary for downstream queries that want fast local counts (`nx catalog`, analytic joins).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `nx collection health` chunk_count equals `nx collection list` chunk_count for every collection
- [ ] Test that seeds a cloud collection with chunks via direct T3 write (bypassing catalog registration) and verifies health reports the T3 count

## Related

- PR #194 introduced `nx collection health` (v4.7.0)
- bb29245 added chash_index coverage column (v4.8.0)
- Surfaced 2026-04-18 during live shakeout of 4.8.0
close_reason: Fixed in PR #214. nx collection health chunk_count now comes from T3 coll.count() instead of catalog SUM — same source as nx collection list, so the two surfaces cannot disagree. Live verification: 144/144 production collections now match (was 14/143 before). 4 new regression tests pin precedence, drift case, backward-compat, and default-catalog-stats surface removal.

title: vatx: per-stage intra-file timing decomposition (--debug-timing)
description:
Follow-up split from nexus-vatx Gap 4 after Gaps 1–3 + 4a shipped (PRs #207, #208, #210 on 2026-04-19).

## Why

vatx Gap 4a shipped an aggregate end-of-run retry-time summary but per-file elapsed is still opaque: the 89–95 s spike from the 2026-04-17 Delos re-index cannot be decomposed into chunking vs embed vs upload vs retry wall time. Operators still cannot tell 'voyage was slow' from 'chromadb was slow' from 'chunking choked on a huge file.'

## Proposed shape

- Add a StageTimers dataclass threaded through IndexContext so per-file timing attributes to each stage.
- Instrument the call sites inside code_indexer.py (chunking + embed + upsert), prose_indexer.py (markdown chunking + CCE embed + upsert), doc_indexer.py (PDF pipeline; batch_index_markdowns), and pipeline_stages.py (concurrent uploader).
- Wall-clock retry wait is already captured by nexus.retry.get_retry_stats(); attribute it to whichever stage was in flight by snapshotting the counter delta around each call.
- Gate the output behind nx index --debug-timing or a structured end-of-run summary.
- Silent by default so normal runs stay tidy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] StageTimers dataclass added; threaded into IndexContext
- [ ] Timer plumbing at 4 call sites above
- [ ] nx index --debug-timing flag emits end-of-run per-stage breakdown to stderr
- [ ] Tests: unit test for StageTimers accumulation + integration test that the four timer buckets each see >0 s on a mocked run

## Related

- nexus-vatx (parent; closed 2026-04-19)
- PR #207 (Gap 1 + 3), #208 (Gap 2), #210 (Gap 4a) — shipped precursors
notes: Scaffold (#216) + extension (#217) cover the three per-file sites (code, prose, PDF) that the nx index repo loop exercises — the 99 percent path for the Delos re-index use case that filed Gap 4b. Two sites remain un-instrumented and require separate design: (1) doc_indexer.batch_index_markdowns is batch-shaped, not per-file; (2) pipeline_stages.uploader_loop is streaming with decoupled threads via a SQLite buffer. Close 7niu when those two are addressed or split to a new bead.
close_reason: Stranded in_progress sweep 2026-05-08. nexus-7niu shipped via PRs #216 + #217 (StageTimers scaffold + prose/PDF instrumentation; src/nexus/stage_timers.py + nx index --debug-timing). nexus-6xqk shipped via PR #485 (cumulative chunks + skipped count in tqdm postfix at src/nexus/commands/index.py:327). nexus-nppx shipped via commit 12b5285b (scripts/spikes/spike_rdr090_5q.py + spike_rdr090_5q_results.jsonl + spike_rdr090_5q_summary.json + bench/queries/spike_5q.yaml; spike over-delivered on Path C). All three were left stranded as in_progress after their PRs landed.

title: Add source_mtime column to catalog documents for stale-source detection
description: RDR-087 Phase 3.4 skipped stale_source_ratio because catalog.documents has no source_mtime column. Adding one at index time unblocks the column. Scope: T2 migration + catalog indexer plumbing + nx collection health backfill. Low priority — current pick: option (c) in 3.4 design = column reports '—' placeholder.
notes: RDR-154 P2 (nexus-2zv75) investigated wiring source_mtime into stale_source_ratio and found a DB-ONLY computation STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: catalog_documents.source_mtime is the file mtime captured AT INDEX TIME (indexer.py stat before read), and indexed_at=now() is written after, so source_mtime <= indexed_at ALWAYS -> a 'modified since indexing' ratio from stored columns is identically zero. Caught by substantive-critic 2026-06-16 (Critical) before merge; the P2 wiring was reverted. To deliver real staleness detection, choose: (a) live filesystem stat at report time comparing current st_mtime vs stored indexed_at (local-mode only; service host may not mount files), or (b) redefine the metric to age-based staleness (indexed_at older than N days) computable DB-only but a different semantic, or (c) a file-watcher event path that refreshes source_mtime to current while leaving indexed_at frozen. Stays OPEN; collection_health.py stale_source_ratio remains the placeholder with this analysis in its module docstring.
close_reason: PR #203: source_mtime column added to catalog.documents with fresh-schema + ALTER-on-open migration, threaded through code/prose/PDF index paths. 11 new tests, 298 neighbor tests clean. Downstream wiring (real stale_source_ratio float) deferred to follow-up — O(N) fs walk out of scope.

title: RDR-087 Phase 1 follow-up: end-to-end engine+CLI silent-zero integration test
description:
## Context

Phase 1.3 code review (code-review-expert) and Phase 1.4 validation
(test-validator) both identified a structural coverage gap: every
silent-zero CLI test in \`tests/test_search_cmd.py\` stubs
\`search_cross_corpus\` with a side_effect that injects a
pre-fabricated \`SearchDiagnostics\` struct into \`diagnostics_out\`.

No test exercises the real engine path from CLI invocation through
ChromaDB threshold filtering to stderr emission. The integration
between the real \`_search_collection\` loop's diagnostics population
and the CLI's \`_maybe_emit_silent_zero_note\` consumer is untested.

## Why this was deferred

Closing the gap requires either a live ChromaDB or a more elaborate
integration fixture (an EphemeralClient with seeded documents at
known distances, plus CLI invocation through CliRunner). Phase 1.1
+ 1.2 unit coverage is comprehensive — all branches of
worst_offender(), all opt-out paths, all edge cases of the
diagnostics struct. The gap is specifically the *wiring* through
the real engine, not the logic inside each layer.

Phase 1 unblocks the user-facing workaround for nexus-rc45; the
end-to-end integration test is polish, not a regression risk.

## Proposed implementation

Add \`tests/test_search_cmd.py::test_silent_zero_end_to_end\`:

  1. Build an EphemeralClient T3 with a small collection whose raw
     distances are known (use \`_voyage_client\` attribute injection
     to force \`apply_thresholds=True\` with MiniLM distances).
  2. Invoke \`nx search\` via CliRunner against that fixture with a
     query that produces non-zero raw candidates all above the
     threshold.
  3. Assert exactly one stderr line matching the RDR-087 format,
     referencing the actual collection name and the actual
     min-dropped-distance from the fixture.

  ~30-40 lines. No live API keys required.

## Acceptance

- New test lets the real \`search_cross_corpus\` populate diagnostics
  (no side_effect stub of the engine).
- Real CLI invocation produces stderr line matching the RDR-087 format.
- Doesn't introduce flakiness — run 3x consecutively without variance.

## Related

- RDR-087 (line 222-246 spec)
- nexus-yi4b.1.1 / nexus-yi4b.1.2 (Phase 1 implementation)
- PR #177 (Phase 1.2 branch where follow-up would land)
notes: Filed 2026-04-17 as a follow-up from Phase 1.3 review + Phase 1.4 validation. Not blocking Phase 2.
close_reason: PR #204: real EphemeralClient+ONNX EF end-to-end silent-zero test. 3-run stability verified (byte-identical stderr). Full test_search_cmd.py green (57 tests).

title: strategic-planner + other planning agents override nx_plan_audit/nx_enrich_beads timeouts below the raised defaults
description:
## Summary

The `strategic-planner` agent (and likely other planning/enrichment
agents) passes explicit short timeouts (180s, 300s) to
`nx_plan_audit` and `nx_enrich_beads` at invocation time. These
overrides bypass the raised defaults from v4.5.3
(`nx_plan_audit` = 600s, `nx_enrich_beads` = 300s), causing the
same timeout-false-positive class that v4.5.3 was supposed to
eliminate.

Observed 2026-04-17 on RDR-087 accept. Same failure mode the ART
instance reported earlier in the week.

## Reproduces

Planning chain during `/nx:rdr-accept <id>` on a multi-phase RDR:

1. Strategic-planner drafts a plan (e.g., 27 beads over 5 phases).
2. Planner calls `mcp__plugin_nx_nexus__nx_plan_audit(plan_json=...,
   timeout=180)`.
3. Audit times out at 180s. Subagent retries at `timeout=300`.
4. 300s retry also commonly times out on large plans that touch
   many files.

Evidence from RDR-087 subagent transcript
(`/private/tmp/claude-501/.../tasks/acb72f13377597f54.output`):

```
16:19:52Z  nx_plan_audit(timeout=180)  -> timed out after 180.0s
16:23:54Z  nx_plan_audit(timeout=300)  -> PASS_WITH_NOTES (~5min run)
```

## Root cause

The timeouts are chosen by the agent LLM at invocation time, not
hardcoded in the agent `.md` file (verified: no `timeout|180|300|600`
matches in `nx/agents/strategic-planner.md`). So the issue is either:

- **Model prior**: the planner has seen prior conversations with
  lower timeouts baked in and defaults to those when not explicitly
  told otherwise.
- **MCP tool schema default is stale**: if the schema the agent
  sees still shows `default=120` or `default=180`, the agent picks
  a timeout near that. The runtime default is 600s (raised in
  v4.5.3, commit 3ece9f9), but the schema the MCP client exposes
  may still surface the old default.

## Proposed fix options

1. **Enforce a floor in the MCP tool body** — `nx_plan_audit` and
   `nx_enrich_beads` clamp the caller's timeout to `max(caller,
   300)`. Fires a `structlog.warning` when the caller's requested
   timeout is below the floor. One-line change in each tool.
2. **Update the strategic-planner agent prompt** to state
   explicitly: "Do NOT pass an explicit `timeout` kwarg to
   `nx_plan_audit` or `nx_enrich_beads` — the raised defaults
   (600s / 300s) are calibrated for multi-phase analytical work."
3. **Verify the MCP tool schema exposed to agents shows the raised
   default**. Current Python signature:
   `timeout: float = 600.0` — but the FastMCP layer may be
   caching the old schema. A `uv sync && reinstall-tool.sh` may
   refresh it.

Options 1 and 2 are compositional: option 1 prevents the bug even
if agents relapse; option 2 makes agents explicit about the right
default.

## Affected surfaces

- `/nx:rdr-accept` planning chain (Step 8c invokes nx_plan_audit
  via strategic-planner)
- `/nx:create-plan` manual re-runs of the planning chain
- Any future agent that calls `nx_plan_audit` or `nx_enrich_beads`
  with an explicit lower timeout

## Acceptance

- `strategic-planner` successfully completes planning chain for
  a 27-bead plan on first attempt (no 180s retry).
- MCP tool warns (via structlog) when a caller's explicit timeout
  is below the enforced floor.
- Docstring on both tools names the floor and the reason.
- Regression test: invoke `nx_plan_audit(timeout=60)` and confirm
  the effective timeout used is the floor, not 60.

## Related

- v4.5.3 commit 3ece9f9 (raised defaults)
- RDR-087 accept 2026-04-17 (triggering incident)
- User feedback file
  `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/feedback_gate_accept_pause.md`
  (indirect — accept flow made this more visible)
notes: Priority P3: recurring behaviour, two known incidents (ART + RDR-087 accept). Not catastrophic (retries eventually succeed) but causes multi-minute delay per invocation and makes the planning chain look broken to the user.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #175 — _clamp_subagent_timeout helper + 5 regression tests. 300s floor enforced on nx_plan_audit and nx_enrich_beads with structlog warning on clamp. Defaults unchanged.

title: RdrResolver matches child RDR files (IMPL/post-mortem); picks candidates[0] — wrong status returned
description:
## Summary

`RdrResolver._fetch()` (after nexus-51j's case-insensitive fix) uses a
regex that matches **any** file whose stem starts with the zero-padded
RDR number, not just the canonical top-level RDR file. In ART's `docs/rdr/`,
several RDRs have sibling implementation-artifact files (e.g. a
calibration report, a supplement) that share the `RDR-NNN-` prefix. The
resolver picks `candidates[0]` (filesystem glob order), and the wrong
file wins for any RDR that has multiple `RDR-NNN-*.md` matches.

Reproduces on nx 4.5.1 with nexus-51j shipped (commit `88933bb`).

## Repro

```bash
cd /path/to/ART
ls docs/rdr/RDR-072-*.md
# RDR-072-cogem-credit-assignment.md         (main RDR, status: closed)
# RDR-072-IMPL-06-calibration-report.md      (IMPL artifact, status: passed)

cat > /tmp/test.md <<'EOF'
RDR-072 status: {{rdr:072.status}}
EOF

nx doc render /tmp/test.md --project-root "$(pwd)"
cat /tmp/test.rendered.md
# RDR-072 status: passed     <-- WRONG
# expected: "closed" (from the main RDR file)
```

The main RDR-072 file's frontmatter has `status: closed`. The IMPL-06
report's frontmatter has `status: passed` (referring to its HARD STOP
gate, not the RDR's lifecycle). The resolver conflates them.

## Root cause

In `nexus/doc/resolvers.py:_fetch()`:

```python
pattern = re.compile(
    rf"^rdr-0*{int(key)}-.+\.md$", re.IGNORECASE,
)
candidates = [
    p for p in self._rdr_dir.glob("*.md") if pattern.match(p.name)
]
```

The regex `^rdr-0*72-.+\.md$` matches any filename starting with
`RDR-072-` followed by any characters. For ART:
- `RDR-072-cogem-credit-assignment.md` (main — desired)
- `RDR-072-IMPL-06-calibration-report.md` (child artifact — undesired)

Both match. `candidates[0]` is filesystem-order-dependent; on macOS HFS+
it's alphabetical, so `IMPL` sorts before `cogem`, and the child wins.

## Impact

Silent failure: the rendered markdown shows a factually wrong status
with no warning. A reader relying on `{{rdr:072.status}}` to surface
RDR lifecycle in the docs sees "passed" (a gate state) instead of
"closed" (the actual lifecycle status).

Affected projects: any project with per-RDR child files sharing the
`RDR-NNN-` prefix. ART has at least RDR-072 with IMPL reports; likely
others as they accumulate post-mortems, calibration artifacts, etc.

## Proposed fix

Prefer the most-specific match. Options (ordered by invasiveness):

### (a) Minimal — prefer files without common "child" suffixes

If multiple files match, prefer ones whose stem has the form
`RDR-NNN-<kebab-title>` without embedded `-IMPL-`, `-post-mortem-`,
`-supplement-`, `-calibration-` tokens.

```python
def _select(cands: list[Path]) -> Path:
    CHILD_MARKERS = ("-IMPL-", "-post-mortem-", "-supplement-",
                     "-calibration-")
    primaries = [c for c in cands
                 if not any(m.lower() in c.stem.lower() for m in CHILD_MARKERS)]
    return (primaries or cands)[0]
```

### (b) Structural — require the match to have the longest shared prefix

Match only files whose stem is `RDR-NNN-<kebab-title>` with the
number followed immediately by a single kebab-cased title (no
uppercase tokens like `IMPL`). Tightest regex:

```python
pattern = re.compile(
    rf"^rdr-0*{int(key)}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\.md$", re.IGNORECASE,
)
# The [a-z] after the number enforces "next segment must start lowercase"
# which excludes IMPL / POST-MORTEM style children.
```

Combined with a fallback for projects that don't follow the all-lower
kebab convention.

### (c) Explicit declaration — add a `parent:` frontmatter key

Child files declare `parent: RDR-072` in their frontmatter; resolver
skips any file whose `parent` key points at the queried RDR. Most
invasive but scales to arbitrary child types.

Recommended: (b) for the immediate fix, (c) for the long-term
structural pattern.

## Related

- nexus-51j (closed, commit `88933bb`) — the case-insensitive fix this
  bug piggybacks on. The test harness for nexus-51j should include a
  multi-child-file fixture to prevent regression.
- ART's `primary-sources.md` Internal RDRs table — the token pilot can
  re-apply after this ships. Currently 14/15 RDRs resolve correctly;
  only RDR-072 returns wrong data.

## Actor context

Observed 2026-04-17 during the re-test of nexus-51j against ART's RDR
corpus after nx 4.5.1 upgrade. Filed as a follow-up to nexus-51j.
close_reason: Fixed via _select_primary_rdr disambiguation in src/nexus/doc/resolvers.py. Primary RDR files win over child artifacts (IMPL / post-mortem / supplement / calibration). Deterministic filesystem-independent sort. 6 regression tests + live smoke on ART RDR-072 repro. Pushed as commit that follows bb29245 on main.

title: F12 — Periodic taxonomy drift detection (nx taxonomy detect-drift)
description:
## Source

Carried from nexus-1uf (ART field report 2026-04-15 §3.3/F12) as a standalone follow-up.

## What ART discovered

RDR-081's `nx taxonomy validate-refs` solves the on-demand case: run it against a specific doc, get drift now. But the broader pattern is periodic:

- A collection receives chunks that match a topic better than its current home → ICF shifts
- Existing docs that cite the old home become stale
- No one runs validate-refs on every doc every day

Nothing in Nexus alerts on the drift without someone initiating the check.

## Proposed capability

Scheduled `nx taxonomy detect-drift`:

```bash
nx taxonomy detect-drift                      # project-wide scan
nx taxonomy detect-drift --since 2026-04-01   # since last audit
nx taxonomy detect-drift --watch              # daemon mode
```

Output: topics whose ICF-weighted best home has shifted since the last audit; referenced in indexed docs that cite the stale home.

## Implementation sketch

1. Snapshot current ICF distribution per topic (persisted as `taxonomy_audit` table).
2. On re-run, diff current vs snapshot.
3. For each shifted topic, identify docs citing the prior-owner collection (using validate-refs's scanner).
4. Report drift, optionally schedule as cron (`nx hooks schedule detect-drift`).

## Dependencies

- RDR-077 projection quality infrastructure (ICF tracking — already shipped)
- RDR-081 validate-refs scanner (reuse)
- Scheduling / daemon mode (new)

## Why this matters beyond ART

Drift is inevitable at scale. Once a project has more than a handful of collections, manual validate-refs doesn't scale. Drift detection is the natural automation layer.

## Related

- RDR-077 projection quality / ICF (substrate)
- RDR-081 validate-refs (on-demand variant)
- nexus-1uf field-report epic (source finding)

title: F7 — Pre-commit substantive-critic gate (nx doc review)
description:
## Source

Carried from nexus-1uf (ART field report 2026-04-15 §3.2/F7) as a standalone follow-up.

## What ART discovered

Substantive-critic invocation is currently post-hoc: author writes docs, commits, merges; critic runs later and finds issues. For the ART architecture collection the critic found 6 issues (2 critical, 4 significant) across 10 files that had been merged weeks earlier. Earlier invocation would have caught each at authoring time.

## Proposed capability

`nx doc review <paths>` command that:

1. Dispatches the substantive-critic agent with:
   - The changed files
   - Relevant cross-collection projection evidence (pre-injected)
   - Current bead / RDR state
2. Reports findings prioritized Critical / Significant / Minor
3. Exit code semantics: fail on Critical, warn on Significant

Git pre-commit hook (or CI gate) invokes `nx doc review` on `docs/**/*.md` changes. Runs against docs-to-be-committed, not HEAD — so it catches issues before they land.

## Dependencies

- Agent-in-loop plumbing (needs `claude_dispatch` to invoke a named agent, probably already possible via RDR-080)
- Projection data injection (already shipped — `nx taxonomy project`)
- Bead DB query (already shipped — `bd show --json`)

## Why this matters beyond ART

Pre-commit quality gates are standard for code; docs lack an equivalent. The critic has enough signal now (projection, taxonomy, bead status) to be in the loop. Makes documentation review gradient-descent instead of post-mortem.

## Related

- RDR-080 claude_dispatch (substrate)
- RDR-083 check-grounding (complementary static validator)
- nexus-1uf field-report epic (source finding)

title: F4 — Per-project notation linter (.nxlint.yml or similar)
description:
## Source

Carried forward from nexus-1uf (Architecture-as-Code epic, ART field report 2026-04-15 §3.1/F4). Filed as a standalone follow-up now that nexus-1uf can close as substantially-delivered (RDR-081/082/083/085 shipped; F4/F7/F9/F10/F12 remain).

## What ART discovered

Architecture collections accumulate multiple coexisting numbering schemes with overlapping alphabets. ART's master doc §0 now declares FIVE schemes in parallel:

- `L1`-`L6` cortical laminae (Grossberg)
- `Layer 1`-`Layer 9` system architecture (spelled out)
- `B1`-`B7` forward boundaries
- `F1`-`F7` feedback loops
- `GM1`-`GM4` Gated Multipole ODE stages

Collisions are silent bugs. Nothing prevented authors from writing `L7` (which doesn't exist in the cortical scheme — only 1-6) when they meant system Layer 7. The mis-use was only caught after-the-fact by a substantive-critic review, with dozens of fixes applied by hand.

## Proposed capability

Per-project notation rules declared once, checked on doc commit. Example `.nxlint.yml`:

```yaml
notation:
  schemes:
    cortical-laminae:
      prefix: L
      range: [1, 6]
      contexts: ["cortical", "laminar circuit"]
    system-layers:
      format: "Layer {n}"
      range: [1, 9]
      abbreviation-disallowed: true  # never write "L7" for system Layer 7
    boundaries:
      prefix: B
      range: [1, 7]
    feedback-loops:
      prefix: F
      range: [1, 7]
```

Violations (L7 appearing in prose, Layer 10 referenced, etc.) fail the lint. Integrates as pre-commit hook or CI gate.

## Scope

- CLI: `nx doc lint <paths>` or `nx taxonomy lint-notation <paths>`
- Config: `.nxlint.yml` per project or `.nexus.yml#notation`
- Exit code semantics matching `validate-refs`

## Why this matters beyond ART

Any project with domain-specific numbering (neural-circuit layers, network stack layers, protocol version numbers, etc.) has this failure mode. Nexus is the natural home since it already tracks per-project glossaries (RDR-085).

## Related

- RDR-071 query sanitizer (same class of input guard)
- RDR-085 glossary-aware labeler (complementary authoring support)

title: nx taxonomy validate-refs: proximity match false-positives on bullet lists + multi-count paragraphs
description:
## Summary

`nx taxonomy validate-refs` (RDR-081) reports **false-positive Drift**
on markdown files where a bullet list mixes chunk counts across
multiple collections. The proximity-match logic appears to treat
adjacent bullet items as "the same paragraph" for count→collection
binding, so the first chunk count gets propagated against every
subsequent collection mention in the list — each of which has its own
distinct chunk-count claim that the validator ignores.

## Repro — seen on ART `docs/architecture/primary-sources.md`

Source (clearly per-bullet claims):

```markdown
## T3 Knowledge Store Keys

- `docs__art-grossberg-papers`: 19,417 chunks (80 Grossberg papers, ...)
- `knowledge__art`: 5,724 chunks (Conscious Mind, Resonant Brain book)
- `docs__ART-8c2e74c0`: 5,006 chunks (project docs, READMEs, plans)
- `rdr__ART-8c2e74c0`: 2,683 chunks (research-design-review docs)
- `docs__art-architecture`: 101 chunks (this document set)
```

Actual T3 state matches every bullet exactly. Validator output:

```
OK     docs__art-grossberg-papers   19,417   19,417    +0   line:102
Drift  knowledge__art               19,417    5,724  -13,693 line:104
Drift  docs__ART-8c2e74c0           19,417    5,006  -14,411 line:106
Drift  rdr__ART-8c2e74c0            19,417    2,683  -16,734 line:107
Drift  docs__art-architecture       19,417      101  -19,316 line:108
```

The validator binds the `19,417` from the first bullet to **every**
subsequent collection in the list, ignoring each bullet's own count.

Same pattern triggers on paragraph-internal prose like:

```
Over 19,400 chunks ... `docs__art-grossberg-papers`. The textbook ...
5,724 chunks ... `knowledge__art`.
```

Here the validator binds `19,400` to both collection names even though
`5,724` is closer to `knowledge__art` and textually paired with it.

## Observed on

nx 4.5.0. ART architecture collection, 2026-04-16.

## Impact

- False-positive "Drift" results erode trust in the validator.
- Users learn to ignore the output or add `--ignore` patterns,
  defeating the purpose.
- Real drift (the `83 → 101` case we also caught) gets buried in noise.
- The correct signal is present (the one real drift was caught
  correctly at line 108); the problem is the false positives
  around it.

## Proposed fix

Tighten the count→collection proximity binding:

1. **Bullet-list context:** treat each list-item as its own
   scope. Don't carry numbers from one bullet into the next.
2. **Paragraph context with multiple collections:** when more than
   one collection and more than one number co-occur in a paragraph,
   bind each number to its **textually nearest** collection rather
   than always the *first* collection encountered. Edit distance or
   token distance both work.
3. **Alternative — explicit warn:** when multiple numbers appear in

title: RdrResolver case-sensitive glob blocks {{rdr:...}} tokens on projects using RDR- uppercase convention
description:
## Summary

`RdrResolver` in `src/nexus/doc/resolvers.py:169` uses case-sensitive
`Path.glob(f"rdr-{key}-*.md")` when locating RDR files for
`{{rdr:<id>.field}}` token resolution. Projects whose RDR filenames use
uppercase `RDR-` prefix (a reasonable convention — it makes RDRs
visually distinct from other `docs/` content) cannot use the
doc-render RDR tokens at all.

## Repro

```bash
cd /path/to/project
ls docs/rdr/
# RDR-068-masking-field-plan-learning.md    (uppercase prefix — common convention)
# RDR-069-language-acquisition.md
# ...

cat > /tmp/test.md <<'EOF'
RDR-068 status: {{rdr:068.status}}
EOF

nx doc render /tmp/test.md
# render error: line 1 col 16:
#   no RDR file matching rdr-068-*.md under /path/to/project/docs/rdr
#   (token='{{rdr:068.status}}')
```

## Observed on

nx 4.5.0. Project: ART (https://github.com/Hellblazer/ART), 70+ RDR
files all using the `RDR-NNN-*.md` convention. First hit during the
2026-04-16 token pilot against `docs/architecture/primary-sources.md`'s
Internal RDRs table.

## Impact

- Doc-render tokens (RDR-082) appear to work in the code but silently
  fail for any project using uppercase `RDR-` prefix.
- No indicator in the error message that case might be the issue — the
  reported "no file matching" looks like a genuine missing-file when
  the files are on disk.
- Workaround requires renaming the entire RDR tree (invasive, breaks
  prose cross-references, touches git history) or symlinking every
  file (hacky, creates a second rdr inventory).

## Proposed fix

The `key.lstrip('0').zfill(...)` normalization in lines 167-178 already
hints at tolerance-for-formatting. Extend the same logic to case:

```python
# In _fetch:
lower_key = key.lower()
# case-insensitive: glob lowercase and uppercase patterns
candidates = (list(self._rdr_dir.glob(f"rdr-{lower_key}-*.md"))
              + list(self._rdr_dir.glob(f"RDR-{lower_key}-*.md")))
if not candidates:
    candidates = list(self._rdr_dir.glob(f"rdr-{key}-*.md"))
    candidates += list(self._rdr_dir.glob(f"RDR-{key}-*.md"))
```

Or — more principled — scan `self._rdr_dir` once and match against a
case-insensitive compiled regex. Either way the cost is a single extra
glob per token, bounded by the already-present per-instance cache.

## Related

- RDR-082 (doc render / tokens) — owner of the resolver registry
- ART field report 2026-04-15 — token pilot deferred pending this fix
- Caller in `src/nexus/commands/doc.py:65` — no change needed there

## Actor context

Observed 2026-04-16 during ART architecture collection's pilot of
RDR-082 doc tokens. Pilot reverted to static text pending this fix; the
Internal RDRs table in `docs/architecture/primary-sources.md` will be
re-tokenized when this bead lands.
close_reason:
Resolved in commit 88933bb (PR #173), shipped in v4.7.0.

Fix: src/nexus/doc/resolvers.py:172-187 — RdrResolver._fetch now
iterates self._rdr_dir.glob('*.md') and matches via re.IGNORECASE
instead of case-sensitive Path.glob('rdr-{key}-*.md'). Numeric keys
still match any zero-padding of the same integer; non-numeric keys
use re.escape for safe literal matching.

Tests: 4 in tests/test_rdr_082_doc_tokens.py::TestRdrResolver all
green:
  - test_resolves_uppercase_RDR_prefix
  - test_mixed_case_cohabitation
  - test_zero_padding_still_works_case_insensitive
  - test_non_numeric_key_case_insensitive

Live smoke (uppercase RDR-068-*.md + {{rdr:068.status}} token):
  nx doc render test.md
  → rendered 1 tokens across 1 file(s)
  → "RDR-068 status: accepted"

Original bead repro (rendered 0 tokens, "no file matching" error) no
longer reproduces.

Error message also improved: now says "case-insensitive" explicitly
so future users see that case is not the issue.

title: Markdown chunker leaves source_title empty; nx store list shows all as 'untitled'
description:
## Summary

Markdown-sourced chunks in T3 consistently have empty `source_title` metadata and no fallback, causing `nx store list` to display all markdown docs as "untitled". PDF-sourced chunks have a different-but-related issue: they set a path-based `title` field (e.g., `docs/papers/foo.pdf:page-1`) but leave `source_title` missing entirely.

Observed on nx 4.4.0 while auditing `docs__art-architecture` during an ART T3 taxonomy rebuild.

## Observed behavior

| Source | extractor | `source_title` | `title` |
|--------|-----------|---------------|---------|
| `docs/GROSSBERG_NLP_CHAT_ARCHITECTURE.md` | markdown_chunker | `''` (empty) | missing |
| `docs/architecture/component-inventory.md` | markdown_chunker | `''` (empty) | missing |
| `docs/papers/carpenter-grossberg-1987-art1.pdf` | mineru | missing | `docs/papers/carpenter-grossberg-1987-art1.pdf:page-1` |

### Effect on `nx store list --docs`

```
docs__art-architecture  (10 documents, 83 chunks)
    1. untitled                                                         4 chunks    0p  markdown_chunker  2026-04-14
    2. untitled                                                         9 chunks    0p  markdown_chunker  2026-04-14
    3. untitled                                                         4 chunks    0p  markdown_chunker  2026-04-14
    ...
```

All 10 markdown docs display as "untitled" — indistinguishable from each other without reading per-chunk `source_path`.

## Expected behavior

For markdown sources, `source_title` should fall back in order of preference:

1. First H1 header (`# Title`) in the file.
2. Filename stem with underscores/dashes normalized (e.g., `GROSSBERG_NLP_CHAT_ARCHITECTURE.md` → `"Grossberg NLP Chat Architecture"`).
3. Leave empty, but ensure `nx store list` displays `source_path.name` instead of `"untitled"`.

For PDF sources, the path-based `title` field (e.g., `docs/papers/foo.pdf:page-1`) is fine as an internal chunk identifier but should be paired with a proper `source_title` derived from:

1. PDF metadata title field (if populated and non-generic).
2. MinerU/Docling-extracted H1 on first page.
3. Filename stem normalized (`carpenter-grossberg-1987-art1.pdf` → `"Carpenter Grossberg 1987 ART1"`).

Note that MinerU *does* often succeed — e.g., the Grossberg paper collection includes entries like `"grossberg 1987 cortical dynamics 3d binocular"` (hyphen-normalized filename) under `title`. So the PDF path has some fallback; it's inconsistent which field it lands in.

## Impact

- **`nx store list` unreadable for markdown-heavy collections** — can't distinguish docs without joining to `source_path`.
- **Taxonomy topic labeling** depends on title context (per `terms` + cluster content). Empty titles mean the Claude labeler sees `untitled untitled untitled` in its input, losing a high-signal disambiguation cue.
- **Document-level search results** in `nx query` lose the human-readable identifier; agents see raw `source_path` or chunk IDs.
- **Catalog entries** (from `nexus-catalog` linking) may inherit the empty title.

## Repro

```bash
# Index any markdown file into T3
nx index md docs/architecture/component-inventory.md --collection docs__test

# Inspect
nx store list docs__test --docs
# -> "untitled  ...  markdown_chunker"

# Or via python:
python -c "
import os, chromadb
c = chromadb.CloudClient(...)
col = c.get_collection('docs__test')
m = col.get(limit=1, include=['metadatas'])['metadatas'][0]
print('source_title:', repr(m.get('source_title')))
print('title:', repr(m.get('title')))
"
# -> source_title: ''    title: (missing)
```

## Proposed fix

In `nexus/indexer_utils.py` (or wherever the markdown chunker currently sits):

1. Add a `derive_title(path, content)` helper that tries H1 extraction, then filename normalization, then path-based fallback.
2. Call it during markdown chunking; always populate `source_title` with a non-empty string.
3. Unify the PDF path: make sure `source_title` is populated from the same resolution logic (MinerU metadata → H1 → filename), and `title` stays as the internal per-chunk identifier.
4. For `nx store list`, when `source_title` is empty or matches the placeholder "untitled", fall back to `Path(source_path).name` so display is still useful.

## Related

- Complements nexus-40t — both issues stem from metadata schema hygiene across extraction paths.
- Relates to RDR-077 projection quality — clean titles help Claude labeler converge on meaningful topic names (e.g., the "Gated Multipole Single Mode Fiber" hallucination in `rdr__ART-8c2e74c0`, which I just had to manually rename to "SSMF Plan-Drive Gated Multipole (RDR-068)" — SSMF is `SelfSimilarMaskingField`, not optical fiber, but the labeler mis-expanded the abbreviation without a disambiguating title anchor).

## Actor context

Observed 2026-04-15 during ART T3 taxonomy rebuild. Collection `docs__art-architecture` (10 markdown files, 83 chunks) displays all entries as "untitled" in `nx store list`. Manual inspection via `source_path` required to identify documents.
close_reason: Fixed: derive_title(path, body) helper in nexus.indexer_utils with H1 → normalised-filename fallback, preserving initialisms (PDF, NLP, ART, RDR + <prefix><digits> like art1→ART1). Wired into _markdown_chunks (frontmatter title wins, then derive_title) and _pdf_chunks (extractor title wins, then derive_title). 12 TDD tests + 139 indexer tests green. Ships in next nexus release alongside RDR-078 P3.

comments.author: Hellblazer
comments.text: Prerequisite for field-report epic nexus-1uf — source_title hygiene is a foundation for F5 (grounding validator) since title context is the Claude labeler's strongest disambiguation signal (see F2 SSMF/optical-fiber incident).

whitelist... Already beaded as nexus-jk88j (LANDMINE) blocking nexus-67qsd."

blocked by nexus-tgrgs (the actual sweep-gap fix), not by nexus-jk88j.

prose, not a process-safety gap, and nothing in the reviewed diff touches the
whitelist. But a reader who acts on "jk88j blocks 67qsd" literally (e.g.
closes jk88j expecting it to unblock 67qsd) will be surprised: the real
gate is tgrgs. Fix: correct the T2 record's §2b wording (or add a
clarifying comment on nexus-jk88j) to name nexus-tgrgs as 67qsd's actual
blocker.

title: Windows deployment parity: native engine-service binary + full local install (embedded PG)
description:
PINNED for later (not now) — full Windows parity, BOTH targets. Likely warrants its own RDR when picked up (spike-then-design); it is NOT part of the RDR-166 arc.

TARGET A — Windows native engine-service binary (cloud-habitat: connects to managed PG via NX_DB_URL, skips embedded PG). MODERATE. Add a windows-amd64 entry to engine-service-release.yml's native-build matrix, modeled on the existing mac-arm64 'build+publish, UNSMOKED' entry (GH non-Linux runners can't run the Docker-based native-smoke.sh). Concrete hurdles: (1) native-image on Windows needs MSVC (vcvars / ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd; iterative to green); (2) ONNX Runtime + DJL JNI libs must resolve win-x64 variants (pom onnx.native.dir/djl.native.dir, lines 542-543) AND the native-image reachability config under META-INF/native-image/traced is linux-traced — may need a Windows re-trace (THE decisive risk: whether native-image builds this app's ONNX+DJL JNI clean on Windows); (3) staging/sha256/ABI-floor steps are POSIX/glibc-shaped (.exe suffix, \ paths, the glibc ABI assert is N/A); (4) unsmoked → CI coverage gap (class of nexus-4xf5m). De-riskable WITHOUT a release via the workflow_dispatch path (build+upload artifact only, no GitHub Release).

TARGET B — full Windows local install (nx init --service with embedded PG). LARGE / multi-week. Pulls in the second release job (PG+pgvector relocatable bundle, engine-service-release.yml line 401) which today builds via manylinux/macos — a relocatable PG16+pgvector for Windows (pgvector via MSVC, bundle harness rewritten) is the dominant cost. PLUS the daemon launcher (binary_lifecycle.py et al.) co-locates native libs with POSIX .so assumptions, and the nx/daemon Python side assumes POSIX paths/signals — pervasive Windows-port work.

Recommended sequencing when picked up: spike Target A via workflow_dispatch first (cheap, reversible, de-risks the native-image unknown), THEN scope Target B as its own effort. Surfaced 2026-06-23 during RDR-166 wrap-up; owner wants full parity.
close_reason: CLOSE-WONTFIX — 2026-08-11 backlog groom (543 open; P3/P4 harsh-bar pass). Not wrong, not actioned: this bead self-reported as low/informational/accepted-risk at filing time, or is deferred refinement of an already-shipped fix, and has aged untouched. Against a backlog this deep an un-actioned bead has negative value — it dilutes the ones that matter. Roster + method: T2 nexus/triage-p3-p4-open-beads-2026-08-11 [22227]. REVERSIBLE: 'bd reopen nexus-neo3e' if it resurfaces — closing WONTFIX is deliberately cheap to undo, which is why the bar was set here rather than lower. Admin close, no code change — review gate overridden deliberately.

description: Follow-on to nexus-xmohw (single-writer serialization, shipped). The serialization eliminates INTRA-daemon write contention (the GH #1137 reproduced trigger). Two coupled hardening steps remain for the CROSS-PROCESS / version-skew double-writer case (nx index direct-fallback, nx taxonomy CLI epsilon-allow connections racing the daemon): (1) 2.1b BEGIN IMMEDIATE — set isolation_level=None and issue explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE on multi-step write txns so a read->write upgrade does NOT return SQLITE_BUSY instantly-ignoring-busy_timeout (catalog_taxonomy.py:243 + audit memory_store/plan_library/aspect_extraction_queue/telemetry/chash_index/document_aspects connections); (2) 2.1c fast-fail serving busy_timeout — SERVING_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 (_tuning.py:19) is too long if BEGIN IMMEDIATE makes busy_timeout actually engage. MUST LAND TOGETHER: adding BEGIN IMMEDIATE alone (with the 30s busy_timeout) would create up to ~181s head-of-line lock-hold under contention; 2.1c bounds it. WHY NOT URGENT: current DEFERRED connections fail-fast on upgrade-busy so the serialized lock-hold stays ~1.55s (backoff, now outside the lock per critic C2 fix); single-writer model + spawn-lock already prevent most cross-process writers. Substantive-critic flagged both as named-but-undone fix directions (correct); deferring is honest scope, not silent reduction. RDR-151 §Revised Plan 2.1b/2.1c. Validate with a cross-process contention soak (daemon + concurrent nx index).
notes: Grooming pass (2026-07-12): LOWER P2->P4. Verified src/nexus/db/storage_mode.py:171-178: SERVICE (Postgres) is now the hard default for all stores including T1/T2; SQLite is an explicit opt-out only. The BEGIN IMMEDIATE/busy_timeout hardening this bead describes only matters on that now-non-default opt-out path -- matches its own already-set superseded-by-rdr-152 label that was never acted on.

title: BACKLOG: blocking_take per-subspace notification channel (v2 redesign)
description:
**Backlog / future work.** From the 360° architectural review + DR-5.

## Motivation

`blocking_take` currently polls every 10ms and wakes on ANY `data_version` increment. For multi-agent multi-subspace deployments, this scales poorly: N callers × M cross-subspace commits = N×M speculative lock acquisitions per tick.

## Direction

Replace data_version polling with a per-subspace `threading.Event` (or asyncio.Event) registry:
- The daemon's writer fires events.set() for each subspace on commit
- blocking_take registers as a waiter on its subspace's Event
- Wakes are subspace-targeted; no spurious

## Status

NOT scheduled. Reactivate when multi-agent multi-subspace deployments hit the contention floor or a concrete latency complaint arrives. Single-user same-subspace contention is fine on the current implementation.
close_reason: Closed

title: reidentify: collapse two-pass into one with snapshot-id-set guard
description:
## Problem

reidentify_collection uses a two-pass design: pass 1 collects all ids (paginated col.get with include=[]), pass 2 fetches by exact id and upserts. This pays a 2x round-trip tax (pass 1 reads ids that pass 2 immediately re-fetches with metadata).

The two-pass form exists to sidestep offset-instability during in-loop upserts (in-loop upserts add records, shifting offset semantics for later pages). Comments at \`t3_reidentify.py:152-166\` explain.

## Fix

Single-pass alternative: collect the snapshot id-set at start (one full paginated walk with include=[]); then iterate the snapshot ids in batches with col.get(ids=batch, include=[everything]). This is essentially what the current two-pass does but expressed as one nested loop, retaining the snapshot-id-set as the offset-stability anchor.

Result: same round-trips, simpler control flow.

## Cost/benefit

Low priority. The two-pass form is correctness-preserving and operationally proven. Refactor is mostly cosmetic; risk of regression on the offset-instability scenario the docstring calls out.

## Out of scope

Does NOT eliminate the 2x round-trip tax (the snapshot-id-set step is the same paginated walk pass-1 does today). For round-trip reduction see the within-collection pipelining bead.

## Refs
- Discussed during Hal/operator exchange in Phase 5 migration session (2026-05-09).
close_reason: Wontfix on inspection. The two-pass form is correctness-preserving and operationally proven across the Phase 5 prod migration. The proposed single-pass refactor doesn't reduce round-trips (snapshot collection step is the same paginated walk pass-1 does today), it's only cosmetic. Risk of regression on the offset-instability scenario the existing docstring (t3_reidentify.py:152-166) explicitly calls out outweighs the cosmetic gain. Round-trip reduction is tracked separately in nexus-zpnq (within-collection pipelining).

title: Flake: test_preflight_registration_idempotent_on_staleness_skip JSONDecodeError on Linux CI
description:
RDR-105 P5 release-prep observation. CI run 25527046864 (the
develop->main merge PR) failed this single test with
``JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 1 column 5 (char 4)`` at
tests/test_doc_indexer.py:1981 reading
``json.loads(result.output)`` where ``result.output`` came from
``nx catalog doctor --replay-equality``.

Same code passed CI on 5 other runs (P4 PR, P4 push, P5-prep PR,
P5-prep push to develop, merge push to main) and 5 local runs +
full-module local run (102/102).

Suspected cause: stdout/stderr interleaving on Linux runner under
load. ``nx catalog doctor`` may emit a log line to stdout that
gets concatenated with the JSON payload before the test reads
``result.output``. CliRunner's ``mix_stderr`` defaults vary across
click versions.

Suggested investigation:

1. Run with ``CliRunner(mix_stderr=False)`` to verify the extra
   data was a log line bleeding from stderr.
2. Audit ``nexus.commands.catalog.doctor_cmd`` (and any helpers it
   calls) for ``click.echo()`` or ``print()`` calls that should
   emit through ``click.echo(..., err=True)`` instead.
3. If the issue is ``structlog`` logging on stdout, redirect to
   stderr in CLI commands that emit JSON.

Filed during the conexus 4.27.0 release. Did not block the
release; the same code passed CI on the merge commit. Track for
when CI flakes accumulate.
close_reason: Closed

title: P3.2 Regression alert: relative >=10% drop AND absolute floor
description: Phase 3 / Item 2 of RDR-090. Add a comparison step to the bench workflow (P3.1) that fails the run when EITHER (a) NDCG@3 on any category drops >=10% relative to the most recent baseline in bench/baselines/, OR (b) absolute floor breach: factual NDCG@3 < 0.3 (or category-specific floors documented in bench/floors.yaml). The absolute floor was a gate-critic recommendation (research-1004 observation 3: CI regression alert is relative not absolute — consider an absolute floor for high-stakes categories). Both checks must fire independently — a slow drift below floor with <10% per-week drop would otherwise sneak through the relative-only check. Implement as scripts/bench/check_regression.py invoked from the workflow; emit a structured failure annotation (GitHub Actions error annotation: two-colon-error-two-colon prefix) naming the category, the previous value, the current value, and which check tripped. Reminder: TDD with synthetic baseline + current JSON pairs covering: clean pass, relative trip, absolute trip, both trip; SPAWN sub-agents; sequential-thinking for the check logic.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/bench/check_regression.py compares two JSON reports and exits non-zero on relative >=10% drop OR absolute floor breach; unit tests cover clean / relative-trip / absolute-trip / both-trip; workflow integration step calls the script and the workflow correctly fails on a synthetic regression artifact; bench/floors.yaml documents per-category floors with rationale; failure messages are actionable (category + delta + which check).
notes: 2026-05-17 audit: downgraded with parent ic83. scripts/bench/check_regression.py absent; depends on P3.1 workflow.

title: P3.1 GitHub Actions weekly bench workflow
description: Phase 3 / Item 1 of RDR-090. Author .github/workflows/bench.yml — weekly cron-triggered (proposed: Monday 06:00 UTC) GitHub Actions workflow that runs scripts/bench/runner.py against bench/queries/*.yaml on a CI runner, uploads the JSON report as a workflow artifact, and commits a versioned snapshot to bench/baselines/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json on a dedicated branch (or PR). Estimated runtime per RDR: 30 queries × 3 paths × ~2s = ~3 min — well within free-tier budget. Workflow inputs: Voyage AI API key (existing repo secret VOYAGE_API_KEY), ChromaDB Cloud creds (existing). manual workflow_dispatch trigger for ad-hoc runs. Reminder: SPAWN sub-agents for the YAML scaffold; sequential-thinking only if non-trivial concurrency/cost questions arise; smoke-test locally first via 'act' or scoped repo run.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/bench.yml runs weekly on schedule + manual trigger; uploads JSON artifact; produces a deterministic-name baseline snapshot per run; one successful CI run completes within 10 min wall clock; failure modes (Voyage 429, ChromaDB quota) emit useful error logs and don't silently no-op.

title: P2.3 Author 10 compositional queries (multi-RDR decision chains)
description: Phase 2 / Item 3 of RDR-090. Author 10 compositional (3+-hop, requires plan composition) queries from multi-RDR decision chains. Example per RDR §Technical Design: 'What retrieval architecture decisions were made across RDR-078, 079, 080, and what was the sequence of tradeoffs?' Output: bench/queries/compositional.yaml. EXPECT some queries to require force_dynamic to land non-zero NDCG@3 — spike Q5 finding (research-1002): plan #38 (the matched plan) was a 2-step search→summarize wrapper that reduced path C to a thin wrapper on path A; true path C value emerges only when the plan library carries genuinely-multi-step plans OR when force_dynamic skips matching. ANNOTATE per-query whether plan-library depth is suspected to be the bottleneck (per RDR §Path C compositional contingency note). Coarser metric per RDR §Risks: 'did the system retrieve at least 3 of 5 listed documents?' rather than exact ranking — encode as multi_hop_required: [...] in YAML. Reminder: SPAWN sub-agents; sequential-thinking for chain decomposition; chunk-aware authoring discipline still applies.
acceptance_criteria: bench/queries/compositional.yaml with 10 hand-authored compositional queries; each lists ≥3 required documents in GT; per-query annotation flagging whether plan-library depth is the suspected path-C bottleneck; bench harness runs all 10 cleanly across 3 paths and computes multi-hop precision metric; committed alongside authoring notes.

title: P2.2 Author 10 comparative queries (cross-RDR + cross-corpus)
description: Phase 2 / Item 2 of RDR-090. Author 10 comparative (two-chunk, different-document) queries with cross-RDR and where viable cross-corpus comparisons (ART + Delos + RDR). Examples per RDR §Technical Design: 'Compare the RDR-049 catalog model with the paper's KG approach.' Cross-corpus reduces author bias (RDR §Risks: GT-labeling bias from author who is also primary RDR author). Output: bench/queries/comparative.yaml. Same chunk-aware authoring discipline as P2.1: refine query if expected docs don't surface. Spike Q4 (comparative on hooks) returned NDCG@3=0.469 path A, 0 paths B/C — comparative is a real discriminator class even at N=5. Relevance grades 0–3. Reminder: SPAWN sub-agents; sequential-thinking for cross-corpus framing; consult catalog graph (nx catalog links-for-file) to find genuinely-comparable doc pairs.

title: P2.1 Author 10 factual queries with chunk-aware authoring discipline
description: Phase 2 / Item 1 of RDR-090. Author 10 factual (single-hop, single-chunk-answer) queries against real Nexus corpora and label ground truth. Examples per RDR §Technical Design: 'Which RDR introduced catalog tumblers?' Output: bench/queries/factual.yaml with the schema documented in RDR-090 §Ground truth format. CHUNK-AWARE AUTHORING (mandatory, from spike Q2 lesson): inspect top-K chunk results during authoring; if the expected RDR does NOT surface, refine the QUERY, not the GT. Q2 ('Which RDR added the content-hash chunk index?') got NDCG@3=0 universally because GT vocab 'content-hash chunk index' did not match the chunks' actual vocab. Discipline mirrors RDR-090's anti-circularity stance — refine query semantics until corpus can answer, never pad GT post-hoc. Time budget: ~5–10 min per query authored + GT (extrapolated from spike). Relevance grades 0–3 per RDR. Reminder: SPAWN sub-agents; sequential-thinking for tricky query semantics; TDD via bench harness re-run after each batch of 5.
acceptance_criteria: bench/queries/factual.yaml with 10 hand-authored queries on real Nexus corpora, each with corpus, ground_truth (chunk-keyed by RDR-prefix substring matching the spike convention), graded 0–3, and an acceptance.ndcg_at_3 floor; bench harness runs all 10 successfully on all 3 paths (no schema errors, no resolver failures); none returns universal-zero NDCG@3 across paths (universal zero means query-vocab failure — refine and re-author); committed alongside a brief authoring notes file.

title: RDR-090 Realistic AgenticScholar Benchmark

title: nx doctor --check=quotas: voyage + chromadb headroom
description:
Follow-up split from nexus-vatx Gap 5 after Gaps 1–3 + 4a shipped (PRs #207, #208, #210 on 2026-04-19).

## Why

Operator has no way to check 'are we near a rate limit?' before or during a long indexing run. nx doctor already covers schema + search probes (RDR-087 Phase 3) but not transient-error headroom.

## Proposed shape

- nx doctor --check=quotas queries current Voyage + ChromaDB quota usage and compares against QUOTAS in src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py.
- Report per-operation headroom (writes/reads in flight vs MAX_CONCURRENT_*, records/document sizes vs caps).
- Surface a red-yellow-green verdict plus the most-constrained resource.

## Acceptance

- [ ] --check=quotas flag on nx doctor
- [ ] Voyage probe returns current requests/min and computes headroom against the 300-rpm target
- [ ] ChromaDB probe returns per-collection concurrency observed vs MAX_CONCURRENT_READS/MAX_CONCURRENT_WRITES
- [ ] JSON + table output modes match existing doctor checks
- [ ] Integration test against a fake voyage/chromadb client

## Priority

P4 per parent bead description: 'future, larger' — not critical but enables pre-flight diagnostics.

## Related

- nexus-vatx (parent; closed 2026-04-19)
- src/nexus/db/chroma_quotas.py (QUOTAS dataclass, QuotaValidator)
close_reason: Fixed in PR #215. nx doctor --check-quotas emits a three-section report (ChromaDB Cloud limits + reachability probe, Voyage AI model caps + VOYAGE_API_KEY presence, cumulative retry accumulator). --json for dashboards. Exit 1 on unreachable cloud. Live-verified on production. 6 new tests in TestCheckQuotas. Acceptance item 'current requests/min' scoped down to retry-accumulator summary — see PR scope note.

title: nx search: per-prefix distance threshold silently drops hits from dense-prose collections
description:
## Summary

`nx search --corpus <name>` returns zero results against collections
whose content is dense prose (scholarly PDFs) even though the content
is indexed and reachable. The same query against a markdown-heavy
collection returns hits; the same query via the prefix broadcast
(`--corpus docs`) returns hits too — but not from the dense-prose
collection. Users conclude their collection is broken.

This is a **silent threshold-filter** behaviour, not a routing bug.

Affected installs: any user with a collection of scholarly PDF chunks
under the `docs__` (or similarly thresholded) prefix.

## Reproduces on nx 4.5.3 (2026-04-17).

## Repro

```bash
# Content verification — chunks exist:
nx collection list | grep docs__art-grossberg-papers
# Output: docs__art-grossberg-papers    19417 chunks

# Exact collection name — returns "No results.":
nx search "Grossberg neural" --corpus docs__art-grossberg-papers -m 3
# Output: No results.

# Markdown collection — works:
nx search "Grossberg neural" --corpus docs__art-architecture -m 3
# Output: multiple hits

# Prefix broadcast — also works, but hits come from sibling
# markdown-heavy collections (docs__ART-8c2e74c0, docs__default),
# NOT from docs__art-grossberg-papers:
nx search "Grossberg neural" --corpus docs -m 10 --json
# All 10 hits from docs__ART-8c2e74c0 and docs__default; zero
# from docs__art-grossberg-papers.
```

## Root cause

Per-prefix distance threshold in `src/nexus/config.py`:

```python
"distance_threshold": {
    "docs": 0.65,
    ...
}
```

Applied in `src/nexus/search_engine.py:226-234`:

```python
raw = t3.search(query, [col], n_results=per_k, where=effective_where)
for r in raw:
    distance = r["distance"]
    if threshold is not None and distance > threshold:
        dropped += 1
        continue
    ...
```

Direct ChromaDB probes (voyage-context-3, input_type="query"):

| Collection                       | Content type            | Top-3 cosine distances |
|----------------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|
| docs__art-grossberg-papers       | scholarly PDF prose     | 0.81 / 0.81 / 0.82     |
| docs__art-architecture           | markdown headers/lists  | 0.51 / 0.53 / 0.55     |

The 0.65 threshold calibrated for markdown/README-style `docs__`
content drops every scholarly-PDF hit. CCE query↔document alignment
has an intrinsic floor: re-embedding a chunk's verbatim text as a
query yields cos_sim 0.87 (cos_dist 0.13), not 1.0 — dense prose
is never going to hit the same similarity ceiling that short
markdown chunks do.

## Not-the-cause list (verified 2026-04-17)

- ❌ Hyphen-splitting in corpus parser — `resolve_corpus` at
  `src/nexus/corpus.py:113-117` treats `__`-containing names as
  atomic exact-match. No hyphen manipulation.
- ❌ Embedding-model mismatch — both collections stored with
  `embedding_model: voyage-context-3`; query path uses the same.
- ❌ Collection registration error — appears correctly in
  `list_collections()` and `resolve_corpus` match.
- ❌ ChromaDB quota / rate limit — direct query returns 19,417 chunks
  with valid distances.

## Impact

- **Silent failure** is the real ergonomic cost. Users see "No
  results." and conclude the collection is empty or broken. The
  threshold filter drops N candidates without reporting.
- **RDR research passes** targeting a specific PDF collection must
  fall back to prefix broadcasts, losing specificity and pulling in
  unrelated collections.
- **nexus-51j** (case-sensitive glob) was a similar class: silent
  name-handling mismatch with zero-result symptom.

## Fix options (not mutually exclusive)

1. **Log threshold-drop rate when all candidates are dropped**
   (cheapest; debug-only by default; flip to stderr one-liner when
   `result_count == 0 AND raw_count > 0`). Prevents future
   misdiagnosis of the same class.
2. **Expose per-query threshold override**:
   `nx search --threshold 1.0` / `--no-threshold`. Cheap user
   workaround when users know their collection is dense prose.
3. **Per-collection calibrated thresholds** in T2 (similar to
   taxonomy-projection-tuning). Automated from recent-query history
   or nightly calibration. Higher-cost, best UX.
4. **Raise the docs default** (e.g. 0.85) — risks more false
   positives on normal docs content; not recommended without
   calibration methodology.

Recommended v1: option 1 + option 2 together. Low-risk, unblocks
users, makes the class of bug discoverable.

## Related

- RDR-081 (ART side) — grounding migration was forced onto
  `knowledge__art` because `docs__art-grossberg-papers` returned
  empty.
- nexus-51j (case-sensitivity in RDR resolver glob) — same failure
  shape: name handling silently drops input.
notes:
## Root cause (2026-04-17 investigation)

NOT a corpus-router bug. `resolve_corpus` at src/nexus/corpus.py:113-117
already treats `__`-containing names as atomic exact-match. No hyphen
splitting anywhere in the search path (registry.py:107 rsplit is for
sibling discovery, not routing).

**Actual cause**: distance-threshold-vs-content mismatch.

- The `docs` prefix default distance threshold is 0.65 (config.py).
- `docs__art-grossberg-papers` (scholarly PDF chunks) top-3 cosine
  distances are 0.80–0.82 for the query "Grossberg neural".
- `docs__art-architecture` (markdown headers/lists) top-3 distances
  are 0.51–0.55 for the same query.
- Threshold filter in search_engine.py:226-234 drops all grossberg
  hits silently; CLI/MCP returns "No results."

**Why the prefix-broadcast "worked"**: sibling collections in the docs
prefix (docs__ART-8c2e74c0 and docs__default) contain the same or
similar content at lower cosine distance (0.34–0.49 — markdown/README
chunks that mention Grossberg in headers). The prefix broadcast
returns those hits; users misread the source collection.

**Empirical verification** (direct ChromaDB CloudClient + voyage-context-3,
input_type="query"):
- Stored-chunk round-trip: re-embedding verbatim stored text as query
  yields cos_sim 0.87 (dist 0.13), NOT 1.0 — CCE query↔document
  alignment has an intrinsic floor, worse for scholarly prose than
  for markdown headers.
- Distances are content-class-dependent, not collection-name-dependent.

## Revised fix

Options (not mutually exclusive):

1. **Expose per-query threshold override**: `nx search --threshold 1.0`
   (or `--no-threshold`) to bypass the config default when the user
   knows their collection is dense prose.
2. **Calibrate threshold per-collection** instead of per-prefix. T2
   could store a calibrated threshold from recent query history
   (similar to how taxonomy-projection thresholds are tuned).
3. **Emit a log/warning when a collection returns zero post-threshold
   hits** but returned raw hits pre-threshold (distinguish "empty
   collection" from "all filtered by threshold"). This would have
   immediately shown the cause during the RDR-081 investigation.
4. **Raise the docs threshold** to something like 0.85 — BUT this
   risks more false positives for normal docs content. Calibration
   methodology needed.

The user-facing "silent zero" is the real ergonomic bug. Option 3
(debug-logged threshold-filter-rate) is the cheapest fix and would
prevent future misdiagnosis. Option 1 is the cheapest user workaround.

Downgrade to P4 or reclassify as UX bug pending priority call.
close_reason: Superseded by RDR-087 Phase 1 (nexus-yi4b.1.1 + nexus-yi4b.1.2). Both recommended v1 fixes shipped: (1) silent-zero stderr note via _maybe_emit_silent_zero_note in search_cmd.py fires when post-threshold results=0 but raw_count>0, with suggested --threshold value; (2) --threshold DISTANCE and --no-threshold flags on nx search, plus --quiet to suppress the note. 16 threshold/silent-zero tests green. No residual code work.

title: F10 — Graph-first doc authoring: markdown views over catalog graph
description:
## Source

Carried from nexus-1uf (ART field report 2026-04-15 §3.3/F10) as a standalone follow-up.

## What ART discovered

Current architecture docs are 10 flat markdown files with duplicated cross-references, drift-prone "see X.md" prose, and repeated author-extension disclaimers. Each piece of content exists in exactly one place; moving it breaks references. Refactoring the collection is high-effort because every link is path-addressed.

## Proposed capability

Catalog-graph as primary representation. Every claim is a node, every citation a typed edge, every doc a named view:

```bash
nx doc render view:architecture-master   # produces a master doc
nx doc render view:layer4-semantic       # produces layer-4 deep-dive
```

Refactoring becomes a graph rewrite (move/merge/split nodes), not a file-path edit.

## Status

Partially covered by RDR-078 (unified context graph — traverse + graph_many) which ships the navigation primitive. The authoring layer (views, rendering templates, node editing) is separate scope.

## Dependencies

- RDR-078 shipped (prerequisite)
- RDR-083 chash tokens + corpus evidence (citation primitive exists)
- RDR-086 chash resolution (verification layer — currently draft)
- Rendering template system (new)

## Why this matters beyond ART

Graph-native documentation scales better than flat markdown for any substantial project. The catalog-graph substrate already exists for search/retrieval; authoring is the natural extension.

## Related

- RDR-078 unified context graph and retrieval (prerequisite)
- RDR-083 corpus-evidence tokens (citation primitive)
- RDR-086 chash span resolution (verification)
- nexus-1uf field-report epic (source finding)

title: F9 — Symbol-analysis integration for live Implemented-but-Not-Wired views
description:
## Source

Carried from nexus-1uf (ART field report 2026-04-15 §3.3/F9) as a standalone follow-up.

## What ART discovered

`component-inventory.md` §Implemented but Not Wired is hand-maintained. During the 2026-04-15 session, ART confirmed `SemanticResponseField` was wired despite a prior MEMORY.md entry claiming it was dead code — meaning the manual table had drifted. A call-graph analyzer would answer "zero production callers" deterministically.

## Proposed capability

Integrate repo indexing with JVM / Python / TypeScript symbol analysis. Expose call-graph queries via:

```bash
nx code call-graph <class-name>
nx code find-unused <glob>
nx code list-callers <symbol>
```

Allows documentation to embed queries rather than hand-maintained tables. Natural fit as a `nx doc` token extension:

```markdown
{{code:SemanticResponseField.caller-count}}
{{code:chatsome-language/unused-classes}}
```

## Dependencies

- Serena JetBrains backend (already integrated for Claude Code) — extension point
- LSP integration for non-JVM projects
- Probably a new `nexus.code` module parallel to `nexus.doc`

## Why this matters beyond ART

Any project with drift between implementation and documentation has this failure mode. Call-graph-backed tables shift the correctness burden from "manual discipline" to "tool invariant."

## Related

- RDR-078 traverse (adjacent graph-walking primitive)
- Serena MCP integration (extension point)
- nexus-1uf field-report epic (source finding)
